Casparus Brochmandus p. m. sed rectius negatur eodem cum Judæis die à Christo Pa- scha celebratum esse.

Et Græci quidem recentiores Christum an- ticipasse volunt legalem Paschatos terminum, de- cimum quartum Nisan, adeoque decimo tertio ultimum suum Pascha celebrasse: quod videre etiam est in Jeremiæ Patriarchæ Constantinopolitani censura confessionis August. c. 13. quorum vero sententia merito ab Occidentalibus reprobata est: siquidem ita Christus contra legem egisset, & com- minationi divinæ Num. IIX, 13. obnoxius factus fuisset: qui vero omnem legis justitiam implevit Matth. III, 15. Adde, quod Christus ultimum suum Pascha celebravit primo die Azymorum, quæ diverso respectu fuit decimus quartus & decimus quintus, nullatenus decimus tertius: uti B. Ger- hardus, Harm. c. 166. pag. 1067. observavit: quod decima quarta dies fuerit initium esus azymorum Exod. 12, 18. juxta civilem computationem, qua vespera illa mactationis, & esus agni relata ad diem præcedentem ceu clausula ejusdem, utpote media nocte inchoatam: juxta legis vero dispositionem relata fuerit ad diem sequentem decimam quintam, vi cujus dies festi incipiebant à vespera, Levit. 23. vers. 32.

Alii notant, quod initium ejus azymorum fuerit die 14. exeunte, & 15. ineunte, mactatio au- tem agni paschalis facta sit intra duas vesperas, ho- ra 3. nostra promeridiana Exod. XII, 6. Confer. Joh. Wichmann. Chronol. Sacr. libr. 1. pag. 12. 14. qui observat diem 14. ab Evangelistis Matth. 26. vers. 17. Marc. 14, 12. Luc. 22, 7. vocatum primum azymorum, quod eo mox post prandium fermen- tum omne ex ædibus fuerit eliminatum panesque azymi parati, qui vespera sequenti, quæ diem 15.

inchoabat, manducari cœperunt. Denique quid luculentius verbis Lucæ c. 22. v. 7. venit dies azymo- rum, in quo necesse erat occidi Pascha: Necesse utique erat juxta legem, quam noluit violatam, sed obser- vatam Salvator.

Alii ergo post Paulum Burgensem Christum legalem terminum observasse, Judæos vero non eo- dem die, sed sequenti decimo quinto Pascha come- disse solide docent, quæ plerorumque nostratium, ut & Reformatorum, Calvini, Deodati, Piscatoris, Scaligeri, Casauboni, Baflii, Annotatorum Angli- canorum, ut & è Pontificiis Jansenii, Maldonati, Petavii est sententia: Judæos in fine diei decimi quinti, ac principio decimi sexti feria sexta finiente, & septimana incipiente Pascha suum tum celebras- se. Quæ probatur primo è Joh. 18. v. 28. quod Judæi noluerint intrare in prætorium, cum mane Jesus à Caipha in prætorium deductus est, ut non contaminarentur, sed ut manducarent Pascha. Nondum ergo tum comederant Pascha: quod Christus jam præterita nocte comederat: quem evidentissimum locum aliter elidere non potuit Cardinalium doctissimorum triga, Toletus, Bellar- minus, Baronius, quam tali commento, quod pla- ne textui contrariatur, Johannem non intelligen- dum esse de agno Paschali, sed de sacrificiis, quæ septem diebus azymorum offerebantur. At Jo- hannes diserte, ut manducarent PASCHA, non ut offerrent sacrificia: item, ut non contaminarentur, quod maxime solemnitas, & sanctitas ipsius Pascha- tos requirebat.

Quod vero Marcus Antonius de Dominis lib. V. de Rep. c. 6. §. 272. præeunte, ut ostendit Casaubonus Exercitat. 16. §. 12. Cedreno, Petro A- lexandrino, Metrodoro, & alio quodam anonymo, Christum negat in ultima cœna agnum Pascha- lem comedisse, palam refragatur Evangelistis, Matth. 26, 17. seqq. & Luc. 22, 15. quodque illos sequentes Hugo Grotius ad Matth. 28, 18. ejusque asseda Hamondus ad Marc. 14, 12. Christum fin- gunt μνημονευτικὸν tantum Pascha comedisse, non θύσιμον, adeoque, etsi die decimo tertio comede- rit, legem non violasse, quia Pascha illud memo- rativum lege non fuit mandatum, sed ritus volun- tarius, quo sine agno panes azymi cum herbis amaris in memoriam paschatis comesti, non vacat blasphe- mia, quod nempe Christus, neglecta lege divina, superstitionem voluntariam sequutus fuerit, quodque Pascha ejus non fuerit pascha, nisi æqui- voce; uti Grotius diserte, hæc cœna commemora- tiva Paschatis quanquam ἄθυτος, vocatur πάσχα ὁμωνύμως.

Deinde Joh. 13, 1. Christus ante diem festum Pa- schatos ultimam cœnam celebrasse dicitur, quod non potest aliter accipi, quam, uti nostra habet senten- tia, quod cœnam suam, & in ea Pascha celebrarrit ante diem festi Paschatos Judæorum.

Accedit tertio, quod Christus Joh. XIX, 14. condemnatus dicatur in Parasceve Paschatos, adeoque ante Pascha Judæorum, qui jam præte- rita nocte Pascha suum cum discipulis celebrarar.

Quarto cum Joh. 19, 31. Sabbatum post mortem Christi dicitur magnum, aliunde id non est, quam quod primus azymorum juxta celebrationem, quæ à Judæis fiebat, in Sabbatum inciderit; unde major illis erat istius diei solemnitas, quia primus azymorum festus erat, adeoque Sabbatum hac fe- stivitate auctum magnum habebatur. Sive au- tem ex ignorantia Sacerdotum, & incerta Novilu- niorum calatione, quod Petavio post Ludov. Die- vium visum est, sive à translatione primi Azymo- rum in Sabbatum, ne duæ magnæ folemnitates fe continuo fequerentur, primus Azymorum inci- derit in Sabbatum, quod Paulus Burgenfis, Scaliger & Cafaubonus è teftimoniis Rabbinorum probant, & ad decretum Synedrii referunt, parum refert: quamvis hæc fententia vero fit fimilior, neque translatio ifta feriarum temere cum Gerh. Joh. Voffio, Dievio & Cochio neganda videatur, & lucu- lenta Judæorum teftimonia, & confenfum Chro- nologorum & Philologorum præcipuorum, è qui- bus B. Gerhardus laudavit Joh. Lucidum, Onu- phrium, Stöflerum, Bunting. Liveleum, Calvi- fium, Hentenium, Gagneum, Janfenium, Salme- ron. Maldonatum, Münsterum, Ofiandrum, Flacium, Bucerum, Chemnitium, Hunnium, & qui his præivere, Paulum de S. Maria Burgen- fem, nec non Paulum Mittelburgenf. Forofempro- nienfem Epifcopos, ut & priorem illis Rupertum in c. 26. Matth.

5. Quinto fi eodem cum Chrifto die Judæi pa- fcha celebraffent, luna nempe decima quarta, fe- quente utique die, ceu primo Azymorum, adeoque fefto fervilia opera illicita fuiffent, à quibus reli- gione Sabbati abftinuiffent. At decima quinta die, feu feria fexta caufas agebant capitales, & Chriftum crucifigebant, & alia opera à fefto die aliena peragebant, etiam illi, qui maxime fuperfti- tiofi erant in obfervatione legis ceremonialis, atque ideo quoque, ne tumultus oriretur, fefto fo- lemni talia tentare verebantur, tefte Matthæo c. 26. v. 5. dicebant enim: Non in die fefto, ne tumultus fiat in populo.

6. Sexto Nicodemus, & Jofephus eo die, quo Chriftus Pafcha celebraverat, emerunt unguenta, ac fyndonem, & Chrifti crucifixi corpus tulerunt de cruce, & unctum fepelierunt, Marc. 15. v. 46. Luc. 23, 53. quod non permififfent ipfis Judæi, fi Pafcha eo die celebraffent. Et teftatur Marcus aperte, quod tum adhuc fuerit προσάϐϐατον. Jo- hannes c. 19. 42. addit, factum id effe, quod Chriftum in monumentum repofuerint, propter parafeven Ju- dæorum: ut ante Pafchalem eorum feftivitatem hoc officio defungerentur.

7. Septimo quid luculentius effe poteft illa Jo- hannis relatione cap. 19, 31. Judæi ergo quoniam pa- rafeve erat (nondum itaque Pafcha celebrarant) ut non remanerent in cruce corpora Sabbato (fefto Pafchatos) erat enim magnus ille dies Sabbati. Un- de evidentiffime conftat, imminuiffe adhuc feftivi- tatem Pafchatis Judæorum, cum Chriftus jam ex- fpirasset, non vero jam Pafcha cum Chrifto ab iis- dem celebratum fuiffe.

Quod objicitur è Matth. 26, 2. fcitis, quod poft biduum fiet Pafcha, intelligendum, quod Pa- fcha fecundum legem futurum fit, atque celebrari debuerit. De quo etiam Marci verba cap. 14, 12. accipienda, quando Pafcha immolabant, id eft, quando neceffe erat immolari Pafcha, ut explicat Lucas cap. 22, 17. adeoque immolabant etiam illi, qui, miffis traditionibus, legis erant obfervantes, quales nonnullos penes Judæos adhuc fuiffe, ve- rifimile eft. Erant certe ex informatione Chrifti ejus difcipuli, ad quos verba illa, quando immola- bant Pafcha, non male etiam referri poffe obfervat Bailius. Vid. de hac quæftione plura in Harm. B. Gerhard. c. 166. p. 1077. & in difcurfu Pauli Bur- genfis de Pafchatis ςαυρωσίμꙋ à Chrifto & Judæis in- ftituta celebratione, notis D. Joh. Behm. illuftrato, nec non in Annotat. noftris Anti-Grot. ad Evange- liftarum loca citata.

An Christus feria quinta passus sit, an vero sexta?

POsterius unanimi consensu affirmant Ecclesiæ Doctores, & S. literarum Interpp. ac Chronologi: à quo vero abire placuit Wilhelmo Langio, qui libr. II. de annis Christi pag. 379. non dubitavit asserere, quod infallibilis ac ἀναντίλεϰ[τος] passionis character sit, quod incidat in feriam quintam, sive diem Jovis; non feriam sextam, sive diem Veneris, sicut hactenus, ut ait, perperam creditum. Et pag. 422. Christum, inquit, in Parasceve Paschatis, feria quinta passum esse, ita ex Scripturis demonstratur, ut nemini Christiano contra fari integrum sit. Quam temeritatem ex merito castigavit Dn. D. Wandalinus jam præcipuus in regno Daniæ Episcopus, amicus noster singularis, Diatribe Historico - Theologica de feria passionis Lipsiæ anno 1651. edita. Refragatur certe novella opinio expressissimis Scripturæ testimoniis: quæ diem passionis Christi Parasceven nominat: & quidem non solum παρασκευὴν τõ πάσχα, Joh. 19, 31. ne forte negetur Pascha Judæorum in Sabbatum incidisse, sed absolute παρασκευὴν, quo nomine absolute posito semper feria sexta designatur, dies scilicet illa, quæ Sabbatum antecedit, quemadmodum contra, ubi festi alicujus annui Parasceve insinuatur, semper festi illius mentio adjicitur; imo ut luculentius constaret, Parasceven Sabbati hebdomadalis fuisse, Lucas diem ita describens, ἡμέρα ἦν παρασκευῆς c. 23, 54. addit: καὶ σάββατον ἐπέφωσκε: quod nempe dies fuerit sexta, quam σάββατον ἐπιφῶσκον Sabbatum hebdomadale illucescens statim excepit: ubi B. Lutherus recte: Und es war der Rüst-Tag und der Sabbath brach an. Vox παρασκευῆς enim tum ὁλικῶς sumitur de die Veneris Joh. 19, 14. tum μερικῶς de ultima dici vigilia, quæ incipit ab hora nona, secundum Judæorum computum, uti ex Josepho in edicto Augusti Cæsaris & Joh. c. 19, 42. constat. Adde, quod Marcus, ne quid ad evidentiam rei desit, c. 15, 42. quænam fuerit Parasceve, Periphrasi longe luculentissima definiat: ὅ ἐςι προσάββατον, quod est pridie Sabbati: quo προσάββατο nomine nihil uspiam aliud notatur, quam feria sexta Sabbatum hebdomadale immediate antegrediens, quod interpres reddidit: ante-Sabbatum. Erat enim pridiana dies Sabbati, dies proxime præcedens Sabbatum, in quod Paschatos festum Judæi referunt. Apud nos est feria sexta, dies scilicet illa, in qua Deus hominem, totius universi epitomen, condidit, Gen. I, 31. Theod. q. 72. in Exod. Ergo quod Christus eodem die voluit mortis supplicio adjudicari, eo ipso ostenditur, quod Christus morte sua opus redemtionis, quæ est ἀνάκτησις, καὶ ἀνάπλασις quædam, ut loquitur Justinus, perfecerit, uti habet B. Gerhard. in Harm. Pass. c. 11. Unde Arabs diem congregationis, id est, feriam sextam, quæ sic vocatur à Mahummetistis, quod ea feria suas congregationes habeant, quas Christiani feria prima instituunt, interpretatus est, & Nonnus in Paraphrasi vocat eam Sextam diem.

(2.) Pascha Judæorum, in cujus Parasceve Christus passus est, tum incidisse in Sabbatum, Lucas non modo cap. 23, 54. sed & v. 56. docet, cum testatur mulieres, Christo sepulto, reversas Sabbati quietem observasse: καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχησαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν. Et S. Johannes vocat festum illum diem Paschatos diem Sabbati, nec non diem ma- gnum, ex observantia Judæorum, ἧν γὰρ μεγάλη ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη τῦ Σαββάτη, erat enim magna dies illa istius Sabbati: cap. 19, 31. Unde dubitare non licet, quin fuerit dies Sabbati: quæ ideo magna censebatur Judæis, quod juxta ipsorum decreta & observantiam concurrerent eadem die festum Pa- schatos, & Sabbatum hebdomadale.

(3.) Diem illam, quæ passionem & mortem Christi immediate excepit, qua Pontifices & Pharisæi convenerunt, ut deliberarent de custo- diendo sepulcro Domini, fuisse ipsum Sabbatum hebdomadale, quod immediate Parasceven sequi- tur, Matthæi descriptio indicat, cap. 27, 62. ἡ ἐπαύ- ριον ἥτις ἐςὶ μετὰ τὴν παρασκευὴν, altera die, quæ est post Parasceven, convenerunt principes Sacer- dotum: Quum ergo fuerit hæc feria septima, Pa- rasceven, ceu sextam, proxime sequuta, Chri- stumin Parasceve passum, feria sexta passum esse oportet.

(4) Dies quietis in sepulcro naturalis unica tantum integra designatur, nempe dies illa, qua quieverunt ob religionem Sabbati & festi magni (quod in Sabbatum incidit) piæ mulieres Luc. 23, 56. καὶ τὸ μὲν Σάββατον ἡσύχησαν. Non dixit, quievisse per duo Sabbata, vel per biduum; sed tantum per Sabbatum; adeoque unicum diem in- tegrum cum noctibus, præcedente & sequente, nec non particula pridianæ lucis postrema. Unicum ergo Sabbatum mulieres in quiete, Christus in se- pulcro exegerunt.

(5.) Diserte numerantur à Luca cap. 23. (1.) dies passionis & sepulturæ, παρασκευὴ vers. 54. (2.) dies quietis post sepulturæ diem, dies Sabba- ti, vers. eodem & 56. nec non (3.) dies resurre- ctionis cap. 24, 1. ceu immediate se excipientes, quam postremam ita exprimit Marcus cap. 16, 1. διαγενομένε τῦ Σαββάτε cum intercessisset Sabba- tum, ut Grotius & Casaubonus recte exponunt: vel exacto intercedente Sabbato, ut Beza interpretatus. Conf. Actor. 25, 13. cap. 27, 9. Intercessit ergo so- lum dies Sabbati, seu feria septima passioni & re- surrectioni, adeoque sexta feria passus est Chri- stus, & exacta septima interveniente, prima feria resurrexit.

(6.) Confirmant hoc in apparitione Christi di- scipuli, qui in vicum Emaus tendebant, Luc. 24, 21. ἀλλάγε σὺν πᾶσι τύτοις τρίτην ταύτην ἡμέραν ἄγει σήμερον ἀφ’ ὗ ταῦτα ἐγένετο, quæ verba B. Lutherus optime reddidit: Und über das alles ist heute der dritte Tag, dass solches geschehen ist. Re- cte enim observavit Grotius, activum hic imper- sonaliter sumtum pro passivo, ut sæpe, ac sensum esse: agitur jam tertia dies, ut Syrus quoque & Arabs expressere: Jam si feria quinta passus esset Christus, quarta illa dies fuisset, non tertia. Nu- merentur enim quinta, sexta & septima feria cum illa, quæ agebatur, prima, & quartam hanc esse patebit. Quod autem hæc apparitio ipsa die re- surrectionis Christi acciderit, collatio vers. 1. & 13. aperte docet.

(7.) Quid quod tertia die Christum resurre- cturum, & resurrexisse, non semel, sed sæpius in Scripturis habeatur: quod prædixerat Oseas cap. 6, 2. & Christus ipse, diversis vicibus. Matth. 16, 21. cap. 18, 33. cap. 20, 19. Marc. 10, 34. Luc. 9, 22. Johann. 2, 18. 19. ac testati sunt Angeli Luc. 24, 7. & Apostoli Actor. 10, 39. 40. 1. Corinth. 15, 4. At si asseratur, Christum die Jovis passum, non tertio, sed quarto die resurrexisset, non ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέ- ραις in tribus diebus, vel intra tres dies, ut præ- dixit, Johann. 2, 18. 19. sed præterlapsis tribus die- bus, templum corporis sui erexiffet.

Quæ omnia ut in Solis disco exposita sunt, ita nemo de illis unquam dubitavit, omnes uno ore eandem sententiam professi sunt, utpote Chri- stum tertia die excitasse templum, quod à Judæis solutum erat. Ignatius Epist. ad Smyrn. intra triduum resurrexisse, quod Epist. ad Trallian. ita explicat: in Parasceve ante occasum Solis sepultus est, Sabbato sub terra in monumento remansit, in quo posuit eum Joseph Arimathæus, illucescente Do- minico die, resurrexit ex mortuis, juxta id, quod di- xerat. Complectitur itaque parasceve passio- nem, Sabbatum sepulturam, Dominicus dies re- surrectionem. Irenæus lib. 5. adv. hæres. cap. 23. Manifestum est, inquit, quoniam in illa die mortem sustinuit Dominus obediens Patri, in qua mortuus est Adam inobediens Deo. Hunc itaque diem re- capitulans in semetipsum Dominus venit ad passio- nem pridie ante Sabbatum, quæ est sexta conditionis dies, in qua homo plasmatus est; secundam plasma- tionem eam, quæ est à morte, per suam passionem do- nans. Quam sententiam Gaudentius Episcopus Brixiensis Tractat. 1. in Exod. similiter tradidit: sexta feria, qua hominem Deus fecerat, pro eodem passus est, & die Dominica, quæ dicitur in Scriptu- ris prima Sabbati, in qua sumserat mundus exor- dium, resurrexit. Et ut multa paucis complectar, sextæ feriæ Passionem Domini, uti quartæ pactum Judæ proditionis magno consensu affixerunt Pa- tres ac tota Ecclesia, quæ ideo in memoriam ven- ditionis ac Passionis Christi duabus illis feriis je- junia instituit.

Quo de Petrus Alexandr. Episcopus & Mar- tyr in Synodico adducto à Fr. Sylburgio in Not. ad Clem. Alexandr. Strom. 7. Nemo nos repre- hendat, qui quartam & sextam ferias observamus, in quibus ut jejunemus secundum traditionem, con- venienter constitutum est: quartam quidem feriam propter consilium à Judæis de proditione Servatoris initum; sextam vero propter passionem ejus pro no- bis susceptam. De quibus feriis Clem. Alexandr. loc. cit. & Tertull. de jejun. adversus Psych. cap. 14. Cyrillus Alexandr. lib. 10. in Levit. Leo M. Serm. IV. in Quadrag. videri poterunt, nec non Epiphanius hæres. LXXI. qui ad universalem con- sensum provocat: Quis est uspiam terrarum, qui non in eo consentiat, quartam, sextamve feriam solemni in Ecclesia jejunio consecratam? Ad con- sensum etiam universalem de die Passionis provo- cavit Augustinus Epist. LXXXVI. ad Casulanum: Hoc ergo die intermisso, passus est Dominus, QUOD NULLUS AMBIGIT, sexta Sabbati (vel Septi- manæ) quapropter & ipsa sexta (feria) recte je- junio deputatur; ut & Beda, qui lib. de tempor. rat. l. XL. hanc sententiam illis accenset, de qui- bus dubitare nemini licet CATHOLICO. Unde Brugthonus in Anglico, & Jacobus Genius in La- tino concentu Scripturæ S. pag. 136. Mortuus est Christus die eodem, quo Satan homicida factus est in rerum principio Genes. 3. & per mortem abolevit eum, qui mortis habet imperium. De Adami die consentiunt Hebræi, Chaldæi, Arabes, Græci, Latini.

Quanquam vero idem Beda videatur libr. de æquinoct. vern. in contrarium allegare Theophili Cæsariensis sententiam, cujus testimonio nititur Langius, quod passus Dominus sit ab XI. Cal. April. qua nocte à Judæis traditus est, & à septimo Kal. April. resurrexerit, hæc tamen ita accipienda, ut locus jam adductus, quod nemini Catholico du- bitare liceat de sexta feria σαυρωσίμῳ, & libri ejus- dem de rat. tempor. cap. 11. & 45. permittunt; ubi hæc leguntur: Passum esse Dominum ab XI. Kal. A- pril. & à VII. Kal. April. resurrexisse. De initio er- go passionis intelligendus videtur, quæ vespera XI. Kal. April. sequuta incepit, quum noctem indicet, qua à Juda traditus est, siquidem non XI. Kal. A- pril. sed X. Christum crucifixum asseruit, teste Be- da lib. de rat. tempor. cap. LXV. unde merito cre- ditur, si non verior sententia vincit, quod beatus Theophilus cum cæteris non solum Palæstinæ, sed & permultis aliarum regionum Episcopis, de Pascha di- sputans, scripsit, eodem X. Kalend. April. die Domi- num fuisse crucifixum. Decebat enim una eadem- que non solum hebdomadis, sed & mensis die, se- cundum Adam pro generis humani salute vivifica morte sopitum de productis è latere suo Sacramentis cœlestibus sponsam sibi sanctificare Ecclesiam, qua vi- delicet die primum Adam, Patrem humani generis, ipse creaverat, eique de latere costam tollens ædifi- cavit mulierem, cujus adjutorio genus propagavit humanum.

Frustra itidem Chrysostomus allegatur à Lan- gio, quem tribus diebus mortuum Christum esse voluisse dicit Homil. XLIV. in Matth. Nam Chry- sostom. de diebus civilibus seu νυχθημέροις loqui- tur, & Sermon. LXXXII. diem, quo de Paschate ce- lebrando Christum quæsivere, quintum Sabbati, (vel Septimanæ) vocat, qui diem Passionis imme- diate antecedebat. Sexta ergo feria Christum pas- sum esse agnovit.

Unde ad objectionem primariam è Matth. XII, 40. de tribus diebus & noctibus, in promtu est responsio: non quidem, quod à captivitatis ini- tio (non à sepultura) initium capiendum sit, quod Erasmo visum fuit, annot. ad Marc. VIII, 31. nec quod citius resurrexerit, ad declarandam potentiam suam, ut Chrysostomus, Isidorus, Leo M. censue- re, neque quod Judæi more Romanorum diem à XII. noctis hora inceperint, ut Torniellus, Spon- danus, Cornel. à Lapide, aliique existimarunt, ve- rum quod intelligendi non sint tres dies natura- les XXIV. horarum, distincte computati: sed ci- viles, seu tria νυχθήμερα, Ebraïsmo recepto, cujus gratia conferatur 1. Sam. 30, 12. Esth. 4, 16. quo non expletis tribus diebus, sed ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις, & τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ resurgere debuit Christus, Joh. 2, 17. 18. Matth. 17, 23. Luc. 9, 22. eaque non integra, sed synecdochice accepta; siquidem in Parasceve Pa- schatis & Sabbati passus sit Christus, & hora nona (quæ tertia est nostra pomeridiana) Spiritum emi- serit, hora decima, vel nostra quarta sepultus, un- de duæ adhuc reliquæ erant horæ ex isto νυχθημέ- ρῳ, à quibus dies illa civilis Synecdochice, ceu totum à partibus denominari poterat, cui dies Sabbati integra in sepulcro transacta successit, ceu alterum νυχθήμερον: ac tertium cœpit circa vesperam Sab- bati, à qua ad horam resurrectionis in tertio die horæ circiter decem elapsæ. Quo pacto explicant in Latina Ecclesia Hieronymus ad Matth. 12. quod Synecdochice totum intelligatur ex parte, non quod omnes tres dies in inferno Dominus steterit (in se- pulcro) sed quod in parte Parasceves, & Dominicæ & tota die Sabbati, tres dies & totidem noctes intel- ligantur: Et S. Augustinus L. III. de Cons. Evang. cap. IV. Restat ergo, ut illo Scripturarum usitatissimo loquendi modo, quo à parte totum intelligitur, inve- niamus extremum diem, tempus Parasceves, quo cru- fixus & sepultus est Dominus, & ex ipsa extrema par- te totum diem, cum sua nocte, qui jam peractus fue- rat, accipiamus: medium vero, idest, Sabbati die- non à parte, sed integre totum. Tertium rursus à parte sua prima, id est, à nocte totum cum suo diurno tempore: ac sic erit triduum, quemadmodum illi octo dies, post quos ascendit in montem, quorum medios in- tegros attendentes Matthæus & Marcus dixerunt, post sex dies, quod Lucas dixit post octo dies. Et libr. IV. de Trin. cap. VI. Ipsum autem triduum non totum & plenum fuisse, Scriptura testis est, sed primus dies à parte extrema totus annumeratus est: dies vero ter- tius à parte prima, & ipse totus: medius autem inter eos, id est, secundus dies, absolute totus, viginti qua- tuor horis suis duodecim nocturnis & duodecim diur- nis. Crucifixus est enim primo Judæorum vocibus hora tertia, cum esset dies sexta Sabbati. Deinde in ipsa cruce suspensus est hora sexta, & spiritum tra- didit hora nona. Ab hora ergo mortis usque ad dilu- culum resurrectionis horæ sunt quadraginta, ut etiam ipsa hora nona commemoretur. A vespere autem sepulturæ usque ad diluculum resurrectionis triginta sex horæ sunt, qui est quadratus senarius. Atque idem etiam de mora Jonæ in ventre ceti, ceu Chri- sti typo statuit Isidorus Pelusiota, quod non integros tres dies & noctes in eodem hæserit, sed in ipso quoque temporis spatio cum antitypo convenerit, ac totidem horas in ceti ventre, quot Christus in corde terræ exegerit. lib. I. Epist. CXIV. Is, qui se Jonæ typum expressurum receperat, cum eum exa- cte nosset, (quippe qui etiam Jonæ adesset cum in pro- fundum præceps ageretur, atque è profundo ejicere- tur) eum quoque haud dubie explevit, tanto nimi- rum temporis spatio in sepulcro commoratus, quanto Jonas in ceti ventre.

QUÆSTIO XIII. Qua hora Christus crucifixus sit, & qua hora animam expirarir?

GOttfried Vogelius in computo suo Chronolo- gico Germanico pag. 194. Septuaginta septi- manas Danielis à VII. Artaxerxis Longimani in- choans, & in morte Christi præcise finiens, non tantum annos integros 490. sed menses, sed dies, sed etiam horas ipsas inde ad mortem Christi ἀπο- τόμως congruere opinatur: nam à 7. Aprilis VII. anno Artaxerxis Longimani, quem facit Annum M. 3548. edictum exiisse vult, à Gabriele indicatum Dan. 9. & inde usque ad 3. April. Anni Mundi 4037. quo Christum crucifixum statuit, numerat annos 489. & 11. menses, additisque à 7. Aprilis Ann. Mun- di 3547. usque ad 3. Aprilis Ann. Mundi 4037. non- dum computatis 26. diebus, & quatriduo, quod ob Æquinoctium juxta Calendarium Julianum ad- dendum censet, 490. annos integros producit: Denique non improbabile esse arbitratur, Esdram ea- dem hora, qua Christus exclamavit, consummatum est, animamque expiravit, ab Artaxerxe edictum, vel concessionem Regiam de edicto accepisse, ut nec illa dies, ac ne hora quidem ulla in computo Gabrielis desiderari possit: sed quum D. Vogelius multa in illo compu- to assumat precario, atque in termino Epochæ Ga- brielis aperte erret, eandem in morte Christi fini- ens, 50χασμῷ illi nullus relinquitur locus.

Nos hic soliciti tantum sumus de conciliatione Evangelistarum, ut hora crucifixionism pariter & mor- tis Christi ex historia recte definiatur. Marcus enim horam tertiam fuisse dicit cap. 15, 25. cum cru- cifixus est Christus, quam vero Johannes cap. 19, 14. ὡσεὶ ferme sextam fuisse testatur: ubi non opus est, ut vel cum Petr. Alexandr. Theophylact. & Came- rario textum Johannis corruptum esse, & loco horæ sextæ tertiam legendam esse horam, statuamus: vel cum Petro Comestore Marci textui corruptionem affricemus; quod est non solvere, sed secare nodum: nec periculo vacat, cum Scriptura avthentica de- pravata saltem alicubi statuitur; quod enim alicui accidit textui, cuivis accidere potuit. Proni tamen sunt in hanc sententiam de textus moderni sacri de- pravatione non Pontificii tantum Thomas Aquinas, Cajetanus in Marc. 15, 25. Sixtus Senensis Bibl. lib. VI. ann. 131. Melchior Canus, Petavius, qui apud Marcum legendum esse volunt hora sexta, quam lectionem habent Biblia Æthiopica, sed etiam è nostris Wilhelmus Langius in Marco pro E extri- tis binis inferioribus lineis r irrepsisse ratus, ad- eoque legendum esse illic ὥρᾳ πέμπτῃ pro τρίτῃ: nec non è Reformatis Jacobus Usserius, qui Jo- hannis potius textum corruptum esse annuit; at- que in hanc sententiam allegat Casaubonus Exer- cit. XVI. num. CX. Nonnum vetustissimum Para- phrastem, quod apud Johannem vel legerit ipse, vel legendum censuerit, ὥρα ὡσεὶ τρίτη, quum ita reddiderit: ἦν δὲ τιταινομένη τριτάτη θανατη- φόρῳ ἠώς. Et Petrum Alexandr. in disput. de Pa- schate, qui ad autographum Johannis provocarit: ἦν δὲ παρασκευὴ, ὥρα ἦν ὡσεὶ τρίτη· καθὼς τὰ ἀκρι- βῆ βιβλία περιέχει, ἀυτότε τὸ ἰδιόχειρον τῦ Εὐαγγε- λιςῦ· ὅπερ μέχρι τῦ νῦν πεφύλακται χάριτι Θεῦ ἐν τῇ Ἐφεσίων ἁγιωτάτῃ ἐκκλησίᾳ· καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν πι ςῶν ἐκεῖσε προσκυνεῖται. Erat Parasceve Pascha tis, hora quasi tertia: sicut habent libri accurate de- scripti; atque adeo ipsum avtographum manu pro- pria Evangelistæ Johannis scriptum: quod gratia Dei ad hanc diem servatum, extat in sanctissima Ephe- siorum Ecclesia, & à fidelibus eo accedentibus magna cum reverentia visitur. Refert & Joachim Came- rarius in annot. ad Marc. 15. quod veterem quen- dam codicem manuscriptum habuerit, in quo apud Johannem lectum fuerit ὥρα δὲ ὡς τρίτη. Pro- vocat quoque Robertus Stephanus & Theodorus Be- za hic ac vetera Græca exemplaria: neque dubitat Usserius dissert. ad Polyc. & Ignat. cap. 11. p. 75. apud Johannem saltem lectum ab interpolatore tum Cle- mentinar. Constitut. tum Epistolæ Ignatii ad Tral- lian. fuisse ὥρα ὡσεὶ τρίτη, siquidem ita habuerit τὸ ἰδιόχειρον Evangelistæ Johannis; quod ad hæc usque tempora in Ephesiorum Ecclesia servatum fuisse asse- ruit autor Chronici Constantinopolitani, quod Ale- xandrini nomine à Matthæo Radero est editum p. 518.520.

Sed recte Jesuita Maldonatus Comment. in Matth. 27, 45. nimis audax semper mihi ea conje- ctura, apud Marcum scriptorum culpa vitiatum es- se numerum, visa est, & quia non alio nititur argu- mento, quam quod, qui ea utuntur, non possunt hu- jus loci difficultatem explicare: Et non debemus, ut Scripturam interpretemur, corrumpere. Neque Hugo Grotius, qui cæteroquin facile propendet in corruptionem textus sacri, causam lectionis mutandæ hîc vidit, & annot. ad Marc. 15, 25. pro- fitetur: nihil in Scriptura Marci, aut Johannis con- tra vetustissimorum Codicum, & μεταφρασῶν aucto- ritatem immutandum. Et Hieronymi illi in Psal- mos commentarii non Hieronymi sunt, sed supposi- titii, quibus nihil simile habet Hieronymus in com- mentariis ad Matth. & Marc. Tum quod Petri Alexandrini nomine citatur de avtographo Jo- hannis, Roberto Bailio non immerito mera vide- tur fabula: quis enim ejus diebus Johannis avto- graphum extitisse credat? Ideoque sententiam hanc, ceu à Pontificiis, ac Protestantibus cæteris omnibus rejectam improbat Bailius, utpote quæ ni- mis latam portam temerariis ingeniis pandat cor- rigendi sacras Scripturas. Neque si Johannis sal- tim textum corruptum cum Ufferio dicamus, har- monia erit cum aliis Evangelistis, aut Ignatio. Nam si Christus hora tertia circiter condemnari cepit, hora tertia crucifixus, juxta Casaubonum, dici non poterit, (quod à Marco asseritur) siquidem inter hanc Pilati vocem: Ecce Regem vestrum, & exor- tum tenebrarum Casaubono certum sit tempore opus fuisse non modico, ut Dominus condemnare- tur, traderetur, deduceretur ad locum supplicii extra urbem, irrideretur, crucifigeretur, omnium propemodum Doctorum sententia. Quomodo ergo juxta Marcum hora tertia crucifixus; si ho- ra demum sexta crucifixus est? Annon ita etiam Marci locum corruptum esse dicendum, ut tum apud Johannem legenda sit hora quasi tertia, cum condemnari Christus cepit, tum apud Marcum hora sexta, quam sententiam Petri Comestoris esse refert B. Gerhardus in Harm. Pass. c. 11. Quo pacto demum Ignatii testimonium sibi constabit Epist. ad Trallian. ut & Clementis in Constitut. l. 5. cap. 13. quorum illud ita habet: τῇ ἴν παρασκευῇ τρίτῃ ὥρᾳ ἀπόφασιν ἐνδέξατο παρὰ τῶ Πιλάτῳ, συγ- χωρήσαντος τῷ πατρὸς, ἕκτῃ ὥρᾳ ἐσαυρώθη, ἐννά- τῃ ἀπέπνευσε, πρὸ ἡλίγ δύσειον ἐτάφη. In Para- sceve itaque hora tertia sententiam accepit à Pilato, permittente id Patre. Sexta hora crucifixus est. Hoc vero sic refertur ab Usserio l. c. Δήμιοι δὲ παραλα- βόντες τὸν τῆς δόξης κύριον, ἕκτῃ μὲν ὥρᾳ ςαυρώσαν- τες ἀυτὸν, τρίτῃ δὲ ὥρᾳ τὴν ἀπόφασιν δεξάμενοι τὴν περὶ ἀυτῶ υςι. ὅς καὶ περὶ τὴν ἐννάτην ὥραν ἀναβο- ήσας, ἀπέπνευσε καὶ θάπτεται πρὸ ἡλίγ δύσεως ἐν μνημείῳ καινῷ. Carnifices vero cum prehendissent Dominum gloriæ, ligno crucis hora quidem sexta af- fixerunt, hora vero tertia sententiam contra eum pro- nunciatam acceperunt &c. Qui circa horam nonam, emisso clamore, expiravit, & sepultus est ante occasum Solis in sepulcro novo. At neque Ignatiana illa, nec Clementi adscripta pro γνησίοις agnoscit, sed ab interpolatore aliquo profecta esse censet Usserius ipse, & fatetur, contra omnium exemplarium fidem Marco lectionem illam horæ sextæ tributam esse, ac Theodorus Beza solutionem eam violentam dicere non dubitat.

Neque secundo satisfacit argutior, quam solidior Augustini responsio utraque, tractat. in Johann. cap. 17. & in Psalm. 64, 3. Prior, quod ter- tia crucifixus fuerit Christus linguis Judæorum blas- phemantium, sexta autem hora manibus militum, quæ non convenit textui. Aperte enim loquitur de crucifixione non Metaphorica, sed propria: altera, quod sexta hora fuerit non diei, sed παρα- σκευῆς, quæ ab hora noctis nona cœperit: quam non improbat Thomas part. III. sum. quæst. XLVI. se- cundo ad secund. & in Caten. ad Matth. 27, 25. At- qui parasceve ὁλικῶς dicta prima diei hora, εἰδικῶς vero vel μερικῶς intellecta nona cepit ante vespe- ram, in qua comedebatur Pascha, non vero nona nocturna!

Nec assensum præbere possumus Johanni Pi- scatori, etsi Erasmus ad Matth. 27, 45. Ludov. de Dieu ad Marc. 15, 45. Annotatores Belgici ad Joh. 19, 14. Anglicani ad Luc. 23, 44. eo etiam abeant, ut & B. D. Asselm. quod Johannes More Romano- rum, horas diei ab ortu Solis, Marcus more Ju- dæorum à media nocte inchoantium loquatur, quodque sexta à media nocte in tertiam ab ortu Solis, qui in Judæa quarta matutina tum exortus fuerit, inciderit: siquidem nec in æquinoctio, quod coincidit in Judæa cum Paschate, unquam Sol ante horam sextam matutinam oriatur, & Christus jux- ta istorum sententiam novem, vel sex niminum horis in cruce pependisset, à sexta post medi- am noctem ( à tertia post ortum Solis ) usque ad tertiam pomeridianam, vel ut alii interpo- lant Piscatoris sententiam, ab hora nona matuti- na ad tertiam, quum tamen tres tantum horæ in cruce assignandæ Christo sint, Joh. XIX, 14. de quibus videatur Bailius Oper. Histor. Chron. II. pag. 87.

Aliam ergo adferunt conciliandi rationem Ba- ronius, Maldonatus, Barradius, Ferus, Valen- tia, Suarez, Jansenius: & è Reformatis Calvi- nus, Gualterus, Rollocus, Deodatus, Alstedius, Bailius, ut & è nostris B. Gerhardus, B. Walthe- rus, & alii præeuntibus autoribus Centur. Magde- burg. cent. I. lib. I. cap. X. pag. 140. Diem in qua- tuor quadrantes vel horas majores tributam fuisse, uti nox in quatuor divisa fuit vigilias: quomodo primæ vigiliæ mentio fit Thren. II, 19. ita ut singulis quadrantibus & vigiliis tres horæ assignatæ sint: & quadrantem secundum ab initio suo Marcus voca- vit horam tertiam, Johannes vero à fine suo sex- tam: intra quam crucifixio contingebat, h. e. tempore inter tertiam & sextam horam interme- dio: quadrante nempe illo, qui ab hora tertia incipit, & in sextam desinit. Quod ita expli- cat Bailius pag. 89. Christum dici crucifixum à Marco hora tertia, quia crucifixus est intra spatium istius quadrantis, qui à tertia denominatur: dein- de dici crucifixum à Johanne & reliquis hora sexta, aut hora fere sexta, quia quadrantis illius secundi sexta fuit alterum extremum, ita ut actiones intra tertiam & sextam peractæ, dicerentur peragi vel ter- tia, vel sexta, denominatæ scilicet ab utrolibet ex- tremo, pro loquentium arbitrio. Quæ ratio con- ciliandi expedita admodum, dicende B. Affelman- no in Tetrad. verborum Testam. thes. 9. esset, si modo certa. De quo vero modeste dubitat: si- quidem nullo antiquitatis testimonio nitatur hæc numerandi ratio, & nequidem Censorini, quem mala fide hanc in rem allegari ait. Noctem in quatuor vigilias Judæos distinxisse largitur, quas vigilias φυλακὰς ternarum horarum observatio- nem haberi Augustinus tradidit, & cum eo Arno- bius. Sententiæ autem de divisione diei in quatuor horas, & hac enumeratione, unde, inquit, tan- dem fidem facies? Addo, quod quadrantes diei & à principio, & à fine denominari consvevisse nullo documento constet, ut scilicet ab hora sex- ta non minus, quam tertia denominatus fuerit alter diei quadrans: & Synonyma illa habenda sint, secunda diei quadrante, hora tertia, hora sexta. Etsi enim secundus diei quadrans, posita illa distinctione, trihorium à tertia ad sextam complectatur, & quæ à tertia in sextam fiunt, se- cundo quadrante fiunt, & hora tertia fieri, & hora sexta ideo non dicuntur; quum etiam quarta aut quinta fieri potuerint.

Porro annon ita incerta redditur hora crucifixio- nis Christi, quam tamen definire studiose voluere S. Evangelistæ? Nam quod intra tertiam & sextam horam factum, vel secundo quadrante diei, de eo certo pronunciare non possum, quartane an quinta an denique ipsa sexta factum sit hora. Quod aliorum explicatio magis adhuc dubium reddit, qui ita conciliant: sexta hora judicatus est Christus, diei nempe, quum circa eam nondum auditam ea contigerunt, quæ Johannes narrat: sed tertia crucifixus, h. e. tertio diei quadrante, qui à sexta diei hora incipiebat & in nonam de- sinebat, inter hunc terminum vero crucifixus est. Nam si ita de diversis quadrantibus, atque ab aliis is aliter explicentur Evangelistæ, ne de quadrante quidem diei supererit certitudo, quo crucifixus sit Christus, nedum de hora ςαυρωσίμῳ.

Atque hinc idem jam erit etiam judicium de simili conciliatione, distinctione inter horas ora- tionis, & diei petita; quod illæ quaternario com- prehensæ fuerint, hæ duodenario, ac proinde Evangelistæ passionem Domini, utpote rem sa- cram describentes, horas templi & orationis sequu- ti fuerint. Quam suam hic fecit Grotius anno- tatis ad Matth. XXVII, 45. pag. 489. Mos loquen- di natus ex Templi consuetudine, ubi sacrificia & preces fieri solebant hora tertia, sexta, nona: ut docemur Numer. X, 10. quo factum, ut hæ horæ tan- quam notiores vulgo celebrarentur; neque alia no- mina horarum reperies, ubi statarum precationum sit mentio. Vid. Actor. III, 1. cap. X, 3. 9. & Tertul- lianum de jejuniis, ubi has horas insigniores ait in rebus humanis, quæ diem distribuunt, quæ nego- tia distinguunt, quæ publicæ resonant. Quocum congruunt, quæ scribunt Cyprianus de oratione Do- minica, & Hieronymus tum ad Lætum, tum ad De- metriadem. Atque eo pertinet, quod est supra, XX, 3. 5. ubi inter tertiam, sextam & nonam nulla hora nominatur, cum post nonam undecimæ fiat men- tio. Factum autem tertia, aut sexta hora dici- tur, quicquid inter illa stata precandi tempora evenerat, ut solent, quæ in medio sunt posita, nunc ad hunc, nunc ad illum terminum referri. Perinde enim hoc est, ac si diceretur, factum aliquid ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ τριώρῳ ut loquuntur Genethliaci. Tu- bæ sono partes diei etiam apud Græcos quosdam signi- ficatas docet nos Hesychius, quo loco ἀσάλπιγ- κτον ὥραν Sophocli vocari ait canticinium noctis. Hæc Grotius: quæ testantur, incertum ex histo- ria relinqui Evangelica, quanam hora cruci affi- xus sit Christus. Factum enim tertia aut sexta ho- ra diei, quod inter illa stata precandi tempora evenerat; qua autem hora evenerit, ita minime definiri.

Convenientius ergo erit, si omnino distinctio illa per trihoria, vel quadrantes diei in Marco admittatur, ut in Johanne horam sextam non de quadrante secundo diei, à sexta hora de- nominato, sed de hora ipsa, quæ à diei exordio numeratur sexta, intelligamus: tametsi Marcus forte quadrantem secundum diei designarit, ut ita tempus indicatæ crucifixionıs à Johanne definitum sit: quod hora quasi sexta fuerit, cum Pilatus Je- sum ad crucem condemnavit, & Judæis tradidit: adeo ut nondum quidem audita sexta fuerit, im- minente tamen hora illa traditus Christus, ac pau- lo post, ipsaque adeo illa hora crucifixus sit, quem- admodum Matthæus & Lucas indicarunt, cum à sexta hora, tempore, ac momento illo, quo ipse cruci affixus inter latrones suspensus hærere ce- pit, tenebras exortas usque ad momentum mor- tis, horam nempe nonam durasse, testantur: quod à Marco etiam notatum cap. XV, 33. Qua- propter penes eundem Marcum cum vers. 25. ἦν δὲ ὥρα τρίτη καὶ ἐςαύρωσαν αὐτὸν, hora crucifi- xionis diei tertia designata esse minime potest: quia imminente hora diei sexta demum ad cru- cem condemnatus, & Judæis traditus est; quo- modo ergo hora tertia diei crucifixus dici potest? Posita itaque prædicta distributione diei in qua- drantes, & denominatione quadrantis cujusvis à prima ejus hora, ut primus quadrans à prima, se- cundus à tertia, tertius à sexta, quartus à nona de- nominctur, adeoque per horam magnam tertiam secundus quadrans intelligatur, Marcus indicasse censendus est non horam diei tertiam, ἀποτόμως

& εἰδικῶς, sed trihorium, & quadrantem γενικῶς & κοινῶς, cui tertia hora & initium & denominatio- nem conciliat. Sed quum illa denominatio dubia & incerta sit, quemadmodum diximus, neque satis conve- niat, quia ab initio secundus quadrans non ter- tiæ, sed quartæ, qua incipit, horæ nomine in- signiendus esset, uti tertius non sextæ, sed septi- mæ, & quartus non nonæ, sed decimæ nomine; forte approbanda potius Danielis Heinsii ad Marc. XV, 26. explicatio, quam à Marcello Monacho Ro- mano doctissimo accepisse ipsum, licet dissimulet, censet Bailius, quam innuit quoque Ludovicus de Dieu (etsi non sequatur) nec non Balduinus Wa- læus, quod nempe hora tertia inde à crucifixione divisio vestium Christi facta sit: ut verba Marci sic reddenda sint: ἦν δὲ ὥρα τρίτη, καὶ ἐςαύρωσαν αὐτὸν, & tertia erat, vel jam agebatur hora, ex quo actus fuerat in crucem, ut si dicas τρίτη δὲ μετὰ τὸ ςαυρωθῆναι αὐτὸν, sive τρίτη τῆς ςαυ- ρώσεως ἀυτῦ ὥρα ἦν, tertio post crucifixionem ejus, aut crucifixionis ejus hora: ut Ebraïsmus in copu- la non dividat; sed conjungat. Similis est locus

Jos. VII, 25. καὶ κατέκησαν ἀυτὰ ἐν πυρὶ, καὶ ἐλιθοβόλησαν ἀυτὲς ἐν λίθοις, quæ non redden- da sunt: & combusserunt igni, & lapidaverunt la- pidibus, quæ interpretatio Augustinum, ex igno rantia Ebraïsmi mirifice torsit, sed uti Thargu- mista reddidit, combusserunt igni, POSTQVAM lapidaverunt eos saxis: ita hîc καὶ ἐςαύρωσαν ἀυτὸν idem est Heinsio, quod ἐξ ὅ ἐςαύρωσαν, ex quo, sive postquam crucifixissent eum. Atque ita etiam

Persa. Postquam enim κατὰ πόδα Græcum trans- tulit, non per ταυτολογίαν, ut arguit eum Bai- lius, sed ἐξηγήσεως, & evolvendi Ebraïsmi gra- tia, hæc addidisse videtur: postquam eum in cru- cem suspendissent. Quanquam etiam præsumere liceat, tempus ita designatum ab hoc interprete fuisse impositæ inscriptionis in cruce, quod nempe tertia hora à crucifixione imposuerint titulum, quem Matthæus innuere videtur, post divisionem ve- stium impositum demum fuisse: sic enim inte- gra habet translatio Persica: Et cum eum in cru- cem egissent, in tertia hora. Ex quo eum in cru- cem suspenderant. Prætextus mortis ejus in libro scriptus est. Qui sensus si fuit Persici interpretis, nova hæc erit conciliandi ratio, sed omittetur particula καὶ, quam Marcus vers. 26. inseruerit: καὶ ἦν ἡ ἐπιγραφὴ, quæ impedit, quo minus ho- ram tertiam de impositionis tituli tempore accipia- mus. Et concedit Bailius Persicum interpretem (quod vero similius) de tempore divisionis vesti- um horam tertiam intellexisse, quamvis postea Æ- thiopicam versionem cum Persica confundat. Eadem etiam ratione interpretatur Dievius Arabicam ver- sionem: Et illud de tertia hora quum crucifixus esset, conjungit cum versu præcedenti, ubi de di- visione vestium Christi actum. Id factum, inquit, tertia hora à crucifixione. Non intelligit ergo ter- tiam horam fuisse, quum Christus crucifigeretur: sed cum milites partirentur ipsius vestes, tum terti- am fuisse horam, ex quo affixus erat cruci. Ad eum sensum ἐςαύρωσαν per plusquamperfectum vertendum esset, hoc modo, erat autem hora ter- tia, quum crucixerant eum. Hæc ille de sensu Arabicæ versionis, quam non intellexit Bailius, Dievium temere redarguens: in quam sententiam etiam Syrum interpretatur: cujus versionem me- lius ita reddi quum crucifixissent eum, quam ut Tre- mellius, quum crucifigerent eum: & linguam Græ- cam facile plusquamperfectum hîc admittere docet Dievius.

Reprobant quidem explicationem illam Suarezius, & Bailius, sed argumentis minus firmis. Primum urget Bailius, quod ita Marcus præterijffet tempus crucifixionit, & tempus actionis minus nobilis designasset. Verum non præteriit Marcus, sed eadem, qua Matthæus & Lucas, ratione, tempus crucifixionisin dicavit vers. 53. Charactere nempe tenebrarum exortarum designatum: ac si arguendus ille, quod præterierit, Matthæus & Lucas itidem arguendi fuerint: sed quum à Johanne expressum id sit, à cæteris charactere illustri notatum, quomodo à Spiritu S. præteritum dici potest? Neque tam ignobilis est illa divisionis vestium circumstantia, ut operæ pretium nullum fuerit, tempus ejus notasse: quum à S.S. in V. T. diserte Psalm. XXII. prædicta, cujus complementum omnes Evangelistæ descripsere, quem actum etiam imprimis operose S. Johannes commemoravit. Ut taceamus, quod hora illa tertia, ex quo crucifigi cœpit, hora divisionis & rapinæ vestium Christi horam illam respicere videatur, qua protoplasti nuditatem suam sentientes, ficus foliis se tegere, ac vestire conati sunt: non enim poterat homo revestiri, dicente Bernardo serm. 1. in annunciatione B. Mariæ, vel ablata sibi recipere vestimenta (originalis justitiæ) nisi Christus amitteret sua: sicut enim vivificari in anima, nisi interveniente morte corporali Christi non potuit, ita nec revestiri sine ejus despoliatione.

Urget secundo Bailius Evangelistas, etiam Marcum ipsum divisionem vestium immediate subjungere crucifixioni: non ergo differre eum hunc potuisse in tres integras horas, post crucifixionem, sed hæc opposita non sunt: annon enim immediate recensio subjungi potest ejus rei, quæ horis tribus postea sequuta?

Tertio arguit ita Bailius: divisæ sunt vestes secundum Matthæi, Marci, & Lucæ relationes ante obortum tenebrarum. Atqui si tenebræ (nedum actiones ante tenebras) non sunt obortæ horis tribus post crucifixionem, tum Christus pependisset in cruce diutius sex horis. At licet commemorentur tenebræ post divisionem vestium, non tamen obortæ post eandem demum sunt, sed cum ipsa crucifixione: nam ipsa hora sexta exortæ dicuntur. At erat hora ὡσεὶ ἕκτη cum tribunal conscenderet Pilatus, Christum condemnaturus Joh. XIX, 14.

Quarto inculcat, nullum adferri posse textum, ubi in uno versiculo suis punctis circumcluso determinatum tempus certæ actioni per conjunctionem copulativam, in quo istud idem tempus ab eadem actione separandum sit, & ad aliam referendum: Quod concedimus primo de conjunctione copulativæ COPULATIVE acceptæ; quem sensum hic necessario retinendum esse, probari nequit: quum notissimum sit particulam copulativam multis aliis modis sæpissime accipi, non semper copulative intelligi. Secundo non referri potest ad aliam actionem, nisi textus ipse aliam suggerat: quod hic fit: vers. 24. καὶ ςαυρώσαντες ἀυτὸν διεμέριζον τὰ ἱμάτια ἀυτõ ἦν δὲ τρίτη ὥρα. Tertio refertur utique ad crucifixionem, non ut tempus cœptæ crucifixionis indicetur, sed hora tertia postquam crucifixus esset, non autem ipsa hora crucifixionis designetur tertia fuisse hora, quod Johanni repugnaret.

Addimus tamen aliam solutionem eruditis expendendam: annon apud Marcum hora tertia intelligi à traditione Pilato facta debeat? ut Evangelista ita omnes actus principales trihorio definitos insinuarit, ac primo quidem diei trihorio Synedrii conventus celebratus sit, ac hora prima diei Pa- rasceves Marc. XIV, 1. consultatio instituta, no- vum examen susceptum à toto Synedrio Luc. XXII, 67. seqq. decretum factum, quomodo Pi- lato tradendus sit. Ab illa ergo traditione circa horam diei tertiam facta tribus scilicet horis ante crucifixionem, hora enim tertia erat (ab illa tra- ditione) cum crucifigeretur, evenerunt ea, quæ coram Pilato & à Pilato gesta sunt, donec Chri- stum condemnaret, & crucifigendum traderet; quod proinde circa horam sextam diei factum vel tempore meridiano, ut Æthiopica versio ἐξηγή- σεως gratia addidit Johann. XIX, 14. Et Para- sceve Paschæ fuit tempore meridiano sexta hora. Quam sextam diei horam Marcus ipse quoque ex- pressit vers. 33. Tertium, quod ceu præcipuum in hac die passionis magna, post Synedrii nem- pe consultationem, & decretum, post accusa- tionem in Prætorio, & condemnationem Christi ad mortem, post crucifixionem ipsam Salvatoris commemoratur à Marco in nonæ horæ, seu tertii trihorii & quadrantis diei exitum, & ultimi ini- tium incidens est mors Christi, quem proinde sub tenebrarum finem, hora nona, animam expirasse commemorat.

Atque hæc communis est Doctorum sententia, hora sexta crucifixionem factam esse, cum obortæ sunt tenebræ, & tribus horis pependisse Chri- stum in cruce: Neque hic difficultatem eam creat collatio Johannis XIX, 14. cum Luc. XXIII, 44. ut opus sit cum Casaubono Exercit. XVI. n. LX. hic dicere, expectandum esse Eliam, qui τὰ ἄπορα Scripturarum solvat. Quid enim obstat, quo mi- nus nodus ille ita solvatur, ut juxta Johannem ὥρα ὡσεὶ ἕκτη fuerit, cum condemnari cœpit Chri- stus, quia imminebat brevi sexta: juxta Lucam au- tem eo sensu hora quasi sexta fuisse intelligatur, quia non ita diu præterita fuit sexta: vel etiam ut hora quasi sexta illa etiam peracta intelligan- tur, quæ horæ dimidio ante vel post sextam per- acta: illa autem facile intra horam peragi potue- re imprimis ab hostibus Christi ex furore etiam malitiæ omni vi & studio exitum Christi deprope- rantibus, & præcipitantibus: utpote condemna- tio, traditio, deductio ad locum supplicii, & cru- cifixio. Neque verba Evangelistarum in Mathe- matico intelligenda rigore, sed ὡς ἐν πλάτει & mo- raliter, vel secundum usum civilem, ideo addi- tur particula ferme.

Cæterum utut momentum crucifixionis non ita determinate expressum sit, neque de eodem ea- dem omnino omnium sit sententia, de hora tamen mortis Christi non facile dissensus reperitur: siqui- dem omnes hora diei nona, vel tertia, ut nos lo- quimur pomeridiana Christum animam expirasse, conveniant, plerique etiam circa meridiem, ho- ra nempe diei sexta, crucifixionem factam con- sentiant, qua hora etiam Adamus lapsus censetur, ut non minus hora, quam dies prævaricationis, horæ, & diei redemtionis conveniat: quemadmo- dum observat Theophylactus: Sexta die homo est conditus, qui & sexta hora de ligno comedit: qua igitur hora Dominus hominem condidit, eadem & lapsum curavit, sexta die & sexta hora cruci affixus. Ita conferri etiam poterit hora mortis Christi cum tempore judicii protoplastorum & promulgationis Prot-Evangelii. Venit enim dominus ad quie- tem diei, ut reddidit Genes. III, 8. verba Mosis ad auram diei Targum Onkelos, id est, circa vespe- ram hora circiter nona diei: ad quod tempus E- bræi, hoc referunt Lyrano teste, ut citaret & con- demnaret, ac simul voce Evangelii erigeret, ac vivificaret protoplastos, qui circa vesperam mundi, ut Irenæus lib. V. advers. hæres. monuit, in novis- simis diebus, itidem circa diei passionis magnæ ve- speram mortem subire, ac morte sua à condemna- tione & morte nos liberare ac vivificare debuit. Agnus paschalis mactandus erat intra duas vesperas Exod. XII, 6. hoc est, hora tertia pomeridiana, an- te quintam, vel Solis occasum Deuter. XVI, 6. vel Sole ad occasum declinante, ideo, ut Josephus tra- dit lib. XVI. Antiq. cap. X. ab hora nona usque ad undecimam diei secundum Ebræos victimæ paschales cæsæ sunt. Christus verus Agnus paschalis circa vesperam diei hora nona, quæ nostra est tertia, mactari pro nobis voluit.

QUÆSTIO XIV.

Quomodo se habeat altera medietas postremæ hebdomadis Danielis?

ALteram medietatem ratione termini à quo à passione & morte Christi inchoandam esse, è verbis Danielis indubitato certum est. Terminus ergo ad quem in quarto anno à morte Christi quæ- rendus. Non autem est, ut præcise ac Mathema- tice anni quarti à morte Christi medietatem inda- gemus, quemadmodum nec ita præcise in me- dium quarti anni ministerii Christi passio ejus in- cidit: satis erit ad complementum vaticinii an- gelici, si quadriennio circiter post Christum pas- sum Character completæ Epochæ Danielis sese mani- festet. Qualem esse censemus tum receptionem gentilium ad communionem Ecclesiæ, tum denomi- nationem novam fidelium, quam à Christo Antio- chiæ sortiti sunt. Nam quadriennio circiter à passione, morte, resurrectione, & ascensione Christi Petrus ingressus est ad gentes Actor. X. & cum Paulo contulit Galat. I, 17. ac nomenclatu- ra Christianorum incepit Actor. XI. ut observant post B. Lutherum Leonhardus Crenzhemius ad ann. M. 4008. Bucholzerus in indice Chronolog. & Alstedius in Chronolog. Quarto anno à morte Christi Petrum visione lintei pleni serpentibus didi- cisse prædicandum Evangelium etiam gentilibus, & baptizasse Centurionem, cum familia, & Tirinus in Chronico sacro cap. L. notat, atque in autu- mno anni istius finit LXX. hebdomadas Danie- lis. Consonat Johannes Temporarius Chronolog. demonstrat. libr. III. pag. 198. hebdomadas 69. Danielis, hoc est annos 483. definite cadere in an- num XV. Tiberii, quo Christus in Jordane à Jo- hanne ablutus est: Tum enim, inquit, Messias ap- paruit, proclamatus in cælo: Hic est filius meus dilectus: Proclamatus in terris: Ecce Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. Ex eo tempore cœpit Christus munus suum obire, ad quod ante secula destinatus fuerat. Adsciscit discipulos, in nuptiis divinæ potentiæ signa exerit. Mercatores ejicit è do- mo Patris sui, Evangelium publicat, docens com- pletum esse tempus, & instare regnum Dei. Matth. IV. Marc. I. Luc. III. & Johann. I. Porro Chri- stum excindendum fuisse, docet Temporarius, ultimam hebdomadam, non tamen absolutam, sed dimidium hebdomadis LXX. finem facere debuisse sacrificiis, & victimis, quæ umbra fuerunt agni se- mel immolati. Chronicon etiam Carionis lib. III. pag. 125. hebdomadas 69. finit in Baptismo Christi, & in dimidio ultimæ Christi passionem locat anno

Christi 34. Porro 35. Christi, Tiberii 19. Paulum conversum esse, ac commoratum in urbe Damasco at- que ob insidias ex muro demissum in Arabiam disces- sisse, & ibi triennium docuisse observat, postea ve- nisse Hierosolymam & ibi quindecim dies apud Pe- trum mansisse, atque hinc congressum Petri & Pau- li aut in ultimo Tiberii aut in Caligulae initia incidif- se, in annum nempe Christi 38. Sic Septimanam ul- timam ordiuntur cum Ministerio Christi, ac fini- unt in quarto anno à morte Christi Belgici annota- tores, Vorstius item, nec non Wilhelmus Langius & Philippus Lansbergius, qui libr. II. Chron. sacr. cap. 11. docet septimo Artaxerxis Longimani an- no iniisse LXX. hebdomadas, inde ad baptismum Christi fluxisse LXIX. in medio ultimae septimana per mortem Christi abolita esse sacrificia, ac scisso aulaeo templi significatam esse sacrificiorum & cultuum legalium cessationem. Quadriennio post mortem Christi Paulum cum Petro convenisse Hierosolymis, & inde profectum in regiones Syriae, & Ciliciae, gen- tibus praedicasse Evangelium ac completas esse LXX. hebdomadas. Annuit etiam de fine hebdoma- dum Johannes Wichmannus lib. I. Chronologiae sacrae pag. 171. quod Christus ipse docendi munere publico dimidia ultimae septimanae parte functus sit, hoc est annis 3 1/2. post mortem autem per Apostolos residua parte septimanae illius. Taceo, quod ob- servent nonnulli fere quadriennio post ascensio- nem Christi Concilium Hierosolymitanum celebra- tum fuisse: in quo conclusum sine discrimine Ju- daeos & gentes ad Ecclesiam pertinere, quibus etiam Annotationum Vinariensium autores suffra- gantur. Fere tertio anno post resurrectionem Chri- sti in concilio Apostolorum publico decreto legem ab- rogatam, & libertatem à lege promulgatam esse B. Lutherus censet, in Chronologia Tom. IV. Jenens. exhibita, pag. 600. Et fere 3. aut 4. anno post re- surrectionem id factum esse in explicatione LXX. heb- domadum Danielis, id est, dimidio ultimae hebdo- madis statuit idem Megalander pag. 617. Quod postremum si quis è Chronotaxi in dubium revo- cet, priores tamen Characteres facile sufficiunt alterius medietatis LXX. hebdomadum fini desi- gnando. Atque hic etiam finis sit Chronici no- stri Biblici: pro quo concesso Triunus Deus benedi- ctus sit sine fine, in secula seculorum Amen.

## 1:1 Introduction: In the Name of Jesus. A Discussion of the New Biblical Chronology of Mr. Christian Ravius
In the name of Jesus. A discussion of the new Biblical chronology of Mr. Christian Ravius, of Berlin, Royal Professor of Hebrew and Oriental Languages at Uppsala, published this year at Kiel, by way of a supplement, subjoined for the benefit of his auditors in the domestic lecture hall, proposed in the Biblical Chronicle, published out of love for heavenly truth alone, by the author Mr. Abraham Calovius, Primary Professor, General Superintendent of the Electoral Saxon Circle.

Prefixed is his own address to the cultivators of Holy Scripture, concerning the various deviations of Scaliger and others in Sacred Chronology from the one infallible Canon of Holy Scripture, and their errors regarding the same, and the necessity and utility of a more corrected Sacred Chronicle, as well as a letter from Ravius sent to the author.

Address to the cultivators of Sacred letters.

May the Lord give us understanding in all things!

Summary.

The calculation of Scripture is to be preferred to all others. Nor is it to be called into doubt in any way. Outside of which we know the epoch of the years of the world together with the most ignorant, the confession of Ptolemy. The accuracy of Scripture in that epoch, and in the ancient series of years, is acknowledged by all. Nor therefore is it to be denied in other epochs. Chronologists not rarely deviate from the Canon of Scripture. And among these is the illustrious Scaliger, in whose favor it is a matter of conscience for us to abandon Scripture. Contention between chronological characters, even celestial ones, and the characters of the divine Word. In almost no epoch from the foundation of the world to the end of the seventy weeks (as neither in the years of the ministry, nor in the birthday of Christ) does Scaliger insist upon Holy Scripture. Concerning which is adduced the opinion of the blessed Affelmann, from our own; of Robert Baillie, from the Reformed; concerning Scaliger. his arrogance, especially concerning the seventy weeks of Daniel: and concerning certain new discoveries of his, such as concerning Darius, under whom the temple began to be repaired, and concerning the last week of Daniel. A judgment concerning the characters boasted of by Scaliger and others. The epoch of the exodus of the Israelites is set forth as an example. Concerning which Ussher, pitting Lansberg with the Scaligerians, although both boast of characters. The injuries of Scaliger and certain followers against the authority and sincerity of Holy Scripture. Concerning the beginning of the reign of Ahaziah, and concerning the words of St. Stephen in Acts 7. Concerning which the dangerous opinion of the blessed

Dr. Behm is produced. As also concerning the passage Acts 13:20. And also concerning Jeremiah 23:1. Likewise concerning the diminished number of years of the Babylonian captivity. And how the same author has attempted to render the canonical authority of the book of Esther suspect. Some Scaligerians are compared with Goclenius, who called Scaliger his Bible. The warning of the blessed Hutter, that Scaliger should be silent in the Church. The candor of the blessed Dr. Behm is praised, because in his old age he retracted his Scaligerian and own hypotheses, concerning the new discovery about the threefold beginning of the reign of Cyrus; and concerning the term from which the Babylonian captivity is dated. In which he was once too unfair to the truth, later rendered doubtful, finally he rejected Scaliger's opinion; having confessed that the Scaligerians postpone the authority of Jeremiah. To whom he wished a sounder mind. Their main pretext from Ezekiel is refuted. The years of the Babylonian servitude were defined not by Ezekiel, but by Jeremiah, by Daniel. The deportation made under Jehoiakim was the beginning of the captivity. The error of Cornelius a Lapide. That true beginning is confirmed. Necessary warnings about not moving ancient landmarks, and about adding nothing, taking nothing away from the Canon of Scripture. Temporarius is praised. The necessity of an accurate investigation of Biblical epochs. The utility of this work: I. for the explanation of Scripture. II. for the reconciliation of apparent chronological contradictions. III. for the preservation of the authority, purity, and truth of Scripture. IV. for the confirmation of the certainty of the promises concerning the Messiah. V. for the demonstration of the harmony of the Old and New Testaments. VI. for the recognition of divine Wisdom. VII. for the illustration of historical truth. The causes of the undertaking. And its method, and goal. It is concluded with a prayer.

Latin:

I. N. J. DISCUSSIO INFALLIBILITATIS NOVÆ CHRONOLOGIÆ BIBLICÆ DN. CHRISTIANI RAVII, Berlinat. Ebrææ, & Oriental. Linguar. Professoris Regii Upsaliensis, hoc anno Kilonii editæ, MANTISSÆ LOCO, CHRONICO BIBLICO In Acroaterio domestico proposito In Dn. Auditorum suorum gratiam subjuncta, SOLIUS VERITATIS COELESTIS AMORE PUBLICATA, AUTORE DN. ABRAHAM CALOVIO, P. P. PRIMARIO, CIRCULI ELECTORAL. SAXO- NICI SUPERINTENDENTE GENERALI.

Præmissa est Ejusdem προσφώνησις ad S. Literarum Cultores, de va- riis Scaligeri, & aliorum, in Chronologia Sacra, ab unico infallibili S. Scripturæ Canone di- varicationibus, & in eundem ἁμαρτήμασι, ac CHRONICI SACRI emendatioris necessitate, & utilitate, nec non Epistola Raviana ad autorem data.

ΠΡΟΣΦΩΝΗΣΙΣ Ad Sacrarum literarum Cultores.

Δώη ἡμῖν ὁ κύριος σύνεσιν ἐν πᾶσιν!

SUMMARIUM.

Scripturæ calculus anteferendus aliis omnibus. Nec in dubium vocandus uslatenus. Extra quem Epocham annorum mundi juxta cum igna- rissimis scimus, Confessio Ptolemæi. Ἀκρίβεια Scri- pturæ in illa Epocha, & prisca annorum serie, agnita ab omnibus. Nec ergo neganda in aliis Epochis. A Canone Scripturæ non raro defle- ctunt Chronologi. Et inter hos illustr. Scaliger, in cujus gratiam Scripturam relinquere nobis re- ligio. Contentio inter characteres chronologi- cos, etiam cælestes, & inter characteres Verbi divini. In nulla fere Epocha à Mundi conditu ad finem LXX. hebdomadum (uti nec in annis mini- sterii, nec in die Natali Christi) Sacræ Scripturæ insistit Scaliger. De quo adducitur B. Affelman- ni sententia, è nostris; Roberti Bailii, è Refor- matis; de Scalig. ἀυθαδείᾳ, imprimis circa LXX. hebdomadas Danielis: & de novis quibusdam ejus ἐνρήμασι, utpote de Dario, sub quo tem- plum reparari cœpit, & de hebdomada ultima Da- nielis. Ἐπίκρισις de characteribus à Scaligero, & aliis jactatis. In exemplum sistitur Epocha exitus Israelitarum. De qua Usserius, Lansbergium cum Scaligerianis, etsi utrique characteres jactent, committens. Injuriæ Scaligeri, & Sectatorum quorundam in Scripturæ S. autoritatem, & since- ritatem. De initio regni Achaziæ, & de S. Ste- phani verbis Actor. VII. De quibus periculosa B.

D. Behmii opinio producitur. Ut & circa locum Act. XIII, 20. Nec non circa Jer. XXIII, 1. Item de diminuto numero annorum captivitatis Babylo- nicæ. Et quomodo idem suspectam reddere cona- tus sit autoritatem Canonicam libri Esther. Com- ponuntur Scaligeriani nonnulli cum Goclenio, qui Scaligerum sua Biblia dixit. B. Hutteri monitum, taceat Scaliger in Ecclesia. Laudatur B. D. Beh- mii candor, quod in senectute Scaligerianas, & proprias hypotheses retractarit, circa novum ἔυ- ρημα de trino regni Cyri initio; & de termino à quo captivitatis Babylonicæ. In quo veritati ini- quior quondam fuit, post dubius redditus, demum reprobavit Scaligeri sententiam; fassus Scaligeria- nos Jeremiæ autoritatem posthabere. Quibus sa- niorem mentem optavit. Πρόφασις eorum ex Ezechiele præcipua diluitur. Non ab Ezechiele, sed à Jeremia, à Daniele definiti anni servitutis Ba- bylonicæ. Deportatio sub Jojakimo facta capti- vitatis initium. Error Cornelii Lapidei. Confir- mur verum illud initium. Monita necessaria de non movendis antiquis terminis, & de nihil ad- dendo, nihil detrahendo Scripturæ Canoni. Lau- datur Temporarius. Necessitas accuratæ indagati- onis Epocharum Biblicarum. Utilitas operæ hu- jus I. ad Scripturæ explicationem. II. ad contradi- ctionum apparentium Chronologicarum concilia- tionem. III. ad autoritatis, puritatis & veritatis Scri- pturæ conservationem. IV. ad certitudinis promis- sionum de Messia confirmationem. V. ad harmo- niæ Veteris & Novi Testamenti ostensionem. VI. ad divinæ Sapientiæ agnitionem. VII. ad veritatis Historicæ illustrationem. Causæ instituti. Ejusque modus, & meta. Concluditur voto.

## 1:1 Introduction: In the Name of Jesus
In the name of Jesus.

No pious person doubts that the chronological calculation, which the pure and limpid sources of Scripture exhibit on every side, is to be preferred by far to any human divination or reasoning of anyone whomsoever, even of the most excellent mathematicians and chronologers, and that it is superior to every exception and entirely ἀνυπεύθυνον (unaccountable). For to the Word of God, in all things which it delivers and proposes, whether it be done by design or as the occasion arises (not only in the doctrine of faith), all the διαλογισμοί (reasonings) of human reason yield. Nor are those to be heard at all who dictate that Holy Scripture is less accurate, or that it speaks only παχυλῶς (roughly) and popularly about those things which do not pertain to faith, and that it does not have an exquisite regard for either philosophy or chronology, or who, with Baranzano, even derogate from the credibility of the Sacred Writers in physical, mathematical, or other matters not precisely pertaining to faith and religion, and prattle that they spoke according to their own sense, as if ignorant of those disciplines. It is manifest that such people exalt themselves in their own judgment above the Holy Spirit Himself, the author of Scripture, and attribute and claim greater authority, or at least ἀκρίβεια (accuracy), for exotic observations and their own reasonings than for the infallible testimonies of the Sacred Letters. In the computation of the years of the world, we certainly know nothing at all outside of Scripture, so much so that Ptolemy himself in book III of the Almagest found it necessary to profess: We think it alien for those who are led by a zeal for learning and knowing the truth to consider the observations of the whole world or of other manifold time. Since, therefore, the sacred letters are entirely accurate in the ancient series of years, and all are bound to acknowledge this, unless perhaps someone should dare to undermine and remove all certainty of calculation from the very origin of the world: surely it is not to be presumed that the Holy Scriptures are less accurate in other chronological epochs, and that exotic observations are more accurate: since all things in the Holy Letters have proceeded from the same author and infallible Master of truth. And if any error is admitted to such a height of authority, in the judgment of St. Augustine in Epistle VIII to Jerome, no particle of these books remains which cannot be called into doubt. Nor ought the very prophecies and oracles of faith concerning Christ and His kingdom to be lightly endangered, for the sake of which primarily the computation of times was instituted in Holy Scripture, 1 Pet. 1:11, Dan. 9:24, to say nothing of other ἀτασθήματα (absurdities) which overflow from that hypothesis, overturning the entire faith from the foundations. For among those with whom the account of time does not cohere, among them no account of truth or historical faith can stand, as Tatian, an ancient writer in the Church, affirms.

It would therefore be desirable that all who have devoted effort to the subject of Chronology should, above all things, have attended everywhere to the undoubted standard and rule of Holy Scripture, and should not have allowed themselves to be led astray from it either to the right or to the left, and finally that they should have neither added anything to it nor taken anything away: just as, according to Varinus, a measure ought to be ἀδιάψευστον [infallible], admitting no addition or subtraction. That this has not always been observed, the examples of not a few, even of the most excellent Chronologers, abundantly testify. It is not easy to find today one who would render the first place among the Chronologers of this age doubtful for the illustrious Scaliger, whose supreme erudition the learned world deservedly esteems and venerates, and acknowledges that these studies also owe more to him than to others. Whom, therefore, we also hold in the highest regard, and vehemently admire and cherish, but only up to the altar. For where that infallible Rule of Truth in Epochs and Chronological numbers teaches otherwise, it is a matter of conscience for us, for the sake of a GREAT MAN, to postpone the voice of the Holy Spirit, or to twist clear Scripture into a foreign sense by some invented gloss, however plausible. Let there be CHRONOLOGICAL CHARACTERS, especially celestial ones, which no sane person would call into controversy, if they are true characters, and if the observations, as can easily happen, do not fail. But the characters of the divine Word are everywhere most true, and are undoubtedly certain down to the very last iota or tittle, nor can they ever fail; furthermore, they are exceedingly clear and perspicuous, written by the very rays of the Sun of righteousness, provided that human rashness, out of preconceived opinion, does not cast any darkness upon them. For why? Could not God, the artificer of both mind and language, speak clearly? Nay, rather, by supreme providence He willed that those things which are divine should lack obscurity, so that all might understand what He Himself was speaking to all, as Lactantius testifies, lib. IV. instit. cap. XXI. But is it pious, or holy, or worthy of a Christian man, to force or twist the word of God to the opinions of men, which have been conceived in the mind from profane writers, who are most prone to errors, and besides this, much at variance among themselves, and often dissenting from themselves, and finally lacking the true origin of years, however much they may sometimes rely on this or that character: about which, however, both mathematicians and chronologers themselves (for who does not appeal to characters?) not rarely contend, and the dispute is still under judgment: in which also, whether in recording an observation or in transmitting what has been recorded to us through writings over many centuries of years, various errors could have crept in, since no privilege of infallibility has been granted to them, as it has to Holy Scripture and its authors, and the infinite contentions of the most accurate mathematicians and chronologers concerning Epochs and years, from which most of them boast of Chronological Characters, and even celestial observations, with great παῤῥησίᾳ [boldness], even though they disagree with one another δὶς διὰ πασῶν [altogether], abundantly testify that those characters are not rarely less certain or undoubted, much less to be preferred to the infallible and open Word of God, concerning which Truth itself teaches in Luke 16:17 that it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for any tittle to fall out.

But if the Great Chronologer, whom we have mentioned, had everywhere held this in such regard as is due, and had never failed to assign the first place to Scripture in Sacred Chronology, he would have more easily carried every point. But in truth, when we examine and recall the Epochs from the foundation of the world to the end or conclusion of the mystical weeks of Daniel to the Canon of Holy Scripture, it clearly appears that in almost no Epoch—which we say ἄνευ παθῶν [without passion] in honor of the one celestial truth—has that glory been left to the Word of God κατὰ πάντα [in all things].

Most notable in the Scriptures are those four Epochs: the calling of Abraham, the Babylonian captivity, the liberty to build the new temple, and the beginning and end of the weeks of Daniel, and in all these (to say nothing now of the years of the ministry, and of the birthday of Christ, or those new inventions of Scaliger, that Christ celebrated five Passovers, and that He was conceived at the beginning of January and born at the beginning of October, and others of this bran) how much did the great man deviate from the line of Scripture! Yet no one is ignorant that the principal part of Sacred Chronology depends on them. Nor is this our judgment alone concerning the new discoveries of the Great Man. For they are truly new, which either began with him or newly are interpolated, or certainly deviate from the ancient Rule of truth. Both theologians and chronologists of the highest rank have marked these with a black mark, as the saying goes. And a comparison of the Scaligerian novelties with Holy Scripture itself and with true antiquity sufficiently convicts them. Fifty years have now passed since the theologian of the Rostockers, Johannes Affelmann, a man most celebrated for the singular sharpness of his judgment, who is now among the saints, passed this censure upon Scaliger in his Resolution of the Tetrad of words from the seven Words of Christ's Testament, theses VII and VIII. For we cannot side with the Scaligerians, who contend that Scripture itself errs by prochronism from Abraham to the building of the temple, and by metachronism from the building to the destruction, but that the intervals of exotic history are more correct, and that from the first Olympiad to any other interval there is no error, and therefore that Eusebius accommodates sacred history to the Canon of exotic history, and not exotic to sacred. In which error, since they firmly persist, thinking that the sacred writings do not contain an exact calculation of times, as being not at all necessary for the scope of Scripture or the salvation of men, but that this matter is to be sought from profane writers, hence it cannot be told how anxiously they sometimes trouble their brains and weary their miserable calculations, so that they may conform to their own abacus. Although, however, we cannot approve of Pareus's animadversions on Scaliger's Chronology, which are often ridiculous, more often irrelevant, and most often false, far be it from us, however, that following Scaliger, we should look at the chronology of profane authors with the right eye and that of sacred authors with the left, and that, so that the truth of each may stand, we should bend not the former to the latter, but the latter to the former. In which, those who depart from us not only tear down the FAITH OF THE CHURCH concerning the oracles about Christ, which relied most heavily on the moments of time, but also, not without SACRILEGE, take away from sacred History the light commonly granted to profane histories. Furthermore, the Holy Spirit either could not, or would not, or certainly neglected to reveal a matter so necessary to the Church: none of which, whatever you may affirm, will be free from absurdity. These things were said long ago by the blessed Affelmann. But very recently, and seven years ago, a work was published in the Glasgow Academy, Historical and Chronological, by Mr. Robert Baillie, the primary Professor of Theology there, to whose author even the Scaligerians themselves do not deny the praise of a MOST ACCURATE CHRONOLOGER, in which, however, the errors of Scaliger are frequently noted and criticized. The author affirms (book 1, page 194) that he [Scaliger] now commands the whole nation of chronologists with a very haughty brow and with a completely dictatorial authority, and now argues (book

1, page 157.) Discussing the seventy Danielitic Weeks, he says that it is very trivial for Scaliger to rise up against ALL MORTALS for what he deems to be true. And so that I may pass over many other things of this kind with a dry foot, Baillie complains vehemently about Scaliger (book 1, page 155) that he pronounces all who dissent from him to be men of no talent, malicious, dullards, asses, and madmen. Discussing Darius, in whose time the temple began to be rebuilt (Ezra 4:24) (book 1, chapter X, page 159), he criticizes Scaliger's new or interpolated opinion, that Darius NOTHUS is designated there, as follows: Almost all the ancient Hebrews, Greeks, and Latins hold that he is Darius HYSTASPES. Joseph Scaliger, however, after Sulpitius Severus, drew many of the moderns, especially in the Reformed Church, into a new opinion, by his authority rather than by reasons, which, as it seems to us at least, do not in any way outweigh the foundations of the ancient opinion. Seth Calvisius, Scaliger's amanuensis, reduced these into order in chapter XLII of his Isagoge and polished them as best he could: Junius, Rainoldus, and Emmius follow these parts: Nisbet, Howe, and the English Annotators in both editions also incline toward them: but with such hesitation and ambiguity that they seem to be drawn to it with reluctant minds. Concerning Scaliger's singular opinion about the last week of Daniel, and his truly new discovery, that Robert says the following in question XV (page 170.) It is to be disapproved that Scaliger here imperiously insists that the half is not to be referred to the one week mentioned immediately before, but to a completely different week, namely, that which followed all seventy. This opinion is so PARADOXICAL that I do not remember any interpreter of Scripture among the Protestants who follows it: certainly Junius, Diodati, and the most recent English Annotators, who hold most of Scaliger's OTHER PARADOXES, here desert their Master. But concerning the Characters, which were held in the highest regard by Scaliger, Baillie judges as follows (book 1, chapter X, page 144.) Here, however, we shall premise that we by no means place as much importance in establishing the limits and characters of these ancient times, or in the Eclipses of the Sun or Moon, or in the motions of the fixed stars observed by the Chaldeans and others in the Persian and Greek empires, as I see being placed by various chronologists, both Protestant and Papist, especially by Petavius after Scaliger. Certainly, if tables of the motions of the fixed stars and planets from the beginning of the world to this day were perfectly at hand, and thus the precise limits of all eclipses were presented to the eyes (which for accurate mathematicians in this day would not be very difficult to do), and if, just as Ptolemy recorded a few, so other ancient authors worthy of belief had recorded many, whether of the Sun or of the Moon, with the Kings and Republics were found to have compared [them] with the deeds, we would admit that a most elegant, most clear, and most certain method of fixing times, which are otherwise most fleeting, could have been derived from this. But since an interval of a single half-hour, let alone a day, month, or year, constitutes a great discrepancy and a quite different appearance in the motion and position of the heavens, stars, and eclipses, and indeed very few Chronologers, if one can find ANYONE at all, who do not differ from others in the calculation of times by whole years, and also, the eclipses which have been noted and joined with histories are read to be very few: in this famous argument from celestial motions, we certainly do not think that weight should be placed on establishing times, as many boast. Thus far Bailius. There are twin [statements] which the same man handed down in book 11, chapter 1, page 35: In many cases this argument is firm, indeed in all it would be irrefutable, if only mathematicians had given a perfect calculation of ancient eclipses, and historians had marked the deeds of many with the characters of eclipses. I confess, however, that this argumentation often makes doubtful, indeed sometimes false, not only contrary opinions, but also the palpable errors of Scaliger, Petavius, Calvisius, and other most excellent mathematicians in those things which they profess to prove and demonstrate by an accurate calculation of eclipses. Certainly Lansbergius most confidently cries out that he has proven by most certain and most clear demonstrations from celestial motions that from the burning of the temple to the capture of Babylon by Cyrus, 70 years precisely had elapsed, which, however, we showed above to be false, and repugnant to Scripture and to the most solid interpreters of Chronologers. And thus far again Bailius. But that we may speak in particular of at least something concerning the Scaligerian hypotheses, by way of example, the Great man boasts about the Epoch of the exodus of the Israelites from Egypt, that it, previously unknown, was established by him as the most certain foundation of sacred and exotic history, from which all the calculations of the times of Biblical history depend, so that you may truly call it the mother of the other Epochs. See Animadv. Euseb. p. 31 and l. 3 Canon. Isagog. p. 282. That he erred excessively in establishing it, however, while he relegated it to the year M. 2453, is most certain from Scripture. Provided that you subtract 60 years from Terah begetting Abraham: And that Scaliger is not consistent with himself has already been observed by his own disciples and followers, because he wishes Arphaxad to have been born at the beginning of the 601st year of Noah: whence the Exodus can fall into neither the year 2453 nor the third year of the annalistic week, so far has B. D. Behmius long since departed from his Master here. We add what Jac. Ussher, Archbishop of Armagh, has concerning these matters in Chronolog. Sacr. chap. XI, page 188.
