He perverts the text of Daniel in more than one way, and so that we may add here first concerning the former 7 weeks, since the rest pertain to the last epoch of Ravius, he rendered verse 24 of chapter IX of Daniel thus: 70 weeks are cut, intersected, and distinguished into parts, intervals, and spaces for the good of your peoples and polity, and of your holy city, that then the guilt of transgression may begin to be finished, and the liability obliterated, and idolatry expiated, and eternal salvation procured, and vision and prophecy sealed, when the most holy one shall have been baptized. But he interpreted the following 25th verse thus: Attend therefore, that you may learn, and become a chronologist, from the promulgation of the next decree of Cyrus concerning the restoring of the people, and concerning the rebuilding of Jerusalem, there are first seven weeks of years that will endure beyond Christ the mediator (and afterwards in 62 weeks the wide gates and walls will be rebuilt) although with the intercalary distress of those times. Thus far the Ravian paraphrase of the first two clauses of the angelic prophecy. In which we find these things wanting (1.) Nothing is held in the text concerning the weeks being cut into parts, intervals, and spaces. The Hebrew word נֶחְתַּךְ is sometimes [used for] determined, or the weeks are clarified, or each one of them. For the singular verb is used, constructed with a plural noun, and Avenarius notes this in his Lexicon, so that it may be understood that those weeks are to be fulfilled as certainly as if it were one. Whence the continuity of these weeks is gathered, and not that they are discontinued: because this Ravian discontinuation is utterly repugnant to unity, and does not in any way contribute to a clear determination, but renders the divine definition doubtful, uncertain, and as far as it lies in him, most unclear. (2.) Over the people of Daniel, and over the city of his holiness, seventy weeks are said to be decided or determined, not into spaces and intervals; they are declared to be cut for the good of the people and the polity: and thus the object, namely the people of the Lord and the city, is designated, and not the end, or its good. (3.) The consummation of transgressions is not to be understood concerning the end or limit of the guilt of the Israelite people, but concerning the meritorious removal of the iniquities of the whole human race; Cf. Zech. 3, 9. Heb. 9, 26. 28. where it is described by ἀθέτησιν ἁμαρτίας and τὸ πολλῶν ἀνε- νεγκεῖν ἁμαρτίας. Nor indeed is the sealing of sins, or the expiation of iniquities, to be restricted to the sins or idolatry of the people, since Christ had to bear the sins of the world John 1, 29. and had to become a propitiation for the sins of the whole world 1 John 2, 2. as one to whom also eternal salvation was to be meritoriously procured or brought by himself for the whole [world]. (4.) Gabriel hands down nothing explicitly concerning the Baptism of Christ: but concerning the anointing of the most holy one: nor does he teach that the guilt of the Jewish people will have an end when Christ shall have been baptized: but he joins these with the same reason and construction: namely that 70 weeks are determined to finish the transgression and to anoint the Most Holy. We admit that the end, that is, the final cause, is the consumption or ἀθέτησιν of transgressions and the expiation of iniquities: but we do not concede that the consumption of transgressions is to be restricted to the time of the anointing, or even of the baptism. (5.) The decree of Cyrus is rashly injected into the paraphrase of the text: because the angel expresses nothing other than the going forth of the word, which is explained either concerning the Prophetic word, or concerning the Royal decree; nor the decree of Cyrus, which was concerning the rebuilding of the temple and was made in large part void: but such a one, which will be joined with success, and indeed is viewed here as the rebuilding of the walls and streets, and thus the very city and polity of Jerusalem being repaired. Therefore, it is not a question in this place of restoring the people, but of rebuilding the city: for the Hebrew phrase imports that, to return and to build, that is, to rebuild, or to return to the building of Jerusalem: Nor (7.) concerning Jerusalem enduring BEYOND Christ the Mediator, verse 25.

has anything of the literal sense of the prophecy. Doubtless the meaning of the little word עד, which is UNTIL, not indeed BEYOND, is perverted: and the time of the duration of Jerusalem, which is by no means defined by these words, is rashly thrust into them. For nothing is held, in this place at least, concerning Jerusalem PERSEVERING, or how long it is to be preserved. The time is defined, or the Epoch from the going forth of the word concerning the rebuilding of Jerusalem until Messiah the Prince: the terminus a quo of which Epoch is the going forth of the word, the terminus ad quem is Christ the Prince, publicly declared, which we admit to have happened at the Baptism. But by the Ravian paraphrase the terminus ad quem is utterly subverted, so that it cannot be established how long that Epoch defined from the going forth of the word extends itself here: and thus the sense of the oracle concerning the time of the advent of Christ the Prince is plainly perverted, so that no certainty remains, much less can a conviction of the Jews be derived from it. (8.) That parenthesis is invented beyond necessity concerning the 62 weeks of years. For those LXII weeks cohere with the preceding seven, nay, they must necessarily be connected, so that thus the LXIX weeks determined until Christ the Prince may be indicated; which it pleased the Holy Spirit to distribute into two parts, and that, as it appears, for the reason that He might denote that seven whole weeks of years, not interrupted or intercalated (for Scripture is ignorant of these, nor does the present computation admit them) but continuous, were to be spent on the structure of the city. (9.) The Ravian parenthesis is not consistent with itself. For why? were 62 weeks of years required so that the gates and walls might be rebuilt? (10.) What is intercalated here concerning the intercalary distress of times (which is primary in this Ravian Chronology) is altogether alien to the words of Gabriel, for not one iota is held in them concerning intercalation, nor if it were to agree with them in the highest degree, would it in any way suffice to prove that manifold ἐμβολισμὸν, which we reviewed above according to the Ravian opinion. Certainly no one could carve the same out of those words: nor has anyone hitherto presumed to carve out or assert the same. Mention is made of the constriction and distress of times, as even the learned Dr. Wasmuth, most skilled in Hebrew literature, himself rendered it: but not of intercalary distress, nor of the intercalation of YEARS, much less of such varied intercalation, least of all so discontinuous, through intervals of times cut short and defined. Whatever therefore they bring forward here concerning that distinct intercalation is ἐξ ἰδίας ἐπιλύσεως (from private interpretation): nor can it be proved by any pact from history, whether sacred or profane, and therefore it is rejected with the same ease with which it is asserted. (11.) Here Dr. Ravius appeals to the vindications of the Hebrew text by Dr. Wasmuth, Part II, p. 241. But there has already been an abundant response to those in our Anti-Grotian writings on Dan. IX. (12.) That there are 72 intercalary years and that they are to be thrust in under various Emperors, Cyrus and certain of his successors up to Darius Nothus inclusive, are merely precarious hypotheses; because there is deep silence in the Scriptures concerning the intercalating of so many years. And these things also concerning the XI Epoch.

THE TWELFTH, and last, is of the LXIII weeks of years, the remainder of Daniel, which he begins from the seventh year of Darius Nothus, and ends in the passion of Christ, of 441 years. Which he distributes into two parts: The prior is of LXII weeks of years, being 13 years of Darius Nothus and 20 of Artaxerxes Memnon, in whose seventh year he thinks Ezra, and in whose twentieth Nehemiah, went to Jerusalem, so that thus the city was destitute of walls for 153 years; taking the rest from the Ptolemaic Canon.

Where we note these things: 1. That he wrongly says things were done in the time of Artaxerxes Mnemon which we have shown in the Chronicle were done under the empire of Longimanus. 2. That he inconsistently asserts the city was left without walls for a full 153 years, and thus for over a century and a half. 3. He assumes the Canon of Ptolemy for the support of his chronology, and indeed for a great many years, which he nevertheless boasts with Pareus that he seeks solely from the Scriptures. 4. He previously called the Canon of Ptolemy into doubt in more than one way: but now, having changed his position, he vehemently commends it because it rests upon the presumption of certainty from the Catalogue of the Kings and Emperors of the Medes, Greeks, Egyptians, and Romans, and because everything in it is correct,

The second part of this Epoch is the last week of Daniel, in which Ravius first hunts for the beginning of the latter half, then in chapter LX of Isaiah v. 21, as if GOD the Father were speaking there to the Son about the time of the descent of the Holy Spirit upon him, when the discourse there is rather about the Church being perpetually informed and governed by the Holy Spirit, and no word touches upon the prophetic office of Christ himself: then in Isaiah 61:1, as if it were likewise dealing there with the visible descent of the Holy Spirit upon Christ at his Baptism, which Ravius assumes as certain. This passage, he says, everyone will easily concede deals with the temporal day of baptism. Yet he has not been able to find anyone thus far from the whole crowd of interpreters who has asserted that the day of Baptism is defined here. He also argues from there ἀνακολύθως that everyone will consequently concede that this passage deals with the temporal Jubilee year: which, however, interpreters commonly explain as the spiritual Jubilee year. Meanwhile, he attempts to prove this from a collation of other passages, such as Lev. 25:20, Jer. 34:8, 15, and 16, Ezech. 46:17, but with an argument that is clearly weak and flimsy. For what, I ask, is this consequence: In those passages the temporal Jubilee year is understood: Therefore, Isaiah LXI must also be understood as temporal, and not spiritual? None: because there the discourse was about the Jubilee of the Old Testament, which was typical: but here the Prophet is prophesying about the Jubilee year which Christ was to announce in the New Testament, which was shadowed and prefigured by that one. Nor is the time of the Evangelical proclamation of Christ defined in this passage, namely that he was to begin it in the Jubilee year, but the object of this Evangelical preaching is designated, that he was to announce the year of favor, or of grace, and of spiritual liberty. Finally, even with this postulate admitted concerning the temporal Jubilee year indicated by Isaiah, many more parasangs and detours, and those parasyllogistic, will be needed for it to be made to serve the Ravian goal.

Furthermore, in order to descend from here to the month and day of the passion of Christ and indeed of his conception, by dividing the Old Testament year into two, namely into the 15th of September, when the feast of Tabernacles began, and the 15th of Nisan, when the Passover was celebrated, since Christ suffered on the 15th of Nisan, he concludes that he was born on the 22nd of October, which was a Sabbath. But the firmness of this inference does not appear, since it rests primarily on the foundation that the feast of Tabernacles marks the first coming of Christ to the Fathers: which he himself extends by private authority even to the birthday falling on the day of that feast, and yet, which you might wonder at, he pretends it is the divine authority of Scripture.

Finally, not to examine how that reduction of months and days from the 15th of September to the 22nd of October stands, and upon how firm a foundation it rests, the Ravian hypotheses certainly do not agree with themselves. For from the 22nd of October, which he makes the birthday of Christ, to the 15th of Nisan, which day he establishes as the passion of Christ, not half a year intervenes, but 38 days are still lacking for the half-year span: yet Ravius contends that precisely half a year with three years is required from the time of the Baptism of Christ (which he says coincides with the birthday of Christ in terms of month and day) just as he decides that Christ was also precisely 30 years old when he was baptized, and contends that the passage in Luke 3:23 is to be taken in no other way: arguing that the word ὡσεὶ means precisely, and thus rendering the words of the text: Moreover, that very Jesus was precisely (on that day) beginning to be 30 years old: whereas interpreters have commonly explained the particle ὡσεὶ until now as ABOUT or AS IF, and not precisely. And how do those things agree with themselves, that Ravius once says Christ suffered on the 15th of Nisan, but again asserts in express words, because Adam fell on the 14th of Nisan, as the Synod of Caesarea and other Fathers defined, also the 14th Nisan that Christ ought to have died; and he adds that Christ died on the 14th of Nisan, on the 6th day of the week, 3 1/2 years after he undertook his baptism? These things are certainly ἀσύστατα [inconsistent]. Nor have we yet warned anything concerning this authority of scripture, as he calls it, about the fact that Ravius rashly assumes the Epoch of Gabriel ends on the day of Christ's passion, which we have demonstrated in its proper place to be terminated three years and a half-year after the passion of Christ.

He adds, however, yet another authority of Holy Scripture, namely from Zech. 1:7, because on the 24th day of the 11th month, Sebath, in the second year of Darius, the Prophet saw a man among the myrtle trees, who is called Jehovah: and thus the Θεάνθρωπον [God-man]. Whence he infers that on that 24th day of the 11th month, or January, Christ was conceived. But what kind of logic of consequence is this? We grant, indeed, that that Man is the Son of God: but it must be proven that here we have an image of the temporal conception of the Son of God. It is an image of the presence of the Son of God in the midst of the Church, and among his own: but not of his conception: nay, not even of his ἐνσαρκώσεως [incarnation]; for although those places exhibit some prelude of the duality of natures in Christ and of his ἐνανθρωπήσεως [becoming man], in which the Son of God appeared in human form assumed κατ' οἰκονομίαν [by divine dispensation] for a time, yet the seat of the ἐνσαρκώσεως is not to be fixed in all those places, as if the act were done there by design so that the incarnation might be shadowed forth, or that the end and cause of the apparition in all those places were the ἐνσάρκωσις itself, much less is the time of the conception of the Son of God defined there. Thus in Josh. 5:13, the Son of God appeared to Joshua in the form of a man, as the prince of the host of the Lord around the Passover: but is it to be inferred from that that the cause of this apparition was the shadowing forth of the ἐνσαρκώσεως and conception of Christ, or to be concluded that Christ therefore ought to have been conceived around the feast of the Passover? By that reasoning, certainly, many and very different times for the conception of Christ would be gathered from Scripture. And why is the time of Christ's birth not concluded from that apparition of Zechariah, but rather his conception? Why not his passion or resurrection, which Rupertus, praised by Mr. Ravius, says was prefigured here?

Nor is the inference any firmer concerning the day of the week, namely that Gabriel came to Mary on the Sabbath day, Luke 1, if indeed as God addresses the Prophets on the Sabbath day, so Gabriel also addressed Mary on that day. For neither does it rest on certain demonstration that the address of the Prophets was ordinarily made on the Sabbath, nor was God therefore more bound to that day for addresses and revelations to Mary, or to others, than Christ was to the apparitions and addresses of the disciples after the resurrection; which, it is certain, took place on the day of the Sun, both before the ascension, and also to John after his ascension, Apoc. 1, 10. Finally, it is rashly, nay falsely, assumed in this apparition of Zechariah that it took place in the second year of Darius Nothus: which, however, we have proven in its proper place to have occurred not in the time of Darius Nothus, but of Hystaspes.

To these two authorities of Scripture, Mr. Ravius adds a third, a typical συγκυρία from the year of the flood: which he feigns was predicted by Lamech, the parent of Tubalcain, as fatal to himself and his own, and as the 1656th year of the world: from Gen. 4, 24, a new Cabbala, if I am not mistaken, is about to deduce it. But what kind of συγκυρία that is, is evident even from these facts: because he wishes the year of the flood, 1656, to be taken two and a half times, so that from it the year of the Nativity of Christ, 4140, may be produced. He gathers the month and day of the conception of Christ to be the 24th day of the eleventh month, because on that day the dove brought the green leaf. But which month ought to have been not of that 4140th year, which he had previously gathered Cabbalistically, but of the preceding 4139th year; since the conception was in the year preceding the birth; nor did that return of the dove with the green leaf fall on the 7th day of the week or the 24th of January, but on the 1st day of the week and the 24th of February, as the blessed Polycarp Lyser teaches. But these things are not worthy of discussion; the rest do not even deserve to be touched upon.

This one thing remains, that we should still examine the Ravian paraphrase of the remaining part of the angelic prophecy, namely of the last two verses: which he provides as follows: v. 26. For the final end, those 62 weeks having elapsed, the Messiah SHALL BE CRUCIFIED, and by ascending into heaven he will not appear. (Afterwards the army of the Western leader will destroy the city itself and the holy temple, so that the end of both may be with the inundation of the flood, so that at the end of the war there may be mere desolations) v. 27. Then he will establish the New Testament for all, at the end of the last single week. For from the latter half of that week the present one will abolish the typical sacrifices and holy rites; and when through the abominable hostile wings desolation has been made, then until the end of the world the decree will press upon the place to lie desolate. Thus far that paraphrase; in which we note the following;

1. That 'for the final end' is not found in the text, nor is there any mention of CRUCIFIXION, but it is said simply: And after sixty-two weeks the Messiah shall be cut off. The word יִכָּרֵת denotes excision everywhere, but crucifixion nowhere.

2. Gabriel has nothing here concerning the ascension into heaven. Nor can the ascension of Christ be gathered from the collation of the phrase וְאֵינֶנּוּ used of Enoch in Gen. 5, 24, because not even there is the assumption of Enoch proved from that word alone, but rather by the following words, and the whole sentence: And he was no more, because GOD took him. But in this place it is treated explicitly of Christ being cut off, not of Christ being taken by GOD; nor is he said for that reason not to have been any longer on earth, because GOD took him into heaven, but he is predicted as about to be cut off, וְאֵין לוֹ and that 'not for himself': not for his own sake, but for our sake, as we said in the Anti-Grot. on this passage.

3. Gabriel designates the army of the coming leader, but not of the Western leader. For although the Hebrew word also occurs regarding the setting of the sun, yet when placed absolutely, without mention of the sun, it never signifies it, nor denotes the West.

4. The Angel is not speaking of the constitution, but of the corroboration of the New Testament, nor does he refer it to the end of the single last seven-year period, but teaches that the covenant will be corroborated by Christ through one and the same entire week: which was done by him partly immediately for about three and a half years in the days of his ministry: and partly mediately accomplished by the Apostles after his death.

5. Not in the latter

in the middle of the last week Christ is said to be about to abolish the typical sacrifices: but in the middle of the last week, so that the time of the passion and death of Christ, through which those were abolished, may be expressed more specifically. For since the Angel had previously said that Christ was to be cut off after 62 weeks, he now defines more expressly the time of his death, which is that he will put an end to the types by his passion and death not at the beginning, nor at the end of the last week, but in its middle, and thus after the completed years of his ministry, which will be three and a half. Whence Mr. Ravius errs not lightly in the computation of the angel, when he casts the abolition of sacrifices and the death of Christ, as the true propitiatory sacrifice, to the end of the seventieth week; which Gabriel referred to the middle of the seventieth week; as we have shown in the Anti-Grot. and in the Biblical Chronicle.

And these things concerning the Ravian Chronology, which was transmitted to me by the author at that very time when I was putting an end to the Sacred Chronicle; whence, having eagerly examined it, since the Author boasted of its infallibility with such great boldness, I decided it must be entirely weighed, not failing in this part to meet your desires, most distinguished Auditors, and thus I have subjected the discussion of that infallibility in place of an appendix. Nor, however, is it my intention with Mr. Author or anyone else to exchange the sword of contention, or to contend, concerning which I solemnly protest here: for it is not free time, nor is it opportune, being distracted by most serious duties and other more necessary works, to spend time in discussing empty and brittle arguments more laboriously, nor does my more advanced age permit it; and I have undertaken this work, whatever it is, solely out of love for heavenly truth to vindicate Sacred Scripture and Biblical Chronology, to which I perceived violence was being done by that new Chronology. I would have wished, however, that Mr. Ravius had communicated those studies of his before their public disclosure, or even before he spent such laborious effort in constructing the Tables. For I do not doubt that, in a similar manner, once those things demanded concerning the Cycles of the Sun, years, months, and weekly holidays are admitted, and the general Ravian hypotheses according to the Epochs, which are expressly defined in the Holy Scriptures and cannot be called into doubt without prejudice to piety, and furthermore without holding the heavenly Canon of Ptolemy, or despising the authority of the best foreign writers, whose credibility should not be rashly challenged, if anyone wishes to spend equal effort, twin chronological tables can be constructed and adorned, in which everything is correct, so that there is no need to introduce into Scripture novel opinions and divinations, nowhere approved either in Sacred or in profane writers, which must be handled with a more sacred hand, to tear words and texts away to preconceived opinions, or to play with them by mere voluntary and unheard-of glosses, or Cabalistic inventions not unlike the trifles of the Jews, and finally to destroy himself and his own works by frequent self-contradiction.

Since, however, those things of Ravius have been sent out into the public (which one might perhaps wonder were not published in the renowned Academy of Uppsala, where the Author holds a public office), I judged not undeservedly that a private ἐπίκρισιν would now be useless and untimely: whence I have almost decided to make public also the present discussion, which the new Chronology seemed to deserve, and which I had initially destined for you alone, O my [friends]: for this reason especially, that to the same world I may understand that votes are being gathered from all sides; so that those who are pleased to compare this consideration of ours at the same time may weigh in an equal balance of judgment the reasons which restrain, or rather prohibit, my vote.

I had long since conceived for the Theological Elenchus, together with this discussion of the new Chronology, might come to light: which Chronology, that I should hold in equal standing with the place itself, that is, as uniquely true and infallible, the CLEAR DIVERGENCES from Scripture, the only infallible source, and the VIOLENT INTERPRETATIONS of the same do not permit, nor are the new εὑρήματα [discoveries] persuaded by TABLES that are MORE SPECIOUS than SOLID, as they are based on barely Topical, let alone Apodictic arguments, and indeed have sprung from precarious hypotheses and almost perpetual paralogisms; and therefore I trust that not even the Mr. Author will take it ill to receive the JUDGMENT which he very amicably sought from me in repeated letters, a copy of which (at least the later ones) it seemed necessary to prefix to these: primarily because they also serve to explain his mind in some matters: which judgment, therefore, without the allurements and circumlocutions of words, and as the matter absolutely demanded, I decided should be rendered with Theological fidelity, and with the same [fidelity] precisely with which the response was rendered to Mr. Dr. Wasmuth in the Conringian cause, in a public capacity: desiring only this, that the Era of Codomannus (for this Ravian one approaches no other more closely) being recognized as increasing the System of the years of the World by more than a just sesquicentury, and also the clear falsity of certain Epochs deviating from the express determination of Scripture, and then indeed the mere Lubricity of the special hypotheses in designating Months, weeks, and days, collected from the characters τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐπιλύσει [by their own interpretation], and without cause, the ancient terms being moved—which unhappily befell Scaliger and others—or, as they say, precipitated from the bridge of ancient history, Mr. Author ὁ Φιλόπονος [the industrious one], or anyone else, may not be reluctant to make a trial through general hypotheses, if he pleases. The thing itself, I think, will teach, emerging with similar appearance and probability, but on the contrary, will commend far more the divine infallibility of Scripture, accepted in its native sense, and will finally bring much clearer utility to the Church in every detail.

But so that it may be openly evident that those things which are almost primary in this Ravian CHRONOLOGY have already been weighed and discussed by me more diligently (before Mr. Author perhaps applied his hand to this work), those things can be compared here which, some years ago, when I was perhaps reviewing my Diatribe on the LXX Weeks, proposed publicly here on October 28, 1663, at the inaugural disputation of Mr. L. Georgius Meier, Pastor of the Lambertine church which is in LÜNEBURG, and when I was reading through the Vindiciae of the Holy Hebrew Scripture of Mr. Matthias Wasmuth, then Professor in the Academy of Rostock, published at Rostock in 1664, Part II, where the place of Daniel ch. 9, 24 seqq. is learnedly treated, I cast onto paper, out of a zeal for truth, and to that end, namely, that the Beroaldian opinion, to which that Alstedian computation of the LXX weeks seemed to approach more than others, having been discussed, I might inform myself and my reader more fully concerning it, as it had been speciously adorned by Mr. Wasmuth most recently at that time, and pass judgment: since that Diatribe, though prolixly asserted, departed from the truth in several points. For those things will, I believe, serve not a little for a fuller discussion of the Ravian opinion, as it is very closely related, in this Danielitic Epoch, to the Alstedio-Wasmuthian one: even if it departs in some things to the contrary, and assigns the term to which primarily in a different way. Each is a friend to me, and has been for many years, because of their rare gifts of genius and excellent erudition in Oriental letters; but because, as the Apostle warns, ὀυδυνάμεθά τι κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας, ἀλλ᾽ ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας [we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth], 2 Cor. 13:8, RAVIUS may be a FRIEND, WASMUTH a FRIEND, but TRUTH must be a greater FRIEND. It pleased Mr. Dr. Wasmuth, for the sake of CHRONOLOGY, to also τὰ ἴδια ἀνασχεῖν [restrain his own views] concerning the last week, which he had most correctly taught with us heretofore should be finished in the profession of the Antiochene Christian name: but now, with the Ravian Tables dazzling his eyes, he terminates it at the death of Christ. It will not be displeasing, therefore, that for the sake of CHRONOLOGICAL TRUTH, these things, which without any harassment, γένοιτο, γένοιτο! [may it be, may it be!]

NOT UNTO US, O LORD, NOT UNTO US, BUT UNTO THY NAME BE THE GLORY. AMEN.

Latin:

I. N. J. DISCUSSIONIS CHRO- LOGIÆ RAVIANÆ.

SUMMARIUM.

TRactatio Generalis. Occasio & causa hujus discussionis. Commendatur diligentia, & peritia linguarum Oriental. Dn. Ravii. Addit is temere Systemati annorum Mundi 140. annos, Biblicis Epochis 190. Nec cum Scriptura orditur captivitatem Babylonicam. Sequutus est Codo- mannum. Qui hactenus nullos facile habuit secta- tores. Nec vero etiam infallibilitatem jactavit. Dn. Ravius Epochas Exoticas incertas & suspectas red- dit. Canonem Ptolemaicum præter rem in dubium vocat. Ejusdem Reges a Beroso confictos suspica- tur. Quem tamen in Summa annorum laudat. Quomodo sola Biblica Chronologia infallibi- lis? E Scriptura sola universam Chronologiam deducit. Eaque Judæos & Atheos convinci posse, censet. Confessio Parei, quod tria hic humano in- genio majora sint. Quæ se præstitisse Ravius jacti- tat. I. De mundi conditi primo initio. Apodixis prima Raviana expenditur e c. Ex. XII. Ut & altera, e feria egressus Abrahamidum ex Ægypto, Exod. XII, 40. 41. 51. Qua ingressum Ægyptum ait Abra- ham. Ex una Epocha Ex. XII. & Gal. III. duas fe- cit Ravius. II. De motuum perpetuorum tabulis. III. De Epocharum & Eventuum singularium alli- gatione. An menses Politici in Scripturis ubique adhibiti sint? De Problematibus quibusdam aliis, de neomenia, tempore Paschatos, & Pentecostes. Paradoxa Raviana. Exempla Raviana, pro con- firmandis tabulis suis adducta, expenduntur. 1. Qua characterem ingressus Abrahæ in Ægy- ptum. Postulatum ejus de annis Epocharum in- tegris. 2. Qua initium structuræ templi. 3. Qua characterem anni tertii Cyri Dan. X. v. 4. Postula- tum Ravianum de diebus revelationum divi- narum. Specialis tractatio DE EPOCHIS XII. Ravianis. In quibus omnes Chronologos taxat. De Epocha PRIMA usq; ad diluvium. DE SECUNDA usq; ad ingressum Abrahæ in Ægyptum. Quæ in Script. expressa non est. DE TERTIA ad ablationem Isaaci, quæ e Scriptura nullam habet ἀπόδειξιν. DE QVARTA exitus Israel. Cujus terminus a quo ita definitus a S. S. non est. Nec ipsa Epocha sic determinata. Nova versio & interpretatio loci Ex. XII, 40. Discutitur. Paulò contraria est Gal. III, 17. Et textui Sacro. De QVINTA Epocha ad primum Iobelealem Mosaicum. Quæ multis eget hypothesibus de Sabbaticis & Iobeleis. Nullum habet fundamentum. Ψευδερμηνεῖα loci Lev. XXV, 2. 9. Contradicitur temerè aliis Chronologis : idque argumentis, quæ ne quidem pro Topicis habenda. Imo & Script. S. SEXTA Epocha planè ἐμβολιμαῖος est, à primo reali Jobeleo, ad finem occupatæ Canaan. A Codomanno primum invecta, à quo tamen Ravius variè dissentit. Scripturæ I. Reg. VI, 1. planè contraria. Cui non satis religiosè opponitur Historia Judicum, & locus Act. XIII. Non sine detorsione Verborum 1. Reg. VI, 1. Quem locum arietare conatur Ravius. De loci Act. XIII, 20. mente. Postulata precaria Ravii circa historiam Judicum. Auctoritatibus destituitur. De verbis Jephthæ Jud. XI, 26. Temeraria divinatio Ravii. Verior computus. SEPTIMÆ Epochæ ad quartum Salomonis initium non rectè assumtum. Circa OCTAVAM de annis peccatorum Judæ errores Raviani. Et divortium à communi sententia voluntarium circa NONAM de annis peccatorum domus Israelis. De loco Ezech. IV, 4. Inconstantia Raviana. Partitio ejus annorum 390. Prima 91. annorum pars est 95. annorum. Difficultas de uno Achasiæ anno è 2. Reg. IIX, 25. 2. Chron. XXII, 2. Triumphus de eodem sibi revelato vanus. Pars altera 164. annorum, qui in Historia Regum Israelis sunt 143. Hoseam Regem eundem cum Hosea Propheta ἀτόπως facit. Pars tertia, periodus 135. annorum. Annos peccatorum Israelis non rectè finit. Malè confundit Salmanassarem, Sennacheribum & Nabonassarum. Error Funccianus. Ravius cum Funccio confundit Nabonassarem & Nebucadnezarem. Evilmerodacho 30. annos tribuit, citra autoritatem. Niricassolassarum, Nabonadium, & Nabopallassarum è Ptolomei Canone eliminat. Belsazari 14. tantùm annos assignat. Annos regum in Can. Ptol. 14 annis locupletat. Merè atbitraria ejus annorum Hiskiæ & æræ Nabonassareæ colligatio. Epocha DECIMA Dn. Ravii. Captivitatem Babyl. malè inchoat à templi exustione. Committitur cum Codomanno. Et secum ipso. An Dan. X, 1. de tertio regni Persici Cyri agatur : UNDECIMA Epocha. Hebdomadum LXX. initium Beroaldistarum malè arreptum. Fundamentum lubricum pro Apodixi. Paralogismus. Rationes pro initio illo discussæ. Ratiuncula à pari. Temerè finguntur edicta Xerxis, & Darii Nothi benevola. Persici Monarchæ quinam Judæorum Patroni ? LXXII. anni temere & falso inserciuntur cyclo LXX. hebdomadum. De locis Zach. I, 12, c. VII, 5. Computus annorum 121. non recte se habet. Peculiarem revelationem (extra Scripturam) jactitat Ravius. Quæ Esdræ & Nehemiæ haud congruit. De Dario Esdr. VI, 14. 15. Mysterium novum Ravii σιδηροξύλινον. Hebdomades LXX. Danielis auget Ravius X. hebdom. & 2. annis. Mirabilis & mere arbitraria intercalatio Raviana disturbationis structuræ : Ut & definitio annorum successus operis. Ex uno Dario duos facit Ravius. Contra apertum locum Esdr. IV, 5. VI, 14. 15. Gabrielen facit Spiritum S. contra Scripturam. Pervertit textum Dan. IX, 24. 25. Paraphrasis Raviana. Quæ in illa desideranda? Verbum Nechtach perperam explicat, quod discontinuationem hebdomadum revincit. Finem cum objectione confundit. Et ter- minum culpæ cum expiatione ejusdem. Peccata mundi ad idololatriam populi restringit. Bapti- smum Christi textui ingerit. Et ad eum finem cul- pæ populi trahit. Edictum Cyri privata ἐπιλύσει af- fuit. Restitutionem populi loco reædificationis ur- bis substituit. Sensum voculæ עד pervertit. Termi- num ad quem Epochæ intervertit. Parenthesin præ- ter necessitatem fingit. Quæ etiam ἀσύσατος est. Intercalarem angustiam, suæ annorum intercalatio- nis gratia, confingit. Quam 72. annorum citra fun- damentum fecit. De XII. Epocha septenniorum, LXIII. Pars prior LXII. septenniorum. Ad Arta- xerxis Memoris tempora rapit, quæ ad regnum Longimani pertinent. Inconvenienter ultra ses- quiseculum urbem mœnibus destituit. Canonem Ptolemei in subsidium vocare cogitur, quem cum placet, vel probat, vel reprobat. Altera pars Epo- chæ, hebdomas ultima. Posterioris dimidii ini- tium. An Es. LX, 21? vel Es. LXI, 1. definitum? An ibi annus Jobeleus temporalis, an vero spiritualis designetur? De mense & die passionis, & conce- ptionis Christi, quem argumentis infirmis probat Ravius. Hypotheses ejus non consonant. Loci Luc. III, 23. Raviana paraphrasis. Ἐαυτομαχία no- va Raviana de die passionis Christi. In quo temere finit Epocham Gabrielis. Nequicquam e Zach. I, 7. colligit diem conceptionis Christi. Infirma il- latio de feria septimanali apparitionis Gabrielis. Falsa alligatio apparitionis Zachar. I. ad tempora Darii Nothi. Commentum plus quam Cabbalisti- cum de prædictione anni diluvialis Gen. IV, 24. Et de συγκυρίᾳ cum anno natali Christi. Ac die & mense conceptionis. Paraphrasis posteriorum com- matum Vaticinii Angelici Raviana. In qua teme- re adjiciuntur illa pro ultimo finali, & de CRUCI- FIXIONE Christi. Ut & de ascensione in cœlum. Loco Gen. IV, 24. nequicquam hic collato. Phrasis NON SIBI quid hic inferat? Confundit Ravius con- stitutionem & Confirmationem Novi Testamenti. Neque ultimi septennii fini; sed toti septimanæ my- sticæ ea tribuenda. Abolitio sacrificiorum non re- cte refertur ad posteriorem medietatem ejusdem. Tempus mortis Christi non est finis hebdomada- rum mysticarum, sed medietas ultimæ hebdomadis. Error Ravii de termino ad quem hebdomadum Da- nielis. Conclusio. Protestatio autoris. De aliis ta- bellis Veritate Scripturæ & Canonis Ptolem. salva, simili tenor e, adornandis. Cur hæc discussio pu- blicanda visa? Cur auctarium additum ex opere Bi- blico? Cur approbari nequeat NOVA Chronolo- gia? Causa additarum literarum Dn. Ravii. Votum autoris finale.

DISCVSSIO INFALLIBI- LITATIS NOVÆ CHRO- NOLOGIÆ RA- VIANÆ.

EDidit Dn. Christianus Ravius, Ebrææ & Orient. Lingv. Professor Regius Upsaliensis nuperrime Chronologiam Biblicam, quam unicam veram & in- fallibilem inscripsit: quia vero de eadem judicium meum binis vicibus solicite rogavit, eamq; publice jam exposuit luci, paucis quid de illa habendum sit, Coronidis loco monendum videtur, ne de Epo- charum in hoc Chronico nostro traditarum certi- tudine per novam illam Chronologiam Biblicam, hactenus magnam partem inauditam, dubius quis reddatur, nec divina circa earundem in sacris literis designationem periclitetur veritas.

Digna sane favore est diligentia, quam studio utilissimo impendit autor, quem ob insignem in orientalibus literis eruditionem a multis annis, ex quo meo in Academia Regiomontana usus est convi- ctu, amo; ideoque non sugillandæ ejus famæ, sed unice vindicandæ Scripturæ autoritati hoc quic- quid est operæ dedico. Addit enim hæc Chronolo- gia Systemati annorum mundi complures, nimirum 140. annos, imo ingerit annos 190. qui in Chronolo- gia Biblica redundant, nec uspiam alias comparent; utpote 118. a primo anno reali Jobelæo Mosi celebrato ad finem itineris Israelitarum s. occupatæ Canaan, & 72. annos intercalares 7. prioribus hebdomadis Da- nielis, hinc inde, pro arbitrio, interjectos; qui non modo in Scriptura non occurrunt, sed etiam Epo- chis a Spiritu S. designatis καδδιάμετρον adversantur; neque cum Scriptura a primo Nebucadnezaris, vel quarto Jojakimi captivitatem Babylonicam orditur, sed a decimo nono Nebucadnezaris, vel ab exusto templo; quæ pleraque non tam ab ipso, quam a Lau- rentio Codomanno jam ante 90. annos inventa, cum aliis plusculis in hac Chronologia tantopere depræ- dicata traditis, cum sacris literis & veritate histori- ca nunquam conciliari poterunt. Non habuit se- ctatores Codomanni Chronologia per integrum fere seculum, etsi valde eam ipse deprædicarit, quod scilicet ea non sinat alios diutius in Labyrinthis Chro- nologicis hærere, sed expediat eos per certitudinem, quam Deus nostri misertus ipsi per laboriosissima media, & κριτήρια etiam apud adversarios pondus habitura largitus est. Quos sectatores nunc eadem a Dno. Ravio post 100. circiter annos incrustata habitura sit, dies docebit; magis tamen laudanda videtur Co- domanni modestia, qui tantum abest, ut infallibilita- tem jactitet Chronologiæ suæ, ut protestetur potius, cum humanum sit errare, & multi accurate contem- plantes plus videant, quam unus, aliorum judicia se non despicere, nec sibi soli sapere velle.

Quanquam vero Epochas etiam Exoticas ple- rasq; (quod a Codomanno factum non est) incertas & suspectas reddere conetur Dn. Ravius, quod eas nullatenus τῇ ὑποθέσει, quam animo præconcepit suo, δουλεύειν, optime intelligat, non tamen de illis solliciti jam multum erimus; id autem tacendum non est, cœlestem Ptolemæi Canonem præter rem in dubium revocari, quem Chronologi meliores ha- ctenus in magno habent pretio, ceu historicæ veri- tati, & cœlestibus observationibus omnino consen- taneum. In limine enim ipso, introductione puta generali §. 4. nimis contemptim de eodem sentit Dn. Ravius, in exemplum incertitudinis rerum exoti- carum, qua incertior dari vix possit, allegans Reges Af- syriorum in Canone Ptolemæi designatos, quod ambi- guum sit, annon a Beroso conficti sint, quem ipse, sed contra antiquitatis fidem, autorem suspicatur esse Canonis Ptolemaici, & in nominibus Regum, regi- minisq; numero eis assignando tantum lusisse, at citra ullam demonstrationem, adeoq; prorsus temere, ju- dicat; quo pacto facile omnia in antiquitate suspe- cta reddi possent; imo pro lubitu annos in Canone disjicit, eundemq; immutat, ac corrigit, etsi agno- scere cogatur, in summa Regum Assyriorum 122. an- norum usq; ad annos Nebucadnezaris inclusive non fal- lere Canonem Ptolemaicum, sed summam verā retinere.

Cæterum Biblicæ Chronologiæ nobis maxime habenda est ratio, quam recte solam infallibilem fa- cit Dn. Ravius, modo non ideo solam veram ita di- cat, ut veritatis laudem dubiam prorsus reddat aut deroget Exoticis, quod utiq; §. 5. & 6. factum: neq; e sola Scriptura universam Chronologiam dedu- cendam credat, quod cum Beroaldo, Brugthono, Da- vide Pareo statuit §. 8. etsi ab illis ex solius Script. S, autoritate id demonstrari tentatum quidem, sed non ad finem deductum agnoscat, a se autem id primum factum censeat. Quod μεγαλίαν f. ἄιτημα, sive πρό- βλημα ita demonstratum vellem, ut mundo congra- tulari (uti autor expetit) fas esset, ipsa certe luben- tia lubentius congratulantibus me jungerem, impri- mis, si inde Judæi & Athei, quemadmodum ipse ven- ditat, infallibiliter convinci possent de tempore nativi- tatis Messiæ, ita ut ad eos convertendos ex V. T. iis ad oculum id demonstrari queat. Sed nisi aliæ demon- strationes, quam per præcisum calculum annorum usque ad adventum Christi, eorumque omnium e sola Scriptura deducendorum, adhibitæ fuerint, valde verendum, ne opus conversionis Judæorum & Atheorum, quod pie meditari videtur Dn. Ra- vius, irritum sit atque frustraneum.

Agnoscit utique Pareus ipse, majus quid huma- no ingenio moliri, qui tempus Astronomicum a primo creationis puncto ad principium æræ Christianæ exa- Etum se nobis dare posse promittunt, idq; inde, quod nec primum punctum motuum a priori certum dari queat, nec a primo puncto ad Christi natales motuum perpe- tuorum veræ & certæ exhiberi possint tabulæ; nec deniq; Epocharum & eventuum singularium vel præcipuorum alligatio ad motuum tabulas vera ac certa designari possit. Hæc tria ingenue professus est Pareus, majora esse humano ingenio, sed ea sese præstare posse, imo præ- stitisse magna confidentia affirmat Dn. Ravius.

Et primum quidem quod attinet Æquinoctium vernum, non autumnale mundi conditi initium fuis- se apodictice e Scriptura S. probari posse persuasus est. Quanquam vero magis probabilem illam senten- tiam esse agnoscamus, quod mundus ceperit vernali tempore, quam multis autoritatibus confirmavi- mus Sect. II. q. I. ἀπόδειξιν tamen, eamque multipli- cem hic jactitare forte nemo præter Dn. Ravium ha- ctenus ausus est. Et magna sane præsumtio est, e c. XII. Exodi pro illa sententia; Sed infallibilem inde confici ἀπόδειξιν, hoc modo: quia illic incepit annus a vere f. M. Nisan, Ergo & primus mundi annus a vere cepit, haud facile quisquam alius dixerit. Porro quomodo cum Codomanno, aut aliis in gratiam redi- turus est noster, qui non in diem primum creationis veris initium, & æquinoctium vernale conjiciunt, sed in diem quartum, cum luminaria creata sunt? Ita enim Beda lib. de nat. rerum c. VI. Primus dies sæcu- li fuit triduo ante æquinoctium vernum, quod diei quarto competit propter luminaria tunc creata. Quem multi alii sequuntur. Si autem ne initium quidem mundi, quoad diem, infallibiliter certum est, quo- modo omnes dies mundi se in numerato habere, & apodictice, ac infallibiliter demonstrare posse præ- sumit Autor? Atq; hæc est prima Chronologi nostri Apodixis.

Altera eo nititur principio, quod eadem die se- ptimanæ feria sc. quinta intrarit Abraham in Ægy- ptum, qua exierint Abrahamidæ ex Ægypto, eademq; feria ceperit uterque annus mundi, tum ingressus Abra- hami, tum egressus Abrahamidarum, anni scil. 2085. & anni 2514. Unde vero illud principium docebitur? Hic confidenter asserit Dn. Ravius Ex. XII, 40. 41, 51. bis hanc συζυγίαν & concentricitatem observari: Sed ego ne semel quidem eam ibi videre potui, nec potuere hactenus alii, satis profecto oculati, inter- pretes & Chronologi. Nullum enim in textu habetur verbum de die vel feria ingressus Abrahami in Ægy- ptum, sed temporis solum mentio sit habitationis fi- liorum Israel in Ægypto, sub quo nomine, etsi Abrahamum comprehendi ceu stirpem admitta- mus, non tamen dies ingressus ejusdem in Ægyptum expressus est, multo minus definita illa συγκυρία & concentricitas, quod eadem feria, qua ex Ægypto e- gressi sunt Israelitæ, ingressus sit Ægyptum Abraham. Porro annus vocationis Abrahæ, quem eundem an- num ingressus ipsius in Ægyptum facit (quod vero expresse in Scriptura definitum non reperitur) non est a mundo condito annus 2085. sed 2083. adeoque annus Exodi est 2513. Assumta vero illa hypothesi, quod anno 2085. Abraham ingressus in Ægyptum sit, & inde numerari debeant 430. anni a Spiritu S. Exod. XII. definiti, prodeunt non anni 2514. sed 2515. Unde textum Exodi, ut suæ conveniat hypothesi, torquere coactus est autor novæ Chronologiæ, de quo postea. Deniq; in subsidium suæ opinionis duas diversas efformat Epochas, cum Scriptura non nisi unam tradiderit, 430. sc. annorum a promissione Ab- rahæ facta ad exitum ex Ægypto Ex. XII, 40. Gal. III, 17. ab ea enim distinguit Ravius Epocham ab ingres- su Abrahæ in Ægyptum, usq; ad egressum Israelitarum ex Ægypto, quam 429. annis integris præcise absolu- tam vult; de qua distinctione Epocharum nec vola nec vestigium in Scripturis apparet.

Jam ergo alterum postulatum Pareanum a Dn. Ravio minime præstitum esse, facile apparet: nam si ne quidem primum illud punctum mundi apodictice constat, quomodo ab eo tabulæ indubitato veræ de- duci potuere? Quod vero assumit Dn. Ravius, seri- em annorum M. usq; ad Hierosolymorum eversionem esse 4212. eamq; bis denunciatam in V. T. legi, non af- ferendum nude, sed solide probandum erat. Nemo enim hactenus invento est, qui semel tantum eorum annorum seriem repererit. Et utut admittatur men- ses in Scriptura non Solares, sed Lunares esse, quod ve- ro multi Chronologorum concessuri haud sunt, non tamen motuum perpetuorum tabulæ certæ quoad menses, hebdomadas & ferias haberi possunt, ubi ne quoad annos quidem certitudo infallibilis suppetit, quod de Raviana Chronologia postmodum consta- bit. Deniq; motuum perpetuorum tabulæ Astrono- mice extructæ nullæ in hac Chronologia visuntur, mirum ergo est, quod easdem hic exhiberi autor tantopere jactitet.

Tertium Parei postulatum erat, ut Epocharum & eventuum singularium vel præcipuarum alligatio ad motuum tabulas vera ac certa fiat, quod a se factum esse persuasissimus est Dn. Ravius, adeo, ut hujusce alligationis suæ, autorem ipsummet Spiritum S. fa- cere non ambigat, Sed quum motuum perpetuo- rum tabulæ ex principiis Astronomicis exstructæ nullæ compareant in Raviana Chronologia, quomodo ad easdem alligatio Epocharum facta dici potest? Si dicat, menses in Scriptura non solares esse, neque Lunares, sive ad φάσιν, sive ad σύνοδον respiciamus, sed Politicos 30. dierum singulos, omnes plenos, nullos cavos, ideoque aliis tabulis opus non esse, nisi quæ e feriarum hebdomadalium observatione adornan- tur, discutiendum id aliis, qui Chronologiæ generali & abstractæ operam navant, relinquimus; hæc enim sententia a nemine fortassis hactenus asserta vel au- dita altioris videtur indaginis. Ita sane magnum erit in Biblica Chronologia compendium, & multis aliis characteribus Astronomicis facile carere poteri- mus. Et non parum probabilis videri possit illa sententia ex anno imprimis diluviali, tum etiam ex eo, quod non consentaneum videatur diversam formam in aliis annis observatam ex lege divina, aut populum rudem ad annos Solares vel Lunares, & observationem Novi - Lunii, aut plenilunii ad- strictum fuisse: unde illi opinioni, si σοχασικῶς proponatur, ceu probabilis, non pro infallibili ven- ditur, locus forte relinqui posset. Similiter ergo disquiri permittimus de illis problematibus, quæ hîc occurrunt, utpote 1. annon νεωμενία potius a novo mense politico, quam a nova Luna ducatur, dicaturǵ;? 2. an primæ ac decimæ quartæ Lunæ s. novilunii & plenilunii observatio uspiam in Scriptura præcepta? 3. an Paschatos ad plenilunium exierint Abrahamidæ ex Ægypto. 4. num Pascha ad Lunam ordinatum fuerit unquam, an vero semper ad decimum quintum diem anni seu mensis primi politici adstrictum? quod posterius cum affir- mat Dn. Ravius, omnem illam Orientis & Occidentis de Paschatibus quæstionem, & Nicenorum Patrum ordinationem vix alicujus esse momenti audacter pronunciat, nosǵ; Christianos semper decimum quintum, 16. 17. 18. 19. 20. 21. Nisan, in quemcunǵ; dies Solis resurrectionis Christi caderet, feriari posse, censet. 5. an Ebræi suam Pentecosten semper tempore Vet. Test. ut nos Christiani in N. T. die Solis, feriati sint, idǵ; juxta legem Levit. XXIII, 15. 16. quam reddit, Mimmachorath hassabath, h. e. a die crastina Sabbati in hebdomadam Paschalem incidentis numerandam esse Pentecosten, non vero a crastina Paschatis. Quæ explicatio ejus si admittenda, ubi Pascha inciderit in feriam secundam, a die Solis, vel Dominica Sabbatum hebdomadale sequenti demum incipienda fuisset numeratio septem hebdomadum ad Pentecosten, neq; 50. dies cum intercessissent Paschatos & Pentecostes festo, sed 57. quod quomodo Legi & praxi Judaicæ sub Vet. Test. consentaneum sit, non video. Hactenus certe illa ἀνίσoματα omnia pro paradoxis habita, nec facile audita talis Legis divinæ fuit interpretatio ante Codomannum, qui libro I. Chron. c. 9. illam cum Paschate Jos. V, 14. celebrato nequicquam conciliare conatus est. In magnis utique erroribus huc usque perpetuo tot seculis hæsisset totus orbis literatus, Chronologorum imprimis, & Interpretum Scripturæ, non Judæorum tantum, sed etiam Christianorum, si admittendæ forent istæ Ravianæ hypotheses. Quicquid vero de istis sit, qua permittit Scripturæ S. autoritas, disquiri fortassis illa τοπικῶς poterunt, definiri autem ἀποδεικτικῶς vix quidem possunt.

Pro confirmandis autem tabulis suis adfert Dn. Ravius exempla nonnulla, sed quia illa cum petitione principii conjuncta sunt, non attinet operose iisdem immorari. Ex ipsa Epocharum discussione, verane an vana sint Ravii de alligationis certitudine persuasio, satis apparebit. Videamus tamen paucis Exempla. In primo citra probationem & gratis assumitur, Abrahamum decimo quinto mensis Nisan feria quinta Ægyptum intraffe. Ubi enim hoc vel in libro Scripturæ, vel naturæ, ad quem utrumque provocat, scriptum? Id vero Scripturæ etiam contrariatur, quod in eodem exemplo 429. annos tantum intercessisse ait. Terminum etiam a quo hujusce Epochæ non figendum esse in introitu Abrahæ in Ægyptum, sed in promissione ipsi facta e Gal. III, 17. manifestum est. Quam Apostoli Epocham non esse diversam a Mosaica Ex. XII, 40. sed eandem prorsus, & collatio docet locorum, & ab omnibus hactenq creditum est. Nec vero solidum est, quod hic, & passim αἰτήματος vel ἀξιώματος instar supponit, quasi anni Epocharum ratione termini a quo & ad quem sic ἀποτόμως integri sint, & integre accipiendi, ut dies etiam exacte conveniant, ac nominatis 430. annis, totidem quot illi conficiunt dies definiti sint a Spir. S. quod nec de hac, nec de aliis Epochis præcise demonstrabitur. Neque vero quia dies egressus hîc designatus est 15. Nisan, & numerati sunt anni incolatus Abrahamitarum, consequens est, a primo die incolatus ad primum exitus diem annos illos quoad menses, septimanas, ac dies- integre absolutos fuisse, ut ne una dies desideretur: nam annos tantum numeratos esse a Spiritu S. quo- ad tempus commorationis vel incolatus, non autem collatum esse terminum incepti, & finiti incolatus, quo- ad ipsosmet dies, (nedum feriam etiam eandem he- bdomadæ in termino a quo & ad quem illorum an- norum definitam esse) litera textus docet. Nec sane convenit illa præcisa determinatio, quia Moses ter- minum ad quem Epochæ hujusce constituit exitum post annum 430. factum, Paulus vero terminum ad quem ejusdem facit promulgationem legis: utut 50. abs se diebus distabant Exodus & νομοθεσία; quod luculento est indicio, non attendi præcise dies, sed annos Epochæ hujus solum definiri.

Similiter ἀντίγραφον est in exemplo secundo, Templum Salomonis in 481. anni mensem 2. diem 2. incidisse quoad structuræ initium, cum 480. annus, mensisq; ejus secundus aperte definitus sit 1. Reg. 6, 1. quo initium ejus factum.

In tertio exemplo de anno tertio Cyri Dan. 10, 4. temere asseritur, Spiritum S. addidisse characterem anni calendalem, diem Jovis, & apud Haggeum, c. 1. & VI. pariter, ut & Zachariam characterem Diei Mar- tis: nam in nullo apud hos Prophetas loco diei Mar- tis, vel feriæ tertiæ mentio facta, sive κατὰ γράμμα s. κατὰ πρᾶγμα. Atq; ita de aliis. Sed hæc de gene- rali introductione dicta sunto; quæ quam longe absit ab ἀποδείξει infallibili, jam liquere potest. Diluci- dius tamen id in speciali introductione, & demonstra- tione, quam vocat, infallibilitatis ex libro Naturæ & Scripturæ, patebit.

Id vero præmittendum adhuc de fundamentis Chronologiæ istius, quod eam quidem e libro Na- turæ & Scripturæ deductam esse asserat autor, sed circa ea, quæ ad libri Naturæ collationem faciunt, assumat hoc ceu διδόμενον, (cætera enim huc non spectant, neq; nostræ sunt professionis: videant de eo Mathematici, & qui in abstracto Chronologiam tractant, quomodo ipse omnes fere characteres incer- tos, periodum vero Julianam inutilem reddere cone- tur) quod revelationes divinæ semper vel feria septima, die sabbati festo, vel die antefesto feria sexta, quæ Vene- ris est, vel interfesto die Martis feria tertia factæ sint; quod vero ut ipsi concedatur & admittatur nulla est necessitas. Et cùm ubiq; demonstrationes ven- ditet, quænam obsecro hujus hypotheseos proferri poterit demonstratio, sive a priori, sive a posteriori?

Cæterum de Epochis, quas e S. literis in suo temporum breviario, in hac Chronologia distincte produxit, imprimis hîc dispiciendum, de quibus generatim ita monuit: Omnes hactenus Chronologi omittunt hinc inde alii alios, vel inferciunt alios a se ef- fictos annos, mutant quadrata rotundis, & rotunda quadratis. Grave ἔγκλημα adversus non quosdam fortè, sed OMNES Chronologos. Fecit autem Ipse XII. Epochas, quas tamen post ad novem redegit. De PRIMA a mundi initio ad diluvii annum non est, quod moneamus; ὁμοψηφίαν enim nostram Sectio II. Chronici docebit.

SECUNDA ab anno diluvii inclusive ad Ab- rahæ introitum in Ægyptum exclusivê 429. annorum expressè in Scriptùris non habetur; nuspiam enim vel numerus ille annorum 429. vel initium Epochæ ad certum diem alligatum reperitur, aut terminus ejusdem ita designatus est. Epocha vero a diluvio ad Ἐπαγγελίαν Abrahæ factam 427. annorum Se- ctione III. Chronici definita est.

TERTIA ad annos ablactationis Isaaci exclusivè 29. annorum, etsi ceu probabilis admitti forsan pos- sit, apodicticè e S. literis nunquam evincetur.

QVARTA ad annum exitus 400. annorum expressa quantum ad numerum annorum in Sacris, sed initium eam capere ab Isaaci ablactatione, defi- nitum non est. Neq; vero ita numerus annorum ex- pressus est, uti Ravius vult: nam ad tempus exitus sic numerantur 400. anni a Spir. S. ut 430. elapsi di- cantur a promissione Abrahæ ad Exodum, neq; initio anni 430. exodus assignetur, nedum ad eandem men- sis diem, aut feriam septimanalem, qua ingressus Ab- raham est Ægyptum, alligetur, Exod. 12, 40. unde suam hypothesin salvare non potuit Dn. Ravius, quin novam & versionem & interpretationem tex- tus Sacri excogitarit, quod τεχνύδριον valde ipsi so- lemne esse, ea quæ de prioribus Geneseos capp. no- væ versionis & interpretationis ante aliquot annos edidit specimina, affatim docuerunt, quæ proinde publica autoritate in inclyto regno Suecico repressa sunt. Sic enim locum exodi reddendum & accipi- endum esse in literis 20. Martii anni hujus 1670. Ki- lonio ad me datis contendit: Sub initium anni 430. ac- cidebat, ut eadem feria septimanali exirent copiæ mili- tares Jehovæ e regno, sc. qua Abraham Ægyptum intra- vit. Quæ versio & interpretatio hactenus vere in- inaudita est, neque e textu authentico effertur, sed fertur eidem. Nihil enim illic de Abrahami ingres- su in Ægyptum expressum, nihil prorsus de feria se- ptimanali vel obscure indicatum, nedum de eadem feria, qua Abraham in Ægyptum ingressus est. Porro non initium anni 430. sed finis ibi comme- moratur vocabulo קֵץ, quod non est sub initium, sed a fine 430. anni, vel post 430. annum : Quemad- modum etiam S. Paulus habet Gal. 3, 17. μετὰ ἔτη τετρακόσια κὶ τριάκοντα, post annos 430. Adde quod in textu Mosis diferte habeatur, habitationem filio- rum Israelis in Ægypto fuisse non tantum annorum 429. sed annorum 430. ne quis si forte uspiam קֵץ occurrat pro initio, (quod tamen hactenus ostensum non est, nec vocis significationi convenit, quæ finem notat, non initium) hîc terminum anni initialem in- telligat. Verba illa בְּעֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה quæ Pagninus & Ariasmontanus reddunt in corpore diei hujus, Junius & Tremellius eodem ipso die, a nemi- ne, quod sciam, interpretum vel Doctorum accipi- untur cum relatione ad feriam illam septimanalem, qua ingressus est Abraham Ægyptum, sed respicere censentur illum diem, de quo ibi egit Moses, quo nempe celebratum est Pascha. Neq; illa relatio ad diem ingressus e textu colligi potest, imo noctis men- tio sit, in qua sc. & Pascha celebratum, & egressus fa- ctus dicitur, eaq; non ideo observabilis, & ut ob- servetur ab Israelitis, præcipitur, ut constet respe- ctum haberi ad ingressum Abrahæ in Ægyptum, sed ut memoria conservetur temporis egressus. Quales ergo sint apodixes Ravianæ, iterum ab hoc exemplo constat.

QVINTA Epocha ad primum annum realem Jubilæum Mosi celebratum & κληρυχίας exclusive an- norum 39, inde ab exodo, multis eget hypothesibus, ut hîc nemo præter Dn. Ravium temere apodixin admissurus sit. 1. Non dicam de Sabbaticis & Jobelæis prolepticis ante latam legem celebratis, qui vere ima- ginarii sunt, qui tamen ab autore, si non hoc in loco, alias subinde ingeruntur. 2. Annus Jobelæus Mosis realis nullum fundamentum in re habet; nam Mo- sen præcepisse quidem annorum Jobelæorum ce- lebrationem, e Lev. XXV. constat, celebrasse ve- ro ipsummet, nuspiam legimus. 3. Prædixisse Mosen 38. annis ante realem hunc Jobelæum, vel etiam sabbaticum annum, ab ἰδίᾳ ἐπιλύσει est. Nullibi ea prædictio in S. literis exstat. Lev. 25, 2. non Prophetia habetur, sed mandatum; quem lo- cum proinde nova & versione, & versionis suæ in- terpolatione Vir Clarissimus suæ hypothesi aptare conatus est, sed non sine perversione. Quos auto- res versionis & expositionis istius habeat, ipse vide- rit. Nimirum Dominus præcepit, ut post ingres- sum in terram Canaan & deinceps Sabbatizet terra Sabbatum Domino, v. 2. quod exponit Moses ul- terius versibus seqq. quomodo observandum sit, ita nempe, ut sex annis ab ingressu in terram Canaan se- minetur terra, anno vero septimo quiescat. Dn. Ravius vero versum 2. a seqq. quantum ad sensum, divellit, & versu 2. Prophetiam de quiete terræ & Sab- bato primo coacto 6. prioribus mensibus in regnis Cis- Jordanicis, 6. posterioribus in terra Canaan celebrando facit, reliquis autem versibus institutionem Sabbati spontanei Ebræorum exhiberi vult: quæ mera est ψευδερμηνεία. Nullum hîc vaticinium esse, sed præ- cepta solum a Mose proponi, & antecedentia satis docent, & consequentia. 4. Mosis ultimum vitæ annum primum Sabbaticum & Jobelæum realem fu- isse annum mundi 2553. apodictice probandum erat. Alii enim magno consensu ab autumno anni 2554. post mortem Mosis, quo post cessationem Mannæ terram primum serere Israëlitis contigit, uti nume- rant primum τῆς γεωργίας annum, ita radicem etiam annorum Sabbaticorum ibi figunt, vi hujusce loci Lev. 25, 2. & 9. ut & Deut. 15, 1. & 9. 31, 10. Quæ vero pro novella sententia adferuntur argumenta, ne probabilia quidem sunt, nedum apodictica. Dicit, prædictum fuisse totis 38. annis ante, diem 10. Septem- bris, quo cum Sihone Rege depugnatum est, fore propi- tium, ab eoq́; die inchoatum esse illum coactum Sabba- ticum annum, qui simul Jubelæus fuit, quia mera jubi- la vigebant inter Israëlitas victores ubiq́; locorum. Sed illa prædictio frustra fingitur, nec ullum testimoni- um de isto initio anni sabbatici coacti, annove ipso proferri potest ex universis scriptis Mosaicis: neq; Jobelæus annus uspiam ita dicitur ob mera victoria- rum Jubilea, sed ob alias causas & fines, quorum gra- tia anni Jobelei sanciti sunt. Deniq; anni illi 39. qui huic Epochæ assignantur ab autore, inclusi jam sunt annis alterius Epochæ, utpote quam deinde recen- set ab exitu Israëlitarum ad quartum Salomonis an- num, quam in ordine septimam facit Dn. Ravius e 1. Reg. 6, 1. quod omnino dicendum est, nisi Spiritui S. ita Epocham eam illic assignanti contradicendum sit. Atq; hæc ad quintam Epocham Ravianam di- xisse sufficiat.

SEXTA itidem plane ἐμβολιμαῖος est, a pri- mo anno reali Jobeleo Mosi celebrato ad finem itineris Israëlitarum seu occupatæ Canaan a duodecim tribu- bus exclusive 79. annorum designata. De qua nec in Scripturis S. nec in antiquitate ullum reperitur vestigium. Debet autem hanc Epocham Dn. Ra- vius (etsi hoc dissimulet) Laurentio Codomanno, qui eundem in Systema Chronologicum primus inve- xit, sed hactenus applausores non invenit; a quo etiam in plusculis discessit ipse Dn. Ravius; utpote annum mundi 2514. faciens exoticum (quem Codo- mannus fecit 2515.) & primum annorum Jobeleorum Mosi assignans, celebratum Anno 2553. devicto Si- hone, (quum Codomannus demum Anno M. 2554. Sihonem devictum, & anno 2561. primum Jobeleum sub Josua celebratum statuat; ) & finem itineris seu occupatæ Canaan fingat in ann. M. 2631. quem ponit Codomannus in ann. M. 2633. & quæ aliæ notari possent discrepantiæ. Nec vero tantum ἀτεχ γραφῆς fingitur hæc Epocha, sed ἀντίγραφός etiam palam est, siquidem 1. Reg. 6, 1. ab exitu Israe- litarum ex Ægypto usq́; ad templum a Salomone strui cœptum non nisi 480. anni numerentur a S. S. quem numerum immutare omnibus piis mentibus reli- gio est: a qua vero definitione Codomannus & Ra- vius abeunt, non 480. sed 599. annos ab exitu Israe- litarum ad initium templi numerantes : unde se tor- quet circa hunc locum Codomannus l. 1. Chron. c. 17. præferens consensum historiæ Judicum, & narratio- nis Paulinæ Act. XIII. testimonio præsenti Spiritus S. (qui tamen cum illo consensu probe consistere po- test, nec ei opponi, sed juxta cum Historia Judicum & Paulina relatione sancte suscipi debet) adeoque; ita detorquet Epocham illam libri Regum: terminum a quo, qui exitus Israëlitarum expresse illic constitui- tur, non esse exitum eorum ex Ægypto, sed finem occu- pationis terræ Canaan, 25. nempe annum post Athnielis victoriam, cum primum tribus Dan sua forte potieba- tur: quæ utique; toto cœlo distant: siquidem longe a- liud sit exitus Israëlitarum ex Ægypto, aliud vero finis occupationis terræ Canaan, quæ in Scriptura æqui- pollere ad Calendas Græcas docebitur : ac quiesce- re tamen huic non tam explicationi, quam depra- vationi Codomanni videtur Dn. Ravius, nec aliam suæ præconceptæ opinioni convenientem in- venire potuit ἐπίλυσιν. Non autem satis reveren- ter in autorem Scripturæ Spiritum S. Codomannus l. c. Chron. p. 113. Deus ipse, inquit, duorum fide di- gnorum testimonio non vult præferri asseverationem u- nius testis, (quod de testibus humanis verum est, ad testimonium autem Spiritus S. quod sive semel tan- tum proferatur, seu sæpius, semper est ἀξιόπιστον & ἀνυπεύθυνον, minus pie applicatur) quem aut falsa, aut interpretationem occultam, neque; cuivis obviam (at- qui verba non obscura sunt, sed luculentissima, & cuivis maxime obvia in loco 1. Reg. 6, 1.) admitten- tia loqui necesse est &c. Ecquis Spiritum S. falsa alicu- bi loqui admittet, nisi impius plane sit?

Sed ad Ravium revertamur: qui non veretur argumentis nonnullis magnum hunc numerum li- bri Regum arietare, suamque contra sententiam de inserendis 118. annis itineris ex Ægypto ad finitam occupationem terræ promissæ stabilire. 1. Quod alias non darentur 450. anni ad initium Samuelis mi- nistri publici, quos assignare Lucam Act. 13, 20. ait. At non assignat Lucas annos tot a distributione ter- ræ Josuanæ ad Samuelem, sed intre 450. annos circi- ter illa peracta dicit, quæ retulerat, siquidem inde a nativitate Isaaci ad distributionem terræ, de quibus e- gerat, 447. anni elapsi sint, & μετὰ ταῦτα post illa peracta datos esse Judices usque; ad Samuelem Prophetam perhibet: ut supra sub finem quintæ sectionis monui- mus. 2. Quod liber Judicum recenseat 430. annos continuos a prima servitute, quibus si addantur 20. Se- niorum anni, qui post Josuam præfuere, 450. Lucæ an- nos prodituros ait Ravius. Sed longe aliter nume- randos esse annos in Judicum libro, suo loco, h. e. quæstione tertia Sect. V. monuimus, neque inveniri a morte Josuæ ad excessum Eli 450. sed solum 339. annos, ibidem ostendimus. Multa precario assumit Dn. Ravius in speciali annorum istorum 450. com- puto, qua annos regiminis Judicum; de quibus hic non attinet speciatim dicere, quum e loco dicto de iis judicium fieri possit. 3. Librum Josuæ annos hoc κρινομένως 118. demonstrare censet, sed nullam adfert ἀπόδειξιν: Primum ait annos 40. Mosis tacite in li- bro Josuæ supponi: Sed illi inclusi sunt in illustri Epo- cha illa 480. annorum. Non ergo abripi possunt ad annos eam antegressos, aut Epocham aliquam an- tecedaneam : Jam 70. illi anni, qui decem tribubus ad occupandas sedes sibi assignatas tribuuntur, ita ut singulæ septennio suas occuparint, temere, & ex ingenio humano finguntur: e quibus 20. & plures annos vivo Josua impensos esse, parili, hoc est, nul- lo nititur fundamento: quum Josuam 20. annis (excluso regimine Seniorum post fata Josuæ) præ- fuisse, nullo constare possit documento. Denique octo Cusaris anni, qui illis 40. Mosis, & 70. occupa- tionis decem tribuum accedunt, ex autoris mente incidunt in tempora Isaschar: necessum autem est, ut etiam ad tempora Asser sese porrigant, quia cui- libet tribui 7. nulli 8. tributi ab ipso sunt anni, (li- cet mere voluntaria sit ista assignatio) neq; si ad Isa- schari tempora referantur, seorsim numerari præ- ter dena illa septennia possunt, ut a Ravio factum, cum intra complexum illorum septenniorum con- tineantur. 4. Argumentum a feriali charactere desumitur, sed quum feriam determinare fas non sit, anno integro, imo annis pluribus repugnantibus computo sacro, non est quod illud moremur.

Quintum ab autoritatibus non juvat Dn. Autorem: quia ex illis 21. autoribus nemo est, qui eidem suf- fragetur in computo, vel in assignandis illis irrepti- tiis 118. annis: nec quenquam facile ex antiquitate, forte nec e neotericis, præter Codomannum, produ- cturus est sibi ὁμόψηφον. In specie ergo singulas illas autoritates excutere supervacaneum est. Excedunt nonnulli numerum annorum ab exitu ad templum 480. nonnulli etiam transcendunt annorum a Ravio assignatorum numerum. Parum inde solatii pro definitione annorum 118. præcisa. Nihil aliud varie- tas ista docet, quam quod infeliciter procedant, qui deserunt Epocham expressissime a Spiritu S. 1. Reg. 6, 1. designatam. Nusquam enim sibi constat men- dacium; sola veritas immobilis est. 6. Verba

Jephthæ Jud. 11, 26. de 300. annis a tempore habita- tionis Israel nihil faciunt ad hos supernumerarios 118. annos ἀγράφως; ut autem cogantur congrue- re, 71. annos quinque servitutum, quos antea distincte numerarat Ravius, jam quiescere vel omitti jubet, ne in computum veniant, sibiq; inutiles sint, utpote 8. Cusanis, 18. Eglonis, 20. Jabini, 18. Ammon. 7. Mi- dianitarum; & ut numerum adimpleat, sex annos sui regiminis adhuc futuri Prophetice Jephtham, etsi de elapsis, non futuris annis loquatur, adjecisse ait, ac 25. annos regiminis Josuæ, 20. Seniorum guber- nationi pro lubitu (extra Scripturam certe) assi- gnat. En præclaram ἀπόδειξιν! Annon hoc est mu- tare quadrata rotundis? Numeratis vero annis 248. qui e Scriptura constant, a morte Josuæ usque ad Jephtham, quibus ultimus Mosis, & 17. principatus Josuæ accedant, fiunt 266. anni: per rotundatio- nem ergo numeri facile 300. anni dici poterant, quod propemodum tribus seculis terras illas posside- rint Israelitæ; ut opus non sit ad ejusmodi violentum & tumultuarium calculum sese recipere. Atque hæ sunt demonstrationes illæ infallibiles, de quibus autor pronunciare circa hanc fictitiam Epocham non veretur; Cui hæc non satisfaciunt ad 118. annos itineris Israelitici demonstrandos nihil satisfacit. Di- xerim potius qui hæc apodictica haud esse non videt, nihil videt. Addit autem postliminio demonstra- tionem annorum ducatus Josuæ ex annis Jobeleis, & Sab- baticis, sed quæ, qualis & quanta illa sit, ex iis, quæ antea de annis Jobeleis & Sabbaticis diximus, jam patere potest. Hæc ergo etiam de Sexta Epocha.

SEPTIMA est ad quartum annum Salomonis templi strui cœpti, exclusive 480. quæ recte quidem se habet, sed quia initium ejus non assumitur juxta du- ctum Spiritus S. ab exitu Israelitarum, ideo in cal- culo error committitur, dum 3111. anni numeran- tur a mundo condito ad templum Salomonis, Co- domanno numerante 3112. Veriorem calculum in no- stro tradidimus Chronico. OCTAVAM assignat ad finem Idololatriæ do- mus Judæ, sive ad Schisma Israelis exclusive 40. an- norum. Sed idololatriam domus Judæ & cum quarto anno Salomonis cepisse, & finem habuisse quarto an- no Rehoboami, temere & ἄτερ γραφῆς dicitur, imo Scripturæ contrarium est: quæ Salomonem, cum templum Domini exstrueret, cui septennium im- pendit, neutiquam statim idololatriæ deditum, sed postmodum demum ab uxoribus alienigenis eo se- ductum fuisse, satis docet, 1. Reg. 8. & 11. capp. & Schisma Israelis mox cum initio regiminis Jero- boami cepisse, testatur, 1. Reg. XII. ut taceam, quod explicari non possit, quomodo anni peccatorum Ju- dæ quarto Rehoboami anno finem consecuti sint.

NONA itaque Epocha annos Idololatriæ domus Israelis usque ad templum exustum complectens, in eo citra causam divaricatur a communi sententia de annis peccatorum domus Judæ, & domus Israelis, quod seorsim utrosque annos computet, & finiat: quum in eodem termino finem consequantur. Ratio contraria, quod Epocha illa Ezech. 4, 4. de peccatis Judæ & Israelis duo habeat latera, dextrum & sinistrum, ideoque sub annis Josiæ & sequentibus neque- ant simul concipi, nullius est momenti, quia duobus lateribus incumbere debeat Ezechiel, non quod an- nis discontinuis pœnæ idololatriæ sustinendæ essent domui Judæ & domui Israelis, sed quod domus Ju- da postremo etiam, quia per Josiæ pientissimi Regis commonitiones & exemplum ad pœnitentiam con- tinuandam revocari non poterat, sed ad vomitum revertebatur, ad pœnas abripienda, & cum Israeliticis reliquiis exscindenda ob peccata, & idololatriam fit. Pareus certe, qui seorsim annos illos numerat, summam istam ex historia Regum Juda, & Israelis indagare desperavit, adeoque incertum esse professus est, unde hi anni inchoandi & ubi finiendi sint. Ra- vius vero assignat 40. annos a 4. Salom. Regis ad Re- habeami primum, (quum tamen tantum 37. eo usque elapsi sint, nec quartus annus Rehabeami cum pri- mo confundi possit, aut debeat) reliquos 390. annos dividit in tres partes; prima est 91. annorum usque ad unicum Achasiæ annum. Altera annorum 164. ad Hiskiæ sextum inclusive. Tertia 135. usque ad destru- ctionem Hierosolymorum. In priori autem parte non 91. invenit annos, sed 95. nimirum Rehabeami 17. Abiæ 3. Asæ 41. Josaphat 25. Jorami 8. Achasiæ 1. in annis Regum Judæ: in annis vero Regum Israelis 98. utpote Jeroboami 22. Nadab. 2. Baasæ 24. Elæ 2. Simri 7. dies, Omri 12. Achab 22. Achasiæ 2. Jo- rami 12. quos, quomodo exæquare satagat, non atti- net disquirere. Conferri poterit nostra exæqua- tio e Tabula Regum Juda & Israelis. Difficultatem autem illam unius anni Achasiæ Judæi 2. Reg. 8, 25. 2. Chron. 22, 2. quomodo dicatur Achasias cum Patre Joramo illic filius 22. annorum, hic vero 42. annorum regnasse, quum post patrem 40. annos natum mortuum successor fuerit filius annos natus 42. 2. Chron. 21. v. 20. adeoque ita statuendus sit biennio major Patre suo fuisse, ita expedire conatur, quod Achasias fue- rit 22. annorum ætatis, atque unicum annum suum in 42. seculi sui incidentem habuerit: in qua concilia- tione sibi revelata admodum triumphat Ravius, quod nemo hactenus hanc S. Scripturæ conciliationem observarit. Sed seculi annos definire nuspiam Scri- ptura consuevit, ut nempe dicat hunc illo, vel isto seculi currentis a Mundo condito anno regnasse, aut hoc vel istud egisse: sine exemplo ergo est illa, ἔκθεσις, quam in præsidium suæ Chronologiæ ex- cogitavit, quasi seculi mundi trigesimi tertii annus 42. vel annus Mundi 3242. per 42. Achasiæ indigitetur. Rectius autem annus ille numeratur ab initio æræ Samaritanæ, quæ 6. anno Omri proavi materni cœ- pit, ut in Chronico notavimus. Vid. Anti-Grot. nostra ad 2. Par. 23, 2.

Quod ad secundum ordinem parallelorum Re- gum Judæ & Israelis, 164. annorum, recensentur 165. anni Regum Judæ in eodem, utpote Athaliæ 6. Joasi 40. Amasiæ 29. Josiæ 52. Jothami 16. Achasi 16. & Hiskiæ 6. Regum vero Israelis 143. a Jehu usq; ad Hoseæ 9. quorum exæquatio Raviana cum nostra in tabula Regum tradita conferatur: ] Id autem me non capere fateor, qui Hoseam, Regem & Prophetam simul dicat, quum Rex Israeliticus Hoseas a Propheta hu- jus nominis maxime distinguatur; siquidem illum interfecto Peka regnum invasisse ac impie regnasse constet 2. Reg. 15, 30. c. 17, 1.

Tertium membrum 390. annorum Israeliticæ Idolatriæ secundum Ravium absolvitur periodo 135. annorum, a fine nempe Regni Israelitici ad finem regni Judaici: sed rectius finiuntur anni peccatorum Israelis anno 23. quam 19. Nebucadnezaris, cum a Ne- buzar Adan omnes Judæorum reliquiæ e Judæa ab- ductæ sunt, quinto excidii Hierosolymitani anno, Jer. 52, 30. Quem terminum etiam adsignat Codo- mannus l. III. Chron. cap. XVI. Ravius cum videat non posse se illum numerum 135. annorum confice- re ex annis regum Judæ post finem regni Israelitici, e mensibus tribus Joachas annum facit integrum, ac pariter annum e Jechoniæ 3. menses & 10. diebus, ut alia jam non attingamus, quæ in computo ejus desi- derari queant. Ubi, ut obiter exotica attingam, Ra- vius Salmanasserem, Sennacheribum & Nabonassarum confundit, ac pro eodem Rege habet. Sed Scriptu- ra Sennacheribum a Salmanassare distinguit 2. Reg.

XVI. & XVIII. filiumq; Sennacheribi facit Assarha- donem, 2. Reg. XIX, 37. Unde Codomannus illos et- iam distinxit, & Salmanassarem patrem Sennacheribi fecit: tametsi cum Funccio Salmanassarem ipsum Na- bonassareum esse velit; quem errorem B. D. Bebmius l. II. Chronol. Manud. Tit. III. c. IV. prolixe e sacris literis, & Exoticis Scriptoribus confutavit, quo Dn. Ravium remissum volumus. Salmanassar fuit Rex Assyriæ seu Ninives 2. Reg. 17, 31. Nabonassar Rex Ba- byloniæ; quæ duo regna diversa tum fuisse ex historia Ezechiæ constat: quia post interitum Sennacheribi Assyriorum Regis, Merodach Babyloniæ Rex ad Eze- chiam legatos misit, gratulandi ergo 2. Reg. XIX. Adde & Jer. L, 17. 18. Ezech. XXXI, 11. ubi hæc re- gna aperte distinguuntur. Similiter confundit Ra- vius cum Funccio Nabopallassarem Ptolemæi cum Nebucadnezare Scripturæ, quem istius filium esse Jo- sephus e fragmento Beros. lib. III. Antiquit. c. 11. do- cuit: quemque Ptolemæus Nabopallassaris nomine insignivit. Porro hujus famosissimi Regis Nebu- cadnezaris filio Evilmerodacho 30. annos tribuit Ra- vius, eosque Scripturam S. habere ait, sed ubi habeat Scriptura, nec ipse indicat, nec ego invenio. Ptole- mæus Ilvarodamo filio Nabopallassaris non nisi duos assignavit annos. Niricassolassarum & Nabonadium æque ac Nabopallassarum in Ptolemei Canone, etsi consentiat eidem Berosi Sacerdotis Beli fragmentum, propria auctoritate exterminat Ravius, & Belfaza- rem immediate Evilmerodacho, cum 14. annis regimi- nis succenturiat, quot Scripturam requirere confiden- ter asserit: quum ex adverso Nabonidus ultimus As- syriorum Monarcha, quem Danielis Belfazarem es- se constat, 17. annis præfuerit, juxta cœlestem Ptole- mæi Canonem. De suo ergo addit Dn. Ravius illos 14. annos, quos Belfazari tribuit, ejusdem annos, in Ca- none Ptolemei (quorum tamen summam assumit) locupletans, ut ab Hiskiæ anno primo incepisse pri- mum Nabonassaris, ex quo ad Cyrum 209. Ptolemeus numerat, concludat, adeoq; Nabonassaris primum cum primo Hiskiæ connectat: quæ vero compu- tatio & alligatio mere arbitraria, omniumque Chro- nologorum calculo contraria est, ut vel ex eo con- stat, quod juxta Ravium ad Christum natum 740.

anni Nabonassaris computandi sint: cum, obí rvan- te Usserio in annal. V. T. p. 88. ad ann. M. 3257. a me- ridie primi Thot mensis Ægyptiaci ante vulgarem no- stram æram Christianam anno 747. (non 740.) Na- bonassari Epocham SUMMO CONSENSU dedu- cant OMNES Astronomi. Nostro calculo æra Nabo- nassarea neque a primo; neque a septimo Hiskiæ, sed a 12. Jothami 20. annis ante Hiskiam inchoanda est. Sed hæc alias.

Progrediendum jam nobis est ad DECIMAM Epocham, quam captivitatis Babylonicæ cum Cyri primo annorum 71. facit Ravius, ordiens eandem ab exustione templi: quam vero non inde cœpisse, sed a quarto Jojakimi, in Chronico nostro oftendi- mus, nec est, ut quicquam hic porro addamus: com- mittimus solum Codomannum cum Ravio. Ille enim annum exusti templi facit a mundo condito 3534. quem hic constituit 3541. & uterq; non modo Sab- baticis sed & Jobeleis nititur, uterque dies cum men- sibus computat. Neque conciliare possumus illa Raviana, quod anno M. 3541. teinplum exustum, & ab eo numerandi sint anni captivitatis Babylonicæ, qui in Cyri initio desinant: & quod tertius Cyri fue- rit A. M. 3586. nam additis ad illos 3541. annis 70. us- que ad Cyrum, & duobus Cyri, non erit annus 3586. sed 3614. Si dicat forte, annum tertium regni Persici esse 3586. annum M. non vero Monarchiæ Cyri ter- tium: temere assumitur, Danielem c. 10, 1. de Cyri Persici regni tertio anno loqui, non de Monarchiæ e- jusdem tertio, quod textui repugnat: quia sub finem capitis Darii Medi primi anni, ceu jam præterlapsi, mentio sit, qui utique Cyri tertio regni Persici non- dum ad imperium adspirarat. Conf. Dan. 5, 30. 31.

UNDECIMAM Epocham facit annorum 121. & orditur a primo Cyri, quæ conflata est e 7. septen- niis prioribus Danielis, cœpti & finiti, ut ait, templi se- cundi, & 72. annis Zachariæ c. 1, 12. c. 7, 5. Hic autem primo fallitur Dn. Ravius, dum primum Cyri annum, vel potius secundum initium facit hebdomadum LXX. Danielis. Quæ sententia in Beroaldistis jam pridem est profligata, ac ne Codomanno ipsi, cujus vestigiis libenter inhæret Ravius, sese probare po- tuit. Vid. quæ adversus eam diximus Chron. S. Sect. VIII. quæst. 3. Fundamentum tamen Ravii hic expen- dendum, quod inprimis e Charactere anni tertii Cy- ri, sex secundi cœpti templi, anni nempe M. 3614. e Dan. 10, 4. petit; quod pro apodictico venditat. Sed ne quidem topicum id agnoscimus. Dicit, diem illam 24. mensis primi fuisse diem Sabbathi, inde concludit: Ergo annus cœpit a die Jovis: E. fuit annus M. 3586. Sed quid hoc facit ad ann. M. 3614. quem probatum ibat: Et unde constat, quod dies illa 24. fuerit dies Sabbathi, non vero dies Solis, aut etiam Martis, vel Veneris, quos etiam dicatos fuisse revelationibus censet?
