Cui etiam usque adeo absurdum non est, si quis dicat, Codicem τῶν LXX. & illum Hieronymi, duos esse fontes Hebræos; utque insuper pronunciet, totum Scripturarum (authenticarum) corpus diffu- sum & permixtum esse, tum in Ebraicis fontibus, tum in quibuslibet translationum rivulis, (ad quam Cri- tici hypothesin recte eruditissimus Buxtorfius, sub- tilissima hîc requiretur & paucis data ars Chimica sacra, qua quinta hæc essentia artificiosissimo quo- dam alembico destilletur, & extrahatur) ac conten- dat, non haberi hodie talem Codicem, ad quem in dis- crepantiis Interpretum & locis de lectione vera contro- versis possis reverti, neque talem esse Codicem hodier- num Ebraicum, nec esse necesse, ut talis Codex habea- tur, qui sit infallibilis & immobilis norma transla- tionum; quia in quamplurimis adeoque innumeris locis illapsa sit in codicem Ebræum, DEO permittente, ex humana & ἀδιαβλήτῳ infirmitate, ex Scriba- rum incuria & temeritate, multiplex variatio & im- mutatio; Unde magno molimine Capellus colle- git ingentem numerum variarum, quas vocat, le- ctionum per decem distinctas classes, ex variorum V. T. librorum inter se collatione, ex Vet. & N. T. lo- cis parallelis, ex Judæorum Keri & Ketib, variis lectio- nibus Orientalium & Occidentalium, Ben Ascheris item, & Ben Napthali, ex Codice Pentateuchi Sa- maritano, ex variis editionibus textus Ebraici inter se collatis, ex translationibus Græcis LXX. Interpp. Aquilæ, Theodotionis & Symmachi; ex Targumim, seu paraphrasibus Chaldaicis, ex translatione Lati- navulgata, ex fragmentis antiquorum Latinorum, ex Judæorum scriptis Thalmudè, Rabboth, Masora, & Rabbinorum commentariis, ex novis & propriis etiam conjecturis, è quibus omnibus, collatis etiam trans- lationibus Syriacis & Arabicis ac recentiorum In- terpret. si Criticus quis, κρίσει sua adhibita, ve- ram lectionem ostiatim conquirat, & quasi emen- dicet, aut liberaliori, ut ipse vocat, inquisitione eru- at, proditurus tum demum genuinus codex, aut genuino proximus, vel certe multo propior, ipsius judicio, in innumeris locis, quam nunc est Judai- cus, & Masoreticus ille hodiernus, quem ita per con- temtum appellare solet.

§. VIII. Non ovum ovo tam simile est, quam αἰτήματα Grotiana aut κυρίαι δόξαι, quæ passim in Annotationum opere sese produnt, plerisque his- ce Capellianis, ut aut vitula ejus arasse, aut per κακο- ζηλείαν æmulari eundem, aut certe adhibita sua κρί- σει, collatis etiam, quæ ille non adhibuit, aut fortas- sis adhibere non potuit, Syriacis & Arabicis transla- tionibus, spicilegium post messem instituere volu- isse, credendus sit. Quæ vero hypotheses aut refu- tatæ jam alibi sunt à nobis, aut vanitate sua ultro concidunt. Literæ Ebrææ cur peregrinæ statuendæ sint, Assyriorum vel Phœnicum, uti Grotius vult an- notatis ad libr. I. de verit. relig. Christ. §. XV. p. 18. aut cur Samaritanæ habendæ pro Ebraicis anti- quis, etsi magna eo inclinent nomina, causas suffi- cientes non video. Proprias esse Ebræorum in Critico Sacro pag. 325. asserui, nec quod in aliam mentem pertrahere potuerit, observavi hactenus: Communem eam ac receptam apud Hebræos esse sen- tentiam, Buxtorf. dissert. de literis veris Hebraicis docuit. Quanquam illa quidem hypothesis, de mu- tato charactere Ebræo, parum officiat veritati fon- ris Ebræi, dummodo illi non superstruatur autori- tas Pentateuchi Samaritani; gravior est altera de punctis vocalibus & accentibus Ebræis à Masorethis

(fictitiis) Tiberiensibus oriundis: quam vero in Capello jam confutavimus Crit. sacro p. 331. seqq. argumentis historicis & Chronologicis, Rabbinorum item, & Thalmudicis testimoniis, nec non Verbis

Christi Matth. V, 18. è punctorum vocalium natura, revelationis divinæ certitudine, Scripturæ S. perspicui- tate ac perfectione, quæ ab exceptionibus Capelli vindicata & argumenta ej9 contraria profligata ibi- dem sunt. Edidit interea Dn. Buxtorfius tractatum de punctorum vocalium & accentuum Ebraicorum ori- gine & antiquitate, in quo se ostendisse dicit, omnes tam veteres, quam recentes Hebræos pro punctorum an- tiquitate stare & militare, & vel eorum originem ad Mosen & autores sacrorum librorum ipsos, vel saltem ad Esdram eorum inventionem, & ad libros sacros ad- scriptionem referre, uno excepto Elia, recenti Ebræo- rum Grammatico, qui superiori seculo floruit. Quam- vis enim punctorum Vocalium originem alii ad Adamum referant secundum R. Azaria in Meor E- najim, quibus Anton. Rudolphus & Petrus Cavalle- rius, Matth. Flacius & Gvilhelm. Postellus subscri- bunt: alii ad Mosis tempora, quem una cum ipsa lege primum puncta à DEO edoctum esse, auto- ritate Zohar, Cosri, Bechai, Kimchii statuunt: alii ad Esdram, & alios viros Synagogæ M. utpote Ephodeus, Abarbenel &c. omnes tamen puncto- rum antiquitatem propugnant, solus Elias cum aliis nullatenus conferendus, Tiberiensibus Post-Tal- mudicis eadem tribuit: omnes tum qui ante ipsum, tum qui post ipsum floruere omnium nationum Rabbinos ab Elia illo discrepare, Germanos, Gallos, Polonos, Bohemos, Hispanos, Italos, Cretenses, Ara- bes, Palæstinos, Babylonios, Africanos, &c. Buxtorfius Tract. laudato part. II. c. IV. asserit; & conciliari fortassis illæ veterum Judæorum sententiæ pote- runt, si dicatur, punctorum quidem vocalium origi- nem ad Adami tempora referendam esse, quæ autem puncta vocalia legi divinæ conveniant, & juxta quæ illa legi debeat, id Mosi à DEO traditum, & à Mo- se, ac posteris per traditionem vivæ vocis usque ad Esdram conservatum ac propagatum esse viventi- bus & vigentibus adhuc Prophetis, & viris θεοπνεύ- στοις, ut non infida esset παράδοσις; ab Esdra autem, priusquam deficerent Prophetæ, Codici Sacro ea- dem illa divino Spiritu adscripta, atque ita ad no- stra tempora, divina providentia transmissa esse. De quo alii viderint.

§. IX. Multum adhuc periculosior est hypo- thesis de Codicibus Hebræis, non qua puncta solum, sed & literas & consonantes ad versiones varias, Pen- tateuchum Samaritanum, loca parallela & judicium nostrum sine Codicum vel Interpretum autoritate, emendandis, deque novellis, è facili punctorum, vel literarum conmutatione inveniendis lectionibus. Quo pacto corruptionis arguetur Codex Ebræus θεόπνευστος, in infinitis locis. Quæ vero ante Ma- sorethas facta dici non potest, quum in Talmud, in Médraschim antiquis, in Cabbalistis nec vola, nec ve- stigium ejusmodi mutationis deprehendatur, ne- que deinceps fieri potuit, quum Masora, veluti quo- dam sepimento, à corruptione munis præstitus sit textus sacer. Digna est Aben Ezræ de Masoretha- rum stupenda diligentia, observatio, quæ hîc etiam observetur; Quum ad Exod. XXV, 31. de verbo תיעשה agit: Inspexi, inquit, libros, quos explora- runt Sapientes Tiberiados. Et jurejurando affirma- bant, quindecim ex senioribus ipsorum, quod ter atten- te considerabant, singulas dictiones & singula puncta, omne plenum & omne defectivum, & ecce scriptum fuit Jod in voce תעשה etiamsi non ita scriptum in- veni in libris Hispanicis & Gallicis, & transmarinis. Ad quem Aben Ezræ locum Schickardus in Bechi- na pag. 12. exclamat: O incredibilem in minutissimis quoque diligentiam! ó singulare numinis beneficium! ó mirandam tot exemplarium per omnes Europæ, A- fricæ, Asiæque angulos dispersorum, per tot secula ad nos usque propagatorum, ac salutarem harmoniam s Hæc Schickardus uberius illic de Masora agens, & id imprimis observans, Lectionum in Hebraicis Bi- bliis varietates Masora antiquiores esse, & ab ea omnes accurate notari. Porro, quum reperiantur inter Judæos, inter Christianos in Oriente, in Occidente non pauca pervetusta exemplaria ante sex, septem aut plura secula conscripta, quis credet, in nullo istorum quasdam saltem è variis illis lectionibus, quæ ex Versionum discrepantia finguntur, relictas, si secus ipforum Codices Hebræi habuerint; & quomodo Codices hi ita sublati sunt, ut, quum habiti transla- torum ætate fuerint authentici, nullus eorum su- peret amplius? Si vel Antiochi persecutione, vel Pharisæorum & Scribarum ceu hostium versionis τῶν LXX. invidia, quod etiam vult Capellus, in contemtum adducta, ac tandem penitus exoleta Codicum, quibus usi sunt, Ebræorum eisque simi- lium, exemplaria universa, quonam devenerunt er- go illi Codices Ebræi, quibus usi sunt Chaldæi Interpretes, Jonathan, Onkelos, Autor Targum Hie- rosolymit. vel Græci cæteri, Aquila, Symmachus, Theo- dotio, vel Hieronymus, ut nusquam reperiri Ca- pellus dicat illas, quas hîc ex ipsorum versionibus fingit, diversas lectiones? Neque ullatenus est veri- simile, tantam varietatem fortuito subrepere po- tuisse scribis, sine ulla Rabbinorum advertentia, quanta hîc fingitur. Corrumpendi autem studio eam factam, nec ipse Capellus admittit, imo Ju- dæos fortiter se ab hoc crimine liberare profitetur; tametfi mox sui immemor, ex temeritate & auda- cia eos modo diversas voces componere, modo composi- tas dividere, affirmet, quæ vere ἀσύςατα sunt. Non enim adeo imperiti, & ignari fuere scribæ, sed inter Judæos Doctores haud infimum subsellium, uti Buxtorffius notat, obtinuerunt, qui legi descri- bendæ adhibebantur; reque fieri potuit, quin de- prehensi & emendati fuissent errores, ex imperitia aut ἀβλεψίᾳ enati, quum tot fuerint penes Judæos exemplaria legis, non modo singulorum locorum synagogis, sed etiam singulis propemodum ædi- bus, ac inde ab Esdræ ætate continuo versu lecta singulis sabbathis sit lex & explicata publice. Sed Masoretharum initium ac studium ad Esdræ tempo- ra referendum esse, & ad CXX. viros Synagogæ magnæ istius ætatis, Joh. Buxtorfius Senior demon- strat in Tiberiade; cui nec ipse Morinus, minus alioquin æquus de acatholicis, quos vocat, arbiter, & summus veritatis Ebraicæ hostis, laudem suam abrogare potuit, quin fateretur, animadvers. in censor. Exercit. Samarit. p. 397. 367. Buxtorfium primum & solum Christianorum hactenus hanc Criti- cam (Masoretarum) intellexisse: At durarunt usque ad Simeonem justum viri Synagogæ magnæ, ex quo tempore usque ad LXX. Interpp. versionem vix se- culum integrum effluxit; per quod discipulos à Synagogæ M. viris relictos, fida custodia propagas- se codicem Ebræum, nullum esse potest dubium; siquidem nulla insignis calamitas interea Judæis obvenerit, qua correcta exemplaria omnia interiisse præsumi queat, neque tantæ varietates, sine ulla me- moria, irrepere potuerint, ante Antiochi tempo- ra, quo Criticorum studium adhuc viguit, adeoque remedium adversus corruptelas haud defuit. Si- quidem vix 80. anni à tempore versionis LXX. In- terpp. usque ad Antiochi tempora intercesserint. Aut si omnino variationes ejusmodi sese isto tem- pore insinuassent, an credemus, vel à subsequenti- um temporum Criticis, quorum diligentiam & fi- dem maximopere laudat Capellus, easdem non fuiss¿e accuratas, vel si Judæorum hîc invidia, & malevolentia adversus LXX. Interpp. versionem se in ipsos Codices Hebræos exonerasse, uti præter omnem fidem fingitur, annon Christus redarguisset Judæos suo tempore, ac de Canone, uti par erat, commonefecisset? Ad quem vero ipse sine ulla cautela & commonefactione remisit.

§. X. Tum vero an divinam providentiam admissuram fuisse credemus, ut Scripturæ S. textus Originalis, quem normam perpetuam Ecclesiæ esse voluit, tantopere corrumperetur, ac perturbaretur, innumeris scil. diversis lectionibus ita invectis, ut nemini in Ecclesia, etiamsi in unum congregentur omnes totius Orbis Doctores, indubitato dicere denique liceat, quænam in locis infinitis propemodum vera & genuina sit lectio? Quo pacto omnis certitudo Codicis sacri prorsus labefactatur, fidei fundamentum subruitur, & solo æquatur, nec ulla amplius fidei πληροφορία superesse potest, nihilque porro restat, quam ut merus Pyrrhonismus in his, quæ divina constant revelatione, admittatur, adeoque atheismus ipse tandem caput extollat ac triumphet. Qua enim facilitate universalis corruptio in illa loca innumera irrepere potuit, Veteris pariter ac Novi Testamenti, quam commiscitur Criticus, eadem in alia quoque & quidem in ista, quæ fidei axiomata continent, irruere aut irrepere potuisse, mens humana ad Pyrrhonismum perquam propensa ita præsumet, ut distinctione illa inter dogmata fundamentalia & alia fundamentum non concernentia hîc sese expeditura neutiquam sit.

אלו ואלו דברי אלהים חיים tam hæc, quam illa, tam magna quam parva, sunt verba DEI viventis, ajunt Hebræi. Proinde omnium hactenus eadem est ratio, quæ in Scripturis habentur. Πᾶσα γραφὴ θεόπνευστος. 2. Tim. III, 16. Et quo tandem abitura est illa corrigendi licentia, si tanta ei aperiatur porta, ut textum Ebræum fas sit non tantum è versionibus, sed etiam è propriis conjecturis emendare? Si ita faciendum & ita facere licet uni, annon licebit idem pluribus? Si Rubeni, cur non item Simeoni, & cuivis alii? Imo, quidni, inquit Capellus, & huic & illi, & item alteri, imo cuivis liceat, modo id possit & cum judicio faciat? Sed quis patietur, sibi abjudicari judicium? quis, præsertim è Criticis, qui audaculi sæpe esse solent, sefe κρίσεως & judicio suo non efferet? Quæ tum supererit contentionum norma, si ab hoc fastigio dejectus fuerit Ebræus Codex? Et quomodo ille tum fontis, quomodo veritatis Ebraicæ ἀξίωμα, quod illi deferunt omnes, obtinere deinceps poterit, permissa cuivis tanta in eundem licentia, ut jam è Chaldæis versionibus, jam è Græcis, jam è Latina, jam ex aliis, jam è Pentateucho Samaritano, jam è collatione locorum & propriis conjecturis emendetur, novæque lectiones fingantur ac refingantur, sine mensura, sine numero; Ut versiones pro fonte, vel fontis diversis lectionibus obtrudantur, atque procudendus adeo demum sit textus Originalis ex variis versionibus, ratiociniis & conjecturis, ac, donec illud fiat, textu authentico careat prorsus Ecclesia.

§. XI. Mirari itaque oportet Viros clarissimos, Matthæum Cotterium, Guilhelmum Eyre, Arnold. Bootium, Isaac. Vossium, Frideric. etiam Spanhemium, quod huic tam periculosæ Criticæ subscripserint. De Grotio id non mirum, qui Vertumnus in his, quæ ad religionem spectant, semper fere fuit, sub extremam imprimis ætatem. Quod autem Vossius Commentariolo de vera mundi ætate, bene, si quisquam, Ludovicum Capellum de Scripturis divinis præclaro opere illo meritum esse, pronunciat aliosque jubet lumini huic affvesieri, ut discussa ingenii nebula agnoscant, se in luce cæcutiisse, in eo ipsum persuasione vana & cæca de isto suo lumine, vera luce se privasse existimamus. Nam de Judæis, quibus Apostolus concredita τὰ λόγια τοῦ Θεοῦ testatur, au- dacter affirmat, quæcunque illi tradunt, de perpe- tua constanti librorum Sacrorum conservatione, meras esse imposturas. Masoretarum verò labo- rem etsi non omnino improbare possit, graviter reprehendit, quod è versionibus, & cumprimis τῶν ὁ Codicis sphalmata non emendarint; nævos & lacu- nas Ebraico textui plurimas inesse, asseverat; LXX. Interpp. versionem non tantum inter translationes omnium optimam esse; sed Ebrais etiam Codicibus mo- dernis præferri debere, decernit. Quæ quis æquo animo, ac sine detestatione legat? Sed Spanhemius ad δευτέρας φροντίδας perductus est, lectoque Bux- torfiano de punctis tractatu, Criticam illam repro- bavit, quod factum quoque à Boëtio scripta ad Ar- mathanum Epistola de textus Ebræi certitudine contra Lud. Capelli Criticam. Quam etiam viris doctis & gravibus, sed in talibus non exercitatis imposuisse, An- dreas Rivetus indicavit: qui vero eam pessimam & prophanam ipse judicat; quæ si obtineat, actum fere de Scriptura tota V. T. eamque nihil aliud fore, quàm co- thurnum Theramenis, omnibus aptandum pedibus, pronunciat: Johannes Deodatus periculosissimam dicit sectionem primi fundamenti doctrinæ divinæ la- pidis. Alius quidam è meditullio Galliæ Criticam Capellianam Alcorani fulcimentum, impietatis buc- cinam, errorum omnium propagatricem, sapientum omnium judicio habendam, proclamavit. Christian. Schotanus, Franequeranus Theologus, in Tohu, vel Bibliotheca Historiæ Sacræ per duas ætates de pri- ma mundi ætate p. 174. Vossii, per annos minimum 1440. natale mundi tempus vulgarem æram antici- pare contendentis, novum commentum exami- nans, Ludov. Capelli novum dogma Canonicam auto- ritatem disttribuentis in Ebræum & Samaritanicum Co- dicem, & in omnes antiquas Versiones Clar. Buxtor- fium præter alios ita contrivisse, & discussisse cen- set, ut noctuas esse oporteat, qui ad claram lucem cacu- tiant. Atque hæc quidem elogia penes Reforma- tos in fide ὁμοψήφως reportavit Capelli Critica:

Non multo benignius excepta fuit in ipso Papatu, in quo alias parvi fieri Ebræum textum, longeque præferri Vulgatam versionem, aut etiam LXX. In- terpp. translationem, notissimum. Significavit enim quidam magni inter Romano-Catholicos nominis, Ebraistas Parisienses sese Criticæ illi oppo- nere, ideo quod inde sequatur, textum Ebræum multis in locis corruptum & erroneum esse, atque inde nos in religione Christiana nihil certi posse constituere: Qua- les enim rivi, si fontes corrupti? Alius quidam claris- simus Ecclesiæ illius Doctor, maximum allaturam illam Reipubl. Christianæ detrimentum judicavit: A- lius, totum istud Capelli opus malignum atque lethale venenum illo poculo aureo propinare, ac nisi versutiæ il- læ discussæ fuerint, tempus fore, quo periclitari & nu- tare videatur Sacrorum Bibliorum autoritas; Qui cum perfidissimi impostoris Mahometani Alcora- no conferre illud non dubitavit, &, quod memora- tu dignum est, retulit; cum nonnulli editione Gallica Alcorani offensi, de privilegio concesso conquesti fue- rint, à quodam insigni Doctore pariter non absimilem institutam fuisse querelam de Ludovici Capelli Sacra, imo execranda Critica, qua quilibet textus Biblicus, Hebraicus, Græcus, Latinus, Arabicus, Syriacus &c. versatilis, dubius & anceps inducitur & proponitur, qua proinde fidei & pietatis dogmata convelluntur & ad Atheismum lata via sternitur. Si canon ille Cri- ticus valet, scripsit in simili causa Marinus Mersen- nus, nihil amplius certi habemus in libris Hebraicis. Si quibuslibet conjecturis in restituendo Ebræo textu locus sit, valde vereor, ne pro divina Scriptura huma- na tandem nobis obtrudatur, scribit alicubi Simeon de Muys, Parisiensis Regius Professor. Sed hæc & plura alia in eruditissimo Anti-Critico D. Buxtorfii proposita sunt; qui Criticæ perversissimæ ac veræ Diabolicæ ita larvam detraxit, ut neminem am- plius terrere aut turbare ea facile possit. Repeten- da inde nonnulla duximus, ut non illius tantum, sed etiam Grotii, cujus judicio multum ille trium- phat, admiratores intelligant, quo loco & censu haberi debeant istæ artes, quæ in opere Grotiano u- tramque fere faciunt paginam, & habitæ sint, ab il- lis etiam, inter quos vixit ipse, & quorum scenæ se- se accommodavit. Nunquam enim desunt inge- nia, quæ falcem ejusmodi Criticam in Sacram istam messem lubenter immittant, aut aliis immit- tentibus facile, sed minus caute ac prudenter, ap- plaudant. Quo autem ea tantem abeat, exemplo suo ostendit Isaac Vossius, de quo Schotanus libr. 5. Vellem prius manus sinu exeruisset, easque ad DEUM Opt. Max. sustulisset, & lumina, precatus axilium lu- cemque, quam de re tanta pronuntiasset, universæ Ec- clesiæ judicio & communi consensui petulanter insulta- bundus: 1. Quod credimus, Judæis credita esse DEI eloquia, & Canonem sanum, integrumque pervenisse ad nos, id Judæorum fabellis niti profatur. Ipse vero ex Judæorum fabellis adversus fidem Christianam dispu- tat. 2. Sacrorum Codicum tantam fuisse olim dis- crepantiam & confusionem, ut vix aliquid certi ex tanta dictionum varietate elici potuerit, fateri Rab- binos dicit. Ubi autem, & qui dixerunt? Fortasse in mente habuit locum ex Juchasin, quem laudat do- ctissimus Cunæus lib. 1. de Rep. Hebr. cap. 18. Sed autor ille testatur in regno Leon librum ארבעה ועשרים erratum esse, quem exaraverat Rabbi Hillel, atque ex ejus fide emendata esse omnia exemplaria. Non lego ita confusa & corrupta fuisse, ut nihil certi ex illis elici potuerit. 3. Masoretis deberi putat æquabilitatem il- lam, quæ exinde in exemplaribus Hebræi Codicis in- venta est. Id est, arbitratur ipsos ex suo ingenio resti- tuisse, seu potius formasse opus quoddam, quod ab illis, qui Hebræum Codicem sequuntur, varie & inepte ha- beatur pro Mosis authentico. Nempe humanam eva- disse farraginem ex inextricabili confusione, quam bo- ni viri habeant pro canone divino. 4. Masoretas re- prehendit, quod suo judicio confisi in confusione evol- venda non adhibuerint versiones, & præcipue illam LXX. optimam & antiquissimam. Dicendumne est ex eo sequi, ipsos judicio suo fisos tantum opus ag- gressos, quia versiones non adhibuere in consilium? versiones istæ omnes vel interpretatæ sunt Hebræam le- ctionem, vel sui ingenii emendationem. Hebrææ le- ctionis omnem varietatem codices ipsi, quos Maso- retæ collegerant, complexi fuerunt. Hoc sufficit, emen- dationem ex ingenio tuto reliquerint. Nisi putes po- tuisse Hebræi Codicis aliam lectionem secutos esse in- terpretes, quam non invenerunt in suis Codicibus Masoretæ. Id non est verisimile, aut si ita est, fuit ali- quis obscurus, & nullius nominis Codex. Nam Ma- soretæ quicquid per omnes Judæorum Scholas & Syna- gogas Codicum erat probatorum, habere potuerunt, & si tam diligentes fuerunt, ut prædicatur, nec negat Vossius, collegerunt. Si enim non fecissent, Schola illa & Synagoga, quæ suum Codicem, assuetamque lectio- nem vidisset insuper habitum esse, emendatos à Maso- retis Codices non recepisset. Constat etiam publice emendatum & receptum esse in lectione Sacri Codicis, quicquid emendatum & receptum est. Nec emendatio facta est, sed notata tantum varietas lectionum, qua- rum alia per punctationem, id est, קרי, alia per literas, id est, כתיב posita sunt. Hactenus Schotanus.

§. XII. Audire hîc potius debuisset Capellus & Grotius Judæos, è quibus R. Joseph Albo prolixe probat, legem, quæ hodie est in manibus nostris, secundum continuatam cabbalam à Patribus ad filios eandem esse, quæ data fuit Mosi in monte Sinai, sine ulla mutatione; si reperiatur apud alias gentes diversitas, mutationem esse ex parte translatorum, qui non satis in lege exercitati fuerint. Autor libri Cosri ejusque commentator R. Jehuda Muscatus negat mutandum esse, si quid præter vel contra lectionem, proportionem vel collationem videatur, etiamsi unus aut alter Codex faveat; quia si ratiocinatio, electio & judicatio illa dominetur in istis & similibus, mutabuntur libri toti, primo in literis, mox in vocibus, dehinc in sententiis, punctis & accentibus, & sic mutabitur ubique sensus. R. Aben Ezra, absit hoc longe, absit, exclamat: hoc enim non est rectum in verbis autorum prophanorum, quanto minus in verbis DEI vivi. Atque ideo damnant Judæorum Rabbini Carræos, Autor Cosri, Muscatus, Aben Ezra, quod pro suo arbitrio mutent lectionem Legis, (quamvis Andreas Legerus, Genevensis Theologus, & ex literis ejusdem Hottingerus sub calcem Thesauri sui Philologici Carræos agnoscere asserat, ipsa etiam puncta vocalia textus sacri à Mose & Prophetis esse) imo R. Moses Nachmannides in Novellis suis in caput Talmudicum ישניחרין fol. 91. correctionem librorum ex opinione vel conjectura, dicit, absolutam esse transgressionem, & propter eam mereri quem, ut excommunicetur: in Talmud ipso gravissima hac de re extant monita in Sota c. 3. Mi fili, esto cautus in opere tuo, si opus tuum sit opus cæli; (divinum, circa Scripturam occupatum.) Quod si enim forte detrahas aut superaddas vel unicam literam, perinde habeberis, ac si vastares totum mundum. In Talmud Sanhedrim cap. ult. Quicunque etiam de litera unica legis dicit, quod non sit de cælo, est ex iis, de quibus scriptum est, Verbum Domini sprevit. (Num. 15, 31.) Sed in aliis, ubi errant, sequi Judæos non dedignatus est Capellus, hìc autem, ubi sequendi merito erant, in alia omnia potius ire voluit. Nobis ad Grotium nostrum revertendum.

§. XIII. E Commentariis Veterum Hieronymi & Chrysostomi operam imprimis laudat Grotius: sed quod ob linguæ Ebrææ, locorumque, ac historiarum notitiam istum; hunc vero in illis, quæ Judæorum Antiochenorum ope observavit, tantum celebret; neutrius vero operam vel in contextuum scrutinio, vel in scopo proprio ac nucleo Propheticorum scriptorum eruendo sequatur, id probandum minime est. Christum enim, qui est σκοπὸς & σκοπιμώτατος sacrarum litterarum, præ nimio historiarum studio & cæco erga Judæos affectu videre in illis non potuit. Hac mente cum fuerit, nostræ ætatis labores & Comẽntarii, quorum non pauci eruditissimi extant, parum ad palatum ipsi fuerunt. Solum Vatabli & Franc. Junii non spernendos dicit, Jesuitæ tamen Johan. Stephani Menochii & quos ille contractos exhibuit, omnibus præferre videtur, si ea, quæ suo ingenio excogitavit, aut à Judæis hausit, excipias. Quid mirum, quia hic cum suis catholicus, isti vero acatholici sunt Grotio? Qui annotationum suarum opus Jesuitæ Dionysio Petavio, quem insignem Theologum dicit, censendum, locupletandum, corrigendum committere non dubitavit, testibus ad Petavium datis literis, quæ inter Epistolas ad Gallos postremæ leguntur: Rogo, scribit ad eundem, ut, quam primum cum commodo tuo, id est, publico id fieri poterit, habeam, quæ observasti; ac liceat mihi tua ope addere, demere, corrigere, quæ opus erit ad verum pacemque promovendam. Item: Annota, si qua in rebus ipsis mutanda videbuntur: magni hoc beneficii loco accipiam. Item: Si legere vacaveris, rogo, ubi id feceris, me admoneas, quæ omittenda

& mutanda censeas: Quæ in priorem (annotatio- num in V. T.) partem aut tibi aut alteri, cui ea le- genda dederis, in mentem venerint, expectabo. Quo nomine etiam gratias Jesuitæ egit, ac lumen de lu- mine ejus ulterius accendi expetiit: Plurimas co- mitati tuæ gratias debeo, quod eorum, quæ ad V.T. no- tavimus, inspectionem sibi gravem esse noluerit, quod exactiorem lectionem mandaverit iis, quibus plus erat otii, & quod commendatione sua provehere hoc opus voluerit. Nunc cum videam viam aliquam evulgan- di ejus operis, rogo te, ut cumprimum poterit, cum monitis ad me redeat. Ubi descripta erit pars altera, in qua nunc laboratur, audebo iterum laboribus tuis, quanquam & gravissimis & utilissimis intervenire, & uti humanitate tam obvia. Lutetiæ Kal. Novembr. anno cIƆ IƆc XLI. Aliis literis deprædicat opem Jesuitæ feliciter sibi præstitam 16. August. cIƆ IƆc XLII. Lutetiæ datis; quas antea produximus. Quantum ergo Jesuitis in annotata sua permiserit, quanti Papistarum judicia in interpretatione Scri- pturæ fecerit, & quanta προθυμία se ad monita eo- rum, quæ quis ambiget Romano-Catholicæ do- ctrinæ accommodata fuisse, composuerit, ita ob- scurum amplius non est.

§. XIV. Ab antiquis tamen Judæorum Magi- stris se in lege sensum & causam præceptorum, & mo- res eo pertinentes maxime sumpsisse fatetur, quod ve- ro pariter de vaticiniis Propheticis profiteri debuit, in quibus Judæorum Magistros eidem præ Chri- stianis placuisse, res ipsa docet. Sed nec dememinif- se debebat moniti Christi, si cæcus cæcum sequatur, ambos in foveam cadere. Jactat tamen, se plurimum operæ in Prophetiis posuisse; sed ita (neque enim id dissimulat) ut locos, quos Veteres ad Christum & Evangelii tempora retulere, ad historias ævo Prophe- tarum propiores, relictas sub involucro figura Christi & Evangelicorum temporum, retulerit. Ita ergo Ve- terum vestigia deseruit, & in omnia alia ivit. Ad- hæsitfe autem presse Judæis, iisque recentioribus potius, quam antiquis, collatio testatur. Papistam itaque exuisse tum oportuit: neque Papistæ Catho- lici ei fuere amplius, aut Catholicos curavit mul- tum, Rabbinico ebrius spiritu.

§. XV. Regulas in voto p. 139. præscripserat de observanda traditione, & in iis justam esse præsum- ptionem ab Apostolis traditam, quæ ubique in Ecclesia reperiuntur; sed traditionem Veterum Doctorum in explicandis vaticiniis ex oculis removit. Nos eos, inquit, audimus testes, quos semper probavit Ecclesia. Sed quos testes ab Ecclesia probatos glossarum suarum prodet? Commendat necessitatem tradi- tionum in Scripturarum interpretatione, sed glos- sas suas cum traditione Christianorum convenire nunquam docebit. Laudat Regulam Concilii Tri- dentini, de non interpretanda Scriptura contra una- nimem consensum Patrum; sed eandem insuper ha- buit in plerisque Prophetiis.

§. XVI. Dicit, male cohærere verborum rerum- que apud Prophetas seriem, nisi referantur vaticinia ad historias propiores, quæ cæteroqui pulcherrima est. Sed ne dicam, quod opus non sit, ut series cohære- at in vaticiniis, quoad tempora Prophetis vicinio- ra, quum non raro ab illis, Spiritu suggerente, ad meliora Novi Testamenti tempora sese converte- rint, cum ut ad præcipuum, quem sibi fixum ha- bent, scopum deducerent fideles, tum ut à typo ad antitypum, à pœnis & suppliciis ad fontem & apicem omnium consolationum, à sensu rerum imminentium aut præsentium, ad spem & expectationem futurorum animos eveherent, ac nusquam non officii sui pri- marii memores, quod erat ad Messiam, & fidem in ipsum homines perducere, id data opera per- agerent: Sapientior certe non debebat Grotius sibi videri omnibus Christianis, veteribus & recentioribus, qui collaetionem utiq; monstrarunt, etsi vaticinia de Christo & temporibus N. Testamenti explicarint. Quid? num Apostolis ipsis, num ipsomet Christo, aeterna Patris sapientia, sapientior fuit? At docent

Apostoli, Spiritum Christi, qui in Prophetis fuit, προμαρτυρόμενον praetestificatum esse Christi passiones, & post easdem gloriam, 1. Pet. 1, 11. Docent, OMNES Prophetas testimonium perhibere Christo, quod remissionem peccatorum accipiant per nomen ejus omnes, qui credunt in ipsum, Act. X, 43. Protestantur, se nihil docere extra ea, quae Moses & Prophetae futura dixerunt, Act. 26, 22. Grotii autem si admittendae glossae, nullum facile habebimus Prophetam de passionibus & gloria Christi testificantem, qui clarissima etiam illa testimonia Ps. 16. & Es. 53. de Christo interpretari noluit, prius ad Davidem, posteri9 ad Ieremiam detorquens. Quae ab ipsis met Judaeis antiquioribus de Messia explicantur. Prius a R. Mose Hadarsch. in Ps. 49, 11. Hic versus dictus est de Rege Messia, qui morietur, ut redimat Patres, & postea vivat in aeternum. Posteri9 in ipso Thargum Jonath. in libro Sanhedrim c. Heleck. in l. Siphre in Midrasch Ruth, c. 2, 14. a R. Mose Hadarschā in Gen. 1, 3. c. 24, 67. & Ps. 49. ideo R. Aben Ezra in Es. 52, 13. seq. ut & R. Abarbaneel sic Veteres Ebraeorum Magistros, ut & R. Mosen Nachmannidem, magni inter recentiores nominis, exponere docent: ex cujus unius vaticinii lectione etiam se ad fidem Christianam conversum fuisse testatur J. Isaacus adv. Lind. Tantum vero abest, ut Grotius OMNIBUS Prophetis hoc relinquat, quod de remissione peccatorum per fidem in nomine Christi testati sint, ut vix ulli Prophetarum hoc assignaturus sit, qui remissionem peccatorum potius primum a Christo annuntiatam esse, Socino asserenti credit: neque de fide in nomine Christi & remissione peccatorum per fidem; illam consequenda quicquam in annotatis suis in Prophetas tradidit. Nihil autem docuisse Apostolos extra ea, quae Moses & Prophetae in scriptis suis docent, in quibus audiendi proponuntur a Christo Luc. 16, 29. quomodo credere potuit, qui non modo multa alia Apostolos oretenus docuisse, quae plane non sint scripta, cum Papistis persuasus fuit, sed nihil pene eorum, quae Apostoli docuere de Christo, in Mose & Prophetis per annotata sua relinquit!

§. XVII. Christus vero, quem solū audiendum esse, coelestis vox proclamavit, scrutari ita jussit Scripturas Veteres, ut vitā aeternam, quae in iisdem habetur & testimonium, quod de Christo perhibent, ad consequendam per fidem in ipsum vitam, ἐρευνήσεις illa indagemus, Joh. 5. 39. non ut testimonia de vita aeterna, & de Christo vitae aeternae autore, aut fide in Christū praetermittamus, vel ad alia quaevis detorqueamus. Non credidit certe Grotius, in Scriptura V. T. de vita aeterna testimonia haberi, quia Socini τῷ σκοτεινῷ opinionibus fascinatus fuit: De Christo autem, ut in eodem per fidem vitam aeternam habeam9, nec volā nec vestigiū reperire licet in annotatis Grotianis. Explicavit & Christus Scripturas V. T. sed ita, ut demonstraret e Mose, Psalmis & Prophetis passionem & resurrectionē suam. Haec sunt, inquit, verba, quae locutus sum ad vos, cum adhuc essem vobiscum, quoniam necesse est impleri omnia, quae scripta sunt in lege Mosis & Prophetis & Psalmis de me. Tunc aperuit, addit S. Lucas, illis sensum, ut INTELLIGERENT Scripturas, & dixit, quoniam sic scriptum est, & sic oportebat Christum pati, & resurgere a mortuis tertia die, & praedicari in nomine ejus poenitentiam & remissionem peccatorum in omnes gentes, incipientibus ab Hierosolyma. c. 24, 44. seqq. Si vero Grotii glossae obtineant, ne in Psalmis quidem & Prophetis, nedum in Mose quicquam de passione & resurrectione a mortuis Christi, ac praeconio in nomine ejus, & initio ejusdem Hierosolymis fa- ciendo exhibebitur, quia sc. series verborum & re- rum ad tempora propiora spectat.

§. XVIII. Totum ergo V. Testamentum Judæis uni- ce relinquendum, nihil de eodem ad nos spectabit, si paucula vaticinia, tria forte vel quatuor, de tempore adventus Messiæ excipiantur. Quid itaq; fiet dispu- tationibus Christi & Apostolorum, aut locis ab iisdem adductis e V. T. quæ ipsi de Messia interpretantur? In spongiam incumbent, neque illis convinci Judæi poterunt, aut quondam potuere, si Grotium audias, utpote quæ de rebus longe aliis agant. Ne jam An- gelus, Matt. 1, 23. impletum dicat, quod a Domino per Esaiam dictum est, Ecce virgo in utero habebit: Non de Christo virginis filio, sed de filio Esaiæ id dictum fuit. Ne dicat, adimpletum esse, quod per Prophetam Esaiam de terra Zabulon & Naphthalim & Galilæa gentium di- ctum est, cum Christus in fines illos pervenit, ibique prædicare cœpit. Non illa, sed Ezechiæ tempora respe- xit propheta, & liberationem a Sennacheribo: Non Christus, sed Ezechias est puer ille natus, consiliarius, (Grotius pervertit consultor) Deus fortis, (per Grotii σφεέλστη[α legendū Consultor Dei fortis) Pater æterng.

§. XIX. Ne testetur Matthæus c. 8, 17. Esaiam de Christo loquutum esse, cum nostros ipsum pertasse dolores cecinit c. 53, 4. aut Petrus, Christum esse, cujus livore sanati sumus, in cujus ore dolus non inventus est, 1. Ep. 2, 22. 24. aut Marcus, Jesum illum esse, quem præ- dixit inter sceleratos reputatum iri c. 15, 28. neque de Christo hæc explicet Philippus Act. 8, 32. quia de Je- remia vaticinatus ibi est Esaias. Neq; est, quod tam prolixe a Christo impletum dicat Matthæus c. 12, 18. Esaiæ vaticinium, de servo non contendente, judicium Dei gentibus manifestaturo, in cujus nomine sperabunt gentes, c. 42, 1. De seipso enim vaticinatus est Prophe- ta: aut quod Zachariæ Prophetiam c. 9, 9. de ingressu Christi super asinam adducat, cum Matthæo c. 21, 5. Johannes c. 12, 15. de Zorobabele enim hæc accipienda sunt; aut quod uterq;, Matthæus c. 27, 35. & Johannes c. 19, 21. cum dividerentur vestimenta Christi, Davidis prophetiam Ps. 22, 19. impletam esse doceat, hoc enim de Davide ipso intelligendum est μεταφορικῶς, quod fortunas suas confiscatas inter se partiti sint, uti Latini spolium dicunt de re quavis, quum proprie spolia sint vestes. Aut quod S Johannes c. 19, 37. transfixionem Christi prædictam affirmet a Zacharia c. 12, 10. Noster sensus, inquit Grotius, optimus est, configere Deum di- cuntur, qui eum probris lacessunt.

§. XX. Neq; Petrus Act. 2. c. demonstrare potuit, vel effusionem Spiritus S. super Apostolos factam a Joele c. 2, 28. prædictam; vel resurrectionem Christi e Davidis vaticinio, Ps. 16, 8. quod sanctus Dei cor- ruptionem videre non debeat; vel testari, Act. 3. cap. quod Moses prædixerit, Messiam ceu magnum Pro- phetam e fratribus Judæorum excitatum iri, Deut. 18, 5. Joel enim de Esaia & aliis Prophetis loquitur. David de seipso agit, Moses de Propheta quocunq;, ex- citando, ubi magna necessitas aut evidens utilitas id ex- egerit. Neq; urgere potuit apodixin suam cum Petro Act. 2, 29. Apostolus gentium, c. 13, 36. quod David viderit omnino corruptionem, adeoque de Messia, non de seipso locutus sit. Sensus enim hic solum est non fore potestatem Sauli interficiendi Davidem. Non provocare poterunt Paulus & Barnabas, c. 13, 47. Dominum sibi mandasse, ut convertantur ad gentes, cum per Esaiam prædixit c. 49, 6. Christum fore lumen gentium. Testatus enim de semetipso Esaias est, se quoque plurimos gentium conversurum. Neque confirmare Apostoli in Concilio Hieroso- lymitano Actor. 15, 16. vocationem gentium ex Amoso cap. 9, 11. Tabernaculum enim David, quo de agit, in Zerubabele jam suscitatum fuit.

Neq; est, quod provocent Marcus c. 1, 3. aut Lucas c. 3, 4. ad Esaiam c. 40. quod de Johanne cecinerit in de- serto prædicaturo. Monuit saltem Propheta, ut illi, qui exilii tempore victuri essent Prophetæ clamarent, utq́; in deserto viam pararent Domino.

§. XXI. Sed & Christo ipsi tacendum erit, ne Matt. 21, 47. dicat, se esse lapidem, quem Architectos, Pharisæ- os & Sacerdotes reprobaturos prædixerit David Ps. 118, 22. quum de seipso reprobato a Saulo & aula ejus loquu- tus sit; aut (Luc. 21, 37.) se esse illum, qui, Esaiæ c. 53, 12. vaticinante, inter sceleratos reputandg fuerit, quia de Jeremia accipi debent verba Prophetæ; aut (Matth. 26, 21.) Marc. 14, 27. Pastorem, quem Zacharias (c. 13, 7.) prædixit percutiendum, hic enim Judas est Maccabæg, qui in prælio cum Bachide interiit. Ne exclamet (Luc. 4, 18.) lecto vaticinio Esaiæ (c. 4, 1.) Spiritus Domini est super me, hodie impleta est hæc Scriptura in auribus ve- stris. De se enim ipso loquutg est Esaias. Et quid tandē supererit in Scripturis Propheticis, quod de Christo & temporibus Vet. Test. agat, si ea, quæ luculentissi- me Christus & Evangelistæ, quæque Apostoli Christi explicarunt, ejusmodi comentis in sensum plane a- lium detorqueantur? Judicet æquus lector; huic e- nim judicium permittit Grotius: annon hoc sit præ- ferre glossas infidelium Judæorum Christi & Aposto- lorum sententiæ, h. e. tenebras luci, Belialem Christo?

§. XXII. Nimis ergo sibi blanditus fuit Grotius συνεχείας abs se excogitatæ pulchritudine, ut eam glossis suis fundamenti instar supposuerit, quum fa- cile sit, ubi de subjecto & materia, quanı vocant, substrata, ex ore Christi & Apostolorum, imo ex emphasi etiam oraculorum Spiritus Sancti certi su- mus, συνέχειαν textus monstrare. Neq; vero sufficit ad explicationẽ Christi & Apostolorum sustinendā, quod statuat Grotius, vaticinia illa involutam habere figuram Christi & Evangelicorum temporum, Deumq́; non per verba tantum, sed & per res nobis Messiā & be- neficia ejus exhibere. Quia e figuris solis demonstratio invicta peti non potest; peribit ergo vis probatio- num Christi & Apostolorum: neq; ut typi adducun- tur ista, ut cum Agnus paschalis, & alia ceu typi si- stuntur, sed ut vaticinia, quæ de Christo agant, inq́; eo impleta sint: non in rebus tantum ipsis figuram inesse Christus docet, uti cum figuram in sona involutam i- pse evolvit, aut Apostoli, siquidem verborū & vati- ciniorum sensum propriū urgeant: qui si alios con- cernat, non Christum, ceu falsa reprobari poterit eo- rū interpretatio. Triumphabunt ergo hostes Chri- stiani nominis, Julianus, Porphyrius, Lipomannus, & similes? Si dicat, mystico sensu illa ad Christum appli- cata esse, literali de alio loqui, ridebunt Judæi, aliique Christianorum hostes, mysticum sensum, typicamq; accomodationem loco probationis solide, ac demon- strationis semper adhiberi, nuspiā Prophetarum pro- prium urgeri sensum, nuspiam Prophetas de Christo vaticinatos esse, aut de beneficiis ejus, semper tantū typis & figuris rem involutam esse, & vitā adumbratam Sanctorum, quæ tamen adumeratio neq; tum consti- terit populo, aut e verbis factisve haberi potuerit, neq; hodie constare possit. Quam forte nec Prophe- tis ipsis, qui vaticinia illa protulere, tum cognitam, cum Judæis, quorum placita libenter sequitur, asse- ret Grotius. Cui ergo usui fuerat illa adumbra tio? Tum vero certum est, unius dicti unum tantum esse sensum, eumq; literalem ac genuinum: plures sen sus eodem dicto inferri, si cum Papistis sensit Grotiu reclamat natura vocum, quæ semel positæ in eadem sententia unam eandemq; certam significationem obtineant, necessum est, quia significatio est form vocis, unam autem unius rei formam esse, indubium est: Reclamat intentio divina, quæ fuit certi quid in dicare oraculis suis, non vero ambiguam orationem aut sententiam proponere, quam possis aliter atq; aliter pro re nata intelligere, imo debeas diversimoda ratione interpretari, semel de aliis, qui olim vixere, iterum vero de Messia; Reclamat ἑρμηνείας genuina ratio: vi cujus e contextu non nisi unica sententia menti loquentis consona eruenda est; Nisi forte Cardinalis Bellarmini ineptiæ l. III. de verb. Dei cap. 3. placuerint Grotio, ut Scripturæ, quia Deum habent autorem, id proprium esse crediderit, ut plures contineat sensus, literalem & mysticum, aut Capelli sui Papizans hypothesis in Critic. Non video, cur negari debeat, Dei spiritum variis in locis non ubiq́;) non unum tantum, sed duplicem, aut vere triplicem etiam literalem sensum intendisse; hoc enim pertinet ad πολυποίκιλον ejus sapientiam declarandam: aut Rabbinorum commentum: Nusquam Scriptura est absq́; sensu simplici, sed habet pariter uti mysticum, ita simplicem, his duobus non est, ut careat. Scil. juxta illud Salomonis Prov. 25, 11. poma aurea in cancellaturis argenteis verbum dictum secundum ambas facies ejus. Quæ perspicuitati & fini Scripturæ S. qui est certos nos reddere de mente divina, penitus repugnant. Ubi enim æquivocatio, vel ἀμφιβολία, ibi in diversos sensus abripimur, nullamq; βεβαιότητα de sententia certe loquentis habere possumus. Et annon ita Christi & Apostolorum probationes plane inefficaces reddentur, si ex solo figurato sensu institutæ, nunquam e literali propriaǵ; oraculorum sententia depromtæ sint? Nota est Irenæi sententia l. II. c. 46. Quia Parabolæ possunt multas recipere absolutiones, ex ipsis de inquisitione DEI affirmare derelinquentes quod certum & indubitatum & verum est, valde præcipitantium se in periculum & irrationabilium esse, quis non amantium veritatem confitebitur? Nota Hieronymi observatio Matth. 13. Nunquam parabola & dubia ænigmatum intelligentia potest ad autoritatem dogmatum proficere. Notum judicium S. Augustini Ep. XLVIII. ad Vincent. Donatist. Quis non impudentissime nitatur aliquid in allegoria positum pro se interpretari, nisi habeat alibi manifestissima testimonia, quibus obscura illustrantur. Quos si audire noluisset, debebat solum non dememinisse regulæ Thomæ part. 1. q. 1. art. 10. solus sensus literalis est argumentativus, quæ axiomatis instar obtinet inter Pontificios, ut Bellarminus ipse hoc ceu indubium supponat. CONSTAT, inquit l. III. de V. D. c. 3. inter nos & adversarios, ex solo sensu literali peti debere argumenta efficacia. Nisi ergo argumenta Christi & Apostolorum inefficacia dicenda, fateri oportet, sensum illum literalem & proprium fuisse, quem ursisse & adhibuisse leguntur cum in dictorum factorumq; confirmationibus, tum in disputationibus cum adversariis. Quod tota hactenus credidit Ecclesia, solus Grotius, etsi traditionem interpretem Scripturæ faciat, Judæorum hîc pascitur commentis. Cuj9 studiu præcipuu id fuisse videtur, ut Rabbinorum, sive quod in scriptis eorum se versatum oftentarit, seu quod potius fascinatus glossis eorum fuerit, interpretamenta Christianis venditaret, & traditiones ipsas Rabbinicas, nonnunquam etiam nugas Talmudicas potius, quam Scripturam sui ipsius interpretem ἀνυπεύθυνον, in consilium adhiberet. Ut saniores hic e Judæis ipsis illi videantur, quos קראים cæteri per contemtum vocant, textuales scripturarios, quod missis traditionibus, & Thalmude, solam Scripturam pro fidei fundamento admittant, legisque expositionem ex ipsis legis verbis depromendam censeant. Sed Scripturarius esse noluit Grotius: Quod nobis instar criminis impingunt Papistæ. Et parum abfuisse videtur a Rabbinorum sententia, qui articulum de Messia dicunt credi tantum per traditionem, NULLUMQUE esse vaticinium, neque in lege, neque in Prophetis, quod necessario ejus adventum prædicat, adeo, ut ex locorum circumstantiis aliter sumi non possit; quam mente plurimorum Interpretum (Judæorum) esse, R. Joseph Ben Albo testat9 est, qui eo tandem ab- iit, ut Orat. IV. c. 42. in lib. Ikkarim assereret, fides, qua creditur Messiæ adventus, non est fundamentum ta- le, ut lex in universum concidat, si quis fidem istam non habuerit. Vid. Abrah. Hülfig in Theol. Judaic. part. I. qu. II. Improbat enim R. ille sententiam Maimonidis, quod fides de futuro Messia fundamentum conternat, quia sc. ita numerandus esset inter Apostatas, & defici- entes a Religione, quibus non est pars in futuro seculo, R. Hillel. Quem vero ita excusat Orat. I. c. I. non credidit R. Hillel, futurum Messiam, sed tamen ideo inter Aposta- tas recensendus non est, uti scripsit Maimonides, utpote quæ sine eo consistit. In eo certe R. Josepho Albo nihil cedit Noster, imo palmam præripit, quod cum ille circa vaticinia aliquot de Messia nobilissima varias dubitandi rationes proposuerit, annon jam modo partim sub templo primo, partim sub secundo in hoc vel illo impleta esse dici possint, ac R. Hillelis sententiam admittat, quòd vaticinia Esaiæ Regem Ezechiam respe- xerint, Grotis pene omnia non σκεπτικῶς, sed κατη- γορικῶς de alio, quãMessia interpretetur, & vaticinia Esaiæ ad Regem Ezechiam perversissima ratione de- torqueat; mirum, quod nõHilleli etiam id concesse- rit, quod Israelitæ temporibus Ezechiæ Messia suo potiti sint, quum in Esaia Prophetarum omnium luculen- tissimo deMessia vate & præcone loco Messiæ subin- de Ezechiam substituatur, & quoad sensum literalem Messiam in toto Esaiæ libro non inveniat, aut re- linquat. Judæos certe ex Esaia & plerisq; aliis prophe- tis convincere de Messia non potuit Grotius, quum omnia pene vaticinia in sensum plane alienum de- torserit, nulla cum Christianis dextre interpretetur.

§. XXII. At Judæis convincendis vel pauca Christum & tempus, quo is venturus erat, directe describentia, suffici- unt. Pauca omnino relinquit Grotius; Vix tria vel quatuor. E Genesi unum, Jacobi vaticinium, e Daniele unum, de LXX. hebdomadibus, unum ex Haggæo de altero templo, ut & e Malachia de prodromo Christi: Quid vero aliis fiet Prophetis? Num illi muti deChri- sto fuere? Num David de Messia Dei Jacob confirmatus de Christo nihil, nihil Esaias, ob illustria vaticinia Ev- angelista veris, quam Propheta habitus, nihil Hoseas, Zacharias, cæteriq; Prophetæ? Qui ergo OMNES te- stimonium perhibuere de Christo, quod Petrus ait Act. 10, 43. Qui Moses & OMNES PROPHETÆ a Sa- muele, & deinceps, qui loquuti sunt, indicaverunt dies istos, quod idem Petr9 coram Judæis, nihil illis recla- mantibus, quia indubitatum erat penes omnes, affir- mavit, Act. 3, 23? Nec vero solum Judæi convincendi de tempore adventus Messiæ, sed de miraculis, benefi- ciis, partib9 officii; & aliis notis & characterib9 ejusdẽ.

§. XXIII. Si in his applicandis fallat aut inefficax fit Novi Testamãnti scriptura, Judæi in erroribus confirmabuntur, aut advenisse quidem Messiam con- vincentur, Jesum tamẽ Nazarenum promissum illum Messiam esse, minime convinci poterunt, imo si o- mnia illa vaticinia de alio, quam Messia secundum literã agere credantur, falsitatis convincerent Chri- stum & Apostolos, quod ea in alium sensum abripue- rint, nullumq; dictum pro se adferre potuerit Chri- stus, nullum proChristo Apostoli. Nec vero uspiam illa de tempore Gen. 49. Dan. 9. Hag. 2. adducta sunt in N. Testamento. Malachiæ vaticinia c. 3. & 4. adducta quidem, sed pariter, uti Esaiæ Prophetia adducitur, ut e Marco c. 1, 2. 3. liquet. Quum ergo hæc sensu lite- rali non agat de Messia, ejusq; prodromo secundum Grotium, illa etiam ita accipi poterit, ceu nõ addu- cta, quoad sensum propriũ. Et annon parili facilitate in istis residuis Grotio vaticiniis Judæi poterunt fin- gere alium sensum literale, ac verba imprimis Mala- chiae vel Haggæi de alio quopiam interpretari? quem- admodum vaticinium e Mose Jacobæum eludendi non exiguam prębuit ansam, cum vocem שילח imprimis respexisse piscinam Siloah contendit. Quā- vis & illa e Prophetis Judaicis commentis pervertat Grotius: dum in Danielis loco Christum ducem indi- gitari vult, qui populum ab impendentib9 malis libera- re debuerit, si ei paritum fuisset, & in malachia domina- torem ita explicat: Ille promissus Siloh, qui vobis maxi- ma bona etiam in statu publico allaturus est, si ei parea- tis. Quæ uti somniis Judæorum de terreno Messiæ re- gno aperte favent, ita manifestum oppido est, Judai- zantem Grotium fundamentum Christianismi maxi- me labefactare, ac si terrenum regnum & bona terre- na promissa fuerint per Messiam Judæis, ac promissa de Messia hypothetica solum, ac conditionata fuerint. Habent ergo Judæi, suæ quod prætexant ἀπιστίᾳ, et- iam de tempore adventus Messiæ; quod promissus Dominator politicus nondum advenerit, quodque promissiones illæ solum conditionatæ fuerint, quæ conditio quum impleta non sit a Judæis, non mi- rum esse, quod dominator Siloh promissus non ad- venerit, vel plane adventurus non sit, uti hodie de- sperati ex ipsis dicunt. Argumentum certe eorum ἀδιάλυτον. Messias promissus est Dominator politicus, statum publicum Judæorum restauraturus, sub conditio- ne, si illi parituri sint. Quæ Grotiana est propositio. Jesus Nazarenus non est Dominator politicus, qui pro- testatur sive parituri ipsi Judæi, sive non, regnum suum non esse de hoc mundo. E. Jesus Nazarenus non est Mes- sias promissus. Euge, triumphate Judæi, magnum hy- peraspisten nacti estis!

§. XXIV. Sed quid mirum, Grotium per hypotheses ita labefactare fundamentum Christianismi, quū di- recte Scripturas Canonicas, quæ fundamentum sunt fi- dei nostræ, evertat. Si enim, ut postremo loco de li- bris, quos explicandos sumsit, hîc in limine id obser- vem9, quæratur, quidnā de autoritate eorundē habeat Groti9, non credit utiq;, omnes illos a Sp. S. profectos, quos universa tales credidit Ecclesia. Evangeliū sane Lucæ, in voto p. 136. scriptum fuisse divino afflatu dictan- te, inficiatur, hoc argumento, quod testium mentio- nem fecerit, quod prorsus futile est: quia nisi afflatu Spiritus gubernatus fuisset, in testium delectu eo- rumq; testimoniis facile errare potuisset, ideoq; o- mnino opus eodem habuit. Quē vero occultis stimu- lis Sp. S. coactum & excitatum ad scribendum, Epiphani9 hæresi LI. Spiritusq; cœlesti afflatum scripsisse Titus Bo- strensis affirmat; cuj9 etiam libros tota Ecclesia indu- bitato pro canonicis semper habuit. Neq; unum Lu- cam in dubium revocat Grotius, negat, omnes libros, qui sunt in Hebræo canone, dictatos a Sp. S. vel op9 fuisse, historias ab eo dictari. Distinguit inter afflatum divi- num & pium motum. At pio motu scribunt multi, qui in scribendo non sunt ἀνυπεύθυνοι, & infallibiles. O- portet ergo canone V. T. excidere magnā librorum sacrorum partem. Ita historici libri in Scrip. S. imo & historiæ, quæ aliis scriptis, utpote Esaiæ & Prophetis reliquis insertæ quandoq; sunt, pio quidem motui tri- buentur, non autem divino afflatui, neq; in Canone locum habebunt. Unde non mirum, Criticā manum ita illis adhibere Grotium, virgstulamq; censoriam, ac si in humanis versetur scriptis. Ut haud omnino alie- n9 fuisse videatur a Capelli sui sententia, nō esse impos- sibile, imo forte revera esse nonnulla hujusmodi in Scri- pturis σφάλματα leviora, quæ vel ipsis sacris Sscriptori- bus (quatenus homines infirmi fuere) tribuenda: quæ vero non satis congruunt alteri ejusdē Critici effato: Non res duntaxat, sed & verba & phrases arcano Spir. Dei motu atq; afflatu fuerunt Prophetis & sacris scri- ptoribus veluti dictata, seu inspirata. Insaniam, si aliter sentiam. Neq; vero monitus de errore gravissimo Grotius, vel rationib9, vel ipsorum etiam Ebręorum

R. Mosis Ægyptii, qui omnes hagiographos libros agno- scit per Sp. S. scriptos, aut Jachiadis, qui Esdram librum suum & Chronicorum per Sp. S. scripsisse, fassus est, autoritate, quam alias magni facere solet, moveri potuit, quin adhuc in Discussione, scripto novissimo, Historicorum S. Codicis in dubium revocaret auto- ritatẽ Canonicam. Addidit imo etiã morales sententias Ebræorum (de Canone Ebræorum disputatio est) ut- pote quæ tales non sint, de quibus dubitare nefas sit. qui- bus conferenda ea, quæ de Proverbiorum libro habet sub initium ejus; videtur hic esse ἐκλογὴ optimarum sententiarum ex plurimis, qui ante Salomonem fuere, scriptoribus, quales ἐκλογὰς multi Imperatorum Con- stantinopolitanorum conscribi in usus suos fecere. Qua- lia judicia aut non multum absimilia de aliorum li- brorum plerorumq; consignatione in Codice sacro etiam tulisse legitur. atq; huc etiam facit, quod in Ex- plicat. Decal. p. 26. Mosen verba in Exodo descripta in Devteronomio MEMORITER referre scripserit; ac si humano studio, non vero afflatu Sp. S. & inspiratio- ne divina ea, quæ in Devteronomio habentur, propo- sita sint, ac perscripta. Vix ergo media pars super- erit in Canone, divino scripta afflatu, quam vero tã infida manu tractat, addendo, detrahendo, corrigendo, pervertendo, ut nihil ferme divini in eadem reliquũ esse, indubitato credidisse, censendus sit. Nec vero puncta solum vocalia in dubiũ revocat, literas, vo- ces ipsas immutat, aut suspectas reddit, adeoq; scri- pturis sacris certitudinis parum relinquit; Quas de- niq; non multum æstimasse hominem oportuit, quũ Scripturam ad Dei voluntatem agnoscendam neceffaria haud fuisse, neq; Apostolos mandato Christi scripsisse, multas etiam fuisse barbaras gentes, quæ in Christum crediderint, sine CHARTA, & ATRAMENTO, & quæ alia ejusmodi Papistica ejus sunt emblemata, in no- viss. scripto discuss. p. 147. professus sit Ne dicam, quod cum de N. Testamenti Canone disputat, quæstionem de nudis historiis, neq; magni momenti esse, dicat, vera sint, quæ narrantur talia, annon sint vera: unde colli- git Rivetus (dialys. p. 493.) perinde ipsi esse, an historiæ, quæ in N. T. libris recensentur, vera sint vel falsæ, quo pacto Evangeliorum sacrorum authentia plane e- vertitur.

MANTISSA.

Papistis procul dubio gratificatur etiam in eo Grotius, cum multas Pauli Epistolas periisse affirmat in Appendic. de Anti-Christ. Quanquam enim di- stinguendũ sit inter scripta sacra a viris θεοπνεύσοις profecta, & scripta Canonica, perpetuo Ecclesiæ Cano- ni divinitus consecrata, nec, si scripta quædam sacra Apostolorũ perierint, de Canonicis Scripturis quas- dam desiderari illico consequatur, imo agnoscant quoq; e Papistis Salmero proleg. IX. can. 4 Stapletonus de princ. doctr. fidei Contr. V. l. IX. c. 5. libros Cano- nicos nullos periisse, ne Ecclesiæ negligentia arguetur in deposito sibi concredito: Solent tamen Pontificii pleri- que tum ut Canoni Scripturæ perfectionem dero- gent; quæ vero non e numero librorum, sed e volun- tate divina, & sufficientia informationis, ac dogmatum æstimanda, tũ in vilipendium S. literarum contende-

## 1:1 Introduction: D. Abrah Prolegomena Chum
D. ABRAH PROLEGOMENA CHUM

Philo, Josephus, Patricides, R. Gedalia, Aben Ezra, Clemens Alex. (Strom. I), Procopius, Rabanus, Lyranus, Tirinus, Hottinger (in Exerc. Anti Mor. p. 48 & Smegmat. p. 398) hold the name of Moses to be Egyptian. But that it is Hebrew is not obscurely hinted at in Ex. 2:10, when the daughter of King Pharaoh is said to have called him משׁה, because, she says, I drew him out of the waters (משׁיתהו): for משׁה is from the matter, not a few things from the writings inspired by God (θεοπνεύςοις), and indeed some things from the Canonical books also have perished, the cause of which Grotius pleads as much as he can. As for 1 Cor. 5:9, it cannot be gathered from that without doubt that a certain Epistle to the Corinthians has perished, as Estius and some others wish. Indeed, they incline toward that with Ambrosiaster, and from the Reformed, Calvin, Beza, Pareus, Marloratus, Drusius, and from our own, Mylius, Aeg. Hunnius, Luc. Osiander, Sal. Gesnerus, Dav. Rungius, but in such a way that they deny that it was destined for the perpetual Canon of the Church, and thus that it was Canonical: concerning which we have treated in the Crit. sacro p. 237. Yet most of the ancients, Jerome, Theodoret, Chrysostom, Theophylact, with the support of Erasmus in his Paraphrase, Sixtus Senensis, Cornelius a Lapide, and Tirinus, judge that the very Epistle which was then being written by the Apostle to the Corinthians is indicated there, whose 11th verse in this 5th chapter B. Balduinus does not deny is being looked back upon here: nor does Beza deny that the words of the Apostle can be accepted in that way. But what Grotius contends, that a certain Epistle of Paul written to the Thessalonians has also perished, that is purely precarious, and up to this point has not been heard of even among the Papists: nor can it be elicited with any appearance of truth from 2 Thess. 2:15, since that Epistle to the Thessalonians which the whole Christian Church acknowledges as the first is openly designated there. That the second Epistle to the Thessalonians was written not long after the beginning of the reign of Gaius, and that some things were predicted in it concerning Gaius, and that it was prior in the order of time to the latter, and indeed that an Epistle was written to them before Paul had come to Thessalonica and before a Christian Church had yet been established there, as Grotius affirms, are demands that are entirely frivolous, thought up for the sake of Grotius's fictitious Anti-Christ: since from 2 Thess. 2:2, it is manifest that the Epistle which is held and called the second is entirely later than that which is now named the first in the sacred Canon, and that it was written after the death of Gaius to the Church gathered there from Gentilism, and it has been undoubted up to this point among the whole Church that the former Epistle, which is so called, is truly the first to the Thessalonians, and there does not remain in antiquity either a trace or a vestige that three were written to the same people, or that the first perished, and that the later one, which is now held, should be considered the second, and that which is called the first should be considered the third: The words of 2 Thess. 3:17, ἐν πάσῃ ἐπιϛολῇ (in every epistle), do not look back to certain lost epistles, but to the surviving Epistles of Paul. Finally, what Grotius maintains in the Proœm. Epist. ad Ephes. That the Epistle to the Laodiceans has perished seems to be done for the sake of the Vulgate version: for which reason he did not even hesitate to invent, without the authority of any Greek manuscript, that Col. 4:16 should be read τὴν λαοδικείας of the Laodiceans (Epistle), which, namely, might refer to them, in his notes on this passage, when all copies of the original text consistently read τὴν ἐκ λαοδικείας, just as the Syriac Interpreter also has, and likewise from the Greeks Chrysostom and Theodoret; whence Gagnejus, Cornelius a Lapide, and Johannes a Gorcum admit that an Epistle sent from Laodicea is to be understood, and not some Pauline Epistle to the Laodiceans which has perished, a fact which Bellarmine was also forced to acknowledge in the revision of his works.

Latin:

D. ABRAH PROLEGOMENA CHUM

NOmen Mosis pro Ægyptio quidem haben Philo, Josephus, Patricides, R. Gedalia, Aben Ezra, Clemens Alex. Strom. I. Procopius, Ra banus, Lyranus, Tirinus, Hottinger. in Exerc. Anti Mor. p. 48. & Smegmat. p. 398. Sed Ebræum id eff haud obscure Ex. 2, 10. innuitur, cum filia Regi Pharaonis eum משׁה vocasse dicitur, quia ex a quis, inquit משׁיתהו extraxi eum: nam משׁה est e re, non pauca e scriptis θεοπνεύςοις, imo e Canoni- cis quoque nonnulla intercidisse, quorum causam quantum potest, agit Grotius. Quod ad 1. Cor. 5, 9. nō potest ex illo indubitato colligi Epistolam quandam ad Corinthios perscriptam periisse, uti Estius, & alii nonnulli volunt. Inclinant quidem eo cum Ambrofi- astro, e Reformatis Calvinus, Beza, Pareus, Marlora- tus, Drusius, e nostris Mylius, Æg. Hunnius, Luc. Osian- der, Sal. Gesnerus, Dav. Rungius, sed ita, ut eam Cano- ni Ecclesiæ perpetuo destinatam, adeoq; Canoni- cam fuisse, inficientur: quo de in Crit. sacro egimus p. 237. Veteres tamen pleriq;, Hieronymus, Theodore- tus, Chrysostomus, Theophylactus, suffragantibus Era- smo in Paraphrasi, Sixto Senensi, Cornelio a Lapide, Ti- rino, censent illam ipsam, quæ tunc ab Apostolo ad Corinthios exarabatur, Epistolam ibi indigitari, cu- jus versum 11. in hoc V. cap. hic respici haud abnuit B. Balduinus: neq; diffitetur Beza, ita verba Apostoli ac- cipi posse. Quod vero Grotius contendit, etiam Pauli quandā ad Thessalonicenses scriptam interiisse, id mere precarium, atq; hactenus ne inter Papistas quidem auditum est: neq; ulla specie veri e 2. Thess. 2, 15. elici potest, quum ibi aperte designetur illa ad Thessalo- nicenses, quam tota Ecclesia Christiana pro prima agnoscit. Quod Epistolam secundam ad Thessalonicen- ses non multo post initia principatus Cajani scriptam, ing, ea de Cajo nonnulla prædicta, tum ordine temporis illam posteriori priorem, imo antequam Paulus Thes- salonicam venisset, & antequam adhuc ibi Ecclesia Christiana constituta esset, Epistolam ad illos perscri- ptam esse, affirmat Grotius, postulata sunt prorsus fri- vola, ob Anti-Christum fictitium Grotii excogitata: siquidem e 2. Thess. 2, 2. manifestū sit, Epistolam, quæ secunda habetur ac dicitur, omnino posteriorem il- la esse, quæ in Canone sacro prima nuncupatur, eam- que post obitum Caji, ad Ecclesiam e Gentilismo ibi collectam, exaratam esse, ac penes totam Ecclesiam indubitatum hactenus id fuerit, priorem Epistolam, quæ ita dicitur, vere primam esse ad Thessalonicen- ses, nec in antiquitate vel vola vel vestigium super- sit, quod tres ad eosdem exaratæ fuerint, aut quód prima interierit, quodq; posterior, quæ nunc habe- tur, secunda, & quæ prima vocatur, tertia haberi de- beat: Verba 2. Thess. 3, 17. ἐν πάσῃ ἐπιϛολῇ non respi- ciunt quasdam deperditas, sed superstites Pauli Epi- stolas. Tandem quod pertendit Grotius in Proœm. Epist. ad Ephes. Epistolam ad Laodicenses periisse, id in gratiam Vulgatæ versionis fieri videtur: cujus ergo etiam comminisci non dubitavit, sine ullius Græci Codicis autoritate Col. 4, 16. legendum esse τὴν λαο- δικείας Laodicensium (Epistolam) quæ sc. ad ipsos spe- ctet, in notis ad h. l. quum constanter exemplaria o- mnia textus originalis legant τὴν ἐκ λαοδικείας, quē- admodum etiam habet Syrus Interpres, nec non e Græcis Chrysostomus, & Theodoretius; unde Epistolam e Laodicea missam, non autem Epistolam quandam ad Laodicenos Paulinam, quæ interierit, intelligi fa- tentur Gagnejus, Cornelius a Lap. Joh. a Gorcum, quod Bellarminus etiam in recognitione operum suorum agnoscere coactus fuit.

## 1:1 Introduction: N. J. [---]am Calovii [---]a on the Pentateu- [---]m of Moses
N. J. [---]AM CALOVII [---]A ON THE PENTATEU- [---]M OF MOSES.

to draw out of the waters 2 Sam. 22:16. But there is no need for us to say that the King's daughter gave him a name in her own language, which the Hebrews later translated into their own, as Münster reports from Aben Ezra, who maintains that it was called in the Egyptian language מניוס Monjos, which sounds in Hebrew like משוי. For she was not ignorant of the Hebrew language, whence she imposed upon the Hebrew boy not an Egyptian, but rather a Hebrew name.

The five books of Moses are called by the Hebrews חֲמִשָּׁה חֻוּמָשִׁים, five fifths: because any book of Moses is called חֹומֶשׁ, as Hottinger notes in Thes. Phil. p. 460: one fifth part of the law. By the Greeks they are called πεντάτευχον, or ἡ πεντάτευχος (sc. βίβλιος) from τεύχω, I construct, as if to say, a five-fold structure or a writing distributed into five volumes. In the Scriptures, the Pentateuch is called תּוֹרָה, the law, and the book of the law, the book of the law of Moses, 2 Chron. 25:4, 34:14, Ezra 6:18, Neh. 11:1, Luke 24:44, as also the book of the covenant, Ex. 24:7, 2 Kings 23:21, 2 Chron. 24:30.

Concerning the divine and canonical authority of the books of Moses, concerning their antiquity, and that Moses was not indeed the first writer absolutely, but nevertheless made the beginning of the canonical Scripture among the inspired men, as also concerning the Mosaic monuments, that this very Scripture which we call Mosaic, namely the Pentateuch, proceeded from Moses, and finally concerning the chief scope of Moses, we have spoken in the Prolegomena to the Commentary on Genesis. The singular excellence of Moses was brought about by (1) his miraculous extraction from the waters, (2) his royal education in the royal court by the daughter of Pharaoh, Ex. 2, and (3) his instruction in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, Acts 7:22, (4) his illustrious calling made face-to-face by the Son of God Himself from the burning bush. (5) The granting of necessary gifts with a clearly unusual miraculous power for a most solemn and no less eminent embassy, so that he might be mighty in words and in deeds, Ex. 3 and 4, Acts 7:22. (6) The liberation and leading out of the Israelite people from Egypt. (7) Their miraculous leading through the Red Sea. (8) His imperial power over the whole people of the Lord, and his theocratic government of the same. (9) The most singular revelation of God, by which God dealt not as with His other servants, but in a more eminent manner and far more familiarly with Moses His servant in all His house, the whole Church of Israel, faithful, Heb. 3:2, and manifested Himself to him by speaking with him mouth to mouth, Num. 12:7 seq. (10) His long and repeated conversation with God on the mountain, by which he was present with God for 40 days and nights on two occasions, Ex. 24:18, ch. 34:28, whence his face shone so much that the Israelites could not bear its splendor. (11) The receiving from God of the tables of the law, on which the Decalogue was inscribed by God. (12) The authentic consignment of the divine laws. (13) The investiture and ordination of the High Priest, Lev. 8. (14) The erection of the tabernacle of the covenant. (15) The exaltation of the bronze serpent in the desert, Num. 21. (16) The defeat of the King of the Amorites and the King of Bashan. (17) The repetition of the divine law, Deut. 1. (18) The divine burial of Moses, Deut. 34. (19) The taking up of the resurrected Moses into heaven, which seems to have happened shortly after the burial, when the Devil wanted to prostitute his body to idolatry, for which he was not only rebuked by Michael the Archangel, but the body of Moses was also taken up into heaven, as he in whom he was seen in glory at the transfiguration of Christ

Matt. 17:3, with the prophet Elijah. Furthermore, he did not approach the most divine and holy work of the PENTATEUCH by his own will, but instructed by divine command, Ex. 34:27, and moved by the internal impulse of the Holy Spirit, 2 Pet. 1:21, 2 Tim. 3:16. Of whose inspiration and divine authority God Himself is frequently introduced as a witness not only in the Mosaic writings themselves, but also in other Holy Scriptures throughout the whole Code of the Old and New Testament, and the condition of the things themselves which it exhibits proves the same, such as the history of creation, the fall, the Proto-Evangelium, the events before the flood, in the flood, and after the flood, regarding the propagation of nations, the confusion of languages, the lives of the Patriarchs, the promulgation of divine laws, oracles, and divine prophecies, and other things which he could not have had from elsewhere except from divine revelation, as well as the indubitable character of the divine speech, to say nothing of other internal criteria. We have brought forward exotic testimonies concerning Moses in the cited prolegomena from Eupolemus, that Moses was a prophet and the first wise man; from Artapanus, that he handed down many things most useful to the human race, and was called Mercury because of his interpretation of sacred letters and received honor equal to the gods; from Numenius, that his prayers to God were most powerful, by which he brought the most grievous calamities upon Egypt; from the Mohammedans, such as Beidawi, that he alone spoke with God, as also from Kessaeus, that the law sent down to the children of Israel is the book of God and His word; from the Alcoran itself, that Moses spoke with God, and the law of Moses is a book which carries a torch in religion, etc. Orpheus in Eusebius, book XIII, Praeparatio Evangelica, ch. 12, according to the emendation of Scaliger and the approval of Grotius in the annotations to book I of De veritate religionis. Christ, thus sang of Moses: Ὡς λόγος ἀρχαίων, ὡς ὑδογενὴς διέταξεν, Ἐκ θεόθεν γνώμαισι λαβὼν κατὰ δίπλακα θεσμὸν, As is the report of the ancients, as the water-born commanded, who received from God the laws according to the double tablet, which he drew into his senses.

Africanus cites Polemon, and Eusebius from Africanus in his Chronicles, testifying thus concerning the exodus from Egypt: Ἐπί Ἄπιδος τοῦ Φωρωνέως μοῖρα τοῦ Αἰγυπτίων στρατοῦ ἐξέπεσον Αἰγύπτου, οἱ ἐν τῇ Παλαιστίνῃ λεγο- μένῃ Συρίᾳ οὐ πόῤῥω Ἀραβίας ᾤκησαν. In the reign of Apis, son of Phoroneus, a part of the Egyptian army left Egypt, and they dwelt in that Syria which is called Palestine, not far from Arabia. Josephus, however, against Apion, concerning the same exodus, cites from the Egyptians themselves Manetho, Lysimachus, and Chaeremon, although they mix false things with true, from whom it is evident that the Hebrews, sprung from the Assyrians, took possession of a part of Egypt: there they led a pastoral life: but afterwards, oppressed by servile labor, they left Egypt, with certain Egyptians also accompanying them under the leadership of Moses, and through the lands of the Arabs they finally arrived in Syria Palestine, and there followed institutions contrary to the institutions of the Egyptians. Diodorus Siculus, among those who have ascribed the authors of their laws to GODS, mentions Moses in these words in book 1: παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις δὲ Μωσῆν τὸν Ἰάω ἐπικαλούμενον Θεὸν, Moses among the Jews [ascribes his laws to] the GOD who is called Jao. He refers to the tetragrammaton name יהוה. Justin, in his Exhortation to the Greeks, besides Diodorus Siculus, names also Apion, Ptolemy, Mendesius, Hellanicus, Philochorus, Castor, Thallus, and Alexander Polyhistor. Compare also Cyril, book I against Julian. Strabo, book XVI, teaches that the sacred institutions and rites [instituted] by Moses were neither burdensome in expense nor hateful through frenzied madness. Attributing to him not obscure divine precepts. Juvenal says, they learn and observe and fear the Jewish law.

Whatever Moses handed down in his secret volume.

Dionysius Longinus, who lived in the time of the Emperor Aurelian, in his book on the sublime style of speaking, sets forth Moses as an example in this way, [showing] how those who speak about GOD ought to take pains to present Him to us as great, pure, and unmixed. He acted thus, he says, even he who founded laws for the Jews, a man of no common genius, as one who both conceived and expressed the power of GOD worthily, writing these things immediately at the beginning of his laws: He said, he says, GOD. What? Let there be light, and there was light; Let there be earth, and there was earth. Chalcidius says of Moses: The most wise Moses, animated not by human eloquence, but, as they say, by divine inspiration.

We have treated of the Object and principal Scope of Moses in a certain Academic program, which it pleases us to subjoin here: Just as the most important goal, the beginning and the end, the Alpha and the Omega of all Holy Scripture, both Prophetic and Apostolic, is Christ the God-man: so especially has the saving passion of Christ been handed down and proposed in the Scripture of both covenants by the holy men of God; so that a certain theologian piously said that Scripture should be read as if it were written in the blood of Christ. For just as in the New Testament the leader of the Apostles professed that he knew nothing else except Jesus Christ, and him crucified, 1 Cor. 2, 2. So in the Old Testament the Spirit of Christ, who was in the Prophets, foretold the sufferings which are in Christ and the subsequent glories, as St. Peter testifies, 1 Ep. 1, 11. Nor indeed was it right to be silent about Him in whom the salvation of all is uniquely situated, by whose knowledge and faith the Ancients were justified no less than we are today in the time of the New Covenant. By his knowledge shall my righteous Servant himself justify many, he says, Is. ch. 53, 11. What other knowledge of the righteous servant is that, than the one about which the Prophet there expressly and so clearly prophesied, that it deserved to be called by the Evangelist, Jerome, and Augustine, the knowledge of his passion and death, as the reason immediately added teaches; And he himself shall bear their iniquities. Because for this reason he himself was made sin for us, that we might be made the righteousness of God in him, 2 Cor. 5, 21. Which is the only method of justification and justifying faith proposed in Scripture, so that besides it no other can be devised, unless the entire Scripture is overturned. So that the piously learned cannot wonder enough, by what Spirit he was agitated (certainly not by the Spirit of CHRIST, who was in the Prophets) when, among other burdensome sayings, Calixtus uttered in his Refutation, th. 19, that nothing is read about the passion of Christ in the earlier books of the Psalms of David; 'From Isaiah the suffering and death of the Messiah is also prophesied more clearly than happened before, of which nothing is to be read in the previous books before David wrote his Psalms.' For what is this other than to contradict to his face the Holy Spirit, who testified most clearly that the passion of Christ was predicted by MOSES just as much as by the other Prophets, Acts 10, 38. & especially Acts 26, 22, where Paul with a clear voice professes that he has said nothing outside of those things which the Prophets and Moses said would come to pass, namely that Christ would suffer, and would be the first to announce light from the resurrection of the dead to the people and to the Gentiles. What is this other than to contradict to the face of Christ himself, who demonstrated his passion and resurrection not only from the Psalms and Prophets, but also from Moses, both to the disciples on the road to Emmaus and to the Apostles, Luke 24, 25. He himself said to them: O foolish and slow of heart to believe all that the Prophets have spoken; (let Calixtus also think this saying applies to himself) Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and so to enter into his glory? And beginning at MOSES and ALL THE PROPHETS, he expounded to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself. If he demonstrated from Moses equally and from the Prophets that 'ought not Christ to have suffered, and so to enter into his glory,' with what face will it be denied that the passion of Christ was predicted in Moses equally and in the Prophets? And verse 44 and following: He said to them, these are the words which I spoke to you, while I was still with you, that all things must be fulfilled which were written in the law of Moses, in the Prophets, and in the Psalms. Then he opened their understanding, that they might understand the Scriptures. Which ones? Of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms, as his own words have it. And he said to them: For thus it is written: but what is written? Thus it behooved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day, and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations. These things Christ, to whom Calixtus opposes himself diametrically, saying that nothing of the sort, whether concerning the passion or the resurrection of Christ from the dead, is written in Moses. To which of the two shall we give credence? To Christ, who is the truth itself? Or indeed to Calixtus? But if we piously examine the way and the reason by which the faithful before David obtained salvation with us, certainly no other way is to be opened than that which is shown as the sole and unique way in the Scriptures through the blood of Jesus Christ, not with the faithless and damned Photinian heretics: because the Mouth of the Apostles, St. Peter, protests that there is salvation in no other, nor is any other name given under heaven among men, by which we must be saved, than the name of Jesus Crucified, and raised from the dead, that corner-stone rejected in his passion, Acts 4, 10 seqq., outside and beyond whom no other is placed as a foundation of salvation, whether by the Prophets of the Old, or by the Apostles of the New Testament, Eph. 2, 20. Therefore the Holy Scripture teaches that the righteousness of God, which is had through faith in the blood of Christ, has been manifested without the law, or the works of the law, and is approved by the testimony of the LAW and the Prophets, namely that we are justified freely by the grace of GOD, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God set forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood, Rom. 3, 21. 24. He does not say, it is given, says Chrysostom in this place, but it is manifested, so that he may cut off the objection of novelty: For that which is manifested, is manifested as old, and as that which had been hidden for some time. Nor only this, but also the things which follow sufficiently show that the righteousness of which he speaks is not new and recently born. For when he said, it is manifested, he adds that it is approved by the testimony of the law and the Prophets. Do not be deterred, he says, from it, because it is now first given, nor be troubled, as if it were a temporary and foreign thing. Now, indeed, from the very beginning the Law and the Prophets predicted that. And lest any doubt remain, Abraham, the Father of all believers, is introduced in Rom. IV, and is set forth as an example of justification through the imputation of faith. But what is that faith? That by which we believe in him who raised our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead, inasmuch as he was delivered up for our sins and raised for our justification, v. 23, 24. But also in Heb. XI, a cloud of witnesses of the Old Testament is exhibited, who looked toward Jesus and his cross by faith, from the very beginning of the Church, so that it may be demonstrated that we obtain salvation by faith in the passion of Christ, which is the scope of that entire treatise, concerning which see B. Athanasius, hom. in S. Patr. & Prophet. Faith, which directs our feet into the way of the knowledge of God and a virtuous and irreproachable conversation, does not have a recent beginning, as the impious and lost Jews affirm: but it is derived from the holy and pious fathers, I mean Abel and Enoch, and Noah, and Abraham, and all the other righteous ones. Athanasius executes this more prolixly in the same place. That magnificent eulogy of Mosaic faith, which esteemed the reproaches of Christ as greater riches than any treasures of Egypt, v. 28, does not allow one to doubt that Moses diligently propagated among the people of GOD the true faith concerning the saving passion of Christ, which he deemed preferable to all the riches of the world. Now, if one descends to the θεόπνευσα (God-breathed) writings, with what appearance of truth can it be denied that the Passion of Christ was proposed in the Holy Scriptures before the times of David, both by illustrious oracles and by excellent types? In the very first πρωτευαγγελίῳ (proto-evangelium), Gen. 3:15, which Calixtus—however much he may otherwise not rarely Judaize—explains in l. c. Bb 3 as concerning the Messiah who would crush the head of the serpent, that is, who would destroy the works of the Devil and take away the power from sin, death, and condemnation, which were introduced by the Devil, it was predicted that the Devil would bruise his heel, to designate the passion of the seed of the woman, and that most grievous one, which the word תשופנו concerning the most grievous wounds and afflictions of Job, used in ch.
