Ac DEO quidem mortem ludũ esse, quivis facile credit, sed quod idem mihi & in meo corpore statuendum sit, mortem non esse mortem, hoc nec Medicus, nec Philosophus, nec Juris Consultus unquam persuadebit. Quis enim illa conjunget & conciliabit, mors non est mors, sed vita. Moses ipse contrarium affirmat. Si enim legem audias, dicet : Media vita in morte, juxta veterem illam & pi- am cantionem in Ecclesia, sed est legalis tantum. Ev- angelium autem & fides invertunt hanc cantionem, & sic canunt : Media morte in vita sumus ; teRedemto- rem laudamus, suscitasti nos de morte, & salvasti nos. Hinc Paulus triumphat Col. 2. Expolians Prin- cipatus & Potestates, ostentavit eos palam. Item 2. Cor. 6. Quasi morientes, & ecce vivimus. Hæc fides vis est, quæ ita mediat inter mortem & vitam, & transmutat mortem in vitam & immortalitatem, quam scit donatam per Christum. Unde mirabilem & præ- claram descriptionem mortis constituit divinus vir; Mors habet animam & corpus. Corpus est extinctio mortis animæ. Anima mortis est ipse pavor & horror mortis. Quod si anima mortis est mortua, corporis mors est somnus. Hoc credimus, ideo morti insul- tamus læti : Mors ubi stimulus, ubi victoria tua? Me- dia morte in vita sumus. Non moriar &c. Qui hanc artem novit, gratias agat DEO. Sed danda est opera, ut non solum speculative in ore, sed virtualiter eam & toto pectore teneamus. Hæc est sapientia Dei, scientia Sanctorum, sublimis cognitio super captum mundi. Atque ea non vacuos nos, nec sine fructu consti- tuit &c.

## 22:12
vers. 12. NOW I HAVE KNOWN THAT THOU FEAREST GOD) By this tenth and greatest of all experiments: after which Abraham was not tempted further. Now there are ten temptations of Abraham: the departure from his country: the famine by which he is driven into Egypt: his wife taken away: the war with four Kings: the despair of offspring, whence he applied himself to Hagar: circumcision: his wife taken away again: the expulsion of Hagar now a mother: the sending away of Ishmael: the offering of Isaac.

Vers. eod. FOR MY SAKE) This is added from the Greek, Samaritan and Syriac: which consensus shows that it was once in the Hebrew Codices.

The authority of the Samaritan and Syriac Codex is not so great, that the Hebrew text should be amended from it.

One interpreter, as is wont to happen, followed another. And indeed there are found very many additions in the Greek and Latin version. Shall we believe that the Hebrew codex is now lacking in them? Although here in the Hebrew text that particle is not missing. Which Grotius ought to have compared more correctly. Thou hast not prohibited or restrained thy only son, ממני, FROM ME. The said Interpreters expressed the sense: Thou hast not spared thy son for my sake.

Latin:

vers. 12. NVNC COGNOVI QVOD TIMES DEUM ) Decimo hoc & omnium maximo experimento: post quod tan- tatus Abraham ultra non fuit. Decem autem tentationes Ab- rahami sunt: exitus e patria : fames quo in Ægyptum expelli- tur : uxor abducta : bellum cum quatuor Regibus : desperatio prolis, unde ad Agarem se applicuit : circumcisio: uxor abducta iterum : expulsio Agaris jam matris : ablegatio Ismaelis : obla- tio Isaaci.

Vers. eod. PROPTER ME) Additum hoc ex Græco, Sa- maritano & Syriaco : qui consensus ostendit in Hebræis Codi- cibus id olim fuisse.

Samaritani & Syriaci Codicis autoritas tanti non est, ut inde Ebræus textus emendandus sit.

Unus interpres, ut fieri amat, fequutus est alium. Et reperiuntur sane additiones in Graeca & Latina versione longe plurimae. Num in illis deficere nunc Ebraeum codicem credemus? Quanquam hic in E- braeo textu particula illa non desit. Quem rectius conferre debuisset Grotius. Non prohibuisti vel cohi- buisti filium tuum unicum, ממני, A ME. Sensum expreffere dicti Interpretes: Non pepercisli filio tuo propter me.

## 22:14
Vers. 14. IN THE MOUNT THE LORD WILL SEE] The Hebrew words bear best to be translated thus: In the mount of the Lord it shall be looked upon: that is, to use the words of Euripides: God found a way for the unexpected. Others take the name יְהוָה in the nominative case, rendering it actively with the Vulgate, that the Lord saw and looked upon Abraham, and provided for him another victim: as if Abraham unknowingly had predicted it in verse 8: The Lord will provide, if indeed the simple word of seeing is sometimes used for providence. Some prefer to interpret it with the LXX. passively, or in the past, The Lord has been seen by me, or showed himself to be seen, or in the future, The Lord shall be seen, which passed into a proverb, and was accustomed to be used, when they expected the help of the lord in perplexed affairs, that he would appear from a machine. Weidner in his treatise on the principal places of faith, tract 2. fixes the prophecy here concerning the future manifestation of the son of God i.e. The Lord God incarnate shall be seen to be sacrificed and crucified in this place. To which perhaps those things of R. Salom. Jarchi from the Midrash Agdala can be referred, The Lord will be propitious to Israel, and will deliver him from punishments: therefore it is said in the ages and times to come in the mount the Lord shall be seen. We confess however that the Hebrew text by the force of the accentuation, is rather to be rendered thus: In the mount of the Lord it shall be seen, or shall be provided, because from this apparition that mount received its name, and was called the mount of the Lord by way of excellence or at least peculiarly, but that by this proverb also that singular providence was prophetically designated, and economy, which would one day appear in this mount, as that in which both the Hierosolymitan temple was built, and Christ by teaching, and performing miracles, nay even by offering himself on the altar of the cross on some ridge of that mount, provided for our salvation. Conf. Comment. in Genesin.

Latin:

Vers. 14. IN MONTE DOMINVS VIDEBIT] Hebraeae voces optime ferunt sic verti: In monte Domini prospicietur: id est, ut Euripidis utar verbis: Τῶν ἀδοκήτων πόρον εὗρε θεός. Alii nomen יְהוָה in casu recto accipiunt, cum Vulgato active reddentes, quod Dominus viderit & respexerit Abrahamum, eique de alia victima prospexe- rit: quasi Abraham nescius id verf. 8. praedixerit: Dominus providebit, siquidem simplex verbum vi- dendi quandoq; pro providentia adhibeatur. Non- nulli malunt id interpretari cum LXX. passive, vel in praeterito, Dominus visus est mihi, aut visendum se praebuit, vel in futuro, Dominus videbitur, quod in dicterium abiit, & adhiberi consuevit, cum in re- bus perplexis domini auxilium expectarunt, quod ἀπὸ μηχανῆς appariturus sit. Weidnerus in locis fidei praecip. tract. 2. prophetiam hic figit de futura manifestatione filii Dei q. d. Dominus Deus incarnatus videbitur immolari & crucifigi isto loco. Quo refer- ri forte poterunt illa R. Salom. Jarchi ex Midrasch Agdala, Dominus Israeli propitius erit, eumq; liberabit a poenis: proinde dicitur seculis & aetatibus venturis in monte Dominus videbitur. Fatemur tamen Ebraeum textum vi accentuationis, ita potius reddendum: In monte Domini videbitur, vel providebitur, quod ab hac apparitione mons ille nomen acceperit, & ἐξο- χικῶς vel certe peculiariter mons Domini dictus sit, sed quod hoc etiam dicterio Prophetice designata sit singularis illa providentia, & οἰκονομία, quae olim in hoc monte apparitura sit, utpote in quo & Hieroso- lymitanum templum extructum, & Christus docen- do, & miracula patrando, imo etiam sese in ara cru- cis in jugo aliquo montis istius offerendo saluti no- strae prospexit. Conf. Comment. in Genesin.

## 22:17
Ver. 17. AS THE STARS OF HEAVEN, AND AS THE SAND, WHICH IS ON THE SEA SHORE) Ovid, Tristia, book 1. - - - as many stars as shine in the ether, And as many bodies as dry dust contains.

THE GATES OF HIS ENEMIES] Even the most fortified cities.

Latin:

Vers. 17. SICVT STELLAS COELI, ET VELVT ARE- NAM, QVAE EST IN LITTORE MARIS) Ovidius Tri- stium l. 1. - - - quot in aethere fidera lucent, Parvaq, quot siccus corpora pulvis habet.

PORTAS INIMICORVM SVORVM] Vrbes etiam muni- tissimas.

## 22:21
ver. 21. BUZ HIS BROTHER) Whence the fortress Busan not far from Singara, which Ammianus Marcellinus mentions in book 18.

CAMUEL THE FATHER OF THE SYRIANS] More correctly, the father of Aram. For the Syrians, who are the Ἄριμοι to the ancients and the Ἐρεμβοὶ to Homer, are from the older Aram, mentioned above at 9, 22. This son of Nahor was therefore called Aram, because he was born among the Mesopotamian Syrians: just as Jacob is also called Aram, that is, a Syrian, because he had lived there, Deut. 26, 3. From this Aram, son of Nahor, it is credible that a fortress near the fortress of Busan took its name, and was called Reman in the aforementioned place of Ammianus, namely with the omission of the very thin letter, just as the Syrians themselves, who by others are called ראם, are called רם in Job 32, 2. and 2 Chron. 22, 6. And another Aram, son of Esrom, in Luke 3, 33. in Hebrew, רם both in Ruth 4, 18. and 1 Chron. 2, 8. with the letter ן added besides at the end, just as in Busan.

Latin:

vers. 21. BVZ FRATREM EJVS) Vnde Busan castellum non longe a Singaris, cujus meminit Ammianus Marcellinus libro 18.

CAMV EL PATREM TRORUM] Rectius patrem Ara- mi. Nam Syri, qui Ἄριμοι veteribus & Ἐρεμβοὶ Homero, sunt ab Aramo vetustiore, nominato supra 9, 22. Dictus ergo hic Nachoris filius Aram, quod natus esset inter Syros Mesopota- mienses: sicut & Jacobus Aram, id est, Syrus dicitur, quod ibi habitasset, Deut. 26, 3. Ab hoc autem Aramo Nachoris filio credibile est nomen habuisse castellum castello Busan propin- quum, dictumque Reman Ammiani dicto loco, nimirum omif- sa litera tenuissima, sicut Syri ipsi, qui aliis ראם, dicuntur רם Jobi 32, 2. & 2. Paral. 22, 6. Et alius Aram Efronis filius Luc. 3, 33. in Hebraeo, רם tum Ruth 4, 18. tum 1. Paral. 2, 8. addita praeterea ad finem litera ן perinde ut in Busan.

## 23:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIII. Sarah's death, and burial.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIII. Sara mors, & Sepultura.

## 23:2
Ver. 2. IN THE CITY OF ARBE) In Hebrew קרית ארבע. The former word, which the Syrians pronounce קרתא, signifies a city, whence Tigranocerta, the city of Tigranes, Carathiocerta, Vologesocerta in Pliny, Artaxata in Stephanus, Chartachadta, a new city, whence corruptly Καρχηδὼν and Carthage, Cariara among the Etruscans, and in Arabia Carthara, the city of Luria, for Çarthiara, Carteja, a colony of the Phoenicians in Spain, an insular city, Cartennæ in Mauritania, the city of the spring, Carcome for Carthcome in the same place, a high city, Carepula for Carthpula an obscure city in the same place. In this word therefore the middle ו was added by the Hebrews, or omitted by the Syrians, just as עלוין the name of God עלין Alon was for the Phoenicians, as Sisenna and Plautus testify. And at the end י is found in Job 29:7.

Moreover, this city is called Arbe from the giant Arba, a famous man among the sons of Anak, who either founded or enlarged it, Josh. 14:15, ch. 15:13. It was called therefore Kiriath Arba like Κους αντινόπολις, not indeed because it was a τετράπολις: much less from the IV Patriarchs buried there, namely Adam, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For the tradition about Adam is entirely uncertain: and the name Kiriath-Arba it had itself before Abraham, later called Hebron.

Latin:

Verf. 2. IN CIVITATE ARBE) Hebraice קרית ארבע. Vox prior quam Syri קרתא enunciant, urbem significat, unde Tigranocerta urbs Tigranis, Carathiocerta, Vologeso- certa apud Plin. Artcesicerta apud Stephanum, Chartachadta urbs nova, unde corrupte Καρχηδὼν & Carthago, Cariara in Hetruscis, & in Arabia Carthara urbs Luriae, pro Çarthiara, Carteja Poenorum colonia in Hispania, urbs insularis, Cartennæ in Mauritania urbs fontis, Carcome pro Carth- come ibidem urbs alta, Carepula pro Carthpula urbs obscura i- bidem. In hac ergo voce medium ו additum est ab Hebræis, aut omissum a Syris, quomodo עלוין Dei nomen עלין Alon fuit Pœnis, teste Sisenna & Plauto. Et fine י invenitur Jobi 29, 7.

Est autem civitas hæc Arbe dicta a gigante Arba, viro celebri inter filios Enakim, qui eam vel condi- dit, vel ampliavit, Jos. 14, 15. c. 15, 13. Dicta ergo Ki- riath Arba ut Κους αντινόπολις, non vero quod fuerit τετράπολις : multo minus a IV. Patriarchis ibi se- pultis & Adam, Abraham, Isaac & Jacob. Nam tra- ditio de Adamo prorsus incerta est: & nomen Ki- riath-Arba ipsa habuit ante Abrahamum, postea Hebron dicta.

## 23:9
v. 9. THAT HE MAY GIVE ME THE DOUBLE CAVE. The LXX Interpreters explained it thus, as if it were an appellative, τὸ σπήλαιον τὸ διπλῦν: and Aben Ezra said the cave was in the middle of a cave, others a pit through which access to the cave was opened, others with Salmasius, in Exercit. Plinian., a double hiatus or opening, and an entrance from two parts, so that the size of the cave is meant to be designated: But since it is not only called the cave המכפלה, but also וגי Cave במכפלה in Machpelah, which cannot be rendered, Cave in doubleness, but must be understood locally in the place of Machpelah, especially also, because it is added that it was opposite Mamre, therefore it is more correctly taken as a proper name. Compare Mr. Varenius on this passage. Nor does Grotius profit regarding Benjamin. Tudel. around v. 19, challenging: For to say nothing of the doubtful faith of this Benjamin, he himself does not call either that field, or the double cave, or of duplication, even if it is so called in the version of Constantine L'Empereur, but with the added name המכפלה, whether he uses it as a proper name, or indeed as an appellative, does not appear, since it can be translated no less in that way than in this. He reports, however, about that cave (let the faith be with the author) that Christians have made six sepulchers there, to which they have assigned the names of Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebecca, Jacob, and Leah, saying to pilgrims that these are the sepulchers of the Patriarchs, so that money may be contributed: But to a Jew approaching, who pays the fee for the cave to the gatekeeper, an iron gate is opened, which had been constructed way back from the times of the Patriarchs: and whoever descends here, with a burning torch, indeed discovers nothing in the first cave, but not even in the second, until he arrives at the third and there are those six sepulchers, which are opposite one another, sealed with individual letters carved, and a lamp is lit in the cave, which burns day and night at the sepulchers.

Latin:

v. 9. UT DET MIHI SPELUNCAM DUPLICEM. LXX. Interpp. ita exposuere, ceu appellati- vum, τὸ σπήλαιον τὸ διπλῦν : & Aben Esra Spelun- cam fuisse in medio speluncæ, alii fossam, per quam aditus ad speluncam patuerit, alii cum Salmasio, in Exercit. Plinian. duplicem hiatum vel aperturam, & ex duabus partibus ingressum, ut speluncæ ma- gnitudo innuatur designari ajunt: Sed quum non tantum spelunca dicatur המכפלה, sed etiam וגי Spelunca במכפלה in Machpelah, quod reddi ne- quit, Spelunca in duplicitate, sed localiter intelli- gendum in loco Machpelah, imprimis etiam, quia additur, quod fuerit e regione Mamre, ideo rectius pro nomine proprio habetur. Confer Dn. Varenius in b. l. Neq; proficit Grotius ad Benjam. Tundel. cir- ca v. 19. provocando: Nam ut nihil de Benjaminis istius dubia fide dicam, non vocat ipse vel agrum il- lum, vel speluncam duplicem, vel duplicationis, etsi ita vocetur in versione Constantini L'Empereur, sed ad- dito nomine המכפלה, quod an ceu proprium adhibeat, an vero ut appellativum, non apparet, quum non minus isto, quam hoc modo verti possit. Refert autem de illa spelunca (fides penes autorem sit) quod Christiani ibi sex sepulcra fecerint, qui- bus ab Abrahamo, Sara, Isaaco, Rebecca, Jacobo & Lea imposuerint nomina, peregrinantibus dicentes, hæc Patriarcharum esse sepulcra, ut pecunia eroge- tur: Sed Judæo accedenti, qui mercedem speluncæ janitori solvat, aperiri portam ferream, quæ jam inde a Patriarcharum temporibus confecta fuerit: & qui huc descendit, cum ardente face, nihil quidem in prima spelunca deprehendere, sed nec in secunda, donec deveniat in tertiam ibique sex esse sepulcra illa, quæ sibi invicem opposita, singulis literis inci- sis obsignata, & accendi lampada in spelunca, quæ die nocteque ad sepulcra ardeat.

## 23:12
Vers. 12. ABRAHAM BOWED DOWN BEFORE THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND) He showed them a sign of honor, such as was among the Greeks to move the hand to the mouth, προσκυνεῖν to the Greeks, to adore to the Latins: but to the Hebrews there are many degrees: to bow the head, which is קדד, to bow the whole body, to place oneself on the knees, which is ברך, to prostrate oneself on the ground. Here in the Hebrew it is ישתחו, in the Hithpael, from שחה by which is signified the bending of the body, an honor neither too familiar, nor entirely submissive. See below 33, v. 3. For Abraham was subject to no one, and of his own right, above 14, and here in verse 6. Therefore he is called βασιλεύσαι by Nicolaus of Damascus, he is called king by Justin book 36, the anointed of GOD Ps. 105 v. 15. Note, however, that the most ancient kingdoms were of such a kind that some right remained to the people, as Aristotle notes Polit. 3, 14. The same appears in Alcinous in Homer Odyss. θ'. Eurip. Plisthene: Do not hang all power on the people, nor again do them harm.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ADORAVIT ABRAHAM CORAM POPULO TERRÆ) Honoris signum eis exhibuit, quale apud Græcos e- rat manum admovere ori, προσκυνεῖν Græcis, adorare Latinis : Hebraæis autem multi gradus: flectere caput, quod est קדד, flectere corpus totum, in genua se ponere, quod est ברך, pro- sternere se humi. Hic in Hebræo est ישתחו, in Hithpael, a שחה quo significatur flexio corporis, honor nec familia- ris nimium, nec plane submissus. Vide infra 33. v 3. Erat enim Abraham nulli subditus, ac sui juris, supra 14. & hic commate 6. Ideo βασιλεύσαι dicitur Nicolao Damasceno, rex vocatur Justino l. 36. unctus DEI Ps. 105 v. 15 Nota autem regna anti- quissima ejusmodi fuisse, ut populo aliquod jus maneret, ut no- tat Aristoteles Polit. 3, 14. Apparet idem in Alcinoo apud Ho. mer. Odyss. θ'. Eurip. Plisthene: Δήμῳ δὲ μήτε πᾶν ἀναρτήσῃς κράτος, Μή τ' αὖ κακώσῃς.

Vers. 18. IN THE SIGHT OF THE SONS OF HETH] This is a cession in law.

Latin:

Vers. 18. VIDENTIBUS FILIIS HETH] Hæc est in jure cessio.

Vers. 19. IN THE DOUBLE CAVE OF THE FIELD) See Benjamin of Tudela.

We have already seen about that at verse 9.

Vers. 19. IN SPELUNCA AGRI DUPLICI) Vide Ben- jaminem Tudelensem.

De eo jam vidimus ad versum 9.

## 24:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIV. Rebecca the Bride, and wife. The death of Sarah.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIV. Rebecca Sponsa, & uxor. Saræ mors.

## 24:2
Vers. 2. PUT YOUR HAND UNDER MY THIGH] A custom of swearing at that time accepted among those nations, as Josephus notes. See below 47, 29. as if they were saying, if I deceive, may I perish by your sword. For the place of the sword is at the thigh. Jud. 3:16, 21. Ps. 45:4. But Aben Ezra says it was a sign of homage, to place the right hand under one who is sitting. Thus for the Romans to possess comes from sitting.

R. Solomon thinks that rite was used because of the Sacrament of circumcision: others give this reason for it, that the thigh is a symbol of generation and life: as if the oath were accustomed to be made by Life, or by GOD the author of life. Some observe from Chrysostom and Jerome that the Messiah was to come from the thigh of Abraham, thus designated, and that faith in the same was declared by the saints by this ceremony. These reasons can be joined, indeed one may even add a fourth, that namely servants to their masters, sons to their parents, swore with the hand placed under the thigh as a sign of subjection. He was sitting, says Mr. Varenius on this passage, he to whom the oath was rendered as Lord with the thigh raised, under which the servant or son placed his hand, as if he were saying: By this my right hand placed under you, I acknowledge your Lordship, and my subjection owed to you, and I swear that I will faithfully execute the business committed to me by you. Thus I am your servant. Aben-Ezra is a witness that this custom still obtained in India in his time. Grotius's conjecture relies neither on authority nor on any reason. It arose without doubt from the fact that some posit an ellipsis in the formulas of an oath, as for example v. 38. If you do not go to the house of my Father, I would call down curses upon you. But there is no need for that ellipsis, nor is it to be considered sufficiently pious; indeed, it is horrible and profane. Compare what is said at Num. 32, 12 and below v. 38.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PONE MANUM TUAM SUBTER FEMUR MEUM] Mos jurandi eo tempore apud illas gentes recep tus, ut Josephus notat. Vide infra 47, 29. quasi dicerent, si fallam, ense tuo peream. Nam ad femur locus ensis. Jud. 3, 16. 21. Ps. 45, 4. At Abenesdra homagii signum fuisse dicit, sedenti dextram supponere. Sic Romanis possidere a sedendo.

RItum illum ob Sacramentum circumcisionis fuisse adhibitum R. Salomo censet : alii ejus hanc dant causam, quod femur Symbolum sit generationis & vitæ : quasi juramentum fieri consueverit per Vitam, vel autorem vitæ DEUM. Nonnulli e Chrysostomo & Hieronymo observant Messiam e femore Abrahami proditurum ita designatum, ac fidem in eundem hac ceremonia a sanctis declaratam fuisse. Conjungi possunt hæ causæ, imo etiam quartam addere licet, quod nempe ministri Dominis, filii parentibus in subjectionis signum manu sub femore posita jurarint. Sedebat, inquit Dn. Varenius in h. l. ille, cui juramentum præstabatur Dominus elevato femore, cui supponebat servus vel filius manum, ac si diceret : Hac mea dextera tibi supposita, tuum Dominium, meam vero subjectionem tibi debitam agnosco, meque commissum mihi a te negotium fideliter executurum juro. Ita sim servus tuus. Morem hunc adhuc in India suo tempore obtinuisse testis est Aben-Esra. Grotiana conjectura nec autoritate nititur, nec ratione ulla. Orta sine dubio inde, quod in formulis juramenti nonnulli ellipsin statuant, utputa v. 38. Si non iveris ad domum Patris mei, dira tibi imprecarer. Sed ea ellipsi opus non est, nec illa satis pia censenda, imo horrida est & prophana. Conf. quæ ad Num. 32, 12. & infra v. 38.

## 24:3
vers. 3. THAT YOU SHALL NOT TAKE A WIFE FOR MY SON FROM THE DAUGHTERS OF THE CANAANITES) The Persian writer Hama al zel, translated by Rabbi Chomer, does not correctly infer from this passage that Laban, whose daughters Jacob married, was not an idolater, nor that the Teraphim were not idols, because Abraham wished marriages with the Canaanites to be avoided only on account of idolatry. But in truth, Laban could have been better than the Canaanites, and his daughters of a more curable disposition, for the reason that Laban retained the worship of the supreme God, although with some things mixed in that were not to be approved; below 31, 49, 53, 54. The Canaanites, however, had completely fallen away from the supreme God and had defiled their lives with many shameful acts. Of evils, the least.

Latin:

vers. 3. UT NON ACCIPIAS UXOREM FILIO MEO DE FILIABUS CANANÆORVM) Non recte ex hoc loco colligit Scriptor Persa Hama al zel translatus a Rabbino Chomer, Labanem, cujus filias duxit Jacobus, non fuisse idololatram, neque Teraphim idola, quia conjugia tantum cum Cananæis ob idololatriam vitari voluerit Abrahamus. At vero potuit Laban melior esse Cananæis, & filiæ ejus sanabilioris ingenii, ideo quod Laban cultum summi Dei, quanquam admixtis quibusdam non probandis retinebat; infra 31, 49. 53. 54. Cananæi autem a summo Deo plane defecerant, vitamque multis flagitiis inquinaverant. De malis minimum.

## 24:7
V. 7. HE SHALL SEND HIS ANGEL. Abraham desired and prayed for this with certain confidence: it shall be rendered, HE SHALL SEND, in the optative mood. If, however, you think he predicted it in the prophetic manner, HE SHALL SEND, we do not deny it. Both explanations cannot stand at the same time, because the verb must be of a certain mood. If it is of the optative mood, it is certainly not of the indicative. However, the optative seems preferable here, because there is added

Latin:

V. 7. IPSE MITTET ANGELUM SUUM. Id optavit & precatus est Abraham cum certa fiducia : ita reddetur, ipse MITTAT, modo optativo. Si tamen Prophetico more prædixisse id, MITTET, censeas, non abnuimus. Utrag, explicatio simul stare nequit, quia verbum certi modi esse oportet. Si optativi est modi : non est utique indicativi. Præferendus autem hîc videtur optativus : quia additur

## 24:8
Vers. 8. BUT IF THE WOMAN WILL NOT FOLLOW YOU, YOU SHALL BE RELEASED FROM THE OATH) So great was the religion of the ancients regarding oaths that they would expressly except even those things which ought to be understood as tacitly excepted. See a similar instance in the Iphigenia in Tauris of Euripides.

Latin:

Vers. 8. SIN AVTEM MVLIER NOLVERIT SEQVI TE, NON TENEBERIS JVREJVRANDO) Tanta erat Veterum in juramentis religio, ut etiam quæ tacite excepta intelligi debeant, nominatim exciperent. Vide simile in Iphigenia Taurica Euripidis.

## 24:15
vers. 15. HAVING A PITCHER ON HER SHOULDER) That was the duty of virgins at that time. See Ex. 2, 16. Homer. Κούρῃ τε ξύμβλητο πρὸ ἄστεος ὑδρευούσῃ.

Latin:

vers. 15. HABENS HYDRAIM IN SCAPVLA SVA) Munus id erat virginum eo tempore. Vide Ex. 2, 16. Homer. Κούρῃ τε ξύμβλητο πρὸ ἄστεος ὑδρευούσῃ.

## 24:38
v. 38. BUT TO THE HOUSE OF MY FATHER YOU SHALL GO. In Hebrew it is אם לא which some render IF NOT, as if there were an ellipsis, and the formula of swearing ought to be supplied, to wit: If you do not go, I will call down curses upon you, or you shall perish by my sword, as Grotius at v. 3 seems to have understood it, just as is gathered from Num. 32, 11 and other places. But in truth, Hebrew philologists rightly observe that the little words אם לא strongly affirm, and are not always to be taken conditionally: as if he were saying, YOU SHALL BY ALL MEANS go to the house of my Father, and so the Vulgate did not render it badly as BUT.

Latin:

v. 38. SED AD DOMUM PATRIS MEI PERGES. In Ebr. est אם לא quod reddunt nonnulli SI NON, quasi ellipsis sit, & suppleri debeat formula jurandi h. m. Si non iveris, dira tibi imprecarbor, vel ense meo periturus es, ut Grotius ad v. 3. videtur accepisse, quemadmodum e Num. 32, 11. aliisq; locis colligitur. Verum enim vero recte observant Philologi Ebræi voculas אם לא vehementer affirmare, non vero conditionate semper accipiendas esse : quasi dicat OMNINO ad domum Patris mei perges, adeoque non male Vulgatus reddidit SED.

## 24:47
vers. 47. EARRINGS) A jewel placed on the nose. Thus in the Hebrew: and thus ἔνωτια is to be supplied above at 22. Such ornaments still exist among the Indians.

Latin:

vers. 47. INAURES) Monile impositum naso. Sic in Hebræo : & ita supplenda ἔνωτια supra 22. Sunt adhuc apud Indos ornamenta talia.

## 24:48
Vers. 48. THE DAUGHTER OF MY MASTER'S BROTHER] That is, granddaughter, just as the Romans also often speak, l. Filii D. de verborum signific.

Latin:

Vers. 48. FILIAM FRATRIS DOMINI MEI] Id est, neptem, quomodo & Romani sæpe loquuntur l. Filii D. de verborum signific.

## 24:49
vers. 49. TO THE RIGHT) Where the Ishmaelites are. TO THE LEFT) Where Lot is with his people.

Latin:

vers. 49. AD DEXTRAM) Ubi Ismaelitæ. AD SINISTRAM) Ubi Loth cum suis.

## 24:50
Vers. 50. LABAN AND BETHUEL) No mention here of the mother and the girl herself. So great was the paternal right at that time, see 1 Cor. 7:36.

But although no express mention of the girl is made here, there is nevertheless no doubt that the consent of Rebecca was added, because without the free consent of the contracting parties, betrothals are not valid, and an interpretative consent is implied, indicated by her presence and the acceptance of the earnest money offered to her. Nor was the consent of the contracting persons ever excluded; indeed, 1 Cor. 7:36 is openly designated by the interpreter Grotius himself in that place as γαμείτωσαν: namely, she herself (the virgin) and he who desires her, because this matter cannot be carried out except between two.

Latin:

Vers. 50. LABAN ET BETHVEL) Matris & puellæ ipsius nulla hic mentio. Tantum valebat jus paternum eo tempore, vid. 1. Cor. 7, 36.

At tametsi expressa puellæ mentio hic non fiat: nullum tamen dubium est consensum Rebeccæ accessisse, quia sine libero partium contrahentium consensu sponsalia rata non sunt, & interpretativus consensus innuitur, indicata præsentia & susceptio- ne arrhæ ipsi oblatæ. Nec consensus personarum contrahentium unquam exclusus, imo 1. Cor. 7, 36. aperte designatus est: interprete ibidem ipso Gro- tio γαμείτωσαν: nempe ipsa (virgo) & qui ipsam de- siderat, quia res hæc nisi inter duos peragi non potest.

## 24:53
Vers. 53. AND WHEN THE SILVER AND GOLDEN VESSELS WERE BROUGHT FORTH) For in heroic times men gave a dowry to their brides, not brides to their men. The scholiast notes this on Euripides' Medea.

Latin:

Vers. 53. PROLATISQVE VASIS ARGENTEIS ET AVREIS) Nam heroicis temporibus viri nuptis dotem da- bant, non nuptæ viris. Notat ad Euripidis Medeam Scholia- stes.

## 24:55
Vers. 55. TEN DAYS) From the Greek ἡμέρας ὡσεὶ δέκα. Perhaps Josephus better understands a year by ימים, in the way that word is taken in Leviticus 25:29 and Amos 4:4, and is translated by ימין in 2 Kings 20:6 and Job 38:21. But he understands עשור, that is, a decade, as months. And Solomon Jarchi thinks no differently.

Latin:

Vers. 55. DECEM DIES) Ex Græco ἡμέρας ὡσεὶ δέκα. Melius forte Josephus per ימים intelligit annum, quomo- do ea vox sumitur Levitici 25, 29. & Amos 4, 4. & per ימין ver- titur 2. Reg. 20, 6. Job. 38, 21. עשור autem, id est, decada intel- ligit mensium. Nec aliter Salomo Jarchius.

## 24:60
Vers. 60. THOU ART OUR SISTER) You may rightly translate the Hebrew אחתנו את as O our sister. For with them, the second person takes the place of the vocative.

Latin:

Vers. 60. SOROR NOSTRA ES) Hebræum אחתנו את recte vertas o soror nostra. Est enim illis secunda per- sona vice vocativi.

## 24:63
Vers. 63. TO MEDITATE) Those who translate it as 'to pray' are not wrong. See Ps. 102:1.

Latin:

Vers. 63. AD MEDITANDVM) Non male qui vertunt ad orandum. Vide Pf. 102, 1.

## 24:65
Vers. 65. HE IS MY MASTER) The younger lord. Even while the father is alive, sons are in a way masters of the paternal property.

TOOK A VEIL AND COVERED HERSELF) For 'veil' in Hebrew there is צעיף, the Greeks translated it θέριστρον. She covered her face after the manner of matrons, 1 Cor. 11:10; see above 20:16, and what Jerome has to say about the women of Arabia and Mesopotamia on Isaiah chapter 3, and the Alcoran, Azoara 24, of the Latin edition. Cincius, in Festus, relates that brides and weddings were named from that custom of veiling.

Latin:

Vers. 65. IPSE EST DOMINVS MEVS) Herus minor. Filii etiam vivente patre quodammodo Domini rerum pater- narum.

TOLLENS CITO PALLIVM OPERVIT SE) Pro pal- lio in Hebræo est צעיף, Græci θέριστρον verterunt. Ope- ruit autem vultum more matronarum 1. Cor. 11. v. 10. vide supra 20, 16. & quæ Hieronymus habet de Arabiæ ac Mesopo- tamiæ fœminis ad Esaiæ cap. 3. Et Alcoranus Azoara 24. edi- tionis Latinæ. Ex eo velandi more dictas nuptas & nuptias tradit apud Festum Cincius.

## 24:67
Vers. 67. INTO THE TENT OF SARAH THY MOTHER) For women had their own tents separately, as it were a γυναικωνῖτιν: see above 18:10, 23:2.

Latin:

Vers. 67. IN TABERNACVLVM SARÆ MATRIS TVÆ) Habebant enim fœminæ tentoria sua seorsim, quasi γυναικωνῖτιν: vide supra 18, 10. 23, 2.

## 25:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXV. Abraham's new marriage with Keturah, his children, and death; Ishmael dies having fathered 12 princes. Isaac's twins Esau and Jacob, and the oracle concerning them. The sale of the birthright.

vers. 1. WIFE) With marriage contracts indeed made, but a handmaid nonetheless, as the Hebrews teach. Therefore she is called a wife, and yet her children receive only gifts, such as the unequal marriage among the Germans, the 'Morgangabicam'. See what was said by us in book 2, chapter 5, section 15, of the Law of War and Peace, and in the Annotations. A concubine among the Hebrews is a handmaid, or another of low status given for cohabitation without a contract, without earnest money, without rites.

One must be careful, however, that Keturah (as some of the Rabbis say) is not confused with Hagar, since it is said that Abraham took another wife.

Latin:

CAPUT XXV. Abrahami cum Kethura novum conjugium, li- beri, & mors, Ismael procreatis 12. duci- bus moritur. Isaaci gemelli Esau & Jacob. & oraculum de iis. Venditio primogeni- turæ.

vers. 1. VXOREM) Pactis quidem dotalibus factis, sed an- cillam tamen, ut docent Hebræi. Ideo & uxor vocatur, & ta- men liberi ejus dona tantum accipiunt, quale apud Germanos matrimonium impar, adMorgangabicam. Vide quæ dicta no- bis lib. 2. c. 5. §. 15. de jure belli ac pacis, & in Annotatis. Con- cubina apud Hebræos est ancilla, aut vilis alia ad concubitum data sine Scriptura, sine arrhis, sine ritibus.

CAvendum autem, ne Kethura (sic ex Rabbinis nonnulli) cum Hagare confundatur, siquidem ex声esse aliam uxorem duxisse Abraham dicatur.

## 25:4
Vers. 4. OPHER) In Greek ὦφείρ. From whom the Africans and Africa. See what we have produced in the first book on the truth of the Christian Religion.

Concerning the children of Keturah, Alexander Polyhistor, in Josephus, book 1, ch. 16, and Eusebius, book 9 of the Preparation for the Gospel, ch. 20, says: Cleodemus, called the Prophet Malchas, in his book about the Jews, says the same things as Moses, who established laws for the Jews, that many children were born to Abraham from Keturah, three of whom are named by him: Afer, Afur, and Afra. From Assur, Assyria is named. From the other two, Afer and Afra, the city of Afra and the land of Africa. These were fellow-soldiers of Hercules in Libya, and of Antaeus. Hercules, however, having married Afra, the daughter, begat from her a son named Dedor. Grotius notes that the Hercules to be understood is not the Theban one, but a much older Phoenician one, whom Philo of Byblos also mentions in Eusebius, book 1 of the Preparation, ch. 10. Whence, therefore, the Ethiopians, a great part of the Africans, received circumcision, is by no means obscure.

Latin:

Vers. 4. OPHER) Græcis ὦφείρ. A quo Afri & Africa. Vide, quæ producta a nobis id librum primum de veritate Religionis Christianæ.

De liberis nempe Cethuræ Alexander Poly- histor apud Josephum libr. 1. c. 16. & Euseb. l. 9. Præpar. Evangel. c. 20. Cleodemus, inquit, Prophe- ta Malchas dictus in libro de Judæis eadem dicit, quæ Moses, qui Judæis leges condidit, ex Cethura Ab- rahamo multos esse natos liberos, quorum tres ab ipso nominantur, Afer, Afur, Afra: Ab Assur dictam Assyriam. Ab aliis duobus Afer & Afra urbem Afram, terramque Africam. Hos Herculis fuisse commilites in Lybiam, & Antæum. Herculem autem cum Afra duxisset filiam, & ex ea filium genuisse Dedorumnomi- ne. Herculem autem intelligendum non Theba- num, sed multo antiquiorem Phœnicem Grotius monet, cujus & Philo Biblius meminit, apud Euseb. l. 1. præpar. c. 10. Unde ergo Æthiopes magna Afro- rum pars circumcisionem receperint, minime ob- scurum est.

## 25:8
verf. 8. DEFICIENS MORTVVS EST (GIVING UP THE GHOST) The verb גוע among the Hebrews is used for death without pain.

Aben Ezra says, every גווע is מיתה (death), but not the reverse. That death is easy, devoid of much pain. Moreover, it is added IN A GOOD OLD AGE, that is, pleasant and tranquil, and that he was gathered to his people; for just as the damned are said to be gathered with sinners, Ps. 26:9, so the death of the righteous is a certain gathering to the people or communion of the triumphant Church, Is. 57:1. Indeed, even the wicked are said to sleep with their fathers, see ch. Jeroboam, 1 Kings 14:20, but only those who die in the faith are said to be gathered to their people: Compare Gen. 35:29, ch. 49:33, Num. 20:24, 26, Deut. 34:20, whence it seems there is no reason to doubt the salvation of Ishmael, because the Holy Scriptures describe his death in this way, Gen. 25:17.

PLENUS DIERVM (FULL OF DAYS) So also the Greeks. In the Hebrew it is שבע, satisfied, that is, of days, which the Samaritans and Syrians added for the sake of explanation. The full Hebrew expression is below 25:8, 35:29, 1 Chron. 23:1, 29:28, Job 42:16.

Latin:

verf. 8. DEFICIENS MORTVVS EST] Verbum גוע apud Hebræos dicitur de morte sine dolore.

AbenEzr. omnis גווע, ait, est מיתה, sed non contra. Illa mors facilis est, multi doloris ex- pers. Additur autem IN CANITIE BONA, hoc est jucunda, & tranquilla, & quod congregatus sit ad po- pulum suum; ut enim damnati congregari cum pecca- toribus dicuntur Ps. 26, 9. ita mors justorum colle- ctio quædam est ad populum vel communionem Ecclesiæ triumphantis Es. 57, 1. Obdormire cum Patribus dicuntur quidem etiam impii, verb. c. Je- roboam 1. Reg. 14, 20. at ad populum suum congrega- ri dicuntur tantum, qui in fide decedunt: Confer Gen. 35, 29. cap. 49, 33. Num. 20, 24. 26. Deuter. 34, 20. unde etiam de Ismaëlis Salute, quia sic mortem ejus describit S. S. Gen. 25, 17. dubitandum non videtur.

PLENUS DIERVM] Sic & Græci. In Hebræo est שבע satur, dierum scilicet, quod explicandi causa addidere Samaritæ & Syri. Plena locutio Hebræa infra 25, 8. 35, 29. 1. Paral. 23, 1. 29, 28. Job. 42, 16.

## 25:9
vers. 9. IN SPELVNCA DVPLICI (IN THE DOUBLE CAVE) in the ancestral tomb.

PART IV. OF GENESIS, THE HISTORY OF ISAAC.

Latin:

vers. 9. IN SPELVNCA DVPLICI) sepulchro gentilitio.

PARS IV. GENESEOS, HISTORIA ISAACI.

## 25:13
Vers. 13. NEBAJOTH) Here Ναβάτης in Stephanus. Whence the Nabataeans in Pliny and almost all the poets.

CEDAR) Whence the Cedreni in Pliny, Book 5, ch. 11. The Cedareni in Lampridius.

Latin:

Vers. 13. NEBAJOTH) Hic Ναβάτης apud Stephanum. Vnde Nabathæi Plinio & Poetis prope omnibus.

CEDAR) Vnde Cedreni Plinio Lib. 5. c. 11. Cedareni Lam- pridio.

## 25:14
MASMA QVOQVE ET DVMA ET MASSA (MASMA ALSO AND DUMA AND MASSA) Good names: for they signify hearing, silence, and patience. Duma with the frequent addition רומת דומאה, Δέματα, a city of Arabia in Stephanus.

Latin:

MASMA QVOQVE ET DVMA ET MASSA] Bona nomina: significant enim audientiam, silentium & patientiam. Duma cum additamento frequenti רומת דומאה Δέματα πόλις ᾿Αραβίας Stephano.

## 25:15
THEMA] A city name in Ptolemy. Tamna is in Strabo.

JETVR) Whence the Ituraeans, as appears in 1 Chron. 5:19. Strabo mentions them in book 16, Pliny in book 5:23, Cicero, Virgil, Lucan, and others.

Latin:

THEMA] Urbis nomen apud Ptolemæum. Tamna est a- pud Strabonem.

JETVR) Vnde Ituræi, ut apparet 1. Paralip. 5, 19. Meminit Strabo lib. 16. Plinius lib. 5, 23. Cicero, Virgilius, Lucanus, alii.

## 25:16
Verse 16. TWELVE PRINCES OF THEIR TRIBES] see what is above 17, 20.

Latin:

Vers. 16. DVODECIM PRINCIPES TRIBVVM SVA RVM] vide quæ supra 17, 20.

## 25:20
Verse 20. WHEN HE WAS FORTY YEARS OLD, HE TOOK REBECCA TO WIFE] Aristotle wishes men to apply themselves to marriage around the thirty-seventh year of their age. Polit. 7, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 20. CVM QVADRAGINTA ESSET ANNORVM, DVXIT VXOREM REBECCAM] Aristoteles viros vult ad conjugium se applicare circa annum ætatis suæ septimum & tricefimum. Polit. 7, 16.

## 25:22
THE LITTLE ONES WERE STRUGGLING WITHIN HER] Apollodorus narrates something similar in Library 2: Acrisius and Proetus, even while they were still in the womb, were at variance with one another.

TO CONSULT THE LORD) Through the mouth of Heber, who is thought to have been alive even then. Thus Maimonides, Rabbi Solomon, and others.

Heber was indeed still alive at that time; in fact, he outlived Abraham himself. For these things happened in the year of the world 2168. But Heber died in the year of the world 2187, who lived the longest of all those born after the flood.

Latin:

COLLIDEBANTVR IN VTERO EJVS PARVVLI] Simile aliquod narrat Bibliothecæ 2. Apollodorus: ᾿Ακρίσιος καὶ προῖτος, ἤτοι καὶ κατὰ γαστρὸς μὲν ἔτι ὄντες ἐστασίαζον πρὸς ἀλλήλως.

VT CONSVLERET DOMINVM) Per os Heberi, qui etiam tunc vixisse putatur. Ita Maimonides, Rabbinus, Salo- mon & alii.

Vixit omnino tunc adhuc Heber, imo ipsi Ab- rahamo superstes fuit. Hæc enim contigere Anno M. 2168. Mortuus autem Heber est anno M. 2187. qui omnium post diluvium natorum diutissime vi- xit.

## 25:23
THE ELDER SHALL SERVE THE YOUNGER) Josephus: The children would have names that were significant; and the one who seemed to be the lesser would surpass the greater.

This is not to be understood primarily of the persons of Esau and Jacob, for the former did not serve the latter, but of the nations, as the oracle clearly sounds: two nations are in your womb. Certainly, the descendants of Jacob had that prerogative over those of Esau, not only in that they alone were brought into the land of Canaan, while these were granted the rugged and barren mountainous regions of Idumea. But the Idumeans were also subjected to the descendants of Jacob in the time of David: whence the Calvinists wrongly prove from this oracle, cited in Romans 9, verse 12, the absolute rejection of Esau to establish their absolute and horrible decree; since, as has been said, it is not a matter here of the person of Esau, nor of rejection from eternal salvation; the Apostle is also very far removed from absolute predestination, and indeed teaches in the cited passage that justification and therefore election are not from works, but from grace, 'not of works, but of Him that calleth,' concerning which see Theol. Apost. Rom. on Romans 9.

That Jacob obtained the prerogative over Esau in this, that the promised seed came from his loins, not the other's, is not in the least doubtful; but this does not make for the salvation of Jacob, or the exclusion of Esau from salvation: it is an external dignity to be established in the line of the Messiah, doing nothing for the blessedness of the soul, and although Esau did not belong to the fathers of Christ according to the flesh, he ought not on that account to have been excluded from the number of the spiritual children of Christ and their proper benefits, just as neither Abel, nor other believers not belonging to the genealogical line of Christ, such as the Prophets and countless others, were excluded from salvation.

Latin:

MAJOR SERVIET MINORI) Josephus: Φερώνυμα ἔσε- σθαι τοῖς παισὶν ἕδνη· τῶ δὲ μείζονος προτερήσειν τὸ δοκεῖν ἔλασ- σον εἶναι.

Non de personis præcipue Esavi & Jacobi, ille enim huic non servivit, sed de gentibus, ut aperte sonat oraculum, duæ gentes sunt in utero tuo, hæc ac- cipienda. Nimirum non tantum prærogativam illam Jacobi posteri habuere præ Esavi, quod illi soli in terram Canaan introducti, his montanis hor- ridis & sterilibus Idumeæ locis concessis. Sed sub- jecti etiam sunt Idumei Davidis tempore Jacobi posteris: unde perperam Calviniani ex hoc ora- culo Rom. 9. vers. 12. adducto absolutam Esavi reje- ctionem pro absoluto suo & horribili decreto sta- biliendo probant: quum uti dictum nec de Esavi persona, nec de rejectione a Salute æterna hic aga- tur; Apostolus etiam longissime alienus sit ab ab- soluta prædestinatione, imo justificationem adeoq; electionem non ex operibus, sed ex gratia fieri loco laudato doceat, ἐκ ἐξ ἔργων, ἀλλ᾽ ἐκ τῶ κα- λῶντος, quo de in Theol. Apost. Rom. ad Rom. 9.

In eo tamen prærogativam Jacobo præ Efav obtigisse, quod ex illius, non hujus lumbis seme benedictum prodierit, minime dubium est; Se hoc ad Salutem Jacobi, vel exclusionem a Salute E favi non facit: Dignitas externa est in linea Messia constitui, ad beatitudinem animæ nihil faciens, & quamvis ad Patres Christi secundum carnem non per tinuerit Efavus, a filiorum tamen Christi spirituali um numero & beneficiis eorum propriis excludi id eo non debuit, quemadmodum nec Abel, nec ali fideles ad lineam genealogicam Christi haud perti nentes, ceu sunt Prophetæ, & innumeri alii, a salute exclusi fuere.

## 25:25
HISPID) Which is a sign of a strong spirit, as noted by Aristotle and others who treat of physiognomy.

ver. 25. HE HELD HIS BROTHER'S HEEL BY THE HAND) This allegorically signifies patience. The shade of Protesilaus, as Philostratus relates, said to an athlete asking ὅ, τι πράττων ὑπερέσοιτο τῶν ἀντιπάλων, that he should be trodden upon. From that saying he discovered τὸ ἀποπτερνίζειν, עקב, whence יעקוב is the supplanter to Philo, that is, as Philo interprets, τὴν ἀρετὴν ἐκ ἀκονιτὶ κτώμενος.

Latin:

HISPIDVS) Quod fignum fortis animi notat Aristoteles & alii, qui physiognomonica tractant.

vers. 25. PLANTAM FRATRIS TENEBAT MANU) Id allegorice patientiam fignificat. Protesilai umbra, ut narrat Philostratus, athletæ roganti ὅ, τι πράττων ὑπερέσοιτο τῶν ἀν- τιπάλων, πατούμενος ἔφη. Ille ex eo dicto reperit τὸ ἀπο- πτερνίζειν, עקב, unde יעקוב ὁ πτερνιστής Philoni, id est, ut Philo interpretatur, τὴν ἀρετὴν ἐκ ἀκονιτὶ κτώμενος.

## 25:27
ver. 27. HE DWELT IN TENTS) He led a pastoral life, moving himself and his belongings now here, now there. Their characters suited their way of life. Jacob was good, as a shepherd: Esau was savage, as a hunter.

Latin:

vers. 27. HABITABAT IN TABERNACULIS) Pastora- lem vitam agebat, nunc huc, nunc illuc se & sua transferens. Ingenia conveniebant vitæ generi. Jacobus bonus, ut pastor: Efavus sævus, ut venator.

## 25:31
ver. 31. THY BIRTHRIGHT) The right of the priesthood. See Job 1:5, 42:8, Num. 3:12, 40, ch. 8:16. The right of the birthright could be lost by sinning, as we noted above at 4:7. Moreover, it was also a sin to despise a right so holy: whence Esau is called profane, Heb. 12:16. The mystical sense of this passage was not poorly explained by Philo: πρεσβύτερα μὲν φαῦλος ἡγεῖται τὰ σώματος, ὁ d' ἀσεβὴς τὰ ψυχῆς, ἃ καὶ πρὸς ἀλήθειάν ἐστιν ἐ χρόνῳ ἀλλὰ δυνάμει καὶ ἀξιώματι πρεσβύτερα καὶ πρῶτα ὄντως.

Latin:

vers. 31. PRIMOGENITA TVA) Jus sacerdotii. Vid. Job. 1,5. 42,8. Num. 3,12. 40, c. 8,16. Jus primæ genituræ amitti de- linquendo poterat, ut supra notavimus 4,7. Erat autem & hoc delictum, jus tam sanctum contemnere: unde profanus dicitur Esau Hebr. 12,16. Mysticum hujus loci sensum non male expli- cuit Philo: πρεσβύτερα μὲν φαῦλος ἡγεῖται τὰ σώματος, ὁ δ' ἀσεβὴς τὰ ψυχῆς, ἃ καὶ πρὸς ἀλήθειάν ἐστιν ἐ χρόνῳ ἀλλὰ δυνάμει καὶ ἀξιώματι πρεσβύτερα καὶ πρῶτα ὄντως.

## 25:32 Addition
To chap. 25. v. 32. AND I AM DYING p. 295. a.

If the conjecture of Lipsius is to be heard, it was the same time in which he both sold his birthright to Esau and Isaac went to Gerar, and it was the same famine which extorted the birthright from Esau and also compelled Isaac to seek a living elsewhere; but in the judgment of Estius and Rivetus, it is by no means to be thought that all food was lacking to him in his most opulent paternal family. Because, however, he had seen the pottage prepared and had smelled the aroma, he is entirely intent on obtaining it, caring nothing for the rest. The Targum Hierosolymitanum says: He went and despised the birthright, and made light of a portion of the world to come, and denied the resurrection of the dead.

Latin:

Ad cap. 25. v. 32. EN MORIOR p. 295. a.

Si Lipsoii ςοχασμὸς audiendus, tempus idem fuit, quo & Esavo vendidit primogenita, & Isaac ivit ad Gerar, eademque fuit fames, quæ Esavo primogenituram extorsit, Isaacum etiam coëgit alibi victum quærere; Sed Estio & Riveto judice, nullo modo existimandum est, ei omnem cibum defuisse in familia paterna opulentissima. Quia tamen paratam viderat offam, & nidorem senserat, totus in eo est, ut potiatur eadem, reliqua non cu- rans. Targum Hierosol. Abiit, inquit, & contemptit primogenituram, & flocci fecit partem futuri seculi, negavitque resurrectionem mortuorum.

## 26:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVI.

The promise of the land and the Messiah to Isaac in Gerar, where he said his wife was his sister, and the multiplication of his seed in Beersheba: Whence he preached in the name of the Lord, and erected a tent there, having entered into a covenant with Abimelech. Esau took Hittite wives.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVI.

Isaaco promissio terræ, & Messiæ in Gerar, ubi u xorem suam sororem dixit, & in Bersabe multiplicationis seminis facta: Unde de nomine Domini prædicavit, & taberna- culum ibi erexit fœdere cum Abimelecho inito. Esau uxores Chittæas duxit.

## 26:8
ver. 8. SPORTING WITH REBECCA HIS WIFE) παίζοντα LXX. which corresponds well to the Hebrew, that is, caressing her more freely than custom allowed toward a stranger.

vers. 8. JOCANTEM CUM REBECCA VXORE SVA) παίζοντα LXX. quod Hebræo bene respondet, id est attrectan- tem eam liberius quam mos ferebat in alienam.

## 26:10
Ver. 10. THOU HADST BROUGHT UPON US A GREAT SIN] But the LXX. [say] ἄγνοιαν, just as the Hebrew word אשם is translated in 2 Chron. 28:13, Ezek. 40:40, 42:13, 44:29, which elsewhere is πλημμέλεια, πλημμέλημα, πλημμέλησις, and sometimes ἁμαρτία. The Greek interpreters therefore restricted a sufficiently general word to that species which was being dealt with here, as if שגגה had been clearly placed.

Latin:

Vers. 10. INDVXERAS SVPER NOS GRANDE PEC- CATVM] At LXX. ἄγνοιαν, quomodo vox Hebræa אשם vertitur 2. Par. 28,13. Ezech. 40,40.42,13.44,29. quæ alibi πλημ- μέλεια, πλημμέλημα, πλημμέλησις, interdum ἁμαρτία. Vocem igitur satis generalem restrinxere Græci interpretes ad speciem eam, de qua hic agebatur, quasi plane positum esset שגגה.

## 26:11
Ver. 11. AND HE COMMANDED ALL THE PEOPLE] This the barbarians would say: he gave him a safeguard.

Latin:

Vers. 11. PRÆCEPITQVE OMNI POPVLO] Hoc Bar- bari dicerent: dedit illi salvagvardiam.

## 26:12
ver. 12. HE FOUND IN THAT SAME YEAR A HUNDREDFOLD] We showed above from Pliny that harvests in those places are sometimes returned with a hundredfold interest.

Latin:

vers. 12. INVENIT IN IPSO ANNO CENTVPLVM] Cum centesimo fœnore in illis locis messes interdum reddi ex Plinio supra ostendimus.

## 26:15
ver. 15. THEY STOPPED UP THE WELLS.

When they have done this, with what appearance of truth then do they say in verse 29, 'We have not done that which would hurt thee'? In the Hebrew, 'We have only done good with thee'? The Jesuits Cornelius and Marius say it was vain boasting. Others think that the injury of these shepherds was not known to the satraps. But these had induced the King to order Isaac to change his place, verses 16, 27. The words therefore must be understood κατὰ τὶ: because it is by no means probable that they were boasting without cause when they wished to enter into a covenant. They only mean that they received a stranger kindly, and did not offer him violence when disputes arose. Blessed Luther says in this place, Abimelech excuses himself as much as he can. He did not indeed take away his goods from Isaac, he robbed him of nothing, so that it seems a just extenuation, but yet his mind was so exasperated by his servants that he ordered Isaac to depart from the land. Otherwise, since you were a stranger, says Abimelech, in our region, we sent you away kindly and in peace, without any offense, etc.

Latin:

vers. 15. PUTEOS OBSTRUXERUNT.

Hoc quum fecerint, qua ergo veritatis specie dicunt vers. 29. Non fecimus, quod te læderet. In Ebræo, fecimus tecum duntaxat bonum? Vanam jactantiam fuisse Cornelius, & Marius, Jesuitæ ajunt. Alii Satrapis de injuriis istis Pastorum non constitisse putant. Sed hi induxerant Regem, ut juberet Isaac locum mutare vers. 16. 27. Verba er- go κατὰ τὶ intelligenda: quia gloratos ipsos præter rem fuisse, quum fœdus inire vellent, neutiquam est probabile. Id solum volunt, quod peregrinum comiter susceperint, nec exortis litibus vim ei intule- rint. Excusat se, inquit B. Lutherus in h. l. Abi- melech, quantum potest. Non quidem abstulit Isaa- co bona sua, nihil ei rapuit, adeo ut justa extenuatio vi- deatur, sed tamen per famulos animus ejus ita exacer- batus fuit, ut jusserit Isaac terra excedere. Alioqui eum esses peregrinus, inquit Abimelech, in nostra re- gione, benigne & in pace te dimisimus, absque ulla of- fensione &c.

## 26:16
verse 16. DEPART FROM US, FOR THOU ART BECOME MUCH MIGHTIER THAN WE) Ostracism. See Aristotle, Politics 3, 13.

Latin:

vers. 16. RECEDE A NOBIS, QVONIAM POTEN- TIOR NOBIS FACTVS ES VALDE) Ostracismus. Vide Aristotelem Polit. 3,13.

## 26:18
verse 18. THE SERVANTS OF HIS FATHER ABRAHAM) Thus the Samaritan, the Syriac, and the LXX, who all seem to have read עמי instead of בימי, which is sometimes translated as παῖδες, sometimes as δοῦλοι.

We have said that one interpreter followed others: just as Grotius acknowledges that the Vulgate followed the Greek interpreters. In the Hebrew it is, 'which they dug in the days of his father Abraham' בימי. We care little what he read who first substituted 'servants,' for we are scrupulous about saying here that the Hebrew reading is corrupt. Could not the exemplar which the Greeks had be corrupt somewhere? It is the not improbable opinion of some critics that the codices which the Alexandrian Jews had were not corrected, but that the most corrected ones were kept by the Jerusalemites. To others it seems likely that they made the translation not from the Hebrew, but from the Syriac text, or from the Samaritan codex. What wonder, then, if it agrees more in some places with them than with the Hebrew text?

Latin:

vers. 18. SERVI PATRIS SUI ABRAHAM) Sic Samari- tanus, Syrus LXX, qui omnes pro בימי videntur legisse עמי quod interdum παῖδες, interdum δοῦλοι vertitur.

Diximus, unum interpretem alios sequutum: uti Vulgatum Interpretes Græcos sequutum agno- scit Grotius. In Ebræo est, quos foderunt in diebus Patris ejus Abrahæ בימי. Quid legerit, qui primum servos substituit, parum curamus, quibus lectionem Ebræam corruptam hîc dicere religio est. Annon potuit exemplar, quod Græci habuere, corruptum alicubi esse? Non fuisse emendatos Codices, quos Alexandrini Judæi habuere, sed emendatissimos as- servatos penes Hierosolymitanos, Criticorum non- nullorum est sententia non improbabilis. Aliis eosdem non ex Ebræo, sed e Syriaco textu translatio- nem fecisse, aut e Samaritano Codice, verisimile videtur. Quid ergo mirum, si illis alicubi magis consonat, quam Ebræo textui?

## 26:20
Verse 20. CALUMNY) The Greeks [say] ἀδικία. That would be עשק with a Schin with a right-hand dot. But now in the Hebrew it is written with a left-hand one. It appears that those distinctions did not exist formerly.

But that does not appear from that. How much more correctly will it be said that the dot was not well placed in the codex which the Greeks had, if the error of the translation is from that, and not a παρόραμα of the interpreters? For reason of the name from the context teaches that the left-hand dot is the genuine one. Because the place was called עשק [contention] on account of the contention and litigation stirred up there. But how will the Latin 'calumnia' be saved by the Greek ἀδικία, and what has this to do with the naming of that place and the history of the text? For no mention of calumny is made there. Pagninus and Arias Montanus took it as a proper name.

Latin:

Vers. 20. CALUMNIAM) Græci ἀδικία. Id esset עשק cum Schin dextri puncti. At nunc in Hebræo sinistrum scribi- tur. Apparet ea discrimina olim non fuisse.

Id vero non apparet inde. Quanto rectius dicetur, non bene punctum collocatum in Codice, quem Græci habuere, si inde translationis error, & non παρόραμα interpretum sit? Sinistrum enim punctum genuinum esse, ratio nominis e contextu docet. Quia עשק contentio dictus est locus ob con- tentionem & litigium ibi excitatum. Quomodo vero per Græcorum ἀδικία Latini calumnia salvabi- tur, & quid hoc ad loci istius denominationem & ad historiam textus? Nullius enim calumniæ ibi facta mentio. Pagninus, & Arias Montanus accepere, ut nomen proprium.

## 26:26
verse 26. AND OCHOZATH HIS FRIEND. The Targum and Vatablus take it as an appellative. The LXX and the Vulgate, however, more correctly take it as a proper name. Vatablus therefore renders this place 'and the company of his friends,' noting however in the margin that some of the Hebrews read 'Ahuzath his friend.' The LXX explain 'friend' as ὁ νυμφαγωγός. Among the Persians, the King's paranymph was an intimate friend called Surenus, who crowned the kings and was in charge of the royal cohort consisting of the most select and friendly men.

Latin:

vers. 26. ET OCHOZAT AMICUS EJUS. Targum & Vatablus ut appellativum accipiunt. LXX. vero & Vulgatus rectius pro nomine proprio habent. Reddit ergo Vatablus h. m. cœtusq́; ami- corum ejus, ad marginem tamen observans, quod Ebræorum quidam legant, Ahuzath amicus ejus. Amicum exponunt LXX. ὁ νυμφαγωγός. Apud Per- sas Regis Paranymphus erat amicus intimus Surenus dictus, qui Reges coronabat, Regiæque cohorti ex selectissimis & amicissimis constanti præerat.

## 26:32
verse 32. WE HAVE FOUND WATER. The LXX erroneously [say], 'we have not found water': in a sense clearly contrary.

Latin:

vers. 32. INVENIMUS AQVAM. LXX. mendose, non invenimus aquam: sensu plane contrario.

## 26:33
verse 33. ABUNDANCE) Here also the Latin reads a left-hand Schin, but the Greeks a right-hand one, as the Hebrew codices now have: for they read ὅρκος φρέαρ, so that as above in 24, it is a name κατὰ πρόληψιν. The same name for a like reason [is given] to the other place above 21, 33. באר a well: whence Stephanus makes the name Berytus, and Hesychius from him.

Thus he asserts that the Greek codices sometimes agreed with the modern Hebrew ones, and sometimes disagreed, just as it pleases him: as if the only cause of the diversity of interpreters were a variant reading, and there were no παροράματα of the interpreters. Which he ought to have noticed here in the Vulgate, rather than to indulge in his own suspicions, by which the purity of the Hebrew text is troubled. Because it is manifest that that name was given to the place from the oath in verse 3, which is called שבועה by the Hebrews with a right-hand dot, not from abundance. The reading of the Vulgate must therefore be corrected here. He who below in XLVI, 1 and elsewhere said 'well of the oath,' not 'of abundance.'

Latin:

vers. 33. ABUNDANTIAM) Hic quoque Latinus legit Schin sinistrum, at Græci dextrum, ut Hebræi codices nunc ha- bent: legerunt enim ὅρκος φρέαρ, ut supra 24. sit nomen κατὰ πρόληψιν. Idem nomen ex pari causa loco alteri supra 21, 33. באר puteus: unde Beryto nomen facit Stephanus, & ex eo Hesychius.

Ita modo Græcorum Codices consensisse cum modernis Ebræis asserit, modo discrepasse, prout ipsi placet: quasi diversitatis interpretum una cau- sa sit varia lectio, nulla vero interpretum sint παρο- ράματα. Quod hic in Vulgato potius advertere debuisset, quam suspicionibus suis indulgere, qui- bus Ebræi textus puritas sollicitatur. Quia mani- festum est, a juramento nomen id datum loco e v. 3. quod שבועה Ebræis cum puncto dextro dicitur, nõ ab abundantia. Corrigenda ergo hic Vulgati lectio. Qui infra XLVI, 1. & alias puteum juramenti dixit, non abundantiæ.

## 26:35
Verse 35. THEY HAD OFFENDED THE MIND OF ISAAC AND REBECCA) Because they abhorred the doctrine of piety.

Bb 4

Latin:

Vers. 35. OFFENDERANT ANIMUM ISAAC ET RE- BECCÆ) Quod abhorrerent a doctrina pietatis.

Bb 4

## 27:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVII. Jacob snatches away the blessing from Esau.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVII. Jacob benedictionem præripit Esavo.

## 27:15
ver. 15. WITH THE VERY GOOD GARMENTS OF ESAU.] From this passage, says Jerome in the Hebrew traditions, the Hebrews hand down that the firstborn performed the office of priests and possessed a priestly garment, clothed in which they offered victims to GOD before Aaron was chosen for the priesthood.

Latin:

verf. 15. VESTIBUS ESAU VALDE BONIS.] EX hoc loco, inquit Hieron. in traditione He- braic. tradunt Hebræi primogenitos functos fuisse officio Sacerdotum & habuisse vestimentum Sacerdota- le, quo induti DEO victimas offerebant antequam Aa- ron in Sacerdotium eligeretur.

## 27:27
Ver. 27. FULL] This word seems to have fallen out of the Hebrew Codices. For it is in the Greek, and in the Samaritan, and in the old Syriac, as Diodorus reports. Pliny, book XVII, ch. V, treating of the earth: And when it has been moistened by rain after continuous dryness, then it emits that divine breath of its own conceived from the sun, to which no sweetness can be compared.

But here a pleonasm abounds: For what is a field, which the Lord has blessed, other than a full field? It was added, therefore, in those [versions], as Interpreters are wont to add words for the sake of a fuller explanation, not always rendering word for word. We have spoken once about the Samaritan and Syriac text. There is no reason for Grotius to exalt himself so much over them, if he cannot otherwise bring aid to the Vulgate. Whoever desires more about those Codices will be able to consult Hottinger in his Thesaurus Philologicus.

Latin:

Verf. 27. PLENI) Hæc vox ex Hebræis Codicibus excidisse videtur. Est enim & in Græco & in Samaritano & in Syriaco veteri, referente Diodoro. Plinius lib. XVII. c. V. de terra a- gens : Et cum a ficcitate continua immaduerit imbre, tunc emit- tit illum suum halitum divinum ex sole conceptum, cui compara- ti suavitas nulla possit.

Sed hîc pleonasmus abundat : Quid enim ager, cui benedixit Dominus, aliud quam ager plenus? Additum ergo in illis, uti solent Interpp. uberioris explicationis gratia quandoq; addere voces, non semper κατὰ πόδα reddere. Diximus semel de Samaritano, & Syriaco textu. Non est, quod illis tantopere se efferat Grotius, si Vulgatæ alias sup- petias ferre non possit. Qui plura de illis Codici- bus desiderat, Hottingerum in thesauro Philolog. conferre poterit.

## 27:29
ver. 29. LET PEOPLES SERVE THEE] The Edomites. AND LET TRIBES ADORE THEE] In the Hebrew, leummim. The Chaldean [translates]: Kingdoms. The LXX: rulers. The kingdoms of Arabia and Syria born from Hagar, Keturah, Laban. HE WHO SHALL CURSE THEE, LET HIM BE CURSED] Like Balaam. AND HE WHO SHALL BLESS THEE, LET HIM BE FILLED WITH BLESSINGS] Like Moses. ver. 40. WHEN THOU SHALT SHAKE OFF AND LOOSE HIS YOKE] For the fulfillment, see 1 Kings 8:20. The Hebrews note, however, that this was the will of God following, because at that time the Israelites had shaken off the yoke of the law.

Latin:

verf. 29. SERVIANT TIBI POPULI] Idumæi. ET ADORENT TE TRIBUS) In Hebræo לאמים. Regna Chaldæus : LXX. ἄρχοντες. Regna Arabiæ & Syriæ or- ta ex Agate, Cethura, Labano. QVI MALEDIXERIT TIBI, SIT ILLE MALEDICTUS] Ut Balaam. ET QVI BENEDIXERIT TIBI, BENEDICTIONIBUS REPLEATVR) Vt Moses. verf. 40. CVM EXCVTIAS ET SOLVAS JVGVME- JVS) Implementum vide 1. Reg. 8, 20. Notant autem Hebræi hanc fuisse voluntatem Dei ἐπομένην, ideo quod eo tempore Israelitæ excussissent jugum legis.

## 28:1 Argument
PART V. OF GENESIS. HISTORY OF JACOB. CHAPTER XXVIII. The Ladder of Heaven.

Latin:

PARS V. GENESEOS. HISTO- RIA JACOBI. CAPUT XXVIII. Scala Cœli.

## 28:10
vers. 10. AND HE CALLED THE NAME OF THE CITY BETHEL.

The Hebrews, Lyranus, and others [say] that Bethel was Moriah and the city of Jerusalem: But as Abulensis and Adrichomius note, it was distant from there about 18 miles. For Bethel was situated in the tribe of Ephraim near Sichem, in which, as also in Dan, as the extreme limits of his land, Jeroboam erected golden calves, abusing for the purpose of persuading the people the example of Jacob, who erected a statue there.

Latin:

vers. 10. APPELLAVITQUE NOMEN UR- BIS BETHEL.

Ebræi, Lyranus, & alii Bethel fuisse Moria & urbem Jerusalem: Sed ea notante Abulensi & Adri- chomio 18. circiter miliaribus inde distabat. Bethel enim in tribu Ephraim sita erat juxta Sichem, in qua uti & in Dan, ceu extremis terræ suæ limitibus Jero- boam vitulos aureos erexit, abusus ad persuaden- dum populo exemplo Jacobi, qui ibi statuam ere- xit.

## 28:12
ver. 12. AND HE SAW IN DREAMS A LADDER STANDING UPON THE EARTH, AND ITS TOP TOUCHING HEAVEN] A similar dream is in the third of Aristides' Sacred Orations: in which there were ladders separating what is under the earth and above the earth, and on both sides the power of God. ANGELS ALSO OF GOD] Who are the four winds, Zech. 6. ASCENDING AND DESCENDING] Receiving and executing commands. Cf. John 1:51.

Grotius is not consistent with himself. For if the winds of Zech. VI, which he wishes to designate four empires there, are understood here, how will that agree with this vision of the Patriarch, or the explanation of Christ in John I? Where it is manifest that the angels are understood as the ministering spirits. And Grotius himself acknowledges that such angels are to be understood here.

Latin:

verf. 12. VIDITQUE IN SOMNIIS SCALAM STAN- TEM SUPER TERRAM, ET CACVMEN ILLIVS TAN- GENS COELVM) Simile somnium apud Aristiden sacrarum orationum tertio : ἐν οἷς ἅτε δὴ κλίμακες ἦσαν αἳ τὸ ὑπὸ γῆς κ ὑπὲρ γῆς ἀφορίζουσαι, καὶ ἑκατέρωθι κράτΘ- τοῦ Θεῦ. ANGELOS QVOQVE DEI) Qui quatuor venti Zach. 6. ASCENDENTES ET DESCENDENTES) Mandata accipientes & exequentes. Conf. Joh. 1, 51.

NOn constat sibi Grot. Nam si venti Zach. VI. quos ibi vult imperia quatuor designare, hic intelligantur, quomodo id congruet huic vision Patriarchæ, vel explicationi Christi Joh. I. Ub Angelos τὰ πνεύματα λειτουργικὰ intelligi manife stum est. Et agnoscit ipse Grotius tales Angelo hîc intelligendos esse.

## 28:13
ver. 13. AND THE LORD LEANING UPON THE LADDER] A more distinguished Angel, who was representing the person of God.

If it is permitted to pervert Scripture in this way, who finally will remain certain in it? Moses said JEHOVAH was leaning upon the ladder; Grotius, a more distinguished Angel representing the Person of GOD. Moses did not say this alone: He himself who was seen leaning upon the ladder testified: I am the Lord of Abraham thy Father, the GOD of Isaac, and he described himself at length, so that it could be a doubt to no one that it was the Lord who was seen here. Is some more distinguished Angel the GOD of Abraham, the GOD of Isaac? Is it the work of an Angel to give land by his own authority to peoples? Is this the speech of an Angel, And I will be thy keeper, whithersoever thou shalt go, and I will bring thee into this land, nor will I forsake thee, until I have fulfilled all things which I have said to thee? Jacob also acknowledged that the Lord was present with him, not a mere angel, Truly the Lord is in this place, and I knew it not; and he made a vow to this Lord, that he wished to acknowledge and worship the same as his GOD. Would he have done that to an Angel? The presentation of such a person is Comical: it has no place in Sacred histories. God does not give his honor to another, nor his name. Is. XLII, 8. Which was deduced in Vol. II in Augustinus against the Socinians. The Chaldean here mixes the Word of the Lord, ver. 20. If the WORD OF THE LORD shall be for my help, the WORD OF THE LORD shall be for me as GOD; which ought to be accepted concerning the hypostatic Word. For the uttered word is not for us as GOD. Concerning the top of the ladder, it is held in the Chaldaic Paraphrase that the glory of the Lord stood upon it. Who is the glory of the Lord, if not the Word? Heb. 1:3. We do not disagree, however, that the Holy Trinity was seen by Jacob, provided that from the Lord a Minister is not formed, and from GOD an angel representing the person of GOD.

Latin:

verf. 13. ET DOMINVM INNIXVM SCALÆ) Insignio rem Angelorum, qui Dei personam referebat.

Si ita pervertere licet Scripturam, qui tandem certi in ea supererit? Moses JEHO VAM dixit innixum Scalæ; Grotius insignio rem Angelum DEI Personam referentem. Ne id Moses solum dixit: testatus est ipse ille, q innixus scalæ visus est : Ego sum Dominus A brahæ Patris tui DEUS, Ifaaci DEUS, ac prolixe se descripsit, ut nulli dubium esse posset, Dominum es- se, qui hîc visus. Num Angelus aliquis insignior DEUS Abrahæ, DEUS Ifaaci? Num Angeli est ter- ram dare αὐτεξυσίως populis? Num hæc oratio An- geli, Et ero custos tuus, quocunq; perrexeris, & indu- cam te in terram hanc, nec dimittam, nisi complevero u- niversa, quæ dixi tibi? Agnovit etiam Jacob Domi- num sibi præsto fuisse, non angelum ψιλὸν, Vere Dominus est in illo loco, & ego nesciebam; ac votum fecit huic Domino, quod eundem agnoscere & co- lere velit, ceu DEUM suum. Num id fecisset Ange- lo? Præsentatio talis personæ Comica est: in Sacris historiis locum non habet. Deus alteri honorem su- um non dat, neq; nomen suum. Ef. XLII, 8. Quod fu- se Tom. II. in August. Conf. adversus Socinianos di- ductum. Chaldæus hîc miscet Verbum Domini vers. 20. Si fuerit VERBUM DOMINI in adjutori- um meum, erit mihi VERBUM DOMINI in DEUM; quæ de λογῳ ὑποσατικῷ accipi oportet. Verbum enim πϱοφοϱικὸν nobis non est in DEUM. De summitate scalæ in Chaldaica Paraphrasi habetur, quod gloria Domini in ea steterit. Quis Domini gloria, nisi ὁ λόγος? Ebr. 1, 3. Non refragamur tamen, S. S. Trinitatem visam Jacobo, modo ne e Domino Minister, e DEO angelus, personam DEI referens efformetur.

## 28:14
Vers. eod. AND THY SEED SHALL BE AS THE DUST OF THE EARTH) Hecataeus rightly calls the nation of the Jews πολυανθρωπότατον (most populous).

Latin:

Vers. eod. ERITQUE SEMEN TUUM QUASI PULVIS TERRÆ) Gentem Judæorum πολυανθρωπότατον vocat Hæ- cataus merito.

## 28:18
vers. 18. HE SET IT UP FOR A PILLAR] In the manner of a column. Such stones erected or heaped up were at that time used for an altar. See below 31, 46.

POURING OIL UPON THE TOP OF IT) A custom of those places, which also reached the Greeks. Clement of Alexandria, Strom. VII: πάντα λίθον, τὸ δὴ λεγόμενον, λιπαρὸν προσκυνῶντες (worshipping every stone, as the saying is, that is anointed with oil). In the first book of the Florida of Apuleius: A stone smeared with ointment. Arnobius, book I: If ever I caught sight of a lubricated stone, and one set in order with olive ointment, as if a present power were in it, I would flatter it. Minucius: To stumble against stones fashioned and anointed and crowned.

Latin:

vers. 18. EREXIT IN TUMULUM] Columnæ in morem. Tales lapides erecti tau congesti tunc erant pro altari. Vide infra 31, 46.

FVNDENTES OLEUM DESUPER) Mos illorum loco- rum, qui & ad Græcos devenit. Clemens Alexandrinus Strom. VII. πάντα λίθον, τὸ δὴ λεγόμενον, λιπαρὸν προσκυνῶντες. Primo Floridorum Apuleii: Lapis unguine delibutus. Arno- bius lib. I. Si quando conspexeram lubricatum Lapidem, & ex olivi unguine ordinatum, tanquam ineffet vis præsens adulabar. Minutius: In lapides impingere effigiatos fane & unctos & coro- natos.

## 28:19
vers. 19. BETHEL] Hence the Βαιτύλια (Baetylia) among the Phoenicians. See Philo of Byblos in Eusebius.

WHICH WAS CALLED LUZ BEFORE) He took אולם as a mere affirmation, as did Aquila. But the LXX and others [took it] as part of the name: καὶ ὐλαμλεὺζ ἦν ὄνομα τῇ πόλει τὸ πρότερον (and Ulam-Luz was the name of the city before). That is, the portico of the nut trees. Below it is called only Luz, 35, 5.

Latin:

vers. 19. BETHEL] Hinc Βαιτύλια apud Phœnicas. Vide Philonem Byblium in Eusebio.

QUÆ PRIVS LUZA VOCABATUR) Accepit אולם pro mera affirmatione, ut & Aquila. At LXX. & alii pro parte nominis: καὶ ὐλαμλεὺζ ἦν ὄνομα τῇ πόλει τὸ πρότερον. id est, porticus nucum. Infra Luza tantum dicitur 35, 5.

## 28:20
vers. 20. IF GOD WILL BE WITH ME) If He will be a help to me, as the Chaldean rightly explains. See what [is said] at Matt. 28, 20.

AND WILL GIVE ME BREAD TO EAT, AND RAIMENT TO PUT ON) That is, even if I have nothing beyond those things which are necessary for nature.

Latin:

vers. 20. SI FUERIT DEUS MECUM] Si auxilio mihi fuerit, ut recte exponit Chaldæus. Vide quæ ad Matth. 28, 20.

ET DEDERIT MIHI PANEM AD VESCENDUM, ET VESTIMENTUM AD INDUENDUM) Id est, etiamsi nihil habeam præter ea, quæ naturæ sunt neceffaria.

## 29:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIX. The marriage of Jacob with the daughters of Laban.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIX. Nuptia Jacobi cum filiabus Laban.

## 29:8
vers. 8. AND WE WILL ROLL THE STONE FROM THE WELL'S MOUTH) They shall roll it, namely the shepherds. Thus the LXX: ἀποκυλίσουσι (they shall roll away).

Compare Mark 16:3, where the same word ἀποκυλίσει [is used]. It was too heavy to be moved by women.

The Vulgate is correctly corrected. But how could Jacob alone remove the stone? To some it seems that this was done by joining efforts with the shepherds: but it is more correctly ascribed to his remarkable strength in the prime of his age, which he wished to demonstrate in this way.

Latin:

vers. 8. ET AMOVEAMUS LAPIDEM DE ORE PU- TEI) Amoveant, scilicet pastores. Sic LXX. ἀποκυλίσουσι.

Confer Marcum 16,3. ubi idem verbum ἀποκυλίσει. Gravius id erat, quam ut a fœminis præstaretur.

REcte corrigitur Vulgata. Quî vero solus Jacob amovere potuit lapidem? Nonnullis videtur, quod conjunctis cum pastoribus operis id factum: sed rectius id adscribitur insigni ejus robori in ἀκμῇ ætatis: quod ita demonstrare voluerit.

## 29:14
verse 14. YOU ARE MY BONE AND MY FLESH) A blood relative. See what [is said] above [at] 2:23.

Latin:

vers. 14. OS MEUM ES ET CARO MEA) Propinquus sanguine. Vid. quæ supra 2,23.

## 29:24
verse 24. WHEN JACOB HAD ENTERED TO HER ACCORDING TO CUSTOM.

By those words, 'according to custom,' Franciscus Haraeus in his scholia on this passage wishes to imply how Jacob did not recognize Leah until morning was made: because, namely, according to custom, the bride was brought to the groom with a veiled face for the sake of modesty, whence 'nuptiae' [weddings] comes from 'nubendo' [veiling]. But those words 'according to custom' are not held in the original text: nor is it certain whether that custom was accepted there at that time. Laban, however, abused the benefit of the darkness for this fraud. But what is to be thought about that substitution and about Jacob's marriage, we have said in our commentary on this passage: Laban sinned voluntarily and fraudulently by promoting incest, Leah by imprudently submitting herself, Jacob by not dismissing Leah once the fraud was known. We have recalled Grotius's opinion concerning the celibacy of sisters for censure in that same place. There is, therefore, no reason for us to do what has already been done.

Latin:

vers. 24. AD QUAM CUM EX MORE JA- COB FUISSET INGRESSUS.

Verbis illis, ex more Franciscus Haræus in Schol. ad h. l. innui vult, quomodo Jacob non agnoverit Leam nisi facto mane: quia sc. ex more sponsa obve- lata facie ad totum traducta pudoris causa, unde nu- ptiæ a nubendo. Sed illa ex more in textu originali non habentur: nec an mos ille tum istic receptus fuerit constat. Abusus autem beneficio tenebrarum ad hanc fraudem Labanus. Quid vero de illa sub- stitutione, & de matrimonio Jacobi habendum, di- ximus in Comment. ad h. l. peccavit Laban volunta- rie & fraudulenter incestum promovendo, Lea im- prudenter se submittendo, Jacobus Leam fraude cognita non dimittendo. Grotii de sororum ἀγα- μίᾳ sententiam ad censuram revocavimus l. c. Non est ergo, quod actum agamus.

## 29:26
verse 26. FULFILL THE WEEK OF THE DAYS OF THIS UNION) Seven days dedicated to nuptial joy, according to the custom of those regions, Judges 14:15.

Latin:

vers. 26. IMPLE HEBDOMADAM DIERUM HVJVS COPVLÆ) Dies septem nuptiali lætitiæ dicatos, ex more il- larum regionum Jud. 14, 15.

## 29:27
AND I WILL GIVE YOU THIS ONE ALSO] With a new nuptial feast after those seven days, but under the condition of seven years of labor.

Josephus indeed thinks that Jacob married Rachel only after the second seven-year period of service was completed. But that contradicts the text. Compare verse 30.

Latin:

ET HANC QVOQVE DABO TIBI] Cum novo convi- vio nuptiali post illos septem dies, sed sub lege operarum se- ptennii.

Josephus quidem putat, quod Jacobus demum post secundum septennium servitii exactum duxerit Rahelem. Sed id repugnat textui. Conf. v. 30.

## 29:32
verse 32. NOW MY HUSBAND WILL LOVE ME) For this reason the Latins call children 'pignora' [pledges].
