Id vero argutum nimis est, quod e voce פסח eruitur, ut vult Rivetus, quod notet subsilire, & de transitu illo tunc accipienda sit, quo e pluribus quædam prætere- untur, & ea non attingendo transiliuntur, quod deinde eo abripit, ut figat in illo figni rationem, agnum esse vel significare ejusmodi transilitionem & Pascha hic accipi de transitu, quo transilieban- tur ædes Ifraelitarum. Non enim פסח femper ejus- modi transitum & præteritionem notat, qua non- nulla transiliuntur. Vid. 1. Reg. 18, 20. Ef. 30, 5. & derivatur inde nomen פסח claudus, qui certe a transiliendo per intervalla dictus non est. Neque transilitio illa per agni manducationem, nedum per feftinationem manducationis fignificabatur: nuspiam certe in illa manducatione aut festinatione hæc significandi ratio constituitur. Mactatio signum erat mactationis Christi 1. Cor. 5, 7. manducatio non signum transitus, sed medium sacramentalis perceptionis Christi veri agni, pro nobis mactan- di. Postium aspersio sanguine agni facta figura erat illinendi sanguine Christi postes cordis: quam etsi signum & transilitionis Domini sive præteritionis ædium illitarum fuisse, non negamus, non tamen id ad hanc propositionem, transitus ipse Domino, quicquam facit, quasi ista significandi ratio per eundem tradita sit, quia ibi in subjecto, cum propo- sitionem inde efformant Calviniani, non est san- guis agni postibus ædium illitus, sed agnus come- dendus, quam vocem e verbis immediate præce- dentibus ipsi eruunt, & in hac propositione pro subjecto adstruunt. Neque convenit inter Calvi- nianos, in quonam analogia signi ad signatum poni hic debeat inter agnum & transitum sive transitio- nem, quod a variis diverse explicari & quibusdam eam ad manducationis festinationem referenti- bus, aliis ad aliud, Rivetus refert. Sed ipse nescit, ubi pedem figere debeat, omnes in id consentire ait, quod instituta fuerit hæc ceremonia in memoriam transitus illius vers. 25. 26. & 27. ut hoc sensu in- telligenda sit propositio: agnus est transitus; id est, agnus est signum memoriale transitus. Sed non quæ- ritur de ceremonia deinceps instituta in memo- riam transitus, quod demum factum est infra ver- sibus cit. 25. 26. sed de propositione illa, quæ ha- betur vers. 11. est enim Phase Domini. Porro quia transitus ille nondum factus fuerat in prima illa enunciatione, quomodo dici poterat, agnus ille est signum memoriale transitus: quod cum inconve- niens esse videat Rivetus, jam immutat illam propositionem, & EST præsentis in verbum fu- turi temporis pervertit: erit vobis agnus ille transi- tus, id est, significabit vobis & in memoriam revoca- bit transilitionem. Verum ita non de hac prima enunciatione, nec de his præsentibus verbis Domi- ni, sed de subsecuto festo paschali sermo erit, quid nempe temporibus sequentibus religio festi Pa- schatos signifi catura sit, ut habetur vers. 27. præ- terea illic alia habetur propositio, nim. hæc: victi- ma transitus Domini est, de qua non est quæstio, si- quidem in hac: est Phase Domini, metonymiam suam sacramentariam quærunt Calviniani. Sic er- go illud, in quo omnes consentire ait Rivetus, ipse de- serit, & meliorem se explicationem allaturum confidit e vers. 13. erit vobis sanguis agni in signum; hæc enim verba, inquit, explicant præcedentia & locutionem figuratam mutant in propriam. Sed quo- modo hæc verba exegetica haberi possunt, cum aliud plane hic sit subjectum, nimirum sanguis, aliud item prædicatum: erit in signum, neque transitus mentio in hac propositione fiat. Et quid opus est, ut hæc locutio in propriam mutetur, cum nihil im- proprietatis in ea contineatur; cum enim dico, transitus hic est transitus Domini, nullus tropo re- linquitur locus, nulla Metonymia obtinet. Instat Rivetus, conferendo propositionem Gen. 17, 10. ubi de circumcisione dicitur: hoc est pactum meum: quam propositionem postea vers. 11. sic explicari censet: & erit in signum fœderis, atque hinc con- cludit, in h. l. pariter ἰσοδυναμῦντα esse: agnus est transitus, id est, confirmabit fidem vestram de transi- litione promissa. Verum fallitur in eo, quod illam propositionem, hoc est pactum meum, pro impro- pria & figurata habeat, cum circumcisio citra tro- pum, proprie pactum sit & fœdus gratiæ, non tan- tum signum sit fœderis: fallitur in eo quoque, quod altera propositio: Et erit in signum fœderis, habea- tur pro exegetica, cum diversa plane sit; nam & pa- ctum dicitur circumcisio, quia ὁλικῶς consideratur, integrum nempe sacramentum circumcisionis, & signum dicitur fœderis, qua μερικῶς spectatur, ra- tione externæ amputationis præputii. Fallitur de- nique in eo, quod illas propositiones de circum- cisione, cum hisce confert, de agno Paschali; siqui- dem maxime diversæ sint. Nam in priori transitus ipse Domini, non ipse agnus Paschalis, aut sacra- mentum integrum agni Paschalis; sed transitus ille explicatur, ejusque velocitas & festinatio, ac causa ejusdem declaratur; in posteriori sanguis quidem agni signum transitus non incommode di- citur, sed quid hoc ad circumcisionem, qua est si- gnum fœderis; siquidem sanguis agni non tam ad ipsam sacramenti substantiam, quam ad παρα- σκευὴν pertinuerit, aut ad sacrificium prævium Sa- cramento, ut nonnulli explicant: ac signum transi- tus dicatur, quod fidem de transitione confirma- rit, de quo postea. Unde illatio Riveti nulla est, cum ita concludit: Ergo sanguis agni est signum, transitus Dei est res signata, & tamen agnus vel agni sanguis dicitur transitus; atque ita res significata di- citur de signo. Dicit quidem ipse, nihil clarius dici posse, nec aptius exemplum proferri sacramen- talis illius locutionis, hoc est, metonymiæ sacramen- tariæ. Sed ubi vel agnus vel agni sanguis dicitur transitus? Nuspiam id monstrabitur. Tum si agnus hoc in loco transitus dicitur, ut communi- ter contendunt Reformati, quomodo ergo sub- stituitur jam loco agni sanguis agni? Convincamus Rivetum ex Riveto ipso. Id enim, juxta ipsum, signum transitus dicitur h. l. quod jussi sunt comedere Israelitæ: at agnum, non autem sanguinem agni jussi sunt comedere; Ergo. Manifestum itaque est, quod Rivetus cogatur confundere agnum manducan- dum cum sanguine agni, quo postes erant illi- nendi. Denique cum aspersio illa postium san- guine agni non semper facta fuerit in celebratio- ne paschatos, & manducatione agni paschalis, jux- ta Riveti sententiam; ergo tum celebrari, juxta eundem, non potuisset sacramentum, quod sine analogia sacramenti propria locum juxta Calvi- nianos non habet, aut non quærenda erit illa ana- logia inter sanguinem agni & transilitionem. Si in- stes, quodnam ergo sit subjectum in hac propositione: est Phase Domini? Resp. Supponi in hac quæ- stione, propositionem hic haberi integram, & EST tertii adjecti, ut vocant; quod si maxime id admittamus, supplenda erit propositio ea ratione, ut fieri oportet in aliis demonstrativis, h. m. ille transitus est transitus Domini percussuri sc. Ægy- ptum, vos autem sospitaturi, ubi manifestum est, nullum tropum, nullam metonymiam locum ha- bere. Novissime observandum, quod ipsimet Zwinglii discipuli explicationem istam repro- bent, quotquot sc. malunt in prædicato proposi- tionum sacramentalium tropum collocandum es- se, quam in verbo substantivo EST, quæ hodie præ- cipuorum est sententia; ut taceam, quod agnoscant nonnulli, copulam non esse capacem tropi, id quod pluribus demonstratum dedimus in Stereom. con- tra Berg. p. 124.

## 12:12
Vers. 12. AGAINST ALL THE GODS OF EGYPT.

Which is rightly explained by the Hebrews concerning the idols of the Egyptians, with the agreement of Jerome and Eusebius in book 9 of the Praeparatio Evangelica, last chapter, with which Isaiah 19:1 may be compared. However, how the Lord executed this judgment against the idols of the Egyptians is not equally certain. The Hebrews say that stone idols were crushed into dust, wooden ones rotted or reduced to ashes, but metallic ones were melted down and liquefied, which we leave in its own place; the thing itself is certain, that the idols of the Egyptians were struck by divine judgment, just as happened to Dagon, the god of the Philistines. But Scripture says nothing about the manner. Rivet’s gloss, however, is too far-fetched and inappropriate, that the judgment of God exerted upon the gods of Egypt was mediate, insofar as he showed, by afflicting all their worshippers in various ways, how vain, fallacious, and destitute of all power to bring help they were, and also immediate, when the very animals which the Egyptians worshipped religiously were given over to slaughter. For here the judgment of God against the gods of the Egyptians is clearly distinguished from the striking of the Egyptians themselves and their cattle, or from the judgment which was exercised against the Egyptians and their cattle.

Latin:

Vers. 12. IN OMNIBUS DIIS ÆGYPTI.

Quod ab Hebræis recte de idolis Ægyptiorum exponitur, annuente Hieronymo & Eusebio lib. 9. de præpar. Evang. cap. ult. quocum conferri poterit Es. 19, 1. Quomodo autem hoc judicium Dominus exuerit adversus idola Ægyptiorum, non æque certum est. Hebræi dicunt, idola lapidea fuisse comminuta in pulverem, lignea putrefacta, aut in cinerem redacta, metallica vero resoluta & liquefacta, quod nos suo relinquimus loco; res ipsa constat, idola Ægyptiorum judicio divino percussa esse, quale Dagon Philistæorum Deo contigit. De modo autem nihil perhibet scriptura. Nimis vero remota, & inconveniens est Riveti glossa, judicium Dei in Ægypti Deos exertum fu- isse mediate, quatenus eorum cultores omnes va- riis modis affligendo ostendit, quam vani essent, fallaces, & vi omni ferendæ opis destituti, nec non immediate, cum animalia ipsa, quæ Ægyptii religio- se colebant: internecioni data sunt. Nam distingui- tur hic aperte judicium Dei adversus Deos Ægy- ptiorum a percussione ipsorum Ægyptiorum & pecorum eorum, vel a judicio, quod adversus Ægy- ptios & pecora ipsorum exercitum fuit.

## 12:13
Ver. 13. IT SHALL BE FOR A SIGN UNTO YOU.

Although the Lord says that he will see that sign, and upon seeing it will pass over the houses, he wished to give this sign not for himself, but for the Israelites, so that they might indeed be confirmed regarding their liberation and immunity from the plague. Therefore he says: it shall be FOR A SIGN UNTO YOU. By faith, therefore, they were bound to embrace this promise of liberation, and in this faith they were confirmed by this sign, the blood, which they themselves, by divine ordinance, accompanied by this promise, smeared upon the doorposts: for as truly as that blood was exposed to the sight of the passing Lord, so truly would they be immune from his plague; nor were they made more certain only of this liberation, but even primarily of the spiritual liberation of Christ, whose blood terrifies Satan, lest he dare to touch the faithful, as being he through whom we have been redeemed from his power Col. 1, 7. and whose empire has been destroyed Heb. 2, 14. because the Paschal lamb was a type of Christ, as the Apostle testifies 1. Cor. 5, 7. and therefore the faith of Moses is celebrated, to which the faith of other faithful Israelites was twin, namely that he himself performed the Passover through faith, and that shedding of blood, so that he who was destroying the firstborn might not touch them, Heb. 11, 28. For what is that faith, of which the Apostle speaks there, if not faith in the Messiah, to whose constancy he exhorts the Hebrews, by the example of the faithful of old, by which indeed Christ is regarded, as being he who endured the cross for us, that he might be ἀρχηγὸς καὶ τελειωτὴς the beginner, author, and finisher of our faith chap. 12, 1.

The end, therefore, of the sacrament of the Paschal lamb is gathered from this to be not a bare signification, but a true and actual enjoyment, not only of liberation from the striking angel, made through the intervention of the blood of the Paschal lamb, but primarily from the power of Satan, through the blood of Christ, the true lamb, who takes away the sins of the world, because the faithful Israelites were confirmed by this sacrament, that they would be liberated from the captivity of Satan by the Lamb of God as certainly as they were to be liberated from the servitude of Egypt and the slaughter of the striking angel by the lamb being slaughtered and eaten. Rivet does not deny this end; indeed, he places it beyond controversy that Christ was the principal scope of that sacrament, and that this was the primary end proposed by faith, that the faithful might acknowledge that they were to be redeemed from the servitude of sin and death through the Messiah who was to come, and that for this reason Christ is called the lamb, and is often signified by the name of the lamb. See his Commentary on this passage, p. 221. The ancients seek here also the figure of the cross, because indeed the lintel resting upon both doorposts had to be stained with the blood of the lamb, which exhibited the figure of the cross: concerning which see Cyprian, book 2, testimonies against the Jews, ch. 22. And this was the reason why none were admitted to this sacrament unless they were circumcised, because, namely, the enjoyment of that benefit of Christ is proper only to the circumcised, and the grace which the Israelites had received in circumcision was sealed to them in the Paschal lamb. Nor is there any doubt that the Apostle looks to that enjoyment when he says in 1 Cor. 5, 7: therefore let us keep the feast, because Christ our passover is sacrificed for us, because indeed the Israelites were able to enjoy the benefits of this true lamb through faith in the Paschal Sacrament, and for that reason pass the feast with joy, even though they had only the typical lamb: how much more, therefore, do we enjoy the same, who have that true Lamb of God. Add that the sacrament of the Supper has succeeded into the place of the Paschal lamb; as therefore in that we truly enjoy the benefits of Christ, which he acquired for us by his death, so also the faithful Israelites were able to enjoy the same, through faith in the Messiah, whom the Paschal lamb figured to them. Finally, the tradition of the ancient Hebrews contributes to this, which Fagius and Eugubinus in Exod. 12, as also Masius in ch. 5 of Joshua, p. 92, bring forward from the Talmudic Tractate Rosch Haschana, which teaches not obscurely that the faith of the ancient Hebrews was the same, insofar as they believed that on the same day that liberation was once made by Moses from Egypt, on that same day, i.e., the first day of unleavened bread, the people of Israel would be redeemed by the Messiah. Wherefore there was not lacking in this sacrament the heavenly matter, which is required for every sacrament, since a spiritual effect does not belong to an earthly thing by itself; the earthly element or earthly matter in this sacrament was the roasted lamb with the prior sprinkling of blood, since the eating or drinking of the same was forbidden by the ancient law, Gen. 9, 4. But the heavenly matter was Christ, the lamb sacrificed for us, about to shed his blood, 1 Cor. 5, 7. See more concerning this sacrament in B. Gerhard, in Loc. Com., and in the Mysteriosophia of the learned D. Dannhauer, Sect. 2, art. 2, who here presents a διατύπωσιν, and a comparison of the Paschal lamb with its antitype in the New Testament.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ERIT VOBIS IN SIGNUM.

Etsi dicat Dominus se visurum id signum, eo- que viso transiturum ædes, non sibi tamen, sed Israe- litis hoc signum dare voluit, ut nempe ipsi confir- marentur de liberatione & immunitate a plaga. Ideo dicit: erit VOBIS in signum. Fide ergo de- buere hanc promissionem liberationis amplecti, & in hac fide confirmabantur per hoc signum, san- guinem, quem ipsimet ex ordinatione divina, hac promissione stipata illinebant postibus: quam ve- re sc. sanguis ille patebat adspectui transeuntis Do- mini, tam vere se immunes ab ipsius plaga fore; neq; tantum de hac liberatione certiores reddebantur, sed vel imprimis de liberatione spirituali Christi, cujus sanguis terret Satanam, ne ausit fideles attin- gere, utpote per quem e potestate ejus redemti su- mus Col. 1, 7. destructumque ejus est imperium Ebr. 2, 14. quia agnus Paschalis typus fuit Christi, teste Apostolo 1. Cor. 5, 7. ideoque celebratur Mosis fi- des, cui gemina fuit fides aliorum Israelitarum fi- delium, quod nempe ipse Pascha peregerit per fidem, & effusionem illam sanguinis, ne qui perimebat pri- mogenita ipsos tangeret, Ebr. 11, 28. Quæ enim fides illa est, de qua ibi Apostolus, nisi fides in Messiam, ad cujus constantiam Ebræos, exemplo fidelium majorum, hortatur, qua nempe respicitur Christus, utpote qui crucem pro nobis sustinuit, ut esset ἀρχηγὸς καὶ τελειωτὴς inceptor, autor & consummator fidei nostræ cap. 12, 1.

Finis ergo sacramenti agni paschalis hinc col- ligitur non nuda significatio, sed vera & actualis fruitio, non solum liberationis ab angelo percussore, per sanguinis agni paschalis interventum facta, sed imprimis a Satanæ potestate, Per sanguinem Chri- sti, veri agni, qui tollit peccata mundi, quia confir- mabantur hoc sacramento fideles Israëlitæ, tam certo se liberatum iri e captivitate Satanæ per agnum Dei, quam certo agno mactato & mandu- cato e servitute Ægypti & strage angeli percussoris erant liberandi. Quem finem non diffitetur Rive- tus, imo extra controversiam ponit, Christum fuis- se præcipuum scopum illius sacramenti, & finem fide propositum hunc fuisse primarium, ut agnosce- rent fideles, se per Messiam venturum redemtum iri a servitute peccati & mortis, & idcirco Chri- stum agnum appellari, & agni nomine sæpe signi- ficari. Vid. Comment. ejus in h. l. p. 221. Vetere quærunt hic etiam figuram crucis, quod nempe su- perliminare utrique posti incumbens cum iisdem sanguine agni tingendum fuerit, quæ figuram cru cis exhibuerint: de quo vid. Cypr. l. 2. testim. con tra Judæos c. 22. Atque hæc causa fuit, cur non ali admissi sint ad hoc sacramentum, nisi circumcif quia scil. fruitio istius beneficii Christi propria fo lum est circumcisorum, & quam in circumcision acceperant gratiam Israëlitæ, ea obsignabatur ips in agno paschali. Neque dubium est, ad illam frui- tionem respicere Apostolum, cum 1. Cor. 5, 7. ait: itaq; & nos festum agamus, quia pascha pro nobis im- molatum est Christus, quod nempe Israelitæ per fi- dem frui potuerint in Sacramento Paschali bene- ficiis hujus veri agni, eoque nomine festum cum hi- laritate transigere, etsi agnum solum typicum ha- berent: quanto ergo magis nos fruimur iisdem, qui verum illum agnum Dei habemus. Adde quod suc- cesserit sacramentum Cœnæ in locum agni pascha- lis; ut ergo in illo vere fruimur beneficiis Christi, quæ morte sua nobis acquisivit, ita & fideles Israe- litæ frui poterant iisdem, per fidem in Messiam, quem figurabat ipsis agnus paschalis. Denique facit huc veterum Ebræorum traditio, quam Fagius & Eugub. in Exod. 12. c. ut & Masius in c. 5. Josuæ p. 92. ex Talmudico Tract. Rosch Haschana addu- cunt, quæ eandem veterum Ebræorum fidem fuis- se haud obscure docet, siquidem crediderint, in qua die olim per Mosen ex Ægypto facta est liberatio, eadem die, i. e. prima azymorum populum Israël per Messiam redemtum iri. Quapropter non defuit in hoc sacramento materia cælestis, quæ ad omne sa- cramentum requiritur, cum rei terrenæ per se effe- ctus spiritualis non conveniat; Elementum terre- num sive materia terrena in hoc sacramento fuit agnus assatus prævia sanguinis aspersione, siquidem ejusdem comestio, aut bibitio lege prisca vetita erat, Gen. 9, 4. Materia autem cælestis erat agnus pro nobis immolatus, Christus, sanguinem suum pro- fusurus 1. Cor. 5, 7. Plura vid. de hoc sacramento apud B. Gerhard. in Loc. Com. & in Mysterioso- phia Ln. D. Dannh. Sect. 2. art. 2. qui hic exhibet διατύπωσιν, & collationem agni paschalis cum suo antitypo in N. T.

## 12:14
Ver. 14. BUT YOU SHALL COUNT THIS DAY FOR A MEMORIAL.

Because the Lord wished the perpetual memory of this benefit to be preserved among His people, He instituted its solemn annual celebration, and you shall celebrate it. חגג is to dance, as also to keep a feast, from which comes חג, a feast, because in feasts the Hebrews declared their joy with leaps and dances. There is held, therefore, here the institution of the feast of the Passover made immediately by God. Because this was not only μνημονευτικὸν (a memorial) of a past benefit, but also τυπικὸν (a type) of a future one, it could not be instituted except by God: for to institute types of sacred things, to which the truth must respond in its own time, belongs to God alone, who can provide the truth.

Latin:

Vers. 14. NUMERABITIS AUTEM HUNC DIEM IN MONUMENTUM.

Quia perpetuam hujus beneficii memoriam in populo suo conservatam voluit Dominus, anni- versariam ejus celebrationem solemnem instituit, & celebrabitis eam. חגג est saltare, ut & festum agitare, a quo חג festum, quia in festis lætitiam Ebræi sal- tationibus & choreis declarabant. Habetur ergo hic institutio festi paschatos a Deo immediate facta. Quod quia non solum μνημονευτικὸν fuit præteriti beneficii, sed etiam τυπικὸν futuri, non potuit nisi a Deo institui: nam typos rerum sacrarum institue- re, quibus veritas suo tempore debeat respondere, solius Dei est, qui veritatem præstare potest.

## 12:15
Vers. 15. SEVEN DAYS YOU SHALL EAT UNLEAVENED BREAD,) It was not permitted for the priests to touch leavened flour. Servius from the Fulda codex on Aeneid 1. Doubtless ἄζυμα (unleavened bread) have the significance of purity. 1 Cor. 5, 7. and of a submissive mind; for leaven is pride. But the Hebrews prefer to draw the significance of bitter herbs to the slavery, and unleavened bread to the liberty obtained. Tacitus: The Jewish bread is kept without any leaven as a proof of stolen grain.

THAT SOUL SHALL PERISH FROM ISRAEL) כרת; this signifies premature death: which penalty is found applied above in Gen. 17, 14 to the precept of circumcision: furthermore to twenty-three other precepts. But all of which are of the class of prohibitions.

Unleavened bread seems to have been used, because memory is more vivid from the sense and experience of a similar thing, therefore in remembrance of the hurried departure, which did not even grant time for fermentation, and of the lack of more suitable food, as also of the affliction in Egypt, an unusual bread was commanded, which is called the bread of affliction in Deut. 16, 3, because it had to be prepared in haste, and for that reason, while the Jews use unleavened bread on the Passover night, this is, they say, the bread of affliction, which our fathers ate in the land of Egypt. Therefore God adds also bitter herbs in memory of the bitterness of the misery which they had experienced in

Egypt. But the question is here, whether the Passover could also be celebrated with the heavenly manna; which we affirm with the Blessed Hunn.; for it was true bread, and it had that property which was required in the Paschal bread, that is, it was unleavened or unfermented; therefore in Num. 9 it is read that the Israelites in the 2nd year from the exodus kept the Passover at the command of the Lord. But it is certain that they had no other bread then than that which rained down daily from the clouds.

Latin:

Vers. 15. SEPTEM DIEBVS AZTMA COMEDETIS,) Flamines farinam fermentatam contingere non licebat. Ser- vius ex codice Fuldenfi ad I. Æn. Nimirum ἄζυμα significa- tionem habent puritatis. 1. Cor. 5, 7. & animi submissi; nam fermentum est ὑπεροχὴ. Sed Hebræi herbas amaras ad servi- tutis, azyma ad libertatis partæ significationum malunt trahere. Tacitus: raptarum frugum argumentum panis Judaicus nullo fermento detinetur.

PERIBIT ANIMA ILLA DE ISRAEL) כרת; mor- tem immaturam id significat: quæ pœna supra Gen. 17, 14. præcepto circumcisionis invenitur apposita: præterea aliis præceptis XXIII. Sed quæ omnia sunt ex vetantium genere.

Azymus adhibitus videtur panis, quia me- moria vivacior est ex sensu, & experientia rei simi- lis, ideo in recordationem festinati discessus, qui ne fermentationi quidem tempus concedebat, & inopiæ cibi commodioris, ut & afflictionis in Ægy- pto panis insolitus præceptus est, qui dicitur panis afflictionis Deut. 16, 3. quia in festinatione paran- dus erat, atque ea de causa, dum azymis paschali no- cte utuntur Judæi, hic est, inquiunt, panis afflictio- nis, quem comederunt Patres nostri in terra Ægypti. Ideo addit Deus etiam herbas amaras in memo- riam amaritudinis miseriæ, quam experti erant in

Aegypto. Quæritur autem hic, an etiam Pascha celebrari potuerit in manna cælesti; quod cum B. Hunn. affirmamus; erat quippe panis verus, & ha- bebat eam proprietatem, quæ in Paschali pane re- quirebatur, id est, erat azymus sive infermentatus; ideo Num. 9. legitur Israelitas anno 2. ab egressu ad mandatum Domini fecisse Phase. Certum autem est, quod tum alium panem non habuerint, quam qui indies depluebat e nubibus.

## 12:15 Addition
To Exod. 12. verse 15. at page 371. a. noted near the end.

But by those words THAT SOUL SHALL PERISH FROM ISRAEL, Vatablus says that an exemption from the catalogue of the Israelites is noted. Oleastrius, Cornelius à Lapide, Piscatus, and Rivetus understand the penalty of death to be inflicted by the Magistrate: because this transgression, as Rivetus holds, was interpretatively an Apostasy from the true Religion and a rejection of the covenant entered into. For such persons renounced the benefit of past liberation and the future promise concerning the Messiah.

Latin:

Ad Exod. 12. vers. 15. ad pag. 371. a. sub finem notar.

Per verba autem illa PERIBIT ANIMA ILLA DE ISRAEL, Vatablus exemtionem è Ca- talogo Israëllitarum notari ait. Occisionis pœnam Oleastrius, Cornel. à Lapide, Piscat. Rivetus intelli- gunt à Magistratu inferendam: quia interpretative hæc transgressio, ut Rivetus habet, Apostasia fuit, a vera Religione, & fœderis initi rejectio. Renun- ciabant enim tales beneficio liberationis præteri- tæ, & promissioni futuræ de Messia.

## 12:16
Verse 16.

YOU SHALL DO NO WORK IN IT) מלאכה

The LXX here and in Leviticus and in Numbers translate it ἔργον λατρευτὸν, certainly from Leviticus 23, where it is added for the sake of explanation מלאכת עבודה. That ancient Roman Pontifical law called it servile work. Cicero, On Laws II: 'From holidays let disputes be removed, and let them be held as servile works performed.' Tertullian in Against the Jews and Jerome on Isaiah 28 translate it as servile work. See also Servius on Georgics 1.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

NIHIL OPERIS FACIETIS IN EO) מלאכה

LXX. hic & in Levitico & in Numeris vertunt ἔργον λατρευ- τὸν, nimirum ex Levit. XXIII. ubi additur explicandi causa מלאכת עבודה. id vetus Romanorum jus Pontificium vocabat opus famulum. Cic. de Legibus II. Feriis jurgia amovento, eaque in famulis operibus patratis habento. Opus servile vertit Tertullianus adversus Judæos, & Hieronymus ad XXVIII. Esaiæ. Vide & Servium ad 1. Georg.

## 12:17
Verse 17.

BY A PERPETUAL RITE.

It is called a statute of the age עולם, which word does not always denote absolute perpetuity, but sometimes a definite one according to the nature of the subject, as here the rite is perpetual for the people as long as they are a people, just as in Deut. 15:17 it is said: 'he shall be your servant forever,' that is: as long as he shall survive: and therefore the Jews are mistaken, who believe that those ceremonies are to be observed now, and the Passover celebrated until the end of the world, for those things pertained to the Israelite people as long as they were a people, which they ceased to be when their polity and temple were overturned: and since the sacrifices connected to the Passover, according to the law, ought not to have been offered anywhere but in Jerusalem, there is certainly no longer any place for the celebration of the Passover, according to all its ceremonies, now that the temple and city are overturned, which Justin urges against them in his Dialogue against Trypho; cf. Deut. 16:5, 2 Chron. 30:35. Although indeed the exiled and dispersed Hebrews have also recalled a memorial Passover, they could not, however, celebrate a sacrificial and solemn Passover elsewhere, and this is the reason the Jews even now are accustomed to object as to why they cannot now observe all those prescribed ceremonies at the Passover: See Buxtorf in Synagoga Judaica, ch. 13, p. 336. The Armenian Christians also erred in Judaizing in this, that they still celebrate the Paschal lamb with the Jews, anoint the thresholds, and keep ash from burnt bones, with blood, as a sign of expiation; see Vol. 3 of the Bibliotheca Patrum, Fragment of Nicon on the religion of the Armenians.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

RITU PERPETUO.

Vocatur statutum seculi עולם quæ vox non perpetuitatem absolutam semper, sed quandoque definitam pro ratione subjecti notat, ut hic ritus populo sit perpetuus, quoad usque est populus, sicut Deut. 15, 17. dicitur: erit tibi servus in perpe- tuum, id est: quoadusque supererit: ideoque fallun- tur Judæi, qui nunc illas ceremonias observandas, & Pascha ad mundi finem celebrandum credunt, pertinebant enim illa ad populum Israeliticum, quamdiu erat populus, quod esse desiit eversa ejus politia, & templo: & cum sacrificia paschati con- nexa non alibi, quam Hierosolymis offerri, secun- dum legem, debuerint, utique paschatis celebra- tioni, juxta ceremonias suas omnes, locus am- plius non est everso templo, & urbe, quod Justi- nus contra ipsos urget Dialog. contra Triphon. conf. Deut. 16, 5. 2. Paral. 30, 35. Quanquam vero Ebræi extorres, ac dispersi pascha mnemo- neuticum etiam recoluerint, non tamen pascha θύσιμον ac solemne alibi celebrare potuere, & hanc causam obvertere solent etiamnum Judæi, cur nempe jam non possint omnes istas præscriptas ceremonias in paschate observare: Vid. Buxt. in Synagog. Jud. c. 13. p. 336. Errarunt etiam Ar- menii Christiani in eo Judaizantes, quod adhuc agnum paschalem cum Judæis celebrent, limina inungant, cinerem servent ex ossibus combustis, cum sanguine, in signum expiationis, vid. Tom. 3. Biblioth. Patrum Fragment. Niconis de Arme- niorum religione.

## 12:18
Verse 18.

IN THE FIRST MONTH ON THE FOURTEENTH DAY AT EVENING.

The fourteenth day is not properly included in the festival, inasmuch as it began towards the evening of that day. For the Jewish method of counting is well known, according to which that final particle of the 14th day is to be referred to the 15th day, and thus the passage in Deut. 23, 6, as well as Num. 28, 16, is to be reconciled with this one of ours. For there the first day of unleavened bread is called the fifteenth day. One must, of course, distinguish between the civil computation, and the customary one, which was made from midnight to midnight: and the legal computation from evening to evening: according to the former it was the fourteenth day: but according to the latter it was the fifteenth, on which the paschal feast began. Moreover, this circumstance of the 14th day has nothing to do with the Christian paschal feast, and therefore the Quartodecimans were not undeservedly condemned for heresy, who wished to bind the consciences of Christians, and established the observation of the 14th day with the Jews as necessary for the celebration of the Christian paschal feast. It must be observed, however, that that heresy cannot be imputed to the Asian Bishops, who, according to the custom observed from the beginning in their Churches, arising from the very practice of certain Apostles (who had initially accommodated themselves in this to the weak Jews), celebrated the Christian Passover on the fourteenth day with the Jews, not for a Jewish purpose, but in memory of the resurrection of Christ; these men, however, did this not by the force of the Mosaic law, nor did they bind consciences to it or urge necessity, which would have been to foist Judaism in place of Christian liberty, but they observed this custom while preserving Christian liberty, and therefore the bolt of excommunication was rashly hurled by Victor, Bishop of Rome, against the Bishops of Asia, who was for this reason deservedly rebuked by Irenaeus and others; which controversy was later settled in the Nicene Synod, where the Eastern and Western Churches agreed in defining the paschal feast to be celebrated in memory of the Lord's resurrection.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

PRIMO MENSE QVARTA DECIMA DIE AD VESPERAM.

Decima quarta dies festivitati proprie non in- cluditur, utpote quæ sub vesperam ejus cœpit. Nota enim est Judaica numerandi ratio, juxta quam extrema illa diei 14. particula referenda est ad diem 15. atque ita conciliandus est locus Deut. 23, 6. ut & Num. 28, 16. cum hoc nostro. Ibi enim dies primus azymorum dicitur dies decimus quintus. Distinguendum nempe est inter com- putationem civilem, atque usualem, quæ fiebat a media nocte ad mediam noctem : & computa- tionem legalem a vespera ad vesperam: juxta illam erat decima quarta dies: juxta hanc vero decima quinta, qua festum paschale cœpit. Cæterum hæc circumstantia diei 14. nihil ad festum Chri- stianorum paschale facit, ideoque Tessaradecatitæ non immerito hæreseos condemnati sunt, qui conscientias Christianorum adstringere volebant, & observationem 14. diei cum Judæis, ad festi paschatos Christiani celebrationem necessariam statuebant. Observandum tamen, illam hæresin impingi non posse Asiaticis Episcopis, qui more ab initio in Ecclesiis suis observato ex ipsa quorundam Apostolorum consuetudine (qui se in eo infirmis Judæis primitus accommodarant,) oriundo decima quarta die cum Judæis pascha Christianum non Judaico fine, sed in memoriam resurrectionis Christi celebrabant, hi autem id faciebant non vi legis Mosaicæ, neque conscientias ad id adstringebant aut necessitatem urgebant, quod fuisset Judaismum loco libertatis Christianæ obtrudere, sed salva libertate Christiana hunc morem observabant, ideoque temere fulmen anathematis a Victore Episcopo Romano in Asiæ Episcopos vibratum est, qui ob id merito ab Irenæo, & aliis reprehensus est; quæ controversia postea sopita fuit in Nicena Synodo, ubi Orientales, & Occidentales Ecclesiæ convenerunt in definiendo festo paschatos, in memoriam resurrectionis Dominicæ celebrando.

## 12:20
Verse 20.

SACRIFICE THE PASSOVER.

Understand the Paschal lamb, not that this was a proper name for the paschal lamb, such as are Ishmael and Isaac, and other proper names, as Leonhardus Marius the Jesuit foolishly claims; but that the lamb, to be eaten in memory of the passing over and liberation, was called so metonymically: from which, however, the Calvinists gather their sacramental metonymy in vain: for although to sacrifice the passover signifies nothing other than the slaughtering of the lamb itself, it does not therefore follow, if such a proposition were to be found (as it is not found), 'the lamb is the passover', that a Sacramental metonymy has a place there: for it is one thing for the lamb to be called the passover by metonymy, but it is another thing for the word IS to be tropically (whether you call it metonymy or any other trope) the same as what it signifies.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

IMMOLATE PASCHA.

Agnum Paschalem intellige, non quod agno paschali hoc nomen proprium fuerit, qualia sunt Ismael & Isaac, & alia propria nomina, ut ineptit Leonhardus Marius Jesuita; sed quod metonymice agnus, in memoriam transitus & liberationis manducandus, ita appellatus fuerit: ex quo tamen nequicquam Calviniani colligunt metonymiam suam sacramentariam: nam licet immolare pascha nihil aliud significet quam agni ipsius mactationem, non tamen ideo sequitur, si talis propositio reperiretur, (uti non reperitur) agnus est phase, metonymiam ibi Sacramentalem locum habere: nam aliud est, agnum per metonymiam vocari pascha, aliud vero est verbum EST topice (sive metonymiam dicas sive alium quemcunque tropum) idem esse, quod significat.

## 12:22
Verse 22.

A BUNDLE OF HYSSOP.

Regarding hyssop, one may read at length in Casaubon, Exercit. 16 against Baronius, no. 88. Piscator and Rivet understand it as Libanotis, which is commonly called Rosemary, because that plant seems most suitable for sprinklers. Levinus Lemnius explains it as a certain herb which he calls maidenhair, led by the reasoning that it is both small and clings to a wall, from 1 Kings 4:33. Rabbi David Kimchi in the Book of Roots thinks it is the herb which the Latins call Origanum. Heinsius in Aristarchus Sac. p. 513 explains it as greasy wool, whose opinion Ludovicus de Dieu modestly examines in his Commentary on John 19:29, where he is sufficiently prolix on this word; he himself, however, thinks it should be understood as ὕσσωπον κηρωτὴν: and he is led by a peculiar conjecture, both that the aromatic reed was used in the passion of Christ in John 19 and the herb hyssop, and indeed for the same purpose, namely to refresh the senses, strengthen the brain, and restore the spirits of the suffering Christ. But we know from Psalm 69:22 that those things were applied not for the sake of Christ's recreation, but so that they might cause him distress. Casaubon says there is need of some Elijah who might untie this knot, as to what hyssop is. But we do not see the reason why not let us understand it as the herb hyssop, which we name, which Augustine in Psalm 51 says is a humble medicinal herb suitable for cleansing the lungs, clinging to rock with its roots. For the fact that in 1 Kings 4:33 it seems to be numbered among trees, since Solomon is read to have discoursed from the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that comes out of the wall, and Josephus understands it as a δένδρον (tree), there is no force in that; because for the Hebrews עֵץ and for the Greeks δένδρον is a common noun, signifying wood and subsequently a tree, because it is wood; so that by this name hyssop can be called a tree, even if it is not properly a tree, because, namely, it is a plant with woody branches, as Ludovicus de Dieu notes in the cited place, and that passage in 1 Kings 4 indicates the two extremes, not precisely of trees, but in the genus of plants, that is, among vegetables, namely the cedar and the hyssop.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

FASCICULUM HYSSOPI.

De hyssopo prolixe legi poterit Casaubonus Exercit. 16. contra Baronium num. 88. Piscat. & Rivet. de Libanotide, quæ vulgo Rosmarinus appellatur intelligunt, quod ea planta ad aspergilla videatur aptissima. Levinus Lemnius de herba quadam, quam vocat capillum veneris, explicat, ea ratione ductus, quod & exigua sit & parieti adhæreat, e 1. Reg. IV, 33. R. David Kimchi in Lib. Radicum putat, herbam esse, quam Latini Origanum appellant, Heinsius in Aristarcho Sac. p. 513. de lana succida explicat, cujus sententiam modeste examinat Ludov. de Dieu. in Comm. ad Joh. 19, 29. ubi satis prolixus est in hac voce, intelligendam autem censet ipse ὕσσωπον κηρωτὴν: & conjectura peculiari ducitur, & calamum odoratum in passione Christi adhibitum Joh. 19. & herbam hyssopum, & quidem ad eundem usum, nimirum ad reficiendos sensus, roborandum cerebrum & restaurandos spiritus Christi patientis. At non recreationis Christi causa, sed ut ægre ipsi facerent, ista adhibita esse e Psalmo LXIX, 22. novimus. Casaubonus Elia quodam opus esse dicit, qui hunc nodum expediat, quid hyssopus sit. Sed non videmus causam, cur non de hyssopo herba, quam nos vocamus, quam Aug. in Psal. LI. dicit esse humilem herbam medici- nalem purgandis pulmonibus aptam, saxo hærentem radicibus, intelligamus. Nam quod 1. Regum IV, 33. videtur arboribus annumerata, cum a cedro quæ est in Libano, usque ad hyssopum, quæ egreditur de pa- riete, disseruisse Salomo legitur: & Josephus δέν- δρον intelligit, in eo vis nulla est; quia Ebræis עֵץ & Græcis δένδρον commune est nomen, lignum si- gnificans & postmodum arborem, quia lignum est; ut isto nomine hyssopus dici possit, etiamsi arbor proprie non sit, quia scil. planta est ligneis ramis, ut notat Ludov. de Dieu l. c. & locus ille 1. Reg. 4. extrema duo, non arborum præcise, sed in genere plantarum indicat, hoc est, inter vegetabilia, cedrum nempe, & hyssopum.

## 12:22 Addition
To v. 22. at p. 371. b.

It makes for hyssop that it is called by a similar word Ezoba in Chaldean and Ezob in Ethiopic, and that the LXX and Josephus, who has ὕσσωπον, while the Republic was standing, in which the daily use of זובא flourished, were not ignorant of what they were. Add especially the authority of the Apostle, Heb. 9, 19. Compare Bochart, Hierozoic. l. 2. 50. 587.

Latin:

Ad v. 22. ad p. 371. b.

Pro hyssopo facit, quod Chaldaice simili voce Ezoba & Æthiopice Ezob nuncupetur, quodque LXX. & Josephus, qui ὕσσωπον habet, stante Re- publ. in quo quotidianus זובא usus vigebat, non ignorarint, quid fuerint, Adde imprimis autorita- tem Apostoli, Ebr, 9, 19. Conf. Bochart. Hierozoic. l. 2. 50. 587.

## 12:26
Verse 26.

AND WHEN YOUR CHILDREN SAY TO YOU) In the twelfth year, children were led by their parents to the temple, Luke 2:42. From that time they began to partake of the Passover and other holy things. Compare what is below at 13:8 and 14. Hyrcanus in Josephus 12:4: 'because there is a law among them forbidding the one born to taste of the sacrifice before he comes to the temple and sacrifices to God.'

Latin:

Vers. 26.

ET CUM DIXERINT VOBIS FILII VESTRI) An- no XII. filii a parentibus ad templum ducebanrur Luc. II, 42. Ab eo tempore incipiebant de Paschate & aliis sacris vesci. Confer quæ infra XIII, 8. & 14. Hyrcanus apud Josephum XII, 4. ὅτι νόμος ἐστὶ παρὰ ἀυτῷ κωλύων τὸν γεννηθέντα γεύ- σασθαι θυσίας, πρὶν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἔλθῃ καὶ θύσῃ τῷ Θεῷ.

## 12:27
Verse 27.

IT IS THE VICTIM OF THE LORD'S PASSAGE.

The Sacramentarians seek their metonymy here again, and in order to find it here, they pretend that in the case which is not oblique, but direct, the word 'Passover' is to be understood here in this way: the victim is the passing over of the Lord, that is, it signifies and recalls to memory the passing over of the Lord. But the very manner of speaking and the state of the regimen and the interposed Maqqef sign sufficiently testify to the oblique case here; which indeed openly teaches that these do not cohere as subject and predicate, but must be rendered entirely as the blessed Luther renders it: 'Es ist das Pascha Opffer' (It is the Passover sacrifice). Whence the Belgian paraphrasts themselves also interpreted it in the same way: therefore no support for the Sacramentarian metonymy comes from this. However, it is called זֶבַח פֶּסַח (sacrifice of the Passover), not because the Passover was a sacrifice properly so called, as the Papists collect; but with the word זֶבַח (sacrifice) taken more generally, so that the sense may be: it is the slaughtering of the Lord's passage, because this slaughtering was instituted when the Lord was passing over, and so that He might pass over. And thus the Holy Spirit uses the word זֶבַח in 1 Samuel 18:24, chapter 16:3, 1 Kings 1:9 for slaughtering, whence it is even used for the slaughter of men in Isaiah 34:6. And therefore the argument which those who establish that the paschal lamb is a sacrifice are accustomed to seek from this place is too weak; the blessed Hunnus, in his question concerning the Sacrament, chapter 3, page 112, observes that the paschal lamb can be called both a sacrifice and a sacrament in a different respect: a sacrifice on account of the slaughtering and the shedding of blood, which was a very illustrious figure of the sacrifice of Christ and the shedding of His blood. But he notes at the same time, which is entirely to be noted, that this Passover sacrifice had this peculiar feature, that nothing of it was burned on the altar of the Lord, nor did any parts fall to the priests, but the whole was to be eaten: which circumstances separate the paschal lamb from all other sacrifices in his judgment, inasmuch as it is clear from the same that it approaches the nature of a sacrament. And therefore if we wish to be precise, we shall most correctly say that something sacrificial is found in the paschal lamb, on account of which also

The Israelites are then said to have sacrificed, Wis. 18:9, unless one prefers to refer this to the sacrifices connected with the Passover, but properly the paschal lamb is not a sacrifice, for in every sacrifice it was essential that it be offered and burned on the altar, and it did not consist in the slaughtering and shedding of blood alone; cf. B. Chemn. in Exam. Concil. Trid. part 2, on the Mass, pp. 266.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

VICTIMA TRANSITUS DOMINI EST.

Quærunt hic iterum metonymiam suam Sa- cramentarii, & ut eam hic inveniant, fingunt in ca- su non obliquo, sed recto vocem Pascha hic intelli- gendam esse h. m. victima est transilitio Domini, id est, significat & in memoriam revocat transitum Domini. Sed casum obliquum hic ipsa loquendi ratio & status regiminis ac interposita virgula Maccaph satis testatur; quæ utique aperte docet, non cohærere hæc tanquam subjectum & prædi- catum, sed reddi omnino debere ut reddit B. Luth. Es ist das Pascha Opffer. Unde ipsi etiam Para- phrastæ Belgici eadem ratione interpretati sunt: nullum ergo hinc subsidium Sacramentariæ me- tonymiæ accedit. Dicitur autem זֶבַח פֶּסַח non quod pascha fuerit sacrificium proprie dictum, quemadmodum Pontif. colligunt; sed voce זֶבַח ge- neralius accepta, ut sensus sit: mactatio transitus Domini est, quia mactatio hæc instituebatur, cum transiret Dominus, & ut transiret. Atque ita vo- cem זֶבַח usurpat Spiritus S. 1. Sam. 18, 24. c. 16, 3. 1. Reg. 1, 9. pro mactatione, unde etiam de cæde ho- minum usurpatur Es. 34, 6. Ideoque argumen- tum, quod ex h. l. petere solent, qui agnum pascha- lem sacrificium esse statuunt, nimis infirmum est; B. Hunn. qu. de Sacramento cap. 3. pag. 112. obser- vat; agnum paschalem diverso respectu & sacrifi- cium & sacramentum appellari posse: sacrificium ob mactationem & sanguinis effusionem, quæ illustris admodum erat figura sacrificii Christi, & effusionis sanguinis ejus. Sed notat simul, quod omnino notandum est, peculiare hoc habuisse sacrificium phase, quod nihil de eo accensum fuerit in altari Do- mini, nec ullæ partes cesserint sacerdotibus, sed totum manducandum fuerit: quæ circumstantiæ ab omni- bus aliis sacrificiis agnum paschalem ejus judicio separant, utpote quod ad naturam sacramenti eun- dem accedere ex iisdem liquet. Ideoque si ἀκρι- βολογεῖν velimus, rectissime dixerimus aliquid sa- crificiale in agno paschali reperiri, ob quod etiam

Israelitæ tum sacrificasse dicuntur Sap. 18, 9. nisi hoc quis referre malit ad sacrificia Paschati con- nexa, proprie autem agnum paschalem non esse sa- crificium, nam in omni sacrificio essentiale erat, ut offerretur & incenderetur in altari, neque in sola mactatione & sanguinis effusione consistebat; conf. B. Chemn. in Exam. Concil. Trid. part. 2. de Missa pagg. 266.

## 12:27 Addition
To v. 27. page 572. b. noted at the end.

Therefore, Bellarmine has no foundation here for a sacrificial Mass, l. 1. de Miss. c. 7. because the immolation properly so-called took place in the temple by the Priests: but not so the celebration of the Paschal lamb, Matt. 26, 18. 19. It is, however, called an immolation analogically because of the slaughter, and that not a common one, but a religious one: nor was it a type of the Eucharist except insofar as it was a Sacramental act, but not insofar as it had anything sacrificial: for in that way it was a type of the slaughter of Christ on the cross, 1 Cor. 5, 7.

Latin:

Ad v. 27. pag. 572. b. ad finem notar.

Nullum ergo hic fundamentum habet Bellar- mini pro sacrificio Missatico, l. 1. de Miss. c. 7. quia immolatio proprie dicta fiebat in templo a Sacer- dotibus: non autem ita celebratio agni Paschalis Matth. 26, 18. 19. Dicitur tamen analogice immola- tio propter mactationem eamque non vulgarem, sed religiosam: nec erat typus Eucharistiæ nisi qua actus Sacramentalis fuit, non autem qua aliquid Sa- crificiale habebat: sic enim typus erat mactationis Christi in cruce 1. Cor. 5, 7.

## 12:29
Ver. 29.

THE FIRSTBORN OF THE CAPTIVE THAT WAS IN THE PRISON) So also the Greeks. In the Hebrew it is: of the captivity: which you may rightly understand as servants of the worst condition, that is, those put into the mill. Compare above 11:5.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

PRIMOGENITUM CAPTIVÆ QUÆ ERAT IN CARCERE) Sic & Græci. In Hebræo est: captivitatis: quod recte intelligas de servis pessimæ conditionis, id est in pistrinum datis. Confer supra XI, 5.

## 12:30
Ver. 30.

FOR THERE WAS NOT A HOUSE IN WHICH THERE LAY NOT A DEAD MAN.

Understand this not universally, but commonly or universally in a qualified sense, that there was almost no house, or certainly in this way, that no house in which there was a firstborn was without a dead person, because there were not precisely firstborn in all houses who would be struck; cf. Jer. 5:1; John 12:19.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

NEQVE ENIM ERAT DOMUS, IN QVA NON JACERET MORTUUS.

Intellige non universaliter, sed communiter vel universaliter secundum quid, quod fere nulla domus, aut certe hoc modo, quod nulla domus, in qua primogenitus erat, fuerit sine mortuo, quia non in omnibus præcise erant primogeniti, qui cæderentur; Conf. Jerem. V, 1. Joh. 12, 19.

## 12:31
Ver. 31.

AND PHARAOH CALLED MOSES AND AARON.

The phrasing is awkward. The sense is that Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron, which seems to have been done through Pharaoh's ministers, so that Pharaoh did not deal with Moses immediately, nor did Moses come into his sight, just as he had also predicted in ch. 11:3, 'all these thy servants shall come down unto me,' etc., and the last verse of ch. 10, 'I will see thy face again no more.'

Latin:

Vers. 31.

VOCATISQVE PHARAO ET MOSI ET AARON.

Dictio est incommoda. Sensus est vocasse Pharaonem Mosen & Aaronem, quod factum vi- detur per ministros Pharaonis, ita ut non imme- diate Pharao cum Mose egerit, nec Moses in ejus conspectum venerit, sicut id etiam prædixerat c. 11, 3. descendent omnes servi tui ad me &c. & vers. ult. c. 10. non ultra videbo faciem tuam.

## 12:37
Ver. 37.

ABOUT SIX HUNDRED THOUSAND FOOTMEN) One will wonder less that the progeny of Jacob had increased so much in two centuries if one considers that in Egypt women are very fruitful, as Aristotle affirms in History of Animals, book VII, ch. 4, so that many bear seven at one birth; as Paul testifies in book of Antiquities, D. if a part of an inheritance is sought. Add Gellius, book X, ch. 2. Moreover, this number agrees very well with that which is in the passage of Chaeremon in Josephus. For he first puts two hundred and fifty thousand, then three hundred and eighty thousand.

Latin:

Vers. 37.

SEXCENTIA FERE MILLIA PEDITUM VIRO- RUM) Minus mirabitur duobus seculis sic auctam Jacobi progeniem, si quis consideret in Ægypto mulieres esse valde ἐυεκφόρος, ut Aristoteles affirmat de Historia animantium lib. VII. c. 4. ita ut multæ uno partu septenos edant; ut te- statur Paulus l. Antiquit. D. si pars hæreditatis petatur. Ad- de Gellium libro X. c. 2. Valde autem hic numerus conve- nit cum eo qui est in loco Chæremonis apud Josephum. Is enim prius ponit millia ducena quinquagena, deinde millia tercentena octogena.

## 12:39
v. 39. AND THEY BAKED THE DOUGH) In the Hebrew, as Pagninus translates: And they baked the dough, which they brought forth out of Egypt, unleavened cakes, because it had not been leavened, because they were driven out of Egypt, and could not tarry, and also they had not prepared food for themselves. The sense is: because the cakes had not been mixed with leaven due to the haste of their departure, therefore the Hebrews had not baked them at their departure. But when they came to Succoth, with the leaven added which they had brought with them, they baked them; as also other foods.

Latin:

v. 39. COXERUNTQVE FARINAM) In Hebræo, ut vertit Pagninus: Et coxerunt conspersionem, quam eduxerunt ex Ægypto, placentulas infermentatas, quia non fermentatum fuerat, quia expulsi fuerunt ex Ægypto, & non demorari po- tuerunt, & etiam escam non sibi fecerant. Sensus est: quia placentæ ob festinationem exitus fermento mixtæ non fue- rant, ideo eas non coxerant Hebræi in exitu. Sed ubi Suc- cothas venerunt, addito quod secum attulerant fermento, coxere eas; ut & cibos alios.

## 12:40
40. NOW THE DWELLING OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL WHICH THEY DWELT IN EGYPT, WAS FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY YEARS) Since the Israelites were not in Egypt for more than two hundred and ten years, interpreters have judged that something must be added here by way of interpretation. The LXX add after Αἰγύπτω, κᾀι ἐν τῇ γῇ Καναάν: in certain books it is added also after καῴκησαν, κᾀι οἱ πατέρες ἀυτῶν. Augustine acknowledges both additions in book II on Exodus, question 47. That the LXX have it otherwise here than the Hebrew codices is noted in both Talmuds. That 'and in the land of Canaan' is added from the LXX and the Samaritan. Rabbi Solomon Jarchi wishes it to be understood as 'and in other lands' as well. The sense will not be bad if you interpret that Egyptian exile as having lasted until the four hundred and thirtieth year, from the time when God had pre-signified it to Abraham. Gen. XV, 13. and following. And that space of years having elapsed, that God exercised vengeance upon the Egyptians, just as He had then predicted, to which those things which immediately follow pertain.

But since he praised the LXX interpreters and the Samaritan Codex regarding this addition, to which he otherwise attributes so much that he sometimes even postpones the Hebrew text, it might seem that he wished to bring the same into suspicion here also of some depravation or castration: of which John Morin has accused the Hebrew text entirely.

Moreover, the consensus of all the Codices, as well as the Chaldean Paraphrases, and also the Arabic of R. Saadia Gaon, and the Latin Vulgate, easily vindicates the same: even of the Talmud itself, both of them, in which, as Grotius admits here, this difference between the Hebrew text and the Chaldean Paraphrase is observed, and R. Levi, a commentator both Hebrew and Christian, gives the reason why mention of Egypt is made here only: because the exile of the Ishmaelites, from which the denomination was made as if it were the more important one, was the principal one there. Augustine explains in book XVI of the City of God, chapter 24, not concerning the continuous duration of the Egyptian oppression, but that it would happen within those years. Eugubinus indeed and Genebrardus wish for the servitude to have lasted those entire 430 years: But this is repugnant to history: and to the Apostle in Galatians 3. But the beginning of the number is more correctly established at the beginning of the calling of Abraham, from which to the descent of Jacob into Egypt 215 years elapsed, and just as many from this until the exodus. Wherefore it must be said that the entire pilgrimage is comprehended by synecdoche as a dwelling in Egypt, so that it is not necessary to invent a σφάλμα, or error, in the sources.

Latin:

40. HABITATIO AUTEM FILIORUM ISRAEL QVA MANSERUNT IN ÆGYPTO, FUIT QVA- DRINGENTORUM TRIGINTA ANNORUM) Cum ul- tra ducentos & decem annos in Ægypto non fuerint Israeli- tæ, aliquid hic interpretamenti vice addendum censuere in- terpretes. LXX. addunt post Αἰγύπτω, κᾀι ἐν τῇ γῇ Καναάν: in quibusdam libris additur etiam post καῴκησαν, κᾀι οἱ πατέ- ρες ἀυτῶν. Agnoscit utrumque additamentum Aug. lib. II. in Exodum, quæst. 47. Aliter hic habere LXX. quam He- bræos codices notatum in utroque Thalmode. Illud & in terra Canaan ex LXX. additum & Samaritano. Rabbi Sa- lomon Jarchi vult subintelligi & in terris aliis. Sensus non malus erit, si interpreteris exilium illud Ægyptiacum duras- se ad annum usque quadringentesimum & tricesimum, (ex quo Deus id Abrahamo præsignificaverat. Gen. XV, 13. & sequentibus. Eo autem spatio annorum elapso, Deum vin- dictam in Ægyptios, ita ut tunc prædixerat, exercuisse, quo pertinent ea quæ statim sequuntur.

Sed quum LXX. interpp. & Samaritanum Co- dicem, quoad additamentum hoc, laudavit, quibus alias tantum tribuit, ut nonnunquam etiam post- ponat Ebræum textum, videri posset, quod in suspicionem etiam hic adducere eundem voluerit alicujus depravationis vel castrationis: Cujus omnino textum Ebræum reum egit Joh. Morin.

Cæterum facile vindicat eundem confensus Codicum omnium, Paraphrasium item Chaldaicarum, nec non Arabicæ R. Saadæ Gaon, ac Vulgatæ Latinæ: Thalmudis etiam ipsius utriusque, in quo fatente hîc Grotio, observata hæc differentia Ebræi textus & Paraphraseos Chaldaicæ est, & Commentatorum cùm Ebræorum tum Christianorum R. Levi causam, cur mentio Ægypti hîc tantum fiat, reddit: quod ibi præcipuum fuerit Ismëlitarum exilium à quo ceu potiori facta sit denominatio. Aug. explicat l. XVI. de C. D. cap. 24. non de continua duratione oppressionis Ægyptiacæ, sed quod ea intra illos annos futura sit. Eugubinus quidem & Genebrardus volunt servitutem durasse totos illos 430. annos: Sed hoc repugnat historiæ: & Apostolo Galat. 3. Rectius autem initium numeri statuitur in principio vocationis Abrahæ, à quo ad descensum Jacobi in Ægyptum effluxere 215. anni & totidem ab hoc usque ad exitum. Quapropter dicendum, quod tota peregrinatio comprehendatur Synecdoche incolatus in Ægypto, ut necesse non sit fingere σφάλμα, vel mendam in fontibus.

## 12:45
Verse 45.

A STRANGER AND A HIRED SERVANT SHALL NOT EAT OF IT] Namely, unless they wish of their own accord to be circumcised; for there was no right to compel them. This is understood both from the preceding words and from Numbers 9:14.

Latin:

Vers. 45.

ADVENA ET MERCENARIUS NON EDENT EX EO] Nempe nisi sponte velint circumcidi; neque enim eos cogendi jus erat. Intelligitur id tum ex præcedentibus verbis, tum Num. 9, 14.

## 12:46
Verse 46. NEITHER SHALL YOU BREAK A BONE OF IT.

Because of the parallel passage in John 19:39, some invent a double sense here: namely, literal and mystical. But there is no need for a double sense if we say that this concerns only the Paschal lamb (as the words of the text sound entirely only concerning that), whose bones were not to be broken: but that this is applied to Christ in John 19 because in Him was fulfilled what was prefigured in the type. Therefore, the significance of that act is indicated by John, not a new sense of the words is introduced, concerning which we spoke in the prolegomena of our Commentary on Genesis.

Latin:

Vers. 46. NEC OS ILLIUS CONFRINGETIS.

Ob locum Joh. 19, 39. geminum hîc nonnulli fingunt sensum: literalem nempe & mysticum. Sed non opus est sensu gemino, si dicamus, hîc tantum agi de agno Paschali (uti omnino tantum de illo verba textus sonant) cui consringi ossa non debuere: applicari autem hoc ad Christum Johan. 19. quia in ipso impletum est, quod in typo præfiguratum erat. Actus ergo istius significatio à Johanne indicatur non novus verborum sensus introducitur, qua de re diximus in prolegomenis Commentarii Nostri ad Genesin.

## 12:48
Verse 48. IF HE WISHES TO CROSS OVER AS A COLONY, AND KEEP THE PASSOVER OF THE LORD] The LXX: 'And if any proselyte comes to you to keep the Passover to the Lord.' In the Hebrew: 'When a stranger shall have sojourned with you and shall have made a passing over to the Lord': that is, he shall have subjected himself to the divine law, and shall have become a גר צדק.

Latin:

Vers. 48. VOLUERIT TRANSIRE COLONIAM, ET FACERE PHASE DOMINI] LXX. ἐὰν δέ τις προσέλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς προσήλυτος ποιήσαι τὸ πάσχα κυρίῳ. In Hebræo: Cum peregrinatus fuerit tecum peregrinus & fecerit transitum Domino: id est, divinæ legi se subjecerit, factus sit גר צדק.

## 13:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIII. The consecration of the firstborn. The pillar of cloud and fire.

Latin:

CAPUT XIII. Primogenitorum consecratio. Columna nubis, & ignis.

## 13:2
Verse 2. SANCTIFY UNTO ME EVERY FIRSTBORN.

The word sanctification is taken here for consecration, by which a thing is separated from common and profane use and destined for sacred use; because the firstborn was to be sanctified or consecrated to the Lord. But the firstborn is understood as that which is born first, whether second-born children followed or not; whence Helvidius wrongly concluded from the appellation of firstborn in Matthew 1:25 that the virgin Mary had other children by Joseph afterwards, because an only-begotten is also a firstborn. Moreover, the occasion and cause of the law concerning the firstborn to be consecrated to GOD is designated here: but that law is not promulgated so that it would obtain the force of obligation from that time. For this law was sanctioned only on the occasion of the liberation of the firstborn in Egypt; but it is not to be thought that Moses then immediately separated the firstborn in act at that time, when all were occupied in the departure, since in verse 11 it is designated that this law is to be observed in the land of Canaan. Even if, therefore, the status of the firstborn was also taken into account in the desert, which seems likely, because they could not immediately enter the land of Canaan, and even during that long time the order of this law seemed to require some observance: it is nevertheless manifest from Deut. 12, 1. 8. 9. that the Israelites were by no means so precisely obligated to observe such statutes in the desert.

Same verse. THAT WHICH OPENETH THE WOMB.

That the discourse here is about Christ and that he alone opened his mother's womb, that is, that he came forth from it while it was closed up to that point, whereas in other women the opening occurs through marital intercourse, some of the Fathers maintain: Origen, Hom. 14 on Luke; Ambrose on chapter 2 of Luke; Jerome, book 2 against Jovinian; Chrysostom, Homily on the Meeting of Christ; Amphilochius, Homily on the Purification; Isidore of Pelusium, book 1, Epistle 23; and especially Tertullian, book on the Flesh of Christ. But this explanation is too subtle and departs from the letter of the text, which deals with every firstborn: whence by this word or periphrasis, 'that which openeth the womb,' is designated the beginning of maternal generation, namely, that in this law the firstborn are to be understood with respect to the mother. Therefore, as far as the right of primogeniture is concerned, which involved priestly and royal dignity and a double inheritance, the reason is different: for in that, the firstborn held preeminence by reason of the father, Gen. 49, 3. Deut. 21, 17. But here the firstborn of the mother is referred to, in which sense Jacob had four firstborns: Reuben, Joseph, Gad, and Dan; compare Exod. 34, 19. And it seems that by this periphrasis, male offspring are also excluded if they are not the first born from the mother, but she had given birth to a female first. Some, with Cyril of Jerusalem in his Homily on the Meeting of the Lord and Pope Hormisdas in Epistle 1, chapter 3, think that that phrase does not denote only the offspring that is born first, but also that which comes forth in a natural way. Therefore, they deny that Christ pertains to this law, if indeed he was brought into the light with the womb closed. But Rupert of Avila and others more correctly observe that this phrase implies nothing other than the male offspring who is born first to his mother, because the usage of Scripture so dictates, where it deals with a closed or opened womb, to signify a barren or fruitful woman, and God is said to open it when He causes a woman to give birth, and the offspring when it is born. And in this sense Christ is truly said to have opened the womb when born, since this law is openly applied to him in Luke 2, 23, which, if it were to be said that it should be taken only regarding the birth of others, an inept sense would emerge: that Christ was brought to Jerusalem to be presented to the Lord, just as the firstborn ought to be presented, as it is written in the law of the Lord, namely for others, not for Christ, as being not so much excepted from this law as not comprehended under it. Nor, however, is it necessary that we believe with the Calvinists and certain others that Christ was born with the womb opened, since it is one thing when the womb is said to be opened by a phrase of Scripture simply by reason of birth, and another when the opening of the womb is understood physically, so that Mary is said to have given birth by the law of a breached body, which, since we deny it with most of our theologians, there is no need to leave room for Marcionite delusions or to attribute to Christ a phantastic body, which accusation of Rivet does not redound so much upon us as upon almost the entire choir of the Holy Fathers, inasmuch as they constantly assert that Christ was born with the womb closed, rose from a closed tomb, and entered to the disciples through closed doors.

Verse same. FOR ALL THINGS ARE MINE.

Thus the Vulgate ambiguously. The discourse is not about all things in common, but about the firstborn: the Hebrew text is clear: To me the very thing, to wit, that which opens the womb. But all firstborn are said to be of GOD by the special title of deliverance, because they were preserved so as not to be touched by the destroying angel, and also by the title of sanctification, because by the force of this law GOD willed them to be His own, inasmuch as He had redeemed them for Himself.

Latin:

Vers. 2. SANCTIFICA MIHI OMNE PRIMOGENITUM.

SAnctificationis vox hîc pro consecratione accipitur, qua res à communi & profano usu separatur & in sacrum usum destinatur; quia primogenitum Domino sanctificandum vel consecrandum erat. Primogenitum autem intelligitur id, quod primo natum est, sive successerint secundogenita, sive non; unde Helvidius perperam ex appellatione primogeniti, Matth. 1, 25. conclusit, virginem Mariam ex Josepho postmodum alios liberos sufcepisse, quia unigenitus etiam est primogenitus. Designatur autem hîc occasio & causa legis de primogenitis DEO consecrandis: non vero lex illa promulgatur, ut ex illo tempore vim obligationis obtineret. Nam occasione solum liberationis primogenitorum in Ægypto hæc lex sancita est; non autem putandum, quod tum statim actu separaverit Moses primogenitos eo tempore, quo omnes in egressu occupati erant, siquidem vers. 11. designatur, quod hæc lex in terra Canaan observanda fit. Etiamsi ergo in deserto quoque ratio primogenitorum habita sit, quod verisimile videtur, quia non statim in terram Canaan ingredi poterant, atque isto etiam diuturno tempore ordo hujus legis aliquam observationem requirere videbatur: neutiquam tamen adeo præcise ad talia statuta in deserto observanda obligatos fuisse Israëlitas, è Deut. 12, 1. 8. 9. manifestum est.

Vers. eod. QVOD APERIT VVLVAM.

De Christo hîc sermonem esse eumque solum uterum matris aperuisse, id'est, ex illo eo usque clauso prodiisse, cum in aliis mulieribus apertio fiat per maritalem συνꙋσίαν, è Patribus nonnulli statuunt, Origen. Hom. 14. in Luc. Ambros. in cap. 2. Luc. Hieron. lib. 2. contra Jovinian. Chrysost. Hom. de occursu Christi, Amphilochius Hom. de purificatione, Isid. Pelus. libr. 1. Epist. 23. & cumprimis Tertull. lib. de carne Christi. Sed hæc explicatio nimis arguta est, & abit à litera textus, qui de omni primogenito agit: unde sub hac voce vel periphrasi, quod aperit uterum, designatur principium generationis maternæ, quod nempe in hac lege primogeniti intelligendi sint respectu matris. Quocirca quantum ad jus primogenituræ, quod concernebat dignitatem sacerdotalem, regiam, ac duplæ hæreditatis, diversa est ratio: in eo enim primogenitus ratione patris ἐξοχὴν obtinebat, Gen. 49, 3. Deut. 21, 17. hic vero respicitur primogenitus matris, quo sensu Jacob quatuor primogenitos habuit, Rubenum, Josephum, Gad & Dan, conf. Exod. 34, 19. Et videtur hac periphrasi excludi quoque proles mascula, si non primo ex matre nata sit, sed fœminam ea prius ediderit. Nonnulli cum Cyrillo Hierosolymitano Homil. de occurs. Domini & Hormisda Papa Epistola 1. cap. 3. putant, phrasin illam non notare tantum prolem, quæ primo nascatur, sed etiam, quæ naturali modo egrediatur. Ideo negant, Christum ad hanc legem pertinere, siquidem is utero clauso in lucem editus sit. At rectius Rupertus Abulensis & alii observant, nihil aliud eam phrasin inferre, quam prolem masculam, quæ primo nascitur matri suæ, quia usus Scripturæ ita fert, ubi de clausa aut aperta vulva agit, ut significet sterilem, vel fœcundam mulierem, eamque aperire Deus dicitur cum efficit, ut mulier pariat, proles vero cum nascitur. Atque hoc sensu Christus vere natus matricem aperuisse dicitur, siquidem eidem Luc. 2, 23. lex hæc aperte applicetur, quæ si quoad aliorum nativitatem tantum accipienda dicatur, ineptus sensus prodibit: adductum fuisse Christum Hierosolymam, ut sisteretur Domino, quomodo sisti debebant primogenita, prout scriptum est in lege Domini, nimirum pro aliis, non pro Christo, utpote ab hac lege non tam excepto, quam sub eadem non comprehenso. Neque tamen necessum est, ut cum Calvinianis & aliis quibusdam credamus, Christum aperta Matrice natum esse, siquidem aliud est, cum aperta matrix phrasi Scripturæ dicitur ratione nativitatis simpliciter, aliud cum apertio matricis physice intelligitur, ut Maria peperisse dicatur patefacti corporis lege, quod cum negamus cum plerisque nostratibus Theologis, minime opus est, ut Marcioniticis deliriis locum relinquamus, aut Christo corpus phantasticum tribuamus, quod ἔγκλημα Riveti non tam in nos redundat, quam in S. Patrum Chorum fere universum, utpote qui Christum clauso utero natum, clauso sepulchro resurrexisse & per clausas fores ad discipulos intrasse, constanter asserunt.

Verf. eod. MEA ENIM SUNT OMNIA.

Ita ambigue Vulgata. Non de omnibus com- muniter, sed de primogenitis sermo est: textus E- bræus perspicuus est: Mihi ipsum scil. quod matri- cem aperit. DEI autem dicuntur esse omnia pri- mogenita titulo peculiari liberationis, quia con- servabantur, ne ab angelo exterminatore tange- rentur, nec non titulo sanctificationis, quia vi hu- jus legis ea DEUS sua esse voluit, utpote quæ sibi redemerat.

## 13:3
Verse 3. OUT OF THE HOUSE OF BONDAGE.

House is taken for a dwelling, or a place in which they served hard bondage, as Deut. 5, 6. Micah 6, 4. and thus it is called the house of the prison, Gen. 39, 20. the house of the bound, Judg. 16, 21.

Latin:

Verf. 3. DE DOMO SERVITUTIS.

Domus pro habitatione accipitur, vel loco, in quo duram serviebant servitutem, ut Deut. 5, 6. Mich. 6, 4. atque ita domus carceris, Genes. 39, 20. domus vin- ctorum Jud. 16, 21. dicitur.

## 13:4
Verse 4. IN THE MONTH OF NEW FRUITS.

In Hebrew the month אביב. Pagninus wrongly rendered it, the month of July, confusing the word אב by which July is denoted with אביב, which is taken appellatively, and therefore by the Chaldean it is called the month of ears, that is, in which the ears come out from the stalks, since the word אביב denotes a stalk, at the extremity of which is an ear. And therefore the month Nisan, corresponding to our March, is understood, in which also on the second day of unleavened bread a sheaf of grains first toasted, then beaten into flour, had to be offered, Lev. 2, 14. thus therefore by reason of the produce of the earth the festivities were chiefly assigned; the Passover was celebrated when the first fruits were appearing, the feast of Pentecost at the beginning of the new harvest, the feast of tabernacles when all the fruits had already been collected, so that in these sacred solemnities the paternal providence of GOD might be celebrated.

Latin:

Verf. 4. MENSE NOVARUM FRUGUM.

In Ebr. mense אביב. Pagninus perperam red- didit, mense Julio, vocem אב qua Julius notatur cum אביב confundens, quæ appellative accipitur, ideoque à Chaldæo mensis spicarum dicitur, id est, quo spicæ è calamis exeunt, siquidem vox אביב calamum notet, in cujus extremitate spica est. Ideo- que mensis Nisan Martio nostro respondens in- telligitur, quo etiam altera azymorum die manipu- lus tostis primum granis, deinde in farinam contu- sis offerri debebat, Lev. 2, 14. ita ergo ratione pro- ventuum terræ festivitates præcipue assignatæ fuere, Pascha celebratum erat cum primæ fruges se profe- rebant, festum Pentecostes sub initium novæ messis, festum tabernaculorum, cum omnes fruges jam colle- ctæ essent, ut in hisce sacris solemnibus providentia DEI paterna celebraretur.

## 13:8
Verse 8. THIS IS THAT WHICH THE LORD DID FOR ME.

Here Rivetus seeks the significant τὸ EST, or the tropical use of the substantive verb EST in the Vulgate; this is, he says, it cannot be understood otherwise than by reason of signification, this signifies, this represents that which the Lord has done for me. But there is no reason why the verb EST should be taken here otherwise than properly, that is, namely, that very thing which the Lord has done for me, which is clearer from the Hebrew text itself; for this the Lord has done for me, that is, for this, which the Lord has done for me, I celebrate that feast solemnly, etc. What shadow of a trope is here?

Latin:

Verf. 8. HOC EST, QUOD FECIT MIHI DO- MINUS.

Hic τὸ EST σημαντικὸν, vel usum tropicum verbi subst. EST in Vulgata quærit Rivetus, hoc est, inquit, non aliter intelligi potest, quam significa- tionis ratione, hoc significat, hoc repræsentat id, quod fecit mihi Dominus. Sed nulla causa est, cur aliter quam proprie verbum EST hîc accipi debeat, hoc est, scil. illud ipsum, quod fecit mihi Dominus, quod clarius ex ipso Ebræo textu liquet; propter hoc fe- cit Dominus mihi, id est, propter hoc, quod Dominus mihi fecit, festum illud solemniter celebro, &c. Quæ hic vel umbra tropi?

## 13:9
Ver. 9. AND IT SHALL BE AS A SIGN UPON THY HAND AND AS A MEMORIAL.

The Jews understand this grossly; therefore they affix the law of GOD inscribed on parchments to the arm, the forehead, the fringes, and the doorposts of the house, which are the Φυλακτήρια and fringes, which were widened by them, Matt. 23:5. Concerning the manner in which they are accustomed to be written by the Jews, see at length Sebastian Münster in his notes to the Hebrew Matthew, and especially Paulus Fagius on this passage. Drusius observes in book 2 on the three sects of the Jews that the Jews had even reached such a point of folly that they attributed Φυλακτήρια to GOD himself, in which it is written, what nation is as the people of Israel in the earth, which he drew from Jerome, a converted Jew of the holy faith. The Hebrew word Totaphot is derived by Schindler from טפף, because frontlets were worn. Aben-Ezra says it is like a memorial, ὡσεὶ μνημόσυνον. But it is manifest that those plates of the Jews or written parchments have no support here, because that proverbial locution of Scripture is most well-known, by which that is said to be for a sign or for a memorial in the hand or upon the arm, etc., which ought perpetually to be before the eyes or rather the mind. Compare.

Latin:

Verf. 9. ET ERIT QUASI SIGNUM IN MANU TUA ET QUASI MONUMENTUM.

Id Judæi crasse intelligunt, ideo legem DEI membranis inscriptam brachio, fronti, fimbriis, & ostiis domus affigunt, quæ sunt Φυλακτήρια & fim- briæ, quæ dilatabantur ab ipsis Matth. 23, 5. de mo- do, quo scribi ea solent à Judæis, prolixe Sebast. Münster. in notis ad Matth. Ebraicum, & impri- mis Paulus Fagius ad h. l. Drusius observat lib. 2. de tribus sectis Judd. eo etiam stultitiæ venisse Ju- dæos, ut DEO ipsi Φυλακτήρια tribuerint, in qui- bus scriptum sit, quæ est gens ut populus Israël in terra, quod hausit ex Hieronymo à sancta fide converso Ju- dæo. Vox Ebræa Totaphot à Schindl. à טפף incessit, deducitur, quia frontalia portabantur. Aben-Ezra dicit esse כמו זכרון ὡσεὶ μνημόσυνον. Manifestum autem est, laminas illas Judæorum aut conscriptas membranulas nihil hîc habere præsidii, quia locu- tio ista proverbialis Scripturæ notissima est, qua in signum aut in monumentum in manu aut super brachium &c. esse dicitur, quod perpetuo ocu- lis vel potius animo obversari debet. Confer.

## 13:11
Ver. 11. AND WHEN THE LORD SHALL HAVE BROUGHT THEE.

From this others gather that the law concerning the firstborn and unleavened bread was not observed in the desert. But we noted before that the Passover was also celebrated in the desert, and the Lord demanded the firstborn from the Israelites toward the end of the year of the exodus from Egypt, Num. 3:10 and 11, when he took the Levites in their place, the redemption of the firstborn having nevertheless been made. Compare what is at v. 2.

Latin:

Vers. 11. CUMQUE INTRODUXERIT TE DEUS.

Ex hoc colligunt alii legem de primogenitis & de pane azymo non fuisse in deserto observatam. Sed notavimus antea, etiam pascha in deserto celebratum esse, & exegit Dominus sub finem an- ni exitus ex Ægypto primogenita ab Israëlitis Num. 3, 10. & 11. cum eorum loco Levitas assumsit, facta tamen primogenitorum redemtione. Conf. quæ ad v. 2.

## 13:12
Ver. 12. IF ANY THING THAT IS FIRSTBORN IS AMONG THY CATTLE]

In Hebrew כל־פטר שגר, the former Hebrew word is explained by the latter Chaldean one.

Latin:

Vers. 12. SI QUID PRIMITIVUM EST IN PECORIBUS TUIS]

In Hebr. כל־פטר שגר vox prior Hebræa per Chaldæ- am alteram explicatur.

## 13:13
YOU SHALL EXCHANGE A SHEEP]

For a lamb, or a kid. For שׂה is in Hebrew, which, as we have said, signifies either one.

The word בהמה denotes not only beasts of burden, such as horses, donkeys, and camels; but also cattle. Some think that only the offering of cattle, sheep, goats, and oxen was commanded, because those which were to be offered here, verse 15, had to be sacrificed. But horses, mules, and camels were not sacrificed, Lev. 1, 2, and 10. They also bring forward a reason why the exchange of only the donkey among beasts of burden is enjoined here, with the mention of others omitted: namely, that the Hebrews in Egypt had almost only oxen, sheep, and goats among cattle, and donkeys among beasts of burden, whose firstborn GOD spared, since they were accustomed to use donkeys in place of horses and camels: whence even the princes themselves are read to have ridden on donkeys, Judg. 10, 4, and ch. 12, 14. But in Num. 18, 15, it is commanded that every firstborn (from every unclean animal) must be redeemed, under which not only donkeys, but also horses and camels are included; for these, therefore, a price of redemption was given: but for a donkey, a sheep was to be substituted, the use of which was in sacrifices and food. This opinion is certain: for that Tostatus and Cornelius understand an unclean animal in Num. 18 not as one that is such according to its species, but one that is unclean by accident, that is repugnant to all the circumstances of the passage, and to the usage of the word 'unclean' in this matter, and also to the exception of the price of a dog, which the Lord did not want to be brought into the sanctuary: whence it is evident that only that animal which was unclean according to its species was excepted, which God did not want to be redeemed.

Ver. 13. BUT IF YOU WILL NOT REDEEM IT, YOU SHALL KILL IT]

That was added so that the redemption would not be omitted.

Ver. same. EVERY FIRSTBORN OF MAN AMONG YOUR SONS YOU SHALL REDEEM WITH A PRICE.

For GOD did not want men to be sacrificed to Him, because the sacrifice of one man was destined for the sins of the whole world, who had to offer Himself for all, 1 Tim. 2, 5. Moreover, that price is expressed in Num. 18, 26, namely, five shekels. GOD could have consecrated the firstborn to Himself for worship; but because He had chosen the tribe of Levi for His own sake, He was content with such a price for the use of the sanctuary.

Latin:

MUTABIS OVE]

Agno, vel hædo. Nam שׂה est in He- bræo, quod, ut diximus, utrumvis significat.

Vox בהמה non tantum animalia bajula, qua- lia sunt equi, asini, cameli; sed etiam pecora notat. Putant aliqui tantum pecorum, ovium, caprarum & boum oblationem præceptam esse, quia immo- lari debebant, quæ hîc offerenda erant vers. 15. At equi, muli, cameli, non immolabantur, Lev. 1, 2. & 10.
