Causam etiam adferunt, cur solius asini è ju- mentis commutatio hîc injuncta sit, prætermissa aliorum mentione: quod sc. Ebræi in Ægypto fe- re tantùm habuerint boves, oves, & capras è peco- ribus, & asinos è jumentis, quorum primogenitis pepercerit DEUS, siquidem & asinis loco equo- rum, & camelorum uti consueverint: Unde ipsi quoque Principes asinis vecti leguntur Judic. 10, 4. & cap. 12, 14. At Num. 18, 15. jubetur, omne primogenitum (ex omni animali immundo) redi- mendum esse, sub quo non tantum asini, sed etiam equi & cameli comprehenduntur; pro his ergo pretium redemtionis dabatur: at pro asino repo- nenda erat ovis, cujus in sacrificiis & cibis usus. Quæ sententia certa est: nam quod animal immun- dum Num. 18. Tostatus & Cornelius intelligunt non quod tale est secundum speciem, sed quod ex accidenti immundum est, id repugnat omnibus loci circum- stantiis, & usurpationi vocis immundi in hac mate- ria, nec non exceptioni pretii canis, quod in sanctua- rium deferri noluit Dominus: unde constat, illud solum animal immundum secundum speciem exce- ptum fuisse, quod noluerit Deus redimi.

Vers. 13. QUOD SI NON REDEMERIS INTERFICIES]

Id ad- ditum ne omitteretur redemtio.

Vers. eod. OMNE PRIMOGENITUM HOMINIS DE FILIIS TUIS PRECIO REDIMES.

Noluit enim DEUS sibi homines sacrificari, quia unius hominis sacrificium destinatum erat pro peccatis totius mundi, qui pro omnibus se ipsum offerre debuit, 1. Tim. 2, 5. Pretium autem il- lud expressum est Num. 18, 26. quinque nempe Siclo- rum. Potuisset DEUS sibi primogenitos conse- crare in cultum; sed quia ejus causa elegerat tri- bum Levi, contentus fuit pretio tali in usum sanctuarii.

## 13:14
Ver. 14. TOMORROW] In the future. See Matt. 6, 34. Ver. 16. FRONTLETS] See Deut. 6, 8. Ver. 17. THINKING LEST PERCHANCE HE MIGHT REPENT, IF HE HAD SEEN WARS RISING UP AGAINST HIM] For long servitude breaks spirits.

Spoken anthropopathically. The cause, therefore, of the circuitous journey was the timidity of the people, lest, having seen the most warlike enemies, the Philistines, they might meditate on making a return to Egypt. There are, however, other causes for this detour: the drowning of Pharaoh in the Red Sea, the temptation of the Israelites in the desert, and their confirmation. through various miracles, the filling of the measure of the sins of the people of Canaan, Gen. 15, 16. A foreshadowing of the state of the faithful, who are led through the desert of the world into the heavenly inheritance, Heb. IV. Furthermore, ים סוף is commonly rendered as the Red Sea, but Mr. Varenius in this place, p. 204, argues that it should be rendered as the Sea of Reeds, because there were especially reeds there. While we willingly admit this, we nevertheless do not doubt that it is also rightly called the Red Sea. See what is said at Ex. 10, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 14. CRAS] In posterum. Vide Matth. 6, 34. Vers. 16. FRONTALIA] Vide Deut. 6, 8. Vers. 17. REPUTANS NE FORTE POENITERET EUM, SI VIDISSET ADVERSUM SE BELLA CONSURGERE] Longa enim servitus frangit animos.

Dictum ἀνθρωποπαθῶς. Causa ergo ambagum itineris erat populi meticulositas, ne sc. visis hostibus bellicosissimis Philistæis reditum acturum in Ægy- ptum meditaretur. Sunt tamen & aliæ hujus circum- ductionis causæ, submersio Pharaonis in mari rubro, tentatio Israëlitarum in deserto, & confirmatio eorum per varia miracula, impletio mensuræ peccatorum populi Canaan, Gen. 15, 16. adumbratio status fide- lium, qui per desertum mundi deducuntur in cœ- leftem hæreditatem, Ebr. IV. Cæterum ים סוף mare rubrum redditur communiter, quod vero mare algosum reddendum esse, quod maxime ibi fuerint arundines, disputat Dn. Varenius in h. l. p. 204. Quod uti lubenter admittimus, recte tamen mare rubrum id etiam vocari non dubitamus. Vid. quæ ad Ex. 10, 16. dicta.

## 13:18
Ver. 18. AND ARMED THEY WENT UP] In Hebrew חמשׁים

fifthed. Theodotion: acting by fives. The LXX interpret this as the fifth generation. But Kimchi: girded at the fifth rib in a military manner: for the noun חמשׁ stands for the fifth rib, 2 Sam. 2, 23. Following this sense, Aquila & Symmachus translated it here as καθωπλισμένοι (armed), and the LXX themselves in Joshua 1, 14 as εῡζωνοι (well-girded), and in the same book 4, 12 as διεσκευασμένοι (equipped).

It also does not seem sufficiently convenient to others that the Hebrew word חמשׁים be rendered as armed, since it denotes those who are fifthed, that is, by fives, or as Theodotion expresses it word for word, πεμταίζοντες, proceeding in a number of five. Meanwhile, it cannot be denied that that word also sometimes denotes armed men, as R. Abraham, Aben-Ezra, Masius & others observe at Jos. 1, v. 14, and thus Aquila & Symmachus rendered it here as καθωπλισμένοι, and Jerome, in question 2 to Damasus, teaches that all the benches of the synagogues testify that it is rightly translated so. For since soldiers armed in battle proceed by fives, metaleptically חמשׁים or by fives denotes armed men: whether, however, in this place only the order & military disposition is designated, that they were arranged in groups of five, and did not set out in confusion like those in a tumult or fugitives, or whether it is also designated that they proceeded armed, can be a matter of doubt here, because it is not probable that the needy Hebrews had procured arms for themselves in Egypt, or that, as Cornelius wishes, they had received them on loan from the Egyptians, and Josephus and Philo testify that they went out of Egypt unarmed: nor is there reason to say with Rivetus that the word went up should sometimes be taken more broadly, so that it is not restricted to the first day of the departure; for he himself thinks that they were not unarmed afterwards, but rather that they used the arms of the Egyptians washed up on the shore: that does not fit this place, where Moses wished to indicate what kind of state they were in when they departed in the very exit.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET ARMATI ASCENDERUNT] In Hebræo חמשׁים

quintati. Theodotion πεμταίζοντες. Id LXX. interpretantur generatione quinta. At Kimchi: accincti quintam costam militariter: nam nomen חמשׁ pro quinta costa est 2. Sam. 2, 23. Hunc sensum secuti Aquila & Symmachus verterunt hic καθωπλισμένοι, & ipsi LXX. Josuæ 1, 14. εῡζωνοι, & eodem li- bro 4, 12. διεσκευασμένοι.

Non satis commode etiam aliis videtur vox Ebræa חמשׁים reddi armati, cum notet quintatos, hoc est, quinos, vel ut Theodotio ad verbum expri- mit, πεμταίζοντες numero quinario incedentes. In- terim negari non potest, vocem etiam illam quandoque armatos notare, quemadmodum è R. Abraham, Aben-Ezra, Masius & alii ad Jos. 1. cap. v. 14. observant, atque ita reddidit hîc Aqui- la & Symmachus καθωπλισμένοι, & recte ita ver- ti, universa Synagogarum subsellia testari docet Hieron. quæst. 2. ad Damasum. Nam cum qui- ni in acie incedant milites armati, metaleptice חמשׁים vel quini notat armatos: utrum tamen hoc in loco solum designetur ordo & dispositio militaris, quod in quincurias dispositi, non more tumultu- antium & fugitivorum confusi profecti sint, an vero etiam designetur, quod armati incesserint, dubium hîc esse potest, quia non probabile sit, Ebræos inopes sibi arma comparasse in Ægypto, aut quod Cornelius vult, ab Ægyptiis ea commo- dato accepisse, & testatur Josephus ac Philo, quod inermes ex Ægypto egressi sint: neque est, quod dicas cum Riveto, verbum ascenderunt aliquan- do latius accipiendum esse, ut non adstringatur ad primum diem profectionis; putat enim ipse postmodum non inermes fuisse, imo arma Ægyptio- rum in littus expulsa in usum vocasse: id non con- gruit huic loco; ubi quales in ipso egressu discesse- rint, Moses indicare voluit.

## 13:19
Ver. 19. AND MOSES TOOK THE BONES OF JOSEPH WITH HIM.

Some gather from Acts 7, 16 that Moses also carried with him the bones of the other Patriarchs, the brothers of Joseph, even though only Joseph is mentioned here, because of the oath which he had exacted from the Israelites; others, however, think that the rest of the patriarchs were translated by their own people into the land of Canaan immediately after their death: compare what we said at Genesis 47, verse 29.

Latin:

Vers. 19. TULIT QUOQUE MOSES OSSA JOSEPH SECUM.

Etiam aliorum Patriarcharum fratrum Jose- phi ossa secum extulisse Mosen, nonnulli ex Act. 7, 16. colligunt, utut hic Josephi tantum mentio fiat, ob Juramentum, quod ab Israëlitis exegerat; alii tamen cæteros patriarchas immediate post mortem à suis in terram Cananæam translatos fu- isse arbitrantur: conf. quæ diximus ad Genes. 47. vers. 29.

## 13:21
Ver. 21. IN A PILLAR OF FIRE AND CLOUD.

Interpreters note four miracles given to the Hebrews in their departure: (1.) that none of them was sick in such a great crowd that he had to be left in Egypt, Psalm 105, 37. (2.) That their sandals & clothes grew with the children for 40 years, and were not worn out, (3.) Manna, (4.) the pillar of fire and cloud, which some consider to be different. But others more correctly, from verse 19 of chapter 14. & Num. 9, 21. They conclude that there was one and the same cloud, similar to a pillar, as far as straightness and shape are concerned, and narrow in terms of thickness, which at night rose up into a fiery pyramidal shape; but by day it was spread out in the manner of a cloud: nor was it truly fire, but the appearance or species of fire, as is held in Num. 9, 15, namely a glowing brightness, such as appears in denser clouds into which solar rays opportunely insinuate themselves; for true fire would have been inconvenient because of the power of heating and burning, unless one imagines that it was inhibited by a continuous miracle. Moreover, this cloud also provided the Israelites with the use of a covering and a kind of parasol, when they had to travel during the day, since the pillar of cloud was used not only to show the way, which no one knew, by which i.e. GOD had decided to lead them through the deserts of Arabia; but it also had to protect the camp from the heat of the sun, which Cajetan and Tostatus rashly deny, since that is quite openly concluded from Psalm 104, 39 and Wis. 10, 17. Whence it must be said that that cloud, in which the Lord went before, not only went ahead, but also spread itself out and, as it were, scattered another cloud from itself during the day, so that the Hebrews walked under that cloud as if under a parasol. Some distinguish the cloud from the pillar from Num. 14, 14, 'Let your cloud protect them and in a pillar of cloud you go before them,' and they make one cloud protecting, another directing; but this Num. 14 can be taken as an explanation: and only a twofold use of the cloud is indicated, directive and protective, but not therefore is the cloud to be distinguished from the pillar or a double cloud to be imagined, since the same material which rose up into a pyramidal shape could spread itself out in the manner of a cloud and provide that twofold use. Jerome seems to assert that this cloud first appeared in Etham. But it is more correctly established that it was first seen in Rameses, from where the Hebrews departed, because it had to direct them throughout the entire journey; for mention is also made of it first at that station of the bones of Joseph, which nevertheless were carried from Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 21. IN COLUMNA IGNIS ET NUBIS.

Notant Interpretes quatuor miracula Ebræis in profectione data, (1.) quod nemo eorum æger fuerit in tanta turba, ut relinqui debuerit in Æ- gypto, Psalm. 105, 37. (2.) Quod calcei & vestes per 40. annos cum pueris creverint, nec absumti sint, (3.) Manna, (4.) columnam ignis & nubis, quam nonnulli pro diversa habent. Rectius autem alii ex vers. 19. cap. 14. & Num. 9, 21. unam & eandem nu- bem fuisse colligunt columnæ similem, quantum ad rectitudinem & figuram & quoad crassitudinem an- gustam, quæ noctu in figuram pyramidalem igne- am exsurrexerit; die vero expansa fuerit in mo- dum nubis: neque vero verus ignis fuit, sed aspe- ctus ignis vel species, ut habetur Num. 9, 15. ruti- lans nempe fulgor, qualis apparet in nubibus den- sioribus, in quas se opportune radii solares infi- nuant; nam ignis verus incommodus fuisset ob vim calefaciendi & urendi, nisi eam continuo mi- raculo inhibitam fuisse quis fingat. Hæc autem nubes usum etiam præbebat Israëlitis velaminis, & umbellæ cujusdam, cum interdiu incedendum esset, siquidem non tantum ad ostendendam viam columna nubis adhibita fuerit, quam nemo no- verat, qua sc. DEUS eos per deserta Arabiæ de- ducere constituerat; sed etiam castra ab æstu solis protegere debuerit, quod temere negant Cajeta- nus & Tostatus, cum id satis aperte colligatur è Psalm. 104, 39. & Sap. 10, 17. Unde dicendum, quod nubes illa, in qua præcedebat Dominus, non tantum præiverit, sed etiam sese expanderit & quasi aliam nubem interdiu ex se sparserit, ut ambularent Ebræi sub nube ista quasi sub umbella. Nonnulli distinguunt nubem à columna è Num. 14, 14. Nubes tua protegat illos & in columna nubis præcedas eos, faciuntque aliam nubem protegentem, aliam dirigentem; sed hæc Num. 14. κατ' ἐπεξή- γησιν accipi possunt: & geminus solum nubis usus indicatur, directorius, & protectorius, non autem ideo vel nubes à columna distinguenda vel gemi- na nubes fingenda est, cum expandere se potue- rit in modum nubis eadem materia, quæ in figu- ram pyramidalem exsurgebat, usumque gemi- num istum præstare. Nubem hanc in Ethan pri- mum apparuisse, videtur asserere Hieronymus. Sed rectius statuitur primum visa in Rameses, unde egreffi Ebræi sunt, quia in tota profectione ipsos dirigere debebat; Nam & primum mentio fit in illa statione ossium Josephi, quæ tamen ex Ægypto translata sunt.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV. The drowning of Pharaoh.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV. Pharaonis submersio.

## 14:2
Verse 2.

OVER AGAINST PI-HAHIROTH WHICH IS BETWEEN MIGDOL AND THE SEA OVER AGAINST BAAL-ZEPHON

It was an idol for guarding the borders and for preventing flight from the kingdom. It is named for this reason, so that it may appear how it could do nothing against the Israelites.

These things smack of the fables of the Hebrews, from which Fagius [derived] those things. See Selden, On the Syrian Gods, Syntagma 1, ch. 3. Baal-zephon was a city, Num. 33, 7. Baal is numbered among the towns, 1 Chron. 5, 33, and can be explained, in Selden's judgment, as בעל צפון, the northern Baal. Compare Eusebius, book IX, Preparation. Clement of Alexandria, Stromata 1. The LXX render that פי החירות with the word 'of the farmstead,' Flaminius Nobilius [renders it] 'over against' the suburbs: others more correctly [render it] the mouth or valley of Hiratha, which they derive from חור, a hole, i.e., an entrance into a cave, because it was a valley between two high rocks; מגדול denotes a tower, a castle, or a fortification. Everything contributes to expressing the place, which was clearly designated by these marks when Moses was writing.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

E REGIONF PHIHAHIROTH QVÆ EST INTRA MAGDALUM ET MARE CONTRA BEELSEPHON]

Idolum erat finibus custodiendis, & ad impediendam fugam è regno. Ideo nominatur, ut appareat quam nihil contra Israë- litas potuerit.

Sapiunt hæc fabulas Ebræorum, è quibus ista Fagius. Vid. Seldenus de Diis Syr. Synt. 1. c. 3. Baalzephon urbs fuit Numer. 33, 7. Baal inter op- pida numeratur 1. Par. 5, 33. & explicari potest, Seldeno judice בעל צפון Baal septentrionalis. Conf. Eusebius l. IX. Præparat. Clemens Alex. Strom. 1. Illud פי החירות, LXX. reddunt voce ἐπαύλεως, Fla- minius Nobilius (è regione) suburbiorum: alii re- ctius os vel vallem Hiratha, quod à חור foramen deducunt q. d. ingressum in speluncam, quia vallis fuit inter duas rupes excelsas; מגדול turrim, castel- lum, sive munitionem notat. Omnia ad locum ex- primendum faciunt, qui hisce notis, cum Moses scriberet, luculenter designatus fuit.

## 14:4
Verse 4.

I WILL HARDEN THE HEART OF PHARAOH.

When Pharaoh had seen that they had not betaken themselves into the desert for three days only, but that Moses was fleeing altogether with the people, and that they were hemmed in by the Red Sea and the rocks, the Pharaonic malice and tyranny seized upon this opportunity, which was presented to his imagination either by messengers or immediately by GOD, with God permitting, but not positively intending, his obstinacy, so that he might at length be hurried to the punishment which he had long deserved.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

INDURABO COR PHARAONIS.

Cum Pharao vidisset, non ad tres dies tan- tum in desertum se contulisse, sed omnino fu- gere Mosen cum populo, ac mari rubro, & rupi- bus concludi, quam occasionem sive per nuncios, si- ve immediate à DEO Phantasiæ ejus objectam ma- litia & tyrannis Pharaonica arripuit, Deo permit- tente, non autem positive intendente obstinationem ejus, ut ad pœnam, quamdiu promeruerat, tan- dem raperetur.

## 14:7
Verse 7. SIX HUNDRED CHARIOTS.

Because they used to fight in ancient times with scythed chariots: with which they mowed down men, and beasts of burden, and crops, and from which soldiers fought at the same time.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SEXCENTOS CURRUS.

Quia pugnabant olim falcatis curribus: quibus demetebant homines, & jumenta atque segetes & e quibus simul milites præliabantur.

## 14:13
Verse 13. FOR THE EGYPTIANS WHOM YOU NOW SEE.] He reads as we do, כי אשר. But the LXX read כאשר, in the manner of.

That is therefore an oversight of the LXX Interpreters, as many such things are discovered, which Hottinger noted in his Thesaurus Philologicus, and we in the Critico Sacro. But a different reading is not to be gathered from this.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ÆGYPTIOS ENIM QUOS NUNC VIDETIS.] Legit ut nos, כי אשר. At LXX. כאשר, τρόποι.

Παρόραμα ergo illud LXX. Interpp. uti multa talia deprehenduntur, quæ notavit Hottinger. in The-saur. Philol. & nos in Critico Sacro. Non vero hinc diversa lectio colligenda.

## 14:17
Verse 17. BUT I WILL HARDEN THE HEART OF THE EGYPTIANS, THAT THEY MAY PURSUE THEM.

Which was done while GOD set before their eyes and minds the tracks of the Hebrews crossing on dry foot, and took away fear from them, and so blinded them that, pursuing the Israelites, they were overwhelmed by the sea.

Latin:

Vers. 17. EGO AUTEM INDURABO COR ÆGYPTIORUM, UT PERSEQUAN-TUR EOS.

Quod factum est, dum oculis & mentibus eo-rum vestigia Ebræorum sicco pede transeuntium objecit DEUS, & metum ipsis ademit, adeoque ipsos excæcavit, ut insequentes Israëlitas mari ob-ruerentur.

## 14:19
Verse 19. BEHIND.

The pillar of cloud stood within the camps of the Egyptians and the Israelites, yet it emitted certain rays from afar before the front line of the Israelites, which showed them the way. It is called the Pillar of cloud, from which Cajetan gathers that these things happened by day, because the pillar of cloud appeared during the day. But this does not agree with those things which are added immediately, and the cloud was dark and illuminated the night. And therefore it must be said that it is called the pillar of cloud, which previously went before the Israelites until they arrived at the Red Sea; but at night the fiery pillar provided light. This is what we said before; that the cloud was behind the Israelites, but that it projected rays of light and fire from itself to the Hebrews from afar, and thus was like a pillar of fire, so that it is clear that it was entirely the same pillar which clouded the Egyptians, but illuminated the Israelites.

But it appears that the Hebrews approached the sea at the beginning of the night and the first watch, and after a burning and strong wind had continuously blown and divided the channel, from the beginning of the night until midnight, the Hebrews entered the channel of the sea after midnight in the third watch, and around the middle of the fourth watch they all escaped to the other shore. But the Egyptians, pursuing the Hebrews, entered the sea around the end of the third watch: but as morning approached in the fourth watch, when the Hebrews were already at the ford, with Moses striking the waters, they were overwhelmed by them returning to their original place.

Latin:

Vers. 19. POST TERGUM.

Stetit columna nubis intra castra Ægyptio-rum & Israëlitarum, radios tamen emisit quos-dam eminus ante primam aciem Israëlitarum, qui viam ipsis ostenderent. Vocatur Columna nubis, unde colligit Cajetanus, hæc de die contigisse, quia columna nubis interdiu apparebat. Sed hoc non congruit illis, quæ adduntur immediate, & nu-bes erat tenebrosa & illuminabat noctem. Ideoque dicendum, columnam nubis vocari, quæ antea præ-cessit Israëlitas, donec ad mare rubrum perveni-rent; noctu autem igneam factam columnam lu-men præbuisse. Hoc est, quod antea diximus; fuisse nubem post tergum Israëlitarum, sed Ebræis ex se radios lucis & ignis eminus projecisse, adeoque in-star columnæ ignis fuisse, ut constet, eandem omni-no fuisse columnam, quæ obnubilavit Ægyptios, il-luminavit autem Israëlitas.

Sub initium autem noctis & primæ vigiliæ E-bræos ad mare accessisse apparet, postquam vero ventus urens & validus jugiter flando alveum divi-sisset, ab initio noctis usque ad noctem mediam, Ebræi post mediam noctem in tertia vigilia maris alveum ingressi sunt, & circa medium quartæ vigi-liæ evaserunt omnes ad alterum littus. Ægyptii vero circa finem tertiæ vigiliæ Ebræos insequentes ingressi sunt mare: sed mane approximante in quarta vigilia, cum Ebræi jam in vado essent, Mose aquas percutiente, ab iisdem in pristinum locum redeuntibus oppressi sunt.

## 14:20
Verse 20. AND THE CLOUD WAS DARK AND ILLUMINATING THE NIGHT.

It was dark to the Egyptians, because it was so thickened that they could neither see nor grasp the Hebrews: but they were following the cloud going before. But to the Hebrews the same cloud was fiery, and was illuminating the night: whence the Chaldean did not poorly render: There was a cloud and darkness to the Egyptians, but to Israel there was light all the night.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET ERAT NUBES TENEBROSA ET ILLUMINANS NOCTEM.

Tenebrosa erat Ægyptiis, quia ita densaba-tur, ut Ebræos neque cernere neque apprehende-re potuerint: nubem autem præcedentem inseque-rentur. Sed Ebræis eadem nubes ignea erat, no-ctemque illuminabat: unde non male reddidit Chaldæus: Erat nubes & obscuritas Ægyptiis, Israëlï autem erat lux tota nocte.

## 14:21
Ver. 21. AND WHEN MOSES HAD STRETCHED OUT HIS HAND OVER THE SEA, THE LORD TOOK IT AWAY BY A BLOWING WIND.

From this translation a doubt is rendered, whether the division of the sea was made by means of the wind, or not? Most interpreters judge that the same is not to be attributed to the wind, since the wind ceased while the Hebrews were crossing, but the sea remained divided; who therefore attribute to the wind only that it dried up the channel already divided and emptied of waters, and that it took away what still remained of the moist and muddy, so that they might cross on dry foot. But from the Hebrew it is manifest that the wind was employed for the division of the sea, since the words of the source are thus: And the Lord made the sea go away by an east wind. Concerning which wind Mr. Varenius speaks at length on page 217, noting that it is poorly rendered by the Vulgate as BURNING, when it ought to be explained as EASTERN and the Southeast wind is understood. Compare Exod. 10, 13. And therefore, although the extraordinary power of GOD was exerted here, both in exciting such a wind and in producing by the same an effect superior to every natural cause, yet the division of the sea was made by GOD through the wind propelling and drying the waters, as Basil rightly observed in the Catena. If it be said that the same wind could not impel and dry the waters and at the same time hold them back, lest they flow down into the empty channel, one must admit this regarding a wind acting by natural force; but here the operation was extraordinary; nor is it to be doubted that GOD also acted immediately here, even though that extraordinary wind also had its own extraordinary operation, especially since it is likely that the wind ceased while the Hebrews were crossing; for then it is necessary that by a hidden divine power the waters, which GOD had first separated by the wind, were held back until they had crossed. The fiction of the Gentiles and Memphites in Eusebius, book IX of the Preparation, last chapter, that the division was made by the natural reciprocation of the sea, has no place, because the reflux of the sea only bares the shores of waters, but does not truly cleave the sea so that a wide path is made in the middle of it and a passage through the dry sea is opened, nor is it in any way likely that the Egyptians, whose empire reached as far as the Red Sea, were ignorant of that flux and reflux of the sea, and that it was known to Moses alone.

Ver. same. AND THE WATER WAS DIVIDED.

There must have been a huge division and gap, so that such a great multitude of men and animals and so many ranks could cross at the same time, because they all crossed in half a night. Adrichomius teaches that the width of the Red Sea is six leagues. The tradition of Origen, that that sea was divided into 12 sections so that the 12 tribes could cross at the same time, rests on no foundation; indeed, it contradicts the text, because the waters are said to have stood like a wall on the right and on the left, whence there must have been only a single division of the sea, but a very wide gap, as Philo, Theodoret, and Euthymius observe.

They are therefore called divisions in Psalm CXXXV, v. 13, either because of that amplitude, because one division was like many, or so that the two divided sides might be designated.

Sanctius from Wisdom 19, verse 7, adds another miracle, namely that the riverbed suddenly sprouted and bloomed like a field. But there is no trace of it in Canonical Scripture. Jansenius therefore rightly understands that in the book of Wisdom figuratively, that they passed through so pleasantly, as if they were passing through a field blooming with leaves and flowers.

That the traces of the entry and passage of the Hebrews and the tracks of the chariots and the ruts of the wheels still remain in the Red Sea is a story of Orosius, book 1, chapter 10.

Latin:

Vers. 21. CUMQUE EXTENDISSET MOSES MA-NUM SUPER MARE, ABSTULIT ILLUD DOMINUS FLANTE VENTO.

Ex hac translatione dubium redditur, an di-visio maris mediante vento facta fuerit, nec ne? Plerique Interpp. eandem non esse tribuendam vento censent, siquidem ventus cessarit, dum transirent Ebræi, mare autem divisum manebat; qui proinde vento id tantum tribuunt, quod alveum jam divisum, & aquis evacuatum plane exsiccarit, & quod adhuc supererat humidi & lutulenti abstulerit, ut sicco pede transirent. Sed ex Ebræo manifestum est, ventum adhibitum fuisse ad maris divisionem, cum ita habeant verba fontis: Et Dominus abire fecit mare per ventum orientalem. De quo vento prolixe Dn. Varenius pag. 217. quod male à Vulg. URENS reddatur, cum exponi debeat ORIENTALIS & Eurus intelligatur. Conf. Exod. 10, 13. Ideoque licet vis extraordinaria DEI hîc exserta sit, tum in excitando tali vento, tum in effectu per eundem omni causa naturali superiore edendo, facta tamen divisio maris à DEO est per ventum aquas propellentem & exsiccantem, ut recte observavit Basil. in Catena. Si dicatur, eundem ventum non potuisse aquas impellere & siccare & simul easdem sistere, ne in alveum vacuum defluerent, fateri id oportet de vento vi naturali agente; sed hîc extraordinaria fuit operatio; neque dubitandum est, immediate quoque DEUM hîc aliquid egisse, etsi ventus quoque ille extraordinarius suam habuerit extraordinariam operationem, inprimis cum verisimile sit, ventum cessasse, dum transirent Ebræi; tum enim necessum est, occulta vi divina aquas, quas DEUS primo per ventum separaverat, fuisse retentas, donec transiissent. Gentilium & Memphitarum apud Euseb. l. IX. præpar. cap. ult. commentum, quod reciprocatione maris naturali divisio facta fuerit, locum nullum habet, quia refluxus maris nudat tantum aquis littora, non vero mare findit, ut in medio ejus amplum iter fiat, & transitus per siccum pateat mare, neque ullo modo verisimile sit, Ægyptios, quorum imperium usque ad mare rubrum pertingebat,illum maris fluxum & refluxum ignorasse, eumque soli Mosi notum fuisse.

Vers. eod. DIVISAQUE EST AQUA.

Ingentem oportet fuisse divisionem & hiatum, ut tanta hominum & animantium multitudo ac tot ordines simul transire possent, quia dimidia nocte omnes transiere. Maris rubri latitudinem sex leucarum esse docet Adrichomius. Origenis traditio, quod in 12. sectiones mare illud divisum fuerit, ut simul 12. tribus transirent, nullo nititur fundamento, imo contrariatur textui, quia aquæ dicuntur stetisse instar muri à dextra & à sinistra, unde unicam tantum oportet fuisse maris divisionem, sed hiatum amplissimum, ut Philo, Theodoretus & Euthymius observant.

Dicuntur ergo divisiones Psalm. CXXXV. v. 13. five ob amplitudinem istam, quia una divisio erat instar plurium, seu ut designentur latera duo divisa.

Sanctius è Sap. XIX. vers. 7. addit aliud miraculum, quod nempe alveus subito germinarit & vernarit instar campi. Sed ejus in Scriptura Canonica nullum est vestigium. Recte ergo figurate id intelligit in libro Sapientiæ Jansenius, quod ita jucunde transierint, ac si per campum frondibus & floribus vernantem transirent.

Vestigia ingressus & transitus Ebræorum & tractus curruum, rotarumque orbitas adhuc manere in mari rubro, Orosii fabula est libr. 1. cap. 10.

## 14:22
THROUGH THE MIDST OF THE DRY SEA] A semicircle having been made in the sea: not from shore to the opposite shore.

Latin:

Vers. 19. PER MEDIUM SICCI MARIS] Semicirculo in mari facto: non à littore ad littus oppositum.

## 14:24
Verse 24.

AND THE LORD LOOKING DOWN UPON THE CAMP OF THE EGYPTIANS THROUGH THE PILLAR OF FIRE] The angel mentioned above in verse 19, representing the person of GOD. Because the Angel is called Lord, it must be said that this angel did not represent the person of GOD, for that is never done in that manner, so that an angel is called Jehovah Lord in the nominative case, or that he claimed for himself that name most proper to GOD, which the Hebrews call κατ’ ἐξοχὴν שׁם, and which GOD protests he wishes to give to no one, Isa. 42:6, but that the angel of the face of the Lord was truly a divine person, who REDEEMED AND SAVED the people, Isa. 63:13, who alone is called both Angel and Jehovah. Who also promised the leading out and liberation to his people in Exod. 3, and now executes that promise. For the text indicates most evidently that Jehovah himself, αὐτοπροσώπως, looked forth from the pillar of fire and cloud. Teaching that the same one looked forth, who caused terror in the Army of the Egyptians, and cast them down: and who spoke to Moses in verse 26, 27, which Moses testifies in those same verses was done by Jehovah himself, in whom the people believed, as also in verse 30, 31. To whom he sang the Ecclesiastical Canticle with the people, chap. 15, Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously magnified, he has cast the horse and his rider into the sea. My strength and my praise is the Lord, and he has become my SALVATION. זה אלי this is my GOD, Who is that Lord, who has become for us לישועה for salvation, if not the Son of God, who has become our Jesus? For of him the Apostle says: JESUS Christ yesterday, today the same and forever, Heb. 13:8. Whom he also designates in verse 13 by the word גאל, peculiarly proper to the Son of God the Redeemer. Therefore the Latin Church, according to the Vulgate version, which Grotius cannot despise because of the authority of the Council of Trent, celebrated the same thus: Jud. v. 5. Since Jesus, saving the people from the land of Egypt, secondly destroyed those who did not believe. Nor is it said here alone that Jehovah himself was present in the cloud and led the Israelites. For this is always attributed to the Lord, never to a created Angel: Num. 14:14. They have heard that you, O Lord, are among this people, and your cloud stands over them and you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day, and in a pillar of fire by night, verse 15, that you have killed such a multitude, Deut. 31:3. Jehovah your GOD himself will go before you, Numbers 12:5 ff. The Lord descended in a pillar of cloud, and stood at the entrance of the tabernacle, and said to Aaron and Miriam, Deut. 31:16. The Lord appeared there in a pillar of cloud. Conf. Psalm 99:7, Exod. 33:2 ff., chap. 34:5 ff. The same Angel, who led the Israelites and is called Jehovah, who descended in the cloud, and preached about Jehovah, and is called the face of the Lord and all the goodness of GOD, and is finally introduced as Mediator between GOD and men, lest GOD, who is a consuming fire, destroy and wipe out the people because of sins. But who is that Angel of the Lord, if not the Son of GOD, the Angel of the new covenant, GOD blessed forever above all, Rom. 9:5, Jehovah our righteousness, Jer. 23:6, who is called the face of GOD, the image of GOD the Father, χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως καὶ ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ, Col. 1:18, Heb. 1:3, in whom is all the goodness of GOD, because as the Father has life in himself, so he has given to the Son to have life in himself, John 5:26. All things, he says, that the Father has, are mine, John 16:15. Who is the one mediator of GOD and men, 1 Tim. 2:5. and here he offered himself to be seen by Moses in an assumed human form: as one to whom it had been said, you will not be able to see my face (NAKED): but you will see my back parts or back, namely in an assumed form, which was a type and shadow of the human nature to be assumed in the fullness of time. All of which will become even clearer if they are compared with Exod. 23:20, and

what we shall say there. Certainly some of the Hebrews also, because it was too manifest that the Angel is here called the Lord, saw—what Grotius could not see here—that the Son of GOD is designated. R. Moses Gerundensis says, it is written, And the angel of his face saved them. Doubtless that Angel, who is the face of GOD; of whom it was said: my face will go before and I will cause you to rest. Finally, that is the Angel of whom the Prophet says: And suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to his temple, and the angel of the covenant, whom you desire. And again in another place, where he explains that verse, My face will go before and I will cause you to rest, he left it written thus; to bring it into a few words: Observe, he says, attentively, what these things mean. For Moses and the Israelites always desired the first angel; but who that was, they could not truly understand. For they did not perceive it from others; nor did they sufficiently attain it by prophetic notion. But the face of GOD signifies GOD himself, which is confessed by all Interpreters. But that no one could understand these things even in a dream, unless he is learned in the mysteries of the law. And after a few words: My face will precede, that is, the angel of the covenant, whom you desire: in whom my face will be seen, of whom it was said: In an acceptable time I will hear you. For my name is in him, and I will cause you to rest, or I will cause that he himself be gentle and kind to you. Nor may he lead you by rigid law; but placidly and clemently. These things are from Moses Gerundensis in Andreas Masius on Josh. chap. 5. Which the Targum Onkelos also seems to hint at: chap. 14:31, explaining the words of Moses, They believed in the Lord, thus: They believed in the WORD OF THE LORD: and that chap. 15, verse 7, THE LORD has become for me for salvation, illustrating it with this paraphrase: He said to his Word, and (the word) was for me as a Redeemer. But among the orthodox Fathers it is entirely beyond doubt and ὁμολογυμένως certain that the angel, who appeared in the pillar of cloud, and is called Jehovah, did not represent the person of the Lord, but was the divine person of GOD. Which was defined in the Council of Antioch: whose words we shall transcribe here from the Synodal Epistle: And elsewhere: And the Lord said to Moses: And this word, which you have spoken, I will do for you: And he said: show me your glory: And he said: I will pass before you in my glory and I will call in the name of the Lord before you, and I will have mercy on whom I have had mercy and I will show mercy to whom I will have mercy. Which indeed is fulfilled thus: And the Lord descended in a cloud and stood before him there and called in the name of the Lord. And the Lord passed before his face, and the Lord GOD called. For he who had promised above that he would cross over, the Son of God the Lord, and called in the name of the Lord, who is the Father, this is he who truly says: Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from GOD, he has seen the Father: And in the same Gospel: Neither have you ever heard his voice, nor seen his form. And: No one has ever seen GOD: the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him.

Verse of the same. BY A PILLAR OF FIRE AND CLOUD.

There was therefore one pillar (not twin, as the Hebrews wish) which appeared by day, such as in reality was a cloud, but erected like a pillar, whereas by night it shone like fire; as Num. 9, 15. but from evening it was over the tabernacle as it were the appearance of fire until morning. It is said therefore Ex. 13, 21. 22. fire κατὰ δόξαν, because to those looking it seemed to be fire, and burning, or a flame, Wis. 18, 3. not from heat, but from color. For it had a double office: by day it overshadowed the camps, as a cloud: by night it illuminated the same, as a torch of fire. Philo also acknowledges that there was one pillar. It was similar only to a cloud as regards material and color; but it differed from a cloud, because (1.) it was purer and clearer, (2.) denser and more solid, (3.) it always retained the shape of a column, it was always like itself. (4.) It was not moved by circular motion but by straight, now forward, now backward, now to the side: sometimes before the standard of Judah, sometimes it returned from the standard of Judah to the tabernacle, which was in the middle of the camp, Num. 2, 2. chap. 10, 13. 14. (5.) It accommodated itself to the strength of the Hebrews, according as they were able to advance on account of the old men, the little ones, and their flocks. (6.) It rested twice daily even in the movement of the camp, namely at lunch and at supper, likewise at night, when the Israelites were resting. (7.) A cloud is moved by winds: but this column was moved by the uncreated Angel, the Son of GOD, yet the cloud itself was not uncreated, as Servetus dreamed, noting in Calvin on Exod. 13 that it was the Deity of Christ. For Deity by its nature is ἀσώματος. Cyril on Num. 8 hands down this mystical meaning: The Church of the faithful is fixed, Christ covers it from above: overshadowing those who are of the day, that is, illuminated by the splendor of life and doctrines, and driving away the heat of temptations, and sending into them refreshment and recreation of soul: but to those who sleep as if in the night in the darkness of sin, lighting a torch, and illuminating them to knowledge and truth: For the more imperfect indeed have need of being led to that which is better, but the more perfect have need of help, so that they may be able to bear the burden and heat of the day. And immediately chap. 5 above, Christ is the cloud, which dissipating the heat of temptations, and recreating the soul, overshadows those who recede from ignorance to knowledge, and from infidelity to faith, and progress in the course of piety. For without me, he says, you can do nothing. Moreover, he is added during the day, who walk in the light of good works, he is accustomed to bring help, and to recreate them. But they moved the camp by the Lord's command, since there is need also of the word or reason, inciting to progress, and of obedience to divine commands.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

RESPICIENS DOMINUS SUPER CASTRA ÆGYPTIORUM PER COLUMNAM IGNIS] Angelus supra dictus v. 19. DEI personam referens. Quia Angelus dictus Dominus, angelum hunc non personam DEI præsentasse dicendum, id enim ea ratione nunquam factum, ut angelus casu recto Jehovah Dominus nuncupatus sit, aut nomen illud DEO propriissimum, quod κατ’ ἐξοχὴν שׁם Ebræi dicunt, & quod DEUS nemi- ni se dare velle protestatur Esa. 42, 6. sibi vendi- carit, sed personam divinam revera fuisse ange- lum faciei Domini, qui REDEMIT ET SAL- VAVIT populum Esa. 63, 13. qui solus & Ange- lus & Jehovah dicitur. Qui & promisit edu- ctionem ac liberationem populo suo Exod. III. & nunc promissum id exequitur. Quod enim Jehovah ipse αὐτοπροσώπως è columna ignis & nu- be prospexerit, textus evidentissime indicat. E- undem prospexisse docens, qui terrorem fecit in Exercitu Ægyptiorum, & præcipitavit eos- dem: quique ad Mosen loquutus vers. 26. 27. quod à Jehova ipso, in quem credidit populus, factum, Moses testatur versibus iisdem, ut & vers. 30. 31. Cui Canticum Ecclesiasticum cecinit cum populo, cap. XV. Cantemus Domino, gloriose enim magnificatus est, equum & adscensorem dejecit in mare. Fortitudo mea & laus mea Dominus, & factus est mihi in SALUTEM. זה אלי iste est DEUS meus, Quis est Dominus ille, qui nobis factus est לישועה in salutem, nisi Filius Dei, qui Jesus noster factus? De eo enim Apostolus: JE- sus Christus heri, hodie idem & in secula, Ebr. 13, 8. Quem etiam verbo גאל Filio Dei Redemtori peculiariter proprio designat vers. 13. Ideo Ec- clesia Latina juxta vulgatam versionem, quam contemnere non potest Grotius ob Synodi Tri- dentinæ autoritatem, eundem ita celebravit: Jud. v. 5. Quoniam Jesus populum de terra Ægypti sal- vans, secundo eos, qui non crediderunt, perdidit. Neque hic solum Jehovah ipse in nube præsto fu- isse, & Israëlitas duxisse dicitur. Semper enim Domino, nunquam Angelo creato hoc tribuitur: Num. 14, 14. Audiverunt, quod tu Domine sis in populo isto, & nubes tua stet super eos & in columna nubis præcedas eos per diem, & in columna ignis per noctem, vers. 15. quod occideris tantam multitudi- nem, Deuter. 31, 3. Jehovah DEUS tuus ipse ante te præcedet Numer. 12, 5. seqq. Descendit Dominus in columna nubis, & stetit in introitu tabernaculi, & dixit ad Aaronem & Mirjam Deuter. 31, 16. Appa- ruit Dominus ibi in columna nubis. Conf. Psalm. 99, 7. Exod. 33, 2. seqq. cap. 34, 5. seqq. Angelus idem, qui Israëlitas deduxit & Jehovah dicitur, qui in nu- be descendit, & de Jehovah prædicavit, & facies Domini & omne bonum DEI vocatur, ac introdu- citur denique tanquam Mediator inter DEUM & homines, ne DEUS, qui ignis consumens est, populum propter peccata perdat & deleat. Quis autem ille Angelus Domini, nisi Filius DEI An- gelus fœderis novi, DEUS benedictus in secula super omnia, Rom. 9, 5. Jehovah justitia nostra Jer. 23, 6. qui facies DEI, imago DEI Patris χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως καὶ ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης αὐτõ dicitur Col. 1, 18. Ebr. 1, 3. in quo omne DEI bonum, quia uti vitam habet Pater in semetipso, ita Filio dedit vi- tam habere in semetipso Joh. 5, 26. Omnia, inquit, quæ Pater habet, mea sunt, Joh. 16, 15. Qui unus est DEI & hominum mediator, 1. Tim. 2, 5. & hic se Mosi in forma humana assumta conspiciendum præbuit: utpote cui dictum erat, faciem meam (NUDAM) non videre poteris: posteriora autem mea sive tergum videbis, in forma nempe assumta, quæ typus erat, & umbra assumendæ in plenitudine temporis humanæ naturæ. Quæ omnia luculen- tiora adhuc evadent, si conferantur Exod. 23, 20. &

quæ ibi dicemus. Sane ex Ebræis quoque nonnulli, quia nimis manifestum, Angelum hic dici Domi- num, viderunt, quod hic videre non potuit Gro- tius, Filium DEI designari. R. Moses Gerundensis, scriptum est, inquit, Et angelus faciei ejus salvos fecit ipsos. Nimirum ille Angelus, qui est DEI facies; de quo dictum est: facies mea præibit & efficiam, ut qui- escas. Denique ille Angelus est, de quo Vates: Et subito veniet ad templum suum Dominus, quem vos quæri- tis, & angelus fœderis, quem cupitis. Et rursus alio loco, ubi illum versiculum exponit, Facies mea præ- ibit & efficiam, ut quiescas, sic scriptum reliquit; ut in pauca conferam: Animadverte, inquit, attente, quid ista sibi velint. Moses enim & Israëlitæ semper optaverunt angelum primum; cæterum quis ille esset, vere intelligere non potuerunt. Neq; enim ab aliis per- cipiebant; neq; prophetica notione satis assequebantur. Atqui facies DEI ipsum significat DEUM, quod apud omnes Interpretes est in confesso. Verum ne per somnium quidem ista intelligere quisquam possit, nisi sit mysteriis legis eruditus. Et post pauca: Facies mea præcedet, hoc est, angelus fœderis, quem vos cupitis: in quo videbitur facies mea, de quo dictum est: Tempo- re accepto exaudiam te. Nomen enim meum in eo est, Faciamque ut quiescas, sive efficiam, ut ipse tibi sit lenis & benignus. Neq; te ducat per jus rigidum; sed pla- cide & clementer. Hæc è Mose Gerundensi An- dreas Masius in Jos. cap. V. Quod etiam innuere videtur Targum Onkelos: cap. 14, 31. verba Mosis, Crediderunt Domino, ita exponens: Crediderunt in VERBUM DOMINI: & illa cap. 15. vers. 7. DO- MINUS factus est mihi in salutem, hac paraphrasi illustrans: Dixit ad Verbum suum, & fuit (verbum) mihi in Redemtorem. Penes orthodoxos Patres vero id prorsus in dubium & ὁμολογυμένως certum, angelum, qui in columna nubis apparuit, & Jeho- vah dicitur, non personam Domini repræsentaf- se, sed divinam personam DEI fuisse. Quod defi- nitum fuit in Concilio Antiocheno: cujus verba hic adscribemus ex Epistola Synodica: Et alias: Et dixit Dominus ad Mosen: Et hunc sermonem, q.em dixisti faciam tibi: Et dixit: ostende mihi glo- riam tuam: Et dixit: Ego transibo prius te in gloria mea & vocabo in nomine Domini coram te, & mise- rebor, cui misertus sum & misericordiam præstabo, cui miserebor. Quod quidem sic perficitur: Et de- scendit Dominus in nube & stetit coram eo illic & vo- cavit in nomine Domini. Et transivit Dominus an- te faciem ejus, & vocavit Dominus DEUS. Qui enim supra promiserat, se transiturum, Filius Dei Dominus, & vocavit in nomine Domini, qui est Pater, hic est, qui vere ait: Non quia Patrem vidit quisquam, nisi qui est à DEO, hic vidit Patrem: Et in eodem Evangelio: Neq; vocem ejus unquam audistis, neque speciem ejus vidistis. Et: DEUM nemo vidit un- quam: unigenitus Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, ipse enarravit.

Vers. eod. PER COLUMNAM IGNIS ET NUBIS.

Una ergo fuit columna (non gemina, ut Ebræi volunt) quæ per diem apparebat, qualis revera erat nubes, at erecta instar columnæ, noctu autem in- star ignis splendebat; ut Num. 8, 15. à vespere autem super tentorium erat quasi species ignis usque mane. Dicitur ergo Ex. 13, 21. 22. ignis κατὰ δόξαν, quia in- tuentibus videbatur ignis esse, & ardens, vel flamma, Sap. 18, 3. non à calore, sed à colore. Habebat enim duplex officium: per diem obrumbrabat castra, quasi nubes: per noctem illuminabat eadem, qua- si fax ignis. Unam columnam fuisse agnoscit etiam Philo. Similis solum nubi erat quoad ma- teriam & colorem; sed differebat à nube, quia (1.) purior erat, & lucidior, (2.) densior & solidior, (3.) semper retinebat figuram columnæ, semper sui similis erat. (4.) Non movebatur motu cir- culari sed recto, nunc antrorsum, nunc retrorsum, nunc ad latus: modo ante vexillum Judæ, modo à vexillo Judæ redibat ad tabernaculum, quod erat in medio castrorum, Num. 2, 2. cap. 10, 13. 14. (5.) Accommodabat se ad vires Ebræorum, prout illi ob senes, parvulosque & greges suos progredi valebant. (6.) Quiescebat bis quotidie etiam in motu castrorum, puta in prandio, & in Cœna, item noctu, cum quiescebant Israëlitæ. (7.) Movetur nubes à ventis: hæc vero columna movebatur ab Angelo increato, Filio DEI, non tamen nubes ipsa increata fuit, ut somniavit Ser- vetus notante Calvino ad Exod. 13. eam fuisse Dei- tatem Christi. Deitas enim natura sua est ἀσώ- ματος. Significationem mysticam Cyrillus ad Num. 8. hanc tradit: Fixa est fidelium Ecclesia, Christus eam texit desuper: eos quidem, qui sunt di- ei, hoc est, illuminati vitæ & dogmatum splendore, obumbrans & æstum tentationum abigens, refrige- riumque & recreationem animi eis immittens: eis autem, qui tanquam in nocte in tenebris peccati dor- miunt, facem accendens, & eos illuminans ad agni- tionem & veritatem: Nam imperfectioribus qui- dem opus est ad deducendum id, quod est melius, perfectioribus autem auxilio, ut ferre possint diei onus & æstum. Et statim cap. 5. sup. Christus est nubes, quæ æstum tentationum dissipans, & animam recreans eos obumbrat, qui recedunt ab ignoratio- ne ad cognitionem, & ab infidelitate ad fidem, & proficiunt in cursu pietatis. Nam sine me, inquit, nihil potestis facere. Adjectus est autem inter- diu, qui ambulant in luce bonorum operum, solet opem ferre, & eos recreare. Per Domini autem jussum castra movebant, quoniam & verbo seu ratio- ne opus est, incitante ad profectum, & obedientia divi- norum mandatorum.

## 14:25
Ver. 25. HE SLEW THEIR ARMY.

Some explain that a part of the army was slain by thunders, lightnings, stones, and fiery darts, since another part, terrified by this heavenly slaughter, cried out, let us flee from Israel, for the Lord fights for him. Others understand it of the whole army being slain, or extinguished in the Red Sea, but for that reason which follows thereafter, by suffocation, so that the Egyptians cried out not having seen the slaughter of their other companions, but when the wheels of the chariots were overturned by that tempest. Truly in the Hebrew text it is not, he slew, but he broke and crushed, which the Chaldean rendered, he disturbed, and the LXX. συνετάραξε; others refer it to the consternation of the mind; that God rendered the Egyptians astonished. Others say they were crushed and prostrate, when thunders in that dense and dark cloud, flashing with frequent fires, not only roared, but also lightnings and stones were cast.

Latin:

Vers. 25. INTERFECIT EXERCITUM EO- RUM.

De parte exercitus nonnulli explicant per tonitrua, fulmina, lapides, ignita tela, interfecta, siquidem alia pars strage hac cœlesti perterrita clamarit, fugiamus Israëlem, Dominus enim pu- gnat pro illo. Alii de toto exercitu interfecto, vel extincto in mari rubro, sed ea ratione, quæ de- inde sequitur, per suffocationem intelligunt, ut clamarint adeo Ægyptii non visa strage aliorum Sociorum, sed cum subverterentur rotæ cur- ruum per istam tempestatem. Verum in Ebræo tex- tu non est, interfecit, sed fregit & contrivit, quod Chaldæus reddidit, conturbavit, & LXX. συνετά- ραξε; alii ad consternationem animi referunt; quod Deus Ægyptios attonitos reddiderit. Alii con- tritos & prostratos dicunt, cum tonitrua in densa illa & caliginosa nube crebris ignibus intermican- te non fremerent tantum, sed & fulmina ac lapides jacerentur.

## 14:27
Ver. 27. IT RETURNED AT THE FIRST DAWN TO ITS FORMER PLACE.

In the Hebrew it returned to its strength, that is, to its vigor, just as the Chaldean rendered it, because previously the troubled waters had as it were lost their vigor at the presence of the Lord, and had yielded against their nature, Psalm 77. verse 14. Cornelius decides that the angels had suspended and held back the waters of the sea until then, and now released them again without cause. GOD could perform that by His own nod alone without angels.

Ver. same. AND THE LORD INVOLVED THEM IN THE MIDST OF THE WAVES.

According to the Hebrew text: GOD shook them into the midst of the sea: which word David also uses in Psalm 136, 15. because they were thrown down from horses and chariots, and thus were precipitated into the midst of the sea. Josephus counts of the Egyptians who perished, two hundred thousand shield-bearing infantry and fifty thousand cavalry.

Abulensis asserts that Pharaoh perished last along with the Hebrews, so that he might indeed see the slaughter of his own people first, and be tormented longer and more severely. Apollonius the Abbot, in Palladius’s Lausiac History, ch. 52, reports that the rest of the Egyptians who were left at home, having heard of this miraculous slaughter of their people, called the God of the Hebrews their own God and turned to Him: which we leave in its own place.

Latin:

Vers. 27. REVERSUM EST PRIMO DILUCULO AD PRIOREM LOCUM.

In Ebr. reversum est ad robur suum, hoc est, ad vigorem suum, veluti reddidit Chaldæus, quia antea turbatæ aquæ ad præsentiam Domi- ni vigorem suum quasi amiserant, & contra na- turam suam cesserant, Psalm. 77. vers. 14. Angelos aquas maris eo usque suspendisse, & detinuis- se, nunc eas iterum dimittere citra causam statuit Cornelius. Solo nutu suo id præstare sine Angelis potuit DEUS.

Verf. eod. ET INVOLVIT EOS DOMINUS IN MEDIIS FLUCTIBUS.

Juxta Ebr. textum: excussit DEUS eos in medium maris: quo verbo etiam utitur David Psalm. 136, 15. quia ex equis & curribus dejicieban- tur, atque ita præcipitabantur in medium maris. Numerat autem Josephus Ægyptiorum, qui perie- re, ducenta millia scutatorum peditum & equitum quinquaginta millia.

Pharaonem ultimum periisse cum Ebræis Abu- lensis asserit, ut nempe prius suorum cladem vide- ret, ac longius & gravius cruciaretur. Apollonius Abbas apud Palladium in Lausiacis c. 52. refert, cœ- teros Ægyptios, qui domi relicti sunt, audita hac mi- raculosa suorum strage Deum Ebræorum Deum suum vocasse & ad eum conversos esse: quod suo lo- co relinquimus.

## 14:29
Ver. 29. BUT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL WENT THROUGH THE MIDST OF THE DRY SEA.

Namely, they crossed the entire breadth of the sea from one shore to the opposite one. Because the waters of the sea were divided, and they are said to have crossed through the midst of the sea in a parallel place, Num. XXXIII, 8, into the desert; therefore Josephus, book 2, observes that they crossed to the opposite shore. They did not, therefore, make a semicircle, or return to the same shore, as some think with the Hebrews Aben-Ezra and R. Hiskuni (concerning whom see Paulus Fagius), especially Tostatus and Burgensis; for thus there would have been a circuit and a certain gyration of the sea, not an upright standing of the sea, which is said to have stood like a wall; furthermore, the sea had to be crossed in order for them to arrive at Sinai, as can be seen from Adrichomius, page 116. But as for the fact that they are said to have come into Ethan having left the sea, Numbers XXXIII, v. 8, Cajetan rightly observes that the desert of Ethan was most vast and extended both on this side of and beyond the sea: But how could such a great army with beasts of burden and little ones complete six miles within five hours so quickly? Nothing prevents us, since all things in this crossing are miraculous, from believing that some miracle also occurred in the speed of the crossing, which is certainly better than departing from the manifest text. The Hebrews, and with them Cajetan and Genebrard, imagine that the mountains danced and leaped during this crossing of the Israelites, citing Psalm CXIII, 4 to that effect. But there is deep silence in the Scriptures concerning that miracle, nor is anything else regarded in that Psalm than the earthquake at the promulgation of the Law on Mount Sinai.

Latin:

Vers. 29. FILII AUTEM ISRAEL PERREXERUNT PER MEDIUM SICCI MARIS.

Scil. totam maris latitudinem transiere ab uno littore in aliud oppositum. Quia aquæ maris fis- sæ erant, & transiisse per medium maris in loco parallelo Num. XXXIII, 8. in desertum dicuntur; ideo Josephus lib. 2. observat, eos in adversum littus transivisse. Non ergo fecerunt semicircu- lum, aut redierunt ad idem littus, ut cum Ebræis Aben-Ezra & R. Hiskuni, (de quibus Paulus Fa- gius videatur) nonnulli putant, inprimis To- status, & Burgensis; sic enim circuitus & gyratio quædam maris, non erecta maris statio fuisset, quod instar muri stetisse dicitur, adhæc pertransiri mare debuit, ut in Sina pervenirent, quemad- modum ex Adrichomio pag. 116. videre est. Quod vero in Ethan venisse dicuntur egressi mare, Numer. XXXIII, v. 8. recte observat Cajet. desertum Ethan fuisse vastissimum & tam cis, quam ultra mare sese extendisse: Sed quomodo tam celeriter sex milliaria, intra quinque horas conficere potuere tan- ti exercitus cum jumentis & parvulis? Nihil ob- stat, cum omnia in hoc transitu miraculosa sint, quo minus in celeritate etiam transeundi aliquod miraculum contigisse credamus, quod utique præstat, quam à manifesto textu discedere. E- bræi, & cum illis Cajetan. & Genebr. fingunt mon- tes tripudiasse & saltasse in hoc transitu Israëlita- rum, adducentes Psalm. CXIII, 4. in eam sen- tentiam. Sed de eo miraculo altum est in Scri- pturis silentium, nec in Psalmo isto aliud, quam terræmotus in promulgatione Legis in monte Sinai respicitur.

## 14:31
Ver. 31. AND THEY BELIEVED THE LORD AND MOSES HIS SERVANT.

In the Hebrew it is word for word: They believed in the Lord and in Moses his servant. Whence some Papists gather that one must also believe in the saints, but the Photinians think that the argument for the Deity of Christ is undermined thereby, which Catholics draw from the trust to be placed in Christ; if indeed the Israelites are said to have believed also in Moses; but the Papists, since they believe the Vulgate is authentic, cannot cling to this argument for ἁγιολατρείᾳ [saint-worship], nor does anything depart from our argument for the divine nature of Christ, because he is expressly pronounced cursed who has trust in a mere man, Jer. 17, 5. And therefore Christ must be not ψιλὸν ἄνθρωπον [a mere man], but true God, because not only must trust be placed in him, but this is the one and only cause of eternal blessedness, when we trust in him.

Psalm 2:13. Trust in a mere man, however, cannot be the cause of eternal blessedness. Therefore, as far as this passage is concerned, Piscator indeed thinks that trust can be placed in man secondarily; but Rivetus rightly refutes him on this passage, since πεποίθησις (confidence) in someone is one thing, and faith in someone is another: we hope well for many, in whom, however, we neither believe nor place our trust. And the Apostle connects these, trust and invocation, that trust is to be placed in the same one whom we invoke religiously, Rom. 10:14: how shall they invoke him in whom they have not believed? Drusius more correctly observes that it is a Hebraism to believe in Moses, and that it denotes nothing other than to believe that Moses is truthful: therefore, however much the Latins distinguish the phrases, to believe someone and to believe in someone: by the former they only denote believing that he who speaks is truthful; by the latter they express trust and hope placed in someone; yet in Hebrew these are not always distinguished in this way; indeed, the phrase, to believe in someone, sometimes denotes only faith applied to the words of someone. But this passage is best explained if it is said that the Lord and Moses his servant are joined here, so that the sense is that the Israelites had faith in the word of God announced by Moses, and one object of faith is designated, namely the word of the Lord, insofar as it had been preached by Moses the minister, by the name of the Lord, because it is not added rashly, his servant, but it is indicated that they believed Moses to be the servant of GOD and to have spoken in His name, in which manner also 2 Chron. 20:20. Jehovah is joined with the Prophets by a similar manner of speaking. For the ב here serves to express the Dative case, just as the verb 'believed' is constructed elsewhere. See Deut. 28:66, 1 Sam. 27:12, Ps. 78:22. Elsewhere it is expressed by ל. Deut. 9:13, Isa. 43:10. Both locutions are found in Psalm 106, v. 12, 26. Cf. Mark 1:15. Therefore, historical faith is understood, not saving faith. But when trust is said to be placed in Christ, it is to be placed not as in a minister of the word, but as in the true God, the author of the word and the primary object of faith, and the cause of eternal salvation: which is not historical faith, but saving faith: Cf. James 2:19, John 5:46.

Wherefore it must be observed that faith in Moses or in the Prophets is never praised absolutely in the Scriptures, but only by reason of their preaching, so that Moses and the Prophets are taken for the doctrine of which they were the heralds: as in Luke 16:28, they have Moses and the Prophets, let them hear them.

Latin:

Vers. 31. ET CREDIDERUNT DOMINO ET MOSI SERVO EJUS.

In Ebr. est ad verbum: Crediderunt in Do- minum & in Mosen servum ejus. Unde Pontificii nonnulli colligunt, etiam in sanctos credendum esse, Photiniani vero labefactari inde putant ar- gumentum Deitatis Christi, quod à fiducia in Chri- stum collocanda petunt Catholici; siquidem etiam credidisse dicantur Israëlitæ in Mosen; sed Pontificii cum Vulgatam credant authenticam huic argumento inhærere non possunt pro ἁγιολατρείᾳ, neque nostro argumento quicquam decedit pro divina Christi natura, quia expresse maledictus pro- nunciatur ille, qui fiduciam habet in mero homine, Jer. 17, 5. Ideoque Christum oportet esse non ψιλὸν ἄνθρωπον, sed verum Deum, quia in ipsum non mo- do fiducia collocanda est, sed hæc una & sola est beatitudinis æternæ causa, cum in ipso confidimus

Pfalm. 2, 13. fiducia autem in purum hominem non potest æternæ beatitudinis causa esse. Quod ergo ad h. l. attinet, existimat quidem Piscator, fiduciam collocari posse in hominem secundario; sed illum recte refellit Rivetus in h. l. cum aliud sit πεποίθησις de ali- quo, aliud fides in aliquem: de multis bene speramus, in quos tamen nec credimus nec fiduciam collocamus. Et connectit hæc Apostolus, fiduciam & invocationem, in eundem esse collocandam fiduciam, quem invo- camus religiose, Rom. 10, 14. quomodo invocabunt, in quem non crediderunt? Rectius observat Drusius, Ebraismum esse, credere in Mosen, nihilque aliud notare, quam credere veracem esse Mosen: Utut ergo distinguant Latini phrases, credere alicui, & credere in aliquem: priori tantum notent, credere veracem illum esse, qui loquitur; posteriori exprimant fi- duciam, & spem in aliquem collocatam; in Ebræo tamen hæc ita non semper distinguuntur; imo phrasis, credere in aliquem, notat quandoque tan- tum fidem dictis alicujus adhibitam. Optime autem expeditur hic locus, si dicatur conjungi hic Domi- num & Mosen servum ejus, ut sensus sit, fidem ha- buisse Israëlitas verbo Dei à Mose enunciato, unum- que fidei objectum designetur, verbum nempe Domi- ni, quatenus à Mose ministro prædicatum erat, no- mine Domini, quia non temere additur, servo ejus, sed indicatur, credidisse ipsos Mosen esse servum DEI & ipsius nomine locutum fuisse, quo pacto etiam 2. Chron. 20, 20. Jehova cum Prophetis con- jungitur simili loquendi ratione. Inservit enim ב hîc Dativo casui exprimendo, uti etiam alias ver- bum credidit construitur. Vid. Deut. 28, 66. 1. Sam. 27, 12. Ps. 78, 22. Alibi exprimitur per ל. Deut. 9, 13. Es. 43, 10. utraque loquutio habetur Psalm. 106. v. 12, 26. Conf. Marc. 1, 15. Fides ergo historica in- telligitur, non salvifica. At cum in Christum col- locanda dicitur fiducia, non ut in ministrum verbi, sed ut in verum Deum, auctorem verbi & primarium fidei objectum, causamq; æternæ salutis fiducia collo- canda est: quæ non historica fides est, sed salvifica: Conf. Jac. 17, 5. Job. 5, 46.

Quapropter observandum, nunquam in Scri- pturis fidem in Mosen vel in Prophetas absolute lauda- ri, sed tantum ratione prædicationis eorum, ita, ut Moses & Prophetæ pro doctrina, cujus erant præcones, accipiantur: uti Luc. 16, 28. habent Mosen & Prophe- tas, audiant eos.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAPTER XV.

The people's song of victory. The waters at Marah.

Verse 1. THEN MOSES AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SANG THIS SONG TO THE LORD] There is a verb of the future tense in the Hebrew, יָשִׁיר אָז: but Abenesdra notes that the particle אָז, which means 'then', has this power among the Arabs, that it converts a verb of the future into the meaning of the past. Which the Hebrews also sometimes follow, as Deut. 4:41, Josh. 10:12.

This is the first Song which Scripture mentions, which is 300 years and more older than the songs of the Greeks, Linus, Musaeus, and Orpheus. What its meter is, we believe is clear to no one today. Josephus says that it runs in hexameter verse. But that is more easily said than taught. Meanwhile, you may detect another style and poetic figures, paronomasias, homoioteleuta, and the like in it. And it is so full of an exulting spirit that you seem not so much to hear as to see the choir leaping to the festive song. The author of the wonders of Scripture among

Augustine, perhaps on the occasion of the passage in Wisdom 10, verse 20, invented a miracle here, as if, with Moses leading, the whole people had sung the Canticle to the Lord in a harmonious song, as if with one mouth, taught by no previous warning. But in that passage nothing else is held than that wisdom opened the mouths of the dumb, which can be understood without that miracle, in this sense, that those who had previously been dumb in divine matters are now loosed into praises of GOD.

Latin:

CAPUT XV.

Epinicion populi. Aquæ in Mara.

Vers. 1. TUNC CECINIT MOSES ET FILII ISRAEL CARMEN HOC DOMINO] Est in Hebræo verbum futuri temporis, יָשִׁיר אָז: sed notat Abenesdra אָז particulam, quæ tunc significat, hanc vim apud Arabes habere, ut futuri verbum in præteriti significationem convertat. Quod & Hebræi inter- dum sequuntur, ut Deut. 4, 41. Jos. 10, 12.

PRimum hoc Canticum est, cujus scriptura me- minit, quod Græcorum, Lini, Musæi, & Or- phei carmina 300. annis, & ultra antiquius est. Mé- τρον ejus quale sit, hodie nemini constare arbitra- mur. Hexametro versu id decurrere dicit Josephus. Sed id facilius dicitur, quam docetur. Interim alium stylum, & schemata poëtica, paroromasias, ὁμοιο- τέλευτα, & similia in eo deprehendas. Estque id adeo plenum exultante spiritu, ut chorum subsi- lientem ad carmen festivum non tam audire, quam videre videaris. Autor mirabilium scripturæ apud

Augustinum forte occasione loci Sap. 10. vers. 20. miraculum hic commentus est, quasi Mose conci- nente, consono carmine Canticum Domino uni- versi pariter decantassent, uno quasi ex ore, nulla edocti præmonitione. Sed in loco illo nihil aliud habetur, quam quod sapientia aperuerit ora mutorũ, quod citra illud miraculum intelligi potest, hoc sensu, quod qui antea muti fuerant in rebus divinis, nunc solvantur in laudes DEI.

## 15:2
Verse 2. AND HE BECAME MY SALVATION.

In Hebrew, 'and he was to me for salvation', the ו is taken causally, and ought to be rendered 'because' or 'for', since a reason is brought forward why he always wishes to praise the Lord and to have him as his strength. To be for salvation is a Hebraism, see 2 Kings 7:14. It denotes, therefore, the same as for such a thing to happen, to become a Savior, because the Lord became a Savior to the people in this deliverance: meanwhile the word יֵשׁוּעָה also points to the Lord Jesus, who was the Leader of the people, 1 Cor. 10:4, 9; Jude v. 5, whom Moses also seems to have pointed out as if with his finger, while he adds: 'this is my God', by which name the Angel of Jehovah, the Son of GOD, is described in Exodus 3, as the God of the fathers and the God of Israel. And the Hebrews observe that the demonstrative pronoun 'this' is used because of the visible and conspicuous form of this warrior, in which the Lord went before and fought, who, since he is also called an Angel, is none other than the Son of God, that angel in whom the name of God is, Exod. 23:20.

Latin:

Verf. 2. ET FACTUS EST MIHI IN SALUTEM.

In Ebr. & fuit mihi in salutem, ו sumitur αἰτιολογικῶς, & reddi debet, quia, nam causa adfertur, cur laudare Dominum, eumque pro fortitudine habere semper velit. Esse in salutem, Ebraismus est, vid. 2. Reg. 7, 14. Notat ergo idem, quod fieri tale quid, fieri Salvatorem, quia Salvator factus est populo Dominus in hac liberatione: interim vox יֵשׁוּעָה monstrat quoque Dominum Jesum, qui Dux erat populi, 1. Cor. 10, 4. 9. Jud. v. 5. quem etiam quasi digito ostendisse videtur Moses, dum addit: iste Deus meus, quo nomine Angelus Jehovah Filius DEI Exod. 3. descriptus est, ceu Deus patrum & Deus Israëlis. Et observant Ebræi pronomen demonstrativum iste adhibitum esse, ob formam hujus bellatoris visibilem & conspicuam, in qua præivit & præliatus est Dominus, qui cum Angelus etiam vocetur, nullus alius est, quam Filius Dei, angelus ille, in quo nomen Dei est, Exod. 23, 20.

## 15:4
Verse 4. HE CAST HIS ARMY INTO THE SEA.

יָרָה he cast. As easily as an archer sends forth an arrow, so easily did the Lord cast the Egyptians.

Verse of the same. HIS PRINCES] It appears from comparing the passages 2 Kings 7:2 and 9:25 that those are understood whom the Roman histories of a later age call protectors; but why is the name derived from the number three for them? Origen thinks it arose from the fact that the kings of those places entered battles in chariots. Now there were in the chariot a king, a charioteer, and a protector.

Latin:

Vers. 4. EXERCITUM EJUS PROJECIT IN MARE.

יָרָה ejaculatus est. Quam facile sagittarius sagittam emittit, tam facile Ægyptios projecit Dominus.

Vers. eod. PRINCIPES EJUS] Eos intelligi, quos Romanæ historiæ posterioris ævi vocant protectores apparet collatis locis 2. Reg. 7, 2. & 9, 25. sed cur à ternario numero illis nomen? Origenes inde id ortum censet, quod illorum locorum reges in curribus prælia inirent. Erant autem in curru rex, auriga, & protector.

## 15:8
Verse 8. THE DEPTHS WERE GATHERED IN THE MIDST OF THE SEA.

The word קָפַא means to coagulate, to freeze, to condense. The LXX render it ἐπάγη, they coagulated, whence some assert that those waters were frozen on both sides by that east wind, and thus stood frozen like walls constructed of ice. But Moses did not indicate that in the history, and that word generally denotes condensation, nor does Vatablus supply the sign of comparison here inconveniently; the depths stood as if they had been coagulated or solidified.

Latin:

Vers. 8. CONGREGATÆ SUNT ABYSSI IN MEDIO MARI.

Verbum קָפַא est coagulare, congelare, condensare. LXX. reddunt ἐπάγη, coagularunt, unde nonnulli asserunt, aquas istas ab utraque parte conglaciatas fuisse per ventum illum orientalem, & ita congelatas stetisse instar murorum, è glacie constructorum. Sed id Moses in historia non indicavit, & verbum illud generaliter condensationem notat, neque incommode Vatablus supplet hîc notam similitudinis, abyssi ita steterunt, ac si coagulatæ, aut concretæ fuissent.

## 15:10
Verse 10. THY SPIRIT BLEW AND THE SEA COVERED THEM.

Cajetan explains it as wind, Cornelius and others as the wrath or impetus of God. But nothing prevents us from understanding it, with Augustine (q. 55) and Ambrose (lib. 3 de Spiritu Sancto c. 4), as the Holy Spirit, because the name of the Spirit of GOD, when placed simply, does not easily occur in the Scriptures as anything other than the Holy Spirit. And by the right hand of the Lord in verse 6, the Son of God is rightly understood, because strength is attributed to that right hand: therefore, it is not the strength itself that is designated by it, but the ὑπόστασις of the Son of God. And so the Fathers not inappropriately understand the spirit as the Holy Spirit. Certainly, both the Son of God and the Holy Spirit show their power here; the former as a man of wars, i.e., most powerful in war, cf. 1 Sam. 17:34, demonstrated his strength; the latter exercised vengeance against the enemies of the Church as the Spirit of judgment. Just as the Holy Spirit was borne over the face of the abyss in the work of creation to give life, so he is borne in this place over the Red Sea, so that the sea might cover the enemies of the Church, of which David also speaks in Psalm 138:7, 'Whither shall I go from thy Spirit?' To whom, finally, the destruction of enemies is attributed. Isa. 11:4, 2 Thess. 2:8, as also Isa. 63:9.

Latin:

Vers. 10. FLAVIT SPIRITUS TUUS ET OPERUIT EOS MARE.

De vento explicat Cajetanus, de ira vel impetu Dei Corn. & alii. Sed nihil obstat, quo minus cum August. qu. 55. & Ambrof. lib. 3. de Spiritu Sancto c. 4. Spiritum S. intelligamus, quia non facile aliter Spiritus DEI nomen simpliciter positum, quam de Spiritu S. occurrit in Scripturis. Et per dextram Domini vers. 6. Filius Dei recte intelligitur, quia dextræ illi tribuitur fortitudo: non ergo per eam ipsa fortitudo, sed ὑπόστασις Filii Dei designatur. Ideoque non incommode spiritum de Spiritu S. Patres intelligunt. Sane ostendit uterque Filius Dei & Spiritus S. hîc vim suam; ille tanquam vir bellorum, h. e. in bello potentissimus, conf. 1. Sam. 17, 34. fortitudinem suam demonstravit; hic vindictam adversus hostes Ecclesiæ exercuit tanquam Spiritus judicii. Uti super faciem abyssi ferebatur Spiritus S. in opere creationis ad vivificandum; sic fertur hoc in loco super mare rubrum, ut mare hostes operiat Ecclesiæ, de quo etiam David Psalm. 138. v. 7. quo ibo à Spiritu tuo. Cui denique tribuitur hostium deletio. Esa. 11, 4. 2. Thess. 2, 8. ut & Esa. 63, 9.

## 15:11
Vers. 11. WHO IS LIKE UNTO THEE AMONG THE MIGHTY, O LORD?] Not unlike that Hesiodic saying: For he himself is king and lord of all the immortals; and there is no one who has vied with him in power.

In Hebrew. In gods, namely of the nations, as the LXX. which comparison with the gods of the gentiles to explain the majesty of GOD is frequent in the scriptures, not that anything is attributed to the gods of the gentiles in truth or in reality, for idols are nothing 1 Cor. 8, 6. but so that the gentiles might be confounded in their boasting. From the initial letters of the words in Hebrew according to the Cabbala, which they call notarikon, when one letter is a sign of an entire word, not a few think the name מכבי is derived, Mercerus, Schindlerus, Buxt. likewise Sixtus Senensis & Genebr. because they carried those initial letters from this verse on their banners as a symbol, who were thence called Maccabees: which indeed does not please Scalig. l. 5. de emend. temp. nor Full. l. 2. Miscell. c. 13. because that Cabbalistic invention seems too recent to be referred to the times of the Maccabees. Rivetus especially opposes this to him, that 1. Macc. 2, 2. it is indicated, that from the beginning Judas was surnamed Maccabeus, before he was in charge of the army. But that reason does not seem sufficiently cogent to us; for Judas could have chosen this symbol for himself beforehand, which was afterwards inscribed on public banners, he could have observed it from this text, even if the art of notarikon had not yet commonly prevailed. Rivetus is too hostile to images, and therefore also, which he does not hide, he calls this symbol into doubt; yet he could not suggest another more convenient etymon or foundation for the name Maccabeus; and therefore we do not see a reason why we should depart from the passive opinion, which Junius also especially approves at 1 Maccab. 1.

Vers. same. TERRIBLE AND PRAISEWORTHY.

Hebrew. נורא often denotes, to be revered. The Lord is therefore said to be not terrible, but to be revered with praises, because he is to be celebrated with all veneration & glory; thus GOD is said to be terrible in work Psalm 66, 5. that is, illustrious & glorious, and therefore reverend; so also terrible things are called Deut. 10, 21. mighty, and the day of the Lord is designated by this word Malach. 4, 5. not because he is terrible, but because he is truly to be revered & glorious. Therefore Tremell. & Jun. here rightly render the word reverend.

Latin:

Vers. 11. QUIS SIMILIS TUI IN FORTIBUS DOMINE?] Non dissimile Hesiodeum illud: Αὐτὸς γὰρ πάν- των βασιλεὺς κῂ κοίραγός ἐσιν Ἀθανάτων· ἔο δ᾽ ὅτις ἐρήρισται κρά- τει ἅλλος.

In Ebr. In Diis, gentium scil. ut LXX. quæ comparatio cum gentilium Diis ad majestatem DEI explicandam frequens est in scripturis, non quod aliquid κατ᾽ ἀλήθειαν aut revera gentium Diis tribuatur, idola enim nihil sunt 1. Cor. 8, 6. sed ut gentes in gloriatione sua confundantur. Ex literis vocum initialibus in Ebræo secundum Cabbalam, quam νοταριακὴν vocant, cum una litera signum est integræ dictionis, non pauci nomen מכבי desumtum esse censent, Mercerus, Schindlerus, Buxt. Sixtus item Senensis & Genebr. quod pro symbolo literas illas initiales ex hoc versu in vexillis gesserint, qui inde Maccabæi nuncupati sunt: quod vero non placet Scalig. l. 5. de emend. temp. nec Full. l. 2. Miscell. c. 13. quod inventum illud Cabbalisticum recentius videatur, quam ut ad Maccabæorum tempora referendum sit. Rivetus id cumprimis ei opponit, quod 1. Macc. 2, 2. indigitetur, inde ab initio Judam Maccabæum cognominatum fuisse, antequam exercitui præesset. Sed ea ratio nobis satis prægnans non videtur; poterat enim Judas antea hoc Symbolum sibi elegisse, quod postmodum vexillis publicis inscriptum fuerit, poterat id ex hoc textu observasse, etiamsi ars notarica communiter tum nondum obtinuisset. Infestus nimis est Rivetus imaginibus, & ideo etiam, quod non dissimulat, hoc symbolum in dubium revocat; non potuit tamen aliud commodius Etymon aut fundamentum nominis Maccabæi suggerrere; ideoque non videmus causam, cur à passiva sententia, quam imprimis etiam Junius ad 1. Maccab. 1. comprobat, discedamus.

Vers. eod. TERRIBILIS ATQUE LAUDABILIS.

Ebr. נורא notat sæpe, verendus. Dicitur ergo non terribilis Dominus, sed verendus laudibus, quia omni veneratione & gloria celebrandus; sic DEUS terribilis opere dicitur Psalm. 66, 5. id est, illustris & gloriosus, adeoque reverendus; ita etiam terribilia dicuntur Deut. 10, 21. fortia, & dies Domini hac voce designatur Malach. 4, 5. non quod terribilis sit, sed quod vere sit verendus & gloriosus. Ideo Tremell. & Jun. hîc recte reddunt vocem reverendus.

## 15:13
Vers. 13. AND THOU HAST CARRIED HIM IN THY STRENGTH UNTO THY HOLY HABITATION.

These things are spoken prophetically, therefore the other part of the Canticle is to be established here; the former was Eucharistic for a past benefit; but this one is prophetic concerning future benefits, because victories against the Philistine, Edomite, and Moabite enemies are predicted, with prayers & sighs mixed in, whence it is also in part euktike.

By the holy habitation they understand the land of Canaan, which was not only inhabited by the holy Patriarchs, but was also divinely destined as the seat of the Church, in which God had also decreed to fix for himself a habitation and house of the sanctuary Psalm 132, 13. indeed in which the holy of holies, the Messiah, was to dwell. John 1, v. 14. Conf. Deut. 1, 31. This is not therefore to be understood of Mount Sinai, which is nowhere called the habitation of GOD, much less the mountain of God's inheritance and sanctuary.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET PORTASTI EUM IN FORTITUDINE TUA AD HABITACULUM SANCTUM TUUM.

Hæc prophetice dicuntur, ideo hîc altera pars Cantici constituenda; prior erat Eucharistica pro beneficio præterito; hæc vero prophetica est de futuris beneficiis, quia prædicuntur victoriæ contra hostes Philistæos, Edomitas, Moabitas, admistis tamen precibus & suspiriis, unde ex parte etiam est εὐκτικὴ.

Per habitaculum sanctum terram Canaan intelligunt, quæ non tantum à Patriarchis sanctis habitata, sed etiam in sedem Ecclesiæ divinitus destinata erat, in qua etiam habitaculum & domum sanctuarii sibi Deus figere decreverat Psalm. 132, 13. imo in qua habitare debebat sanctus sanctorum Messias. Joh. 1, v. 14. Conf. Deut. 1, 31. Non ergo de monte Sinai hoc intelligendum, qui nuspiam habitaculum DEI dicitur, nedum mons hæreditatis Dei & sanctuarii.

## 15:16
Verse 16. LET THEM BECOME IMMOVABLE.

In Hebrew: Let them be silent as a stone. LXX: ἀπολιθωθήτωσαν, let them become stone. B. Luth. most fittingly, that they may stiffen like stones. Moses prays that they may not be moved by the enemy

of the Hebrews, but that they may be forced to fall silent, until the people of the Lord pass through.

Latin:

Vers. 16. FIANT IMMOBILES.
