Dicta haec sunt προλεπτικῶς, quia tum non- dum constructum erat tabernaculum; neque enim cum Lyrano & aliis statuendum, Ebraeos parvum quoddam tabernaculum habuisse, priusquam ma- gnum illud exstrueretur. Nam quod 33. cap. vers. 7. legitur de tentorio conventus extra castra, ἀλλό- τριον est; siquidem illud erectum demum in Horeb fuerit, & manifestum est indicium προλήψεως histo- ricae, quod manna reponi debuerit coram Domino, seu ante testimonium; arca enim foederis certe tum nondum constructa fuit.

## 16:35
Verse 35. BUT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL ATE MANNA FOR FORTY YEARS.

There is a doubt as to how these things could have been added by Moses, since it seems that Moses did not complete those forty years; some say that these things were added by Moses through the revelation of the Spirit: to others it seems that this was inserted rather by Joshua or another prophet; just as The narrative concerning the death of Moses, Deut. 34, 5, was added by another. But there does not seem to be a need for this answer; for this could have been written by Moses, as B. Rungius observes, in the fortieth year after the exodus from Egypt, in which most also believe the other books of Moses were written. But when the manna ceased, that was indicated by Joshua in ch. 5, 12.

Latin:

Versus 35. FILII AUTEM ISRAEL COMEDE- RUNT MANNA QUADRAGINTA AN- NIS.

Dubium est, quomodo haec a Mose ad- jici potuerint, cum videatur, Mosen quadra- ginta illos annos non explevisse; nonnulli di- cunt, ex revelatione Spiritus haec a Mose adje- cta esse: aliis videtur a Josua potius aut alio propheta hoc insertum fuisse; quemadmodum narratio de morte Mofis Deut. 34, 5. ab alio adjecta fuit. Sed non videtur opus esse hoc responso; scribi enim hoc potuit a Mose, ut B. Rungius ob- servat, quadragesimo demum anno post exitum ex Ægypto, quo & cæteros libros Mofis pleriq; con- scriptos censent. Quando autem Manna desierit, id a Josua indicatum est c. 5, 12.

## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII. Water from the Rock. The smiting of the Amalekites.

Verse 1. ACCORDING TO THE COMMANDMENT OF THE LORD.

In the Hebrew, 'according to the mouth of the Lord,' just as in Num. 9, 18, it is likewise held, 'according to the mouth of the Lord the children of Israel set out,' that is, at the command of the Lord; for there is no need for us to establish that Moses was taught the will of the Lord concerning every station by an oracle of a living voice through special revelation, which Rivetus desires, since the divine nod could have been known through the pillar of cloud while it was proceeding, as they followed its movement.

verse same. IN REPHIDIM.

This was the eleventh station; for two intermediate ones, the ninth and the tenth, are omitted here, in Dophkah and Alush, see Num. 33, 13, 14.

Verse same. WHERE THERE WAS NO WATER TO DRINK.

The Hebrews imagine that the manna provided the place not only of food, but also of drink. But that is repugnant to this passage, because in that way the Israelites could not have been pressed by thirst.

Latin:

CAPUT XVII. Aqua de Petra. Amalecitarum percussio.

Versus 1. JUXTA SERMONEM DOMINI.

IN Ebr. juxta os Domini, quemadmodum Num. 9, 18. itidem habetur, super os Domini proficisceban- tur filii Israel, id est, ad imperium Domini; neq; enim opus est, ut statuamus vivæ vocis oraculo volunta- tem Domini de quavis statione per specialem reve- lationem Mosen edoctum fuisse, quod vult Rivetus, cum nutus divinus cognosci potuerit per columnam nubis, dum illa procederet, utpote cujus motum se- quebantur.

vers. eod. IN RAPHIDIM.

Hæc fuit undecima mansio; duæ enim inter- mediæ, nona, & decima hîc omissæ sunt in Daphka & Alus, vid. Num. 33, 13. 14.

Vers. eod. UBI NON ERAT AQUA AD BI- BENDUM.

Ebræi fingunt, manna non tantum cibi, sed etiam potus vicem præbuisse. Sed id repugnat huic loco, quia ita siti premi non potuissent Israelitæ.

## 17:2
Verse 2. WHO QUARRELED AGAINST MOSES.

This was a most grave sin, both because they rioted against Moses as their legitimate leader, and because, having forgotten GOD, they demand water from Moses in the desert; 'give us water': cf. Gen. 30, 1, 2. And therefore they are said to have tempted God here, and in v. 7. Furthermore, the history which is held in Num. 20 is not the same, but different from the present one: because this happened in Rephidim, and indeed in the first year of the exodus: but that one in Kadesh toward the beginning of the 40th year. Therefore the murmurers say in Num. 20, 'Would that we had perished among our brothers!' which the people, not yet affected by that slaughter, could not say here.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QUI JURGATUS CONTRA MO- SEN.

Gravissimum hoc fuit peccatum, tum quod contra Mosen ceu legitimum principem tumultua- ti sunt, tum quod DEI obliti a Mose in deserto a- quam poscunt; da nobis aquam: conf. Gen. 30, 1. 2. Ideoque Deum tentasse dicuntur hic, & v. 7. Cæte- rum Historia quæ Num. 20. habetur, non eadem, sed diversa est a præsente: quia hæc contigit in Raphi- dim, & quidem anno primo egressus: illa vero in Cades sub initium anni 40. Ideo dicunt murmu- rantes Num. 20. Utinam periissemus inter fratres nostros! quod hic dicere non poterat populus clade illa nondum affectus.

## 17:5
Verse 5. WITH WHICH YOU STRUCK THE RIVER.

Understand the Nile turned into blood, Exod. 7, with Augustine, quest. 64, which Moses had struck through his brother Aaron. But that others wish the Red Sea to be designated does not fit; for nowhere does that sea come under the name of a river. Moreover, it had to be done in the presence of the elders of Israel, but not in the presence of the whole people, because such a great multitude could not be summoned to conveniently inspect the miracle. Whence it is gathered that the river emanated from some part of the rock; but one that would suffice for all for drinking. The power of the miracle is in this, that at the sign of the striking of the rod, copious waters flowed from the rock, where before there were none, cf. Psalm 78, verse 15. That they still flowed water from that rock, by the testimony of Abulensis, as he says, of certain cosmographers, he thinks, nay, he believes, that Arabia, which had been uninhabitable before because of excessive drought, was made habitable thereby. But that does not quite fit the history, for if water had always flowed in the desert, how would the Israelites have lacked it afterwards? Concerning this water, it is held in 1 Cor. 10, v. 4, which is called spiritual there, because of its spiritual signification, because, namely, it figured the drink of the soul, nay, it was even a figure of the blood of Christ, by which we are given to drink in the Holy Supper, which the Apostle indicates there. He adds, however, 'and they drank from the spiritual rock following them, which was Christ.' Where the Calvinists understand the material rock, which Moses struck, and from this they try to carve out their EST σημαντικὸν: 'The rock, however, was Christ,' that is, it signified Christ. But they are mistaken, because the Israelites are said to have drunk ἐκ πνευματικῆς πέτρας, from the spiritual Rock, and the Apostle testifies concerning this spiritual Rock that it was Christ, but he does not pronounce concerning the material one that it signified Christ. For Christ is truly the spiritual rock, as he is often called, Ps. 118, v. 22, Is. 8, 14, ch. 28, 16, Matt. 16, 18, Acts 4, 11, Rom. 9, 33, 1 Pet. 2, 8. Furthermore, the Apostle speaks of the Rock following the Israelites: But that material rock did not follow them as they set out. For what the Jews say, that that rock was moved from its place and carried around on carts for the whole 40 years, or what others wish, that it was carried in Mary's bosom, is a ridiculous fable: nor does it deserve greater faith that they say the waters flowing from the rock followed the camps wherever they went through channels, or conduits, which the princes made with their staffs, which they dragged behind them on the ground; from which the Calvinists' fiction differs little, concerning the waters following the Israelites everywhere, who also in this passage of the Apostle understand by the rock that followed them the waters produced from the rock, such as Calvin, Beza, Piscator, Rivetus, and others. But the Apostle says the Israelites followed the rock, not the waters; if by metonymy the waters are understood by the rock (because the Calvinists take refuge in that), it must be said that Christ was signified not by the rock, but by the waters, and thus this statement will emerge: the rock was Christ, that is, the waters gushing from the rock were, that is, signified Christ. And it is false, and contrary to Mosaic history, that the waters followed the Hebrews, because they felt a shortage of water several times afterwards. Therefore Junius himself rejects this fiction in book 2, paral. 36. But that they are said to have drunk from the spiritual rock, Christ, even those in whom there was no good pleasure: Blessed Hunnius wishes that to have been done in type, as far as the impious are concerned. But it is more conveniently said that the particle ἐκ has the sense of an efficient cause, that they drank and were given to drink or received drink from the spiritual rock, Christ, accompanying them, who was the author and source of the miraculously produced water: for he was leading the Israelites in the desert. Where it is to be observed that the verb ἀκολουθεῖν does not only denote following one who goes before; but generally signifies to make a journey together with someone, whether you go before, or follow, or join yourself as a companion at his side; from the particle α, which among the Greeks has the meaning of τοῦ ὁμοῦ, together, and from the noun κέλευθος, way, as Fr. Junius notes. Which sense of the verb the Syrian also expressed, 'they drank from the rock of the Spirit, which was coming or going with them.' The Calvinist Musculus also supports us when he says: 'they drank from the spiritual rock'; he diverts the minds of those following from the bodily rock to Christ the spiritual rock, whence he also adds: 'the rock, however, was Christ.' The corporeal rock can also be called spiritual, because it was a figure of the spiritual rock. But since he adds, 'which was following,' I think it must be understood of Christ himself: for he was following the people in the desert, and was supplying them with water by a miraculous gushing. in the sponge therefore falls the argument of the Calvinists, which they seek from this place for their metonymical EST, since Christ is truly the rock, not only figuratively; whence the Syrian emphatically rendered: but that rock itself was Christ. And therefore Musculus acknowledges, when the Apostle says: but the rock was Christ, it is not to be expounded: that rock signified Christ; but just as the words sound: that rock, which followed them, was Christ: Conf. B. Luther. Tom. 2. Jen. Germ. fol. 222.

Finally, the Calvinists are mistaken when they make the rock, as also the Manna, Sacraments of the O.T. and conclude from them the nature of the sacraments: for although they were figures or types of spiritual things, they were not, however, Sacraments or means of grace.

Latin:

Vers. 5. QUA PERCUSSISTI FLUVIUM.

Nilum intellige in sanguinem conversum, Exod. 7. cum Augustino quæst. 64. quem Moses per fratrem Aaronem percusserat. Quod autem alii mare rubrum designari volunt, non congruit; nuspiam enim mare illud fluvii nomine venit. Cæ- terum coram senioribus Israel id fieri debebat, non autem coram toto populo, quia tanta multitudo accerfi non poterat, ut commode inspectaret mi- raculum. Unde colligitur, ex aliqua parte rupis fluvium emanasse; sed qui sufficeret omnibus ad potum. Miraculi vis in eo est, quod ad signum ictus virgæ aquæ copiosæ e petra effluxerint, ubi antea nullæ erant, conf. Psalm. 78. vers. 15. Adhuc fluxere aquam ex illa rupe, Abulensis testimonio, ut dicit, Cosmographorum quorundam, arbitra- tur, imo putat, Arabiam, quæ ob nimiam siccita- tem inhabitabilis antea fuerit, inde factam esse habitabilem. Sed id historiæ non admodum con- gruit, nam si semper fluxisset aqua in deserto, quo- modo eadem caruissent deinceps Israelitæ? De hac aqua habetur 1. Cor. 10. v. 4. quæ spiritualis ibi vo- catur, ob significationem spiritualem, quia sc. figura- bat animæ potum, imo etiam figura erat sanguinis Christi, quo potamur in S. Cœna, quod indicat ibi Apostolus. Addit autem, bibebant vero de petra spirituali sequente eos, quæ erat Christus. Ubi Calvi- niani petram materialem intelligunt, quam Moses percussit, & hinc exsculpere conantur suum EST σημαντικὸν: Petra autem erat Christus, id est, signifi- cabat Christum. Sed falluntur, quia bibisse dicun- tur Israelitæ ἐκ πνευματικῆς πέτρας e spirituali Pe- tra, & de hac Petra spirituali testatur Apostolus, quod fuerit Christus, non autem de materiali pro- nunciat, quod significarit Christum. Vere enim Christus est spiritualis petra, uti sæpe appellatur, Ps. 118. v. 22. Es. 8,14. cap. 28,16. Matth. 16,18. Actor. 4, 11. Rom. 9,33. 1. Petr. 2,8. Adhæc loquitur Aposto- lus de Petra insequente Israelitas: At illa materialis petra secuta ipsos proficiscentes non est. Nam quod Judæi dicunt petram illam loco motam & curri- bus circumvectam esse per totos 40. annos, aut quod alii volunt, Mariæ gremio portatam, fabula ridicula est: nec majorem fidem meretur, quod ajunt, aquas e petra promanantes castra quocunque proficiscerentur subsecutas fuisse per canales, seu ductus, quos Princi- pes baculis suis, quos in terra post se traxerint, fece- rint; a quibus parum abit Calvinianorum commen- tum, de aquis Israelitas undequaque secutis, qui etiam in hoc Apostoli loco per petram ipsos consequu- tam aquas e petra productas intelligunt, utpote Cal- vinus, Beza, Piscat. Rivetus & alii. At Apostolus de petra dicit Israelitas sequuta, non de aquis; si meto- nymice per petram aquæ intelligantur (quia eo re- fugiunt Calviniani) dicendum erit, Christum non per petram, sed per aquas significatum fuisse, adeo- que hæc prodibit enunciatio: petra erat Christus, id est, aquæ e petra scaturientes erant, id est, significabant Christum. Et falsum est, atque historiæ Mosaicæ contrarium, aquas secutas esse Ebræos, quia senserunt aliquoties deinceps aquæ penuriam. Ideo repro- bat ipse Junius hoc commentum libr. 2. paral. 36. Quod autem bibisse dicuntur de petra spirituali Chri- sto, etiam ii, in quibus non fuit beneplacitum: id in typo factum esse, Beat. Hunnius vult, quantum ad impios. Sed commodius dicitur, particulam ἐκ sensum habere caufæ efficientis, quod biberint & po- tati sint vel potum acceperint a spirituali petra Chri- sto ipsos comitante, qui autor & scaturigo erat aquæ miraculose productæ: hic enim deducebat Israeli- tas in deserto. Ubi observandum, verbum ἀκο- λουθεῖν non tantum notare sequi præeuntem; sed ge- neraliter significare, facere iter cum aliquo simul, sive præeas, sive sequaris, sive te comitem ad latus ejus adjungas; a particula α, quæ apud Græcos habet significationem τοῦ ὁμοῦ simul & a nomine κέλευθος via, ut Fr. Junius notat. Quem sensum verbi ex- pressit etiam Syrus, bibebant de petra Spiritus, quæ veniebat seu ibat cum illis. Suffragatur nobis etiam Musculus Calvinianus, cum dicit: biberunt de spirituali petra; avocat mentes sequentium a petra corporali ad Christum petram spiritua- lem, unde & subdit: petra autem erat Christus. Po- test & petra corporea spiritualis dici, propterea quod fi- gura fuit spiritualis petræ. Verum quoniam addit, quæ sequebatur, intelligendum esse puto de ipso Chri- sto: is enim consequebatur populum in deserto, & a- quas illi miraculosa scaturigine subministrabat. In spongiam ergo incumbit argumentum Calviniano- rum, quod pro EST suo metonymico hinc petunt, si- quidem Christus vere sit petra, non tantum significa- tive; unde Syrus emphatice reddidit: petra autem il- la ipse erat Christus. Ideoque agnoscit Musculus, cum dicit Apostolus: petra autem erat Christus, non esse exponendum: petra illa significabat Christum; sed quemadmodum verba sonant: petra illa, quæ seque- batur eos, erat Christus: Conf. B. Luther. Tom. 2. Jen. Germ. fol. 222.

Denique falluntur Calvinia- ni, cum petram, ut & Manna Sacramenta faciunt V. T. & ex iis rationem sacramentorum concludunt: nam etsi figuræ aut typi fuerint rerum spiritualium, non tamen Sacramenta vel media gratiæ erant.

## 17:8
Ver. 8. BUT AMALEK CAME) Which people had their seats in Gobolitis and Petra according to Josephus.

Amalek, that is, the people of Amalek, whose Prince was Amalek the son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau, Gen. 36, 16. But whether all the Princes or Kings of this people obtained the same name Amalek, which seems so to some, is doubtful; the cause also, which some here bring forward for this war, that it was the ancient hatred of Esau and his descendants against Jacob and his descendants on account of the stolen blessing, is less likely: for it does not appear that they had thought then about the promises given to Israel through the blessing, as if they ought to be fulfilled already; nay, it is rather credible that the Amalekites were induced by the hope of plunder or some other wicked desire to attack the Hebrews in war.

Latin:

Vers. 8. VENIT AUTEM AMALEK) Cui populo sedes in Gobolitide & Petra secundum Josephum.

Amaleck, id est, populus Amalek, cujus Prin- ceps fuit Amalek filius Eliphaz, nepos Esavi, Gen. 36, 16. utrum autem omnes Principes vel Reges populi hujus idem nomen Amalek obtinuerint, quod non- nullis videtur, dubium est; Causa etiam, quam hic nonnulli adferunt hujus belli, quod fuerit anti- quum odium Esavi & posterorum adversus Jacobum & posteros ob præreptam benedictionem, minus verisimilis est: nam cogitasse tum eos de promissio- nibus per benedictionem Israeli datis, quasi jam im- pleri debeant, haud apparet, imo potius credibile est, spe prædæ aut alia prava cupiditate inductos fuis- se Amalekitas, ut bello Ebræos adorirentur.

## 17:9
v. 9. MOSES SAID TO JOSHUA.

This battle is committed to Joshua, because he was to lead the people into the land of Canaan, and therefore he had to be accustomed to war little by little. But he is called Joshua, who seems to have been named Hosea before, Num. 12, 9. whence that name in this place will be proleptic, conveniently applied, because here Joshua showed himself truly a Joshua, that is, a savior of the people.

Ver. same. WENT OUT TO FIGHT AGAINST AMALEK] To forestall the attempts of enemies before they grow strong. Ver. 10. HUR) He had married Miriam, the sister of Moses and Aaron.

Latin:

v. 9. DIXIT MOSE AD JOSUE.

Committitur hoc prælium Josuæ, quia is po- pulum erat in terram Canaan introducturus, ideo- que assuescere bello paulatim debebat. Vocatur autem Josua, qui prius videtur nominatus fuisse Hoseas, Num. 12, 9. unde nomen illud hoc in loco e- rit proleptlicum, commode adhibitum, quia hic Josua præstitit se vere Josuam, hoc est, salvatorem populi.

Vers. eod. EGRESSUS PUGNA CONTRA AMALEC] Prævertendi hostium conatus, priusquam invalescant. Vers. 10. HUR) Is Mariammen duxerat sororem Mosis & Aaronis.

## 17:11
Ver. 11. ISRAEL PREVAILED.

Josephus reports that the victory was bloodless for the Hebrews; those things can therefore be reconciled if the Amalekites are said to have conquered at some point, not by killing any of the Israelites, but by forcing them to retreat until, having resumed their strength while Moses raised his hands, they pressed on more fiercely.

Latin:

Vers. 11. VINCEBAT ISRAEL.

Josephus refert, incruentam fuisse Ebræis vi- ctoriam; conciliari ergo illa ita poterunt, si dicantur vicisse aliquando Amalekithæ, non aliquos ex Isra- elitis occidendo, sed eos cogendo, ut retrocede- rent, donec resumtis viribus Mose manus levante acrius insisterent.

## 17:12
v. 12. BUT THE HANDS OF MOSES WERE HEAVY.

Not so much on account of old age, because after almost 40 years his vigor was still intact, Deut. 34, 7, as on account of exhaustion in the raising of his hands: because to raise a hand for the space of even one hour continuously, and indeed with a staff extended in the manner of a standard-bearer, produces exhaustion. Therefore the hands of Moses were supported by two standing on each side, who helped Moses, who was holding the staff, by turns.

Latin:

v. 12. MANUS AUTEM MOSI ERANT GRAVES.

Non tam ob senium, quia post annos fere 40. vigor ejus integer adhuc erat, Deut. 34, 7. quam ob defatigationem in elevatione manuum: quia manum vel unius horæ spacio continuo elevare, & quidem protenso baculo more vexilliferi, defatigationem parit. Ideo sustentabatur manus Mosis a duobus ex utraq; parte stantibus, qui alternis vicibus bacu- lum tenentem Mosen juvabant.

## 17:13
Verse 13. AND JOSHUA PUT AMALEK TO FLIGHT.

In Hebrew it is 'weakened' or 'prostrated' partly by killing the Amalekites, partly by putting them to flight; 'in the mouth of the sword,' that is, in the edge of the sword, where however the complete phrase, 'he struck with the edge of the sword,' seems to imply a slaughter of extermination, because he destroyed the army even to extermination. It is called the mouth of the sword metaphorically, because men are consumed by the sword just as food is chewed by the mouth. But inept is the explanation of Franciscus

Ribera, 'in the will of the sword' or 'as much as the sword strikes.'

Latin:

Versus 13. FUGAVITQUE JOSUE AMALEK.

In Ebr. debilitavit, vel prostravit partim oc- cidendo Amalekitas, partim in fugam agendo; in ore gladii, id est, in acie gladii, ubi tamen phrasis integra, percussit in ore gladii, videtur stragem in- ternecinam inferre, quod exercitum deleverit us- que ad internecionem. Dicitur os gladii metapho- rice, quia gladio viri consumuntur, quemadmodum cibi ore manduntur. Inepta vero est Francisci

Riberæ explicatio, in voluntate gladii vel quantum gladius ferit.

## 17:14
v. 14. WRITE THIS FOR A MEMORIAL IN A BOOK.

God ordered it to be written, not only so that the history might pass to posterity, but primarily also because of the edict of the Lord concerning the blotting out of the memory of the Amalekites; such commands of writing occur here and there, Exod. 24, 4, chap. 34, 27, Deut. 31, 19, Jos. 24, 26, Ps. 102, 19, from which and similar ones it is permitted to gather that the Holy Scriptures did not come forth without divine command.

For it is not necessary that we should seek this book among the lost ones, since this very book exhibits the history of the law, written down by the command of GOD. It seems consistent to B. Rungius that Moses immediately wrote the history of the war of the Amalekites, which he subsequently, when he was finishing the Pentateuch near the end of his life, inserted into his books, and thus the same thing was written in a separate book, which is now read in Exodus 17 from verse 8 up to the last, as also in Deuteronomy 25, verse 17.

Verse of the same.

FOR I WILL BLOT OUT THE REMEMBRANCE OF AMALEK FROM UNDER HEAVEN.

This severe edict of the Lord against the Amalekites is sanctioned on account of their malice described in Deuteronomy 25, verse 18, because without any declaration of war, provoked by no injury, they did not hesitate to treacherously rush upon the Israelites, their kinsmen, and indeed those who were walking more slowly, separated from the rest of the multitude, and to slaughter and despoil them, exhausted by hunger and labor, which vengeance God executed through Saul, having delayed it until then out of μακροθυμίᾳ, 1 Samuel 15:3. Haman the Agagite, from the stock of Agag, King of Amalek, also felt it in the judgment of some, Esther 3:1, 1 Samuel 15:32, when his own far more grievous guilt was added.

Latin:

vers. 14. SCRIBE HOC OB MONUMENTUM IN LIBRO.

Scribi jussit Deus, non tantum, ut historia ad posteritatem transiret, sed imprimis etiam ob edi- ctum Domini de delenda memoria Amalecitarum; ta- lia mandata scriptionis occurrunt passim Exod. 24, 4. cap. 34, 27. Deut. 31, 19. Jos. 24, 26. Ps. 102, 19. ex quibus & similibus colligere licet, non sine mandato divino scripturas S. prodiisse.

Neque enim neces- sum est, ut hunc librum inter deperditos quæramus, quum hic ipse liber legis historiam exhibeat, ex mandato DEI descriptam. B. Rungio consenta- neum videtur, Mosen statim scripsisse historiam bel- li Amalecitarum, quam deinceps cum circa finem vitæ Pentateuchon absolveret, libris suis inseruerit, atque sic idem fuisse scriptum in libro separato, quod nunc Exod. 17. a vers. 8. usq; ad ult. legitur, ut & Deut. 25. vers. 17.

Vers. eod.

DELEBO ENIM MEMORIAM AMALEC SUB COELO.

Edictum hoc severum Domini contra Ama- lecitas sancitur ob malitiam eorum Deut. 25. versu 18. descriptam, quod sine ulla belli denunciatione nulla injuria provocati proditorie in Israelitas co- gnatos atq; illos quidem, qui tardius incedebant, separati a reliqua multitudine, irruere, eosq; cæde- re ac spoliare non dubitarint, fame ac labore confe- ctos, quam vindictam Deus per Saulem executus est, eo usque ex μακροθυμίᾳ dilatam 1. Sam. 15, 3. Sensit eam etiam judicio nonnullorum Haman A- gagites ex stirpe Agag Regis Amalec Esth. 3, 1. 1. Sam. 16, 32. cum propria culpa longe gravissima accede- ret.

## 17:15
Verse 15. AND MOSES BUILT AN ALTAR.

This seems to have been built not for sacrificing, but only for the memory of the event, such as that which is described in Joshua 22, verse 29.

Verse of the same.

AND HE CALLED THE NAME OF IT THE LORD MY EXALTATION.

In Hebrew, Jehovah נסי, which Tremellius and Junius render: Jehovah my banner; but whether it is rendered in the oblique or in the nominative, which pleases us more, Jehovah is my banner, neither can the Photinians conclude from it that the name of Jehovah was absolutely given to the altar; nor can the Papists (who pour cold water upon them) infer that divine names are communicated to images or other monuments; because this name occurs not absolutely, but μετὰ συμπλοκῆς, the altar is not called Jehovah, but a symbolic and memorial name is exhibited in a complete proposition, Jehovah is my banner.

Jehovah, therefore, is called the banner or exaltation of Israel, because they trusted in Jehovah, and held him for their strength and exaltation, in which sense Cornelius himself explains it, denying that the name of God is communicated to the altar, since the sense is: by this altar, as if by a trophy, I testify or signify that GOD is my exaltation.

These words have a difficulty in the Hebrew, sounding thus: because the hand is upon the throne of the Lord. B. Luther rendered it: It is a sign by the throne of the LORD, that is, this sin of the Amalekites is marked as if on a scroll OF GOD, that he may always be in his sight. The Chaldean paraphrast explains it concerning an oath, and by the hand, the Hebrews understand the hand of God extended, by which God swore by his throne that he would destroy the Amalekites. Tremellius and Junius wish it to be signified that God, sitting on the throne of majesty, has his hand stretched out against the Amalekites. Others explain it concerning Moses, with hand raised toward the throne of God, swearing. Rivetus, in almost the same way, speaks of the hand of Moses raised toward Heaven, which is the throne of the Lord, but not for the sake of an oath, but rather for obtaining victory against the Amalekites, so that it may be indicated that this will also be so from generation to generation, which sense seems the simplest, because it overflows from the very words. I would not say that it must be asserted with the Hebrews that God swore with hand raised, since such a thing concerning an oath of GOD by a hand raised above the throne of the Lord is not found in the Scriptures. Nor does it appear how Grotius's explanation, that the hand is understood as divine power, fits the Hebrew text. For what is this, the hand, that is, divine power upon the throne of the Lord?

Latin:

Vers. 15. ÆDIFICAVITQUE MOSES AL- TARE.

Non hoc ad sacrificandum, sed ad memoriam rei tantum extructum videtur, quale fuit quod Jos. 22. v. 29. describitur.

Vers. eod.

ET VOCAVIT NOMEN EJUS DOMINUS EXALTATIO MEA.

In Ebr. Jehovah נסי quod Trem. & Jun. red- dunt : Jehovah vexilli mei; sed sive in obliquo redda- tur, sive in recto, quod magis nobis placet, Jehovah est vexillum meum, non possunt vel Photiniani ex eo concludere nomenJehovæ absolute datum esse alta- ri; vel Papistæ, (qui frigidam iis suffundunt) infer- re, imaginibus aut aliis monumentis nomina divina communicari; quia occurrit hoc nomen non abso- lute, sed μετὰ συμπλοκῆς, non altare dicitur Jeho- vah, sed nomen symbolicum & memoriale integra propositione exhibetur, Jehovah est vexillum meum.

Jehovah ergo dicitur vexillum vel exaltatio Israelis, quia in Jehovah confidebant, eumque pro robore & exaltatione sua habebant, quo sensu explicat ipse Cornelius, negans Dei nomen altari communicari, siquidem sensus sit: altari hoc, quasi trophæo testor vel significo, quod DEUS sit exaltatio mea.

Difficultatem habent hæc verba in Ebræo ita sonantia : quia manus super thronum Domini. B. Lutherus reddidit : Es ist ein Mahlzeichen bey dem Stul des HERRN, id est, hoc peccatum Amalecitarum consignatum est quasi in folio DEI, ut semper illi sit in conspectu. Chaldæus paraphrastes de juramento explicat, & per manum, manum Dei extensam intelligunt Ebræi, qua jurarit Deus per thronum suum, se Amalekitas deleturum. Tremel. & Jun. id significari volunt, Deum solio majestatis insidentem manum exertam habere contra Amalecitas. Alii de Mose elevata manu versus solium Dei jurante explicant. Rivetus fere similiter de manu Mosis versus Cœlum, qui est thronus Domini, elata, sed non juramenti causa, verum ob victoriam contra Amalecitas obtinendam, ut indicetur, id deinceps quoque fore de generatione in generationem, qui sensus videtur simplicissimus, quia ex ipsis verbis redundat. Deum jurasse manu elata, cum Ebræis asserendum non dixerim, siquidem tale quid de juramento DEI per manum super thronum Domini elevatam in Scripturis haud reperitur. Nec apparet, quomodo Ebræo textui conveniat explicatio Grotii, quod manus divinæ potentiæ intelligatur. Quid enim hoc, manus, id est, potentia divina super throno Domini?

## 18:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVIII. Jethro's Counsel.

AND WHEN JETHRO HAD HEARD) Moses gives us an excellent example of naming those through whom we have made progress.

Verse same. PRIEST OF MIDIAN.

Although the name כהן may be more general, the Vulgate opinion concerning Jethro as a priest of the true God does not seem entirely to be rejected, such as it is gathered from the scriptures that some existed among the descendants of Abraham, and it is confirmed by this example, when Jethro is said to have offered sacrifices; even if it were polluted here and there by the mixing and worship of idols.

Latin:

CAPUT XIIX. Jethronis Consilium.

Vers. 1. CUMQUE AUDISSET JETHRO) Dat nobis egregium exemplum Moses, nominandi eos, per quos profecimus.

Vers. eod. SACERDOS MADIAN.

QUanquam nomen כהן generalius sit, non videtur tamen omnino improbanda Vulgata sententia de Jethrone Sacerdote veri Dei, quales apud Abrahami posteros fuisse quosdam, ex scripturis colligitur, & hoc exemplo, cum Jethro obtulisse dicitur sacrificia, confirmatur; etsi simulacrorum mixtione & cultu passim pollueretur.

## 18:2
TOOK ZIPPORAH THE WIFE OF MOSES WHOM HE HAD SENT BACK.

It is doubtful, when did Moses send her back? Some think he sent her back from Egypt, because he saw that the business committed to him was grave and extremely arduous, and could not be dispatched in a few days. Others finally judge that after the crossing of the Red Sea, Moses sent his wife and sons back to his father-in-law for the sake of greeting and saying farewell, because they were then not far from the borders of the Moabites. Others render the Hebrew words in this place, as Fagius observes, as 'after her gifts,' as if Moses had sent gifts to his wife and children, so that Jethro might more easily bring them to him. The former opinion seems probable, if you weigh the circumstances of the history; however, the choice is left free to everyone.

Latin:

Vers. 2. TULIT SEPHORAM UXOREM MOSI QUAM REMISERAT.

Dubium est, Quando remiserit Moses? Nonnulli ex Ægypto remisisse putant, quia videbat, negotium sibi commissum grave, & perquam arduum esse, nec paucis diebus expediri posse. Alii demum post transitum maris rubri Mosen uxorem & filios ad socerum remisisse salutandi & valedicendi causa censent, quia tum non procul erant a finibus Moabitarum. Alii verba Ebræa hoc in loco reddunt, ut observat Fagius, post munera ejus, quasi Mofis uxori & liberis munera miserit, ut Jethro eos sibi facilius adduceret. Prior sententia probabilis videtur, si historiæ circumstantias expendas; libera tamen relinquitur cuique optio.

## 18:5
BY THE MOUNT OF GOD.

He does not understand the station at Rephidim, but Mount Sinai or Horeb, which is called the mountain of GOD, Ex. 3:1. And therefore it is evident that these things were inserted προληπτικῶς (proleptically), because in the following chapter it is finally reported that the Israelites had arrived at Mount Sinai. However, this arrival was perhaps mentioned because Jethro, stirred by the fame of the victory obtained against the Amalekites in the vicinity, betook himself to Moses.

Regarding the time of arrival, hardly anything certain can be defined. Abulensis refers it to the end of the first year of the exodus, because in Deut. 1:6 ff. Moses is said to have created magistrates shortly before the camp was to be moved from Sinai, which was moved in the 2nd month of the second year, Num. 10:11. Jerome and Augustine, however, accommodate the reasoning of the time to the end of the narrative. We leave the matter in the middle, provided that this at least remains: that Jethro came before the people of GOD left Mount Sinai.

Latin:

Vers. 5. JUXTA MONTEM DEI.

Non intelligit stationem in Raphidim, sed montem Sinai vel Horeb, qui mons DEI vocatur, Ex. 3,1. Ideoque προληπτικῶς hæc inserta esse constat, quia cap. seq. demum referuntur Israëlitæ ad montem Sinai pervenisse. Memoratus autem hic adventus fuit forte, quia Jethro fama victoriæ contra Amalecitas in vicinia obtentæ excitus ad Mosen se contulit.

De tempore adventus vix certi quicquam definiri potest. Abulensis refert illum ad finem primi anni exitus, eo quod Deut. 1, 6. seqq. Moses dicatur Magistratus creasse, paulo ante quam movenda essent castra ex Sinai, quæ menses 2. anni secundi mota sunt, Num. 10, 11. Hieronymus vero & August. accommodant rationem temporis ad finem narrationis. Nos rem in medio relinquimus, dum id saltim maneat, venisse Jethronem, antequam montem Sinai relinqueret populus DEI.

## 18:7
Verse 7. HE ADORED AND KISSED.

In Hebrew: he bowed himself, or with inclined body he greeted his father-in-law; which honor was not only of servitude, but also of charity among the Orientals, to which a kiss was added as a sign of love, although this also was sometimes a sign of subjection and reverence, see Ps. 2:12.

Verse same. AND WHEN HE HAD ENTERED THE TABERNACLE.

Some wrongly understand the tabernacle of GOD. For it is not evident that it had been erected at the time of Jethro's arrival, nor could Moses have immediately introduced a foreigner into the tabernacle of God without scandal; and therefore it is to be understood of the tabernacle in which Moses dwelt.

Latin:

Verf. 7. ADORAVIT ET OSCULATUS EST.

In Ebræo: incurvavit se, vel inclinato corpore focerum salutavit; qui honor non servitutis tantum, sed charitatis etiam erat apud Orientales, cui oscu- lum accedebat amoris signum, etsi & hoc quandoq; subjectionis & reverentiæ signum esset, vid. Pf. 2, 12.

Verf. eod. CUMQUE INTRASSET TABER- NACULUM.

Perperam intelligunt nonnulli tabernaculum DEI. Nam neque illud erectum fuisse sub adven- tum Jethronis constat, nec alienigenam statim in ta- bernaculum Dei introducere potuisset Moses sine scandalo; ideoque de tabernaculo, in quo Moses ha- bitabat, id intelligendum est.

## 18:10
Verse 10. AND JETHRO REJOICED.

The Hebrew word implies immense joy. The LXX rendered it: ἐξέστη, he was astonished, because as if he were snatched into an ἔκστασιν (ecstasy) from joy.

Latin:

Verf. 10. LÆTATUSQUE EST JETHRO.

Verbum Ebræum gaudium ingens infert. LXX. reddiderunt: ἐξέση, obstupuit, quod præ gaudio qs. in ἔκστασιν raptus sit.

## 18:11
Verse 11. NOW I HAVE KNOWN THAT THE LORD IS GREAT ABOVE ALL GODS.

Now I know with more certain knowledge: for this must be understood as an increase of knowledge, because Jethro was not devoid of the knowledge of the true God, nor must it be determined, with Corn. a Lap. and others, that he had only some obscure knowledge of the God of Israel, remaining from the tradition of Midian, but mixed with idolatry, because Moses would not have married his daughter unless he had either been led to the knowledge of the true God, or could have been led to it through Moses' instruction; then indeed we see in this place that Jethro offers sacrifices to God, and receives the material for sacrifices from Moses, which would by no means have been granted to him if he had only now, as a Neophyte, aspired to the true faith. Furthermore, there is no doubt that through the works of Jethro the faith of the true God was propagated to his descendants, from whom also the Rechabites originated, 1 Chron. 2:55. I pass over the fact that it is by no means likely that Moses, the man of God and Prince of the Lord's people, received the form of governing the people of God from this Gentile, or from a Neophyte.

The Lord is great, he says, above all gods; indicating the gods of the nations, not because he attributes any divinity to them, and brings them into contention with his God in that respect, but because in the opinion of their worshippers they were believed to be gods: whence the comparison is not of the thing in itself, as it is, but as it was in the estimation of men: Cf. Exod. 12:12; similar things are found in Ps. 86:10, Ps. 135:5, 6.

verse of the same. FOR THAT THEY DEALT PROUDLY AGAINST THEM) Thus also some Greeks ὑπερηφανεύσαντο. The origin signifies alienation, the sense a hostile mind, as can be seen below 21:14, where the LXX explain this word, as also here, by ἐπιθέσθαι, to lie in wait. By translation it is led to those who sin with contempt of God, as Deut. 1:43, Jer. 1:29.

These words are not without difficulty, especially because of the ellipsis in the Hebrew text, which is rendered word-for-word thus: because in the thing in which they acted proudly, above or against them. The ellipsis is most simply supplied by the verb 'was', which often comes to be understood, and a clear sense redounds from it of this kind: The Lord is great above all gods, because in the thing in which they acted proudly, or in that very thing in which the gods of the Egyptians and the Egyptians most exalted themselves, the Lord was against or above them, that is, in that he prevailed and overcame them, because there was a kind of battle and conflict between the gods of Egypt and the GOD of Israel, when they opposed themselves through the fictitious miracles of the magicians to the GOD performing miracles through Moses, just as it is established that demons deluded the Egyptians with wondrous prestidigitations, and in that most especially acted proudly; which sense is confirmed by the passage Exod. 12:12, I will execute judgments against all the gods of the Egyptians. In those judgments, therefore, God was above them, whose catastrophe was in the suffocation of Pharaoh, through whom the gods of the Egyptians and the demons themselves boasted, having become hardened against GOD and exalting themselves. For the fact that others supply an elliptical expression in this way, 'in that in which the Egyptians boasted in the same did GOD punish them,' is too arbitrary: for the name of the Hebrews is assumed, which is not in the text: a punishment is also added, about which Moses says nothing. Therefore, although the thing itself may be true, it cannot be sculpted from those words.

Latin:

Verf. 11. NUNC COGNOVI QUIA MA- GNUS DOMINUS SUPRA OMNES DEOS.

Nunc cognovi cognitione certiori: accipien- dum enim hoc de auxesi notitiæ, quia Jethro non fuit expers cognitionis veri Dei, neque vero cum Corn. a Lap. & aliis statuendum, quod obscuram tantum aliquam notitiam Dei Israelis habuerit, e traditione Madianis reliquam, sed permixtam ido- lolatria, quia neque Moses filiam ejus duxisset, nisi ad notitiam veri Dei vel perductus fuisset, vel per Mosis informationem perduci potuisset; tum vero videmus hoc loco, quod Jethro offerat Deo sacrifi- cia, & a Mose sacrificiorum materiam accipiat, quod ei minime concessum fuisset, si tanquam Neophytus nunc demum ad veram fidem adspirasset. Porro dubium non est, quin opera Jethronis fides veri Dei ad posteros propagata fuerit, a quo etiam Re- chabitæ orti sunt, 1. Paral. 2, 55. Taceo quod for- mam gubernandi populi Dei ab hoc gentili, aut a Neophyto accepisse Mosen, virum Dei & Princi- pem populi Domini, nequaquam verisimile sit.

Magnus Dominus, inquit, supra omnes Deos; indi- gitans Deos gentium, non quod illis aliquid Deita- tis tribuat, & in contentionem cum Deo ejus ratio- ne adducat, sed quia cultorum suorum opinione Dii credebantur: unde comparatio sit non rei in se, qua- lis ipsa est, sed qualis erat in æstimatione hominum: Conf. Exod. 12, 12. similia habentur Psal. 86, 10. Psal. 135, 5. 6.

verf. eod. EO QUOD SUPERBE EGERINT CONTRA ILLOS) Sic & quidam Græci ὑπερηφανεύσαντο. Origo alie- nationem significat, sensus hostilem animum, ut videre est in- fra 21. 14. ubi LXX. verbum hoc, ut & hic per ἐπιθέσθαι insi- diari exponunt. Translatione ducitur ad eos, qui cum Dei contemptu peccant, ut Deut. 1, 43. Jer. 1, 29.

Verba hæc difficultate non vacant, maxime ob Ellipsin in textu Ebræo, qui κατὰ πόδα ita red- ditur: quia in re, qua superbierunt, supra vel contra eos. Simplicissime suppletur Ellipsis per verbum fuit, quod sæpius subintelligendum venit, atq; sen- sus perspicuus inde redundat ejusmodi: Magnus Dominus supra omnes Deos, quia in re, qua super- bierunt, vel in illo ipso, quo Dii Ægyptiorum & Ægyptii maxime se efferebant, contra vel supra eos fuit Dominus, hoc est, in eo prævaluit & superavit eosdem, quia pugna quædam veluti & conflictus fuit inter Deos Ægypti & DEUM Israelis, cum illi per miracula fictitia Magorum sese opponerent DEO, miracula per Mosen patranti, quemadmo- dum constat, dæmones miris præstigiis illusisse Æ- gyptiis, inque eo maxime superbiisse; quem sensum firmat locus Exod. 12, 12. exerciturus sum judicia in omnes Deos Ægyptiorum. In iis ergo judiciis su- pra eos fuit Deus, quorum Catastrophe erat in suffo- catione Pharaonis, per quem induratum adversus DEUM sese efferentem superbierunt Dii Ægyptio- rum & dæmones ipsi. Nam quod alii supplent el- lipticam locutionem hoc modo, in quo superbierunt Ægyptii contra Ebræos, in eodem punivit illos DEUS; nimis arbitrarium est : assumitur enim nomen E- bræorum, quod in textu non habetur: additur etiam pœna, de qua nihil Moses. Itaque licet res ipsa ve- ra sit, e verbis tamen illis exsculpi non poterit.

## 18:12
Verse 12. JETHRO THEREFORE OFFERED.

In the Hebrew: he took. Tremellius and Junius render it: he offered what was taken. For he took for the sake of an offering, burnt offerings and sacrifices. Therefore it is said that he took for the Lord, that is, to offer to the Lord. He confirms his confession, therefore, by an external act, offering both burnt offerings for the expiation of sins, and peace or eucharistic sacrifices for thanksgiving. Nor indeed can it be said that he offered through Aaron, because it is signified that he himself received from Moses, and indeed to be offered to the Lord; nay, Aaron with the elders of Israel did indeed come to Jethro, but so that they might eat bread with him, not so that Aaron might offer his sacrifices. Whence it is evident that the name כהן in the more famous meaning is to be taken for a priest; and that Jethro was not a priest of idols; for thus he would not have been permitted to sacrifice to the Lord, nor would Aaron with the elders have been present among the guests at a banquet adorned from the offering.

Verse same. THAT THEY MIGHT EAT BREAD BEFORE GOD.

They gathered as a symbol of public joy and gratitude: but they are said to have eaten bread before GOD, that is, to have celebrated a banquet, either because the banquet was prepared from the food of the victims offered to God, or also because the feast was celebrated before the altar on which the offering had been made. Those who think the tabernacle had already been erected say that the banquet was instituted in it or next to it. Augustine, Question 66, renders 'before GOD' as 'in honor of God'; others, 'in the sight of,' that is, in the fear and reverence of God. But the former sense agrees more with similar phrases of Scripture, as well as with established custom. Compare Deut. 12:12, 1 Sam. 1:5, 1 Cor. 8:10.

Latin:

Vers. 12. OBTULIT ERGO JETHRO.

In Ebræo : accepit. Trem. & Jun. reddunt: acceptum obtulit. Nam accepit oblationis causa, holocausta & hostias. Ideo dicitur accepisse Domino, hoc est, ad offerendum Domino. Confessionem er- go suam externo actu confirmat offerens tum holo- causta pro expiatione peccatorum, tum hostias paci- ficas sive evcharisticas pro gratiarum actione. Nec vero dici potest, per Aaronem obtulisse, quia a Mose ipse accepisse significatur, & quidem Domino offe- renda, imo Aaron cum senioribus Israel venit qui- dem ad Jethronem, sed ut comederent panem cum eo, non ut Aaron sacrificia ipsius offerret. Unde con- stat, nomen כהן in significatu famosiori accipien- dum esse pro sacerdote; & Jethronem non fuisse sa- cerdotem Idolorum; sic enim Domino sacrificare non permissus fuisset, neq; convivio ex oblatione adornato Aaron cum senioribus hospites interfuif- serit.

Vers. eod. UT COMEDERENT PANEM CORAM DEO.

Convenerunt in symbolum publicæ lætitiæ & gratitudinis: panem autem coram DEO comedisse dicuntur, h. e. convivium celebrasse, sive quia de cibo victimarum Deo oblatarum paratum fuit convivi- um, sive etiam, quia epulum coram altari, in quo facta erat oblatio, celebratum est. Qui erectum jam fuisse tabernaculum putant, in illo vel juxta illud institutum fuisse convivium, dicunt. Augustin. quæst. 66. coram DEO reddit, in honorem Dei; alii; in conspectu, h. e. in timore & reverentia Dei. Sed prior sensus Scripturæ similibus phrasibus magis congruit, ut & receptæ consuetudini. Conf. Deut. 12,12. 1. Sam. 1,5. 1. Cor. 8,10.

## 18:15
Verse 15. SEEKING THE SENTENCE OF GOD.

In the Hebrew, 'seeking God,' or 'that he may inquire of God.' The Septuagint, looking to the sense, render it 'judgment from God,' because they wanted to be judged by Moses: 'But according to the sentence of God.' But because no law had yet been written down at that time, Moses consulted God, who was present to his mind, and wisely attended to His eternal law. Augustine, Questions on Exodus 67, rightly asserts; for there was no need for God to answer Moses immediately in all cases by some extraordinary revelation, because it was sufficient to have a divine rule to which sentences were to be adapted; yet it cannot be denied that Moses was instructed by God out of the ordinary with that habitual knowledge and wisdom, from which he could draw the decision of the most serious cases, consistent with the divine mind and will and the rule of justice.

Latin:

Vers. 15. QUÆRENS SENTENTIAM DEI.

In Ebr. quærens Deum, vel ut inquirat Deum. LXX. sensum respicientes reddunt judicium a Deo, quia judicari volebant a Mose: Sed juxta sententi- am Dei. Quia vero lex tum nulla adhuc conscri- pta erat, Deum menti suæ præsentem consuluisse Mo- sen, legemque ejus æternam sapienter attendisse. Aug. quæst. in Exod. 67. recte asserit; neque enim opus erat, ut Mosi Deus immediate responderet in omni- bus causis extraordinaria quadam revelatione, quia sufficiebat regulam habere divinam, cui adaptandæ erant sententiæ; non tamen negandum, Mosen extra ordinem ea cognitione, & sapientia habituali a Deo instructum fuisse, ex qua depromere potuerit cau- sarum gravissimarum decisionem menti & volunta- ti divinæ ac regulæ justitiæ consentaneam.

## 18:18
Verse 18. YOU WILL BE CONSUMED BY FOOLISH LABOR.

The Vulgate is too harsh. נָבֹל תִּבֹּל denotes not only to be foolish, but also to wither away and be consumed; it is noted, therefore, that by consuming he consumes himself; thus the LXX: Φθορᾷ καταφθαρήσῃ ἀνυπομονήτῳ, you will be corrupted with an intolerable corruption. And the Chaldean: you will be wearied by weariness, which is explained more clearly afterwards, the matter or business is heavy for you, it is beyond your strength, you alone cannot sustain it. God willed that Moses, most wise, should learn from a foreigner, showing thus that it is given to no one to be wise alone and in all things and always correctly. God does not give all things to one. Cf. 1 Cor. 12,8.

Latin:

Versus 18. STULTO LABORE CONSUME- RIS.

Duriter nimis Vulgatus. נָבֹל תִּבֹּל non so- lum stultum esse notat, sed etiam defluere & consumi; notatur ergo quod consumendo consumat sese; ita LXX. Φθορᾷ καταφθαρήσῃ ἀνυπομονήτῳ, corru- ptione corrumperis intolerabili. Et Chaldæus: defa- tigando defatigaberis, quod postmodum clarisu ex- plicatur, gravis præ te res, vel negotium est ultra vires tuas, solus illud non potes sustinere. Voluit Deus, ut disceret Moses sapientissimus ab homine alienigena, ostendens ita, nemini datum esse, ut solus & in omnibus semperq́; recte sapiat. Non uni dat cuncta Deus. Conf. 1. Cor. 12,8.

## 18:19
Vers. 19. AND THE LORD WILL BE WITH YOU.

The success of the counsel is denoted, i.e., and it will be well for you, the matter will succeed prosperously. Cf. Gen. 19,2.

vers. eod. BE YOU FOR THE PEOPLE IN THOSE THINGS WHICH PERTAIN TO GOD.

In Hebrew: Be you for the people before God. The LXX, however, rendered it as the Vulgate did, τὰ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν, which phrase also occurs in Heb. 3,1. It is noted, however, that this properly means that Moses ought to be the messenger and interpreter of the people to God in bringing difficult cases before Him. Whence the Chaldean: be you for the people seeking doctrine from the face of the Lord: which is also declared by what is added, that you may report what is said to Him.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET ERIT DOMINUS TECUM.

Denotatur successus consilii, q. d. & bene tibi erit, prospere res succedet. Conf. Gen. 19,2.

vers. eod. ESTO TU POPULO IN IIS, QUÆ AD DEUM PERTINENT.

In Ebr. Esto tu populo ante Deum. LXX. tamen ita reddiderunt, ut Vulgatus τὰ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν, quæ phrasis etiam occurrit Ebr. 3,1. Notatur autem id proprie, quod Moses debeat esse internuncius, & interpres populi ad Deum in causis arduis ad eum perferendis. Unde Chaldæus: esto tu populo quærens doctrinam a facie Domini: quod etiam declarant, quæ adduntur, ut referas, quæ dicuntur, ad eum.

## 18:20
Vers. 20. AND SHOW THE PEOPLE THE CEREMONIES.

There were two duties of Moses (1.) to refer the people's business to GOD, then to prescribe to the people in the name of God what needed to be done, and to show the will of God, because he was the legislator teaching the people the statutes, ceremonies, and the rite of worshipping God, indeed he was also the Interpreter of God to the people concerning all things which God required of them, whence he taught them the way by which they ought to walk, and the work which they ought to do.

Latin:

Vers. 20. OSTENDASQUE POPULO CEREMONIAS.

Duo erant Mosis officia (1.) populi negotia ad DEUM referre, deinde populo nomine Dei præscribere, quid facto opus esset, & ostendere voluntatem Dei, quia erat legislator populum docens statuta, ceremonias & ritum colendi Deum, imo erat Interpres etiam Dei ad populum de omnibus, quæ Deus ab eo requirebat, unde viam, per quam ingredi debeant, & opus quod facere debeant, ipsos docebat.

## 18:21
Vers. 21. WISE MEN.

So the Vulgate, although the Roman Codices read: powerful men, which agrees with the Hebrew, in which they are called men of virtue, just as the LXX and the Chaldean also rendered it: Concerning the virtues of a Magistrate, which are required here and in Deut. 1,13, see at length B. Gerh. de Magistr. §. 99. & 287. Grotius explains this concerning wealth in this way:

חַיִל signifies the wealthy: For such people both better maintain their dignity, and are further removed from the suspicion of dishonest gain.

But the Hebrew word, as the Targum and others observe, is also accustomed to be used to designate the strength of mind and body. Therefore some understand it as robust men who are sufficient for bearing a burden, others as wise men who have the skill of ruling a multitude. But that opinion is deservedly preferred which maintains that the strengths of the mind are regarded, which are primarily necessary for those holding the magistracy, as in Ruth 3:11. Ruth is called a woman of חַיִל, of virtue. Such are then wisdom and prudence, Deut. 1:13, then magnanimity and constancy, Deut. 1:17, Sirach 7:9. For the internal gifts of a good magistrate, not external goods, which are for the most part fragile, are here regarded and enumerated.

Verse of the same. TRIBUNES AND CENTURIONS AND CAPTAINS OF FIFTY AND DECURIONS) The Hebrews calculate the number thus: Commanders of a thousand, 600. Centurions, 6000. Prefects of fifty, 12000. Decurions, 46000. The sum is 64600. In the place of these succeeded the urban judges: the Sanhedrin, however, in the place of Moses himself. Num. 11:14, 15, 16.

Grotius entered upon a large number of them with the Hebrews: But without foundation. He says that urban judges succeeded into their place; but the Sanhedrin into the place of Moses himself. Which latter cannot be proven; Num. 11:14, 15, 16, the contrary is rather held, namely that the 70 elders were joined to Moses, and taken into a share of the government, so that he would not bear the burden alone, not substituted into his place. He who succeeded him was Joshua, divinely chosen and appointed to that office; not, however, the Sanhedrin. But perhaps Grotius intends by this substitution that one Moses was worth as much as the Sanhedrin and vice versa, so that he may teach that the authority of the Roman Pontiff is no less than that of a universal Council. Papists are accustomed to compare Moses to him, but how unskillfully, everyone sees. For Moses was not a Pontiff, but a Prince and leader of the people, a political person, not an Ecclesiastical one; to pass over other things, which are not of this place.

Moreover, some think that the distribution of the people into certain classes is only indicated here, from which judges are to be chosen. But because the text is clear, while it refers the predicate, to judge the people at all times, to all of them, which is also to be seen in the parallel passage Deut. 1: therefore with Corn. Bertram on the Jewish polity ch. 6, it is not inappropriately said that those chiliarchs and centurions were not counted by reason of heads, but by reason of families; nor the decurions by reason of persons, but that the decuries of families should be looked at, and that from them, distributed into 13 tribes, the Princes of 70 families ought to have been taken, to whom Moses and Aaron were added, and that in these seventy-two the supreme judgment consisted: Conf. Num. 11, 16. Whence although for lighter causes the chiliarchs, centurions, fifty-men, and decurions together with their prefects would first take cognizance, each in his own chiliad, century, pentecost, or fifty-men group, and decury, yet the whole matter in more serious business was to be referred subsequently to the 70 and their prefects, Moses and Aaron: which opinion seems most likely.

Latin:

Vers. 21. VIROS SAPIENTES.

Ita Vulgata, quanquam Romani Codices legant: viros potentes, quod Ebræo consonat, in quo nominantur viri virtutis, quemadmodum etiam LXX. & Chaldæus reddidere: De virtutibus Magistratus, quæ hîc & Deut. 1,13. requiruntur, prolixe vid. B. Gerh. de Magistr. §. 99. & 287. Grotius de opulentia exponit hoc modo:

חַיִל opulentos significat: Tales enim & dignitatem tuentur melius, & longius absunt ab inhonesti quæstus suspicione.

Verum vox Ebræa Targum aliisque observantibus, ad robur animi & corporis designandum etiam adhiberi solet. Ideo nonnulli viros robustos, qui oneri ferundo sufficiant, alii sapientes, qui peritiam habent regendi multitudinem, intelligunt. Merito autem præfertur ea sententia, quæ vires animi respici autumat, quæ imprimis necessariæ sunt Magistratum gerentibus, uti Ruth. 3, 11. Ruth mulier חַיִל virtutis dicitur. Quales sunt tum Sapientia, & prudentia Deut, 1, 13. tum magnanimitas, & constantia Deut. 1,17. Syrac. 7,9. Interna enim boni Magistratus dotes, non externa bona, quæ plerumque fragilia sunt, hic respiciuntur & recensentur.

Vers. eod. TRIBUNOS ET CENTURIONES ET QUINQUAGENARIOS ET DECANOS) Numerum Hebræi sic ineunt: Chiliarchæ 600. Centuriones 6000. præfecti quinquaginta 12000. Decuriones 46000. Summa 64600. Horum in locum successere Judices urbani: Synedrium autem in ipsius Mosis locum. Num. 11,14. 15. 16.

Magnum iniit eorum numerum cum Ebræis Grotius: Sed sine fundamento. In eorum locum Judices urbanos successisse, ait; Synedrium vero in ipsius Mosis locum. Quod posterius probari non potest; Num. 11, 14. 15. 16. contrarium potius habetur, nempe adjunctos fuisse LXX. Seniores Mosi, & in partem gubernationis ascitos, ne solus ipse onus ferret, non in ejus locum substitutos. Qui ei successit, Josua fuit, divinitus ad id munus electus & constitutus; Non vero Synedrium. Sed intendit fortassis hac substitutione id Grotius, quod unus Moses tantum valuerit, quantum Synedrium & vice versa, ut Pontificis Romani non minorem, quam Concilii universalis autoritatem esse doceat. So- lent Mosi hunc comparare Papicolæ, sed quam im- perite, nemo non videt. Moses enim non Ponti- fex, sed Princeps & dux populi fuit, persona politica, non Ecclesiastica; ut alia taceam, quæ hujus non sunt loci.

Cæterum censent nonnulli, distributionem populi in certas classes hîc tantum indicatam esse, ex quibus eligendi sint judices. Sed quia textus lu- culentus est, dum prædicatum, judicare populum o- mni tempore, ad illos omnes refert, quod etiam in loco parallelo Deut. 1. videre est: ideo cum Corn. Bertramo de politia judaica c. 6. non incommode di- citur, chiliarchas & centuriones illos non ratione capi- tum numerari, sed ratione familiarum; neq; decuriones ratione personarum, sed ut spectentur decuriæ familia- rum, & ex illis in tribus 13. distributis 70. familiarum Principes depromi debuisse, quibus accedebant Moses & Aaron, atq; in his septuaginta duobus constitisse su- premum judicium: Conf. Num. 11, 16. Unde quam- vis de causis levioribus primum chiliarchi, centu- riones, quinquagenarii & decuriones una cum suis præfectis cognoscerent, quivis in sua chiliade, cen- turia, pentecoste, seu quinquagenaria, & decuria, tamen res tota in gravioribus negotiis deferenda deinceps fuerit ad 70. & præfectos eorum, Mosen & Aaronem: quæ sententia maxime verisimilis vide- tur.

## 18:22
v. 22. LET THEM REFER TO THEMSELVES) Just as Roman governors used to institute a report to the Emperor concerning more serious matters.

Latin:

vers. 22. REFERANT AD SE) Sicut Romani præsides de rebus gravioribus relationem instituebant ad Imperato- rem.

## 18:23
v. 23. YOU WILL FULFILL THE COMMAND OF GOD.

According to the Hebrew you may explain it more correctly: according to the command of GOD; for Jethro seems to have added this condition, that Moses should execute this counsel, if, namely, the command of GOD, which is noted by the word צוּה, should arrive; and thus he subjected it to divine approval; which Rungius observed is also the interpretation of the Hebrews.

v. same. AND ALL THE PEOPLE WILL RETURN TO THEIR PLACES IN PEACE. Some wrongly understand these things concerning the land of Canaan, as if the form of the judgments ought to have lasted only until they arrived in the land of Canaan. Nothing else is hinted at, than that the people should not have to go far, nor wait long, but that they would have as it were a domestic judge in the vicinity, so that they could easily be dispatched at any time, just as the comparison with verse 14 teaches, all the people wait from morning until evening.

Latin:

v. 23. IMPLEBIS IMPERIUM DEI.

Juxta Ebræum rectius exponas: secundum imperium DEI; nam videtur Jethro hanc conditio- nem addidisse, ut exequeretur hoc consilium Mo- ses, si scil. mandatum DEI, quod voce צוּה nota- tur, accesserit; adeoque id subjecisse divinæ appro- bationi; quam etiam Ebræorum esse interpretatio- nem Rungius observavit.

Vers. eod. ET OMNIS POPULUS REVER- TETUR AD LOCA SUA IN PACE. Male hæc nonnulli de terra Canaan intelli- gunt, quasi forma judiciorum durare tantum ita debuerit, donec in terram Canaan pervenirent. Ni- hil aliud innuitur, quam quod ita populo non pro- cul eundum sit, nec diu expectandum, sed in pro- pinquo habituri sint veluti domesticum judicem, ut facile quovis tempore expediri possint, quemad- modum id collatio cum versu 14. docet, omnis popu- lus præstolatur de mane usq; ad vesperam.

## 18:24
v. 24. WHICH HE HAD SUGGESTED TO HIM) Here the Samaritan Codex inserts verses, which are below in Deut. 1 and 9 to 17, for the same reason as we observed above in a similar addition. That this is old in the Samaritan appears from Procopius of Gaza on the passage of Deuteronomy. But the verse which follows here is omitted in the same Codex, as not necessary, because the same sense is sufficiently understood from the preceding 21 and 23: but there is need for neither addition nor subtraction.

Latin:

vers. 24. QUÆ ILLI SUGGESSERAT) Hic Samaritanus Codex inserit versus, qui infra sunt Deut. 1. & 9. ad 17. pari de causa ei quam supra in simili additione observavimus. Vetus hoc esse in Samaritano ex Procopio Gazæo ad Devteronomii locum apparet. Qui autem sequitur hic versus, is in eodem Codice omittitur, ut non necessarius, quia ex superioribus 21. & 23. sensus idem satis intelligitur: verum neque additione, neque detractione opus.

## 19:1 Argument
PART II. DOGMATIC EXODUS CONCERNING THE PROMULGATION OF LAWS. CHAPTER XIX. The appearance of GOD on Sinai.

v. 1. IN THE THIRD MONTH OF THE DEPARTURE OF ISRAEL FROM THE LAND OF EGYPT ON THIS DAY THEY CAME INTO THE WILDERNESS OF SINAI) He occupies Mount Synan. Justin from Trogus concerning Moses. Strabo calls it Σινᾶν in book 16.

Appion says that Moses went up into the mountain between Egypt and Arabia, which is called Sinai, and was hidden for forty days. The laws of God are to be learned in the desert, that is, with a mind purged from those affections which the crowd generates and nourishes, as Philo noted.

There is a doubt concerning the time of arrival. Most Roman Catholics, in order to defend the Vulgate, explain 'on this day' as 'on the same day,' namely the third day of the third month, which interpretation Ribera approves in book 5, chapter 7, on the temple. But because that manner of speaking, 'in the third month, on this day,' that is, 'on a similar day' or 'on the third day,' cannot be proven from the Scriptures, others interpret the word חדש not as 'month,' but as the first day of the month, as νεομηνίᾳ or new moon, in this sense: on the new moon of the third month, that is, on that very day of the new moon, they came into the desert of Sinai. This opinion seems preferable, and therefore the Israelites arrived on the first day of the third month, i.e., Sivan, which sense Abulensis approves. On the second day, Moses ascended to God and received the commands of GOD for the people; on the third, he gathered the elders of the people and explained to them the commands of GOD, verses 7 and 8. On the fourth, he returned again to God to report the promise of the people, verses 9 and 10. On the sixth day of the month Sivan, the Law was promulgated. For it is agreed among all interpreters that the νομοθεσίαν (legislation) took place on the fiftieth day after the departure from Egypt. Let there now be counted from the second day of unleavened bread, or the sixteenth day of the first month, 30 days of the second and 6 more of the third month, and you will have Pentecost, or 50 days. Furthermore, since they departed from Sinai in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day, as is evident from Numbers 10:11, it is manifest that they remained in Sinai for an entire year, except for 10 days. Therefore, all those things which are described from this chapter 19 through the whole book of Exodus, and through the whole of Leviticus, and in Numbers up to chapter 10:11, happened in the desert of Sinai. And therefore Jerome says: 'In Sinai,' he says, 'was the twelfth station, where the middle part of Exodus, and the whole of Leviticus, and the precepts of Numbers, and the distribution of the people by individual tribes, and the offering of the princes were described.'

Latin:

PARS II. EXODI ΔΟΓΜΑΤΙΚΗ DE LEGUM PROMUL- GATIONE. CAPUT XIX. Apparitio DEI in Sinai.

Vers. 1. MENSE TERTIO EGRESSIONIS ISRAEL DE TERRA ÆGYPTI IN DIE HAC VENERUNT IN SO- LITUDINEM SINAI) Montem Synan occupat. Justi- nus ex Trogo de Mose. Σινᾶν vocat Strabo libro 16

Appion Mosem εἰς τὸ μεταξὺ τῆς Αἰγύπτου καὶ τῆς Ἀραβίας ὄρος, ὃ καλεῖται Σινᾷον, ἀναβάντα φησὶν ἡμέρας τεσσαράκον- τα κρυφθῆναι. Leges Dei discendae in deserto, id est, animo purgato ab iis affectibus quos turba gignit ac nutrit, ut Philo notavit.

Dubium est de tempore adventus. Pontificii plerique ut Vulgatam tueantur, in die hac, ex- ponunt, in die eadem sc. tertia mensis tertii, quem sen- sum Ribera probat lib. 5. de templo c. 7. sed quia modus ille loquendi mense tertio, in die hac, id est, in die simili, vel in die tertia e scripturis probari nequit, alii vocem חדש non de mense interpretantur, sed de prima die mensis, de νεομηνίᾳ vel novilunio, hoc sensu: in novilunio tertii scil. mensis, in illa ipsa die nempe novilunii venerunt in desertum Sinai, quæ sententia præferenda videtur, ideoque advenerunt Israelitæ die prima mensis tertii i. e. Sivan, quem sensum probat Abulensis, altero die Moses ascendit ad Deum & accepit mandata DEI ad populum, ter- tio congregavit seniores populi eisq; exposuit man- data DEI v. 7. & 8. Quarto iterum rediit ad Deum, ut referret sponsionem populi v. 9. & 10. Sexto die mensis Sivan Lex promulgata est. Nam inter o- mnes Interpretes de eo convenit, νομοθεσίαν fa- ctam esse qvinquagesimo die post exitum ex Ægypto. Numerentur jam a secundo die azymorum vel decimo sexto die mensis primi 30. dies secundi & adhuc 6.tertii mensis, & habebis pentecosten, vel 50. dies. Por- ro cum e Sina discesserint anno secundo mense secun- do die vigesimo, uti constat e Num. 10, 11. manifestum est, hæsisse eos in Sina, per annum integrum, exceptis 10. diebus; ea ergo omnia, quæ ab hoc cap. 19. per totum Exodi librum, quæque per totum Leviticum & in Numeris usque ad cap. 10, 11. descripta sunt, in deserto Sina acciderunt. Ideoque Hieronymus: in sta Sina, inquit, fuit duodecima mansio, ubi media pars Exodi, & totus Leviticus, & Numerorum præcepta, & populi per singulas tribus distributio, & oblatio princi- pum descripta sunt.

## 19:3
Verse 3. BUT MOSES ASCENDED TO GOD.

Others translate: 'he had ascended,' and 'he had called.' But there is no necessity for this; we retain the order of the history. He ascended, however, to Mount Sinai, on which God was once seen by him (Exodus 3). And he ascended not αὐτομάτως (spontaneously), as if he were going to consult God about a sacrifice, since God indicated in Exodus 3 that sacrifices would be offered to Him on this mountain, as Cornelius thinks; but he was commanded by God, or moved by a peculiar divine instinct. For it would not have been his presumption or rashness to ascend to God without either the instinct or the command of God, concerning whose presence on Mount Sinai and peculiar manifestation he could not have been certain without His revelation.

Latin:

Vers. 3. MOSES AUTEM ASCENDIT AD DEUM.

Alii reddunt: ascenderat, & vocaverat. Sed nulla ejus est necessitas, retinemus ordinem histo- riæ. Ascendit autem in montem Sinai, in quo Deus olim ipsi conspectus est Exod. 3. Et ascendit non αὐτομάτως, quasi consulturus Deum de sacrificio, quum indicarit Deus Exod. 3. in hoc monte sibi sacri- ficia oblatum iri, uti Cornelius putat; sed jussus a Deo, vel peculiari motus instinctu divino. Non enim ejus fuisset præsumtionis aut temeritatis, sine Dei vel instinctu vel jussu ad Deum ascendere, de cujus præsentia in monte Sinai, & manifestatione peculiari sine ejusdem revelatione ipsi constare non poterat.

## 19:4
Verse 4. EGYPT IS) So both the Greeks and the Samaritan. Wherefore the reading received in the Hebrew is better than that which is in other books, במצרים.

It is not better because the Greeks, the Vulgate, and the Samaritan agree, but because it was found in better Hebrew [manuscripts], and for that reason was accepted. For the norm is not to be adjusted to the thing regulated, but the thing regulated to the norm.

Verse same. UPON THE WINGS OF EAGLES.

GOD delights in this simile in describing the gracious leading of the people; compare Deuteronomy 32:11, which they explain thus: just as eagles do not carry their young with their claws and feet, but place them upon their wings and carry them so high that no one can attack them even with a weapon; so GOD lifted up the Israelites with the wings of providence and grace, and rendered them secure from every weapon and danger. Jerome to the chapter.

LXVI. Es. does not have it: Those who have written about the natures of living creatures say that in all beasts, and cattle, and flocks, and birds, there is an innate affection for their offspring and young: but that the love of eagles is the greatest, which place their nests in high and inaccessible places, so that a snake may not harm their young: and that an amethyst stone is also found among their young, by which all poisons are overcome. If this is true, the affection of GOD for His creatures is rightly compared to eagles, who protects His children with every guard, so that the Dragon, and the ancient serpent the devil, and Satan may not creep up on the new-born young, so that at the name of the stone, which is placed in the foundations of Zion, all the snares of the adversaries may be broken. This is Jerome. Grotius has this to say about this phrase:

HOW I HAVE CARRIED) By a cloud, of course, which covered the Israelites no less than an eagle covers its brood with its wings. Not very conveniently. For He did not carry them by a cloud, even if He led them in a cloud. That comparison is far more emphatic, as we have said, and as is clear from Deut. 32:11. It is certainly sure and undoubted that the simile refers to the love and care and defense of the people, since, as Aelian testifies in Book II of On the Nature of Animals, ch. 40, the eagle is the most zealous of all animals for its young, and fiercely pursues anyone it sees invading its nest, and does not let them go unpunished or unavenged, but rather tears them with its wings and talons. Since God in that way tore apart the Egyptians who were flying at the Israelite Church, which was nesting there. Furthermore, just as eagles, contrary to the custom of other birds, as the Hebrews observe, carry their young and support them on their shoulders, and gradually excite them to fly: so God supported and carried the Israelites and cherished them with the expansion of His wings. See Ps. 17:7, Ps. 36:5, Ps. 57:2, Ps. 61:5, Ps. 63:8, Ps. 91:1. There is a similar comparison of Christ in Matt. 23:37.

Latin:

vers. 4. ÆGYPTI IS) Sic & Græci & Samaritanus. Quare lectio recepta in Hebræo melior, quam quæ est in aliis libris במצרים.

Non ideo melior, quia Græci, Vulgatus, & Samaritanus consonant, sed quia in melioribus E- bræis reperta, atque idcirco recepta fuit. Non enim norma ad normatum exigenda, sed normatum ad normam.

vers. eod. SUPER ALAS AQUILARUM.

Delectatur hac similitudine DEUS in descri- benda gratiosa deductione populi, conf. Devt. 32, 11. quam ita explicant: sicut aquilæ pullos suos non unguibus & pedibus transferunt, sed eos super alas imponunt, & adeo alte vectant, ut nullus eas vel telo petere possit; ita DEUS alis providentiæ & gratiæ sustulit Israelitas, eosque ab omni telo & periculo securos præstitit. Hieronym. ad cap.

LXVI. Es. non habet : Qui de animantium scripsere naturis, omnium quidem bestiarum & jumentorum & pecudum aviumque ingenitum esse ajunt in filios pullos- que suos affectum : sed maximum esse amorem aquila- rum, quæ in excelsis, & inaccessis locis nidos collocant, ne coluber fœtus violet : Amethysten quoque inter pul- los ejus lapidem reperiri, quo omnia venena superentur. Si hoc verum est, recte affectus DEI in suas creaturas aquilis comparatus est, qui omni custodia protegit libe- ros suos, ne Draco, & coluber antiquus diabolus, & Sa- tanas obrepat novellis fœtibus, ut ad nomen lapidis, qui ponitur in fundamentis Zion, omnes adversariorum frangantur insidiæ. Hæc Hieronymus. Grotius de hac Phrasi ita habet :

QUOMODO PORTAVERIM) Nube scilicet, quæ non minus obtegebat Israëlitas, quam aquila alis suam pulli- tiem. Parum commode. Nube enim non portavit, etsi in nube deduxerit. Longe ἐμφατικώτερον, ut diximus, & e Deut. 32, 11. liquet, est illa comparatio. Certum utique & indubium est, referri similitudi- nem ad amorem & curam & defensionem populi, quum Æliano lib. II. Hist. animal. cap. 40. teste, aquila ex omnibus animalibus maximo studio in fœtus suos exi- stat, acriter persequatur, quem in nidum suum inva- sisse conspexerit, nec inultum impunitumq; dimit- tat, imo alis & unguibus laceret. Quandoquidem ita Deus Ægyptios, Ecclesiam Israëlitiçam ibi velut nidulantem, involantes, dilacerarit. Porro uti a- quilæ præter aliarum avium morem, quod Ebræi observant, pullos portant, humerisq́; suis sustinent, eos- que ad volandum sensim excitant : Ita sustinuit Deus & gestavit Israëlitas ac alarum suarum expansione fovit. Vid. Ps. 17, 7. Ps. 36, 5. Ps. 57, 2. Ps. 61, 5. Ps. 63, 8. Ps. 91, 1. Similis comparatio est Christi Matth. 23, 37.

## 19:5
verse 5. AS A PECULIAR TREASURE.

In Hebrew: סְגֻלָּה which denotes a chosen part or portion, a dear and precious thing, just as gems and other precious things are accustomed to be kept in treasuries. Hence the people are called the Lord's portion, Deut. 32:9. Theodotion translates: περιποίησιν, an acquisition. Symmachus: ἐξαίρετον, excellent or preeminent. The Chaldean: you shall be beloved before me. The Vulgate: peculium, i.e., you shall be my whole flock, because all the substance of the ancients was in their flock. St. Peter, with the LXX Interpreters, renders it: περιούσιον, select, excellent, and as it were set apart, 1 Ep. 2:9.

Latin:

vers. 5. IN PECULIUM.

In Ebræo : סְגֻלָּה quod partem sive portio- nem electam, rem caram, & pretiosam notat, ceu gem- mæ & aliæ res pretiosæ sunt in thesauris asservari so- litæ. Dicitur hinc populus pars Domini, Deut. 32, 9. Theodotio vertit : περιποίησιν acquisitionem. Sym- machus, ἐξαίρετον egregium vel præcipuum. Chal- dæus : dilecti eritis coram me. Vulg. peculium q. d. eritis totum pecus meum, quia omnis substantia vete- rum erat in pecore. S. Petrus cum LXX. Interpre- tibus reddit : περιούσιον selectum, eximium & quasi segregatum 1. Ep. 2, 9.

## 19:6
verse 6. AS A KINGDOM OF PRIESTS.

That is, a kingdom not profane but sacred, devoted to my worship and sacrifices. Peter inverts this in the place cited, calling it a royal priesthood, which the Papists twist to serve the Majesty and preeminence of their Pope. But in a marvelous way; for they say that royal dignity was perfect among the Jews, but rendered more imperfect among Christians, whereas the priesthood, which is most excellent among Christians and dominant over Kings, was imperfect among the Jews. It was a task of such great magnitude to establish the Roman Pope. But the Apostle subjects every soul to the higher powers, Rom. 13:1. And therefore he neither exempts the Pontiff from this subjection, nor does it appear in what way royal dignity is inferior today than it was formerly, except that the Pontiffs dare to depress all Kings below the lowest of the priestly order among them. Others, with Ascanio Martinengo, say that a royal priesthood is attributed to the N.T. because it is the time of grace, but a kingdom of priests to the Old, because it was the time of justice. But that hunting for words is superfluous and superstitious, since Peter used the words of the Apostle from the edition of the LXX Interpreters. St. John, however, in Apoc. 1:6, c. 5:10, when he says that we have been made Kings and Priests, placed royal dignity before priestly; whence Esthius himself, in 1 Pet. 2, says that this argument vanishes, which some think must be established in the distinction between the Priesthood of the Old and New, refuting not only Martinengo, but Hugo the Cardinal, Thomas the Englishman, and others.

Grotius has this to say on these words:

AS A KINGDOM OF PRIESTS) The Greeks, with an inverted construction, βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα: as in 1 Pet. 2:9. In Hebrew: a kingdom of priests. The Chaldean interprets it as kings and priests, as in Apoc. 5:10, which he expressed elsewhere, 1:6, as βασιλέαν καὶ ἱερεῖς. All Israelites were kings to some extent before kings were established. And priests at the Passover. Philo, in the third book on Moses: ἐν τῷ πάσχα σύμπαν τὸ ἔθνος ἱερᾶται. Christians are kings, because they have conquered the flesh, sin, the world, the devil; they are priests by prayers, alms, and martyrdom in deed or in purpose.

R. But who were all the Israelites as kings, when they had their own head and leader? Who were priests at the Passover? When the Passover, by Grotius's own admission, was only a Eucharistic banquet, and should not be considered a sacrifice? Christians, he says, are kings, because they have conquered the flesh, sin, the world, the Devil: they are priests by prayers, alms, and martyrdom in deed or in purpose. He omits the principal things, such as faith, through which they present the sacrifice of Christ to God, and obedience, in respect of which they offer themselves to God as living sacrifices, Rom. 12:1. But why does he not attribute these to the Israelites as well? The cause is at hand, because he thinks only carnal things of them, and regarding spiritual things he assigns that huge difference between Israelites and Christians, having followed the lead of Socinus as well as Pelagius. Of which elsewhere. Peter certainly, for the same reason, and from this very place, does not make it βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα 1. Epist. 2, 9. in which the Jews are said to be chosen for this: nor did Christ make only Christians by his merit βασιλεῖς καὶ ἱερεῖς Apoc. 1, 6. indeed, just as he loved all, and washed all from sin with his blood, into whomever sin had spread thence from the fall of the Protoplasts: So also all, as far as the virtue and efficacy of the merit and also as far as the purpose and intention of the one meriting, have been made a kingdom and priests of God. Therefore in heaven by the four living creatures and the 24 Elders in the name of all the Elect, whether they be Jews or Christians, whether they lived under the O.T. or under the New, Christ is celebrated because he made them kings and Priests to God. Apoc. 5, 10.

Latin:

vers. 6. IN REGNUM SACERDOTALE.

Hoc est, regnum non profanum sed sacrum, cul- tui meo & sacrificiis addictum. Invertit hoc Pe- trus l. c. vocans sacerdotium regale, quod eo detor- quent Papistæ, ut inserviat Majestati & præminen- tiæ sui Papæ. Sed modo mirabili ; quia regalis digni- tas, inquiunt, apud Judæos perfecta fuit, apud Chri- stianos imperfectior reddita est, sacerdotium vero quod apud Christianos præstantissimum & prædomi- nans Regibus, imperfectum erat apud Judæos.
