How Josephus flattered the Romans in the explanation of this law, we have warned the Readers in Book III. de Jure belli ac pacis cap. 6. §. 2.

The law does not deal with mere naming: for they are named even in the law itself: But it commands that we do not call them Gods and, as it were, invoke them as witnesses, by swearing by them, as Tertull. has in l. de idol. c. 19. The Grotian gloss Judaizes.

WHEN YOU HAVE GATHERED ALL THE FRUITS) To the Hebrews it is חג האסף, that is, literally ἑορτὴ τῆς συγκομι- δῆς, which the Greeks called θαλυσία. See Theocritus in the Idyll of the θαλυσίων, and the learned men there. This is called differently among the Hebrews σκηνοπηγία. See Levit. 23, 33. Num. 29, 12. Deut. 16, 13. and following, and what is noted there.

Of the Solemnity of the ingathering (which name the Vulgate rashly omitted), it is called the third, that is, the principal feast, because it was to be celebrated AT THE GOING OUT OF THE YEAR: whence not a few Chronologists conclude that the beginning and the going out of the year was in the month Tisri, and that in the same month the world was founded and had its beginning: But that can by no means be concluded from that word: which only respects the end of the labors of the harvest, because the feast of tabernacles was ordained for the gathering of all the fruits which had grown throughout the whole year: as the marginal gloss of B. Luther has it: Des Jahres Ausgang heisset er den Weinmond, daß alsdann aus ist mit Frucht wachsen und sammlen: And Osiander: in the going out of the year; at which time of the year, that is, the labors of gathering and of again bearing fruits are finished. That feast fell in Judea in our September: otherwise the end and beginning of the year for the Jews was in March. I desire therefore, (says the Lord), that when the labors of sowing and reaping have ceased, you celebrate the feast of the ingathering. Whence it is manifest how weak the argument is, by which Petavius says he is chiefly moved to establish the head of the year before Moses in the autumn. At the Passover, the ears of ripening barley, at Pentecost, the first fruits of all the produce of the whole wheat harvest were to be offered: Lev. 23, 17. But when the collection of fruits was made in Judea, the feast of tabernacles was to be celebrated, so that they might give thanks to God for them.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

NOMEN EXTERNORVM DEORVM NON JVRABITIS, NEQVE AVDIETVR EX ORE VESTRO] Ne nomen quidem falsorum Deorum pronunciare ipsis permissum, quo longius à veneratione abessent. Itaque pro בעל שמין dicebant בעל זבוב pro בית אל dicebant בית און, & ita in cæteris. Quomodo in hujus legis explicatione Romanis blanditus sit Josephus, monuimus Lectores in Libro III. de Jure belli ac pacis cap. 6. §. 2.

Non de nuda nominatione lex agit: nam & in ipsa lege nominantur: Sed jubet, ne Deos eos vocemus & q. Deos in testes invocemus, jurando per eos, ut Tertull. habet l. de idol. c. 19. Judaizat glossa Grotiana.

QVANDO CONGREgAVERIS OMNES FRVGES) Hebraeis id חג האסף ,id est, ad verbum ἑορτὴ τῆς συγκομι- δῆς quam θαλυσία vocabant Graeci. Vide Theocritum in Idyl- lio θαλυσίων, & ibi eruditos. Hoc apud Hebraeos aliter voca- tur σκηνοπηγία. Vide Levit. 23, 33. Num. 29, 12. Deut. 16, 13. & sequentibus, & quae ibi notata.

De Solemnitate collectionis (quod nomen te- mere omisit vulgata) tertio sc. festo praecipuo dici- tur, quod IN EXITU ANNI celebranda sit: unde colligunt Chronologi non pauci, quod men- se Tisri anni initium & exitus fuerit, & quod eo- dem mense mundus conditus sit, & initium cepe- rit: Sed id concludi ex ea voce minime potest: quae solum respicit finem laborum messis, quia festum tabernaculorum ordinatum erat pro collectione omnium fructuum, qui per totum annum creve- rant: ut B. Lutheri glossa marginalis habet: Des Jahres Ausgang heisset er den Weinmond, daß als- dann aus ist mit Frucht wachsen und sammlen: Et Osiander: in exitu anni; quo sc. anni tempore labo- res colligendi, & iterum ferendis frugibus finiuntur. Id festum incidebat in Judaea in Septembrem no- strum: alias finis & initium anni erat Judaeis in Martio. Volo igitur, (inquit Dominus) ut cessanti- bus laboribus serendi & metendi, celebres festum col- lectionis. Unde quam infirmum sit argumentum, quo praecipue se moveri ait Petavius, ut anni caput ante Mosen in autumno statuat, manifestum est. In Paschate spicae hordei maturescentis, in Pente- coste primitiae frugum omnium totius messis triti- ceae offerendae erant: Lev. 23, 17. Collectio autem fru- gum ubi facta in Judaea, celebrandum erat taberna- culorum festum, ut de iis gratias agerent Deo.

## 23:17
Vers. 17.

THREE TIMES IN THE YEAR SHALL EVERY MALE APPEAR.

See Exod. 34, 23. 24. Deuter. 16, 16. Dionysius in Deut. 16, 16 thinks that only those who lived far away were obliged to go up to Jerusalem for the feast of the Passover; some say that it was granted that they should appear at the feast of the Passover only once in three years. But the law of the Lord is clear: and all who lived in Palestine could easily arrive there three times every year. Proselytes living outside Palestine were not bound by that law. The feast of the Passover exhibited a type of the true Paschal lamb to be sacrificed for us, and of the liberation through his blood from the hand of the destroying angel, or the power of Satan: the feast of Pentecost, of our spiritual offering, who have received the first fruits of the Spirit: because the loaves of the first fruits were then offered; the feast of tabernacles, of our dwelling in a terrestrial tabernacle in this life. To which feasts correspond three solemnities of the Christians. At the feast of the Passover, the Pascha, by which we celebrate the resurrection of the sacrificed lamb and the triumph of Christ over Satan and hell; at the feast of Pentecost, our Pentecost, by which we recall the mission of the Holy Spirit, who sanctifies us into a holy offering; and at the feast of tabernacles, the Solemnity of the incarnation of the Son of GOD, who came from heaven into the tabernacle of our flesh, so that we might aspire from this earthly tabernacle to the heavenly inheritance, John 1, 14. Most people say that the feast of Pentecost was a type of the mission of the Holy Spirit made to the Apostles on the feast of Pentecost for the reason that in the ancient Pentecost the memory of the law promulgated on the fiftieth day after the exodus was recalled, and similarly the doctrine of the Gospel was to be promulgated on the fiftieth day from the resurrection of Christ when the Holy Spirit was sent upon the Apostles. But nowhere in the sacred scriptures is this end assigned to the feast of the ancient Pentecost, the memory of the promulgated law: and at least 130 days had elapsed since the departure, when Moses first reported to the Israelites concerning Pentecost: which was done only 80 days after the promulgation of the Decalogue. Cf. B. Affelmann, dissertation on the person of the Holy Spirit, held in the year 1620 at Rostock in the προαυλίῳ. Furthermore, from this law the Papists rashly infer that the current celebration of festivals is a part of divine worship, as in the Old Testament. Bellarmine, book 3, on the worship of Saints, chapter 10. For the reason was far different in the Old Testament, where God himself determined the festivals, than in the New, where we are bound to no festivals by any law, Col. 2:15, but the Church institutes festivals out of Christian liberty. See Jerome on Galatians 4; Socrates, book 5 of Church History, chapter 21.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

TER IN ANNO APPAREBIT OMNE MASCULINUM.

Vid. Exod. 34, 23. 24. Deuter. 16, 16. Dionys. in Deut. 16, 16. putat, multum remotos solum obli- gatos festo Paschatos Hierosolymam ascendere; non- nulli ajunt, quod indultum fuerit, ut solum in trien- nio semel festo Paschatos comparerent. At lex Domini luculenta est: poterantque facile omnes ter singulis annis eo pervenire, qui in Palaestina ha- bitabant. Proselyti extra Palaestinam habitantes ista lege non obstringebantur. Festum Pascha- tos typum exhibebat veri agni Paschalis pro nobis immolandi, & liberationis per sanguinem ejus è manu angeli percussoris, vel potestate satanae: fe- stum Pentecostes oblationis nostrae spiritualis, qui primitias Spiritus accepimus: quia panes primitia- rum tum offerebantur; festum tabernaculorum ha- bitationis nostrae in terreno tabernaculo in hac vi- ta. Quibus festis respondent tres Christianorum so- lemnitates. Paschatos festo Pascha, quo resuscitatio- nem agni immolati & triumphum Christi de sata- na, & inferno celebramus; Pentecostes festo nostra Pentecoste, qua S. S. missionem recolimus, nos sanctificantis in sacram oblationem; & taber- naculorum festo Solemnitas incarnationis Filii DEI, qui de coelo in nostrae carnis tabernaculum venit, ut nos ex hoc terrestri tabernaculo ad coele- stem haereditatem adspirare possemus Johan. I, 14. Plerique Pentecostes festum typum missionis S. S. in festo Pentecostes Apostolis factae ea ratione fuis- se ajunt, quod in antiqua Pentecoste recolere tur memoria legis quinquagesimo post eductionem die promulgatae, ac similiter quinquagesimo à resurre- ctione Christi die misso super Apostolos S. S. do- ctrina Evangelii promulganda fuerit. Sed nuspiam hic finis festo Pentecostes veteris assignatus est in sacris literis, memoria legis promulgatae: & ad minimum 130. dies elapsi erant ab egressu, cum de Pentecoste primum Moses ad Israëlitas retulit: quod post 80. à promulgato Decalogo dies demum factum. Conf. B. Affelmann. disp. de persona S. S. Ann. 1620. Rostoch. habita in προαυλίῳ. Cæterum ex hac lege temere Pontificii colligunt hodiernum festorum celebrationem esse partem cultûs divini, ut in V. Test. Bellarmin. l. 3. de cult. Sanctor. c. 10. Longe enim alia ratio fuit V. T. ubi Deus ipse festa determinavit, quam in Novo, ubi nulla lege ad festa adstringimur, Col. 2, 15. sed ex libertate Christiana Ecclesia festa instituit. Vid. Hieronym. ad Gal. 4. Socrat. l. 5. Histor. Eccles. c. 21.

## 23:18
Verse 18.

YOU SHALL NOT SACRIFICE THE BLOOD OF MY VICTIM UPON LEAVEN.

In the Hebrew: My. Blessed Luther in the marginal gloss, and Osiander, Rivet, and others explain this concerning the Paschal lamb from a comparison with chapter 34: you shall not slaughter the Paschal lamb unless all leaven has first been cast out of your house. Just as the law subjoined is also to be understood.

NOR SHALL THE FAT OF MY SOLEMNITY REMAIN UNTIL MORNING.

That is, nothing of the Paschal lamb, not even the fat, shall be kept until the next day. Osiander gives this mystical significance: he who has not been a partaker of Christ through faith in this world, will not enjoy Christ in the other, that is, on the last day.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

NON IMMOLABIS SUPER FERMENTO SANGUINEM VICTIMÆ TUÆ.

In Ebr. Meæ. Hoc recte B. Luther. Gloss. margin. & Osiander, Rivet, & alii de agno Paschali è collatione c. 34. explicant: non mactabis agnum Paschalem, nisi prius è domo tua ejecto omni fermento. Sicut etiam lex subjuncta intelligenda.

NEC REMANEBIT ADEPS SOLEMNITATIS MEÆ USQUE MANE.

Id est, nihil de agno Paschali, ne adeps quidem seservabitur usq; in alterum diem. Significationem mysticam hanc reddit Osiander: qui in hoc mundo Christi per fidem particeps non fuerit, altero, h. e. novissimo die non fruetur Christo.

## 23:19
Verse 19.

YOU SHALL BRING THE FIRST FRUITS OF THE EARTH INTO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD]

Diodorus teaches us that the Egyptians did the same; Pliny [teaches us] concerning the ancients: They would not even taste new fruits or wines before the priests had offered the first fruits, book 18, 20. Josephus says that this was observed by the Jews with such great religious devotion that even in that famine which occurred while Claudius was ruling at Rome, these fruits and others dedicated to God arrived at the Temple untouched by anyone.

YOU SHALL NOT COOK A KID IN THE MILK OF ITS MOTHER]

This, like many other things, was forbidden because it was accustomed to be done by neighbors in honor of idols.

This custom of neighboring nations cannot be shown by any document. Regarding the Paschal lamb, as with the preceding, some accept this not inappropriately: because the lamb had to be weaned, and separated from the rest of the flock for several days, therefore it was not to be cooked as long as it was still sucking its mother's milk. This allegory being added: that Christ as a suckling could not be killed by Herod or others before a mature age, and the time predetermined by the Father. August. q. 90. in Exod. Chrysost. hom. de Innocent. Rivetus observes from Levit. 23, 17. that to be under the mother's udder is the same as to be even in the mother's milk, and thus to cook a kid with its mother's milk is to cook it too soon after birth; and thus God wished to provide for the cleanliness and health of the Priests, that they should not eat meat still fresh from the mother's womb, and to warn that we should learn to show humanity to our neighbor even in animals, so that we are not cruel or inhuman, he concludes, following Fagius. But because this regulation is joined to festive and Paschal laws, the former explanation is deservedly preferred. And if it is explained altogether generally, as was done also by Vatablus and Oleaster, that you shall not kill and cook a suckling kid as long as it flees its mother's milk; it must be understood regarding cooking for eating: for the kid could be sacrificed and offered on the eighth day, Levit. 22, 27. The superstition of the Jews, about which Fagius writes, who do not want to cook meat and milk in the same pot, not even successively, relies on a false interpretation of the passage.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

PRIMITIAS FRVGVM TERRÆ DEFERES IN DOMVM DOMINI]

Idem fecisse Ægyptios docet nos Diodorus: Plinius de antiquis: Ne degustabant quidem novas fruges aut vina, antequam Sacerdotes primitias libassent, libr. 18, 20. Tanta autem religione hoc servatum ab Judæis, ait Josephus, ut etiam in fame illa, quæ fuit Claudio Romæ imperante, hæ fruges aliæque Deo dicatæ intactæ ab omnibus in Templum pervenerint.

NON COQVES HOEDUM IN LACTE MATRIS SUÆ]

Hoc, ut multa alia, vetitum ideo, quia ad idolorum honorem id fieri à vicinis solebat.

Hæc vicinarum gentium consuetudo nullo documento ostendi potest. De agno Paschali, ut præcedentia, hoc accipiunt nonnulli non incommode: quia agnus debuit esse ablactatus, & per aliquot dies à grege reliquo separatus, ideo non coquendus, quam diu adhuc lac matris sugeret. Addita hac allegoria: Christum lactentem non potuisse ab Herode aliisve occidi ante maturam ætatem, & tempus à patre præfinitum. August. q. 90. in Exod. Chrysost. hom. de Innocent. Rivetus observat è Levit. 23, 17. esse sub ubere matris, idem esse, quod cum vel in lacte matris esse, adeoque coquere hædum cum lacte matris esse, recentem nimis à partu coquere; atque ita Deum voluisse consulere munditiei & sanitati Sacerdotum, ne vescerentur carnibus à ventre matris adhuc recentibus, & monere, ut in animantibus etiam discamus humanitatem proximo exhibere, ne crudeles, vel inhumani simus, præeunte Fagio, statuit. Sed quia hæc constitutio legibus festivis, & Paschalibus adjungitur, prior explicatio merito præfertur. Et si omnino generaliter explicetur, uti à Vatablo etiam & Oleastr. factum, ne occidas & coquas hædum lactentem, quamdiu fugit lac matris; intelligendum erit id de coctione ad esum: Ad sacrificia enim immolari, & offerri poterat hædus octavo die Levit. 22, 27. Judæorum superstitio, de qua Fagius, qui in eadem olla carnes & lac coquere nolunt, ne successive quidem, loci ψευδερμηνείᾳ nititur.

## 23:20
Vers. 20. I WILL SEND MY ANGEL

My is not here in the Hebrew, but below in 23. Rightly, however, it was transferred from there to here, and it signifies in my name and power, as will now follow. This, as Nehemanides teaches, God took away from the Israelites after the worship of the calf and gave them a lesser Angel with merely Angelic power. See below 33, 3. and 4.

Latin:

Vers. 20. MITTAM ANGELUM MEUM]

Meum hic non est in Hebr. sed infra 23. Recte tamen inde huc translatum, & significat in meo nomine ac potestate, ut jam sequetur. Hunc ut docet Nehemanides, Deus post cultum vituli ab Israëlitis abstulit, & minorem Angelum illis dedit cum potestate mere Angelica. Vide infra 33, 3. & 4.

## 23:21
DO NOT THINK HE IS TO BE DESPISED] In Greek μὴ ἀπειθῇς αὐτῷ. Properly, do not provoke him.

FOR HE WILL NOT FORGIVE WHEN YOU HAVE SINNED] Namely contumaciously, which things God does not pardon, Jos. 24, 19.

AND MY NAME IS IN HIM] In the Hebrew: because my name is in him. So also the Greeks. The sense is: for he will have in himself the power of vengeance not to be sought far away: for name often signifies authority.

Latin:

NE CONTEMNENDUM PUTES] In Græco μὴ ἀπειθῇς αὐτῷ. Proprie ne irrita eum.

QVIA NON DIMITTET CUM PECCAVERIS] Nem- pe contumaciter, qualia nec Deus condonat, Jos. 24, 19.

ET EST NOMEN MEUM IN ILLO] In Hebræo: quia nomen meum in illo. Sic & Græci. Sensus est: habebit enim in se non longe petendam vindictæ potestatem: nam no- men sæpe ἐξουσίαν significat.

## 23:22
Vers. 22.

BUT IF HEARING HIS VOICE] Schemo Rabba here rightly: If you receive from him, you will receive from me. See a similar passage, John 5, 23.

Grotius defends the Vulgate version here first, because it added the pronoun my, which is not in the Hebrew: Transferred from v. 23. But it is the duty of an interpreter to add nothing, not even from elsewhere. Not without reason. He is called Angel simply, so that that one whom Moses peculiarly commemorated in this history might be indicated. But that, because it is trivial, we easily pass over. But as for what he further wishes that MY to signify, in my name and power, and understands a created Angel, armed with divine power, a Jewish fable approved, that God after the worship of the calf took that Angel away from the Israelites, and gave them a lesser Angel, with merely Angelic power, that contradicts entirely the magnificent description of the Angel, whose presence and guidance the Lord here promises. The discourse is about an Angel so called in the singular, not one of many, namely about the Son of God, the uncreated Angel. To whom is commanded to be shown the religious veneration due to God alone: Observe his face, and hear his voice, lest you be rebellious against him. Such honor is nowhere read to have been bestowed upon any created angel. Where are we commanded to observe the face, or to beware of the face of a created Angel, and to obey his voice, and not to sin against him by rebelling? Furthermore, this Angel has the power of forgiving sins, or not forgiving: which likewise befits no created Angel. To the ministers of the word as stewards of the mysteries that power is attributed ministerially, Matt. 18, 18. John 20, 23. But it is nowhere read to be attributed to Angels. But this judicial power of punishing the disobedient is an axiom proper to the Son of God, to whom GOD the Father has given all Judgment, John 5, 23. Furthermore, the name of the Lord is said to be in this Angel: which Grotius explains too jejunely, he will have in himself a power of vengeance not to be sought from afar: The Name of the Lord imports the very essence of the Lord, and his glory, Is. 42, 8. It is noted, therefore, that in this Angel is the essence of God, or that he himself is true God by nature and essence. Let not only the Manichaean, says Augustine in book 17 against Faustus, ch. 19, but also the Jew, examine this passage, whether he said of any Angel, GOD, My name is in him, except of this leader of the people. For Jesus is the Ruler and leader of the people into the inheritance of eternal life, of whom Joshua was a type in name and in fact. Which is more abundantly confirmed from a comparison of passages. For without doubt this same Angel is the leader of the people, who promised in Exod. 3, 17 that he would lead the Israelites into the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, which his own testimony clearly confirms to be Jehovah the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob. The same who led the people in the pillar of cloud and fire, Exod. 14, whom we showed in that place to have been not a created, but an uncreated angel. The same who called himself the prince of the host of Jehovah, Josh. 5, 14, and is there called Jehovah, ch. 6, 2. The same who is celebrated as the Angel of the presence, who saved the people, Is. 63, 9, whom it is evident from that Eucharistic song is the Son of God, the only redeemer. Who led the Israelites, and was tempted by them 1 Cor. 10, 9, whose voice all ought to hear, Deut. 18, 20, Matt. 17, 5, whose voice GOD calls his own: since these things [are said] of one and the same be held; If you shall hear the voice of him (the Angel) & if you shall do all things which I speak. And it is indeed clear that that Angel did not always speak through himself immediately, but often through Moses, who truly testified that he did not have from a created angel, but from the ONE GOD, the things which he proposed to the people. Whence it is necessary that that Angel was Jehovah himself. Wherefore Justin Martyr in his Dialogue with Trypho, Tertullian in his book against the Jews, Athanasius on the common essence of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, Hesychius in book VII on Leviticus chapter 16, and Augustine in the same book, explain this of the Son of GOD, from whom the Antiochene Fathers against Samosatenus in their Synodical Epistle are not alien. Among the Papists, although some, with Corn. à Lap., maintain that Michael is a created angel, the President of the Jewish Synagogue, Masius, however, a man most learned in Hebrew, openly contradicts them: I think, he says, that that Angel is not Michael, but the true eternal Son of GOD and the perpetual Prince and leader of the people of GOD. Nor are there wanting those among the Rabbis who have confessed this. R. Moses Gerundensis himself, the son of Nachman, makes this Angel in the bush the Redeemer Jehovah. This Angel (in the bush), he says, if we speak of the thing itself, is the Angel Redeemer, of whom it is written, because my name is in him: That, I say, Angel, who was saying to Jacob, I am the GOD of Bethel. We cited the place above at chapter III. The same R. Moses Gerund. on Exodus XXIII does not admit the opinion of the Rabbis that Michael is understood. But in truth, he says, that Angel who is promised to them here is the Angel Redeemer, in whom is that great name of GOD, because in the name יהוה יה is the rock of ages, Is. XXVI, 4. & he is the same one who says, I am the God of Bethel, Gen. 31, 13. (that is, the house of God). For it is the custom of a King that he should dwell in his house. But the Scripture calls him an Angel, for the reason that the whole government of the world is done through him in that way. Our Rabbis say it is מטטרון Metatron, or Metator, which name signifies ὁδηγὸν, a leader of the way. Furthermore, neither does R. Bechai deny it. For he calls this Angel the LORD, and the ruler of all, the LORD of the whole house of God, and of all the faculties of God, the guardian and preserver of the world and of Israel; he says that all things are subject to him; which things certainly do not befit Michael, a created Angel, but the Son of God. How Abarbenel also entangled himself here, so that he left behind manifest traces of the truth, Buxtorff has shown in his History of the Ark of the Covenant, chapter 14, page 135. We shall look into the passage of Exodus 33 and the opinion of Nachmanides brought forward here when we are led to it. That it is more correct to be wise here with some Papists and Jews than with Grotius, who so perverts these things for the sake of the Papists, Samosatenians, and Jews, is in the open. Since he admits that the Angel, instructed with divine authority, had in himself a power of vengeance not to be sought from afar, which includes also the power of forgiving sins, or separates such a divine power, which is truly infinite, from the divine essence, it is necessary that he either acknowledge that that Angel Leader is a participant in the divine essence. Whom, finally, he wishes to be called Jehovah in chapter 24, 1. But he who is called Jehovah there, and was seen, was no other than the supreme God himself. That Angel, therefore, in whom is the name of GOD Jehovah, is that supreme GOD to whom Moses was ordered to ascend, and whose glory he saw there. To which place we shall now proceed.

This is repeated in Exod. 34, 11. But in Deut. 7, 1, the Girgashite is added: in Gen. 15, 8, the Kenites also and the Kenizzites, and furthermore the Kadmonites, and the Rephaim (passing over the Hivites) are enumerated? Resp. The Girgashites are omitted and included under others because they were fewer, nay, they had been subjugated by the Amorites, who are also sometimes taken synecdochically for all the inhabitants of the land: because the Amorites were more distinguished and famous than the rest, and when they had occupied those two kingdoms beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, having increased with a numerous offspring, they seem to have sent colonies afterwards into various parts of the promised land, Deut. 1. Thus also, by the name of the Canaanites, sometimes all those peoples are generally designated, as being those who were of the descendants of Canaan, Gen. 10, 15, and sometimes those who among others specially obtained this name. And although in the first occupation the Israelites obtained only those seven nations, under David and Solomon, however, they had the rest also subjected. Add Augustine, q. 21 on Joshua. Finally, even if God promised to Abraham the land of all those nations, yet because the Israelites did not keep the conditions added to the covenant and the promise, only seven nations were defeated by them, the rest being left for the exercise of obedience and patience. Which is the answer of Jerome and Andr. Masius on chapter 1 of Joshua, v. 4.

Moreover, the Amorites were inhabitants of Bashan and Gilead, Deut. 2, originating from the fourth son of Canaan. The Hittites were situated towards the Euphrates, to the East, Jos. 1, 4. The Perizzites seem to have dwelt in Bezek, whose King was Adoni-Bezek, Jud. 1. The Canaanites dwelt in the mountains, who are said to have come there to the aid of the Perizzites and Adonibezek. The Hivite inhabited Mount Hermon, or its roots in the land of Maachah near Antilibanus: which place had been destined for the tribe of Asher. Jebus, from whom the Jebusites have their name, was the founder of the city of Jebus, which was afterwards called Jerusalem, Jos. 18, 28. The Girgashite had his seat in the region which was called Galilee, the parent of the Gergesenes, Matth. 8, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

QVOD SI AUDIENS VOCEM EJUS] Schemo Rabba hic recte: Si ab illo acceperitis, à me accipietis. Vide si- mile Joh. 5, 23.

Grotius defendit hic primum Vulgatam versio- nem, quod pronomen meum, quod in Ebræo non est, adjecerit: Translatum è v. 23. Sed interpretis est nihil addere, ne quidem aliunde. Non abs re. Angelus simpliciter dicitur, ut ille unus, quem pecu- liariter in hac historia commemoravit Moses, in- digitetur. Verum id, quia leve, facile transmit- timus. Quod vero illud MEUM porro significare vult, in meo nomine ac potestate, Angelumque crea- tum intelligit, divina potestate armatum, fabula Ju- daica approbata, quod Deus post cultum vituli Israë- litis Angelum illum abstulerit, & minorem Ange- lum illis dederit, cum potestate mere Angelica, id re- fragatur prorsus magnificæ Angeli, cujus παράστα- σιν & ὁδήγησιν hic promittit Dominus, descriptioni. De Angelo sermo est μοναδικῶς ita dicto, non uno è multis, nimirum de Filio Dei, Angelo increato. Qui exhiberi ipsi jubetur religiosa unique Deo de- bita veneratio: Observes faciem ejus, & audi vocem ejus, ne rebellis sis in eum. Qualis honor nuspiam an- gelo ulli creato delatus legitur. Ubinam jubemur observare faciem, vel cavere à facie Angeli creati, vocique ejus obedire, nec adversus eum peccare re- bellando? Porro Angelus hic potestatem habet re- mittendi peccata, aut non remittendi: quæ itidem nulli creato Angelo convenit. Ministris verbi tan- quam œconomis mysterium potestas illa διακονικῶς tributa, Matth. 18, 18. Joh. 20, 23. Angelis autem nuspiam tributa legitur. Hæc autem potestas judi- ciaria animadvertendi in inobedientes axioma proprium est Filio Dei, cui DEUS Pater dedit omne Judicium, Joh. 5, 23. Adhæc nomen Domini in hoc Angelo esse dicitur: quod nimis jejune explicat Grotius, habebit in se non longe petendam vindictæ potestatem: Nomen Domini essentiam ipsam Do- mini importat, ejusque gloriam, Es. 42, 8. Notatur ergò, in hoc Angelo esse Dei essentiam, vel ipsum esse verum natura & essentia Deum. Scrutetur hunc lo- cum, inquit Augustinus lib. 17. contra Faustum c. 19. non solum Manichæus, sed etiam Judæus, utrum de aliquo Angelo dixerit DEUS, Nomen meum est in illo, nisi de hoc ductore populi. Jesus enim est Rector & ductor populi in hæreditatem vitæ æternæ, cujus ty- pus fuit Josua nomine & re. Quod uberius confir- matur è locorum collatione. Idem enim sine du- bio Angelus hic est populi ductor, qui promisit Exod. 3, 17. se deducturum Israëlitus in terram Ca- nanæorum, Hethitarum, quem esse Jehovam Deum Abraham, Deum Isaac, Deum Jacob, luculenter ipsiusmet testificatio confirmat. Idem, qui in colu- mna nubis & ignis deduxit populum, Exod. 14. quem non creatum, sed increatum fuisse angelum ibidem ostendimus. Idem, qui principem militiæ Jehove se dixit Jos. 5, 14. & Jehovah illic nuncupatur, cap. 6, 2. Idem, qui celebratur ceu Angelus faciei, qui salva- vit populum, Es. 63, 9. quem Filium Dei esse redem- ptorem unicum ex illa cantione Eucharistica evi- denter constat. Qui duxit Israëlitas, & ab illis ten- tatus fuit 1. Cor. 10, 9. cujus vocem audire omnes de- bent, Deuter. 18, 20. Matth. 17, 5. cujus vocem DEUS suam ipsius dicit: quum hæc pro uno & eodem habeantur; Si audieris vocem ejus (Angeli) & si feceris omnia, quæ loquor. Et liquet sane, non femper locutum Angelum illum per se immediate, sed per Mosen sæpe, qui vero non ab angelo crea- to, sed ab UNO DEO se habere, quæ populo proponebat, testatus est. Unde oportet Angelum illum fuisse ipsummet Jehovam. Quapropter de Filio DEI explicant Justinus Martyr Dial. cum Tryph. Tertull. l. adv. Judæos. Athanas. de com- mun. essent. P. F. & S. S. Hesychius l. VII. in Lev. c. 16. August. l. c. à quibus alieni non sunt Patres Antiocheni contra Samosaten. Epist. Synodica. E Pontificiis quamvis nonnulli Michaelem angelum creatum, Præsidem Synagogæ Judaicæ, cum Corn. à Lap. statuant, Masius tamen Ebraice doctissimus palam illis refragatur: Eum, inquit, Angelum pu- to non esse Michaelem, sed verum æternum DEI Fi- lium & perpetuum Principem ductoremque populi DEI. Nec desunt è Rabbinis, qui id confessi sunt. Ipse Nachmani Filius R. Moses Gerundensis hunc Angelum in rubo Redemtorem Jehovam facit. Hic, inquit, Angelus (in rubo) si rem ipsam dicamus, est Angelus Redemtor, de quo scriptum est, quoniam nomen meum in ipso est: Ille, inquam, Angelus, qui ad Jacob dicebat, Ego DEUS Bethel. Locum su- pra ad c. III. adduximus. Idem R. Moses Gerund. ad Exod. XXIII. Rabbinorum sententiam, quod Michael intelligatur, non admittit. Sed in veritate inquit, Angelus ille, qui hic ipsis promittitur, est An- gelus Redemtor, in quo est nomen illud DEI ma- gnum,quia in nomine יהוה יה est rupes seculorum Es. XXVI, 4. & idem ille est, qui dicit, Ego sum Deus Be- thel, Gen. 31,13. (h. e. domus Dei) Nam consuetudo Re- gis est, ut habitet in domo sua. Vocat autem eum Scriptum Angelum, eo quod tota mundi gubernatio eo modo per ipsum fiat. Rabbini nostri dicunt esse מטטרון Metatron s. Metatorem, quod nomen signi- ficat ὁδηγὸν viæ ductorem. Porro neque R. Bechai abnuit. Dicit enim Angelum hunc DOMI- NUM, & dominatorem omnium, DOMINUM totius domus Dei, & omnium facultatum Dei, cu- stodem & conservatorem mundi, & Israëlis, omnia dicit ei esse subjecta; quæ certe non congruunt Mi- chaëli, creato Angelo, sed filio Dei. Quomodo etiam Abarbenel hic sese implicarit, ut manifesta reliquerit veritatis vestigia, Buxtorffius in Histor. arcæ Fœder. c. 14. p. 135. docuit. De loco Exod. 33. & sententia Nachmanidis hic adducta dispi- ciemus, cum eo feremur. Rectius Grotio hæc in gratiam Papistarum, Samosatenianorum & Judæo- rum ita pervertente, hic sapere cum Papistis quos- dam, tum Judæos, in aprico est. Qui quum fatea- tur Angelum divina ἐξοσία instructum habuisse in se non longe petendam vindictæ potestatem, quæ com- plectitur potestatem etiam dimittendi peccata, aut divinam ejusmodi potestatem vere infinitam ab es- sentia divina separet, necessum est, aut agnoscat divinæ essentiæ participem esse Angelum illum Du- ctorem. Quem denique Jehovam dici vult cap. 24, 1. Is vero, qui ibi Jehovah dicitur, & visus est, nullus alius, quam ipse summus Deus fuit. An- gelus ergo ille, in quo nomen DEI Jehovah, est summus ille DEUS, ad quem adscendere jussus est Moses, cujusque gloriam illic vidit. Ad quem locum jamjam accedemus.

Id repetitur Exod. 34, 11. At Deut. 7, 1. addi- tur Gergeseus: Gen. 15, 8. Cinæi etiam ac Genezæi, nec non Cedmonæi, & Raphaim (præteritis Hevæis) recensentur? Resp. Gergeseos omitti, & sub aliis comprehendi, quia pauciores erant, imo ab Amor- rhais subjugati erant, qui etiam pro cunctis ha- bitatoribus terræ Synecdochice accipiuntur quan- doque: quia Amorrhæi cæteris insigniores & cele- briores erant, & quum occupassent duo illa regna trans Jordanem Sehan & Ogi, numerosa prole au- cti postea immisisse videntur colonias in diversas terræ promissas partes, Deut. 1. Sic etiam Cana- næorum nomine quandoque generaliter omnes illi populi, utpote qui è posteris Kenahan fuere, Gen. 10, 15. quandoque illi, qui inter alios specialiter hoc nomen obtinuere, designantur. Et quamvis in prima occupatione solum septem illas gentes ob- tinuerint Israëlitæ, sub Davide ac Salomone tamen reliquas etiam subjectas habuere. Adde August. q. 21. in Jos. Denique etsi promiserit Deus Abrahæ omnium istarum gentium terram, tamen quia con- ditiones fœderi, & promissioni adjectas non serva- runt Israëlitæ, septem tantum gentes ab ipsis debel- latæ sunt, reliquis in exercitium obedientiæ & pa- tientiæ relictis. Quæ est Hieronymi & Andr. Masii, responsio in cap. 1. Jos. v. 4.

Cæterum fuerunt Amorrhæi Basanis, & Ga- ladis incolæ, Deut. 2. è quarto filio Canaan oriun- di. Hethæi versus Euphratem siti erant, ad Ori- entem Jos. 1, 4. Pherezæi videntur habitasse in Be- zek, quorum Rex fuerit Adoni-Bezek Jud. 1. Ca- nanæi habitarunt in montanis, qui illic Pherezæis, & Adonibeseck in auxilium venisse dicuntur. He- væus montem Hermon incoluit, seu radices ejus in terra Maacha prope antilibanum: qui locus tribui Aser destinatus fuerat. Jebus, à quo Jebusæi nomen habent, urbis Jebus conditor fuit, quæ postea Jeru- salem dicta Jos. 18, 28. Gergesæus in regione sedem habuit, quæ Galilæa dicta est, parens Gergesenorum Matth. 8, 8.

## 23:23
Ver. 23. AND MY ANGEL SHALL GO BEFORE THEE, AND SHALL BRING THEE IN UNTO THE AMORITE, AND THE HITTITE, AND THE PERIZZITE, AND THE CANAANITE, AND THE HIVITE, AND THE JEBUSITE, WHOM I WILL DESTROY.

Let 60,000 Trajan paces, or at least 15 German miles, be mentioned; Varenius noting here that Mercator conceived the length from South to North and the breadth from West to East in such a way that he assigned 67 miles to the former in smaller leagues, and 16 or 18 to the latter.

Latin:

Vers. 23. PRÆCEDETQUE TE ANGELUS MEUS, ET INTRODUCET TE AD AMORRHÆ- UM, ET HETHÆUM, ET PHEREZÆUM, CANANÆUMQUE, ET HEVÆUM, ET JEBUSÆUM, QUOS EGO CONTERAM.

Trajanos 60000. saltem passuum sive 15. German. miliarium memoretur, notante hîc Varenio Mercator longitudinem à Meridie ad Septentrionem & latitudinem ab Occidente ad Orientem ita concepit, ut illi leucis minoribus 67. miliaria, huic 16. vel 18. assignarit.

## 23:25
Verse 25. YOUR BREAD AND WATERS] Food and drink.

Latin:

Vers. 25. PANIBUS TUIS ET AQUIS] Cibo & potui.

## 23:26
Verse 26. I WILL FULFILL THE NUMBER OF YOUR DAYS] To

those years you will arrive, which the temperature of the body allows, which is much.

It is more correctly understood concerning the longevity of life, that they will arrive at a just age, which does not always depend on the temperament of the body, but more on divine grace.

Latin:

Vers. 26. NUMERUM DIERUM TUORUM IMPLEBO] Ad

eos annos pervenies, quos fert corporis temperatura, quod multum est.

Rectius de longævitate vitæ, quod ad justam ætatem perventuri sint, intelligitur, quæ non sem- per à temperamento corporis pendet, sed magis à divina gratia.

## 23:28
Ver. 28. SENDING FORTH COALS FIRST, WHICH WILL PUT TO FLIGHT THE HIVITE.)

In the Hebrew the place is first before thy face; however, even if it is not read how they were put to flight by coals, there is nevertheless no reason to doubt the fulfillment of the promise. Cf. Deut. 7, 20. Jos. 24, 12. Wis. 12, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 28. EMITTENS CARBONES PRIUS, QUI FU- GABUNT HEVÆUM.)

In Ebræo loco prius est ante faciem tuam; ut- ut autem non legatur, quomodo à carbonibus fugati sint, non tamen de complemento promis- sionis dubitandum. Conf. Deut. 7, 20. Jos. 24, 12. Sap. 12, 8.

## 23:31
Ver. 31. BUT I WILL SET THY BORDERS.

The borders are the Sea of Suph, the weedy sea, which is the Red Sea on the East, and the sea of the Philistines, or the Mediterranean on that side where it washes Palestine, to the West. The desert of Egypt, Paran, to the South. The river Perath to the North. However, it happened through the fault and negligence of the Israelites that those regions were not occupied, which nevertheless were eventually made tributary, 1 Kings 3. Furthermore, from Lebanon to the river of Egypt, or from Dan even to Beersheba, from the North to the South are assigned 128 stadia, 160 Italian miles, or 40 German miles: which distance would be the entire size of the region, since where it is longest, namely from the port of Joppa to the mountains

Latin:

Vers. 31. PONAM AUTEM TERMINOS TUOS.

Termini sunt mare Suph juncosum, quod est rubrum ab Oriente, & mare Palæstinorum, vel me- diterraneum ea parte, qua Palæstinam alluit, ad Occidentem. Desertum Ægypti Paran ab Au- stro. Flumen Perath ad Septentrionem. Factum autem Israëllitarum culpa, & negligentia, ut regio- nes illæ occupatæ non fuerint, quæ tamen tandem factæ sunt tributariæ, 1. Reg. 3. Cæterum à Li- bano ad fluvium Ægypti, vel à Dan usque ad Ber- seba, ab Aquilone ad meridiem affignantur 128. stadia, 160. miliaria Italica, vel 40. Germanica: quæ distantia integra effet regionis magnitudo, cum ubi longissima est, utpote à portu Japho ad montes

## 23:32
Verse 32. YOU SHALL NOT ENTER INTO A COVENANT WITH THEM.

There is added an exegesis in verse 33 concerning the granting to them of a habitation in the promised land, because the covenant concerning bearing with them is prohibited. Cf. chap. 34, 15. Deut. 7, 2. You shall not enter into a covenant with them, nor shall you have pity on them.

Martyr in the cited places, Class 4, chapter 16, and Alberico Gentili, book 1 on the Law of War, chapter 10, gather in vain from this that covenants with men of a different religion are illicit in the New Testament. For covenants are of a different kind; one must distinguish between covenants of non-aggression, as also those instituted for the sake of defense, and those which are entered into for the purpose of attacking a third party, and to which is annexed a condition against all and towards all, where it can easily happen that a believer binds himself to provide aid to an infidel for the purpose of attacking believers. Whence one must further distinguish between those covenants which are made with infidels against other infidels, and those which are made against believers: likewise between those which have only political conditions attached without danger or prejudice to the true religion, and those which are to the detriment of religion; those which are entered into when necessity and utility demand it, and those which are entered into beyond necessity or significant utility: likewise between political covenants regarding public external peace and commerce, and ecclesiastical covenants concerning religion. Covenants of the former kind are licit, of which sort there are examples of Jacob with Laban, Genesis 31, 44; of Solomon with Hiram, 1 Kings 5, v. 12; of Judas Maccabeus with the Romans, 1 Maccabees 8, 20; of Jonathan and Onias with the Romans and Spartans, 1 Maccabees 12, 1, 6; of Simon with the same, 1 Maccabees 14, 18, 25, which are nowhere read to have been disapproved by GOD, and others. Covenants of the latter kind are not likewise licit. Indeed, Becanus argues in his Scholastic Theology, part 2, Volume 2, chapter 25, and Dominic Bannes, question 40, article 1, that it is in itself and by its nature licit not only to call upon infidels for help in a just war against believers, but also to provide help to infidels against believers, provided that there is no consideration of faith. But if we are dealing with infidels properly so called, that is, non-Christians, a covenant entered into with them against those who are of the same mind as us in the faith is illicit. The case is different if, although they profess the Christian name, they are nevertheless idolaters and our persecutors; for then, even if one should not arrive at this point without safeguards, yet when we are attacked by those who only usurp the name of religion and are worse and more cruel than any infidel, even infidels can be called to our aid and covenants can be entered into with them; but not unless a huge necessity urges and compels it, and therefore covenants with men of a different and heterodox religion will be much less illicit in themselves. But provided that covenants with infidels have only political conditions attached, and bring no prejudice to religion: such as, for example, it would be if the faithful party, during the war, were to abstain from the public exercise of religion, or were to communicate with the infidel in any way, whether directly or indirectly and interpretatively. It must also be observed, so that every perverse opinion may be removed from the minds of the faithful, that trust primarily in such a bruised reed of Egypt, which is cursed, Jeremiah 17, 5. Nor should one weigh only what is licit, but also what is expedient, 2 Corinthians 6, 21; chapter 10, 23; and scandal must be avoided, lest the faithful appear to seek help from infidels because they place their trust in them, and not solely

trust in God, or be thought to be their partners in impiety, or to make nothing of the difference between religions. Furthermore, one must guard against the danger of subversion, lest from such a covenant there follow a desertion of the worship of GOD, or idolatry, or an increase of heterodoxy; one must also guard against the danger of perfidy, since pacts are often not kept by infidels and heretics, and from that a greater danger to the Church or the state could be brought on, just as the King of Moab did not keep his pact with the King of the Israelites, 2 Kings 3, 5; and Demetrius and Tryphon did not keep theirs with the Maccabees, 1 Maccabees 11, 53; 2 Maccabees 16, 26.

Reasons why it is licit in some case to enter into covenants with infidels are provided by: (1.) Natural law, by which legitimate defense is established, to which it pertains that we use those instruments which are at hand, and the work of those who can help. (2.) That infidels can of themselves undertake a just war against any enemies whatsoever, and therefore can also help others in a just war against any enemies whatsoever. (3.) That the Gospel does not abolish states, and therefore neither the defenses or foundations of states, which for the most part consist of covenants that are of a merely political and civil nature. To which are added the examples brought forward above.

As to the argument to the contrary from the present interdict, I respond that this is special, and concerns certain nations devoted to destruction: with whom the Israelites could in no case contract knowingly and willingly (Joshua did indeed contract a covenant with the Gibeonites, but ignorant that they were nations devoted to destruction) and that it was given to the Israelites, whose situation was different, because they were established in a separated land, than that of Christians established throughout the world, and in the midst of infidels or heretics. All covenants with all nations foreign to the Israelite Republic are indeed prohibited in this, that no one should enter into a covenant with their gods, namely in the business of religion. But in other matters, which pertain to commerce, and to some war, especially defensive against common enemies, with necessary exceptions having been set, it is evident from many examples that a covenant could be entered into with men of an otherwise different cult, and that even the Israelites could do so, provided it was done according to God.

As to the covenant of Asa with Ben-hadad, 2 Chron. 16, 7, GOD disapproves of it because the war was not just, and a covenant entered into with the King of the Israelites was violated: however, the covenant of Jehoshaphat with Ahab and Ahaziah was not even necessary, because the war was offensive, and in these and other cases the Prophets rebuke especially a preposterous trust in foreign aids, 2 Chron. 16, 7; ch. 19, 2; ch. 20, 37; Isa. 8, 14; ch. 30, 2; ch. 31; Hos. 5, 13. Let Becanus's objection from 1 Sam. 28, 2 be seen discussed in the same place.

But as concerns ecclesiastical covenants, when it is asked specifically: whether it is lawful by our own will and volition (it is another matter when covenants are extorted by a superior force or were extorted from our ancestors, or entered into by them for any reason, so that they also concern descendants, which it is necessary to tolerate) to contract covenants of patronage, or defensive and social (we are not dealing with peace treaties, which are lawful) with infidels or a profane people, or with men of a different religion, e.g., whether, when some greater force from the Papists, or other enemies of ours unjustly invading us, is pressing upon us, it is lawful for Lutherans to enter into a new covenant of defense with Calvinists? The blessed Tarnovius defends the negative in his treatise on covenants annexed to his commentary on Obadiah, praising the opinion of the blessed Luther, that the Zwinglians should not be admitted into the Smalcaldic league, and the response of the Elector of Saxony, John, given to the envoys of the Swiss, in Sleidan, fol. 6 and 8; Chytræus in his Chronicle; Thuanus, Book 2 of his History; the Counsel of the Ministers of the Word at Nuremberg, in the year 1530; the Disputation of the blessed Polycarp Lyser the Younger concerning leagues, held at Leipzig in the year 1620; the Tract of the blessed D. Hutter concerning a league. See also concerning this whole matter from our own: the blessed Gerhard, Commentary on Deut. 7:3; from the Reformed: Polanus, Book 1, Syntagma, chap. 11; Paræus in his Commentary on Gen. 14; Andreas Rivetus on Hosea, chap. 5. Compare also the counsels given on this cause by the blessed Luther and his colleagues in the Theological Counsels of Wittenberg, Vol. III, Title III, no. 5, as also the blessed Luther’s 'Warnung an seine liebe Deutschen', Vol. V, Jena, German.

However, a distinction must be made here, lest we simply condemn leagues of such a kind: for leagues are either merely political, not concerning the cause of religion, or religious, or finally mixed. Concerning those of the first kind, even Tarnovius acknowledges that they are lawful with the heterodox, provided they are about a lawful matter and are entered into in a lawful manner, so that the pure religion suffers no harm from them. But concerning the rest, of the second and third kind of leagues, he denies that they are lawful. Where, however, we judge that caution is needed: Since a league of defense against greater force, when the Orthodox are unjustly invaded, can be lawfully entered into with the heterodox in the same Republic or kingdom, provided that, first, no prejudice is created thereby for the pure religion, and second, that the Orthodox do not cooperate in such a league, either directly or indirectly, in the propagation or fostering of heterodoxy, nor do they enter into those conditions by which detriment to orthodoxy and the orthodox Church, or the increase or patronage of heterodoxy, is procured: Furthermore, if, third, the common safety of the Republic demands common effort, and they are members of the same republic or kingdom, so that their common rights are endangered, or fundamental laws undergo a crisis, and the common overthrow, suppression, and displacement of the same members of the Republic, both of the orthodox and of the heterodox who are united by a political bond, is imminent, so that they may protect themselves from injury and destruction by joined and associated effort and arms, and sustain and defend their common rights and common safety, peace, and tranquility against imminent force. Where, if the heterodox tolerated in the Republic intend that they themselves should not only be tolerated further and not oppressed, but also obtain a privilege of religion, the orthodox must take care that they do not in any way serve this intention, end, and purpose; which would be to aid the propagation of false doctrine; nor should they enter into leagues for the defense of the common state and public rights under such a condition or law, but rather should trust in the one God, and relying on His παραστάσει (presence/assistance), protect their own rights, rather than in any way help to procure security and immunity for heterodoxy. Concerning which, see the response given to the Most Serene Elector of Saxony, John George I, by the blessed Dn. D. Hoë in the 'Oraculum Dodonaeum' resolved by him. Fourth, when force is brought to bear only on account of the Gospel, the defense of which GOD reserves to Himself alone, the blessed Luther is the author of the view that such a confederation with the heterodox, such as the Zwinglians, is by no means lawful, the end of which is that the doctrine of the Gospel should be defended by the patronage of such a league, because thus hope and trust are placed not in the one God and our covenant with God, but in a league with those who are alien to the true God, whence by such leagues the glory of God is obscured, and the praise of victory and the defense of the Church, which is owed to God alone, is transferred to the enemies of the truth, the impious are confirmed in their error, the weaker among our own are offended, the Orthodox involve themselves in the guilt of others and in those punishments which are decreed for the enemies of the truth, and they commit themselves to present danger, which easily threatens from their fraudulent counsels; therefore Jehoshaphat was gravely rebuked because he joined himself to Ahab, King of Israel, 2 Chron. 19:2. and when they had entered into a naval alliance with Ahaziah, he gained this, that he was deprived of his entire fleet, 2 Chron. 20:35 seqq. And how the Prophets rebuke the conjunction with the nations can be seen in Isa. 30, Ezek. 16, Hos. 2:5, ch. 5:11, ch. 7:8 and 11:3, Amos 6:1, 2, Mic. 4:9, etc. The cause of the rebuke is the συζυγία (yoking together) with infidels, which is forbidden by God: 'Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers,' 2 Cor. 6:16.

Latin:

Vers. 32. NON INIBIS CUM IIS FOEDUS.

Additur ἐξήγησις vers. 33. de concedenda ipsis habitatione in terra promissa, quod foedus de illis ferendis prohibeatur. Conf. cap. 34, 15. Deut. 7, 2. Non inibis cum eis foedus, nec misereberis eorum.

Nequicquam inde colligit Martyr in LL. CC. Class. 4. cap. 16. Alber. Gentil. l. in de jure Bell. cap. 10. foedera cum hominibus diversae religionis in Novo Testamento esse illicita. Nam foedera sunt diversi generis; distinguendum inter foedera de non offendendo, ut & defensionis causa instituta, & ea, quae ad oppugnandum tertium ineuntur, & quibus annexa est conditio erga omnes, & contra omnes, ubi facile fieri potest, ut fidelis se adstringat ad suppetias infideli ad fideles opprimendos. Unde distinguendum porro inter ea foedera, quae cum infidelibus contra alios infideles, & quae contra fideles panguntur: item inter ea, quae politicas duntaxat conditiones conjunctas habent citra periculum vel præjudicium veræ religionis, & quæ in fraudem religionis; quæ necessitate & utilitate exigente, & quæ præter necessitatem aut insignem utilitatem ineuntur: item inter foedera politica pacem publicam externam & commercia respicientia, & foedera Ecclesiastica religionem concernentia. Prioris generis licita sunt, de qualibus prostant exempla Jacobi cum Labano, Genes. 31, 44. Salomonis cum Hieramo 1. Reg. 5. v. 12. Judæ Maccabæi cum Romanis 1. Macc. 8, 20. Jonathanis & Oniæ cum Romanis & Spartanis, 1. Maccab. 12, 1. 6. Simonis cum iisdem, 1. Maccab. 14, 18. 25. quæ nuspiam à DEO leguntur improbata, & aliorum. Posterioris generis non itidem licita sunt. Disputant quidem Becanus Schol. Theol. part. 2. Tom. 2. cap. 25. Dominic. Bannes q. 40. art. 1. per se, & natura sua licitum esse non solum in bello justo vocare in auxilium infideles contra fideles, sed etiam infidelibus contra fideles auxilium præbere, ubi modo nulla fidei est ratio. Sed si de infidelibus proprie dictis agamus, id est, non Christianis, illicitum cum illis foedus est adversus eos initum, qui in fide nobis sunt ὁμόψηφοι. Alia ratio est, si quamvis profiteantur Christianum nomen, sint tamen idololatræ, & perseqvutores nostri, tunc enim etsi non sine cautionibus huc deveniendum esset, tamen cum ab iis impetimur, qui religionis tantum nomen usurpant, & quovis infideli deteriores sunt & crudeliores, possunt etiam infideles in subsidium vocari, ac foedera cum iis iniri; sed non nisi ingenti necessitate urgente & cogente, ideoque multo minus per se illicita erunt foedera cum diversæ & heterodoxæ religionis hominibus. Sed ut foedera cum infidelibus politicas tantum conditiones adjunctas habeant, nullum religioni præjudicium adferant: quale v. g. foret, si pars fidelis durante bello abstinere ab exercitio publico religionis, aut cum infideli ulla ratione, seu directe seu per indirectum & interpretative communicare deberet. Observandum etiam, ut omnis è fidelium animis perversa opinio tollatur, fiducia imprimis in tale brachium arundineum Ægypti, quæ maledicta, Jer. 17, 5. Neque perpendendum tantum quid liceat, sed etiam quid expediat, 2. Corinth. 6, 21. cap. 10, 23. & evitandum scandalum, ne videantur auxilium petere fideles ab infidelibus, quod in illis fiduciam collocent, non soli

Deo confidant, aut putentur esse illorum socii in impietate, aut nihili facere discrimen religionum. Cavendum insuper periculum subversionis, ne ex tali fœdere sequatur desertio cultus DEI, aut idolatria, aut incrementum heterodoxias, cavendum etiam periculum perfidiæ, quum sæpe pacta non serventur ab infidelibus & hæreticis, atque inde majus periculum Ecclesiæ vel politiæ accersi possit, uti Rex Moab pactum cum Rege Israëlitis, 2. Reg. 3, 5. Demetrius & Tryphon cum Maccabæis, 1. Macc. 11, 53. 2. Macc. 16, 26. haud servarunt.

Rationes, quod in aliquo casu fœdera inire licitum sit cum infidelibus, præbet (1.) Jus naturale, quo legitima defensio stabilitur, ad quam pertinet, ut iis instrumentis utamur, quæ sunt ad manum, & eorum opera, qui possunt juvare. (2.) Quod infideles possint ex se suscipere justum bellum contra quoscunque hostes, ideoque etiam possint alios juvare in justo bello contra quoscunque hostes. (3.) Quod Evangelium non aboleat Politias, ideoque nec politiarum munimenta, vel firmamenta, quæ utplurimum fœderibus constant, quæ sunt conversationis mere politicæ, & civilis. Quibus accedunt exempla supra adducta.

Quod ad argumentum contrarium à præsenti interdicto, Respond. hoc speciale esse, ac concernere certas gentes excidio devotas: cum quibus nullo casu potuere Israëlitæ contrahere scientes & volentes (Josua fœdus cum Gibeonitis contraxit quidem, sed ignarus eos esse gentes exitio devotas) & datum id esse Israëlitis, quorum alia ratio, quia in terra separata constituti erat, quam Christianorum per orbem terrarum, & in medio infidelium, aut hæreticorum constitutorum. Omnia quidem fœdera cum omnibus gentibus alienis à Rep. Israëlitis in eo prohibentur, ut cum diis eorum nemo fœdus ineat, nempe in religionis negotio. At in aliis rebus, quæ ad commercia pertinent, & ad bellum aliquod maxime defensivum contra communes hostes positis exceptionibus necessariis, posse fœdus iniri cum disparis alioqui cultus hominibus, etiam Israëlitas id potuisse, dummodo id fieret secundum Deum, ex multis exemplis constat.

Quod ad fœdus Asa cum Benhadad 2. Paral. 6, 7. improbat id DEUS, quod bellum justum non esset, ac violaretur fœdus cum Rege Israëlitis initum: Josaphati autem fœdus cum Ahabo & Ochozia neque necessarium erat, quia bellum erat offensivum, & reprehendunt in his & aliis Prophetæ imprimis præposteram in alienis auxiliis fiduciam, 2. Par. 16, 2. cap. 19, 2. c. 20, 37. Es. 8, 14. c. 30, 2. cap. 31. Hos. 5, 13. Becani objectio è 1. Sam. 28, 2. ibidem discussa videatur.

Ecclesiastica vero fœdera quod attinet, cum quæritur speciatim: an liceat sponte & voluntate nostra (alia res est, cum per vim superiorem extorquentur fœdera aut extorta sunt majoribus nostris, vel quacunque ratione inita ab iis, ut etiam posteros concernant, quæ tolerare oportet) fœdera patrocinii, vel defensiva ac socialia, (non de pacificatoriis agitur, quæ licita sunt) cum infidelibus vel prophano populo, aut cum diversæ religionis hominibus contrahere, v. g. an vi aliqua majori à Pontificiis, vel aliis nostris hostibus injuste nos invadentibus ingruente, cum Calvinianis liceat Lutheranis de novo fœdus defensionis inire? Negativam propugnat B. Tarnovius tractat. de fœder. commentar. in Obadiam adjuncto, laudans B. Lutheri sententiam, ne Zwingliani in fœdus Smalcal- dicum reciperentur, & responsum Electoris Saxon. Johannis Helvetiorum legatis datum apud Schlei- danum f. 6. & 8. Chytr. in Chron. Thuan. lib. 2. Hi- stor. Consilium Ministrorum verbi Noribergens. An- no 1530. B. Polycarpi Lyseri Junior. Disput. de fœ- deribus Anno 1620. Lipsiæ habitam, B. D. Hutteri Tract. de fœdere. Vid. etiam de universa hac ma- teria è nostris B. Gerhard. Comment. in Deut. 7, 3. è Reformatis Polan. lib. l. X. Synt. cap. 11. Paræus in Comm. in Gen.14. Andr. Rivetus in Os. 5. cap. Conf. quoque consilia in hanc causam à B. Luthero & Col- legis data in Consil. Theol. Witeb. Tom. III. Tit.III. n. 5. ut & B. Lutheri Warnung an seine liebe Deut- schen. Tom. V. Jen. Germ.

Distinguendum autem hic, ne simpliciter fœ- dera ejusmodi improbemus: nam vel mere politica sunt fœdera, causam religionis non concernentia, vel religiosa, vel denique mixta. De illis primi ge- neris agnoscit etiam Tarnovius quod licita sint cum heterodoxis, modo sint de re licita, & modo legitimo inita, ne quid damni inde patiatur pura religio. Sed de reliquis secundi & tertii generis fœderibus negat, quod licita sint. Ubi tamen cau- tione opus esse censemus: Siquidem defensionis fœdus adversus vim majorem cum injuste invadun- tur Orthodoxi, cum heterodoxis in eadem Re- publ. vel regno iniri licite possit, dum primo nullum religioni puræ creatur inde præjudicium, neque secundo heterodoxiæ propagandæ, vel fovendæ, seu directe seu indirecte cooperantur ejusmodi fœdere Orthodoxi, nec eas conditiones ineunt, quibus orthodoxiæ, & orthodoxæ Ecclesiæ detrimen- tum, heterodoxiæ incrementum, aut patrocinium concilietur: Adhæc si tertio communis Reipublicæ salus communem operam poscat, & membra sint ejusdem reipublicæ vel regni, ut jura eorum com- munia periclitentur, aut leges fundamentales di- scrimen subeant, & communis eorundem Reip. membrorum eversio, suppressio & supplantatio, cum orthodoxorum, tum heterodoxorum, qui vin- culo Politico uniti sunt, immineat, ut sese ab inju- ria, & interitu conjunctis, sociatisq; operis, & ar- mis tueantur, communia jura communemque salu- tem, pacem & tranquillitatem adversus vim immi- nentem sustineant, & defendant. Ubi si hetero- doxi tolerati in Republ. id intendant, ut deinceps ipsi non tolerentur modo ulterius, nec oppriman- tur, sed etiam privilegium religionis consequan- tur, cavendum orthodoxis est, ne huic intentioni, fini, ac scopo ullo modo velificentur; quod esset falsæ doctrinæ propagationem juvare; neque ea conditione, aut lege fœdera defensionis commu- nis status, & jurium publicorum ineant, quin po- tius uni Deo confidant, ejusque freti παραστάσει, jura sua tueantur, quam heterodoxiæ securitatem & immunitatem conciliare ullo pacto juvent. Quo de vid. responsum Sereniss. Electori Saxon. Joh. Georgio I. à B. Dn. D. Hoë datum in orac. Dodoneo ab ipso resoluto. Quarto cum vis tan- tum infertur propter Evangelium, cujus defensio- nem sibi soli servat DEUS, B. Lutherus autor est, talem confœderationem cum heterodoxis, utpote Zwinglianis minime licitam esse, cujus finis ille sit, ut Evangelii doctrina fœderis ejusmodi patrocinio defendatur, quia sic spes & fiducia non in unum Deum, & fœdus nostrum cum Deo, sed in fœdus cum iis, qui à vero Deo alieni sunt, collocatur, un- de fœderibus ejusmodi gloria Dei obscuratur, & laus victoriæ, ac defensionis Ecclesiæ soli Deo de- bita in hostes veritatis transfertur, impii in errore confirmantur, infirmiores ex nostris offenduntur, Orthodoxi involvunt se alieno reatu, & pœnis il- lis, quæ hostibus veritatis decretæ sunt, committunt se præsenti periculo, quod ex fraudulentis eorum consiliis facile imminet, ideo graviter reprehensus fuit Josaphat, quod Regi Israëlis Achabo se conjun- xerit, 2. Chron. 19, 2. & quum societatem navalem iniissent cum Ahasia, id lucratus est, ut tota sua classe privatus fuerit 2. Chron. 20, 35. seqq. Et quomodo Prophetæ conjunctionem cum gentibus reprehen- dant, videre est Es. 30. Ez. 16. Os. 2, 5. c. 5, 11. c. 7, 8. & 11, 3. Am. 6, 1. 2. Mich. 4, 9. &c. Causa reprehensionis est συζυγία cum infidelibus à Deo prohibita : nolite jugum cum infidelibus ducere, 2. Cor. 6, 16.

## 24:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIV. The covenant is ratified. Moses ascends the mountain.

Ver. 1. ASCEND TO THE LORD] To that Angel armed with the power of God. Ver. 4. TITULOS] Pillars.

Grotius, as we have said, understands a created angel, and thinks that the discourse in the preceding chapter, ver. 10, was about the same one. But a created angel is never called Jehovah in the nominative case. Which name is proper to God alone; שם המפורש שם העצם, as the Jews call it. And he who appears here is called the God of Israel, v. 10. And they who saw the GOD of Israel; which likewise is a name that fits no Angel, but only God. A manifestation of Him that is altogether majestic is had here: under His feet as it were a work of sapphire stone, and as it were the heaven when it is clear. By this symbol was signified the most splendid and most excellent majesty of God, which far transcends and treads underfoot all the splendor and brightness of heaven and of gems. For the sapphire is the gem of gems, shining with golden points as if with stars, as Corn. à Lap. has it here. And v. 15. When Moses had ascended, a cloud covered the mountain, and the glory of the Lord dwelt upon Sinai, covering it with a cloud for six days: but on the seventh day He called him from the midst of the darkness. And the appearance of the glory of the Lord was like a burning fire upon the top of the mountain, in the sight of the children of Israel. Nowhere and never did any of the Angels appear in such a way. And when it is said somewhere that the glory of the Lord dwelt, it is implied that the Lord Himself, the glory, was present in a peculiar way. Furthermore, that God Himself, not any Angel, was present in the midst of the fire and spoke from the midst of the fire, Moses testifies at length, and in this he places the excellence of the people above all the nations of the earth, Deut. 4:32, 33. Ask about the ancient days, which were before you, from the day that God created man upon the earth, from the highest heaven even to the lowest part of it, if such a thing has ever happened, or if it has ever been known, that a people should hear the voice of God speaking from the midst of the fire, as you have heard and lived. That Lord is understood, to whom the others were not to approach, whom Moses alone was to ascend, whom they were to worship from afar, v. 1. 2. For they were not to ascend to the darkness in which that Lord God dwelt. To whom did they sacrifice peace offerings, and offer burnt offerings, who spoke those words of the law, and with whom is that covenant said to have been made? That Lord, who gave the stone tablets of the law, and wrote his commandments on them v. 12. Which it is certain were inscribed by the finger of God, and not by a created Angel. And to whom but God himself do those words refer v. 11. Nor did he lay his hand upon those of the children of Israel who had withdrawn from afar (the God of Israel), and they saw God, and did eat and drink. He did not lay his hand, or his power, upon them to strike them: See for this phrase similar places Gen. 37, 22. 1 Sam. 24, 7. Ps. 138, 7. even though they saw the Majesty of God. Nothing, therefore, is more certain than that God manifested himself here αὐτοπροσώπως; not an Angel alone.

Ver. same. AND SEVENTY ELDERS. Who c. 18. were chosen by the counsel of Jethro. But Num. 11, 16. 24. they are said to be gifted with the Spirit of God, but not then first chosen, but rather confirmed, and as it were solemnly inaugurated. The number LXXII. pleased, because it corresponds to the number of persons who went down into Egypt with Jacob, so that it might be seen in those who represented the people, into how great a multitude they had grown.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIV. Fœdus sancitur. Moses in montem ascendit.

Vers. 1. ASCENDE AD DOMINUM] Ad Angelum illum Dei potestate armatum. Vers. 4. TITULOS] Columnas.

Angelum creatum, ut diximus, intelligit Gro- tius, deque eodem cap. præcedente vers. 10. ser- monem fuisse censet. At creatus Angelus nun- quam in casu recto Jehovah nuncupatur. Quod nomen uni soli Deo proprium est; שם המפורש שם העצם, ut Judæi vocant. Et qui apparet hîc, Deus Israël dicitur v. 10. Et qui viderunt DEUM Israël; quod itidem nomen nulli Angelo, soli vero Deo convenit. Hujus Φανέρωσις prorsus Majesta- tica hîc habetur: sub pedibus ejus quasi opus lapidis Sapphirini, & quasi cælum, cum serenum est. Signa- batur hoc Symbolo splendidissima, & præstantissi- ma Dei majestas, quæ omnem cœli, & gemmarum splendorem & fulgorem longe transcendit, & pe- dibus premit. Est enim Sapphirus gemma gem- marum aureis punctis q. stellis collucens, ut hic habet Corn. à Lap. Et v. 15. Cum ascendisset Moses, operuit nubes montem & habitavit gloria Domini super Sinai, tegens illum nube sex diebus: Septimo autem die vocavit eum de medio caliginis. Erat autem spe- cies gloriæ Domini quasi ignis ardens super verticem montis, in conspectu filiorum Israël. Nusquam & nunquam Angelorum ullus ita apparuit. Et cum habitasse gloria Domini dicitur alicubi; Dominus ipse gloria peculiariter præsto fuisse innuitur. Porro Deum ipsum, non Angelum aliquem in medio ignis præsentem, & de medio ignis loquutum fuisse, prolixe testatur Moses, & in eo excellentiam populi præ omnibus nationibus terræ locat Deut. 4, 32. 33. In- terroga de diebus antiquis, qui fuerint ante te, ex die quo creavit Deus hominem super terram, summo cœ- lo usq́; ad imum ejus, si facta est aliquando hujuscemodi res, aut unquam agnitum est, ut audiret populus vo- cem Dei loquentis de medio ignis, sicut tu audisti & vi- xisti. Dominus ille intelligitur, ad quem cæteri non appropinquare, solus Moses ascendere debebat, quem procul adorare debebant, v. 1. 2. Non n. debu- erunt ascendere ad caliginem, in qua habitabat Deg Dominus ille. Cui immolaverunt victimas pacificas, & holocausta obtulerunt, qui locutus est verba illa legis, & cum quo fœdus illud factum dicet? Dominus ille, qui dedit tabulas lapideas legis, & scripsit in iisdem mandata sua v. 12. Quæ digito Dei exarata fuisse, non vero ab Angelo creato, certum est. Et quem nisi Deum ipsum referunt illa v. 11. Nec super eos, qui pro- cul recesserant de filiis Israël, misit manum suam (Deus Israël) videruntq́; Deum, ac comederunt & biberunt. Non misit manum, seu potentiam suam super eos ad percutiendum eosdem: Vid. qua phrasin similia lo- ca Gen. 37, 22. 1. Sam. 24, 7. Ps. 138, 7. etsi Majestatem Dei viderint. Nihil ergo certius, quam Deum αὐτο- προσώπως hic se manifestasse; non Angelum solum.

Vers. eod. ET SEPTUAGINTA SENES. Qui c. 18. e consilio Jethro electi. At Num. 11, 16. 24. Spiritu Dei donati, non autem tum primum electi dicuntur, sed confirmati potius, & quasi sole- mniter inaugurati. Numerus LXXII. placuit, quod ille respondeat numero personarum, quæ in Ægy- ptum cum Jacobo descenderunt, ut in iis, qui popu- lum repræsentabant videretur, in quantam multitu- dinem illæ excreverint.

## 24:4
ver. 4. TITLES) Pillars.

Latin:

vers. 4. TITULOS) Columnas.

## 24:5
ver. 5. AND HE SENT YOUNG MEN OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. Some understand the firstborn with the Chaldean, others the Levites, others generally the active young men from the children of Israel, who could minister in the sacrifices, where many things were done for the preparation of the victim, in which there was need of bodily strength. But that they are said to have slaughtered the victims, and to have made the burnt offering ascend, that is to be understood either of Aaron, or insofar as Moses and Aaron, as Rivetus rightly observes, used their ministry for those things which they could not do alone.

Latin:

vers. 5. MISITQUE JUVENES DE FILIIS ISRAEL. Nonnulli primogenitos cum Chaldæo, alii Le- vitas intelligunt, alii generatim juvenes expeditos e filiis Israel, qui ministrare poterant in sacrificiis, ubi multa fiebant ad præparationem victimæ, in quibus opus erat robore corporis. Quod autem mactasse dicuntur victimas, & ascendere fecisse ho- locaustum, id vel de Aarone intelligendum, vel quatenus Moses, & Aaron, ut recte observat Rive- tus, eorum ministerio usi sunt ad ea, quæ soli facere non poterant.

## 24:8
ver. 8. BUT HE TOOK THE BLOOD AND SPRINKLED IT UPON THE PEOPLE. Some understand it as sprinkled upon the 12 titles or pillars representing the people; but there is no need for this figurative explanation, if it be said that Moses extended his arm toward the whole multitude, and thus sprinkled the people, even if the sprinkling fell upon a few. However, the passage in Heb. is to be compared.

9, 17. where the Apostle taught that a sprinkler of wool and hyssop was used from the ϑεοπνευσία (divine inspiration) of the Holy Spirit (which were very suitable for this both because of their retentive power, since they are absorbent of moisture, like a sponge, and because of their density, and the wool indeed figured the flesh of Christ, white in itself, but reddened with blood for our sake; but the hyssop figured his humility.) And that water was mixed with the blood, (which was also done at other times Lev. 14, 6. 51. 52. Num. 19, 6. 18. and was a type of the water and blood from the side of Christ John 19.) and that he sprinkled the book at the same time in which the precepts, or words of God were, (because when he laid the book on the altar or around the altar, when he prepared himself for the sprinkling, and all things were purified with water, the book was also sprinkled, which the Apostle teaches was done by institution, mentioning also the blood of goats, even if Moses did not mention them. Since not only in such a solemn confirmation of the covenant were sacrifices for sin also used, but also in peace offerings goats were accustomed to be sacrificed, Lev. 3, 12. otherwise than Riebera thought regarding Heb. 9.) But because he took the book, and read, it is necessary that Scripture already existed then, and that the beginning of writing was not finally made when God inscribed the tablets with His own finger: which seemed so to some of our Theologians. For this happened only afterwards Exod. 31, 18. nor does any ὑσερολογία (hysteron proteron) have a place here. A doubt is also raised, since Moses names a covenant, why Paul substituted a Testament? but the Hebrew name is general, which is taken not only for a covenant between parties with mutual pledge and restipulation, but also for a declaration of will or promise, which proceeds from one: nor does it stand in the way that one and the same convention is both a covenant and a testament at the same time, that is, as a confederation between two parties under certain conditions: and nevertheless the testamentary disposition of one, with death intervening; especially if such a condition is set, which is fulfilled by the testator himself in some part, which was done here.

AND HE SAID, THIS IS THE BLOOD OF THE COVENANT, WHICH THE LORD HATH MADE WITH YOU.

Similar is the utterance of Christ, when in the institution of the Holy Eucharist, He says, This is My blood of the New Testament, and therefore just as Moses indicates by these words blood truly present, not a signification or type of blood, and his words are to be accepted concerning the blood of victims, which was then poured out without a figure, and properly, so Christ likewise testifies that His blood is truly present, not merely signified, or that a type or figure of it is exhibited, and He speaks of the blood, as the words sound, which He poured out for the remission of sins, which must be accepted entirely without trope and figure, lest the words be perverted and distorted by tropes according to our own pleasure, and rendered ambiguous. If the Old Testament was sanctioned by the true blood of victims, which referred to Christ, the New Testament is certainly to be understood as sanctioned not merely by a figure of blood, but by the very blood of Christ himself, which was shadowed forth by the blood of the victims, since Christ openly testifies to this in as many words, and looks back to this confirmation of the Old Covenant, using similar words, so that we might be made more certain that not a different, but the same sense underlies them. As truly, therefore, as the people were sprinkled there with typical blood, so truly is the blood of Christ also dispensed to us in the Holy Supper, and indeed according to the command of Christ, Drink, this is my blood, to be perceived by the mouth.

Nor is Rivet's exception of any moment; that it would follow that, just as the blood of calves was sprinkled in a visible manner, the sprinkling of the blood of Christ must also be visible, nay, that the blood of Christ itself is a sign, just as the blood of calves was a sign. For that it is visible is an accident; but the truth of the present blood pertains to the substance of the thing, namely to the matter, which was communicated to the people, and the words of Moses, This is the blood of the covenant, sound only concerning the truth and substance, not concerning the accidents of the blood, that it was visible, that it was corruptible, etc. Wherefore the consequence proceeds rightly from the truth of the substantial presence of the blood of the victims in the Old Covenant to the truth of the substantial presence of the blood of Christ in the New Testament, but not likewise from the accidents, which can vary. Nor was the blood of calves only a sign of the covenant, but a means of sanctioning and confirming the same: which must also be believed entirely concerning the blood of Christ, by which the covenant of grace is both sanctioned in the shedding of the same, and confirmed in the dispensation in the Holy Eucharist, and [is given] to us not through his ἀπουσίαν [absence], but through a true, real, and substantial παρουσίαν [presence], which the most truthful words of Christ testify: This is my blood of the New Testament, etc.

Verse of the same.

UPON ALL THESE WORDS.

Rivet wrongly restricts these words to divine precepts, excluding the promises. He says in this place, p. 127, that those who understand these words as being about divine promises are mistaken, confirming this by the reasoning that they refer manifestly to the precepts which were being read from the book, upon the observation of which, as a condition necessary on the part of the people, that covenant depended. For it was a book of precepts, not of promises. For then under the Old Testament the condition of keeping the law was proposed; which under the New is not required, but is announced as having been performed for us in Christ and is received by faith. But Rivet is greatly mistaken: because the words In the book sprinkled with blood, Moses proposed not fewer promises than precepts; and just as the covenant on the part of the Israelite people included the condition of obedience, so God bound Himself by this covenant, that He would be the God of this people, intending to do them good here and forever. And although that condition of perfect obedience could hardly be fulfilled, the promises made divinely for obedience are not therefore to be denied; because the infidelity of men does not make void the faithfulness of God, Rom. 3:4. Not to mention that the law was a schoolmaster unto Christ, in whom we have τὸ πλήρωμα νόμꙋ, Rom. 10:4, and that in the book of the law and those sermons were also comprised those things by which Christ was prefigured, just as the confirmation of the covenant made with the blood of victims, and the very shedding of the blood of victims, were nothing other than a foreshadowing and type of those things whose body and substance we have in Christ, Col. 2. That sprinkling, says Pelargus in this place, was a silent admonition of the human condition, that we are all unclean by nature, and then of the future expiation through Christ; and a most certain symbol of the covenant which God was about to enter into with us, with our altar sprinkled with the blood of Christ, Is. 63:2, 3, and with us washed by His own blood.

Latin:

vers. 8. ILLE VERO SUMTUM SANGUI- NEM RESPERSIT IN POPULUM. Nonnulli sparsum intelligunt in 12. titulos vel columnas populum repræsentantes; sed hac figura- ta explicatione opus non est, si dicatur, quod Moses versus totam multitudinem brachium extenderit, atque ita populum adsperserit, etsi in paucos asper- sio ceciderit. Conferendus autem est locus Ebr.

9, 17. ubi Apostolus aspergillum ex lana & byssopo ad- hibitum e ϑεοπνευσία S.S. docuit (quæ tum ob vim retentricem, quum humoris bibula sint, ut spongia, tum ob densitatem ad id percommoda erant, & figu- rabant lana quidem coccinea carnem Christi per se candidam, at ob nos sanguine rubricatam; byssopus vero humilitatem ejusdem.) Et aquam admistam sanguini fuisse, (quod etiam alias factum Lev. 14, 6. 51. 52. Num. 19, 6. 18. & typus erat aquæ & sanguinis e latere Christi Joh. 19.) & librum simul in quo præ- cepta, vel sermones Dei erant, consfersisse, (quia cum librum in altari vel circa altare, quum ad asper- sionem se accinxit, deponeret, & omnia lustraren- tur aqua, etiam liber aspersus fuit, quod ex institu- to factum docet Apostolus, sanguinem etiam hirco- rum commemorans, etsi Moses eorum non memi- nerit. Siquidem non tantum in tam solemni fœ- deris confirmatione sacrificia etiam pro peccato ad- hibita, sed etiam in pacificis sacrificiis hirci immolari consueverint, Lev. 3, 12. secus atque Riebera ad Ebr. 9. censuit.) Quia vero librum accepit, & legit, o- portet jam tum extitisse Scripturam, nec demum scribendi initium factum esse, cum Deus tabulas suo digito inscripsit: quod nonnullis Theologis nostris visum. Hoc enim postea demum contigit Exod. 31, 18. neque ulla ὑσερολογία hic locum habet.
