verse 34. SO THAT THERE BE A GOLDEN BELL, AND A POMEGRANATE] Of which the former by sound, the latter by color, would represent thunder and lightning. Thus Josephus.

Latin:

vers. 34. ITA VT TINTINNABVLVM SIT AVREVM, ET MALVM PVNICVM] Quorum illud sono, hoc colore tonitrua & fulmen referrent. Ita Josephus.

## 28:35
v. 35. THAT THE SOUND MAY BE HEARD.

By which the people were warned to prepare their heart, as the Hebrews note. Josephus and other Jews, and from them Jerome, refer the four colors of the robe to the 4 elements, but the bells to their harmony and congruence. And some wish this to be indicated in Wisd. 18, 24, where the Vulgate has: in the robe of the priest, which he had, the whole world was. But these are Jewish inventions. That they look to the Messiah is evident from the Epistle to the Hebrews: therefore the variety of colors makes for his beauty and majesty, the bells for the sound of the Gospel and doctrine, which has gone out into all the world. Rupertus refers the bells to preaching, the pomegranates to the miracles of Christ. They can also be applied analogically to the ministers of the word, of whom Greg. M. l. 1. Epist. 14. In walking, the Priest has bells, so that with the sound of the tongue, the very good works of the Priest may also cry out, and it is said: join the pomegranates, i.e., that in everything you say, you may hold the unity of faith. Because Beda on this passage says, just as in one pomegranate many grains are protected inside by the outer rind, so the unity of the holy Church gathers innumerable peoples, whom the diversity of works holds within. Jerome in Ep. ad Fabiol. says: the knowledge and erudition of the Priest of God ought to be so great that his steps and movements and everything should be vocal. Let him conceive truth in his mind and let him resound it in his whole habit and adornment, so that whatever he does, whatever he speaks, may be doctrine for the peoples: for without bells and diverse colors and gems and flowers of virtues, he can neither enter the holy place nor possess the name of a Prelate. Finally, Origen also applies these to all believers as spiritual Priests, Ap. 1, 6. See hom. 9. in Exod.

Latin:

v. 35. UT AUDIATUR SONITUS.

Quo moneretur eodem populus, ut cor suum præpararet, uti Ebræi notant. Josephus aliique Judæi, & ex iis Hieronymus quatuor colores pode- ris ad 4. elementa referunt, tintinnabula autem ad eorum concentum & congruentiam. Atque id nonnulli volunt Sap. 18, 24. indicatum, ubi Vulgata habet: in veste poderis, quam habebat, totus erat orbis terrarum. Sed haec inventa Judaica sunt. Ad Messiam ea spectare ex Epist. ad Hebraeos constat: varietas ergo colorum ad pulchritudinem & majestatem ejus, tintinnabula ad sonum Evangelii, & doctrinae faciunt, qui in omnem orbem exivit. Rupertus tintinnabula ad praedicationem, mala punica ad miracula Christi refert. Applicari etiam possunt analogice ad verbi Ministros, de quibus Gregor. M. l. 1. Epist. 14. In incessu Sacerdos habet tintinnabula, ut vitae viam cum linguae sonitu, ipsa quoq; bona opera Sacerdotis clament, diciturq;: mala punica jungite q. d. per omne quod dicitis, unitatem fidei teneatis. Quia Beda in h. l. dicente, sicut in malo punico uno exterius cortice multa interius grana muniuntur, sic innumeros populos sanctae Ecclesiae congregat unitas, quos intus diversitas operum tenet. Hieron. in Ep. ad Fabiol. Tanta, inquit, debet esse scientia & eruditio Pontificis Dei, ut & gressus ejus & motus, & universa vocalia sint. Veritatem mente concipiat & toto eam habitu resonet, & ornatu, ut quicquid agit, quicquid loquitur, doctrina sit populorum: absq; tintinnabulis enim, & diversis coloribus, & gemmis floribusq; virtutum nec sancta ingredi potest, nec nomen Antistitis possidere. Denique applicat etiam haec Origenes ad omnes credentes ceu spirituales Sacerdotes Ap. 1, 6. Vid. hom. 9. in Exod.

## 28:36
Verse 36. HOLY TO THE LORD. These two names קדש ליהוה, Holiness of the Lord, LXX. ἁγίασμα κυρίῳ, had to be inscribed on a plate of the purest gold, and not only the tetragrammaton name, as some Hebrews wish. It is thus hinted that this priest sanctified the Lord by his holiness, so that the gifts and offerings of the Israelites which he is about to offer to the Lord, even if they are not in every part pure and absolute, may nevertheless be held holy and acceptable in the eyes of God. Therefore, through the same, the uncleanness of the sacrifices themselves was sanctified and expiated, sanctified by the Lord, and by him wearing the plate in testimony of that thing, in type of Christ, through whom all our gifts are considered holy and held acceptable, who by his purity and holiness covers their impurity.

Latin:

Vers. 36. SANCTUM DOMINO. Haec duo nomina קדש ליהוה Sanctitas Domini, LXX. ἁγίασμα κυρίῳ, insculpi debuere laminae de auro purissimo, non vero solum nomen τετραγράμματον, ut Ebraei nonnulli volunt. Innuitur ita, hunc sacerdotem sanctificasse Dominum sua sanctitate, ut quae dona & munera Israelitarum oblaturus est Domino, ea tametsi non sint ex omni parte pura, & absoluta, tamen in oculis Dei sancta habeantur & grata. Per eundem ergo sanctificata sunt, & expiata ipsorum sacrificiorum immundities, sanctificatum a Domino, & gestantem laminam in ejus rei testimoniū, in typum Christi, per quem nostramunera omnia sancta censentur, & grata habentur, qui sua puritate & sanctitate eorum impuritatem tegit.

## 28:38
vers. 38. AND AARON SHALL BEAR THE INIQUITIES OF THE THINGS WHICH THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL HAVE OFFERED AND SANCTIFIED] In the Hebrew: And Aaron shall bear the iniquity of the sanctifications, which the Children of Israel shall sanctify in all the gifts of their sanctifications. As also the Greek. The sense is, if anything be done less rightly in offering or sacrificing, this also shall be expiated by Aaron.

Latin:

vers. 38. PORTABITQVE AARON INIQVITATES EORUM QUÆ OBTVLERUNT ET SANCTIFICARUNT FILII ISRAËL] In Hebraeo: Et portabit Aaron iniquitatem sanctificationum, quas sanctificabunt Filii Israel in omnibus donis sanctificationum earum. Quomodo & Graecus. Sensus est, si quid in offerendo aut immolando minus rite factum sit, hoc quoque ab Aarone expiabitur.

## 28:39
v. 39. AND THOU SHALT WEAVE THE TUNIC OF FINE LINEN. In the Hebrew: thou shalt make a tunic of fine linen: which was woven without seam from the top throughout, such as was the tunic of Christ, John 19. And it was an inner garment covering the whole body on every side, and that most white: shadowing forth the innocence and holiness of Christ.

v. eod. AND THOU SHALT MAKE A FINE LINEN TIARA. This tiara was of the high priest alone, called מִצְנֶפֶת from the wrapping: that of others (the priests) was of another form and name, מִגְבָּעוֹת, named from the sharpness, as it were little hills. Josephus attributes a triple crown to the high priest, which Baronius, Ribera, and Corn. a Lap. snatch at for the triple crown of the Roman Pontiff: but Salianus, T. 2. Ann. 2544, rightly warned that Barradius is deservedly to be wondered at, since without any authority of Scripture, which pursues even the least things in these matters, it is affirmed by Josephus that a certain golden crown surrounded the hyacinthine cap in a triple order, and he concludes that he can with impunity pass over the golden calyces, and the triple order of the crown, and if there are any other things from Josephus, or from more ancient Jews besides the authority of Scripture introduced. Now the Tiara was a type of cap worn on the head, which formerly only kings and princes used. For Christ our Priest is also King, although his kingdom is not of this world.

AND A BELT OF EMBROIDERED WORK.

Namely, Phrygian: it was a girdle and belt by which garments were bound so they would not hang loose: denoting the justice and faithfulness of Christ, Isa. 11. v. 5. and that he is always girded to undertake the duties of Priest (interceding) and King (governing), just as the Orientals used a girdle so that they might be more ready for all works.

Latin:

v. 39. STRINGESQUE TUNICAM BYSSO. In Ebraeo: facies tunicam e Bysso: quae inconfutilis fuit contexta a summo per totum, qualis erat Christi tunica Joh. 19. Fuitque vestis interior totum corpus undiquaque tegens, eaque candidissima: innocentiam & sanctitatem Christi adumbrans.

v. eod. ET TYARAM BYSSINAM FACIES. Tyara haec solius summi Sacerdotis erat מִצְנֶפֶת ab involutione vocata: aliorum (Sacerdotum) alterius formae & nominis fuit מִגְבָּעוֹת ab acumine, tanquam colliculi nominata. Josephus triplicem coronam summo Sacerdoti tribuit, quod Baronius, Riebera, Corn. a Lap. abripiunt ad Pontificis Romani coronam triplicem: sed recte Salianus T. 2. Ann. 2544. monuit, mirari merito Barradium, sine ulla Scripturae autoritate, quae in his minima quaeque persequitur, a Josepho affirmari coronam quandam auream triplici ordine hyacinthinum pileum circumdedisse, concluditque se impune missos facere posse calyculos aureos, & triplicem coronae ordinem, & si quae sunt alia a Josepho, vel ab antiquioribus Judaeis praeter autorita- tem Scripturæ introducta. Fuit autem Tiara pi- lei genus in capite gestatum, quo non nisi reges & principes olim utebantur. Christus enim Sacerdos nofter etiam Rex est, licet regnum ejus non sit mundanum.

ET BALTHEUM OPERE PLUMARI.

Phrygionico nempe: Zona & cingulum erat, quo vestes, ne diffluerent, constringebantur: de- notans Christi justitiam & fidelitatem, Esa. 11. v. 5. & quod semper accinctus sit ad subeunda Pontificis (intercedentis) & regis (gubernantis) munia, uti orientales cingulo utebantur, ut ad omnia opera expeditiores essent.

## 28:40
V. 40. FOR THE SONS OF AARON YOU SHALL PREPARE LINEN TUNICS AND BELTS AND TIARAS] Thus also the Egyptian priests used linen garments inside and out.

The tunics did not differ from the High Priest's tunic: (they are indeed called linen tunics in Exod. 39, but Moses seems to use the words for Byssus and linen interchangeably at times: although here in the Hebrew it is not added, which the Vulgate added, that they were linen:) nor, as far as is known, did the belts. The tiaras, however, were different, as we said at verse 39. The High Priest's turban was wound, as R. Levi notes; the tiaras of the other priests were placed upon the head and resembled the appearance of a helmet. Afterwards, linen breeches are ordered to be made, to cover the flesh of shame from the loins even to the thighs: Thus, therefore, as the High Priest had eight garments—the breastplate, the Ephod, the robe, the tight or checkered tunic, the turban, the plate, and the undergarments—so the inferior ones had four: the tunic, the belt, the tiara, and the undergarments or breeches: of which some were for adornment, others for necessity and for covering shame. The linen tunics of the priests signify that Christians, spiritual priests, have put on Christ in baptism, by whose holiness all their infirmities and iniquities are covered. The belts admonish that everyone should be prepared to perform their duties, and that we should stand with our loins girded with the belt of truth, Eph. 6. The tiara or mitre on the head promises divine protection to those walking in their vocation. The breeches admonish that we ought to maintain public decency.

Latin:

V. 40. FILIIS AARON TVNICAS LINEAS PARABIS ET BALTHEOS AC TIARAS] Sic & Ægyptii Sacerdotes vestibus usi lineis intrinsecus & extrinsecus.

Tunicæ non variabant à Pontificis tunica: (di- cuntur quidem in Exod. 39. tunicæ byssinæ, sed videtur Moses voces Byssli & lini quandoque indifferenter usurpare: quamvis hic in Ebræo non addatur, quod addidit vulg. lineas eas fuisse:) nec, quod constet, baltei. Tiaræ autem diversæ erant, ut ad vers. 39. diximus. Pontificis Cidaris involuta erat, notante R. Levi, aliorum Sacerdotum tiaræ pone- bantur super caput, & galeæ speciem referebant. Postea fæminalia linea fieri jubentur, ut operiant carnem turpitudinis à renibus usque ad femora: Sic ergo uti summi Sacerdotis octo erant vestimen- ta, pectorale, Ephod, pallium, tunica stricta vel ocellata, Cidaris, lamina & subligacula: ita inferio- rum erant quatuor: tunica, balteus, tiara & subli- gacula seu femoralia: quorum alia ad ornatum, alia ad necessitatem & turpitudinem tegendam facie- bant. Byssinæ Sacerdotum tunicæ significant Christianos, spirituales Sacerdotes, Christum in baptismo induisse, cujus sanctitate tegantur omnes eorum infirmitates, & iniquitates. Baltei admo- nent, ut quisque ad obeunda munia sit paratus, & ut lumbis stemus cinctis balteo veritatis, Ephes. 6. Tiara vel mitra in capite protectionem divinam ambulantibus in sua vocatione promittit. Femo- ralia admonent, quod publicam honestatem tueri debeamus.

## 28:41
Vers. 41. AND YOU SHALL CONSECRATE THE HANDS OF ALL.

In the Hebrew: you shall fill the hands: This rite, as Mercer notes, was accepted because those to whom the power of sacrificing was given had their hands first filled with a portion of the sacrifices, whence afterwards 'to fill the hand' was accepted for 'to initiate into sacred rites'; therefore it is added, 'and you shall sanctify them, that they may perform the Priesthood for me.' Cf. Jud. 17. v. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 41. ET CUNCTORUM CONSECRA- BIS MANUS.

In Ebræo: implebis manus: Ritus hic fuit notante Mercero, receptus, quod iis, quibus da- batur sacrificandi potestas, prius manus impletæ parte sacrificiorum, unde postea implere manum acceptum pro initiare sacris, ideo additur sancti- ficabisque illos, ut Sacerdotio fungantur mihi. Conf. Jud. 17. v. 5.

## 28:42
Vers. 42. YOU SHALL ALSO MAKE BREECHES] This also was opposed to the neighboring nations, whose priests used to uncover the parts that should be covered before the idol Pehor.

Latin:

Vers. 42. FACIES ET FEMINALIA] Oppositum & hoc gentibus vicinis, quarum flamines tegendas partes coram Pehore idolo nudabant.

## 29:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIX.

The Consecration of Priests.

Ver. 1. TAKE A BULLOCK FROM THE HERD.

IN Hebrew: Take a young bull, the son of an ox. Tremellius and Junius do not conveniently restrict it, and translate it as a suckling, that is, not yet weaned from milk. For the Hebrews note that it is the son of an ox even when it is three years old. The materials for the sacrifices of the initiation of the Priests are described here: since for the expiatory victim or for sin they had to offer a bullock or a young bull, for the burnt offering a ram, and for the Eucharistic or peace offering likewise a ram, for which latter sacrifice there was also need of a whole of bread, cakes mingled with oil, and wafers, to be made from the purest wheat flour without leaven: by which was signified the unblemished lamb Christ, 1 Pet. 1 v. 19, who offered himself to GOD Heb. 9 v. 14, and is the bread descending from heaven John 6 v. 50, infected by no leaven of the old nature 2 Cor. 5 v. 20, to whom those who are grafted in must also be purged from leaven 1 Cor. 5 v. 8.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIX.

Consecratio Sacerdotum.

Vers. 1. TOLLE VITULUM DE ARMENTO.

IN Ebræo: Cape juvencum filium bovis. Non commode Tremell. & Jun. restringunt, & ver- tunt subrumum, id est, nondum à lacte depulsum. Nam Ebræi notant bovis filium etiam esse, cum trium annorum est. Describuntur hic materialia ad sacrificia initiationis Sacerdotum: quum ad hostiam expiatoriam vel pro peccato vitulum vel ju- vencum, ad holocaustum arietem, ad Eucharisticum vel pacificum sacrificium itidem arietem offerre debuere, ad quod posterius Sacrificium etiam opus erat tota panis, crustula conspersa oleo, & la- gano, ex purissima farina triticea absque fermento conficienda: quibus significatus fuit agnus incontaminatus Christus, 1. Petr. 1. v. 19. qui DEO seipsum obtulit Ebr. 9. v. 14. & panis est de cœlo descendens Joh. 6. v. 50. nullo infectus veteris naturæ fermento 2. Cor. 5. v. 20. cui qui inseruntur, etiam expurgandi à fermento sunt 1. Cor. 5. v. 8.

## 29:4
Ver. 4. AND WHEN YOU HAVE WASHED THE FATHER WITH HIS SONS WITH WATER.

Aaron had to be washed with his sons, that he might foreshadow our High Priest Christ, who is pure and separated from sinners Heb. 7 v. 26, and the purity which GOD requires in the ministers of the word Tit. 2 v. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 4. CUMQUE LAVERIS PATREM CUM FILIIS SUIS AQUA.

Debuit Aaron cum filiis lavari, ut adumbraret Pontificem nostrum Christum, qui purus & separatus est à peccatoribus Ebr. 7. v. 26. & puritatem, quam in ministris verbi requirit DEUS Tit. 2. vers. 7.

## 29:5
Ver. 5.

AND UPON THE EPHOD] There is more in the Hebrew, namely, And upon the ephod cast over, which Theodotion expresses thus, τὸν ἐπενδυτην τῆς ἐπωμίδος.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ET SUPER HUMERALI] Plus est in Hebræo, nempe Et superinjectum humerali, quod sic exprimit Theodotio, τὸν ἐπενδυτην τῆς ἐπωμίδος.

## 29:6
Ver. 6. AND YOU SHALL PUT THE MITRE UPON HIS HEAD]

Wool wrapped around the head. Plutarch describes the attire of the high priest among the Jews thus: Ὁ ἱερεὺς μιτροφόρος, νεβρίδα χρυσόπαστον ἐνημμένος, χιτῶνα δὲ ποδήρη φέρων καὶ κοθόρνους; κώδωνες δὲ πολλοὶ κατακρέμανται τῆς ἐσθῆτος.

AND THE HOLY PLATE UPON THE MITRE]

He well explained נֵזֶר, which signifies a crown, as a plate in this place, from a comparison of other passages.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET PONES TIARAM IN CAPITE EJUS]

Lanam capiti circumplicatam. Plutarchus habitum summi apud Judæos Sacerdotis sic describit: Ὁ ἱερεὺς μιτροφόρος, νεβρίδα χρυσόπαστον ἐνημμένος, χιτῶνα δὲ ποδήρη φέρων καὶ κοθόρνους; κώδωνες δὲ πολλοὶ κατακρέμανται τῆς ἐσθῆτος.

ET LAMINAM SANCTAM SUPER TIARAM]

Bene נֵזֶר quod coronam significat hoc loco laminam explicavit, ex collatione locorum aliorum.

## 29:7
Ver. 7. AND YOU SHALL POUR THE ANOINTING OIL UPON HIS HEAD

Upon the forehead, making a cross, or χιασμόν. So all the Rabbis.

With this oil only was the High Priest anointed, Num. 4, v. 3, 16, therefore he is called the anointed absolutely. Conf. chap. 35, 25. Ps. 133. Whence in the investiture of the sons no mention of anointing is made in this place, v. 8. Yet the sons were also sprinkled with the ointment and blood, and their garments, Lev. 8, 30, not anointed in the same way as Aaron, whence in Num. 3, 3 they are called מְשֻׁחִים not on account of anointing or pouring upon the head, which was peculiar to Aaron, but on account of that common sprinkling designated in the cited place, Lev. 8, 30.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET OLEUM UNCTIONIS FUNDES SUPER CAPUT EJUS]

Super frontem faciendo decussim, sive χιασμόν. Ita Rabbini omnes.

Oleo isto tantum ungebatur summus Sacerdos Num. 4. v. 3. 16. ideo unctus absolute dictus. Conf. cap. 35, 25. Psal. 133. Unde in filiorum investitura nulla unctionis facta mentio h. l. v. 8. Adsperfi tamen filii etiam unguento sunt & sanguine, ac vestes eorum Lev. 8, 30. non item ut Aaron inuncti, unde Num. 3, 3. מְשֻׁחִים dicuntur non ob unctio- nem vel effusionem super caput, quæ Aaroni propria erat, sed ob aspersionem illam communem loco citato Lev. 8, 30. designatam.

## 29:10
V. 10. AND AARON AND HIS SONS SHALL LAY THEIR HAND UPON HIS HEAD.

This laying on of hands was a sign, and as it were a protestation of guilt and deserved punishment, by which the one offering the sacrifice confessed that he was worthy to be sacrificed with the victim, that he was guilty of sin, and worthy of death, but that he requested that all guilt be transferred to the victim, which was a type of Christ, upon whom all our sins were transferred, Is. 53, 1. Pelargus observes in this place that by this act of χειροθεσία was signified both the transfer of the guilt of the ministers onto Christ, and the peculiar devotion of those who dedicate themselves to God.

Latin:

V. 10. IMPONENTQUE MANUM AARON, ET FILII EJUS SUPER CAPUT ILLIUS.

Impositio hæc manuum signum, & q. protestatio fuit culpæ & pœnæ promeritæ, quæ offerens hostiam fatebatur, se dignum esse, qui cum hostia immolaretur, se reum peccati, & dignum morte esse, petere autem, ut in victimam transferretur omnis reatus, qui typus erat Christi, in quem omnia nostra peccata translata sunt Es. 53, 1. Significatam hoc χειροθεσίας actu & reatus ministrorum in Christum translationem, & devotionem peculiarem eorum, qui se Deo addicunt, observat in h. l. Pelargus.

## 29:11
Ver. 11. AND YOU SHALL SLAUGHTER IT.

The slaughtering by Moses, to whom it was here peculiarly enjoined, the Priesthood not yet being established, was done extraordinarily; he who was already to consecrate others to the priesthood, therefore he is numbered among the Priests, Ps. 99, 5; when they were established in their office, neither did Moses perform such duties, nor were his sons numbered among the Priests, but were reduced to the order of the Levites.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET MACTABIS EUM.

Mactatio à Mose, cui peculiariter hic injuncta, nondum constituto Sacerdotio, extraordinarie facta, qui alios ad sacerdotium jam consecrare debebat, ideo Sacerdotibus annumeratur Ps. 99, 5. quibus in officio suo constitutis neque Moses talibus functus est officiis, neque filii ejus inter Sacerdotes numerati, sed in ordinem Levitarum redacti sunt.

## 29:12
Ver. 12. BESIDE THE BASE OF IT.

The horns of the altar were to be touched with blood, the rest of the blood was to be poured beside the base of the same; some report that it was to the inner part of the altar, because it was hollow, in which, since fire was perpetually burning, it could easily be consumed. Moreover, atonement was made by blood, because the soul, that is, the life, is in the blood: and that blood was a type of the blood of Christ cleansing us from all sin, 1 John 1, 7; it was signified, therefore, that the altars of our hearts and all holy things would be cleansed by his blood.

Latin:

Vers. 12. JUXTA BASIN EJUS.

Tingenda erant sanguine cornua altaris, reliquum sanguinis fundendum juxta ejusdem basin, ad interiorem partem altaris, quia id concavum fuit, referunt nonnulli, in qua cum ignis perpetuo arderet, facile consumi potuit. Sanguinis autem facta est expiatio, quia anima, id est, vita in sanguine est: fuitque sanguis ille typus sanguinis Christi mundantis nos ab omni peccato 1. Joh. 1, 7. significatum ergo, ipsius sanguine altaria cordis nostri & omnia sacra mundatum iri.

## 29:13
Verse 13. YOU SHALL TAKE ALSO THE WHOLE FAT.

The burning of the fat signified not only the mortification of our concupiscence, but also the offering of Christ himself for us on the altar of the cross, where the victim was offered in place of man, and its fat was consumed upon the altar: because we were to be consumed with our concupiscences by the fire of divine wrath, but since Christ was offered in our stead, it is right to mortify our concupiscences, while we ourselves are preserved safe. The fat, says Theodoret, q. 61 in Exod. the pleasures lurking beneath the belly: the lobe of the liver, the irascible power of the soul: for to this adheres the receptacle of bile. He commands all these to be sacrificed, and their wicked actions to be given as it were to death: but as our old Adam was crucified in Christ, so also in the same all these have been abolished: because He, void of them, offered Himself for us as a sacrifice of sweet fragrance, and in our stead made the incense of His body ascend before God. Which mortification is necessary for all men, but especially for the ministers of the word, who ought to be a pattern for others,

Latin:

Vers. 13. SUMES ET ADIPEM TOTUM.

Adipis incensio significabat non tantum nostræ concupiscentiæ mortificationem, sed etiam ipsius Christi pro nobis in ara crucis oblationem, qua hominis loco victima offerebatur, ejusque adeps super altari consumebatur: quia nos cum concupiscentiis nostris igne iræ divinæ consum- debebamus, Christo autem nostri vice oblato mor- tificare tamen concupiscentias fas est, dum ipsi nos salvi conservamur. Adeps, inquit Theodoret. q.61. in Exod. ventriculum tegens morbum gulæ significat: renes autem voluptates sub ventre latentes: fibra vero epatis irascibilem animi vim: huic enim adhæret re- ceptaculum bilis. Quæ omnia sacrificare jubet, & eorum improbas actiones veluti morti dare: ut autem in Christo vetus noster Adam crucifixus est, sic etiam in eodem omnia hæc abolita sunt: quia ipse expers eorum se pro nobis obtulit hostiam bonæ fragrantiæ, & nostri vice suffimentum cor- poris sui coram Deo fecit ascendere. Quæ morti- ficatio cum omnibus hominibus, tum imprimis verbi ministris, qui aliorum typus esse debent, ne- cessaria est,

## 29:14
Vers. 14. YOU SHALL BURN OUTSIDE THE CAMP.

They were to burn the flesh of the calf and the dung outside, in testimony of the wrath of God against sins, who willed that sacrifices be consumed even to the dregs, and commanded that this be done outside the camp for the detestation of sins, and by that wished to indicate the magnitude of the sin of the Priests: for whom the calf was also to be sacrificed, when for the sins of the princes and the common people lesser animals were offered, goats or rams. Hence in type of Christ, who willed to take this ignominy upon Himself, and to suffer outside the city, Heb. 13, 11. But the priests were to be expiated in such a way, as those who, being about to expiate others, ought not to be left in their sins, if indeed it pleased God to use the ministry of such as were not themselves immune from sins, but stood in need of expiation.

Latin:

Vers. 14. COMBURES FORIS EXTRA CASTRA.

Carnes vituli & fimum foris comburere debe- bant, in testimonium iræ Dei adversus peccata, qui sacrificia volebat ad feces usque consumi, & ad de- testationem peccatorum id fieri jubebat extra castra, eoque indicare voluit magnitudinem peccati Sacer- dotum: pro quibus immolandus etiam erat vitulus, quum pro peccatis principum & plebejorum mino- ra offerrentur animalia, capræ vel arietes. Dehinc in typum Christi, qui ignominiam hanc in se reci- pere, & extra urbem pati voluit Ebr. 13, 11. Expi- andi autem ita erant sacerdotes, utpote qui alios expiaturi non in peccatis relinqui debebant, siqui- dem Deo placuerit talium ministerio uti, qui ipsi à peccatis immunes non erant, sed expiatione in- digebant.

## 29:16
Vers. 16. YOU SHALL TAKE OF ITS BLOOD, AND POUR IT AROUND THE ALTAR] That blood is poured on the altar, says Servius on 2. Georg. Lucian, book on sacrifices, pouring the blood around the altar. See also Lev. 1, 5. 17, 6.

These things do not serve here otherwise than to teach the bad zeal of the Gentiles in their own not-at-all-sacred rites, and the diabolical illusion of the rites of the Lord.

Latin:

Vers. 16. TOLLES DE SANGUINE EJUS, ET FUNDES CIRCA ALTARE] Sanguinem in ara fundi, ait Servius ad 2. Georg. Lucianus l. de sacrificiis, τὸ ἅιμα τῷ βωμῷ περιχέων. Vid. & Lev. 1, 5. 17, 6.

Ista non aliter huc faciunt, quam ut doceatur κακοζηλία gentilium in ipsorum sacris minime sa- cris, & illusio sacrorum Domini diabolica.

## 29:18
Vers. 18. AND YOU SHALL OFFER THE WHOLE RAM AS A BURNT OFFERING UPON THE ALTAR.

In this second sacrifice, namely the burnt offering, it was peculiar that the victim, cut into parts with the intestines washed and the head placed upon the altar, ascended whole to God, nor was anything left of it for the priest except the skin: by which some wish to shadow forth Christ, who after He offered Himself to GOD ascended whole into heaven: or also the entire oblation and consecration of our bodies and souls, and especially regarding those who are initiated into sacred things. By the division of the parts, says Pelargus, the right cutting of the word of truth is without doubt shadowed forth: by the washing of the intestines, the purgation of all things interior: by the burnt offering itself, the complete or entire consecration and oblation of our bodies and souls.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET OFFERES TOTUM ARIETEM IN- CENSUM SUPER ALTARI.

In hoc sacrificio altero, nempe holocausto id fuit peculiare, quod hostia in partes secta cum inte- stinis lotis omnibus & capite altari imposita tota ad Deum ascendit, nec quicquam ex ea relictum sa- cerdoti sit præter pellem: qua adumbratum volunt nonnulli Christum, qui postquam DEO se obtulit totus ascendit in cœlum: aut etiam integram cor- porum animorumque nostrorum & imprimis quo- ad eos, qui sacris initiantur, oblationem, & conse- crationem. Divisione partium, inquit Pelargus ὀρ- θοτομία verbi veritatis dubio procul adumbrata est: in- testinorum ablutione interiorum omnium purgatio: holocausto ipso ἐντελὴς sive integra corporum animo- rumque nostrorum consecratio & oblatio.

## 29:20
Vers. 20. YOU SHALL PUT IT UPON THE TIP OF THE EAR.

In the third initiatory sacrifice, which was a peace offering, the right ears and the thumbs of the hands and feet of the Priests had to be anointed, so that it might be signified that all the sufficiency and aptitude of pious ministers flows from the blood, that is, the death and merit of Christ, who prepares both the ears for perceiving the word and the thumbs for sacred actions, by His sprinkled blood, so that they may rightly perform their office.

Latin:

Vers. 20. PONES SUPER EXTREMUM AURICULÆ.

In tertio sacrificio initiatorio, quod erat paci- ficatorium inungi debuerunt Sacerdotum auriculæ dextræ & pollices manuum & pedum, ut significare- tur à sanguine, id est, morte & merito Christi omnem piorum ministrorum sufficientiam & aptitudinem di- manare, qui tum aures verbo percipiendo, tum polli- ces actionibus sacris præparat, asperso suo sanguine, ut officio recte fungantur.

## 29:22
Vers. 22. AND THE RIGHT SHOULDER, BECAUSE IT IS THE RAM OF CONSECRATION.

before

In Hebrew: of completion. The reason is given why the right shoulder, which later fell to the share of the Priest in peace offerings, had to be burned here, namely because this sacrifice is of the Priest's initiation. For since the Priests were then being sanctified for the first time, they did not receive those parts which were otherwise owed to them in the sacrifices of the people, in which the right shoulder fell to the High Priest and his sons, but the breast fell to the remaining Priests: here, however, the right shoulder was to be burned to GOD, and the breast was to be left to Moses, who was then performing the office of Priest: the rest of the victim, which in other peace offerings was then to fall to the people, was left to Aaron and his sons, so that they might eat those meats, because their condition then was such as that of the offering people later. Therefore, this second ram was presented here before the Lord and slaughtered by Moses, who with its blood would touch the lower ear and the thumbs of the Priests, and sprinkle the altar, and the Priests themselves and their garments: but when the parts were divided, he would place one with the libation and the drink offering into the hands of Aaron and his sons for waving before the Lord, until it was burned; he would reserve the breast for his own private use, and would burn the right shoulder with the fat and the sacrificial gift to GOD as a whole burnt offering.

Moreover, by that waving of the breast and lifting up of the shoulder, we are warned before GOD that we must be vigilant with our whole heart and work, with a spirit always aroused. By the distribution of the parts, the communion of the Saints with GOD is indicated. But it is not without mystery that the tail of the victim is also commanded to be offered to the Lord on the altar, so that, namely, we may also complete every good thing that we begin with the end of perseverance.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ARMUMQUE DEXTRUM EO QUOD SIT ARIES CONSECRATIONIS.

ante

In Hebræo: impletionis. Causa redditur, cur armus dexter, qui postea cessit in partem Sacerdotis in Sacrificiis pacificis, hic cremari debuerit, quia nempe hoc sacrificium est initiationis Sacerdotis. Quoniam enim tum primum sanctificabantur Sacerdotes, non accipiebant partes illas, quæ ipsis alias debebantur in sacrificiis populi, in quibus armus dexter summo Sacerdoti & filiis ejus, pectus vero reliquis Sacerdotibus cedebat: hic vero armus dexter DEO cremandus, & pectus Mosi, qui tum munere Sacerdotis fungebatur, relinquendum erat: reliquum hostiæ, quod in aliis sacrificiis pacificis deinde populo cedere debebat, Aaroni & filiis relinquebatur, ut carnes illas comederent, quia conditio eorum talis tum fuit, qualis postea populi offerentis. Sistebatur ergo hic aries alter coram Domino & mactabatur à Mose, qui sanguine ejus imam auriculam, & pollices Sacerdotum tangeret, aram aspergeret, & Sacerdotes ipsos eorumque vestes: partibus vero divisis unam cum libatione & libamento manibus Aaronis & filiorum imponeret in agitationem coram Domino, donec adoleretur; pectus in usum privatum sibi reservaret, armum dextrum cum adipe & dapali munere DEO in holocaustum incenderet.

Agitatione autem illa pectoris & exaltatione armi, coram DEO monemur, toto pectore & opere invigilandum esse, excitato semper animo. Partium distributione indicata communio Sanctorum cum DEO. Sed nec mysterio vacat, quod cauda etiam hostiæ in altari Domino offerri præcipitur, ut scil. omne bonum, quod incipimus, etiam perseverantiæ fine impleamus.

## 29:24
AND YOU SHALL SANCTIFY THEM] Rather, those things offered, of course. ἀφοριεῖς αὐτὰ [you shall separate them] LXX. But the Hebrew word properly signifies waving to the right and to the left; just as that which is done forward and backward is תרומה [heave offering]. By these motions, GOD's dominion over all parts of the world was signified.

Grotius rightly corrects the Vulgate here: for in the Hebrew it is 'you shall lift them up,' namely those things which are offered, not 'them,' that is, the Priests. For how would they have been lifted up? I say, the discourse is about the offerings, not about the Priests. Moses is commanded to place those things in the hands of the Priests, and to wave them in that way through their ministry: which he later receiving from their hands burned before the Lord. He also deservedly corrects the version of the LXX Interpreters, ἀφοριεῖς αὐτὰ. Because the Hebrew word signifies waving; which some wish to be expressed by this word Tenupha when done to the right and to the left, but by the word Theruma that which is done forward and backward, Exod. 25. v. 2. Others, however, prefer to hold them as synonyms, and think that waving done in any direction is expressed by both. But the meaning of that waving is less correctly held than Grotius hands it down: namely, that GOD's dominion over all parts of the world was shadowed forth by it. For since sacrifices were shadows of THINGS TO COME, and prefigured the sacrifice of Christ, most Christian Interpreters explain this waving better regarding the efficacy of Christ's sacrifice, which extends to the whole world. Some, with Lyranus, observe that the aforementioned ventilation, by which the victims were first lifted upward, then drawn back downward, and then led toward the East and West, to the North and South, was done in the manner of a Cross, and that the cross of Christ was figured by it. Some add a moral meaning: that by the waving of the breast and the lifting up of the shoulder, we were warned that we must be vigilant with our whole heart and work in divine matters, with a spirit always aroused; the elevation was made for this reason, so that it might be hinted that upward hearts are to be lifted up: which here proves itself to Rivetus in his Commentary on this passage.

Latin:

ET SANCTIFICABIS EOS] Imo ea oblata scilicet. ἀφοριεῖς αὐτὰ LXX. Sed vox Hebræa proprie agitationem significat dextrorsum, & sinistrorsum; Sicut quæ prorsum & retrorsum fit est תרומה. His motionibus significabatur DEI dominium in omnes mundi partes.

Recte corrigit hic Grotius Vulgatam: In Hebræo enim est elevabis ea, scilicet quæ offeruntur, non eos, id est, Sacerdotes. Qui enim illi elevandi fuissent? De oblatis, inquam, sermo est non de Sacerdotibus. Illa jubetur Moses ponere in manibus Sacerdotum, & ea ita agitare per eorum ministerium: quæ postea ex eorum manibus accipiens adolevit coram Domino. Corrigit etiam merito LXX. Interpp. versionem ἀφοριεῖς αὐτὰ. Quia vox Ebræa agitationem significat; quam dextrorsum & sinistrorsum factam exprimi nonnulli hac voce Tenupha volunt, voce vero Theruma eam, quæ prorsum & retrorsum fit, Exod. 25. v. 2. alii tamen malunt ea pro Synonymis habere, ac agitationem quaquaversum factam utraque exprimi putant. Significatio vero agitationis illius minus recte se habet, quam tradit Grotius: DEI nempe Dominium in omnes mundi partes eadem adumbratum fuisse. Quum enim Sacrificia umbræ FUTURORUM fuerint, & Christi sacrificium præfigurarint, melius Interpp. Christiani plerique hanc agitationem de sacrificii Christi efficacia, quæ ad totum mundum se porrigit, explicant. Prædictam ventilationem, qua elevabantur primo victimæ sursum, postea retrahebantur deorsum, & deinde deducebantur versus Orientem & Occidentem ad Aquilonem & Meridiem, in modum Crucis factam, eaque figuratam esse crucem Christi, nonnulli cum Lyrano observant. Addunt quidam moralem significationem: Agitatione pectoris, & armi exaltatione monitos nos fuisse, toto pectore & opere invigilandum esse divinis, excitato semper animo; ideo elevatio facta, ut innueretur, sursum elevanda esse corda: quæ hic sese probat Riveto in Commentar. ad h. l.

## 29:26
Verse 26. AND YOU SHALL TAKE THE BREAST.

These things which are contained in verses 26, 27, and 28 do not pertain to that first initiation of Aaron performed by Moses, but concern the perpetual law regarding the right of the Priests in the Sacrifices: that the breast and the right shoulder ought to fall to them, so that it might be noted that the Priests are established in the place of GOD, since the best parts, which were owed to Him, are assigned to them in the victim as ministers of GOD, and the Priests are admonished that those parts are the most excellent, and that it is their duty to excel others, and to be as it were the breast and shoulders of the people, to provide for them and as it were to sustain them. Concerning which see Gregory the Great, part 1, book 2 of the Pastoral Care, chapter 3. Moralia, chapter 80: by divine law the Priest receives the right shoulder for a sacrifice, and it is set apart, so that his work may not only be useful, but also singular, and that he may not only do what is right among the wicked, but that he may also lead his subjects to do such things, just as he surpasses them in the honor of his order, so he should also transcend them in the manner of his virtues, to whom in the eating also the breast is given with the shoulder, so that he may learn to sacrifice himself as the author of that which he is commanded to take from the sacrifice. From these things, however, the Apostle draws that moral lesson in 1 Corinthians 9:13, that those who serve the Gospel should live from the Gospel.

Latin:

Vers. 26. SUMESQUE PECTUSCULUM.

Hæc quæ v. 26. 27. 28. habentur, non ad illam primam initiationem Aaronis à Mose factam per- tinent, sed legem perpetuam concernunt de jure Sa- cerdotum in Sacrificiis: quod ipsis cedere debeant pectus, & armus dexter, ut ita notaretur Sacerdotes DEI loco constitui, quum partes optimæ, quæ ei de- bebantur, in victima ipsis ceu ministris DEI assi- gnentur, & admoneantur Sacerdotes, quod illæ partes sint præstantissimæ, quod officii eorum sit, ut præstent præ aliis, & pectus quasi sint & humeri populi, qui ei prævideant & eum veluti sustineant. De quo Gregor. M. part. 1. 2. pastor. c. 3. l. 1. Mo- ral. c. 80. divina lege armum Sacerdos dextrum in sacrificium accipit, & separatum, ut non solum sit ejus operatio utilis, sed etiam singularis, neque inter malos tantummodo, quæ recta sunt, faciat, sed talia quoque operantes subditos, sicut honore ordinis superat, ita etiam more virtutum transcendat, cui in esu quo- que pectusculum cum armo tribuitur, ut quod de sa- crificio præcipitur sumere, hoc de semetipso auctore discat immolare. Ex hisce autem illud morale col- ligit Apostolus 1. Cor. 9. v. 13. ut qui Evangelio ser- viunt, ex Evangelio vivant.

## 29:30
Verse 30. HE SHALL USE IT FOR SEVEN DAYS.

This treats of the Holy garment of the successors of Aaron, lest anyone think it was proper to Aaron alone: and seven continuous days are set before their consecration, not because he ought to use the same garment only on those seven days, in which he certainly ought to walk whenever he ministered to God, but because it must be used in that continuous seven-day period until the consecration is completed, nor was he to depart from the tabernacle during all those seven days, Leviticus 8:33. By the septenary number of days, as a perfect one, he was warned to dedicate the whole course of his life continuously to GOD. However, the garments were not sprinkled anew on each day, but both the anointing and their sprinkling were done once.

Latin:

Vers. 30. SEPTEM DIEBUS UTETUR ILLA.

De veste Sancta successorum Aaronis hic agi- tur, ne quis putet eam soli Aaroni propriam fuisse: ac septem dies continui eorum consecrationi præfi- guntur, non quod septem illis diebus tantum ea- dem veste uti debeat, quibus utique debebat ince- dere, quoties Deo ministrabat, sed quod in illo septiduo continuo eadem utendum sit, donec con- secratio compleatur, neque in totis illis septem diebus recedendum ipsi erat à tabernaculo, Levit. 8. vers. 33. Per numerum autem septenarium die- rum ceu perfectum, monebatur totum vitæ suæ curriculum DEO continue addicere. Non au- tem singulis diebus aspergebantur de novo vestes, sed semel facta est & unctio & adspersio eorum.

## 29:31
Verse 31. AND YOU SHALL TAKE THE RAM OF CONSECRATION.

Now it treats of the feasts which followed the peace offerings. Concerning that ram of consecration, by which the Priests were consecrated, the remaining parts of which, except for the fat, the right shoulder, and the breast, they were to cook before the doors of the tabernacle with fire not sent from heaven, but common fire, and were to eat with the sacred breads which had been brought in the basket, when a part had been burned, it fell rather to the use of those offering for the Sacred feasts. Thus also GOD provided for the Priests, who served the sacred rites for seven whole days, and took care that they should not fall to any but holy persons, because they were consecrated to God: and therefore it is added

Latin:

Vers. 31. ARIETEM AUTEM CONSECRA- TIONIS TOLLIT.

Jam de epulis agitur, quæ sequebantur sa- crificia pacifica. De ariete consecrationis illo, quo Sacerdotes consecrabantur, cujus partes re- siduas exceptis adipibus, armo dextro, & pecto- re, ante fores tabernaculi coquere igne non cœlitus demisso, sed communi, & comedere debe- bant cum sacris panibus, qui in canistro allati fue- rant, quum pars incensa fuerat, potius in usum offerentium ad epulas Sacras cedebat. Ita & pro- spiciebat DEUS Sacerdotibus, qui per integros septem dies inserviebant sacris & præcavebat, ne aliis quam sanctis personis ea cederent, quia Deo sa- crata erant: ideoque additur

## 29:33
Verse 33. A STRANGER SHALL NOT EAT OF THEM] זָר ἅλλογε- νής. He is to be understood here who is not of the blood of Aaron, as also below in verse 33.

Which seems to be understood in such a way that those who are not of the family of Aaron, Numbers 16:40, may not eat of them (as the interpreters easily agree). To whom alone these sacred meats of the sacrifices were granted: therefore the reason was subjoined: because they are holy: where the Vulgate is also to be corrected, when it renders it, that it may be a placable sacrifice: since it ought to have rendered it, by which expiation was made, because this is the reason why they ought to be eaten by the Priests alone, since they were offered as a peace offering; but the end is not indicated, namely that they might be a placable sacrifice. For by the eating they did not become a placable sacrifice. Which was also the reason why, if anything remained until the next day, it had to be consumed by fire; therefore, the holiness of those meats which were offered for the consecration of the Priests was greater than in other sacrifices which were made for a vow or voluntarily: for it was permitted to eat of these even on the second day, Lev. 7. verse 16. The purpose of this matter, however, was that no corruption might creep in which would infect the worship of God or render it contemptible.

Latin:

Vers. 33. ALIENIGENA NON EDET EX EIS] זָר ἅλλογε- νής. Intelligendus, hic qui non est ex sanguine Aaronis, ut & infra 30. v. 33.

Quod videtur ita accipiendum, ut qui non sunt de familia Aaronis, Num. 16, 40. de iis non comedant. (uti consentiunt facile interpp.) Qui- bus solis hæ sacræ carnes sacrificiorum concede- bantur: ideo ratio subjuncta fuit: quia sacrata sunt: ubi corrigenda etiam vulgata, cum reddit, ut sit pla- cabile sacrificium: siquidem reddere debuerit, per quæ expiatio facta est, quia hæc causa est, cur à Sa- cerdotibus solis comedi debeant, siquidem obla- ta fuerint in sacrificium pacificum; non vero finis indicatur, nempe ut essent placabile sacrificium. Nam per comestionem non fiebant placabile sacrificium. Quæ etiam causa fuit, cur si quid in crastinum re- manserit, igne comburi debuerit, major itaque fuit sanctitas illarum carnium, quæ pro consecratio- ne Sacerdotum offerebantur, quam in aliis sacrifi- ciis, quæ fiebant pro voto, vel sponte: nam de his etiam secundo die comedere licebat Lev. 7. vers. 16. Finis autem ejus rei fuit, ne qua obreperet corruptela, quæ cultum Dei inficeret, vel redderet contemptibilem.

## 29:36
Verse 36. AND YOU SHALL CLEANSE THE ALTAR WHEN YOU HAVE SACRIFICED THE SIN OFFERING.

In the cleansing of the altar, which was now being done for the first time, so that, namely, sin might not be committed in its very use, and that the altar itself might render the gift or offering holy, Matth. 23. verse 29, and might remind them that GOD did not wish victims to be offered to Him in any other place than that which was once consecrated to His name, 2. Reg. 16. verses 11, 12, Ezech. 16. verse 24, and thus might prefigure another altar uniquely pleasing to GOD and consecrated by GOD, of which Heb. 13. verse 10. That young bull was a sacrifice by which the Priests were consecrated, above in verse 10. By which sacrifices the altar also had to be expiated, verse 37. But whether the offerings of the young bull and those two rams had to be repeated during those seven days of the consecration of the Priest and the expiation of the altar, which Bonfrerius thinks, does not appear from the text: rather, since mention is made here only of the young bull, it does not seem to be established that the offering of the rams had to be repeated on each day. Josephus reports that a bull and a ram were sacrificed on alternate days. But that does not agree with this passage, which teaches that only a calf was to be offered on each day.

Latin:

Vers. 36. MUNDABISQUE ALTARE CUM IMMO- LAVERIS HOSTIAM EXPIATIONIS.

In mundatione altaris, quæ nunc primum fie- bat, ne scilicet in ipsius usu committatur peccatum, & ut donum vel oblationem sanctam redderet ipsum altare Matth. 23. vers. 29. ac commoneret, nolle DEUM alio loco sibi offerri victimas, quam illo nomini suo semel consecrato, 2. Reg. 16. vers. 11. 12. Ezech. 16. vers. 24. adeoque figuraret aliud DEO unice gratum, & à DEO consecra- tum altare, de quo Ebr. 13. vers. 10. Sacrificium erat ille juvencus, quo consecrabantur Sacerdo- tes supra versu 10. Quibus sacrificiis etiam ex- piandum erat altare versu 37. An autem per se- ptem illos dies consecrationis Sacerdotis, & expiatio- nis altaris, & juvenci, & arietum illorum duorum oblationes repetendæ fuerint, quod Bonfrerius exi- stimat, è textu non apparet: quin potius, quum juvenci solius mentio hic fiat, arietum oblationem repetendam singulis diebus fuisse haud statuendum videtur. Josephus alternis diebus taurum & arie- tem immolatum esse tradit. Sed id huic loco non convenit, qui solum vitulum diebus singulis offe- rendum fuisse docet.

## 29:37
Verse 37. AND IT SHALL BE MOST HOLY.

That is, most holy, in the customary Hebrew phrase. Therefore it is added, everything that (the Vulgate has, everyone who) touches it shall be sanctified. It is not a matter of persons, as if only sacred persons ought to touch or approach the altar, but the reason is given why the altar is called most holy: because through it the gifts themselves are also sanctified, as Christ interprets in Matth. XXIII. verse 29, not that the altar has any power of sanctifying in itself, but by divine institution, it is a moral cause of sanctification, not only because of the relation to the sacrifice to be offered there to GOD, but primarily because of the nature of the type, because, namely, through our altar, when we offer gifts upon it, all things are sanctified, which is truly the holy of holies, Heb. 13. v. 10. Nor is there any reason for anyone to say, if unclean things were offered on the altar, that they were not sanctified by it, because the altar did not sanctify the gifts by itself, but by divine institution; therefore it is no wonder that it did not sanctify those things which were offered against the divine institution.

Latin:

Vers. 37. ET ERIT SANCTUM SANCTORUM.

Id est, sanctissimum, phrasi consueta Ebræa. Ideo additur omne quod (vulg. habet, omnis qui) tetigerit illud, sanctificabitur. Non de personis agitur, quasi sacræ tantum personæ altare tangere vel ac- cedere debeant, sed causa redditur, cur altare san- ctissimum dicatur? quia per illud etiam dona ipsa sanctificantur, interprete Christo Matth. XXIII. versu 29. non quod altare vim sanctificandi ali- quam habeat, sed ex instituto divino, causa mora- lis sit sanctificationis non solum propter relatio- nem ad sacrificium ibi DEO offerendum, sed im- primis ob typi rationem, quia nempe per altare nostrum, cum in illo offerimus dona, omnia san- ctificantur, quod vere sanctum sanctorum est Ebr. 13. v. 10. Nec est, quod quis dicat, si res immundæ oblatæ in altari, eas non sanctificatas fuisse per il- lud, quia altare dona non per se sanctificavit, sed ex instituto divino, ideo non mirum, quod ea non sanctificavit, quæ contra institutum divinum offe- rebantur.

## 29:38
Verse 38. THIS IS WHAT YOU SHALL DO ON THE ALTAR.

Junius and Tremellius render it 'you shall offer': but the general word 'you shall do' is more correctly retained. For although the species of the act is expressed afterward, which is an offering, when it deals with the daily or continual sacrifice, that word עשׂה is nevertheless general in itself: so here also it must be rendered generally: lest the Papists seize from this an opportunity to confirm their Mass-sacrifice from the words of the Supper: which argument, however, is refuted by Estius himself on 1. Cor. 11: The word, he says, 'do this,' is not the same as 'sacrifice,' as some have interpreted against the mind of Scripture. For in that which is said in the Canon: As often as you shall do this, you shall do it in memory of me, to do can by no means be explained as to sacrifice, except in a forced manner. Blessed Luther rightly: And that you should do with (on) the altar. But if anyone should drag the following words, you shall make yearling lambs, here, the Athnach accent interposed and the absence of the accusative sign stand in the way: and therefore those words seem rather to be supplied from the following: But this is what you shall do to the altar, two yearling lambs daily, one lamb you shall make in the morning &c. Furthermore, that those are to be explained thus: You shall make a lamb, that is, you shall offer, is because from the added sacrifice there, the force and that special meaning of the verb is gathered. Let the Mass-makers therefore prove that that 'This', in the words of the Lord, 'do this', is a sacrifice, before they assume the verb 'to do' is 'to offer', since it is certain that Christ is not speaking of the thing to be offered, but of the whole action which the Apostle had preceded.

Verse of the same. TWO YEARLING LAMBS.

Because it has dealt with the priests and the altar being initiated, it now deals with the sacrifice to be offered upon the altar, in which the principal use of the altar consisted: since some sacrifices were ordinary, others extraordinary, and those were either daily, or Sabbatical, or annual. For the daily one, which the Greeks call ἐνδελεχισμὸν, and which Josephus testifies was offered at public expense, lib. 3. c. 10, because it had to be performed on every single day, even if they were feast days, Numbers 28:10, there was need of a yearling lamb, and that whole and without blemish, with the offering of Mincha from fine flour, oil, and wine for a libation, by which a pleasing savor might be offered to the sacrifices, or rather it might be noted that faith and repentance were to be brought to them, which are pleasing to GOD, because there was a daily need for the people to be reconciled to GOD, and to betake themselves continually to his mercy and the expiation of Christ, who was daily figured to them by that lamb, John 1:29. St. Cyprian, book 2. Epistle 3 to Caecilius teaches that the evening lamb signified Christ's death on the cross and the time of his death: because he died and was offered in the evening. Compare Daniel 9:27.

Latin:

Vers. 38. HOC EST, QUOD FACIES IN ALTARI.

Junius & Tremell. reddunt offeres: sed rectius generalis vox facies retinetur. Nam quamvis deinde species facti exprimatur, quod sit oblatio, cum de quotidiano vel jugi sacrificio agitur, ver- bum tamen illud עשׂה ut in se generale est: ita hic etiam generaliter reddendum: ne Pontificii hinc sacrificium suum Missaticum è verbis cœnæ con- firmandi ansam arripiant: quod argumentum ta- men ab ipso Estio 1. Cor. 11. reprobatur: Verbum, inquit, hoc, facite, non est idem quod sacrificate, quo- modo nonnulli interpretati sunt contra mentem Scri- pturæ. Nam in eo, quod in Canone dicitur: Hoc quo- tiescunque feceritis, in mei memoriam facie- tis, facere nequaquam nisi coacte pro sacrificare potest exponi. Beat. Luther. recte: Und das solt du mit (auf) dem Altar thun. Si autem verba sequentia agnos anniculos quis huc trahat, facies agnos, obstat accentus Athnach interjectus, & signi accusativi absentia: ideoque illa verba e sequenti- bus potius videntur supplenda: Hoc est autem quod facies altari, agnos anniculos duos indies, agnum unum facies mane &c. Porro quod illa sic expli- canda: Agnum facies, id est, offeres, inde est, quod illic ex addito sacrificio vis, & significatio illa ver- bi specialis colligatur. Probent ergo Missifices, illud Hoc, in verbis Domini, hoc facite, esse sacri- ficium, priusquam assumant verbum facere esse offerre, quum certum sit, Christum non de re offe- renda, sed de tota actione, qua Apostolus præive- rat, loqui.

Vers. eod. AGNOS ANNICULOS DUOS.

Quia de Sacerdotibus & altari initiandis actum, jam de Sacrificio super altari offerendo agit, in quo præcipuus erat altaris usus: siquidem alia sacrificia fuerint ordinaria, alia extraordinaria, & illa vel quotidiana, vel Sabbataria, vel anniversa- ria. Ad quotidianum, quod ἐνδελεχισμὸν Græci vocant, quodque publicis impensis oblatum fuisse testatur Josephus lib. 3. c. 10. quia singulis diebus, etiamsi festi essent, peragendum erat Numer. 28, 10. agno anniculo, eoque integro & immaculato opus erat, cum oblatione Mincha ex simila, oleo, & vi- no ad libandum, quo gratus sapor ad sacrificia of- ferretur, vel notaretur potius, fidem & pœnitentiam ad ea adferendam, quæ DEO grata, quia populo opus quotidie fuit, ut DEO reconciliaretur, & jugiter ad ejus misericordiam, & expiationem Christi, qui per agnum illum quotidie ipsis figura- batur Joh. 1, 29. se reciperet. S. Cyprianus l. 2. Ep. 3. ad Cæcil. docet agnum vespertinum signasse Christi mortem in cruce & tempus mortis: quia sub vesperam mortuus & oblatus est. Conf. Dan. 9, 27.

## 29:39
Verse 39. IN THE EVENING] That is, at the ninth hour: as Josephus explains in Antiquities of the Jews, book 14, 8. By this morning and evening sacrifice, God is acknowledged as the creator of night and day.

By this morning and evening sacrifice, God is acknowledged as the creator of night and day, says Grotius. We desire that, because he makes rare or no mention in explaining these significations of the sacrifice of Christ, which is the principal one, as the Apostle testifies, Colossians 2 and Hebrews 10. The morning and evening sacrifice to be presented to GOD in the morning and evening foreshadows the sacrifice of Christ, to whom it is necessary to attribute both the remission of sins and our salutary preservation; so that there may be a constant memory of it among the faithful, and it may be constantly presented to God, for which alone we are acceptable to GOD, in which one alone all grace and salvation is obtained. Therefore, a lamb had to be offered in this constant sacrifice, so that Christ, that lamb of GOD, might be presented, who takes away the sin of the world, John 1, verse 29. For the people had to exercise themselves daily in the memory of the future expiation through Christ, and not forget it either morning or evening, so that they might think again and again that they had need of reconciliation, and thus, being reminded of their guilt and condemnation, might continually flee to the mercy of God, through and because of the sacrifice of the Messiah. The oracle of Daniel 9, verse 27, expressed this end not obscurely, where it indicated the completion of the constant sacrifice thus: (The Messiah) shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the middle of the week the victim and the sacrifice shall fail; or he shall cause the constant sacrifice to cease and

Mincha, because the shadow ceases when the body arrives. It is a wonder that he did not seek the sacrifice of the Mass here with the Papists. But he saw without doubt that the constant sacrifice ought to cease in the New Testament, by the force of the cited oracle. Nor can the Mass be celebrated morning and evening, according to the Papal institution: and therefore they are in vain who seek the Mass here in the constant sacrifice.

Latin:

Vers. 39. VESPERE] Id est, hora nona: ut explicat Jose- phus Antiquæ historiæ lib. 14, 8. Matutino hoc & vespertino sacrificio agnoscitur Deus noctis & diei creator.

Matutino hoc & vespertino sacrificio agnosci Deum noctis & diei creatorem, ait Grotius. Id desideramus, quod raram aut nullam in hisce significationibus explicandis mentionem sacrificii Christi, quæ præ- cipua est, teste Apostolo Coloss. 2. & Ebr. 10. faciat. Matutinum & vespertinum sacrificium mane & vesperi DEO sistendum Christi sacrificium adum- brat, cui & remissionem peccatorum & conserva- tionem nostram salutarem acceptam ferre opor- tet; ut jugis ejus sit memoria penes fideles, jugiter- que id Deo sistatur, ob quod unice DEO accepti sumus, in quo uno omnis gratia & salus obtinetur. Ideo agnus offerendus erat in jugi hoc sacrificio, ut Christus agnus ille DEI sisteretur, qui tollit pecca- tum mundi Joh. 1. vers. 29. Debebat enim populus quotidie se in memoria futuræ per Christum ex- piationis exercere, ejusque nec mane nec vesperi oblivisci, ut identidem sibi opus esse reconcilia- tione cogitaret, adeoque reatus ac damnationis suæ admonitus jugiter ad misericordiam Dei, per & propter sacrificium, Messiæ, confugeret. Ex- pressit hunc finem non obscure oraculum Dan. 9. v. 27. ubi complementum sacrificii jugis ita indica- vit: Confirmabit (Messias) pactum multis hebdoma- da una: & in dimidio hebdomadis deficiet hostia & sacrificium; vel cessare faciet juge sacrificium &

Mincha, quia adventante corpore ceffat umbra. Mirum, quod hîc cum Papiftis non quæfiverit facrificium Missæ. Sed vidit fine dubio cessare debere in Nov. Test. sacrificium juge, vi adducti oraculi. Nec Missam mane & vesperi celebrari posse, ex instituto Papali: adeoque frustra esse, qui hîc in jugi sacrificio Missam quærunt.

## 29:40
Verse 40. THE TENTH PART OF FINE FLOUR.

The tenth part, namely of an Ephah: that is, a Gomor. Compare Num. 28. verse 5. Exod. 16. v. 36. Epiphanius on weights & measures. A Gomor, he says, is the tenth part of a large measure, i.e., an artaba, which contains seven sextarii and a fifth part of a sextarius. A Gomor contained as much as 43 eggshells and a fifth part of an egg can hold.

WITH BEATEN OIL THAT HAS THE FOURTH PART OF A HIN.

Beaten oil was required, i.e., not expressed by the grinding of a mill, which is usually more impure, but well beaten with a pestle. They hold the measure of the fourth part of a Hin to be 18 eggs and to contain about three pounds: for a Hin contained 72 eggs, or 12 Logim. A Log, however, is a measure of 6 eggs: of Palestine, that is, which are larger than ours.

Latin:

Vers. 40. DECIMAM PARTEM SIMILÆ.

Decimam partem scil. Ephæ: hoc est, Gomor. Conf. Num. 28. vers. 5. Exod. 16. v. 36. Epiphanius de pondere & mens. Gomor, inquit, est decima pars mensuræ magnæ, h. e. artabæ, quæ continet septem sextarios & quintam sextarii partem. Gomor continebat quantum capiunt testæ ovorum 43. & quinta ovi pars.

OLEO TUSO QUOD HABEAT QUARTAM PARTEM HIN.

Oleum contusum requirebatur, h. e. non attritu molæ expressum, quod impurius esse solet, sed pilo bene contusum. Mensuram autem quartæ partis Hin volunt esse 18. ovorum ac continere tres circiter libras: Hin enim continebat 72. ova, sive 12. Logim. Log autem mensura est 6. ovorum: Palestinæ scil. quæ nostris majora.

## 30:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXX.

The altar of incense. The census. The holy oil.

Ver. 1.

YOU SHALL ALSO MAKE AN ALTAR TO BURN INCENSE] Hecataeus also mentions this gilded altar. It is the custom of almost all nations to apply incense to sacred rites, as all things pleasing to men were accustomed to be used in divine honor. For this reason they are called ἀρώματα from ἀράųαι. And Porphyry noted that ϑύειν in its primary meaning was to burn incense, and from there comes the Latin thus. But there was also some use for dispelling the odor from living creatures, and for purifying the air. The mystical meaning is that hearts are to be held upward.

It seemed appropriate to transcribe the entire passage of Grotius: Now we add what we find lacking in it. The first is that here and elsewhere he frequently mixes the profane things of the Gentiles with things divinely instituted. If this were done for the sake of history, so that it might be indicated how the Gentiles emulated the sacred rites of the Jews, or rather, how Satan mocked them through those things which he wished to be adorned for himself among the heathens, as the ape of God, it would not be to be disapproved: but Grotius held both in almost an equal position: namely, instead of mere ceremonies, he not only wished to illustrate divine institutions from those diabolical illusions, but he even sometimes sought the meaning of these from the profane rites of the Gentiles: which is to compare Belial with Christ, the table of demons with the table of the Lord. The second concerns the use of sacred incense in particular, which he also derives from the custom of the Gentiles, because incense was employed, since all things pleasing to men were accustomed to be used in divine honor, and because it was useful for dispelling the stench from living creatures and purifying the air, and lastly, so that the mystical significance might not be passed over, that it indicated that hearts must be held upward. But nothing was employed in divine honor because it was pleasing to men, but because God so ordained it, who bound the people ἀποτόμως to the ceremonies instituted by Himself, so that not even one thing among them might be observed otherwise. Therefore, He wished to be cautious against ἐϑελοϑρησκείαις, lest they should creep in. Nothing was employed except that by which divine Wisdom might intimate a mystical significance, which was then without doubt better known, when the people were taught through shadows and figures, than now, when there is no use for them. But shall we believe that God was so solicitous about dispelling the stench and purifying the air, that he took care to have a special, so precious altar of incense built for himself for this reason, lest that foul smell be troublesome to his nostrils! Away with those rotten absurdities! We have from the Apostle in Eph. 5:2 that those scents looked toward the εὐωδία (fragrance) of Christ, or the pleasing odor of rest, in which alone GOD finds rest. Grotius explains this passage concerning the oblation performed on earth and the expiation, by which God is moved to remit sins for us, in defens. fid. Cathol. de satisf. Christi cap. 10. p. 141. Those odors, therefore, served to flee the stench of sins, but by the power of the oblation made on the altar of the cross, from which comes all the εὐωδία (fragrance) of sacrifices, namely that of the expiatory death of Christ, as also by the power of the incense of prayers, which he offered in the days of our flesh for our sake, Heb. 5:7. The proper meaning here, therefore, is not ἠθικὴ (ethical) concerning the lifting up of hearts, but truly μυστικὴ (mystical) concerning the expiatory sacrifice of Christ and the prayers offered for us, because he was to offer himself into an odor of sweetness on the altar of the cross and by that oblation, as also by his intercession, was to procure the εὐωδία (fragrance) for us by the spiritual scents of the prayers of the faithful. Concerning which David, Psalm 141:2: Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight, the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.

Therefore in Apocal. 5:8, the scents, with which the golden vials are full, are said to be the prayers of the saints. As it is gathered from the cited passage Eph. 5:2 that this looked toward the εὐωδία (fragrance) of the death of Christ, so also it is not obscurely evident from a comparison of Apoc. 8:3, 4, 5 that the incense of the Angel of the covenant, which are the intercessions of the Son of GOD, are figured by them, as being those by which the εὐωδία (fragrance) of our prayers is procured. Moreover, that OTHER Angel with the golden censer is the unique High Priest of the New Testament, Christ, to whom much incense was given, that he might give of the prayers of the saints upon the golden altar, which is before the throne of GOD: because this office was given to him, that he might make the prayers of the saints pleasing and ratified by his intercession: Whence the smoke of the incense from the prayers of the Saints ascends from the hand of that Angel before GOD. It is too clear that the ancient sacred rites look toward the Apocalyptic passage, and Apocal. 8:5 is especially worthy of being compared here with Lev. 16:12, 13. It is not our task to pursue those things. It is certain that the incense of prayers of our High Priest is not pleasing unless it ascends from the hand of the Angel of the covenant, and his incense is added: outside of whom, he who remembers incense is as one who blesses an idol, Isa. 66:3, and the fumigation itself is an abomination to Jehovah, Isa. 1:13.

Thirdly, that Grotius wishes θύειν (to sacrifice) in its primary meaning to be to burn incense is refuted no better than by Grotius himself in defens. fid. Cathol. de satisf. Christi cap. 10. pag. 141. ALL the books of the Greeks and ALL the books of the Latins indicate that a θυσία (sacrifice) is performed when a victim is given to death. Whence it happens that to slaughter signifies both to sacrifice, and also, by a meaning extended from sacrifices to other things, to kill in any way. Hence Ammonius distinguishes between θύειν (to sacrifice) and σφάττεσθαι (to be slaughtered) as the appellations of genus and species. For θύεσθαι (to be sacrificed) is for the sake of honoring a god, but σφάττεσθαι (to be slaughtered) is to be killed for whatever cause. And Plutarch says it was believed by the Gauls and Scythians that the gods are those who rejoice in the blood of slaughtered men, and that this is the most perfect sacrifice. Therefore, there is a sacrifice in the slaughtering. Nor does Scripture speak otherwise on this subject. These things Grotius wrote when he was still standing for the Catholic faith against Socinus, which, as being solid, are still unmoved.

Furthermore, since the brazen altar of holocaust was treated in chapter 27, now the golden altar of fumigation is treated: and it is described by its material, measure, ornament, position, and use, both daily, because it was burned upon morning and evening, and annually on the feast of expiation. In this altar, a shadow of Christ is perceived, whose divinity is figured by gold, his humanity by wood; his empire, which extends through the whole world, by its magnitude and figure; his power and strength by the horns; his firmness, which cannot be shaken, by the square figure; his royal dignity by the crown; his ministry by the staves; his presence by its position; the incense is an image of prayer, Psalm 141:2, Apocal. 5:6, cap. 8:3, which is ordered to be offered when the lamps are trimmed: because prayers are then accepted when the light of faith precedes, especially when they have been stained and sprinkled with the blood of Christ: the fumigation of which is necessary even every single day, morning and evening, Luke 18:1. Thessal. 5:17. The burning coals are our prayers, which are afflictions: and just as Aaron had to offer incense on this altar, so it is necessary that it ascend through the incense of the prayers of Christ alone, Apocal. 8:3. Finally, the altar was sprinkled with the blood of the expiatory victim: Thus no one is pleasing to God in prayer, unless expiation has been made by the blood of Christ, Eph. 1:6.

Whether the golden censer, which the Apostle points out in Heb. 9, was this golden altar? Interpreters are accustomed to inquire here. Some affirm it, and place this altar inside the veil of the Holy of Holies, and say that the high priest entered it every single day twice, morning and evening, to perform the fumigation, even though it was permitted to enter with blood only once a year. But it is certain, both from this chapter Exod. 30:10 compared with Levit. 16, and especially from Heb. 9:7, 25, that it was not permitted for the high priest to enter the Holy of Holies except only once a year: nor do the Hebrews admit that the altar of fumigation is located in the Holy of Holies, which they all constantly place outside the veil. Therefore, by χρυσoῦν θυμιατήριον, Buxtorf understands a special golden censer destined for that end and use, so that the Priest might enter the Holy place with it every year, and he maintains that the Holy of Holies is said to have had a golden censer, not because it was enclosed and kept in it, but because it served this use in the Holy of Holies: since in Siphra, and in Maimonides, and Abarbanel, among other differences between the feast of atonement and others, this is assigned, that on other days the High Priest, about to make an offering of incense, took coals from the altar in a silver censer, and emptied them from it into a golden censer: but on this feast he took the coals from the golden censer, and kept them in it, or entered into the Holy of Holies with it, see Histor. arc. fœd. cap. 5. pag. 76. Anselm, Thomas, and Lyranus do not dissent from this opinion. Others, however, with Origen hom. 6. in Lev. and Abulensis in Exod. 25. verf. 46. prefer to understand the golden altar in Heb. 9. verf. 4. as that which is in Exod. 30. verf. 1. But they deny that it was in the Holy of Holies: they think, however, that it is said to have had the Holy of Holies because that altar was opposite to it: therefore it is also called the altar of the oracle 1. Kings 6, 21. that is, because it was at the oracle, namely, on the exterior wall of the oracle. Conf. Gerhard. in Ebr. 9. v. 3.

Latin:

CAPUT XXX.

Ara thymiamatis. Capitatio. Oleum sanctum.

Vers. 1.

FACIES QUOQUE ALTARE AD ADOLENDUM THYMIAMA] Hujus quoque altaris aurati meminit Hecatæus. Suffitum autem adhibere sacris mos gentium ferme omnium, ut solebant cuncta hominibus grata in divino honore usurpari. Ob id ἀρώματα dicta παρὰ τὸ ἀράųαι. Et ϑύειν primo significatu fuisse suffire notavit Porphyrius, & inde thus Latinum. Sed & usus aderat aliquis ad discutiendum nidorem ex animantibus, purgandumque aërem. Mystica significatio est, sursum habenda corda.

Locum integrum Grotii adscribere visum fuit: Jam quæ in eo desideremus, addimus. Primum est, quod hîc & alias passim prophana Gentilium sacris admisceat divinitus institutis. Quod historiæ si fieret causa, ut quomodo æmulati sint gentiles Judæorum sacra, vel potius, quomodo his illuserit satanas per ea, quæ sibi, ut Dei simia adornari volebat, inter Ethnicos, indicaretur, non improbandum foret: at Grotius parili fere loco utraque habuit: pro nudis nempe ceremoniis, adeoque non illustrare modo è diabolicis istis illusionibus divina instituta voluit, sed significationem etiam horum è gentilium prophanis ritibus quandoque petiit: quod est Belialem cum Christo comparare, mensam Dæmoniorum cum mensa Domini. Alterum concernit usum thymiamatis sacri in specie, quem è more Gentilium etiam derivat, quod adhibitus suffitus, quia cuncta hominibus grata in divino honore consueverint usurpari, & quia utilis erat, ad discutiendum nidorem ex animantibus, purgandumque aërem, novissime ideo, ut ne taceatur mystica significatio, quod sursum habenda esse corda indicarir. At nihil in divino honore adhibitum ideo quod hominibus gratum, sed quod Deus ita ordinarit, qui ἀποτόμως ad ceremonias abs se institutas alligabat populum, ut ne unum quidem in illis secus observaretur. Ideo ἐϑελοϑρησκείαις cautùm voluit, ne illæ irreperent. Nihil adhibitum, nisi quo significationem mysticam divina Sapientia innueret, quæ tum notior sine dubio erat, ubi per umbras & figuras docebatur populus, quam nunc, ubi earum usus nullus est. Num autem credemus adeo solli- citum fuisse Deum de nidore discutiendo & aëre pu- gando, ut peculiarem thymiamatos aram tam pre- tiosam idcirco extrui sibi curaret, ne se. fœtor il- naribus ejus molestus esset! Apage putidas illas in- eptias! Ad εὐωδίαν Christi seu gratum quietis odo- ramentum, cui uni DEUS acquiescit, respexiss odoramenta illa, ab Apostolo habemus Eph. 5, 2 Quem locum de oblatione in terris peracta & ex- piatione, qua Deus ad remittendum nobis peccata mo- vetur, explicat Grotius in defens. fid. Cathol. de satisf. Christi cap. 10. p. 141. Odores ergo illi ad fœ- torem peccatorum fugiendum faciebant, sed vir- tute oblationis in ara crucis factæ, à qua omnis sa- crificiorum εὐωδία, mortis nempe Christi expiato- riæ, ut & virtute thymiamatos precum, quas in die carnis nostræ causa obtulit Ebr. 5, 7. Significatio ita- que propria hîc non est ἠθικὴ de sursum habendis cordibus, sed vere μυστικὴ de Christi sacrificio expia- torio & precibus pro nobis oblatis, quod se in odo- rem suavitatis oblaturus sit in ara crucis & oblatio- ne illa, ut & intercessione sua, pro nobis spirituali- bus odoramentis precibus fidelium τὴν εὐωδίαν conciliaturus. De quibus David Psalm. 141. v. 2. Dirigatur oratio mea sicut incensum in conspectu tuo, elevatio manuum mearum sacrificium vespertinum.

Ideo Apocal. 5, 8. odoramenta, quibus aureæ phialæ plenæ sunt, dicuntur esse orationes sanctorum. Ut ad εὐωδίαν mortis Christi hæc respexisse è loco ad- ducto Eph. 5. v. 2. colligitur, ita & incensa Angeli fœderis, quæ sunt intercessiones Filii DEI, figurata illis esse, utpote quibus incensis orationum nostra- rum εὐωδία conciliatur, è collatione Apoc. 8, 3. 4. 5. haud obscure patet. Angelus autem ille ALIUS cum thuribulo aureo est unicus Nov. Test. Pontifex Christus, cui data sunt incensa multa, ut daret de orationibus sanctorum super altare aureum, quod est ante thronuus DEI: quia datum ei hoc est munus, ut præstet intercessione sua orationes sanctorum gratas & ratas: Unde ascendit fumus incensorum de orationibus Sanctorum de manu Angeli illius coram DEO. Respicere locum Apocalypticum vetera sa- cra nimis luculentum est, & conferri hîc meretur cumprimis Apocal. 8. v. 5. cum Lev. 16, 12. 13. No- strum non est illa persequi. Certum est, nonnisi cum de manu Angeli fœderis ascendunt precum thymiamata nostri Pontificis, ejusque accedunt incensa, grata esse: extra quem qui recordatur thu- ris, est quasi qui benedicit idolo Esa. 66, 3. & suffimen- tum ipsum est abominatio Jehovæ Esa. 1, 13.

Tertio quod Grotius θύειν primo significatu vult esse suffire, non rectius, quam ex ipso Grotio refellitur defens. fid. Cathol. de satisf. Christi cap. 10. pag. 141. Peragi θυσίαν tunc, cùm morti datur hostia, OMNES Græcorum, OMNES Latinorum libri indicant. Unde evenit, ut mactare tum sacrifi- care significet, tum etiam à sacrificiis ad alia porrecta significatione quovis modo interficere. Hinc Am- monius θύειν καὶ σφάττειν distinguit, ut appellatio- nes generis & speciei. Θύεσθαι μὲν γάρ ἐστιν ἐπὶ τιμῇ θεῦ, σφάττεσθαι δὲ τὸ δὶ ἥντινα ἂν αἰτίαν φονεύεσθαι. Et Plutarchus Gallis & Scythis ait creditum, θεὸς εἶναι χαίροντας ἀνθρώπων ΣΦΑΤΤΩΜΕΝΩΝ αἵματι καὶ ταύτην τελειοτάτην ΘΥΣΙΑΝ. Est ergo θυσία ἐν τῷ σφάττεσθαι, in mactatione sacrificium. Neque aliter in hoc argumento loquitur Scriptura. Hæc Gro- tius, cum adhuc staret pro fide Catholica contra Socinum, quæ utpote solida adhuc immota sunt.

Cæterum quum de altari æneo holocausti cap. 27. actum, jam de altari aureo suffimenti tracta- tur: idque à materia, mensura, ornatu, situ, atque usu cum quotidiano, quia mane & vesperi in eo adolebatur, tum anniversario in festo expiationis, describitur. In altari hoc umbra deprehenditur Christi, cujus divinitas auro, humanitas ligno figurata, magnitudine & figura imperium ejus, quod per totum se extendit orbem; cornibus vis atque robur ejus, figura quadrata firmitas, quæ convelli non possit, corona regalis dignitas, vectibus ministerium, situ ejus præsentia; Thymiana imago precationis est Psalm. 141, 2. Apocal. 5, 6. cap. 8, 3. quod offerri jubetur cum lucernæ adornantur: quia tum acceptæ sunt preces, ubi fidei præcedit lumen, imprimis ubi sanguine Christi tinctæ fuerint, atque aspersæ: quarum suffimentum singulis etiam diebus mane & vesperi necessarium est, Luc. 18. verf. 1. 1. Thessal. 5. verf. 17. Carbones inflammantes nostras preces sunt afflictiones: & quemadmodum in hoc altari Aaron incensum offerre debuit, sic per Christi unius precum thymiana ascendere oportet, Apocal. 8. verf. 3. Denique sanguine victimæ expiatoriæ ara aspersa: Sic nemo in oratione Deo placet, nisi sanguine Christi facta sit expiatio, Eph. 1. v. 6.

Num Thuribulum aureum, quod Apostolus Ebr. 9. indigitat, hoc altare aureum fuerit? disquirere hîc solent Interpretes. Quod affirmant nonnulli, & altare hoc locant intra velum Sancti Sanctorum, idque Sacerdotem summum singulis diebus bis, mane & vesperi ad suffitum faciendum ingressum dicunt, etsi cum sanguine non nisi semel in anno ingredi licuerit. Sed non licuisse nisi tantum semel in anno Sacerdoti summo Sanctum sanctorum ingredi, tum è cap. hoc Exod. 30, 10. collato cum Levit. 16. tum imprimis ex Ebr. 9. verf. 7. 25. certum est: neque admittunt Ebræi altare suffitus in Sancto sanctorum locari, quod omnes constanter extra velum ponunt: ideo per χρυσoῦν θυμιατήριον Buxtorsius peculiare thuribulum aureum in eum finem & usum destinatum, ut cum eo Sacerdos quotannis in Sanctum ingrederetur, intelligit, ac Sanctum sanctorum dici habuisse thuribulum aureum vult, non quod in eo fuerit inclusum & asservatum, sed quod huic usui in Sancto sanctorum inserviret: siquidem in Siphra, & apud Maimonidem, atque Abarbanelem inter alias differentias festi expiationis & aliorum hæc assignetur, quod aliis diebus suffitum facturus Pontifex prunas de altari ceperit in thuribulo argenteo, & ex eo illas evacuarit in thuribulum aureum: hoc vero festo decerpserit prunas thuribulo aureo, & in illo eas retinuerit, vel cum illo in Sanctum sanctorum ingressus fuerit, vid. Histor. arc. fœd. cap. 5. pag. 76. Cui sententiæ non abnuunt Anshelmus, Thomas, Lyranus.
