Alii tamen cum Origene hom. 6. in Lev. & Abulensi in Exod. 25. verf. 46. altare aureum intelligere malunt Ebr. 9. verf. 4. id de quo Exod. 30. verf. 1. Sed id negant fuisse in Sancto sanctorum: dici autem id habuisse Sanctum sanctorum putant, quod altare illud sibi habuerit obversum: ideo dici etiam altare oraculi 1. Reg. 6, 21. id est, quod erat oraculo, scil. in pariete oraculi exteriore. Conf. Gerhard. in Ebr. 9. v. 3.

## 30:3
AND ITS GRATE] The Greeks [use] ἐσχάραν. But the Hebrew word signifies a roof, which is more suitable here, that is, ἐυρανίσκον, with which the altar of incense was covered: but the other one for burnt offerings was without a roof.

Latin:

TAM CRATICULAM EJUS] Græci ἐσχάραν. At Hebræa vox tectum significat, quod hic convenientius, id est, ἐυρανίσκον, quali tegebatur altare suffituum: alterum autem holocaustumatum sine tecto erat.

## 30:5
Vers. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

## 30:6
Vers. 6.

AND YOU SHALL PLACE THE ALTAR AGAINST IT. Between the lampstand and the table toward the eastern side: as Josephus observes: for Origen and Augustine wrongly place it in the Holy of Holies. Conf. cap. 40, 22. 28.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

PONESQUE ALTARE CONTRA ILLUM. Inter candelabrum & mensam ad plagam orientalem: observante Josepho: nam perperam id in Sancto sanctorum collocant Origenes & Augustinus. Conf. cap. 40, 22. 28.

## 30:10
Verse 10.

ONCE A YEAR] Prepared by chastity and sobriety for seven days. See the manner of making atonement in Lev. 16.

It treats there at length of this anniversary festival of atonement, and it is an especially illustrious figure of the atonement of Christ, as will be taught in the same place.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

SEMEL PER ANNUM] Castimonia & sobrietate septem dierum præparatus. Modum expiandi vide Lev. 16.

Agitur illic fuse de hac anniversaria expiatio- nis festivitate, & illustris ea imprimis est figura ex- piationis Christi, ut ibidem docebitur.

## 30:12
Verse 12. WHEN YOU TAKE THE SUM OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.

In Hebrew, 'when you take the head of the children of Israel.' Tremellius and Junius, 'when you shall count the individual heads'; others, 'when you shall lift up': because the numbering was done by the counted lifting up their own heads. Now, therefore, so that the expenses might suffice for building the tabernacle, GOD ordained a census, or a head-counting of the Israelites, so that all males who had entered or exited their 20th year of age should pay half a shekel of the Sanctuary, which corresponded to a fourth part of a Joachimicus, or thaler, because a shekel is worth 20 Gerahs, Num. 12, 47 [sic]; Ezek. 45, 2. But one Gerah corresponds to 7 small Mishnaic coins. Arias Montanus and, following him, others commonly do indeed distinguish the shekel of the sanctuary from the shekel of currency: but Villalpandus in his commentary on Ezekiel teaches that it was not distinct, as does Bonfrerius in this place, since it is called the shekel of the Sanctuary, not because it was larger than the common one, but because it was of the most exact and just weight, inasmuch as Scripture always attributes to the shekel the value of twenty obols, nor did Josephus mention different shekels anywhere, nor does Scripture ever vary regarding the shekel: and the coins of shekels and half-shekels which are found today bear the same weight; and Ezekiel chapter 45, exhorting the Princes to use just weights and measures, defines the shekel as 20 obols, even though he speaks of the common weight. Although, indeed, in 2 Sam. 14, 26, mention is made of a Royal weight, these are nevertheless the same, the Royal weight and the weight of the sanctuary, namely, the just weight, nor is there any evidence that they are different. And the passage is very clear in Lev. 27, 15, 'every valuation shall be weighed by the shekel of the sanctuary,' where it also treats of political contracts of buying and selling: nor is it read anywhere that another kind of shekel was used in civil contracts, 1 Sam. 9, 4; 2 Kings 7, v. 1, 16, 18; Jer. 32, 9; Ez. 4, 10. Furthermore, it is gathered from 1 Chron. 23, v. 29 that the Priests were in charge of weights and measures, which were kept in the sanctuary, so that other weights and other measures might be tested against them. Josephus, book 3, chapter 9, teaches that the shekel was a silver coin equal in weight to an Attic tetradrachm. Rabbi Solomon Jarchi and Moses Gerundensis equate the shekel to half an ounce of silver: a type of which I myself still possess, which has this inscription on one side, 'Shekel of Israel,' with the image of the vessel of manna, and on the other, 'Holy Jerusalem,' with the flowering rod of Aaron. The value of a shekel, therefore, is half a Joachimicus. But the men were numbered from the 20th year up to the 50th, because those older had the calling of the militia and did not come into the census, Ex. 28, 26 [sic]. Thus, the sum of the people in Exod. 38, 16 and Num. 1, 46, calculated as 633,700 men fit for war, comes to 15,887 Joachimici and a half. But GOD wills that we contribute something from our resources, received from His kindness, for the use of the Church. Deut. 25, 3; Prov. 3, 9, 10. But here the Israelites were warned at the same time about the true ransom which Christ paid for the redemption of our souls, Matt. 20, 28. Cyril, book 2 on John, brings forward these additional reasons for the tribute: first, because no one is the Lord of his own head, but we all have one Lord, whom we acknowledge by the deposition of the tribute. Then, in a bodily thing, he was describing a spiritual tribute, namely, the price in spirit and truth, John 4, 23, 24.

It seems not improbable to some that a tribute of this kind was collected every year at the feast of atonement for the preservation and repair of sacred things and for the expenses of the continual sacrifice and other sacred things, and that there was no need for a special command of GOD for that work, which is the opinion of Pelargus and Rivetus; but the Junius-Tremellius notes observe more correctly here that this was commanded to Moses in such a way that this head-counting was done only once: almost all the Hebrews think this command was not temporary, but perpetual; so that from the collection, the daily burnt offerings, the sacrifices on feast days, and the remaining offerings for the whole congregation might be provided: but because it is nowhere read about an anniversary collection, it seems more likely that it was a command to Moses that it be done only once: first, from the end: for this head-counting was ordered for the atonement of the people recently brought back from Egypt: secondly, from the words and the example of Moses, who neither calls this statute perpetual, as he does all the others, nor is he read to have repeated it thereafter, not even when he numbered the people a second and a third time, Num. 1 and 26; thirdly, from the example of all his successors, who are nowhere read to have ordered this head-counting. (It is indeed read that Joash, 2 Chron. 24, used the example of Moses so that he might provide for an extraordinary necessity with an extraordinary collection: but what is written there 'from year to year' etc. does not pertain to the payment, as is commonly thought, but to the assiduous restoration of the temple: as that which was not the work of one year: not to mention that the kind of collection was different: as appears from the fact that Jehoiada hesitated to collect it, and that it was then cast into the chest or box of the Church by each person as a voluntary offering according to his own will.) Finally, from the use of this collection: for this money is said to be established as a memorial, v. 16, that is, for the ministry of the tabernacle, which remained; but not to be spent on things which are consumed (such as sacrifices were), and for that reason Nehemiah, a most studious observer of the Law, having returned after the exile, did not rely on the authority of the Law, but on equity itself, and imposed a third of a shekel for that use, Nehem. 10, 3, which he would have been the least likely of all to do if he had understood that it was provided for by this law.

Vers. on the same. PRICE FOR SOULS] Excellent. Thus also the LXX. λύτρα ψυχῆς. By that poll tax the Israelites testified that they were redeemed by God. It was to be done, however, as often as a census of the people was taken, which, having been omitted by David, cost him dearly, 2 Sam. 24.

Nay, they prefigured the redemption to be provided by Christ. For these things also were a shadow of things to come. The money collected was to be delivered for the uses of the tabernacle of the testimony, that it might be a memorial for the Israelites before the Lord, and that he might make atonement for their souls, v. 16. What else did they testify by this, than that they believed they would be as truly redeemed by the ransom of the Messiah as they were truly paying the prescribed price, and that in this price, as in a type, God would look upon the price of the redemption of the soul to be paid one day as the antitype (for that was the memorial before God) and for the sake of this would be propitious to their souls. For he was not propitious to them on account of that silver, except in the power and virtue of the one expiatory ransom, the precious blood of the Messiah. For as we, so also the Israelites were bought with a great price 1 Cor. 6, 20, certainly not with corruptible gold or silver, but with the precious blood of the lamb without blemish, 1 Pet. 1, 18. For the Son of man came to give his life a ransom for many, Matt. 20, v. 28. Mark 10, v. 45. a ransom for all 1 Tim. 2, 5. Hence that ransom in v. 15 is called typical, an offering to Jehovah given by the Israelites to make atonement for their souls. The LXX interpreters render it thus, in giving the contribution to the Lord to make atonement for your souls. Which things, explaining the type and its virtue, have been omitted by the Vulgate Interpreter; which indeed Grotius, sharp-sighted in the errors of the Hebrew Code, when they are none, here either did not see, or did not wish to annotate for the sake of the Tridentines.

Latin:

Vers. 12. QUANDO TULERIS SUMMAM FILIORUM ISRAEL.

In Ebræo, cum accipies caput filiorum Israël. Tremell. & Jun. cum recensebis singula capita; alii cum levabis: quia numeratio fiebat numeratis ca- pita sua elevantibus. Jam itaque ut sumtus suffice- ret extruendo tabernaculo, ordinavit DEUS cen- sum, sive capitationem Israëlitarum, ut mares omnes annum ætatis 20. ingressi aut egressi dimidium pen- derent siclum Sanctuarii, qui quartæ parti Joachi- mici, vel thaleri respondebat, quia Siclus valet 20. Geris Num. 12, 47. Ezech. 45, 2. Una autem Gera re- spondet 7. nummulis Misnicis. Distinguunt qui- dem siclum sanctuarii a siclo monetæ Arias Monta- nus & ex eo communiter alii: sed non distinctum fuisse Vilalpandus in Ezech. docet, ut & Bonfrerius in h. l. quum siclus Sanctuarii dicatur, non quod major esset communi, sed quod exactissimi & justi esset ponderis, siquidem Scriptura semper Siclo tri- buat valorem viginti obolorum, nec Josephus diver- sorum siclorum mentionem uspiam fecit, neque Scriptura de Siclo unquam variat: ac numismata siclorum & semisiclorum, quæ hodie reperiuntur, idem pondus referunt; Et Ezech. cap. 45. hortans Principes, ut justis ponderibus & mensuris utan- tur, siclum 20. obolis definit, etsi de communi lo- quatur pondere. Quamvis vero 2. Sam. 14, 26. pon- deris Regii mentio fiat, idem tamen hæc sunt pon- dus Regium & pondus sanctuarii, justum nempe pondus, nec ea diversa esse ullo indicio constat. Et locus oppido manifestus est Lev. 27, 15. omnis æsti- matio siclo sanctuarii ponderabitur, ubi de contracti- bus politicis emtionum, venditionum etiam actum: neque in civilibus contractibus legitur uspiam aliud genus Siclorum adhibitum 1. Sam. 9, 4. 2. Reg. 7, v. 1. 16. 18. Jer. 32, 9. Ez. 4, 10. Porro Sacerdotes præ- fuisse ponderibus & mensuris colligitur e 1. Par. 23. v. 29. quæ asservatæ in sanctuario, ut ad ea exige- rentur alia pondera, & aliæ mensuræ. Joseph. l. 3. c. 9. docet, siclum numisma argenteum fuisse par Attico tetradrachmo pondere. R. Sal. Jarchi & Mo- ses Gerund. dimidiæ unciæ argenti siclum æquant: cujus typus apud antiquarios inscriptionem hanc habet ab una parte, שקל ישראל cum vasculi mannæ effigie, ab altera ירושלים קדשה cum vir- ga florida Aaronica: qualem & ego etiamnum ha- beo. Valor ergo sicli est dimidium Joachimici. Nu- merati autem sunt viri a 20. anno usque ad 50. quia majores natu vocationem militiæ habebant, nec in censum veniebant, Ex. 28, 26. summa itaque popu- li Exod. 38, 16. Num. 1, 46. ad 63370. viros ad bellum idoneos computata prodeunt 15887. Joachimici cum dimidio. Vult autem DEUS, ut ex nostris faculta- tibus ab ipsius benignitate acceptis aliquid ad usum Ecclesiæ conferamus. Deuter. 25, 3. Prov. 3, 9. 10. Sed hic monebantur Israëlitæ simul de vero λύτρῳ quod pro animarum nostrarum redemtione per- solvit Christus Matth. 20, 28. Cyrillus l. 2. in Joh. has præterea causas tributi adfert, primum quia ne- mo sui capitis Dominus est, sed unum omnes ha- bemus Dominum, quem tributi depositione fate- mur. Deinde in re corporali spirituale tributum de- scribebat, pretium nimirum in spiritu & veritate Joh. 4, 23. 24.

Non improbabile videtur quibusdam singu- lis annis in festo expiationis ejusmodi tributum fuisse collectum ad rerum sacrarum conservatio- nem & reparationem & ad sumtus jugis sacrificii, aliarumque rerum sacrarum, neque peculiari ad id opus fuisse semper DEI mandato, quæ Pelargi & Riveti est sententia; sed rectius hic observant notæ Junio-Tremellianæ, hoc ita Mosi mandatum fuisse, ut semel tantum fieret hæc capitatio: Hebræi fere omnes hoc mandatum non temporarium, sed perpe- tuum fuisse putant; ut ex collecta compararentur holo- causta quotidiana, sacrificia in dies festos, & reliquæ oblationes pro toto cœtu: sed quia nusquam de anniver- saria collecta legitur, verisimilius videtur mandatum fuisse Moschi, ut semel tantum fieret: primum à fine: nam hæc capitatio ad expiationem populi recens ex Ægypto reducti imperata est: secundo à verbis, ex- emploque Moschis, qui neque hoc statutum perpetuum vocat, ut cætera omnia, neque deinceps repetisse legitur, ne tum quidem quum iterato & tertio populum recen- suit. Num. 1, & 26. tertio ab exemplo successorum omnium, qui nusquam leguntur hanc capitationem imperasse. (Legitur quidem Joasch 2. Chron. 24. exemplum Moschis adhibuisse, ut extraordinariæ necessitati extraordinaria collecta consuleret: sed quod ibi scribitur de anno in annum &c. non ad pensitationem, ut vulgo putatur, sed ad assiduam templi instaurationem pertinet: ut quæ non esset unius anni opus: ut illud taceamus, quod diversum fuit collectæ genus: ut apparet ex eo, quod cun- ctabatur Jojada eam colligere, & quod deinde tan- quam voluntaria oblatio, in arcam sive cippum Ec- clesiæ ab unoquoque pro arbitrio suo conjecta est) Postremo ab hujus collectæ usu: nam pecunia hæc in monumentum statuenda dicitur v. 16. hoc est, in mini- sterium tabernaculi, quod manebat; non autem in res, quæ consumuntur (qualia sacrificia erant) impen- denda, ac propterea Nechemia legis studiosissimus ob- servator Ismaëlitis postliminio reversus non Legis au- ctoritate, sed ipsa æquitate fretus ad illum usum trien- tem sicli indixit, Nehem. 10, 3. quod minime omnium facturus erat, si hac lege caveri intellexisset.

Vers. eodem. PRETIUM PRO ANIMABUS] Opti- me. Sic & LXX. λύτρα ψυχῆς. Ea capitatione testabantur Israëlitæ, se à Deo redemtos. Faciendum autem quoties census agebatur populi, quod à Davide omissum magno ei ste- tit, 2. Reg. 24.

Imo figurabant λύτρωσιν à Christo præstan- dam. Nam & hæc erant FUTURORUM umbra. Pecunia collecta tradenda erat in usus tabernaculi testimonii, ut esset monumentum Israë- litarum coram Domino, & PROPITIARETUR animabus eorum, v. 16. Quid aliud ita testabantur, quam quod crederent tam vere λύτρῳ Messiæ se redemtum iri, quam vere persolvebant pretium præscriptum, & in hoc pretio ceu τύπῳ DEUM pretium redemtionis animæ olim persolvendum ceu ἀντίτυπον respecturum (id enim monumentum erat coram DEO) hujusque causa propitium anima- bus suis futurum. Non enim ob argentum illud ipsis erat propitius: nisi in vi ac virtute unius λύτρε expiatorii, pretiosi sanguinis Messiæ. Nam ut nos, ita & Israëlitæ magno emti sumus pretio 1. Cor. 6, 20. non certe auro vel argento corruptibili, sed pretioso sanguine agni immaculati, 1. Petr. 1, 18. Venit enim Filius hominis dare animam suam λύτρον pro multis, Matth. 20. v. 28. Marc. 10. v. 45. ἀντίλυτρον pro omni- bus 1. Tim. 2, 5. Hinc λύτρον illud v. 15. τυπικὸν dici- tur oblatio Jehovæ ad expiandum animas suas ab Israëlitis data. LXX. Interpp. ita reddunt, ἐν τῷ δι- δόναι τὴν εἰσφορὰν κυρίῳ ἐξιλάσθαι περὶ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν, in dando oblationem Domino ad propitiandu pro animabus vestris. Quæ luculentius explicantia typum ejusque virtutem, omissa sunt a vulgato Interprete quod vero Grotius, oculatus in Ebræi Codicis mendis, cum nulla sunt, hîc aut non vidit, aut in gra- tiam Tridentinorum annotare noluit.

## 30:18
Verse 18. YOU SHALL MAKE A BRONZE LAVER WITH ITS BASE.

We are taught in Exodus 38:8 that it was made from the mirrors of the women, which Pliny, book 33, 29 and book 34, 17, notes were once of bronze or tin. The form is gathered from the molten sea in 1 Kings 7:23; R. Solomon hands down that it was wide at the bottom and narrow at the top, and that it emitted water through 12 pipes, so that as many priests could be washed at the same time; that there was a basin at the base which would catch the flowing water, and it appears that the washing was done not in the vessel itself, but at the bronze base, whose height and capacity were so great that no one could have descended into it without danger of drowning. The purpose of the washing was external cleanliness, but because it was sanctioned under penalty of death, there must have been more serious reasons underlying it: such as when symbolically, because GOD requires the purity of all actions (of which the hands and feet are the means and symbols) Psalm 73:13. Isaiah 1:16, and because it signified that sacred things are not to be handled with unwashed hands: then mystically: so that the bronze laver might figure the washing of baptism, Zechariah 13:1, Ephesians 5:26, and because the washing of hands and feet is enjoined upon priests already sanctified, so that it might be noted that even the holy have need of daily repentance and washing through the blood of Christ, Psalm 32:6, 1 John 1:7.

Latin:

Vers. 18. FACIES ET LABRUM ÆNEUM CUM BASI SUA.

Ex speculis mulierum id factum, quæ olim ærea, vel stannea fuisse Plinius lib. 33, 29. lib. 34, 17. no- tat, Exod. 38, 8. docemur. Forma ex mari fusili 1. Reg. 7, 23. colligitur, R. Salomo inferne amplum & superne strictum, perque fistulas 12. aquam emisisse tradit, ut simul totidem sacerdotes abluerentur ad basin abacum fuisse, qui defluentem aquam exciperet, nec in ipso vase, sed in basi lotionem fa- ctam ex mari æneo apparet, cujus tanta erat alti- tudo, & capacitas, ut nemo potuisset in id descen- dere sine submersionis periculo. Finis ablutio- nis erat externa mundities, sed quia sub pœna mortis ea sancita erat, graviores causas subfuisse oportet: quales sunt cum Symbolice, quod DEUS requirat actionum omnium (quarum media & symbola manus sunt & pedes) puritatem Psalm. 73, 13. Esa. 1, 16. quodque significarit sacra non esse il- lotis manibus tractanda: tum mystice: ut figura- ret labrum æneum lavacrum baptismi Zachar. 13. v. 1. Eph. 5. v. 26. & quia Sacerdotibus jam sanctifi- catis injungitur manuum & pedum ablutio, ut notaretur sanctis etiam opus esse quotidiana pœ- nitentia & ablutione per sanguinem Christi Ps. 32, 6. 1. Joh. 1, 7.

## 30:19
Verse 19.

AARON AND HIS SONS WASHED THEIR HANDS AND FEET IN IT] It was a custom even among the Gentiles to wash before a sacred rite. Hesiod, Homer, and Plautus in the Rudens make mention of it. Lavers were placed for this purpose before the Temple, concerning which Vitruvius writes in book 2. Cincius used to say that a delubrum was a place before a temple where water runs, from the word for washing (diluendo), as Servius teaches us in his commentary on the Aeneid. The Hebrews also call this washing sanctification.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

LAVABANT IN EA AARON ET FILII EJUS MA- NUS SUAS AC PEDES] Etiam gentibus mos lavandi an- te sacrum. Meminere Hesiodus, Homerus, Plautus Ruden- te. In id posita labra ante Templum, de quibus Vitruvius li- bro 2. Cincius dicebat delubrum esse locum ante templum, ubi aqua currit à diluendo, ut nos docet Servius ad Ænei- dos. Hanc lotionem etiam sanctificationem Hebræi vo- cant.

## 30:22
Verse 22.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

## 30:23
TAKE FOR YOURSELF SPICES OF THE FINEST MYRRH AND CHOICE] You would translate more correctly from the Hebrew: Take for yourself the choicest spices, namely five hundred shekels of unadulterated myrrh, etc. For מר־דרור is myrrh free from mixture, namely ἀτρεφογενέων.

Others here render it spices of the head (that is, the choicest) of free myrrh (that is, flowing). But the Vulgate wrongly draws the word ראש to myrrh, since the accent does not permit it. Others also take the choicest spices generally, so that the species subjoined are designated in a common way; some, however, understand balsam, which, since it is to be reckoned among the choicest spices or in the first place, they think was used here. It pleased others to understand balsam under the name Mor, so that מר is a tear, because a freely flowing tear is balsam. Moreover, since no weight was added to the first name of the choicest spices, most interpreters have taken it as a genus. But it is rightly observed in the notes of Junius and Tremellius that balsam would not have been neglected if the Israelites had been in Canaan at that time, to which it was native. Therefore, myrrh flowing of its own accord is that which they call the first, and which is more excellent than the second myrrh, which flows from an incision.

Verse 23.

CINNAMON] So too the Greeks, and the Hebrew word sounds exactly the same. Nevertheless, Kimchi interprets it as aloes, as does Rabbi Solomon, who says that בשם was added so that it might be noted that it is not that medicinal aloe, but the aromatic one, ἐυώδης according to Oribasius. But that same aloe is clearly distinguished from קנמון, and is called by its own name in Cant. 4:14. Wherefore there is no reason why we should trust those later Rabbis too much in their interpretations of gems, herbs, and trees. Things that pertain to law have been preserved well enough through a certain succession of books: the tradition concerning physical matters has perished over so many centuries, and therefore they follow conjectures; it is no wonder if they sometimes wander.

It is better, therefore, to retain the customary meaning with the LXX and the Vulgate. Moreover, it is called Cinnamon of aromatics (which word the Vulgate omitted) and calamus, where likewise in the Hebrew aromatics is added, etc. For aromatic Cinnamon is called so for the sake of distinction because of another kind, which has no or little scent, and aromatic calamus for the distinction from the non-aromatic. Finally, Cassia is added, not the purgative one, which has no scent, but another, about which Pliny writes in book XII, ch. 19, and Dalecampius, referring to seven kinds of cassia in his commentary on him, from which they prefer Daphnocide, and Isocinnamum, which equals cinnamon in goodness and strength, or even in price, which they are accustomed to equate with gold. Cf. Salmasius in his Plinian exercises on Solinus. See also regarding that oil, Schickard in his work on royal law, page 23. Because these species were thicker, olive oil was added, so that it might be more liquid and more suitable for the pouring of the ointment, which is celebrated in Psalm 133:2. Pelargus applies these things in such a way that by myrrh it was mystically signified that our wounds are glued together by the merit of Christ, that the foul breath of the mouth is taken away, and the dull voice is raised, that is, through him our mouths and hearts are excited to ardent prayers. The power of cinnamon is, according to Dioscorides book I, chapter 13, to drive away the poisons of beasts and to dispel the dimness of the eyes; indicated by this is the repression of the infernal asp, and in the midst of the clouds of tribulations, the clarity and serenity of our souls; by the aromatic calamus, which is believed to heal the superfluities of humors, is signified charity, which covers a multitude of sins. Cassia, which according to Pliny helps against the bites of vipers, is a symbol of the blood of Christ, in which there is a most ready remedy for us against the bites of the infernal viper. Moreover, oil is added in such quantity that it may be noted that from our anointing, that is, the Holy Spirit, all spiritual gifts proceed. The exceeding weight of myrrh warns that more affliction happens to us in this life than joy and tranquility.

Latin:

SUME TIBI AROMATA PRIMÆ MYRRHÆ ET ELECTÆ] Rectius ex Hebræo vertas: Sume tibi aromata præcipua, nempe myrrhæ non adulteratæ quingentos siclos, &c. Nam מר־דרור est myrrha libera à mixtura, scilicet ἀτρεφο- γενέων.

Alii hîc reddunt aromata capitis (id est, præ- cipua) myrrhæ libertatis (id est, fluentis.) Perperam vero Vulgata vocem ראש trahit ad myrrham, quum accentus id non permittat. Aromata præcipua etiam alii generaliter accipiunt, ut species subjunctæ ita designentur κοινῶς, nonnulli tamen balsamum in- telligunt, quod quum inter præcipua fit aromata vel primo recensendum loco, hic adhibitum fuisse pu- tant. Aliis sub nomine Mor libuit balsamum intel- ligere, ut מר sit lacryma, quia libere fluens lacry- ma balsamum est. Cæterum quum non addi- tum sit pondus nomini primo aromatum præci- puorum, pro genere id accepere Interpp. pleri- que. Recte autem observatur in Jun. Tremell. notis balsamum non neglectum fuisse, si in Ca- nanæa tum fuissent Israëlitæ, cui illud proprium erat. Quapropter myrrha sponte fluens illa est, quam primam vocant, quæque præstantior est quam myr- rha secunda, quæ ex incisione manat.

Vers. 23.

CINNAMOMI] Sic & Græci, & vox Hebræa pla- ne idem sonat. Attamen Kimchi Aloën interpretatur, ut & Rabbi Salomo, qui additum ait בשם, ut notetur A- loë non illa medica, sed aromatica, ἐυώδης Oribasio. At eadem Aloë à קנמון manifeste distinguitur, suoque nomi- ne appellatur Cant. 4, 14. Quare non est, quod ferioribus illis Rabbinis in gemmarum, herbarum, arborum interpreta- mentis nimis fidamus. Quæ ad jus pertinent, librorum qua- dam successione satis bene servata sunt: De physicis intercidit per tot secula traditio, ideoque conjecturas sequuntur; non mirum, si interdum aberrantes.

Præstat ergo retinere usitatam significationem cum LXX. & Vulgata. Dicitur autem Cinnamo- mum aromatis (quam vocem omisit Vulgatus) & calamus, ubi itidem in Ebræo additum est aroma- tis &c. Aromaticum enim Cinnamomum distin- ctionis causa dicitur ob aliud, quod nihil vel pa- rum odoris habet, & calamus aromaticus ad di- stinctionem non aromatici. Denique Casia ad- ditur non purgativa, quæ nullius odoris, sed alia, de qua Plinius lib. XII. c. 19. & in illum Dalecam- pius septem genera casiæ referens, è quibus præ- ferunt Daphnocidem, & Isocinnamum bonitate & viribus cinnamomum æquantem, aut etiam pre- tio, quod auro æquiparare solent. Conf. Sal- mas. in exercit. Plinian. ad Solin. Vid. etiam de oleo illo Schickardus de jure regio pag. 23. Hisce speciebus quia spissiores erant, oleum olivarum ac- cessit, quod liquidius foret & ad effusionem aptius unguentum, quod celebratur Psalm. 133, 2. Appli- cat hæc Pelargus ita, quod myrrha significatum mystice fuerit, vulnera nostra Christi merito glu- tinari, fœtentem oris halitum tolli, vocemque ob- tusam elevari, hoc est, per ipsum excitari ora & corda nostra ad ardentes preces. Cinnamomi vis est juxta Dioscoridem lib. I. cap. 13. bestiarum pelle- re venena caliginemque oculorum discutere; in- dicata eo aspidis infernalis repressio, inque me- diis tribulationum nubibus animorum nostrorum claritas & serenitas; calomo odorato, qui super- fluitatibus humorum mederi creditur, significata est charitas, quæ multitudinem peccatorum ope- rit. Casia, quæ juxta Plinium viperarum ictibus subvenit, sanguinis Christi Symbolum est, in quo ictibus viperæ infernalis remedium nobis est præ- sentissimum. Oleum autem additur in tanta quan- titate, ut notetur, ab unctione nostra, hoc est, Spi- ritu S. omnia charismata spiritualia proficisci. Pondus myrrhæ exuperantius monet plus afflictio- nis in hac vita nobis evenire, quam lætitiæ & tran- quillitatis.

## 30:24
Verse 24. BY THE WEIGHT OF THE SANCTUARY. The weight is required according to the shekel of the Sanctuary, just as the weights of precious aromatics are accustomed to be required according to the weight of a gold coin. Five hundred shekels of myrrh make twenty pounds and 10 ounces. Moreover, two shekels make an ounce. 500 shekels make 250 ounces, and in a pound there are 12 ounces, and therefore 250 ounces are 20 pounds and 10 ounces.

A MEASURE OF HIN.

This measure, according to Josephus book III, ch. 10, held two Attic choes: to the Hebrews twelve logs, which Arias Montanus reduces to 72 eggs.

Latin:

Vers. 24. PONDERE SANCTUARII. Pondus ad siclum Sanctuarii exigitur, uti pondera pretiosorum aromatum ad aurei corona- ti pondus exigi solent. Quingenti sicli myrrhæ viginti libras & 10. uncias faciunt. Duo autem sicli faciunt unciam. 500. sicli efficiunt 250. uncias, in libra autem sunt 12. unciæ, ac proinde 250. un- ciæ sunt 20. libræ & 10. unciæ.

MENSURAM HIN.

Hæc mensura secundum Josephum lib. III. c. 10. capiebat duos choas Atticos: Ebræis duodecim logos, quos Arias Montanus reducit ad 72. ova.

## 30:32
Verse 32. THE FLESH OF MAN SHALL NOT BE ANOINTED WITH IT. All those alien to the priestly family are excluded, whom he designated in verse 33 by the name of stranger: and therefore, even if Prophets and Kings were also anointed, nevertheless their anointing could not be done with this holy oil. For what Simler says, that it did not conflict with the law, provided that an exception was made by GOD himself, is merely begging the question, since nowhere is an exception made by GOD read of. And how could David be anointed with the sacred oil, when the tabernacle at the time he was being anointed King of Judah was in Gibeon, which Ishbosheth the son of Saul held? Nor is it likely that Hazael, King of Syria, a stranger to the true GOD, or even Jehu, a worshiper of calves, anointed by Elisha, were smeared with the priestly oil, even if some oil prepared for that purpose was used by the Prophet; but not with that composition which is prescribed here for sacred things. Moreover, this Priestly Chrism was a figure of the anointing of Christ our High Priest, who was anointed with the oil of gladness in Psalm 45:8.

Latin:

Vers. 32. CARO HOMINIS NON UNGE- TUR EX EO. Excluduntur omnes alieni à Sacerdotali fami- lia, quos v. 33. nomine alieni designavit: ideoque etsi Prophetæ, & Reges etiam ungerentur, non ta- men eorum unctio hoc sancto oleo fieri poterat. Nam quod Simlerus dicit, id non repugnasse legi, siquidem exceptio à DEO ipso facta sit, eo tan- tum principium petitur, cum nuspiam exceptio facta à DEO legatur. Et quomodo David oleo sacro ungi potuit, quum tabernaculum eo tempo- re, quo in Regem Juda ungebatur, fuerit in Ga- baon, quam Isboseth Saulis filius tenebat? Neque verisimile est Hasaëlem Regem Syriæ alienum à vero DEO, aut etiam Jehu cultorem vitulorum ab Elisæo unctos, sacerdotali delibutos fuisse oleo, etsi oleum aliquod ad id præparatum à Pro- pheta fuerit; sed non ea compositione, quæ hic ad sacra præscribitur. Erat autem hoc Chrisma Sa- cerdotale figura unctionis Christi Pontificis nostri, qui oleo lætitiæ unctus est Psalm. 45, 8.

## 30:34
Verse 34.

TAKE UNTO THEE SWEET SPICES, STACTE AND ONYCHA. GALBANUM OF GOOD ODOR AND FRANKINCENSE] Philo refers stacte to water, onycha to earth, galbanum to air, frankincense to fire. By these is prescribed the composition of the incense which was to be offered to GOD: from a fourfold material. Stacte, according to Dioscorides, is the fatness of fresh myrrh, not that which flowed spontaneously, or was expressed from crushed myrrh, as Salmasius notes in his notes on Pliny, p. 570, but that which remained, whence stacte, 'strained'. For the former was used for ointment, but the latter for the composition of incense. Onycha, an aromatic, according to Dioscorides, book 2, chapter 92, is a covering like a fingernail, lucid like a shell, which is found in the nard-bearing lakes of India, of sweet odor, whose chief power is for healing wounds, even old ones, as Pliny teaches, book XXXII, chapter 10. Galbanum is a species of aromatic resin, and it warms, extracts, disperses, kills serpents, and removes old coughs and difficulty in breathing. But it is not understood here as that which is sold in shops under that name, which is of a heavy and foul odor, but such as was in use in Syria, of a more pleasant odor. To these was added frankincense, which is collected among the Sabaeans by cutting the bark of the tree. Dioscorides, book I, chapter 83. Tradition of the Hebrews holds that 70 pounds of each were taken, 'bad be-bad', so much for so much, which they commonly call 'ana'. Junius and Tremellius: Let the weight of one be as the weight of the other. Vulgate: all things shall be of equal weight: so also the Chaldean, weight shall be with weight. The mystical significance is gathered from Revelation 5:8, chapter 8:3, as also from Psalm 141. Sirach 26:16. As well-compounded incense delights the man who smells it: so the prayer of the righteous is sweet before GOD, according to Chrysostom, homily XIII, of the Imperfect Work. The crushing of the spices denotes the humiliation of a contrite and crushed heart, which is necessary in prayers. As stench is driven away by frankincense, and the air is purified: so vices are warded off by prayer, and the mind is purified. If anyone wishes to make sweet incense, let him mix, according to Nilus, in equal weights according to the law, lucid frankincense, cassia, onycha, and stacte. These indeed are the four virtues: for if they are sufficiently full and equal, the mind is not betrayed. Equality of weight indicates that that prayer is best which is undertaken from faith, hope, charity, and gratitude. Stacte has the power of warming and cleansing: so prayer heals us with sins cleansed. James 5. Sirach 38. Onycha, by its whiteness, adumbrates prayer that is 'anupokriton' [unfeigned], and by its odor, the pleasant odor of prayer, it exhibits the power of prayer to heal wounds through the virtue of the passion of Christ. Galbanum, when ignited, kills serpents; prayer, burning with faith, kills the infernal serpent. Which things are more fitting than that comparison of Philo with the IV Elements. The position from the region of the mercy seat prefigures Christ, without whom no prayers can please GOD.

Verse the same.

ALL THINGS SHALL BE OF EQUAL WEIGHT] 'ison iso estai', the Greeks. In Hebrew: 'Alone with Alone'; that is, each shall be weighed separately, so that they may be equal. We have already spoken of that. The interpretation of Grotius does not differ.

Latin:

Verf. 34.

SUME TIBI AROMATA, STACTEN ET ONYCH. GALBANUM BONI ODORIS ET THUS] Philo stacten ad aquam refert, onycha ad terram, galbanum ad aërem, thus ad ignem. His præscribitur thymiamatis compositio quod DEO offerendum erat: ex quadruplici materia. Stacte Dioscoridi est recentis myr- rhæ pinguedo, non quæ sponte fluebat, aut ex myrrha contusa exprimebatur, notante Salmas. in not. Plin. p. 570. sed quæ remanebat, unde 5a- κτὴ eliquata. Illa enim ad unguentum, hæc vero ad compositionem incensi adhibita. Onycha aro- ma Dioscor. autore lib. 2. cap. 92. est unguis in- star lucidum conchylii tegumentum, quod in In- diæ nardiferis lacubus reperitur suavis odoris, cu- jus vis præcipua est ad curanda vulnera quamvis vetusta, docente Plinio lib. XXXII. cap. 10. Gal- banum species est resinæ aromaticæ, ac calefacit, extrahit, discutit, serpentes necat, tussimque ve- terem & difficultatem spirandi tollit. Non autem intelligitur hic, quod in officinis eo nomine ven- ditur, quod odoris gravis & fœtentis est, sed quale in Syria in usu erat, gratioris odoris. Qui- bus addebatur thus, quod apud Sabæos inciso ar- boris cortice colligitur. Dioscorid. lib. I. cap. 83. Uniuscujusque libras 70. acceptas fuisse Ebræo- rum fert traditio בד בבד tantum in tanto, quod vul- go ana vocant. Junius & Tremell. Pondus unius sicut pondus alterius esto: Vulgata: æqualis ponde- ris erunt omnia: sic etiam Chaldæus, pondus cum pondere erit. Significatio mystica ex Apocal. 5, 8. cap. 8, 3. colligitur, ut & è Psalm. 141. Syrach. 26, 16. Sicut thymiama bene confectum delectat hominem odorantem: sic oratio justi suavis est ante DEUM, secundum Chrysostomum homil. XIII. imperfect. Operis. Aromatum contusio notat contriti & con- tusi cordis humiliationem in precibus necessariam. Ut thure abigitur fœtor, & aër purgatur: sic oratio- ne vitia arcentur, & mens purgatur. Si quis confice- re vult thymiama odoratum, commisceat, Nilo auto- re, æquis ponderibus secundum legem thus lucidum, cassiam, onychen & Stacten. Hæc vero sunt qua- tuor virtutes: etenim si satis ea plena & æquales fue- rint, non proditur mens. Æqualitas ponderis indicat eam orationem optimam esse, quæ ex fide, spe, charitate, ac gratitudine suscipitut. Stacte ca- lefaciendi & abstergendi vim habet: sic oratio ab- stersis criminibus nos sanat. Jac. 5. Syr. 38. Ony- cha candore orationem ἀνυπόκριτον, odore suo gratum orationis odorem adumbrans vim oratio- nis ad curanda vulnera, virtute passionis Christi exhibet. Galbanum accensum serpentes, oratio fide ardens infernalem serpentem enecat. Quæ magis conveniunt, quam Philonis illa comparatio cum IV. Elementis. Situs è regione propitiatorii Christum præfigurat, fine quo preces nullæ DEO placere possunt.

Verf. eod.

ÆQUALIS PONDERIS ERUNT OMNIA] ἶσον ἴσῳ ἔσαι Græci. Hebraice: Solum cum Solo; id est, seorsim quæque ponderabuntur, ut sint æqualia. De eo jam diximus. Non discrepat Grotiana interpretatio.

## 30:37
Verse 37.

YE SHALL NOT MAKE SUCH A COMPOSITION FOR YOUR OWN USES. Perfumes are not prohibited, nor are ointments, which often refresh and exhilarate man, Proverbs 27:9, Psalm 104:15, provided that abuse is absent, Amos 6:6, and they are a sign of divine grace, just as, conversely, in a calamitous time or of fasting, they abstained from them. And therefore it is taught that this sacred perfume only is not to be converted to other uses: so that it may be hinted that the worship of religious invocation ought not to be exhibited to any other than God, Isaiah 42:8.

Latin:

Verf. 37.

TALEM COMPOSITIONEM NON FA- CIATIS IN USUS VESTROS. Non prohibentur suffimenta, uti nec unguen- ta, quæ sæpe hominem recreant & exhilarant Prov. 27, 9. Pf. 104, 15. modo abusus absit Am. 6, 6. ac signum sunt divinæ gratiæ, quemadmodum contra tempore calamitoso, aut jejunii ab iis absti- nebant. Ideoque tantum hoc sacrum suffimentum non esse in usus alios convertendum docetur: ut innuatur religiosæ invocationis cultum alii, quam Deo exhiberi non debere, Esa. 42, 8.

## 31:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXI. Architects of the tabernacle. Observation of the Sabbath. Tables of the law.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXI. Architecti tabernaculi. Sabbathi observatio. Tabulæ legis.

## 31:2
Verse 2. I HAVE CALLED BY NAME BEZALEEL THE SON OF URI THE SON OF HUR.

God himself chose and called and furnished with his gifts the architects of the sanctuary: to indicate that he chooses and calls to the Holy Ministry, and renders suitable, those whom he wishes to be employed. Acts 20:28. 1 Corinthians 12. Ephesians 4. He is said to be called by name: because he has all known by name, cares for them, and designates them for their duties. Isaiah 43:1, chapter 45:4. The name Bezaleel is 'in the shadow of GOD', because he was employed for those things by which God and divine things were adumbrated. His grandfather Hur was a famous man from the tribe of Judah, of whom mention was made in chapter 24:14. Aholiab denotes 'desirous of the tabernacle', who was from the tribe of Dan, born of almost the lowest: because GOD employs the noble and the ignoble for the structure of the temple.

Latin:

Vers. 2. VOCAVI EX NOMINE BESALEEL FILIUM URI FILII HUR.

Elegit Deus ipse ac vocavit donisque suis in- struxit architectos sanctuarii: ut indicaret, se ad S. Ministerium eligere ac vocare, & idoneos reddere, quos adhibitos vult. Actorum 20, 28. 1. Corinth. 12. Ephes. 4. Nomine vocatus dicitur: quod nomina- tim omnes cognitos habeat, curet, atque ad mu- nia sua designet. Esa. 43, 1. cap. 45, 4. Nomen Be- zaleel est in umbra DEI, quia adhibebatur ad ea, quibus Deus & res divinæ adumbrabantur. Avus ejus Hur vir clarus è tribu Juda fuit, cujus cap. 24, 14. mentio facta. Ahaliath notat tabernaculi cu- pidum, qui è tribu Dan, fere ultima oriundus: quia DEUS nobiles & ignobiles ad templi structuram adhibet.

## 31:3
Verse 3. AND I HAVE FILLED HIM WITH THE SPIRIT OF GOD.

The Son of GOD speaks of the Spirit of GOD the Father: and thus this is a testimony of the H. Trinity. He does not find one suitable, but makes one: for whom GOD calls, him He renders suitable for the works of his calling 1 Cor. 4, 7. 2 Cor. 3, 4. from whom are not only sanctifying gifts, but also ministering ones 1 Cor. 12, 3. seqq. and not only wisdom for divine matters, but also for arts, and other expeditions. Zech. 1, 14. Therefore it is implied that the entire structure of the tabernacle is not from Moses, but from GOD, because God admits nothing of human invention or institution when it concerns His worship.

AND WITH BRASS] There is more here in the Greek than in the Hebrew or Latin: Καὶ τὴν ὑάκινθον, καὶ τὴν πορφύραν, καὶ τὸ κόκκινον τὸ νητόν: some Codices add: καὶ τὴν βύσσον τὴν κεκλωσμέ- νην. Compare above 25, 4. where the same words are in the Greek, except that it has διπλῆν instead of νητόν.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET REPLEVI EUM SPIRITU DEI.

Loquitur Filius DEI de Spiritu DEI Patris: adeoque testimonium hîc est SS. Trinitatis. Non idoneum invenit, sed facit: quem enim DEUS vocat, eum ad opera vocationis idoneum reddit 1. Cor. 4, 7. 2. Cor. 3, 4. à quo non tantum dona sanctificantia sunt, sed etiam ministrantia quæque 1. Cor. 12, 3. seqq. nec tantum sapientia ad res di- vinas, sed etiam ad artes, & expeditiones alias. Zach. 1, 14. Itaque innuitur, totam tabernaculi structuram non à Mose, sed à DEO esse, quod nihil humanæ adinventionis vel institutionis admittat Deus, cum de cultu ipsius agitur.

ET ÆRE] Plus hîc est in Græco, quam in Hebræo, vel Latino: Καὶ τὴν ὑάκινθον, καὶ τὴν πορφύραν, καὶ τὸ κόκκινον τὸ νητόν: addunt quidam Codices: καὶ τὴν βύσσον τὴν κεκλωσμέ- νην. Confer supra 25, 4. ubi eadem in Græco verba, nisi quod διπλῆν pro νητόν.

## 31:7
Verse 7. THE TABERNACLE OF THE COVENANT.

Those things are recounted which were to be fashioned by men instructed by the Spirit of prudence for such tasks: in which you may see an image of those things which those called to the sacred ministry and instructed by the Spirit of God ought to attend to, and in which they ought to be occupied: namely, in the construction of the tabernacle of the Lord or the building up of the Church, which is the house of the living GOD 1 Tim. 3, 15. in the ark, containing the law of God, that is, the explanation of the Holy Bibles, 1 Tim. 4, 16. 2 Tim. 3, 14. in the exhibition of the mercy seat and throne of grace Rom. 3, 24. in the dispensation of the laver of baptism, in the adornment of the spiritual table, in the care of the altar of burnt offering, and the presentation before God of the passion of Christ, who offered Himself for us as a burnt offering, in the offering of the incense of prayers, in the purification of the light of the word from the darkness which heretics bring upon it, in the communication of the gifts of the H.S. as a heavenly anointing, in the putting on of the garments of righteousness and salvation, etc. But who is sufficient for these things, 2 Cor. 2, 16. God alone is He who makes us sufficient, c. 3, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 7. TABERNACULUM FOEDERIS.

Recensentur ea, quæ à viris Spiritu pruden- tiæ ad talia instructis confici debebant: in quibus imaginem videas eorum, quæ ad sacrum ministe- rium vocati & Spiritu Dei instructi curare, & in quibus occupari debeant: utpote in tabernaculi Domini exstructione vel Ecclesiæ, quæ domus DEI viventis est 1. Tim. 3, 15. ædificatione, in arca, le- gem Dei continentis, hoc est, Bibliorum Sacrorum explicatione, 1. Tim. 4, 16. 2. Tim. 3, 14. in propitia- torii & throni gratiæ exhibitione Rom. 3, 24. in la- vacri baptismi dispensatione, in mense spiritualis adornatione, in altaris holocausti cura, & passionis Christi, qui se pro nobis in holocaustum obtulit, coram Deo præsentatione, in suffimentorum pre- cum oblatione, lucis verbi à tenebris, quas hæretici eidem inferunt, depuratione, donorum S.S. ceu unctionis cælestis communicatione, vestium justitiæ & salutis induitione &c. Ecquis vero ad hæc ido- neus est, 2. Cor. 2, 16. Deus solus est, qui nos idoneos facit, c. 3, 6.

## 31:8
Verse 8. THE PUREST CANDLESTICK] Clean from blood, which epithet pertains both to the table and to the vessels of both.

It does not appear from the text that that pertains to these: and it is called purest, not because it is clean from blood, but because it was made pure from gold. For the discourse here is about the workmanship.

Latin:

Vers. 8. CANDELABRUM PURISSIMUM] Mundum à sanguine, quod ἐπίθετον & ad mensam, & ad vasa utrius- que pertinet.

Non apparet è textu ad hæc illud pertinere: & purissimum dicitur, non quod mundum à san- guine, sed quod ex auro purum factum. De fabri- ca enim hîc sermo est.

## 31:13
Verse 13. SEE THAT YOU KEEP MY SABBATH.

The law concerning the Sabbath is subjoined, partly so that the architects or the people might not be led, either by the holiness of the work or by its necessity, to allow themselves to be induced to work even on the Sabbath, and partly so that the Israelites might be warned above all things about the true use of the tabernacle, which consisted in the religious observance of feast days and especially of the Sabbath. Nor would it be ἄλογον to suppose with the Hebrews that the foundation of all the precepts, which preceded the commandments and confirmed the faith of the created world, should have been repeated here toward the end: so that the other laws might return as if in a circle to that first one, which is concerning the Sabbath, as Pelargus thinks in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 13. VIDETE, UT SABBATUM MEUM CUSTODIATIS.

Lex de Sabbato subjungitur, partim ne archi- tecti sive operis sanctitate, sive ejusdem necessi- tate, paterentur sej adduci, ut etiam Sabbato labo- rarent, partim ut Israëlitæ ante omnia de vero usu tabernaculi monerentur, qui consistebat in festo- rum dierum & imprimis Sabbati religiosa observa- tione. Neque ἄλογον fuerit opinari cum Ebræis, præceptorum omnium fundamentum, quod an- tecessit mandata, fidemque conditi mundi firma- vit, repetendum hic fuisse sub finem: ut leges cæte- ræ velut circulo redirent in primam illam, quæ est de Sabbato, ut censet h. l. Pelargus.

## 31:16
Ver. 16. AN EVERLASTING COVENANT.

In the Hebrew, a covenant of the age. The word Olam for a defined age not infrequently occurs for the subject matter. Thus here the measure of this age is the duration of the Republic of Israel and of the Jewish Synagogue up to the times of the Messiah. Therefore it is said in their generations, that is, while that Mosaic republic and polity stood, in which the distinction of tribes and generations was preserved until the Messiah, this law of the Sabbath was to be observed. Furthermore, Augustine rightly advises in question 139, although the seventh day has been transferred to the Lord's Day, that the care of the Sabbath religion has been most strictly enjoined upon us also, and that it is to be preserved until the end of the age: as far as the moral part of the law is concerned, even if the ceremonial part was abolished by the coming of the Messiah. Acts 20:7; 1 Cor. 16:2.

Latin:

Vers. 16. PACTUM SEMPITERNUM.

In Ebræo pactum seculi. Vox Olam de seculo definito non raro occurrit pro subjecta materia. Ita hic seculi istius mensura est duratio Reip. Israë- lis, & Synagogæ Judaicæ usque ad Messiæ tempora. Ideo dicitur in generationibus suis, hoc est, stante republ. & politia illa Mosaica, in qua distinctio tribuum & generationum conservata fuit ad Mes- siam usque, Sabbati legem istam observandam. De cætero recte monet Augustinus qv. CXXXIX. quamvis septimus dies in Dominicum traductus sit, nobis etiam severissime demandatam esse religionis Sabbati curam, eamque conservandam esse usque ad consummationem seculi: quantum ad morale legis, etsi ceremoniale adventu Messiæ abolitum sit. Act. 20, 7. 1. Cor. 16, 2.

## 31:18
Ver. 18. AND THE LORD GAVE TO MOSES.

The tables of the law are said to have been given by GOD to Moses. But in Gal. 3:29, the law is held to have been given by the hand of a mediator. Which things, however, agree properly. For that mediator, as the Fathers establish with great consensus and rightly, is Christ: for GOD did not give the tables of the law to Moses without His Son, but through the Son, if by the Lord here one is not to understand this very Son, who delivered the law as the κύριον αἴτιον, not as a ministerial cause.

WRITTEN WITH THE FINGER OF GOD.

By whom Augustine in 'De Catechizandis Rudibus' and others not incorrectly understand the Holy Spirit: concerning whom Theophylact in Luke 11 says: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ δάκτυλος ὁμούσιός ἐστι τῷ ὅλῳ σώματι, ὕτω κὲ τὸ πνεῦμα ὁμούσιόν ἐστι τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ ὑἱῷ. But however much the arm and hand of God may sometimes denote power indefinitely; it is nevertheless also sometimes taken for the Son of God Himself, as in Ps. 118 and Isa. 53; thus it does not prevent the finger of God from being used essentially concerning the power of God in Exod. 8:17, and personally concerning the Holy Spirit in Luke 11:20, and so here the work of writing is appropriately attributed to the Holy Spirit, whose work it also is to inscribe the law upon the tables of our hearts, 2 Cor. 3:3.

Latin:

Vers. 18. DEDITQUE DOMINUS MOSI.

Tabulas legis DEUS Mosi dedisse dicitur. At Gal. 3, 29. per manum mediatoris lex data perhi- betur. Quæ vero probe conveniunt. Nam me- diator ille, ut magno consensu, & recte Patres sta- tuunt, Christus est: non enim absque Filio suo, sed per Filium DEUS tabulas legis Mosi dedit, si non per Dominum hic ipse Filius intelligendus, qui le- gem ceu κύριον αἴτιον, non tanquam causa diακο- νικῃ tradidit.

SCRIPTAS DIGITO DEI.

Per quem Augustinus de Catech. rudib. & alii non inrecte Spir. S. intelligunt: de quo Theophil. in Luc. 11. ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ δάκτυλος ὁμούσιός ἐστι τῷ ὅλῳ σώματι, ὕτω κὲ τὸ πνεῦμα ὁμούσιόν ἐστι τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ ὑἱῷ. Utut vero brachium & manus Dei poten- tiam indefinite quandoque notet; accipitur tamen etiam aliquando pro ipso Filio Dei, utpote Ps. 118. Esa. 53. ita non obstat, quo minus digitus Dei & es- sentialiter de potentia Dei adhibeatur Exod. 8, 17. & personaliter de Spiritu S. Luc. 11, 20. adeoque hic ap- propriative opus Scriptionis Spiritui S. tribuatur, cujus etiam est legem cordis nostris tabulis inscri- bere 2. Cor. 3, 19.

## 32:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXII. The calf-worship of the people. The zeal of Moses.

Ver. 1. BUT THE PEOPLE SEEING] This whole part of the history is absent from Josephus, who feared, I believe, to offend the Romans, who both worshipped a serpent in place of Aesculapius and approved of and protected the cult of Apis in Egypt.

Ver. same. ARISE, MAKE US GODS.

Arise, not as if he were sitting, as Ussher wishes, compelled by the people to rise, but so that he might gird himself for the work. In the Hebrew, Elohim designates one calf: which they name in the plural number, because they were seeking to have represented to themselves the image of GOD, in whom they were not ignorant of a true plurality, or because, seeing the pillar which was their guide on the way standing, and hastening into the promised land, they desired another visible leader in whom they might acknowledge and worship GOD, or because, accustomed in Egypt to the cult of images through the misguided zeal of the Egyptians, who worshipped the image of a calf or ox, which they called Apis, into which they believed the Deity to insinuate itself. Expecting from such an idol or image responses and guidance into the land of Canaan. Which was true idolatry.

Verse of the same.

FOR THIS MAN MOSES.

For this man Moses, they say, who brought us up out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened. They speak of Moses as if he were unknown: certainly, those words do not convey the reverence which they themselves owed. They perhaps believed he had been devoured by beasts, as it seemed to Josephus, or had been snatched away by GOD.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXII. Μοσχολατρεία populi. Mosis Zelus.

Vers. 1. VIDENS AUTEM POPULUS] Tota hæc Histo- riæ pars abest à Josepho, verito, credo, Romanos offendere, qui & serpentem pro Æsculapio coluere, & Apidos cultum in Ægypto probabant, ac tutabantur.

Vers. eod. SURGE, FAC NOBIS DEOS.

SUrge, non quasi sederit, ut Usserius vult, com- pulsus à populo, ut surgeret, sed ut se ad opus accingat. In Ebræo אלהים unum vitulum de- signat: quem ita nominant plurali numero, quia DEI imaginem, in quo veram pluralitatem non ignorabant, sibi repræsentari eodem expetebant, sive quod columnam, quæ ipsis viæ dux erat stare videntes, & in terram promissam festinantes alium visibilem ducem, in quo DEUM agnoscerent, & colerent, desiderarent, seu quod assueti in Ægypto cultui imaginum per κακοζηλίαν Ægyptiorum, qui imaginem vituli aut bovis, quem Apin vocabant, in quem se Numen insinuare credebant, venerabantur. A tali idolo vel simulacro responsa, & deductionem in terram Canaan expectantes. Quae vera erat idololatria.

Vers. eod.

MOSI ENIM HUIC VIRO.

Huic Mosi, inquiunt, viro, qui ascendere nos fecit ex Aegypto, nescimus quid acciderit. De Mose, quasi incognito loquuntur: certe non referunt verba illa eam reverentiam, quam ipsi debebant. Credidere fortassis eum a bestiis devoratum esse, uti Josepho visum, aut a DEO raptum esse.

## 32:2
Verse 2. TAKE OFF THE EARRINGS.

They think they were requested; because Aaron wanted to divert the Israelites from their purpose, as they would not easily give their earrings or tear them from their dearest ones: which women and daughters, being greedy and very fond of ornaments, would also be reluctant to part with. Nevertheless, wickedness prevailed. In vain does Franc. Moncaeus excuse Aaron from idolatry under the title 'Aaron Purgatus', which book was marked with censure by the Pontificians themselves; it was also refuted by the Sorbonne theologian Visorius. For this collection was made by the order of Aaron: he himself caused the golden calf to be made: which work is therefore attributed to Aaron himself morally, he formed it by a casting work, and made a molten calf: because what someone does through another, he is seen to have done himself. It is a Rabbinic fable that it was made by the works of Egyptian magicians: about which nothing is held in history. Furthermore, Aaron proclaimed a feast by a herald, and built an altar v. 5. It is absurd what Montejus says, even if Gregory also Francus in Lex. Rabbin. p. 248, does not disapprove that Aaron wanted to represent the Cherubim in the form of a calf, as that sign of GOD by which the people sought to be led in the absence of Moses into Canaan: and thus did nothing other than what Moses was going to do by erecting a Cherub in the form of a calf, as a sign of divine presence. Indeed, he falsely assumes that Moses interpreted the promise of GOD concerning the angel leading the people, Exod. 23, 20, as God preceding in some visible sign: he likewise falsely assumes that this sign was the ark with the mercy seat and the Cherub; and no less falsely does he base his opinion on the idea that the form of the Cherubim exhibited a calf, and that Aaron wanted to express that. And Visorius rightly answers, fol. 14. He ordered the Cherubim to be placed on the mercy seat not as a likeness of GOD, nor so that they might be worshipped as God or with divine honors, but so that, being reverent through the mercy seat, they might provoke us by their example to the worship of the invisible GOD. And afterwards: it is false that the Cherubim in the Mosaic religion were an object of adoration: for the Jews never worshipped the Cherubim, nor honored them with divine honors, but one invisible God, who gave his answers from the mercy seat, in the space between the Cherubim. But leaving those futile hypotheses aside, for whatever reason Aaron finally formed the calf, it is certain that idolatry was introduced by him, for which God punished the people so severely, and Moses sharply rebuked Aaron, who made Israel sin, v. 21. What did this people do to you, that you should bring upon it a very great sin, such as idolatry certainly is: whence also v. 25, Aaron is said to have stripped the people, indeed GOD wanted to destroy Aaron himself with the people, with only Moses saved v. 10. Conf. Deut. 9, 20. Therefore, it is not permitted to restrict this to only some part of the people with Montejus; as if only some committed idolatry by worshipping the calf itself and not God, not even relatively, with others being immune from idolatry, who with Aaron worshipped GOD in a calf: For whom will Montagu, or any other Papist, persuade that any of the Israelites, let alone any significant multitude of them, held the calf to be GOD, who had led them out of Egypt, and were so stupid and foolish that they believed this calf, which they had only just fashioned from earrings, had led them out of Egypt before it existed in the nature of things? And therefore their idolatry did not consist in the fact that they believed the calf to be the very God who had led them out of Egypt, but in that they worshipped that same God in it, contrary to GOD's commandment about not making idols or images so that God might be worshipped in them. Nor is anything else implied in Ps. 106:20 when they are said to have changed their glory, that is, God, who was their glory, into the form of an ox; for that was not done by worshipping a living ox in a molten ox, and referring the adoration to that brute creature, not to God: for thus they would have had living oxen at hand, which they could have worshipped, but by worshipping GOD in the form of an ox, which eats grass: since God expressly forbade that they should represent Him under the form of any animal exposed for worship, or that God should be worshipped in it.

Latin:

Vers. 2. TOLLITE INAURES.

Eas postulatas censent; quod divertere voluerit Aaron Israëlitas ab instituto, utpote non facile inaures suas daturos aut charissimis suis erepturos: quas mulieres & filiae avarae & ornatus studiosissimae aegre etiam dimissurae sint. Praevaluit tamen improbitas. Frustra Aaronem ab Idololatria excusat Franc. Moncaeus sub tit. Aaron purgati, qui liber censura ab ipsis Pontificiis notatus est; refutatus etiam a Theologo Sorbonico Visorio. Nam jussu Aaronis collatio haec facta est: ipse fieri fecit vitulum aureum: Quod opus ideo Aaroni ipsi tribuitur moraliter, formavit opere fusorio, & fecit vitulum conflatilem: quia quod quis per alium facit, ipse fecisse videtur. Fabula Rabbinica est, quod opera Magorum Aegyptiorum factus sit: de quo nihil in historia habetur. Adhaec festum indixit Aaron per praeconem, altare aedificavit v. 5. Ineptum est, quod dicit Montejus, etsi hoc etiam Gregor. Francus in Lex. Rabbin. p. 248. non improbet, voluisse Aaronem repraesentare Cherubinos in forma vituli, ceu illud signum DEI, quo deduci peteret populus absente Mose, in Chanaan: adeoque nihil aliud fecisse, quam quod Moses facturus erat erecto Cherubino, forma vitulina, ceu signo divinae praesentiae. Nimirum falso supponit, Mosen promissionem DEI de angelo ductore populi Exod. 23, 20. interpretatum fuisse de Deo praecedente in aliquo signo visibili: falso itidem assumit, signum illud fuisse arcam cum propitiatorio, & Cherubin; nec minus falso id sententiae suae substernit, formam Cherubim exhibuisse vitulum, eamque exprimere voluisse Aaronem. Et recte respondet Visor. fol. 14. Jussit Cherubos propitiatorio imponi non tanquam similitudinem DEI, neque ut pro Deo aut divinis colerentur honoribus, sed ut per propitiatorium venerabundi existentes suo veluti exemplo ad invisibilis DEI cultum nos provocarent. Et postea: falsum est Cherubos in Mosaica religione fuisse objectum adorationis: neque enim Judaei Cherubos unquam adoraverunt, aut divinis honoribus coluerunt, sed unum Deum invisibilem, qui e propitiatorio, medio inter Cherubos spatio, sua responsa dabat. Relictis vero hypothesibus illis futilibus, quacunque de causa tandem Aaron vitulum formarrit, idololatriam ab ipso invectam esse certum, ob quam adeo graviter Deus populum punivit, acriterque Aaronem, qui peccare fecit Israëlum, reprehendit Moses v. 21. Quid tibi fecit hic populus, ut induceres super eum peccatum maximum, quale utique idololatria est: unde etiam v. 25. populum nudasse dicitur Aaron, imo cum populo Aaronem ipsum delere voluit DEUS, solo Mose servato v. 10. Conf. Deut. 9, 20. Non ergo restringere hoc ad aliquam tantum populi partem licet cum Montejo; quasi nonnulli tantum Idololatriam commiserint adorantes ipsummet vitulum non Deum, ne relative quidem, aliis immunibus ab ido- lolatria, qui cum Aarone DEUM in vitulo colu- rint: Cui enim persuadebit Montæjus, aut aliu Papista, quenquam Israëlitarum, nedum insignen aliquam eorum multitudinem vitulum pro DE habuisse, qui ipsos eduxerit ex Ægypto, adeoqu ita stupidos, & stultos fuisse, ut crederent hun vitulum, quem nunc demum ex inauribus confla fecerant, antequam in rerum natura fuit, ipsos e Ægypto eduxisse? ideoque idololatria eorum no in eo sita fuit, quod vitulum crediderint esse ipsum met Deum, qui eos ex Ægypto eduxerat, sed quo in eodem Deum illum coluerint, contra DEI man datum de non faciendis idolis vel imaginibus, ut in iis Deus colatur. Nec aliud Ps. 106, 20. innuitur cum mutasse dicuntur honorem suum, id est, Deum, qui gloria ipsorum erat, in formam bovis; non enim id factum in bove fusili adorando vivum bovem, ac referendo adorationem ad creaturam illam bru- tam, non ad Deum: sic enim vivos boves in prom- tu habuissent, quos adorare potuissent, sed DEUM in forma bovis, qui herbam comedit, colendo: quum diserte Deus interdixerit, ne se repræsentarent sub forma alicujus animalis ad cultum expositi, vel ut adoretur Deus in eodem.

## 32:3
Ver. 3. AND THE PEOPLE DID WHAT HE HAD COMMANDED.

In the Hebrew: Breaking off, therefore, all that people took off their golden earrings for themselves. It is said to be understood generally of the whole people, of the whole community, not distributively of individuals: since very many of the sons of Levi were of Jehovah, and did not consent to that very idolatry, ver. 21, whom therefore God blessed, v. 29; therefore only some are called idolaters, 1 Cor. 10:7.

Latin:

Vers. 3. FECITQUE POPULUS QUÆ JUSSERAT.

In Ebræo: Rumpentes ergo detraxerunt sibi totus ille populus inaures aureas. De toto populo dicitur communiter accipiendum, de tota commu- nione, non distributive de singulis: siquidem filii Levi quam plurimi Jehovæ fuerint, nec in ipsam idolomanıam consenserint vers. 21. quibus proinde benedixit Deus v. 29. ideo quidam saltim dicuntur idololatræ, 1. Cor. 10, 7.

## 32:4
Ver. 4. AND HE MADE FROM THEM A CALF.

Not the head of a calf, as Cyprian, lib. de bon. nat., Ambrose, Epist. LXII, Jerome in Am. 5, Augustine in Psalm 37, wished, but a calf, and indeed, as can be gathered from Jeroboam's similar idolatry and the testimony of Josephus, lib. 8, c. 3, a heifer: which cannot be distinguished from the head. For the Egyptians, whom the Hebrews imitated, did not worship the head of a heifer, but the heifer, which they called Apis or Serapis. See Lactantius, l. IV, c. 10. But the Jews are foolish and ridiculous who invent fables that this molten calf was animated, walked, and ate, and that when Aaron saw this, he built an altar to it. Compare concerning this calf and the Apis of the Egyptians, Athanasius, quaest. 50, Jerome, Comm. in Hos. 4, Chemnitz, part 4, Exam. Conc. Trid. p. 42, Rainold, T. II, de libr. Apocryph. pag. 1, 97, 1244, Selden, de Dis. Syr. p. 136, Fuller, Miscell. l. 2, cap. 7, Cunaeus de Rep. Ebr. p. 335. Herodotus, l. 3, in Thalia, as translated by Valla, describes Apis thus: He is black over his whole body, having a brightness on his forehead of a square shape, on his back the likeness of an eagle, a beetle on his palate, and double hairs on his tail.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET FECIT EX EIS VITULUM.

Non vituli caput, ut Cyprian. lib. de bon. nat. Ambrof. Epist. LXII. Hieronym. in Am. 5. August. in Psalm. 37. voluit, sed vitulum, & quidem ut ex Je- roboami simili idololatria ac testimonio Josephi lib. 8. c. 3. colligere est vitulam: quæ è capite dignosci non potest. Non enim vitulæ caput colebant Ægyptii, quos imitati sunt Ebræi, sed vitulam, quam Apin vel Serapin dixere. Vid. Lactant. l. IV. c. 10. Inepti autem atque ridiculi sunt Judæi, qui fabulantur, hunc vitulum conflatilem animatum fuisse, ambulasse, comedisse, quod cum vidisset Aaron, altare ei ædificasse. Conf. de hoc vitulo & Api Ægyptior. Athanas. quæst. 50. Hieron. Comm. in Hos. 4. Chemnit. part. 4. Exam. Conc. Trid. p. 42. Rainold. T. II. de libr. Apocryph. pag. 1. 97. 1244. Selden. de Dis. Syr. p. 136. Fuller. Miscell. l. 2. cap. 7. Cunæus de Rep. Ebr. p. 335. Herodotus l. 3. in Tha- lia interprete Valla ita describit Apim: Toto cor- pore est niger, in fronte habens candorem, figuræ qua- dratæ, in tergo effigiem Aquilæ, cantharum in palato, duplices in cauda pilos.

## 32:5
Ver. 5. WHICH WHEN AARON HAD SEEN] The Rabbis add: and Hur slaughtered before him.

What Grotius means by this note and whence or how that addition comes about does not appear.

Ver. same. HE BUILT AN ALTAR BEFORE IT.

Aaron, therefore, cannot be excused, as if he did not consent because he was induced, but yielded because he was constrained, as Augustine, lib. 14, de Civ. Dei, and Bernard, Epist. 83, excuse him, because he freely built the altar himself and proclaimed a feast, whence in Deut. 9:20 it is said that GOD, stirred to anger against him, wished to destroy him, had not Moses intervened as a suppliant for him. Since, therefore, Aaron not only polluted himself with idolatry but also publicly sanctioned and instituted it among the people, and proclaimed an idolatrous feast, he who was then the head of the people and the Pontiff designated immediately by God, how do the Pontificians, who designate a Pontiff without God, maintain that he is infallible in promulgating decrees of faith? For what Cornelius objects, that he did not fail in faith, but in the profession of faith, just as Peter did not lose his faith but sinned against its confession, has nothing to do with the matter: where the question is, is the Pontiff infallible when promulgating decrees concerning faith and divine worship? Nor is it to be admitted in any way: because idolatry, like the denial of Christ, cannot in any way consist with faith. But that Aaron was made subject to idolatry, Abulensis, Cajetan, and Lorinus in this place and Acts 7:4, as also Esthius in this place, and even Cornelius à Lapide himself here acknowledges: and although he objects that he was not yet Pontiff then, elsewhere, however, Acts 7:41, from Cajetan in Ex. 32, he observes and approves the contrary; note, he says, that God permitted two HIGH PONTIFFS, one of the Old, the other of the New Testament, to slip in a matter as grave as was idolatry and the denial of Christ, namely St. Peter, and Aaron, that he might teach them, and their descendants, to sympathize with the lapses of their subjects. But what he says there, that the fear of death, and the fury of the people, and compulsion diminish the voluntary nature which is required for guilt and sin, in that he neither agrees with Scripture, which makes this sin so great that Aaron ought to have been cut off for it: nor with himself, who a little before in the same place had said: it is certain that Aaron sinned gravely here: because he ought rather to have exposed himself to death than to fashion an idol for the raging people. Thus Cyril of Jerusalem, Catech. 2.

Verse of the same. THE SOLEMNITY OF THE LORD IS] They hoped that the Spirit of the God whom they worshipped would come into that image, just as other nations thought concerning the spirits of the stars.

But whence is it evident to Grotius that the Jews cherished this opinion of the Gentiles, and hoped for that? Do the Papists perhaps hope for the same thing, when they adore divine images, that the Spirit of God comes into them, or when they venerate the statues of the saints, that their spirit is present in them, when they argue that the honor of the prototype can be deferred to them. So that that honor is not exhibited to the images and statues themselves, but to the Divinity or the Saint present in them. Therefore, will the male or female saints then leave heaven, or will they be omnipresent; will they be able to be in heaven equally, and everywhere present in images throughout the world? Absurd. Moreover, it is sufficiently manifest that the Israelites made themselves guilty of idolatry, not because they believed the golden calf was Jehovah himself, or that the Lord who had led them out of Egypt was truly in it in a peculiar way, but because they thought the calf was representatively Jehovah; and they both fashioned for themselves and worshipped God under the image of a calf. Because it is idolatry, both when another is worshipped than GOD, and when GOD is worshipped otherwise than in the divine manner, that is, which He Himself prescribed. But it seems that Grotius wished to introduce this fiction, so that the Papists, if they do not cherish that opinion about images animated by the Spirit of GOD, might not henceforth be compared to the idolatrous Israelites. But since Aaron, the leader of the calf-worship, was by no means so foolish as to believe that the calf which he himself had cast was the supreme God, or that he had been persuaded in the manner of the Gentiles that the Spirit of God would specifically come into this calf, why then is he himself, with the Israelites, accused of idolatry, 1 Cor. 10:7, Acts 7:41, unless it is because they served the true God in that calf as if in the image of the true God, against the express word of God, and thus bowed themselves to a molten image, and changed their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, Ps. 106:20. Just as there were also those from the Gentiles, as Augustine notes in Enarr. Psalm. 113.

conc. 13. they might say: I worship neither an image nor a demon, but through a physical likeness I contemplate the sign of that thing which I ought to worship: who nevertheless could by no means be absolved from idolatry.

Latin:

Vers. 5. QUOD CUM VIDISSET AARON] Addunt Rabbini: & Hurem coram se jugulatum.

Quid hac nota sibi velit Grotius & unde aut quomodo illud additamentum sese habeat, non apparet.

Vers. eod. ÆDIFICAVIT ALTARE CORAM EO.

Excusari ergo non potest Aaron, quasi non consenserit inductus, sed cesserit obstrictus, ut Au- gust. lib. 14. de Civ. Dei, & Bernhard, Epist. 83. eum excusat, quia libere ipse altare extruxit, & festum indixit, unde Deuter. 9, 20. dicitur DEUS ira in eum percitus eundem perdere voluisse, nisi pro eodem supplex intervenisset Moses. Quum er- go idololatria non se tantum polluerit Aaron, sed etiam publice penes populum eam sanciverit, atque instituerit, ac festum idololatricum promul- garit, qui tum caput populi, & Pontifex fuit à Deo immediate designatus, quomodo Pontificem, quem sine Deo designant Pontificii, infallibilem esse in promulgandis fidei decretis dictitant? Quod enim Cornelius excipit, non in fide defecisse, sed in pro- fessione fidei, sicut Petrus non fidem perdiderit, sed peccarit contra ejus confessionem, nihil ad rem facit: ubi quæstio est, an decreta circa fidem & cultum divinum promulgans Pontifex infallibilis est? nec ul- latenus admittendum : quia idololatria, ut & ab- negatio Christi cum fide nullo modo consistere po- test. Idololatriæ autem obnoxium factum esse Aaronem Abulensis, Cajetanus, & Lorin. in h. l. & Act. 7, 4. ut & Esthius in h. l. imo ipse Cornel. à La- pide hic agnoscit : & quanquam obvertat, eum tum nondum Pontificem fuisse, alibi tamen, Actor. 7, 41. è Cajetano in Ex. 32. contrarium observat, & ap- probat; nota, inquit, Deum permisisse duos SUM- MOS PONTIFICES, unum Veteris, alterum Novi Testam. labi in re tam gravi, qualis erat idolola- tria, & negatio Christi, scil. S. Petrum, & Aaronem, ut doceret eos, & posteros compati lapsibus subdito- rum. Quod autem illic ait, metum mortis, & fu- rorem populi ac coa­tionem minuere voluntarium, quod ad culpam & peccatum requiritur, in eo nec cum Scriptura consonat, quæ tantum hoc peccatum facit, ob quod exscindendus fuerat Aaron : nec secum ipso, qui paulo ante eodem loci dixerat: cer- tum est Aaronem hic graviter peccasse : quia debebat potius morti se exponere, quam furenti populo idolum fabricare. Ita Cyrill. Hieros. Catech. 2.

Vers. eod. SOLEMNITAS DOMINI EST] Sperabant Dei, quem colebant, Spiritum in eam imaginem venturum, sic- ut de astrorum spiritibus gentes aliæ senriebant.

Sed unde Grotio constat, hanc opinionem gentium fovisse Judæos, idque sperasse? Num for- te idem etiam sperant Papistæ, cum imagines divi- nas adorant, Dei Spiritum in illas venire, aut cum sanctorum statuas venerantur, spiritum ipsorum in illis præsto esse, cum prototypi honorem illis de- ferri posse disputant. Utita non exhibeatur ho- nos ille imaginibus & statuis ipsis, sed Numini aut Divo in illis præsenti. Sancti ergo sanctæve aut cœlum tunc relinquent, aut omnipræsentes erunt; In cœlo pariter, & passim in imaginibus per or- bem præsto esse poterunt? Ἄτοπον. Cæterum manifestum satis, Israëlitas idololatriæ se reos fecisse, non quod crederent, vitulum aureum Jehovam ipsum esse, aut in eo esse revera peculiari modo Do- minum, qui eduxerat eosdem ex Ægypto, sed quod repræsentative vitulum Jehovam esse putarent; De- umque sub imagine vituli & fingerent sibi & cole- rent. Quia idololatria est, & cum alius colitur, quam DEUS, & cum DEUS aliter colitur, quam divino modo, hoc est, quem ipse præscripsit. Vi- detur autem hoc commentum ingerere voluisse Grotium, ne Papistæ, si eam opinionem de imagi- nibus Spiritu DEI animatis haud foveant, Israëlitis Idololatriis deinceps componantur. Sed quum Aa- ron μοσχολατρείας antesignanus neutiquam adeo desipuerit, ut crediderit vitulum, quem ipse con- flaverat, supremum Deum esse, vel etiam Spiri- tum Dei peculiariter in hunc vitulum venturum, gentilium more persuasus fuerit, cur ergo ipse cum Israëlitis idololatrias arguatur, 1. Cor. 10, 7. Actor. 7, 41. nisi ideo, quod Deo vero in vitulo illo servie- rint tanquam in veri Dei imagine, adversus expref- sum Dei verbum, adeoque incurvarint se conflatili, & mutarint gloriam suam in exemplar bovis come- dentis herbam, Ps. 106. 20. Sicut etiam ex gentibus erant, qui, notante Augustino in Enarr. Psalm. 113.

conc. 13. dicerent: Nec simulacrum, nec Dæmonium colo, sed per effigiem corporalem ejus rei signum intueor, quam colere debeo: qui tamen ab idololatria absolvi minime poterant.

## 32:6
Verse same: THE PEOPLE SAT DOWN TO EAT AND TO DRINK, AND ROSE UP TO PLAY] To play here is to dance: Virgil to Silenus: Then indeed you might see Fauns and beasts in rhythm playing. Moreover, what is described here is a πανδησία (banquet), such as Suidas teaches us was held by the Egyptians in honor of Apis. See below 18,

Latin:

Vers. eodem: SEDIT POPULUS MANDUCARE ET BIBERE, ET SURREXERUNT LUDERE] Ludere hic est saltare: Virgilius Sileno: Tum vero in numerum Faunosq; fe- rasq; videres Ludere. Est autem quod hîc describitur πανδησία qualem actam Ægyptiis in Apidis honorem Suidas nos docet. Vide infra 18,

## 32:9
Verse 9. OF STIFF NECK.

This is, that the people are refractory and of invincible rebellion, a metaphor taken from untamed oxen or refractory heifers, which cannot accustom themselves to the yoke: which expression is frequent in the Scriptures. Deut. 9, 6. 13. ch. 31, 17. Isa. 42, 4. Jer. 7, 26. ch. 27, 23. Acts 7, 51.

Latin:

Vers. 9. DURÆ CERVICIS.

Hoc est, refractarium & invictæ rebellionis esse populum, metaphora à bobus indomitis: vel juvencis refractariis, qui jugo assuescere non pos- sunt, desumta: quæ loquutio frequens in Sacris est. Deut. 9, 6. 13. cap. 31, 17. Esa. 42, 4. Jerem. 7, 26. cap. 27, 23. Act. 7, 51.

## 32:10
Verse 10. LET ME ALONE,

He threatens the excision of the people in place of punishment, but in such a way that He shows the most splendid ray of His Φιλανθρωπίας (philanthropy) with this word, by which, according to Greg. M. l. 9. Moral. c. 12, He incites Moses, so that he might extinguish the fire of His fury with a shower of prayers. For what else is it to say to a servant 'let me alone,' than to offer the boldness of praying, as if it were said openly to him: weigh how much you are worth to me, and if you pray for anything, how easily you might obtain it. Thus He insinuates ανθρωποπαθω̃ς (anthropopathically) that Moses could detain Him by his intercession, so that He might at once sharpen and commend to the people the charity of Moses, to whom He had given the option, because He wished to make Moses into a great nation if they were destroyed, that is, to give him a numerous posterity, so that in him the promises made to the Fathers might be fulfilled, even with the rebellious people exterminated. Compare Gen. 12, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 10. DIMITTE ME,

Minatur pœnæ loco excisionem populi, sed ita, ut Φιλανθρωπίας suæ radium splendidissimum hac voce ostendat, qua juxta Gregor. M. l. 9. Mo- ral. c. 12. accendit Mosen, ut ignem furoris sui pre- cum imbre extinguat. Quid enim est aliud servo di- cere dimitte me, quam precandi audaciam præbe- re, ac si aperte diceretur ei: expende quantum apud me valeas, & si quid ores, quam facile obtinere illud queas. Ita ανθρωποπαθω̃ς insinuat, Mosen se deti- nere posse deprecatione sua, ut acueret simul atque populo commendaret Mosis charitatem, cui optionem dederat, quod illis deletis Mosen in gen- tem magnam facere velit, id est, numerosam dare posteritatem, ut in ipso implerentur promissiones Patribus factæ, etiam exterminato rebelli populo. Confer. Gen. 12, 2.

## 32:13
Verse 13. REMEMBER ABRAHAM, ISAAC AND ISRAEL.

As regards the covenant and the promises concerning the Messiah, and confirmed to them by oath on account of the Messiah, as is added: to whom you swore by yourself, but not as regards their intercession in heaven for the same: Because Abraham is ignorant of us, and Israel does not know us, Isa. 63, 16. nor did Moses as it were allege the merits of the Saints, but that he might recall to GOD the covenant entered into with the Patriarchs. Conf. 2 Kings 8, 25. Dan. 9, 17. for the tribe of Judah being destroyed, how could the Messiah have come forth from it? Whence those words of the Lord seem to be: 'Let me alone' etc. spoken πειραστικω̃ς (temptingly) to Moses, because the Lord could not rescind the categorical, not hypothetical, promise concerning the Messiah arising from the tribe of Judah. Otherwise, the Israelites having been destroyed, He could have entirely made Moses into a great nation.
