And therefore also Moses' reason from the oath of GOD, 'I will multiply your seed' etc., did not bind except by the force of the covenant sanctioned through Christ. The reason from the merit of the Fathers which Bellarmine pretends, l. 1. de Beat. Sanct. cap. 19, is here alleged to be rejected by the saints themselves, Deut. 9, 4. ch. 10, 14. Ezek. 16, 3. 6. Hos. 9, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 13. RECORDARE ABRAHAM, ISAAC ET ISRAEL.

Quantum ad fœdus, & promissiones de Messia, & propter Messiam juramento ipsis firmatas, ut additur: quibus jurasti per temetipsum, non vero quoad deprecationem ipsorum in cœlis, pro iisdem: Quia Abraham ignorat nos, & Israël nescit nos, Esa. 63, 16. nec quasi allegarit Moses merita Sanctorum, sed quod fœdus cum Patriarchis initum DEO in memoriam revocaret. Conf. 2. Reg. 8, 25. Dan. 9, 17. deleta enim tribu Juda, quomodo ex eadem prodire potuisset Messias? Unde videntur illa Domini: Dimitte me &c. πειραστικω̃ς ad Mo- sen dicta, quia non poterat Dominus promissio- nem de Messia ex tribu Juda oriundo, catego- ricam, non hypotheticam rescindere. De cæ- tero omnino potuisset deletis Israëlitis reliquis Mosen in gentem magnam facere. Atque ideo etiam Ratio Mosis à juramento DEI, multiplicabo se- men vestrum &c. non stringebat nisi vi fœderis per Christum sanciti. Rationem à merito Patrum quam prætendit Bellarm. l. 1. de Beat. Sanct. cap. 19. hic allegari reprobant ipsimet sancti, Deut. 9, 4. cap. 10, 14. Ezech. 16, 3. 6. Hos. 9, 10.

## 32:14
Verse 14. AND THE LORD WAS APPEASED, THAT HE MIGHT NOT DO EVIL.

There is no change here in God. For what He had said He would do, was spoken in the threatening both πειραστικω̃ς (temptingly) and ὑποθετικω̃ς (hypothetically), if He wished to take account of the sins of the people, the gravity of which He so insinuated, and unless Moses intervened in the breach before the Lord, Ps. 106, 27. but now He defines absolutely that He will not do it, because God did not wish to deal with the people according to their merits, and He left room out of mercy for the intervention of Moses by the power of the intercession of Christ, our eternal mediator shadowed forth in Moses, and rendering his intercession valid. Rightly Greg. M. l. 20. Moral., just as when the Lord strikes faults, He is said to be angry, although He is moved by no perturbation of mind, so when He Himself, being immutable, changes what He willed, He is said to repent, although He changes the thing, He does not change His counsel.

Latin:

Vers. 14. PLACATUSQUE EST DOMINUS, NE FACERET MALUM.

Nulla hîc in Deo mutatio. Nam quod se fa- cturum dixerat, in comminatione tum πειραστικω̃ς, tum ὑποθετικω̃ς dictum fuit, si peccatorum populi rationem habere vellet, quorum gravitatem ita infi- nuavit, ac nisi Moses, in ruptura coram Domino in- terveniret Ps. 106, 27. nunc vero absolute definit, se non facturum, quia noluit Deus pro meritis cum populo agere, & interventioni Mosis vi interces- sionis Christi, æterni mediatoris nostri in Mose adumbrati, ejusque intercessionem ratani reddentis locum ex misericordia reliquit. Recte Gregor. M. l. 20. Moral. sicut cum culpas percutit Dominus, di- citur irasci, quamvis nulla animi perturbatione mo- veatur, sic cum ipse immutabilis id, quod voluerit, mutat, pœnitere dicitur, quamvis rem mutet, consilium non mutet.

## 32:16
Vers. 16. WRITTEN ON BOTH SIDES.

The Decalogue was not written here once on the front side and again on the back, as is done with hanging tablets, which some have supposed on the occasion of the Vulgate; but since עבריהם signifies two faces, or the front parts of the tablets, Oleastrius thinks they were closed in the manner of the tablets of a book, which not only corresponds better to the name, but also to their reverence and custody, since closed tablets preserved the law better, in the judgment of Rivetus.

Latin:

Vers. 16. SCRIPTAS EX UTRAQUE PARTE.

Non hic fuit scriptus Decalogus, semel a parte anteriori, atque iterum a posteriori, ut in pensilibus tabulis fit, quod nonnulli occasione Vulgatæ arbitra- ti sunt, sed quum עבריהם duas facies significet, aut anteriores partes tabularum, clausas eas fuisse ad modum tabularum libri censet Oleastrius, quod non solum nomini melius respondet, sed etiam reveren- tiæ illarum & custodiæ, quoniam tabulæ clausæ me- lius servabant legem, judice Riveto.

## 32:18
Vers. 18. THE VOICE OF THEM THAT SING] Correctly from the Hebrew.

Less correctly, the Samaritan Codices [have] ענו, which the Greek Scholiasts translate as φωνὴν ἁμαρτιῶν.

Latin:

Vers. 18. VOCEM CANTANTIUM] Recte ex Hebræo.

Minus recte Samaritani Codices ענו quod Græci Scho- liastæ vertunt φωνὴν ἁμαρτιῶν.

## 32:20
Vers. 20. WHICH HE STREWED UPON THE WATER]

He cast it into the torrent, Deut. 9, 21. What was accustomed to be done with Apis out of superstition, he did with the pulverized [gold] as a punishment. Papinius in the Protrepticon to Metius Celer: Or into what whirlpool of the Nile does the adored Apis plunge himself for the trembling shepherds.

All these things were done out of heroic zeal, and not without the impulse of the Holy Spirit, concerning which Hugo Victorinus rashly doubts, that he broke the tablets, even though made and signed by the hand of God, that he burned the calf and ground it even to dust, that he strewed it into the water and gave it to the children of Israel to drink, which calf he calls the sin of the Israelites because it was an idol, Deut. 9, 21, so that he might designate the atrocity of the sin to the men, and teach the people to despise that idol, which was worshipped with such great honor, [by showing that it] was received into the bowels of those eating and passed into dung, which he had seen could be cast into the privy. For the torrent descending from the mountain flowed down into the camp of the Israelites situated below, nor was there any other water in the camp than that which overflowed from this torrent.

Vers. same. HE MADE THEM DRINK.

It was not water of trial, such as in Num. 5, 17. That is a fiction of the Hebrews. He offered the water of this gold for drink to the ignominy of the false gods, who are consumed by their own worshippers and cast out through the privy, truly dung-gods.

Latin:

Vers. 20. QUEM SPARSIT IN AQUAM]

Projecit in torrentem Deut. 9, 21. quod Apide fieri solebat per superstitio- nem, id comminuto fecit in pœnam. Papinius Propremptico Metii Celeris: Aut quo se gurgite Nili Mergat adoratus trepi- dis pastoribus Apis.

Omnia hæc ex Zelo heroico, nec sine impulsu Spiritus S. de quo temere dubitat Hugo Victorinus, facta, quod tabulas fregerit, etiamsi manu Dei fa- ctas & consignatas, quod vitulum combusserit, & ad pulverem usq; contriverit, quod in aquam spar- serit, & ex eo potum filiis Israel dederit, quem vi- tulum peccatum Israëlitarum vocat, quia idolum erat, Deut. 9, 21. ut peccati atrocitatem homini- bus designaret, atque idolum istud tanto populi ho- nore cultum inter vescentium viscera receptum in fimum abiisse populumq; ita contemnere doceret, quod in secessu projici posse viderat. Torris enim ex monte descendens delabebatur in castra Israëli- tarum subjecta, nec alia in castris erat aqua, quam quæ ex hoc torrente redundabat.

Vers. eod. BIBERE FECIT.

Non fuit aqua probatoria, qualis Num. V, 17. Ebræorum id commentum est. Præbuit auri hu- jus aquam in potum in ignominiam falsorum Deorum, qui a propriis cultoribus absumuntur, & per secessum ejiciuntur, vere Dii stercorarii.

## 32:22
Vers. 22. THAT HE IS PRONE TO EVIL] In the Hebrew: Thou knowest the people, that it is in evil, ἐν τῷ πονηρῷ κεῖται: 1 John 5, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 22. QUOD PRONUS SIT IN MALUM] In Hebræo: Nosti populum, quod in malo est, ἐν τῷ πονηρῷ κεῖται: 1. Joh. 5, 19.

## 32:25
Vers. 25. NAKED] Unarmed.

Vers. same. FOR AARON HAD STRIPPED HIM.

He had despoiled him of his glory, which was the true God, and thus the people had been so stripped, which the LXX do not render so conveniently as 'scattered', others more correctly as that the people had been cast off: but the Vulgate holds itself well: Moses therefore seeing the people, that it had been stripped, (For Aaron had despoiled him on account of the ignominy or infamy: the LXX have ἐπίχαρμα, a laughingstock, filth, and he had set him naked among enemies) because to those destitute of their glory, the true God, nothing else remained on account of the ignominious idol, which was also reduced by Moses into the highest ignominy joined with filth, therefore indeed naked among enemies, and despoiled of their fame and glory, who previously were called worshippers of the one GOD, now having become most base idolaters, they contracted the highest ignominy, and could deservedly be held in contempt: who, knowing them to be worshippers of idols, would easily rise up against them, destitute of the protection of their GOD.

Latin:

Vers. 25. NUDATUS] Inermis.

Vers. eod. SPOLIAVERAT ENIM EUM AARON.

Spoliaverat eum gloria sua, quæ erat verus Deus, adeoque ita nudatus erat populus, quod non ita commode reddunt LXX. dissipatus, alii rectius, quod abjectus esset populus: sed probe se habet Vulgata: videns ergo Moses populum, quod esset nudatus, (Spoliaverat enim eum Aaron propter igno- miniam vel infamiam: LXX. ἐπίχαρμα ludibrium habent, sordes, & inter hostes nudum constituerat) quia destitutis gloria sua, Deo vero, nihil supere- rat aliud propter ignominiosum idolum, quod in ignominiam summam cum sorde conjunctam eti- am redactum a Mose fuit, ideo vero inter hostes nudi, & fama ac gloria sua spoliati, quæ antea unius DEI cultores dicti, jam turpissimi idololatræ facti, summam ignominiam contrahebant, & comtemti merito haberi poterant: qui scientes eos idolo- rum cultores, in eos DEI sui protectione destitutos facile insurgerent.

## 32:26
Vers. 26. AND STANDING IN THE GATE OF THE CAMP.

In the ordinary place of judgment, he says, if anyone is the Lord's, let him be joined to me. He makes and promulgates a decree: and at the same time executes it: but he called them the Lord's to be those who, repenting in time, adhere to GOD with true faith and piety, or rather, those who had been peculiarly consecrated to the Lord. For all the sons of Levi are said to have gathered to him. Concerning this process, Gregory the Great beautifully says in the same place: 'A legate on both sides, a strong man, an admirable mediator on both sides, he pleaded the cause of the people before GOD with prayers, and the cause of GOD before the people with swords. Loving within, he resisted the divine wrath by supplicating; raging without, he consumed the guilt by striking; he succored all more quickly by showing the death of a few. And therefore almighty GOD heard his faithful servant more quickly as he acted for the people, because He saw that he would act for GOD over the people.' In the governance of the people, however, Moses mingled both, so that discipline might not be lacking to mercy, nor mercy to discipline.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET STANS IN PORTA CASTRORVM.

Ordinario judicii loco, ait, si quis est Domini, jungatur mihi. Decretum facit & promulgat: atque exsequitur simul: Domini autem eos dixit esse, qui mature resipiscentes vera fide & pietate DEO adhaerescunt, vel potius, qui Domino pe- culiariter consecrati erant. Siquidem dicuntur ad eum omnes filii Levi congregati. De hoc processu pulcre Gregor. M. l. c. Utrobique legatus, fortis, utrobique mediator admirabilis, causam populi apud DEUM precibus, causam DEI apud popu- lum gladiis allegavit. Intus amans, irae divinae sup- plicando obstitit: foris saeviens culpam feriendo con- sumsit, succurrit citius omnibus, ostensa morte pauco- rum. Et idcirco omnipotens DEUS fidelem famu- lum suum citius exaudivit agentem pro populo, quia vidit, quod super populum acturus esset pro DEO. In regimine autem populi utrumque Moses miscuit, ut nec disciplina deesset misericordiae, nec misericordia disciplinae.

## 32:27
Verse 27. THROUGH THE MIDST OF THE CAMP.

They are not commanded, with exquisite diligence applied—which Moncaeus asserts, imagining that the ignominious ulcers from which those who were to be killed could be distinguished arose in the Israelites from the drunk water mixed with the gold of the idol—but to strike whomever GOD made them encounter without investigation; whether they were associates, or friends, or brothers. What is said concerning brothers, however, must be understood a little more generally; for they cannot properly be understood as brothers, or at least any from the tribe of Levi; because all of these are said to have been employed for the execution; therefore none of them were struck.

Latin:

Vers. 27. PER MEDIUM CASTRORUM.

Non jubentur exquisita diligentia adhibita, quod Moncaeus statuit, ignominiosa ulcera unde di- gnosci quiverint, qui occidendi sint fingens, in Israëli- tis ex epota aqua auro idoli mixta oriunda, sed quos- cunque ipsis DEUS occurrere fecerit sine discuf- sione, percutere; seu socii, seu amici, seu fratres fuerint. Quod tamen de fratribus dicitur, acci- piendum est paulo generalius; nam proprie fra- tres intelligi nequeunt, aut aliqui saltim de stirpe Levi; quia hi omnes dicuntur ad exequutionem adhibiti; non ergo feriebantur ulli ex iisdem.

## 32:28
Verse 28. ABOUT TWENTY-THREE THOUSAND.

The Vulgate added twenty thousand: nor did the Pontiffs amend this, even though the Chaldean, the LXX, and other interpreters, and even certain Latin copies of the Hebrew, entirely agree. Behold the illustrious correctors! Behold the Papal infallibility, which reveals itself likewise in countless places! If they looked to the passage 1 Corinthians 10:8, that is a new oversight. For it would be of excessive ignorance not to have understood that a far different history is designated there, which is held, namely, in Numbers 26:9.

Latin:

Vers. 28. QUASI VIGINTI TRIA MILLIA.

Addidit Vulgata viginti millia: nec id emen- darunt Pontifices, etsi Ebraeo Chaldaeus, LXX. alii- que interpp. Latina etiam quaedam exemplaria prorsus consentiant. En praeclaros correcto- res! En Papalem infallibilitatem, quae in in- numeris locis pariter se prodit! Si respexere ad locum 1. Corinth. 10, 8. novum id παρόραμα. Ibi enim historiam longe aliam, quae scil. Num. 26, 9. habetur, designari, nimiae imperitiae fuerit, quod non intellexerint.

## 32:29
Verse 29. AND MOSES SAID.

These things are to be rendered thus: For Moses had said: because before the execution it was said to the sons of Levi, and the word מלאו is an imperative: consecrate your hands today to the Lord: so that they might understand that by that action they would consecrate their hands to God, and would bring back the divine blessing: which is also observed here by Lipomanus. Cf. Deut. 33:9.

Latin:

Vers. 29. ET AIT MOSES.

Haec ita reddenda: Nam dixerat Moses: quia ante exequutionem dicta filiis Levi, & verbum מלאו imperativum est: consecrate manus vestras ho- die Domino: ut intelligerent, se ea actione manus suas Deo consecraturos, & benedictionem divi- nam relaturos: quod hic etiam Lipomano observa- tum. Conf. Deut. 33, 9.

## 32:30
Verse 30. IF BY ANY MEANS I MAY BE ABLE TO ENTREAT HIM.

These are not the words of one doubting, but of one hoping well, just as the word אולי is accustomed to excite to good hope, and not for the sake of casting in doubt, Joel 2:14, Jonah 3:9, Zephaniah 1:3, which R. Solomon also makes a particle of wishing, Gen. 50:15; indeed, that those words are of asserting, not of doubting—'perhaps,' 'perchance,' 'peradventure'—in the Vulgate version, Josh. 14:12 (Cf. Num. 14:24, 25), 1 Sam. 14:6, 2 Sam. 16:12 (Cf. 2 Sam. 7:10), is clear, nor does Salmero deny it, Proleg. 16, p. 320, that they are often taken for 'truly,' 'undoubtedly,' 'altogether,' 'certainly,' 'indeed,' Ps. 50:54, etc. Cornelius à Lapide in Chapter 32 of Genesis, p. 118, says that the little word 'perchance' is not of one doubting but of one affirming and continuing. Although if there is any doubt in this place, it concerns not the forgiveness of sins, but of temporal punishments. Whence it would do nothing for the Pontifical dogma concerning the uncertainty of the grace of justification. In which way the passages Joel 2:14. Jonah 3:4. Sanctius and Castrius accept it, namely, concerning the mitigation of afflictions or castigations, which GOD sends upon His own even after reconciliation for testing and amendment; thus also Tirinus explains the passage Joel 2:14, and to that opinion he also brings Jerome, Theodoret, Rufinus, and Rupert.

Latin:

Vers. 30. SI QUOMODO QUIVERO EUM DEPRECARI.

Haec non dubitantis, sed bene sperantis verba sunt, uti vox אולי solet ad spem bonam excitare, non vero dubitationis injiciendae causa Joel. 2, 14. Jon. 3, 9. Soph. 1, 3. quam etiam optantis particu- lam facit R. Salomo Gen. 50, 15. imo asserendi vo- ces illas esse, non ambigendi, forte, forsan, forsitan, in Vulgata versione Jos. 14, 12. (Conf. Numer. 14, 24. 25.) 1. Sam. 14, 6. 2. Sam. 16, 12. (Conf. 2. Sam. 7, 10.) luculentum est, nec diffitetur id Salmero Pro- leg. 16. p. 320. saepe eas capi pro sane, haud dubie, prorsus, certe, utique Ps. 50, 54. &c. Cornel. à Lap. in Cap. 32. Gen. p. 118. voculam forsitan non dubitan- tis sed affirmantis & continuantis esse, ait. Quan- quam si hoc loco dubitatio ulla sit, ea non pecca- torum, sed temporalium poenarum veniam con- cernat. Unde nihil ea faceret ad Pontificium dogma de incertitudine gratiae justificationis. Quo pacto loca Joel 2, 14. Jon. 3, 4. Sanctius, & Castrius accipiunt, de mitigatione nempe affli- ctionum, aut castigationum, quas DEUS suis etiam post reconciliationem immittit in probatio nem & emendationem, sic etiam Tirinus ex- plicat locum Joel 2, 14. & in eam sententiam ad- ducit quoque Hieronymum, Theodoretum, Ruffinum & Rupertum.

## 32:31
Ver. 31. AND RETURNING TO THE LORD HE SAYS.

Tostatus and others maintain that these things, and what is further reported that Moses did with the Lord, happened after his repeated ascent into the mountain: because, forsooth, Moses said before in v. 30, I will go up unto the Lord, if by any means I might reconcile him. But Moses did not go up to the Lord into the mountain unless commanded by the Lord, which was finally done in ch. 34, 1, 2, after other stone tablets had been hewn out. And therefore, even if he says here I WILL GO UP to the Lord, this is not to be understood of that ascent into the mountain, in which he spent 40 days there with the Lord and brought the tablets of the law with him to the Lord: but he says that he wishes to meet the Lord for the sake of intercession and supplication: otherwise it would have to be said that he climbed the mountain again and again, and that this was done even without GOD'S command, and this historical narrative would be rendered obscure by various prolepses, as can be seen in Tostatus. (Conf. what is at ch. 33, 4.) which, on account of the word ASCENT alone, seems by no means to be admitted; which sometimes, though more rarely, denotes only a departure, without an elevation to a higher place, Isa. 11, 24, ch. 23, 46, Exod. 3, 17, and the place in which Moses spoke with GOD could have been higher, even if he did not ascend the Mountain to GOD. For that solemn ascent was instituted for the sake of dwelling there with God and receiving the law anew, according to the express command of God, and after the reconciliation of the people with God.

Latin:

Vers. 31. REVERSUSQUE AD DOMINUM AIT.

Hæc & quæ porro egisse cum Domino refertur Moses, Tostatus & alii post ascensum ejus in montem iteratum contigisse volunt: quia nempe antea dixit Moses v. 30. Ascendi ad Dominum, si quomodo qui- vero eum reconciliare. Sed non ascendit Moses ad Dominum in montem, nisi jussus à Domino, quod demum factum c. 34, 1. 2. excisis tabulis aliis lapi- deis. Ideoque etsi hîc dicat ASCENDAM ad Dominum, non de illo ascensu in montem hoc ac- cipiendum, quo per 40. dies cum Domino ibi egit, tabulasque legis secum ad Dominum addu- xit: sed convenire se Dominum velle intercessio- nis & deprecationis causa ait: alioquin dicen- dum foret iterum iterumque montem conscen- disse, idque etiam factum esse citra DEI jussum, & Historica hæc narratio per diversas προλήψεις obscura reddetur, ut apud Tostat. videre est. (Conf. quæ ad cap. 33, 4.) quod ob solum ASCENSUS verbum minime admittendum videtur; quod quandoque, licet rarius, solum profectionem no- tat, citra elevationem in altiorem locum Esa. 11, 24. cap. 23, 46. Exod. 3, 17. & potuit locus sublimior esse, in quo cum DEO loquutus est Moses, etsi non ascenderit in Montem ad DEUM. Solemnis enim ille ascensus ibidem cum Deo commorandi & legem denuo accipiendi gratia institutus est juxta expressum Dei mandatum, & post reconciliationem populi cum Deo.

## 32:33
V. 33. WHOSOEVER HATH SINNED AGAINST ME, HIM WILL I BLOT OUT OF MY BOOK] Against me, that is, in opposition to me, I being despised, which the Greeks well express by ἐνώπιόν μου. See Rom. 9, fol. 150.

Latin:

V. 33. QVI PECCAVERIT MIHI, DELEBO EVM DE LIBRO MEO] Mihi, id est, adversum me, me comtemto, quod Græci bene exprimunt ἐνώπιόν με. Vid. Rom. 9. fol. 150.

## 32:34
Ver. 34. BUT I IN THE DAY OF VENGEANCE WILL VISIT AND THIS SIN OF THEIRS.

It is asked, what is that day of vengeance? Cornelius à Lapide, with Rabbi Solomon and Abulensis, understands it of that day which is treated of in verse 33, and takes the following words, the Lord therefore struck the people, as referring to some plague sent shortly after on account of that idol, e.g., a pestilence. Osiander explains it of the time when it shall please GOD to punish the impenitent with eternal destruction; others, however, explain it of the time of the Babylonian captivity; others finally, like Pelargus and Junius, explain it of the time of exile and wandering in the desert, during which they were all destroyed; and they interpret the words of v. 35 concerning the preceding slaughter by way of recapitulation. Of which opinions the first seems the most convenient, because verse 35 refers itself to the preceding: and as the Lord threatens in verse 34 some peculiar visitation, not particular but common, so the execution of the same threatening is subjoined immediately in v. 35.

Latin:

Vers. 34. EGO AUTEM IN DIE ULTIONIS VISITABO ET HOC PECCATUM EORUM.

Quis dies ille ultionis sit, quæritur? De die illo, quo de vers. 33. agitur, intelligit Cornel. à Lap. cum R. Salomone & Abulensi, ac verba sequentia, percussit ergo Dominus populum, de plaga quadam accipit ob idolum illud paulo post immissa, v. g. peste. Osiander de tempore, quod DEO placue- rit impœnitentes æterno exitio punituro, alii au- tem de tempore captivitatis Babylonicæ, alii deni- que ut Pelargus & Junius de tempore exilii & pe- regrinationis in deserto explicant, quo interemti omnes sunt; & verba v. 35. de cæde præcedente κατ' ἀνακεφαλαίωσιν interpretantur. E quibus sententiis prima videtur convenientissima, quia versus 35. ad præcedentem sese refert: & ut peculiarem aliquam visitationem non particularem, sed communem mi- natur Dominus vers. 34. sic subjungitur ejusdem comminationis exequutio statim v. 35.

## 33:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIII. The repentance of the people. The face of GOD.

Ver. 1. AND THE LORD SPOKE.

Tremellius and Junius take it in the pluperfect, Jehovah had indeed proclaimed, so that these things may be referred to those which are contained in ch. 32, 4. But it is more correctly established that this is a preparation for the repentance of the people, which is treated of in the following.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIII. Resipiscentia populi. Facies DEI.

Vers. 1. LOQUUTUSQUE EST DOMINUS.

IN plusquamperfecto accipit Tremellius & Ju- nius edixerat autem Jehovah, ut referantur hæc ad ea, quæ cap. 32, 4. habentur. Sed rectius sta- tuitur hic præparatio ad pœnitentiam populi, de qua in sequentibus agitur.

## 33:2
Ver. 2. AND I WILL SEND A PRECURSOR ANGEL.

The Lord does not promise this now, but testifies that He promised it beforehand, and therefore these things cohere thus: Go, ascend into the land which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, I will give it to your seed, and I will send a precursor Angel: in the Hebrew: an Angel (the only-begotten Son) before your face, etc. He had promised these things before, but now He threatens the contrary: I will not ascend with you, because you are a stiff-necked people, i.e., because the people soon violated my covenant, which they had struck, and do not even today acknowledge, as is right, such a sin, I am no longer bound to them to bring them into that land: you therefore go with your people, by whatever way shall seem best: I will no longer take care of you: I will be neither your leader nor your companion, as Osiander rightly says. Therefore there is no need to inquire anxiously with Augustine whether an angel can have greater mercy than God, or with Rivetus to say that God the Father is described as less indulgent and bearing with sinners, but the Angel as less prone to vengeance. For the Father and the Son are one, John 10:30. Conf. Exod. 23:20. This judgment of God, however, is not definitive, but only interlocutory and conditional, as is evident from the following. And thus verse 12 fits perfectly: you command that I lead this people and you do not indicate to me whom you will send with me, i.e., and you deny that you will go along, nor do you signify whose guidance we ought to follow.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET MITTAM PRÆCURSOREM ANGE- LUM.

Hoc nunc non promittit Dominus, sed se antea promisisse testatur, ideoque cohærent hæc ita : Vade ascende in terram, quam juravi Abraham, Isaac, & Jacob, dicens, femini tuo dabo eam, & mittam præcur- sorem Angelum: in Ebræo: ante faciem tuam Angelum (Filium unigenitum) &c. Hæc promiserat antea, sed jam minatur contrarium: Non ascendam tecum, quia populus duræ cervicis es, q. d. quia populus fœ- dus meum, quod pepigerat, mox violavit, ac ne ho- die quidem agnoscit, ut par est, tantum peccatum, non sum illi amplius obstrictus, ut eum introducam in istam terram: tu ergo vade cum populo tuo, qua via videbitur: ego vestri curam non amplius geram: nec dux nec comes vester ero, ut recte Osiander. Ideo opus non est cum Augustino anxie quærere, anne majorem misericordiam habere angelus possit, quam Deus, aut cum Riveto dicere, Deum Patrem ut minus conniventem, & peccatores ferentem, Angelum autem ut minus pronum ad vindictam describi. Pater enim & Filius unum sunt, Joh. 10, 30. Conf. Exod. 23, 20. Hæc tamen sententia Dei non est definitiva, sed interlocutoria tantum, & conditionalis, ut è seqq. pa- tet. Atque ita v. 12. apprime congruit: præcipis, ut educam populum istum & non indicas mihi quem mis- surus es mecum, q. d. & negas te una profecturum, ne- que significas, cujus ductum sequi debeamus.

## 33:4
Verse 4. THEY MOURNED AND NO ONE PUT ON HIS ATTIRE ACCORDING TO CUSTOM.

Cornelius, with Abulensis, determines that these things concerning the repentance of the people and the public mourning were not inserted in their order by the command of God, but were spoken by prolepsis. But there is no necessity for anticipation: for God did not institute this conversation with Moses on the mountain, which they suppose, but these things happened before the repeated ascent into the mountain, concerning which Moses finally received a command after this conversation in chapter 34, verse 2: whence there is no need to imagine as if he descended from the mountain again after that conversation, and cut the tablets, and ascended to God with them: since he received the command about cutting the tablets and ascending the mountain after this conversation was finished. Conf. Exod. 34:28.

Latin:

Vers. 4. LUXIT ET NULLUS EX MORE INDUTUS EST CULTU SUO.

Hæc de pœnitentia populi & luctu publico ex man- dato Dei instituto non inferta esse ordine suo, sed per prolepsin dicta cum Abulensi Cornelius statuit. Sed nulla est anticipationis necessitas: non enim hoc colloquium Deus cum Mose in monte instituit, quod illi supponunt, sed hæc ante iteratum ascensum in montem, de quo demum post hoc colloquium c. 34, 2. mandatum accepit Moses, contigere: unde non opus est, fingere quasi post colloquium illud de monte descenderit denuo, & tabulas exciderit, ac cum iisdem ad Deum ascenderit: quum finito hoc colloquio acceperit mandatum de excindendis ta- bulis, & monte conscendendo. Conf. Exod. 34, 28.

## 33:5
Verse 5. I WILL ASCEND ONCE IN THE MIDST OF YOU, AND I WILL DESTROY YOU.

These things are obscure: but the Hebrew text is clear enough: In one moment I will ascend in the midst of you and I will destroy you: i.e., if I were to ascend with you, it could easily happen that I would suddenly be moved to anger because of your contumacy, and destroy you in a moment: or rather simply and categorically, as Luther says, You are a stiff-necked people, I will one day suddenly come upon you, and destroy you. They are therefore commanded to lay aside their ornaments, and so, as is customary to be done in public penitential mourning, to put on sackcloth and ashes or the vilest clothing, and to mourn their sin with serious acts of repentance. Conf. 1 Kings 21, Jonah 3, Dan. 9.

THAT I MAY SEE WHAT I SHALL DO TO YOU.

God speaks ἀνθρωποπαθῶς, after the manner of a man who learns from new events what he must do: that is to say, I will conduct myself after the fashion of one who learns from events, so that I may know from your works of repentance what good or evil I should do to you.

Latin:

Vers. 5. SEMEL ASCENDAM IN MEDIO TUI, ET DELEBO TE.

Obscura hæc sunt: Ebræus vero textus luculentus satis: Momento uno ascendam in medio tui & delebo te: i. e. si tecum ascenderem, facile contingere posset, ut subito ira commoverer, propter contumaciam tuam, teque momento delerem: vel potius simplici- ter & categorice, ut Lutherus, Ihr seyd ein halsstar- rig Volck, Ich werde einmal plötzlich über dich kom- men, und dich vertilgen. Jubentur ergo deponere or- natum suum, adeoque, ut in publico luctu pœniten- tiali fieri consuevit, saccum & cilicium seu vilissimum vestitum induere, ac peccatum suum seria acta pœni- tentia, lugere. Conf. 1. Reg. 21. Jon. 3. Dan. 9.

UT VIDEAM, QUID FACIAM TIBI.

Loquitur Deg ἀνθρωποπαθῶς more hominis ex factis novis cognoscentis, quid faciendum sibi sit: q. d. ad in- star cognoscentis ex factis me geram, ut scia ex ope- ribus tuis pœnitentiæ, quid boni vel mali tibi facia.

## 33:7
Verse 7. MOSES ALSO TAKING THE TABERNACLE PITCHED IT OUTSIDE THE CAMP] For himself, the Hebrew text adds. Understand the tent of Moses, which served in place of the sacred tent not yet made.

He wished to testify by this symbol that the camp had contracted uncleanness from the worship of the idol, and to admonish the people of their unworthiness, because of which God refused to dwell in the midst of the camp. Therefore he pitched that TABERNACLE outside the camp, i.e., that which was his own: for the public one, which ought to have been like a portable temple for the whole people, was not yet constructed, much less erected: nor yet was it a merely private tabernacle, because Moses was the leader of the people, and the elders were accustomed to gather there with Moses to hold council: and the pillar of cloud rested upon it, and God manifested Himself there. There, therefore, God instituted the conversation with Moses, which is described here. Grotius's observation is therefore correct here.

Latin:

Vers. 7. MOSES QVOQVE TOLLENS TABERNA- CULUM TETENDIT EXTRA CASTRA] Sibi, addit textus Hebræus. Tentorium Mosis intellige, quod vice fuit sacri tentorii nondum facti.

Testari voluit hoc Symbolo, immundiciem castra contraxisse ex cultu idoli, & admonere po- pulum indignitatis suæ, propter quam Deus detre- ctaret habitare in medio castrorum. Ideo extra ca- stra tetendit TABERNACULUM illud, sc. quod ipsi proprium erat: nam publicum, quod instar tem- pli portatilis esse toti populo debebat, nondum erat constructum, nedum erectum: neque tamen id merum privatum erat tabernaculum, quia Moses erat populi dux, eoque convenire solebant seniores cum Mose concilium acturi : & incumbebat ei columna nubis, ac Deus ibi se manifestabat. Illic ergo colloquium instituit Deus cû Mose, quod hîc describitur. Recte ergo hic se habet Grotii observatio.

## 33:11
V. 11. BUT THE LORD SPOKE. Not some created angel, as the Papist interpreters wish, but the Lord Himself spoke with Moses in person. Because one must not depart from the letter of the text without reason: nor are theophanies and angelophanies to be confused.

Latin:

V. 11. LOQUEBATUR AUTEM DOMINUS. Non angelus aliquis creatus, ut Pontificii interprett. volunt, sed Dominus ipse αὐτοπροσώπως loquutus cum Mose est. Quia non est citra rationem discedendum à textus litera : nec ϑεοφανείαι & ἀγγελοφανείαι confundendæ sunt.

## 33:12
V. 12. I KNOW YOU BY NAME] I know you by name: that is, especially above all others, as the Greeks here.

Latin:

V. 12. NOVI TE NOMINE] Novi te nominatim : id est, eximie παρὰ πάντα, ut hic Græci.

## 33:13
Vers. 13. SHOW ME THY FACE] That is, δόξαν, as some Greeks: but in the Hebrew it is: Make known to me thy way: which the Rabbis interpret concerning the divine properties, which they call מדות: but the passage shows that it is treated here of the manner by which God governs all things, which Moses wished to imitate.

He rightly corrects the Vulgate thus rendering, and the Greeks, who render δόξαν, from the Hebrew, which has, Make known to me thy way; Whence it is fitting that the Hebrew fountains be purer than the Latin or Greek rivulets. But while he says that it is treated here of the manner by which God governs all things, which Moses wished to imitate, he does not attain the scope of Moses: who was not seeking to be taught the manner of God by which all things are governed, but the way which he ought to go, by which way, by what means he wishes to lead them into the land of Canaan through so horrible a desert, and through so notable enemies; as Osiander; or the will of God, whether he might still deign to lead them himself, as the Weimar notes conveniently have. Moreover, from this chapter v. 3 and 4, Grotius above concluded at c. 23, 20 that God, after the worship of the calf, had taken away from the Israelites the Angel armed with his power, and had given them a lesser Angel, with merely Angelic power. Of which fable there is no trace here. That indeed seems to some, as if God here says that he had promised an angel as a companion or guide, but that he himself is unwilling to ascend with the Israelites, lest by chance he consume them on the way. Therefore some Interpreters wonder, who is an angel more kind than God, which Andr. Rivetus accepts concerning the Son of God, the Angel of the covenant, the Mediator destined to lead sinners in such a way that he does not rage against them, who ought to have appeased God toward the human race, since God the Father cannot overlook, namely unless the pledge of the Mediator is interposed. Who, however, speaks less piously in this, when he says that God the Father is described as less overlooking and bearing with sinners; but the Son as less prone to vengeance: when the mercy and justice of the Father and the Son are the same. Moreover, neither is anything had about that in the text: God only indicates that he had indeed promised before that he would give the land of Canaan to the Israelites, and would send an Angel as a Leader: (whom we acknowledge to be the Son of God) but now, angered by the idolatry of the people, he is unwilling to ascend with them, or to lead them through the Angel Son, in whom is the name of the Lord, because the people is stiff-necked. By which declaration, however, he only wished to recall the people to repentance: because that sentence, as Rivetus rightly says, was not definitive, but only interlocutory, and conditional: Since God afterwards, when the people performed repentance, promised his presence anew at the intercession of Moses v. 12. 13. Thou commandest that I lead out this people, whom thou art about to send with me, whether the sentence still stands, to withdraw the Angel Leader, and not to ascend with us. If therefore I have found grace in thy sight, make me know thy way, and I shall find grace before thine eyes, look upon thy people, this nation, and ascend with it, accompany and lead it through the Angel thy Son ὁμούσιον, in whose midst is thy name. The divine promise has it thus: My face shall go before thee, and I will give thee rest; My only-begotten Son, who is my face, the character of my hypostasis and the brightness of my glory, whom he who sees, sees me, will go before you. Which promise, Moses urging and repeating his solicitation, when he recognized the Lord vehemently irritated by the sin of the people, God, who is his infinite clemency, not only confirmed anew, but also made Moses more certain of his grace with most sweet words: And I will do this word, which you have spoken, for you have found grace before me, and I know you by name. Who from these will gather: an Angel instructed with lesser power, substituted in the place of the Angel Leader instructed with more eminent power? Is the face of God an Angel merely instructed with angelic power, just as the Lord himself? Is it not clear, when Moses so earnestly and insistently asked, if YOU YOURSELF do not go before, do not lead us out from this place, UNLESS YOU SHALL HAVE WALKED with us; and he was heard by the Lord; This word, which he has spoken, I will do; that THE LORD HIMSELF went before, the Lord himself walked with the Israelites, when the FACE OF THE LORD went before; for the Lord promised nothing other than this. For that word גם here in v. 17 must be translated CERTAINLY, altogether, which meaning of it Lexicographers have observed elsewhere, not ALSO. Certainly or altogether I am about to do this word. For it is not a new promise, but a confirmation of the former that is held here: just as Moses was not asking for anything new, he only desired to be confirmed more and more, concerning the Lordly leading or the going before of the face of the Lord. Nothing, therefore, is more certain than that the Angel, who had to go before, in whom is the name, i.e., the essence of the Lord, who is of the same power, Majesty, and essence as the Lord, and the Face of God going before them, are one and the same subject, namely the Son of God, the Angel of the face of the Lord, and the image of God the Father and thus the face of the same, who himself testifies in John 14, he who sees me, sees the Father. Therefore God himself went before, God himself walked with them: because the Son is not different from the Father: I and the Father are one, John 10:30. Unless perhaps with Mr. Varenius, Decad. Exod. p. 211, one might prefer to say that פנים is the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, but that מלאך אלהים is a person from פנים and that a middle one: so that nevertheless the Angel Leader remains A DIVINE PERSON. Where Grotius found that fiction about a lesser angel in Nachmanides, it is not evident. Something else from Nahmanides Gerundensis, Andr. Masius taught in his Joshua c. 1. p. 95, these things of his being brought forward: Furthermore it is written: And the Angel of his face saved them: Namely that Angel, who is the face of God: of whom it was said: My face will go before, and I will cause that he may rest. Finally, that Angel is he, of whom the Prophet, and suddenly the Lord will come to his temple, whom you seek, and the Angel of the covenant, whom you desire. R. Moses Gerundensis, son of Nahman, noted indeed to this place Exod. 33, that the Jews desired the first Angel; but he does not say that the same was denied to them, and a lesser one substituted, nor does he understand by that one any other than the Son of God. Observe, he says, attentively, what these things mean: for Moses and the Israelite always desired the first Angel: or the Prince: namely the Leader of the armies of the Lord, Jos. 5:14. But who that was, they could not truly understand: For neither did they perceive it from others, nor did they attain it sufficiently by Prophetic notion, (which we indeed do not approve of at all, unless it is taken comparatively concerning a clearer knowledge.) But the face of God signifies God himself, which is confessed among all Interpreters. But not even in a dream could anyone understand these things, unless he is learned in the mysteries of the law. And after a few things: My face will go before, i.e., the Angel of the covenant, whom you desire, in whom my face will be seen, of whom it was said: in an acceptable time I will hear you, for my Name is in him. These things Gerundensis: Masius adds: How consistent these are with our mysteries, I think no one does not see. For the Name of God is the very essence of God, for this is signified by the name Jehovah, which God himself revealed to Moses as peculiarly his own. That the essence of GOD is in Christ, is held as the first among our mysteries. But that Nehmannus thinks the name of Angel looks to the governance of the world, he says that not absurdly. For the eternal Son of God is the ruler and moderator and indeed the architect of the world; or with the Apostle and Solomon as witnesses. Augustine, however, to me indeed it certainly seems to be that which we were saying: because he was destined as a legate to us by the Father from the time the world was founded, for that reason he is called an Angel. And for the same reason he can also seem to be called the face of God; since in that legation he represented to us in himself the face of his Father, unknown to the human race after the sin of Adam. Truly not without cause was that said by him: Philip, he who sees me, sees also my Father. But let us dismiss the Jews. It is certain that the face of God went before the Israelites, when Moses was the leader of the people. And that that face was God himself. For both Moses was demanding that it happen, and God was promising that he would perform it. Furthermore Paul among the Corinthians. openly testifies that Christ accompanied them, who, since he is the most express image of the substance of the Father, is truly and properly called his face. And these things the most learned Masius.

Latin:

Vers. 13. OSTENDE MIHI FACIEM TUAM] Id est, δόξαν, ut quidam Græci : sed in Hebræo est: Fac mihi notam viam tuam : quod Rabbini de proprietatibus divinis interpretantur, quas מדות vocant : sed locus ostendit agi hîc de modo, quo Deus cuncta gubernat, quem imitari volebat Moses.

Recte corrigit Vulgatam ita reddentem, & Græcos, qui reddunt δόξαν, ex Ebræo, quod habet, Fac mihi notam viam tuam ; Unde puriores oportet fontes Ebræos esse, quam rivulos Latinos aut Græcos. Sed dum de modo hîc agi, quo Deus cuncta gubernat, quem imitari Moses voluerit, ait, non assequitur scopum Mosis : qui non Dei modum, quo cuncta gubernantur, sed viam, quam ire debebat, edoceri expetebat, qua via, quibus mediis in terram Canaan per tam horridum desertum, & per tot insignes hostes velit eos deducere ; ut Osiander ; vel voluntatem Dei, an ipsos αὐτοπροσώπως deducere adhuc dignaturus sit, uti commode notæ Vinarienses habent. Cæterum ex hoc capite v. 3. & 4. Grotius supra colligebat ad c. 23, 20. Deum post cultum vituli ab Israëlitis abstulisse Angelum potestate sua armatum, & minorem Angelum illis dedisse, cum potestate mere Angelica. Cujus fabulæ nullum hîc est vestigium. Id nonnullis quidem videtur, ac si Deus Angelum hîc dicat se promisisse comitem vel ductorem, se v. nolle cum Israëlitis ascendere, ne forte eosdem consumat in via. Ideo mirantur Interprepp. nonnulli, qui Angelus Deo benignior sit, quod Andr. Rivetus de Filio Dei accipit, Angelo fœderis, Mediatore destinato ita deducente peccatores, ut in eos non sæviat, qui Deum placare debuit erga genus humanum, quum Deus Pater connivere non possit, nempe nisi interposita sponsione Mediatoris. Qui v. in eo minus εὐσεβῶς loquitur, cum Deum Patrem, ceu minus conniventem & ferentem peccatores ; Filium a. ceu minus pronum ad vindictam describi ait : quum eadem sit misericordia, & justitia Patris & Filii. Cæterum nec de eo in textu quicquam habetur : indicat solum Deus, quod antea promiserit quidem, se daturum Israëlitis terram Canaan, & Angelum missurum Ductorem : (quem Filium Dei esse agnoscimus) nunc v. per idololatriam populi iratus nolit adscendere cum illis, vel deducere eosdem per Filium Angelum, in quo est nomen Domini, quia populus duræ cervicis est. Qua v. declaratione ad pœnitentiam solum revocare voluit populum : quia sententia illa, ut recte Rivetus, non erat definitiva, sed interlocutoria tantum, & conditionalis : Siquidem præsentiam suam postmodum, ubi populus pœnitentiam egit, denuo promiserit Deus ad intercessionem Mosis v. 12. 13. Præcipis, ut educam populum istum, quem missurus es mecum, an adhuc stat sententia, Angelum Ductorem subtrahere, nec nobiscum ascendere. Si ergo inveni gratiam in conspectu tuo, fac me scire viam tuam, & inveniam gratiam ante oculos tuos, respice populum tuum, gentem hanc, & ascende cum ea, comitare ac deduc eum per Angelum Filium tuum ὁμούσιον, in cujus medio est nomen tuum. Promissio divina ita habet : Facies mea præcedet te, & requiem dabo tibi ; Filius meus unigenitus, qui est facies mea, character hypostaseos & fulgor gloriæ meæ, quem qui videt, me videt, præcedet te. Quam promissionem, urgente & iterante solicitationem suam Mose, quum Dominum vehementer irritatum peccato populi agnosceret, Deus, quæ est infinita ejus cle- mentia, non tantum confirmavit denuo, sed Mo- sen etiam de gratia sua suavissimis verbis certiorem reddidit: Et faciam verbum istud, quod loquutus es, invenisti enim gratiam coram me, & teipsum novi ex nomine. Quis ex his colliget: Angelum minore po- tentia instructum, substitutum loco Angeli Ductoris eminentiori potestate instructi? Num facies Dei est Angelus mere angelica potestate instructus, sicut ipse Dominus? Annon luculentum est, quum Moses tam enixe & instanter petierit, si non TU IPSE præcedas, ne educas nos de loco isto, NISI AMBU- LAVERIS nobiscum; & exauditus sit à Domino; Verbum istud, quod locutus est, faciam; IPSUM DOMINUM præcessisse, ipsum Dominum am- bulasse cum Israelitis, cum FACIES DOMINI præcessit; nihil enim aliud, quam hoc pollicitus fuit Dominus. Illud enim גם vertendum hic v. 17. CERTE, omnino, quam significationem ejus ob- servarunt alibi Lexicographi, non ETIAM. Certe vel omnino Verbum hoc facturus sum. Non n. nova promissio, sed prioris confirmatio hic habetur: quemadmodum neq; novi quid petebat Moses, so- lum confirmari magis magisq; cupiebat, de Domi- nica deductione vel faciei Domini antecessu. Nihil ergo certius, quam Angelum, qui præcedere de- buit, in quo nomen, i. e. essentia Domini est, qui ejus- dem cum Domino est potestatis, Majestatis & essen- tiæ, & Faciem Dei præcedentem ipsos, unum idemq; subjectum esse, Filium nempe Dei, Angelum faciei Domini, & imaginem Dei Patris adeoque faciem ejus- dem, qui testatur ipse Joh. 14. quime videt, videt Pa- trem. Ideo Deus ipse præcessit, Deus ipse ambula- vit cum iisdem: quia Filius diversus non est à Patre: Ego & Pater unum sumus Joh. 10, 30. Nisi forte cum Dn. Varenio Decad. Exod. p. 211. dicere quis ma- lit פנים esse Patrem, Filium & S. S. at מלאך אלהים personam esse ex פנים eamq; mediam: ut nihilomi- nus angelus Ductor maneat PERSONA DIVINA. Ubi in Nachmanide Grotius commentum illud de angelo minore invenerit, non constat. Aliud è Nah- manide Gerundensi Andr. Masius docuit in Josua suo c. 1. p. 95. his ejus adductis: Præterea scriptum est: Et Angelus faciei ejus salvos fecit ipsos: Nimi- rum ille Angelus, qui est Dei facies: de qua dictum est: Facies mea præibit, & efficiam, ut quiescat. Deniq; ille Angelus est, de quo Vates, & subito veniet ad tem- plum suum Dominus, quem vos quæritis, & Ange- lus fœderis, quem cupitis. Id notavit quidem R. Mo- ses Gerund. Nehmani filius ad hunc locum Exod. 33. quod Judæi Angelum primum optaverint; non autem eundem denegatum ipsis dicit, & minorem substi- tutum, nec per illum alium, quam Filium Dei intel- ligit. Animadverte, inquit, attente, quid ista sibi velint: Moses enim & Israëlita semper optaverunt Angelum primum: vel Principem: Ducem nempe exercituum Domini Jos. 5, 14. Cæterum quis ille esset, vere intelli- gere non potuerunt: Neque enim ab aliis percipiebant neq; Prophetica notione satis assequebantur, (quod nos quidem minime probamus, nisi de clariori no- titia συγκριτικῶς accipiatur.) Atqui facies Dei ipsum significat Deum, quod apud omnes Interpp. est in con- fesso. Verum ne per somnium quidem ista intelliger quisquam possit, nisi sit in mysteriis legis eruditus. Et post pauca: Facies mea præcedet, h. e. Angelus fœde- ris, quem cupitis, in quo videbitur facies mea, de quo dictum est: tempore accepto exaudiam te, Nomen enim meum est in eo. Hæc Gerundensis: Addit Masius: Quæ quam sint nostris mysteriis consentanea, nemo opinor, non videt. Nomen a. Dei est ipsa Dei essentia, hæc enim nomine Jehovah, quod ut peculiariter suum Deus ipse Mosi patefecit, significatur. Esse autem DEI essentiam in Christo, inter nostra mysteria vel primum habetur. Sed quod Angeli nomen ad mundi modera- tionem spectare existimat Nehmannus, haud absurde id quidem dicit. Est enim æternus Dei Filius rector mode- ratorque atque adeo architectus mundi; vel Apostolo & Salomone testibus. Augustinus tamen, mihi quidem certe illud esse videtur, quod nos dicebamus: propterea quod à Patre inde à condito orbe ad nos est destinatus legatus, idcirco Angelum vocari. Atque eadem ratione etiam facies Dei dictus videri potest; cum in ea lega- tione Patris sui faciem post Adæ peccatum humano generi ignotam, in se ipse nobis repræfentaverit. Vere non ab ipso dictum illud est: Philippe, qui videt me, vi- det & Patrem meum. Sed dimittamus Judæos. Certum est, Dei faciem præivisse Israëlitus, cum Moses dux esset populi. Eamque faciem fuisse Deum ipsum. Id enim & Moses, ut fieret, flagitabat & Deus præstiturum se spon- debat. Adhæc Paulus apud Corinth. Christum esse co- mitatum illos, aperte testatur, qui cum sit imago sub- stantiæ Patris expressissima, proprie profecto facies ejus dicitur. Atque hæc eruditissimus Masius.

## 33:18
Vers. 18. SHOW ME THY GLORY] The splendor of thy countenance, to which the back is soon opposed. But the countenance and the former parts signify the causes and reasons, according to which God dispenses his benefits, the back the benefits themselves. These things we feel. Those we now for the most part do not know, Rom. 11:33, 34, 35, but the Ancients knew much fewer, Rom. 16:25, 26. These things which follow show this sense.

It must not be said that Moses was so rash as to desire to have known the reasons and causes of the unsearchable counsels of God a priori: nor do we know anything about them. Who has investigated the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counselor? Nor is the discourse in Rom. 16:26 about them, but about the mystery kept secret for eternal times, yet manifested through the Prophetic Scriptures, from which even the Ancients could have known it: which makes for the obedience of faith: but to know the reasons and causes of the counsels and decrees of God a priori is not required for the obedience of faith. Nor is it to be believed that Moses wished to behold the glory of God, as great as it is, in itself and immediately in the substance of His Deity, of which he could not have been ignorant that he was unequal: and therefore most learned Interpreters not undeservedly judge that Moses desired a certain glorious manifestation of the Majesty of the Lord in an august form, which God perhaps had assumed at that time: but what its excellence was, such that not even that could any mortal be able to sustain: whence the Lord testified: You will not be able to see my face, for man shall not see me and live. Since indeed it could not be beheld by a mortal man in the substance of the Deity, nor even in such a more excellent corporeal form, from which the divine Majesty shines forth with full and most brilliant rays. Therefore in this assumed form he could then see only from behind and as to the back parts, he could not see his face. Indeed, he even had to be protected by the palm of the Lord in the passing, lest he perish v. 23. That assumed form was therefore of such a kind from its anterior part, that by its excessive brightness it would not only have dazzled the eyes of the beholder, but would have even killed the spectator: Whence Moses had to be hidden in the cleft of the rock and covered by the palm of the Lord: but from the posterior part it was tempered to the visual faculty, so that it could be beheld without danger to life. Whether, however, that was a human form, or another, is not sufficiently clear: and therefore it must be left in the middle. That the Hebrews wish the same form to have appeared here to Moses which appeared in Isa. 6, Ez. 1, and 10, Grotius observed at v. 22. But whence is this certain to them? Meanwhile, we do not deny that it was signified that the counsels of God cannot be known by us a priori, and that we ought to be content with that grace of God, that they are offered to be known a posteriori. To be willing not to know what the best Master did not wish us to know is a learned ignorance.

But the significance of a vision is one thing, and the vision and apparition itself is another. Nor does Grotius seem to deny this, noting on v. 22: And when my glory shall pass by, the former part of that which appears. Implying that the former part of the ὁράματος (vision) is called glory.

Latin:

Vers. 18. OSTENDE MIHI GLORIAM TUAM] Splendorem vultus tui, cui mox opponitur tergum. Signifi- cat autem vultus & partes priores, causas ac rationes, secun- dum quas Deus beneficia sua dispensat, tergum ipsa bene- ficia. Hæc sentimus. Illas magna ex parte nos nunc ignoramus Rom. 11, 33. 34. 35. multo pauciora autem norant Veteres Rom. 16, 25. 26. Hunc sensum monstrant, quæ se- quuntur.

Non dicendum, Mosen tam temerarium fuisse, ut consiliorum Dei ἀνεξερευνήτων rationes ac cau- sas à priori novisse desiderarit: neque de illis nos quicquam scimus. Quis investigavit sensum Domi- ni, aut quis ei consiliarius fuit? nec de illis sermo est Rom. 16, 26. sed de mysterio temporibus æternis tacito, patefacto autem per Scripturas Propheticas, unde illud etiam Veteres cognoscere potuere: quod ad obedien- tiam fidei facit: rationes autem & causas consiliorum & decretorum Dei à priori novisse, ad obedientiam fidei non requiritur. Neque credendum, Mosen gloriam Dei, quanta quanta est, in se & immediate in substantia Deitatis suæ conspicari voluisse, ad quod imparem se esse, non poterat ignorare: ideoque non immerito censent Doctissimi Interpp. desiderasse Mosen Ma- jestatis Domini gloriosam quandam in specie augusta manifestationem, quam Deus forte tunc assumserat: quæ vero ejus fuerit excellentia, ut ne eam quidem susti- nere ullus mortalium valeret: unde testatus Domi- nus: Non poteris videre facies meas, quia non videbit me homo, & vivet. Siquidem nec in substantia Dei- tatis à mortali homine conspici possit, neque etiam in ejusmodi excellentiori specie corporea, è qua ple- nis & fulgentissimis radiis Majestas divina effulget. Ideo in hac specie assumta nonnisi à tergo & quoad posteriora videre tum potuit, faciem ejus videre non potuit. Imo protegendus etiam vola Domi- ni fuit in transitu, ne periret v. 23. Fuit ergo forma illa assumta ab anteriori sui parte ejusmodi, ut ni- mio suo fulgore oculos videntis non solum perstrin- xiffet, sed etiam spectantem exanimasset: Unde Mo- ses in foramine petræ abscondendus & vola Domi- ni tegendus fuit: à posteriori autem parte contempe- rata facultati visivæ, ut absque periculo vitæ conspi- ci potuerit. Utrum a. humana illa forma fuerit, an alia non satis liquet: ideoq; in medio relinquendum. E- bræos velle, eandem formam hic Mosi apparuisse, quæ Esa. 6. Ez. 1. & 10. Grotius ad v. 22. observavit. Sed unde hoc ipsis constat? Interim non negamus, id si- gnificatum fuisse, Dei consilia à priori cognosci à nobis non posse, contentos nos esse debere illa Dei gratia, quod à posteriori eadem cognoscenda præbeantur. Nescire velle, quæ Magister opt. nos scire noluit, erudita est inscitia.

Aliud autem est visionis significatio, aliud visio & apparitio ipsa. Neque abnuere videtur Grotius ad v. 22. hæc annotans: Cumque transibit gloria mea, pars prior ejus quod apparet. Partem anteriorem ὁράματος gloriam dictam innuens.

## 33:19
Ver. 19.

I WILL SHOW ALL GOOD TO THEE] The good things which I am about to do for the people of Israel.

All good does not pertain only to the people of Israel. Nor did the Lord here cause goods proper to them to pass by, and showed them ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ (as in passing). What those things are, we are taught in the sermon held by the Son of God in the following chapter. Interpreters note that the Lord describes His own all-good with ten epithets: that He is (1.) אל (God) the strong, who is able to crush all opposing powers. (2.) Merciful, who preserves from a fall. (3.) Gracious, raising up the fallen. (4.) Long-suffering, not immediately condemning one who has fallen into sins, or abandoning him. (5.) Of much mercy, or abounding in mercies toward the unworthy. (6.) Of much truth, because He fulfills promises. (7.) Keeping mercy or kindness for thousands, because He is a liberal and munificent benefactor. (8.) Taking away iniquity, transgression, and sin, namely for the penitent and converted. (9.) Who by no means clears the guilty, namely the impenitent and the one who pleases himself in his sins. (10.) Visiting the iniquity of the Fathers upon the Children: most justly punishing those who persevere in sins both in themselves and in their posterity, who adhere to the footsteps of their Fathers. Are those goods proper to the Israelites? Nor is the ascent or passing of the Son of GOD before Moses, in whom is all the εὐδοκία (good pleasure) of God, referred to as OMNIS BONI (all good) amiss: concerning which see the Weimar Bible.

Ver. same.

I WILL CALL IN THE NAME OF THE LORD BEFORE THEE] A Hebrew idiom, for which it may be permitted to say, I will proclaim my name by pronouncing יהוה, by which, to be sure, you may be the more certain that I shall be constant in fulfilling promises, which is signified by the name יהוה. See above VI, 3.

But He did not only proclaim the name Jehovah, but also showed him all His good, and recounted His attributes to him; and this incomparable Orator proclaimed here not only truth, but also justice and power, and especially the grace and mercy of GOD. The matter was not only about the promises made to Moses, but about all the good of God, and whatever we have to expect from Him. And two persons are openly designated here: Jehovah, who proclaims, and Jehovah, whose name He proclaims, just as we have proven that the plurality of persons is shown by this manner of speaking. See the demonstration of the plurality of persons from the Old Testament, chap. XVII. A scruple could be moved for someone, because God the Father speaks here, who promises the leading of His face and of the Angel: but the Son of God is introduced as the herald of divine goodness in the following chapter, and thus is said to be about to proclaim here in the name of Jehovah, or God the Father [proclaims] the name of the Son; but if we examine that most magnificent sermon itself, the Father does not proclaim the name of the Son, but the Son of GOD descending in the Cloud [proclaims] in the name of the Lord, or the name of the Lord God the Father, if that mode of speaking implies a diversity of persons. But by this permutation is indicated that mutual περιχώρησις (indwelling) of the divine persons, and the indivisibility of works ad extra (outwardly). For while the Son proclaims, the Father also proclaims, because the Father is in the Son, and the Son in the Father, and the Father and the Son are one. Then indeed that mutual revelation is also noted: that the Father reveals the Son and the Son reveals the Father: concerning which Christ says: no one knows the Son, except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father, except the Son, and he to whom the Son wills to reveal Him. Matt. 11. v. 27. For the Father proclaims the name of the Son when He reveals the Son: the Son proclaims the name of the Father when He reveals the Father. Which are also deservedly interchanged here for this reason: because the name of the Father and of the Son which is proclaimed here is one and the same, namely the essential name, Lord God merciful, gracious, etc. For these names and all attributes are common to the Father and the Son. And just as the Father is sometimes said to send the Holy Spirit in the name of the Son, John 14, 26, and sometimes the Son is said to send Him from the Father, John 15, 26, so that by that permutation the equal authority of the Father and the Son is insinuated, but no confusion of persons is introduced; so [it is] that the Father sometimes proclaims the name of the Son, and sometimes the Son [proclaims] the name of the Father, to signify the identity of the proclamation of the Father and the Son, and of the name of both: by no means, however, are the persons therefore confused among themselves. Nor would it be inconsistent if we say, when the Son proclaims the mercy of God the Father, the name of the Son is proclaimed by the Father Himself, because mercy does not reach us except in the Son: or justice: because the Father has given all judgment to the Son: or honor and glory: because the Father does not wish to be honored, except in the Son, John 5, 23.

Vers. eod. I WILL HAVE MERCY ON WHOM I WILL HAVE MERCY, AND I WILL BE GRACIOUS TO WHOM IT SHALL PLEASE ME] I will forgive certain sins, I will not forgive others, and I will forgive the same sins to these, not to those, for reasons hidden from men, but known to me. The Latin translator rendered it well: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, instead of I will have mercy on whom I will. For as Servius says at the beginning of the 3rd Aeneid: Whenever a reason or judgment does not appear, it is thus presented as having seemed so. Donatus on Terence and Abarbanel on Isaiah 53 have the same meaning for the word חפץ. It is a proverb of the Hebrews: One must not curiously inquire after the works of God, for He has made all things wisely, even though they are hidden from the eyes of the wise. Origen against Celsus: For there are certain connections and sequences, ineffable and indescribable, concerning the diverse economy regarding human souls. Arnobius book II. For it is not easy for anyone to see the mind of God, or by what ways He has ordered His affairs; man, a blind animal and ignorant of himself, cannot attain it by any reasoning. What ought to be done, when, or by what manner, the Father, Moderator, and Lord of all things alone knows. Salvianus: That which the divinity does is not therefore not just, because man is not able to grasp the force of divine justice. Just as God is more than human reason, so to me it ought to be more than reason that I know all things are done by God.

Under this gloss there can also lie the Socinian absurdity concerning certain sins which God is unwilling to forgive, which easily leads to Cain's despair, so that one might say: My iniquity is greater than that it can be forgiven; and it cries out against the praises of divine Mercy everywhere met with in the Scriptures; as also the horrible Calvinist decree; from which, however, it is established that Grotius abhors. The same sins are indeed forgiven to these, but not likewise to others: but the cause is not hidden: For they are forgiven to the penitent. Who are truly penitent and who are not, that indeed is hidden; but that access to grace lies open to every penitent, and that God does not wish anyone to perish in their sins, but rather wishes that all should be converted and live, is sufficiently evident from the Scriptures. Ez. 18 and 33. 2 Pet. 3, 9. Moreover, that oracle, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, has nothing to do with an absolute decree, but is entirely contrary to it, even as it is adduced by the Apostle, Rom. 9, in Theol. Apost. orac. LXIIX. we have prolixly proven. Where it is also shown that the Apostle in those three chapters IX, X, XI, does not treat by design of Predestination, but of gratuitous justification, which explanation our Dn. D. Weller also praised in his most learned commentary on this Epistle, p. 525.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

OSTENDAM OMNE BONUM TIBI] Bona, quæ po- pulo Israëlis facturus sum.

Omne bonum non tantum pertinet ad Israëlis po- pulum. Nec bona illi propria hîc transire fecit, & ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ ostendit Dominus. Quæ autem illa sint, concione, capite sequente à Filio Dei habita, edoce- mur. Notant Interpp. decem Epithetis omne bo- num suum describere Dominum: quod sit (1.) אל fortis, qui conterere valeat omnes adversarias pote- states. (2.) Misericors, qui à lapsu præservet. (3.) Cle- mens, lapsum erigens. (4.) Longanimus, non actu- tum condemnans prolapsum in peccata, aut relin- quens. (5.) Multæ miserationis, seu abundans mise- rationibus erga indignos. (6.) Multæ veritatis, quia implet promissa. (7.) Custodiens misericordiam seu benignitatem in millibus, quia liberalis & munificus benefactor. (8.) Auferens iniquitatem, defectionem & peccatum, pœnitentibus nempe & conversis. (9.) Qui nullo pacto absolvit fontem, nempe impœniten- tem & in peccatis suis sibi placentem. (10.) Visitans iniquitatem Patrum in Filiis: justissime puniens per- severantes in peccatis tam in se, quam in posteris, ve- stigiis Patrum inhærentibus. Num illa propria sunt Israëlitarum bona? Neque male ascenssionem, vel transitum coram Mose OMNIS BONI transitus Filii DEI, in quo est omnis εὐδοκία Dei, refertur: quo de vide Biblia Vinariensia.

Vers. eod.

VOCABO IN NOMINE DOMINI CORAM TE] Locutio Hebræa, pro qua dicere liceat, clamabo nomen me- um יהוה pronunciando, quo magis scilicet certus sis con- stantem me fore in promissis implendis, quod nomine יהוה significatur. Vid. supra VI, 3.

At non tantum nomen Jehovah clamavit, sed ostendit ei etiam omne bonum suum, & attributa sua eidem enarravit; Nec solum veritatem, sed etiam justitiam & potentiam & cumprimis gratiam & misericordiam DEI hic Orator incomparabilis deprædicavit. Non de promissis solum Mosi factis res erat, sed de bono omni Dei, & quicquid nos ab eo expectare habeamus. Et aperte hîc duæ personæ designantur: Jehovah, qui prædicat, & Jehovah, cu- jus nomen prædicat, quemadmodum hîc loquendi ratione pluralitatem personarum ostendi evicimus demonstrat. plur. person. è Vet. Test. cap. XVII. Scru- pulus alicui moveri posset, quod hîc loquatur Deus Pater, qui faciei suæ & Angeli ductum pollice- tur: præco autem divinæ bonitatis cap. sequenti in- troducatur Filius Dei, adeoque hîc prædicaturus di- catur in nomine Jehovah, vel nomen Filii Deus Pa- ter, si autem ipsam concionem istam magnificen- tissimam expendamus, prædicet non Pater nomen Filii, sed Filius DEI in Nube descendens in nomine Domini, vel nomen Domini Dei Patris, si loquendi modus ille diversitatem personarum inferat. Sed hac permutatione indicatur mutua illa περιχώρησις personarum divinarum, & operum ad extra indivi- sio. Prædicante enim Filio prædicat etiam Pater, quia Pater est in Filio, & Filius in Patre, & Pater & Filius unum sunt. Tum vero notatur etiam mu- tua illa revelatio: quod Pater Filium & Filius Pa- trem revelet: qua de Christus: nemo novit Filium, nisi Pater, neque Patrem quis novit, nisi Filius, & cui voluerit Filius revelare. Matth. 11. v. 27. Prædicat enim nomen Filii Pater, cum revelat Filium: præ- dicat nomen Patris Filius, cum revelat Patrem. Quæ hîc etiam ideo merito permutantur: quia num idemque nomen est Patris & Filii, quod hic præ- dicatur, nomen sc. essentiale, Dominus Deus miseri- cors, gratiosus &c. Hæc enim nomina & attributa omnia Patri & Filio sunt communia. Et ut modo Pater in nomine Filii Spiritum S. mittere dicitur Joh. 14, 62. modo Filius à Patre ipsum diciur mit- tere Joh. 15, 26. ut illa permutatione æqualis Patris & Filii autoritas insinuatur, nulla vero personarum confusio invehitur; Ita modo Pater nomen Filii præ- dicare, modo Filius nomen Patris, ad identitatem præconii Patris & Filii, & nominis utriusque signifi- candam: Neutiquam v. ideo personæ inter se con- funduntur. Neque inconcinnum fuerit, si dicamus, cum Filius prædicat misericordiam Dei Patris, prædi- cari à Patre ipso Filii nomen, quia non nisi in Filio no- bis obtingit miseratio: vel justitiam: quia omne judi- cium dedit Pater Filio: vel honorem & gloriam: quia non vult honorari Pater, nisi in Filio, Joh. 5, 23.

Vers. eod. MISEREBOR, CUI VOLUERO, ET CLEMENS ERO, IN QVEM MIHI PLACUERIT] Peccata quæ- dam condonabo, quædam non condonabo, & eadem peccata his condonabo, non illis, ob causas latentes hominibus, mi- hi cognitas. Bene autem Latinus transtulit: miserebor cu- jus miserebor, pro miserebor cui voluero. Nam ut Servius ait ad initium III. Æneidos: Quotiescumque ratio vel judicium non apparet, sic visum interponitur. Habet idem Donatus ad Terentium, & Abarbanel ad Es. 53. hanc significationem esse dicit in voce חפץ. Proverbium est Hebræorum: Non est curiose quærendum post opera DEI, omnia enim sapienter fecit, tametsi abscondita sunt ab oculis sapientum. Origenes contra Celsum: Εἰσὶ γάρ τινες εἱρμοὶ καὶ ἀκολουθίαι ἄφατοι καὶ ἀνεκ- διήγητοι περὶ τῆς κατὰ τὰς ἀνθρωπίνας ψυχὰς διαφόρου οἰκονο- μίας. Arnobius lib. II. Neque enim promptum est cuiquam Dei videre mentem, aut quibus modis ordinarit res suas, homo animal cæcum & ipse se nesciens ullis potest rationibus consequi. Quid oporteat fieri, quando, vel quo genere, ipse cunctarum re- rum pater, moderator & Dominus scit solus. Salvianus: Non ideo non justum est, quod divinitas agit, quia capere vim divinæ justitiæ homo non valet. Sicut plus est Deus, quam humana ratio, sic mihi plus esse debet quam ratio, quod a Deo agi cuncta co- gnosco.

Sub hac glossa latere potest & Socinianum ἄτοπημα de peccatis quibusdam, quæ Deus condona- re nolit, quod ad Caini desperationem facile ducit, ut quis dicat: Major est iniquitas mea, quam ut con- donari possit; & elogiis Misericordiæ divinæ in Scripturis passim obviis reclamat; ut & Calvinia- num horribile decretum; à quo tamen abhorrere Grotium constat. Peccata eadem condonantur quidem his, aliis non item: sed causa non latet: Con- donantur enim pœnitentibus. Qui pœnitentes ve- re sint, qui non, id utique latet; at cuivis pœnitenti aditum ad gratiam patere, nec quenquam velle Deum perire in peccatis, imo velle, ut omnes convertantur & vivant, è Scripturis satis patet. Ez. 18. & 33. 2. Petr. 3, 9. Oraculum autem illud, Miserebor, cujus mise- rebor, nihil ad absolutum decretum facere, prorsus ei- dem refragari, etiam prouti ab Apostolo adductum est, Rom. 9. in Theol. Apost. orac. LXIIX. prolixe evicimus. Ubi ostensum etiam Apostolum tribus illis capitib. IX. X. XI. ex instituto non de Prædesti- natione, sed de gratuita justificatione agere, quam explicationem Dn. D. Wellerus noster in eruditissimo commentario hujus Epistolæ quoq; laudavit p. 525.

## 33:20
Vers. 20. FOR NO MAN SHALL SEE] Cf. Jud. 6, 23 and 13, 22. Pausanias in Phocis: The saying of Homer seems to be true, that it is not with any good omen that the gods are clearly seen by the race of men. Callimachus: The Cronian laws say thus, that whoever looks upon any of the immortals, when the god himself does not choose it, shall see him at a great price.

Latin:

Vers. 20. NON ENIM VIDEBIT] Conf. Jud. 6, 23. & 13, 22. Pausanias Phocide: τὸ ἔπος ἐν ἀληθεύειν ἔοικε τὸ Ὁμήρου σὺν οὐδενὶ αἰσίῳ τὲς θεὸς τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐναργῶς ὁρᾶ- θαι. Callimachus: Κρόνιοι δ᾽ ὧδε λέγοντι νόμοι, Ὃς κε τιν᾿ ἀθανάτων, ὅκα μὴ θεὸς αὐτὸς ἕληται, Ἀθρήσῃ, μισθῷ τῦτον ἰδεῖν μεγάλῳ.

## 33:21
V. 21. THERE IS A PLACE BY ME] A place near to the vision.

Latin:

V. 21. EST LOCUS APUD ME] Locus propinquus viso.

## 33:22
Vers. 22. AND WHILE MY GLORY PASSES BY] The prior part of that which appears. The Hebrews believe, however, that the same form appeared here to Moses, Isaiah ch. 6, Ez. ch. 1 and 10.

I WILL PROTECT WITH MY RIGHT HAND] Divine power inhibits curiosity in us. Who has first given to Him? Rom. 11, verse 35.

Latin:

Vers. 22. CUMQUE TRANSIBIT GLORIA MEA] Pars prior ejus quod apparet. Credunt autem Hebræi eandem formam apparuisse hîc Mosi, Esaiæ c. 6. Ez. c. 1. & 10.

PROTEGAM DEXTRA MEA] Potestas divina in nos curiositatem inhibet. Quis prior dedit illi? Rom. 11. vers. 35.

## 33:23
Ver. 23.

YOU SHALL SEE MY BACK PARTS: BUT MY FACE YOU SHALL NOT BE ABLE TO SEE] This was a conviction held by all nations. Homer, Iliad 13. For I knew the tracks of the feet and legs of the god as he departed. Servius on that line in Aeneid 10. Following behind. This is said for the reason that they do not wish their faces to be seen: whence Eclogue 8. Do not look back. The same in the Fulda codex on Aeneid 2: Divinities are generally shown to have been present by their departure, when they have suddenly ceased to appear.

Latin:

Verf. 23.

VIDEBIS POSTERIORA MEA: FACIEM AUTEM MEAM VIDERE NON POTERIS] Persuasum id gen- tibus cunctis. Homerus Iliados ιʹ. Ἴχνια γὰρ μετόπιϐε ποδῶν ἠδὲ κνημάων Θεῦ ἔγνων ἀπιόντος. Servius ad illud 10. Æneid. Pone sequens. Hoc quidem ideo dictum tradunt, quod adversa videri nolunt: unde Ecloga 8. Ne respexeris. Idem in Fuldensi codice ad 2. Æneidos: Ab- scessu plerumque numina demonstrantur fuisse, cum subito ap- parere desierint.

## 34:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIV. New tablets. The evangelical sermon of the Son of God. The tradition of Moses.

Ver. 1.

HEW FOR YOURSELF TWO STONE TABLETS.

The first two were hewn and inscribed without the work of man and were entirely the work of GOD: here, however, God divides the work between Himself and Moses: so that Moses should prepare the blank tablets, upon which God might inscribe His law: Doubtless He wished that difference to remain, so that with the scar of the sin left behind, on account of which the former tablets were broken, some memory might always be present in this change, and the misery of that condition might not perish through any oblivion.

It was also signified by the tablets of the law broken through the Adamic transgression that a renewal must take place through the mediation of a ministry, since the divine law must be inscribed anew into our hearts by the Spirit of GOD, Jer. 31, 33. 2 Cor. 3, 3.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIV. Novæ tabulæ. Evangelica Filii Dei concio. Mosis traditio.

Vers. 1.

PRÆCIDE TIBI DUAS TABULAS LA- PIDEAS.

Priores duæ sine hominis opera dolatæ & in- sculptæ totæ opus DEI fuêre: hic vero partitur Deus opus inter se & Mosen: ut Moses tabulas ra- sas præparet, quibus Deus inscribat legem suam: Nimirum discrimen illud superesse voluit, ut cica- trice relicta peccati, ob quod priores tabulæ confractæ, memoria aliqua in hac mutatione semper obversetur, & conditionis illius miseria nulla oblivione inter- cidat.

Significatum etiam fuit tabulis legis per trans- gressionem Adamicam confractis, mediante ministe- rio renovationem fieri debere, cum per Spiritum DEI in corda nostra denuo lex divina inscribenda, Jer. 31, 33. 2. Cor. 3, 3.

## 34:5
Ver. 5.

MOSES STOOD WITH HIM CALLING UPON THE NAME OF THE LORD] Better in the Hebrew: The Lord descended in a cloud, and stood there with him, and called in the name of יהוה, so that both stood and called, may be said of God consistently with those things which are above 34, 19. Thus also the LXX.

He rightly corrects the Vulgate from the Hebrew source: But the fact that he speaks comparatively, better in the Hebrew, is suspect. For the authentic text is not to be called into any contention with the versions.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

STETIT MOSES CUM EO INVOCANS NOMEN DOMINI] Melius in Hebræo: Descendit Dominus in nube, & ibi stetit cum eo, & clamavit in nomine יהוה, ut & stetit, & clamavit, de Deo dicantur congruenter iis, quæ supra 34, 19. Sic & LXX.

Merito corrigit Vulgatum ex Ebræo fonte: Sed quod comparate loquitur, melius in Hebræo, suspe- ctum est. Non enim in ullam contentionem vocan- dus est textus avthenticus cum versionibus.

## 34:6
Ver. 6.

AS HE PASSED BEFORE HIM HE SAID] 'Before' here signifies not sight, but perception. For Moses perceived the passing of that vision by the overshadowing foretold to him above at 33, 22. Thus על פני is also said of hearing at Genesis 19, 13, and of smelling at Exodus 30, 8. Moreover, the Hebrew Codices are also more correct here: And God passed before him, and called, Lord, Lord. So that these things which follow were also called out by God, just as the LXX also have it.

Ver. the same.

LORD LORD GOD] More correctly, as I have said, in the nominative: Lord Lord God.

The Vulgate is deservedly corrected again from the Hebrew source. Why then does he dare elsewhere to correct the Hebrew text from the Vulgate? Streams before rivers!

Latin:

Vers. 6.

QUO TRANSEUNTE CORAM EO AIT] Coram hic non conspectum, sed sensum significat. Transitum enim visi illius percipiebat Moses ex obumbratione sibi prædicta supra 33, 22. Sic על פני etiam de auditu dicitur Genes. 19, 13. & de olfactu Exod. 30, 8. Ceterum & hic rectius He- bræi Codices: Et transivit Deus coram eo, & clamavit, Do- minus, Dominus. Ut & hæc quæ sequuntur a Deo clamata sint, quomodo & LXX.

Vers. eod.

DOMINATOR DOMINE DEUS] Rectius, ut dixi, in nominativo: Dominus Dominus Deus.

Merito iterum emendatur Vulgata ex Ebræo fonte. Cur ergo alias audet Ebræum textum corri- gere è Vulgata? ῥεύματα πρὸ ποταμῶν!

## 34:7
Ver. 7.

MERCIFUL AND GRACIOUS, PATIENT AND OF GREAT MERCY AND TRUTHFUL, WHO KEEPEST MERCY FOR THOUSANDS, WHO TAKEST AWAY INIQUITY, WICKEDNESS AND SIN] In the Hebrew, he keeps and takes away: but the beneficent properties of God are expressed by many words, because those things greatly prevail in God: Jeremiah 2, 13. Therefore the Hebrews say there are 13 מדות, or properties of God, among which only one is vindictive.

AND NO ONE WITH THEE IS INNOCENT BY HIMSELF] The Greek: and he will not clear the guilty. In the Hebrew: by purifying he will not purify, i. e., he will not spare, as the Chaldean here, namely the contumacious. Tertullian, 2 against Marcion: God is milder toward things subdued, who was formerly more austere toward the unsubdued.

Malvenda rendered it 'by emptying he will not empty.' Lud. de Dieu refers it to the goodness of God, because נקה will be emptied, Zach. 5, 3. Every one that sweareth shall be emptied, that is, utterly cut off, and Isaiah 3, 26, she shall sit empty on the ground, that is, utterly desolate. So here, by emptying he will not empty, he will not utterly cut off, but will punish only to the 3rd and 4th generation. So Jeremiah 30, 11, chap. 46, 28, I will correct thee in judgment, that is, moderately, and by cutting off I will not cut thee off, where the same word is had as here. Jonathan: by destroying I will not destroy thee. That interpretation, however, 'I will by no means hold thee innocent,' is rejected also by Mercer, because there is a manifest opposition here between the clemency which he would use toward his own, and the severity which he would use toward enemies. Compare Numbers 14, 18. Most, however, explain it so that it easily agrees with the Vulgate. By making innocent he will not make innocent, Vatablus and Oleaster have. By purifying he will not purify, Montanus; by absolving he will not absolve, Syr. Pagn. Jun. Tremell. But they supply the source, or the guilty, or those who do not repent. Which sense agrees with what follows.

Ver. the same.

UNTO THE THIRD AND FOURTH GENERATION] Not in all crimes, but in those which are directed against the majesty of God. Such are primarily defection from God, and the worship of false gods. For in punishing these, God uses not only that judicial right, but also his lordly right over descendants.
