Nomen autem obtinet præsens liber apud Ebræos partim וידבר חומש, tum a voce initiali וידבר & locutus est, tum inprimis a voce significatiori versus primi במדבר in deserto: quod breviter SUMMAM libri comple- ctitur, uti jam diximus: quia quamvis etiam in Exo- do & Levitico quædam in deserto acta descripta, illa tamen unius tantum anni, hæc unius mensis solum acta sunt, hîc vero per 39. annos IN DESERTO acta describuntur: partim אלה פקודים cum vocatur ספר פקודים liber Numerorum, nec non ספר הפקודים liber recensionum, a Græcis nomine ἀριθμοὶ, ac pa- riter a Latinis Numerorum nomine designatur, quia hoc peculiare habet pro reliquis libris Mo- saicis, quod in recensione ac numero, tam persona- rum, puta bellatorum, primogenitorum, Levitarum, numerorum in consecratione tabernaculi & altaris, ut & Veteris a cap. 1. ad 26. & deinde novi populi post decessum Patrum in deserto, quam stationum, ac in deserto tempore peregrinationis possessionum ma- gnam partem occupetur, doceatque, quomodo in numerato habere debuerint, quæ ad profectionem spectabant, unde dici potest ITINERARIUM Israelitarum. Ideo Abuiensis: A numeris ma- gis, inquit, appellatus, quam a reliquis, quæ in eo sunt; quoniam nihil est, per quod liber iste specialiùs a cæteris differat quam per numeros. In eo quippe tria describuntur, a quibus nomen accipere potuisset: videlicet præcepta, numerationes, & temporum histo- riæ: a præceptis nominari non decuit: nam de nullis hîc agitur, nisi judicialibus & ceremonialibus quibusdam. Sed non debuit appellari a judicialibus, quia plura tra- duntur in Deuteronomio: nec a ceremonialibus, quo- niam de his in Levitico principaliter agitur. Ab hi- storiis quoq; nomen accipere non debuit, quia illæ insunt libris etiam cæteris: Solæ igitur numerationes manent, a quibus liber iste per differentiam potuit nuncupari. Interpp. præter eos, qui in universa Biblia vel Vet. Testam. vel Pentateuchum solum scripsere, occur- runt pauci, qui in hunc solum libum operam contu- lerint: Hippolytum, qui An. 220. floruit commemo- rat Hieronymus, quod librum unum in Numeros adornarit. Extat & Cajetanus in Numeros; ut & Job. Wolsius. In Bibliis Duacensibus adducuntur A- cacius, de an. 350. & Severianus de Anno 400. qui in Genesin & Numeros: Greg. Nyssenus An. 380. qui in Exod. & Numeros, & Apollinaris junior An. 380. qui in Leviticum & Numeros quædam contulere.

Cæterum Ordinem respectu præcedentis libri nonnulli assignant istum: quod in Levitico ratio cul- tus divini & politicæ gubernatio certis quibusdam gradibus & classibus ordinetur, quo habeatur sedes etiam novæ Ecclesiæ & resonantis in ea doctrinæ de DEO, & Messia promisso. Sed quum non minus Levitarum & Sacerdotum munia, consecratio, & confirmatio eodem describatur, rectius ordo e Chronologia petitur, quia quæ erecto tabernaculo, de quo in Exodo, mense primo anni secundi ab egressu dictata & consignata in Levitico sunt, excipit nume- ratio populi in deserto, sub principium secundi Mensis, quam hic liber describit, adeoq; continet gesta 38. annorum & 9. mensium, videlicet a primo die secundi mensis in secundo exitus anno, usq; ad primum diem undecimi mensis in quadragesimo post exitum anno; ut ergo in Genesi præcipue eminet & elucet PRO- de CHRISTO semine benedicto, Adæ & Abrahæ tradita, & Historia Creationis Mundi, & Ec- clesiæ mirabiliter inde usque ab initio a DEO condi- tæ, propagatæ & defensæ: in Exodo, LEX DEI, seu promulgatio DECALOGI in monte Sinai, & consti- tutio Ecclesiæ ac Politiæ Judaicæ: in Levitico, Leges de sacrificiis, quæ sunt typi sacrificii & beneficiorum Christi & hostiarum spiritualium acceptarum Deo per Christum: in Deuteronomio, copiosa & luculen- ta enarratio Decalogi: ita in Numeris, Historia mi- randæ gubernationis populi Israël, triginta novem an- nis in deserto vagantis, recitatur.

Distribuitur autem secundum διχοτομίαν vel ratione materiæ, uti a B. Gerhardo in Exeg. de Scri- ptura S. factum, quod describat iter Israëlitarum per desertum, & ejus tum antecedentem præparationem, tum consequentem stationem, qua occasione exempla obedientiæ præmiis honoratæ, vel inobedientiæ pœnis visitatæ inferuntur, vel ratione Chronologiæ, a D. Pelargo, quod primo ea quæ in deserto usque ad 40. annum gesta sunt, tradat c. 19. Deinde reliquis ea, quæ quadragesimo anno secuta sunt. Aliis τρι- χοτομία placet cum Abulensi, quod primo justam ad profectionem Israëlitarum dispositionem usque ad c. 10. tum profectionem a monte Sinai ad solitudinem Moab usque ad c. 23. & historiam gestorum, quæ ac- cidêre istius peregrinationis tempore, persequatur, denique rationem exhibeat adeundi terram promis- sionis, & proximas stationes, ubi jam attigerunt limi- tes vel ipsam terram Canaan, usque ad finem libri. Nonnulli juxta tria deserta tres partes libri assi- gnant: Ad desertum Sinai historiam referentes a c. 1. ad 10. Ad desertum Cadesch, quod magnum duci- tur (Deut. 1, 19.) a c. 10. ad 20. Ad desertum Moabi- tarum a c. 29. ad finem libri. Alii 4. Sectiones fa- ciunt, ut prima recensionem populi tribuumq; ejus ad c. 4. altera legum quarundam commemorationem usque ad 10. c. Tertia historicam relationem variorum gestorum usque ad c. 28. Quarta denique tum le- gum quarundam cæremonialium, tum historiarum de- signationem mixtim exhibeat, quam distributionem cæteris præferimus, quia leges quæ c. 5. usque ad 10. traduntur, non tam ad profectionis παρασκευὴν pertinent, quam perpetuæ observationis sunt. Ideo pars prima dicatur ἀριθμητικὴ, numeratrix: pars secunda διατακτικὴ, legum quarundam ordinatrix: pars tertia ἱσορικὴ rerum gestarum commemoratrix: pars ultima mixta partim νομικὴ de sacrificiis, celebra- tione septimi mensis, redditione votorum, partim ἱσορι- κὴ de strage Midianitarum, partim κληροχικὴ, qua sortem duarum & dimidiæ tribuum, & post recen- sitas stationes, possessionem reliquarum tribuum & decisionem querelæ filiorum Manasse capp. ulti- mis.

## 1:1 Argument
PART I. ARITHMETICAL, In which both the popular or non-Ecclesiastical persons, whose Review occurs in c. 1. The military arrangement, c. 2. and the Ecclesiastical occur, such as Priests and Levites, c. 3. whose ministries are distributed, c. 4. CHAPTER I. The number of men of war besides the Levites, who carry the tabernacle. Verse 1.

AND THE LORD SPOKE TO MOSES.

These are the words of Moses, relating those things which the Lord spoke to him in the desert; from which some vainly suspect that not Moses himself, but Ezra, or another inspired man is the author of the book, because he speaks in the third person: He spoke to Moses. For that is not new, for an author to speak of himself in the third person: and the same is detected in the other books of Moses, Exodus, Leviticus, Deuteronomy not rarely, which nevertheless no one has therefore adjudged away from Moses. But the Lord spoke to Moses, not an angel bearing the person of the Lord, as Cornelius wishes, but the Lord himself, because the name Jehovah is nowhere used of an angel: nor can a place be shown in which an angel has so borne the person of God that he is called Jehovah in the nominative case: and what certainty will there be of historical narration, if it is permitted to understand an angel where the Lord is said to have spoken? And since Cornelius feels that the Lord spoke here from the Holy of Holies itself, how were these things said through an Angel? For not an angel, but the Lord sat in the Holy of Holies above the Cherubim.

IN THE DESERT OF SINAI.

Namely, in the twelfth station, which was in Sinai, which had a name distinct from Mount Sinai. They came there on the 3rd day of the 3rd month of the 1st year of the departure from Egypt, Exod. 19, 1. and since they finally departed from this station on the 20th day of the 2nd month of the following year, as is held in Num. 10, 11, it is manifest that they stayed there for an entire month, except for 13 days: from which it may further be gathered that all things which were done from chapter 19 of Exodus, through the whole book of Exodus, through Leviticus likewise as also the beginning of Numbers up to c. 10, were done in the desert of Sinai.

IN THE TABERNACLE.

Therefore, says Cornelius, GOD, that is, the Angel of GOD, did not speak with Moses at the door of the tabernacle, in the sight of the people (as at other times), but from the Holy of Holies itself, namely from the mercy seat, as is clear in chapter 7, at the end. But the angel did not answer from the mercy seat in the Holy of Holies, but GOD himself, nor were angels accustomed to be asked there, but GOD. Therefore, the distortion is to be rejected, that GOD spoke, that is, the angel of GOD, by which the minister is formed from the Lord, and the angel from GOD. Athanasius says that GOD spoke through the Son, orat. 4, with this reason added: ἃ λαλεῖ ὁ Θεὸς πρόδηλον ὅτι διὰ τῦ λόγε λαλεῖ, καὶ ἑ δι᾿ ἄλλε : it is manifest that the things which GOD speaks, He speaks through His Word, not through another.

Latin:

PARS I. ΑΡΙΘΜΗΤΙΚΗ, In qua tum personæ populares seu non Ecclesia- sticæ, quarum Recensio. c. 1. Castrensis ordi- natio, c. 2. tum Ecclesiasticæ occurrunt, ut- pote Sacerdotes & Levitæ, c. 3. quorum ministeria distribuuntur, c. 4. CAPUT I. Numerus virorum bellicorum præter Levitas, qui tabernaculum deferunt. Versus 1.

LOCUTUSQUE EST DOMINUS AD MO- SEN.

Verba hæc Mosis sunt, referentis ea, quæ Do- minus ad se locutus in deserto; e quibus fru- stra nonnulli suspicantur, non Mosen ipsum, sed Es- dram, aut alium virum θεόπνευςον autorem libri ef- se, quod in tertia persona dicat : Locutus est ad Mo- sen. Id enim novum non est, autorem de se in ter- tia persona loqui : & deprehenditur idem in cæteris Mosis libris, Exodo, Levitico, Devteronomio non ra- ro,quos tamen ideo nemo Mosi abjudicavit. Do- minus autem ad Mosen loquutus, non angelus per- sonam Domini gerens, ut Cornelius vult, sed Domi- nus ipse, quod nomen Jehovah nuspiam de angelo adhibetur: nec locus monstrari potest, in quo ange- lus ita personam Dei gesserit,ut Jehovah in casu re- cto dictus sit: & quæ certitudo erit narrationis hi- storicæ, si angelum intelligere licebit, ubi Dominus loquutus dicitur? Et quum ex ipso Sancto Sancto- rum hic loquutum esse Dominum sentiat Corne- lius, quomodo hæc per Angelum dicta sunt? non e- nim angelus, sed Dominus in Sancto Sanctorum su- per Cherubim sedebat.

IN DESERTO SINAI.

In duodecima nempe mansione, quæ fuit in Si- na, quod distinctum a monte Sina nomen habuit. Venerunt eo die 3. Mensis 3. anni 1. exitus ex Ægy- pto, Exod. 19, 1. & quum discesserint demum ex hac mansione anni sequentis mense 2. die 20. ut habetur Num. 10,11. per integrum mensem, exceptis 13. die- bus ibi hæsisse, manifestum est: unde porro colli- gere licet,omnia quæ inde a cap. 19.Exod. gesta sunt, per totum Exodi librum, per Leviticum item ut & initium Numerorum usque ad c. 10. in deserto Sina gesta esse.

IN TABERNACULO.

Non ergo in oftio tabernaculi, inquit Cornelius, in conspectu plebis (uti alias aliquando) cum Mose locutus est DEUS, id est, Angelus DEI, sed ex ipso Sancto Sanctorum, puta ex propitiatorio, ut patet cap. 7. ult. At e propitiatorio in Sancto Sanctorum non respondebat angelus, sed DEUS ipse, nec ibi ange- li rogari solebant, sed DEUS. Reprobanda ergo detorsio, loquebatur DEUS, id est, angelus DEI, qua ex Domino minister, ex DEO angelus formatur. Athanasius per Filium loquutum esse DEUM ait orat. 4. addita hac ratione : ἃ λαλεῖ ὁ Θεὸς πρόδηλον ὅτι διὰ τῦ λόγε λαλεῖ, καὶ ἑ δι᾿ ἄλλε : quæ loquitur DEUS, manifestum est, ea loqui per verbum suum, non per alium.

## 1:2
Vers. 2.

TAKE THE SUM.

In Hebrew, Take the heads, that is, head, or count the heads of all the Hebrews. This was a second census. For the former was made before the construction of the tabernacle and on account of the expenses to be spent on it, Ex. 38. But this one, on account of the camps being rightly arranged around the newly constructed tabernacle, and the line of warriors being ordered, excluding the Levites. Finally, when the entry into the land of Canaan was imminent, they were numbered a third time under Moses in the plains of Moab, Num. 26 (since those previously numbered in the desert had died) on account of the inheritance soon to be entered. Whence the diversity of the numbers and persons in the enumeration, or the numbers of the one numbering and the one numbered.

OF THE WHOLE CONGREGATION OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.

Because the children of Israel were to be numbered according to their tribes, and were numbered, proselytes or Egyptians did not come into the census, not admitted to their assembly, Ex. 12:38, who, dispersed through the various tribes, adhered to them, because whatever was of the male sex, from the twentieth year and above of all strong men, had to be numbered, therefore women, and those who were within the twentieth year, and the decrepit, who of the strong men could not be included by name, they are not numbered, as being unfit for war. GOD does not want in the Ecclesiastical militia either effeminate and soft and inconstant persons Matth. 11,8. Luc. 9,62. Eph. 4,14, or those who are children in understanding 1. Cor. 14, 20. not occupied by servile fear 2. Tim. 1, 11. or the slavery of sin Rom. 6,19. but stout-hearted and constant men 1. Cor. 13, 11. who, clothed in spiritual armor, may be able to resist in an adverse time, and having finished all, to stand Eph. 6, 13. As long as there is in any of us, says Origen hom. 1. a childish or slippery sense, or a feminine and lax sloth, or we bear Egyptian and barbarian manners, we do not deserve to be held among God in the holy and consecrated number.

BY THEIR KINDREDS AND HOUSES.

The root of the word מִשְׁפָּחָה (family) in the Hebrew language is now unused, but in the related Ethiopic language the word פשח is used for to extend Matth. 8,3. because a family is an extension of the race from a man and a woman. Generation seems to be a common name: family and house are special names: for a family embraces a large generation and sometimes several houses: But house is a particular signification, therefore v. 20. it is said BY GENERATIONS, and (Vav is exegetical, that is,) their families and houses.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

TOLLITE SUMMAM.

In Ebr. Tollite capita, hoc est, capitate, seu nu- merate capita omnium Ebræorum. Erat hic alter census. Prior enim ante structuram tabernaculi & ob sumtus in eum impendendos factus est Ex. 38. Hic vero, ob castra recte disponenda circa taberna- culum recens extructum, & aciem bellatorum ordi- nandam exceptis Levitis. Demum cum ingressus in terram Canaan immineret, tertium sub Mose nu- merati sunt in campestribus Moab Num. 26. (quum prius numerati in deserto obiissent) ob hæredita- tem mox adeundam. Unde numerorum & per- sonarum in numeratione diversitas seu numeri nu- merantis & numerati.

UNIVERSÆ CONGREGATIONIS FI- LIORUM ISRAEL.

Quia filii Israel juxta tribus numerandi erant, & numerati sunt, in censum non venerunt prosely- ti,vel Ægyptii,cœtui ipsorum non admisti, Ex. 12,38. qui per diversas tribus dispersi iisdem adhæserunt, quia numerari debuit quicquid sexus est masculi- ni, a vigesimo anno & supra omnium virorum fortium, ideo mulieres, & qui intra vigesimum annum erant, ac decrepiti, qui fortium virorum nomine comprehendi non poterant, non numerat sunt, utpote ad bella inepti. Non vult DEUS in Ecclesiastica militia vel effoeminatos & molles & in- constantes Matth. 11,8. Luc. 9,62. Eph. 4,14, vel eos, qui pueri sunt intelligentia 1. Cor. 14, 20. non occu- patos timore servili 2. Tim. 1, 11. aut servitute peccati Rom. 6,19. sed cordatos, constantes q́; viros 1. Cor. 13, 11. qui panoplia spirituali induti resistere queant tem- pore adverso, & omnibus confectis stare Eph. 6, 13. Donec inest, inquit Origenes hom. 1. alicui nostrum ver- puerilis vel lubricus sensus, vel fœminea & resoluta se- gnities, vel Ægyptios & barbaros mores gerimus, habe- ri apud Deum in sancto & consecrato numero non me- remur.

PER COGNATIONES ET DOMOS SUAS.

Vocis מִשְׁפָּחָה familia in Ebræa lingua ra- dix nunc est inusitata, in cognata Æthiopica vero usitatum est verbum פשח pro extendere Matth. 8,3. quod familia sit generis e viro & muliere extensio. Generatio videtur esse commune nomen : familia & domus nomina specialia sunt: familia enim amplam generationem & plures quandoque domos com- plectitur : Domus vero est particularis significatio, ideo v. 20. dicitur PER GENERATIONES, & (Vav est exegeticum, id est,) familias & domos suas.

## 1:4
Verse 4. CONCERNING RUBEN.

The princes of the tribes are reviewed according to the order of the marriage bed, so that first the sons of Leah, then of Rachel, thirdly of the handmaids are placed. The tribe of Levi is omitted. Yet the number of the XII tribes is completed, because the sons of one Joseph made two tribes, Ephraim, who is placed before the firstborn Manasseh, because he had been preferred by his grandfather, by divine instinct Gen. 48, 19. But all were firstborn, whose names are 1. Elisur, strength of GOD, or rock, 2. Selumiel, peace of GOD, 3. Naasson, augury, 4. Nathanael, GOD gave, 5. Eliab, GOD is Father, 6. Elisama, God of hearing, or my God hears, 7. Gamaliel, Retribution of God, 8. Abidam, father of judgment or my father is judge, 9. Abiezer, brother of help or my brother is helper, 10. Phegiel, encounter of God, 11. Eliasaph, God gathering, God added, 12. Achira, friend of my brother. Rabanus applies these names to the sacred order, Rupertus to all Christians: saying, these names are almost all splendid, and signify the beautiful profession of us all, who run in the present life, who all cross the sea of Baptism, and were all baptized in the cloud and in the sea, but in that which was signified by the cloud and the sea.

Latin:

Versus 4. DE RUBEN.

Recensentur principes tribuum juxta thori ordinem, ut primum Leæ filii, deinde Rachelis, ter- tio ancillarum ponantur. Prætermittuntur tribus Levi. Completus tamen est numerus XII. tribuum, quod unius Josephi filii duas tribus fecerint, Ephra- im, qui Manassi primogenito proponitur, quod ab avo prælatus erat, divino instinctu Gen. 48, 19. O- mnes autem erant primogeniti, quorum nomina E- lisur, DEI fortitudo, vel petra, 2. Selumiel, pax DEI, 3. Naasson augurium, 4. Nathanael DEUS dedit, 5. Eliab DEUS Pater. 6. Elisama, Deus exauditionis, vel Deus meus audit, 7. Gamaliel Re- tributio Dei. 8. Abidam pater judicii vel pater meus judex. 9. Abiezer frater adjutorii vel fra- ter meus adjutor, 10. Phegiel, occursus Dei, 11. E- liasaph, Deus congregans, Deus addidit, 12. Achira fratris mei amicus. Quæ nomina applicat Rabanus ordini sacro, Rupertus omnibus Christianis : Hæc inquiens, nomina fere omnia splendida sunt, & pul- chram omnium nostrorum professionem significant, qui in præsenti vita currimus, qui mare Baptismi omnes transimus, & omnes in nube & mari, sed in eo, quod per nubem & mare significatum, baptizati sumus.

## 1:4 Addition
To Num. ch. 1. v. 4. PRINCES p. 507. a.

Not by right of primogeniture, but by election according to the deeds performed, in the judgment of Bonfrerius. Which he proves as follows:

1. Naason, Prince of Judah, was not born from Judah's firstborn Sela (who nevertheless left sons, Num. 26, 20), but from Phares, his younger brother. 2. Otherwise those Princes, Numbers 34, would have been the sons of these: but now they are all different; as is evident in Caleb, Prince of Judah, the son, not of Naason, but of Jephone.

Latin:

Ad Num. c. 1. v. 4. PRINCIPES p. 507. a.

Non primogenituræ jure, sed electione secun- dum res gestas, judicio Bonfrerii. Quod ita probat:

1. Naason Princeps Juda non fuit natus ex Judæ primogenito Sela, (qui tamen filios reliquit, Num. 26, 20.) sed ex Phares, juniore ejus fratre. 2. Aliter Principes illi, Numer. 34. fuissent horum filii: Jam vero diversi sunt omnes; ut patet in Caleb, Principe Judæ, filio, non Naassonis, sed Jephone.

## 1:18
Ver. 18.

REVIEWING THEM BY KINDREDS) A Hebrew word, they made them to be generated, that is, they recorded their origins in the public registers. The LXX use ἐπεξοῦσαν with an Attic word.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

RECENSENTES EOS PER COGNATIONES) Hebræa vox, fecerunt eos generari, id est, in tabulas publicas retule- runt eorum origines. LXX. ἐπεξοῦσαν voce Attica.

## 1:20
Ver. 20. CONCERNING THE SONS OF JUDA.

This tribe is very numerous, and we see in it also the fulfillment of the Jacobite prophecy Gen. 49, 10. Thy brethren shall praise thee. For the family of Joseph was greatly increased on account of the grandfather's blessing, but Ephraim prevailed over Manasseh the firstborn in number and size on account of the transposition of hands Gen. 48. Which happiness, however, was later turned into the other numbering of this book on account of sins. Num. 26.34. The tribe of Ruben felt the force of the paternal curse, by which the honor and preeminence of the firstborn was taken from him, nor is his tribe as rich in number as the others.

Latin:

Vers. 20. DE FILIIS JUDA.

Numerosissima hæc tribus est, atque videmus in eo quoque complementum vaticinii Jacobæi Gen. 49, 10. Laudabunt te fratres tui. Aucta enim val- de Josephi familia ob Avi benedictionem, sed Ma- nassi prævaluit Ephraim numero & amplitudine ob manuum transpositionem Gen. 48. Quæ tamen feli- citas deinde ob peccata, conversa in numeratione hujus libri altera. Num. 26.34. Rubenis tribus sensit vim paternæ imprecationis, qua primogenituræ ho- nor, & præcellentia ipsi ablata, nec tribus ejus tam dives numero, uti aliæ.

## 1:42
ver. 42. BY GENERATIONS, AND FAMILIES AND HOUSES OF THEIR KINDREDS.

These, and the remaining words, are recounted by the names of individuals from the 20th year and above, all who were able to go forth to war, are repeated twelve times, namely by each individual tribe, nor yet is this tautology idle, but the repetition has its causes without a doubt most grave: such perhaps are also these, 1. lest any tribe be believed to be committed to memory by a voice of men either more neglected or more honored; nor 2. that the oblivion of ages should delete any tribe, which by such a diligent and uniform report was reduced to writing, to be recited in all ages: 3. and that such a prodigy of numbers should be proposed to the whole world in neither few nor dissimilar words: 4. and that it might be equally evident that God, with whom there is no respect of persons, cares no less for one than another or for each individual tribe: and what makes for our instruction as well as consolation, that even today God holds individual elect ones in no more neglected a place or number than the Jews of old: to whom is not unknown even the number of sparrows falling upon the earth or of our hairs. Matt. 10, 29. 30.

Latin:

vers. 42. PER GENERATIONES, ET FAMILIAS AC DOMOS COGNATIONUM SUARUM.

Hæc, & reliqua verba, recensiti sunt nominibus singulorum a 20. anno & supra omnes, qui poterant ad bella procedere, duodecies repetuntur, nimirum per- nes singulas tribus, nec tamen otiosa est hæc ταυτολογία, sed repetitio causas suas habet dubio procul gravissimas : Quales forte etiam hæ sunt, 1. ne aliqua tribus vel neglectiore vel honoratiore voce hominum memoriæ commendata credatur; neve 2. Seculorum oblivio ullam deleret tribum, quæ tam diligenti, conformique relatione in literas redacta, omnibus seculis recitanda erat: 3. utque tantum numerorum prodigium, nec paucis nec dissimilibus verbis universo mundo proponeretur: 4. & ut constaret pariter, Deum, apud quem nulla προσωποληψία, non minus unam quam alteram singulasve curare tribus: & quod ad nostram facit tum institutionem, tum consolationem, etiamnum hodie Deum non neglectiore loco numerove habere singulos electos, quam olim Judæos: Cui ignotus non est vel passerculorum super terram cadentium vel capillorum nostrorum numerus: Matth. 10, 29. 30.

## 1:46
ver. 46. SIX HUNDRED THREE THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED FIFTY MEN.

In the prior numbering of Ex. 38, the same number is repeated, and yet 23 thousand were slain between each census on account of calf-worship. Wherefore it must be believed that in the place of those slain, as many entered in, who in those few months completed their 20th year, so that the number might respond exactly. But why did God wish the number to be collected here? This was not done as if God did not have them in his count, but both so that the number of valiant men and the proceeds of the censuses might be certainly known to the Leader, because everyone paid half a shekel in the ordinary census for the use and maintenance of the ministry, Ex. 30, and so that a document might exist of divine truth, concerning the multiplication of the seed of Abraham, and of power, concerning the sustenance of such a great army, and of fatherly love, that like a shepherd he counts his own property, and that he has registered the names of his Elect. Luke 10, 20.

Latin:

vers. 46. SEXCENTA TRIA MILLIA VIRORUM QUINGENTI QUINQUAGINTA.

In priori numeratione Ex. 38. idem repetitur numerus, & cæsa tamen inter utrumque censum 23. millia ob μοσχολατρίαν. Quapropter credendum est, totidem cæsorum loco subintrasse, qui paucis illis mensibus annum 20. expleverint, ut numerus exacte responderet. Cur autem numerum hic Deus colligi voluit? Non id factum, quasi Deus eos non haberet in numerato, sed tum ut Duci numerus virorum fortium, & censuum proventus certo constaret, quia quilibet pretium in censu ordinario in usum & conservationem ministerii dimidium sicli solvebat, Ex. 30. tum ut documentum extaret divinæ veritatis, de multiplicatione seminis Abrahæ, & potentiæ, de sustentatione tanti exercitus, & amoris paterni, quod pastoris instar peculium suum numeret, quodque Electorum suorum nomina consignarit. Luc. 10, 20.

## 1:47
ver. 47. BUT THE LEVITES IN THE TRIBE OF THEIR FAMILIES WERE NOT NUMBERED WITH THEM.

For they were not to fight in war, but to handle sacred things. The case of the Maccabees is different, who at the same time presided over the government. It was indeed extraordinary that the Levites were employed by Moses for the execution of vengeance, when the people had fashioned the calf, Ex. 32, 28. In vain therefore does Cornelius pretend a difference between the sacred rites of the O. and N. T. that the Levites were occupied with other sacred rites than the clergy. Why also; when by the sacred rites of the N. T. it is not permitted to the Clergy, the Bishops themselves wage wars, and the supreme Pontiff himself handles all political matters.

Latin:

vers. 47. LEVITÆ AUTEM IN TRIBU FAMILIARUM SUARUM NON SUNT NUMERATI CUM EIS.

Non enim in bello pugnare, sed sacra tractare debebant. Alia est Maccabæorum ratio, qui simul imperio præerant. Extraordinarium vero fuit, quod Levitæ adhibiti a Mose ad executionem vindictæ, cum populus vitulum fabricarat Ex. 32, 28. Frustra ergo prætendit Cornelius differentiam sacrorum V. & N.T. quod Levitæ circa alia sacra occupati fuerint, quam clerici. Eccur item; quum per sacra N. T. id non liceat Clero, ipsimet Episcopi bella gerunt, ac politica quæq; ipse etiam summus Pontifex tractat.

## 1:51
ver. 51. WHOSOEVER OF THE OUTSIDERS APPROACHES, SHALL BE PUT TO DEATH.

Viz. who is not a Levite even by tribe and origin. Otherwise a stranger is taken in c. 3, 10. 38. c. 18, 7. who is indeed not a Priest, whence in this way even Levites are strangers. Moses is excepted, however, on account of his eminence.

Latin:

vers. 51. QUISQUIS EXTERNORUM ACCESSERIT, OCCIDETUR.

Sc. qui ne tribu quidem & origine Levita sit. Aliter extraneus sumitur c. 3, 10. 38. c. 18, 7. qui nempe Sacerdos non est, unde ita etiam Levitæ extranei sunt. Excipitur tamen Moses propter eminentiam.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II. The arrangement of the tribes according to the quarters of the world.

Latin:

CAPUT II. Collocatio tribuum juxta plagas mundi.

## 2:2
AROUND THE TABERNACLE OF THE COVENANT.

In the authentic text it is held otherwise, 'they shall pitch camp around the tent of meeting.' For the figure of the camp was square or rather quadrangular (not made in a circle), which figure Vegetius called the best. The atrium in width, and thence the eastern and western side, had 90 cubits, in length 100 cubits, which were also the dimensions of the southern as well as the northern side. In the middle was the tabernacle. At the eastern side were Moses, Aaron, and the sons of Aaron, whom Judah surrounded, and under him Zabulon and Issachar. To the west the Gersonites, whom Ephraim walled in, and under him Manasseh and Benjamin. To the south the Kohathites, which side Reuben protected, and below that tribe the tribes of Simeon and Gad. To the north the Merarites, whom Dan encircled, with Asher and Naphtali. The East, as Dionysius holds, is Christ, or faith illuminated by the Sun of wisdom, or it denotes the state of beginners, where Judah, that is confession, Issachar prayer, and Zabulon conversation has its place. The South is the prosperity of the Church, or the ardor of holy love, or the abundance of higher charisms, where Reuben is the vision of the brightness of truth, Simeon the hearing of charity, Gad happiness, or the sweetness of the mind. The West is a salutary death or the end of the world, and denotes the state of those who have progressed, where Ephraim is progress in spiritual things, Manasseh the forgetting of temporal things, Benjamin the love of heavenly things. The North is adversity, and the hardness of temptations, by which all who are fighting must be exercised. Where Dan denotes the tenor of the final judgment, Naphtali the shame of reproach, Asher the beauty of eternal happiness. Furthermore, the Tabernacle was in the middle of the camp, so that the Israelites might not doubt that the Lord was equally present to all Ex. 33, 14. 2. 2 Par. 32, 7. 8. nor that they should design anything unworthy of themselves in his sight. Which most elegant arrangement of the camp is a type of the ordered camps of the Church Cant. 6, 3. gathered from the four quarters of the world, in whose middle is God, so that it may not be moved Ps. 46, 3. 4. and also of the heavenly Jerusalem, which is placed in a square Apoc. 21, 16. The Hebrews hand down that the Israelites were so encamped around the tabernacle that a space of a thousand paces intervened. Junius and Tremellius conclude that a space of two thousand cubits intervened between the camp of the Israelites and the Ark of the covenant from the fact that this was commanded during the crossing of the Jordan Jos. 3. Thus this expansion of the camps in the desert would have been of many thousands. This square site of the others was only when the camps were fixed, but when they proceeded and were moved, it was done in a long and extended order v. 9.

Latin:

PER GYRUM TABERNACULI FOEDERIS.

In textu authentico aliter habetur, e regione circum tentorium conventus castra metabuntur. Quadrata enim vel potius quadrangula erat castrorum figura (non in gyrum acta) quam figuram Vegetius optimam dixit. Atrium in latitudine, ac inde orientale, & occidentale latus habebat 90. in longitudine 100. cubitos, quot etiam erant meridionalis, ut & septentrionalis lateris. In medio erat tabernaculum. Ad Orientale latus Moses, Aaron, & filii Aaronis, quos circumdabat Juda, & sub eo Zabulon & Isaschar. Ad occidentem Gersonitæ, quos vallabat Ephraim, & sub eo Manasse, & Benjamin. Ad meridiem Koharitæ, quod latus tuebatur Ruben, & infra illam tribum Simeonis & Gadis tribus. Ad Septentrionem Meraritæ, quos cingebat Dan, cum Asser & Naphthali. Oriens, uti Dionysius habet, Christus est, vel fides illuminata a Sole sapientiæ, vel notat statum incipientium, ubi Judas, id est confessio, Isaschar oratio, & Zabulon conversatio locum habet. Meridies est Ecclesiæ prosperitas, vel ardor sancti amoris vel affluentia superiorum charismatum, ubi Ruben visio fulgor veritatis, Simon auditio charitatis, Gad felicitas, vel dulcor mentis. Occidens est mors salubris vel finis mundi, & statum notat profectorum, ubi Ephraim profectus in spiritualibus, Manasse oblivio temporalium, Benjamin amor cœlestium. Septentrio adversitas est, & tentationum durities, qua exerceri oportet omnes militantes. Ubi Dan notans judicii ultimi tenorem. Naphthali opprobrii pudorem, Aser felicitatis æternæ decorem. Porro Tabernaculum in medio castrorum erat, ne dubitarent Israëlitæ omnibus æque præsentem esse Dominum Ex. 33, 14. 2. Par. 32, 7. 8. nec quid se indignum in conspectu ejus designarent. Quæ elegantissima castrorum dispositio typus est castrorum ordinatorum Ecclesiæ Cant. 6, 3. ex quatuor plagis mundi collectæ, in cujus medio est Deus, ut non commoveatur Ps. 46, 3. 4. nec non cælestis Hierosolymæ, quæ in quadro posita Apoc. 21, 16. Ebræi tradunt Israëlitas ita castrametatos esse circa tabernaculum, ut intercesserit spatium mille passuum. Junius & Tremellius bis mille cubitorum spatium intervenisse inter castra Israëlitarum & Arcam fœderis ex eo colligunt, quod in transitu Jordanis id mandatum fuerit Jos. 3. Sic multorum millium fuisset expansio ista castrorum in deserto. Cæterorum hic quadratus situs tantum erat, cum castra figebantur, at cum procedebant, & movebantur, fiebat id longo, & extento ordine v. 9.

## 2:3
Ver. 3. TO THE EAST JUDAH.

To him the first and principal place was assigned, and he led the column when it was necessary to proceed c. 10, 14. with his tribe and those which were subject to him as to an Arch-Leader, Issachar and Zabulon, because this tribe was the strongest, destined for rule, and for the lineage of Christ. Then Reuben with Simeon and Gad (we indicate the tribes) because he was the firstborn. Thirdly Ephraim, with Manasseh and Benjamin: Finally Dan with Asher and Naphtali. This site of Judah warns Princes and Magistrates to pitch their camps towards the East, that is, to direct all their counsels and studies so that they may look toward the entrance of the tabernacle, and by their own example lead others to piety, so to fix their seats that they may be able to direct their eyes to all things subject to them, and finally that they may dwell near the Pontiff and be defenders of the Ministry. The Hebrews assign to the standards of the first battle line of Judah a lion, to the second of Reuben a man, to the third an ox, to the fourth an eagle. Which Andr. Masio on 6. Jos. v. 9. by the fitting type saying they signified our propitiatory Christ, and his ark the Church, which was situated between these standards to be spread to all the quarters of the world by the signs of the four Evangelists.

Latin:

Vers. 3. AD ORIENTEM JUDAS.

Huic primus & præcipuus assignabatur locus, & agmen ducebat, cum procedendum erat c. 10, 14. cum tribu sua & quæ ipsi ceu Archi-Duci subjectæ erant, Isaschar, & Zabulon, quia hæc tribus fuit fortissima, regimini destinata, & prosapiæ Christi. Deinde Ruben cum Simeone & Gad (tribus indigitamus) quia erat primogenitus. Tertio Ephraim, cum Menasse, & Benjamin: Denique Dan cum Asser & Naphthali. Situs hic Judæ monet Principes & Magistratus, ut versus Orientem castra locent, hoc est, consilia & studia sua omnia dirigant, ut introitum tabernaculi respiciant, & suo exemplo aliis ad pietatem præeant, ita sibi sedes suas figant, ut ad omnia sibi subjecta oculos dirigere possint, ac denique juxta Pontificem morentur, ac Ministerii defensores sint. Hebræi vexillis primæ aciei Judæ leonem, secundæ Rubenis hominem, tertiæ bovem, quartæ aquilam assignant. Quæ Andr. Masio ad 6. Jos. v. 9. dicente apto typo significabant propitiatorium nostrum Christum, arcamq; ejus Ecclesiam, quæ inter hæc vexilla sita erat per quatuor Evangelistarum signa ad omnes mundi plagas diffundenda.

## 2:5
Vers. 5. SINGULI PER TURMAS, SIGNA ATQVE VEXILLA ET DOMOS COGNATIONVM SVARVM CASTRA METABANTVR) See, below 10, 10.

From the Hebrew, Cornelius rendered these things thus: every man by his own standard, with the ensigns of their father's house pitched camp: because besides the common standard of the battle line, there were special standards of the families or rather of the tribes.

Latin:

Vers. 5. SINGULI PER TURMAS, SIGNA ATQVE VEXILLA ET DOMOS COGNATIONVM SVARVM CASTRA METABANTVR) Vide, infra 10, 10.

EX Ebræo hæc ita perfecit Cornelius: singuli juxta vexillum suum in signis domorum Patrum suorum castra metabantur : quod præter vexillum aciē commune, specialia familiarum vel potius tribuum fuerint vexilla.

## 2:9 Addition
To ch. 2. v. 9. THEY SHALL GO FORTH FIRST. p. 508. b.

Whether because for the most part they went towards the east: or because those proceeding first and last had the largest armies for the protection of the sanctuary.

Latin:

Ad cap. 2. v. 9. PRIMI EGREDIEN- TUR. p. 508. b.

Sive quod ut plurimum orientem versus ibant: sive quod primo & ultimo procedentes maximos exercitus habuerint in tutelam san- ctuarii.

## 2:17
Ver. 17. BUT THE TABERNACLE OF THE TESTIMONY SHALL BE LIFTED UP BY THE OFFICES OF THE LEVITES.

Cornelius rightly notes that in the Hebrew it is: the tabernacle of the testimony shall set out, and the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camps. Which is not to be understood precisely of the middle, as if all the Levites were in the middle, because the Merarites and Gershonites followed the first battle line of Judah, or the first three tribes under the Arch-Leader Judah, but the Kohathites the second battle line of the camps, who precisely held the middle, ch. 20, 17. 21. And that was so observed in the procession of the camps. But when they fixed the camps, the Levites were located in the middle, as we observed at v. 2. We are taught by this divine order that Levites and Priests ought to be segregated from the rest, to adhere to the tabernacle, and to be situated in the midst of all, so that they may serve all and be able to care for the whole flock, Acts 20, 28.

Verse of the same. BY THE OFFICES OF THE LEVITES AND THEIR DIVISIONS) In the Hebrew: The encampment of the Levites in the midst of the Camps. The camps were square: in the middle of these were the sacred things, as among the Romans.

The Vulgate is rightly amended. But a doubt occurs in Num. 10, 33, where the contrary seems to be held: because the ark, which was in the tabernacle, is said to have set out not in the midst of the camps, but a three days' journey before them. To reconcile which, R. Solomon says that there were two arks for the Israelites, one of Moses, the other of Bezalel: in the former the fragments of the tablets were kept, in the latter the whole tablets, and that this one always proceeded in the midst of the camps: But Abarbanel answers more correctly: that the tent of meeting ORDINARILY set out in the midst of the camps, by virtue of this passage: but that the ark of the covenant of the Lord in Num. 10. WENT BEFORE the Israelites in that first setting out, that was done out of order, so that, namely, a convenient place for encampment might be explored: and similarly in the last setting out, when they crossed the Jordan, Jos. 3. which Abarbanel thinks was observed in this way to show honor to the Israelites, whom GOD wished to accompany for a certain distance of the way, as a man is accustomed to accompany his friend. Which is also the reconciliation of R. Aben-Ezra. Add that it may be said that in this place, Num. 2, the discourse is about the tabernacle of meeting, and the remaining vessels of the Sanctuary, except the ark, which according to Num. 10 went before the camps; since it is not absurd that the ark was then in one place, the tent of meeting in another. Compare what [we said] at Exod. 25, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 17. LEVABITUR AUTEM TABERNACULUM TESTIMONII PER OFFICIA LEVITARUM.

Recte notat Cornelius, in Ebræo esse : proficiscetur tabernaculum testimonii, & castra Levitarum in medio castrorum. Quod non præcise de medio intelligendum, quasi omnes Levitæ in medio fuerint, quia Meraritæ & Gersonitæ sequuti sunt primam aciem Judæ, vel primas tres tribus sub Archi-Duce Juda, Cahatbitæ vero secundam aciem castrorum, qui præcise tenuere medium, c. 20, 17. 21. Atque id ita observatum in processu castrorum. Cum autem castra fixerunt, in medio Levitæ locati fuere, ut ad v. 2. observavimus. Docemur hac τάξει divina, Levitas & Sacerdotes a reliquis debere segregatos esse, tabernaculo adhærescere, ac in medio omnium versari, ut omnibus inserviant, totumque gregem curare possint Actor. 20, 28.

Vers. eod. PER OFFICIA LEVITARUM ET TURMAS EORUM) In Hebræo : Metatio Levitarum in medio Castrorum. Castra erant quadrata : in horum medio sacra, ut apud Romanos.

Recte emendatur Vulgata. Sed dubium occurrit Num. 10, 33. ubi contrarium videtur haberi : quia non in medio castrorum, sed tridui itineris ante ipsas profecta dicitur arca, quæ erat in tabernaculo. Quæ ut conciliet R. Salomo, duas arcas Israëlitis fuisse, alteram Mosis, alteram Bezaleelis : in illa fragmenta tabularum asservata, in hac tabulas integras, & hanc in medio castrorum semper incessisse, ait : Sed rectius Abarbenel respondet : tentorium conventus ORDINARIE profectum fuisse in medio castrorum, vi hujus loci : quod autem arca fœderis Domini Num. 10. ANTE Israëlitas iverit in prima illa profectione, id factum fuisse extra ordinem, ut nempe exploraretur commodus castrametationis locus : ac similiter in profectione ultima, cum Jordanem trajicerent, Jos. 3. quod ita observatum putat Abarbenel ad honorem deferendum Israëlitis, quos ad certum viæ spatium comitari voluerit DEUS, ut homo solet amicum suum. Quæ etiam est R. Aben-Esræ conciliatio. Adde quod dici possit, hoc in loco Num. 2. sermonem esse de tabernaculo conventus, & reliquis vasis Sanctuarii, excepta arca, quæ juxta Num. 10. præcesserit castra; cum absurdum non sit, arcam tum fuisse in uno loco, tentorium conventus in alio. Conf. quæ ad Exod. 25, 16.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III.

The number of the Levites, and the redemption of the firstborn.

Verse 1.

AND MOSES) And yet there is nothing here about the offspring of Moses. For that Gershon mentioned in verse 17 was before Moses, as appears in Ex. 6, 16. 6.16. Doubtless Moses had adopted Aaron's sons as if they were his own, and had instructed them in all things necessary for the performance of the priesthood, judging them, as Abraham's descendants by both bloodlines, more fit for the Priesthood than those whom he himself had begotten by the Ethiopian woman. For the word תולדת extends thus far, as has been said elsewhere. See the Gemara on the title concerning the Sanhedrin.

That the word תולדת extends to adopted sons cannot be proven from the Scriptures. Nor are Aaron's sons adopted by Moses, even if he instructed them in those things necessary for a Priest. For he did this as a lawgiver and Governor of the people, prescribing laws from the mouth of GOD. Nor was the judgment as to who were more fit for the priesthood in the hands of Moses: God himself had chosen Aaron and his family, entrusting to Moses not the Priesthood, but the leadership. Did Grotius perhaps join the Papists, who said that the leadership was joined with the Priesthood in Moses? Nor is there any need for us to resort to adoption. Another reason can be given why Moses is mentioned here: Luke. Osiander, and with him the Weimar Paraphrasts, express it thus: These are the generations of Aaron and Moses in the day that the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, that is, the Levitical tribe (from which Aaron and Moses, the heads of God's people, originated) will now be described as to how great it was in number when God ordered it to be numbered on Mount Sinai. And such is also the Junius-Tremellius note. This opinion is supported if the word תולדת is taken to mean kinship. Stephanus Menochius says that the generation of both is recounted in verses 27 and 28 of this chapter: where the discourse is about the Amramite Levites. For these are the sons of Aaron and Moses, who had Aaron as their father. He felt that the descendants of Moses remained in a lower rank of the Levites, and therefore were numbered in a later place with the remaining Kohathite Levites. Nor is the interpretation of Piscator and the Belgian Paraphrasts inappropriate, who render the word תולדות as 'what happened to Moses and Aaron': since Conr. Kirchner observed in his Commentary that ילד is taken in a general sense for events which time brings forth as a mother; therefore Piscator renders it, 'this however is what has come to pass with Aaron and Moses.' For that word seems to be used in that way in Gen. 6:19, ch. 25:18, ch. 37:2, where the Belgian Paraphrase renders it 'these are Jacob's histories'; what happened to him in his family: as the added notes have it. Which sense the added words also seem to demand, concerning the time, 'in the day that the Lord spoke,' and the place, 'on Mount Sinai,' because the circumstances of place and time agree with events, but not likewise with generations.

same verse.

ON MOUNT SINAI.

Tremellius rendered it: To Mount Sinai, i.e., to the tent of meeting. That Moses was no longer on the mountain itself is clear from verse 4, because Nadab and Abihu had already been killed. The same sense is in Leviticus 21, verse 1.

Latin:

CAPUT III.

Levitarum numerus, & primogenitorum redemtio.

Vers. 1.

ET MOSI) Atqui nihil hic de Mosis sobole. Nam Gerson iste memoratus commate 17. ante Mosem fuit, ut apparet Ex. 6, 16. 6.16. Nimirum Moses Aaronis filios velut sibi adoptaverat, institueratq; ad omnia, quæ ad sacerdotium obeundum erant, necessaria, illos, ut Abrahamidas ex utroque sanguine, aptiores Sacerdotio judicans, quam quos ipse ex Æthiopissa genuerat. Vox enim תולדת hucusque porrigitur, ut dictum alibi. Vid. Gemaram ad titulum de Synedrio.

VOcem תולדת ad filios adoptivos extendi e Scripturis probari nequit. Neque adoptati a Mose Aaronis filii sunt, etsi eos instituerit de iis, quæ ad Sacerdotem necessaria. Hoc enim fecit ceu νομοθέτης & Gubernator populi, leges præscribens ex ore DEI. Nec penes Mosen erat judicium, quinam aptiores sacerdotio sint: Elegerat Deus ipse Aaronem ejusque familiam, Mosi non Sacerdotium, sed principatum committens. Num forte Grotius Papistis accessit, qui in Mose conjunctum cum Sacerdotio principatum dixere? Nec opus est, ut ad adoptionem deveniamus. Reddi potest alia ratio, cur hic Moses commemoretur: Luc. Osiander, & cum eo Paraphrastæ Vinarienses ita exprimunt: Hæ sunt generationes Aaron & Mosi in die, qua locutus est Dominus ad Mosen in monte Sinai, id est, describetur nunc tribus Levitica (ex qua oriundi sunt Aaron & Moses, capita populi Dei) quanta numero fuerit, cum Deus eam in monte Sinai numerari juberet. Atque ita etiam Junio-Tremelliana nota. Pro qua sententia faciet, si vox תולדת de cognatione accipiatur. Stephanus Menochius v. 27. & 28. hujus capitis utriusque generationem recenseri ait: ubi sermo est de Levitis Amramitis. Hi enim sunt filii Aaron & Mosis, qui Patrem Aaron habuerunt. Posteros Mosis in inferiori Levitarum gradu hæsisse sensit, ideoque cum reliquis Levitis Caathitis posteriori loco numeratos esse. Nec inconcinna est Piscatoris & Paraphrastarum Belgicorum interpretatio: vocem תולדות reddentium, quæ acciderunt Mosi & Aaroni: quum ילד in genere de eventibus, quos tempus tanquam mater gignit accipi Conr. Kirchnerus in Comment. observarit; ideo reddit Piscator, diß aber ists, was sich zugetragen hat mit Aaron und Mose. Ita enim usurpari videtur illa vox Gen. 6, 19. c. 25, 18. c. 37, 2. ubi reddit Paraphrasis Belgica diet syn Jacobs geschiedenissen; quod ipsi in familia ejus accidit: uti notæ adjectæ habent. Quem sensum etiam postulare videntur verba addita, de tempore, in die, qua locutus est Dominus; & loco, in monte Sinai, quia circumstantiæ loci & temporis eventibus conveniunt, non item generationibus.

vers. eod.

IN MONTE SINAI.

Tremellius reddidit: Ad montem Sinai, eten- torio sc. conventus. Non amplius fuisse Mosen in ipso monte e v. 4. liquet, quia interfecti jam erant Nadab & Abihu. Idem sensus est Levit. 21. v. 1.

## 3:2
verse 2.

AND THESE ARE THE NAMES OF THE SONS OF AARON.

Nadab, liberal. Abihu, he is my father: Eleazar, GOD is helper. Ithamar, palm: or from מורר & איתן, excellent and strong Doctor.

Latin:

vers. 2.

ET HÆC NOMINA FILIORUM AARON.

Nadab, liberalis. Abihu, pater meus ille: Eleazar, DEUS adjutor. Ithamar palma: vel ab מורר & איתן præstans & fortis Doctor.

## 3:3
verse 3.

Whose hands were filled and consecrated.

Some say that this expression 'He had filled his hand' arose from the fact that, by the handing over of certain parts of the sacrifices into the hands of the priests, they were put into possession of the Priesthood, and it was subsequently transferred to any consecration whatsoever. See Exod. 28, 41. 29, 9. 32, 29. It may be added that hands were also filled by the anointing of oil. Compare 1 Kings 22, 33. 2 Chron. 13, 9.

This was the first separation of the Levites, from which a second is distinct, which occurred after the death of Aaron in the 40th year from the exodus, Deut. 10, 8, when his son Eleazar had succeeded him; concerning which reformation and renewal Moses speaks there in a way as if it were a new institution. Thus GOD is said to have separated the tribe of Levi, when in the census of the Israelites He confirmed the Priesthood to the tribe of Levi.

Latin:

vers. 3.

QUORUM REPLETÆ ET CONSECRA- TÆ MANUS.

Nonnulli inde hanc loquutionem Impleverat manum, natam dicunt, quod traditione certarum partium sacrificiorum in manus sacerdotum immissi fuerint in possessionem Sacerdotii, ac porro transfumtam ad quamvis consecrationem. Vid. Exod. 28, 41. 29, 9. 32, 29. Addi potest, quod etiam unctione olei manus impletæ. Conf. 1. Reg. 22, 33. 2. Par. 13, 9.

Prima haec erat Levitarum separatio, a qua di- versa est altera, quae post mortem Aaronis anno ab exitu XL. contigit Deut. 10, 8. cum ei successisset fi- lius Eleazar, de qua reformatione & renovatione Mosis ibi quodammodo tanquam de nova institu- tione loquitur. Sic dicitur DEUS tribum Levi se- parasse, quando in recensione Israelitarum tribui Levi Sacerdotium confirmavit.

## 3:6
Verse 6. THAT THEY MAY MINISTER TO HIM.

These were the duties of the Levites: (1.) To minister to the priests, which is taught here. Compare ch. 18. (2.) To keep watch, by divisions, in the sanctuary, to sing psalms to the Lord there, and to pray for the people, Num. 8, 19. Ps. 134, 1, 2. (3.) To guard the sacred furniture, which is entrusted to them in verse 8. (4.) To carry and erect the sanctuary during the journey and the pitching of the camp, chapter 4; whence Augustine, Vol. 4, Questions from both Testaments: 'What presumption of rashness is it to compare the hewers of wood and carriers of water to the priests who are the bearers of the tabernacle and all its vessels?' For this was the office of the Levites.

Latin:

Vers. 6. UT MINISTRENT EI.

Levitarum haec erant munia, (1.) Sacerdoti- bus ministrare, quod hic docetur. Conf. c. 18. (2.) Excubare, per ordines, in sanctuario, ibidem Domino psallere, & pro populo orare Num. 8, 19. Psal. 134, 1. 2. (3.) sacram supellectilem asservare, quod v. 8. ipsis commendatur. (4.) Portare & erigere sanctua- rium in profectione & castrorum metatione cap. 4. unde August. T. 4. quaest. ex utroq; Test. Que temeritatis praesumtio Sacerdotibus bajulis tabernacu- li & omnium vasorum ejus & lignorum concisores & portatores aquae conferre? Hoc enim officium fuit Levi- tarum.

## 3:7 Addition
To ch. 3. verse 7. p. 509. b, AND THEY SHALL KEEP WATCH AND OBSERVE WHATEVER PERTAINS TO THE WORSHIP OF THE MULTITUDE.

In the Hebrew it is: and they shall keep his charge and the charge of the whole assembly, as Fagius, Oleaster, Munster, Osiander. His charge, namely Aaron's, that is, those things which Aaron is bound to observe. If you listen to Vatablus and Malvenda, they wish them to be, as it were, guardians of the law, both of the Priestly and the public law. You would more correctly say that there is committed to them the keeping of the tabernacle, the charge of Aaron, i.e., that they should minister to him regarding all things which were committed to his inspection, custody, and care as High Priest, so that those things might be observed, and that they should keep the charge of the multitude, that is, what was committed and enjoined to the people in sacred worship: that it might be kept in its duty, kept away from sacred things, and instructed and warned as to by what rite and by what ceremonies GOD is to be worshipped, and that it might conduct itself reverently in sacred matters. A third duty of theirs is added; that they should keep the vessels of the tabernacle; AND GENERALLY their office is thus comprised, that they were ordained to serve the service of the tabernacle, or to minister every ministry in the tabernacle; so that they were Ministers, both of Aaron and the Priests, and of the people or the Church, and also of the tabernacle or temple, and its furnishings. To which R. Aben-Ezra, as noted by Drusius on Num. 8. v. 24, also warned that singing pertains. Such as are called CUSTODIANS among us today, upon whom the duty of singing also falls.

Latin:

Ad cap. 3. versu 7. p. 509. b, ET EXCUBENT ET OBSERVENT QUIC- QUID AD CULTUM PERTINET MULTITUDINIS.

In Ebr. est: & custodiant custodiam ejus & cu- stodiam totius cœtus, ut Fagius, Oleaster, Munster. Osiander. Custodiam ejus, Aaronis scil. id est, ea quæ Aaron observare tenetur. Si Vatablum & Malvendam audias, eos esse volunt q. nomophy- lacas tam juris Sacerdotalis quam publici. Rectius dicas committi eis custodiendam tabernaculi custo- diam Aaronis, h. e. ut ministrent ei, quoad omnia quæ inspectioni, custodiæ, & curæ ejus, ut sum- mi Sacerdotis commissa erat, ut ea observarentur, & custodiant custodiam multitudinis, hoc est, quæ populo commissa & injuncta erant, in cultu sacro: ut in officio contineretur, a sacris arceretur, & quo ritu, quibusve ceremoniis DEUS veneran- dus sit, & ut reverenter se in sacris gereret, in- strueretur, & moneretur. Additur tertium eo- rum munus; ut custodiant vasa tabernaculi; ET GENERATIM officium eorum ita comprehen- ditur, quod nempe ad serviendam servitutem ta- bernaculi, vel ad ministrandum omne ministerium in tabernaculo ordinati fuerint; Ut ita Ministri es- sent, tum Aaronis & Sacerdotum, tum populi vel Ecclesiæ, tum etiam tabernaculi vel templi, ejusque supellectilis. Quo etiam cantum pertinere R. Aben-Ezra, notante Drusio ad Num. 8. v. 24. monuit. Quales hodie CUSTODES apud nos dicuntur, quibus etiam canendi officium in- cumbit.

## 3:10
Verse 10. BUT AARON AND HIS SONS WERE APPOINTED OVER THE SERVICE OF THE PRIESTHOOD.

Their duties were (1.) to sacrifice, (2.) to burn incense, (3.) to have charge of the inner sanctuary, (4.) to sprinkle blood for atonement, (5.) to offer public prayers for the people and to bless them, (6.) to set out the showbread every Sabbath, (7.) to light the lamps every evening. There was, therefore, an ecclesiastical ministry among the people of Israel, as Chytræus says on p. 659, by the command of teaching the divine Law, and illustrating the promise concerning the coming seed, Christ, and offering sacrifices divinely instituted, so that they might be types of the person, office, and benefits of Christ: and of administering the other Levitical ceremonies, judging between the unclean and the clean, announcing the remission of sins to many and to individuals, excommunicating the contumacious and the unclean, and receiving the same back if they had repented and been duly cleansed. From this definition, eight principal offices of the ministers, or Levitical priests, appear. Although these pertain especially to the priests, to whom the inferior ministers, the Levites, were subject: yet let it not be thought that the Levites were merely bearers or butchers, but they simultaneously cultivated studies of the doctrine concerning God, and other arts necessary for the Church and the Republic: and they were at hand to the priests in the propagation of heavenly doctrine, of letters, of the doctrine of the year, of the medical art, of music, in judging controversies of dogmas, and in instructing and confirming doubting consciences.

Latin:

Vers. 10. AARON AUTEM EX FILIIS EJUS CON- STITUTUS SUPER CULTUM SACERDO- TII.

Eorum munia erant (1.) sacrificare, (2.) adole- re incensum, (3.) interioris sacrarii curam gerere, (4.) sanguinem ad expiandum spargere, (5.) preces publi- cas pro populo fundere, eique benedicere, (6.) sin- gulis Sabbatis panes propositionis apponere, (7.) quotidie vesperi lucernas accendere. Fuit ergo mi- nisterio Ecclesiastico in populo Israel, dicente Chy- traeo p. 659. mandato docendae Legis divinae, & il- lustrandae promissionis de venturo semine Christo & offerendi sacrificia divinitus institutum, ut Typi essent personae, officii & beneficiorum Christi: & administrandi caeteras Ceremonias Leviticas, diju- dicandi immunda & munda, annunciandi remissio- nem peccatorum multis & singulis, excommuni- candi contumaces & immundos, & eosdem, si egis- sent poenitentiam & rite mundati fuissent, recipien- di. Ex hac definitione octo principalia Ministro- rum, seu sacerdotum Leviticorum officia compa- rent. Quae etsi Sacerdotibus praecipue congruunt, quibus inferiores ministri Levitae fuerunt: tamen nec Levitae tantummodo bajuli aut lanii fuisse exi- stimentur, sed studia doctrinae de Deo, & alias artes Ecclesiae & Reipublicae necessarias simul coluerunt: & sacerdotibus in propagatione caelestis doctrinae, literarum, doctrinae de anno, artis medicae, musicae, in dijudicandis dogmatum controversiis, in erudi- endis & confirmandis ambigentibus conscientiis praesto fuere.

## 3:12
Verse 12. I HAVE TAKEN THE LEVITES FROM THE SONS INSTEAD OF EVERY FIRSTBORN THAT OPENETH THE WOMB.

He who is born first from the mother, Exod. 13, v. 12, is said to have been taken by God, because He had decreed it, and was even then executing that decree. All the Israelites were indeed obligated to the worship of God, but the firstborn were so in a singular manner, to whom life was given precariously in the slaughter of the Egyptians, Exod. 12, 32, and who, the Hebrews hand down, had performed the priesthood from the beginning, in whose place He now substituted the Levites. until that firstborn should come, who would not redeem himself, but offer himself for us Lev. 9, 11.

Latin:

vers. 12. EGO TULI LEVITAS A FILIIS PRO O- MNI PRIMOGENITO, QUI APERIT VUL- VAM.

Qui primo ex matre nascitur Exod. 13, v. 12. Tulisse dicitur Deus, quia decreverat, & decre- tum illud jamjam exequebatur. Erant quidem omnes Israelitae ad cultum Dei obligati, sed singu- lari ratione primogeniti, quibus in clade Aegy- ptiorum precario vita data Exod. XII, 32. & quos inde ab initio Sacerdotio functos fuisse, Ebraei tradunt, quorum loco nunc substituit Levitas, donec veniret primogenitus ille, qui seipsum non redi- meret, sed pro nobis offerret Lev. 9, 11.

## 3:16
ver. 16. FROM ONE MONTH OLD.

Before one month they were considered unclean, and from one month, when they were counted, they almost equaled the number of the firstborn. But when it is a matter of their ministry, the Levites are counted from the 25th or 30th year.

Latin:

vers. 16. AB UNO MENSE.

Ante mensem unum impuri habebantur, & ab uno mense numeratis iisdem æquabant pene pri- mogenitorum numerum. Cum vero de ministerio eorum res est, numerantur Levitæ a 25. vel 30. anno.

## 3:17
ver. 17. AND THE SONS OF LEVI WERE FOUND BY THEIR NAMES, GERSON, AND CAATH AND MERARI.

In the Hebrew: And these were the sons of Levi. Then they were not found, because they had long since died, because they had entered into Egypt with their grandfather Jacob 217 years before. Cf. Exod. 6, 18. So that Cornelius may help the Vulgate, he says they were found, not in life, but in this census and number. But whence is it certain that the deceased came into the census and number? That is certainly false. For the living were counted from one month old and onwards, but not the dead. Those counted pitched their camps, which could not be done by the dead. Furthermore, the Gersonites and Merarites guarded, and in the journey carried, the parts of the tabernacle and the court. The former indeed the coverings, namely the veils and curtains with their ropes v. 26. The latter, however, the boards, columns, bases, pegs, and bars v. 36. But to the Caathites, who were preferred on account of Moses and Aaron, who descended through Amram from Caath, and over whom also Eleazar, the elder son of Aaron, was set, the sacred vessels were entrusted. The Levites exhibit a type of the holy ministry. For just as the Levites guard, carry, and assemble the individual parts of the Mosaic tabernacle: so the ministers and Doctors of the Church, carrying the word and Sacraments around in this wilderness of the world, are individual pastors and guardians of the flock committed to them, who by their doctrine, counsel, faith, and labor sustain the mass of the Church's government, and strive diligently that the individual members of the Church may be one, teach one, and confess one.

Latin:

vers. 17. ET INVENTI SUNT FILII LEVI PER NO- MINA SUA, GERSON, ET CAATH ET ME- RARI.

In Ebr. Et fuerunt isti filii Levi. Tum non in- venti sunt, quia jam pridem obierant, quia ingressi illi cum avo Jacobo in Ægyptum ante 217. annos. Conf. Exod. 6, 18. Ut juvet Vulgatam Cornelius, in- venti, inquit, sunt, non in vita, sed in censu hoc & nume- ro. Sed unde constat, in censum & numerum de- functos venisse! Id utique falsum. Numeraban- tur enim viventes a mense uno, & deinceps, non autem defuncti. Castra metabantur numerati, quod a defunctis fieri non potuit. Cæterum Gersonitæ & Meraritæ custodiebant, & in profectione portabant tabernaculi & atrii partes. Illi quidem operimen- ta, puta vela & cortinas cum suis funibus v. 26. Hi autem tabulas, columnas, bases, paxillos, & vectes v. 36. Caathitis vero, qui ob Mosen & Aaronem, qui per Amram ex Caath descenderunt, præferebantur, quibus etiam Eleazar Senior Aaronis filius præfe- ans, vasa sacra credita erant. Typum exhibent Levitæ S. ministerii. Ut enim Levitæ singulas ta- bernaculi Mosaici partes custodiuut, gestant, & coagmentant: sic ministri, & Doctores Ecclesiæ, verbum & Sacramenta in hoc mundi eremo cir- cumferentes, singuli gregis sibi commissi pastores & custodes sunt, qui doctrina, consilio, fide & labo- re suo molem gubernationis Ecclesiæ sustinent, ac ut singula Ecclesiæ membra sint unum, doceant u- num, fateantur & unum, sedulo elaborant.

## 3:26
ver. 26. THE TABERNACLE ITSELF AND ITS COVERING, THE TENT, WHICH IS DRAWN BEFORE THE DOORS OF THE TABERNACLE OF THE COVENANT.

By the tabernacle is to be understood the lowest veil of the tabernacle of ten curtains Exod. 26, 1; by the covering, however, the triple other veil placed over it, namely, the goats' hair, the rams' skins dyed red, and the violet skins. By the tent, the veil which is drawn before the doors of the roof, or the tabernacle, which was covered and veiled on all sides, which was its entrance and as it were its door. Finally, by the tent which is hung at the entrance of the court of the tabernacle, the veil of the court is indicated, which was before the tabernacle, just as the preceding veil was of the tabernacle itself. All these veils were committed to the Gersonites.

AND WHATEVER PERTAINS TO THE RITE OF THE ALTAR.

The Interpreter has hallucinated here, and the Abulensis acknowledges a distorted sense. In the Hebrew it is, and its ropes for all its work, and so also the Chaldean and the LXX, which differ greatly; whence other Papists sweat in vain in the reconciliation of the Vulgate, as if to say, and whatever (of the veils) pertains to the rite of the altar; for what do the veils have to do with the rite of the altar? It is not a matter of the rite of the altar, nor of the veils, which had already been commemorated.

The other curtains were entrusted to the Gershonites alone. But here the veil of the Kohathites is committed, which was spread over the Holy of Holies. Because to them the sacred vessels with the ark were entrusted, and the ark was to be wrapped in this veil.

Latin:

vers. 26. IPSUM TABERNACULUM ET OPERI- MENTUM EJUS, TENTORIUM, QUOD TRAHITUR ANTE FORES TECTI FOEDE- RIS.

Intelligendum est per tabernaculum infimum tabernaculi velum decem cortinarum Exod. 26, 1. per operimentum vero triplex aliud velum illi su- perpositum, sc. cilicinum, ex pellibus arietum rubri- catis, & janthinum. Per tentorium velum, quod trahitur ante fores tecti, vel tabernaculi, quod un- dique tectum & velatum erat, quod ingressio, & velut janua ejus erat. Per tentorium denique, quod appenditur in introitu atrii tabernaculi velum indigi- tatur atrii, quod erat ante tabernaculum, quemad- modum præcedens velum erat ipsius tabernaculi. Omnia hæc vela Gersonitis committebantur.

ET QUICQUID AD RITUM ALTARIS PERTINET.

Hallucinatus hic est Interpres, & sensum di- stortum agnoscit Abulensis. In Ebræo est, & funes ejus ad omne opus ejus, atq; ita etiam Chald. & LXX. quæ maxime differunt; unde frustra sudant alii Pon- tificii in conciliatione Vulgatæ, q. d. & quicquid (velorum) ad ritum altaris pertinet, quid enim vela ad ritum altaris? non de ritu altaris, nec de velis a- gitur, quæ jam commemorata erant.

Cætera vela Gersonitis commendata erant so- lum. Sed hic Caathitis velum committitur, quod oppandebatur Sancto Sanctorum. Quia his sacra vasa cum arca credebantur, & huic velo involvenda erat arca.

## 3:32
Ver. 32. BUT THE PRINCE OF THE PRINCES OF THE LEVITES ELEAZAR.

But was not Aaron himself the Prince of the Princes of the Levites? That he was the High Priest is undoubted, and therefore he is understood as the Prince of the Princes of the Levites as a General Superintendent, since Aaron was the most general one. Thus Zephaniah is called the second priest in Jer. 52:24, because he held a similar office.

Latin:

Vers. 32. PRINCEPS AUTEM PRINCIPUM LEVI- TARUM ELEAZAR.

At annon Princeps Principum Levitarum e- rat Aaron ipse? Hunc fuisse summum Sacerdotem, indubium est, ideoq; Princeps Principum Levita- rum intelligitur quasi Generalis Superintendens, quum Aaron fuerit generalissimus. Ita Sacerdos secundus dicitur Sophonia Jer. 52, 24. quod similem spartam gesserit.

## 3:36
Ver. 36.

THEY SHALL BE UNDER THEIR CUSTODY, THE BOARDS] In the Greek it is closer to the Hebrew: The oversight of the charge of the sons of Merari, the heads, etc. The Hebrew word פקדה signifies a function, which they here render as oversight, in Psalm 109:8 as bishopric, just as Luke does in Acts 1:21.

Latin:

Vers. 36.

ERUNT SUB CUSTODIA EORUM TABULÆ] In Græco propius ad Hebræum: Ἡ ἐπίσκεψις τῆς φυλακῆς υἱῶν Μεραρὶ τὰς κεφαλίδας &c. Vox Hebræa פקדה functio- nem significat quam hic ἐπίσκεψιν reddunt, Psal. 109, 8. ἐπι- σκοπὴν, quomodo & Lucas Actorum 1, 21.

## 3:37
Verse 37. THE PINS WITH THE CORDS.

Because the discourse is about the Merarites, the cords are to be understood by which the pillars of the tabernacle were stretched and fastened, as Josephus has it; for the Gershonites, along with the curtains and hangings themselves, guarded and carried those [cords] by which the curtains were to be fastened to the pins fixed in the ground and the hangings were to be spread out.

Latin:

Versus 37. PAXILLI CUM FUNIBUS.

Quia de Meraritis sermo est, funes intelligen- di, quibus distendebantur & firmabantur columnæ tabernaculi, uti habet Josephus; nam illos, quibus ve- la paxillis in terra fixis firmanda & cortinæ expan- dendæ erant, custodiebant & portabant Gersonitæ, cum ipsis velis & cortinis.

## 3:38
ver. 38. MOSES, AND AARON WITH HIS SONS.

Aaron's sons were indeed joined to them, as being consecrated to the Priesthood: but concerning the sons of Moses, it could be a matter of doubt, for these were not numbered separately from the other Kohathites, as will be said at v. 39. On the eastern side, where Judah, the principal Arch-Duke, dwelt, not only Moses as supreme Commander, but also Aaron had his seat, so that they might not be torn from each other, but that the political and ecclesiastical magistracy might be more closely joined. Sacerdotal holiness, says Rupertus, needs the rods of leaders and prelates, and the swords of kings, and nothing is safer when they agree with each other, nothing more pernicious when they disagree.

Latin:

vers. 38. MOSES, ET AARON CUM FILIIS SUIS.

Aaronis quidem filii ipsi juncti erant, utpote Sacerdotio consecrati: de Mosis filiis vero dubium esse possit, hi enim non fuere seorsim ab aliis Caathi- tis numerati, ut ad v. 39. dicetur. Ad orientalem plagam, ubi Juda præcipuus Archi-Dux moraba- tur, non solum Moses ceu summus Imperator, sed etiam Aaron sedem suam habebat, ne a se invicem divellerentur, sed conjunctiores essent magistratus politicus, & Ecclesiasticus. Ducum & præsulum fa- scibus, ait Rupertus, atque Regum gladiis eget Sacerdo- talis sanctitas, & nihil tutius, cum sibi conveniunt, nil pernitiosius, cum dissentiunt.

## 3:39
ver. 39. ALL THE LEVITES TWENTY-TWO THOUSAND.

The sum collected from the Gershonites is 7500, from the Kohathites 8600, from the Merarites 6200, which is 22300. That therefore only 22000 are numbered is done not so much for the sake of rounding the number, as because the 300 firstborn of the Levites were subtracted, since they themselves had to be redeemed, and not redeem others, although the Levites did not pay for their own firstborn, because they were the peculiar property of God, and the Levites received the firstborn of others and the tithes in place of God. Those 22000 Levites, therefore, were taken for as many firstborn of the sons of Israel, but under this number of Levites, Moses and Aaron are also included: because it is said that ALL the Levites made up this number, nor was Aaron a firstborn, because he had an older sister, Miriam, Exod. 2:7. Aaron was then three years old, when Miriam was already a grown girl. And therefore the sons of Moses are also commemorated here, which some gather from v. 1: as those who were reckoned among the Kohathites; compare 1. 1 Chron. 23:13, 14, since they were ignoble Levites, and therefore were not numbered separately like the sons of Aaron, as being destined for the Priesthood.

Latin:

vers. 39. OMNES LEVITÆ VIGINTI DUO MIL- LIA.

Summa collecta e Gersonitis 7500. Caathitis 8600. Meraritis 6200. est 22300. Quod ergo so- lum 22000. numerantur, non tam ob numeri rotun- dationem factum, quam quia demti primogeniti Levi- tarum numero 300. siquidem & ipsi redimi debue- rint, non vero alios redimere, quanquam non sol- verint Levitæ primogenita sua, eo, quod peculium Dei essent, & aliorum primogenita, & decimas loco Dei acciperent Levitæ. Illi ergo 22000. Levita- rum accipiebantur pro totidem primogenitis filio- rum Israel, sub isto autem Levitarum numero etiam comprehensi sunt Moses & Aaron: quia dicuntur OMNES Levitæ hunc numerum fecisse, nec primo- genitus erat Aaron, quia seniorem habuit sororem Mariam Exod. 2, 7. Aaron tum triennis erat, cum Miriam puella jam grandis esset. Ideoque etiam filii Mosis hic commemorati, quod nonnulli e v. 1. colligunt: utpote qui Caathitis accensebantur; conf. 1. Par. 23, 13. 14. quum ignobiles Levitæ fue- rint, ac proinde non ut Aaronis filii, utpote Sacer- dotio destinati, seorsim numerati sint.

## 3:39 Addition
To v. 39. at the end of the notes. to p. 510. b.

But since there were more firstborn among the 22,000 Levites than 300. For thus only every seventy-fourth would have been a firstborn, Bonfrerius observes 1. that such firstborn were not counted who had already become the head of some family (which he had also noted concerning the Egyptian firstborn), 2. where the first offspring was not male, there was no firstborn. 3. It is likely that only those were counted as firstborn, both in this and in the remaining tribes, who were born from that slaughter of the Egyptian firstborn, from which day God retained the right over them.

Latin:

Ad vers. 39. sub finem notarum. ad p. 510. b.

Quum vero plures fuerint ex 22000. Levi- tis primogeniti quam 300. Sic enim duntaxat se- ptuagesimus quartus quisque fuisset primogeni- tus, observat Bonfrerius 1. tales primogenitos non recensitos fuisse, qui jam effecti sunt familiæ ali- cujus caput (quod etiam de primogenitis Ægy- ptiis monuerat) 2. ubi prima proles non erat ma- scula, nullum fuisse primogenitum. 3. Verisimile esse, eos tantum primogenitos & in hac & in re- liquis tribubus fuisse computatos, qui nati erant ab illa Ægyptiorum primogenitorum cæde, a quo die jus in illos Deus retinuit.

## 3:42
Vers. 42. MOSES NUMBERED AS THE LORD HAD COMMANDED THE FIRSTBORN OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. The reasons why God wished them to be numbered and redeemed can be given as these: (1) that they might be reminded of the miraculous liberation of Israel from the servitude of Egypt, and the preservation of the firstborn during the slaughter of the firstborn throughout the whole kingdom; (2) of the consecration of this people, because in the firstborn all the children of Israel are to be named as God's own peculiar and proper people to serve Him holily; (3) of the dignity of the same above other peoples, who is held as πρωτογενεὸς, and the firstborn of peoples, and feels that affection of the eternal Father, such as is wont to be of parents toward their firstborn; (4) of the support of the sacred ministry, for whose sake the individual firstborn, who exceeded the number of the Levites, had to be redeemed with five shekels, that is, two and a half Joachimic shekels, Num. 18. (5) Concerning the firstborn Son of GOD, who was to come as the true and supreme Priest, and was to offer Himself to God, Luke 2.

But which of the firstborn were to be redeemed, Tostatus and Cornel. a Lap. and below Grotius, think was discovered by lot with R. Solomon.

Latin:

Vers. 42. RECENSUIT MOSES SICUTI PRÆCEPERAT DOMINVS PRIMOGENITOS FILIORVM ISRAEL. Causæ, cur Deus eos recenseri & redimi voluerit, hæ reddi possunt, (1) ut monerentur de miraculosa Israel liberatione e servitute Ægypti, & conservatione primogenitorum in cæde primogenitorum per universum regnum; (2) de consecratione hujus populi, quod in primogenitis Deo universi filii Israel in peculium & proprium populum ad sancte ipsi inserviendum nuncupandi sint; (3) de dignitate ejusdem præ aliis populis, qui velut πρωτογενεὸς, & primogenitus populorum habeatur, & eum sentiat affectum æterni Patris, qualis solet esse genitorum erga primogenitos; (4) de sustentatione ministerii sacri, cujus gratia primogeniti singuli, qui excedebant numerum Levitarum, quinq. siclis, hoc est duobus Joachimicis & dimidio redimi oportebat Num. 18. (5) De primogenito Filio DEI, qui venturus ceu verus, & summus Sacerdos, & seipsum Deo oblaturus erat, Luc. 2.

Quinam autem ex primogenitis redimendi fuerint, per sortem exploratum censet cum R. Salomone Tostatus & Cornel. a Lap. & infra Grotius.

## 3:49
Vers. 49. WHO WERE MORE.) Who by chance remained after the deed.

Latin:

Vers. 49. QVI FVERANT AMPLIVS.) Qui forte facta restabant.

## 4:1 Argument
CHAPTER IV. The rites and duties of the Levites.

Latin:

CAPUT IV. Ritus & officia Levitarum.

## 4:3
Vers. 3. FROM THE THIRTIETH YEAR) Yet they seem to have performed certain lesser tasks from the twentieth year, 1 Chron. 23, 24, 27. Then slightly greater ones from the twenty-fifth year, below 8, 24.

Previously the number of the Levites was taken from one month and upwards, because a bare substitution for the firstborn had to be made, but here, since they are to be set apart for the work of the ministry, to carry and guard the things of the sanctuary, strong men of 30 years are designated for it. Israelites were taken for battle from the age of 20, but for the sacred ministry from 30, by which it is taught that the burden of the sacred ministry and divine warfare is heavier than that of civil tasks and human warfare. For what the Vulgate has, OF ALL WHO ENTER TO STAND. In Hebrew it is, everyone who enters for warfare or military station, as Mercerus and Forsterus note that צבא is called an army or station.

Latin:

Vers. 3. A TRICESIMO ANNO) Minores tamen operas quasdam videntur præstitisse ab anno vicesimo 1. Paral. 23, 24, 27. Deinde paulo majores ab anno quinto & vicesimo, infra. 8, 24.

ANtea numerus Levitarum capiebatur ab uno mense, & deinceps, quia nuda surrogatio pro primogenitis fieri debebat, hic vero cùm ad opus ministerii segregandi sint, ad portandas & custodiendas res sanctuarii, viri fortes 30. annorum ad id desti- nantur. Ad pugnam assumebantur Israelitæ ab anno ætatis 20. sed ad ministerium sacrum a 30. quo docetur gravius esse onus sacri ministerii & militiæ divinæ, quam civilium operarum & militiæ humanæ. Nam quod habet Vulgat. OMNIVM QVI INGREDIVNTVR VT STENT. In Ebr. est, omnis qui ingreditur ad militiam vel stationem militarem, uti Mercerus, Forsterus צבא exercitum, stationem vocari notant.

## 4:3 Addition
To chapter 4, verse 3, towards the end of the notes, page 511, column a.

Regarding the fact that in Num. 8, verse 24, mention is made of 24 years, the Hebrews explain it thus: that they began to learn the ministry in the 25th year, and to exercise it in the 30th. Aben-Ezra says that in the 25th year they began the ministry of the tents (such as guarding the tabernacle, so that no one else might enter, and singing), and in the 30th year the ministry of the burden. But as for the fact that in the time of David, 1 Chron. 23, v. 24, and of Hezekiah, 2 Chron. 31, v. 17, and of Ezra, chapter 3, v. 8, they were employed from the 20th year, a change was made in that, David so willing and being inspired by GOD, 1 Chron. 28, v. 13.

v.13. et seqq. And this was required both by the necessity of the greater multitude of furniture and sacrifices in the temple than in the tabernacle, and for the greater magnificence of the temple, Ainsworth observes. Although it may be gathered from 1 Chron. 23 et seqq. that those of 20 years of age were not present with the sacrificing priests, but performed other lighter duties. But as for the fact that 25 is read instead of 30 in this place according to the LXX, Bonfrerius thinks this was done deliberately, so that it might not seem to the Gentiles to contradict the passage in Num. 8:24.

marriage through the adultery of the woman rather than the man, for another's offspring is substituted. And hence a married man having relations with an unmarried woman was not stoned; but a woman having a husband who committed fornication with an unmarried man was to be stoned, Lev. 20, Deut. 22. Moreover, this law was enacted, 1. lest husbands should rage against suspected wives: 2. so that wives might be kept in their duty and restrained from unchastity.

Latin:

Ad cap. 4. versu 3. sub finem notarum. pag. 511. a.

Quod Num. 8. versu 24. anni 24. mentio fit, Ebræi ita explicant: quod ceperint anno 25. addiscere ministerium, anno 30. exercere. Aben- Ezra anno 25. ministerium tentoriorum cepisse, ait (quales erat custodire tabernaculum, ne alius intraret, & canere) anno 30. ministerium oneris. Quod autem tempore Davidis 1. Chron. 23. v. 24. & Ezechiæ 2. Chron. 31. vers. 17. & Ezræ cap. 3. v. 8. ab anno 20. adhibiti, in eo mutationem factam Davide DEO ita volente & inspirante, 1. Reg. 28. v. 13.

v.13. seqq. idque tum exigente id necessitate ob ma- jorem multitudinem supellectilis, & sacrificiorum in templo, quam in tabernaculo, tum ad majorem templi magnificentiam, observat Ainsvvorth. quan- quam illos anno 20. non Sacerdotibus sacrificanti- bus adfuisse, sed alia quædam leviora officia præsti- tisse, colligatur e 1. Chron. 23. seqq. Quod vero pe- nes LXX. legantur 25. pro 30. hoc in loco, id con- sulto factum, ne Ethnicis id videretur repugnare loco Num. 8, 24. Bonfrerius putat.

conjugium per adulterium fœminæ quam viri, nam aliena proles substituitur. Et hinc vir uxora- tus cum soluta rem habens non est lapidatus; at mu- lier habens virum cum soluto fornicata lapidanda erat, Lev. 20. Deut. 22. Lata autem fuit hæc lex, 1. ne mariti sævirent in uxores suspectas : 2. ut uxores continerentur in officio, & ab impudicitia coerce- rentur.

## 4:4
