Not only does the triple repetition of the name Jehovah occur, but twice three benefits are commemorated, when namely the first is thus vowed by Jehovah: The Lord bless thee and keep thee, and the second thus: The Lord make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee, and finally the third, the Lord lift up his face upon thee, and give thee peace. Which συζυγία of two benefits in each clause, according to Rupert and others, denotes both θέσιν καλῶν and ἀφαίρεσιν κακῶν, or positive & privative thanks. But the triple συζυγία exceptionally hints at the mystery of the H. H. Trinity. For whatever other causes are handed down will either be rendered ἄτερ γραφῆς or will not sufficiently teach why a triple συζυγία of benefits was precisely ordered in such a solemn blessing singularly prescribed by God. But from the mystery of the H. H. Trinity the reason is clear and solid, by which these things pertain peculiarly to the three persons of the divinity, according to the tenor of scripture. That Jehovah or Lord is therefore pointed out in the first clause of the blessing, to whom the blessing is attributed in the Holy Scriptures as the source & origin of every blessing, both spiritual & corporal, of soul as well as body, with the benefit of conservation. But these things are attributed peculiarly to God the Father. For this is the fountain of blessing through Christ, and on account of Christ, and indeed in Christ we are said to be blessed everywhere, but God the Father is established as the fountain and source of every blessing, for which Christ also was ordained and sent to us, that we might be blessed. See Gen. 9, 1. c. 24, 36. c. 28, 3. Deut. 2, 7. c. 7, 13. Eph. 1, 3. 1. Petr. 1, 3. etc. The keeping of both soul and body respects the benefit of preservation, sustenance, protection, defense, and the ordination of angelic guardianship, which is known from the Apostles' Creed to pertain to the first article concerning creation, and is established from very many places of Scripture Job 10, 12. Ps. 17, 8. Ps. 121, 2. 3. 4. 7. 8. Ps. 27, 1. as also Ps. 91, 4. 11. etc.

Furthermore, that Jehovah or Lord is pointed out in the second member of the blessing, to whom is peculiarly attributed the shining of his face upon us and his pity for us, by which the same distinct benefits are hinted at, apart from keeping and preservation. But this is the Son of God, who makes his face shine upon the human race, since outside that shining of his face there is mere darkness after the fall, namely the darkness of ignorance, of sin, of misery, and the final infernal darkness, from which we are not otherwise delivered than when the Son of God, that true light, makes the face of grace shine upon us, and shone in the darkness, as is held in John 1:5, and ἐπιφάνη, his saving grace shone upon all men, Tit. 2:11, chap. 3:4. For this is that light which arose when darkness filled the earth 1:9, c. 3:19, c. 8:12, c. 9:6, c. 12:35, 46. The Dayspring from on high visiting us ἐπιφᾶναι τοῖς ἐν σκότει ϰὴ σκιᾷ ϑανάτε, Luke 1:78, 79, a light to the Gentiles, Isa. 42:6, & c. 49:6, Luke 2:32. This shepherd of Israel (who is also David's shepherd, Ps. 23:1) Asaph addresses in Psalm 80:4. Lord, make your face shine and we shall be saved, because all salvation consists uniquely in the shining of the face of the Son of God, Acts 4:12, so that the night was illuminated, the darkness of sadness and anxiety dispelled, and the light of confidence and joy arose, when the Son of God, the uncreated angel, went before the Israelites in the pillar of cloud and fire, Exod. 14:19, 20, when his face shone upon them, and led them, as the Son of God promised to Moses, Exod. 33:14 (for he appeared there to the man of God): My face shall go with you: Thus, uniquely through the Son of God, whose face of grace shines upon the whole world, the light of confidence and joy arose, when otherwise there was nothing but the darkness of despair and eternal sadness over the entire human race. Nor did this escape the Rabbis, nor was it disapproved of by them, because they attributed to the Son of God that grace and salvation come to us through his shining, for thus they explain that in Ps. 36:10. (to pass over other things now that are to be produced in their own place) With you is the fountain of life, and in your light we see light, in Midrash Tehillim, as is clear from the words of R. John in the same place: It is like a man who travels by night with the help of a certain lamp to the light; which indeed, having been extinguished by the wind, he lights again and again extinguishes, and he himself lights it and does this again and again, finally he himself says, why will there be such labor from this? I want to wait until the Sun comes out, by whose light I will make my journey. In a similar way, the children of Israel were subjugated in Egypt and Moses and Aaron coming delivered them, then they were subjugated in the time of Sisera, and Barak and Deborah coming delivered them. And so in every time, until they said: We are greatly wearied in deliverances, because for the reason that it was through carnal men we are immediately afflicted as before. But now from this point on we do not wish to be delivered except by God, and this is what David says in Psalm 118: THE LORD GOD and he has shone upon us. R. Hanna said: Moses glorified Israel saying: Blessed are you O Israel, who is like you, O people, who are saved in the Lord? Deut. 33. He did not say, whom the Lord saves, but who are saved by the Lord, because God said thus: In this world you are saved by the hands of men, but in the time to come I myself will be your redeemer, so that henceforth you are by no means to be judged or subjugated by another. See Hieronym. de sanct. fide lib. 1. cap. 5. Hebræomast. p. 52. Furthermore, since that shining of the face of the Lord is indicated here, by which, having pity on our miseries, he shines upon us with his grace, we who are all devoid of grace and are nothing but children of wrath, of whom shall we more rightly accept this, according to the analogy of Scripture, than of the Son of God, who out of supreme and infinite charity had pity on us, and shone upon us with his most gracious face, when we were sinners, so that we might be delivered from wrath? Rom. 5:8, John 15:13, John 3:16. Therefore, so that we may enjoy this mercy unto eternal salvation, the Apostles are accustomed to pray for the grace of Jesus Christ, as is evident from 2. Cor. 13:13 and other places, because the shining of the face of the Lord upon us, and the pity of the Son of God, is to be attributed to whatever grace and salvation comes to us, as he who, turning his face toward us and having pity on our plight, took upon himself the roles of mediator and surety, and deigned to deliver us from all misery, out of mere grace and mercy, whence comes all our wealth, salvation, and happiness. For we know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for our sake he became poor, so that by his poverty we might become rich, 2 Cor. 8:9. Waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life, Epist. Jude v. 21. In this Christ, and on account of this our Lord, the Son of God, the face of the grace of God the Father shines upon us uniquely, just as Daniel prayed in c. 9:17: O Lord God, make your face shine upon your sanctuary for the Lord's sake. Of whom also the Apostle in 1. Cor. 4:6: God, who said that light should shine out of darkness, has shone in our hearts πρὸς φωτισμὸν for the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of God ἐν προσώπῳ in the face of Jesus Christ. Nor does God show us grace and mercy otherwise than in Christ the Son, and through the same: because indeed the Son turns his face toward us and, having pity on us, as the mediator of God and men, reconciled us to his Father, and obtained his grace for us, Eph. 1:6, John 1:17. Therefore the Hieronymian Psalmist addressed and besought the Son of God for this pity thus, Psalm 2:14: You, O Lord, will arise, you will have pity on Zion, for the time to have pity has come. Whom the Psalmist addresses and invokes here, that he may arise and have pity on Zion, the Priests prayed for from him in the Ecclesiastical blessing: May Jehovah make his face shine upon you, and have pity on you. But above all, the Davidic commentary on Ps. 67 is clear, in which this part of the ecclesiastical blessing is explained thus: God be merciful unto us, and bless us, and cause his face to shine upon us, that we may know thy way upon earth, thy saving health among all nations. The holy psalmist prays, May God be merciful to us, and bless us, illuminating his face upon us, which is the second part of the ecclesiastical blessing, and afterwards, so that it may be manifest that that divine person to whom he directs his prayer is distinct from that divine person whose mercy and illumination of face he seeks, he says, not that we may know his way, but that we may know thy way and furthermore thy saving health, whence it is evident that GOD the Father is being addressed. For it is his saving health, and that saving health is called his, the knowledge of which he desires to be spread among all nations Isa. 49, 6. Luke 2, 30. as if to say. Would that the eternal Son of God, blessed for evermore, might have mercy on us, and deign to bless us (for in him every blessing is obtained); would that the Son of GOD might illuminate his face upon us, that we may know thy way upon earth, that we may know the way of salvation, and understand thy saving health, from whom and in whom is our eternal salvation, that by true faith in that saving health of THINE, we may obtain the light of grace, of salvation, and of eternal joy, that in that light we may see thy light. For no one knows the Father, except the Son, and he to whom the Son wills to reveal him Matt. 11, 27. No one has seen God, the Son who is in the bosom of the Father, ἐκεῖνος ἐξηγήσατο he himself has declared him John 1, 18. Whence the Son says, he who sees me, sees the Father, John 14, 9. Some make those latter words of the Psalm explanatory of the former; thus Bellarmine: that we may know thy way upon earth, that is, that thy Savior may be known among all nations. Who adds, the Hebrews have it more clearly, that thy way may be known upon earth, thy Savior among all nations, which Isaiah also predicted when he said, all flesh shall see the salvation of God, as St. Luke reports c. 3. This, therefore, he accepts as a desire for the coming of the Son of God. He is said to illuminate his countenance upon us when he grants that we may behold him as if with the veil removed, which he did most especially when, through the mystery of the incarnation, he was seen on earth and conversed with men, as is said in Baruch 3. And this is what the holy Prophet seems to be asking for in this place, that God might show his countenance, if not in the form of GOD, at least in the form of man. Which he also seeks, when he says in Ps. 78. (80. in Hebrew) You who sit upon the Cherubim, shine forth before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. And since this is the mercy which he sought at the beginning, he therefore repeats (in the Vulgate) And may he have mercy on us, that is, and thus by illuminating, namely his face upon us Bellarmine, which is also the explanation of Theodoret regarding this second part of the Ecclesiastical blessing, question 11 in Numbers. The second blessing foretells the appearance of God and our Savior. For the dispensation of God and our Savior according to the flesh is full of mercy, for which reason he has also granted us reconciliation toward God. Which, however, is not to be taken exclusively, but so that it includes whatever pertains to the mediatorial and saving office of the Son of God. For he did not only illuminate his face upon us when he was manifested in the flesh, but as often as he makes the serene face of his grace shine upon us, not only when he acquired salvation for us, but also when he applies the same to us, not only in the incarnation, but also in the illumination of us through the true knowledge of himself, in justification through faith, in the transformation into his image through the irradiation of his splendor: As the Sun is the fountain of light, says Chytraeus p. 668 in this place. and of vital heat, illuminates the whole world, and provides a vivifying power to all growing things: so the Son of God our Lord Jesus Christ, the fountain of light and eternal life, illuminates through the Gospel the minds of men oppressed by the most sad darkness of the ignorance of God, of sin, and of death; that is, he kindles in them the light of the true knowledge of God, and true consolation, righteousness, life, and the joy of a conscience liberated from the terrors of the law, the Devil, and death; finally, he kindles eternal life and gladness in them. This, Aaron, John the Evangelist, Isaiah, Micah, and other Prophets call TO ILLUMINATE. For LIGHT in the Hebrew language signifies not only this light of the sky, which is perceived by bodily eyes, but also the knowledge of the mind, by which we recognize God and other things not subject to the eyes, and life, gladness, liberation from great evils, divine governance, defense, and eternal happiness, just as on the contrary Darkness denotes ignorance, sin, most sad calamities, death, and desperation. Therefore, the Priest prays in this prayer in summary, that the Lord and Redeemer of the Church, the Son of God, the Sun of righteousness and Light of the world, may illuminate, teach, govern, and rule our minds, and vivify and exhilarate us with saving and joyful consolation and with his light. May the Lord illuminate his face upon you, that is, may he look upon you with a serene and joyful face, may he show himself appeased and clement to you, may he exhilarate and recreate you just as the Sun rising in the morning recreates and gladdens all men and living creatures with its serene and joyful light.

The third part of the Ecclesiastical blessing is as follows: Jehovah lift up his face upon you, and give you peace. That this is to be referred to the Holy Spirit, both the comparison of the preceding parts of the blessing, which pertain to the Father and the Son, and the analogy of other places of Scripture teach. For the Holy Spirit lifts up his face upon us, so that he may give us the internal peace of conscience, and the eternal peace of heavenly blessedness, when he confirms us and makes us certain of the grace of God and eternal salvation through the Word and Sacraments. God the Holy Spirit is invoked, that he may lift up and raise his gracious face upon us, so that his grace, sanctification, and consolation may stand out, and by his splendor overwhelm all temptations, not otherwise than as the Sun, emerging from dark clouds and storms, exerts its radiance, and having driven away the darkness, brings back a pleasing and saving light. For the Holy Spirit is the true paraclete, through whom we are recreated against all calamities by vivifying consolation: the Spirit of gladness, by whom we are exhilarated in every sadness: the Spirit of certainty, through whom we are confirmed against any temptations whatsoever regarding the perennial grace of God. And therefore there is need that he turn his face to us, not turn it away from us, nay rather that he lift up and extol that same face, so that in the word and through the word the same may be present to our eyes, and we, even in the midst of darkness and the shadow of death, beholding his gracious face, may be illuminated and refreshed by the splendor of his countenance. Whence the gift of peace is joined to this vow, and may he give, or rather, place peace upon you, which word, corresponding to the Hebrew, Lorinus acknowledges to have greater force, and to import a certain firmness. Because the Spirit, of whom David says in Psalm 51, v. 13, 'Confirm me with a Principal Spirit,' places or renders peace firm for us. Who makes us certain that we are the children of God, Romans 8, v. 16, by whose power we have full hope, Romans 8, v. 13, by whom we are sealed as with a seal and earnest of the inheritance, 2 Cor. 1, 21. Therefore the kingdom of God is said to consist in righteousness (of Christ), in peace with GOD through Christ, which the Holy Spirit places and confirms for us, and so also in joy in the Holy Spirit, Rom. 14, 17. Since the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of grace and peace, who kindles the light of true faith, gladness, and consolation in us, and fosters peace in our hearts according to the third article of the Apostolic Creed, it is not obscure that this third part of the blessing is not undeservedly referred to him. To which explanation Rabanus easily agrees in his exposition, book 1, on Leviticus 10. In that which is said: The Lord bless you, it is desired that the gifts of spiritual charisms (which we especially understand here) be poured out from heaven: but by the words, keep you, it is requested that what has been received by blessings may be preserved by his grace. In the following blessing, may he show his face to you, and have mercy on you, it is vowed that he may be propitious and grant true salvation according to that (Psalm 81, verse 48, show your face and we shall be saved, and Psalm 85, v. 8, Show us your mercy, and give us your salvation) finally, may he turn his face to you, and give you peace, he says, is the outcome of divine mercy, just as in the turning away of the face indignation is expressed (look upon me, and have mercy on me, Psalm 86, v. 16. Why do you turn away your face?) But when God has delivered us by turning his face to us from all our enemies, he bestows perpetual peace upon you. Rupert says this, who also notes that in this threefold blessing, the name of God is added a third time, on account of the most holy Trinity. Rickelius in the first member observes the collation of the gifts of grace and their multiplication, as well as of temporal goods to sufficiency, with preservation from evils, and conservation in goods. In the second, gracious illumination in this life, and leading to the beatific vision, with the gratuitous remission of sins, and compassion in our evils, so that we may be relieved in them. In the third, that he may look mercifully, piously prevent, mercifully console, and thus show himself gracious and familiar to us, and finally that he may bestow the peace of time, the peace of the heart (which is the rest of the mind in God) and the peace of eternity. B. Osiander explains it succinctly and not inelegantly thus: THE LORD BLESS THEE AND KEEP THEE, that is, God the Father multiply thee and all thy things, and keep thee from all evil. THE LORD MAKE HIS FACE SHINE UPON THEE, Hebr. illuminate, AND BE GRACIOUS UNTO THEE, that is, God the Son descend from heaven, be incarnate for thy sake: and having pity on thee, redeem thee with his blood from thy sins. THE LORD LIFT UP, Hebr. lift up HIS COUNTENANCE UPON THEE, AND GIVE THEE PEACE, that is, God the Holy Spirit mercifully take upon himself the care of thee: let him grant there faith in Christ: and let him apply to you through the ministry of the Gospel all the benefits of Christ: so that you may have in your conscience peace with GOD, because nothing in these lands can happen to a man more blessed. The Weimar Osiandrian paraphrase agrees, and both are foster-siblings to our explanation already delivered.

Fourthly, the mystery of the Most Holy Trinity is confirmed from the collation and harmony of similar passages, where by the triple repetition of the divine name the Holy Trinity is designated, and especially where the blessing or the prayer for grace is likewise made in the name of the three divine persons, such as Gen. 48. vers. 15. 16. 2. Cor. 13. vers. 13. Ap. 1. v. 4. as also Psalm 67. last verse. Let Elohim God the Father bless us, Elohenu, our God the Son of GOD, let Elohim God the Holy Spirit bless us, and let all the ends of the earth fear him (the triune God), concerning which Gregory the Great, book 29 of Morals, chap. 16, says: David, in order to show God as the author of all things in the Trinity, said: May GOD, our GOD, bless us, may God bless us; and lest by naming God a third time he might be thought to have said three Gods, immediately insinuating the unity of the same Trinity, he added, and let all the ends of the earth fear him. Add also the triple repetition of the name HOLY in the Seraphic δοξολογίᾳ (doxology) in Isaiah 6. Concerning all of which see Vol. III of the System of Theology.

To these finally is added the consensus and ὁμοψηφία (unanimity) of Christian interpreters, who teach with us that this blessing embraces the mystery of the Most Holy Trinity. Athanasius, book on the Common Essence. Cyril, Fulgentius in his response against the Arians on heresy. Procopius, Strabo, Fuldensis, Rabanus, Rupertus, and most of the more recent ones. Let our blessed Gerhard be consulted concerning this ecclesiastical blessing in his special Disputation, which is found in the Separate Volume of Theological Disputations 2, page 1147 et seqq. And this is regarding that solemn blessing, which to Augustine seems so divine that he judges it should be repeated at every moment of time: because it embraces every kind of salvation in very few words.

Latin:

Vers. 23. SIC BENEDICETIS] Stando, expansis mani-bus, clara voce.

Observanda de hac solemni benedictione Ec-clesiastica sequentia: (1) Autor principalis DEUS, quieam præscripsit & Sacerdoti summo Aaroni perMosen demandavit: Loquere Aaron, & Filiis ejus,ut per Mosen cæteras leges promulgavit, quempopulo Imperatorem ac veluti Regem præfecit,quem Nomothetam hic esse oportet, & quibus jusνομοθεσίας convenit: Ita hanc etiam legem de benedictione non immediate Aaroni dedit, sedMosen jussit eandem Aaroni tradere. Quum ergoa Deo ipso præscripta fuerit formula, in magnopretio merito fuit apud Israelitas, ac proinde se-quioribus temporibus mutari non debuit, substi-tuto loco nominis tetragrammati alio nomine, utpostea dicetur. (2) Causa ministerialis recitandæ be-nedictionis nominatur Aaron, unde εὐλογία Ἀαρὼνdicitur Syr. 36, 9. & filii ejus, quibus Sacerdotiumtum commissum jam erat, ad quod pertinebat nontantum docere & sacrificare, sed etiam orare & bene-dicere 2. Paralip. 30. v. 27. Syr. 45. v. 19. Erat autemin eo Sacerdos summus Christi Pontificis unici N.T. typus & figura; ut Aaron post expletas in docen-di & sacrificandi munere partes, antequam popu-lum dimitteret, benedictionem ei impertivit, sicChristus post expletum in terris ministerium, & incruce sacrificium, antequam Discipulos a se dimit-teret, benedictionem illis conferre voluit, quæ verofimiliter ad omnes tum Judæos Act. 3,25. tum gentesse porrigit Gen. 12,3. Gal. 3,14. (3) Ceremoniæ, quæadhibentur in hac benedictione. Tres indicatGrotius, quod facta fuerit stando, expansis manibus,& clara voce. Ebræi, unde hæc habet Grotius,addunt adhuc alia tria, ut proferatur hæc bene-dictio lingua sancta, ut facies dirigatur versus po-pulum, ut exprimatur nomen DEI tetragramma-ton ad singulas benedictiones, quod alias religioipsis fuerit efferre. Conf. Drusius in Num.

p. 371. Illam vero manuum expansionem P. Fagius ita factam monet, ut non solum pansis in cœlum ma- nibus orarint pro implendis istis benedictionibus, (quæ elevatio manuum commonefactio fuit de ani- ma ad Deum elevanda Ps. 25, 1. Ps. 68, 4. Ps. 118, 6.) sed manus etiam suas expanderint vel protenderint, super populum Lev. 5, 22. Syr. 50, 22. quasi Ecclefiæ u- niversæ capitibus easdem imposituri, acceptamque e cœlo gratiam manibus suis (hac χειροθεσίᾳ in- terveniente) in Ecclesiam ipsam deposituri. Quod ipsorum ministerium nequaquam infructuosum fuit, quia voluit per illud Deus benedictiones istas impertire, ut verbis promissionis hoc annexum ha- bet: Ego sum benedicturus eis, h. e. efficiam, ne fru- stra aut precati sint aut nomen meum super popu- lum posuerint, gratiamque meam illi annunciarint, unde etiamnum benedictio sacerdotalis maximi æstimanda, monente August. in quæst. ex V. & N. T. Cons. Syr. 36, 19. c. 3, 11. Matth. 10. 12. non tamen fuit vera χειροθεσία, sed aliquid analogon, eandem repræsentans, cum toti populo benedictio facta. Quando vero uni alicui singulari personæ ea collata, adhibitam manuum impositionem forte non negan- dum. Quod Junius & Tremellius v. 27. ita red- dunt: Et imponentes (manus) filiis Israel (invoca- bunt) nomen meum, textui non congruit authentico, in quo neque manuum, neque invocationis facta mentio. Ponere jubentur nomen Domini super filios Israel, manus imponere eis non jubentur. Illa ve- ro phrasis, ponere nomen Domini super aliquem, idem est, atque benedicere alicui in nomine Domini: ut e collatione Deut. 6, 18. c. 21, 5. c. 28, 10. 2. Sam. 6, 8. pa- tet: unde etiam nomen Domini in tabernaculo & templo positum dicitur, quia prædicatio & invoca- tio nominis Domini ac benedictio in eodem illis facta 1. Reg. 9, 3. c. 14, 21. 2. Reg. 21, 4. 2. Par. 33, 7. Ad ritus etiam pertinet, quod observatum a Weidnero in loc. fidei Christ. præcip. tr. 1. His benedictionibus Sa- cerdos alicui benedicens, protensas ante vultum suum palmas utrasœ́, tenebat, cum vero diceret DOMINUS tres digitos priores, pollicem videlicet, indicem atque medium manus utriusque erectos altius erigebat, & dicto ita Domino, digitos ut prius remittebat. Quod ille quidem ad mysterium S. S. Trinitatis signifi- candum adhibet: Quid trium digitorum elevatione melius, quam Trinitatis excellentia poterit allegoriza- ri? sed ægre e Rabbinorum testimoniis illa signifi- catio probabitur. Nonnulli e Ps. 67, 8. colli- gunt, cum Sacerdotes in hac benedictione dixere: Benedicat tibi Dominus, populum ex vera fide re- spondisse: Benedictus nobis Deus, Deus noster, bene- dicat nobis Deus.

(4.) Benedictionis hujus frequentatio. Vi- detur nonnullis verisimile eam singulis diebus ma- ne & vesperi, cum oblata sunt sacrificia in Ecclesiæ congregatione pronunciatam esse, quoties nempe populum Sacerdotes dimisere. Quæ pie in Ec- clesia nostra adhuc adhibetur, siquidem non ad ce- remonias Leviticas pertineat, sed ad promissionem de gratiosa Dei præsentia in Ecclesia Ex. 20, 24. Ex- cusari autem non potest Judæorum temeritas, quod ausi sint hanc benedictionem a DEO ipso præscri- ptam e mera superstitione mutare, ac loco nominis τετραγραμμάτε vel voces הקדוש ברוך הוא Sanctus benedictus ille substituere, ut notat Reuchli- nus in Cabal. vel uti in Pesickta habetur, & a Drusio Comment. in Num. 25. adductum est, vocem Adonai aut nomen aliud ea (ipsorum opinione) sanctius usurpare.

(5.) Mysterium S. S. Trinitatis in benedictione ista solemni designatum. Quod pernegant quidem Judæi, rident Sociniani; (Smal. contr. Schopper. p. 13. & alii)exagitant etiam nonnulli Calviniani, & imprimis Danæus in Comm. in h. l. Lombard. dist. 6. p. 42. Sed haud obscure confirmat (1.) Trina no- minis Jehovah repetitio, quod non semel aut bis, aut quater aut pluries, sed tribus vicibus id in hac bene- dictione recitandum fuerit. Quum enim hæc my- sterio non careat, neq; alia e Scriptura solide afferri possit, si a mysterio S. S. Trinitatis abeas, dubitan- dum non est, id hic designatum esse. Siquidem nullus apex in ejusmodi succincta & nervosa bene- dictione supervacaneus sit. (2.) Prædicati ratio. Dominus enim ille, a quo benedictio & vovenda est & impetranda, in solemni hac benedictione indigi- tatur, ejusque nomen super filios Israel ponitur. At Pater, Filius & Spir. S. sunt Jehovah vel Dominus, a quo benedictio vovenda & impetranda; E. Pater, Filius & Spir. S. in solemni benedictione indigitan- tur, & nomen Patris, Filii & Spir. S. ponitur super filios Israel. Minorem confirmant omnia illa testi- monia, quæ S.S. Trinitatis mysterium comprobant, de quibus vid. Tom. 3. System. Theolog. (3.) Di- stinctorum benedictionis membrorum consideratio. Non trina tantum repetitio occurrit nominis Jeho- vah, sed bis tria commemorantur beneficia, cum nempe primum a Jehova ita vovetur: Benedicat ti- bi Dominus & custodiat te, ac secundo ita: Illuminet Dominus faciem suam super te, & misereatur tui, ac denique tertio, attollat Dominus faciem suam super te, & donet tibi pacem. Quæ συζυγία duorum be- neficiorum in quolibet commate, juxta Rupertum, & alios tum θέσιν καλῶν tum ἀφαίρεσιν κακῶν, vel gratias positivas & privativas denotat. Trina au- tem συζυγία eximie S. S. Trinitatis mysterium in- nuit. Nam quæcunque aliæ traduntur causæ vel ἄτερ γραφῆς reddentur, vel non sufficienter do- cebunt, cur in tam solemni benedictione singulari- ter a Deo præscripta trina beneficiorum συζυγία præcise ordinata fuerit. E mysterio vero S. S. Tri- nitatis ratio luculenta est, atque solida, qua personis tribus divinitatis ea peculiariter, juxta tenorem scripturæ, conveniunt. Ille ergo Jehovah vel Do- minus in primo benedictionis commate indigita- tur, cui peculiariter benedictio tanquam fonti & o- rigini omnis tum spiritualis tum corporalis benedi- ctionis, animæ pariter & corporis cum beneficio conservationis in S. literis tribuitur. At Deo Pa- tri hæc tribuuntur peculiariter. Hic enim fons est benedictionis per Christum, & propter Christum, nec non in Christo passim benedici dicimur, sed sons & scaturigo omnis benedictionis Deus Pater consti- tuitur, ad quod etiam Christus nobis ordinatus & missus est, ut nos benediceremur. Vid. Gen. 9, 1. c. 24, 36. c. 28, 3. Deut. 2, 7. c. 7, 13. Eph. 1, 3. 1. Petr. 1, 3. &c. Custodia cum animæ tum corporis respicit bene- ficium conservationis, sustentationis, protectionis, de- fensionis, angelicæ custodiæ ordinationis, quæ ad articu- lum primum de creatione pertinere, e Symbolo A- postolico notum est, & e plurimis Scripturæ locis constat Job. 10, 12. Ps. 17, 8. Ps. 121, 2. 3. 4. 7. 8. Ps. 27, 1. ut & Ps. 91, 4. 11. &c.

Porro ille Jehovah vel Dominus indigitatur secundo benedictionis membro, cui peculiariter tribuitur illucescentia faciei super nos & miseratio nostri, qua eadem distincta beneficia a custodia & conservatione innuuntur. At hic est Filius Dei, qui super genus humanum lucere facit faciem suam, quum extra illam faciei ejus illucescentiam meræ sint tenebræ post lapsum, tenebræ nempe ignoran- tiæ, peccati, miseriæ & novissimæ tenebræ infernales, à quibus aliter non liberamur, quam cum Filius Dei lux illa vera faciem gratiæ nobis illuscescere facit, & in tenebris luxit, ut Joh. 1, 5. habetur, & ἐπιφάνη illuxit gratia ejus salutifera omnibus hominibus Tit. 2. v. 3. cap. 3. v. 4. Hic enim est lux illa, quæ orta est, cum tenebræ replerent terram Esa. 60, 1. lux mun- di, quæ illuminat omnes homines venientes in hunc mundum Joh. 1, 9. c. 3, 19. c. 8, 12. c. 9, 6. c. 12, 35. 46. Oriens ex alto visitans nos ἐπιφᾶναι τοῖς ἐν σκότει ϰὴ σκιᾷ ϑανάτε Luc. 1. versu 78. 79. lux gentium Esa. 42, 6. & c. 49, 6. Luc. 2, 32. Hunc pastorem Israëlis (qui & Davidis pastor Ps. 23, 1.) compellat Assaph Psal. 80. v. 4. Domine lucere fac faciem tuam & servabi- mur, quia in illucescentia faciei Filii DEI unice consistit omnis salus Act. 4, 12. ut illuminata nox, discussæ tenebræ tristitiæ, & anxietatis, exorta lux fiduciæ & lætitiæ, cnm in columna nubis & ignis præcessit Israëlitas Filius DEI angelus increatus Exod. 14, 19. 20. cum facies ejus ipsis illuxit, eoque de- duxit, uti promisit Filius Dei Mosi Exod. 33. v. 4. (hic enim apparuit ibi viro Dei) Facies mea tecum ibit : Sic unice per Filium Dei facie gratiæ suæ illu- cescentem orbi universo, lux fiduciæ & lætitiæ ex- orta, cùm meræ cæteroquin fuerint tenebræ de- sperationis, & tristitiæ sempiternæ super univer- fum humanum genus. Nec latuit hoc Rabbinos, aut improbatum ab ipsis fuit, quia Filio DEI vindi- carunt, quod per ejus illucescentiam gratia & salus no- bis obtingat, fic enim explicant illud Ps. 36, 10. (ut alia nunc taceamus suo loco producenda) Tecum est fons vitæ, & in lumine tuo videmus lumen, in Mi- drasch Thellim, ut è verbis R. Joann. ibidem li- quet : Simile est homini, qui per iter auxilio cujus- dam lucernæ pergit ad lucem in nocte; quam quidem extinctam à vento iterum accendit & rursum extin- guit, & ipse incendit & hoc facit sæpe & sæpe, demum ipse dicit, ut quid inde tantus labor erit ? Volo expecta- re, donec Sol exeat, ad cujus lucem faciam iter meum. Simili modo fuerunt filii Israël subjugati in Ægypto & venientes Moses & Aaron liberaverunt eos, de- inde fuerunt subjugati in tempore Sissaræ, & venien- tes Barac & Debora liberarunt eos. Et sic in quolibet tempore, donec dixerunt : Valde sumus in liberatio- nibus fatigati, quia eo quod fuerit per carnales ho- mines confestim sicut prius tribulamur. Sed jam à modo nolumus, nisi per Deum, liberari & hoc est, quod dicit David Psalm. 118. DEUS DOMINUS & illuxit nobis. Dixit R. Hanna : Moses glorificavit Israël dicens : Beatus es tu Israël, quis similis tui po- pule, qui salvaris in Domino? Deut. 33. Non dixit, quem salvat Dominus, sed qui salvaris à Domino, quia Deus dixit sic : In hoc mundo vos estis per ma- nus hominum salvati, sed in tempore venturo ego- met redemptor vester ero, ita, ut deinceps nequa- quam ab alio judicandi sitis, sive subjugandi. Vid. Hieronym. de sanct. fide lib. 1. cap. 5. Hebræomast. p. 52. Porro quum illa hic indigitetur faciei Domi- ni illucescentia, qua miseriæ nostræ misertus no- bis gratia sua illucescit, qui omnes expertes gratiæ, nec nisi filii iræ sumus, de quonam id rectius, juxta Scripturæ analogiam, accipiemus, quam de Filio DEI, qui ex charitate summa, & infinita nostri mi- sertus, facie sua gratiosissima nobis illuxit, cum pec- catores essemus, ut ab ira liberaremur ? Rom. 5, 8. Joh. 15, 13. Joh. 3, 16. Ideo ut hac misericordia ad æ- ternam salutem fruamur, solent Apostoli gratiã Jesu Christi precari, ut è 2. Cor. 13, 13. aliisque locis con- stat, quia illucescentia faciei Domini super nos, & mi- serationi Filii Dei tribuendum, quicquid gratiæ, & salutis nobis obtingit, utpote qui faciem suam ad nos convertens vicem nostri misertus, mediatoris & vadis partes in se suscepit, nosque ab omni miseria, ex mera gratia, & misericordia, liberare dignatus est, unde omnis nostra opulentia, salus ac felici- tas. Scimus enim gratiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi, quod propter nos egenus factus est, cum dives esset, ut illius inopia nos divites essemus 2. Cor. 8, 9. Expe- ctantes misericordiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi ad vitam æternam Epist. Jud. v. 21. In hoc Christo, & propter hunc Dominum nostrum, Filium DEI, unice illucescit nobis facies gratiæ Dei Patris, quem- admodum Daniel oravit c. 9, 17. Domine Deus, fac lucere faciem tuam super sanctuarium tuum propter Dominum. De quo etiam Apostolus 1. Cor. 4, 6. Deus, qui dixit ex tenebris lucem splendescere, illuxescit in cordibus nostris πρὸς φωτισμὸν ad illuminationem cognitionis gloriæ Dei ἐν προσώπῳ in facie Jesu Christi. Nec aliter gratiam & misericordiam exhibet nobis Deus, nisi in Christo Filio, & per eundem : quia nem- pe Filius faciem suam ad nos convertit nostrique misertus, ceu mediator Dei & hominum, nos patri suo reconciliavit, ejusque gratiam nobis impetra- vit Eph. 1, 6. Joh. 1, 17. Ideo Hiero-Psaltes Filium Dei ob hanc miserationem sic compellavit ac soli- citavit Psal. 2. v. 14. Tu Domine exurges, misereberis Sion, quia tempus miserendi. Quem hic compellat, & invocat Psaltes, ut exurgat, misereatur Sionis, ab eo precabantur Sacerdotes in benedictione Eccle- siastica : Jehova illucere faciat faciem suam super te, & misereatur tui. Sed imprimis luculentus est com- mentarius Davidicus Ps. 67. quo hæc benedictio- nis Ecclesiasticæ pars ita explicatur : Deus miserea- tur nostri, & benedicat nobis, illuminet faciem suam super nos, ut sciamus in terra viam tuam, in omnibus gentibus salutare tuum. Precatur Hieropsaltes, mi- seratur Deus nostri, & benedicat nobis, illuminans faciem suam super nos, quæ est secunda pars benedi- ctionis Ecclesiasticæ, ac postmodum, ut personam illam divinam, ad quam orationem suam dirigit, distinctam esse ab illa divina persona, cujus misera- tionem & faciei illuminationem petit, manifestum sit, ait, non ut sciamus viam ejus, sed ut sciamus viam tuam ac porro salutare TUUM, unde constat DE- UM Patrem compellari. Hujus enim salutare est, & dicitur salutare illud, cujus notitiam in omnibus gentibus divulgari desiderat Esa. 49, 6. Luc. 2, 30. q. d. Utinam æternus Dei Filius benedictus in secula nostri misereatur, & benedictione sua nos digne- tur (in ipso enim omnis benedictio contingit) uti- nam faciem suam Filius DEI illuminet super nos, ut sciamus in terra viam tuam, viam salutis cogno- scamus, & salutare tuum, à quo & in quo nostra æterna salus est, intelligamus, vera fide in illud salu- tare TUUM, luce gratiæ, salutis & æternæ lætitiæ potiamur, in lumine illo videamus lumen tuum. Nemo enim novit Patrem, nisi Filius, & cui vult Fi- lius revelare Matth. 11, 27. Deum nemo vidit, Filius qui est in sinu Patris, ἐκεῖνος ἐξηγήσατο ipse enarravit eum Joh. 1, 18. Unde Filius inquit, qui videt me, vi- det Patrem, Joh. 14, 9. Verba illa posteriora Psalmi nonnulli faciunt ἐξηγητικὰ priorum ; sic Bellarm. ut cognoscamus in terra viam tuam, id est, ut cognoscatur inter omnes gentes Salvator tuus. Qui addit, clarius habent Ebræi, ut nota fiat in terra via tua, in omni- bus gentibus Salvator tuus, quod etiam Esaias præ- dixit, cum ait, videbit omnis caro salutare Dei, ut re- fert S. Lucas c. 3. Hoc ergo accipit ceu desiderium adventus Filii Dei. Dicitur illuminare vultum suum super nos, quando præstat, ut eum q. remoto vela- mine intueamur, quod maxime præstitit, quando per incarnationis mysterium in terris visus est, & cum hominibus conversatus est, ut dicitur Baruch 3. At- que hoc videtur hoc loco petere S. Propheta, ut Deus vultum suum, si non in forma DEI, saltem in forma hominis nobis oftendat. Quod etiam petit, cum ait in Ps. 78. (80. in Ebr.) Qui sedes super Cherubim ma- nifestare coram Ephraim, Benjamin & Manasse. Et quoniam haec est misericordia, quam initio petiit, ideo repetit (in Vulgata) Et misereatur nostri, id est, & sic illuminando, videl. vultum suum super nos, mi- sereatur nostri. Haec Bellarminus, quae etiam expli- catio est Theodoreti quod hanc secundum partem benedictionis Ecclesiasticae attinet quaest. 11. in Num. Secunda benedictio Dei ac Salvatoris nostri apparitionem praenuntiat. Nam misericordia plena est Dei ac Salvatoris nostri dispensatio secundum car- nem, quapropter reconciliationem etiam erga Deum largitus est nobis. Quod tamen non accipiendum ex- clusive, sed ut includatur, quicquid ad officium Fi- lii Dei mediatorium ac Salvatorium pertinet. Non enim faciem suam super nos illuminavit modo, cum in carne manifestatus est, sed quoties nobis gra- tiae suae faciem serenam lucere facit, non solum, cum acquisivit nobis salutem, sed & cum eandem no- bis applicat, non modo in incarnatione, sed & in nostri per veram sui cognitionem illuminatione, per fi- dem justificatione, per splendoris sui irradiationem in imaginem suam transformatione: Ut Sol fons lucis, inquit Chytraeus p. 668. in h. l. & caloris vitalis, to- tum mundum illustrat, & vim vivificam omnibus re- bus nascentibus praebet: ita Filius Dei Dominus noster Jesus Christus, fons lucis & vitae aeternae, per Evange- lium mentes hominum tristissimis tenebris ignorationis Dei, peccati & mortis oppressas illuminat, hoc est, lu- cem verae agnitionis Dei, & veram consolationem, justitiam, vitam, gaudium conscientiae, a terroribus legis, Diaboli, mortis liberatae, denique vitam & laeti- tiam aeternam in eis accendit. Id nominant Aaron, Jo- hannes Evangelista, Esaias, Michaeas, & alii Prophe- tae ILLUMINARE. Significat enim LUX in Hebraeo sermone, non solum hoc caeli lumen, quod oculis corpo- reis percipitur, sed etiam notitiam mentis, qua Deum & alias res non subjectas oculis agnoscimus, & vitam, laetitiam, liberationem ex magnis malis, divinam gu- bernationem, defensionem & aeternam felicitatem, sicut e contra Tenebrae, ignorationem, peccatum, tri- stissimas calamitates, mortem & desperationem deno- tant. Ideo orat in hac precatione in summa Sacer- dos, ut Dominus & Redemtor Ecclesiae Filius Dei, Sol justitiae & Lux mundi, nostras mentes illustret, doceat, gubernet, regnat, & salutari ac laeta consola- tione, & luce sua nos vivificet & exhílaret. Illumi- net Dominus faciem suam super te, id est, serena & laeta facie te aspiciat, ostendat se tibi placatum & clementem, exhílaret, & recreet te sicut Sol mane oriens sereno & laeto lumine omnes homines & animantia recreat & laetificat.

Tertia pars benedictionis Ecclesiasticae ita ha- bet: Jehovah elevet faciem tuam super te, & ponat tibi pacem. Quam ad Spir. S. referendam esse, tum collatio praecedentium benedictionis partium, quae ad Patrem & Filium pertinent, tum analogia alio- rum Scripturae locorum docet. Nam Spir. S. attollit super nos faciem suam, ut nobis donet pacem consci- entiae internam, & pacem beatitudinis caelestis aeter- nam, cum nos de gratia Dei, ac salute aeterna con- firmat & certos reddit per Verbum & Sacramenta. Invocatur Deus Spiritus sanctus, ut attollat atq́; ele- vet super nos faciem suam gratiosam, ut emineat ipsius gratia, sanctificatio, & consolatio, suoque splen- dore omnes tentationes obruat, non secus, atque Sol ex atris nubibus, & tempestatibus emergens exerit suum jubar, & pulsis tenebris gratam & sa- lutarem lucem reducit. Est enim Spiritus sanctus verus paracletus, per quem adversus omnes cala- mitates vivifica consolatione recreamur: Spiritus lætitiæ, quo in omni tristitia exhilaramur: Spiritus certitudinis, per quem adversus quasvis tentationes de perenni Dei gratia confirmamur. Ideoque opus est, ut convertat faciem suam ad nos, non avertat a nobis, imo ut elevet & extollat faciem eandem, quo in verbo & per verbum eadem nostris oculis ob- versetur, nosque in mediis etiam tenebris, ac um- bra mortis faciem ejus gratiosam intuentes, splen- dore vultus ejus illustremur ac reficiamur. Unde conjungitur huic voto donum pacis, & det, vel po- tius, ponat tibi pacem, quod verbum Ebræo re- spondens, majorem vim habere agnoscit Lorinus, ac firmitatem quandam importare. Quia pacem nobis ponit seu firmam reddit Spiritus, de quo Da- vid Psalm. 51. v. 13. Spiritu Principali confirma me. Qui certos nos reddit, quod simus filii Dei Roman. 8. v. 16. cujus virtute plenam spem habemus Roman. 8. v. 13. quo tanquam sigillo & arrhabone hæreditatis nos obsignamur 2. Cor. 1, 21. Ideo regnum Dei dicitur consistere in justitia (Christi) pace cum DEO per Christum, quam ponit & firmat nobis Spiritus S. adeoque etiam gaudio in Spiritu Sancto Rom. 14, 17. Quum Spir. S. sit Spiritus gratiæ & pacis, qui lu- cem veræ fidei, lætitiæ & consolationis in nobis accendit, & pacem in cordibus fovet juxta tertium articulum Symboli Apostolici, non immerito ter- tiam hanc benedictionis partem ad ipsum referri, haud obscurum est. Cui explicationi consentiunt facile Rabani exposit. libr. 1. in Lev. 10. In eo quod dicitur: Benedicat te Dominus, optari spiritualium charismatum dona (quæ nos præcipue hic intelli- gimus) cœlitus effundi: verbis autem, custodiat te, postulari, ut quod benedictionibus perceptum est, gra- tia ejus conservetur. Sequenti benedictione, osten- dat faciem suam tibi, & misereatur tui, voveri, ut propitietur & veram salutem concedat juxta illud (Psal. 81. versu 48. ostende faciem tuam & salvi erimus, & Psalm. 85. v. 8. Ostende nobis miseri- cordiam, & salutare tuum da nobis) postrema de- nique convertat vultum tuum ad te, & det tibi pa- cem, ait, sit misericordiæ divinæ proventus, quem- admodum in aversione vultus indignatio exprimi- tur (respice in me, & miserere mei Psalm. 86. v. 16. Quare faciem tuam avertis?) Cum vero eruerit nos Deus convertendo vultum suum ad nos ab omnibus inimicis nostris, tribuit perpetuam pacem tibi. Hæc Rupertus, qui etiam notat, in hac benedictione tri- pliciter formata, nomen Dei tertio additum esse, ob sanctissimam Trinitatem. Rickelius in primo mem- bro observat collationem donorum gratiæ & multi- plicationem, nec non & temporalium bonorum ad sufficientiam, cum præservatione a malis, & conser- vatione in bonis. In secundo illuminationem gra- tiosam in hac vita, & perductionem ad visionem bea- tificam, cum remissione peccatorum gratuita, ac condolentia in malis nostris, ut relevemur in eis. In tertio, ut clementer aspiciat, pie præveniat, miseri- corditer consoletur, sicque gratiosum & familiarem se nobis exhibeat, ac denique ut largiatur pacem tem- poris, pacem pectoris (quæ est quies mentis in Deo) & pacem æternitatis. B. Osiander succincte, nec in- concinne ita explicat: BENEDICAT TIBI DOMINUS ET CUSTODIAT TE, id est, Deus pater multiplicet te & tua omnia, servetque te ab omni malo. OSTENDAT, Hebr. illumi- net DOMINUS FACIEM SUAM TIBI, ET MISEREATUR TUI, id est, Deus Filius de- scendat de cœlis, incarnetur tua causa: & misertus tui redimat te sanguine suo a peccatis tuis. CON- VERTAT, Hebr. attollat DOMINUS VUL- TUM SUUM AD TE, ET DET TIBI PA- CEM, id est, Deus Spiritus Sanctus clementer tui curam suscipiat: donet ibi fidem in Christum: appli- cetque per ministerium Evangelii tibi omnia Christi beneficia: ut habeas in conscientia tua pacem cum DEO, quia nihil in his terris homini contingere po- test beatius. Consonat paraphrasis Vinariensis Osi- andrina, & utraque nostræ explicationi jam tradi- tæ collactea est.

Quarto confirmatur mysterium SS. Trinita- tis e collatione & harmonia similium locorum, ubi trina repetitione nominis divini S. Trinitatis designa- tur, & imprimis, ubi benedictio vel gratiæ precatio itidem in nomine trium personarum divinarum fa- cta est, utpote Gen. 48. vers. 15. 16. 2. Cor. 13. vers. 13. Ap. 1. v. 4. ut & Psalm. 67. vers. ult. Benedicat no- bis Elohim Deus Pater, Elohenu, Deus noster Filius DEI, benedicat nobis Elohim Deus Spiritus Sanctus, & metuant illum (triunum Deum) omnes fines ter- ræ, de quo Gregor. M. l. 29. Moral. cap. 16. Da- vid ut autorem omnium Deum in Trinitate ostende- ret, dixit; Benedicat nos DEUS, DEUS no- ster, benedicat nos Deus, ac ne tertio Deum nomi- nans, tres dixisse Deos putaretur, ilico unitatem ejus- dem Trinitatis insinuans, addidit, & metuant eum omnes fines terræ. Adde etiam trinam nominis SANCTUS repetitionem in δοξολογίᾳ Sera- phica Es. 6. De quibus omnibus vid. Tom. III. System. Theol.

Quibus postremo accedit consensus & ὁμοψη- φία Interpp. Christianorum, qui hanc benedictionem S. S. Trinitatis mysterium complecti, nobiscum docent. Athanas. l. de Comm. essentia. Cyrillus, Fulgent. resp. contr. Arian. in hæres. Procopius, Strabo, Fuldensis, Rabanus, Rupertus, & recentio- res plerique. Conferatur de hac benedictione Ec- clesiastica B. Gerhardus noster Disp. peculiari, quæ habetur Volum. Separat. Disp. Theol. 2. pag. 1147. seqq. Atque hæc de solemni illa benedictione, quæ August. tam divina videtur, ut quolibet temporis mo- mento judicet ab optimo quoque esse repetendam: quia paucissimis verbis omne salutis genus complectitur.

## 6:26
Verse 26. THE LORD TURN HIS FACE TO YOU] May He be favorable to you.

Latin:

Vers. 26. CONVERTAT DOMINUS VULTUM SV- VM AD TE] Sit tibi favens.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAPTER VII. The offerings of the gifts of the Princes.

v. 1. AND IT CAME TO PASS ON THE DAY THAT MOSES HAD FULLY SET UP THE TABERNACLE, AND HAD ANOINTED IT, AND SANCTIFIED IT WITH ALL ITS VESSELS, THE ALTAR ALSO, AND ALL THE VESSELS THEREOF.

Moses proceeds to describe the offering of the Princes of Israel made after the erection and consecration of the tabernacle and the altar of burnt offering. The Papists, adhering to the Vulgate version, gather from it that it is indicated that on the same day that the tabernacle was erected, and its consecration took place, the offering of the Princes began to be made. Therefore they seek various reconciliations, since they think that it does not agree with the account in Exod. 40. v. 17, that the tabernacle was erected on the 1st day of the 1st month of the 2nd year of the exodus. But the numbering of the people described above in Num. 1 was instituted on the 1st day of the 2nd month of the same year, and in the consecration of Aaron and his sons, seven days after the erection were spent on the consecration of Aaron, and then the Princes began their offerings, which lasted for 12 days, and thus were finished only on the nineteenth day of the first month; how then could the Passover have been celebrated on the fourteenth? Regarding the former doubt, some seize upon the distinction of R. Solomon, found in Lyra, between the daily erection of the tabernacle made for seven days, and the stable erection until the moving of the camps. Regarding the latter, they invent that the Passover was not celebrated in that year at its proper time, because it was not permitted to celebrate two general feasts at the same time, the dedication (by the offering of the Princes) and the Passover. Others say that the consecration of the Priests and the offering of the Princes were begun on the same day, and thus the former was completed on the 7th day, but the latter on the twelfth day of the first month. Cornelius a Lapide and Lorinus, in order to extricate themselves from these doubts, invent a hysterology in the narrative of Moses; and Lorinus is quite prolix in discussing these matters. But there is no need for all these, nor is there any reason to posit a ὕστερον πρότερον (hysteron proteron). For the words of the sacred text do not indicate that the offering of the Princes was made on the same day that the tabernacle was completed and erected and anointed, since ביום (on the day) can be taken of time in a general sense, just as it has been rendered by the blessed Luther: And when Moses had set up the tabernacle (in the pluperfect) and had anointed and sanctified it, with all its vessels, and also had anointed and sanctified the altar with all its vessels, then the Princes of Israel offered, etc.

Thus, in just order without anticipation or confusion of times, the present chapter coheres with the preceding ones, concerning the census of the people and the substitution of the Levites in the place of the firstborn, and their office, as also the removal of the unclean from the camp, on which occasion the law concerning jealousy and the purgation of a suspected woman in Num. 5 was inserted, and concerning the purification of the Nazarites, if they had become unclean, in ch. 6. And thus, after that ordered assumption of the Levites and the removal of the unclean, the command of the ecclesiastical blessing, which Moses subjoins in this place, was given. Nor does any necessity compel us to posit a ὑστερολογίαν (hysterology), as if Moses had disturbed the order, whose commentaries have been the most accurate of journals until now. For not on the same day that the tabernacle was erected, i.e. On the first day of the first month of the second year, the offering of the Princes is said to have been made; it is only indicated that all things had been completed concerning the tabernacle and the altar of burnt offering before these offerings of the Princes began. Tremellius and Junius indeed explain the word ביום as 'day,' but they distinguish between the consecration of the tabernacle and the consecration of the altar of burnt offering. They say the former was done on the first day of the first month and the days following; but the latter on the second day of the second month, and that this is indicated in the present passage, because the offering then began to be made by the Princes when the consecration of the altar of burnt offering itself, and of all the vessels, had also been fully completed, thus rendering the text: And it came to pass, on the day that Moses had finished setting up the tabernacle, and had anointed it and sanctified it with all its instruments, and the altar with all its instruments (that is, on the second day, in the second month, of the second year from the exodus out of Egypt, for on the first day of the first month the tabernacle was erected, Exod. 40:2; afterwards, however, in the remainder of that same month it was consecrated, as is taught in the book of Leviticus; but this altar, namely of burnt offering, remained to be consecrated in the last place and in its own order with all its ministry, a good part of which ministry, since they were Levites, the dedication of the Levites very well preceded the consecration of this altar), when, I say, he had anointed these things, and had sanctified these things (which were the last that remained to be consecrated. For until now the tabernacle, and those things which were within, Moses had sanctified Lev. 8, 10. with their ministers in the same place, but now the matter concerns the sanctification of the altar of burnt offering, and of its ministers and instruments) that the Princes of Israel might offer &c. But it is nowhere taught that these things were done on the second day of the second month; and the space seems too narrow, if we attribute only a single day to the numbering and census and ordering of all the twelve tribes of that huge army, likewise to the numbering and substitution of the Levites in the place of the firstborn, and the redemption of these, and all the rest which have been related in the six preceding chapters, and more could have been spent on that matter, and even seven whole days, because only on the twentieth day of the second month did they begin to move the camp from Sinai, and twelve days were spent on the offering of as many Princes, described here. Nor is it to be admitted that the consecration of the altar of burnt offering was done only now. For burnt offerings had already been offered on it, when Aaron was performing the firstfruits of his office Lev. 8. and therefore it was necessary that that altar had already been consecrated. Wherefore the version of B. Luther, praised before, is here entirely to be preferred, lest the ordered narrative be disturbed for us. The consecration of the altar of burnt offering, which had already been completed before the beginning of the Aaronic Priesthood, is one thing; the dedication of that altar, which is described in this chapter, is another. That the altar was sanctified with all its vessels even before Aaron celebrated his firstfruits is evident from Lev. 8. v. 11. 15. But with no probability does Lorinus with Cornelius maintain that the present chapter should have been subjoined immediately to Exodus according to the order of history, because the consecration of the tabernacle and of Aaron and the offering of the Princes were done on the same day, and that here the order of subject matter is regarded rather than that of history: Since Moses, after the description of the tabernacle and the altars made in Exodus, wished to subjoin the description of the sacrifices. For in Leviticus (1.) it is nowhere taught that all these things were done on the same day. (2.) Seven days were spent on the consecration of Aaron Lev. 8. (3) The offering of Aaron was made before the offerings of the princes. See Lev. 9. v. 1. (4) Nadab and Abihu had already been killed when the Princes offered these gifts. Compare Levit. 10. verse 1. Num. 3. verse 4. (5) Thus the Mosaic narrative will be thoroughly disturbed without cause regarding the event described in Leviticus, such as the consecrations of the Priests and what are recounted in Numbers, which is not at all fitting. (6) Nor does Lyranus object without reason, how could Moses alone have sacrificed the victims of the Princes during the first seven days of the offerings of the Princes, before the consecration of Aaron and his sons was completed, if indeed each one offered twenty-one victims daily? Add that this is appropriate for the Priests, and therefore without doubt it was done by them after their consecration.

Nor does the conjecture of Cornelius have any place, that Aaron and his sons only flayed, cut up, washed, and placed the victims on the altar, but Moses alone slaughtered, killed, and sacrificed them. For this was not the office of Moses, nor were those things appropriate for Aaron and his sons, but rather for the Levites. And therefore, since God is a God of order and not of confusion, in that solemn offering of the Princes, without doubt, He willed that all things be done in order, and that each one administer his own duty. Nor is the reason for the other five Princes to be judged with the Abulensis as different from the first seven, as Cornelius maintains: since the reason for all was the same in the offering, as Moses describes in wordy terms, using the same words with set purpose for each, whence it is not to be doubted that the same reason was also observed in the immolation of the victims offered by them.

(7) If the first seven days of the offerings of the Princes are the same as the seven days of the consecration of Aaron, and the eighth is the same as the inaugural or auspicious day of the Aaronic office, Aaron and his sons could not have been free for those duties of the Levites in flaying, cutting up, and washing, because the consecration did not permit it, concerning which Lev. 8. v. 33. 'and you shall not go out from the door of the tabernacle for seven days until the day on which the time of your consecration is completed.' For the consecration is finished in seven days. It is sufficiently clear, as Bonfrerius admits, that the victims were not to be offered before the eighth day, on which Aaron and his sons began to offer, when they were offered by the Princes for sacrifice, but it was fitting that the tabernacle, the altar, and the Priests should have been sanctified first, before either the victims were offered or the rest of the apparatus of the offerings for performing the sacred rites was made. Nor indeed to me, the same Bonfrerius continues, page 756. does it seem probable, what some seem to want, that Moses offered these victims during those first seven days, but only those sacrifices which were necessary for the consecration of the Priests, the altar, and the rest of the temple utensils.

(8) How could Aaron on the eighth day both celebrate his firstfruits and at the same time offer the victims of the eighth Prince of Israel? (9) Would not those festive solemnities of the 12 days of the offering of the Princes have been interrupted by that fatal slaughter of the sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, which Cornelius says happened on that eighth day, or shortly after, at Lev. 10. v. 1. (10) Let the wise weigh how congruously those who maintain this opinion teach with Cornelius at this chapter verse 16, that Moses sacrificed during the first seven days, that Aaron began to perform the Priesthood on the eighth, and at the same time sacrificed the victims of the eighth Prince, and also the victims of the people, which, to wit, the people offered for the new consecration of the Priests, and that on the same day fire came from heaven which consumed the sacrifices of Aaron (by what fire, therefore, were the sacrifices of the Princes offered in the previous days consumed, if then for the first time fire came from heaven, was not heavenly fire required for all the sacrifices?) Finally, that on the same day Nadab and Abihu were killed. But these were killed because they used strange fire, Lev. 9. verse 1. Therefore Moses would have deserved the same punishment if he had burned the offerings of the first seven Princes with strange fire. Lastly, since in v. 2 the people are said to have already been numbered, the numbering must have preceded this offering, whence it cannot be admitted that some refer the offering of the wagons and oxen to the time of the erection of the tabernacle, and wish the designation of time made in v. 1 to refer only to that offering, because v. 2 testifies that it was made after the numbering of the people.

Verse of the same. AND ALL ITS VESSELS.

Rabanus, affirming that the basins, flesh-hooks, shovels, and the bronze laver were prefigured in Moses, applies both the Jewish people and Christ, and also the tabernacle, to the Church, which Christ completed and erected, when, redeeming it with His blood, He rendered it perfect for Himself through devotion, and raised it up in faith and hope to seek future glory; moreover, He anointed it with the oil of gladness, and sanctified it by the grace of the Holy Spirit with all its vessels, namely, the elect, who have been ordained for diverse ministries within the Church: he wishes the altar to signify either the Church in general, or all those perfect ones in whom the spices of virtues and holy prayers may be burned, or the humanity of Christ, in which he presented the pleasing gifts of our redemption to God the Father, being himself the same Priest and victim, and also the altar, because he offered himself of his own accord, holding death in his own power, so that no one might take his soul from him, nor would anyone have power over him, unless it had been given to him from above.

Latin:

CAP. VII. Oblationes munerum Principum.

v. 1. FACTUM EST AUTEM IN DIE QVA COMPLEVIT MOSES TABERNACULUM, ET EREXIT ILLUD, UNXITQVE, ET SAN- CTIFICAVIT CUM OMNIBUS VASIS SUIS, ALTARE, SIMILITER ET VASA EJUS.

PRogreditur Moses, ad describendum oblatio- nem Principum Israel post erectionem & con- secrationem tabernaculi & altaris holocausti fa- ctam. Pontificii Vulgatæ versioni adhærentes ex ea colligunt indicari, quod eadem illa die, qua ere- ctum est tabernaculum, & consecratio ejus facta sit, & Principum oblatio fieri cœperit. Ideo varias conciliationes quærunt, siquidem id non conve- nire putent relationi Exod. 40. v. 17. quod taberna- culum erectum sit die 1. Mensis 1. anni 2. exitus. Nu- meratio autem populi supra Num. 1. descripta die 1. Mensis 2. ejusdem anni instituta, & in consecra- tione Aaronis & filiorum ejus septiduum post ere- ctionem impensum consecrationi Aaronis ac de- inde ceperint Principes oblationes suas, quæ per 12. dies durarint, adeoque finitæ sint decimo nono demum die Mensis primi; quomodo ergo decima quarta tunc celebrari potuerit Pascha? Ad prius dubium nonnulli arripiunt R. Salomonis distinctio- nem apud Lyranum, inter erectionem tabernaculi quotidianam septem diebus factam, & erectionem stabilem usque ad motionem castrorum. Circa posterius fingunt Pascha celebratum non fuisse an- no illo, tempore suo, quia non licuerit duo festa generalia celebrare simul, dedicationem (per obla- tionem Principum) & Pascha. Alii dicunt, eodem die inchoatam Sacerdotum consecrationem & Principum oblationem, adeoque 7. die illam, duo- decimo vero die Mensis primi hanc completam fuisse. Cornelius a Lapide & Lorinus, ut dubiis hisce sese expediant, hysterologiam in Mosis nar- ratione comminiscuntur; & prolixus admodum est Lorinus in hisce discutiendis. Sed iis omnibus opus non est, neque præter causam ὕστερον πρότε- ρον statuendum. Verba enim textus sacri non in- dicant, eodem die factam esse Principum oblatio- nem, quo completum & erectum & unctum est tabernaculum, quum ביום accipi possit de tempore generatim, quemadmodum a B. Luthero reddi- tum est: Und da Mose die Wohnung auffgerich- tet hatte (in plusquamperfecto) und sie gesalbet und geheiliget, mit all ihrem Geräth, darzu auch den Altar mit allen seinem Geräthe gesalbet und ge- heiliget, da opfferten die Fürsten Israel &c.

Ita justo ordine sine anticipatione, aut tem- porum confusione cohæret caput præsens cum præcedentibus, de censu populi & surrogatione Le- vitarum in locum primogenitorum, atque officio eorundem, ut & remotione immundorum e castris, qua occasione inserta est lex de zelotypia & purga- tione suspectæ mulieris Num. 5. & de Nazaræorum, si immundi facti fuerint, mundatione c. 6. Atque ita post ordinatam istam Levitarum assumtionem, & immundorum remotionem benedictionis Ecclesia- sticæ, quam illis subjungit hoc loco Moses, præce- ptum datum est. Nec ulla cogit necessitas, ut sta- tuamus ὑστερολογίαν, quasi Moses ordinem turba- rit, cujus commentarii hactenus fuerunt epheme- rides accuratissimæ. Non enim eodem die, quo erectum est tabernaculum, h. e. die primo mensis primi, anni secundi dicitur facta Principum obla- tio, solum indicatur omnia peracta fuisse circa ta- bernaculum & altare holocausti, priusquam cœ- perint hæ oblationes Principum. Tremellius & Ju- nius exponunt quidem vocem ביום diem, sed di- stinguunt inter consecrationem tabernaculi, & conse- crationem altaris holocausti. Illam factam dicunt primo die mensis primi & sequentibus; hanc vero die secundo mensis secundi, atque hoc in præsenti indicari, quod oblatio tum fieri cœperit a Princi- pibus, cum plene absoluta fuerit consecratio etiam ipsius altaris holocausti, & vasorum omnium, ita reddentes textum: Fuit autem, quo die absolverat Mosche erigens tabernaculum, & ungens illud san- ctificaverat illud cum omnibus instrumentis ejus, & altare cum omnibus instrumentis ejus (id est, die se- cundo, secundo mense, anni secundi ab exitu ex Æ- gypto, nam primo die mensis primi erectum fuit tabernaculum Exod. 40, 2. postea vero mense eo- dem reliquo consecratum, ut docetur in libro Levi- tici, hoc autem altare nimirum holocausti postremo loco, & suo ordine restabat consecrandum cum to- to ministerio suo, cujus ministerii bona pars, quum fuerint Levitæ, optime Levitarum deditio antecessit hujus altaris consecrationem) quum inquam un- xisset ista, & sanctificasset ista (quæ postrema resta- bant consecranda. Nam hactenus tabernaculum, & quæ intus erant, Moses sanctificaverat Lev. 8, 10. cum administris ipsorum ibidem, nunc vero de sanctificatione agitur altaris holocausti, & administrorum ac instrumentorum ejus) ut offerrent Principes Israelis &c. At nuspiam docetur secunda die mensis secundi hæc facta esse; nimisque angustum videtur spatium, si unicum tantum diem tribuamus numerationi & censui atque ordinationi omnium duodecim tribuum ingentis istius exercitus, numerationi item ac surrogationi Levitarum in locum primogenitorum, horumque redemtioni, & reliquis omnibus, quæ sex cap. præcedentibus relata sunt, & plures eam ad rem, ac vel integri septem dies impendi potuerint, quia vigesimo die mensis secundi demum cœperunt castra moveri e Sinai, 12. autem dies impensi fuere oblationi totidem Principum, hic descriptæ. Neque admittendum consecrationem altaris holocausti nunc demum factam. Nam oblata jam erant in eodem holocausta, cum primitias officii sui perageret Aaron Lev. 8. ideoque oportuit altare illud jam consecratum fuisse. Quapropter versio B. Lutheri antea laudata hic omnino præferenda, ne ordinata relatio nobis perturbetur. Aliud est altaris holocausti consecratio, quæ jam peracta fuerat, ante auspicium Sacerdotii Aaronici, aliud, altaris illius dedicatio, quæ hoc capite describitur. Sanctificatum fuisse altare, cum omnibus vasis suis jam antequam primitias celebrararit Aaron, e Lev. 8. v. 11. 15. constat. Nulla autem verisimilitudine Lorinus cum Cornelio statuit juxta historiæ ordinem caput præsens subnectendum fuisse proxime Exodo, quod eadem die facta sit consecratio tabernaculi, & Aaronis, & oblatio Principum, atque hic non tam historiæ, quam materiæ spectari ordinem: Siquidem Moses post descriptionem tabernaculi & altarium in Exodo factam, subjungere voluerit descriptionem sacrificiorum. Nam in Levitico (1.) nuspiam docetur eadem die hæc facta esse omnia. (2.) Ad Aaronis consecrationem septem dies inpensi sunt Levit. 8. (3) Aaronis oblatio prius facta est, quam oblationes principum. Vid. Lev. 9. v. 1. (4) Nadab & Abihu jam occisi erant, cum Principes hæc munera offerrent. Conf. Levit. 10. vers. 1. Num. 3. vers. 4. (5) Sic turbabitur penitus narratio Mosaica citra causam rei gestæ in Levitico descriptæ, utpote consecrationes Sacerdotum, & quæ in Numeris recensentur, quod minime convenit. (6) Nec immerito objicit Lyranus, quomodo primis septem diebus oblationum Principum, antequam peracta consecratio Aaronis & filiorum ejus, Moses solus potuerit victimas Principum immolare, siquidem unusquisque obtulerit quotidie viginti & unam victimas? Adde quod conveniat hoc Sacerdotibus, ideoque sine dubio post consecrationem eorum ab ipsis factum sit.

Neque locum habet Cornelii conjectura, quod Aaron & filii solum excoriarint, conciderint, laverint, aræ imposuerint victimas, Moses autem solus mactarit, jugularit, immolarit easdem. Hoc enim Mosis officium non erat, neque ista Aaroni, & filiis ejus, sed Levitis potius conveniebant. Ideoque cum Deus ordinis Deus non confusionis sit, in illa solemni Principum oblatione, sine dubio, ordinate omnia peragi, & unumquemque suum munus administrare voluit. Nec alia ratio cæterorum quinque Principum cum Abulensi censenda, quam priorum septem, ut Cornelius statuit: quum omnium eadem ratio in oblatione fuerit, uti verbis prolixis describit Moses, eadem de singulis data opera adhibens verba, unde dubitandum non est, eandem etiam in victimarum ab ipsis oblata- tum immolatione observatam esse rationem.

(7) Si priores septem oblationum Principum dies cum septem diebus consecrationis Aaronis, octavus vero cum inaugurali vel auspicali muneris Aaronici iidem sunt, non potuit Aaron cum filiis suis vacare illis officiis Levitarum in excoriando, concidendo, lavando, quia id non permittebat consecratio, de qua Lev. 8. v. 33. de ostio quoque ta- bernaculi non exibitis septem diebus usque ad diem quo complebitur tempus consecrationis vestræ. Se- ptem enim diebus finitur consecratio. Satis li- quet, fatente Bonfrerio, victimas ante diem octa- vum, quo cœperunt Aaron & filii ejus offerre, offeren- das non fuisse, cum a Principibus ad sacrificium offer- rentur, conveniens autem fuit, ut prius tabernacu- lum, altare & Sacerdotes sanctificati essent, antequam vel victimæ offerrentur, vel reliquus apparatus obla- tionum ad sacra peragenda fieret. Neque vero mihi, pergit idem Bonfrer. pag. 756. verisimile sit, quod videntur aliqui velle, Mosen has victimas primis illis septem diebus obtulisse, sed tantummodo eas ho- stias, quæ consecrationi Sacerdotum, altaris & cætero- rum templi utensilium erant necessariæ.

(8) Quomodo octavo die Aaron & primi- tias suas celebrare potuit, & offerre simul victimas octavi Principis Israelis? (9) Annon festivæ illæ solemnitates 12. dierum oblationis Principum in- terruptæ fuissent funesta illa clade filiorum Aaro- nis Nadab & Abihu, quam Cornelius illo octavo die, vel paulo post contigisse dicit ad Lev. 10. v. 1. (10) Expendant cordati, quam congrue, qui hanc sententiam sustinent, doceant cum Cornelio ad hoc cap. vers. 16. primis septem diebus immolasse Mosen, octavo cœpisse Aaronem fungi Sacerdotio, ac simul immolasse octavi Principis victimas, nec non victimas populi, quas sc. populus offerebat ob novam consecrationem Sacerdotum, & eadem die venisse ignem de cœlo, qui sacrificia Aaronis absumpse- rit (quo ergo igne absumta Principum sacrificia in prioribus diebus oblata, si tum primum ignis de cœlo venit, annon ad sacrificia omnia ignis cœle- stis requirebatur?) Denique eadem die occisos esse Nadab & Abihu. At hi occisi, quod ignem alienum adhibuerint Lev. 9. versu 1. Idem ergo sup- plicium meritus fuisset Moses, si septem Princi- pum priorum oblationes alieno igne adolerit. Po- stremo quum v. 2. populus jam numeratus dicatur, oportet numerationem præcessisse ante hanc ob- lationem, unde admitti nequit, quod nonnulli plaustrorum & boum oblationem ad tempus ere- cti tabernaculi referunt, & temporis designatio- nem v. 1. factam illam solum oblationem respicere volunt, quia v. 2. testatur, eam factam esse post nu- merationem populi.

Vers. eod. ET OMNIA VASA EJUS.

Cujusmodi lebetes, fuscinulæ, forcipes, ignium receptacula, labrum æneum Rabanus in Moyse præfiguratum affirmans tum populum Ju- dæum tum Christum, tabernaculum quoque ad Ecclesiam applicat, quam Christus complevit & erexit, cum eam sanguine suo redimens perfectam sibi devotione reddidit, & in fide ac spe ad fu- turam gloriam appetendam erexit; unxit autem oleo lætitiæ, & sanctificavit gratia Spiritus San- cti cum omnibus vasis ejus, electis videlicet, qui ad diversa ministeria intra Ecclesiam ordina- ti sunt: altare vel generaliter Ecclesiam signifi- care vult, vel perfectos quosque, in quibus aromata virtutum, atque sanctarum orationum adoleantur vel humanitatem Christi, in qua grata munera re- demtionis nostrae DEO Patri exhibuit, utpote idem Sacerdos & hostia, altare etiam, quia sponte ob- tulit seipsum, in sua potestate mortem tenens, ita ut nemo tolleret animam illius ab ipso, nec haberet po- testatem quis in eum, nisi datum esset ipsi desuper.

## 7:2
Verse 2. THE PRINCES OF ISRAEL AND THE HEADS OF THE FAMILIES, WHO WERE OVER EACH OF THE TRIBES, AND THE PREFECTS OF THOSE WHO HAD BEEN NUMBERED.

Those three are synonyms: Princes of Israel, heads of families by tribes, prefects of those who had been numbered. However, it is not understood as the prior numbering, as Cornel. Lorinus and others wish in Exod. 38:25, for the Princes were not designated there: But that which Moses had instituted a little earlier, in this very second month, described above in chapter 1, which designates all those Princes and established their order in chapter 2, which was observed here in the offering. Those men rashly assert that the numbering (described at the beginning of this book of Numbers) was later than this offering of the Princes.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PRINCIPES ISRAEL ET CAPI- TA FAMILIARUM, QVI ERANT PER SINGULAS TRIBUS, PRÆFECTIQVE EO- RUM QVI NUMERATI FUERANT.

Synonyma sunt illa tria: Principes Israel, ca- pita familiarum per tribus, præfecti eorum, qui nu- merati erant. Intelligitur autem non numeratio prior, ut Cornel. Lorinus & alii volunt Exod. 38, 25. ibi enim designati non sunt Principes: Sed ea, quam paulo antea instituerat Moses, hoc ipso mense se- cundo descripta supra c. 1. quæ designat omnes illos Principes & ordinem eorum constituit cap. 2. qui hic observatus in oblatione fuit. Numerationem (in hoc libro Numerorum sub initium descriptam) posteriorem fuisse hac Principum oblatione teme- re isti asserunt.

## 7:3
Verse 3. SIX COVERED WAGONS.

The wagons were offered for the vessels of the tabernacle to be carried through the desert, and they were six in number, one from every two Princes, since just as many were required for convenient transport: they were covered, moreover, so that the vessels would not be damaged by rain or hail. Others add also, so that they could not be seen by the people. Each wagon was drawn by two oxen, because the Jews used oxen and horses rather than donkeys. Therefore, each of the Princes offered one ox. Two wagons and four oxen were given to the sons of Gershon, the remaining four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari; because the burdens of these were heavier, being of columns, boards, and bases, than those of the others, to whom the curtains were entrusted. Abulensis thinks that the sons of Merari could not have placed all their burdens on these four wagons, but that some had to be carried by them, but because most were difficult to carry, and it is said only of the sons of Kohath that they carried their burdens on their shoulders, it should rather be believed that more wagons were procured from sacred revenues, so that everything could be carried. Marius calculates how great those burdens of the Merarites and Gershonites were from chapter 38 of Exodus, where the quantity of gold, silver, and bronze that was offered is listed: 29 talents and 730 shekels of gold, 100 talents and 1775 shekels of silver, 2070 talents and 400 shekels of bronze, which make a sum of 274,996 pounds, for which burden neither the Merarites and Gershonites, nor six wagons alone would in any way suffice, since one wagon today does not carry a weight of 3,000 pounds. In which calculation, however, it is doubtful how that entire quantity of gold, silver, and bronze is attributed to the burden of the Merarites and Gershonites, since Marius acknowledges that to the Merarites belonged only the custody of the boards of the tabernacle, that is, of the atrium, the coverings, the columns, the bases, the pegs, and the ropes; to the Gershonites, the custody of the veils, the coverings of the curtains, the tent, the ropes of the tabernacle, and its utensils, and whatever pertains to the rite of the altar of holocausts was entrusted. But to the Kohathites, with the ark, the table of proposition, the vessels of the sanctuary, the veil of the holy of holies, the altar of incense, and the golden candlestick, which was of only one talent, that is, 3,000 half-ounces or shekels, or 125 pounds, when a pound is taken as 12 ounces, was entrusted.

He (Moses) did not give wagons and oxen to the sons of Kohath, because they served in the sanctuary, that is, in the holy place and in the holy of holies, guarding the vessels pertaining to it, and therefore they were bound to carry those vessels not in wagons, but on their own shoulders because of the holiness and reverence of the vessels.

Latin:

Vers. 3. SEX PLAUSTRA TECTA.

Plaustra oblata sunt ad vasa tabernaculi per desertum vehenda, eademque sex numero, a binis Principibus unum, quum totidem requirerentur ad commodam vectionem: tecta autem erant, ne læderentur vasa ab imbri, aut grandine. Alii addunt etiam, ne conspici a populo possint. Singu- la plaustra a duobus bobus trahebantur, quia Ju- dæi bobus, & equis potius quam asinis utebantur. Ideo quisque Principum unum obtulit bovem. Duo plaustra & quatuor boves dabantur filiis Ger- son, quatuor reliqua plaustra & octo boves filiis Me- rari; quia horum onera graviora erant, utpote co- lumnarum, tabularum, basium, quam istorum, qui- bus aulæa commissa erant. Abulensis existimat filios Merari non potuisse omnia onera sua his quatuor plaustris imponere, sed quædam ab iis por- tari debuisse, sed quia difficilia pleraque portatu fuere, & de filiis solum Caath dicitur, quod onera sua humeris portarint, credendum potius compa- rata fuisse plura plaustra ex reditibus sacris, ut vehi omnia potuerint. Marius onera illa Merarita- rum & Gersonitarum quanta fuerint colligit e c. 38. Exod. ubi recensetur quantitas auri, argenti & æris quod fuit oblatum, auri 29. talenta, & 730. Sicli, argenti 100. talenta 1775. sicli, æris 2070. ta- lenta ac 400. sicli, quæ efficiunt summam librarum 274996. cui oneri neque Meraritæ & Gersonitæ, neque sola sex plaustra ullo modo suffecerint, cum unum plaustrum hodie non vehat 3000. librarum pondus. In quo tamen computo dubium est, quo- modo illa auri, argenti, & æris quantitas univer- sa oneri Meraritarum & Gersonitarum accensea- tur, quum Meraritis agnoscat Marius solum cu- stodiam tabularum tabernaculi, id est, atrii, ve- stium, columnarum, basium, paxillorum & funi- um; Gersonitis custodia velorum, operimentorum cortinarum, tentorii, funium tabernaculi, & utenfilium ejus, & quicquid pertinet ad altaris holocaustorum ritum commendata. Caathitis autem cum arca, mensa propositionis, vasis san- ctuarii, velo sancti sanctorum, altari thymiamitis, candelabrum aureum, quod solum unius talenti, id est, semiunciarum vel siclorum 3000. seu libra- rum 125. fuit, quando libra 12. unciarum sumitur, commissum fuisse.

Filiis Caath non dedit (Moses) plaustra, & bo- ves, quia in sanctuario, h. e. in sancto, & in sancto sanctorum serviebant, vasa eo pertinentia custo- diendo, ideoque vasa illa non in plaustris vehere, sed humeris propriis ferre tenebantur ob vasorum sanctitatem & reverentiam.

## 7:10
Verse 10. FOR THE DEDICATION OF THE ALTAR.

The discourse is about the altar of holocausts, to whose honor this offering of the princes was consecrated. Cornelius observes that this altar, besides the anointing common with the other vessels of the tabernacle, had another special dedication for seven days, namely the daily anointing and sacrifices prescribed in Exodus 29:36-37: whence also the Princes offered their gifts daily in turn and individually for the dedication of the tabernacle, and indeed of the whole, but especially of this altar; but he confuses dedication with consecration.
