That altar had its own consecration, both common and also that special seven-day one; that had already been completed before Aaron began his office: here, however, it is not a matter of the consecration of the altar of holocausts, but of its solemn dedication made through the gifts and victims of the princes. The tabernacle had been consecrated, the altar of holocausts had been consecrated, and all the vessels before the offering of the Princes, as is evident from chapter 40 of Exodus, verse 27, and Leviticus 8, verses 11 and 15, but it was being dedicated, and was being affected with solemn honor in the name of the people, and was being initiated through that offering of the Princes, made for themselves and in the name of the people. If, however, it pleases one to also designate this initiation and inauguration as consecration, from the Vulgate version of verse 84 (where the word for anointing is in the Hebrew), it will nevertheless have to be admitted that the altar of holocausts had already been consecrated before the beginnings of the Aaronic Priesthood. But here, with the numbering of the people instituted, the Princes of the tribes ordered, and the arrangement made, both political and ecclesiastical, regarding the order of the camps and the duties and offices of the Priests and Levites, the altar of holocausts was consecrated with this public pomp for the sake of a more solemn consecration from the voluntary offerings of the Princes: so that it might appear as if anointed anew, or if the anointing of the altar of burnt offering was also performed on this day, and the words of verse 1 speak of that anointing, it must be said that the anointing and sanctification of the altar and its vessels is indeed joined with the anointing and sanctification of the tabernacle, but that both are not restricted to the same day, only this is implied, that the offering of the Princes was not made before the tabernacle and its vessels had been anointed, as also the altar of burnt offerings with its vessels, even though that anointing was done at the erection of the tabernacle in Exodus 40, but this one at this time of the offering of the Princes, and between this very solemn dedication through the spontaneous offerings of the Princes and the erection of the tabernacle, the consecration of Aaron described in Leviticus 8 intervened.

But why was the altar of burnt offering treated with such honor, unless it was a type of the true altar, not of the wood of the cross, but of Christ himself crucified for us, who is both Priest and victim and our altar, as the Apostle testifies in Hebrews 13:10, 'We have an altar,' where Thomas understands Christ himself, from which altar to eat is to perceive the fruit of the passion of Christ, and to be incorporated into him as the head.

ON THE DAY IT WAS ANOINTED.

The word 'day' is again understood as time, according to the custom accepted by the Hebrews. Because during that time, in which the altar was anointed—for which anointing seven days were required, Exod. 29:36, 37—the offering of the Princes was made, which is rightly said, even if the Princes did not offer precisely at that very time and immediately after the completion of the altar's anointing, but because of other intervening matters, such as the first fruits of the Aaronic offering, the sad slaughter of Nadab and Abihu, etc., the solemn dedication was delayed for a few days. Because within the space of one month both the erection of the tabernacle and the consecration of the altar of holocausts and of the High Priest and the rest described in Leviticus were performed and delivered divinely, yet the solemnities of the Passover were also celebrated, as will be said in chapter 10, and at the beginning of the next month the numbering and ordering of the people, the Princes, and the Levites were made, and subsequently the dedication of the tabernacle and the altar of holocausts through the offerings of the Princes. And therefore Bonfrerius acknowledges that 'day' can be taken indeterminately in this place for time, without designating a certain and determined day, so that 'in the day' is the same as 'at that time' or 'during that time,' and thus it seems it must necessarily be taken below in verse 84.

Latin:

Vers. 10. IN DEDICATIONEM ALTARIS.

De altari holocaustorum sermo est, cujus ho- nori haec oblatio principum consecrata fuit. Cor- nelius observat altare hoc praeter unctionem cum aliis tabernaculi vasis communem habuisse aliam specialem dedicationem per septem dies videlicet quotidianam unctionem & sacrificia Exod. 29. v. 36. 37. praescripta: unde & quotidie in taberna- culi & quidem totius, sed maxime altaris hujus de- dicationem obtulerint Principes vicissim & viri- tim sua munera; sed confundit dedicationem cum consecratione. Habebat altare illud & consecratio- nem suam tum communem, tum etiam illam spe- cialem septiduanam; ea jam peracta erat, ante- quam auspicaretur munus suum Aaron: hic vero non de consecratione altaris holocaustorum sed de ejusdem solemni dedicatione agitur per princi- pum munera & victimas facta. Consecratum erat tabernaculum, consecratum & altare holo- causti, ac vasa omnia ante oblationem Principum, ut e cap. 40. Exod. versu 27. Lev. 20. versu 11. 15. constat, sed dedicabatur, & solemni honore no- mine populi afficiebatur, & initiabatur per obla- tionem illam Principum, pro se, ac nomine po- puli factam. Si vero lubeat hanc initiationem & inaugurationem etiam indigitare consecrationem, e Vulgata versione vers. 84. (ubi in Ebraeo habetur verbum unctionis) fateri tamen oportebit, antea altare holocausti jam consecratum fuisse ad auspi- cia Sacerdotii Aaronici. Sed hic instituta nume- ratione populi, ordinatis Principibus tribuum, fa- ctaque dispositione, cum Politica tum Ecclesiasti- stica, quoad castrorum ordinem & Sacerdotum ac Levitarum munia & officia, solemnioris conse- crationis gratia e voluntariis Principum oblationi- bus hac publica pompa consecratum fuisse altare holocausti: ut veluti de novo inunctum videri pos- sit, vel si hac etiam die unctio peracta fuit altaris holocausti, atque de illa unctione verba vers. 1. lo- quantur, dicendum quod conjungatur quidem altaris & vasorum ejus unctio ac sanctificatio, cum unctione & sanctificatione tabernaculi, sed non restringatur utraque ad eundem diem, id so- lum innuatur, non prius factam Principum oblationem, quam uncta fuerint tabernaculum & vasa ejus, ut & altare holocaustorum cum va- sis suis, etsi illa unctio in erectione tabernacu- li Exod. 40. haec vero hoc oblationis Principum tempore facta, & inter hanc dedicationem per- quam solemnem per spontaneas Principum obla- tiones & erectionem tabernaculi, intercesserit Aaronis consecratio Lev. 8. descripta.

Cur vero tanto honore afficiebatur altare holocausti, nisi quod typus fuerit veri altaris, non ligni crucis, sed ipsius Christi pro nobis crucifixi qui & Sacerdos & victima & ara nostra est, teste Apostolo Ebr. 13. v. 10. Habemus altare, ubi Tho- mas ipsum Christum intelligit, de quo altari edere est fructum passionis Christi percipere, & ipsi tan- quam capiti incorporari.

DIE QVA VNCTUM EST.

Intelligitur iterum tempus voce diei, more Ebræis recepto. Quia sub illud tempus, quo un- ctum fuit altare, ad quam unctionem septem dies requirebantur Exod. 29. v. 36. 37. oblatio Princi- pum facta est, quod recte dicitur, etiamsi non præ- cise illo ipso tempore, ac statim post peractam al- taris unctionem Principes obtulerint, sed ob alia intervenientia, utpote primitias oblationis Aaro- nicæ, tristem occisionem Nadab & Abihu &c. ad paucos dies dilata fuerit solemnis dedicatio. Quia intra unius mensis spatium & erectio tabernaculi & consecratio altaris holocausti & Sacerdotis sum- mi & reliqua in Levitico descripta peracta, & tra- dita sunt divinitus, celebrata tamen paschatos etiam solemnia, ut c. 10. dicetur, sub alterius mensis initium numeratio & ordinatio populi, Princi- pum, ac Levitarum facta, ac porro dedicatio ta- bernaculi, & altaris holocausti per oblationes Principum. Ideoque agnoscit Bonfrerius diem posse indeterminate hoc loco accipi pro tempore, non designando certum & determinatum diem, ut in die idem sit, quod eo tempore, vel sub illud tem- pus, atque ita videri necessario sumendum infra versu 84.

## 7:11
Ver. 11.

AND THE LORD SAID TO MOSES] Alone, without the people hearing, which sometimes happened. The voice, however, sounded from the mercy seat between the two Cherubim.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

DIXITQVE DOMINUS AD MOSEM] Solum, non audiente, quod interdum fiebat, populo. Vox autem sonabat e propitiatorio inter duos Cherubinos.

## 7:13
Ver. 13. A SILVER BOWL.

The word קערת denotes a broad and wide dish: it was 130 shekels in weight, which weigh 65 Joachimics. For our Joachimics are ounce-sized, each of which contains two half-ounces of silver or two shekels. A SILVER VIAL having 70 shekels, weighing 35 Joachimics. מזרק a vessel from which, or into which, something is poured, A MORTAR. כף a small curved and concave vessel. The Seventy and Josephus render it θυϊσκην, which some interpret as a censer, others as a mortar, because θυϊα is a mortar in which things are ground: some explain the Hebrew word as a spoon. TEN GOLDEN SHEKELS, that is, according to Bonfrerius, five ounces of gold, if indeed the gold shekels were of the same weight as the silver ones, whence ten gold shekels will equal 120. Shekels of silver, or 60 ounces, if a twelvefold proportion is maintained between silver and gold, or rather 100 silver shekels; for a tenfold proportion between gold and silver seems most ancient. In which, however, Lorinus does not agree with Bonfrerius, assuming a twelvefold proportion. He says, ad h. l., the gold and silver shekel were of equal weight, but a single gold one was equal to twelve silver ones. Chytreus estimates it at 45 Rhenish gold coins: for 9 Rhenish gold coins weigh two half-ounces, or two shekels. 72 Rhenish gold coins make a mark of pure gold. He thinks these vessels were given to the temple for the sake of the sacred feasts, which were celebrated by those offering victims at the tabernacle. Another cause is hinted at in the text, because the bowl and the silver vial were vessels full of fine flour mingled with oil for a sacrifice when they were offered, but the golden mortar was full of incense, whence the former were used for storing the fine flour mingled with oil for the use of the altar of holocausts. To Bonfrerius it is likely that the bowls had this purpose, that in them the cooked shoulder and the libations of flour with oil were offered, but the vials, that wine might be poured from them on the altar. The golden mortars, however, were for the use of the sanctuary itself, all of whose vessels and instruments had to be of gold, which the incense itself also sufficiently indicates; with which they were full, which was offered only in the sanctuary at the altar of incense.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ACETABULUM ARGENTEUM.

Vox קערת patinam latam & amplam notat: Pondo fuit 130. Siclorum, qui pendunt 65. Joachi- micos. Nostri enim Joachimici sunt unciales, qui singuli duas argenti semiuncias seu duos siclos continent. PHIALAM argenteam habentem 70. Siclos, pondere 35. Joachimicorum. מזרק vas ex quo, vel in quod aliquid funditur MORTARIO- LUM. כף parvum vas curvum & concavum. Se- ptuaginta & Josephus θυϊσκην reddunt, quod non- nulli thuribulum, alii mortariolum, quia θυϊα mor- tarium est, in quo res conteruntur, interpretan- tur: nonnulli Ebr. per cochleare exponunt. DE- CEM SICLIS AUREIS, hoc est, juxta Bonfre- rium, auri unciis quinque, si tamen auri sicli ejus- dem ponderis fuerint, atque argenti, unde decem auri sicli æquabunt 120. Siclos argenti, seu uncias 60. si duodecupla servetur, inter argentum & au- rum proportio, vel potius 100. argenti Siclos; nam decupla inter aurum & argentum proportio videtur antiquissima. In quo vero non consonat Bonfrerio Lorinus, duodecuplam proportionem assumens. Erat, inquit ad h. l. Siclus aureus & argenteus æqualis ponderis, sed argenteis duodecim par erat aureus unicus. Chytreus æstimat 45. aureis Rhenensibus: nam 9. aurei Rhenenses duas se- miuncias, seu duos siclos pendunt. 72. aurei Rhe- nenses marcam auri puri. Donata autem hæc va- sa templo putat propter convivia sacra: quæ ab im- molantibus victimas ad tabernaculum celebraban- tur. Alia causa in textu innuitur, quia acetabulum & phiala argentea vasa plena erant simila conspersa oleo in sacrificium, quum offerrentur, mortariolum vero aureum plenum erat incenso, unde illa ad similam oleo conspersam reponendam adhibita in usum altaris holocausti. Bonfrerio verisimile est ace- tabula hunc finem habuisse, ut in illis armus coctus & libamina e farina cum oleo offerrentur, phialas vero, ut ex iis vinum in altari libaretur. Mortariola vero aurea in usum ipsius sanctuarii cedebant, cujus omnia vasa & instrumenta aurea esse debue- runt, quod ipsum etiam satis indicat incensum; quo plena fuerunt, quod tantummodo in sanctua- rio ad altare incensi offerebatur.

## 7:16
ver. 16. AN OX FROM THE HERD.

Cyril hands down the mystical meaning of these offerings and all the gifts, from whom Lorinus repeats it on page 247. Mystically, says Cyril of Alexandria, l. 10 de adorat., he declares the victims for a holocaust to be of Christ, who is all holy and full of the odor of sweetness; others, which were not entirely burned, to be of us, because no one is clean from filth, no one understands the sins to which he is obviously liable; the fine flour in the bowl or dish and in the vial to be of the same Christ, who is the bread of life, and is signified as in food and drink; because the dish pertains to food, the vial to drink: he said, however, that those who would not eat the flesh of the son of man and drink his blood would not have life in themselves; the oil, with which the fine flour was mingled, to be of the same one, who is sung as anointed with the oil of gladness above his fellows: the mortar, that is, a kind of censer in the likeness of a mortar, to be of the same one, who is a good odor, and a censer, not having an odor from without, as we do, who have only a certain participation of holiness; but from himself and his own nature, and in a way that is above the world and every creature, and fills the whole world, since he is truly God, and in his own nature has received the odor of the Father's knowledge: the ox, the ram, the lamb, the kid from the goats, to be still of the same one, who is called an ox or a calf because of his supreme strength; and because that animal is the most excellent of tame and clean animals, and excels in the size of its body; the ram because of perfection, the lamb because of innocence; the kid because he was slain for sinners. He adds concerning the oxen of the wagons, that the Church rests in Christ, and he carries us; but he himself does not allow the sacred race of men to succumb to labors that are beyond their strength. Then the sacrifices of peace offerings, which were offered by the princes, which in a certain way they consecrated for themselves and that as a tabernacle, and offered to God for a sweet-smelling savor, and they were two heifers (for so he reads), five rams, he-goats, and as many lambs, he refers to us ourselves, who are spiritually sacrificed; but we are considered heifers, in respect of Christ the heifer, on account of our imperfection, just as the female sex is more imperfect and subject to the male; for who shall be equal to God among the sons of God? But let the two denote the Church brought together from two peoples: in the five rams, lambs, and he-goats he attends to the multitude of believers, which happened in the fifth time, as it were, at which time He arrived who said: When I shall be lifted up from the earth, I will draw all (so he also reads) to myself, but in such a way that by the rams is designated the perfection of the prudence of believers, and the completion of the spiritual age by which we grow in Christ; by the lambs, simplicity and innocence, so that they may not be children in sense, but infants in malice, yet perfect in sense; by the he-goats for sin, that we always have need of expiation and the remission of sins, and ought to say, forgive us our debts, since there is no time in which it is not necessary for those who are certainly of perfect prudence, and not ignorant of human weakness, to cry out, who understands his faults, and cleanse me from my secret ones. Now indeed he considers in the offering of the silver bowl, or dish and vial, with fine flour moistened or sprinkled with oil, since silver is a mark of splendor: of life fine flour, as that from which bread exists, which preserves life, oil of gladness ought to be offered by us to GOD, who is above all things; in the splendor of life, gladness, through the hope which is in Christ, that we may be rejoicing in hope, and our life hidden with Christ in GOD, so that when our life should appear, then we also may appear with him in glory. By the golden mortar full of incense, he wishes to signify the beauty of the Saints, and that fragrance of holiness as if in sacred vessels, which is then offered to GOD as a certain gift, truly most fragrant. He repeats next, through the oxen of the wagons, the two peoples figured as joined together patiently and bravely under the one yoke of the Savior; and since the ox is most tolerant of labor and most robust, he indicates the worshippers of piety, and those who sustain Christ as if a yoke imposed upon them, of which the tabernacle is a figure, and the body the Church: the vessels of the holy man, as Paul was surnamed a vessel: by the ram and the lamb, the older and the more recent people, brought to spiritual dedication; and as in the oxen, tolerance and fortitude are designated: so in the sheep, that abundance along with meekness of those who have been justified through faith in Christ, and according to the precept of Christ give to everyone who asks, etc. and according to another of Paul, they do not litigate, but are all meek, etc. He says that kids are added, so that even the justified may know that they are in need of the purgation of penance and the forgetting of offenses; since if the Lord should observe iniquities, there is no one who can sustain it: and he who says, or proposes to confess injustice against himself, iniquity is remitted to him: and the former says his iniquities, who wishes to be justified. Exactly the same things are read in Procopius, who in his own manner transcribed Cyril of Alexandria, with his name left silent. But what both have concerning the fifth time, in which Christ came, agrees with the parable of those called to the vineyard in the morning, at the third, sixth, ninth, and eleventh hour.

Latin:

vers. 16. BOVEM DE ARMENTO.

Significationem mysticam harum oblationum & munerum omnium tradit Cyrillus, ex quo repe- tit eam Lorinus pag. 247. Mystice, inquit, Cyrillus Alexandr. l. 10. de adorat. declarat victimas in ho- locaustum de Christo, qui totus sanctus est, ac odore suavitatis plenus facerque : alias, quæ non totæ crema- bantur, de nobis, quia nemo mundus a sorde, deli- cta nullus intelligit, quibus videlicet obnoxius est; similam in acetabulo, sive catino & in phiala de eo- dem Christo, qui est panis vitæ, significaturque tanquam in cibo & potu; quia catinus ad cibum per- tinet, phiala ad potum : dixit vero vitam non habi- turos in semetipsis, qui carnem filii hominis non manducarent, & sanguinem ejus non biberent: ole- um, quo simila conspersa erat, de eodem, qui oleo lætitiæ unctus canitur præ participibus suis : morta- riolum, id est, speciem thuribuli ad similitudinem mortarii, de eodem, qui est bonus odor, ac thuri- bulum, non extrinsecus odorem habens, ut nos, qui participationem tantum quandam habemus sancti- tatis; sed ex se suaque natura, ac modo, qui supra mundum, creaturamque omnem est, & omnem re- plet orbem terrarum, cum sit revera Deus, & in sua ipsius natura paternæ cognitionis odorem acce- perit: bovem, arietem, agnum, hædum e capris, adhuc de eodem, qui bos sive vitulus dicatur, pro- pter summam firmitatem; & quia illud animal mansuetorum, mundorumque animantium præstan- tissimum est, magnitudineque corporis excellens; aries ob perfectionem, agnus propter innocentiam; hædus, quia pro peccatoribus occisus est. Addit de bobus plaustrorum, quod in Christo conquiescat Eccle- sia, & illa nos ferat; ipse vero laboribus, qui su- pra vires sunt, sacrum hominum genus succumbe- re non sinat. Deinde Sacrificia pacificorum, quæ a Principibus offerebantur, quæ quodammodo pro seipsis, ac illa tanquam tabernaculo consecrabant, offerebantque Deo in odorem suavitatis, & erant vitulæ duæ (sic enim legit) arietes quinque, hirci, & agni totidem, refert ad nos ipsos, qui spirituali- ter sacrificemur; vitulæ autem censeamur, respe- ctu Christi vituli, ob imperfectionem nostram, sicut sexus fœmineus imperfectior est, masculo- que subjectus; quis enim æquabitur Deo in filiis Dei? Duæ vero denotent ex duobus populis confla- tam Ecclesiam : in quinis arietibus, agnis, hircis attendit multitudinem credentium, quæ quinto qua- si tempore contigit, quo tempore ille advenit, qui dixit: Cum exaltatus fuero a terra, omnes traham (sic quoque legit) ad meipsum, sed ita ut per arie- tes designetur credentium prudentiæ perfectio, & spiritualis ætatis, qua in Christo crescimus, abso- lutio; per agnos simplicitas & innocentia, ut non sint pueri sensibus, sed malitia parvuli, sensibus au- tem perfecti; per hircos pro peccato, semper nos expiatione ac remissione peccatorum opus habere, dicereque debere, dimitte nobis debita nostra, cum nullum sit tempus, quo non iis certe, qui perfecta sunt prudentia, humanæq; imbecillitatis haud igna- ri, clamare necesse sit, delicta quis intelligit, & ab occultis meis munda me. Jam vero considerat in oblatione argentei acetabuli, sive catini & phialæ, cum simila oleo madefacta sive conspersa, quoniam nota splendoris est argentum : vitæ simila, utpote ex qua panis existat, qui vitam con- servat, oleum hilaritatis offerri debere a nobis DEO, qui est super omnia; in splendore vitæ hilaritatem, per spem, quæ in Christo est, ut simus spe gauden- tes, vitamque nostram absconditam cum Christo in DEO, ut cum appareret vita nostra, tunc & nos appareamus cum ipso in gloria. Aureo mortario- lo incensi pleno significari vult Sanctorum pul- chritudinem, & illam tanquam in vasis sacris suaveolentiam sanctitatis, quæ deinde offertur DEO velut donum quoddam sane fragrantissi- mum. Repetit deinceps per boves plaustrorum figuratos populos duos sub uno Salvatoris jugo to- leranter, fortiterque conjunctos; cumque bos laboris tolerantissimus sit, & robustissimus, in- dicari pietatis cultores, quique Christum, quasi jugum sibi impositum sustineant, cujus figura tabernaculum, & corpus Ecclesia: vasa viri san- cti, ut Paulus vas cognominatus: per arietem & agnum, populum antiquiorem & recentiorem, ad spiritualem dedicationem adductos; & ut in bobus tolerantia fortitudoque designatur: sic in ovibus illa cum mansuetudine ubertas eo- rum, qui per fidem in Christum justificati sunt, & juxta Christi præceptum omni petenti tri- buunt, &c. secundum vero aliud Pauli, non li- tigant, sed mansueti sunt omnes, &c. Adjungi dicit hædos, ut sciant etiam justificati, purgatione se pænitentiæ, offensarumque oblivione indigere; quo- niam si Dominus iniquitates observaverit, non est qui sustineat: & qui dicit, seu proponit confiteri ad- versus se injustitiam, remittitur ei iniquitas: & prior dicit iniquitates suas, qui vult justificari. Ea- dem prorsus leguntur apud Procopium, qui suo more Cyrillum Alexandrinum, tacito ejus nomi- ne transcripsit. Quod vero uterque habet de quinto tempore, quo Christus venit, congruit pa- rabolæ vocatorum ad vineam mane, hora tertia, sexta, nona, undecima.

## 7:18
Vers. 18. NATHANAEL OFFERED.

This man and those following offered similar things, and are reported to have offered them in exactly the same words, whence in the Hebrew no points are added to their offerings, because they are already established by the offering of the first Prince. But why Moses repeated everything in the same number of words for each individual Prince, the Interpreters give these causes; partly because that is the custom of repeating among the Orientals, Muscovites, and other nations, and partly because by that repetition he wished not only to indicate the total identity of the gifts, but also to show equal honor to each, and to testify how greatly God is delighted by offerings, and how acceptable he holds them. Then because some mystery underlies it, about which Rupert and from him Lyranus: All offered equal things, and the pen of Moses is not fatigued to repeat the same things so many times in each with the same words, with almost the same Syllables. What does this mean (since indeed the quantity of things contained under the different tribes is so disparate) unless it is because the letter of the law covers a great mystery in this place as well? namely, concerning the twelve Apostles, which will be weighed afterwards. Such a diligent and accurate enumeration, and the expression of each by their own proper names, insinuates how acceptable the offering was to God.

vers. 84. ON THE DAY THAT IT WAS CONSECRATED.

It was said in note 1 and 10 that day is taken for time. Bonfrerius agrees, although he also observes that the consecration can be understood not of the anointing itself but of the dedication described here: Day is taken for time, not restrictively, for the day on which the consecration was done. And indeed here it is absolutely necessary to be taken in that way, so that this day may comprehend that whole period of twelve days, in which that offering was made; or finally, by the name of dedication and consecration, one can understand not the anointing and sanctification of the altar itself, but the consecration which was done by the very immolation and burning of the victims.

vers. 89. AND WHEN MOSES ENTERED.

Access therefore was always open to Moses to the Holy of Holies in doubtful cases, even though it was permitted to the High Priest to enter only once every year on the day of atonement, to figure the entry of Christ made once into the Sanctuary of heaven. Cajetan understands the voice heard from the propitiatory as only an intelligible voice, whom Antonius Fonseca rightly refutes from the circumstances of the locution, namely that the voice was heard from above the ark, and also from the midst of the Cherubim, and therefore an express utterance of a voice is to be understood. But Tostatus is inept when he denies that a voice could be formed by GOD, because he cannot act through succession, since succession in the air does not argue succession in God. But GOD spoke to Moses not always from the propitiatory, but sometimes also at the door of the tabernacle, near the altar of holocausts Exod. 29, 42. However, Cyril in book X on adoration does not badly fix the beginning of that locution from the propitiatory here, because with the sacrifice already brought by the princes of each tribe, which was offered as if for all, GOD began to speak for the first time in the tabernacle with Moses, the interpreter of sacred things, to which it is no obstacle that in v. 4 and 5 he received answers from the Lord: for these could have been given at the door of the tabernacle. The same Cyril also observes, allegorically, and after him Procopius, that with the tabernacle already finished, and that true sanctification, that is, the Church, manifested to the world, then at last the voice of GOD sounded to us; for he has spoken to us in the Son, whom we say is the propitiation for our sins according to the Scriptures. They say the voice was heard from above the Cherubim, because GOD is superior to every creature and beyond it, and by essential and inherent excellence surpasses all created things, and when he was sending the true propitiatory, that is, the Son, to us, he was saying those voices that were superior and uttered by the Father: The words which I speak are not mine, but his who sent me.

Latin:

Vers. 18. OBTULIT NATHANAEL.

Hic & sequentes similia obtulere, & obtu- lisse referuntur iisdem prorsus verbis, unde in E- bræo in eorum oblationibus nulla adjiciuntur puncta, quod ea e primi Principis oblatione jam constent. Cur autem Moses totidem verbis omnia penes sin- gulos Principes repetierit, Interpp. has causas red- dunt; tum quod ille repetendi mos sit apud Orien- tales, Moscovitas & alias gentes, tum quod repe- titione illa non modo identitatem omnimodam munerum indicare, sed singulis etiam parilem ho- norem exhibere voluerit, ac testari quantopere delectetur Deus oblationibus, & quam gratas eas habeat. Tum quod mysterium aliquod subsit, de quo Rupertus & ex eo Lyranus: Æqualia ob- tulerunt universi, & non fatigatur calamus Moysi toties eadem repetere in singulis eisdem verbis, eisdem pene Syllabis. Quid hoc sibi vult (cum scilicet tam sit dispar quantitas contentorum sub diversis tribubus) nisi quia mysterium grande isto quoque loco legis litera subtegit? nempe de duodecim Apostolis, quod postea perpendetur. Tam diligens, & accurata enumera- tio, atque singulorum per nomina propria expressio, in- sinuat, quam fuerit Deo grata oblatio.

vers. 84. IN DIE QUA CONSECRATUM EST.

Dictum est adv. 1. & 10. diem pro tempore ac- cipi. Consonat Bonfrerius, etsi etiam observet consecrationem non de ipsa unctione sed dedicatio- ne hic descripta intelligi posse: Dies pro tempore sumtur, non restricte, pro die quo facta est consecra- tio. Et vero hic omnino necesse est eo modo sumi, u- dies hic comprehendat totum illud tempus duodecim dierum, quo oblatio illa facta est; vel denique nomi- ne dedicationis & consecrationis intelligi potest non unctio ipsa & sanctificatio altaris, sed conse- cratio, quæ facta est ipsa hostiarum immolatione & crematione.

vers. 89. CUMQUE INGREDERETUR MOSES.

Patuit ergo Mosi semper accessus ad Sanctum Sanctorum in causis dubiis, etsi summo Sacerdoti se- mel tantum quotannis in die expiationis introire licuerit, ad figurandum ingressum Christi semel factum in cœli Sanctuarium. Cajetanus vocem auditam de propitiatorio de sola intelligibili voce in- telligit, quem vero recte refellit Antonius Fonse- ca e circumstantiis locutionis, utpote quod de- super arcam, item ex medio Cherubinorum vox au- dita sit, ideoque intelligatur expressa vocis loquutio. Ineptus autem est Tostatus, cum negat, vocem for- mari potuisse a DEO, quod agere non possit per suc- cessionem, siquidem successio in aere non arguat successionem in Deo. Loquutus autem DEUS est Mosi non semper de propitiatorio, sed quan- doque etiam ad ostium tabernaculi, penes altare holocaustorum Exod. 29, 42. Illius tamen loquutio- nis de propitiatorio initium hic non male figit Cyrillus X. de adorat. quod allato jam a singulis tri- buum principibus sacrificio, quod tanquam pro omni- bus offerebatur, DEUS primum in tabernaculo cum Mose sacrorum interprete colloqui cœperit, cui non obstat, quod v. 4. & 5. responsa acceperit a Do- mino: hæc enim ad ostium tabernaculi dari potue- re. Observat etiam idem Cyrillus, allegorice, postque ipsum Procopius, quod consummato jam tabernaculo, & vera illa sanctificatione, id est, Ec- clesia, mundo manifestata tum deniq; vox DEI, ac no- bis insonuit; locutus est enim nobis in Filio, quem propitiationem esse dicimus pro peccatis nostris secun- dum Scripturas. Desuper Cherubim vocem audi- tam dicunt, quia superior omni creatura, atque ulte- rior est DEUS, & essentiali ac insita excellentia omnibus rebus conditis præstat, & cum verum pro- pitiatorium, id est, Filium ad nos transmitteret, su- peras illas & editas a Patre voces dicebat: Verba quæ ego loquor non sunt mea, sed ejus, qui mi- sit me.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII. The lampstand, and the lamps as also the age, and the consecration of the Levites. Ver. 1. AND THE LORD SPOKE UNTO MOSES.

The position of the lampstand is described, and the consecration of the Levites; Marius, Cornelius, Lorinus, and others think that both are related here by hysteron proteron or recapitulation: Because the lampstand had already been placed when the tabernacle was erected, Exod. last. But the Levites were consecrated to the Lord when they were chosen in place of the firstborn of the Israelites, Num. III. But these things do not prove a hysteron proteron. For although Moses had already placed the lampstand at the erection of the tabernacle, he had not yet received the perpetual law from GOD to be delivered to Aaron: which is done here. Moreover, the substitution of the Levites in the place of the firstborn was indeed related above. But the consecration was not yet performed there, the rites of which are prescribed here. And indeed if all those numberings of the people and of the Levites in chapters 1, 2, and 3 had been made at the same time, this would seem to be clear, since the numbering of the people and of the warriors in chapter 1 was made on the first day of the second month; for if And then the Levites were numbered, and were offered to God for the firstborn, since this numbering, and the substitution in place of the firstborn, ought to have preceded their consecration, it follows that they could not have been consecrated before the second month, and thus many days after the completion of the consecration of the Priests, as Bonfrerius holds here.

But the Lord is said to have spoken to Moses, not to Aaron at the same time, even though that matter concerned the latter, because a command was to be given concerning a thing which Aaron was to execute, and to receive it from his brother the lawgiver, as Lorinus notes. Therefore, in such matters, the Ecclesiastical Ministry depends on Magistrates and Princes, and consequently the supreme Roman Pontiff with his clergy ought not to withdraw himself from the authority and power of these.

WHEN YOU SHALL PLACE THE SEVEN LAMPS. The Hebrew has it thus: when you shall light or set up the lamps, they shall shine against the face of the candlestick. But in the Vulgate many things are added, to wit: when you shall place the seven lamps, let the candlestick be set up on the south side. Command this, therefore, that the lamps may look toward the North, over against the table of the loaves of proposition. Which are brought here from Exod. ch. 25, 37; ch. 26, 35; ch. 40, 22. To wit, seven lamps were to be placed upon the seven-branched candlestick, which were to be lit, and the candlestick was to be placed on the South side of the tabernacle, so that it might cast its light toward the opposite North side, in which was the table of the loaves of proposition, in order to illuminate it, because this table was as it were a divine banquet, which therefore was to be illuminated, since the tabernacle, covered on all sides with curtains, was dark, even though it admitted some light during the day through the front veil, which was folded back and raised to some extent, and which served in place of a door. Concerning the meaning, Cyril and Procopius say thus: that the golden candlestick was a figure of Christ, whose divine nature is compared to gold: beaten work, because he is beautiful in form above the sons of men: the branches rising from either side to an equal height signify his manifold efficiency, so that nevertheless nothing in him is adventitious, just as the spheres, branches, and lilies in the candlestick were of the candlestick itself, and the whole was beaten work of pure gold, that is, he is wholly GOD on all sides, not sanctified in the same way as those things which have been created, nor as the Angels, however much they are adorned with grace and endowed with the gift of the Spirit: seven lamps on account of the various gifts of grace, of which the Apostle speaks, which Christ, being most perfect by his own nature, did not have by measure, but from his fullness others have received. Finally, as regards the present passage, he explains the seven lamps turned toward the face of the candlestick, and which cast light upon those looking at them, because that divine and spiritual light does not illuminate those who are behind, and in a certain way turned away from GOD; but those who have been brought into his sight through sanctification, and now turn their faces toward him with faith, liberty, and the noble honesty of living rightly: for just as those who persist in wickedness and stubbornness are to be abhorred and execrated, so are those who are obedient and tractable, and placed in the sight of GOD, dear.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII. Candelabrum, & lucernæ ut & ætas, & conse- cratio Levitarum. Vers. 1. LOCUTUSQUE EST DOMINUS AD MOSEN.

DEscribitur situs candelabri, & consecratio Le- vitarum; utrumque per ὑστερολογίαν vel ἀνα- κεφαλαίωσιν hic tradi putant Marius, Cornelius, Lorinus, alii: Eo quod candelabrum positum jam fue- rit, quando erectum fuit tabernaculum Exod. ult. Levitæ autem consecrati sint Domino, quando electi sunt pro primogenitis Israelitarum Num. III. Sed hæc non evincunt ὑστερολογίαν. Etsi enim Mo- ses jam posuerit tabernaculum in erectione ta- bernaculi, nondum tamen legem a DEO perpe- tuam acceperat Aaroni tradendam: quod hic fit. Levitarum autem surrogatio in locum primoge- nitorum assumtio supra quidem tradita. Con- secratio autem ibi nondum facta, cujus ritus hic præscribuntur. Et vero si omnes illæ populi & Levitarum dinumerationes capp. 1. 2. 3. factæ es- sent eodem tempore, videretur hoc esse perspi- cuum, cum populi & bellatorum dinumeratio cap. 1. facta sit primo die mensis secundi; nam si & tunc dinumerati Levitæ, Deoque pro primoge- nitis fuerunt oblati, cum hæc dinumeratio, & in locum primogenitorum substitutio debuerit eo- rum consecrationem antecedere, sequitur, non potuisse consecrari ante mensem secundum, atque adeo multis diebus post completam Sacerdotum consecrationem, ut hic habet Bonfrerius.

Loquutus autem ad Mosen dicitur Domi- nus, non simul ad Aaronem, etsi res ea hunc con- cerneret, quia præceptum erat dandum de re, quam exequi debebat Aaron, & id accipere a fra- tre legislatore, ut notat Lorinus. Dependet er- go in talibus Ministerium Ecclesiasticum a Ma- gistratibus & Principibus, ac proinde horum im- perio ac potestati se subducere non debebat sum- mus Pontifex Romanus cum clero suo.

CUM POSUERIS SEPTEM LUCERNAS. Hebræa ita habent, cum accendere facies vel compones lucernas contra faciem candelabri luce- bunt. In Vulgata vero multa adduntur h. m. cum posueris septem lucernas, candelabrum in australi parte erigatur. Hoc igitur præcipe, ut lucernæ con- tra Boream e regione respiciant ad mensam panum propositionis. Quæ e cap. 25, 37. cap. 26, 35. cap. 40. 22. Exod. huc traducta. Sc. candelabro septifi- do imponendæ erant septem lucernæ, quæ accen- dendæ erant, & collocandum candelabrum in Au- strali parte tabernaculi, ita ut lumen suum ejacula- retur in partem Borealem oppositam, in qua erat mensa panum propositionis, ut eam illuminaret, quia mensa hæc erat quasi convivii divini, quæ proinde illuminanda, cum tabernaculum undique cortinis tectum tenebrosum fuerit, etsi per ve- lum anterius reflexum, & aliquo usque eleva- tum, quod loco ostii erat, lumen aliquod inter- diu admiserit. De significatione Cyrillus, & Procopius ita, candelabrum aureum figuram fuisse Christi, cujus natura divina auro comparatur: tor- natile, quia speciosus forma præ filiis hominum: ca- lamos ex latere utroque ad parem altitudinem exur- gentes multiplicem efficientiam ipsius, ita ut nihil tamen in eo adscititium sit, sicut sphærulæ, calami, lilia in candelabro essent ipsi candelabro, totumque torna- tile ex auro puro, id est, totus undique DEUS, non perinde atque ea quæ orta sunt, sanctificatus, neque ut Angeli, quantumvis gratia decorati, & Spiritus munere præditi: septem lucernas propter varia gratiæ dona, de quibus Apostolus, quæ Christus sua- pte natura perfectissimus, non ad mensuram habuit, sed de plenitudine ejus alii acceperunt. Denique quod ad præsentem facit locum, septem lucernas ad fa- ciem candelabri versas, & quæ lumen in aspicientes immittant, explicat, quia non qui a tergo sunt, ac quodammodo a DEO aversi, divinum illud & spi- rituale lumen illustrat; sed eos, qui in illius conspe- ctum per sanctificationem perducti sunt, ac jam fi- dem, libertatem, & honestatem recte vivendi præcla- ram, ora illi obvertunt: ut enim abominandi sunt & execrandi, qui in nequitia & pervicacia versantur, ita chari & in DEI conspectu positi obtemperantes, atque tractabiles.

## 8:4
ver. 4. NOW THIS WAS THE WORKMANSHIP OF THE CANDLESTICK.

From Exod. 25, 31; ch. 37, 27.

Latin:

vers. 4. HÆC AUTEM ERAT FACTURA CAN- DELABRI.

De Exod. 25, 31. c. 37, 27.

## 8:7
Ver. 7. LET THEM BE SPRINKLED WITH THE WATER OF LUSTRATION.

Which, to wit, is mixed with the ashes of the red heifer, of which ch. 19. This was the rite of the consecration of the Levites. First, Aaron sprinkled them with the water of lustration, because no one can be consecrated to GOD without the cleansing of the blood of Christ, which was figured there in Exod. 9, 13. Marius confirms the use of holy water from this, but this is to Judaize, and to bring back those corporal and shadowy ceremonies which ceased in the New Testament. (2.) The shaving of the hair took place, both because all superfluities of earthly things are to be rejected, and because depraved concupiscences are to be removed through spiritual filth, dead and foul-smelling works, as Theodoret says, because hair represents something dead and does not feel pain: whence Greg. M. lib. V. moral. cap. 23: It is necessary for Levites to shave the hair of the flesh, because he who is assumed into divine services ought to appear clean before the eyes of GOD from all thoughts of the flesh. Thirdly, they washed their garments, that is, the stains of their former life. Fourthly, they offered two oxen, to indicate that they offered themselves to the strong and constant labor of the divine ministry. Fifthly, they were to be presented before GOD, because they were consecrated to his service. Sixthly, the Israelites laid their hands upon them, the Princes, to wit, in the name of the people, because they were offering them to GOD in place of their firstborn. Seventhly, Aaron offered the Levites by the rite of waving, that is, by shaking and slightly lifting them toward the four quarters of the world in the manner of a cross, so that it might be indicated that they were offered to GOD, who is the Lord of the whole world. Eighthly, the Levites laid their hands upon their two oxen, as if they were laying their sins upon them, so that Aaron might then sacrifice them for them. What is said by Moses, you shall purify them; that is to be understood as done by Aaron, already consecrated as Priest. For what one does through another, he is considered to have done himself. But it seems that Aaron consecrated only those who were to serve in the tabernacle at this time by the act itself. For he could not have consecrated three thousand Levites man by man to the Lord with that rite, as Cornelius notes, or it must be said with Leonhard Marius, that Aaron performed the waving only for certain primary ones, yet in such a way that when he turned or lifted these, others also turned themselves of their own accord, and leaped from the ground with them, unless it is rather to be believed that this word is taken here in a more general sense, as the Vulgate rendered it: And he shall offer. But Abulensis wrongly determined that those thus consecrated were not admitted in the desert thereafter: whom Marius therefore refutes from this command.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ASPERGANTUR AQUA LUSTRATIO- NIS.

Quæ sc. mista est cineribus vaccæ rufæ, de quibus cap. 19. Hic fuit ritus consecrationis Le- vitarum. Primo aspersit eos Aaron aqua lustra- tionis, quia consecrari nemo potest DEO sine mundatione sanguinis Christi, quæ ibi figurata Exod. 9, 13. Marius usum aquæ benedictæ hinc confirmat, sed hoc est Judaizare, ac corpora- les & umbratiles istas ceremonias, quæ cessa- runt in Nov. Testam. reducere. (2.) Pilorum rasio fiebat, tum quod rejiciendæ sint omnes super- fluitates rerum terrenarum, tum quod tollendæ pravæ concupiscentiæ per sordes spirituales, mor- tua & male olentia opera, ut ait Theodoret. quia pili mortuum quid repræsentant nec dolorem sentiunt: unde Gregor. M. lib. V. moral. cap. 23. Oportet Levitas pilos carnis radere, quia is, qui in obsequiis divinis assumitur, debet ante DEI oculos a cunctis carnis cogitationibus mundus appa- rere. Tertio laverunt vestes suas, id est, prio- ris vitæ maculas. Quarto obtulerunt duos bo- ves, ut indicarent, quod seipsos offerrent ad fortem & constantem laborem divini ministerii. Quinto sistendi erant coram DEO, quod servi- tio ejus consecrati sint. Sexto Israëlitæ impo- fuerunt illis manus suas, Principes sc. nomine populi, quia illos primogenitorum suorum loco, DEO offerebant. Septimo Aaron ritu tenuphæ obtulit Levitas, hoc est, agitando & modice ele- vando eos ad quatuor plagas mundi in modum cru- cis, ut indicaretur eos offerri DEO, qui to- tius mundi est Dominus. Octavo Levitæ bo- bus suis duobus imponebant manus suas, quasi imponerent ipsis peccata sua, ut Aaron deinde eos pro ipsis immolaret. Quod a Mose dici- tur purificabis eos; id intelligendum per Aaro- nem factum, jam in Sacerdotem consecratum. Nam quod quis per alium facit, ipse fecisse censetur. Videtur autem illos solum consecras- se Aaron, qui ipso actu erant tabernaculo de- servituri hoc tempore. Non enim potuisset tria millia Levitarum viritim isto ritu Domino consecrare, ut notat Cornelius, vel dicendum cum Leonhard. Mario, quod tenupha Aaron pri- mariis solum quibusdam fecerit, ita tamen, ut cum ille hos verteret vel elevaret, etiam alii se verterent sponte sua, & a terra exilirent cum ipsis, nisi potius credendum sit hanc vo- cem generaliori significatione hic accipi, uti Vulgatus reddidit: Et offeret. Male autem Abu- lensis statuit, in deserto deinceps non admissos ita consecratos: quem ideo ex hoc mandato refellit Marius.

## 8:9
vers. 9. THE WHOLE MULTITUDE HAVING BEEN CONVOKED.

For the consecration and inauguration of the Levites, the whole multitude was to be convoked, and the children of Israel laid their hands upon them, so that by their χειροθεσίᾳ they might approve and ratify their office. For although their election and calling was made immediately by GOD himself, who set them apart for himself and commanded them to be set apart immediately, yet so that the consent and ratification of the people, for whose sake they were deputed to this ministry, might be added, they testified to the same by public χειροτονίᾳ. Therefore, the Jesuit Marius wrongly concludes from the immediate calling of the Priests and Levites that the suffrage of the people is nothing in Ecclesiastical offices, which right of electing and calling the Pope and Bishops seize for themselves alone in the Papacy. But from an immediate calling to a mediate the consequence is invalid. If the Roman Pontiff were to show that he was commanded immediately by GOD to set apart these or those, and to call them to sacred offices, we would not object. Furthermore, it is not evident from this example how the Magistrate ought to be excluded, since Marius himself admits that Moses held the primary role here, by whom the multitude was also to be convened: nor should the people be barred, but convened for the induction of the Levites into sacred office, and indeed testify to their consent by solemn χειροτονίᾳ. What of the fact that it is established from Cyprian and other Fathers that the votes of the citizens, the testimonies of the peoples, and the judgments of the honorable were expected, as Leo the Roman Pontiff himself holds in Ep. XXCVII, and Marius himself admits that the people were admitted to a share of the suffrage at some times and places: which B. Luther rightly proved from Cyprian concerning the power of the Pope. The words of the holy martyr are as follows: GOD commands that a Priest be constituted before the WHOLE Synagogue, that is, He institutes and shows that priestly ordinations OUGHT NOT TO BE DONE EXCEPT under the awareness of the assisting people, so that in the presence of the laity, either the crimes of the wicked may be detected or the merits of the good may be proclaimed. These things imply not only presence, but the right of suffrage and of voting, since they can be repelled by crimes and admitted by approved merits, as the conscience of the people shall dictate, which St. Cyprian deduces from divine tradition and Apostolic observation. For which reason it is diligently to be observed and held, according to divine tradition and Apostolic observation, which is also held among us and in almost ALL PROVINCES, that for ordinations to be duly celebrated, the nearest Bishops of the same Province should convene to that laity to whom the prelate is being ordained, and the Bishop is chosen in the presence of the laity, who knows most fully the life of each one and has perceived the act of each one concerning his conduct. What is achieved by this reasoning from the knowledge of the laity, except that the votes of the laity should also be heard, not excluded? Marius adds, certain passages indeed occur in other Fathers in which the laity also seems to have elected, but that was by indulgence, not by right, for if it had been a right, it would have been done so in all elections. But what is done by divine tradition is of right; if it is neglected anywhere, it is either a matter of fact, not of law, or it may be that the people resolve their vote into the votes of the Elders and Princes, just as here the Princes of the tribes laid on hands in the name of the people; which χειροθεσίαν, done in the name of the children of Israel, Marius says signified three things: (1.) That the children of Israel offer the Levites to GOD for a peculiar ministry (for the imposition of hands was a rite of offering). (2.) That they transfer all their sins onto them. (3.) That they send themselves away, as it were, by hand, and have them exempt from civil burdens. Finally, he acknowledges that votes are accustomed to be indicated by the imposition of hands, and that Demosthenes in Philipp. 1 notes election by votes with that word ὔτε βυλῆς, ὔτε δήμȣ χειροτονήσαν- τος ἀυτὸν, when neither the senate nor the people elected him. Conf. 2 Tim. 1, 6. Act. 13, 3.

Latin:

vers. 9. CONVOCATA OMNI MULTITU- DINE.

Ad Levitarum consecrationem & inaugura- tionem convocanda erat omnis multitudo, ac po- nebant filii Israël manus super eos, ut χειροθεσίᾳ sua eorum officium approbarent, ac ratum ha- berent. Quanquam enim electio eorum, & vocatio immediate fuerit a DEO ipso facta, qui eos sibi segregavit & segregari immediate jussit, ut tamen populi, cujus gratia huic mi- nisterio deputabantur, consensus & ratiha- bitio accederet, χειροτονίᾳ publica eandem te- stabantur. Ideo perperam Jesuita Marius ex immediata Sacerdotum & Levitarum vocatio- ne concludit populi suffragium nullum esse in of- ficiis Ecclesiasticis, quod jus eligendi & vocandi Pontifex, & Episcopi sibi solis rapiunt in Pa- patu. At a vocatione immediata ad mediatam non valet consequentia. Si Pontifex Romanus ostenderit, sibi a DEO immediate præceptum esse, ut hos vel illos segreget, ac vocet ad sa- cra officia, non refragabimur. Porro, hoc ex- emplo non patet, quomodo excludi Magi- stratus debeat, quum hic potiores partes fuisse Mosis Marius profiteatur, a quo etiam mul- titudo convocanda erat: nec populus arceatur, sed convocetur ad immissionem Levitarum in officium sacrum, imo χειροτονίᾳ solemni consen- sum suum testetur. Quid quod e Cypriano, ali- isque Patribus constet, vota civium, testimonia populorum, honoratorum arbitria expectata fuisse ut habet Leo ipse Pontifex Roman. Ep. XXCVII. fatente ipsomet Mario, populumque aliquibus temporibus & locis admissum fuisse in partem suf- fragii, agnoscat idem Marius: quod e Cypria- no B. Luther. de potest. Papæ recte probavit. Verba sancti martyris ita habent: Coram O- MNI Synagoga jubet DEUS constitui Sacerdo- tem, id est, instituit & ostendit ordinationes Sacer- dotales NON NISI sub populi assistentis con- scientia fieri OPORTERE, ut plebe præsente vel detegantur malorum crimina, vel bonorum me- rita prædicentur. Quæ non solum præsentiam, sed jus suffragii, & votorum inferunt, cum per crimina repelli, & per merita approbata admitti possint, prouti conscientia populi tulerit, quod ex traditione divina, & observatione Apostolica de- ducit S. Cyprian. Propter quod diligenter de tra- ditione divina, & Apostolica observatione obser- vandum & tenendum, quod apud nos quoque & fere per PROVINCIAS UNIVERSAS te- netur, ut ad ordinationes rite celebrandas, ad eam plebem, cui præpositus ordinatur, Episcopi ejusdem Provinciæ proximi quique conveniant & Episcopus delegatur plebe præsente, quæ singulorum vitam ple- nissime novit, & unius cujusque actum de ejus con- versatione perspexit. Quid ista ratione a notitia plebis efficitur, nisi quod plebis vota audienda etiam sint, non excludenda? Addit Marius, in aliis Patribus occurrunt quidem loca quædam, in quibus etiam plebs elegisse videtur, sed indulti id fuit, non debiti, nam si debitum fuisset, in omnibus electio- nibus ita factum fuisset. At quod ex divina tra- ditione fit, debiti est, si alicubi negligitur, vel res facti est, non juris, vel fieri potest, ut po- pulus resolvat votum suum in Seniorum & Prin- cipum vota, quemadmodum hic populi nomi- ne manus imposuerunt Principes tribuum; quem χειροθεσίαν nomine filiorum Israelis factam, tria significasse ait Marius: (1.) Filios Israel Le- vitas DEO in peculiare ministerium offerre (manuum enim impositio oblationis ritus erat.) (2.) Se in ipsos transferre omnia peccata sua, (3.) seipsos quasi manu mittere, & a civilibus oneribus habere exemptos. Denique agnoscit suffragia indicari solere manuum impositionibus, ac Demosthenem Philipp. 1. voce illa electionem per suffragia notare ὔτε βυλῆς, ὔτε δήμȣ χειροτονήσαν- τος ἀυτὸν, cum neque senatus neque populus eum eligeret. Conf. 2. Tim. 1, 6. Act. 13, 3.

## 8:14
Vers. 14.

THAT THEY MAY BE MINE) Namely, that they may be free from burdens and military duties, keepers of the sanctuary, doorkeepers, singers. For these are the offices of the Levites. To make atonement was given to the Priests alone.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

VT SINT MEI) Nempe ut sint liberi ab oneribus, belli- que muniis, custodes sanctuarii, janitores, cantores. Hæc enim Levitarum officia. Expiare, solis Sacerdotibus da- tum.

## 8:17
Vers. 17.

FROM THE DAY THAT I SMOTE) Day here, as often, stands for time. Otherwise, when that which is mentioned here was being done, it had been night.

For carrying the burdens of the tabernacle, the Levites [were taken] from the 30th year, chap. 4, 3, 1 Chron. 23, 3. But for ministering in the tabernacle they were taken from the twenty-fifth year, and in David's time, when there was need for more persons for the offices of Doorkeepers, Singers, and the like, which he himself instituted, they were employed from the twentieth year of age.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

EX DIE QVO PERCVSSI) Dies hîc, ut sæpe pro tempore. Alioquin cum id ageretur, cujus hic mentio, nox fuerat.

Ad portandum onera tabernaculi Levitæ a 30. anno cap. 4, 3, 1. Par. 23, 3. Sed ad miniflran- dum in tabernaculo a vigefimo quinto anno affu- mebantur, ac Davidis tempore, quum pluribus opus effet perfonis ad officia Janitorum, Canto- rum, & fimilium, quæ ipfe inftituit a vigefimo æta- tis anno adhibiti funt.

## 8:26
Ver. 26. AND THEY SHALL BE MINISTERS OF THEIR BRETHREN] That is, Counselors.

Grotius ought to have corrected the Vulgate here rather than bolster it with a merely precarious interpretation, which falls into the sense of no reader. For who, reading 'minister of his brethren', will understand 'counselor of his brethren'? Nor is there anything in the sources for 'counselor': according to which he ought to have rendered it, with the Chaldean and the LXX, 'he shall minister with his brethren'.

Latin:

Verf. 26. ERUNTQVE MINISTRI FRATRUM SVORVM] Id eft, Confiliarii.

Corrigere hic potius debuiffet Vulgatam Grotius, quam interpretatione mere precaria, quæ in nullius lectoris fenfum cadat, fulcire. Quis enim legens miniftrum fratrum intelliget fratrum confiliarium? Nec in fontibus quicquam habetur pro confiliario : juxta quos reddere de- buiffet cum Chaldæo & LXX. miniftrabit cum fratribus fuis.

## 9:1 Argument
CHAPTER IX. The time of the Passover. The cloud covering the tabernacle and leading the people.

Ver. 1. THE LORD SPOKE.

The Holy Scriptures refer this commandment concerning the Passover to the time of the first month. Therefore, these things are inserted καθ' ὑσερόπρωτον on the occasion of the ordained Sacerdotal and Levitical ministry, and also of the law concerning the unclean previously delivered. And it may be said that the decision of that case concerning those who were unclean, or far away, who could not keep the Passover at the appointed time, is repeated here, since the fourteenth day of the second month was drawing near, by the tenor of which divine decision those who, on account of uncleanness in the preceding month, could not do so, were bound to celebrate the Passover. Thus the order of the history will be consistent. Although, indeed, at the time of their departure through the desert, the Israelites were free from the observance of almost all ceremonies, yet they were commanded to celebrate the Passover in this second year, both because the whole pilgrimage was nothing else than a continued benefit of their deliverance, which was begun at the time of the Passover, and because that repeated celebration ought to have taught them that the Passover in Egypt was not ordained for one time only, but was to be observed by them thereafter also, when they should arrive in the promised land. For in the desert, after their departure from Mount Sinai, they do not seem to have celebrated the Passover any more, because they were entirely uncertain when they ought to move their camp, whence they are not thought to have celebrated other feasts either, because they departed from there before Pentecost.

But there is a doubt as to how the Passover could be celebrated with unleavened bread in the desert. Bonfrerius answers: Just as for the sacrifices, as is evident from the previous chapter, they could have flour from the neighboring Midianite territory, and for the making of the showbread, as long as they were in the desert: so also for the eating of the Paschal victim, there could be procured for individual families as much flour as would suffice for the making of a small unleavened bread.

Latin:

CAPUT IX. Tempus Pafchatos. Nubes tabernaculum ope- riens, & populum deducens.

Verf. 1. LOQUUTUS EST DOMINUS.

HOc præceptum de Pafchate ad tempus pri- mi menfis refert S. S. Ideo hæc inferta funt καθ' ὑσερόπρωτον occafione ordinati minifterii Sa- cerdotalis & Levitici, nec non legis de immun- dis antea traditæ. Et dici poteft decifionem ca- fus illius de immundis, vel procul diffitis, qui Pafcha ftato tempore facere non poffint, hic re- petitam effe, cùm immineret decima quarta dies menfis fecundi, quo tenore decifionis iftius divi- næ tenebantur illi, qui ob immunditiem præ- cedente menfe id non poterant, Pafcha cele- brare. Ita conftabit fibi hiftoriæ ordo. Quan- quam vero profectionis tempore per defertum Ifraelitæ ab omnium fere ceremoniarum obfer- vatione liberi fuerint, Pafcha tamen hoc fecundo anno celebrare juffi funt, tum quod tota pere- grinatio nihil aliud fuerit, quam continuatum eductionis beneficium, quæ Pafchali tempore inchoata, tum quod illa iterata celebratio ipfos docere debuerit, Pafcha in Ægypto non fuiffe in- dictum pro una folum vice, fed deinceps quoque fibi obfervandum effe, quando in terram pro- miffam pervenerint. Nam in deferto poft dis- ceffum a monte Sinai, non videntur amplius ce- lebraffe Pafcha, quia incerti prorfus erant, quan- do movere deberent caftra, unde nec alia fefta ce- lebraffe putantur, quia difcefferunt inde ante Pen- tecoften.

Dubium autem eft, quomodo azymis in de- ferto celebrari potuerit Pafcha. Refpondet Bon- frerius: Quemadmodum ad facrificia, ut patet ex fuperiori capite habere potuerunt farinam ex vicina Madianitide, & ad panes propofitionis conficiendos, quamdiu fuerunt in deferto: Ita etiam ad victimam Pafchalem edendam fingulis familiis tantum farinæ comparari potuit, quan- tum fufficeret exiguo pani azymo conficiendo.

## 9:3
ver. 3. AND HIS JUSTIFICATIONS.

In the Hebrew it is Judgments. For laws are called judgments, because they are not only established and ought to be observed with judgment: but because according to them a man judges himself and his own acts, and is judged by another, whether they are legitimate and in accordance with the divine will.

Latin:

verf. 3. ET JUSTIFICATIONES EJUS.

In Ebr. eft Judicia. Vocantur enim leges judicia, quia non folum cum judicio ponuntur & obfervari debent: fed quia fecundum eas homo fe- ipsum actusque suos judicat, & ab alio judicatur, num legitimi sint, ac voluntati divinæ consen- tanei.

## 9:5
ver. 5. ON MOUNT SINAI.

In the Hebrew, Chaldean, and Septuagint it is held as in the desert of Sinai.

Latin:

vers. 5. IN MONTE SINAI.

In Ebr. Chald. & LXX. habetur in deserto Sinai.

## 9:6
ver. 6. ANYONE UNCLEAN UPON THE SOUL OF A MAN.

That is, upon a dead man. Soul for man by synecdoche. Serarius also received a decision concerning this uncleanness alone in chapter 5 of Joshua, question 28; but because every legal uncleanness barred one from eating the lamb (Exodus 12:4), by parity of reasoning it must be extended to every uncleanness, even if this dispensation seems to have been granted for a special case specifically given concerning those unclean from contact with a corpse, and not only for the unclean, but also for those detained by another legitimate impediment, sickness, war, etc., because of a similar argument: primarily because in 2 Chronicles 30, King Hezekiah celebrated the Passover in the second month, not because of uncleanness, but because of other legal impediments, because there were not sufficient priests, because the people had not yet been called to Jerusalem from the Assyrian slaughter, and because the temple could not yet be perfectly cleansed.

Latin:

vers. 6. QUIDNAM IMMUNDI SUPER ANIMA HOMINIS.

Id est, super homine mortuo. Anima pro ho- mine per Synecdochen. De hac solum immun- ditie etiam decisionem accepit Serarius in cap. 5. Jos. qv. 28. sed quia omnis immundities legalis arcebat ab esu agni Exod. 12, 4. ex paritate ratio- nis ad omnem immunditiem eadem extendenda, etsi casu speciali specialiter data de immundis e contactu cadaveris, nec solum immundis, sed eti- am alio legitimo impedimento, morbo, bello, &c. detentis videtur hæc dispensatio, ob argumentum simile, indulta : imprimis, quia 2. Par. 30. Ezechi- as Rex mense 2. Pascha celebravit, non ob immun- ditiem, sed ob alia legalia impedimenta, quod de- essent sufficientes Sacerdotes, quod populus non- dum ab Assyriaca clade Hierosolymam evocatus esset, quod templum nondum perfecte emundari potuerit.

## 9:7
ver. 7. WHY ARE WE DEFRAUDED.

In the Hebrew, why are we prohibited or diminished in power, that is, and thus rendered as if inferior to others.

Latin:

vers. 7. QUARE FRAUDAMUR.

In Ebr. quare prohibemur vel diminuimur po- testate sc. ac veluti inferiores aliis ita reddimur.

## 9:10
Ver. 10. OR ON A JOURNEY AFAR OFF) The Romans called this the festival of fools, on which day those sacrificed who, on the solemn day, either had not been able to perform the divine service or had been ignorant of it. Festus teaches this.

These festivals of the secondary Passover are not piously enough called the festival of fools. For they were holy, ordained by GOD himself.

Latin:

Vers. 10. SIVE IN VIA PROCUL) Romani id voca- bant stultorum ferias, quo die sacrificabant ii, qui solenni die aut non potuerant rem divinam facere, aut ignorarant. Docet Festus.

Non satis pie hæc sacra Paschatos secundarii feriæ vocantur stultorum. Sancta enim erant ab ipso DEO.

## 9:11
ver. 11. IN THE SECOND MONTH, ON THE FOURTEENTH DAY.

But what if the unclean person had also been the same at that time? Augustine responds that such people either celebrated the Passover in the third month, or certainly if they had not performed the Passover in that year, they did not sin. The latter is to be preferred, because here only the second month is prescribed. Compare 2 Chronicles 30:15, 18.

Latin:

vers. 11. IN MENSE SECUNDO, QUARTADECI- MA DIE.

Quod si vero immundus tum etiam idem fu- isset? Resp. Augustin. tales aut celebrasse Pascha tertio mense, aut certe si Pascha illo anno non egissent, non peccasse. Quod posterius præfe- rendum, quia hic tantum secundus mensis præscri- bitur. Conf. 2. Par. 30, 15. 18.

## 9:13
ver. 13. THAT SOUL SHALL BE CUT OFF.

Therefore, Abulensis concludes that no one could even by a vow exempt himself from the observance of the Paschal law, if anyone had vowed an annual abstinence from meat. But those vows of abstinence from meat, and the distinction of foods, of meats and fish, are nowhere found in the Scriptures, and are merely Papistic inventions. Cornelius, however, rightly observes that vows contrary to the commandment of GOD are void; therefore, monastic vows, which cannot be reconciled with the commandment of GOD, cannot be valid. 1 Cor. 7, 2. 23. 35. Gal. 5, 1. 1 Thess. 5, 21. 1 Tim. 5, 9.

Latin:

vers. 13. EXTERMINETUR ANIMA SUA.

Ideo ne quidem per votum quenquam se potu- isse a legis Paschalis observatione eximere, colligit Abulensis, si quis abstinentiam annalem a carnibus vovisset. Sed illa vota abstinentiæ a carnibus, & discrimen ciborum, carnium & piscium in Scri- pturis nuspiam inveniuntur, & commenta tantum sunt Papistica. Recte tamen observat Cornelius, irrita esse vota præcepto DEI contraria, ideo rata non possunt esse vota monastica, quæ cum præce- pto DEI conciliari non possunt 1. Cor. 7, 2. 23. 35. Gal. 5, 1. 1. Thess. 5, 21. 1. Tim. 5, 9.

## 9:14
Vers. 14. AND IF A STRANGER AND SOJOURNER SHALL BE AMONG YOU, LET THEM KEEP THE PASSOVER. The Greeks are better and more in agreement with the Hebrew: 'But if a proselyte shall come to you in your land, and shall keep the passover to the Lord, according to the law of the passover and according to his ordinance, so shall he keep it.' An inhabitant is not compelled to keep the Passover: but if he wishes to do so, he must do it according to the law and therefore also be circumcised. See what we said above on Exodus 12, 45.

There is only one word in Hebrew, גֵּר, denoting a sojourner, and it is understood as a Jew or one initiated into Judaism. For these alone could celebrate the Passover. It is added: IF THEY SHALL BE AMONG YOU. Those, therefore, who lived in places very far removed from the temple of the Lord were excused if they did not betake themselves there. But those who had been initiated into the sacred rites of the Jews were bound to celebrate the Passover with them when they were in their land.

Latin:

Vers. 14. PEREGRINUS QVOQVE ET ADVENA SI FUERINT APUD VOS, FACIANT PHASE] Melius & Hebræo convenientius Græci: ἐὰν δὲ προσέλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς προσήλυτος ἐν τῇ γῇ ὑμῶν, καὶ ποιήσῃ τὸ πάσχα κυ- ρίῳ, κατὰ τὸν νόμον τῦ πάσχα καὶ κατὰ τὴν σύνταξιν αὐτῶ ποι- ήσει ἀυτὸ. Incola non cogitur Paschatizare: sed si id velit facere, debet id facere secundum legem ac proinde & circum- cidi. Vide quæ supra diximus ad Exodi 12,45.

Una vox tantum est in Ebr. גֵּר advenam no- tans, & intelligitur Judæus aut Judaismo initia- tus. Hi enim soli poterant Pascha celebrare. Ad- ditur: SI FUERINT APUD VOS. Qui ergo habitabant in locis valde dissitis a templo Domini, excusati erant, si eo se non conferrent. At qui sacris Judæorum initiati erant, teneban- tur Pascha cum ipsis celebrare, quum fuerant in terra ipsorum.

## 9:19
Vers. 19. THAT IT MIGHT REMAIN FOR A LONG TIME UPON IT.

If after midday, when the meal was already finished, or after the nightly rest in the morning, the pillar was still resting, it was a sign that they were to remain there. They stood, therefore, ON WATCH, or as if keeping watch and waiting for the movement of the cloud, when GOD was about to move the cloud, and they themselves were about to set out at his nod. The Jews are therefore mistaken when they teach that the pillar of fire and cloud vanished immediately after the death of Aaron. On the contrary, Deut. 31, 5, it appeared to Moses and Joshua shortly before the death of Moses, and led the Israelites into Canaan itself.

Latin:

Vers. 19. UT MULTO TEMPORE MANERET SUPER ILLUD.

Si post meridiem, absoluto jam prandio, vel post nocturnam quietem mane adhuc quiesceret columna, signum erat, ibi hærendum esse. Sta- bant ergo IN EXCUBIIS, vel quasi excubanres & advigilantes ad motum nubis, quando DEUS nubem moturus, ipsique profecturi erant ad nutum ejus. Falluntur ergo Judæi, cum docent, colu- mnam ignis & nubis statim post mortem Aaronis evanuisse. Ex adverso Deut. 31, 5. paulo ante Mosis mortem apparuit Mosi, & Josuæ, ac deduxit Israe- litas in ipsam Cananæam.

## 9:20
Vers. 20. AND THEY DID NOT SET OUT FOR AS MANY DAYS AS THE CLOUD HAD BEEN UPON THE TABERNACLE. In the Hebrew, that 'they did not set out' pertains to the preceding sense. Then it follows: 'And when the cloud was upon the tabernacle for a number of days, according to the word of the Lord they pitched their tents, etc.' Where 'days of number,' ἡμέρας ἀριθμῷ, as the LXX have it, understand 'a few days' as opposed to 'many,' of which he spoke in the preceding verse. A comparison of the passages Gen. 34, 30, Deuteron. 4, 27, Ezech. 12, 19, Job 15, 20 shows this.

The sense is, as Lorinus notes on p. 309, that the direction and sign of the cloud for standing or proceeding had to be heeded, whether the cloud stood over the tabernacle for a long or a short time, or departed from there. He who translated from the Chaldean into Latin put 'a few days,' and R. Solomon also explained ימים מעטים as 'a few days.' Augustine explains 'days of number,' that is, a certain number, which number is pleasing to GOD. Because a certain space of time was necessary for packing up the tabernacles and baggage, it is reasonable to believe that the cloud began to move in this way, and by its slow motion gave a sign so that it might be convenient for all to prepare themselves for the journey. Furthermore, Cajetan's scholiast, Antonius Fonseca, suspects that, because the Israelites could not without great labor unpack and again repack the baggage of such a great multitude on the road, even if the cloud rested over the tabernacle for many days; if, however, those days did not exceed a certain number, they did not pitch camp; but the people were as if keeping watch, and always ready for the journey. But if the cloud remained beyond a certain number of days, which perhaps Moses had foretold to them, then the children of Israel, as if by the command of the Lord, pitched camp, as if they were to remain there for a long time, and they erected the tabernacle with the court and the furnishings, as Lorinus holds here.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET NON PROFICISCEBANTUR QUOT DIEBUS FUISSET NUBES SUPER TABERNACULUM) In Hebræo illud: non proficiscebantur ad præcedentem sen- sum pertinet. Sequitur deinde: Et cum esset nubes diebus numeri super tabernaculum, juxta sermonem Domini castra metabantur, &c. Ubi dies numeri ἡμέρας ἀριθμῷ, ut habent LXX. intellige dies paucos oppositos multis, de quibus præ- cedenti commate. Ostendit id collatio locorum Gen. 34, 30. Deuteron. 4, 27. Ezech. 12, 19. Job. 15, 20.

Sensus est, notante Lorino p. 309. directio- nem ac signum nubis ad standum, vel proceden- dum attendi debuisse, sive longo, sive brevi tem- pore nubes vel staret supra tabernaculum, vel in- de recederet. Qui transtulit ex Chaldæo Latine, paucos dies posuit, & R. Salomon etiam exposuit ימים מעטים dies paucos. Augustinus declarat dies numero, id est, certo numero, qui numerus DEO placeat. Quia necessarium erat aliquan- tum spacium temporis ad componenda taberna- cula, & sarcinas, par est credere, sic nubem mo- veri cepisse, ac suo lento motu signum dedisse, ut liceret commode cunctis sese ad iter comparare. Quin etiam suspicatur Cajetani Scholiastes, Anto- nius Fonseca, quod, quia non sine magnis labori- bus possent Israelitæ tot tantæque multitudinis sar- cinas in via explicare, & rursus replicare, quamvis nubes per multos dies super tabernaculum inside- ret; si tamen illi dies certum numerum non exce- debant, castra non figebantur; sed erat populus tanquam agens excubias, ac semper paratus ad vi- am. Si autem nubes manebat ultra numerum dierum certum, quem forte illis Moyses prædixe- rat, tunc filii Israel tanquam jussu Domini castra figebant, quasi diu jam illic mansuri, & erigebant tabernaculum cum atrio & supellectile, ut hic ha- bet Lorinus.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAP. X. The use of the trumpets. The setting out of the people.

Latin:

CAP. X. Tubarum usus. Populi profectio.

## 10:2
Vers. 2. MAKE THEE TWO TRUMPETS OF BEATEN SILVER. The Jews' trumpets were small, which Plutarch also noted in his Symposiacs.

Two had to be made because of the difference in meaning, since the sound of one indicated one thing, and the sound of both another; they were silver both for the reverence of divine worship and for a clearer resonance. Two were sufficient at the beginning; more were not prohibited.

Josephus, Book 8 of the Antiquities, ch. 2, reports that Solomon made 20 myriads, or two hundred thousand, of such trumpets. Let the credit rest with the author. They were ductile, that is, consisting of plates drawn out by the striking of hammers, yet rigid, not altogether thin. Concerning their form, see the same writer of Jewish antiquities, Book 3, ch. 2. Cyril understands by these two trumpets a twofold kind of preaching: the first which strengthens faith, the second which corrects morals. Procopius says, one trumpet is doctrinal, the other moral. They are silver or spiritual trumpets because of their splendor and utmost sincerity. Ductile, because it is necessary that those who preach the life to come should grow through the present tribulations, through twistings and drawings, as Gregory the Great says, Book 30 of the Morals, ch. 7; to which it contributes that the trumpets were to be sounded by the priests, as Josephus testifies, Book 8, ch. 5, and Book 9, ch. 1. Compare Joshua 6. Their use was for calling the people to the tabernacle, for moving the camp, for battles against enemies, and at the time of festive sacrifices, as well as feasts. The use, therefore, was partly ecclesiastical in the convocation of the synagogue, in festive sacrifices, calends, and sacred feasts, and partly political for moving the camp on journeys. For the former, as the principal one, they are called sacred trumpets by Josephus. The Vulgate, therefore, must be corrected here when it renders 'BY WHICH YOU MAY CALL THE MULTITUDE, WHEN THE CAMPS ARE TO BE MOVED.' In the source, a copulative particle intervenes, as also in the Chaldean and the LXX interpreters, so that two duties are designated: for gathering sacred assemblies and for moving the camp. Cornelius excuses the Latin interpreter in vain, because he took the particle 'Vau' exegetically. It should not have been taken so. For these two cannot be confounded into one, as is more evident from what follows, as Bonfrerius admits. For the use of convocation to the tabernacle is explained distinctly in verse 3, and the indication of moving the camp in verse 5; nor was the multitude to be called when the camp was to be moved, whence also Abulensis and Lorinus refute the Vulgate here.

Latin:

Vers. 2. FAC TIBI DVAS TVBAS ARGENTEAS DUCTI- LES) Erant parvæ Judæorum tubæ, quod & Plutarchus no- tavit in Symposiacis.

Duæ fieri debuere ob differentiam significatio- nis, quum aliud unius, aliud utriusque so- nus indicarit, argenteæ tum ob cultus divini re- verentiam, tum clariorem resonantiam. Duæ sufficiebant initio, non prohibebantur plures.

Josephus l. 8. Ant. c. 2. refert Salomonem talium tubarum 20. myriades seu ducenta millia confecisse. Fides sit penes autorem. Ductiles erant, hoc est, constantes laminis malleorum contusione diductis, rigidis tamen, non omnino tenuibus. De quarum forma videatur idem antiquitatum Judaicarum Scriptor l. 3. c. 2. Cyrillus per has duas tubas duplex genus prædicationis intelligit: primum quod fidem roborat, secundum quod mores corrigit. Procopius, una, inquit, tuba doctrinalis est, altera moralis, Argenteæ he Spirituales tubæ sunt ob splendorem summamque sinceritatem. Ductiles, quia necesse est, ut hi, qui venturam vitam prædicant, tribulationum præsentia torsionibus & ductibus crescant, dicente Gregor. Magn. l. 30. Moral. c. 7. quo facit, quod a Sacerdotibus clangendæ erant tubæ, teste Josepho l. 8. c. 5. l. 9. c. 1. conferat. Jos. 6. Usus earum fuit ad evocandum populum ad tabernaculum, ad movenda castra, ad prælia contra hostes, & sacrificiorum festorum, ut & epularum tempore. Usus ergo partim Ecclesiasticus in Synagogæ convocatione, in sacrificiis festis, calendis, & epulis sacris, partim politicus ad movenda castra in profectionibus. A priori ceu præcipuo vocantur tubæ sacræ a Josepho. Corrigenda itaque hic Vulgata, cum reddit QUIBUS CONVOCARE POSSIS MULTITUDINEM, QVANDO MOVANDA SUNT CASTRA. In fonte intercedit particula copulativa ut & in Chald. & LXX. Interpp. ut duo designentur officia ad cœtus sacros congregandos, & ad movenda castra. Frustra excusat Interpretem Latinum Cornelius, quod particulam Vau exegetice acceperit. Non debebat ita accipi. Non enim hæc duo in unum confundi possunt, ut magis sit perspicuum ex sequentibus, fatente Bonfrerio. Nam distincte explicatur usus convocationis ad tabernaculum vers. 3. & indicationis movendi castra vers. 5. nec convocanda erat multitudo, quando movenda castra, unde etiam hic Vulgatam refellunt Abulensis, & Lorinus.

## 10:4
verse 4. IF YOU SHALL SOUND BUT ONCE.

The interpreter has hallucinated again here, because the difference between the convocation of the whole multitude and the convocation of the princes in the Hebrew, with which the Chaldean and LXX agree, is not constituted by a single or repeated blast, but by the blast of one or the other trumpet. For when both sounded, the whole multitude was called, but when only one sounded, it was a signal that the princes of the tribes were called. Cyril notes that the leaders are called by one trumpet, because it is sufficient to give an occasion to a wise man so that he may be wiser (Prov. 9:9), and the people by two, because they need much exhortation and admonition.

Latin:

vers. 4. SI SEMEL CLANGUERIS.

Hallucinatus hic iterum est interpres, quia differentia convocationis totius multitudinis & convocationis Principum in Ebræo, cui consonant Chald. & LXX. non in unico, aut iterato clangore constituitur, sed in clangore unius, alteriusque tubæ. Nam quum utraque sonaret, tota multitudo convocabatur, quum vero una, principum tribuum convocatorum indicium erat. Cyrillus notat una tuba convocari Duces, quia sufficit dare occasionem sapienti, ut sit sapientior (Prov. 9, 9.) duabus populum, quia eget multa exhortatione & admonitione.

## 10:5
Verse 5. BUT IF A LONGER AND BROKEN BLAST SHALL SOUND, THEY SHALL MOVE THE CAMP]

Thus among the ancient Romans, one sound of the trumpet was for battle, another for retreat: which distinction, having been poorly omitted in later times, Procopius teaches in Gothic War II.
