Et quum in Symbolo resurrectionem carnis, & vitam æternam credamus ejus rei causa ; ut doceamus, animam non extingui cum corpore, additamento illo tam obscuro, aut peculiari articulo de descensu ad inferos opus non erat: Quid quod descensus ille ad inferos Christo proprius & peculiaris sit, non vero communis cum aliis hominibus : quod sequutus sit descensum ille ad inferos sepulturam Christi, quod- que Christus ζωοποιηθεὶς vivificatus jam spiritu de- scenderit ad inferos, uti è 1. Petr. 3, 18. & serie ar- ticulorum Symboli colligitur. Quia post sepul- turam ad inferos descendere non potuit, nisi vivi- ficatus. Descendens ergo prius inferis vivum se demonstravit, post hominibus se redivivum osten- dit; denique superis in Cœlo per ascensionem glo- riosam, ut in nomine Jesu omne genu flectatur Cæle- stium, terrestrium, & inferorum Phil. 2, 10.

## 16:35
Verse 35.

BUT THAT FIRE HAVING GONE OUT FROM THE LORD KILLED TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY MEN) With body intact. Thus the Hebrews think. See what is above on Leviticus 10:2.

Latin:

Vers. 35.

SED IS IGNIS EGRESSUS A DOMINO INTERFE- CIT DVCENTOS QVINQVAGINTA VIROS) Corpo- re integro. Ita censent Hebræi. Vide quæ supra Levit. 10, 2.

## 16:38
Verse 38.

IN THE DEATHS OF THE SINNERS: In Hebrew: The censers of these sinners have been sanctified in their souls: ἐπειδήγιασαν τὰ πυρεῖα τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν τούτων ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς αὐτῶν: where the active is impersonal in the Hebrew manner for the passive: The sense is: the things themselves were no less consecrated to God by that crime than was their life. Those are said to sin against their own soul who make themselves guilty of death by a capital crime. 1 Kings ch. 11, v. 23.

Latin:

Vers. 38.

IN MORTIBUS PECCATORUM: Hebráice: Sancti- ficata sunt thuribula peccatorum istorum in animabus eorum : ἐπειδήγιασαν τὰ πυρεῖα τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν τούτων ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς αὐτῶν : ubi activum impersonale more Hebræo pro passivo : Sensus est : non minus isto crimine Deo consecratæ sunt res ipsum quam vita. Peccare in animam suam dicuntur, qui capitali culpa se mortis reos faciunt. 1. Reg. cap. II. v. 23.

## 16:38 Addition
Verse 38, near the end, note of Grotius, page 536, column b.

Others more correctly say they were sanctified because they were ordered to be offered and kept as a monument to the crime and the vengeance, and because by God's appointment they were thereafter to serve for the glorification of God's glory.

Latin:

Vers. 38. sub finem not. Grot. pag. 536. b.

Rectius sanctificata ea alii dicunt, quod jussa ea sint offerri, & servari in monumentum sceleris, & ultionis, quodque ex deputatione Dei deinceps servire debuerint gloriæ Dei illustrandæ.

## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII. Aaron's budding rod.

Latin:

CAPUT XVII. Virga frondens Aaronis.

## 17:5
Ver. 5. WITHOUT AARON'S ROD.

This translation must be corrected: For if there were 12 rods without Aaron's rod, there must have been 13. But there were only as many rods as there were tribes of Israel. For although the Levites did not have an inheritance, they were nevertheless counted here as being capable of the Priesthood. The Hebrew text has: And in the midst of them Aaron's rod. Moreover, each of these rods was from one and the same almond tree, so that it might be established by clear evidence which tribe the Lord had chosen above the others, as Fagius rightly observed.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ABSQUE VIRGA AARON.

Corrigenda hæc translatio: Si enim virgæ fue- runt XII. absque virga Aaron, XIII. oportet eas fuisse. At fuere tantum tot virgæ, quot tri- bus Israel. Nam licet Levitæ non haberent hæredi- tatem', hîc tamen ceu capaces Sacerdotii annume- rati sunt. Ebræus textus habet: Et in medio earum virga Aaron. Cæterum singulæ hæ virgæ ab una & eadem fuere amygdalina arbore, ut luculento in- dicio constaret, quam tribum præ aliis elegerit Do- minus, ut recte observavit Fagius.

## 17:6
Ver. 6. IN THE TABERNACLE OF THE TESTIMONY.

Before the ark, which is called the testimony because of the law which was kept in it, or because God would there testify His will to the people, Exod. 25.

Latin:

Vers. 6. IN TABERNACULO TESTIMONII.

Coram arca, quæ testimonium vocatur propter legem, quæ in ea asservabatur, vel quod Deus ibi voluntatem suam testaretur populo, Exod. 25.

## 17:8
Ver. 8. HE FOUND THE ROD OF AARON BUDDED]

It was to bud פָּרַח: then follows צִיץ a flower: then פְּרִי fruit: when this has ripened, by a metaphor taken from infants, it is said to be weaned, גָּמַל, i.e., removed from the mother.

Fagius also noted that it first budded, then put forth flowers, and finally brought almonds to maturity; but פָּרַח can be understood of the sprouting of leaves, because this rod first produced leaves, and afterwards flowers, contrary to the nature of the almond tree: which increased the miracle. The Hebrews give the reason why it brought forth almonds rather than another fruit, because that fruit breaks forth more easily, whence the almond tree in Hebrew שָׁקֵד has its name from watching and hastening. But since the rods were almond rods, which they themselves believe, and is handed down by Josephus, book IV of Antiquities, ch. 4, and by Cyril in the Catena, they produced similar fruits, not others. They say they were not recently cut from trees, or still green, but had been carried for a long time by the hands of the princes, who boast of them as scepters, which they carried primarily when administering justice, as insignia of princely dignity. In order to magnify the miracle, because there was no hope of reflourishing for those that were thoroughly dried up. Moreover, the matter of the miracle lies in the fact that this rod, above the others, in one night brought forth both leaves and flowers and fruit, which also never afterwards withered but always remained budding, flowering, and fruit-bearing; so that it might remain a perpetual memorial of the Aaronic Priesthood, which is shadowed forth here: as Ambrose observes, book 10, Epist. 82. That budding rod of Aaron, what else does it show, but that the priestly grace never withers, and in the highest humility holds the flower of the power committed to it in its office: and so that it might be preserved as a type of Christ, Isa. 11, 1; Jer. 23, 5; ch. 33, 15, who was to sprout forth from a virgin above the course of nature: from the dry root of the Davidic stock.

Ver. same. WERE TRANSFORMED INTO ALMONDS)

To signify that vigilance is primarily required in the High Priest. For the word שָׁקֵד signifies both that fruit and this virtue.

The pious Ancients do not rest in this signification; they say that Christ is shadowed forth here as in other figures, partly by reason of his person, because he came forth from the dry root, as it were, of the Jewish stock, Isa. 11, 1; partly by reason of his office, both priestly, because, withering like a potsherd on the altar of the cross, Ps. 22, 16, he came forth like a flower in the resurrection, and royal, because he governs his Church with a rod of righteousness, Ps. 45, 7. Which figure others explain more fully, that not only the condition of his lineage was shadowed forth, because he came forth from the family of David, which was already dried up, Isa. 11, 2, but also the condition of his mother: that just as Aaron's rod brought forth fruit not by natural fecundity in the ordinary way, but by supernatural power, so Mary conceived by the supernatural power of the Holy Spirit. Bernh. advent. 3. Behold, the rod brought forth what it did not have before, not by a planted root, not by a buried cutting, not quickened by sap, not fertilized by a nursery, and yet, when all the laws of nature were absent there, the rod brought forth what could be supplied neither by seed nor by root. If the rod, therefore, could produce nuts against nature, could not a virgin produce a son against the laws of nature? Petrus Damianus, sermon on the Annunciation. As the flower that arose on Aaron's rod did not corrupt it, but rather adorned it: so Christ, born of Mary, did not violate her virginity, but illustrated it with wondrous beauty. At the same time, the fruit of Christ's nativity is foreshadowed. Almonds provide the use of food and medicine: so Christ, born of a virgin, is both food for our soul, John 6:50, and medicine: because a poultice was made from God and man, which heals all our infirmities, as Bernard says, Sermon III on the Vigil of the Nativity. Just as in Aaron's rod buds, flowers, and fruits were seen at the same time: so in Christ the blessed verdure of the Deity, the delicious flower of humanity, and the saving fruit of beatitude germinate simultaneously: He is the germ of grace, the frond of joy, the flower of purity, and the fruit of justice. In the resurrection, He is the rod, through power; the flower, through fragrance; the fruit, through the sweetness of taste; the fronds, through diligent progress, as Bernard says with Gregory. He germinates faith in us, and brings forth flowers through confession, and fruits through the execution of good works: finally, He causes that from our dry dust, irrigated by the most grateful dew of His blood, Isaiah 26:19, new things may come forth as germs, Job 12:24, and our bones may germinate like grass, Isaiah 66:4. Thus Justin, Dialogue with Trypho, p. 241, Isaiah foretold that CHRIST would be born from the root of Jesse. Thus Chrysostom in his oration against the Jews: He who in the beginning said, 'Let the earth bring forth germs,' the same also made that wood, which was dry and unfruitful, to germinate without earth and without root; the same also gave Mary the power from on high to bring forth that saving germ without male seed. Thus Augustine, Sermon 18 on the seasons. Just as Aaron's rod germinated among the people of the Jews: so the cross of Christ flourished among the people of the Gentiles. Likewise, in these things we clearly recognize the sacrament of the resurrection from the dead. For the dry rod germinates when the extinguished body begins to revive. And Scripture leads us to this as well, when it says that that rod was לאות, for a sign of the confirmed Aaronic Priesthood, and of Him whose shadow it was. To this also pertain the descriptions which are held concerning Christ, Prophetic, Isaiah 11:1, 16:8, 53:2, Jeremiah 23:5, 33:16, Zechariah 3:8, 6:12, and especially the rationale of the type and antitype of the High Priest of the Old Testament, Aaron, and of the New Testament of Jesus of Nazareth, which the Apostle explains most diligently in the golden Epistle to the Hebrews. Nor do the Rabbis themselves seem to have hinted at anything else, even if they proposed those mysteries in their own way under the wrappings of fables, with R. Solomon in Galatinus, book 6, on the secrets of the Catholic Religion, last chapter. That the tree was cut from the tree of life in Paradise by the hands of Angels, which they sent to Adam when he had sent his son Seth to Paradise to implore the mercy of God for his sin, concerning which the Angels told Seth to plant it, and as soon as it bore fruit, the mercy of God would descend upon him and the gates of Heaven, which had been barred, would be opened. That this tree was shown so that waters might be made sweet: that the bronze serpent was placed upon it: that through it God instituted the saving of the whole world and the sending of His mercy upon Adam when the King Messiah should come; for then this tree would bear fruits, by which the bitter waters would a second time be made sweet, and they will purge the first sin and all the offenses which men have committed and are about to commit. They say that the rod of Moses was cut from this tree, and that it sprouted here. Who does not see that the very mysteries of our salvation are wrapped up in those fictions? Concerning which, see our Commentary on Genesis near the end of chapter 3.

Latin:

Vers. 8. INVENIT GERMINASSE VIRGAM AARON]

Fuit gemmasse פָּרַח: sequitur צִיץ flos: deinde פְּרִי fructus: is ubi maturuit, translatione ab infantibus sumta, dicitur abla- ctari, גָּמַל q. a matre depelli.

Primum gemmas fuisse Fagius etiam notavit, tum emisisse flores, denique ad maturitatem per- duxisse amygdala; sed פָּרַח de germine foliorum ac- cipi potest, quod hæc virga primo folia produxerit, postea flores contra amygdali naturam: quod au- xit miraculum. Ebræi causam reddunt cur magis amygdala quam alium fructum protulerit, quia is fructus facilius erumpat, unde amygdalus arbor in Ebr. שָׁקֵד ab evigilando, & festinando nomen ha- bet. Sed quum virgæ fuerunt amygdalinæ, quod ipsi credunt, & à Josepho lib. IV. antiqv. cap. 4. & Cyrillo in Catena traditur, similes fructus, non alios protulere. Non recenter ab arboribus exci- sas, aut adhuc virides, sed manibus principum diu gestatas fuisse ajunt, qui pro Scipionibus eas- dem venditant, quas in jure dicendo imprimis illi gestarint, ceu insignia principalis dignitatis. Ut miraculum amplificent, quod de penitus arefactis nulla spes reflorescendi fuerit. Cæterum miraculi res in eo sita, quod virga hæc præ aliis una nocte, & frondes & flores & fructus protulerit, quæ etiam nunquam exinceps desiccata semper mansit ger- minans, florida, ac fructifera; ut perpetuum exta- ret memoriale Sacerdotii Aaronici, quod hîc ad- umbratum: observante Ambrosio lib. 10. Epist. 82. Virga illa Aaronis, quid aliud florens ostendit, nisi quod nunquam Sacerdotalis marcescat gratia, & in summa humilitate habeat in suo munere commissa si- bi potestatis florem: utque typus Christi asservare- tur Esa. 11, 1. Jerem. 23, 5. cap. 33, 15. qui ex virgine supra naturæ cursum progerminaturus erat: ex ari- da Davidicæ stirpis radice.

Vers. eod. IN AMYGDALAS DEFORMATI SUNT)

Ad signi- ficandum vigilantiam imprimis requiri in summo Sacerdote. Vox enim שָׁקֵד & fructum illum, & hanc virtutem signi- ficat.

Non acquiescunt huic significationi pii Vete- res, Christum ut in aliis figuris etiam hîc adumbra- tum dicunt, partim ratione personæ, quod ex arida velut radice stirpis Judaicæ egressus sit Esa. 11, 1. par- tim ratione officii cum Sacerdotalis, quod instar te- stæ exarescens in ara crucis Psal. 22, 16. in resurre- ctione floris instar prodierit, tum Regii, quod Ec- clesiam suam virga rectitudinis gubernet Psal. 45, 7. Quam figuram alii plenius explicant, quod adum- brata fuerit non solum conditio generis, quod è fa- milia Davidis jam arefacta prodierit Esa. 11, 2. sed etiam conditio matris: quod uti virga Aaronis non ex naturali fœcunditate ordinario more, sed ex su- pernaturali virtute fructificavit, sic Maria ex super- naturali Spir. S. virtute conceperit. Bernh. advent. 3. Virga ecce protulit, quod ante non habuit, non radi- cata plantatione, non defossa furculo, non animata succo, non fœcundata seminario, & tamen cum illic deeffent universa naturæ jura, protulit virga, quod nec semine fuggeri potuit, nec radice. Virga ergo po- tuit contra naturam nuces producere, virgo non po- tuit contra naturæ jura filium generare? Petrus Da- mian. serm. de annunc. Ut flos in virga Aaronica ex- ortus eandem non corrupit, sed potius ornavit: Sic Christus ex Maria natus virginitatem non violavit, sed mirabili decore illustravit. Adumbratur simul fructus nativitatis Christi. Amygdalæ usum præ- stant cibi & medicinæ: ita Christus ex virgine na- tus animæ nostræ & cibus est, Joh. 6, 50. & medici- na: quia ex Deo & homine factum est Cataplasma, quod sanat omnes infirmitates nostras, ut ait Bernbar- dus Serm. III. in Vigil. Nativ. Sicut in virga Aaro- nica simul conspiciebantur germina, flores & fru- ctus: Sic in Christo simul germinat benedicta vi- riditas Deitatis, delitiosus flos humanitatis & sal- vificus fructus beatitatis: ipse germen est gratiæ, frons lætitiæ, flos munditiæ & fructus justitiæ. Est in resurrectione virga, per potentiam; flos, per fra- grantiam; fructus, per saporis dulcedinem; frondes, per sedulam profectionem, uti cum Gregorio Bern- hardus. Ipse in nobis germinat fidem, & profert flores per confessionem, ac fructus per boni ope- ris exequutionem: efficit denique, ut ex aridis no- stris pulveribus rore gratissimo sanguinis sui irri- gatis Esa. 26, 29. nova prodeant quasi germina Job. 12, 24. & offa nostra tanquam herba germinatura sint Esa. 66, 4. Ita Justinus Dial. cum Tryph. p. 241. è radice Jesse nasciturum effe CHRISTUM Esaias preloquutus est. Ita Chrysostomus oratione adv. Ju- dæos: Qui initio dicebat, germina terra; idem & il- lud lignum, quod erat aridum & infrugiferum, fecit absque terra sine radice germinare; idem etiam Ma- riæ virtutem ex alto dedit sine virili semine germen il- lud salutare proferendi. Ita Augustinus serm. 18. de temp. Sicut virga Aaron germinavit in populo Ju- dæorum: ita crux Christi floruit in populo gentium. Item, in his resurrectionis ex mortuis Sacramentum evidenter agnoscimus. Virga enim arida germinat, cum corpus extinctum cœperit reviviscere. Atque eo etiam deducit nos Scriptura, cum virgam illam לאות in signum fuisse dicit confirmati Aaronici Sacerdotii, ac præfigurati ejus, cujus umbra extitit. Quo faciunt quoque descriptiones, quæ de Christo habentur, Propheticæ Esa. 11, 1. c. 16, 8. c. 53, 2. Jer. 23, 5. c. 33, 16. Zach. 3, 8. c. 6, 12. & imprimis ratio typi & antitypi summi Pontificis V. Test. Aaronis & N. Test. Jesu Nazareni, quam in aurea ad Ebræos Epistola imprimis diligenter explicat Apostolus. Nec aliud videntur ipsimet Rabbini innuisse, etsi sub fabularum involucris mysteria illa more suo proposuerint cum R. Salomo apud Galat. lib. 6. de arc. Cath. Rel. cap. ult. Arborem excisam fuisse ab arbore vitæ in Paradiso Angelorum manibus, quam miserint Adamo, cum ille Seth filium misisset ad Para- disum, misericordiam Dei imploraturum de suo pec- cato, de qua dixerint Angeli Setho, ut plantaret eam, quæ quamprimum fructum ferret, misericordiæ Dei in eum descendet aperienturque portæ Cœli, quæ obse- ratæ sint. Hanc arborem ostensam ut aquæ redderen- tur dulces: in hac serpentem æneum impositum: per eam Deum universum orbem salvum facere instituisse & mittere misericordiam suam super Adam, cum ve- nerit Rex Messias; tunc enim hanc arborem fru- ctus gestaturam, quibus secundo aquæ amaræ efficien- tur dulces, purgabuutque primum peccatum omnia- que delicta, quæ fecerunt, facturique sunt homines. Ex hac arbore excisam fuisse virgam Mofis, eamque hic germinasse, ajunt. Quis non videt, commentis illis involuta esse ipsa salutis nostræ mysteria? De quo videatur Commentar. noster in Genesin sub finem cap. 3.

## 18:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVIII. The burdens of the Priests and Levites, and their stipends.

Vers. 1. YOU AND YOUR SONS] All the priests are sons of Aaron: and therefore all, except him who succeeded Aaron, are equal among themselves. Thus in the Church, presbyters are mystically generated by bishops.

The status of bishops is not the same as that of Aaron. He was instituted by God; they are distinguished from presbyters only by human law.

YOU SHALL BEAR THE INIQUITY OF THE SANCTUARY] If anything is sinned in the ceremonies, you shall pay for it, you whose duty it is to know such things and to show them to others.

Latin:

CAPUT XVIII. Onera Sacerdotum, & Levitarum, ac stipen- dia eorum.

Vers. 1. TV ET FILII TVI] Omnes Sacerdotes filii Aa- ronis : ideoque omnes excepto eo, qui Aaroni succedebat, in- ter se æquales. Sic in Ecclesia presbyteri mystice ab Episco- pis generati.

Non eadem Episcoporum, quæ Aaronis est ra- tio. Hic à Deo institutus, illi à presbyteris ju- re tantum humano distinguuntur.

PORTABITIS INIQVITATEM SANCTVARII] Si quid in ceremoniis peccabitur, vos luetis, quos talia scire & monstrare aliis æquum est.

## 18:7
Vers. 7. AND WITHIN THE VEIL.

More correctly, in the house at or near the veil, because פָּרֹכֶת is everywhere the inner veil; see Bonfrerius here.

SHALL BE ADMINISTERED BY THE PRIESTS.

In Hebrew: And you shall serve the service of the gift (because the Priesthood was concerned with gifts or offerings, as Malvenda says, or as Oleastrius says, it is called the service of the gift on account of the gifts which were handed over to the Priests by right of Priesthood, which explanation is confirmed by those things which follow) which I have given to your Priesthood.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET INTRA VELUM.

Rectius in domo ad vel juxta velum, quia פָּרֹכֶת ubique est velum interius, vid. Bonfrer. hic.

PER SACERDOTES ADMINISTRABUN- TUR.

In Ebr. Et servietis servitutem doni (quia versa- batur Sacerdotium circa dona, vel oblationes, ut Malvenda, vel ut Oleastrius, servitus doni vocatur, ob dona, quæ Sacerdotibus tradita erant jure Sa- cerdotii, quæ explicatio ex eis, quæ subjiciuntur, confirmatur) quod dedi Sacerdotio vestro.

## 18:8
Vers. 8. I HAVE GIVEN TO YOU THE CUSTODY OF THE FIRSTFRUITS: ALL THINGS WHICH ARE SANCTIFIED.

With the right of using and consuming. Hence the revenues of the Levites and especially of the Priests are gathered to be most ample. That tribe was three or four times smaller than any other, and it received the tenth part of the revenues of the whole land, with the remaining nine parts to be distributed among the 12 tribes. To Aaron and his two sons was given the hundredth part of all fruits. And as the number of Priests grew, the number of Israelites and the abundance of revenues grew likewise; to the Priests were also given the firstfruits of the annual revenues, which according to Jerome were the sixtieth part of all revenues. And besides these, there were their votive and spontaneous offerings, firstborns and victims, and furthermore their own cities, so that they might serve God more eagerly and be more removed from all care of earthly things. See Bonfrerius and Tirinus on verse 20.

Latin:

Vers. 8. DEDI TIBI CUSTODIAM PRIMI- TIARUM: OMNIA, QUÆ SANCTIFICAN- TUR.

Cum jure utendi, & consumendi. Hinc proven- tus Levitarum & imprimis Sacerdotum amplissimi colliguntur. Erat ea tribus quavis alia triplo, vel quadruplo minor,& decimam partem proventuum totius terræ accepit, reliquis novem partibus in 12. tribus distribuendis. Aaroni & duobus ejus filiis dabatur centesima pars omnium fructuum. Et cre- scente numero Sacerdotum crescebat pariter nu- merus Israëlitarum, & copia proventuum; Sacer- dotibus etiam dabantur primitiæ proventuum an- nuorum, quæ secundum Hieronymum erant sexa- gesima pars omnium proventuum. Et præterea erant eorum oblationes votivæ & spontaneæ, pri- mogenita & victimæ, & propriæ insuper civitates, ut tanto alacrius servirent Deo, & ab omni cura re- rum terrenarum remotiores essent. Vid. Bonfrer. & Tirin. ad vers. 20.

## 18:9
Vers. 9. WHICH ARE SANCTIFIED.

Some offerings are called holy, some holy of holies, that is, most holy, Levit. 6:17, which only the Priests could eat; some are common, which could be eaten by anyone, and in any place, which are treated here from verse 10 to 14.

Latin:

Vers. 9. QUÆ SANCTIFICANTUR.

Quædam oblationes vocantur sanctæ, quædam sanctæ sanctorum, id est, sanctissimæ, Levit. 6,17. quas soli Sacerdotes comedere poterant; quædam com- munes, quæ à quibusvis comedi poterant, & in quoli- bet loco, de quibus hic agitur à vers. 10. ad 14.

## 18:10
Vers. 10. IN THE SANCTUARY) The Holy of Holies is spoken of here in the Hebrew, not as elsewhere, that innermost adytum, but that part of the Temple dedicated to the offices of the Priests, as being holier than the external part of the Temple.

Latin:

Vers. 10. IN SANCTVARIO) Sanctum Sanctorum hic in Hebræo dicitur, non ut alibi, intimum illud adytum, sed pars illa Templi Sacerdotum officiis dicata, ut externa parte Templi sanctior.

## 18:11
Vers. 11. FIRSTFRUITS.

It refers to the portions of the Priests from the peace offerings. In Hebrew it is, this shall be for you the heave offering of their gift. Because unless it is here, nowhere in this whole chapter are the revenues from the peace offerings treated.

Latin:

Vers. 11. PRIMITIAS.

Respicit portiones Sacerdotum ex pacificis. In Ebr. est, hoc tibi erit elevatio doni eorum. Quia nisi hic nuspiam in toto hoc capite de proventibus ex pacificis agitur.

## 18:12
Vers. 12. OF THE FIRSTFRUITS.

They paid fourfold firstfruits: 1. Of the ears of corn, Jerem. 23:10. 2. Of the loaves at Pentecost, Levit. 23:17. 3. Of the loaves, which they paid weekly, Num. 15:21. 4. At the feast of tabernacles when the fruits were gathered. Menoch. & Cornel. à Lap.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PRIMITIARUM.

Quadruplices primitias pendebant: 1. Spicarum Jerem. 23, 10. 2. Panum in Pentecoste, Levit. 23,17. 3. Panum, quos hebdomadatim pendebant, Num. 15, 21. 4. In festo tabernaculorum collectis frugibus. Menoch. & Cornel. à Lap.

## 18:13
Vers. 13. THE BEGINNINGS OF THE FRUITS.

Namely, the first things, those which are born first, either absolutely, as the first fruits, or of the first year from a tree, or by comparison of the same year, and of the fruits of the same kind subsequently produced in the same year: It can be taken here for both, but so that the whole offering may be free and spontaneous. For those in Jerem. 19:23 did not fall to the Priests, but were given to widows, orphans, or friends. See Bonfrer.

THE CLEAN SHALL EAT IN THE HOUSE.

If they had been sacrificed to God: for if they had been offered to the Priests alone, they could be consumed by anyone, even the unclean. However, the Priests could not sell such things, nor even give them away indiscriminately to outsiders, but to other families of the Priests, or to the clean needy.

Latin:

Vers. 13. FRUGUM INITIA.

Primitiva scil. ea, quæ primo nascuntur, vel ab- solute, ut fructus primos, vel primi anni ex arbore, vel comparatione ejusdem anni, & frugum ejusdem generis eodem anno postmodum provenientium: De utrisque sumi hic potest, sed ut oblatio tota sit libera, & spontanea. Nam illa Jerem. 19, 23. non Sa- cerdotibus cedebant, sed viduis, pupillis, vel ami- cis donabantur. Vid. Bonfrer.

MUNDUS IN DOMO VESCETUR.

Si Deo immolatæ fuerint: nam si solis Sacerdotibus fuissent oblatæ, poterant à quibusvis etiam immundis consumi. Non poterant autem Sacerdotes talia vendere, neque etiam passim externis donare, sed aliis Sacerdotum familiis, aut indigentibus mundis.

## 18:14
Vers. 14. EVERY CONSECRATION] חרם. That happens in war.

Latin:

Vers. 14. OMNIS CONSECRATIO] חרם. Id in bello sit.

## 18:20 Addition
To chapter 18, verse 20. YOU SHALL POSSESS NOTHING.

Naturally, they did not have a portion separated from the remaining parts. For God wished them to be entirely dedicated to divine ministries, and not to be involved in the cultivation of fields; He wished thus to excite both the charity of the remaining tribes and the diligence of the Levites in the ministry; He wished that in sacred matters all should depend on the Priests, and these on them for the bodily supports of life.

Latin:

Ad cap. 18. v. 20. NIHIL POSSIDE- BITIS.

Nimirum non habebant portionem separa- tam a reliquis partibus. Deus enim voluit eos totos divinis ministeriis dicatos, nec implicari agrorum cultura; Voluit ita & charitatem reliqua- rum tribuum, & Levitarum diligentiam in ministe- rio excitare; voluit ut in sacris omnes penderent a Sacerdotibus, & hi ab illis in corporalibus vitæ sub- sidiis.

## 18:21
Vers. 21. BUT TO THE CHILDREN OF LEVI I HAVE GIVEN ALL THE TITHES) Hecataeus: οἱ πάντες ἱερεῖς τῶν ἰκδαίων οἱ τὴν δεκά- την τῶν γινομένων λαμβάνοντες, καὶ τὰ κοινὰ διοικῶντες, περὶ χιλίες μάλισα καὶ πεντακοσίας εἰσίν.

Latin:

Vers. 21. FILIIS AUTEM LEVI DEDI OMNES DE- CIMAS) Hecatæus: οἱ πάντες ἱερεῖς τῶν ἰκδαίων οἱ τὴν δεκά- την τῶν γινομένων λαμβάνοντες, καὶ τὰ κοινὰ διοικῶντες, περὶ χιλίες μάλισα καὶ πεντακοσίας εἰσίν.

## 18:27
Verse 27.

THAT IT MAY BE RECKONED TO YOU AS THE OFFERING OF THE FIRSTFRUITS) In Hebrew: And your heave offering is reckoned to you, as the corn from the threshing floor.] תרומה, i.e., heave offering, ἀφαίρεμα, is said of the tithe itself, whether of private individuals or of Levites. Just as private individuals gave a tithe of their fruits to the Levites, so the Levites gave a tithe of the received tithe to the Priests. This tithe of the tithe benefited them in the same way that the first tithes benefited private individuals, namely, that being released from that obligation, they could certainly eat the rest freely, below 31. Thus the word נחשב is also placed below, and it often signifies the equating of one thing with another. The Hebrews say, however, that to a Priest who is found to be negligent in sacred rites and ceremonies, the tithe should not be given, lest it become fatal to him by the Law, Lev. 22, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

VT REPVTETVR VOBIS IN OBLATIONEM PRIMITIVORVM) In Hebræo: Et reputatur vobis vestra elevatio, sicut frumentum de area.] תרומה, i. e. elevatio, ἀφαίρεμα, dicitur ipsa decima sive privatorum, sive Levita- rum. Sicut privati de fructibus dabant decimam Levitis, ita Levitæ de percepta decima decimam Sacerdotibus. Hæc de- cima decimæ eodem modo ipsis proderat, quo decimæ primæ privatis, nempe ut soluti eo nexu, reliquo vesci utique libere possent, infra 31. Sic vox נחשב & infra ponitur, & signifi- cat sæpe adæquationem rei unius cum re altera. Dicunt au- tem Hebræi, Sacerdoti, qui compertæ sit in sacris ceremoniis- que negligentiæ, non dandam decimam, ne ipsi exitialis fiat ex Lege Lev. 22, 9.

## 18:28
Verse 28.

TO AARON THE PRIEST) Or to his children, who are considered the same as he is.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

AARON SACERDOTI) Aut liberis ejus, qui iidem cum ipso censentur.

## 19:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIX.

The red heifer, and the water of lustration.

Latin:

CAPUT XIX.

Vacca rufa, & aqua lustrationis.

## 19:2
Verse 2.

THIS IS THE RELIGION OF THE VICTIM] In Hebrew: This is the constitution of the law. In Greek: ἄυτη διατολὴ τῶ νόμκ. In Hebrew: חקת, in Greek Διατολαὶ, ἐντολαὶ, ἐντάλματα are called those things which have their origin not from evident natural reason, but from the will of God, as we said concerning the Law of War and Peace, book 1, ch. 1, § 9. Such are all things concerning Sacrifices, especially this one concerning the red heifer. For why this heifer should have had to be red rather than of another color, the Hebrews say that not even Solomon understood. There are, however, those who think that by the redness is signified sin, the penalty of which is taken by blood.

That חקת or חקה is not always said of those things which consist solely of the will of God; examples teach that moral laws and those known by nature also come under this name, e.g., Deut. 6, 2. Ps. 119, 8. etc. That matter of the red heifer, why it should have had to be of this color rather than another, ought to have been investigated not so much among the Hebrews, blind guides in such matters, as among Christians. For that it was a figure of Christ, who was reddened with his own blood, Isa. 63, is gathered not obscurely from the fact that Paul, Heb. 9, 13. 14, himself instituted that comparison of the cleansing made through the red heifer and through the blood of Jesus Christ: that we are purged by the blood of him who was slaughtered and as it were reduced to ashes, and are expiated from sins by the lustral water of the virtue of his own blood: If the ashes of a heifer sprinkling the defiled sanctifies to the purity of the flesh, how much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal spirit offered himself blameless to GOD, purge our conscience from dead works, to serve the living GOD? However, therefore, we do not altogether deny that by the red color the foulness of sin is designated, Is. 1, 18, yet on the other hand it must by no means be denied that the bloody passion of Christ is especially prefigured: concerning which Augustine. The female sex is because of the infirmity of the flesh: the red heifer is because of the bloody passion. But it had to be led outside the camp and there be sacrificed and burned: by which what else was signified again, than that Christ ought to suffer outside the city and be held as a piacular offering? Heb. 13, 12. 13.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ISTA EST RELIGIO VICTIMÆ] Hebraice: Hæc est constitutio legis. Græce: ἄυτη διατολὴ τῶ νόμκ. He- braice: חקת, Græce Διατολαὶ, ἐντολαὶ, ἐντάλματα ea di- cuntur, quæ non ex evidenti ratione naturali, sed ex Dei vo- luntate ortum habent, ut diximus de Jure Belli ac Pacis lib. 1. c. 1. §. 9. Talia sunt omnia de Sacrificiis, præsertim hoc de vacca rufa. Cur enim vacca hæc rufa potius esse debuerit, quam alterius coloris, ne Salomoni quidem patuisse dicunt Hebræi. Sunt tamen, qui putant rubedine significari pec- catum, cujus pœna sanguine sumitur.

NOn semper חקת vel חקה dici, quæ sola Dei vo- luntate constant; leges etiam morales ac natura notas hoc nomine venire exempla docent, v. g. Deu- ter. 6, 2. Ps. 119, 8. &c. Illud de vacca rufa, cur ea potius hujus, quam alterius coloris esse debuerit, non tam apud Ebræos, cæcos in talibus Ductores, quam Christianos indagandum erat. Figuram enim fuisse Christi, qui sanguine suo rubefactus est, Esa. 63. ex eo haud obscure colligitur, quod Paulus Ebr. 9, 13. 14. eam collationem ipse instituerit mundatio- nis per vaccam rufam & per sanguinem Jesu Christi factæ: quod ipsius mactati, & quasi cinerati sangui- ne purgemur, & aqua ejus lustrali virtute sanguinis ipsius à peccatis expiemur: Si cinis juvencæ aspersus inquinatos sanctificat, ad carnis puritatem, quanto magis sanguis Christi, qui per spiritum æternum se- ipsum obtulit inculpatum DEO, purgabir conscien- tiam nostram à mortuis operibus, ad serviendum DEO vivo? Utut ergo non omnino inficias ea- mus, per colorem rubrum peccati fœditatem desi- gnatam, Es. 1, 18. vicissim tamen negandum mini- me est, præcipue cruentam Christi passionem præ- figuratam: quo de Augustin. Sexus fœmineus est, propter infirmitatem carnis: rufa vacca est, propter cruentam passionem. Extra castra autem educi ibique immolari debuit atque comburi : quo quid aliud ite- rum significatum, quam quod Christus extra ur- bem pati & piaculi instar haberi debeat? Ebr. 13, 12. 13.

## 19:3
Ver. 3.

AND DELIVERING IT TO ELEAZAR.

To him, not to Aaron; because Eleazar was to be prepared for the Priesthood, chap. 16, 37. and he wished Aaron to be as far removed as possible from all uncleanness, and always ready to handle sacred things: nor was that a solemn or festive victim, that Aaron should sacrifice it, but mournful and lustral. OUTSIDE THE CAMP: on account of the type, Heb. 13, 12. and because it was considered very unclean, as that which took upon itself the sins of the whole people.

Ver. same.

HE SHALL SACRIFICE IN THE SIGHT OF ALL) The Greeks and Hebrews: in his sight, supply of the Priest, he shall sacrifice, that is, he who offers shall cause it to be sacrificed, which the Greeks expressed by the plural σφάξουσι.

For this slaughter did not have the nature of a Sacrifice.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

TRADENSQUE EAM ELEASARO.

Huic, non Aaroni; quia præparandus erat Elea- zar ad Sacerdotium, cap. 16, 37. & Aaronem vo- luit ab omni immunditie, quantum fieri posset alie- num, & semper ad sacra tractanda expeditum: nec solemnis ea erat victima vel festiva, ut illam Aaron immolaret, sed lugubris, & lustralis. EXTRA CASTRA : ob typum, Ebr. 13, 12. & quia valde immunda censebatur, ut quæ totius populi pecca- ta in se susciperet.

Vers. eod.

IMMOLABIT IN CONSPECTU OMNIUM) Græci & Hebræi : in conspectu ejus, supple Sacerdotis, immolabit, id est, immolari faciet is qui offert scilicet, quod Græci per plurale extulere σφάξουσι.

Hæc enim jugulatio non habebat rationem Sa- crificii.

## 19:4
Ver. 4.

OPPOSITE THE DOORS OF THE TABERNACLE.

Facing toward them, although from a distance. By which it was signified that we are bound to God by our sins for punishment, and that purification from sins is made to Him, and through this victim satisfaction is, as it were, made to Him.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

CONTRA FORES TABERNACULI.

Obversus ad eas, quamvis è longinquo. Quo significatum Deo nos peccatis nostris ad pœnam obstringi, eique lustrationem à peccatis fieri, & per hanc victimam illi quasi satisfieri.

## 19:6
CEDAR WOOD ALSO AND HYSSOP AND SCARLET) Concerning the meaning of these see Levit. 14, 4.

Latin:

LIGNUM QUOQUE CEDRINUM ET HYSSO- PUM COCCVMQVE) De horum significatu vid. Levit. 14, 4.

## 19:9
Ver. 9.

WATER FROM THE SPRINKLING) Water mixed with ash shows man of what he consists. The best purification is to know oneself. That the people were purified with the ash of calves, you have also in Ovid, Fasti IV.

FOR SIN.

In Hebrew, 'sin' itself, which they refer to the cow, because the victim was an expiator of sin, which however Bonfrerius teaches was only improperly a victim, because it bore a certain likeness of a sacrifice, or because it was burned to remove legal uncleanness: but it was not a true sacrifice: 1. because it was not immolated in the holy atrium. 2. Nor were its fats burned on the altar. 3. Nor was its blood poured at the base of the altar, all of which were done in sacrifices for sin. 4. Nor was the blood brought into the tabernacle, which was to be done in the sacrifice for the sin of the Pontiff and the people. Others refer it to the waters. 'Water of sin' it is, Jun. Trem. So also Piscat. Ainswort. and Malvend., namely, of the expiation of sin. But the former explanation is more convenient. The name of water in the plural precedes. Here it is singular: 'Sin itself'. I add that it is similar to a victim because it was a type of Christ (1.) by reason of election: What is figured by the cow if not the infirmity of the Lord's incarnation assumed for sacrifice? This cow is called red, because the humanity of the Lord was red through the blood of the passion (Cant. 5:10); without spot, because he did no sin; of full age, because all his operation was perfect; it bore no yoke, because it succumbed to no sin, as Rabanus in Num. lib. 2, cap. 24. (2.) by reason of the leading out, Heb. 13:12. That the cow is immolated outside the camp designates the passion of the Savior accomplished outside the gate of Jerusalem, says Theodoret, Questions on Numbers 36. (3.) by reason of the burning, because Christ sustained the fire of the wrath of God, which we had deserved by our sins, Deut. 29:20, cap. 32:22, Ps. 22:16. The rust of sin could not be removed except by the fire of torment, says Gregory the Great. Furthermore, the skin and flesh signify the body, the blood the soul, the dung the infirmity. For what it had from the defect of our mortality, it was to be cast away in it as dung. For what is designated by the dung, if not weariness, thirst, hunger, fear of death, and whatever sufferings were assumed from humanity, says Rabanus. The sprinkler made of cedar, hyssop, and twice-dyed scarlet was also to be cast into the flame; where the cedar staff signifies the strong and incorruptible cross, the hyssop the humble and efficacious emptying of the Lord, the scarlet thread the blood, as Jansen teaches in Ps. 51 and Hesychius in Levit. lib. 4. The sprinkler is also accustomed to be applied to Baptism and the holy ministry, because it as it were sprinkles the efficacy of the cross and blood of Christ upon us through the Holy Spirit, 1 Pet. 2. Whence Theodoret in Lev. quest. 19. by the incorruptible cedar wood, he says, the divinity is represented; by the twisted scarlet (as the LXX interpreters have it) the humanity consisting of soul and body; by the hyssop the heat and sweet odor of the Holy Spirit. By these, those who are baptized are freed from the leprosy of the soul. Conf. the same in Lev. 24:4. Finally, these things seem to some to denote faith through charity and active hope. The cedar wood is hope, which ought to dwell firmly in heavenly things: Hyssop is faith, which, since it is a humble herb, clings to the rock with its roots: scarlet is charity, which testifies to the fervor of the Spirit with its fiery color. (4) by reason of the sprinkling, Heb. 9:13. Conf. Pelarg. in h. l. and B. Joh. Henr. Ursinus, Sacror. adversar. p. 295 et seqq., who also shows the remnants of this Mosaic theology in the most ancient institutions of the gentiles, and shows the rotten corpse of the consequence to Alexander I and Cornelius, who prove the Papistic lustral water (injurious to the blood of Christ) from this.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

AQVAM EX ASPERSIONE) Aqua cineri mixta often- dit homini ex quibus constet. Optima purgatio, semet nosse. Vitulorum cinere purgari populum, habes & apud Ovidium Fastorum IV.

PRO PECCATO.

In Ebr. peccatum ipsa, quod ad vaccam referunt, quod victima fuerit peccati expiatrix, quam tamen improprie tantum victimam fuisse docet Bonfreri- us, quod speciem quandam sacrificii referret, vel quia ad tollendam legalem immunditiam crema- batur: verum enim sacrificium non erat : 1. quia non in atrio sancto immolata. 2. Nec adipes ejus cremabantur in altari. 3. Nec sanguis ad basin al- taris fundebatur, quæ omnia in Sacrificiis pro pec- cato fiebant. 4. Nec sanguis illatus est in taberna- culum, quod faciendum in sacrificio pro peccato Pontificis, & populi. Alii ad aquas referunt. Aqua peccati est, Jun. Trem. Sic etiam Piscat. Ainswort. & Malvend. nimir. expiationis peccati. Sed prior explicatio convenientior. Aquæ nomen in plurali præcedit. Hic singulare est : Peccatum ipsa. Addo, quod victimæ similis sit, quia typus Christi fuit (1.) ratione electionis : Quid per vaccam nisi assumta ad sacrificium infirmitas incarnationis Dominicæ fi- guratur? Vacca hæc russa dicitur, quia humanitas Domini rubra fuit per cruorem passionis (Cant. 5, 10.) sine macula, quia peccatum non fecit: ætatis integræ, quia omnis ejus operatio perfecta, jugum minime portavit, quia nulli peccato succubuit, ut Raban. in Num. l. 2. c. 24. (2.) ratione eductionis Ebr. 13, 12. Quod vacca immolatur extra castra, passionem Salvatoris extra portam Jerusalem desi- gnat peractam, ait Theodoret. quæst. in Numer. 36. (3.) ratione combustionis, quia ignem iræ Dei, quem peccatis promeriti nos eramus, sustinuit Christus Deut. 29, 20. c. 32, 22. Ps. 22, 16. Rubigo pec- cati tolli non potuit, nisi igne tormenti ait Gregor. M. Porro pellis & caro corpus, sanguis animam, fimus infirmitatem significat. Quod enim ex defectu no- stræ mortalitatis habuit, quasi fimus in eo abjiciendum. Quid enim per fimum, nisi lassitudo, sitis, esuries, ti- mor mortis, & quæque ex humanitate suscepta pativo- luit designantur, ait Rabanus. Aspergillum ex cedro, hyssopo & cocco bis tincto, etiam in flammam mit- tendum erat; ubi Cedrinus baculus crucem fortem, & imputribilem, hyssopus exinanitionem Domini humilem, & efficacem, coccineum filum sanguinem significat docente Jansen. in Ps. 51. & Hesych. in Le- vit. l. 4. Applicari etiam adspergillum solet ad Ba- ptismum & SS. ministerium, quod efficaciam cru- cis & sanguinis Christi quasi adspergit nobis per S. S. 1. Petr. 2. Unde Theodor. in Lev. quæst. 19. per lignum cedrinum incorruptibile, ait, repræsentari di- vinitatem; per coccinum retortum (ut habent LXX. interpp.) humanitatem ex anima, & corpore constan- tem: per hyssopum calorem, & suavem odorem S. S. Per hæc qui baptizantur ab animæ lepra liberantur. Conf. idem in Lev. 24, 4. Denique notare hæc qui- busdam videntur fidem per charitatem & spem ope- rosam. Lignum cedrinum spes est, quæ debet in super- nis firmiter habitare: Hyssopus fides, quæ cum sit herba humilis radicibus hæret in petra: coccinum charitas, quod fervorem Spiritus igneo colore testatur. (4) ra- tione aspersionis Ebr. 9, 13. Conf. Pelarg. in h. l. & B. Joh. Henr. Ursinus Sacror. adversar. p. 295. seqq. qui etiam reliquias hujus Theologiæ Mosaicæ in gentium institutis antiquissimis monstrat, & Alex. 1. ac Cornelio aquam lustralem Papisticam (sanguini Christi injuriosam) hinc probantibus, putidum consequentiæ cadaver ostendit.

AND THE STRANGER) It is peculiar to this law and a few others that it also obliges guests who are not circumcised.

AND HIS GARMENTS) Servius on Aeneid IV: In sacred rites, a garment is called pure which is neither funereal nor has a stain from a dead person.

## 19:11
Verse 11.

WHOEVER TOUCHES THE CORPSE OF A MAN AND ON ACCOUNT OF THIS SHALL BE UNCLEAN FOR SEVEN DAYS)

Euripides in Taurica: Ἥτις βροτῶν μὲν ἄν τις ἅψηται φόνου Ἤ κὰι λοχείας ἢ νεκρῦ θίγῃ χεροῖν Βωμῶν ἀπείργει. In the books of Chrysippus it is said to be forbidden to come from a bed or from death to a temple.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

QVI TETIGERIT CADAVER HOMINIS ET PRO- PTER HOC SEPTEM DIEBUS FVERIT IMMVNDVS)

Euripides in Taurica: Ἥτις βροτῶν μὲν ἄν τις ἅψηται φόνου Ἤ κὰι λοχείας ἢ νεκρῦ θίγῃ χεροῖν Βωμῶν ἀπείργει. In Chrysippi libris vetitum dicitur, προελθεῖν ἀπὸ λέχυς ἢ θανάτε πρὸς ἱερόν.

## 19:21 Addition
To chapter 19, verse 21, page 539, column b. EVERYONE WHO TOUCHES THE WATERS OF PURIFICATION SHALL BE UNCLEAN.

Is it strange that the waters which cleansed made people unclean? However, the imperfection of the legal rites is thus signified, so that they might lead to Christ. Heb. 7:27, 28; chapter 10:1, following; and as Isidorus Clarius advises, that he who cleanses others ought to be reverent, lest in the very purification of others he be defiled, and remember that he also has something that he must cleanse.

Latin:

Ad cap. 19. vers. 21. pag. 539. b. OMNIS QUI TETIGERIT AQUAS EXPIA- TIONIS IMMUNDUS ERIT.

Mirum, quod aquæ, quæ mundabant, im- mundos reddebant? Significatur autem ita imper- fectio rituum legalium, ut ad Christum deducerent. Ebr. 7, 27. 28. cap. 10, 1. seqq. & Isidoro Clario mo- nente, quod alios qui mundat, reveri debeat, ne in ipsa aliorum purificatione sordidetur, & meminisse, habere & se quod purget.

## 20:1 Argument
CHAPTER XX. The death of Miriam, the Waters of Contradiction. The death of Aaron.

Verse 1.

AND THE PEOPLE REMAINED IN KADESH] Both in this and the following chapter, and in the first two of Deuteronomy, the locations of the journey from Egypt to the Jordan are diligently described, lest anyone should perhaps exist who might say that those places were fruitful or well-watered, and thus evade the power of the miracles.

This Kadesh must be distinguished from Kadesh-barnea, which was on the southern border of the land of Canaan, Num. 34:4, Josh. 15:3. For this one was far away from the land of Canaan, in the extreme borders of Idumea tending toward the South, Num. 20:15, situated not far from the Red Sea. Although Kadesh-barnea is also called Kadesh in Deut. 1:46, whence it is rashly confused with this Kadesh by Cajetan, Tostatus, Masius, and others. See Torniellus, Cornelius à Lapide, Menochius, Ainsworth.

Latin:

CAPUT XX. Mors Miriam, Aquæ contradictionis. Obi- tus Aaronis.

Vers. 1.

ET MANSIT POPVLVS IN CADES] Diligenter tum hoc & sequenti capite, tum Deuteronomii duobus primis, loca itineris ex Ægypto in Jordani adsita describuntur, ne quis for- te existiteret, qui ea loca aut frugifera, aut aquosa fuisse di- ceret, ac fic miraculorum vim eluderet.

CAdes hæc à Cadesbarne, quæ erat in confinio Australi terræ Canaan Num. 34, 4. Jos. 15, 3. distinguenda. Hæc enim longe aberat à terra Ca- naan in extremis finibus Idumææ ad Austrum ver- gentibus Num. 20, 15. non procul à mari rubro sita. Etsi Cadesbarne etiam Cades Deuter. 1, 46. dicatur, unde à Cajet. Tostat. Mas. & aliis cum hac Cades te- mere confunditur. Vid. Torniell. Corn. à Lap. Me- noch. Ainswort.

## 20:6
Verse 6.

AND THEY CRIED OUT TO THE LORD] This whole phrase about the crying out is not in the Hebrew, nor in the Greek, nor even in the Chaldean [Targums] which we currently possess. Therefore, this verse deservedly should have been cut out as an interpolation and an intrusion by the Roman Pontiffs who amended the Vulgate; since this was not done, the Vulgate, even as corrected by Sixtus and Clement, is here argued to be corrupt, as in very many other places, when compared with the Hebrew, Greek, and Chaldean Codices.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

CLAMAVERUNTQUE AD DOMINVM] Totum hoc de clamore non est in Hebræo, nec in Græco, sed nec in Chaldæis, quæ quidem nunc habemus. Merito ergo versus hic ceu ἐμβολιμαῖος & ir- reptitius resecandus fuisset à Pontificibus Romanis, qui vulgatam emendarunt: quod quum factum non sit, ab Ebræis, Græcis, Chaldæisque Codicibus vul- gata etiam à Sixto & Clemente correcta, ut in aliis quam plurimis locis, corruptionis hic arguitur.

## 20:9
Verse 9.

THE ROD WHICH WAS IN THE SIGHT OF THE LORD] The rod which was Aaron's, a sign of authority over the Levites.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

VIRGAM QUÆ ERAT IN CONSPECTU DOMI- NI] Virgam quæ erat Aaronis, signum imperii in Levitas.

## 20:10
Ver. 10. CAN WE BRING FORTH WATER FOR YOU OUT OF THIS ROCK) 'Can' is that of one doubting, as appears in ver. 12. See a similar 'Can' in Gen. 18, 13.

They had doubted, however, not concerning divine power, but concerning the will and affection, whether God wished to provide water miraculously for such a rebellious people: although He had promised it simply and without condition.

Latin:

Verf. 10. NUM DE PETRA HAC VOBIS AQUAM POTERIMUS ELICERE) Num illud est dubitantis, ut ap- paret 12. Simile Num vide Gen. 18, 13.

Dubitarant autem non de divina potentia, sed de voluntate & affectu, an Deus vellet tam rebelli populo miraculose aquam sufficere: quum tamen simpliciter & sine conditione id promiserit.

## 20:11
Ver. 11. STRIKING WITH THE ROD] Striking with the rod mystically signifies afflictions. Water signifies the consolation which follows them. Thus the Rock was Christ.

He refers to the passage 1 Cor. 10, 4. 'And the Rock was Christ,' by which it is taught not only that that struck rock signified Christ: but the Apostle is dealing with the rock which accompanied the Israelites and led them, which cannot be said of a material rock. Concerning which see Disput. on the pre-existence of the Son of God, Sect. 1, ch. 8, § 121, seq. Meanwhile, we do not reject the allegory of Augustine, lib. 16, against Faustus, ch. 17. Moses was acting the part of the people of the Jews placed under the law, and was figuring him in prophetic announcement: As therefore Moses, striking the rock with his rod, doubted the power of GOD: so that people, who were held under the law given through Moses, fastening Christ to the wood of the cross, did not believe Him to be the power of God. But just as water flowed from the struck Rock for the thirsty: so the plague of the dire passion became life for believers. Furthermore, Moses ought not to have struck, but only to have spoken to the rock, ver. 8. For the taking up of the rod does not immediately imply the end, the striking. But the diffidence of Moses is sufficiently evident from his words, ver. 10. 'Can we bring forth water for you out of this rock?' Where Grotius rightly: 'Can' is that of one doubting, as appears in ver. 12. See a similar 'Can' in Genesis 18, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 11. PERCUTIENS VIRGA] Percussio per virgam mystice afflictiones significat. Aqua consolationem, quae eas sequitur. Sic Petra fuit Christus.

Respicit locum 1. Corinth. 10, 4. Petra autem erat Christus, quo vero non significasse tantum petram illam percussam Christum docetur: sed agit Apo- stolus de petra, quae comitata Israelitas deduxit eos- dem, quod de petra materiali dici non potest. Quo- de videatur Disput. de praexist. Filii Dei Sect. 1. c. 8. §. 121. seq. Interim non reprobamus Augustini al- legoriam lib. 16. contr. Faust. c. 17. Moses populi Ju- daeorum sub lege positi personam gerebat, eumque in pro- phetica praenunciatione figurabat: Sicut ergo Moses petram virga percutiens de DEI virtute dubitavit: ita ille populus, qui sub lege per Mosen data teneba- tur, Christum ligno crucis affigens, eum virtutem Dei non esse credidit. Sed sicut percussa Petra manavit aqua sitientibus: sic plaga dirae passionis effecta est vi- ta credentibus. Caeterum non percutere, sed allo- qui tantum petram debuit Moses, vers. 8. Assumtio enim virgae non statim infert finem percussionem. At diffidentia Mosis satis e verbis ejus patet v. 10. Num de petra hac vobis aquam poterimus elicere? Ubi recte Grotius: Num illud est dubitantis, ut apparet v. 12. Simile Num vide Genes. 18, 13.

## 20:12
Ver. 12. THAT YOU MIGHT SANCTIFY ME) That you might openly proclaim my omnipotence to the people.

Latin:

Vers. 12. UT SANCTIFICARETIS ME) Vt aperte praedicaretis populo omnipotentiam meam.

## 20:16
Ver. 16. AND HE SENT AN ANGEL, WHO HAD BROUGHT US OUT OF EGYPT) There is no mention of an Angel in the bringing out of Egypt: Therefore Maimonides understands the minister of God, namely Moses himself. Thus Judg. 2, 1, the Hebrews interpret that מַלְאַךְ יְהוָה as Phinehas. And 2 Chron. 36, 16, מַלְאֲכֵי הָאֱלֹהִים are the Prophets, as the following shows. And Haggai 1, 13, he says he spoke in the embassy of God, where the LXX [says] 'and the Angel said to the angel of the Lord'.

It is strange that Grotius did not observe that the Angel who brought the people out of Egypt [is mentioned in] Exod. 3, or that what he observed there, he forgot here at ch. 4, 27. For without doubt the Angel who was seen there and promised the bringing out of Egypt, also performed the same. That he was not a created Angel, but Jehovah Himself (the Son of God), both the text there clearly testifies, and we have shown at that passage. In Judg. 2, 1, one should not understand Phinehas with the Jews, but rather the same Angel whom we have already mentioned, as we shall teach in that place, § 9.

Latin:

Vers. 16. MISERITQVE ANGELUM, QVI EDUXE- RAT NOS DE AEGYPTO) Nulla Angeli mentio in edu- ctione ex Aegypto: Ideo Maimonides intelligit Dei mini- stram, ipsum scil. Mosem. Sic Judic. 2, 1. illud מַלְאַךְ יְהוָה Hebraei interpretantur Phineam. Et 2. Paralip. 36, 16. מַלְאֲכֵי הָאֱלֹהִים sunt Prophetae, ut sequentia ostendunt. Et Ag- gaeus 1, 13. se locutum dicit בְּמַלְאֲכוּת יְהוָה in le- gatione Dei, ubi LXX. καὶ εἶπεν Ἄγγελος ἀγγέλῳ κυρίου.

Mirum, non observasse Grotium, Angelum, qui ex Aegypto eduxit populum Exod. 3. aut quod ibi observavit, ad cap. 4, 27. hic id memoria eidem ex- cidisse. Sine dubio enim Angelus, qui illic visus eductionem promisit ex Aegypto, eandem etiam praestitit. Quem vero non fuisse creatum Angelum, sed ipsummet Jehovam (Filium Dei) & Textus ibi clare testatur, & nos ad locum illum ostendimus. Jud. 2, 1. non cum Judaeis Phineam, sed potius Ange- lum eundem intelligendum, quem jam diximus, ibi- dem §. 9. docebimus.

## 20:17
Ver. 17. THAT WE MAY PASS THROUGH THY LAND) This is what the Greeks call 'to ask for a road and a market': and so Josephus here. See what we [wrote] in the second book on the Law of War and Peace, ch. 2, § 13 and 19.

Latin:

Vers. 17. VT NOBIS TRANSIRE LICEAT PER TERRAM TUAM) Hoc est, quod ὁδὸν καὶ ἀγορὰν αἰτεῖν dicunt Graeci: & ita hic Josephus. Vide quae nos libro secundo de Jure Belli ac Pacis cap. 2. §. 13. & 19.

## 20:25
Ver. 25. UNTO MOUNT HOR) In which Josephus says Petra was a city. Concerning it, see Pliny.

Latin:

Vers. 25. IN MONTEM HOR) In quo Petram fuisse urbem Josephus dicit. De ea vide Plinium.

## 20:26
Ver. 26. SHALL BE GATHERED) He shall go to his fathers, Gen. 25, 8. nay, to his peoples, as the text adds, to the assemblies of the elect. ver. 24.

Latin:

Vers. 26. COLLIGETVR) Ibit ad plures, Gen. 25, 8. imo ad populos suos, ut addit textus, ad coetus electorum. v. 24.

## 20:28 Addition
To chapter 20, verse 28. AARON AND HIS SON. to page 540, column b.

Lev. 21:11. The High Priest is forbidden to be present even for a dying father. Eleazar, however, is present here: but by a special command of God, and at that time he was certainly not yet High Priest. Add that the discourse there is about a dead person who died by a natural or usual violent death: but the death of Aaron is clearly singular.

Latin:

Ad cap. 20. v. 28. AARON ET FILIUM EJUS. ad p. 540. b.

Lev. 21, 11. prohibetur Pontifex adesse & mo- rituro Patri. Eleazarus tamen hic adest: sed pe- culiari Dei mandato, & tum certe nondum Ponti- fex erat. Adde quod ibi sermo sit de illo mortuo, qui morte naturali vel violenta usitata interiit: Aa- ronis autem mors plane singularis est.

## 21:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXI. The bronze serpent. Seon & Og defeated.

Ver. 1. BY THE WAY OF THE SPIES. The LXX took that אֲתָרִים as a proper noun: nor do the spies sent long ago from Kadesh seem to have traveled through these detours, but to have entered the land directly.

Latin:

CAPUT XXI. Serpens aeneus. Seon & Og devictus.

Vers. 1. PER EXPLORATORUM VIAM. LXX. illud אֲתָרִים pro nomine proprie habue- re: neque videntur exploratores e Kadesch olim missi per has ambages incessisse, sed terram recte intrasse.

## 21:3 Addition
To chapter 21, verse 3. HE CALLED THE NAME OF THE PLACE HORMAH.

Because the name Hormah was imposed on the city of Zephath, Judg. 1:17, from Bonfrer and Ainsworth. Poole concluded that Moses wrote these things prophetically, or that other hagiographic writers inserted them: but there is no need for those. For what is strange about different cities being marked with the same name, Hormah, that is, a place of devotion or of a curse; as in truth the cities of Arad and Zephath are different.

Latin:

Ad cap. 21. v. 3. VOCAVIT NOMEN LOCI HORMA.

Quia nomen Horma impositum urbi Sephaat Jud. 1, 17. e Bonfrerio & Ainswortho. Polus collegit Prophetice hæc scripsisse Mosen, vel alios Scriptores hagiographos ea intexuisse: sed istis opus non est. Quid enim mirum eodem nomine diversas ci- vitates insignitas, Horma, id est, locus devotionis, seu anathematis; uti revera diversæ sunt civitates Arad & Sephaad.

## 21:6
Ver. 6. FIERY SERPENTS) Lucan, book 9: 'And the greedy Prester, stretching out its foaming mouth.' And afterwards he describes one wounded by a Prester thus: 'The scorching Prester struck Nasidius, a cultivator of the Marsian field,' etc.

There are good Angels, the Seraphim: there are evil Angels, the Seraphim, whom you could express by no figure better than the Prester. And Bachai thinks that the first seducer of the human race used such a one.

What Bechai thought, we leave to its own place. But if he understands the fiery Serpents here to be evil Angels, and thinks they are called Seraphim, he errs vehemently. For it is manifest from the text that they were true Serpents. Nor has anyone doubted this until now. That they were evil Angels, no one, so far as I know, has asserted. But because there might be a doubt here concerning the mind of Grotius, there is no reason to be more laborious about these. Plutarch, from Agatharchides, records: 'Around the Red Sea, those seized by the disease were vexed with other unheard-of accidents, and then serpents from the fire, which were born with protruding heads, would destroy the thighs and arms, and when touched, would again enter the flesh, and through the muscular parts would excite an intolerable inflammation. And no one has discovered that this kind of disease happened before or after to any others.' That evil angels are called Seraphim has not yet been shown in any place.

Latin:

Vers. 6. IGNITOS SERPENTES) Lucanus libro 9. Oraque distendens avidus spumantia Prester. Et postea vulneratum a Prestere sic describit: Nasidium Marsi cultorem torridus agri Percussit Prester, &c.

Sunt boni Angeli Seraphim: sunt mali Angeli Seraphim, quos nulla figura melius, quam Prestere exprimas. Et tali usum primum humani generis seductorem putat Bachai.

Quid putarit Bechai, suo relinquimus loco. Si autem hic ignitos Serpentes Angelos intelligat ma- los, Seraphimque dictos putet, vehementer errat. Nam Serpentes veros fuisse, e textu manifestum. Nec quisquam de eo hactenus dubitavit. Ange- los malos illos fuisse nemo, quod sciam, asseruit. Sed quia de mente Grotii hic dubium esse possit, non est, quod de his operosius. Plutarchus ex A- gatarchide commemorat: Circa rubrum vero mare morbo correpti cum aliis inauditis accidentibus sunt vexati, tum angues ex igni, quinati sunt exertis ca- pitibus furas & brachia perderent, & tactis rursum carnem subirent, ac per musculosa serpentes inflam- mationem vim intolerabilem excitarent. Idque morbi genus prius aut posterius ullis aliis obtigisse, nemo com- perit. Angelos malos Seraphim dici nullo adhuc loco ostensum est.

## 21:8
Ver. 8.

THE BRONZE SERPENT) Bronze naturally harms those bitten by serpents. But when God wishes to show His power exceptionally, He works through opposites.

SET IT FOR A SIGN) The Greeks: θὲς αὐτὸν ἐπὶ σημείῳ. Rabbi Solomon interprets the word נס, which is in the Hebrew, by the Latin 'furca' (fork). See what has been said at John 3:14.

God did not only wish to show His power: He wished at the same time to exhibit to them a type of healing from the bites of the infernal serpent through the exaltation of Christ on the cross, who in His passion was a worm, not a man, Ps. 22:2. Which most elegant figure Christ explained to Nicodemus, a Master in Israel, John 3:14. Indeed, its power was not unknown then. To which the Rabbis also seem to have looked, when they said that the tree on which the bronze serpent was erected had been cut from the tree of life in Paradise, as we noted at chapter 17. Since, therefore, the Israelites carried that serpent with them into the land of Canaan, and it was kept there among the faithful for 1000 years until Hezekiah, there is no doubt that they did so for the grateful memory of the figure and the desire for the antitype. Some observe that the words על נס, 'for a sign,' as the Vulgate rendered it, hint at a typical meaning. John 3:14, where the word ὕψωσε is found, the Syrian explains by זקף, which R. David Kimchi interprets as זקף, whence זקיפא, which signifies a cross to the Syrians. Justin, Apol. 2, says: 'λαβεῖν τὸν Μωσέα χαλκὸν κὴ ποιῆσαι τύπον σαυρõ κὴ τῦτον ςῆσαι ἐπὶ τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ': that Moses, by the inspiration of God, took bronze and made the sign of the cross, and placed it at the holy tabernacle, and said to the people, if you look at this type and sign, and believe, you will be saved in it. Which things were observed by Grotius himself at John 3:14. We add another illustrious passage of Justin, and it will not be tedious to observe how his interlocutor was convinced by the evidence of this figure. Justin urges his interlocutors in the Dialogue with Trypho in this manner, p. 251. For he declared a secret mystery through this, as I said before: by which it was signified that the power of the serpent, who had also been the author of the transgression committed by Adam, would be overturned; but salvation was promised to those believing in Him who was shadowed forth by that sign, and was foretold to be about to die on the cross, from the bites of the serpent, which are wicked actions, the worship of idols, and other iniquities. For unless this has been considered thus in your minds, give me a reason for what purpose Moses placed the bronze serpent for a sign and commanded those who were harmed by a bite to look at it. Whence also they were healed, when indeed the author of this command was he who ordered that no likeness at all be made. And one of them, who had arrived on the other day: You have spoken truly, he says. For we do not have a reason which we may return. For I myself have also asked our Masters about this several times: But no one explained the reason. These things the most holy Martyr in the same place. Augustine tract. 12 on John. What are the biting serpents? Sins from the mortality of the flesh. Who is the exalted serpent: The death of the Lord on the cross. For because in the serpent there is death, through the likeness of the serpent death was figured: the bite of the serpents is lethal: the death of the Lord is vital: the serpent is hung up, so that the serpent may have no power: death is hung up, so that death may have no power. Others can also be compared, differing sweetly and elegantly about this type, since the Greeks, Athanasius against those who attack human nature, Epiphanius heresy 37, Gregory of Nyssa on the life of Moses, Nazianzen. oration 2 on Easter. Chrysostom homily 26 on John. Cyril book 2 on John chapter 10. Macarius homily 11, etc., then the Latins Tertullian against the Jews chapter 3, Ambrose Sermon 50, and also Augustine book 3 on the Trinity chapter 10, book 1 on the merit and remission of sins chapter 37, Sermon 101 on the season and Sermon 23 on the words of the Apostle. Philo the Jew also says, These things seem portentous, a serpent speaking with a human voice deceived Eve, and a serpent again brought salvation to others by its look alone.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

SERPENTEM ÆNEUM) Æs naturaliter nocet ὀφιοδάκ- τοις. Sed Deus cum vim suam eximie vult ostendere, ope- ratur per contraria.

PONE EUM PRO SIGNO) Græci: θὲς αὐτὸν ἐπὶ ση- μείῳ. Rabbi Salomo vocem נס, quæ in Hebræo est, interpre- tatur per Latinam פרק furca. Vide, quæ dicta ad Joann. 3, 14.

Non solum vim suam ostendere voluit Deus: exhibere simul voluit ipsis typum sanationis a mor- sibus serpentis infernalis per exaltationem Christi in cruce, qui in passione vermis fuit, non homo Ps. 22, 2. Quam figuram elegantissimam Magistro in Israel Nicodemo explicavit Christus Joh. 3, 14. Si- quidem non ignota ejus vis tum fuerit. Ad quam etiam respexisse videntur Rabbini, cum arborem, in qua æneus serpens erectus, excisam fuisse ab arbore vitæ in Paradiso dixere, uti ad cap. 17. no- tavimus. Quum ergo Israelitæ serpentem illum in terram Canaan secum traduxerint, ibique per I0 cc. annos usque ad Ezechiam servatus apud fide- les fuerit, ad gratam memoriam figuræ & desideri- um antitypi fecisse, nullum est dubium. Quidam observant, quod verba על נס pro signo, uti Vul- gatus reddidit, significationem typicam innuant. Joh. 3, 14. ubi verbum ὕψωσε habetur, Syrus expo- nit per זקף, quod R. David Kimchi interpretatur זקף, unde זקיפא, quæ crucem Syris significat. Justinus Apol. 2. dicit: λαβεῖν τὸν Μωσέα χαλκὸν κὴ ποιῆσαι τύπον σαυρõ κὴ τῦτον ςῆσαι ἐπὶ τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ: Mosem per inspirationem Dei æs accepisse & si- gnum crucis fecisse, idque ad sanctum tabernaculum posuisse, ac populo dixisse, si inspexeritis typum & si- gnum hoc, & credideritis, salvi in eo eritis. Quæ ob- servata ipsimit Grotio ad Joh. 3, 14. Addimus al- terum illustrem Justini locum, neque pigebit ob- servare, quomodo per hujus figuræ evidentiam convictus fuerit collocutor ejusdem. Urget Ju- stinus in Dial. cum Tryph. suos Collocutores hoc pacto p. 251. Sacramentum namque arcanum per hunc, prout antea dixi, denunciavit: quo serpentis qui- dem, qui etiam prævaricationis ab Adamo com- missæ auctor fuerat, potestatem eversum iri signifi- cabatur; salus autem credentibus in istum, qui per signum id adumbrabatur, & in cruce moriturus esse præmonstrabatur, a serpentis morsibus, qui sunt actiones pravæ, idolorum cultus, & aliæ iniquitates, promittebatur. Nisi enim hoc sic in animis vestris consideratum fuerit, date mihi rationem, cujus gratia æneum serpentem Mo- ses pro signo collocaverit & inspicere id, qui morsu lædebantur præceperit. Unde etiam illi curabantur, cum quidem auctor jussionis hujus fue- rit is, qui nullam prorsus similitudinem fieri jussit. Et alter eorum, qui altero advenerant die: Vera di- xisti, inquit. Non enim habemus, quam reddamus rationem. Nam & ipse aliquoties de hoc Magi- stros nostros sum percontatus: Nullus autem ratio- nem explicuit. Hæc ibidem Martyr sanctissimus. Augustinus tract. 12. in Joh. Quid sunt serpentes mor- dentes? Peccata de mortalitate carnis. Quis est serpens exaltatus: Mors Domini in cruce. Quia enim in ser- pente mors, per serpentis effigiem figurata est mors: mor- sus serpentum lethalis: Mors Domini vitalis: appendi- tur serpens, ut nihil valeat serpens: appenditur mors, ut nihil valeat mors. Conferri & alii possunt suaviter ac eleganter de hoc typo differentes, cum Græci, Athanas. contra eos, qui humanam naturam impu- gnant, Epiphanius hær. 37. Greg. Nyssen. de vita Mos. Nazianz. orat. 2. in Pasch. Chrysost. hom. 26. in Joh. Cyrill. l. 2. in Joh. c. 10. Macarius hom. 11. &c. tum Latini Tertul. adversus Jud. c. 3. Ambrosius Serm. 50. itemq; August. l. 3. de Trin. c. 10. l. 1. de peccati me- rito & remissione c. 37. Serm. 101. de tempore & Serm. 23. de verb. Apost. Philo etiam Judæus, Portentosa, in- quit, hæc videntur, serpens humana voce loquens Evam decepit, & serpens rursq aliis solo aspectu salutē attulit.

## 21:13
Verse 13. ARNON IS THE BOUNDARY OF MOAB) The most ancient boundaries of the nations of the river. Sihon had extended the borders of the Amorites up to this point: not the one of this time, but some older one.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ARNON TERMINUS EST MOAB) Fluvii vetustissimi gentium termini. Sehon hucusque Emoræo- rum fines protulerat: non ille hujus temporis, sed vetustior aliquis.

## 21:14
Verse 14. IN THE BOOK OF THE WARS OF THE LORD) The word ספר can be translated as narrative, so that we may understand certain ancient poems, by which notable deeds were celebrated. But the deeds performed by the Amorites are called the wars of God, because they, as it seems, at that time about which this narrative is, worshipped God the creator of the world, the Moabites their enemies worshipped Chemosh, below 28.

This does not please Drusius: who in his Commentary on difficult places of Numbers p. 454, says this about the matter: Two whole verses are cited from it (the book), which certainly were not described from a catalogue, but from a proper book, which Moses praises to that end, that he may prove that Arnon is between the Moabites and the Amorites. Augustine book 18 of the City of God thinks it is not to be denied that this book was written before the times of Moses. To some it seems that the books of Moses themselves are indicated, in which the wars of the Lord are recorded. To others the book of Judges, because in chapter 12 the borders of the Moabites and Amorites are described: since in the text there is לאמר it will be said in the future. Others wish a certain Political book to be designated, which existed in the time of Moses. Nor is it to be denied, says Augustine question 42 on Numbers, that there were already books either of the Chaldeans, from where Abraham departed; or of the Egyptians, where Moses had learned all their Wisdom, or of any other nation, in any of which books this could have been written. Which, however, is not for that reason to be assumed into those Scriptures, by which divine authority is commended. If the narrative is understood by the word ספר, with Lyranus this sense can be rendered; when the wars are narrated, which the Children of Israel performed, protected by the help of God, that which is added will also be narrated. Thus also Pelargus: He says, this place is memorable for all ages, so that in the review or relation of the wars of Jehovah his memory may never perish.

Verse of the same. AS HE DID IN THE RED SEA) The Hebrew words here are obscure, I believe by the loss of one letter, and another slightly changed. For the sense requires את־מואב בסופה, against Moab in Supha, supply it was fought successfully. את is for against, Jeremiah 15:11 and elsewhere. But in the region of the Moabites is Supha, Deuteronomy 1:1, where it is wrongly translated as the Red Sea because of homonymy. From this place the people are the Sophanites in Ptolemy. Compare what is below 26. You may learn that the Scripture has varied here also from the LXX, who have ζωὸβ for יהב, unless there was also once μωαβ there.

Mere conjectures about the original text and likewise the Greek translation. And there is no reason for any of them. For if because of any difficulty the letter of the text must be changed, so that מ is converted into נ, one letter into another, and other letters also, of which in no manuscript of the original text, and in no translation does any trace appear, are added at will, as here the letter ה is added, and so new words are formed, anything can be made from anything by such a metamorphosis. Thus truly for Grotius the Scripture is a nose of wax, and more so perhaps than for any of the Papists. These vary the sense, he changes the letter itself. He also criticizes the Vulgate with this comment, which nevertheless the Council of Trent proposed as authentic. But why could that והב not be taken for a proper name Vaheb in Supha (in the region of the Moabites, others in a whirlwind) and the torrents of Arnon. And the outpouring of the torrents, which declined to the habitation of Ar, and leans upon the border of Moab. Some render this sense of these; that namely in the book of the wars of the Lord it is recited that the city of Vaheb situated at the torrent of Arnon was overturned and destroyed by a whirlwind, and the torrent itself was directed elsewhere and now holds another course, and its very spring pours out water elsewhere, namely near the city of Ar, which is in the borders of the Moabites. Which is Osiander's exposition in his Paraphrase. Others wish there to be two verses taken from the book of the wars of the Lord, by which simply only the description of the place or Chorography of the mountain and river is noted, which separate the regions of the Moabites from the Amorites, and they understand Vaheb as a proper name for a high rock exposed to whirlwinds or winds, which hides its head among the clouds on the mountain of Arnon itself. Which opinion Pelargus recites in this place. What they wish the name Vaheb of the King of the Moabites to be, who once possessed that whole region called Suph, according to the courses of the streams of Arnon, before it had been occupied by armed force by Sihon. In which manner Junius and Tremellius rendered and explained it: For Arnon is the boundary of the Moabites between the Moabites and the Amorites. (It had indeed been before under the dominion of the Moabites, but Sihon the Amorite had subdued it by war along with the further territory, as is narrated below v. 26. Therefore the Israelites occupied nothing that was then of the Moabites.) Therefore it is accustomed to be said in the review of the wars of Jehovah (which were waged by the providence and guidance of Jehovah against the Moabites by the Amorite, so that the Moabites might be chastised, Sihon being puffed up might more boldly provoke the Israelites to war, and an inheritance might be prepared for the Israelites, see Jud. 11.) against Vaheb in the region of Suph (a King overcome by Sihon, concerning whom see below v. 26; but concerning Suph see in Deut. 1, 1.) and against the rivers, the rivers of Arnon) against Arnon, which is divided into diverse brooks and streams, as the following verse explains.) For the course of those streams, which turns aside to the site of Ar, rests upon the boundary of the Moabites (that is, it was brought about by this war that the dominion of the Moabites was bounded by that brook which inclines toward Ar; for Sihon claimed the further brooks for himself.) Thus Junius; and thus also Piscator: And the Belgian translation: which includes verse 14 in a parenthesis: (therefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord AGAINST VAHEB in a whirlwind, that the Lord himself fought against Vaheb in a whirlwind and against the rivers of Arnon) so that the following verse may cohere with the preceding one as to the sense. Those who defend the Vulgate, since they deny that Vaheb was the name of a city, because the shore of the Red Sea was not habitable, say that Vaheb is said by a certain metathesis for Jahab, so that the sense may be, just as God had begun to wage war magnificently in the Red Sea (in a whirlwind); so he continued that same grace in Arnon. For just as the Red Sea showed itself passable to the Hebrews, but overwhelmed the Egyptians with its waves: So the cliffs of Arnon, in which and under which the Amorites were hiding, were inclined and rolled down into a plain and overwhelmed the Amorites and presented an open and easy way to the Hebrews. Thus Tirinus, appealing to the Rabbis, likewise Lyranus, Hugo, Tostatus, and Adrichomius. Thus Menochius also explains the Vulgate, which here reads as follows: As he did in the Red Sea, so he will do in the torrents of Arnon: The rocks of the torrents were inclined, that they might rest in Ar, and lie down in the borders of the Moabites. Which opinion P. Fagius also brings forward from R. Solomon. He adds: Nor are there wanting those who think the Hebrew word ים סוף is not to be taken for the Red Sea, but for the end, that is, for the last days, when the greatest blood is to be shed, so that its flow may extend into Ar, and thence to the border of Moab, and again from Moab into Beer. I approve the reading of our Chaldean Paraphrast: what the Lord did at the Red Sea, and the great deeds in the torrent of Arnon. And in the following verse, the outpouring of the torrents, which are led against Lehajath, and reaches even to the border of Moab, he adds: that is, he conquered the region through which the streams flow down from Arnon as far as Ar, and flow down into the Moabite region. Note that by the Hebrew word Esched, that is, descent or flow: and by the Chaldean Schephuc, that is, outpouring, is understood the tract of the streams from Arnon as far as Ar, or Lehajath, as the Chaldean has it. These are his words. In a most obscure matter, which however in its own time was not unknown to the Hebrews, let each one follow for me whichever opinion he wishes, provided that nothing is changed in the letter of the text, which is forbidden.

Latin:

Vers. 14. IN LIBRO BELLORUM DOMINI) Potest ספר verti narratio, ut intelligamus carmina quædam ve- tusta, quibus res gestæ insignes celebrabantur. Dicuntur au- tem res ab Emoræis gestæ bella Dei, quia illi, ut videtur, eo tempore, de quo hæc narratio est, Deum opificem mundi colebant, Moabitæ eorum hostes Chamosum, infra 28.

Non placet hoc Drusio: qui in Comment. ad loc. diffic. Num. p. 454. ita hac de re: Duo integri versus ex eo (libro) citantur, quæ sane e catalogo descripta non sunt, sed e justo libro, quem eo fine laudat Moses, ut probet Arnon esse inter Moabitas & Amorrhæos. Au- gust. l. 18. C. D. censet non esse negandum, librum hunc ante Mosis tempora fuisse conscriptum. Qui- busdam videtur libros ipsos Mosis indigitari, in quibus bella Domini consignata sunt. Aliis librum Judicum, quia in c. 12. fines Moabitarum & Amorita- rum describuntur: quum in textu habeatur לאמר dicetur in futuro. Alii librum quendam Politicum designari volunt, qui tempore Mosis extiterit. Neq; negandum est, inquit August. q. 42. in Num. fuisse jam libros sive Chaldæorum, unde egressus est Abra- ham; sive Ægyptiorum, ubi didicerat Moses omnem illorum Sapientiam, sive cujuscunq; gentis alterius, in quorum librorum aliquo potuit hoc esse scriptum. Qui tamen non ideo sit assumendus in eas Scripturas, qui- bus divina commendatur auctoritas. Si narratio vo- ce ספר intelligatur, cum Lyrano hic sensus reddi po- test; quando narrabuntur bella, quæ fecerunt Filii Is- rael, Dei adjutorio protecti, narrabitur etiam istud, quod subditur. Sic etiam Pelargus: Fere locum hunc, ait, seculis omnibus memorabilem, ut in recensione vel relatione bellorum Jehovah memoria ejus nunquam sit interitura.

Vers. eod. SICVT FECIT IN MARI RUBRO) He- bræa hic obscura sunt, credo unius literæ facto dispendio, al- teraque paullum mutata. Sensus enim exigit את־מואב בסופה, contra Moabum in Supha, supple feliciter bel- latum est. את pro contra est Jer. 15, 11. & alibi. In Moabi- tarum autem regione est Supha Deut. 1, 1. ubi male mare ru- brum vertitur ἐξ ὁμωνυμίας. Ab hoc loco populus Sophani- tæ Ptolemæo. Confer quæ infra 26. Variasse hic Scripturam etiam ex LXX. discas, qui pro יהב habent ζωὸβ, nisi & ibi olim μωαβ fuerit.

Meræ conjecturæ circa textum originalem pariter & translationem Græcam. Nec ulla earum ratio. Si enim ob quamvis difficultatem litera tex- tus immutanda, ut מ in נ una litera in aliam con- vertatur, aliæ etiam literæ, quarum in nullo Codi- ce textus originalis, in nulla etiam translatione ul- lum apparet vestigium, pro lubitu, adjiciantur, uti hic litera ה adjicitur, adeoque novæ voces effor- mentur, quidvis ex quovis per ejusmodi μεταμόρ- φωσιν fieri poterit. Ita vere Scriptura Grotio na- sus est cereus, ac magis quam forte ulli Papistarum. Hi sensum variant, ille ipsam literam immutat.
