Vul- gatam etiam hoc commento taxat, quam tamen ceu authenticam proposuit Tridentinum Conci- lium. Quidni vero possit illud והב pro nomine proprio accipi Vaheb in Supha (Moabitarum re- gione, alii in turbine) & torrentes Arnon. Et effu- sio torrentium, quæ declinavit ad habitationem Ar, & innititur termino Moab. Quorum hunc sensum reddunt nonnulli; quod nempe in libro bellorum Domini recitetur, urbem Vaheb ad torrentem Ar- non sitam, turbine eversam deletamq; esse, ipsumq́; torrentem alio directum alium nunc tenere cursum, ipsamq́; ejus scaturiginem alibi effundere aquam, nempe juxta civitatem Ar, quæ est in finibus Moa- bitarum. Quæ est Osiandri expositio in Para- phrasi. Alii versus esse volunt duos ex libro bellorum Domini desumtos, quibus simpliciter sola loci descri- ptio sive Chorographia notetur montis & fluvii, qui Moabitarum regiones ab Amorrhæis disterminant, & Vaheb nomen proprium rupem intelligunt excel- sam turbinibus seu ventis expositam, quæ caput in- ter nubila condat in ipso monte Arnon. Quam sententiam recitat Pelargus in h. l. Quidnam Va- heb nomen Regis Moabitarum esse volunt, qui totam illam regionem quondam Suph dictam, secundum de- cursus fluentorum Arnonis possederit, priusquam vi ar- mata a Sichone fuisset occupata. Quo pacto red- didit & exposuit Junius & Tremellius: Nam Arnon terminus Moabitarum inter Moabitas & Emoræos est. (Fuerat quidem ante ditionis Moabitarum, sed Si- chon Emoræus bello ipsum cum ulteriori agro sube- gerat, ut narratur infr av. 26. Itaque Israëlitæ nihil quod tum Moabitarum esset, occuparunt) Idcirco dici solet in recensione bellorum Jehovah (quæ Jeho- væ providentia & ductu contra Moabitas ab Emo- ræo gesta sint, ut Moabitæ castigarentur, Sichon e- latus Israëlitas audacius in bellum provocaret & Is- raëlitis hæreditas pararetur, vid. Jud. 11.) contra Va- hebum in regione Suph (Regem a Sichone devictum, de quo infra v. 26. de Suph autem vide in Deut. 1, 1.) & contra flumina, flumina Arnonis) contra Arno- nem, qui in diversos rivos ac fluenta dividitur, ut sequens versus ἐξηγεῖται.) Decursus enim istorum fluminum, qui divertit ad situm Arnæ, innititur termi- no Moabitarum (id est, hoc bello factum est, ut Moabitarum ditio eo rivo terminaretur, qui ver- git ad Haran; Nam Sichon sibi ulteriores rivos vendicavit.) Ita Junius; atque ita etiam Pisca- tor: Et translatio Belgica: quæ versum 14. parenthesi includit: (ideo dicitur in libro bellorum Domini CONTRA VAHEBUM in turbine, quod Dominus ipse contra Vahebum in turbine pugnavit & contra flu- mina Arnon) ut vers. sequens cum præcedenti qua sensum cohæreat. Qui Vulgatam tuentur, quum negent Vaheb nomen urbis fuisse, quod littus maris rubri non fuerit habitabile והב quadam μεταθέσει pro יהב dictum ajunt, ut sensq sit, quemadmodum ce- perat Deus in mari rubro (בסופה) magnifice bella- re; sic eandem illam gratiam continuavit in Arnon. Nam sicut mare rubrum Hebræis se transmeabile exhibuit, Ægyptios vero suis undis oppressit: Ita rupes Arnon, in quibus & sub quibus Amor- rhæi latitabant, inclinatæ sunt & in planiciem devolutæ oppresserunt Amorrhæos & viam aper- tam ac facilem Ebræis exhibuerunt. Ita Tirinus, ad Rabbinos, Lyranum item, Hugonem, Toftatum & A- drichomium provocans. Ita explicat etiam Meno- chius Vulgatam, quæ hic ita habet : Sicut fecit in mari rubro, sic faciet in torrentibus Arnon : Scopuli torren- tium inclinati sunt, ut requiescerent in Ar, & recumbe- rent in finibus Moabitarum. Quam sententiam et- iam e R. Salomone adducit P. Fagius. Addit : Nec defunt qui vocem Hebraicam ים סוף non pro mari rubro, sed pro fine, hoc est, pro novissimis diebus acci- piendum esse putant, quando maximus effundendus sanguis sit, ut fluxus ejus extendatur in Ar, & inde ad terminum Moab, & rursus a Moab in Beer. Mihi probatur lectio Paraphrastis nostri Chaldæi: quæ fecit Dominus ad mare rubrum, & magnalia in torrente Arnon. Et in versu sequenti, effusio torrentium, qui ducuntur contra Lehajath, & pertingit usque ad terminum Moab, addit : id est, expugnavit regionem, per quam defluunt amnes ab Arnon usque ad Ar, de- fluuntque in regionem Moabitidem. Nota per vo- cem Hebraicam Esched, id est, decursus, sive fluxus: & per Chaldaicam Schephuc, id est, effusio, intelligi tractum Amnium ab Arnon usq; ad Ar, sive Lecha- jath, ut habet Chaldæisinus. Hæc ille. In re ob- scurissima, quæ vero suo tempore non ignota fuit Ebræis, per me sequatur quisque, quam volet sen- tentiam, modo non immutetur quidquam in textus litera, quod nefas.

## 21:16
Vers. 16. FROM THAT PLACE APPEARED A WELL) In the Hebrew: Thence into Beer, this is a well. That is, that place was called Beer, because a trench was led thither from the rock, through which the waters followed to the camp. Everything that is dug is called באר.

Latin:

Vers. 16. EX EO LOCO APPARUIT PUTEUS) In Hebræo: Inde in Beer, hic est puteus. Id est, locus ille dictus est Beer, quod eo usque a rupe perductus sit sulcus, per quem aquæ ad castra sequebantur. Omne quod foditur dicitur באר.

## 21:25
V. 25.) IN HESEBON) Hence the Esbonite Arabs Plin. 5, 11. AND ITS VILLAGES) In the Hebrew: In all its daughters. Thus are called in Hebrew the castles and villages, and smaller towns, the appendages of great cities. Note, however, that those things are also acquired by war which our enemy had sought for himself by war. See on the Law of War and Peace, book 3, ch. 6, § 7.

Latin:

V. 25.) IN HESEBON) Hinc Esbonitæ Arabes Plin. 5, 11. ET VICULIS EJUS) In Hebræo : In omnibus filiabus ejus. Ita vocantur Hebræis castella & vici, & oppida mino- ra, accessiones magnarum urbium. Nota autem bello acquiri etiam quæ hostis noster bello sibi quæsiverat. Vide de Jure Belli ac Pacis libro 3. c. 6. §. 7.

## 21:30
Vers. 30. AS FAR AS MEDABA) Which is Μήδαβα in Ptolemy.

Latin:

Vers. 30. USQVE MEDABA) Quæ Ptolemæo Μήδαβα.

## 21:33
Vers. 33. KING OF BASAN) That is, of Galadene and Gaulonitis. Josephus.

Latin:

Vers. 33. REX BASAN) Id est Galadenæ & Gaulonitidis. Josephus.

## 21:33 Addition
To verse 33. IN EDREI.

Which is called Adara, a place in Arabia, by Eusebius and Jerome in the Hebrew places.

Latin:

Ad vers. 33. IN EDRAI.

Quæ Eusebio & Hieronymo in loc. Ebr. voca- tur Adara locus Arabiæ.

## 21:35 Addition
Verse 35. AND ALL THE PEOPLE.

Those who survived from the dominion of Og do not stand in the way, Num. 32:39, Josh. 13:29. For he understands here the people who were then present in the King's army, who are said to have been entirely cut off. Although they also occupied the land itself once the military forces were destroyed, they did not immediately cut off all the inhabitants of the land.

Latin:

Vers. 35. UNIVERSUMQUE POPU- LUM.

Non obstant, qui e ditione Og superstites fue- runt Num. 32, 39. Job. 13, 29. Nam populum hic intelligit, qui in exercitu Regis tum præsto erat, qui totus excisus dicitur. Licet autem etiam ipsam terram militaribus copiis deletis occuparent, non tamen omnes terræ incolas statim exciderunt.

## 22:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXII. Balaam called: rebuked by the ass.

Latin:

CAPUT XXII. Bileam vocatus: ab asina correptus.

## 22:5
Vers. 5. SOOTHSAYER) The LXX make it a proper name Φαθουρὰ, which is Φαθουρὰ in Eusebius, so that it may be the name of Balaam's fatherland, added to the Euphrates, which he will now call the river κατ' ἐξοχὴν. That it is so is proven by what is below 23, 7. But that place seems to have had the name of Syria, from the fact that it was the seat of those who professed themselves to be ὀνειροκρίτας. See Gen. 40, 5. 8. 12. 18. and what is above 10, 15.

The Vulgate also wrongly made the proper name Ammon from the word עמו of his people (Balak's). B. Luther rendered both names more correctly.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ARIOLUM) Nomen proprium faciunt LXX. Φαθουρὰ, quæ Eusebio Φαθουρὰ, ut sit nomen Patriæ Balaami, adcita Euphrati, quod jam flumen vocabit κατ' ἐξοχὴν. Id ita esse evincit quod infra est 23, 7. Videtur autem is locus Syriæ nomen habuisse, inde quod sedes esset eorum qui se ὀνειροκρίτας profitebantur. Vide Gen. 40, 5. 8. 12. 18. & quæ supra 10, 15.

PErperam etiam Vulgatus e voce עמו populi sui (Balacki) fecit nomen proprium Ammon. Re- ctius utrumque nomen reddidit B. Lutherus.

## 22:5 Addition
To Num. 22:5, p. 542, col. a, after the end of the notes.

Jerome wrongly makes this Balaam into Elihu in his traditions on Genesis, because Elihu was the son of Barachel, while Balaam was the son of Beor (he is called Bosor in 2 Peter 2:5). The former was an Arab from Uz, according to the Septuagint interpreters, but the latter was a Syrian, not an Arab, from Pethor, a city of Syria by the Euphrates, as is held here and in Deuteronomy 23:4. Gregory of Nyssa in his account of the life of Moses considers Balaam a soothsayer, and Eugubinus in this passage considers him an interpreter of dreams, and Augustine in book 11 to Simplicianus considers him a reprobate impostor. Tostatus and B. Georg König in Vindic. Sacr. loc. 63 establish both, not incongruously considering Balaam both by reason of his person and by reason of his extemporaneous ministry. By reason of his person, he says he was both a magician and a reprobate man, but by reason of his extemporaneous ministry, for which God occasionally employed him, he asserts that he is called a Prophet of God, ch. 24:3.

Latin:

Ad Num. 22. v. 5. p. 542. a. post finem notarum.

Hunc Balaamum Hieronymus perperam E- lihu facit, in tradit, ad Gen. quia Elihu filius Bara- chel, Balaam filius Beor (2. Petr. 2, 5. dicitur Bosor) extitit. Ille Arabs fuit ex Hus, juxta LXX. Interpp. hic autem Syrus non Arabs ex Bethor, urbe Syriæ ad Euphratem, ut hic & Deuteronom. 23, 4. habetur. Bileamum autem pro hariolo habent Gregor. Nys- sen. in enarrat. vit. Mos. & Eugubinus in hunc locum pro somniorum interprete, & impostore reprobo Au- gustinus libr. 11. ad Simplic. pro Propheta Dei To- status, B. Georg. König. in Vindic. Sacr. loc. 63. u- trumque statuit, non incongrue Balaamum confi- derans tum ratione personæ suæ, tum ratione extem- poranei sui ministerii. Ratione personæ suæ & ma- gum & hominem reprobum fuisse ait, ratione ministe- rii autem extemporanei, ad quod eundem Deus oc- casionaliter adhibuerit, Prophetam Dei dici asserit c. 24. v. 3.

## 22:7
Vers. 7. AND THE ELDERS OF MOAB AND THE ELDERS OF MIDIAN WENT) Peoples always hostile to each other conspire in their hatred of the Israelites. See a similar case in Luke 23, 12.

Vers. same. PRICE OF DIVINATION) In the Hebrew: divinations: that is, all the equipment which was thought necessary for the prophet: namely, a seat and lots. See Euripides in the Phoenissae concerning Tiresias.

This is a rash correction of the Vulgate. For it is not the instruments of divination but the rewards that are noted. See Is. 21, 7. μισθὸς ἀδικίας. 2 Pet. 2, 15. 16. The Elders of Moab and Midian had no need to bring instruments of divination to Balaam.

Latin:

Vers. 7. PERREXERVNTQVE SENIORES MOAB ET MAJORES NATU MADIAN) Populi inter se sem- per inimici odio Israëlitarum conspirant. Simile vide Luc. 23, 12.

Vers. eod. DIVINATIONIS PRETIUM) In Hebræo: divinationes : id est, omnem apparatum, qui vati necessarius putabatur : nempe sedem & sortes. Vide Euripidem in Phœnissis de Tiresia.

Temeraria hæc Vulgatæ est correctio. Non enim instrumenta divinationis sed præmia notantur. Vid. Es. 21, 7. μισθὸς ἀδικίας. 2. Petr. 2, 15. 16. Non Seniores Moab & Midian opus habebant Bileamo adferre instrumenta divinationis.

## 22:12
Ver. 12. AND GOD SAID) By an Angel, below 22, 31. That is noted by Maimonides, Guide for the Perplexed 2, 41.

It does not appear from the text that these things which God said to Balaam in verse 12 were said by an Angel: nor is Scripture accustomed to speak in such a way when God manifests something through an Angel. The authority of the Jew moves us little where the text does not shine forth. The things which are held in verses 22 and 31 teach that the Angel of the Lord was sent afterwards: where Balaam did not obey the divine warning made ἀμέσως [immediately], so that, namely, he might resist the same. Maimonides also dreams that all the things which are related here concerning the Angel were done in a vision, just as he also judges concerning those things which are related in Gen. 32, 14 and Jos. 5, 13-14. Is it right to follow the Guide for the Perplexed in that as well? But the letter of the history is more evident in this place than to allow one to feign a mere vision here. Nor does our author seem to offer assent to Maimonides, moved especially by histories, as it appears, of the profane, which whether they are found or not, the divine narrative stands on its own footing. Nor for does the truth of the history of Balaam's ass, which spoke words to him, depend upon the histories of similar portents of a lamb or an ox speaking in Livy and others (which, whether they be so or not, nothing is detracted from the Mosaic relation).

Latin:

Vers. 12. DIXITQVE DEVS) Per Angelum, infra 22, 31. Notatum id Maimonidæ, Duce dubitantium 2,41.

Non appatet e textu, hæc quæ 12. dixit Deus Bileamo, per Angelum dicta esse: nec ita loqui solet Scriptura, cum per Angelum Deus quid manife- stat. Autoritas Judæi parum nos movet, ubi textus non prælucet. Quæ v. 22. 31. habentur, An- gelum Domini postmodum missum docent: ubi monitioni divinæ ἀμέσως factæ non paruit Bile- am, ut scil. resisteret eidem. Somniat etiam Maimonides, quæ hic referuntur de Angelo, o- mnia facta esse in visione, uti de illis quoque censet, quæ referuntur Gen. 32, 14. Jos. 5, 13. 14. Num etiam in eo Ducem dubitantium sequi fas est? At litera hi- storiæ evidentior est hoc in loco, quam ut liceat me- ram hic visionem fingere. Nec assensum Maimo- nidæ videtur præbere noster, motus imprimis hi- storiis, ut apparet prophanis, quæ sive reperiantur, seu minus, narratio divina suo stat talo. Neq; enim a similium portentorum historiis de agno aut bove lo- quuto apud Livium & alios (quæ sive ita sese habeant, seu non, relationi Mosaicæ nil derogatur) historiæ de asina Bileami, quæ verba ad ipsum fecit, veritas dependet.

## 22:12 Addition
To verse 12, page 542, col. b, near the end of the notes.

Furthermore, what God says here, 'Do not go with them,' but in verse 35, 'Go with these men,' is to be explained thus: not that there is a contrary will in God, one of sign and another of good pleasure; but that according to his antecedent will GOD first prohibited it, but afterwards by his consequent will, he did not indeed command it, but permitted it, just as words of command are sometimes taken permissively, 2 Kings 2:17, Matthew 8:13. Compare Luke 8:32. Concerning which Augustine, book 4, Questions on Numbers, question 48: 'The Lord, seeing his desire captured and overcome by gifts, permitted him to depart, so that by the beast of burden on which he was riding, he might restrain his avarice.

Latin:

Ad vers. 12. pag. 542. b. sub finem notar.

Cæterum quod hic ait Deus, noli ire cum eis: versu vero 35. vade cum istis, ita explicandum, non quod in Deo contraria sit voluntas, alia figni alia vero beneplaciti; sed quod secundum volunta- tem antecedentem DEUS primum id prohibuerit, post autem voluntate consequente, non mandarir quidem, sed permiserit, uti verba mandati permissivē quandoque accipiuntur 2. Reg. 2. v. 17. Matth. 8. vers. 13. Conf. Luc. 8. vers. 32. Quo de Augustin. libr. 4. Quæst. in Numer. quæst. 48. Dominus vi- dens ejus cupiditatem captam devictamque muneri- bus, permisit eum abire, ut per jumentum, quo vehe- batur, ejus avaritiam coerceret.

## 22:22
Ver. 22.

AND THE ANGEL OF THE LORD STOOD IN THE WAY) Maimonides thinks all these things were done in a vision: as in Gen. 22, 24 [sic]; Jos. 5, 13-14. Yet histories of similar portents are not lacking. A lamb spoke while Bocchoris was reigning in Egypt, according to Eusebius. An ox spoke often according to Livy, and according to Eusebius. Pliny, Polybius, and Plutarch also mention it.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

STETITQVE ANGELVS DOMINI IN VIA) Hæc omnia Maimonides facta putat in visione: ut Gen. 22, 24. Jos. 5, 13. 14. Neque tamen similium portentorum desunt historiæ. Agnus locutus Bocchoride in Ægypto regnante apud Eusebium. Bos locutus apud Livium sæpe, & apud Eusebium. Meminere & Plinius, Polybius, Plutarchus.

## 22:27
AND WHEN THE ASS HAD SEEN THE ANGEL STANDING, IT FELL UNDER THE FEET OF THE RIDER)

From this the Pythagoreans took the idea that one should not proceed on a road where an ass has fallen. Hermippus mentions this, and Josephus from Hermippus. The allegorical sense is that those things which are above our strength should not be attempted. That is said otherwise, μὴ πρὸς κέντρα λακτίζειν [not to kick against the pricks]: which proverb, worn out by Aeschylus and Euripides, and afterwards by many, Christ uses to Saul in Acts 9, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 27. CVMQVE VIDISSET ASINA STANTEM ANGELVM CONCIDIT SVB PEDIBVS SEDENTIS)

Hinc sumsere Pythagorici, non pergendum in via ubi asi- nus procuberit. Meminit Hermippus, & ex Hermippo Jo- sephus. Sensus allegoricus est, non tentanda ea quæ supra nostras sunt vires. Id aliter dicitur, μὴ πρὸς κέντρα λακτί- ζειν : quod proverbium Æschylo & Euripidi, & postea mul- tis tritum, Christus ad Saulum usurpat Act. 9, 5.

## 22:31
V. 31. AND HE WORSHIPPED HIM BOWED DOWN TO THE EARTH) In the Hebrew it is ויקד וישתחו, that is, with his head first inclined, then also with his whole body he showed a sign of reverence to him.

Latin:

V. 31. ADORAVITQVE EVM PRONUS IN TER- RAM) In Hebræo est ויקד וישתח id est, capite primum inclinato, deinde & toto corpore reverentiæ signum ipsi ex- hibuit.

## 22:38
Ver. 38. EXCEPT THAT GOD HATH PUT IN MY MOUTH) By the ministry of an Angel, as above, so also in 23, 5.

When God is said to put words into the mouth of the Prophets, it is nowhere understood as the ministries of Angels, but always as a divine revelation or inspiration made immediately, by which He instilled both concepts into the mind and words into the tongue, so that they might know what they ought to speak, and be able to bring it forth. We ask for it to be demonstrated by even a single example that the ministry of Angels intervened when God put words into the mouths of the Prophets. To instill concepts into minds is a divine and immediate work, to which no creature contributes anything. To inform the tongue, and to put the word of God into the mouth, is the work of the Holy Spirit. Therefore the Prophets and Apostles were moved immediately by the Holy Spirit, by which they preached the word of God, as the Spirit gave them to speak. Acts 2, 1-2; 2 Pet. 1, 21. As for what pertains to v. 35: The Angel says: Go with these men, and see, take heed that you speak nothing other than what I shall command you: If you consider Grotius's hypothesis, it must be said that the Angel here sustained the person of GOD, and thus spoke from the person of God. It remains, therefore, that God himself commanded Balaam what he ought to speak, which is manifest in ch. 38 [sic] and ch. 23, 5, and Balaam himself openly testifies in Num. 24, 3: 'He said, the hearer of the words of the Lord,' and v. 13: 'Whatever the Lord shall say, this I will speak.' But that that Angel not only sustained the person of God, but in truth was God himself, namely the Son of God, whom Grotius did not deny to be true God, is gathered not obscurely from the circumstances of the text. For that Angel, who resisted Balaam in the way, and before whom his ass fell upon its knees, is called by the name Jehovah, and the divine work is attributed to him, that he opened the mouth of the ass: which miraculous work is of no created Angel: ch. 22, 8. 'And the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and it spoke:' Then indeed he claims for himself the divine ἀξίωμα [authority/dignity], and speaks not as a minister of the Lord, but as the Lord himself authoritatively, and with that reasoning which no minister ever usurped for himself, v. 32: 'I came to oppose you, because your way is perverse and contrary TO ME.' For we know that sin is committed against God alone from Ps. 51, 6. And furthermore: 'And unless the ass had turned from the way, giving place to the one resisting, I would have killed you, and she would live.' Who of the ministers could have spoken thus? Who has that power

sovereign, so that he can either kill a man or save him, unless it is the one God, the LORD of life and death? Jas. 4:12. Furthermore, Balaam also acknowledged God himself to be present: I have sinned, he says v. 55, I did not know that YOU were standing against me, and now if IT DISPLEASES YOU that I go, I will return. He confesses that he has sinned against this Antagonist of his, who resisted him on the way, he acknowledges His supreme authority, and he venerates it religiously and reverently, he submits himself to the same at a nod in the prophetic work, and promises the most humble obedience, which prophets render, and are bound to render, to GOD the director: he does not speak with that angel as a minister of GOD, but as with GOD himself, who alone, by His own authority, directs the prophets and their way, according to His own pleasure and will, which he ascribes to this angel. Moreover, that authentic and sovereign permission was joined with a similar instruction: Go with these men, and see that you speak nothing other than what I have commanded you: what else does this argue but the Lord himself present here? For never has an angel, a minister, spoken to any of the prophets with such authority. Now if you compare the words of this angel with the words of Balaam in this verse 35 and 38, and with the narrative of Moses ch. 23:5, an invincible argument of this kind is born: He who put words into the mouth of the prophet Balaam, and commanded him what he should speak, is Jehovah: which is manifest from v. 38 of this chapter: Behold I am here; can I speak anything else, except what God has put into my mouth? etc. XXIII. Balaam said to Balak: stay a little while by your burnt offering, until I go, if perhaps the LORD meets me, and whatever He commands, I will speak to you; and when he had gone quickly, God met him v. 5. For the LORD put a word in his mouth. That Lord, to whom the sacrifice was offered, who certainly could not be a created angel: For to him, even if he is believed to represent the person of the Lord, it is a sin to offer sacrifice. And v. 12 again: Can I speak anything else, except what the LORD has commanded? Again v. 16. To whom when the LORD had met him and put a word in his mouth, He said, Return to Balak: and you shall speak these things to him v. 7. To whom Balak: what, he says, has the LORD spoken? Similar things are had in v. 26, 27, and ch. 24:13. Add what is read in ch. 24:1, when Balaam had seen that it pleased the LORD that he should bless the people, etc. Therefore v. 2 it is said that the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and Balaam said: the hearer of the words of God has spoken, who has looked upon the vision of the Almighty. But when God commanded something to any of the prophets by the work and ministry of an angel, it is never said that the spirit of the Lord rushed upon him, nor do those things about the vision of the Almighty and the hearing of His words correspond to an angelic apparition. But these things are repeated again in verse 15, so that from all these it is most clear that the Lord spoke to Balaam personally and immediately. Wherefore that major proposition is entirely indubitable and immovable. He who gave the words into the mouth of the prophet Balaam, and commanded him what he should speak, is Jehovah, since this is claimed for and befits one and only Jehovah. We now subsume: But the angel of the Lord, who appeared to Balaam, is he who gave the words into the mouth of the prophet Balaam, and commanded him what he should speak: which is expressly had in ch. 22:30. The Angel says: Go with these men and take care that you speak nothing other than what I have commanded you. Therefore, the angel of the Lord, who appeared to Balaam, is Jehovah. These things having been thus proven, it is now certain and indubitable that these predicates, both to be Jehovah himself and to be the angel of the Lord, befit no other subject except the one and only Son of GOD, whom Grotius acknowledges is called an angel, and does not deny is Jehovah. Nor indeed is there any reason why one should deem it unworthy of the Son of God, with Calixtus, to meet a false prophet and to resist him. For how often did Jehovah oppose himself to false prophets and resist them? Is it unworthy of the Son of God to avert a curse from the people, and to turn it into a blessing, to resist the Devil and his instruments, to put words into the mouths of prophets, to reveal His way to them, to call them back from a wicked plan, to elicit good from evil, and never fail to promote the salvation of His people, and to direct all things to the same?

Latin:

Vers. 38. NISI QVOD POSUERIT DEVS IN ORE MEO) Angeli ministerio, ut supra, sic & 23, 5.

Cum Deus verba ponere dicitur in ore Prophe- tarum, nuspiam Angelorum ministeriis, semper im- mediate facta revelatio vel inspiratio divina, qua & menti conceptus & verba linguæ indidit, ut quid lo- qui deberent, scirent, atque proferre id possent, in- telligitur. Petimus vel unico exemplo demonstra- ri, quod Angelorum ministerium intervenerit, cum Deus verba in ora Prophetarum posuit. Conce- ptus mentibus ingerere divinum & immediatum o- pus est, ad quod nulla creatura quicquam confert. Linguam informare, atque in os verbum Dei ponere, Spiritus S. est opus. Ideo Prophetæ & Apostoli im- mediate acti fuere a Sp. S. qua prædicarunt verbum Dei, prout Spiritus illis dedit eloqui. Act. 2, 1. 2. Petr. 1, 21. Quod ad v. 35. attinet: Ait Angelus : Vade cum istis, & vide, ne aliud, quam præcepero tibi loquaris : si Grotii hypothesin respicias, dicendum fuerit, Ange- lum hic personam DEI sustinuisse, atque ex persona Dei sic loquutum esse. Manet ergo, Deum ipsum præcepisse Bileamo, quæ loqui debuerit, quod ev. 38. & c. 23, 5. manifestum est, & Bileam ipse aperte testatur Num. 24, 3. Dixit auditor sermonum Domi- ni, & v. 13. Quicquid Dominus dixerit, hoc loquar. Sed Angelum illum non tantum sustinuisse perso- nam Dei, verum revera fuisse ipsummet Deum, Fi- lium nempe Dei, quem verum Deum esse non ne- gavit Grotius, e textus circumstantiis haud obscure colligitur. Vocatur enim Angelus ille, qui restitit in via Bileamo, & coram quo in genua procidit asina ejus, nomine Jehovab, & tribuitur ei opus di- vinum, quod os asinæ aperuit: quod miraculosum opus nullius Angeli creati est: c. 22, 8. Aperuit- que DOMINUS os asinæ, & loquuta est: Tum ve- ro divinum ἀξίωμα sibi vendicat, & loquitur non ut minister Domini, sed ut Dominus ipse auctoritati- ve, atque ea ratione, quam nunquam usurpavit sibi ullus minister v. 32. EGO veni, ut adversarer tibi, quia perversa est via tua MIHIque contraria. So- li enim Deo peccari novimus e Ps. 51, 6. Et porro : Et nisi asina declinasset de via, dans locum resistenti, te occidissem, & illa viveret. Quis ministrorum ita loqui potuisset? quis habet illam potestatem

ἀὐτοκρατορικὴν, ut vel occidere hominem possit vel servare nisi unus Deus vitæ necisq; DOMINUS? Jac. 4, 12. Porro agnovit quoque Bileam Deum ipsum præsentem: Peccavi, inquit v. 55. nescivi, quod TU stares contra me, & nunc si DISPLICET TIBI, ut vadam, revertar. Fatetur se peccasse contra hunc Antagonistam suum, qui sibi restitit in via, agnoscit supremam ejus autoritatem, eamq; veneratur reli- giose, & reverenter, submittit sese eidem ad nu- tum in opere prophetico, ac obedientiam humilli- mam promittit, quam Prophetæ DEO directori præstant, & præstare tenentur: non loquitur cum angelo illo, ut ministro DEI, sed uti cum ipso DEO, qui ἀὐτεξοσίως solus Prophetas & viam eorum di- rigit, pro lubitu & voluntate sua, quod huic angelo adscribit. Adhæc permissio illa authentica & ἀὐ- τοκρατορικὴ cum parili instructione conjuncta fuit: Vade cum istis, & vide ne aliud, quam præcepi Tibi, loquaris: quid aliud, quam ipsum Dominum hîc præsentem arguit? Nunquam enim ita Angelus minister cum tanta autoritate ulli Prophetarum lo- quutus est. Jam si conferas verba Angeli hujus cum verbis Bileami versu hoc 35. & 38. & cum nar- ratione Mosis cap. 23, 5. argumentum nascitur invi- ctum ejusmodi: Is qui dedit verba in ore Prophetæ Bileam, & præcepit ei, quid loquatur, est Jehovah: quod e v. 38. hujus capitis manifestum est: Ecce ad- sum; nunquid loqui potero aliud, nisi quod Deus po- suerit in ore meo? & c. XXIII. Dixit Balaam ad Balak: ito paulisper juxta holocaustum tuum, donec vadam, si forte occurrat mihi DOMINUS, & quod- cunque imperaverit, loquar tibi; cumque abiisset ve- lociter, occurrit illi Deus v. 5. DOMINUS enim posuit verbum in ore ejus. Dominus ille, cui sacri- ficium offerebatur, qui certe Angelus creatus esse non potuit: Huic enim, etiamsi personam Domini repræsentare credatur, sacrificium offerre nefas est. Et v. 12. iterum: Num aliud possum loqui, nisi quod jusserit DOMINUS? Rursus v. 16. Cui cum DOMINUS occurrisset posuissetque verbum in ore ejus, ait, Revertere ad Balak: & loqueris hæc ei v. 7. Ad quem Balak: quid, inquit, locutus est DO- MINUS? Similia habentur v. 26. 27. & c. 24, 13. Adde quæ leguntur cap. 24, 1. cum vidisset Balaam quod placeret DOMINO, ut benediceret populo &c. Ideo v. 2. dicitur irruisse in eum Spiritus Dei, & dixisse Balaam: dixit auditor sermonum Dei, qui vi- sionem omnipotentis intuitus est. Cum autem ope- ra & ministerio Angeli Deus aliquid præcepit alicui Prophetarum, nunquam dicitur irruisse spiritus Domini in eum, neque illa de visione omnipotentis, & auditione sermonum ejus angelicæ apparitioni congruunt. Hæc autem repetuntur denuo versu 15. ut adeo ex his omnibus luculentissimum sit, ἀυ- τοπροσώπως & immediate Dominum loquutum es- se Bileamo. Quapropter major illa propositio in- dubia prorsus est & ἀμετακίνητος. Is qui verba in ore Prophetæ Bileam dedit, eique quid loquatur, præcepit, est Jehovah, quum uni atq; soli Jehovæ hoc vindicetur, ac conveniat. Subsumimus nunc: Atqui angelus Domini, qui Bileamo apparuit, est is, qui verba in ore Prophetæ Bileam dedit, eiq; præcepit, quid loqua- tur: quod diferte habetur c. 22, 30. Ait Angelus: Vade cum istis & cave, ne aliud quam præcepero tibi lo- quaris. E. Angelus Domini, qui Bileamo apparuit, est Jehovah. His ita evictis, certum jam est, atque indubitatum, hæc prædicata, simul & Jehovah ipsum esse, & Angelum Domini, nulli alii subjecto convenire, nisi uni & soli Filio DEI, quem & Angelum dici agnoscit Grotius, & Jehovam esse haud diffitetur. Nec vero est, quod cum Calixto indignum quis autumet Filio Dei, occurrere Pseudo - Prophetæ, eidemq; resi- stere. Quoties enim Jehovah sese opposuit Pseudo- Prophetis, iisq; restitit? Num indignum Filio Dei avertere maledictionem a populo, & convertere eam in benedictionem, resistere Diabolo, & organis ejusdem, Verba indere Prophetis, iisdem revelare viam suam, a pravo instituto revocare, bonum e ma- lo elicere, salutemq; populi sui nunquam non pro- vehere, & omnia ad eandem dirigere?

## 23:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIII. Balaam, instead of a curse, blesses and prophesies.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIII. Baleam loco maledictionis benedicit & vatici- natur.

## 23:10
Ver. 10. WHO COULD COUNT THE DUST OF JACOB) That huge multitude. Compare Gen. 13:16, ch. 28:14. The scholiast on the Acharnians of Aristophanes: the word 'psammakosia' was used for a multitude. Eupolis: to count the spectators by the hundreds of thousands.

AND KNOW THE NUMBER OF THE STOCK OF ISRAEL) In the Greek: and who shall number the people of Israel. But the Hebrew text has: And the number of the fourth part of Israel: that is, not only could no one comprehend the number of the whole army, but not even of one division, which is the fourth part of the army. See what is above 10:15.

LET MY SOUL DIE THE DEATH OF THE RIGHTEOUS) That is, a death neither violent nor immature, which was promised to the Israelites who observe the law. Gemara in this place. Yet a deeper mystical sense lies hidden.

Beautifully Bernard, Sermon 7 on Ps. 91. For recall also the false prophet, I mean Balaam, who, though himself wicked, desired the death of the righteous, and prayed that his own last end might be like theirs. So great is the fruit of piety, so great the reward of justice, that it cannot but be desired even by the impious and unjust themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QVIS DINVMERARE POSSET PVLVE- REM JACOB) Ingentem illam multitudinem. Confer Gen. 13, 16. c. 28, 14. Scholiastes ad Acharnenses Aristopha- nis : τὸ ψαμμακόσια ἐπὶ πλήθες ἐτίθετο. Eupolis : ἀριθμεῖν θεατὰς ψαμμακοσίως.

ET NOSSE NVMERVM STIRPIS ISRAEL) In Græ- co : καὶ τίς ἐξαριθμήσεται δήμος Ισραήλ. At Hebræus textus habet : Et numerum quartæ partis Israel: id est, non modo numerum totius exercitus nemo possit comprehendere, sed nec unius vexillationis, quæ pars quarta exercitus. Vide quæ supra 10, 15.

MORIATVR ANIMA MEA MORTE JVSTOVRM) Id est, morte nec violenta, nec immatura, quod Israëlitis promissum, legem observantibus. Gemara h. l. Latet tamen altior sensus mysticus.

Pulchre Bernhardus Serm. 7. in Ps. 91. Nam & Pseudo-Prophetam recolite, Balaam dico, qui ipse ini- quus justorum mortem optabat, & novissima sua horum similia fieri precabatur. Tantus est pietatis fructus, tanta justitiæ merces, ut ne ab ipsis quidem non deside- rari queat impiis & injustis.

## 23:10 Addition
To chapter 23, verse 10, after the end of the notes, at page 543, column b.

However, a double sense is not to be admitted. He desires a blessed death, as Vatablus, Bonfrerius, Tirinus, and Malvenda acknowledge; so that he may become an heir of eternal life with the righteous. It is common for the wicked to wish for themselves the death of the righteous, and not to pursue their life.

Latin:

Ad cap. 23. versu 10. post finem notarum. ad pag. 543. b.

Non autem admittendus geminus sensus. Mortem optat beatam, ut agnoscunt Vatablus, Bon- frerius, Tirinus, Malvenda; ut hæres cum justis fiat æternæ vitæ. Familiare est malis justorum mortem sibi exoptare, vitam non sectari.

## 23:19
Ver. 19. THAT HE SHOULD LIE) That he should change his decrees, whether pure or conditional, once the condition is fulfilled. LXX: to be changed, others: to be shaken: Philo: to be proven false. And perhaps Jude 8:13 looks to this passage, where now 'diaitēthēnai' is read, which perhaps was 'diartēthēnai'. There are four reasons why men do not keep their promises: because they promised deceitfully: or because they repent of the promise: or because something unforeseen happens: or because the matter is beyond their strength. All these are very far from God.

Latin:

Vers. 19. VT MENTIATVR) Vt decreta sua sive pura sive conditionalia, conditione impleta, mutet. LXX. διαρτη- θῆναι, alii σαλευθῆναι: Philo, διαψευσθῆναι. Et forte hunc lo- cum respicit Jud. 8, 13. ubi nunc διαιτηθῆναι legitur, quod for- te fuit διαρτηθῆναι. Quatuor sunt causæ cur homines promis- sis non stent, quia fallaciter promiserunt: aut quia promissi pœnitet : aut quia improvisum quid supervenit : aut quia res est supra vires. Hæc omnia absunt a Deo longissime.

## 23:19 Addition
To Numbers 23:19, towards the end of Grotius's notes, page 543, column b.

That τῷ διαταρτηθῆναι, the scholion which exists in the Roman edition, τῦτ’ ἔσι σαλευθῆναι: τὰ γὰρ κρεμάμενα σαλεύονται, that is, to be agitated, to fluctuate; for those things which are suspended are agitated here and there, and fluctuate. Lactantius, book 18, On True Wisdom, chapter 18, seems to have accepted this properly concerning hanging, when he brings forward the passage as a prophecy concerning Christ being suspended and crucified, concluding from thence that God was to be suspended, yet not as a mere man. But he who has tasted Hebrew with his first lips understands how foreign those things are, in which it is a matter of the truthfulness and constancy of God: God is not a man, that he should lie, etc.

Latin:

Ad Num. 23, 19. sub finem not. Grotii pag. 543. b.

Illud τῷ διαταρτηθῆναι, Scholion quod ex- tat in editione Romana, τῦτ’ ἔσι σαλευθῆναι: τὰ γὰρ κρεμάμενα σαλεύονται, id est, agitari, fluctua- re; ea enim, quæ suspensa sunt, agitantur huc illuc, & fluctuant. Lactantius lib. 18. de vera Sapient. c. 18. videtur id proprie accepisse de suspendio, cum lo- cum ceu vaticinium de Christo suspendendo & cru- cifigendo adducit, inde colligens, Deum suspenden- dum, non tamen ut ψιλὸν ἄνθρωπον. Sed quam aliena illa sint, intelligit, qui primis labris Ebræa degustavit, in quibus de Dei veracitate & constantia agitur, Deus non est vir, ut mentiatur &c.

## 23:21
Ver. 21. THE BLAST OF THE VICTORY OF THE KING IN HIM) Perpetual triumph.

Latin:

Vers. 21. CLANGOR VICTORIÆ REGIS IN ILLO) Triumphus perpetuus.

## 23:28
v. 28. UPON THE TOP OF MOUNT PISGAH.

IN which the idol so named is celebrated, just as the city also received its denomination from the same idol, called Beth-peor, i.e., house or shrine of the idol Peor, Deut. 3:29, ch. 4:46, ch. 34:6, Josh. 13:20. Therefore, the idol did not get its name from the mountain, but the mountain, as well as that shrine, obtained its name from the idol which was worshipped there. However, opinions differ greatly as to what that idol is. Some say that a lord who lived there, called Peor, was numbered among the gods, to which Cocceius in Ps. 106:18 agreed, as did Selden in De Diis Syris, p. 262. Drusius, however, in Hos. 9, p. 130, wishes Baal-Peor to be called Jupiter Phegorius, just as Jupiter is called Olympius or Capitolinus: but in that way the idol would have been named from the mountain, which is less likely. Jerome in his Commentary on Hos. 9 and Book 1 against Jovinian, and Isidore in his Etymologies. Some judge the idol Peor to be Priapus, who, because of the size of his virile member, was translated into the number of the gods by the Greeks and was placed in charge of gardens because of their fertility. But this Moabite idol was far older. Others bring forward other things. It seems safer to suspend judgment, since nothing certain is held about this idol, nor about the origin of this word, except that that minor deity is called by another name, Chemosh, as noted by Jerome in ch. 15 of Isaiah, and that Baal-Peor, according to the same author in his Interpretations of Hebrew Names, is a species of turpitude, and according to Isidore, an image of ignominy, which most derive from פער, to bare, to open: whether because this most shameful minor deity was worshipped by the baring of the anus and the opening and breaking of wind, according to Rashi on Num. 25:3 and Serarius in Minerval, book 3, ch. 4, or because it was accustomed to be worshipped by the baring of the private parts, according to Isidore, Theophylact, Rieber, and others. Whatever it may be concerning that most foul mode of worship, which Selden calls into doubt, the idol was certainly foul and abominable: to whose worship the Israelites were seduced by the Midianite women. Num. 25, 3. Ps. 106, 28. Concerning which L'Empereur reports from the Jerusalem Gemara in Middoth, p. 117, that the daughters of the Midianites, inviting the Israelites, and the invited ones being inflamed with love, did not admit them to intercourse before they warned them, 'Separate yourself from the law of Moses,' and produced the idol Phegor from their bosom, so that worship might be exhibited to it, at least by the uncovering of the private parts. See more in Corn. a Lap. on Num. 25, 3. What the Samaritans have handed down in their books concerning that seduction of the Israelites by the Midianite women can be read in Hottinger in Smegma Orientale, p. 444 et seqq.

Latin:

v. 28. SVPER VERTICEM MONTIS PHOGOR.

IN quo celebratur idolum ita dictum, quemadmo- dum ab eodem idolo urbs etiam denominatio- nem accepit Bethphogor dicta, q. domus vel fanum idoli Phogor Deut. 3, 29. c. 4, 46. c. 34, 6. Jos. 13, 20. Non ergo idolum a monte, sed mons, ut & fanum illud ab idolo, quod ibi colebatur, nomen obtinuit. Quod- nam autem illud idolum sit, valde discrepant sen- tentiæ. Nonnulli Dominum, qui illic habitarit, Peor dictum, in Deorum numerum relatum ajunt, quibus Coccejus in Ps. 106, 18. accessit, ut & Seldenus de diis Syris p. 262. Drusius vero in Hos. 9. p. 130. Baal-Phe- gor Jovem Phegorium, sicut Jupiter Olympius, vel Ca- pitolinus dicitur, vocatum vult : sed ita a monte ido- lum nuncupatum foret, quod minus verosimile est. Hieronymus in Comm. ad Hos. 9. & l. 1. advers. Jovi- nian. & Isidor. in Etym. Idolum Phegor Priapum esse censent, qui ob magnitudinem membri virilis in numerum Deorum translatus a Græcis, hortis ob eorum fœcunditatem præfectus fuit. Sed hoc ido- lum Moabiticum longe antiquius fuit. Alii alia pro- ferunt. Tutius videtur τὸ ἐπέχειν, quum nihil certi de hoc idolo habeatur, neq; de vocis hujus origine, nisi quod Deaster ille Chamos alio nomine dictus, notante Hieronymo in c. 15. Es. quodq; Baal-Phegor, autore eodem in interpp. Ebr. nominum, species sit turpitudinis, & secundum Isidorum simulacrum igno- miniæ, quod a פער nudare, aperire deducunt pleriq;: sive quod nudatione podicis & apertione ac crepitu ventris cultus fuerit hic Deaster turpissimus, juxta Rasche in Num. 25, 3. & Serarium in Minerval. l. 3. c. 4. seu quod coli consueverit pudendorum nudatione juxta Isidorum, Theopyl. Rieber. & alios. Quicquid autem de modo illo cultus foedissimo sit, quem in dubium vocat Seldenus, foedum certe atq; abomi- nabile fuit idolum: ad cujus cultum per mulieres Midianiticas seducti Israelitae sunt. Num. 25, 3. Pfal. 106, 28. Quo de L' Empereur e Gemara Hierosolym. in Middoth. p. 117. refert, quod filiae Midianitarum Israelitas invitantes, invitatosque amore succensos, non prius ad concubitum admiserint, quin monue- rint, separa te a lege Mofis, & e sinu idolum Phegor producerent, ut illi cultus, saltim pudendorum nuda- tione exhiberetur. Plura vid. apud Corn. a Lap. ad Num. 25, 3. Quae Samaritani in libris suis de illa seductione Israelitarum a Midianiticis foeminis fa- cta tradiderint, legi apud Hottingerum possunt in Smegmate Orient. p. 444. seqq.

## 24:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIV.

Balaam's prophecy concerning Christ and his kingdom.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIV.

Bileami de Christo, & regno ejus Prophetia.

## 24:4
Ver. 4. WHOSE EYE IS SHUT) For those who are inspired are alienated from their senses, a good or evil spirit governing them. Iamblichus on the mysteries of the Egyptians, section 2, chapter 24. B. Luther expressed the Hebrew more correctly: 'the man whose eyes are opened.' Namely, the eyes of the heart, Eph. 1, 17. 18. c. 3, 18. 19. Ver. 6. AS THE VALLEYS. Others prefer to render the word כאהלים based on the punctuation as 'like sandalwood.' Which is the name of a tree. Cf. Salmas. in Sol. Polyh. p. 1032. Ver. 7. HE SHALL BE TAKEN BECAUSE OF AGAG HIS KING, AND HIS KINGDOM SHALL BE TAKEN AWAY) Better in the Hebrew: 'His King shall be exalted above Agag, and his kingdom shall be lifted up.' Agag is the name of the Kings of the Amalekites. See the fulfillment 1 Sam. 15, 8. The LXX and Symmachus read מגוג instead of מֹאגג. For they have, 'his kingdom shall be exalted above Gog.' Symmachus is closer to the Hebrew: 'his king shall be exalted above Gog.' But what is read in the Hebrew is truer. The LXX seem to have understood it of the Messiah. and Mr. Varenius also explains it of him, calling him the imperial star. Ver. 14. GOING TO MY PEOPLE) Before I return to Mesopotamia. But the Gemara says to Gehenna, with little probability. Ver. 17. I SHALL SEE HIM, BUT NOT NOW) More correctly: 'I see him, but not so now.' Him, that is, his great things: namely, of the Israelite people. Ver. same. A STAR OUT OF JACOB) Illustrious men are called stars. Ver. same. AND A ROD SHALL ARISE OUT OF ISRAEL) In the Hebrew שבט, that is, a scepter, as Gen 49, 10. The Chaldean rightly interprets it as King. David is designated, illustrious among Kings, who partly killed the Moabites and partly subjected them to himself. 2 Sam. 8, 2. See also Psalm 60, 10. 108, 10. Maimonides also interprets it mystically of the Messiah, whose total victory all ancient victories shadowed forth. Ver. same. AND SHALL DESTROY ALL THE CHILDREN OF SETH) Nothing is more likely than that Seth was the name of some excellent king among the Moabites. Ver. 20. TAKING UP HIS PARABLE) Speaking apophthegmatically. Ver. same. WHOSE LATTER END SHALL BE) In the Hebrew: 'his latter end unto destruction.' Which the LXX rightly interpret: 'their seed shall perish.' It excelled for a long time among the neighboring nations: but the time will come when it will be given to destruction: that was fulfilled 1 Sam. 15, 7. Cf. the prophecy Exod. 17, 14. Ver. 21. THE KENITE) The Chaldean says Salmaean. See above Genesis 15, 19. From here was Jethro, whose relatives joined themselves to the Israelites. Jud. 1, 18. 4, 11. 1 Sam. 15, 6. Ver. same. THY NEST) קנך is an allusion to the name of the Kenite. Ver. 23. AND HAVING TAKEN UP HIS PARABLE) The Greeks read more here. For they prefix, 'and seeing Og,' that is, beholding the kingdom of Bashan. See above 21, 33.

Not only mystically, but according to the literal sense, the Messiah is promised here. The names teach this: the name STAR is nowhere attributed to David, because it is attributed to the Messiah. Rev. 22, 16, he is called ὁ ἀστὴρ ὁ λαμπρὸς καὶ ὀρθρινὸς, the bright and morning star, which seems to be deduced from the words of Balaam. Concerning which let Origen, hom. 13 on Num., be read. And 2 Pet. 1, 19 he is called Φωσφορος, the Day Star, which rises in our hearts: when he illuminates us with the light of faith, grace, and salvation: whose Deity is also designated by the word star, as he is according to which he is the 'brightness of the glory of God' Heb. 1, 3, and the 'dayspring from on high' Luke 1, 78. Cf. Zech. 6, 12, and his office, which is to illuminate those sitting in darkness Isa. 9, 1, indeed all men John 1, 9. Who therefore deigned to be manifested under his rising in the lower hemisphere of this world, with a new star assisting, Matt. 2, 2, which some of the Ancients believed to have been designated by this appellation also. The name שבט designates by way of excellence the Scepter out of Israel as unique, which has had nothing similar to itself; which therefore the Chaldean explained concerning the King Messiah; 'and a king shall arise from Jacob and the Messiah shall be magnified from Israel.' The name of Scepter is common, and is attributed to all the Kings of Judah Gen. 49, 16. Since therefore the kingdom is claimed for this star out of Jacob in a unique way, for that reason, not that it is common to any other, but that it belongs to him most singularly; it is manifest that not David, but rather the Messiah is to be understood. He is called absolutely the RULER to come out of Jacob, just as the Messiah is said to be the Ruler to come out of Bethlehem Mic. 5, 2. Which name is proper to Christ in a peculiar and eminent way; who therefore is also commonly indicated by the name Lord in the N.T. The victories predicted against the enemies concerning this King confirm that. For did David so strike the Princes of the Moabites and ALL the children of Seth, and destroy them utterly? Was all Idumea his inheritance and possession? Did David also destroy the remaining cities, and how? Which things, if they are taken together especially, were not fulfilled in David as all these things are predicted here: But that they were fulfilled in Christ most eminently, in that sense which he insinuated to Balaam under allegorical words and in the manner customary to the Prophets according to the mind and intention of the Holy Spirit, one cannot doubt. For by the Moabites are designated here the idolaters, whom Christ struck down along with their leaders, the devils: by the sons of Seth the Jews, whom David did not lay waste: but Christ, when they rendered themselves unworthy of His kingdom, laid waste and rejected them. By the Edomites, descended from Esau and inhabiting the mountains of Seir, are figured all the nations, which have been made a possession for the Messiah and His Christians, not for David. By the remaining cities, and the persecutors of the Church, which is called the city of God, and false brethren, and the impious in the assembly of the Church, especially the man of perdition with his retinue is denoted. All of whom the Messiah destroys partly by the sword of His mouth in this age Is. 11, 4. 2 Thess. 2, 8. partly by the brightness of His coming, and by extreme punishment in the other age, when they are to pay the penalty of eternal destruction from the face of the Lord and the glory of His power 2 Thess. 1, 9. Add that similar things are hinted at concerning the power of His scepter and the breaking of His enemies Ps. 2, 9. Ps. 110, 2. seqq. Is. 11, 4. Rev. 2, 27. ch. 19, 15. etc. To this also pertains that the kingdom of Christ is predicted to destroy all kingdoms Dan. 2, 44. Balaam intimated this eternal kingdom, which is never to be dissipated; but that it will dissipate the others. Furthermore, the victory of Israel predicted here also confirms this: namely, that Israel, all the faithful and pious, shall act bravely against their enemies, and shall overcome them: of which victory scarcely even a shadow was found in the bodily victories of David. 2 Sam. 8, 2. 24. Ps. 60, 10. For the faithful, who are called the Israel of God, conquer all their enemies—the devil, death, sin, and the world itself. Gal. 6, 16. Eph. 6, 13. John 5, 4. 1 Cor. 15, 57. To which is added also the scope of the whole history, namely that the Israelite people were here to be blessed by Balaam, instead of cursed. c. 23, 8. 20. Behold, I am brought to bless, and I cannot hold back the blessing. c. 24, 9. He who blesses you shall himself be blessed. He who curses you shall be reckoned in a curse. For it is not credible, since the Son of God Himself met Balaam and directed his way, and the individual words of the blessing look toward the promise of the Messiah, in whom the Israelites, and indeed all the nations of the earth, are uniquely blessed, Gen. 12, 3. Gal. 3, 14. Eph. 1, 3. that they were here recalled to that one fountain of blessing, according to the custom familiar to the Holy Spirit; especially because this hearer of the words of God, who knew the doctrine of the Most High and had visions of the Almighty, prophesies about those things which were to happen in later times, and which the prophets especially desired to see; I SHALL SEE him, but NOT NOW, I shall behold him, but not near. For who is he, whom the ancients so greatly desired to see, except Christ? Luke 10, 23. 24. John 8, 57. 1 Pet. 1, 10. 11. Whom Balaam can be said to have seen in his descendants, namely in the Magi from the East who were led to the manger of the Lord, Matt. 2. Naturally, the enemies of the Church were to be reminded of its perpetual defender; but the exiles and those wandering in the wilderness, the Jacobites, were to be raised up and led into the most certain hope of perfect liberation, even through this wicked man who had intended to curse them. Whence the ancients, whose tradition Grotius holds as a rule for the interpretation of Scripture—which it is certainly not right to neglect rashly—have explained this oracle concerning Christ: Justin Martyr, Apol. II for the Christians, p. 57. A bright star has indeed arisen out of Jacob, and a flower has ascended from the root of Jesse, our Christ. And Dial. with Trypho, p. 261. And that he himself would arise as a star from the race of Abraham, Moses declared in passing, saying thus: A star shall rise out of Jacob and a leader out of Israel. And another Scripture says: (Zech. VI,) Behold the Man, whose name is the Rising: Indeed, as soon as he was born, a star arose in the heavens, from which the Arab Magi were taught, and they came and worshipped him. Cyprian on the Star and the Magi: These (Magi) heard long ago from the prophecies of Balaam that a star would rise in Jacob, and a man in Israel, whose strength is as that of a rhinoceros, to whom those would come in ships from Italy, who would overcome the Assyrians and lay waste the Hebrews, at which time there would be neither idol in Jacob nor image in Israel. For a long time those men awaited the outcome of this prophecy, and when the fullness of time came, with a new star suddenly risen, recurring to ancient volumes, they arrived in Judea, fortified as much by testimony as by the sign, carried by dromedaries, with the star as their guide. Theodoret rebukes those who in his own age interpreted them otherwise. Quest. 45 on Numbers. Nor yet should it be ignored that it pleased some that he predicted nothing about our Savior, who certainly ought to have understood that the coming of God and our Savior was revealed even to Nebuchadnezzar himself, however impious. 2.) He, therefore, who foretold these things through him, also announced the salvation of the world through this one, so that such announcements might be preserved even among the nations. See also Athanas. de incarnat. verb. DEI T. I. Oper. pag. m. 86. Basilius M. T. I. Oper. orat. de hum. Christi gener. pag. 510. Ambrosius in Luc. 2. Hieronymus in Matth. 2. Augustinus Serm. CIII. de Tempore.

Maximus, Sermon 3 on the Epiphany. Leo the Great, Sermon IV, etc. Many of the ancients among the Jews themselves also interpreted the oracle concerning the Messiah, along with the Chaldean Paraphrase. The author of the Fasciculus Myrrhae observed that by the word כוכב (star), the tetragrammaton name יהוה is signified cabalistically, in that the first letters of the Hebrew word כ and ו are constituted in the number 26, which the letters of the divine name make. The value of the later כ and כ in numbers is 22, which is the number of letters in the alphabet, so that it may be designated that the whole law of God is to be perfectly fulfilled in the times of the Messiah. R. Solomon compares here Ps. 72 concerning the dominion of King Messiah, and understands this oracle to be about the same. R. Moses Hadarschan in Gen. 49, 10. This is, he says, what Balaam says: And a star has gone forth out of Jacob. And when will this prophecy be completed? When Shiloh comes, that is, King Messiah. Which interpretations explain the oracle concerning the Messiah not only in a mystical sense, but in a literal one. In order to obscure this, Grotius feigns that the words, I shall see him, but not now, are to be taken thus: I see him, but not at that time: Him, that is, his great things, namely of the Israelite people: but that these are to be understood of that King who was to arise out of Jacob is too manifest. But what is said about the sons of Seth, he explains as the sons of some Moabite king, whom he affirms, without any document or witness, to have been named Seth. Almost all the Fathers take it as Seth the son of Adam, as do the LXX, R. Solomon, R. Aben-Ezra, the Vulgate, Vatablus, Luther, and others. The Chaldean explained it as he shall have dominion over all the sons of men, which fits the Messiah alone. See another interpretation in the later edition of Junius. Moreover, the words themselves, I shall see him, but not now, I shall behold him, but not near, teach that Balaam looked not so much to the nearer as to the most remote times. And since Grotius explains the later things as referring to more remote times, namely the times of Alexander the Great and the Roman Empire, why does he now drag these things, which Balaam begins with that preface that they are NOT NOW to happen, and are NOT NEAR, to the times of David? For these things, which Balaam predicted most recently, v. 23, 24, Alas, who shall live when the Lord does these things? They shall come in triremes from Italy, they shall overcome the Assyrians, and they shall lay waste the Hebrews, and in the end they themselves shall perish; thus Grotius has interpreted it:

Latin:

Vers. 4. CVJVS OBTVRATVS EST OCVLVS) Nam afflati abalienantur a sensibus, spiritu bono aut malo eos gubernan- re. Jamblichus de mysteriis Aegyptiorum, segmento 2. cap. 24. EBræum rectius expressit B. Luther. der Mann, dem die Augen geöffnet seyn. Oculi nempe cordis Eph. 1, 17. 18. c. 3, 18. 19. vers. 6. SICUT TEXTORIA. Vocem כאהלים ex punctatione alii malunt reddere sicut Santalos. Quod nomen arboris. Conf. Salmas. in Sol. Polyh. p. 1032. Vers. 7. TOLLETVR PROPTER AGAG REX EJVS, ET AVFERETVR REGNVM ILLIVS) Melius in Hebræo: Exaltabitur prae Agag Rex ejus, & elevabitur ejus regnum. Agag nomen Regum Amalecitarum. Implementum vide 1. Sam. 15, 8. LXX. & Symmachus pro מֹאגג legerunt מגוג. Habent enim illi, ὑψωθήσεται ἡ Γὼγ βασιλεία. Symmachus propius ad Hebr. ὑψωθήσεται ὑπὲρ Γὼγ βασιλεὺς ἀυτẽ. Sed verius quod in Hebræo legitur. De Messia intellexisse videntur LXX. & de il- lo explicat quoque Dn. Varenius, eum stellam im- perialem vocans. Vers. 14. PERGENS AD POPVLVM MEVM) Priusquam rede- am in Mesopotamiam. At Gemara ad gehennam, parum probabiliter. Vers. 17. VIDEBO EVM, SED NON MODO) Rectius: Video eum, sed non tam modo. Eum, id est, res ejus magnas: Israeliti- ci scilicet populi. Vers. eod. STELLA EX JACOB) Sidera vocantur Viri illustres. Vers. eod. ET CONSVRGET VIRGA DE ISRAEL) In Hebræo שבט, id est, sceptrum, ut Gen 49, 10. Regem bene interpre- tatur Chaldæus. David designatur, illustris inter Reges, qui Moabitas partim interfecit, partim sibi subjecit. 2. Sam. 8, 2. vide & Pfalm. 60, 10. 108, 10. Mystice de Messia interpre- tatur & Maimonides, cujus summam victoriam omnes vete- res victoriae adumbrarunt. Vers. eod. VASTABITQVE OMNES FILIOS SETH) Nihil vero propius quam Seth nominatum fuisse regem aliquem eximi- um inter Moabitas. Vers. 20. ASSVMENS PARABOLAM) Loquens ἀπο- φθεγματικῶς. Vers. eod. CVJVS EXTREMA PERDENTVR) In He- bræo: ultima ejus ad exitium. Quod recte interpretantur LXX. τὸ σπέρμα ἀυτῶν ἀπολεῖται. Excelluit diu inter vici- nas gentes: sed veniet tempus cum exitio dabitur: Impletum id 1. Sam. 15, 7. Conf. Vaticinium Exod. 17, 14. Vers. 21. CINÆVM) Salmæum Chaldæus. Vide supra Ge- nefeos 15, 19. Hinc fuit Jethro, cujus propinqui Israelitis se adjunxere. Jud. 1, 18. 4, 11. 1. Sam. 15, 6. V. eod. NIDVM TVVM) קנך allusio ad nomen Cinæi. Vers. 23. ASSVMPTAQVE PARABOLA) Plus hîc le- gere Græci. Præmittunt enim, καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ὠγ, id est, con- spiciens regnum Basan. Vide supra 21, 33.

Non mystice tantum, sed juxta sensum literalem hic promissus est Messias. Docent id nomina: STELLÆ nomen nuspiam Davidi attributum est, quia Messiæ id tribuitur. Apoc. 22, 16. ὁ ἀστὴρ ὁ λαμ- πρὸς καὶ ὀρθρινὸς dicitur, stella splendida & matu- tina, quod ex verbis Bileami deductum videtur. Quo de legatur Origenes hom. 13. in Num. Et 2. Pet. 1, 19. dicitur Φωσφορος Lucifer, qui exoritur in cor- dibus nostris: cum nos luce fidei, gratiæ & salutis collustrat: cujus & Deitas voce stellæ designatur, utpote secundum quam est ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης Θεῦ Ebr. 1, 3. & oriens ex alto Luc. 1, 78. Conf. Zach. 6, 12. & officium, quod est illuminare sedentes in tenebris Esa. 9, 1. imo omnes homines Job. 1, 9. Qui proin- de sub exortum suum in hemisphærio inferiori hu- jus mundi, stella nova adminiculante, manifestari dignatus est Matth. 2, 2. quod hac appellatione etiam designatum fuisse, nonnulli Veterum crediderunt. Nomen שבט κατ᾽ ἐξοχὴν Sceptrum ex Israele mo- nadicum, quod simile sibi non habuerit, designat; quod proinde de Rege Messia explicavit Chal- dæus; וקים מלכא מיעקב ויתרבא משיחא מישראל. Nomen Sceptri commu- ne est, & omnibus Regibus Judæ tribuitur Gen. 49, 16. Cum ergo huic stellæ ex Jacob μονοτρόπως vindicetur regnum, ea se. ratione, non quæ commu- nis sit alii ulli, sed singularissime ipsi conveniat; ma- nifestum est, non Davidem, sed Messiam potius in- telligendum esse. Vocatur absolute DOMINA- TOR e Jacob proditurus, perinde uti Messias Domi- nator e Bethlehem proditurus dicitur Mich. 5, 2. Quod nomen Christo peculiariter & eminenti ratione proprium est; qui proinde nomine κυρίῳ commu- niter etiam in N. T. indigitatur. Confirmant id victoriæ adversus hostes de Rege hoc prædictæ. Num enim ita David Principes Moabitarum & O- MNES filios Seth percussit, & vastavit penitus? Num universa Idumæa hæreditas ejus & possessio fuit? Num & quomodo reliquas civitates perdidit David? Quæ profecto si conjunctim imprimis ac- cipiantur, in Davide ita impleta non sunt, prout hic prædicuntur omnia: At in Christo eminentissime completa esse, eo sensu, quem sub verbis allegori- cis, moreque Prophetis usitato juxta mentem & in- tentionem Spiritus Sancti insinuavit Bileamo, dubi- tare non licet. Per Moabitas enim designantur hic idololatræ, quos cum ducibus suis diabolis percuf- sit Christus: per filios Seth Judæi, quos non vastavit David: Christus vero quum indignos seipsos red- derent regno suo, vastavit & reprobavit. Per E- domitas ab Esau oriundos & habitantes in montibus Seir figurantur gentes omnes, quæ factæ sunt Messiæ & Christianis suis inimicis possessio, non Davidi. Per reliquas civitates, & Ecclesiæ, quæ civitas Dei voca- tur, persequutores, falsique fratres, & impii in Ec- clesiæ cœtu, imprimis homo perditionis cum suo sa- tellitio denotatur. Quos omnes perdit Messias partim gladio oris sui in hoc seculo Ef. 11, 4. 2. Thess. 2, 8. partim illustratione adventus sui, & extremo sup- plicio in seculo altero, cum pœnas daturi sunt in inte- ritu æternas a facie Domini & gloria virtutis ejus 2. Thess. 1, 9. Adde, quod de virtute sceptri ejus & confractione similia hostium innuantur Psal. 2, 9. Ps. 110, 2. seqq. Ef. 11, 4. Ap. 2, 27. c. 19, 15. &c. Quo etiam facit, quod regnum Christi universa regna perditu- rum prædicatur Dan. 2, 44. Regnum hoc æternum intimavit Bileam, quod nunquam dissipandum; cæ- tera vero dissipaturum sit. Porro confirmat hoc quoque victoria Israelis hic prædicta: quod nempe Is- rael, fideles ac pii quiq; fortiter acturi sint contra ho- stes, eosq; devicturi: cujus victoriæ vix umbra solum quædam in Davidis fuit corporalibus victoriis. 2. Sam. 8, 2. 24. Pf. 60, 10. Univerfos enim hoftes fuos, diabolum, mortem, peccatum, mundum ipfum fideles vincunt, qui Ifrael Dei dicuntur Gal. 6, 16. Eph. 6, 13. Joh. 5, 4. 1. Cor. 15, 57. Quibus accedit etiam fcopus totius hiftoriæ, quod nempe populus Ifraeliticus a Bileamo hic, loco maledictionis, benedici debuerit c. 23, 8. 20. Ecce ad benedicendum adductus sum, & benedictionem prohibere non valeo. c. 24, 9. Qui benedixerit tibi, erit & ipfe benedictus. Qui maledixerit, in maledictione reputabitur. Non enim credibile eft, cum ipfe Filius DEI obviam factus Bileamo fuerit, viamque ejus direxerit, ac verba fingula benedictionis promiffionem Meffiæ refpiciant, in quo Ifraelitæ, imo omnes nationes terræ benedicuntur unice Gen. 12, 3. Gal. 3, 14. Eph. 1, 3. quin ad fontem illum unicum benedictionis, more Spiritui Sancto confueto, revocati hic fuerint; maxime quia auditor hic fermonum Dei, qui novit doctrinam altiffimi & vifiones omnipotentis habebat, de iis vaticinatur, quæ pofterioribus temporibus eventura erant, quæque videre imprimis defiderabant Prophetæ; VIDEBO eum, fed NON MODO, intuebor illum, fed non prope. Quis enim ille eft, quem tantopere defiderarunt videre Veteres, præter Chriftum Luc. 10, 23. 24. Joh. 8, 57. 1. Pet. 1, 10. 11. Quem vidiffe Bileam in pofteris fuis dici poteft, nempe in Magis ex Oriente ad præfepe Domini perductis Matth. 2. Nimirum commonefieri debebant hoftes Ecclefiæ de perpetuo ejus promacho; exules vero & in folitudine errantes Jacobitæ erigendi erant, & in fpem certiffimam perfectæ liberationis, etiam per hunc nefarium hominem, qui maledicere illis inftituerat, perducendi. Unde magno confenfu Veteres, quorum traditionem pro regula interpretationis Scripturæ habet Grotius, temere certe negligere fas non eft, de Chrifto hoc oraculum expofuere : Juftinus Martyr Apol. II. pro Chriftian. p. 57. Stella fane lucida ex Jacob exorta est, & flos adfcendit e radice Jeffe, Chriftus noster. Et Dial. cum Tryph. p. 261. Et quod tanquam astrum exorturus fuerit ipse idem ex genere Abrahæ, Mofes obiter declaravit, ita dicens: Orietur ftella ex Jacob & dux ex Ifraele. Et alia Scriptura inquit: (Zach. VI,) Ecce Vir, oriens nomen ejus: Enimvero ftella, fimulatque natus est, in cœlo exorta, Magi Arabes unde edocti, affuerunt & adoraverunt illum. Cyprianus de Stella & Magis: Hi (Magi) ex vaticiniis Balaam olim audierunt, stellam oriri in Jacob, & hominem in Ifrael, cujus fortitudo quafi Rhinocerotis, ad quam in turribus de Italia venirent, qui superarent Assyrios, & vastarent Hebræos, quo tempore nec in Jacob idolum, nec in Ifrael simulacrum effet. Diu homines illi hujus prophetiæ proventum expectarunt, & ubi venit plenitudo temporis, orto repente novo fidere, ad antiqua recurrentes volumina tam testimonio muniti, quam figno, dromadis invecti in in Judæam, ftella duce, perveniunt. Theodorethus reprehendit illos, qui fua jam ætate fecus interpretabantur. Quæft. 45. in Numer. Nec tamen ignorandum est quibus dam placuiffe, nihil illum prædixiffe de Salvatore nostro, qui utique debuerunt intelligere ipfi quoque Nebucadnezari licet impiiffimo, adventum Dei ac Salvatoris nostri revelatum effe. (Dan. 2.) Qui igitur per illum ista prædixit, per hunc etiam Salutem orbis prænuntiavit, ut & apud gentes hujusmodi prænunciationes confervarentur. Vid. etiam Athanas. de incarnat. verb. DEI T. I. Oper. pag. m. 86. Bafilius M. T. I. Oper. orat. de hum. Chrifti gener. pag. 510. Ambrofius in Luc. 2. Hieronymus in Matth. 2. Augustinus Serm. CIII. de Tempore.

Maximus Serm. 3. de Epiphan. Leo M. serm. IV. &c. E Judæis etiam ipsis plerique Veteres de Messia ora- culum interpretati sunt, cum Chaldaica Paraphrasi. Autor fasciculi Myrrhæ per כוכב stellam observavit significari Cabalistice nomen tetragrammaton יהוה primis literis vocabuli Ebraici כ & ו 26. in numero constitui, quot efficiunt literæ nominis divini. Posteriorum autem כ & כ valorem in nu- meris esse 22. quot literæ sunt Alphabeti, ut designe- tur, totam Dei legem temporibus Messiæ perfecte im- plendam. R. Salomo consert hic Ps. 72. de dominio Regis Messiæ, ac de eodem oraculum hoc intelligit. R. Moses Hadarschan in Gen. 49, 10. Hoc est, inquit, quod ait Balaam: Et egressa est stella ex Jacob. Et quando complebitur Prophetia hæc? Cum veniet Silo, id est, Rex Messias. Quæ interpretationes non tan- tum sensu mystico, sed literali oraculum de Messia exponunt. Quod ut obscuret Grotius, fingit ver- ba, videbo eum, sed non modo, ita accipienda esse: Video eum, sed non tum modo: Eum, id est, res ejus magnas, Israelitici sc. populi: quæ vero intelligenda esse de Rege illo, qui ex Jacob exoriturus erat, nimis manifestum est. Quæ autem de Filiis Seth dicun- tur, exponit de filiis regis alicujus Moabitici, quem Seth nominatum fuisse, sine ullo documento, vel teste affirmat. De Seth filio Adam omnes pene Pa- tres accipiunt, ut & LXX. R. Salomo, R. Aben-Ezra. Vulgata. Vatablus, Lutherus, & alii. Chaldæus ex- posuit dominabitur in omnes filios hominum, quod Messiæ uni convenit. Aliam interpretationem vid. in posteriori edit. Junian. Cæterum non tam ad propiora, quam remotissima tempora respexisse Bileamum, verba ipsa, videbo eum, sed non modo, in- tuebor illum, sed non prope, edocent. Et quum de remotioribus posteriora explicet Grotius, nempe de Alexandri M. & Romani Imperii temporibus, cur nunc hæc, quæ cum illa præfatione, quod NON MO- DO eventura sint, NON PROPE sint, orditur Bile- am, ad tempora Davidis trahit? Hæc enim, quæ no- vissime prædixit Bileam, v. 23. 24. Heu quis victu- rus est, quando ista faciet Dominus? venient in trieri- bus de Italia, superabunt Assyrios, vastabuntq; Ebræos, & ad extremum etiam ipsi peribunt; sic interpretatus est Grotius:

## 24:17 Addition
To Numbers 24, verse 17, at page 544, column a.

By the sons of Seth, Münster, Fagius, Vatablus, Drusius, Ainsworth, Bonfrerius, and Menochius understand all men; but because the Messiah was not to eradicate all men, or destroy all peoples, and this prophecy is concerning a certain kind of men under the name of Moabites, Edomites, and Amalekites, it is not indeed a people bordering on the Jews, or the Canaanites, as Oleastrius wishes, but the Jewish people themselves are understood, for whom destruction was often predicted to be future in the time of the Messiah.

Latin:

Ad Num. 24. vers. 17. ad pag. 544. a.

Per filios Sethi omnes homines intelligit Mün- sterus, Fagius, Vatablus, Drusius, Ainsworthus, Bon- frerius, Menochius; sed quia non eradicare omnes homines debuit Messias, aut omnes populos de- struere, & de certo genere hominum sub nomine Moabitarum, Edomitarum, & Amalekitarum hic va- ticinium est, non quidem populus Judæis finitimus, aut Cananæi, ut Oleastrius vult, sed ipse populus Ju- daicus intelligitur, cui sæpius excidium tempore Messsiæ futurum prædictum fuit.

## 24:18
Ver. 18. AND EDOM SHALL BE HIS POSSESSION) The same thing predicted 25. 6. 3. See the fulfillment 2 Kings 8. 6. 14.

Not at that time, but toward the coming of the Messiah, that it was fulfilled and that the prophecy and the context of the prophecy and the historical fulfillment sufficiently teach that it pertains to that.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET ERIT IDVMÆA POSSESSIO EJVS) Ea- dem res prædicta 25. 6. 3. Implementum vide 2. Reg. 8. 6. 14.

Non isto tempore, sed sub adventum Messiæ illa impleta esse eoq; pertinere prophetiam collatio & contextus prophetiæ, & complementi historici fatis docet.

## 24:22
Ver. 22. AND THOU SHALT BE TAKEN CAPTIVE BY THE KIN) Who is the prince of the race; the Hebrews wrongly read Kain. The Latin reads לבעיר not בחור. But the LXX read כי אם יהוה לבער קן ערמה. For they translate καὶ ἐὰν γένηται τῷ Βεὼρ νοσσιὰ πανουργίας. The sense in the Hebrew is: Nevertheless, the Kenite shall be for burning. That people will gradually be diminished until it is carried away with the Israelites. Now in the time of Saul it appears their affairs were modest 1 Sam. 15. ver. 6.

He wrongly corrects the Hebrew text: since all the Codices agree. But why could not the prince of the Kenites be called קין, just as the fratricide was once called?

Latin:

Vers. 22. ET FVERIS ELECTVS DE STIRPE CIN) Qui princeps generis; male Kain legunt Hebræi. Legit Lati- nus לבעיר non בחור. At LXX. legerunt כי אם יהוה לבער קן ערמה. Vertunt enim καὶ ἐὰν γένηται τῷ Βεὼρ νοσσιὰ πανουργίας. Sensus in Hebræo est: Attamen erit Cin depastui. Paulatim imminuetur is populus donec cum Israë- litis avehatur. Jam tempore Saulis apparet modicas fuisse eorum res 1. Sam. 15. vers. 6.

Male corrigit textum Ebræum: quum conso- nent omnes Codices. Quidni vero princeps Ke- neorum קין vocari potuit, uti fratricida olim voca- tus est?

## 24:23
WHO SHALL LIVE) How great will the slaughter be then?

Latin:

QVIS VICTVRVS EST) Quanta tunc erit inter- necio?

## 24:24
Vers. 24. THEY SHALL COME FROM THE SHIPS) By the word כתים were first meant the Cypriots, among whom was Citium, a Phoenician colony: and from them all the Greeks: And so Alexander is said to have been ἐκ τῆς γῆς χεττίιμ 1 Macc. 1, 1. who is the King of יון, that is, of the Greeks to Daniel. These, however, are they who subdued both the Assyrians and their successors the Medes and Persians with their arms, having crossed the Hellespont.

AND THEY SHALL AFFLICT THE HEBREWS( עבר, which signifies those who are across the river. Understand the river Euphrates. The arms of the Macedonians or Greeks will also cross the Euphrates. And that this pertains to Alexander, everyone sees.

Thus Grotius. Although he does not limit this prophecy to the time of Alexander the Great, but extends it to the times of Titus Vespasian, when the Cittaei of Italy afflicted the Hebrews. For עבר here denotes the Hebrew nation just as אשור does: and according to the Chaldean and the Rabbis themselves, the Romans are understood by Cittim: as also B. Luther. Cittim are those from Europe, like Alexander the Great, who also finally perish. Compare Genesis 10, 4. Add to these the things which follow in the same verse in Grotius.

AND AT THE LAST THEY ALSO SHALL PERISH) The Greeks: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἀπολοῦνται. In the Hebrew: And he himself also shall go into destruction, supply, he will go. The sense is that Macedonia, that conqueror of nations, together with all of Greece, will succumb to the arms of the Romans.

Since, therefore, as Grotius admits, what is predicted here is not only the destruction of the Amalekites and Kenites, but also of the greatest empires, the Assyrian and the Greek, the perpetual kingdom of the Messiah is aptly contrasted with the perishable empires of the world, as in the similar prophecy of Daniel, Dan. 2. The sense is, according to the interpretation of Pelargus, that the Assyrians, Persians, and Medes will be destroyed by the Greeks; and the Jewish nation, and finally the Romans themselves, will be destroyed by the Romans; and that the kingdom of Christ alone will remain forever. The prophecy of Daniel, ch. 2, 44, ch. 7, 14, agrees exactly with these. Cf. Micah 4, 7. Luke 1, 33. Most interpreters agree on this, from whom we are loath to depart for the sake of the Grotius commentaries.

V. same. THEY SHALL COME IN SHIPS FROM ITALY, THEY SHALL OVERCOME THE ASSYRIANS, AND THEY SHALL LAY WASTE THE HEBREWS, AND IN THE END THEY THEMSELVES SHALL PERISH.

Coccejus, Ult. Mos. § 1267. He says that Balaam, Num. 24, 24, connects in a summary the greatest matters, which were to precede the end of the age, and links the order of the whole prophecy, divided into certain articles, in one series; the first of these articles is the subjection of the Assyrians by ships coming near the Chittim; from the west, that is, the subjection of the Persians by the Greeks, which was the occasion for the liberty of the Hebrews, and for occupying Edom as an inheritance and Seir, their enemies, and for acting strenuously, at which time he who was to rule from Jacob would rule, who destroys the survivor from the city, that is, the Son of GOD, who at that point in time was to establish his kingdom, see v. 18 and 19. The second article is the subjection of Eber, or the Hebrews; likewise by ships coming from the side of the Chittim, that is, by the armies of the westerners invading Palestine through and along Asia Minor, understand the Romans. This article brings the end of the Republic of the Hebrews, but it does not take away the kingdom of him who rules from Jacob, or Christ; rather, it frees that kingdom, diffused through the whole world, from the yoke. The third is the destruction of that one too. Even he, he says, to destruction. Truly the empire that was sending ships along the Chittim into Assyria and Eber. Above, v. 19, he had said that He who was to rule from Jacob would destroy the survivor from the city. Whence it is to be gathered that the city that would oppress Eber, the city that would have dominion over the kings of the earth, the city that would suffer its own turns, and finally be established in the survivor, would eventually also yield this to the kingdom of Christ, and be abolished by him. Cf. 2 Thess. 2, 8. Rev. 17, 11. 18, 21. Dan. 2, 44. ch. 7, 24 (where the survivor of the city is the little horn) 25, 26, 27. These things having been done, it remains that he who rules from Jacob, or the scepter rising from Israel (still gathered in the polity), should destroy all the sons of Seth, i.e. all men, who are all from Seth through Noah, and thus prostrate all flesh by death or transformation at his glorious coming. Which Balaam says in v. 17. Which coincides with the absolute inflammation of the foundations of the mountains. These are the words of Coccejus. The same, § 271, makes the exaltation of the Republic of the Hebrews in the subjugation of the neighboring nations and the kingdom of the Priests the immediate circumstance of the revelation of the kingdom of Christ from this prophecy of Balaam, v. 18, 19. And Edom shall be an inheritance, and Seir shall be an inheritance for his enemies, and Israel shall act strenuously; then (someone) shall rule from Jacob, and shall destroy the survivor from the city, that is, then the kingdom of Christ will begin, which will conflict with the kingdoms of the nations, so that neither the city of Jerusalem, nor the city of Rome and great Babylon, can stand before it. The fulfillment [is] especially after the death of Antiochus Pius, see Josephus, b. 13, ch. 17, and following. We add what he has in § 1462, Num. 24, 19. And (absolutely) someone shall rule from Jacob, and shall destroy the survivor from the city. The kingdom of Christ will proceed so far that no opposing kingdom shall stand before it. I know it can be said that at the last judgment every opposing kingdom will be removed, but (1) this is said distinctly by Balaam through the overthrow of all the sons of Seth. (2) Compared with other passages, as this one of ours, it is understood by the dominion which Christ exercises in the world through the Gospel, that every survivor must be taken from the city. These are his words. It is to be praised that he understands v. 17 of Christ, not with Junius of the kingdom of the people of God begun in David, completed in Christ. Although from those things which are handed down in v. 23, when compared with these, it appears that he takes the earlier words of v. 17 of the Kingdom of David itself. For thus it is there: a star shall proceed from Jacob, and shall strike the corners of Moab, the Kingdom of David. The rest smack of a private interpretation, because (1) it separates the destruction of all the sons of Seth and the possession of Edom, which the text joins, by such a long interval that the latter precedes the first coming of Christ, and the former is to be referred to the second coming, (2) by sons of Seth he understands all men: the sons of Seth or of the rear part by reason of Balaam's location, the Ammonites, Midianites, and other Orientals as far as the Euphrates, from Isa. 20, 4, or the sons of the siege, pressing the Israelites with a perpetual siege, or their bitter enemies, Junius understands, not the sons of Seth. Most of those who interpret the sons of Seth as the Jews, who were accustomed to boast of their carnal origin and to offer themselves to the Patriarchs, of whom Seth was the head after Adam, wish them to be noted. (3) He thinks the corporal subjugation of the Edomites is designated before the coming of the Messiah; others explain it more correctly concerning the majesty of the scepter of the kingdom of Christ, after the rising of this star from Jacob, extending itself to the Edomites and Moabites, that is, the enemies of the Church. (4) He takes Israel acting strenuously as Israel according to the flesh, which is rather to be understood of Israel according to the Spirit, or the Israel of God, i.e., of Christians overcoming their enemies. (5) He assumes gratuitously that Rome is understood by the city. Nowhere in the O.T. is Rome so absolutely designated. Others think rather that the Church is designated by the city, and they constitute the remnants of the city in the western Anti-Christ, heretics, persecutors, and false brethren, and any impious ones whatsoever. Junius explains: any most fortified enemy. Some understand the remnants of pagan Rome, even Corn. a Lap. with Abulensis, because through Constantine M. the whole city, and the remnants of the Gentiles of the city, and of other provinces subject to it, were made subject to Christ, and paganism was overturned even in its remnants. (6) He explains ships coming from the Kittim sometimes as the Greeks, subduing the Persians, sometimes as the Romans, the Hebrews. Which different senses cannot stand together. (7) By the Assyrians he understands the Persians. But what kind of license is this, to confuse nations and empires in such a way? Others wish for the Assyrians and Hebrews to be denoted here as having been tamed by the forces of the Greeks and Seleucids, which is also the interpretation of Junius.
