The Papists, clinging to the Vulgate, say that 'they shall come in galleys from Italy' predicts the power of the Romans, by whom the Assyrians, the masters of affairs, were first subdued, and afterwards even the Hebrews by Pompey and Augustus. (8) It is falsely said that the little horn is a survivor from the city, Dan. 7, 24. For by the little horn the Eastern Anti-Christ is understood. (9) Finally, it is precariously assumed here that the passage deals with the prostration of all flesh through the second coming of Christ, v. 17. Since the rise of the star out of Jacob testifies that it deals there with his first coming, and interpreters easily agree on this, both the Jews, who recognize the Messiah here, and the Christians. The prophecy also concerning Israel about to conquer the Edomites was fulfilled at the imminent first coming of Christ, when through Hyrcanus M. the Idumeans were subdued, so that they were no longer called Idumeans, but Israel, and they undertook the law of circumcision, having been made proselytes. Cf. Joseph. b. 13. ch. 17. Am. 9, 12. Mark 3, 8. Therefore neither does Cocceius deserve credit here, nor even the observation of Grotius on

Latin:

Vers. 24. VENIENT DE TRIERIBVS IN ITALIA) Voce כתים primo dicti Cyprii, apud quos κίττιον Phœni- cum colonia: & ab iis omnes Græci: Itaque Alexander di- citur fuisse ἐκ τῆς γῆς χεττίιμ 1. Macc. 1, 1. qui Rex יון, id est, Græcorum Danieli. Hi autem sunt, qui & Assyrios & eo- rum Successores Medos ac Persas armis suis subegere, trans- vecti Hellespontum.

VASTABVNTQVE HEBRÆOS( עבר, qui trans flu- men sunt, significat. Flumen Euphratem intellige. Etiam Euphratem transgredientur Macedonum sive Græcorum arma. Et hoc ad Alexandrum pertinere, nemo non videt.

Hæc Grotius. Quanquam non finiat hoc va- ticinium tempore Alexandri M. sed porrigat se ad tempora Titi Vespaf. cum Cittæi Itali afflixerunt E- bræos. Nam עבר gentem Ebræam hic notat uti אשור: & secundum Chald. & Rabbinos ipsos per Cittim Romani intelliguntur: uti & B. Luther. Cittim sind die aus Europa, als der Grosse Alexan- der, welche auch zuletzt untergehen. Conf. Genes. 10, 4. Adde his ea, quæ sequuntur versu eodem apud Grotium.

ET AD EXTREMVM ETIAM IPSI PERI- BVNT) Græci: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἀπολοῦνται. In He- bræo: Et ipse etiam in exitium, supple, ibit. Sensus est, il- lam victricem gentium Macedoniam cum Græcia omni suc- cubituram Romanorum armis.

Quum ergo, fatente Grotio, hic prædicatur non tantum Amalecitarum & Cinæorum, sed etiam summorum Imperiorum, Assyriaci & Græci destru- ctio, concinne, uti in Vaticinio Danielis simili Dan. II. opponitur Regnum Messiæ perpetuum caducis mundi imperiis. Sensus est, Interprete Pelargo, a Græcis Assyrios, Persas & Medos: a Romanis gentem Judaicam, & ipsos denig, Romanos excisum iri: Christi solius imperium perpetuo mansurum esse. Cum his ex- acte congruit vaticinium Danielis c. 2, 44. c. 7, 14. Conf. Mich. 4, 7. Luc. 1, 33. Conveniunt in eo pleriq; Interpp. a quibus in Grotianorum commentorum gratiam discedere nobis religio.

V. eod. VENIENT IN TRIERIBUS DE ITA- LIA, SUPERABUNT ASSYRIOS, VASTA- BUNTQUE HEBRÆOS, ET AD EXTREMUM IPSI PERIBUNT.

Coccejus ult. Mos. §. 1267. Bileam inquit, Num. 24, 24. compendio res maximas, finem seculi antecessu- ras conjungit, & ordinem prophetiæ totius in certos di- visum articulos una serie connectit; horum articulorum primus est Assyriorum subactio per naves venientes juxta Chittæos; ab occasu, hoc est, subactio Persarum per Græcos, quæ occasio libertatis Hebræorum, & occupandi Edomum tanquam hæreditatem & Seir ho- stes suos, & strenue agendi, quo tempore dominatu- rus erat ex Jacobo is, qui superstitem ex civitate per- dit, hoc est, Filius DEI, qui eo articulo temporis re- gnum suum erat erecturus, vid. v. 18. & 19. Secun- dus articulus est subactio Heberi, sive Hebræorum; item per naves a latere Chittæorum venientes, hoc est, per exercitus occidentalium Palæstinam per & secundum Asiam minorem invadentes, intellige Romanos. Hic articulus facit finem Reip. Ebræo- rum, sed regnum dominantis ex Jacobo, sive Chri- sti non tollit, imo illud diffusum per totum mun- dum liberat a jugo. Tertius est interitus etiam il- lius. Etiam ille, inquit, ad interitum. Imperium sane, quod mittebat naves secundum Chittæos in Assyrium & Heberum. Supra v. 19. dixerat, Eum qui dominaturus erat ex Jacobo, perditurum supersti- tem ex urbe. Unde colligere est urbem oppressu- ram Heberum, urbem imperium habituram in re- ges terræ, urbem suas vices passuram: tandemq; in superstite constitutam, denique & hunc regno Chri- sti cessurum, & ab illo abolendum. Conf. 2. Thess. 2, 8. Ap. 17, 11. 18, 21. Dan. 2, 44. c. 7, 24. (ubi superstes urbis cornu parvum) 25. 26. 27. Hisce factis, reliquum est, ut dominans ex Jacobo, sive sceptrum surgens ex Is- raele(adhuc congregato in politia) diruat omnes fi- lios Sethi, h.e. omnes homines, qui omnes ex Setho sunt per Noachum, & sic omnem carnem per mor- tem aut mutationem illustri sui adventu prosternat. Quod Bileam dicit v. 17. Quod cum inflammatio- ne absoluta fundamentorum montium coincidit. Hæc Coccejus. Idem §. 271. exaltationem Reipubl. Ebræorum in subjugatione gentium vicinarum & re- gno Sacerdotum circumstantiam facit proximam re- velationis regni Christi ex hoc vaticinio Bileami v. 18. 19. Et erit Edom hæreditas, & erit hæreditas Seir inimici ejus & Israele faciente strenue; tum domi- nabitur (aliquis) ex Jacobo, & perdet superstitem ex civitate, hoc est, tum regnum Christi incipiet, quod confliget cum regnis gentium, ut nec urbs Hierosolyma, nec urbs Roma & magna Babylon coram eo subsistere possint. Implementum post mortem imprimis Antiochi Pii, vide Joseph. l. 13. cap. 17. & seqq. Addimus quæ habet §. 1462. Num. 24, 19. Et dominabitur (absolute) ali- quis ex Jacobo, & perdet superstitem ex urbe. Profi- ciet eo usque imperium Christi, ut nullum regnum contrarium coram ipso subsistat. Scio dici posse, ultimo judicio omne regnum adversarium subla- tum iri, sed (1) distincte hoc dicitur a Bileamo per e- versionem omnium filiorum Seth. (2) Comparate locis aliis, ut hoc nostro, intelligitur per dominatio- nem, quam Christus exercet in mundo per Evange- lium, debere omnem superstitem de urbe tolli. Hæc ille. Laudandum quod v. 17. de Christo intelligat, non cum Junio de regno populi Dei cœpto in Davide, completo in Christo. Quanquam ex iis quæ v. 23. tradita, cum his collatis appareat, priora v. 17. verba ipsum de Regno Davidis accipere. Sic enim ibi, procedet stella ex Jacob, & defliget angulos Moabi Re- gnum Davidis. Cætera ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν sapiunt, quod (1) destructionem omnium בני שת & possessionem Edom, quæ conjungit textus, tanto sejungit interval- lo, ut hæc antecedat adventum Christi primum, illa ad adventum secundum referenda sit, (2) per בני שת omnes homines intelligit: filios Sethis vel posti- cæ partis ratione situs Bileami, Ammonitas, Midiani- tas, Orientales cæteros ad Euphratem usq́, e Jes. 20, 4. vel filios obsidionis, perpetua obsidione Israelitas pre- mentes, seu hostes eorum infensos Junius intelligit, non filios Seth. Pleriq; eorum, qui interpretantur fi- lios Seth Judæos, qui carnalem suam originem jacta- re, & Patriarchis, quorum Seth post Adam caput e- rat, se offerre solebant, notari volunt. (3) Edomita- rum subjugationem corporalem ante adventum Messiæ defignari putat; alii de sceptri regni Christi post ex- ortum hujus stellæ ex Jacob majestate porrigente se ad Edomæos & Moabitas, hoc est, hostes Ecclesiæ, re- ctius explicant. (4) Israelem strenue facientem de Is- raele secundum carnem accipit, qui de Israele secun- dum Spiritum, vel Israele Dei potius intelligendus, h. e. de Christianis hostes suos vincentibus. (5) Per civitatem Romam intelligi, gratis assumit. Nuspiam in V. T. ita absolute Roma indigitata. Alii potius per civitatem Ecclesiam designari putant, & reliquias civitatis in Anti-Christo occidentali, hæreticis, per- sequutoribus & falsis fratribus, atq; impiis quibus- vis, constituunt. Junius exponit: hostem quemvis munitissimum. Reliquias Romæ Ethnicæ intelligunt nonnulli, etiam Corn. a Lap. cum Abulens. quod per Constantin. M. tota urbs, & reliquiæ gentilium ur- bis, & aliarum Provinciarum ipsi subjectarum Chri- sto subjectæ, & gentilismus etiam in reliquiis ever- sus sit. (6) Naves venientes juxta Chittæos modo de Græcis explicat, Persas subigentibus, modo de Romanis Ebræos. Qui diversi sensus simul consi- stere nequeunt. (7) Per Assyrios Persas intelli- git. At quæ hæc est licentia, ita gentes & imperia confundendi? Alii Assyrios & Ebræos per Græcorum, Seleucidarumq́; copias domitos hic denotari volunt, quæ etiam Junii est interpretatio. Pontificii Vul- gatæ inhærentes, venient in trieribus de Italia, Roma- norum potentiam prædici ajunt, a quibus rerum Do- mini Assyrii primum, post etiam Ebræi subjugati per Pompejum & Augustum. (8) Superstitem ex urbe cornu parvum esse Dan. 7, 24. falso dicitur. Per cornu enim parvum Anti-Christus Orientalis intelli- gitur. (9) Deniq; precario assumitur hic de pro- stratione omnis carnis per adventum secundum Christi agi, v. 17. Siquidem de primo ejus adventu ibidem agi ortus stellæ ex Jacob testetur, & facile in eo con- veniant Interpp. cum Judæi, qui Messiam hic agno- scunt, tum Christiani. Vaticinium etiam de Is- raele Edomitas victuro impletum est imminente ad- ventu Christi primo, cum per Hircanum M. Idumæi subacti sunt, ut non amplius Idumæi, sed Israel. vocarentur, legemque circum cisionis susciperent, proselyti facti. Conf. Joseph. l. 13. c. 17. Am. 9, 12. Marc. 3, 8. Non ergo vel Coccejus hic calculum meretur, vel etiam observatio Grotii ad

## 24:25
Ver. 25. AND BALAAM ROSE UP AND RETURNED TO HIS PLACE) He went home indeed: but soon returned to the Midianites. Below 31. 8. Before his departure, however, he gave counsel, the execution of which is in the following chapter; that is held from tradition, which Peter 2 Ep. 2, 15, Jude 11, and John in Rev. 2, 14 approve.

Grotius wishes to support traditions, without doubt for the sake of the Papists. But Peter has nothing explicitly about that counsel, Jude has nothing: St. John hints at it. But from divine inspiration, and indeed Φερόμενοι ὑπὸ πνεύματος ἁγίου, by which the holy men of God were moved when they wrote. If the Pope, decreeing that traditions are to be received with an equal affection of piety as the written word of God, can solidly demonstrate such inspiration—after he has defined them, although no one among those bastard Successors of Peter has hitherto believed himself to be filled with such a rich Spirit as to presume to define their number and species—we will receive them with a ready and religious affection. But that will happen at the Greek Calends. Meanwhile, we do not deny that the counsel of Balaam was known from tradition at that time, as Josephus in book 4 of the Antiquities of the Jews, ch. 6, and Philo Judaeus on the life of Moses have also brought forward. He paid the penalty for that counsel when he was killed in battle by the sword of the Israelites. Cf. Num. 31, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 25. SVRREXITQVE BALAAM ET REVER- SVS EST IN LOCVM SVVM) Domum quidem iit: sed mox rediit ad Madianitas. Infra 31. 8. Ante abitum autem dedit consilium, cujus exequutio in sequenti est capite; id habetur ex traditione, quam probat Petr. 2. Ep. 2,15. Judas 11. Johannes in Apoc. 2, 14.

Juvare vult traditiones Grotius, sine dubio in Papistarum gratiam. At de consilio illo expresse nihil Petrus, nihil Judas habet: S. Johannes id innuit. Sed ex inspiratione divina, & quidem Φερόμενοι ὑπὸ πνεύματος ἁγίου, quo agitati scripserunt San- cti Dei homines. Qualem inspirationem si Papa traditiones pari pietatis affectu cum verbo Dei scri- pto suscipiendas decernens, cum illas definierit, quanquam earum numerum & speciem ut definire præsumeret, nemo hactenus tam opulento Spiritu sese impletum crediderit e nothis illis Petri Succef- soribus) solide demonstrare poterit, prono & reli- gioso eas suscipiemus affectu. Fiet autem id ad Calendas Græcas. Interim non negamus, consi- lium Bileami e traditione cognitum tum fuisse, ut- pote quod Josephus lib. 4. Antiq. Jud. c. 6. & Philo Judæus de vit. Mosis etiam adduxerunt. Pœnam consilii istius dedit, cum in prælio occisus est Israe- litarum gladio. Conf. Num. 31, 8.

## 25:1 Argument
CHAP. XXV.

The fornication of Israel with the Moabites punished, and the zeal of Phinehas praised.

Latin:

CAP. XXV.

Fornicatio Israel cum Moabitis punita, & Phi- neæ zelus laudatus.

## 25:3
ver. 3. AND ISRAEL WAS INITIATED TO BAAL PEOR. He was associated, it is said in the Heb. and Chald. LXX. or as Vatsbl. rendered it, he was joined. See concerning this idol what is at ch. 23, 28.

Latin:

vers. 3. INITIATUSQUE EST ISRAEL BEEL PHEGOR. ASsociatus est, dicitur in Ebr. & Chald. LXX. vel ut Vatsbl. reddidit conjugatus est. Vide de hoc idolo quæ ad c. 23, 28.

## 25:4
Ver. 4. TAKE ALL THE PRINCES OF THE PEOPLE) Take to yourself the chiliarchs, centurions, and the rest. AND HANG THEM) Cause that those magistrates make those who have sinned be hanged. The Hiphil form generally signifies a double action: but here a triple one: for this verb is h. l. יוצא לשנים פעלים, as the Hebrews say, i. e. passing into two passives. Moreover, suspension according to the Hebrew custom requires that the execution precede. Deut. 21. v. 22.

But the affix is referred to the leaders of the people. These, therefore, were the ones to be hanged. For הוקיע means to hang perpetually, without a double transitive, which Grotius rashly invents.

Latin:

Vers. 4. TOLLE CVNCTOS PRINCIPES POPVLI) Affume tibi Chiliarchos, centuriones ac cæteros. ET SVSPENDE EOS) Fac ut illi Magistratus eos qui de- liquerunt faciant suspendi. Forma Hiphil plerumque du- plicem actionem significat: hic vero triplicem: est enim hoc verbum h. l. יוצא לשנים פעלים, ut Hebræi loquun- tur, i. e. transiens in duo passiva. Suspensio autem ex more Hebræo requirit ut supplicium præcedat. Deut. 21. v. 22.

At affixum refertur ad primores populi. Hi ergo ipsi suspendendi erant. Nam הוקיע perpe- tuo suspendere est, sine duplici transitiva, quam te- mere fingit Grotius.

## 25:8
Verse 8. IN THE GENITAL PLACES) This is to be referred to the woman only, אל-קבתה. The cistern which in the gentile language the Syrians call Cubam. Jerome in the life of Paul. See Isaiah 51, v. 1.

Latin:

Vers. 8. IN LOCIS GENITALIBVS) Hoc referendum ad mulierem tantum אל-קבתה. Cisterna quam gen- tili sermone Syri Cubam vocant. Hieronymus in vita Pauli. Vide Esaiam 51. v. 1.

## 25:9
Verse 9. TWENTY-FOUR THOUSAND MEN WERE SLAIN) Partly by the hands of men, partly by death sent divinely.

The hanging of the Princes, which comes into the count here at the same time, must not be passed over, since otherwise there were only twenty-three thousand slain, as the Apostle testifies in 1 Cor. 10, 8. Whence there is no need to have recourse here to an error committed by scribes, from which Pelargus is not averse in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 9. OCCISI SVNT VIGINTI QVATVOR MIL- LIA HOMINVM) Partim hominum manibus, partim mor- te immissa divinitus,

Non prætereunda suspensio Principum, quæ hic simul in computum venit, cum alias occisorum vi- ginti tria millia tantum fuerint, teste Apostolo 1. Cor. 10, 8. Unde opus non est, ad mendam hic recurrere a librariis commissam, a qua alienus non est Pelargus in b. l.

## 25:12
Verse 12. AN EVERLASTING COVENANT OF PRIESTHOOD) Very long-lasting, namely after the times of Zadok. See Sirach 45, verse 24.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PACTVM SACERDOTII SEMPITERNVM) Diuturnum admodum, nempe post Sadoci tempora. Vide Sirach 45. vers. 24.

## 25:12 Addition
To chapter 25:12, page 547, column b. BEHOLD I GIVE TO HIM THE PEACE OF MY COVENANT.

Not concerning the stability of the Priesthood, as Lyranus, Tostatus, Oleastrius, Fagius, Vatablus, Bonfrerius, and Menochius [think], because this is promised in the following words, but this must be accepted concerning the grace to be shown to him, of peace and tranquility of conscience: as Osiander rightly [says]: I promise to him, and I bind myself to him, that he shall have me as a merciful God: inasmuch as I approve this deed of his and will compensate him with every kind of benefit.

Latin:

Ad cap. 25, 12. pag. 547. b. ECCE DO EI PACEM FOEDERIS MEI.

Non de stabilitate Sacerdotii, ut Lyranus, To- status, Oleastr. Fagius, Vatablus, Bonfrerius, Meno- chius, quia hæc sequentibus verbis promittitur, sed de gratia ipsi exhibenda, pacis & tranquillitatis conscientiæ hoc accipiendum: ut recte Osiander: Ego promitto ei, & obligo me ipsi, quod habiturus me sit Deum clementem: quippe qui approbo hoc ipsius factum & omni genere beneficiorum ipsi compensabo.

## 26:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVI.

The numbering of the Israelites, and the distribution of the land assigned according to it.

Verse 1. FROM TWENTY YEARS OLD AND UPWARD) Neither to those younger than that age, nor to women were lands given, though the right of succeeding according to the laws was preserved for them.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVI.

Israelitarum numeratio, & terræ juxta eam demandata distributio.

Vers. 1. A VIGINTI ANNIS ET SV PRA) Nec mino- ribus ea ætate, nec mulieribus dati fundi, servato tamen il- lis secundum leges succedendi jure.

## 26:1 Addition
To chapter 26, verse 1. AFTER THE BLOOD OF THE GUILTY HAS BEEN SHED.

In Hebrew, after the plague. The Chaldean and the Arab render it 'after the pestilence.' Malvenda understands that pestilence by which all were consumed according to Numbers 14. Others refer it to the idolatrous plague of Peor that followed, and therefore Osiander draws that particle back to the preceding chapter. But there is no need to depart from the distinction of the authentic text. And the new census implies that the threat of excision made in Numbers 14 had been completed, and that this plague is hinted at here: Which census was made so that, as they were about to enter the land of Canaan, they might rightly and proportionally distribute it among the tribes, having known the number of each, as Menochius wishes, or rather, so that, as is indicated in the text, it might be clear what the number was of those who would proceed to war, and so that the divine providence might shine forth, which in so short a time propagated the nation that had been destroyed, and thus abundantly fulfilled in turn the promise made to Abraham.

Latin:

Ad cap. 26, vers. 1. POSTQVAM NOXIORUM SANGUIS EFFUSUS EST.

In Ebr. post plagam. Chald. & Arabs reddunt post pestem. Illam autem pestem intelligit Mal- venda, qua omnes absumti juxta Numer. 14. Alii ad plagam idololatricam Phegor sequutam referunt, ideoque particulam illam ad præcedens caput re- trahit Osiander. Sed non opus est, a textus au- thentici distinctione discedere. Et census novus Innuit completam fuisse comminationem excisio- nis Numer. 14. factam, eamque plagam hic innui: Qui census factus est, ut jamjam ingressuri terram Canaan recte & proportionaliter eam inter tribus, cognito cujusque numero, distribuerent, ut Me- nochius vult, vel potius, ut, quod in textu indica- tur, quantus esset numerus eorum, qui ad bella procederent, constaret, útque divina elucesceret providentia, quæ deletam gentem tam parvo tem- pore propagaverit, & ita Abrahæ factam promif- sionem in illa largiter vicissim impleverit.

## 26:10
Verse 10. AND A GREAT MIRACLE WAS DONE, THAT WHILE KORAH PERISHED, HIS SONS DID NOT PERISH) The Greeks, with the Hebrew, better refer that καὶ ἐγεννήθησαν εἰς σημεῖον to the preceding things. But what is said about the sons of Korah shows the distinction between them and the sons of Dathan and Abiram, arising, of course, from the fact that the sons of Korah detested their father's crime, and therefore the prayers poured out to God by Moses profited them, above 16, verse 22.

The Vulgate is rightly corrected, from which the fable arose about the sons of Korah being suspended in the air for so long by divine power, until the earth closed up again beneath them.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET FACTVM EST GRANDE MIRACV- LVM, VT CORE PEREVNTE, FILII ILLIVS NON PERIRENT) Melius Græci cum Hebræo illud καὶ ἐγεννήθη- σαν εἰς σημεῖον referunt ad priora. Quod autem de Core filiis dicitur, discrimen ostendit inter eos & inter filios Da- than & Abiram, nimirum inde ortum, quod filii Core pater- num crimen detestati sint, ac propterea Mosis preces ad De- um fufæ ipsis profuerint, supra 16. vers. 22.

REcte corrigitur Vulgata, e qua fabula orta de Korachi filiis tam diu in aere suspensis divina virtute, donec terra sub illis iterum coiret.

## 26:39
Verse 39. HUPHAM, FROM WHOM THE FAMILY OF THE HUPHAMITES) It is not in the Greek: But he who is here חופם in Gen. 46, v. 21 is חפים and in 1 Chron. 8, חורם, both corruptly, as are many in proper names.

We acknowledge no corruption here, nor elsewhere in the original text. Let what we said at Gen. 47, 20 be compared.

Latin:

Vers. 39. HVPHAM, EX QVO FAMILIA HVPHA- MITARVM) Non est in Græco: Sed qui hic est חופם Gen. 46. v. 21. est חפים & 1. Paral. 8. חורם utrumque cor- rupte, qualia multa in nominibus propriis.

Nullam hic corruptionem agnoscimus, nec alias in textu originali. Conferantur quæ ad Gen. 47, 20. diximus.

## 26:51
Ver. 51. SIX HUNDRED THOUSAND AND ONE THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED THIRTY) The division having been made more according to what the lands were worth than according to their areas into twelve parts, another division was made into as many as the number here reports, not however plainly by heads, but by representation and primogeniture of those who had gone out from Egypt.

Latin:

Vers. 51. SEXCENTA MILLIA ET MILLE SEPTIN- GENTI TRIGINTA) Divisione facta magis secundum quod valebant terræ, quam secundum spatia in partes duo- decim, altera divisio facta est in tot, quot hic refert numerus, non tamen planè in capita, sed per repræsentationem & pri- mogenituram eorum qui ex Ægypto exierant.

## 26:53
Ver. 53. ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF NAMES) Which were written on slips, as were also the names of the lands: thus two slips were drawn equally.

Latin:

Vers. 53. JVXTA NVMERVM VOCABVLORVM) Quæ scripta in schedulis, ut & terrarum nomina: sic duæ schedæ pariter trahebantur.

## 26:59
Ver. 59. JOCHABED) Is this Jochebed [mentioned in] Pliny, Natural History, book 30, chapter 1?

Latin:

Vers. 59. JOCHABED) An hæc Jochabeta Plinio Natu- ralis Histor. lib. 30. cap. 1.?

## 26:59 Addition
To Numbers 26:59, page 547, column b, after Grotius's notes.

Capellus contends that in this verse the LXX read otherwise than the Hebrew Codex now has it, namely אותם instead of אותה, and indeed that that reading is better: But against all other interpreters, and although the variation of the LXX is indeed an interpretation from the Hebrew, it does not follow that a variant reading is immediately to be argued in the Hebrew: which text (the Hebrew) is explained thus by R. Solomon, R. Kimchi, Don Aben Jechijah: whom (Jochebed) Levi bore, (let אשתו, his wife, be understood in the Hebrew manner) concerning which Aben-Ezra: he mentions Jochebed for the honor of her sons, but he does not mention her who bore her (her mother, the wife of Levi) out of a desire for brevity, as in 1 Chronicles 7:14, Aschriel whom she bore, namely his mother. See also 1 Kings 1:6. But on the contrary, he refutes the LXX interpreters. Augustinus Stevchus, Eugubinus, because they did not correctly render ἣ ἔτεκε τότες τῷ λευῒ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ: which, he says, is known not to be true: for she did not bear them to Levi himself, but to the man Amram, their father. Therefore, besides the fact that the meaning is corrupted and does not render what is in the context, what he says is also false. For Jochabed, the wife of Hamram, bore Moses and Aaron to Amram himself, not to Levi himself, just as wives are said among the Hebrews to bear sons to their husbands. Therefore, what was said about the one being born, Jochabed, the seventy translated as her bearing. An intolerable slip. For the article אותה, 'her', could have abundantly taught them of whose birth it was being spoken. Furthermore, was the absurdity not known, because it is soon inferred, καὶ ἔτεκε τῷ Ἀμβρὰμ τὸν Ἀαρὼν, καὶ τὸν Μωϋση, that is, She bore to Hamram himself, Aaron and Moses: did they not say before that she bore them to Levi? Thus far he.

Latin:

Ad Num. 26. v. 59. pag. 547. b. post not. Grot.

Capellus hoc in versu LXX. aliter legisse, quam nunc habet Codex Ebræus contendit, nimirum אותם pro אותה, imo lectionem illam melio- rem esse: Sed invitis omnibus aliis interpretibus, & varians quidem τῶν ὁ est interpretatio ab Ebræo, non autem ideo statim varia lectio arguenda in E- bræo: quem textum (Ebræum) ita explicant R. Sa- lomo, R. Kimchi, Don Aben Jechijah: quam (Joche- bed) peperit Levi, (subintelligatur more Ebræo אשתו uxor ejus) quo de Aben-Ezra: meminit Jochebedæ propter honorem filiorum ejus, non memi- nit autem ejus quæ illam peperit (matris ejus uxo- ris Levi) brevitatis studio sicut 1. Chronic. 7. v. 14. Aschriel quem peperit, scilicet mater ejus. Vid. & 1. Reg. 1, 6. Ex adverso vero redarguit LXX. Interpp. Augustinus Stevchus, Eugubinus, quod non recte reddiderint ἣ ἔτεκε τότες τῷ λευῒ ἐν Αἰγύ- πτῳ: quod, inquit constat non esse verum: non enim peperit eos ipsi Levi, sed viro Amram, Patri eorum. Præterquam igitur, quod sententia depravata est, & non reddit, quæ sunt in contextu, etiam quod dicit est falsum. Jochabed enim Uxor Hamram, peperit Mosen & Aaron, ipsi Amram, non ipsi Levi, quemad- modum dicuntur apud Hebræos uxores Viris suis Fi- lios gignere. Quod ergo dicebatur de nascente Jo- chabed, septuaginta de ea pariente transtulerunt. Lapsus non ferendus. Nam articulus אותה Eam, poterat eos abunde docere, de quorum partu dicere- tur. Deinde, nonne absurditas nota erat, quia mox infertur, καὶ ἔτεκε τῷ Ἀμβρὰμ τὸν Ἀαρὼν, καὶ τὸν Μωϋση, id est, Peperit ipsi Hamram, Aaron & Mo- sen: nonne dixerunt prius, eos peperisse ipsi Levi? Hæc ectenus ille.

## 27:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVII.

The inheritance of the daughters of Zelophehad. The death of Moses intimated with his successor.

Ver. 1. DAUGHTERS OF ZELOPHEHAD) Compare Joshua 17, ver. 4 and following.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVII.

Filiarum Salphaad hæreditas. Mors Mosis intimata cum successore.

Vers. 1. FILIÆ SALPHAAD) Conf. Jos. 17. v. 4. & se- quentibus.

## 27:7
V. 7. AND TO HIM YOU SHALL CAUSE TO PASS) In the Hebrew: you shall cause to pass: which the Samaritan interprets as you shall give.

Latin:

V. 7. ET EI IN HÆREDITATEM SVCCEDANT) In Hebræo: transire facietis: quod Samaritanus interpretatur dabitis.

## 27:8
Ver. 8. WHEN HE SHALL HAVE DIED WITHOUT A SON) Among most other nations, daughters succeed along with sons. Among the Hebrews, they are not admitted unless sons are lacking, as in certain fiefs. And in truth, the Israelite land was bound to God in the manner of a fief. A dying son transmitted his future right to his own sons, or if there were no sons, to his daughters.

Latin:

Vers. 8. CVM MORTVVS FVERIT ABSQVE FI- LIO) Apud alias gentes plerasque filiæ cum filiis succe- dunt. Apud Hebræos non admittuntur, nisi filiis deficienti- bus, ut in feudis quibusdam. Et revera terra Israëlitica Deo feudi more devincta erat. Filius moriens jus futurum in suos filios, aut si filii non essent, filias transmittebat.

## 27:9
Ver. 9. IF HE SHALL NOT HAVE A DAUGHTER, HE SHALL HAVE HIS BROTHERS AS SUCCESSORS) The father is preferred to the brothers, except for the brother who marries the widow. But for the sake of avoiding an evil omen, Moses [passed over] this succession, as it is against the wish of the parents, as Papinian speaks in law Julianus, Digest, If anyone has passed over [a child] in silence. Papinian elsewhere in the law, For even if to parents, Digest, Concerning the inofficious [will], says that this inheritance is against the disturbed order of mortality. Therefore it is called mournful and sad, law children, Code, concerning the inofficious, last law, Code, Concerning Institutions, and § 2, Institutes, concerning the Tertullian Senatusconsultum, a solace for harsh fortune, law If any, Code, to the Tertullian Senatusconsultum. Pliny in the Panegyric: Thus also it is an abundantly miserable thing, for a father to be the sole heir to his son. Philo in book 3, on the life of Moses, consistently says this: Since it is the law of nature that parents should be inherited by children, but not that they should inherit them, he kept silent on the detestable and ill-omened matter, so that a father and mother might not seem to be seeking gain from the inconsolable griefs over children who died before their time; but he called them indirectly by permitting the uncles.

Latin:

Vers. 9. SI FILIAM NON HABUERIT, HABEBIT SVCCESSORES FRATRES SVOS) Pater fratribus præ- fertur, excepto fratre, qui viduam ducit. Sed vitandi mali ominis causa hanc successionem, ut quæ contra votum sit parentum, ut Papinianus loquitur l. Julianus. D. Si quis omissa causa silentio præteriit Moses. Papinianus alibi in l. Nam & si parentibus D. De inofficioso, hanc hæreditatem ait turbato ordine mortalitatis. Ideo luctuosa dicitur & tristis l. liberi c. de inofficioso l. ult. C. De Institu- tionibus, & §. 2. Inst. de Senatusconsulto Tertulliano, duræ fortunæ solatium. l. Si qua. C. ad Senatuscons. Tertullianum. Plinius in Panegyrico: Sic quoque abunde misera res est, pater filio solus hæres. Philo libro 3, de vita Mosis his congruen- ter sic ait: ἐπειδὰν ὁ νόμος τῆς φύσεώς ἐστι κληρονομεῖσθαι τὺς γονεῖς ὑπὸ παίδων, ἀλλὰ μὴ τύτες κληρονομεῖν, τὸ μὲν ἀπευκταῖον κὰι παλίμφημον ἡσύχασεν, ἵνα μὴ πατὴρ κὰι μή- τηρ προσοδεύεσθαι δοκῶσι τὰ ἐπὶ ἀκυμόροις τέκνοις ἀπαρη- γόρητα πένθη· πλαγίως δ' αὐτὲς ἐκάλεσε τὲς θείυς ἐφιείς.

## 27:10
BUT IF THERE SHALL NOT BE BROTHERS EITHER)

Supply 'nor sisters': which is understood from the preceding mention of daughters: nor a grandfather, who is in the place of a father. TO THE BROTHERS OF HIS FATHER) Note that by Hebrew custom, paternal uncles are preferred to the sons of brothers, as being nearer to him from whom the goods came. The same custom came through the Phoenicians into Africa. See what we have noted on the Law of War and Peace, book 2, § 24, verse 11. TO THOSE WHO ARE NEAREST TO HIM) Namely, the agnates. For there is no משפחה, which word Moses uses here, that is maternal: for a woman is both the head and the end of her own family. l. Pronunciatio. D. de verborum signific. Hence the husband succeeded the wife, besides the dowry which went to the children, or whence it had come. משפחה is a part of a tribe, to the Greeks πατριά from the paternal line, sometimes also by the more common name συγγένεια. Therefore, after sisters, neither females nor males joined through females are admitted to succession by Hebrew law. Pity introduced daughters and sisters. In other respects, the laws of families are observed. Therefore, brothers are to be understood here as from the father, the opinion of Aben Ezra, who admits uterine brothers, being commonly rejected. The Greeks sometimes use φυλὴν where it concerns a πατριᾶς, as in this place: 'he shall give the inheritance to his kinsman who is nearest to him of his tribe, he shall inherit his things': which impropriety the old collator of the laws of Moses and the Romans followed. 'If a man shall die, and shall not have sons, you shall give the inheritance to his nearest of his tribe, and he shall possess all his things.' Thus the law of the 12 tables: 'If anyone shall have died without male or female children, and without brothers and sisters from the same father, the inheritance came to the agnate, and indeed the nearest.' D. de suis & legitimis hæredibus, and Instit. de legitima agnatorum successione. Ulpianus Instit. title de legitimis hæredibus. Thus also in Attic law, after brothers and sisters, the ἄῤῥενες ἐξ ἀῤῥένων are called. After these words, 'to those who are nearest to him', is added for the sake of explanation in the Hebrew, 'and he shall inherit it'. In Greek κληρονομήσει τὰ αὐτῦ, which the Samaritan explains, 'he shall receive it as heir': that is, he shall have it by the title of heir, as succeeding into every right of the deceased, and therefore also acknowledging the burdens. Those born from a handmaid or a foreigner were considered neither agnates nor cognates. But a proselyte, unless he had begotten an Israelite, had no heir, but the goods became the property of the occupant. Thus, what had been of the law of nations, the law had reduced to citizens, as also the Roman law, which did not want there to be a power of making a will with foreigners. Verse 16. GOD OF THE SPIRITS OF ALL FLESH. In the Hebrew, by the force of the accent Tipheha, it should be rendered, 'God of the spirits (and) over all flesh.' Compare c. 16, 22. Therefore, the immediate creation of our souls cannot be proved from this, nor should it be said that our flesh is today created immediately by God. Verse 17. AS SHEEP WITHOUT A SHEPHERD) Even to the Greeks, princes are ποιμένες λαῶν. Verse 21. HE SHALL CONSULT THE LORD) In the Hebrew more clearly: 'He shall consult for him the response of Urim before the Lord,' that is, at the mercy seat. Since David, who was not a Priest, is also said to have inquired of the Lord through the Ephod, 1 Sam. 30, 8, some observe that there was a double Ephod: one proper to the Pontiff, the other common to all Priests. See B. Waltherus in Harmon. ad h. l. But here Eleazar consulted the Lord for Joshua, as is clear from the authentic text.

PART IV OF THE BOOK, partly νομικὴ concerning sacrifices, especially on feasts, the Sabbath, the Passover, and Pentecost, chapter 28, as well as of the seventh month, then the New Moon, chapter 29, then the Feast of Atonement, then of tabernacles, c. 30, partly ἰσορικὴ concerning the inheritance of Israel, amplified by the spoils of the Midianites, c. 31, partly κληροχικὴ concerning the assignment of lands on this side of the Jordan, c. 32, and after the order of the dwellings and journeys of the people, c. 33, concerning the lot of the remaining tribes, c. 34, and the cities of the Levites, c. 35, and also specifically concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, chapter 36.

Latin:

QVOD SI ET FRATRES NON FVERINT)

Supple nec Sorores: quod ex præcedente filiarum mentione intelligitur: nec avus, qui patris loco est. FRATRIBVS PATRIS EJVS) Nota Hebræo more pa- truos fratrum filiis præferri, ut propiores ei a quo bona ve- nerunt. Idem mos per Phœnicas in Africam venit. Vide quæ a nobis notata de Jure Belli ac Pacis l. 2. §. 24. Vers. 11. HIS QVI EI PROXIMI SVNT) Nempe agna- ti. Nulla enim est משפחה, qua voce hic Moses utitur, materna: Mulier enim familiæ suæ & caput & finis est. l. Pro- nunciatio. D. de verborum signific. hinc uxori succedebat maritus, præter dotem quæ ibat ad liberos, aut unde vene- rat. משפחה est pars tribus, Græcis πατριά a paterno gene- re, interdum & communiori nomine συγγένεια. Ergo post sorores nec fœminæ nec mares per fœminas conjuncti ad- mittuntur ad successionem jure Hebræo. Filias & sorores mi- seratio introduxit. In cæteris familiarum jura servantur. Pro- inde fratres intelligendi hic ex patre, rejecta communiter opinione Abenesdræ, qui uterinos admittit. Græci interdum φυλὴν ponunt, ubi περὶ πατριᾶς agitur, ut h. l. δώσεται τὴν κληρονομίαν τῷ οἰκείῳ τῷ ἔγγιστα αὐτῦ ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς αὐτῦ κλη- ρονομήσει τὰ αὐτῦ: quam improprietatem secutus collator vetus legum Mosis & Romanarum. Homo si decesserit, & fi- lios non habuerit, dabitis hæreditatem proximo ejus de tribu ejus, & possidebit omnia ejus. Sic lege 12. tabularum: Si quis fine liberis maribus aut fœminis, ac fine fratribus ac sorori- bus ex eodem patre decessiss t, ad agnatum, & quidem pro- ximum veniebat hæreditas. D. de suis & legitimis hæredibus, & Instit. de legitima agnatorum successione. Vlpianus In- stit. titulo de legitimis hæredibus. Sic & jure Attico post fra- tres & sorores vocantur ἄῤῥενες ἐξ ἀῤῥένων. Post verba hæc bis qui ei proximi sunt, additur explicandi causa in Hebræo, & hæreditabit eam. Græce κληρονομήσει τὰ αὐτῦ, quod Sa- maritanus explicat, éam ut hæres accipiet: id est, titulo hære- dis eam habebit, ut succedens in omne jus defuncti, ac pro- inde & onera agnoscens. Nati ex ancilla aut peregrina neque agnati neque cognati censebantur. Proselytus vero, nisi Israëlitam genuisset, non habebat hæredem, sed bona fie- bant occupantis. Ita quod juris gentium fuerat, lex ad cives redegerat, ut & Romana, quæ cum peregrinis noluit esse te- stamenti factionem. Vers. 16. DEUS SPIRITUUM OMNIS CAR- NIS. IN Hebræo vi accentus Tipheha reddendum, Deus spirituum (&) super omnem carnem. Conf. c. 16, 22. Non ergo hinc immediata animarum nostrarum creatio probari potest, neque etiam dicendum, car- nem nostram hodie immediate a Deo creari. Vers. 17. SICVT OVES ABSQVE PASTORE) Etiam Græcis principes ποιμένες λαῶν. Vers. 21. CONSULET DOMINVM) In Hebræo clarius: Consulet pro eo responsum Vrim coram Domino, id est, apud propitiatorium. Cum David, qui Sacerdos non erat, etiam di- catur interrogasse Dominum per Ephod, 1. Sam. 30, 8. observant nonnulli duplex fuisse Ephod: unum Pon- tificis proprium, alterum omnibus Sacerdotibus commune. Vid. B. Waltherus in Harmon. ad h. l. Sed hic Eleazar consului Dominum pro Josua, ut e textu authentico liquet.

PARS IV. LIBRI, Partim νομικὴ de sacrificiis, imprimis in fe- stis, Sabbato, Paschate, & Pentecoste cap. 28. nec non septimi mensis, tum Neomeniæ cap. 29. tum Festi expiationis, tum taber- naculorum, c. 30 partim ἰσορικὴ de hære- ditate Israël. per spolia Midianitarum am- plificata c. 31. partim κληροχικὴ de terra- rum cis Jordanem assignatione c. 32. & post mansionum & profectionum populi or- dinem c. 33. de reliquorum tribuum sorte c. 34. & Levitarum urbibus c. 35. nec non spe- ciatim de filiabus Salphaad cap. 36.

## 27:20 Addition
To chapter 27, verse 20. LAY THY HAND UPON HIM. at page 548. a.

By this laying on of hands, there was signified: both the commission of a new function, because he was handed over and devoted to the Lord, so that he might serve Him in that function, and because a new burden is now imposed upon him: and the gifts to be placed upon him divinely, necessary for this office, which were conferred at the prayers of Moses through the laying on of hands: and divine protection, because he was to be protected by the hand of the Lord in his vocation.

Latin:

Ad cap. 27. vers. 20. PONE MANUM TUAM SUPER EUM. ad pag. 548. a.

Hac χειροθεσίᾳ tum novæ functionis com- missio quod Domino q. traditus & devotus sit, ut ei in illa functione inserviret, quodque novum illi onus jam imponatur: tum dona divinitus in ipsum ponenda ad hoc officium necessaria, quæ ad pre- ces Mosis per impositionem manuum confereban- tur significata: tum tutela divina, quod manu Do- mini protegendus in sua vocatione sit, designata fuit.

## 28:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVIII. Daily sacrifices, and Sabbatic, as also of the Calends. Feasts of Unleavened Bread and of weeks.

Latin:

CAP. XXVIII. Sacrificia quotidiana, & Sabbatica, ut & Ca- lendarum. Festa Azymorum & hebdo- madum.

## 28:2
Verse 2. OBLATION AND BREAD) Better in the Hebrew: 'my oblation, my food.' See what is above 15, 4. Laws are to be repeated where disuse intervenes. Sacrifice here and in the following chapter is understood as wheaten or Mincha, but the burnt offering is not incense, but a victim burned to God, just as by 'bread' are understood not the loaves of proposition, but victims, which are bread or food to God. Finally, the perpetual holocaust is called the continual sacrifice of the lamb.

Latin:

Vers. 2. OBLATIONEM ET PANES) Melius in He- bræo: oblationem meam cibum meum. Vide quæ supra 15, 4. Leges repetendæ, ubi desuetudo intervenit. SAcrificium hic & sequenti capite farreum intelli- gitur vel Mincha, incensum vero non Thymiama est, sed victima incensa Deo, uti & per panes non pro- positionis panes, sed victimæ, quæ sunt Deo panis, vel cibus, intelliguntur. Holocaustum denique sempi- ternum vocatur juge sacrificium agni.

## 28:8 Addition
To chapter 28, verse 8. ACCORDING TO ALL THE RITE OF THE SACRIFICE. at p. 548. b.

Of the meal offering, namely: not that the lamb was to be sacrificed as a Mincha or as a drink offering, which would be an inept expression; but that both a meal offering was to be added, and wine to be poured out in the exact same way as was done in the morning, as Osiander rightly says. Whence Arias, Junius and Tremellius, and others render it, as the morning gift, and as its drink offering.

Latin:

Ad cap. 28. v. 8. JUXTA OMNEM RITUM SACRI- FICII. ad p. 548. b.

Cibarii scilicet: non quod agnus sacrifican- dus ut Mincha vel ut libamen, quæ inepta foret lo- quutio; sed quod & sacrificium cibarium esset ad- dendum, & vinum libandum eodem plane modo, quo mane factum, ut recte Osiander. Unde Arias, Junius & Tremellius & alii reddunt, sicut munus ma- tutinum, & sicut libamen ejus.

## 28:10
Verse 10. WHICH ARE RITUALLY POURED OUT EVERY SABBATH FOR A PERPETUAL HOLOCAUST) In the Hebrew there is another sense: 'The Sabbatic holocaust with its libation shall be made on the Sabbath over the continual holocaust.' That is, besides the daily holocaust, another proper to the Sabbath shall be added. Thus also the Greeks: ὁλοκαύτωμα σαββάτων ἐν τοῖς σαββάτοις ἐπὶ τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως τῆς διαπαντὸς καὶ τὴν σπονδὴν ἀυτᾶ.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QVÆ RITE FVNDVNTVR PER SINGV- LA SABBATA IN HOLOCAVSTVM SEMPITERNUM) In Hebræo alius est sensus: Holocaustum Sabbaticum cum suo libamine in Sabbatho fiet super holocaustum juge. Id est, præ- ter holocaustum quotidianum addetur & alterum proprium Sabbati. Sic & Græci: ὁλοκαύτωμα σαββάτων ἐν τοῖς σαβ- βάτοις ἐπὶ τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως τῆς διαπαντὸς καὶ τὴν σπονδὴν ἀυτᾶ.

## 28:11 Addition
Verse 11. IN THE CALENDS.

Bonfrerius and Cornelius a Lapide deny that the New Moons were properly feasts; but Tostatus, Sanctius, Tirinus, and Ainsworth in Pole affirm it more correctly. For 1. then journeys and servile works were prohibited, 1 Kings 20 and Amos 8:5. 2. Special sacrifices were then offered. 3. Then they went to the prophets and ministers to hear the word of God; 2 Kings 4:23.

Latin:

Vers. 11. IN CALENDIS.

Novilunia proprie festa fuisse negat Bonfrerius & Cornelius a Lapide; sed rectius affirmant Tostatus, Sanctius, Tirinus & Ainsvvorthus apud Polum. Nam 1. tunc itinera & opera servilia sunt prohibita, 1. Reg. 20. & Amos. 8, 5. 2. Specialia tum sacrificia offe- rebantur. 3. Tunc Prophetas & Ministros adi- bant ad audiendum verbum Dei; 2. Reg. 4, 23.

## 28:15
Verse 15. A GOAT ALSO SHALL BE OFFERED TO THE LORD) Not to the Moon, as was accustomed to be done by neighboring nations. Maimonides.

Latin:

Vers. 15. HIRCVS QVOQVE OFFERETVR DOMI- NO) Non Lunæ, ut fieri a vicinis gentibus solebat. Mai- monides.

## 28:26 Addition
Verse 26. WHEN THE WEEKS ARE COMPLETED.

The Vulgate is correct in this, as is evident from Lev. 23:15, 16: even though in the Hebrew it is 'in the weeks'. For ב sometimes is taken for AFTER, and for the complement. Isa. 20, 1. Luke 9, 36.

Latin:

Vers. 26. EXPLETIS HEBDOMADIBUS.

Recte ita vulgata, ut e Lev. 23, 15. 16. constat: etsi in Ebræo sit in septimanis. Nam ב quandoque pro POST, & de complemento accipitur. Esa. 20, 1. Luc. 9, 36.

## 28:27 Addition
Ver. 27. AND YOU SHALL OFFER A BURNT OFFERING.

Besides those which were to be joined with the firstfruits by the law Lev. 23, 18. For thus those passages are to be reconciled: as Menochius on Lev. 23 and Junius on this passage observed.

Latin:

Vers. 27. OFFERETISQUE HOLOCAUSTUM.

Præter illa, quæ cum primitiis conjungenda erant ex lege Lev. 23, 18. Sic enim loca illa conci- lianda: ut Menochius ad Lev. 23. & Junius ad hunc lo- cum observavit.

## 28:30
Verse 30. BESIDES THE HOLOCAUST) For no oblation of those concurring at the same time is omitted for that reason.

Latin:

Vers. 30. PRÆTER HOLOCAVSTVM) Oblationum enim in idem tempus concurrentium nulla ob id omittitur.

## 29:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIX. Sacrifices of the Feast of Trumpets, of Atonement, and of Tabernacles.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIX. Sacrificia Festi Tubarum, expiationis & Taber- naculorum.

## 29:1 Addition
On chapter 29, verse 1. DAY OF BLASTING.

For they used to sound with trumpets on this day, which Münster notes was done among the Jews from the hour of the rising Sun until night: and from that day the days were counted until the feast of atonement, likewise until the feast of tabernacles; likewise the Sabbatical years, as also the years of Jubilee. This feast of trumpets signified the preaching of John the Baptist, which preceded the sacrifice of the atonement of Christ the high Priest, as Osiander says.

Latin:

Ad cap. 29. versu 1. DIES CLANGO- RIS.

Clangebant enim tubis hoc die, quod apud Judæos fieri ab hora radiantis Solis usque ad no- ctem, notat Münsterus: & ab illo die numeraban- tur dies usque ad festum propitiationis, item us- que ad festum tabernaculorum; item anni Sabbati- ci, ut & anni Jubilæi. Hoc festum tubarum signi- ficabat prædicationem Johannis Baptistæ, quæ præ- cessit sacrificium expiationis Christi summi Sacer- dotis, ut dicit Osiander.

## 29:3
Verse 3. FOR EACH OF THE CALVES. In the Hebrew 'for a calf': for only one calf was accustomed to be offered annually at the feast of trumpets. The Vulgate, therefore, had to be corrected here.

Latin:

Vers. 3. PER SINGULOS VITULOS. IN Ebræo per vitulum: unus enim tantum vitulus quotannis in festo tubarum offerri solebat. Cor- rigenda ergo erat hic Vulgata.

## 29:11
V. 11. BESIDES THOSE THINGS WHICH ARE ACCUSTOMED TO BE OFFERED FOR SIN IN EXPIATION. Therefore, besides those things already prescribed in Lev. 16, the burnt offerings designated here were sacrificed in honor of the Feast.

Vers. 39. IN A DRINK OFFERING. Corn. a Lap. notes that a drink offering was never offered by itself alone, but always with a sacrifice: whence, when the sacrifice was free and spontaneous, the drink offering was also free and spontaneous.

Latin:

V. 11. ABSQUE HIS QUÆ OFFERRI PRO DELICTO SOLENT IN EXPIATIONEM. Præter illa ergo Lev. 16. jam præscripta, ad ho- norem Festi immolabantur holocausta hic designata.

Vers. 39. IN LIBAMINE. Notat Corn. a Lap. libamen nunquam per se solum oblatum fuisse, sed semper cum sacrificio: unde, quando liberum & spontaneum fuit sacrifici- um, liberum & spontaneum fuerit etiam libamen.

## 29:12 Addition
Ver. 17. SEVEN DAYS.

Not that one had to be free from servile work for so long, but that one had to remain in tabernacles, and sacrifices had to be offered, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 17. SEPTEM DIEBUS.

Non quod tamdiu vacandum esset ab opere servili, sed manendum in tabernaculis, & sacrifi- cia offerenda &c.

## 29:31 Addition
ver. 31. BESIDES THE PERPETUAL BURNT OFFERING.

That is, besides the continual burnt offering. For however much the sacrifices were accumulated, the Lord nevertheless did not want anything to be taken away from the daily burnt offering; Because as the virtue of the sacrifice of Christ always endures, so the memory of the same ought to be renewed daily among us through the ministry of the word.

Latin:

vers. 31. ABSQUE HOLOCAUSTO SEMPI- TERNO.

Id est, præter juge holocaustum. Utcunque enim cumularentur sacrificia, noluit tamen Do- minus, ut de quotidiano holocausto aliquid dece- deret; Quia ut sacrificii Christi virtus semper du- rat, ita ejusdem memoria quotidie per ministe- rium verbi inter nos renovari debet.

## 29:36 Addition
Ver. 36. ONE BULLOCK.

This day was the last and greatest of the feast, John 7:37. Yet there were fewer sacrifices on it than on any other day; as if God wished to call them away from the multitude of carnal sacrifices to His own spiritual worship: which was also done by Christ on that day, as Ainsworth notes.

Latin:

Vers. 36. VITULUM UNUM.

Hic dies erat ultimus & maximus festi Job. 7, 37. In eo tamen pauciora sacrificia erant, quam alio quopiam die; quasi Deus avocare eos vellet a multitudine carnalium sacrificiorum ad spiritualem ipsius cultum: quod & a Christo illo die factum, no- tante Ainswortho.

## 30:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXX. Vows and oaths of men, girls, and wives.

Latin:

CAPUT XXX. Vota ac juramenta Virorum, puellarum, & uxorum.

## 30:2
Vers. 3. SHALL VOW A VOW UNTO THE LORD, OR SHALL BIND HIMSELF BY AN OATH) A vow is made to God, an oath by God. Vows were not considered binding unless uttered in words: as here and Deut. 23, 23. Moreover, nothing ought to be vowed except that which pertained to the honor of God or piety, such as the Nazirite vow, victims, money for the uses of the Temple or the poor, fasts, and similar σκληραγωγίαι (austerities).

Concerning vows, compare what we have said at Deut. 23, 21.

Latin:

Vers. 3. VOTVM DOMINO VOVERIT, AVT SE CONSTRINXERIT JVRAMENTO) Votum fit Deo, ju- ramentum per Deum. Vota non censebantur obligare nisi verbis prolata: ut hîc & Deut. 23, 23. Voveri autem nihil debebat, nisi quod ad Dei honorem aut pietatem pertinebat, ut Naziræatus, victimæ, pecuniæ in usus Templi aut pau- perum, jejunia, similesque σκληραγωγίαι.

De votis conf. quæ diximus ad Deut. 23, 21.

## 30:2 Addition
On chapter 30, verse 3. VOW.

The Hebrews make a threefold kind of vows, as Fagius, Münster, and Oleastrius observe. 1. Holy vows, e.g., of offerings, and of those things which the law mentions. 2. Of abstinence, by which they macerate the body. 3. Compelled, which are made through ignorance or error, or through the persuasion or admonition of another. These do not need the resolution of the Sages. Concerning the relaxation of vows, they hand down this rule: He who has bound his soul with a vow shall not violate his word: But others can retract his vow.

Latin:

Ad cap. 30. v. 3. VOTUM.

Triplex votorum genus Ebræi faciunt, ut ob- servat Fagius, Münsterus & Oleastrius. 1. vota sancta v. g. oblationum, & eorum, quorum meminit lex. 2. Abstinentiæ, quibus corpus macerant. 3. Coa- cta, quæ fiunt per ignorantiam vel errorem, vel per alterius persuasionem sive admonitionem. Hæc non egent solutione Sapientum. De votorum relaxatione hanc regulam tradunt: Qui voto con- strinxerit animam suam non violet verbum suum: Sed alii possunt retractare votum ejus.

## 30:3
Vers. 4. WHICH IS IN HER FATHER'S HOUSE) The same in a son. But a daughter, until she had a husband, was accustomed to remain in her father's house: a son, as long as it pleased his father: and those things which were thus in the father's house were nourished by the father's food: but most vows were concerning food. It is required, however, for a vow to be valid, that there be also the just age of the one vowing, which is 13 years in a male, 12 in a female.

See Thomas 2. secundæ q. 88. Bonavent. in 4. sentent. distinct. 38.

IF HER FATHER SHALL HEAR HER VOW) Aptly to this matter Servius on that line of the 11th Aeneid, 'To thee, O Virgin daughter of Latona, dweller of the groves, I myself, the father, vow this handmaid.' Well said 'I myself, the father': because fathers alone have the power of authorization.

AND SHALL HOLD HER PEACE) Euripides, Iphigenia in Aulis: Αὐτὸ δὲ τὸ σιγᾶν ὁμολογοῦντός ἐσι σᾶ (Silence itself is the sign of one agreeing). Taciturnity imitates consent. Cicero, De Inventione, book one. See the law 'Qui tacet' (He who is silent), D. de reg. juris. Paulus, Sententiarum book 1, tit. 9, concerning Minors. Facundus, book 8. But this very fact that they were silent in time, when they lacked neither great knowledge to understand nor suitable speech to respond, can deservedly be held as consent.

Latin:

Vers. 4. QVÆ EST IN DOMO PATRIS SVI) Idem in filio. Sed filia donec maritum haberet sulebat in patris manere domo: filius quamdiu patri placeret: quæ autem sic in domo erant patris, cibo patris alebantur: pleraque au- tem vota de cibo. Requiritur autem, ut votum valeat, justa etiam ætas voventis, quæ est annorum 13. in mare, 12. in fœmina.

Videatur Thomas 2. secundæ q. 88. Bonavent. in 4. sentent. distinct. 38.

SI COGNOVERIT PATER VOTVM) Apposite ad hanc rem Servius ad illud 11. Æneidos, Alma tibi hanc nemorum cultrix Latonia Virgo Ipse pater famulam voveo. Bene ipse pater: quia auctoramenti potestatem nisi patres non habent.

ET TACVERIT) Euripides Iphigenea in Aulide: Αὐτὸ δὲ τὸ σιγᾶν ὁμολογοῦντός ἐσι σᾶ. Taciturnitas consensionem imitatur. Cicero de inventione primo. Vide l. Qui tacet. D. de reg. juris. Paulum senten- tiarum libro 1. tit. 9. de Minoribus. Facundus libro 8. At hoc ipsum quod tacuerunt in tempore, cum eis ad intelligendum magna scientia, & ad respondendum sermo non defuisset idone- us, pro consensu teneri merito potest.

## 30:8 Addition
Verse 9. IF HE SHALL MAKE VOID.

It is asked what the difference is between this law and that in verse 10. Bonfrerius answers, and Matthew Poole from him: That this deals with the vows of a wife or a newly married bride, but who is still in her father's house, which is to be understood from the preceding law. For it could rightly be doubted whether, and by whom, those vows could be made void, by the parent or the husband. Augustine holds that this deals with vows which a girl vowed before she married, which, after she had married, the husband could make void; which is not in doubt, if they prejudiced his right. Verse 11 deals with a wife already brought to the husband's house. I add what the same author has on verse 10: I understand here also, from verse 4, concerning a widow, etc., who might be outside her father's house. Scripture wished to deal with a woman constituted in any state, but who lived in her father's house, before it came to a married woman.

Latin:

Vers. 9. SI IRRITAS FECERIT.

Quæritur, quid intersit inter hanc legem & illam vers. 10. Respondet Bonfrerius, & ex eo Matth. Polus. Quod hic agatur de votis uxoris vel sponsæ recens nuptæ, sed quæ adhuc est in domo Patris sui, quod ex præcedenti lege intelligendum. Merito enim dubitari possit an, & a quo ea vota ir- ritari possent, a parente an marito. Augustinus vult hic agi de votis quæ vovit puella, antequam nuberet, quæ postquam nupsisset, maritus irritare potuit; quod non est dubium, si suo juri præjudi- carent. Vers. 11. agit de uxore jam ad mariti do- mum traducta. Addo quæ ad vers. 10. idem ha- bet: Intelligo & hic ex versu 4. de vidua &c. quæ extra domum Patris esset. Voluit Scriptura de muliere in quocunque statu constituta, sed quæ in domo Patris ha- bitaret, prius agere, quam ad conjugatam veniret.

## 30:13 Addition
Verse 14. AS BY FASTING.

The Jews indeed restrict this only to vows of fasting, but others more correctly establish that the reason for the rest is the same, and they say that these things are added concerning fasting rather for amplification than for limitation or restriction. They think, however, that mention of these was made primarily because it happens more frequently in these that husbands resist their wives: 1. Because these are more evident. 2. Such things diminish the beauty of wives and weaken them. See Cornelius a Lapide and Bonfrerius.

Latin:

Vers. 14. UT PER JEJUNIUM.

Judæi hoc quidem ad vota jejunii solum re- stringunt, sed rectius alii eandem reliquorum ra- tionem esse statuunt, & addi hæc de jejunio potius in amplificationem, quam in limitationem, vel restrictionem ajunt. Mentionem autem horum imprimis factam putant, quia in his frequentius contingit maritos uxoribus resistere, 1. quod hæc magis pateant. 2. Uxorum formam talia minuant, easque debilitent. Vid. Cornelius a Lapide & Bonfrerius.

## 30:15 Addition
Verse 16. AFTER HE KNEW.

This law is not superfluous. For the question was, What if after the parent or husband has been silent, and the vow is thus confirmed, they nevertheless afterwards object and do not wish the vow to be fulfilled? God answers, In that case the woman shall be free from the fulfillment of the vow, but they shall bear her iniquity or punishment.

Latin:

Vers. 16. POSTQVAM RESCIVIT.

Non superfluit hæc lex. Quæstio enim erat, Quid si postquam Parens vel maritus tacuit, & sic firmatum est votum, ipsi tamen postea repugnent, & votum adimpleri nolint? Respondet Deus, Eo casu libera erit mulier ab impletione voti, at illi portabunt iniquitatem vel pœnam ejus.

## 31:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXI. The slaughter of the Midianites.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXI. Cædes Midianitarum.

## 31:6 Addition
On chapter 31, verse 6. WHEN PHINEHAS. at page 549, a.

Because he had already previously given an excellent specimen of fortitude and divine zeal, chap. 25, Moses makes him as it were the leader of this expedition, as Osiander rightly says. Bonfrerius indeed prefers to appoint Joshua as leader here. But there is nothing in the text about Joshua: therefore Menochius and Cornelius more rightly leave this to Phinehas, and Polus himself here, contrary to his custom, deserts Bonfrerius. By the name of the sacred vessels, the ark is understood from Num. 14, verse 44, by most, because it consisted of various parts: some, however, understand the trumpets themselves, so that the vav is exegetical, in this way: Vessels and trumpets, for vessels, that is, trumpets, as in Gen. 13, verse 15. Thus Oleaster, Vatablus, Piscator, Ainsworth. Which is more convenient.

Latin:

Ad cap. 31. vers. 6. CUM PHINEES. ad pag. 549. a.

Quia jam antea fortitudinis & Zeli divini specimen egregium dederat, cap. 25. Moses eum facit hujus expeditionis quasi Principem, ut recte Osiander. Bonfrerius quidem mavult Josuam hic Ducem constituere. Sed de Josua nihil in textu habetur: Ideo rectius Menochius & Cornelius Phinees hoc relinquunt, & deserit Polus ipse hic, præter morem, Bonfrerium. Vasorum sacrorum nomine arca intelligitur e Num. 14. versu 44. a plerisque, quia variis partibus constabat: nonnulli tamen ipsas tubas intelligunt, ut vav exegeticum sit, hoc modo: Vasa & tubæ, pro vasa, id est, tubæ, ut Genes. 13. vers. 15. Ita Oleaster, Vatablus, Piscator, Ainsworthus. Quod commodius est.

## 31:7
Ver. 7. AND WHEN THEY HAD FOUGHT AGAINST THE MIDIANITES) In the Hebrew: They pitched camp against the Midianites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. Namely, with some part left free from the camp, through which the Midianites, if they wished, might escape; so the Hebrews will have it. See what we have said in book 3 of the Law of War and Peace 11, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 7. CUMQVE PUGNASSENT CONTRA MA- DIANITAS) In Hebræo: Castra posuere contra Madianitas, ita ut Dominus Mosi præceperat. Nempe aliqua parte libera relicta a castris, per quam Madianitæ, si vellent, effugerent, ita volunt Hebræi. Vide quæ diximus libro 3. de Jure Belli ac Pacis 11, 14.

## 31:7 Addition
Vers. 7. THEY SLEW ALL THE MALES.

Namely, those who were captured in this battle; meanwhile, many could have fled, who afterwards grew in number and power, Jud. 6, as the elder B. Quistorp holds.

Latin:

Vers. 7. OMNES MARES OCCIDERUNT.

Nempe qui in hoc prælio capti erant; Interim multi potuerunt aufugere, qui postea numero & potentia creverunt Jud. 6. ut B. Quistorp. Senior habet.

## 31:8
Ver. 8. THEIR KINGS) Kings of their own peoples, but under the King of the Midianites; such as were many in Persia. Aeschylus in the Persians: Βασιλεῖς βασιλέως ὕποχοι μεγάλυ. AND THEY ALSO SLEW BALAAM THE SON OF BEOR WITH THE SWORD) Who, having set out for Syria when he had learned of the slaughter of 24,000 Israelites, selling this fruit of his counsels, had come to receive his reward, the price from the Midianites. Thus the Hebrews, with whom Rev. 2, ver. 14 agrees.

Latin:

Vers. 8. REGES EORUM) Reges suorum populorum, sed sub Rege Madianitarum; quales multi in Perside. Æschy- lus Persis: Βασιλεῖς βασιλέως ὕποχοι μεγάλυ. BALAAM QUOQUE FILIUM BEOR INTERFE- CERVNT GLADIO) Qui in Syriam profectus cùm intel- lexisset occidionem 24. millium IsraëBackgroundITARUM, suorum consi- liorum hunc fructum venditans, mercedem a Madianitis pretium venerat. Sic Hebræi, quibuscum consentit Apoc. 2. vers. 14.

## 31:8 Addition
Vers. 8. AND BALAAM.

Others, among whom is Tirinus, prefer that he had still remained among his friends in some part of Midian, intending to cross over into Mesopotamia when it was convenient, not without divine providence, so that, lingering on the way with the perishing Midianites, he, the author of the crime, might perish at the same time.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET BALAAM.

Alii, inter quos Tirinus, malunt ipsum hæsisse adhuc inter amicos in parte aliqua Madianitidis, inde in Mesopotamiam, quando commodum fuerit, trajecturum non absque divina providentia, ut hæsitans in via cum pereuntibus Madianitis ipse autor flagitii simul periret.

## 31:12
Ver. 12. THE PREY AND ALL THINGS THAT HAD BEEN TAKEN AS WELL FROM MEN AS FROM BEASTS) So also, for the most part, the Greeks. In the Hebrew there are three nouns, of which שבי signifies captive men, מלקוח captured animals, שלל captured goods.

Here the Vulgate contradicts the Hebrew, as Steuchus noted: because it is added in the Vulgate: But the remaining utensils they carried to the camp. A double error: For both the utensils are wrongly added, about which there is nothing in the Hebrew, and the camp is ineptly distinguished from the assembly of the Israelites.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PRÆDAM ET UNIVERSA QVÆ COEPE- RANT TAM EX HOMINIBUS QVAM EX JUMEN- TIS) Sic ferme & Græci. In Ebræo tria sunt nomina, quo- rum שבי homines captivos significat, מלקוח animalia capta, שלל res captas.

REpugnat hic Vulgata Ebrææ, ut notavit Steu- chus: quia additur in Vulgata: Reliqua autem utensilia portaverunt ad castra. Error geminus: Nam & perperam adduntur utensilia, de quibus ni- hil in Ebræo, & inepte castra a cœtu Israelitarum di- stinguuntur.

## 31:17 Addition
vers. 17. KILL ALL.

This is a notable example of the most severe wrath of GOD; and the women indeed were killed because the Israelites had been deceived by them, and could have been deceived again; but the little ones, so that the whole nation might perish with the hope of posterity cut off, and that for the greater detestation of the crime and the punishment of the parents in them, and so that the little ones might not avenge the slaughter of their parents.

Latin:

vers. 17. CUNCTOS INTERFICITE.

Exemplum hoc insigne est severissimæ DEI iræ; & mulieres quidem occisæ sunt, quod per easdem decepti sint Israëlitæ, rursumque decipi potuissent; parvuli autem, ut tota gens posteritatis spe recisa interiret, idque ad majorem detestationem facinoris & parentum in ipsis punitionem, & ne parvuli parentum necem ulciscerentur.

## 31:18 Addition
Vers. 18. KEEP THE VIRGINS.

As wives or handmaids, so that for that reason they might still be able to be converted to the acknowledgment of the true GOD.

Latin:

Vers. 18. VIRGINES RESERVATE.

In conjuges, vel ancillas, ut quæ ea ratione adhuc ad agnitionem veri DEI converti potuerint.

## 31:19 Addition
Verse 19. WHOEVER HAS KILLED &c. SHALL BE PURIFIED.

The observation of B. Osiander is beautiful: Although the slaughter of the Midianites in this place was a good work, since it was commanded and ordered by God: nevertheless the soldiers are commanded to cleanse and expiate themselves: so that it may be signified that such is the corruption of our nature that, even when doing good works, we nevertheless mix in some sin; so that even when doing well, we must nevertheless pray: Forgive us our debts etc. so that we may be cleansed from sins by faith in Christ.

Latin:

Versus 19. QUI OCCIDERIT &c. LUSTRABITUR.

Pulchra est observatio B. Osiandri: Tametsi cædes Madianitarum hoc loco bonum opus erat; quippe a Deo præceptum & mandatum: tamen emundare sese, & expiare jubentur milites: ut significetur, tantam esse naturæ nostræ corruptionem, ut etiam bona opera facientes, nonnihil tamen peccati admisceamus; ita ut etiam bene agentes, tamen orare opor- teat: Remitte nobis debita nostra &c. ut fide in Christum purgemur a peccatis.

## 31:21 Addition
Verse 21. THIS IS THE PRECEPT OF THE LAW.

There is no reason why we should have recourse with Menochius to some precept handed down by word of mouth only: since what is commanded in verse 17 is taken from Num. 25:17: so that this, which is now commanded, can be understood here with Osiander: as if to say, you shall observe this statute imposed by the command of GOD, in purifying or expiating the booty taken from the enemies.

Latin:

Vers. 21. HOC EST PRÆCEPTUM LEGIS.

Non est, quod cum Menochio ad præceptum aliquod voce tantum traditum recurramus: quum quod versu 17. præceptum e Num. 25, 17. habeatur: ut hoc, quod nunc præcipitur, intelligi hic possit cum Osiandro: q. d. hoc statutum ex mandato DEI imposserum observabitis, in lustranda seu expianda præda capta de hostibus.

## 31:23
Ver. 23. BUT WHATEVER SHALL NOT BE ABLE TO ENDURE FIRE, IT SHALL BE SANCTIFIED BY THE WATER OF EXPIATION) Two things were believed to have a cleansing power: Fire by burning, water by washing. Porphyry teaches us that the Egyptians also thought the same.

Latin:

Vers. 23. QVICQVID AUTEM IGNEM NON PO- TERIT SVSTINERE, AQVA EXPIATIONIS SAN- CTIFICABITUR) Duo credita vim habere purgantem: Ignis exurendo, aqua eluendo. Ita & Ægyptios censuisse do- cet nos Porphyrius.

## 31:27 Addition
Verse 27. YOU SHALL DIVIDE EQUALLY.

Thus those fighting (who were only 12,000) received half of the entire booty; which was far more than fell to each one of the crowd; and deservedly so, since the others did not endure the hazard of the battle. You will say, there was an equal share for the one going to war and the one remaining with the baggage, 1 Sam. 30:24. I reply: It is no wonder, since they themselves had also set out with their minds prepared for fighting, and had sat down because of exhaustion, so that with their bodies refreshed they might also rush upon the enemies, and they had not been entirely out of danger. Thus Polus from Bonfrerius and Cornelius a Lapide. See also here our Osiander.

Latin:

Vers. 27. DIVIDES EX ÆQVO.

Ita pugnantes (qui tantum 12000. erant) dimidium totius prædæ acceperunt: quod longe plus erat, quam singulis e turba obtigit; & merito, cum reliqui pugnæ aleam non sustinerent. Dices, Æqua sors erat eunti ad bellum, & manenti ad sarcinas 1. Sam. 30, 24. Resp. Nihil mirum, cum & ipsi animo ad pugnandum comparato egressi essent, & præ lassitudine consedissent, ut refecto corpore etiam in hostes irruerent, nec omnino extra periculum fuissent. Ita e Bonfrerio & Cornelio a Lapide Polus. Vid. & hic Osiander noster.

## 31:35
Ver. 35. THE SOULS OF MEN OF THE FEMALE SEX) It is noted here that the noun אדם pertains to both sexes.

Latin:

Vers. 35. ANIMÆ HOMINUM SEXUS FEMINEI) Notatur hic nomen אדם ad utrumque sexum pertinere.

## 31:53
Ver. 53. FOR EVERY MAN HAD TAKEN WHAT HE HAD SEIZED IN THE PREY, IT WAS HIS OWN) Understand prey here strictly: excluding the captives and the living creatures, about which [we spoke] above.

Latin:

Vers. 53. VNVSQVISQVE ENIM QVOD IN PRÆ- DA RAPUERAT, SUUM ERAT) Prædam hic stricte in- tellige: exceptis captivis & animantibus, de quibus supra.

## 32:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXII. The portion of Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXII. Portio Rubenis, Gad, & dimidiæ tribus Ma- nassis.

## 32:3
Ver. 3. AND BEON) So also in the Hebrew בען: but one must consider whether it might have been written מען as below 38, and Josh. 13, 18. There is no need for this suspicion: For it is known that proper names, as in other languages, so also in Hebrew very often vary as to syllables or letters, and their permutation or transposition, likewise contraction, or addition, and other variations of that kind. Thus the city Behon is called by contraction Bahalmehon v. 38: and Bet Bahalmehon Josh. 13, 17, and again by another syncope and contraction Bethmehon Jer. 28, 13. Will you carve out as many corruptions from that? Let us be silent about others of that kind. For they are met with everywhere. But far be it from us that we should either ourselves build up, or allow to be built up, a corruption of the sacred fountains on account of such jejune suspicions.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET BEON) Sic & in Ebræo בען: sed cogitan- dum, an non scriptum fuerit מען ut infra 38. & Jos. 13,18. NOn opus hac suspicione: Notum enim est, quod nomina propria, ut in aliis linguis, ita etiam in Ebræa sæpissime varient, quoad syllabas aut literas, earumque permutationem aut transposi- tionem, contractionem item, vel additionem, & quæ ejus generis aliæ sunt variationes. Ita Civitas Be- hon per contractionem nuncupata, Bahalmehon v. 38. vocatur: & Bet Bahalmehon Jos. 13, 17. ac rursus per aliam syncopen & contractionem Bethmehon Jer. 28, 13. Num totidem inde exsculpes deprava- tiones? Alia ejus generis taceamus. Passim enim obvia sunt. Absit vero, ut jejunis ejusmodi suspi- cionibus depravationem fontium sacrorum aut su- perstruamus ipsi, aut superstrui patiamur.

## 32:6
Ver. 6. YOUR BRETHREN SHALL GO TO THE FIGHT, AND YOU SHALL SIT HERE) It is unjust for honey to be eaten by drones, says Belisarius in a similar case in Procopius.

Latin:

Vers.6. FRATRES VESTRI IBVNT AD PVGNAM, ET VOS HIC SEDEBITIS) Iniquum est mel a fucis edi, ait in simili re Belisarius apud Procopium.

## 32:11
Ver. 11. IF THEY SHALL SEE) A formula of swearing. It is understood: may it not be held as God. There is no need for such an ellipsis, which is certainly harsh and profane, if the particle אם is explained from philological observation, that the particle אם לא strongly affirms, truly, entirely, but the little word אם without לא strongly denies, as Gen. 21, 23. Behold, אם Do not lie to me, c. 24, 38. אם לא truly you shall go.

Latin:

Vers. 11. SI VIDEBVNT) Formula jurandi, Subauditur, ne pro Deo habear. Ellipsi tali, quæ horrida utiq; & prophana, opus non est, si explicetur particula אם ex observa- tione Philologica, quod particula אם לא vehe- menter affirmet, profecto, omnino, vocula autem אם sine לא vehementer neget, ut Gen, 21, 23. Ecce, אם Ne mentiaris mihi, c. 24, 38. אם לא profecto ibis.

## 32:12
Ver. 12. AND THEY WOULD NOT FOLLOW ME) In Hebrew: They did not complete after me, that is, they did not perfectly follow me. See above 14,24.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET NOLVERVNT SEQVI ME) In Hebr. Non compleverunt post me, id est, non perfecte me sequuti sunt. Vide supra 14,24.

## 32:12 Addition
To chapter 32, verse 12. EXCEPT CALEB THE SON OF JEPHUNNEH THE KENIZZITE.

Not that Jephunneh was also called Kenez, as Sa wishes: but because some one of the ancestors was called Kenez, who however is not to be confused with the parent of Othniel, who was also so named. For if Caleb had been the brother of Othniel, which he wishes, then he would not have married the daughter of Caleb, since this is contrary to the law, Lev. 18:14. And therefore either the name of brother in Jos. 15:17, Jud. 1:13 is to be taken generally for any kinsman, or, since that is less consistent with the accurate genealogy which is held there, the Hebrew words there are to be translated in this manner: Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took her, as Pagninus and Arias Montanus translated, by which arrangement Othniel married his cousin, which was not contrary to the law. And therefore Bellarmine in his work on matrimony, ch. 27, rashly urges this example to prove that the Saints joined in marriages in the degrees prohibited in Leviticus. We have here the Jesuit Bonfrerius agreeing.

Latin:

Ad cap. 32. vers. 12. PRÆTER CALEB FILIUM JEPHUNNE KENEZÆUM.

Non quod Jephonne etiam Kenez dictus, ut Sa vult: sed quia aliquis e majoribus Kenez vocatus, qui tamen confundendus non est cum Othonielis Parente, ita etiam nuncupato. Nam si Caleb Othonielis frater fuisset, quod ille vult, tum non duxisset filiam Caleb, siquidem hoc legi adversetur Lev. 18, 14. Ideoque vel nomen fratris Jos. 15. v. 7. Jud. 1, 13. generaliter pro quolibet cognato accipiendum, vel quum id minus congruat accuratæ, quæ ibi habetur, genealogiæ, verba Ebræa ibi vertenda h. m. erunt: Cepit eam Othoniel filius Cenaz fratris Caleb, ut Pagninus & Arias Montanus verterunt, quo pacto Othoniel patruelem suam in uxorem duxit, quod legi non adversabatur. Ideoque temere Bellarminus de matrimonio c. 27. hoc exemplum urget ad probandum Sanctos in gradibus in Levitico prohibitis connubia junxisse. Habemus hic Bonfrerium Jesuitam consentientem.

## 32:33
Ver. 33. AND TO THE HALF TRIBE OF MANASSEH) These things are to be understood from this place, where mention is made above of Reuben and Gad. Nor are nine solid parts commemorated, but rather the particles of the past; the Samaritan, as in other places, so here out of excessive diligence, also added this half-tribe in the previous places, which is also noted here in the Greek scholia. Ver. 38. WITH CHANGED NAMES) As victors are accustomed to do.

Latin:

Vers. 33. ET DIMIDIÆ TRIBVI MANASSIS) Hæc subintelligenda ex hoc loco, ubi supra Rubenis & Gadis fit mentio. Neque novem solidas partes commemorari, præter- iti vero particulas, Samaritanus ut in aliis, ita hic nimiæ di- ligentiæ, etiam locis superioribus dimidiam hanc tribum semper addidit, quod & in scholiis Græcis hic annotatum. Vers.38.VERSIS NOMINIBVS)Vt solent facere victores.

## 32:39 Addition
Verse 39. THEY WENT INTO GILEAD. at p. 549. b.

More specifically so called: for otherwise they were already in Gilead. For the word Gilead is taken 1. most broadly for the whole land across the Jordan, verses 26, 29; 2. more strictly, for the portion of the tribe of Gad and the half of Manasseh; 3. most strictly for the region of the half-tribe of Manasseh, and it does not even comprehend all of it: for they occupied the kingdom of Bashan besides this. See Jos. 13:29.

Latin:

Vers. 39. PERREXERUNT IN GALAAD. ad p. 549. b.

Specialius ita dictam: nam alias jam erant in Galaad. Vox enim Galaad sumitur 1. fusissime pro tota terra trans Jordanem, versu 26. 29. 2. pressius, pro portione tribus Gad & dimidiæ Manasse; 3. pressissime pro regione dimidiæ tribus Menasse, nec quidem eam totam comprehendit: nam præter hanc & regnum Basan occuparunt. Vid. Jos. 13. vers. 29.

## 32:40
v. 40. MACHIR THE SON OF MANASSEH.

He was indeed the son of Segub from the tribe of Judah, but he is reckoned among the Manassites, both by reason of inheritance and also of his grandmother. For the daughter of Machir the Manassite, father of Gilead, bore Segub to Hezron, who was sixty years old, the father of Jair, 1 Chron. 2, 21. 22. Doubtless Jair took the whole tract of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maachathites, and called the villages of Bashan taken by him by his own name, Havoth-Jair, whence 1 Chron. 2, 21. 22 it is said that he possessed 23 cities in the land of Gilead and had taken Geshur and Aram, with the villages of Jair, and also Kenath with its villages, 60 cities: although under Kenath with its villages Nobah had taken them, and called them Nobah after his own name, as is reported here in v. 42.

Latin:

v.40. MACHIR FILIO MANASSE.

Fuit ille quidem Segubi e tribu Juda filius, sed Manassitis accensetur, tum hæreditatis ratione,tum etiam aviæ. Filia enim Machiris Manassitæ, patris Gileadis, Hezroni sexagenario Segubum peperit, Patrem Jairis 1. Chron. 2, 21.22. Nimirum totum tra- ctum Argobi usque ad terminum Geshuritarum & Mahacathitarum cepit Jair,& villas Basanis a se ca- ptas vocavit de nomine suo Havoth Jair, unde 1. Chron. 2,21.22. dicitur possedisse 23. civitates in ter- ra Gilead & cepisse Gessurem,& Aramum, cum villis Jairis, Kenatham quoq; cum villis ejus 60. civitates: licet sub Kenatham cum villis ejus Nobachus cepe- rit,& de nomine suo Nobachum appellaverit, ut hic v. 42. refertur.

## 32:40 Addition
Verse 40. MACHIR.

That is, to the sons of Machir, as in Jud. 1:3. For if Machir himself were understood, he would have been at least 210 years old at that time.

Latin:

Vers. 40. MACHIR.

Id est, filiis Machir, ut Jud. 1, 3. Nam si Machir ipse intelligeretur, ad minimum 210. annorum tum fuisset.

## 33:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIII. The 42 encampments of the Israelites. Concerning the extermination of the Canaanites and their idols.

Ver. 1. THESE ARE THE ENCAMPMENTS OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. Jerome explains these 42 encampments in a special treatise to Fabiola mystically, which may be seen. I. Rameses: Exod. 12, 37. Where they had been placed by Joseph Gen. 47, 11, and there they had all gathered among the Egyptians, scattered to seek stubble Ex. 5, 12, no less than those who lived mixed with the Egyptians c. 3, 22. II. Succoth v. 5 here: Ex. 13, 20, where Moses gave them commands concerning the annual rite of the Passover and the consecration of the firstborn. III. Etham in the extremity of the desert v. 6, where they were led by the pillar of fire and cloud going before, Ex. 13, 20. 21. IV. Pi-Hahiroth between Migdol and the sea over against Baal-Zephon v. 7 here, where Pharaoh with his army overtook them, and they were led through the Red Sea into the desert of Etham Ex. 14, and in the Canticle, which is the first and most ancient of all, Ex. 15, 1, Ap. 15, 3, they celebrated God as the author of the victory. Which the Hebrews say was done on the 21st day of the 1st month, that is, the last day of unleavened bread, on which a holy convocation was to be held according to God's institution, Exod. 12, 16. Thence, by a continuous three-day journey on the 22nd, 23rd, and 24th days, they proceeded through the desert of Etham, finding no water, v. 8 here, Ex. 15, 22, until V. in Marah they found bitter waters, which Moses indeed made sweet, Ex. 15, 23. VI. In Elim there were 12 springs of water and 70 palm trees, where the Israelites encamped, v. 9 here, Ex. 15, 27. VII. By the Red Sea, v. 10 here. VIII. The desert of Sin between Elim and Sinai, where they arrived on the 15th day of the 2nd month, where they received quails in the evening and manna in the morning, Exod. 16. IX. Dophkah, v. 12 here. X. Alush, v. 13. XI. Rephidim, where water was supplied from the Rock, v. 14 here, when the people murmured, whence the name Meribah and Massah was given to the place. Conf. Ex. 17, Deut. 9, 21, Ps. 78, 16, 20, Ps. 105, 41. And Joshua defeated the Amalekites who were attacking the weary people and striking those who were weakened in the rear guard, Ex. 17, 8, Deut. 25, 17. XII. The desert of Sinai, where they encamped on the third day of the third month, and remained for almost an entire year over against Mount Horeb, because in the 2nd year from the exodus, on the 20th day of the 2nd month, they moved from there, Num. 10, 11, 12. For there the law was promulgated, Ex. 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, Deut. 4, 13, 14, for 10 days and nights Moses was on the mountain with God, Ex. 24, 9, Deut. 9, 9, and he received the commands proposed concerning the structure of the tabernacle, the priests, and the sacrifices, Ex. 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31. In the fourth month, when those 40 days were finished, Moses broke the tablets of the law, skillfully made by the hand of God and written by the finger of God, because of the people's calf-worship, Ex. 32. Afterwards, having been reconciled by the prayers of God, he fashioned other tablets at His command, and having stayed on the mountain again for 40 days, he brought back from the mountain the Decalogue, written anew by God Himself on the tablets, Ex. 34. And he proposed the divine commands, primarily concerning the observance of the Sabbath and the offering for the work of the tabernacle, c. 35, which contribution was made c. 36, 6. 38, 24, and the work was fabricated in the first semester of this year, which was 2514 from the creation of the world, with the equipment pertaining to it, Ex. 36. 37. 38. Whence, in the second year of the exodus, on the first day of the first month, after Moses had received the express command concerning it, the tabernacle was erected and filled with the glory of God, Ex. 40, from which God delivered to Moses at intervals those laws which are described in the 7 prior chapters of Leviticus. In the same year, in the first month, the Israelites, warned by God, celebrated the second Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day.
