Nec est quod ob- jiciatur juramentum per pavorem Isaaci Gen. 31, 52. item per vitam Pharaonis Gen. 42, 15. Nam ibi per pavorem Isaaci Deus ipse intelligitur, quem coluit & timuit Isaacus, Confer. Es. 8, 13. Hìc vero non ju- ramentum sed obtestatio solum est: atque ea ratio- ne etiam obtestari solemus, per Evangelium vel veritatem Evangelii, ubi juramus per Deum. Cum autem formula adhibetur: ita me Deus adjuvet & sanctum ejus Evangelium, non per Evangelium juramus, sed hic est formulae sensus, ut me Deus adjuvet per sancta Evangelia. Non ergo est, quod hanc formulam arguat Rivetus in Explic. Decal p. 88. quasi superstitionis Papisticae reliquiae eadem contineantur. Videre potius debuisset, quomodo exculpari posset Calvinus, in Harmonia ad Matth. 23. 16. seqq. cum non improbat juramenta omnia per creaturas concepta, sed ea tantum, quae transcribunt creaturis quod Dei est, quem defendere non potuit Spanhemius part. 2. Dub. 124. §. 9. Matth. 23. Christus docet solum juramenta per templum, & altare concepta in se redundare & obligatoria esse, non autem probat ea, sed perstringit, ut hypocritica, & contumeliosa in se. Neque vero omnia licita, ut fiant, quae obligatoria, postquam facta sunt.

Est autem juramentum si in genere illud definiendum orationis confirmatio, per Dei attestationem. Nonnulli addunt execrationem, quod vel aperte vel tacite Deus ut judex supplicium pro perjurio decernens appelletur, non tantum ut testis. Sed non est in omni juramento execratio. Jurat & Deus, sed citra execrationem. Dicunt quidem Deum non jurare, sed quasi jurantem tantum induci, cum asseverantius promittit. At Petrus & promissum & juramentum Deo attribuit Act. 2. 30. ut & Paulus Ebr. 6, 16. ubi haec duo tanquam distincta proponuntur. Jurat ergo Deus, licet non possit juramentum execratorium praestare, quod ad superiorem respicit, qui perdere potest, & ejus solum est, qui potest delinquere ac peierare. Unde distinguendum inter juramentum simplex & execratorium. Cum vero hic praecipiatur in nomine Domini juretis, manifestum est, juramentum esse licitum. Essaei omne juramentum prohibuisse videntur. Vid. Joseph. lib. 2. de Bell. Jud. c. 7. quod etiam Manichaeis tribuitur, sed illos per Paracletum jurasse Aug. refert. Pelagius juramentum in N. T. prohibitum esse contendit in Epist. ad Demetr. apud Hieron. T. 2. oper. p. 20. vid. & T. 4. Hieron. ad Coelest. p. 63. Quem sequuntur Anabaptistae in Coll. Embd. qui tamen in Coll. Franck. art. 11. errore illo misso rectius se declararent, quod tantum vana, futilia & temeraria juramenta improbanda sint. Sociniani licere quidem Christiano jurare fatentur, sed non ita id licere, ut olim in V. T. licitum fuerit, nempe quavis de causa jurare, modo quis non peieraret. Quod ideo contendunt, ut Christum aliquid huic praecepto addidisse obtineant, quod non solum non intellectum fuerit a Pharisaeis, sed quod & verbis legis significatum non fuerit, nimirum ut non juretur temere aut irreverenter. Quo etiam abit Maldonatus in cap. 5. Matth. Sed recte observat Schvvarez, Tom. 2. de Relig. lib. 1. de jur. cap. 2. fuisse illam falsam Judaeorum (tempore Nov. Testam. Pharisaeorum) opinionem, non peccari jurando, modo perjurium vitetur. Non fuit Christus novus νομοθέτης, nec indigebat lex quae perfecta est regula justitiae, aliquo adjumento, sed repurgatione a corruptelis Pharisaicis opus erat. Praeceptum de non assumendo nomine Domini in vanum perjurium tantum, sed quodlibet etiam vanum & temerarium juramentum prohibet, uti vox שָׁוְא non tantum falsum & dolosum sed quicquid vanum, frustraneum ac leve est, notat, Psal. 127, 2. Jer. 4. 30. Mal. 3. 14. ideo tria haec requiruntur ad juramentum Jer. 4, 2. jures vere, id est, sine fuco & simulatione ac fraude; rite: id est, non temerario & praecipiti casu, sed ubi necessitas postulat: ac juste, id est, in rebus justis ac licitis, & di- gnis, quæ juramento confirmentur. Adde inter- pretationem Hiero-Pfaltis Pf. 15, 4. & Syracid. c. 23, 10. 17.

Quod ad verba Christi Matth. 5, 34. (quibus gemina sunt Jacobi c. 5, 20.) non illa ad legem Mofis perficiendam sed Pharisæorum corruptelam emendan- dam pertinent, non autem juramentum simpliciter prohibent, uti videntur accepisse Bafil. in Pf. 15. Chrys. hom. XVII. in Matth. & Theophyl. in c. V. Matth. in quam sententiam de juramento in N. T. prohibito Sixtus Senensis l. VI. Bibl. S. annotat. 26. adduxit & Athanas. Epiph. Hilarium. Sed ple- rique illi benignius explicari fortassis poterunt. Non solum in V. T. sed etiam in N. jurarunt pii & Sancti homines. Rom. 1, 9. c. 9, 2. 1. Cor. 15, 31. Ebr. 1, 20. Gal. 1, 20. Phil. 1, 8. 1. Thess. 2, 5. 2. Thess. 2, 1. Et habentur de juramentis tempore N. T. Pro- phetiæ Es. 45, 24. Jerem. 12, 16. Grotius lib. II. de jure belli & Pacis c. 13. respondet, non juramentum assertorium, sed promissorium interdici a Christo. Sed nec omne promissorium juramentum illicitum est: alioquin facile omnes contractus in civili so- cietate abolendi erunt, neque Reges ac Principes mutuo pacisci poterunt, neque subditi præstare homagium, aut juramento fidem suam astringere, ideoque promissoria juramenta minime interdicta sunt: de quibus observandum, quod etiam de fu- turis fiant: nec semper eventus in promittentium manu sit; iisdem non tam adseratur rei promissæ eventus infallibilis, quam stabiliatur propositum & voluntas promittentis. Neque admittunt verba Christi hanc restrictionem. Probandum enim ef- set Pharisæos, contra quos agit Christus, perjurium non agnovisse nisi in promissionibus juramento con- firmatis, non item in assertionibus & testimoniis ju- ratis, imo legem de perjuriis vitandis non ulterius respexisse. Alii ergo (2.) putant, Christum prohi- buisse non juramentum simpliciter & absolute, sed formulas juramenti obliquas, & indirectas : quibus putabant Pharisæi, non se magna religione teneri ad præstanda, quæ promiserant, aut non graviter peccare, si sub talibus formulis assererent ea, quæ levia essent, non usurpato directe Dei nomine. (3.) Præstat dicere. omnia juramenta de re inutili, & non necessaria quovis modo præstita contra mandatum Dei prævaricari. Quapropter vetari felicitatem & temeritatem in juramentis, sive no- men Dei directe adhibeatur, sive oblique. Proinde opposita est hæc Christi explicatio & vindicatio le- gis duabus Pharisaicis corruptelis (1.) non esse ju- ramentum, neque obligare ad perjurium, ubi nomen Dei directe non adhibetur, utpote cum per tem- plum vel per altare jurabant. Ubi Pharisæi aurum & donaria templi, ac sacrificia, propter avaritiam templo & altari præferebant. Matth. 23, 16. seqq. Nam & cum per creaturas juratur, oblique, indire- cte, relative, & implicite per Deum juratur. Quo de B. Luther. in enarrat. Secundi Præcepti Tom. II. Witteberg. semper is qui jurat per ea, quæ Dei sunt, vel ei applicata, etiam per Deum jurat, ex quo, in quo & in quem sunt omnia. (2.) Perjuria tan- tum interdicta esse, non autem quævis temeraria juramenta. Ideoque ὅλως omnino jurandum non esse monet Christus; ut illud OMNINO ad subje- ctam materiam referendum sit, neq́; directe neq́; in- directe jurandum esse in communi sermone, ubi nego- tia per simplicem affirmationem aut negationem ex- pediri possunt. Non ergo vox illa ὅλως id importat, quod nullo tempore, aut nullo casu licitum sit jurare. Prohibetur cacoëthes jurandi ex levitate; non pro- hibetur juramentum, quod incumbit ex necessi- tate.

Juramentum ergo aliud est licitum, aliud illi- citum. Licitum, quod non pugnat cum verbo Dei, nec temere, sed ex necessitate, nec nisi de re- bus veris certo cognitis suscipitnr. Illicitum est vel ratione modi, cum non juxta verbum Dei, per nomen Dei, sed per creaturas juramentum fit, uti Pontificii per angelos sanctos & reliquias jurant, vel ratione objecti, cujus gratia fit juramentum: cum de rebus falsis vel impossibilibus, vel incertis vel illi- citis, vel levibus & futilibus suscipitnr. Juramen- ta licita, quæ in Dei & proximi dilectionem non impingunt, servanda omnino sunt, etiam vi aut do- lo extorta, aut latroni & hosti facta, Lev. 19, 11. Matth. 5, 34. Illicita vero per errorem vel infir- mitatem, aut quomodocunque facta, quæ non sine offensa gloriæ Dei & salutis proximi servantur, minime servanda sunt, ne peccatum peccato cu- muletur: quia qui juramentum illicitum servat, bis peccat, semel male jurando, iterum male juratum servando, unde Regulæ: in male promissis rescinde fidem: Quod male juratum pejus servatur. Ideo David juramentum e nimio fervore emissum de delenda tota domo Nabalis recte non servavit. 1. Sam. 25, 21.

Scholastici observant adversus præceptum de juramento peccari sex modis: 1. dum scienter jura- tur falsum, 2. dum dolose juratur verum quod pu- tatur esse falsum, 3. dum ignoranter juratur falsum quod creditur esse verum, 4. Dum non servatur pro- missum juramento firmatum. 5. Dum juratur illi- citum. 6. Dum juratur indiscrete vel temere. Ad- de 7. dum juratur per creaturas, vel idola, non per nomen Dei. Aliud autem est in juramento exe- cratorio, quo vel nos vel nostra, quæ chara habe- mus, devovemus & velut oppignoramus Deo ju- dici, si scientes prudentes fallamus: ita enim non juratur per creaturas, sed tantum nostro sermoni fides adstruitur cum aliqua obtestatione. Vid. Job. 31, 16. seqq. Ps. 7, 5. 6. 8. Dum juratur æquivoce, vel cum reservata mentali conditione. Graviter enim errant Jesuitæ, cum æquivocis juramentis patrocinantur, de quo vid. B. Meisner. Disp. de æ- quivocationibus Jesuiticis. Toletus instruct. Sa- cerdot. lib. IV. c. 21. disputat, aliquando tantum, non autem semper teneri hominem non solum secun- dum mentem propriam jurare, sed etiam secundum mentem aliorum, id est, uti significatione commu- ni, quam qui audit, mente concipit, & non uti aliqua æquivocatione: aliquando tamen non teneri, sed licere uti æquivocatione, & decipere audientem. Item si vir ab uxore petat, an sit adultera, ista po- test dicere non sum, quamvis verum fuerit, intelli- gendo ut tibi revelem. Similiter qui cogitur ju- rare se accepturum aliquam in sponsam, potest ju- rare se accepturum, si postea placuerit. Et c. 20. posse hominem captum a latronibus æquivoce jura- re, ratione coactionis, dicendo: juro me daturum, & intra se, si mihi libuerit, & tunc non teneri, quia absolute non juraverit se daturum. Similia apud Sanchiez, Navarrum, Gregorium de Valentia, Swarezium, Lessium & alios reperias. At Scri- ptura mendacium & dolum omnino prohibet, ma- xime vero in juramentis Levit. 19, 11. Jerem. 9, 8. Psalm. 12, 4. Psalm. 15, 3. 5. Eph. 4, 25. Qua vero veritatis specie negari potest, in talibus æquivocationibus intervenire mendacium & do- lum? Negant hoc Jesuitæ ea προφάσει, quod non animo fallendi, sed seipsum conservandi stu- dio æquivocans falsum enunciet, & inculpatam id vocant tutelam : sed vanum est hoc schema. Qui enim aliud loquitur, aliud corde premit. vel aliter sentit, quam loquitur, is utique alterum fallit, & fallere sermone suo intendit. Id enim quod dicit, non alia mente profert, nisi ut diversam opinionem in alterius animo generet, quod est fallere. Quemcunque igitur finem statuant, sive ut periculum evadant, seu alium quemlibet, medium est dolus, quia fallendo finem consequi intendunt : quod est contra regulam Apostoli Rom. III, 8. malo Ethico mendacio nempe, ac perjurio, malum physicum amoliri : adeoque non inculpata, sed maxime culpanda & improbanda tutela est. Nec vero limitatio in mente reservata prolatis addita veram potest efficere propositionem in Dei conspectu pariter & loquentis sensu, ac mendacio excludendo sufficere. Nam veritas & mendacium respiciunt justitiam & injustitiam, quæ est ad extra, & ad proximum : non ergo ex iis, quæ in animo foventur & retinentur; sed ex iis, quæ sermone proferuntur, æstimanda. Tum vero vel e Logicis constat, nullam esse admittendam limitationem, quæ nec ex verborum varia significatione, aut ancipiti sententiæ compositione, aut ex diversa circumstantiarum dispositione, aut ex loquentis scopo & occasione elici possit. Supplementum autem mentale nihil tale exhibet. Non ergo est limitatio; sed dolus & simulatio. Sed nec æquivocationes proprie sunt istiusmodi æquivocationes: quia nec in terminis simplicibus, nec in complexis hæret æquivocus ille sensus, sed in mente tantum & iis, quæ mente refervantur. Quid, quod mentale reservatum tollat id, quod verbis profertur, contradictorie, non limitet, non verbis ὁμωνύμως sonantibus velatum sistat: v.g. si quæratur: esne Jesuita? & respondeatur, non sum, aperta inficiatione, in mente autem occulterur limitatio (ψευδωνύμως ita dicta) nempe, ut tibi indicem : manifestum est, si hoc reservatum jungatur primæ responsioni, redundaturum non ejusdem limitationem, sed prorsus contradictoriam propositionem h. m. sum quidem Jesuita, non autem teneor tibi indicare : vel si quæratur proditor, aut sicarius, veneritne ad regicidium, vel clandestinas molitiones, & respondeat, se non venisse, cum reservato mentali, non venisse rheda, vel non venisse ex Borussia, vel non venisse Cal. Martii, vel cum intentione se prodendi Magistratui &c. & si exigatur juramentum, id præstet secundum restrictiones suas mentales, etsi præstare videatur secundum sensum quærentis : annon hic dolus, mendacium, perjurium, ludificatio Magistratus, negatio contra conscientiam ejus de quo quæritur? quia non de modo adventus, vel loco aut causis aliis quærebatur, sed de illo fine adventus, quem verba apertissime indicant. Ideoque contradictionem, mendacium, perjurium non excludit diversus respectus, quia is nec ex parte interrogantis vel proponentis attenditur, nec in responsione vel juramento conspicitur. Porro damnat Scriptura palam eos, qui corde aliud sentiunt, aliud loquuntur ore, & vult, ut non tantum coram Deo, sed etiam apud omnium hominum conscientiam in manifestatione veritatis nosmetipsos commendemus. Jer. 9, 8. 2. Cor. 4, 2. At id agnoscit, & confirmat Episcopus Antverpiensis, Malderus tract. de abus. restrict. mental. quod contra veracitatem hoc sit, restrictionis mentalis malagmate corrigere falsitatem enunciationis, quodque hoc sit contra simplicitatem & sinceritatem sermo mixtus ex mentali & verbali exteriori, nec sit loqui veritatem cum proximo, sed mentiri recocto in mente mendacio. Et quomodo juramentum erit omnis controversiæ finis apud homines, uti esse debet, Ebr. 6, 16. si æquivocationibus talibus ac mendaciis in juramento locus esse potest? annon lites ita multiplicabuntur in immensum, cum nihil fit, unde parti alteri constare possit de alterius fide, nec commercia solum ita oporteat perturbari in- ter homines, sed etiam Dei consilium de litibus per juramentum finiendis irritum prorsus redda- tur. Quod si licet enunciationem aperte falsam ex addita, quam pro lubitu quisque concipiat in ani- mo, limitatione veram efficere, frustra latæ erunt leges contra mendacium & perjurium, nec enim re- perietur facile, qui non posset talem limitationem in animo effingere. Frustra erunt judicia, frustra consilia Principum, nec ipse Pontifex cum suis con- sultare, vel pronunciare aliquid poterit in judicio, ubi adhibenda sunt suffragia, vel testimonia, quin eludatur eximie artificio hocce Jesuitico, si reser- vationibus & restrictionibus ejusmodi mentali- bus locus sit, imo casus nullus dari poterit, in quo non vel verum negari, vel falsum asseri, sine men- dacio & perjurio possit, adeoque peribit fides publica, peribit summorum capitum digni- tas & securitas, peribunt omnia commercia, pereunte veritate & sinceritate. Et annon stultos fuisse martyres ac veritati cœlesti sibique maxime injurios credemus, quod hoc artificio se non sup- pliciis & morte crudeli subduxerunt? Supererat enim illis si Jesuitice sapuissent, præsidium istud in- culpatæ tutelæ? Sed nolebant illi æquivocationibus Deo & hominibus illudere more Jesuitico, ut pe- ricula evaderent.

Nec est, quod effugere conentur Jesuitæ di- stinctione inter judicem competentem, & non com- petentem. Nam si judex competens non sit, dicere quidem licebit, non teneri ad respondendum; Ve- rum ubi quis responsum reddit sive judex sit competens, sive non, respondere debet præsertim adhibito juramento, ex veritate. Nec solum do- cent Jesuitæ, quod is, qui inique vel non secundum ordinem juris interrogatur, licet sceleris reus sit, judicem eludere possit per quasdam amphibolo- gias, dicendo, nescio, nimirum, ut dicam tibi, non memini nempe ad dicendum. Tolet. l. c. Lessius l. II. c. 31. dubit. 3. n. 8. Greg. de Valent. Tom. III. Disp. V. q. 13. punct. 2. Sed statuunt etiam nonnulli, quod etiam tunc, quando reus juridice interrogatur non peccet mortaliter, si maxime neget veritatem co- ram judice. Vid. Lessius l. c. n. 16. qui idem tenere quoque Petrum Navarrum & Eman. a Saa in ver- bo Reus, & quosdam alios recentiores observat. Adde Tolet. lib. IV. instr. sac. c. 58. Et editus est a sacerdote Anglicano libellus de equivocandi arte ante ab Archi-Presbytero Angliæ Blackwello & provinciali Henrico Garnetto approbatus, in quo docetur, quomodo subditi Reginæ Angliæ inqui- renti, num Papisticos ministros hospitio excepissent? num Romani peregre abiissent? annon hunc vel illum vidissent, tuto respondere possint, retinendo apud se mentalem propositionem, non vidi, id est, visio- ne beatifica, non illinc veni, ut urbem hanc peste in- ficerem; quod approbat Andreas Eudemon-Johan- nes in Apologia pro Garnetto, & Abrahamum, Christum ac Apostolos autores hujus disciplinæ facit p. 30. 44. in quo libello laudatur quoque Francisci Treshami juramentum, quod conjurationis Hi- spanicæ adversus Regem Angliæ convictus agoni- zans deposuit, se Garnettum sedecim annis transa- ctis non vidisse, sub hac æquivocatione, quod Romæ aut Venetiis eum non viderit, p. 89. 133. Garnetti Jesuitæ perjurium & horrenda execratio de conju- ratione tollendi Regem, & senatum Angliæ per supposita comitiis aliquot pulveriis pyrii dolia, qua elusit summum & legitimum Magistratum, videri poterit in actione proditoria regni Angliæ in Gar- netum & socios pag. 101. Quæ artes adeo detestan- dæ sunt, ut easdem etiam reprobarint ipsimet sin- ceriores Papistæ, utut Navarrus in C. Humanæ Aures 22. q. 5. eas a Magno suo Patriarcha Franci- sco deducat, qui a lictoribus homicidam perse- quentibus interrogatus, an illuc, ubi Franciscus erat, transiisset, immissis manibus intra manicas re- sponderit, hac non transiisse, subintelligendo tacite non transiisse per illas manicas. Ideo reprobat illas reservationes mentales Malderus in Navarro, San- chiez, Valentia, Toleto, Schvarezio, &c. ostendens luculenter, nullum esse exterius prolatum sermo- nem, qui cum alioqui falsus sit, verificari sola additio- ne vel restrictione mentali possit, tract. de abus. re- strict. mental. Refellit easdem & Paulus Laymann. l. IV. Theol. moral. c. 13. Sed imprimis reprobat & refutat eas prolixo de æquivocat. Cemmenta- rio Josephus Barnesius, quem Facultas Theologi- ce Parisiensis judicio suo approbavit. Confer. Tho- mas Morton. Apolog. Cathol. l. II. c. 13. B. Meisn. disp. de æquiv. Papist, Anno 1613. habita.

## 6:16
V. 16. YOU SHALL NOT PUT THE LORD YOUR GOD TO THE TEST.

The testing of God is when divine omnipotence, omniscience, or providence or truth is solicited either through rashness or through incredulity, e.g., when we test God as to whether He can help, Ex. 17. v. 1, 7, or whether He knows what we are attempting, Acts 7, 9. God is also tested when someone precipitates himself into danger out of rashness, for he, relying on no word of God, provokes God, Matt. 4; when we prescribe to God the time and manner, Judith 7, 23, c. 8, 11; when someone pursues things foreign or superior to his own grasp, without his calling and ability, etc. But there is another testing, which is not from incredulity or rashness, but from πληροφορίᾳ or good intent, for the sake of strengthening faith, such as that of Abraham, Gen. 15, 8, and of Gideon, Jud. 6, 39.

Latin:

V. 16. NON TENTABIS DOMINUM DEUM TUUM.

Tentatio Dei est, cum sollicitatur omnipoten- tia divina, omniscientia, vel providentia aut veritas sive per temeritatem, sive per incredulitatem, v. g. cum Deum tentamus, num possit opitulari Ex. 17. v. 1. 7. utrum sciat, quæ nos molimur Act. 7, 9. Ten- tatur Deus etiam, cum ex temeritate quis se in pe- riculum præcipitat, is enim nullo verbo Dei nixus Deum provocat, Matth. 4. cum Deo tempus & modum præscribimus Judith. 7, 23. c. 8, 11. cum aliena, vel suo captu superiora quis sectatur, citra vocationem, & facultatem suam &c. Alia autem est tentatio, quæ non ex incredulitate vel temerita- te, sed ex πληροφορίᾳ vel bono animo, fidei corro- borandæ gratia sit, qualis Abrahami Gen. 15, 8. & Gideonis Jud. 6, 39.

## 6:21
V. 21. YOU SHALL SAY TO HIM: WE WERE SERVANTS) He brings forward three reasons why the Israelites ought to obey God: Benefits received, utilities promised, and grace before God, in which the Hebrews think that things greater than the promises, i.e., eternal things, are tacitly involved.

This is not merely a conjecture or opinion of the Hebrews, but the eternal truth itself, that the grace and mercy of GOD also comprehend eternal things: because the mercy of God is eternal, nor is it circumscribed by the limits of this life or by ages. That the promises to the Hebrews were only corporal, not eternal goods, is a Socinian hypothesis, which we have already noted often in Grotius. Meanwhile, here in the Hebrew it is held word for word thus: And it will be righteousness for us, which the LXX render, καὶ ἐλεημοσύνη ἔσαι ἡμῖν: The Vulgate, He will be merciful to us. The Chaldean, a reward also will be for us; because צדקה denotes not only righteousness, but also beneficence and the alms proceeding from it, Ps. 25, 5, Dan. 4, 24. Bonfrerius gives the reason: For there is also a certain mercy which has the character of righteousness, of which kind is that by which God rewards the works of virtue, in which way the Latin also seems to have understood it. The interpreter of the Chaldaic paraphrase, and a reward will be for us.

Latin:

V. 21. DICES EI: SERVI ERAMUS) Tres causas ad- fert, cur Israëlitæ parere Deo debeant: Beneficia accepta, uti- litates promissas, & gratiam apud Deum, in qua tacite in- volvi majora promissis, i. e. æterna, Hebræi putant.

Non hæc tantum conjectura, vel opinio E- bræorum est, sed ipsa æterna veritas, gratiam, & misericordiam DEI æterna etiam comprehendere: quia æterna est Dei misericordia, neq; terminis hu- jus vitæ aut seculis circumscribitur. Promissa tan- tum Ebræis fuisse corporalia, non æterna bona, hy- pothesis Sociniana est, quam sæpius jam in Grotio notavimus. Interim hic loci in Ebræo ad verbum ita habetur: Et erit justitia nobis, quod LXX. red- dunt, καὶ ἐλεημοσύνη ἔσαι ἡμῖν : Vulgatus, Erit nostri misericors. Chaldæus, præmium quoque erit nobis; quia צדקה non justitiam modo, sed etiam benefi- centiam & eleemosynam inde profectam notat Ps. 25, 5. Dan. 4, 24. Rationem reddit Bonfrerius: Nam & quædam misericordia est, quæ justitiæ habet rationem, cujusmodi est illa, qua Deus præmiatur virtutis opera, quomodo etiam videtur accepisse La- tinus. Chaldaicæ paraphrasis interpres, & præ- mium erit nobis.

## 6:24
Vers. 24. ALL THE DAYS OF OUR LIFE AS IT IS TODAY) In the Hebrew: to keep us alive according to this day: that is, that we may be preserved living, as we now live. The Greeks, ἵνα ζῶμεν ὧσπερ κὶι σήμερον.

Latin:

Vers. 24. CUNCTIS DIEBUS VITÆ NOSTRÆ SIC- UT EST HODIE) In Hebræo: ad vivificandum nos se- cundum diem hanc: id est, ut conservemur viventes, sicut nunc vivimus. Græci, ἵνα ζῶμεν ὧσπερ κὶι σήμερον.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAPTER VII. The communion of the nations is to be avoided.

Vers. 1. SEVEN NATIONS MUCH GREATER IN NUMBER THAN YOU, AND STRONGER THAN YOU.

This is to be understood not distributively with Dionysius the Carthusian, but collectively, if those nations should join together to oppose the Israelites.

Latin:

CAPUT VII. Vitanda gentium communio.

Vers. 1. SEPTEM GENTES MULTO MAJORES NUMERI, QUAM TU ES, ET ROBUSTIO- RES TE.

Non distributive cum Dionysio Carthuf. fed collective hoc intelligendum, si gentes illæ conjun- ctim se Israelitis opponant.

## 7:2
Vers. 2. YOU SHALL STRIKE THEM EVEN TO DESTRUCTION: YOU SHALL NOT ENTER INTO A COVENANT WITH THEM, NOR HAVE MERCY ON THEM) The Egyptians seize upon these things in the institutions of Moses out of hatred for the Jews indiscriminately. Manetho: συνάπτεσθαι δὲ μή τινι πλὴν τῶν συνωμοσμένων. Chaeremon: μήτε ἀνθρώπων τινὶ εὐνοήσειν. Tacitus, having followed the Egyptian writers: Among them (the Jews) faith is obstinate, mercy is ready, but against all others there is hostile hatred. See what has been gathered by us on this matter in book II. of the Law of War and Peace, ch. 15, §. 9. Let Dion Cassius on the Jews be added: κεχωρίδεται δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐς τὰ περὶ τὴν δίαιταν πάνθ' ὡς εἰπεῖν.

Grotius wishes this to be understood with a benign exception at Deut. 20, 10, unless some should have obeyed at the first proclamation. Following as usual the Hebrews Maimonides and Moses of Coucy. But how could either peace be offered to them or sparing be granted for the partition of surrender, if indeed they were simply devoted to destruction, as those who had filled the measure of their iniquities, Gen. 25, 16, and it was forbidden to the Israelites that they should enter into a covenant with them, nor should they have mercy on them. Compare Ex. 23, 32, 33, c. 34, 12, seqq. Therefore, only the case of conversion is excepted, because repentance is never too late, provided it be true, and indirectly our blessed Luther in the annotations to this place, Tom. III. Lat. Jen. f. 96. Here it must be noted that Moses does not judge that those nations were to be destroyed simply, but if they persisted in their hardness; otherwise peace was to be offered to them, and they themselves were to be tolerated, if they were CONVERTED to Israel, as happened to the Gibeonites and Rahab the harlot, Jos. 2, 14. c. 6, 15. c. 9, 15. Outside of this case, the Canaanites were to be utterly cut off, but a covenant of peace was not to be entered into with them. Therefore they are gravely rebuked because they made a covenant of peace with the inhabitants of the land of Canaan, Jud. 2, 2. Wherefore Dionysius, Brentius, Osiander, and others explain the words of Deut. 20, 10 concerning peace being first offered to cities, and v. 15, thus you shall do to all the cities which are far from you, and are not of these cities which you are about to receive into your possession. Wherefore they interpret this precept concerning peace being first offered not of cities in the land of Canaan, but outside of it, since God himself distinguishes between cities situated far away and those which they were about to receive into their possession in the land of Canaan. Which distinction Tremellius and Junius restrict to the deletion of all living things in the promised land, since in other places they ought to spare women, infants, and beasts. But in the text it is sufficiently clear that this distinction refers to all the preceding matters, and that the deletion of all in the land of Canaan was simply enjoined, without a prior offer of peace, or the exception of any living soul. Nor is it read in the history of Joshua that peace was offered to any city first; indeed, from the very example of the Gibeonites it is manifest that peace was not to be offered to them, since even after the oath of indemnity was provided, the Israelites still judged that they were to be destroyed by slaughter, because they believed themselves to be bound to that by the force of this divine constitution, when they saw them dwelling in the midst of the land of Canaan. Whence Joshua with all Israel said to the same, Jos. 9, 1, Lest perhaps you dwell in the land which is perhaps owed to us, and we cannot enter into a covenant with you; for they understood well that this divine constitution stood in the way: where Grotius, l. II. de Jur. Bell. ac Pac. c. 4, objects in vain. That response of Joshua COULD have this meaning, that the Gibeonites be questioned as to what kind of pact they desire, whether an alliance, or a surrender, or also that the Hebrews might show that it was not lawful for them to enter into a covenant with certain peoples, or also that they deny that they can spare the lives of those who surrender themselves. Neither the request of the Gibeonites, nor that doubt which Joshua raises, nor the response of the Gibeonites teaches that the matter was about the question of what kind of covenant, social or of surrender, should be established: but simply about the question, whether it exists? Since the Israelites testified that this was not permitted to them, by force of a divine interdict, perhaps [saying] 'you who live in my midst, how could I make a treaty with you?' For the Hebrews do not show only that a social covenant was not permitted for them to enter into, but they protest absolutely that they cannot enter into a covenant of peace with them and spare their lives if they dwell in the midst of Israel, and they enter into a covenant of peace with them regarding not destroying them only upon that representation, that the Gibeonites had come from a very distant land. And what need would the Hebrews have had to show that it was not permitted for them to enter into a social covenant, when the Gibeonites did not ask for that, but surrendered themselves voluntarily, and asked only that their lives be spared. 'We are your servants,' they say, 'and yet Joshua still asks, who are you, and where have you come from?' They certainly obtained peace from the Israelites by deceit, and without that pretext they would not have obtained it at all, which, having been confirmed by an oath, was kept by Joshua, not without the contradiction of the Israelites, because of the religious obligation of the oath. The example of Rahab does not apply here, for she was already spared in her life because she had received the spies into her home and saved them; that was a case excepted from that law, because those who accepted the faith of the Hebrews had to be spared.

But it is truly singular and extraordinary that Solomon gave peace to the remnants of the Canaanites and made them tributaries, 1 Kings 9:20. Add that they were left behind by the fault of the Israelites themselves, who had behaved too negligently in driving out all the Canaanites and had not obeyed the voice of the Lord, as a punishment or trial of the Israelites, Judg. 2:2 seqq., and therefore Solomon was not bound to destroy those who had been left in their midst by the just judgment of God, yet he made them tributaries. Times must therefore be distinguished here, and the judgment and punishment of God himself is not opposed to the divine constitution. For previously, by divine law, they should not have spared the Canaanites; afterwards, by the judgment of God intimated in Judg. 2 and confirmed by oath in v. 15, they were forced to tolerate them among themselves because of their untimely mercy toward them, and therefore Solomon was content with the fact that he made them tributaries to himself.

Nor does Jos. 11:19, 20 help Grotius. There was no city that surrendered itself to the children of Israel, except the Hivite who lived in Gibeon: for he took them all by fighting. For the sentence of the Lord had been that their hearts should be hardened and they should fight against Israel, and fall, and not deserve any clemency, and perish as the Lord had commanded Moses. This rather contradicts the Grotian opinion. For if, according to the command of Moses given by God from their foreseen idolatry and persistent malice and hardening, they were to be cut off without mercy, then a covenant of surrender should certainly not have been entered into with them, nor should peace have been offered to them. Therefore it cannot be concluded from that, that if they had accepted the offered peace, they could have been saved just as the Gibeonites were saved; and it is rashly supposed that the Hebrews were ordered to offer peace to the Canaanites, regarding whom Moses had received an express command that they were simply to be destroyed: nor was peace offered to the Gibeonites by the Hebrews, but it was obtained from them by deceit, which Grotius affirms, against the history, that they would have obtained under the condition of obedience if they had indicated the matter itself without deceit. No other way remained for the Canaanites to save their lives than a serious conversion to the God of Israel, by which Rahab was saved, and many others could have been saved.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PERCUTIES EAS USQVE AD INTER- NECIONEM: NON INIBIS CUM EIS FOEDUS, NEC MISEREBERIS EARUM) Hæc in odium Judæo- rum indiscriminatim arripiunt Ægyptii in Mosis institutis. Manetho: συνάπτεσθαι δὲ μή τινι πλὴν τῶν συνωμοσμένων. Chæremon: μήτε ἀνθρώπων τινὶ εὐνοήσειν. Tacitus secutus Ægyptios scriptores: Apud ipsos (Judæos) fides obstinata, misericordia in promptu, sed adversus omnes alios hostile odi- um. Vide quæ ad hanc rem a nobis congesta libro II. de Ju- re Belli ac Pacis cap. 15. §. 9. Accedat Dion Cassius de Ju- dæis: κεχωρίδεται δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐς τὰ περὶ τὴν δίαιταν πάνθ' ὡς εἰπεῖν.

HOc cum benigna exceptione intelligi vult Grotius ad Deut. 20, 10. nisi si quæ ad pri- mam denunciationem paruerint. Sequutus pro more Ebræos Maimonidem, & Mosen de Kotzi. At quomodo illis vel pax offerri vel ad partitionem deditionis parci potuisset, siquidem simpliciter exitio devoti fuerint, utpote qui mensuram iniqui- tatum suarum impleverant Gen. 25, 16. atque inter- dictum Israelitis, ut fœdus cum eis inirent, nec eo- rum misererentur. Conf. Ex. 23, 32. 33. c. 34, 12. seqq. Solus ergo casus conversionis excipitur, quia pœnitentia nunquam est sera, modo sit vera, atque indirecte B. Lutherus noster in annot. ad h. l. Tom. III. Lat. Jen. f. 96. Hic attendendum est, quod Moses gentes istas non simpliciter perdendas censet, sed si induratæ perseverarent, alioqui pax illis offerenda fuit, & ipsæ ferendæ, si CONVERTERENTUR ad Israel, sicut Gibeonitis & Rachab meretrici conti- git Jos. 2, 14. c. 6, 15. c. 9, 15. Extra hunc casum omnino exscindendi erant Cananæi, non autem fœdus pacis ineundum cum iis. Ideo reprehen- duntur graviter, quod cum habitatoribus terræ Ca- naan fœdus pacis fecerint Jud. 2, 2. Quapropter Dionysius, Brentius, Osiander & alii verba Deut. 20, 10. de pace primum civitatibus offerenda explicant, & v. 15. sic facies cunctis civitatibus, quæ a te procul sunt, & non sunt de his urbibus quas in possessionem ac- cepturus es. Quapropter non de civitatibus in terra Canaan, sed extra eam hoc præceptum de pace pri- mum offerenda interpretantur, siquidem Deus ipse distinguat inter civitates procul dissitas, & eas, quas in possessionem accepturi erant in terra Canaan. Quod discrimen Tremellius & Junius restringunt ad deletionem omnium viventium in terra promis- sa, quum in aliis locis mulieribus, infantibus ac ju- mentis parcere debeant. Sed in textu satis luculen- tum est, ad omnia antecedentia istam distinctio- nem se referre, ac simpliciter injunctam esse dele- tionem omnium in terra Canaan, citra præviam pa- cis oblationem, aut ullius animæ viventis exceptio- nem. Neque in historia Josuæ legitur, ulli civi- tati prius oblatam esse pacem, imo ex ipso Gibeoni- tarum exemplo manifestum est, illis pacem offe- rendam non fuisse, siquidem etiam post juramen- tum indemnitatis præstitum Israelitæ adhuc eos internecione delendos esse, judicarint, quod vi hu- jus constitutionis divinæ se ad id obstrictos cre- diderint, ubi eos in medio terræ Canaan habitare vi- derunt. Unde Josua cum toto Israele dixit iisdem Jos. 9, 1. Ne forte in terra, quæ nobis forte debetur, habitetis, & non possimus fœdus inire vobiscum; ob- stare enim hanc divinam constitutionem probe in- telligebant: ubi nequicquam excipit Grotius l. II. de Jur. Bell. ac Pac. c. 4. Illud Josuæ responsum hunc sensum habere POSSE, ut interrogentur Gi- beonitæ, quale pactum desiderent, socialene, an dedi- tionis, aut etiam, ut ostendant Hebræi, licitum sibi non esse cum quibusdum populis fœdus inire, aut etiam quod negent dedentibus se vitam relinquere posse. Hoc neque petitum Gibeonitarum, neque du- bium illud quod Josua movet, neque responsio Gibeonitarum docet: de quæstione, quale fœdus sociale ne an deditionis erigendum sit, rem fuisse: sed simpliciter de quæstione, an sit? Siquidem sibi id non licere, vi interdicti divini, testati sint Israëlitæ, fortasse in medio mei habitas, quomodo tecum paci- fierer? Neque enim ostendunt Ebræi solum fœ- dus sociale licitum sibi non esse inire, sed absolute protestantur, se cum ipsis pacis fœdus inire ac par- cere ipsorum vitæ non posse, si in medio Israëlis habitent, nec nisi ad eam significationem, quod Gibeonitæ ex terra valde longinqua venerint, ine- unt cum iis fœdus pacis de iis non delendis. Et quid opus habuissent Ebræi ostendere sibi fœdus sociale inire non esse licitum, quum id non petie- rint Gibeonitæ, sed ultro se dederint, ac vitæ suæ solum parceretur, rogarint. Servi tui sumus, in- quiunt, & adhuc tamen quærit Josua, quinam estis vos, & unde venistis? Pacem utique dolo ab Israëlitis impetrarunt, sine illo εὐσχήματι minime eandem impetraturi, quæ cum jurejurando firma- ta fuit non absque contradictione Israëlitarum a Josua ob juramenti religionem servata. Exem- plum Rahab huc non facit, jam enim ob explora- tores hospitio susceptos & servatos in vita servata est, exceptus casus ab illa lege fuit, quia fidem E- bræorum suscipientibus parcendum erat.

Id vero singulare atque extraordinarium est, quod Salomo reliquiis Cenanæorum pacem dede- rit, eosque tributarios fecerit 1. Reg. 9, 20. Adde quod illæ, culpa ipsorum Israëlitarum, qui negli- gentiores se gesserant in Cananæis omnibus pel- lendis, neque voci Domini paruerant, relictæ fue- rint, in pœnam vel δοκιμασίαν Israëlitarum Jud. 2, 2. seqq. ideoque illos, qui justo judicio Dei in me- dio illorum relicti erant, non tenebatur Salomo delere, tributarios tamen ipsos fecit. Distin- guenda ergo hic tempora, neque Dei ipsius judi- cium & pœna opponitur divinæ constitutioni. Nam prius per divinam legem parcere non debuis- sent Cananæis, postea per judicium Dei Jud. 2. in- timatum, & juramento firmatum v. 15. ob intem- pestivam in ipsos misericordiam, tolerare eos in- ter se coacti fuere, ideoque eo contentus fuit Sa- lomo, quod eos sibi tributarios fecerit.

Nec Grotium juvat Jos. 11, 19. 20. Non fuit civitas, quæ se traderet filiis Israël, præter Hevæum, qui habitabat in Gibeon: omnes enim bellando cepit. Domini enim sententia fuerat, ut indurarentur cor- da eorum & pugnarent contra Israël, & caderent, & non mererentur ullam clementiam & perirent sicut præceperat Dominus Mosi. Refragatur id potius Grotianæ sententiæ. Nam si juxta præceptum Mo- si e prævisa ipsorum in idololatria & pertinaci ma- litia & induratione, datum a Deo, excindendi erant citra misericordiam, utique non debuit cum illis fœdus deditionis iniri, nec debuit ipsis pax of- ferri. Non ergo id inde concludi potest, si pa- cem oblatam recepissent, eos servari potuisse æ- que, ut Gibeonitæ servati sunt; & temere suppo- nitur pacem offerre Cananæis jussos esse Ebræos, de quibus simpliciter delendis Moses mandatum expressum acceperat: nec Gibeonitis pax oblata ab Ebræis, sed per dolum ab ipsis impetrata fuit, quam sub parendi conditione ipsos impetraturos fuisse, si absque dolo rem ipsam indicassent, invita historia af- firmat Grotius. Nulla alia vitæ servandæ Cana- næis supererat ratio, quam seria ad Deum Israelis conversio, qua Rahab servata fuit, pluresque alii servari potuissent.

## 7:3
NEITHER SHALL YOU MAKE MARRIAGES WITH THEM) Not even with those converted to the law. Whence they infer that Rahab was not from the VII nations.

We cannot prove this: because Deut. 21:11 expressly permits the Israelites to take as wives women captured in war. And such marriages are prohibited here for a certain reason. 'You shall not give your daughter to his son, nor shall you take his daughter for your son; because he will seduce your son.' Therefore, the reason for the law ceasing, the law itself ceased. Add that the opportunity for conversion would thus have been taken away: since it would not have been permitted to be joined in marriage even to those who wished to pass over to the Israelite religion. And did not Boaz take Ruth the Moabitess, Ruth 4:13? David took Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, King of Geshur, of the race of the Canaanites, 2 Sam. 3:3. Samson took a Philistine, to say nothing of others. Finally, whence is it certain that Rahab, who lived in the midst of the Canaanites, was not a Canaanite, whom Salmon, prince of the tribe of Judah, took, Matt. 1:8? Grotius believes the Jews too easily.

Latin:

NEQVE SOCIABIS CVM EIS CONJUGIA) Ne conversis quidem ad legem. Unde Rahabam colligunt non fuisse ex VII. populis.

Probare hoc non possumus: quia Deut. 21, 11. diferte permittitur Israelitis, ut in bello captas mulieres in uxores ducant. Et certa ratione hic prohibentur ejusmodi conjugia. Filiam tuam non dabis filio ejus, nec filiam illius accipies filio tuo; quia seducet filium tuum. Cessante ergo illa ratione legis, cessavit lex ipsa. Adde quod ita ademta fuisset occasio conversionis: cum ne illis quidem matrimonio jungi licitum fuisset, qui ad Israeliticam religionem transire voluerint. Et annon Booz Ruth Moabitidem Ruth. 4, 13. David Maacham filiam Tholmai Regis Gessur e genere Cananæorum 2. Sam. 3, 3. Simson Philistæam duxit, ut alios taceam. Denique unde constat, Rahabam, quæ in medio Cananæorum habitavit, Cananæam non fuisse, quam Salmon princeps tribus Judæ duxit Matth. 1, 8. Nimis facile credit Judæis Grotius.

## 7:5
Vers. 5.

OVERTHROW THEIR ALTARS, AND BREAK THEIR STATUES) Hecataeus concerning the Jews: 'Those who arrived in the country to them, and had built altars and temples, they tore all these down.' But Chaeremon, when he recounts the institutions of Moses: 'And to overthrow the temples and altars of the gods wherever they might encounter them.'

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ARAS EORVM SVBVERTITE, ET CONFRINGITE STATVAS) Hecatæus de Judæis: τῶν γε μὲν εἰς τὴν χώραν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἀφικνομένων καὶ βωμοὺς καὶ νεὼς κατασκευασάντων ἅπαντα ταῦτα κατέσκαπτον. Chæremon autem ubi Mofis instituta recitat: Θεῶν τε νεὼς καὶ βωμοὺς οἷς ἂν προστύχωσιν ἀνατρέπειν.

## 7:8
Vers. 8.

HE KEPT THE OATH WHICH HE PROMISED TO YOUR FATHERS) God loves the Israelites, mindful of those from whom they have sprung, below X, 15. This is the ἐκλογὴ Rom. 11, 28.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

CVSTODIVIT JVRAMENTVM QVOD PROMISIT PATRIBVS VESTRIS) Amat Deus Israelitas, memor eorum e quibus orti sunt, infra X, 15. Hæc est ἐκλογὴ Rom. 11, 28.

## 7:10
Vers. 10.

REPAYING THOSE WHO HATE HIM IMMEDIATELY) In the Hebrew: to his faces, that is, openly.

LXX. κατὰ πρόσωπον. The Targum, R. Solomon, and David Kimchi say that the good things which the wicked do are repaid in this life, but so that God may destroy them in the future life. Vatablus: to their face, that is, in their lifetime. But the explanation of Grotius is correct, for that indicates that it will be repaid openly and to his face, and in such a way that he may see, feel, and be forced to acknowledge the retribution of the Lord. Thus, to reproach to the face, that is, to reproach something openly, at close quarters, and plainly. Thus Arias and Oleaster: to the face is the same as publicly. B. Gerhard says almost the same, repaying them to the face, that is, openly and fearlessly so that they cannot escape the sight of the punishing God, so that they may feel the hand of the avenging God Ps. 50:21, I will reprove you, and set them before your face.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

REDDENS ODIENTIBVS SE STATIM) In Hebræo: ad facies ejus, id est, palam.

LXX. κατὰ πρόσωπον. Targ. R. Salomon & David Kimchi reddi ajunt in hac vita bona, quæ impii faciunt, sed ut in futura eos perdat Deus. Vatablus in faciem ipsorum, id est, in vita ipsorum. Recte autem habet Grotii explicatio, id enim indigitatur palam & in faciem ei retributum iri, atque ita ut videat, sentiat, & agnoscere cogatur retributionem Domini. Sic in faciem exprobare, id est, palam cominus atque aperte aliquid exprobare. Sic Arias, & Oleaster: in faciem idem est quod publice. Similiter fere B. Gerhardus, retribuens eis in faciem, hoc est, aperte & intrepide ut non possint conspectum Dei punientis effugere, ut vindicis Dei manum sentiant Ps. LI, 21. arguam te, & statuam contra faciem tuam.

## 7:12
vers. 12.

IF AFTER YOU HAVE HEARD THE JUDGMENTS.

Pagninus and Arias translate the word עקב as reward, i.e., And it shall be a reward, if you hear the judgments. But the Vulgate has nothing about a reward. And that word is more correctly explained by חלף as the Targum of Onkelos and Jonathan translate: For that, or because that, so that the sense may be: And it shall be, or it shall come to pass because you have heard, etc., which sense the parallel passages Lev. 26:3, Deut. 28:1 confirm. Thus that word is also taken in Gen. 22:18, ch. 26:5. And so there is no need for an ellipsis of the particle אִם If. Nor does the particle ו stand in the way. But if the discourse flows: And it shall come to pass because you have heard these judgments and have kept and done them, the Lord will keep (it shall come to pass that the Lord also will keep) the covenant for you.

Latin:

vers. 12.

SI POSTQVAM AUDIERIS JUDICIA.

Vocem עקב Pagnin. & Arias reddunt merces, h. m. Et erit merces, si audieritis judicia. Sed vulgata nihil habet de mercede. Et vox illa rectius exponitur per חלף ut Targ. Onkel. & Jonath. reddunt: Eo quod, vel propterea quod, ut sit sensus: Et erit, sive fiet propterea quod audieritis &c. quem sensum loca parallelela Lev. 26, 3. Deut. 28, 1. confirmant. Sic accipitur etiam vox illa Gen. 22, 18. c. 26, 5. Atque ita non opus est ellipsi particulæ אִם Si. Neque obstat particula ו. Si autem fluit oratio: Et fiet propterea quod audiveritis judicia ista & custodiveritis & feceritis ea, custodiet Dominus, (fiet ut & Dominus custodiat) tibi pactum.

## 7:20
vers. 20.

MOREOVER THE LORD ALSO SENT HORNETS.

Aben-Ezra explains the word הַצִּרְעָה as leprosy; others explain it metaphorically as distresses and terrors, a view not denied by Augustine in q. 93 on Exodus, who is nevertheless doubtful elsewhere whether wasps are to be understood in q. 27 on Joshua. But that word properly denotes hornets, Josh. 24:12, Wis. 12:8. And something similar happened in the army of Sapor, King of the Persians, Theod. bk. II, Hist. Eccl. ch. 30. Hail was sent against the Amorites, Josh. 10:11; a storm put the Philistines to flight, 1 Sam. 7:9. Whence, distinctly, Exod. 23:28 lists terrors and hornets. Although the sending of hornets is nowhere described in history, the matter is nevertheless certain from this prediction; because not all things are expressed circumstantially everywhere in narratives. Which, therefore, ought by no means to be denied.

Latin:

vers. 20.

INSUPER ET CRABRONES MISIT DOMINUS.

Vocem הַצִּרְעָה lepram exponit Aben-Ezra, alii metaphorice de angustiis & pavoribus explicant, non abnuente August. q. 93. in Exod. qui tamen dubius alibi est, anne vespae intelligendae sint q. 27. in Jos. Sed vox ea crabrones proprie notat Jos. 24, 12. Sap. 12, 8. & accidit simile quid in exercitu Sapo- ris Regis Persarum, Theod. l. II. Hist. Eccl. c. 30. In Amorrhaeos grando immittebatur Jos. 10, 11. Phi- listhaeos tempestas fugavit 1. Sam. 7, 9. Unde distin- cte Exod. 23, 28. recensetur pavores, & crabrones. Quamvis vero nuspiam in historia crabronum im- missio describatur, res tamen ex hac praedictione certa est; quia non omnia περιστατικῶς ubique in narrationibus expressa sunt. Quae ideo minime ne- gari debent.

## 7:22
Verse 22.

LITTLE BY LITTLE AND BY PARTS) How appetites are overcome by Christians.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

PAVLATIM ATQVE PER PARTES) Quomodo a Christianis appetitus debellantur.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII. The benefits of God, as also the afflictions of the people, are recounted.

Verse 1. TAKE HEED DILIGENTLY THAT YOU DO.

What is this, 'take heed,' that you do this command? Marius says the sense is: attend, that you may do. Cornelius: 'take heed,' that is, observe cautiously. But who speaks in this way? The Vulgate, therefore, is to be corrected here.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII. Beneficia Dei, ut & afflictiones populi repe- tuntur.

Vers. 1. CAVE DILIGENTER UT FACIAS.

QUid hoc est, cave, ut hoc mandatum facias? Marius sensum esse dicit: attende, ut facias. Cornel. cave, id est, caute observa. Sed quis ita lo- quitur? Corrigenda ergo hic Vulgata.

## 8:2
Verse 2. THAT HE MIGHT AFFLICT AND TEST) For God tests men not only with hard things, but also with prosperous ones, as will now follow. See also below 32:15.

Latin:

Vers. 2. VT AFFLIGERET ATQVE TENTARET) Non enim solis rebus duris, sed & prosperis Deus homines tentat, ut jam sequetur. Vide & infra 32, 15.

## 8:3
Verse 3. I GAVE THEE FOOD MANNA) A highly nourishing food.

BY EVERY WORD THAT PROCEEDS FROM THE MOUTH OF GOD) See at Matt. 4:4. Some explain this concerning the food of the soul, because while the body of man is sustained by bread, the word of God is required for the sustenance of man as regards the soul. But the discourse is about one and the same life, namely, the bodily one: for the preservation of which not only bread, but also the word of God avails, apprehended by faith, where bread is lacking, because God is not bound to the means of natural sustenance, but can preserve life without them; as He sustained Elijah, and Christ for 40 days without bread by the power of His word, and fed the Israelites in the desert for 40 years without bread, when they could not plow, sow, reap, gather crops, much less bake bread; nor would bread suffice to preserve life, unless divine blessing were added. If God withdraws this, even if bread is present in great abundance, it will not be able to sustain life. Just as this bodily life, so also faith is not fed, except by the word of divine promise, says Luther, Tom. II. Lat. p. 266.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DEDI TIBI CIBVM MANNA) Valde vege- tantem cibum.

IN OMNI VERBO QVOD EGREDITVR DE ORE DEI) Vide ad Matth. 4, 4. Hoc nonnulli de cibo animae explicant, quod pane quidem hominis corpus sustentetur, ad su- stentationen autem hominis quoad animam re- quiratur verbum Dei. Verum de vita una & eadem nempe corporali sermo est: ad quam conservandam non solum panis, sed etiam verbum Dei facit, fide apprehensum, ubi deficit panis, quia Deus non est alligatus ad media sustentationis naturalis, sed sine iis vitam conservare potest; ut Eliam, & Christum per 40. dies sine pane sustentavit verbi sui virtute, & Israelitas in deserto per 40. annos sine pane, quum non possent arare, serere, metere, fruges col- ligere, nedum panem pinsere, aluit; neque panis ad conservandam vitam sufficeret, nisi benedictio di- vina accederet. Hanc si Deus subducat, etsi panis in magna adsit copia, vitam sustentare non poterit. Sicut haec vita corporalis, ita & fides non pascitur, nisi promissionis divinae verbo, ait Luther. Tom. II. Lat. p. 266.

## 8:4
Verse 4.

YOUR CLOTHING, WITH WHICH YOU WERE COVERED, did not fail from age. The Hebrews report that the garments were not only not worn out, but also grew with their stature. Estius, in his annotations on this passage, indeed denies that the garments grew with their bodies by a miracle, since they could have been provided for otherwise if the boys received the clothing of dying adults; but this is related by the Holy Spirit as something singular, therefore it is more correctly established with the Hebrews, and Justin in his Dialogue with Trypho, that there was a miracle in the growth of the garments: meanwhile, it is not denied that material for the boys' clothes was taken from the garments of those who were passing away. The garments received from the Egyptians and Amalekites could not have lasted so long unless this miracle had occurred.

Verse of the same.

YOUR FOOT IS NOT WORN AWAY (לא בצקה your foot was not swollen: that is, it was not unshod: thus in Nehemiah 9:21 it is translated: τὰ ὑποδήματα ἀυτῶν ὀ διεῤῥάγησαν

B. Luther, Schindl. in Lex., Cajetan, Pag., Arias, Tigur. are more correct, along with the Hebrews R. Aben-Ezra, R. Mos. Gerund., R. Mardoch. Nathan, [saying it] did not swell, as feet are accustomed to swell for travelers. Münster on this passage [notes] the word בצק signifies to make dough, but dough when heated swells. Thus they correctly rendered the sense, even if not the words of the LXX. οἱ πόδες ὐκ ἐτιλώθησαν, they did not become calloused, as is read in Theodoret in the Royal, Sixtine, and Frankfurt Wichelian Codices. Basil incorrectly has ἐλυτρώθησαν, they were redeemed. This benefit, therefore, is singular and distinct: the prohibition of swelling in the feet [is distinct] from the prohibition of wearing out in the footwear, Deut. 29:5, Neh. 9:21. Therefore, Bonfrerius is not correct: the foot is said here not to have been worn away because the shoes were not worn away.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

VESTIMENTVM TVVM, QVO OPERIEBARIS NEQVAQVAM VETVSTATE DEFECIT) Non tantum non attrita fuisse, sed & cum statura crevisse vestimenta tra- dunt Hebraei. Negat quidem Estius in annot. ad h. l. crevisse per miraculum vestimenta cum corporibus, quum aliter potuerit ipsis provideri, si pueri acciperent vestimentum adultorum morientium; sed refertur hoc a Sp. S. ut aliquid singulare, ideo rectius cum Ebreis, & Justino Dial. cum Tryph. in vestium ac- cretione miraculum statuitur: interim materiam ad puerorum vestes ex decidentium vestibus adhi- bitam fuisse, non negatur. Vestes ab Aegyptiis & Amalekitis acceptae non potuissent tamdiu durare nisi miraculum hoc accessisset.

Vers. eod.

PES TVVS NON EST SVBTRITVS (לא בצקה non conspersus fuit pes tuus: id est, non fuit discalceatus: sic in Nehem. 9, 21. vertitur: τὰ ὑποδήματα ἀυτῶν ὀ διεῤῥάγησαν

Rectius B. Lutherus, Schindl. in Lex. Caje- tan. Pag. Arias, Tigur. cum Ebræis R. Aben- Ezra. R. Mos. Gerund. R. Mardoch. Nathan, non tumuit, uti viatoribus solent pedes tumescere. Münster. in h. l. verbum בצק significat pastam face- re, pasta autem calefacta intumescit. Ita recte sen- sum, etsi non verba reddidere LXX. οἱ πόδες ὐκ ἐτι- λώθησαν, non occalluerunt, uti legitur apud Theo- doretum in Codd. Regiis, Sixtino & Francof. Wi- cheliano. Basil. perperam habet ἐλυτρώθησαν re- demti sunt. Singulare ergo & distinctum hoc est beneficium prohibitio tumoris in pedibus a pro- hibitione attritionis in calceamentis Deut. 29, 5. Neh. 9, 21. Non ergo recte Bonfrerius: pes hic dicitur non fuisse attritus, quia calcei non fuerunt attriti.

## 8:5
verse 5. SO THE LORD YOUR GOD DISCIPLINED YOU.

In Hebrew, He corrected you, for that is what the verb יסר in Piel denotes. See Deut. 22:10, 1 Kings 10:12, etc., which verb παιδεύειν, which the LXX used here, also denotes. Luke 23:22, Heb. 12:6, paternal chastisement is denoted, such as that of children, not judicial or that of enemies. To this pertains the verb He afflicted in verses 2 and 3.

Latin:

vers. 5. SIC DOMINUS DEUS TUUS ERUDI- VIT TE.

In Ebr. Corripuit te, id enim notat verbum יסר in Piel. vid. Deut. 22, 10. 1. Reg. 10, 12. &c. quod verbum παιδεύειν, quo LXX. hic usi, etiam notat. Luc. 23, 22. Ebr. 12, 6. denotatur castigatio paterna, qualis est liberorum, non judiciaria, aut hostium. Quo pertinet verbum afflixit v. 2. & 3.

## 8:8
Verse 8. A LAND OF WHEAT.

This eulogy was also reported by enemies, 2 Kings 18:32. Corn. Tacitus attributes rich soil to it, Book V of the Histories. Euripides in the Bacchae: The field flows with milk, it flows also with wine, it flows with the nectar of bees, etc. Which is to be observed against Strabo, Book 16 of his Geography, who disparages the praises and fertility of this land. Compare Jer. 11:5, ch. 33:22, Joel 3:18. The very abundance of its inhabitants demonstrates its fertility, if indeed that land was not so extensive.

Latin:

Vers. 8. TERRA FRUMENTI.

Elogium hoc etiam ab hostibus reportavit 2. Reg. 18, 32. Corn. Tacitus uber ei solum tribuit lib. V. Hist. Euripid. in Bacch. Campus fluit la- cte, fluit etiam vino, fluit apum nectare &c. Quod contra Strabonem lib. 16. Geograph. laudibus & fertilitati hujus terræ derogantem observandum. Conf. Jer. 11, 5. c. 33, 22. Joel. 3, 18. Fertilitatem ejus vel ipsa inhabitantium copia, siquidem non adeo ampla fuerit illa terra, demonstrat.

## 8:9
verse 9. WHOSE STONES ARE IRON.

That is, endowed with iron, in which iron mines abound, in whose bowels are kept stones full of iron, which is afterwards smelted from them in furnaces. Compare Job 29:2, Deut. 33:25. See B. Gerhard on this passage.

Latin:

vers. 9. CUJUS LAPIDES FERRUM SUNT.

Id est, ferro præditi, in qua abundant ferri fo- dinæ, in cujus visceribus servantur lapides ferro pleni, quod in fornacibus postea ex illis excoqui- tur. Conf. Job. 29, 2. Deut. 33, 25. Vid. B. Ger- hard. in h. l.

## 8:10
Verse 10. YOU SHALL BLESS THE LORD YOUR GOD) δι' ἐπαίνων καὶ ὕμνων. Philo, περὶ φυτεργίας. Josephus calls it, γεραίρειν τὸν Θεὸν ὡς χορηγὸν τῆς τροφῆς.

Latin:

Vers. 10. BENEDICAS DOMINO DEO TVO) δι' ἐπαίνων καὶ ὕμνων. Philo, περὶ φυτεργίας. Josephus vocat, γεραίρειν τὸν Θεὸν ὡς χορηγὸν τῆς τροφῆς.

## 8:15
vers. 15. IN WHICH WAS A BURNING SERPENT AND A SCORPION, AND A DIPSAS.

In Hebrew, through the desert of the burning serpent (abounding in such) and of the scorpion (Num. 21, 6.) and of the thirsty place. For צִמָּאוֹן is derived from צָמֵא, thirst. For it was ἄνυδρον, as is approached, in which there was no water (Ez. 17. v. 1. Num. 20, 2.). The LXX render it δίψα, which denotes thirst. The Vulgate has Dipsas by mistake, because δίψας is a certain species of serpent. For the Targum also rendered it by a place where there was dryness. And Bonfrer acknowledges that the Hebrew word is elsewhere used for a parched and thirsty place, in which way R. Mardoch. Nathan, Forsterus, Tigur. Pagnin. Arius also explained it.

Latin:

vers. 15. IN QUA ERAT SERPENS FLATU ADU- RENS ET SCORPIO, AC DIPSAS.

In Ebr. per desertum serpentis adurentis (tali- bus abundans) & scorpionis (Num. 21, 6.) & loci siticulosi. Nam צִמָּאוֹן a צָמֵא Siti dicitur. Fuit enim ἄνυδρον, uti aditur, in quo non aquæ (Ez. 17. v. 1. Num. 20, 2.) LXX. reddunt δίψα, quod si- tim notat. Vulgat. habet per errorem Dipsas, quia δίψας ripæ quædam species est. Nam & Targum reddidit per locum ubi erat siccitas. Et agnoscit Bonfrer. vocem Ebræam alibi pro loco arenti, & siticuloso poni, quo pacto etiam exposuere R. Mar- doch. Nathan, Forsterus, Tigur. Pagnin. Arius.

## 8:16
Vers. 16. AND AFTER HE AFFLICTED AND PROVED, AT THE LAST HE HAD MERCY ON THEE) In the Hebrew: That he might afflict thee and test thee with the intention of doing thee good afterwards. For to this end do God's temptations tend, if one uses them rightly. But how these things could turn out well for the Israelites, the following verses explain.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ET POSTQVAM AFFLIXIT AC PROBAVIT, AD EXTREMVM MISERTVS EST TVI) In Hebræo: Vt affligeret te ac tentaret animo postea benefaciendi tibi. Huc enim tendunt Dei tentationes si quis recte utatur. Quomodo autem ista bene cedere Israelitis potuerint, explicant se- quentia.

## 8:18
Vers. 18. THAT HE HIMSELF GAVE THEE STRENGTH) It is added

in the Hebrew: to acquire wealth. Thus חיל is taken also in Num. 24, 18. and Prov. 31, 3. and 29. Job 20, 18. and elsewhere: and it is often translated into Greek as πλῦτος: elsewhere δύναμις, as here.

Latin:

Vers. 18. QVOD IPSE VIRES TIBI PRÆBVERIT) Additur

in Hebræo: ad acquirendas opes. Sic חיל sumitur & Num. 24, 18. & Prov. 31, 3. & 29. Job. 20, 18. & alibi: ac sæ- pe Græce vertitur πλῦτος: alibi δύναμις, ut hic.

## 9:1 Argument
CHAP. IX. The pride of Israel is repressed, with the mention of the μοσχολατρεία [calf-worship], and murmuring, and the intercession of Moses for the people.

Latin:

CAP. IX. Reprimitur elatio Israelis, commemorata μοσχολατρεία, & murmuratione, Mo- fisque pro populo intercessione.

## 9:3
Ver. 3. A DEVOURING AND CONSUMING FIRE) By which the power of God is signified through burnt offerings.

Assistance, protection, guidance, and the abolition of enemies are promised: Jehovah GOD himself shall pass over before thee. (The Targum renders: His Word shall pass over before thee, the Son of God, that uncreated Angel: who led the Israelites, and fought for them Exod. 14, 29. chap. 23, 20. Is. 63, 9. 1 Cor. 10, 9.) A devouring, or consuming fire, which as a fire is about to consume his enemies quickly, so that nothing of them may remain any longer. It is therefore compared to fire partly because of the speed of the consumption, as is explained in the following verse 4: partly because of the totality of the consumption, if I may so say, Deut. 32, 22. Nah. 1, 9. But as for burnt offerings, which alone were also consumed by fire, their significance was not directed toward indicating the deletion of enemies, but toward the true antitype of sacrifices, the burnt offering of Christ, both so that the quality of his sacrifice might be hinted at, that Christ, being whole in soul and body, God and man, had to undergo, experience, and sustain that consuming fire of divine justice and wrath against the sins of the whole world Galat. 3, 13. and so that its efficacy might be indicated, that by this sacrifice our sins were to be thoroughly abolished, and by plenary expiation, and by extirpation, which we who are freed from the body of this death expect in every way: that also all our spiritual enemies are to be consumed and destroyed. Is. 9, 5. Heb. 2, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 3. IGNIS DEVORANS ATQVE CONSVMENS) Qua vis Dei per holocausta significatur.

PRomittitur assistentia, protectio, deductio & hostium abolitio: Jehovah DEUS ipse transibit ante te. (Targum reddit: Verbum ejus transibit ante te, Filius Dei Angelus ille increatus: qui deduxit Israelitas, & pro iis pugnavit Exod. 14, 29. cap. 23, 20. Es. 63, 9. 1. Cor. 10, 9.) Ignis comedens, sive consumens, qui velut ignis consumturus est cito hostes suos, ut nihil eorum supersit amplius. Com- paratur ergo igni partim ob consumtionis velocita- tem, uti vers. seqv. 4. explicatur: partim ob consum- tionis totalitatem, ut ita dicam Deut. 32, 22. Nah. 1, 9. Quod vero ad holocausta attinet, quæ sola etiam consumebantur igne, non fuit significatio eorum directa ad indicandam hostium deletionem, sed ad verum sacrificiorum antitypum, holocaustum Chri- sti, tum ut innueretur sacrificii ejus qualitas, quod Christus totus anima, & corpore, Deus, & homo ignem illum consumentem divinæ justitiæ atq; iræ adversus peccata totius mundi subire, experiri, atque sustinere debuerit Galat. 3, 13. tum ut indi- caretur ejusdem efficacitas, quod isto sacrificio pec- cata nostra penitus abolenda, & per expiationem plenariam, & per extirpationem, quam liberati a corpore mortis hujus expectamus omnimodam: quod etiam universi hostes nostri spirituales consu- mendi sint, atque delendi. Esa. 9, 5. Ebr. 2, 14.

## 9:5
Ver. 5. FOR NOT BECAUSE OF THY RIGHTEOUSNESSES) The first benefits of God happen without merits: Their introduction into the land: To us, faith itself. See also above VII, 7.

Not only are the first benefits gratuitous, and happen without merits, as Grotius, who is leaning toward Popery, wishes here, not only is faith given out of grace, but justification itself is also gratuitous; nay, salvation is gratuitous, or the introduction into eternal life, which corresponds to the introduction into the land of Canaan Heb. 3, 10. Eternal rest, says Basil the Great, hom. on Ps. 104, is proposed to those who have lawfully contended in this life, which is not repaid according to debt and merit, but is exhibited according to the grace of the most magnificent God to those who have hoped in him. For this does not come to us through merits of condignity, as the Papists contend; but it is a χάρισμα τꭓ̃ θεꭓ̃ [gift of God] Rom. 6, 23. By grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; not of works, lest anyone should boast Eph. 2, 8. 9. But if by grace, then not of works, otherwise grace would not be grace Rom. 11, 6. Blessed is the man to whom God imputes righteousness χωρὶς ἔργων [without works] Rom. 4, 6. Augustine excellently says, Tom. II. Epist. CV. Just as from the beginning of faith we have obtained mercy, not because we were faithful, but that we might be. So in the end, what will be in eternal life he will crown us, as it is written, in his pity and mercy he will prevent me, and his mercy will follow me. And Fulgentius, lib. I. de Praedest. ad Monim. From grace is given not only to the justified a good life, but also to the glorified eternal life. Which we know from the preaching of Paul saying: The wages of sin is death: But the grace of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. But why is death called wages, and eternal life grace? Unless it is because the former is rendered, the latter is given.

The [Augsburg] Confession encrusts Popery regarding salvation to be obtained through works: because a wise man might require certain things in one whom he admits to friendship: more, so that he may maintain friendship with him: and holiness can be in the mind through the grace of God before works, [but] cannot endure without pious works, and through the works of faith the favor of God toward men and their right to eternal life is maintained. God does not behave himself as a man, nor is justification like a friendship contracted between men. What a man requires in a friend, he does not do himself, but expects from the ability of him with whom he enters into friendship. The case of God is different, who, when he admits some to friendship, does not admit them coming of their own accord, but draws them to himself, and whatever he requires of them, so that they do not fall from his favor, he himself does and works in them: from whom is both the willing and the performing, and the beginning and the continuation, and even the end itself: who therefore by his grace provides what is required for maintaining friendship. That the favor of God and the right to life are maintained through the works of faith is an inverted statement. Scripture teaches the contrary, that faith is maintained through the favor and grace of God, and works are made pleasing to God; that we are guarded in faith unto salvation and life through the grace and favor of God, 1 Pet. 1, 5. Our works are too imperfect, too unclean, too impotent to maintain faith, to guard the right of eternal life. Does the fruit maintain the tree, or does the tree maintain or foster the fruit?

Latin:

Vers. 5. NEQVE ENIM PROPTER JVSTITIAS TVAS) Prima Dei beneficia sine meritis contingunt: Illis introdu- ctio in terram: Nobis ipsa fides. Vid. & supra VII, 7.

Non tantum prima beneficia gratuita sunt, ac sine meritis contingunt, ut hic Papizans Grotius vult, non fides tantum ex gratia donatur, sed gra- tuita etiam est ipsa justificatio, imo gratuita est sal- vatio, seu in vitam æternam introductio, quæ in- troductioni in terram Cananæam respondet Ebr. 3, 10. Proposita est, inquit Basilius M. hom. in Ps. 104. æterna requies his, qui legitime in hac vita decertarunt, quæ non secundum debitum ac meritum retribuitur, sed juxta magnificentissimi Dei gratiam his, qui in ipsum sperarunt, exhibetur. Neque enim hæc per merita de condigno, uti Papistæ contendunt, nobis obtingit; sed χάρισμα τꭓ̃ θεꭓ̃ est Rom. 6, 23. Ex gratia salvati estis per fidem, & hoc non ex vobis, Dei donum est; non ex operibus, ne quis glorietur Eph. 2, 8. 9. Si autem ex gratia, non ex operibus, alias gratia non esset gratia Rom. 11, 6. Beatitudo est hominis, cui imputat Deus justitiam χωρὶς ἔργων sine operibus Rom. 4, 6. Præclare Augustinus Tom. II. Epist. CV. Sicut ab initio fidei misericordiam consequuti sumus, non quia fideles eramus, sed ut es- semus. Sic in fine, quod erit in vita æterna corona- bit nos, sicut scriptum est, in miseratione & miseri- cordia ejus præveniet me, & misericordia ejus subse- quetur me. Et Fulgent. lib. I. de Prædest. ad Mo- nim. Ex gratia datur non solum justificatis vita bo- na, sed etiam glorificatis vita æterna. Quod Pauli te- nemus prædicatione compertum dicentis: Stipen- dium peccati mors: Gratia autem Dei vita æterna in Christo Jesu Domino nostro. Cur autem mors sti- pendium, vita æterna gratia dicitur? nisi quia illa redditur, hæc donatur.

gustanæ Confessionis incrustat Papismum de salute per opera consequenda: quia vir sapiens quædam requirat in eo, quem ad amicitiam admittat: plura, ut cum eo amicitiam servet: & sanctitas in animo esse possit per Dei gratiam, ante opera, durare sine piis operibus non possit, ac per opera fidei servetur Dei in homines favor, & jus ipsorum ad vitam æternam. Non habet se Deus ut homo, non justificatio, ut amicitia inter homines contractus. Quæ requirit homo in amico, non facit ipse, sed ab ejus facultate expectat, cum quo amicitiam init. Alia Dei ratio est, qui cum admittit aliquos ad amicitiam, eos non admittit sponte venientes, sed ad se trahit, & quicquid ab illis requirit, ut favore non excidant, ipse in iis facit & operatur: a quo & velle & perficere est, & initium & continuatio, adeoque finis ipse: qui proinde gratia sua præstat, quæ ad amicitiam servandam requirit. Per opera fidei servari favorem Dei, & jus vitæ inversus sermo est. Contrarium Scriptura docet, per favorem & gratiam Dei servari fidem, & effici opera Deo grata; per gratiam & favorem Dei nos custodiri in fide ad salutem & vitam, 1. Petr. 1, 5. opera nostra nimis imperfecta, nimis immunda, nimis impotentia sunt ad conservandam fidem, ad custodiendum jus vitæ æternæ. Num fructus servat arborem, an vero arbor servat, aut fovet fructum?

## 9:6
Ver. 6. SINCE THE PEOPLE IS OF A MOST STIFF NECK.

A metaphor from oxen or beasts of burden, which do not know how to submit their necks to the yoke. One who is inflexible of mind. LXX. λαὸς σκληροτράχηλος, which is repeated in Acts 7:5. Thus the Israelites are called in Exod. 32:9, ch. 33:3, 5, ch. 34:9, Deut. 9:13, ch. 31:33, 2 Kings 17:14, Neh. 9:16, Jer. 7:26, ch. 19:15. For although the rebels had died, the histories of Joshua and the Judges taught that the survivors were nevertheless endowed with the same disposition, equally prone to idolatry and disobedience.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CUM DURISSIMÆ CERVICIS SIT POPULUS.

Metaphora a bobus vel jumentis, quæ colla sua jugo subjicere nesciunt. Qui mentis est inflexibilis. LXX. λαὸς σκληροτράχηλος, quod repetitur Act. 7, 5. Sic vocantur ísraelitæ Exod. 32, 9. c. 33, 3. 5. c. 34, 9. Deut. 9, 13. c. 31, 33. 2. Reg. 17, 14. Neh. 9, 16. Jer. 7, 26. c. 19, 15. Licet enim rebelles mortui fuerint, superstites tamen eodem præditos ingenio fuisse, æque ad idololatriam, & inobedientiam proclives Josuæ & Judicum historiæ docuerunt.

## 9:13
Ver. 13. OF A STIFF NECK) To speak with Horace, Not yet able to bear the yoke with an unsubdued neck.

Latin:

Vers. 13. DVRÆ CERVICIS) Vt cum Horatio loquar, Nondum subacta ferre jugum valens Cervice.

## 9:14
ver. 14. I WILL MAKE THEE OVER A NATION, WHICH IS GREATER AND STRONGER THAN THIS.

The Vulgate sounds as if it refers to another nation, over which Moses is to be set, and some so understand it. Jerome adapts it to the calling of the Gentiles in Jer. 17. The sense is plain in the Hebrew: And I will make thee into a nation robust and great beyond that one. As He made Jacob into this great and robust nation, so it was easy for the Lord to make Moses into a robust and greater nation.

Latin:

vers. 14. CONSTITUAM TE SUPER GENTEM, QUÆ HAC MAJOR ET FORTIOR SIT.

De alia gente, cui præficiendus Moses sit, Vulgata sonat & nonnulli accipiunt. Ad vocationem gentium Hieronymus accommodat in Jer. 17. Sensus planus est in Ebr. Et faciam te in gentem robustam & magnam præ illo. Ut Jacobum in hanc gentem magnam & robustam fecit, ita facile erat Domino, Mosen in gentem robustam & majorem facere.

## 9:17
Ver. 17. I BROKE THEM.

The Hebrews say that the letters of the law flew off from the tablets after they were brought into a place polluted by idolatry, and that for this reason Moses cast them away. But these are trifles. Moses saw that they had made a calf against the covenant of the Lord, therefore he threw down the tablets of the covenant and broke them. Theodoret, q. 68 in Exod., says: Since the tablets had the form of marriage settlement documents, and the bride had turned aside to commit adultery on the very threshold of the bridal chamber, he rightly broke the marriage documents.

Latin:

Vers. 17. CONFREGI EAS.

Ebræi dicunt literas legis a tabulis avolasse, postquam delatæ fuere in locum idololatria pollutum, ideo eas abjecisse Mosen. Sed hæ nugæ sunt. Videbat Moses vitulum eos fecisse contra fœdus Domini, ideo tabulas fœderis projecit, & confregit. Theod. q. 68. in Exod. cum Tabulæ ejusmodi, inquit, dotalium instrumentorum formam haberent, sponsa vero in ipso limine thalami nuptialis ad committendum adulterium declinaverit, jure profecto dotales literas effregit.

## 9:20
ver. 20. AGAINST AARON ALSO HE WAS VEHEMENTLY ANGRY.

Marius and Bonfrerius acknowledge that Aaron sinned. Cf. 5:21 and Exod. 32:4, 5. If High Priests

The men of the Old Testament could err, whose order was instituted by God; how much more will the Roman Pontiffs be able to err, whose order is only from men? But one must not yield to Bellarmine, lib. III. de Eccl., and the Jesuits at the Ratisbon Colloquy, f. 63, that Moses was then high priest, and Aaron had not yet been consecrated. For Moses was not a priest, but performed priestly duties only extraordinarily, whereas Aaron was an ordinary priest, which Cornelius a Lapide acknowledges in Acts 7. What he brings forward, that Aaron did not defect from the faith but from the profession of faith, does not pertain to the matter, because it is sufficient that he erred in the public profession of faith, and it is in no way consistent with the truth. For to fall into idolatry and to induce others to it, which Cornelius concedes regarding Aaron in Ex. 32, cannot consist with faith. Tanner in Exam. narrat. de Coll. Ratisbon denies that he erred in defining, but how does he who proposes idolatrous worship to the people by public voice not err in defining?

Latin:

vers. 20. ADVERSUS AARON QUOQUE VEHEMENTER IRATUS.

Peccasse Aaronem agnoscit Marius & Bonfrerius. Conf. 5, 21. & Exod. 32, 4. 5. Si Pontifices

V. T. errare potuere, quorum ordo a Deo institu- tus, quanto magis errare poterunt Pontifices Ro- mani, quorum ordo solum est ab hominibus? Non vero assurgendum Bellarmino lib. III. de Eccl. ac Jesuitis Ratisbon. Colloq. f. 63. quod Moses tunc Sa- cerdos summus, & Aaron nondum consecratus fue- rit. Moses enim Sacerdos non fuit, sed extraordi- narie tantum functus est officiis sacerdotalibus, Aaron vero ordinarius Sacerdos fuit, quod agno- scit Cornel. a Lap. in Act. 7. Quod adducit, Aaro- nem non a fide, sed professione fidei defecisse, nec ad rem facit, quia sufficit in publica fidei professione eum errasse, nec ullatenus vero est consentaneum. Nam in idololatriam prolabi, aliosque ad eam indu- cere, quod de Aarone concedit Cornel. in Ex. 32. cum fide consistere non potest. Tanner. in Exam. narrat. de Coll. Ratisb. negat eum errasse in defi- niendo, sed qui idololatricum cultum populo pro- ponit per publicam vocem, quomodo non errat in definiendo?

## 9:21
Verse 21.

BUT YOUR SIN) Both the occasions and the punishments of sins are called sins by the Hebrews.

Verse same. I BURNED WITH FIRE, BREAKING IT INTO PIECES, AND REDUCING IT ALTOGETHER INTO DUST, I CAST IT INTO THE TORRENT.

There was no need for herbs to be added so that it might be melted into a mass, or for some hidden art, as Torniellus wishes, or a miracle, so that it might be reduced to dust, if indeed the text teaches that this was done by breaking it into pieces, and the pieces could have been reduced into very small parts by a file, or pounded in a mortar.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

PECCATVM AVTEM VESTRVM) Tam occasiones, quam poenæ peccatorum peccata vocantur Hebræis.

Vers. eod. IGNE COMBUSSI IN FRU- STA COMMINUENS, OMNINOQUE IN PULVEREM REDIGENS PROJECI IN TOR- RENTEM.

Non opus vel herbis admissis, ut liquaretur in massam, vel occulta quadam arte, ut Torniellus vult, aut miraculo, ut in pulverem redigeretur, siquidem id comminutione in frustra factum textus doceat, ac lima in minutissimas partes redigi frusta potue- rint, aut in mortario contundi.

## 9:22
Verse 22. ALSO BY FIRE AND IN TEMPTATION AND IN THE SEPULCHRES OF CONCUPISCENCE YOU PROVOKED THE LORD.

The Hebrew names are proper names of places: Even in Taberah and in Massah and in Kibroth-hattaavah. The first rebellion is held in Taberah, Num. 11, 1, arising from the weariness of the journey. The second in Massah, Ex. 17, 1, on account of the lack of water. The third in Kibroth-hattaavah on account of the desire for meat, Num. 11, 4. To these is added v. 23, a fourth in Kadesh-barnea, on account of the report of the spies of the land of Canaan, Num. 13, 26 seqq., which, so that those notable rebellions might be proposed to them at once, he joins with that which happened in Horeb: even though those in Taberah, in Kibroth-hattaavah, and in Kadesh-barnea occurred after the second encampment on the mountain, to which he returns in v. 25. Osiander considers that in Taberah and Kibroth-hattaavah to be one and the same, but it arose in different places, from different causes, and was punished with different punishments. The former by fire falling upon the extremities of the camp. The latter by a great striking or sudden pestilence.

Latin:

Vers. 22. INCENDIO QUOQUE ET IN TENTATIONE ET IN SEPULCRIS CON- SCIENTIÆ PROVOCASTIS DOMINUM.

Nomina Ebræa propria sunt locorum nomi- na: Etiam in Thabera & in Massa & in Kibrothha- vah. Prima rebellio in Tabera habetur Num. 11, 1. orta e tædio itineris. Altera in Massa Ex. 17, 1. ob defectum aquæ. Tertia Kibrotis thaava ob de- siderium carnium Num. 11, 4. His additur v. 23. quarta in Cadesbarnea, ob relationem explorato- rum terræ Cannaan Num. 13, 26. seqq. quas, ut simul illis rebelliones illæ insignes proponantur, con- jungit cum illa, quæ in Horeb accidit: etsi illæ in Tabera in Kibroth thaava in Cadesbarnea post se- cundam mansionem in monte, ad quam v. 25. redit, contigere. Osiander illam in Tabera & Kibrotisthaa- vah pro una, & eadem habet, sed in diversis locis, ex diversis causis orta est & diversis pœnis castigata. Prior igne extremitati castrorum incidente. Poste- rior percussione magna vel subitanea pestilentia.

## 9:25
Verse 25. AND I LAY BEFORE THE LORD FORTY DAYS.

The Hebrews say that Moses was on the mountain for three periods of forty days, to which Cajetan and Salian in Annal. agree. But since in Exodus at least two are commemorated, where the history is described more fully, those things which are held in v. 18 and 25 are to be referred to the same time: for those things in v. 25 do not pertain to the immediately preceding things and the history of the deeds in Kadesh-barnea, but by repetition Moses goes back to those things which were done on Mount Horeb and mentioned in v. 18 (concerning which c. 10, 10), whence those things which are inserted between them are to be read as a parenthesis.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ET JACUI CORAM DOMINO QUADRAGINTA DIEBUS.

Ebræi Mosen tribus quadragesimis in monte fuisse dicunt, quibus annuit Cajetanus & Salian. in Annal. Sed quum in Exodo duæ saltim commemo- rentur, ubi plenius historia describitur, ea quæ v. 18. & 25. habentur ad idem tempus referenda: Non enim illa in v. 25. pertinent ad immediate an- tecedentia & historiam gestorum in Cadesbarnea, sed per repetitionem regreditur Moses ad ea, quæ in monte Horeb facta & v. 18. memorata (de qui- bus c. 10, 10.) sunt, unde quæ illis interferta, per parenthesin legenda.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAP. X.
