The restoration of the tables of the law is repeated, and the separation of the Levites, and the fear and observance of the commandments of the Lord are inculcated.

Latin:

CAP. X.

Tabularum legis instauratio repetitur, ac Levi- tarum separatio, & inculcatur timor & observatio mandatorum Domini.

## 10:6
BUT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL MOVED THEIR CAMPS FROM BEEROTH OF THE CHILDREN OF JACAN TO MOSERA) This clause, and what follows, can be seen to have crept into a strange place through some error of a scribe, who was unwilling to render his copy useless by deleting anything (for it was not permitted to have such copies). For they do not pertain here at all. And the journey was not directed from the habitation of the children of Jacan to Mosera, but on the contrary from Mosera to there, as we warned above on Num. 33, 31. Nor did Aaron die in Mosera but in Hor: after many days' journeys from Mosera, Num. 33, 38. That it is an ancient error, however, you may know from the Greek. But in these and similar matters let us suspend judgment until better Greek codices appear, the edition of which is being prepared in England.

There is no reason why we should imagine a corruption here: the versions agree with the Hebrew text; in none is a trace of such an error detected. Which, therefore, Grotius invents without necessity and against the honor due to the Holy Scripture. If it is permitted to suspect such things in difficult places, to what will the Holy Codex not be subject by suspicions? This is to cut the knot which you cannot untie. To expect an emendation from England from better Greek codices, and indeed an emendation of the Hebrew Codex, is to expect the purification of the fountain from the rivulets. And whence that certainty of better codices, regarding this or another difficult text? Other interpreters of whatever parties, Jews, Christians, Catholics, Reformed, our own, are more rightly concerned with the reconciliation of these apparent contradictions. Most people think that this clause and the following one, indeed the following ones up to the tenth, should be read parenthetically, and they assign the reason for the inserted parenthesis: both because those benefits given to the people at the same time are recalled to mind, and because God not only renewed the covenant through the restoration of the tables, but also continued the priesthood through the substitution of Eleazar in the place of the deceased Aaron, and because, having made mention of the tables, He wished to indicate at the same time to whom God had entrusted the custody of this deposit, namely, to the high priest of sacred things and to the Levitical tribe. Thus, therefore, the parenthesis is by no means foreign, but has its own reasons.

That in Num. 33, 30, the journey is said to have been instituted from Mosera to the habitation of the children of Jacan does not conflict with this contrary departure, provided that in that long wandering in the desert they could have measured the distance between them twice, once from Mosera to Beeroth of the children of Jacan, as is commemorated in Num. 33, and again from this place to Mosereth according to this account. When this reconciliation came to my mind, I saw it also approved by our blessed Gerhard in his commentary on this passage. Which, as being most convenient, I judge to be preferred to the diverse explanations of the Rabbis and others. Although, therefore, Aaron died in Hor, the mountain of Hor nevertheless also included Moseroth, or, as others prefer, was a certain part of the region of Mosera (because this name is general). Whence, when they came to Mosera a second time, Aaron died on that mountain. Therefore the verb נָסְעוּ is to be rendered, THEY HAD DEPARTED. Cf. the blessed Gerhard on this passage. Mr. Dr. Varenius in Decad. on Num. ch. 33, 31, p. 102, observes these things for the reconciliation: 1. In the passage of Num. 33, the name of the station is always Moseroth, in Deuter. Mosera. 2. The other station is called simply of the children of Jakan: thus Beroth Bee Jakan or of the wells, which were of the children of Jakan. 3. Mosera here is not Milel, but Milra. 4. Moseroth is something other than Mosera. 5. This is the name of a very extensive desert, stretched as far as the mountains of Hor, and thus Aaron could have died both on Mount Hor and in Mosera, even if not in that station called Moseroth, in the places of Num. 33, 30, 31.

Latin:

FILII AVTEM ISRAEL MOVERVNT CASTRA EX BEEROTH FILIORVM JACAN IN MOSERA) Hoc comma, & quod sequitur, videri potest errore quodam Librarii, nolentis sibi inutile Exemplar reddere aliquid de- lendo (talia enim exemplaria habere non licebat) irrepsisse in locum alienum. Neque enim huc quicquam pertinent. Et iter non ab habitatione Filiorum Jacan in Mosera, sed con- tra a Moseris illuc directum fuit, ut monuimus supra Num. 33, 31. Neque Aaron mortuus est in Mosera sed in Hor: post multa dierum itinera a Mosera Num. 33, 38. Veterem tamen errorem esse, ex Græco cognoscas. Sed in his & similibus su- stineamus sententiam, donec meliores Codices Græci pro- dierint, quorum editio in Anglia adornatur.

Non est, quod hic fingamus corruptelam: Consonant cum Ebræo textu versiones; in nulla vestigium erroris ejusmodi deprehenditur. Quem proinde præter necessitatem, & contra honorem Sacrosanctæ Scripturæ debitum comminiscitur Grotius. Si ita suspicari in locis difficilibus liceat, quibus non suspicionibus obnoxius erit Sacer Co- dex? Hoc est nodum scindere, quem solvere non possis. Ab melioribus Codd. Græcis expectare emen- dationem ex Anglia, & quidem Ebræi Codicis emen- dationem, est a rivulis expectare fontis purifica- tionem. Et unde illa meliorum Codd. certitudo, quoad hunc aliumve difficilem textum? Rectius alii Interpp. quarumcunque partium, Judæi, Chri- stiani, Pontificii, Reformati, Nostri de conciliatione soliciti sunt harum ἐναντιοφανειῶν. Comma hoc & sequens, imo sequentia usque ad decimum παρενθε- τικῶς legenda esse plerique censent, ac causam in- fertæ Parentheseos assignant, tum quod beneficia il- la simul populo data ad animum revocentur, tum quod Deus non solum fœdus per reparationem ta- bularum renovarit, sed etiam sacerdotium per sur- rogationem Eleazari in locum Aaronis demortui continuarit, tum quod facta tabularum mentione, simul quibus hujus depositi custodiam commiserit Deus, indicare voluerit, sacrorum scil. summo An- tistiti, ac Leviticæ tribui. Sic ergo parenthesis mi- nime aliena est, sed rationes suas habet.

Quod Num. 33, 30. iter a Mosera ad habita- tionem filiorum Jacan institutum dicitur, non pu- gnat cum hac contraria profectione, siquidem po- tuerint in diuturna illa oberratione in deserto bis inter illud demetiri, semel ex Mosera in Beeroth, fi- liorum Jacan, ut Num. 33. commemoratur, atque iterum ex hoc loco in Mosereth juxta hanc relatio- nem. Quæ conciliatio ubi in mentem mihi venit, vidi eam etiam B. Gerhardonoftro approbatam Comment. in h. l. Quam uti convenientissimam, Rabbinorum & aliorum diversis explicationibus præferendam judico. Quamvis ergo Aaron mor- tuus in Hor sit, mons tamen Hor complectebatur etiam Moseroth, aut, ut alii malunt, fuit regionis Mo- seræ (quia nomen hoc generale est) pars quædam. Unde cum altera vice in Mosera venirent, in monte illo mortuus est Aaron. Ideo verbum נָסְעוּ red- dendum est, PROFECTI ERANT. Conf. B. Gerhardum in h. l. Dn. D. Varenius in Decad. ad Numer. cap. 33, 31. p. 102. hæc pro conciliatione observat. 1. In loco Num. 33. semper stationis no- men Moseroth, in Deuter. Mosera, 2. altera sta- tio appellatur simpliciter filiorum Jakan: Sic Be- roth Bee Jakan seu puteorum, qui fuerint filiorum Jakan. 3. Mosera hic non Milel, sed Milra. 4. Mo- seroth aliud quam Mosera. 5. Hoc nomen amplis- simi deserti, protensi ad usque montana Hor, & sic Aaron mori potuit & in monte Hor, & in Mosera, etsi non in illa statione, Moseroth dicta, in loca Numer. 33, 30. 31.

## 10:8
Vers. 8.

HE SEPARATED THE TRIBE OF LEVI, THAT

TO CARRY THE ARK OF THE COVENANT OF THE LORD AND TO STAND BEFORE HIM IN MINISTRY, AND TO BLESS IN HIS NAME. The LXX understand a common blessing: καὶ ἐπεύχεσθαι καὶ εὐλογεῖν. Prayers, hymns, and canticles in divine worship and Levitical sacrifices were blessings. But if it is understood concerning the solemn blessing in Num. 6:23, it is certain that it belonged to the Priests, who were of the same tribe as the Levites, 2 Chron. 24:13. And therefore these things must be taken distributively, because carrying the ark of the Lord was of the lower order of the Levites (even if the Priests also carried it in solemn acts), while standing before the face of the Lord to sacrifice, and to bless, belonged to the Priests alone.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

SEPARAVIT TRIBUM LEVI, UT

PORTARET ARCAM FOEDERIS DOMINI ET STARET CORAM EO IN MINISTE- RIO, AC BENEDICERET IN NOMINE IL- LIUS. Benedictionem communem intelligunt LXX. καὶ ἐπεύχεσθαι καὶ εὐλογεῖν. Preces, hymni, & can- tica in cultu divino & Sacrificiis Leviticis erant be- nedictiones. At si de benedictione solemni Num. 6, 23. intelligatur, certum est, eam Sacerdotum fuis- se, qui ejusdem tribus cum Levitis erant 2. Par. 24, 13. Ideoque distributive hæc accipienda erunt, quia portare arcam Domini Levitarum erat infe- rioris ordinis, (etsi etiam in solemnibus actibus Sacerdotes eam portarent) stare ante faciem Do- mini ad sacrificandum, & benedicere solum Sacer- dotum.

## 10:9
Verse 9.

THE LORD HIMSELF IS HIS POSSESSION) Which is mystically fulfilled in Christians.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

IPSE DOMINVS POSSESSIO EJVS EST) Quod mystice impletur in Christianis.

## 10:12
Verse 12.

WHAT DOES THE LORD THY GOD REQUIRE OF THEE, BUT THAT THOU SHOULDST FEAR THE LORD THY GOD, AND WALK IN HIS WAYS, AND LOVE HIM, AND SERVE THE LORD THY GOD WITH ALL THY HEART AND WITH ALL THY SOUL) All precepts tend to this: this is the end of the law, which the grace of the Gospel effects.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

QVID DOMINVS DEVS TVVS PETIT A TE, NISI VT TIMEAS DOMINVM DEVM TVVM, ET AMBVLES IN VIIS EJVS, ET DILIGAS EVM, AC SERVIAS DOMINO DEO TVO IN TOTO CORDE TVO ET IN TOTA ANIMA TVA) Omnia præcepta huc tendunt: hic finis est legis, quem efficit gratia Evangelii.

## 10:13
Verse 13.

THAT IT MAY BE WELL WITH THEE) Not with God, to whom our services contribute nothing, although He Himself generously repays them as if they were conferred upon Him. HEAVEN OF HEAVENS) The heaven of heavens, i.e., the highest heaven above the air and the ether: the third heaven: the seat of the Angels and of the divine Majesty.

Nowhere does Scripture teach that the heaven of heavens is constituted by reason of its location above the air or the ether: nowhere does it place there the third heaven, which Paul calls by that name: nor does it set the Angels above the firmament, and fix them to those places above the spheres of the stars, much less the divine majesty: which the heavens of heavens do not contain, 1 Kings 8:46, since God fills heaven and earth with His majesty, Jer. 23. The heaven of heavens, therefore, is said to be so by reason of excellence, according to the custom of the Hebrews, who thus express the superlative degree and eminence; when it is indicated to be above, it designates the sublimity not of place or situation, but of majesty. In which sense Athanasius also explains the words of the sacred psalmist, Tom. I, p. 663. He who says the heaven of heavens is the Lord's, but the earth He has given to the children of men, does not assign heaven to the Lord as a place of domicile, and the earth to men: but he subjects to the eyes the excellence of God and His magnificence. Since, therefore, majesty and magnificence in God are named as something super-celestial: that which is contrary to this is said to be humble, earthly, and to dwell on earth: you will very easily discover that the descent of the Word is an inclination from incorporeal majesty to the vileness of the body, when He gave Himself into a bodily form, out of love for the human race and the saving providence of all: and therefore He will be found to have been sent, since by the ineffable will of the incorporeal Father He delivered Himself to a body. Let not these bodily terms, therefore, i.e., descent and emission, be brought forward to infect His incarnation, since God neither descends nor is sent locally: but let them hear the Apostle explaining that matter and such comparisons and metaphors, who, when He was in the form of God, did not think it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men. For this is to descend, this is to be sent and included in a garment viler than befits His own dignity. The descent is likewise the superinduction and investment of the human form, instituted according to the will of the Father. But if the Word is not circumscribed by place and body, He will not be torn away from the incorporeal Father on account of the tempering of His body: for the body receives Him willingly, insofar as human nature is fit to receive God: He remains nevertheless in His own nature, which existed before the incarnation. Wherefore the descent from heaven was not a departure from heaven: nor likewise was the emission from heaven a separation from the sending Father. These are the words of Athanasius. See what we have said concerning this heaven in Tom. III, System. Theol. c. 5, Q. 2.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

VT BENE SIT TIBI) Non Deo, cui nostra obsequia nihil conferunt, quanquam ipse velut sibi collata large re- pensat. COELVM COELI) Cœlum Cœlorum, i. e. supremum cœlum supra aërem ætheremque: Cœlum tertium: sedes Angelorum, & divinæ Majestatis.

Nuspiam Scriptura docet, cœlum cœlorum esse, ratione situs supra aerem vel æthera constitutum: nuspiam cœlum tertium, quod ita Paulus vocat, ibi collocat: nec Angelos supra firmamentum ponit, locisque istis supra sphæras stellarum affigit, nedum majestatem divinam: quam cæli cælorum non com- prehendunt 1. Reg. 8, 46. quum Deus majestate sua cœlum & terram impleat Jer. 23. Cœlum cœlorum ergo ob excellentiam more Ebræis, qui ita ἐξοχὴν & superlativum gradum exprimunt, usitato, dici- tur; Cum sursum esse indicatur, sublimitas non lo- ci, seu situs, sed majestatis designatur. Quo sensu etiam verba Hieropsaltis explicat Athanasius Tom. I. p. 663. Is qui dicit cœlum cœlorum Domini, ter- ram autem dedit filiis hominum, non pro loco domici- lii cœlum adsortitur Domino, & hominibus terram: sed excellentiam Dei magnificentiæq́; oculis subji- cit. Cum igitur majestas & magnificentia in Deo su- percœleste quiddam nominatur: id quod huic contra- rium est, humile terrenum dicatur & in terris ver- sari: facillime comperies, descensum verbi inclina- tionem esse ex incorporali majestate ad vilitatem cor- poris, cum seipsum dederit in corporalem speciem, hu- mani generis amore & salutari universorum provi- dentia: ideoq́; missus comperietur, quoniam ineffa- bili Patris incorporei voluntate seipsum corpori tra- diderit. Ne igitur corporales istæ voces h. e. descensio & emissio ad inficiendam ejus incarnationem produ- cantur, quoniam localiter neq́; descendit Deus neq́; e- mittitur: sed audiant Apostolum id negotii, & ejus- modi comparationes metaphorasq́; explicantem, qui cum in forma Dei esset, non rapinam arbitratus est, esse se æqualem Deo, sed seipsum exinanivit, formam servi accipiens, in similitudinem hominum factus. Hoc enim est descendere, hoc emitti includique in a- miculum vilius, quam pro ipsius dignitate. Descensus item humanæ speciei superinductio atq́; investitio est, secundum Patris voluntatem instituta. Quod si loco & corpore verbum non circumscribitur, non avelle- tur ab incorporali Patre ob corporis sui attempera- mentum: nam excipit eum volentem corpus, quate- nus idonea est humana natura Deum suscipere: ma- net nihilominus in sui ipsius natura, quæ ante incar- nationem fuit. Quamobrem descensus e cælo non fuit digressio e cælo: neque item emissio e cælo, a Patre mit- tente segregatio. Hæc Athanasius. Vide quæ de hoc cœlo diximus Tom. III. System. Theol. c. 5. Q. 2.

## 10:16
Verse 16. CIRCUMCISE THEREFORE THE FORESKIN OF YOUR HEART) The Chaldean: Take away foolishness: Cf. Jer. 4:4. The same work is ascribed to man, as here; and to God, as below 30:6. To God as the principal cause, to man as the intervening cause.

These things are said from the perspective of the Papists: who attribute ἐνέργειαν to man in conversion, and allow the work of conversion between God and the powers of free will, truly Pelagianizing. If he had called man a material cause, or had explained from the Scriptures how man is commanded to circumcise the foreskin, he would not have left room for such a distribution of the divine work, which God claims entirely for Himself. For it is God who takes away the heart of stone and puts in a heart of flesh Ez. 36, who CREATES a new heart in us Ps. 51, to which certainly man can contribute nothing, just as he could contribute nothing to his own conversion. And thus the circumcision of the foreskin of our heart is done by a divine hand and power, and is not of human effort. Man behaves merely παθητικῶς or passively. It is God who works both to will and to perform Phil. 2. But they are commanded to circumcise the foreskin of the heart, so that they do not resist God, who circumcises our heart, and do not exclude the means ordained for spiritual circumcision. Meanwhile, as regards the regenerate and converted, to whom these things are also said, not because they are uncircumcised in heart, as those hearers of Stephen were Acts 7, but because circumcision here is only done μερικῶς, and is never made perfect: where we are renewed not entirely, but in part: the old man and the flesh are still always left, and something of the carnal foreskin, which has need to be circumcised: we readily grant that they can, and indeed ought to, cooperate with the Holy Spirit, and in that sense we do not disapprove of spiritual circumcision being ascribed to God as the principal cause, and to man, namely the regenerate, as the intervening cause, just as we are commanded to be renewed more and more, to progress in sanctification, and to be transformed into the image of God, from glory to glory, Eph. 4, 23. 1. Cor. 3, 18. c. 4, 16. c. 7, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 16. CIRCVMCIDITE IGITVR PRÆPVTIVM CORDIS VESTRI) Chaldæus: Auferte stultitiam: Conf. Jer. 4, 4. Idem opus & homini adscribitur, ut hîc; & Deo ut infra 30, 6. Deo, ut causæ principi, homini ut causæ inter- venienti.

Hæc e sensu Pontificiorum dicuntur: qui ἐνέρ- γειαν tribuunt homini conversione, & inter De- um ac vires liberi arbitrii patiuntur conversionis opus, vere Pelagianizantes. Si hominem causam materialem dixisset, vel quomodo circumcidere jubeatur homo præputium, explicasset e Scripturis, tali distributioni divini operis, quod Deus in soli- dum sibi vendicat, locum non reliquisset. Deus enim est, qui aufert cor lapideum & indit cor carneum Ez. 36. qui cor novum in nobis CREAT Ps. 51. ad quod certe homo nihil conferre potest, æque ut nihil ad sui conversionem poterat conferre. Atque ita circumcisio præputii cordis nostri divina manu ac virtute fit, non autem humanæ opis est. Homo se habet mere παθητικῶς vel passive. Deus est, qui & velle & perficere operatur Phil. I!. Circumcide- re autem jubentur præputium cordis, ut Deo, qui cor nostrum circumcidit, ne repugnent, mediaque circumcisioni spirituali ordinata ne excludant. Interea quod ad regenitos & conversos attinet, qui- bus etiam hæc dicuntur, non quod incircumcisi sint corde, uti Auditores illi Stephani erant Act. 7. sed quod circumcisio hic tantum fiat μερικῶς, & perfe- cta nunquam fit: ubi renovamur non ex asse, sed ex parte: semper adhuc vetus homo & caro relinqui- tur, ac præputii carnalis quidpiam, quod circumci- di opus habet: facile largimur, quod cooperari illi possint, atq; debeant Spiritui S. & eo sensu non im- probamus, Deo ut causæ principi, homini, scil. rena- to, ut causæ intervenienti circumcisionem spiritualem adscribi, quemadmodum ipsi subinde magis magisq; renovari, in sanctificatione proficere, & ad imaginem Dei transformari jubemur, de claritate in clarita- tem, Eph. 4, 23. 1. Cor. 3, 18. c. 4, 16. c. 7, 7.

## 10:17
Vers. 17. GOD OF GODS) That is, of the Angels. And hence it appears, as often as אלהים is joined to a singular, that there is an ἔλλειψιν of the word אלהי as in חכמות & נחמות & similar ones. The full expression is here.

LORD OF LORDS) Of kings and others eminent among men, as 1 Tim. 6, 16. Certain Hebrews interpret the dominant ones as the stars, which have great power over human affairs.

That distribution of Gods and Lords, so that by the former only Angels are understood, and by the latter kings and princes, seems more subtle than solid. For by the name of Gods, not only Angels, but also Magistrates are accustomed to be included, Psalm 26, 1. There are Θεοὶ λεγόμενοι both in heaven and on earth, as the Apostle testifies 1 Cor. 8, 6. Nor is the name of Lords attributed only to earthly Kings, since there are also dominions κυριότητες in heaven, Col. 1, 16. But that the stars should be indicated by the name of Lords and have dominion over human affairs is foreign to the Scriptures. They do not dominate, but serve men: indeed the wise man, as it is said, will dominate the stars. But as for the word אלהים, as often as it is joined to a singular, that it is used elliptically, and that the singular אל God of Gods ought to be understood, whence will it be proved? For because here GOD of Gods is said, it does not follow that always where אלהים occurs constructed in the singular it must also be explained as GOD of Gods. It is used immediately at the beginning of creation Genesis 1, 1. בראשית ברא אלהים, where there were as yet no Gods. Nor is an ellipsis to be invented where there is no There is no cause for it. And that there is no place for the same, parallel passages teach, since now that noun is joined in the same singular matter, now in the plural, so that it is understood to be taken truly πληθυντικῶς. We have previously warned that a mystery of the plurality of divine persons underlies this locution; which argument, having been deduced elsewhere against the Socinians and Jews, Grotius, as if doing something else, attempted to undermine with this little grammatical observation for the sake of the Socinians and Jews.

Latin:

Vers. 17. DEVS DEORVM) Id est, Angelorum. Atque hinc apparet, quoties אלהים singulari jungitur, esse ἔλ- λειψιν vocis אלהי ut in חכמות & נחמות & similibus. Plena locutio hic est.

DOMINVS DOMINANTIVM) Regum aliorumque inter homines eminentium, ut 1. Tim. 6, 16. Hebræi qui- dam dominantes interpretantur astra, quorum in res huma- nas magna vis.

Distributio illa Deorum & Dominantium, ut per illos Angeli soli, per hos reges & principes intelligantur, argutior videtur, quam solidior. Nam Deorum nomine non Angeli solum, sed etiam Ma- gistratus comprehendi solent Psal. 26, 1. Θεοὶ λεγό- μενοι sunt & in cælis, & in terris, teste Apostolo 1. Cor. 8, 6. neque nomen Dominantium Regibus so- lum terrenis tribuitur, quum & dominationes κυ- ριότητες in cælis sint, Col. 1, 16. Astra autem Domi- nantium nomine indigitari & dominium in res hu- manas habere, a Scripturis alienum est. Non domi- nantur, sed inserviunt hominibus: imo sapiens, ut dicitur, dominabitur astris. Vocem autem אלהים quoties singulari jungitur, elliptικῶς adhiberi, & lobim subintelligi debere singulare אל Deus Deorum, unde probabitur? Nam quia hic DEVS Deo- rum dicitur, semper ubi אלהים occurrit singu- lariter constructum etiam explicari debet DEVS Deorum. Adhibetur statim in principio creatio- nis Genes. 1, 1. בראשית ברא אלהים, ubi nul- li erant adhuc Dii. Ne ellipsis fingenda est, ubi nul- nulla ejus causa est. Neque locum eidem esse, loca parallela docent, cum modo nomen illud in eadem materia singulari, modo plurali jungitur, ut vere πληθυντικῶς accipi inrelligatur. Subesse autem my- sterium pluralitatis personarum divinarum huic lo- cutioni, antea monuimus; quod argumentum ali- bi contra Socinianos & Judæos deductum hac obser- vatiuncula sua Grammatica in gratiam Sociniano- rum & Judæorum labefactare, quasi aliud agens, conatus est Grotius.

## 10:18
Vers. 18. HE EXECUTETH JUDGMENT FOR THE FATHERLESS AND WIDOW) That is, he vindicates them.

AND THOU SHALT SWEAR BY HIS NAME. Concerning the swearing of an oath in the name of GOD alone, not by creatures, we spoke against the Papists at Deut. 6, 13. The Jesuit Marius ought to have borne witness to the truth here in his Commentary on this passage. Since an oath is a protestation of omniscience and omnipotence, it ought not to be made except in the name of the true GOD. Rivetus also argues not obscurely against our countrymen regarding the superstitious Papistical abuse, by which the honor of God is not left unviolated, when in oaths the words are conceived thus: 'so may God help me, and these holy Gospels,' or he who swears touches the codex of the Gospels or the holy Bible with his hand, in Explic. decal. page 88. For he says of that formula, if the words are so conceived, that the remnants of superstition cannot be excused: but concerning the rite of touching the book of the Gospel when someone swears that he is speaking the truth before God, just as he believes the things that are read in the Gospel to be true, although Rivetus seems to judge otherwise, he nevertheless adds immediately that it is safer to abstain from all such things in which a superstitious abuse has flourished for so long and still flourishes, so that God's honor may remain unviolated. But just as we taught in the aforementioned place that there are no remnants of superstition there, so that explanation which Rivetus gives concerning the truth of the Gospel does not suffice to exhaust the force of the formula; because it is not the truth, but the ἐνέργεια and efficacy of the same that is alleged: 'so may God help me, and the holy Gospel': which is indeed the power of God unto salvation, Rom. 1, 16. Nor is there any superstition or detraction from divine honor, when divine power is attributed to the word of the Gospel, because what is ascribed to organic causes is referred primarily to the principal cause.

Latin:

Vers. 18. FACIT JUDICIUM PUPILLO ET VIDUÆ) Id est, vindicat eos.

JURABISQUE IN NOMINE EJUS. De juramento in solo DEI nomine præstando, non per creaturas adversus Papistas diximus Deut. 6, 13. Veritati testimonium hic perhibere debuit Jesuita Marius in Comm. ad h. l. Juramentum cum sit protestatio omniscientiæ & omnipotentiæ, non de- bet fieri nisi in nomine veri DEI. Rivetus nostrates etiam non obscure arguit abusus superstitiosi Papi- stici, quo Dei honor non relinquatur illibatus, cum in juramentis verba ita concipiuntur, ita me Deus ju- vet, & hæc sacra Evangelica, vel manu tangit Evan- geliorum codicem, aut Biblia sacra, qui jurat, in Ex- plic. decal. pag. 88. Nam de formula illa dicit, si ita verba concipiantur; excusari non posse reliquias su- perstitionis: de ritu vero tangendi librum Evange- lii, cum quis jurat, coram Deo sè vera dicere, quem- admodum vera credit, quæ in Evangelio leguntur, etsi secus videatur judicare Rivetus, addit tamen statim, tutius esse a talibus omnibus abstinere, in qui- bus tamdiu viguit, & adhuc viget abusus superstitio- sus, ut Deo suus honor illibatus maneat. Sed ut reli- quias superstitionis nullas ibi esse, l. c. docuimus, ita non sufficit illa explicatio ad vim formulæ ex- hauriendam, quam dat Rivetus de veritate Evan- gelii; quia non veritas, sed ἐνέργεια & efficacia ejus- dem allegatur: ita me juvet Deus, & sanctum Ev- avgelium: quod utique est potentia Dei ad salutem, Rom. 1, 16. nec ulla superstitio, aut honoris divini de- tractio est, cum verbo Evangelii vis divina tribui- tur, quia quod caufæ organicæ adscribitur, ad prin- cipalem primo refertur.

## 11:1 Argument
CHAP. XI. Blessing, and cursing.

Latin:

CAP. XI. Benedictio, & maledictio.

## 11:2
Vers. 2. KNOW YE THIS DAY, WHICH YOUR CHILDREN HAVE NOT KNOWN.

B. Gerhard renders the Hebrew thus: And you shall know this day, that not with your children, who have not known, and who have not seen the chastisement of Jehovah your God, his greatness, his mighty hand, and his stretched-out arm, etc. BUT (this meaning occurs in Jud. 1, 19. Psal. 37, 10. Jerem. 48, 45.) I speak with you, whose eyes see all the great work of Jehovah, which he did. The matter comes to the same thing if we understand the word 'I speak' immediately from the beginning with the others, that (I do not speak) with your children, who have not known, and who have not seen, etc. And the word may have the force of asseveration: certainly your eyes have seen, or if we render it by 'indeed': Know, or by metalepsis: consider this day, that I do not speak with your children, or, the Lord initiates this covenant, from Deut. 5, 3, who have not known, and who have not seen, etc. Because your eyes have seen; he speaks with those and initiates the covenant with those who have actually seen those things, not only with the children who have not seen them. For although those who were older than twenty years at the exodus had died in the desert, those nevertheless who had not yet reached their twentieth year, and were survivors, e.g., born in this last year of Moses, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59 years old, saw the works of the Lord in Egypt, when they were 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 years of age.

Latin:

Vers. 2. COGNOSCITE HODIE, QUÆ IGNORANT FILII VESTRI.

EBræa ita reddit B. Gerhardus: Et scietis hodie, quod non cum filiis vestris, qui non cognoverunt, & qui non viderunt castigationem Jehovæ Dei ve- stri, magnitudinem ejus, manum ejus validam, & brachium ejus extentum &c. SED (hæc signifi- catio occurrit Jud. 1, 19. Psal. 37, 10. Jerem. 48, 45.) vobiscum loquor, quorum oculi videntes omne opus Jehovæ magnum, quod fecit. Eodem res redit, si cum aliis verbum loquor statim subaudiamus ab initio, quod non cum filiis vestris (loquor.) Et verbum asseverandi vim habeat: certe oculi vestri vide- runt, aut si id per equidem reddamus: Scitote, vel per metaleptin: considerate hodie, quod non cum fi- liis vestris loquor, vel, Dominus hoc pactum init, e Deut. 5, 3. qui non cognoverunt, & qui non vide- runt &c. Quia oculi vestri viderunt; cum illis lo- quitur, & pactum init, qui adhuc viderunt illa, non solum cum filiis, qui ea haud viderunt. Quanquam enim, qui viginti annis majores erant in egressu, in deserto mortui essent, illi tamen, qui tum nondum attigerant annum vigesimum, & superstites erant, e. g. hoc Mosis postremo anno nati 55. 56. 57. 58. 59. annos, opera Domini viderunt in Ægypto, quum essent 15. 16. 17. 18. 19. annorum.

Vers. 10.

WATERS ARE LED IRRIGATED) In the Hebrew: with your foot you irrigate: what this may be, Philo, who lived in Egypt, explains very well: ὥσπερ ἡ ἁλιξ τὸ ὑδρηλὸν ὄργανον ἔχ᾿ κατὰ γὰρ μέσον αὐτῆς γεγόνασι βαθμοί τινες, ὧν ὁ γεωπόν@ ὅταν ὀτελήσῃ ποτίσαι τὰς ἀκύρας ἐπιβαίν᾽ μὲν περιολισθαίν᾽ δ᾽ ἀναγκαί- ως, &c. Vitruvius mentions it in passing, when he says that certain paddles force the wheel to turn, and at the end of the works, having been turned by the force of the river itself, it provides what is needed for use. It is about that treading of the works that is treated here.

## 12:1 Argument
CAP. XII. Idolatry and groves are exterminated; the place which the Lord shall choose is to be observed. The eating of blood is prohibited.

Latin:

CAP. XII. Idololatriæ & luci exterminantur; observandus locus, quem elegerit Dominus. Esus sanguinis prohibetur.

## 12:2 Addition
On Deut. 11. v. 18. TEACH YOUR CHILDREN.

Hence the Jews train their infants from an early age in the reading of the divine law, who often make such progress that the Jewish infants can strike shame into the elderly Christians themselves: for their axiom is: that the world would relapse into its ancient chaos, unless it were sustained by the habit and Spirit of the little ones and the innocent Thalmudim, that is, those learning the law. Therefore, they deem every land, city, and village in which there are only ten Israelites worthy of anathema, if they do not immediately procure for themselves a teacher and master for the little ones.

OVERTHROW ALL PLACES, IN WHICH THEY WORSHIPPED THE NATIONS &c.

Since this commandment is expressly referred to the idolatry of the Gentiles living in the holy land, Episcopius, l. 3. instit. c. 9. n. 1., judges that it, as it stands, does not pertain to the idolatry of the ten tribes, or that introduced by Jeroboam, inasmuch as it was not a little different from the idolatry previously practiced by the Gentiles in the land of Canaan, which, however, he rightly determines, if not of equal and the same, yet of a similar or very close mark and guilt of idolatry, and thus that GOD also wished it to be extirpated from the Jewish people, if He had gained control of affairs in that empire, and that too by the force of this law, as was done by certain Kings of Judah, 2 Chron. 14, ch. 17, v. 6.

Latin:

Ad Deut. 11. v. 18. DOCETE FILIOS VESTROS.

Inde Judæi infantes a prima ætate exercent in legis divinæ lectione, qui sæpe ita proficiunt, ut senibus ipsis Christianis infantes Judæi rubo- rem incutere possint : Axioma enim eorum est: mundum in chaos antiquum suum relapsurum: nisi habitu & Spiritu parvulorum atque innocentium Thalmudim, id est, legem discentium, sustineretur. Ideo terram, civitatem & pagum omnem, in quo decem tantum Israelitæ sunt anathemate dignum censent, si pædagogum parvulorum Doctorem & Magistrum e vestigio sibi non procurent.

SUBVERTITE OMNIA LOCA, IN QUIBUS COLUERUNT GEN- TES &c.

Quum præceptum hoc diserte referatur ad idololatriam gentilium in terra sancta habitantium, Episcopius l. 3. instit. c. 9. n. 1. id prout jacet ad ido- lolatriam decem tribuum, aut a Jeroboamo invectam non pertinere censet, utpote quæ a gentilium in terra Canaan ante exercita idololatria non parum diversa fuerit, quam tamen recte statuit, si non paris, & æqualis, attamen consimilis aut proximæ ad primam idololatriæ notam & culpam habuisse, adeoque DEUM etiam exstirpatam voluisse a populo Judaico, si rerum in eo imperio potitus fuiffet, idque ex vi etiam legis hujus, uti a Regibus quibusdam Juda factum 2. Paralip. 14. cap. 17. v. 6.

## 12:8
Vers. 8. NON FACIETIS, QUÆ NOS HIC FACIMUS HODIE [You shall not do what we do here today]) You shall not offer victims in just any places, but in one. That place was first Shiloh: then the Temple in Jerusalem. In the intermediate time this law ceased, because there was no fixed place for the sacred tent. For it was at Mizpah, Gilgal, Nob, Gibeon, and in the house of Obed-Edom.

Grotius follows the Rabbis. Thus Lyranus, from R. Solomon, teaches that in the desert, even after the construction of the tabernacle, it was possible to offer sacrifice and voluntary offerings elsewhere than in the tabernacle, but not the sacrifices and offerings which were offered out of obligation; nor did this precept about not offering voluntary sacrifices except in the tabernacle bind the Hebrews until they possessed the promised quiet land, i.e., after the distribution was made in 14 years and they had entered it. In the intermediate time, says R. Solomon, before the destruction of Shiloh and the completion of Solomon's temple, votive sacrifices and offerings could be made elsewhere than where the ark was, because at that time they did not have a stable dwelling. Just as also when they were in the desert. But this cannot be said of Shiloh, because there the ark had a stable dwelling for a long time, namely 343 years, which flowed from the 14th year of the leadership of Joshua, in which the ark was placed in Shiloh, until the death of Eli, when it was captured by the Philistines. Thus also Fagius teaches that the high places were lawful where the ark of the Lord was in Nob and Gibeon. Blessed Gerhard, however, thinks it should be deservedly doubted, since ἐθελοθρησκεία [will-worship] and high places are so strongly reprobated in the Scriptures, whether during the time of the sojourn in the desert, and likewise during the time intermediate between the destruction of Shiloh and the completion of the Solomonic temple, votive sacrifices ought to have been offered elsewhere than in the place of the ark of the covenant. Where the law does not distinguish, we ought not to distinguish. The examples of Gideon (Judg. 6:19), Manoah (Judg. 13:19), David (2 Sam. 22:25), and Elijah (1 Kings 18:33) were singular, and an extraordinary motion of the Holy Spirit intervened there. The Hebrews were bound to send sacrifices, as also tithes and firstfruits, to the place of the ark of the covenant, by which they were admonished that grace and the remission of sins were to be sought in the Messiah alone, and that spiritual sacrifices are not pleasing except in Him; whence also, when the Jerusalem temple was destroyed and the Jews were led away into captivity, they sent their gifts to Jerusalem. Baruch 1:6.

Latin:

Vers. 8. NON FACIETIS, QUÆ NOS HIC FACI- MUS HODIE) Non offeretis victimas quibusvis in lo- cis, sed in uno. Is locus fuit primum Silo: deinde Templum Hierosolymis. Medio tempore cessavit hæc lex, quod nullus sacro tentorio certus esset locus. Fuit enim Masphatæ, Gilgale, Nobæ, Gibeone, in domo Obededomi.

SEquitur Grotius Rabbinos. Sic Lyranus e R. Salomone docet, in deserto etiam post constru- Etionem tabernaculi potuisse offerri sacrificium & oblationes voluntarias alibi, quam in tabernaculo, non autem sacrificia & oblationes, quæ offereban- tur ex debito,neque hoc præceptum de non offeren- dis sacrificiis voluntariis, nisi in tabernaculo obli- gasse Ebræos, nisi postquam quietam terram pro- missam possiderent, h. e. post factam distributionem annis 14. & ingressum eam. Tempore medio, inquit R. Salomo, ante destructionem Silo, & consumma- tionem templi Salomonis sacrificia votiva, & obla- tiones poterant alibi fieri, quam ubi erat arca, quia eo tempore non habebant stabilem mansionem. Sicut etiam quando erant in deserto. Sic autem non potest dici de Silo, quia ibi arca habuit diu stabilem mansio- nem scil. 343. annis, qui fluxerunt a 14. anno ducatus Josuæ, quo fuit posita arca in Silo usque ad mortem He- li, quando fuit capta a Philistæis. Sic etiam Fagius ex- celsa licita fuisse docet, ubi in Nob & Gibeon arca Domini erat. B. Gerhardus vero censet, merito du- bitandum esse, cum ἐθελοθρησκεία, & excelsa in Scri- pturis adeo reprobentur, tempore commorationis in deserto, itemque tempore inter destructionem Silo & consummationem templi Salomonæi intermedio, sa- crificia votiva alibi, quam in loco arcæ fœderis offerri decuisse. Ubi lex non distinguit, nec nos distinguere debemus. Gideonis Jud. 6, 19. Manoæ Jud. 13, 19. Da- vidis 2. Sam. 22, 25. Eliæ 1. Reg. 18, 33. exempla singu- laria fuere, & intervenit ibi extraordinarius Spir. S. motus. Tenebantur Ebræi sacrificia, ut & decimas, & primitias mittere ad locum arcæ fœderis, quo ad- monebantur, in solo Messia gratiam quærendam esse, ac remissionem peccatorum, nec grata nisi in ipso esse spiritualia sacrificia, unde etiam templo Hierosol. destructo, Judæi in captivitatem abdu- cti, dona sua Hierosolymam mittebant. Bar. 1, 6.

Ver. 11. AND THE FIRSTFRUITS (תרומת ידכם חרמה is a name that extends quite widely: but here it signifies voluntary offerings, not votive ones: for it follows concerning votive ones. See Levit. 7, 16.)

## 12:15
Verse 15.

KILL AND EAT) Acts 10:13. ϑῦσον και φάγε. וְזָבַחְתָּ Źábaʿ, is to ritually cut the veins of the neck. But this is commanded to be done with tame animals, not with wild ones like the stag and the roe deer: which it was permitted to eat no matter how they were killed.

In the desert, if anyone wished to eat the flesh of animals, he was compelled to slaughter them before the door of the tabernacle, from which the unclean could not eat of them, because the peace offerings, being holy, were suitable only for the clean. Therefore, two things are now permitted to them as they are about to enter the land of Canaan: to eat profane flesh, i.e., not offered in sacrifice, and that it should also be permitted for those who were unclean to eat flesh. In the desert, they ate roe deer, or fawns, and stags with impunity, since they were not sacrificial animals, i.e., fit for sacrificing, but cattle could not be eaten unless they had first been offered in sacrifice. But in this place, He gives the power of eating flesh even if not offered in sacrifice. When they were wandering in the desert, they made peace offerings daily, provided they had the tabernacle of the Lord present, and thus the eating of meat did not fail them; but when they had come into the land of Canaan and were indeed at a long distance from the tabernacle, for the sake of avoiding trouble and expense, it was granted to them that they might eat meat anywhere, even if it had not first been brought to the tabernacle and sanctified through an offering.

Question 11 in Deuteronomy, it is sufficiently established, Lyranus rashly denies them. But Dionysius correctly observed them in this place. Some say that the children of Israel separated tithes from all their goods every year for the work of the Levites, then afterwards they tithed the nine remaining parts again, and this was the second tithe, which is treated here. For they would gather from individual cities in Jerusalem three times a year, namely at the Passover, Pentecost, and the Feast of Tabernacles, carrying with them the second tithes, and the second firstborn, and the second firstfruits, and from there they feasted in the city of divine worship. The Master of the Histories approves this exposition, saying it is a tradition of the Hebrews. Abulensis, Cajetan, Oleaster, Cornelius a Lapide, and Leonhard Marius also agree in this place. Bonfrerius on Leviticus 18:4. Finally, fourthly, there were certain tithes which were separated every third year for the use of the poor, widows, orphans, strangers, and needy proselytes, and likewise the triennial tithe of the Levites, which were called מַעֲשַׂר עָנִי πτωχοδεκάτη, the tithe of the poor, which the poor Levites, travelers, orphans, and widows enjoyed, but not the heads of households or their domestics, Deut. 14:28, ch. 26:12. For it was not permitted for heads of households to eat any tithes within their gates, Deut. 12:17; for the tithes of the first order were destined for the Levites, the second for the priests, the third for feasts in sacred places, and the fourth for the poor.

Latin:

Verf. 15.

OCCIDE ET COMEDE) Act. 10, 13. ϑῦσον και φάγε. וְזָבַחְתָּ Źábaʿ, est rite fecare venas colli. Id autem præcipi- tur ut faciant de manfuetis animalibus, non de feris ut cervo & caprea: quibus quomodocumque interfectis vesci licebat.

In deserto, si cui liberet animalium carnibus vesci, cogebatur ea mactare ante oftium tabernacu- li, unde immundi ex illis non poterant manducare, quia victimæ pacificorum, utpote sanctæ mundis tantum conveniebant. Duo ergo nunc ipsis in- gressuris in terram Canaan permittuntur; vesci carnibus prophanis h. e. non oblatis in sacrificium, & ut carnibus etiam liceret vesci illis, qui immundi erant. In deserto capreis, sive hinnulis, & cervis ve- scebantur impune, cum tantum non essent immola- titia animalia, h. e. ad sacrificandum apta, pecora autem non poterant manducari, nisi prius in Sa- crificium essent oblata. Sed hoc loco dat pote- statem vescendi carnibus etiam non oblatis in sa- crificium. Cum in deserto vagarentur, faciebant quotidie sacrificia pacificorum, siquidem taberna- culum Domini præsens habuerunt, & sic non de- fuit eis esus carnis, at cum in terram Canaan venis- sent & quidem longo intervallo abessent a taber- naculo, vitandæ molestiæ & sumtuum causa, con- cedebatur illis, ut ubivis locorum vescerentur car- nibus, etsi non fuerint prius ad tabernaculum ad- ductæ, & per oblationem sanctificatæ.

quæst. 11. in Deut. satis constet, temere eas negat Lyranus. Recte autem eas observavit Dionysius h. l. Dicunt quidam, quod filii Israel singulis annis de omnibus bonis suis separabant decimas ad opus Le- vitarum, poftea iterum decimabant novem partes re- siduas & hac erat secunda decima, de qua hic agitur. Conveniebant enim e singulis civitatibus in Jerusa- lem ter in anno, videl. in Pascha, Pentecoste, & Sce- nopegia, secum portantes secundas decimas, & secun- da primogenita, & secundas primitias & inde epula- bantur in urbe divini cultus. Hanc expofitionem Magifter in Hiftoriis approbat, dicens, eam effe He- bræorum traditionem. Annuunt etiam Abulensis, Cajetan. Oleaftr. Cornel. a Lap. & Leonh. Marius ad h. l. Bonfrerius in Lev. 18, 4. Quarto denique erant decimæ quædam, quæ tertio quoque anno sepa- rabantur in usum pauperum, viduarum, orphano- rum, advenarum, proselytorum indigentium, item- que Levitarum decima triterica, quæ vocabantur מַעֲשַׂר עָנִי πτωχοδεκάτη decima pauperum, quibus Levitæ pauperes, peregrinantes, orphani, viduæ fruebantur, non autem Patresfamilias, vel dome- stici ejus Deut. 14, 28. c. 26, 12. Nullas enim de- cimas in portis suis comedere licuit Patribusfa- milias Deut. 12, 17. nam primi ordinis decimæ Levitis, secundi Sacerdotibus, tertii epulis in locis sacris, quarti pauperibus destinatæ erant.

OR IF IT BE UNCLEAN, THAT IS BLEMISHED AND WEAK, OR CLEAN) In the law, an animal that has a blemish is not called unclean. Therefore, the Hebrew text is more correct: the clean and the unclean shall eat it. Thus also the Greeks: ὁ ἀκάθαρτος ἐν σοὶ κὰι ὁ καθαρὸς ἐπὶ τὸ ἀυτὸ φάγεται αὐτὸ.

## 12:16
YOU SHALL POUR OUT) And you shall cover, so that it may not be seen.

The fact that the blood of sacrifices is commanded to be poured out like water has something of a shadow and a type for prefiguring the shedding of the blood of Christ, Ps. 22:15: I am poured out like water.

The female, namely. It was permitted to eat these before the Lord; they were to be slaughtered in the manner of peace offerings and consumed in sacred feasts, Deut. 14:23, not the male, for these were to be offered to God in memory of the firstborn of the Egyptians who were killed and the Israelites who were preserved, Exod. 13:12, ch. 14:14, Num. 3:14, Deut. 15:19. And therefore they fell entirely to the priests, Num. 18:17, if they were sacrificial. But if they were not sacrificial on account of some blemish, they were to be redeemed for a price, and the money offered to the priests.

## 12:17
THE FIRSTBORN OF THE HERDS.

## 12:17
AND ALL THAT YOU SHALL VOW AND VOLUNTARILY WISH TO OFFER.

The Vulgate is rightly corrected here, which referred [the text] to the object or the meats, whereas in the source it is referred to the subject or the eater, as was also done by the Chaldean; yet this is to be understood only of those unclean by a lesser legal uncleanness, which was not communicated by contagion, but not of a greater uncleanness, which was communicated. For those unclean from contact with corpses, the flux of seed, a leper, a menstruating woman, etc., were kept away from common social intercourse. But if the whole family was polluted by such greater uncleanness on account of a human corpse, they all ate together in common.

These things are to be eaten in the place which the Lord had chosen, v. 18. If, indeed, someone vows something for a certain use, such as if he vows a certain sum of money or grain to the poor, strangers, or widows, such votive offerings were spent on sacred feasts instituted with the poor, strangers, and widows. But if they vow something to God absolutely without determination to a certain use, Levit. 27:9 seqq., it fell to the Priests, converted into money, unless it were a sacrificial animal, Numbers 18:14; for such a one had to be sacrificed in the manner of peace offerings, and thus the fat and blood were to be burned or poured out to God, but the meats remained for the Priests.

YOU SHALL NOT BE ABLE TO EAT WITHIN YOUR TOWNS THE TITHES OF YOUR GRAIN AND OF YOUR WINE, AND OF YOUR OIL.

There were four kinds of tithes: (1.) Of all animals and fruits growing from the earth, which were simply called דַנְדְתָּ and were to be given to the Levites. 2. Tithes of tithes, מַעֲשַׂר מִן מַעֲשַׂר or מַעֲשַׂר שֵׁנִי, second tithes, δευτεροδεκάτη, which the Levites gave to the Priests from those tithes. 3. Annual tithes, from which sacred feasts were prepared in the place of divine worship, and to these, especially, the Levites were to be invited, along with the household and friends of him who offered them, Deut. 12:12, 17; c. 14:22. These were separated after the Levitical tithes, and either in kind or converted into money, were sent to the place of the tabernacle or the temple, and from them peace offerings and other things necessary for sacred feasts were procured. Concerning which, since from the passage Deut. 14:22, 'Thou shalt tithe by tithing,' and from Josephus, book 4 of Antiquities, last chapter, Jerome in Ez. 45, Theodoret.

Namely, the spontaneous ones, consecrated to God, which are specifically named afterwards, which someone may vow, because it is also permitted to eat those before the Lord which are not offered to God by vow but spontaneously, provided only that those which were owed to the Priests by law were left to them.

Latin:

ET OMNIA QUÆ VOVERIS ET SPON- TE OFFERRE VOLUERIS.

Recte corrigitur hic Vulgata, quæ retulit ad objectum vel carnes, quum in fonte referatur ad subjectum vel manducantem, ut a Chald, etiam fa- ctum, id tamen intelligendum de immundis solum immunditie legali minori, quæ contagione non communicabatur, non autem immunditie majori, quæ communicabatur. Arcebantur enim immun- di ex contactu cadaverum, seminislui, leprosi, men- struatæ &c. a communi convictu. Quod si tota familia ejusmodi immunditie majori ob cadaver hominis erat polluta, omnes simul in commune vescebantur.

Hæc comedenda in loco, quem elegerat Domi- nus v. 18. Si nempe quis voverit aliquid ad certum usum, utpote si certam summam pecuniæ aut fru- menti in pauperes, peregrinos, viduas voverit, ejus- modi votiva in epulas sacras cum pauperibus, pe- regrinis, viduis institutas expendebantur. Si autem absolute Deo quid vovent fine determinatione ad certum usum Levit. 27, 9. seqq. id Sacerdotibus cedebat redactum in pecuniam, nisi esset animal immolatitium Numer. 18, 14. nam tale more pa- cificarum hostiarum immolari debebat, adeoque adeps & sanguis erat Deo adolendus vel libandus, carnes autem remanebant Sacerdotibus.

NON POTERIS COMEDERE IN OPPI- DIS TUIS DECIMAM FRUMENTI ET VI- NI, ET OLEI TUI.

Decimarum quatuor genera erant (1.) omnium ani- malium, & fructuum terræ nascentium, quæ simpliciter vocabantur דַנְדְתָּ & Levitis dandæ erant. 2. De- cimarum decimæ מַעֲשַׂר מִן מַעֲשַׂר vel מַעֲשַׂר שֵׁנִי decimæ secundæ δευτεροδεκάτη, quas Levitæ ex illis decimis dabant Sacerdotibus. 3. Decimæ annuæ, a quibus epulæ sacræ parabantur in loco divini cul- tus & maxime ad eas invitandi erant Levitæ, cum domesticis & amicis ejus, qui eas offerebat, Deut. 12, 12. 17. c. 14, 22. Quæ post decimas Leviticas separabantur, & vel in specie, vel in pecuniam reda- ctæ, ad tabernaculi locum vel templum mitteban- tur, & ex iis victimæ pacificæ, & alia ad epulas sa- cras necessaria comparabantur. De quibus, quum e loco Deut. 14, 22. Decimando decimabis, & e Jo- sepho l. 4. antiqq. c. ult. Hier. in Ez. 45. Theodoret.

Sc. Spontaneas, Deo consecratas, quæ spe- ciatim nominantur postea, quæ quis voverit, quod & illas liceat coram Domino comedere, quæ non ex voto sed sponte Deo offeruntur, dum solum illæ, quæ Sacerdotibus lege debebantur, iis relinque- rentur.

## 12:23
Verse 23.

YOU MUST NOT EAT THE SOUL WITH THE FLESH) That is, the flesh together with the blood. See what was said in Gen. 9:4. For this is a precept not newly given through Moses, but repeated from antiquity, which a comparison of the places makes manifest.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

NON DEBES ANIMAM COMEDERE CUM CARNIBUS) Id est, carnes simul cum sanguine. Vide quæ dicta Gen. 9, 4. Est enim hoc præceptum non noviter per Mosen datum, sed ex antiquo repetitum, quod locorum col- latio manifestum facit.

## 12:31
Verse 31.

FOR ALL THE ABOMINATIONS WHICH THE LORD HATES THEY HAVE DONE TO THEIR GODS) A sacrilege rather than a sacred rite, in Curtius book IV; a bloody religion of sacred rites, and a crime for a remedy, in Justin book XVIII.

Latin:

Vers. 31.

OMNES ENIM ABOMINATIONES QVAS AVER- SATVR DOMINUS FECERUNT DIIS SVIS) Sacri- legium verius quam sacrum, Curtio libro IV. cruentam sacrorum religionem, & scelus pro remedio, Justino libro XVIII.

## 13:1 Argument
CHAP. XIII. The punishment of false prophets.

Latin:

CAP. XIII. Pseudo-Prophetarum pœna.

## 13:6
Ver. 6.

IF THY BROTHER, THE SON OF THY MOTHER, SHALL PERSUADE THEE] Which relationship, as it is more certain, so it binds more tightly. See Gen. 20, 12. He did not say: Thy father: For it was not fitting that any right should be given to a son over a father for any cause whatsoever. Note 'shall persuade'. For this crime, because of its gravity, is punished even if not consummated, which is otherwise in other cases.

Tostatus, Bishop of Avila, is of the same mind, that a son has no right over a father: But others judge more correctly, that the father is not to be spared; and that the reason for the father and the brother or son is the same, as far as this cause is concerned: since the love and honor owed to the divine majesty ought to be preferred to love and honor toward parents. And does not a son have a certain right over a father, when he is viewed as a public person or judge, by divine authority? He who loves father and mother more than me, is not worthy of me, says Christ, Matt. 10, 37. Luke 14, 26.

Ver. the same.

STRANGE GODS, WHICH THOU AND THY FATHERS HAVE NOT KNOWN) Not those of Terah, not the calf, but those taken from the neighborhood. For the novelty itself aggravates the guilt.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

SI TIBI VOLVERIT PERSVADERE FRATER TV- VS, FILIVS MATRIS TVÆ] Quæ cognatio ut certior ita stringit arctius. Vide Gen. 20, 12. Non dixit: Pater tuus: Neque enim ullum jus ex qualicunque causa filio in Patrem dari decuit. Nota voluerit. Hoc enim crimen ob sui gra- vitatem etiam non consummatum punitur, quod in aliis ali- ter se habet.

EAdem etiam mens est Tostato Abulensi Episco- po, quod nullum jus filio in Patrem sit: Sed alii rectius censent, Patri non esse parcendum; ac eandem esse Patris & fratris vel filii, quantum ad hanc causam, rationem: siquidem amor & honor divino numini debitus amori & honori adversus Parentes præferri debeat. Et annon filius in Pa- trem, cum ille ut persona publica aut judex hujus spectatur, jus quoddam habet ex autoritate divina? Qui amat Patrem & matrem plus, quam me, non est me dignus, ait Christus, Matth. 10, 37. Luc. 14, 26.

Vers. eod.

DIIS ALIENIS, QVOS IGNORAS TV ET PA- TRES TVI) Non illis Tharæ, non vitulo, sed de vicinia de- sumtis. Gravat enim culpam ipsa novitas.

## 13:8
Ver. 8.

NEITHER SHALL THINE EYE PITY HIM) So that in this crime alone it was permitted even to use guile to detect the guilty party. Even one who had been acquitted could be accused again and again: nor was the cause of the deed inquired into.

Grotius drew this, like the rest in this place, and many other things, from the traditions of the Hebrews, as can be seen in the annotations of Paul Fagius on the Chaldean paraphrase. But guile is never permitted, and a holy process is required in judgments; what is just must also be executed justly, and through legitimate means, not by guile, which is illicit. Therefore, let Grotius be farewell with his Jewish traditions.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

NEQVE PARCAT EI OCVLVS TVVS) Ita ut in hoc solo crimine etiam dolis uti liceret ad detegendum reum. Etiam absolutus semel iterum accusari poterat: neque causa facti inquirebatur.

Id hausit Grotius, ut reliqua hic loci, & alia mul- ta, ex Ebræorum traditionibus, ut videre est in an- notat. Paul. Fagii ad Chaldaic. paraphras. At doli nunquam liciti sunt, & sanctus requiritur processus in Judiciis; quod justum est, juste etiam, ac per me- dia legitima, non dolis, qui illiciti sunt, exequi fas est. Valeat ergo cum traditionibus Judaicis Grotius.

## 13:9
IMMEDIATELY) Whereas in other crimes the guilty party was accustomed to be kept for a day and a night after the sentence, so that if he could bring forward anything further for himself, he might bring it; false prophets were excepted from this benefit, and he who solicits Israelites to new gods. And not only this, but execution was permitted to anyone, without waiting for a judge: the same was practiced against those who committed sacrilege against the Temple: priests who performed sacred duties while polluted: and against those who cursed God by the name of an idol: likewise against those who lay with an idolatrous woman: but especially against those who denied that the law given through Moses proceeded from God. Moreover, this had to be done before the people, that is, no fewer than ten men, which they themselves call עדה. See Num. 15, 30. and what is said there. The LXX, as with other laws, so with this one, which might have seemed harsher to the Greeks, wished to soften it, and for 'thou shalt immediately kill' they placed ἀναγγέλλων ἀναγγελεῖς, contrary to the words and the custom of the interpreter of words. See. Chald. in this place. This is not to be wondered at in so grave a crime, since even the kinsman of the slain could kill a homicide with impunity outside the cities of refuge. That people, in those places and times, had need of such remedies. See also what will follow now.

Latin:

STATIM) Cum in aliis criminibus soleret reus servari post sententiam diem ac noctem, ut si quid amplius pro se ad- ferre posset, adferret; excepti sunt ab hoc beneficio Pseudo- prophetæ, & is, qui sollicitat Israëlitas ad deos novos. Nec hoc tantum, sed cuilibet permittabatur executio, non expe- ctato judice: idem usurpatum in sacrilegos Templi: sacerdo- tes, qui polluti sacris operam dabant: & in eos, qui Deo per idoli nomen maledicebant: item in eos, qui cum idolatride fœ- mina concumbebant: maxime vero in eos, qui legem per Mo- sem datam a Deo profectam negabant. Fieri autem hoc de- bebat coram populo, id est, hominibus non minus decem, quod ipsi dicunt עדה. Vid. Num. 15, 30. & quæ ibi dicta. LXX. ut alias leges ita hanc, quæ durior Græcis videri pote- rat, emollire voluerunt, & pro statim interficies, posuere αναγ- γέλλων ἀναγγελεῖς, contra verba & morem verborum inter- pretem. Vid. Chald. h. l. Non mirandum hoc in tam gravi cri- mine, cum & homicidam extra receptus loca interficere im- pune potuerit proximus interfecti. Talibus remediis opus habebat ille populus, illis locis atque temporibus. Vide & quæ jam sequentur.

## 13:12
Ver. 12.

IF YOU HEAR IN ONE OF YOUR CITIES) Idolatry is to be punished not only in individuals, but also in the community, but only after it has been warned beforehand.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

SI AVDIERIS IN VNA VRBIVM TVARVM) Non in singulis tantum punienda idololatria, sed & in universita- te, verum præmonita prius.

## 13:13
Ver. 13.

THE CHILDREN OF BELIAL HAVE GONE OUT) All penal laws require a restricted interpretation: especially those which are directed at a community, where it is necessary that many who are not entirely evil be involved in the punishments of the majority. Therefore, all interpreters have seized every opportunity to narrow this law. And first, since יצאו could be taken as an adjective common to either sex, they take it from the masculine alone, which has more cunning and authority to seduce others. Hear what follows.

But the law is general, and speaks of all cities: If you hear IN ONE OF YOUR CITIES, which the Lord your God will give you to dwell in, some saying: Children of Belial have gone out from the midst of you, and have turned away the inhabitants OF THEIR CITY (whichever it may be) &c. ver. 15. you shall immediately strike the inhabitants OF THAT CITY. Moreover, to go out from the midst is a Hebrew phrase, which does not precisely refer to the middle itself or the intermediate parts, opposed to the extreme ends, but to communion and society. To be from the midst of a province is what pertains to that province; he goes out from the midst of a people who belongs to that people, even if he does not dwell in the middle places, but even on the very extreme border of the people or province. Why then do the Jews, and Grotius applauding them, limit it, where the law itself does not limit it? And would not an opportunity for prevarication have been left in the limit, if indeed such a great punishment were not to be feared by them as by others? Others note that to go out is to attack some thing. The Targum renders the words 'gone out from the midst of you': gone out from the doctrine of your Lord and of the wise men who are among you. Not all derive the name Belial from בלי, but some from על 'above', others from יעל 'he profited', others from עול 'yoke', others from עלה 'he ascended', because he profits no one, bears no yoke (of obedience), does not ascend upward, and bears no one above himself; by which name some wish the Devil to be denoted, who in 2 Cor. 6:15 is ἐξαιρέτως so called, and was the first to shake off the yoke, and seduced others to shake it off. But here it seems rather to be an appellative noun, and to denote nefarious men, who are called children of Belial, that is, of impiety, as the Chaldean rendered it, by a Hebrew phrase, as in 2 Sam. 7:7 'children of strength', because they are extremely impious men. Gloss. Talmud. in Gemara: Children of Belial are those who have broken the yoke of heaven, and have cast it off from their neck.

Ver. same.

THEY HAVE TURNED AWAY THE INHABITANTS OF THEIR CITY) They say, therefore, it is not the same if some foreigner has done it.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

EGRESSI SVNT FILII BELIAL) Leges omnes pœna- les restrictam interpretationem desiderant: maxime vero, quæ in universitatem feruntur, ubi necesse est multos non plane malos majorum pœnis involvi. Ideo interpretes omnes occasiones captarunt ad arctandam hanc legem. Ac pri- mum cum יצאו posset sumi tanquam adjectivum commune utrique sexui, sumere de solo masculino, cui plus ad sedu- cendum alios versutiæ & auctoritatis. Audi quæ sequentur.

At lex generalis est, & de omnibus urbibus lo- quitur: Si audieris IN UNA URBIUM TUA- RUM, quas Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi ad habi- tandum, dicentes aliquos: Egressi sunt Filii Belial de medio tui, & everterunt habitatores URBIS SUÆ (cujuscunque) &c. vers. 15. statim percuties habi- tatores URBIS ILLIUS. De medio autem egredi phrasis Ebræa est, quæ non respicit præcise ipsam medietatem aut intermedia, finibus extremis op- posita, sed communionem & societatem. De medio alicujus provinciæ est, quod ad provinciam illam pertinet; de medio alicujus populi exit, qui ad popu- lum illum spectat, etiamsi non habitet in locis me- diis, sed vel in ipsa populi aut provinciæ extrema ora. Cur limitant ergo Judæi, & applaudens ipsis Grotius, ubi lex ipsa non limitat? Et annon ita in limite occasio relicta fuisset prævaricandi, siquidem ipsis tanta pœna metuenda non fuerit, quanta aliis? Alii notant egredi esse rem aliquam aggredi. Tar- gum verba egressi de medio tui reddit: egressi e doctri- na Domini tui & sapientum, qui inter vos. Nomen Be- lial a בלי non deducunt omnes, sed alii ab על super, alii a יעל profuit, alii ab עול jugum, alii a עלה ascendit, quod nemini prosit, jugum non ferat (obe- dientiæ) non ascendat sursum, neminem supra se fe- rat; quo nomine Diabolum nonnulli notari vo- lunt, qui 2. Cor. 6, 15. ἐξαιρέτως sic vocatur, ac primus jugum excussit, aliosque ad excutiendum seduxit. Sed videtur hic potius esse nomen appellativum, hominesque nefarios notare, qui filii Belial, id est, impietatis, ut Chaldæus reddidit, phrasi Ebræa di- cantur, uti 2. Sam. 7, 7. filii roboris, quod homines extreme impii sint. Gloss. Talmud. in Gomara: Fi- lii Belial sunt, qui fregerunt jugum cæli, & abjece- runt illud de collo suo.

Vers. eod.

AVERTERVNT HABITATORES VRBIS SVÆ) Non ergo idem ajunt, si peregrinus aliquis id fecerit.

## 13:14
Ver. 14.

AND THIS ABOMINATION PERPETRATED IN DEED] By the greater part, from which a community is accustomed to be judged.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET ABOMINATIONEM HANC OPERE PERPE- TRATAM] A majori parte, ex qua censeri solet universitas.

## 13:15
Ver. 15.

AND ALL THINGS THAT ARE IN IT] In other crimes (except blasphemy) goods are preserved. In this crime, the goods even of the innocent who remained in such a city perish by fire; but the goods of those who committed the crime, wherever they are found. Thus custom has interpreted the law.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ET OMNIA, QVÆ IN ILLA SVNT] In aliis cri- minibus (excepta blasphemia) bona servantur. In hoc cri- mine bona etiam innocentium, qui in tali urbe manserunt, igne pereunt; bona vero eorum, qui crimen admisere, quo- cunque loco reperta fuerint. Ita mos legem interpretatus est.

## 13:16
Ver. 16.

IN THE MIDST OF ITS STREETS) Into the marketplace.

TO THE LORD THY GOD) In honor of GOD, that you may obey His commandment.

SO THAT THOU MAYEST CONSUME ALL TO THE LORD THY GOD) Profane things without a price: those things which had been consecrated to God, with His price having been paid first. For it was not right that God should lose His due.

IT SHALL NOT BE BUILT AGAIN) Whether gardens could be made in such a place is a matter of legal controversy.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

IN MEDIO PLATEARVM EJVS) In forum.

DOMINO DEO TVO) In DEI honorem, ut præcepto ejus obedias.

ITA VT VNIVERSA CONSVMAS DOMINO DEO TVO) Profana fine pretio: ea quæ Deo sacrata fuerant, pre- tio ejus prius persoluto. Neque enim æquum erat, Deum jus suum amittere.

NON ÆDIFICABITVR AMPLIVS) An horti in tali loco fieri potuerint, juris est controversi.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV.

The rite of the nations concerning the dead is forbidden. The distinction of clean and unclean animals. Tithes are to be paid.

Vers. 1.

YE SHALL NOT CUT YOURSELVES] See what is at Levit. 19, 28. The Greek books here had also φοιβήσεσθε, as appears from Cyril and Theodoret.

NOR SHALL YE MAKE BALDNESS OVER THE DEAD) He omitted here what is in the Hebrew, between your eyes. In Greek ἀναμέσον τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν. Doubtless the neighboring nations let their hair grow in mourning, but cut it in the middle of the forehead. A great part of the Law acts to this end, that the Israelites may be as far as possible from the customs of idolatries, even in indifferent things (ἀδιαφόροις): because those things do not stand still where they begin. This is what follows, because thou art a holy people, separated from other nations for the sake of piety. The mourning of the Hebrews was for seven days, neither to be washed nor anointed.

He speaks not generally of any incision whatsoever, but of an incision upon the dead, as the added words teach: Compare Lev. 19, 28. chap. 12, 6. For the nations were accustomed, on account of the death of their neighbors and kinsmen, to wound and cut themselves in mourning; some used to cut off their hair and offer it to the dead, others would pluck it out. Herodotus lib. 9, concerning the Persians and Egyptians, reports that at the funerals of their relatives they shaved their heads and impressed marks upon their faces. Conf. Alex.

from Alex. lib. 3. Genial. dier. c. 7. He therefore prohibited it, both so that they would not communicate in the rites of the gentiles, so that they would not become accustomed to their idolomania, and so that the people, from whom the Messiah was to arise, would not be confused with other peoples, and also so that they would not make immoderate mourning over the dead, as if he had perished entirely, 1 Thess. 4, 13.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV.

Gentium ritus super mortuo vetitus. Mundo- rum & Immundorum animantium discretio. Decimæ solvendæ.

Vers. 1.

NON VOS INCIDETIS] Vide quæ ad Levit. 19, 28. Græci libri hic habuerunt & φοιβήσεσθε, ut ex Cyrillo & Theodoreto apparet.

NEC FACIETIS CALVITIVM SVPER MORTVO) Omisit hic, quod in Hebræo est, inter oculos vestros. Græce ἀναμέσον τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν. Nimirum gentes vicinæ capillum in luctu promittebant, sed incisum in media fronte. Legis magna pars id agit, ut Israëlitæ quam longissime absint ab idololatriarum moribus, etiam in rebus ἀδιαφόροις: quia non stant ista, ubi incipiunt. Hoc est, quod sequitur, quia popu- lus sanctus tu, separatus ab aliis gentibus pietatis causa. Lu- ctus Hebræorum erat per septem dies nec lavari nec ungi.

LOquitur non generaliter de quacunq́; incisura, sed de incisione super mortuo, uti verba addita docent: Confer Lev. 19, 28. cap. 12, 6. Solebant enim gentes ob proximorum, & cognatorum obi- tum in luctu se vulnerare & incidere, nonnullæ ca- pillos præsecabant & mortuis offerebant, aliæ evel- lebant. Herodotus lib. 9. de Persis, & Ægyptiis re- fert, quod in funeribus propinquorum capita sua ra- serint, & stigmata faciei impresserint. Conf. Alex.

ab Alex. l. 3. Genial. dier. c. 7. Id ergo prohibebat, tum ne in ritibus cum gentilibus communicarent, ne assuescerent idolomaniæ eorum, & ne populus, ex quo Messias erat oriundus, cum aliis populis con- funderetur, tum ne immoderatum facerent luctum super mortuum, ac si penitus periisset, 1. Thess. 4, 13.

## 14:3
Verse 3. DO NOT EAT, WHICH ARE UNCLEAN.

The cause of the interdict was threefold: (1) νομικὴ, or legal, so that the Jewish people might be distinguished from the gentiles until the New Testament, by which that distinction was abolished, Acts 10, 15. Col. 2, 16. Tit. 1, 15. And the middle wall of partition was broken down, Eph. 2, 14. Whence the Papists ineptly prove their traditions concerning the distinction of foods from this constitution. That pertained to the Old Testament. And since the distinction of foods, established by God himself, has now been abolished, let no one judge us in food and drink, Col. 2, 16; much less can consciences be bound or judged by human traditions. (2) Φυσικὴ or natural, since the eating of most of these prohibited animals was little suited to health in those warmer regions especially. Whence by this pact also God wished to testify to his provident care for the health of his own. Dionys. Carth. in Lev. 11. The division of the hoof or the cleft is a sign of a temperate complexion, but rumination is a sign of good digestion. (3) μυσικὴ & spiritual, because by this prohibition of unclean foods they were reminded of the uncleanness of nature after the fall, and of the pursuit of spiritual cleanliness. Whence St. Augustine, contr. Adimant. cap. 15, teaches that those precepts imposed upon a carnal people prophesied the future spiritual discipline of the people, and in lib. contr. Jud.: Whatever they avoid in cattle, we avoid in morals.

Latin:

Vers. 3. NE COMEDATIS, QUÆ IM- MUNDA SUNT.

Causa interdicti triplex fuit (1) νομικὴ, sive lega- lis, ut populus Judaicus a gentibus discerneretur usque ad Novum Testamentum, quo sublatum est illud discrimen Actor. 10, 15. Col. 2, 16. Tit. 1, 15. Et solutus paries intergerinus Eph. 2, 14. Unde inepte ex hac constitutione traditiones suas de discrimi- ne ciborum probant Papistæ. Pertinebat ea ad Vet. Testamentum. Et quum discrimen ciborum a Deo ipso constitutum, nunc sublatum sit, ne quis nos judicet in cibo & potu, Col. 2, 16. multo minus traditionibus humanis conscientiæ ligari aut judi- cari possunt. (2) Φυσικὴ sive naturalis, siquidem ple- rorumque istorum animalium prohibitorum esus, in regionibus maxime illis calidioribus parum sa- nitati conveniens erat. Unde hoc etiam pacto Deus providam de sanitate suorum curam testari voluit. Dionys. Carth. in Lev. 11. Divisio ungulæ sive scissio signum est temperatæ complexionis, rumi- natio autem bonæ digestionis. (3) μυσικὴ & spiritua- lis, quia commonefiebant hac prohibitione im- mundorum ciborum de naturæ immunditie post lapsum, & studio spiritualis munditiei. Unde S. Au- gust. contr. Adimant. cap. 15. præcepta ista carnali populo imposita futuram disciplinam spiritualem po- puli prophetasse, docet, & l. contr. Jud. Quicquid illi vitant in pecoribus, vitamus in moribus.

## 14:5
Verse 5. THE DEER AND THE GOAT.

Dionys. Carth. By the deer, he says, the spiritual man is signified, who with the fervor of his affections hastens to the fatherland, and is armed with horns, with which he resists the injuries of the tempter, especially by discretion and constancy he transcends all earthly things, and when he has grown old in body, he is renewed in soul, and draws the asp from the cavern, while he induces the sinner to confess, whose sin when he has heard, he hastens to the fountain of mercy, and obtains pardon for the penitent. By the buffalo the spiritual fighter is understood, who, animated in the Lord, protests: I will pursue my enemies. By the tragelaphus the progressing man is designated, who is still attacked by passions, and yet like a deer hastens to the higher streams of virtues and wisdom. Others explain it in this way: The ox is an image of labor and industry, Deut. 25, 4. 1 Cor. 9, 9; the lamb of patience, Is. 53, 7; the kid of leadership, Dan. 8, 5. Jer. 50, 8. the deer of desire and ardor, Ps. 42, 1; the goat of joy, Cant. 2, 7. 9. The camelopard designates him who through charity accommodates himself to the morals of all, 1 Cor. 9, 22: I have become all things to all men, that I might save all.

Latin:

Vers. 5. CERVUM ET CAPREAM.

Dionys. Carth. Per Cervum, inquit, homo spiri- tualis signatur, qui fervore affectuum festinat ad pa- triam, cornibusque armatur, quibus læsionibus tenta- toris resistit, præsertim discretione atque constantia transcendit quæque terrena, cumque senuerit corpore, renovatur in anima, extrahitque aspidem de caverna, dum peccatorem ad confitendum inducit, cujus cum peccatum audierit, ad fontem misericordiæ properat, & veniam impetrat pœnitenti. Per bubalum spiri- tualis pugnator accipitur, qui animatus in Domino protestatur: Persequar inimicos meos. Per tragela- phum homo proficiens designatur, qui adhuc passioni- bus impugnatur, & tamen ut cervus ad altiora vir- tutum ac sapientiæ fluenta accelerat. Alii hoc modo declarant: Bos est imago laboris & industriæ, Deut. 25, 4. 1. Cor. 9, 9. agnus patientiæ, Es. 53, 7. hædus principatus, Dan. 8, 5. Jer. 50, 8. cervus desiderii & ardoris, Psal. 42, 1. caprea lætitiæ, Cant. 2, 7. 9. Camelopardus designat eum, qui per caritatem omnium moribus se accommodat 1. Cor. 9, 22. omni- bus omnia factus sum, ut omnes salvos facerem.

## 14:7
Verse 7. THEY DO NOT CLOVEN THE HOOF.

The negative is not present in the Hebrew, nor is it to be established by ellipsis: The sense is: You shall not eat any of those animals which indeed chew the cud, but do not have a hoof split into two parts, as being not cloven-footed, but solid-hoofed, nor the hare, nor the rabbit, as being indeed possessed of split hoofs, but not split into two parts only, but into more parts, to be considered as clean animals, and you ought to eat of their flesh, even though they chew the cud.

Latin:

Vers. 7. UNGULAM NON FINDUNT.

Negativa in Ebræo non habetur, nec ellipsi ejus statuenda: Sensus est: Nullum eorum anima- lium comedetis, quæ ruminant quidem, sed non ha- bent ungulam in duas partes fissam, utpote non fis- sipedem, sed solidipedem, nec leporem, nec cu- niculum, utpote habentes quidem ungulas fissas, sed non in duas tantum, verum plures partes fissas pro mundis animalibus censere, & eorum carni- bus vesci debetis, utut illi cibum ruminent.

## 14:21
Ver. 21. BUT WHATEVER IS DEAD OF ITSELF, YOU SHALL NOT EAT OF IT.

In the Hebrew: You shall not eat any carcass, i.e., any at all, according to the customary Hebraism: yet to the foreigner who was near the gates, i.e., in their cities, it was given to be eaten: not to him who, born of the nations, had been inserted into the people: for this man had the same right as the natives, Num. 9, 14, such as were the Shechemites, the younger Hittite, Achior, etc. Such a foreigner is called by the Hebrews גֵר צֶדֶק a proselyte of righteousness, of truth, or a true one, but that one who had not undertaken the Jewish religion, whom they call גֵר שַׁעַר a proselyte of the gate, who lived in their gate, concerning this see Grotius on ch. 15, 3. To such a foreigner dead carcasses and unclean foods were given to be eaten: to the alien they were sold. The Vulgate neglected this distinction of the foreigner living among the Jews and the alien who lived in the vicinity or was traveling through them, which is observed only in the Hebrew.

Ver. same. YOU SHALL NOT BOIL A KID IN THE MILK OF ITS MOTHER) This parity of reason extended also to lambs and calves.

Latin:

Vers. 21. QUICQUID AUTEM MORTICI- NUM EST, NE VESCAMINI EX EO.

In Ebr. Non comedetis omne cadaver, h. e. ullum, juxta usitatum Ebraismum: peregrino tamen, qui juxta portas, h. e. in civitatibus ipsorum erat, illud dabatur, ut comederetur: non illi, qui ex gentibus oriundus insertus populo erat: hujus enim idem jus erat cum indigenis Num. 9, 14. quales erant Si- chemitæ, Junior Hettæus, Achior &c. Ejusmodi pe- regrinus dicitur Ebræis גֵר צֶדֶק proselytus justitiæ, veritatis, vel verus, sed isti, qui non susceperat reli- gionem Judaicam, quem vocant גֵר שַׁעַר proselytum portæ, qui in porta ipsorum habitabat, de hoc vid. Grot. ad c. 15,3. Tali peregrino dabantur morticina, & immundi cibi ad manducandum: alienigenæ vendebantur. Quod discrimen peregrini inter Ju- dæos habitantes, & alienigenæ, qui in vicinia habi- tabat aut peregrinabatur per ipsos solum in Ebræo observatum neglexit Vulgatus.

Vers. eod. NON COQVES HOEDVM IN LACTE MATRIS SVÆ) Hoc paritas rationis & ad agnos & ad vi- tulos produxit.

## 14:22
Ver. 22. YOU SHALL SEPARATE A TENTH PART OF ALL YOUR FRUITS) This is the second tithe: from which a feast was made in the Temple, just as also from the firstfruits Exod. 23, 19 and 34, 26.

The second tithe is not noted here: for this was owed to the priests. But the annual tithes are indicated. See what we noted on Deut. 12, 17.

Latin:

Vers. 22. DECIMAM PARTEM SEPARABIS DE CVNCTIS FRVCTIBVS TVIS) Hæc est δευτεροδεκάτη: de qua epulum fiebat in Templo, quomodo & de primitiis Exod. 23, 19. & 34, 26.

Non δευτεροδεκάτη hic notatur: hæc enim Sa- cerdotibus debita. Sed decimæ annuæ indigitantur. Vide quæ ad Deut. 12, 17.

## 14:26
Ver. 26. WHETHER FROM THE HERDS OR FROM THE FLOCKS] For there is no joy without meat, say the Talmudists.

Latin:

Vers. 26. SIVE EX ARMENTIS SIVE EX OVIBUS] Nulla enim lætitia sine carnibus, ajunt Thalmudistæ.

## 14:29
Ver. 29. AND THE FOREIGNER AND THE ORPHAN AND THE WIDOW) This tithe in the third year, and the sixth of the annual week, succeeded in the place of the second tithe: and this tithe is called the completion of the tithes, as that in which the love of one's neighbor appeared more openly.

These are again to be corrected from those things which we noted on chapter 12, 17.

Latin:

Vers. 29. ET PEREGRINVS ET PVPILLVS ET VI- DVA) Hæc decima tertio anno, & sexto hebdomadis anna- lis succedebat in locum decimæ secundæ: & vocatur hæc de- cima consummatio decimarum, ut in qua dilectio proximi apertius appareret.

Hæc iterum emendanda ex iis, quæ ad cap. 12, 17. notavimus.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAPTER XV. The Sabbatism of years. The firstborn sacred to the Lord.

Ver. 1. IN THE SEVENTH YEAR] That which is here in the Hebrew מִקֵּץ sounds indeed 'from the end': but to the Hebrews the beginning of the end is also called so. And so מִקֵּץ is sometimes translated by the Greeks as 'beginning'.

That the sense is, in every seventh year, verse 9 teaches. For מִקֵּץ is said to happen at the extreme, or from the end of any year, by a Hebrew phrase, because it happens when that year is approaching. Conf. ch. 14, 28. Jer. 34, 14. For the extreme is twofold, namely, of the beginning and of the end. The year of remission is called from thence שְׁמִטָּה, because the cultivation of the lands rested in it, Exod. 23, 20.
