Wherefore it must be said that these things are expressed thus in the plural, because of the mystery of the Holy Trinity: Namely, our rock, says God the Father concerning the Son, because this rock was constituted for the Church not by His own counsel alone, but by the counsel of the whole Holy Trinity, and our enemies, because they are designated as enemies of the whole Holy Trinity: just as also in v. 36 the Father speaks of the Son, the Lord of the Lord: For the Lord shall judge His people, and v. 44 rejoice, O nations, with His people, namely, of the Messiah. For just as Christ is called the Salvation of God, Is. 49:6, because He was constituted by God as savior and salvation of the world, so nothing prevents Him from also being called the Rock of God, because He was placed by God as the rock of salvation, Is. 28:16.

Latin:

Vers. 31. NON ENIM EST DEUS NOSTER UT DII EORUM. In Ebr. Non enim ut Petra, vel rupes nostra, sic petra ipsorum (hostium) quæ inulta sinit culto- rum suorum peccata, quæque impotens est, ut se suosque ulciscatur, & alicui benefaciat, vel malefa- ciat, cujus rei testes sunt etiam inimici nostri, qui po- tentiam, severitatem, & justitiam Dei, præ suis ido- lis, experti sunt, ut Ægyptii, Amalecitæ, Amorrhæi & cæteræ gentes, ut verba Mosis sint, vel Ecclesiæ, in parenthesi legenda : quemadmodum Interpp. nonnullis visum fuit, siquidem antecedentia, & con- sequentia Dei sint. Apostrophe Mosis, inquit Ju- nius, quia causam deditionis in servitutem explicat, quod Deus opem ferat suis, adversetur desertoribus, quorum neutrum fictitiis diis adscribi debet. Inclu- dit ea etiam parenthesi Piscator. Personæ mutatio- nem hic esse, quum non Deus illa, sed populus loquatur, observat Castellio. Ecclesiæ hæc esse verba, pari- ter Vatabl. in notis ad h. l. innuit, aut ipsius Mo- sis. Coccejus objicit: quod uno veluti halitu illa dican- tur: Rupes ipsorum vendiderat ipsos: quia non ut rupes nostra rupes ipsorum est. Si ergo rupes illo- rum esset rupes Judæorum, esset ipse Jehovah rupes Ecclesiæ, & quomodo tunc rupes eorum negaretur esse, ut rupes Ecclesiæ? Resp. in priori, rupes ipso- rum vendidit eos, Jehovam rupem Israelis intelligi, dubium nullum esse potest, ob infallibilem ἐξήγη- σιν à S. S. subjunctam. At in his verbis, quæ paren- thesi inclusa dicuntur, & Mosi, vel Ecclesiæ vindi- cantur, non ut rupes nostra rupes ipsorum est, oppo- sitio inter rupem Ecclesiæ instituitur, & rupem ipso- rum: ubi per hos ipsos alii inimicos intelligunt, quo- rum & antea mentio facta erat, & verbis immedia- te subjunctis denuo fit mentio: alii Israelitas in po- testatem hostium venditos, quod rupem non- Deum sibi fecerint, quum alienis diis servierunt, verum Deum reprobarunt, vel ut Osiander, quod cultu à Deo non præscripto idololatriam commi- serint, & ita non coluerint verum Deum, qui suos cultores non confundi sinit, ut mirum non sit eos succumbere. Sed simplicior est prior sensus: quia ut rupes Ecclesiæ non est gentium, vel hostium Ec- clesiæ rupes, ipsorummet hostium proprio testi- monio. Quo tendit B. Lutheri commentarius: Quia Petra eorum non est sicut nostra Petra, cujus rei testes sunt ipsi hostes nostri. Hoc intellige dici, quod cæteri dii, & deorum cultores confessi fuerint, Deum Israel esse talem, quo non tradente, ipsi nunquam sta- re potuerunt, ut Bileam regi Moab ideo consulit, ut populum ad peccatum induceret, & sic vinceret. Hic ergo Bileam unus est testium, de quibus Mose hic dicit, qui magnifica de Deo dixit. Testes & Æ- gyptii, qui dixerunt Exod. 14. Fugiamus Israelem, Dominus enim pugnat pro eis. Testes & Philistini, 1. Reg. 5. qui timebant ab arca Dei. Nulli ergo dii sic suis populis adfuerunt, sic potentiam ostende- runt &c. Non est enim alia natio tam grandis, ut su- pra cap. 3. Illud: Et inimici nostri sunt judices, ita interpretatur Sebast. Münsterus: licet inimici nostri jam sint judices nostri, id tamen non habent à Diis suis, sed à Deo nostro, qui nos tradidit in manus eorum. Cæterum quum Oratio continua ipsius DEI sit, nec conveniat, mutationem personæ loquentis introducere, ubi nullum in textu est vestigium, uti hoc loco non modo in antecedentibus v. 26. & 27. Deus loquitur, sed etiam sine ullo alterius personæ indicio continuatur divina oratio, & in consequentibus v. 34. 35. extra controversiam est, Deum ipsummet loqui: nonne hæc condita sunt apud me, & signata in thesauris meis? etsi verba etiam illa Deo tribuenda erunt, Petra eorum non est sicut Petra nostra, cujus rei testes sunt ipsi hostes nostri. Non enim integrum est parentheses figere, ac fingere, ubi textus nullum suggerit indicium. Quapropter dicendum, hæc ita πληθυντικῶς efferri, ob mysterium S. S. Trinitatis: Nimirum rupes nostra, inquit Deus Pater de Filio, quia non suo solius, sed totius S. S. Trinitatis consilio hæc rupes constituta est Ecclesiæ, & hostes nostri, quia totius S. S. Trinitatis hostes designantur: quemadmodum etiam v. 36. de Filio loquitur Pater, Dominus de Domino: Judicabit enim Dominus populum suum, & v. 44. exultate gentes, cum populo ejus, Messiæ scil. ut enim Christus dicitur Salus Dei, Es. 49, 6. quia constitutus est à Deo salvator, & salus orbis, ita nihil obstat, quo minus etiam Petra Dei dicatur, quia à Deo in Petram salutis positus est, Esa. 28. v. 16.

## 32:32
Vers. 32. FOR THEIR VINE IS OF THE VINE OF SODOM, AND OF THE SUBURBS OF GOMORRAH.

In Hebrews. Concerning the field of Gomorrah. He returns to the Jews, rendering the reason why, when the rock of the Jews is far different from the gods of the Gentiles, even by the testimony of the hostile nations themselves, they are nonetheless put to flight by enemies, and sold, and why Jehovah sold them, because indeed their vine has become of the vine of the Sodomites, that is, most wicked, having imitated the Sodomites and Gomorrahites, as if they had been born from them, and not from the holy Fathers. Whence also THEIR GRAPE IS A GRAPE OF GALL, that is to say, the grapes of such a vine, i. e., the fruits and works of the Jews are gall-like, most bitter, and most wicked. Hence also THE GALL OF DRAGONS AND THE INCURABLE VENOM OF ASPES. That is to say, the wine, i. e., the doctrine expressed and flowing from those so impious, which they themselves offer to others, so that they may transfuse their own crimes into them, is poisoned and lethal, like the gall of dragons, and cruel and incurable venom, which destroys and kills all who drink it, as Cornelius has it. Cons. Is. 1, 10. Ez. 16, 3. For when they ought to bring forth good fruits from faith, good works, piety, love, chastity, etc., they bring forth from Epicureanism and contempt of the Gospel the worst fruits, lusts, avarice, neglect of the poor, and they are covered with huge crimes and scandals; furthermore, their grape is a grape of gall, and their clusters are most bitter to them; those degenerate and cursed vines bring forth grapes full of gall and bitterness. The gall of dragons, i. e., their wine, which is born from them as if from vines, is a deadly poison, and they produce the incurable or lethal venom of asps in place of wine, i. e., they pursue Christ, his Gospel, and all who have given their name to the Gospel of Christ with most bitter and most virulent hatred, so that if they could and dared to take them all out of the way, they would spare no one, as Osiander rightly says in this place. Coccejus understands their life as their Republic. Ecclesiastical, erected by the Romans, after they had vindicated the Church from the persecution of idolaters, and he snatched away all these things to the times of the Roman Anti-Christ, and those things which preceded or followed it, by a truly wonderful gloss. For he wishes in §. 1283. v. 27. with words which he renders thus: LEST THEIR ENEMIES ALIENATE, that Moses prophesied the stubbornness of the Romans (the Gentiles) in their superstitions and idolatry, so that they did not acknowledge that those things which were perpetrated by the Romans themselves, the enemies and attackers of the Jews, were done by God and Christ, but on the contrary attributed all that glory to their own idols. (2.) By the words OUR HAND IS EXALTED, he predicted the exaltation of others from the Gentiles, so that they might glory that they were victors, that power and empire had been granted to them, or even that they had attained the knowledge of God and entered His kingdom by their own works, by their own strength, and by the liberty of their own will. (3.) By the words: AND JEHOVAH HAS NOT WROUGHT ALL THIS, he indicated that there would again be others who, while they do not deny that God and Christ did these things, nevertheless think that Christ is not Jehovah, and likewise that a mere man was assumed by Jehovah and His Christ to plant that kingdom, which man is the Anti-Christ. But how can these things be extracted from those words? Which are therefore not assertive or prophetic, but hypothetical: that the enemies of the Jews would have gloried thus, if the memory of them had been utterly extinguished by them, which did not happen, nor was it willed to happen, lest they should glory.

Furthermore, Cocceius draws that passage about flight in v. 30 to the flight of the idolaters, when Maxentius and Licinius, the protectors of idols, were defeated by Constantine the Great and stripped of their empire, and almost the whole world conceded to the Christian name. From those words, our enemies are judges, he elicits the peace that then followed in the Church, where the Church had to be nourished by the Gentiles and their kings; but from the words: Their vine is from the vine of Sodom, he extracts in §. 1343 the Roman Anti-Christ, with his assembly, in this way: Because that vine, or the stem or root of the branches, which is not from heaven but from the world and Sodom, from carnal men, emulates Christ and professes to act in His place, but in reality is against Christ, who alone is the vine, it is clear that the words of Moses say this, that an Anti-Christ will come who calls himself the vicar of Christ, as if he were another vine, and by that name demands the dependence of the faithful upon himself as branches, etc. But these things are twisted, not clear and lucid; where is this vine said to emulate Christ? Where is it said to be against Christ? Where is it said to arise in the time of the kingdom of Christ? Or to arise among the Gentiles, after the fall of the Jewish Republic as a peculiar Ecclesiastical Republic? Moses deals with the Jews, he predicts their punishment, therefore he indicates the cause of their destruction by this figurative expression, that their vine is not indeed from the vine of Sodom, but is similar to the vine of Sodom, or rather surpasses it. Whence rightly the blessed Luther: the vine of Sodom, etc., that is, for the sweet fruit of piety they bring forth the most bitter and worst fruits of idolatry, worthy to perish just as Sodom and Gomorrah; their wine is the poison of dragons, i.e., their doctrine is so harmful and poisonous that it destroys many irretrievably. THEIR VINE IS FROM THE VINE OF SODOM, render Junius and Tremellius. i.e., it produces worse fruit; but what the evil fruits are that grow in the Asphaltite Lake, Josephus, Tacitus, and others express. Thus he metaphorically describes a life badly led. Cf. Jer. 2:21, Is. 5:2. Cornelius à Lapide and Lorinus and others commonly explain it as referring to the Jews as well. Therefore, Vatablus, Castellio, and Quiros interpret it strangely regarding the Gentiles and their fruits.

Latin:

Vers. 32. DE VINEA ENIM SODOMORUM VINEA EORUM, ET DE SUBURBANIS GOMORRHÆ.

In Ebr. De agro Gomorrhæ. Redit ad Judæos, causam reddens, cur, quum testibus ipsis gentibus inimicis eorum longe alia sit Judæorum petra, quam dii gentilium, nihilo secius fugandi ipsi ab hostibus sint, & vendendi, & cur Jehovah ipsos vendiderit, quia nempe vinea eorum de vinea Sodomorum, h. e. pessima facta est, imitata Sodomitas & Gomorrhæos, ac si ab eis, non à sanctis Patribus prognati fuissent. Unde & UVA EORUM UVA FELLIS, q. d. Uvæ talis vineæ, i. e. fructus & opera Judæorum sunt fellea, amarissima, & pessima. Hinc & FEL DRACONUM ET VENENUM ASPIDUM INSANABILE. q. d. Vinum, i. e. doctrina ab iis tam impiis expressa & manans, quam ipsi aliis propinant, ut in eos sua scelera transfundant, est venenata, & lethifera, velut fel draconum, & venenum crudele, ac insanabile, quod omnes bibentes perdit & occidit, ut habet Corn. Cons. Es. 1, 10. Ez. 16, 3. Nam quum deberent ex fide proferre bonos fructus, bona opera, pietatem, dilectionem, castitatem &c. proferunt ex Epicureismo & contemtu Evangelii pessimos fructus, libidines, avaritiam, neglectum pauperum, suntque operti ingentibus sceleribus & flagitiis, præterea uva eorum uva fellis, & botri amarissimi sunt eis, uvas plenas felle & amaritudine proferunt istæ degeneres, & maledictæ vites. Fel Draconum, i. e. exitiale venenum est vinum eorum, quod ab ipsis tanquam vitibus enascitur, & venenum aspidum insanabile, seu lethale producunt loco vini, i. e. acerbissimo & virulentissimo odio prosequuntur Christum, ejus Evangelium, & omnes qui Evangelio Christi nomen dedere, ita ut si possent & auderent eos omnes è medio tollere, nulli parcerent, ut recte h. l. Osiander. Coccejus per vitam ipsorum intelligit ipsorum Rempubl. Ecclesiasticam erectam à Romanis, postquam Ecclesiam à persequutione idololatrarum vindicassent, & hæc omnia ad tempora Anti-Christi Romani, & quæ ea præcessere, aut sequuta sunt, glossa sane mirabili, abripuit. Vult enim §. 1283. v. 27. verbis, quæ ita reddit: NE ALIENENT HOSTES IPSORUM, Mosen prophe- tasse Romanorum (gentilium) pertinaciam in suis su- perstitionibus & idololatria, ut non agnoscerent à Deo, & Christo facta esse illa, quæ per ipsos Roma- nos hostes & oppugnatores Judæorum erant per- petrata, sed contra suis idolis omnem istam gloriam affererent. (2.) Per verba MANUS NOSTRA ELATA EST, aliorum è gentibus elationem præ- dixisse, ut se victores, sibi potestatem & imperium concessum esse gloriarentur, aut etiam sè suis operibus iustitiam, suis viribus & libertate arbitrii sui conse- cutos esse cognitionem Dei, & intrasse regnum ipsius. (3.) Per verba: ET NON JEHOVAH OPE- RATUS EST OMNE HOC, indicasse, rursus alios fore, qui cum non negent, Deum & Christum hæc fecisse, tamen Christum esse non Jehovam, item, qui hominem merum à Jehovah, & Christo ejus assum- tum esse ad regnum illud plantandum, existiment, qui homo sit Anti-Christus. Sed quomodo hæc ex istis verbis exsculpi queant? Quæ propterea non asser- tiva, aut prophetica sunt, sed hypothetica: ita glo- riaturos fuisse hostes Judæorum, si horum memo- ria penitus extincta per ipsos fuisset, quod factum non est, nec fieri voluit, ne illi glorientur.

Porro illa de fuga v. 30. trahit Coccejus ad fu- gam idololatrarum, cum à Constant. M. Maxentius & Licinius idolorum tutatores victi & imperio exuti sunt, totusq; propemodum orbis in Christianum nomen concessit. E verbis illis, inimici nostri judices, pacem elicit tum sequutam in Ecclesia, ubi Ecclesia nutri- ri debuit à gentibus & regibus illorum, è verbis autem: Ex vite Sodomæ est vitis eorum, exsculpit §. 1343. Romanum Anti-Christum, cum suo cœtu, hoc modo: Quia vitis ea sive stipes radixve palmi- tum, quæ non est ex cælo, sed ex mundo & Sodoma, ex hominibus carnalibus æmulatur Christum, & ejus vi- cem se obire profitetur, at revera est contra Christum, qui solus est vitis, claret verba Mosis hoc dicere, ven- turum Anti-Christum, qui se vicarium Christi dicat, tanquam vitem alteram, & eo nomine dependentiam fidelium à sese exigat ut palmitum &c. Sed hæc con- torta sunt, non clara & luculenta; ubi vitis hæc di- citur æmulari Christum? ubi esse contra Christum? ubi tempore regni Christi oritura dicitur? aut in gen- tibus extitura, post occasum Reipubl. Judæorum ceu Resp. peculiaris Ecclesiastica? De Judæis agit Moses, eorum pœnam prædicit, ideo causam excidii eo- rum hac loquutione figurata indicat, quod vitis ipsorum non quidem ex vite Sodomæ, sed viti So- domæ similis sit, vel potius eam superet. Unde re- cte B. Luther. vitis Sodomæ &c. id est, pro fructu suavi pietatis fructificant amarissimos & pessimos fructus idololatriæ digni, qui sic pereant sicut So- domą & Gomorrha, vinum eorum fel draconum, h. e. doctrina eorum sic noxia & venenata est, ut plu- rimos irrecuperabiliter perdat. PRÆ VITE SODOMÆ est vitis ipsorum, reddunt Junius & Tremell. h. e. fructum deteriorem edit, quam sint autem mali fructus in lacu Asphaltite nascentes, ex- primunt Josephus, Tacitus, alii. Sic metaphorice vi- tam male actam describit. Conf. Jer. 2, 21. Es. 5, 2. De Judæis etiam explicat Cornel. à Lapid. & Lorin. & alii communiter. Aliene itaque Vatablus, Castellio, & Quiros de gentilibus, eorumque fructibus inter- pretantur.

## 32:34
Verse 34. ARE NOT THESE THINGS LAID UP? In the Hebrew: Are not these things hidden with me and sealed (or signed) in my treasures: i.e., in my secrets? As if he were saying: this, which is now a mystery concerning the hardening of the Jews (how they will persecute the Gospel, and that for this reason they are to be cast off), is something that is now hidden from the Jews: which no one will believe can happen, until in its own time the event responds to the prophecy, and the Jews persecute the Christian religion with Vatinian hatred, as Osiander rightly says. Thus also the blessed Luther: I hold all these impious things known and secret, although outwardly I am compelled to do good to those impious ones for the sake of my name, but they themselves do not see what has been defined by me concerning them. And Münster, the more freely they bring forth these bitter fruits, the more they think I am ignorant of these things, or do not notice them, when nevertheless there is nothing of these that is not hidden in my treasury, I who see not only the past and present with me, but also what things are to be, as if they were already done. Cocceius, claiming these words for the Son, provides this paraphrase: I, as sent by God with authority, have received this diploma from Him, which is also sealed in my archives, to be brought forth and put into execution in its own time. The former explanation is simpler; and the fact that God the Father speaks the things which he testifies concerning the Son in v. 36 teaches this.

Latin:

Vers. 34. NONNE HÆC CONDITA? In Ebræo: Nonne hæc abscondita sunt apud me & signata (seu obsignata) in thesauris: i. e. arcanis meis? quasi diceret: hoc, quod nunc de indura- tione Judæorum (quomodo persequuturi sint Ev- angelion, quodque ideo abjiciendi) mysterium est adhuc, quod Judæis nunc est absconditum: quod nemo fieri posse credet, donec suo tempore eventus vaticinio respondeat, & Judæi Vatiniano odio Christianam religionem insectentur, ut recte Osiander. Sic etiam B. Luth. Hæc impia omnia novi & secreta teneo, licet foris cogar benefacere impiis illis propter nomen meum, ipsi autem non vident, quid apud me super eos definitum sit. Et Münsterus, eo licentius hos amaros proferunt fructus, quo me putant hæc igno- rare, aut non advertere, cum tamen nihil horum sit, quod non sit reconditum in thesauro meo, qui nedum apud me præterita & præsentia, verum & quæ futu- ra sunt, tanquam jam facta essent, conspicio. Coc- cejus Filio hæc verba vendicans, hanc tradit para- phrasin: Ego ut missus à Deo cum auctoritate hoc di- ploma ab ipso accepi, quod & in scriniis meis obsigna- tum, suo tempore depromendum & executioni man- dandum. Simplicior est prior explicatio; & Deum Patrem loqui ea, quæ de Filio v. 36. testatur, docent.

## 32:35
Verse 35. VENGEANCE IS MINE. Some explain שׁלם nominally, others verbally, so that the sense is: vengeance is mine, and it will repay them according to their works, as Münster notes. Here again Osiander's paraphrase pleases: It is my office to punish, and this sin of contumely against the Messiah, and other crimes and wickedness, both of this people and of others, and I will repay them for their impiety, in a time opportune for me: but I will repay them in such a way that their foot may slip, i.e., that they may stumble (more and more) against Christ the cornerstone, by their own fault and infidelity, and that in other matters and endeavors of theirs, they may have no success: but may fall shamefully everywhere. Nor is there any reason why they should promise themselves long-lasting impunity: for the day of perdition, or of calamity, is near, (the word 'their' is missing), and the times hasten to be present: i.e., much sooner than they think they will be overwhelmed by the predicted evils: For indeed, after almost forty years, after they began to persecute and despise the Gospel of Christ, when they feared no danger, the devastation of Jerusalem and the whole nation, and perpetual exile, was at hand. We omit Cocceius, who fixes the sudden calamity of the Anti-Christ and the time of vengeance here, both from the state of the same, in which he will stand and conquer, and when his foot will waver (which he ascribes to the time of the reformation), and from the state of the Church after the flight of the idolatrous Gentiles; for he thinks it is insinuated in §. 1382 (1.) a long-lasting struggle with the kingdom of the Anti-Christ until the shedding of blood, verses 32, 33, 37, 43. (2.) separation from the communion of the Anti-Christ, v. 36. (3.) The ingratitude and depravity of the church thus separated, v. 36. (4.) The chastisement of the church, v. 36. (5.) help, v. 39. which hardly any lynx-eyed person could have found in the Mosaic words.

Latin:

Vers. 35. MEA EST ULTIO. Quidam exponunt שׁלם nominaliter, alii verbaliter, ut sit sensus: mea est ultio, & illa reddet eis juxta opera eorum, notante Münstero. Placet hic iterum Osiandri paraphrasis: Mei officii est punire, & hoc peccatum contumeliæ in Messiam, & alia, cum hujus populi, tum aliorum etiam scelera, & impro- bitatem, & ego retribuam eis impietatem eorum, in tempore mihi opportuno: sic autem retribuam, ut la- batur pes eorum, i. e. ut impingant (magis ac magis) in Christum angularem lapidem, sua ipsorum culpa & infidelitate, utque in aliis etiam rebus & conatibus suis, nullum habeant successum: sed turpiter ubique corruant. Nec est, quod diuturnam sibi impunitatem promittant: juxta enim seu prope est dies perditio- nis, seu calamitatis, deest, eorum, & adesse festi- nant tempora: i. e. citius multo ipsorum opinione ob- ruentur prædictis malis: Etenim post quadraginta fere annos, postquam Evangelion Christi persequi & contemnere ceperunt, cum nullum periculum metuerent, aderat Hierosolymorum, & totius gen- tis vastatio, & exilium perpetuum. Mittimus Coc- cejum, qui calamitatem Anti-Christi repentinam & vindictæ tempus hic figit, tum ex statu ejusdem, quo stabit & vincet, & cum vacillabit pes ejus, (quod tempori reformationis adscribit) tum ex statu Ec- clesiæ post fugam idololatrarum gentilium; nam insinuatum §. 1382. putat (1.) certamen cum regno An- ti-Christi diuturnum usque ad effusionem sanguinis vers. 32. 33. 37. 43. (2.) separationem à communione Anti-Christi v. 36. (3.) Ecclesiæ sic separatæ ingratitu- dinem & depravationem v. 36. (4.) Ecclesiæ castigatio- nem v. 36. (5.) auxilium, v. 39. quæ in verbis Mosai- cis vix lynceus aliquis invenerit.

## 32:36
Vers. 36. THE LORD SHALL JUDGE HIS PEOPLE.

The causal particle FOR is omitted by the Vulgate. He shall judge his people. He will not be able to connive any longer at the sins of his once people, yet (since he still has some elect among them, he will not destroy it entirely, but) he will have mercy on his servants. Münster correctly expressed this sense: after he has chastised it with just scourges, he will repent, and he will have mercy on them, especially when he sees all power taken away from them, and them destitute of all help, and as it were reduced to nothing. Vatablus understands it as the vengeance to be taken by the Lord of the people upon their enemies. But this sense is foreign: since the Lord threatens punishment to the people on account of the guilt which he had described at length; although he simultaneously promises grace to the faithful in that most grievous judgment of the people. But if, however, anyone prefers to take these things as said by way of explanation, the Lord shall judge his people, and he will have mercy on his servants, because God also judges his people when he pleads their cause. Cf. Gen. 30. v. 6. Psalm 25. v. 1. Psalm 54. & 72. etc. so that the vav may bear not a copulative, but an adversative notion, yet the preceding things are not to be taken with Vatablus of the punishment of enemies, but of the destruction of the Israelites, as the continuity and scope of the canticle require. Moreover, the Lord speaks of the Lord, the Father of the Son; the Lord will judge, says the Lord, his people, just as often elsewhere the distinction of the divine persons is wont to be designated. For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son, John 5:22.

Verse same. HE SHALL SEE THAT THE HAND HAS BEEN WEAKENED) Literally: The hand has departed. For it is a Syriac word which appears in Dan. 2:17, 6:18, Ezra 4:23, 5:8, 13. The sense is, when he shall see that their strength has been taken away.

SHUT UP) That is, captives.

THE REMAINING) Those who have escaped captivity.

Coccejus thus: He will be affected with repentance over his servants, when he shall see that the hand has departed, and he will be shut up and left to us. He places here the chastisement of the Church, so that the hand may depart, and the strength of the Church be small, Apoc. 3:8, i.e., so that the strength of the Church may be exhausted, and it all but perishes, agitated and left behind. But because the Lord has mercy on his servants, this is not the chastisement of the Church, but rather some relief. Osiander's paraphrase is correct: For he shall see that their hand (power) has been weakened (more correctly, taken away); he shall consider that it is all over with the empire and strength of this people, and those shut up also have failed: and the remaining have been consumed, i.e., that not only those who were eminent in authority, counsel, nobility, wealth, and power have been destroyed. But that there has been cruelty even against the captives (otherwise neglected and abject men), so that almost no remnants of so great a people (if you look at its former multitude and happiness) survive. Thus also Cornelius à Lapide. The Seventy translate παραλελυμένους καὶ ἐκλελυμένους. Seeing therefore this extreme misery, he will have mercy on them. For here the tribulation of the Jews is described, says Abulensis, after the manner of a city which is besieged by enemies, in which first the defenders of the walls are wearied and die: then, the city being captured, those who shut themselves up in strong forts and impregnable towers are killed by hunger and thirst, and at length the remaining unwarlike crowd is captured and consumed. Cf. 2 Kings 14:26. Rabanus wishes the final conversion of the Jews after the fullness of the Gentiles to be denoted here. Thomas Jorgius in Ps. 17, apud Lorin. in h. l., adapts it to Christ, who, having pursued the malignant spirits, caused those shut up to fail and the remaining to be consumed, i.e., both those shut up in hell and those left in this air. Osiander in Isa. 59 applies it to the incarnation of Christ. He saw that there was no one who could deliver the human race from death, sin, and Satan. But these things are foreign.

Latin:

Vers. 36. JUDICABIT DOMINUS POPU- LUM SUUM.

Omissa à Vulgat. particula causalis NAM. Ju- dicabit populum suum. Non poterit diutius ad po- puli olim sui peccata connivere, attamen (quum in eo adhuc habeat aliquos electos, non delebit eum totum, sed) servorum suorum miserebitur. Quem sensum recte expressit Münsterus: postquam flagellis justis eum castigaverit, pœnitebit eum, & miserebitur eorum, præsertim cum viderit ab eis sublatam omnem potentiam, atq; eos omni destitutos auxilio, & veluti in nihilum redactos. Vatablus ultionem populi Do- mini de inimicis sumendam intelligit. Sed hic sen- sus alienus est: quum pœnam populo minetur Do- minus ob culpam, quam prolixe descripserat; Et- si gratiam simul fidelibus in isto judicio populi gra- visssimo polliceatur. Quod si tamen hæc κατ' επε- ξήγησιν dicta quis accipere malit, judicabit popu- lum suum Dominus, & servorum suorum miserebitur, quia judicat Deus etiam populum, cum causam ejusdem agit. Conf. Genes. 30. v. 6. Psalm. 25. v. 1. Psalm. 54. & 72. &c. ut vav non copulativæ, sed ad- versativæ notionem sustineat, non tamen cum Va- rablo antecedentia de pœna hostium, sed de perditio- ne Israelitarum, ut requirit συνέχεια, & scopus can- tici, accipienda. Cæterum loquitur Dominus de Domino, Pater de Filio, judicabit Dominus, inquit Dominus, populum suum, quemadmodum sæpe alias ita discrimen personarum divinarum designa- ri solet. Pater enim neminem judicat, sed dedit Filio omne judicium Joh. 5, 22.

Vers. eod. VIDEBIT QVOD INFIRMATA SIT MANUS) Ad verbum: Abierit manus. Est enim vox Sy- riaca quæ apparet Dan. 2, 17. 6, 18. Esdræ 4, 23. 5, 8. 13. Sensus est, cum videbit, vires illis ademptas esse.

CLAUSI) Id est, captivi.

RESIDUI) Qui captivitatem evaserint.

Coccejus ita; Super servis suis pœnitudine afficie- tur, quum videbit, quod abierit manus, & nobis erit inclusus & relic̄tus. Ponit hic Ecclesiæ castigationem, ut manus abeat, & parva sit vis Ecclesiæ Apoc. 3, 8. i. e. ut exhauriantur vires Ecclesiæ, & tantum non pereat concitata & relicta. Sed quia miseretur Dominus servorum, non hæc est castigatio Ecclesiæ, sed ali- qua opitulatio potius. Recte se habet Osiandri pa- raphrasis: Videbit enim quod infirmata (rectius ab- lata) sit manus (potentia) eorum; considerabit, quod actum sit de hujus populi imperio & viribus, & clausi quoque defecerunt: residuiq; consumpti sunt, i. e. quod non modo, qui autoritate, consilio, no- bilitate, divitiis, potentia eminebant, deleti sint. Sed quod in captivos etiam (alias neglectos & ab- jectos homines) sævitum sit, ut fere nullæ reliquiæ de tanto populo (si priorem ejus multitudinem, & felicitatem spectes) supersint. Sic etiam Cornelius à Lapide. Septuaginta vertunt παραλελυμένυς κὰι έκ- λελυτότας. Videns ergo extremam hanc miseri- am, eorum miserebitur. Describitur enim hic tri- bulatio Judæorum, inquit Abulens. ad modum civi- tatis, quæ ab hostibus obsidetur, in qua primo de- fendentes muros lassantur, & moriuntur: Deinde capta civitate illi, qui in fortibus castris & turribus inexpugnabilibus se concludunt, fame & siti ene- cantur, ac tandem imbelle vulgus reliquum capi- tur & consumitur. Conf. 2. Reg. 14, 26. Rabanus conversionem ultimam Judæorum post plenitudinem gentium hic denotari vult. Thomas Jorgius in Ps. 17. apud Lorin. in h. l. aptat ad Christum, qui spiritus malignos persequutus effecerit, ut clausi deficerent, residui consumerentur, h. e. tum inferno clausi, tum in hoc aere relicti. Osiander in Esa. 59. applicat ad incarnationem Christi. Vidit, quod non esset, qui hu- manum genus liberare posset à morte, peccato, Satana. Sed hæc aliena sunt.

## 32:37
Verse 37. AND HE SHALL SAY, WHERE ARE THEIR GODS?

Who is to say it? And of whom? Coccejus wishes it to be said by the enemies and the common people concerning the Church: that they will judge beforehand, when the strength of the Church is so exhausted, that its cause was evil, that it was heretical, that it had fled to alien gods, that its sufferings were not sacrifices pleasing to God, that in truth the vicar of God, the Roman Pontiff, must be acknowledged, and that the vine of Sodom is the planting of God. He notes that this triumph of the enemies and this prejudice of men in v. 37, 38 is marked under the harlot's song in Isa. 23:15, 16, and that its beginning is compared to the year 70 after the spiritual Tyre was forgotten, i.e., from the peace of the Church first granted in the year of Christ 1552, and thus to the year of Christ 1622. But this sense is brought into these prophecies; it cannot be brought out of them. For neither Moses in this canticle, nor Isaiah in the cited passage, prophesies about the times of the Anti-Christ, or the peace given to the reformation, and the chastisement following the same. But Moses sings of the judgments against the Jewish people. Isaiah of the ancient merchant Tyre.

Hugo, Rupertus, Lyranus, Vatablus, Abulensis, and Valentia ascribe these words of mockery to the enemies of the Jewish people, when they saw them conquered by them and reduced to extreme desolation. And this is also the explanation of R. Aben-Esdra, as if the enemy speaks such things to the captive Jews out of pride and contempt: where is your God? let him arise and bring you help. Which insult God, not bearing, answers: you shall see now that I am the true God, when I shall bring upon you vengeance, from which no one will be able to save you. Which opinion, however, Quiros, a Pontifical interpreter, refutes (1) because the LXX expressed that the Lord said these things: (2) when a similar mockery is attributed to the Gentiles against the Hebrews, the name of God is not wont to be expressed by a plural name, 2 Kings 18:35, 2 Chron. 32:12, Psalm 89:19, Isa. 36:10, Joel 1:7. (3) The eating of fats was severely forbidden to the Hebrews, Lev. 3:16, as was the drinking of wine from libations, which was all to be poured out. (4) The idols of the Gentiles are frequently mocked in scripture because they were not able to help their worshippers, Isa. 44:9, Jer. 2:28, c. 11:12, Hab. 2:18. Ludov. de Leon in MS. apud Lorin. mentions an exposition concerning the enemies of the Hebrews reproaching them with the weakness of their God, even if under the plural name of gods, just as the commander of Sennacherib's army reproached them, 2 Kings 18:22, and the Philistines spoke in the plural, 1 Sam. 4:8 (see also 2 Kings 19:10), and that God induces the enemies to be said to object to the Hebrews the mixing of idol-sacrifices and the drinking of libation wine, insofar as they measured others by themselves: that God brings forward this cause among others why he has mercy on the people, not only because he sees them almost consumed, but also because the most arrogant enemies were most impiously slandering them. Which explanation is sufficiently probable, which I also see Mart. Borrhaus following in Marloratus on the Song of Moses, where the words are rendered thus: And (when) he will say (the enemy) whom he brings in mockingly insulting the miserable people. Osiander thinks that this will be said of the people by anyone who has considered their destruction and the cause of their destruction: Where are their gods, the rock in which they had confidence? where now is their fictitious and hypocritical religion, by which, being proud, they thought themselves to be superior to all evils? behold what outcome the fictitious and elective worship, which is truly the worship of idols, has had. Of whose victims they ate the fat: and drank the wine of the libations, that is, in whose sacrifices and worship they delighted themselves, (for formerly after sacrifices were offered, they celebrated feasts with hilarity, from the remains of the sacrifices) but since it was illicit for the Jews to eat the fat of the sacrifices: and the wine of the libations was not to be drunk, but to be poured out on the altar: God signifies that even in this part they practiced idolatry: because they did not observe the LEGITIMATE manner in it. For even when we presume to worship the true God in a way other than he himself commanded, that very thing is to worship idols. Let those feigned gods (whom you served) therefore rise up now and help you, and protect you in necessity. For no true protection can be hoped for from a false religion. This speech can also be referred to GOD himself: And the Lord will say: and thus the LXX Interpreters καὶ εἶπε κύριος, and the Greek Fathers, Cornel. à Lapide, and especially Quiros: Where are their gods, where is the Rock, in which they had confidence, let them rise up, let them help you, where an enallage of persons of the third and second is not unusual in such a pathetic speech. For the Jews were formerly accustomed to the worship of idols. Some therefore wish misery to be reproached to them by God, so that they may be recalled to a better mind and, recognizing the weakness of the gods whom they had worshipped, they may confess him alone to be the true

God. But because such worship of false gods did not prevail among them in the time preceding the latest πανολεθρίαν (total destruction) of the Jews, these things will be more correctly understood concerning the gods worshipped by the Gentiles: where are the gods (of the Gentiles) and the rock in which they trusted? (of which mention was made in v. 3. Of whose victims they ate the fat, or those gods as Agellius says: because the Gentiles believed their gods were fed by them) or men eating things sacrificed to idols, and drinking the wine of libations (for the Gentiles also had their sacrifices, οἰνόσπονδα: and others. See Jud. 9, 27. c. 16, 23 1. Cor. 8, 10. which explanation the diverse pronouns also favor, so that there is no need to posit an enallage. Where are the gods of the Gentiles, let them arise and be opulent for you, i.e. Lord: if you do not wish to acknowledge these judgments of mine, or if there are even found those who attribute the victories of enemies to their own gods with sacrilegious impiety, come, let those gods arise and help you, which since you expect in vain, see at last and know that I alone am, and there is no other God besides me. Concerning the Jews, Münster observes on this passage that from it they gathered a negative precept, that wine of any kind belonging to the Gentiles, which they use in their sacred rites, is not to be drunk by a Jew: and that the Rabbis added another thing to this precept, namely that the wine of Christians is not to be drunk at all by a Jew, which even today the more stubborn Jews strictly observe: indeed, some write that every wine which a Christian has touched is forbidden, even if a Christian has touched the wine of the Jews. Hence it is that the Jews abhor the company of Christians and execrate their table, lest on this occasion they transgress the law of God, drinking the wine of libations, or eating swine's flesh, and defiling their souls.

Latin:

Vers. 37. ET DICET, UBI SUNT DII EO- RUM?

Quis dicturus est? & de quo? Coccejus ab hosti- bus & vulgo id dictum iri vult de Ecclesia: quod præjudicaturi sint, quum ita exhaustæ erunt Eccle- siæ vires, malam fuisse ejus causam, fuisse hæreticam, confugisse ad Deos alienos, passiones illius non fuisse Deo grata sacrificia, revera agnoscendum esse vicari- um Dei Rom. Pontif. & vitem Sodomæ esse plantatio- nem Dei. Hunc triumphum hostium & hoc præju- dicium hominum v. 37. 38. sub carmine meretricio notari Esa. 23, 15, 16. & ejus initium conferri in an- num 70. postquam oblivioni fuit Tyrus spiritualis, h. e. à pace Ecclesiæ primitus concessa Anno Christi 1552. adeoque in annum Christi 1622. Sed hic sensus infertur in has prophetias, efferri ex iisdem non potest. Non enim vaticinatur vel Moses in hoc can- tico, vel Esaias loco laudato de temporibus Anti- Christi, aut reformationi data pace, eandemq́ sequu- ta castigatione. Sed Moses canit de judiciis adversus populum Judaicum. Esaias de Tyro negotiatrice an- tiqua.

Hugo, Rupertus, Lyranus, Vatablus, Abulensis & Valentia hæc irrifionis verba hoftibus populi Ju- daici adscribunt, cum viderent illos à se devictos, & ad extremam vastitatem redactos. Atque hæc etiam est R. Aben-Esdra explicatio, quasi ex superbia & contemtu loquatur talia hostis ad Judæos capti- vos, ubi est vester Deus? surgat & opem ferat vobis. Quam contumeliam Deus non ferens respondeat, videbitis nunc, quod ego sim Deus verus, cum indu- xero super vos vindictam, à qua nemo salvare vos po- terit. Quam vero sententiam inde refellit Quiros, Pontificius Interpres, (1.) quia LXX. expresserunt hæc Dominum dixisse: (2.) cum similis irrisio tribui- tur gentibus contra Ebræos, non solet nomen Dei nomine plurali efferri 2. Reg. 18, 35. 2. Paral. 32, 12. Psalm. 89, 19. Esa. 36, 10. Joel. 1, 7. (3.) Comestio adi- pum severe inhibita Ebræis Lev. 3, 16. ut & vini potus ex libaminibus, quod totum effundendum erat. (4.) Idola gentium frequenter in scriptura irriden- tur, quod suis cultoribus opitulari non valerent Es. 44, 9. Jer. 2, 28. c. 11, 12. Ab. 2, 18. Ludov. de Leon. in MS. apud Lorin. meminit expositionis de hosti- bus Hebræorum exprobrantibus illis imbecillitatem Dei sui, etsi sub nomine plurali Deorum, quemad- modum Sennacheribi exercitus Dux iis exprobra- bat 2. Reg. 18, 22. & Philistæi 1. Sam. 4, 8. in plurali loquuti sunt (vid. etiam 2. Reg. 19, 10.) & inducere Deum hostes dictos, objicientes Hebræis commi- stionem idolothytorum, & potum vini libaminum, quatenus ex seipsis alios metiebantur: Deum hanc inter alios causam afferre, cur miserreatur populi, non solum, quia videt pene consumtos, verum etiam, quoniam hostes arrogantissimi ipsis impiissime detrrhebant. Quæ explicatio satis est probabilis, quam etiam video sequi Mart. Borrhai apud Mar- loratum in Cantic. Mos. ubi sic redduntur verba: Et (quando) dicet (hostis) quem inducit ludibun- de insultantem misero populo. Osiander de popu- lo id dictum iri à quovis, qui ejus interitum & in- teritus causam consideraverit, existimat: Ubi sunt Dii eorum, petra in qua habebant fiduciam? ubi nunc est fictitia & hypocritica eorum Religio, qua super- bientes putabant, se omnibus malis esse superio- res? en quem exitum habuerit cultus fictitius & electitius, qui vere est cultus idolorum? De quo- rum victimis comedebant adipes: & bibebant vinum libaminum, id est, quorum sacrificiis, & cultibus se oblectabant, (olim enim post oblata sacrificia, convivia cum hilaritate celebrabant, de sacrificio- rum reliquiis) cum autem adipem sacrificiorum edere Judæis illicitum esset: & vinum libaminum non bibendum, sed fundendum esset in altari: signi- ficat Deus, eitam hac in parte eos idololatriam exer- cuisse: quod modum in eo LEGITIMUM non observaverint. Nam & cum verum Deum alio modo, quam ipse præcepit, colere præsumimus, idipsum est colere Idola. Surgant ergo nunc illi commentitii Dii (quibus servistis) & opitulen- tur vobis, & in necessitate vos protegant. Non enim ullum verum præsidium à falsa religione sperari potest. Referri etiam ad DEUM ipsum potest hæc oratio: Et dicet Dominus: atque ita LXX. Interpp. καὶ εἶπε κύριος, & Græci Patres, Cornel. à Lapide, & imprimis Quiros: Ubi sunt Dii eorum, ubi Petra, in qua habebant fiduciam, surgant, opitulentur vobis, ubi enallage in oratione ejusmo- di pathetica non insolens personarum tertiæ & se- cundæ occurrit. Nam assueti olim erant cultui idolorum Judæi. His ergo exprobrari à Deo mi- seriam nonnulli volunt, ut revocentur ad meliorem mentem & agnoscentes imbecillitatem Deorum, quos coluerant, fateantur ipsum solum esse verum

Deum. Sed quia talis Deorum falsorum cultus tem- pore novissimam Judæorum πανολεθρίαν antegres- so penes ipsos non viguit, rectius de diis a gentibu- cultis hæc accipientur: ubi sunt dii (gentium) & pe- tra, in qua illi confidebant? (cujus v. 3. mentio facta. De quorum victimis comedebant adipes, vel Dii illi ut Agellius: quia credebant gentiles Deos suos illi- pasci) vel homines idolothytis vescentes, & vinum li- baminum bibentes (habebant enim & gentiles sua sacrificia, οἰνόσπονδα: & alia. V. Jud. 9, 27. c. 16, 23 1. Cor. 8, 10. cui explicationi etiam favent pronomi- na diversa, ut non opus sit, enallagen ponere. Ub- sunt dii gentium, surgant & opulentur vobis, q. d. Dominus: si hæc mea judicia agnoscere non vultis, aut reperiuntur etiam, qui victorias hostium diis ipsorum sacrilega impietate tribuant, agite, sur- gant Dii illi, & vobis succurrant, quod quum frustra expectetis, videte tandem atque cognoscite quod ego sim solus, & non sit alius Deus præter me. De Ju- dæis observat Münsterus ad h. l. quod ex eo colle- gerint præceptum negativum, quod vinum quale- cunque gentium, quo in sacris suis utuntur, à Judæo non sit bibendum: quodque huic præcepto Rabbini aliud addiderint, nempe quod vinum Christianorum penitus non sit bibendum à Judæo, quod & hodie per- tinaciores Judæi fortiter observant: imo scribunt quidam, quod omne vinum, quod tetigit Christianus, sit interdictum, etiamsi Christianus contigerit vinum Judæorum. Hinc est, quod Judæi horrent consor- tium Christianorum & execrantur mensam illo- rum, ne hac occasione prævaricentur legem Dei, bibentes vinum libaminum, aut comedentes car- nem suillam, animasque suas inquinantes.

## 32:39
Vers. 39. SEE THAT I ALONE AM.

In Hebrew: See now, that I, I am, and there is no God with me, that is, acknowledge even now at last, that I am the true God, who can destroy and save. I kill and I will make to live, I wound and I will heal, and there is none who can deliver out of my hand (or power). Compare 1 Sam. 2, 6. Job 5, 17. 18. Hos. 6, 2. Tob. 13, 2. Wis. 16, 13. 14. 15.

Chiliasts, as Cocceius notes, §. 1425, from the words see now: I make alive, gather that Christ will return from heaven to the Church before the last day, and that there will be some particular resurrection before the universal one. Cocceius, admitting a vivification preparatory to the vivification of the flesh, calls it an awakening from blindness and afflictions, and the Church being pacified from the persecution of the Anti-Christ, and he opines that, the destroyers of the earth having been destroyed (Apoc. 11, 18.), the Gospel will be preached again, and all kingdoms will be Christ's: Dan. 7, 27. Apoc. 10, 8. 17. Thus the dead will rise again anew (for he calls the first resurrection the conversion of the Gentiles through the first preaching of the Gospel: this to be followed by apostasy and the second death, and the dominion of hell Apoc. 20. of which also Ap. 6, 8. c. 13, 1. c. 15, 3. Dan. 7, 2.) Ez. 37. John 5, 25. and that that multitude of those rising again will be innumerable Apoc. 7, 9. To which he wishes to apply Deut. 32, 43. Isa. 19, 20. But these are almost similar to the dreams of the Chiliasts. They certainly do not have more solid foundations in the scriptures. It is not established by any document that Christ speaks these things, even if they are rightly applied to Him, because of the ὁμοθσίαν (consubstantiality) with the Father, by Hilary, in Ps. 68. August. lib. 3. contr. Maxim. cap. 23. However, these do not treat of mortification through contrition of the law, and vivification through grace announced in the Gospel, as Osiander: not of the killing of vices in us, and the vivification of the Spirit or the new man, as Ambros. serm. 29. Not of the mortification of the flesh, and the vivification of the Spirit, which is in Baptism, as Basil homil. 13. not of the killing of the flesh through diseases, so that the soul may be vivified, as Bernard somewhere, all of which only serve for the application of this sentence; nor of death inflicted and life restored, as Epiphan. haeres. 64. n. 29. But of killing and preservation in life, of being cast into danger of life, and liberation from danger of life, as Nazianzen. Orat. 32. Hieron. in Thren. 3. Ephrem de Vit. Spirit. Procop. in Isa. 38. etc. Armachanus, as Cornelius cites here, in quaest. Armen. asserts that he received from a certain learned Hebrew that the Hebrew words are to be pointed passively in this way: אני אמות ואחיה מחצתי ואני ארפא, that is, I shall be killed, and I shall live, I shall be pierced, and I shall be healed: and so it is written, says Cornelius, in the Codex written by the hand of Ezra, which is kept at Bologna among the Dominican Fathers: (let faith be with Cornelius, and those who persuaded him of it) as if this were a prophecy concerning Christ, and it is said of him that he himself is to be killed by the Jews, and soon by his own power to rise again from death, as the Lord of life and death. Marcionites in Tertull. l. 2. contr. Marc. c. 14. l. 4. c. 1. and 34. l. 5. c. 10. from these and similar places gathered that God is the creator of evils, which Tertullian concedes concerning the evils of punishments, not of sins. It is noted in l. 2. c. 24. that even among the Greeks sometimes evils are used for vexations and injuries, not for malignities.

Latin:

Vers. 39. VIDETE QUOD EGO SIM SO- LUS.

In Ebr. Videte nunc, quod ego, ego sim, & non sit Deus mecum, id est, agnoscite vel nunc tandem, quod ego sim Deus verus, qui perdere potest ac servare. Ego occido & vivere faciam, vulnero & sa- nabo, & non est, qui de manu (seu potestate) mea pos- sit eruere. Conf. 1. Sam. 2, 6. Job. 5, 17. 18. Hos. 6, 2. Tob. 13, 2. Sap. 16, 13. 14. 15.

Chiliastæ, notante Coccejo, §. 1425. è verbis vi- dete nunc: Ego vivifico, colligunt Christum ante ul- timum diem reversurum esse è cælo ad Ecclesiam, & fu- turam particularem aliquam resurrectionem ante universalem. Coccejus vivificationem præambu- lam vivificationis carnis admittens, eam dicit ex- citationem è cæcitate & afflictionibus, ac pacificata Ecclesia à persequutione Anti-Christi, & opinatur, destructis destructoribus terræ (Apocal. 11, 18.) iterum prædicatum iri Evangelium, & omnia regna futura Christi: Dan. 7, 27. Apoc. 10, 8. 17. Sic mortuos denuo resurrecturos (primam enim resurrectionem dicit conversionem gentium per prædicationem Evangelii primam: hanc sequuturam apostasiam & mortem se- cundam, & dominatum inferni Apoc. 20. de quo etiam Ap. 6, 8. c. 13, 1. c. 15, 3. Dan. 7, 2.) Ez, 37. Joh. 5, 25. & multitudinem eam resurgentium innumerabilem futu- ram Apoc. 7, 9. Quo facere vult Deuter. 32, 43. Esa. 19, 20. Sed hæc similia fere Chiliastarum somniis. Fundamenta certe solidiora in scripturis non ha- bent. Christum hæc loqui, nullo documento constat, etsi eidem recte, ob ὁμοθσίαν cum Pa- tre applicentur ab Hilario, in Psal. 68. August. lib. 3. contr. Maxim. cap. 23. Agunt autem hæc non de mortificatione per contritionem legis, & vivificatione per gratiam in Evangelio annunciatam, ut Osiander: non de occisione vitiorum in nobis, & vivificatione Spiritus vel novi hominis, ut Ambros. serm. 29. Non de mortificatione carnis, & Spiritus vivificatione, quæ sit in Baptismo, ut Basilius homil. 13. non de oc- cisione carnis per morbos, ut vivificetur anima, ut Bernhardus alicubi, quæ omnia solum ad applica- tionem hujus sententiæ faciunt; nec de morte illa- ta & restituta vita, ut Epiphan. hæres. 64. n. 29. Sed de interfectione & conservatione in vita, de injectio- ne in periculum vitæ, & liberatione è vitæ periculo, ut Nazianzen. Orat. 32. Hieron. in Thren. 3. Ephrem de Vit. Spirit. Procop. in Esa. 38. &c. Armachanus, citante hic Cornelio, in quæst. Armen. asserit, se à quodam docto Hebræo accepisse, Hebræa pun- ctanda esse passive hoc modo: אני אמות ואחיה מחצתי ואני ארפא, id est, ego occidar, & vivam, transfigar, & sanabor: itaque scriptum esse, ait Cor- nelius, in Codice conscripto manu Esdræ, qui Bo- noniæ apud Patres Dominicanos servetur: (fides sit penes Cornelium, & qui ei id persuasere) quasi hic sit Prophetia de Christo, de eoque dicatur, quod ipse à Judæis sit occidendus, mox à morte propria virtute resurrecturus, quasi Dominus vitæ & mor- tis. Marcionitæ apud Tertull. l. 2. contr. Marc. c. 14. l. 4. c. 1. & 34. l. 5. c. 10. ex his & similibus locis col- ligebant, Deum esse malorum conditorem, quod de malis suppliciorum concedit Tertull. non delicto- rum. Notatur l. 2. c. 24. etiam apud Græcos inter- dum malitias pro vexationibus, & læsuris, non pro malignitatibus poni.

## 32:41
Vers. 41. I WILL LIFT UP MY HAND TO HEAVEN, AND I WILL SAY, I LIVE FOREVER.

I, swearing with the greatest solemnity (the Lord speaks ἀνθρωποπαθῶς, for those swearing used to lift up the hand) solemnly affirm that I will avenge the injuries inflicted upon my people as certainly as it is certain that I live forever. Therefore, Cocceius does not firmly gather from this mode of speaking that God speaks these things ἔνσαρκον (in the flesh).

Latin:

Vers. 41. LEVABO AD COELUM MANUM MEAM, ET DICAM, VIVO EGO IN Æ- TERNUM.

Ego maxima solemnitate jurans (ἀνθρωποπα- θῶς loquitur Dominus, levabant enim manum ju- rantes) solemniter affirmo, ulturum me illatas po- pulo meo injurias tam certo, quam certum est, me vivere in æternum. Non ergo firmiter ex hoc loquendi modo colligit Coccejus, Deum ἔνσαρκον hæc loqui.

## 32:42
Vers. 42. IF I SHARPEN MY SWORD LIKE LIGHTNING.

In Hebrew. The lightning of my sword (that is, when I shall have sharpened my sword as if flashing and coruscating: Cf. Gen. 3, 24. Psalm 7, 13. Job 20, 25. Ezek. 21, 9. 19. Nahum 3, 3. Hab. 3, 11.) AND MY HAND SHALL HAVE TAKEN HOLD OF JUDGMENT (that is, when I shall have begun to execute sentence) I WILL RENDER VENGEANCE TO MY ENEMIES (I will avenge my people of their enemies: for these are also my enemies.) AND TO THEM THAT HATE ME I WILL REPAY, I will treat them according to their merit. I WILL MAKE MY ARROWS DRUNK WITH BLOOD, AND MY SWORD SHALL DEVOUR FLESH FROM THE BLOOD OF THE SLAIN, AND FROM THE CAPTIVITY OF THE BARE HEAD OF THE ENEMIES. That is, from the blood of the captives, who are stripped of their head, from the captives and overcome enemies, who will walk sad and mourning with bare head (as was the custom then), I will bring back a most glorious victory. For I shall make such a slaughter of enemies that I shall seem to have made my weapons drunk with blood, and to have prepared a banquet for my sword; whence it will be sated by devouring the enemies. This victory, according to Osiander and others, is partly by the Gospel of the word: while incredulity and impiety are laid low: partly when God destroys his enemies, the Gospel being preserved, and thrusts them down to Tartarus (still dripping with blood), which happened to Julian the Apostate and other tyrants and persecutors of the Gospel. Cf. concerning the phrase Isa. 34, 8. c. 49, 25. Jer. 46, 10. Ez. 39, 18. 19. regarding inebriation, and also concerning the devouring of the sword Isa. 1, 20. Jerem. 2, 30. chap. 12, 12. chap. 46, 10. etc. Thence, bare head, Antonius Guevara in Lorinus page 603, in this place, explains as abject captivity, so that the sense may be: I will consume my enemies both by death and also by captivity, and servitude most vile and most abject: inasmuch as they are of a shorn and shaved head, or of those having shorn and shaved heads; which did not happen to all captives and servants, since some of them were held in value and honor, as Joseph in Egypt, Tobias in Nineveh, King Joachim of Judah, and Daniel and his companions in Babylon. Vatablus explained: When I shall take vengeance on my enemies, then my sword shall devour the flesh from their heads, i.e., I shall cut off the heads of the enemies with the sword. He also notes that it can be translated: In the beginning in the vengeances of the enemy, or in the beginning of the vengeances of the enemy, that is, when I first take punishment from my enemies. The explanation of B. Luther pleases: And the head of the enemies shall be bare, that is, they shall be deprived of the kingdom, so that without the glory of the kingdom they may be dispersed through the world.

Coccejus understands by the enemy head the Roman Anti-Christ, and by the hairs and the head of hair many peoples depending on him, and he thinks the vengeance of the Anti-Christ is now connected to the chastisement of the Church, comparing Apoc. 6, 12. seqq. cap. 9. cap. 10, 16. cap. 11, 14. cap. 16, 14. 17. cap. 19, 17. seqq. cap. 20, 9. as also Es. 19, 20. 21. 22. 23. cap. 59, 16. 17. 18. Ezech. 38, 39. Dan. 12, 8. 11. 13. But just as this comparison is merely arbitrary, so in most of those places it is assumed precariously that the Anti-Christ is indicated: from Dan. 12 he gathers that after the first peace indicated in Deut. 32, 36. 37. (which he refers to the year 1552) and the persecution of the Church, for the chastisement of the same, by enemies, this vengeance of the enemies will follow, and he gathers the time from which, namely, the daily sacrifice (the passions of Christians, and prayers, and charity, and discipline) shall have been removed, through the flight of the idolaters, which he refers to the time of Constantine. M. compares, up to the abomination 1290 years. But let us leave these dreams, or enigmas, to those who are delighted by such things: we freely profess that we cannot perceive such things from these Mosaic Prophecies, of Isaiah, Daniel, and John, which is our astonishment.

Latin:

Vers. 42. SI ACUERO UT FULGUR GLA- DIUM MEUM.

In Ebr. Fulgur gladii mei (id est, ubi gladium meum quasi fulgurantem & coruscantem acuero: Conf. Genes. 3, 24. Psalm. 7, 13. Job. 20, 25. Ezech. 21, 9. 19. Nehem. 3, 3. Abac. 3, 11.) ET ARRIPUE- RIT JUDICIUM MANUS MEA (id est, quan- do cepero sententiam exequi) REDDAM UL- TIONEM HOSTIBUS MEIS (ulciscaf popu- lum meum de hostibus ipsius: hi enim & mei ho- stes sunt.) ET HIS QUI ODERUNT ME RE- TRIBUAM, tractabo eos pro merito. INEBRI- ABO SAGITTAS MEAS SANGUINE, ET GLADIUS MEUS DEVORABIT CARNES DE CRUORE OCCISORUM, ET DE CA- PTIVITATE NUDATI INIMICORUM CA- PITIS. Id est, de cruore captivorum, qui nudati sunt capitis, de captivis, & superatis hostibus, qui mœsti & lugentes nudato capite (ut moris erat tum) ince- dent, gloriosissimam victoriam reportabo. Tantarn enim stragem faciam hostium, ut arma mea quasi sanguine inebriasse videar, & gladio meo convivi- um præparasse; unde devorandis hostibus exatie- tur. Hæc victoria secundum Osiandrum, & alios par- tim sit Evangelio verbi: dum incredulitas & impie- tas prosternitur: partim cum Deus hostes suos, conser- vato Evangelio, perdit, & ad Tartara, (sanguine ad- huc madentes) detrudit, quod Juliano Apostatæ, & aliis Tyrannis & persecutoribus Evangelii contigit. Conf. de phrasi Esa. 34, 87. c. 49, 25. Jer. 46, 10. Ez. 39, 18. 19. qua inebriationem, nec non de devoratio- ne gladii Esa. 1, 20. Jerem. 2, 30. cap. 12, 12. cap. 46, 10. &c. Inde capite nudato Antonius Guevara apud Lorinum pag. 603. in h. l. explicat de capti- vitate abjecta, ut sensus sit: Absumam inimicos meos tum nece, tum etiam captivitate, ac servi- tutæ vilissima, abjectissimaque: utpote nudati & abrasi capitis, sive nudata & abrasa capita habenti- um; quod non omnibus captivis ac servis contin- gebat, cum eorum quidam in pretio, & honore haberentur, ut Joseph in Ægypto, Tobias in Ni- nive, Joachim Rex Judæ, & Daniel, sociique in Babylone. Vatablus exposuit: Cum sumam vindi- ctam de hostibus meis, tunc devorabit gladius meus car- nes è capitibus eorum, h. e. ense amputabo capita ho- stium. Notat etiam verti posse: In principio in ul- tionibus inimici, aut in principio vindictarum inimici, hoc est, quum primum sumam pœnas de inimicis meis. Placet B. Lutheri explicatio: Et caput inimicorum nudum erit, id est, privabuntur regno, ut sine gloria regni sint dispersi per orbem.

Coccejus per caput inimicum Anti-Christum Romanum, per pilos & cæsariem multos populos ab eo dependentes intelligit, & castigationi Ecclesiæ jam connecti putat vindictam Anti-Christi, conferens Apoc. 6, 12. seqq. cap. 9. cap. 10, 16. cap. 11, 14. cap. 16, 14. 17. cap. 19, 17. seqq. cap. 20, 9. ut & Es. 19, 20. 21. 22. 23. cap. 59, 16. 17. 18. Ezech. 38, 39. Dan. 12, 8. 11. 13. Sed uti hæc collatio mere arbitraria, ita in ple- risque illis locis Anti-Christum indicari precario assumitur: è Dan. 12. colligit post primam pacem Deut. 32, 36. 37. indicatam (quam ad ann. 1552. re- fert) & persequutionem Ecclesiæ, ad castigationem ejusdem, per hostes, vindictam hanc hostium se- quuturam, ac tempus colligit, ex quo nempe re- motum fuerit sacrificium juge (passiones Christiano- rum, & preces, & charitas & disciplina,) per fu- gam idololatrarum, quam in tempus Constant. M. confert, usque ad abominationem 1290. annos. Verum hæc somnia, vel ænigmata relinquamus il- lis, qui delectantur talibus: nos talia ex hisce Pro- phetiis Mosaicis, Esaiæ, Danielis, & Johannis, qui noster est stupor, percipere non posse, ultro profi- temur.

## 32:43
Vers. 43. LAUDATE) It is in Hiphil. Therefore Aquila translated ἀἰνοποιήσατε.

The sense, according to some, is: Let the nations make his people praise, or provoke the Jewish people, concerning whom the Lord previously: I will make them jealous with a non-people. In the chain according to Theodoret from Aquila is had ἑνοποιήσατε make one, or unite to yourselves the nations, his people, which Procopius also reports, Lorinus renders it thus: Personate nations his people, change to jubilation. Osiander thus: Jubilate nations (who are) his people, so that it may be taught that the greatest part of the Church consists of nations converted to Christ. Thus also the learned among the Hebrews according to Vatablus, O nations, who are his people, praise, sub-understand Jehovah. Kimchi, Cajetanus, and Coccejus, sing O nations his people, which explanation is also approved by us, because the sign of the accusative case is not had. The Chaldean, however, has it, and most others, nor is it improbable, in the judgment of Lorinus, that the nations converted to Christ are invited to praise the Jews, the people once of God, from whom they had received the cradles as it were of faith, and the rudiments of Christian doctrine. For when they praise the people of God because of the benefits of God, they confess God as the author of them. And therefore the Apostle concluded from these words that the calling of the nations and their communion with the people of God in the Church is hinted at here, Rom. 15, 10. bringing in the version of the LXX Interpreters, which rendered the same thing paraphrastically. Although indeed some wish other places of scripture to be hinted at there; Thomas Es. 66, 10. rejoice with Jerusalem, and exult in her all you who love her, Lyranus Esa. 35, 1. the desert and the pathless place shall rejoice, and the solitude shall exalt; others Psal. 67, 5. let the nations rejoice and exult etc. Origenes, however, Sedulius, Haymo, Anselmus, Remigius, Burgensis, Toletus, Justinianeus, Salmeron, Cornelius, Saa, and our own, and easily all the Reformed to Rom. 15. as also to this place, Agellius likewise, Quiros, Clichtoveus, Valentia, Lorinus in this place, acknowledge that these words of the canticle were brought in by the Apostle. The whole in the LXX edition has it thus: ἐὐφράνθητε ὀρανοὶ ἅμα ἀὐτῷ καὶ προσκυνήσάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες ἄγγελοι θεῦ: rejoice O heavens together with him, and let all the angels of God adore him (which latter words Procopius thinks to have crept in here from Ps. 96: but the collector of the Scholia to the Sixtine Greek Bible, Justin in Tryph. Hilar. in Ps. 67. Epiph. haeres. Arian. Hieron. in Zach. 8. notes that these words attributed these words to this place) ἐὐφράνθητε ἔθνη μετὰ τῶ λαῶ αὐτῶ, καὶ ἐνισχυσάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες ὑὑοὶ θεῦ, rejoice O nations with his people (which were brought in by Paul) and let all the sons of God be strengthened in him, or according to other books angels of God, angels of God. The Apostolic allegation agrees perfectly with our explanation. For if the nations rejoice in the Lord, as his people, certainly they rejoice in the Lord with his people, those, namely, who from the Israelites are still the people of God. Therefore the perversion of the place by Isaac Karo in Toledot Isaac is to be detested, interpreting these words ironically, and by ellipsis, sing O nations because of his people i.e. weep O nations; and Abarbenel, with Isaac, Aram. Make the nations sing his people, namely by your weeping. Coccejus carries these to the last times and assumes that the Gospel will be preached to them among very many nations, among whom it had not been preached before, or among whom it had ceased to be preached before that article of grace, drawing hither also Matth. 24, 14. Apoc. 7, 8. & c, 20. Num. 24, 10. Ps. 68, 32. 33. Ps. 72. Ps. 86, 9. Ps. 90, 13. Ps. 107, 41. 42. Ps. 110, 2. seqq. Es. 2, 4. c. 11, 11. c. 23, 18. c. 24, 23. c. 25, 2. 3. c. 46, 8. c. 58, 14. c. 59, 16. c. 60, 5. c. 61, 8. seqq. c. 66, 19. 20. 21. Ezech. 37, 23. Dan. 7, 27. Hos. 2, 25. c. 14, 5. 6. Joël. 4, 10. 11. 12. Amos. 9, 13. 14. 15. Mich. 4, 6. 7. Habac. 3, 18. 19. Soph. 3, 19. 20. Zach. 10, 10. seqq. c. 14, 8. seqq. But in these places neither did the Ancients find a universal proclamation under the newest times, nor will anyone rashly find one besides Coccejus. The same must be held concerning the gloss of the last words.

Vers. eod. AND HE SHALL BE PROPITIUS TO THE LAND OF HIS PEOPLE.

By which Cocceius wishes to indicate (1.) that the peace of the land is to be restored in the last times to the Church, which has suffered persecution Ps. 85, 2. 3. 4. 9. Isa. 19, 18. 19. 20. 21. 22. (2.) that the kingdom of GOD is to be restored in all places from which it has been expelled Ezek. 36, 33. 34. 35. 36. (3.) that the Jews are also to be received into favor, and indeed with the tranquility of their own land, yet in such a way that no carnal temple is to be rebuilt, but that the Jews as Christians are to obtain their land without the servitude of the elements of the world, just as it was once possessed by Christians Lev. 26, 44. 45. Ps. 80, 1. Ps. 106, 47. Isa. 6, 13. Jer. 3, 21. chap. 31, 39. 40. Ezek. 39, 25. Hos. 3, 5. He draws what speaks of the spiritual communion of the Church to the possession of the corporal land; and what speaks of the perennial successive conversion of the Jews, to a simultaneous one that will happen in the last times. Finally, to the expiation of the land he also adds the purging from sins and scandals, and to this end he seizes Ps. 85, 11. Isa. 4, 4. chap. 59, 21. chap. 60, 1. 3. 21. Ezek. 39, 15. 16. as also Isa. 2, 18. 21. Mic. 5, 13. 21. chap. 7, 19. 20. Hos. 14. and thus he promises I know not what golden ages still to the Church to be gathered from all nations and the Jews before the coming of the Lord. But that these things treat of the last times is established by no evidence, nor are they to be understood of the Jews or the land of the Jews, but of the people of the Lord, who for the greatest part consisted of the Gentiles, and those things began to be fulfilled already in the time of the Apostle Rom. 15. verse 19.

God is therefore propitious to the land of His people, when He looks upon it with His grace, and cherishes the Church, to which it must be attributed that He sometimes also grants it internal tranquility, so that after calamities and persecutions it may be able to breathe, until, having overcome in this warfare, it may triumph eternally, and enjoy heavenly blessedness in the end. The Paraphrase of the Blessed Luther is correct here, at v. 43. Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people, (that is, the Gentiles shall be joined with the remaining believers in faith.) Because He will avenge the blood of His servants (namely, in the slayers of the Prophets and Apostles.) And He will be propitious to the land of His people: namely, to the remnant of Israel, which shall have been converted, for this one He will prepare a new kingdom under Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 43. LAUDATE) Est in Hiphil. Ideo Aquila ver- tit ἀἰνοποιήσατε.

Sensus, juxta nonnullos, est: Laudare faciant gentes populum ejus, seu provocent populum Judai- cum, de quo Dominus antea: Zelare eos faciam in non populo. In catena apud Theodoret. ex Aquila habetur ἑνοποιήσατε unum facite, sive unite vobis gentes, populum ejus, quod etiam refert Procopius, Lorinus ita reddit: Personate gentes populum ejus, exmutate ad jubilum. Osiander ita: Jubilate gentes (qui estis) populus ejus, ut doceatur maximam Ec- clesiæ partem constare ex gentibus ad Christum conversis. Sic etiam doctus inter Hebræos apud Vatabl. ô gentes, quæ estis populus ejus, laudate, sub- intell. Jehovam. Kimchi, Cajetanus, & Coccejus, cantate gentes populus ejus, quæ explicatio etiam nobis probatur, quia non habetur signum accusa- tivi casus. Chald. tamen id habet, & plerique alii, nec improbabile est, judice Lorino, invitari gentes ad Christum conversas, ut laudent Judæos, populum quondam Dei, à quo fidei velut incunabula, doctrinæ- que Christianæ ceperant rudimenta. Cum enim laudant populum Dei ob beneficia Dei, Deum confitentur ipso- rum auctorem. Ideoque gentium vocationem & communionem cum populo Dei in Ecclesia hic innui Apostolus ex his verbis conclusit Rom. 15, 10. adducens LXX. Interpp. versionem, quæ eadem paraphrastice reddidit. Quamvis enim nonnulli alios scripturæ locos ibi innui velint; Thomas Es. 66, 10. lætamini cum Jerusalem, & exultate in ea omnes, qui diligitis eam, Lyranus Esa. 35, 1. lætabitur deserta & invia, & exaltabit solitudo; alii Psal. 67, 5. lætentur & exultent gentes &c. Origenes tamen, Se- dulius, Haymo, Anshelmus, Remigius, Burgensis, To- letus, Justinianeus, Salmeron, Cornelius, Saa, & no- strates, ac Reformati facile omnes ad Rom. 15. ut & ad h. l. Agellius item, Quiros, Clichtoveus, Valen- tia, Lorinus h. l. agnoscunt, hæc cantici verba ab Apostolo adducta esse. Integra in LXX. edit. ita habent: ἐὐφράνθητε ὀρανοὶ ἅμα ἀὐτῷ καὶ προσκυ- νησάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες ἄγγελοι θεῦ: lætamini cæ- li simul cum eo, & adorent eum omnes angeli Dei (quæ posteriora verba Procopius è Ps. 96. huc irrepsisse pu- tat: at collector Scholiorum ad Biblia Sixtina Græ- ca, Justinum in Tryph. Hilar. in Ps. 67. Epiph. hæref. Arian. Hieron. in Zach. 8. hæc verba huic loco tribu- isse notat) ἐὐφράνθητε ἔθνη μετὰ τῶ λαῶ αὐτῶ, καὶ ἐνισχυσάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες ὑὑοὶ θεῦ, lætamini gen- tes cum populo ejus (quæ à Paulo adducta) & roboren- tur in eo omnes filii Dei, aut secundum alios libros ἄγγελοι θεῦ, angeli Dei. Congruit apprime alle- gatio Apostolica explicationi nostræ. Nam si gen- tes lætentur in Domino, ceu populus ejus, utique cum populo ejus, illis, qui nempe ex Israelitis adhuc po- pulus Dei sunt, in Domino lætantur. Detestanda ergo loci est perversio Isaaci Karo in Toledot Isaac, ironice, & per ellipsin verba hæc interpretantis, cantate gentes ob populum ejus q. d. flete gentes; & A- barbenelis, cum Isaaco, Aram. Facite cantare gentes populum ipsius, nimirum vestro fletu. Coccejus hæc ad ultima tempora rapit iisque Evangelium prædi- catum iri autumat apud plurimas gentes, apud quas antea non fuerat prædicatum, vel apud quas desie- rat ante illum articulum gratiæ prædicari, huc etiam trahens Matth. 24, 14. Apoc. 7, 8. & c, 20. Num. 24, 10. Ps. 68, 32. 33. Ps. 72. Ps. 86, 9. Ps. 90, 13. Ps. 107, 41. 42. Ps. 110, 2. seqq. Es. 2, 4. c. 11, 11. c. 23, 18. c. 24, 23. c. 25, 2. 3. c. 46, 8. c. 58, 14. c. 59, 16. c. 60, 5. c. 61, 8. seqq. c. 66, 19. 20. 21. Ezech. 37, 23. Dan. 7, 27. Hos. 2, 25. c. 14, 5. 6. Joël. 4, 10. 11. 12. Amos. 9, 13. 14. 15. Mich. 4, 6. 7. Habac. 3, 18. 19. Soph. 3, 19. 20. Zach. 10, 10. seqq. c. 14, 8. seqq. Sed in his locis universale præconium sub novissima tempora, neque Vete- res invenere, neque temere quis præter Coccejum inveniet. Idem habendum de glossa verborum ul- timorum.

Vers. eod. ET PROPITIVS ERIT TERRÆ POPULI SUI.

Quibus designari vult Coccejus (1.) restituendam esse novissimis temporibus pacem terræ Ecclesiæ, quæ persecutionem passa est Psalm. 85, 2. 3. 4. 9. Esa. 19, 18. 19. 20. 21. 22. (2.) restituendum esse regnum DEI omnibus locis, unde expulsum est Ezech. 36, 33. 34. 35. 36. (3.) in gratiam etiam recipiendos Judæos, & quidem cum tranquillitate terræ ipsorum, ita tamen, ut nul- lum templum carnale reædificandum sit, sed Judæi ut Christiani terram suam sine servitute elemento- rum mundi obtenturi sint, quemadmodum olim à Christianis possessa fuit Levit. 26, 44. 45. Ps. 80, 1. Ps. 106, 47. Esa. 6, 13. Jer. 3, 21. cap. 31, 39. 40. Ezech. 39, 25. Hos. 3, 5. Quæ de spirituali communione Ec- clesiæ loquuntur, ad possessionem terræ corporalis tra- hit; quæ de perenni successiva conversione Judæo- rum, ad simultaneam novissimis temporibus futuram. Denique expiationi terræ etiam adjungit expurga- tionem à peccatis & scandalis, eoque rapit Psalm. 85, 11. Esa. 4, 4. cap. 59, 21. cap. 60, 1. 3. 21. Ezech. 39, 15. 16. ut & Esa. 2, 18. 21. Mich. 5, 13. 21. cap. 7, 19. 20. Hos. 14. atque ita nescio quæ aurea secula adhuc pollicetur Ecclesiæ ex gentibus omnibus, & Ju- dæis congregandæ ante adventum Domini. At de novissimis temporibus hæc agere, nullo docu- mento constat, neque de Judæis, aut terra Judæo- rum illa accipienda, sed de populo Domini, qui ma- ximam partem è gentibus constabat, & impleri cœ- perunt illa jam tempore Apostoli Rom. 15. vers. 19.

Propitius ergo Deus terræ populi sui est, cum gra- tia sua respicit, ac fovet Ecclesiam, cui tribuen- dum, quod interdum etiam tranquillitatem inter- nam ei donat, ut post calamitates, & persequutio- nes ea respirare queat, donec militia hac superat æternum triumphet, ac cœlesti beatitudine, fin fine fruatur. Recte se hic habet Paraphrasis B. Lu- theri, ad v. 43. Exultate gentes cum populo ejus, (i est, cum reliquis fidelibus gentes copulabuntur in fide.) Quia sanguinem servorum suorum ulciscetu (scil. in occisoribus Prophetarum, & Apostolo- rum.) Et propitius erit terræ populi sui: nempe re- liquis de Israel, qui conversus fuerit, huic novum regnum parabit sub Christo.

## 32:47
Vers. 47. BECAUSE THEY ARE NOT IN VAIN FOR YOU, BUT THAT EACH ONE MIGHT LIVE IN THEM.

In Hebrew: For it is not an empty word for you, but it is your life. Since he says life simply, this life is not understood, but eternal life, from which he himself also distinguishes τὴν μακροβιότητα [long life], when he adds, and in this word you shall prolong your days in the land, concerning which the Apostle Rom. 8, 10. The body indeed is dead because of sin, but the spirit is life because of righteousness, i.e., when the body dies. The spirit, however, does not see death, but passes into glory. Which is contrary to the delirium of Socinus: it is to be noted that God did not make a covenant with the Israelites concerning eternal life, or that the promise of eternal life was not added to the law of Moses. The Jews are sounder here. R. Maimonides, Hal. on repentance, chap. 8, explains the passage Deut. 5, 16 thus: The good prepared for the righteous is the life of the world to come, life without death, good without the mixture of evil, as it is written in the law, that it may be well with you, and you may prolong your days. Indeed, they learned from tradition that that, that it may be well with you, is to be understood of the world which is entirely good, and that, that you may prolong your days, is to be taken of the world which is entirely long, and this is the world to come, as rightly Theodor. Hackspan, Oration on the Necessity of Sacred Philology, p. 33, who adds a very useful warning: you who say that this sense of Holy Scripture is mystical, beware that you do not ignore that the deeper secrets of the law are judged by the circumcised to be the very sense of Scripture.

Vers. same. THAT EACH ONE MIGHT LIVE IN THEM) That life which is promised in the law, long and sweet.

We have already often noted that Pelagian and Socinian error, that only temporal life was promised in the law, and its longevity and sweetness. From which preconceived opinion this Paraphrase flowed. But here both are attributed to the word of God, both that it is their life, and that by the word of God days can be prolonged upon the earth. The former pertains to spiritual promises, and also looks to eternal life: the latter to temporal ones. We have proven elsewhere that both are found in the O.T., nay, even in the law itself. We do not wish, therefore, to do what is already done. And the matter is evident even from chapter 30, which, as the Blessed Franz says in Disp. 13 on Deut., shines like the morning star and Lucifer in the whole Pentateuch; and the whole thing is Evangelical, as are most of the primary things, and not only an explanation of the first promise in Gen. 3, 15, preserved and propagated among the Fathers until now, but also the Fountain from which the Prophets drew all their sweetest consolations for troubled consciences. He promises there gratuitous mercy, remission of sins, conversion, spiritual circumcision, and blessing: and indeed unto life. And v. 6 he proposes life and death, blessing and cursing, so that life may be chosen, and the Israelites may live v. 19. Which are to be understood especially of spiritual blessing and eternal life. Whence the Apostle teaches, Rom. 10, that the word of faith and the righteousness of faith are proposed here.

Therefore, the observation of Cocceius §. 1518 in the Old Testament is not correct here, that the pious were so subjected to earthly promises that they were forced ordinarily to fear death as contrary to the promise, and thus as some punishment and execration: but that in the New we are not subjected to earthly promises, because we can glory even in afflictions. For neither was there any condemnation to be feared by the faithful in the Old Testament, Acts 15, 11, nor are the pious in the New destitute of earthly promises, 1 Tim. 4, 8, and that the ancients also gloried in afflictions, not only Job is a witness, and David, but the Holy Spirit Himself set forth an entire catalog of such people for the Hebrew faithful under the New Testament as an example, Heb. chap. 11.

Latin:

Vers. 47. QUIA NON IN CASSUM PRÆ- CEPTA SUNT VOBIS, SED UT SINGULI IN EIS VIVERENT.

In Ebr. Nam non est verbum inane vobis, sed est vita vestra. Quum vitam simpliciter dicat, non intelligitur hæc vita, sed æterna, à quo etiam ipse την μακροβιότητα distinguit, cum addit, & in hoc verbo prolongabitis dies in terra, de quo Apostolus Rom. 8, 10. Corpus quidem mortuum est propter peccatum, sed spiritus est vita propter justiciam h. e. quando corpus moritur. Spiritus tamen non videt mortem, sed transit in gloriam. Quod contra Socin. delirium: Deum non fecisse fœdus cum Israelitis de vita æterna, aut legi Mosis non fuisse adjectam pro- missionem æternæ vitæ notandum. Saniores hic Ju- dæi sunt. R. Maimonid. Hal. de pœn. cap. 8. locum Deut. 5, 16. sic exponit: Bonum justis paratum est futuri vita seculi, vita sine morte, bonum sine mixtu- ra mali, uti scriptum est in lege, ut bene tibi sit, & prolonges dies. Nimirum didicere ex traditione, illud, ut bene tibi sit, intelligendum esse de seculo, quod totum bonum est, & illud, ut prolonges dies, capiendum de seculo, quod totum longum est, at- que hoc est seculum venturum, ut recte Theodor. Hackspan. Orat. de Necess. S. Philol. p. 33. qui ad- dit monitionem perutilem: qui sensum hunc S. Scri- pturæ mysticum esse dicis, cave ignores, penitiora le- gis secreta ipsum Scripturæ sensum à recutitis judi- cari.

Vers. eod. VT SINGULI IN EIS VIVERENT) Vita illa quæ in lege promissa est, longa ac suavi.

Sæpius jam errorem illum Pelagianum & Soci- nisticum notavimus, in lege tantum promissam esse vitam temporalem, ejusque longævitatem ac suavi- tatem. E qua præconcepta opinione hæc Paraphra- sis fluxit. At verbo Dei hîc utrumque tribuitur, & quod vita ipsorum sit, & quod per verbum Dei pro- longari dies super terram possint. Prius ad spirituales promissiones pertinet, & vitam æternam quoque respicit: Posterius ad temporales. Utrumque in V. T. reperiri, imo etiam in ipsa lege, alias probavimus. Nolumus itaque actum nunc agere. Et res evidens est vel è cap. 30. quod dicente B. Franzio Disp. 13. in Deut. velut hesperus, & Lucifer in toto Pentateucho emicat; totumque est Evangelicum, qua pleraque pri- maria, & non tantum explicatio primæ promissionis Genes. 3, 15. hucusque inter Patres conservatæ & pro- pagatæ, sed etiam Scaturigo, unde omnes suas dulcissi- mas consolationes pro consternatis conscientiis hause- runt Prophetæ. Promittit ibi gratuitam miseratio- nem, peccatorum remissionem, conversionem, spi- ritualem circumcisionem, & benedictionem: & quidem ad vitam. Et vers. 6. proponit vitam & mor- tem, benedictionem & maledictionem, ut vita eliga- tur, & vivant Israelitæ v. 19. Quæ præcipue de bene- dictione spirituali & vita æterna intelligenda sunt.
