But if those exceptions have a place, as Grotius wishes, Rahab's speech could be cleared of guilt by the two latter ones; nor would there have been need to take refuge in the distinction of times before the Gospel and under the Gospel, nay, this refuge will be vain and useless, if indeed those exceptions according to the mind of Grotius are for all times.

Latin:

Vers. 4. TOLLENSQVE MULIER VIRUM ABSCONDIT.

Ebræum textum ita reddit Vatablus: Acceperat autem mulier duos illos viros, non alterum tantum ut nugantur Rabbini, sed unumquemque illorum seorsim, ut recte Montanus, ut distributive accipiatur, idiotismo Ebræo. Reddendum in plusquamperfecto verbum: quia ante adventum Regiorum nunciorum, quum vicini de inquisitione instituenda mussitarent sine dubio, eosdem abdiderat.

Vers. eod. NESCIEBAM VNDE ESSENT: CVMQVE PORTA CLAVDERETVR IN TENEBRIS, ET ILLI PARITER EXIERVNT) Ante Evangelium mendacium viris bonis salutare, culpæ non ducebatur. Vide quæ collegimus de Jure Belli ac Pacis libro 3. c. 1. §. 16. Et in Annotatis. Laudatur hoc factum, ut illi tempori congruens, tum dicto ad Hebræos loco, tum Jac. 2, 25.

Mendacia nullo tempore licita fuere. Quicquid legi morali repugnat hodie, repugnavit eidem semper. Evangelium uti non sustulit Legem, ita neque novas leges tulit. Nihil enim aliud est, quam lætum nuncium de remissione peccatorum, & gratia Dei per Christum. Nihil ergo ipsi commercii cum lege. Ante Evangelium de Christo exhibito, vel ante Novi Testamenti tempora nulla ἀνομία, adeoque nulla ἁμαρτία licita erat, nulla non culpæ ducebatur, perinde uti sub Novo Testamento erat. In eo enim nulla figi temporum istorum potest diversitas. Mendacium autem sine dubio est ἀνομία, adeoque ἁμαρτία 1. Joh. 5. vers. 4. Quicquid Deus prohibet & damnat, id citra controversiam, peccatum est. At prohibuit, & damnavit etiam in Vet. Test. omne mendacium Lev. 19. v. 11. Non mentiemini, nec decipiat unusquisque proximum suum. Psal. 5, v. 7. Perdes omnes, qui loquuntur mendacium. Prov. 6, 16. Sex sunt, quæ odit Dominus, & septimum detestatur anima ejus, oculos sublimes, linguam mendacem cap. 12, 22. Labia mendacia abominatur Dominus c. 12, 45. Verbum mendax justus detestabitur. Sap. 1. v. 11. Os, quod mentitur, occidit animam. Eccles. 7. v. 14. Noli velle mentiri omne mendacium. Non habentur clariora interdicta in Novo Testamento. Nec ut nova ibi tradun- tur, sed vicissim repetuntur, & inculcantur. Et agnoscunt Jesuitæ, æquivocationibus alias mendacibus nimis faventes, mendacium ex natura sua peccatum esse, non tantum τῇ θέσει, quod probat Becanus Tomo 2. Opusc. 1. cap. 6. ita inter alia concludens, è Joh. 8, 44. Id cujus primus Autor & inventor est Diabolus, non potest esse nisi malum. Cum è contrario Deus sit Autor omnis boni. Sed Diabolus est Autor & inventor mendacii. E. mendacium non potest esse nisi malum.

Quod ad exemplum Rahabæ, respondet quidem Junius, non necessarium esse, ut mendacium hic tribuatur Rahabæ, Potuisse enim alios apud eam ceu cauponam divertisse, de quibus illa responderit, ut opus fuerit divinæ providentiæ alios hospites receptos indicari ex veritate & alios ex fide & charitate dissimulari: Sed missa illa solutione, si exploratio hostium gravibus pœnis alioquin obnoxia, non tamen improba est adversus hostes Dei, sed receptatio merito etiam celebratur, ut actus fidei, animi scil. πολυθεΐαν, ob audita miracula, abdicantis, quod censet ad v. 1. Grotius, nec improba erit occultatio sive verbis, sive opere ipso facta exploratoribus, qui adversus hostes Dei, & mandato divino emissi sunt. Magis enim est obtemperandum Deo, quam hominibus. Neque veritatis dissimulatio statim pro mendacio habenda est: Et aliud est non dicere veritatem, aliud mentiri, quum in mendacio dolus sit, qui non semper adest, ubi quis veritatem non dicit, Hic certe non ex dolo malo, sed è reverentia Numinis protulit Rahab, quicquid protulit: neque intentione improba, sed justa, servandi Legatos Domini supremi, cujus honorem, gloriam, & auctoritatem omni humanæ ἐξουσία longe anteferendam esse, pietas dictitat. Et nota est vulgaris mendacii distinctio à Lombardo lib. 3. Sent. Dist. 38. quod vel officiosum sit, vel jocosum, vel perniciosum. Quam non pauci sic tuentur, ut solum perniciosum proprie dictum mendacium agnoscant. Officiosum, quando quis falsum dicit aut simulat, non temere aut ex levitate aliqua, aut cum voluntate fallendi vel nocendi, sed quia requirit id DEI honor & salus publica, aut proximi, aut etiam propria, neutiquam pro mendacio veri nominis habeant. Quæ vero nos suo loco relinquimus. Quum enim mendacium per se malum sit, nullo casu bonum id aut licitum fieri posse certum est. Neque quod formaliter & intrinsece vitiosum est, ab externis, fine puta, temporis, loci aut personarum circumstantiis licitum evadere potest. Nam circumstantiæ extrinsecæ non possunt mutare intrinsecam rei naturam. Unde Apostolus docet Rom. 3. v. 5. non esse facienda mala, ut eveniant bona; quia quod ex se malum est, non potest fieri licitum propter intentionem boni finis. Disputant quidem nonnulli quando mentiendo nemini nocemus, nonnullis autem prodesse possumus, aut bonum promovere, licitum id esse. Sicut Plato cum Socrate docuit, Magistratibus, ut Reipubl. medicis, interdum opus esse mendacio libr. 3. de Republ. ac Sophistæ apud Clementem Alexand. l. 2. Stromat. similia tradidisse observantur; neque Priscillianistæ tantum, qui docebant, in corde retinendum esse, quod verum est, oreque ad alienos proferre falsum, nullum esse peccatum: apud August. contra mendac. c. 2. & Origenes mendacia aliquo casu licita propugnavit; sed Chrysostomus etiam lib. de Sacerd. & in cap. 12. & 17. Genes. Officii causa viro bono aliquando mentiendum esse asseruit, nec non Cassianus collat. 17. v. 17. mendacio utendum esse quasi helleboro, ad discrimen aliquod magnum depellendum; Immo communem propemodum hanc fuisse opinionem Augustinus indicat. Quæst. 68. in Levit.

Pene OMNIBUS videtur, quod ubi nemo læditur, pro salute mentiendum est. Abulensis eo etiam abit, q. 30. in Jos. quod Rahab à DEO mota sit ad peccatum veniale mendacium officiosum, & quod mentiri liceat propter magnum aliquod bonum. Sed refragatur Axioma Apostoli Rom. 3. v. 8. Refragatur mendacii natura, quod per se malum est, cadens super indebitam materiam; quia verba instituta sunt, ut recte Durandus lib. 3. Dist. 38. lib. 1. non ut per ea homines se fallant, sed ut cogitationes suas notificent aliis. Indebitus igitur actus est, cum aliquis utitur verbis, ad significandum id, quod non habet in mente. Unde S. Augustinus Enchir. ad Laurentium: Omnis qui mentitur contra id, quod animo sentit, loquitur voluntate fallendi. Et utique verba propterea sunt instituta, non per quæ se invicem homines fallant, sed per quæ in alterius quisque notitiam cogitationes suas proferat. Verbis igitur uti ad fallendum, non ad quod instituta sunt, peccatum est. Digna sunt imprimis quæ hic legantur, quæ Augustinus ex professo hac de re scripsit; Liber nempe ejus de mendacio, & Liber contra mendacium, quorum illius pars magna inquisitionis disputatione versatur, in hoc autem toto aperta sit mendacii oppugnatio, quod ipse monuit lib. 1. Retractat. cap. ultimo. Conferri etiam merentur, quæ Epistol. 8. & 9. ad Hieronymum eam in rem perscripsit Augustinus, siquidem ille in Epistolam ad Gal. 2. docuerit, idque Epistola ad Augustinum scripta defendere laborarit, Petrum à Paulo simulate tantum fuisse reprehensum, ipsumque Petrum simulatione usum esse, quum se subduceret à mensa supervenientibus Judæis. Adfert Augustinus in utramque partem, libro de mendacio ad Consent. scripturæ loca, an id aliquando licitum sit, sed concludit cap. ultimo; Elucet igitur discussis omnibus, nihil aliud illa testimonia hominem monere, nisi nunquam omnino esse mentiendum. Quisquis autem aliquod genus mendacii esse, quod peccatum non sit, putaverit, decipiet seipsum turpiter, cum honestum se deceptorem arbitratur aliorum. Et libr. contra mendacium cap. 1. docet, non licere mentiri, ut hæreticos convertamus. Quomodo igitur mendacio mendacia recte potero prosequi? An & latrocinio latrocinia, & sacrilegio sacrilegia, & adulterio adulteria prosequenda? Si autem veritas Dei in meo mendacio abundaret, nunquid & nos dicturi sumus, faciamus mala, ut eveniant bona &c. Ideo monet in genere cap. 7. Interest quidem plurimum, qua causa, quo fine, qua intentione quid fiat, sed ea, quæ constat esse peccata, nullo bonæ causæ obtentu, nullo quasi bono fine, nulla velut bona intentione facienda sunt. Item: si propterea justa sunt mendacia, quia hoc animo fiunt, ut occulti hæretici destruantur, poterunt isto modo, tantum eodem animo fiant, casta esse adulteria. Quis est qui dicat, ut havitiis, aut testimonia falsa vendamus? Quis ista dicat, nisi qui res humanas, omnesque conatur mores, legesque subvertere? Quod enim sceleratissimum facinus, quod turpissimum flagitium, quod impiissimum Sacrilegium non dicatur posse fieri recte, atque juste, si semel concesserimus, in omnibus malis operibus hominum, non solum quid fiat, sed quare fiat esse quærendum, ut quæcunque propter bonas causas facta reperiuntur, nec ipsa mala esse judicentur. Gemina istis habentur in Enchir. ubi c. 18. quærit, utrum ad officium hominis justi pertineat aliquando mentiri? Quæ tandem cap. 22. ita expediuntur: Nec ideo ullum mendacium putandum est non esse peccatum, quia possumus aliquando alicui prodesse mentiendo. Possumus enim & furando alicui prodesse, si pauper, cui palam datur, sentit commodum, & dives, cui clam tollitur, non sentit incommodum. Nec ideo tale furtum quisquam dixerit non esse peccatum. Possumus & adulterando prodesse, si aliqua, nisi ad hoc ei consentietur, appareat amando moritura, & si vixerit pœnitendo purganda, nec ideo peccatum negabitur tale adulterium. Si autem merito nobis placet castitas, quid quæso offendit veritas, ut propter alienam utilitatem illa non violetur adulterando, & violetur ista mentiendo? Non ideo mendacium poterit aliquando laudari, quia nonnunquam pro salute quorumdam mentiamur. Sententiam Augustini sequuntur alii Patres, Isidorus lib. 2. Sentent. cap. 31. Gregorius M. in lib. 18. Moral. cap. 14. &c. Scholastici Durandus, Bonaventura, Thomas II. 2. qu. 110. Art. 13. Et Pontificii plerique Sotus, Gregorius de Valentia, Becanus & alii. Et acriter merito suo hic Tostatum taxat Cornelius: Falfa illa, inquit, sunt (quæ antea ex Abulensi adducta) & paradoxa. Deus enim nullius peccati potest esse autor, cum sit summa puritas, veritas & sanctitas. Rursum mentiri non licet, etiamsi inde totius mundi salus sequeretur: Non enim sunt facienda mala, ut eveniant bona, nec mendacium necessarium est ad salvandum alterius vitam. Quod autem addit, Potest enim quis in tali casu uti amphibologia, Jesuiticum animum prodit, & cauteritatum. Dolus enim ille æquivocationum non minus illicitus est, quam mendacium, ut alias ostendimus. Nec in eo sibi constat Cornelius, quod modo mulierem rudem, paganam & vafram dicat, modo cordatam admodum fide ac pietate.

Ad exemplum itaque Rahabæ & alia similia respondendum erit, non probari mendacium, neque licitum id tum temporis fuisse, sed laudari in Rahab alia, utpote quod fidem adhibuerit Legatis Dei, eosdem per fidem benevole susceperit, Ebr. 11, 31. occultarit, ac per aliam viam dimiserit Jac. 2. verf. 25. Utitur quidem Augustinus alia responsione cum generali, quod in V. Testamento, non solum dicta, verum etiam facta figurata conscripta sint, quia & figurate gesta: In figuris autem, quod velut mendacium dicitur, bene intellectum, verum inveniatur: libr. contr. mendac. cap. 12. Lib. de mendacio cap. 5. In Vet. Vest. quicquid gestum est, figurate accipi potest, quamvis revera contigerit. Quicquid autem figurate sit ac dicitur, non est mendacium. Omnis enim enunciatio ad id, quod enunciat, referenda. Omne autem factum, aut dictum, aut figuratum hoc enunciat, quod significat iis, quibus intelligendum prolatum est. Tum speciali, quod Rahab tum nondum plane conversa fuerit Cap. 12. Et Rahab quidem ex Hiericho liberata, in Dei populum transitum fecit, ubi proficiens posset ad æterna & immortalia munera pervenire, quæ nullo sunt quærenda mendacio. Tunc tamen, quando illud opus bonum & pro suæ vitæ conditione laudabile Israëlitic exploratoribus præstitit, nondum erat talis, ut ab ea exigeretur, sit in ore vestro est est, & non non. Quod Erasmus vel quisquis marginalia ad Augustinum adjecit, eo interpretatur, quod tolerabilius potuerint mentiri in veteri Lege, quam nova. Sed eam mentem non fuisse Augustino, qui hic solum Rahabæ statum respicit, quod non plene adhuc tum conversa fuerit, manifestum est è libr. de Mendacio c. 5. quum probet ille è V. T. nunquam mentiendum esse, ne pro salute quidem proximi, quoniam in ipso Decalogo scriptum est: Falsum testimonium ne dicas, quo genere, ait, complectitur omne mendacium. Quisquis enim aliquid enunciat, testimonium perhibet animo suo. Sed ne quis contendat, non omne mendacium falsum testimonium esse appellandum, quid dicturus est ad id quod scriptum est (Sap. 1.) os, quod mentitur, occidit animam. Quod ne quis arbitretur de certis aliqui- bus mentientibus posse intelligi, alio loco legat (Ps. 5.) Perdes omnes, qui loquuntur mendacium. Caeterum quia Rahab a fide commendatur in susceptione ex- ploratorum, fides autem locum non habet, nisi in renatis & conversis, rectius sese habet S. Augusti- ni alia Responso, qua utitur libr. contra Mendac. cap. 17. Proinde Rahab in Hiericho, quia peregrinos homines Dei suscepit hospitio, quia in eorum Deum credidit, quia diligenter eos, ubi potuit, occultavit, quia per aliam viam remeandi consilium fidelissimum dedit, etiam supernae Hierusalem civibus imitanda laudatur. Quod autem mentita est, etiamsi aliquid ibi Propheticum intelligenter exponitur, non tamen imitandum sapienter proponitur; Quamvis DEUS memorabiliter illa bona honoraverit, hoc malum cle- menter ingnoverit. Quod explicat cap. 15. quod scri- ptum est: bene Deum fecisse cum Hebraeis obstetrici- bus, & cum Rahab Hierichuntina meretrice, non ideo factum est, quod mentitae sint, sed quod in homines DEI misericordes fuerunt. Non est itaque in eis enumerata fallacia, sed benevolentia; benignitas mentis, non ini- quitas mentientis. Sicut enim malum, absurdumque non esset, si alio prius tempore commissa ab eis aliqua opera mala Deus propter posteriora opera bona vellet ignoscere: Ita mirandum est, quod uno tempore in una causa Deus utrumque conspiciens, id est, factum mise- ricorditer, factumque fallaciter, & bonum remunera- vit, & propter hoc bonum, malum illud ignovit. In- firmitati ergo adscribendum, quod Rahab in an- gustia constituta, quum aliter exploratorum saluti consulere nesciret, mendacio officioso Legatos Dei a praesentissimo periculo liberandos censue- rit, quae ipsi ob fidem gratiose condonata est. Fa- tetur id Lorinus comment. in Epist. Jacob. 2. v. 25. & in eam sententiam adversus Josephum Abba- tem, Chrysostomum item atque Hieronymum addu- cit, cum Augustino & Gregorio M. Thomam & In- nocentium III. Tertullianus lib. de Pudicit. inter de- licta quotidianae incursionis, quibus omnes sumus objecti, ponit necessitate mentiri. Grotius autem hic sibi ipsi adversatur: Nam quum hic ante Evangelium solum mendacia viris bonis salutaria, a culpa absol- vat lib. de jure belli & pacis, etiam sub Evangelio ea- dem culpa in certis casibus vacare adserit: Utpote eum non aegre laturum, qui novit mendacium, imo gratias eo nomine quempiam habiturum, quia volenti non fiat injuria. e. g. Siquis aut aegrotantem amicum persuasione non vera solatur, aut in praelio periclitanti ex falso nuncio animum addit, quo incitatus victoriam & salutem sibi pariat, ac sic deceptus non capiatur: Item, quoties qui habet jus supereminens in omnia ju- ra alterius, eo jure bono ipsius, sive proprio, sive publico utitur: Quo pacto Platonis sententiam exclusat: It. quoties vita innocentis aut par aliquid alteri servari & ab improbi facinoris perfectione aliter averti non potest: Denique quod apud hostem falso sermone uti liceat. Quam exceptionem a Platone, Xenophonte, Philone & Chrysostomo addi observat. Illae vero ex- ceptiones si locum habeant, quemadmodum vult Grotius, e duabus posterioribus a culpa expediri poterit Rahabae sermo; nec opus fuerit ad discri- men temporum ante Evangelium & sub Evangelio confugere, imo κρησφύγετον hoc vanum atque inutile erit, siquidem exceptiones illae juxta men- tem Grotii omnium sunt temporum.

## 2:9
V. 9. I KNOW THAT THE LORD HAS GIVEN YOU THE LAND.

If the force of the past tense is retained, it is to be understood as having given regarding dominion, although He had not yet given regarding possession, as Bonfrerius wishes: or as having given regarding the decree, because He decreed to give, not regarding the act; as having given in promise, although not yet in actual concession. But Lyranus, Abulensis, and Magalianus prefer to understand the past for the future; not badly, both on account of the certainty of the thing and on account of the actual tradition now imminent, concerning which there was certain faith, not from signs only, although these did serve to strengthen faith, such as the fear of their own people, the dejection of spirit, despair, the fame of the divided Red Sea, the suffocated army of Egypt, and the kings and peoples conquered and cut down beyond the Jordan from the Amorites. If it be asked in what language the spies spoke with Rahab? Bonfrerius, and Cornelius with Serarius, answer that the language of the Canaanites was either the same as the Hebrew, or not very different, which they prove from the name Beersheba imposed on the place equally by Abraham and the Canaanites, Gen. 21, and the proper names of the Canaanites, Melchizedek, Adonizedek, Adonibezek, Abimelech, Rahab, as also of the cities Jericho, Salem, Shechem, Bethlehem, Segor, etc. But it is doubtful whether those names are of the Canaanite language, concerning which we spoke at Gen. 11, verse 1. If that tradition is true, that that land fell to Shem of old, which Jacob of Edessa, Moses bar Cepha, Serapion the Abbot, Augustine, and Epiphanius, heresy 66, admit, it would not be a wonder that Hebrew names prevailed there, even if the Canaanites did not use that language thereafter, the descendants of Shem having been expelled. But the Canaanite language in Is. 19:18 is not the Hebrew language, but the religion which flourished in Canaan, because the whole worship is expressed by the name of language and confession. Nor is there need that we assume this hypothesis for the sake of the spies: for since Moses and Joshua knew that that land was to be given to them, it is likely that they took pains that some should apply themselves solely to the language of the Canaanites; And who would doubt that in such a great assembly of Israelites there were some skilled in languages who could be employed? Philo the Hebrew indeed says that Caleb's sons, Cenez and Seeniajam, were employed, whose parent had also been sent there 38 years before, not ignorant of the Canaanite language: which could be learned all the more easily by the Hebrews if, as seems to some, those peoples used that Syriac idiom.

Latin:

V. 9. NOVI, QVOD DOMINUS TRADI- DERIT VOBIS TERRAM.

Si praeteriti vis retineatur, tradidisse intellige- tur quoad dominium, licet nondum tradidetit quoad possessionem, ut vult Bonfrerius: vel tradidisse quoad decretum, quia decrevit tradere, non quoad actum; tradidisse in promissione, licet nondum in actuali concessione. Sed Lyranus, Abulensis, Magalianus malunt præteritum pro futuro intelligere; non male tum ob rei certitudinem, tum ob imminentem jam actualem traditionem, de qua fide certa fuit, non ex signis tantum, licet hæc ad fidem firmandam fecerint, utpote suorum pavor, animi dejectio, desperatio, fama divisi maris rubri, suffocati exercitus Ægypti, devictorum, & excisorum regum ac populorum trans Jordanem ex Amorrhæis. Si quæratur qua lingua collocuti cum Rahabe exploratores sint? respondet Bonfrerius, & Cornelius cum Serario, linguam Chananæorum vel eandem fuisse cum Ebræa, vel non admodum diversam, quod è nomine Bersabee ab Abrahamo & Cananæis pariter loco imposito Gen. 21. & propriis Cananæorum nominibus Melchisedech, Adonisedech, Adonibezec, Abimelech, Rahab, ut & urbium Hiericho, Salem, Sichem, Bethlehem, Segar &c. probant. Sed nomina ista linguæ Canonicæ esse, dubium est, quo de ad Gen. 11. vers. 1. diximus. Si vera ista traditio, quod Semo terra illa obtigerit olim, quam Jacob Edessenus, Moses Bar Cephe, Serapion Abbas, August. & Epiph. hær. 66. admittunt, mirum non fuerit, Ebræa nomina illic obtinuisse, etiamsi Cananæi ea lingua deinceps usi non fuerint, expulsis Semi posteris. Lingua vero Cananæa Es. 19, 18. non est lingua Ebræa, sed religio, quæ in Cananæa viguit, quia linguæ & confessionis nomine cultus totus exprimitur. Neque opus est, ut exploratorum causa hanc hypothesin assumamus: nam quum Moses & Josua sceiverint, terram illam ipsis tradendam esse, verisimile est, operam dedisse, ut aliqui solum linguæ Cananæorum incumberent; Et quis ambiget in tanto Israëlitarum cœtu quosdam linguarum peritos fuisse, qui adhiberi potuerint? Philo quidem Ebræus, Calebi filios Cenez, & Seeniamjam adhibitos fuisse, ait, quorum parens ante 38. ann. etiam eo missus erat, non ignarus Cananææ linguæ: quæ eo facilius ab Ebræis disci potuit, si quod nonnullis videtur, Syriaco illi populi usi fuere idomate.

## 2:12
Vers. 12. SWEAR TO ME) In such matters, which do not violate the public state, those sent by the people bind the people. Wherefore this faith was also kept below 6:25. For a similar history see Jud. 1:25.

Latin:

Vers. 12. JURATE MIHI) In talibus, quæ publicum statum non violant missi a populo populum obstringunt. Quare & servata hæc est fides infra 6, 25. Matth. 1, 5. similem historiam vide Jud. 1, 25.

## 2:17
Vers. 17. WE SHALL BE INNOCENT OF THIS OATH WHICH YOU HAVE MADE US SWEAR) Whose words you have set before us, ὧ ὥρκισας ἡμᾶς, Theodotion. See what is at Levit. 5, 1. & Matth. 26, 23. We shall be innocent, unless you perform those agreements which will now follow, added immediately. Similar is that exception of Pylades in Euripides' Iphigenia in Tauris: Grant me this exception, if the ship should suffer anything and the tablet should vanish in the surge of the waves, but I should save my body alone, that the oath should no longer be binding.

Latin:

Vers. 17. INNOXII ERIMUS A JVRAMENTO HOC QVO ADJVRASTI NOS) Cujus verba nobis præivisti, ὧ ὥρκισας ἡμᾶς, Theodotion. Vide quæ ad Levit. 5, 1. & Matth. 26, 23. Innoxii erimus, nisi ea, quæ jam sequentur, pacta in continenti adjecta præstes. Similis illa exceptio Pyladæ in Taurica Iphigenia Euripidis: Ἐξαίρετόν μοι δὸς τόδ' ἤν τι ναῦς πάθῃ Χ' ἡ δέλτος ἐν κλύδωνι χρημάτων μετὰ Ἀφανὴς γένηται, σῶμα δ' ἐκσώσω μόνον Τὸν ὅρκον εἶναι τὸν δὲ μηκέτ' ἔμπεδον.

## 2:19
Vers. 19. WHOEVER SHALL HAVE GONE OUT OF THE DOOR OF YOUR HOUSE HIS BLOOD SHALL BE UPON HIS HEAD) By the law of war, those who do not separate themselves from the resistors in a captured city fall.

Latin:

Vers. 19. QVI OSTIUM DOMUS TUÆ EGRESSUS FUERIT SANGVIS IPSIUS ERIT IN CAPUT EJVS) Jure belli cadunt qui in urbe capta a resistentibus se non abjungunt.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III. The crossing of the Jordan.

Latin:

CAPUT III. Transitus per Jordanem.

## 3:4
Vers. 4. AND THERE SHALL BE BETWEEN YOU AND THE ARK A SPACE OF TWO THOUSAND CUBITS) Compare Num. 2, 2. Since one ought to go from the camps to the ark especially on Sabbaths, from this the wise men took the argument for defining the Sabbath day's journey, which is not defined in the law itself. Among labors are long journeys, which it was sufficiently agreed were not permitted on the Sabbath, Matth. 24, 20. Ovid: -- force your unwilling feet to run. Nor wish for rain: nor let foreign Sabbaths delay you. To forbid every departure would have been harsh: and that this was not the meaning of the law concerning the Sabbath, was evident from this law. See Acts 1, 12.

Two thousand cubits, that is, three thousand feet, or five stadia, which make 625 paces, is noted by Josephus, book 20 of the Antiquities, chapter 6, to be the Sabbath day's journey. This interval, partly for the sake of reverence, partly so that all might more conveniently behold the ark and the miracle of the Jordan divided by itself from afar with joy, as Augustine notes in question 3; indeed, Joshua himself hints at it, so that you might see from afar and know the way by which you should enter. Therefore, the pillar of cloud did not go before any longer, as the interpreters note with Augustine. In vain has R. Solomon imagined here that besides the ark of the covenant, the ark containing the bones of Joseph also went before. Which is neither consistent (for the holiness of the ark of the covenant did not bear that proximity on account of the uncleanness of the dead) nor does it agree with the text.

Latin:

Vers. 4. SITQVE INTER VOS ET ARCAM SPATIUM CVBITORVM DVVM MILLIVM) Confer Num. 2, 2. Cum e castris ad arcam Sabbatis maxime iri deberet, hinc sumsere argumentum sapientes definiendi iter Sabbati in ipsa lege non definitum. Inter labores sunt magna itinera, quæ non permitti Sabbato satis constabat, Matth. 24, 20. Ovidius: -- invitos currere coge pedes. Nec pluvias opta: nec te peregrina morentur Sabbata. Omnem egressum vetare, durum fuerat: nec eum sensum esse legis de Sabbato, ex hac lege constabat. Vide Act. 1, 12.

DUo millia cubitorum, id est, tria millia pe- dum, vel quinque Stadia, quæ efficiunt 625. passus, iter Sabbati esse notat Josephus l. 20. Antiq. cap. 6. Quod interstitium partim reverentiæ causa, partim ut omnes commodius arcam & miraculum divisi per se am Jordanis eminus cum gaudio spe- ctarent, ut notat August. q. 3. imo Josua ipse in- nuit, ut procul videre possitis & nosse viam, per quam ingrediamini. Non ergo præivit amplius columna nubis, ut notant cum Augustino Interpp. Frustra hic R. Salomo finxit præter arcam fœde- ris etiam arcam continentem ossa Josephi præiisse. Quod nec consentaneum est, (non enim sanctitas arcæ fœderis ob immunditiem defunctorum eam viciniam ferebat,) nec textui congruit.

## 3:5
Verse 5. SANCTIFY YOURSELVES, FOR TOMORROW THE LORD WILL DO WONDERS AMONG YOU.

He demands not only outward sanctification or purification, which was done by washing clothes and abstaining from wives, but primarily inward holiness: that they should adhere to divine promises by faith, place their hope in God, and strive for true holiness of life.

Cornelius observes here that Joshua commanded the priests as a Prophet, not as a Prince, because the care of walls is committed to the Emperor, and the care of sacred things to the Bishop, according to Ambrose, Epistle 13 to Marcellus. Although it is certain that Joshua did these things by divine instinct, he did not do them as a Prophet, much less as a Bishop or Priest (an office he never held), but as an Emperor; nor is the care of sacred things to be so restricted to the Bishop that the Emperor is entirely excluded even from external governance. For he is, as Constantine used to say, a Bishop outside the Church, as far as external direction is concerned, although he is not a Bishop inside the Church, as far as the preaching of the word and the administration of the Sacraments are concerned, which is the proper care and function of Priests and Bishops.

Concerning the day of the crossing, it must be noted that it was the tenth of the month of Nisan. Therefore, the third day of the παρασκευῆς having passed, as the Hebrew text has in verse 2, toward the evening of the ninth day the heralds proclaimed the crossing and the manner of crossing. On the following day, the crossing was instituted. For since Joshua seems to have been confirmed in his office by a divine voice on the third of Nisan, after the days of mourning instituted for Moses had passed, and on that same day, as some believe and it appears likely, the spies were sent, and they sufficiently perceived from Rahab the fear and the state of the city upon their arrival, so that they had no need to spend the whole following day on exploration, as some believe with Josephus (for thus they would have exposed themselves to danger), they were let down that same night after their arrival and remained hidden for three days in the mountains, because the territory of Jericho is surrounded on all sides by mountains, according to Adrichomius, that is, on the fourth, fifth, and sixth days of Nisan, toward the evening of which they returned to Joshua, whence on the seventh, eighth, and ninth following days, the preparation for the crossing was immediately made: where indeed on the morning of the seventh day Joshua had moved the camp to the Jordan from Shittim, and had proclaimed by a herald that all should prepare themselves for the crossing, which would take place after three days. Therefore, it is not to be maintained with the Hebrews that Joshua departed from Shittim only on the morning of the ninth day: which the three days of preparation in chapter 1, verse 11, do not admit. Which began with the departure from Shittim: Whence those three days, the end of which is noted in chapter 3, verse 2, are not different from the three days already mentioned, as Bonfrerius rightly observes.

Latin:

Vers. 5. SANCTIFICAMINI, CRAS ENIM FACIET DOMINUS INTER VOS MIRABILIA.

Non tantum exteriorem sanctificationem vel lustrationem, quæ fiebat lavando vestes & ab- stinendo ab uxoribus, sed imprimis interiorem sanctitatem postulat: ut fide divinis promissis ad- hæreant, spem in Deum collocent & veræ sancti- tati vitæ studeant.

Observat hic Cornelius, Josuam ut Prophe- tam Sacerdotibus imperasse, non ut Principem, quia Imperatori cura murorum, Episcopo cura Sa- crorum commissa est juxta Ambrosium Epist. 13. ad Marcell. Quanquam vero Josuam divino instin- ctu hæc egisse certum sit, non tamen ut Propheta, nedum Episcopus, aut Sacerdos, (quo officio functus nunquam fuit) hæc egit, sed ut Imperator, nec ita sacrorum cura ad Episcopum restringenda est, ut prorsus etiam ab externo regimine exclu- datur Imperator. Est enim, ut Constantinus aje- bat, Episcopus extra Ecclesiam, quoad externam di- rectionem, licet non sit Episcopus intra Ecclesiam, quoad verbi prædicationem, & Sacramentorum administrationem, quæ cura & functio Sacerdo- tum & Episcoporum propria est.

De die transitus monendum, quod fuerit de- cimus mensis Nisan. Tertio ergo die παρασκευῆς exacto, ut Ebræus textus v. 2. habet, sub vesperam diei nonæ præcones transitum & modum transe- undi proclamarunt. Sequenti autem die institutus est transitus. Nam quum tertio Nisan videatur Josua, post exactos dies luctus ob Mosen instituti, ad officium, divina voce, confirmatus, eodemque statim die, ut nonnulli credunt, & verisimile ap- paret, exploratores missi sint, ac satis ex Rachabe metum, statumque urbis, sub adventum suum, per- ceperint, ut non opus habuerint sequentem totum diem, quod nonnulli cum Josepho credunt, explora- tioni insumere (sic enim periculo se exposuissent) eadem nocte post adventum demissi & dimissi per triduum in montanis, quia ager Jericho undique montanis circumdatus, Adrichomio teste, latue- runt, hoc est quarto, quinto & sexto die Nisan, sub cujus vesperam reversi ad Josuam sunt, unde septi- mo, octavo & nono sequentibus diebus, statim fa- cta ad transitum præparatio: ubi nempe mane diei septimæ Josua castra ad Jordanem è Setim mo- visset, & per præconem edixisset, ut se ad transi- tum, post tres dies futurum, omnes præparent. Non ergo cum Ebræis statuendum, quod mane nonæ demum diei egressus de Setim Josua sit: quod non admittit triduum præparationis cap. 1. versu 11. Quod cœpit cum egressu è Setim: Unde tres illi dies, quorum finis notatur cap. 3. vers. 2. non sunt alii à triduo jam dicto, ut recte observat Bonfrerius.

## 3:7
Verse 7. I WILL BEGIN TO EXALT THEE BEFORE ALL ISRAEL) From the times of Moses to the times of Saul, God showed, either by miracles or by deeds exceeding human hope, whom He wished to be the Princes of His people. See below 4, 14, and passim in the book of Judges.

The reason was that God Himself ruled His people at that time, whence this state is deservedly called theocracy or theokratia; when they rejected the rule of GOD and sought a King after the manner of the nations, or a monarchy, that designation of the Rulers or Judges of the people by miracles and other singular deeds ceased.

Latin:

Vers. 7. INCIPIAM EXALTARE TE CORAM OMNI ISRAELE) A Mosis temporibus ad Saulis tempora, Deus aut miraculis, aut factis humanam spem excedentibus monstrabat, quos Principes esse populi sui vellet. Vide infra 4, 14. & passim in Judicum libro.

Causa erat, quod tum Deus ipse rexerit populum suum, unde hic status merito ϑεαρχία vel ϑεοκρατεία dicitur: quum regimen DEI rejicerent, ac Regem more gentium, vel μοναρχίαν expeterent, cessavit illa per miracula & alia singularia facta Rectorum vel Judicum populi designatio.

## 3:8
Verse 8. TO THE PRIESTS WHO CARRY THE ARK.

That was the duty of the Levites, and was entrusted to the Kohathites, Numbers 4, verse 15, but when it was done for a mere ministry: here, however, the ark was to be carried on account of the miracle, or the celebration of the matter to be performed, indeed on account of the manifestation of God present at the ark through the miracle of the dried-up Jordan, which is not to be attributed to the ark itself with Cornelius, who draws here the error of the Vulgate, Psalm 97:5, adore the footstool of his feet, that is, the ark: nor to the Priests, but to God there peculiarly present, inasmuch as he alone does wonders, Psalm 72, last verse.

Verse the same. WHEN YOU SHALL HAVE ENTERED THE PART OF THE WATER OF THE JORDAN.

In Hebrew it is קצה, which Cornelius absurdly interprets as the middle, since it denotes the extremity, nor does Masius understand it conveniently as the further bank. How could the Priests cross the Jordan and stand at its extremity near the opposite bank before the river was dried up: must a new miracle be invented thus? Others, however, rightly with Serarius judge that the nearer bank is meant, because then the Priests placed the soles of their feet in the waters of the Jordan, as is held in verse 13. (in Hebrew it is, when the soles of the feet shall have been able [to rest] in the waters of the Jordan, so that rest and a station may be indicated, the waters flow down) whence, lest we convert the extremity into the middle, with Bonfrerius and Serarius two stations of the Priests carrying the ark must be brought forward, one on the nearer bank itself, and at the first touch of the water, until the lower waters gradually flowed down, soon as the middle channel dried up, they gradually moved themselves into the middle of the channel, the ark placed opposite to hold back and suspend the upper waters into a stable mass, until the whole people had crossed: so that the other station of them was in the middle of the river, of which verse 17 and chapter 4, 3.

Latin:

Vers. 8. SACERDOTIBUS QVI PORTANT ARCAM.

Id Levitarum erat, & Caathitis demandatum Numer. 4. vers. 15. sed cum ad nudum ministerium fiebat: hic vero portanda arca ob miraculi, vel rei peragendæ celebritatem, imo ob Dei ad arcam præsentis per miraculum siccati Jordanis manifestationem, quod non arcæ ipsi tribuendum cum Cornelio, qui huc errorem Vulgatæ Psal. 97, 5. adorate scabellum pedum ejus, id est arcam, trahit: nec Sacerdotibus, sed Deo illic peculiariter præsenti, utpote qui mirabilia facit solus Psal. 72. vers. ult.

Vers. eod. CUM INGRESSI FUERITIS PARTEM AQUÆ JORDANIS.

In Ebr. est קצה quod absurde Cornelius de medio interpretatur, quum extremitatem notet, neque convenienter Masius de ulteriori ripa intelligit. Quomodo transire Jordanem & in extremitate ejus juxta adversam ripam stare poterant Sacerdotes, priusquam siccaretur fluvius: num novum sic fingendum miraculum? recte autem alii cum Serario citeriorem ripam notari censent, quia tum posuere Sacerdotes vestigia pedum suorum in aquis Jordanis, ut habetur v. 13. (in Ebræo est, cum quiverint plantæ pedum in aquis Jordanis, ut quies & statio indicetur, aquæ decurrent) unde ne extremum in medium convertamus, cum Bonfrerio & Serario duæ Sacerdotum arcæ bajulorum afferendæ sunt stationes, una in ipsa ripa citeriore, & primo attactu aquæ, donec paulatim aquæ inferiores decurrerent, mox alveo medio exarescente sensim sese in medium alveum immisisse, arca opposita in molem stabilem superiores aquas coërcituros, ac suspensuros, donec totus populus transmisisset: ut altera ipsorum statio in medio flumine fuerit, de qua v. 17. & c. 4, 3.

## 3:10
Verse 10. AND THE AMORITE.

There were already two Amorite Kings in the Eastern land across the Jordan, Num. 32, 33, Deut. 3, 12, 13, but there was still some part of the Amorites in the western region of the Jordan, to which the Israelites were now about to cross.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET AMORRHÆUM.

Erant jam duo Amorrhæi Reges in terra Orientali trans Jordanem deleti. Num. 32, 33. Deuter. 3, 12. 13. sed fuit adhuc pars aliqua Amorrhæorum in occidua Jordanis regione, ad quam nunc Israëlitæ transituri erant.

## 3:11
Verse 11. BEHOLD THE ARK OF THE COVENANT OF THE LORD OF ALL THE EARTH.

Masius wrongly renders it by apposition, the ark of the covenant the Lord, nor does the Tarcha accent help him, for it does not serve the distinctions. More correctly the Chaldean, the LXX, Jerome, Pagninus, Arias, the Tigurines, Luther, and others [render it] in the genitive, the ark of the covenant of the Lord: for it is clearly unusual that this ark should be called the Lord, and if anywhere that appellation should seem to be deferred to the ark, the words are directed not to it, but to God sitting upon the ark, as Bonfrerius rightly [notes] at this place.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ECCE ARCA FOEDERIS DOMINI OMNIS TERRÆ.

Male reddit per appositionem Masius arca fœderis Dominus, nec Accentus Tarcha ipsum juvat, non enim servit distinctionibus. Rectius Chaldæus LXX. Hieronymus, Pagninus, Arias, Tigurini, Lutherus, & alii in regimine, arca fœderis Domini: nam plane insolens est, ut arca hæc Dominus appelletur, & sicubi ea appellatio arcæ videretur deferri, non ad illam, sed ad Deum arcæ insidentem verba diriguntur, ut recte Bonfrerius h. l.

## 3:12
Verse 12. PREPARE TWELVE MEN.

Cajetan thinks these are others than those who are noted in ch. 4, v. 2, because the word CHOOSE is used there. But in the Hebrew it is, take: therefore no election is made there; but those who were chosen are called, and what is to be done by them is specifically set forth, and thus they are the same in both cases. However, it seems doubtful whether the stone was also taken up for the tribe of Levi? Which we think must be affirmed, because those stones were meant to be a memorial of all the tribes, just as the 12 stones in the breastplate of the High Priest, Ex. 28, 9 seqq., in which the Levitical tribe does not seem to be excluded.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PARATE DUODECIM VIROS.

Cajetanus alios hos esse putat ab illis, qui c. 4. v. 2. notantur, quia ibi habetur verbum ELIGE. Sed in Ebræo est, accipite: ideo non electio ibi fit; sed qui electi erant advocantur, & quid ipsi agendum, specialiter exponitur, adeoque iidem utrobique sunt. Dubium autem videtur, an etiam pro tribu Levi lapis sublatus sit? quod affirmandum putamus, quia lapides illi debebant memoriale esse omnium tribuum, quemadmodum & 12. lapides in pectorali summi Sacerdotis Ex. 28, 9. seqq. in quibus non videtur exclusa Levitica tribus.

## 3:15
Ver. 15. BUT THE JORDAN HAD FILLED THE BANKS OF ITS CHANNEL AT THE TIME OF HARVEST.

In the Hebrew: And the Jordan was being filled, that is, it was overflowing over all its banks at the time of the new fruits, so that it did not only fill the banks, but overflowed over all the banks, as Masius and Vatablus render it. The time of harvest began there in Nisan. Exod. 13, 4. Lev. 23, 10. Deut. 16, 1. Jos. 5, v. 11, of which month it was then the tenth day. At which time the Jordan was accustomed to overflow, because melted snows from the neighboring mountains poured themselves into it. Hence the miracle of the drying up was greater. For the crossing was made a little above the mouth of the Jordan, where it flowed in a very wide and very deep channel, and at the time of harvest it filled both banks and went out, 1 Par. 22. Syr. 24. Concerning this river, let those things be seen which are at Num. 33, 51.

Latin:

Vers. 15. JORDANIS AUTEM RIPAS ALVEI SUI TEMPORE MESSIS IMPLEVERAT.

In Ebr. Et Jordanis implebatur, id est, exundabat super omnes ripas suas tempore novarum frugum, ut non impleverit tantum ripas, sed super omnes ripas exundaverit, ut Masius & Vatablus reddunt. Tempus messis a Nisan incipiebat ibidem. Exod. 13, 4. Lev. 23, 10. Deut. 16, 1. Jos. 5. v. 11. cujus mensis dies tunc erat decimus. Quo tempore solebat Jordanis exundare, quod a montibus vicinis nives liquatæ se in eum effunderent. Inde majus erat exiccationis miraculum. Factus enim transitus est paulo supra ostium Jordanis, ubi latissimo & profundissimo alveo fluebat, & messis tempore utramque ripam implebat, & egrediebatur 1. Par. 22. Syr. 24. De hoc fluvio videantur quæ ad Num. 33, 51.

## 3:16
Ver. 16. THE WATERS STOOD) Why is that which is usually attributed more to God not easy for God? Ovid: And by art he turns back the liquid waters to their source. Lucan: - - - the torrent hung fixed from the severed cliff, and the river ran not where it was inclined.

What do these poetic or magical things have to do with divine things, which are specifically noted by the Spirit of God as signal miracles of divine power, which alone performs miracles? How a demon may indeed emulate divine miracles, but delude its own worshippers with mere tricks, is not for us to recount, and it is very well known to all. Therefore, magic and divine things are as far apart as heaven and earth.

Ver. same. THE WATERS STOOD DESCENDING IN ONE PLACE AND LIKE A SWELLING MOUNTAIN FAR FROM THE CITY WHICH IS CALLED ADOM EVEN TO THE PLACE SARTHAN.

In the Hebrew: And the waters descending stood, they stood from above in one heap very far from the city Adom, which is from the side of Sarthan: so that that heap of waters appeared raised like a mountain from the place of the crossing, which is thence called Bethabara, i.e., house of the crossing, or even swelled in a continuous series as far as the city Adom, which has Sarthan as a neighbor on its side, that is, as far as the lake of Gennesaret. 1 Reg. 4, v. 12, which is a distance of twenty leagues or hours. See Masius in this place. Compare Jos. 15, 4.

IN THE SEA OF THE WILDERNESS) Rather the sea of the plain, which succeeded into the place of the fields. For ערבה araba, which is placed here, signifies flat places, the uninhabited plain of Aquila, yet not sterile: for in them fodder is born, which is called mixture.

Jerome more often translates this sea of the wilderness: which is also rendered by Symmachus: sea of the uninhabited, sea of the desert, or of the uninhabitable place: the Septuagint and Theodotion retain the Hebrew word araba. Jerome also interprets araboth sometimes as plain and level ground. And the Hebrew word signifies both not only a plain or level ground, but also a wilderness and desert, whence the name Arabia, which is also called desert. Now this sea is the Asphaltite lake, into which Sodom or the Pentapolis was turned after the heavenly fire,

and it is called the dead sea, because no animal lives in it, which also touches the desert of Sin, and is truly a sea of the wilderness, since it nourishes no living animal, nor can anything dwell near it because of the foul smell: although it can also rightly be called the sea of the plain or of the flat land, because it filled all that most pleasant plain in which the Pentapolis once was. In this sea, therefore, the Jordan flows and is absorbed by it, it is plain from this place, whence Bochart was hallucinating when he determined that the waters of the Jordan are not mixed with the dead sea, but are absorbed before they arrive there, and that the Jordan is a league away from it. But if it were so, what need would there have been for the drying up of the Jordan, since the crossing lay open there by land? Pliny also teaches that the Jordan flows into the dead sea, l. 5, cap. 15, as also Jerome in his book of Hebrew places and Epistol. 28 to Lucinus and cap. 47 of Ezekiel, and also Adrichomius.

Latin:

Vers. 16. STETERUNT AQUÆ) Quidni Deo facile quod magis tribui solet? Ovidius: Inque caput liquidas arte recurvat aquas. Lucanus: - - - de rupe pependit Abscissa fixus torrens, amnisque cucurrit Non qua pronus erat.

Quid hæc Poetica aut Magica ad divina, a Spiritu Dei, ceu insignia miracula divinæ virtutis, quæ sola facit miracula, peculiariter notata? Quomodo Dæmon æmuletur quidem divina miracula, sed cultores suos meris præstigiis eludat, nostrum non est recensere, & notissimum est omnibus. Toto ergo cœlo magica a divinis distant.

Vers. eod. STETERUNT AQUÆ DESCENDENTES IN LOCO UNO ET AD INSTAR MONTIS INTUMESCENTIS PROCUL AB URBE QUÆ VOCATUR ADOM USQVE AD LOCUM SARTHAN.

In Ebræo: Et steterunt aquæ descendentes, desuper steterunt acervo uno procul valde ab urbe Adom, quæ ex latere Sarthan: ut acervus ille aquarum instar montis elatus a loco trajectus, qui inde Bethabara dictus est, h. e. domus transitus, apparuerit, vel etiam continua serie intumuerit usque ad urbem Adom, quæ ex latere Sarthan vicinam habet, hoc est, usque ad lacum Genezareth. 1. Reg. 4. v. 12. quod est spatium viginti leucarum seu horarum. Vid. Masius h. l. Conf. Jos. 15, 4.

IN MARE SOLITUDINIS) Mare campestre potius, quod camporum in locum successit. Nam ערבה ἄραβα quod hic ponitur, loca significat plana, πεδινὴν ἀοίκητον Aquilæ, non tamen sterilia: in iis enim pabulum nascitur, quod μίγμα dicitur.

Mare hoc solitudinis sæpius vertit Hieronymus: quod etiam a Symmacho: θάλασσα τῆς ἀοικήτου redditur, mare deserti, seu loci inhabitabilis: Septuaginta & Theodotio vocem Ebræam ἄραβα retinent. Interpretatur & Hieronymus ערבוֹת quandoque planitiem & campestria. Et significat utrumque vox Ebræa non solum planitiem vel campestria, sed etiam solitudinem ac desertum, unde nomen Arabia, quæ deserta etiam dicitur. Est autem mare hoc lacus Asphaltites, in quem Sodoma vel Pentapolis conversa fuit post cœleste incendium,

& vocatur mare mortuum, quod nullum animal in eo vivat, quod & desertum Sin attingit, & vere solitudinis mare est, quum nullum animal vivum alat, nec juxta illud quicquam ob graveolentiam commorari possit: quamvis etiam recte mare campestre vel planitiei dici possit, quod totam illam planitiem amoenissimam, in qua Pentapolis olim fuit, oppleverit. In hoc ergo mare Jordanem illabi, & ab eo absorberi, ex hoc loco planum est, unde hallucinatus est Bochardus, cum statuit, aquas Jordanis mari mortuo non admisceri, sed absorberi, priusquam eo perveniant, & leuca ab eo abesse Jordanem. Quod si ita haberet, quid opus fuisset exsiccatione Jordanis, quum transitus illac terra pateret? Influere Jordanem in mare mortuum etiam Plinius docet l. 5. cap. 15. ut & Hieronymus de locis Hebraic. & Epistol. 28. ad Lucin. & cap. 47. Ezech. nec non Adrichomius.

## 3:17
Ver. 17. BUT THE PEOPLE WERE MARCHING AGAINST JERICHO.

Opposite Jericho. For it was before their eyes as they were crossing. This place was named from this crossing of the Israelites, where John is read to have baptized, John 1:28. Whence, since the crossing of the Jordan prefigured baptism, as Augustine teaches, Sermon 106 de Temp., Jesus Christ, the antitype of Joshua, wished to descend into the Jordan, inasmuch as he leads the faithful through baptism into the promised heavenly inheritance. It is called in Judges 7:24 Beth-barah, the house of corn: which Adrichomius and Bunting indeed wish to be different from Bethabara, where John baptized, judging this one to be situated beyond the Jordan, but he who first baptized preached in the wilderness properly so called of Judea, the borders of which did not extend beyond the Jordan: for it is gathered from Luke 1:40 that Father Zacharias lived in that region. Therefore, those who came to John are said to have come to the Jordan, with no mention ever made of a crossing of the Jordan by them. Whence Jerome in his Hebrew places calls this place Bethabara, where John baptized unto repentance, and Arias Montanus teaches it to be the same as that in Judges 7:24.

THEY STOOD UPON DRY GROUND IN THE MIDST OF THE JORDAN.

If the priests stood there until the people crossed, how could they go before the people at an interval of two thousand cubits, which they were commanded to do in verse 4? Indeed, how did this interval have a place in that crossing, if the width of this river was not 2000 cubits, as Masius opines, but, as Serarius teaches in part 2, chapter 3, question 3, ordinarily only thirty cubits? We think, with Bonfrerius, that it must be said that the Israelites did not cross the riverbed there where the priests were standing and had the mountain of waters suspended on their right, but a little to the left, further down, where the riverbed had already dried up, at that interval, namely, of 2000 cubits, because it was not fitting, or consistent with the divine command, for the Israelites crossing the riverbed to pass near the ark; or certainly it must be established that this interval was to be observed by them only in the progress, not in the actual crossing of the Jordan.

ARMED.

The Hebrew חלוצים, the LXX, Aquila, and Symmachus render it 'prepared to cross.' Masius, 'by preparing, namely, the crossing for the people': others, 'rightly, and thus, as they had begun,' to which the translation of B. Luther agrees. For the verbs of the Hiphil infinitive are often taken as adverbs, see Hos. 5, 2. ch. 9, 9. Jon. 4, 4. whence to strengthen is the same as firmly, with fixed foot, as is evident from ch. 4, verse 3.

Latin:

Vers. 17. POPULUS AUTEM INCEDEBAT CONTRA JERICHO.

Ex adverso Jericho. Erat enim illis transeuntibus ante oculos. Dictus hic locus est ab hoc transitu Israelitarum, ubi baptizasse legitur Johannes Joh. 1, 28. unde quum transitus Jordanis baptismum praefiguravit, docente August. Serm. 106. de Temp. Jesus Christus Josuae antitypus in Jordanem descendere voluit, utpote qui per baptismum fideles traducit in promissam haereditatem caelestem. Vocatur Jud. 7. vers. 24. Bethbera domus frumenti: quam Adrichom. quidem & Bunting. diversam esse volunt a Bethabara, ubi Johannes baptizavit hanc trans Jordanem sitam esse, censentes, sed πρωτοβαπτισης in eremo proprie dicta Judaeae praedicavit, cujus fines ultra Jordanem non pertinebant: nam in eo tractu Patrem Zachariam habitasse e Luc. 1, 40. colligitur. Ideo qui ad Johannem veniebant, venisse επι τον Ιορδανην dicuntur, nusquam facta trajecti ab eis Jordanis mentione. Unde Hieronymus in locis Hebraicis hunc locum Bethabara dicit, ubi Johannes in poenitentiam baptizavit, & Arias Montanus eundem esse cum illo Jud. 7, 24. docet.

STABANT SUPER SICCAM HUMUM IN MEDIO JORDANIS.

Si Sacerdotes illic stabant, donec populus transiret, quomodo ad interstitium cubitorum duum millium praeire potuere populum, quod jussi sunt vers. 4. imo quomodo hoc interstitium locum in isto transitu habuit, siquidem latitudo hujus fluminis non fuerit 2000. cubitorum, uti opinatur Masius, sed ut Serarius parte 2. c. 3. q. 3. docet, ordinarie tantum triginta cubitorum. Existimamus, cum Bonfrerio dicendum esse Israelitas non illac alveum transiisse, ubi Sacerdotes consistebant, & a dextris aquarum montem suspensum habebant, sed paulo a sinistris inferius, ubi alveus jam exaruerat, intervallo scil. isto 2000. cubitorum, quia conveniens non erat, aut mandato divino consentaneum Israelitas fluminis alveum transeuntes prope arcam illum transmittere, aut certe statuendum erit, quod tantum in progressu, non in ipsa Jordanis transmissione ipsis hoc interstitium servandum fuerit.

ACCINCTI.

Ebr. רכח, LXX. Aquila & Symmachus reddunt parate ad transeundum. Masius parando scilic. populo transitum: alii recte, & sic, uti ceperant, quibus accedit B. Lutheri translatio. Nam verba infinitivi Hiphil saepe pro adverbiis accipiun- tur, vid. Hos. 5, 2. c. 9, 9. Jon. 4, 4. unde firmando idem est, quod firmiter, pede fixo, ut e cap. 4. vers. 3. patet.

## 4:1 Argument
CHAPTER IV. Stones of the monument.

Latin:

CAPUT IV. Lapides monumenti.

## 4:2
Verse 2. CHOOSE TWELVE MEN.

The Vulgate must be emended. In Hebrew it is not choose, but take, because they had already been chosen in ch. 3, v. 12, as Bonfrerius acknowledges in the same place.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ELIGE DUODECIM VIROS.

EMendanda est Vulgata. In Ebr. habetur non elige, sed accipite, quia jam electi erant c. 3. v. 12. ut agnoscit ibidem Bonfrerius.

## 4:3
Verse 3. VERY HARD STONES.

That very hard is not found in the Hebrew: But the word הכין pertains to the firm station of the Priests, of which we spoke at the last verse of the preceding chapter.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DURISSIMOS LAPIDES.

Illud durissimos non habetur in Ebræo: Sed vox הכין ad stationem firmam Sacerdotum perti- net, de qua ad vers. ult. cap. præcedentis diximus.

## 4:5
Verse 5. EACH ONE A STONE) Concerning this kind of monument see Gen. 31, 46. & below 21. This sign and trophy ought to have been of the conquered and as it were of the Jordan itself, both before posterity and before other nations v. 25, so that they might acknowledge the power of God, and religiously venerate and fear the same.

Latin:

Vers. 5. SINGULI SINGULOS LAPIDES) De hoc genere monumentorum vide Gen. 31, 46. & infra 21. Signum hoc & trophæum esse debuit victi victique quasi Jordanis tum penes posteros, tum penes alias gentes v. 25. ut Dei potentiam agno- scant, eundemq; religiose venerentur ac timeant.

## 4:9
Verse 9. HE PLACED IN THE MIDDLE OF THE JORDAN BED.

Just as the first 12 stones in Gilgal, where they first pitched their tents after the crossing, were to be erected into a monument, so Joshua, undoubtedly by divine instinct, placed another 12 stones in the middle of the Jordan, which Bonfrerius maintains were brought there from the Jericho bank rather than from another place in the bed, so that they might be a sign of the station of the ark and the Priests in the middle of the Jordan, at which the waters partly stood motionless, and partly fled away. But how could they be a sign in the middle of the Jordan if they could not be seen by those who stood on the bank? Bonfrerius makes them a sign, not because they could be seen, but because they could be made known by report, or recognized by the sound of the waters at those stones: But there is no doubt that, if they were placed as a sign, they ought, just like the previously designated 12 stones, to have met the eye as a peculiar monument. Masius says they were placed on the further bank of the Jordan. But the text contradicts this, when it says they were placed in the middle of the Jordan bed. Others therefore think they were placed not indeed on the bank, but not precisely in the middle, but rather below the middle, or not far from the middle towards the bank, as that word in the middle is sometimes wont to be taken ὡς ἐν πλάτει, so that they could be seen. But were they erected on high, or were they placed in order? The latter seems more probable, because they were meant to represent the 12 tribes of Israel. So that if they could not be seen by those who stood on the bank, at least they could be seen by those who were crossing the river, or when the waters were receding, very large stones were taken, and each one somewhat elevated, which could be observed in the very pure and most transparent waters of the Jordan. Tertullian therefore was mistaken, l. 4. against Marcion, ch. 13, when he said they were stored in the ark of the Covenant.

Latin:

Vers. 9. POSUIT IN MEDIO JORDANIS ALVEO.

Ut priores 12. lapides in Galgalis, ubi pri- mum tentoria post transitum figebant, erigendi erant in monumentum, ita Josua, ex instinctu pro- cul dubio divino, in medio Jordanis alios 12. lapi- des, quos ex Hierichuntina potius ripa, quam ex alio alvei loco eo illatos vult Bonfrerius, colloca- vit, ut signum essent stationis arcæ & Sacerdotum in medio Jordanis, ad quam aquæ partim stete- runt immotæ, partim diffugerunt. Quomodo au- tem signum esse potuere in medio Jordanis, si videri non potuerunt ab iis, qui in ripa consisterent? Bonfrerius signum illos facit, non quod videri, sed quod per famam divulgari, vel ex strepitu aquarum ad istos lapides dignosci potuerit: Sed dubium nullum est, si positi sunt in signum, eosdem æque, ut prius designatos 12. lapides debuisse, ceu pecu- liare monumentum, in visum incurrere. Masius in ulteriori ripa Jordanis eosdem positos dicit. Sed refragatur textus, cum in medio Jordanis alveo col- locatos ait. Alii ergo non in ripa quidem, sed nec præcise in medio, verum sub medium, aut non lon- ge a medio versus ripam positos censent, ut solet ea vox in medio nonnunquam ὡς ἐν πλάτει accipi, quo conspici possent. Sed num in altum erecti, an vero ordine collocati sunt? Posterius videtur proba- bilius, quia referre debebant 12. tribus Israel. Ut ergo si non ab iis, qui in ripa consisterent, saltim ab illis, qui fluvium trajicerent, aut aquis decre- scentibus conspici possent, lapides assumti sunt prægrandes, & elati quodammodo singuli, qui in Jordanis aquis purissimis, & maxime perspicuis observari potuerint. Hallucinatus ergo est Tertull. l. 4. contr. Marc. cap. 13. cum in arca Testamenti eos conditos dixit.

## 4:10
Ver. 10. AND MOSES HAD SAID TO HIM.

What is it that Moses had said to Joshua should be commanded to the people concerning the crossing of the Jordan? The Rabbis understand those things which were to be proclaimed at Ebal according to the commandment of the Lord in Deut. 27. But these things could not be carried out there in the Jordan, and they are reported as having been done finally in chapter 8. Bonfrerius notes that Moses spoke generally about miracles, or even specifically about those things which Joshua did both at this crossing and subsequently. But here the matter concerns a commandment given to Joshua by Moses, not predictions of prodigies. Cornelius thinks it is the summary of the law repeated and commended with sharp exhortation after the example of Moses. But the words do not speak of an example, but of some commandment of Moses, namely that the priests stood in the middle of the Jordan until all things were completed which the Lord had commanded Joshua to speak to the people, and Moses had said to him. The Vinarians understand the commandment to be about the obedience to be shown to the Lord in all things, inculcated in Joshua by Moses, and thus Junius notes that the summary of it is contained in Num. 27:21. Osiander wishes to refer to the commandment which he had received from Moses, that he should lead the people through the Jordan into the land of Canaan. But a plain explanation seems to be had from v. 12, where the execution of that commandment is reported, about which one may read in Num. 32, v. 28. Therefore, just as Joshua had been ordered to speak to the people about taking up 12 stones and carrying them to Gilgal and crossing the Jordan securely and confidently, so he particularly inculcated to the sons of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, just as he had received from Moses, that they should go before the sons of Israel armed, which they are said to have done, just as Moses had commanded them, and now Joshua had recalled that to memory. Although it may also be said not inappropriately that they were stirred up to obedience and worship of the Lord, who was manifesting Himself to them by this wonderful prodigy; for Joshua had been ordered by Moses to do this diligently.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET DIXERAT EI MOSES.

Quidnam est, quod de Jordanis transitu Moses Josuæ populo præcipiendum dixerat? Rabbini ea, quæ ad Hebal juxta præceptum Domini Deut. 27. proclamanda erant, intelligunt. Sed hæc ibi ex- pediri non poterant in Jordane, & 8. demum capite gesta referuntur. Bonfrerius generaliter Mosen de miraculis, vel etiam specialiter de iis, quæ tum in hoc transitu, tum deinceps Josua egit, prædixis- se notat. Sed hic de præcepto Josuæ dato a Mose, non de prædictionibus prodigiorum agitur. Cor- nelius summam legis repetitam, & acri exhortatio- ne commendatam ad exemplum Mosis, putat. Ve- rum non de exemplo loquuntur verba, sed de præ- cepto aliquo Mosis, quod nempe steterint eo us- que Sacerdotes in medio Jordanis, donec omnia complerentur, quæ Josuæ, ut loqueretur ad popu- lum, præceperat Dominus, & dixerat ei Moses. Vinarienses mandatum de obedientia Domino in omnibus præstanda Josuæ a Mose inculcato intel- ligunt, atque ita Junius summam ejus Num. 27, 21. contineri notat. Osiander mandatum respici vult, quod a Mose acceperat, ut populum per Jordanem traduceret in terram Canaan. Sed explicatio pla- na videtur e v. 12. haberi, ubi refertur exequutio illius mandati, de quo legere est Num. 32., verf. 28. Ut ergo de lapidibus 12. tollendis, & in Galgal de- ferendis, & secure ac confidenter per Jordanem transeundo loqui ad populum jussus erat Josua, ita peculiariter filiis Ruben, Gad, & dimidiæ tribui Manassis inculcavit, quemadmodum a Mose acce- perat, ut præirent filios Israel armati, quod fecisse dicuntur, sicut eis præceperat Moses, & nunc illud in memoriam revocarat Josua. Quamvis etiam non incommode dicatur, ad obedientiam & cul- tum Domini, qui mirabili hoc prodigio sese ipsis manifestabat excitatos fuisse, hoc enim ut sedulo faceret, Josua a Mose jussus erat.

## 4:11
Ver. 11. AND THE ARK OF THE LORD CROSSED OVER, AND THE PRIESTS WENT BEFORE THE PEOPLE) That is, after crossing the Jordan, the Ark and the priests were in the vanguard, not in the middle of the column as in the desert.

This is indicated when the whole multitude of the people had crossed, that the Ark of the Lord, with the priests who were standing in the middle of the river, had also crossed the rest of the Jordan and again had gone before the whole host of the Israelites by two thousand cubits, as Tostatus, Serarius, Salianus, and others note. The Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh followed it.

Latin:

Vers. 11. TRANSIVIT ET ARCA DOMINI, SACER- DOTESQUE PERGEBANT ANTE POPVLVM) Id est, post transitum Iordanem Arca & Sacerdotes in primo sue- runt agmine, non in medio agmine ut in deserto.

Id indicatur, cum tota populi multitudo transiisset, arcam Domini, cum Sacerdotibus, qui in medio fluvii stabant, reliquum Jordanis quo- que transiisse atque iterum tota agmina Israeli- tarum per bis mille cubitos præivisse, ut Tostatus, Serarius, Salianus, & alii notant. Eam sequu- ti sunt Rubenitæ, Gaditæ, & dimidia tribus Ma- nassis.

## 4:13
Ver. 13. THEY WENT) In the Hebrew is added, before the Lord, that is, the Ark.

The Ark is not called the Lord; that is nowhere to be read, but they are said to have walked before the Lord, who walked before the Ark, because the Lord was particularly present at the Ark. Grotius is therefore mistaken, along with the Socinians and certain Jews, in thinking that the name of the Lord was attributed to the Ark.

Latin:

Vers. 13. INCEDEBANT) In Ebræo additur, coram Domino, id est, Arca.

Non arca dicitur Dominus, id nuspiam le- gere est, sed coram Domino dicuntur incessisse, qui coram arca, quod ad arcam Dominus pecu- liariter præsens esset. Fallitur ergo Grotius, cum Socinianis & Judæis quibusdam, arcæ nomen Domi- ni tributum esse sentiens.

## 4:15
Ver. 15. AND HE SAID TO HIM.

It must be rendered: he had said, as Masius translates. See ver. 11, for it is repeated more clearly how the priests ascended from the Jordan according to the very commandment of God, so that it may be reported when the waters returned to their channel, which the history does not state whether it happened gradually, as Masius and Bonfrerius wish, or by a simultaneous rush.

Latin:

Vers. 15. DIXITQVE AD EUM.

Reddendum est: dixerat, ut Masius vertit. Vid. vers. 11. nam repetitur clarius, quomodo ex ipsius Dei præcepto e Jordane ascenderint Sacer- dotes, ut referatur, quando reversæ aquæ sint in alveum suum, quod an sensim, ut Masius & Bon- frerius volunt, an impetu simultaneo factum, non perhibet historia.

## 4:19
Ver. 19. IN GILGAL.

In the place which later received that name, c. 5, 9, and is very famous in this history: for here was the first station after the entry into the land, and the camp of Joshua remained for a very long time, and the sacrament of circumcision, as also of the Passover, was celebrated, and for some years the tabernacle with the ark was set up, and later Saul was also inaugurated there as King, 1 Sam. 11. It was distant from Jericho by 10 stadia, from the Jordan by 50, as is evident from book 5 of the Antiquities of Josephus, c. 1, and from the War, book 5, c. 4, whence it is less correctly placed by Adrichomius as nearer to the Jordan than to Jericho.

Latin:

Vers. 19. IN GALGALIS.

In loco, qui postea id nominis accepit c. 5, 9. & valde celebris est in hac historia: nam hic & pri- ma fuit post ingressum terræ statio, & diutissime castra Josuæ manserunt, & circumcisionis, ut & Paschatos Sacramentum celebratum, & per ali- quot annos tabernaculum cum arca constitutum fuit, postmodum etiam Saul ibidem inauguratus in Regem est 1. Sam. 11. Distabat ab Hierichunte 10. stadiis, a Jordane 50. ut e l. 5. Antiqq. Joseph. c. 1. & de Bell. l. 5. c. 4. constat, unde ab Adrichomio minus recte Jordani, quam Hierichunti vicinior constituitur.

## 4:20
Vers. 20. JOSHUA ALSO SET UP THE TWELVE STONES WHICH THEY HAD TAKEN FROM THE BED OF THE JORDAN IN GILGAL.

He did not set it up as an altar, in order to sacrifice upon it, which was the opinion of Josephus and the Rabbis in Masius on Josh. 8. (who, against history, say that on the very day of the crossing an altar was erected on Mount Ebal,) not so that he might inscribe the law for them, according to Deut. 27, 2. (for these were different stones. V. Jos. 8, 30.) but he placed them as a monument of the dried-up Jordan and of the miraculous leading of Israel through the same, just as the words of Joshua v. 21. seqq. teach, by which very words he commends a grateful memory of so great a benefit, and reverence for the divine name: there is no word held about an altar, nor were the stones to be erected on high, but to be placed in order separately, so that each one might represent each tribe. And sacrifices were ordinarily to be offered upon the altar of burnt offerings Lev. 1. 3. 4. 7. 17. It is not therefore probable that Joshua built another altar: which he himself sharply reproached the Reubenites for in chap. 22.

Latin:

Vers. 20. DUODECIM QVOQVE LAPI- DES QVOS DE JORDANIS ALVEO SUM- SERANT, POSUIT JOSUE IN GALGALIS.

Non erexit in aram, ut in eo sacrificaret, quod Josepho visum & Rabbinis apud Masium in Jos. 8. p. 151. (qui invita historia, in die ipso transitus al- tare in monte Hebal erectum dicunt,) nec ut legem illis inscriberet, juxta Deut. 27, 2. (hi enim diversi fuere lapides. V. Jos. 8, 30.) sed in monumentum eos posuit exiccati Jordanis & deductionis Israelis per eundem miraculosæ, quemadmodum verba Josuæ v. 21. seqq. docent, quibus ipsis gratam tan- ti beneficii memoriam, & nominis divini reveren- tiam commendat: de altari nullum habetur ver- bum, nec in altum erigendi, sed ordine seorsim collocandi erant Lapides, ut singuli singulas tri- bus repræsentarent. Et offerri ordinarie debebant sacrificia super altari holocaustorum Lev. 1. 3. 4. 7. 17. Non ergo probabile est, Josuam aliud altare condi- disse: quod Rubenitis ipse acriter exprobrabat cap. 22.

## 4:24
Vers. 25. THAT ALL THE PEOPLES OF THE EARTH MAY LEARN)

It ought not to be doubted that the neighboring nations were vehemently struck upon hearing the wonders which had happened in Egypt at the departure, in the desert, and at the entry into the land: see Josh. 12. at the end.

THAT YOU ALSO MAY FEAR THE LORD.

Under the name of fear, all religion and worship of God is comprehended, whence the LXX render it σέβησθε, not because the old law was of fear and the new is of love, as Cornelius wishes; for both love is commanded in the Old and fear in the New Testament, Matt. 22, 39. 1. Pet. 2. v. 18. But because filial fear flows from love, and love from true faith, which was required no less in the Old Testament than in the New, because through faith the hearts of the pious of old were also purified, and grace and salvation were brought to them, Acts 15, 9. 11. Gal. 5, 6. whence Cornelius himself declares the words of Psalm 33, verse 10, Fear the Lord all his saints, with this added explanation, with a fear not servile, but filial, just as children fear to offend their parents, lest they displease them, namely, out of love, not out of fear.

Latin:

Vers. 25. VT DISCANT OMNES TERRARVM POPVLI)

Dubitari non debet, quin vehementer perculsæ fuerint vici- næ gentes auditis ostentis, quæ contigerant in Ægypto in exitu, in deserto, & in terræ introitu: vid. Job. 12. in fine.

UT ET VOS TIMEATIS DOMINUM.

Timoris nomine omnis religio & cultus Dei comprehenditur, unde LXX. reddunt σέβησθε, non quod lex vetus timoris fuerit, nova amoris sit, ut Cornelius vult; nam & amor in veteri & timor in Nov. Test. præcipitur Matth. 22, 39. 1. Petr. 2. v. 18. Sed quia timor filialis ex amore, amor e vera fide fluit, quæ non minus in Vet. Test. quam in novo requirebatur, quia per fidein purificata etiam pio- rum veterum corda sunt, & gratia ipsis ac salus fa- cta est Act. 15, 9. 11. Gal. 5, 6. unde Cornelius ipse verba Psalm. 33. verf. 10. Timete Dominum omnes san- cti ejus, declarat hac addita ἐξηγήσει, timore non servili, sed filiali, sicut filii timent offendere pa- rentes, ne eis displiceant, scil. ex amore, non ex timore.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAP. V. The terror of the Canaanites. The circumcision and Passover of the Israelites. The manna ceases. The Angel as leader of the army.

Vers. 1. THE KINGS OF THE AMORITES.

Who, namely, dwelt on the western side of the Jordan, as the text adds. For others in the eastern side had already been destroyed. They are said to have dwelt BEYOND THE JORDAN comparatively with respect to those regions from which the Israelites had departed, since otherwise, in the more accepted phrase of Scripture, those are called Trans-Jordanites who were situated on the eastern side. Furthermore, here the Amorites are called those closer to the people of the Jordan on the western side, the rest, who were more remote near the Western or Mediterranean Sea, are called Canaanites, and by both these names all seven peoples, whose land God had promised to the Israelites, are comprehended. The LXX call those who are here called Canaanites, Phoenicians, because Tyre and Sidon, the metropolises of Phoenicia, once belonged to the Canaan promised to the Jews, even though the Hebrews, because of their sloth, never obtained them. See Masius and Arias Montanus. For also Dion. For Africanus and Strabo, under the name of Phoenicia, comprehend that whole region by the sea as far as Egypt.

Latin:

CAP. V. Terror Chananæorum. Circumcisio & Pascha Israelitarum. Manna cessat. Angelus dux exercitus.

Vers. 1. REGES AMORRHÆORUM.

QVi scil. ad occidentalem Jordanis plagam habi- tabant, uti textus addit. Alii enim in Orien- tali plaga jam deleti erant. Illi dicuntur TRANS JORDANEM habitasse συγκριτικῶς respectu ea- rum regionum a quibus recesserant Israelitæ, quum alias receptiori Scripturæ phrasi trans - Jordanini dicantur, qui in Orientali plaga siti erant. Cæte- rum hic Amorrhæi vocantur ad Occidentalem plagam populi Jordani viciniores, reliqui remotio- res juxta mare Occidentale seu mediterraneum Cananæi, & utroque hoc nomine omnes septem populi, quorum terram Deus Israelitis promise- rat, comprehenduntur. LXX. eos, qui Cananæi hic dicuntur, vocant Phœnices, quia Tyrus & Sidon metropoles Phœniciæ olim ad Cananæam Judæis promissam pertinuere, etsi Ebræi ob suam gna- viam nunquam iis potiti sunt. Vid. Mas. & Arias Montan. Nam & Dion. Afro & Straboni Phœniciæ nomine tota illa regio ad mare usque ad Ægyptum comprehenditur.

## 5:2
vers. 2. MAKE THEE KNIVES OF STONE.

Pagninus, Vatablus, and the Tigurines, along with the Chaldean, prefer to render it sharp knives. But because the word צור signifies a rock, and is not easily taken otherwise, and because a rock was used by Zipporah in the circumcision of her son, as the Chaldean and Pagninus explain in Exod. 4, 25, and because stones, Samian shards, and flints were once accustomed to be used for castration, and indeed for sharpening reeds, as Bonfrer teaches from Catullus, Pliny, and the Greek Epigrams, and the use of stone knives has also been found among the Americans, the LXX, the Vulgate, Augustine, Theodoret, Masius, and others rightly interpret them as stone knives: which were used, both because there was an abundance of rocks in that place, and not of iron or steel around Arabia, and because it was foreshadowed that through Christ, who is the spiritual rock, not indeed the flesh is circumcised from the foreskin, but the mind from vices, as Theodoret and Procopius have noted.

CIRCUMCISE A SECOND TIME.

Not that those once circumcised, with the foreskin drawn or regrown, were to be circumcised again, as Symmachus and others fleeing from the Jews to the Samaritans did, nor in the sense that this was finally a second circumcision from that which was performed by Abraham, Gen. 17, as Theodoret and Masius wish; for this sense is false; for circumcision had been performed very often during those 400 years, nor with respect to the first, which was performed by Moses in Sinai, as Vatablus wishes, about which history has nothing: nor that the second is the same as by turns, as R. Kimchi and Cajetan wish, i.e., circumcise one part of the people after another: but rather in this sense, that that people, first circumcised in their parents in Egypt, because they celebrated the Passover there, which no one could eat unless circumcised, Ex. 12, is now circumcised in the land of Canaan, on account of the circumcision being interrupted in the desert, which Augustine, q. 6. and Tostatus thought, or what is simpler, that the second circumcision signifies nothing other than a repeated circumcision, which had already been interrupted for some time. Although Theodoret's explanation could also be admitted in this way, if this is called a second circumcision with respect to the Abrahamic one, because as Abraham was ordered by a special divine command to circumcise his whole family, so Joshua has now received a special command concerning the circumcising of all the Israelites, namely those who were not yet circumcised, and that this was a second solemn and general circumcision in the land of Canaan, provided that the prior one was solemnly instituted by Abraham in the same place: which opinion is approved by B. Balduinus, Conc. 16 in Jos. p. 202, Lyranus, Abulensis, and even Augustine not denying it, T. 4, Q. 6 in Jos.

Latin:

vers. 2. FAC TIBI CULTROS LAPIDEOS.

Cultros acutos reddi malunt Pagninus, Vata- blus, Tigurini cum Chald. Sed quia vox צור petram significat, nec aliter facile accipitur, & a Sephora in circumcisione filii petra adhibita est, uti Chald. & Pagn. Exod. 4, 25. exponunt, ac lapides, testas Sa- mias, atque filices olim adhiberi consuevisse ad ca- strationem, imo ad acuendos calamos e Catullo, Pli- nio, & Græcorum Epigrammatis docet Bonfrer. cul- trorumque lapideorum usus etiam apud America- nos inventus est, recte LXX. Vulgat. August. Theo- dor. Masius & alii lapideos cultros interpretantur: qui adhibiti, tum quod eo loci petrarum copia fuerit, non ferri aut chalybis circa Arabiam, tum quia adumbratum, per Christum, qui spiritualis petra est, non quidem carnem apræputio, sed men- tem a vitiis circumcidi, ut Theod. & Procop. notarunt.

CIRCUMCIDE SECUNDO.

Non quod semel circumcisi attracto vel re- crescente præputio iterum circumcidendi fuerint, ut Symmachus, & alii a Judæis ad Samaritas transfu- gientes fecerunt, nec eo sensu, quod hæc altera de- mum fuerit circumcisio ab ea, quæ ab Abrahamo facta Gen. 17. ut Theodor. & Masius volunt; nam hic sensus falsus est; sæpissime enim facta erat cir- cumcisio per illos 400. annos, nec respectu pri- mæ, quæ a Mose in Sina facta, ut Vatabl. vult, de qua nihil habet historia: nec ut secundo idem sit quod per vices, uti R. Kimchi, & Cajetan. volunt, q. d. circumcide unam populi partem post aliam: sed vel hoc sensu, ut populus ille primo in parentibus in Ægypto circumcisus, quia celebrarunt ibi Pascha, quod comedere nemo poterat nisi circumcisus Ex. 12. nunc circumcidatur in terra Canaan, ob inter- missam in deserto circumcisionem, quod August. q. 6. & Tostato visum, vel quod simplicius est, secun- da circumcisio nihil aliud significet, quam repeti- tam circumcisionem, quæ jam aliquo tempore in- termissa fuerat. Quanquam etiam Theodoreti ex- plicatio hoc pacto admitti posset, si hæc secunda dicatur circumcisio respectu Abrahamiticæ, quod ut Abraham peculiari divino mandato, totam fami- liam jussus est circumcidere, ita Josua mandatum nunc peculiare de circumcidendis Israëlitis omni- bus, qui scil. nondum circumcisi erant, acceperit, quodque hæc altera solennis & generalis in terra Canaan fuerit circumcisio, siquidem prior ab Ab- rahamo in eadem solemniter instituta fuerit: quæ sententia B. Balduino Conc. 16. in Jos. p.202. Ly- rano, Abulensi, etiam Augustino non abnuente T. 4. Q. 6. in Jos. probata.

## 5:3
Vers. 3. HE CIRCUMCISED THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL) It is the mark of a good Prince to recall interrupted rites. See 2 Kings 23. Grotius considers circumcision and the Passover, which Josiah ordered to be celebrated in 2 Kings 23, as a meritorious rite. But they were not mere rites, but Sacraments divinely instituted, and thus divine means of salvation: in whose place in the N.T. the Sacrament of Baptism and the Lord's Supper succeeded. Nor did Joshua perform the circumcision by private judgment, but by divine command, verse 2.

Latin:

Vers. 3. CIRCVMCIDIT FILIOS ISRAEL) Boni Prin- cipis est ritus intermissos revocare. Vide 2. Reg. 23. Pro merito ritu circumcisionem & Pascha, quod 2. Reg. 23. celebrari jussit Josias, habet Grotius. At non erant nudi ritus, sed Sacramenta divinitus instituta, adeoque divina salutis media: in quorum locum successit in N. T. Sacrameutum Baptismi, & Cœnæ Dominicæ. Neque privato arbitrio cir- cumcisionem peragebat Josua, sed divino manda- to vers. 2.

## 5:5
Vers. 5. HE WAS UNCIRCUMCISED.

Why did the people remain uncircumcised for 40 years in the desert? The Hebrews trifle that it was done because the North wind, which is a wind that heals wounds, did not blow there: Others with Augustine think circumcision was interrupted through disobedience, others with Masius, Pererius, Vasquez in 3. part. disp. 164. c. 2. say that the children were left uncircumcised as a punishment for the murmuring of the people, others with Theodoret and Jerome, l. 1. in Epist. ad Gal. and Damascene, l. 4. Orth. fid. c. 26. [say it was] because in the desert the people were sufficiently distinct and separated from the nations, but this was not the primary end of circumcision. Others say best that it was interrupted on account of the wandering, which cause the text itself hints at: But the people who were born in the desert For 40 years of the journey of the very wide wilderness he was uncircumcised: by which words not only are the subjects noted which were not yet circumcised, but also a reason is rendered why circumcision was interrupted, because the Hebrews had no certain and stable seat in the desert, but whenever the pillar of cloud was moved, they had to follow and move camp. See Thomas 3. p. q. 70. art. 4. Abulensis, Lyranus, Masius, Serarius, &c.
