But in the land of Canaan, where a fixed seat was defined for them, there were laws to be observed by them, and therefore with the 14th day of Nisan impending, the Passover was to be celebrated, whence the circumcision of the people had necessarily to be set before it. After, therefore, they crossed the Jordan on the tenth day, they were circumcised immediately on the eleventh, and not, as others wish, was the circumcision performed over three whole days, but completed in one day, so that the days of pain might pass, which lasts until the third day Gen. 34, 25, before the solemnity of the Passover was to be celebrated with joy.

How, however, could such a great multitude be circumcised in one day? Resp. Because the circumcision could be performed by the work of the circumcised, and also of the mothers and other women in this case of necessity: indeed, some could even circumcise themselves, as was done by Abraham. But were the Reubenites, Gadites, and Manassites who were left across the Jordan also circumcised? Resp. That seems likely to some, who wish that they were warned about it by some legates sent by Joshua from Gilgal, or certainly by the Levites left there.

Latin:

Vers. 5. INCIRCUMCISUS FUIT.

Cur incircumcisus populus mansit per 40. an- nos in deserto? Ebræi nugantur id factum, quia ibi non spirarit Boreas, qui ventus plagis medeatur: Alii cum Augustino intermissam circumcisionem putant per inobedientiam, alii cum Masio, Pererio, Vasquetz in 3. part. disp. 164. c. 2. in pœnam ob murmur populi filios incircumcisos relictos dicunt, alii cum Theodor. & Hieronym. l. 1. in Epist. ad Gal. ac Damasceno l. 4. Orth. fid. c. 26. ideo, quod in deserto populus satis distinctus & separatus erat a gentibus, sed hic non erat primarius circum- cisionis finis. Optime intermissam alii dicunt ob peregrinationem, quam causam textus ipse innuit: Populus autem, qui natus est in deserto per 40. annos itineris latissimæ solitudinis incircumci- sus fuit : quibus verbis non modo subjecta notantur quæ nondum circumcisa, sed etiam ratio redditur, cur intermissa circumcisio, quia nullam certam & stabilem sedem habuere Ebræi in deserto, sed quandocunque movebatur columna nubis, sequi, & castra movere debuerunt. Vid. Thomas 3. p. q. 70. art. 4. Abulens. Lyran. Masius, Serarius, &c. In terra autem Canaan, ubi fixa iis sedes definita erat, leges observandæ ipsis fuere, ideoque immi- nente 14. die Nisan Pascha celebrandum, unde ne- cessario præmittenda erat populi circumcisio. Postquam ergo decimo die Jordanem transierunt, undecimo statim circumcisi sunt, nec, ut alii vo- lunt, per integrum triduum peracta circumcisio, sed uno die absoluta, ut transirent dies doloris, qui ad tertium diem durat Gen. 34, 25. ante Paschatos so- lemnitatem cum lætitia celebrandam.

Quomodo autem tanta multitudo uno die circumcidi potuit? Resp. quia circumcisorum ope- ra, nec non matrum & aliarum fœminarum in ca- su hoc necessitatis peragi potuit circumcisio: imo potuere etiam nonnulli seipsos circumcidere, ut ab Abrahamo factum. Num autem etiam trans Jordanem relicti Rubenitæ, Gaditæ, & Menassitæ, circumcisi sunt? Resp. Id verisimile quibusdam videtur, qui volunt, quod de eo per legatos aliquos a Josua e Galgale missos moniti sint, aut certe a Levitis ibi relictis.

## 5:7
Vers. 7. THE SONS OF THESE SUCCEEDED IN THE PLACE OF THEIR FATHERS) They obtained those promises which their fathers had fallen short of. UNTIL THEY WERE HEALED) See Gen. 34, 25. μετὰ χαλεπῶν ἀλγηδόνων. Philo, περὶ περιτομῆς. The particle until here does not exclude the subsequent time: for they remained there even after health was recovered. And soon it follows concerning the Passover celebrated there.

Latin:

Vers. 7. HORVM FILII IN LOCVM SVCCESSE- RVNT PATRVM) Adepti sunt ea promissa, quibus Pa- tres exciderant. DONEC SANARENTVR) Vide Gen. 34, 25. μετὰ χαλεπῶν ἀλγηδόνων. Philo, περὶ περιτομῆς. Particula donec hic non excludit subsequens tempus: nam & post sanitatem recuperatam ibi manserunt. Et mox sequitur de Paschate illic cele- brato.

## 5:9
Vers. 9. THE REPROACH OF EGYPT. It was turned to reproach by the Israelites against the Egyptians, and likewise against other nations, that they did not apply circumcision, not because of the foreskin, which by its nature is a reproach to no one, but because they were strangers to the covenant and the people of the circumcised God, from which reproach the Egyptians, among whom the Israelites had lived, could be freed above others, not lacking information about the true worship of God, and they were so much the more a reproach to them. But what is held in Diodorus Siculus l. 1, Herodotus in Euterpe, Strabo l. 17, concerning the circumcision of the Egyptians, pertains to later times, and is referred by some to the age of Solomon, who cultivated trade with them.

AND THE NAME OF THAT PLACE WAS CALLED GILGAL.

From גלל to roll, to roll down. Jerome, Bede, and Lyranus translate it as the wheel of revolutions, but Josephus and Theodoret interpret it poorly as liberty. The place was also called the hill of foreskins verse 3, not because there were so many foreskins that a hill was raised from them, as the Rabbis trifle, but because the foreskins were cast away or buried on the hill that was there.

Latin:

Vers. 9. OPPROBRIUM ÆGYPTI. Opprobrio vertebatur ab Israëlitis Ægyptiis, ac pariter cæteris gentibus, quod non adhiberent circumcisionem, non ob præputium, quod natura sua nemini est probro, sed quod alieni essent a fœ- dere ac populo Dei præputiati, a quo opprobrio Æ- gypti, inter quos Israëlitæ vixerant, poterant præ aliis liberari, informatione de vero Dei cultu non carentes, ac tanto magis ipsis erant opprobrio. Quod autem apud Diodor. Sicul. l. 1. Herodotum in Euterpe, Strabon. l. 17. de circumcisione Ægyptio- rum habetur, ad posteriora tempora pertinet, ac re- fertur a nonnullis ad ætatem Salomonis, qui com- mercia cum illis coluit.

VOCATUMQVE EST NOMEN LOCI ILLIUS, GALGALA.

A גלל volvere, devolvere. Hieron. Beda, & Lyran. vertunt rotam revolutionum, male vero Jo- seph. & Theod. interpretantur libertatem. Dictus etiam est locus collis præputiorum vers. 3. non quod fuerint tot præputia, ut collis ex iis excitatus fue- rit, ut Rabbini nugantur, sed quod in colle, qui ibi erat, abjecta vel sepulta sint præputia.

## 5:10
Vers. 10. AND THEY KEPT THE PASSOVER. This was the third Passover. For the first was in Egypt at the departure, the second near Mount Sinai. But did those across the Jordan also celebrate this Passover? Resp. They could not celebrate it in their own land, because it was restricted to the place of the tabernacle Deut. 16. v. 2. 6. 7. nor were they obligated in that year to betake themselves to this place, because they did not know about the celebration of this feast, then to be instituted there.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET FECERUNT PHASE. Pascha hoc tertium fuit. Nam primum in Ægypto sub egressum, alterum juxta montem Sinai. Num autem hoc Pascha etiam trans-Jordanini celebra- runt? Resp. In terra sua celebrare nequiverunt, quia erat adstrictum ad locum tabernaculi Deut. 16. v. 2. 6. 7. nec isto anno obligati erant ad hunc lo- cum se conferre, quia nescierunt de hujus festi ce- lebratione, tum illic instituenda.

## 5:11
Vers. 11. AND THEY ATE OF THE FRUITS OF THE LAND ON THE SECOND DAY UNLEAVENED BREAD.

What indeed did they eat on the very day of the Passover with the Paschal lamb? Abulensis thinks they ate manna, in which there was no leaven; but because they were commanded to have unleavened bread Ex. 12, it is likely they had the same fruits from the region across the Jordan, just as in Num. 9, 3, at the Passover at Mount Sinai they were able to have flour from the neighboring Midianite land.

But by that other day, Bonfrerius and Cornelius understand not the 15th of Nisan with Abulensis and Arias, but the 16th, because this was prescribed so that on it a sheaf of ears of grain might be offered to God from the new crops, in the name of firstfruits, before the offering of which it was not lawful for anyone to eat of the new crops. Lev. 23. v. 14. Joseph. b. 3. ch. 10.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET COMEDERUNT DE FRU- GIBUS TERRÆ DIE ALTERO AZYMOS PANES.

Quidnam vero ipso Paschatos die cum agno Paschali comederunt? Abulensis putat manna, in quo nihil erat fermenti, comedisse; sed quia præ- cepti erant panes azymi Ex. 12. e trans Jordanina re- gione fruges eosdem habuisse verisimile est, ut Num. 9, 3. in Paschate ad montem Sinai farinam ex vicina Madianitide habere potuerunt.

Per alterum autem illum diem non 15. Nisan cum Abulensi, & Aria, sed 16. intelligit Bonfrer. & Cornelius, quia hic præscriptus erat, ut in eo de novis frugibus manipulus spicarum Deo offer- retur, primitiarum nomine, ante cujus oblatio- nem nemini licitum erat de novis frugibus edere. Lev. 23. v. 14. Joseph. l. 3. c. 10.

## 5:12
Ver. 12. AND THE MANNA CEASED) Extraordinary things cease where there is room for ordinary things, say the Jurisconsults.

It ceased on the 17th day of Nisan. For in the Hebrew it is held thus: and the manna ceased on the day after, when they had eaten of the grain of the land.

Latin:

Vers. 12. DEFECITQVE MANNA) Cessant extraor- dinaria, ubi ordinariis locus est, aiunt Jurisconsulti.

Defecit die 17. Nisan. Nam in Ebræo ita ha- betur: & cessavit Manna postridie, dum comedissent de frumento terræ.

## 5:13
Ver. 13. IN THE FIELD OF THE CITY OF JERICHO) He explained well what is in the Hebrew, in Jericho, that is, near Jericho. Thus Luke 13, 33.

JERICHO, either from ירח Moon, Lüneburg, perhaps because they were accustomed to observe the new moon there on account of the feast of the new moons, or ריח is smelling, from the fragrance of the Balsam, which is born there with the greatest fertility. Josephus says that that field was an exceedingly delightful and almost divine tract, b. 5. Bell. 4. The city was situated in the tribe of Benjamin, Jos. 16, 7. ch. 18, 12. in the valley of Aulon, Joseph. l. c. in a most pleasant and fertile plain, surrounded on all sides by mountains, and gardens of balsam, and most noble palm groves, celebrated also by Pliny b. 13. ch. 4. b. 5. ch. 14. Strabo and others, whence it is also called the city of palms, Deut. 34, 3. Jud. 1, 15. ch. 3, 13. 2. Par. 28, 15. of which many were found there, varied as much in taste as in names, and which, when pressed by very rich heels, emitted much honey, not much worse than other honey. See Joseph. and Strab. Captured by Joshua and leveled to the ground, although it began to be restored and inhabited again by Abiel, Jud. 3. v. 12. 2. Sam. 10, 5. and was the seat of the School of Elisha, 2. Kings 2, as also of Zacchaeus, who received Christ at a banquet, Luke 19, 1. moreover fortified with walls under Herod, and called by the new name Cyprus, as Josephus testifies in b. 1. Bell. ch. 16, yet it was cut down again by the Romans: finally it was raised again in following times, but also destroyed again, so that now it is permitted to see only fields and ruins there.

Latin:

Vers. 13. IN AGRO VRBIS JERICHO) Bene explicavit, quod in Hebræo est, in Jericho, id est, apud Jericho. Sic Luc. 13, 33.

JERICHO vel a ירח Luna, Lüneburg, forte quod novilunium ibi observare ob neomenias fe- stum consueverint, vel ריח odoratus est, a fragrantia Balsami, quod ibi maxima fertilitate nascitur. Fuisse agrum illum supra modum delitiosum & pro- pe divinum tractum ait Josephus l. 5. Bell. 4. Sita fuit urbs in tribu Benjamin Jos. 16, 7. cap. 18, 12. in valle Aulone Joseph. l. c. in campo amœnissimo & fertilissimo, montibus undique circumdato, & hor- tis balsami, & palmetis nobilissimis, apud Plinium etiam l. 13. c. 4. l. 5. c. 14. Strabonem & alios cele- brato, unde & civitas palmarum dicta Deut. 34, 3. Jud. 1, 15. c. 3, 13. 2. Par. 28, 15. quarum plurima tam sapore, quam nominibus varia ibi reperta, & qui- bus pinguissimæ calcibus pressæ plurimum mellis emiserunt, non multo alio melle deterius. Vid. Jo- seph. & Strab. A Josua capta & solo æquata, etsi ab Abiel instaurari, & habitari iterum ceperit Jud. 3. v. 12. 2. Sam. 10, 5. ac sedes Scholæ Elisæi fuerit 2. Reg. 2, ut & Zachæi, qui Christum convivio ex- cepit Luc. 19, 1. muris insuper sub Herode munita, & novo nomine Cyprus dicta Josepho l. 1. Bell. c. 16. teste, excisa tamen denuo a Romanis: postremo iterum sequentibus temporibus excitata, sed & de- structa iterum, ut nunc campos solum & rudera ibi videre liceat.

## 5:14
Ver. 14. I AM PRINCE OF THE HOST OF THE LORD) Michael. Dan. 12. v. 1.

Grotius understands that man who appeared to Joshua in the field of Jericho, and called himself Prince of the Host of the Lord, to be a created angel. Following according to his custom, not only the Socinians, to whom he attributes much, and the Arminians, but also the Papists, who likewise contend that Michael, the prefect of the Jewish people, as he is called, was seen here by most, indeed, whom I perhaps ought to have named in the former place, by the estimation of Grotius, the Rabbis, blind leaders of the blind: by whom it is certain that some of the Reformed Doctors, and also our Calixtine innovators, have been seduced. All those accept it as a created angel, although no one has progressed to such rashness and audacity, except the Rabbis and some Papists, as to define precisely that it was Michael who appeared here. But the apparition is more illustrious than that which ought to be explained concerning a certain ministering Angel, or some creature. Which can be gathered first from the occasion and the end of the apparition. The Lord had commanded in Joshua 5, verse 2, that the Israelites should be circumcised, and having finished that, He had testified that He had taken away the reproach of Egypt in verse 9, certainly not through an Angel, but immediately. Soon, after the Passover had also been celebrated in that field, since the city, being well closed and fortified, could not easily be occupied, lest the people, being terrified, should lose heart at the very beginning of the battle, the Lord Himself wished to appoint and strengthen the leader of the people. Therefore, just as the Lord frequently appeared to Moses, and stood by him not through the Angel Michael or another, but in person, so He deigned to present Himself to Joshua as a helper, indeed as the supreme Commander of the war; and that by the power of the promise made to him in chapter 15. No one shall be able to resist you all the days of your life; as I was with Moses, SO will I be with you; I will not leave you, nor forsake you.

Which the Lord repeats again in chapter 7, 7. When He wished to dry up the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua: Today I will begin to exalt you before all Israel, that you may know that as I was with Moses, SO I am with you. Whence we conclude: Just as God was with Moses, so also, by the tenor of the divine promise, it is certain that He was with Joshua. But He was with Moses in such a way that He was present to him not through some created Angel, but in person, and led him with the people, which is manifest from the History itself, and is celebrated elsewhere throughout Scripture. For that Angel, who was promised to him as a conductor in Exodus 23, 20, was not some created and ministerial Angel, a ministering spirit, but an uncreated Angel, the Lord, whose voice all were bound to hear, and who had the sovereign power of forgiving or not forgiving sins. Wherefore it must also be believed that the Lord was with Joshua in this way. Which also appears from the whole History of Joshua, because He never acted through a certain created Angel, or stood by him, or addressed him. It is nowhere read in his entire history that a created Angel appeared to him or helped him as a helper. Then, from the promise made to the people, it is manifest what kind of man appeared here. That promise from chapter 23, verse 20 of Exodus has already been touched upon, in which the Lord had promised: Behold, I will send my Angel, who may go before you, and keep you in the way, and bring you into the place which I have prepared; and verse 23: My Angel will go before you, and will bring you to the Amorite, and the Hittite, etc. Therefore, what was promised to them is here performed in reality. Whence, as a parallel passage to this text, Exodus 23, verse 23 is written in the margin. Nor would anyone easily doubt that this man appeared here for the sake of fulfilling that promise, and that he is the same Angel, the leader of the people promised by GOD. But since we have taught in the notes to that passage that he was the very Son of God, it must be established that he also showed himself here as a helper to Joshua. Thirdly, the argument is by no means obscure from the name of this man, who calls himself the Prince of the host of the Lord in verse 14, and is also called so by the Holy Spirit in verse 15. For by this name a created Angel cannot be designated. For whoever is named from the created Angels, it is certain that he will be one from the very Host of the Lord: by which name it is clear that all Angels are included from Genesis 32, verse 2, 1 Kings 22, verse 19, and Nehemiah 9, verse 6, Psalm 103, verse 21, Luke 2, verse 13. He, therefore, who is distinguished from the created Angels designated by the host of the Lord, as their Leader and Prince, is not himself any created Angel. For if he were, he would be included under that host, from which, however, we see this Prince distinguished. Nor is the militant Church inconveniently included at the same time under the name of the Host of the Lord (unless only that is designated here, which pleases some), which is ordered as an army of camps is ordered, Canticles 6, 13, Psalm 68, 13, 14, whose Prince is not some created Angel, but the Son of GOD alone. Nor is such an axiom ever attributed to any created Angel, that he should be called the Prince of the Host of the Lord, which is proper to GOD alone; for he is called the Prince of the host of heaven in Daniel 8, verse 11. As for the great leader Michael in Daniel 12, verse 1, it will be demonstrated elsewhere that the Son of God is understood by him, and it is not obscurely evident from the comparison of Revelation 12, verse 7, and it is confessed by most Doctors, if you except the heterodox. Wherefore we believe that the Son of God also designated himself here by that name, who presides over all Angels, and is their Prince; for all serve him, revere him, and adore him, Psalm 97, verse 7, Hebrews 1, verse 6, Matthew 4, verse 11, Revelation 5, verse 12, whence Origen here: For who else is the Prince of the host of the virtues of the Lord, but our Lord Christ. For all the host of heaven, whether Angels, or Archangels, or virtues, or Dominions, or principalities, or powers, all these, which were made through him, fight under him as prince, who is the prince of princes, and who bestows principality upon princes. Further, fourthly, this is confirmed from the veneration and adoration of Joshua. For Joshua, the supreme leader of the people himself, falling on his face, adores this Prince of the host of the Lord, and calls him his Lord, and himself his servant, which honor men of God were accustomed to show not to created Angels, but to God, the Lord of Angels, nor do created Angels admit this worship, but on the contrary protest that they are fellow-servants of the men of God, and that such honor is not due to them, but to God alone, Revelation 20, verse 10, chapter 22, 9. Fifthly, the Grotian commentary is refuted by the commanded removal of the shoes. For he who appears to Joshua commands him to take off his shoes from his feet: because the place on which he stands is holy. Implying that Joshua himself, a holy man of God, is impure and unworthy of his most holy presence, which who would presume of a created Angel? By no means, indeed, has a created Angel ever demanded that holy men of God should take off their shoes for him. He who demanded this in Ex. 3 from Moses was God himself, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, Jehovah: and indeed the eternal Son of God, the Second Person of the Holy Trinity. Which the περι- στάσεις of the history and parallel passages in that same place have confirmed. And therefore from the analogy and comparison of that apparition it is rather to be gathered that the Son of God appeared here likewise to Joshua, as a warrior, when he was about to fight with his enemies, until he should overcome them in perpetual wars, just as he appeared to Moses in the burning bush, when he was about to lead the afflicted people out of the fiery furnace. As the priests serving in the tabernacle were required to perform sacred rites with bare feet, as Theodoret reports in q. 7 on Exodus, which was done on account of the divine presence; so when Joshua is here commanded to take off his shoes, it is certain that the divine presence is signified. Therefore God himself, and not a created angel, appeared here. Sixthly, a special argument can be drawn from the sanctification of the land, for whence is it that he says, because the place on which you stand is holy? That land certainly was not holy in itself, but defiled by many abominations, nay, cursed by the Lord, and dedicated to anathema, and therefore it must have been sanctified, and meanwhile, while the Prince of the host of the Lord stood there, liberated from the divine curse: because it was considered too holy to bear the presence of Joshua, unless he himself took off his shoes: by which symbol his impurity, and preparation for greater holiness, and the estimation of a holier place is designated. But that the earth cursed by the Lord himself was so sanctified by a created angel, no one would say. To the Holy of Holies, the Son of God, who alone takes away every curse and is the source and origin of all holiness, is that due; Who sanctified this earth, so that it might be consecrated for his appearance and advent, both his advent into the flesh, his nativity, and the office of teaching, of which there was a symbol there. Seventh, therefore, a peculiar argument can be observed from the Symbolic Appearance. For the form of a man, in which the Prince of the host of the Lord was seen for a time in these places, fits perfectly the Son of God himself, who is called the Lord man, and is designated by the name איש, when his advent into the flesh is treated, Gen. 4, 1. Zach. 6, 12. and by that symbol he prefigured his ἐνσάρκωσιν; when indeed he appeared as a certain man Gen. 32. verse 23. Ezech. 8. v. 2. It is indeed admitted that angels also appeared in the form of a man, but this man is altogether singular, and is seen clothed in such circumstances as exhibit the Son of God, that mighty warrior Ps. 24, 8, the man of war, whose right hand has been magnified, Ex. 15, 3. 6, not a created angel. Which is taught invincibly, Eighth, from the denomination of Jehovah. For that name is nowhere attributed to any created angel. But this man, after he had prepared and consecrated Joshua to hear his precepts, as we have said, now teaches what he wills and what needs to be done. Concerning which the text, chap. 6. v. 2. And the LORD said to Joshua: Behold I have given into your hand Jericho. For there is no doubt that the same one who had commanded for the sake of preparation, loose your shoe, is here continuing his speech. Otherwise that appearance would have been useless, and would have had no end, if indeed that man had commanded nothing else than the taking off of shoes. Since, therefore, the Holy Spirit openly calls that man the Lord Jehovah, who will be of such a hard forehead as to say that he is a created angel? To whom that most eminent name, proper to the one and only God, is neither attributed anywhere, nor can it truly be attributed. But that the Messiah is understood by the man the Lord is entirely consistent with the scriptures, Gen. 4, 1. Es. 9, 6, as he is θεάνθρωπος, and was accustomed to prefigure his future ἐνανθρώπησιν by such appearances. But Grotius interferes here with the words through an angel to no purpose. For the Lord is not said to have spoken through an angel, but that man who appeared is indicated to have been the Lord himself. Nor is it sound, when the Lord is reported to have said something, to insert an angel; otherwise no θεοφάνεια, no immediate speech of God will be left. And with equal ease, whenever the word of the Lord is said to have come to the Prophets, an intermediary angel could always be inserted. Furthermore, throughout the entire History of Joshua, where Jehovah is said to have spoken to him, which occurs quite often, it is evident that Jehovah himself spoke immediately, not by means of an angel: Nor will a dissimilar example be given. There is no doubt, therefore, that God is speaking these things, just as the Prayer itself is so constructed that it befits no messenger of God, but only God himself. Whence the ninth Argument arises from the αὐτοκρατορικῇ (sovereign) victory over enemies. Behold, says that Prince of the Host of the Lord, I have given into your hand Jericho and its King, and all the mighty men. Which speech no creature can use. For victory is from God alone Deut. 31. verse 29. Psalm 18. verse 30. Ps. 108, 14. 118, 11. 144, 10. Prov. 21, 31. whence the invincible conclusion: He who claims for himself as author the sovereign victory over enemies and the city, and both infallibly predicts it and miraculously performs it, is the true God. But that man, the Prince of the Host of the Lord, thus claims for himself the victory which he predicted here, and brought about by a supreme miracle with the walls of the city leveled by the mere blast of trumpets. Therefore he is not a created angel, but the true GOD. To which finally is added the Authority of the ancients, Justin Martyr, Dialog. with Trypho p. 221. There was a time when he (the Word) said he was the archduke, appearing in the form of a man to Joshua the son of Nun. Likewise Origen, hom. 6. on Joshua. Joshua recognized, not only that he was from God, but that he is God. For he would not have worshipped, unless he had recognized God. For who else is the Prince of the host of the virtues of the Lord, if not our Lord Jesus Christ. Cyprian. book 2. against the Jews, chap. 18. who proves from this that Christ is the Bridegroom, having the Church as his Bride, because he ordered Joshua to take off his shoes, because, namely, he himself was not the Bridegroom. For it was in the Law that whoever refused marriage should take off his shoe, but he who was the Bridegroom should be shod. Eusebius, book 1. Eccl. Hist. chap. 2. and others. Some of the Jews also recognized this: Masius, in his commentary on this place, cites the book Tanhum, as well as Rabbi Moses Gerundensis. Trypho the Jew himself, when Justin had brought forward this passage concerning the Son of God, gave up his hands as defeated, and professed in Dial. p. 222 that it had been demonstrated ἰσχυρῶς, strongly and most validly. And yet Grotius, a Christian, far blinder than the blind Jew, did not wish to acknowledge it in such great light. Masius opposes himself to the other Papists, asserting with us that the Son of GOD appeared in this place. Nor does Tostatus concede that the angel Michael is to be understood, but he tries to prove against his Socinians that Gabriel took care of the Hebrew nation and appeared here. Finally, since it pleased Grotius to rise up with the Papists, it can be asked, because they, with Gregory the Great, make two orders of angels, some indeed assisting, others ministering, from which order was this angel? If he was from the order of the assisting, how was he sent? since they are never considered to be sent: if from the ministering, how did he profess himself to be the Prince of the Host of the Lord, and thus an angel.

Latin:

Vers. 14. SVM PRINCEPS EXERCITVS DOMINI) Michael. Dan. 12. v. 1.

Virum illum, qui in agro Hierichuntico Josuæ apparuit, seque Principem nominavit Ex- ercitus Domini, de Angelo creato intelligit Gro- tius. Sequutus pro more suo, non tantum So- cinianos, quibus multum tribuit, & Arminia- nos, sed etiam Pontificios, qui pariter Michaelem præfectum populi Judaici, ut vocatur, hic vi- sum esse contendunt plerique, imo, quos priori fortassis loco, ex æstimatione Grotii, nominare debebam, Rabbinos cæcos cæcorum duces: a qui- bus etiam nonnullos e Reformatis Doctoribus, nec non Novatores nostros Calixtinos seductos esse constat. Omnes illi de Angelo creato ac- cipiunt, etsi eo nemo temeritatis & audaciæ pro- gressus sit, præter Rabbinos & Papistas nonnullos, ut præcise definierit, quod ex illis Michaël hic comparuerit. Sed illustrior est apparitio, quam quæ de Angelo quodam ministro, aut creatura ali- qua explicari debeat. Quod primum ab occasione ac fine apparitionis colligi potest. Jusserat Dominus Jos. 5. vers. 2. ut circumciderentur Israelitæ, eoque peracto se abstulisse opprobrium Ægypti testatus erat v. 9. non certe per Angelum, verum immedia- te. Mox celebrato etiam Paschate in agro isto, quum civitas probe occlusa, & munita non occupari facile posset, ne deterritus populus in ipso prælii ini- tio animo frangeretur, Dominus ipse principem populi instituere ac corroborari voluit. Proinde uti Mosi Dominus frequenter apparuit, eidemque non per Angelum Michaelem, aut alium, sed αὐ- τοπροσώπως adstitit, ita & Josuæ se Parastatam, imo supremum belli Ducem sistere dignatus est; idq; vi promissi eidem facti c. 15. Nullus poterit vobis resiste- re, cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ, sicut fui cum Mose, ITA ero tecum, non dimittam, nec derelinquam te.

Quod iterum repetit Dominus cap. 7, 7. cum exsiccare vellet Jordanem, dixit Dominus ad Josuam: Hodie incipiam exaltare te, coram omni Israel, ut scias, quod sicut cum Mose fui, ITA & tecum sim. Unde concludimus: Quemadmodum Deus cum Mose fuit, ita etiam, tenore promissionis divinæ, cum Josua eum fuisse certum est. At cum Mose ita fuit, ut eidem non per Angelum aliquem creatum, sed αὐτοπροσώπως præsto fuerit, eundemque cum populo deduxerit, quod ex Historia ipsa manife- stum est, & passim alias celebratur in Scriptura. Angelus enim ille, qui Ex. 23, 20. conductor eidem promissus est, non fuit creatus aliquis, & ministe- rialis Angelus πνεῦμα λειτεργικὸν, sed increatus Angelus, Dominus, cujus vocem audire tenebantur omnes, & qui potestatem habebat αὐτοκρατορικὴν, peccata dimittendi, vel non dimittendi. Quapropter etiam cum Josua ita fuisse Dominum credendum est. Quod e tota etiam Historia Josuæ apparet, quia nuspiam per Angelum quendam creatum egit, aut adstitit eidem, aut compellavit ipsum. Nuspiam Angelus creatus eidem apparuisse, aut ut opitulator eidem subvenisse, legitur in universa ejusdem historia. Deinde e promissione populo facta manifestum est, qualisnam vir hic apparuerit. Ta- cta jam est illa promissio e cap. 23. vers. 20. Exod. qua pollicitus erat Dominus: Ecce ego mittam An- gelum meum, qui præcedat te, & custodiat in via, & in locum introducat, quem paravi; & v. 23. Præcedet te Angelus meus, & introducet te ad Amorrhæum, & Hethæum &c. Quod ergo illi promissum fuit, id hic reipsa præstatur. Unde instar loci paralleli ad hunc textum margini adscribitur Exod. 23. vers. 23. Neque de eo facile quis dubitaverit, hic ejus pol- licitationis præstandæ gratia virum illum compa- ruisse, eundemque esse Angelum illum, a DEO promissum populi Ducem. Quem vero, quia ipsummet Filium Dei fuisse, annotatis ad istum lo- cum docuimus, eundem etiam hic Josuæ opitula- torem se ostentafse, statuendum est. Tertio Argu- mentum minime obscurum est ab nomine viri hu- jus, qui sese appellat Principem exercitus Domini v. 14. atque ita etiam a Spir. S. appellatur v. 15. Hoc namque nomine creatus Angelus indigitari non potest. Quisquis enim ex Angelis creatis nomine- tur, eum certum est fore aliquem ex ipso Exercitu Domini: quo nomine omnes Angelos compre- hendi e Gen. 32. vers. 2. 1. Reg. 22. v. 19. & Neh. 9. v. 6. Psal. 103. v. 21. Luc. 2. v. 13. liquet. Qui ergo ab Angelis creatis per exercitum Domini designatis distinguitur, tanquam Dux & Princeps eorum, is non est ipse Angelus aliquis creatus. Nam si esset, sub illo exercitu comprehenderetur, a quo tamen hunc Principem distingui videmus. Neque incom- mode simul comprehenditur nomine Exercitus Domini (nisi sola illa hic ita designetur, quod qui- busdam placet) militans Ecclesia, quæ ordinata est, ut castrorum acies ordinata, Cant. 6, 13. Ps. 68, 13. 14. cujus Princeps non est Angelus aliquis creatus, sed solus DEI Filius. Nec vero uspiam Angelo alicui creato hujusmodi axioma tribuitur, ut Princeps Exercitus Domini vocetur, quod soli DEO pro- prium est; is enim vocatur Princeps exercitus cœli Dan. 8. v. 11. Quod ad magnum Ducem Michaelem attinet Dan. 12. v. 1. per eum Filium Dei intelligi alias demonstrabitur, & e collatione Apoc. 12. v. 7. haud obscure patet, ac penes plerosq; Doctores, si heterodoxos excipias, in confesso est. Quapropter Filium Dei etiam hic eo sese designasse nomine cre- dimus, qui Angelis omnibus præest, eorumque Princeps est; Huic enim serviunt, hunc venerantur & adorant omnes Psal. 97. v. 7. Ebr. 1. v. 6. Matth. 4. v. 11. Apoc. 5. v. 12. unde Origenes hic: Quis enim alius est Princeps militiæ virtutum Domini, nisi Do- minus noster Christus. Omnis namq; militia cœli, sive Angeli, sive Archangeli, sive virtutes, sive Domina- tiones, sive principatus, sive potestates, omnia hæc, quæ per ipsum facta sunt, sub ipso principe militant, qui est principum princeps, & qui largitur principibus principatum. Ulterius quarto confirmatur hoc e Jo- suæ veneratione & adoratione. Principem enim hunc exercitus Domini Josua Dux ipse populi summus, procidens in faciem suam adorat, eundemque Do- minum suum, & se servum ipsius vocat, quem ho- norem, viri Dei non Angelis creatis, sed Deo, An- gelorum Domino, exhibere consueverunt, neque admittunt Angeli creati hunc cultum, sed contra protestantur, se conservos esse virorum Dei, sibi ho- norem ejusmodi non deberi, sed soli Deo Ap. 20. v. 10. c. 22, 9. Quinto refellitur Grotianum com- mentum a demandata calceorum depositione. Jubet enim is, qui Josuæ apparet, calceos exuat de pedibus suis: quod locus, in quo stet, sanctus sit. Josuam ipsum virum Dei sanctum, impurum esse, atque indignum præsentia sua Sacrosancta innuens, quod de Ange- lo creato quis præsumat? Neutiquam profecto creatus Angelus id postulavit unquam, ut sancti Dei viri calceos sibi exuant. Qui id postulavit Ex. 3. a Mose, Deus ipse fuit, Deus Abrahe, Deus Isaac, Deus Jacob, Jehovah: Et quidem Filius æternus Dei, Secunda S. S. Trinitatis persona. Quod περι- στάσεις historiæ & parallela loca ibidem confirma- runt. Ideoque ex Analogia & collatione istius ap- paritionis colligendum potius, Filium Dei hic pa- riter Josuæ, ut bellatorem, visum esse, quum is pu- gnaturus esset cum hostibus, donec illos expugnaret bellis perpetuis, qui Mosi in rubo ardente visus est, quum is populum afflictum e fornace ignea edu- cturus esset. Ut Sacerdotes in tabernaculo deservi- entes nudis pedibus Sacra peragere debebant, re- ferente Theodoreto q. 7. in Exod. quod ob præsen- tiam divinam factum; ita quum hic calceos exuere jubetur Josua, præsentiam divinam innui certum est. Deus ergo ipse non vero angelus creatus, hic apparuit. Sexto e Terræ sanctificatione peculiare de- promi potest argumentum, unde enim est, quod di- cit, quia locus, in quo stas, sanctus est? Terra certe illa per se sancta non erat, sed abominationibus multis defœdata, imo maledicta a Domino, & anathema- ti dicata, ideoq; sanctificatam eam fuisse oportet, ac a maledictione divina interea, dum ibi Princeps exercitus Domini stabat, liberatam: quia sanctior censebatur, quam ut ferret præsentiam Josuæ, nisi ipse calceos exueret: quo Symbolo ejus impuri- tas, ac præparatio ad majorem sanctitatem, loci- que sanctioris æstimatio designatur. Ab Ange- lo autem creato ita terram ab ipso Domino ma- ledictam sanctificari, nemo dixerit. Sancto Sancto- rum, Filio Dei, qui omnem maledictionem unus tollit, omnisq; sanctitatis fons est & origo, id debe- tur; Qui sanctificavit hanc terram, ut nunc appari- tioni & adventui suo, tum adventui in carnem, na- tivitati & muneri docendi, cujus illic Symbolum erat, consecraretur. Septim. proinde observari po- test peculiare argumentum e Symbolica Apparitione. Forma enim viri, in qua istis locis visus est Prin- ceps exercitus Domini ad tempus assumpta, apprime convenit ipsi Filio Dei, qui vir Dominus appellatus est, & nomine איש, cum de adventu ipsius in carnem agitur, designatur Gen. 4, 1. Zach. 6, 12. atq; eo Sym- bolo suam ἐνσάρκωσιν præfiguravit; cum nempe ut vir quidam apparuit Gen. 32. vers. 23. Ezech. 8. v. 2. Fatetur quidem Angelos etiam in forma viri ap- paruisse, sed hic vir singularis prorsus est, iisq; cir- cumstantiis vestitus conspicitur, quæ Filium Dei, fortem illum bellatorem Psal. 24, 8. virum pugnato- rem, cujus dextera magnificata est, Ex. 15, 3. 6. non Angelum creatum exhibeant. Quod cumprimis Octavo e Jehovah denominatione invicte docetur. Id enim nomen nulli creato Angelo uspiam tribui- tur. Hic vero vir postquam præparasset & conse- crasset Josuam ad audiendum præcepta sua, quem- admodum diximus, jam, quid velit, & quid facto opus sit, docet. De quo textus cap. 6. v. 2. Dixitq́ DOMINUS ad Josuam: Ecce dedi tibi in manum tu- am Jericho. Eundem enim qui jusserat παρασκευῆς ἕνεκα, solve calceamentum, hic continuare oratio- nem suam, dubium nullum est. Alioquin inutilis fuisset illa apparitio, nullumque finem habuisset, si nempe nihil aliud vir ille mandasset, quam cal- ceamentorum depositionem. Quum itaq; aperte Spiritus sanctus virum illum Dominum Jehovam appellet, quis tam duræ frontis erit, ut Angelum creatum ipsum dicat? cui nec tribuitur uspiam, nec vere tribui potest eminentissimum illud nomen, uni solique Deo proprium. Per virum autem Domi- num Messiam intelligi scripturis prorsus consenta- neum, Gen. 4, 1. Es. 9, 6. utpote θεάνθρωπος est, & futuram suam ἐνανθρώπησιν ejusmodi apparitioni- bus præfigurare consuevit. Ne quicquam autem hic interferit Grotius verba per Angelum. Non enim per Angelum Dominus dixisse dicitur, sed vir ille, qui apparuit, Dominus ipse fuisse indigitatur. Neque integrum est, cum Dominus aliquid dixisse perhibetur, angelum ingerere, alioquin nulla θεο- φανεία, nulla immediata Dei λαλιὰ relinquetur. Et parili facilitate semper, cum verbum Domini ad Prophetas factum dicitur, Angelus intermedius ingeri poterit. Adhæc per integram Josuæ Histo- riam, ubi Jehovah eidem loquutus dicitur, quod sæpius occurrit, Jehovam ipsum immediate, non mediante Angelo, loquutum esse constat: Neque dispar exemplum dabitur. Nullum ergo dubium, Deum hæc loqui, quemadmodum etiam Oratio ipsa ita comparata est, ut nulli Dei legato, sed uni- ce ipsi Deo conveniat. Unde nonum Argumentum nascitur ab αὐτοκρατορικῇ hostium devictione. Ecce inquit Princeps ille Exercitus Domini, dedi in ma- num tuam Jericho & Regem ejus, omnesq́, fortes vi- ros. Qua oratione uti nulla creatura potest. A Deo enim sola victoria est Deut. 31. vers. 29. Psalm. 18. vers. 30. Ps. 108, 14. 118, 11. 144, 10. Prov. 21, 31. unde conclusio invicta: Qui sibi ut auctori victoriam hostium & civitatis αὐτοκρατορικὴν vindicat, ean- demque & infallibiliter prædicit, & miraculose præstat, is verus est Deus. At vir ille, Princeps Exer- citus Domini sic vindicat sibi victoriam, quam hic prædixit, summoque miraculo prostratis muris civitatis per solum buccinarum clangorem repor- tavit. Proinde non est angelus creatus, sed verus DEUS. Quibus denique accedit Autoritas ve- terum, Justini Martyris Dialog. cum Tryph. p. 221. Fuit quando archiducem seipsum dixit (verbum) in hominis forma Josuae Nave filio apparens. Orige- nis item hom. 6. in Jos. Cognovit Josua, non solum, quod ex Deo esset, sed quia Deus est. Non enim adorasset, nisi agnovisset Deum. Quis enim alius est Princeps militiae virtutum Domini, nisi Dominus no- ster Jesus Christus. Cyprian. lib. 2. adversus Jud. cap. 18. qui hinc probat, quod Christus sit Sponsus, Ec- clesiam habens Sponsam, quia Josuam jussit excalcea- re se, quod scil. ipse sponsus non esset. Erat enim in Lege, ut quisquis nuptias recusaret, calceamentum deponeret, calcearetur vero ille, qui Sponsus esset. Eu- seb. lib. 1. Hist. Eccl. cap. 2. & aliorum. Agnove- runt id etiam e Judaeis nonnulli: Librum Tanhum, nec non Rabbi Mosen Gerundensem allegat Masius comment. in h. l. Trypho ipse Judaeus, cum locum istum Justinus adduxisset de Filio Dei, victas dedit manus, & ἰσχυρῶς fortiter ac praevalide id demon- stratum esse, professus est in Dial. p. 222. Nec ta- men id agnoscere in tanta luce voluit Grotius, Christianus, caeco Judaeo longe caecior. Pontifi- ciis caeteris opponit sese Masius, Filium DEI hoc loco apparuisse, nobiscum asserens. Neque con- cedit Tostatus, Michaelem Angelum intelligendum esse, sed adversus Sociennos suos probare conatur, Gabrielem principalem egisse gentis Ebraeorum curam, atque hic apparuisse. Denique quum Pontificiis assurgere libuerit Grotio, quaeri potest, quia illi duos cum Gregorio M. faciunt Angelorum ordines, alios quidem assistentes; alios vero ministrantes, ex utro ordine hic Angelus fuerit? Si ex assistentium ordine fuit, quomodo missus est? siquidem illi nunquam mitti censeantur: si ex ministrantium, quomodo Principem Exercitus Domini, adeoque Angelum sese professus est.

AND EVERYONE WENT UP BY THE PLACE WHICH WAS OPPOSITE HIM) A surrounding formation was made.

## 6:23
AND THEY MADE THEM REMAIN OUTSIDE THE CAMP OF ISRAEL) Namely, until Rahab and the women were aggregated to the people through baptism, and the males of her house through circumcision.

What sort of baptism Grotius understands, and whence he has these things, that women ought to have been aggregated to the people through baptism, just as males through circumcision, let others see; it is certain from the scriptures that circumcision, as a sacrament of initiation and a means of salvation and a seal of the righteousness of faith, was divinely ordained for male infants: in its place, and for a like purpose, any baptism in

That it existed in the Old Testament, destined for women or infants of the female sex, appears nowhere in the Scriptures.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET EXTRA CASTRA ISRAEL MANERE FECERVNT) Donec scilicet Rahab & foeminae per bapti- smum, mares de domo ejus per circumcisionem populo ag- gregarentur.

Qualemnam baptismum intelligat Grotius, & unde haec habeat, quod per Baptismum foemi- nae, perinde uti mares per circumcisionem populo aggregari debuerint, alii viderint, id e scripturis certum est, circumcisionem, ceu sacramentum initiationis & medium salutis ac sigillum justitiae fidei, masculis infantibus divinitus ordinatum esse: Ejus loco, ac parili fine baptismum ullum in

Veteri Testamento fuisse, pro mulieribus vel in- fantibus foeminei sexus destinatum, nuspiam in Scripturis comparet.

## 6:25
Verse 25. AND THEY DWELT IN THE MIDST OF ISRAEL UNTO THIS PRESENT DAY) Similar to 4,9 above. Was this added by Joshua, or by Ezra?

Vers. 25. ET HABITAVERUNT IN MEDIO ISRAEL VSQVE IN PRÆSENTEM DIEM) Simile supra 4,9. A Josua hoc, an ab Esdra additum?

## 6:26
Verse 26. CURSED BE THE MAN BEFORE THE LORD, THAT RAISETH UP, AND BUILDETH THE CITY JERICHO) Namely, so that the memory of so celebrated a victory might always be in sight. The Greeks call this καταρᾶσθαι. Strabo in book XIII, concerning Ilium: 'so that even when Agamemnon's city was cursed according to ancient custom, just as Croesus, having taken Sidyne, into which the tyrant Glaucias had fled, laid curses upon those who would wall the place again.' God, however, held the curses of Joshua to be ratified, as appears in 1 Kings 16:34.

Latin:

Vers. 26. MALEDICTVS VIR CORAM DOMINO, QVI SVSCITAVERIT, ET ÆDIFICAVERIT CIVI- TATEM JERICHO) Nempe ut tam celebris victoriæ me- moria semper in conspectu esset. Hoc καταρᾶσθαι dicunt Græci. Strabo libro XIII. de Ilio: ὥστε καὶ κατηρασμένης τῆς Ἀγαμέμνονος κατὰ παλαιὸν ἔθος, καθάπερ καὶ ὁ Κροῖσος ἐξελὼν τὴν Σιδήνην εἰς ἣν ὁ τύραννος κατέφυγε Γλαυκίας, ἀρὰς ἔθετο κατὰ τῶν τειχιούντων πάλιν τὸν τόπον. Josuæ au- tem diras ratas Deus habuit, ut apparet 1. Reg. 16,34.

## 7:6
ver. 6. HE RENT HIS GARMENTS. A rite accustomed to be used in mourning, in grave calamity, and in wickedness for which one should mourn, and in public penance. Cf. Gen. 37, 34. Matth. 26, 65. Joel 2, 13.

AND THEY CAST DUST UPON THEIR HEADS. This was also a habit of mourners, and a sign of humility and penance 1 Sam. 4, 12. Job 4, 12. ch. 42, 6. Esth. 4, 1. Is. 46, 1. Ez. 27, 30. Dan. 9, 2. Jon. 3, 6. It was also used by profane nations: but it was first given to our first parents Gen. 3, 19.

Latin:

vers. 6. SCIDIT VESTIMENTA SUA. Ritus in luctu, gravi calamitate, & flagitio, ob quod lugeatur, ac pœnitentia publica adhiberi solitus. Conf. Gen. 37, 34. Matth. 26, 65. Joel. 2, 13.

MISERUNTQUE PULVEREM SUPER CAPITA SUA. Fuit & hic habitus lugentium, ac signum hu- militatis, & pœnitentiæ 1. Sam. 4, 12. Job. 4, 12. cap. 42.6. Esth. 4, 1. Ef. 46, 1. Ez. 27. 30. Dan. 9, 2. Jon. 3, 6. usurpatum etiam a prophanis gentibus: at pri- mum datum protoplastis Gen. 3, 19.

## 7:8
ver. 8. MY LORD. In Hebrew, IN ME. Which some interpret as an interjection of one beseeching, 'I beseech,' others 'κατὰ πόδα' [at the foot], namely, 'look upon me,' that you may behold me with kind eyes.

Latin:

vers. 8. MI DOMINE. In Ebr. IN ME. Quod nonnulli interpre- tantur ceu interjectionem obsecrantis, obsecro, alii κατὰ πόδα in me scil. respice, ut benignis oculis me intuearis.

## 7:9
ver. 9. THEY SHALL BLOT OUT OUR NAME FROM THE EARTH, AND WHAT WILL YOU DO FOR YOUR GREAT NAME?

The sense is, since they are about to blot out our name, whom you have taken into your people and raised up to this place with such great wonders, what will become of your name? Our name is of little importance, but will the honor of your name be consulted in this way if you blot us out? For you promised us this land, and by what people will your name be worshipped if you have now blotted out our name? This is an effective prayer, and it compels God to have mercy: such as are frequently found in the works of the great Luther. And similar ones are held in Ex. 32, 12. Num. 14, 13. Deut. 9, 28.

Latin:

vers. 9. DELEBUNT NOMEN NOSTRUM DE TERRA, ET QUID FACIES MAGNO NOMINI TUO?

Sensus est, cum deleturi sint nomen nostrum, quos assumsisti in populum tuum, & tantis pro- digiis huc evexisti, quid fiet nomini tuo? Exigui momenti est nomen nostrum, sed num consule- tur ita honori nominis tui, si nos deleveris: Nam promisisti nobis hanc terram, & a quo populo nomen toum coletur, si nomen nostrum jam de- leveris? Efficax haec est oratio, ac Deum cogit ad miserendum: quales frequentes penes Mega- landrum Lutherum reperiuntur. Et habentur similes Ex. 32, 12. Num. 14, 13. Deut. 9, 28.

## 7:10
Ver. 10. ARISE, WHY DO YOU LIE PROSTRATE ON THE EARTH? There is no place here for deprecation: nor can the people be expiated except by the punishment of the source of the sin.

The words are rather those of one raising up than of one terrifying; therefore Osiander more correctly says 'παραθρασύνει' [he encourages]: you are too fearful and dismayed. I will not utterly forsake my people: nor will I make my promises void, nor will I allow my name to be blasphemed among the nations. I will cause you to know what must be done to repair the disaster.

Latin:

Vers. 10. SVRGE CVR JACES PRONVS IN TERRA) Nullus hic deprecandi locus: neque nisi poena fontis expia- ri populus potest.

Verba potius sunt erigentis, quam terrentis, ideo rectius Osiander παραθρασύνει: nimium es me- ticulosus & consternatus. Non ego in universum deseram populum meum: neq; irritas faciam pro- missiones meas, neq; concedam, ut nomen meum in- ter gentes blasphemetur. Faciam, ut scias, quid facto sit opus ad cladem resarciendam.

## 7:11
Verse 11. BUT THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL HAVE TRANSGRESSED THE COMMANDMENT) The people are held accountable for the crime committed by one against God, until he has punished it. Thus, in Virgil, the Achaean fleet is burned: 'For the guilt and madness of one, Ajax the son of Oileus.' Namely, because when Ajax was seizing Cassandra, 'he suffered nothing from the Achaeans, nor did he hear from them,' as Euripides speaks.

The community is not indeed ordinarily held accountable for the crime of one person, but God sometimes shows by a public disaster, on account of one person's crime, with how much hatred He pursues sin, especially where He has published a prohibition to the whole community: and He warns that magistrates should keep watch over individuals, lest the sin of one redound upon the whole congregation, or the contagion infect it all, and that individuals also should be solicitous about their own places, lest they bring destruction upon them.

ACHAN THE SON OF CHARMI, THE SON OF ZABDI. In the passage 1 Chron. 2:7 he is called Achar: and his grandfather is called Zamri. Each therefore had two names, and Achan was truly called Achar, from עכר, he troubled, because, as is held in the cited place, he troubled Israel. Hence the name of the place was the valley of Achor, Josh. 7:26.

Latin:

Vers. 11. FILII AVTEM ISRAEL PRÆVARICATI SVNT MANDATVM) Ex crimine unius in Deum com- misso tenetur populus, donec punierit. Sic apud Virgilium exuritur classis Achiva: Vnius ob noxam & furias Ajacis Oilei. Nempe quia cum Cassandram Ajax raperet, οὐδέν γ᾽ Ἀχαιοῖσιν ἔπαθεν, οὐδ᾽ ἤκουσ᾽ ὕπο, ut Euripides loquitur.

NOn tenetur quidem ordinarie ex unius cri- mine communio, sed Deus quandoq; publi- ca clade ob unius crimen ostendit, quanto odio prosequatur peccatum, maxime ubi toti commu- nioni interdictum publicavit: monetq; ut tum Magistratus singulis invigilent, ne unius pecca- tum in totam congregationem redundet, aut eam totam contagio inficiat, tum singuli etiam de locis suis soliciti sint, ne exitium iisdem accersant.

ACHAN FILIUS CHARMI, FILII ZABDI. In loco 1. Par. 2, 7. dicitur Achar: & avus vocatur Zamri. Fuit ergo binominis uterque, & vere Achan dictus est Achar, ab עכר turbavit, quia ut habetur l. c. turbavit Israel. Inde nomen loci fuit, vallis Achor Jos. 7, 26.

## 7:21
Verse 19.

MY SON, GIVE GLORY TO THE LORD GOD OF ISRAEL) It seems to be rightly gathered from this that there is some hope regarding the persistence of souls after death. For by what other hope was this man led to confess a capital crime? It is, however, the opinion of the Jews that by confession and death, pardon for such crimes is obtained from God. We have here a formula for the examination of the accused. Thus also witnesses were interrogated. See what is noted at John 9:24.

Just as we easily admit that the faithful Jews cherished hope regarding the persistence of souls after death, so we are certain that they held not just SOME doubtful or PROBABLE hope, such as Grotius, along with the Socinians, attributes to the Jews, but a hope entirely certain and indubitable, resting on the faith of a promise; for they certainly had promises of eternal life, and who would doubt that the believers of that time added faith to them? Job is an illustrious example, who sustained himself with that faith, chapter 19:29. And how could the Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and other faithful ones be set before us as an example of faith to stir up patience, so that we may obtain the promise, which is done at length in chapter 11 of the golden Epistle to the Hebrews, if they themselves could not have faith in eternal life from divine promises? How could the Old Scripture be able to make us wise unto salvation through faith in Christ, how could we have solid hope from it through patience and consolation, both of which the Apostle attributes to the same in 2 Tim. 3:15 and Rom. 15:4, if it offered no promise of salvation and life?

It is no wonder that Grotius, Judaizing in many things, praises the opinion of the Jews regarding the manner of obtaining pardon for more serious crimes. But where has Scripture taught that pardon for crimes is obtained from God through confession and death? Scripture always requires repentance, and thus true contrition, to which confession and faith pertain; but just as faith alone is what receives the remission of sins, with all the Prophets as witnesses in Acts 10:43, so without faith there is no saving confession or contrition, or sorrow according to God, 2 Cor. 7:10, because without faith it is impossible to please God, Heb. 11:6. Death does nothing to obtain pardon, but if it is to be suffered for offenses, it is the punishment of sin, not a means or method of obtaining pardon.

SCARLET CLOAK) In Hebrew: אדרת שנער, that is, a Babylonian cloak, for שנער is Babylonia. See Gen. 11:2. Σεναὰρ τῆς Βαβυλωνίας in Hestiaeus the Milesian, Singara in Ptolemy and Pliny, Singarana in Sextus Rufus: Babylon most celebrated weaving diverse colors into pictures, and gave it its name, says Pliny in book 8, c. 48. Hence also 'Babylonica' to the poets.

AND COVETING I TOOK) Well, for ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν. James 1:15.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

FILI DA GLORIAM DOMINO DEO ISRAEL) Vi- detur hinc recte colligi spes aliqua de animorum permansio- ne post mortem. Qua enim alia spe adductus hic homo est, ut crimen capitale fateretur? Est autem sententia Judæorum, confessione & morte criminum talium veniam a Deo impe- trari. Formulam hic habemus examinis reorum. Sic & te- stes interrogabantur. Vide quæ notata ad Joan. 9, 24.

Ut facile admittimus spem de animorum per- mansione post mortem fovisse Judæos fideles, ita non tantum spem ALIQUAM dubiam, vel PROBA- BILEM, qualem cum Socinianis Grotius tribuit Judæis, sed spem omnino certam & indubiam, fide promissionis nixam, eosdem habuisse, certi sumus; quia habuere utiq; promissiones vitæ æternæ, qui- bus fidem credentes istius temporis adjunxisse ec- quis ambiget? Exemplo illustri est Job, qui fide ista se sustentavit cap. 19, 29. Et quomodo nobis in fidei exemplum Patriarchæ Abraham, Isaac & Ja- cob, aliique fideles, ad patientiam excitandam sisti possent, quo promissionem consequamur, quod prolixe c. 11. aureæ ad Ebræos Epistolæ factum, si fidem æternæ vitæ e promissis divinis habere ne- quiverint ipsi? quomodo Scriptura Vetus ad salu- tem per fidem in Christum nos σοφίσαι sapientes redde- re posset, quomodo ex illa per patientiam & consola- tionem spem solidam habere possemus, quod utrumq; eidem tribuit Apostolus 2. Tim. 3, 15. Rom. 15, 4. si salutis & vitæ nullam exhiberet promissionem?

Judæorum sententiam, de modo veniam conse- quendi criminum graviorum, non mirum laudare Grotium, Judaizantem in plurimis: Sed ubi Scriptu- ra per confessionem & mortem criminum a Deo veniam impetrari docuit? Pœnitentiam semper re- quirit Scriptura, adeoq; veram contritionem, ad quam pertinet Confessio & fides; sed uti fides sola est, quæ accipit remissionem peccatorum, testibus omnibus Prophetis Act. 10, 43. Ita sine fide nulla est salutaris confessio aut contritio, vel tristitia se- cundum Deum 2. Cor. 7, 10. quia sine fide impossi- bile est placere Deo Ebr. 11, 6. Mors ad veniam im- petrandam nihil facit, sed si pro delictis luenda est, pœna est peccati, non medium vel ratio veniæ consequendæ.

PALLIVM COCCINEVM) In Hebræo: אדרת שנער, id est, pallium Babylonicum, nam שנער Babylo- nia. Vide Gen. 11, 2. Σεναὰρ τῆς Βαβυλωνίας apud Histiæ- um Milesium, Singara Ptolomæo & Plinio, Singarana Sexto Rufo: Colores diversos picturæ intexere Babylon maxime cele- bravit, & nomen imposuit, ait Plinius libro 8. c. 48. Hinc Babylonica etiam Poëtis.

ET CONCVPISCENS ABSTVLI) Bene, nam ἡ ἐπιθυ- μία συλλαβῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν. Jac. 1, 15.

## 7:24
Verse 24.

AND HIS DAUGHTERS AND SONS) It may be explained that they were brought so that they might be instructed together with all the people by Joshua, and warned to beware of such things for themselves; not that they were to be killed with their father. Those who think thus, understand what follows, they stoned them (for so the Hebrew text has it, not him), as referring to Achan and his beasts.

Grotius follows the Jews. But this fiction is sufficiently refuted by the text. They were not brought to be spectators of the father's punishment. But just as the oxen and sheep with all the furniture of the tabernacle, and the tabernacle itself, so also the sons and daughters were brought with their father to destruction, not so much because they were free participants in the crime, as that Achan might be punished in them, and a divine fear and a greater detestation of sin might be struck into all Israel. For God is accustomed to involve children even in temporal punishments on account of the transgressions of their parents, but not in eternal ones, Ex. 20, 5. Deut. 13, 16. Num. 31, 7. 2 Sam. 21. Nor is there any doubt that the punishment is more grievous to parents when their children are condemned to punishment while they themselves are still living: yet it is not simply true, as Abulensis affirms here, that God never commands children to be killed for the guilt of their parents after their death. For the grandsons of Saul are also read to have been crucified on account of his crime, 2. Sam. 21. at the same time it was also signified, as Augustine notes, q. 8, how much evil would be done if that whole congregation had sinned, when not even one could be judged in such a way that the others could be secure from him.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

FILIAS QVOQVE ET FILIOS EJVS) Potest expo- ni eos adductos ut cum omni populo simul ab Josua erudi- rentur, monerenturque sibi a talibus cavere; non ut interfi- cerentur cum patre. Qui sic sentiunt, id quod sequitur la- pidarunt eos (ita enim habet textus Hebræus non eum) in- telligunt de Achane & jumentis ejus.

Sequitur Grotius Judæos. Sed e textu satis refellitur hoc commentum. Non adducti ut spe- ctatores sint paterni supplicii. Sed uti boves & oves cum omni suppellectile tabernaculi, & taber- naculum ipsum, ita filii quoq; & filiæ cum Patre ad- dicebantur exitio, non tam quod participes fuerint liberi delicti, quam ut in ipsis Achan puniretur, ac toti Israeli divinus timor, peccatiq; major detesta- tio incuteretur. Nam solet Deus etiam pœnis tem- poralibus liberos involvere ob parentum prævari- cationes, non autem æternis Ex. 20, 5. Deut. 13, 16. Num. 31, 7. 2. Sam. 21. Neq; dubium est, gravio- rem pœnam esse parentibus, cum ipsis adhuc vi- ventibus liberi supplicio addicuntur: nec tamen simpliciter verum, quod hic affirmat Abulensis, Deum nusquam jubere filios occidi ob culpam paren- tum post eorum necem. Nam & nepotes Saulis ob ejus scelus crucifixi leguntur 2. Sam. 21. simul etiam significatum est, ut monet August. q. 8. quantum mali fieret, si universa illa congregatio peccasset, quan- do ne unus quidem ita potuit judicari, ut ab eo cæteri possent esse securi.

## 7:25
Vers. 25.

BECAUSE YOU HAVE TROUBLED US) There is in the Hebrew an allusion to the similar words עכן and עכר. From this saying of Joshua the place received its name.

Indeed, it also received the name, if Achan was not already called Achar, 1 Chron. 2, 7, as we noted at verse 1.

MAY THE LORD TROUBLE YOU.

In the Hebrew, he will cast you out from the camps of Israel, and from the land of the living: these are not the words of one cursing to destruction, but of one threatening, or indicating from the mouth of God, or of a judge pronouncing sentence upon the guilty and confessed party. Because it is added IN THIS DAY, some take this as referring to temporal death. And indeed, it seems that only temporal destruction is indicated, even if it is not proven by that word, which only teaches that the punishment was to be taken from him immediately on that day. Cassian indeed and the Council of Aachen under Pepin condemn Achan: Augustine seems to doubt his salvation, quest. 9. But the Rabbis, Cajetan, Masius, Serarius, Megalian, Abulensis, Bonfrerius, and Cornel. a Lapide say that he was saved: because he humbly confessed his sin, truly I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel, and he did penance. What Cornel. adds, that he escaped eternal punishment through the satisfaction of stoning, and redeemed the eternal fire of Gehenna with a bodily fire, is repugnant to the analogy of faith, and is utterly absurd; because eternal punishment cannot be redeemed by temporal punishment, and no mortal can make satisfaction for the sin by which eternal guilt is contracted: and what need would there have been for the satisfaction and redemption of the eternal Son of God, if man could have satisfied divine justice with death and temporal punishment, and redeemed himself from eternal death? Meanwhile, Augustine, with whom we seize upon the τὸ ἐπέχειν, rightly pronounced that if Achan truly repented, he was not worthy of the fire of Gehenna: because true repentance includes faith, through which we are snatched from the fire of hell, not because we are not worthy of the same by our sins, but because GOD deems us worthy of grace and salvation in view of the faith, by which we are rendered worthy in Christ Eph. 1, 6. AND ALL ISRAEL STONED HIM. The sentence had been passed that he should be burned with fire v. 15. when therefore he is stoned, it must be believed that after he was stoned, he was cast into the fire, and with all his substance reduced to ashes: not, however, as Serarius and Bonfrer wish, that he was first burned alive, and then his ashes were covered with stones. For that gathering of a heap of stones over him, of which v. 25 speaks, is not the stoning itself: But the erection of a monument of the stoning and burning made forever, on account of the sacrilege. Vain is the opinion of the Hebrews that when Achan was being cremated with fire, a shower of stones was poured out, and he was thus killed by the people. But it contradicts verse 25, where stoning is placed before the cremation: which was the penalty for the violation of the Sabbath, committed also by Achan, as it seems to some, mentioned in Num. 15, 35.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

QVIA TVRBASTI NOS) Est in Hebræo allusio vi- cinarum vocum עכן & עכר. Ab hoc dicto Josuæ locus nomen accepit.

Imo nomen etiam accepit, si ante διώνυμος non fuit Achan, dictus Achar 1. Par. 2, 7. ut ad vers. 1. notavimus.

EXTVRBET TE DOMINVS.

In Ebræo, exturbabit e castris Israel, & e terra viventium: non sunt verba exitium imprecantis, sed comminantis, vel indicantis ex ore Dei, aut ju- dicis sententiam in reum & confessum promulgan- tis. Quia additur IN DIE HAC, de morte tempo- rali nonnulli hoc accipiunt. Et sane indicari vide- tur tantum temporale excidium, etiamsi illa voce id non probetur, quæ solum docet, statim illa die sup- plicium de ipso sumtum iri. Cassianus quidem & Concilium Aquisgran. sub Pipino damnant Acha- nem: August. dubitare videtur de ejus salute quæst. 9. salvatum autem eum esse Rabbini, Cajetan. Ma- sius, Serarius, Megalian. Abulensis, Bonfrerius, Cornel. a Lapide ajunt: quia humiliter confessus est peccatum, vere ego peccavi Domino Deo Israel, & pœnitentiam egit. Quod Cornel. addit, eum per satisfactionem lapidationis evasisse pœnam æternam, & incendio corporali redemisse incendium æternum gehennæ, analogiæ fidei repugnat, ac pror- sus absonum est; quia pœna temporali æterna pœ- na redimi, ac pro peccato, quo æternus reatus contrahitur, satisfieri, a nullo mortalium potest: & quid opus fuisset æterni Filii Dei satisfactione, ac redemtione, si homo morte ac pœna tempo- rali satisfacere justitiæ divinæ, seque a morte æter- na redimere potuisset? Interea Augustinus, cum quo τὸ ἐπέχειν arripimus, recte pronunciavit, si vere Achan pœnituit, dignus non erat igne gehennæ: quia vera pœnitentia fidem includit, per quam eri- pimur ab igne gehennæ, non quia peccatis nostris digni non sumus eodem, sed quia gratia & salute nos dignatur DEUS intuitu fidei, qua digni reddi- mur in Christo Eph. 1, 6. LAPIDAVITQUE EUM OMNIS ISRAEL. Sententia lata erat, ut igni combureretur v. 15. cum ergo lapidatur credendum, postquam lapida- tus est, in ignem conjectum, & cum omni substan- tia in cineres redactum: non autem ut Serarius & Bonfrer. vult, vivum prius combustum, deinde cineres ejus lapidibus obrutus esse. Nam con- gregatio illa acervi lapidum super eum, de qua v. 25. non est ipsa lapidatio: Sed acervi in perpetuum lapidationis & combustionis, ob sacrilegium fa- ctæ, monumentum erectio. Vana est Ebræorum opinio in Achanem cum igne cremaretur, lapi- dum imbrem effusum, eumq; ita interemtum a po- pulo. At repugnat vers. 25. ubi cremationi la- pidatio præmittitur: quæ pœna erat Sabbati vio- lationi, ab Achane etiam, ut quibusdam videtur, commissæ, dicta Num. 15, 35.

## 7:26
Verse 26. A GREAT HEAP OF STONES) an ignominious burial, as Josephus speaks here.

CHAPTER VIII. Ai is taken by storm. The Law is inscribed on stones. The people are blessed.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ACERVVM MAGNVM LAPIDVM) τα- φὴν ἄτιμον, ut hic loquitur Josephus.

CAPUT VIII. Hai expugnatur. Lex lapidibus inscribitur. Po- pulo benedicitur.

## 8:2
verse 2. HAI, WHICH IS BESIDE BETHAVEN ON THE EAST SIDE OF THE TOWN OF BETHEL.

Hai, by Josephus Ada, and Aina, by Jerome Agai, a city once most beautiful, and in the mountainous region, in Isaiah Ajath, through which Sennacherib passed, intending to attack Jerusalem, ch. 10. Compare Jer. 49:1, Ezra 2:2. Adrichomius says it is situated on the western side of Bethel, not far distant from it. But here it is openly established on the eastern side, and it is also placed thus in the very chorography of Adrichomius. Bethaven is distinguished in this place from Bethel, which nevertheless was surnamed Bethaven in Hosea 4, that is, the house of iniquity or vanity on account of the idols placed there by Jeroboam. Some deny that Bethaven existed before the idolatry of Jeroboam: but this passage confirms it: because those two neighboring towns, Bethel and Bethaven, are introduced here: on account of which proximity Bethel obtained the name of the other, Bethaven, because the idolatry instituted there deserved it.

Latin:

vers. 2. HAI, QUÆ EST JUXTA BET- AVEN AD ORIENTALEM PLAGAM OP- PIDI BETHEL.

Hai Josepho Ada, & Aina, Hieronymo A- gai, civitas quondam pulcherrima, & in montanis, in Esaia Ajath, per quam Sennacherib transiit, op- pugnaturus Jerusalem c. 10. Conf. Jer. 49, 1. Esdr. 2, 2. Eam ad occidentalem plagam Bethelis dicit si- tam Adrichomius, non multum ab ea distantem. Sed hic ad orientalem plagam aperte constituitur, & ita etiam in ipsa chorographia Adrich. collo- cata est. Bethaven distinguitur hoc loco a Bethel, quæ tamen Bethaven cognominata est Os. 4. hoc est, domus iniquitatis vel vanitatis ob collocata ibi- dem idola, a Jeroboamo. Fuisse Bethaven ante Idololatriam Jeroboami nonnulli negant: Sed hic locus id confirmat: quia ut vicina illa duo oppi- da Bethel & Bethaven hic introducuntur: ob quam viciniam Bethel nomen alterius Bethaven, quia merebatur id idololatria ibi instituta, consequu- ta est.

## 8:2
Verse 2. SET AN AMBUSH) For who would ask in an enemy whether it be deceit or valor? See what has been said by us in the third book of the Law of War and Peace, ch. 1, §. and the 6 following.

Xenophon indeed in the Hipparchicus says, Nothing is more useful in war than deceits; but military stratagems are not culpable deceits. Because no injustice intervenes there, nor is faith given to the enemy broken, but the matter is managed by military skill and prudence, by which it happens that the enemy's war plans are hidden, and victory is more certain, and is obtained with less loss of soldiers. Therefore Augustine, q. 10 on John: When a just war is undertaken, whether one fights with open force or from ambush, it makes no difference to justice. But flight itself by design signifies nothing (as words by design have their meaning) even if the enemies accept it as a sign of fear, which the other party of the combatants is not bound to prevent, using their liberty of going here or there, and more or less quickly, and with this or that gesture or bearing. The matter is likewise one way in words, another in deeds; because the former signify by convention, therefore in them deceit brings in a lie, and is illicit, whence Cajetan: a lie is not committed as easily by deeds as by words. For words are properly instituted to signify the concepts of the mind, not deeds. Nor did Joshua flee to signify that he feared the men of Ai, even if they interpreted it so, but to lure them out of the city to pursue him; but that they interpreted this flight in such a way, he was not bound to prevent. The flight, however, was in reality material, not formal: they were fleeing, that is, they were turning their backs. Therefore they do not lie, nor do those who flee in such a way intend to signify a true flight by turning their backs; even if the enemies, thinking they are truly fleeing, deceive themselves by their own suspicion and imprudent and rash judgment.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PONE INSIDIAS) Nam Dolus an virtus, quis in hoste requirat? Vide quæ dicta nobis libro de Jure Belli & Pacis tertio c. 1. §. & 6. sequentibus.

XEnophon sane in Hipparcho, Nihil, ait, in bello dolis utilius; sed strategemata bellica non sunt doli culpabiles. Quia nulla ibi intervenit in- justicia, nec fides hosti data frangitur, sed solertia & prudentia militari res geritur, qua fit, ut & ho- stibus belli consilia occultentur, ac victoria cer- tior sit, & minori militum jactura comparetur. Ideo Augustin. qv. 10. in Joh. Cum justum bellum suscipitur, vi aperta pugnet quis, aut ex insidiis, nihil ad justitiam interest. Fuga autem ipsa ex instituto nihil significat (uti verba ex instituto suam signifi- cationem habent) licet hostes eam acceptent, ut signum pavoris, quod altera bellantium pars cavere non tenetur utens libertate sua huc vel illuc eundi, & magis minusve celeriter, & hoc vel illo gestu ha- bituve. Aliter item; se res habet in vocibus, aliter in factis; quia illæ significant κατὰ συνθήκην, ideo in iis dolus mendacium infert, ac illicitus est, unde Cajetanus: mendacium non tam facile committitur factis quam verbis. Verba enim proprie instituta sunt ad significandum mentis conceptus, non facta. Neq; fugit Josua, ut significaret, se metuere Ha- jenses, etsi illud ita hi interpretarentur, sed ut eos ex urbe eliceret ad se insequendum, quod vero hi fugam hanc ita interpretati fuerint, id præcavere ipse non tenebatur. Fuga revera tamen mate- rialis erat, non formalis: fugiebant, id est, terga ver- tebant. Non ergo mentiuntur, nec fugam veram terga vertentes significare intendunt, qui ita fu- giunt; licet hostes putantes eos vere fugere, su- spicione, ac imprudenti, & temerario judicio suo seipsos fallant.

## 8:7
ver. 7. WE HAD REMAINED BEYOND THE JOR-

A lapse and lack of confidence by Joshua: For they had not crossed over by their own will, but by divine command. Too quickly did the threefold exhortation of Jos. 1, 6, 'be strong and of good courage,' slip from his mind. Truly, therefore, the Psalmist says that all Saints ought to seek the remission of sins, Ps. 32, 6. He wishes, however, that he had remained beyond the Jordan, namely in the kingdoms of Og and Bashan: but how then would he have occupied the promised land, for which task he was divinely chosen and confirmed?

Latin:

vers. 7. MANSSISSEMUS TRANS JOR- DANEM.

Lapsus & diffidentia Josuae: Transierant enim non suopte arbitrio, sed jussu divino. Nimis cito excidit animo trina paraenesis Jos. 1, 6. confortare & esto robustus. Vere ergo Psaltes quod omnes Sanctos oporteat petere remissionem peccatorum Psal. 32, 6. Optat autem ut mansisset trans - Jorda- nem in regnis nempe Og & Basan: sed quomodo ita occupasset terram promissam, ad quod munus divinitus electus & confirmatus fuit?

## 8:12
verse 12. BUT HE HAD CHOSEN FIVE THOUSAND MEN, AND HAD SET THEM IN AMBUSH.

Regarding the 30,000 chosen for the ambush, it is held in verse 3. It must be said, therefore, that 5,000 were ordered so that when the men of Ai went out, they would invade and burn the city, but the remaining 25,000 were destined to be a help to the 5,000 who were to invade the city, if they were discovered or attacked, and to join themselves with Joshua, who was already fighting in open battle, from the side: or also to occupy the side paths and safer places, because perhaps flight could have been open through that valley, if it happened that the men of Ai fled and sought an exit for flight.

BETWEEN BETHEL AND AI) Thus also the Hebrew books which we use. But the Oriental books [read] Beth-Aven, and certain Greek codices [read] Beth-Aven, which name was given to Bethel in place of a reproach, from the time it served profane rites. Therefore, where in Hosea 4:15 it is in the text Beth-Aven, Jonathan placed Bethel, which exposition Amos 5:5 confirms.

Our codices are correct: because at that time Bethel had not yet been dishonored by the name Beth-Aven; indeed, Beth-Aven was distinct from Bethel, as is evident from Joshua 7:2.

ON THE WESTERN SIDE OF THE SAME CITY) From the Hebrew which we use, in which [it is] to the city. But the Oriental codices [read] to the city as above [verse] 9. Thus also the Greeks [read] from the sea of the land, and the Chaldean here [reads] no differently.

This discrepancy of reading varies nothing in the sense. For the subject matter teaches that the city of Ai is understood. There is, therefore, no reason why our reading should be rejected. The Chaldean and the Greeks had employed the proper name of the city for the sake of explanation.

Latin:

vers. 12. QUINQUE AUTEM MILLIA VIROS ELEGERAT, ET POSUERAT IN INSIDIIS.

De 30000. ad insidias electis habetur vers. 3. Dicendum ergo quod 5000. ordinata fuerint, ut egressis Hajensibus urbem invaderent & confla- grarent, reliqua vero 25000. destinata, ut insidiis quing, millium urbem invasuris, si illæ detegeren- tur, aut invaderentur, auxilio essent, utq; se se cum Josua, aperto marte jam pugnante, a latere con- jungerent: vel etiam ut diverticula & loca tutio- ra occuparent, quia forte poterat patere fuga per vallem illum, si contingeret Hajenses refugere & exitum ad fugam quærere.

INTER BETHEL ET HAI) Sic & Hebræi libri qui- bus utimur. At Orientales libri בית־און, & Græci quidam Codices βηθαὺν, quod nomen probri loco datum Betheli, ex quo profanis ritibus serviit. Ideo ubi in Osea 4, 15. est in textu בית־און Jonathan posuit Bethel, quam expositionem firmat Amosus 5, 5.

Recte se habent Codices nostri: quia tum non- dum Bethel nomine Beth-Aven dehonestatum, imo Beth-Aven a Bethel distinctum fuit, ut e Jos. 7, 2. constat.

EX OCCIDENTALI PARTE EJUSDEM CIVITA- TIS) Ex Hebræo, quo utimur, in quo לעיר. At Orien- tales Codices עי ut supra 9. Sic & Græci ἀπὸ τῆς θα- λάσσης τῆς γαὶ, nec aliter hic Chaldæus.

Nihil in sensu variat hæc discrepantia lectio- nis. Urbem enim Hai intelligi, materia substra- ta docet. Non ergo causa est, cur nostra lectio re- probetur. Chaldæus & Græci proprium nomen ur- bis adhibuerant, explicationis gratia.

## 8:13
Ver. 13.

AND HE STOOD IN THE MIDST OF THE VALLEY) For the sake of meditating and praying, as it seems, having advanced outside the camp, which was in the same valley. See Gen. 24:62.

Others say that he stood there with the army. For there is here a recapitulation. And the order of the event is as follows: that Joshua, having sent the ambush ahead by night, followed them with the whole people that same night to the middle of the valley, but in such a way that the greater part was covered by a hill, ditches, chariots, or woods, so that the men of Ai would not be terrified, nor dare to go out of the city. But toward the end of the night or at early dawn, he hastened with a few chosen men toward the city to lure the men of Ai out, namely, as the night was ending. Darkness favored the plan. For it is not to be thought, with Masius, that the ambush lay hidden for a full day: but they lay hidden only for the full night. Nor does Josephus disagree with this order.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET STETIT IN VALLIS MEDIO) Meditandi & precandi causa, ut videtur, extra castra, quæ in eadem valle erant, progressus. Vide Gen. 24, 62.

Alii cum exercitu ibi stetisse ajunt. Esse enim hic ἀνακεφαλαίωσιν. Et ita se habere ordinem rei gestæ: Josuam noctu præmissis insidiis, eos cum toto populo eadem nocte ad dimidium vallis subsecutum esse, sed ita ut major pars colle, fossis, curribus, aut sylvis tegeretur, ne Hajenses terre- rentur, nec urbe egredi auderent. Sub finem au- tem noctis vel summo mane paucis secum delectis versus urbem ad Hajenses foras pelliciendos con- tendisse, NOCTE sc. finiente. Favebant consilio tenebræ. Non enim cum Masio existimandum, quod diem solidum insidiæ latuerint: sed noctem tantum solidam latuere. Nec abnuit huic ordini Josephus.

## 8:14
ver. 14. WHOM THE LOT SHALL FIND.

In Hebrew, 'whom the Lord shall apprehend.' The Rabbis say he was apprehended in such a way that he was forced to stand motionless. Others say it was shown through Urim and Thummim. But these do not fit. Therefore, the Vulgate correctly explains it as discovery by lot, with which Josephus and R. Levi Ben-Gerson agree. Thus Jonathan is said to be caught by lot 1 Sam. 14, 42, because a lot directed by the Lord is taken and caught by lot Prov. 16, last verse. And Joshua used it in the distribution of the land ch. 14, seqq. Whence it is clear that the use of lots cannot be simply disapproved, nor were lots used only in the Old Testament, but also in the New, Acts 1, 17. Therefore, one should not subscribe to Chrysostom, who clearly rejects that method of inquiring about doubtful matters in the New Testament and refers it to the imperfection of the Old. Lots must be distinguished, some of which are divine, some human, and some magical and diabolical; the divine were an extraordinary means, which have no place today, now that divine revelation has ceased. That magical lots, instituted by demons through an express or tacit pact, are illicit, no pious person doubts: hence the name of sorcerers is infamous. Human lots are either political or playful, such as those of gamblers and the like, in which there is vanity or rashness. Political lots are not by their nature illicit, and are sometimes even necessary, such as those that are primarily divisive, as they are called. For commonly, following Thomas 2. 2. quaest. 95. art. 8., they are distinguished into divisive lots, such as that in John 19:24 (to which some also refer the elections of persons that are made by lot) and consultative lots, when in ambiguous matters, it is inquired by lot what should be done: and also divinatory [lots], when the truth of a hidden or future matter is sought. In Greek, one kind of lot is called διαιρετικὴ, another βουλευτικὴ, another μαντικὴ: Divisory and Consultory [lots] are not illicit, as Augustine teaches in book 2 of De doctrina Christiana, chapter 28, and Epistle 180 to Honoratus; and they are instituted regarding matters subject to our own judgment, and they rely on the authority of laws or the consent of those casting lots, provided that fraud or superstition does not mix itself in. But divinatory [lots] are superstitious and illicit, unless they are instituted by God's command.

But what should be held regarding the casting of lots by the pages of the Gospel, which once prevailed among Christians? Augustine rightly reproves it in Epistle 119 to Januarius, whose words are repeated in Caus. 26, q. 2, cap. 3; he says that this custom displeases him, to wish to turn divine oracles toward secular business that speaks of another life. Which seems to have arisen from Virgilian lots, which the heathens used, inquiring about their doubts by opening [the book]. In which manner Martin Delrio notes in Disquis. Magic. book 4, c. 2, q. 7, that among Christians, the opening of the Old or New Testament succeeded this vanity of the Gentiles, which they called, not without impiety, the lots of the Apostles or Saints. See B. D. Balduin, book 3, Cas. Consc. c. 6, c. 9; Rivetus in explication of the Decalogue, p. 96 et seqq.

Latin:

vers. 14. QUEM SORS INVENERIT.
