Promissio ergo hæc non absolu- ta fuit, sed conditionalis; si populus in cultu Dei con- stans permanserit. Et segnities Judæorum in culpa est, quod loca sibi promissa non occuparint. Da- vidis tamen tempore & Salomonis illæ regiones Ju- dæis vectigales factæ sunt.

## 13:8
Ver. 8. WITH WHOM.

Scil. the tribe of Manasseh: but not with half of it, of which mention was made before. For one part and another was the half-part of that tribe, which received a possession across and on this side of the Jordan. Therefore that, with whom, refers to the tribe, not the half-tribe.

Latin:

Vers. 8. CUM QUA.

Sc. tribu Manasse: non vero cum dimidia ejus parte, cujus antea mentio facta. Nam alia & alia pars dimidia istius tribus erat, quæ trans & quæ cis Jordanem possessionem accepit. Itaque illud, cum qua, tribum refert, non dimidiam tribum.

## 13:9
Ver. 9. THE PLAINS OF MEDEBA EVEN TO DIBON.

Two cities across the Jordan formerly of the Moabites, but snatched from them by Sihon. Medeba fell to the Reubenites, Dibon to the Gadites Jos. 15. Cf. Num. 21, 30.

Latin:

Vers. 9. CAMPESTRIA MEDABA USQUE DIBON.

Duæ civitates trans Jordanem olim Moabita- rum, sed iis a Sehone ereptæ. Medaba Rubenitis, Dibon Gaditis cessit Jos. 15. Conf. Num. 21, 30.

## 13:14
V. 14. TO THE TRIBE OF LEVI HE GAVE NO POSSESSION.

They indeed had cities which they inhabited, which were specifically assigned to them, but they did not possess fields or vineyards by hereditary right: they had only a bare dwelling in the cities, and suburbs for feeding their beasts of burden. Cf. Deut. 12, 12. Jos. 21, 2.

Latin:

V. 14. TRIBUI LEVI NON DEDIT POS- SESSIONEM.

Habuere quidem urbes, quas inhabitabant, quæ ipsis certæ assignatæ, sed non possidebant agros aut vineas jure hæreditario: nudum solum habe- bant domicilium in urbibus, & suburbana ad alenda jumenta. Conf. Deut. 12, 12. Jos. 21, 2.

## 13:17
Ver. 17.

HESEBON) These places were given in common to the Reubenites and Gadites. See below 31, 39.

Thus Masius and Bonfrerius regarding Dibon, because here it is ascribed to the Reubenites, Num. 32, 24, and to the Gadites, it seems to have been common to both tribes, since it was on the borders of both tribes. Which they also note concerning Hesebon from Num. 32, 17. Jos. 21, 37. 1 Chron. 6, last. For they had some cities placed on the border of the two tribes, [having] inhabitants of both those tribes.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

HESEBON) Hæc loca communiter data Rubenitis & Ga- ditis. Vide infra 31, 39.

Ita Masius & Bonfrerius de Dibon, quia hic Rubenitis, Num. 32, 24. Gaditis adscribitur, videri utrique tribui communem fuisse, cum in utriusque tribus finibus esset. Quod etiam de Hesebon notant e Num. 32, 17. Jos. 21. 37. 1. Par. 6, ult. Habuisse enim nonnullas urbes in duarum tribuum confinio posi- tas, utriusque illius tribus incolas.

## 13:20
Ver. 20.

ASEDOTH PHASGA) Aquila takes this latter word as an epithet of Azotus. For he translates it λαξευτὴν, that is, fortified out of stone.

See what is said at ch. 10, 40.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

ASEDOTH PHASGA) Posteriorem hanc vocem pro epi- theto Azoti accipit Aquila. Vertit enim λαξευτὴν, id est, e lapide munitam.

Vid. quæ ad c. 10, 40. dicta.

## 13:21
Ver. 21. AND ALL THE CITIES OF THE PLAIN, AND ALL THE KINGDOMS OF SEHON THE KING.

The Vulgate must be corrected from the Hebrew text, which Masius rendered thus, with Bonfrerius approving: And all the cities of the plain, which all had been of the kingdom of Sehon. Therefore the Reubenites did not receive everything that King Sehon had possessed, which the Vulgate indicates. For the Gadites also had their lot there, v. 27. But those cities of the plain which they received are said all to have previously belonged to Sehon.

WHOM MOSES SMOTE WITH THE PRINCES OF MADIAN.

Not in one war, but in different ones: For the slaughter of Sehon is reported in Num. 21. But that of their princes in Num. 31, 8. Yet Moses himself smote these no less than that one, who perhaps had been made tributary to Sehon, and obeyed him to some extent. The smiting of the princes of Madian and of Balaam is mentioned, so that it may be recalled to the memory of the Reubenites what hostile acts the Israelites suffered from them within those borders which were assigned to that tribe.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET OMNES URBES CAMPE- STRES, UNIVERSAQUE REGNA SEHON REGIS.

Corrigenda est Vulgata ex Ebræo textu, quem ita reddidit Masius, approbante Bonfrerio: Atque omnes urbes planitiei, quæ omnes fuerant regni Sehonis. Non ergo quicquid Rex Sehon possederat, Rubeni- tæ accepere, quod Vulgata indicat. Nam & Gadi- tæ ibi sortem suam habuere v. 27. Sed urbes illæ planitiei, quas acceperunt, omnes prius ad Sehonem pertinuisse dicuntur.

QUEM PERCUSSIT MOSES CUM PRIN- CIPIBUS MADIAN.

Non uno bello, sed diversis: Nam Sehonis clades refertur Num. 21. Principum vero eorum Num. 31, 8. Hos tamen non minus quam illum idem Moses percussit, qui Vectigales Sehoni forte facti, & aliquo usque ei paruere. Refertur percussio Principum Madian & Balaami, ut in memoriam Ru- benitis revocetur, quam hostilia ab illis Israelitæ in- tra istos fines, qui illi tribui assignati, passi fuerint.

## 13:25
Ver. 25. AND ALL THE CITIES OF GALAAD.

This does not seem to agree with v. 31, because half of Galaad fell to the half-tribe of Manasseh. I answer by limiting it thus: that all the cities of Galaad fell to the Gadites, which, to wit, were contained within the borders assigned to them.

THE HALF PART OF THE LAND OF THE CHILDREN OF AMMON.

But concerning the land of the children of Ammon, the Lord did not wish to give them anything, Deut. 2, 19. The interpreters respond that Sihon had snatched from the Ammonites a part of the territory of Sur, which, upon the defeat of Sihon, fell to the Israelites: whence the King of the Ammonites demanded restitution, Jud. 11, 3. But undeservedly; because the Israelites possessed it by right of war. Therefore, in the passage Deut. 2, 19, only those things are excepted which the Ammonites were then ruling, which God wishes to be left to them, and thus He forbids only that they should invade the Ammonites and contend with them in war.

WHICH IS OVER AGAINST RABBAH.

That is: In the region opposite to it. This royal city of the children of Ammon, which is also called Rabbath, and was later called Philadelphia, the Israelites never seem to have possessed, which, however, David conquered long afterwards, 2 Sam. 12. But Bonfrerius understands it as referring to Ar of the Moabites, which was also called Moab Rabbah, as Jerome testifies in his book of Hebrew places.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ET OMNES CIVITATES GALAAD.

Non videtur hoc congruere v. 31. quia dimi- dia pars Galaad cessit dimidiæ tribui Manasse. Resp. hæc ita limitando: Gaditis omnes civitates Galaad obvenisse, quæ sc. intra terminos sibi assignatos contine- bantur.

DIMIDIAM PARTEM TERRÆ FILIO- RUM AMMON.

At de terra filiorum Ammon nolebat Dominus illis quicquam dare Deut. 2, 19. Respondent Interpp. Sehon Ammonitis partem ditionis Sur eripuisse, quæ profligato Sehon Israelitis cesserit : Unde resti- tutionem postulavit Rex Ammonitarum Jud. 11, 3. Sed immerito ; quia jure belli possidebant Israelitæ. Proinde in loco Deut. 2, 19. ea tantum excipiuntur, quibus nunc dominabantur Ammonitæ, quæ eis relin- qui vult Deus, adeoque vetat solum, ne Ammonitas invadant, & cum eis bello decertent.

QUÆ EST CONTRA RABBA.

Id est : E regione ei opposita. Hanc regiam urbem filiorum Ammon, quæ & Rabbath dicitur, ac postea Philadelphia vocata est, nunquam Israelitæ videntur possedisse, quam tamen diu postea David expugna- vit 2, Sam. 12. Bonfrerius vero intelligit de Ar Moa- bitarum, quæ etiam dicta fuerit Moab Rabba, teste Hieron. in loc. Ebr.

## 13:30
V. 30. AND ALL THE KINGDOMS OF OG KING OF BASHAN.

There seem to have been three, namely the region of Argob, Bashan, and a part of Gilead: yet often the others are also included by one of them.

AND ALL THE VILLAGES OF JAIR.

The Vav here is exegetical, that is, and all the villages: because the villages of Jair are no others than those which were contained in the kingdoms of Og. They fell to Jair, who, being the grandson of Machir the son of Manasseh through his daughter, even though he was of the tribe of Judah, was joined to the descendants of Machir, 1 Chron. 2, 21. Compare Num. 32, 41. Deut. 3, 14. 1 Kings 4, 13. 1 Chron. 2, 23.

Latin:

V. 30. ET CUNCTA REGNA OG REGIS BASAN.

Tria videntur fuisse, Regio nempe Argob, Ba- san & pars Galaad : Sæpe tamen uno eorum cætera quoque comprehenduntur.

OMNESQUE VICOS IAIR.

Vav hic est exegeticum, id est, omnes vicos : quia non alii sunt vici Jair, quam qui in regnis Og conti- nebantur. Jairi obtigerunt, qui Machiris filii Me- nassis ex filia nepos, etsi de tribu Juda fuerit, aggre- gatus est posteris Machir 1. Par. 2, 21. Conf. Num. 32, 41. Deut. 3, 14. 1. Reg. 4, 13. 1. Par. 2, 23.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV. Caleb's inheritance of Hebron.

Vers. 1. ELEAZAR THE PRIEST AND JOSHUA THE SON OF NUN AND THE HEADS OF THE FAMILIES) See above 8, 33. 9, 15. 18. and below 19, 51.

The Jesuit Bonfrerius rashly concludes from the order of the Priest placed first, that the Pontiff was superior in dignity to Joshua, and by the old law was superior to the secular Prince. It is too slippery a foundation to build upon the order of placement or enumeration, which is not always observed according to the order of dignity. Was not Moses to Aaron in the place of God? Exod. 4, 16. And the Abulensis acknowledges that in the old law the King, or the Prince of the people, of which kind Joshua was, was greater in dignity than the Priest. Nor does it stand in the way that in Num. 27, 21, Joshua is commanded to go in and out at the mouth of Eleazar: because there Joshua is bound only to the divine response, but is not truly subjected to Eleazar: nay, he is set over both the whole congregation and the Pontiff himself as Leader and successor of Moses, v. 16. Compare Rom. 13.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV. Calebi hæreditas Hebron.

Vers. 1. ELEAZAR SACERDOS ET JOSVE FILIVS NVN ET PRINCIPES FAMILIARVM) Vide supra 8, 33. 9, 15. 18. & infra 19, 51.

EX ordine prius collocati Sacerdotis temere col- ligit Jesuita Bonfrerius, Pontificem dignitate præi- visse Josuæ, ac lege veteri superiorem fuisse Principe secu- lari. Nimis lubricum est ab ordine collocationis, seu recensionis fundamentum, qui non semper juxta or- dinem dignitatis observatur. Annon Moses Aa- roni erat vice Dei ? Exod. 4, 16. Et agnoscit Abulen- sis in veteri lege Regem, vel populi Principem, cujusmo- di fuit Josue, dignitate majorem fuisse Sacerdote. Nec obstat, quod Num. 27, 21. jubeatur Josua ad os Elea- zari ingredi & egredi : quia illic solum ad responsum divinum alligatur Josua, non vero Eleazaro subjici- tur : imo præficitur cum communioni toti, tum etiam ipsi Pontifici tanquam Dux & successor Mosis v. 16. Conf. Rom. 13.

## 14:2
BY LOT) See what has been said on Numbers 34.

Latin:

SORTE) Vide quæ dicta ad Numerorum 34.

## 14:4
V. 4. BUT IN THEIR PLACE SUCCEEDED THE SONS OF JOSEPH DIVIDED INTO TWO TRIBES MANASSEH AND EPHRAIM.

The sense is ambiguous, nor can it be easily resolved. For how did the sons of Joseph succeed into the place of the Levites? In the Hebrew it is held thus: And he gave no inheritance to the Levites in their midst. Because Joseph had two tribes, to whom proper possessions were owed without the Levites. This explanation is therefore added, how there were still 12 tribes without counting the Levites, because, namely, the sons of one Joseph constituted two tribes. It is therefore manifest that the Vulgate errs from the Hebrew text, in which there is nothing about succession. Nor does that succession into the place of the Levites even hold together for itself: whence Masius rightly wrote 'I shall say' here of the Vulgate. Which Bonfrerius and Cornelius defend in vain, that they did not indeed succeed into the right or possession, but that they might supply the number twelve in the allotment of the tribes: For thus only one or the other son of Joseph was to be said to have supplied the place of the Levites: for how shall two tribes be said to have supplied the place of one in the reckoning of the number? Therefore Cornelius does not escape the mark of impudence, because he still dares to pronounce the Vulgate version to be clearer here than the Hebrew text.

THEIR SUBURBS FOR FEEDING THEIR BEASTS AND CATTLE) Not fields, not vineyards, but pastures, and those themselves more for use than for profit.

Latin:

V. 4. SED IN EORUM SUCCESSERUNT LOCUM FILII JOSEPH IN DUAS DIVISI TRIBUS MANASSE ET EPHRAIM.

Ambiguus est sensus, nec facile expediri potest. Quomodo enim filii Joseph in locum Levitarum suc- cesserunt ? In Ebræo ita habetur: Et Levitis non dedit hæreditatem in medio eorum. Quia fuerunt Joseph duæ tribus, quibus possessiones propriæ debebantur absq; Levitis. Additur ergo hæc explicatio, quomodo non annumeratis Levitis adhuc 12. tribus fue- rint, quia scil. unius Josephi filii duas consti- tuere tribus. Manifestum ergo est, Vulgatam ab- errare a textu Ebræo, in quo nihil de Successione. Neque etiam sibi constat illa in locum Levitarum successio: unde Masius merito dicam hic scripsit Vulgatæ. Quam nequicquam tuetur Bonfrerius, ac Cornelius, quod non quidem in jus vel possessionem successerint, sed ut numerum duodenarium in tri- buum sortitione supplerent: Sic enim alteruter tan- tum filius Josephus dicendus erat locum Levitarum supplevisse: duæ enim tribus quomodo dicentur u- nius locum supplevisse in numeri ratione? Ideo im- pudentiæ notam non effugit Cornelius, quod adhuc ausit pronunciare hic clariorem esse versionem vulga- tam Ebræo textu.

SVBURBANA EARVM AD ALENDA JUMENTA ET PECORA SVA) Non arva, non vineta, sed pascua, ea- que ipsa usui magis, quam fructui.

## 14:6
AND CALEB SPOKE TO HIM) Lest a good name should become a bad one by not interceding.

Lest he should be a dumb dog, because he has his name from a dog: Others say Caleb is the same as heart or denotes a man of heart. The Rabbis interpret the son of Jephunneh from מבט as eyed, sagacious, but that is the proper name of the father of Caleb, who was truly eyed and prudent. There is another Caleb, the great-grandfather of Bezalel, and the immediate son of Hezron 1 Chron. 2, 18.

KENIZZITE.

Not by reason of nation, but of family, he was so called from his grandfather or great-grandfather, but not from his stepfather, as some wish. There was without doubt a Cenez, an excellent man, whence that name was given to others in the family for the sake of memory, honor, and name; for also the brother of Caleb was called Cenez, the father of Othoniel the judge, and a grandson of Caleb from his son was so named, Jos. 15, 13. Jud. 1, 13. 1 Chron. 4, 13. 15.

Latin:

LOCVTVSQVE EST AD EUM CALEB) Ne nomen bonum non interpellando malum fieret.

Ne canis mutus esset, quia nomen a cane habet: Alii Caleb dicunt idem esse quod cor vel cordatum notare. Rabbini filium Jephunne a מבט interpre- tantur oculatum, sagacem, sed id nomen proprium est patris Calebi, qui vere oculatus & prudens fuit. Alius est Caleb atavus Befelebeel, & filius immedia- tus Efron 1. Par. 2, 18.

CENEZÆUS.

Non ratione nationis, sed familiæ ab avo vel proavo ita vocatus est, non autem a vitrico, ut non- nulli volunt. Fuit sine dubio Cenez vir eximius, un- de illud nominis aliis in familia memoriæ, honoris, & nominis causa etiam datum; nam & frater Calebi vocatus est Cenez Pater Othonielis judicis, & nun- cupatus ita Calebi ex filio nepos Jos. 15, 13. Jud. 1, 13. 1. Par. 4, 13. 15.

## 14:7
WHAT SEEMED TRUE TO ME) According to the opinion of the mind, as the Romans used to say.

Latin:

QVOD MIHI VERVM VIDEBATVR) Ex animi sen- tentia, ut Romani loquebantur.

## 14:10
V. 10. FORTY AND FIVE YEARS ARE.

From this passage the chronology of this book receives light. For since Caleb was sent as a scout in the second year from Egypt, Num. 10 & 13, from which time he teaches here that forty-five years have elapsed, it is manifest that this is the seventh year from the entry of Joshua into the land of Canaan, inasmuch as it happened in the 40th year of the exodus from Egypt, and thus in the thirty-eighth year from the time the scouts were sent. Therefore, six years were consumed in subduing and cutting off the Canaanites, and in the seventh the division of the land was instituted, when Caleb was already 85 years of age.

Latin:

V. 10. QUADRAGINTA ET QUINQUE ANNI SUNT.

Ex hoc loco lumen accipit Chronologia hu- jus libri. Nam quum explorator missus sit Caleb an- no secundo ex Ægypto Num. 10. & 13. ex quo tem- pore quadraginta & quinque annos effluxisse hic docet, manifestum est, septimum annum hunc esse ab ingressu Josuæ in terram Canaan, utpote, qui fa- ctus 40. exitus ex Ægypto anno, adeoque trigesimo octavo anno a tempore missorum exploratorum. Sexennium ergo consumtum domandis & exscin- dendis Cananæis, ac septimo terræ divisio instituta, cum Caleb jam esset annorum 85.

## 14:12
V. 12. GIVE THEREFORE TO ME THIS MOUNTAIN WHICH THE LORD PROMISED.

That promise is nowhere expressed, but because it was made in the hearing of Joshua, Caleb appeals to it. That mountain is the mountainous region of Judah, as often elsewhere; or the mountain in which Hebron, Debir, and Anab are situated. One must recognize here the providence of God and the παρρησία [boldness] and heroic fortitude of Caleb, in that he had to and wanted to attack those fortified cities with the giants, who had struck terror into the whole people, but concerning whose easy conquest Caleb had once made a promise with great confidence, so that what he had professed in words full of confidence might be fulfilled in reality.

IN WHICH THE ANAKIM ARE. Although they were cut off by Joshua in ch. 11, 12, some nevertheless, having either escaped by flight or having stayed among the Philistines, returned and fortified the place, while Joshua was occupied with war in the northern part. Cf. Jos. 15, 14.

Same verse.

AND SHALL BE ABLE TO DESTROY THEM) He wishes to undertake the war with private forces by public authority, like the Fabii of the Romans. Joshua, however, deemed it fair that the public pledge should be redeemed by public resources. For this is an ἐπάνοδος [return] to that which was said above 10, 36. As Caleb, so Joshua had a city ἐξαίρετον [set apart] below 19, 50.

Latin:

V. 12. DA ERGO MIHI MONTEM ISTUM QUEM POLLICITUS EST DOMINUS.

Nuspiam autem expressa est illa pollicitatio, sed quia Josua audiente facta, ad eam provocat Caleb. Mons ille est montana regio Judæ, ut alibi sæpe; vel mons, in quo sita Hebron, Dabir & Anab. Agno- scenda hic Dei providentia & παρρησία Calebi ac fortitudo Heroica, quod illas urbes munitas cum gigantibus, qui terrorem populo universo incusse- rant, de quibus vero facile expugnandis Caleb olim magna fiducia spem fecerat, aggredi debuerit, ac voluerit, ut impleretur reapse, quod professus erat verbis fiducia plenis.

IN QUO ENACIM SUNT. Etsi a Josua excisi c. 11, 12. nonnulli tamen vel fuga elapsi, vel apud Philistæos versati, reversi locum mu- niere, Josua in Aquilonari parte bello occupato. Conf. Jos. 15, 14.

Vers. eod.

ET POTVERIT DELERE EOS) Vult publica aucto- ritate privatis viribus bellum suscipere, ut Romanorum Fa- bii. Josue autem æquum censuit, ut publica fides publicis opibus liberaretur. Est enim hic ἐπάνοδος ad id quod di- ctum supra 10, 36. Ut Caleb ita Josue urbem habuit ἐξαίρε- τον infra 19, 50.

## 14:15
WAS FORMERLY CALLED CARIATH ARBE) See what is said at Gen. 23, 2. and below 15, 13. Verse 17. ADAM MAXIMVS IBI INTER ENACIM SITVS EST] A great man even among the giants. This version, which put a proper name in place of a common one, is the source of a wondrous number of fables. See shortly 15, 14.

Cornelius, along with Masius and Bonfrerius, as well as the Chaldean, Cajetan, Vatablus, Arias, Pagninus, and others, acknowledges that the words should be rendered thus: 'Hebron however was called Cariath Arbe, that man had been the greatest among the Enakim; for that city, having been occupied by the giant Arbe, the father of Enack, Jos. 15, 13. ch. 12, 11. was called the city of Arbe.' Who was the greatest not so much in power or the glory of his deeds, as in the stature of his body. Away, therefore, with the fiction of the Hebrews in Bereschith Rabba, which Lyranus, Dionysius, Hugo, and Abulensis made their own: that Hebron was formerly called the city of the four men, because Adam, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were buried in it, to which fiction about Adam being buried here Jerome also inclines in ch. 27 of Matthew, in his questions on Chronicles, and in the Epitaph of St. Paula, as do Isidore and others, as well as more recent writers like Saligniacus, Bredenbachius, Borchardus, Adrichomius, etc. whom Cornelius refutes by means of another tradition about Adam being buried not in Hebron, but in Golgotha: which Vilalpandus reconciles thus: that he was buried first indeed in Cariath Arbe, but afterwards on the mount of Calvary, when Noah had brought the bones of Adam into the ark, and had given the skull to Shem. But Ciriath Arbe was founded not before, but after the first flood. See what is at Jos. 10, 3. These are not worthy of old wives' tales, on which we should dwell.

Latin:

ANTE VOCABATVR CARIATH ARBE) Vide quæ dicta ad Genes. 23, 2. & infra 15, 13. Verf. 17. ADAM MAXIMVS IBI INTER ENACIM SITVS EST] Homo magnus etiam inter gigantes. Versio hæc quæ nomen proprium pro communi posuit, mirum quantis fabulis originem dederit. Vide mox 15, 14.

Agnoscit Cornelius cum Masio & Bonfrerio. itemque Chaldæo, Cajetano, Vatablo, Aria, Pagnino, & aliis sic reddenda esse verba: Hebron autem vocata est Cariath Arbe, is homo maximus fuerat inter Enakim; occupata enim civitas illa ab Arbe gigante patre Enack Jos. 15, 13. c. 12, 11. civitas Arbe dicta est. Qui maximus fuit non tam imperio, aut rerum gestarum gloria, quam corporis statura. Facessat ergo commentum Ebræorum in Bereschith Rabba, quod suum fecerunt Lyranus, Dionysius, Hugo, Abulensis: Hebron prius vocatam esse civitatem quatuor virorum, quod in ea sepulti Adam, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, in quod commentum de Adamo hic sepulto etiam Hieronymus propendet in c. 27. Matth. in quæst. in Paralip. & in Epitaph. S. Paulæ, nec non Isidorus, & alii, ut & e recentioribus Saligniacus, Bredenbachius, Borchardus, Adrichomius & c. quos refellit Cornelius ex alia traditione de Adamo sepulto non in Hebron, sed in Golgatha: quæ ita conciliat Vilalpandus: quod primo quidem Cariath Arbe, deinde vero in Calvariæ monte, cum Noah ossa Adami in arcam intulerit, & calvarium Semo donarit, sepultus fuerit. At Ciriath Arbe non ante, sed post diluvium primum condita. Vid. quæ ad Jos. 10, 3. Non digna hæc anilia sunt, in quibus immoremur.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAP. XV. The Lot of Judah.

Vers. 1. THEREFORE THE LOT OF THE CHILDREN OF JUDAH) The boundaries are described very accurately for the tribe of Judah as the tribe of the Prince, where the royal city was to be, from which the kings would come, so that no one might do injury to the common people by crossing those boundaries. The division was made not by equal measure, but according to what the lands were worth: Josephus said τιμητῶς μᾶλλον ἢ μετρητῶς τὰς κλήρους (by value rather than by measure the allotments).

The casting of lots was not done by Urim and Thummim, as Arias wishes, because an oracle is one thing, and a lot is another, but as Josephus notes, by names drawn from an urn, or rather, as the Rabbis observed, by two urns, from one of which the name of the tribe was first extracted, and afterwards from the other the name of the described region, just as the lot had given by divine direction.

Latin:

CAP. XV. Sors Judæ.

Vers. 1. IGITVR SORS FILIORVM JUDÆ) Valde accurate termini describuntur tribus Judæ ut tribuum Principis, ubi futura erat urbs regia, unde reges, ne quis eos terminos transgrediendo popularibus injuriam faceret. Facta autem divisio non æquali mensura, sed pro eo quod terræ valebant: τιμητῶς μᾶλλον ἢ μετρητῶς τὰς κλήρους dixit Josephus.

Sortitio non per Urim & Thumim facta, ut Arias vult, quia aliud est oraculum, aliud vero sors, sed ut Josephus notat, per educta ex urna nomina, aut potius, ut Rabbini observarunt, per duas urnas, e quarum una nomen tribus primùm, ac postea ex altera nomen descriptæ regionis extractum, prouti sors divina directione dederat.

## 15:2
Vers. 2. ITS BEGINNING FROM THE SUMMIT OF THE HIGHEST SEA AND FROM ITS TONGUE. The extremity of the Dead Sea or Lake Asphaltites and its tongue, i.e., its bay, is noted, where, namely, its narrower part runs out into the mainland in the appearance of a tongue, where this sea ends, near Idumea. See Masius and Adrichom.

Latin:

Vers. 2. INITIUM EJUS A SUMMITATE MARIS ALTISSIMI ET A LINGUA EJUS. Extremitas maris mortui seu lacus Asphaltites & lingua h. e. sinus ejus notatur, quo scil. ejus pars angustior in continentem excurrit in speciem linguæ, ubi hoc mare definit, juxta Idumæam. Vid. Masius & Adrichom.

## 15:3
Vers. 3. AGAINST THE ASCENT OF THE SCORPION) The Greeks translate עקרבים both here and in Num. 34, 4 as a proper name, ἀκραβῖν. But this also seems to have become a proper name from the frequency of scorpions. See Deut. 8, 15. It is a part of Idumea, called ἀκραββατίνη by the writer of the Maccabees 5, 3. Ptolemy places Acraba in Mesopotamia.

The Hebrew name ought by all means to have been retained with the LXX, as was done by the blessed Luther, Vatablus, the Tigurines, and others. And Procopius in Jud. 1, Arias, Masius, Ortelius, and indeed even Jerome at Obad. 1, observed this name of the mountain, even though it may have been given from the multitude of scorpions dwelling there, as R. David Kimchi, Mercerus, Forsterus, Lyranus, Abulensis, and Adrichomius judge.

Latin:

Vers. 3. CONTRA ASCENSVM SCORPIONIS) Græci עקרבים & hic & Num. 34, 4. vertunt, ut proprium ἀκρα-βῖν. Sed nomen etiam hoc proprium videtur factum a frequentia scorpionum. Vide Deuter. 8, 15. Est pars Idumææ, dicta ἀκραββατίνη scriptori Maccabæorum 5, 3. Ptolemæus in Mesopotamia ponit Acrabam.

Debebat omnino retineri nomen Ebræum cum LXX. uti a B. Luthero, Vatablo, Tigurinis, aliis factum. Et nomen hoc montis Procopius in Jud. 1. Arias, Masius, Ortelius, imo etiam Hieronymus ad Obad. 1. observarunt, etsi a scorpionum ibi de- gentium multitudine inditum fuerit, ut R. David Kimchi, Mercerus, Forsterus, Lyranus, Abulensis, Adri- chomius censent.

## 15:5
V. 5. AND THOSE THINGS WHICH LOOK TOWARD THE NORTH FROM THE TONGUE OF THE SEA AS FAR AS THE SAME RIVER JORDAN.

The Hebrews have it thus: And the boundary of the northern side from the tongue of the sea from the extremity of the Jordan. The meaning of which, with Bonfrerius as interpreter, seems to be this: that here is the beginning of the description of the northern boundary, which, namely, has its beginning where the eastern boundary ends, from the extremity of the salt sea toward the North, which it likewise calls a tongue here, just as it called the other southern extremity a tongue above, or, which is the same thing, from the extremity or mouth of the Jordan, for there, having been swallowed by the Dead Sea, it ceases to appear thereafter. The Septuagint version presents the same meaning: And the following things agree wonderfully with this meaning; for soon in the following verse and thereafter that northern boundary is described, and is led through various places one by one. And indeed it is manifest that a tongue or a protruding bay of the sea is also posited on that side; for the same tongue of the sea is dealt with below in ch. 18, 19, where the southern boundary of the Benjaminitic tribe is described, which is the same as the northern boundary of the tribe of Judah, at least as far as the greater part is concerned, for which reason the same places are assigned for the boundaries in both cases, except that where the boundaries of the northern tribe of Judah begin here, there is the end of the description of the southern boundary and of all the boundaries of the Benjaminitic tribe, for it proceeds in the opposite order there. Since, therefore, that southern limit of the Benjaminitic tribe ends opposite, or at the tongue of the most salt sea, where it is likewise said to be the end of the Jordan, in the same way the northern limit of the tribe of Judah ought to be led from the same tongue and bay of the sea, and the extreme mouth of the Jordan. These are the words of Bonfrerius: He does not deny that the Vulgate interpretation differs from these, and is a little more obscure, or even lies in error.

Latin:

V. 5. ET EA QUÆ RESPICIUNT AD A- QUILONEM A LINGUA MARIS USQUE AD EUNDEM JORDANIS FLUVIUM.

Hebræi ita habent : Et terminus plagæ Aquilonis a lingua maris ab extremitate Jordanis. Quorum hic, Bonfrerio interprete, videtur esse sensus : ut hic initium sit descriptionis Aquilonaris termini, qui vi- delicet initium suum habeat, ubi Orientalis termi- nus desinit, ab extremitate maris salsi adversus Aqui- lonem, quam itidem hic linguam vocat, sicuti ut su- pra alteram extremitatem Australem linguam appel- lavit, sive quod idem est, ab extremitate, seu ostio Jor- danis, ibi enim a mari haustus mortuo deinceps ap- parere desinit. Eundem sensum exhibet versio Septuaginta : Et huic sensui mire sequentia conci- nunt; mox enim v. seq. & deinde terminus ille A- quilonaris describitur, & per varia sigillatim loca ducitur. Et vero manifestum est, etiam ab ea par- te linguam seu procurrentem maris sinum statui ; nam de eadem lingua maris infra agitur c. 18, 19, ubi terminus Australis tribus Benjaminicæ describi- tur, qui idem cum termino Aquilonari tribus Judæ, saltem quoad majorem partem, quocirca eadem u- trobivis loca pro terminis assignantur, nisi quod un- de hic inchoantur termini tribus Judæ Aquilonaris, ibi finis est descriptionis termini Australis omni- umque terminorum tribus Benjaminiticæ, nam contrario ibi ordine proceditur. Cum itaque li- mes ille Australis tribus Benjaminiticæ finiatur con- tra, sive ad linguam maris salsissimi, ubi itidem dici- tur finis esse Jordanis, pari modo limes Aquilonaris tribus Judæ ab eadem maris lingua ac sinu, Jorda- nisque extremo ostio duci debet. Hæc Bonfreri- us : A quibus vulgatam interpretationem discrepa- re, ac paulo obscuriorem esse, aut etiam in mendo cubare, haud diffitetur.

## 15:6
Verse 6. AND THE BORDER ASCENDED TO BETH-HOGLAH.

Beth-Hoglah is as it were the place of a circle and a gyre, because there, in the manner of mourners, they went around at the funeral of Jacob, which was once called the threshing floor of Atad, Gen. 50:10, in the tribe of Benjamin, Jos. 18:21.

ASCENDING TO THE STONE OF BOHAN, THE SON OF REUBEN.

That tribe had nothing on this side of the Jordan, but the place seems to be named after this Bohan the Reubenite, on account of some deed done there which concerns him, just as below in v. 37 it is called Migdal-gad.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ASCENDITQUE TERMINUS IN BETHHAGLA.

Beth Hagla quasi locus circuli & gyri, quod ibi more plangentium circumierint in funere Jacob, qui olim dicebatur Area Athad Gen. 50, 10. in tribu Benjamin Jos. 18, 21.

ASCENDENS AD LAPIDEM BOEN, FILII RUBEN.

Nihil habuit ea tribus cis Jordanem, sed locus videtur ab hoc Boane Rubenita denominatus, pro- pter rem aliquam gestam ibi, quæ ipsum attingat, sicut infra v. 37. Migdal Gadis dicitur.

## 15:7
V. 7. LOOKING TOWARD GILGAL, WHICH IS OVER AGAINST THE ASCENT OF ADUMMIM.

Adummim was a place on the road to Jericho infested with robbers, named from redness on account of the frequent shedding of blood, Luke 10:30. Masius thinks this Gilgal is the same as the Gilgal in which there were idols in the time of Ehud the judge, Jud. 3:19. Bonfrerius proves it to be different from that in which the camps were fixed.

ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF THE TORRENT.

Understand the torrent Kidron, which flows through the valley of Jehoshaphat near Jerusalem, and finally glides into the Dead Sea, as Adrichom holds.

AND IT PASSED OVER THE WATERS WHICH ARE CALLED THE FOUNTAIN OF THE SUN.

That border passes: for it ought to be referred to the fountain of the Sun, ch. 18:17.

AND ITS GOINGS OUT SHALL BE AT THE FOUNTAIN OF ROGEL.

The meaning is: And the same goes out, or arrives at the fountain of Rogel, ch. 18, 18. That is, of the fuller, which was near Jerusalem, 2 Sam. 17, 17; 1 Kings 1, 9. So called because the waters drawn from this fountain served the fullers' workshops. Cf. Is. 7, 3.

Latin:

V. 7. RESPICIENS GALGALA, QUÆ EST EX ADVERSO ADSCENSIONIS ADOMMIM.

Adommim locus erat in via Jerichuntis infestus latronibus, dictus a rubedine ob crebram sanguinis effusionem Luc. 10, 30. Galgalam hanc Masius pu- tat eandem esse cum Galgalis, in quibus erant Idola, tempore Ehud judicis Jud. 3, 19. Aliam esse ab ea, in qua castra fixa erant, Bonfrerius probat.

AB AUSTRALI PARTE TORRENTIS.

Torrentem Cedron intellige, qui per vallem Josaphat juxta Jerusalem fluit, & tandem labitur in mare mortuum, ut habet Adrichom.

TRANSIVITQUE AQUAS QUÆ VOCAN- TUR FONS SOLIS.

Terminus ille transit : eo enim referri debet de fonte Solis c. 18, 17.

ET ERUNT EXITUS EJUS AD FONTEM ROGEL.

Sensus est : Et idem egreditur, vel pervenit ad fontem Rogel c. 18, 18. hoc est fullonis, qui erat juxta Jerusalem 2. Sam. 17, 17. 1. Reg. 1, 9. ita dictus, quod ab hoc fonte deductæ aquæ fullonum officinis servi- rent. Conf. Es. 7, 3.

## 15:8
Verse 8. AND IT ASCENDS THROUGH THE VALLEY OF THE SON OF HINNOM] Whence the name of Gehenna [is derived] from the likeness of the fire by which children were killed.

Hinnom is the name of some man, according to Jerome in Jer. 7; whence the valley of Hinnom גיא הנם, and the valley of the sons of Hinnom, in a suburban place on the eastern side of the city of Jerusalem. But to the south is the valley of Jehoshaphat. A most pleasant place, wooded, with streams flowing through it, and, as Jerome testifies, entirely composed for delights, which fact gave occasion for many wicked deeds and infamous idolatry, inasmuch as the idol Moloch was placed in that valley, to whom the Israelites sacrificed their sons alive by fire, namely by placing fire under that bronze idol, which received the children with outstretched arms and burned them alive; from which thing and place the name of Gehenna was taken by analogy and, as it seems, first transferred by Christ to signify the punishments and fires of hell.

THIS IS JERUSALEM. That side, namely, and the fortress of the Jebusites is Jerusalem; not that that southern side alone is the whole city, but one part of the city: the other, lower part, called the daughter of Zion, was to the north of the line drawn here: and it belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.

AND FROM THENCE RISING TO THE TOP OF THE MOUNTAIN. Understand Mount Moriah, on which the temple was. The meaning is: the northern boundary of Judah, after it arrives from the valley of Hinnom at the side of the Jebusite, rises at the foot of Mount Moriah, and is extended further to the top of that same mountain, which mountain is opposite or over against the valley of Hinnom to the west, so that it faces the valley of Hinnom before it towards the east; which same mountain is then terminated on the other side towards the western region of the city at the most northern extremity of the valley of Rephaim, as Bonfrerius has it in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ASCENDITQVE PER VALLEM FILII EN- NOM] Unde Gehennæ nomen ex similitudine incendii, quo pueri necabantur.

Ennom nomen viri alicujus, secundum Hiero- nym. in Ier. 7. unde vallis Ennon גיא הנם, & vallis fi- liorum Ennom in loco suburbano ad partem Orien- talem urbis Hieros. Sed ad Austrum vallis Josaphat. Locus amœnissimus, nemorosus, aquis interfluen- tibus, totusque, Hieronymo teste, ad delicias com- positus, quæ res multis flagitiis, ac infami idololatriæ occasionem dedit, siquidem in ea valle collocatum Idolum Moloch, cui filios suos Israëlitæ vivos per ignem sacrificarant, subjecto nempe igne æneo isti idolo, quod brachiis expansis pueros excipiebat, vi- vosque cremabat, a qua re & loco gehennæ nomen ex analogia sumtum & a Christo, ut videtur, primum ad inferni pœnas, & incendia significanda transla- tum.

HÆC EST JERUSALEM. Illud videl. latus & arx Jebusæorum est Jeru- salem; non quod latus illud solum Australe sit tota urbs, sed urbis pars una: altera pars inferior filia Sion vocata ad Aquilonem lineæ hic productæ erat: & ad tribum Benjamin pertinebat.

ET INDE SE ERIGENS AD VERTICEM MONTIS. Intellige montem Moria, in quo erat templum. Sensus est: funiculum Judæ Aquilonarem, postquam a valle Ennom pervenit ad latus Jebusai, in pede montis Moriæ sese erigere, & ulterius produci ad verticem mon- tis ipsius, qui mons est contra seu e regione vallis En- nom ad Occidentem, ut adeo vallem Ennom ante se respiciat versus Orientem; qui deinde idem mons terminatur ab altera parte versus occidentalem ur- bis plagam in extremitate vallis Raphaim maxime Aquilonari, ut habet Bonfrerius h. l.

## 15:10
V. 10. AND IT CIRCLES FROM BAALAH WESTWARD UNTO MOUNT SEIR.

This Mount Seir is far different from that which runs along a long stretch among the Idumeans. Let it be noted, however, that the western boundaries of the tribe of Judah begin here: yet so that these boundaries belong to the tribe of Judah according to its first extent, which later became narrower, with the whole tribe of Simeon included within its boundaries, as is said below in ch. 19, v. 9, and with some cities subtracted from it and ascribed to the tribe of Dan.

V. 10. AND IT PASSES BY THE SIDE OF MOUNT JEARIM TO THE NORTH INTO CHESALON. In the Hebrew it is: And it shall pass to the side of Mount Jearim from the north: it is Chesalon itself. It is noted, therefore, that Mount Jearim itself, or at least its northern part, is Chesalon, or that the village of Chesalon is situated in it. Mount Jearim is the mountain of woods, just as Kiriath-jearim is the city of woods, because of the dense forests in those places.

AND IT DESCENDS INTO BETH-SHEMESH. It was a priestly city in the tribe of Judah, Josh. 21; 1 Sam. 6, called the house of the Sun: although it is not counted here among the cities of Judah, unless perhaps under another name it is wrongly placed by Adrichomius in the tribe of Dan.

AND IT REACHED TOWARD THE NORTH OF THE PART OF ACCARON. Therefore the tribe of Judah had this Satrapy of the Philistines, Accaron, or rather all five Satrapies of the Philistines, because it had everything from Accaron to Gaza according to the first allotment v. 25, even if Accaron was later torn away and granted to the tribe of Dan c. 19, 43, and indeed even the remains of the Satrapy, with only Ascalon and Gaza left to Judah, Joseph. l. 5. Ant. c. 1. Accaron was therefore conquered by the tribe of Judah Jud. 1, not because it was contained within its borders, but because it was of great importance that the forces of the Philistines be worn down, so that the Jews could live quietly within their own borders. Although neither the tribe of Judah nor Dan ever held those Satrapies in firm possession, but they were extorted from them again by the Philistines. But Bonfrerius, who is accurate in these matters, notes with the agreement of Cornelius a Lapide, that this delineation of the boundaries, which is held here, was that first and rough one, which was made for the first time, perhaps not yet with the extent sufficiently discovered, nor with an accurate measurement of the whole promised land made, whence these boundaries, because they were looser than was just, had to be contracted, so that the tribe of Judah had to grant a place within the lot assigned to it to the whole tribe of Simeon, and to the West, a sufficient place had to be left for the Danite tribe by the tribes of Benjamin and Judah; yet in such a way that the tribe of Dan and the tribe of Simeon were not joined, which Adrichomius does, but that the tribe of Judah ran between both as far as Gaza; nor indeed can you read anywhere that Beitsames was torn away from the tribe of Judah, or attributed to the Danites, although this was near to the Philistines, or that Ascalon and Gaza were ascribed to the tribe of Simeon, all of which Adrichomius nevertheless establishes, in which matter he perverts many things in the judgment of Bonfrerius, who warns concerning him, lest anyone attribute more than is proper to the Chorography of the Holy Land of Adrichomius, otherwise sufficiently accurate, and create obstacles for himself in the understanding of Holy Scripture.

Latin:

V. 10. ET CIRCUIT DE BAALA CONTRA OCCIDENTEM USQUE AD MONTEM SEIR.

Hic mons Seir longe diversus est ab eo, qui a- pud Idumæos longo tractu excurrit. Notetur au- tem hic inchoari terminos Occidentales tribus Judæ: ita tamen ut hi termini sint tribus Judæ secundum primam suam amplitudinem, qui postmodum angustiores sunt facti, intra ipsius terminos inclusa tota tribu Simeon, ut infra c. 19. dicitur v. 9. & sub- tractis eidem nonnullis urbibus tribusque Dan ad- scriptis.

V. 10. TRANSITQUE JUXTA LATUS MONTIS IARIM AD AQUILONEM IN CHE- BLON. In Ebr. est: Et transibit ad latus montis Jarim ab Aquilone: ipsa est Chesalon. Notatur ergo ipsum montem Jarim vel certe ejus partem Aquilonarem esse Chesalon, aut in ea villam Chesalon sitam esse. Mons Jarim est mons Silvarum, ut Cariat Jarim urbs Silvarum, ob densas in iis locis silvas.

ET DESCENDIT IN BETHSAMES. Urbs Sacerdotalis erat in tribu Juda Jos. 21. 1. Sam. 6. dicta domus Solis: etsi hic non numeretur inter urbes Juda, nisi forte sub alio nomine perpe- ram ab Adrichomio locatur in tribu Dan.

ET PERVENIT CONTRA AQUILONEM PARTIS ACCARON. Habebat ergo tribus Juda hanc Satrapiam Philistinorum Accaron, imo omnes quinque Satra- pias Philistinorum, quia omnia ab Accaron usque ad Gazam secundum primam sortitionem habuit v. 25. etsi Accaron postea avulsa, & tribui Dan concessa fuerit c. 19, 43. imo etiam reliquiæ Sa- trapiæ, relictis Judæ solum Ascalon & Gaza Joseph. l. 5. Ant. c. 1. Expugnata ergo Accaron a tribu Juda Jud. 1. non quod intra ejus fines contineretur, sed quod permagni interesset Philistæorum vires at- teri, ut Judæi intra fines suos quieti vivere possent. Quanquam neque tribus Iuda, neque Dan Satrapias istas unquam firma possessione tenuerit, sed a Phili- stinis iterum iis extorta sint. Notat vero Bonfre- rius, qui in hisce accuratus est, annuente Cornelio a Lapide, hanc terminorum delineationem, quæ hic habetur, fuisse primam illam & rudem, quæ prima vice facta fuit, nondum forte satis comperta ampli- tudine, neque facta accurata dimensione totius ter- ræ promissæ, unde hi termini, quia justo laxiores e- rant, contrahendi fuerunt, ita ut toti tribui Simeo- nis tribus Juda locum intra sortem sibi assignatam concedere debuerit, & ad Occidentem tribus Benja- min & Judæ tribui Daniticæ sufficiens locus relin- qui debuerit; ita tamen ut non jungerentur tribus Dan & tribus Simeon, quod facit Adrichomius, sed ut inter utramque tribus Iuda procurreret Gazam usque; neque vero usquam legas Beitsames tribui Iudæ fuisse avulsam, aut Danitis attributam, cum ta- men hæc Philistinis vicina esset, aut Ascalonem & Gazam tribui Simeonis adscriptas, quæ tamen o- mnia statuit Adrichomius, qua in re multa pervertit judicio Bonfrerii, qui de eo monet, ne quis Choro- graphiæ terræ sanctæ Adrichomii, alias satis accura- tæ plus quam oportebat, tribuat, remorasque sibi i- psi in Scripturæ S. intelligentia faciat.

## 15:13
Verse 13.

BUT TO CALEB THE SON OF JEPHUNNEH HE GAVE A PART IN THE MIDST OF THE CHILDREN OF JUDAH. You would translate more correctly with Bonfrerius: But to Caleb the son of Jephunneh a part was given in the midst of the children of Judah according to the word of the Lord to Joshua. For the name or subject to which the verb HE GAVE refers is not held in the text. But that command was given to Joshua either through Moses or immediately now in the allotment.

CARIATH ARBE) Not the city itself, but the field. For the city itself was of the Levites Jos. 21, 13.

Latin:

Versus 13.

CALEB VERO FILIO IEPHUNE DEDIT PARTEM IN MEDIO FILIORUM IUDA. Rectius vertas cum Bonfrerio: Caleb vero filio Jephune data fuit pars in medio filiorum Juda juxta sermonem Domini ad Josue. Non enim habetur in textu nomen vel subjectum, ad quod se referat ver- bum DEDIT. Præceptum autem id Josuæ vel per Mosen vel immediate nunc in sortitione.

CARIATH ARBE) Non ipsam urbem, sed agrum. Urbs enim ipsa Levitarum erat Jos. 21, 13.

## 15:14
Ver. 14.

THREE SONS OF ENAC] The remnants of those whom Joshua had slain. Above 11, 21.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

TRES FILIOS ENAC] Reliquias eorum quos Josue in- terfecerat. Supra 11, 21.

## 15:15
Ver. 15.

CARIATH SEPHER) That is, the city of letters. In Chaldean קרית ארכי the city of Libraries. A Phoenician Gymnasium to Xenophon.

The same is also called דביר, as if the oracle of wisdom, or the house of eloquence: and קרית שנא, the city of sharpness, in which matters were disputed acutely about individual things. It was the first and most ancient Academy of the world, which we read of in Scripture, as noted here by Cornel. a Lap. Cf. Lyranus, Abulensis, Serarius h. l. Driedo l. 4. de Dogmat. var. p. 238. Midendorp. l. de Acad. origine.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

CARIATH SEPHER) Id est, civitas literarum. Chaldæo קרית ארכי urbs Bibliothecarum. Gymnasium Phœni- cum Xehophonti.

Vocatur eadem etiam דביר quasi oraculum sapientiæ, vel domus eloquentiæ: & קרית שנא urbs acuminis, in qua acute de rebus singulis disputatum fuit. Fuit prima & antiquissima orbis Academia, quam in Scriptura legimus, notante hic Cornel. a Lap. Conf. Lyranus, Abulensis, Serarius h. l. Drie- do l. 4. de Dogmat. var. p. 238. Midendorp. l. de A- cad. origine.

## 15:16
Verse 16.

I WILL GIVE HIM ACHSAH MY DAUGHTER TO WIFE) Great was the paternal power among those nations in the marriages of daughters. See Jud. 1, 13. 1 Sam. 17, 25. You have similar things in the histories of the Greeks concerning Oenomaus, Schoeneus, and others.

AND OTHNIEL THE SON OF KENAZ, CALEB'S YOUNGER BROTHER, TOOK HER.

By brother some understand a kinsman, a brother's son, or a nephew by a brother. The Chaldean and Vatablus translate in the genitive, Son of Kenaz, brother of Caleb. The interpreters added the word younger here on their own from parallel passages Jud. 1, 13. c. 3, 9.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

DABO EI AXAM FILIAM MEAM IN VXOREM) Ingens potestas patria apud illas gentes in filiarum matrimo- niis. Vid. Jud. 1, 13. 1. Sam. 17, 25. Similia in Græcorum historiis habes de Oenomao, Schœneo, & aliis.

CEPITQUE EAM OTHONIEL FILIUS CENEZ FRATER CALEB JUNIOR.

Per fratrem intelligunt nonnulli cognatum, fratris filium, sive nepotem ex fratre. Chald. & Va- tabl. vertunt in Genitivo, Filius Cenez, fratris Cale- bi. Junioris vocem hic de suo addidere Interpp. e locis parallelis Iud. 1, 13. c. 3, 9.

## 15:18
Verse 18.

AND AS THEY WENT TOGETHER. That is, when Achsah the bride was being led into the house of her bridegroom, accompanied by a crowd of relatives, for which purpose they used donkeys, mules, or horses for the sake of honor, or because of the distance of the places.

AND SHE SIGHED AS SHE SAT ON THE DONKEY) Some seem to translate it better: She descended from the donkey. For that is a sign of reverence. Genesis 24:64. See Valerius Maximus, book II, chapter 10, number 4.

Masius, Vatablus, and Pagninus thus emend the Vulgate. Cornelius is not to be listened to when he speaks of sighs moving parents, which he makes an art of women.

Latin:

Verf. 18.

QUÆ CUM PERGERENT SIMUL. Hoc est, cum Axa sponsa deduceretur in domum sponsi sui, comitante turba cognatorum, ad quam rem asinis, mulis vel equis utebantur honoris causa, vel ob locorum distantiam.

SVSPIRAVITQVE VT SEDEBAT IN ASINO) Me- lius aliqui videntur vertere: Descendit de asino. Id enim reverentiæ fignum. Genes. 24, 64. Vide Valerium Maximum libro II. cap. 10. num. 4.

Ita emendat Vulgatam Masius, Vatabl. Pagnin. Non audiendus est Cornelius cum suspiriis paren- tes permoventibus, quam artem fœminarum fa- cit.

## 15:19
THOU HAST GIVEN ME A DRY [LAND]) A dry house complains of being warmed by no heat, Martial, book 9, Epigram 18.

The southern land was dry. For the south wind, blowing to the Jews from the vast wilderness of Arabia, is hot, burning, and dry, whereas the east wind coming from the sea is rainy and fruitful. 1 Kings 18:44, Amos 5:8, Luke 12:54.

AND CALEB GAVE HER THE UPPER AND THE LOWER SPRINGS) As a dowry, and not by law or custom, but out of liberality, such as Agamemnon promises to Achilles.

Masius renders them as whirlpools of water or springs, the upper ones by which hilly places, and the lower ones by which flatter places could be irrigated. Along with the springs, she also received their lands. Theodoret, book 2 on the book of Judges, and Procopius on Judges. For daughters could also be heirs of lands if they married a man of their own tribe and family, nor was there any fear of the confusion which is only forbidden in Numbers 36:6.

Latin:

ARENTEM DEDISTI MIHI) Sicca domus queritur nullo fevore foveri, Martialis libro 9. Epigr. 18.

Terra Australis arens erat. Auster enim Iudæ- is a vasta Arabiæ solitudine spirans est calidus, urens & ficcus, ventus vero Orientalis e mari veniens plu- vius & fœcundus 1. Reg. 18, 44. Am. 5, 8. Luc. 12, 54.

DEDIT ITAQVE EI CALEB IRRIGVVM) In do- tem, neque id ex lege aut more, sed ex liberalitate, qualem Agamemnon Achilli pollicetur.

Vortices aquarum sive scatebras reddit Masius superiores, quibus clivosa, & inferiores, quibus pla- niora loca irrigari possent. Cum scatebris autem etiam fundos earum accepit. Theodoret. l. 2. in l. Iud. & Procop. ad Iudic. Poterant enim & filiæ fundorum esse hæredes, si nuberent viro tribus & familiæ suæ, nec metuenda erat confusio, quæ solum vetatur Num. 36, 6.

## 15:21
Verse 21.

FROM THE UTMOST PARTS OF THE CHILDREN OF JUDAH) You could translate it: partly of the children of Judah: for partly they were of Simeon, below 19:29. So that there were 29 towns of Judah, as is said below 31, but the nine that remain are of Simeon.

Latin:

Verf. 21.

AB EXTREMIS PARTIBUS FILIORVM JUDA) Possis vertere: partim filiorum Juda: nam partim erant Simeonis infra 19, 29. Ita ut 29. oppida fuerint Judæ, ut di- citur infra 31. novem autem quæ restant Simeonis.

## 15:32
Verse 32.

AND AIN AND REMMON] which merged into one city in the course of time and buildings. Nehemiah 11:29.

Thus some reconcile with the Jews the number of 29 counting cities, and 31 counted, so that nine or two having coalesced into one, eight are handed over to Simeon: Masius, however, Serarius, Bonfrer, Cornelius judge that only the cities of Judah, which fell to it in the first assignment, are being enumerated, from which some afterwards yielded to Simeon, namely Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual, Ezem, Eltolad, Hormah, Ziklag, Ain and Rimmon Josh. 19. but that 29 cities are added, some villages, or larger hamlets. Thus also the Osiandrine paraphrase: All the cities twenty-nine, and (certain principal ones) their villages, some of which were enumerated among the aforesaid cities. Thus also v. 33. fourteen cities are collected, when nevertheless fifteen are enumerated, because one among the villages, but a principal one, was added to the cities. But v. 34. and 35. mention is indeed made of villages, but they are not enumerated. From these, however, Eshtaol and Zorah, as also Ether and Ashan, were afterwards torn away from the tribe of Judah, and the former yielded to the Danite, the latter to the Simeonite tribe. Whence the Rabbinic reconciliation of Grotius does not seem to agree. For why would Scripture in v. 23 set aside cities which afterwards fell to the Simeonites, and then in v. 34 not set them aside, in v. 36 set aside one, but not the other?

Latin:

Verf. 32.

ET AEN ET REMON] quæ in unam urbem coaluere processu temporis & ædificiorum. Nehem. 11, 29.

Ita cum Iudæis conciliant nonnulli numerum numerantem 29. oppidorum, & numeratum 31. ut no- vem vel duobus in unam coalitis octo Simeoni tra- dantur: Masius tamen, Serarius, Bonfrer. Cornelius solum Iudæ civitates, quæ in prima assignatione ei- dem obtigerint, recenseri censent, e quibus non- nullæ postmodum Simeoni cesserint, utpote Bersa- bea, Molada, Haserfual, Asem, Eltholad, Harma, Si- celeg, Ain & Remmon Iof. 19. addi autem 29. utbi- bus villas aliquas, seu viculos majores. Ita etiam O- siandrina paraphrasis: Omnes civitates viginti novem, &(præcipuæ quædam) villæ earum, quarum aliquæ inter prædictas urbes fuerunt enumeratæ. Sic etiam v. 33. urbes quatuordecim colliguntur, quum tamen quindecim recenseantur, quia una inter villas, sed principalis, urbibus addita est. At v. 34. & 35. vil- larum quidem fit mentio, sed ex non enumerantur. Ex his tamen Esthaol & Serea, ut & Ether & Asan a- vulsæ postea sunt a tribu Iuda, & priores Daniticæ, posteriores Simeonis tribui cesserunt. Unde Gro- tii Rabbinica conciliatio non congruere videtur. Cur enim v. 23. seponeret Scriptura urbes, quæ Si- meonitis postea obvenerunt, & deinde v. 34. non se- poneret, v. 36. unam seponeret, aleram non item?

## 15:36
ver. 36.

Latin:

vers. 36.

## 15:38
Ver. 38.

JOKTHEEL) You may learn that this name was not given to the city of the Arabs before the times of Amaziah 2 Kings 14, 7.

If this is that city Joktheel, of which mention is made in the latter book of Kings, which is there called a rock or the metropolis of Arabia Petraea, it does not follow from that passage, however, that it was not called by this name before the times of Amaziah. The text there rendered it thus

The Tremellius-Junius version: whose name (everyone) calls Joktheel unto this day.

Latin:

Verf. 38.

JECTHEL) Hoc nomen urbi Arabum datum non ante Amasiæ tempora discas 2. Reg. 14, 7.

Si hæc est illa civitas Joktheel, cujus in poste- riori Regum mentio facta, quæ ibi petra vocatur vel metropolis Arabiæ petrææ, non tamen ex eo loco colligetur, eam non ante Amasiæ tempora hoc nomine vocatam. Textum ibi sic reddidit

Tremellio-Juniana versio : cujus nomen vocat (quis- que) Joktheelem usque in diem hunc.

## 15:39
ver. 39.

Latin:

vers. 39.

## 15:59
SIX CITIES AND THEIR VILLAGES.

After this verse are added in the Sixtine edition two others, which in the LXX, as witnessed by Jerome on Micah 5, were held: Theca and Ephrata, this is Bethlehem etc. for which Capellus fights: But Buxtorf replies in Vindic. p. 690, that they are held neither in the Hebrew, nor the Chaldean, nor the Masora, nor in Hebrew commentaries, nor in all Greek copies, nor in the Syriac written a thousand years ago according to Masius, nor in the Vulgate (Clementine).

Latin:

CIVITATES SEX ET VILLÆ EARUM.

Post hunc versic. adduntur in Sixtina edit. duo alii, qui in LXX. teste Hier. ad Mich. 5. habe- bantur : Theca & Ephrata, haec est Bethlehem &c. pro quibus Capellus pugnat : Sed respondet Buxtorff. in Vindic. p. 690. nec in Hebræo, nec Chaldaeo, nec Ma- sora, nec Ebrais commentar. nec omnibus Graecis exem- plaribus, nec Syriaco ante mille annos scripto apud Ma- sium, nec in Vulgata (Clementina) haberi.

## 15:62
ver. 62.

AND THE CITY OF SALT

It is not to be read here as Solis, but Salis. This city was called by this name because it was near the Dead Sea, or salt sea, or because near it Lot's wife was turned into a pillar of salt, as some think it is Zoar, into which Lot fled, Gen. 19:23. Bonfrerius raises a doubt whether all the cities of Judah listed here are those which existed in the time of the Canaanites before the entry of the Israelites into the promised land: Because neither Bethlehem or Ephrath, nor the three priestly cities Eshtemoa, Holon, Beth-shemesh are enumerated? But those are either found here under other names, or were omitted for the reason that they were to be dealt with under the catalog of priestly cities, Josh. 21:14, 15. Regarding Bethlehem, it may be said that it was still among the villages and hamlets at that time, inasmuch as it was first built into a city by Salma the son of Caleb, 1 Chron. 2:50, or, if it was already a city, it may be designated by another name among those which are listed here. It does not seem consistent, when the cities are defined with numerical accuracy, that that number is not correct. But it would not be correct if some were omitted, and were not supplied anywhere in Joshua.

Latin:

vers. 62.

ET CIVITAS SALIS

Non Solis hic legendum, sed Salis. Dicta est haec civitas hoc nomine, quod vicina esset mari mor- tuo, sive salso, aut quod juxta eam uxor Lothi in sta- tuam Salis conversa, uti nonnulli eam Segor esse, in quam Loth fugit, arbitrantur Gen. 19, 23. Dubium movet Bonfrerius, anne omnes civitates Judae hic re- censitae, quae Cananaeorum tempore extitere ante in- gressum Israelitarum in terram promissam : Quia nec Bethlehem sive Ephrata, nec tres urbes Sacerdota- les Estomo, Holon, Bethsames enumerantur? sed illae vel sub aliis nominibus reperiuntur hic, vel ideo praetermissae, quod de illis sub Sacerdotalium cata- logo agendum fuerit Jos. 21, 14. 15. De Bethlehem dici possit, quod inter villas & vicos tum adhuc fue- rit, utpote a Salma filio Calebi primum in civitatem aedificata 1.Par. 2, 50. aut, si civitas jam fuit, alio no- mine inter illas, quae hic recensitae, designata sit. Non videtur consentaneum, quum numerice accu- rate definiantur civitates, numerum illum recte se non habere. Non autem recte haberet, si aliquae praetermitterentur, nec uspiam in Josua suppleren- tur.

## 15:63
BUT THE CHILDREN OF JUDAH COULD NOT DESTROY THE JEBUSITE INHABITANT OF JERUSALEM.

Not because it was not permitted to them, because the Jebusites were descended from Abimelech, with whom Abraham had entered into a covenant, Gen. 21, as R. David Kimchi wishes, but because of sloth and sins, Judg. 2:20. Although Joshua took Jerusalem, the Jebusites still held the citadel, and afterwards they occupied the city in turn, just as they also recovered Hebron and Debir, whence Jerusalem had to be conquered again by the children of Judah. Judg. 1.

UNTIL THE PRESENT DAY) From this also it appears that this book was written or at least completed neither by Joshua, nor near his time.

Concerning the completion, as it now stands, one must admit it. Which, as it is not to be extended until the times of Ezra, so it does not seem to be referred to Eleazar, but is more correctly attributed by Abulensis to Samuel.

Latin:

JEBUSÆUM AUTEM HABITATOREM JERUSALEM NON POTUERUNT FILII JU- DA DELERE.

Non quod illis id non licuerit, quia Jebusaei ex Abimelecho, cum quo Abraham foedus inierat Gen. 21. orti, ut R. David Kimchi vult, sed ob socordiam & peccata Jud. 2, 20. Etsi autem Jerusalem Josua ce- pit, arcem tamen adhuc tenebant Jebusaei, & postea urbem etiam vicissim occuparunt, sicuti etiam He- bron & Dabir recuperarunt, unde a filiis Juda Iero- solyma expugnanda denuo fuit. Iud. 1.

VSQVE IN PRÆSENTEM DIEM) Hinc quoque ap- paret, neque a Josue, neque prope ejus tempora scriptum aut certe consummatum hunc librum.

De consummatione, prouti nunc habet, fate- ri id oportet. Quae uti non ad Esdrae usque tempo- ra proroganda, ita nec ad Eleazarum referenda vi- detur, sed Samueli rectius ab Abulensi tribuitur.

## 16:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVI. The lot of Ephraim.

ver. 1.

THE LOT ALSO FELL TO THE CHILDREN OF JOSEPH.

The southern boundary of the half-tribe of Manasseh and of the tribe of Ephraim is described jointly: because they held contiguous possessions, although in reality it is only the southern boundary of the tribe of Ephraim, which had the tribe of Benjamin to the south, but the tribe of Manasseh to the north.

Latin:

CAPUT XVI. Sors Ephraim.

vers. 1.

CECIDIT QUOQUE SORS FILIORUM IOSEPH.

DEscribitur conjunctim dimidiae tribus Manaf- fis & tribus Ephraim terminus Australis : quia conjunctas possessiones obtinebant, etsi revera tan- tum tribus Ephraim terminus Australis sit, quae ad meridiem habebat tribum Benjamin, a septentrio- ne vero tribum Manasse.

## 16:2
Ver. 2. AND HE GOES OUT FROM BETHEL TO LUZ.

Bonfrerius thinks that two names of one city are joined, Gen. 28, 19. Junius denies that this is the Bethel which was so named from the vision of Jacob, and posits another not very remote, built by a certain Bethelite, Jud. 1, 26. Nor does he hold Luz and Bethel to be the same, on account of a distinguishing accent, therefore he renders: Thence he proceeds from Bethel to Luz.

Latin:

Verf. 2. ET EGREDITUR DE BETHEL LUZA.

Duo nomina unius urbis jungi putat Bonfrerius, Genef. 28, 19. Junius eam Bethel, quae ex Jacobi vifione ita dicta est, hanc esse negat, aliamque sta- tuit non remotam admodum, a Bethelita quodam extructam Jud. 1, 26. Nec Luzam & Bethel pro eo- dem habet, ob accentum distinguentem, ideo red- dit: Inde progreditur Bethele Luzam.

## 16:3
Ver. 3. JEPHLETI) Who are the Phelethi 2. Sam. 8, 18. c. 15, 18. So also others. Junius [calls them] Japhletin, or (as they are called elsewhere here and there) Pelethei, said to be so by the change of one letter, as 2. Sam. 9, 4. 15. 18.

Latin:

Verf. 3. JEPHLETI) Qui Pheleshi 2. Sam. 8, 18. c. 15, 18. Sic & alii. Junius Japbletin, sive (ut alibi passim appellatur) Pelethei per unius literae mutationem dicti, ut 2. Sam. 9, 4. 15. 18.

## 16:8
Ver. 8. INTO THE VALLEY OF THE REED-BED.

In Nahal-cana, the torrent of reeds. Osiander judges that this name here is of a town, not of a torrent.

INTO THE MOST SALT SEA.

The Dead Sea cannot be understood here, from which the tribe of Ephraim was far distant. Therefore Serarius corrects the Vulgate, because that MOST SALT [sea], by which name the Dead Sea is accustomed to be expressed, has crept into it; in the Hebrew it is held simply as THE SEA, and the Mediterranean is understood. Cf. c. 17, 9.

Latin:

Verf. 8. IN VALLEM ARUNDINETI.

In Nahal-cana, torrentem arundinum. Quod nomen hic oppidi esse, non torrentis censet Ofi- ander.

IN MARE SALSISSIMUM.

Non potest mare mortuum hic intelligi, a quo longe aberat tribus Ephraim. Ideo corrigit Se- rarius Vulgatam, quod in eam illud SALSISSI- MUM, quo nomine mare mortuum exprimi folet, irrepferit; in Ebraeo simpliciter MARE habetur, & mediterraneum intelligitur. Conf. c. 17, 9.

## 16:9
Ver. 9. IN THE MIDST OF THE POSSESSION OF THE CHILDREN OF MANASSEH.

To the tribe of Ephraim, because it was very populous, certain cities and villages were given which were situated in the region of the tribe of Manasseh: because half the tribe of Manasseh already had a possession across the Jordan, so that the remainder had enough land, and could concede certain cities to the Ephraimites.

WHO DWELT IN GEZER.

For the Gezerite was there until the times of Solomon, during which the King of Egypt conquered the Canaanites and gave Gezer to his son-in-law 1. Kings 9, 16.

Latin:

Verf. 9. IN MEDIO POSSESSIONIS FILIO- RUM MANASSE.

Tribui Ephraim, quia valde populosa fuit, datae quaedam urbes & villae, quae in regione tribus Manaf- se fitae erant: quia dimidia tribus Manasse jam ha- bebat possessionem trans Jordanem, ita ut reliqua satis haberet agri, & possit Ephraitis quasdam ur- bes concedere.

QUI HABITAVIT IN GAZER.

Fuit enim Gezereus ibi usque ad Salom. tempo- ra, quibus Rex Aegypti Cananaeos expugnavit, & Genero suo Gezeram donavit 1. Reg. 9, 16.

## 16:10
Verse 10.

TRIBUTARY) Thus also below 17, 12. 1 Kings 9, 16. It is credible that the laws imposed on them were those given to Adam and Noah.

We have spoken elsewhere of the opinion regarding those laws. They sinned, however, because they did not destroy, but only subjected the impious nations to themselves, and lived among them with danger and loss to the true religion. Judges 2.

Latin:

Verf. 10.

TRIBVTARIVS) Sic & infra 17, 12. 1. Reg. 9, 16. Cre- dibile est impositas eis leges Adamo & Noae datas.

De legibus illis alias diximus sententiam. Pecca- runt autem, quod non deleverint, sed sibi solum subjecerint impias gentes, iisque cohabitarint cum periculo, & dispendio verae religionis. Jud. 2.

## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII. The half-tribe of Manasseh, and the lot of the daughters of Zelophehad.

Verse 1.

FOR HE IS THE FIRSTBORN OF JOSEPH) Jacob had indeed once prophesied greater things for Ephraim, 48, 19. But he had not taken away the right of the firstborn from Manasseh: nor had Manasseh deserved that.

MACHIR THE FIRSTBORN OF MANASSEH THE FATHER OF GILEAD, WHO WAS A MAN OF WAR.

Machir was the firstborn, indeed the only begotten of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, who was a man of war in Egypt in the wars of the Ephraimites, 1 Chronicles 7, 21, not in Canaan.

Latin:

CAPUT XVII. Media tribus Manassis, & filiarum Salphaad sors.

Verf. 1.

IPSE ENIM EST PRIMOGENITVS JOSEPHI) Res quidem aliquando majores Ephraimo vaticinatus erat Ja- cobus 48,19. Sed jus primorum natalium Manassi non abs- tulerat: neque id meritus erat Manasses.

MACHIR PRIMOGENITO MANASSE PA- TRI GALAAD, QUI FUIT VIR PUGNA- TOR.

Machir primogenitus, imo unigenitus fuit Ma- nassis, pater Galaad, qui vir pugnator in Aegypto in bellis Ephraimitarum, 1. Paralip. 7, 21. non in Canaan.

## 17:2
Verse 2.

AND THE LORD COMMANDED BY THE HAND OF MOSES] See Numbers 27, 3.

Latin:

Verf. 2.

ET DOMINVS PRAeCEPIT PER MANUM MOSI] Vide Num. 27,3.

## 17:5
Verse 5.

AND THERE FELL TEN PORTIONS TO MANASSEH) Six for the families of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. The four daughters of Zelophehad took four parts, two for their grandfather, as he was the firstborn: one for their father, one for their uncle, who all having come out of Egypt had transferred the right to their descendants. Thus some Hebrews.

Nay, to five sons only five portions fell. For the sixth, Hepher, had no sons, but only a son, Zelophehad, who left five daughters, to whom the remaining five portions seem to have fallen.

Latin:

Verf. 5.

ET CECIDERUNT FVNICVLI MANASSI DE- CEM) Sex pro Abeozeri, Heleci, Ezridis, Sechemi, Hephe- ri, Semidae familiis. Selophcadi filiae quatuor partes cepe- re, duas pro avo,utpote primogenito: unam pro patre,unam pro patruo, qui omnes ex Aegypto egressi jus ad posteros transtulerant. Sic Hebraei quidam.

Imo quinque filiis tantum quinque funiculi cesse- re. Nam sextus Hepher non filios habuit, sed filium Salphaad tantum, qui filias quinque reliquit, qui- bus reliqui quinque funiculi videntur obtigisse.

## 17:8
Ver. 8. IN THE LOT OF MANASSEH HAD FALLEN THE LAND OF TAPPUAH, WHICH IS BY THE BORDERS OF MANASSEH OF THE SONS OF EPHRAIM.

In the Hebrew the sense is clearer, as Bonfrère, Cornelius, and other Papists admit: The land of Tappuah was Manasseh's own. But Tappuah was on the border of Manasseh (and) of the sons of Ephraim. Because the tribe of Ephraim was more numerous, it therefore received some cities in the lot of Manasseh, though the neighboring fields were left to the tribe of Manasseh, because the fields of Ephraim were so fertile that they sufficed for them, as Cornelius à Lapide says with Masius.

Latin:

Vers. 8. IN SORTE MANASSE CECIDE- RAT TERRA TAPHUÆ, QUÆ EST JUX- TA TERMINOS MANASSE FILIORUM E- PHRAIM.

In Ebræo clarior sensus est, fatente Bonfrer. Cor- nel. & aliis Pontificiis: Ipsius Manasse fuit terra Ta- phæ. Taphua vero in termino Manasse (fuit) filiorum Ephraim. Quia copiosior fuit tribus Ephraim, in- de in sorte Manasse aliquas accepit urbes, relictis tamen agris vicinis tribui Manasse, quod agri E- phraim ita fertiles fuerint, ut illis sufficerent, ut cum Masio Cornelius à Lap.

## 17:11
Ver. 11. IN ISSACHAR AND IN ASHER.

In the border, and as it were in the embrace of them, or next to those tribes.

BETH-SHEAN.

Afterwards it was called Scythopolis or the city of the Scythians, according to Josephus, Antiquities book 5, chapter 1; 2 Maccabees 12:29.

Latin:

Vers. 11. IN ISASCHAR ET IN ASAR.

In confinio, & quasi complexu earum, vel juxta illas tribus.

BETHSAN.

Postea dicta est Scythopolis vel Scytharum civitas apud Joseph. lib. 5. Antiq. c. 1. 2. Maccab. 12, 29.

## 17:14
Ver. 14.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

## 17:18
IT SHALL BE THINE, AND THOU SHALT CLEAR IT FOR HABITATION, AND THOU SHALT BE ABLE TO PROCEED FURTHER WHEN THOU HAST SUBDUED THE CANAANITE) Those who complain of the narrowness of their borders ought not to expel their own people, but their enemies, or occupy and cultivate vacant places. Add that 19:47.

Some understand 'forest' literally, with whom Junius and Osiander agree. Others, and among them Cornelius à Lapide, think that the land of Canaan is metaphorically called a forest, because just as a forest is cut down so that the ground may be plowed, the Canaanites were to be cut down so that the Josephites might occupy their land. But there is no reason why we should depart from the literal meaning of the word. For even if there had been cities in those mountainous regions, this designation could still have been taken from the more prominent feature. But the text indicates that the Canaanites, whom the Ephraimites feared, lived rather in the plain; therefore they say that because of them they do not dare to cut down the forests belonging to them in the mountains. Joshua, however, did not wish either to recede from his decree or to foster unbelief in them. Therefore he commands them repeatedly to cut down the forests, and that they themselves would have sufficiently extended borders.

Latin:

SUCCEDET TIBI ATQVE PVRGABIS AD HA- BITANDUM SPATIA, ET POTERIS VLTRA PRO- CEDERE CVM SVBVERTERIS CANANÆUM) Qui de finium angustiis queruntur, non populares, sed hostes de- bent expellere, aut loca vacua occupare & colere. Adde quod 19, 47.

Nonnulli proprie silvam intelligunt, cum qui- bus facit Junius & Osiander. Alii, & inter eos Cor- nelius à Lapide metaphorice terram Cananæam silvam vocari putant, eo quod sicut silva excinditur, ut lo- cus arari possit, excindendi fuerint Borezari, ut eo- rum terram Josephitæ occuparent. Sed non est, cur à proprietate vocis discedamus. Etsi enim in illis montanis etiam fuissent civitates, à potiori ta- men denominatio hæc peti poterat. Sed textus indicat in terra campestri potius Cananæos, quos E- phraitæ metuebant habitasse, ideo dicunt, sese pro- pter illos non audere silvas ad eos pertinentes in monta- nis excindere. Noluit tamen Josua vel à decreto suo recedere, vel incredulitatem in illis alere. Id- eo iterato jubet, silvas excindant, & habituros ipsos terminos satis prolatos.

## 18:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVIII.

The describers of the remaining land. The lot of Benjamin.

Ver. 1. AND ALL THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL WERE GATHERED TOGETHER IN SHILOH.

By all the children, understand those who sustained the person of the whole people, the Priests, the Nobles, the Elders, the heads of families, and any principal persons whatsoever. Peace having been obtained, the Israelites celebrated these first assemblies in the land of Canaan, and in them they erected first of all the sacred Tabernacle, in which the worship of God might be exercised, as that which ought to be the first and most important care in assemblies. Shiloh was distant from Jerusalem only two leagues or hours towards the North. It was situated in the strong tribe of Ephraim in a beautiful and very pleasant place on a mountain and surrounded by the most robust tribes of Judah, Manasseh, and Ephraim. That mountain is called today the mountain of Samuel, and by Borchard and Breitenbach, Ramah. The ark remained there for 350 years and more from Joshua until Samuel 1 Sam. 14, 18, or, as Tirinus wishes, until the times of David, when, fleeing from Saul, it was transferred to Nob 1 Sam. 21, which was done on account of idolatry Jer. 7, 12, Psalm 78, 60. But it was transferred from Gilgal, situated on the threshold of the land of Canaan, to Shiloh as if to the interior of the land, so that it might be approached more conveniently, or because Joshua the Prince was from the tribe of Ephraim, or rather, because that place had been designated by divine oracle Deut. 12, 5 seqq. That was done in the year, not the 14th as the Rabbis say, but the eighth year as Torniellus and others wish of the leadership of Joshua. It was placed not in any house, as it seemed to Abulensis, but in the open air, just as it had been for many years in the desert. The other business in these assemblies was concerning the drawing of lots for the remaining inheritances, for which a new drawing of lots at Shiloh seemed necessary, because the previous one at Gilgal had only been begun, and was not sufficiently accurate.

AND THE LAND WAS SUBJECT TO THEM. Not all the cities of Canaan were yet subject to them. Therefore, it is indicated only that they did not resist them, nor did the Canaanites, being unequal in number, dare to attack and provoke the Israelites in war.

Latin:

CAPUT XVIII.

Terra reliquæ descriptores. Sors Benjamin.

Vers. 1. CONGREGATIQUE SUNT OMNES FILII ISRAEL IN SILO.

PEr omnes filii, intellige eos, qui totius populi personam sustinebant, Sacerdotes, Proceres, Se- niores, capita familiarum, & præcipuos quoslibet. Parta pace prima hæc comitia celebrarunt Israelitæ in terra Canaan, & in iis imprimis Tabernaculum sa- crum, in quo cultus Dei exerceretur, erexerunt, utpote quæ prima in comitiis & potissima cura esse debet. Distabat Silo à Jerusalem tantum duabus leucis vel horis versus Septentrionem. Sita in for- te tribus Ephraim loco pulcro & peramœno in monte & circumpositu robustissimarum tribuum Juda Manassis & Ephraim. Vocatur hodie mons ille mons Samuelis, & à Borcardo & Breitenbachio Ra- ma. Mansit ibi arca 350. annis & amplius à Josua usque ad Samuelem 1. Sam. 14, 18. vel, ut Tirinus vult, usque ad Davidis tempora, quo fugiente à Saule, translata in Nobe 1. Sam. 21. quod ob idolo- latriam factum Jerem. 7, 12. Psalm. 78, 60. Tradu- cta vero fuit è Galgalis in limine terræ Canaan sitis in Silo velut ad interiora terræ, ut commodius adi- ri possit, vel quod è tribu Ephraim esset Josua Prin- ceps, vel potius, quod locus ille oraculo divino de- signatus fuerit Deuter. 10, 5. seqq. factum id anno non 14. ut Rabbini, sed anno octavo ut Torniellus & alii volunt Ducatus Josuæ. Collocata non in aliqua domo, ut Abulensi visum, sed sub dio, quemadmo- dum pluribus annis fuerat in deserto. Alterum negotium in his Comitiis fuit de ducendis hæredita- tum residuarum sortibus, qua nova fortitione Silunti- na opus visum, quod prior Galgalæa inchoata so- lum, nec satis accurata fuerit.

ET FUIT EIS TERRA SUBJECTA. Nondum Cananææ urbes iisdem subjectæ o- mnes erant. Id ergo indicatur solum, quod non restiterint ipsis, aut ausi fuerint, utpote numero impares Cananæi bello aggredi & lacessere Israe- litas.

## 18:4
Ver. 4. THREE MEN) land-surveyors. See below 8. 9.

ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF EACH MULTITUDE. He wishes that they describe the remaining land according to the number of the tribes, that is, for the seven tribes, and divide it into as many parts, taking into account the size of the tribe, as he explains in verse 6.

Latin:

Vers. 4. TERNOS VIROS) γεωδαίτας. Vide infra 8. 9.

JUXTA NUMERUM UNIUSCUJUSQUE MULTITUDINIS. Vult, ut juxta numerum tribuum, hoc est, pro septem tribubus terram reliquam describant, & in tot partes dividant pensi habita tribus numero- sitate, ut explicat vers. 6.

## 18:6
Ver. 6. THE LAND BETWEEN THEM. In the Hebrew those words are not present: THE LAND BETWEEN THEM, nor in the Targum or the version of the LXX. And they contradict history, because the lot of the seven tribes extended beyond the lot of Ephraim and Manasseh as far as Lebanon. Therefore, the Vulgate must be corrected here. Nor can the Papist interpreters, Bonfrerius, Menochius, Cornelius, help it.

Latin:

Vers. 6. MEDIAM INTER HOS TER- RAM. In Ebræo non habentur illa: MEDIAM IN- TER HOS, neque in Targum aut versione LXX. Et repugnant historiæ, quia sors septem tribuum ultra sortem Ephraim & Manasse extendebatur ad Libanum usque. Castiganda ergo hic Vulgata. Nec juvare eam possunt Pontificii Interpp. Bon- frer. Menochius, Cornelius.

## 18:7
Ver. 7. THE PRIESTHOOD OF THE LORD IS THEIR INHERITANCE. Understand the priesthood of the Lord metonymically as the priestly income, of offerings, tithes, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SACERDOTIUM DOMINI EST EORUM HÆREDITAS. Sacerdotium Domini intellige metonymice de proventu Sacerdotali, oblationum, decima- rum &c.

## 18:8
Ver. 8. THAT THEY MIGHT PROCEED TO DESCRIBE THE LAND. Security was singularly provided to these surveyors by GOD: although the Canaanites were also greatly dismayed by the recent disasters and feared to give cause for a new war.

Latin:

Vers. 8. UT PERGERENT AD DESCRI- BENDAM TERRAM. Geometris hisce a DEO præstita est singulariter securitas: quamvis etiam valde consternati fuerint Cananæi ex recentibus cladibus novique belli cau- sam dare metuerint.

## 18:9
Ver. 9. THEY DIVIDED IT INTO SEVEN PARTS. It is added in the Hebrew: by cities: For for a perfect chorography it was necessary that the cities also be inscribed.

Ver. 9. AND THEY RETURNED TO JOSHUA TO THE CAMP AT SHILOH. Josephus says they returned after six months, which they had spent in the description of the land.

Latin:

Vers. 9. IN SEPTEM PARTES DIVISE- RUNT. Additur in Ebræo: per Urbes: Nam ad perfe- ctam chorographiam opus erat, ut urbes etiam adscriberentur.

Vers. 9. REVERSIQUE SUNT AD JOSUE IN CASTRA SILO. Post sex menses reversos dicit Josephus, quos con- sumserint in terræ descriptione.

## 18:11
Ver. 11. THE LOT CAME UP. From the urn, that is.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ADSCENDIT SORS. De urna scilicet.

## 18:13
Ver. 13. TO ATAROTH-ADDAR. Therefore not as far as the Mediterranean Sea, as Josephus wished in book 5, chapter 3.

Latin:

Vers. 13. IN ATHAROTH ADAR. Non ergo usque ad mare mediterraneum, ut Joseph. voluit lib. 5. cap. 3.

## 18:16
Ver. 16. AND IT DESCENDED TO THE PART OF THE MOUNTAIN THAT FACES THE VALLEY OF THE SONS OF HINNOM. Understand Mount Moriah. Compare ch. 15, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 16. DESCENDITQUE IN PARTEM MONTIS, QUI RESPICIT VALLEM FILI- ORUM ENNOM. Montem Moria intellige. Conf. c. 15, 8.

## 18:18
Vers. 18. HE PASSED OVER EVEN TO THE MOUNDS. In Hebrew, even to Geliboth, which is the proper name of a city, chap. 15, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 18. PERTRANSIT USQUE AD TU- MULOS. In Ebr. usque ad Geliboth, quod nomen urbis proprium cap. 15, 7.

## 18:21
Vers. 21. AND THE CITIES OF HIS. Interpreters note that either these cities have other names or some have been omitted here, on account of the enumeration in chapter 21, where the names Anathoth and Almon also occur.

VALLEY OF CUTTINGS. It is the name of a valley and of a city situated in it not far from Jericho. They are called as if the valley of incision, because in it balsam was cut not with iron, but with sharp glass, bone, or stone, because if it is cut with iron, as Pliny testifies in chapter 12, 25, and Josephus in book 14 of the Antiquities, chapter 7, the shrub dies.

Latin:

Vers. 21. FUERUNTQUE CIVITATES E- JUS. Notant Interpp. vel urbium istarum quibus- dam alia esse nomina vel aliquas hic omissas esse, ob cap. 21. recensionem, ubi etiam occurrunt no- mina Anathot & Alonoa.

VALLIS CASIS. Nomen est vallis & urbis in illa sitæ non pro- cul à Jericho. Dictama sunt quasi vallem incisio- nis, quod in ea balsamum non ferro, sed acuto vi- tro, osse vel lapide incideretur, quia si ferro incida- tur, teste Plinio cap. 12, 25. & Josepho lib. 14. Antiq. c. 7. frutex emoritur.

## 18:24
Vers. 24. GABAE. This city is that which is frequently called elsewhere Gabaa of Benjamin.

Latin:

Vers. 24. GABAE. Urbs hæc ea est, quæ alibi frequenter Gabaa Gabat Benjamin dicitur.

## 18:26
Vers. 26. AND MESPHE AND CAPHARA. The former is called elsewhere Mispha, or Misphat, in which Mesphe was a place of prayer; the latter is called Caphira in chapter 9, 17.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET MESPHE ET CAPHARA. Illa vocatur alias Mispha, vel Misphat, in qua Mesphe orationis locus fuit, hæc cap. 9, 17. dicta est Ca- Caphara. phira.

## 18:28
Vers. 28. WHICH IS JERUSALEM) An ancient city in the part of the Benjamites, but an addition was made from the part of Judah.
