The part of the city which was to the north belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, that which was to the south to Judah. It seemed to Abulensis, however, that either by the exchange of another city, Jerusalem was left by the Benjamites to the tribe of Judah, or by a certain pusillanimity, because they despaired that the Jebusites could ever be conquered by them.

FOURTEEN CITIES. A double sum of these cities: one comprises 12, the other 14; in the first, the eastern cities seem to be collected.

Latin:

Vers. 28. QUÆ EST JERUSALEM) Vetus urbs in parte Benjamitis, sed accessio facta ex parte Judæ. Urbis pars, quæ ad Septentrionem erat, ad tribum Benjamin pertinebat, quæ ad meridiem ad Judam. Abulensi tamen visum, vel urbis alterius permuta- tione Jerusalem à Benjaminittis relictan tribui Juda vel μικροψυχίᾳ quadam, quod dissiderent Jebusæos unquam à se expugnari posse.

CIVITATES QUATUORDECIM. Duplex istarum urbium summa: una XII. alte- ra XIV. complectitur, in prima videntur colligi urbes orientales.

## 19:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIX. The lot of the six remaining tribes.

Vers. 1. AND THEIR INHERITANCE WAS IN THE MIDST OF THE POSSESSION OF THE CHILDREN OF JUDAH. Whether because it was conterminous, or because, since the tribe of Judah had too wide spaces, some part was ceded to the tribe of Simeon, and not because the tribe of Simeon was in the previous lot and dispersed in Israel—which is a fiction that the Rabbis rashly strive to carve out, openly contrary to this passage, from the curse made upon Simeon in Genesis 49, 7. Compare this verse 9.

Latin:

CAPUT XIX. Sex reliquarum tribuum Sors.

Vers. 1. FUITQUE HEREDITAS EORUM IN ME- DIO POSSESSIONIS FILIORUM JUDA. SIve, quod contermina fuerit, sive, quod de tri- bu Juda, quum nimis laxa haberet spatia, tri- bui Simeonis pars aliqua cesserit, non vero quod in sortitione præterita fuerit tribus Simeon & di- spersa in Israele, quod commentum huic loco aper- te contrarium è maledictione Simeoni facta Genes. 49, 7. temere exsculpere satagunt Rabbini. Conf. hic vers. 9.

## 19:2
Vers. 2. BETHSEBAE, AND SABAE. Menochius and Bonfrerius note that these are two names for one place, because otherwise the number of cities would not agree with verse 6. Add 1 Chronicles 4, 28. The 'vav' here, therefore, is exegetical.

Vers. same. AND SABEAE (שבע is now read in the Hebrew: but it appears the LXX read שמע, who translate it Samaa. And this place is called Shema above at 15, 26. Where in the Greek it is wrongly written Salmaa for Samaa. It seems to be the same place which is written Jeshua in Nehemiah 11, 26, where perhaps it was Jeshma, with the letter 'yod' prefixed to the word: as above at 16, 3, and elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 2. BETHSEBAE, ET SABAE. Unius loci duo nomina esse Menochius & Bonfre- rius notant, quia alias numerus urbium non con- grueret vers. 6. Adde 1. Paral. 4, 28. Vav ergo hic exegeticum.

Vers. eod. ET SABEÆ( שבע in Hebræo nunc legitur: sed שמע legisse LXX. apparet, qui vertunt σαμαᾶ. Et שמע hic locus vocatur supra 15, 26. Vbi in Græco male σαλμαὰ scribitur pro σαμαᾶ. Videtur idem esse locus, qui Nehemiæ 11, 26. scri- bitur ישוע, ubi forte fuerit ישמע præposita ad vocem jod litera: ut supra 16, 3. & alibi.

## 19:3
Ver. 3. AND ASEM. The names of the cities listed here in 1 Chron. 4:28 ff. vary somewhat, as for example Hasersusa is called Aasersugim, Bethlebach is called Bethberai, Sarohem Saarim, Athar Etham. However, Thochen is added there, which was either newly built, or not all of them are precisely listed here.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET ASEM. Nomina urbium hic recensitarum 1. Paral. 4, 28. seqq. non nihil variant, ut v. g. Hasersusa vocatur Aasersugim, Bethlebach vocatur Bethberai, Saro- hem Saarim, Athar Etham. Additur tamen illic Thochen, quæ vel de novo exstructa, vel non re- censitæ hic præcise omnes.

## 19:6
Ver. 6. VILLAGES] The LXX translates חצריהן well as κώμας. It would have been more correct as ἐπαύλεις.

Latin:

Vers. 6. VILLÆ] Bene vertit חצריהן LXX. κώμας. Rectius fuerat ἐπαύλεις.

## 19:7
Ver. 7. FOUR CITIES. This number is separated from the previous twenty-one, because the former includes larger cities surrounded by walls, while this one includes smaller cities, or cities without walls, which are called villages in 1 Chron. 4:32.

Latin:

Vers. 7. CIVITATES QUATUOR. Hic numerus à priori XXI. separatur, quod il- le majores muris septas, hic minores, vel sine mœ- nibus civitates complectatur, quæ villæ 1. Paral. 4, 32. vocantur.

## 19:8
Ver. 8. AS FAR AS BAALATH, BEER, RAMATH. These are not three distinct places, but that is the name of the high well of one place; in 1 Chron. 4 it is called Baal.

Latin:

Vers. 8. USQUE AD BAALATH, BEER, RA- MATH. Non sunt tria distincta loca, sed nomen il- lud putei excelsi unius loci est, 1. Paral. 4. vocatur Baal.

## 19:9
Ver. 9. IN THE POSSESSION AND LOT OF THE CHILDREN OF JUDAH, BECAUSE IT WAS GREATER) Adjustment. See what was said at Num. 34.

Latin:

Vers. 9. IN POSSESSIONE ET FUNICULO FILIO- RVM JVDA, QVIA MAJOR ERAT) Adæquatio. Vide quæ dicta ad Num. 34.

## 19:11
Ver. 11. TO THE TORRENT, WHICH IS AGAINST JECONAM. Masius says it is that torrent near the borders of the Sidonians, which they call the Pagida or Belus, which provided sand very suitable for glass works. See Plin. lib. 5. cap. 19. lib. 36. cap. 26. Joseph. lib. 2. Bell. cap. 9.

Latin:

Vers. 11. AD TORRENTEM, QUI EST CONTRA JECONAM. Mafius dicit esse torrentem illum juxta Sidonio- rum fines, quem Pagida vel Belum vocant, qui are- nam præstabat ad opera vitraria percommodam. Vid. Plin. lib. 5. cap. 19. lib. 36. cap. 26. Joseph. lib. 2. Bell. cap. 9.

## 19:12
Ver. 12. TO THE BORDERS OF CHESEL AND THABOR. It seems to Bonfrerius that it is the same city which is called Chafaloth after ver. 18 in the tribe of Issachar, near Mount Thabor.

AND IT GOES OUT TO DABERETH AND ASCENDS AGAINST JAPHIE. Dabereth was left to the tribe of Issachar, chap. 21, 28. Japhie seems to have been assigned to Zebulun according to Adrichomius. They think it is the one which is called Japha by Josephus, lib. 2. Bell. cap. 25.

Latin:

Vers. 12. IN FINES CHESEL ET THA- BOR. Eandem urbem esse, quæ post vers. 18. in tribu Isaschar appellatur Chafaloth Bonfrerio videtur juxta montem Thabor.

ET EGREDITUR AD DABERETH A- SCENDITQUE CONTRA JAPHIE. Dabereth relicta est tribui Isaschar cap. 21, 28. Japhie videtur Zabuloni assignata juxta Adricho- mium. Putant illam esse, quæ Josepho lib. 2. Bell. cap. 25. Japha vocatur.

## 19:13
Ver. 13.

AND IT GOES OUT TO REMMON. Although no mention is made of the Sea of Gennesaret around the eastern boundary of this tribe, it is nevertheless certain from Josephus lib. 5. cap. 1, Isa. 9, 1, Matt. 4, 13, that the Zebulunites reached there. Joshua preferred, however, to describe that boundary rather by the cities which were on the way to that lake, inasmuch as they were then most well-known: nor is it therefore to be denied, with Masius, that that boundary reached to the Jordan or the Sea of Gennesaret.

AND IT CIRCLES TO THE NORTH HANATHON. In the Hebrew, it turns itself from the north of Hanathon, for To Hanathon, by understanding the preposition א, as the LXX, Pagninus, the Tigurines, and Vatablus do: for the northern boundary is described towards Hanathon.

AND ITS OUTGOINGS ARE THE VALLEYS OF JEPHTAHEL. That is: and that boundary ends in the valley of Jephtahel, about which also ver. 27, but nowhere else. Masius thinks it is a part of the valley of Carmel, about which Bonfrerius disputes.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

ET EGREDITUR IN REMMON. Etsi non mentio fiat circa Orientalem termi- num hujus tribus maris Genezareth, eo tamen per- venisse Zabulonitas, è Josepho lib. 5. cap. 1. Ef. 9, 1. Matth. 4, 13. constat. Maluit autem Josua termi- num illum ab urbibus potius, quæ in via illius la- cus erant, describere, utpote, quæ tum fuere no- tissimæ : neque ideo cum Masio negandum ter- minum illum ad Jordanem vel mare Genezareth pertigisse.

ET CIRCUIT AD AQUILONEM HA- NATHON. In Ebr. circumagit se ab aquilone Hanathon, pro Ad Hanathon, subintelligendo præpositio- nem א, ut LXX. Pagninus, Tigurini, Vata- blus: describitur enim terminus Aquilonaris ver- sus Hanathon.

SUNTQUE EGRESSUS EJUS VALLES JEPHTAHEL. Hoc est: & finitur terminus ille in valle Jephta- hel, de qua etiam vers. 27. sed alibi nusquam. Par- tem vallis Carmeli putat Masius, de quo disputat Bonfrerius.

## 19:15
Ver. 15. AND BETHLEHEM.

It is not Bethlehem of Judah, but a different one, and not a little distant from it.

TWELVE CITIES.

If the number is calculated, there will be XIX, but not all the places which are listed belong to the tribe of Zabulon. For the bordering ones are also named. Which ones, however, were Zabulonitic seems to be gathered from verses 13 and 15, because those five and these five looked toward that tribe. For the former five, toward the eastern boundary, which was circumscribed by the Jordan or the sea, necessarily belonged to the tribe of Zabulon, and the latter five, which are referred to in this verse, were assigned to that tribe. To these X cities let Jecnam be added from chapter 21, 34, where Cartha and Damna also occur, as in 1 Chronicles 6, 77; furthermore, Remmono and Thabor are read, either because not all the cities are precisely listed here, or because some had different names.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET BETHLEHEM.

Non est Bethlehem Juda, sed diversa, & non pa- rum ab ea dissita.

CIVITATES DUODECIM.

Si numerus ineatur, XIX. erunt, sed non omnia loca, quæ recensentur, ad tribum Zabulon perti- nent. Nominantur enim etiam contermina. Quæ- nam vero Zabuloniticæ fuerint, colligi videtur è vers. 13. & 15. quod illæ & hæ quinque ad tribum istam spectarint. Priores enim quinque ad termi- num orientalem, qui Jordane vel mari circum- scriptus fuit, necessario ad tribum Zabulon per- tinebant, & posteriores quinque, quæ versu hoc referuntur, tribui illi assignatæ sunt. His X. ur- bibus addatur Jecnam è cap. 21, 34. ubi etiam oc- currunt Cartha & Damna, uti 1. Paral. 6, 77. insu- per leguntur Remmono & Thabor, sive quod hic non omnes urbes præcise recensitæ, seu quod nonnullæ diversa habuerint nomina.

## 19:18
Verse 18. JEZRAEL.

This is distinct from that Jezrael situated in the tribe of Judah in chapter 15, 56, not in the tribe of Manasseh, as Adrichomius wishes, but as is openly taught here, in the tribe of Issachar, perhaps on the border of the tribe of Manasseh, since it is assigned in the Hebrew Manassite locations. It was at one time the seat of the Israelite kings, at least a secondary one, since it had a royal palace, a garden, a vineyard, and other things for royal recreation

Latin:

Vers. 18. JEZRAEL.

Distincta hæc ab illa Jezrael in tribu Juda cap. 15, 56. sita non in tribu Manasse, ut A- drich. vult, sed uti hic aperte docetur, in tribu Isaschar, forte in confinio tribus Manassis, quum in locis Ebraicis Manassiticis assignetur. Fuit aliquando Israëlitarum Regum sedes saltim se- cundaria, quum habuerit regium palatium, hor- tum, vineam, & alia ad regiam recreationem

## 19:22
AS FAR AS THABOR.

The name here is of a city: for otherwise the number of cities would not be consistent, even if the city is so called from the nearby mountain. The same is ascribed to the tribe of Zabulon in 1 Chronicles 6, 77, because it was situated on its border.

BETHSAMES.

This is without doubt different from that which was a Levitical city situated in the tribe of Judah, chapter 21, 16. This word sounds like 'house of the Sun.' Regarding the cities of Issachar, there is doubt from chapter 21, 28 and 1 Chronicles 6, 73. But it must be held that Jaremoth is also called Ramoth and Rameth, and Anem is Engannim, by the contraction of two words into one. Which one, however, is that which is called by another name Dabereth, is not certain. Polyonymy is frequent among the Hebrews. Furthermore, that the tribe of Issachar did not reach the sea, about which Masius raises a doubt, seems to be gathered from chapter 17, 10, because the tribe of Asher is said to be to the north of the Manassites and to join them there; but how could it join them if the tribe of Issachar reached the sea? For thus every access would be cut off for the tribe of Asher, so that it would not touch the Manassites, as Bonfrerius observes.

Latin:

USQUE THABOR.

Nomen hic est urbis: alias enim sibi non constaret urbium numerus, etsi à vicino monte urbs ita dicta. Eadem 1. Paralip. 6, 77. tribui Za- bulon adscribitur, quod in ejusdem confinio sita fuerit.

BETHSAMES.

Hæc sine dubio diversa est ab ea, quæ in tri- bu Juda sita erat Levitica civitas cap. 21, 16. So- nat hæc vox domum Solis. De urbibus Isaschar du- bium est è cap. 21, 28. 1. Paralip. 6, 73. Sed tenen- dum Jaremoth etiam Ramoth vocari & Rameth, Anem vero Engannim, duarum vocum in unam contractione. Quænam vero sit quæ Dabereth alio nomine dicta, non constat. Polyonymia frequens est apud Ebræos. Cæterum non per- tigisse tribum Isaschar ad mare, quo de dubium movet Masius, è cap. 17, 10. videtur colligi, quia dicitur tribus Aser Manassensibus esse ab Aquilo- ne, ibique eis conjungi, quomodo autem conjun- gi posset, si tribus Isaschar ad mare pertigit? Ita enim omnis aditus præscinderetur tribui Aser, quo minus Manassitis contingeret, ut observat Bon- frerius.

## 19:27
Verse 27. BETH DAGON.

This is distinct from the Beth Dagon within the borders of the tribe of Judah, chapter 22, which was called the shrine of Dagon, because in those places the idol Dagon was worshipped, having its name from fish, concerning which Clement of Alexandria in his Exhortation to the Gentiles: Those who inhabit Phoenicia, the Syrians, worship doves and fish.

Verse the same.

TO THE LEFT CABUL) Which name that land near to the Tyrians received from Hiram in the time of Solomon, 1 Kings 9:13, from which a conjecture can be made about the time when this book was written. Indeed, none. For from where is it established that this name Cabul drew its origin from the naming of Hiram?

Latin:

Vers. 27. BETH DAGON.

Distincta hæc est à Beth Dagon intra fines tribus Jude cap. 22. quæ fanum Dagon dicta, quod illis in locis idolon Dagon coleretur, à piscibus nomen habens, de quo Clemen. Alexandr. in exhort. ad Gent. Qui Phæniciam incolunt, Syri, columbas & pisces colunt.

Vers. eod.

AD LÆVAM CABAL) Quod nomen terra illa vicina Tyriis ab Hiromo accepit tempore Solomonis 1. Reg. 9, 13. unde de tempore, quo scriptus hic liber, conjectura capi potest. Imo nulla. Unde enim constat hoc nomen Cabal à denominatione Hiromi Cabul originem traxisse.

## 19:29
Verse 29. AS FAR AS THE MOST FORTIFIED CITY TYRE.

Adrichomius claims this was founded by Thiras, son of Japheth, Genesis 10:2, but in that way it would be older than Sidon, founded by Sidon, grandson of Canaan, whose daughter Tyre is called in Isaiah 23:12, as being founded by the Sidonians, according to Justin, History book 18. And they differ greatly in Hebrew, צור and תיר, or Tyre. It was most fortified, however, because it was once entirely on an island separated from the mainland by 700 paces according to Pliny, and by four stadia according to Curtius, with the sea tide flowing around it on all sides; therefore it is said to be situated in the heart of the sea, Ezekiel 27:4, and the daughter of the sea, Isaiah 23:10. Yet it was conquered by a fleet of 60 ships by Shalmaneser, according to Josephus, book 9, chapter 14, and afterwards under Nebuchadnezzar, with mounds brought from all sides and the intervening channel filled in, the city was joined to the land, conquered, and razed to the ground, as was predicted in Isaiah 23 and Ezekiel 27; subsequently, after two centuries, it was conquered again by Alexander the Great, with the channel once more filled with stones and mounds. It was a most illustrious city in Phoenicia, vying with Sidon in splendor and opulence, and sometimes even surpassing it.

AND ITS BORDERS SHALL BE TO THE SEA BY THE MEASURING LINE OF ACHZIB.

The meaning is: This boundary of the Asherites shall be finished, with the measuring line now having been led around in part to the sea, which touches those lands that are subject to the jurisdiction of the city of Achzib, which is called Ecdippa by Pliny. For by the measuring line, the inheritance is noted here metonymically, as it is accustomed to be called everywhere.

Latin:

Vers. 29. USQUE AD CIVITATEM MUNITISSI- MAM TYRUM.

Hanc à Thiram filio Japhet Genes. 10, 2. conditam vult Adrichomius, sed ita antiquior fuerit Sidone, condita à Sidone Cennis nepote, cujus filia Tyrus dicitur Esa. 23, 12. utpote à Sidoniis condita teste Justino histor. lib. 18. Et differunt maxime in Ebræo צור & תיר vel Tyrus. Munitissima autem fuit, quia tota olim in insula à continente 700. passibus juxta Plin. & Hieronym. quatuor stadiis juxta Curti- um revulsa, marino æstu undique circumfluente, ideo in corde maris dicitur sita Ezech. 27, 4. & filia maris Esa. 23, 10. Expugnata tamen classe navium LX. à Salmanassare teste Joseph. lib. 9. c. 14. & post- ea sub Nebucadnezare, comportatis undique ag- geribus, & alveo interfluente oppleto urbs terræ conjuncta devicta, & ad solum diruta, uti prædictum Esa. 23. Ezech. 27. deinceps iterum post duo secula ab Alex. M. alveo denuo saxis & aggeribus opple- to, expugnata. Fuit urbs in Phœnicia illustrissima cum Sidone de splendore & opulentia certans, eam- que interdum etiam superans.

ERUNTQUE EXITUS EJUS IN MARE DE FUNICULO ACHZIBA.

Sensus est: Finietur iste Asevitarum terminus cir- cumducto scil. jam ex parte funiculo ad mare, quod terras illas, quæ urbis Achziba, quæ à Plinio Ecdip- pa vocatur, jurisdictioni subsunt, attingit. Nam per funiculum hæreditas hic notatur metonymice, uti solet ea passim vocari.

## 19:34
Verse 34. AND IN JUDAH BY THE JORDAN TOWARD THE SUNRISING.

In Hebrew: And in Judah by the Jordan, or through the Jordan from the rising of the Sun: Bonfrerius renders this sense: that it does not reach Judah by the contact of borders, but by an easy passage through the Jordan, which is toward the rising of the Sun, so that it may be signified that the prophecy of Deuteronomy 33:23 is fulfilled concerning Naphtali, who was to possess the sea and the south, which, even though this tribe was remote from the sea and other tribes, especially Judah, which held the most southern region, yet by easy commerce, namely by the crossing of the Jordan, it could enjoy all the goods which are brought by sea, or could be carried from the southern tribes.

Latin:

Vers. 34. ET IN JUDA AD JORDANEM CONTRA ORTUM SOLIS.

In Ebræo: Et in Juda Jordane, vel per Jordanem ab ortu Solis: Sensum hunc reddit Bonfrerius: in Judam pervenire non terminorum contactu, sed facili voragine per Jordanem, qui est ad ortum Solis, ut impleta innuatur Prophetia Deuter. 33: 23. de Naphthalim possessuro mare & meridiem, quod etsi à mari & aliis tribubus imprimis Juda, quæ plagam maxime Australem tenebat, remota esset hæc tribus, facili tamen commercio, nempe per Jordanem trajectu omnibus bonis frui possit, quæ mari advehuntur, vel à tribubus Australibus adsportari possent.

## 19:35
Verse 35. CENERETH.

From this city the lake of Gennesaret seems to have received the name Cenereth, which seems to Masius and Arias to be Tiberias, but not to Bonfrerius, but rather Capernaum, or another city nearby.

Latin:

Vers. 35. CENERETH.

Ab hac civitate videtur lacus Genesareth nomen Cenereth accepisse, quæ Tiberias Masio & Ariæ videtur, non idem Bonfrerio, sed vel Caphernava, vel civitas alia proxima.

## 19:37
Verse 37. CEDES.

It is called elsewhere Cades, and for the sake of distinction on account of other cities of the same name, Cedes of Naphtali, assigned to the Levites in chapter 21:32, 1 Chronicles 6:76.

EDRAI.

Other [cities] of this name in the kingdom of Og of Manasseh occur in chapters 12 and 13.

Latin:

Vers. 37. CEDES.

Dicitur alias Cades, & distinctionis causa propter alias urbes ejusdem nominis Cedes Naphthali Levitis assignata cap. 21, 32. 1. Paral. 6, 76.

EDRAI.

Alia hujus nominis in regno Og Manassitis tributa cap. 12, 13. occurrit.

## 19:38
Verse 38. NINETEEN CITIES.

There is no doubt that those which are named from verse 35 onwards are the names of nineteen cities. Two other cities are also mentioned in chapter 21, 32, Hamonath Dor and Chaitan, which in 1 Chronicles 7 are called Hamon and Ceriathaim, unless perhaps Hamath Dor is the same as Emath.

Latin:

Vers. 38. CIVITATES DECEM ET NOVEM.

Illa, quæ inde à vers. 35. nominata sunt novemdecim civitatum esse nomina, dubium non est. Referuntur & aliæ duæ civitates cap. 21, 32. Hamonath Dor & Chaitan, quæ 1. Paral. 7. vocantur Hamon & Ceriathaim, nisi forte Hamath Dor eadem sit, quæ Emath.

## 19:41
Verse 41. AND THE BORDER OF ITS POSSESSION WAS.

He does not draw a measuring line, as in the other tribes, but lists almost only the Danite cities. The tribe was situated by the sea, or not far from the sea, as the city of Joppa indicates, surrounded by the tribes of Benjamin and Judah on the east. It obtained several cities previously assigned to the tribe of Judah: Zorah, Eshtaol (the homeland of Samson, Judges 13), Timnah (from which Samson took a wife), Ekron, and perhaps also Eltekeh and Baalath.

Latin:

Vers. 41. ET FUIT TERMINUS POSSESSIONIS EJUS.

Non ducit funiculum, ut in aliis tribubus, sed urbes fere tantum Daniticas recenset. Sita tribus ad mare, vel non procul à mari, ut indicat urbs Joppen tribubus Benjamin & Judæ ab oriente circumsepta. Nacta est urbes nonnullas prius tribui Judæ adscriptas Sara, Esthaol (Samsonis patriam Judic. 13.) Themna (ex qua Samson uxorem duxit,) Accaron, fortassis & Eltheca, & Balaath.

## 19:46
Verse 46. WITH THE BORDER THAT FACES JOPPA.

Which is in the region of Joppa: a city that takes its name from its beauty, a very famous port of all Judea.

Latin:

Vers. 46. CUM TERMINO QUI RESPICIT JOPPEN.

Qui è regione Joppe: quæ à pulchritudine nomen habet urbs, percelebris totius Judææ portus.

## 19:47
Verse 47. AND IT IS CONCLUDED BY THE SAME BORDER.

In the Hebrew: And the border of the children of Dan went out from them (the Joppites). Bonfrerius thinks this can be explained in such a way that it preceded them, and the border ended there from the north; namely, rejecting Masius's explanation that the Danites emigrated outside themselves or their inheritance to seek other seats, for it is one thing for a border to go out, and another for the Danites to go out of their boundaries. For thus B. Luther: And at the same the border of the children of Dan ends. The Zurich translators render: and from these the border of the children of Dan goes out. Vatablus, Serarius, and Em. Saa, however, think otherwise, that a sufficient portion was lacking for the Danites, either because a large part of it was taken away, or because it was not occupied due to prevailing enemies.

AND THE CHILDREN OF DAN WENT UP) This happened after the death of Joshua. See Judges 18. Let this be added to the conjectures of the time when this book was written, about which we said something above at 15, 63.

The occasion for this narrative is indicated here by the LXX in the Roman Codex, because the Danites, who were in the mountain, were harassed by the Amorite living in the valley, and were not permitted to descend into the valleys. Compare Judges 1.

CALLING ITS NAME LESEM DAN. According to the Vulgate, the city was called by the compound name Lesem Dan, but that is nowhere to be found, nor does it agree with the Hebrew, in which it is indicated that the city of Lesem was called by the name of Dan; therefore Masius rightly corrects the Vulgate here.

Verse same. AND BY THE NAME OF DAN THEIR FATHER] That is, from the name of the victorious tribe, which bore the name from the Prince of its own race.

Latin:

Vers. 47. ET IPSO FINE CONCLUDITUR.

In Ebr. Et exivit terminus filiorum Dan ab eis (Joppensibus.) Quod ita explicari posse, censet Bonfrerius, quod eos prævenerit, & ibi desierit terminus à Septentrione; scil. reprobans Masii explicationem, quod Danitæ extra se vel hæreditatem suam emigrarint ad alias sedes quærendas, aliud enim est terminum exire, aliud Danitas limitibus suis exire. Ita enim B. Lutherus: Und an demselben endet sich die Gräntze der Kinder Dan. Tigurini reddunt: & ab his exit limes filiorum Dan. Aliter tamen Vatablus, Serarius, Em. Saa, quod Danitis sufficiens portio defecerit, sive quod illius magna pars detracta, sive, quod non occupata prævalentibus hostibus.

ASCENDERVNTQVE FILII DAN) Post mortem Josuæ hæc facta. Vide Judicum 18. Accedat hoc ad conjecturas temporis, quo scriptus hic liber, de quo aliquid diximus supra ad 15, 63.

Occasio indicatur narrationis hujus factæ hic à LXX. in Codice Romano, quod ab Amorrhæo in valle habitante Danitæ, qui in monte erant, vexati sint, nec permissi in valles descendere, Conf. Judic. 1.

VOCANTES NOMEN EJUS LESEM DAN. Juxta Vulgatam dicta fuerit civitas composito nomine Lesem Dan, sed id nuspiam habetur, nec Ebræo congruit, in quo Lesem civitatem nomine Dan nuncupatam indigitatur, ideo merito hic ca- stigat Vulgatam Masius.

Vers. eod. ET NOMINE DAN PATRIS SVI] Id est, ex nomine tribus victricis, quæ a generis sui Principe nomen ferebat.

## 19:49
Verse 49. ACCORDING TO THE COMMANDMENT OF THE LORD. In Hebrew: According to the mouth of the Lord. See Numbers 14:24, Joshua 15:9, from which it seems to be gathered that the Lord had indeed assigned a place to Caleb in Kadesh-barnea, but had commanded concerning Joshua that whatever place he himself should choose for himself, that should be assigned to him as an inheritance.

Latin:

Vers. 49. JUXTA PRÆCEPTUM DOMINI. In Ebr. Juxta os Domini. Vid. Numer. 14, 24. Jos. 15, 9. è quo colligi videtur, Dominum in Ca- desbarne Calebo quidem locum assignasse, de Jo- sua autem præcepisse, ut quem ipse eligeret sibi lo- cum, is ei hæreditario assignaretur.

## 19:50
Verse 50. THAMNATH-SERAH IN THE MOUNT OF EPHRAIM.

Joshua the commander asked for only a single city, and that one almost in ruins, because it is added HE BUILT IT. For a city is often said to be built when an old one, already almost in ruins, is restored. Furthermore, it was arid and narrow, not fertile, pleasant, or ample, which seems to be called Saraa from the heaviness of the trees and the sterility of the soil, as Montanus notes, and it was situated on Mount Gaas, or of the tempest, commotion, and storm, Joshua 24:30, Judges 2:9, 2 Samuel 23:30, on the northern side of which he also wished to be buried. St. Paula marveled at this modesty of such a great commander, according to Jerome in the Life of Paul. There was a type in him of Christ, who for our sake wished to become poor, when He was rich and the King of glory, as Origen notes in Homily 24, and Theodoret in Question 16. He taught, as the same Theodoret advises, that those who are established in any magistracy ought to serve not their own conveniences, but the utility of their subjects.

Latin:

Vers. 50. THAMNATH SARAA IN MON- TE EPHRAIM.

Josua imperator unicam urbem tantum petiit, eamque pene dirutam, quia additur ÆDIFICA- RET EAM. Sæpe enim ædificari dicitur civitas, cum vetus jam propemodum diruta restituitur. Adhæc aridam & angustam, non uberem, amœ- nam aut amplam, quæ ab arborum graveolentia, & soli sterilitate videtur Saraa dicta, notante Mon- tano, & sita fuit in monte Gaas vel tempestatis, com- motionis, & procellæ, Jos. 24, 30, Judic. 2, 9. 2. Sam. 23, 30. in cujus latere septentrionali sepeliri etiam voluit. Quam tanti Imperatoris modestiam mira- ta est S. Paula apud Hieronym. in vita Paul. Typus in eo fuit Christi, qui pro nobis voluit pauper fieri, quum dives esset ac Rex gloriæ, notante Origene hom. 24. Theodor. quæst. 16. Docuit, ut idem Theo- dor. monet, eos, qui in Magistratu aliquo consti- tuti sunt, non suis commodis, sed utilitati subdito- rum debere inservire.

## 19:51
Verse 51. AND THEY DIVIDED THE LAND. In Hebrew: And they finished from dividing the land. This Vulgate is not sufficiently convenient. For the completion of the partition is indicated. Therefore, B. Luther is more correct: And thus they finished the dividing of the land.

Latin:

Vers. 51. PARTITIQUE SUNT TERRAM. In Ebræo: Et finierunt à dividenda terra. Non satis commode hæc Vulgata. Nam partitionis consummatio indicatur. Rectius ergo B. Luthe- rus: Und vollendeten also das Austheilen des Lan- des.

## 20:1 Argument
SECTION II. OF PART II. KYBERNETIKE, or CONCERNING THE GOVERNMENT OR REGIMEN OF JOSHUA. CHAPTER XX. Cities of refuge.

Verse 1. SEPARATE THE CITIES OF THE FUGITIVES. In Hebrew: Cities of refuge, to which he who has killed someone by chance may flee, Numbers 35, Deuteronomy 19. Masius rightly detests here that temples, cemeteries, and monasteries are granted as asylums to criminals and murderers, to which Tirinus pretends in vain the holiness of the places, because when wicked men are admitted to holy places, no honor redounds from it to those places, from which they themselves ought rather to be warded off and driven away: although the places in themselves are not holy, but relatively so on account of the presence of the most holy God, which is tied to no place, nor promised except to faithful and holy men.

Latin:

SECTIO II. PARTIS II. ΚΥΒΕΡΝΗΤΙΚΗ, seu GUBERNATIONEM VEL REGIMEN JOSUÆ ATTINENS. CAPUT XX. Civitates refugii.

Vers. 1. SEPARATE URBES FUGITIVO- RUM. IN Ebræo: Urbes refugii, ad quas confugiat, qui fortuito aliquem occiderit Numer. 35. Deuter. 19. Merito hic Masius detestatur, quod templa, cæme- teria, cænobia, facinorosis & homicidis pro asy- lis concedantur, cui nequicquam Tirinus sanctita- tem locorum prætendit, quia cum admittuntur ad sancta loca scelerati, nullus inde honor ad loca illa redundat, à quibus ipsi potius arcendi & fugandi essent: quamvis loca in se non sint sancta, sed σχε- τικῶς ob præsentiam Dei sanctissimi, quæ nulli lo- co alligata, nec nisi fidelibus & sanctis hominibus promissa est.

## 20:3
Verse 3. SHALL HAVE STRUCK UNKNOWINGLY] The Greeks translate it as akousios (involuntarily). See what is said in Numbers 35:4, Deuteronomy 19:2.

Latin:

Vers. 3. PERCVSSERIT NESCIVS] בשגגה Græ- ci vertunt ἀκουσίως. Vide quæ dicta Num. 35, 4. Deut. 19, 2.

## 20:6
Verse 6. UNTIL HE STANDS BEFORE THE JUDGMENT.

For he was bound to prove his innocence, that he had killed the man involuntarily and by accident. He had to remain in the city of refuge until he was brought out for the case to be discussed by public judgment Num. 35, 12. and thus, having been brought back, he was bound to remain in that city until the High Priest died Num. 35, 25. By this figure was signified the liberation which has been obtained for us through the death of Christ.

Latin:

Vers. 6. DONEC STET ANTE JUDICIUM.

Probare enim tenebatur innocentiam suam, quod involuntarie & fortuito hominem occiderit. Morandum ei erat in urbe refugii, donec educere- tur ad causam publico judicio discutiendam Num. 30, 12. atque ita reductus eo usque in urbe illa sub- sistere tenebatur, donec Pontifex moreretur Num. 35, 25. Significata hac figura liberatio, quæ per Chri- sti mortem nobis parta est.

## 21:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXI. The cities of the Levites.

Verse 1. TO THE LEADERS OF THE CLANS.

Hebrew: Princes of the Fathers, that is, the princes of the families throughout the tribes of Israel, chapter 14, 1.

Latin:

CAPUT XXI. Urbes Levitarum.

Vers. 1. AD DUCES COGNATIONUM.

EBr. Principes Patrum, Principes puta familia- rum per tribus Israel cap. 14, 1.

## 21:3
Verse 3. AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL GAVE FROM THEIR POSSESSIONS.

The Levites were dispersed throughout the possessions of all the tribes, firstly for the instruction of the people, so that all the tribes might be educated in the Holy Scriptures and the divine law. For these colleges were like seminaries of religion and piety, from which the neighboring cities could seek the seeds of heavenly doctrine and examples of a holier life: then for the distribution of the burden, so that one tribe would not be burdened more than another; thirdly, because of the divine prediction in Genesis 49, 7, where dispersion among the brothers is indeed decreed for the sons of Levi as a punishment, but that punishment, by divine compassion, was turned for them into honor and glory. More cities were also given to the Levites than to the other tribes, both for the honor of the Priesthood and because the other tribes had fields and villages with their cities, whereas the Levites had only the suburbs for a thousand paces, as Tostatus notes.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DEDERUNTQUE FILII ISRAEL DE POSSESSIONIBUS SUIS.

Dispersi erant Levitæ per possessiones omnium tribuum primo ob populi informationem, ut de S. li- teris & lege divina omnes tribus erudirentur. E- rant enim hæc Collegia quasi seminaria religionis & pietatis, ex quibus civitates vicinæ cælestis doctri- næ semina, & sanctioris vitæ exempla petere pote- rant: tum ob oneris partitionem, ne una tribus præ alia oneraretur; tertio ob divinam prædictionem Ge- nes. 49, 7. ubi in pœnam quidem filiis Levi sancitur dispersio inter fratres, sed ea pœna, divina com- miseratione ipsis conversa in honorem & gloriam. Plures etiam urbes Levitis datæ, quam cæteris tribubus tum ad honorem Sacerdotii, tum quia cæteræ tribus urbes habebant pagos & vicos, Levi- tæ autem tantum suburbana ad mille passus, notan- te Tostato.

## 21:4
Verse 4. THIRTEEN CITIES.

Of the 48 cities of the Levites, 13 were given in the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin to the priests, who established their domicile there, not only because of the fertility of the soil, but also because of the proximity of the place where God had destined the temple for Himself. In the parallel passage 1 Chronicles 6, 60, only the names of eleven cities are listed; therefore, the number must be supplemented from this history, and Ain and Gabaon must be added. Abnath is there, which here is Asmon, and Asan seems to be Jesa. Compare Joshua 15, 56; chapter 19, 7. But why were so many cities given to the priests, who were almost all 24 in the crossing of the Jordan? Menochius answers: The people wanted to be generous with the Levites, and they did not look at how much they had grown, but how much they could grow in the future.

Verse of the same.

OF THE TRIBES OF JUDAH AND SIMEON AND BENJAMIN] The territory remained with the tribes. The habitation, however, in the towns, and the fields nearby for pasture, fell to the Levites. Thus according to Siculus: The jurisdiction in the fields which were assigned remained with those from whose territory they were taken. See on the Law of War and Peace, book 2, chapter 3, section 4.

Latin:

Vers. 4. CIVITATES TREDECIM.

E civitatibus XLVIII. Levitarum in tribubus Juda, Simeon, & Benjamin XIII. Sacerdotibus da- tæ, qui ibi domicilium figebant, non modo ob soli fertilitatem, sed etiam ob loci, in quo tem- plum Deus sibi destinarat, propinquitatem. In loco parallelo 1. Paral. 6, 60. recensentur tantum undecim civitatum nomina, supplendus ergo ex hac historia numerus & addendæ Ain & Gabaon. Abnath ibi est, quæ hic Asmon, & Asan videtur Je- sa esse. Conf. Jos. 15, 56. cap. 19, 7. Cur autem tot civitates Sacerdotibus, qui in transitu Jordanis omnes fere fuere 24. datæ? Respondet Menochius. Populus cum Levitis largus esse voluit, & non quan- tum crevissent respexit, sed quantum imposterum crescere possent.

Vers. eod.

DE TRIBVBVS JVDA ET SIMEON ET BENJA- MIN] Territorium manebat penes tribus. Habitatio vero in oppidis, & agri juxta pascui Levitis cedebant. Sic apud Siculum: Iurisdictio in agris qui assignati sunt, penes eos re- mansit, ex quorum territorio sumti sunt. Vide de Jure Belli ac Pacis libro 2. cap. 3. §. 4.

## 21:9
Vers. 9. THERE WERE FORTY EIGHT) Namely, those six dedicated from the beginning for refuge, and then these 42, which themselves also had the right of refuge, but in such a way, if the inhabitants of the cities were willing, and at the expense of the refugees.

Vers. 41.

AND THE LORD GOD GAVE TO ISRAEL ALL THE LAND. That does not seem to have been done. For many of the Canaanites still remained to be defeated, chap. 13, Judg. 1. Therefore, let it be understood that He gave it as regards Right and Dominion in the distribution itself, intending to give shortly also what remained, as regards use and possession, provided they remained in duty and the worship of God. For it was not expedient that all things be given immediately and at once, lest the land become overgrown for lack of cultivators. Exod. 23:29, 30.

Vers. 42.

AND PEACE WAS GIVEN BY HIM TO ALL NATIONS ROUND ABOUT. In the Hebrew: And the Lord gave them rest round about according to all that God swore to their fathers.

ALL WERE REDUCED INTO THEIR DOMINION. Namely, those who opposed them. For otherwise the Canaanites still remained in their midst, who were not defeated.

Latin:

Vers. 9. FUERUNT QUADRAGINTA OCTO) Nem- pe sex illæ ab initio confugio dicatæ, & deinde hæ XLII. quæ & ipsæ jus confugii habuere, sed ita, si habitatores urbium vellent, & sumptu confugarum.

Vers. 41.

DEDITQUE DOMINUS DEUS ISRAELI OMNEM TERRAM. Id non videtur factum. Multi enim adhuc è Cananæis debellandi mansere cap. 13. Judic. 1. Ergo dedisse intelligatur quoad Jus & Dominium in ipsa distributione, daturus brevi etiam quæ restabant, quoad usum & possessionem, modo permanerent in of- ficio & cultu Dei. Neque enim expediebat omnia statim ac simul dari, ne terra cultorum defectu sil- vesceret. Exod. 23, 29. 30.

Vers. 42.

DATAQUE AB EO PAX IN OMNES PER CIRCUITUM NATIONES. In Ebr. Et requiem dedit Dominus eis in circui- tu juxta omnia, super quibus juravit Deus Patribus eorum.

CUNCTI IN EORUM DITIONEM RE- DACTI SUNT. Qui scil. iis se opposuerunt. Superabant enim cæteroquin adhuc Cananæi in medio ipsorum, qui non debellabantur.

## 21:11
Verse 11. HEBRON.

Therefore, either the field of Hebron alone was given to Caleb, as Magalianus wished, even though he conquered Hebron itself, or if the city was also given to him, he donated it to the Levites, and retained for himself only the field and the villages, with the taxes and other revenues of the city, because the Levites only obtained the right of dwelling, as Tostatus, Serarius, and Menochius hold.

Latin:

Vers. 11. HEBRON.

Calebo ergo vel ager Hebron tantum datus, ut Magalianus voluit, etsi Hebron ipsam expugna- vit, vel si data etiam ipsi civitas, donavit eam Le- vitis, & agrum ac vicos sibi tantum retinuit, cum vectigalibus aliisque proventibus urbis, quia Le- vitæ tantum jus habitandi adepti sunt, ut Tostatus, Serarius, Menochius.

## 21:36
Verse 36.

OF THE TRIBE OF RUBEN) These two verses were not in the most ancient Hebrew codices: and therefore the Masora does not count them either. Wherefore they seem to have been added from the Chronicles, as Kimchi judges: whence they came into the Greek, Syriac, and Latin versions, and into certain of the Chaldean Codices. There are found also in certain books words slightly changed, such as קדיסת or קדמת, likewise מגרשר instead of מגרשוה instead of קדמות.

These things seem to teach that other editions as well as versions must be tested against the most ancient Hebrew codices, especially if the Masora, which is often the law, agrees with them. But by no means, as is otherwise customary for Grotius, should the ancient Hebrew Codices be corrected from the versions. That this verse certainly did not exist in any copies in the time of Rabbi Hai, who lived eight hundred years ago, is proven by the same ancient Rabbi, R. David Kimchi. But if Grotius wishes from this to undermine the reliability of modern Hebrew Codices, he will contradict himself. Because he is accustomed to oppose modern Codices to those which the LXX, the Chaldeans, the Syrian, or the Latin interpreters used: who, however, here agree with the modern Hebrew codices. From that, therefore, the authority of those Codices which he thinks were used by those interpreters in translation would also have to be endangered, which, however, he himself wishes to remain intact. Nothing else, therefore, will be gathered from this than a variety of readings in the Hebrew Codices; and so that not all modern editions of the Hebrew text in general are troubled, as far as this passage is concerned, the later Venetian editions published with the Masora, by the work of R. Jacob Chajim, and also the Basle edition which followed them, intervene. For these do not have those verses. Furthermore, what Ludovicus Capellus disputed about those verses with Johannes Buxtorf the Younger, who contended that they were omitted wrongly and unjustly, can be read in his Vindic. Verit. Ebraic. Part 1, chapter 4, page 105. And thus against Grotius we have previously stood with Buxtorf. But when we weigh the matter more accurately, and do not dispute only according to human reasoning, but diligently compare the entire text, we are strongly moved (for we do not deny it) by these things primarily, namely that verse 7. Cities are reported to have been given to the Merarites from the tribe of Ruben no less than from the tribe of Gad and Zabulon, which therefore were not to be omitted here in the complete description of the Levitical cities assigned according to the tribes; then because the total sum of the cities designated for the Merarites by Joshua, which is 12, demands it, to complete which these four cities from the tribe of Ruben are required; finally, because the total sum of the Levitical cities is established here, namely that there were 48. But if these 4 cities are omitted, there will be only 44. By which reasons I am easily led to believe that those two verses, 36 and 37, are not interpolations in the Vulgate, but genuine. Nor, however, can the Hebrew source be argued from this, with Bonfrerius and other Jesuits, to be a source of universal corruption. For not only do most Codices in our times have them, but some ancient Codices also had them, just as Kimchi, who flourished around the year of Christ 1190, testifies concerning an old copy in which he found them himself, which are also held in the Chaldean M.S. Complutensian Codex in Masius, and in the Chaldean of the Royal Work, as also in the Greek version of the LXX Interpreters, and also in the Latin and Syriac. Nothing, therefore, other than a diversity of reading of the Hebrew Codices can be proven from this, which cannot consist with universal corruption. But if the Hebrew text is considered corrupt for the reason that some Hebrew Codices do not have these verses, and formerly did not have them, one must establish the same thing about the Latin version: for however much modern editions may have them, the Louvain scholars alone observed ten manuscripts in which it did not exist. If you say that this is also evident from this example, that those Hebrew Codices with which the Masora agrees are not always to be preferred: we can easily grant that. For we have never made the Masora authentic: nor yet, because of some errors of the Masora, would anyone affirm that the whole Masora is to be rejected, which Buxtorf warns of here, l. c. If the Biblical text gives assurance to the Codex, certainly greater account must be taken of the συνεχείας & συναφείας of the undoubted Scripture, with the faith of some Codices supporting it, than of the Masora. Which is what happened here, whence the Clementine edition rightly retained these verses, provided that the context declares them to be γνησίους. In no way to be excused: that it inserted those words BEYOND THE JORDAN AGAINST JERICHO, inasmuch as they are held in no Hebrew Codices, nor in the Chaldean text. The same must be held regarding the words IN THE WILDERNESS, AND MISOR AND JAER (which were placed in the stead of Chedemoth, although the LXX distinguish Ἰαζὴρ & Γεδσὼν. For they omit Jethson.) For neither do those appear in the Hebrew or Chaldean, nor are they held in the Complutensian and Royal Latin Bibles, and they are prefixed by Tostatus. But most of those seem to have been brought back from 1 Chron. 6:78.

Latin:

Vers. 36.

DE TRIBV RVBEN) Duo hæc commata in antiquis- simis Hebræorum codicibus non fuere: itaque nec Maso- ra hos numerat. Quare adjecti videntur ex Paralipomenis, ut censet Kimchi: unde venere in versiones Græcam, Syram, Latinam, & in Chaldaicorum Codicum quosdam. Repe- riuntur & in libris quibusdam voces paulum mutatæ, ut קדיסת aut קדמת, item מגרשר pro מגרשוה pro קדמות.

Hæc docere videntur ad antiquissimos codi- ces Ebræos exigendas esse alias cum editiones, tum versiones, maxime si Masora, quæ sæpe le- gis est, istis consentiat. Neutiquam vero, quod Grotio alias solemne est, è versionibus Codices Ebræos antiquos corrigendos esse. Hunc certe versum in nullis exemplaribus tempore Rabbi Hai, qui ante octingentos annos vixit, extitisse, ex eodem Rabbi antiquo R. David. Kimchi pro- bat. Quod si hinc Grotius fidem Codicum mo- dernorum Ebræorum labefactare velit, sibi ipsi adversabitur. Quia opponere solet modernos Co- dices istis, quos adhibuerint LXX. Chaldæi, Syrus, aut Latinus Interpretes: qui vero hic consenti- unt modernis Ebræis codicibus. Inde ergo pe- riclitari etiam oporteret illorum Codicum Auto- ritatem, quos ab istis Interpp. in translatione ad- hibitos censet, quam tamen ipse salvam cupit. Nihil itaque aliud hinc, quam lectionum varietas in Codicibus Ebræis colligetur; ac ne in genere omnes modernæ editiones textus Ebraici solici- tentur, quoad hunc locum, posteriores editio- nes Venetæ cum Masora editæ, opera R. Jaco- bi Chajim, nec non quæ illas sequuta est, Ba- siliensis editio intercedunt. Hæ enim versus il- los non habent. Porro, quæ de illis versibus cum Johanne Buxtorffio Juniori Ludovic. Capellus disputavit, hoc perperam & injuria istos omif- sos contendente, legi poterunt in illius Vindic. Verit. Ebraic. Part. 1. cap. 4. p. 105. Atque ita ad- versus Grotium nos antehac cum Buxtorffio. Cæterum ubi accuratius rem expendimus, nec κατʼ ἄνθρωπον tantum disputamus, sed textum in- tegrum conferimus sedulo, valde (non enim dif- fitemur) nos movent hæc imprimis, quod nem- pe v. 7. Meraritis ex tribu Ruben civitates datæ non minus perhibeantur, quam ex tribu Gad & Zabulon, quæ proinde hic in integra descriptione civitatum Leviticarum juxta tribus assignatarum prætermit- tendæ non erant; tum quod summa id postulet ci- vitatum Meraritis à Josue designatarum numero 12. ad quam supplendam quatuor hæ civitates è tribu Ruben requiruntur, denique quod summa to- ta civitatum Leviticarum hic constituta sit, quod scil. fuerint XLVIII. At si prætermittantur hæ IV. civitates, XLIV. tantum erunt. Quibus rationi- bus facile inducor, ut credam, versus illos duos 36. & 37. non esse embolimæos in Vulgata, sed germa- nos. Neque tamen inde cum Bonfrerio, aliisque Je- suitis Ebræus fons universalis corruptionis argui potest. Nam non habent tantum eosdem plerique Codices nostris temporibus, sed habuere etiam Co- dices antiqui nonnulli, quemadmodum Kimchi, qui circa annum Christi 1190. floruit, testatur de exemplari vetusto, quod in eodem ipsos invene- rit, quos etiam in Codice Chaldeo M. S. Complu- tensi apud Masium, & in Chaldeo Oper. Regii ha- beatur, ut & in versione Græca LXX. Interpp. nec non in Latina & Syriaca. Nihil ergo aliud quam diversitas lectionis Codicum Ebræorum hinc probari poterit, quæ cum corruptione uni- versali consistere nequit. Si corruptus vero ideo censeatur Ebræus textus, quod nonnulli Codicum Ebræorum hos versus non habeant, & olim non habuerint, oportet idem statuere de versione La- tina: nam utut modernæ editiones habeant, Lo- vanienses tamen soli decem manuscripta obser- varunt, in quibus non extiterit. Si dicas, id etiam ab hoc exemplo patere, non præferendos semper Codices illos Ebræos, quibus Masora consentit: fa- ciles id largiri possumus. Non enim Masoram au- thenticam unquam fecimus: nec tamen propter er- rores nonnullos Masoræ, totam Masoram rejicien- dam quisquam affirmarit, quod hic monet Bux- torff. l. c. Si textus Biblicus fidem faciat Codici, major utique συνεχείας & συναφείας Scripturæ in- dubitatæ ratio habenda, Codicum aliquorum fide adstipulante, quam Masoræ. Quod hic usu venit, unde Clementina editio merito hos versus retinuit, siquidem contextus eos γνησίους esse, dictitet. Nul- latenus excusanda: quod verba illa ULTRA JOR- DANEM CONTRA JERICHO inseruerit, ut- pote quæ in Ebræis Codd. nullis habentur, nec in textu Chaldæo. Quod pariter habendum de ver- bis IN SOLITUDINE, ET MISOR ET JAER (quæ loco Chedemoth posita, licet Ἰαζὴρ & Γεδσὼν distinguant LXX. Jethson enim omittunt.) Nam nec illa in Ebr. aut Chald. comparent, nec in Com- plut. & Regiis Bibl. Latin. habentur, & à Tostato præ- mittuntur. Pleraque autem illa reducta videntur è 1. Paral. 6, 78.

## 22:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXII. The altar of witness, and the contention concerning the same.

Latin:

CAPUT XXII. Altare testimonii, & contentio de eodem.

## 22:2
Vers. 2. YOU HAVE DONE ALL) From the Hebrew) שמרתם. But the Greeks read שמעתם: for they translate it ἀκηκόατε.

Latin:

Vers. 2. FECISTIS OMNIA) Ex Hebræo) שמרתם. At שמעתם legere Græci: vertunt enim ἀκηκόατε.

## 22:3
Vers. 3. FOR A LONG TIME.

For an entire seven-year period. For with the three wars finished, these returned home. The Hebrews err in Seder Olam, counting two seven-year periods, whom Masius and Magalianus nevertheless followed.

Latin:

Vers. 3. LONGO TEMPORE.

PEr integrum septennium. Bellis enim confectis tribus hæ domum reversæ sunt. Errant Ebræi in Seder Olam, duo septennia numerantes, quos se- quuti tamen sunt Masius & Magalianus.

## 22:8
Verse 8.

DIVIDE THE SPOILS OF THE ENEMIES WITH YOUR BRETHREN) That is, go away happy with that part of the spoils which falls to you.

Do not divide it man by man, but into equal parts, so that the warriors retain one half, and the brethren who remained with the baggage and guarded it in Gilead retain the other half: such a division was also observed by Moses in Num. 31. Afterwards, however, a division of this kind was sanctioned by David, which was to be made man by man, so that the portion of the one remaining with the baggage and the one contributing to the fight might be equal, 1 Sam. 30.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

DIVIDITE PRÆDAM HOSTIVM CVM FRATRI- BVS VESTRIS) Id est, læti abite cum ea parte prædæ, quæ vos contingit.

Non viritim dividite, sed in partes æquales, ut dimidium bellatores retineant, alterum dimidium fratres, qui ad sarcinas manserunt, illasque tutati sunt in Galaadite: qualis divisio etiam à Mose ob- servata Num. 31. postea tamen à Davide sancita est ejusmodi divisio, quæ viritim fiat, ut æqua esset por- tio remanentis ad sarcinas & pugnam conferentis 1. Sam. 30.

## 22:9
OF SHILOH WHICH IS SITUATED IN CANAAN SO THAT THEY MIGHT ENTER GILEAD.

Canaan here denotes the land of the nine tribes across the Jordan, but Gilead denotes the land on this side of the Jordan for them. Otherwise, Canaan signifies the whole land of the 12 tribes. But Gilead sometimes denotes only the portion of the tribe of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, which lies adjacent to this mountain.

Latin:

DE SILO QUÆ SITA EST IN CANAAN UT INTRARENT GALAAD.

Canaan notat hic terram trans Jordanianam novem tribuum, Galaad vero terram eis Jordanem. Alias Canaan totam terram XII. tribuum significat. Galaad vero quandoque tantum fortem tribus Gad, ac dimidiæ tribus Manassis notat, quæ huic monti adjacet.

## 22:10
Verse 10. AND WHEN THEY HAD COME TO THE MOUNDS OF THE JORDAN.

That is, to the embankments which, placed against the waters of the Jordan, restrained them.

THEY BUILT BY THE JORDAN AN ALTAR OF INFINITE SIZE.

In place of infinite size, in the Hebrew it is: A great altar to the sight. It was to be built on the western bank of the Jordan, namely before they crossed the river, not as Josephus wishes, after the crossing on the western bank. For they wished to testify to the right which they had in the land of Canaan, primarily to sacrifice in the place chosen by the Lord for that purpose, and to the altar, as common to the Israelite tribes.

OVER AGAINST THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL.

In the region, or opposite them, but not against them. For they were not erecting it for the sake of schism, but for the sake of communion.

Latin:

Vers. 10. CUMQUE VENISSENT AD TUMULOS JORDANIS.

Id est, ad aggeres, qui Jordanis aquis objecti illas coercebant.

ÆDIFICAVERUNT JUXTA JORDANEM ALTARE INFINITÆ MAGNITUDINIS.

Loco infinitæ magnitudinis in Ebr. est: Altare magnum ad conspectum. In ripa Jordanis Occidentali, priusquam scil. fluvium trajicerent, id exstruendum, non ut Josephus vult, post trajectum in ripa occidentali. Testari enim voluere jus suum quod haberent in terra Canaan imprimis ad sacrificandum in loco à Domino ad id electo, & altari, ceu tribubus Israëlitis communi.

CONTRA FILIOS ISRAEL.

E regione, vel ex opposito eorum, non vero adversus eosdem. Non enim schismatis, sed communionis causa id erigebant.

## 22:11
Verse 11. AND WHEN THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL HAD HEARD) The whole has a right over its parts, and the greater part has the right of the whole: as is said in the book of the Law of War and Peace, book 2, chapter 5, § 17, and Deut. 13, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 11. QVOD CUM AVDISSENT FILII ISRAEL) Universitati jus est in suas partes, & major pars jus habet universitatis: ut dictum de Jure Belli ac Pacis libro 2. cap. 5. §. 17. & Deuter. 13, 12.

## 22:13
Ver. 13. PHINEHAS THE SON OF ELEAZAR THE PRIEST.

The Hebrew fiction which Peter Damian followed, that Phinehas is Elijah, whom he says will live here until the end of the world, Cornelius refutes here and at Num. 21, 13 as a paradox.

Latin:

Vers. 13. PHINEES FILIUM ELEAZARI SACERDOTIS.

Ebræorum commentum quod sequutus est Petrus Damian. Phineen esse Eliam, quem hic victurum esse dicit ad finem mundi, ceu paradoxon refutat hic & ad Num. 21, 13. Cornelius.

## 22:16
Ver. 16. THUS COMMANDS ALL THE PEOPLE OF THE LORD) Just as a formal declaration is required between two nations by the law of nations, so also when a dissension has arisen between citizens, it is used in the same way, either so that the accused state may purge itself or make satisfaction, or so that the innocent may separate themselves from the guilty.

Latin:

Vers. 16. HÆC MANDAT OMNIS POPVLVS DOMINI) Denunciatio sicut jure gentium inter duas gentes requiritur, ita etiam orto inter cives dissidio ex æquo usurpatur, vel ut civitas accusata se purget aut fatisfaciat, vel ut innocentes à nocentibus se separent.

## 22:17
Ver. 17. AND UNTO THIS PRESENT DAY THE STAIN OF THIS CRIME REMAINS IN US.

Understand this not as a stain of guilt or punishment, because that had been remitted for the penitent, and it is false that guilt once remitted still demands punishment from GOD: but of infamy, which remained upon the whole people on account of that crime.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET USQUE IN PRÆSENTEM DIEM MACULA HUJUS SCELERIS IN NOBIS PERMANET.

Intellige non de macula culpæ aut pœnæ, quia ea remissa erat pœnitentibus, & falsum est remissa culpa pœnam adhuc poscere DEUM: sed infamiæ, quæ manebat totum populum ob id scelus.

## 22:18
Ver. 18. AND TO-MORROW AGAINST ALL ISRAEL HIS WRATH WILL RAGE) See above 7, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ET CRAS IN VNIVERSVM ISRAL IRA EJVS DESÆVIET) Vide supra 7, 1.

## 22:19
Ver. 19.

If on account of the crimes of the former inhabitants your land seems unclean to you, which you are not permitted to expiate by sacrifices, as we are, who have the altar of the Lord in Shiloh, so that you have thought it necessary to build a new altar across the Jordan in your vicinity, which you might easily approach, dwell among us. We will yield to you a part of our land. They wished to redeem the aversion of schism at such a price: that they did not even hesitate to assign lands to these tribes from their own possessions. The LXX agree with the Hebrew. See chapter 7.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

Si ob scelera priorum incolarum videtur vobis terra vestra immunda, quæ vobis per sacrificia expiare non liceat, uti nobis, qui in Silo altare Domini habemus, ut inde opus censueritis altari novo trans Jordanem in vicinia vestra, quod adire facile possitis, habitate inter nos. Cedemus vobis partem terræ nostræ. Tanti redimere volebant schismatis aversionem: ut de suis fortibus terras istis tribubus assignare etiam non dubitarent. LXX. conveniunt cum Ebræo. Vid. cap. 7.

## 22:22
Ver. 22. THE MOST MIGHTY GOD THE LORD.

Most are accustomed to allege those three divine names in an oath to attest to the power, justice, and majesty of God. But as we grant that the first, El, denotes the power of God: so the second, Elohim, denotes the glory of God, because he is σέβασμα, a Deity to whom worship is owed; the third, Jehovah, denotes the nature of God, because he is an independent essence, from whom all things depend. As for that threefold repetition of El Elohim Jehovah, El Elohim Jehovah, he himself knows that it is not lacking in mystery; parallel passages teach this, in which a similar repetition is observed, significant of the mystery of the Trinity, Psalm 2:1, Isa. 33:22, Exod. 20:7, Deut. 6:4, Ps. 42:2, 3, Jer. 33:2, Dan. 9:19. Cf. Ps. 67:7, Isa. 6:3. In Midrash Tillim on Ps. 50:1, these things are read: And why is the name of the holy God, blessed be he, mentioned three times? Namely, so that you may learn that in these three names the holy God, blessed be he, created his world according to the three מדות (properties) in which the world was created. Furthermore, what did they mean by repeating these twice? namely, because in them the world was created, and in them the law was given.

Latin:

Vers. 22. FORTISSIMUS DEUS DOMINUS.

Tria illa nomina divina in juramento allegare plerique solent ad contestandam DEI poten- tiam, justitiam & majestatem. Sed uti primum El Dei potentiam notare largimur: sic alterum Elo- him Dei gloriam, quod sit σέβασμα Numen, cui cultus debeatur, tertium Jehovah Dei naturam, quod sit independens essentia, à qua dependeant omnia, notat. De trina autem illa repetitione El Elohim Jehovah, El Elohim Jehovah ipse scit, quod ea non careat mysterio, loca parallela docent, in quibus similis observatur repetitio, mysterii Tri- nitatis σημαντικὴ, Psalm. 2, 1. Esa. 33, 22. Exod. 20, 7. Deuter. 6, 4. Ps. 42, 2. 3. Jerem. 33, 2. Dan. 9, 19. Conf. Pf. 67, 7. Es. 6, 3. In Midrasch Tillim super Ps. 50, 1. hæc leguntur: Et quare nomen Dei sancti benedicti me- moratur tribus vicibus? scil. ut discas, quod in tribus istis nominibus creavit Deus sanctus Benedictus mun- dum suum juxta tres מדות proprietates, in qui- bus mundus creatus est. Porro quid sibi voluerunt, quod bis hæc iterarunt? nempe, quia in iis mundus creatus est, & in iis lex data est.

## 22:23
Verse 23. HE HIMSELF SHALL SEEK AND JUDGE. That is, he shall avenge and punish. For inquiries and judgments, which are made concerning crimes, refer to the inflicting of punishments; therefore, to seek and to judge is a phrase of Scripture used for to avenge and to punish. Moncaeus is mistaken in book 1 de Aar., as if it were lawful to sacrifice at this altar outside the days of Passover, Pentecost, and Tabernacles, and that they built it with that intention. Which they clearly deny here.

Latin:

Vers. 23. IPSE QUÆRAT ET JUDICET. Id est, ulciscatur & puniat. Nam quæstiones & judicia, quæ de criminibus fiunt, referuntur ad irroganda supplicia, ideo quærere & judicare phra- si Scripturæ usitata est ulcisci & punire. Fallitur Moncæjus l. 1. de Aar. quasi licitum fuerit extra dies Paschatis, Pentecostes & Scenopegiæ in hoc altari sacrificare, eoque animo id extruxerint. Quod hic plane negant.

## 22:24
Verse 24. WHAT HAVE YOU TO DO WITH THE LORD GOD OF ISRAEL. See similar phrases in Judg. 11:12, 2 Sam. 16:10, 1 Kings 17:18, 2 Kings 3:13, Joel 3:4; it signifies that no business intervenes, as is explained in v. 25, 27, you have no part in the Lord. Cf. 1 Kings 12:16, Josh. 13:8. They declare, therefore, that the altar was erected solely as a testimony of the communion of faith, religion, and the worship of the one God, because they wished to worship the same God with the same faith and religion beyond the Jordan, whom the Hebrews worshipped in Canaan.

Latin:

Vers. 24. QUID VOBIS ET DOMINO DEO ISRAËL. Similes phrases vide Judic. 11, 12. 2. Sam. 16, 10. 1. Reg. 17, 18. 2. Reg. 3, 13. Joel. 3, 4. significat nihil commercii intercedere, ut explicatur v. 25. 27. par- tem non habetis in Domino. Conf 1. Reg. 12. v. 16. Jos. 13, 8. Declarant ergo solum in testimonium com- munionis fidei, religionis & cultus unius Dei altare erectum, quod eundem Deum eadem fide ac reli- gione colere velint eis Jordanem, quem colebant Ebræi in Canaan.

## 22:27
Verse 27. FOR A TESTIMONY) See above 8:30.

Latin:

Vers. 27. IN TESTIMONIVM) Vide supra 8, 30.

## 22:30
Verse 30. AND THE PRINCES OF THE DELEGATION OF ISRAEL WHO WERE WITH HIM) In the Hebrew: and the princes of the congregation, and the chiliarchs: in Greek, πάντες οἱ ἄρχοντες τῆς συναγωγῆς, that is, the senate and the highest of the minor magistrates. These make a προβούλευμα (preliminary decree), which the people follow below in 33. See above 8:33, 9:11.

Latin:

Vers. 30. ET PRINCIPES LEGATIONIS ISRAEL QVI ERANT CVM EO) In Hebræo: & principes cœtus, & chiliarehi: Græce, πάντες οἱ ἄρχοντες τῆς συναγωγῆς, id est senatus & minorum magistratuum summi. Hi προβούλευμα faciunt, quod sequitur populus infra 33. Vid. supra 8, 33. 9, 11.

## 22:31
Verse 31. AND YOU HAVE DELIVERED THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL FROM THE HAND OF THE LORD. You have delivered, not by averting a plague already rushing in, but by keeping yourselves immune from sin and schism, and by not giving cause for a plague to be inflicted.

Latin:

Vers. 31. ET LIBERASTIS FILIOS ISRAEL DE MANU DOMINI. Liberastis non avertendo plagam jam irruen- tem, sed à peccato & schismate vos immunes ser- vando, nec dando causam plagæ infligendæ.

## 22:32
Verse 32. FROM THE LAND OF GILEAD, THE BORDERS OF CANAAN. This error of the Vulgate is not to be borne. For Gilead did not belong to Canaan. In the Hebrew it is: From the land of Gilead into the land of Canaan, and so also the Chaldean and the LXX have it, as do the Royal Codex and several others. Whence Bonfrerius did not hesitate to correct the Sixtine edition here (the authority of the Pope being disregarded).

Latin:

Vers. 32. DE TERRA GALAAD, FINIUM CHANAAN. Error hic Vulgatæ non ferendus. Nam Ga- laad non pertinebat ad Chanaan. In Ebræo est: De terra Galaad in terram Chanaan, atque ita etiam Chald. & LXX. habent, ut & Regius Codex & alii nonnulli. Unde castigare hic Sixtinam (insuper habita Pontificis autoritate) non dubitavit Bon- frerius.

## 22:34
Verse 34. OUR TESTIMONY THAT HE IS GOD. Bellarmine in his tract on images, Vasquez in his book on adoration, Serarius, and Cornelius gather from this here that it is right to manufacture images and structures which refresh the memory of God, Christ, and the saints. Which is not badly asserted against the Iconoclasts, provided that the worship of them and idolatry be absent.

Latin:

Vers. 34. TESTIMONIUM NOSTRUM QUOD IPSE SIT DEUS. Bellarm. tract. de imag. Vasquetz libr. de adorat. Serarius & Cornel. hic colligunt inde, recte imagi- nes & fabricas fabricari, quæ memoriam Dei, Chri- sti & sanctorum refricent. Quod adversus Iconocla- stas non male asseritur, modo absit cultus earum & idololatria.

## 23:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIII.

Assembly and exhortation to keep the commandments of GOD.

Vers. 1. JOSHUA CALLED ALL ISRAEL. I understand either some of the people or the Princes, so that the following Vav is exegetical. Moreover, he called them in the last year of his life, not in Thamnath-serah, as Serarius and Menochius do with the Rabbis, but rather in Shiloh, where the tabernacle was, as Bonfrer rightly [argues].

Latin:

CAPUT XXIII.

Comitia & exhortatio ad servanda DEI præ- cepta.

Vers. 1. VOCAVIT JOSUE OMNEM IS- RAELEM. INtelligo vel nonnullos ex populo vel Principes, ut Vav sequens sit exegeticum. Vocavit autem anno vitæ suæ ultimo non in Thamuat Sare, ut cum Rabbinis Serarius & Menochius, sed potius in Silo, ubi erat tabernaculum, ut recte Bonfre- rius.

## 23:2
Vers. 2. AND THE MASTERS) In Hebrew שוטריו. See above 8, 33. below 27, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET MAGISTROS) In Hebræo שוטריו. Vide supra 8, 33. infra 27, 1.

## 23:4
Vers. 4. HE DIVIDED. In Hebrew it is the first person: I divided. Thus also the Chaldean has it, as does the version of the LXX.

Latin:

Vers. 4. DIVISIT. In Ebr. est prima persona: Divisi. Sic etiam Chal- dæus habet, ut & LXX. viralis versio.

## 23:7
Vers. 7. AFTER YOU HAVE ENTERED UNTO THE NATIONS. The word for entering, by the force of the Hebrew phrase, is either taken specifically regarding the familiarity and relationship which is begun by marriage, or rather in general regarding all familiarity.

SWEAR IN THE NAME OF THEIR GODS) In Hebrew: Do not mention the name of their gods, nor swear. See Exod. 23, 13. Therefore, those words: do not mention, are wrongly omitted in the Vulgate. Nor does He wish the names of other gods to be mentioned, namely for the sake of worship: nor an oath to be taken in the name of other gods. However, the superstition of Cornelius is not to be approved, who dare not name idols at all. For worship or honorable commemoration, as Bonfrer acknowledges, is forbidden, not simple commemoration.

Latin:

Vers. 7. POSTQUAM INTRAVERITIS AD GENTES. Vox intrandi ex vi phraseos Ebrææ, vel specia- tim accipitur de familiaritate ac necessitudine, quæ conjugio initur, vel potius in genere de omni fami- liaritate.

JVRETIS IN NOMINE DEORVM EORVM) In Hebræo: Ne commemoretis nomen deorum earum, neque jure- tis. Vide Exod. 23, 13. Perperam ergo illa: ne commemoretis, in Vulga- ta omissa. Nec commemorari vult nomina Deo- rum aliorum scil. cultus gratia: nec in Deorum ali- orum nomine juramentum præstari. Non tamen probanda cum Cornelio superstitio, qui nullate- nus nominare audent idola. Cultus enim vel com- memoratio honorifica, ut agnoscit Bonfrer. non simplex commemoratio prohibetur.

## 23:12
Vers. 12. TO MIX MARRIAGES AND TO JOIN FRIENDSHIPS) Against the law of Exod. 34. v. 15. 16. Deut. 7, 2. The Israelites sinned in these things after the times of Joshua, Jud. 3. verse 5.

Latin:

Vers. 12. MISCERE CONNVBIA ATQVE AMICITIAS CO- PVLARE) Contra legem Exod. 34. v. 15. 16. Devt. 7, 2. In has post Josuæ tempora peccarunt Israelitæ Jud. 3. versu 5.

## 23:13
Vers. 13. LET THEM BE TO YOU AS A PIT. In Hebrew, לפח, a pit, is not held, but לצד, a snare. It is a discourse about a scandal of guilt: not a scandal of punishment, which Cornelius wrongly calls it so; or [it is] a punishment, for the following words treat of that, warning of the removal from the land of Canaan or ejection. Conf. Numer. 33, 55.

Vers. eod. A STUMBLING BLOCK FROM YOUR SIDE) In Hebrew: A whip in your sides. For it was the custom for sides to be struck with thongs. Ecclesiast. 30, 12. & 41, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 13. SINT VOBIS IN FOVEAM. In Ebræo non habetur לפח fovea, sed לצד la- queus. De scandalo culpa sermo est: Non scandalo pœnæ, quod ita perperam vocat Cornelius; vel pœ- na, de ea enim sequentia verba agunt, ablationem de terra Canaan vel ejectionem monentia. Conf. Numer. 33, 55.

Vers. eod. OFFENDICVLVM EX LATERE VE- STRO) Hebraice: Flagellum in vestris lateribus. Lora enim latera cædi mos erat. Ecclesiast. 30, 12. & 41, 6.

## 23:14
Vers. 14. I AM ENTERING THE WAY OF ALL THE EARTH. That is, of mortals living on the earth: by metonymy: It is called elsewhere the way of all flesh, and it is a periphrasis of death, for every man tends toward it, and this way must be trodden by all. LXX. ἀποτρέχω, I run through, because our life is a continuous course toward death.

Latin:

Vers. 14. INGREDIOR VIAM UNIVERSÆ TERRÆ. Id est, viventium in terra mortalium: per me- tonymiam: Dicitur alias via universæ carnis, estque periphrasis mortis, ad eam enim tendit omnis ho- mo, & hæc via calcanda est omnibus. LXX. ἀπο- τρέχω percurro, quia vita nostra est continuus ad mortem cursus.

## 24:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIV.

The covenant of the people with the Lord. The death of Joshua. The burial of the bones of Joseph. The death of Eleazar the High Priest.

Vers. 1. IN SHECHEM) In Shiloh. Which is a place in the land of the Shechemites.

Grotius followed Menochius, Tirinus, and Serarius, because the LXX read Silo instead of Sichem, although in the Complutensian and Royal Bibles it is read in Sichem. But the Chorography contradicts this. For Silo was not in the field of Sichem, but was distant from it by ten miles, as Jerome notes in loc. Ebr. These latest assemblies were held shortly before the death of Joshua in Sichem, so that in that place, where Abram first entering the land of Canaan offered a sacrifice to God Gen. 12, 6.7. and was established by God as the heir of Canaan, his descendants, having entered upon the inheritance, might solemnly swear to the law of God, and where the Patriarchs, the sons of Jacob, were buried Acts 7, 16. Josh. 24, 32. he might bid his last farewell to the Israelites by the repetition of the law and of the covenant with God. Add that the same covenant had formerly been renewed at the entry into the land near Shechem, on the mountains of Gerizim and Ebal, Josh. 8.

IN THE SIGHT OF THE LORD.

Before the ark of the covenant, which therefore it is necessary to have been translated by the command of Joshua from Shiloh to Shechem for that purpose, so that the covenant might be sanctioned before the Lord. But whether it was translated with the tabernacle, they raise a doubt, since where necessity required, it could be detached from the tabernacle, 1 Sam. 4, concerning which see at verse 26. Others simply [take it as] in the sight of the Lord, that is, with the true fear of God, as Gen. 15, 1, or that they are implied to be gathered by divine authority. Compare Gen. 27, 7.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIV.

Fœdus populi cum Domino. Mors Josuæ. Se- pultura ossium Josephi. Mors Eleazaris Pontificis.

Vers. 1. IN SICHEM) Silunte. Qui locus in Sicimitarum terra.

SEquutus est Menochium, Tirinum & Serarium Grotius, quia LXX. pro Sichem legunt Silo, quamvis in Bibliis Complut. & Regiis legatur in Si- chem. Sed repugnat Chorographia. Nam Silo non erat in agro Sichem, sed distabat ab eo decem mil- liaribus notante Hieronymo in loc. Ebr. Comitia hæc novissima paulo ante obitum Josuæ celebra- ta in Sichem, ut eo loco, ubi Abram primum ter- ram Canaan ingrediens sacrificium Deo obtulit Genes. 12, 6.7. ac hæres Cananææ à Deo institutus est, posteri ejus hæreditate adita in Dei legem so- lemniter jurarent, & ubi Patriarchæ filii Jacobi se- pulti sunt Actor. 17, 16. Jos. 24, 32. legis & foederis cum Deo repetitione, Israëlitis ultimum vale dice- ret. Adde quod foedus idem olim in ingressu terræ juxta Sichem, in montibus Garizim & Hebal inno- vatum fuerit Jos. 8.

IN CONSPECTU DOMINI.

Coram arca fœderis, quam proinde oportet jussu Josuæ è Silunte in Sichem ea fini translatam esse, ut coram Domino fœdus sanciretur. An ve- ro cum tabernaculo translata fuerit, dubium mo- vent, siquidem ubi necessitas requirebat, divelli potuerit à tabernaculo 1.Sam. 4. de quo ad vers. 26. Alii simpliciter in conspectu Domini, id est, cum vero Dei timore ut Gen. 15, 1. vel ut divina autoritate con- gregati innuantur. Conf. Genes. 27, 7.

## 24:2
Ver. 2. BEYOND THE RIVER.

The Euphrates in Mesopotamia.

AND THEY SERVED STRANGE GODS.

Augustine, Abulensis, and Pererius understand this of Terah and Nahor, not of Abraham; yet Serarius, citing various authors, and Tirinus in this place, affirm this also of the younger [Abraham]. Which opinion is truer. For it is said in the plural: Your fathers served strange gods, and Terah, Abraham, and Nahor are expressly named, and the grace of God is celebrated therefrom, because they were liberated from that idolatry, and for that end Abraham was called by God, so that through him, having renounced the worship of strange gods, the true worship of God and the doctrine concerning the blessed seed might be propagated: That he had been addicted to the religion of the Sabaeans, by whom the stars, and especially the sun and the remaining planets were worshipped, not only the Arabs assert, as is to be seen in the Alcoran, Beidavi, and Kesseus, and the Hebrews Maimonides in More Nev. page 424, and the Commentary on the Mishnah, chap. 4, fol. 4, but also not a few Christian doctors: see Eusebius, Hist. Eccles. lib. 1, c. 5, Masius in the Commentary on Joshua, p. 333. Rainold. de idolol. p. 169. Cunaeus de Republ. Hebr. p. 295. Hottinger. Thesaur. Phil. 1. cap. 1. sect. 8. p. 55. and Histor. Orient. lib. 1. cap. 8. p. 163. 172. B. Balduin. Concion. in libr. Jos. in h. l. Hackspan. in edit. Nizzachon p. 490. See Gen. 11, 31.

Latin:

Vers. 2. TRANS FLUVIUM.

Euphratem in Mesopotamia.

SERVIERUNTQUE DIIS ALIENIS.

De Thare & Nachor hoc intelligunt Augustin. Abulens. Perer. non de Abrahamo: de quo juniore tamen id etiam affirmat Serarius adducens varios autores, & Tirinus in h. l. Quæ sententia verior est. Nam in plurali dicitur: Patres vestri servierunt Diis alienis, & nominantur expresse Thare, Abraham & Nahor, & celebratur inde gratia Dei, quod ab illa idololatriæ liberati sint, eoque fine Abraham à Deo vocatus, ut per eundem abdicato cultu alie- norum Deorum verus Dei cultus, & doctrina de benedicto semine propagaretur: Quem Sabæorum religioni: à quibus Stellæ, & imprimis Sol, ac pla- netæ reliqui colebantur, addictum fuisse non Ara- bes tantum, ut in Alcorano, Beidavi, & Kesseo videre est, & Ebræi Maimonid. in More Nev. pag. 424. & Commentar. in Mischn. cap. 4. f. 4. sed & Christi- ani Doctores non pauci asserunt: vid. Euseb. Hist. Eccles. lib. 1. c. 5. Masius in Comment. in Jos. p. 333. Rainold. de idolol. p. 169. Cunæus de Republ. Hebr. p. 295. Hottinger. Thesaur. Phil. 1. cap. 1. sect. 8. p. 55. & Histor. Orient. lib. 1. cap. 8. p. 163. 172. B. Balduin. Concion. in libr. Jos. in h. l. Hackspan. in edit. Niz- zachon p. 490. Vid. Genes. 11, 31.

## 24:3
Verse 3. AND I GAVE YOU A LAND IN WHICH YOU DID NOT LABOR, AND CITIES WHICH YOU DID NOT BUILD, SO THAT YOU MIGHT DWELL IN THEM, VINEYARDS AND OLIVE GROVES WHICH YOU DID NOT PLANT) From Deuteronomy 6, 11. Antiphanes: τοῖς πολεμίοις ἔυχεσθαι δεῖ τἀγαθὰ πα- ρεῖναι χωρὶς ἀνδρείας. &c.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DEDIQVE VOBIS TERRAM IN QVA NON LABORASTIS, ET VRBES, QVAS NON ÆDI- FICASTIS, VT HABITARETIS IN EIS, VINEAS ET OLIVETA QVÆ NON PLANTASTIS) Ex Devteron. 6, 11. Antiphanes: τοῖς πολεμίοις ἔυχεσθαι δεῖ τἀγαθὰ πα- ρεῖναι χωρὶς ἀνδρείας. &c.

## 24:9
Ver. 9. FOUGHT AGAINST ISRAEL) Not by force, but by guile, which the following [verses] also explain, and the history itself shows.

Latin:

Vers. 9. PUGNAVIT CONTRA ISRAELEM) Non vi, sed dolis, quod & sequentia explicant, & ipsa Historia ostendit.

## 24:11
Ver. 11. AND THE MEN OF HIS CITY FOUGHT AGAINST YOU, THE AMORITE AND THE PEREZZITE, AND THE CANAANITE, AND THE HITTITE, AND THE GIRGASHITE AND THE HIVITE AND THE JEBUSITE) The Greeks well [translate it] ἐπολέμησαν πρὸς ὑμᾶς. For נלחם often signifies not a fight, but a war, and some of the peoples who are named here did nothing other than close the gates.

Augustine, the fight, he says, was an armed defense. And they prepared themselves for the fight. The words of the Hebrews often signify an act not completed, but begun, and sometimes even only an affection and an attempt, not an effect.

Ver. same. THE AMORITES AND THE PEREZZITES.

Which some interpret in such a way that some from all those peoples were in Jericho when it was being fought. But it is manifest that the peoples who were conquered by Joshua are indicated.

Latin:

Vers. 11. PUGNAVERUNTQUE CONTRA VOS VI- RI CIVITATIS EJUS, AMORRHÆUS ET PHERE- ZÆUS, ET CANANÆUS, ET HETHÆUS, ET GER- GEZÆUS ET HEVÆUS ET JEBUZÆUS) Græci bene ἐπολέμησαν πρὸς ὑμᾶς. Nam נלחם sæpe non pugnam, sed bellum significat, & populorum, qui hic nominantur, qui- dam nihil aliud quam portas clauserunt.

August. pugna, inquit, fuit armata defensio. Et pararunt se ad pugnam. Verba Ebræorum sæpe actum non perfectum, sed inchoatum, quandoque etiam affectum & conatum duntaxat significant, non effectum.

Vers. eod. AMORRHÆOS ET PHERE- SÆOS.

Quod quidam ita accipiunt, quod ex omnibus istis populis aliqui in Jericho fuerint, cum pugna- retur. Sed manifestum est, indicari populos, qui devicti sunt à Josua.

## 24:12
Verse 12. AND I SENT HORNETS BEFORE YOU AND DROVE OUT.

In the Hebrew it is the third person HE DROVE OUT, so that it may refer to the hornet (for it is held in the singular). The hornet drove them out, that is, God through the hornet, as His army. Hornets indeed so wore down the Amorites that the Hebrews, following them, easily slaughtered them with their own swords and pierced them with arrows. Augustine metaphorically understands the hornets as the stings of fear from rumors flying ahead, or as demons. But the literal sense is to be preferred, Exod. 23, 21. Wis. 12, 8. which sense Augustine also does not reject, while he adds: unless perhaps someone says: not all things that were done are written down, and this also was done visibly, so that he wishes true wasps to be understood.

Latin:

Vers. 12. MISIQUE ANTE VOS CRABRO- NES ET EJECI.

In Ebr. est tertia persona EJECIT, ut ad cra- bronem (habetur enim in singulari) referatur. Ejecit illos crabro, id est, Deus per crabronem, ceu exercitum suum. Crabrones nempe ita attrive- runt Amorrhæos, ut eos sequentes Ebræi facile ipsos gladiis suis trucidarint, & sagittis confixerint. Augustin. metaphorice crabrones intelligit de acu- leis timoris è rumoribus prævolantibus, aut dæmoni- bus. Sed præferendus est sensus proprius, Exod. 23, 21. Sap. 12, 8. quem sensum etiam non reprobat Au- gustinus, dum addit: nisi forte quis dicat: non omnia, quæ facta sunt, esse conscripta, & hoc quoque visibi- liter factum, ut veras vespas velit intelligi.

## 24:19
Verse 19. AND JOSHUA SAID TO THE PEOPLE) A stipulation.

FOR GOD IS HOLY.

In the Hebrew, Because Elohim Kedoschim or Holy HE. By which plural number with a singular pronoun, a plurality of persons in one divine essence is designated. We argue here thus: More than one קדשים HOLY ONES, who are אלהים, are more than one person, because a plural substantive with a plural adjective signifies a true plurality of the thing signified, which is evident from an induction of passages. In Jehovah or the divine essence there are more than one קדשים HOLY ONES, who are and are called אלהים. Therefore. Which argument is confirmed (1.) from the subject, which here is the name Jehovah, which applies to more than one אלהים, since in the Scriptures Jehovah sending and Jehovah sent are introduced, etc. (2.) from the substantive noun to which it is joined, which name אלהים we showed above to imply more than one person in God. And therefore there is no reason why we should admit an enallage here, but rather it must be believed that more than one holy Elohim is hinted at: but it is also corroborated (3.) from the distribution of the thing signified: For the divine holiness is distributed among more than one person, or rather is common to more than one person, since not only is the Father a holy God, but the Son is also a holy God (who is a person distinct from the Father), that ἅγιος Acts 3, 14. 1 John 2, 20. the true holy one Apoc. 3, 7. קדש קדשים Holy of Holies or Most Holy of all Dan. 9, 24. Holy and the Holy Spirit. Hence that קדוש is acclaimed to God by the Holy Angels three times Isa. 6, 3. Furthermore (4.) from the object of religious service: since one must serve not only the one person of the Father, but also the Son with religious worship, and therefore more than one person: since all ought to honor the Son as the Father John 5, 23. (5.) Finally from the cause of religious service, which is brought forward here, that Jehovah Elohim led the people out of Egypt and liberated them.
