Quæ posterior pars velut appendix prioris est : quum non historiam continuet, quæ præcesserat, sed tantum nonnulla ἀξιομνημόνευτα, quæ contigere ante Judi- cum excitationem commemoret: unde in priori tan- tum chronotaxis justa deprehenditur: posterior autem negligit eandem, imo regreditur ad prio- rem anarchicum statum, ne ille intactus plane relin- quatur, & historiæ negligantur, quas observasse utile judicavit S. S. Unde Character istorum tem- porum exprimitur aliquoties, quod ea fuerint, quibus non erat Rex in Israele, sed quisque quod re- ctum erat in oculis suis, faciebat, Jud. 17, 6. cap. 18, 1. cap. 19, 1. cap. 21, 25. hoc est, quum nullus esset Ma- gistratus supremo præditus imperio, qui populum in pietatis & honestatis officio contineret, quæ tempora erant Seniorum post Josuæ Mortem se- quuta, priusquam sub servitutem à Chusane redige- rentur: quibus ἀναρχία fuit, & Israelitæ à vero Dei cultu in terra Canaan primum defecerunt, at- que idololatria sese commacularunt Judic. 2, 7. 14. de quo digna sunt, quæ ad cap. 17, 1. observantur in annotatis Junio-Tremellianis, quæ hîc repe- tantur: Quæcunque ab hoc capite usque ad finem libri narrantur, ad ea pertinent, quæ scribuntur supra 2. v. 11. & sequentibus, ut non multo post mortem Jeho- schuhæ gesta fuisse appareat: primum quod ad histo- riam hujus & sequentis capitis attinet, eo quod veri- simile non est tribum Danis, quæ numerosa erat, diu potuisse propria possessione carere, ut caruisse dicitur infra 18, 1. & confirmatur Jehos. 19, 47. Deinde eo quod is, quem in Sacerdotem tribus Danitica adopta- vit, juvenis & pronepos Moschis ex Menasche erat ut apparet ex 18, 30. Tertio quia hanc historiam, ante sequentem de Benjaminitis gestam esse ostendit auctor infra 20, 1. Similiter quod ad sequentem historiam cap. 19. & seqq. sub idem tempus eam contigisse probatur primum ex Pinchaso, qui tum temporis Sacerdotio fungebatur, ut apparet ex 20. v. 28. de- inde ex eo, quod Jeruschbalaimorum (quæ Jebus di- cebatur) ea pars, quæ ad Benjaminem spectabat, adhuc à Jebusæis tenebatur, ut docetur infra cap. 19. vers. 12. Vide supra cap. 1. vers. 8. & 21. postremo ex verbis Deboræ Judic. 5. vers. 14. Est ergo hujus & sequentium capitum status Israelitarum Rempubl. tam in religione, quam in moribus fuisse corruptissi- mam: quia ex parvis initiis brevi tempore totæ tribus in idololatriam & aperta scelera ruerunt, quod satis fuit unico tantum in utroque genere ex- emplo confirmasse. Finis autem est, ut judiciorum Dei (quæ supra à cap. 3. hucusque commemorata sunt) justitia elucescat.

Pars prior particulares quasdam expeditiones tradit cap. 1. & quantum ad universæ terræ promissæ statum pertinent, exequitur: idque partim genera- tim, occasionem & causam vicisitudinum servitu- tis vel pressuræ, ac quietis terræ exponens cap. 1. re- liquo à vers. 22. ut & cap. 2. cap. 3. ad. vers. 2. partim speciatim easdem sub judicum regimine ordine exe- quens: quos in priores distinguimus ante Abimele- chum, qui per tyrannidem invasit regimen & per Sichemitas rex creatus est, ac judicis nomine in- dignus est: & in posteriores, qui post interemtum Abimelechum Israeliticum populum sospitarunt. Priorum Judicum & Salvatorum populi tres, utpo- te Athniel, Ehud & Samgar, quod ad liberationem populo præstitam describuntur cap. 3. à v. 8. Postea cap. 4. Deboræ regimen & victoria: & cap. 5. ejus carmen Eucharisticum exhibetur: denique tribus sequentibus capitibus historia Gideonis, utpote cap. 6. qua vocationem & confirmationem ejusdem divi- nam, cap. 7. qua victoriam & populi liberationem: & cap. 8. qua consequentia, interfectionem Succotano- rum, reliquorum Principum Midianitarum puni- tionem, & terræ Israelitarum tempore Gideonis quietem. Sequenti 9. capite historia Tyrannidis Abimelechi, & exitus ejusdem describitur.

Dehinc posteriores Judices secundum seriem tem- porum regiminis commemorantur, & juxta gemi- nam novam Israelitarum apostasiam, ac consequen- tem pressuram, ac servitutem primo sub Philisti- nis & Ammonitis, quæ describitur quoad anteceden- tem quietam gubernationem sub Thola & multiva- riam sub Jairo idololatriam pœnamque gravissimam cap. 10. ut & quoad divinam ab hostibus liberatio- nem per Jepthath, cujus victoria contra Ammonitas & votum cap. 11. nec non bellum contra Ephraimitas seditiosos cap. 12. traditur: Quo sequentes etiam Judices Ebzan, Elon, & Abdon succincte describun- tur. Secundo sub Philistinis: à quorum potestate liberati sunt Israelitæ per Simsonem. De ejus na- tivitate agitur cap. 13. de Conjugio cap. 14. de tradi- tione in manus Philistinorum à tribu Juda facta, & ho- stium interfectione, cap. 15. de proditione Delilæ, & Philistinorum in morte oppressione cap. 16.

Atque hæc prior est pars Judicum: in altera com- memoratur historia de Idolo Michæ, cujus erectio in domo Michæ cap. 17. ereptio à tribu Dan, & idolola- tria in illa tribu cap. 18. exponitur: tum debello Ben- jaminico: cujus causa facinus Benjaminitarum, stu- prum nefarium cap. 19. & prælium ipsum Israelitarum contra tribum Benjamin cap. 20. & quæ illud conse- quuta sunt, quomodo residuis Benjaminitis de uxo- ribus prospectum fuerit, servatis virginibus in Ja- bes, ac deletis conjugatis, nec non per raptum puel- larum Siluntinarum cap. 21.

De Chronologia libri magna est autorum discre- pantia: Nonnulli cum Josepho intervallum, ex quo Judices præfuerunt, justo longius faciunt. Nam Josephus servitutum tempus seorfim nume- rat à tempore judicatuum, utpote 8. annos Meso- potamicæ, 18. Moabiticæ, 20. Cananiticæ, 7. Midia- niticæ, 18. Ammoniticæ, 40. Philistinæ servitutis; at- que ita præterea 40. annos Othonielis, 80. Ehud, 1. Samgar, 40. Deboræ, 40. Gideonis, 3. Abimele- chi (23. Tholæ anni omittuntur in Josepho: quod vero sine dubio sphalma est. Vid. Jud. 10. vers. 1. 2.) 22. Jair, 6. Jephthe, 7. Ebzam, 10. Elon, 8. Abdon (quamvis hunc nominet Josephus sine mentione numeri annorum, quod spalmatis indicium non obscurum est,) 20. Simsonis. Atque ita etiam ha- bent se numeri Laur. Codoman. ut & Woltheri, nec non Nicolai Reimari Ursi, nisi quod Josephus Samgari annum tribuat & annos 18. ἀναρχίας ante Mesopo- tamicam servitutem seorfim numeret, Woltherus 21. Codomannus 20. regiminis seniorum annos ei- dem præmittat, quos 20. annos tamen in Simsonis Judicatu prætermittit Codomannus servitutis Phi- listinæ annis eosdem includens. Quo pacto Jose- phi calculo prodituri sunt 429. anni, Woltheri 431. Codomanni & Raimari 410. à morte Josuæ ad ex- cessum Simsonis: nec ullatenus salvare licebit ma- gnum illum ac celebrem numerum 480. annorum ab egressu Israelitarum è terra Ægypti usque ad tem- pus cœpti ædificii templi Salomonici 1. Reg. 6. vers. 1. aperte designatum. Nam indubitatis illis 40. an- nis errationis in deserto addendi sunt anni domi- natus Josuæ, quos 25. Principatus Eli, quos 40. ju- dicatus Samuelis & Saulis, quos 50. Josephus assi- gnavit, (cui consentiunt in hisce prædicti autores, nisi quod 40. solum, & rectius Samueli & Sauli adscribant, Woltherus 26. annos principatus Josuæ, Raimarus 7. tantum constituat) cum 40. annis re- gni Davidici, ut tribus primordialibus Salomonis, atque ita summa inde collecta, immane quantum excedet numerum 480. à S. S. designatum. Non ignoramus sane multos, nec ignobiles Scriptores isti seorsivæ numerationi annorum servitutum & judicatuum, quamvis non una omnes ratione, calculum adjicere: utpote Hieronymum Epist. 132. ad Vitalem, Augustinum lib. 15. de Civ. Dei c. 13. Sulpitium Severum, Nicephor. Constantinopol. Cedrenum in Chronic. Philastr. p. 3. hær. 63. Sigonium in Sulpitium, Serarium in 1. Reg. 6. Canum l. 1. de loc. ad argum. 12. Codomannum item, Petavium, Petrum Possinum, Nicolaum Abrami & alios: Sed quia numerus ille annorum exitus usque ad templum intercedit, utique aliis merito à litera & verbis luculentis Regum libri discedere religio fuit: alium igitur iniere plerique calculum, cum Ebræis, & Eusebio servitutum annos comprehendentes sub annis regiminis seu principatuum: quo pacto Eusebius per errorem prætermittens Elonisedecennalem judicatum numeravit annos 289. ab excessu Josuæ ad obitum Simsonis: alii vero plerique Elonem haud omittentes, annos 299. utpote 40. annos Othnielis (Jud. 3, 11.) 80. Ehudi (c. 3, 30.) Sangari paucos menses, 40. Deboræ (c. 5. v. ult.) 40. Gideonis (c. 8, 28.) 3. Abimelechi (c. 9, 22.) 23. Tholæ (c. 10, 2.) 22. Jair. (c. 10, 3.) 6. Jephthæ (c. 12. 7.) 7. Ebzon (c. 12, 9.) 10. Elonis (c. 12, 11.) 8. Abdonis (c. 12, 14.) 20. Simsonis (c. 15. v. ult.) quam sententiam plerique amplectuntur: nonnulli tamen Ammoniticæ saltem servitutis annos 18. de quibus Judic. 10, 8. seorsim accipiunt, illisque ducentis nonaginta novem annis adjiciunt, unde summa prodit 370. annorum. D. Johannes Behrm. v. sex annos Jephthe connumerandos censet annis illis 18. Ammoniticæ servitutis. Sed rectius anni servitutis Ammoniticæ, (uti cæteri servitutum anni) comprehenduntur annis judicatuum Jairi, de quo ad cap. 10. Judicum dicturi sumus: atque ita apprime sibi constabit numerus ille magnus 1. Reg. 6. Si nempe anni ducenti nonaginta novem cum paucis mensibus numerantur usque ad obitum Simsonis: cui summæ è libro Judicum collectæ, si anni 40. prævii ab egressu ex Ægypto usque ad mortem Josuæ, & 17. regiminis Josuæ addantur, ac porro anni 40. judicatus Eli (1. Sam. 4, 18.) atque iterum 40. regiminis Samuelis, & Saulis (Act. 13, 21.) ut & 40. anni regni Davidici (1. Reg. 2, 11.) & priores 4. regni Salomonici accedant, summa universa inde proditura erit 480. annorum, quod scil. designati sunt ab exitu usque ad initium structuræ templi Salomonici.

Quæ Chronotaxis præ aliis antea commemoratis expeditissima videtur: cui vero id imprimis à Cano, Codomanno, Petavio, & aliis obvertitur, quod anni servitutis confundendi non sint cum annis judicatuum, siquidem absurdum sit, terram eodem tempore & quievisse, & bello infestatam fuisse; Ad quam difficultatem B. D. Behmius respondet: potuisse etiam tempore servitutis Israëlitarum inter Israëlitas & pressores pacem fuisse, siquidem anni servituti, non vero belli dicantur. Quo pacto citra ἀντικείμενον ἐν προσκειμένῳ, quo eam sententiam urget Codomannus, includentur annis 40. Othonielis octo anni servitutis Israëliticæ Mesopotamicæ (Judic. 3. v. 8.) annis 80. judicatus Ehud comprehendentur anni 18. servitutis Moabiticæ (c. 3, 14.) Sub annis regiminis Deboræ 40. continebuntur itidem anni 20. servitutis Cananiticæ (c. 4, 3.) ac porro añis 40. ducatus Gideonis 7. anni Midianiticæ servitutis includendi erunt (c. 6, 1.) pariterque sub annis 22. præfecturæ Jairi comprehendendi anni 18. servitutis Ammoniticæ (c. 10, 7. 8.) sub Simsonis vero & præcedentium trium Judicum annis (qui conjun- ctim efficiunt 45.) vel quod alii malunt, sequentis judicis Eli prioribus 20. annis concludendi anni 40. servitutis Philistinæ, de quibus Jud. 13, 1. Servi- tus itaque illa non necessario ita accipienda, ut ex- cludatur præfectura Judicum: quam Grotius solum ita intelligit, quod tributarii illis, quibus serviisse dicuntur, facti fuerint Israëlitæ, qualis servitus lo- cum habere potuit, etiamsi suum Israëlitæ habue- rint Judicem, quem Deus pro re nata, cum cla- marunt ad Dominum Israëlitæ pressi, vel aliis etiam servitutum oneribus vexati, ad liberandum popu- lum excitavit, ut opus non sit, statuere, eum tum demum regnare cepisse, cum ad liberationem à spi- ritu Domini excitatus est: quum antea jam potue- rit judicatui præfuisse. De temporibus utique ju- dicatus Deboræ constat e Jud. 4, 3. quod servierint per 20. annos Jabini regi Israëlitæ, etiam ubi judi- catui Debora præfuit: & Simson judicasse dicitur Israelitas per 20. annos temporibus Philistinorum, vel sub pressura eorundem cap. 15, 20. Novam ta- men, nec forte inconvenientem in annis Judicum assignandis nuper iniit rationem Doctissimus Ar- chi-Episcopus Hiberniæ, Jacobus Usserius Ar- machanus in Chronolog. Sacra Oxoniæ Anno 1660. edita, parte altera c. 12. p. 197. qui belli qui- dem, & servitutum tempora à pacis & quietis tem- poribus secernenda esse agnovit, sed annorum no- tatione quieti terræ apposita, quietis illius initium, non autem vel ipsius quietis vel præfecturæ Judi- cum durationem designari statuit, ut ita illud וַתִּשְׁקֹט & quievit, sit, quiescere cepit, uti Gen. 5, 32. c. 11, 26. genuit juxta ipsum est gignere cepit, 1. Reg. 6. vers. 1. ædificavit, est ædificare cepit, & cum Rex aliquis tot vel tot annorum fuisse dicitur, בִּמְלֹכוֹ, id est, cum regnare inciperet. Quum ergo nume- rorum in temporum notatione ea sit ratio, ut in- terdum, quando res aliqua contigerit, indicet, in- terdum, quamdiu ea durarit, in annis oppressorum posteriorem explicitam, in annis vero quietis ter- ræ priorem sic accipiendam censet Usserius, ut sub Othoniele terra Jud. 3. v. 11. non 40. annos quie- visse intelligatur, sed anni 40. effluxerint inde à præcedenti aliqua Epocha, puta à celeberrima terræ quietę, quæ (devictis Cananææ Regibus, qui junctis viribus & totis copiis adversus Israëlitas in- surrexerunt) à Josua constituta, partitioni ter- ræ prævia memoratur Jos. 11, vers. 23. cap. 14, 15. vel quod eodem recidit, anno quadragesimo ab ista quiete Josuana ceperit quies sub Othniele, ut nu- merus Cardinalis ex Ebræorum consuetudine, pro ordinali adhibitus dicatur. Superatis igitur Me- sopotamensibus (qui post illos Cananææ Reges devictos primi alienigenarum UNIVERSÆ TER- RÆ Israëliticæ bellum intulerunt) quies (annis post prioris illius initium 40.) reddi cepta est, vi- ctore deinceps Othoniele, usque ad mortem, Rempubl. administrante, & populum in vero Dei cultu continere satagente, quod præcipuum horum Judicum opus fuit c. 2, 17. 18. 19. Atque hanc nu- merationem per quietis terræ intervalla in priore Historiæ Judicum parte post summatim exposi- tam oppressionum & liberationum seriem Jud. 2. v. 14. ad 19. specialiter appositis notis temporum, sex sequentibus capitibus traditam esse, in poste- riori vero per præfecturæ Judicum spatia calculum institui censet Usserius. Juxta hanc computandi rationem satis concinnam ejusmodi exhibere lice- bit libri Judicum Chronotaxin:

I. A quiete Josuana (Jos. 11, 23.) ad Cusaris op- pressionem anni - - - 32.

Et inde ad liberationem & quietem sub Otho- niele reddi ceptam anni - - 8.

(Hi sunt 40.anni Jud. 3,11. usque ad quietem, quæ sub Othonielis judicatu reddi cœpit: quam antecefsit octennalis prefsura Mesopotamica v. 33. Ad illos ergo annos 40.referendi 10. anni regimi- nis Josuæ, ab illa quiete terræ sub Josua usque ad obi- tum ejus: 8. anni (ut eos ita probabiliter pona- mus) Regiminis seniorum, qui post Josuam supe- rabant (ut ita concilietur sententia celeberrima de 17. annis Principatus Josuæ, cum traditione Jose- phi l. 5. Antiqu. c. 1. de 25. annis dominatus Josuæ, ad- dito nempe octennio gubernationis Seniorum) & 18. anni ἀναρχίας, (quot annos sine Magistratu fuisse Israëlitus Josephus l. 6. Antiqu. c. 6. tradidit) necnon 8. anni Mesopotamiensis servitutis (apud Josep. l. 5. c. 3.) summa prodit 44. annorum. For- te dicere licebit 4. priores annos servitutis inclu- di 18. annis ἀναρχίας, quod quadriennio circiter nullum Principem sui generis habuerint, quodque quarto demum anno datus sit iisdem ex ipsismet aliquis Magistratus, aut etiam præfectus sit Oth- niel Judex manente adhuc per quadriennium ser- vitute, quem deinceps ob gemitus Israelis excita- rit, & spiritu suo induerit Dominus ad liberan- dum Israelem, & per quem reddita terræ sit quies, anno quadragesimo à Josuana quiete, debellato Cufsane, Mesopotamiæ Rege.)

II. Ab illo tempore usque ad servitutem & op- pressionem Moabiticam anni - 62. Oppressionis istius anni - - - 18. (Qui additi efficiunt annos 80. Jud. 3, 30. à quiete terræ reddita sub Othniee usque ad quietem per Ehudem, occiso Eglone Moabitarum Rege terræ restitutam.)

III. Inde ad Jabinis oppressionem (Jud. 4, 3.) anni 20. quæ duravit usque ad liberationem De- boræ per annos - - - - 20. (Hi anni 40. numerantur à quiete terræ per E- hudem restituta ad quietem per Deboram & Barac, interfecto Jabine, terræ redditum Jud. 5, 3.)

IV. Inde ad Midianiticam oppressionem (de qua Jud. 6, 1.) anni - - - 33. Ex quo duravit illa oppressio per annos 7. (Atque hi anni 40.designati sunt c. 8,28.à quiete scil. per Deboram reddita usque ad quietem per Gedeo- nem Midianitis devictis restitutam)

V. Inde ad initium regni Abimelechi filii Ge- deonis - - - - - - 10. Hos decem annos non expressit S. S. sed col- ligi possunt per subductionem ex integra 479. an- norum summa usque ad structuram templi Salo- monei: perindi uti per subductionem 16. vel 17. annos præfecturæ Josuanæ colligunt, qui à morte Josuæ primos quietis annos dinumerant, & in se- quentis Judicis excessu terminant.)

VI. Abimelechi anni fuere (Jud. 9, 22.) - 3.

VII. Thola judicatui præfuit (Jud. 10, 2.) per annos. - - - - - - 23.

IIX. Jair præfuit (c.10, 3.) per annos. - 22. (In quibus includuntur 18. anni oppressionis Philistinorum, & Ammonitarum c. 10. 28.)

IX. Jephte præfuit (c. 12, 7.) annis - 6.

X. Ibsan præfuit judicatui (c. 12, 9.) annis 7.

XI. Elon præfuit (c. 12, 11. annis - 10.

XII. Abdon præfuit (c. 12, 14.) per annos 8.

XIII. Samson præfuit (c. 15,20. c. 16, 21.) per an- nos - - - - - - 20. (Qui judicavit Israëlem in diebus Philistino- rum seu oppressionis eorum, quæ per 40. annos duravit cap. 13, 1.)

Quorum annorum summa,309.anni,intervallum integrum erunt à Josuana quiete, (quam decennio ante Josuæ excessum constitutam censemus) usque ad obitum Simsonis: adeoque ab obitu Josuæ huc usque numerandi erunt anni 299. & menses for- taffis aliquot: Quibus, ut antea monuimus, ad- ditis annis 57. ab exitu ad Josuæ obitum & 123. ab excessu Simsonis ad initium structuræ templi prodit summa 479. annorum, & mensium ali- quot. Usserius tribuit intervallo à quiete per Ge- deonem terræ restituta usque ad initium regni A- bimelechi tantum 9. annos 2. menses, & à transi- tu Jordanis ad finita bella & quietem per Josuam datam 6. annos 4. menses constituit. At Simsonis, Eli, Samuelis & Saulis annos facit 101. quos cum tantum centum assignatos inveniamus, maluimus decem annos numerare à quiete Gideonica ad A- bimelechi tyrannicam regiminis occupationem. Aliter etiam illos Judicum posteriorum & Saulis annos distribuit Usserius (cujus rei rationes, quia opus morte præventus tantum produxit ad Abdo- nis excessum, non reddidit) quam communiter di- stribui solent, præeunte Scriptura: Assignat enim Eli & Samsonis regimini conjuncto 40. annos: Sa- muelis 12, Saulis 40. At Scriptura Samsoni tribuit 20. annos c. 15, 20. 16, 21. Eli 40. 1. Sam. 4, 18. Sa- muelis autem & Saulis regimini itidem 40. Act. 12, 41. Sequutus forte quoad annos Eli & Samsonis Usserius D. Behmium: qui 20. annos Samsonis, ut & 40. Eli includens 40. annis Philistinæ servitutis l. 1. Chronolog. Manuduct. Tit. 3, c. 6. pag. 50. tum Simsonem tum Eli sub Philistina servitute conjun- ctim populum judicasse, ex eo colligit, quod & Simson dicatur populum Domini judicasse Phili- stinorum temporibus, Jud. 15, 20. & Eli adhuc tem- poribus, ac post mortem etiam ejus, ad tempora usque Samuelis Philistini Judæis superiores fuerint 1. Sam. 5, 6. 7. Nihil absurdi putans, si dicatur, Domi- ni populum in sui liberatione unum & alterum judi- cem conjunctim sibi elegisse, quorum anni in libro Ju- dicum divisi numerantur, sed hac hypothesi admis- sa nulla erit certitudo de annis judicum, an divisim numerentur, qui conjunctim imperarunt, nec ne? Etsi autem sub Samsonis judicatu, ut & sub priori- bus annis Eli comprehendi annos 40. Philistinæ servitutis faciles admittamus, non tamen illi 40. anni exhauriunt omnes tum Simsonis tum etiam Eli regiminis annos, utpote qui conjunctim 60. annos efficiunt. Neque inde colligere licet, per totum regimen Eli durasse servitutem & pressu- ram Philistinorum, quod hi post fata Eli prævalue- rint, siquidem potuerint denuo in posterioribus 20. annis regiminis Eli Philistæi superiores evasisse Israelitis, quos deinde etiam capta arca Domini devicere, quod nuncium causa erat casus & obitus Eli.

Huic Chronotaxi libri Judicum favere vi- dentur non obscura documenta: utpote quod di- stincta plane phrasi utatur S. S. in priori parte hi- storiæ Judicum usque ad regnum Abimelechi: Nam de Abimelecho, Regnavit itaque, inquit, A- bimelech super Israël tribus annis Jud. 9, 21. de Thola cap. 10, 2. Judicavitque Israel 23. annis mortuusque est ac sepultus in Samir. De Jair. v. 23. Judicavit Isra- elem per viginti & duos annos, v. 5. Mortuusque est Jair &c. De Jephte c. 12, 6. Judicavit itaque Jephthe Galaadites Israëlem 6. annis & mortuus est, ac sepul- tus in civitate sua Galaad, & v. 9. de Absan: Qui se- ptem annis judicavit Israël, mortuusq́; est ac sepultus in Bethlehem. Similiter de Elon c. 12, 11. cui successit Ahjalon Zabulonites & judicavit Israel decem an- nis, mortuusque est ac sepultus in Zabulon: & de Ab- don v. 13 Post hunc judicavit Israel Abdon, v. 14. Ju- dicavit Israel octo annis mortuusque est, ac sepultus in Pharathon. Denique de Samsone cap. 15, 20. judica- vit Israel in diebus Philistiim viginti annis, Quæ uti luculentissime annos singulorum istorum Ducum & Judicum definiunt, ita nullum de iis dubium re- linquunt. At non ita loquitur de prioribus judicibus; nullam facit mentionem annorum judicatus, nul- lam immediatæ aliorum successionis ; omnia ad terræ quietem, cum illa restitui cœpit, reducit, ac non successionem alterius judicis, sed novam præva- ricationem ac servitutem, annosque hujus subjun- git, ac tempus denique quietis iterum restitutæ defi- nit. Ita cap. 3, 11, Quievitque terra quadraginta annis (vel anno quadragesimo) & mortuus est Othoniel, & post victoriam Ehud v. 30. & quievit terra octo- ginta annis. De morte hujus Judicis nihil additur. Similiter post descriptam victoriam, & odem Eu- charisticam Deboræ nihil aliud habetur, nisi quod terra quieverit per 40. annos cap. 5, 32. Post humi- liationem Midiam additur c. 8, 18. quievit terra per 40. annos : ubi tamen subjicitur simul in vulgata, quibus præfuit Gedeon. Sed Ebræus textus reddi po- test, quiescere cœpit terra quadragesimo anno (scil. à su- periori restitutione quietis per Deboram facta) in diebus Gideonus. Quum ergo ubique variet phrasis, nec quicquam de tempore præfecturæ cœptæ, sive desitæ hic tradatur, sed solum de quiete terræ red- dita, in aprico esse videtur, intervalla exhiberi re- stitutæ subinde quietis, non vero regiminis Judi- cum, (2) si tempus gubernationis Judicum desi- gnare voluit S. S. qui factum, quod nullo verbo mentio fiat de Samgari vel curriculo regiminis, vel obitus ? Saltim post Ehud Samgar fuisse dicitur (judex scil.) & servasse etiam Israel c. 3, 31. non au- tem definitur, quamdiu judicarit populum, aut quando mortuus sit. (3) De Ehud dubium videri queat, anne proximo statim anno post mortem Othniel judicare populum cœperit; nihil enim de eo textus habet; imo subjicit potius prævarica- tionem Israelis, quæ fata Othnielis sequuta est, & excitationem Eglon Regis Moab adversus Popu- lum, ac servitutis Moabitice annos c. 3, 12. seqq. Neque post commemoratum Samgar subjungitur, quod statim post obitum ejus (de quo nihil habe- tur, uti diximus) eidem successerit Debora, sed potius, quod addiderint filii Israel facere malum in conspectu Domini, & quod tradiderit eos Dominus in manus Jabin (v. 2.) & quod clamaverint ad Domi- num v. 3. illo que tempore (cum clamaret populus) judicarit populum Debora. Non ergo certum vide- tur, quod statim cœperit judicatus Deboræ post Samgarum, aut etiam post Ehudem. (4.) Neque id luculenter expressum est, quod statim post ex- cessum Deboræ cœperit Gideonus gubernatio. Con- trarium potius videri possit è cap. 6, 1. seqq. quia subjungitur post designationem 40. annorum (quos tribui putant Deboræ judicatui) quod malum fecerint porro Israëlitæ, quod in manus Midianitarum traditi sint ad septennium, & valde humiliati de- mum ad Dominum clamarint, atque dehinc refer- tur excitatio Gideonus : ut appareat eam demum accidisse post annos servitutis Midianiticæ, & conversionem ac preces Israelitici populi ad Do- minum. (5) Etsi in posteriori historiæ Judicum par- te servitutes & pressuræ Israelitarum itidem com- morentur, eædem tamen subjiciuntur guber- nationi Judicum, & ad annos ejusdem reducuntur: secus se res habet in priori parte : utpote in qua revocatur tempus excitationis servatorum ad an- nos pressuræ, non constitutis annis judicatus eo- rum, & ratio habetur non durationis regiminis, sed cœptæ restitutionis quietis. (6.) Congruet ita facile numerus annorum 300. à Simsone designatus à morte Mosis, vel devictione Amorrhæorum us- que ad sua tempora, quia ad Simsonis regimen sic numerabuntur 289. anni à Josuana terræ quiete: quibus additis septem annis pugnæ Josuanæ à mor- te Mosis prodituri sunt 296. anni.

Dubium autem non leve adversus geminam illam supputandi rationem sive priorem Eusebia- nam secundum sola intervalla regiminis judicum, sive hanc posteriorem jam expositam, qua partim intervalla redditæ quietis, partim intervalla tem- poris regiminis respiciuntur, movetur ex Actor. 13. vers. 20. quod Apostolus à distributione terræ per Josuam & Eleazarum facta ad Samuelem Prophe- tam videatur numerare annos 450. Nam si anni Eli 40. adjiciantur hisce annis à Josuana quiete ad obitum Samsonis 309. prodibunt 349. anni. Quo- modo ergo 450. anni numerantur ? Unde ex hoc loco sententiam suam stabiliunt, qui servitutum & judicatuum tempora per omnes Judices in hoc li- bro seorsim numerari volunt, Codomannus, & alii. Et sane ex illa collectione annorum servitutum & judicatuum prodeunt 410. anni, quibus additis 40. annis Judicis Eli, oriuntur anni à morte Josuæ 450. à distributione terræ Josuanæ 460. Nodum hunc quum solvere nescierint, secundum duxere nonnulli, cum in Pauli verbis pro voce τριακοσίγ vocem τετρακοσίγ per errorem nunc legi asserue- re, quibus etiam assensum præbuit D. Behmius: Sed quia religio nobis merito est, puritatem fon- tium in dubium vocare, aut cum Beroaldo lib. 3. Chron. c. 4. Paulo tribuere, quod receptam Judæo- rum sententiam, utut erroneam, sequutus sit in re, quæ non fidei est, sed numerationis, præferenda omnino eorum explicatio, qui initium vel termi- num à quo non in terræ distributione hic figi volunt annorum 450. sed in tempore nativitatis Isaac; terminum vero ad quem non Samuelis regimen, sed terræ distributionem, quia à nativitate Isaaci ad ἔξο- δον sunt anni 405. Gen. 15, 13. Exod. 12, 40. inde ve- ro ad distributionem terræ 47. anni intercesse- runt, ut intervallum integrum sit 452. Unde Sanct. Paulus vocem ὡς vel quasi adhibuit: Textus itaque Græcus ita habebit: καὶ μετα ταῦτα ὡς ἔτεσι τετρα- κοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα (γενόμενα) ἔδωκε κριτὰς, & post illa annis 450. (peracta) dedit Judices : cujus- modi participii ellipsis in Christi genealogia Matth. 1. versu 11. constituitur. Quanquam ea el- lipsis opus non sit, secundum antiquum codicem A- lexandrinum, qui in Anglia habetur magnis exara- tus literis teste Armachano l. c. p. 195. qui ita legit: Κατεκληροδότησεν ἀυτοῖς τὴν γῆν ἀυτῶν ὡς ἔτεσι τε- τρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἔδωκε κριτάς: quæ lectio etiam reperitur inter eas diversas lectiones, quas Novo Testamento Parisiis Anno 1568. Græce à se excuso Robertus Stephanus subji- ciendas curavit; consentiente quoque codice quo- dam Græco alio Parisiis item edito, à Beza in an- not. ad h. l. producto, & Novi Collegii apud Oxo- ninenses exemplari MS. altero, ut & Vulgata versio- ne: Sorte distribuit eis terram eorum, quasi post qua- dringentos, & quinquaginta annos: & post hæc dedit Judices. Ideoque anni illi 450. non ad judicum du- rationem, sed ad tempus partitionis terræ referen- di, ut principium supputationis à primis orationis Apostoli verbis vers. 17. pendeat, Deus populi hu- jus Israël elegit Patres nostros, in Isaac scil. vel inde à nato Isaaco. Conferantur quæ ad 1. Reg. 6. vers. 1. Aliena est Grotii supputatio, quasi anni 450. ab exitu ex Ægypto numerentur usque ad il- lud tempus, quo David Jebusæos ejecit. Cum no- stra explicatione consentiunt Beda, Glossa, Hugo, Lyranus, Dionysius, Walterus, Junius, Usserius, Ludovic. de Dieu, Salianus, Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, &c.

Summa annorum libri Judicum juxta vulga- rem computum est 299. h. m.

Anni collecti 299. à Josuæ excessu ad mortem Simsonis.

Sic ergo à quiete per Josuam reddita, decen- nio ante ejusdem mortem, uti juxta nostrum calculum supra, flexere anni 309. ab ingressu in terram promissam 315. anni & menses aliquot: ab egressu a. ex Ægypto 356. anni numerantur usque ad Simsonis mortem.

SEQVITUR PRÆF. GROTIAN.

HEBRÆIS, Tyriis & Carthaginensibus שׁוֹפְטִים dice- bantur κατ' ἐξοχὴν (alioqui enim vox latius patet, ut jam sæ- pe observavimus) summi Magistratus, quos Græci hic κρι- τὰς, Josephus in Tyriorum rebus δικαςὰς vocat. Latini in Pu- nica historia servato Punico vocabulo Suffetes. αὐτοκράτορες, ἡγεμόνες Josepho. Vide de his quæ ad Deut. 17, 9. Adde lo- cum infra 5,13. Videtur autem his temporibus omissa per incuriam creatio Synedrorum LXXII. Quemadmodum & ante Josaphati tempora 2. Paralip. 19, 5. Itaque ubi tales extra ordinem viros Deus non excivit, erat dissolutum Rei- publ. corpus, nec quicquam in commune agebatur. Tribus singulæ suas res suo periculo ac commodo agebant, nisi si quæ ex usu temporum foedus inter se fecerant infra 3. Josephus: συνέβαινεν ἤδη τὴν ἀριςοκρατίαν διεφθάρθαι. καὶ τὰς γερυσί- ας ἐκ ἀπεδείκνυσαν, ϗ' ἀρχὴν ἄλλην ὐδεμίαν τῶν πρότερον νε- νομισμένων : item: μετακινηθέντων τὲ κόσμυ τῆς πολιτείας ὑπ' ἀναρχίας ἐνόσι τὰ πράγματα. Talis fuit Græci status Concilio Achaico Romanorum artibus dissoluto, & Galliæ ante Cæsaris tempora: Germaniæ vero, & Britanniæ multo etiam serius.

De judicibus ita tradiderat Grotius ad Deut. 17. vers. 9. Tales interreges & apud Tyrios fuere eodem nomine שׁפטים quod nomen Josephus acta Tyriorum in Græcum vertens adversus Appio- nem libro priore vertit δικαςάς. Nam post Itho- balum & Baalem reges, sic ait: μετὰ τῦτον δικαςαὶ κατιςάθησαν καὶ ἐδίκασαν ἀυτοὶ, Ἐκνίβαλος Βασ- λάχε μῆνας δύο, χέλβις Ἀβδαίε μῆνας δέκα, Ἄββα- ρος ἀρχιερεὺς μῆνας τρεῖς, μύγγονος καὶ Γεράστρα- τος τῶ Ἀβδηλίμο δικαςαὶ ἔτη ἕξ. Α Tyriis idem no- men veniat ad Carthaginenses Tyriorum traduces, apud quos summi Magistratus dicti suffetes, ut ex Calidio nos docet Festus. Summum magistratum dixi cum Livio, qui & alibi eorum imperium ait fu- isse velut consulare. Suffetes pro שׁופטים est aut ex molliori pronunciatione, qualis erat Ephratæorum Jud. 12, 6. aut corruptum per Latinos Scriptores.

Isti v. apud Hebræos שפטים plane similes erant Romanis interregibus, ac postea dictatoribus, ne- que à regibus Hebræis ulla re differebant, præter quod Satellitium & pompam regiam non habe- bant: ac propterea nec tributa nec vectigalia exi- gebant. Cæterum erant, ut Josephus loquitur, ἡγε- μόνες ἀυτοκράτορες. Itaque & reges vocantur Jud. 9, 6. Constituerunt regem Abimelech, id est, δικαστὴν Jud. 18, 1. mortuo Samsone: In diebus illis non erat Rex in Israel: id est Δικαστής. Ac sicut reges absque Synedrio jus interficiendi habebant, ut docet Thal- mudicus titulus de rege & 2. Sam. 1, 15. & loca alia, sic & isti δικασταὶ, sive interreges, ut apparet exem- plo Gedeonis Jud. 8, 16. 17. & Jephthæ Jud. 12, 6. quæ recte notata Abarbanieli ad initium libri Ju- dicum. Hæc ibi Grotius. Cum quibus conferri poterunt, quæ de judicibus in præloquio diximus. Neque dubium est, majorem dignitatem sibi sum- sisse Abimelechum, quam habebant cæteri judices, adeoque uti Rex vocatus est, ita Regia usurpasse axiomata, vel affectasse saltem.

Quod autem de intermissa creatione LXXII. virorum Synedrii, ac dissoluto Reip. corpore con- jectat Grotius, nulla firma ratione nititur. Quod enim consuluerint Deum, ecquis exercitum ad- versus Cananæos ducere debeat, factum inde est, quod semper, etiam constituto Synedrio, talia ad os Domini suscipere tenebantur. Commendatur utique status Reip. post obitum Josuæ, quoadusque superstites fuere seniores σύγχρονοι Jos. 24, 31. ne- que Synedrium intra breve istud tempus defecisse, vero affine est. Et quid de regimine ac statu, judi- cum tempore, penes Israelitas habendum, antea monuimus. Integris illis tribus seculis dissolutum fuisse Reip. corpus, nisi extra ordinem excitatis ju- dicibus, nec credibile sit, neque ullo indicio soli- de docebitur. Et successisse sibi post Abimele- chum ordine Judices ex historia liquet, usque ad Samsonem. Denique cum quies terræ de tota Israe- litica terra intelligatur, quomodo tam dissolutum Reip. Israeliticæ corpus statui potest? Frustra enim pax aut quies Reipubl. fingitur dissoluto corpore Reipublicæ.

## 1:1 Argument
PART I. ACTS UNDER THE JUDGES. SECT. I. OF THE KIND. CHAPTER I.

Judah with Simeon conquer the cities of the gentiles. Adonibezek captured. Jerusalem is occupied by Judah, Hebron by Othniel. The Canaanites are kept as tributaries.

Verse 1. AFTER THE DEATH OF JOSHUA THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL CONSULTED THE LORD.

This was not done immediately after the death of Joshua, but when the days of mourning were completed, and perhaps many others. Moreover, they consulted the Lord through the high priest, either Eleazar or his son Phinehas, as Josephus wills in book 5, chapter 1, wearing the breastplate, and Urim and Thummim, according to the prescription of the Lord Num. 27, 21. Compare Jud. 18, 5; ch. 20, 18, 23, 27; 1 Sam. 10, 22; ch. 14, 37. But those deeds seem to be before the raising up of Othniel, indeed even before the eight-year oppression under the King of Syria: although all these things are comprehended in the 40 years designated in Jud. 3, 11; namely, how many flowed from the rest of the land restored under the government of Joshua the Prince. Some think that immediately after the departure of Joshua, Othniel began to stand out above the others among the princes of the tribe of Judah, and to have given certain specimens of his future government, to which he was divinely destined, as in the occupation of Kiriath-Sepher, through which he became the son-in-law of Caleb, whose authority was great among the people and among the elders. Josephus in the cited book relates that after the death of Joshua the Israelites lacked a Prince for 18 years: after which, because of the invasion of the King of Mesopotamia, God designated Othniel as prince. Thus, therefore, the people were governed by the princes of the tribes and the men of the Sanhedrin through those 18 years: which the Hebrews also relate in Seder-Olam, but those years of the interregnum will have to be included in the 40 years, concerning which ch. 3, 11, about which we warned above.

WHO SHALL BE THE LEADER OF THE WAR?

They do not seek a leader of the Republic or a judge, but a leader of the war, not one who might preside over the whole army, but one who might undertake a partial war in his own tribe, lest the Israelites, being entirely at rest, the Canaanites resume their spirits and strength; and so that by the example, success, and victory of that leader or tribe, the remaining Israelites might be excited to defeat and expel the Canaanites.

Latin:

PARS I. ACTA SUB JUDI- CIBUS. SECT. I. GENERIS. CAPUT I.

Juda cum Simeone civitates gentilium expu- gnant. Adonibezeck comprehensus. Je- rusalem à Juda, Hebron ab Othoniele oc- cupatur. Cananæi tributarii servati.

Vers. 1. POST MORTEM JOSUÆ CON- SULUERUNT FILII ISRAEL DOMINUM.

NOn immediate post mortem Josuæ id factum, sed expletis luctus diebus, & forte aliis pluribus Consuluerunt autem Dominum per summum Sa cerdotem sive Eleazarum, seu filium ejus Pinehas, ut vult Josephus l. 5. c. 1. rationali, ac Urim & Thumin indutum, juxta præscriptum Domini Num. 27, 21 Conf. Jud. 18, 5. c. 20, 18. 23. 27. 1. Sam. 10, 22. c. 14, 37 Facta vero illa videntur ante Athnielis excitatio nem, imo etiam ante oppressionem octennalem sub Rege Syriæ: licet in annis 40. Jud. 3, 11. designatis hæc omnia comprehendantur; quot nempe efflu xerunt à quiete terræ reddita sub gubernatione Jo suæ Principis. Nonnulli statim post excessum Jo suæ eminere præ aliis in tribu Juda reliquarum principe, cepisse Athnielem, atque specimina quæ- dam edidisse futuræ gubernationis, ad quam divi- nitus destinatus erat, censent, utpote in occupatio- ne Ciriath Sepher, per quam Calebi, cujus magna erat in populo, & inter Seniores autoritas, gener fa- ctus est Josephus l. c. tradit post mortem Josuæ Israëlitas 18. annis caruisse Principe: post quos ob invasionem Regis Mesopotamiæ Deus principem designarit Othonielem. Ita ergo per Principes tri- buum, & viros Synedrii gubernatus per illos 18. annos fuerit populus: quod etiam Ebræi in Seder-Olam tradunt, sed illi anni interregni includendi erunt 40. annis, de quibus c. 3, 11. quo de supra monuimus.

QVIS ERIT DVX BELLI?

Non quærunt Ducem Reip. vel Judicem, sed Ducem belli, non qui toti exercitui præsit, sed qui partiale bellum in sua tribu suscipiat, ne quiescen- tibus prorsus Israëlitis, Cananæi animos & vires resumant; & ut illius Ducis, vel tribus exemplo, successu & victoria reliqui Israëlitæ excitentur ad debellandos, & expellendos Cananæos.

## 1:2
Verse 2. AND THE LORD SAID, JUDAH SHALL ASCEND.

To the tribe of Judah, by the prophecy of the Patriarch Jacob, Gen. 49, the command in the promised land had been assigned; therefore, after they had been introduced into the same by Joshua, and he had met his day, this preeminence was divinely granted to the tribe of Judah, that it should lead the army against the Canaanites, which was also superior among the tribes of Israel in dignity and number; from the same, also by divine constitution, the first judge was given to the people, Othniel; therefore, by Judah here the tribe of Judah is understood, v. 22, which seems to have created Caleb as leader of the war, inasmuch as his fortitude, prudence, and authority were most celebrated.

Latin:

Vers. 2. DIXITQVE DOMINUS, JU- DAS ASCENDET.

Tribui Judæ vaticinio Patriarchæ Jacobi Gen. 49. assignatum erat imperium in terra promissa, ideo postquam in eandem introducti essent, per Jo- suam, Israëlitæ, isque diem suum obiisset, tribui Ju- da hæc ἐξοχὴ divinitus tribuitur, ut ducat exerci- tum adversus Cananæos, quæ etiam potior erat inter tribus Israelis dignitate, & numerositate, ex eadem primus quoque divina constitutione judex datus est populo, Othoniel; per Judam ergo hic tri- bus Juda intelligitur, v. 22. quæ sibi videtur Ducem belli creasse Calebum, utpote cujus fortitudo, pru- dentia, & autoritas erat celebratissima.

## 1:3
Vers. 3. AND JUDAH SAID TO SIMEON HIS BROTHER.

To the tribe of Simeon: They are called brothers for a special reason, because they are not only from the same mother, but Simeon had also received a large part of his possessions in the tribe of Judah, Jos. 19, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET AIT JUDAS SIMEONI FRA- TRI SUO.

Tribui Simeonis: Vocantur fratres peculiari ratione, quia non solum ex eadem matre sunt, sed Simeon magnam etiam partem receperat posses- siones suas in tribu Juda, Jos. 19, 1.

## 1:4
Vers. 4. THE LORD DELIVERED THE CANAANITE AND THE PERIZZITE INTO [THEIR] HANDS. This is an ἐπάνοδος to those things which are narrated in Jos. 15. Therefore it could be translated by the pluperfect. The reason is given why the leadership was given to the tribe of Judah.

Without a solid reason an Epanodos is invented, and the translation is adorned in the pluperfect. For all these things cohere in the text as having been done at that time.

Latin:

Vers. 4. TRADIDIT DOMINUS CANANÆUM ET PHERIZÆVM IN MANVS [EORVM) Est hic ἐπάνο- δο ad ea quæ narrantur Jos. 15. Itaque verti posset per plusquamperfectum. Causa redditur, cur Judæ tribui du- ctus datus sit.

Citra solidam causam fingitur Epanodos, & versio adornatur in plusquamperfecto. Cohærent enim ista omnia in textu, ceu tum gesta.

## 1:5
Vers. 5. ADONIBEZEK.

Lord in Bezek, which had its name from lightning or brightness. A city in the tribe of Judah, not far from Bethlehem, which it had to the East, Jerusalem to the North.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ADONIBEZEK.

Dominus in Bezek, quæ à corruscatione vel fulgore nomen habuit. Urbs in tribu Juda, non procul Bethlehem, quam habebat ob Oriente, Je- rusalem à Septentrione.

## 1:6
Vers. 6. HAVING CUT OFF THE EXTREMITIES OF THE HANDS AND FEET.

In Hebrew, thumbs, as Chald., Lyran., Vatabl., Pagnin., Cajet., B. Luther, Förster, Kircher, the Tigurines translate; even the Vulgate itself rendered the word בהונור thus, Exod. 29, 20, Lev. 8, 23, etc. In which punishment there was, besides the pain, a certain disgrace, because they had been cowardly with their hands and swift with their feet; then a mutilation, so that they could neither wield weapons with their hands nor escape with their feet. He acknowledges the punishment of retaliation. Conf. Exod. 21, verse 24, Eph. 33, v. 1, Hab. 2, v. 8, Wis. 11, verse 7, Matt. 26, v. 52, Luke 6, v. 38, Rev. 13, v. 10. Whence some infer that he did penance, having been led to Jerusalem.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CÆSI SUMMITATIBUS MA- NUUM AC PEDUM.

In Ebr. pollicibus, uti Chald. Lyran. Vatabl. Pagnin. Cajet. B. Lutherus, Försterus, Kircherus, Ti- gurini vertunt, etiam Vulgatus ipse ita vocem בהונור reddidit Exod. 29, 20. Lev. 8, 23. &c. In quo supplicio erat præter dolorem tum opprobri- um quoddam, quod manu ignavi, pedibus fugaces extitissent: tum mutilatio, ut nec arma manu tra- ctare neque pedibus effugere possent. Pœnam ta- lionis agnoscit. Conf. Exod. 21. versu 24. Ef. 33. v. 1. Abac. 2. v. 8. Sap. 11. vers. 7. Matth. 26. v. 52. Luc. 6. v. 38. Ap. 13. v. 10. Unde pœnitentiam egisse, in Je- rusalem ductum, nonnulli colligunt.

## 1:7
Vers. 7. SEVENTY KINGS WITH THE EXTREMITIES OF THEIR HANDS AND FEET AMPUTATED GATHERED [THE SCRAPS OF FOOD] UNDER MY TABLE.

Concerning King Sesostris, Plin. 33, cap. 3. Sesostris, king of Egypt, was so proud that it is reported that in whatever years, by lot, he was accustomed to yoke individual kings from his subject peoples to his chariot, and thus to triumph. Lucan in book 10: Sesostris came to the sunset and the ends of the world, and drove his Pharian chariot over the necks of kings. Tamerlane carried Bajazet, the Emperor of the Turks, when captured, in a cage, and gave him from the fragments of his table what he might eat. Lysimachus fed Telesphorus the Rhodian, mutilated on all sides, when he had cut off his ears and nose, in a cage for a long time like some new and unusual animal, since the deformity of his truncated and mutilated mouth had lost the human face. Seneca narrates this in On Anger, book 3, chapter 17. But let no one wonder at the number of 70 kings; let him see what was said above at Joshua 12.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SEPTVAGINTA REGES AMPVTATIS MA- NVVM AC PEDVM SVMMITATIBVS COLLIGE- BANT SVB MENSA MEA [CIBORVM RELIQVIAS)

De Sesostri Rege Plin. 33. cap. 3. Sesostri Ægypti rege tam superbo, ut prodatur annis quibusque forte reges singulos e sub- sctis jungere ad currum solitus, sicque triumphare. Lucanus libro 10. Venit ad occasum, mundique extrema Sesostris, Et Pharios currus regum cervicibus egit. Bajazetem Turcarum Imperatorem captum Tamerlanus in cavea vexit, deque mensæ suæ fragmentis dedit, quod ederet. Lysimachus Telesphorum Rhodium, undique de curtatum, cum aures illi nasumque abscidisset, in cavea velut animal novum aliquod & inusitatum diu pavit, cum oris detruncati mutilatique deformitas humanam faciem perdidisset. Nar- rat Seneca de Ira l. 3. c. 17. Numerum autem 70. regum ne quis miretur, videat quæ supra dicta ad Jos. 12.

## 1:8
Verse 8. THE CHILDREN OF JUDAH THEREFORE FIGHTING AGAINST JERUSALEM.

Joshua had captured the city in chapter 10, 1. But the Jebusites retained the citadel, and afterwards even recovered the city. Therefore the tribe of Judah besieged it anew, not only because it had a part in it with the tribe of Benjamin, but also because the first expeditions had been divinely enjoined upon them. The citadel was finally taken from the Jebusites in the time of David, 2 Samuel 5, verse 7.

Latin:

Vers. 8. OPPUGNANTES ERGO FILII JUDA JERUSALEM.

Ceperat urbem Josua c. 10, 1. Sed Jebusæi ar- cem retinere, ac postea urbem etiam recupera- runt. Ideo expugnavit eam denuo tribus Juda, non modo quia partem habebat in ea cum tribu Benja- min, sed etiam quia illi primæ expeditiones divi- nitus injunctæ erant. Arx demum Davidis tempo- re Jebusæis ademta 2 Sam. 5. vers. 7.

## 1:10
Verse 10. CARIATH-ARBE.

We have spoken of this at Joshua 10, 3; 14, 7.

Verse same. HE SMOTE ESSAI, AND AHIMAN, AND THOLMAI) He had smitten them under the leadership of Caleb, while Joshua was still alive. Joshua 15, 14. Thus also he had departed immediately.

Thus, therefore, according to Grotius, it seems it must be said that all those things which are recounted here from verse 4 up to verse 15 were already done in the time of Joshua, contrary to what almost all interpreters have thought, who judged that those things which occur here as duplicates of the history of Joshua 20 were handed down there by prolepsis, but have their proper place here.

Latin:

Vers. 10. CARIAT ARBE.

De hac diximus ad Jos. 10, 3. 14, 7.

Vers. eod. PERCVSSIT ESSAI, ET AHIMAM, ET THOLMAI) Percusserat duce Calebo, vivente adhuc Josua. Jos. 15, 14. Sic & statim abierat.

Ita ergo juxta Grotium dicendum videtur, omnia illa, quæ à v. 4. usque adv. 15. hic recensentur, tempore Josuæ jam gesta esse, secus atque censuerunt plerique omnes interpretes, qui ea, quæ hic gemi- na occurrunt historiæ Jos. 20. ibi per πρόληψιν tradita, hic propriam sedem habere judicarunt.

## 1:11
Verse 11. DABIR WHOSE NAME WAS OF OLD CARIATH-SEPHER, THAT IS, THE CITY OF LETTERS.

The interpreter added this explanation of the city's name on his own. We have spoken of that city at Joshua 15, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 11. DABIR CUJUS NOMEN VE- TUS ERAT CARIATH SEPHER, ID EST, CIVITAS LITTERARUM.

Hanc nominis civitatis expositionem de suo adjecit interpres. De urbe illa diximus ad Jos. 15, 13.

## 1:12
Verse 12. HE THAT SHALL SMITE CARIATH-SEPHER, AND SHALL LAY IT WASTE, I WILL GIVE HIM AXA MY DAUGHTER TO WIFE,

These things did not happen rashly or by chance, but by divine direction, so that an opportunity might be given to Othniel, whom God had destined as a judge for the people, to demonstrate his fortitude, and the way might be paved for that dignity: and Caleb undoubtedly hoped well concerning the providence of God, so that neither would such a person be obtained with whom marriage would be illicit, nor would anyone unworthy of such a marriage be obtained: although it also seems that a tacit condition is inherent in such promises, unless such a marriage is against the laws, or an honest reason persuades that one should withdraw from that promise.

Latin:

Vers. 12. QVI PERCUSSERIT CIRIAT- SEPHER, ET VASTAVERIT EAM, DA- BO EI AXAM FILIAM MEAM UXOREM,

Non hæc temere aut fortuito, sed directione divina accidere, ut Othnieli, quem Deus destinarat judicem populo, occasio daretur fortitudinem de- monstrandi, & via sterneretur ad istam dignitatem: & speravit sine dubio bene Calebus de Dei provi- dentia, ut nec talis aliquis obtingeret, cum quo matrimonium illicitum foret, neque quisquam ta- li matrimonio indignus: quamvis etiam videatur talibus sponsionibus tacita inesse conditio, nisi con- tra leges sit ejusmodi conjugium, aut honesta ratio suadeat, ut ab ea sponsione recedatur.

## 1:13
Verse 13. OTHNIEL THE SON OF CENEZ, THE YOUNGER BROTHER OF CALEB.

Who (Cenez) was the younger brother of Caleb: or of Cenez the younger brother of Caleb. For thus the Hebrew text can be rendered here, and below ch. 3, 9. and Jos. 15. v. 13. and so the LXX rendered it in the Roman and Basil. editions in the genitive ἀδελφῦ, as also Pagninus, the Tigurines, &c. Othniel therefore was the grandson of Caleb from his younger brother Cenez. Others say the name of the brother is noted here as a relative. The matter comes to the same thing, that he was a grandson from a brother: Thus therefore Othniel took his cousin as his wife, which was not prohibited by divine law.

Latin:

Vers. 13. OTHONIEL FILIUS CENEZ FRATER CALEB MINOR.

Qui (Cenez) erat frater Caleb minor: vel Cenezi fratris Caleb minoris. Sic enim Ebræus tex- tus reddi potest hic, & infra c. 3, 9. & Jos. 15. v. 13. atque ita reddidere LXX. in Rom. & Basil. edit. in genitivo ἀδελφῦ, ut & Pagninus, Tigurini, &c. Othoniel ergo erat Calebi ex fratre natu minore Cenez nepos. Alii nomen fratris hic cognatum no- tare dicunt. Res eodem recidit, quod ex fratre nepos fuerit: Sic ergo Othniel duxit patruelem suam in uxorem, quod lege divina prohibitum non fuit.

## 1:14
Vers. 14. WHICH AS SHE WAS GOING ON THE WAY HER HUSBAND ADVISED.

That is, when Achsah the bride was being led into the house of the bridegroom, which was accustomed to be done with a great crowd singing, and if the bridegroom's house were further distant from her father's, with mules also, or donkeys, or horses and camels Gen. 24, 64. In the Hebrew it is said in the contrary sense to have urged

Achsah the bridegroom, and not indeed he her. The Vulgate must therefore be corrected here.

WHO WHEN SHE HAD SIGHED SITTING ON THE DONKEY.

Again the Vulgate has departed from the sources, having followed the LXX: for nothing is held concerning those sighs, nothing concerning sitting on a donkey: but rather the contrary: she descended from the donkey. For the verb צנח is she jumped down, she was let down, she slipped down, and transitively she let down, it has a kinship with נזה and נתר she sprang forth, as Avenarius notes in his Lexicon. Forster observes that it signifies actively to strike, to imprint with force, when it governs an accusative after it, as Jud. 4, 2. and that it is taken absolutely outside of government neutrally for to be let down, to slip down. With these Buxtorf agrees along with the remaining Lexicographers, as also Kircher. Nor did the Chaldean, R. David, R. Solomon, the Tigurines, Junius, Vatablus, Pagninus, Cajetan render it otherwise, all of whom Bonfrerius, raving for love of the Vulgate, judges to be raving, vexing the Hebrew word so as to extort the sense of the Vulgate, as if to say, she fixed herself upon the donkey, that is, she fixed herself with grief and cares, that is, she sighed. Behold the follies of the Jesuit! Ludov. de Dieu, deriving the sense of the word from the Ethiopian language, translates, and she waited from above the donkey, which may be seen here. But we have no cause to depart from the consensus of the interpreters, who certainly also knew the Hebrew language, were Hebrews, and were excellently versed in Hebrew literature, and to fetch a meaning from the Ethiopian.

Latin:

Vers. 14. QVAM PERGENTEM IN ITI- NERE MONUIT VIR SUUS.

Id est, cum duceretur Achsa Sponsa in do- mum Sponsi, quod magna turba cantante fieri so- lebat, ac si longius distarent ædes Sponsi à pater- nis, mulis quoque, asinis, vel equis & Camelus Gen. 24, 64. In Ebr. dicitur sensu contrario impulisse

Achsa Sponsum, non vero ipse illam. Emendanda ergo hic Vulgata.

QVAE CVM SVSPIRASSET SEDENS IN ASINO.

Iterum a fontibus discessit Vulgatus LXX. sequutus: nihil enim de suspiriis illis habetur, ni- hil de sessione in asino: sed contrarium potius: de- scendit de asino. Nam verbum צנח est desiliit, demissus est, delapsus est, & transitive demisit, co- gnationem habet cum נזה & נתר prosiliit, notante Avenario in Lex. Forsterus observat tum active significare impingere, imprimere vi, cum post se re- git accusativum, ut Jud. 4, 2. tum absolute extra re- gimen sumi neutraliter pro demitti, delabi. Qui- bus consentit Buxtorfius cum reliquis Lexicogra- phis, ut & Kircherus. Nec aliter reddidere Chal- dæus, R. David, R. Salomo, Tigurini, Junius, Va- tablus, Pagninus, Cajetanus, quos omnes delirare, præ amore Vulgatæ delirans Bonfrerius judicat, Ebræam vocem vexans, ut extorqueat Vulgatæ sensum, q. d. desixit se supra asinum, id est, mœ- rore & curis se confixit, hoc est, suspiravit. En in- eptias Jesuitæ! Ludov. de Dieu e lingua Æthiopica verbi sensum deducens vertit, & expectavit de- super asinum, qui hic videatur. Sed non habe- mus causam a consensu interpp. qui utique etiam linguam Ebræam calluere, Ebræi, & in Ebraica literatura præclare versati, discedendi, & ex Æ- thiopica significatum arcessendi.

## 1:15
Vers. 15.

BECAUSE YOU HAVE GIVEN ME A DRY LAND, GIVE ALSO ONE IRRIGATED BY WATERS.

That daughters could also receive hereditary estates as a dowry up to the year of Jubilee is argued from the Law of Levit. 25. because it was permitted even to sell a field to an outsider is gathered: but especially it seems that this was permitted when they married men of their own tribe and family, because in that way a confusion of inheritances in the tribes did not occur.

CALEB THEREFORE GAVE HER THE UPPER IRRIGATED LAND, AND THE LOWER IRRIGATED LAND.

Aquila here, as Procopius testifies, placed a foreign word, as also the LXX did in Jos. 15, he gave the upper and lower Gollath. Symmachus explained it as a possession in the upper and lower parts. In the Hebrew are held upper and lower springs; fountains in the upper and lower places. Cajetan and others interpret them as fountains bursting forth from the earth (upper) and lower spring-wells. Lyranus, Estius, Saa, as a field in which there were fountains in the upper and lower part; which conform more to the description of a good land in Deut. 8, 7, than Bonfrerius's gloss about one and the same estate irrigated from above by rains, and from below by rivulets and fountains.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

QVIA TERRAM ARENTEM DEDISTI MIHI, DA ET IRRIGUAM AQVIS.

Potuisse etiam filias fundos hæreditarios ac- cipere in dotem usque ad annum Jubilæum ar- gumento Legis Levit. 25. quod licuerit etiam agrum externo vendere colligitur: sed imprimis id licitum fuisse videtur, cum suæ tribus & familiæ viris nuberent, quia ita non fiebat hæreditatum in tribubus confusio.

DEDIT ERGO EI CALEB IRRI- GUUM SUPERIUS, ET IRRIGUUM IN- FERIUS.

Aquila hic, teste Procopio, vocem barba- ram, ut & LXX. Jos. 15. posuere, dedit Gollath su- periorem & inferiorem. Symmachus exposuit pos- sessionem in superioribus & inferioribus. In Ebr. ha- bentur scaturigines superiores & inferiores; fontes in locis superioribus & inferioribus. Cajetanus & alii, fontes prorumpentes e terra (superius) & pu- teos scaturigines inferiores interpretantur. Lyra- nus, Estius, Saa, agrum in quo erant fontes in parte superiore & inferiore; quæ descriptioni ter- ræ bonæ Deut. 8, 7. magis conveniunt, quam Bon- frerii glossa de uno eodem fundo pluviis superne, ri- vulis & fontibus inferne irriguo.

## 1:16
Vers. 16. BUT THE SONS OF THE KENITE) ושלש & here the Chaldean as in Gen. 15, 19. & elsewhere.

KINSMEN OF MOSES) In the Hebrew: Of the father-in-law of Moses, that is, those Kenites who were present with Jethro below 4, 11. for otherwise this nation was among the condemned.

THEY WENT UP FROM THE CITY OF PALMS) From the territory of Jericho, which the Kenites held until the building of the Temple by King Solomon.

This was singular: because at the invitation of Moses they followed the camps of the Hebrews, who had promised them what was best in the promised land Num. 10, 32. The city of palms is Jericho, abounding in palms and palm groves just as in balsam and an abundance of all things: where the earlier harvest is nearly two weeks earlier on account of the remarkable heat than at Jerusalem, as witnessed by

Nic. Christ. Radzivil Epist. 2. Hierof. peregrin. page 106. Having therefore left so pleasant and fertile a place, the sons of the Kenite chose the desert of Judah, not from a desire for the monastic and anchoritic life, as Serarius, Salianus, and Cornelius foolishly imagine, but from a desire to dwell with Judah, to whom the promise concerning Shiloh was made, Gen. 49:10, just as Moses chose the reproach of Christ rather than the treasures of Egypt, Heb. 10. R. David, praised by Drusius in this place, has it thus: when the sons of Judah were taking Hebron, the Kenites were dwelling with the Canaanites in Hebron in a neighboring city, which is called the city of palms, and when the sons of Judah had taken Hebron, they went up from there in peace and dwelt or settled in the desert of Judah with the sons of Judah. Verse of the same. AND DWELT WITH HIM) The Hebrew text: with the people, namely, of the Israelites. Thus we see that at that time a portion was given to proselytes no less than to citizens. In Heb. And he went, and dwelt with the people; which therefore is to be referred to the Kenite: because the Kenite, who is believed to be Jethro, had once departed from his own country, and had dwelt with the Israelite people: Therefore, a plot of land in the lot of Judah is given to his sons as compensation.

Latin:

Vers. 16. FILII AVTEM CINÆI) ושלש & hic Chal- dæus ut Genes. 15, 19. & alibi.

COGNATI MOSI) In Hebræo: Soceri Mosi, id est, illi Kinæi, qui Jethroni aderant infra 4, 11. nam alioqui gens hæc inter damnatas.

ASCENDERUNT DE CIVITATE PALMARVM) Hierichuntino agro, quem Cinæi tenuere usque ad ædifica- tionem Templi R. Salomo.

Singulare hoc erat: quia ad invitationem Mosis sequuti sunt castra Ebræorum, qui promise- rat eis, quod in terra promissa optimum erat Num. 10, 32. Civitas palmarum est Jericho palmis ac pal- metis æque ac balsamo omniumque rerum copia abundans: ubi ad duas fere septimanas messis prior ob calorem insignem, quam Hierosolymis teste

Nic. Christ. Radzivil Epist. 2. Hierof. peregrin. pag. 106. Relicto ergo adeo amœno & fertili loco defertum Juda elegerunt filii Cinæi, non desiderio monasticæ, atque anachoreticæ vitæ, uti ineptiunt Serarius, Salianus, Cornelius, sed desiderio cohabi- tandi cum Juda, cui tribui promissio facta de Schi- lo Gen. 49, 10. quemadmodum Moses elegit op- probrium Christi præ thesauris regis Ægypti Ebr. 10. R. David laudante Drusio in h. l. ita habet: cum filii Juda caperent Hebronem, habitabant Cenei cum Chananæis in Hebron in civitate vicina, quæ vocatur civitas palmarum, & cum cepissent filii Juda Hebro- nem, ascenderunt inde in pace & habitarunt aut con- sederunt in deserto Judæ cum filiis Juda. Vers. eod. ET HABITAVERUNT CVM EO) He- bræus textus: cum populo, Israelitarum scil. Ita videmus eo tempore proselytis fortem datam non minus quam civibus. In Ebr. Et ivit, & habitavit cum populo; quod proinde ad Cinæum referendum est: quia Cinæus, qui Jethro creditur, profectus quondam erat de patria sua, & habitaverat cum populo Israelitico: Ideo filiis ejus in compensationem datur fundus in sorte Juda.

## 1:18
Verse 18. AND JUDAH TOOK GAZA. After the tribe of Judah had finished the war with the Canaanites in the eastern region, he now attacks three satrapies in the western and maritime region, Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron, and defeats the Philistines. In the LXX version, Roman edition, it is held: that Judah did not possess Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron, which the Catholic interpreters themselves rightly criticize, although Bonfrerius wishes that he indeed took them, but did not possess them. But one should not have departed from the Sacred text, in which it is said that Judah took those satrapies, but nothing is held concerning possession: nor is there any mention of Ashdod, which in that version is likewise added to the others.

Latin:

Vers. 18. CEPITQVE JUDAS GAZAM. Postquam in Orientali plaga tribus Juda cum Cananæis bellum confecisset, jam tres Satrapias in Occidentali & maritima regione, Gazam, A- scalonem, Accaron aggreditur, & Philistæos debel- lat. In versione LXX. edit. Rom. habetur: quod non possederit Juda Gazam, Ascalonem, Accaron, quam merito castigant ipsimet Pontificii Interpp. quamvis Bonfrerius velit, cepisse quidem eas, non autem possedisse. Sed non discedendum erat à textu Sacro, in quo cepisse dicitur Satrapias illas Juda, de possessione vero nihil habetur: neque Azoti mentio sit, quæ in illa versione itidem reli- quis additur.

## 1:19
Verse 19. HE COULD NOT DRIVE OUT THE INHABITANTS OF THE VALLEY) In Hebrew, not to drive out the inhabitants of the valley. Here begins to open the source of great evils thereafter, sloth or mercy against God's law. The tribe of Judah is still to be excused: because it is said that the will was not lacking to it, but the ability: because it was not able to drive them out, because they abounded in iron chariots, which, armed with scythes, mowed down those in their way and everything in their path, Josh. 17:16. Concerning the form of the scythed chariots used in wars, see Xenophon, book 6, Cyropaedia; Q. Curtius, book 4; Frontinus, book 2, ch. 3; Dempster in Rosinus, p. 1647. For although it was forbidden to make treaties with the Canaanites, yet it was not forbidden to abstain for a time from such powerful enemies, and not unsuccessfully to harass them. The case of the remaining tribes is different, which, whether because of untimely mercy or rather because of sloth, did not want to drive out the Canaanites.

Latin:

Vers. 19. NON POTUIT DELERE HABITATIONES VALLIS) In Hebr. non ad expellendum habitatores vallis. Incipit hîc aperiri fons magnorum deinceps malorum, desi- dia aut misericordia contra Dei legem. Excusanda adhuc tribus Juda: quia non de- fuisse ipsi dicitur voluntas, sed facultas: quod non valuerit eos expellere, quia falcatis curribus abun- dabant, qui falcibus armati obvios, & obvia quæ- que demetebant Jos. 17, 16. De forma autem Cur- ruum falcatorum in bellis usitatorum vid. Xenoph. 1. 6. παιδ. Κύρ. Q. Curt. l. 4. Frontinus l. 2. c. 3. Dem- psterus in Rosin. p. 1647. Etsi enim prohibitum erat, ne fœdera facerent cum Chananæis, tamen prohibitum non erat, ut ad tempus à tam poten- tibus hostibus abstinerent, nec infeliciter eos la- cesserent. Alia ratio est reliquarum tribuum, quæ sive ob intempestivam misericordiam, sive ob de- sidiam potius noluerunt Cananæos expellere.

## 1:20
Verse 20. HEBRON) See what was said at Josh. 15:13.

Latin:

Vers. 20. HEBRON) Vide quæ dicta Jos. 15, 13.

## 1:21
Verse 21. AND THE JEBUSITE DWELT WITH THE SONS OF BENJAMIN IN JERUSALEM. When the Jebusites possessed the Citadel as the sons of Judah were withdrawing, the Benjaminites also permitted them to dwell with them in the city itself: that was not to be endured, that the nations should dwell with the Israelites, whom they ought to have destroyed entirely.

Latin:

Vers. 21. HABITAVITQVE JEBUSÆUS CUM FILIIS BENJAMIN IN JERUSALEM. Quum Arcem Jebusæi possiderent recedenti- bus filiis Juda, Benjaminítæ etiam permittebant eosdem in ipsa urbe secum habitare: id ferendum non erat, ut gentes Israelitis cohabitarent, quas delere omnino debuissent.

## 1:22
Verse 22. THE HOUSE OF JOSEPH ALSO WENT UP TO BETHEL. Understand the tribe of Ephraim. That Bethel was called Luz before, Josh. 18:13. Therefore, two cities of this name are not to be imagined with Adrichomius. Bethel was situated on the border of the tribe of Ephraim and Benjamin, whence it happens that it is assigned now to one tribe, now to the other.

Latin:

Vers. 22. DOMUS QVOQVE JOSEPH ASCENDIT IN BETHEL. Tribum Ephraim intellige. Bethel illa dicta antea Luza Jos. 18, 13. Non ergo duæ civitates hujus nominis fingendæ cum Adrichomio. Sita fuit Be- thel in confinio tribus Ephraim, & Benjamin, unde sit, ut modo huic, modo alteri tribui assignetur.

## 1:23
Verse 23. WHEN THEY WERE BESIEGING THE CITY. More correctly, when they were scouting the city. That they might observe from every side the situation and nature of the place, how the city could be more easily taken. Verse 42. AND THEY SAID TO HIM: SHOW US THE ENTRANCE TO THE CITY, AND WE WILL SHOW THEE MERCY) And the Israelites were able to use the work of this man rightly, and the man himself sinned in nothing, if he knew God's decree concerning those peoples. See Joshua 2:1 and below 4:17. They ask that it be shown to them by what part they might be able to penetrate into the city more easily. They receive that they themselves will show mercy, and they kept the faith given to him deservedly, whether he handed over the city out of faith (like Rahab) or out of fear of death: For although God ordered the Canaanites to be killed, it was not forbidden to spare their lives if they were converted to the worship of God or were willing to withdraw outside of Canaan; just as he withdrew here with his whole kindred.

Latin:

Vers. 23. CUM OBSIDERENT URBEM. Rectius cum explorarent urbem. Undiquaque observarent situm & naturam loci, quomodo fa- cilius capi posset urbs. Vers. 42. DIXERVNTQVE AD EVM: OSTENDE NOBIS INTROITVM CIVITATIS, ET FACIEMVS TIBI MISERICORDIAM) Et Israelitæ hujus hominis opera recte uti potuerunt, & ipse homo nihil peccavit, si no- tum habuit Dei de illis populis decretum. Vid. Josue 2, 1. & infra 4, 17. Ostendi sibi postulant, qua parte in urbem facilius penetrare possint. Recipiunt se ipsi mise- ricordiam exhibituros, eique fidem datam serva- runt merito, sive ex fide (ut Rahab) tradiderit ur- bem, sive ex metu mortis: Quamvis enim jusserit Deus Chananæos occidi, non tamen prohibitum erat vitam condonare, si ad cultum Dei converte- rentur, aut extra Chananæam secedere vellent; quem- admodum hic cum tota cognatione secessit.

## 1:26
Verse 26. HE WENT INTO THE LAND OF THE HITTITES. It is not Cyprus, as Procopius thinks from Is. 23:1. For here it is written with Chet, not with Caph. But what place it is, is not certain. It seems to have been a land neighboring Canaan, either Syria or neighboring Arabia, in which was the city of Assa, according to Josephus, book 14, ch. 2.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ABIIT IN TERRAM HETTIM. Non est Cyprus, uti Procopius putat ex Es. 23. v. 1. Hic enim per Chet scribitur, non per Caph. Quis autem locus sit, non constat. Videtur terræ Chananææ vicina fuisse sive Syria, sive Arabia vici- na, in qua civitas Ἄσσα apud Joseph. l. 14. c. 2.

## 1:28
Verse 28. HE MADE THEM TRIBUTARIES) Not converted from idolatry, and after the first warning spurned by them, neither of which was permitted. That was done against divine commands. They ought not to have made the Canaanites subject to tribute for themselves, but to kill them.

Latin:

Vers. 28. FECIT EOS TRIBVTARIOS) Non conver- sos ab idololatria, & post primam denuntiationem ab ipsis spretam, quorum neutrum licuit. Factum id contra mandata divina. Non ve- ctigales debebant sibi Chananæos facere, sed inter- ficere.

## 1:31
Verse 31. ACCHO. Afterward called Ptolemais, as witnessed by Procopius and Jerome in the Hebrew place, a maritime city. Otherwise, the same name was of a mountain near Ptolemais.

Latin:

Vers. 31. ACCHO. Dicta deinde Ptolemais, teste Procopio & Hier. in loc. Ebr. urbs maritima. Alias idem no- men montis fuit juxta Ptolemaidem.

## 1:34
Verse 34. AND THE AMORITE PRESSED THE SONS OF DAN. The tribe of Dan was treated very badly: for others either destroyed the Canaanites or made them tributaries: but this one was severely afflicted by the Amorites, whence it was later forced to seek other seats, Josh. 19, Jud. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 34. ARCTAVITQVE AMOR- RHÆUS FILIOS DAN. Pessime habita fuit tribus Dan: nam aliæ aut deleverunt Chananæos aut vectigales fecerunt: hæc autem ab Amorrhæis graviter afflicta fuit, un- de postea alias sedes quærere coacta Jos. 19. Jud. 18.

## 1:35
V. 35. IN MOUNT HARES, WHICH IS INTERPRETED AS TESTACEOUS. The Vulgate added this interpretation of its own: which others read worse as testimony. Cajetan prefers to interpret Mount Hares as Mount of the Sun. The word sometimes denotes scabies. Those who adhere to the Vulgate wish it to be called a mountain thus, because many fragments of potsherds had been heaped upon it. The LXX in the Royal edition add: where bears and foxes are. But these are absent from the sources: where proper names occur. In Ajalon, the valley of which is mentioned in Jos. 10, 12. SALEBIM, which city occurs in 1 Kings 4, 9. Jos. 9, 42.

Latin:

V. 35. IN MONTE HARES, QVOD IN- TERPRETATUR TESTACEO. Hoc interpretamentum de suo adjecit Vulga- tus: quod pejus alii legunt testatio. Cajetanus ma- vult montem Hares interpretari montem Solis. Notat vox quandoque scabiem. Ita dictum montem vo- lunt, qui Vulgatæ inhærent, quod multa in eum va- forum fragmenta aggesta fuerint. LXX. in Regia edit. addunt: ubi ursæ & vulpes. Sed hæc à fonti- bus absunt: ubi propria occurrunt nomina. In A- jalon, cujus vallis mentio fit Jos. 10, 12. SALEBIM quæ urbs occurrit 1. Reg. 4, 9. Jos. 9, 42.

## 1:36
Vers. 36. THE BORDER OF THE AMORITE FROM THE ASCENT OF THE SCORPION. The LXX take Akrabbim as the proper name of a place. R. David Kimchi, Procopius, Dionysius the Carthusian, Lyranus, Abulensis, Masius, Pagninus, the Tigurines, Mercetus, Serarius, Montanus, Torniellus, B. Luther, Forster in his Dictionary, Ortelius, and Bonfrerius on Num. 34, verse 4, says he knows of no one who disagrees, except for Eugubinus alone, unless it be that Oleaster is doubtful, and wishes it to be a city built in a high place, which received its name from the scorpions that were plentiful there, and was called Acrabatena. 1 Macc. 3, 3. Josephus, book 12, Antiquities, ch. 2. Situated indeed in Idumaea, but reckoned to Judea, in the borders of which it was. Pliny, book 5, ch. 14. Josephus, book 3, War, ch. 2.

ROCK AND THE HIGHER PLACES.

Bonfrerius acknowledges here that the Hebrew text is clearer, which the LXX, Pagninus, the Tigurines, and Cajetan translated as Rock and above. Furthermore, the word סלע which denotes a Rock, was a city in the mountains and at the extreme borders of Canaan to the South, according to Josephus, book 3, Antiquities, chapter 2, who says it was of the Amalekites, and Jerome in 'Locis Hebraicis', who calls it of the Idumeans. For the Amalekites, being sprung from the same Esau, can be considered Edomites, and it was in the border of Idumea. Compare Isaiah 42:11, where there is another Petra: when 'AND ABOVE' is added, it is implied that the Amorites not only reached the city of Selah, or even sometimes inhabited that city, but also extended their habitation further toward the summits of those southern mountains.

Latin:

Vers. 36. TERMINUS AMORRHÆI AB ASCENSU SCORPIONIS. Akrabbim pro nomine proprio loci habent LXX. R. David Kimchi, Procopius, Dionys. Carthsi- sianus, Lyranus, Abulensis, Masius, Pagninus, Tigurini, Mercetus, Serarius, Montanus, Tor- niellus, B. Lutherus, Forsterus in Diction. Ortelius, nec ullum se scire, qui repugnet, ait Bonfrerius ad Num. 34. vers. 4. præter unicum Eugubinum, nisi quod Oleaster dubitet, urbemque esse vult in edito loco ædificatam, quæ à Scorpionibus nomen acce- perit ibi copiosis, & Acrabatena dicta sit. 1. Macc. 3, 3. Joseph. l. 12. Antiq. c. 2. In Idumæa quidem sita, sed Judææ accensita, in cujus finibus erat. Plin. l. 5. c. 14. Joseph. l. 3. Bell. c. 2.

PETRA ET SUPERIORA LOCA.

Ebræum textum clariorem esse agnoscit hic Bonfrerius, quem LXX. Pagninus, Tigurini, Caje- tanus verterunt Petra & supra. Cæterum vox סלע quæ Petram notat, urbs in montibus erat & extre- mis finibus Cananææ ad Austrum apud Jose- phum lib. 3. Antiq. cap. 2. qui eam Amalecitarum,& Hier. in Loc. Hebraic. qui Idumæorum dicit. Pos- sunt enim Amalecitæ ab eodem Esau oriundi Edo- mei censeri, eratque in Idumææ confinio. Conf. Es. 42, 11. ubi alia Petra: cum additur ET SU- PRA, innuitur Amorrhæos non solum ad urbem Selah pertigisse, aut urbem etiam istam interdum incoluisse, sed etiam ulterius versus montium isto- rum australium culmina habitationem suam pro- duxisse.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II. Disobedience rebuked by the Angel to the People, and their repentance.

Verse. AND THE ANGEL ASCENDED FROM GILGAL) The added place causes the Hebrews to understand that some man is designated here by the name of Angel, whom they think to have been Phinehas, whose mention is below 20:8. Thus the Prophet is called an Angel, Haggai 1:13, and the Priest in Malachi 2:8, where see what we shall say. Moreover, there is in this chapter a very clear summary of the following history: which shows the utility of royal power to the people by the things themselves, and thus imposes a bridle on defections.

We do not deny that the Prophet is called an Angel, Haggai 1:13, and the Priest, Malachi 2:8. But that either Phinehas the Priest or some prophet is understood here, appears by no document. For the fact that he is said to have ascended from Gilgal proves nothing. The Angel could have had his work there too; and are not the angels who appeared to Abraham in Mamre said to have departed from there and proceeded to Sodom, Genesis 18:22? Furthermore, the discourse itself teaches that it was not some ministering person, but the uncreated Angel. For he claims for himself the leading of the people out of Egypt, and the introduction into the Land of Canaan, and the sanctioning of the covenant with the people, as God. And lest it be said that he does this in the name of God, that solemn phrase is not added here, 'thus said the Lord,' as in Haggai 1:13. Haggai speaks of the Angel of the Lord: 'I am with you, says the Lord.' Nor is anything detected here which teaches that this Angel spoke not in his own name, but in another's. Therefore, that Angel is to be understood who had promised the land of Canaan to the Fathers, Exodus 3. He who had led them out of Egypt, Exodus 14. He who had gone before them, to introduce them into the land of Canaan, Exodus 23:20. 'I led you out,' he says, 'from Egypt, and brought you into the land for which I swore to your Fathers.' Which Angel is none other than the Son of God himself. Concerning which places, see above in the Annotations on Exodus. One may also compare concerning them the dissertation of D. D. Dorfcheus on the name Jehovah, no. 26, p. 35. He who had made a pact with the same, and whose voice they ought to have heard religiously. He who had the 'autokratoriken' (sovereign) power of destroying enemies, who did not destroy them all as a punishment. 'I promised,' he says, 'that I would not make my covenant with you void forever, only so that you would not strike a covenant with the inhabitants of this Land, but would overthrow their altars, and you would not hear my voice; why have you done this?' Which again are not of a created angel: but they fit the Son of God perfectly; for they ought to have heard his voice, Ex. 23:21. 'Wherefore,' continues that Angel, 'I would not destroy them from before your face, that you may have enemies, and their Gods may be for your ruin.' That these are not the words of a minister, but of God, anyone sees, and it is most manifest from verses 20 and 21. Therefore, the Angel of the Lord is to be understood, namely the Son of God, who has the power of destroying enemies, indeed is one with God the Father, John 10:30. To this Lord also the people offered sacrifices there in Bochim, verse 5. Finally, it is proper to him to seek the lost sheep, and to call sinners to repentance, Matthew 9:13, Luke 15:2, etc. Which was done here. Bonfrerius the Jesuit, when he weighed most of these things, thought the Rabbis were to be laughed at because they want Phinehas to be this Angel, because it does not fit

such a discourse of a Prophet. But he offers himself no less to be laughed at by understanding it as Michael the created Angel. For do those things fall upon Michael: 'I led you out of Egypt, and brought you into the Land for which I swore to your Fathers,' and what follows thereafter? For God everywhere attributes this to himself alone—these are the words of Bonfrerius on this place—in Scripture, that he led them out of Egypt and brought them into the promised Land, but much more that oath made to the Patriarchs is to be ascribed to God alone, not to Angels. Moreover, that a created angel speaks in the person of God in this way, could not be taught by any example from the Scriptures thus far. It remains, therefore, that it be admitted that the uncreated Angel is speaking here. Nor does that departure from Gilgal stand in the way of this explanation concerning the Son of God: indeed, it rather strengthens it: for thus the apparition and the promise made there, shortly after the crossing of the Jordan, Joshua 5, is recalled to the memory of the Israelites, with the renewal of the covenant instituted there by circumcision, and it is taught not obscurely that this was the same Angel who, appearing to Joshua, said that he was the Prince of the Host of the Lord, which Bonfrerius also acknowledged here after Theodoret and Serarius. That he was the Son of God, we showed there. Both the Weimar Paraphrasts of the German Bibles and the authors of the Notes to the Belgian translation subscribe to this opinion, who acknowledge that it is clearly evident that the Son of God, not a created angel, is designated here. Which is to be noted on account of Calvin and most others in his School. For they are accustomed to take and interpret such apparitions as concerning another rather than the Son of God.

verse same. TO THE PLACE OF WEEPERS.

In Bochim. For it is a proper name, even if imposed from the weeping instituted there, verse 5. Josephus, book 7, ch. 4, wants it to have been a place near Jerusalem, a forest in which David hid, 2 Sam. 5:22, where the apparition was made, because that place was in the vicinity and view of Jerusalem, where the temple was eventually to be built. But these things were not done while Joshua was still living, as Abulensis, Torniellus, and Salianus thought: because in his time the Hebrews did not publicly worship idols, but served the true God: but after his death, and that of the contemporary elders, a new generation began to worship the idols of the Baalim and Ashtaroth from dealings and conversation with the neighboring nations, the Tyrians and Sidonians, v. 9, 10. Therefore, Procopius, Cajetanus, Serarius, and others teach that these things happened after the death of Joshua.

Latin:

CAPUT II. Inobedientia ab Angelo Populo exprobrata, ejusque pœnitentia.

Vers. ASCENDITQVE ANGELVS DE GALGALIS) Locus additus facit, ut Hebræi hominem aliquem hic Ange- li nomine designari intelligant, quem putant fuisse Phineam, cujus mentio infra 20, 8. Sic Propheta Angelus dicitur Agg. 1, 13. & Sacerdos Malachiæ, 2, 8. ubi quæ dicemus vide. Est autem in hoc capite summa historiæ sequentis valde di- lucida: quæ utilitatem regiæ potestatis populo rebus ipsis ostendit, ac sic defectionibus frænum imponit.

NOn negamus Prophetam Angelum dici Hagg. 1, 13. & Sacerdotem Mal. 2, 8. Sed hic intelli- gi vel Phineam Sacerdotem, vel Prophetam aliquem, nullo apparet documento. Nam quod de Galgalis ascendisse dicitur, nihil probat. Potuit ibi quoque suum habuisse opus Angelus; Et annon Angeli, qui apparuerant Abrahamo in Mamre, inde abiis- se, & Sodomam profecti esse dicuntur Gen. 18, 22, Cæterum oratio ipsa docet, non fuisse personam aliquam ministrantem, sed Angelum increatum. Vindicat enim sibi eductionem populi ex Ægy- pto, & introductionem in Terram Canaan, ac fœ- deris sanctionem cum populo, ut Deus. Ac ne di- catur nomine Dei id facere, non additur hic illud solenne, sic dixit Dominus, uti Hagg. 1, 13. Angelus Domini Haggæus loquitur: Ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus. Nec quicquam hic deprehenditur, quod doceat, nomine non suo, sed alieno locutum esse hunc Angelum. Ille ergo Angelus intelligendus est, qui promiserat Patribus terram Canaan Exod. 3. Ille, qui eduxerat eos ex Ægypto, Exod. 14. Ille qui præiverat ipsis, ut introduceret in terram Canaan Exod. 23, 20. Eduxi vos, inquit de Ægypto, & intro- duxi in terram, pro qua juravi Patribus vestris. Qui Angelus alius non est, quam ipse Filius Dei. De quibus locis supra in Annotatis ad Exodum. Con- ferri etiam poterit de illis Dn. D. Dorfcheus disserta- tionis de nom. Jehovah n. 26. p. 35. Ille, qui pactum fe- cerat cum iisdem, & cujus vocem audire debebant religiose. Ille, qui potestatem habebat αὐτοκρατο- ρικην delendi hostes, qui in pœnam eosdem non o- mnes delevit. Pollicitus sum, inquit, ut non facerem irritum pactum meum vobiscum in sempiternum, ita duntaxat, ut non feriretis fœdus cum habitatoribus Terræ hujus, sed aras eorum subverteretis, & noluistis audire vocem meam, cur hoc fecistis?
