Saulem ex virtutibus vitiisųue mixtum, & in utrisque incon- stantem, qualis Alcibiades. Davidem ex privato Principem, fortem, ingeniosum, bello felicem, victoriis inclytum, gen- tium domitorem, clementem admodum, sed mulierosum, qualis Cæsar Dictator. Scriptor horum librorum quatuor, Hebræorum eruditissimis creditur esse Jeremias. Sermonis forma non discrepat : vide quæ dicemus ad 1. Reg. 6, 2. Eum vero credibile est usum commentariis illis Nathanis & Gadis Prophetarum, quorum mentio 1. Paralip. 29,29. Et sub Jeremiæ nomine citat hos libros Concilium Franco- furtense.

ALii autorem libri I. Samuel. fa- ciunt ipsum Samuelem usque ad cap. 25. continuatorem ve- ro Nathan cum Gade, vel ali- quem e Samuelis discipulis, qui etiam posteriorem librum con- scripserit. Sed de his vix quicquam certi determi- nare licet, nisi quod 1. Paralipp. 29. vers. 29. di- cantur res gestæ Davidis descriptæ in verbis SA- MUELIS videntis, scil. quantum ad initium : quum continuatio eorum ab aliis necessario fa- cta sit. Interpp. in libros Regum a Sixto Se- nensi celebrantur, e veteribus Diodorus Tarsen- sis circa Ann. 360. Eucherius Lugdunensis, & Isidorus Senior Cordubens. Episcopus, anno Domini 430. & circa Ann. 500. Procopius Ga- zæus. Particulas quasdam ex Historia Regum exposuere Hippolytus, Methodius, Theodotins Anastæus, Ambrosius, Augustinus, Gregorius M. & Bernhardus. Laudat & Sixtus Angelomum Mo- nachum, qui lib. 4. Stromatum in libros Regum Anno 830. Et Andream Gallum, qui Postillam Scholasticam in eosdem ante Lyranum scripse- rit. E recentioribus in Libros Samuelis & Re- gum Victorinus Strigelius, Sanctius & Serarius commentati sunt; in Samuelis autem libros se- orsim scripsere Hieronymus Wellerus, ut & Pe- trus Martyr. In libros Regum idem Martyr, & Mendoza, qui etiam ad lib. 1. Sam. quædam edidit. Chronologia libri 1. Samuelis est 40. annorum : quot sc. præfuit Samuel, & Saul, Actor. 13, 20. seqq. Partes tres sunt, 1. Historia Samuelis, usque ad c. 9. 2.Historia Saulis Regis usque ad reprobationem ejus- dem, ad c. 16. 3. Historia ejus reliqua, & de perse- quutionibus Davidis usque ad interitum Saulis, c. 31.

OREM SAMUELIS EBRÆOS, LATINOS REGUM.

aut juxta διχοτομίαν 1. Historia Samuelis, 2. Hi- storia Saulis. Illius describitur primum Nativitas c. 1. & ob eam Hannæ matris hymnus Eucharistico- Propheticus. Porro rudimenta ministerii Samuelis, & impietas filiorum Eli ceu causa rejectionis ipso- rum, & occasio assumtionis Samuelis c. 2. Tertio vocatio Samuelis & prædictio pœnæ Eli, per quam in officio Prophetico Samueli magna conciliatur auctoritas, cap. 3. exhibentur: cum complemento vaticinii, devictis Israelitis, & capta arca Domini, misere pereunte Eli, c. 4. & consequente Dagonis, & Philistinorum percussione, ab arca Domini facta, c. 5. ejusque cum muneribus aureis ad Bethsemitas dimissione, atque horum ob irreverentiam supplicio, c. 6. Quarto traducta arca in Kiriathjearim Sa- muel populum ad resipiscentiam revocat, & abdi- catis idolis pro eodem apud Deum interpellat, ju- dex populi in Mizpa, & vindex adversus Philistinos tonitru miraculoso percussos, & humiliatos, re- gens populum in Ramoth, & visitationes Eccle- siasticas instituens, in pace, c. 7, Quinto cum de- generarent filii Samuelis, Regem postulavit popu- lus, cujus jura ipsi proposuit Samuel c. 8.

Historia Saulis distribuitur in duas Se- ctiones: Prima est Saulis electi & probati. Al- tera rejecti & reprobati. In priori Saulis pri- mum occurrit vocatio cap. 9. tum ejusdem un- ctio, Prophetia, & in Regem confirmatio cap. 10. ac porro res gestæ in regimine ejus describuntur usque ad reprobationem ejusdem: utpote (1.) Victoria adversus Ammonitas, cum subsequa nova confir- matione c. 11. & exhortatione Samuelis, ad timorem & cultum Dei, c. 12. (2.) Victoria adversus Phi- listæos, cum consequente Saulis sacrificio, eidemque ideo denunciata reprobatione, c. 13. (3.) Jonatha- nis victoria adversus Philistinos, quam prosequu- tus Saul fortiter hostes profligavit. (4.) Reliquæ Saulis victoriæ cap. 14. & imprimis adversus A- malecitas, quorum pecudibus & Regi parcens Saul secundo a regno rejicitur, c. 15.

In posteriori Sectione ea, quæ post reprobatum Saulem gesta sunt, exponuntur, utpote 1. Davi- dis electio cap. 16. 2. Goliathi percussio cap. 17. 3. Varia a Saule persecutio, (1.) Tentata 200. præputiorum Philistinorum postulatione cap. 18. (2.) Lanceæ confixione, & cum effugeret Michalis ope, apparitorum emissione cap. 19. (3.) Ac por- ro, quum a Jonathane, prævio sagittarum signo, di- missus in fugam se conjiceret cap. 20. & accepto ab Achimelecho gladio ad Achis Regem Geth, c. 21. & inde in speluncam Odollam se reciperet, ac collecta aliqua manu in Judæam reverteretur, con- tinua Davidis insectatione tum ante fœdus cum Da- vide initum: occisis Achimelecho, aliisque Sacer- dotibus & excisa urbe eorum cap. 22. Destinata Davidis in Kegila captivatione, & in deserto Maon apprehensione cap. 23. nec non in deserto Engedi, ubi fidem Davidis agnovit Saul, & fœdus cum eo percussit, cap. 24. tum etiam post initum istud fœdus: ubi post mortem Samuelis, & ignominiam Davidi a Nabale illatam cap. 25. nova Davidi accidit apud Ziphæos persequutio, sed Saul con- clufus in manus Davidis, quem interfici nolebat, agnovit culpam suam, Davidi securitatem polli- citus, cap. 26. 4. Davidis apud Regem Gathi in Zicklag commoratio, & gentium vicinarum per- cussio cap. 27. 5. Belli Philistini expeditio: in cu- jus descriptione referuntur (1.) Sauli metu per- cusso Pythonissam consulentis denunciatus interi- tus, cap. 28. (2.) Davidis e bello dimissi cap. 29. cum Zicklagi deprædatoribus Amalekitis felix con- flictus, cap. 30. (3.) Saulis devicti miserabilis vitæ exitus cap. 31.

VNAM DE FILIABVS BELIAL) Servus tuus, ancilla tua, sunt verba honoris apud Hebræos ut Gen. 33, 5. c. 42, 10. Ruth. 3, 9. Homines בליעל, id est, sine jugo, ut interpretatur Hieronymus, dicuntur qui vivendi legem nullam habent: ita- que Græci modo vertunt παράνομοι, modo λοιμοί, modo ἄσε- βεις, modo ἄφρονες. Et hoc loco LXX. habent, εἰς θυγατί- ρα λοιμήν: Theodotio, ὡς μίαν τῶν ἀπαιδεύτων.

Vers. 17. DEVS ISRAEL DET TIBI PETITIONEM TVAM) Sacerdotis verba sæpe Deus regit. Vide Johan. 11, 51.

Vers. 18. VVLTVSQVE EJVS NON SVNT AMPLIVS IN DIVERSA MVTATI) Adeo erat plena bonæ spei.

PARS I. LIBRI PRIORIS SA- MUELIS. HISTORIA SAMUELIS.

## 1:4
Vers. 5. AND HE GAVE TO PHENENNA HIS WIFE AND TO ALL HER SONS AND DAUGHTERS PORTIONS] Those who offered peace offerings, the Priest, after deducting his own portions, returned the rest, from which a feast was prepared; the host, however, gave the guests such portions as he wished, as in Gen. 43, 34.

Latin:

Vers. 5. DEDITQVE PHENENNÆ VXORI SUÆ ET CUN- CTIS FILIIS EJUS ET FILIABUS PARTES] Qui offere- bant שלמים, iis Sacerdos, detractis suis partibus, cætera reddebat, de quibus instruebatur convivium, convivator autem convivis dabat partes quas vellet, ut Gen. 43, 34.

## 1:11
CHAPTER I. Samuel born to the barren Hannah, is dedicated to GOD by a vow.

Latin:

CAPUT I. Hannæ sterili natus Samuel, DEO dedicatur ex voto.

## 1:11
Vers. 11. LORD OF HOSTS) In Hebrew it is: יהוה צבאות. But there seems to have been more in other codices: for the LXX translate κύριε ἐλωὲ σαβαώθ, and Chrysostom in 6. to the Ephesians cites Ἀδωναὶ ἐλωῖ σαβαὼθ, where ἀδωναὶ is the received pronunciation of the word יהוה, and κύριε is its interpretation.

It is wrongly gathered from the Greek version and its citation against the purity of the Hebrew source, all of whose codices agree.

I WILL GIVE HIM TO THE LORD) That he may serve in the temple, as we said at Jud. 11, 31. but this vow of the mother began to be valid only when the father approved it Num. 30, 7. below 21, 23.

Therefore it cannot be concluded from there with the Papists, that that son of that age, as Cornelius has it, was destined by a vow. Nor does this vow have anything in common with the superstitious and impious Monastic vows, which rely on no word of GOD.

AND A RAZOR SHALL NOT COME UPON HIS HEAD) We said at Num. 6 that this is not a vow of Nazariteship, but an imitation of something from it. See also Jud. 13.

Latin:

Vers. 11. DOMINE EXERCITUUM] In Hebræo est: יהוה צבאות. At plus videtur fuisse in codicibus aliis: nam LXX. vertunt κύριε ἐλωὲ σαβαώθ, & Chrysosto- mus in 6. ad Ephesios citat. Ἀδωναὶ ἐλωῖ σαβαὼθ, ubi ἀδω- ναὶ est pronuntiatio recepta vocis יהוה, κύριε autem ejus interpretatio.

Male colligitur e versione Græca, ejusque cita- tione adversus puritatem fontis Ebræi, cujus Co- dices omnes consentiunt.

DABO EUM DOMINO] Ut in templo serviat, sicut diximus ad Jud. 11, 31. sed hoc matris votum ratum tum demum esse cœpit, cum id probavit pater Num. 30, 7. infra 21, 23.

Non ergo inde concludi cum Pontificiis potest, quod religiosus illius ævi, ut habet Cornelius, filius ille voto destinatus fuerit. Nec quicquam com- mune habet hoc votum cum superstitiosis & im- piis votis Monasticis, nullo DEI verbo nitentibus.

ET NOVACULA NON ASCENDET SUPER CA- PUT EJVS) Votum non esse Nazaræatus, sed aliquid inde imitari diximus ad Num. 6. vide & Jud. 13.

## 1:13
Ver. 13. AND ONLY HER LIPS WERE MOVING] The Jews command that this be done, because they consider prayer by thought alone to be too cold.

Latin:

Vers. 13. TANTUMQVE LABIA EJUS MOVEBAN- TUR] Ita fieri præcipiunt Judæi, quod precationem solo co- gitatu nimis frigidam arbitrentur.

## 1:16
Ver. 16. AND COUNT THINE HANDMAID AS the sense of a single sentence, just as there is one form of a single thing. For sense is the form of a statement. If, therefore, these things treat of Christ and the propagation of the Gospel, they must not be taken as referring to David and his Kingdom. Furthermore, if we weigh the matter accurately, the literal sense here is of Christ: whose kingdom's amplitude the Prophetess Hannah The subject here is the anointed one, not of Samuel, but of the Lord; and κατ’ ἐξοχὴν (by way of eminence) the anointed one is designated as the Messiah, the Son of God, as in Ps. 2:2, whose kingdom and power is hinted at, extending here to the ends of the earth. For the Lord is said to be about to judge the ends of the earth, and to be about to give to His King dominion, namely, up to the ends of the earth: because through this King He is about to judge, to Whom He gave all judgment, John 5:18, who rules from sea to sea and to the ends of the earth, Ps. 72:8, whose horn is to be exalted, Ps. 99:25. Compare Is. 2:2, Luke 1:69. Thus the ancients explain it with us, Theodoret, Euthymius, and others, and most of our modern Theologians; the Vinarian Paraphrasts, as well as from the Reformed, Conr. Pelican, Marloret, Piscator, Junius, Strigelius, and the Belgian Interpreters with notes added to the new translation: as well as from the Pontificals, Menochius, praised elsewhere by Grotius, and others. Cornelius a Lapide observes that Hannah is the first who expresses the name of the Messiah in the Scriptures, and as it were from afar applauds and gives thanks to Christ who was to be born after thirteen hundred years. Cass. Sanctius the Jesuit says, the Prophetic discourse is fittingly indicated concerning Christ, now King and judge, because he had said that princes had previously been deposed from their royal or near-royal throne, but the poor and just had been exalted. Of these, Christ was the Master and exemplar, the last of men, Is. 53. but exalted, to whom God handed over supreme dominion, for which opinion Sanctius praises the Chaldean, Abulensis, Hugo, Lyranus, Dionysius, and Jansenius.

Latin:

Vers. 16. AC REPUTES ANCILLAM TUAM QUASI unius sententiæ sensum, ut una est unius rei forma. Sensus enim forma est dicti. Si ergo hæc de Christo & propagatione Evangelii agunt, de Davide & Re- gno ejus accipienda non erunt. Porro si rem accu- rate expendimus, Literalis sensus hic de Christo est : cujus regni amplitudinem Hanna Prophetissa hic prædixit. Agitur hic de uncto non Samuelis, sed Domini ; & κατ’ ἐξοχὴν unctus indigitatur Messias Filius Dei, ut Pf. 2, 2. cujus regnum & potentia in- nuitur,usque ad fines terræ hic extenditur. Dicitur enim Dominus terræ fines judicaturus, & daturus Regi suo imperium, scil. usq; ad fines terræ : quia per huncRegem judicaturus est, Cui omne judicium de- dit, Joh. 5, 18. qui a mari ad mare dominatur & ad fi- nes terræ, Ps. 72, 8. cujus cornu exaltandum Ps. 99, 25. Conf. Es.2, 2. Luc. 1, 69. Ita explicant nobiscum veteres, Theodoretus, Euthymius, & alii, & plerique nostrates moderni Theologi ; Paraphrastæ Vina- rienses, nec non è Reformatis Conr. Pelicanus, Mar- loratus, Piscator, Junius,Strigelius,Interpretes Belgi- ci notis translationi novæ adjectis: nec non e Pon- tificiis Menochius , Grotio alias laudatus, & alii. Cornelius a Lapide observat, Hannam primam esse, quæ in Scripturis exprimat nomen Messiæ, & Christo post mille & trecentos annos nascituro eminus quasi applaudere & gratulari. Cass. Sanctius Jesuita, com- mode, inquit, de Christo jam Rege & judice sermo in- dicatur Propheticus, quia prius depositos esse dixerat e regali aut regali proximo folio principes,pauperes vero & justos exaltatos. Horum Magister & exemplar fuit Christus,virorum novissimus Es.53. sed exaltatus, cui Deus summum tradidit imperium, in quam senten- tiam laudat Sanctius Chaldæum, Abulensem, Hugo- nem, Lyranum, Dionysium, Jansenium.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II. The Song of Hannah. The malice of the sons of Eli.

Latin:

CAPUT II. Canticum Hannæ. Filiorum Heli malitia.

## 2:4
Vers. 4. THE BOW OF THE MIGHTY IS OVERCOME) Those things which happen unexpectedly show the providence of God most of all.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ARCVS FORTIVM SVPERATVS EST) Providenti- am Dei ea maxime ostendunt, quæ inopinata eveniunt.

## 2:5
Vers. 5. UNTIL THE BARREN HATH BORNE MANY) In the Hebrew: seven. But the sense is correctly expressed: for that number signifies a multitude. Prov. 24, 16. Ps. 119, 164. Lev. 26, 18.

Latin:

Vers. 5. DONEC STERILIS PEPERIT PLVRIMOS) In Hebræo: septem. Sed sensus recte expressus est: is enim numerus multitudinem significat. Prov. 24, 16. Psal. 119, 164. Lev. 26, 18.

## 2:7
Vers. 7. HE HUMBLETH AND EXALTETH) Hesiod: For easily he makes strong, and easily he afflicts the strong, easily he diminishes the conspicuous, and increases the obscure, and easily he makes straight the crooked and withers the proud, Zeus who thunders on high, who dwells in the highest houses.

Latin:

Vers. 7. HVMILIAT ET SVBLEVAT) Hesiodus: ῥέα μὲν γὰρ βριάει, ῥέα δὲ βριόοντα χαλέπτει ῥεῖα δ̓ ἀρίζηλον μινύθει, κὰι ἀδηλον ἀέξει ῥεῖα δέ τ̓ ἰθύνει σκολιὸν κὰι ἀγήνορα κάρφει Ζεὺς ὑψιβρεμέτης, ὃς ὑπέρτατα δώματα ναίει.

## 2:12
Verse 12. NOW THE SONS OF ELI, SONS OF BELIAL, NOT KNOWING THE LORD] The sons of excellent men have often turned out to be the worst. Besides physical causes, these are the reasons: that those eminent men are carried away with their whole soul toward public affairs, so that they might provide food worthy of a great spirit, and therefore neglect private matters: then that pride accrues to children from paternal honor, and laziness from the easy hope of dignities. It happens sometimes, as in Eli, that goodness, which when it is excessive, deserves to lose its own name and rather be called a dissolution of discipline.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PORRO FILII HELI, FILII BELIAL, NE- SCIENTES DOMINVM ] Virórum Excellentium sæpe filii pessimi exstiterunt. Causæ præter Physicas, hæ sunt : quod viri illi eminentes toto animo ad publica ferantur, ut digna magno animo pabula,privatamque rem ideo negligant : deinde quod liberis ex paterno honore accedat superbia, & pigritia ex spe facili dignitatum. Accedit interdum ut in Heli, bonitas, quæ ubi nimia est, nomen suum amittere, & dissolutio potius disciplinæ vocari meretur.

## 2:13
Verse 13. NOR THE DUTY OF THE PRIESTS) The interpreter connects these with the preceding. Others interpret משפט (mishpat), δικαίωμα (ordinance), as a custom, although a bad one: and refer it to what follows.

Latin:

Vers. 13. NEQVE OFFICIVM SACERDOTVM) Con- nectit hæc interpres cum præcedentibus. Alii משפט δι- καίωμα,interpretantur consuetudinem, quamvis malam: & referunt ad sequentia.

## 3:1 Argument
vers. 1. IN THY SALVATION. In Hebrew: in thy salvation. The LXX render it σωτήριον. Which is the name of Christ, Luke 2, 30. outside of whom there is no solid joy, and who is the foundation of all true joy.

Vers. 1. ON THE APPOINTED DAYS) In the Hebrew: from days to days. In Greek δὲ ἡμερῶν εἰς ἡμέρας. But that is, every year. Others explain the appointed days as the feasts of the Passover, Pentecost, and Tabernacles.

Latin:

vers. 1. IN SALUTARI TUO. IN Ebr. in salute tua. LXX. reddunt σωτήριον. Quod nomen Christi est, Luc. 2, 30. extra quem nullum est solidum gaudium, quique omnis gaudii veri fundamentum est.

Vers. 1. STATVTIS DIEBVS) In Hebræo: diebus in dies. Græ- ce δὲ ἡμερῶν εἰς ἡμέρας. Id autem est, quotannis. ALii dies statutos explicant de festis Paschatos, Pentecostes & tabernaculorum.

## 3:6
Ver 6. HER RIVAL) ἡ ἀντίζηλος in Greek. A tranquil house rarely happens to those who have several wives. Therefore Euripides in Andromache says that twin beds are δίδυμα λέκτρα, strife and hostile griefs.

Latin:

Ver 6. ÆMULA EJUS) ἡ ἀντίζηλος Græce. Raro con- tingit domus tranquilla iis qui plures uxores habent. Itaque δίδυμα λέκτρα Euripedes in Andromacha dicit esse ἔριν δίκαιν, δυσμενεῖς τε λύπας.

## 3:7
Vers. 7. NECDUM SCIEBAT DOMINVM) He did not yet know that the Lord deals with His prophets in a voice so subdued, which for that reason is called קול דממה. Thus Maimonides.

Latin:

Vers. 7. NECDUM SCIEBAT DOMINVM) Non sciebat Dominum cum Prophetis suis agere voce tam sub- missa, quæ ob id קול דממה dicitur. Sic Maimonides.

## 3:8
Vers. 8. FOR THE PILLARS OF THE EARTH ARE THE LORD'S AND HE HATH SET THE WORLD UPON THEM) The earth has its poles, by which it either sustains itself in rest, or, as others wish, balances itself in motion: which the magnet imitates.

BUT TO ANNA HE GAVE ONE PART SAD] For sad in Hebrew is אפים which they interpret as honorable. What if we understand the other cheek? For the Priest had the other.

Grotius seems to waver, whether the earth moves or rests? But that the earth is immovable and rests, against some mathematicians and others, we have proven in Vol. 3, System. Theol. Art 5. c. 2. Quest. 7. p. 1086. et seqq. We have also said some things about that theological judgment repeated against M. Henric. Nicolai, who quite impiously attacked this passage, in the additions to Th. 20. concerning the daily revolution of the Earth; Thus, he says, he calls the earth the pillars of the Earth, upon which he placed the habitable world. That this IS OTHERWISE in accurate consideration is certain. Therefore this man seems wiser or more accurate to himself than the Holy Spirit himself. But would it not have been better to interpret Scripture accurately than to argue that the text of Scripture is inaccurate? But that the Vulgate interpreted it as pillars, R. David rendered it columns of the earth, just as the Vulgate was also amended in this way by Lucas Osiander in his Paraphrase. Rabbenu Jesaias, as noted by Drosius, on this passage, explained it as foundations of the earth, Arias Montanus as stations of the earth; but the two former expositions, of R. David Kimchi, R. Esaias, which is also in the Lexicons of Avenarius and Schikard, agree more, and contain nothing inaccurate, nay rather they confirm the immobility or rest of the earth. For the foundations of the earth are immovable, upon which God placed the world. For He himself founded the immovable world 1 Chron. 16, 30. Cornelius a Lapide himself corrects the Vulgate here from the Hebrew in this place, because the word מצוקי ought not to be rendered by pillars, but foundations of the earth, and because it is designated here that the earth stands stable, firm, and immovable.

BECAUSE HE LOVED ANNA, BUT THE LORD HAD SHUT UP HER WOMB] The unhappy are wont to be loved more tenderly. But both sterility and fecundity are ascribed to God. See what was said in Gen. 30, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 8. DOMINI ENIM SVNT CARDINES TER- RÆ ET POSVIT SVPER EOS ORBEM) Habet terra su- os polos, quibus aut sustinet se in quiete, aut, ut alii volunt, in motu se librat: quod imitatur magnes.

ANNÆ AUTEM DEDIT PARTEM UNAM TRI- STIS] Pro tristis in Hebræo est אפים EN quod interpretan- tur honorabilem. Quid si intelligamus maxillam alteram? nam alteram habebat Sacerdos.

FLuctuare videtur Grotius, moveaturne terra, an quiescat? Immobilem autem esse terram, & quiescere, adversus Mathematicos nonnullos, & alios, probavimus Tom. 3. System. Theol. Art 5. c. 2. Quæst. 7. p. 1086. seqq. Diximus etiam nonnulla de eo judicio Theologico repetito adversus M. Henric. Nicolai, qui impie satis hunc locum exagitabat, adden- dis ad Th. 20. de quotidiana Telluris revolutione; Sic cardines Terræ, inquit, terram vocat, quibus im- posuit orbem habitabilem. Quod in accurata confide- ratione ALITER SE HABERE certum est. Sa- pientior ergo vel accuratior hic homo sibi videtur ipsomet Spiritu S. Annon vero præstabat accurate interpretari Scripturam, quam inaccurationis ar- guere textum scripturæ. Quod autem cardines in- terpretatus est vulgatus, R. David columnas terræ reddidit, quemadmodum etiam Luca Osiandro ita emendata est vulgata in Paraphrasi. Rabbenu Jesaias, notante Drosio, ad hunc locum, fundamenta terræ exposuit, Arias Montanus stationes terræ; sed prio- res duæ expositiones, R. Davidis Kimchi, R. Esaiæ, quæ Avenarii etiam & Schikardi in Lexicis est, magis congruunt, nihilque inaccurati continent, imo terræ immobilitatem, vel quietem confir- mant. Terræ enim fundamenta immota sunt, super quæ posuit Deus orbem. Ipse enim fundavit orbem immobilem 1. Chron. 16, 30. Corrigit hic ex Ebræo vulgatam ipse Cornelius a Lapide in h. l. quod non per cardines, sed fundamenta terræ, vox מצוקי reddi debeat, & quod designetur hic, quod terra stabilis, firma & immota consistat.

QVIA ANNAM DILIGEBAT, DOMINUS AUTEM CONCLUSERAT VULVAM EJUS] Tenerius amari so- lent infelices. Tam autem sterilitas quam fœcunditas Deo ascribuntur. Vide quæ dicta Gen. 30, 2.

## 3:8
Vers. 8. AM NOT I BETTER TO THEE THAN TEN SONS) In a harmonious marriage there is more good than in fecundity itself.

Latin:

Vers. 8. NUMQVID EO MELIOR TIBI SUM QVAM DECEM FILII) In concorde matrimonio plus boni est quam in ipsa fœcunditate.

## 3:10
Ver. 10. HE SHALL GIVE STRENGTH UNTO HIS KING, AND EXALT THE HORN OF HIS ANOINTED] He is going to propagate most widely the borders of that King whom Samuel is about to anoint, that is, David. Mystically, however, these things are rightly referred to the Gospel.

The Jews do not deserve to be heard here: for sighs also are pleasing to God, as is evident from the example of Moses, Ex. 14, 15. ch. 17, 11. St. Cyprian, concerning St. Anna, in his book on the Lord's Prayer, says: she was speaking, he says, not with her voice, but with her heart, because she knew that God hears in this way. Cf. Chrysost. Homil. 2 on Anna.

Grotius owes to the Papists the double sense of one saying, one literal and the other mystical: who in this annotation has followed Cornelius a Lapide the Jesuit and others. We acknowledge only one.

Latin:

Vers. 10. DABIT IMPERIVM REGI SVO, ET SVBLIMABIT REGNVM CORNU CHRISTI SUI] Latissime propaga- turus est fines Regi illi quem uncturus est Samuel, id est, Da- vidi. Mystice tamen ad Evangelium hæc recte referuntur.

Non hic audiri merentur Judæi: nam & suspi- ria Deo grata sunt, ut exemplo Mosis constat Ex. 14, 15. c. 17, 11. S. Cyprianus de S. Anna l. de orat. Dominica, loquebatur, inquit, non voce, sed corde, quia sic Deum sciebat audire. Conf. Chrysost. Ho- mil. 2. de Anna.

Geminum unius dicti sensum liter alem uuuum, & mysticum alterum Papistis debet Grotius: Qui in hac annotatione Cornelium a Lapide Jesui tam & alios sequutus est. Nos non nisi unum agnoscimus

## 3:13
NOVERAT INDIGNE AGERE FILIOS SVOS) In the Hebrew: מקללים להם but the Hebrews note that for להם there was once לי, and thus the LXX read it; for they translate ὅτι κακολογῦντες τὸν Θεὸν οἱ ὑίοὶ αὐτῶ.

Latin:

NOVERAT INDIGNE AGERE FILIOS SVOS) In Hebræo: מקללים להם sed notant Hebræi pro להם olim fuisse לי, & sic legerunt LXX. vertunt enim ὅτι κακολογῦντες τὸν Θεὸν οἱ ὑίοὶ αὐτῶ.

## 3:17
Verse 17. BECAUSE THEY WERE DRAWING MEN AWAY FROM THE SACRIFICE OF THE LORD) The manifest sins of Priests turn the people away from true religion, and therefore God punishes them severely, both in those who commit them and in those who connive at them, 3:12. Nor yet is the Priesthood defiled by this, to which even in such times the pious piously minister, as the following things now show.

Verse 24. DO NOT, MY SONS, FOR IT IS NOT A GOOD REPORT THAT I HEAR) Those who have the right to punish do not fulfill their duty by merely warning. There is no need here to repeat what was gathered in the second book on the Law of War and Peace, ch. 30, 11, and in the Annotations. See below 3:13.

Verse 23. IF A MAN SHALL SIN AGAINST A MAN, GOD CAN BE APPEASED FOR HIM: BUT IF A MAN SHALL SIN AGAINST THE LORD, WHO SHALL PRAY FOR HIM) All sins indeed offend God: but especially those which are directed straight against His Majesty. See Acts 5:5 and what was said by us at Matt. 12:31. In such crimes, however, God does not always hear prayers, as appears below 3:14, Ezek. 8:18, Jer. 7:15, and 1 John 5:16.

Grotius confuses the sin against the Holy Spirit with other sins. That is treated in Matt. 12:31 and 1 John 5:16. But in the other added passages, it does not appear that the discourse is about blasphemy against the Holy Spirit. For the requirements of that sin are not found there. Ananias indeed had lied to the Holy Spirit, and had tempted the same, Acts 5:9. But that it is not stated in the text that he designated that blasphemy which is joined with the impious rejection of all means of salvation. The sons of Eli, although they sinned against the first table and also immediately against God, are not yet proven guilty of the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, which was treated in Matt. 12. And although GOD sometimes threatens his judgments, which He does not wish to revoke, to an entire family and its posterity, as here to Eli the Priest, ch. 3:14, and sometimes to a whole people, which was done in Is. 8:18, Jerem. 7:14, yet those crimes ought not to be confused with the sin against the Holy Spirit, concerning which Christ testifies in Matt. 12:31-32, that it will not be forgiven, neither in this age nor in the next. For neither can all those in the family or the entire people be judged to have committed the sin against the Holy Spirit, nor do the judgments which God threatened to them there concern eternal punishment after this life, but only temporal punishment in this life.

Verse of the same.

AND THEY DID NOT HEAR THE VOICE OF THEIR FATHER, BECAUSE GOD WILLED TO KILL THEM] God takes away prudence from those who sin both gravely and for a long time and often, so that before the punishment their wickedness may be made manifest. This is peremptory hardening. This is what Aeschylus meant: God indeed prepares a cause for mortals when He wishes to destroy a house utterly. Velleius Paterculus on Varus: The fates were already prevailing over counsels, and had bound up all the strength of his mind. Indeed, the matter is such that, for the most part, he who is about to change fortune corrupts counsels. Ammianus Marcellinus in book 14 says that when the fates lay their hand upon men, their senses are dulled and blunted. True this, true. See 2 Chron. 10:15.

Some observe that the word כִּי is sometimes to be explained as 'although', as for instance the blessed Joh. Tarnovius in his Exercitations; but whence was this will of God evident to them? Buxtorf, Glassius, and Walther render it 'therefore', as this word is taken in Psalm 116:10 and Jeremiah 4:10. Not badly. For even if, as Hackspan brings forward, another reason is held in the text, namely that they sinned against God, yet this disobedience toward the Father was also added to it. Although even if the Vulgate exposition is retained with Osiander, they obtain nothing for their absolute decree from Calvin: because these things sound of a consequent and judicial will, to punish on account of preceding sins: nor is there anything for the necessity of all things, which Hackspan rashly imputes to the mind of the blessed Luther: as we have demonstrated in the Antapologia rendered to the Rintelenses: because this disobedience was voluntary, not coerced.

Verse 27.

BUT THE MAN OF GOD CAME TO ELI] Prophets in the exercise of their office are greater than both kings and priests.

Verse 30.

I HAVE SPOKEN] That is, I had clearly proposed.

BUT NOW THE LORD SAYS] The decrees of God are not all absolutely defined, such as those of which we treated above in 25, but many contain a condition within themselves, which failing, they fail.

Verse 31. THAT THERE BE NO OLD MAN IN THY HOUSE] That is, endowed with dignity. See below 36.

Verse 32.

AND THOU SHALT SEE THINE EMULATOR IN THE TEMPLE] In Hebrew: an oppressor in the Sanctuary. See this fulfilled in 4:11.

IN ALL THE PROSPERITY OF ISRAEL] In other prosperous things, so that it may appear that this evil happens because of the profaned sacred things.

BUT THAT THINE EYES MAY FAIL AND THY SOUL MAY PINE AWAY] Therefore they will live for some time, so that they may be a source of the greatest grief to you, which is explained more openly in the following words.

Verse 35. AND I WILL RAISE ME UP A FAITHFUL PRIEST] How? By inclining the hearts of the kings, to whom the right belonged to choose the high priest, but from the family of Aaron as long as it existed. The same right belonged to the Sanhedrin, as often as there were no kings. Properly, however, this treats of Zadok. See the history in 1 Kings 2:34, 1 Chronicles 29:22.

AND HE SHALL WALK BEFORE MY CHRIST] Before Solomon solemnly anointed as king. See the passage of Chronicles already mentioned.

VENIAT VT ORETVR PRO EO) In Hebrew: Let him come bowed down. He shall be the least among the Priests, to whom it is permitted to pray to nothing else but God, not to perform greater things.

OFFERAT NUMMUM ARGENTUM) In Hebrew: a small piece of silver, on account of poverty. Let him offer, namely, into the treasury.

Another reason for the offered coin is brought forward later, namely that the High Priest might be conciliated, so that he might admit the offerer to some part of the ministry, vers. 36.

ET TORTAM PANIS) For a sin, not an ox or a sheep, and not even a bird, on account of that same poverty, of course. Lev. 5, 11. 12.

MITTE ME OBSECRO AD VNAM PARTEM SACERDOTALEM) In Hebrew: join me I pray to one of the priesthoods: In Greek: παράῥῥιψόν με ἐπὶ μίαν τῶν ἱερατειῶν, that is, make me a helper of even some minimal work, so that I may earn a living.

Here we have the explanation why the candidate for office is to offer both the coin and the loaf of bread, not into the treasury, nor for a sacrifice, but for the sake of courting the favor of the High Priest.

VT COMEDAM BVCCELLAM PANIS) Meager food, such as was accustomed to be given to Priests prohibited from performing their duty. 2 Kings 23, 9. Ezek. 44, 13. However, these things seem to be understood concerning the descendants of Abiathar, removed from the High Priesthood on account of the crime of treason.

CHAPTER III. The calling of Samuel. The prediction of the destruction of Eli.

SERMO DOMINI ERAT PRETIOSUS IN DIEBUS ILLIS) It was rare for God to reveal Himself to anyone. See below 21.

NON ERAT VISIO MANIFESTA) Vision is here taken generally for any revelation whatsoever.

Latin:

Vers. 17. QVIA RETRAHEBANT HOMINES A SA- CRIFICIO DOMINI ) Peccata manifesta Sacerdotum po- pulum a vera religione avertunt, & proterea graviter ea Deus punit, & in iis, qui admittunt, & in iis qui connivent 3, 12. Neque tamen per hoc impuratur Sacerdotium, cui & talibus temporibus pii pie inserviunt, ut ostendunt jamjam sequentia.

Vers. 24. NOLITI FILII MEI, NON ENIM EST BO- NA FAMA QVAM EGO AVDIO ) Qui puniendi jus ha- bent, ii monendo tantum non defunguntur officio. Nihil opus hic repeti quæ congesta libro secundo de Jure Belli ac Pacis c. 30, 11. & in Annotatis. Vide infra 3, 13.

Vers. 23. SI PECCAVERIT VIR IN VIRVM PLA- CARI EI POTEST DEVS: SI AVTEM IN DOMI- NVM PECCAVERIT VIR, QVIS ORABIT PRO EO) Omnia quidem peccata Deum offendunt: sed maxime ea,quæ directe contra ejus Majestatem feruntur. Vid. Act. 5, 5. & quæ dicta nobis ad Matth. 12, 31. In talibus autem crimini- bus Deus deprecationes non semper audit, ut apparet infra 3, 14. Ezech. 8, 18. Jer. 7, 15. & 1. Joh. 5, 16.

Confundit Grotius peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum cum aliis peccatis. De illo agitur Matth. 12. v. 31. & 1. Joh. 5. v. 16. At in cæteris additis locis de blasphemia in Spiritum Sanctum ser- monem esse, non apparet. Non enim ibi re- quisita istius peccati deprehenduntur. Ananias quidem mentitus erat Spiritui Sancto, & tenta- rat eundem Actor. 5. v. 9. Sed blasphemiam il- lam, quæ cum impia rejectione omnium medio- rum salutis conjuncta est, eundem designasse, in textu non perhibetur. Filii Eli, etsi contra tabulam primam & contra Deum immediate etiam peccarint, non tamen rei peraguntur blasphemiæ in Spiritum S. de qua Matth. 12. actum est. Et quanquam DEUS quandoque integræ familiæ ejusque posteritati, uti hic Eli Sacerdotis, cap. 3. v. 14. quandoque toti populo judicia sua, quæ re- vocare non vult, minetur, quod Es. 8. v. 18. Jerem. 7. v. 14. factum, non tamen illa crimina cum pec- cato in Spiritum Sanctum de quo Christus Matth. 12. v. 31. 32. testatur, quod neque in hoc, neque in altero seculo remittetur, confundi debent. Nam neque omnes illi in familia, aut populo integro peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum commisisse censeri possunt, neque judicia, quæ ibi illis minatus est Deus, concernunt pœnam æternam post hanc vi- tam, sed tantum temporalem pœnam in hac vita.

Vers. eod.

ET NON AVDIERVNT VOCEM PATRIS SVI, QVIA DEVS VOLVIT OCCIDERE EOS] Iis qui & gravia & diu & sæpe moniti peccant Deus prudentiam adi- mit, ut ante pœnam improbitas eorum aperta fiat. Hæc est in- duratio peremtoria. Hoc est quod voluit Æschylus: Θεὸς μὲν αἰτίαν φύει βροτοῖς Ὅταν κακῶσαι δῶμα παμπήδην θέλῃ. Vellejus Paterculus de Varo: Prævalebant jam fata consiliis, omnemque animi ejus vim præstrinxerant. Quippe ita se res ha- bet, ut plerumque, qui fortunam mutaturus est, consilia corrum- pat. Ammianus Marcellinus libro 14. ait manum injicienti- bus fatis hebetari sensus hominum & obtundi. Vera hæc, vera. Vide 2. Paral. 10. v. 15.

Observant nonnulli vocem כִּי ut alias quan- doque explicandam esse per quamvis, utpote B. Joh. Tarnovius Exercit. sed unde constabat illis de hac voluntate DEI? Buxtorf. Glassius & Wal- ther, reddunt IDCIRCO, uti sumitur hæc vox Psalm. 116. v. 10. Jer. 4. v. 10. Non male. Etsi enim, quod Hackspanius adfert, ratio alia in tex- tu habeatur, quod sc. peccaverint in Deum, ac- cessit tamen eidem etiam hæc inobedientia erga Patrem. Quamvis etiam retenta cum Osiandro Vulgata expositione, nihil Calv. obtineant pro suo absoluto decreto: Quia de voluntate consequenti, & judiciali hæc sonant, ob antegressa peccata pu- niendi: Nihil etiam pro verum omnium necessita- te, quam temere Hackspanius B. Lutheri im- putat menti: ut in Antapologia Rintelensibus reddita demonstravimus: quia voluntaria, non coacta fuit hæc inobedientia.

Vers. 27.

VENIT AVTEM VIR DEI AD HELI] Prophetæ in exercitio muneris sui & regibus & sacerdotibus majores.

Vers. 30.

LOQVENS LOCVTVS SVM] Id est, plane propo- sueram.

NVNC AVTEM DICIT DOMINVS] Decreta Dei non omnia sunt absolute definita, qualia illa de quibus egi- mus supra 25. sed multa conditionem in se continent, qua de- ficiente deficiunt.

Vers. 31. VT NON SIT SENEX IN DOMO TVA] Id est, dignitate præditus. Vide infra 36.

Vers. 32.

ET VIDEBIS ÆMVLVM TVVM IN TEMPLO] Hebraice: oppressorem in Sanctuario. Impletum hoc vide 4, 11.

IN VNIVERSIS PROSPERIS ISRAEL] Cæteris rebus prosperis, ut appareat accidere hoc malum ob profanata sacra.

SED VT DEFICIANT OCVLI TVI ET TABE- SCAT ANIMA TVA] Ideo vivent ad tempus aliquod, ut tibi summo dolori sint, quod verbis sequentibus apertius ex- plicatur.

Vers. 35. ET SVSCITABO MIHI SACERDOTEM FIDELEM] Quomodo? inclinando corda regum, quibus jus erat eligere summum Sacerdotem, sed ex Aaronis familia quamdiu ea exstabat. Idem jus Synedrio fuit, quoties reges non erant. Proprie autem hic de Sadoco agitur. Vide histo- riam 1. Reg. 2, 34. 1. Par. 19, 22.

ET AMBVLABIT CORAM CHRISTO MEO] Co- ram Solomone in regem solemniter uncto. Vide dicta jam Paralipomenon locum.

VENIAT VT ORETVR PRO EO) In Hebræo: Ve- niat incurvatum se. Erit inter Sacerdotes minimus, cui ni- hil aliud quam Deum orare liceat, non majora pera- gere.

OFFERAT NUMMUM ARGENTUM) In Hebræo: minutum argenti, præ paupertate. Offerat, nempè in Gazo- phylacium.

Alia causa oblati nummi asfertur postea, ni- mirum ut Pontifex concilietur, quo admittat offe- rentem ad partem aliquam ministerii, vers. 36.

ET TORTAM PANIS) Pro peccato, non bovem aut pecudem, ac ne avem quidem, præ eadem paupertate scilicet. Lev. 5, 11. 12.

MITTE ME OBSECRO AD VNAM PARTEM SACERDOTALEM) In Hebræo: adjunge me quæso uni sa- cerdotiorum: Græce: παράῥῥιψόν με ἐπὶ μίαν τῶν ἱερατειῶν, id est, fac me vel minimæ alicujus operæ adjutorem, ut vi- ctum merear.

Hic habemus explicationem, cur & nummum & tortam panis non in Gazophylacium, nec ad sa- crificium, sed pro captanda Pontificis gratia obla- turus sit candidatus officii.

VT COMEDAM BVCCELLAM PANIS) Alimenta te- nuia, qualia dari solebant Sacerdotibus a munere fungendo prohibitis. 2. Regum 23, 9. Ezech. 44, 13. Videntur autem hæc intelligenda de Abiatharis, ob crimen majestatis a sum- mo Pontificatu demoti, posteris.

CAPUT III. Vocatio Samuelis. Prædictio exitii Eli.

SERMO DOMINI ERAT PRETIOSUS IN DIEBUS ILLIS) Rarum erat ut cuiquam se Deus revelaret. Vide in- fra 21.

NON ERAT VISIO MANIFESTA) Visio hîc gene- raliter sumitur pro quavis revelatione.

## 3:17
HÆC FACIAT TIBI DEVS ET HÆC ADDAT, SI ABSCONDERIS SERMONEM) ἐξορκισμὸς, or in the sense of the Latins, an adjuration. See Jud. 17, 2. Ruth. 2, 17.

Latin:

HÆC FACIAT TIBI DEVS ET HÆC ADDAT, SI ABSCONDERIS SERMONEM) ἐξορκισμὸς, sive La- tinorum sensu, obsecratio. Vide Jud. 17, 2. Ruth. 2, 17.

## 3:18
DOMINVS EST: QVOD BONVM EST IN OCV- LIS SVIS) A praiseworthy example of one patiently submitting himself to God who is punishing. Praiseworthy also below, because he is touched more by the sense of public calamity than private. 18.

Theodoret, Procopius, Lyranus, and others gather the repentance of Eli from this: as Chrysostom, book 3, On the Monastic Life. Compare Ps. 119, 137. Dan. 3, 27. Ambrose in the Psalm, l. c. The Lord is just in dangers, just in losses, just in punishments, not only because each one justly pays for the faults of his own punishment, but also while one suffers, very many are corrected.

JVXTA VERBVM DOMINI: In the Hebrew: in the word of the Lord: that is: by the word: not in a dream, or otherwise.

Latin:

DOMINVS EST: QVOD BONVM EST IN OCV- LIS SVIS) Laudabile exemplum patienter se submittentis Deo punienti. Laudabile & infra, quod sensu publicæ ca- lamitatis magis quam privatæ tangitur. 18.

Pœnitentiam Eli hinc colligunt Theodor. Procop. Lyran. alii : ut Chrysost. lib. 3. Vit. mo- nast. Conf. Pf. 119, 137. Dan. 3, 27. Ambros. in Psalm. l. c. Justus Dominus in periculis, justus in damnis, justus in ultionibus est, non solum quia unus- quisq; juste pœnæ suæ culpas luit, verum etiam dum unus patitur, plurimi corriguntur.

JVXTA VERBVM DOMINI: In Hebræo: in serbo Domini: id est: per verbum: non in somnio, aut aliter.

## 4:1 Argument
CHAPTER IV. The Israelites slaughtered: the ark captured. Hophni and Phinehas slain. Eli and his daughter-in-law expired from grief.

Latin:

CAPUT IV. Israelitæ casi: arca capta. Ophni & Pinehes trucidati. Heli cum nuru sua præ mœrore expirarunt.

## 4:3
Ver. 3. LET US BRING UNTO US FROM SHILOH THE ARK OF THE COVENANT OF THE LORD) Those not cleansed from their sins place their hope in God in vain.

Transgressors of the law, as the wonderful Author of Holy Scripture says, book 2, chapter 7, the ark of the law by no means protects: But the law which was in it convicts, says Theodoret.

Latin:

Vers. 3. AFFERAMVS AD NOS DE SILO ARCAM FOEDERIS DOMINI) Non purgati a peccatis suis fru- stra spem in Deo collocant.

LEgis transgressores, dicente Aučore mirabil. S. Script. l. 2. c. 7. nequaquam legis arca tuetur: Sed quæ in ea lex erat, arguit, ait Theodor.

## 4:8
Ver. 8. THESE ARE THE GODS THAT SMOTE EGYPT] They speak of the God of the Hebrews, not as of the God of the universe, but as of the God of that people. Compare 1 Kings 20:23, 28; 2 Kings 19:12.

Latin:

Vers. 8. HI SVNT DII QVI PERCVSSERANT ÆGY- PTVM ] De Deo Hebræorum, non ut de Deo universi, sed ut de Deo populi illius loquuntur. Confer. 1. Reg. 20, 23. 28. 2. Reg. 19, 12.

## 4:18
FORTY YEARS.

The LXX wrongly read 20; the Chaldean and Josephus agree with the Hebrew Codex. Ahitub, his grandson by his son, succeeded Eli in the High Priesthood, 1 Sam. 14:3, but Samuel in the Principate.

Latin:

QUADRAGINTA ANNIS.

Perperam LXX. legunt 20. consentit Ebræo Codici Chald. & Josephus. Heli successit Achitob ejus ex filio nepos in Pontificatu, 1. Sam. 14, 3. in Prin- cipatu vero Samuel.

## 4:21
Ver. 21. THE GLORY IS DEPARTED FROM ISRAEL) The ark upon which God was accustomed to appear gloriously.

This happened in the 83rd year before the temple was built, and thus in the year of the world 2910.

Latin:

Vers. 21. TRANSLATA EST GLORIA DE ISRAEL) Arca super quam Deus gloriose apparere solebat.

Accidit id anno ante conditum templum 83. adeoque anno M. 2910.

## 5:4
CHAPTER V. The ark prostrates Dagon and the Philistines.

Latin:

CAPUT V. Arca prosternit Dagonem, & Philistæos.

## 5:5
THEREFORE NEITHER THE PRIESTS OF DAGON, NOR ANY THAT COME INTO DAGON'S HOUSE, TREAD ON THE THRESHOLD OF DAGON IN ASHDOD) God willed that a monument of the miracle performed by Him should exist in the very rites of the idolaters.

Dagon is believed to have been like the Nereids, Tritons, and Sirens, with a woman's face and ending in a fish: because the Syrians and Palestinians worshipped fish, as witnessed by Clem. Alexand. in his exhortation to the Gentiles; whence Josephus says Dagon is Derceto, that is, Venus, according to Lyra, Abulensis, Scaliger, and Serarius.

Latin:

PROPTER HANC CAUSAM NON CALCANT SACERDOTES DAGON, ET OMNES QVI INGRE- DIVNTVR TEMPLVM EJUS, SVPER LIMEN DA- GON IN AZOTO) Voluit Deus miraculi a se dati monu- mentum exstare in ipsis idololatrarum ritibus.

DAgon instar Nereidum, Tritonum, & Sire- num facie muliebri fuisse, & in piscem de- siisse creditur : quia Syri & Palæstini pisces co- luere, teste Clem. Alexand. exhort. ad gent. unde Josephus Dagonem dicit esse Decerten, hoc est, Venerem, juxta Lyran. Abulens. Scaliger, & Sera- rium.

## 5:6
IN THE SECRET PART OF THE BUTTOCKS) In Hebrew it is written עפלים, it is read טחורים, as also in Deuteronomy 28:27. In which places the LXX [have] εἰς τὴν ἕδραν, and εἰς τὰς ἕδρας. Symmachus, περιελύθησαν αὐτῶν αἱ ἕδραι. Figs or hemorrhoids seem to be understood. But Josephus thinks it was dysentery: Aquila, according to Theodoret, [thinks it was] phagedaena.

AND MICE WERE BORN.

Which, according to Josephus, were devouring gardens, fields, vineyards, and all crops, produce, and fruits. Abulensis notes that they were supernatural, because no natural cause could have produced them so suddenly and in such great numbers.

THEY GATHERED ALL THE SATRAPS OF THE PHILISTINES). The Philistines were therefore governed by an oligarchy.

Latin:

Vers. 6. IN SECRETIORE PARTE NATIUM) In He- bræo scribitur עפלים legitur, טחורים ut & Deuteron. 28, 27. quibus locis LXX. εἰς τὴν ἕδραν, & εἰς τὰς ἕδρας. Sym- machus, περιελύθησαν αὐτῶν αἱ ἕδραι. Fici aut mariscæ vi- dentur intelligi. At Josephus δυσεντερίαν fuisse putat : Aqui- la, referente Theodoreto, φαγέδαιναν.

ET NATI SUNT MURES.

Qui Josepho teste, hortos, agros, vineas omnes. que segetes, fruges, & fructus depascebantur. Quos supernaturales fuisse Abul. notat, quia nulla causa naturalis eos tam subito & in tanto numero producere potuisset.

CONGRECAVERUNT OMNES SATRAPAS PHI- LISTHINORUM). Fuere ergo Philisthini ὀλιγαρχέμενοι.

## 5:9
AND THEIR PROMINENT PARTS WERE ROTTING) In Hebrew the sense seems to be: And before this, hemorrhoids had been unknown to them: so that the very novelty of the disease might increase the portent.

The Vulgate adds: and they made for themselves leather seats: about which the Papists are anxious as to what they should do: But in vain, because there is nothing about them in the Hebrew or Chaldean text.

Latin:

ET COMPUTRESCEBANT PROMINENTES EX- TALES EORVM) In Hebræo sensus videtur esse: Et an- te ignota illis fuerant mariscæ: ut ipsa novitas morbi osten- tum augeat.

Vulgata addit : & fecerunt sibi sedes pelliceas : de quibus quid faciant, anxii sunt Papistæ : Sed frustra, quia nihil de iis in Ebr. aut Chald. textu.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI. Cows draw the returned ark straight to the Bethshemites. Who, looking into it, are struck down.

Latin:

CAPUT VI. Arcam remissam vaccæ recta ad Bethsamitas pertrahunt. Qui eam inspicientes percu- tiuntur.

## 6:3
Verse 3. RENDER TO HIM FOR THE SIN) Doubtless according to the opinion of idolaters: Believe me, gifts appease both men and gods. Which is thus set down in Homer: Δῶρα θεοὺς πείθει, δῶρ᾽ αἰδοίυς βασιλῆας. Plato criticizes this in Book 3 of the Republic.

Latin:

Vers. 3. REDDITE EI PRO PECCATO) Nimirum ex Idololatrarum sententia: Munera crede mihi placant hominesque deosque. Quod apud Homerum sic positum : Δῶρα θεοὺς πείθει, δῶρ᾽ αἰδοίυς βασιλῆας. Reprehendit Plato 3. de Republica.

## 6:7
Verse 7. PREGNANT COWS) The ancient Italians used to call them 'fordas', according to Varro in book 5.

TO WHOM THE YOKE HAS NOT BEEN IMPOSED) The Greeks call them ἀδμήτας; the Latins, injuges, according to Festus. See what was said at Num. 19, 2.

AND IF INDEED IT SHALL GO UP BY THE WAY OF THEIR OWN BORDERS AGAINST BETH-SHEMESH) οἰωνισμὸς.

Latin:

Vers. 7. VACCAS FOETAS) Fordas vocabant Itali ve- teres, teste Varrone libro 5.

QVIBVS NON EST IMPOSITVM JVGVM) ἀδμή- τας vocant Græci : injuges Latini, Festo teste. Vide quæ di- cta Num. 19, 2.

ET SIQVIDEM PER VIAM FINIUM SUORVM ASCENDERIT CONTRA BETSAMES) οἰωνισμὸς.

## 6:11
AND THE LIKENESSES OF YOUR EMERODS) The Scholiast on Aristophanes' Acharnians teaches us that something similar was done by the Attics; for when the god was angry (the discourse is about Father Liber), a disease settled upon the private parts of the men, &c.

UNTO ABEL THE GREAT) It is read now in the Hebrew אבל, but the LXX read אבן. For they translate it λίθον.

Latin:

ET SIMILITUDINES ANORUM) Simile quid ab At- ticis factum docet nos ad Acharnenses Aristophanis Scholia- stes; Μηνίσαντος γὰρ τῦ Θεῦ (de Libero patre sermo) νόσος κατέσκηψεν εἰς τὰ αἰδοῖα τῶν ἀνδρῶν, &c.

USQVE AD ABEL MAGNUM) Legitur nunc in Hebræo אבל sed LXX. legerunt אבן. Vertunt enim λίθον.

## 6:19
Vers. 19. BECAUSE THEY HAD SEEN THE ARK OF THE LORD] Among all nations it has been held as an abomination for mysteries to be looked upon except by the initiated.

This is not to be sought from the custom of the nations. There is an express prohibition of God in Numbers 4:5, 20, the reason for which punishment is rightly given by R. Rabbenu Jeschajath and R. David Kimchi, who on verse 13 has it thus: They rejoiced so much at seeing the ark that, because of the greatness of their joy, they broke through to look into the ark, opening it and seeing what was in it, for which they were punished according to that which is written in Num. 4:20. For the ark was not covered with a lid in vain, and therefore no one without divine command ought to have removed it and looked into it under penalty of death. Others of the Rabbis give other reasons, but ἄτεργραφῆς [without written authority]. R. Solomon, that they received it with light and reckless joy, and did not look upon it with the due trembling: R. Levi Ben Gerson, that seeing the ark of the Lord they did not leave off their work, for they were then reaping the wheat harvest. Others, that they uttered ignominious words against the ark: as can be read in the Talmud Sota. Abarbenel, that they cast the ark out from among them, and did not wish to grant it a dwelling among them. The Chaldean Paraphrast gives this reason for the smiting of the Bethshemites, that they had rejoiced at seeing the ark of the Lord captured. But as I have said, all those things are said outside of Scripture. A greater difficulty is concerning the number of the smitten, because it is said, and he smote בעם שבעים which they render, in the people seventy men, fifty thousand men: which the Chaldean and Lyranus accept in such a way that he smote 70 men among the elders of the people, and 50,000 among the assembly of the commoners. The Talmudists R. Ashu and R. Eleazar dispute about it: one of them says there were only 70, each of whom was worth 50,000. The other says 50,000 were smitten, each of whom was equal to 70 assessors of the Sanhedrin. To Abarbenel it seems absurd that 50,000 men were smitten in the small town of Bethshemesh. Therefore he says this number is of all who died because of the ark, rendering the text thus: And he smote בעם שבעים איש TOGETHER WITH 70 men (of Bethshemesh, who had looked into the ark) in total 50,000. Which plague of 70 men in Bethshemesh he says is called great, because in respect to that small place this plague was very great. Others, however, judge that those 70 were of the priestly class, and with R. David Kimchi, understanding the 'vau' as a copulative, as in 1 Chron. 2:1, Hab. 3:11, they say those 50,000 were designated from all the Israelites who had rushed together in great numbers from various places, not from the Bethshemites alone; see Petr. Martyr, Deodatus, Junius, and Tremellius, the Belgian Bible, the Vinar. Paraphrast, etc.

Latin:

Vers. 19. EO QVOD VIDISSENT ARCAM DOMINI] Apud omnes gentes nefas habitum mysteria conspici nisi ab ini- tiatis.

NOn ex gentium more hæc petenda. Habetur expressum Dei interdictum Numer. 4, 5. 20. quam pœnæ hujus causam recte reddit R. Rabbenu Jeschajath & R. David Kimchi, qui ad vers. 13. ita habet: Adeo lætati sunt videntes arcam, ut præ magni- tudine lætitiæ prorumperent ad introspiciendum in ar- cam, eam aperientes & videntes, quid in ea sit, unde & puniti fuerunt juxta id, quod scriptum est Num. 4, 20. Non enim frustra erat arca operimento tecta, ideoque nemo sine mandato divino debebat illud auferre, eamque inspicere sub pœna mortis: Alii alias causas reddunt è Rabbinis, sed ἄτεργραφῆς. R. Salomo, quod gaudio levi ac temerario eam ex- ceperint, neque adspexerint cum debito tremore: R. Levi Ben Gerson, quod videntes arcam Domini non dereliquerunt opus suum, erant enim tunc me- tentes messem triticeam. Alii, quod verba ignomi- niosa contra arcam protulerint: Ut in Talmud So- ta legere est. Abarbenel, quod ejecerint arcam è medio sui, neque ei voluerint habitationem inter se concedere. Paraphrastes Chaldæus hanc percus- sorum Bethlehemitarum rationem reddit, quod lætati essent videntes arcam Domini captam. Sed uti dixi, ea omnia extra Scripturam dicuntur. Ma- jor difficultas est de numero percussorum, quia dici- tur, & percussit בעם שבעים quod reddunt, in populo septuaginta viros, quinquaginta mille viros: quæ Chaldæus & Lyranus ita accipiunt, quod per- cusserit in senioribus populi 70. viros, & in cœtu plebejorum 50000. Talmudici R. Ashu & R. Elea- zar disputant de eo: unus eorum dicit LXX. tan- tum erant, quorum quisq; valebat 50000. Alter 50000. percussi erant, quorum unusquisq; æquipalebat LXX. assessoribus Synedrii. Abarbeneli absonum videtur in Bethsemesch oppido parvo 50000. viros percus- sos. Ideo numerum hunc dicit esse omnium, qui mortui fuere propter arcam, ita reddens textum: Et percussit בעם שבעים איש UNA cum 70. viris (Bethsemesch, qui inspexerant arcam) sum- matim 50000. Quam plagam in Bethsemesch 70. virorum magnam dicit vocari, eo quod respectu parvi illius loci hæc plaga maxima fuerit. Alii ta- men 70. illos de Sacerdotum genere fuisse censent, & cum R. David Kimchi vau copulativum, ut 1. Chro- nic. 2, 1. Hab. 3, 11. subintelligentes, illos 50000. ex Israelitis omnibus, qui è variis locis confestim magna frequentia accurrerint, non ex solis Bethschemi- tis designatos dicunt; vid. Petr. Martyr, Deodatus, Junius, & Tremellius, Biblia Belgica, Paraphrast. Vi- nariens. &c.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAPTER VII. The ark is transferred to Kiriath-jearim. The covenant with GOD is renewed. The Philistines, struck by thunder, are routed, and humbled for the whole time of Samuel.

Vers. 1. THE MEN OF KIRIATH-JEARIM.

It is distant 4 miles from Jerusalem, according to Adrichom, a city formerly of the Gibeonites, afterwards of the tribe of Judah. Gabaa was a hill or higher place in that city, in which was situated the house of Abinadab: whose son Eleazar, of Levitical lineage, was sanctified by Achitob the High Priest living in Shiloh, to guard the ark, as the Chaldean, Josephus, Abulensis, and Vatablus have it: for he was not the High Priest himself, nor is he read in the catalog of High Priests in 1 Paral. 6.

Latin:

CAPUT VII. Arca in Kiriathjearim transfertur. Fœdus cum DEO renovatur. Philisthæi tonitru perculsi profligantur, toto Samuelis tempore humi- liati.

Vers. 1. VIRI CARIATHIARIM.

DIstat Hierosolymis 4. miliaribus, secundum Adrichom. urbs prius Gabaonitarum, postea tribus Juda. Gabaa erat collis sive locus excelsior in illa urbe, in quo sita erat domus Abinadab: cu- jus filius Eleazar generis Levitici sanctificatus per Achitob Pontificem in Silo degentem, ut arcam as- servaret, ut Chald. Joseph. Abul. Vatabl. habent: non enim fuit Pontifex ipse, nec in catalogo Pon- tificum legitur 1. Paral. 6.

## 7:2
Vers. 2. FOR IT WAS NOW THE TWENTIETH YEAR.

Namely, from the time the ark was transferred to Kiriath-jearim, when all the house of Israel lamented (the Vulgate wrongly says 'rested'), publicly performing penance, as they were still oppressed by the Philistines: whence Samuel exhorted the Israelites to the renunciation of idols. This year, therefore, was the 20th of Samuel's leadership, as he succeeded Heli immediately. For there was no interregnum: nor is he introduced here as finally being appointed to leadership, but as a leader governing the people, from which time it is credible that he had already governed them for a decade, as we have noted in the Chronicle. The people were therefore still oppressed during those 20 years, even though they had recovered the ark: because the strange gods Baalim and Ashtaroth had not yet been renounced: when these were renounced and they served God alone, Samuel judged the Israelites in peace.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ERAT QUIPPE JAM ANNUS VI-GESIMUS.

Scil. ex quo in Kiriathjarim translata arca, cum lamentata est (Vulg. perperam requievit) omnis do-mus Israel, publice acta poenitentia, utpote adhuc pressa a Philistaeis: unde Samuel ad abdicationem idolorum Israelitas exhortatus est. Annus ergo hic 20. fuit pricipatus Samuelis, utpote qui Heli immediate succeslit. Non enim interregnum fuit: neque hic ut praeficiendus demum principatui Sa-muel introducitur, sed ut princeps populum gu-bernans, ex quo adhuc per decennium eundem gu-bernasse, credibile est, ut in Chronico monuimus. Pressus ergo populus per illos 20. annos adhuc fuit, etsi arcam recuperarat: quia Dii alieni Baa-lim & Astharoth nondum erant abdicati: quibus abdicatis cum soli Deo servirent, quiete judicavit Samuel Israelitas.

## 7:3
Vers. 3. PREPARE YOUR HEARTS UNTO THE LORD) This is the chief thing in repentance.

Latin:

Vers. 3. PRAPARATE CORDA VESTRA DOMINO) Hoc in poenitentia praecipuum.

## 7:5
Vers. 5. IN MIZPAH) See Jud. 20:1.

Latin:

Vers. 5. IN MASPHATH) Vide Jud. 20, 1.

## 7:6
Vers. 6. THEY DREW WATER, AND POURED IT OUT BEFORE THE LORD) Poured-out water signifies tears.

Latin:

Vers. 6. HAVSERVNT AQVAM, ET EFFVDERVNT IN CONSPECTU DOMINI) Aqua effusa lacrymas signi-ficat.

## 7:10
Vers. 10. AND THE LORD THUNDERED WITH A GREAT CRASH ON THAT DAY UPON THE PHILISTINES, AND TERRIFIED THEM) Ovid: And thunders destined to move human minds. Hence in Greek ἐμβρόντητοι, and in Latin attoniti (thunderstruck).

Latin:

Vers. 10. INTONUIT AUTEM DOMINUS FRAGORE MA-GNO IN DIE ILLA SUPER PHILISTHIIM, ET EX-TERRUIT EOS) Ovidius: Et humanas motura tonitrua mentes. Inde Graece ἐμβρόντητοι, & Latine attoniti.

## 7:13
Vers. 13. AND THE PHILISTINES WERE HUMBLED, AND THEY CAME NO MORE INTO THE BORDERS OF ISRAEL, AND THE HAND OF THE LORD WAS UPON THE PHILISTINES ALL THE DAYS OF SAMUEL] That is, up until the reign of Saul the Philistines did not dare to enter the borders of the Israelites with an army. But afterwards they grew strong again, as appears below 13, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET HUMILIATI SUNT PHILISTIIM, NEC APPO-SUERUNT ULTRA, UT VENIRENT IN TERMINOS ISRAEL, FACTA EST ITAQVE MANVS DOMINI SUPER PHILISTHAEOS CUNCTIS DIEBUS SAMUE-LIS] Id est, ad Regnum usque Saulis Philisthaei non ausi cum exercitu intrare fines Israelitarum. Postea vero inva-luere iterum, ut apparet infra 13, 19.

## 7:14
Vers. 14. AND THERE WAS PEACE BETWEEN ISRAEL AND THE AMORITE) That is, there was an abstention from every hostile act, not out of a treaty, but out of mutual fear.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ERATQVE PAX INTRA ISRAEL ET AMORRHAUM) Id est, abstinebatur ab omni actu hostili, non ex federe, sed ex mutuo metu.

## 7:15
Vers. 15. SAMUEL ALSO JUDGED ISRAEL ALL THE DAYS OF HIS LIFE] Namely, from the death of Eli until the reign of Saul.

Indeed, all the days of his life, says the text. For although after substituting his sons (who did not administer the Republic laudably) he anointed Saul as King, nevertheless while he lived, he did not entirely cast off the care of the Republic, as Osiander rightly says.

Latin:

Vers. 15. JUDICABAT QVOQVE SAMUEL ISRAELEM CUNCTIS DIEBUS VITAE SUAE] Nempe a morte Helis ad regnum usque Saulis.

Imo cunctis vitae suae diebus, ait textus. Tametsi enim post substitutos suos filios (qui non laudabi-liter administrarunt Remp.) Saulem in Regem in-unxit, tamen dum vixit, non omnino curam Rei-publicae abjecit, ut recte Osiander.

## 7:16
Vers. 16. HE WENT YEAR BY YEAR CIRCUITING BETHEL AND GILGAL] In the Hebrew it is בשנה בשנה: the Greeks say κατ' ἐνιαυτὸν, ἐνιαυτὸν, that is, every year. But Josephus: Twice a year he visited the cities, and judged them.

This was an anniversary visitation of the Ecclesiastical and Political state. But that Samuel built an altar in RAMAH, where he had his seat, does not prove that he was a Priest, as Cornelius a Lapide wishes, because he could offer sacrifices through others: and it was extraordinary, from a special revelation of God (for he was a Prophet), not undertaken out of ἐθελοθρησκείᾳ (will-worship).

Latin:

Vers. 16. IBAT PER SINGULOS ANNOS CIRCUIENS BE-THEL ET GALGALA] In Hebraeo est בשנה בשנה: Graeci κατ' ἐνιαυτὸν, ἐνιαυτὸν, id est, quotannis. At Josephus: Δὶς τοῦ ἔτους ἐπερχόμενος τὰς πόλεις, ἐδίκαζεν αὐτοῖς.

Fuit haec anniversaria visitatio status Ecclesia-stici, & Politici. Quod autem in RAMATH, ubi sedem habebat, altare aedificavit Samuel, non arguit ipsum Sacerdotem fuisse, uti Cornelius a La-pide vult, quia per alios sacrificia offerre potuit: & extraordinarium fuit ex speciali Dei revelatione, (Erat enim Propheta) non ex ἐθελοθρησκείᾳ su-sceptum.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII.

Samuel's sons administer badly: a King is requested, whence the grievances of Monarchy are proposed. But the people do not desist from their purpose.

Vers. 1. HE MADE HIS SONS JUDGES OVER ISRAEL] In his stead.

AND THEY TOOK BRIBES AND PERVERTED JUDGMENT] Hesiod:

And as the roar of the lawsuit is dragged along, where men who are gift-eaters lead, and judge judgments with crooked verdicts.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII.

Samuelis filii male administrant: postulatur Rex, unde Monarchiae proponuntur grava-mina. Sed non desistit a proposito populus.

Vers. 1. POSUIT FILIOS SUOS JUDICES ISRAEL] Vice sua.

ACCEPERUNTQVE MUNERA ET PERVERTE-RUNT JUDICIUM] Hesiodus:

Τῆς δὲ δίκης ῥόθον ἑλκομένης, ᾗ κ’ ἄνδρες ἄγωσι Δωροφάγοι, σκολιαῖς δὲ δίκαις κρίνωσι θέμιστας.

## 8:4
Verse 4.

ELDERS) The leaders of the tribes.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

MAJORES NATU) Tribuum primores.

## 8:5
Verse 5.

YOUR SONS DO NOT WALK IN YOUR WAYS: APPOINT A KING FOR US) They could have requested of Samuel that he remove his sons from their delegated office, and that he himself, not traveling through the lands, but at home, should judge controversial matters. That would have been more equitable than to depose an old man and a prophet who had served so well.

THAT HE MAY JUDGE US) That he may vindicate us from our enemies. For this is also called משפט: and the following verses below, 20, require this sense more.

AS ALSO ALL THE NATIONS HAVE) The neighboring ones. For they thought, as Josephus says, that it was nothing strange for them to have the same form of government as the neighboring peoples who were ruled by kings.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

FILII TUI NON AMBULANT IN VIIS TUIS: CONSTITUE NOBIS REGEM) Potuerant a Samuele po- stulare, ut demoveret filios a vicaria functione, & ipse, non terras obiens, sed domi res controversas dijudicaret. Id æqui- us fuerat, quam senem & Prophetam optime meritum de- trudere.

UT JUDICET NOS) Ut vindicet nos ab hostibus. Nam & hoc משפט dicitur: & hunc sensum magis requirunt sequentia infra 20.

SICUT ET UNIVERSÆ HABENT NATIONES) Vicinæ. Putabant enim, ut ait Josephus, ὐδὲν ἄτοπον εἶναι τῶν πλησιοχώρων βασιλευομένων τὴν ἀυτὴν ἔχειν αὐτοὺς πολιτείαν.

## 8:7
Verse 7.

HEAR THE VOICE OF THE PEOPLE) It is one thing to will that something should happen, another to permit it to happen. See Hosea 13:11.

FOR THEY HAVE NOT REJECTED YOU, BUT ME, THAT I SHOULD REIGN OVER THEM) This is explained in 10:19. God reigns through those whom He inspires with His Spirit, such as those judges were. Therefore, when they cast off Samuel, they vote God out of the kingdom, as Josephus speaks here. A similar expression is in Luke 10:16. And from this, interpret what is below in 12:17, 19. At another time, they could have made a king for themselves without fault. Deut. 18:14. See what was said there.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

AUDI VOCEM POPULI) Aliud est velle aliquid ut fiat, aliud sinere fieri. Vide Oseam 13, 11.

NON ENIM TE ABJECERUNT, SED ME, UT RE- GNEM SUPER EOS) Exponitur hoc 10, 19. Deus regnat per eos, quos Spiritu suo afflat, quales erant judices illi. Sa- muelem ergo cum destituunt, θεὸν ἀποχειροτονῦσι τῆς βα- σιλείας, ut loquitur hic Josephus. Similis locutio Luc.10,16. Et hinc interpretare quod est infra 12, 17. 19. Alio tempore regem sibi facere sine culpa potuissent. Deut. 18,14. Vide quæ ibi dicta.

## 8:10
Verse 10.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

## 8:11
THIS WILL BE THE RIGHT OF THE KING) Concerning the meaning of the word משפט in this place, see what was said concerning the right of war and peace, book 1, chapter 4, section 7. Josephus explains the sum of what follows, saying that it would come to pass that the King would treat them like slaves bought for a price. For neighboring kings commanded their subjects whatever they wished, as being unaccountable. Livy says the Syrians were born for servitude; Apollonius says they think nothing of liberty; Julian says their hands are patient, as we showed at chapter 4, section 20, book 1, of the Right of War and Peace. And therefore, subjects are everywhere in these books called the slaves of kings. This royal dominion, however, carried with it that the kings, at their own discretion, would make levies, impose head taxes and forced labor on men, and tributes on fields and taxes on merchandise, with no one contradicting. For that saying had a place there: I am king, I seek nothing further from a commoner. And to do anything with impunity, that is to be a king. If they sinned gravely against the law of God, vengeance belonged to God, not to individuals, and not even to the people. See what follows: & below 26, 10. 23.

I do not find that word explained in the cited passage. Nothing else is contained there that pertains to the present matter, except that it notes that the first men, not by God's command but brought by the experience of the weakness of families or groups against violence, came together into civil society, whence civil power has its origin, and that it is therefore called a human ordinance in 1 Pet. 2:13. Although elsewhere it is called a divine ordinance, because God approved of a salutary institution of men. These do not deserve consideration: because we know indeed that the Magistrate is called ἀνθρωπίνην κτίσιν, by reason of the instrumental and mediate cause, because he is ordained through men; by reason of the subject, because he is administered by men; by reason of the mode, because it is in a human way; by reason of the end, because it is for the utility of men: yet it cannot be proven that it is so called by reason of the principle, that it is a human invention; since God immediately instituted the Political state, just as the other states, the Ecclesiastical and the Economic: Prov. 8:15, 16. Dan. 2:37, 44. Wisd. 6:4, 5. Sir. 17:13, 14. Rom. 13:2. But in the same chapter § 3. I observe that Grotius touches upon this right of the King: That which is in Samuel concerning the right of the King, to one looking at it quite correctly, appears not to be understood as TRUE RIGHT, that is, the faculty of doing something honestly and justly (but a far different way of living is prescribed to the King in that part of the law which is about the duty of the King, Deut. 17:14), nor to indicate a bare fact; for there would be nothing exceptional in that, since private individuals are also accustomed to do injuries to private individuals: But a fact which has some effect of right, that is, the obligation of not rescinding. Therefore it is added: that the people, oppressed by these injuries, would implore God's aid, because, to wit, no human remedies existed. Thus, therefore, this right is called, just as a praetor is said to render right, even when it is decreed unjustly, l. jus pluribus, d. de justit. & jure. These things are in the same place in Grotius. Therefore, concerning tyrannical dominion joined with injuries or unjust, he explains the word משפט not as a Royal right granted by God: Following most Papists, Estius, Tirinus, and others, with whom some Calvinists and Photinians also agree. Otherwise, almost all of our people have solidly proven that this right of the King is not unjust or usurpatory, but granted by God, and such that the Magistrate, when necessity urges, can use it with a clear conscience. Those who perhaps go in another direction here, rashly misrepresent the blessed Luther, as has been demonstrated by the blessed Gerhard, on the Political Magistrate § 125. The matter is manifest: For there would be nothing exceptional, to use the words of Grotius, in it, if only a bare custom, even if it brings with it an obligation of not resisting, were indicated by that word, because they knew that such injuries were also inflicted by unjust judges and praetors, which did not import an obligation of not resisting. Then indeed the name משפט in a more famous meaning introduces true right from שפט, he judged. Nor is it indeed related, when the people demanded a King, that God wished to answer them concerning the custom not of Kings, but of Tyrants, or by assenting to the demands for appointing a King, had only indicated the abuse of royal dignity, but had signified nothing at all concerning the use of the same and legitimate power, and the proper and true right of the King. Furthermore, if all those things which are recounted there in that משפט are attended to, there is nothing unjust in them, so far is it from the case that the משפט itself ought to be considered unjust. For what is unjust in it, if the King, when the condition and majesty of his state, or the very necessity of the Republic urges, takes some of his subjects, and puts them in his chariots, and makes for himself horsemen, and precursors of his chariots; if he appoints for himself Tribunes, and Centurions, and plowmen of his fields, and Reapers of his harvests, and smiths of arms, and of his chariots: If he also makes their daughters for himself perfumers and cooks, and bakers. What is unjust, if he takes the best fields and vineyards and olive groves of his subjects in a case of necessity, and destines them for his servants keeping watch for the safety of the Republic? The King certainly needs many men, who sees with others' eyes, labors with others' hands, runs with others' feet; And those who are designated here are all necessary to Kings: As, for instance, satellites, or bodyguards, who may be present at home for protection, and accompany him abroad for the sake of public dignity. Court ministers, who serve partly in the bedchamber, partly at the table, for which end Maimonides observes that the best youths are selected, who are most highly commended for the beauty of body and mind. Furthermore, bakers and cooks are also required for the sustenance of life: likewise smiths and artisans, if it is necessary to build anything; and farmers and vintners, and shepherds, for the economy; Captains, Centurions, etc., are required for the sake of public security. Nor is this to be understood as an acceptance which is done through force or plunder, or fraud and deceit: since the goods of subjects can be taken with consent, and on the condition of compensation. The King uses the service of free men, if any wish to devote their effort for wages, or the hope of favor, with the consent of their parents or those whose interest it is, according to Maimonides; and that is all that is granted to him here. Nor is it a matter of that acceptance which is done only for the sake of one's own advantage, increasing one's wealth, or one's treasury, but which yields to the use and necessity of the republic. The acceptance of tithes also is no more must be considered unjust, than the exaction of tributes, which the Magistrate claims for himself by divine right Rom. 13, 2. And lest any doubt remain that the true Royal right is sanctioned here, it is not only signified in this place that the people submitted themselves to this form of government, with that burden also in verses 19 and 20, and that God accepted that submission: and under this condition contracted with the same, and by that Law set a King over them in verse 22. But that Royal right also had to be recorded there by divine command, and preserved in the archives like some sacred deposit: chap. 10, 25, not only for terror, but also for the perpetual preservation of the notice of the obligation of the subjects.

Nor is there anything contrary to this משפט in the right described in Deut. 17. The excessive multiplication of horses there is forbidden for the purpose that the King might not lead the people back into Egypt, supported by the number of cavalry; then that he might not covet weights of silver and gold, through avarice and rapacity; and that he might not be lifted up above his brothers through pride: which are by no means granted here. And everyone sees that those passages are disparate: for in Moses the office of the King is handed down; here, however, that of the subjects; there the manner of commanding is described, here the necessity of obeying; therefore, even if certain things were listed here which were not permitted to the King (which we do not in fact concede), it is nevertheless taught that it is not permitted for subjects to resist them, but that they must be obeyed.

But what is held in verse 18 of this our passage concerning the cry to the Lord does not precisely regard the injuries of future Kings, but only the worse state of the people, as they were by no means accustomed to such things, and who under the Theocracy could enjoy a far more serene liberty; and even if it did regard injuries, they are not, however, inflicted by virtue of this משפט, but from the abuse of power and Royal right, and thus de facto. Therefore, it can be said that a twofold argument of dissuasion is employed by the Lord; the one from the Royal right, which would be unaccustomed to them, and thus comparatively harsh, with respect to that golden liberty which they enjoyed; the other from the abuse of that right, that they are not to be heard even then, if Kings should oppress them beyond what is right, and should be more unjust, because once, having rejected God and His government, they sought another King, and even a crooked one must be obeyed, into whose rule one has been brought, let alone one whom he himself sought, or to whom he knowingly and prudently consented, 1. Petr. 2, 18. But it is no wonder that Grotius here interprets משפט as a usurpatory right, and as a Tyrannical custom, since he extends it greatly; this Royal dominion, he says in the annotations to this place, carried with it that Kings could make levies at their own discretion, impose poll taxes and labors on men, tributes on fields, and customs on merchandise, with no one contradicting. For that saying had a place there: I am a King, I seek nothing beyond a commoner. And to do anything with impunity, that is to be a King. These are the words of Grotius. But where will it be proven that all those things are contained in this Royal right according to the mind of God, the condition of the one proposing, or the people receiving? These things are not permitted entirely to the private will and lust of Kings, but are indulged for the necessity and safety of the Republic, from which a measure and determination ought to be established for them: Nor is such an excess or extension of power, going beyond the measure of legitimate government, granted; But power is restrained within the bounds of justice and equity, so that the government may be conducted in the fear of the Lord, and all things directed to the glory of God and the safety of the Republic, which are the supreme laws. Who will admit that God indulges a King, either here or elsewhere, to do anything and whatever his mind pleases, and that in this authentic document, by which the Israelite Kings were to be established on the Royal throne, and which therefore had to be kept in the archives, He defined a King thus: to do anything with impunity, that is to be a King. My venerable father-in-law, Dr. Hülsemann, has solidly and accurately asserted this right after our blessed Gerhard in his Extensio Breviar. Theolog. chap. 20. §. 12, as has also Dr. Wandelinus, now Archbishop of the Danes, a friend to be singularly honored, in his learned books published on Royal Right. We certainly see no reason why we should side here with the Jews R. Judah and Levi Gerson, the Calvinists, Pezel, Zepper, Toussain, Calvin himself, and the Papists, Becanus, Adam à Conzen, and others, and interpret the passage as concerning a usurped right. For we think that what Wilhelm Schickardus argues at length concerning Royal right can be settled without difficulty from what we have said. Our Hebrews too easily place faith in the Rabbis who extend their fringes everywhere; hence it is no wonder that men otherwise learned are led away from the genuine sense of scripture.

The principal argument of the opposing party may seem to be that tithes were of divine institution for sacred persons: from which, however, R. Moses Maimonides asserts that political persons were not entirely excluded. And although the King's tithes are not mentioned elsewhere, yet Kings are never read to be excluded from them, and it is not necessary that the word for tithes here be taken strictly as a tenth part, since the species of tribute can be understood as placed for the genus.

Latin:

HOC ERIT JUS REGIS) De significatu vocis משפט hoc loco vide quæ dicta de jure belli ac pacis l. 1. c. 4. §. 7. Summam eorum quæ sequuntur, explicat Josephus, dicens fore, ut Rex eos tractet tanquam pretio emtos servos. Vi- cini enim Reges subditis suis imperabant quæ vellent, ut ἀνυπεύθυνοι. Syros servituti natos ait Livius: de libertate eos nihil cogitare Apollonius: manus patientes esse Julia- nus, ut ostendimus ad cap. 4. §. 20. l. 1. de Jure Belli & Pacis. Ideoque subditi passim in his libris servi Regum dicuntur. Dominatus autem hic regius secum ferebat, ut pro arbitrio reges delectus facerent, capitationes & operas, hominibus, tri- buta agris, mercibus vectigalia imponerent, contradicente nemine. Illud enim ibi locum habebat, Rex sum, nil ultra quæro plebejus. Et impune quidvis facere, id est regem esse. Si peccarent graviter in Dei legem, ad Deum ultio pertinebat, non ad singulos, ac ne ad populum quidem. Vide quæ se- quuntur: & infra 26, 10. 23.

Non explicatam invenio vocem istam loco lau- dato. Nihil aliud ibi, quod ad rem præsentem fa- ciat, habetur, quam quod notet, primos homines non Dei præcepto, sed sponte adductos experimento infirmitatis familiarum seu gregum adversus violen- tiam in societatem civilem coiisse, unde ortum habeat potestas civilis, eamque ideo humanam ordinationem vocari 1. Petr. 2, 13. Quanquam alibi divina ordi- natio vocetur, quia hominum salubre institutum De- us probavit. Quæ calculum non merentur: quia novimus quidem Magistratum ἀνθρωπίνην κτίσιν di- ci, ratione causæ instrumentalis & mediæ, quod per homines ordinatus sit, ratione subjecti, quod ab hominibus administretur, ratione modi, quod hu- mano modo, ratione finis, quod in hominum utili- tatem: non tamen probari potest, quod ita dica- tur ratione principii, quod inventum humanum sit; siquidem Deus immediate statum Politicum insti- tuerat, æque ut reliquos status, Ecclesiasticum & Oeconomicum: Proverb. 8, 15. 16. Daniel. 2, 37. 44. Sap. 6, 4. 5. Syrac. 17, 13. 14. Rom. 13, 2. Sed in eodem capite §. 3. Grotium tangere hoc jus Regis obser- vo: Quod vero apud Samuelem est de jure Regis, omnino recte inspicienti apparet, nec de JURE VE- RO intelligendum, id est, de facultate honeste & juste aliquid agendi (longe autem alia vivendi ratio præ- scribitur Regi in ea parte legis, quæ est de officio Regis Deuter. 17, 14.) neque nudum factum indicare; nihil enim esset in eo eximium, cum injurias facere & pri- vati privatis soleant: Sed factum, quod effectum ali- quem juris habeat, id est, non rescindendi obligatio- nem. Ideo additur: populum pressum istis injuriis Dei opem imploraturum, quia scil. humana remedia nulla exstarent. Sic ergo hoc jus vocatur, quomodo prætor jus reddere dicitur, etiam cum inique decerni- tur, l. jus pluribus, d. de justit. & jure. Hæc ibidem Grot. De Tyrannico ergo dominio cum injuriis con- juncto vel iniquo explicat vocem משפט non de jure Regio divinitus concesso : Sequutus Pontificios plerosque Estium, Tirinum & alios, quibuscum fa- ciunt & Calvinistæ nonnulli & Photiniani. Cæte- rum Nostri plerique omnes, jus hoc Regis non iniquum aut usurpativum, sed à Deo indultum, & tale esse, quo Magistratus urgente necessitate, salva conscientia uti queat, solide evicere. Qui hic in alia forte eunt, B. Lutherum temere deferunt, uti à B. Gerhardo demonstratum, de Magistratu Polit. §. 125. Res manifesta est : Nihil enim eximium, ut Grotii verbis utar, in eo esset, si nuda tantum con- suetudo, etsi obligationem non resistendi inferens, vo- ce illa indicaretur, quia injurias tales inferri etiam ab iniquis judicibus & prætoribus noverant, qua- les non resistendi obligationem importabant. Tum vero nomen משפט famosiori significatu jus verum infert à שפט judicavit.
