Those things which follow explain it, namely by raising up a seed for him, after he shall have completed his days, and by establishing his kingdom for him: which would build a house for the divine name in such a way that, by that covenant, the house of David himself might be built, and his Kingdom be established. For the house which his seed, to be raised up AFTER his death, the Messiah, was to build, is a spiritual House, of which He Himself is the foundation Ef. 28, 16. and upon which the faithful are built up through faith Ephes. 2, 16. 1 Pet. 2, 6. whence Holy Scripture introduces Him as the builder of this house Zach. 6, 12. 13. and Christ Himself professed that He wishes to build and construct this house of the living God, the Church (1 Tim. 3, 15) Matthew 16, 18. The Kingdom, which was to be established for David by virtue of this promise, had to endure forever, and therefore it is not a terrestrial, but a spiritual kingdom 2 Sam. 7, 16. That faithful, or rather immovable, house and eternal kingdom is therefore the very house of God and Kingdom of God, so that these are not different, but mutually declare one another: The Lord will make a house for David; and the seed of David will build a house for my name. Thus the house of David will be constant, or his Kingdom even unto eternity: And I will establish his Kingdom (the seed of David's) and I will settle the throne of the kingdom of the seed, or of the Davidic sprout, unto eternity: whence it is manifest: That in those words, the Lord foretells to you that the Lord will make a house for you; the Lord (God the Father) foretells that the Lord (God the Son, because the Lord speaks of the Lord) will make a house for you, is contained the proposition and the sum of those things which follow, and that by the subsequent words that proposition is explained and everything is set forth more fully. Nor can there be any doubt any longer that all those things are to be understood of the Messiah.

The other thing which is objected is that it treats here of such a person who could sin: If he shall have done anything iniquitously, I will rebuke him with the rod of men and with the stripes of the sons of men. Which cannot be understood of the Messiah; but that is easily resolved. For if you take that concerning His own person, as the words themselves suggest, although Christ by Himself was subject to no sin, yet He took upon Himself the sins of the sons of men, or of mortals, and although He Himself knew no sin, He willed to be made sin for us 2 Cor. 5, 21, and God cast upon Him all our iniquities Isaiah 53, 5. Whence Holy Scripture, to teach how truly our sins were imputed to Him in the Judgment of God, and how truly He took our iniquities upon Himself, was accustomed to speak of Him as if He Himself had sinned or had done anything iniquitously. Which is not only done here, but is also found elsewhere in the prophecies concerning the Messiah: My iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see, they are multiplied above the hairs of my head, says the Messiah Himself Psalm 40, 13, speaking of the sins cast upon Him no otherwise than of His own sins. Nor did He speak otherwise of the same in Ps. 31, 15. My strength has failed because of MY INIQUITY, or Psalm 69, 6. O God, YOU KNOW my foolishness, and MY FAULTS are not hidden from you. For He wished to testify that He had most truly taken those upon Himself, and was most grievously anguished and afflicted on account of them, that He felt the burden of them and sustained their punishments, as our surety, sponsor, and mediator, who laid down His soul for us and for our sins. Therefore, just as our iniquities are not only called His iniquities, but are also truly reckoned as such in the Judgment of God, so also the rod and the stripes, which were hanging over the sons of men on account of those iniquities, are foretold to be most truly and realistically endured by Him. So that the prophecy here is simultaneously presented as passional; concerning the satisfactory and meritorious passion of the Messiah. For the rod of men, of miserable and mortal beings (such as we all are through the fall and after the fall) and the stripes of the sons of Adam are the afflictions and punishments which we have deserved, and to which all the Sons of Adam are subject, which He sustained for us; Whence Isaiah 53, in which place they are more fully explained, He Himself is called stricken by the same word which occurs here concerning the stripes of the Sons of Adam. Which the opposite promise also confirms, I will not take away my mercy from him, by which it is taught that the Messiah is not to be utterly abandoned in those stripes, just as the impious Saul was abandoned and removed from the face of the Lord finally and unto eternity: But that the mercy of liberation from those punishments and of elevation to an eternal Kingdom would be exhibited to Him: which mercies of God we previously observed were understood by David in Psalm 16 concerning the resuscitation of Christ to an eternal empire, and explained in the New Testament by the Holy Apostles, Peter in Acts 2 and Paul in Acts 13. The rod of this antithesis, those stripes concerning death, from which He was resuscitated, concerning hell, from which the Messiah was liberated, so that His soul might not be left in Hell, and His flesh might not see corruption, and so that, triumphing over hell and death in soul and flesh, He might reign forever, are to be explained.

But it is no wonder that in Psalm 89, 31 ff. these things are prolixly transferred to the sons of the Messiah concerning transgressions and punishments: but if his sons shall have forsaken my Law, and shall not have walked in my judgments, if they shall have profaned my righteousnesses, and shall not have kept my commandments, I will visit their iniquities with a rod and their sins with stripes: Since even Christ Himself concludes thus in Luke 23, 31. If they do these things in the green wood, what will be done in the dry? By these things, however, the sacred singer wished to teach that, although our iniquities were transferred to the Messiah by virtue of the promise made to him, and he was afflicted with stripes on account of the same, and sustained the punishments for them, it is nevertheless not permitted for his children to sin with impunity and to transgress the law of God, but that God will also visit their iniquities and sins: Therefore, the Messiah is to be received by faith in such a way that we do not abuse divine grace for sins, but that the χάρις σωτήριος παιδεύουσα ἡμᾶς may recall us from impiety Tit. 2, 12. St. Augustine, book 17 of The City of God, ch. 9, wishes it to be said of Christ, which is to be understood of his body; because he himself is the head, and appropriates to himself those things which happen to the body Acts 9, 5. But that explanation is more elegant, by which the seed of Christ is transferred to the faithful Is. 53, 11. Ps. 89, 31 [20, 31]. And so his spiritual children are said to have transferred to them those things which were said of Christ in the very original promise κατὰ διάνοιαν, and by arguing from the lesser to the greater, that since our or others' iniquities were so punished in Christ, in his children, if they have failed by prevaricating, their own iniquities are to be punished much more. Where, however, it deserves observation that David immediately returns to the promise concerning the Messiah: But I will not scatter my mercy FROM HIM, nor will I harm in my truth. He does not say FROM THEM, namely his children, but FROM HIM; so that he may signify that the promised grace is to be granted first to the Messiah himself, for which he himself anxiously panted in his stripes Ps. 31, 10. Ps. 40, 12. 13. 14. Ps. 69, 1. 14. 17. having been heard by God Is. 49, 8. Heb. 5, 7. then indeed, on account of the Messiah, also to his children who are doing penance, and to the Church, or the kingdom of the Messiah, so that they may not be cast away, and his kingdom may remain stable. Therefore he adds, nor will I profane my covenant, and the things that proceed from my lips, I will not make void. Once have I sworn in my holiness, if I lie unto David, his seed shall endure for ever: and his throne as the Sun before me, and as the moon perfect for ever, and a faithful witness in heaven.

The third thing that can be objected to our opinion is that 1 Chron. 22, 9. this promise is explained concerning Solomon by David: and also by Solomon himself 1 Kings 5, 5. chap. 8, 17. seqq. 2 Chron. 6, 7. But we deny that these passages refer to the promise made here 2 Sam. 7. or are parallel to this oracle, concerning which we have already warned above. That promise 1 Chron. 22, 9. which the other passages refer to, was later in time than this one of ours, which is repeated in the books of Chronicles 1 Chron. 17, 11. seqq. The former is about a son to be born to David: the latter is about a seed to be raised up long after the death of David: The former deals with a material house and the Jerusalem Temple: The latter deals with a spiritual house and an eternal kingdom: There the promise was made with a condition, and was Legal, if Solomon should keep the law of the Lord: Here it is without condition and simple: so that even if he should act wickedly, he is indeed to be rebuked with the stripes of the sons of men, but the mercy of the Lord is nevertheless not to be taken away from him. See B. Luther, Vol. 8, Jena, German, 'On the Jews and Their Lies'.

Latin:

IPSE ÆDIFICABIT DOMVM NOMINI MEO) Pax sacris aptior. 1. Par. 22, 8.

ET STABILIAM THRONVM REGNI EJVS VS- QVE IN SEMPITERNVM) עד־עולם apud He- bræos tempus non infinitum, sed pro materia, de qua agitur, bene longum significat. Itaque in possessionibus privatis ad 50. annos porrigitur, in regnis longius. Duravit autem in posteritate Davidis regnum per annos plus quingentos suc- cessorum serie ultra viginti: quod satis rarum.

SUscitare de utero semen, ubi sit in solio collocare in Scripturis non invenio; ac ne quidem, ubi semen suscitare? Hoc vero communiter de procreatio- ne, vel conceptione prolis accipi notissimum est, & quum addatur illud de utero tuo, tanto manifestius redditur, non de collocatione in throno, sed de excita- tione seminis è lumbis Davidis, vel è visceribus ejus, uti vocem Ebræam Montanus interpretatur, pro- missionem dari. Illud vero de utero tuo, cur red- dendum de uxore tua? Cur non accipiendum de Davide ipso, uti sonat? Num uxor mariti est uterus ejusdem, & ubi ita indigitatur in Sacris Literis? Lo- cum enim similem nullum invenit Grotius. Aut cur non Tertulliani explicationi locus relinquen- dus? quæ ex collatione Psal. 131. Matris Messiæ vir- ginitatem in hac phrasi indagat l. 3. c. Marcion. c. 20. Atqui hinc magis Christum intelligere debebis ex Da- vid deputatum carnali genere ob Mariæ virginis cen- sum. De hoc enim promisso juratur in Psalmo ad Da- vid: Ex fructu ventris tui collocabo super Thronum tuum. Quis iste venter est? Ipsius David? utiq; non. Neq; enim pariturus esset David. Sed nec uxoris ejus. Non enim dixisset, ex fructu ventris tui, sed potius ex fructu ventris uxoris tuæ. Ipsius ergo dicendo ven- trem, superest, ut aliquem de genere ejus ostenderit, cujus ventris futurus esset fructus caro Christi, quæ ex utero Mariæ floruit. Ideoque & fructum ventris tantum nominavit, ut propriè ventris, quasi solius ventris, non etiam viri: Et ipsum ventrem ad Da- vid redegit, ad principem generis & familiæ patrem. Nam quia viro deputare non poterat virginis eum ventrem, patri deputavit. Itaque in Christo nova dis- positio invenitur hodie: Hæc erat quam tunc creator pollicebatur, religiosa & fidelia David appellans, quæ erant Christi, quia Christus ex David: immo ipsa e- rit caro ejus, religiosa & fidelia David tam sancta relligione, & fidelis ex resurrectione. Nam & Nathan Propheta in secundo Basiliarum, professionem ad Da- vit facit: Semen tuum quod erit, inquit, ex ventre tuo. Hoc si in Salomonem simpliciter edisseres, risum mihi incuties, videbitur enim David peperisse Salo- monem. An & hic Christus significatur, ex eo ventre semen David, qui esset ex David, id est, Mariæ? Sed placuit Grotio ista glossa, ne oraculum divinum de Messia acciperetur, utpote qui è Bathseba, uxore Davidis, semen ejus haberi non potest. Totam e- nim promissionem cum Judæis ad Salomonem de- torquet. Quæ vero illustrissimum vaticinium con- tinet de Messia. (1.) Quia agitur hîc de semine exci- tando de utero, vel lumbis Davidis, ut alias Scriptu- ra loquitur, post Davidis tempora. Non ergo de Salomone, qui post Davidem fato functum non est natus, imo nec post ejus fata in Solio ejus collo- catus, sed ipso adhuc vivente, ac mandante. Nec se- dit in solio Davidis post ipsum, sed ante faciem ipsius & loco ipsius, ut habetur 1. Reg. 1, 30. seqq. Neq; (2.) Salomoni thronus regni ejus in seculum stabilitus est: Sed Messiæ. Quia regnum Salomonis in æternum durasse dici non potest, quoad ad ipsum Salomonem, ac ne quidem, quod Filios ejusdem: quia regnum Israelis mox in filio ejus ita fuit discerptum, ut non medium Regnum, nec tertia ejus pars, sed ne quar- ta quidem ipsi remanserit. Salomo filium Regem re- liquit ex sextante, inquit Grotius præfatione ad lib. 3. Reg. Bipartito regno videbis Israelis Reges omnes malos, Judæ Reges malos aliquot, mediocres satis mul- tos; bonos tot, quot facile in annulo inscribi possent. Tum vero nec in posteritatis Davidicæ regno figi potest duratio illa עד עולם. Non enim usque a- deo rarum hoc est, per quingentos annos durare regnum alicujus familiæ, quæ periodus multarum fuit familiarum: Hic autem aliquid prorsus fin- gulare & eximium promitti certum est, & indu- bium penes omnes. Adhæc non agitur hîc de posteritate Davidis universa, sed de semine mona- dico: non de seminibus ut pluribus, sed de semi- ne ut uno, quæ accurate distinguere docuit in ta- libus oraculis Apostolus Galat. 3, 16. De per- sona una agitur, uti cumprimis è verbis subjun- dis patet, IPSE ædificabit domum nomini meo. Hæc enim individuum designant, non totam fami- liam. Illi ergo personæ thronus regni stabiliendus promittitur, usque in sempiternum, non vero uni- versæ familiæ. Pronomen illud הוּא de semine u- surpatum Davidis, remittit nos haud obscure ad הוּא illud Prot-Evangelii Genes. 3, 15. de semine Evæ ibi promisso: ut id jam ad familiam Davidis hoc oraculo restringi intelligamus, quod ante, per promissiones Abrahæ, Isaaco, Jacobo, de semine ipso- rum datas ad Abraham, Isaacum, Jacobum, & per oraculum Jacobæum Genes. 49, 10. ad tribum Juda restrictum erat. Ideoque manet integra vis verbis עַד־עוֹלָם usq; in sempiternum, ut proprie dicta æter- nitas designetur, è significatu vocum maxime pro- prio, non tantum in tempus longum; Siquidem non semel, sed iterum atque iterum de regno fir- mando promissio facta v. 12. 13. 16. & de æterna du- ratione ejusdem tribus vicibus repetatur v. 13. & 16. ut & 1. Par. 18, 12. 14. imo protestetur Deus, se nol- le misericordiam suam ab illo tollere 2. Sam. 7, 15. Adde, quod de hoc regno & throno David ipse cecinerit, quod in æternitatem omnem durare debeat Ps. 45, 7. Ps. 72, 7. 17. Ps. 89, 30. 37. & Esaias teste- tur, quod regnum ejus vere æternum sit, neque fi- nis ejus ullus futurus cap. 9, 6. Multiplicabitur ejus im- perium, & pacis non erit finis: super solium David, & super regnum ejus sedebit, ut confortet illud, & corroboret in judicio, & justitia à modo, & usque in sempiternum. Quæ etiam Angeli Gabrielis expli- catio est Luc. 1, 32. Dabit illi Dominus Deus sedem David Patris ejus, & regnabit in Domo Jacob in æ- ternum, & Regni ejus non erit finis. Hæ interpreta- tiones oraculi de semine, vel filio Davidis, & Re- gno ejus æterno, omni exceptione superiores, præ- ferendæ utique erant commentis & somniis Rab- binicis.

Porro (3) quod ædificaturus hic Filius Davi- dis dicitur domum nomini Domini, non de templo materiali Salomonæo, etsi occasione destinatæ ex- structionis templi dictum, accipiendum est, sed de Domo spirituali, Ecclesia Dei, quæ domus est Dei vi- ventis 1. Tim. 3, 15. Quia domus nomini Dei ædifi- canda non minus æternum durare debebat, quam Regnum hujus seminis, à quo illa ædificanda. Ideo enim promittitur illi regnum æternum, non quia domum iterum devastandam, & incendio peritu- ram, sed quia æternam domum Domini nomini æ- dificaturus erat. Quod de alio, quam Messia intel- ligi non potest. Conferri etiam hic accurate de- bent verba 2. Sam. 7, 16. cum 1. Par. 18, 14. Quod ibi dicitur; Fidelis vel firma erit domus tua & re- gnum tuum usque in æternum ante faciem tuam, & thronus tuus erit firmus jugiter: Id hic ita effertur; Statuam eam in domo mea, & in regno meo, & thro- nus ejus erit firmissimus in perpetuum. Domus ergo Domini, & regnum Domini, ac domus Davidis & regnum ejus permutantur. Firma est domus Davi- dis, & semen ejus statuetur in domo Domini; firmum est regnum Davidis, & semen ejus statuetur in regno Domini, sese mutuo explicant. Non ergo de domo & familia Davidica in æternum stabilienda, sed de spirituali domo & regno Davidis, quæ est Ecclesia, domus Domini & regnum ejus, agitur. In qua domo regnat Messias; ideo domus illa est firmissima. In domo certe materiali, templo Salomonæo, non de- buit statui semen Davidis, nec firma erat illa do- mus, nec illa erat ipsum regnum Domini.

Locus ille, quem ut parallelum confert Gro- tius 1. Par. 22, 9. parallelus hic non est: Quod jam pridem solide demonstravit Beat. Lutherus noster Tom. 8. Jen. German. fol. 69. & seqq. & agnoscit

Cajetanus atque Sanctius. Agit de plane alia appari- tione: qua Deus Davidi ob multum effusum sangui- nem, non concedebat domus suae aedificationem: & promittebat nativitatem filii pacifici Salomonis, qui per totam vitam pace & tranquillitate fruitu- rus, & divino nomini templum extructurus sit: De quibus in hoc Dei responso per Nathanem Davidi facto nihil plane habetur. Longe vero alia in hac manifestatione tradi, αὐτοψία docet: In qua Deus protestatur, se nunquam postulasse domus Cedrinae aedificationem: & promittit Davidi, se domum ejus aedificare velle, & firmam futuram ipsius domum, & thronum ejus in aeternum duraturum. Prior est pro- missio gratiae, & sine conditione facta de Messia 2. Sam. 7. Posterior est promissio legalis, cum conditione probitatis Salomonis. Nec enim de Salomone in priori, sed de semine Davidis post fata ejus ipsi ex- citando, h. e. Messia agitur, ejusque throno & re- gno sempiterno.

(4) Quod utut hactenus abunde ostensum, in- super confirmari potest ex splendidissima illa pro- missione: Ego ero ei in Patrem, & ipse erit mihi in Filium. Haec enim tanta est, ut nemini mortalium, ac ne Angelorum quidem ulli eam dictam Paulus doceat: utpote quae Filium Dei ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτῆρα τῆς ὑποστάσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ ex- primat Ebr. 1, 6. Quam cum illo Davidico Ps. 2, 7. Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te, conjunxit Apo- stolus ad aeternam Deitatem Filii Dei demonstran- dam, penes ipsos Ebraeos, utpote penes quos illud negari non poterat, sicuti omnis disputatio è con- cessis & communibus procedere debet principiis. Quid quod & David ipse hanc promissionem difer- tissime de Messia explicavit Psal. 89. de aeterna gratia Dei exortitura v. 3. de semine Davidis (spirituali) aeter- no, & de throno ejus perpetuo vers. 5. de manu ejus in mari, & dextra in fluminibus ponenda v. 25. de ex- altando eodem ceu primogenito supra omnes Reges terrae v. 28. de semine aeterno ipsi donando, & de thro- no ejus conservando, dum dies caeli, dum Sol & Luna erit, imo in aeternum v. 30. 37. 38. de illo UNCTO, absque quo si esset, omnes homines frustra conditi essent, cujus vestigia opprobrio sunt hostibus Ec- clesiae v. 48. 51. 52. Quae aliter quam de Messia expli- cari non possunt. Nisi enim esset unus Filius homi- nis substantia Israel, inquit Augustinus lib. 17. de C, D. cap. 11. per quem Filium hominis liberarentur multi filii hominum, in vanum utique constituti essent omnes filii hominum.

(5) Nec praetereundum hic est responsum Da- vidis 2. Sam. 7, 20. 21. & 1. Paral. 17, 17. 18. quae de Messia promissionem hic factam esse, haud obscu- re docet. Quia tanti eam facit David, ut caetera o- mnia, & quod ipse è domo exigua tantopere exal- tatus fuit, exiguo loco habenda censeat, si compa- rentur cum illis, quae hic Deus ipsi loquutus erat de Domo ejus. (Ad quae verba Junius fatetur de semine olim venturo Christo hic agi, nec posse ea solum ad Sa- lomonem referri.) Et promissionem istam למרחוק in longinquum, vel in longe post futura secula respice- re à Spiritu Christi scrutante in tempora N. T. teste Petro 1. Epist. 3. edoctus, docet: ac propterea ad- dit: haec est Lex hominis, qui est Dominus Deus: designans Christum Θεάνθρωπον; quem & verbum Domini & servum Domini vocat, ut ejus cum divi- nam, tum humanam naturam exprimat, ut è se- quentibus patebit.

Porro (6) quum negari non possit in aliis Scri- pturae oraculis respici ad promissionem Messiae Da- vidi factam Psal. 2, 7. Ps. 72. 7. seqq. Ps. 89, 50. Es. 9, 6. 7. Jer. 23, 5. c. 33, 15. 16. Unde etiam Ps. 81, 11. com- memorantur misericordiae Davidis, (vel Davidi promissa) fideles & constantes Es. 55, 3. (qui locus de Messia aperte agit, Conf. v. 1. 2. 4. 5. Act. 13, 34.) fateri omnino oportet, hic ipsi promissionem factam! siquidem aliud oraculum, quod ista loca designent, non inveniatur. Quo facit, quod Act. 2, 31. innuatur, Davidem vi hujus promissionis de Regno Messiæ æterno, de resurrectione Messiæ palam vaticinatum esse Ps. 16. Propheta igitur cum esset, & sciret, quia jurejurando jurasset illi Deus, de fructu lumbi ejus sedere super sedem ejus, (quod nisi hic factum, ubi tandem factum est?) providens locutus est de resurrectione Christi, quia neque derelictus est in inferno, neq; caro ejus vidit corruptionem. Quæ etiam vis & δείνότης est argumenti Pauli, è fidelibus sanctis (Davidi promissis) de regno Messiæ æterno concludentis, Messiam non debuisse in morte manere, sed resurgere Actor. 13, 34. Quod autem suscitavit eum à mortuis amplius non reversurum in corruptionem, ita dixit; Quia dabit vobis sancta David fidelia, Es. 55. 2. Sam. 7. promissa. Ideoque & alias dicit: Non dabis Sanctum tuum videre corruptionem.

Addimus his tandem (7) suffragia & consensum Interpp. Cum Christianorum Tertull. l. c. Lactantii lib. 4. c. 13. Augustini, Eucherii item, Ruperti in h. l. Lyrani, Burgensis, Abulensis, Angelomi, Catharini, Sanctii, Cornelii a Lap. Estii, & aliorum Pontificiorum: Nec non e nostris B. Lutheri, Hunnii, Gerhardi, Crameri, Helvici, Waltheri, Mülleri, Glassii, Vinariensium Theologorum, & cæterorum omnium, denique Calvinianorum etiam plerorumque, Junii, Piscatoris, Parei, Auctorum Notar. Belgic. &c. Tum veterum Ebræorum quoque, qui etiam agnovere, in hoc oraculo promissionem de Messia exhiberi, à quibus omnibus hic sese in gratiam nonnullorum recentiorum Judæorum separat Grotius, totum oraculum ad Salomonem, imo etiam ad Successores ejus detorquens. Fatentur sane Judæi, Davidi promissionem factam esse de Messia. At si ea hic facta non sit eidem, quem alium ex Historia Davidica locum designabunt, ubi ea facta sit? Ideo Rabbi Lusitanus in colloquio Mittelburgensi fassus est, quod hic Davidi promissus fuerit Messias. De Judæis observat August. lib. 17. de C. D. c. 8. quod & ipsissilium hic promissum intelligant non fuisse Salomonem. Ut hic proinde magis cæcutiat Grotius, quam Judæi isti. Lubet solum locum Tertulliani adscribere è lib. 3. c. Marc. c. 20. qui variis argumentis probat de Christo hic sermonem esse. Primum ab utero Davidis ex occasione supra adductum fuit integrum. Sequuntur nunc alia, quæ ibidem addit; Quia & ædem Dei, inquit, magis Christus ædificaturus esset, hominem scil. sanctum, in quo potiore templo inhabitaret Dei Spiritus, in Dei filium magis Christus habendus esset, quam Salomon Filius David. Denique & Thronus in ævum, & regnum in ævum magis Christo competit, quam Salomoni, temporali st. Regi. Sed à Christo misericordia Dei non abscessit. Salomoni vero etiam ira Dei accessit post luxuriam & Idololatriam. Suscitavit enim illi Satan, id est, hostem Idumæum. Quum ergo nihil horum competat in Salomonem, sed in Christum, certa erit ratio interpretationum nostrarum, ipso etiam exitu rerum probante, quas in Christum apparet prædicatas, & ita in hoc erunt sancta & fidelia David. Hunc Deus testimonium nationibus posuit, non David Principem & imperantem nationibus, non David, qui soli Israeli imperavit. Christum hodie invocant Nationes, quæ eum non sciebant, & populi ad Christum hodie confugiunt, quem retro ignorabant. Non potest futurum dici, quod vides fieri.

Non dissimulandum quidem, quod Interpretes nonnulli locum præsentem etiam de Salomone ex- plicent, quod quoad nonnulla prædicata de ipso secundum literam accipi debeat, sed id secus aliis videtur, qui nobiscum locum integrum de Christo, quantum ad sensum literalem, interpretantur, uti Glossæ auctor, Angelomus, B. Luther. & c. Coccejus in ult. Mos. §. 989. ita de hoc vaticinio habet: Promittitur Davidi semen 1. omnes peccatores gratia Dei participes. 2. Hæres regni secundum modum carnalem, qui ædificet templum, & cujus regnum duret omni tempore Pædagogiæ legalis sub conditione observantiæ. 3. Semen quod habeat revera regnum æternum, & quod ædificet domum Deo spiritualem, & semper stet coram Deo in domo ipsius, quod est cælum, & sit Rex in regno Dei. Sed tertia explicatio solum congruit; priores duæ alienæ sunt, nec simul triplex sensus in uno & eodem loco obtinere potest. Si semen Davidi hic promissum Christus est, non potest esse Salomo, non omnes peccatores gratiæ Dei participes. Si domus ædificanda domus spiritualis est, per eam intelligi templum materiale nequit. Cæterum si à Judæis perduellibus Messiæ abeas, non invenietur facile, qui de Salomone solo hoc oraculum, cum Grotio, accipiat, qui hic prorsus tacuit de Messia, eique nullum in eodem reliquit locum. Pleriq; agnoscunt, nonnulla tantum prædicata de Christo ἐξ ἀνάγκης explicanda esse; nec aliter secundum literam intelligi posse. Cornel à Lapide, penes Papistas, de fide est, inquit, locum intelligi de Christo. Junius in Calvini Schola non postremus interpres, de illo, solium Tuum erit stabile USQVE IN SECULUM v. 16. hoc, inquit; & consequentia omnia proprie non nisi Christo competere possunt. Sic etiam Belgici Interpp. hæc oportet nos proprie intelligere de regno Christi spirituali æterno. Alii totum locum de Salomone quidem suo modo explicari posse, sed quum nonnulla plene ac integre nonnisi Christo conveniant, prouti δείνότης oraculi infert, quædam dici de Salomone per se, quædam vero, uti erat Typus Christi, cum Augustino lib. 17. de Civ. Dei c. 8. & 9. existimant, vel de Salomone secundum sensum literalem interpretantur, ita tamen, ut Spiritus S. etiam sensum mysticum intenderit, imo præcipue hic Christum, cujus typus erat Salomo, respexerit. Hanc tam grandem promissionem, inquit August. qui putat in Salomone fuisse completam, multum errat. Attendit enim, quod dictum est: Hic ædificabit mihi domum: Quoniam Salomon templum illud nobile struxit: & non attendit, fidelis erit domus ejus usque in æternum coramme. Facta est quidem nonnulla imago rei futuræ etiam in Salomone, in eo, quod templum ædificavit, & pacem habuit secundum nomen suum, & in exordia regni sui mirabiliter laudabilis fuit; Sed eadem sua persona, quæ umbram futuram prenunciabat, etiam ipse Christum Dominum nostrum exhibebat. Unde quædam de illo ita scripta sunt, quasi de ipso ita prædicta sint, dum Scriptura Sacra etiam rebus gestis prophetans quodammodo in eo figuram delineat futurorum.

Præcipua, quæ nostræ sententiæ opponuntur, quod hic non possint omnia de Messia explicari, hæc videntur. Primum, quod de illius templi ædificatione sine dubio agatur in responso Divino, de quo in Davidis consilio actum fuit. Quæ vero consequentia non nisi ex parte concedenda est. Fatemur agi in responso Dei de templi materialis exstructione, sed κατ̓ ἄγσιν vel ἄρνησιν. Nunquid tu ædificabis mihi Domum ad ædificandum? Rationes adfert Deus negativæ responsionis suæ: tum quod non habitarit in Domo inde à deductione Israelitarum ex Ægypto, tum quod nunquam hoc postularit, aut dixerit: Quare non ædificastis mihi Domum cedrinam? Neque vero habitat Deus in templo materiali, quod agnovit ipse Salomo, in ipsa templi inauguratione 1. Reg. 8, 27. Conferatur Es. 66, 1. Quod vero ad responsio- nem θετικὴν & affirmativam, invertit Deus in pro- missione sua propositum Davidis, in hoc quidem Oraculo, non Davidem sibi, sed vice versa, se Davi- di domum ædificaturum : Prædicit tibi Dominus (v. 11.) quod domum tibi faciat Dominus. Quomo- do vero? Id explicant, quæ sequuntur, nimirum ex- citando ipsi semen, postquam compleverit dies suos, ei- que firmando regnum : quod ædificaturum sit domum nomini divino ita, ut eo pacto ædificetur domus ipsius Davidis, & Regnum ejus firmetur. Nam domus, quam semen ejus post fata ipsius OLIM excitan- dum, Messias exstructurus erat, spiritualis Domus est, cujus ipse fundamentum est Ef. 28, 16. & cui per fidem superædificantur fideles Ephes. 2, 16. 1. Petr. 2, 6. unde Scriptura S. ipsum, ut domus hujus ex- structorem introducit Zach. 6, 12. 13. & Christus ipse professus est, quod velit hanc domum Dei vi- ventis Ecclesiam (1. Tim. 3, 15.) extruere, atque ædifi- care Matth. 16, 18. Regnum, quod firmandum Da- vidi erat, vi hujus promissionis, in æternum durare debuit, ideoque regnum non terrenum, sed spiritu- ale est 2. Sam. 7, 16. Domus ergo illa fidelis, seu immo- ta, & regnum æternum est ipsa domus Dei, & Regnum Dei, ut hæc non diversa sint, sed mutuo se decla- rent: Domum faciet Davidi Dominus; & semen Davidis ædificabit domum nomini meo. Ita domus Davidis erit constans, vel Regnum ejus usque in æter- num: Et firmabo Regnum ejus (seminis Davidis) & stabiliam thronum regni feminis, vel germinis Davidici usque in sempiternum : unde manifestum est: Verbis illis, prædicit tibi Dominus, quod do- mum faciat tibi Dominus; prædicit Dominus (Deus Pater) quod domum tibi faciat Dominus (Deus Fi- lius, quia loquitur Dominus de Domino) conti- neri πρότασιν, & summam eorum, quæ sequuntur, & verbis subsequentibus propositionem illam ex- plicari, & uberius omnia exponi. Neq; dubium am- plius esse potest, omnia illa de Messia accipienda esse.

Alterum, quod obvertitur, est, quod de tali aga- tur hic persona, quæ peccare queat: Qui si inique ali- quid gesserit, arguam eum in virga virorum & in pla- gis Filiorum hominum. Quæ de Messia intelligi non possint; Sed id εὐδιάλυτον est. Nam si de persona ipsi- us, uti verba ipsa præ se ferunt, id accipias, tametsi Christus per se nulli peccato obnoxius fuerit, pec- cata tamen filiorum hominum, vel mortalium in se suscepit, & quum non norit ipse peccatum, fieri pro nobis peccatum voluit 2, Cor. 5, 21. conjecitq́; Deus in ipsum omnes iniquitates nostras Es. 53, 5. Unde Scri- ptura Sacra, ut doceat, quam vere in Judicio Dei ipsi imputata fuerint peccata nostras, quam vere in sese susceperit iniquitates nostras, ita de ipso loqui consuevit, ac si ipse peccarit, aut iniqui quid egerit. Quod non hic tantum factum, sed & alibi in vatici- niis de Messia deprehenditur: Comprehenderunt me iniquitates meæ, & non potui ut viderem, multi- plicatæ sunt super capillos meos, ait Messias ipse Psal. 40, 13. de peccatis in se conjectis non aliter lo- quens, ac de suis propriis peccatis. Nec aliter de iis- dem loquutus est Ps. 31, 15. Labefactata est propter INIQVITATEM MEAM, fortitudo mea, ve Psal. 69, 6. Deus TU SCIS insipientiam meam, & DELICTA MEA à te non sunt abscondita. Te- stari enim voluit se verissime illa suscepisse, ac gra- vissime ob illa angi, & affligi, onus illorum sentire pœnasque illorum sustinere, tanquam vadem, spon sorem, ac mediatorem nostrum, qui animam suam po suit pro nobis, & pro peccatis nostris. Idcirco uti ini quitates nostræ ipsius iniquitates non dicuntu tantum, sed revera etiam in Judicio Dei censentur, ita virga etiam ac plagæ, quæ filiis hominum incum- bébant, propter iniquitates istas veriffime ac realis- fime ab ipso exantlandæ prædicuntur. Ut Prophetia hic simul exhibeatur passionalis; de Messiæ passione satisfactoria & meritoria. Virga enim אנשים homi- num miserorum & mortalium (quales per lapsum & post lapsum sumus omnes) & plagæ filiorum Adam sunt afflictiones & pœnæ, quas meriti sumus, & qui- bus obnoxii sunt omnes Filii Adam, quas ipse pro nobis sustinuit; Unde Es. 53. quo loco plenius ex- plicantur, ipse מנגע plagatus dicitur ab eadem vo- ce, quæ hic occurrit de plagis Filiorum Adam בנגעי. Quod confirmat etiam opposita promissio, misericordiam meam non auferam ab eo, utpote qua docetur, non derelinquendum prorsus Messiam in istis plagis, quemadmodum impius Saul derelictus, & amotus à facie Domini fuit τελικῶς finaliter, at- que in æternum: Sed misericordiam ipsi exhibitum iri liberationis ex istis suppliciis, & evectionis ad æ- ternum Regnum: quas misericordias Dei fideles de resuscitatione Christi ad æternum imperium, & in- tellectas esse à Davide Psal. 16. & explicatas in No- vo Testamento à Sanctis Apostolis, Petro Actor. 2. & Paulo Act. 13. antea observavimus. Virgo hu- jus ἀντιθέσεως plagæ illæ de morte, è qua resuscita- tus, de inferno, è quo liberatus est Messias, ne anima ejus relinqueretur in Inferno, & caro ejus videret corruptionem, & ut anima ac carne triumphans de inferno ac morte, in æternum regnaret, explicandæ veniunt.

Non mirum autem, quod Psal. 89, 31. seqq. hæc de prævaricationibus & pœnis prolixe ad filios Messiæ transferantur: si autem dereliquerint filii ejus Legem meam, & in judiciis meis non ambulaue- rint, si justitias meas prophanaverint, & mandata mea non custodierint, visitabo in virga iniquitates eorum & in verberibus peccata eorum: Siquidem etiam Christus ipse ita concludat Luc. 23. 31. Si in viridi ligno hæc faciunt, in arido quid fiet? Docere autem istis Hieropsaltes voluit, tametsi in Messiam, vi promissionis sibi factæ, iniquitates nostræ translatæ sint, isq́; plagis affectus sit propter easdem, & pœnas ea- rum sustinuerit, non tamen filiis ejusdem impune li- cere peccare, & legem Dei transgredi, quin visitatu- rus etiam sit Deus iniquitates & peccata eorum: Ideoq; ita fide suscipiendum esse Messiam, ut gratia divina non abutamur ad peccata, sed ut χάρις σω- τήριος παιδεύουσα ἡμᾶς revocet nos ab impieta- te Tit. 2, 12. S. Augustinus lib. 17. de Civ. Dei c. 9. de Christo dici vult, quod de corpore ejus intelligen- dum est; quia ipse caput est, & ea sibi appropriat, quæ corpori eveniunt Act. 9, 5. Sed concinnior est illa explicatio, qua ad fideles semen Christi Es. 53, 11. Pfal. 20, 31. adeoq; Filios ejusdem Spirituales trans- ferri dicuntur, quæ de Christo in promissione ipsa primæva dicta sunt κατὰ διάνοιαν, & arguendo à mi- nori ad majus, quod quum in Christo nostræ vel alienæ ita punitæ sint iniquitates, in filiis ejus, si prævaricati defecerint, multo magis puniendæ sint iniquitates pro- priæ. Ubi tamen observationem meretur, quod re- vertatur David statim ad promissionem de Messia: Misericordiam autem meam non dispergam AB EO, neque nocebo in veritate mea. Non dicit AB EIS, filiis nempe ejus, sed AB EO; Ut primum ipsi Messiæ præstandam esse promissam gratiam si- gnificet, quam anxie anhelavit in plagis suis ipse Pf. 31, 10. Pf. 40, 12. 13. 14. Pf. 69, 1. 14. 17. exauditus à Deo Ef. 49, 8. Ebr. 5, 7. tum vero propter Messiam etiam filiis ejus pœnitentiam agentibus, & Ecclesiæ, vel regno Messiæ, ut illi non abjiciantur, & stabile ma- neat regnum ejus. Ideo addit, neque prophanabo te- stamentum meum, & quæ procedunt de labiis meis, non faciam irrita. Semel juravi in sancto meo, si David mentiar, semen ejus in æternum manebit: & thronus ejus, sicut Sol in conspectu meo, & sicut Luna perfecta in æternum, & testes in cælo fideles.

Tertium, quod nostræ obverti potest sententiæ, est, quod 1. Par. 22, 9. hæc promissio explicetur de Salomone à Davide: nec non à Salomone etiam ipso 1. Reg. 5, 5. cap. 8, 17. seqq. 2. Par. 6, 7. Sed hæc loca negamus respicere promissionem hic factam 2. Sam. 7. aut oraculo huic parallela esse, quo de supra jam monuimus. Ista promissio 1. Par. 22, 9. quam cætera loca respiciunt, tempore posterior fuit, quam hæc nostra, quæ in libris Chronicorum repetita est 1. Par. 17, 11. seqq. Illa de filio Davidi nascituro: hæc de semine excitando longe post fata Davidis: Illa de domo materiali & Templo Hierosolymitano: Hæc de domo spirituali & regno æterno agit: Ibi promissio cum conditione facta, & Legalis, si custodierit Salomo legem Domini: Hic sine conditione & simplex: adeo ut etiamsi inique gesserit, arguendus quidem sit plagis filiorum hominum, sed auferenda tamen non sit ab ipso misericordia Domini. Vid. B. Lutherus Tom. 8. Jen. Germ. wider der Jüden Lügen.

## 7:14
Ver. 14.

I WILL BE TO HIM A FATHER, AND HE SHALL BE TO ME A SON) I should think this is to be understood not only of the first, that is, of Solomon, but of each of the Kings from the blood of David: namely, that God wishes to deal with them paternally, that is, very mercifully, for the sake of David's memory.

That the promise is to be understood not of Solomon, but of the Messiah, has already been proven. Much less, therefore, is it to be understood of his posterity: from which most were unfaithful, impious, and idolaters; not sons of God, but sons of Belial. How then is such a magnificent promise to be understood of each of the Kings born from the blood of David, and thus even of the impious and idolaters? Nor does God indeed only promise that He wishes to act paternally or very mercifully, but that He will be a Father to that seed, and he will be a Son to God, which is far more eminent, and does not merely import temporal benefits, but primarily spiritual and everlasting ones, when it occurs concerning the faithful or sons of God by grace, Gen. 17, 7. Exod. 3, 6. Matt. 22, 31. 2 Cor. 6, 16. Rev. 21, 3. Here, however, it is not a matter of a son spoken of improperly, but of a proper Son, not of a son by regeneration, but of a son who is such by φύσει, nature and generation. For there is no reason why one should depart here from the literal meaning of the word Father and Son. Indeed, there are grave reasons why one should not depart from it, namely, that David himself understood this of the Son begotten from eternity and ὁμοουσίῳ, as witnessed by Ps. 2, 7. 11. of the firstborn Son, as is held in Ps. 89, 28. Add that here the discourse is about a singular person building the house of the Lord: not about an entire lineage, or a series of successors: and that it concerns such a seed, which is to be eternal, and is to have an eternal throne and kingdom. Which does not fit Solomon, or even the succeeding kings, whether individually or collectively. Furthermore, what more certain Interpreter shall we give than the Holy Spirit in the New Testament, explaining it concerning Christ, Heb. 1, 5. where it is denied that this was said even to any of the Angels; I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son. But there is no doubt concerning paternal benevolence toward the Angels; therefore something far more eminent is introduced, and indeed an axiom of such a kind that it suits none of the Angels, and exceeds all the dignity of the Angels by a great distance. Namely, that this seed of David is to be, and in the fullness of time has been made, the Son of God, or that he himself is the Son of God from eternity (according to Ps. 2, 7. which passage the Apostle joins there) begotten from the substance of the Father, Ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑπο- σάσεως αὐτᾶ through whom as the co-eternal and consubstantial Son the Father created τὲς αἰῶνας, and who carries and sustains all things by the word of his power. For the Apostle here has undertaken to demonstrate that this is Christ, and thus that he himself excels the angelic dignity and nature by infinite parasangs, and he demonstrates this before all else from the generation of the Son of God from eternity from Ps. 2, and he proves from 2 Sam. 7. that Christ as man is the same Son of God; whom as the πρωτότοκον firstborn Son of God, just as David introduced him in Ps. 2, so when he again introduces the same into this world, namely as he was to be manifested in the flesh, and was to come to the earth, he testified in Ps. 97, 8. that all the Angels of God ought to worship him. Since the Holy Spirit applies all these things to that seed of David, what is more evident than that it ought not to be understood of Solomon in the cited oracle, but must necessarily be understood of the Messiah? Which David's own commentary on this oracle also clearly confirms, namely in Psalm 72 and Ps. 89. For it is manifest that in both places it is explained concerning the Son of God, the Messiah. I pass over the fact that no one has easily been found who was so cold in this illustrious oracle as Grotius, that it should be taken concerning the successors of David, even the impious ones, and concerning some sort of grace of God.

I see one thing that can be brought forward for Solomon, though not for the other successors: namely, that those words of 1 Chron. 22 are read as spoken expressly concerning Solomon. But as was already observed before, that a different promise is referred to there, so since the Subject is different, the predicate also will have to be explained differently in each place; Because predicates must be explained according to the nature of the subject; and the predicate is such as is permitted to be by the subject. Concerning the Messiah it is said that he is the Son of God by generation; concerning Solomon, that he is the Son of God by adoption. The former is the essential and natural Son of God: The latter, however, is a son of God only by grace, and by faith: for he could fall from that grace, and in fact did fall, when he abandoned the law of God; because the promise made to Solomon was conditional.

Ver. same.

I WILL REBUKE HIM WITH THE ROD OF MEN) I will send diseases. AND WITH THE STRIPES OF THE CHILDREN OF MEN) The barrenness of the fields.

Those expositions are merely precarious, confirmed by no example or document of Scripture. For where do the rod of men signify diseases, and the stripes of the children of men signify barrenness? Moreover, since it has been shown that the discourse here is about the Messiah, the punishments deserved by sins are to be understood, to which he himself was made liable for our sins taken upon himself.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

EGO ERO EI IN PATREM, ET IPSE ERIT MIHI IN FILIUM) Hoc non de primo tantum, id est, de Salomone, sed de singulis Regibus e Davidis sanguine intelligendum putem: velle scilicet Deum paterne, id est, valde clementer, cum illis agere, ob Davidis memoriam.

Promissionem non de Salomone, sed de Messia intelligendam esse, jam evictum. Multo ergo minus de posteritate ejusdem intelligenda: è qua plerique infideles, impii, & idololatræ fuere; non filii Dei, sed filii Belial. Quomodo ergo de singulis Regibus è Davidis sanguine oriundis, adeoque etiam de impiis & idololatris tam magnifica promissio intelligenda? Nec vero tantum promittit Deus, se velle paterne vel valde clementer agere, sed se futurum semini illi in Patrem, & ipsum Deo futurum in filium, quod longe eminentius est, nec beneficia tantum temporalia importat, sed Spiritualia imprimis & sempiterna, cum de fidelibus vel filiis Dei per gratiam occurrit, Genes. 17, 7. Exod. 3, 6. Matth. 22, 31. 2. Cor. 6, 16. Apoc. 21, 3. Hic vero non de filio improprie dicto, sed de Filio proprio, non de filio per regenerationem, sed de filio, qui φύσει, natura & generatione talis est, agitur. Nulla enim causa est, cur à proprietate vocis Patris & Filii hic recedatur. Imo causæ graves sunt, cur ab ea recedendum non sit, nimirum, quod David ipse de Filio ab æterno genito & ὁμοουσίῳ id intellexerit, teste Psal. 2, 7. 11. de Filio primigenito, ut habetur Psal. 89, 28. Adde, quod hic de persona singulari exstructura domum Domini, sermo sit: non de integra prosapia, vel successorum serie: quodque de semine agatur tali, quod æternum futurum sit, & thronum & regnum æternum habiturum. Quod non quadrat in Salomonem, aut reges etiam successores, sive singulos, sive universos. Porro quem certiorem dabimus Interpretem, quam Spiritum S. in N. Testam. id explicantem de Christo, Ebr. 1, 5. ubi negatur etiam Angelorum ulli dictum hoc esse; Ego ero ei in Patrem, & ipse erit mihi in Filium. At de paterna benevolentia erga Angelos dubium nullum est; proinde longe eminentius quid infertur, & quidem ejusmodi ἀξίωμα, quod Angelorum nulli conveniat, omnem Angelorum dignitatem longissime excedat. Quod nempe hoc semen Davidis futurum sit, & factum in temporis plenitudine sit in Filium Dei, vel quod ipse Filius Dei sit ab æterno (secundum Psal. 2, 7. quem locum jungit ibi Apostolus) e Patris substantia genitus, Ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑπο- σάσεως αὐτᾶ per quem ut coæternum & confub- stantalem Filium Pater condidit τὲς αἰῶνας, quique omnia portat & sustentat verbo virtutis suæ. Hunc enim esse Christum, adeoque infinitis parasangis ipsum excellere Angelicam dignitatem & naturam demonstrare hic aggressus est Apostolus, idque an- te omnia è generatione Filii Dei ab æterno è Psal. 2. de- monstrat, & quod Christus homo sit ipse idem Filius Dei è 2. Sam. 7. evincit; quem πρωτότοκον primo- genitum Filium Dei, uti Psal. 2. introduxit David, ita cum iterum eundem introducit in hunc mundum, uti nempe manifestandus erat in carne, & adventu- rus in terras, testatus est Pf. 97, 8. quod adorare eum debeant omnes Angeli Dei. Quæ omnia quum semi- ni illi Davidis applicet Spiritus Sanctus, quid evi- dentius est, quam quod illud de Salomone intelligi non debeat in oraculo adducto, sed de Messia ne- cessario intelligendum sit? Quod ipsius etiam Da- vidis commentarius in hoc oraculum luculenter comprobat, Psalmo nempe 72. & Pf. 89. Utrobi- que enim de Filio Dei Messia id explicari, manife- stum est. Taceo, quod nemo facile repertus sit, qui in illustri oraculo tam frigidus, uti Grotius, fuerit, quod id de successoribus Davidis, etiam impiis, & de qualicunque gratia Dei accipi debeat.

Unum video, quod pro Salomone afferri possit, non tamen pro cæteris successoribus: quod nempe verba illa 1. Paral. 22. de Salomone expresse dicta legantur. Sed uti antea jam observatum, ibi diver- sam respici promissionem, ita cum Subjectum di- versum sit, prædicatum etiam aliter atque aliter utrobique explicandum erit; Quia prædicata o- portet pro ratione subjecti explicare; & tale est prædicatum, quale permittitur esse à subjecto. De Messia dicitur, quod sit Filius Dei per generationem; de Salomone, quod Filius Dei sit per adoptionem. Ille essentialis & naturalis Dei Filius: Hic vero nonnisi per gratiam filius Dei est, & per fidem: gratia enim il- la excidere potuit, ac revera excidit, quando le- gem Dei dereliquit; quia promissio Salomoni fa- cta conditionalis fuit.

Vers. eod.

ARGUAM EUM IN VIRGA VIRORUM) Morbos immittam. ET IN PLAGIS FILIORUM HOMINUM) Agrorum sterilitatem.

Mere precariæ sunt illæ expositiones, nullo Scripturæ exemplo vel documento firmatæ. Ubi enim virga virorum morbos, & plagæ filiorum ho- minum sterilitatem significant? Cæterum cum o- stensum sit, de Messia hic sermonem esse, pœnæ in- telligendæ peccatis promeritæ, quibus ipse ob pec- cata nostra in se suscepta obnoxius factus.

## 7:15
Ver. 15.

BUT I WILL NOT TAKE MY MERCY AWAY FROM HIM, AS I TOOK IT FROM SAUL, WHOM I REMOVED FROM MY SIGHT) I will not take the kingdom away from them for such a long time, as I took it from the posterity of Saul. This interpretation is the best, it is Josephus's, and that of other Hebrews.

We have already spoken about the true sense. Compare the Paraphrase of Osiander and what we observed regarding Psalm 89.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

MISERICORDIAM AUTEM NON AUFERAM AB EO, SICUT ABSTULI A SAUL, QVEM AMOVI A FACIE MEA) Regnum in tam longo tempore illis non au- feram, ut Saulis posteritati abstuli. Hæc interpretatio opti- ma, Josephi est, & aliorum Hebræorum.

De vero sensu jam diximus. Conf. Paraphra- sis Osiandr. & quæ ad Pf. 89. observavimus.

## 7:19
Ver. 19. FOR THIS IS THE LAW OF ADAM O LORD GOD) The Greeks: ὗτος δὲ ὁ νόμος τᾶ ἀνθρώπε κύριέ με κύριε. The true sense is: you deal with me familiarly, as men are accustomed to deal with men.

There are various interpretations of this passage, but that the word תּוֹרַת here does not signify law, as the LXX and the Vulgate render it, but disposition and form, the parallel passage in which the masculine תּוֹר occurs, 1 Chronicles 17:17, openly convinces. And although some, with Grotius who here deserts the Vulgate, interpret the passage as referring to familiar conversation, the interpretation of Blessed Luther is nevertheless entirely to be preferred, as flowing from the words and being entirely consistent with the context, that is a manner of a man, who in the height is God the Lord, which the marginal gloss explains, that is, you speak with me of such an eternal kingdom, where no one can be King, he must be God and man, because he is my Son, and yet shall be King forever and ever, which belongs to God alone. וזאת תורת האדם אדני יהוה And this is the form of that man, who is the Lord God. In the parallel passage 1 Chron. 17, it is thus held: וראיתני כתור האדם המעלה יהוה אלהים And you have seen me according to the form of the man of excellence, the Lord God. The Messiah, therefore, of whom God has spoken, is called the man Lord God, or the man of excellence God Lord, that is, the God-man; for this form was shown to David in that oracle, because the promised seed had to come forth from the womb or loins of David, as true man, and was to be the natural Son of God, to the Father ὁμοούσιος as true God. And since God is said to have seen and regarded David in the same form, it can be piously thought that the Son of God, in human form, so that He might prelude His incarnation, offered Himself to be seen by David in that vision. Blessed Glassius gives this paraphrase in Onomat. Messiæ p. 120. I have indeed heard from You, O God, that a Son is promised to me as Heir of the Israelite Kingdom, but furthermore a more eminent Son is also promised, namely that man of the excellence of Jehovah Elohim, or the Messiah the God-man, of whom my son ought to be a type and prefiguration. Therefore in Philol. Sacr. L. 3. part. 1. Tr. 2. Sect. 7. p. m. 345. he thinks the word תורת refers to a delineation and prefiguration: But we have proved that the discourse here is uniquely about the Messiah, whence the former interpretation of Blessed Luther is deservedly to be preferred. Meanwhile, the name of the Messiah the God-man is rightly sought from this; which others of our own have also confirmed with their suffrage. Blessed D. Cramer in Scholis Propheticis Class. 2. Vatic. 2, Blessed D. Helvicus in Elencho 2. against the Jews class 1. Thes. ult. Dn. D. Walther in Offic. Bibl. f. 949. Dn. D. Muller in Judaismo f. 163. as also the Vinariean Theologians in their Paraphrase. I add the suffrage of our Dn. D. Dorscheus, and the arguments demonstrating the matter vigorously from Pentadec. dissert. on Ps. 2. th. 24. David 2. Sam. 7, 18. placed in the recess of his mind, meditating on the mysteries of God, having meditated on his own frailty, having embraced in his mind the sublimity of the glory to be conferred upon his house, having looked into the far-off future wonders of the Davidic tribe, finally, how he might receive God's prophecy concerning the mercy to be conferred upon him in an ineffable way, and the inscrutable sonship to be planted in his posterity, he asserts his opinion: that it seemed to him that this law, according to which in future ages God is to send the Son from the innermost bowels of mercy, requires this from the inevitable postulate of divine justice, that that Son be האדם אדני יהוה or as it is said in 1 Chron. 17, 17. המעלה האדם יהוה אלהים. An altogether admirable law, according to which God and man are coupled in the far-off future, according to which an unhoped-for divine dispensation will bring it about that the excellence of some certain and individual man arising from the Davidic posterity should consist in this, that he is the man Jehovah Elohim.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ISTA ENIM EST LEX ADAM DOMINE DEUS) Græci: ὗτος δὲ ὁ νόμος τᾶ ἀνθρώπε κύριέ με κύριε. Verus sensus est: familiariter mecum agis, quomodo homines cum hominibus agere solent.

Variæ hujus loci sunt interpretationes, sed vo- cem תּוֹרַת hic non significare legem, uti LXX. & Vul- gata reddunt, sed dispositionem & formam, paralle- lus locus, in quo masculinum תּוֹר occurrit 1. Paral. 17, 17. aperte convincit. Et quanquam nonnulli cum Grotio vulgatam hic deserente, de familiari conversatione locum interpretentur, præferenda tamen omnino B. Lutheri interpretatio, utpote è verbis fluens, & contextui prorsus consentanea, das ist eine Weise eines Menschen, der in der Hohe GOtt der HErr ist, quam exponit glossa margina- lis, das ist, du redest mit mir von solchem ewigen Reich, da niemand kan Konig seyn, er muß GOtt und Mensch seyn, weil er mein Sohn, und doch fur und fur soll Konig seyn, welches allein GOtt gehoret. Quam interpretationem B. Lutherus defendit Tom. 8. Jun. Germ. f. 158. Sic enim fluunt verba in fonte: וזאת תורת האדם אדני יהוה Et hæc forma istius hominis, qui est Dominus Deus. In loco parallelo 1. Par. 17. sic habetur: וראיתני כתור האדם המעלה יהוה אלהים Et vidisti me secundum formam hominis ex- cellentis Domini Dei. Dicitur ergo Messias, de quo locutus est Deus, homo Dominus Deus, vel homo ex- cellens Deus Dominus, hoc est, θεάνθρωπος; hæc enim forma Davidi exhibita fuit in isto oraculo, quia semen promissum & ex utero vel lumbis Davi- dis prodire debuit, ut verus homo, & futurum erat Filius Dei naturalis, Patri ὁμοούσιος ceu verus Deus. Et quum eadem forma vidisse Deus & respexisse Davidem dicatur, pie cogitari potest, Filium Dei in forma humana, ut suæ ἐπανθρωπήσει præluderet, ista visione David se conspiciendum præbuisse. B. Glassius hanc reddit paraphrasin in Onomat. Mes- siæ p. 120. Audivi quidem à Te, o Deus, promitti mihi Filium Regni Israelitici Hæredem, sed insuper eminentior etiam promittitur Filius, nempe homo ille excellentiæ Jehovah Elohim, seu Messias θεάνθρωπος, cujus typus & præfiguratio esse debet Filius meus. Ideo in Philol. Sacr. L. 3. part. 1. Tr. 2. Sect. 7. p. m. 345. vocem תורת delineationem ac præfiguratio- nem respicere putat: Sed probavimus, unice de Mes- sia hic sermonem esse, unde prior B. Lutheri inter- pretatio merito præferenda. Interim recte hinc Mes- siæ θεανθρώπꙋ nomen petitur; quod etiam alii No- strates suffragio suo firmarunt. B. D. Cramerus in Scholis Propheticis Class. 2. Vatic. 2, B. D. Helwi- cus Elencho 2. contra Judæos classe 1. Thes. ult. Dn. D. Waltherus Offic. Bibl. f. 949. Dn. D. Mul- lerus in Judaismo f. 163. ut & Vinarienses Theologi in Paraphrasi. Addo Dn. D. Dorschei Nostri suffra- gium, & argumenta nervose rem demonstrantia e Pentadec. dissert. super Ps. 2. th. 24. David 2. Sam. 7, 18. in recessu animi, Dei mysteria meditantis, con- stitutus, suam tenuitatem meditatus sublimitatem glo- riæ in domum suam conferendæ mente complexus, in longinquum futura admiranda tribus Davidicæ in- tuitus, tandem, quomodo Dei vaticinium de miseri- cordia in ineffabili in se conferenda, & filiatione imper- scrutabili in suam posteritatem plantanda acciperet, suam sententiam asserit: sibi visum fuisse eam le- gem, secundum quam futuris seculis ex intimis mise- rationis visceribus Deus missurus est Filium, hoc ex justitiæ divinæ inevitabili postulato requirituram, ut Filius ille sit האדם אדני יהוה vel ut 1. Paral. 17, 17. dicitur המעלה האדם יהוה אלהים. Admirabi- lis omnino lex, secundum quam in longinquam copu- labuntur Deus & homo, secundum quam insperata di- vina dispensatio efficiet, ut certi, & individui alicujus hominis ex posteritate Davidica oriundi excellentia μονοτροπος in eo consistat, quod sit homo Jehovah Elohim.

## 7:21
Vers. 21.

FOR THY WORD'S SAKE) It is in the Hebrew בעבור דברך. But in Chron. 17, where the rest is the same, it is בעבור עבדך as the LXX also read here in their books, for they translate διὰ τῆς δοῦλόν σου.

There is no need for the sources to be corrected here, nor is it lawful for that to be done from the modern Greek text of the LXX Interpreters. For who will guarantee that the modern Greek Codices agree with the older ones here, or if they do agree at all, that the interpreters did not hallucinate, so that one must admit that the moderns differ from the ancients, and that the Hebrews therefore differ? Since it is certain on the contrary that God has preserved the sources, and the authentic text rather than the rivulets and human interpretations. Furthermore, if the reading of both places is retained, as the Hebrew truth has it, it is manifest that he who is called the servant of the Lord in the book of Chronicles, is called the Word of the Lord in the book of Samuel: And thus both names fit the designating of the Messiah perfectly, who is the Word John 1, 1. and the servant of the Lord Is. 53, 1. For thy word's sake, therefore, or for thy seed's sake, is for the sake of the Messiah. For for his sake God did all these great things for David. And thus Junius explains 2 Sam. 7, 12. for thy word's sake: that is, for the sake of Christ thy servant, who is the eternal word, or the eternal word ὁμοόσιος to the Father. On which matter Junius connects the passage 1 Sam. 3, 21. After Jehovah had revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh in the word of Jehovah, that is, in Christ Jesus, who in earlier times, as the notes of the same have it, was called the Angel of Jehovah in the preceding books, but afterwards, as he revealed himself more clearly in succeeding time, is called the word of Jehovah, as 2 Sam. 7, 21. Thus here by Jehovah revealing himself the Holy Spirit is understood, by the Word the Son of God, by Jehovah, whose Word he is, God the Father, and the mystery of the Trinity will be designated, which we observe παραφυαδικῶς. The Belgic Interpreters also understand it of the hypostatic Word in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

PROPTER VERBVM TVVM) Est in Ebræo בעבור דברך. At in Paral. 17. ubi cætera eadem est בעבור עבדך quomodo & hic legerunt in suis libris LXX. vertunt enim διὰ τῆς δοῦλόν σου.

Non opus est, ut corrigantur hic fontes, nec fas est, ut e moderno LXX. Interpp. Græco textu id fiat. Ecquis enim præstabit, Græcos Codices mo dernos antiquioribus hic consonare, aut si conso- nent omnino, interpretes minime hallucinatos es- set se, ut Ebræorum ideo dissonare, modernos ab anti- quis, fateri oporteat? Cum certum ex adverso sit, Deum conservasse fontes, & textum authenticum potius, quam rivulos, & interpretationes humanas. Porro si utriusque loci lectio retineatur, prouti ve- ritas Ebræa habet, manifestum est, eum qui in li- bro Paral. servus Domini vocatur, in libro Samue- lis vocatum esse Verbum Domini: Adeoque Mes- siæ designando utrumque nomen optime conve- nit, qui ὁ λόγος est Joh. 1, 1. & servus Domini Es. 53, 1. Propter verbum tuum ergo, vel propter semen tuum, est propter Messiam. Hujus enim gratia fecit Deus Davidi omnia magnalia ista. Atque ita ex- ponit Junius 2. Sam. 7, 12. propter sermonem tuum: id est, propter Christum servum tuum, qui verbum æternum est, vel æternus sermo patri ὁμοόσιος. In quam rem consert Junius locum 1. Sam. 3, 21. Post- quam revelasset se Jehovah Samueli in Silo in sermo- ne Jehovah, id est, in Christo Jesu, qui superioribus temporibus, ut notæ ejusdem habent, Angelus Je- hovæ dictus est, in libris præcedentibus, deinceps vero, prout succedente tempore se patefecit clarius, sermo Jehovah appellatur, ut 2. Sam. 7, 21. Ita hic per Je- hovam se revelantem Spiritus sanctus intelligetur, per Sermonem Filius Dei, per Jehovah, cujus ille est Sermo, Deus Pater, mysteriumque Trinitatis desi- gnabitur, quod παραφυαδικῶς observamus. De verbo ὑποστατικῷ etiam intelligunt Interpretes Belgici h. l.

## 7:23
Vers. 23.

FOR WHICH GOD WENT) There is no nation that can predicate the same thing about those whom it thinks are gods. There is no reason why the word אלהים should not be taken properly for the true God. Because there is no nation for which God went in such a manner as was done for the Jewish people. The plural name with a plural verb insinuates the mystery of the plurality of persons in God. For Socinus himself confirms from the parallel passage 1 Chron. 17, 11. that the discourse is about the true God, because it has WENT in the singular, and uses the demonstrative ה, in fragment. p. 50. Enjedinus in explicat. locor. p. 35. acknowledges that this testimony cannot be contradicted, because it treats of one God alone: provided that in the source it is held to be about God, who redeemed the Israelite people.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

PROPTER QVAM IVIT DEVS) Nulla gens, quæ de iis, quos deos putat, idem possit prædicare. Nihil causæ est, cur vox אלהים non accipiatur proprie de vero Deo. Quod nulla gens sit, ob qua m Deus iverit ea ratione, uti populo factum Judaico. Plurale nomen cum verbo plurali mysterium plu- ralitatis personarum in Deo insinuat. Nam de ve- ro Deo sermonem esse Socinus ipse è loco parallelo 1. Par. 17, 11. confirmat, quod habeat IVIT in sin- gulari, & ה notificativum adhibeat, in fragment. p. 50. Enjedinus in explicat. locor. p. 35. contradici non posse huic testimonio agnoscit, quod de uno so- lo Deo agat: siquidem in fonte habeatur de Deo, qui redemit Israeliticum populum.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII. The Philistines, Moabites, Zobah, Syrians, and Edomites are made tributary to David. The King of Hamath sends congratulatory gifts. The chief ministers of David are designated.

Ver. 1.

DAVID TOOK THE BRIDLE OF TRIBUTE FROM THE HAND OF THE PHILISTINES) In the Hebrew מתג האמה, that is, the barriers of the mountain of Ammah: there was the town of Gath 2 Chron. 18, 1.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII. Philistæi, Moabitæ, Soba, Syri, & Idumæi, tribu- tarii Davidi redduntur. Rex Emath mittit dona gratulatoria. Ministris Davidis præci- pui designantur.

Vers. 1.

TVLIT DAVID FRÆNVM TRIBVTI DE MANV PHILISTHIIM) In Hebræo מתג האמה, id est, clau- stra montis Ammæ: ibi erat Gitta oppidum 2. Par. 18, 1.

## 8:2
Ver. 2.

AND HE SMOTE MOAB) Here those magnificent promises begin to be fulfilled. Gen. 15, 18. Num. 24, 17. HE MEASURED THEM WITH A LINE) He designated three parts of the Moabite land, in one of which only he left the natives as survivors, having killed the others, so that the guarding would not be difficult. SERVING UNDER TRIBUTE) See shortly 6, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET PERCVSSIT MOAB) Hic impleri incipiunt pro- missa illa magnifica. Gen. 15, 18. Num. 24, 17. MENSVS EST EOS FVNICVLO) Tres desi- gnavit partes terræ Moabiticæ, in quarum una tantum in- digenas reliquit superstites, occisis cæteris, ne difficilis esset custodia. SERVIENS SVB TRIBVTO) Vide mox 6, 14.

## 8:3
Ver. 3.

WHEN HE WENT TO RECOVER HIS DOMINION AT THE RIVER EUPHRATES) In the Hebrew: when he (David) went to repel his hand (going) to the river Euphrates. That King of Zobah, a neighbor to the Philistines, as can be gathered from 1 Sam. 14, 47, carrying war to the inhabitants of the Euphrates, without having requested an innocent passage, had invaded the borders of the Israelites by force: and he paid the penalty for that matter.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

QVANDO PROFECTVS EST, VT DOMINARE- TVR SVPER FLVMEN EVPHRATEM) In Hebræo: cum iret ipse (David) ad repellandam manum ejus (euntem) ad flumen Euphratis. Rex ille Sabæ Philisthinis vicinus, ut colligere est 1. Sam. 14, 47. in Euphratis accolas bellum fe- rens, non postulato innoxio itinere, fines Israelitarum vi in- vaserat: ejusque rei pœnas dedit.

## 8:4
Ver. 4.

HE HOUGHED ALL THE CHARIOT HORSES) That is, he cut the hamstrings. Thus Hannibal cut the thighs and hams of the Roman men. Livy book 22. Valerius Maximus says that some left by him had the lowest part of their feet cut 9, 11.

ONE THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED HORSEMEN) The Greeks: χίλια ἅρματα καὶ ἑπτὰ χιλιάδες ἱππέων, as it is in 1 Chron. 18, 3. But Josephus likewise ἅρματα χίλια: but ἱπποτῶν πεντακισχιλίυς. Thus in these, no less than in the codices of other histories, the writing of numbers has long since varied. Compare what you will see below at 10, 8; these preserve the proportion of the Greeks or of Josephus more.

The version of the 70 Interpreters, or the account of Josephus, was not to be preferred to the Hebrew truth, whose authority ought to be greater for us than the translation or historian of any other. Therefore, others have more religiously devoted effort to reconciling such passages, in the books of Kings and Chronicles sometimes appearing to differ. And most people reconcile this passage with 1 Chron. 18, 3 in such a way that the former number refers to chariots, so that David took a thousand chariots; the other, concerning seven hundred horsemen, refers to as many decuries of horsemen: which ellipsis they order to be observed in the method of counting. It is similar when among the Latins it is said fifty sixty, H.S. and the like, and they are generally understood as thousands, as Junius notes at this place, which is also the explanation of Piscator, the Wine-country Paraphrasts, as well as the Belgian Interpreters, and also Serarius, and Cornelius à Lapide. Others, with Salianus and Sanctius, say that 1700 horsemen properly so-called are designated in the book of Samuel, and no mention is made of chariots; but in Chronicles, chariots are added and those who sat in chariot-horses are also counted as horsemen: since it is not new for those who are carried in chariots to be called horsemen, which Menochius proves here from Isa. 21, 7 and chap. 22, 6. But who would doubt that five thousand and three hundred horsemen could be carried in a thousand chariots? says Sanctius on this passage. Others, with Abulensis and Rabbi David Kimchi, want only the primary horsemen to be counted in this passage, and those who were of the Royal Guard: but in Chronicles, they want all of them to be counted clearly. Which opinion also pleases Menochius, and is not disapproved of by Corn. à Lapide. One can choose whichever opinion pleases: nor will there be a need to flee to that desperate ἄτυπωα concerning corrupt Hebrew codices. For have not the 70 Interpreters or their copyists been able to have taken that number from the book of Chronicles, so that it is not even necessary to admit that the writing of numbers in Hebrew codices has long since varied. Nevertheless, the latter reconciliation seems preferable to us, as the simplest.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

SVBNERVAVIT OMNES JVGALES CVRRVVM) Id est, suffragines succidit. Sic hominibus Romanis Annibal succidit femina & poplites. Livius libro 22. Valerius Maximus quosdam ab eo relictos ait infima pedum parte succisa 9, 11.

MILLE SEPTINGENTIS EQVITIBVS) Græci: χίλια ἅρματα καὶ ἑπτὰ χιλιάδες ἱππέων, quomodo est in 1. Par. 18, 3. At Josephus item ἅρματα χίλια: at ἱπποτῶν πεντακισχιλίυς. Ita in his non minus, quam in aliarum historia- rum Codicibus jam olim variavit numerorum scriptura. Con- fer quod infra 10, 8. videbis hæc Græcorum aut Josephi ma- gis servare proportionem.

Non erat LXX. Interpp. versio, aut Josephi relatio præferenda Ebraicæ veritati, cujus major nobis auctoritas esse debet, quam ullius translatio- nis aut historici. Proinde religiosius alii operam locarunt in conciliandis talibus locis, in libris Re- gum, & Paralipomenon quandoque in speciem dis- fidentibus. Et hunc quidem locum plerique ita conciliant cum 1. Paral. 18, 3. ut numerus prior cur- rus referat, ut nempe currus mille ceperit David; al- ter de septingentis Equitibus, totidem decurias equi- tum: quam ellipsin observari jubent in ratione nu- merandi. Simile est, quum apud Latinos dicun- tur quinquagies sexagies, H. S. & similia, & intelli- gantur fere millia, uti notat Junius ad h. l. quæ eti- am est Piscatoris, Vinariensium Paraphrastarum, ut & Belgicorum Interpp. nec non Serarii, & Cornel. à Lapide explicatio. Alii cum Saliano & Sanctio dicunt 1700. equites proprie dictos designari libro Samuelis, curruumque nullam fieri mentionem; In Parali- pomenis vero currus adjici & equitibus accenseri etiam, qui equis currulibus insidebant: siquidem novum non sit eos, qui quadrigis vehuntur, equites appellari, quod probat Menochius hic ex Esa. 21, 7. & cap. 22, 6. Quis autem dubitet, in quadrigis mille quinque mille & trecentos equites vehi posse? ait Sanctius in hunc locum. Alii cum Abulensi & Rabb. David Kimchi hoc loco primarios tantum equites, & qui ex Regio Satellitio fuerint: In Paralipomenis vero plane omnes numerari volunt. Quæ sententia Menochio etiam placet, nec improbata est Corn. à Lapide. Eligi potest, quæ arriserit sententia: nec opus erit ad desperatum illud ἄτυπωα de corruptis Ebræis Codd. confugere. Annon enim LXX. In- terpp. aut exscriptores eorum potuere numerum illum è libro Paralipomenon sumsisse, ut ne id qui- dem necessum sit admittere, jam olim variasse in Ebræis codicibus numerorum scripturam. Præ- ferenda tamen postrema conciliatio nobis videtur, ceu simplicissima.

## 8:5
Verse 5.

AND THE SYRIANS OF DAMASCUS CAME) Concerning this victory of David, you have the passage of the Damascene in Josephus, who brought out the name of the King of Syria, which he expressed as Adados in the Damascene, in one place in the same way, in another as Ader: undoubtedly because those letters ד and ר not only have a very similar form, but are also easily changed between themselves because of some affinity of sound, just as in Latin aqua Arseria from adferendo.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

VENIT QVOQVE STRIA DAMASCI) De hac Da- vidis victoria habes Damasceni locum apud Josephum, qui Regis Syriæ nomen, quod Damasceno Αδαδός, alibi eodem modo, alibi Ader extulit: nimirum quia literæ illæ ד & ר non modo formam persimilem habent, sed & ob soni aliquam affinitatem facile inter se mutantur, sicut Latinis aqua Arse- ria ab adferendo.

## 8:6
Verse 6. HE PLACED A GARRISON) See shortly 14. Verse 10.

GOLDEN VESSELS AND SILVER VESSELS AND BRASS VESSELS, WHICH KING DAVID SANCTIFIED TO THE LORD, WITH THE OINTMENT AND GOLD WHICH HE HAD SANCTIFIED FROM ALL THE NATIONS WHICH HE HAD SUBDUED) Above 7, 8. Concerning this custom of consecrating a part of the booty, see Gen. 14, 20 and in the third book of the Law of War and Peace, chap. 6, no. 20.

Latin:

Vers. 6. POSUIT PRÆSIDIVM) Vide mox 14. Vers. 10.

VASA AUREA ET VASA ARGENTEA ET VA- SA ÆREA, QVÆ ISPA SANCTIFICAVIT DAVID REX DOMINO, CUM VNGVENTO ET AVRO QVÆ SANCTIFICAVERAT DE VNIVERSIS GEN- TIBVS QVAS SUBEGERAT) Supra 7. 8. De hoc mo- re prædæ partem sacrandi vide Genes. 14, 20. & libro tertio de Jure Belli ac Pacis cap. 6. num. 20.

## 8:13
Verse 13.

TEN THOUSAND AND EIGHT THOUSAND BEING SLAIN) Partly of the Syrians, partly of the Idumeans, who were allies to them. Abisai killed six thousand of these, then Joab twelve thousand 1 Chron. 18, 12. Ps. 60, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

CÆSIS DECEM ET OCTO MILLIBVS) Partim Sy- rorum, partim Idumæorum, qui eis erant socii. Horum sex millia occidit Abisai, deinde Joab duodecim millia 1. Paral. 18, 12. Pf. 60, 2.

## 8:14
Verse 14.

AND HE PLACED GUARDS IN IDUMEA) And a prefect, who would administer justice, as 1 Kings 22, 48, as the Romans did at Capua and elsewhere. See in the second book of the Law of War and Peace, chap. 9, § 6, and in the Annotations to that passage.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET POSVIT IN IDUMÆA CUSTODES) Et præfe- ctum, qui jus redderet, ut 1. Reg. 22, 48. ut Romani Capuæ & alibi. Vide secundo libro de Jure Belli ac Pacis cap. 9. §. 6. & in Annotatis ad eum locum.

## 8:15
Verse 15.

AND DAVID DID JUDGMENT] He administered justice according to the law.

AND JUSTICE) He gave rewards to those who deserved well.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

FACIEBAT QVOQVE DAVID JUDICIUM] Jus ad- ministrabat secundum legem.

ET JUSTITIAM) Præmia dabat bene meritis.

## 8:18
Verse 18.

OVER THE CHERETHITES AND THE PELETHITES) Jerome in some places thinks these names, as also what immediately preceded, are of the distinguished senators of the great Sanhedrin, just as the Greeks also seem to have thought: for they say καὶ Βαναίας υἱὸς Ἰωδαὲ σύμβουλος καὶ ὁ Χελεθὶ καὶ ὁ Φελεθί. But some of the Hebrews judge them to have been Israelite families, the Chaldean [interprets them as] archers, from which meaning Corytus does not depart: others again [think they were] parts of the Philistines: if we admit this, perhaps these כרתי will be the descendants of the Cretans: certainly it appears sufficiently that they were soldiers 20, 23.

BUT DAVID'S SONS WERE PRIESTS] That could not happen according to the law. But there is an error in the word. The verb כהן, from which that noun comes, signifies to perform a service: thence the participle, passing into a verbal signification, if it is referred expressly or tacitly to God, signifies a minister of God, a priest: if to the King, his minister, for instance a court official, as the LXX have placed here, in which way the Chaldeans also take it here, and the Hebrews, who add that Absalom was indignant that such a court office had not fallen to him as well. And the noun כהן does not seem to be taken otherwise below 20, 26. And in Chronicles it is explained by the first at the King's hand. 1. 18, 17. The same office seems to be called in 1 Kings 4, 5, over the officers, where the Greeks [say], over those who were appointed.

Grotius here corrects the Vulgate version, which he otherwise held as authentic. Note also here the confession of Cornelius à Lapide, who not obscurely acknowledges the error of the Vulgate in the word Priest.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

SVPER CERETHI ET PHELETHI) Hieronymus ali- cubi putat hæc nomina, ut & quod proxime præcessit, esse eximiorum senatorum magni Synedrii, quomodo & Græci sensisse videntur: dicunt enim καὶ Βαναίας υἱὸς Ἰωδαὲ σύμβουλος καὶ ὁ Χελεθὶ καὶ ὁ Φελεθί. At Hebræorum alii familias Israeliticas fuisse censent, Chaldæus sagittarios, a qua significatione non abit Corytus: rursum alii partes Philisthinorum: quod si admittimus, forte horum כרתי, posteri erunt Cretes: certe milites fuisse satis apparet 20, 23.

FILII AVTEM DAVID SACERDOTES ERANT] Fieri id non potuit per legem. Sed error est in voce. Verbum כהן, unde id nomen venit, significat λειτουργεῖν: inde participium in verbalis significationem transiens, si ad Deum expresse aut tacite referatur, significat λειτουργὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ, sacerdotem: si ad Regem, ejus ministrum, puta αὐλάρχην, ut hic posuere LXX. quomodo & Chaldæi hic sumunt & Hebræi, qui addunt indignatum Absalomum, quod non & ipsi talis ἀυλαρχία obtigisset. Nec aliter nomen כהן sumi videtur infra 20, 26. Et in Paralipomenis explicatur per primos ad manum Regis. 1. 18, 17. Videtur idem officium 1. Reg. 4, 5. vocari על הנצבים, ubi Græci, ἐπὶ τῶν καθεσταμένων.

Corrigit hic Grotius vulgatam versionem, quam alias pro authentica habuit. Notanda etiam hic Cornel. à Lapide confessio, qui haud obscure vulgatæ errorem agnoscit, in voce Sacerdotis.

## 9:1 Argument
CHAPTER IX. David restores Saul's lands to Mephibosheth, joins Ziba to him as steward, and places him at his royal table.

Latin:

CAPUT IX. David Mephibosetho fundos Saulis restituit, Sibam œconomum ei adjungit, istumque ad regiam suam mensam collocat.

## 9:7
Verse 7.

I WILL RESTORE TO THEE ALL THE LANDS OF SAUL THY FATHER) Confiscated for the reason that Saul's descendants had been on the side of Ishbosheth. The decision regarding such goods rested with the King. See below 12, 8.

Understand the lands which Saul had before he became King: for it is agreed by common law that those which he acquired after becoming King devolved to the successor King.

AND THOU SHALT EAT BREAD AT MY TABLE CONTINUALLY) Thus the King released him from the law established by himself, that the lame should not enter into the palace.

That passage 2 Sam. 7, 8. is ignorant of this law. Let those things be seen which we have observed there.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

RESTITVAM TIBI OMNES AGROS SAVL PATRIS TVI) Confiscatos ideo quod Saulis posteri in partibus fuerant Isbosethi. Talium bonorum penes Regem erat arbitrium. Vide infra 12, 8.

Fundos intellige, quos Saul antequam Rex fieret, habebat: quos enim Rex factus comparavit, ad successorem Regem devolutos esse jure communi constat.

ET TV COMEDES PANEM IN MENSA MEA SEMPER) Ita Rex eum solvit lege a se constituta, ne claudi in regiam intrarent.

Locus ille 2. Sam. 7, 8. hanc legem ignorat. Videantur, quæ illic observavimus.

## 9:10
Verse 10.

WORK THEREFORE AND THE LAND) By the right of sharecroppers, as it seems.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

OPERARE IGITVR ET TERRAM TV) Jure coloni partiarii, ut videtur.

## 9:11
Verse 11.

HE SHALL EAT AT MY TABLE AS ONE OF THE KING'S SONS) If he should wish to lodge with me, it will be an honor to him as to a King's son.

The passage is rightly explained conditionally with Sanctius, so that it may not conflict with the preceding words. Compare Cornelius à Lapide here.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

COMEDET SVPER MENSAM MEAM QVASI VNVS DE FILIIS REGIS) Si apud me divertere voluerit, honor ei erit ut Regis filio.

Recte conditionaliter explicatur locus cum Sanctio, ne pugnet cum verbis præcedentibus. Confer. Cornel. à Lapide hic.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAPTER X. The King of Ammon, having treated David's envoys with injury, is defeated along with the Syrians.

Latin:

CAPUT X. Rex Ammon legatis Davidis injuria affectis, cum Syris cæditur.

## 10:2
Verse 2.

I WILL SHOW KINDNESS) The Hebrew חסד signifies every kind of benevolence.

CONSOLING HIM BY HIS SERVANTS CONCERNING THE DEATH OF HIS FATHER) A custom of friendly Kings among themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

FACIAM MISERICORDIAM) חסד Hebræum omne benignitatis genus significat.

CONSOLANS EVM PER SERVOS SVOS SVPER PATRIS INTERITV) Mos amicorum Regum inter se.

## 10:3
Verse 3.

DO YOU THINK THAT FOR THE HONOR OF YOUR FATHER DAVID HAS SENT CONSOLERS TO YOU, AND NOT FOR THE PURPOSE OF INVESTIGATING) I might not poorly adapt here those lines from Seneca's Oedipus: CR. What if I am innocent? OED. Kings are accustomed to fear doubtful things as true. CR. He who fears vain terrors confesses true ones.

There is nothing so good that it does not sometimes receive corrupt interpreters in the court.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

PVTAS QVOD PROPTER HONOREM PATRIS TVI MISERIT AD TE DAVID CONSOLATORES, ET NON IDEO VT INVESTIGARET) Non male hic aptaverim illa ex Oedipode Senecæ: CR. Quid si innocens sum? OED. Dubia pro veris solent Timere Reges. CR. Qui pavet vanos metus Veros fatetur.

Nihil est tam bonum, quod non in aula pravos interdum interpretes recipiat.

## 10:4
Vers. 4.

AND HE SHAVED OFF HALF OF THEIR BEARD] Thus to pluck the beard is among the most insulting of acts.

HE CUT OFF THEIR GARMENTS IN THE MIDDLE) Namely from the middle to the bottom, so that those parts might be exposed which modesty wishes to be covered.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

RASITQVE DIMIDIAM PARTEM BARBÆ EORVM] Sic barbam vellere inter contumeliosa maxime.

PRÆSCIDIT VESTES EORVM MEDIAS) Nempe a medio ad imum, ut ea nudarentur quæ tegi vult honestas.

## 10:7
Vers. 7. JOAB SENT AND ALL THE ARMY OF WARRIORS) The Romans undertook wars against the Tarentines, Illyrians, Ligurians, Senones, Issians, and Corinthians because of ambassadors treated contumeliously, as we noted in the second book of the Law of War and Peace, chapter 18, at the end. We also read that the Germans and Turks once undertook wars for a similar reason: nor is it a wonder, since the law of nations, which ought to be most sacred, was violated, as well as the dignity of him who sent them. See the severe punishments exacted for this crime at the end of the following chapter.

Latin:

Vers. 7. MISIT JOAB ET OMNEM EXERCITVM BELLATORVM) Ob legatos contumeliose habitos Ro- mani bella sumsere in Tarentinos, Illyrios, Ligures, Seno- nas, Issios, Corinthios, ut notavimus ad librum secundum de Jure Belli ac Pacis cap. 18. in fine.
