Etiam Germanos & Tur- cas olim pari de causa bella suscepisse legimus: nec mirum cum & jus gentium violaretur, quod sanctissimum esse de- bet, & ejus qui misit dignitas. Vide graves poenas de hoc crimine exactas fine capitis sequentis.

## 10:14
Vers. 14. BECAUSE THEY HAD FLED) As those are often accustomed to do who, with no regard for the cause, fight for pay alone: as those who, having been rashly gathered, had neither honor in victory nor disgrace in flight: Tacitus says in History 2: wherefore Joab prudently judged that the foreign and mercenary troops should be attacked first, before the armies of the enemies were joined.

Latin:

Vers. 14. QVIA FVGISSENT STRI) Vt saepe solent qui nullo causae respectu, mercede sola militant: Vt quibus temere collectis, neque in victoria decus esset, neque in fuga fla- gitium: ait Histor. 2. Tacitus: quare prudenter Joab, ante- quam conjuncti essent hostium exercitus, externos & pretio conductos prius impugnandos censuit.

## 10:15
Vers. 15. THEY WERE GATHERED TOGETHER) Fearing that, as is wont to happen, David might exact punishment from the helper of his enemies: which also happened. See below 19.

Latin:

Vers. 15. CONGREGATI SVNT PARITER) Metuen- tes, ne, ut fieri solet, ab auxiliatore hostium suorum poenas David deposceret: quod & factum est. Vid. infra 19.

## 10:18
Vers. 18. SEVEN HUNDRED CHARIOTS) More correctly 1 Chron. 19:18, seven thousand chariots. An error of number committed here by the copyists.

Again, there is no necessity that we admit an error here, where the translations also agree with the Hebrew text. For it can be said with Tirinus that the 700 were principal chariots of illustrious persons, and heavy or more ample and larger chariots for the nobler riders: but seven thousand chariots in total: Or it may be understood, as seems to others, in the book of Chronicles, seven thousand soldiers fighting in or from the chariots, by seven thousand chariots, because ten soldiers fought in individual chariots, as Menochius reconciles, as well as the Weimar Paraphrasts, and the Belgian, likewise Junius, and Piscator. For there are added to the number of the slain horsemen of the others, forty thousand, in Chronicles as many footmen, so that the total sum of the slain is 80,000, besides those 7,000 who fought from the chariots; to which opinion Menochius brings Lyranus, Abulensis, Vatablus, Salianus, and Sanctius, which is also the calculation of Cornelius a Lapide and our Dr. Walther in his Harmony of the Bible. Or if with Tirinus seven thousand less principal chariots are meant, and it is also said that some horsemen from that sum of slain horsemen were seated, likewise 80,000 will be counted as killed, besides those nobler ones who fought carried in the seven hundred prior chariots, the number of whom was not expressed.

SOBACH) שׁוֹבַךְ: but 1 Chron. 19:18, שׁוֹפַךְ. Which is more correct, I would not say.

Latin:

Vers. 18. SEPTINGENTOS CVRRVS) Rectius 1. Par. 19, 18. septem millia curruum. Error numeri hic commissus ab exscriptoribus.

Iterum nulla est necessitas, ut errorem hic ad- mittamus, ubi consonant etiam textui Ebraeo trans- lationes. Dici enim potest cum Tirino, 700. cur- rus principales fuisse illustrium personarum, & equi- tibus nobilioribus graves, vel ampliores currus, & majores: Septem millia autem curruum in univer- sum: Vel intelligi, quod aliis videtur, in libr. Para- lip. septem millia militum in curribus, vel ex curribus pugnantium, per septem millia curruum, quia in sin- gulis curribus decem pugnarunt milites, uti Me- nochius conciliat, nec non Paraphrasta Vinarienses, & Belga, Junius item, ac Piscator. Adduntur enim numero caesorum equitum caeterorum quadragin- ta millium, in Paralipomenis totidem pedites, ut sum- ma universa caesorum sit 80000. praeter illos 7000. qui de curribus pugnarunt; in quam sententiam Menochius adducit Lyranum, Abulensem, Vata- blum, Salianum & Sanctium, quae etiam est Cornelii a Lapide, & Dn. D. Waltheri nostri supputatio in Harm. Bibl. Vel si cum Tirino septem millibus curru- um minus principalium, etiam dicantur equites non- nulli de ista caesorum equitum summa insedisse, itidem 80000. occisi numerabuntur, praeter illos nobiliores, qui curribus septingentis prioribus invecti pugnarunt, quo- rum numerus expressus non fuerit.

SOBACH) שׁוֹבַךְ: at 1. Paralip. 19, 18. שׁוֹפַךְ. Vtrum rectius, non dixerim.

## 10:19
Vers. 19. AND THEY SERVED THEM) They became tributaries.

PART II. THE UNHAPPY STATE OF DAVID.

SECTION I. THE CAUSE OF THE MORE UNHAPPY STATE.

CHAPTER XI. David's fall into adultery and homicide.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET SERVIERVNT EIS) Vectigales facti sunt.

PARS II. INFELIX DAVIDIS STATUS.

SECTIO I. CAUSA INFELICIORIS STATUS.

CATUT XI. Lapsus Davidis in Adulterium, & homici- dium.

## 11:1 Argument
Vers. 1. AT THE TIME WHEN KINGS ARE ACCUSTOMED TO GO FORTH TO WAR) In the spring, as Kimchi interprets here. Thus 1 Chron. 20:1.

BUT DAVID REMAINED IN JERUSALEM) Ovid: The question is asked why Aegisthus became an adulterer: the cause is at hand, he was idle.

THEY BESIEGED RABBAH) Which is Rabathamana, that is, of Ammon, according to Polybius.

Latin:

Vers. 1. EO TEMPORE QVO SOLENT REGES AD BEL- LVM PROCEDERE) Vere, ut hic interpretatur Kimchi. Sic 1. Paral. 20, 1.

DAVID AVTEM REMANSIT IN JERVSALEM) Ovidius: Quaeritur Aegisthus quare sit factus adulter: In promtu causa est, desidiosus erat.

OBSEDERVNT RABBA) Quae Rabathamana, id est, Ammonis Polybio.

## 11:2
Ver. 2. WASHING HIMSELF) For they had baths in their gardens, imprudently.

Latin:

Vers. 2. SE LAVANTEM) Habebant enim in hortis balnea, im- prudenter.

## 11:4
AND HE SLEPT WITH HER) In vain do the Jews excuse both this and the murder of Uriah, procured by evil counsel, contrary to what Nathan showed him, and he himself acknowledged in Psalm 51, and Josephus, who rightly calls it a terrible fall, and God judged below 27. 12, 11. Doubtless, long power and flatterers easily corrupt even the best Kings. By the indulgence of fortune and

by depraved teachers they learn and dare, says Tacitus, Histories 2, who also elsewhere says that by long duration they are changed into pride.

Ver. 4.

AND IMMEDIATELY SHE WAS SANCTIFIED FROM HER UNCLEANNESS) In the Hebrew: and she was then purified from her uncleanness. This was added for this reason, so that we might not wonder that she conceived immediately. Φύσει καὶ ἐν ἧ σύλληψις γίνεται μετὰ τὴν τότων ἀπαλλαγὴν ταῖς γυναιξὶ, says Aristotle in the History of Animals, book 7, chapter 20. Bathsheba seems to have been a woman not unchaste, but one who, in the hope of dominion, like Agrippina the mother of Nero, would deny nothing. So much more burning is the desire for ruling than all other passions, as Tacitus says, Annals 15, c. 53.

Latin:

ET DORMIVIT CVM EA) Frustra & hoc & cae- dem Vriae malo consilio procuratam excusant Judaei, con- tra quam Nathan ei ostendit, & ipse agnovit Psal. 51. & Jo- sephus, qui πταῖσμα δεινὸν merito vocat, & Deus judicavit in- fra 27. 12, 11. Nimirum etiam optimos Reges facile longa potentia & adulatores corrumpunt. Indulgentia fortuna &

pravis magistris discunt audentque, ait Tacitus Histor. 2. qui & alibi diuturnitate eos in superbiam mutari dicit.

Vers. 4.

STATIMQVE SANCTIFICATA EST AB IM- MVNDITIA SVA) In Hebræo: & ipsa tunc purgatur ab immunditia sua. Hoc ideo additum, ne miraremur illico eam concepisse. Φύσει καὶ ἐν ἧ σύλληψις γίνεται μετὰ τὴν τότων ἀπαλλαγὴν ταῖς γυναιξὶ, ait Aristoteles de Historia Animantium libro 7. cap. 20. Videtur Bethsabea fuisse fœ- mina non impudica, sed quæ spe dominationis, ut Agrippina mater Neronis nihil abnueret. Adeo cupido dominandi cun- ctis affectibus flagrantior est, ut Tacitus ait Annal. 15. c.53.

## 11:9
Ver. 9.

AND HE DID NOT GO DOWN TO HIS HOUSE) God willing that this shameful act of a King so well instructed should be made manifest.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ET NON DESCENDIT AD DOMVM SVAM) Deo volente patefieri hoc Regis tam bene instituti flagitium.

## 11:11
Ver. 11.

THE ARK OF GOD) Which was accustomed to be carried into the camps as a testimony of God's favor.

BUT the ark of the covenant remained in Zion, 2 Sam. 6, 12; 1 Kings 8, 1, nor was it to be moved from its place except by the special command of God: Whence Don Isaac Abarbanel, in his Commentary on the former Prophets, observes that the Israelites, when they had been slaughtered by their enemies, sinned gravely and were punished for seeking and bringing it out of the tabernacle without the permission of God and without consulting His mouth, and that the ark itself was captured. He therefore explains this passage as referring to another ark, in which were the Ephod with Urim and Thummim, which they led with them into war, and with it the Priest, so that when necessity compelled them, they could consult the word of the Lord through him. And he understands the passage 1 Sam. 14, 18 also to refer to this ark; for the ark of the covenant was then in Kiriath-jearim, not in the hands of Ahijah, 1 Sam. 7. Compare 1 Sam. 30, 8, concerning which one may read Buxtorf, History of the Ark of the Covenant, chapter 3, p. 44, et seqq.

MY LORD JOAB) Master of the soldiers.

THEY REMAIN UPON THE FACE OF THE EARTH) They lie on the ground, as is the custom in camps. He shows himself as a good soldier to be away from luxuries.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ARCA DEI) Quæ in castra ferri solebat, ut testimonium Dei faventis.

AT arca fœderis in Sione manebat, 2. Sam. 6, 12. 1. Reg. 8, 1. neque transferenda fuit de lo- co suo, nisi ex speciali Dei mandato: Unde Israeli- tas, cum ab inimicis suis cæsi essent, eam sine venia Dei, & ore ejus inconsulto ex tabernaculo peten- tes, & educentes graviter peccasse, & punitos, ar- camque ipsam captam fuisse observat Don Isaac A- barbenel in Comment. in priores Prophetas. Hunc ergo locum explicat de alia arca, in qua fuerunt E- phod cum Urim & Thummim, quam secum in bellum ducebant, & cum ea Sacerdotem, ut necessitate cogente per ipsum verbum Domini consulere pos- sint. Et de hac arca intelligit etiam locum 1. Sam. 14, 18. nam arca fœderis tum erat in Kiriathjearim, non in manibus Achiæ, 1. Sam. 7. Conf. 1. Sam. 30, 8. quo de legi poterit Buxtorff. Histor. arc. fœder. cap. 3. p. 44. seqq.

DOMINVS MEVS JOAB) Magister militum.

SVPER FACIEM TERRÆ MANENT) Humi cu- bant, ut fit in castris. Ostendit se ut bonum militem abesse a delitiis.

## 11:14
Verse 14.

DAVID WROTE A LETTER TO JOAB, AND SENT IT BY THE HAND OF URIAH) Thus Proetus gave Bellerophon letters to Iobates, by which the death of Bellerophon was ordered. Homer and others mention this.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

SCRIPSIT DAVID EPISTOLAM AD JOAB, MI- SITQVE PER MANVM VRIÆ) Sic Prœtus Bellero- phonti dedit literas ad Jobaten, quibus Bellerophontis nex mandabatur. Meminit Homerus & alii.

## 11:15
Verse 15.

AND ABANDON HIM THAT HE MAY BE STRUCK DOWN AND DIE) Although it is indeed permitted for a King to use the service of subjects in dangers, he who does so for the purpose of possessing the wife of another, even if adultery had not preceded it, would commit a sin against the law: Thou shalt not covet. Furthermore, if those who abandon good fellow-soldiers in such dangers sin, what of him who orders them to be abandoned? Tiberius exposed Germanicus, who was hateful to him, to treachery and accidents. Tacitus narrates this in Annals 2.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ET DERELINQVITE EVM VT PERCVSSVS INTEREAT) Licet quidem Regi subditorum opera in pe- riculis uti, sed qui ideo id facit, ut uxore alterius potiatur, et- iam si adulterium non præcessisset, committeret in legem: Non concupisces. Deinde si peccant qui talibus in periculis bonos commilites deserunt, quid qui deseri jubet? Tiberius Germanicum sibi invisum dolo & casibus objectabat. Taci- tus narrat Annal. 2.

## 11:21
Verse 21.

WHO STRUCK ABIMELECH?) See Judges 9:53 and the notes there.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

QVIS PFRCVSSIT ABIMELECH?) Vide Jud. 9, 53. & ibi notata.

## 11:26
Verse 26.

AND SHE MOURNED FOR HIM) With such tears as Caesar did for Pompey. Concerning whom Lucan says: - - - and the good father-in-law thought it was now safe to be. Thus, no one mourned the death of Germanicus more ostentatiously than those who were most joyful. These are the words of Domitius Celer in Book 2 of Tacitus' Annals.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

ET PLANXIT EVM) Lachrymis qualibus Cæsar Pompejum. De quo Lucanus: - - - tutumque putavit Iam bonus esse socer. Sic periisse Germanicum nulli jactantius mœrebant, quam qui maxime lætabantur. Verba sunt Domitii Celeris An- nal. 2. Taciti.

## 11:27
Verse 27.

AND THIS THING WAS DISPLEASING) That is, the matter, namely the adultery joined to the marriage, 12:9. Nor, however, were those nuptials invalid, nor was the son born afterwards any less legitimate on that account. For many things in this category are not done properly, which are nevertheless valid. Nor is it in vain that Bathsheba is explicitly named in the genealogy of Christ, so that the Jews, warned by her example, might be less averse to those foreigners who, once covered in vices, had amended their lives.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

ET DISPLICVIT VERBVM HOC) Id est, res, nempe adulterium nuptiis conglutinatum 12, 9. Neque tamen ir- ritæ fuere eæ nuptiæ, neque filius postea natus ob id minus legitimus. Multa enim in hoc genere non probe fiunt, quæ tamen rata sunt. Nec frustra Bethsabea in genealogia Chri- sti diferte nominatur, ut ejus exemplo moniti Judæi minus aversarentur illos alienigenas, qui vitiis quondam obsiti vi- tam emendaverant.

## 12:1 Argument
CHAPTER XII.

Nathan's correction. David's penitence. The death of the little son, and the birth of Solomon. Rabbah captured.

Ver. 1. TWO MEN WERE) It is an αἶνος both apt and prudent. For because, as is in the old proverb, A man always carries one thing in himself, and judges another in someone else, therefore he proposed the matter in such a way that the Prophet had no need to condemn the King, but the King condemned himself.

Latin:

CAPUT XII.

Nathanis ἐπανόρθωσις. Davidis pœnitentia. Mors filioli, & nativitas Salomonis. Rabba capta.

Vers. 1. DVO VIRI ERANT) Est αἶνος & appositus & prudens. Nam quia ut in vetere proverbio est, Semper homo aliud in se fert, aliud in alio judicat, ideo ita rem propofuit, ut non opus haberet Propheta Re- gem damnare, sed Rex semet ipse damnaret.

## 12:5
HE IS A SON OF DEATH) He has deserved death, on account of his extreme wickedness, which causes the penalty to be extended often even beyond the laws.

Latin:

FILIVS MORTIS EST) Mortem meruit, ob summam improbitatem, quæ facit ut sæpe etiam supra leges pœna in- tendatur.

Verse 6.

Verse 8.

I GAVE THEE THE HOUSE OF THY MASTER) By title of confiscation, on account of the faction of Ishbosheth.

THY MASTER'S WIVES INTO THY BOSOM) The widows of a King could not marry anyone except the King, according to custom.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

DEDI TIBI DOMVM DOMINI TVI) Titulo con- fiscationis, ob partes Isbosethi.

VXORES DOMINI TVI IN SINV TVO) Viduæ Regis nisi Regi nubere non poterant ex moribus.

## 12:9
Verse 9. THOU HAST KILLED HIM WITH THE SWORD OF THE CHILDREN OF AMMON) As if to say: you exposed him to wild beasts. He kills who gives an unjust occasion for death.

Latin:

Vers. 9. INTERFECISTI EVM GLADIO FILIO- RVM AMMON) Quafi diceres: feris eum objecisti. Inter- fecit qui injustam morti occasionem dat.

## 12:10
Verse 10. THE SWORD SHALL NEVER DEPART FROM THINE HOUSE) As long as you live. For thus the word עד-עולם is taken differently according to the subject matter. These things are to be referred to the violent deaths of the sons of David, Amnon, Absalom, and near the very end of David's life, Adonijah,

Latin:

Vers. 10. NON RECEDIT GLADIVS TVVS DE DO- MO TVA VSQVE IN SEMPITERNVM) Dum vives. Ita enim vox עד-עולם fumitur pro subjecta materia diverse. Referenda hæc ad mortes violentas filiorum Da- vid, Ammonis, Absolomi, & sub ipsum finem Davidis, Adoniæ,

## 12:11
Verse 11. I WILL RAISE UP EVIL AGAINST THEE OUT OF THINE OWN HOUSE) God is said to do what He does not prevent. Thus also to take away and to give in the following.

I WILL TAKE THY WIVES BEFORE THINE EYES, AND GIVE THEM UNTO THY NEIGHBOUR) That is here, to your son: below 16, 21.

Latin:

Vers. 11. SVSCITABO SVPER TE MALVM DE DOMO TVA) Deus facere dicitur, quod non impedit. Sic & tollere & dare in fequentibus.

TOLLAM VXORES TVAS IN OCVLIS TVIS, ET DABO PROXIMO TVO) Id est hic, filio tuo: infra 16, 21.

## 12:13
Verse 13. I HAVE SINNED AGAINST THE LORD) A confession of repentance is a welcome companion.

YOU SHALL NOT DIE) David was indeed above the punishments of the law, as King, and after him even the Queen. But God had threatened that He would be the avenger of those things which the magistrates could not or would not punish, Leviticus 26:14. Yet He had not thereby taken away from Himself the power of pardoning, which He uses here in such a way that He frees David from the sole penalty of death and the loss of the kingdom, though He was to inflict many other evils upon him otherwise.

Latin:

Vers. 13. PECCAVI DOMINO) Confessio pœnitentiæ grata comes.

NON MORIERIS) Erat quidem David supra legis pœ- nas, ut Rex, & post ipsum etiam Regina. Sed Deus eorum quæ magistratus punire non poterant aut nolebant, se vindi- cem fore minatus erat Levitici 26, 14. Non eo tamen sibi ademerat ignoscendi potestatem, qua hic ita utitur, ut sola mortis pœna & amittendi regni, Davidem liberet, multa alioqui mala alia ei inflicturus.

## 12:14
Verse 14. BECAUSE YOU HAVE CAUSED THE ENEMIES OF THE LORD TO BLASPHEME) A grave addition to the sin, to give occasion to the impious nations to think ill of the divine law which they see despised by the leaders of the Hebrews.

Latin:

Vers. 14. QYONIAM BLASPHEMARE FECISTI INIMICOS DOMINI) Gravis ad peccatum accessio, oc- cafionem dare impiis gentibus male sentiendi de lege divina quam sperni a primis Hebræorum videant.

## 12:16
Verse 16. HE FASTED A FAST AND WENT IN AND LAY ON THE GROUND) Fasting, sleeping apart from one's wife, squalor, sleeping on the ground, vile garments, weeping, are the nourishment of prayer. See below 20, 21, 24. That David was affectionate appears not only from this history, but also from his indulgence regarding Absalom and Adonijah.

Latin:

Vers. 16. JEJVNAVIT JEJVNIO ET INGRESSVS SEORSVM JACVIT SVPER TERRAM) Jejunium, se- cubatio ab uxore, illuvies, χαμευνία, viles vestes, fletus, ali- menta sunt precationis. Vide infra 20. 21. 24. Fuisse Davide n Φιλόσοργον, non ex hac tantum historia, sed & ex indulgen- tia circa Absalomum & Adoniam apparet.

## 12:23
Verse 23. BUT NOW SINCE HE IS DEAD, WHY SHOULD I FAST?) It is no light sign of repentance to acquiesce in the punishments which God has sent on account of sins.

Verse 23. I SHALL RATHER GO TO HIM) The Romans used to say: Farewell, we shall all follow you in the order that nature permits: as Servius testifies on the 3rd Aeneid, and in inscriptions. Antiphanes: 'The same road which all must necessarily travel, they have already gone.'

The gloss is too diluted. For such things are not to be learned from the Gentiles, who have no hope of either blessedness or resurrection, 1 Thess. 4:9. They hinted at nothing other than the necessity of dying incumbent upon all; they had no knowledge of the state of eternal life. But shall we judge the same of David, filled with the Spirit of the Lord? David is certainly consoling himself here, and raising himself up with the hope of a future reunion, as the express words have it: I shall go to Him. Therefore, that cold gloss of Grotius does not even reach the mark; for what comfort is there from that dire dart of the necessity of death? Nor does it express the force of the words. For he does not say only that he will go the way of all flesh, nor that he will follow in his own time, but he says, I shall go to him, and thus he trusts that he will be joined with him after his death, in the life of the blessed, when his soul shall be bound in the bundle of the living, 1 Sam. 25:29. But such jejune Grotian interpretations betray the Pelagian error of the man, which he sets forth more openly elsewhere; that the ancients did not have a certain promise, confidence, and hope of a blessed life, which is refuted by the plain words of David in Psalm 17:15 (to say nothing of others now), nay, it can be convicted even from this passage.

Latin:

Vers. 23. NVNC AVTEM QVIA MORTVVS EST, QVARE JEJVNEM?) Non leve fignum pœnitentiæ, in pœnis quas Deus ob peccata immisit, acquiescere.

Vers. 23. EGO VADAM MAGIS AD EVM) Romani dicebant: Fale, nos te ordine quo natura permiserit, cuncti se- quemur: Teste Servio ad 3. Æneidos, & in inscriptionibus. Antiphanes: τὴν ἀυτὴν ὁδὸν ἣν πᾶσιν ἐλθεῖν ἐς᾿ ἀναγκαίως ἔχου προεληλυθασιν.

Glossa nimis diluta. Nec enim talia a gentilibus discenda, qui nullam spem vel beatitudinis vel resurrectionis habent 1. Thessal. 4, 9. Hi nihil aliud, quam moriendi necessitatem omnibus incumbentem innuerunt, de statu æternæ vitæ nihil cognitum habuerunt. Num vero idem de Davide censebimus, pleno Spiritu Domini? Solatur utique hic David, atque erigit semetipsum spe futuræ conjunctionis, uti verba expressa habent: Ego vadam ad Eum. Itaque nec scopum frigida illa Glossa Grotii attingit, ecquid enim solatii a diro illo necessitatis mortis telo? Nec verborum vim exprimit. Non enim tantum se viam universæ carnis iturum, non se tempore suo sequuturum dicit, sed vadam, inquit, ad eum, adeoque se cum ipso post fata sua conjunctum iri, in vita beatorum, confidit, cum in fasciculum viventium colligabitur anima 1. Sam. 24, 29. Sed jejunæ ejusmodi interpretationes Grotianæ produnt errorem hominis Pelagianum, quem alias apertius edifferit; quod veteres certam promissionem, fiduciam, ac spem beatæ vitæ non habuerint, qui desertis verbis Davidis Psalm. 17. ult. (ut alia nunc taceamus) refellitur, imo ex hoc etiam loco convinci potest.

## 12:28
Verse 28. TAKE IT) Curtius relates a similar matter regarding Craterus at the siege of Artacacna: He, with all things prepared, awaited the arrival of the King, yielding the title of the captured city (as was right).

Latin:

Vers. 28. CAPE EAM) Curtius rem similem de Cra- tero narrat in Artacacnæ obsidione: Ille omnibus preparatis Regis expectabat adventum, capta urbis titulo (sicut par erat) cedens.

## 12:30
Verse 30. IT WAS PLACED UPON THE HEAD OF DAVID) In the Hebrew: it was upon the head of David, which they interpret: it fit David's head so well, as if it had been properly destined for him. Not only the crown, but all the finery and furniture of the conquered King yielded to the conquering King, as the Talmudists note. A similar thing is found among the Macedonians: It was a handed-down custom that they should receive the victor in the tent of the conquered king, according to Curtius. See what we have annotated on the third book of the Law of War and Peace, chapter 6, § 24, and add 1 Chronicles 20:2.

It is said to have had the weight of a talent of gold. A talent of gold is 120 pounds, equivalent to 12,000 Hungarian gold pieces: as we said in Exodus 25:39 and chapter 38:25. How could such a weight be placed upon a head? Therefore, others understand a smaller talent, which was 60 pounds: some wish for the Syrian talent to be understood, which was only 25 pounds: but since this weight is also very inconvenient for a head, and Villalpandus does not recognize different species of talents, it pleases some to explain the name Melachim there not as King, but as the idol of the Ammonites, which could have borne such a weight. But history hardly admits that an idol is meant, since King is opposed to King, namely David to the King of the Ammonites: and because that diadem is said to have been placed upon the head of David, the difficulty still remains, how it could have been sustained? Which perhaps will not be badly solved if the name mishqal, which is translated as weight, is taken for the value and price, that this crown was estimated at a talent of gold, or was worth that much in price, on account of the craftsmanship and gems with which it was adorned.

Latin:

Vers. 30. IMPOSITVM EST SUPER CAPVT DA- VID) In Hebræo: fuit fupra caput David, quod interpre- tantur: ita bene convenit Davidis capiti, quasi ei proprie fu- isset destinata. Regis victi non corona tantum, sed omnis ornatus ac supellex Regi victori cedebat, ut Thalmudistæ no- tant. Simile illud apud Macedonas: Tradito more ut victorem vistivegis tabernaculo exciperent, apud Curtium. Vide quæ annotavimus ad librum tertium de Jure Belli ac Pacis cap. 6. §. 24. & adde 1. Paralip. 20, 2.

Dicitur babuisse pondus talenti auri. Auri talentum est 120. librarum, æquivalens 12000. aureis Ungaricis: ut Exod. 25, 39. cap. 38, 25. diximus. Quomodo tantum pondus capiti imponi potuit? Ideo alii talentum minus intelligunt, quod fuerit 60. librarum: nonnulli talentum Syrorum, quod tantum 25. librarum fuerit, intelligi volunt: sed quum & hoc pondus capiti valde incommodum, nec agnoscant Villalpandus talenti diversas species, placet quibusdam nomen Melachim ibi explicare non pro Rege, sed pro idolo Ammonitarum, quod ferre tantum pondus potuerit. At historia vix admittit idolum intelligi, quum Rex Regi opponatur, David nempe Ammonitarum Regi: & quia Davidis capiti impositum illud diadema Regis Ammonitarum dicitur, manet adhuc difficultas, quomodo id sustineri potuerit? Quæ fortassis non male solvetur, si nomen משקל quod pondus vertitur, accipiatur pro valore & pretio, quod corona ista æstimata fuerit talento auri, vel valuerit tanto pretio, propter artificium & gemmas, quibus ornata fuit.

## 12:31
Vers. 31. HE SAWED) A punishment not unknown to those lands, by which the Hebrews say Isaiah was also afflicted by Manasseh. See Heb. 11, 37. The Emperor Valens used the same against certain soldiers. Examples of this punishment are also in Swedish, Turkish, and Neapolitan history.

SECTION II.

EVILS THAT FOLLOWED THE SIN OF DAVID IN HIS HOUSE AND KINGDOM.

Latin:

Vers. 31. SERVAVIT) Non incognitum istis terris supplicium, quo & Esaiam affectum a Manasse ajunt Hebræi. Vide Hebr. 11, 37. Idem in milites quosdam usurpavit Valens Imperator. Sunt ejus supplicii exempla & in Historia Suedica, Turcica & Neapolitana.

SECTIO II.

MALA SEQUUTA PECCATUM DAVIDIS IN DOMO ET REGNO EJUS.

## 13:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIII.

The incest of Ammon with Tamar, and the killing done by Absalom, on account of which he was a fugitive.

Latin:

CAPUT XIII.

Ammonis incestus cum Thamar, & occisio per Absolomum facta, ob id profugum.

## 13:2
Vers. 2.

AND HE LOVED HER EXCEEDINGLY) Love conceived from beauty alone, the more dishonest it is, the stronger it is wont to be, as the human disposition strives toward what is forbidden. Ammon, like Domitian in Tacitus, played the prince's son through debaucheries and adulteries.

THAT HE FELL SICK) For physicians also count among diseases that which is contracted from love.

Pale, the son of Orion wandered in Lyrisen.

WHEN SHE WAS A VIRGIN] That is, she was well guarded, as virgins were accustomed to be. See at Matt. 1, 23.

IT SEEMED DIFFICULT TO HIM TO DO ANYTHING DISHONESTLY WITH HER) In the Hebrew it is to do, which in that language, no less than in Latin, signifies what this interpreter expressed through circumlocution. Thus Gen. 19, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET DEPERIRET EAM VALDE) Amor ex forma fola conceptus, quo magis est inhonestus, eo solet effe validior, nitente in vetitum humano ingenio. Ammon, ut Domitianus apud Tacitum, stupris & adulteriis filium Principis agebat.

UT ÆGROTARET) Nam & Medici morbis accensent eum, qui ex amore contrahitur.

Pallidus in Lyrisen filius errabat Orion.

CUM ESSET VIRGO] Id est, bene custodiretur, ut folebant Virgines. Vide ad Matth. 1, 23.

DIFFICILE EI VIDEBATUR UT QVIPPIAM INHONESTE AGERET CUM EA) In Hebræo est facere, quod in ea lingua non minus quam Latina id significat, quod interpres hic per circumlocutionem expressit. Sic Genes. 19, 8.

## 13:5
Vers. 5. TO WHOM JONADAB ANSWERED) One of those whose custom it is to praise everything of princes, honest and dishonest alike, as Tacitus speaks in the third book of the Annals.

Latin:

Vers. 5. CVI RESPONDIT JONADAB) Vnus eorum, quibus omnia Principum, honesta atque inhonesta, laudare mos est, ut Tacitus loquitur tertio Annalium.

## 13:12
Verse 12.

FOR THIS IS NOT RIGHT IN ISRAEL] He had heard enough that this people ought to be holier than other peoples.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

NEQVE ENIM HOC FAS EST IN ISRAEL] Satis audierat populum hunc sanctiorem aliis populis esse debere.

## 13:13
Verse 13.

FOR I SHALL NOT BE ABLE TO BEAR MY REPROACH) Τὴν ὕβριν, as the Greeks say. LXX. τὸ ὀνειδος μου.

AND YOU WILL BE AS ONE OF THE FOOLISH IN ISRAEL) ὡς ἓ' ἀφρόνων here in the LXX. For ἀφροσύνη is said by a certain proper right concerning matters of Venus, Hecuba in the Troades of Euripides:

Τὰ μῶρα γὰρ πάντ' ἐςὶν ἀφροδίτη βροτοῖς, Καὶ τοὔνομ' ὀρθῶς ἀφροσύνης ἄρχει θεᾶς.

BUT RATHER SPEAK TO THE KING, AND HE WILL NOT DENY ME TO YOU) The girl, by no means skilled in the law, thought the right of the King was so great that marriage was not by law could permit the incest of the nations: or he even thought that the marriages of brothers and sisters who were not ὁμομήτριοι were not forbidden: or he said anything whatever to withdraw himself from the present danger. The Hebrews wish Tamar to have been born from David's first intercourse with a woman captured in war: and that for those born in such a way there is no kinship.

On this and other Rabbinical commentaries, consult here Sanctius, and Theodor Hackspan on this passage.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

EGO ENIM FERRE NON POTERO OPPROBRIVM MEVM) Τὴν ὕβριν, ut Græci loquuntur. LXX. τὸ ὀνειδος μκ.

ET TV ERIS QVASI VNVS DE INSIPIENTIBVS IN ISRAEL) ὡς ἓ' ἀφρόνων hic LXX. Nam ἀφροσύνη proprio quodam jure de rebus Venereis dicitur, Hecuba in Troasin Euripidis:

Τὰ μῶρα γὰρ πάντ' ἐςὶν ἀφροδίτη βροτοῖς, Καὶ τοὔνομ' ὀρθῶς ἀφροσύνης ἄρχει θεᾶς.

QVIN POTIVS LOQVERE AD REGEM, ET NON NEGABIT ME TIBI) Puella minime perita juris, tantum esse jus Regis existimavit, ut connubium non jure gentium incestum posset permittere: aut etiam putavit non interdictas nuptias fratrum & sororum qui non essent ὁμο- μήτριοι: aut quidvis dixit ut se præsenti periculo subtrahe- ret. Hebræi natam volunt Thamarem ex primo concubitu Davidis cum bello capta: ita autem genitis nullam esse cognationem.

DE hoc & aliis Rabb. commentis cons. hic San- ctius, & Theodor. Hackspan. in h. l.

## 13:15
Verse 15.

AND HE HATED HER WITH A HATRED VERY GREAT) Olympiodorus, whose excerpts we have by the favor of Photius, narrates the same thing concerning love changed into hatred after desire was satisfied, in the case of Honorius toward his sister Placidia.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ET EXOSAM EAM HABVIT ANNON ODIO MAGNO NIMIS) Idem de amore post cupiditatem ex- pletam in odium mutato Honorii in sororem Placitliam nar- rat Olympiodorus, cujus excerpta habemus Photii bene- ficio.

## 13:18
Verse 18.

WHO WAS CLOTHED IN A ROBE REACHING TO THE ANKLES) What he translates here as reaching to the ankles is פם in the Hebrew, and it signifies a particle and the palm of the hand; those who looked to the former meaning translated it as variegated, that is, πολὺμιτον: those who looked to the latter understood it as having sleeves, which the Greeks, as Gellius also testifies, and as Symmachus had translated here, called χειριδωτὸν: Aquila, a follower of the origins, in this place called it καρπωτόν.

AND SO HIS MINISTER CAST HER OUT) Juvenal: The freedman says, pack up your bundles and get out.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

QVÆ INDUTA ERAT TALARI TUNICA) Quod hic talarem vertit est פס in Hebræo פם & particu- lam significat & volam; qui ad priorem significatum respexe- re, verterunt variam, id est πολὺμιτον: qui ad posteriorem, in- tellexere manuleatam, quam Græci, ut & Gellius testatur, & hic Symmachus verterat, dixere χειριδωτὸν: Aquila originum sectator, hoc loco καρπωτόν.

EJECIT ITAQVE EAM MINISTER ILLIUS FO- RAS) Juvenalis: Colligefarcinulas dicit libertus & exi.

## 13:19
Verse 19.

WHO SPRINKLING ASHES ON HER HEAD, HER ROBE REACHING TO THE ANKLES TORN, AND HAVING PLACED HER HANDS UPON HER HEAD, WENT ALONG CRYING OUT] Similar sadness to that of Lucretia in Livy, book 1.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

QVÆ ASPERGENS CINEREM CAPITI SUO, SCISSA TALARI TUNICA, IMPOSITISQVE MANI- BUS SUPER CAPUT SUUM, IBAT INGREDIENS ET CLAMANS] Similis Lucretiæ mœstitia apud Livium libro 1.

## 13:20
Verse 20.

BUT NOW SISTER BE SILENT: HE IS THY BROTHER) Domestic evils are to be covered over with silence: this is not badly said. Yet Absalom did not feel this, but he did not wish to reveal his deeply hidden plan of taking revenge before the opportunity.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

SED NUNC SOROR TACE: FRATER TUUS EST) Domestica mala silentio obtegenda: non male hoc dictum. Neque tamen hoc sentiebat Absalomus, sed alte ab- ditum ulciscendi consilium prodere ante occasionem no- lebat.

## 13:21
Verse 21.

AND HE WOULD NOT VEX THE SPIRIT OF AMNON HIS SON, BECAUSE HE LOVED HIM, BECAUSE HE WAS HIS FIRSTBORN] These are in the Greek, not in the Hebrew.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

ET NOLUIT CONTRISTARE SPIRITUM AMNO- NIS FILII SUI, QVONIAM DILIGE U, QVIA PRIMOGENITUS ERAT EI] Hæc sunt in Græ- co, non in Hebræo.

## 13:22
Ver. 22.

ABSALOM SPOKE TO AMNON NEITHER GOOD NOR BAD) Concerning that matter, to be sure. For two whole years he dissembled that matter as if he knew nothing of it.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

NON EST LOCUTUS ABSALOM AD AMNON NEC BONUM NEC MALUM) De ea re scilicet. Bien- nio toto eam rem ita dissimulavit, quasi nihil ejus sciret.

## 13:23
Ver. 23.

AND ABSALOM'S SHEEP WERE BEING SHEARED) Cato the Elder, when asked what was the first thing in managing a household, replied 'to graze well,' as Cicero teaches us. At that time, such profit was not thought to be unbecoming to the sons of kings. - - - The gods also inhabited the woods, and Dardanian Paris, as it is in Virgil's second Eclogue.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

ET TONDERENTUR OVES ABSALOM) Cato se- nex interrogatus quid in re familiari esset primum, respondit bene pascere, ut Cicero nos docet. Is tum quæstus Regum filios dedecere non putabatur. - - - habitarunt Dî quoque sylvas Dardaniusque Paris. ut apud Virgilium est Ecloga secunda.

## 13:24
Ver. 24.

BEHOLD THY SERVANTS' SHEEP ARE BEING SHEARED) Just as there was a κουρεῶτις ἑορτή (shearing festival) for boys in the cities, so there was for sheep in the country. For the flocks were counted then, and there was rejoicing over the increase.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ECCE TONDENTUR OVES SERVI TUI) Sicut puerorum in urbibus erat κουρεῶτις ἑορτή, ita ovium ruri. Numerabantur enim tunc pecudes, & de incremento gau- debatur.

## 13:28
Ver. 28.

SMITE HIM AND KILL HIM) Incest drew on parricide, as between Thyestes and Atreus.

FOR I AM HE WHO COMMANDS YOU] The King's son, dear to the King, and with Amnon dead, the heir to the kingdom. From all these things he promised impunity both to himself and to his helpers. See 14, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

PERCUTITE EUM ET INTERFICITE) Incestus traxit parricidium, ut inter Thyesten & Atreum.

EGO ENIM SUM QUI PRÆCIPIO VOBIS] Filius Regis, Regi carus, & Amnone mortuo regni hæres. Ex his omnibus impunitatem & sibi & adjutoribus pollicebatur. Vid. 14, 7.

## 13:37
Ver. 37.

HE FLED TO TALMAI THE SON OF AMMIHUD KING OF GESHUR) He fled to his maternal grandfather, where the laws of God had no place. For cities of refuge would not have delivered up a parricide, although a cause for anger had been given; only murder could be avenged with impunity by the next of kin of the slain man through private action: not other injuries, however grave.

Latin:

Vers. 37.

ABIIT AD THOLOMAI FILIUM AMMIUD RE- GEM GESSUR) Ad avum maternum confugit, ubi leges Dei locum non habebant. Nam urbes receptus non taxis- sent deliberato parricidam, quanquam data iræ causa; sola cædes vindicari privato ausu impune ab occisi proximo pote- rat: non & aliæ quantumvis graves Injuriæ.

## 13:39
Verse 39.

KING DAVID CEASED TO PURSUE ABSALOM] LXX. ἐκόπασεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Δαβὶδ τῦ ἐξελθεῖν πρὸς Ἀβε- σαλὼμ ὄτι παρεκλήθη ἐπὶ Ἀμνὼν ὄτι ἀπέθανε. Thus the Chaldean: The soul of David desired to go out. And the Chaldean word כלת from which here is תכל is thus sometimes taken.

Regarding the desire to go out to Absalom, and to visit him, which is here attributed to David (in Hebrew the feminine number תכל indicates the soul of David, which is put for David, in the customary manner), the English, Piscator, and Amama accept it: Since it is nowhere written that David went out against Absalom, and here אל is held, not על, nor does כלה in Piel denote to cease. But even if it is not read elsewhere, let it suffice here that the cessation of the going out is indicated, from which one may gather that David had previously gone out; nor is the word כלה in Piel inconsistent with the meaning of finishing, Lamentations 4:11, 1 Kings 3:1. Indeed, that אל is taken for על or against is not unusual, Isaiah 32:6, Ezekiel 13:9, 20. And the subsequent words of the Vulgate, which Luther and Osiander followed, favor this, in that he had already comforted himself over the death of his son Amnon.

Latin:

Vers. 39.

CESSAVIT REX DAVID PERSEQUVI ABSALOM] LXX. ἐκόπασεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Δαβὶδ τῦ ἐξελθεῖν πρὸς Ἀβε- σαλὼμ ὄτι παρεκλήθη ἐπὶ Ἀμνὼν ὄτι ἀπέθανε. Sic Chal- dæus: Cupiit anima Davidis egredi. Et vox Chaldæa כלת unde hîc est תכל sic interdum sumitur.

De desiderio excurrendi ad Absolomum, eum- que invisendi, quod hic Davidi (in Ebr. fœmini num תכל iñuit animam Davidis, quæ pro Davi de ponitur, more consueto) tribuatur, Angl. Piscat & Amama accipiunt: Siquidem scriptum nuspiam fit, quod contra Absol. egressus sit David, & hic אל habeatur, non v. על, neque כלה in Piel notet cessare. Sed etiamsi alias id non legatur, hic tamen innui sufficiat cessationem egressus, unde colligere licet antea egressum esse Davidem; neque disconvenit vox כלה in Piel pro significatu fi- niendi Thren. 4, 11. 1. Reg. 3, 1. אל vero pro על vel contra accipi non insolitum Esa. 32, 6. Ezech. 13, 9. 20. & consequentia verba vulgatæ, quam sequu- tus Lutherus & Osiander est, favent, eo quod conso- latus (se) jam esset super morte filii sui Amnon.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV.

The woman of Tekoa reconciles Absalom to David: for whom Joab finally prepares access to the King.

Verse 1.

BUT JOAB UNDERSTANDING) He who, by this favor, wished to bind to himself him whom he hoped would be the heir of the kingdom, as he did Adonijah later. And David, as he was shrewd, easily smelled out that this plan had its origin from this. Below 14:19.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV.

Thecuita Absolomum Davidi reconciliat: cui tandem Joab aditum ad Regem parat.

Vers. 1.

INTELLIGENS AUTEM JOAB) Qui beneficio hoc eum quem sperabat hæredem regni fore sibi devincire voluit, ut postea Adoniam. Et hinc ortum hoc consilium, David ut erat solers facile olfecit. Infra 14, 19.

## 14:9
Verse 9.

UPON ME, MY LORD O KING, BE THE INIQUITY) If there is any evil in this matter, I will pay for it.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

IN ME, DOMINE MI REX, SIT INIQVITAS) Si quid hac in re mali est, ego mater luam.

## 14:10
Verse 10.

AND HE SHALL NO MORE ADD TO TOUCH THEE) That he may be troublesome to you. David said this moved by a certain sudden mercy, without taking time to reconsider the law. For even if the avenger had ceased, it was for the senate to inquire about the homicide and exact penalties, and if the senate had ceased, it was for him who bears the sword, that is, the King.

Others, however, excuse David, both because the law in Deuteronomy 17:6 commands that no one be killed unless convicted by two witnesses, and here it was a secret fratricide, verse 6; and because the law commands that a voluntary homicide be killed, but not one who is sudden and accidental: Vatablus alleges the former, Cajetan and others the latter.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET ULTRA NON ADDET UT TANGAT TE) Ut molestus sit tibi. Subita quadam misericordia motus hoc dixit David, non sumto ad legem recogitandam spatio. Nam etiamsi vindex cessasset, senatus erat inquirere de homicidio, & pœnas exigere, & si senatus cessasset, ejus qui gladium gerit, id est, Regis.

ALii tamen excusant Davidem tum, qui lex Deut. 17, 6. jubet ne quis occidatur, nisi duo- bus testibus convictus, hic vero erat fratricidium secretum, v. 6. tum, quia lex jubet occidi homici- dam voluntarium, non vero repentinum & casua- lem: Prius Vatabl. posterius Cajetan. & alii al- legant.

## 14:17
Verse 17.

THAT THE WORD OF MY LORD THE KING MAY BE AS A SACRIFICE) It is rather the expression of one wishing, as the LXX took it: εἴη δὴ (not es ἤδη, as is commonly read) ὁ λόγος τοῦ κυρίου μου τοῦ βασιλέως εἰς θυσίας. Where the word θυσίας corresponds to the Hebrew מנחה which is an offering of fine flour, concerning which Leviticus 2; for the LXX often call this θυσίαν. The sense is, may this answer be as acceptable to God as a gift of fine flour is wont to be.

FOR AS THE ANGEL OF GOD, SO IS MY LORD THE KING) He spoke so mercifully, as the messengers of divine goodness are wont to do. All these things pertain to this, that the King might not bind himself to the law: how badly this turned out for him, the following history will show.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

UT FIAT VERBUM DOMINI MEI REGIS SICUT SACRIFICIUM) Potius optantis est, ut LXX. sumsere: εἴη δὴ (non es ἤδη, ut vulgo legitur) ὁ λόγος τοῦ κυρίου μου τοῦ βα- σιλέως εἰς θυσίας. Ubi vox θυσίας respondet Hebrææ מנחה quæ est oblatio ex simila, de qua Levit. 2. id enim LXX. sæpe θυσίαν vocant. Sensus est, sit Deo hoc responsum tam acceptum, ut solet esse munus e simila.

SICVT ENIM ANGELVS DEI, SIC EST DOMI- NVS REX) Ita clementer locutus est, ut Angeli solent di- vinæ bonitatis nuntii. Hæc omnia eo pertinent, ne Rex se legi adstringat: quod quam male ei cesserit, sequens historia ostendet.

## 14:30
Verse 30.

GO THEREFORE AND SET IT ON FIRE] We had a similar instance above, Judges 15:5. It appears that Absalom's character was bold and violent, and in addition to this, he was magnificent, popular, eloquent, and through all these things powerful for inciting even seditions, so that you could compare the Gracchi to him.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

ITE IGITVR ET SVCCENDITE EVM IGNI] Si- mile habuimus supra Jud. 15, 5. Apparet audax & violen- tum fuisse Absalomi ingenium, ad hæc ipsum magnificum, popularem, eloquentem, ac per hæc omnia ad seditiones etiam excitandas validum, ut Gracchos ei comparare possis.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAPTER XV.

Absalom's conspiracy against David, his flight, and the sending back of the Ark and Hushai into the city.

Verse 1.

ABSALOM PREPARED HIMSELF CHARIOTS AND HORSES AND FIFTY MEN TO RUN BEFORE HIM) He procured a bodyguard for himself when he was girding himself for revolution. I do not doubt that readers not unskilled in human affairs will wonder how Absalom could have incited such a part of the people against a King so distinguished by such merits and victories, and add also, by his virtues: let them therefore consider that there were many among the people who were once dear to Saul, now not in equal honor and favor. Many who had followed the party of Ishbosheth, either feared for themselves, or certainly had despaired of success. Then indeed, as Tacitus says, because of the envy of one man, all are sinned against. Joab's pride and his impunity in atrocious crimes burdened the King, who allowed him to rage against the citizens with impunity. To the other ministers of David also, just as prudence was not absent, so from long power and fortune long flattering, their minds had become more haughty and less popular. David's own sins were indeed few, but those against Uriah were grave. After adultery, murder; after murder, marriage had rendered all men uncertain of the things most dear to all, marriage and life. It is credible that among women, too, the name of Bathsheba was infamous, her power hated. To these causes of hatred was added a vengeful God, allowing minds once inflamed to be carried wherever they wished. Well said Euripides in the Erechtheus: 'May power never cause the fortunate to pursue shameful loves of the citizens. Which draws on both iron and nooses, if one should shame the children of good poor men.' Lust overthrew the Pisistratidae, lust the Tarquins from their kingdom, and many others, whose mention is in Aristotle, book one of the Politics, chapter 10.

Latin:

CAPUT XV.

Absolomi conjuratio adversus Davidem, hu- jus fuga, & remissio Arcæ & Chusai in urbem.

Vers. 1.

FECIT SIBI ABSALOM CVRRVS ET EQVI- TES ET QVINQVAGINTA VIROS QVI PRÆ- CEDERENT EVM) Satellitium sibi comparavit, cum se ad res novas accingeret. Non dubito quin miraturi sint le- ctores rerum humanarum non imperiti, quomodo Absalo- mus tantam populi partem concitare potuerit in Regem tantis meritis ac victoriis, adde & virtutibus præclarum: ii igitur considerent fuisse in populo multos Sauli quondam caros, nunc non pari in honore & gratia. Multos qui Isbo- sethi partes secuti fuerant, sibi aut metuisse, aut certe de pro- fectu desperasse. Tum vero, ut ait Tacitus, unius invidia ab omnibus peccatur. Joabi superbia & in atroci facinore im- punitas Regem onerabat, qui eum impune sineret in cives grassari. Cæteris quoque Davidis ministris, sicut prudentia non aberat, ita ex longa potestate, & diu blandiente fortuna elatiores minusque populares facti erant animi. Davidis ipfius pauca quidem erant peccata, sed illa in Vriam gravia. Post adulterium cædes, post cædem nuptiæ omnes homines incertos reddiderant rerum omnibus carissimarum, conjugii & vitæ. Apud fœminas quoque infame fuisse Bethsabææ no- men, invisam potentiam, credibile est. Ad has odii causas accesfit vindex Deus, ferri qua vellent sinens accensos semel animos. Bene dictum Euripidis in Erechteo: Ἐξουσία δὲ μήποτ' ἐυτυχῶν τέκνοι Αἰσχροὺς ἔρωτας δημοτῶν διωκάθειν. Ὁ καὶ σίδηρον, ἀγχόνας τ' ἐφέλκεται, Χρηστῶν πενήτων ἄν τις ἀισχύνη τέκνα. Libido Pisistratidas, libido Tarquinios regno evertit, multos- que alios, quorum mentio apud Aristotelem libro primo Po- liticorum cap. 10.

Verse 2.

OF WHAT CITY ARE YOU?) Doubtless as Horace says: 'This one has much influence in the Fabian tribe, that one in the Velina.' FROM ONE OF THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL, I AM YOUR SERVANT] That is, I am of the tribe of Judah, Benjamin, or another.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

DE QVA CIVITATE ES TV?) Nimirum uti Hora- tius ait: Hic multum in Fabia valet, ille Velina. EX VNA TRIBV ISRAEL, EGO SVM SERVVS TVVS] Id est, sum de tribu Judæ, Benjamin, aut alia.

## 15:3
Verse 3.

YOUR WORDS SEEM TO ME EXCELLENT AND JUST) By art. Thus Demea in the Adelphi: 'Little by little I am making the common people my own.' And what follows: 'I consider them worthy.' And 'You are a thrifty man.' Manlius Capitolinus in Livy, book 6: 'In vain would I have saved the Capitol and the citadel with this right hand, if I were to see my fellow citizen and comrade-in-arms being led into slavery and chains, as if captured by the victorious Gauls.'

Latin:

Vers. 3.

VIDENTVR MIHI SERMONES TVI EGREGII ET JVSTI) Ex arte. Ita Demea in Adelphis: Paulatim plebem primulum facio meam. Et quod sequitur dignos arbitror. Et frugi homo es. Manlius Ca- pitolinus apud Livium libro 6. Ego nequicquam hac dextera Capitolium arcemque servaverim, si civem commilitonemque meum, tanquam Gallis victoribus captum, in servitutem ac vin- cula duci videam.

BUT THERE IS NO ONE APPOINTED BY THE KING TO HEAR YOU] He especially accuses the brothers from another mother, who were set over the court and the reporting of the citizens' desires to the King.

Verse 6.

Vers. 4.

## 15:5
HE WAS EXTENDING HIS HAND AND TAKING HOLD WAS KISSING HIM] He was grasping, to speak in Latin. Thus Otho was not lacking in extending his hands, to adore the common people, to throw kisses, and everything servilely for the sake of dominion. Tacitus, Histories 1.

Latin:

Vers. 5. EXTENDEBAT MANVM SVAM ET AP- PREHENDENS OSCVLABATVR EVM] Prensabat, ut Latine loquar. Sic Otho non deerat protendens manus, ad- orare vulgum, jacere oscula, & omnia serviliter pro domina- tione. Tacitus Histor. 1.

## 15:7
Verse 7.

BUT AFTER FORTY YEARS) There is undoubtedly an error here in the Scripture, with two letters added to the word ארבע. For Josephus said that four years had intervened, and Theodoret says no differently. And the thing itself speaks that this is true.

Wonderful is the man's genius! Everywhere he insults the fountains of Hebrew truth. Even here, where all Hebrew Codices agree and the Chaldean, Greek, or Latin ones do not differ, just as the Roman Pontiff amended them. What Cajetan and Abulensis say, that there were not forty, but only four in the Latin version, we leave in its place. But Cornelius à Lapide denies this, and asserts that Jerome, Angelomus, the Gloss, Lyranus, Dionysius, and the other interpreters, ancient and modern, read forty. The Sixtine correction is certainly approved by all Papists, and it should not have been disapproved by Grotius himself, who leans toward the Pope. Nor does Lyra admit that four years fit the chronology. If you ask, how do forty fit? The Hebrews, as Jerome has in their traditions, and also the author of the Scholastic History, Angelomus, Lyra, Dionysius, Hugo, and the Gloss count them from the priests killed by Saul, because some sin of David intervened there, a lie, to be avenged here through Absalom; but it is certain that David's adultery and homicide are punished here from chapter 12, 11. Therefore, others more correctly fix the beginning of these forty years either at the first anointing of David done by Samuel, or at the epoch of the changed form of the Republic, when Saul was substituted as King in place of the judges, just as such epochs are most accepted in the calculation of times. Which Sanctius explains more fully in his commentary. And these two later opinions easily coincide, since David's anointing was done a few months after the first beginnings of Saul's reign: and thus it falls back into almost the same era as Saul's. Whence R. David Kimchi, Abulensis, Joh. will easily agree here. Mariana, Paul Burgensis, Em. Saa, Tirin, Salianus, as well as Corn. à Lapide, Menochius. And from our own, B. Luther, the Weimar editors, Walther, and others. But the beginning should not be fixed at the first demand for Royal Rule, with R. Solomon and Vatablus, or even at the beginning of David's reign, which pleased Piscator and Junius. For chronology favors neither: since more than forty years elapsed from the time when the King was first demanded by the Israelites to the rebellion of Absalom, and fewer passed from the beginning of the Davidic reign itself, if indeed that rebellion did not fall into the last and fatal year of David, but occurred at least seven years before David's death. Others count from the death of Saul, others from the slaying of Goliath, others from the birth of Absalom, but Cornelius à Lapide rightly observes that the number of years does not correspond. In the explanation of B. Luther, however, it corresponds perfectly.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

POST QVADRAGINTA AVTEM ANNOS) Haud dubius hic errror Scripturæ additis ad vocem ארבע literis duabus. Quatuor enim annos intercesfisse dixit Josephus, nec aliter Theodoretes. Et hoc verum esse res ipsa loquitur.

Mirum hominis ingenium! Ubique insultat fon- tibus Ebraicæ veritatis. Etiam hic, ubi con sonant Ebræi Codices omnes neque discrepant Chal- dæi, Græci, aut Latini, prout hos Pontifex Roma- nus emendavit. Quod Cajetanus & Abulensis di- cunt, non quadraginta, sed quatuor tantum fuisse in Latina versione, suo loco relinquimus. Negat au- tem id Cornel. à Lapide, ac Hieronymum, Angelo- mum, Glossam, Lyranum, Dionysium, cæterosque In- terpretes, priscos ac modernos quadraginta legisse asferit. Sixtina certe correctio omnibus Pontificiis probatur, ipsique Grotio Papizanti improbari non debuit. Neque annos quatuor Chronologiæ congru- ere Lyra admittit. Si quæras, quomodo quadraginta congruant? Ebræi, ut Hieronymus in traditionibus eorum habet, Autor item Historiæ Scholasticæ An- gelomus, Lyra, Dionysius, Hugo, & Glossa numerant eosdem ab occisis à Saule Sacerdotibus, quod ibi in- tervenerit Davidis peccatum aliquod, mendacium, hic per Absolonem vindicandum; sed puniri hic adulterium & homicidium Davidis è cap. 12, 11. cer- tum est. Ideo rectius alii initium istorum quadra- ginta annorum figunt vel in unctione prima Davidis per Samuelem facta, vel in Epocha mutatæ formæ Reipubl. cum pro judicibus Rex suffectus fuit Saul, quemadmodum tales Epochæ in temporum calcu- lo maxime receptæ sunt. Quod uberius explicat Sanctius in comment. Atque hæ duæ posteriores sententiæ facile coincidunt, quum paucis mensibus post prima regni Saulis initia Davidis unctio facta sit: Adeoque in idem fere cum æra Saulis recidat. Unde facile hic convenient R. David Kimchi, Abu- lensis, Joh. Mariana, Paul Burgensis, Em. Saa, Tirin. Salianus nec non Corn. à Lapide, Menochius. Et è nostris B. Lutherus, Vinarienses, Waltherus, aliique. Non autem in prima Regii Regiminis postulatione, cum R. Salomone & Vatablo, initium figendum, vel etiam in initio Regni Davidis, quod Piscatori & Ju- nio placuit. Neutri enim Chronologia favet: Quum plures, quam quadraginta anni effluxerint ab eo tempore, quo primum Rex postulatus fuit ab Israelitis, ad rebellionem Absolonis, & pauciores ab ipso Davidici regni initio transierint, siquidem rebellio illa in postremum & fatalem Davidis haud inciderit, sed septennio ad minimum ante fata Da- vidis acciderit. Alii numerant à morte Saulis, alii à cæde Goliath, alii à nativitate Absolon, sed recte ob- servat Cornel. à Lapide non respondere numerum annorum. In B. Lutheri v. explicatione optime respondet.

## 15:10
Verse 10.

BUT ABSALOM SENT SPIES) That is, agitators of the mob, Saturnine, Pescennine, and others of that craft, among whom perhaps there were also Priests and Levites, a class of men most suited for disturbing affairs where they might indulge their own passions.

SAY: ABSALOM HAS REIGNED IN HEBRON] That is, he is acknowledged as King. Which, in such a matter, is the most difficult thing, the first word. Tacitus, Histories, book two.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

MISIT AVTEM ABSALOM EXPLORATORES) Id est, concitores vulgi, Saturninos, Pescenninos, & alios ejus artificii, in quibus forte erant & Sacerdotes & Levitæ, genus hominum ad res turbandas, ubi suis indulgerent affectibus, maxime idoneum.

DICITE: REGNAVIT ABSALOM IN HEBRON] Id est, pro Rege est agnitus. Quod in re tali difficillimum, prima vox. Tacitus Histor. secundo.

Latin:

## 15:12
Verse 12. ABSALOM ALSO SUMMONED ACHITOPHEL THE GILONITE) Those to whom the counsels of Kings are known can do the greatest harm to Kings.

AND WHEN HE WAS SACRIFICING VICTIMS) When he had sacrificed, rather, that is, at the banquet. Thus Civilis, having called the leaders of the people and the most ready of the mob to a sacred grove under the guise of a feast, when he sees them heated by the night and by joy, beginning from the praise and glory of the people, enumerates their injuries and seizures and the other evils of servitude. Tacitus, Hist. 4.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ACCERSIVIT QVOQVE ABSALOM ACHI- TOPHEL GILONITEN] Plurimum nocere Regibus ii possunt, quibus nota sunt Regum consilia.

CVMQVE IMMOLARET VICTIMAS) Cum immo- lasset, potius, id est in convivio. Sic Civilis primores gentis & promtissimos vulgi, specie epularum sacrum in nemus voca- tos, ubi nocte ac lætitia incaluisse videt, à laude gloriaque gen- tis orsus, injurias & raptus, & cætera servitii mala enumerat. Hist. 4. Taciti.

## 15:14
Verse 14. ARISE, LET US FLEE) A huge panic, such as that of Pompey, of whom Lucan says: The city, crowded with peoples and conquered nations, and capable of holding a throng of human kind, the hands cowardly abandoned as easy prey to the coming Caesar. When the Roman soldier, pressed by the enemy, is shut up on foreign shores, he escapes nocturnal dangers with a small rampart, and a sudden mound of turf snatched up provides secure sleep within the tents; you alone, Rome, at the mere rumor of wars, are deserted: one night not entrusted to your walls.

Latin:

Vers. 14. SVRGITE, FVGIAMVS) Pavor ingens qualis Pompeji, de quo Lucanus: urbem populis victisque frequentem Gentibus, & generis, coeat si turba, capacem Humani, facilem venturo Cæsare prædam Ignave liquere manus. Cum pressus ab hoste Clauditur externis miles Romanus in oris, Effugit exiguo nocturna pericula vallo, Et subitus rapti munimine cespitis agger Præstat securos intra tentoria somnos, Tu tantum audito bellorum murmure Roma Desereris: nox una tuis non credita muris.

## 15:33
Ver. 33.

BUT IF YOU RETURN TO THE CITY, AND SAY TO ABSALOM I AM YOUR SERVANT, O KING, AS I WAS YOUR FATHER'S SERVANT, SO WILL I BE YOUR SERVANT, YOU WILL DISSIPATE THE COUNSEL OF ACHITOPHEL) David did not abandon his own arts in such great evils: but where the lion's skin did not avail, he assumes the fox's, truly ἀγχίνους, and clever at finding what was of use.

This was not assuming the fox's skin, or carnal craftiness, but singular prudence and counsel, which God was directing, making foolish the counsel of Achitophel according to the prayers of David.

Latin:

Vers. 33.

SI AVTEM IN CIVITATEM REVERTARIS, ET DIXERIS ABSALOMO SERVVS TVVS SVM, REX, SICVT FVI SERVVS PATRIS TVI, SIC ERO SER- VVSTVVS, DISSIPABIS CONSILIVM ACHITO- PHEL) Non deferebant in tantis malis Davidem suæ artes: sed ubi leonina non proderat, assumit vulpinam, vere ἀγχί- νους, & quæ ex usu erant reperire solers.

Non erat hoc vulpinam assumere, aut carnalis versutiæ, sed singularis prudentiæ & consilii, quod dirigebat Deus, Achitophelis consilium juxta Da- vidis preces infatuans.

CHAPTER XVI.
