And Vol. 7. Wittenberg. Latin book on the Jews, folio 183. To render it more closely from the Hebrew, my house is certainly not of such value, that is, my house is not worthy; that the word כּי is to be rendered as 'indeed' was also noted by Ludov. de Dieu, because it is often not causal, but confirmatory, as Genesis 22:17, where the LXX have ἦ μὴν. Therefore, our divine Luther interprets excellently concerning the kingdom of the Messiah, what is added concerning that covenant ordered in all things and secured. The following two words, Arucha and Schemura, well ordered and kept, are set with diligence for doctrine and comfort; for if you look at the histories, it will seem to you that GOD has forgotten His covenant, and has not kept it, so desolate, disorderly, and strange do things go in David's house and descendants. Yet it has been kept not only until the Messiah, but everything has remained well and sound in its order, against all devils and men, and no one has been able to change or suppress it, but they have had to let it go and stand, a scepter of Judah, as it is promised until the Messiah. But after the Messiah, His kingdom, the Church, is outwardly to be seen as much more desolate and disorderly, so that there is no more torn, miserable, and worthless government or dominion than the Christian Church, Christ's dominion; here the tyrants tear it and desolate it with fire, water, sword, and all power, here the sect-spirits and heresy dig it up and ruin it. The false Christians do the same with their evil life, as if there were no more shameful, disorderly dominion on earth; and all these work toward this, or rather the evil spirit through them, that Christ's dominion should be nothing or ever a miserable, disorderly thing. And in sum, Christ acts as if He had forgotten His dominion, and were nowhere at home, so that here neither Arucha nor Semura is seen by reason, nor is it called Arucha, Becol, and Schemura, everything well ordered and kept; although we do not see it, He sees it, who says, in the last chapter of the Song of Songs, my vineyard is before me, in the last chapter of Matthew, see, I am with you until the end of the world, John 16, be of good cheer, I have overcome the world. Nevertheless we see that there has always remained and remains a people that honors the name of Christ, has his Word, Baptism, Sacrament, keys, and Spirit, even against all the gates of hell. Hæc Megalander, quem sequitur Osiandrina Paraphrasis: And that kingdom of the Messiah shall be firm. Hebr. ordered in all things, i.e., although in the kingdom of Christ there seem to be many confusions, while it is now infested by persecutions, now disturbed by heresies, now deformed by scandals: yet there will appear at length the singular and admirable wisdom of GOD, by which it will be recognized that He has disposed all things rightly: namely, that He has permitted no evil from which some great good has not followed. And although Satan desires to overturn that kingdom with great assaults, yet it will be firm, and fortified, or more correctly: guarded (i.e., God will guard His own as the apple of the eye, nor will He allow the Gospel to be entirely destroyed before the last day.

There remain those words concerning the Davidic desire: For all my salvation, and all my will, nor is there anything of it that does not sprout: which (1.) Cocceius explained concerning the non-sprouting house of David at the time of the rise of Christ, referring to these things thus: Let the Sun of righteousness arise, when my house shall lie as if in ashes (not about to sprout to kingdom and splendor Jerem. 22, 30.) to begin the heavenly kingdom, namely, that He may prepare salvation for me, and for all the Saints who have hoped in Him, not that we are then first saved, on account of Him, but that He himself may be a perfect savior by the very offering of the sacrifice, and may merit every εὐδοκίαν of the Father Ps. 16, 3. Cocceius notes that the little word כי is not only taken etiologically for because, and adversatively for but, but also objectively for that or ὅτι, and also as an adverb of time, when: and he wishes that

David: my house will not sprout, but the sun will rise, and indeed in my house, and from my house. Heb. 7, 14. but not by the fertility of my house, and the virtue of carnal fecundity. But these are in a way forced. (2.) More simple is the explanation of B. Luther in the marginal gloss, and Tom. 8. Jen. Germ. fol. 169. that without respect to time the kingdom of David is compared, or rather opposed to the kingdom of Christ, i.e., My kingdom, and whatever I do, with respect to the kingdom of the Messiah is only as it were a dry branch, or trunk. Which explanation the Weimar Paraphrasts have embraced. (3.) Franc. Vatablus thus adduces the explanation of R. David Kimchi; The Doctor among the Hebrews explains, it will not be like the sprout of the field, which vanishes, but he who is my salvation, and my desire, Christ, who will descend from the seed of David, will reign perpetually. (4.) The Osiandrine Paraphrase seems most convenient: For all my salvation, understand, consists in the spiritual kingdom of Christ, and all my desire, that it may not grow: that is, I desire nothing so much as that it might be permitted to see that rising sun of righteousness, Christ in the flesh, and that kingdom of peace to grow, which will refresh consciences, that most pleasant heavenly Paradise: Ah, why does it not grow already? I long for it, that it will not grow right now. Which sense can be helped thus, all my salvation, and all my pleasure or all my desire is in that, which does not yet grow: or also in that (Christ or the kingdom of Christ) it is: although it does not yet grow, yet in that one is all my salvation, and all my pleasure. Thus the subjoined antithesis responds best. For as the faithful with David place all their salvation, and all their pleasure solely in Christ, whom for that reason the pious ancients so greatly desired, with our King and Prophet, so on the contrary the unfaithful men of Belial reject this salvation, who as useless and harmful thorns are all to be removed, and will be burned by burning with fire: which B. Luther refers specifically to the Jews, although he includes other enemies of the kingdom of Christ as well, and judges that the destruction of those is primarily designated here: David calls Kotz the great evil prickly thistles, or the other thistles, which our farmers call Tollgraet, which one must separate with scythes, sickles and rakes, or spear-wood in the harvest, for no one can touch them both with their hands, and they serve no purpose, but for the fire, but tares are used for the cattle, thus the hardened Jews are such evil prickly thistles and Tollgraete, that they have not been and are not yet to be converted by any benefit or miracle of GOD, but are cast out by the iron and spears of the Romans, and burned with their city in their own dwelling, also with bodily fire, beyond that they still burn now in themselves, where they are in misery, with the spiritual fire of Divine wrath, thus David has announced to this people their destruction and final ruin, because they did not want to have this King, as the LORD Luke 19. also prophesies about it, and Daniel 9. Zach. 14. Coccejus also interprets this concerning the destruction of the Jews, and also of the Anti-Christ; although he does not exclude others. Osiander notes that the discourse here is principally about the Jews, yet in general about the remaining impious as well, because they are thorns, at least to be plucked from the field of the Lord on the last day, and to be burned with inextinguishable fire. Lyranus and Alphonsus Tostatus have also interpreted it peculiarly concerning the Jews, and concerning their destruction. But the Prophet speaks of the sons of Belial IN GENERAL, and of all who do not have delight in Christ and his salvation, as the opposition convinces, of all who are thorns, useless, and harmful, to whom he threatens combustion; and thus the external destruction of the unfaithful is properly treated here. Just as David, with all the faithful, places eternal salvation solely in the Messiah, and has all his pleasure in him: so by the force of the opposition, all the sons of Belial, who shake off the yoke of the Messiah, Ps. 2,3. and do not wish to be subject to his kingdom or commands, not only fall away from eternal salvation and blessedness, but are also subjected to eternal destruction: as they, like grass, by the virtue of the splendor of the sun of righteousness, and the rain of saving doctrine, joyfully come forth and grow in the Paradise of the Lord: so the unfaithful are like thorns, which as useless and harmful are to be plucked up and burned with fire.

That ימלא is explained by Ludov. de Dieu, with Levi Gerson preceding, not as a man about to attack those thorns, arming or fortifying himself, but as the prickles of the thorns, which fill the wounds of the hands; but the common interpretation is simpler: for he is not filled with iron and spear who is wounded by them: but when he is armed and fortified with them, he is not badly said to be filled: for he does not attack the thorns with bare hands, but fills his hands with iron, or a mattock, and a sickle, with which he may cut them down, or with the shaft of a spear, with which he may drive away or push them, so that he is not hurt by them, as Vatablus; or with a pre-sharpened wood to the likeness of a spear, as Sanctius explains: The Vulgate rendered it, is armed: Junius, is fortified: And the nouns can be rendered by a Hendiadys, armed with iron and the wood of a spear, that is, with the iron of the spear-wood, to which the aforementioned Sanctian interpretation leads. A man, says David, will make an attack upon them armed: A man, (not a boy) strong, robust. And they will be burned by burning with fire, בַּשָּׁבֶת, which most render as in the habitation or in the place, and seat, i.e., the same where the thorns were born; for thorny herbs, and prickly shrubs are accustomed to be set on fire, and burned in the very fields where they have come forth, and grown. Which are correct concerning the protasis of the similitude, when one persists in the comparison of the thorns; so that the apodosis concerning the enemies of the kingdom of Christ, the men of Belial, the impious, and the unfaithful is tacitly insinuated, and is to be gathered from that protasis: and yet those words are not used beside the point in the protasis itself, which in the apodosis are aptly fitted to the destruction of the impious, and agree with the judgment of God against the sons of Belial. For God is accustomed to attack them like an armed man, or even to employ men armed with sword and lance: and He burns them with the fire of His wrath, both of temporal destruction and of everlasting ruin, which the Jews experienced first of all, being more famous among the sons of Belial, and of a special sort: concerning whom B. Luther rightly says, that they do not yet cease to burn, wherever they are in their conventicles, and they are most miserably exiled by that eternal fire of divine wrath. But the unquenchable fire of Gehenna will follow, IN THE MANSION prepared from eternity for the Devil and the infidels, that is, in hell, Matt. 25, 41. Psalm 49, v. 15. Cf. Matt. 3, 12. ch. 13, 30. 38. 42. John 15, 6. Rev. 20, 10. For even if that word HABITATION pertains to the protasis of the similitude, just declared, the Holy Spirit nevertheless deliberately uses such words in comparisons, which are more suitable and analogous to the things understood in the apodosis, and allude to the same: and therefore He assigns His habitation or seat to thorns in this place, by allusion to the seat and habitation of the wicked, which is prepared for them from eternity, and is their own forever. Cocceius renders it IN THE ASSEMBLY: and wishes the assembly of the Church to be noted: but that does not suit the protasis, of which, however, account must entirely be taken. And therefore we acquiesce in the common interpretation concerning habitation:

which is also B. Luther's, and Osiander's, thus correcting the Vulgate's entirely alien translation, UNTO NOTHING. For concerning that nothing, nothing is held in the Hebrew: whence also by Pagninus, and the Jesuit Casp. Sanctius, the Vulgate has been corrected here: because שֶׁבֶת is a seat, a dwelling, from יָשַׁב to sit, to dwell. And these things are concerning the last words of David. It is helpful, however, to append what Coccejus has in the last words of Moses concerning this passage §. 989. For my house is not right with God (my posterity is not better, or more worthy before God, than that of other men. See Psalm 51, 7. Job 14, 4.) but he has placed an eternal covenant, a Testament and a promise for me, set forth in all things, so that all men may be able to hope for salvation in that covenant, and preserved without repentance; that all MY SALVATION and all future complacency shall be, when my house shall not sprout. At that time, when my house shall no longer bear a rod for ruling, Ezek. 19, 14. But a branch shall have been set over, Isa. 10, 33. my house not standing in the commandments of God: then nevertheless God will give me a house and seed, through which SALVATION may be procured, not of the body, but of the soul, indeed MY [salvation], long since dead, so that my sins may be expiated through it; and all complacency, i.e., all grace, by which God remits sins and imputes righteousness. These are Coccejus', concerning which a judgment can be made from the above.

It is also pleasing here to append a program proposed for the festival of the Nativity in the year 1664, contributing to the illustration of the last words of David. Which is of this tenor:

Who exists, instructed with such a great abundance of things and words, who could proclaim the grace of this day with worthy praises? Today is the birthday of the Savior, in which, as St. Augustine says, light was added to the world, and immortality, which had perished through sin, was restored to mortals: Today the virgin brought forth him who would exclude the sentence of transgression, take away the punishment of death, and grant eternal life to those who believe. What praises shall we give to the charity of GOD, what thanks shall we render, who so loved us that for our sake he became in time, through whom the times were made, he became man, who made man, was created from the mother whom he created, was carried by the hands which he formed, sucked the breasts which he filled, in the manger the Word wailed in mute infancy, without whom human eloquence is mute! The Angels are stunned by such great mysteries, the Archangels marvel, the highest Principalities and thrones yearn to look upon them trembling. But they exult because of these gifts of grace, and with incredible joy the heavenly Legates announce the same to the world. The whole army, the choir from above, fills both heaven and earth with a song, the sweetest that it ever sang: Glory to GOD in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men. When once the shining Seraphim still beheld from afar the glory of the flesh of Christ, which was to be raised to the throne of most eminent majesty, they veiled their faces at the immense brightness, and joyfully sang their perennial trisagion: Holy, Holy, Holy Jehovah Zebaoth, the whole earth is full of his glory. With how much greater astonishment shall we believe the heavenly dominations and powers were struck, and imbued with joy, when they beheld before them the immense GOD, whom the heavens of heavens do not contain, surrounded by the covering of flesh, an infant, wailing in a cradle, flashing with the infinite glory of the only-begotten from the Father, so that the exiles of heaven might be restored to the angelic society, and might be received anew into the fellowship of heavenly joy. Wherefore they invite mortals to the concert of their trisagion with a sweet voice, and most sweetly illustrate it with a new and hitherto unheard hymn, in praise of the glorious Trinity; Holy GOD the Father, Holy GOD the Son, Holy GOD the Holy Spirit, Holy that Triune Jehovah Zebaoth, his glory is now filling the whole earth. Because the Savior is born to the whole earth. Glory to GOD the Father, who gratifies the world with this Salvation out of mere mercy. Glory to GOD the Son, who deigns to appear on earth, as true PEACE, pacifying all things in heaven and on earth. Glory to GOD the Holy Spirit, in whom is εὐδοκία among men, out of the grace of the Father, through the Son the Prince of Peace. Let the heavens therefore now rejoice, and let the earth exult, let the sea be moved, and the fullness thereof, the fields shall rejoice, and all that is in them. Let all the trees of the woods exult before the face of the Lord, because HE HAS COME. The heavens have announced his righteousness, and all peoples have seen his glory! Adore him all his Angels: Sion heard, and was glad. And the children of Judah exulted, because of thy judgments O Lord. Light has risen for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart: Rejoice you righteous in the Lord, and confess the memory of his holiness. We will sing the mercies of the Lord forever, from generation to generation we will announce thy truth with our mouth.

Thus long ago the Hiero-Psalmist stirred us, when in the Spirit he foresaw the great joy, which the angel and the angelic choir have now announced to the whole world. For neither he, nor any of the Saints of the Old Testament was devoid of this joy, and the excellent Psalmist of Israel was confirmed particularly concerning the Christ of the GOD of Israel: The Strong One of Israel spoke to him (the Rock, which was Christ, as the Apostle testifies,) whom in his last words, so that he might testify that he would migrate to the Fathers in this faith, he professed, the Ruler among men, the just Ruler in the fear of GOD; And so he prophesied, that some King is to be in Israel, who is to reign in justice, and in the fear of the Lord: When the dawn shines, he says, the Sun shall rise, the morning shall be without clouds from the brightness, from the rain there shall be a sprout 2. Sam. 23, 4. Which are mysterious, and indicate this, that about the time of night, or the end of the shadows, as if with the dawn and the Morning Star, John the Baptist, shining before, the Sun of righteousness is about to rise. Furthermore, that the densities and clouds are to be dispersed by his splendor, when as if from rain a righteous sprout is about to come forth from the earth. Which most understand concerning the fruit of the Gospel, which like rain makes the earth sprout. Coccejus in the last words of Moses wishes it to be signified that the rising of the Sun of righteousness will be humble, without clouds, promising the hope of rain and divine blessing, yet then from his splendor through divine blessing a sprout will come forth from the earth. But all things look to the rising of the righteous sprout, which is celebrated in Jeremiah ch. 23, 6, with whom all righteousness began to sprout, from whom also, and in whom is all the fruitfulness of the Gospel, as these things likewise in his last Psalm, which is 72. (where after the kingdom was handed over to Solomon his Son, he was entirely fixed upon the kingdom of the Messiah) the most holy of Prophets and Kings interpreted: He shall descend like rain upon the fleece, and like showers dripping upon the earth. For, thus the sacred psalmist continues, my house is not right before GOD, (which is the sense of the Hebrew phrase 2 Sam. 23, 5) but he has established an eternal covenant for me out of mere grace, or as the Vulgate rendered the sense, my house or family is not so great before GOD, that he should enter into an eternal covenant with me, firm in all things, and fortified, which others interpret, exposed in all things, so that, namely, all men might hope for salvation in that covenant, irrevocably kept or to be kept, because all my salvation, and all my delight (εὐδοκία) shall be, when my house shall not sprout, at that time, when my house shall no longer bear a rod for ruling Ezek. 19, 14. but a branch shall have been appointed Isa. 10, 39. my house not standing in the commandments of GOD, then nevertheless GOD will give me a house and seed, through which my Salvation may be procured, and all complacency a little differently, namely by way of a vow, not as a designation of time: And all desire, that it may not grow; that is, I desire nothing so much as that it might be permitted to see that rising Sun of righteousness, Christ, in the flesh, and to see that Kingdom of peace grow, which will refresh consciences, that most pleasant heavenly paradise. Oh why does it not grow already? I long for it, that it does not want to grow right now. For all my salvation consists in the spiritual kingdom of Christ, my Son who is one day to be born: πᾶσα σωτηρία μ8, καὶ πᾶν θέλημα ἐν Κυρίῳ, as the LXX Interpreters rendered the immediately preceding words. Indeed, the man after God's own heart had in his heart his JESUS, whom he longed for greatly, repeatedly doubling his sighs, burning with the highest love and desire for him: My soul has failed for your salvation (your JESUS): I wait for your salvation (your JESUS) O Lord. I have desired your salvation (your JESUS) O Lord. Who will give salvation (JESUS) to Israel out of Zion? Psal. 119, 8. 166. 174. Ps. 14, 7. Ps. 53, 7. Nor had he himself received any other ETERNAL covenant than that concerning our little JESUS, that in him alone blessing and salvation might be obtained by all who are concluded under the curse and condemnation. Which is the sum, and Substance, so to speak, of the eternal covenant, not first initiated and sanctioned with David, but with Abraham the Father of believers, nay, with Adam and Eve the parents of all the living: THE SEED OF THE WOMAN shall crush the head of the serpent: in your SEED, which is CHRIST, as the Apostle interprets, all nations shall be blessed. Therefore, when that Salvation is specifically promised in the seed of David, it does not pertain to the substance of the covenant that it is that SEED OF DAVID, but to the circumstance, and the distinguished prerogative with which GOD adorned the Davidic lineage and his Royal throne. This eternal covenant, therefore, being absolutely ἀμεταμέλητον, clothed with this circumstance, was that alone which 2. Samuel 7, 12. 13. 14. 15. 16. GOD had sanctioned, concerning the Seed from his body, to be raised up after his death, whose kingdom shall be eternal, and whose throne shall stand forever; because of which inestimable magnificence of his house the King exclaims: Who am I O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me thus far? But even this seemed little in your sight, O Lord, unless you also spoke of the house of your Servant for a long time to come. This is the form of THAT man, (for the He Hajediah must not be neglected here) who is GOD Jehovah, whom namely the MAN JEHOVAH Eve the mother of all living already expected, whom I now receive with the greatest joy, as he is about to come forth from my loins. Which promise is simple and absolute: made then to David through Nathan, when the Lord protested that he required no house, and by way of exchange promised that he himself would build a house for David, and would produce a Seed from his loins, his eternal Son, by whom alone a house would be built for the divine name, not of material stones, but of living stones, not fragile and perishable, but eternal and lasting without end. Whence this categorical promise (the Holy faithful things of David, the Holy Spirit calls them τὰ ὅσια τὰ πισὰ Acts 13, 34. from Isa. 55, 3. where the faithful things of David, that is, the mercies promised to David, are called) is by no means to be confused with the hypothetical and conditional promise concerning preserving the royal throne for the Davidic posterity, if, namely, he kept the commandments and statutes of the Lord, which were not made through Nathan, but immediately to David by the Lord, when the Lord did not reject the building of the temple, but reserved it for Solomon 2. Chron. 23, 8. 13. 1. Kings 8, 17. 25. And under the same condition repeated to Solomon 1. Kings 9, 4. 5. 6. Wherefore Ethan distinguished these accurately in his Maskil, or Didactic poem, when he celebrated the grace promised to David in a distinguished song, Psalm 89. The former promise of the Lord, confirmed by an oath, was devoid of any condition, to be kept forever, ἀμεταμελήτως, which is proclaimed in v. 4. and following: I have disposed a testament to my elect: I have sworn to David my servant. The sum is in the profession of the faithful verse 18. and the divine promise verse 19. upon which the faithful rely, glorying and exulting in the Lord: as is had in verses 16. and 17. O Lord, they shall walk in the light of your countenance, and in your name they shall exult all the day, and in your righteousness they shall be exalted. For you are the glory of their strength, and in your good pleasure our horn shall be exalted (this is the εὐδοκία in the raised and exalted horn of our Salvation Luke 1, 67.) because our shield is from the Lord and our King from the Holy One of Israel: that is, the Messiah is given to us by GOD, who sanctifies Israel, as a shield, Redemption, righteousness, sanctification, etc. Which sense our blessed Bugenhagius rendered happily from the translation of the Hebrew text made by Felix. The basis of this confidence, glorying, exultation, and exaltation of the faithful is the divine promise made to the Saints, to Nathan and David; Then you spoke in a vision to your Saints, and said: I have placed help upon a mighty one, and have exalted an Elect one from the people. I have found David my servant, with holy oil I have anointed him. Which latter words, although some explain them of Christ with St. Augustine, the Pauline interpretation in Acts 13, 22. does not allow us to doubt are to be understood of David. But that Gibbor, in whom help or aid is placed for the faithful, so that they may glory and exult, is none other than the son given to us, the child born to us, Christ, whose name is El gibbor Isa. 9, 6. who is also that Elect one from the people, or from the Israelitic seed, and the tribe of Judah, and from the Fathers according to the flesh, whom the Father exalted for the sake of our Salvation: to whom, David having been sent, because of the promise which was made to him, he is celebrated here, and Ethan returns to his throne, which this ELECT HERO was to possess, having introduced him, and graphically depicts his exaltation, covenant, spiritual Seed, throne, and kingdom. Therefore, he sings further concerning that eternal covenant: verse 34. I will not profane my covenant, and what proceeds from my lips, I will not make void: Once I have sworn by my Holy (name, as the Chaldean, or by my holiness) if I lie to David, his seed shall remain FOREVER, and his throne, as the Sun in my sight, and as the moon perfect forever, and a faithful witness in heaven. And these things concerning the former promise. The latter promise had a condition annexed, and that ceasing, it ceased, concerning which Ethan complains gravely in his prophecy from verse 38 up to verse 46. But you have rejected, and despised, you have deferred your Christ, you have overturned the covenant of your servant etc. Therefore, the eternal kingdom of GOD is one thing, in which there is grace, and the King from the Seed of David, expected by all the Saints; the external, worldly, shadowy kingdom given to the sons of David is another, which he shows in the Spirit to have fallen, even before the revelation of the Messiah; whence he prays, and supplies the prayers of the pious of that time, by which he seeks the acceleration of the mission of Christ the true King, with true grace v. 47 seq.

may they seek: how long, O Lord, do you turn yourself away? Where are your ancient mercies, O Lord, as you swore to David in your truth? Be mindful, O Lord, of the reproach of your servants, which I have borne until now (the Church groaning) in my bosom, which your enemies have reproached, which indeed they have reproached the footsteps of your Christ (hissing and mocking the progress of your kingdom, and the delay of its coming, the slowness of the footsteps of the Messiah, as the Chaldean has it) whom indeed, because the Esrahite believed he would surely follow in his certain time, he breaks forth into this doxology: BLESSED BE THE LORD FOREVER, AMEN, AMEN. And in this sense also the son Solomon accepted the covenant established with the Father, Ps. 132 (for he acknowledges him as the author here, as appears from the whole structure of the Psalm) when concerning the principal promise, he swore, he says v. 9. the Lord David the truth, and he will not frustrate him: of the fruit of your womb I will set upon your throne: but concerning the other under condition v. 12. If your sons keep my testament, and these my testimonies, which I will teach them, and their sons even unto the age shall sit upon your throne: and lest a doubt remain concerning the former and principal promise, he added v. 17. His priests (who are all the faithful, the Royal Priesthood of the Lord) I will clothe with Salvation, and his saints shall exult with exultation: There I will bring forth the HORN of David, I have prepared a LAMP for my Christ (David) which horn is nothing else than that of which Zacharias sings in Luke 1:69, nor is the lamp any other than that great light, of which the son of Zacharias testified in John 1:9. But it is not permitted to pursue these things at present. And Gabriel the Archangel has already brought light to them all in Luke 1:32. And the Lord GOD will give to him the throne of his father David and he shall reign in the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there shall be no end. Therefore in this lamp, in this horn of salvation, which the LORD HAS MADE TO SPROUT for us, let us rejoice, let us sing these eternal mercies, and let us celebrate these solemn feasts in such a way as becomes a royal priesthood; Denying impiety and worldly desires, let us live soberly toward ourselves, justly toward our neighbor, and piously toward GOD in this age. For this reason the grace of GOD our Savior has shone upon us, instructing us: for this reason also now a torch burning in heaven portends the burning wrath of the Lord to the Christian world, which let us avert by serious and holy repentance. May the Lord JESUS grant this in us, whose ministers you shall not cease, having laid down your gifts at the altar, to testify your gratitude. The Lord clothes his enemies with confusion, that is, the impious and ungrateful, but upon the just his Diadem shall flourish. P.P. Christmas Eve. In the year 1664.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DEVS ISRAEL MIHI LOCVTUS EST) Per Natha- nem: Vide supra 7.

NOn est, quod hoc ad revelationem istam specia- tim restringatur: Etsi eam etiam hic respici, nullum dubium sit. Quæ enim generaliter dicta sunt, non sunt pro nostro arbitrio restringenda. Generatim autem hæc dicta esse, ea quæ adduntur, haud obscure docent.

Vers. eod. FORTIS ISRAEL, DOMINATOR HOMI- NUM, JVSTUS DOMINATOR IN TIMO- RE DEI.

Fortis Israel est Filius DEI: qui conjungitur Spiritui Domini, qui loquutus est per Davidem, & cujus sermo factus est per linguam ejus: & DEO Israelis, quo nomine designatur DEUS Pater, ut habeatur hic insigne testimonium SS. Trinitatis. B. Meisnerus in λογολογίᾳ vel Disput. in Joh. 1. per Sermonem Domini intelligit verbum hypostaticum: At rectius B. Lutherus de verbo προφορικῷ acci- pit: & Deum Israelis DEUM Patrem dici notat: qui promissiones Davidi dedit, Petram vero seu rupem & fortem Israelis, dominatorem justum in- ter homines Filium DEI vocari censet: qui hic pro- ducatur, tanquam versans inter homines, & itidem loquens, & adferens promissiones: ideoque ita con- cludit lib. de novissimis verb. David. Tom. 3. Lat. Witeb. f. 95. sunt igitur Tres Personæ loquentes, & ta- men unus idemque Deus loquitur, idem est promissor, eadem promissio sicut unus Deus, benedictus in secula. Suffragatur Coccejus in commentario ad Psalmos adjecto: Non inepte hic, si ad proprietatem atten- damus, distingui judicabimus tres personas. Spiritus Jehovæ vers. 2. Deus Israelis, qui Israelem adjura- vit, ut crederet sibi, quod ipsi futurus esset DEUS, quem scil. nominare, cui jurare, in quo gloriari posset. Rupes Israelis, is, ad quem Israel con- fugit, ut est Psalmo secundo vers. 12. qui Israelem portat potenti verbo suo Esa. 63, 9. imo merito suo, ut salvator. De qua salute est vers. 5. Non potest hoc videri ineptum, aut non necessarium, ei, qui consideraverit, verbum, quod hic commemorat David, esse verbum Testamenti, & fœderis, de fide ad justitiam, cujus fundamentum est Dei revelatio in carne, ad præstandam εὐδοκίαν. Ab his rebus de- nominari Deum verbi auctorem, minime ineptum est. Imo morosum esset, & plenum ἀπειθείας, nolle id in verbis intelligere, quod in eis intelligi potest, attenta eorum emphasii. Denique non est putandum, verba illa sine causa fuisse multiplicata. Tribuit autem scriptura Christo peculiariter nomen Petræ Psalm. 118, 22. Cantic. 2, 13. Esa. 8, 14. cap. 28, 16. Matth. 16, 18. 1. Corinth. 10, 4. quia Ecclesiæ fundamentum solidissimum est, ceu ædificii DEI 1. Corinth. 3, 9. 11. Matth. 16, 19.

Vers. eod. DOMINATOR HOMINUM, JUSTUS DO- MINATOR IN TIMORE DEI.

Hæc jam ad argumentum Prophetiæ pertinent, non vero recte ad præcedentia trahuntur: quod distinctivus accentus Atnach indicat. De Filio tamen DEI sonant: cujus proinde mentio, cum recenserentur personæ Trinitatis, postremo re- servata loco fuit, quia de eo porro dicendum erat, ut Apocal. 1, 4. Hunc solet Scriptura Dominatorem vocare in Israele Mich. 5, 2. Jerem. 30, 21. Hic unicus est ille justus dominator, quem ita celebra- S. S. Jerem. 23, 5. Zachar. 9, 9. Esa. 11, 4. 5. Id er- go est, quod vaticinatur de Petra Israelis: Erit do- minator hominum, justus dominator in timore DEI, sive quia ipse timorem DEI maxime inculcabit, ac propagabit, sine quo timori Domini nullus fuisset locus, & in timore Domini universum ejus Domi- nium instituetur, Esa. 11, 3. 5. sive quod speciali- ter illis, qui in timore DEO serviunt, ipse domi- netur Psalm. 2, 11, ut vel regni, aut regis, vel subdi- torum adjunctum, aut Epitheton id habendum sit. Priori modo interpretatur B. Lutherus l. c. Domi- nator efficiens timorem DEI. David sua guberna- tione ne unum quidem hominem justum & timentem DEI reddidit, imo ne se quidem ipsum, ac ne Moses quidem ipse legis & politiæ constitutor, sed quicun- que unquam fuerunt justi timentes DEUM, ii per hunc Dominum justificati, & ad verum timorem DEI perducti sunt. Posteriori modo explicat San- ctius, Cornel. & Tirinus, quod Dominator eorum sit, qui timent Deum. Recte hîc observat Coccejus: verba illa jam ad argumentum revelationis pertine- re: non autem convenienter ea trahit ad Da- videm: qui in verbis novissimis non de se & do- minio suo, quod jam depositurus erat cum vita, sed de Messia vaticinatur. Alienus ergo hactenus ille Commentarius: Est non tantum prædictio de Davide, sed promissio, eum dominaturum in timo- re Domini. Rectius exposuit Chaldæus, qui, no- tante ipso Coccejo, verba illa accipit, ut de Chri- sto dicta: Sic enim παραφράζει: Dixit David, DEUS Israelis de me locutus est, qui potestatem habet in filiis hominum, veritatem judicans, dicit se constituturum mihi Regem, nempe Messiam in futu- rum, qui surget & imperabit in timore Domini. Et agnoscit Coccejus vers. 4. immediate sequentem, qui hanc orationem vel promissionem continuat per Vav copulativum, (quod ab Interpp. quibus- dam temere negligitur.) Et lucente matutino (vel, ut luce matutini) exorietur sol: de Christo, & re- gno ejus agere: atque in eo Interpretes CONVENI- RE, quod de Messia ibi agatur: etiam Judæos. Cur ergo immediate cohærentia, idemque subjectum referentia non ad Messiam, sed ad Davidem tra- hit? Quanquam nec de Judæis id simpliciter verum sit, qui solum sensu mystico de Messia hæc interpre- tantur, nec de aliis Interpp. universis. Siquidem & Pontificii, Cornel. à Lapid. aliique & Calviniani nonnulli Judæos ea in parte sequuntur: quidam etiam simpliciter de Davide explicent cum Ludov. de Dieu, aut de iis, qui magna prosperitate fruun- tur, ut Ravanell. in Bibliothec. in voce Lux &c. Quod vero Coccejus ait: non videri eos bene conne- ctere, quia putant copulative prædicari de מושל dominatore, quod sit instar lucis matutini, adeoque non appareat sic, quam bene cohæreat τὸ וזרח exo- rietur, facile expeditur: Nam copulative prædi- cari potest ratione sensus, ut subjectum idem sit, dominator inter homines existens, & sol ille exori- ens, etiamsi non ratione vocum hæc in unam pro- positionem copulentur, sed distinctas efficiant pro- positiones. Prior hæc est: Erit dominans inter ho- mines, justus dominator timoris DEI: Altera vero hæc: Et lucente matutino exorietur sol justitiæ: De hoc enim sole agi fatetur Coccejus. Idque ita probat pag. 591. Nulla enim ratio est, quare hîc τὸ ῥητὸν urgeamus, & de ortu solis proprio & diluculo, & pluvia & gramine, quod boves comedunt, sermo- nem habitum putemus. Magna autem ratio est, qua- re aliud significatum arbitremur, & esse hæc verba ἀλληγορύμενα, & hoc significare, quod πνευματι- xῶς significare possunt & solent. David enim, qui gratias hîc agit Deo pro maximis beneficiis, & in eo- rum enumeratione assurgit, ubi loquitur de εὐδοκία πάσῃ & σωτηρίᾳ ἀυτõ, non potest oblitus esse Filii sui, solis justitia. Et postea: Non puto Davidi con- venire, & ipsius modestiæ, ut regnum suum com- paret soli puro, sine nubibus, & magis magisque pro- ficienti. David non fuit sol, non luxit ut sol, non attulit lætitiam, quam sol. Reliquit populum in sua servitute & in suo desiderio. Ipse peccavit, & pec- catis suis Israelem contristavit & conturbavit; & re- gnum ipsius passum est Eclipsin: & splendor domus ipsius imminutus est. Aliud ipsum dicentem mox au- diemus. Hæc rectissime Coccejus. Verba וּכְאוֹר בֹּקֶר geminum sensum habere possunt: primo comparationis: Et, sicut, luce mane, vel tanquam luce matutini, exorietur sol: deinde temporis; Et, cum lucebit matutinum, exorietur sol. Neuter in- conveniens est de sole justitiæ. Priorem probat Coccejus h. m. Quando lux in mundum venit, dies factus est, & tanquam matutinum. Visa enim gloria ipsius tanquam unigeniti à Patre. Qui ipsum viderunt & cognoverunt, iis fuit dies clarus, ut matu- tinum. Posteriorem tamen etiam non reprobat, ut alienum, etsi illum simpliciorem censeat: Tempus, inquit, Veteris Testamenti est tempus umbrarum & noctis. Post illam noctem erit matutinum in παρ8- σίᾳ χρισõ in carne. Mox exorietur sol, Christo re- surgente ex mortuis, & ascendente in cælum, ut lu- ceat in majestate & gloria. Qui nobis non incon- cinnus videtur. Et quid obstat τὸ mane ita acci- pere, ut designetur tempus resurrectionis, quo ex- oriri cœpit sol justitiæ, cum Christus per mortem ingressus est in gloriam suam; vel si mavis, ut saltim ea voce hic eo, ut in vaticiniis fieri, in similitudi- nibus, amat, alludatur, taciteque illud tempus in- sinuetur? Nam peculiariter exortus est sol ille ju- stitiæ, cum summo mane Christus prodiret è sepul- cro: Mox illustrare cœpit mulierum corda, Mariæ Magdalenæ, & earum quæ ad sepulcrum excurre- runt: ac Simonis Petri: ac post, illustratis Aposto- lis, pleno jubare radios suæ majestatis explicare cœpit per universum orbem. Sic verba subjuncta hunc habebunt sensum: Mane illo non erunt nu- bes (ignorantiæ, & miseriæ, vel tristitiæ, & mœro- ris, utpote quas sol justitiæ ortu suo discutiet) à splendore, à pluvia germen ex terra erit. Splendor solis illius, cum pluvia Spiritus, causæ erunt ferti- litatis spiritualis, ut germina è terra proditura sint spiritualia, h. e. credentes, magno numero, & proventu: Coccejus sensum adversative exponit, hoc modo: Etiamsi mane illo non erunt nubes, ta- men à fulgore & ab imbre, nascetur gramen ex tota terra, h. e. etiamsi in Christi παρ8σίᾳ non erit ma- gna apparentia pluviæ sive benedictionis conjecti in terram seminis à Christo, h. e. verbi ab ipso prædi- cati: nihilominus tamen cum jubare cælesti etiam pluvia cadet, nimir. Spiritus Sanct. copiose effusus, qui faciet enasci germina ex toto mundo. Voce ex terra notatur secundum Coccejum magna, multi- tudo. Statim prima pentecoste aliquot millia credi- derunt ex omni tribu & ex omni loco; etiam prosely- ti. Et lux illa non desinit lucere in posterum, & plu- via cum luce cadit in terram, per quam totus mundus sit frugifer. Eam copiam similitudine roris copio- se terram operientis alias expressit David, utpote Psalm. 110, 3.

Alii in hisce similibus, quæ hoc loco vers. 4. in verbis novissimis adhibita sunt, ita nude acquie- scunt; ut tantum de sole, ac nubibus, physice ac- ceptis, de splendore etiam, ac pluvia, qua fertili- tatem germinis terreni, & materialis promovent, haec interpretentur, ac si nullum iis subesset myste- rium; quo pacto Lud. de Dieu haec adduci vult: ut- pote in quibus nulla sit constantia, vel stabilitas, ni- hil ordinatum ubique & in suo ordine firmiter custo- ditum. Nam quod ad solem attinet, oritur luce matutini, sed idem rursus occidit sub vespera. De- inde quod ad serenitatem aurorae, solet ea quidem primo splendoris ortu discutere nubes, sed cum jam aliquandiu sol supra horizontem adscendit, rede- unt nubes, aut succedunt aliae, quae coelum obscu- rant, & contristant. Tertio, quod ad teneram her- bam attinet, quae per pluviam e terra progerminat, laeta ea est, & utilis, sed quae tamen subito flaccescit. Ut ita subjurgatur κατ' αντιθεσιν: Non sic est do- mus mea coram DEO, aeternum ea foedus habet, quod ubique recte ordinatum est, & in eo ordine custodi- tur. Sed non adhibentur similia illa in sensu se- quiori, nec quicquam de inconstantia, aut insta- bilitate sive splendoris solis, sive serenitatis aurorae, sive progerminationis herbarum indicatur (quae aliis verbis efferenda fuiffet) imo illa potius ut grata, jucunda, & utilia celebrantur, exortus so- lis, aurea serenitas, terrae a splendore & pluvia foe- cunditas: ut ipse verborum tenor docet. Et quid stabile ac aeternum in domo Davidis, quid recte ordinatum, & firmum magis fuit, quam in sole, cujus ortus & occasus certa lege firmatus, ordina- tiffimusque nullam patitur exorbitantiam? Quod vero Diepius observat, etsi Davidis domus adver- sa multa, & mutationes varias subierit, mansisse tamen semper illud, quod in foedere DEI cum ipso initum erat, id documento est, quicquid hic de stabilitate, & ordinata, firmaque constitutione ha- betur, non ad familiam, vel domum Davidis, sed ad promissionem de Messia, regnoque ejus, quo de foe- dus proprie sancitum erat, pertinere, imo ab ipsa Davidis domo removeri illam certitudinem, ac stabilitatem, verba textus sonora testantur: Nam non sic (vel recta aut stabilis, quia utroque modo vocem illam כֵּן reddi posse observant Interpp.) est domus mea apud DEUM: sed foedus perpetuum posuit mihi expositum inter omnes, & servatum: quod omnis salus mea, & omne beneplacitum; quam non germinabit domus mea; ut interpretatur Coc- cejus.

Convenientius alii illis verbi de sole, aurora, splendore, pluvia graminisque copioso proventu πρό- τασιν quidem solum contineri similitudinis censent, ἀπόδοσιν vero tacite simul insinuari, quod nempe applicatio eorum fieri debeat, non ad domum & familiam Davidis, sed ad Messiam, ejusque re- gnum, ut ortus solis justitiae, serenitasque eodem exoriente, nubium expers, & a splendore ejus, plu- viaque ab eo dimissa (quam vel de doctrina hominem irrigante, ut justitiam operetur, cum autore ope- ris imperfecti in Matthaeum hom. 20. e Deuter. 32, 2. Esa. 55, 10. 11. vel de pluvia Spiritus Sancti e Psalm. 68, 10. intelligunt) terrae foecunditas Spiritualis per ea similia insinuetur. Quae interpretatio B. Lu- theri fuit, πρότασιν insuper speciatim ad tempus Vernale vi collationis Cantic. 2, 11. 12. referentis Tom. 8. Germ. Jen. Von den letzten Worten Da- vids fol. 168. Er vergleicht die Herrschafft oder das Reich Messia, der die Gerechtigkeit und Gottes- furcht soll wiederbringen und auffrichten, dem schö- nen lieblichen Wesen des Lentzen, wenn gegen dem Sommer die liebe Sonne wieder zu uns nahet; so thut sich die Erde auf, grünet, blühet, reucht alles schön, wird alles neue, und die Welt gleich wieder lebendig, und frölich: Also ist die Herr- schafft und das Reich der Gnaden auch eine fröliche lustige Zeit, darinnen Messias uns gerecht und gottesfurchtig macht, daß wir grůnen, blůhen, wohl riechen, wachsen, und fruchtbar werden, denn Er ist die Sonne der Gerechtigkeit, darum Er auch hat wollen lieblich im Lenzen, oder April, in der lustigen Zeit von den Todten aufferstehen, und sei- ne Herrschafft anfahen. Et postea: Zu Messia Zeiten (spricht David,) wenn der ZUR Jsrael selbst herrschen wird, mit Gnaden uns gerecht und selig zu machen, wirds so lieblich seyn, als die beste Zeit im Lenzen, da es vor Tages einen lieblichen warmen Regen gethan hat, (das ist, das tröstliche Evangelium geprediget ist,) und flugs darauf die Sonne Christus auffgehet in unsern Hertzen, durch rechten Glauben, ohne des Mose Wolcken, Don- ner und Blitzen, da wächsts, grůnets, blůhets al- les nach, und ist der Tag freudenreich und frieden- reich, deßgleichen das gantze Jahr nicht hat; denn hie heißts Winter, Wolcken, Donner, Sůnde, Tod und alles Schrecken überwunden, und einen schönen frölichen Ostertag gehalten biß in Ewigkeit; siehe, das heißt David seines Sohns Messia Herr- schafft gleich seyn einem Tag im Lenzen, da es frů- he geregnet, darauf die Sonne auffgehet auffs al- lerlieblichste, und machet grůn, blůhend, riechend, und alles lebendig und frölich; frage dich selber drum, obs nicht die beste und frölichste Zeit im Jahre sey? Eadem ratione Luc. Osiander in pul- cherrima sua paraphrasi, postquam Ebraicum tex- tum ita reddidit: sicut lux matutina, cum oritur sol mane sine nubibus de splendore (&) de pluvia herba ter- ræ enascitur; id est: Quemadmodum in vere, cum post pluviam mane sol clarissime oritur, terra non mo- do solis splendore illustratur, sed etiam calefit, & gi- gnit herbas ac flores, ut omnia sint eo tempore amœ- nissima: sic cum post fœcundam Evangelii pluviam ex- oritur Christus, sol justitiæ, in cordibus credentium, omnia fiunt amœna & jucunda: ita ut homo, quippe cujus conscientia per Evangelion Christi pacata est, videatur sibi è tenebris inferni in jucundissimam lucem, è tristi carcere in Paradismum, denique de morte in vitam ingressus. Itaque filius meus Christus, inquit David, reparabit in hoc mundo credentibus cælestem Paradisum.

Quod itaque ad verba, quæ sequuntur de do- mo Davidis, ea, uti diximus, non deprædicant stabilitatem regni Davidi positive, sed rectius ab in- terpp. plerique remotive explicantur, seu quod iisdem κατ᾽ ἄρσιν testetur Propheta, se non jam de domo sua, sed de Messiæ regno fœdere sibi confirmato agere, ut Coccejus exposuit, seu quod profiteatur, domum suam tanti non esse, quæ digna sit ista gratia, ut nempe ex eadem pro- diturus sit Christus Rex æternus: quem sensum am- plectitur Osiander præeunte B. Luthero, è colla- tione 1. Paralip. 17. Nec tanta est domus mea apud DEUM, ut pactum æternum iniret mecum. Ach was bin ich? was ist mein Haus gegen GOTT? Es ist ja nicht ein solch Haus, das bey GOTT sol- cher unaussprechlichen Ehren wůrdig sey, von wel- chem Messia, der ZUR Jsrael, GOttes Sohn, der gerechte Herrscher unter den Menschen soll ge- bohren werden. Et Tom. 7. Witteberg. Lat. libr. de Judæis fol. 183. Ut propius reddam ex Ebræo, mea domus certe non est tanti, id est, domus mea non est digna; vocem כּי reddendam esse utique etiam Ludov. de Dieu notavit, quod sæpe ea non sit causalis, sed confirmativa, ut Genes. 22, 17. ubi LXX. habent ἦ μὴν. De regno ergo Messiæ præ- clare interpretatur divinus noster Lutherus, quæ adduntur de pacto illo ordinato in omnibus atque munito. Die folgende zwen Worte, Arucha und Schemura, wohl geordnet und gehalten, sind mit Fleiß gesezt zur Lehre und Trost; denn so du ansihest die Historien, wird dich düncken, GOTT habe seines Bundes vergessen, und den nicht ge- halten, so gar wüste, unordig und seltzam gehts zu in Davids Hause und Nachkommen. Noch ists biß auf Messia nicht allein gehalten, sondern ist alles in seiner Ordnung wohl und sein blieben, wider alle Teuffel und Menschen, und hats nie- mand können ändern noch dämpffen, sondern ha- bens müssen lassen gehen und stehen, ein Scepter Juda, wie es verheissen ist biß auf Messia. Aber nach Messia ist sein Reich, die Kirche, äusserlich an- zusehen viel wüster und unordiger, daß kein zurisse- ner, elender, nichtiger Regiment oder Herrschafft ist, denn die Christliche Kirche, Christi Herrschafft, hie zureissens und wüstens mit Feuer, Wasser, Schwerdt und aller Macht die Tyrannen, hie zuwühlen und verderbens die Rotten-Geister und Ketzerey. So machens die falschen Christen mit ihrem bösen Leben auch also, als sey kein schändlicher, ungeordenter Herrschafft auf Erden; und diese alle arbeiten da- hin, oder vielmehr der böse Geist durch sie, daß Christi Herrschafft solle nichts oder ie ein elend unor- dig Ding seyn. Und Summa, Christus stellet sich, als habe Er seiner Herrschafft vergessen, und sey nirgend heime, daß hie weder Arucha, noch Semura von der Vernunfft gesehen wird, noch heist sie Arucha, Be- col und Schemura, alles wohl geordnet und gehal- ten, ob wirs nicht sehen, so siehet Ers, der da spricht, Cantic. ultimo, mein Weinberg ist für mir, Matth. ultimo, siehe, ich bin bey euch biß an der Welt En- de, Joh. 16. seyd getrost, ich habe die Welt überwun- den. Gleichwohl sehen wir, daß immer blieben ist und bleibt ein Volck, das den Nahmen Christi ehret, sein Wort, Tauffe, Sacrament, Schlüssel und Geist hat, auch wider alle Pforten der Höllen. Hæc Megalander, quem sequitur Osiandrina Paraphra- sis: Atque regnum illud Messiæ erit firmum. Hebr. ordinatum in omnibus, i. e. quanquam in regno Christi videantur multæ esse confusiones, dum jam persequutionibus infestatur, jam hæresibus perturbatur, jam offendiculis deformatur: tamen apparebit tandem singularis & admiranda sapien- tia DEI, qua omnia recte disposuisse agnoscetur: quod scil. nihil mali permiserit, ex quo non ma- gnum aliquod bonum sit consecutum. Et tamet- si Satan regnum illud magnis insultibus cupiat evertere, tamen firmum erit, atque munitum, rectius: custoditum (i. e. Deus suos ut pupillam oculi custodiet, nec sinet Evangelion ante novis- simum diem omnino deleri.

Supersunt illa de desiderio Davidico: Cun- cta enim salus mea, & omnis voluntas, nec est quic- quam ex ea quod non germinet: quæ (1.) de non ger- minante domo Davidis Coccejus exposuit ad tem- pus exortus Christi hæc ita referens: Sol justitiæ exoriatur, quum domus mea quasi in cineribus ja- cebit (non germinatura ad regnum & splendorem Jerem. 22, 30.) ad inchoandum regnum cæleste, ut scil. paret salutem mihi, & omnibus Sanctis, qui spe- raverunt in ipsum, non ut tum primum salvemur, propter ipsum, sed ut ipse perfectus salvator sit ipsa oblatione sacrificii, & omnem εὐδοκίαν Patris pro- mereatur Ps. 16, 3. Notat Coccejus voculam כי non solum ætiologice accipi pro quia, & adversative pro sed, verum etiam objective pro quod vel ὅτι, nec non ut adverbium temporis, quando: atque id velle

Davidem: domus mea non germinabit, sed sol orie- tur, & quidem in domo mea, & ex domo mea. Ebr. 7, 14. sed non domus meæ γονιμότητι, & virtute carnalis fœcunditatis. Sed hæc coacta quodam- modo sunt. (2.) Simplicior est B. Lutheri expli- catio in glossa marginali, & Tom. 8. Jen. Germ. fol. 169. quod citra respectum temporis comparetur, aut opponatur potius regnum Davidis regno Chri- sti, q. d. Regnum meum, & quicquid ago, respectu regni Meffiæ est tantum veluti aridus ramus, aut trun- cus. Quam explicationem amplexi sunt Vinarien- ses Paraphrastæ. (3.) Franc. Vatablus ita adducit R. David Kimchii explicationem; Doctor inter He- bræos exponit, non erit ut germen agri, quod eva- nescit, sed perpetuo regnabit ille qui est salus mea, & desiderium meum Christus, qui de semine Davi- dis descendet. (4.) Convenientissima videtur Osiandrina Paraphrasis: Cuncta enim salus mea, sub- audi, consistit in spirituali regno Christi, & totum desiderium, quod non crescat: id est, nihil æque desi- dero, quam ut liceret videre exorientem illum solem justitiæ, Christum in carne, & crescere regnum illud pa- cis, quod reficiet conscientias, amœnissimum illum Pa- radisum cœlestem: Ach, warum wächst es doch nicht schon? es verlanget mich, daß es nicht gleich jetzt wachsen will. Qui sensus ita juvari poterit, cun- cta salus mea, & omnis voluptas vel totum desiderium in eo est, quod nondum crescit: vel etiam in eo (Chri- sto aut regno Christi) est: quamvis nondum crescat, temen in illo uno cuncta salus mea, & omnis voluptas mea est. Sic optime respondet antithesis subjun- cta. Nam uti fideles cum Davide in Christo unice omnem salutem, & omnem voluptatem suam col- locant, quem ideo tantopere desiderabant pii ve- teres, cum Rege ac Propheta nostro, sic ex adver- so infideles viri Belial hanc salutem reprobant, qui ut spinæ inutiles, & noxiæ amovendi omnes, & igne cremando cremabuntur: quod speciatim ad Judæos refert B. Lutherus, etsi alios etiam hostes regni Chri- sti complectatur, & istorum exitium imprimis hic designari censet: David heisset Kotz die grossen bösen stachlichen Disteln, oder die andern Disteln, so unsere Bauren Tollgraet heissen, die man mit Sensen, Sicheln und Harcken, oder Spiessholtz aussondern muß in der Erndte, denn mit Händen kan sie alle beyde niemand angreiffen, und dienen nirgend hin, denn ins Feuer, aber Trespen braucht man für das Vieh, also sind die verstockten Jüden solche böse stachliche Disteln und Tollgraete, daß sie mit keiner Wohlthat noch Wunder GOttes zu be- kehren gewest und noch sind, sondern durch der Rö- mer Eisen und Spiesse ausgestossen, und mit ihrer Stadt in ihrer eigen Wohnung verbrandt, auch mit leiblichem Feuer, über das brennen sie noch jetzt in ihnen selber, wo sie im Elende sind, mit Geistlichem Feuer Göttliches Zorns, also hat David diesem Volck seine Verstörung und endlich Verderben verkündigt, darum, daß sie diesen König nicht ha- ben wollten, wie der HERR Luc. 19. auch da- von weissagt, und Daniel 9. Zach. 14. De Judæo- rum exitio etiam interpretatur Coccejus, nec non de Anti-Christi; etsi nec alios excludat. Osiander principaliter de Judæis sermonem hic esse, in univer- sum tamen reliquos etiam impios, quia spinæ sunt, saltem in novissimo die de agro Domini evulsum, & igne inextinguibili combustum iri, notat. De Judæis etiam peculiariter interpretatus est Lyranus, & Alphonsus Tostatus, deque eorundem exitio. Sed Propheta loquitur de filiis Belial IN UNIVER- SUM, & de omnibus, qui non delectationem ha- bent in Christo & salute ejus, ut oppositio con- vincit, de omnibus qui spinæ sunt, inutiles, & noxiæ, quibus combustionem minatur; adeoque de exter- no exitio infidelium hic proprie agitur. Quemad- modum æternam salutem David, cum omnibus fide- libus, in Messia unice collocat, in eoque omnem vo- luptatem habet: ita vi oppositionis, filii Belial uni- versi, qui jugum Messiæ excutiunt, Ps. 2,3. nec regno, aut mandatis ejus subjici volunt, non tantum æterna salute ac beatitudine excidunt, sed æterno etiam exi- tio subjiciuntur: ut illi, graminis instar, virtute splen- doris solis justitiæ, & pluviæ doctrinæ salutiferæ læ- te proveniunt, ac crescunt in Paradiso Domini: sic infideles instar spinarum sunt, quæ ceu inutiles & no- xiæ evellendæ & igne comburendæ sunt.

Illud ימלא non de homine aggressuro illas spinas, sese armante, vel muniente, sed de aculeis spi- narum, præeunte Levi Gersone explicat Ludov. de Dieu, qui manus vulnera replent; sed simplicior est communis interpretatio: non enim impletur is fer- ro & lancea, qui vulneratur iisdem: at cum arma- tur & munitur illis, impleri non male dicitur: non enim nudis manibus aggreditur spinas, sed manus implet ferro, vel ligone, ac falce, quo succidat eas, aut hastili lanceæ, quo abigat aut propellat easdem, ne ab iis lædatur, ut Vatablus; aut præserrato ligno ad hastæ similitudinem, ut Sanctius exponit: Vulgata reddidit, armatur: Junius, munitur: Et possunt no- mina per Hendyaden reddi, armatus ferro & ligno hastæ, id est, ferro ligni hastæ, quo interpretatio præ- dicta Sanctiana abit. Vir, inquit David, impetum in illos faciet armatus: Vir, (non puer) validus robu- stus. Et igne cremando cremabuntur, בַּשָּׁבֶת, quæ in habitatione reddunt plerique aut in loco, ac sede, eadem sc. ubi natæ sunt spinæ; solent enim spinosæ herbæ, & aculeati frutices in ipsis agris, ubi prodie- runt, ac creverunt, incendi, & comburi. Quæ de προτάσει similitudinis recte se habent, cum persi- stitur in comparatione spinarum; ut tacite ἀποδό- σις de hostibus regni Christi, viris Belial, impiis, & infidelibus ita insinuetur, & ex illa προτάσει colli- genda sit: neque tamen præter rem in ipsa προτάσει ea adhibentur verba, quæ concinne, in ἀποδόσει, impiorum exitio aptentur, ac judicio Dei conve- niant adversus filios Belial. Solet enim Deus in- star viri armati eosdem aggredi, vel etiam viros ferro & lancea armatos adhibere: crematque eos igne iræ suæ, cum temporalis excidii, tum sem- piterni exitii, quod experti imprimis Judæi sunt, inter filios Belial celebriores, & præcipui commatis: de quibus B. Lutherus recte, quod adhuc non desi- nant ardere, ubicunque sunt in conventiculis suis, & miserrime exulet, illo æterno igne iræ divinæ. Quem vero sequetur ignis inextinguibilis gehennæ, IN MANSIONE ab æterno Diabolo, & infidelibus pa- rata, h. e. in inferno Matth. 25, 41. Psalm. 49. v. 15. Conf. Matth. 3, 12. cap. 13, 30. 38. 42. Joh. 15, 6. Ap. 20, 10. Etiamsi enim ad similitudinis πρότασιν il- la HABITATIONIS vox pertineat, modo decla- rata, de industria tamen, in similibus, ejusmodi vo- cibus utitur Spir. Sanct. quæ convenientiores sunt & analogæ rebus in ἀποδόσει subintellectis, & ad easdem alludant: adeoque habitationem, vel sedem suam spinis tribuit hoc loco, per allusionem ad sedem & habitationem impiorum, quæ ab æterno ipsis pa- rata, eorumque propria est in æternum. Coccejus reddit in CONSESSU: & consessum Ecclesiæ nota- ri vult: sed id non convenit τῇ προτάσει, cujus ta- men omnino habenda est ratio. Ideoque com- muni interpretationi de habitatione acquiescimus:

quæ etiam B. Lutheri est, & Osiandri, sic corrigen- tis Vulgati prorsus alienam translationem, US- QUE AD NIHILUM. Nam de eo nihilo nihil habetur in Ebræo: unde & a Pagnino, & Jesuita Casp. Sanctio vulgata hic castigata est: quia שֶׁבֶת est sedes, habitatio a יָשַׁב sedere, commorari. Atque hæc de ultimis verbis Davidis. Juvat tamen ad- scribere, quæ Coccejus in ultimis Mosis de hoc loco habet §. 989. Nam non recta est domus mea cum Deo (non melior, aut dignior est posteritas mea apud Deum, quam aliorum hominum. Vide Psalm. 51, 7. Job. 14, 4.) sed fœdus æternum, Testamentum & promissionem posuit mihi, expositum in omnibus, ut omnes homines in eo fœdere salutem sperare pos- sint, & servatum sine pœnitentia; quod omnis SA- LUS MEA & omnis complacentia futura sit, quum non germinabit domus mea. Eo tempore, quo do- mus mea non feret amplius virgam ad dominandum, Ezech. 19, 14. Sed ramus prefectus fuerit, Esa. 10, 33. domo mea non stante in mandatis Dei: tum nihilomi- nus dabit mihi Deus domum & semen, per quod pro- curetur SALUS non corporis, sed animæ, quippe MEA, jamdudum mortui, ut peccata mea per illud expiantur; & omnis complacentia h. e. omnis gra- tia, qua Deus remittit peccata & justitiam imputat. Hæc Coccejus, de quibus judicium e superioribus fieri potest.

Placet etiam hic subjicere programma festo nativitatis Anno 1664. propositum, ad Novissimo- rum verborum Davidis illustrationem conducens. Quod hujus est tenoris:

Quis tanta rerum verborumque copia instru- ctus existat, qui hujus diei gratiam dignis possit lau- dibus prædicare? Natalis est hodie Salvatoris, in quo dicente S. Augustino, lumen additum mundo est, & immortalitas, quæ per peccatum perierat, mortalibus reddita est: Hodie illum peperit virgo, qui sententiam prævaricationis excluderet, pœnam mortis eriperet, & vitam perpetuam credentibus donaret. Quas laudes charitati DEI dicamus, quas gratias agamus, qui nos ita dilexit, ut propter nos fieret in tempore, per quem facta sunt tempora, homo fieret, qui hominem fecit, crearetur ex ma- tre, quam creavit, portaretur manibus, quas forma- vit, sugeret ubera, quæ implevit, in præsepi muta vagiret infantia Verbum, sine quo muta est humana eloquentia! Stupent tanta mysteria Angeli, miran- tur Archangeli, trementes inspicicere gestiunt sum- mi Principatus ac throni. Exultant autem ob ista gratiæ munera, & cum gaudio incredibili eadem orbi annunciant cœlestes Legati. Totus exercitus superni chorus, & cœlum & terram implet cantu, qualem decantavit unquam, dulcissimo: Gloria in excelsis DEO, in terra pax, hominibus bona vo- luntas. Quum olim fulgentes Seraphim eminus adhuc conspicarentur gloriam carnis Christi, quæ in thronum eminentissimæ majestatis evehenda e- rat, faciem velabant ad immensum fulgorem, & tris- hagium suum perenne læti concinebant: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Jehovah Zebaoth, plena est gloria ejus universa terra. Quanto majori credemus perculsas stupore, delibutas gaudio cœlestes do- minationes, & potestates, ubi coram intueban- tur DEUM immensum, quem cœli cœlorum non capiunt, tegumento carnis circumdatum, in- fantem, in cunis vagientem, infinita gloria uni- geniti a Patre coruscantem, ut exules cœli Societa- ti angelicæ iterum adsererentur, & ad cœlestis gau- dii consortium denuo susciperentur. Quapro- pter ad concentum trishagii sui mortales dulci vo- ce invitant, illudque novo, & hactenus inaudito hymno, in laudem gloriosæ Trinitatis, suavissime illustrant; Sanctus DEUS Pater, Sanctus DEUS Filius, Sanctus DEUS Spiritus Sanctus, Sanctus Triu- nus ille Jehovah Zebaoth, gloria ejus nunc repletur u- niversa terra. Quia terræ universæ natus est Salva- tor. Gloria in excelsis DEO Patri, qui hanc Salutem ex mera misericordia orbi gratificatur. Gloria DEO Filio, qui in terra apparere dignatur, ut PAX vera, o- mnia pacificans in cœlo & in terra. Gloria DEO Spiritui Sancto, in quo εὐδοκία in hominibus, ex gratia Patris, per Filium Pacis Principem. Lætentur itaque nunc cœli, & exultet terra, commoveatur mare, & ple- nitudo ejus, gaudebunt campi, & omnia quæ in eis sunt. Exultent omnia ligna sylvarum, a facie Domini, quia VENIT. Annunciarunt cœli justitiam ejus, & vide- runt omnes populi gloriam ejus! Adorate eum omnes Angeli ejus: Audivit, & læta est Sion. Et exultarunt filii Judæ, propter judicia tua Domine. Lux orta est justo, & rectis corde lætitia: Lætamini justi in Domino, & confitemini memoriæ sanctificationis ejus. Miseri- cordias Domini cantabimus in æternum, in generatio- nem & generationem aununciabimus veritatem tuam ore nostro.

Ita jam olim excitavit Nos Hiero-Psaltes, cum in Spiritu prævidit gaudium magnum, quod toti mundo nunc annunciavit angelus & chorus angeli- cus. Non enim vel ipse, vel quisquam Sanctorum Veteris Testamenti hujus gaudii expers fuit, & con- firmatus erat peculiariter de Christo DEI Israel, egre- gius Psaltes Israel: Locutus ei est Fortis Israel (Petra, quæ erat Christus, teste Apostolo,) quem in verbis suis novissimis, ut testaretur, se in hac fide ad Patres migraturum, professus est, Dominatorem inter ho- stes, justum Dominatorem in timore DEI; Adeoque vaticinatus est, quod Rex aliquis futurus sit in Isra- ele, qui regnaturus sit in justitia, & in timore Domini: Lucente, inquit, aurora, orietur Sol, matutinum sine nubibus erit a splendore, a pluvia germen erit 2. Sam. 23, 4. Quæ μυςηριώδη sunt, atque id indicant, quod circa tempus noctis, vel finis umbrarum, quasi cum diluculo & Phosphoro, Johanne Baptista, præ- lucente Sol justitiæ oriturus sit. Densitates porro, & nubes discussum iri a splendore ejus, cum velut a pluvia germen justum e terra proditurum. Quæ plerique de Evangelii fructu intelligunt, quod plu- viæ instar terram germinare facit. Coccejus in ul- timis Mosis significari vult, ortum Solis justitiæ fore humilem, sine nubibus, spem pluviæ & benedictionis divinæ pollicentibus, attamen tum a splendore ipsius per divinam benedictionem germen ex terra proven- turum esse. Sed ortum germinis justi, quod Jere- miæ est celebratum cap. 23, 6. cum quo omnis ju- stitia germinare cœpit, a quo etiam, & in quo omnis est Evangelii fœcunditas, omnia respiciunt, uti hæc in ultimo itidem Psalmo suo, qui est 72. (ubi post traditum regnum Salomoni Filio, in Messiæ regno totus defixus fuit) Prophetarum & Regum Sanctissimus interpretatus est: Descendet sicut plu- via in vellus, & sicut stillicidia stillantia super terram. Nam, ita pergit Hieropsaltes, non recta est domus mea coram DEO, (qui phrasis Ebrææ sensus est 2. Reg. 7. vers. 9. Jerem. 8. vers. 6.) sed fœdus æter- num posuit mihi ex mera gratia, vel ut sensum red- didit Vulgatus, non tanta est domus, aut familia mea apud DEUM, ut pactum æternum iniret me- cum, firmum in omnibus, atque munitum, quod alii interpretantur, expositum in omnibus, ut scil. omnes homines in eo fœdere salutem sperare pos- sint, ἀμεταμελήτως servatum aut servandum, quod omnis salus mea, & omnis complacentia (εὐδοκία) futura sit, cum non germinabit domus mea, eo tem- pore, quo domus mea non feret amplius virgam ad dominandum Ezech. 19, 14. sed ramus præfectus fuerit Esa. 10, 39. domo mea non stante in mandatis DEI, tum nihilominus dabit mihi DEUS domum & semen, per quod procuretur Salus mea, & omnis complacentia, vel gratia. Quæ postrema paulo ali- ter, per modum nempe voti, exposuit Osiandrina paraphrasis, non pro designatione temporis ha- buit: Et totum desiderium, quod non crescat; id est, nihil æque desidero, quam ut liceret videre exorientem illum Solem justitiæ, Christum, in carne, & crescere Regnum illud pacis, quod reficiet conscientias, amæ- nissimum illum paradisum cælestem. Ach warum wächset es doch nicht schon? Es verlanget mich, daß es nicht gleich jetzo wachsen will. Cuncta enim salus mea consistit in regno Spirituali Christi, Filii mei olim nascituri: πᾶσα σωτηρία μ8, καὶ πᾶν θέλημα ἐν Κυρίῳ, ut LXX. Interpretes immediate antecedentia reddidere. Nimirum in corde ha- bebat vir secundum cor DEI, JEsum suum, quem maximopere anhelabat, subinde ingeminans su- spiria, summo adversus eum amore ac desiderio flagrantia: Defecit in salutare tuum (JESUM tuum) anima mea: Expecto salutem tuam (JESUM tuum) Domine. Concupivi salutare tuum (JESUM tuum) Domine. Quis dabit ex Sion salutare (JESUM) Is- rael? Psal. 119, 8. 166. 174. Pf. 14, 7. Pf. 53, 7. Nec a- liud pactum ÆTERNUM acceperat ipse, quam de JESULO nostro, quod in ipso uno benedictio, & salus omnibus, qui sub maledictione & condemnatio- ne conclusi sunt, obtingat. Quæ summa est, & Substantia, ut ita dicam, æterni fœderis, non cum Davide primum, sed cum Ahrahamo Patre cre- dentium, imo cum Adamo & Eva omnium vi- ventium parentibus, initi atque sanciti: SEMEN MULIERIS conteret caput serpentis: in SEMINE tuo, quod est CHRISTUS, Apostolo Interprete, benedicentur omnes gentes. Ideo cum peculiari- ter ea Salus in semine Davidis promissa est, non ad substantiam fœderis id pertinet, quod id SEMEN DAVIDIS, sed ad circumstantiam, & insignem prærogativam, qua ornavit DEUS stemma Davi- dicum, & thronum ejus Regium. Hoc ergo fœ- dus æternum prorsus ἀμεταμέλητον, hac circum- stantia vestitum, id solum erat, quod 2. Samuel. 7, 12. 13. 14. 15. 16. DEUS sanciverat, de Semine e cor- pore ejus, post fata ipsius, excitando, cujus regnum æternum erit, & thronus in æternum consistet; ob quam domus suæ magnificentiam inæstimabilem exclamat Rex: Quis ego sum Domine DEUS, & quæ domus mea, quia adduxisti me hucusque? Sed & hoc parum visum est, in conspectu tuo, Domine, nisi etiam loquereris de domo Servi tui in longin- quum. Ista est forma ILLIUS hominis, (non enim negligendum hic He Hajediah) qui est DEUS Jehovah, quem scil. VIRUM JEHOVAM jam Eva παμμήτης expectavit, quem e lumbis meis proditurum, summo cum tripudio nunc ac- cipio. Quæ promissio simplex est, & absoluta: tum Davidi per Nathanem facta, quum nullam se requirere domum protestabatur Dominus, & κατ' ἀμοιβὴν polliceretur, seipsum & Davidi do- mum ædificaturum, & e lumbis ejus Semen produ- cturum, æternum Filium suum, a quo Solo nomini divino domus exstruetur, non e lapidibus ma- terialibus, sed e vivis lapidibus, non fragilis, & caduca, sed æterna, & sine fine duraturá. Unde hæc categorica promissio (Sancta fidelia Davidis, τὰ ὅσια τὰ πισὰ vocat Spiritus Sanct. Act. 13, 34. ex Es. 55, 3. ubi fideles Davidis, id est, Davidi pro- mit- missæ, misericordiæ dicuntur) nullatenus confunden- da, cum hypothetica & conditionata pollicitatione, de Throno regio posteritati Davidicæ conservando, si sc. mandata & statuta Domini servarit, quæ non per Nathanem, sed immediate Davidi a Domino facta, quum templi ædificationem non resspueret Domi- nus, sed Salomoni reservaret 2. Par. 23, 8. 13. 1. Reg. 8, 17. 25. Et sub eadem conditione Salomoni repe- tita 1. Reg. 9, 4. 5. 6. Quapropter hæc accurate in suo Maskil, vel Eruditivo distinxit Ethan, cum grati- am Davidi promissam carmine insigni celebraret, Psalm. 89. Prior Domini promissio jurejurando confirmata, omnis conditionis expers fuit, in æter- num, ἀμεταμελήτως servanda, quæ v. 4. & seqq. de- prædicatur: Disposui testamentum electis meis: jura- vi David servo meo. Summa est in professione fide- lium vers. 18. & promissione divina vers. 19. cui innixi fideles gloriantur & exultant in Domino : ut habe- tur versu 16. & 17. Domine, in lumine vultus tui am- bulabunt, & in nomine tuo exultabunt tota die, & in justitia tuo exaltabuntur. Quoniam gloria virtutis eorum Tu es, & in beneplacito tuo exaltabitur cornu nostrum (hæc est εὐδοκία in erecto & exaltato cornu Salutis nostræ Luc. 1, 67. ) quia a Domino scutum nostrum & a Sancto Israel Rex noster: id est, Messias a DEO, qui sanctificat Israelem, datur nobis scu- tum, Redemtio, justitia, sanctificatio &c. Quem sensum ex Ebræi textus translatione a Felice facta feliciter reddidit B. Bugenhagius noster. Basis hujus fiduciæ, gloriationis, exultationis & exalta- tionis fidelium promissio divina Sanctis, Nathani & Davidi, facta; Tunc locutus es in visione Sanctis tuis, & dixisti: Posui adjutorium in potente, & exaltavi E- lectum de populo. Inveni David servum meum, Oleo sancto unxi eum. Quæ posteriora, etsi de Christo nonnulli cum S. Augustino explicent, de Davide intelligenda esse, non sinit nos dubitare Paulina in- terpretatio Act. 13, 22. Sed Gibbor ille, in quo fide- libus adjutorium, vel auxilium positum, ut glorien- tur, & exultent, alius nullus est, quam filius nobis da- tus, puer nobis natus, Christus, cui nomen El gibbor Esa. 9, 6. qui etiam electus ille de populo, vel ex semi- ne Israelitico, & tribu Judæ, & e Patribus secundum carnem, quem exaltavit, Salutis nostræ causa, Pa- ter: ad quem, misso Davide, ob promissionem, quæ ipsi facta, hic celebratur, & thronum ejus, quem possessurus erat hic HEROS ELECTUS, introdu- cto, revertitur Ethan, ejusque exaltationem, fœdus, Semen spirituale, thronum, & regnum graphice depingit. De æterno itaque illo fœdere ita por- ro cantat: vers. 34. Non profanabo testamentum meum, & quæ procedunt de labiis meis, non faciam irrita: Semel juravi in Sancto meo (nomine, ut Chald. vel per sanctitatem meam) si David men- tiar, semen ejus in ÆTERNUM manebit, & thro- nus ejus, sicut Sol in conspectu meo, & sicut luna perfecta in æternum, & testis in cælo fidelis. Atque hæc de priori promissione. Posterior promissio, conditionem annexam habuit, eaque cessante de- siit, de quo vaticinando graviter conqueritur Ethan a vers. 38. usque ad vers. 46. Tu vero repulisti, & despexisti, distulisti Christum tuum, evertisti testamentum servi tui &c. Aliud ergo est re- gnum DEI æternum, in quo est gratia, & Rex de Semine Davidis, expectatus omnibus Sanctis; aliud regnum externum, mundanum, umbra- tile, filiis Davidis datum, quod in Spiritu o- stendit cecidisse, etiam ante revelationem Mes- siæ; unde precatur, piisque istius temporis preces sufficit, quibus accelerationem missionis Christi veri Regis, cum vera gratia v. 47. seq.

expetant: usque quo Domine avertis te? ubi sunt mi- sericordiae tuae antiquae Domine, sicut jurasti David in veritate tua? Memor esto Domine opprobrii servorum tuorum, quod portavi hactenus (gemens Ecclesia) in sinu meo, quod exprobrarunt inimici tui, quod nimi- rum exprobarunt vestigia Christi tui (exibilantes, & subsannantes progressum regni tui, & adventum e- jusdem dilatum, tarditatem vestigiorum Messiae, ut Chald. habet) quem vero, quia suo tempore certo sequuturum credebat Esrahita, in δοξολογίαν hanc erumpit: BENEDICTUS SIT DOMINUS IN ÆTERNUM, AMEN, AMEN. Atque in hunc sensum accepit etiam foedus cum Patre sancitum, filius Salomo, Psal. 132. (hic enim illum autorem agnoscit, ut e tota Psalmi compage apparet) cum de principe promissione, juravit, inquit v. 9. Domi- nus David veritatem, & non frustrabitur eum: de fru- ctu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam: de altera ve- ro sub conditione v. 12. Si custodierint filii tui testa- mentum meum, & testimonia mea haec, quae docebo eos, & filii eorum usque in seculum sedebunt super se- dem tuam: ac ne de priori, ac praecipua promissio- ne dubium supersit, adjecit v. 17. Sacerdotes ejus (qui sunt fideles omnes, Regale Domini Sacerdoti- um) induam Salutari, & Sancti ejus exultatione ex- ultabunt: Illic producam CORNU David, paravi LUCERNAM Christo meo (Davidi) quod cornu a- liud non est, quam de quo canit Zacharias Luc. 1, 69. nec lucerna alia, quam lux illa magna, de qua te- status est Zachariae filius Joh. 1, 9. Sed haec perfe- qui non licet impraesentiarum. Et lucem illis o- mnibus jam attulit Gabriel Archangelus Luc. 1, 32. Et dabit illi Dominus DEUS sedem Patris ejus Da- vid & regnabit in domo Jacob in aeternum, & regni e- jus non erit finis. In hac ergo lucerna, in hoc cornu salutis, quod nobis GERMINARE FECIT DO- MINUS, laetemur, has Misericordias aeternas can- temus, atque ita festa haec solemnia celebremus, ut regale Sacerdotium decet; Abnegantes impietatem, & secularia desideria, sobrie nobis, juste proximo, & pie DEO vivamus in hoc seculo. Ideo enim illuxit no- bis gratia DEI Salvatoris nostri, nos erudiens: ideo etiam nunc facula in coelo ardens ardentem iram Domini Christiano portendit orbi, quam seria san- ctaque avertamus poenitentia. Faxit id in nobis Dominus JESUS, cujus ministris non intermittetis, depositis ad aram muneribus, testari gratitudinem. Inimicos induit Dominus confusione, h. e. impios & ingratos, super justos vero florebit Diadema ejus. P.P. Vigilia Genethliaca. Anno cIo Iɔc LXIV.

## 23:8
Verse 8.

OF THE MIGHTY MEN OF DAVID) Of the heroes of his time, whose virtue seemed to exceed human measure.

There is also to be observed here in the numbers a contradiction. For one of the mighty men of David is said to have killed 300 men in 1 Chron. 11:11, but here 800. Some think that Jesbeam killed 300 at one time and 800 at another, and that this number, as the greater, was reported here; but that the other, also a sufficiently notable specimen of heroic fortitude, might not be passed over in silence, it was recorded in the books of Chronicles. Others say that he killed 300 with his own hand, and the rest killed by his companions are likewise ascribed to him here as their leader.

Verse of the same.

AS THE MOST TENDER WOOD-WORM) It is a proper name: Hadinus the Eznite. So the Greeks and Hebrews.

Osiander makes his proper name Joseb, and from the parallel place 1 Paral. 12:11, Jesabeam: thus amending the Vulgate, and explaining this verse: sitting in the chair most wise (thus the Vulgate has it: In Hebrew Josfeb Basebeth Thachmoni, that is, that Joseb, who is also called Jesabeam, dwelt in Sebeth: but he was a native of Tachman:) and he was the Prince or chief among the three Heroes. He himself is as the most tender wood-worm, which in Hebrew is Adino Haczeno (but I feel that for עדינו one should read עורו, so that the meaning may be, he lifted his wood, his staff, or his lever. Luther: He lifted up his spear). Concerning that former denomination Joseb, in Schebeth of Thachmoni, where Capellus attaches a corruption to the Hebrew text, let Buxtorf be seen in his Vindications p. 399. He brings forward some things here from Abarbanel and Sanctius; but the Osiandrian explanation already praised is without doubt more convenient; as being a native of Thachman, or the son of Thachman, with the LXX Interpreters, not only Luther, but also Cornel. a Lap. makes him Jesabus, who furthermore observes that Beda, Angelomus, Abulensis, Hugo, the Gloss, Cajetan, Arias, Serarius, Sanctius, and Salianus also establish that he was the first among the heroes of David, and he strives to reconcile this with the Vulgate, because Joseb Baschebeth is here both a proper and an appellative name, which however is inconsistent. For if it is a proper name, how will it be at the same time an appellative name in the same place? But we cannot agree with the latter Osiander, who amends the Hebrew text itself: For neither can that meaning, he lifted his wood, be carved out of that emendation of words, nor is there any necessity for it. Pagninus and Arias-Montanus take those names as proper, Hadinus the Eznite: Junius and Tremellius render it, to this one it was pleasing to the spearman, or to the wood-man to invade at one time those reaching out to be pierced) but although עדינו can be rendered pleasure to him, yet from העצנו a spearman or wood-man will be deduced with difficulty; therefore Pagninus's opinion is to be preferred, which also the LXX. and Vatablus held, namely that that Jesab also had the name Adeno, and that he was an Eznite by country; nor is it disapproved by Cornelius, although he here again (but ineptly) attempted to reconcile his Vulgate's most tender wood-worm, making a wood-worm out of the hero Adino the Eznite, commended by that name for his humility, just as the Holy Spirit likewise commended the son of Thachmoni for his Wisdom, that he was like a wood-worm, which although it is tender and vile, yet by gnawing little by little it wears down and eats away hard wood; Which is to change squares into rounds, and not only to make appellatives out of proper names now, but furthermore to play with appellatives at will. But that that Hero is said to be over eight hundred, that is to be explained from the nature of the language, as observed by B. Glassius in Philol. Sacr. book 3, tract. 6. chap. 1. 12. 'over eight hundred' he was, that is, he conquered them by warring against them; where the verb that is added, חלל, rendered by the Vulgate as 'killed', is more correctly translated by Osiander as 'wounded', inasmuch as it is very often used regarding a wounded body: and thus a reconciliation with the parallel passage 1 Chron. 12:11 is at hand, namely that in one instance, that is, in a single battle, he wounded 800, of whom 300 died; so that there is no need for those things which Buxtorfius, loc. cit. page 405, has prolixly brought forward for the reconciliation of those passages.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

FORTIUM DAVID) Heroum ejus temporis, quorum virtus modum humanum visa excedere.

Est & observanda hic in numeris ἐναντιοφανεία. Nam unus e fortibus Davidis dicitur interfecisse 300. homines 1. Chron. 11, 11. hic vero 800. Nonnulli putant, Jesbeam semel 300. alias 800. occidisse: at- que hunc numerum ceu majorem hic relatum esse; Ne vero alterum etiam satis insigne specimen heroi- cae fortitudinis taceretur, in libros Paralipomenon id redactum esse. Alii dicunt ipsum 300. sua manu nerfecisse, reliquos a sociis ipsius occisos ei ceu duci itidem hic adscribi.

Vers. eod.
