QVASI TENERRIMVS LIGNI VERMICVLVS) Est nomen proprium: Hadinus Hesnita. Ita Graeci & Hebraei.

Osiander nomen proprium ejus facit Joseb, & e loco parallelo 1. Paral. 12, 11. Jesabeam: sic e- mendans Vulgatam, & exponens hunc versum: se- dens in cathedra sapientissimus (sic Vulgata habet: E- braice Josfeb Basebeth Thachmoni, id est, Joseb ille, qui etiam Jesabeam dicitur, habitavit in Sebeth: fuit autem oriundus de Tachman: ) eratque Princeps seu praecipuus inter Heroas tres. Ipse est quasi tenerri- mus ligni vermiculus, qui Ebr. Adino Haczeno (sentio antem pro עדינו legendum עורו, ut sit sententia, levavit lignum suum, sein Stangen, oder Hebtre mel, seu vectem suum. Luther. Er hub seinen Spieß auf. De priori illa denominatione Joseb, in Schebeth de Thachmoni, ubi corruptelam textui Ebræo affin- git Capellus, videatur in vindiciis Buxtorfius p. 399. Adducit ex Abarbenele, & Sanctio huc nonnulla; sed convenientior, sine dubio, est Osiandrina jam laudata explicatio; uti a Thachman parente oriun- dum, vel filium Thachmani, cum LXX. Interpp. non Lutherus tantum, sed etiam Cornel. a Lap. Jesabum facit, qui praeterea eundem primum inter Heroas Davidis fuisse, Bedam quoque Angelom. Abulensem, Hugonem, Glossam, Cajetan. Ariam. Serarium, San- clium, Salianum statuere, observat, idque cum vul- gata conciliare nititur, quod Joseb Baschebeth tam proprium, quam appellativum hic sit, quod vero ἀσύσατον est. Nam si proprium est, quomodo erit simul appellativum nomen in eodem loco? In posteriori autem Osiandro, ipsum Ebræum textum e- mendanti, astipulari non possumus: Nam neque ex illa vocum emendatione exsculpi potest sensus iste, levavit lignum suum, neque ulla ejus est necessitas. Pagninus, & Arias-Montanus habent illa nomina pro propriis Hadino Heznita: Junius & Tremellius reddunt, huic gratum fuit hastato, vel lignato una vi- ce invadere attingentes confodiendos) sed quam- vis עדינו reddi possit voluptas ei, tamen ex העצנו aegre deducetur hastatus, vel lignatus; ideo praefe- renda Pagnini sententia, quae etiam LXX. & Vatabli fuit, quod nempe Jesab ille etiam nomen Adeno ha- buerit, & quod Patriam Hesnita fuerit; nec impro- batur Cornelio, tametsi ille hic iterum (sed inepte) conciliare tentarir vulgatae suae tenerrimum ligni ver- miculum, ex Heroe ille Adino Hesnita teredinem fa- ciens, ab humilitate, illo nomine commendatum, uti filium Tachmoni a Sapientia itidem commendarit Spiritus Sanct. quod fuerit uti teredo, qui licet tener & vilis sit, tamen rodendo sensim durum terit, & exedit li- gnum; Quod est mutare quadrata rotundis, nec ex propriis tantum appellativa jam facere, sed insuper cum appellativis etiam pro lubitu ludere. Quod vero Heros ille dicatur על super octingentos, id ex- plicandum e linguae indole, observata B. Glasfio Philol. Sacr. l. 3. tract. 6. cap. 1. 12. super octingentos is erat, h. e. eos debellando vicit; ubi verbum, quod additur, חלל a vulgato redditum interfecit, rectius ab Osiandro vertitur vulneravit, utpote quod saepif- sime de corpore vulnerato adhibetur: & ita in prom- tu est conciliatio cum loco parallelo 1. Paral. 12, 11. quod nempe una vice, id est, in unica pugna 800. vulnerarit, e quibus 300. mortui sunt; ut opus non sit illis, quae prolixe Buxtorfius l. c. pag. 405. pro loco- rum istorum conciliatione adduxit.

## 23:11
Verse 11.

A FIELD FULL OF LENTILS) This is a different field from that one full of barley, 1 Chron. 11:13. For the names of the warriors also differ.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

AGER LENTE PLENVS) Alius hic ager ab illo ple no hordei. 1. Paral. 11, 13. Nam & bellatorum nomina differunt.

## 23:16
Verse 16.

AND HE WOULD NOT DRINK) Thus Alexander, in a similar necessity, returned the cup full, just as it had been offered: 'I cannot bear to drink alone,' he said, 'nor can I divide so little among all.' Curtius narrates in book 7. Lucan [writes] of Cato in thirsty Africa. The last drinker of water, when at length the fountain was found, the needy youth is forced to drink the liquids, he stands while the camp-follower drinks. He did not want to drink, not because he could not offer it to others, but because the water had cost the danger of life and blood, and to indicate that it was not so much a bodily as a spiritual thirst for the Messiah, who was one day to come forth in Bethlehem, that had excited this desire in him.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

ET ILLE NOLVIT BIBERE) Sic Alexander in pari necessitate poculo pleno, sicut oblatum erat reddito: Nec solus, inquit, bibere sustineo: nec tam exiguum omni- bus dividere possum. Narrat Curtius libro 7. Lucanus de Catone in siticulosa Africa. Vltimus haustor aquæ, cum tandem fonte reperto Indiga cogatur latices potare juventus, Stat dum lixa bibat. Noluit bibere non quod aliis præbere non posset, sed quod periculo vitæ & sanguinis aqua constiterit, & ut indicaret, non tam corporalem, quam spiritualem sitim Messiæ in Bethlehem ali- quando prodituri sibi hoc desiderium excitasse.

## 23:24
Verse 24. ASAHEL THE BROTHER OF JOAB AMONG THE THIRTY.

Among the thirty chief heads, or the principal Heroes of David v. 13.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ASAHEL FRATER JOAB INTER TRI- GINTA.

Inter triginta præcipua capita, sive Heroes principes Davidis v. 13.

## 23:39
Verse 39. ALL THIRTY SEVEN)

Those who are missing here from Asahel to this number, they were the sons of Jasen mentioned above in verse 33. To us, from a collation of 1 Chron. 11, the calculation of these 37 Heroes seems to be established thus: (1) Jaseb (in the book of Chronicles Jasabeam) son of Hachmoni v. 8. (2) Eleasar son of Dodo son of Asahel v. 9. (3) Samma son of Age the Hararite v. 11. These three stood out above all others among David's Heroes. Next to them were three others, who follow: namely (4) Abisai brother of Joab v. 18. and (5) Benaja son of Jojada v. 20. and (6) Asahel brother of Joab, who is therefore said to have been among the 30 Heroes, i.e., more glorious than the others. Conf. v. 23 and 24. Now follow other likewise distinguished Heroes, but not to be compared with the next trio, let alone with the first, to whose glory the second did not reach. There is therefore (7) Elhanan son of Dodo. (8) Samma the Harodite; he is called 1 Chron. 11, 27, Sammoth the Harodite, (he is different from Samma son of Age the Hararite v. 11. and from Samma the Harorite v. 33.) (9) Elika the Harodite (he is not commemorated in the book of Chronicles: for there it was not the intention to recount those 30 Heroes precisely, whence also some others seem to be omitted from the thirty Heroic men. (10) Helez the Paltite (in the book of Chron. he is called Helez the Pelonite) (11) Ira son of Iker of Tekoa. (12) Abieser of Anathoth. (13) Mebunai of Hushath (in the book of Chron. he is called Sibechai of Hushath.) (14) Zalmon the Ahohite (in Chron. Ilai the Ahohite) (15) Maharai the Netophathite. (16) Heleb (in Chron. Heled) son of Baana, who is himself also a Netophathite. (17) Iithai son of Ribai of (the town of) Gaba of the sons of Benjamin. (18) Benaja the Pharathonite. (19) Hidai (in the book of Chronicles, Hurai) of the torrent of Gaash. (20) Abialbon (in Chron. Abiel) the Arbathite. (21) Azmaveth of Barhum. (22) Eliaba of Saalbon. (23) Sons of Jasen (in the book of Chron. sons of Haschem the Gizonite: they are not expressed by proper names in the book of Chronicles) such as Jonathan (he seems here to be different from the Jonathan of 1 Chron. 11, 33; for here he is called the son of Sage the Hararite, but that one was one of the sons of Jasen) Whose brother, not named here, seems (24) to be in order, as Luc. Osiander observed not rashly in this place. Therefore (25) is Samma the Hararite. (26) Ahiam son of Sarar (in the book of Chron. son of Sachar) of Harar. (27) Elipheleth son of Aharbai, son of Maachathi (in the book of Chronicles it is read in this order after Ahiam, Eliphal son of Ur. Whether he is the same person with two names or another, it is not clear) (28) Eliam son of Ahitophel the Gilonite (he is not commemorated in the book of Chronicles, the son of a most cunning, but most wicked father, who became his own executioner: for even from wicked parents sometimes generous sons are born.) (29) Haserai of Carmel. (30) Paerai of Arbi. (And these 30 seem to be those principal Heroes of whom mention was made in v. 23, 24; who also for the most part are all recounted in the book of Chronicles, although some had different names. Those who follow, therefore, the remaining seven, do not indeed seem to have been of equal fame with those 30 Heroes, yet they must have been outstanding and distinguished Heroes, because the Holy Scriptures deign not only to name them but also to number them, whence we see that GOD has illustrious men in his count, and wishes their number, Catalog, and memory to be preserved. Wherefore (31) is Igaal son of Nathan of Zoba. (32) Bani the Gadite. (33) Selea the Ammonite. (34) Naharai the Berothite, armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah. (35) Ira the Jethrite. (36) Garab the Jethrite. (37) Uria the Hittite.

Some, in order to complete this number of 37 Heroes, because only the names of 36 Heroes are found, add Joab. But because he is not numbered among the others here, even though his armor-bearer is named, but is studiously, as it appears, passed over (perhaps because of his unworthy deeds 1 Kings 2, 32) and the sons of Jasen are commemorated among the Heroes, with only one expressed by name, it is not obscure that the other, whose name is not added, is to be reckoned to this catalog to complete the number.

Latin:

Vers. 39. OMNES TRIGINTA SEPTEM)

Qui hic ab Asaële ad hunc numerum desunt, ii fuere filii Jassen supra memorati commate 33. Nobis e collatione 1. Par. 11. calculus horum 37. Heroum ita videtur instituendus. (1) Jaseb (in libro Chronicorum Jasabeam) filius Hachmoni v. 8. (2) Eleasar filius Dodo filii Asahel v. 9. (3) Sam- ma filius Age de Harar v. 11. Hi tres eminebant præ aliis omnibus inter Heroas Davidis. Proximi erant illis alii tres, qui sequuntur: nempe (4) Abisai frater Joabi v. 18. & (5) Benaja filius Jojada v. 20. & (6) Asasael frater Joab, qui ideo dicitur fuisse inter 30. Heroas, sc. gloriosior aliis. Conf. v. 23. & 24. Sequuntur nunc alii insignes itidem Heroes, sed cum proxima triga non comparandi, nedum cum prima, ad cujus gloriam non pertingebat altera. Est er- go (7) Elhanan filius Dodo. (8) Samma Charadita; vocatur 1. Chron. 11, 27. Sammoth Harodita, (diver- sus est a Samma filio Age de Harare v. 11. & a Samma Harorita v. 33.) (9) Elika Haradita (hic non comme- moratur in libro Chronicorum: nam ibi non erat propositum illos 30. Heroas præcise recensere, unde etiam alii nonnulli prætermissi videntur e triginta viris Heroibus. (10) Helez Paltites (in libro Chron. vocatur Helez Pel onites) (11) Ira filius Iker de The- kua. (12) Abieser de Anathot. (13) Mebunai de Husath (in libr. Chron. dicitur Sibechai de Husath.) (14) Zalmon Ahohites (in Chron. Ilai Ahohites) (15) Maharai Netophathites. (16) Heleb (in Chron. Heled filius Baana, qui & ipse Netophathites. (17) Iithai fi- lius Ribai de (oppido) Gaba filiorum Benjamin. (18) Benaja Pharatonites. (19) Hidai (in libr. Chronic. Hurai) de torrente Gaas. (20) Abialbon (in Chron. Abiel) Arbathites. (21) Azmaveth de Barumi. (22) Eliaba de Saalboni. (23) Filii Jasen (in lib. Chron. filii Haschem Chizonitis: non sunt nominibus ex- pressi propriis in libro Chronicorum) utpote Jo- nathan (diversus hic videtur a Jonathane 1. Chron. 11, 33. hic enim filius Sage Haoaritæ dicitur, ille ve- ro unus e filiis Jasen fuit) Cujus frater hic non no- minatus, videtur (24) esse in ordine, uti observavit non temere Luc. Osiander in h. l. Proinde (25) est Samma Hararites. (26) Abiam filius Sarar (in libr. Chron. filius Sachar) de Harare. (27) Eliphe- leth filius Aharbai, filii Maechati (in libro Chroni- corum legitur isto ordine post Ahiam Eliphal filius Ulz. Num idem binominis an vero alius is sit, non liquet) (28) Eliam filius Ahitophel Gilonitæ (hic non commemoratur in libro Chronicorum, Patris astutissimi, sed scelestissimi, qui αὐτόχειρ factus est, filius: nam & e sceleratis parentibus prodeunt quandoque generosi filii.) (29) Haserai de Car- melo. (30) Paerai de Arbi. (Atque hi 30. vi- dentur esse illi præcipui Heroes quorum v. 23. 24. mentio facta; qui etiam plerique omnes in libro Chronicorum recensiti sunt, quantumvis nonnul- li diversa habuerint nomina. Qui ergo sequuntur septem reliqui, non fuisse quidem videntur parilis celebritatis cum 30. istis Heroibus, præstantes tamen & insignes oportet fuisse Heroes, quod non nomi- nare tantum, sed etiam numerare eosdem dignatur S. S. unde videmus, quod DEUS inclutos viros in numerato habeat, eorumque numerum, Catalogum & memoriam conservari velit. Quapropter (31) est Igaal filius Nathan de Zoba. (32) Bani Gadita. (33) Selea Ammonita. (34) Naharai Berotites, ar- miger Joab filii Zeruja. (35) Ira Jethrites. (36) Ga- rab Jethrites. (37) Uria Hethites.

Nonnulli ut numerum hunc 37. Heroum com- pleant, quia nomina tantum 36. Heroum reperiun- tur, Joabum addunt. Sed quia ille cæteris hic an- numeratus non est, etsi armiger ejus nominatus sit, sed studiose, ut apparet, præteritus, (forte ob indi- gna facinora 1, Reg. 2, 32.) & filii Jasen commemo- rantur inter Heroes, uno solum κατ' ὄνομα expres- so, haud obscurum est, alterum, cujus nomen addi- tum non est, huic catalogo ad complendum nume- rum accensendum esse.

## 24:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIV. The punishment of the numbering of the people, the plague, and its removal: and the sacrifice on the threshing floor of Araunah, which David prepared in honor of GOD.

Verse 1.

AND HE MOVED DAVID AMONG THEM] In those days, namely. He moved David, the active for the passive, as often, that is, he was moved, namely by the devil, as we have expressly 1 Chron. 21, 1. But carelessness and negligence regarding the meditation of the law and prayers make room for the devil.

GO, NUMBER ISRAEL AND JUDAH) Namely, without paying the census, which was owed to God by law, Exod. 30, 12, as often as the people were mustered. Moreover, it was no light sin, in such great wealth of things, to wish to defraud God of his right. Thus Josephus and others of the Hebrews interpret this history.

Latin:

## 24:13
Ver. 13.

OR SHALL SEVEN YEARS OF FAMINE COME TO THEE IN THY LAND) Josephus also has seven years. But the LXX here has three, as also in the Hebrew 1 Chron. 21, 12. Numbers seem to have been written formerly by marks, as also among other nations, and hence an easy change. Moreover, that passage of Hesiod agrees well with this place: Πολλάκι καὶ ξύμπασα πόλις κακου̃ ἀνδρὸς ἐπαυρει̃, Ὁςτις ἀλιτραίνει καὶ ἀτάσθαλα μηχανάαται˙ Τοι̃σιν δ' οὐρανόθεν μέγ' ἐπήγαγε πη̃μα Κρονίων Λιμὸν ὁμου̃ καὶ λοιμόν˙ ἀποφθινύθουσι δὲ λαόι. Οὐδὲ γυναι̃κες τίκτουσιν˙ μινύθουσι δὲ οι̃κοι. Ζηνὸς φραδμοσύνηισιν Ὀλυμπίυ˙ ἄλλοτε δ' αυ̃τε Ἠ τ̃ γε στρατὸν εὐρὺν ἀπώλεσεν, ἢ ὁγε τει̃χος, Ἠ νέας ἐν πόντῳ Κρονίδης ἀποτίνυται αὐτω̃ν.

There is no need for a change of number to be admitted. The Hebrew, Chaldean, and Latin codices agree, as does Josephus. The Greeks therefore are to be corrected from them, not vice versa. The reconciliation, however, is not difficult. Some, as Sanctius observes, say that the famine was to have lasted seven years, but that for three it would be so severe that the famine of the other four could be considered abundance. But Sanctius and Cornelius a Lapide, as also Tirinus, prefer that at the beginning a seven-year famine was indeed decreed, but afterwards, when David shuddered at that long-lasting famine and sought mitigation, it was shortened to three years. But a more expeditious reconciliation from the previous history is that three years of famine on account of the Gibeonites had already passed in c. 21, 1, and that these things were done in the fourth year running, whence God threatened yet another three-year period of more vehement famine, which is therefore mentioned here alone; if these years are joined, a seven-year famine will result. This explanation is approved by Junius, Piscator, and the Belgian Interpreters. and from our own, the Weimar Paraphrasts. That conjecture of Grotius concerning numbers written by symbols is proven by no documents regarding Hebrew books, and indeed Biblical Codices: which it is established are of great ἀκρίβεια.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

AUT SEPTEM ANNIS VENIAT TIBI FAMES IN TERRA TVA) Septem annos habet & Josephus. At tres hîc LXX. quomodo & in Hebræo 1.Paral.21,12. Videntur nu- meri olim per notas scripti, ut & apud gentes alias, & inde fa- cilis mutatio. Bene autem cum hoc loco convenit illud He- siodi: Πολλάκι καὶ ξύμπασα πόλις κακου̃ ἀνδρὸς ἐπαυρει̃, Ὁςτις ἀλιτραίνει καὶ ἀτάσθαλα μηχανάαται˙ Τοι̃σιν δ' οὐρανόθεν μέγ' ἐπήγαγε πη̃μα Κρονίων Λιμὸν ὁμου̃ καὶ λοιμόν˙ ἀποφθινύθουσι δὲ λαόι. Οὐδὲ γυναι̃κες τίκτουσιν˙ μινύθουσι δὲ οι̃κοι. Ζηνὸς φραδμοσύνηισιν Ὀλυμπίυ˙ ἄλλοτε δ' αυ̃τε Ἠ τ̃ γε στρατὸν εὐρὺν ἀπώλεσεν, ἢ ὁγε τει̃χος, Ἠ νέας ἐν πόντῳ Κρονίδης ἀποτίνυται αὐτω̃ν.

NOn opus est, ut admittatur numeri mutatio. Consonant codices Ebræi, Chaldæi, & La- tini, ut & Josephus. Græci ergo ex illis emendandi, non vice versa. Conciliatio autem non est diffici- lis. Quidam, observante Sanctio, ajunt, septem an- nos debuisse famem durare, sed tribus eam tam angu- stam futuram, ut aliorum quatuor fames censeri possit abundantia. Sanctius vero & Cornelius a Lapide, ut & Tirinus malunt principio quidem famem septenna- lem indictam, sed postea cum David ad diuturnam illam famem exhorreret, ac mitigationem peteret, ad tres annos fuisse coarctatam. Sed expeditior est ex Historia superiori conciliatio, quod tres anni fa- mis propter Gibeonitas elapsi jam sint c. 21, 1. quarto autem decurrente hæc acta fuerint, unde Deus adhuc aliud triennium famis vehementioris, quod ideo hic solum commemoratur, minatus est, qui anni si jun- gantur, septennalis inde fames proditura est. Quam explicationem probant Junius, Piscator, Belgæ In- terpp. & e nostris Vinarienses Paraphrastæ. Conje- ctura illa Grotii de numeris per notas scriptis nullis documentis probata est, de libris Ebræis, & quidem Codicibus Biblicis: quos magna ἀκρίβεια esse con- stat.

## 24:21
Verse 21.

THAT I MAY BUY THE THRESHING FLOOR FROM THEE) For it is a sin to consecrate another's soil. On this threshing floor the Temple was later built.

TO THE FIRST BOOK AMONG

This book begins with the affairs of Solomon, with only a narrative added at the beginning showing how Solomon arrived at the kingdom. I compare Solomon to Numa. Both were led to the kingdom by a certain fate: both were wise: both built a temple: both introduced external ceremonies. Numa left private sons behind him, Solomon a son as king from a sixth part. In the divided kingdom you will see all the kings of Israel were evil, some kings of Judah were evil, many were mediocre enough, and good ones were as few as could easily be inscribed on rings.

As these books are called the first and second of Kings by the Hebrews, so they are called the books of Kingdoms by the Greeks: and the First describes the deeds of Solomon, and of the four following kings of Judah, Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, whose years are numbered as 126, namely 40 of Solomon, 17 of Rehoboam, 3 of Abijah, 41 of Asa, and 25 of Jehoshaphat. It is divided into two parts, before the division of the king- EMIT ERGO DAVID AREAM) A colon should be placed here: but he bought it for six hundred shekels of gold. 1 Chron. 21:25. What follows is the price, which is much less, namely for the victims.

The reconciliation of Abarbenel and other Rabbis is almost the same. For he says thus: According to the literal sense, it is mentioned here that he bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver, and built an altar there to the Lord. But because the house of the Lord had to be built there, the field of Araunah also had to be bought for him, which was adjacent to that threshing floor where the house was to be built, and for that field he gave 600 shekels of gold. But that is not commemorated here; but in the book of Chronicles, where it is said: so David weighed out to Ornan for that place six hundred shekels of gold by weight. He means to say that David gave that much for the whole field, which is that place of which mention is made there. And Rabbi Abba Jose ben Dosithei also inclined to this view, in the Midrash Samuel and in the tractate Zevahim, when he says, oxen and wood and the place of the altar for fifty shekels of silver. Peter Martyr has it thus, he gives the price of 50 shekels: in Chronicles. 600 is held, but there is no conflict: for 50 shekels were given for the oxen and farm implements, but 600 for the threshing floor and the houses. Or it may be that he gave 50 shekels, and afterwards 600 out of royal munificence. It may also be that 50 were given for the threshing floor, but because the temple was to be built there, and gardens, houses, and buildings were to be occupied, such a sum was therefore given. The Hebrews fable that it had to be public, and to be bought by all the tribes, so that each would give 50 shekels, and thus there would be 600 shekels: for there were 12 tribes. But whether the whole place is for 600, or whether with Grotius it is said that 600 shekels were given for the threshing floor, or with the Hebrews for the whole field, the reconciliation is ready. This latter opinion, however, is more akin to the truth. Because the threshing floor does not seem to have been of such capacity that it sufficed for the building of the temple: Therefore Jerome, Lyranus, Hugo, Cajetan, Serarius, Salianus, Robert Baillie, and the Weimar Paraphrase approved this reconciliation. Let us pray with David (Ps. 132:8, 9): Arise, O LORD, into thy rest; thou, and the ark of thy strength. Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy. Amen. Amen.

VT EMAM A TE AREAM) Nam alienum solum consecrare nefas. In hac area ædificatum postea Templum.

AD LIBRUM PR APUD H QUI APUD TERTIUS

HIc Liber a Salomonis rebus incipit, addita tantum pro initio narratione ostendente quomodo Solomon ad re- gnum pervenerit. Salomoni ego Numam comparo. Vterque fato quodam perductus ad regnum: Sapiens uterque: tem- plum struxit uterque: ceremonias externas uterque introdu- xit. Numa filios privatos post se reliquit, Solomon filium regem ex sextante. Bipartito regno videbis Israëlis reges o- mnes malos, Judæ reges malos aliquot, mediocres satis mul- tos, bonos tot quot facile in annulos inscribi possent.

UT hi libri primus & secundus Regum Ebræis, ita Græcis Regnorum li- bri dicuntur: & describit Primus re- gestas Salomonis, & sequentium quatuor Regum Judæ Roboami, Abiæ, Asæ, Josapha- ti, quorum anni numerantur 126. nimirum 40. Salo- monis, 17. Roboami, 3. Abiæ, 41. Asæ, & 25. Josa- phati. Dividitur in duas partes, ante divisionem re- EMIT ERGO DAVID AREAM) Hic ponendum co- lon: emit autem siclis auri sexcentis. 1. Paral. 21, 25. quod se- quitur pretium est multo minus, victimarum scilicet.

Eadem fere est conciliatio Abarbenelis, & a- liorum Rabbinorum. Ita enim ille: Juxta sensum literalem memoratur hic quod emerit Aream, & Boves pro quinquaginta siclis argenteis, ibique altare Domi- no exstruxerit. Quia vero ibi ædificari debuit domus Domini, emendus ipsi etiam fuit ager Araunæ, qui vi- cinus erat illi Areæ, ubi domus exstrueretur & pro illo agro dedit 600. siclos aureos. Id autem non comme- moratur hic; sed in libro Chronicorum, ubi dicitur: appendit itaque David Ornani pro loco illo siclos aureos pondere justo sexcentos. Vult dicere, Da- videm tantum dedisse pro toto agro, qui est locus ille, cujus ibi sit mentio. Et huc inclinavit etiam Rab- ba, nomine Rabbi Abba Jose ben Dosithei in מדרש שמואל & in זבחים מסכת, quando ait, boves & ligna & locum altaris pro quinquaginta siclis argenti. Petrus Martyr ita habet, dat pretium 50. siclorum: in Paralipom. habetur 600. sed nulla est pu- gna: nam pro bobus & instrumentis rusticis dati sunt 50. sicli, sed pro area & domibus 600. Vel fieri potest, ut dederit 50. siclos, & postea ex regia munificentia 600. potest etiam esse, ut 50. pro area dati sint, sed quia tem- plum ibi erat ædificandum, horti, domus, & ædificia oc- cupanda, tanta est igitur data summa. Hebræi fabu- lantur, publicum esse debuisse, & coëmendum ab o- mnibus tribubus, ut quælibet daret 50. siclos, & sic essent 600. sicli: Tribus enim erant 12. Locum au- tem totum pro 600. sive cum Grotio dicantur pro area dati 600. sicli, seu cum Ebræis pro toto agro, promta est conciliatio. Hæc tamen posterior sen- tentia vero magis affinis est. Quia area non vide- tur tantæ fuisse capacitatis, ut templi ædificio suffe- cerit: Ideo hanc conciliationem probavit Hiero- nymus, Lyranus, Hugo, Cajetanus, Serarius, Salianus, Robertus Bailius & Paraphrasis Vinariensis. Pre- camur cum Davide (Ps. 132, 8. 9.) Surge DOMINE in requiem tuam, tu & arca sanctificationis tuæ. Sacer- dotes tui induantur justitia, & sancti tui exultent. A- men. Amen.

# 1 Kings

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 1). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
N. J. THE FORMER OF KINGS TO THE HEBREWS, AND THE LATIN OF KINGS.

dom, where the history of Solomon is through 11 chapters, and after the division of the kingdom through the remaining eleven chapters, under the aforementioned 4 Kings; whose history, also contemporary, is set forth at the same time in the kingdom of Israel for eight kings from Jeroboam to Ahab.

Part I. The history of the whole kingdom of Israel under Solomon, first sets forth the auspices of his reign, namely the succession of Solomon after David, ch. 1, then the instruction of David, and the punishment of certain transgressors committed by David, and the confirmation of the kingdom, ch. 2, and also the divine concession of wisdom, ch. 3. Then the happy governance of Solomon: (1) Regarding worldly matters, such as his ministers, economy, rule, and fame for wisdom, ch. 4. (2) Regarding sacred matters, because of the building of the Temple magnificent: where the friendship with Hiram, and the number of architects ch. 5. and the structure itself is described ch. 6. as well as the preparation for the temple ch. 7. then the introduction of the ark, and the most solemn inauguration of the temple ch. 8. also the divine apparition ch. 9. finally the fame, by which the Queen of Arabia was excited ch. 10. Finally the unhappy fates, the cause of which were profane marriages and idolatry ch. 11.

Part II. History of the successors of Solomon in the kingdom of Judah (and 8. in the kingdom of Israel,) namely I. REHOBOAM, where the Schism of Rehoboam and Jeroboam both regarding the kingdom, and regarding public worship ch. 12. and the divine revocation of Jeroboam from the Schism in religion attempted through the man of God ch. 13. as also other deeds of Rehoboam in his time, especially the plundering of the Temple done by Shishak ch. 14. II. ABIJAM the impious, and III. ASA the pious, to whom the contemporary Kings of Israel were Nadab, and Baasha the exterminator of the family of Jeroboam ch. 15. as also Elah, and Zimri, and Omri, and Ahab ch. 16. under whom these deeds: (1) Elijah predicted the drought and sustained the woman of Zarephath ch. 17. he slaughtered the Baalites, ch. 18. he appointed Jehu King and Elisha Prophet, ch. 19. (2) Benhadad was defeated, but kept among the living ch. 20. (3) Naboth was killed on account of the vineyard, ch. 21. IV. JEHOSHAPHAT, who having allied himself with Ahab fought against the Syrians, otherwise reigned piously, ch. 22.

VOCAVIT VNIVERSOS FRATRES SVOS) Convi- via apta conjurationibus. Supra 15, 2.

## 1:10
Ver. 10. BUT NATHAN THE PROPHET AND BENAIAH AND THE MIGHTY MEN ALSO AND SOLOMON HIS BROTHER HE CALLED NOT) Partly out of contempt, partly because he believed them to be opposed to his plans, as friends of Bathsheba.

LOMON'S] Prudently: as if he were to say with Mutianus: you must flee to the imperial power, which was the most glorious and likewise the safest thing here.

Latin:

Vers. 10. NATHAN AUTEM PROPHETAM ET BANAJAM ET ROBVSTOS QVOQVE ET SOLOMONEM FRA- TREM SUUM NON VOCAVIT) Partim contemtu, par- tim quod eos suis consiliis adversos crederet, ut amicos Bethsabeæ.

LOMONIS] Prudenter: quasi dicat cum Mutiano: con- fugiendum tibi est ad imperium, quod gloriosissimum idem tutissimum hic erat.

## 1:13
Ver. 13. HAST NOT THOU MY LORD O KING SWORN UNTO ME THINE HANDMAID, SAYING: SOLOMON THY SON SHALL REIGN AFTER ME) Undoubtedly with God as the Author through Nathan the Prophet, which Adonijah confesses below 2, 15. and most openly 1 Paralip. 28, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 13. NONNE TV DOMINE MI REX JURASTI MIHI ANCILLÆ TVÆ, DICENS: SALOMON FILIVS TVVS REGNABIT POST ME) Haud dubie Deo Aucto- re per Nathanem Prophetam, quod fatetur Adonias infra 2, 15. & apertissime 1. Paralip. 28, 5.

## 1:14
Ver. 14. I WILL COME AFTER THEE AND CONFIRM THY WORDS) Thus Calchas arranges everything.

An excellent and very pious comparison of a Greek augur moved by a demon with a Prophet of the Lord, full of the Spirit of God, of Calchas with Nathan! But by the same Spirit with which Grotius everywhere institutes such comparisons of the men of GOD with profane Gentiles, his Annotations for the most part are also written: Of which kind also is that which he adds below v. 52 concerning the constitution of Solomon in the case of Shimei. Ἀὶ γὰρ εὖ πίπτυσιν ὁι θεῶν κύβοι. He measures God-given wisdom by no other standard than human prudence, and what proceeded from God blessed for evermore, he ascribes to the chance of the dice of the gods. Thus he seems to hold the Solomonic Proverbs in a similar place with the Gnomes of the Gentiles at c. 4 below v. 32, while he says that Solomon did not have all those γνώμας as his own discovery: (What pious person will admit that the amanuensis of the Holy Spirit has a discoverer for those things dictated to the Holy Scriptures?) But that they were collected from the writings of historians and poets. Nor does he judge otherwise concerning the Canticle, annotating these things at the same place: And his songs were a thousand and five. He was not only a philosopher, but also a distinguished poet; understand songs such as those of Horace, or Idylls, such as those of Theocritus. One of those Idylls of Solomon is that which remains to us, which the Greeks would have called ἄεισον. The Hebrews call it שיר השירים.

Latin:

Vers. 14. EGO VENIAM POST TE ET COMPLEBO SER- MONES TVOS) Ita digerit omnia Calchas.

EGregia & perquam pia comparatio Græci augu- ris a Dæmone acti cum Propheta Domini, Spiri- tu Dei pleno, Calchantis cum Nathane! Sed quo Spiritu Grotius tales comparationes virorum DEI passim cum gentilibus prophanis instituit, eodem etiam pleræque Annotationes ejus conscriptæ sunt: Cujus generis quoque est, quod de Salomonis con- stitutione in causa Simei infra addit v. 52. Ἀὶ γὰρ εὖ πίπτυσιν ὁι θεῶν κύβοι. Non alio pede sapien- tiam θεόσδοτον metitur, quam humanam pruden- tiam, & quod a Deo benedicto in secula profectum, casui τῶν κύβων τῶν θεῶν adscribit. Ita Proverbia Salomonea parili loco cum Gnomis gentilium habere videtur ad c. 4. infra v. 32. dum ait, γνὼμας illas non omnes Salomonem habuisse repertorem: (Quæ ad S. S. dictata, amanuensem Spiritus Sancti repertorem ha- bere quis pius admittet?) Sed collectas esse ex histori- corum & Poetarum Scriptis. Nec aliter de Cantico judicat, ad eundem locum hæc annotans: Et fuerunt carmina ejus quinque & mille. Non Philosophus tantum fuit, sed & Poeta insignis; Carmina intellige qualia Horatii, aut Idyllia, qualia Theocriti. Eorum Idylliorum Salomonis unum est, quod nobis restat, quod ἄεισον dixissent Græci. Hebræi שיר השירים vocant.

## 1:18
Ver. 18. THOU, MY LORD O KING NOT KNOWING) Both the interpreter here and the Greeks read ואתה, where now in the Hebrew we read עתה.

Latin:

Vers. 18. TE, MI DOMINE REX IGNORANTE) Tam inter- pres hîc quam Græci legerunt ואתה, ubi nunc in Hebræo legimus עתה.

## 1:21
Ver. 21. WE SHALL BE THEREFORE I AND MY SON SOLOMON SINNERS) Guilty of the crime of death for having affected the kingdom.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ERIMVS ERGO EGO ET FILIVS MEVS SALO- MON PECCATORES) Rei mortis crimine regni affectati.

## 1:23
Ver. 23. AND HAD WORSHIPPED HIM BOWING DOWN TO THE GROUND) For he was not coming now as a Prophet, but as a friend of the king.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ET ADORASSET EVM PRONVS IN TERRAM) Non enim veniebat jam ut Propheta, sed ut amicus regis.

## 1:34
Ver. 34. LET ZADOK THE PRIEST ANOINT HIM FOR HIMSELF) The vicar of the high priest performed all his duties in his absence. But what David did here, the same did Artaxerxes after him, who, to cut off contentions among his brothers, made his son Darius king while he was still alive. The same did other Persian Kings, and many of the Roman Emperors. Among the Hebrews, kings were not accustomed to be anointed outside of controversies of the kingdom, but when controversies arose, anointing was applied for greater security.

Latin:

Vers. 34. VNGAT EVM SIBI SADOC SACERDOS) Vicarius summi sacerdotis in ejus absentia omnia ejus munia fungeba- tur. Quod autem hîc fecit David, idem post eum fecit Arta- xerxes, qui ad præscindenda inter fratres certamina vivus Da- rium filium regem fecit. Idem fecere & Persæ Reges alii, Impe- ratorum Romanorum multi. Apud Hebræos, reges extra con- troversiam regni hæredes ungi non solebant, sed exortis con- troversiis adhibita unctio ad majorem cautionem.

## 1:35
Ver. 35. HE SHALL SIT UPON MY THRONE] A legitimate introduction into possession.

Latin:

Vers. 35. SEDEBIT SVPER SOLIVM MEVM] Legi- tima in possessionem introductio.

## 1:41
Vers. 41. AND ADONIJAH HEARD, AND ALL THAT WERE INVITED BY HIM] See what great haste Nathan applied to this business. For it was a plan that could not be praised, unless it were already accomplished.

Latin:

Vers. 41. AVDIVIT AVTEM ADONIAS ET OMNES QVI INVITATI ERANT AB EO] Vide quantam festinatio- nem huic negotio adhibuerit Nathan. Consilium enim erat, quod laudari non poterat, nisi peractum.

## 1:47
Vers. 47. AND THE KING WORSHIPPED UPON HIS BED) He prayed to God that these undertakings might turn out well for Solomon and well for the people.

Latin:

Vers. 47. ET ADORAVIT REX IN LECTVLO SVO) Deum precatus est, ut cœpta hæc bene Solomoni, bene populo verterent.

## 1:50
Vers. 50. TENVIT CORNV ALTARIS) He fled to the altar, not by the institution of the law, but by the custom of the nations, as also Joab 2, 31. See what has been said concerning the Law of War and Peace, book 2, chapter 21, §. 5, and the Comedies passim.

Latin:

Vers. 50. TENVIT CORNV ALTARIS) Ad aram confugit, non ex legis instituto, sed ex gentium more, ut & Joab 2, 31. Vide quæ dicta de Jure Belli ac Pacis libro 2. cap. 21. §. 5. & Co- mœdias passim.

## 1:52
Vers. 52. AND SOLOMON SAID: IF HE WILL BE A GOOD MAN, THERE SHALL NOT SO MUCH AS ONE HAIR OF HIS FALL TO THE EARTH) Solomon shows himself to be possessed of great wisdom from the beginning, undoubtedly sustained by the counsels of the great men Nathan, Zadok, and Benaiah: for Σοφοὶ τύραννοι τῶν σοφῶν συνεσίᾳ. For he pardons the crime of revolution, which would have been odious enough to punish in a brother, and a firstborn at that, but on this condition, that he do nothing in the future whereby he might make himself suspected. Which law was either to be a bridle for Adonijah, or an honorable pretext (πρόσφασις) for Solomon. Not dissimilar is that which Solomon establishes below in the case of Shimei. Ἀεὶ γὰρ εὖ πίπτουσιν οἱ θεῶν κύβοι.

Latin:

Vers. 52. DIXITQVE SALOMON: SI FVERIT VIR BONVS, NON CADET NE VNVS QVIDEM PILVS EJVS IN TERRAM) Magna se ab initio ostendit sapientia Solomo- nis, haud dubie sustentata virorum magnorum Nathanis, Sa- doci & Banajæ consiliis: nam Σοφοὶ τύραννοι τῶν σοφῶν συνεσίᾳ. Condonat enim crimen rerum novarum, quod punire in fratre & quidem primogenito odiosum satis fuerat, sed ea lege si nihil faciat in posterum, quo suspectum se possit fa- cere. Quæ lex aut frænum futurum erat Adoniæ, aut honesta πρόσφασις Solomoni. Non dissimile est quod in causa Semeis infra constituit Solomon. Ἀεὶ γὰρ εὖ πίπτουσιν οἱ θεῶν κύβοι.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II. The last will of David. The execution of Adonijah. The banishment of Abiathar, the punishment of Joab and Shimei.

Verse 1.

AS IT IS WRITTEN IN THE LAW OF MOSES) Deut. 17, 18.

Latin:

CAPUT II. Ultima Davidis voluntas. Adoniæ supplicium. Abjatharis relegatio, Joabi & Simei pœna.

Vers. 1.

SICUT SCRIPTUM EST IN LEGE MOYSIS) Deut. 17, 18.

## 2:6
Verse 6.

DO THEREFORE ACCORDING TO THY WISDOM) Bold men and those strong in authority among soldiers are dangerous in the new kingdom of a young king.

BUT why did David not kill him? Because he feared that he might incite Israel against him, as had been done before by Abner: and afterwards, involved in continuous wars, he could ill afford to be without Joab, and as Theodoret feared, lest he, using his accustomed malice, might harm Solomon.

AND THOU SHALT NOT BRING HIS HOAR HEAD DOWN PEACEABLY TO THE GRAVE) For David had not forgiven him the crime, nor could he forgive it by the law, but he had deferred the punishment of a man both powerful and useful in war. Such is that in Tacitus, Histories 3: Neither did the law of men allow them to honor him, nor did the reason of war allow them to avenge him. And Annals 15: Attila, the mother of Annaeus Lucanus, was passed over without acquittal, without punishment.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

FACIES ERGO JUXTA SAPIENTIAM TUAM) Viri audaces & apud milites auctoritate valentes periculosi sunt in regno novo regis adolescentis.

SED cur non occidit eum David? Quia metuit, ne is Israelem contra se concitaret, uti antea ab Ab- nero factum: & postea bellis continuis implicitus, carere Joabo ægre potuit, & ut Theodor. timuit, ne is solita usus malitia Salomoni officeret.

ET NON DEDUCES CANITIEM EJUS PACIFICE AD INFEROS) Neque enim remiserat illi crimen David, nec per legem remittere poterat, sed distulerat pœnam homi- nis & potentis, & in bello utilis. Tale illud apud Tacitum Histor. 3. Nec illis aut honorave eam eadem jus hominum, aut ulcisci ratio belli permittebat. & Annal. 15. Attila Mater An- næi Lucani, sine absolutione, sine supplicio dissimulata.

## 2:9
Verse 9.

BUT THOU ART A WISE MAN AND KNOWEST WHAT THOU OUGHTEST TO DO UNTO HIM] A man of restless disposition will easily give you an ἔυλογον αἰτίαν. See below 37.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

VIR AUTEM SAPIENS ES UT SCIAS QVÆ FACI- ES EI] Facile homo ingenii inquieti dabit tibi ἔυλογον αἰ- τίαν. Vide infra 37.

## 2:10
V. 10. SO DAVID SLEPT WITH HIS FATHERS.

Concerning this and the following two verses, v. 11 and 12, one may see Sermon 3 and 4, held in honor of the Saxon David, JOHN GEORGE I, in the Memory of the Just, Wittenberg.

Latin:

V. 10. DORMIVIT IGITUR DAVID CUM PATRIBUS SUIS.

De hoc & sequentibus duobus commatibus v. 11. & 12. videri poterit Concio 3. & 4. in honorem Davidis Saxonici JOHANNIS GEORGII I. habi- ta, in Memoria Justor. Witteberg.

## 2:15
Verse 15.

BUT THE KINGDOM HAS BEEN TRANSFERRED AND HAS BECOME MY BROTHER'S: FOR IT WAS ORDAINED BY THE LORD) So that it might not be thought that he took this ill, he both used the name of brother and ascribed the author of the matter to God. Such is that: - - - - Lavinia is your wife: Do not extend your hatred further.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

SED TRANSLATUM EST REGNUM ET FA- CTUM FRATRIS MEI: A DOMINO ENIM CON- STITUTUM EST ISTUD) Quo minus putetur id ægre ferre, & nomen fratris posuit, & rei Deum inscripsit aucto- rem. Tale illud: - - - - tua est Lavinia conjunx: Ulterius ne tende odiis.

## 2:17
Verse 17.

THAT HE MAY GIVE ME ABISHAG THE SHUNAMMITE TO WIFE) There were enough women in Judea: but he wanted this one because she had been the King's. However, the custom of the Hebrews did not allow that either those who had been in royal service should dedicate themselves to the service of any other than the King's successor, or that those who had been wives or concubines should be joined to a private citizen. Desiring her, therefore, he shows that the right to the kingdom pertains to him, and he tests the mind of Solomon, so that if he had conceded this to him out of youthful fear, he might soon dare greater things. He approaches the woman, as one ignorant of reigning, and thus easily swayed by love.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

VT DET MIHI ABISAG SUNAMITIDEM UXO- REM) Multæ satis erant in Judæa feminæ: sed hanc voluit quod Regis fuisset. Non ferebat autem mos Hebræorum, ut aut qui in ministerio fuerant regio, alterius se quam Regis successoris ministerio addicerent, aut quæ uxores aut concu- binæ fuerant, privato sociarentur. Hanc ergo cupiens jus ad se regni pertinere ostendit, tentatque animum Salomonis, ut si metu juvenili hoc ei concessisset, auderet mox majora. Mulierem autem aggreditur, ut regnandi ignaram, ita amori- bus facilem.

## 2:19
Verse 19.

WHO SAT AT HIS RIGHT HAND) Which place is the most honorable after the king's place. See what was said at Matthew 20, 21.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

QVÆ SEDIT AD DEXTRAM EJUS) Qui locus post regis locum honoratissimus. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 20, 21.

## 2:22
Verse 22.

AND HE HAS ABIATHAR THE PRIEST AND JOAB THE SON OF ZERUIAH) Aided by whose counsel and relying on whose authority he builds a step for himself toward the kingdom, unless I should strongly oppose him.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ET HABET ABIATHAR SACERDOTEM ET JOAB FILIUM SARVIÆ) Quorum consilio adjutus & auctoritate fretus gradum sibi ad regnum struit, nisi fortiter obstiterim.

## 2:23
Verse 23.

AND KING SOLOMON SENT BY THE HAND OF BENAIAH THE SON OF JEHOIADA] Thus Romulus almost killed Remus by the centurion Fabius Celer. But just as at Rome at that time all things were governed by the kings by force, so also among the Hebrews formerly. See 2 Samuel 1, 15 and here below 29, 46. Then indeed in civil discords nothing is safer than haste, where there is more need for action than for deliberation. Tacitus, Histories 1. And there are things which do not admit of delay, not for the sake of the haste of punishment, but for the sake of forestalling dangers. Law: If anyone, Digest, concerning an unjust, broken, or void testament. Nor do laws command themselves to be awaited, when for him who wishes to wait, an unjust punishment must be suffered before a just one can be sought, as Cicero says in defense of Milo.

Verse 72.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

MISITQVE REX SOLOMON PER MANUM BE- NAJÆ FILII JOJADÆ] Sic ferme Romulus Remum oc- cidit per centurionem Fabium Celerem. Sicut autem Romæ eo tempore omnia manu a regibus gubernantur, ita & apud Hebræos olim. Vide 2. Sam. 1, 15. & hic infra 29, 46. Tum vero nihil in discordiis civilibus festinatione tutius, ubi facto magis quam consulto opus. Tacitus Histor. 1. Et sunt quæ moram non recipiunt, non pœnæ festinatione, sed præveni- endi pericula causa. L. Si quis D. de injusto, rupto, irrito te- stamento. Nec se exspectari jubent leges, cum ei qui exspe- ctare velit, ante injusta pœna luenda sit, quam justa repeten- da, ut Cicero ait pro Milone.

Vers. 72.

## 2:27
SO SOLOMON CAST OUT ABIATHAR, THAT HE SHOULD NOT BE PRIEST OF THE LORD) High Priests among the Hebrews, just as they were instituted by Kings, as we have said elsewhere, so also they could be removed by the same for a grave fault, and indeed even be punished with death: for they were subjects; and therefore when the King was sitting, the high priest stood.

THAT THE WORD MIGHT BE FULFILLED) In Hebrew: for the fulfilling of the word: where 'ad' is ecbatic, not telic. For Solomon did not have this in view.

Latin:

EJECIT ERGO SALOMON ABIATHAR, VT NON ESSET SACERDOS DOMINI) Summi Sacerdotes apud Hebræos, sicut a Regibus instituebantur, ut alibi diximus, ita & ab iisdem gravi ex culpa destitui imo & morte puniri po- terant: erant enim subditi; ideoque sedente Rege stabat sum- mus sacerdos.

VT IMPLERETUR SERMO) Hebraice: ad implen- dum sermonem: ubi ad est ἐκϐατικὸν, non τελικὸν. Neque enim hoc respiciebat Salomo.

## 2:28
Ver. 28. AND HE CAUGHT HOLD OF THE HORNS OF THE ALTAR) Which ought not to have availed the murderer by the law of Exod. 21:14. Euripides: For whoever, being an unjust man, sits at the altar, bidding the law farewell, I would drag to justice, not fearing the gods. For a wicked man must always suffer wickedly.

Latin:

Vers. 28. ET APPREHENDIT CORNU ALTARIS) Quod homicidæ prodesse non debebat per legem Exod. 21,14. Euripides: Ἐγὼ γὰρ ὅστις μὴ δίκαιος ὢν ἀνὴρ Βωμὸν προσίζει, τὸν νόμον χαίρειν ἐῶν, Πρὸς τὴν δίκην ἄγοιμ' ἂν, ἐ τρέσας θεούς. Κακὸν γὰρ ἄνδρα χρὴ κακῶς πάσχειν ἀεί.

## 2:31
Ver. 31. THOU SHALT REMOVE THE INNOCENT BLOOD WHICH WAS SHED BY JOAB, FROM ME AND FROM THE HOUSE OF MY FATHER) Taken from the law of Num. 35:31 and Deut. 19:13. Not unlike that of Livy, book 1: He turns their punishment upon himself.

Latin:

Vers. 31. AMOVEBIS SANGVINEM INNOCENTEM QVI EFFVSVS EST A JOAB, A ME ET A DOMO PA- TRIS MEI) Sumtum ex lege Num. 35, 31. & Deut. 19, 13. Non dissimile illud Livii libro 1. Illorum pœnam in se vertit.

## 2:34
Ver. 34. AND HE WAS BURIED) From the law of Deuter. 21:23.

Latin:

Vers. 34. SEPULTUSQVE EST) Ex lege Deuter. 21. vers. 23.

## 2:35
Ver. 35. HE APPOINTED SADOC THE PRIEST INSTEAD OF ABIATHAR] By royal right. Thus the priesthood returned to the posterity of Phineas.

Latin:

Vers. 35. SADOC SACERDOTEM POSUIT PRO ABIATHAR] Jure regio. Sic sacerdotium ad Phineæ posteritatem rediit.

## 2:36
Ver. 36. AND THOU SHALT NOT GO FORTH FROM THENCE HITHER AND THITHER] It was credible that a man who was stubborn and wished to be allowed to do everything would not long obey the command. This punishment is that which Marcianus, in the law 'Exsilium' concerning the interdicted and relegated, placed among others, where one is forbidden from all places except one, very suitable for restraining men who could cause disturbances in a crowd.

Latin:

Vers. 36. ET NON EGREDIERIS INDE HUC AT- QVE ILLUC] Credibile erat hominem contumacem & omnia sibi licere volentem non obtemperaturum diu præce- pto. Pœna hæc ea est, quam Marcianus l. Exsilium de in- terdictis & relegatis inter cæteras posuit, ubi omnibus locis præter unum interdicitur, valde apta coercendis hominibus qui in turba turbas facere possent.

## 2:46
Ver. 46. HE STRUCK HIM AND HE DIED) A just punishment for a double reason, because the old crime had not been pardoned to him except under a condition which he did not keep, and because even without that, to violate a special command of the king was a capital offense, no less than if someone had deserted his post. Moreover, what is said concerning Justice by Euripides can be well applied to this Semei: - - - Silent and with slow foot, she creeps and always catches the wicked among mortals. And this: - - - Thus let no evildoer, if he runs the first step well, think he has defeated justice, until he reaches the end of the line and rounds the goal of life. And from Theodectes: But when they are caught having been seen as wicked, they pay penalties in later times.

Latin:

Vers. 46. PERCUSSIT EUM ET MORTUUS EST) Justa pœna duplici ex causa, quia & vetus crimen condona- tum ei non fuerat, nisi sub conditione cui non stetit, & quia etiam sine eo speciale præceptum regis violare capitale erat, non minus quam si quis statione discessisset. Potest autem huic Semeï bene aptari quod dicitur περὶ Δίκης ab Euripide: - - - σῖγα καὶ βραδεῖ ποδὶ Στείχουσα μάρπτει τοὺς κακοὺς ἀεὶ βροτῶν. Et hoc: - - - ὧδέ τις κακοῦργος ὢν, Μή μοι τὸ πρῶτον βῆμ' ἐὰν δράμῃ καλῶς Νικᾷν δοκείτω τὴν δίκην, πρὶν ἂν τέλος Γραμμῆς ἵκηται, καὶ τέλος κάμψῃ βίε. Et à Theodecte: Ὅταν δὲ φωραθῶσιν ὀφθέντες κακοὶ Τίνουσι ποινὰς ὑστέροισιν ἐν χρόνοις

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III.

Solomon asks for wisdom, and obtains it, and wisely settles the dispute of two mothers.

Ver. 1. FOR HE TOOK HIS DAUGHTER) Made subject to the law: for that he did not sin in this marriage is apparent from Psalm 44 and from the Song [of Songs] related in the sacred books.

That Solomon married the daughter of Pharaoh, who was subject to the law, or rather converted to the true God, in that he did not sin, conflicts with the annotations of Grotius on Deut. 7:3. Neither shalt thou make marriages with them, nor even with those converted to the law. Nor indeed must another reason be invented here for the Canaanite women and those of other nations, because the same cause of the divine interdict applies also to other foreign women, if they have not been converted, namely, the danger of seduction. But where women have been converted, whether they be Canaanites or other foreigners, the reason for the law expires, and so, the reason for the law ceasing, the law itself ceases. As for that passage already observed. But then the Holy Spirit interprets that law generally, for the reason indeed added to it (which is the soul of the Law), and indeed in this very case, concerning Solomon's marriage below in chapter 11. But King Solomon loved many foreign women, as well as the daughter of Pharaoh, and Moabites, and Ammonites, Edomites, and Sidonians, and Hittites, from the nations concerning which the Lord said to the children of Israel: you shall not enter unto them, nor shall they enter unto yours: for most certainly they will turn away your hearts, that you may follow their gods. To these, therefore, Solomon was joined with most ardent love. We see here that this prohibition is to be understood not only concerning the Canaanites, but also concerning the Moabite, Ammonite, and Edomite women, by marrying whom Solomon is said to have sinned equally against that law when he took the same [women] not converted to the faith; and while he joined to himself in marriage the Sidonians, i.e., the Canaanites and Hittites. But whether Solomon sinned by taking the daughter of Pharaoh, because she too is listed here, and thus took her not converted to God, opinions vary. To some it seems, because she is joined here to the others while the sins of Solomon are being recounted, that in his marriage he also disregarded the divine law. Thus the Rabbis in Seder Olam, likewise Theodoret, and Procopius. Others, however, most of them—Abulensis, Pineda, Salianus, Serarius, Sanctius, Corn. a Lapide, Menochius, and others—judge that she had been converted to the God of Israel, and therefore that Solomon did not sin in taking her; consequently, that she is mentioned here for this reason alone and in this respect, that there is a full account of Solomon's wives, namely, that he added other foreign women to the daughter of Pharaoh, and in this acted against the law of God. To which opinion we add our vote, since the Holy Scriptures, having explicitly recounted that marriage, add in this chapter 3, 3: 'And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the statutes of David his father, except that he sacrificed in the high places.' That marriage is not excepted, therefore, as illegitimate; but the sacrifice which was made in the high places. I pass over the fact that Eusebius, in book 9 of the Praeparatio Evangelica, recounts letters exchanged between King Pharaoh and Solomon regarding the conversion of the daughter of King Pharaoh. Compare on these matters Rivet in his Commentary on Psalm 45, pp. 302 and 337. That reasoning of Grotius, however, from Psalm 44 and the Song of Songs, is not solid. For even if it could be conceded that there is an allusion there to this marriage, it is not, however, about that which is treated there, but about the spiritual marriage of Christ and the Church, of which we shall speak in its proper place.

Latin:

CAPUT III.

Salomon sapientiam postulat, & impetrat, ac li- tem duarum puerperarum sapienter dirimit.

Vers. 1. ACCEPIT NAMQVE FILIAM EJUS) Factam legi subjectam: nam in hoc matrimonio eum non peccasse, apparet ex Psalm. 44. & ex Cantico in sacros libros relato.

Quod filiam Pharaonis legi subjectam, vel potius ad verum Deum conversam duxerit Salomo, in eo ipsum non peccasse, pugnat cum annotatis Grotii ad Deut. 7, 3. Neque sociabis cum eis conjugia, ned; conversis quidem ad legem. Nec vero hic fingenda alia ratio in fœminis Cananæis, & aliarum gentium, quia eadem interdicti divini causa cum aliis quoq; fœminis alienigenis, si conversæ non fuerint, militat, periculum nempe seductionis. Ubi autem conversæ fœminæ fuerint, sive Cananææ, sive alias alienigenæ fuerint, ratio legis exspirat, adeoque cessante Legis ra- tione, cessat Lex ipsa. Quod ad locum illum jam ob- servatum. Tum vero generaliter legem illam in- terpretatur Spiritus Sanctus, ob rationem nempe il- li adjectam, (quæ anima est Legis) & quidem in hoc ipso casu, de Salomonis conjugio infra c. 11. Rex au- tem Salomon adamavit mulieres alienigenas multas, Filiam quoque Pharaonis, & Moabitidas, & Ammoni- tidas, Idumæas & Sidonias, & Hethæas, de gentibus, su- per quibus dixit Dominus filiis Israel: non ingrediemini ad eas, neque de illis ingredientur ad vestras: certissime enim avertent corda vestra, ut sequamini Deos earum. His itaque copulatus est Salomo ardentissimo amore. Videmus hic non solum de Cananæis, sed etiam de Moabitis, Ammonitis, Idumæis mulieribus id interdictum accipiendum esse, quas ducendo Salomo æque adversus legem illam peccasse dicitur, quum duxit easdem non conversas ad fi- dem; ac dum Sidonias, i.e. Cananæas, & Hethæas ma- trimonio sibi copulavit. An vero filiam Pharaonis ducendo, quia hic quoque recensetur, peccarit Sa- lomo, adeoque eandem duxerit non conversam ad Deum, variant sententiæ. Nonnullis videtur, quia hic cæteris conjungitur, dum peccata Salomonis re- censentur, in ejus matrimonio etiam ipsum legem divinam posthabuisse. Ita Rabbini in Seder Olam, Theodoretus item, ac Procopius. Alii tamen pleriq; Abulensis, Pineda, Salianus, Serarius, Sanctius, Corn. a Lapide, Menochius, & alii censent, eandem conver- sam fuisse ad Deum Israelis, ideoque in ea ducenda Salomonem non peccasse; Proinde mentionem hic ejus fieri hoc solum nomine, ac respectu, quod plena recensio sit conjugum Salomonis, quod nempe ad Pharaonis filiam alias adjunxerit alienigenas, inque hoc contra legem Dei egerit. Cui sententiæ cal- culum adjicimus, siquidem diferte recensito matri- monio illo addat S.S. hoc capite 3, 3. dilexit autem Sa- lomon Dominum, ambulans in præceptis David Patris sui, excepto, quod in excelsis immolabat. Non exci- pitur ergo illud conjugium ceu illegitimum; Sed immolatio, quæ in excelsis facta. Taceo, quod Eu- sebius l. 9. Præpar. Evang. Epistolas inter Regem Pha- raonem & Salomonem commutatas ob conversionem Filiæ Regis Pharaonis recenseat. Confer de his Ri- vet. in Comment. ad Pf. 45. p. 302. & 337. Ratio tamen illa Grotii e Pf. 44. & Cantico Canticorum solida non est. Etsi enim concedi possit, ibi alludi ad hoc con- jugium, non tamen de illo ibidem agitur, sed de con- jugio Spirituali Christi & Ecclesiæ, de quo suo loco dicturi sumus.

## 3:3
Vers. 3.

EXCEPT THAT HE SACRIFICED IN THE HIGH PLACES)

It does not seem to be an exception regarding the integrity of Solomon at that time: but that what was said about the people was the same said about Solomon, namely, because the temple had not yet been built. Sacrifices were made by him in two places where the tabernacle was, that is, at Gibeon (1 Chron. 1:3) and at Jerusalem, where the Ark was (below 8:1).

This annotation is diametrically opposed to the text. For here it openly excepts this sacrifice as illegitimate: since it says Solomon walked in the statutes of his father David, except that he sacrificed in the high places. And the divine prohibitions are manifest, by which sacrifices in the high places were forbidden and restricted to the tabernacle and the Altar destined for them by God (Ex. 34:13, Deut. 7:5, ch. 12:2, and ch. 16:21, Lev. 17:34), whence David, Hezekiah, and Josiah are celebrated by the Holy Scriptures because they either did not tolerate the high places or destroyed those built by others. Asa and Jehoshaphat, however, did indeed abolish the high places, but those consecrated to the true God; which, because of the danger of idolatry—since they emulated the character of the high places of the Gentiles, or were akin to them—and because God had destined another place for sacrifices, were not approved by God, even if those high places in which the worship of God or of idols was performed by the rite of the Gentiles were far more disapproved by God, as being utterly idolatrous. Therefore, Theodoret, Procopius, and also the Papists—Abulensis, Ribera, Sanctius, Menochius, Tirinus—acknowledge that Solomon cannot be excused. But Grotius preferred to follow the opinion of the Jews here, which, however, Lyranus and Serarius propose with this qualification: that the worship in the high places was not indeed absolutely pleasing to God before the Temple was built, yet it was permitted, and thus was licit at that time; but after the Temple was built, it was illicit; to which Augustine also inclines (Quaest. 5 in Judic.) and Corn. a Lapide in this place, as also Pineda on the affairs of Solomon, book 5, ch. 5, n. 5. But the fact that the sacrifice in Gibeon, where there was also a high place, was pleasing to GOD, was because there was the tabernacle and the altar

of Moses, in which sacrifices ought to have been made at that time (1 Par. 21:29, 2 Par. 1:3), whence it is called the great high place, not in quantity, but in dignity, which therefore should not be confused with other places and high places where it was not permitted to sacrifice. Although, indeed, Samuel, Elijah, and other prophets and men of God sometimes offered sacrifices outside the tabernacle, that was done extraordinarily by a special instinct and dispensation of God, who did not bind Himself to the law, but others.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

EXCEPTO, QVOD IN EXCELSIS IMMOLABAT)

Non videtur esse exceptio de integritate Salomonis eo tem- pore: Sed quod de populo dictum fuit, idem dictum de So- lomone, nempe quia nondum structum erat templum. Sa- crificia ab eo facta duobus in locis, ubi erat tabernacu- lum, id est, Gabaone 1. Paral. 1,3. & Hierosolymis, ubi erat Arca infra 8, 1.

Hæc annotatio καδδιάμετρον adversa est tex- tui. Hic enim aperte excipit hanc immolationem ceu illegitimam: Cum ambulasset Salomonem dicit in præceptis Patris David eo excepto, quod in excelsis im- molabat. Et interdicta divina manifesta sunt, qui- bus prohibebantur Sacrificia in excelsis, & restrin- gebantur ad tabernaculum & Altare a Deo illis desti- natum Ex. 34, 13. Deut. 7, 5. c. 12, 2. & c. 16, 21. Lev. 17, 34. unde celebrantur a S.S. David, Hiskias, & Josias, quod excelsa aut non tolerarint, aut ab aliis exstructa dissipaverint. Assa vero & Josaphat aboleverunt qui- dem excelsa, sed vero Deo consecrata; quæ ob pericu- lum idololatriæ, quia æmulabantur gentilium ex- celsorum indolem, vel affinia iisdem erant, & quod Deus destinarit alium sacrificiis locum, Deo haud probabantur, etsi excelsa illa, in quibus ritu genti- lium cultus Dei vel Idolorum peragebatur, longe ma- gis Deo improbata fuerint, utpote prorsus Idolola- trica. Excusari ergo non posse Salomonem agno- scunt Theodoretus, Procopius, nec non Pontificii, Abu- lensis, Riebera, Sanctius, Menochius, Tirinus: Sed Gro- tius Judæorum sententiam hic sequi maluit, quam tamen, cum hoc temperamento, Lyranus ac Serarius proponunt, quod non quidem absolute Deo gratus fuerit cultus in excelsis ante exstructum Templum, permissus tamen, adeoque ita licitus tum fuerit: post exstructum vero templum illicitus: quo etiam Au- gust. propendet Quæst. 5. in Judic. & Corn. a Lap. in h. l. ut & Pineda de rebus Sal. l. 5. c. 5. n. 5. Quod vero Sacrificium in Gibeon, ubi etiam excelsum fuit, DEO placuerit, inde erat, quia illic tabernaculum & altare

Mosis, in quo Sacrificia fieri debebant, isto tempore fuerant 1. Par. 21, 29. 2. Par. 1. 3. unde vocatur excel- sum magnum, non quantitate, sed dignitate, quod proinde cum aliis locis & excelsis, quibus permissum non erat sacrificare, confundi non debet. Quan- quam vero extra tabernaculum etiam Samuel, Elias, alii que Prophetæ & viri Dei quandoque sacrificia obtulerint, id tamen extraordinarie factum ex pe- culiari Dei instinctu & dispensatione, qui legi non se adstrinxit, sed alios.

## 3:5
Vers. 5.

AND THE LORD APPEARED TO SOLOMON IN A DREAM BY NIGHT) An angel speaking in the name of God appeared to him in a dream.

There is nothing in the text about an Angel. Nor is it right for us to foist whatever we please upon the sacred context: if wherever the Lord is said to have appeared, or to have done something, or to have spoken, it were lawful to understand an Angel appearing, acting, and speaking in the name of the Lord, there will be no θεοΦανεία, no ἄμεσος and immediate action or conversation, and ministers will be confused with the Lord, organic or inferior causes with the principal and supreme, creatures with the creator. That apparition is certainly so constituted, and the speech, that it refers to no one but God manifested here ἀμέσως. Jehovah is said to have appeared, v. 5. God is said to have spoken and said: ask what you wish, that I may give it to you. Nor does Solomon address anyone other than the Lord. You have shown great mercy to your servant David my Father. If he had addressed an angel in this way, the Angel would never have endured it, as the apparition made to John in Ap. 19 and 22 testifies. He celebrates him who appeared to him, and with whom Solomon speaks, as God; And now O Lord God. He attributes to him divine attributes, great mercy, and omnipotence, he ascribes to him works truly divine, that he gave to David a son sitting upon his throne, that he made Solomon reign in the place of his parent, that he chose for himself a people, that he grants a docile heart; he vindicates for him divine ἀξιώματα, worship proper to God alone, that David walked in his sight, in truth and justice, and with an upright heart; and that he ought to serve him religiously as Lord. Nor does the text speak otherwise of him who appears here than if the Lord himself had appeared: The speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked for such a thing. Nor does he declare himself to be anyone else: And the Lord said to Solomon: Because you have asked for this word, behold I have done for you according to your words, and I have given you a wise and understanding heart, etc. He attributes to himself the bestowal of wisdom, riches, and glory, as well as the gift of μακροβιότητα, and claims for himself divine honor, so that Solomon may walk in his ways, and keep his precepts. Finally, Solomon afterwards offered victims to this Lord who appeared. All of which clearly confirm that not an Angel, but the Lord himself appeared here.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

APPARVIT AVTEM DOMINVS SOLOMONI PER SOMNIVM NOCTE) Angelus in Dei nomine lo- quens ei in somnio apparuit.

Nihil in textu de Angelo. Neque nobis in- tegrum est, quicquid libuerit, sacro contextui inge- rere: si ubicunque apparuisse, aut egisse aliquid, aut loquutus esse dicitur Dominus, fas sit Angelum in nomine Domini apparentem, agentem & loquen- tem intelligere, nulla erit θεοΦανεία, nulla actio aut collocutio ἄμεσος, & immediata, & confundentur ministri cum Domino, causæ organicæ vel inferio- res cum principali & suprema, creaturæ cum crea- tore. Apparitio certe illa ita comparata est, & o- ratio, ut non referat alium, nisi Deum ἀμέσως hic manifestatum. Jehovah apparuisse v. 5. Deus loquu- tus esse ac dixisse dicitur: postula quod vis, ut dem tibi. Nec alium quam Dominum compellat Salomo. Tu fecisti cum servo tuo David Patre meo misericordiam magnam. Si ita angelum alloquutus esset, nun- quam id tulisset Angelus, quod apparitio Johanni facta Ap. 19. & 22. testatur. Celebrat eum qui ipsi apparuit, & quicum loquitur Salomo, ceu Deum; Et nunc Domine Deus. Tribuit ei divina attributa, mi- sericordiam magnam, & omnipotentiam, adscribit ei opera vere divina, quod dederit Davidi filium, sedentem super Thronum ejus, quod regnare fecerit Salomonem loco parentis, quod elegerit sibi populum, quod cor do- cile donet; vindicat illi ἀξιώματα divina, cultum Deo soli proprium, quod ambularit David in conspe- ctu ejus, in veritate & justitia, & recto corde; quodq; ipsi ut Domino religiosē servire debeat. Nec ali- ter loquitur de eo, qui hic apparet, textus, quam si Dominus ipse apparuerit: Placuit sermo coram Do- mino, quod postulasset Salomo hujusmodi rem. Ne- que alium se esse declarat: Et dixit Dominus Salo- moni: Quia postulasti verbum hoc, ecce feci tibi secun- dum sermones tuos, & dedi tibi cor sapiens & intelli- gens &c. Tribuit sibi Sapientiæ, divitiarum & glo- riæ collationem, nec non μακροβιότητα donum, & vendicat sibi honorem divinum, ut Salomo in viis ipsius ambulet, & præcepta ejus custodiat. Denique huic viso Domino Salomo victimas postea obtulit. Quæ omnia non Angelum, sed Dominum ipsum hic apparuisse luculenter confirmant.

## 3:11
Vers. 11. BUT YOU HAVE ASKED FOR YOURSELF WISDOM)

Indeed, ἐκ τῇς σοφίας κτῆμα τιμιώτερον. And as Sophocles says: Προνοίας ὀυδὲν ἀνθρώποις ἔφυ Κέρδος λαβεῖν ἄμεινον, Ὀυδὲ τῆ σοφῇ. Menander truly: ἐκ ἔστι ὀυδὲν, πάτερ, ἐν ἀνθρώπε φύσει Μεῖζον λογισμῶ τῷ διαθέσθαι πράγματα Ἔκαστός ἐστιν ημών λογιταῦδαυ κατα τρόπον, Αρχων, σρατηγός, ήγεμών δήμε, πάλιν Σύμβελος ό αδιαφερων λογισμω̃ πάντ̓ ἐχει.

Menander vero: ἐκ ἔστι ὀυδὲν, πάτερ, ἐν ἀνθρώπε φύσει Μεῖζον λογισμῶ τῷ διαθέσθαι πράγματα Ἔκαστός ἐστιν ημών λογιταῦδαυ κατα τρόπον, Αρχων, σρατηγός, ήγεμών δήμε, πάλιν Σύμβελος ό αδιαφερων λογισμω̃ πάντ̓ ἐχει.

## 3:24
Verse 24. BRING ME A SWORD) From this appears the excellent ἀγχίνοια (sagacity) of Solomon. Not unlike that is the story of Ariopharnes, king of the Thracians, who, regarding three men claiming to be sons of the king of the Cimmerians, held him to be the son who, when ordered to pierce his father's corpse with javelins, had refused to do so. This history is in Diodorus Siculus. Likewise that of Galba, who, when a question arose about the ownership of a beast of burden, with light arguments and witnesses on both sides, and therefore a difficult conjecture of the truth, decreed that it should be led to the place where it was accustomed to be watered with its head covered, and there, when it was uncovered, it should belong to the person to whom it had spontaneously returned from drinking, as Suetonius relates: who also reports the by no means to be despised judgment of Claudius, who compelled a woman not acknowledging her son, when the credibility of the arguments on both sides was doubtful, to a confession by ordering a marriage with the young man. These are those frauds which Plato in the fifth book of the Republic wishes the Magistrate to use for the good of subjects and in the place of a medicine. Among those signs which rhetoricians call εἰκότα (probabilities), the most valid for investigating a mother is στοργή (natural affection).

SECTION II. THE HAPPY GOVERNANCE OF SOLOMON.

Latin:

Vers. 24. AFFERTE MIHI GLADIVM) Apparet hinc ἀγχίνοια Solomonis egregia. Non dissimile illud Ariopharnis regis Thracum, qui de tribus filios se Cimmeriorum regis di- centibus, eum pro filio habuit, qui jussus cadaver patris jaculis noluerat incessere. Quæ historia est apud Siculum Diodorum. Item illud Galbæ, qui cum de proprietate ju- menti quæreretur, levibus utrimque argumentis & testibus, ideoque difficili conjectura veritatis, ita decrevit, ut ad lo- cum, ubi adaquari solebat, duceretur capite involuto, atque ibi dem revelato, ejus esset, ad quem sponte se a potu recepis- fet, narrante Suetonio: qui & Claudii minime spernendum judicium refert, qui feminam non agnoscentem filium suum, dubia utrimque argumentorum fide, ad confessionem com- pulit, indicto matrimonio juvenis. Hæ sunt illæ fraudes, quibus uti Magistratum bono subditorum & medicamenti vice vult Plato de Republica quinto. Inter illa figna quæ εἰκότα vocant Rhetores, validissimum est ad matrem inda- gandam στοργή.

SECTIO II. FELICIA SALOMONIS GUBER- NACULA.

OVER THE RECORDS) In Hebrew: מזכיר, which the LXX translate: ἀναμιμνήσκων (reminding): he who performs that office is the μνήμων (remembrancer) of Aristophanes' scholiast in the Clouds: Master of Memory, L. Eos qui, C. de Excusationibus munerum, book 10. In English, remembrancer; in French, master of petitions.

## 4:5
Verse 5. OVER THOSE WHO ATTENDED THE KING) על־הנצבים ἐπὶ τῶν καθεσαμένων. But those הנצבים were, as we shall now understand, the overseers of the royal table. He who was in charge of these held an office like that of the Count of the Sacred Patrimony at Constantinople.

FRIEND OF THE KING) He who in the Constantinopolitan court was a patrician.

He is called a Priest in this place, but it is agreed that the word כהן is taken more generally, and thus the prince of the court is noted here, just as David's sons were so called.

Latin:

Vers. 5. SVPER EOS QVI ASSISTEBANT REGI) על־הנצבים ἐπὶ τῶν καθεσαμένων. Ii autem הנצבים erant, ut jam intelligemus, curatores mensæ regiæ. His qui præerat, id munus habebat, quod Constantinopoli comes sa- cri patrimonii.

AMICVS REGIS) Qui in aula Constantinopolitana, patricius.

Idem dicitur Sacerdos h. l. sed vocem כהן ge- neralius accipi constat, adeoque notatur hic aulæ princeps, uti Davidis filii sic vocati sunt.

Verse 6. OVER THE HOUSE) Count of the privy purse at Constantinople.

SVPER TRIBVTA) Comes sacrarum largitionum.

## 4:11
Verse 11. TAPHET HAD THE DAUGHTER OF SOLOMON AS HIS WIFE.

This is a prolepsis: because Solomon was then only 20 years old, therefore he could not have had a marriageable daughter at that time. Likewise also verse 15. All the princes of Solomon are listed, whether they were those who were then, or those who were made so afterwards.

Latin:

Vers. 11. TAPHET FILIAM SALOMONIS HABEBAT UXOREM.

Prolepsis est: quia Salomo tunc 20. tantum annorum fuit, non ergo habere tum potuit filiam nubilem. Sic & v. 15. Recensentur omnes prin- cipes Salomonis sive qui tum erant, sive qui postea facti sunt.

Verse 21. FROM THE RIVER OF THE LAND OF THE PHILISTINES) More correctly, from the river to the land of the Philistines, that is, from the Euphrates, as it appears from the following that the river is to be understood here.
