## 4:24
Verse 24. FROM THAPSA) In Hebrew, תפסח, undoubtedly that town which Pliny calls Thapsacus of old when he describes the Euphrates in book 5, 22.

TO GAZA] See Judges 1, 18.

AND ALL THE KINGS OF THOSE REGIONS)

Those kings were under the faith and protection of Solomon, and for that reason they paid a certain tribute. Verse 29. AND GOD GAVE SOLOMON WISDOM AND PRUDENCE ALSO) In Hebrew, what is rendered here as prudence is intelligence, as above 3, 12. See Deuteronomy 1, 13. Verse 30. THE WISDOM OF ALL THE ORIENTALS) That is, of the Arabs, who were already famous of old in every branch of philosophy. Now Arabia is to the east of Judea. See what was said at Matthew 1, 1. AND OF THE EGYPTIANS) Among whom the priests devoted exceptional effort to the knowledge of the stars, to mathematical arts, and to the knowledge of natural things. Verse 31. WISER THAN ETHAN THE EZRAHITE) Those who are named here as philosophers were sons of Zerah, grandsons of Judah, as appears in 1 Chronicles 2, 5. Whence it is credible that Machol is the name of an educated woman: and it should be read in the Chronicles, as here, דרדע. AND HE WAS RENOWNED AMONG ALL THE NATIONS ROUND ABOUT) Ecclesiasticus 47, verses 16, 17. Verse 32. SOLOMON ALSO SPOKE THREE THOUSAND PARABLES) That is, maxims, excerpts of which we have in the book of Proverbs, concerning the use of which word we have spoken at Matthew 13, 3, and in the Prolegomena to the sayings of the poets in Stobaeus. We shall say in its proper place that Solomon was not the inventor of all those maxims, but that they were collected from the writings of historians and poets. AND HIS SONGS WERE A THOUSAND AND FIVE) He was not only a philosopher, but also a distinguished poet. Understand songs such as those of Horace, or idylls such as those of Theocritus. Of those idylls of Solomon, one is what remains to us, which the Greeks would have called a song of songs, which the Hebrews call שיר השירים. Verse 33. AND HE DISPUTED ABOUT TREES) He treated the history of plants, and what will now follow, of living creatures, the excellent parts of nature.

Latin:

Vers. 24. A THAPSA) In Hebræo, תפסח, haud dubie id oppi- dum quod olim Thapsacum vocatum dicit Plinius ubi Eu- phratem describit libro 5, 22.

AD GAZAM] Vide Jud. 1, 18.

ET CVNCTOS REGES ILLARVM REGIONVM)

Erant illi Reges in Salomonis fide atque tutela, & ob id certi aliquid pensitabant. Vers. 29. ET DEDIT QVOQVE DEVS SAPIENTIAM SALOMONI ET PRVDENTIAM) In Hebræo, quod hic prudentia redditur est intelligentia, ut supra 3, 12. Vide Deuteron. 1, 13. Vers. 30. SAPIENTIAM OMNIVM ORIENTALIVM) Id est, Arabum, qui præclari jam olim in omni parte philosophiæ. Arabia autem ad Orientem Judææ. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 2, 1. ET ÆGYPTIORVM) Apud quos sacerdotes siderum cognitioni, mathematicis artibus, rerumque naturalium cognitioni eximiam operam dabant. Vers. 31. SAPIENTIOR ETHAN EZRAHITA) Qui hîc nominantur Philosophi, filii fuere Zaræ, nepotes Judæ, ut apparet 1. Paralip. 2, 5. Vnde credibile est Machol esse feminæ eruditæ nomen: & legendum in Paralipomenis, ut hic, דרדע. ET ERAT NOMINATVS IN VNIVERSIS GENTIBVS PER CIRCVITVM) Ecclesiastici 47. vers. 16. 17. Vers. 32. LOCVTVS EST QVOQVE SALOMON TRIA MILLIA PARABOLAS) Id est, γνώμας, quarum excerpta habemus in libro משלי, de cujus vocis usu diximus ad Matth. 13, 3. & in Prolegomenis ad dicta Poëtarum apud Stobæum. Dicemus suo loco γνώμας illas non omnes Salomonem habuisse repertorem, sed collectas ex historico rum & poëtarum scriptis. ET FVERVNT CARMINA EJVS QVINQVE ET MILLE) Non Philosophus tantum fuit, sed & poëta insignis. Carmina intellige qualia Horatii, aut Idyllia qualia Theocriti. Eorum Idylliorum Salomonis unum est quod nobis restat, quod ἀορισόν dixissent Græci, Hebræi שיר השירים vocant. Vers. 33. ET DISPVTAVIT SVPER LIGNIS) Tractavit historiam Plantarum, & quod jam sequetur, animantium, egregias naturæ partes.

## 4:29
Vers. 12. GOD ALSO GAVE WISDOM TO SOLOMON) Which shines forth most in the good management of friendships and alliances. AND BOTH STRUCK A COVENANT) For mutual benefits: whence they also called one another brothers; below 9, 12. Vers. 16. WITHOUT THE OVERSEERS WHO WERE OVER THE INDIVIDUAL WORKS) Who were three hundred. These, added to the number of three thousand three hundred, which follow here, make three thousand six hundred, as in 1 Chron. 11, 18. Vers. 18. FURTHERMORE THE GIBLITES) Phoenicians, who hold Gabala. Pliny names the promontory Gabalen in book 5, chapter 20.

Latin:

Vers. 12. DEDIT QVOQVE DEVS SAPIENTIAM SALOMONI) Quæ in amicitiis ac societatibus bene degendis maxime elucet. ET PERCVSSERVNT AMBO FOEDVS) Ad utilitates mutuas: unde & fratres alter alterum vocabant: infra 9, 12. Vers. 16. ABSQVE PRÆPOSITIS QVI PRÆERANT SINGVLIS OPERIBVS) Qui erant trecenti. Hi additi ad numerum ter mille trecentorum, qui hic sequuntur, faciunt ter mille sexcentos, ut 1. Paral. 11, 18. Vers. 18. PORRO GTBLII) Phœnices, qui Gabala tenent. Gabalen promontorium nominat Plinius libro 5. cap. 20.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V. The covenant of Solomon with Hiram concerning timber and workmen for the construction of the temple.

Verse 1. HIRAM KING OF TYRE ALSO SENT HIS SERVANTS TO SOLOMON) Concerning the letters and riddles exchanged between these kings, see what we have collected in the Annotations to the third book on the Truth of the Christian Religion. Verse 4. AND THERE IS NO SATAN) Adversary. The Septuagint translate this here as an opponent. Verse 6. THERE IS NOT IN MY PEOPLE A MAN WHO KNOWS HOW TO CUT TIMBER LIKE THE SIDONIANS) Because of the neighboring forests. Verse 8. MY SERVANTS SHALL BRING THEM DOWN FROM LEBANON) The material was carried from Mount Lebanon by rafts and towers. Curtius, book 4. Menander of Ephesus concerning this same Hiram: he went and cut a supply of timber, from the mountain called Lebanon, cedar wood for the roofs of the temples. TO THE SEA) Namely the internal one, which touches Phoenicia and Judea. For that is to be understood where the sea is named simply. Verse 7. GOD) In Hebrew it is יהוה. By this name the Tyrians, the Gentiles, and others also called the God of Israel: see below 10, 9. The gods of the Tyrians were Belsamen, whom the Greeks call Olympian Jupiter, Astarte, whom they call Venus, and Melicartus, whom they call Hercules.

It is gathered rather from this passage that Hiram, King of the Tyrians, had been converted to the God of Israel, inasmuch as he both acknowledged Jehovah and strenuously cooperated in the building of the temple. For it can be said that he was led to the true religion through his familiarity with David, as well as through the fame and celebrity of Solomon. This is the opinion of many interpreters.

Latin:

CAPUT V. Pactum Salomonis cum Hiram de lignis & operariis ad structuram templi.

Vers. 1. MISIT QVOQVE HIRAM REX TYRI SERVOS SVOS AD SALOMONEM) De epistolis & ænigmatis inter hos Reges mutatis, vide quæ congeffimus in Annotatis ad librum tertium de Veritate Religionis Christianæ. Vers. 4. ET NON EST SATAN) Adversarius. Ἐπίβολον hic vertunt LXX. ἀντικείμενον. Vers. 6. NON EST IN POPVLO MEO VIR QVI NOVERIT LIGNA CÆDERE SICVT SIDONII) Propter vicina nemora. Vers. 8. SERVI MEI DEPONENT EA DE LIBANO) Materies ex Libano monte ratibus & turribus faciendis vehebatur. Curtius libro 4. Menander Ephesius de eodem hoc Hiromo: ὕλην ξύλων ἀπελθὼν ἔκοψεν, ἀπὸ τῶ λεγομένε ὄρες Λιβάνε, κέδρινα ξύλα εἰς τὰς τῶν ἱερῶν σέγας. AD MARE) Nempe internum, quod Phœnicen Judæamque attingit. Id enim intelligendum ubi simpliciter mare nominatur. Vers. 7. DEVS) In Hebræo est יהוה. Hoc nomine etiam Tyrii gentes & aliæ vocabant Deum Israelis: vide infra 10, 9. Dii Tyriorum erant Belsamen, quem Græci Jovem Olympium vocant, Astarte, quam illi Venerem, Melicartus, quem illi Herculem.

Colligitur potius ex hoc loco, ad Deum Israelis conversum fuisse Regem Tyriorum Hiram, utpote qui & agnovit Jehovam & ad ædificationem templi strenue cooperatus est. Dici enim potest, eum per familiaritatem cum Davide, nec non per famam, & celebritatem Salomonis ad veram Religionem adductum. Quæ multorum interpp. est sententia.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI. The construction of the temple.

Verse 1. IN THE FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHTIETH YEAR OF THE DEPARTURE OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL FROM THE LAND OF EGYPT) Many think that the scribe erred in the number, and that the mark of four hundred was placed for five hundred. For it is established that forty years were spent in the desert places from the exodus: the leadership of Joshua lasted no less than seventeen years. From there to the election of the king, 450 years are to be reckoned, as Paul teaches us in Acts 13:16. Saul is believed to have reigned for almost twelve years: it is established from those things which are above in chapter 2, 11, that David reigned for forty years. Now Solomon's reign had lasted some years before he laid the foundations of the Temple. But let others, who have leisure, weigh these things more subtly. It often comes to my mind what I read in Plutarch in his Solon: ὧ μοι δοκῶ προσέσεσθαι χρονικοῖς τισι λεγομένοις κανόσιν ὃς μυρίοι διορθῶντες ἄχρι σήμερον εἰς οὐδὲν αὑτοῖς ὁμολογούμενον δύνανται καταστῆσαι τὰς ἀντιλογίας. Thus also I willingly leave the measurement and form of the Temple to be inquired into by others.

MONTH ZIV) This name of the month, as also Bul below in 38, is Chaldean. And by this it is proven that this book was written late, and perhaps by Jeremiah, as we have said elsewhere.

Grotius brings forward the opinion of those who think that the scribe erred in the number, and that the mark of 400 was placed for 500. And he praises Plutarch in his Solon here regarding chronological contradictions. But since we know that divine providence does not admit universal errors of all codices in the Sacred fountains, nor does divine truth and the infallibility of the sacred writers concede contradictions in the word of God, whether it treats of Chronological matters or any others, it is a matter of religion for us not to compare the divine scriptures with human writings, which are subject to errors, corruptions, and various falsities. Moreover, that there is no error in the number here is confirmed by the highest consensus of the Hebrews, the LXX Interpreters, the Chaldeans, and the Latin codices. Tisinus in his Sacred Chronicle, ch. 18, says that all sacred copies have it thus, even the Greek, the Hebrew, and all the interpreters of this passage, whom he says with one consensus agree with the S. Text, that Solomon began his temple in the 480th year from the exodus of the Hebrews, he observes. Nor is there any certainty in those who perhaps disagree. For Sabellicus and Melchior Canus set the years at 592. According to this calculation of Grotius, 563 years would result, because forty years were spent in the desert places; he attributes 17 to the leadership of Joshua, from there to the election of the King he thinks 450 years; he ascribes 12 years to Saul. David's years are 40. But the building began in the 4th year of Solomon. Nicolaus Serarius counts 580 years. In Josephus, others read with Canus and Ribera 592 years, others 612. What certainty is there here? But how those 480 years are to be calculated can be seen in Tisinus, loc. cit., and Corn. a Lapide on Judges 3:14, who follow here Arius Montanus, Adrichomius, Salianus, and Torniellus; indeed, in counting these years they have the Holy Scripture going before them. But Grotius is mistaken in that he thinks that the 450 years designated by Paul in Acts 13:20 are to be counted from the leadership of Joshua, which others calculate from the birth of Isaac up to the destruction of the Canaanites. As our own Dn. D. Walther in his Harm. Bibl. on Acts 13, as well as Lyranus, Jacobus Salianus, Tisinus, and the Belgian Interpreters, therefore join verse 20 with the words ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν in verse 17. Others, however, join it with the last words of verse 17 concerning the leading out from Egypt, from which time up to the death of Samuel 436 years are counted, which because of the round number can be called about 450, which opinion the aforementioned Belgian Interpreters likewise report. Lud. de Dieu does not approve of Junius's new interpretation from the Arabic translation, but teaches that it is foreign to that translation in his animadversions on the Acts of the Apostles. But he adds a calculation to the former opinion, which, because he explains it more conveniently than others from verse 20 itself in the aforementioned ch. 13 of Acts, I like to transcribe here. Altogether, he says, I agree with those who do not want the years during which the Judges ruled to be calculated here (for thus it seems impossible to reconcile these 450 years with the 480 which are said to have flowed from the exodus from Egypt to the beginning of Solomon's Temple, 1 Kings 6:1), but with those who calculate from the birth of Isaac up to the Judges, as if it were written: καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα πραχθέντα ἔδωκε κρίτας. So that it is not indicated how long the Judges ruled, but when God gave them; namely, after those things which had been narrated in verses 18 and 19, which were done in about 450 years. The calculation agrees. For from the birth of Isaac to the birth of Jacob there are 60 years, from there to the entry into Egypt 130, from there to the exodus 210, from there to the entry into the Land of Canaan 40, from there to the distribution of the land 7 years, which together make 447 years, that is, about 450; for only three are lacking. But that verse 17 is rightly referred to the time of the birth of Isaac: God chose our Fathers: For then God, who had already chosen Abraham from all the peoples of the earth, chose Isaac from all the children of Abraham, in whose family the covenant would consist, saying: In Isaac shall your seed be called. These things are from Ludov. de Dieu. More fully on these matters in the Sacred Chronicle.

Latin:

CAPUT VI. Fabrica templi.

Verf. 1. QVADRINGENTESIMO ET OCTOGESI- MO ANNO EGRESSIONIS FILIORVM ISRAEL DE TERRA AEGYPTI) Multi putant in numero errasse scri- bam, & notam quadringentesimi positam pro quingentesimo. Nam ab exitu quadraginta annos in locis desertis actos con- stat: Josuae principatus non minus feptendecim habuit annis. Inde ad regis electionem annos putandos 450. docet nos Paulus Act. 13, 16. Saul annos ferme duodecim regnasse credi- tur: Davidem annos regnasse quadraginta constat ex iis quae supra cap. 2, 11. Jam Salomonis regnum aliquot duraverat annos priusquam Templi fundamenta jaceret. Verum haec alii, quibus otium est subtilius expendant. Mihi saepe in mentem venit quod apud Plutarchum in Solone legi: ὧ μοι δοκῶ προσέσεσθαι χρονικοῖς τισι λεγομένοις κανόσιν ὃς μυ- ρίοι διορθῶντες ἄχρι σήμερον εἰς οὐδὲν αὑτοῖς ὁμολογούμενον δύνανται καταστῆσαι τὰς ἀντιλογίας. Sic & Templi mensu- ram atque formam libenter aliis inquirendam relinquo.

MENSE ZIO) Nomen hoc mensis ut & Bul infra 38. Chaldaicum est. Eoque convincitur sero scriptum hunc librum, ac forte ab Jeremia, ut alibi diximus.

ADducit Grotius eorum sententiam, qui in nu- mero errasse scribam, & notam 400. positam pro 500. putant. Et Plutarchum in Solone de contradi- ctionibus Chronologicis hic laudat. Sed quum sciamus, neque errores universales omnium Codicum in fontibus Sacris divinam admittere providenti- am, neque contradictiones in verbo Dei, sive Chro- nologica, seu quaecunque alia tractet, concedere di- vinam veracitatem, & Scriptorum sacrorum infalli- bilitatem, religio nobis sit Chronologicis humanis Scriptis, erroribus, corruptelis, falsitatibus variis obnoxiis divinas scripturas comparare. Non esse autem hic in numero errorem, consensus summus Hebraeorum, LXX. Interpp. Chaldaeorum, & Latino- rum codicum confirmat. Tisinus in Chronico Sacro c. 18. ita habere, ait, omnia exemplaria sacra, etiam Graeca, Hebraica, & omnes loci hujus Interpp. quos u- no consensu dicere cum S. Textu, Salomonem cepisse tem- plum fuum 480. anno ab egressu Hebraeorum, observat. Neque ulla est in iis, qui forte discrepant, certitu- do. Nam Sabellicus, & Melchior Canus annos po- nunt 592. Juxta hunc Grotii computum prodi- rent 563. anni, quia quadraginta anni in locis deser- tis acti; 17. Josuae principatui tribuit, inde ad Regis electionem 450. annos putat: Sauli annos 12. adscri- bit. Davidis anni sunt 40. Salomonis autem an- no 4. aedificatio cepit. Nicolaus Serarius numerat annos 580. In Josepho alii legunt cum Cano & Ri- bera annos 592. alii 612. Quae hic certitudo? Quo- modo vero computandi sint anni illi 480. videri poterit apud Tisin. loc. cit. & Corn. a Lapide ad Jud. 3, 14. qui sequuntur hic Ariemontanum, Adrichomi- um, Salianum, & Torniellum; imo in annis istis nu- merandis Scripturam S. praeeuntem habent. Falli- tur autem in eo Grotius, quod annos 450. a Paulo designatos Act. 13, 20. numerandos censeat inde a Jo- suae principatu, quos alii a nato Isaaco, usque ad de- letos Cananaeos supputant. Utpote e nostris in Harm. Bibl. Dn. D. Waltherus ad Act. 13. nec non Lyranus, Jacobus Salianus, Tisinus, Belgici Interpp. proinde conjungunt v. 20. cum verbis ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν v. 17. Alii vero conjungunt illum cum postremis verbis v. 17. de eductione ex Ae- gypto, ex quo tempore usque ad mortem Samuelis numerentur 436. anni, qui ob numerum rotundum circiter 450. dici possunt, quam sententiam referunt itidem praedicti Belgici Interpp. Junii novam ex Ara- bica translatione interpretationem non probat, sed ab illa translatione alienam esse docet Lud. de Dieu in animadversionib. ad Act. Apost. Calculum vero addit priori sententiae, quem quia commodius prae aliis ex ipso v. 20. in praedicto c. 13. Actorum explicat, ad- scribere hic libet. Omnino, inquit, assentior iis, qui hic annos, quibus rexerunt Judices, supputari nolunt (sicenim annos hosce 450. cum 480. qui ab exitu ex Ae- gypto ad Templi Salomonici initium effluxisse dicuntur 1. Reg. 6, 5. conciliare impossibile videtur) sed qui a nato Isaaco usq; ad Judices fluxere, quasi scriptum sit: καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα πραχθέντα ἔδωκε κρίτας. Ut non quam diu re- xerint Judices, sed quando eos Deus dederit, indicetur; nempe post ea, quae v. 18. 19. narrata fuerant, quae 450. circiter annis gesta fuere. Convenit computus. Nam a nato Isaaco ad natum Jacobum funt 60. anni, inde ad introitum in Aegyptum 130. inde ad exitum 210. inde ad introitum in Terram Canaan 40. inde ad distributio- nem terrae anni 7. qui simul faciunt 447. annos, id est, circiter 450. desunt enim solummodo tres. Recte au- tem ad nati Isaaci tempus refertur illud vers. 17. elegit Deus Patres nostros: Tum enim Deus, qui jam Abra- hamum elegerat ex omnibus terrae populis, ex omnibus Abrahami liberis elegit Isaacum, in cujus familia fae- dus consisteret, dicens: In Isaaco vocabitur semen tuum. Haec Ludov. de Dieu. De his uberius in Chronico sacro.

## 6:7
Verse 7.

AND THE HAMMER AND THE AXE AND EVERY IRON TOOL WERE NOT HEARD IN THE HOUSE WHILE IT WAS BEING BUILT) The Hebrews say the stones were split by a worm called שמיר, about which Maimonides wrote a special book. The fable does not deserve to be refuted. Lyranus, Abulensis, and Ribera, book 1, on the temple, chapter 12, rightly observe that in the house while it was being built, the hammer and the axe were not heard for hewing or cutting, because the stones had already been hewn or cut on the mountain.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET MALLEVS ET SECVRIS ET OMNE FERRA- MENTVM NON SVNT AVDITA IN DOMO CVM ÆDIFICARETVR) Ajunt Hebraei sissos lapides a verme di- cto שמיר, de quo specialem librum scripsit Maimonides. Fabula non meretur confutari. Lyran. Abul. & Riebera l. 1. de templ. c. 12. recte observant in do- mo cum aedificaretur malleum & securim non audita ad dolandum, vel secandum, quia jam in monte dolati, vel secti erant lapides.

## 6:12
Verse 12. THIS HOUSE WHICH YOU ARE BUILDING) That is, in this Temple which you are building I will perform my promises, for that is what follows: I will return answers from here: I will protect the Temple and the city, if you and your successors live and reign according to my law.

Latin:

Vers. 12. DOMVS HAEC QVAM ÆDIFICAS) Id est, in Templo hoc quod aedificas promissa mea, id enim sequitur, praestabo: responsa hinc reddam: Templum & urbem tue- bor, si tu successoresque tui secundum legem meam & viva- tis & regnetis.

## 6:18
Verse 18. AND THE WHOLE HOUSE WAS CLAD WITHIN WITH CEDAR) See what was said above at 2 Samuel 7, verse 2.

Vers. 18. ET CEDRO OMNIS DOMVS INTRINSE- CVS VESTIEBATVR) Vide quae dicta supra 2. Sam. 7. v. 2.

## 6:19
Verse 19. BUT THE ORACLE IN THE MIDDLE OF THE HOUSE) That is, this inner sanctuary was in the middle. Tacitus: The temple closed in the innermost parts.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ORACVLVM AVTEM IN MEDIO DO- MVS) Id est, intimum erat hoc penetrale. Tacitus: Tem- plum intimis clausum.

## 6:20
Verse 20.

AND THIRTY CUBITS IN HEIGHT) The sanctuary was ten cubits lower than the Basilica of the Temple. See above 2. Understand, however, thirty cubits without the side-chambers built one upon another. See 2 Chronicles 3, verse 4.

Vers. 20.

ET TRIGINTA CVBITOS IN ALTITVDINE) Erat adytum decem cubitis depressius Basilica Templi. Vide su- pra 2. Triginta autem cubitos intellige sine pastophoriis su- perstructis aliis super alia. Vide 2. Paralip. 3. vers. 4.

## 6:23
Verse 23.

TWO CHERUBIM] See what was said at Exodus 25, 18.

Vers. 23.

## 6:29
Verse 29.

AND HE MADE CHERUBIM IN THEM) Namely, carved ones, which the law does not forbid. See below 32 and Ezekiel 41, 18, 20, 25.

Vers. 29.

ET FECIT IN EIS CHERVBIM) Nempe caelatos, quod lex non vetat. Vide infra 32. & Ezechielem 41, 18. 20. 25.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAPTER VII. The construction of the Royal Palace and the house of the forest of Lebanon and the workmanship of those things which were necessary for the temple.

Latin:

CAPUT VII. Extructio Palatii Regii & domus saltus Libani & fabrica eorum, qua ad templum ne- cessaria erant.

## 7:2
Verse 2.

THE HOUSE OF THE FOREST OF LEBANON) What kind of forest this was can be learned from Jerome on Zechariah and on the Song of Songs. Likewise from Brocardus in his description of the Holy Land.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

DOMVM SALTVS LIBANI) Qui saltus qualis fuerit disci ex Hieronymo potest ad Zachariam & ad Canticum. Item ex Brocardo in descriptione Terrae sanctae.

## 7:8
Verse 8.

AND THE LITTLE HOUSE IN WHICH HE SAT TO JUDGE) In it the king sat almost enclosed, so that he might be safer from ambushes. Servius notes that the thrones of the ancient Latin kings were of such a kind.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ET DOMVNCVLA IN QVA SEDEBATVR AD JVDICANDVM) In ea rex pene clausus sedebat, ut tutior esset ab insidiis. Qualia fuisse & veterum Latinorum re- gum solia notat Servius.

## 7:13
Verse 13. HIRAM OF TYRE) Dwelling in Tyre. THE SON OF A WIDOW WOMAN OF THE TRIBE OF NAPHTALI) That is, of a Danite woman, but who was the widow of a Naphtalite. 2 Chronicles 2:14.

Latin:

Vers. 13. HTRAM DE TTRO) Habitantem Tyri. FILIVM MVLIERIS VIDVAE DE TRIBV NEPH- THALI) Id est, feminae Danitidis, sed quae vidua erat Nephthalitae. 2. Paralipomen. 2, 14.

## 7:15
Verse 15.

ONE COLUMN OF EIGHTEEN CUBITS IN HEIGHT) It was slightly lacking: for the material from which these columns were taken had a height of 35 cubits. 2 Chronicles 3:15.

It is not the case that I believe the precise quantity was neglected; because from a comparison of the parallel passage it is evident, that each column was exactly 17 and a half cubits, just as the writer of Chronicles explained, whose purpose it was either to add or to explain those things which in the books of Kings had either been omitted or handed down more obscurely, as Sanctius observes here. Vatablus and Ribera, in Cornelius, give this reason also, that in each column a half-cubit was inserted into its capital, and being hidden therein, did not appear. Cf. treatise on coins, ch. 14.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

DECEM ET OCTO CVBITORVM ALTITVDINIS COLVMNAM VNAM) Paulum deerat: nam materia un- de istae columnae sumtae erant, habebat in altum cubitos 35. 2. Paralip. 3, 15.

NOn est, ut praecisam quantitatem neglectam credam9; quia e collatione loci paralleli patet, quod exacte quælibet columna fuerit 17. cubitorum cum dimidio, prout sc. exposuit scriptor paralipo- menon, cujus institutum erat ea vel addere, vel ex- plicare, quæ in libris Regum vel omissa erant, vel obscurius tradita, observante hic Sanctio. Vatablus, & Ribera apud Cornel. hanc etiam rationem red- dunt, quod in utraque columna medius cubitus in- fertus fuerit suo capitello, in eoque absconditus non apparuerit. Conf. tract. de numm. c. 14.

## 7:16
Verse 16.

ONE CAPITAL OF FIVE CUBITS IN HEIGHT) Of which five cubits, three were adorned with figures, 2 Kings 25:17.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

QVINQVE CVBITORVM ALTITVDINIS CAPI- TELLVM VNVM) Quorum quinque cubitorum tres erant figuris ornati 2. Regum 25, 17.

## 7:25
Verse 25.

AND IT STOOD UPON TWELVE OXEN) This was against the Law, and therefore Josephus and the Hebrews here take it as the beginning of Solomon's faults. Others conjecture that a command of God, who is above the Law, had intervened.

It does not appear how this was against the law of God. For images of that kind were not prohibited in the law, but those which were set up for idolatry and served it. However, we have noted the ψευδερμηνείαν (false interpretation) of the divine law concerning images in Grotius, in the annotations to Exodus. There is no reason, therefore, why a fault should be invented here in Solomon along with the Jews, who, according to their custom, strain out gnats and swallow camels. Nor is there any doubt that such things were adorned by the command of God, because he had received from GOD the form of the temple and of the sacred apparatus of David: all things, he says 1 Chron. 28:19, came written by the hand of the Lord to me, that I might understand all the works of the pattern. For the inventions of the human heart do not please God in sacred worship, and in those things which pertain to worship, Is. 29:13, Matt. 15:8. For which end He Himself prescribed exactly all things which were to be prepared in the temple, and handed the pattern of them to David by His own hand, so that, namely, nothing might be devised according to one's own will, and that all ἐθελοθρησκεία (will-worship) might be prevented.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

ET STABAT SVPER DVODECIM BOVES) Hoc erat contra Legem, ideoque Josephus ac Hebræi hic sumunt initium culparum Salomonis. Alii conjectant, intercessisse jussum Dei qui supra Legem est.

Non apparet, quomodo hoc contra legem Dei fuerit. Non enim erant ejusmodi imagines prohibitæ in lege, sed quæ ad Idololatriam prosta- bant, eique inserviebant. ψευδερμηνείαν autem le- gis divinæ de imaginibus in Grotio, annotatis ad Ex- odum notavimus. Non ergo est, quod hic culpa fingatur in Salomone cum Judæis, qui pro more suo culices excolant, camelos deglutiunt. Neque dubium est, jussu Dei talia adornata, quia acceperat a DEO formam templi & apparatus Sacri David: omnia, inquit 1. Par. 28, 19. venerunt scripta manu Domini ad me, ut intelligerem universa opera exemplaris. Non enim placent Deo propriæ cordis humani adinven- tiones in cultu sacro, & iis, quæ ad cultum pertinent Es. 29, 13. Matth. 15, 8. Qua fini ipse omnia exacte præscripsit, quæ in templo paranda erant, & exem- plar eorum manu sua Davidi tradidit, ne scil. quic- quam excogitaretur ad proprium arbitrium, & ut omnis ἐθελοθρησκεία præcaveretur.

## 7:26
Verse 26.

IT HELD TWO THOUSAND BATHS] At the maximum it could contain three thousand: but it was not accustomed to be filled except to two thousand. 2 Chron. 4:5.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

DVO MILLIA BATOS CAPIEBAT] Ad summum poterat continere ter mille: sed non solebat impleri nisi ad bis mille. 2. Paralip. 4, 5.

## 7:29
Verse 29.

LIONS AND OXEN AND CHERUBIM) Engraved. Josephus interprets Cherubim here as eagles, but the figure of a man must also be added. For the Cherub consisted of these four. It is, however, a synecdoche. For a part of the Cherub is called a Cherub, just as the ox is a Cherub to Ezekiel 10:13.

CHAPTER XIII. The dedication of the Temple and Solomon's prayers, blessing, and sacrifices. Ver. 1.

THE ELDERS OF ISRAEL) In Hebrew: זקני. They are the senators of the great Sanhedrin.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

LEONES ET BOVES ET CHERVBM) Cælati. Che- rubim hic aquilas interpretatur Josephus, sed addenda & ho- minis figura. Ex his enim quatuor constabat Cherub. Est autem συνεκδοχή. Nam pars Cherubis Cherub dicitur, ut bos est Cherub Ezechieli 10, 13.

CAPUT XIII. Templi dedicatio & Salomonis preces, benedi- ctio & sacrificia. Vers. 1.

MAJORES NATV ISRAEL) In Hebræo: זקני. Ii unt senatores magni Synedrii.

## 8:2
Ver. 2. IN THE MONTH OF ETHANIM.

It is the month of Tishri, corresponding partly to September, partly to October; it is called Ethanim, or [the month] of the strong, either because in this month the fruits are strong, that is, mature and, together with the crops, are collected and stored in barns, by which the heart of man and life is confirmed and strengthened, as Vatablus explains, or because frequent feasts are celebrated in this month, by which God was worshipped by the strong and pious; as it seemed to others. But how was this dedication made in the seventh month, when the temple is said to have been finished only in the eighth month, ch. 6, last [verse]? Here it seems to be said that the dedication was postponed to the following year until the 8th day of the seventh month, when the dedication began for 14 days, so that it ended on the 23rd day of the same month, and the feast of tabernacles was included in those 14 days.

Latin:

Vers. 2. IN MENSE ETHANIM.

Mensis est Tisfri respondens partim Septembri, partim Octobri, dicitur Ethanim vel fortium, seu quia mense hoc fructus sunt fortes, id est, maturi ac cum frugibus collecti reponuntur in horrea, quibus cor hominis & vita confirmatur & roboratur, ut Va- tabl. explicat, seu quia crebra festa hoc mense cele- brantur, quibus a fortibus & piis Deus colebatur; ut aliis visum. Quomodo autem mense septimo hæc dedicatio facta, quum templum octavo mense demum perfectum dicatur c. 6, ult. Hic dicendum videtur dilatam fuisse dedicationem in sequentem annum us- que ad d. 8. Mensis septimi quo cepit dedicatio per 14. dies, ut finita sit 23. die ejusdem mensis, & inclu- sum fuerit 14. illis diebus festum tabernaculorum.

A CLOUD FILLED THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) A witness of divine presence and protection. Exod. 16, 10. 24, 15. 16. Num. 9, 15. Add Ps. 105, 38.

NEBVLA IMPLEVIT DOMVM DOMINI) Testis di- vinæ præsentiæ ac tutelæ. Exod. 16, 10. 24, 15. 16. Num. 9, 15. Adde Psal. 105, 38.

Ver. 27. THE HEAVEN AND HEAVEN OF HEAVENS CANNOT CONTAIN THEE) Virgil: All things are full of Jove. See also the beginning of Aratus. Lucan: Is there any seat of God except the earth and the sea and the air, and heaven and virtue? Concerning substantial omnipresence, see what we said in Vol. III, Syst. Theol. p. 614, seqq.

Latin:

Vers. 27. COELUM ET COELI COELORUM TE CAPE- RE NON POSSVNT) Virgilius: Jovis omnia plena. Vide & principium Arati. Lucanus: Estne Dei sedes nisi terra & pontus & aër, Et cælum & virtus? De substantiali omnipræsentia vid. quæ dixi- mus T. III. Syst. Theol. p. 614. seqq.

Ver. 30. WHATSOEVER THEY SHALL PRAY IN THIS PLACE] Therefore the Temple is called a house of prayer, Matt. 21, 13. Even in exile they prayed with their faces directed toward the Temple. Below 48. Dan. 6, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 30. QVODCVMQVE ORAVERINT IN LOCO ISTO] Ideo Templum dicitur domus orationis Matth. 21, 13. Etiam in exsilio Templum versus directa facie orabant. Infra 48. Dan. 6, 10.

## 8:31
Ver. 31. BECAUSE OF AN OATH BEFORE THY ALTAR) It is the custom of almost all nations to swear by touching the altar. Justin says in book 24, having taken the altars in their hands; in Plautus's Rudens: G. Touch this altar of Venus. L. I touch it. G. By this Venus you must swear. Cicero pro Flacco: If he were to swear holding the altar. Juvenal: Touching the altar and faith; and elsewhere: Fearless are all who touch the altars. Martial: Hannibal the boy had sworn this by the Libyan altars.

Latin:

Vers. 31. PROPTER JURAMENTUM CORAM AL- TARI TUO) Tacto altari jurare mos omnium prope gen- tium. Sumtis in manus altaribus ait Justinus libro 24. in Plauti Rudente: G. Tange aram hanc Veneris. L. Tango. G. Per Venerem hanc jurandum est tibi. Cicero pro Flacco: Si aram tenens juraret. Juvenalis: Tangens aramque fidemque; & alibi: Intrepidi quicunque altaria tangunt. Martialis: Hunc puer ad Libycas juraverat Annibal aras.

Ver. 35. IF THE HEAVEN SHALL BE SHUT UP) Compare these and the following with Deuteronomy 28.

Vers. 35. SI CLAVSVM FVERIT COELVM) Hæc & sequentia confer cum Devteron. 28.

Ver. 42. AND SHALL PRAY IN THIS PLACE) In the place set apart for the pious uncircumcised, which was distinguished from the places of the Israelites by an intervening breastwork. Josephus and the Rabbis mention it.
