Vers. 17. LOCVTVSQVE EST DOMINVS AD ME IN SERMONE DOMINI) Hebraice: Verbum ad me in verbo Domini: id est, præceptum mihi hoc est Dei no- mine atque imperio. Sic & verfu fequente: Angelus locutus est mihi in sermone Domini, id est, mandato.

## 13:19
Verse 19. HE DECEIVED HIM) And he himself. For he ought to have believed more in the revelation made to him, of which he was certain. Therefore it is said below in verse 22, he commanded you emphatically. When the deeds of praised men are not to be praised, as often as they are brought forward in Holy Scripture, something is usually added from which we may understand that it is not approved: which Plutarch also noted is accustomed to be done by Homer in his work On Reading Poets.

Latin:

Vers. 19. FEFELLIT EUM) Et ipse se. Magis enim de- bebat credere revelationi sibi factae, cujus erat certus. Ideo dicitur infra 22. praecepit tibi ἐμφατικῶς. Virorum laudato- rum facta non laudanda, quoties adferuntur in S. literis, so- let aliquid addi, unde intelligamus id non probari: quod & ab Homero fieri solere notavit Plutarchus de legendis Poetis.

## 13:24
Verse 24. A LION FOUND HIM IN THE WAY, AND KILLED HIM] God permitting it, partly so that the prophets might learn to obey commands strictly, partly so that Jeroboam might harden himself more and more in idolatry, and thus the justice of the punishments, which he had long since deserved, might appear more clearly.

Grotius therefore acknowledges, as I have already said, that Jeroboam committed idolatry while he worshipped God at the golden calves, and in them. How then will Papists be immune from idolatry, worshipping God before, or in images, or statues? And why does that little exception wish to help them, that they do not worship images as gods, but worship God in them, and before them? By which pretext even the Gentiles themselves are read to have used, as is found in Maximus of Tyre, Dissertation 38. For he says that the highest, first, and greatest God is worshipped by him in likenesses made of gold and silver and ivory. But what Grotius says here, that it was the mind of God that Jeroboam should harden himself more and more in idolatry, that is impious, nay, it cannot be excused from blasphemy. For whom he wished to be recalled from idolatry through legal sermons and the threats of the most severe punishments, how could he have wished him to harden himself more and more? Grotius is accustomed to gravely tax such blasphemies in the Calvinists who constitute God as the cause of sin, but now he himself is implicated in the same crime.

Latin:

Vers. 24. INVENIT EUM LEO IN VIA, ET OCCI- DIT] Deo id finente, partim ut Prophetae discerent distri- cte parere mandatis, partim ut Jeroboamus in idolatria ma- gis magisque obduresceret, & sic poenarum, quas pridem erat commeritus, justitia magis appareret.

Agnoscit ergo, quod jam dixi, Grotius Jero- boamum idololatriam commisiffe, dum apud vitulos aureos, & in illis Deum adoravit. Quomodo itaque ab idololatria immunes erunt Papistae, coram, vel in imaginibus, vel statuis Deum adorantes? Et cur eosdem juvare vult exceptiuncula illa, quod imagi- nes non adorent ut Deos, sed Deum in iis, & coram iis colant? qua προφάσει etiam gentiles ipsi usi legun- tur, ut est apud Maximum Tyrium Dissert. 38. Di- cit enim summum, primum & maximum Deum à se in simulacris ex auro & argento & ebore factis, coli. Quod vero Grotius hic ait, Dei mentem illam fuis- se, ut Jeroboamus in Idololatria magis magisque obdu- resceret, id impium est, imo à blasphemia excusari non potest. Quem enim ab Idololatria per concio- nes legales, & gravissimarum poenarum comminatio- nes, revocatum volebat, quomodo magis magisque obdurescere voluisset? In Calvinianis Deum cau- sam peccati constituentibus tales blasphemias gra- viter taxare solet Grotius, sed nunc ipse eidem im- plicatur crimini.

## 14:16
Vers. 16. AND HE MADE ISRAEL TO SIN) Cicero, 3 de Legibus: The more perniciously vicious princes deserve of the republic, because they not only conceive vices themselves, but infuse them into the state; and they are harmful not only because they themselves are corrupted, but also because they corrupt: and they do more harm by their example than by their sin. Xenophon, 8 of the Institution of Cyrus: For whatever kind the leaders are, such for the most part do those under them become. And they have become more shameless now than before in this regard. Papinius: And the camp is very like the king. Closest to our argument is Lactantius, book 5 of the Institutions, ch. 6: And since the manners and vices of the king are judged to be a kind of obedience, all cast aside piety, lest they seem to reproach the king's wickedness if they lived piously. Thus, corrupted by constant imitation, they abandoned divine law. Josephus here: The morals of the subjects are corrupted along with the ways of the leaders.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ET PECCARE FECIT ISRAEL) Cicero 3. de Legibus: Quo perniciosius de republica merentur vitiosi prin- cipes, quod non solum vitia concipiunt ipsi, sed ea infundunt in civitatem; neque solum obsunt, quod illi ipsi corrumpuntur, sed etiam quod corrumpunt: plusque exemplo quam peccato nocent. Xenophon 8. Institutionis Cyri: Ὁποῖοι γάρ τινες οἱ προστά- ται ὦσι, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ ὑπ' αὐτοὺς ἐπιτοπολὺ γίγνονται. Ἀδημο- σότεροι δὲ νῦν ἢ πρόσθεν ταύτῃ γεγένηνται. Papinius: Et castra simillima regi. Proxime ad nostrum argumentum Lactantius libro 5. Institu- tionum cap. 6. Et quoniam mores ac vitia regis imitari genus obsequii judicatur, abjecerunt omnes pietatem, ne exprobrare scelus regi viderentur, si pie viverent. Sic assidua imitatione cor- rupti, divinum fas reliquerunt. Josephus hîc: συνδιαφθείρεται τὰ τῶν ἀρχομένων ἤθη τοῖς ἡγεμόνων τρόποις.

## 14:21
Vers. 21. ROBOAM WAS FORTY AND ONE YEARS OLD WHEN HE BEGAN TO REIGN) Learned men think there is an error in the number, and that it should have been written 21, and they bring forward as an argument for their opinion 1 Kings 3:7, 1 Chronicles 22:5, ch. 10:8, ch. 11:17.

Who those learned men are, Grotius does not name, nor is it our business to investigate them laboriously. For thus far, I have found no one who has raised a scruple here regarding the Hebrew text. Nor from the passages which Grotius compares can I detect any reason for doubting, or attain the ἀγχίνοιαν (acumen) of those learned men. We see, however, again with what an itch he is afflicted to attack the Hebrew text, for which cause he seizes opportunities from everywhere.

SEVENTEEN YEARS HE REIGNED) He omits the current months. Compare below 15:1.

AND THE NAME OF HIS MOTHER WAS NAAMAH THE AMMONITESS) Who by her example and wicked instruction corrupted her son, after three years of his reign. 2 Chron. 11:17.

Latin:

Vers. 21. QVADRAGINTA ET VNIVS ANNI ERAT ROBOAM, CUM REGNARE COEPISSET) Putant vi- ri docti errorem esse numeri, & scriptum fuisse 21. afferunt- que in argumentum suæ sententiæ 1. Reg. 3, 7. 1. Paral. 22, 5. c. 10, 8. c. 11, 17.

QUinam viri illi docti sint, non nominat Gro- tius, nec nostrum est, illos operose indagare. Hactenus enim, qui scrupulum hic moverit in tex- tu Hebræo, inveni neminem. Nec è locis, quæ con- fert Grotius, ullam rationem dubitandi deprehen- dere possum, aut ἀγχίνοιαν virorum illorum docto- rum assequi. Videmus autem iterum, quanta pru- rigine laboret, incessendi textum Ebræum, cujus rei causa undecunque occasiones arripit.

DECEM ET SEPTEM ANNOS REGNAVIT) Omit- tit menses excurrentes. Confer infra 15, 1.

NOMEN AVTEM MATRIS EJVS NAHEMA AM- MANITIS) Quæ suo exemplo & prava institutione filium corrupit, post tres regni annos. 2. Par. 11, 17.

## 14:23
Vers. 23. ON EVERY HIGH HILL) After the manner of the ancient fathers, but against the law, the guardian of concord among the people, Deut. 12:5.

Latin:

Vers. 23. SUPER OMNEM COLLEM EXCELSVM) More patrum veterum, sed contra legem, concordiæ in po- pulo custodem, Deut. 12, 5.

## 14:24
Vers. 24. AND THERE WERE ALSO SODOMITES IN THE LAND) Catamites, which kind of wickedness by divine permission usually follows idolatry. Below 15:12. 2 Kings 23:7. Rom. 1:22, 23, 24, 25, 26.

Latin:

Vers. 24. SED ET EFFEMINATI FUERUNT IN TERRA) Catamiti, quod genus flagitii divino permissu plerumque idololatriam sequitur. Infra 15, 12. 2. Reg. 23, 7. Rom. 1, 2. 22. 23. 24. 25. 26.

## 14:25
Vers. 25. SHISHAK KING OF EGYPT) Sesoosis here according to Diodorus Siculus. Josephus thinks this is the one called Sesostris by Herodotus, who, according to the same Herodotus, subdued among other things Palestine Syria.

Latin:

Vers. 25. SESAC REX ÆGYPTI) Σεσόγχης hic Diodo- ro Siculo. Hunc Josephus putat ab Herodoto Sesostrin dici, qui teste eodem Herodoto, tum alia tum Palæstinam Syriam subegerit.

## 14:26
Vers. 26. ALSO THE SHIELDS OF GOLD WHICH SOLOMON HAD MADE) Above 10:16.

Latin:

Vers. 26. SCUTA QVOQVE AUREA, QVÆ FECE- RAT SALOMON) Supra 10, 16.

## 14:27
Vers. 27. INTO THE HAND OF THE CAPTAINS OF THE GUARD) Of the prefects of the runners in the Hebrew, who are in the LXX, the leaders of the runners.

Latin:

Vers. 27. IN MANUM DUCUM SCUTARIORUM) Præfectorum cursoribus in Hebræo, qui apud LXX. οἱ ἡγού- μενοι τῶν παρατρεχόντων.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAPTER XV. Pious Asa succeeds the impious Abijah: He fights against Baasha king of Israel, aided by Ben-hadad. He (Baasha) had killed Nadab and the whole family of Jeroboam.

Latin:

CAPUT XV. Abia impio pius Asa succedit: Contra Baesa re- gem Israel. pugnat, à Benadad adjutus. Ille (Baasa) interfecerat Nadab, & totam fami- liam Jeroboam.

## 15:3
Vers. 3. THE LORD GAVE HIM A LAMP) That is, He gave the kingdom to David even in his descendants. Compare above 11:36 and 4 Kings 8:19, 2 Chron. 21:7.

Latin:

Vers. 3. DEDIT DOMINUS EI LUCERNAM) Id est, regnum Davidi dedit etiam in posteris ipsius. Confer supra 11, 36. & 4. Reg. 8, 19. 2. Paral. 21, 7.

## 15:5
Ver. 5. AND HAD NOT TURNED ASIDE FROM ALL THINGS WHICH HE HAD COMMANDED HIM ALL THE DAYS OF HIS LIFE) He had indeed gone astray in some other matters, but he had not departed from the whole way of piety, except at that one time when he heaped murder upon adultery.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ET NON DECLINASSET AB OMNIBUS, QVÆ PRÆCEPERAT EI CUNCTIS DIEBUS VITÆ SUÆ) Exorbitaverat quidem & aliis rebus nonnullis, sed de tota via pietatis non decesserat, nisi uno illo tempore cum adulterium cæde cumulavit.

## 15:12
Ver. 12. AND HE PURGED ALL THE FILTH OF THE IDOLS) In the Hebrew, he took away all the idols, which idols indeed, because they defile the soul, are called in Hebrew גלולים.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PURGAVITQVE VNIVERSAS SORDES IDOLORUM) In Hebr. abstulit idola omnia, quæ quidem idola, quia impurant animum, Hebræis גלולים dicuntur.

## 15:13
Ver. 13. HE REMOVED HER FROM BEING PRINCESS IN THE SACRED RITES OF PRIAPUS AND IN THE GROVE WHICH SHE HAD CONSECRATED) More correctly thus: He removed her from the honor of Augusta, because she had made a terror in the grove. But because the form of Priapus was accustomed to be placed in the gardens of Greece and Italy, the interpreter therefore placed this word here from a similarity. He removed her from the honor of Augusta, i.e., he took away the military guards, as Nero did to his mother.

Latin:

Vers. 13. AMOVIT NE ESSET PRINCEPS IN SA- CRIS PRIAPI ET IN LUCO EJUS, QUEM CONSE- CRAVERAT) Rectius sic: Amovit eam ab honore Augustæ, quod fecisset Terriculum in luco. Quia autem in hortis Græ- ciæ & Italiæ poni solebat forma Priapi, ideo ex simili hæc vocem hic posuit interpres. Amovit ab honore Augustæ, i. e. excubias militares abstulit, ut matri Nero.

## 15:14
Ver. 14. BUT THE HIGH PLACES HE DID NOT TAKE AWAY) In the Hebrew, the high places were not removed. That is, he did not have enough authority and strength to remove this evil so widely diffused, although he himself (as follows) was very well disposed in the things of God. Sometimes it is better to omit prevailing and inveterate vices than to achieve this, that it becomes manifest to what scandals we are unequal, to use the words of Tacitus from Annal. 3.

Those things which are repugnant to God and his law, and are disapproved by the Holy Scriptures themselves, can be excused by no political reason, were. Cornelius would also gladly excuse, yet Asa finally agreed that he had sinned. But those high places are not the idolatrous temples of Solomon, but those which had been built on high mountains out of mere ἐθελοθρησκείᾳ (will-worship). Which Hezekiah and Josiah destroyed, and for that reason were celebrated by the Holy Spirit. Vers. 15. WHICH HIS FATHER HAD SANCTIFIED AND HAD VOWED INTO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) In the Hebrew: the sanctifications of his father, and the sanctifications of the house of the Lord. The meaning is: both what his father, and what he himself had vowed to the Temple. Vers. 17. THAT NO ONE MIGHT GO OUT OR COME IN FROM THE PART OF ASA KING OF JUDAH) That is, he blocked the exits from his kingdom into the kingdom of Asa, and from the kingdom of Asa into his own, namely so that those mutual dealings might not give his people an occasion to defect. Vers. 18. THEREFORE ASA TOOK ALL THE SILVER AND GOLD THAT REMAINED IN THE TREASURES OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) This usurpation of sacred things is excused by the fear of the greatest evil. See 1 Sam. 21. & on the Law of War and Peace, book 3, chapter 5, § 2, and chapter 21, § 23. Nor can these things be excused: indeed, Asa sinned both because he usurped and alienated the gold of the temple, and because he placed his trust more in the impious Benhadad than in the help of God. As is evident from 2 Chron. 15:1. HE SENT TO BENHADAD) The same name as Adad, and to others Ader, concerning which name we have treated above and in the third book on the Truth of the Christian Religion. Vers. 21. HE RETURNED TO THIRZA) So also the LXX: ἀνέστρεψεν εἰς Θερσὰ, with the points changed, so that it is from שׁוּב, not from ישׁב. Vers. 22. LET NO ONE BE EXCUSED) Where borders must be fortified against an enemy, all immunity ceases, l. ult. C. concerning which duties no one is allowed to excuse himself. Vers. 23. NEVERTHELESS) In the Hebrew it is only: i.e., he was free from diseases, except that in extreme old age he felt the gout. Vers. 28. AND HE REIGNED IN HIS STEAD) In the ten tribes many attained to the kingdom by force, not by succession. In the part of Judah no one reigned except by right of blood, according to the promises made to David. Vers. 33. IN THE THIRD YEAR OF ASA KING OF JUDAH) That is, in the third year after the war had been undertaken by him against Israel: for that must be repeated from the preceding. Compare 2 Chron. 16:1.

Latin:

Vers. 14. EXCELSA AUTEM NON ABSTULIT) In Hebr. excelsa non sunt remota. Id est, non satis auctoritatis viriumque habuit, ut hoc malum tam late diffusum tolleret, cum ipse (ut sequitur) in rebus Dei optime esset animatus. Interdum melius omittere prævalida & adulta vitia, quam hoc assequi ut palam fiat, quibus flagitiis impares simus, ut verbis utar Taciti ex Annal. 3.

EXcusari nulla ratione politica possunt, quæ Deo ejusque legi repugnant, & ab ipso S. S. impro- bantur. Excusaret etiam libenter Cornelius, an- nuit tamen tandem Asa peccasse. Excelsa autem illa non sunt templa Salomonis idololatrica, sed ea, quae in montibus excelsis e mera ἐθελοθρησκείᾳ ex- tructa erant. Quae Ezechias & Josias destruxere, ob id celebrati a Spiritu Sancto. Vers. 15. QUAE SANCTIFICAVERAT PATER SUUS ET VOVERAT IN DOMUM DOMINI) In Hebr. san- ctificationes patris sui, & sanctificationes domus Domini. Senfus est: tum quae pater, tum quae ipse Templo voverat. Vers. 17. UT NON POSSET QUISQVAM EGREDI VEL INGREDI DE PARTE ASA REGIS JUDA) Id est, exitus e suo regno in regnum Asae, & ex regno Asae in su- um obstruxit, nempe ne mutua illa commercia suis deficiendi occasionem darent. Vers. 18. TOLLENS ITAQVE ASA OMNE ARGEN- TUM ET AURUM, QVOD REMANSERAT IN THESAURIS DOMUS DOMINI) Excusatur haec rerum sacrarum usurpatio summi mali metu. Vide 1. Sam. 21. & de Jure Belli ac Pacis lib. 3. cap. 5. §. 2. & cap. 21. §. 23. Neque haec excusari possunt: imo peccavit Asa tum quod aurum templi usurpavit, & alienarit, tum quod magis in impio Benhadad, quam in auxilio Dei fiduciam collocarit. Ut e 2. Par. 15, 1. constat. MISIT AD BENADAD) Idem nomen quod Adad, & aliis Ader, quo de nomine egimus supra & ad tertium librum de Veritate Religionis Christianae. Vers. 21. REVERSUS EST IN THERSA) Sic & LXX. ἀνέστρεψεν εἰς Θερσὰ, mutatis punctis, ut sit a שׁוּב, non a ישׁב. Vers. 22. NEMO SIT EXCUSATUS) Ubi adversus ho- stem muniendi sunt limites, omnis immunitas cessat, l. ult. C. de quibus muneribus nemini liceat se excusare. Vers. 23. VERUMTAMEN) In Hebraeo est tantum: i. e. caruit morbis, nisi quod extrema aetate sensit podagram. Vers. 28. ET REGNAVIT PRO EO) In decem tribu- bus multi ad regnum pervenerunt vi, non successione. In Judae parte nullus regnavit nisi sanguinis jure, secundum pro- missa Davidi facta. Vers. 33. ANNO TERTIO ASA REGIS JUDA) Id est, anno tertio postquam ei susceptum erat bellum in Israelem: id enim repetendum ex superioribus. Conf. 2. Par. 16, 1.

## 16:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVI.

Jehu the Prophet, when he threatened Baasha with destruction, was killed by Ela, the son of the same: whom Zambri deprived of the kingdom and life, and being besieged by Amri, he burned himself with his house. Samaria was built by Amri. To whom, dying, Achab succeeded. Vers. 3. POSTERITY) That is, descendants. DOGS SHALL EAT HIM) Words repeated from the place which is above 14:11; in equal guilt, equal punishment. Vers. 7. AND WHEN THE WORD OF THE LORD HAD COME BY THE HAND OF JEHU THE SON OF HANANI THE PROPHET) You would translate better from the Hebrew: Namely, through Jehu the son of Hanani the word of God had been against Baasha and his house. The writer shows the prophecy fully fulfilled, concerning which he had begun to treat at the beginning of this chapter. FOR THIS CAUSE HE KILLED HIM, THAT IS JEHU THE SON OF HANANI THE PROPHET) Better in the Hebrew: and because he had struck him: namely, Jeroboam his king. For this crime also deserved punishment from God, since he had done it by no command of God. Nor did the LXX mean anything else: ὑπὲρ τοῦ πατάξαι αὐτόν. Vers. 8. ELA THE SON OF BAASHA REIGNED OVER ISRAEL IN THIRZA FOR TWO YEARS) Not full years, as we gather below in verse 10. Vers. 9. AND HE REBELLED) More correctly, he conspired. CAPTAIN OF HALF THE CHARIOTS) Rather, of the scythed chariots, of course. Those are most to be feared by kings who have soldiers beholden to them, such as the Prefects of the Praetorium, Masters of the soldiers, Masters of the Horse, and the like. DRINKING AND DRUNK) Such are the occasions especially that the slayers of kings or princes seize. See Dan. 5:30 and the slaughter of Gontharis in the second book of the Vandalic War by Procopius. You will see this counsel also given to Piso in Tacitus, Annals 15. Vers. 10. AND HE REIGNED IN HIS STEAD) For he had killed him for that reason alone. Vers. 11. HE STRUCK ALL THE HOUSE OF BAASHA) From that precept, which only tyrants approve: 'Foolish is he who, having killed the father, leaves the sons.' AND HIS KINSMEN AND HIS FRIENDS) The five nearest houses, as Philo says in the Life of Joseph it was the custom in those places.

Latin:

CAPUT XVI.

Jehu Propheta, cum minaretur Baasae exitium, occisus est ab Ela, filio ejusdem: quem Zam- bri regno & vita privat, ab Amri obsessus se cum domo succendens. Samaria ab Amri aedificata. Cui morienti successit Achab. Vers. 3. POSTERIORA) Id est, posteros. COMEDENT EUM CANES) Verba repetita ex loco, qui supra 14, 11. in pari culpa, par poena. Vers. 7. CUM AUTEM IN MANU JEHU FILII HA- NANI PROPHETAE VERBUM DOMINI FACTUM ESSET) Melius vertas ex Hebraeo: Nempe per Jehu filium Hanani verbum Dei fuerat contra Baasum & domum ejus. Ostendit scriptor impletam plane prophetiam, de qua agere coeperat capitis hujus initio. OB HANC CAVSAM OCCIDIT EVM, HOC EST JEHV FILIVM HANANI PROPHETAM) Melius in Hebr. & quod percussisset eum: nempe Jeroboamum regem suum. Nam & hoc crimen poenam a Deo merebatur, cum nullo Dei jussu id fecisset. Nec aliud voluere LXX. ὑπὲρ τοῦ πατάξαι αὐτόν. Vers. 8. REGNAVIT ELA FILIVS BASSA SVPER ISRAEL IN THERSA DVOBVS ANNIS) Non plenis, ut colligimus infra 10. Vers. 9. ET REBELLAVIT) Rectius conjuravit. DVX MEDIAE PARTIS EQVITVM) Imo curruum falcatorum scilicet. Metuendi regibus illi maxime, qui mi- lites habent sibi obnoxios, quales Praefecti Praetorio, Magistri militum, Magistri Equitum, & similes. BIBENS ET TEMVLENTVS) Tales praecipue occasio- nes captant regum aut principum percussores. Vide Dan. 5, 30. & Gontharidis caedem secundo Vandalicorum Procopii. Hoc consilium & Pisoni datum videbis apud Tacitum Annal. 15. Vers. 10. ET REGNAVIT PRO EO) Nam ob id solum eum occiderat. Vers. 11. PERCVSSIT OMNEM DOMVM BAASA) Ex illo praecepto, quod non nisi tyranni probant: Νήπιος ὃς πατέρα κτείνας υἱοὺς κατέλειπε. ET PROPINQVOS ET AMICOS EJVS] Quinque proximas domos, ut moris fuisse in illis locis ait Philo vita Josephi.

## 16:12
Vers. 12. AND ZAMBRI DESTROYED) God often uses even evil men against evil men to execute judgments.

Latin:

Verf. 12. DELEVITQVE ZAMBRI] Etiam malis ho- minibus in malos Deus sæpe utitur ad judicia exfequenda.

## 16:13
Vers. 13. IN THEIR VANITIES) In imaginary gods.

Latin:

Verf. 13. IN VANITATIBVS SVIS] In diis imaginariis.

## 16:15
Vers. 15. FURTHERMORE THE ARMY WAS BESIEGING GIBBETHON) Thus those who were in the city had made Otho their Prince, but the army made Vitellius; and when the city had received Vitellius, the army made Vespasian Emperor, and there are many such things in Roman History. And once the army destroyed the decemviral government. For at such a time there are as it were two cities, and the stronger part drags the weaker.

Latin:

Verf. 15. PORRO EXERCITVS OBSIDEBAT GEBBE- THON] Sic Othonem sibi Principem fecerant, qui in urbe erant, exercitus vero Vitellium: & cum Vitellium urbs rece- pisset, exercitus Imperatorem fecit Vespafianum, multaque ta- lia sunt in Historia Romana. Et olim exercitus destruxit de- cemvirale imperium. Sunt enim tali tempore quasi duæ civita- tes, & pars validior infirmiorem trahit.

## 16:16
Vers. 16. MADE HIMSELF KING) ἀντιβασιλέα (a rival king).

Latin:

Verf. 16. FECIT SIBI REGEM] ἀντιβασιλέα.

## 16:18
Vers. 18. HE BURNED HIMSELF WITH THE ROYAL HOUSE) Thus later the Saguntines kindle a pyre: then from above they destroy themselves and their own with all their wealth by sword and fire, says Florus. And after them the Numantines.

Latin:

Verf. 18. SVCCENDIT SE CVM DOMO REGIA] Sic postea Saguntini excitant rogum: tum desuper se suosque cum omnibus opibus suis ferro & igni corrumpunt, ait Florus. Et post eos Numantini.

## 16:19
Vers. 19. IN HIS SINS) In the Hebrew: because of his sins: and the LXX: ὑπὲρ ὧν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτοῦ. Well.

Latin:

Verf. 19. IN PECCATIS SVIS) In Hebræo: ob peccata sua: & LXX. ὑπὲρ ὧν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶ. Bene.

## 16:21
Ver. 21. THE PEOPLE OF ISRAEL WAS DIVIDED INTO TWO PARTS) Among the punishments which God inflicts upon contumacious peoples, division is not the least. Thus, from the whole Hebrew [kingdom] he had made a sixth and a ten-twelfths, now from the ten-twelfths two five-twelfths.

Latin:

Verf. 21. DIVISVS EST POPVLVS ISRAEL IN DV- AS PARTES) Inter pœnas, quas Deus infligit, contumaci- bus populis non minima est divisio. Sic ex asse Hebræo fecerat sextantem & dextantem, nunc ex dextante duas quincunces.

## 16:23
Ver. 23. IN THE THIRTY-FIRST YEAR OF ASA KING OF JUDAH, OMRI REIGNED OVER ISRAEL.

The people indeed acclaimed him in the 27th year of Asa, v. 15, 16, but because he had a rival, Tibni, with whom he contended for the kingdom for five years, only upon his death did he reign fully, and in the sixth year he transferred the royal seat from Tirzah, where Zimri had burned the palace with himself in it, to Samaria.

Latin:

Verf. 23. ANNO TRIGESIMO PRIMO ASA REGIS JUDA REGNAVIT AMRI SUPER ISRAEL.

Acclamavit quidem ei populus anno 27. Asæ, v. 15. 16. sed quia æmulum habuit Thibni, cum quo de regno per quinquennium contendit, eo demum mortuo plene regnavit, ac sexto anno è Therfa, ubi Regiam secum combustserat Zambri, sedem regiam in Samariam transtulit.

## 16:24
Ver. 24. AND HE BOUGHT THE MOUNT OF SAMARIA) Well: for the king possesses all things by imperial right, individuals by ownership, as Seneca says in book 7 of De Beneficiis, ch. 4. It follows concerning the king in ch. 6, that he can both receive a gift, and owe, and buy, and hire.

FOR TWO TALENTS OF SILVER) Today you would hardly buy a modest house for that much.

If a talent contained 3000 shekels, the mount of Samaria cost him that many thalers. Because a shekel is half an ounce, or half a Joachimicus. Exod. 30, 13. See what is said at 1 Chron. 22, 14.

Latin:

Verf. 24. EMITQVE MONTEM SAMARIÆ) Bene: nam omnia rex imperio possidet, singuli dominio, ut ait Seneca lib. 7. de Beneficiis c. 4. Sequitur de rege c. 6. & accipere mu- nus, & debere & emere & conducere potest.

DVOBVS TALENTIS ARGENTI) Hodie modicam do- mum ægre emas tanti.

Si talentum continuit 3000. Siclorum, tot tha- leris constitit ipsi mons Samariæ. Quia Sichus est dimidia uncia, vel dimidius Joachimicus. Exod. 30, 13. vid. quæ ad I. Paral. 22, 14.

## 16:25
Ver. 25. ABOVE ALL WHO WERE BEFORE HIM) Because he compelled the men subject to him to evil worships not only by example, but also by laws. Micah 6, 16.

Latin:

Verf. 25. SVPER OMNES, QVI FVERVNT ANTE EVM) Quia non exemplo tantum, sed & legibus homines sibi subditos coegit ad malos cultus. Mich. 6, 16.

## 16:31
Ver. 31. JEZEBEL) A woman both imperious and cruel. See Rev. 2, 20. Such was Tullia the wife of Tarquin, Fulvia of Antony, Eudoxia of Arcadius.

DAUGHTER OF ETHBAAL) Ἐιθωβάλῳ. Thus Menander of Ephesus writes this name in the Phoenician histories and the acts of the Tyrians.

HE SERVED BAAL) The sun, the primary god of the Sidonians.

Latin:

Verf. 31. JEZABEL) Feminam & imperiosam & crudelem. Vide Apoc. 2, 20. Talis Tullia Tarquinii uxor, Fulvia Anto- nii, Eudoxia Arcadii.

FILIAM ETHBAAL) Ἐιθωβάλῳ. Sic nomen hoc scribit Menander Ephesius in Phœnicicis, & acta Tyriorum.

SERVIVIT BAAL) Soli, Sidoniorum deo primo.

## 16:33
AND HE PLANTED A GROVE) Which was a custom for the Phoenicians and neighboring nations. For that reason it was forbidden by the law, Exod. 34, 13; Deut. 7, 5.

Ver. 33. AHAB ADDED IN HIS WORK) He surpassed his predecessors in impiety.

Latin:

AC PLANTAVIT LVCVM) Qui mos Phœnicibus, & vicinis gentibus. Ob id vetitus lege Exod. 34, 13. Deut. 7, 5.

Verf. 33. ADDIDIT ACHAB IN OPERE SVO) Im- pietate priores superavit.

## 16:34
Ver. 34. INTO THE HAND OF JOSHUA THE SON OF NUN) He preserved the Hebraism, as the LXX are accustomed to do for the most part. Otherwise it would have been clearer to say 'by Joshua'. The words are repeated from the book of Joshua 6:26, where see the things said. An excellent proof of divine providence.

Latin:

Verf. 34. IN MANV JOSVE FILII NVN) Servavit He- braïsmum, ut fere LXX. solent. Alioqui planius fuerat per Jo- suen. Verba repetita ex Josue libro 6, 26. ubi dicta vide Egregium providentiæ divinæ documentum.

## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII.

Elijah, after a drought is proclaimed, is hidden by the brook Cherith and fed by ravens; he multiplies the flour and oil of the widow of Zarephath, and restores her son to life.

Ver. 1. ELIJAH THE TISHBITE) He was a man of high spirit and a sharp defender of the laws, to whom (saving the privilege of piety and prophecy) I would compare Timoleon among the Greeks, and Scipio Nasica among the Romans.

God raised up Elijah so that he might repress the zeal of Ahab and Jezebel in propagating idolatry, and preserve some in Israel in the true faith; he was born in the village of Thesba in the tribe of Gad, situated between Jebaa and Saron, bordering on Arabia. The Hebrews wrongly make him Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron.

IF THERE SHALL BE IN THESE YEARS DEW AND RAIN) Three years and six months. James 5:17. The memory of this immense drought existed among Menander in his Phoenician histories, as Josephus testifies. There is such a description of time in a declamation of Quintilian, which is inscribed 'The Corpse Fed': No rain wiped the dust from the thirsty soil, no shadow of clouds hung over the parched fields. Hot winds blew.

EXCEPT ACCORDING TO THE WORDS OF MY MOUTH) The evil will begin at my imprecations, and will cease at my prayers.

James in the said place: for this reason he says he gives rain 18, 1. ἐπήγαγε λιμὸν says the son of Sirach 48, 2. which kind of manner of speaking you have also in Jeremiah 1, 10. and elsewhere.

Latin:

CAPUT XVII.

Elias indicta siccitate in torrente Carith abscon- ditus à corvis pascitur; Viduæ Sareptanæ farinam & oleum multiplicat, ejusque fi- lium in vitam revocat.

Verf. 1. ELIAS THESBITES) Vir fuit excelsi animi, & acer legum vindex, cui (salvo pietatis & prophetiæ privi- legio) inter Græcos Timoleontem conferam, inter Romanos Scipionem Nasicam.

ELiam suscitavit Deus, ut Achabi & Jezabeli ar- dorem in propaganda idololatria reprimeret, ac in Israele nonnullos in vera fide conservaret; o- riundum ex Thesba vico in tribu Gad inter Jebaa, & Saron sito, Arabiæ contermino. Quem perpe- ram Ebræi Phineen faciunt, Aronis nepotem.

SI ERIT ANNIS HIS ROS ET PLVVIA) Trienni- um & sex menses. Jac. 5, 17. Hujus ingentis ἀνομβρίας memo- ria exstitit apud Menandrum in Phœniciis, teste Josepho. Est talis temporis descriptio in declamatione Quintiliani, quæ in- scribitur Pasti cadaveribus: Nullus imber sitientis soli pulve- rem tersit, nulla supra arentes campos saltem umbra nubium pe- pendit. Calidi spirabere venti.

NISI JVXTA ORIS MEI VERBA) Ad meas impre- cationes incipiet malum, ad meas precationes definet.

Jacobus dicto loco: ideo dare pluviam se dicit 18, 1. ἐπήγαγε λιμὸν ait Sirachides 48, 2. quale genus loquendi habes & Je- remiæ 1, 10. & alibi.

## 17:3
Ver. 3. HIDE BY THE BROOK CHERITH) That is, παρὰ τῷ χειμάῤῥῳ, as Josephus rightly [notes] here.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ABSCONDERE IN TORRENTE CARITH) Id est, παρὰ τῷ χειμάῤῥῳ, ut hic recte Josephus.

## 17:4
Ver. 4. AND I HAVE COMMANDED THE RAVENS TO FEED THEE THERE) To a rapacious bird, above all. Thus God is accustomed to show himself as much the changer of nature as its artificer. Jerome narrates that the same thing happened to Paul the Hermit. Examples of those whom wolves, mares, hinds, and foxes have nourished are found among the poets and Aelian. To make us believe more that Aegisthus was raised by a goat, history provides the boy whom Procopius saw raised in such a way, and he narrates it in the second book of the Gothic War.

Latin:

Vers. 4. CORVISQVE PRÆCEPI VT PASCANT TE IBI) Rapaci imprimis volucri. Ita solet Deus ostendere se naturæ ut artificem ita mutatorem. Paulo eremitæ idem eve- nisse narrat Hieronymus. Quos lupæ, equæ, cervæ, vulpes aluerint exempla sunt apud Poetas & Ælianum. Ægisthum a capra educatum quo magis credamus, facit historia pueri quem sic educatum vidit Procopius, narratque Gothicorum secundo.

## 17:9
Ver. 9. IN ZAREPHATH OF THE SIDONIANS) Which is Sarepta in Pliny 5, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 9. IN SAREPHTHA SIDONIORVM) Quæ Sa- repta Plinio 5, 19.

## 17:15
Ver. 15. THE JAR OF MEAL DID NOT FAIL) God adding a hidden increase as in Matthew 14, 19; chapter 15, 36; and in places of the same subject matter.

SHE WENT AND DID ACCORDING TO THE WORD OF ELIJAH) A faith not different from Evangelical faith.

Faith is nothing other than Evangelical: because it arises solely from the Gospel, and faith is placed in Evangelical grace, the fruits and exercises of which are, when faith is applied to God in temporal promises, overflowing from a confidence in the divine grace announced in the Gospel. One faith, says the Apostle, Eph. 4, 5. Compare Acts 15, 11.

Latin:

Vers. 15. HYDRIA FARINÆ NON DEFECIT) Deo adjiciente incrementum latens ut Matth. 14, 19. c. 15, 36. & ejusdem argumenti locis.

ABIIT ET FECIT JVXTA VERBVM ELIÆ) Fides Evangelicæ fidei non dispar.

Fides nulla alia est, quam Evangelica: quia ex Evangelio unice oritur, & in Evangelicam gra- tiam collocatur fides, cujus fructus & exercitia sunt, cum in temporalibus promissionibus DEO fides adhibetur, redundans ex fiducia gratiæ divi- næ in Evangelio annunciatæ. Una fides, inquit Apostol. Eph. 4, 5. Conf. Act. 15, 11.

## 17:18
Ver. 18. WHAT HAVE I TO DO WITH THEE?) What harm have I done you? See John 2, 4.

THAT MY INIQUITIES MAY BE REMEMBERED) Because you are a Prophet, it is easy for you to find in every life something liable to punishment.

Latin:

Vers. 18. QVID MIHI TECVM?) Quid tibi nocui? Vide Joh. 2, 4.

VT REMEMORENTVR INIQVITATES MEÆ) Quia Propheta es, facile tibi est in omni vita aliquid reperire pœnæ obnoxium.

## 17:21
Ver. 21. HE STRETCHED HIMSELF) So also Elisha 2 Kings 4, 34. This contact had this purpose, that it might be known that not only did God do this, but that he did it on account of Elijah. See a similar instance in John 9, 6.

LET THE SOUL OF THIS CHILD RETURN, I PRAY THEE, INTO HIS INWARD PARTS) When grave vexations were impending on account of religion, God wished to reveal something more to the pious day by day, concerning the persistence of souls.

That was not indicated only then, but just as the immortality of the soul is established by the light of nature, so the resurrection of the dead was always believed in the Church, as is established by the Symbols of the Church, the faith of Job, and the testimonies of Scripture.

Latin:

Vers. 21. EXPANDIT SE) Sic & Elisæus 2. Reg. 4, 34. Hic contactus hunc usum habuit, ut sciretur non tantum Deum hoc facere, sed & facere propter Eliam. Simile vide Joh. 9, 6.

REVERTATVR, OBSECRO, ANIMA PVERI HV- JVS IN VISCERA EJVS) Cum graves imminerent vexa- tiones ob religionem, magis in dies piis aperire Deus aliquid voluit, περὶ τῆς τῶν ψυχῶν διαμονῆς.

Non id indicatum tum demum fuit, sed uti animæ immortalitas naturæ constat lumine, ita resurrectio mortuorum semper in Ecclesia credita fuit, ut e Symbolis Ecclesiæ, fide Jobi, & testimoniis Scripturæ constat.

## 18:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVIII. Elijah slaughters the Baalites and obtains rain and fertility by his prayers.

Latin:

CAPUT XVIII. Elias Baalitas mactat & pluviam ac fœcundita- tem precibus suis impetrat.

## 18:3
Ver. 3. OBADIAH) Here Ἀβδιὰ in the LXX, Ὠβαδίας in Josephus: and names vary everywhere.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ABDIAM) Hic Ἀβδιὰ LXX. Ὠβαδίας Josepho: & passim variant nomina.

## 18:4
Ver. 4. HE HID THEM BY FIFTY AND FIFTY IN CAVES AND FED THEM WITH BREAD AND WATER] Beneficence toward pious men must be exercised in every way even against the edicts of kings, because it is commanded by God, especially toward Prophets. Seneca says in De Beneficiis 3, 20, that servitude does not descend upon the whole man. There is a time when one may say: οὐ γάρ τί μοι Ζεὺς ἦν ὁ κηρύξας τάδε.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ABSCONDIT EOS QVINQVAGENOS, ET QVINQVAGENOS IN SPELVNCIS ET PAVIT EOS PANE ET AQUA] Beneficentia in pios viros omni mo- do etiam contra regum edicta exercenda est, quia a Deo præ- cipitur, maxime in Prophetas. Servitutem non in totum ho- minem descendere ait Seneca de Beneficiis 3, 20. Est ubi dicere liceat: οὐ γάρ τί μοι Ζεὺς ἦν ὁ κηρύξας τάδε.

## 18:7
Ver. 7. AND WHEN HE HAD RECOGNIZED HIM HE FELL UPON HIS FACE AND SAID] Namely, Obadiah venerating Elijah as a Prophet. Thus also the LXX: καὶ Ἀβδιὰ ἔσπευσε καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἀυτᾶ. Josephus wrongly thinks Elijah prostrated himself. For he says: μοιωθέντι δ' ἀυ ἀπὸ τᾶ βασιλέως Ὠβεδίᾳ, συνήντησεν ἀυτῷ ὁ προφήτης Ἠλίας· καὶ πυθόμενος παρ' ἀυτᾶ τις ἔιη, προσεκύνησεν ἀυτόν. ὁ δὲ πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα βαδίζειν ἐκέλευσε.

Latin:

Vers. 7. QVI CVM COGNOVISSET EVM CECI- DIT SVPER FACIEM SVAM ET AIT) Nempe Abdias Eliam ut Prophetam venerans. Sic & LXX. καὶ Ἀβδιὰ ἔσπευσε καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἀυτᾶ. Male Josephus Eliam purat procubuisse. Ait enim: μοιωθέντι δ' ἀυ ἀπὸ τᾶ βασιλέως Ὠβεδίᾳ, συνήντησεν ἀυτῷ ὁ προφήτης Ἠλίας· καὶ πυθόμενος παρ' ἀυτᾶ τις ἔιη, προσεκύνησεν ἀυτόν. ὁ δὲ πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα βαδίζειν ἐκέλευσε.

## 18:9
Ver. 9. WHAT HAVE I SINNED, HE SAYS, THAT YOU DELIVER ME YOUR SERVANT INTO THE HAND OF AHAB, THAT HE MAY KILL ME] We ought to use our liberty in such a way that it does not harm others. See 1 Cor. 10:24.

Latin:

Vers. 9. QVID PECCAVI, INQVIT, QVONIAM TRADIS ME SERVVM TVVM IN MANV ACHAB, VT INTERFICIAT ME] Libertate nostra sic uti debe- mus, ne ea obsit aliis. Vide 1. Cor. 10, 24.

## 18:12
Ver. 12. THE SPIRIT OF THE LORD WILL CARRY YOU AWAY] That is, will command you to go elsewhere, just as it is said in Matt. 4:1, ἀνήχθη ὑπὸ τᾶ πνεύματος. Josephus in this place: ἐυλαβέῖσθαι ἀυτὸν ἔφασκε, μὴ τᾶ θεᾶ φανέντος ἀυτῷ πάλιν ἐις ἄλλον ἀπέλθοι τόπον.

BUT YOUR SERVANT FEARS THE LORD FROM HIS YOUTH) Do not think me to be such as the others of our court. There is a time even for speaking true things about oneself.

Latin:

Vers. 12. SPIRITVS DOMINI ASPORTABIT TE) Id est, imperabit tibi ut eas alio, quomodo ἀνήχθη ὑπὸ τᾶ πνεύ- ματος dicitur Matth. 4, 1. Josephus hoc loco: ἐυλαβέῖσθαι ἀυτὸν ἔφασκε, μὴ τᾶ θεᾶ φανέντος ἀυτῷ πάλιν ἐις ἄλλον ἀπέλθοι τόπον.

SERVVYS AVTEM TVVS TIMET DOMINVM AB INFANTIA SVA) Noli me putare talem esse, quales cæteri aulæ nostræ. Est aliquod tempus etiam de se vera prædi- candi.

## 18:15
Ver. 15. THE LORD OF HOSTS LIVES BEFORE WHOSE FACE I STAND, THAT TODAY I WILL APPEAR TO HIM] Thus Tiresias to King Oedipus in Sophocles:

Εἰ καὶ τυραννεῖς, ἐξισωτέον τὸ γοῦν Ἴσ᾽ ἀντιλέξαι· τῦ δὲ γὰρ κἀγὼ κρατῶ. Οὐ γάρ τί σοι ζῶ δοῦλος, ἀλλὰ Λοξίᾳ.

Latin:

Vers. 15. VIVIT DOMINVS EXERCITVVM ANTE CVJVS VVLTUM STO, QVIA HODIE APPAREBO EI] Sic Tiresias Oedipodi regi apud Sophoclem:

Εἰ καὶ τυραννεῖς, ἐξισωτέον τὸ γοῦν Ἴσ᾽ ἀντιλέξαι· τῦ δὲ γὰρ κἀγὼ κρατῶ. Οὐ γάρ τί σοι ζῶ δοῦλος, ἀλλὰ Λοξίᾳ.

## 18:17
Ver. 17. ARE YOU HE THAT TROUBLES ISRAEL?) Josephus: ὁ τὸν Ἑβραίων λαὸν κακώσας. But the LXX: εἰ σὺ εἶ αὐτὸς ὁ διατρέφων τὸν Ἰσραήλ. Which very word the priests use against our Lord in Luke 23:2.

Latin:

Vers. 17. TVNE ES ILLE QVI CVNTVRBAS ISRA- EL?) Josephus: ὁ τὸν Ἑβραίων λαὸν κακώσας. At LXX. εἰ σὺ εἶ αὐτὸς ὁ διατρέφων τὸν Ἰσραήλ. Qua ipsa voce in Do- minum nostrum utuntur Sacerdotes Luc, 23. v. 2.

## 18:18
Ver. 18. I HAVE NOT TROUBLED ISRAEL, BUT YOU) Πόλεως δ᾽ ἁπάσης κύριον᾽ εἶ, πειθοῖς δ᾽ ἔτι Νόμοισι. Euripides says in Erechtheus. But if this is true of the laws which men have given, how much more of those which God has given? He who violates these, not he who defends them, troubles the republic. Especially, as Maecenas says in Dio, οἱ καινά τινα δαιμόνια ἀντεισφέροντες πολλοὺς ἀναπείθουσιν ἀλλοτριονομεῖν.

Latin:

Vers. 18. NON EGO TVRBAVI ISRAEL, SED TV) Πόλεως δ᾽ ἁπάσης κύριον᾽ εἶ, πειθοῖς δ᾽ ἔτι Νόμοισι. Ait in Erechtheo Euripides, Quod si verum de legibus quas homines dedere, quanto magis de iis quas Deus dedit? Hac qui violat, non qui tuetur, turbat rempublicam. Præcipue ve- το οἱ καινά τινα δαιμόνια ἀντεισφέροντες πολλοὺς ἀναπείθου- σιν ἀλλοτριονομεῖν ait apud Dionem Mæcenas.

## 18:19
ver. 19. AND THE PROPHETS OF THE GROVES FOUR HUNDRED.

Elijah summoned these no less than the Baalites: and although mention is made only of the latter thereafter, there is no doubt, however, that all the false prophets were brought at the will of the Prophet, even the priests of the groves, friends of Jezebel: all of whom he desired to be killed, not without divine instinct. But only the Baalites are named afterwards, as the chief among them: yet in ch. 19, 1, it is openly said that ALL were killed whom Jezebel maintained.

Latin:

vers. 19. PROPHETASQUE LVCORUM QVADRINGENTOS.

Hos accersivit Elias non minus quam Baalitas: & licet horum deinceps solum mentio fiat, dubium tamen non est, quin ad voluntatem Pro- phetæ omnes adducti fuerint Pseudo-Prophetæ, etiam lucorum Sacerdotes Jesabeli amici: qui omnes interfectos cupiebat, non sine instinctu di- vino. Nominati autem solum postea Baalitæ sunt, ceu præcipui eorum: at c. 19, 1. aperte OMNES interfecti dicuntur, quos aluit Jesabel.

## 18:21
Vers. 21.

HOW LONG DO YOU HALT BETWEEN TWO OPINIONS?) Which the Greeks would call ἐπαμφοτερίζετε. One must decide once and for all how one is to live. Otherwise, one is always wavering.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

USQVEQVO CLAVDICATIS IN DUAS PARTES?) Quod Græci dicerent ἐπαμφοτερίζετε. Semel constituendum est quomodo vivendum sit. Alioqui semper fluctuatur.

## 18:24
Vers. 24.

AND THE GOD WHO SHALL ANSWER BY FIRE, HE BE GOD) God is accustomed, where a new religion is to be instituted, as in the time of Moses and Christ, or where some general depravity has invaded religion, to use miracles. See below 36.

God thus answers by fire sent from heaven Abel Gen. 4, 5. Noah Gen. 8, 21. Abraham ch. 15, 17. Aaron Lev. 9, 24. Gideon Jud. 6, 21. Manoah ch. 13, 20. David 1 Chron. 22, 26. Solomon 2 Chron. 7, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

ET DEUS QVI EXAUDIERIT PER IGNEM, IPSE SIT DEUS) Solet Deus ubi nova religio instituenda est, ut Mosis & Christi tempore, aut ubi generalis quædam deprava- tio religionem invasit, uti miraculis. Vide infra 36.

Exaudit ita per ignem cœlitus demissum Deus Abelem Gen. 4, 5. Noachum Gen. 8, 21. Abraha- mum c. 15, 17. Aaronem Lev. 9, 24. Gideonem Jud. 6, 21. Manoe c. 13, 20. Davidem 1. Par. 22, 26. Salomonem 2. Par. 7, 1.

## 18:26
Vers. 26. AND THEY LEAPED UPON THE ALTAR WHICH THEY HAD MADE) עשׂו for עשׂו an enallage: LXX. and they ran upon the altar which they made. The sense is: they danced around the altars, like the Salii. Such also is that in the Epigram: Come to the glorious precinct of grey-eyed Hera, O Lesbian women, planting your delicate steps, where you shall form a beautiful dance for the goddess; and Sappho shall lead you, holding a golden lyre in her hands.

Latin:

Vers. 26. TRANSILIEBANTQVE ALTARE QVOD FECERANT) עשׂו pro עשׂו enallage: LXX. καὶ διέτρε- χον ἐπὶ τῷ θυσιαςηρίῳ ᾧ ἐποίησαν. Sensus est: saltabant cir- cum altaria, ut Salii. Tale & illud in Epigrammate: Ελθετε πρὸς τέμενος γλαυκώπιδος ἀγλαὸν Ἥρας Λεσβίδες, ἁβρὰ ποδῶν βήματ᾽ ἐρεισάμεναι, Ἔνθα καλὸν σήσασθε θεᾷ χορόν· ὔμμι δ᾽ ἐπάρξει Σαπφὼ, χρυσείην χερσὶν ἔχουσα λύρην.

## 18:27
Vers. 27. CRY WITH A LOUDER VOICE) A not unjust mockery against men who are enemies of true piety and corrupters of the people.

Latin:

Vers. 27. CLAMATE VOCE MAJORE) Διασυρμὸς non iniquus in homines veræ pietatis hostes, populi corruptores.

## 18:28
Vers. 28. THEY CUT THEMSELVES AFTER THEIR MANNER WITH KNIVES AND LANCETS) Martial: The arms are lacerated with less savage knives, when the inspired crowd rages to Phrygian modes. See Deut. 14, 1, and what is said there.

Latin:

Vers. 28. INCIDEBANT SE JUXTA RITUM SVVM CVLTRIS ET LANCEOLIS) Martialis: Alba minus sævis lacerantur brachia cultris, Cum furit ad Phrygios enthea turba modos. Vide Deuter. 14, 1. & ibi dicta.

## 18:29
Vers. 29. AND WHILE THEY WERE PROPHESYING) Which the Greeks would call φοιβαζόντων αὐτῶν.

While they were reciting their solemn prayers and songs, which they were accustomed to use in praise of their god Baal. Conf. 1 Chron. 26, 3.

Latin:

Vers. 29. ET ILLIS PROPHETANTIBVS) Quod Græ- ci dicerent φοιβαζόντων αὐτῶν.

Illis recitantibus solemnes suas preces, & canti- ca, quæ in laudem Dei sui Baal adhibere consue- verant. Conf. 1. Par. 26, 3.

## 18:31
Vers. 31. AND HE TOOK TWELVE STONES ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF THE TRIBES OF THE SONS OF JACOB) Showing that the whole people ought to be contained by one bond of religion.

verse same. TO WHOM THE WORD OF THE LORD WAS MADE SAYING, ISRAEL SHALL BE THY NAME.

By the word of the Lord which spoke these things, or said, nothing can be understood except the ὁ λόγος ὑποστατικὸς the Son of God, John 1:3. Compare Gen. 32:28.

Latin:

Vers. 31. ET TVLIT DVODECIM LAPIDES JV- XTA NVMERVM TRIBVVM FILIORVM JACOB) Ostendens omnem populum uno contineri debere religionis vinculo.

vers. eod. AD QUEM FACTUS EST SER- MO DOMINI DICENS, ISRAEL ERIT NO- MEN TUUM.

Per verbum Domini quod hæc loquutum est, vel dixit, non intelligi potest, nisi ὁ λόγος ὑποστατικὸς Filius Dei, Joh. 1, 3. Conf. Gen. 32, 28.

## 18:32
Verse 32. AND HE BUILT AN ALTAR OF STONES) By prophetic right, released from lesser laws, so that he might observe the greater ones.

Not by his own will or choice, but by θεοπνευσία did Elijah do this, or by the inspiration of the Lord, by whose Spirit he was led. Above in v. 30 he is said to have healed the altar, that is, to have restored it, which had been done: now in the verse it is explained how it was restored, namely by using 12 stones from which 4 were made as it were walls, but the middle cavity was filled with earth, according to

Exod. 20:20. Compare below v. 38. The altar, however, was either built there previously by the Prophets under the inspiration of God, but broken down by the impious Israelite Kings, or it was built a little while before by Elijah, upon which the Baalites leaped, and which they broke down: which opinion of Sanctius is not improbable.

verse same. AND HE MADE A WATER CONDUIT AS IF FOR TWO FURROWS.

In Hebrew, according to the measure of two seahs of seed, which some understand as the space that two seahs of grain, when sown, are accustomed to occupy, along with Abulensis, Lyranus, Cajetan, and Sanctius: but in that way this channel would have been larger than the channel of the Tiber or the Rhine, as Cornelius warns: who therefore makes the small area excavated around the altar such that it could hold two seahs, that is, two modii of seed.

Latin:

Vers. 32. ET ÆDIFICAVIT DE LAPIDIBVS ALTA- RE) Jure Prophetico minoribus legibus exsolutus, ut majo- res servaret.

Non ex propria voluntate, aut arbitrio, sed e θεοπνευσίᾳ hoc fecit Elias, vel inspirante Domino, cujus Spiritu agebatur. Superius v. 30. sanasse altare, id est, redintegrasse dicitur, quod factum erat: jam v. explicatur, quomodo redintegratum fuerit, nimi- rum adhibitis 12. lapidibus e quibus 4. quasi parietes facti, media autem concavitas terra repleta est, juxta

Exod.20,20. Conf. infra v.38. Altare autem ibi vel a Prophetis antea instinctu Dei extructum fuit, ab im- piis vero Regibus Israeliticis confractum, vel paulo ante ædificatum ab Elia, in quod Baalitæ insilie- rint, idque confregerint: Quæ Sanctii sententia non improbabilis.

vers. eod. FECITQVE AQVÆ DUCTUM QUASI PER DUAS ARATIUNCULAS.

In Ebr. secundum mensuram duorum satorum seminis, quod nonnulli de tanto spatio intelligunt, quantum occupare solent duo sata frumenti nimi- rum seminata, cum Abulensi, Lyrano, Cajetano, San- ctio: sed ita alveus hic major fuisset alveo Tiberis, vel Rheni, monente Cornelio: qui proinde areolam cir- ca altare excavatam tantam facit, cum Vatablo, quæ capere potuerit duo sata, id est, duos modios seminis.

## 18:38
Verse 38. AND THE FIRE OF THE LORD FELL) Julian: πῦρ γὰρ, φησιν, ὀ κάτεισιν ὥσπερ ἐπὶ Μωσέως τὰς θυσί- ας ἀναλίσκον. For fire, he says, which comes down just as it did in the time of Moses, consuming the sacrifices. This happened once in the time of Moses, and again in the time of Elijah the Tishbite after many years. See what we have said at Gen. 4, v. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 38. CECIDIT AUTEM IGNIS DOMINI) Julia- nus: πῦρ γὰρ, φησιν, ὀ κάτεισιν ὥσπερ ἐπὶ Μωσέως τὰς θυσί- ας ἀναλίσκον. ἅπαξ τοῦτο ἐπὶ Μωσέως ἐγένετο, καὶ ἐπὶ Ἡλίου τοῦ Θεσβίτου πάλιν μετὰ πολλοὺς χρόνους. Vide quæ diximus ad Gen. 4. v. 5.

## 18:40
Verse 40.

HE SLEW THEM THERE) He ordered them to be slain as law-breakers.

This was not done according to the ordinary constitution of the law concerning the killing of false prophets, Deut. 13:9; for this belonged to the political magistrate; but by an extraordinary heroic impulse and a singular inspiration of the Holy Spirit: which example, therefore, is not to be drawn into a rule. Whether, however, all the prophets of Baal and of the groves were killed is doubtful. But because Elijah ordered all to be summoned, and in chapter 19:1 he is said to have killed them all absolutely (even if in the German version a restriction concerning the Baalites is added, that is not found in the sources), we believe, with Basil in Homily 20 on anger, Brentius, and Cornelius, that the prophets of the groves were also killed.

Latin:

Vers. 40.

INTERFECIT EOS IBI) Jussit interfici ut legirupas.

Non hoc factum secundum ordinariam legis constitutionem de Pseudo-Prophetis occidendis Deut. 13. v. 9. hæc enim ad Magistratum Politicum pertinebat; sed heroico extraordinario motu, & sin- gulari S. S. instinctu: quod proinde exemplum non trahendum in Regulam. Num autem omnes & Baalis, & lucorum Prophetæ occisi, dubium est. Sed quia Elias omnes convocari jussit, & cap. 19, 1. absolute omnes occidisse dicitur (etsi in German. addatur restrictio de Baalitis, ea tamen in fontibus non habetur,) cum Basilio hom. 20. de ira, Bren- tio, Cornel. etiam luci Prophetas occisos censemus.

## 18:42
Verse 42.

AND BOWED DOWN TO THE EARTH HE PUT HIS FACE BETWEEN HIS KNEES] About to obtain rain through prayers. Similar is that in Tertullian against Scapula: Marcus Aurelius also, in the German expedition, obtained rain during that drought through the prayers made to God by Christian soldiers.

Latin:

Vers. 42.

ET PRONUS IN TERRAM POSVIT FACIEM IN- TER GENUA SUA] Precibus imbrem impetraturus. Simile illud apud Tertullianum contra Scapulam: Marcus quoque Aurelius in Germanica expeditione Christianorum militum orationibus ad Deum factis, imbres in siti illa impetravit.

## 18:46
Verse 46.

Verse 46. AND THE HAND OF THE LORD WAS UPON ELIJAH] That is, God gave him strength for running greater than human strength.

Latin:

Vers. 46.

Vers. 46. MANUS AVTEM DOMINI FACTA EST SUPER ELIAM] Id est, Deus illi ad currendum vires hu- manis majores dedit.

## 19:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIX.

GOD appears to Elijah fleeing because of Jezebel: He commands Hazael to be anointed, and Jehu, and Elisha: whom he soon took up for the ministry.

Latin:

CAPUT XIX.

Ob Jezabelem fugienti Eliæ apparet DEUS: Hasaelem ungi jubet, & Jehu, ac Elisæum: quem mox ad ministerium affumsit.

## 19:3
Ver. 3. AND ARISING HE WENT) For there is also a time for flight. See what was said at Matt. 4, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET SURGENS ABIIT) Est enim & fugæ tem- pus. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 4, 12.

## 19:5
AND HE FELL ASLEEP IN THE SHADE OF A JUNIPER TREE) Careless of his health. For the shade of the juniper is heavy, as Maro [Virgil] testifies.

But he requested that his soul be taken away: lest, being overcome and defeated by Jezebel, the true religion of God might seem to be defeated with him.

Latin:

ET OBDORMIVIT IN UMBRA JUNIPERI) Valetu- dinis incuriosus. Nam Juniperi gravis umbra. Marone teste.

PEtiit autem ut anima sua auferatur: ne a Je- zabele superatus & victus & cum ipso vera Dei religio victa videretur.

## 19:6
Ver. 6. ASH-CAKE AND A VESSEL OF WATER) God commends frugality by this example. The river and Ceres are enough for the peoples, says Lucan.

Latin:

Vers. 6. SUBCINERICIUS PANIS ET VAS AQVÆ) Frugalitatem hoc exemplo commendat Deus. Satis est populis fluviusque Ceresque, ait Lucanus.

## 19:8
Ver. 8. FORTY DAYS) By the example of Moses, Exod. 34, 28. See what [was said] at Matt. 4, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 8. QVADRAGINTA DIEBUS) Mosis exemplo Exod. 34, 28. Vide quæ ad Matth. 4, 2.

## 19:10
ver. 10. THEY HAVE DESTROYED THINE ALTARS.

By altars is understood metonymically the worship of GOD. For in Israel there were no altars, but only in Jerusalem. Even if it be conceded that in the kingdom of Israel some kept the statutes of the Lord, others the statutes of Jeroboam, it is not therefore to be concluded, with Cloppenburg in Schol. Sacrif. p. 155, that altars dedicated to GOD existed there, upon which the faithful offered, or that the priests of 1 Kings 12, v. 31, who were not of the sons of Levi, the true worshippers of GOD, served: for these could not be held as true priests, nor are altars or offerings in the high places either approved as being to GOD, or is such ἀνομία (lawlessness) of offerings rightly believed to be overlooked by GOD on account of the λῆμμα (taking/remnant) of the elect: because the elect themselves abhorred such ἐθελοθρησκείας (will-worship), and offered their sacrifices in Jerusalem, or remained in hiding, as in the time of Elijah.

Ver. same. THEY HAVE KILLED THY PROPHETS WITH THE SWORD) Whom they know to be such. For those hundred of whom [we spoke] above 18, 4, had not come to the notice of the court.

Latin:

vers. 10. ALTARIA TUA DESTRUXE- RUNT.

Per atlaria intelligi Metonymice cultum DEI. Nam in Israele non erant altaria, sed solum Hiero- solymis. Etsi concedatur in regno Israelis alios servasse statuta Domini, alios statuta Jeroboami, non tamen cum Cloppenburgio in Schol. Sacrif. p. 155. inde colligendum altaria DEO dicata ibi fuis- se, in quibus fideles obtulerint, aut Sacerdotes 1. Reg. 12. v. 31. qui non erant de filiis Levi veri DEI cultoribus, inservisse: nam hi pro veris Sa- cerdotibus haberi non poterant, neque vel proba- ta, altaria, aut oblationes in excelsis DEO sunt, vel dissimulata a DEO talis ἀνομία oblationum propter λῆμμα electorum recte creditur : quia electi ipsi abominati sunt tales ἐθελοθρησκείας, & Hierosolymis sacrificia sua obtulerunt, vel in occulto latuerunt, uti Eliæ tempore.

Vers. eod. PROPHETAS TUOS OCCIDERUNT GLADIO) Quos tales esse norunt. Nam centum illi de quibus supra 18, 4. ad notitiam aulæ non venerant.

## 19:12
Ver. 12. AFTER THE FIRE A WHISPER OF A GENTLE BREEZE) A representation of the Gospel, which did not come with wind, earthquake, and lightnings like the law, Exod. 19, 16. Heb. 12, 18, 19, 20, 21, but with great gentleness. This is that ἄνωθεν σοφία, εἰρηνικὴ, εὐπειθὴς, μεστὴ ἐλέες (wisdom from above, peaceable, gentle, full of mercy), James 3, 17. By the way, Elijah is admonished to beware of anger, to which he was inclined by his own nature.

Not sufficiently pious and untimely is the reproach, which Grotius learned from his intimates, pointing the finger at the Jesuits. For thus Cornelius [a Lapide]: God wished to moderate the zeal of Elijah, so that it would not arise from anger and perturbation of mind, such as was in Elijah, but from gentleness and love of justice. But how will it be denied that Elijah was governed by the Spirit of GOD, if indeed he was full of the Holy Spirit? Better, therefore, St. Irenaeus, book 4, chap. 37: The coming of the Lord was signified after the law, which was given through Moses, as mild and tranquil, and the rest of his kingdom as mild and gentle.

Latin:

Vers. 12. POST IGNEM SIBILUS AURÆ TENUIS) Evangelii figuratio, quod non venit cum vento, terræ motu, fulminibus ut lex, Exod. 19, 16. Hebr. 12, 18. 19. 20. 21. sed cum magna lenitate. Hæc est illa ἄνωθεν σοφία, εἰρηνικὴ, εὐ- πειθὴς, μεστὴ ἐλέες. Jacobi 3, 17. Obiter admonetur Elias, ut sibi ab ira caveat, ad quam natura suapte ferebatur.

Non satis pia tanti Prophetæ, & intempesti- va reprehensio, quam ab intimis suis, Jesuitas in- digito, didicit Grotius. Ita enim Cornelius : Vo- luit DEUS Eliæ zelum moderari, ut non fieret ex ira & perturbatione animi, qualis erat in Elia, sed ex leni- tate, & amore justitiæ. Sed gubernatum a Spiritu DEI Eliam quomodo negabitur, siquidem plenus fuerit S. S. Melius ergo S. Irenæus l. 4. cap. 37. Do- mini adventus significabatur post legem, quæ data est per Mosen mitis & tranquillus, & regni ejus mitis, & mansueta requietio.

## 19:13
Ver. 13.

HE COVERED HIS FACE WITH A MANTLE) A sign of reverence. Thus Helenus to Aeneas: Cover your hair with a purple garment.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

OPERUIT VULTUM SUUM PALLIO) Reverentiæ signum. Sic Helenus Æneæ: Purpureo velare comas ad pertus amictu.

## 19:15
Verse 15.

YOU SHALL ANOINT HAZAEL KING OVER SYRIA] The LXX call him Ἀζαήλ; Josephus calls him Ἀζάηλον: Justin calls him Azelus in Trogus 36, 2. Josephus says in 9, 2 that he was worshipped as a god by the Damascenes. Note also that God indeed cared especially for His own people, but not so that He did not also sometimes bestow testimonies of rare providence upon other peoples, as here upon the Syrians.

Why is RARE added? It is a different matter in Acts 14, 17. chapter 17, 26. et seqq.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

UNGES HAZAEL REGEM SUPER SYRIAM] LXX. Ἀζαήλ; Josephus Ἀζάηλον vocant : Azelum Justinus ex Trojo 36, 2. Hunc ut Deum cultum a Damascenis dicit Josephus 9, 2. Nota item Deum populum quidem suum præcipue curasse, sed non ut non & aliis populis interdum raræ providentiæ te- stimonia largiretur, ut hîc Syris.

Cur additur RARÆ? Aliud Actor. 14, 17. cap. 17, 26. seqq.

## 19:16
Verse 16.

JEHU THE SON OF NIMSHI) This man was brave, by no means indulgent toward faults, of a character like Cato the Younger.

YOU SHALL ANOINT AS PROPHET IN YOUR PLACE] You shall designate him as your successor. Kings, prophets, and priests were anointed as a sign of the gifts that God poured out upon them, if they performed their duty. Elisha was a contemner of wealth, beneficent to many, but a sharp avenger of crimes, to whom you might not badly compare Fabricius, if you look at his spirit, not the offices they held.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

JEHU FILIUM NAMSI) Fuit hic vir fortis, minime ad culpas indulgens, ingenio quali Cato Uticensis.

UNGES PROPHETAM PRO TE] Designabis eum ti- bi successorem. Ungebantur Reges, Prophetæ, Sacerdotes, in signum donorum quæ Deus illis effundebat, si officium face- rent. Fuit Elisæus opum contemtor, in multos beneficus, sed facinorum acer vindex, cui Fabricium non male compares, si animum spectes, non quæ obierunt munera.

## 19:18
Verse 18.

I WILL LEAVE FOR MYSELF IN ISRAEL SEVEN THOUSAND MEN] I will cause to remain. God is the author of constancy, as well as of other virtues, though not without the consent of the will: but just as children are named more from their fathers than from their mothers, so also are actions attributed more to God who brings them forth than to the soul that conceives them. And see how few were the retainers of piety: for what are seven thousand among ten tribes, in which those who bore arms were one million one hundred thousand 1 Chron. 21, 5.

WHOSE KNEES HAVE NOT BOWED TO BAAL] The LXX take the word כרע, which is general enough in itself, here regarding the bending of the knees, for they have ἐκ ὤκλασαν γόνυ, the Apostle Paul ἐκ ἔκαμψαν γόνυ Rom. 14. v. 4. That is frequent in the worship of the true or false God. See Rom. 14. v. 11. Eph. 3. v. 14. Phil. 2. v. 10.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

DERELINQVAM MIHI IN ISRAEL SEPTEM MIL- LIA VIRORUM] Manere faciam. Constantiæ, ut & alia- rum virtutum Deus auctor, quanquam non sine consensu vo- luntatis: sed sicut liberi a patribus magis quam a matribus nominantur, ita & actiones a Deo magis ferente quam ab anima concipiente. Et vide quam pauci fuerint retinentes pie- tatis: quid enim septem millia in decem tribubus, in quibus qui arma ferrent fuere decies centena & centum millia 1. Par. 21, 5.

QUORUM GENUA NON SUNT INCURVATA BA- AL] Vocem כרע satis per se generalem de genuum flexio- ne sumunt hîc LXX. qui habent ἐκ ὤκλασαν γόνυ, Paulus Apostolus ἐκ ἔκαμψαν γόνυ Rom. 14. v. 4. Frequens id in Dei veri aut falsi cultu. Vide Rom. 14. v. 11. Ephes. 3. v. 14. Phil. 2. v. 10.

## 19:19
Verse 19. PLOWING) The Romans had Dictators and Consuls from the plow: the Hebrews had Prophets. See also Amos 1, 1.

HE CAST HIS MANTLE UPON HIM) He gave him the prophetic habit, and thus as it were inaugurated him. See below 2 Kings 1, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ARANTEM) Romani ab Aratro Dictatores & Consules habuere : Hebræi Prophetas. Vide & Amos 1, 1.

MISIT PALLIUM SVVM SUPER ILLUM) Habitum ei Propheticum dedit, & sic eum velut inauguravit. Vide infra 2. Reg. 1, 8.

## 19:20
Vers. 20. LET ME KISS, I PRAY, MY FATHER) I will bid him farewell: Josephus, τοὺς γονεῖς ἀσπάσεσθαι. See what is said at Luke 9, 61.

Latin:

Vers. 20. OSCULER ORO PATREM MEUM) Vale- dicam ei : Josephus, τοὺς γονεῖς ἀσπάσεσθαι. Vide quæ ad Lucam 9, 61.

## 19:21
Vers. 21. FOR WHAT WAS MINE I HAVE DONE TO THEE) In the Hebrew: for what have I done to thee? That is, consider to how great a duty I have recalled you. In sacred rites it was accustomed to be said: Do this.

HE COOKED THE MEATS AND GAVE TO THE PEOPLE) He gave a distribution of meat.

Latin:

Vers. 21. QVOD ENIM MEUM ERAT FECI TIBI) In Hebræo : quia quid feci tibi? Id est, cogita ad quantum munus revocaverim. In sacris dici solebat : Hoc age.

COXIT CARNES ET DEDIT POPULO) Visceratio- nem dedit.

## 20:1 Argument
CHAPTER XX. The Syrians besieging Samaria are slaughtered: and in the second year they are slaughtered again in the plains. Ahab is rebuked because he entered into a treaty with Benhadad and let him go alive.

Ver. 1. BENHADAD KING OF SYRIA) Josephus in the text calls him son of Adad and Adad: in the title of the chapter it is Adar: among the LXX, son of Ader. Adores among Justin from Trogus. Concerning this change of letters, either of sound or of affinity in writing, we have spoken above at 2 Sam. 8, 5.

THIRTY TWO KINGS WITH HIM) Who were in his clientage, but the war is not waged as well through these as through subjects, as appears below in [verse] 24. For they know that their own business is not being transacted.

Does Roman power move the Armenians, whose leader is it? says Caesar in Lucan. Cerialis in Tacitus, Histories IV, sends back the levies held throughout Gaul to their cities, and orders them to announce that the legions are sufficient for the empire: that the allies should return to the duties of peace, secure as if the war were finished which Roman hands had undertaken,

Latin:

CAPUT XX. Syri Samariam obsidentes cæduntur : & altero iterum anno cæduntur in campestribus. Achab reprehenditur, quod fœdus inierit cum Benhadad, eumque vivum dimiserit.

Vers. 1. BENADAD REX STRIAE) Hunc & Ἀδάδη υἱὸς & Ἀδαδὸν vocat in textu Josephus : in titulo capitis est Ἀδὰρ : apud LXX. υἱὸς Ἀδὲρ. Adores apud Justinum ex Trogo. De hac literarum mutatione aut soni aut Scripturæ affinitate di- ximus & supra 2. Sam. 8, 5.

TRIGINTA DVOS REGES SECVM) Qui in clientela ipsius erant, sed per hos non tam bene bellum geritur quam per subditos, ut apparet infra 24. Norunt enim illi non su- am rem agi.

Armeniosne movet Romana potentia cujus Sit ducis? ait apud Lucanum Cæsar. Cerialis apud Tacitum Historia- rum IV. dilectus per Galliam habitos in civitates remittit, ac nuntiare jubet, sufficere imperio legiones : Socii ad munia pa- cis redirent, securi velut confecto bello quod Romanæ manus excepissent,

## 20:4
Ver. 4. I AM THINE AND ALL MINE) I give myself and my possessions into your protection. Thus Ahab understood these words. Benhadad, however, [understood them] concerning the ownership of things. Polybius and Livy record a similar ambiguity between the Romans and the Aetolians. See book III of the Law of War and Peace, chapter 20, § 50.

Latin:

Vers. 4. TVVS SVM EGO ET OMNIA MEA) Do me meaque in tuam fidem. Sic hæc verba Achabus intellige- bat. Benadad autem de rerum proprietate. Simile ambi- guum inter Romanos & Ætolos memorant Polybius & Livi- us. Vide librum III. de Jure Belli ac Pacis cap. 20. §. 50.

## 20:7
Ver. 7. ALL THE ELDERS OF THE LAND) Kings are accustomed to do this even when they are not at all popular, when dangers impend. For those [dangers] are undergone more readily when common consent has preceded.

BECAUSE HE LAYS SNARES FOR ME) That is, he cavils at our words.

Latin:

Vers. 7. OMNES SENIORES TERRÆ) Solent id fa- cere reges etiam minime populares, ubi pericula ingruunt. Promtius enim ea subeuntur, ubi communis consensus præiit.

QVONIAM INSIDIETVR NOMEN) Id est, cavillatur verba nostra.

## 20:8
Ver. 8.

DO NOT HEAR NOR CONSENT TO HIM] That similar [passage] in Tacitus, Annals 15: Nero consulted among the leaders of the state whether an uncertain war or a dishonorable peace was more pleasing: and there was no doubt about war.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

NON AVDIAS NEQVE ACQVIESCAS ILLI] Simi- le illud apud Tacitum Annalium 15. Consuluit inter primores civitatis Nero, bellum anceps, an pax inhonesta placeret : nec du- bitatum de bello.

## 20:10
Ver. 10. IF THE DUST OF SAMARIA SHALL SUFFICE FOR THE HANDFULS OF ALL THE PEOPLE THAT FOLLOW ME) A bold hyperbole. If the individual soldiers take away a handful, nothing will remain of the land of Samaria. Historians relate that rivers were dried up by the army of Xerxes, and that his army could scarcely be contained by all of Greece.

Latin:

Vers. 10. SI SVFFECERIT PVLVIS SAMARIÆ PV- GILLIS OMNIS POPVLI QVI SEQVITVR ME) Au- dax hyperbole. Si milites singuli pugillum auferant, de ter- ra Samariæ nihil remanebit. Ab exercitu Xerxis flumina siccata, Græciamque omnem vix capere exercitum ejus potu- isse narrant historici.

## 20:11
Ver. 11. LET NOT HIM THAT GIRDETH ON HIS ARMOR BOAST AS HE THAT PUTTETH IT OFF) Do not sing a triumph before the victory, upon the attainment of which weapons are laid aside. Ξυνὸς Ἐνυάλιος (The god of war is common to all).

Latin:

Vers. 11. NE GLORIETVR ACCINCTVS ÆQVE VT DISCINCTVS) Noli triumphum canere ante victoriam, qua parta ponuntur arma. Ξυνὸς Ἐνυάλιος.

## 20:13
Ver. 13. I WILL DELIVER HIM INTO THINE HAND THIS DAY) Truly, God follows the proud as an avenger from behind. The Greeks call this part of divine providence Nemesis.

Latin:

Vers. 13. EGO TRADAM EVM IN MANV TVA HODIE) Nimirum, Sequitur superbos ultor a tergo Deus. Hanc divinæ providentiæ partem Nemesim Græci vocant.

## 20:14
Ver. 14. BY THE YOUNG MEN) By the weak crowd.

Latin:

Vers. 14. PER PEDISSEQVOS) Per turbam imbecillem.

## 20:18
APPREHENDITE EOS VIVOS) ζωγρεῖτε. He does not say fight, but take, or kill: clearly as if he had the victory in his own hand.

Latin:

Vers. 18. APPREHENDITE EOS VIVOS) ζωγρεῖτε. Non dicit pugnate, sed capite, aut occidite: plane quasi in sua manu haberet victoriam.

## 20:22
VIDE QVID FACIAS) Press on as much as you can with the victory: then look to your own affairs for the future.

Latin:

Vers. 22. VIDE QVID FACIAS) Insta quantum potes victoriæ: deinde rebus tuis imposterum prospice.

## 20:23
DII MONTIVM SVNT DII EORVM) The Syrians did not acknowledge the God of the universe. But they thought the God of the Israelites was an ὀρειβάτην, by which name Pan is called by the Greeks. They had, of course, heard that the law was given on a mountain.

VT PVGNEMVS CONTRA EOS IN CAMPESTRIBVS) Well thought: for Syria also excelled in cavalry. See below 25.

Latin:

Vers. 23. DII MONTIVM SVNT DII EORVM) De- um universi non agnoscebant Syri. Deum autem Israelis pu- tabant esse ὀρειβάτην, quo nomine Pan à Græcis vocatur. Au- dierant nimirum legem in monte datam.

VT PVGNEMVS CONTRA EOS IN CAMPE- STRIBVS) Bene cogitatum : nam & equitatu præpollebat Syria. Vide infra 25.

## 20:26
IN APHEC) It is a city of the part of the Asherites. Jos. 19, 30. which had been made the Syrians' in this war.

Latin:

Vers. 26. IN APHEC) Vrbs est partis Aseritarum. Jos. 19, 30. quæ hoc bello Syrorum facta fuerat.

## 20:31
SACCOS IN LVMBIS NOSTRIS) A sign of mourning.

ET FVNICVLOS IN CAPITIBVS NOSTRIS) A sign of submission.

Latin:

SACCOS IN LVMBIS NOSTRIS) Signum luctus.

ET FVNICVLOS IN CAPITIBVS NOSTRIS) Si- gnum devotionis.

## 20:32
Vers. 32.

FRATER MEVS EST) A common fortune indeed commends kings to kings, but one must take care that this is not done to the public detriment.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

FRATER MEVS EST) Fortuna quidem communis re- ges regibus commendat, sed cavendum ne id fiat cum malo publico.

## 20:34
Vers. 34.

CIVITATES QVAS TVLIT PATER MEVS A PATRE TVO REDDAM) Those whom the fortune of war has made superiors are accustomed to recover their own.

ET PLATEAS FAC TIBI IN DAMASCO) They are also accustomed to look to their own security for the future. What the Latin here called plateas, חוצות, the LXX translate as ἐξόδους, the origin not denying it. Understand fortifications by which the Damascenes might be restrained, so that they would not break into the lands of the Israelites hereafter. Conf. 2. Sam. 8, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 34.

CIVITATES QVAS TVLIT PATER MEVS A PA- TRE TVO REDDAM) Solent quos superiores belli for- tuna fecit, sua recipere.

ET PLATEAS FAC TIBI IN DAMASCO) Solent & securitati suæ in futurum prospicere. Quod hic Latinus dixit plateas, חוצות, LXX. vertunt ἐξόδους, origine non abnuente. Intellige munitiones quibus reprimerentur Da- masceni, ne in terras Israëlitarum posthac irrumperent. Conf. 2. Sam. 8, 16.

## 20:35
Verse 35.

WHEN I ASKED, HE REFUSED TO STRIKE) Badly: for laws of that kind do not hold against the word of the Prophet.

Latin:

Vers. 35.

PETENTE ME, ILLE NOLVIT PERCVTERE) Male : nam leges ejus generis non valent contra dictum Prophetæ.

## 20:37
Verse 37.

WHO STRUCK HIM) For the ancients spoke not only with words, but with deeds. Compare below 22, v. 11. 2 Chronicles 18, v. 10. See what was said by us at Matthew 21, v. 19.

A mirror, therefore, and an example of obedience is provided here: concerning which Chrysostom, oration 1 against the Jews: He who struck the Prophet escaped unharmed; he who spared him paid the penalty: clearly so that you might understand that in divine commands one ought not to be curious, and to examine the nature of the things that are commanded, but to do nothing other than obey.

Latin:

Vers. 37.

QVI PERCVSSIT EVM) Nam antiqui non verbis tan- tum, sed rebus loquebantur. Confer infra 22. v. 11. 2. Paralip. 18. v. 10. Vide quæ dicta a nobis ad Matth. 21, v. 19.

SPeculum ergo & exemplum obedientiæ hic præbetur: de quo Chrysost. orat. 1. contr. Judæos: Qui percussit Prophetam, evasit incolumis; qui pepercit, dedit pœnas: nimirum ut intelligeres in jussis divinis non oportere curiosum esse, examinareq́; rerum quæ præcipiuntur naturam, sed nihil aliud, quam obtemperare.

## 20:39
Verse 39. YOUR SERVANT WENT OUT TO BATTLE) An excellent art, by substituting other names to convince kings out of their own confession: See 2 Samuel 12 and 14. Thus of old, as Phaedrus says, - - servitus obnoxia (servitude, being subject, because it dared not say what it wanted, transferred its own feelings into fables, and eluded calumny with feigned jests).

Latin:

Vers. 39. SERVVS TVVS EGRESSVS EST AD PRÆLIANDVM) Ars egregia, suppositis nominibus aliis convincere reges ex ipsorum confessione: Vide 2. Sam. 12. & 14. Sic olim, ut ait Phædrus, - - servitus obnoxia Quia quæ volebat non audebat dicere, Affectus proprios in fabellas transtulit, Calumniamque fictis elusit jocis.

## 20:40
Verse 40. THIS IS YOUR JUDGMENT WHICH YOU YOURSELF HAVE DECREED) Suffer the law which you have brought forth.

Latin:

Vers. 40. HOC EST JVDICIVM TVVM QVOD IPSE DECREVISTI) Patere legem quam tuleris.

## 20:42
Verse 42. BECAUSE YOU HAVE LET GO A MAN WORTHY OF DEATH) A stubborn enemy of Israel. Ahab, having obtained victory not by his own virtue, but by the singular gift of God, ought not to have decided anything concerning Hadad, unless God had been consulted through Urim or the Prophets. Compare 1 Samuel 15. YOUR LIFE SHALL BE FOR HIS LIFE) You shall pay for this illicit leniency with death. The fulfillment follows in the last chapter of this book.

Latin:

Vers. 42. QVIA DIMISISTI VIRVM DIGNVM MORTE) Hostem Israelis pertinacem. Achabus victoriam non sua virtute, sed singulari Dei dono nactus, non debuerat de Adado aliquid statuere, nisi Deo consulto per Vrim aut Prophetas. Confer 1. Sam. 15. ERIT ANIMA TVA PRO ANIMA EJVS) Morte lues hanc lenitatem inconcessam. Implementum sequitur cap. hujus libri ultimo.

## 20:43
Verse 43. DISDAINING TO LISTEN AND FURIOUS) In the Hebrew: stubborn and furious. Josephus, σύγκεχυμένω: as also the LXX, who add: καὶ ἐκλελυμένω. However, both in Josephus and in the LXX, this history is later than the history of Naboth, contrary to what is in the Hebrew.

Latin:

Vers. 43. AVDIRE CONTEMNENS ET FVRIBVNDVS) In Hebræo: contumax & furibundus. Josephus, σύγκεχυμένω: quomodo & LXX. qui addunt: καὶ ἐκλελυμένω. Tam autem apud Josephum quam apud LXX. historia hæc posterior est historia de Nabuthe contra quam in Hebræo.

## 21:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXI.

Ahab seizes the vineyard from Naboth, he having been unjustly stoned, to whom and to his wife Elijah announces destruction.

Verse 1. GIVE ME YOUR VINEYARD] Until the Jubilee. For beyond that it was certain that it was not permitted.

Latin:

CAPUT XXI.

Achab vineam Nabotho, eo injuste lapidato, eripit, cui & conjugi exitium denuntiat Elias.

Vers. 1. DA MIHI VINEAM TVAM] Ad Jubilæum usque. Vltra enim certum erat non licere.

## 21:3
Vers. 3. DO NOT GIVE THE INHERITANCE OF MY FATHERS TO THEE) Nor did the law permit it, unless one was pressed by grave poverty. See Deuteronomy 15, 25. Furthermore, we naturally love ancestral things.

Latin:

Vers. 3. NE DEM HEREDITATEM PATRVM MEORVM TIBI) Neque lex id permittebat, nisi egestate gravi presso. Vid. Deuteron. 15, 25. deinde naturaliter amamus res avitas.

## 21:7
Vers. 7. THOU ART OF GREAT AUTHORITY) Clearly as Poppaea used to call Nero a ward, who, being subject to the commands of others, lacked not only imperial power but even liberty. Thus Tacitus, Annals 14.

Latin:

Vers. 7. GRANDIS AVCTORITATIS ES) Plane ut Poppæa pupillum vocabat Neronem, qui jussis alienis obnoxius, non modo Imperii, sed libertatis etiam indigeret. Ita Tacitus Annalium 14.

## 21:8
Vers. 8. TO THE ELDERS AND THE NOBLES) That is, to the judges of the town, who even judged in capital cases. Why did the king himself not judge him? First, because the kings of the ten tribes were satisfied to be exempt from judgments themselves, but left judgments to the common people by whom they had been raised to the kingdom, whereas the kings of Judah often both judged and in civil matters submitted themselves to the judgment of the senate. Furthermore, this method of proceeding had a greater appearance of justice and less hatred. Tacitus called it an image of a trial in Annals III and Histories IV, saying that Nero had mocked cruelty through such images.

Latin:

Vers. 8. AD MAJORES NATV ET OPTIMATES) Id est, ad oppidi judices, qui etiam de capite judicabant. Cur ipse rex eum non judicavit? Primum quia decem tribuum reges satis habebant ipsi judiciis eximi, cæterum judicia relinquebant popularibus a quibus ad regnum erant evecti, cum reges Judæ & judicarent sæpe & in rebus civilibus judicio senatus se sisterent. Deinde vero speciem majorem juris minusque odii habebat ista agendi ratio. Imaginem cognitionis dixit Tacitus Annalium III. & Historiarum IV. Sævitiam Neronis per hujusmodi imagines illusisse.

## 21:9
Vers. 9. PROCLAIM A FAST) As in a grave crime by which the people were defiled, so that the people might the more believe that the matter was being handled piously.

MAKE NABOTH SIT AMONG THE CHIEF OF THE PEOPLE) That is, give him an honorable place in the synagogue. Josephus adds, Εἶναι γὰρ αὐτὸν γένους ἐπιφανοῦς. This was done so that they would not be believed to have condemned out of hatred one whom they had honored, but rather compelled by the testimony of witnesses with their own greatest sorrow.

Latin:

Vers. 9. PRÆDICATE JEJVNIVM) Vt in gravi delicto quo populus attaminabatur, quo magis credat populus rem pie agi.

SEDERE FACITE NABOTH INTER PRIMOS POPVLI) Id est, in Synagoga date ei locum honorificum. Εἶναι γὰρ αὐτὸν γένους ἐπιφανοῦς addit Josephus. Hoc ideo, ne odio damnasse crederentur, quem ipsi honoraverant, sed religione testium coacti cum summo suo dolore.

## 21:10
Vers. 10.

AND SET UP TWO MEN) Thus the LXX. But Josephus posited three, not wrongly if the Hebrew books favored it: for against a man of distinguished fame three witnesses were required. But for wicked kings, such instruments of injustice are never lacking.

SONS OF BELIAL) LXX: lawless men. Josephus: some daring men.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ET SVBMITTITE DVOS VIROS) Sic LXX. At Josephus tres posuit, non male si faverent libri Hebræi: nam adversus insignis famæ virum tres testes requirebantur. Malis autem regibus nunquam defunt talia injustitiæ instrumenta.

FILIOS BELIAL) LXX. παρανόμων. Josephus τολμηρούς τινας.

## 21:13
NABOTH BLESSED GOD AND THE KING) Josephus: ὡς τὸν θεόν τε εἴη βλασφημήσας καὶ τὸν βασιλέα. You have this manner of speaking derived from the contrary in Job 1, v. 5; ch. II, v. 2, 9.

AND CARRY HIM OUT) Outside the gate, as was accustomed to be done in executions.

AND STONE HIM) According to the law of Leviticus 24, 16.

Latin:

BENEDIXIT NABOTH DEVM ET REGEM) Josephus, ὡς τὸν θεόν τε εἴη βλασφημήσας καὶ τὸν βασιλέα. Habes hoc loquendi genus ex contrario eductum Jobi 1. v. 5. cap. II. v. 2. 9.

ET EDVCITE EVM) Extra portam, ut in suppliciis fieri solebat.

ET LAPIDATE) Ex lege Levitici 24, 16.

## 21:15
Vers. 15. AND POSSESS THE VINEYARD OF NABOTH) By title of confiscation, which among the Hebrews had a place in all crimes against royal majesty. See 2 Sam. 9, 7. This is the opinion which Levi Gersonides and David follow

Kimchi is more probable than what others invent, that Naboth was a kinsman of the king, and his children were killed with him as participants in the crime, of which the former seems to be proven by 2 Kings 9:26, but the latter not so.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET POSSIDE VINEAM NABOTH) Titulo confiscationis quæ apud Hebræos locum habebat in omnibus delictis adversus regiam majestatem. Vide 2. Sam. 9, 7. Hæc sententia quam sequuntur Levi Bengerson & David

Kimchi probabilior est, quam quod fingunt alii, Nabuthem agnatum fuisse regis, & liberos cum eo interfectos, ut participes criminis, quorum hoc probari videtur 2. Reg. 9, 26. illud vero alterum non item.

## 21:19
Verse 19.

YOU HAVE KILLED AND ALSO TAKEN POSSESSION) The enormity of the crime is explained in a few words. Such is that in Agricola: to slaughter, to plunder, they call empire by false names. And Pliny says that the treasury under Domitian was a spoliarium of citizens and a cruel receptacle for bloody spoils.

IN THIS PLACE) Better, instead of that which, because the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, that is, for the reason that. For the cause of the judgment is indicated, not the place. Moreover, the dogs had licked the blood of Naboth there where he had been stoned.

IN Jezreel the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, in Samaria, to which it belonged, that of Ahab, as Abulensis, Lyranus, and Vatablus note. In vain do Salianus and Sanchez say that this was fulfilled in Joram the son of Ahab, killed in the field of Jezreel: to whom Cornelius agrees.

THEY SHALL LICK YOUR BLOOD ALSO) Poured out into the chariot, namely, below 22:38.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

OCCIDISTI INSUPER ET POSSEDISTI) Paucis verbis explicatur facinoris immanitas. Tale illud in Agricola: trucidare, rapere, falsis nominibus imperium appellant. Et Plinius ærarium sub Domitiano ait fuisse spoliarium civium, cruentarumque prædarum sævum receptaculum.

IN LOCO HOC) Melius, loco ejus quod linxerunt canes sanguinem Naboth, id est, propterea quod. Causa enim judicii indicatur, non locus. Linxerant autem canes sanguinem Nabothis ibi ubi lapidatus fuerat.

IN Jezrael linxerunt canes sanguinem Nabothi, in Samaria, ad quam illa pertinebat, Achabi, uti notant Abulens. Lyranus, Vatabl. Frustra Salianus & Sanchez id impletum in Joram filio Achab dicunt, occiso in agro Jezrahel: quibus annuit Cornelius.

LAMBENT QVOQVE SANGVINEM TUUM) Effusum in currum scilicet infra 22, 38.

BECAUSE YOU HAVE SOLD YOURSELF TO DO EVIL IN THE SIGHT OF THE LORD] That is, you are a slave to the foulest vices. Thus below 25. Romans 7:14. Horace: For the master, not gentle, presses the mind and applies sharp goads to the weary.

Vers, eod.
