## 22:1 Argument
SECTION III. The History of Jehoshaphat allied with Ahab. CHAPTER XXII.

To Ahab going into war the false prophets predict victory, Micaiah predicts destruction, which came to pass. The deeds of Jehoshaphat, and his fleet: To whom dying succeeded Jehoram, as to Ahab Ahaziah.

Latin:

SECTIO III. JOSAPHATI Achabo confœderati Historia. CAPUT XXII.

Achabo in bellum eunti Pseudo-Prophetæ victoriam, Micheas exitium prædicit, quod evenit. Gesta Josaphati, & classis ejus: Cui morienti successit Joram, uti Achabo Ochozias.

Verse 2. AND THREE YEARS PASSED] Not full ones. 2 Chron. 18, 1.

JEHOSHAPHAT THE KING OF JUDAH WENT DOWN TO THE KING OF ISRAEL] Ahab, whose daughter this evil man had married, as is to be gathered from 2 Chronicles 18, v. 1, which seems to be the principal reason why the Prophet rebuked him 2 Chronicles 19, 2.

EACH ONE ON HIS THRONE) As equals.

## 22:21
Ver. 21. AND THERE CAME FORTH A SPIRIT) Someone from the family of Satan. Thus Satan also appears among the angels, Job 1. But some of the Hebrews think this spirit was the spirit of Naboth, seeking vengeance upon Ahab.

Why does he bring forward that invention of the Hebrews, which is extremely frivolous, when he neither rejects nor refutes it? Perhaps because he is accustomed to value their other trifles, did he judge this one also not so worthy of rejection? But that spirit of Naboth must be ascribed either to the number of the elect or the reprobate. The former cannot be said, since he asserts that he will be a lying spirit in the mouth of the false prophets. But neither can the latter be affirmed. For Naboth was pious and suffered innocently: nor are the souls of the faithful occupied after death in seducing others, or acting as false prophets, and being lying and deceptive spirits in their mouths. This is the work of Satan, not of separated souls.

Latin:

Vers. 21. EGRESSVS AVTEM EST SPIRITVS) Ali- quis ex Satanæ familia. Sic inter Angelos etiam Satan ap- paret Job 1. At Hebræorum nonnulli spiritum hunc putant fuisse Spiritum Nabuthis, vindictam quærentis de Achabo.

CVr Ebræorum commentum istud, perquam frivolum, adfert, quum nec reprobet, nec re- fellat illud? Num uti cæteras nugas eorum æsti- mare consuevit, hoc etiam non adeo reproban- dum censuit? At Spiritus ille Nabathis vel electorum numero adscribendus erit, vel reproborum? Illud di- ci nequit, quum se spiritum mendacem in ore falsorum Prophetarum futurum asserat. Sed neq; hoc affirma- ri potest. Nabath enim pius fuit, & innocenter pas- sus est: neq; animæ infidelium post fata, in seducendis aliis occupantur, aut falsos Prophetas agunt, ac Spiritus mendaces & deceptorii in ore ipsorum sunt. Hoc Satanæ est, non animarum separatarum.

For דבק is a joint, also in Isaiah 41:7, σύμβλημα. But the LXX: between the lung and between the breastplate. Both here and in Chronicles. Josephus: through the breastplate against the lung.

Nam דבק junctura est etiam Esa. 41, 7. σύμβλημα. At LXX. ἀνά- μεσον τοῦ πνεύμονος καὶ ἀναμέσον τοῦ θώρακος. Et hic & in Paralipomenis. Josephus: διὰ τοῦ θώρακος κατὰ τοῦ πνεύμονος.

THE HERALD SOUNDED) In the Hebrew: The proclamation passed: that is, the signal was given for retreat.

## 22:38
IN THE POOL OF SAMARIA) In a collection of water surrounded by stones, which Josephus and the LXX improperly call a fountain here.

AND THEY WASHED THE REINS) Girdles, if I am not mistaken, he wished to say, as if from זון which signifies a belt in Deuteronomy 23:13, although others prefer to translate it as weapons both there and here. But the LXX and Josephus more simply interpret זונות as harlots, and they washed themselves, namely, in that pool polluted with blood, so that this also might have added to the contempt of Ahab; which I do not disapprove. Others believe that harlots were painted on the chariot itself. Others interpret זונות as the visions of Elijah and Micaiah depicted on the same chariot, which I can hardly believe.

ACCORDING TO THE WORD OF THE LORD WHICH HE HAD SPOKEN) Refer this to that which was said concerning the flesh.

ET HABENAS LAVERVNT) Cingulas, ni fallor, di- cere voluit, quasi ab זון quod zonam significat Deuteron. 23, 13. quanquam alii & ibi & hic arma malunt vertere. At LXX. & Josephus simplicius זונות interpretantur meretri- ces, & laverunt scilicet sese, in ista piscina sanguine polluta, ut hoc etiam ad comtemtum Achabi accefferit; quod non im- probo. Alii in ipso curru meretrices pictas fuisse credunt. Alii זונות interpretantur visiones Eliæ & Michææ in eodem curru depictas, quod vix putem.

It lasted until the times of Jehoshaphat: but not long after followed the defection of the Idumeans 2 Kings 8, 20.

# 2 Kings

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 1). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
In the name of Jesus. TO THE LATTER BOOK OF KINGS AMONG THE HEBREWS, WHICH IS THE FOURTH OF KINGS AMONG THE LATINS.

The last of the Kings comprises the deeds of the Kings of Judah from Joram up to Zedekiah, 16 in number, and of the Kings of Israel, 12 from Ahaziah to Hoshea: and it is completed in two parts. I. Concerning both kingdoms still flourishing to some extent, up to the end of the Israelite kingdom, up to chapter 17. II. Concerning the kingdom of Judah after Israel was led away, to the very end of the book, chapter 25, or the burning of the temple. Therefore, the deeds of Joram, Ahaziah, Athaliah, Joash, Amaziah, Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, Josiah, Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah are proposed here, over 307 years, as the computation in this book holds, concerning its reconciliation with the computation of the years of the Kings of Israel in the Sacred Chronicle; And these Kings descended successively from David in a direct line of generation: to whom were contemporary in the kingdom of Israel Ahaziah, Joram, Jehu, Jehoahaz, Joash, Jeroboam II. Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah, Pekah, and Hoshea, under whom this kingdom ceased in the sixth year of Hezekiah. The entire economy of the book is as follows: Part I exhibits the history of both kingdoms still flourishing under 10 Kings of Judah, I. JEHOSHAPHAT, during whose reign under JORAM, son of Ahab, the Israelite King, Elijah was taken up into heaven, chapter 2. Elisha produced waters in the war with the Moabites, chapter 3. He relieved the poverty of the widow and raised the son of the Shunammite, chapter 4. He freed Naaman from leprosy, chapter 5. He struck the Syrians with blindness, chapter 6. He foretold an abundance of provisions for Samaria laboring under famine, which followed immediately, chapter 7. II. JORAM, son of Jehoshaphat, and III. AHAZIAH, son of Joram, chapter 8, who, with NAAM, the Israelite, and Jezebel, his mother, was killed by JEHU, chapter 9, with 70 sons of Ahab also killed, chapter 10. IV. ATHALIAH, who paid the penalty for her tyranny, chapter 11. V. JOASH, who organized the ecclesiastical treasury, chapter 12, in whose time were Jehoahaz and Joash, Kings of Israel. And Elisha died, by whose bones a certain man was raised from the dead, chapter 13. VI. AMAZIAH, by his contemporary, the Israelite Joash, whom he sought in war, and was taken captive, chapter 14. VII. UZZIAH, struck with leprosy, to whom were contemporary JEROBOAM II, ZECHARIAH, SHALLUM, MENAHEM, who was made tributary to Pul the Assyrian, PEKAHIAH, PEKAH, from whom many cities were taken by Tiglath-Pileser. VIII. JOTHAM, to whom Pekah was contemporary, chapter 15. IX. AHAZ, attacked by Pekah and Rezin, who therefore entered into a treaty with Tiglath-Pileser, who killed Rezin, King of Damascus, chapter 16. X. HEZEKIAH, from whose time HOSHEA, King of Israel, was led away into Assyria, and the kingdom of Israel met its end, and the Samaritan syncretistic worship arose, chapter 17.

PART II. Follows the history of the kingdom of Judah after the kingdom was taken away from the Israelites, under 8 Kings of Judah.

1. HEZEKIAH, whose piety and the siege made by Sennacherib, chapter 18. Prayer and deliverance, chapter 19. Lethal sickness and restoration, chapter 20. 2. MANASSEH, concerning whose idolatry and tyranny, chapter 21. 3. AMON, killed by his ministers, chapter 22. 4. JOSIAH, the pious, who repairs the temple, chapter 23, and reforms divine worship, having renounced idolatry. 5. JEHOAHAZ, who was led away captive by Pharaoh, chapter 24. 6. JEHOIAKIM, who was made tributary to Nebuchadnezzar. 7. JEHOIACHIN, who was led away to Babylon, chapter 24. 8. ZEDEKIAH, who was captured, Jerusalem occupied, and the temple burned, chapter 25.

Latin:

I. N. J. AD LIBRUM POSTERIOREM REGUM APUD HEBRÆOS, QUI APUD LATINOS QUARTUS REGUM.

POstremus Regum complectitur res gestas Regum Juda a Joramo usque ad Zedekiam numero 16. & Regum Israel 12. ab Achazia ad Hoseam: & duabus absolvitur partibus. I. De regno utroque simul adhuc quadantenus florente, usque ad terminum regni Israelitici usque ad c. 17. II. De regno Juda post abductum Israel, ad finem usque libri cap. 25. seu exustionem templi. Proponuntur ergo hic gesta Joram, Ochoziæ, Athaliæ, Joas, Amasiæ, Oziæ, Joatham, Achaz, Ezechiæ, Manassis, Amon, Josiæ, Joachas, Joakim, Joachin, & Sedekiæ, per annos 307. ut habet computus in hoc libro, de cujus conciliatione cum computo annorum Regum Israelis in Chronico sacro; Atque hi Reges ex Davide recta generationis serie successive descenderunt: quibus σύγχρονοι fuerunt in regno Israelis Ochozias, Joram, Jehu, Joachas, Joas, Jeroboam II. Zacharias, Sellum, Manahem, Phaceja, Phacee, & Osee, sub quo desiit hoc regnum fexto Ezechiæ. Universa Oeconomia libri sic habet: Pars I. Regni utriusque adhuc florentis historiam exhibet sub 10. Regibus Judæ, I. JOSAPHATO, quo regnante sub JORAMO Achabi f. Israelitico Rege contigit Eliæ in cœlum raptus cap. 2. Elisæus in bello cum Moabitis aquas produxit. c. 3. Viduæ paupertatem sublevavit, & Sunamitidis filium excitavit. c. 4. Naamanum lepra liberavit. c. 5. Syros cæcitate percussit c. 6. Samariæ fame laboranti annonæ copiam prædixit actutum sequutam cap. 7. II. JORAMO Josaphati f. & III. AHASIA Jorami f. c. 8. qui cum NAAMO Israelita & Jesabele ejusdem matre a JEHU peremtus c. 9. interfectis etiam Ahabifiliis 70. c. 10. IV. ATHALIA quæ tyrannidis suæ pœnas luit c. 11. V. JOASO, qui Gazophylacium Ecclesiasticum ordinavit cap. 12. cujus tempore Joahas, & Joas Israel. Reges fuere, mortuusque Elisæus, per cujus ossa vir quidam a morte excitatus est. c. 13. VI. AMAZIA, a συγχρόνῳ Israelita Joaso, quem bello petiit, captivo cap. 14. VII. ASARIA lepra percusso, cui σύγχρονοι fuere JEROBOAM II. SACHARIAS, SALLUM, MENAHEM Phuli Assyrio tributarius factus, PEKAJAH, PEKAH, cui multæ civitates a Tiglachpillafare ademtæ. VIII. JOTHAM, cui coætaneus PEKAH, c. 15. IX. AHAS a Peka, & Rezin oppugnatus, qui fœdus cum Tiglathpillafare ideo iniit, Damasci Regem Rezin interficiente. c. 16. X. HISKIA a cujus tempore HOSEAS Rex Israel. in Assyriam abductus & regnum Israelis finem fortitum, cultusque Samaritanus Syncretismus exortus est. c. 17.

PARS II. Regni Judæ historiam post sublatum Israelitis regnum persequitur sub 8. Regibus Judæ.

1. EZECHIA, cujus Pietas & oppugnatio a Sennacheribo facta c. 18. Oratio, & liberatio, c. 19. Morbus lethalis & restitutio: c. 20. 2. MANASSE, de cujus idololatria & Tyrannide c. 21. 3. AMMONE a ministris occiso c. 22. 4. JOSIA pio, qui templum reparat, c. 23. cultum divinum abdicata idololatria reformat. 5. JOAHAS qui a Pharaone captivus abductus. c. 24. 6. JOJAKIM, qui tributarius Nebucadnezari factus. 7. JECHONIA, qui in Babel abductus c. 24. 8. ZEDEKIA qui captus Hierosolyma occupata temploque exusto c. 25.

## 1:1 Argument
PART I. CONTINUES THE HISTORY OF BOTH KINGDOMS, JUDAH AND ISRAEL, UP TO THE END OF THE ISRAELITE KINGDOM. CHAPTER I.

After Ahaziah, being sick, had consulted Beelzebub, Elijah announces his death, burns up two captains of fifty with their soldiers with heavenly fire, spares the third who was sent to him, and with him goes to the king and in his presence declares his death. Joram his brother succeeds the deceased.

Vers. 1. BUT MOAB REBELLED AGAINST ISRAEL) He fell away from that dominion which he had acknowledged from the times of David, 2 Sam. 8. v. 2.

Latin:

PARS I. REGNI UTRIUSQUE JUDA ET ISRAELIS HISTORIAM CONTINUAT USQUE AD FINEM REGNI ISRAELITICI. CAPUT I.

Ochoziæ ægrotanti postquam Beelzebub consuluisset, Elias mortem denunciat, duos quinquagenarios igne cœlesti cum militibus suis comburit, tertio ad se misso parcit, & cum eo regem adit ac coram ei mortem intimat. Succedit defuncto Joram frater.

Vers. 1. PRÆVARICATUS EST AUTEM MOAB IN ISRAEL) Defecit ab eo imperio, quod a Davidis temporibus agnoverat 2. Sam. 8. v. 2.

## 1:2
CONSULT BEELZEBUB) θεὸν μῦαν [god of flies], Josephus. But it is more likely that this God was called by those Palestinians or Philistines, as also by other Phoenicians, בעל זבוּל [Baal-Zebul], but by the Hebrews for the sake of mockery בעל זבוּב [Baal-Zebub], lord of flies, because his temple was full of flies on account of the victims, which the Hebrews relate never came to the Jerusalem temple, where so many victims were slaughtered. In a similar way Arnobius mocks the Pagans: So, I say, do you not see newts, shrews, mice, and light-shunning cockroaches building nests and dwelling under the hollows of those images? And afterwards: Do not spiders weave nets in the mouth of some image, and treacherous snares, in which they might entangle the flight of buzzing and impudent flies? Do not swallows, finally, fly around within the very domes of the buildings? It is, however, a most grave crime, both to take away the honor of foreknowledge from God, and to give it to those who do not have it. Levit. 19, 31. chap. 20, 6. 27. Deuteron. 18, 10. 11. 14. 15. wherefore it is no wonder if God punishes such things most gravely, as appears both elsewhere and here 16. 17.

Others wish Beelzebub to be called the god of flies, who, when invoked to drive away flies, with which the Ekronites abounded on account of the moist and hot soil from the vicinity of the sea, is said to be invoked just as Smintheus is for driving away mice, which the Cretans call Sminthas, and Parnopius for driving away Parnopas or gnats.

Latin:

CONSULITE BEELZEBUB) θεὸν μῦαν Josephus. Sed verisimilius est vocatum hunc Deum Palæstinis sive Philistinis illis, ut & à Phœnicibus aliis, בעל זבוּל, ab Hebræis vero deridiculi causa בעל זבוּב dominum muscarum, quia templum ejus propter victimas plenum erat muscis, quas ad templum Hierosolymitanum, ubi tot mactabantur victimæ, nunquam adventasse narrant Hebræi. Simili modo Paganos irridet Arnobius: Ita inquam non videtis sub istorum simulacrorum cavis stelliones, sorices, mures, blattasque lucifugas nidamenta ponere atque habitare? Et post: Non in ore aliquanto simulacri ab araneis ordiri retia, atque insidiosos casses, quibus volatus innectere stridularum possint impudentiumque muscarum. Non hirundines denique intra ipsos ædium circumvolantes tholos? Est autem gravissimum crimen, & Deo auferre honorem præscientiæ, & iis dare qui non habent. Levit. 19, 31. cap. 20, 6. 27. Deuteron. 18, 10. 11. 14. 15. quare nec mirum si talia Deus gravissime punit, ut apparet tum alibi tum hic 16. 17.

ALii Beelzebub Deum muscarum dictum volunt, qui invocatus ad abigendas muscas, quibus abundarint Accaronitæ ob solum humidum & calidum ex maris vicinia, uti Smintheus ad abigendos mures, quos Cretenfes vocant Sminthas, & Parnopius ad abigendas Parnopas vel culices, invocatus dicitur.

## 1:8
Vers. 8. A HAIRY MAN] δασὺς [hairy] with long hair and beard, like the Greek Philosophers, and Cato in Lucan: He had allowed his uncut gray hairs to descend onto his rigid forehead, and a sad beard to grow upon his cheeks.

GIRDED ABOUT THE LOINS WITH A LEATHERN GIRDLE]

Latin:

Vers. 8. VIR PILOSUS] δασὺς promisso capillo ac barba, ut Græci Philosophi, & Cato apud Lucanum: Intonsos rigidam in frontem descendere canos Passus erat, mæstamque genis increscere barbam.

ZONA PELLICEA ACCINCTVS RENIBVS] Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 3. v. 4.

## 1:9
Ver. 9.

THE KING COMMANDED THAT YOU DESCEND] Prophets, in performing the duties of their office, are not bound by royal authority. It is otherwise with Priests. Compare what is below at 15, where, having been commanded by God, he does what he had previously refused.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

REX PRÆCEPIT VT DESCENDAS] Prophetæ facien- tes quæ sui sunt muneris, regio imperio non tenentur. Aliud in Sacerdotibus. Confer quod infra 15. ubi a Deo jussus facit quod ante abnuerat.

## 1:10
Vers. 10. LET FIRE DESCEND FROM HEAVEN AND DEVOUR THEE) What Ulpian says in lib. 1. D. Si quis jus dicenti non obtemperaverit, that it is granted to all magistrates to defend their jurisdiction by penal judgment; the same is rightly said of the Prophets, who, as magistrates, are set over the magistrates themselves by God. See shortly 12. Acts 8, 11. c. 2, 24. 1. Cor. 5, 5. 1. Tim. 1, 20. 1. Cor. 4, 21.

Latin:

Vers. 10. DESCENDAT IGNIS DE COELO ET DE- VORET TE) Quod dicit Ulpianus lib. 1. D. Si quis jus di- centi non obtemperaverit, omnibus magistratibus concessum esse, jurisdictionem suam defendere pœnali judicio; idem de Prophetis, qui velut magistratus sunt ipsis magistratibus a Deo impositi, recte dicitur. Vide mox 12. Act. 8, 11. c. 2, 24. 1. Cor. 5, 5. 1. Tim. 1, 20. 1. Cor. 4, 21.

## 1:13
Ver. 13. HE BOWED THE KNEES BEFORE

Latin:

Vers. 13. CVRVAVIT GENVA CONTRA ELIAM] Coram Elia, in honorem ejus ut Prophetæ. Vide supra 8, 7. infra 2, 15.

## 1:17
Vers. 17. IN THE SECOND YEAR OF JORAM) Nay, in the fifth, as we have below 8, 16, with which that which we shall soon have at 3, 1 well agrees. Did the error arise from the notation of the numbers? Or is the variation due to the fact that sons sometimes reigned with their fathers, which also confuses Persian Chronology?

It is not right to have recourse to a suspicion of error. For no error is to be conceded in the Hebrew Codices, where they agree. The later response, therefore, the interpreters embrace with great consensus. Richard of St. Victor in his commentary on the books of Kings and Chronicles, Arias Montanus on Daniel, Salianus, Torniellus, Sanctius, Serarius, Cornelius a Lapide, and others, [maintain] that Joram was called King, or if you prefer, Viceroy, by his father Josaphat when he was about to go to war with Achab in the 17th year of King Josaphat, so that the kingdom would not be left without a king in his absence, 2 Chron. 21, 5, whence the eighteenth year of Josaphat was the second year of the reign of Joram his son, 1 Kings 3, 1, which also pleased Abulensis, Cajetan, the Vinarie Paraphrasts, Mr. Dr. Walther, and others. Furthermore, the above-named authors observe that six years later, namely in the 23rd year. Jehoshaphat declared his son Joram king again while he was still a parent, when he was about to set out with Jehoshaphat to war against the Moabites, 2 Kings 3, so that the eight years during which Joram reigned are to be counted from that time, in such a way that he reigned for three years while his father was still living, four years after his death, and died in the eighth. Therefore, what is stated in 2 Kings 8:16, that in the fifth year of Joram, son of Ahab, King of Israel, Joram, son of Jehoshaphat, King of Judah, began to reign, is to be calculated from 9:29: In the eleventh year of Joram, son of Ahab, Ahaziah began to reign over Judah; with the five years of Joram, son of the King of Judah, subtracted from eleven, six years remain, or the sixth year of Joram, son of Ahab; whence it is rightly said that Joram, son of Jehoshaphat, began his reign in the fifth completed year of the same. See Corn. a Lapide on chapter 8:16.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ANNO SECVNDO JORAM) Imo quinto, ut habemus infra 8, 16. quicum bene congruit id quod habe- bimus mox 3, 1. An ex notis numerorum natus error? An vero varietas inde, quod Filii interdum cum Patribus regna- runt, quod & Persicam Chronologiam confundit?

Non recurrere fas est ad erroris suspicionem. Nullus enim in Codicibus Ebræis, ubi illi consen- tiunt, error concedendus est. Posteriorem ergo re- sponsionem Interpp. magno consensu amplectun- tur. Richardus de S. Victore in concil. lib. Regum & Paralipp. Arias mont. in Daniele, Salianus, Torniel- lus, Sanctius, Serarius, Corn. a Lapide, alii, Joram a Patre Josaphato in bellum ituro cum Achabo an- no 17. Josaphati Regem, vel si malis, Proregem nuncupatum fuisse, ne ipso absente regnum desti- tueretur rege, 2. Chron. 21, 5. unde annus Josapha- ti decimus octavus, annus secundus fuit regni Joram, filii ejus 1. Reg. 3, 1. quod etiam Abulensi, Cajetano, Vinariensibus Paraphrastis, Dn. D. Walthero, aliis- que placuit. Cæterum observant superius nomi- nati auctores, sexennio post, anno nempe 23. Josa- phathi denuo Joram filium ejus a Parente Regem declaratum esse, cum Josaphato in bellum adversus Moabitas proficiscendum esset, 2. Reg. 3. ut inde numerentur anni octo, quibus regnavit Joram, ita ut tribus annis tum cum Patre vivente, quatuor post fata ejus regnarit, octavo mortuus sit. Quod ergo 2. Reg. 8, 16. habetur, anno quinto Joram, Fi- lii Achab, Regis Israel regnavit Joram, Filius Josa- phat, Rex Juda, de eo ita ineundus est calculus e 9, 29. Anno undecimo Joram Filii Achab regnavit O- chozias super Judam: Filii Joram Regis Juda quin- que annis subductis ab 11. relinquuntur sex anni, vel annus sextus Joram filii Achab; unde anno quin- to completo ejusdem recte dicitur cepisse re- gnum Joram Filii Josaphat. vid. Corn. a Lapide in caput 8, 16.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II.

With the mantle of Elijah, who was carried up into heaven, Elisha divides the Jordan, heals the waters with salt, and tears to pieces the mocking boys by sending bears.

Ver. 1. WHEN THE LORD WAS ABOUT TO TAKE UP ELIJAH) He vanished from among men, says Josephus.

Latin:

CAPUT II.

Eliæ evecti in cælum pallio Elisæus Jordanem di- vidit, aquas sale sanat, pueros insultantes immissis ursis dilacerat.

Vers. 1. CVM LEVARE VELLET DOMINVS ELI- AM) ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἠφανίσθη, ait Josephus.

## 2:2
Ver. 2. THE LORD LIVES AND YOUR SOUL LIVES) That is, you. The sense is: as truly as God lives, so may you live. Concerning this type of swearing, see what we have said, which is not to be despised, in the second book of De Jure Belli ac Pacis, chapter 13, section 11.

Latin:

Vers. 2. VIVIT DOMINVS ET VIVIT ANIMA TVA) Id est, tu. Sensus est; quam vere vivit Deus, & ita vivas tu. De hoc jurandi genere vide quæ non spernenda diximus libro secundo de Jure Belli ac Pacis cap. 13. §. 11.

## 2:3
Ver. 3. DO YOU KNOW THAT TODAY THE LORD WILL TAKE YOUR MASTER FROM YOU] God was gradually accustoming those who lived with the prophets to prophecy, revealing to them now this, now that, of His counsels.

Latin:

Vers. 3. NVMQVID NOSTI QVIA HODIE DO- MINVS TOLLET DOMINVM TVVM A TE] Deus eos qui cum Prophetis vivebant, paulatim assuefaciebat Pro- phetiæ, nunc hoc, nunc illud de consiliis suis ipsis aperiens.

## 2:8
Ver. 8. WHICH WERE DIVIDED TO EITHER SIDE AND BOTH CROSSED OVER ON DRY GROUND) See what we said above at Joshua 3:16.

Latin:

Vers. 8. QVÆ DIVISÆ SVNT IN VTRAMQVE PARTEM ET TRANSIERVNT AMBO PER SICCVM) Vide quæ supra ad Jos. 3, 16.

## 2:9
Ver. 9. I PRAY THAT A DOUBLE PORTION OF YOUR SPIRIT MAY BE UPON ME) Some think Elisha is asking to have double the power of the Spirit compared to the spirit of Elijah, which would have been arrogant: whereas on the contrary he is asking to be as it were the firstborn among his disciples. For the firstborn received two parts of the inheritance, while the others received single parts. And

פי which is here in the Hebrew for a portion of the mouth, appears in Deut. 21:17, where there is a discussion about the right of primogeniture, but also in Zech. 13:8. See shortly at 15. This explanation holds itself more correctly than that of Angelomus, that the double spirit is the spirit of prophecy and of miracles; or that of Peter Damian, concerning the twice as many miracles of Elisha.

Latin:

Vers. 9. OPTO VT FIAT IN ME DVPLEX SPI- RITVS TVVS) Putant quidam poscere Elisæum ut du- plam habeat vim Spiritus ad spiritum Eliæ, quod super- bum fuerat: cum contra id postulet ut sit velut primogeni- tus inter discipulos ejus. Primogeniti enim de hæredita- te duas ferebant partes, cum cæteri ferrent singulas. Et

פי quod hic est in Hebræo pro portione fumi apparet Deut. 21, 17. ubi de jure primogenituræ sermo, sed & Zach. 13, 8. Vide mox 15. Rectius habet sese hæc explicatio, quam illa Angelomi, Spiritus duplex est Spiritus Prophetiæ, & miraculorum; vel Petri Damiani, de duplo pluribus miraculis Elisæi.

## 2:11
Ver. 11. A CHARIOT OF FIRE AND HORSES OF FIRE) Angels appearing in that form. Below 6:17. ELIJAH WENT UP BY A WHIRLWIND INTO HEAVEN) Josephus compares him with Enoch.

Latin:

Vers. 11. CVRRVS IGNEVS ET EQVI IGNEI) Angeli ea specie apparentes. Infra 6, 17. ASCENDIT ELIAS PER TVRBINEM IN COELVM) Cum Enocho consert Josephus.

## 2:12
Ver. 12. THE CHARIOT OF ISRAEL AND ITS HORSEMEN] In the Hebrew: His chariot and horsemen: He alludes to what he was seeing, and by a metaphorical manner of speaking shows that he himself had been the strength of the people, through prayers and doctrine.

Latin:

Vers. 12. CVRRVS ISRAEL ET AVRIGA EJVS] In Hebræo: Currus & equites ejus: Alludit ad id quod videbat, & metaphorico loquendi genere ostendit ipsum fuisse robur populi, per preces & doctrinam.

## 2:14
Ver. 14. EVEN NOW] In wondrous ways is translated what is here in the Hebrew אף הוא. The LXX placed the Hebrew word itself, ἀπφώ. Some, thinking that by that word אף הוא something secret and excellent is signified, translated it κρύφιος. The sense is: Where now is that God of Elijah: that is, let Him be present.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ETIAM NVNC] Miris modis vertitur quod hic in Hebræo est אף הוא. LXX. ipsam vocem Hebræam posuerunt ἀπφώ. Quidam voce illa אף הוא putantes aliquid arcanum & excellens significari, verterunt κρύφιος. Sensus est: Ubi nunc ille Deus Eliæ: id est, adsit.

## 2:21
Ver. 21. HE CAST SALT INTO IT) Which by nature renders waters not at all drinkable. Thus God, where He wills, shows Himself the Lord of nature.

Latin:

Vers. 21. MISIT IN ILLVM SAL) Quod per naturam aquas reddit minime potabiles. Ita Deus, ubi vult, ostendit se naturæ Dominum.

## 2:23
Ver. 23. THEY MOCKED HIM) As those brought up in idolatry, the despisers of the true God.

Latin:

Vers. 23. ILLVDEBANT EI] Vt in Idololatria educati veri Dei contemtores.

## 2:24
Ver. 24. HE CURSED THEM IN THE NAME OF THE LORD) See above 1, v. 10.

Latin:

Vers. 24. MALEDIXIT EIS IN NOMINE DOMINI) Vide supra 1. v. 10.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III.

Elisha gives water to the army of the King of Israel without rain and victory against Moab, who, being besieged on all sides, sacrifices his son.

Ver. 1. BUT JORAM THE SON OF AHAB REIGNED OVER ISRAEL] — — unequal to much greater things, knowing the measure of right, yet useful for such an age. To imitate Cato speaking in Lucan about Pompey.

Moreover, since it is said that Joram began to reign in the 18th year of Jehoshaphat, and in chapter 1, verse 17, the beginning of his reign is linked to the second year of Joram the son of Jehoshaphat, it must be held that Jehoshaphat in the 17th year of his reign took his son Joram into partnership of government, whence the 18th year of the Father was the second of the son in the shared kingdom.

Latin:

CAPUT III.

Elisæus exercitui Regis Israel aquam sine pluvia dat & victoriam contra Moab, qui undig obsessus filium suum immolat.

Vers. 1. JORAM VERO FILIVS ACHAB REGNAVIT SVPER ISRAEL] — — multo majoribus impar Nosse modum juris, tali tamen utilis ævo. Ut Catonem apud Lucanum de Pompejo loquentem imiter.

Cæterum cum anno Josaphati 18. dicitur regnare cepisse Joram, & cap. 1. v. 17. anno secundo Jorami filii Josaphat alligatur regni ejus initium, tenendum, quod Josaphat anno 17. regni sui filium Joram afciverit in regiminis consortium, unde annus 18. Patris erat secundus filii in regno socio.

## 3:4
Ver. 4. NOW MESHA KING OF MOAB FED MANY FLOCKS) In the Hebrew, word for word, it was 'he was a sheep-master,' as Cicero speaks in Verrine 4. Lesser kings gave tribute to greater ones from those things in which they abounded. Now the Moabites abounded in sheep, whence also their goddess was in the form of a sheep.

Latin:

Vers. 4. PORRO MESA REX MOAB NUTRIEBAT PECORA MVLTA) In Hebræo verbo ad verbum erat pecuarius, ut Cicero Verrina 4. loquitur. Reges minores majoribus vectigal dabant ex iis rebus quibus abundabant. Abundabant autem Moabitæ ovibus, unde & Deæ eorum in ovium forma.

## 3:5
Ver. 5. HE REBELLED AGAINST THE COVENANT) He had cast off the reverence of the greater empire: for it must not be translated 'is,' but 'was,' by way of recapitulation. Above 1, 1. What was said once is repeated for the coherence of the following history.

Latin:

Vers. 5. PRÆVARICATVS EST FEDUS) Exuerat reverentiam majoris imperii: vertendum enim non est, sed erat, κατ' ἐπάνοδον. Supra 1, 1. Semel dictum repetitur ad cohærentiam historiæ sequentis.

## 3:7
Ver. 7. MY PEOPLE, THY PEOPLE) Above 1 Kings 22, verse 5.

Latin:

Vers. 7. POPVLVS MEVS, POPVLVS TVVS) Supra 1. Reg. 22. v. 5.

## 3:9
Ver. 9. AND THE KING OF EDOM) That is, a prefect in place of a king, such as prefects are called by this name catachrestically, as above 22, 8, where the same word is used twice in the same verse in a different sense. See also Deuteronomy 33, verse 5, Judges 18, verse 1, Chapter 21, verse 24, and the things said there.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET REX EDOM) Id est, præfectus vice regis, quales præfecti καταχρηστικῶς hoc nomine vocantur, ut supra 22, 8. ubi eadem vox in eodem commate bis diverso sensu usurpatur. Vide & Deuter. 33. v. 5. Jud. 18. v. 1. C. 21. v. 24. & dicta ibi.

## 3:11
Ver. 11. WHO POURED WATER ON THE HANDS OF ELIJAH) Who ministered to him. The species for the genus.

Latin:

Vers. 11. QVI FUNDEBAT AQVAM SUPER MANVS ELIÆ) Qui ipsi ministrabat. Species pro genere.

## 3:13
Ver. 13.

WHAT HAVE I TO DO WITH THEE) Why do you present business to me?

Latin:

Vers. 13.

QVID MIHI ET TIBI EST) Quid mihi negotium exhibes?

## 3:15
Ver. 15.

BRING ME A HARPIST) To calm a disturbed mind. See what is said in 1 Samuel 10, v. 5, chapter 16, v. 17.

AND WHEN THE HARPIST PLAYED, THE HAND OF THE LORD CAME UPON HIM) Josephus: πρὸς τὸν ψάλλοντα ἔνθεος γενόμενος. The Hebrews say that the שכינה does not intervene amidst the torments of the mind. The contrary is in the New Testament.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ADDVCITE MIHI PSALTEN) Ad sedandum animum commotum. Vide quæ dicta 1. Samuel. 10. v. 5. cap. 16. v. 17.

CVMQVE CANERET PSALTES, FACTA EST SVPER EUM MANVS DOMINI) Josephus: πρὸς τὸν ψάλλοντα ἔνθεος γενόμενος. Ajunt Hebræi שכינה non intervenire inter animi angores. Contrarium in novo federe.

## 3:19
Verse 19.

AND YOU SHALL CUT DOWN EVERY FRUIT-BEARING TREE) We have said above that one must obey a prophet even when he commands something against special laws. That is what happens here. See Deut. 20, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

ET VNIVERSVM LIGNVM FRVCTIFERVM SVCCIDETIS) Prophetæ etiam contra leges speciales aliquid præcipienti parendum supra diximus. Id hic evenit. Vide Deut. 20, 19.

## 3:22
Verse 22. RED) Reddening in the setting sun.

Latin:

Vers. 22. RVBRAS) Rubentes adverso sole.

## 3:25
Vers. 25. SO THAT ONLY EARTHEN WALLS REMAINED) In the Hebrew: Until he left the stones in the wall of Cheroseth, that is, no constructed stones were found except in the walls of one city, Chareseth.

Vers. eod. AND THE CITY WAS SURROUNDED BY SLINGERS) I think those are meant whom Tacitus calls 'libratores' in Annals 2 and 13, who shake the walls with ballistae and other machines of that kind.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ITA VT MVRI TANTVM FICTILES RE- MANERENT) In Hebræo: Donec reliquit lapides in parie- te Cheroseth, id est, nulli lapides constructi reperiebantur nisi in muris unius urbis Chareseth.

Vers. eod. ET CIRCVMDATA EST CIVITAS A FVNDIBVLARIIS) Puto intelligi eos quos libratores vocat Tacitus Annal. 2. & 13. qui ballistis aliisque id genus machi- nis quassant mœnia.

## 3:26
Vers. 26. THAT THEY MIGHT BREAK THROUGH TO THE KING OF EDOM) That is, they might break through the hostile camps at that part where the prefect of Idumea was in charge.

Latin:

Vers. 26. VT IRRVMPERENT AD REGEM EDOM) Id est, per castra hostilia perrumperent ea parte, ubi curabat Idumææ præfectus.

## 3:27
Vers. 27. AND TAKING HIS FIRSTBORN SON WHO WAS TO REIGN IN HIS STEAD) Τὸν υἱὸν πρεσβύτερον, ὃς μετ' αὐτὸν βασιλεύειν ἔμελλεν, Josephus: His own, I say, not the prefect of Idumea's, as some infer from Amos 2:1, where a different history is referred to.

HE OFFERED A BURNT OFFERING) Namely to the God of the Israelites, as Josephus holds here, imitating the deed of Abraham, although not completed by him.

The King of Moab did not offer this burnt offering to the GOD of Israel, but to his own god, which Porphyry in Eusebius, book 4 of the Preparation, chapter 7, teaches that the Kings of the Phoenicians were also accustomed to do in extreme necessities: The Phoenicians, when they were suffering more severely from war, or famine, or even heat, would sacrifice one of their own kin, chosen by common vote, to Saturn.

UPON THE WALL) So that the Hebrews might see.

AND THERE WAS GREAT INDIGNATION IN ISRAEL) Because such a thing was done outside the commandment of God, and the odium of that deed might fall back upon the religion of the descendants of Abraham.

AND IMMEDIATELY THEY DEPARTED FROM HIM) They raised the siege, lest such a thing should happen again.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ARRIPIENSQVE FILIVM SVVM PRIMO- GENITVM QVI REGNATVRVS ERAT PRO EO) Τὸν υἱὸν πρεσβύτερον, ὃς μετ' αὐτὸν βασιλεύειν ἔμελλεν, Josephus: Suum, inquam, non Idumææ præfecti, ut quidam colligunt ex Amoso 2, 1. ubi alia respicitur historia.

OBTVLIT HOLOCAVSTVM) Nempe Deo Israelita- rum, ut hic habet Josephus, velut Abrahami factum, quan- quam ab eo non completum imitans.

Non DEO Israelis, sed suo Deo hoc holo- caustum obtulit Rex Moab, quod etiam Reges Phœnicum in extremis necessitatibus solitos fuisse Porphyrius apud Eusebium l. 4. de præparat. c. 7. docet: Phœnices, ubi gravius sive bello, sive fame, si- ve etiam æstu laborarent, necessariorum suorum ali- quem Saturno communibus addictum suffragiis im- molabant.

SVPER MVRVM) Vt aspicerent Hebræi.

ET FACTA EST INDIGNATIO MAGNA IN ISRAEL) Quod extra præceptum Dei tale quid fieret, invi- diaque ejus facti in religionem Abrahamidarum recideret.

STATIMQVE RECESSERVNT AB EO) Solverunt obsidionem, ne quid tale iterum fieret.

## 4:1 Argument
CHAPTER IV.

Elisha multiplies oil for a poor widow, obtains a son for the barren Shunammite, and restores the dead to life: He heals a pottage, and feeds many with a few loaves.

Vers. 1. AND BEHOLD THE CREDITOR COMES TO TAKE MY TWO SONS TO SERVE HIM) To lead them into bondage. By Hebrew law, children are the property of their parents. See what was said at Matthew 18:23. You may learn also elsewhere in Asia that children were sold by their parents' creditors from Plutarch in his Life of Lucullus. That the same law once obtained at Athens, from the same Plutarch in his Life of Solon. Also at Rome, from Dionysius of Halicarnassus, book 6.

Joseph, b. 9, c. 2, makes this woman the wife of Obadiah, 1 Kings 18:3, to whom GOD showed this reward for the Prophets sustained by her husband. So also Theodoret.

Latin:

CAPUT IV.

Elisæus viduæ pauperculæ oleum multiplicat, Su- namitidi sterili filium impetrat, ac mortuum resuscitat: Pulmentum sanat, panibus paucis multos cibat.

Vers. 1. ET ECCE CREDITOR VENIT VT TOL- LAT DVOS FILIOS MEOS AD SERVIENDVM SI- BI) Vt in nexum ducat. Liberi jure Hebræo res parentum. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 18, 23. Etiam alibi in Asia liberos venditos a parentum creditoribus discas ex Plutarcho in Lu- cullo. Idem jus olim Athenis obtinuisse, ex eodem Plutar- cho in Silone. Etiam Romæ ex Dionys. Halicarnassensi l. 6.

Hanc mulierem Joseph. l. 9. c. 2. uxorem Oba- diæ facit 1. Reg. 18, 3. cui DEUS hanc remuneratio- nem ob sustentatos a marito Prophetas exhibuerit. Ita & Theodor.

## 4:4
Verse 4. AND POUR INTO ALL THESE VESSELS) A hidden increase made by God, as above 17:12, 13, 14.

Cornelius thinks that angels continually suggested one thing and another, and oil, until all the vessels were filled, and that having done so they withdrew: But there was no need for that, since God could multiply the oil by a mere nod, as was done by Christ in the multiplication of the loaves.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET MITTE INDE IN OMNIA VASA HÆC) Incrementum latens a Deo factum, ut supra 17, 12. 13. 14.

Angelos continuo aliud, & aliud suggessisse oleum, donec omnia vasa implerentur, eoque fa- cto se subduxisse Cornelius putat: Sed eo opus non fuit, quum solo nutu Deus oleum multiplica- re potuerit, uti a Christo factum in multiplicatio- ne panum.

## 4:13
Verse 13. AND DOST THOU WISH TO SPEAK TO THE KING OR TO THE CAPTAIN OF THE HOST?) It is not an unworthy thing for Bishops, just as for Prophets, to commend miserable persons to Princes by their office. In the African Canons we have: It is honorable that Bishops provide intercession for those who are oppressed by unjust force, or if a widow is afflicted, or an orphan is despoiled. Then: That from any province whatsoever, Bishops should send petitions to that brother and our fellow-bishop who resides in the metropolis: so that he may dispatch both his Deacon and the petitions, granting letters of recommendation: in like manner to our brothers and fellow-bishops who at that time are staying in those regions and cities in which the happy and blessed Augustus governs the republic. But if a Bishop has friends in the palace, and desires to obtain something which is nevertheless honorable, he is not prohibited from asking and signifying through his Deacon to those whom he knows can provide kind intercession for the absent, if it is opportune. Again: But those who have come to Rome, as has been said, should hand over the petitions they have to our most holy brother and fellow-bishop of the Roman Church: so that he himself may first examine whether they are honorable and just, and provide diligence and solicitude so that they may be carried to the imperial court.

IN THE MIDST OF MY PEOPLE I DWELL) Soldiers are on the border, usually burdensome to the poor.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET VIS VT LOQVAR REGI SIVE PRIN- CIPI MILITIÆ?) Non indigna res est ut Prophetæ ita & Episcopi officio miserabiles personas commendare Principi- bus. In Canonibus Africanis habemus: Honestum est ut Epi- scopi intercessionem his præstent, qui iniqua vi opprimuntur, aut si vidua affligatur, aut pupillus exspolietur. Deinde: Ut de qua- libet provincia Episcopi ad eum fratrem & Coepiscum nostrum preces mittant, qui in metropoli consistit: ut ille & Diaconum ejus & supplicationes destinet, tribuens commendatitias epi- stolas: pari ratione ad fratres & Coepiscopso nostros, qui in illo tempore in his regionibus & urbibus morantur, in quibus felix & beatus Augustus rempublicam gubernat. Si vero habet Epi- scopus amicos in palatio, qui cupit aliquid, quod tamen hone- stum est, impetrare, non prohibetur per Diaconum suum ro- gare ac significare bis, quos scit benignam intercessionem ab- senti posse præstare, si tamen opportunum fuerit. Rursum: Qui vero Romam venerint, sicut dictum est, sanctissimo fratri & Coepiscopo nostro Romanæ Ecclesiæ preces, quas habent tra- dant: ut & ipse prius examinet, si honestæ & justæ sunt, & præstet diligentiam atque sollicitudinem, ut ad comitatum per- ferantur.

IN MEDIO POPVLI MEI HABITO) In limite sunt milites graves plerumque pauperibus.

Vers. 24. MINA) Veteres baculo minari dicebant pro propellere bovem aut asinum: posteriores minare, unde Galli mener: & par vox apud Italos & Hispanos ex recentiori Latinitate.

AND THE LORD HATH HID IT FROM ME) Until now I was ignorant of it. Similar to 2 Sam. 7:3.

ET DOMINVS CELAVIT A ME) Hactenus id ignorabam. Simile 2. Sam. 7, 3.

Verse 29. IF ANY MAN MEET THEE, SALUTE HIM NOT: AND IF ANY SALUTE THEE, ANSWER HIM NOT) That is, do not let anything take precedence over this business. See what is said at Luke 10:2.

AND TAKE MY STAFF) God very often employs certain signs that meet the eyes, so that it may be more evident that He does what He does in response to the prayers of the Prophets and to win authority for them. ET TOLLE BACVLVM MEVM) Deus plerunquè signa quædam in oculos occurrentia adhibet, quo magis pateat se Prophetarum precibus & ad auctoritatem ipsis conciliandam facere quæ facit. Vide infra 34. cui par historia supra 1. Reg. 17, 21. Vide & mox 5, 10. Suffecerat baculus, si mulier id credidisset. Confer Matth. 9. vers. 18. & similia.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V.

Elisha frees Naaman from leprosy, which is inflicted upon the greedy and simoniacal Gehazi.

Verse 1. FOR BY HIM THE LORD GAVE SALVATION TO SYRIA) For as the writer of the book on the Calling of the Gentiles says: We confess that the care of divine providence has never been lacking to the whole of mankind: which, although it has led the people chosen for itself by special institutions to piety, has nevertheless not withdrawn the gifts of its goodness from any nation of men. Orosius: This is always my firm and undoubted opinion, that God administers His help not only to His body, which is the Church, to which He bestows special gifts of grace on account of the faith of the believers, but also, moreover, administers His long-suffering and eternal clemency to all nations in this world.

Latin:

CAPUT V.

Elisæus Naaman a lepra liberat, quæ avaro & Simoniaco Giezi immittitur.

Vers. 1. PER ILLAM ENIM DEDIT DOMINVS SALVTEM SYRIÆ) Nam ut ait Scriptor libri de Vocatione Gentium: Confitemur quod nunquam universitati hominum divina providentiæ cura defuerit: quæ licet exceptum sibi populum specialibus ad pietatem duxerit institutis, nulli tamen nationi hominum bonitatis suæ dona subtraxit. Orosius: Mea semper hæc est & indubitata sententia, Deum adjutorium suum, non solum in corpore suo, quod est Ecclesia, cui specialia ob credentium fidem gratiæ dona largitur, sed etiam universis in hoc mundo gentibus insuper longanimem sui æternamque clementiam administrare.

Ver. 5. CHANGES OF RAIMENT) Εἵματα δ' ἐξημοιβὰ in Homer.

Vers. 5. MVTATORIA VESTIMENTORVM) Εἵματα δ' ἐξημοιβὰ Homero.

## 5:7
HE RENT HIS CLOTHES) As in deep mourning.

THAT I MAY KILL AND MAKE ALIVE) For leprosy is as it were the death of the skin. Num. 12, 12. Isa. 22, 18. where see what we shall say.

SEE HOW HE SEEKETH OCCASIONS AGAINST ME) προφάσεις, σκήψεις, προκαλύμματα: concerning which see what we have said in the second book, chapter 22, at the beginning, on the Law of War. Sophocles in the Trachiniae: ἔγκλημα μικρὸν αἰτίαν θ' ἑτοιμάσας ἐπιστρατεύει. This wicked custom of many princes is elegantly described under the name of the wolf in the first fable of Phaedrus, of which this is the moral: This fable is written for those men, Who with feigned causes oppress the innocent.

Latin:

SCIDIT VESTIMENTA SVA) Ut in gravi mœrore.

VT OCCIDERE POSSIM ET VIVIFICARE) Est enim lepra velut mors cutis. Num. 12, 12. Esa. 22, 18. ubi quæ dicemus vide.

VIDETE QVOD OCCASIONES QVÆRAT ADVERSVM ME) προφάσεις, σκήψεις, προκαλύμματα: de quibus vide quæ diximus libro secundo cap. 22. initio de Jure Belli. Sophocles Trachiniis: ἔγκλημα μικρὸν αἰτίαν θ' ἑτοιμάσας ἐπιστρατεύει. Mos hic improbus multorum principum eleganter sub lupi nomine describitur fabula prima Phædri, cujus hoc est ἐπιμύθιον: Hæc propter illos scripta est homines fabula, Qui fictis causis innocentes opprimunt.

Ver. 10. IN JORDAN) Jordan and the ground below 17 have respect to God presiding over those places.

Latin:

Vers. 10. IN JORDANE) Jordanis & humus infra 17. respectum habent ad Deum illis locis præsidentem.

Ver. 12. ABANA] Perhaps the Chrysorrhoas of Pliny.

Vers. 12. ABANA] Forte Chrysorrhoas Plinii.

PHARPHARVS) Est ejusdem nominis in Sabinis fluvius, Ovidio: - - amœnæ Farfarus undæ.

## 5:13
CERTE FACERE DEBVERAS) Not even when a master is commanding ought a servant to say, why? Much less ought men to say so to God. Rom. 11, 34.

OBSECRO IGITUR UT ACCIPIAS BENEDICTIONEM) That is, gifts. For the Hebrew בָרַךְ signifies not only to bless, but also to do good.

Latin:
