DE TRICLINIO) In Hebræo non est de sed in. Josephus: βαστάσασα μετ' αὐτῆς εἰς τὸ ταμεῖον. LXX. ἔκλεψεν αὐτὸν ἐκ μέσου τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ βασιλέως τῶν θανατουμένων, αὐτὸν καὶ τὴν τρο- φὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ ταμείῳ τῶν κλινῶν. Ergo prius in cubili fœmi- narum occultatus est, deinde in templo, loco ἀσυλίας.

## 11:3
Verse 3.

FURTHERMORE ATHALIAH REIGNED OVER THE LAND) By mere force, by no right. For the Hebrews had their brothers as Kings, not their sisters. Deuteronomy 17:15. Wherefore it is not to be wondered at if Jehoiada, both a good citizen and established in a high magistracy (for among that people the High Priesthood was also a magistracy) and bound by affinity to the care of the ward King, whose sister he had in marriage, drove out by force her who was reigning by force. He was a man of great spirit, a patriot, like the two Bruti.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

PORRO ATHALIA REGNAVIT SUPER TERRAM) Vi mera, nullo jure. Nam Hebræi fratres suos habebant Re- ges, non sorores. Devteron. 17, 15. Quare non mirandum est si Jojada & civis bonus & in magno magistratu constitutus (nam in illo populo etiam Pontificium erat magistratus) ac per affinitatem obstrictus ad curam Regis pupilli, cujus soro- rem in matrimonio habebat, vi regnantem vi depulit. Fuit is vir magni animi, φιλόπατρις, quales duo Bruti.

## 11:4
Verse 4.

AND TAKING THE CENTURIONS AND SOLDIERS) Here too the Seventy preserved the Hebrew words, τοὺς ἑκατοντάρχους τοῦ Χορρὶ καὶ τοῦ Ῥασίμ. Josephus says there were five of them (namely from 2 Chronicles 23:1) with whom Jehoiada communicated this great plan, that is to say, prefects, some of heavy armor, others of light troops. He took them, moreover, in addition to the Priests and Levites who were under Jehoiada, and to whom he simultaneously gave instructions for what follows. Thus Josephus, quite rightly and conveniently, in the said place of Chronicles 2:2.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

ET ASSUMENS CENTURIONES ET MILITES) Hic quoque septuaginta servarunt voces Hebræas, τοὺς ἑκατον- τάρχους τοῦ Χορρὶ καὶ τοῦ Ῥασίμ. Quinque eos fuisse ait Jose- phus (nempe ex 2. Paralipomenon 23, 1.) quibuscum ma- gnum hoc consilium communicavit Jojadas, præfectos sci- licet alios gravi armaturæ, alios velitibus. Assumsit autem, ad Sacerdotes & Levitas, qui Jojadæ suberant, & quibus simul præcepit quæ sequuntur. Sic Josephus recte admodum & convenienter dict. loc. Paralip. 2, 2.

## 11:6
Verse 6. A THIRD PART OF YOU SHALL ENTER ON THE SABBATH) That is, let them perform their service for seven days. See what I wrote on Luke 1:8. AND SHALL KEEP THE WATCH OF THE KING'S HOUSE) The sense is: the men of that first third part shall keep watch at the Northern part of the Temple, in which the King was being raised. BUT A THIRD PART SHALL BE AT THE GATE OF SUR) At the Eastern gate, towards the city. AND A THIRD PART SHALL BE AT THE GATE WHICH IS BEHIND THE DWELLING OF THE GUARDS) In the Hebrew: behind the runners: that was to the south: which part looked toward the palace from whence Athaliah was to come: one must read here in the Latin 'scutariorum' (of the guards), as below in verse 19. AND YOU SHALL KEEP THE WATCH OF THE HOUSE MESSA) Theodoret explains that 'messa' more correctly as 'from destruction', and adds that 'no harm might occur in the divine house'. That is, you shall take pains that no evil may come to the Temple from the palace. Verse 7. BUT TWO PARTS OF YOU) That is, of the Priests and Levites, as Josephus has it here from that place in Chronicles. 2, 7. ALL GOING OUT ON THE SABBATH) Whose service will be completed. SHALL KEEP THE WATCH OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD AROUND THE KING) That is, let them be bodyguards to the King as he comes out from that temporary dwelling of his into the courtyard. Everything was beautifully provided against any of Athaliah's machinations. Verse 9. AND TAKING EACH HIS MEN) From the Priests and Levites. Verse 10. SPEARS AND ARMS) For spears in the Hebrew is החנית, which the Rabbis and the Latin in Chronicles interpret as lances: the LXX, σειρομάσας. Josephus, δόρατα. For that which we have here as arms, in the Hebrew is השלטים, which the Rabbis interpret as shields: Josephus, quivers: the LXX read שלשים, for they translate it τρισσοὺς. They perhaps understood triple-layered breastplates.

Latin:

Verf. 6. TERTIA PARS VESTRVM INTROEAT SABBATO) Id est, per septem dies suam obeant ἐφημερίαν. Vide quæ ad Lucam 1, 8. ET OBSERVET EXCUBIAS DOMUS REGIS) Sen- sus est: illius primæ partis tertiæ homines excubias agent ad partem Septentrionalem Templi, in qua Rex educabatur. TERTIA AUTEM PARS SIT AD PORTAM SUR) Ad portam Orientalem, versus urbem. ET TERTIA PARS SIT AD PORTAM QUÆ EST POST HABITACULUM SCRUTARIORVM) In He- bræo: post cursores: id erat ad meridiem: quæ pars specta- bat regiam unde venire debebat Athalia: legendum hic in Latino scutariorum, ut infra 19. ET CUSTODIETIS EXCUBIAS DOMUS MESSA] Rectius illud μεσὰς Theodoretus explicat ἀπὸ διαφθορᾶς, ad- ditque ὥςε μηδεμίαν γενέσθαι βλάβην ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τῷ θείῳ. Id est, dabitis operam ne quid à regia mali Templo adveniat. Verf. 7. DUÆ VERO PARTES E VOBIS) Id est, ex Sa- cerdotibus & Levitis, ut hic habet Josephus ex loco illo Pa- ralip. 2, 7. OMNES EGREDIENTES SABBATO] Quorum ἐφη- μερία erit completa. CUSTODIANT EXCUBIAS DOMUS DOMINI CIRCA REGEM) Id est, Regi ex suo illo temporario habi- taculo in atrium prodeunti stipatores sunto. Pulchre provisa omnia contra quasvis Athaliæ molitiones. Verf. 9. ET ASSVMENTES SINGVLI VIROS SV- OS) Ex Sacerdotibus & Levitis. Verf. 10. HASTAS ET ARMA) Pro hastis in Hebræo est החנית, quod lanceas interpretantur Rabbini & Latinus in Paralipomenis: LXX. σειρομάσας. Josephus δόρατα. Pro eo quod arma hic habemus, in Hebræo est השלטים, quod cly- peos interpretantur Rabbini: Josephus, pharetras: LXX. le- gerunt שלשים, vertunt enim τρισσοὺς. Intellexerunt for- te loricas trilices.

## 11:12
Verse 12.

AND HE PUT UPON HIM THE DIADEM) Here too the LXX preserve the Hebrew word נזר. Josephus rightly interprets it as the royal crown. AND THE TESTIMONY) The oil of anointing, if we believe Josephus: if others, the book of the law by the precept of Deuteronomy 17:18. Their explanation does not displease me, who think that by this name are understood the phylacteries, which were attached to the crown through a small hole left in the crown in that part which was to be above the forehead. And those are said to be for a memorial. Exodus 13:9. Jerome's opinion is to be preferred here, which Tostatus and Cajetan on Deuteronomy also support, because it is explained thus in 2 Chronicles 23:11. Compare Deuteronomy 17, verse 18. LONG LIVE THE KING) As in 1 Kings 1:25 and 39.

Latin:

Verf. 12.

ET POSVIT SVPER EVM DIADEMA) Hic quo- que Hebræam vocem נזר servant LXX. Josephus recte interpretatur τὸν ςέφανον βασιλικόν. ET TESTIMONIVM) Oleum unctionis, si Josepho cre- dimus: si aliis, librum legis ex præcepto Devteronomii 17, 18. Mihi illorum explicatio non displicet, qui censent intelligi hoc nomine phylacteria, quæ annexa erant coronæ per caver- nulam in corona relictam in ea parte quæ futura erat supra frontem. Ea autem dicuntur esse לזכרון. Exod. 13, 9. Præferenda hic Hieronymi sententia, cui et- iam suffragatur Tostatus, & Cajetanus de Deutero- nomio, quia ita explicatur 2. Paralip. 23, 11. Conf. Deut. 17. v. 18. VIVAT REX) Vt 1. Reg. 1, 25. & 39.

## 11:14
Verse 14.

SHE SAW THE KING STANDING UPON THE TRIBUNAL) On that platform of which 2 Chronicles 6:13 and here below 23:3. The LXX here say ἐπὶ τῦ ςύλε. But Josephus, ἐπὶ τῆς σκηνῆς, which seems to be corrupted for ἐπὶ τῆς ςήλης. AND SHE CRIED OUT, CONSPIRACY, CONSPIRACY) A word used in a tumult, as appears in Isaiah 8:12.

Latin:

Verf. 14.

VIDIT REGEM STANTEM SVPER TRIBVNAL) In suggestu illo de quo 2. Paralip. 6, 13. & hic infra 23, 3. LXX. hic ἐπὶ τῦ ςύλε. At Josephus, ἐπὶ τῆς σκηνῆς, quod corru- ptum videtur pro ἐπὶ τῆς ςήλης. CLAMAVITQVE, CONJVRATIO, CONJVRATIO) Vox usurpata in tumultu, ut apparet Efa. 8, 12.

## 11:15
Verse 15.

OUTSIDE THE TEMPLE ENCLOSURES) Even here the LXX retained the Hebrew word σαδηρὼϑ, because of the uncertainty of its meaning. Josephus says this place was by the valley of the Kidron.

Latin:

Verf. 15.

EXTRA SEPTA TEMPLI) Etiam hic Ebræam vocem σαδηρὼϑ, ob fignificationis incertum retinuere LXX. Jose- phus hunc locum esse dicit ad vallem Cedronis.

## 11:16
Ver. 16.

BY THE WAY OF THE ENTRY OF THE HORSES BY THE PALACE) To that part through which the King's horses and mules (for Josephus names these here) were accustomed to be brought in.

Latin:

Verf. 16.

PER VIAM INTROITVS EQVORVM JVXTA PA- LATIVM) Ad eam partem per quam introduci solebant equi & muli (nam hos Josephus hic nominat) Regis.

## 11:17
Ver. 17.

AND JEHOIADA MADE A COVENANT BETWEEN THE LORD AND BETWEEN THE KING AND THE PEOPLE, THAT THEY SHOULD BE THE LORD'S PEOPLE) That is, he was the author then, so that both the King and the people might solemnly promise that they would each, for their own part, obey the laws of God. See what has been said on this matter in De Jure Belli ac Pacis, book 1, chapter 4, § 9, and Josephus in this place. AND BETWEEN THE KING AND THE PEOPLE] The people promised that the King's safety would be their concern. Thus the same Josephus here. For it was not the custom among the Hebrews for the King to promise anything to the people. Then, where that custom exists, it is not usually done after the coronation has already been completed.

Latin:

Verf. 17.

PEPIGIT ERGO JOJADA FOEDVS INTER DOMI- NVM ET INTER REGEM ET POPVLVM, VT ES- SET POPVLVS DOMINI) Id est, auctor tum fuit, ut tam Rex quam populus sancte promitterent se legibus Dei pro sua quemque parte parituros. Vide quæ hac de re dicta de Jure Belli ac Pacis libro 1. cap. 4. §. 9. & Josephum hoc loco. ET INTER REGEM ET POPVLVM] Populus promi- sit Regis salutem sibi curæ fore. Ita hic idem Josephus. Nam ut Rex populo quicquam promitteret, moris apud Hebræos non fuit. Tum ubi is mos est, ante coronationem, non ea jam peracta id fieri solet.

## 11:18
Ver. 18.

AND THEY SLEW MATHAN THE PRIEST OF BAAL BEFORE THE ALTARS) According to the law, Exod. 22:20. AND THE PRIEST APPOINTED OFFICERS OVER THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) He appointed gatekeepers from the Levites, who would observe that no unclean person should enter. Thus Josephus here from 2 Chron. 23:19.

Latin:

Verf. 18.

MATHAN QVOQVE SACERDOTEM BAAL OC- CIDERVNT CORAM ALTARI) Ex lege, Exod. 22, 20. ET POSVIT SACERDOS CUSTODIAS IN DOMO DOMINI) Ex Levitis janitores posuit, observaturos, ne quis immundus intraret. Ita hic Josephus ex 2. Paralip. 23, 19.

## 11:19
Vers. 19. AND THE CHERETHITES AND THE PELETHITES LEGIONS) By some error these words have crept into this place. For in the Hebrew it is: את הכרי ואת הרצים. And in the Greek τὸν Χορῥὶ καὶ τὸν Ῥασὶμ: with the Hebrew words retained, as above 4, where see the remarks. In Chronicles instead of these words there are others: ואת־האדירים ואת המושלים : where the Latin has, the most valiant men and the princes of the people. The Greeks: the mighty ones and the rulers of the people. AND HE SAT UPON THE THRONE OF KINGS) On the ancestral throne which Solomon had made 1 Kings 10, 18. IN THE HOUSE OF THE KING) That is, not far from the Palace. See above 16.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET CERETHI ET PHILETHI LEGIONES) Errore quodam hæ voces in hunc locum irrepserunt. Nam in He- bræo est: את הכרי ואת הרצים. Et in Græ- co τὸν Χορῥὶ καὶ τὸν Ῥασὶμ: retentis Hebræis vocibus, ut su- pra 4. ubi dicta vide. In Paralipomenis pro his vocibus aliæ sunt ואת־האדירים ואת המושלים : ubi Latinus, fortissimos viros ac principes populi. Græci: τοὺς δυ- νατοὺς καὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας τοῦ λαοῦ. ET SEDIT SVPER THRONVM REGVM) In Solio avito quod fecerat Salomo 1. Reg. 10, 18. IN DOMO REGIS) Id est, non procul a Regia. Vide su- pra 16.

## 12:1 Argument
CHAPTER XII. Joash restores the temple, redeems the war and the destruction of Jerusalem, is killed by his own servants.

Vers. 1. IN THE SEVENTH YEAR OF JEHU REIGNED JOASH) At the beginning. See above 10, 36. below 13, 1. Vers. 2. AND HE DID THAT WHICH IS GOOD BEFORE THE LORD ALL THE DAYS OF JEHOIADA THE PRIEST) Thus good Nero, as long as he used Seneca as his teacher. Vers. 4. AND JOASH SAID TO THE PRIESTS) It is the duty of kings to have care not only of profane matters, but also of sacred ones: to ensure that the priests perform their duty according to the law: that sacred buildings retain their condition: and to assign both efforts and money for that purpose. ALL THE MONEY OF THE HOLY THINGS THAT SHALL BE BROUGHT INTO THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD BY THEM THAT PASS THROUGH) He wishes to repair the Temple with three kinds of money, which under Athaliah's rule had fallen into decay in many parts. The first kind is that which pious foreigners gave, who had come to worship God in the court of the Temple, of whom there is mention 1 Kings 8, 41. WHICH IS OFFERED FOR THE PRICE OF THE SOUL] The second kind is the poll tax, which individual Israelites were bound to pay for the uses of the Temple, where it was judged to be necessary: that is, the didrachma, of which we treated in Matthew 17, 24, half a shekel, as Moses speaks in the law itself, where this census is instituted in Exodus 30, 13, and Josephus both there and in this place: who also teaches us that a shekel was worth four Attic drachmas. Therefore half a shekel is a didrachma. AND WHICH THEY BRING OF THEIR OWN WILL AND THE CHOICE OF THEIR HEART INTO THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD) The third kind of money is that which is given by the Israelites, with no one compelling, freely and liberally: after the example of that which we have in Exodus 25, 1, ch. 35, 5, ch. 36, 5, 6. Vers. 5. ACCORDING TO HIS ORDER) In the Hebrew: from those known to him: both here and below 7. THEY SHALL REPAIR THE RUINS OF THE HOUSE) The Latins would say, they shall maintain the repairs, as Macer speaks in the law Lex Julia. D. de L. Julia Repetundarum. The phrase 'sarta tecta' is often found in Livy, in Festus with the words 'sarta' and 'producit': and among others. Vers. 6. THEREFORE UNTO THE THREE AND TWENTIETH YEAR OF KING JOASH THE PRIESTS HAD NOT REPAIRED THE RUINS OF THE TEMPLE) Things committed to many are less correctly cared for: and frauds are more hidden. Vers. 7. DO NOT THEREFORE ANY MORE) Henceforth. BUT RENDER IT FOR THE REPAIR OF THE TEMPLE) Which you have already received. Vers. 8. AND THE PRIESTS WERE FORBIDDEN TO TAKE ANY MORE MONEY FROM THE PEOPLE, AND TO REPAIR THE RUINS OF THE HOUSE] The Greeks are better and more expressively according to the Hebrew: and the priests agreed not to take money from the people, and not to strengthen the 'bedek' (for they retained this Hebrew word here and above in the LXX) of the house. The meaning is, in this they obeyed the King, that they would not take money after that time: but not likewise that they should repair the Temple from the money already received. Theodoret interprets 'bedek' as the healing of things destroyed. Vers. 9. AND JEHOIADA THE HIGH PRIEST TOOK ONE CHEST) Thinking, as Josephus says, that the offerings which the people would make of their own accord would be sufficient, if they were managed in good faith, and there would be no need to add the poll tax. Understand 'chest' here as the treasury, from which also the part of the Temple where it was received its name. See what we have said on Mark 12, 41. Vers. 10. THE KING'S SCRIBE WENT UP) Whom the High Priest had wished to be present as an inspector for himself, lest he himself, after so many faults of the lesser priests, be sprinkled with suspicion. Furthermore, the King himself was present, as we learn in 2 Chronicles 24, 11, and from Josephus in this place. AND THEY POURED OUT) In the Hebrew: they bound. LXX.

and they tied up, that is, they put back into bags the money well counted, and that daily as much as had come in.

Latin:

CAPUT XII. Joas restaurat templum, redimit bellum & ex- cidium Hierosolymæ, à servis suis occidi- tur.

Vers. 1. ANNO SEPTIMO JEHV REGNAVIT JO- AS) Ineunte. Vide supra 10, 36. infra 13, 1. Vers. 2. FECITQVE QVOD BONVM EST CORAM DOMINO CVNCTIS DIEBVS JOJADÆ SACERDO- TIS) Sic bonus Nero, quamdiu Seneca usus est magistro. Vers. 4. DIXITQVE JOAS AD SACERDOTES) Re- gum est non profanarum tantum rerum, sed & sacrarum ha- bere curam: efficere ut Sacerdotes secundum legem officium faciant: ut ædes sacræ suum retineant statum: atque in id & operas & pecunias indicere. OMNEM PECVNIAM SANCTORVM QVÆ ILLA- TA FVERIT IN TEMPLO DOMINI A PRÆTEREVN- TIBVS) Triplici pecunia vult reparare Templum, quod sub Athaliæ imperio neglectum multis partibus conciderat. Pri- mum genus est id quod pii alienigenæ dabant, qui Deum in ambitu Templi adoraturi venerant, quorum mentio 1. Reg. 8, 41. QVÆ OFFERTUR PRO PRETIO ANIMÆ] Alte- rum genus est capitatio, quam pendere Israëlitæ singuli de- bebant in usus Templi, ubi opus esse judicaretur: id est, di- drachmum, de quo egimus Matth. 17, 24. dimidium sicli, ut lo- quitur Moses in ipsa lege, ubi hic census instituitur Exodi 30, 13. & Josephus tum ibi, tum hoc loco: qui etiam nos docet siclum valuisse quatuor drachmas Atticas. Ergo dimidium siclum est δίδραχμον. ET QVAM SPONTE ET ARBITRIO CORDIS SVI INFERVNT IN TEMPLVM DOMINI) Tertium pecu- niæ genus est, quod ab Israëlitis nemine cogente ultro ac liberaliter datur: ad exemplum ejus quod habemus Exod.25, 1. c. 35, 5. c. 36, 5. 6. Vers. 5. JVXTA ORDINEM SVVM) In Hebræo: a no- tis sibi: tum hic, tum infra 7. INSTAURENT SARTA TECTA DOMUS) Latini dicerent, præstent sarta tecta, ut loquitur Macer in l. Lex Ju- lia. D. de L. Julia Repetundarum. Vox sartorum tectorum est apud Livium sæpe, apud Festum vocibus sarta & produ- it: & apud alios. Vers. 6. IGITUR USQVE AD VIGESIMUM TER- TIUM ANNUM REGIS JOAS NON INSTAURAVE- RUNT SACERDOTES SARTA TECTA TEMPLI) Mi- nus recte curantur quæ committuntur multis: & magis la- tent fraudes. Vers. 7. NOLITE ERGO AMPLIUS) Posthac. SED AD INSTAURATIONEM TEMPLI REDDI- TE EAM) Quam jam accepistis. Vers. 8. PROHIBITIQVE SUNT SACERDOTES VL- TRA ACCIPERE PECUNIAM A POPULO, ET IN- STAURARE SARTA TECTA DOMUS] Melius & ad Hebræum expresfius Græci: καὶ συνεφώνησαν οἱ ἱερεῖς τοῦ μὴ λαβεῖν ἀργύριον παρὰ τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ τοῦ μὴ ἐνισχῦσαι τὸ βε- δέκ (nam hanc vocem Hebræam retinuere hîc & supra LXX.) τοῦ οἴκου. Sensus est, in hoc paruerunt Regi, ut pecuniam post id tempus non acciperent: at non item ut de jam accepta pe- cunia sartum tectum facerent Templum. βεδὲκ Theodore- tus interpretatur τῶν ἐφθαρμένων θεραπείαν. Vers. 9. ET TULIT JOJADA PONTIFEX GAZOPHTLACI- UM UNUM) Existimans, ut Josephus ait, oblationes quas sponte facturus esset populus suffecturas, si ex fide curaren- tur, neque opus fore adjungi capitationem. Gazophylacium hîc arcam intellige, unde & pars Templi, ubi ea erat, nomen accepit. Vide quæ dicta nobis ad Marcum 12, 41. Vers. 10. ASCENDEBAT SCRIBA REGIS) Quem Pontifex in- spectorem sibi adesse voluerat, ne qua & ipse, post tot mino- rum sacerdotum culpas, suspicione aspergeretur. Præterea Rex ipse aderat, ut discimus 2. Par. 24, 11. & ex Josepho hoc loco. EFFUNDEBANTQVE) In Hebræo: ligabant. LXX.

καὶ ἔσφιξαν, id est, in sacculos reponebant bene numeratam, idque diebus singulis quanta obvenerat.

## 12:11
Vers. 11. INTO THE HAND OF THEM THAT PRESIDED OVER THE MASONS] The contractors, not, as before, the priests. Already then the priestly order, venerable in itself, had begun to slip into vice, so that more faith was found among the common people. Yet for that reason no schism was made, nor should it have been made.

Latin:

Vers. 11. IN MANVM EORVM QVI PRÆERANT CÆMENTARIIS] Redemtorum, non, ut ante, Sacerdotum. Jam tum ordo sacerdotalis, per se venerandus, in vitium labi cœperat, ita ut in plebe plus fidei reperiretur. Neque tamen ob id schisma aut factum est, aut fieri debuit.

## 12:13
Vers. 13. BUT NEVERTHELESS THERE WERE NOT MADE OF THE SAME MONEY BASINS FOR THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD, AND FLESHHOOKS, AND CENSER, AND TRUMPETS, AND ANY VESSEL OF GOLD AND SILVER] The best meaning is that which the LXX have: but they shall not be made. It must be supplied, the King had commanded, namely that no part of the money liberally contributed should be spent on the vessels of the Temple, before the building of the Temple itself had received its integrity. Thus this passage will be best reconciled with that in 2 Chronicles 24, 14. Nor did Josephus understand it otherwise. In the version of the LXX, for 'silver censers', it seems one should read 'thuias', that is, censers, which the interpreters of Chronicles called 'thuiscas'.

Latin:

Vers. 13. VERVMTAMEN NON FIEBANT EX EADEM PECVNIA HYDRIÆ TEMPLI DOMINI ET FVSCINVLÆ, ET THVRIBVLA, ET TVBÆ, ET OMNE VAS AVREVM ET ARGENTEVM] Optimus sensus est, quem habent LXX. πλὴν ὐ ποιηθήσονται. Supplendum autem est, Rex præceperat, nempe ne pecuniæ liberaliter contributæ pars ulla erogaretur in vasa Templi, priusquam ædificium ipsum Templi suam integritatem accepisset. Ita hic locus optime conciliabitur cum illo 2. Par. 24, 14. Neque aliter accepit Josephus. In versione LXX. pro θύσας ἀργυρᾶς, legendum videtur θύας, id est, thuribula, quas θυΐσκας dixere interpretes Paralipomenon.

## 12:15
Vers. 15.

AND THERE WAS NO ACCOUNT MADE WITH THOSE MEN WHO RECEIVED THE MONEY TO DISTRIBUTE IT TO THE WORKMEN, BUT THEY DEALT WITH IT IN FAITH] The meaning is: an account of the money was not demanded from the contractors, because they had to show the approved work at their own faith and their own risk. This is what the LXX also intended: for they do it in their faith: the King trusted them.

So also the Chaldean, Vatablus, and others.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ET NON FIEBAT RATIO IIS HOMINIBVS QVI ACCIPIEBANT PECVNIAM VT DISTRIBVERENT EAM ARTIFICIBVS, SED IN FIDE TRACTABANT EAM] Sensus est: non exigebatur à redemtoribus ratio pecuniæ, quia sua fide suoque periculo opus probatum exhibere debebant. Hoc est quod & LXX. voluerunt ὅτι ἐν πίστ ἀυτῶν ποιοῦσιν : ipsis credebat Rex.

Sic & Chaldæus, Vatablus, & alii.

## 12:16
Verse 16.

BECAUSE IT WAS THE PRIESTS'] From the law Lev. 5, 16.

Vatablus rendered the whole verse thus: the money that remained after the victim for the trespass or sins was bought was not brought into the house of the Lord, because it belonged to the priests. For those who lived far from the temple did not send a victim, but money to one of the priests, who bought the victim, and what remained of the money after the victim was bought, that went to the benefit of the priests.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

QVIA SACERDOTVM ERAT] Ex lege Lev. 5, 16.

Vatabl. ita versum totum reddidit: pecunia quæ supererat emta victima pro delicto vel peccatis, non inferebatur in ædem Domini, quod Sacerdotum esset. Qui enim longe à templo habitabant, non victimam, sed pecuniam mittebant ad unum è Sacerdotibus, qui victimam emebat, & quod reliquum erat pecuniæ empta victima, id cedebat in utilitatem Sacerdotum.

## 12:17
Verse 17.

HE FOUGHT AGAINST GATH) A city of the Philistines 2 Sam. 1, v. 20, which David had made his own in war 2 Sam. 8, v. 1.

AND HE SET HIS FACE TO GO UP TO JERUSALEM) That is, he did everything by which it would be believed that he was going against Jerusalem. See what is said at Luke 9, 51.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

PVGNABAT CONTRA GETH) Vrbem Philistinorum 2. Sam. 1. v. 20. quam David bello suam fecerat 2. Sam. 8. v. 1.

ET DIREXIT FACIEM SVAM VT ASCENDERET IN JERVSALEM] Id est, omnia fecit per quæ crederetur iturus contra Hierosolyma. Vide quæ ad Lucam 9, 51.

## 12:18
Verse 18.

JOASH KING OF JUDAH TOOK ALL THE SANCTIFIED THINGS) We had a similar passage above 1 Kings 15, v. 18, where see what is said.

AND HE SENT TO HAZAEL KING OF SYRIA, AND HE DEPARTED FROM JERUSALEM) Thus often the Roman Emperors removed foreign nations from their borders with a great amount of money.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

TVLIT JOAS REX JVDA OMNIA SANCTIFICATA) Simile habuimus supra 1. Reg. 15. v. 18. ubi quæ dicta sunt vide.

MISITQVE HAZAELI REGI STRIÆ, ET RECESSIT AB JERVSALEM) Sic sæpe Romani Imperatores externas gentes à finibus suis magna vi pecuniæ amoverunt.

## 12:20
Verse 20. BUT HIS SERVANTS AROSE) The punishment for the killing of Zechariah the son of Jehoiada. See Chronicles.

IN THE HOUSE OF MILLO) Concerning which see above 1 Kings 9, 24. In the house, that is, at the house: as above.

IN THE DESCENT OF SILLA) By which one descends from the house to the public road, which with an added letter is called elsewhere מסלוה.

Latin:

Vers. 20. SVRREXERVNT AVTEM SERVI EJVS) Pœna occisi Zachariæ filii Jojadæ. Vide Paralipomena.

IN DOMO MELLO) De qua supra 1. Reg. 9, 24. In domo, id est, apud domum: ut supra.

IN DESCENSV SELLA) Qua descenditur ex domo in viam publicam, quæ cum adjectitia litera alibi dicitur מסלוה.

## 12:21
Verse 21.

FOR JOSACHAR THE SON OF SHIMEATH AND JEHOZABAD THE SON OF SHOMER) Friends of Jehoiada, as Josephus maintains.

AND THEY BURIED HIM WITH HIS FATHERS) That is, in the customary manner, in the city of David, in Zion, not in the sepulchres of the Kings, which Josephus notes here from the Chronicles: some honor was shown to him, but not the highest, because the final part of his life had declined from what was right. See what we have said in the first book of The Law of War and Peace, chapter three, § 16.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

JOSACHAR NAMQVE FILIVS SEMAATH ET JOZABVD FILIVS SOMER) Amici Jojadæ, ut vult Josephus.

ET SEPELIERVNT EVM CVM PATRIBVS SVIS) Id est, more solito, in civitate David, in Sione, non in sepulchris Regum, quod hic ex Paralipomenis notat Josephus: aliquis illi honos habitus, non summus, quia suprema pars vitæ à recto declinaverat. Vide quæ diximus libro primo de Jure Belli ac Pacis capite tertio §. 16.

## 13:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIII.

Kings of Israel. Jehoahaz, Joash, and Jeroboam. Elisha before his death promised a triple victory to Joash: having died, he raised a dead man by the contact of his bones. Death of Hazael, whose successor, his son Ben-hadad, is defeated for the third time by Joash.

Verse 1.

IN THE TWENTY-THIRD YEAR OF JOASH) At the beginning. See above 12.

JEHOAHAZ THE SON OF JEHU REIGNED OVER ISRAEL IN SAMARIA SEVENTEEN YEARS) That is, in such a way that he began the seventeenth year. See below 10.

Latin:

CAPUT XIII.

Reges Israel. Joachaz, Joas, & Jeroboam. Elisaus ante mortem victoriam triplicem Joaso promisit: mortuus mortuum contactu ossium suorum suscitavit. Mors Hasael, cujus successor filius Benadad tertio vincitur à Joaso.

Vers. 1.

ANNO XXIII. JOAS) Ineunte. Vide supra 12.

REGNAVIT JOACHAZ FILIVS JEHV SVPER ISRAEL IN SAMARIA DECEM ET SEPTEM ANNIS) Id est, ita ut annum decimum & septimum inchoaret. Vide infra 10.

## 13:4
Ver. 4.

BUT JEHOAHAZ BESOUGHT THE FACE OF THE LORD, AND THE LORD HEARD HIM] Because the temporal diversity will not be a wonder, if afterwards God is milder for things subdued, who was previously more austere for things unsubdued, says Tertullian. Josephus here concerning God: receiving repentance as a virtue. This is the one cause for God to show mercy, to which a second was added, the memory of ancestral virtues: below 23.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

DEPRECATVS EST AVTEM JOACHAZ FACIEM DOMINI, ET AVDIVIT EVM DOMINVS] Quia nec mirum erit diversitas temporalis, si postea Deus mitior pro rebus edomitis, qui retro austerior pro indomitis, ait Tertullianus. Josephus hic de Deo: τὴν μετάνοιαν ὡς ἀρετὴν ἐκδεχόμενος. Hæc una Deo causa miserandi, ad quam accessit altera, virtutum avitarum memoria: infra 23.

## 13:10
Ver. 10.

IN THE THIRTY-SEVENTH YEAR OF JOASH KING OF JUDAH) After that year was completed. See above 1.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

ANNO TRIGESIMO SEPTIMO JOAS REGIS JVDA) Post eum annum impletum. Vide supra 1.

## 13:14
Ver. 14. NOW ELISHA WAS SICK) He was sick, and soon, he had gone down: for it is a retroversion.

THE CHARIOT OF ISRAEL AND THE HORSEMAN THEREOF) See above 2, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ELISÆVS AVTEM ÆGROTABAT) Ægro- taberat, & mox, descenderat: est enim retrogressio.

CVRRVS ISRAELIS ET AVRIGA EJVS) Vide supra 2, 12.

## 13:15
Ver. 15. AND THE LORD GAVE A SAVIOUR TO ISRAEL.

Not an Angel, nor Elisha, as some wish, but Joash, strengthened by Elisha, who overcame the Syrians three times. Since during the whole time of Jehoahaz Israel was afflicted by the Syrians, ver. 22, Jehoahaz did indeed obtain by his prayers the liberation of the people, but it was to be performed not in his time, but in the time of his son Joash. Compare v. 7.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET DEDIT DOMINVS SALVATOREM ISRAEL.

Non Angelum, nec Elisæum, ut nonnulli volunt, sed Joasum ab Elisæo confortatum, qui tertio Syros superavit. Quum toto tempore Joachaz afflictus Israel fuerit à Syris vers. 22. impetravit quidem precibus liberationem populi Joachaz, at non suo sed filii sui Joas tempore præstandam. Conf. v. 7.

## 13:17
Ver. 17. OPEN THE EASTERN WINDOW)

Because the part of Syria lies opposite to the east of the land of Israel.

IN APHEK) So also the Greeks. Nothing, however, forbids it being translated 'vehemently'.

Latin:

Vers. 17. APERI FENESTRAM ORIENTALEM)

Quia pars Syriæ ad Orientem objacet terræ Israelis.

IN APHEC) Sic & Græci. Nihil tamen vetat verti vehementer.

## 13:18
Ver. 18. TAKE THE ARROWS) Take the arrows, supply 'others'.

Elisha had indeed predicted a signal victory for him: but as often as he was to be victorious, since he did not yet know it, he was warned by God to learn from this sign.

Latin:

Vers. 18. TOLLE SAGITTAS) Sume sagittas, supple alias.

Victoriam quidem insignem ei prædixerat Elisæus: sed quoties victor futurus esset cum nondum sciret, monebatur a Deo ex hoc signo discere.

## 13:20
Ver. 20. THE MAN REVIVED) A greater light daily for the hope of another life.

And God shows how dear his saints are to him, even when dead. The same reason was why God allowed so many miracles to occur at the monuments of the martyrs, as even Porphyry acknowledged, as we noted in the third book on the Truth of the Christian Religion.

There is no doubt that a greater light arose in later times concerning eternal life, especially at the coming of Christ: But that the ancients could have had no hope of another life from the divine revelations and writings of their own times is a Socinian error of Grotius, already noted several times.

Latin:

Vers. 20. REVIXIT HOMO) Major indies lux ad spem vitæ alterius.

Et ostendit Deus quam sibi cari sint sancti, etiam mortui. Eadem causa fuit cur ad martyrum monumenta tam multa mira Deus siverit fieri, agnoscente etiam Porphyrio, ut ad tertium librum de Veritate Religionis Christianæ annotavimus.

Majorem lucem posterioribus temporibus ortam esse de æterna vita, præsertim sub adventum Christi, nullum est dubium: Sed spem vitæ alterius nullam habere potuisse antiquos è divinis temporum suorum revelationibus & scriptis, error Grotii Socinianus est, jam aliquoties notatus.

## 13:24
Ver. 24.

AND BENHADAD HIS SON REIGNED IN HIS STEAD) Who renewed the old name of the Kings of Syria, perhaps born of the maternal line from those ancient Kings.

Latin:

Vers. 24.

REGNAVITQVE BENADAD FILIVS EJVS PRO EO) Qui vetus Syriæ Regum nomen renovavit, materno forte genere ortus ex priscis illis Regibus.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV. The deeds of Amaziah King of Judah, who was defeated and captured in war with Jehoash King of Israel, Jerusalem was plundered, and he was killed by his own people and had his son Azariah as successor. To Jehoash succeeded his son Jeroboam, and to him likewise his son Zechariah in the kingdom of Israel.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV. Amasiæ Regis Judæ gesta, qui in bello cum Joas Rege Israel victus & captus est, Hierosolyma spoliata & à suis occisus filium habuit successorem Azariam. Joaso filius Jeroboam & huic itidem filius Zacharias in regno Israel successit.

## 14:3
Ver. 3.

ACCORDING TO ALL THAT JOASH HIS FATHER DID, HE DID) He stained excellent praise with a base end, as do many Kings.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

JVXTA OMNIA QVÆ FECIT JOAS PATER SVVS, FECIT) Egregiam laudem fine turpi maculavit, ut Regum multi.

## 14:5
Ver. 5.

HE SLEW HIS SERVANTS WHO HAD KILLED HIS FATHER) Such crimes are punished even by those who enjoy the success of them.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

PERCVSSIT SERVOS SVOS QVI INTERFECERANT PATREM SVVM) Puniunt talia facinora etiam qui successu fruuntur.

## 14:6
Ver. 6.

AS THE LORD COMMANDED SAYING] Deut. 24, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

SICVT PRÆCEPIT DOMINVS DICENS] Deuter. 24, 16.

## 14:7
Verse 7.

HE SMOTE EDOM) Alone, having rejected the alliance of the Israelites, which he had bought at a great price: concerning which matter in the Chronicles

For the Idumeans had rebelled against the Jews 60 years before, from the sixth year of Joram King of Judah to the 12th of Amaziah, whom he defeated again, and forced to serve Judah: 2 Chron. 21, 8. chap. 25, 11. After this victory he fell into idolatry, worshipped the gods of the Idumeans, and therefore was smitten and captured by Joash King of Israel, 2 Chron. 25, v. 20.

AND HE TOOK THE ROCK IN BATTLE] A city of Arabia, whence the name of Arabia Petraea. By the Hebrews and Arabs that city is called Sela. The Chronicles, and Josephus here, add that the captives were cast down from that rock, which gave the Greek name to the city.

That city was afterwards restored by Ptolemy Philadelphus and received its name from him, being called Philadelphia.

AND HE CALLED THE NAME OF IT JOKTHEEL) Obedience to God: and that for this reason, because in the captured city he established the laws of Moses.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

IPSE PERCVSSIT EDOM) Solus, repudiata, quam magno emerat, Israelitarum societate: de qua re in Paralipomenis

REbellarant enim Idumæi Judæis ante 60. annos à sexto Joram Judæ R. ad 12. Amaziæ, quos rursum debellavit, & Judæ servire coegit: Par. 21, 8. cap. 25, 11. post hanc victoriam in idololatriam lapsus, coluit Deos Idumæorum, ideoque cæsus & captus est à Joas Rege Israelis, 2. Paralip. 25. v. 20.

ET APPREHENDIT PETRAM IN PRÆLIO] Ara- biæ urbem, unde Arabiæ Petrææ nomen. Hebræis & Ara- bibus ea urbs Sela dicitur. Captivos ab ea rupe, quæ Græ- cum nomen urbi dedit, præcipitatos addunt paralipomena, & hic Josephus.

Urbs illa postea à Ptolemæo Philadelpho re- staurata nomen ab eodem accepit, Philadelphia nuncupata.

VOCAVITQVE NOMEN EJVS JECTEHEL) Obe- dientia Deo: idque ideo, quia in capta urbe jura Mosis con- stituit.

## 14:8
Verse 8. COME AND LET US SEE ONE ANOTHER) Sophocles says in the Antigone: Δείξας ἐν ἀνθρώποισι τὴν ἀβυλίαν Ὅσῳ μέγισον ἀνδρὶ πρόσκειται κακόν. But in the Suppliants, when Theseus says: Εὐψυχίαν ἔσπευσας ἀντ’ ἐυβυλίας, Admetus, taught by his own misfortune, well replies: Ὁ δή γε πολλοὺς ὤλεσε σρατηλάτας.

Latin:

Vers. 8. VENI ET VIDEAMUS NOS) Δείξας ἐν ἀνθρώποισι τὴν ἀβυλίαν Ὅσῳ μέγισον ἀνδρὶ πρόσκειται κακόν. ait in Antigone Sophocles. At in supplicibus dicenti Theseo: Εὐψυχίαν ἔσπευσας ἀντ’ ἐυβυλίας, bene respondet Admetus suo malo edoctus: Ὁ δή γε πολλοὺς ὤλεσε σρατηλάτας.

## 14:9
Verse 9. THE THISTLE OF LEBANON SENT TO THE CEDAR) A fable of the kind in Judges 9, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 9. CARDUUS LIBANI MISIT AD CEDRUM) αἶνος qualis Jud. 9, 8.

## 14:10
Verse 10. THOU HAST INDEED SMITTEN EDOM, AND THINE HEART HATH LIFTED THEE UP] For Fortune makes fools of those whom she favors much. And in prosperous circumstances, as Tacitus says, even excellent leaders become insolent.

WHY DOST THOU PROVOKE EVIL?) Seneca well says: It is not expedient to disturb a happy state.

Latin:

Vers. 10. PERCUTIENS INVALUISTI SUPER EDOM, ET SUBLEVAVIT TE COR TUUM] Nam Fortuna multum quos fovet, stultos facit. Et rebus secundis, ut ait Tacitus, etiam egregii duces insole- scunt.

QVARE PROVOCAS MALUM?) Bene Seneca: Non expedit concutere felicem statum.

## 14:12
Verse 12. AND JUDAH WAS PUT TO THE WORSE BEFORE ISRAEL, AND THEY FLED EVERY MAN TO HIS TENTS) A panic terror seized them, of which we have already had some examples elsewhere: that is, φόβος αἰφνίδιος κὰι κατάπλη- ξις ὅταν θεὸς ἐκ δυσμενὴς ὧν τίθησι, as Josephus speaks very prudently here.

Latin:

Vers. 12. PERCUSSUSQVE EST JUDA CORAM ISRAEL, ET FUGERUNT UNUSQVISQVE IN TABERNACU- LA SVA) Panicus illos terror invasit, cujus alibi exempla jam aliquot habuimus: id est, φόβος αἰφνίδιος κὰι κατάπλη- ξις ὅταν θεὸς ἐκ δυσμενὴς ὧν τίθησι, ut hic valde prudenter lo- quitur Josephus.

## 14:13
Ver. 13. AND HE BROKE DOWN THE WALL OF JERUSALEM FROM THE GATE OF EPHRAIM, EVEN UNTO THE CORNER GATE, FOUR HUNDRED CUBITS) So that the city might always be open to enemies. Totila did the same at Rome.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET INTERRUPIT MVRVM JERVSALEM A POR- TA EPHRAIM, VSQVE AD PORTAM ANGULI QVADRINGENTIS CUBITIS) Ut Urbs hostibus semper pateret. Idem Romæ fecit Totilas.

## 14:15
ver. 15. FROM THE ENTERING OF EMATH. Emath in the tribe of Naphtali, adjacent to the Syrians, not far from Damascus, was an entrance and a gate, as it were, into the Holy Land; it was later called Epiphania after Antiochus Epiphanes, who reigned there. But how are Emath and Damascus called cities of Judah in verse 18, in Israel? Salianus and Sanctius answer that they were subjugated by David, but afterwards occupied by the Syrians, and here restored to Israel: as if to say, Jeroboam brought it about that Damascus and Emath, once subdued and made tributary to David, and thus numbered to the tribe of Judah, should now be tributary to himself and to Israel.

Latin:

vers. 15. AB INTROITU EMATH. Emath in tribu Naphtali contigua Syris, non procul à Damasco, ingressus erat & porta quasi in terram sanctam, ab Antiocho Epiphane, qui in ea regnavit, postea dicta Epiphania. Quomodo ve- ro Emath & Damascus civitates Judæ dicuntur vers. 18. in Israel? Salianus & Sanctius respon- dent eas à Davide subjugatas, sed deinde à Syris occupatas, hic Israeli restitutas: q. d. Jeroboam fecit ut Damascus & Emath olim subactæ, & tri- butariæ Davidi redditæ, adeoque tribui Juda annu- meratæ jam sibi & Israeli forent tributariæ.

## 14:19
Ver. 19. AND A CONSPIRACY WAS MADE AGAINST HIM IN JERUSALEM) The word קשר which is here in the Hebrew, is not usually taken in a good sense. Therefore this deed is not approved: but God shows that He knows how to use even the works of the wicked to execute His judgments.

AND THEY SENT AFTER HIM TO LACHISH) Namely, secret assassins to kill the King, as Josephus says here, much more correctly than those who say that the day was appointed for the King by the conspirators, as if they had been participants in his conspiracy, which they praise. We have a similar deed above 12:20 and below 15:10, 15, in which places there is the same word קשר.

Latin:

Vers. 19. FACTAQVE EST CONTRA EUM CONJURATIO IN JERUSALEM) Vox קשר quæ hic est in Hebræo, non solet sumi in bonam partem. Non ergo probatur hoc faci- nus: sed ostendit Deus se etiam malorum opera uti nosse ad judicia sua exequenda.

MISERUNTQVE POST EUM IN LACHIS) Nempe percussores clancularios, qui Regem interficerent, ut hic Jose- phus, multo rectius quam qui, quasi participes ejus conjura- tionis fuissent, quam laudant, à conjuratis Regi ajunt dictum diem. Simile factum habuimus supra 12,20. & infra 15. v. 10. 15. in quibus locis est idem verbum קשר.

## 14:21
Ver. 21. BUT ALL THE PEOPLE OF JUDAH TOOK AZARIAH, WHO WAS SIXTEEN YEARS OLD, INSTEAD OF HIS FATHER AMAZIAH] Those conspirators would not have done that. Whence it appears that their deed displeased the people, as also above 13:1. We have a similar conspiracy, likewise disapproved, below chapter 21:24.

Latin:

Vers. 21. TULIT AVTEM VNIVERSVS POPVLVS JVDÆ AZARIAM NATUM ANNOS SEDECIM, PATRE EJVS AMASIA] Id non fecissent conjurati illi. Vnde ap- paret eorum factum displicuisse populo, ut & supra 13,1. Si- milem conjurationem improbatam pariter habemus infra cap. 21, 24.

## 14:22
Ver. 22. HE BUILT ELATH, AND RESTORED IT TO JUDAH) Having snatched it from the Idumeans. See Deut. 2:8.

Latin:

Vers. 22. IPSE ÆDIFICAVIT ELATH, ET RESTITUIT EAM JVDÆ) Ereptam Idumæis. Vide Deut. 2. v. 8.

## 14:25
Ver. 25. HE RESTORED THE COASTS OF ISRAEL FROM THE ENTERING OF EMATH] See Num. 34:8.

EVEN UNTO THE SEA OF THE PLAIN) A lake in those level places of Idumea, which are mentioned in Deuteronomy 2:8.

BY HIS SERVANT JONAH THE SON OF AMITTAI THE PROPHET) From this we learn at what time that Jonah lived, whose book we have among the Minor Prophets.

WHO WAS OF GATH. Epiphanius, Theodoret, and Rupert understand it as Gath of the Philistines, but 'in Opher' is added, so that Gath in Zebulun is designated, Josh. 19. v. 13.

Latin:

Vers. 25. IPSE RESTITVIT TERMINOS ISRAEL AB IN- TROITU EMATH] Vide Num. 34, 8.

VSQVE AD MARE SOLITVDINIS) Lacum in locis illis campestribus Idumææ, quorum mentio Deuteron. 2. v. 8.

PER SERVUM SUUM JONAM FILIUM AMATHI PROPHETAM) Hinc discimus quo tempore vixerit Jonas ille, cujus librum inter minores Prophetas habemus.

QUI ERAT DE GETH. Philistinorum Gath intelligunt Epiph. Theo- dor. Rupert. sed additur in Opher, ut designetur Geth in Zabulon Jos. 19. v. 13.

## 14:26
Ver. 26.

TO THOSE SHUT UP IN PRISON AND THE LAST) This is the same manner of speaking here in the Hebrew as we had in 1 Kings 14. v. 10. & 21. v. 21.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

AD CLAUSOS CARCERE ET EXTREMOS) Idem hic in Hebræo loquendi genus quod habuimus 1. Reg. 14. v. 10. & 21. v. 21.

## 14:27
Ver. 27.

AND THE LORD DID NOT SAY THAT HE WOULD BLOT OUT THE NAME OF ISRAEL FROM UNDER HEAVEN, BUT HE SAVED THEM BY THE HAND OF JEROBOAM THE SON OF JOASH) That is, since He had not determined to blot out the people, He raised up a deliverer for them.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

NEC LOCVTVS EST DOMINVS VT DELERET NOMEN ISRAEL DE SUB COELO, SED SALVAVIT EOS IN MANU JEROBOAM FILII JOAS) Id est, cum non constituisset delere populum, vindicem ei excitavit.

## 14:28
Ver. 28.

AND HOW HE RESTORED DAMASCUS) That is, once possessed by David and his descendants, as can be seen in 2 Sam. 8. v. 6, and later lost when the arms of the Syrians prevailed, above 13. v. 3, he subjected it again to the kingdom of Israel.

AND HAMATH TO JUDAH) Which David had once added to the kingdom of Judah, 2 Sam. 8. v. 14. The Edomites, rebelling, had made it their own: now the King of Israel snatches it from the Edomites. Thus the possessions of cities are as changeable as those of fields, concerning some of which is this epigram of Lucian:

I was once the field of Achaemenides, now of Menippus, / And again I shall pass from one to another. / For he too thought he possessed me, and again this one / Thinks so; but I am entirely no one's, but Fortune's.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

ET QUOMODO RESTITUIT DAMASCVM) Id est, olim a Davide posterisque ejus possessam, ut videre est 2. Sam. 8. v. 6. postea amissam prævalentibus Syrorum armis, su- pra 13. v. 3. Israelis regno iterum subjecit.

ET EMATH JVDÆ) Quam Judæ regno olim adjecerat David 2. Sam. 8. v. 14. Eam Idumæi rebellantes suam fece- rant: nunc Rex Israelis eripit Idumæis. Ita ambulatoriæ sunt urbium possessiones non minus quam agrorum, de quo- rum aliquo hoc est Luciani Epigramma:

Ἀγρὸς Ἀχαιμενίδε γενόμην πότε, νῦν δὲ Μενίππου, Καὶ πάλιν ἐξ ἑτέρου βήσομαι εἰς ἕτερον. Καὶ γὰρ ἐκεῖνος ἔχειν με ποτ᾽ ᾤετο, καὶ πάλιν οὗτος Οἴεται∙ εἰμὶ δ᾽ ὅλως οὐδενὸς, ἀλλὰ τύχης.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAPTER XV.

Azariah reigns in Judah, he is struck with leprosy: his son Jotham is substituted for him. In Israel, Zechariah succeeded his father Jeroboam, killed by Shallum; whom Menahem likewise deprived of life and kingdom, who became tributary to Phul, King of the Assyrians. Upon his death, his son Pekahiah succeeded him; whom Pekah killed; Tiglath-Pileser invaded the latter, and carried away a part of Israel into Assyria: Hoshea, however, killed him and became King in Israel. Jotham succeeds his father Uzziah (Azariah), against whom Rezin of Syria and Pekah, King of Israel, rise up: upon his death, his son Ahaz succeeds.

Verse 1.

IN THE TWENTY-SEVENTH YEAR OF JEROBOAM) Very learned men think there is an error in the numbers, and that no more should be written than 17, by the argument of those things which we have above at v. 2 and 23; the same men think that below at v. 8 it was written formerly not 38, but 28.

An error in the numbers cannot be proven by any approved Sacred Codex: indeed, not even by translations. Therefore, a reconciliation is needed, which occurs most notably in both places: And indeed at v. 1, Fr. Riebera posits an interregnum of thirteen years between Amaziah and Azariah, concerning which see Mr. Walther on ch. 14, 21. But because an interregnum is not easily to be admitted in the Chronology of the Kings of Judah, lest it be completely thrown into confusion, it should rather be said with others, Cajetan, Salianus, Cornel. à Lapide, that the 27th year of Jeroboam is counted from that time when he himself began to reign with his father Joash: because otherwise it would be the fourteenth year of the same kingdom, which he alone properly held, as is gathered from 2 Chron. 15, 25. But in the other place at v. 8, the thirty-eighth year of the reign of Azariah, in which he began to reign with his father Azariah, seems to some to be indicated, but the 27th year from which he himself began to reign alone. However, it pleases others that after Jeroboam King of Israel yielded to fate in the 27th year of Azariah King of Judah, there was an interregnum in Israel for 11 years, up to the thirty-eighth year of Azariah, because Zechariah the son of Jeroboam could not obtain the kingdom either on account of his tender age or on account of the rebellion of his subjects or some other cause. This is the explanation of Richard of St. Victor, Lyranus, Abulensis, and Corn. à Lap. See our Biblical Chronicle.

Verse the same.

AZARIAH REIGNED) This King is called in the Hebrew in this place עזריה, in the Greek, Ἀζαρίάς. But in Chronicles עוזיהו; in the LXX version, Ὀζίας, as he is also always called by Josephus. If the ו, which we said later is often παραγωγικὸν (paragogic), be taken away from this name, the name will be the same, except for the letter י interposed, which, whether added or taken away, changes nothing of the meaning of the name. I would have believed his true name to have been עוזי by Dagesh: formerly, before that abbreviation of speech was invented, it was written עזזי: but the second letter ז could easily be changed into י on account of the similarity of form. And that is the more credible because Josephus, who read both books, always calls him Ὀζίαν, but the High Priest who lived at the same time Ἀζαρίαν, as also the LXX, who in the Hebrew of Chronicles with an equal additional ו is עוזיהו,

Grotius contends at length that there is an error in the name, since he was called עוזיהו in Chronicles, but Grotius exhausts himself in vain in this: for that King was of two names. He was called Azariah, which in Hebrew is the help of God, and Uzziah, which is the strength of God, so that there is no need for such a desperate suspicion concerning the corruption of the Scripture of the name; which we do not even judge worthy to be transcribed here.

Latin:

CAPUT XV.

Azarias regnat in Juda, lepra percutitur: Substituitur ei Jotham filius. In Israele Jeroboamo filius Zacharias successit, à Sallum interfectus; quem itidem vita & regno privavit Menahem, qui Phu- li Assyriorum Regi factus est tributa- rius. Ei defuncto successit filius Peca- jah; quem interfecit Pekah, hunc Tiglath- Phalasar invasit, & partem Israelis transstulit in Assyriam: Hoseas autem interfecit eum & Rex factus est in Isra- el. Jotham Usiæ (Azariæ) Patri succedit, adversus quem Rezin Syriæ & Pekah Israelis Rex insurgunt: Ei defuncto fi- lius Ahaz succedit.

Vers. 1.

ANNO VIGESIMO SEPTIMO JEROBOAM) Viri valde docti putant erratum in numeris, nec plus scribendum, quam 17. argumento eorum quæ supra habemus 14. v. 2. & 23. iidem infra 8. scriptum olim putant non 38. sed 28.

ERratum in numeris probari non potest ullo probato Codice Sacro: Imo ne quidem è translationibus. Conciliatione ergo opus est, quæ gemina potissimum occurrit utroque loco: Et ad v. 1. quidem interregnum ponit inter Amasiam & Azariam Fr. Riebera tredecim annorum, de quo vid. Dn. Waltherus ad c. 14, 21. Sed quia non facile in Chronologia Regum Judæ interregnum ad- mittendum est, ne ipsa prorsus turbetur, dicendum potius cum aliis, Cajetano, Saliano, Cornel. à Lapi- de annum 27. Jerobeami numerari ab eo tempo- re, quo ipse cum Patre Joas regnare cœperit: quia alias regni ejusdem, quod solus proprie ob- tinuit, fuerit annus decimus quartus, ut è 2. Par. 15, 25. colligitur. In altero vero loco ad v. 8. annus trigesimus octavus regni Azariæ, quo cum Patre Azaria regnare ceperit, indigitari quibusdam videtur, annus vero 27. ex quo solus ipse regna- re cepit. Aliis tamen placet postquam Jerobe- am Rex Israel anno 27. Azariæ regis Judæ fatis concessit, per 11. annos fuisse interregnum in Israel, usque ad trigesimum octavum annum Azariæ, eo quod Zacharias filius Jerobeam vel propter æta- tem teneram vel propter rebellionem subditorum aut aliam quandam causam regnum obtinere ne- quiverit. Quæ Richardi à S. Victore, Lyrani, Abu- lensis, Corn. à Lap. est explicatio. Vid. Chronicum nostrum Biblicum.

Vers. eod.

REGNAVIT AZARIAS) Rex hic hoc loco in Hebræo vocatur עזריה, in Græco, Ἀζαρίάς. At in Paralipome- nis עוזיהו; in versione LXX. Ὀζίας, quomodo & Josepho semper vocatur. Si auferatur ab isto posterius nobis dicto nomine ו sæpe παραγωγικὸν, idem erit nomen, excepta litera י interposita, quæ addita aut demta de significatione nomi- nis nihil immutat. Crediderim verum ejus nomen fuisse עוזי per Dagesch: olim antequam id compendium di- ctionis inventum est, scriptum עזזי : litera autem ז se- cunda facile in י mutari potuit ob formæ vicinitatem. Est- que id eo credibilius quod Josephus, qui utrosque libros legit, eum semper Ὀζίαν vocat, Pontificem autem qui eodem vixit tempore Ἀζαρίav, quomodo & LXX. qui in Hebræo Parali- pomenon cum pari adjectitio ו est עוזיהו,

Prolixe Grotius erratum esse in nomine con- tendit, quum עוזיהו dictus fuerit in Paralip. sed fru- stra se in eo fatigat Grotius: Rex enim ille bino- minis fuit. Azarias dictus, quod Ebræis est auxi- lium Dei, & Ozias, quod est fortitudo Dei, ut tam desperata suspicione de corruptione Scripturæ no- minis opus non sit; quam ne dignam quidem judi- camus, quæ huc transcribatur.

## 15:5
Verse 5.

BUT THE LORD STRUCK THE KING, AND HE WAS A LEPER) The cause is in Chronicles, because he had usurped for himself the right of offering incense, which belongs to the priests, against the law, and to whom it was not even permitted to enter the basilica of the Temple in which was the altar of incense. Num. 3. ch. 18, v. 2. 5. 7. Leprosy is the punishment for both slander and pride.

AND HE DWELT IN A FREE HOUSE APART) In the country. See what we said above at 7, 3.

BUT JOTHAM THE KING'S SON GOVERNED THE PALACE) He was the King's vicar, who, being segregated from all the people, could not perform the royal power.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

PERCVSSIT AVTEM DOMINVS REGEM, ET FVIT LEPROSVS) Causa est in Paralipomenis, quod ado- lendi jus proprium sacerdotibus sibi usurpaffet contra legem, & cui ne intrare quidem basilicam Templi in qua erat altare suffitus licuerit. Num. 3. c. 18, l. 2. 5. 7. Lepra & maledi- centiæ & superbiæ pœna.

ET HABITABAT IN DOMO LIBERA SEORSVM) Ruri. Vide quæ diximus supra 7, 3.

JONATHAN VERO FILIVS REGIS GVBERNABAT PALATIVM) Vicarius erat Regis, qui ab omni populo se- gregatus fungi regiam potestatem non poterat.

## 15:8
Verse 8.

IN THE THIRTY-EIGHTH YEAR OF AZARIAH KING OF JUDAH) See what was said at the beginning of this chapter.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ANNO TRIGESIMO OCTAVO AZARIÆ REGIS JVDÆ) Vide quæ dicta ad initium hujus capitis.

## 15:12
Ver. 12.

THIS IS THE WORD WHICH HE SPOKE TO JEHU) Above 10, 30.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ISTE EST SERMO QVEM LOCVTVS EST AD JEHV) Supra 10, 30.

## 15:14
Ver. 14.

AND HE KILLED HIM, AND REIGNED IN HIS STEAD) See what was said above in 1 Kings 15, 28. Add shortly 25, 30.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET INTERFECIT EVM, REGNAVITQVE PRO EO) Vide dicta supra l. Reg. 15, 28. Adde mox 25,30.

## 15:16
AND HE RENT THEM) Above 8, 12.

Latin:

ET SCIDIT EAS) Supra 8, 12.

## 15:19
Ver. 19. AND MENAHEM GAVE PUL A THOUSAND TALENTS OF SILVER) With that money he both redeemed the war and bought an alliance.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET DABAT MANAHEM PHVL MILLE TALENTA ARGENTI) Ea pecunia & bellum redemit, & societatem emit.

## 15:20
Ver. 20.

AND MENAHEM EXACTED THE SILVER UPON ISRAEL FROM ALL THE MIGHTY AND RICH) An excellent method of tribute, which burdens only the rich, and indeed in proportion to their wealth.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

INDIXITQVE MANAHEM ARGENTVM SVPER ISRAEL CVNCTIS POTENTIBVS ET DIVITIBVS) Optima tributi ratio, quæ divites tantum onerat, & quidem pro divitiarum modo.

## 15:23
Ver. 23.

FOR THEY WOULD NOT OPEN TO HIM) Thus Caesar to the Massilians who were opening their gates to him: - - you shall pay the penalty for the peace you sought, and you shall learn that there is nothing safer in my age than war under my leadership.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

NOLVERVNT ENIM APERIRE EI) Sic Cæsar Mas- siliensibus portas sibi recludentibus: - - dabitis pœnas pro pace petita, Et nihil esse meo discetis tutius ævo, Quam duce me bellum.

## 15:29
Ver. 29.

THEGLATH-PHALAZAR) Theglaphalasas in Josephus: Thalgathphellasar in the LXX. In the Hebrew of Chronicles a letter is added תגלת פלנאסר : the first part of this name comes from the river Tigris, which is called Diglito by those living near it.

AND CARRIED THEM INTO THE ASSYRIANS) This was the beginning of the deportations, through which God punished the Hebrew people, first in part, then in whole.

AND GALILEE) Whose citizens were treated more harshly in captivity than the Naphtalites, Isa. 9:2.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

THEGLATH-PHALAZAR) Θεγλαφαλάσης Josepho: Θαλγαθφελλασάρ LXX. In Hebræo Paralipomenon litera ad- dita תגלת פלנאסר : prior pars hujus nominis a Ti- gride fluvio venit, qui Diglito accolis.

ET TRANSTVLIT EOS IN ASSTRIOS) Hoc initium fuit μετοικεσ.ῶν, per quas Deus punivit Hebræum populum, ex parte primum, deinde totum.

ET GALILÆAM) Cujus cives in captivitate tractati durius quam Nephthalitæ Ef. 9, 2.

## 15:30
Ver. 30. AND REIGNED IN HIS STEAD IN THE TWENTIETH YEAR OF JOTHAM THE SON OF UZZIAH) That is, from the time Jotham had begun to reign: for Jotham did not reign except for sixteen years.

Latin:

Vers. 30. REGNAVITQVE PRO EO VIGESIMO ANNO JOATHAN FILII OZIÆ) Id est, ex quo regnare cœperat Joathan : non enim regnavit Joathan nisi annos se- decim.

## 15:32
Ver. 32. JOTHAM REIGNED) In Hebrew: Jotham: LXX. Joatham, in Josephus Jotham, who asserts that the Prophet Nahum lived in his time.

Latin:

Vers. 32. REGNAVIT JOATHAN) In Hebræo : Jotham: LXX. Ἰωαθάμ Josepho Ἰώθαμ☉, qui hujus temporibus vixis- se autumat Nahumum Prophetam.

## 16:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVI. Ahaz the idolater, besieged in Jerusalem, calls upon Tiglath-Pileser, who occupies Damascus: Ahaz constructs an altar according to the form of the Damascene altar, and sacrifices upon it, and changes many things in the temple. Upon his death, Hezekiah succeeds him.

Latin:

CAPUT XVI. Achaz idololatra, Hierosolymis obsessus invo- cat Tiglatphalasar, qui Damascum occu- pat: Abas juxta formam altaris Dama- sceni aram conficit, inque ea sacrificat, ac multa in templo immutat. Ei defuncto succedit Hiskias.

## 16:2
Ver. 2. TWENTY [YEARS OLD WAS AHAZ] And what exceeds that. See below 18, 2.

Junius and Tremellius refer the 20 years to the beginning of the reign not of Ahaz, but of his father Jotham; but this is against the clear letter of the text.

Latin:

Vers. 2. VIGINTI [ANNORVM ERAT ACHAZ) Et quod excurrit. Vide infra 18, 2.

JUnius & Tremell. 20. annos referunt ad initi- um regni non Achazi, sed Patris Jotami; at contra literam textus luculentam.

## 16:3
Ver. 3. MAKING PASS THROUGH FIRE) Purifying, as the Latin interpreter speaks in this same history in 2 Chronicles 3, concerning which custom see what we have said at Deuteronomy 18, 10.

Josephus, Abulensis, and Adrichomius think he was burned; Lyranus thinks one of his sons was burned and others were purified by fire; Theodoret and Salianus establish only purification, which the passage in 2 Chronicles 28 seems to favor, and Grotius agrees with this here.

Latin:

Vers. 3. TRANSFERENS PER IGNEM) Lustrans, ut La- tinus interpres in eadem hac historia loquitur 2. Paral. 3. de quo more vide quæ dicta nobis ad Deut. 18, 10.

Josephus, Abulens. & Adrichom. putant crema- tum esse, Lyranus & unum e filiis crematum, & alios per ignem lustratos censet; Theodoret. & Salian. solum lustrationem statuunt, quibus fa- vere videtur locus 2. Paralipom. 28. annuitque hic Grotius.

## 16:4
Ver. 4. HE ALSO SACRIFICED VICTIMS AND BURNED INCENSE IN THE HIGH PLACES, AND ON THE HILLS, AND UNDER EVERY LEAFY TREE) He did not merely tolerate these things, as many kings who were not evil had done before, being unequal to the crowds, but he led the others by his own example, and increased the license contrary to the laws.

Latin:

Vers. 4. IMMOLABAT QVOQVE VICTIMAS ET ADOLEBAT INCENSVM IN EXCELSIS, ET IN COLLIBVS, ET SVB OMNI LIGNO FRONDOSO) Non ferebat hæc tantum, ut antehac fecerant multi Reges non mali, turbæ impares, sed exemplo suo præibat cæteris, & augebat contrariam legibus licentiam.

## 16:5
Ver. 5. THEN REZIN KING OF SYRIA, AND PEKAH SON OF REMALIAH KING OF ISRAEL CAME UP) Compare Isaiah chapter 7.

IN JERUSALEM) That is, against Jerusalem.

Latin:

Vers. 5. TVNC ASCENDIT RASIN REX SYRIÆ, ET PHASEE FILIVS RAMELIÆ REX ISRAEL) Confer Esaiam cap. 7.

IN JERVSALEM) Id est, contra Hierosolyma.

## 16:6
Ver. 6. AILAM) Elath, concerning which see above 14, 22.

AND THE IDUMEANS CAME INTO AILAM) He reads ארימים, as the LXX. But it is more true to read ארומיים, as the Hebrew text has, and Josephus: the Syrians settled in it. Powerful kings are not accustomed to return what they have taken from enemies to those to whom they formerly belonged.

Latin:

Vers. 6. AILAM) Elath de qua supra 14, 22.

ET IDVMÆI VENERVNT IN AILAM) Legit ארימים, ut LXX. At verius est ארומיים, ut habet Hebræus textus, & Josephus: ἐγκατῴκησεν αὐτῇ Σύρυς. Non solent Reges potentes quæ ab hostibus ceperunt iis reddere quorum olim fuerunt.

## 16:7
Ver. 7. I AM THY SERVANT AND THY SON) The Latins would say: We have given the people, the city, the fields, the shrines, and all things divine and human into your dominion. See what we have said concerning the Law of War and Peace, book one, chapter three, § 8, and book three, chapter 20, § 49.

That Ahaz sinned by distrust toward God, who had promised him help, and by confidence in the aid of Tiglath-Pileser, by whom he was despoiled and oppressed, is clear from 2 Chronicles 28, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 7. SERVVS TVVS ET FILIVS EGO SVM) La- tini dicerent: Populum, urbem, agros, delubra, divina huma- naque omnia in tuam ditionem dedimus. Vide quæ dicta nobis de Jure Belli ac Pacis libro primo capite tertio §. 8. & libro tertio capite 20. §. 49.

Peccasse autem Achaz diffidentia erga De- um, qui opem ipsi promiserat, & confidentia in Teglatphalasaris auxilio, à quo spoliatus est, & op- pressus è 2. P. 28, 19. liquet.

## 16:8
Ver. 8. THE GOLD AND SILVER WHICH COULD BE FOUND IN THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) As above 12. ver. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 8. AVRVM ET ARGENTVM QVOD INVENIRI PO- TVIT IN DOMO DOMINI) Vt supra 12. vers. 18.

## 16:9
Ver. 9. AND HE REMOVED ITS INHABITANTS TO CYRENE) In the Hebrew it is, קירה, which cannot be Cyrene, which was not under the Assyrians. Josephus says it is a part of Media, in which is the river Cyrrhus according to Pliny and Ptolemy.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET TRANSTVLIT HABITATORES EJVS CYRENEN) In Hebræo est, קירה, quæ Cyrene esse non potest, quæ sub Assyriis non fuit. Josephus partem esse ait Mediæ, in qua Cyrrhus fluvius Plinio & Ptolemæo.

## 16:11
Ver. 11. AND URIJAH THE PRIEST BUILT AN ALTAR] He obeyed the King wrongly against the law, who ought to have endured anything rather than provide ministry for an illicit thing, like the Jews who under Alexander in Babylon refused to bring material for building the temple of Bel. Tertullian rightly says that we ought to be subject to Magistrates, Princes, and powers in all obedience, but within the limits of discipline. The form of the altar of burnt offerings (for it is that which is treated of here) is prescribed in Exod. 27, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 11. EXSTRVXITQVE VRIAS SACERDOS AL- TARE] Male contra legem Regi paruit, qui quidvis potius perferre debuit, quam ministerium ad rem illicitam præbere, ut Judæi qui sub Alexandro Babylone ad Beli templum ex- struendum materiam aggerere noluerunt. Recte Tertullia- nus, oportere nos in omni obsequio esse subditos Magistratibus, Principibus & potestatibus, sed intra limites disciplinæ. For- ma altaris holocaustorum (de eo enim hic agitur) præscripta est Exod. 27, 1.

## 16:15
Ver. 15. UPON THE GREATER ALTAR) Made after the likeness of the Damascene altar.

AND THEIR SACRIFICES) That is, offerings of fine flour, or also the gifts which accompanied the victims. For מנחת signifies both.

BUT THE BRAZEN ALTAR) Covered with brass: that old one according to the prescription of Moses.

Latin:

Vers. 15. SVPER ALTARE MAJVS) Factum ad instar Dama- sceni altaris.

ET SACRIFICIA EORVM) Id est, oblationes e simila, aut etiam munera quæ victimas comitabantur. מנחת enim utrumque significat.

ALTARE VERO ÆREVM) Ære obductum: illud ve- tus ex Mosis præscripto.

## 16:18
Ver. 18. THE COVERED PLACE ALSO FOR THE SABBATH THAT THEY HAD BUILT IN THE TEMPLE) A certain passage under a roof which they had built (for so it is in the Hebrew) namely the priests, so that they might enter into the Temple on the Sabbath day to begin their ἐφημερίαν.

AND THE KING'S ENTRY WITHOUT) That is the first gate, through which the King was accustomed to enter into the Temple.

HE TURNED INTO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) In the Hebrew: he caused to go around the house of the Lord. In Greek, ἐπέστρεψεν ἐν οἴκῳ

that is, he turned it into another part of the Temple, so that those entering, either the King or the Priests, might not turn their backs to the Assyrian, and by that means seem to reverence the King of Assyria less: for those entries looked toward the East.

Salianus gives this reason, that if anyone wished to go from the Palace into the temple, he would be forced to descend by a great circuit from Mount Zion and cross the whole of Ophel, so that he might come to the roots of Mount Moriah, and thence descend 900 steps into the temple, so that this annoyance of such a long circuit, and difficult ascent, might call away those who were of the King's household from approaching the temple. Whatever the cause may have been, it is sufficiently clear that all these things were done in contempt of divine worship.

Latin:

Vers. 18. MVSACH QVOQVE SABBATI QVOD ÆDIFI- CAVERANT IN TEMPLO) Transiturn quendam sub te- cto quem ædificaverant (nam sic est in Hebræo) nempe sa- cerdotes, ut illac Sabbati die intrarent in Templum ad incho- andam ἐφημερίαν.

ET INGRESSVM REGIS EXTERIVS) Id est primam portam, per quam Rex ingredi solebat in Tem- plum.

CONVERTIT IN TEMPLVM DOMINI) In He- bræo: circuire fecit domum Domini. Græce, ἐπέστρεψεν ἐν οἴκῳ

id est, in aliam partem Templi vertit, ne ingredientes aut Rex aut Sacerdotes tergum obverterent Assyriae, eoque Regem Assyrium minus revereri viderentur: nam ingressus isti ad Orientem spectabant.

Salianus hanc reddit causam, ut nimirum si quis e Regia in templum ire vellet, magno circuitu descendere cogeretur ex monte Sion & trajicere totum Ophel, ut veniret ad radices montis Mo- ria, indeque in templum 900. gradibus descende- ret, ut haec molestia tam longi circuitus, & diffi- cilis ascensus, eos qui erant Regis familiae, a tem- plo adeundo avocaret. Quaecunque autem cau- sa fuerit, satis patet haec omnia in contemtum cul- tus divini facta esse.

## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII.

Hosea denying the tribute to Shalmaneser, to whom he had been made tributary, and being imprisoned on that account, the Israelites who still remained are transferred into Assyria, for which divine punishment they are exposed. Assyrian colonists sent into Samaria serve there both the God of Israel and their own gods.

Ver. 1.

IN THE TWELFTH YEAR OF AHAZ KING OF JUDAH, HOSHEA THE SON OF ELAH BEGAN TO REIGN IN SAMARIA] Namely, by full right. Understand in this way also what is below in ch. 18, v. 1; he had reigned even before, but as a client of the Assyrian; see above 15, v. 30.

Hosea did indeed invade the kingdom after Pekah was killed in the fourth year of Ahaz, which was from the beginning of Jotham King of Judah the twentieth, 2 Kings 16, v. 10, but on account of the intervening disturbances and seditions he could not immediately take possession of the kingdom, whence the Republic was reduced to a certain anarchy for 9 years. And therefore in the 12th year of King Ahaz, (when) the intestine disturbances were settled, he finally took possession of the kingdom, and reigned for nine years. He did not become a client, but only a tributary of the King of Assyria, and that after the twelfth year of Ahaz, therefore there is no room for the Grotian reconciliation.

Latin:

CAPUT XVII.

Hosea tributum Salmanasseri, cui factus erat tributarius, negante, & ob id captivato, Israelitae adhuc reliqui in Assyriam trans- feruntur, cujus poena divina causa expo- nuntur. Assyrii coloni in Samariam missi illic & Deo Israelis & suis diis ser- viunt.

Vers. 1.

ANNO DUODECIMO ACHAZ REGIS JVDA, RE- GNAVIT OSSE FILIVS ELA IN SAMARIA] Nempe pleno jure. Sic accipe & quod infra est 18. v. 1. regnaverat & ante, sed ut cliens Assyrii; supra 15. v. 30.

Invasit quidem Hoseas regnum Peka Rege interfecto quarto Achazi, qui erat ab initio Jo- thami Regis Judae vigesimus 2. Reg. 16. v. 10. sed propter turbas & seditiones intervenientes regno statim potiri non potuit, unde Resp. ad anarchi- am quandam per 9. annos redacta. Ideoque anno 12. Regis Achazi, (desinente) turbis intestinis sedatis regno potitus demum est, annisque novem regnavit. Non cliens, sed tributarius solum fa- ctus est Regis Assyrii, idque post duodecimum Achazi, ideo Grotianae conciliationi non est locus.

## 17:3
Ver. 3.

AGAINST HIM CAME UP SHALMANESER KING OF THE ASSYRIANS) Josephus teaches us that his name existed in the Annals of the Tyrians.

AND BECAME HIS SERVANT) That is, he gave himself to his faith and protection, and testified his obedience by a promised tribute.

The added ἐξήγησις teaches how far he is said to have been made a servant: namely, that he paid an annual tribute to him, but not that he was made subject to him, nor that he reigned by full right. The Vau here is exegetical.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

CONTRA HVNC ASCENDIT SALMANASSAR REX ASSYRIORVM) Hujus nomen in Tyriorum exstitis- se Annalibus docet nos Josephus.

ET FACTVS EST EI SERVVS) Id est, fidei ejus ac tutelae se dedit, obsequiumque promisso tributo te- status est.

Quousque servus factus dicatur, ἐξήγησις addita docet: scil. quod tributum annuum eidem persolverit, non vero quod eidem subditus fa- ctus sit, nec pleno jure regnarit. Vau hic est exe- geticum.

## 17:4
Ver. 4.

THAT HE WAS ENDEAVORING TO REBEL) That is, to fail in his faith.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

QVOD REBELLARE NITENS) Id est, deficere a fide.

## 17:6
Ver. 6.

THE KING OF THE ASSYRIANS TOOK SAMARIA] Which Menander of Ephesus includes under the name of Phoenicia in the passage which we produced for the third book on the Truth of the Christian Religion. See also what is below 18, 10.

IN HALA) In Hebrew: הלח. This is a Calatine part of Assyria touching Adiabene according to Ptolemy.

AND IN HABOR) In Hebrew חבור. This is Chabora by the Euphrates according to the same Ptolemy: Others, however, interpret הלח as the Colchians, and חבור as the Iberians of Asia, both here and in 1 Chronicles 6 at the end, and those who were led there think they are the people whom Herodotus narrates were Colchians of Syrian origin and circumcised: namely those Pontics also mentioned in the Acts and the Epistle of Peter. Certainly, we learn from a passage of Abydenus concerning Nebuchadnezzar, which we produced for the third book of the Truth of the Christian Religion, that the coast of Pontus was under the Chaldean Kings after these times.

BY THE RIVER GOZAN] Whence the region of Gauzanitis is described by the same Ptolemy in Mesopotamia. IN THE CITIES OF THE MEDES] In the Hebrew: and the cities of the Medes: for those former places were partly in Assyria, partly in Mesopotamia. Media, however, was under the same empire.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

CEPIT REX ASSYRIORUM SAMARIAM] Quam sub Φοινίκης nomine comprehendit Menander Ephesius in loco quem produximus ad librum tertium de Veritate Reli- gionis Christianae. Vide & quod infra 18, 10.

IN HALA) In Hebraeo: הלח. Haec est Calatina pars Assyriae Adiabenen tangens apud Ptolomaeum.

ET IN HABOR) Hebraice חבור. Haec est Chabora apud Euphraten eidem Ptolomaeo: Alii vero per הלח Col- chos, per חבור Iberos Asiae, tum hic, tum 1. Paralip. 6. in fine interpretantur, & qui eo deducti sunt putant eos esse, quos Colchos e Syris ortos & circumcisos fuisse narrat Hero- dotus: Ponticos illos scilicet etiam in Actis & Petri epistola memoratos. Certe Ponti oram post haec tempora sub Regibus Chaldaeis fuisse discimus ex Abydeni loco de Nabuchodo- nosoro, quem produximus ad tertium de Veritate Religionis Christianae.

JUXTA FLUVIUM GOZAN] Unde regio Gauzanitis eidem Ptolemæo in Mesopotamia descriptio- IN CIVITATIBUS MEDORUM] In Hebræo: & civi- tatibus Medorum: nam priora illa loca partim in Assyria, par- tim in Mesopotamia erant. Media autem sub eodem erat imperio.

## 17:7
Ver. 7. AND IT CAME TO PASS WHEN THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL HAD SINNED AGAINST THE LORD THEIR GOD] A serious etiology of such serious evils.

Latin:

Vers. 7. FACTUM EST ENIM CUM PECCASSENT FILII ISRAEL DOMINO DEO SUO] Gravis αἰτιολογία tam gravium malorum.

## 17:8
Ver. 8. ACCORDING TO THE RITE OF THE NATIONS WHOM THE LORD HAD CONSUMED IN THE SIGHT OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL] Of the Canaanites, the Amorites, and their neighbors.

Latin:

Vers. 8. JUXTA RITUM GENTIUM QUAS CON- SUMSERAT DOMINUS IN CONSPECTU FILIORUM ISRAEL) Chananæorum, Amorrhæorum, vicinorumque.

## 17:9
Ver. 9. AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL OFFENDED THE LORD THEIR GOD WITH WORDS NOT RIGHT] In the Hebrew: The children of Israel concealed (that is, spoke secretly) words not right against the Lord their God.

FROM THE TOWER OF THE WATCHMEN TO THE FENCED CITY] A proverbial expression, signifying the same thing done in inhabited places and in desert places. Understand the towers of the watchmen as fruit-watchers' huts.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ET OFFENDERUNT FILII ISRAEL VERBIS NON RECTIS DOMINUM DEUM SUUM] In Hebræo: Occultarunt filii Israel (id est, clam locuti sunt) verba non re- cta contra Dominum Deum suum.

A TURRE CUSTODUM USQVE AD CIVITATEM MUNITAM) Proverbiale, significans idem factum in locis habitatis, & in locis desertis. Turres custodum intellige ὀπωροφυλάκια.

## 17:12
Ver. 12. AND THEY WORSHIPPED UNCLEANNESSES] Thus the Hebrews call idols out of contempt.

Latin:

Vers. 12. ET COLUERUNT IMMUNDITIAS] Sic ido- la vocant Hebræi per contemtum.

## 17:13
Ver. 13. AND THE LORD TESTIFIED IN ISRAEL AND IN JUDA BY THE HAND OF ALL THE PROPHETS AND SEERS] The obstinacy against so many monitors sent divinely increases the guilt.

AND AS I SENT TO YOU BY THE HAND OF MY SERVANTS THE PROPHETS] In the Hebrew: and which, supply the law, I sent to you: that is, I commended to you through the Prophets. Those things which are in Nehemiah chapter 10 agree strongly with these.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET TESTIFICATUS EST DOMINUS IN ISRAEL ET IN JUDA PER MANUM OMNIUM PRO- PHETARUM ET VIDENTIUM) Auget culpam contu- macia adversus tot monitores divinitus missos.

ET SICUT MISI AD VOS IN MANU SERVORUM MEORUM PROPHETARUM] In Hebræo: & quam, supple legem, misi ad vos: id est., commendavi vobis per Prophetas. Valde his consonant quæ sunt apud Nehemiam cap. 10.

## 17:16
Ver. 16. THEY WORSHIPPED ALL THE HOST OF HEAVEN] The stars, especially Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, the Moon.

AND THEY SERVED BAAL) The sun, as we have said elsewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ADORAVERUNT UNIVERSAM MILITI- AM COELI) Astra, præcipue Saturnum, Jovem, Venerem, Lunam.

## 17:24
Vers. 24.

AND FROM CUTH) Josephus says that Cuth is a river of Persia: thence the city Cotamba, according to Ptolemy. From this region was the greater part of that colony which was led into Samaria and the neighboring places: hence it happened that those who lived there were called by way of eminence כותיים Χυθαῖοι, as Josephus notes here.

AND FROM AVA] עוא here and 18, 34, although there with different points. Hence the people were called עוי shortly in 31, whom Ptolemy calls Avadias in Bactriana.

AND FROM EMATH] So also below 31 and 18, 33. It is Amathus of Syria, named twice by Herodotus.

AND FROM SEPHARUAIM) It is the city Σιπφάρα according to Ptolemy, called by the Syrians in the dual number because the Euphrates flows between it; the city of the Sippareni according to Abydenus.

Vers. 24.

ET DE AVATH] עוא hic & 18, 34. quanquam ibi punctis aliis. Hinc dictus populus עוי mox 31. quos Avadias vocat Ptolomæus in Bactriane.

ET DE EMATH] Sic & infra 31. & 18, 33. Est Amathus Syriæ, bis nominata Herodoto.

ET DE SEPHARUAIM) Est urbs Ptolemæo Σιπφάρα, dicta Syris numero binionis, quod eam Euphrates interlue- ret Σιππαρηνῶν πόλις Abydeno.
