## 15:12
Ver. 12.

SANCTIFY YOURSELVES WITH YOUR BRETHREN] Those about to perform sacred rites ought to prepare themselves. Μηδέποτ᾽ ἐξ ἠοῦς Διῒ λείβειν αἴθοπα οἶνον Χερσὶν ἀνίπτοισιν. Hesiod says.

What have the profane things of the Gentiles to do with rites divinely instituted? Sanctification was enjoined upon the Levites by the divine law itself, and it had to be done by rites prescribed by God, Num. 8, 6. However, a certain apparent contradiction occurs here. For it is said that the sons of Levi carried the ark according to the prescription of GOD v. 15, and v. 3, that the ark should not be carried by anyone except the Levites. But in 2 Sam. 7, 1, it stands written thus: And they sanctified Eleazar, that he should keep the ark of the Lord. R. David Kimchi replies to 2 Sam. 6: This is to be understood concerning Eleazar regarding the keeping of the house in which the ark was, for preserving it clean, namely, by sweeping it and sprinkling it with water before the ark; not that it was permitted to him to extend his hand to the ark and move it from its place. For no one could do this except the Levites. Others think Eleazar was a Levite. But that does not seem likely, both because the Levites had their own cities, among which Kiriath-jearim was not (Josh. 21), and because Josephus, book VII, ch. 4, seems to have thought so, and the author of the Mirabilia Scripturae in Augustine openly denies it. And therefore he is said to be sanctified by a received phrase of Scripture, that is, destined for the custody of the ark, just as to sanctify is to destine for other uses, even profane ones. This is the opinion of Sanctius on 1 Sam. 6:2. Compare what we have noted on that passage.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

SANCTIFICAMINI CVM FRATRIBVS VESTRIS] Præparare se debent obituri sacra. Μηδέποτ᾽ ἐξ ἠοῦς Διῒ λείβειν αἴθοπα οἶνον Χερσὶν ἀνίπτοισιν. Ait Hesiodus.

Quid gentilium prophana ad sacra divini- tus instituta? Sanctificatio Levitis injuncta erat ipsa lege divina, ritibusque a Deo præscriptis fieri de- bebat Num. 8, 6. Occurrit autem hic ἐναντιοφανὲς quoddam. Nam tulisse filios Levi arcam juxta præ- scriptum DEI v. 15. & v. 3. illicitum esse dicitur, ut a quocunque portetur arca, nisi a Levitis. At 2. Sam. 7, 1. ita scriptum extat: Eleazarum autem sanctifica- verunt, ut custodiret arcam Domini. Resp. R. David Kimchi ad 2. Sam. 6. Hoc de Eleazaro intelligendum esse de custodia domus, in qua arca fuit, ad confer- vandam sc. eam mundam everrendo, & aqua consper- gendo coram arca; non quod ipsi permissum fuerit manum ad arcam extendere, & eam loco movere. Hoc enim nulli poterant facere nisi Levitæ. Alii Elea- zarum Levitam fuisse putant. Sed id verisimile non videtur, tum quia Levitæ habebant suas civita- tes, inter quas non erat Kiriathjarim Jos. 21. tum quia Josephus l. VII. c. 4. ita sensisse videtur, idque aperte negat Autor mirabilium S. Scripturæ apud August. Ideoque sanctificatum dici phrasi Scri- pturæ recepta, id est, destinatum ad custodiam arcæ, qua sanctificare est, ad alios usus etiam prophanos destinare. Quæ est Sanctii sententia in 1. Sam. 6,2, Conf. quod ad istum locum notavimus.

Verse 20.

## 21:5
FOUR HUNDRED SEVENTY THOUSAND.

There is a different number in 2 Sam. 24, 9. For five hundred thousand are read there. But in our passage the regular legions are omitted. For these were already numbered at 288,000, over whom were 12 leaders, each with his own thousand and captains of thousands, from which arises the sum of 12,000; when this number is added to the former, 300,000 result precisely. Thus also in 2 Sam. 24, the leaders and heads are counted in; here, however, only the common soldiers were numbered.

Latin:

QUADRINGENTA SEPTUAGINTA MILLIA.

Alius numerus est 2, Sam. 24, 9. Leguntur enim ibi quingenta millia. Sed in nostro loco præteritæ sunt legiones ordinariæ. Hæ enim jam in numerato erant 288000. quibus præerant 12. duces cum sua quisque chiliade ac chiliarchis, unde surgit summa 12000. quo numero priori addito præcise prodeunt 300000. Sic etiam 2. Sam. 24. annumerantur duces & capita: hîc autem tantum milites vulgares numerati sunt.

Hence it happened that the whole census was not completed, with Joab managing the matter slowly and a divinely-sent evil supervening. See below 27, 24.

## 22:14
Verse 14.

BEHOLD I IN MY POVERTY HAVE PREPARED] A modest expression, by which he excuses himself that he does not leave more to his heir: as among the Romans, in the consulship of C. Asinius Gallus and C. Marcius Censorinus (that was under Augustus), C. Caecilius Claudius Isidorus said in his will that, although he had lost much in the civil war, he nevertheless left 4,115 slaves, 3,600 yoke of oxen, and 257,116 of the rest of the livestock; in cash, 60,000,000 sesterces. Pliny mentions this in Natural History 33, 10.

If the calculation is undertaken according to the common acceptance of a talent, or as it is estimated in the Pentateuch of Moses, where a talent is 3000 shekels (see Exod. 38, verses 25, 26), an immense sum of treasure will be produced. For since the value of a shekel is half an ounce of silver, or half an Imperial or Joachimic thaler, the sum of silver will be 150,000,000 Joachimics or ounces of silver; and because gold is in a twelvefold proportion to silver, 100,000 talents of gold will make 1,800,000,000 ounces of silver or Joachimics; which two sums of silver and gold, if added together, produce in total 3,300,000,000 ounces of silver or Imperials, that is, 33,000 tons of gold, as we call them, of standard currency (each of which is worth 100,000 Joachimics or Imperial thalers), or 3,300 millions. Which sum seemed stupendous and incredible to Capellus in his delineation of the temple, to Edward Brerewood in his book On the Weights and Prices of Coins, chapter 6, and to Brian Walton in his English Polyglot work, it seemed too large: because it far exceeds the treasures of all monarchs, nor was there any way for David, who had received no treasures from his predecessors, to amass such huge heaps as no one has scraped together from immense empires, nor finally did the work of the temple structure demand such an immense sum of gold; whence they conclude that the word ככר denotes something other than a talent, or that there is another notion of a talent besides the Mosaic one: observing that it had a varied meaning among the Ancients, and sometimes a small sum was designated by it: just as Eupolemus in Eusebius, book IX of the Preparation for the Gospel, chapter 34, reported that in counting the cost of the temple, a talent denotes a shekel, that is, 4 drachmas: and that David did not add without reason that he had consecrated these things FROM HIS POVERTY, as if they were the remnants of his afflictions and wars. According to this calculation, therefore, five tons of gold are produced from the sum of gold left over, as Junius and Tremellius also calculate: to which are added 6 tons of gold from the sum of silver left over, if the proportion of the price of gold to silver is twelvefold, or 7 1/2 tons of gold, according to Agricola's fifteenfold proportion, and thus the total sum will make either 11 or 12 1/2 tons of gold. Rabbi Jacob Jehuda Leo in his book On the Jerusalem Temple, page 10, makes the sum larger, namely 107 myriads, that is, tons of gold, and 70,000 Joachimics besides. Let others look into this calculation.

Moreover, the arguments of Brerewood may appear not to be despised, for the reason that David could hardly have amassed such an immense sum. Add that David further added to those sums of gold and silver, as is held in 1 Chronicles 29:3, from his own treasure 3,000 talents of gold and 7,000 of silver, which according to shekels, if indeed talents are taken for shekels, make in total 21,500 Joachimics, but according to the common estimation of the ככר, they again constitute an incredible sum of 64,500,000 Joachimics, that is, 645 tons of gold. Johannes Mariana, with certain others, as reported by Jacobus Tirinus on 2 Chronicles 25:6, makes a talent of silver in the book of Chronicles after the times of Moses 300 Belgian florins, that is, 150 Joachimics or Imperial thalers; according to which calculation David's treasure left for the structure of the temple will indeed be far larger, I will not say than Brerewood's, but even than the aforementioned Rabbinic calculation, yet ten times smaller than the earlier Mosaic calculation had produced, that is, 330 millions of gold. But whence Mariana has that notion of a talent, that a talent of silver is 300 shekels, does not appear, since it is nowhere so defined in the scriptures, but according to the designation of the Holy Spirit, Exod. 28, 25. 26. it contains three thousand, not three hundred shekels. Nor indeed does that notion of a talent suit the books of Chronicles, or other sacred histories, after Mosaic times; For 2 Chron. 25, 6. Amaziah King of Judah hired a hundred thousand of the stronger soldiers of Israel for a hundred talents of silver; but how could he have hired a thousand robust soldiers for 150 Joachimics, or 300 shekels? For how small is this pay, since for one person there would have been to be counted only about three groschen, and thus not even a third part of a shekel would have been spent on each head of either the leaders or the common soldiers: but according to Eupolemus, praised by Brerewood, a thousand soldiers would have been hired for one silver shekel, or half a Joachimic. According to the Mosaic calculation, however, there would have fallen to each one as the price of hiring one and a half Joachimics: which everyone sees is far more convenient. Thus 1 Kings 16, verse 24. Omri King of Israel is said to have bought the mount of Samaria for two talents of silver, which according to Brerewood would amount to no more than one Joachimic, according to Mariana 600 shekels, or 300 Imperials, but according to Moses 6000 shekels, and thus 3000 Imperials, which sum corresponds more to such a space, which was required for a royal city that was by far most ample. Furthermore 2. Kings 18, verse 14. 15. there was need to collect the sum of 300 talents of silver, and 30 talents of gold, so that the treasures of the temple as well as the royal palace might be plundered! But how small a sum that would have been, according to Brerewood, namely 330 Joachimics, which according to Mariana would indeed have made a sum of 99000 Vallenses: But who will believe that for a single ton of gold the royal and sacred treasures were to be exhausted? How much more certain therefore is the Mosaic calculation, according to which nearly ten tons of gold were then to be collected? We will add one more example, and that, if I am not mistaken, even more evident, namely that 2 Kings 23, 33. a public census had to be proclaimed, so that a sum of a hundred talents of silver, and one talent of gold might be collected: which indeed according to Brerewood would amount to a hundred silver shekels, and one gold shekel, that is, 50 and 12 Joachimics or 62, but according to Mariana 16800. Joachimics, that is perhaps a sixth part of a ton of gold, for the sake of which money a public census would certainly not have been proclaimed throughout the entire kingdom: But with the Mosaic calculation retained, 168000 Vallenses, and indeed 336000 silver shekels to be collected, could entirely require a public census: since this sum imports more than an entire ton of gold, and still 18000 Joachimics. Wherefore the Mosaic calculation, as Canonical, and the most certain of all, with the Holy Spirit nowhere hinting at any diversity, is deservedly retained, which therefore no arguments can subvert. For from wherever David obtained such a sum, one must not depart from the letter of the text on account of our ignorance, so that one ought rather to marvel at, and venerate the divine blessing of this shepherd, which procured such immense treasures for him, once raised to the Royal throne: Which, in the judgment of Villalpando, grew into this sum partly from taxes, partly from the spoils of enemies, and tribute paid by subjugated peoples, partly from the annual census of Israel, by which each one paid half a shekel, Exod. 30, 13. and finally partly from the navigation to Ophir: concerning which latter mode Eupolemus himself in Eusebius, book IX, Preparation for the Gospel, ch. 30, handed down: that David, for the sake of collecting treasure to build the temple, having built ships in the city of Achana in Arabia, sent artificers of metal-digging to the island of Urphe in the Red Sea, which abounds in gold mines, who brought back from there a great deal of gold into Judea.

But that which David professed here concerning his POVERTY, was of humility, because he did not attribute this, whatever he obtained, to himself and his own labors and arts, but since he himself was very poor and a needy shepherd, he deemed it to be attributed solely to God, that from his poverty he had emerged thus far, by the ineffable grace and bounty of God: or if the term from which is not designated by that word, or what he himself was before, at least it is indicated what David felt about those earthly riches, namely that they are mere poverty and misery, in respect to the immense treasures of God, not only those which are stored up for us in heaven, but which He himself also possesses on earth, Hag. 2, 9.

Nor indeed does the distinction of Jacques Cappel deserve consideration, Miscell. VII. & book II. on gold coins, definition XIX. or the last, which his brother Louis Cappel approves, and Matthew Poole praises from him in the Synopsis on this passage, that that part of the Davidic treasury in 1 Chron. 29, 3. 4. 7. 8. should be understood as the greater or Stathmic talent, but this one in the present passage as the lesser or numismatic talent, and according to this calculation the sum of the treasury nevertheless seems sufficiently large, as it ascends (in gold) to 126 million gold coins: to which if the sum of silver is added, the proportion of which some make tenfold, and they say the same sum results, unless I am mistaken, according to the opinion of the Cappels the total sum will be 256 million of gold. We see no reason for this distinction: nor is it likely that the author of the books of Chronicles used such an equivocation and a different calculation of the weight of talents; on the contrary, from a comparison of the passages it has already been shown that that invention of a lesser and numismatic talent is vain; whence that of Mariana should rather be inverted, it is madness indeed madness, to equate David's talents with Mosaic ones, it is madness, indeed madness, to establish some Mosaic talents and others Davidic, contrary to scripture.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ECCE EGO IN PAUPERTATE MEA PRÆPARAVI] Modesta locutio, qua se excusat, quod non plus hæredi relinquat: ut apud Romanos C. Asinio Gallo, C. Martio Quirinio Consulibus (id sub Augusto fuit) C. Cæcilius Claudius Isiddrus testamento suo dixit, quamvis multa civili bello perdidisset, tamen relinquere servorum quatuor millia CXV. juga boum tria millia secenta; reliqui pecoris CCCVII. millia centum sexdecim: in numerato HS. sexcenties. Meminit Plinius Historiæ Naturalis 33, 10.

Si computus ineatur secundum talenti communem acceptionem, vel prout in Pentatevcho Mosis æstimatur, ubi talentum est Siclorum 3000. (vid. Exod. 38. versu 25. 26.) immensa proditura est thesauri summa. Quum enim Sicli valor sit dimidia unciæ argenti, vel dimidii Imperialis, aut Joachimici, argenti summa erit 150000000. Joachimicorum, vel unciarum argenti: & quia aurum in proportione duodecupla est ad argentum, talenta auri 100000. efficient 1800000000. uncias argenti, aut Joachimicos: quæ duæ summæ argenti, & auri si addantur, prodeunt in universum 3300000000. unciæ argenti, vel imperiales, hoc est, tonnarum auri, quas vocamus, probæ monetæ, (quarum quæque valet 100000. Joachimicis, vel thaleris imperialibus) 33000. seu millionum 3300. Quæ summa Capello in delineatione templi stupenda & incredibilis, Eduardo Brerevvodo in de Ponderibus, & pretiis nummorum cap. 6. & Briano VValtono in opere Anglicano Polyglotto nimis magna visa est: quod omnium Monarcharum Thesauros longe superet, neque modus ullus Davidi, qui a prædecessoribus suis thesauros nullos acceperat, fuerit, tam ingentes cumulos acervandi, quantos ex immensis imperiis nulli corrasiere, nec denique tam immensam auri summam opus structuræ templi postularit; unde concludunt, vocem ככר vel aliud quam talentum notare, vel aliam esse talenti notionem, præter Mosaicam: observantes, variam ejus significationem fuisse apud Antiquos, & interdum exiguam aliquam summam ea designatam: quemadmodum Eupolemus apud Eusebium libro IX. præparat. Evangelic. capit. 34. in sumtu templi numerando talentum Siclum, id est, 4. drachmas denotare prodidit: & Davidem non præter rem addidisse, se hæc EX PAUPERTATE SUA consecrasse, quasi afflictionum & bellorum suorum reliquias. Juxta hunc ergo computum tonnæ auri e summa auri relicta prodeunt quinque, uti calculum etiam ineunt Junius & Tremellius: quibus accedunt 6. tonnæ auri, ex argenti relicta summa, si proportio pretii auri præ argento sit duodecupla, vel 7 1/2. tonnæ auri, juxta proportionem Agricolæ quindecuplam, adeoque tota summa efficiet vel 11. tonnas auri, vel 12. cum dimidia. R. Jacob Jehuda Leo in de templo Hierosolymitano pag. 10. summam ampliorem facit, Myriadum nempe, hoc est, tonnarum auri 107. & præterea 70000. Joachim. De quo calculo alii dispiciant.

Cæterum argumenta Brerevvodi non contemnenda videri possint, eo quod tam immensam summam vix conflare potuerit David. Adde quod illis auri & argenti summis addiderit porro David, uti 1. Paralip. XXIX, 3. habetur de thesauro suo 3000. talenta auri, & 7000. argenti, quæ juxta siclos, si nempe talenta pro siclis habeantur, in universum efficiunt 21500. Joachimicos, sed juxta communem ככר æstimationem iterum summam incredibilem 64500000. Joachimicorum, hoc est, 645. tonnarum auri constituunt. Johannes Mariana cum quibusdam aliis, referente Jacobo Tirino ad 2. Paralipom. 25. vers. 6. talentum argenti in libro Paralipomenon post Mosis tempora facit 300. florenorum Belgicorum, hoc est 150. Joachimicorum vel Thalerorum imperialium; juxta quem computum thesaurus Davidis in templi stru- cturam relictus longe quidem amplior, non dicam Brerevvoodiano, sed etiam Rabbinico prædicto, de- cuplo tamen minor erit, quam calculus Mosaicus prior tulerat, hoc est, millionum auri 330. unde vero Mariana illam talenti notionem habeat, quod ar- genti talentum 300. ficlorum sit, non apparet, si- quidem in scripturis ita nuspiam definiatur, sed jux- ta designationem Spiritus Sancti, Exod. 28, 25. 26. ter mille, non tercentum siclos contineat. Nec sane convenit illa talenti notio libris Paralipomenon, aliisve sacris historiis, post Mosaica tempora; Nam Paral. 25, 6. Amasias Rex Juda militum Israelis fortiorum centum millia conduxit centum talentis argenti; quomodo autem mille milites robustos 150. Joachmicis, vel 300. siclis conducere potuis- set? Quantilla enim hæc merces, quum uni sic numerandi fuissent tantum tres grossi circiter, adeo- que ne tertia quidem sicli pars in singula seu ducum seu vulgarium militum capita impensa fuisset: se- cundum Evpolemum vero a Brerewoodo laudatum mille milites uno siclo argenteo, vel dimidio Joachimi- co conducti fuissent. Juxta Mosaicum autem cal- culum cessisset unicuique in conductionis pretium sesqui-Joachimicus: quod longe convenientius esse nemo non videt. Ita 1. Regum 16. vers. 24. Am- ri Rex Israelis emisse dicitur montem Samariæ duobus talentis argenti, quæ juxta Brerewoodum non nisi unum Joachimicum, juxta Marianam 600. siclos, vel 300. Imperiales, juxta Mosen vero 6000. siclos, adeoque 3000. Imperiales efficerent, quæ summa magis congruit tanto spatio, quod requi- rebatur ad urbem regiam longe amplissimam. Porro 2. Regum 18. vers. 14. 15. ad summam 300. talentorum argenti, & 30. talentorum auri colli- gendam opus erat, ut expilarentur thesauri tem- pli pariter & palatii regii! At quantilla summa ista fuisset, juxta Brerewoodum, nimirum 330. Joachimicorum, quæ juxta Marianam quidem summam 99000. Vallensium effecerit: Ecquis ve- ro credet, ob unicam auri tonnam regios, & sa- cros thesauros exhauriendos fuisse? Quanto er- go certior est computus Mosaicus, juxta quem de- cem fere auri tonnæ compilandæ tum erant? U- num adhuc adjiciemus exemplum, idque ni fallor adhuc evidentius, quod nempe 2. Regum 23. 33. indicendus fuerit census publicus, ut colligeretur summa centum talentorum argenti, & unius ta- lenti auri: quæ vero juxta Brerevvodum centum siclos argenteos, & unum siclum aureum, hoc est, 50. & 12. Joachimicos vel 62. efficerent, juxta Ma- rianam autem 16800. Joachimicos, hoc est sex- tam forte partem tonnæ auri, cujus pecuniæ gra- tia census publicus per universum regnum sane indicendus minime fuisset: At Mosaico com- puto retento 168000. Vallenses, sicli vero ar- gentei 336000. colligendi, publicum censum o- mnino requirere poterant: siquidem hæc sum- ma supra integram auri tonnam, & dimidiam adhuc 18000. Joachimicos importet. Quapro- pter Mosaicus computus, ceu Canonicus, o- mniumque certissimus, Spiritu Sancto nullam di- versitatem uspiam innuente, merito retinetur, quem proinde nulla subvertere queunt argumen- ta. Nam undecunque David tantam compara- rit Summam, a litera textus, ob nostram igno- rantiam adeo discedendum non est, ut potius mirari, ac venerari oporteat benedictionem divinam hujus opilionis, quæ tam immensos thesauros ipsi ad Regium thronum evecto conciliarit: Qui, Vilalpando judice, partim e vectigalibus, partim ex hostium spoliis, & tributo a subjugatis populis soluto, partim ex annuo Israelis censu, quo quisque dimidium siclum pendebat, Exod. 30, 13. partim denique ex navigatione in Ophir, in hanc summam excreverint: de quo posteriori modo Evpolemus ipse apud Euseb. l. IX. præpar. Evangel. c. 30. tradidit: Davidem colligendi thesauri, ad ædificandum templum, gratia, navibus in Achana Arabiæ civitate exstructis effodiendi metalli artifices Urphen rubri maris Insulam aurifodinis abundantem misisse, qui auri plurimum in Judeam inde retulerint.

Quod autem de PAUPERTATE sua David professus hic est, humilitatis fuit, quod non sibi, suisque laboribus, & artibus hoc, quicquid obtinuit, tribuerit, sed quum pauper admodum ipse fuerit, & egenus opilio, Deo unice accepto ferendum duxerit, quod e paupertate sua eo usque, divina ineffabili gratia, & largitate emerferit: aut si terminus a quo non designatus ea voce sit, vel qualis ipse ante fuerit, saltim indicetur, quid de illis terrenis opibus senserit David, quod nempe mera paupertas & miseria sint, respectu immensorum Dei thesaurorum, non modo qui in cœlis nobis reconditi sunt, sed quos in terris etiam ipse possidet, Hag. 2, 9.

Nec vero calculum meretur Distinctio Jacobi Capelli, Miscell. VII. & libri II. de Nummis aureis definit. XIX. seu ultima, quam Ludov. Capellus frater approbat, & ex eo laudat Matth. Polus in Synops. ad hunc loc. quod pars illa thesauri Davidici 1. Chron. 29, 3. 4. 7. 8. de talento majore, seu Stathmico, hæc vero in præsenti loco de talento minore, vel numismatico accipienda sit, ac juxta hanc computationem thesauri summa nihilominus satis grandis videatur, utpote adscendens (in auro) ad 126. aureorum nummorum milliones: quibus si addatur argenti summa, cujus proportionem nonnulli faciunt decuplam, eandemque summam prodire ajunt, nisi fallor, juxta Capellorum sententiam summa universa erit 256. millionum auri. Rationem hujus distinctionis nullam videmus: nec verisimile est, autorem librorum τῶν παραλειπομένων tali æquivocatione, & diversa ponderis talentorum calculo usum esse, ex adverso vero ex collatione locorum jam ostensum est, vanum esse illud commentum minoris & numismatici talenti; unde invertenda potius illa Marianæ, furor profecto furor, Davidis talenta Mosaicis exæquare, furor, profecto furor, alia Mosaica, alia Davidica talenta, contra scripturam, constituere.

## 23:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIII.

Solomon is made king. The number and offices of the Levites are designated.

Ver. 1.

HE MADE SOLOMON HIS SON KING) Which other kings of the East had also often done. Compare 1 Kings 1, 39. 43.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIII.

Rex constituitur Salomo. Levitarum numerus, & officia designantur.

Vers. 1.

REGEM CONSTITVIT SOLOMONEM FILIVM SVVM) Quod & alii Orientis Reges sæpe fecerant. Confer 1. Reg. 1, 39. 43.

## 23:3
Ver. 3.

FROM THIRTY YEARS OLD] From which time they performed full ministry, Num. 4, 3.

THERE WERE FOUND 38,000 MEN) Besides the priests. A truly great number for that people, so that you may easily understand that many served more for ornament than for necessity.

Junius and Tremellius wish the number of disciples to have been begun here, but with those 288 teachers also counted, of whom [it is spoken] in ch. 25, 7. But there it is a matter of musicians: here, however, of the Levites in general. For there was a triple order of Levites: I. Of those ministering: II. Of musicians. III. Of gatekeepers. The priests are not counted here.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

A TRIGINTA ANNIS] Ex quo tempore pleno ministerio fugebantur Num. 4, 3.

INVENTA SVNT XXXVIII. MILLIA VIRORVM) Præter Sacerdotes. Magnus sane numerus pro isto populo, ut facile intelligas multos ornatui magis serviisse, quam necessitati.

Junius & Tremellius volunt numerum hic initum discipulorum, sed annumeratis etiam docto- ribus illis 288. de quibus c. 25, 7. Verum ibi de Mu- sicis agitur : hic v. de Levitis in genere. Fuit enim triplex ordo Levitarum : I. Ministrantium : II. Mu- sicorum. III. Janitorum. Sacerdotes hic annu- merati non sunt.

## 23:4
Verse 4.

AND OF THE OVERSEERS AND JUDGES SIX THOUSAND) That is, attendants and judges. For the discourse rises.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

PRÆPOSITORVM AVTEM ET JVDICVM SEX MILLIA) Id est, apparitores & judices. Surgit enim oratio.

## 23:27
Verse 27.

ACCORDING TO THE LAST COMMANDS ALSO OF DAVID) By this testament of his, David had provided that the Levites should undertake certain ministries from their twentieth year, for they were not as burdensome as formerly, when the tabernacle and all its instruments had to be carried: and therefore neither was a full discharge given, as formerly in the fiftieth year of age. It was also the right of kings, by the counsel of the Sanhedrin, to declare which laws were perpetual and which were temporary. Junius and Tremellius observe that by the constitution of David, the Levites from boyhood were catechumens up to the 20th year, after 20 they were admitted into the observation of the ministry to which they were appointed, but only in a theoretical capacity, up to 25, and from that time they were occupied in a certain secondary administration until they had reached their thirtieth.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

JVXTA PRÆCEPTA QVOQVE DAVID NOVISSIMA) Hoc testamento suo caverat David, ut Levi- tæ à vicesimo anno aliqua obirent ministeria, neque enim erant tam gravia ut olim, cum portandum esset tabernacu- lum & omnia ejus instrumenta : ideoque nec plena missio da- ta, ut olim anno ætatis quinquagesimo. Regum etiam hoc erat, ex consilio Synedrii declarare, quæ leges perpetuæ es- sent, quæ temporariæ. Junius & Tremellius observant ex constitu- tione Davidis Levitas inde a puero fuisse catechu- menos ad 20. annum usque, post 20. fuisse admissos in observationem Ministerii, ad quod erant institu- ti, sed θεωρικὴν solum, ad 25. usque, ex eo tempore fuisse occupatos in secundaria quadam administra- tione donec trigesimum attigissent.

## 24:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIV. A census of the priests by their families, offices, and orders, as also of the Kohathites and Merarites ministering to them.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIV. Sacerdotum recensio per suas familias, officia & ordines, ut & Kehathitarum & M.- raritarum ipsis ministrantium.

## 24:5
Verse 5.

FOR THEY WERE PRINCES OF THE SANCTUARY AND PRINCES OF GOD) You may rightly translate this last part as Princes of the judges. Since men from both families, as well of Eleazar as of Ithamar, had attained the greatest dignities, both in the Temple and in the republic, they could not have functions distributed to them without great envy otherwise than by lot. See below 19, 31; 25, 8; 26, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ERANT ENIM PRINCIPES SANCTVA- RII ET PRINCIPES DEI) Postremum hoc recte vertas Principes judicum. Cum ex utraque familia tam Eleazari quam Ithamarιs viri essent maximas dignitates con- secuti, tum in Templo, tum in republica, distribui illis fun- ctiones sine magna invidia aliter quam sorte nequierunt. Vi- de infra 19. 31. 25, 8. 26, 13.

## 24:19
Verse 19.

UNDER THE HAND OF AARON THEIR FATHER) Under the inspection of the high priest, who had succeeded into the place of Aaron.

Verse the same.

ONE HOUSE WHICH WAS OVER THE OTHERS ELEAZAR, AND ANOTHER HOUSE, WHICH HAD UNDER IT THE OTHERS ITHAMAR) The families of Eleazar and the families of Ithamar were taken by turns, which the Greeks express in the Hebrew manner of speaking thus: ἗ις ἗ις τῷ Ἐλεάζαρ, καὶ ἗ις ἗ις τῷ Ἰθάμαρ. Whence it appears that they read twice אחד אחד, for which now is read first אחז אחז, then אחז אחז, less conveniently.

The Hebrew Codex is beaten again. But whatever the case may be regarding the LXX Interpreters, it is altogether preposterous to correct the source from a version, since, as Jerome, Augustine, and Canon Law itself advise, versions should rather be corrected from the sources. Moreover, all Hebrew Codices agree here. And the Masora confirms this reading in Num. 31, when it observes that אחז is read four times without a ו, and in this very place it occurs twice. Nor is there any inconvenience in the Hebrew text: which Junius and Tremellius render thus: one paternal family taken from Eleazar, and similarly one taken from Ithamar, whereas in these latter the Hebrew has 'taken taken'. Let the Belgic version be compared, with the notes to this place. Munster understands אחז as: one father's house was retained with Eleazar, and one retained, I say, was retained with Ithamar. The LXX rendered not the words, but the sense which they themselves believed to underlie them. In the Jerusalem Talmud. Massechet Taanith fol. 67. this explanation is brought forward, uttered by R. Jacob son of R. Acha, in the name of R. Jochanan: one father's house was attributed to Eleazar (i.e., other father's houses were added to Eleazar). But what Ithamar had, he retained (without any addition). R. David Kimchi explained it similarly: when David saw that there were more of the heads of the men from the sons of Eleazar than from the sons of Ithamar, he took one from the sons of Abraham and one from the sons of Eleazar, added eight more guards, and ordained that there should be 24, namely 16 from the sons of Eleazar, and eight from the sons of Ithamar. This is what is said: אב בית אחד אחז לאלעזר, one paternal house fell to Eleazar, beyond that which he had from the beginning. ואחז אחז לאיתמר, i.e., what Ithamar had from the beginning, that very thing he now retained, because they added no guard to him anew. Which words R. Salomo takes in the same way: What was possessed from the beginning, that he now also possessed and retained: because no father's house was added to them, as it was to the family of Eleazar. This, therefore, is what it wishes to signify: What the ratio of Ithamar was in the priestly guards in the tabernacle of Shiloh, in that same state he is now also left by David in the house of the sanctuary, or temple. Concerning which, see more in Buxtorf, in Vindiciae Veritatis Hebraicae, p. 987.

Latin:

Vers. 19.

SVB MANV AARON PATRIS EORVM) Sub inspectione summi Sacerdotis, qui in locum Aaronis suc- cesserat.

Vers. eod.

VNAM DOMVM QVÆ CÆTERIS PRÆERAT ELEAZAR, ET ALTERAM DOMVM, QVÆ SVB SE CÆTEROS HABEBAT ITHAMAR) Alternis sume- bantur familiæ Eleazaris, & familiæ Ithamarιs, quod Græci Hebraico loquendi genere fic exprimunt : ἗ις ἗ις τῷ Ἐλεάζαρ, καὶ ἗ις ἗ις τῷ Ἰθάμαρ. Vnde apparet legisse eos bis אחד אחד pro quo nunc legitur prius אחז אחז, deinde אחז אחז, minus commode.

Iterum vapulat Ebræus Codex. Sed quicquid sit de LXX. Interpretibus, præposterum omnino est, e versione fontem corrigere, quum monente Hie- ronymo, Augustino, & jure ipso Canonico versio- nes e fontibus corrigendæ potius sint. Consen- tiunt autem hic omnes Codices Ebræi. Et confir- mat hanc lectionem Masora Num. 31. cum observat אחז quater legi sine ו & in hoc quidem loco bis occur- rere. Nec quicquam est incommodi in Hebræo textu : quem Junius & Tremellius ita reddunt, fa- miliam paternam unam captam ex Eleazare, & simi- liter captam quamque ex Ithamare, quum in his po- stremis Ebræa habeant & captam captam. Con- feratur versio Belgica, cum notis ad h. l. Mün- sterus אחז subintelligit h. m. domus patris una re- tenta est apud Eleazarum, & una retenta, retenta inquam est apud Ithamar. LXX. reddidere non verba, sed sensum, quem ipsi credidere subesse. In Talmud Hierosolymitan. Massechet Taanith fol. 67. haec producitur explicatio R. Jacobi filii R. Acha, nomine R. Jochanan prolata: domus Patrum una attributa fuit Eleazaro (h. e. additæ sunt Elea- zaro aliæ domus patrum) Quod vero Ithamar babe- bat, retinebat (sine ulla additione) Similiter expo- suit R. David Kimchi: cum vidisset David plures esse de capitibus virorum, de filiis Eleazar, quam de filiis Ithamar, accepit unum de filiis Abraham & unum de filiis Eleazar, addidit adhuc octo custodias, ordinavit- que ut essent 24. nempe 16. de Eleazaris, & octo de Ithamaris filiis. Hoc est, quod dicitur אב בית אחד אחז לאלעזר domus paterna una cessit Elea- zaro, ultra id quod habuerat a principio. ואחז אחז לאיתמר h. e. quod Ithamar habebat a princi- pio, illud ipsum nunc retinebat, quia nullam ei custo- diam de novo addiderunt. Quæ verba eodem modo accipit R. Salomo: Quod ab initio erat posses- sum, id nunc quoque possidebat & retinebat: quia illis nulla domus paterna fuit adjecta, ut Eleazaris fami- liæ. Id ergo significari vult: Quæ Ithamar is ratio in custodiis sacerdotalibus fuit in tabernaculo Siloh, in eadem illum relictum nunc quoque esse a Davide in do- mo sanctuarii, vel templo. De quo pluribus Bux- torf. in vind. verit. Ebr. p. 987.

## 24:27
Verse 27.

THE SON ALSO OF MERARI OZIAN AND SOAMAR, AND ZACHUR AND HEBRI] In Greek: υἱοὶ ἀυτῶ ἰσοὰμ καὶ σακχοὺς, καὶ ἀβαὶ: But there are those who think that all these words crept in here by some error, led by the argument of the passage placed above.

There is no error here. Nor is it proven by the cited passage. Everything is correct if the sources are consulted; from which, and from the Chaldean text, Cornel. a Lapide and Tirinus correct the Vulgate. The sons of Merari from Oziahu (or through Oziahu) Benno (or besides Benno, whom he had named before) and Soamar, and Zachor, and Hebri. Others take בנז appellatively: so that the sense may be, The sons of Jahathia, his son (sc. Merari, i.e., the grandsons of Merari from Jehasia his son), as B. Luther translates, as does also Buxtorf in Vindiciae Veritatis Hebraicae, p. 1014. Grotius followed his Capellus again, who boldly asserted that those names were inserted here also in the wrong place. But since all Hebrew Codices have them, and the LXX, the Chaldean, and the Vulgate also retain them, and there is no suspicion of forgery (νοθείας), they are held to be interpolations in vain. Nor does the comparison of the passage 1 Chron. 23:21, 22, 23 contribute anything here. For since those names of the sons of Jehasia are not found in the same, how could they have been transferred or crept in here from that passage? Grotius did not inspect the passage, but allowed himself to be seduced by Capellus; who dreamed that they were read there.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

FILIVS QVOQVE MERARI OZIAN ET SOAMAR, ET ZACHVR ET HEBRI] Græce υἱοὶ ἀυτῶ ἰσοὰμ καὶ σακχοὺς, καὶ ἀβαὶ: Sed has voces omnes errore quodam huc irrepsisse sunt qui censent, ducti argumento loci supra positi

Nullus hic error. Nece loco adducto is pro- batur. Habent se omnia recte, si fontes consulan- tur; e quibus, & Chaldæo textu vulgatum corrigit Cornel. a Lapide & Tirinus. Filii Merari de Oziahu (vel per Oziahu) Benno (vel præter Benno, quem antea nominarat) & Soamar, & Zachor, & Hebri. Alii בנז appellative accipiunt: ut sensus sit, Filii Ja- hafia, filii ejus (sc. Merari, h. e. nepotes Merari de Jehasia filio ipsius) quomodo vertit B. Lutherus, ut & Buxtorf. in vind. verit. Hebr. p. 1014. Sequutus est Grotius iterum Capellum suum, qui nomina illa hic etiam alieno loco inserta esse, audacter asseruit. Sed quum omnes Codices Ebræi ea habeant, LXX. etiam, Chaldæus, ac vulgata illa retineant, nec ulla νοθείας suspicio fit, frustra ea pro embolimæis ha- bentur. Neque collatio loci 1. Paral. 23, 21. 22. 23. huc quicquam facit. Quum enim in eodem no- mina ista non reperiantur filiorum Jehasia, quomo- do ex eo loco huc traduci, vel irrepere potuere? Non inspexit locum Grotius, sed a Capello se passus est seduci; qui ea illic legi somniavit.

## 25:1 Argument
CHAP. XXV.

Sacred musicians distributed into twenty-four orders and their functions.

Verse 1.

WHO SHOULD PROPHESY WITH HARPS) That is, they should apply modes suitable to prophetic songs, as also in the following clause. The Latin also takes the other Hebrew word in this way: above 15:22. Perhaps this exposition can be joined with the explanation of others, for whom to prophesy is to treat the word of God, whether it be done by preaching, or even by singing. Because they also treated the word of God by singing, and by reducing it to modes suitable for singing. Which they commonly call COMPOSITION. In the other passage, the word 'prophesy' is not in the authentic text. Junius explains that passage of 1 Chron. regarding the burden of carrying those things which belonged to the tent, and the prefects who were over those who carried such things.

15, 22. because there in the Hebrew it is in the burden. Osiander explains it thus, the whole burden of managing the music rested upon him, as if he had been the prefect of the musical choir. Vatablus interprets it as in the exaltation of the voice, because the word משא signifies elevation: to which, because they agree with the matter, the Hebrews easily [agree] according to Jerome in the traditions, he presided over the prophecy, that is, they recalled the melodies and words of the prophecy to the memory of the singers: yet the explanation of Vatablus adheres more closely to the words.

Latin:

CAP. XXV.

Musici sacri in viginti quatuor ordines distri- buti & eorum functiones.

Vers. 1.

QVI PROPHETARENT IN CITHARIS) Id est, mo- dos adhiberent propheticis carminibus convenientes, ut & commate sequenti. Sic etiam accipit Latinus vocem alteram Hebræam: supra 15, 22. Conjungi poterit forte hæc expositio cum aliorum explicatione, quibus prophetare est ver- bum Dei tractare, sive id fiat prædicando, sive etiam cantando. Quia & tractarunt verbum Dei can- tando, & in modos, cantui convenientes redigen- do. Quam COMPOSITIONEM vulgo vocant. In altero loco non habetur prophetias vox in textu avthentico. De onere portandi ea, quæ ad tento- rium pertinebant, & præfectis, qui illis, qui portabant talia, præerant, explicat Junius locum illum 1. Par.

15, 22. quia ibi in Ebræo est in onere. Osiand. ita ex- ponit, ipsi totum onus moderandæ Musicæ incumbe- bat, quasi præfectus Chori Musici fuerit. Vatablus interpretatur in exaltatione vocis, quia vox משא elevationem significat: quibus quod rem confo- nant facile Ebræi apud Hieron. in tradit. præerat Prophetiæ, h. e. Prophetiæ melodias, & verba canto- ribus ad memoriam revocabant: pressius tamen verbis inhæret explicatio Vatabli.

## 25:2
Verse 2.

PROPHESYING BY THE KING] In the Hebrew: at the hands of the king: that is, those who prescribed what was to be sung according to the king's command.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

PROPHETANTES JUXTA REGEM] In Hebræo: ad manus regis: id est, qui canenda præscribebant ex regis im- perio.

## 25:3
Verse 3. SIX. This sixth one is indeed omitted, but who he was, to complete the number, is gathered from chapter 5, 17, namely that he was in the tenth order of Shimei: Thus that Uzziel 5, 4, the son of Heman, was not indeed omitted afterwards in the casting of lots, but was listed in verse 14, but by another name, being called Isreela, as if he had two names.

Latin:

Vers. 3. SEX. Hic sextus omissus quidem est, sed quis fuerit, ad numerum complendum, colligitur e cap. 5, 17. quod nempe in decimo ordine fuerit Simei: Sic U- siel ille 5, 4. filius Heman non omissus quidem postea est in sortilegio, sed recensitus v. 14. at alio nomine, dictus nempe Isreela ceu binominis.

## 25:5
Verse 5.

THE KING'S SEER) The prophet who was for the most part present with the king. IN THE WORDS OF GOD] To proclaim the promises of God. TO EXALT THE HORN] Concerning the greatness of the Davidic kingdom. This horn is not to be understood so much of the power or kingdom of David, as of the power and kingdom of the Messiah, whom he especially wished to be exalted through the Psalms, hymns, and his musicians, for whose honor all those things were ordained. Thus the horn of David is said to spring forth in Psalm 132, 17: and in Psalm 18, 3, the horn of salvation is understood of the Messiah. If, therefore, you explain the preceding IN THE WORDS OF GOD with Grotius, to proclaim the promises of God, these things agree very well. For the pinnacle of divine promises was the Messiah.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

VIDENTIS REGIS) Prophetæ qui regi plerumque aderat. IN SERMONIBUS DEI] Ad prædicanda Dei promissa. UT EXALTARET CORNU] De magnitudine regni Davidici. Non tam de potentia, aut regno Davidis hoc cornu accipiendum, quam de potentia & regno Mes- siæ, quem imprimis exaltari per Psalmos, hymnos, & Musicos suos volebat, cujus honori illa ordinata erant omnia. Ita cornu Davidis exoriturum Psal. 132, 17. dicitur: & Pf. 18, 3. cornu Salutis intelligitur de Messia. Si ergo cum Grotio explices præce- dentia IN SERMONIBUS DEI, ad prædicanda Dei promissa, hæc optime congruunt. Nam apex pro- missionum divinarum fuit Messias.

## 26:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVI.

The gatekeepers of the temple, and the guardians of the treasury, and of the vessels from among the Levites.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVI.

Janitores templi, & custodes thesauri, & vasorum e Levitis.

## 26:5
Verse 5.

BECAUSE THE LORD BLESSED THEM) Obed-edom, namely, to whom He granted much offspring on account of the hospitality of the Ark in his house.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

QVIA BENEDIXIT ILLIS DOMINUS) Obededomo scilicet, cui sobolem multam largitus est ob Arcæ hospitium in ejus domo.

## 26:20
Verse 20.

WAS OVER THE TREASURIES OF THE HOUSE OF GOD] Set over those monies which David had destined for the building of the temple: above 22, 14.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

ERAT SUPER THESAUROS DOMUS DEI] Præpo- situs illis pecuniis quas templo faciendo David destinaverat: supra 22, 14.

## 26:27
Verse 27.

CONCERNING WARS AND THE SPOILS OF ESTATES, WHICH THEY HAD CONSECRATED) According to ancient custom. Gen. 14, 20. which custom is also of the nations. Virgil: - - - And we call Jupiter himself to a share of the booty.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

DE BELLIS ET MANUBIIS PRÆDIORUM, QVAS CONSECRAVERANT) More vetusto. Genes. 14, 20. qui mos etiam gentium. Virgilius: - - - Ipsumque vocamus In partem prædamque Jovem.

## 26:29
Verse 29.

FOR THE OUTWARD WORKS OVER ISRAEL TO TEACH AND TO JUDGE THEM) In the Hebrew: for officers and judges: that is, they were in charge of every public work outside the city, and had jurisdiction mandated by the king over those works: some of them were also officers. The word שטרים denotes not officers, but prefects and overseers. Junius renders it moderators: From the Vulgate, which Osiander approves, he understands the interpreters of the law in doubtful cases to be the same. But the papists themselves acknowledge that this passage does not concern doctrine, but works outside the city in cutting and polishing wood and stone, and in cultivating the vineyards, meadows, and fields of the temple.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

AD OPERA FORINSECUS SUPER ISRAEL AD DOCENDUM ET JUDICANDUM EOS) In Hebræo: in apparitores & judices: id est, præerant omni operi publico extra urbem, & jurisdictioniem à rege mandatam habebant in operas illas: quidam etiam eorum apparitores erant. Vox שטרים non apparitores, sed præfe- ctos, & præpositos notat. Junius moderatores red- dit: E vulgata, quam probat Osiander, legis in casi- bus dubiis interpretes intelligit idem. Sed pontifi- cii ipsi agnoscunt non de doctrina, sed operibus ex- tra urbem in lignis & lapidibus cædendis & poliendis, in vineis, pratis & agris templi colendis agi hoc in loco.

## 26:30
Verse 30.

IN ALL THE WORKS OF THE LORD] For preparing wood and stones for the Temple. See above 22, 14.

AND IN THE SERVICE OF THE KING] For collecting tributes destined for the uses of the kingdom. It is not likely that Levites were employed to collect such tributes. The work of God and the service of the king are joined together, because they served the king and performed the ministries commanded by the King in these works of God, chapter 22, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

IN CUNCTIS OPERIBVS DOMINI] Ad paran- dum ligna & lapides Templo. Vide supra 22, 14.

ET IN MINISTERIUM REGIS] Ad colligenda tri- buta regni usibus destinata. Levitas ad colligenda tributa talia adhibitos esse non sit verisimile. Opus Dei & servitium re- gis conjunguntur, quia serviebant regi & ministeria a Rege imperata exequebantur in his operibus Dei cap. 22, 5.

## 26:32
Verse 32.

IN ALL THE SERVICE OF GOD AND THE KING) In the Hebrew: for every matter of God and matter of the King: which interpret as the preceding, for the material of the Temple, and for the tributes. We have already spoken of this gloss.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

IN OMNE MINISTERIUM DEI ET REGIS) In Hebræo: ad omnem rem Dei & rem Regis: quod interpretare ut præcedentia, ad materiam Templi, & ad tributa. De hac glossa jamjam diximus.

## 27:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVII.

Ordinary legions, with their tribunes, according to the XII months of the year. Princes of the tribes and prefects of the Economy and counselors.

Verse 1.

PRINCE OF THE FAMILIES) Who were in charge of 24,000. Such was the multitude of men of military age that, without inconvenience, twenty-four thousand were also available for the infirm each month, to whom others and still others succeeded once the month was finished: nor did the labor return to anyone until the year was completed.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVII.

Legiones ordinariæ, cum suis tribunis, secundum XII. menses anni. Principes tribuum & præfecti Oeconomiæ & consiliarii.

Vers. 1.

PRINCEPS FAMILIARUM) Qui 24. millibus præe- rant. Tanta erat multitudo virorum militaris ætatis, ut sine in- commodo, mense quoq; vicena quaterna millia infirmis essent, quibus exacto mense succedebant alii atque alii: nec redibat labor ad quemquam, nisi anno exacto.

## 27:16
Verse 16.

THEY WERE IN CHARGE OF THE TRIBES] Not of those serving in the military. These were the firstborn of the tribes. But the commanders of the soldiers or tribunes were not the firstborn, but men chosen for their strength of body, magnanimity, and military knowledge.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

TRIBUBUS PRÆERANT] Non militantibus. Hi erant primogeniti tribuum. At præfecti militum vel tribuni non primogeniti, sed viri robo- re corporis, magnanimitate & scientia militari præ- stantes delecti.

## 27:23
Verse 23.

BUT DAVID WOULD NOT NUMBER THOSE FROM TWENTY YEARS OLD AND UNDER, BECAUSE THE LORD HAD SAID THAT HE WOULD MULTIPLY ISRAEL LIKE THE STARS OF HEAVEN) It would have been too much labor to number the younger ones. So many were growing up daily according to God's promise.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

NOLUIT AUTEM DAVID NUMERARE EOS A VIGINTI ANNIS INFERIUS, QVIA DIXERAT DO- MINUS UT MULTIPLICARET ISRAEL QVASI STELLAS COELI) Nimii laboris fuerat juniores numerare. Ita multi quotidie succrescebant ex Dei promisso.

## 27:24
verse 24.

IT IS NOT RECORDED IN THE CHRONICLES OF KING DAVID. It seems that David, led by repentance for the deed, made the census he had instituted void, and took care that it should not be recorded in the public annals: as Junius here.

Latin:

vers. 24.

NON EST RELATUS IN FASTOS REGIS DAVID. Videtur David pœnitentia facti ductus re- censionem a se institutam fecisse irritam, & ne in annales publicos referretur, cavisse: ut hic Ju- nius.

## 27:25
Verse 25.

AND OVER THE KING'S TREASURIES WAS AZMAVETH THE SON OF ADIEL] He was the treasurer who received money from the lesser quaestors and either disbursed it or kept it. AND OVER THESE TREASURIES WHICH WERE IN THE CITIES AND IN THE VILLAGES AND IN THE TOWERS WAS JONATHAN THE SON OF UZZIAH] That is, over the tributes.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

SUPER THESAUROS AUTEM REGIS FUIT AZ- MOTH FILIUS ADIEL] Is Gazophylax fuit qui à mino- ribus quæstoribus accipiebat pecunias, easque aut erogabat, aut servabat. HIS AUTEM THESAURIS QUI ERANT IN URBI- BUS ET IN VICIS ET IN TURRIBUS PRÆSIDEBAT JONATHAN FILIUS OZIÆ] Id est, tributis.

## 27:26
Verse 26.

AND OVER THE RUSTIC WORK AND THE HUSBANDMEN, WHO TILLED THE GROUND] Namely, the royal fields. Understand the following in this way as well.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

OPERI AUTEM RUSTICO ET AGRICOLIS, QUI EXERCEBANT TERRAM] Agros scilicet regios. Sic & fequentia intellige.

## 27:30
Verse 30.

BUT OVER THE CAMELS UBIL THE ISMAHELITE) For the Ismahelites, on account of the abundance of camels in their land, were most skilled in handling them.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

SUPER CAMELOS VERO UBIL ISMAHELITES) Nam Ismahelitæ ob camelorum in sua terra copiam ad eos tractandos peritissimi.

## 27:32
Ver. 32.

BUT JONATHAN DAVID'S UNCLE A COUNSELOR, A PRUDENT AND LEARNED MAN) That is, skilled in the law. For that is what the Hebrew סופר properly signifies.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

JONATHAN AUTEM PATRUUS DAVID CONSI- LIARIUS, VIR PRUDENS ET LITERATUS) Id est, legis peritus. Id enim proprie significat Hebræum סופר

## 27:34
ver. 34.

AFTER ACHITOPHEL WAS JOJADA. To Achitophel, David's counselor, who ended his life with a noose, Jojada and Abiathar succeeded, and were of David's inner circle of counselors. These also in v. 4 and 7 are named as successors of Dudia and Asahel, and not, as Cornelius wishes, as those who were vicars for the absent or the hindered.

Latin:

vers. 34.

POST ACHITOPHEL FUIT JOJADA. Achitopheli Davidis consiliario, qui vitam sibi laqueo finivit, Jojada & Abiathar succeffere, ac Da- vidi fuere ab intimis consiliis. Hic etiam v. 4. & 7. successores Dudiæ, & Asahelis nominati, non vero ut Cornelius vult, qui absentium vel impeditorum essent vicarii.

## 28:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVIII.

David, in the assembly of the kingdom, presents Solomon as King, designated by God to build the temple, and commends to him the law of God, and delivers the plan of the temple and its vessels.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVIII.

David in comitiis regni Salomonem Regem à Deo ad templum extruendum designatum sistit, eique legem Dei commendat, & ideam templi & vasorum ejus tradit.

## 28:3
Ver. 3.

AND DAVID ASSEMBLED ALL THE PRINCES OF ISRAEL, THE LEADERS OF THE TRIBES, AND THE CAPTAINS OF THE COMPANIES, WHO SERVED THE KING, THE TRIBUNES ALSO AND THE CENTURIONS) See what was said at the beginning of chapter 13.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

CONVOCAVIT IGITUR DAVID OMNES PRIN- CIPES ISRAEL, DVCES TRIBVVM, ET PRÆPOSI- TOS TVRMARVM, QVI MINISTRABANT REGI, TRIBVNOS QVOQVE ET CENTURIONES) Vide quæ dicta initio capitis 13.

## 28:8
Ver. 8.

KEEP AND SEEK OUT ALL THE COMMANDMENTS OF THE LORD OUR GOD) Keep what is known, and devote effort to knowing. For supine ignorance protects no one.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

CVSTODITE ET PERQVIRITE CVNCTA MAN- DATA DOMINI DEI NOSTRI) Servate cognita, & ut cognoscatis, date operam. Neque enim tuetur quemquam supina ignorantia.

## 28:9
Ver. 9.

YOU, SOLOMON MY SON, KNOW THE GOD OF YOUR FATHER) By words and deeds acknowledge that there is one true God, whom I have worshipped, the creator of the world.

AND SERVE HIM WITH A PERFECT HEART AND A WILLING MIND) God wishes to be worshipped not only by deeds, but especially by the mind, since He is the inspector of the mind, as follows: a thing which all, but especially Kings, must consider. Diogenes the Stoic: δεῖ γὰρ τὸ ἄριστον ὑπὸ τῷ ἀρίστῳ τιμᾶσθαι, καὶ τὸ ἀγεμονοῦν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγεμονοῦντος.

FOR THE LORD SEARCHES ALL HEARTS, AND UNDERSTANDS ALL THE THOUGHTS OF MINDS) Seneca, Epistle 84. Nothing is closed to God: He is present in our minds, and intervenes in the midst of our thoughts.

IF YOU SEEK HIM, YOU WILL FIND HIM: BUT IF YOU FORSAKE HIM, HE WILL CAST YOU OFF FOREVER) God deals with men by conditional decrees.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

TV SALOMON FILI MI, SCITO DEVM PATRIS TU I) Verbis rebusque agnosce unum esse verum Deum, quem ego colui, mundi opificem.

ET SERVITO EI CORDE PERFECTO ET ANI- MO VOLUNTARIO) Deus non factis tantum coli vult, sed vel præcipue animo, quippe animi inspector, ut sequitur: quod omnibus quidem, sed maxime tamen Regibus cogitan- dum. Diogenes Stoicus: δεῖ γὰρ τὸ ἄριστον ὑπὸ τῷ ἀρίστῳ τιμᾶσθαι, καὶ τὸ ἀγεμονοῦν ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγεμονοῦντος.

OMNIA ENIM CORDA SCRVTATVR DOMINUS, ET UNIVERSAS MENTIVM COGITATIONES IN- TELLIGIT) Seneca Epistola 84. Nihil Deo clausum est: interest animis nostris, & cogitationibus mediis intervenit.

SI QVÆSIERIS EUM INVENIES: SI AUTEM DE- RELINQVES EUM, PROJICIET TE IN ÆTERNUM) Agit Deus cum hominibus decretis conditionatis.

## 28:11
Ver. 11.

DAVID GAVE ALSO TO SOLOMON HIS SON THE DESCRIPTION) In the Hebrew there is more; that which had been in the spirit with him: that is, he gave him a visible form, such as God had inscribed upon his own mind: as is said below in 19.

From verse 19 it is evident that all those things which pertained to the construction of the temple came to David from the hand of the Lord, and thus that David received from the Lord the exemplar or idea of the temple and the sacred vessels, whether he received it from a Prophet, or whether it was shown by the Lord just as the tabernacle was to Moses in Exodus 25.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

DEDIT AUTEM DAVID SALOMONI FILIO SUO DESCRIPTIONEM) In Hebræo plus est; quod fuerat in spiritu cum eo: id est, dedit ei formam conspicuam, qualem Deus animo ipsius inscripserat: ut dicitur infra 19.

E vers. 19. id constat, scripta de manu Domini venisse ad Davidem ea omnia, quæ ad exstructionem templi faciebant, adeoque exemplar, vel ideam à Do- mino accepisse Davidem templi, & vasorum sacro- rum, sive à Propheta acceperit, sive ostensum à Do- mino ut Mosi tabernaculum Exod. 25. instar illud fuerit.

## 28:17
Verse 17.

AND GOLDEN LIONS) Others more correctly translate here and in the following words κρατῆρας. The Greeks, as often in obscure matters, have kept the Hebrew word κεφουρὶ, which Theodoret interprets as σκεύη τινὰ χρυσᾶ ἐν οἷς ἔφυρον τὴν σεμίδα- λιν τῷ ἐλαίῳ. Kimchi understands spoons. The forms of lions and oxen, the beginnings of Solomon's faults.

The Vulgate is deservedly deserted: Vatablus, Pagninus, and Abulensis agree with the Hebrew and the LXX, and no mention of little lions or lions, which the Vulgate introduced here in 1 Kings 7 and 8, occurs: the crater is not called so from the form of a lion, but from the verb כפר he hid, he covered, because it had a lid.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

ET LEUNCULOS AUREOS) Rectius alii hic & in verbis sequentibus vertunt κρατῆρας. Græci, ut sæpe in obscuris, servarunt Ebræam vocem κεφουρὶ, quod Theodore- tus interpretatur σκεύη τινὰ χρυσᾶ ἐν οἷς ἔφυρον τὴν σεμίδα- λιν τῷ ἐλαίῳ. Kimchi cochlearia intelligit. Leonum & boum formæ, initia culparum Salomonis.

Merito deseritur Vulgata: Ebræo & LXX. con- sentiunt Vatablus, Pagninus, Abulensis, nec ulla le- unculorum vel leonum, quos hic invexit Vulg. 1. Reg. 7. & 8. occurrit mentio: Crater non à forma leonis, sed à verbo כפר occultavit, obtexit, dicitur, quia operculum habuit.

## 29:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIX.

The expenditures of David, the princes, and the people for the temple. The King celebrates God, and prays for Solomon, with the people. Solomon is created King, Sadoc High Priest. The death of David.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIX.

Impensæ Davidis, principum & populi ad tem- plum. Rex celebrat Deum, & orat pro Salomone, cum populo. Salomo Rex creatur, Sadoc Pontifex. Davidis obi- tus.

## 29:2
Verse 2.

AND AS IT WERE STIBIUM-LIKE) Similar to stibium.

IN the Hebrew: Stones of paint, which provide paint to those looking at them, as stibium does for women, so that in them appear wonderful and elegant forms of various things: such as Agates. There is added in the Vulgate AND PARIAN MARBLE, from the island of Paros, but this is not held in the Hebrew text, even if it occurs among the LXX: only marble is expressed, which nevertheless was entirely select.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ET QVASI STIBINOS) Stibio similes.

IN Ebr. Lapides fuci, qui intuentibus fucum, ut stibium mulieribus faciunt, ut in iis appareant miræ & elegantes variarum rerum formæ: quales sunt Agates. Additur in Vulg. ET MARMOR PARIUM, ex Paro insula, sed hoc non habetur in textu Ebræo, etsi apud LXX. occurrat: marmor so- lum exprimitur, quod tamen omnino selectum fuit.

## 29:4
THREE THOUSAND TALENTS] Hyrcanus took just as many from the monuments of David when besieged by Antiochus Pius, according to Josephus.

Moreover, these three thousand talents of gold make 540 tons of gold, just as 7000 talents of silver produce 105 tons of gold, that is, 645 tons of gold in total, as we call them. See what we said at 1 Chronicles 22:14.

OF THE GOLD OF OPHIR) Here also the LXX have ἐκ σουφίρ. See what is said in 2 Sam. 9, 28.

BY THE HAND OF JEHIEL THE GERSHONITE) Who with his sons was set over this matter: above 26, 22.

Latin:

TRIA MILLIA TALENTA] Totidem è monumen- tis Davidis abstulit Hyrcanus ab Antiocho Pio obsessus, te- ste Josepho.

Efficiunt autem hæc tria millia talentorum au- ri 540. tonnas auri, uti 7000. talenta argenti pro- ducunt 105. auri tonnas, hoc est, conjunctim 645. tonnas auri, quas vocamus. Vide quæ ad 1. Paral. 22, 14. diximus.

DE AURO OPHIR) Hîc etiam LXX. habent ἐκ σου- φίρ. Vide quæ dicta 2. Sam. 9, 28.

PER MANUM JAKIEL GERSONITÆ) Qui cum filiis suis huic rei erat præpositus: supra 26, 22.

## 29:7
Ver. 7. FIVE THOUSAND TALENTS OF GOLD.

The princes of the people, and the royal prefects contributed five thousand talents of gold, that is, 900 tons of gold, or 90 millions, as we call them, and besides ten thousand solidi; that is, 333½ gold shekels, which make 2000 Joachim thalers, and also 10000 talents of silver, that is, 150 tons of gold. The total sum is 1050 tons of gold, and 2000 Joachim thalers: besides the value and sum of the copper, and iron, and precious stones.

Latin:

Vers. 7. AURI TALENTA QUINQUE MIL- LIA.

Principes populi, & præfecti Regii quinque millia talenta auri, h. e. 900. tonnas auri, vel 90. mil- liones, ut vocamus, contulere, ac prætereà solidos decem millia? hoc est, siclos aureos 333½. qui efficiunt 2000. Joachamicos, nec non 10000. talentorum ar- genti h. e. 150. tonnas auri. Summa tota est 1050. tonnarum auri, & 2000. Joachimicorum: præter æ- ris, & ferri, ac lapidum pretiosorum valorem ac summam.

## 29:9
Ver. 9.

AND THE PEOPLE REJOICED WHEN THEY OFFERED WILLINGLY) God loves a cheerful giver 2 Cor. 9, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

LÆTATUSQVE EST POPULUS CUM VOTA SPONTE PROMITTERENT) Hilarem datorem amat Deus 2. Cor. 9, 7.

## 29:14
Ver. 14.

WHO AM I AND WHO IS THY PEOPLE, THAT WE SHOULD BE ABLE TO OFFER ALL THESE THINGS UNTO THEE?] Whence have we the material for this liberality, if not from thee?

ALL THINGS ARE THINE, AND OF THINE OWN HAND HAVE WE GIVEN UNTO THEE] Thus the Greek Christians say in their offerings, τὰ σὰ ἀπὸ τῶν σῶν.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

QVIS EGO ET QVIS POPULUS TUUS, UT POS- SEMUS HÆC TIBI VNIVERSA PROMITTERE?] Vn- de nobis materia hujus liberalitatis, nisi abs te?

TVA SVNT OMNIA, ET QUÆ DE MANU TUA ACCEPIMUS, DEDIMUS TIBI] Sic Christiani Græci in oblationibus dicunt, τὰ σὰ ἀπὸ τῶν σῶν.

## 29:15
Ver. 15.

FOR WE ARE STRANGERS BEFORE THEE] Not owners, but thy tenants.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

PEREGRINI ENIM SUMUS CORAM TE] Non proprietarii, sed tui coloni.

## 29:18
Ver. 18.

KEEP THIS INTENTION OF THEIR HEART FOREVER, AND MAY THIS MIND ALWAYS REMAIN IN REVERENCE OF THEE) God is said to do this when He suffers nothing to be lacking on His part, giving good teachers, and aids not only necessary, but also abundant.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

CUSTODI IN ÆTERNUM HANC VOLUNTA- TEM CORDIS EORUM, ET SEMPER IN VENE- RATIONEM TUI MENS ISTA PERMANEAT) Fa- cere id dicitur Deus, cum nihil à sua parte desiderari patitur, dans bonos magistros, & auxilia non necessaria tantum, sed & affluentia.

## 29:20
Vers. 20.

THEY WORSHIPPED GOD, THEN THE KING) With the same gesture, but a distinct mind. Josephus on this latter reverence: ἐυχαρίstησαν δὲ καὶ Δαβίδῃ περὶ πάντων ὧν αὐτῶν τὴν βασιλείαν παραλαβόντων ἀπέλαυσαν.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

ADORAVERUNT DEUM, DEINDE REGEM) Pari gestu, animo distincto. Josephus de posteriori ista vene- ratione: ἐυχαρίstησαν δὲ καὶ Δαβίδῃ περὶ πάντων ὧν αὐτῶν τὴν βασιλείαν παραλαβόντων ἀπέλαυσαν.

## 29:22
Vers. 22.

AND THEY ANOINTED SOLOMON THE SON OF DAVID A SECOND TIME) As king now by full right and subject to no one: for this happened after the death of David, to be narrated below.

The former anointing was private 1 Kings 1:39; therefore he had to be anointed publicly here, so that all might know that he was King of Israel, and might honor him as such.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ET UNXERUNT SECUNDO SALOMONEM FILI- UM DAVID) Vt jam pleno jure regem & parentem ne- mini: nam hoc post mortem Davidis infra narrandam con- tigit.

Prior unctio privata fuit 1. Reg. 1, 39. ideo hic publice ungendus erat, ut omnes scirent, eum esse Regem Israelis, ac ut talem colerent.

## 29:24
THEY GAVE THE HAND AND WERE SUBJECT TO KING SOLOMON) The Latin interpreter added these last words, so that the Hebrew manner of speaking, they gave hands under King Solomon, might be more correctly understood. Also among nations sprung from the Germans, to place the hand between the knees is a sign of subjection.

Latin:

DEDERUNT MANUM ET SUBJECTI FUERUNT SALOMONI REGI) Postrema hæc addidit Latinus Inter- pres, ut Hebræum loquendi genus, dederunt manus sub Solomonem Regem, rectius intelligeretur. Etiam apud gen- tes è Germanis ortas manus inter genua ponere subjectionis signum.

## 29:25
Vers. 25.

AND HE GAVE HIM THE GLORY OF THE KINGDOM) Majesty and wealth.

Latin:

Vers. 25.

DEDITQVE EI GLORIAM REGNI) Majestatem & opes.

## 29:26
Vers. 26.

HE REIGNED) He had reigned and soon: he had died: namely when Solomon, as was said before, was reigning by full right.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

REGNAVIT) Regnaverat & mox: mortuus erat: nempe cum Solomon, ut ante dictum est, pleno jure re- gnaret.

## 29:29
Vers. 29.

IN THE BOOK OF SAMUEL THE SEER, AND IN THE BOOK OF NATHAN THE PROPHET, AND IN THE VOLUME OF GAD THE SEER) Whence were taken those four books, which the Hebrews call the two of Samuel and the two of Kings.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

IN LIBRO SAMUELIS VIDENTIS, ET IN LIBRO NATHAN PROPHETÆ, ATQVE IN VOLUMINE GAD VIDENTIS) Vnde sumti sunt libri illi quatuor, quos Samuelis duos & duos Regum Hebræi appellant.

## 29:30
Ver. 30.

OR IN ALL THE KINGDOMS OF THE LANDS) Namely in Philistia, Moab, Amalek, and Damascene Syria, which he subdued in war: in Ammon and other parts of Syria, whose affairs happened in war.

Latin:

Vers. 30.

SIVE IN CUNCTIS REGNIS TERRARUM) Nempe in Philistina, Moabitide, Amalecitide, Syria Damascena, quæ bello subegit: in Ammonitide & aliis Syriæ partibus, quarum res bello accidit.

# 2 Chronicles

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 1). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
SECOND CHRONICLES

This second book deals both with the history of Solomon and with the events that took place after the schism of the kingdom. Describing the state of the Jewish kingdom from Solomon until the liberation from the Babylonian captivity brought about by Cyrus, [it covers] 479 years, namely: the three years of Solomon, in whose fourth year the temple was built; from then until the captivity which occurred in the 4th year of Jehoiakim, 406 years; and the 70 years of captivity, up to the first year of the monarchy of Cyrus. It is completed in two parts. I. Concerning King Solomon, up to chapter 10. II. Concerning the Kings of Judah and Israel, up to the Babylonian captivity, from chapter 10 to verse 17 of chapter 36.

PART I.

It sets forth King Solomon's confirmation in the kingdom, obtained through θεόσδοτον (God-given) wisdom by means of sacrifices and prayers, ch. 1; then the construction of the temple. (1.) Regarding the timber and architects, ch. 2. (2.) Regarding the place, time, and space, ch. 3. (3.) Regarding the preparation of the instruments, ch. 4. (4.) Regarding the introduction of the ark, ch. 5. (5.) With the inaugural prayer subjoined, ch. 6; and (6.) the sending down of fire from heaven and the divine apparition, ch. 7; then the administration of the polity, the economy, and ecclesiastical affairs, ch. 8; then his fame and the visit of the Queen of Arabia, ch. 9.

PART II.

It continues the history of the Kings of Judah; 1. up to the tyrannical reign of Athaliah: then regarding the remaining kings. In the first section, I. The reign of Rehoboam is presented, and under him the schism brought about by Jeroboam, ch. 10, and its confirmation, ch. 11, as well as the defection of Rehoboam from the law and the punishment through Shishak, ch. 12. II. The history of Abijah, and especially his victory against Jeroboam, ch. 13. III. The happy reign of pious Asa, ch. 14, and his confirmation in piety through Azariah, ch. 15, and the confederation with the Syrian against Baasha, disapproved by GOD, ch. 16. IV. The excellent reign of Jehoshaphat and the ecclesiastical visitation, ch. 17; his less fortunate alliance with Ahab, ch. 18; his rebuke by the prophet Jehu, ch. 19; his victory against enemies of a triple kind, ch. 20. V. The unhappy government of impious Jehoram, ch. 21. VI. The one-year reign of Ahaziah, and VII. the tyranny of Athaliah, ch. 22. In the other section, I. The coronation of Joash, ch. 23. and his piety while Jehoiada was living, and after he died, idolatry and punishment, ch. 24. II. Amaziah struck the Edomites, but serving their idols and provoking the King of Israel, he was struck, ch. 25. III. Uzziah first studied piety and had happy successes, but after he attempted to burn incense, he was seized with leprosy, ch. 26. IV. Jotham, pious and happy, made the Ammonites tributary, ch. 27. V. Ahaz, afflicted because of idolatry and profane treaties, ch. 28. VI. Hezekiah, most pious, purges the temple, ch. 29; celebrates the Passover, ch. 30; organizes the priests, Levites, and the ecclesiastical treasury, ch. 31; is delivered from Sennacherib and a lethal disease, ch. 32. VII. Manasseh, impious, performs penance: to whom VIII. succeeds Amon, a perpetual worshiper of idols, ch. 33. IX. Josiah abolishes idols and renews the covenant with God, ch. 34, and celebrates the Passover, ch. 35. There succeed X. Jehoahaz, XI. Jehoiakim, and XII. Jehoiachin, as well as XIII. the captivity of Zedekiah, ch. 36.

PART I. THE HISTORY OF KING SOLOMON.

Latin:

POSTER PARALIP

SECUNDUS hic liber agit cum de Salomo- nis Historia, tum de rebus post scissionem regni gestis. Statum Judaici regni a Salo- mone usque ad liberationem e captivitate Babylonica per Cyrum factam describens, annorum 479. nimirum trium Salomonis, cujus quarto extru- ctum est templum, inde ad captivitatem 4. anno Joa- kimi factam annorum 406. & 70. annorum captivi- tatis, usque ad primum Monarchiæ Cyri. Duabus absolvitur partibus. I. De Rege Salomone ad c. 10. II. De Regibus Juda, & Israelis usque ad ca- ptivitatem Babylonicam, a cap. 10. ad v. 17. c. 36.

PARS I.

REgis Salomonis exponit tum confirmationem in regno, per sapientiam θεόσδοτον sacrificiis & precibus obtentam c. 1. tum templi exstructionem. (1.) Qua ligna, & architectos c. 2. (2.) Qua locum, tempus & spatium, c. 3. (3.) Qua instrumentorum apparatum, c. 4. (4.) Qua arcæ introductionem, c. 5. (5.) Subjuncta oratione inaugurali c. 6. & (6.) Ignis de cælo dimissione, ac divina apparitione cap. 7. tum administrationem politias, Oeconomiæ, & rei Ec- clesiasticæ c. 8. tum celebritatem, & Reginæ Arabiæ visitationem cap. 9.

PARS II.

REgum Judæ Historiam prosequitur; 1. usque ad Athaliæ tyrannicum regimen: Deinde quoad reges cæteros. In priori sectione I. Rehabeami re- gnum exhibetur, & sub eo schisma per Jeroboamum factum, c. 10. idque confirmatum, cap. 11. nec non defectio Rehabeami a lege ac pœna per Sisackum c. 12. II. Abiæ historia, ejusque imprimis contra Jeroboamum victoria cap. 13. III. Assæ pii felix regimen cap. 14. ejusque in pietate per Asariam confirmatio c. 15. & cum Syro contra Baësan, DEO improbata confœderatio cap. 16. IV. Josaphati opti- mum regimen, & visitatio Ecclesiastica cap. 17. minus fausta cum Achabo societas cap. 18. a Jehu prophe- ta reprehensa cap. 19. victoria contra triplicis gene- ris hostes cap. 20. V. Jorami impii infelix gu- bernatio cap. 21. VI. Ahasiæ annuum Regimen, & VII. Athaliæ tyrannis c. 22. In altera sectione I. Joasi coronatio cap. 23. & pietas vivente Jojada, eoque defuncto idololatria & pœna, cap. 24. II. Amazias Edomitas percussit, sed idolis eorum ser- viens, & Regem Israelis provocans percussus est, cap. 25. III. Uziæ primum pietati studuit, & feli- ces successus habuit, post suffimenta adolere cona- tus lepra correptus fuit cap. 26. IV. Jotham pius & felix Ammonitas tributarios fecit cap. 27. V. Ahas ob idololatriam & fœdera profana afflictus c. 28. VI. Hiskias pientissimus templum repurgat c. 29. Pascha celebrat cap. 30. Sacerdotes, Levi- tas & ærarium Ecclesiasticum ordinat, c. 31. a Senna- cheribo, & morbo lethali liberatur cap. 32. VII. Manasses impius pœnitentiam agit: cui VIII. succe- dit Ammon idolorum cultor perpetuus c. 33. IX. Josias idola abrogat, & fœdus cum Deo renovat c. 34. ac Pascha celebrat c. 35. Succedit X. Joahæ, XI. Jojakimi, & XII. Jechoniæ, ut & XIII. Zedekiæ capti- vitas, cap. 36.

PARS I. HISTORIA REGIS SALOMONIS.

## 1:1 Argument
CHAPTER I.

The prayer and sacrifice of Solomon. The promise of wisdom, riches, and glory. A description of his magnificence and wealth.

Latin:

CAPUT I.

Oratio, & sacrificium Salomonis. Promissio Sapientiæ, opum & gloriæ. Descriptio ma- gnificentiæ, & divitiarum ejus.

## 1:2
Verse 2.

AND SOLOMON COMMANDED) In the Hebrew: Solomon said: He exhorted them. For in sacred matters, Kings were accustomed to seek the consent of the people, as we said regarding the previous book 13, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

PRÆCEPITQVE SOLOMON) In Hebræo: dixit Salo- mon: Hortatus est eos. Solebant enim in sacris maxime Re- ges consensum adhibere populi, ut diximus ad librum supe- riorem 13, 1.

## 1:5
Verse 5.

WAS THERE BEFORE THE TABERNACLE OF THE LORD) Before the doors, as also afterwards in the Temple.

Mention is made of twin tabernacles in verses 3, 4, and 5: one in Gibeon, which Moses had made: the other in Jerusalem, which David had fixed for the ark of God, when he transferred it there by divine inspiration: for he was a Prophet of the Lord. Here the discourse is concerning the Mosaic tabernacle.

WHICH SOLOMON ALSO SOUGHT) That is, he approached.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ERAT IBI CORAM TABERNACVLO DOMINI) Ante fores, ut & postea in Templo.

Gemini tabernaculi v. 3. 4. 5. mentio fit: alte- rius in Gibhone, quod fecerat Moses: Alterius in Jerusalem, quod arcæ Dei fixerat David, cum illam eo transferret ex inspiratione divina: Erat enim Propheta Domini. Hic de tabernaculo Mosaico sermo est.

QVOD ET REQVISIVIT SALOMON) Id est, adiit.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II.

Solomon asks King Hiram for wood and a craftsman for the structure of the temple, and he counts the proselytes for this use.

Latin:

CAPUT II.

Salomo petit a Rege Hiram ligna & artificem ad structuram templi, numeratque prose- lytos ad hunc usum.

## 2:7
Verse 7.

AND WHO KNOWS HOW TO CARVE ENGRAVINGS) Works receding inward.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ET QVI SCIAT SCVLPERE CÆLATVRAS) Opera intus refugientia.

## 2:13
Verse 13. MY FATHER.

The Vulgate is wrong in this way: the King did not send his own father, but a skilled man, who was to Hiram my father, he says.

Latin:

Vers. 13. PATREM MEUM.

Male vulgatus ita: non suum Patrem Rex mi- sit, sed virum peritum, qui erat Hiramo Patri meo, inquit.

## 2:14
Verse 14.

THE SON OF A WOMAN OF THE DAUGHTERS OF DAN, WHOSE FATHER WAS A TYRIAN) For it was permitted for Hebrew women to marry a foreign husband, without prejudice to their religion. The Law thought it easier for men to be corrupted by women than women by men.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

FILIVM MVLIERIS DE FILIABVS DAN, CVJVS PATER FVIT TTRIVS) Licebat enim fœminis He- bræis nubere marito extraneo, salva religione sua. Lex facilius putavit viros posse a fœminis depravari, quam fœ- minas a viris.

## 2:16
Ver. 16.

RAFTS) In Hebrew: רפסדות: from the Greek: ῥαψῳδία, which signifies the weaving together of poems, transferred to the weaving together of rafts. Not only in the times of Ezra, but also of Daniel, certain Greek words had penetrated into the Hebrew and Chaldean language through commerce.

Latin:

Vers. 16.

RATIBVS) In Hebræo: רפסדות: ex Græco: ῥα- ψῳδία, quod contexturam carminum significat, translatum ad ratium contexturam. Non Esdræ tantum, sed & Danie- lis temporibus Græca quædam vocabula in Hebræum Chal- dæumque sermonem commercio penetraverant.

## 2:17
Ver. 17.

SOLOMON THEREFORE NUMBERED ALL THE PROSELYTE MEN) In Hebrew: גרים, that is, strangers. Understand those who had not subjected themselves to the law, but observed the precepts given to Noah. For those who had subjected themselves to the law acted with equal right with the citizens.

The Jewish fiction concerning the precepts given to Noah returns. And yet those were called Proselytes who aggregated themselves to the people of God from among the strangers: Whom it was absolutely necessary thereafter to subject themselves to the law: For where is it proven that certain precepts were given peculiarly to Noah, and that they were still in force in the time of Solomon? The moral law was not unknown to Noah, inasmuch as it was also inscribed in nature, which, having been solemnly repeated later through Moses, bound the Proselytes no less than the Jews in the time of Solomon; indeed, it binds all men at all times.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

NVMERAVIT IGITVR SALOMON OMNES VI- ROS PROSELYTOS) In Hebræo: גרים, id est, adve- nas. Eos intellige, qui legi se non subjecerant, sed præcepta Noæ data servabant. Nam qui legi se subjecerant, pari jure cum civibus agebant.

Redit commentum de Præceptis Noæ datis Ju- daicum. Atqui Proselyti dicebantur, qui se populo Dei ex advenis aggregabant: Quos omnino opor- tebat deinceps legi se subjicere: Præcepta enim quæ- dam Noæ data fuisse peculiariter, eaque Salomonis tempore adhuc viguisse, unde probatur? Lex moralis Noæ non erat ignota, utpote quæ naturæ etiam in- sculpta, quæ solenniter per Mosen postea repetita, Salomonis tempore non minus Proselytos obligabat, quam Judæos; imo omni tempore omnes obligat homines.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III.

The place, time, and parts of the built temple: the porch, the veil, and the two bronze columns before the doors of the temple.

Latin:

CAPUT III.

Locus, tempus, partes ædificati templi: porticus, velum, & duæ columnæ æneæ ante fores tem- pli.

## 3:7
Ver. 7.

MOREOVER THE GOLD WAS MOST PROVED) In Hebrew: פרוים. Certain Hebrews interpret it as gold to have been such, that it resembled the color of the blood of bullocks (which are פֿרים in Hebrew). But the LXX believed it to be the name of a region. For they put ἐκ Φαρσίμ. Some conjecture it to be Parbatia of Susiana: perhaps once divided into two cities: for the form of the name in the Hebrew text is dual. They err gravely who understand a part of America the name. That region was indeed not known in those times, nor, as I believe, inhabited: and that name, unknown to the natives, it received from the Spaniards, who found the first man they met with by that name.

Others understand the gold of Ophir by the apheresis of the first letter, from R. פרה, it brought forth fruit, because the region is most fruitful and very rich in gold in the East Indies: and that those gold-bearing regions, Sumatra, Taprobana, and Pegu, were called by these names, Ophir and Parvaim, by Solomon and the Hebrews. But we have spoken of these at 1 Kings 10:22. Junius understands Chavilah, of which in Gen. 2:11, because Parbatia is in it, or in the kingdom of the Characeni, according to Pliny, book 6, ch. 28.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

PORRO AVRVM ERAT PROBATISSIMVM) In Hebræo: פרוים. Interpretantur Hebræi quidam aurum tale fuisse, quod juvencorum (qui פֿרים Hebræis) sanguinem colore referret. At LXX. regionis nomen esse credidere. Ponunt enim ἐκ Φαρσίμ. Quidam conjiciunt esse Parbatiam Susianes: distinctam forte olim in duas urbes: nam forma nominis in Hebræo textu est dualis. Graviter errant, qui Americæ partem Peruanam intelligunt solo nominis sono ducti. Ea vero regio illis temporibus cognita non fuit, nec ut ego credo, habitata: & nomen illud indigenis ignotum accepit ab Hispanis, qui primum hominem sibi obvium eo nomine repererunt.

Alii aurum Ophir intelligunt per aphæresin primæ literæ, a R. פרה fructificavit eo quod regio sit maxime frugifera, & auri feracissima in India Orientali: atque his nominibus Ophir, & Parvaim a Salomone & Ebræis nuncupatas esse regiones illas auriferas Sumatram, Taprobanam, Pegu. Sed de his diximus ad 1. Reg. 10, 22. Chavilam intelligit Junius, de qua Gen. 2, 11. quia in ea seu Characenorum regno Parbacia est teste Plin. 6. c. 28.

## 4:1 Argument
CHAPTER IV. Solomon constructs the altar of burnt offerings, the molten sea, two golden basins, ten golden lampstands, tables, vials, and the rest of the vessels of the temple.

Latin:

CAPUT IV. Salomo fabricat altare holocaustorum, mare fusile, duas conchas aureas, decem candelabra aurea, mensas, phialas, & reliqua templi vasa.

## 4:8
Verse 8. HE ALSO MADE THE COURT OF THE PRIESTS) In the circuit of the basilica of the Temple, where cells were also built for the Priests. AND A GREAT BASILICA) In Hebrew: and a great court: that is, an open-air space for the use of the people. This court of the people surrounded and encompassed the court of the Priests on three sides, and was as it were the temple of the people; in Hebrew it is called azara, that is, a help, because the people praying there felt divine help.

Latin:

Vers. 8. FECIT ETIAM ATRIVM SACERDOTVM) In ambitu basilicæ Templi, ubi & cellæ structæ Sacerdotibus. ET BASILICAM GRANDEM) In Hebræo: & atrium magnum: id est, subdiale in usum populi. Hoc atrium populi cingebat, & ambiebat a tribus lateribus atrium Sacerdotum, eratque quasi templum populi; Ebr. dicitur azara, id est, adjutorium, quia populus illic orans auxilium divinum sentiebat.

## 4:16
Verse 16. HIRAM HIS FATHER. Some think that Hiram the son, and others that his father of the same name, did these things. Osiander makes one craftsman called Hiram Abes.

Latin:

Vers. 16. HIRAM PATER EJUS. Quædam Hiramum filium, quædam vero Patrem ejus nominis ejusdem fecisse putant. Osiander unum artificem facit vocatum Hiram Abes.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V. Solomon brings the treasures and sacred vessels into the temple, and the ark of the covenant into the Holy of Holies. God is worshipped with music and sacrifices, and fills the house with his glory.

Latin:

CAPUT V. Salomo thesauros & vasa sacra, in templum, & arcam fœderis, in Sanctum Sanctorum inducit. Deus Musica & sacrificiis colitur, impletque domum gloria sua.

## 5:11
Verse 11. NOR WAS THE ORDER DIVIDED.
