In Hebrew it is said the order was not observed, which, namely, was exactly observed among the Priests thereafter after the dedication of the temple: because on account of the multitude of sacrifices the Priests, whose turns were at that time, did not suffice, but all being summoned flocked together from all Israel.

Latin:

Vers. 11. NEC ORDO DIVISUS ERAT. In Ebr. dicitur non observatus ordo, qui sc. inter Sacerdotes post templi dedicationem exacte deinceps observabatur: quia ob sacrificiorum multitudinem non sufficiebant Sacerdotes, quorum vices erant isto tempore, sed convocati omnes confluxere ex toto Israele.

## 5:13
Verse 13. GIVE THANKS TO THE LORD, FOR HE IS GOOD) For they were singing Psalm 136, which was accustomed to be used for joyful occasions. See also 7:3 and 20:21.

Latin:

Vers. 13. CONFITEMINI DOMINO, QVONIAM BONVS) Canebant enim Psalmum 136. solitum adhiberi rebus lætis. Vide & 7, 3. & 20, 21.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI. Solomon blessed the people, gave thanks to God for the fulfillment of the promise made to David, and prayed for the hearing of those praying in this temple.

Latin:

CAPUT VI. Salomo populo benedixit, Deo gratias egit de impletione promissionis Davidi factæ, & pro exauditione orantium in hoc templo oravit.

## 6:13
Verse same. SOLOMON HAD MADE A BRASS BASE] That is, a platform, in the manner of a basin, as the Hebrews say. Junius and Tremellius render it a platform called a laver from its shape. AND HAD PLACED IT IN THE MIDST OF THE BASILICA] Understand, in the midst of the court or open-air space: for the basilica is properly היכל.

Latin:

Vers. eod. FECERAT SALOMON BASIM ÆNEAM] Id est, suggestum, in modum conchæ, ut ajunt Hebræi. Junius & Tremell. reddunt suggestum labrum dictum a forma. ET POSVERAT EAM IN MEDIO BASILICÆ] Intellige, in medio atrii sive subdialis: nam basilica proprie, היכל.

## 6:29
Verse 29. IF ANYONE OF THY PEOPLE ISRAEL SHALL HAVE PRAYED) More fully in the Hebrew: Every prayer and every supplication which shall have been made by any man whatsoever or by all thy people Israel. For the copulative conjunction is here, as often elsewhere, placed for a disjunctive. The meaning is: hear the prayers which shall be made here, whether private or public.

Latin:

Vers. 29. SI QVIS DE POPVLO TVO ISRAEL FVERIT DEPRECATVS) Amplius in Hebræo: Omnem orationem, omnemque supplicationem, quæ facta fuerit ab homine quocunque aut ab universo populo tuo Israel. Copulativa enim conjunctio, hîc ut alibi sæpe posita est pro disjunctiva. Sensus est: exaudi, quæ hîc fient preces sive privatæ sive publicas.

## 6:42
Verse 42. DO NOT TURN AWAY THE FACE OF THY CHRIST] Other Latin editions have aberferis more correctly: that is, I ask that thou do not turn away me, made King by thee. Junius and Tremellius: do not turn away the face of thy anointed, with this note added, that is, CHRIST; who is the unique and eternal head of thy anointed ones. Which the following words favor, remember the mercies towards David, thy servant, i.e., the promises made to him, from which that one concerning Christ stands out, 2 Sam. 7, for which mercies of God David sang Ps. 89:2. These are the faithful promises made to David, Isa. 55:3, Acts 13:34.

Latin:

Vers. 42. NE AVERTERIS FACIEM CHRISTI TUI] Alia editiones Latinæ aberferis rectius: id est, rogo ne me Regem abs te factum averferis. Junius & Tremellius: ne avertas faciem uncti tui, addita hac nota, id est, CHRISTI; qui unicum est, æternumque unctorum tuorum caput. Cui fa- vent sequentia, memento misericordiarum erga Davi- dem, servum tuum, h. e. promissionum ipsi factarum, e quibus eminet illa de Christo 2. Sam. 7. ob quas misericordias Dei cantavit David Ps. 89, 2. Hæc sunt fidelia Davidi facta promissa Esa. 55, 3. Actor. 13, 34.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAP. VII.

Solomon, sacrificing, consecrates the house of God, with fire from heaven devouring the victims.

Ver. 1. FIRE DESCENDED FROM HEAVEN) Thus God in this Temple made himself known in two ways, by the cloud (above 5, 14.) and by fire, as formerly in the desert. Add what was said at Gen. 4, 4.

Latin:

CAP. VII.

Salomo sacrificans domum Dei consecrat, igne de cœlo victimas devorante.

Vers. 1. IGNIS DESCENDIT DE COELO) Ita Deus in hoc Templo duobus modis se testatum fecit, per nebulam (supra 5, 14.) & per ignem, ut olim in deserto. Adde quæ dicta ad Gen. 4, 4.

## 7:2
Ver. 2. MAJESTY. A splendid and glorious cloud representing the majesty of God.

Latin:

Vers. 2. MAJESTAS. Nubes splendida, & gloriosa Dei majestatem repræsentans.

## 7:3
Ver. 3. AND FALLING PROSTRATE ON THE GROUND UPON THE PAVEMENT LAID WITH STONE THEY WORSHIPPED] The Hebrew words seem to signify more the faces cast down to the ground, and the body bent.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET CORRVENTES PRONI IN TERRAM SVPER PAVIMENTVM STRATVM LAPIDE ADORAVE- RVNT] Hebrææ voces magis significare videntur vultus humi dejectos, & corpus inflexum.

## 7:6
Ver. 6. HYMNS. In Hebrew, a hymn (namely Ps. 136.) delivered into their hand, as Junius and Tremellius: Vulgate, singing hymns by their hands, namely by playing musical instruments with their hands. The Hebrew way of speaking by the hands implies only ministry, whether hands are applied in the same or not.

Latin:

Vers. 6. HYMNOS. In Ebr. Hymnum (sc. Ps. 136.) traditum in ma- num ipsorum, ut Junius & Tremellius: Vulgat. hy- mnos canentes per manus suas, manibus sc. pulsando instrumenta Musica. Modus loquendi Ebraicus per manus, ministerium solum infert sive manus ad- hibeantur in eodem, seu non.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII.

Solomon builds cities, subjugates the remaining Canaanites, ordains sacred ministries, receives gold from Ophir.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII.

Salomo urbes ædificat, Cananæos reliquos sub- jugat, ministeria sacra ordinat, aurum ex Ophir accipit.

## 8:3
Ver. 3. HE OBTAINED IT. In Hebrew it is he fortified it.

Latin:

Vers. 3. OBTINUIT EAM. In Ebr. est munivit eam.

## 8:4
Ver. 4. PALMYRA. Hebrew Thadmor (a city or fortress.)

AND OTHER MOST FORTIFIED CITIES. In Hebrew, And all the store cities. So also v. 6.

Latin:

Vers. 4. PALMIRAM. Ebr. Thadmor (civitatem vel arcem.)

ET ALIAS CIVITATES MUNITISSIMAS. In Ebr. Et omnes civitates thesaurarias. Sic etiam v. 6.

## 8:6
Ver. 6. AND THE CITIES OF THE HORSEMEN) In which he kept horses brought from Egypt, 1 Kings 10, 28. In this book 1, 14. and below 9, 25. See Basil 1 Macc. 3, 19.

In the Hebrew, horsemen are not considered horses. Others therefore more correctly understand cities, in which war chariots were kept, and in which horsemen lived, which Solomon either fortified or remarkably restored.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET URBES EQVITVM) In quibus equos alebat ex Ægypto advectos, 1. Reg. 10, 28. Hoc libro 1, 14. & infra 9, 25. Vide Basilium 1. Macc. 3, 19.

In Ebr. Equites non equi habentur. Rectius ergo alii urbes intelligunt, in quibus currus bellici asfervabantur, & in quibus equites degebant, quas vel muniverit, vel egregie instaurarit Salomo.

## 8:9
Verse 9. BUT OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL HE MADE NO SERVANTS FOR THE KING'S WORK] Namely, for perpetual work, as the foreigners: but these succeeded one another, 1 Kings 5, verse 13.

Latin:

Vers. 9. PORRO DE FILIIS ISRAEL NON POSUIT, VT SERVIRENT OPERIBVS REGIS] Nempe perpetuis operis, ut extranei: sed horum alii aliis succedebant, 1. Reg. 5. vers. 13.

## 8:10
Verse 10. WHO WERE INSTRUCTING. In the Hebrew, they were ruling, or were set over the people.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QUI ERUDIEBANT. In Ebr. dominabantur, vel præerant populo.

## 8:11
Verse 11. MY WIFE SHALL NOT DWELL IN THE HOUSE OF DAVID KING OF ISRAEL, BECAUSE IT IS SANCTIFIED: FOR THE ARK OF THE LORD HATH COME INTO IT) The sense is; the palace is too narrow to contain the King's family and the Queen's, but that which lies adjacent alone, that must be kept pure out of reverence for the Ark carried therein.

For women are accustomed to suffer from menstrual periods, by which they were barred from entering the temple, until they were cleansed.

Latin:

Vers. 11. NON HABITABIT VXOR MEA IN DOMO DA- VID REGIS ISRAEL, EO QVOD SANCTIFICATA SIT: QVIA INGRESSA EST IN EAM ARCA DO- MINI) Sensus est; regia angustior est, quam ut Regis fami- liam & Reginæ capiat, quod autem soli adjacet, id ob reve- rentiam Arcæ isthac portatæ purum servari debet.

Solent enim mulieres menstruis laborare, quæ ingressu templi arcebantur, donec mundarentur.

## 8:13
ACCORDING TO THE COMMANDMENT OF MOSES) The king is the guardian of the law.

Latin:

Vers. 13. JVXTA PRÆCEPTVM MOSIS) Rex legis custos.

## 8:14
DAVID THE MAN OF GOD) Most acceptable to God both in other matters and especially in this one, 1 Sam. 13:14, Nehem. 12:14, Acts 7:46, 13:22.

Latin:

Vers. 14. DAVID HOMO DEI) Deo tum in rebus aliis, tum in hac præcipue acceptissimus, 1. Sam. 13, 14. Nehem. 12, 14. Act. 7, 46. 13, 22.

## 8:15
AND THEY DID NOT DEVIATE FROM THE COMMANDMENTS OF THE KING, BOTH THE PRIESTS AND THE LEVITES) It is a part of royal care to ensure that the priests also perform their duty.

Latin:

Vers. 15. NEC PRÆTERGRESSI SVNT DE MANDATIS REGIS TAM SACERDOTES QVAM LEVITÆ) Regiæ curæ pars est efficere, ut & Sacerdotes suum faciant officium.

## 8:16
HE HAD ALL THE EXPENSES PREPARED. It is held otherwise in the Hebrew: Solomon prepared all the work until the day of the foundation.

Latin:

Vers. 16. OMNES IMPENSAS PRÆPARATAS HABUIT. Aliter in Ebr. habetur, præparavit omne opus Salomo ad diem fundationis.

## 9:1 Argument
CHAPTER IX.

The Queen of Sheba comes to Solomon: His majesty and riches, ivory throne, chariots, and cavalry, death and burial.

Latin:

CAPUT IX.

Regina Saba venit ad Salomonem: Ejus majestas & divitiæ, solum eburneum, currus, & equitatus, mors & sepultura.

## 9:5
OF YOUR MIGHTY WORKS AND WISDOM) Which appeared also in that orderliness of domestic affairs.

In the Hebrew it is not 'of your mighty works,' but 'of your words,' that is, things pertaining to you, as also the Chaldean and the LXX rendered it, and Cornelius acknowledges.

Latin:

Vers. 5. DE VIRTVTIBVS ET SAPIENTIA TVA) Quæ in ista etiam domesticæ rei ἐνταξίᾳ apparebat.

In Ebræo non est de tuis virtutibus, sed de tuis verbis, id est, rebus, ad te spectantibus, uti etiam Chaldæus ac LXX. reddidere, & agnoscit Cornelius.

## 9:22
THEREFORE SOLOMON WAS MAGNIFIED ABOVE ALL THE KINGS OF THE EARTH FOR RICHES AND GLORY) Namely, of wisdom, as the corresponding passage explains, 1 Kings 10:23. It could be said to him: The gods gave you riches, and the art of enjoying them.

Latin:

Vers. 22. MAGNIFICATVS IGITVR EST SALOMON SVPER OMNES REGES TERRÆ PRÆ DIVITIIS ET GLORIA) Nempe sapientiæ, ut explicat locus huic respondens, 1. Reg. 10, 23. Poterat ei dici: Di tibi divitias dederunt, artemque fruendi.

## 9:25
FORTY THOUSAND HORSES IN STABLES) In the Hebrew: four thousand stalls for horses: namely, ten horses to each stall. See 1 Kings 4:26.

Latin:

Vers. 25. QVADRAGINTA MILLIA EQVORVM IN STABVLIS) In Hebræo: quater mille stabula equorum: nempe singula stabula equis denis. Vide 1. Reg. 4, 26.

## 9:26
HE ALSO EXERCISED POWER OVER ALL THE KINGS) The Greeks: he was the leader of all the kings. He was the arbiter of affairs.

Indeed, all those kings subjected themselves to his dominion and lived under his protection.

Latin:

Vers. 26. EXERCVIT ETIAM POTESTATEM SVPER CVNCTOS REGES) Græci: ἦν ἡγέμενος πάντων ϖ̃ βασιλέων. Rerum erat arbiter.

Imo omnes illi Reges dominio ipsius se subjecerunt, & sub ipsius præsidio degebant.

## 9:29
IN THE WORDS OF NATHAN THE PROPHET, AND IN THE BOOKS OF AHIJAH THE SHILONITE, AND ALSO IN THE VISION OF IDDO THE SEER) See above 1 Chron. 29, 29.

Latin:

IN VERBIS NATHAN PROPHETÆ, ET IN LIBRIS AHIÆ SILONITÆ, IN VISIONE QVOQVE ADDO VIDENTIS) Vide supra 1. Paral. 29, 29.

## 10:1 Argument
PART II. HISTORY OF THE KINGS OF JUDAH. SECTION I. UP TO ATHALIAH. CHAPTER X.

Rehoboam by his harshness turned the people away from him, with only the tribe of Judah and Benjamin adhering to him, while the others chose Jeroboam.

Latin:

PARS II. REGUM JUDÆ HISTORIA. SECTIO I. USQUE AD ATHALIAM. CAPUT X.

Roboam duritie sua populum a se avertit, sola tribu Juda & Benjamin ipsi adhærente, cæteris Jeroboamum eligentibus.

## 10:3
Ver. 3. AND THEY CALLED HIM. Osiander takes this as if the Israelites had already thought of appointing Jeroboam King: But they are said to have called him so that they might go with him to the King's son and present their demands to him. Osiander rightly notes the ingratitude of the people and their unjust complaint about the burdens under Solomon. For they lived under him in the greatest tranquility, liberty, happiness, and joy, 1 Kings 4.

Latin:

Vers. 3. VOCAVERUNTQUE EUM. Id sic accipit Osiander, ac si jam tum cogitassent Israelitæ Jeroboamum Regem constituere: Sed vocasse ipsum dicuntur, ut cum eo ad Regis Filium irent, ac sua postulata ipsi proponerent. Recte autem notat Osiander, populi ingratitudinem, & iniquam de oneribus sub Salomone querelam. Siquidem in summa tranquillitate, libertate, felicitate, atque lætitia sub eo vixerint, 1. Reg. 4.

## 10:15
Ver. 15. FOR IT WAS OF THE WILL OF GOD) In the Hebrew: this was brought about by God: namely, by hardening the heart. The Greeks: ἦν μεταστροφὴ παρὰ τꭥ Θεꭥ.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ERAT ENIM VOLVNTATIS DEI) In Hebræo: erat hoc effectum à Deo: nempe cor obdurando. Græci ἦν μεταστροφὴ παρὰ τꭥ Θεꭥ.

## 10:16
Ver. 16. BUT THE WHOLE PEOPLE, THE KING SAYING HARDER THINGS) In the Hebrew codices it is: the king not listening to them: some codices add וְאֵין before לוֹ that is, when the people saw that they were not heard by the King. Thus also 1 Kings 12, 16.

Latin:

Vers. 16. POPVLVS AVTEM VNIVERSVS REGE DVRIORA DICENTE) In Hebræis codicibus est: rege non audiente illos: quidam Codd. addunt וְאֵין ante לוֹ id est, cum videre populus se a Rege non audiri. Sic & 1. Reg. 12, 16.

## 11:1 Argument
CHAPTER XI.

Rehoboam, wishing to subjugate the ten tribes by arms, is forbidden by Shemaiah the Prophet. The Levites and many faithful from Israel adhere to him. His wives and children.

Of chosen or excellent warriors. And a hendiadys.

Latin:

CAPUT XI.

Roboam subjugare armis volens decem tribus prohibetur a Semaja Propheta. Ei adhærent Levitæ & fideles multi ex Israel. Uxores & liberi ejus.

Electorum vel præstantium bellatorum. Et hendyade.

## 11:5
Ver. 5.

HE BUILT FORTIFIED CITIES IN JUDAH] He fortified the border against the ten tribes.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ÆDIFICAVIT CIVITATES MVNITAS IN JVDA] Limitem munivit contra decem tribus.

## 11:11
Ver. 11.

AND STOREHOUSES FOR FOOD] Granaries, as is usually done in war.

Ver. 11.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

CIBORVMQVE HORREA] Apothecas, ut in bello fieri solet.

Vers. 11.

## 11:12
BUT ALSO IN EVERY CITY HE MADE AN ARMORY) From which he might arm the soldier. Note these three things necessary in suspicious times for preserving the kingdom.

Latin:

SED ET IN SINGVLIS VRBIBVS FECIT ARMAMENTARIVM) Vnde armaret militem. Nota tria hæc suspectis temporibus necessaria servando regno.

## 11:13
Ver. 13.

BUT THE PRIESTS AND THE LEVITES, WHO WERE IN ALL ISRAEL CAME TO HIM) Mindful of the promises made to David. Others who were exceptionally pious followed their example, below 16.

They preferred to be exiled from their homes than to follow the idolatry of Jeroboam.

Latin:

Vers. 13.

SACERDOTES AUTEM ET LEVITÆ, QVI ERANT IN VNIVERSO ISRAEL VENERVNT AD EVM) Memores promissorum Davidi factorum. Horum exemplum secuti & alii eximie pii, infra 16.

Exulare malebant sedibus suis, quam idololatriam Jeroboami sequi.

## 11:21
Ver. 21.

HE HAD TAKEN EIGHTEEN WIVES, AND SIXTY CONCUBINES) He exceeded the limit. See Deut. 17, 17.

Moreover, concubines were not harlots, but legitimate wives, though of an inferior rank, because they drew their origin from ignoble families.

Latin:

Vers. 21.

VXORES DECEM ET OCTO DVXERAT, CONCVBINAS AVTEM SEXAGINTA) Modum excessit. Vid. Deut. 17, 17.

Cæterum concubinæ non erant scorta, sed legitimæ uxores, inferioris tamen gradus, eo quod ex familiis ignobilibus originem ducerent.

## 11:22
Ver. 22.

AND HE APPOINTED ABIJAH THE SON OF MAACAH AS LEADER OVER ALL HIS BROTHERS. FOR HE THOUGHT TO MAKE HIM KING) Because the kingdom was owed to him as the firstborn (as below 21, 3), he therefore accustomed him to command, entrusting the highest affairs to him under himself.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

CONSTITVIT VERO IN CAPITE ABIAM FILIVM MOACHA DVCEM SVPER OMNES FRATRES SVOS. IPSVM ENIM REGEM FACERE COGITABAT) Quia ipsi ut primogenito regnum debebatur (ut infra 21, 3.) ideo eum assuefecit imperio, summam sub se rerum ei credens.

## 11:23
Ver. 23.

BECAUSE HE WAS WISER AND MORE POWERFUL THAN ALL HIS SONS, AND IN ALL THE BORDERS OF JUDAH AND BENJAMIN, AND IN ALL THE WALLED CITIES) Otherwise in the Hebrew: And he caused to instruct and scattered of all his sons in all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, in all the fortified cities: He did not want the younger sons to be together in one place, lest by chance they might start some faction, but he distributed them through various border towns, with masters and inspectors added.

AND HE PROVIDED THEM WITH ABUNDANT FOOD) He gave them 'Panagia', as the French say, by the example of Abraham 25, 8. which also Jehoshaphat is read to have followed 21, 3.

Latin:

Vers. 23.

QVIA SAPIENTIOR FVIT ET POTENTIOR SVPER OMNES FILIOS EJVS, ET IN CVNCTIS FINIBVS JVDÆ ET BENJAMIN, ET IN VNIVERSIS CIVITATIBVS MVRATIS) Aliter in Hebræo: Et erudire faciebat & dispergebat de omnibus filiis suis in cunctis terris Judæ & Benjamin, in omnibus urbibus munitis: Filios minores natu noluit una esse in uno loco, ne forte factionem aliquam inciperent, sed per varia oppida limitanea eos distribuit, additis magistris & inspectoribus.

PRÆBVITQVE EIS ESCAS PLVRIMAS) Dedit illis Panagia, ut loquuntur Galli, exemplo Abrahami 25, 8. quod & Josaphatus secutus legitur 21, 3.

## 12:1 Argument
CHAPTER XII.

Rehoboam, falling away from God, is despoiled and subjugated by Shishak, King of Egypt. Warned by Shemaiah, he is humbled, but relapses into sins. Upon his death, Abijah succeeds him.

Latin:

CAPUT XII.

Roboam a Deo desciscens a Sesak Rege Ægypti spoliatur, & subjugatur. Monitus a Semaja humiliatur, at relabitur in peccata. Mortuo succedit Abia.

## 12:2
Verse 2. SHISHAK KING OF EGYPT.

Sesostris according to Herodotus, and Diodorus in Josephus. They state the cause of the war was that Jeroboam, who had married a kinswoman or daughter of his in Egypt, incited him to invade the unwarlike and effeminate Rehoboam, so that he himself would not be invaded by him and despoiled of his new kingdom.

Latin:

Versus 2. SESAC REX ÆGYPTI.

Sesostris Herodoto, & Diodoro apud Josephum. Causam belli dicunt, quod Jeroboam, qui in Ægypto cognatam, vel filiam ejus duxerat, ipsum excitavit, ut imbellem, & mulierosum Roboamum invaderet, ne ipse ab eo invaderetur, & regno novo spoliaretur.

## 12:3
Ver. 3.

AND THE TROGLODYTES) סֻכִּיִּים in the Hebrew, whom Ptolemy, rendering word for word, called 'skenitas'. According to Pliny, there is a town of Suchae in these regions.

They are peoples of Ethiopia, which lies adjacent to Egypt, about whom Mela 1, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

ET TROGLODYTÆ) סֻכִּיִּים in Hebr. quos σκηνίτας verbum verbo reddens dixit Ptolemæus. Apud Plinium in his locis est oppidum Suchæ.

Populi sunt Æthiopiæ, quæ Ægypto adjacet, de quibus Mela l, 1.

## 12:7
Ver. 7.

BECAUSE THEY ARE HUMBLED, I WILL NOT DESTROY THEM) See a similar passage in 1 Kings 21, 29.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

QVIA HVMILIATI SVNT, NON DISPERDAM EOS) Simile vide 1. Reg. 21, 29.

## 12:8
Ver. 8.

(THAT THEY MAY KNOW THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN MY SERVICE, AND THE SERVICE OF THE KINGDOMS OF THE COUNTRIES) We learn from this that punishment is not always removed, but often only mitigated, for those who acknowledge their guilt: furthermore, that there is less evil in servitude than in destruction: concerning which matter we have treated in the second book of De Jure Belli ac Pacis 24, 6. And that this punishment is imposed upon those who are unwilling to serve God, that they may serve harsh Kings.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

VT SCIANT DISTANTIAM SERVITVTIS MEÆ, ET SERVITVTIS REGNI TERRARVM) Discimus hinc pœnam non semper tolli, sed sæpe minui tantum, culpam agnoscentibus: deinde in servitute minus mali esse quam in internecione: qua de re egimus libro secundo de Jure Belli ac Pacis 24, 6. Et Deo servire nolentibus hanc pœnam imponi ut duris Regibus serviant.

## 12:15
Verse 15.

AND OF ADDO THE SEER AND DILIGENTLY SET FORTH] In the Hebrew it is, while he reviews the lineage: he had inscribed his book Addo as a genealogy, and to each of those whose names he was reviewing, he had added a summary of the deeds performed by them. What is found here התיחש, the Greeks translate as to keep a genealogy, 1 Chron. 5:1, 7:40, 9:1, Ezra 2:16.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

ET ADDO VIDENTIS ET DILIGENTER EXPO- SITA] In Hebræo est, dum genus recenset : Librum suum Addo inscripserat γενεαλογίαν, & singulis quorum nomina re- censebat,addiderat rerum gestarum ab ipsis breviarium. Quod hîc reperitur התיחש, id γενεαλογεῖν vertunt Græci 1. Paral. 5,1. 7, 40. 9, 1. Esdræ 2, 16.

## 13:1 Argument
CHAP. XIII. War is brought upon Abijah by Jeroboam. He slaughters the Israelites. Abijah's wives and children.

Latin:

CAP. XIII. Abiæ bellum infertur a Jeroboam. Ille cædit Israelitas. Abiæ uxores & liberi.

## 13:2
Verse 2.

MICHAIAH] In the Hebrew: מיכיהו : but it is credible that it was once written מעכה, as it is above and in the books of Kings. The same is called the mother of Asa in 1 Kings 15:10, where mother signifies grandmother.

It is still a doubt whether she was the same as Maacah the mother of Abijah, and grandmother of Asa: or whether she was his younger sister, as Cajetan wishes, so that she could be taken in marriage by Asa the son of Abijah? Nor is it new for two or more names to be attributed to one person in the Scriptures, or for the names of persons to vary slightly by a few letters. Examples are available everywhere. There is no need, therefore, for a corruption of the Scripture to be admitted.

DAUGHTER OF URIEL] To whom there is another name Absalom: above 11:19, 20, 1 Kings 15:2.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

MICHAIA] In Hebræo: מיכיהו : sed credibile est olim scriptum fuisse מעכה, quomodo est supra & in libris Re- gum. Eadem Asæ mater dicitur 1. Reg. 15, 10. ubi mater significat aviam.

Dubium adhuc est, an eadem fuerit cum Maa- cha matre Abiæ, & Avia Asæ: an vero fuerit e- jus Soror junior, uti vult Cajetanus, ut posset duci ab Asa filio Abiæ? Neque novum est, uni personæ tri- bui bina vel plura nomina in Scripturis, aut nomina personarum parum variare aliquibus literis. E- xempla passim prostant. Non ergo opus est, ut corruptela Scripturæ admittatur.

FILIA VRIEL] Cui alterum nomen Absalom : supra 11, 19. 20. 1. Reg. 15, 2.

## 13:3
Verse 3.

AND WHEN ABIJAH HAD ENTERED INTO BATTLE] That is, he had entered hostile borders with a hostile army, as appears from what follows.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

CVMQVE INIISSET ABIA CERTAMEN] Id est, in- festo exercitu ingressus esset fines hostiles, ut ex sequentibus apparet.

## 13:4
Verse 4.

WHO SAITH: HEAR O JEROBOAM AND ALL ISRAEL] This speech was made aptly both to terrify the enemies and to exhort his own men. For Abijah shows that the legitimate succession is on his side, and the sacred rites and priests are with him. Abijah was not religious, as appears in 1 Kings 15:3, but he uses the veil of religion, as many Kings do.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

QVI AIT: AVDI JEROBOAM ET OMNIS ISRA- EL] Oratio hæc appositè facta & ad terrendos hostes,& ad suos cohortandos. Ostendit enim Abia pro se esse succesio- nem legitimam, sacra & sacerdotes apud se. Non erat Abia religiosus, ut apparet 1. Reg. 15, 3. sed religionis velo uti notat, ut multi Reges.

## 13:8
Verse 8.

AND HAVING A GREAT MULTITUDE AND GOLDEN CALVES, WHICH JEROBOAM MADE FOR YOU AS GODS] That latter ו, which the Latin here translates as 'and', can more correctly be translated by an adversative. Your crowd is indeed great: but you have images against the law, on account of which God is angry with you. See Judith 5, 18. 19. This was the foundation of the counsel which Balaam gave.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

HABENSQVE GRANDEM MVLTITVDINEM AT- QVE VITVLOS AVREOS, QVOS FECIT VOBIS JE- ROBOAM IN DEOS] Illud posterius ו, quod Latinus hic vertit atque rectius verti per adversativam potest. Ma- gna quidem vestra est turba: sed habetis imagines contra le- gem, propter quas Deus vobis irascitur. Vide Judith 5, 18. 19. Hoc erat fundamentum consilii, quod dedit Balaamus.

## 13:13
Verse 13.

HE WAS SURROUNDING THE UNAWARE JUDAH WITH HIS ARMY] For those who are superior in number are accustomed to act in such a way as to enclose the enemy on all sides. Consider the following words. See an example in Frontinus, book 2, chapter 3, number 16; in Tacitus, Annals 2, where there is a discussion about Cariovalda. Hunters in their war against wild beasts call this an 'indago' (encirclement).

Latin:

Vers. 13.

IGNORANTEM JVDAM SVO AMBIEBAT EXER- CITV] Nam qui numero præpollent id agere solent, ut ho- stem undique includant. Confidera verba sequentia. Exem- plum vide apud Frontinum 2. cap. 3. num. 16. apud Tacitum Annal. 2. ubi de Cariovalda sermo. Venatores in suo adver- sus feras bello indaginem id vocant.

## 13:18
Verse 18.

AND THE SONS OF JUDAH WERE MOST STRONGLY STRENGTHENED, BECAUSE THEY HAD HOPED IN THE LORD GOD OF THEIR FATHERS] This people was better than the King: often God spares the people on account of the King: often also the King on account of the people.

Latin:

Vers. 18.

ET VEHEMENTISSIME CONFORTATI FILII JV- DA, EO QVOD SPERASSENT IN DOMINO DEO PATRVM SVORVM] Erat hic populus melior Rege : sæpe Deus populo parcit ob Regem: sæpe & Regi ob populum.

## 14:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIV. Asa, succeeding his father Abijah, exterminates idolatry, establishes the polity well, fortifies cities, exercises his subjects in the art of warfare, and Zara, King of the Ethiopians, who brings war against him, is routed.

Latin:

CAPUT XIV. Abiæ succedens filius Assa idololatriam extermi- nat, Politiam bene constituit, urbes munit, subditos in arte militandi exercet,cui bellum inferens Zara Ethiopum Rex profligatur.

## 14:5
Verse 5.

AND HE REMOVED FROM ALL THE CITIES OF JUDAH THE ALTARS AND SHRINES, AND HE REIGNED IN PEACE] He removed them from public places. From private places later below 15, 8. Thus also Christian Emperors purged the world of paganism through certain degrees.

Others say that Asa removed the high places sacred to idols, but not likewise the high places dedicated to the true God, 1 Kings 15, 14. Temples also built by Solomon remained until the times of Josiah, 2 Kings 23, 13.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ET ABSTVLIT DE CVNCTIS VRBIBVS JVDA ARAS ET FANA, ET REGNAVIT IN PACE] Abstu- lit ex locis publicis. Ex locis privatis postea infra 15, 8. Sic & Christiani Imperatores orbem paganismo purgarunt per gradus quosdam.

Alii excelsa idolis sacra abstulisse Asam dicunt, non item excelsa Deo vero dicata 1.Reg. 15,14. Tem- pla etiam a Salomone extructa maniere usque ad Josiæ tempora 2. Reg. 23,13.

## 14:7
Verse 7.

AND HE SAID TO JUDAH: LET US BUILD THESE CITIES AND WALL THEM WITH WALLS AND STRENGTHEN THEM WITH TOWERS AND GATES AND BARS, UNTIL ALL THINGS ARE QUIET FROM WAR] In time of peace, one must think about war.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

DIXIT AVTEM JVDÆ: ÆDIFICEMVS CIVITA- TES ISTAS ET VALLEMVS MVRIS ET ROBO- REMVS TVRRIBVS ET PORTIS ET SERIS, DONEC A BELLO QVIETA SINT OMNIA] Tempore pacis de bello cogitandum est.

## 14:9
Verse 9.

ZARA THE ETHIOPIAN] The Ethiopians, strong in number of men, often came by warring as far as the Syrian sea, as Cepheus once did.

Torniellus understands Midianite [land] here by Ethiopia: But others more correctly [understand] true Ethiopia, which is under Egypt c. 16, 8, and near to Judea.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ZARA ÆTHIOPS] Æthiopes, numero hominum vali- di, sæpe ad mare usque Syriacum bellando venere, ut olim Cepheus.

Torniellus per Æthiopiam hic Madianitidem intelligit: Sed rectius alii veram Æthiopiam, quæ sub Ægypto est c. 16, 8. & Judææ vicina.

## 14:11
Verse 11.

LORD, THERE IS NO DIFFERENCE WITH THEE, WHETHER THOU HELP WITH FEW OR WITH MANY] The same sentiment [is in] 1 Sam. 14, 6. See what we have said there.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

DOMINE NON EST APUD TE ULLA DISTAN- TIA, UTRUM IN PAUCIS AUXILIERIS AN IN PLURIBUS] Eadem sententia 1. Sam. 14, 6. Vide quæ ibi diximus.

## 14:12
Verse 12. THEY TOOK THEREFORE MUCH SPOIL] Namely from the slain: for the Hebrew word here is שָׁלָל, whence σκῦλα to the Greeks, with the same meaning.

Latin:

Vers. 12. TULERUNT ERGO SPOLIA MULTA] Nempe de interfectis: nam Hebræa vox hic est שָׁלָל, un- de σκῦλα Græcis, eodem significatu.

## 14:14
Verse 14.

AND THEY CARRIED AWAY MUCH PREY] Prey here in the Hebrew is בִּזָּה: the more elegant Greeks would call it λάφυρα: but our interpreters often translate it διαρπαγὴν, and often προνομὴν: of which the former is accustomed to be said of cities, the latter of fields.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

ET MULTAM PRÆDAM ASPORTAVERUNT] Præda hic in Hebræo בִּזָּה: id Græci elegantiores dicerent λάφυρα: sed nostri interpretes sæpe διαρπαγὴν vertunt, sæpe & προνομὴν: quorum illud de urbibus, hoc de agris dici solet.

## 14:15
Verse 15.

BUT ALSO DESTROYING THE SHEEPFOLDS] אָהֳלֵי מִקְנֶה which the Greeks retained as ἀλιμαζονῆς, signifies the tents of the herdsmen, that is, of the Scenite Arabs, who were allied with the Scenite Ethiopians.

Latin:

Vers. 15.

SED ET CAULAS OVIUM DESTRUENTES] אָהֳלֵי מִקְנֶה quod retinuere Græci ἀλιμαζονῆς, signifi- cat tentoria pecuariorum, id est, Arabum Scenitarum, qui fœ- derati Æthiopibus Scenitis.

## 15:1 Argument
CHAPTER XV.

Azariah exhorts that they continue in true piety, whence Asa uproots idols completely.

Verse 1.

AZARIAH ALSO THE SON OF ODED) Called also himself, like his father, Oded, as appears below in verse 8 in the Hebrew: but distinguished from him by the other name Azariah.

Latin:

CAPUT XV.

Azarias hortatur, ut in vera pietate pergant, unde Asa idola extirpat funditus.

Vers. 1.

AZARIAS AUTEM FILIUS ODED) Vocatus & ipse, ut pater, Oded, ut apparet infra 8. in Hebræo: sed ab eo di- stinctus altero Azariæ nomine.

## 15:2
Ver. 2.

THE LORD IS WITH YOU, BECAUSE YOU HAVE BEEN WITH HIM] In the Hebrew: while you have been with him. The Greeks: ἐν τῷ εἶναι ὑμᾶς μετ' ἀυτῦ. Very well indeed: nor does that of Sallust depart far: For it is established to me as true, that the life of all mortals is watched over by divine power: and that neither the good nor the evil deed of anyone is held for nothing, but that according to their different nature rewards follow the good and the bad.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

DOMINUS VOBISCUM, QUIA FUISTIS CUM EO] In Hebræo: dum vos fuistis cum eo. Græci: ἐν τῷ εἶναι ὑμᾶς μετ' ἀυτῦ. Bene admodum: nec longe abit illud Sallustii: Nam- que mihi pro vero constat, omnium mortalium vitam divino nu- mine invisi: neque bonum neque malum facinus cujusquam pro nihilo haberi, sed ex natura diversa præmia bonos malosq; sequi.

## 15:3
Ver. 3.

BUT MANY DAYS SHALL PASS IN ISRAEL] In the Hebrew that word 'shall pass' is not there: whence you might more correctly supply what is missing: 'there were'. In Israel: that is, in the ten tribes. They were, under Jeroboam.

WITHOUT THE TRUE GOD) Without true piety toward God.

WITHOUT A PRIEST TEACHER) For all the priests had joined themselves to the tribe of Judah.

AND WITHOUT LAW) For the ten tribes, along with many other things against the law, also had Teraphim.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

TRANSIBUNT AUTEM MULTI DIES IN ISRAE- LE] In Hebræo non est illud transibunt: unde rectius quod deest impleas perfuerunt. In Israele: id est, in decem tribu- bus. Fuerunt, sub Jeroboamo.

ABSQUE DEO VERO) Absque vera pietate in Deum.

ABSQUE SACERDOTE DOCTORE) Nam Sacerdo- tes omnes tribui Judæ se adjunxerant.

ET ABSQUE LEGE) Nam decem tribus cum multa alia contra legem, tum & Theraphim habebant.

## 15:4
Ver. 4.

AND WHEN THEY SHALL HAVE RETURNED IN THEIR DISTRESS TO THE LORD) More correctly: if they had returned, for indeed that did not happen.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

CUMQUE REVERSI FUERINT IN ANGUSTIA SUA AD DOMINUM) Rectius: si conversus fuisset, neque enim id evenit.

## 15:5
Ver. 5. IN THAT TIME) At this time, as long as they despise God.

THERE SHALL BE NO PEACE TO HIM THAT GOETH OUT AND COMETH IN, BUT TERRORS ON EVERY SIDE AMONG ALL THE INHABITANTS OF THE LANDS) Nowhere shall there be a safe dwelling: so infested shall all things be, not only by external wars, but also by internal discords. See this prophecy fulfilled in 1 Kings 15, 16, and 20; 2 Kings 9, 10, and 15.

Latin:

Vers. 5. IN TEMPORE ILLO) Hoc tempore, quam- diu Deum aspernantur.

NON ERIT PAX INGREDIENTI ET EGREDI- ENTI, SED TERRORES UNDIQUE IN CUNCTIS HABITATORIBUS TERRARUM) Nusquam tuta erit se- des: ita infesta erunt omnia non externis tantum bellis, sed & internis discordiis. Impletum hoc vaticinium vide 1. Reg. 15. 16. & 20. 2. Reg. 9. 10. & 15.

## 15:6
Verse 6.

FOR NATION SHALL FIGHT AGAINST NATION) Understand nation as tribe. And see what is said in Matthew 24.

AND CITY AGAINST CITY) It could not be but that this would happen, where there was no certain succession of the kingdom, but whoever killed the King hoped for the kingdom, often not without an adversary, such as the times in Rome before Vespasian.

BECAUSE THE LORD SHALL TROUBLE THEM IN EVERY STRAIT) He will set them against one another with much blood and all the evils that are accustomed to accompany civil wars.

YOU THEREFORE] You from the tribe of Judah and Benjamin with the Priests and Levites.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

PUGNABIT ENIM GENS CONTRA GENTEM) Gentem intellige tribum. Et vide quæ dicta Matth. 24.

ET CIVITAS CONTRA CIVITATEM) Fieri non poterat quin id eveniret, ubi nulla certa erat regni successio, sed quisquis Regem occidisset regnum sperabat, sæpe non sine adversario, qualia Romæ tempora ante Vespasianum.

QUIA DOMINUS CONTVRBABIT EOS IN OMNI ANGUSTIA) Committet eos inter se multojcum sanguine ac malis omnibus, quæ bella civilia comitari solent.

VOS ERGO] Vos ex tribu Judæ & Benjaminis cum Sa- cerdotibus & Levitis.

## 15:7
BE STRENGTHENED] Take courage. You have to deal with men hateful to God.

AND LET NOT YOUR HANDS BE WEAKENED] Do not be sluggish.

FOR THERE IS A REWARD FOR YOUR WORK] Great will be the rewards of your warfare against them: if indeed you worship God according to the law.

Latin:

CONFORTAMINI] Animos sumite. Res vobis est cum hominibus Deo exosis.

ET NON DISSOLVANTUR MANUS VESTRÆ] Ne pigramini.

EST ENIM MERCES OPERI VESTRO] Magna erunt militiæ in illos vestræ præmia: si nempe Deum colatis ex lege.

## 15:8
Verse 8. HE TOOK AWAY THE IDOLS] See above 14, 5.

HE DEDICATED THE ALTAR, WHICH WAS BEFORE THE PORCH OF THE LORD) In Hebrew for porch is אולם, whence the Latin aula (hall). It is properly called so, because it is enclosed by four porticoes, as Servius says on the third book of the Aeneid. The altar of holocausts was in the first part of the open-air space or hall for the priests coming from the basilica.

FROM THE CITIES, WHICH HE HAD TAKEN OF MOUNT EPHRAIM) Cities belonging to the tribe of Benjamin by the King Asa had recovered those of the ten tribes captured in war: see above 13, 19. And he brought them back to the observance of the law, as was right. Ver. 11. THEY SACRIFICED TO THE LORD ON THAT DAY FROM THE SPOILS AND BOOTY WHICH THEY HAD BROUGHT. There are not two words in Hebrew, but one שָׁלָל, which elsewhere, as we have said, is σκῦλα: but here by a certain catachresis it signifies τ λεĩαν. Ver. 13. BUT IF ANYONE SHALL NOT HAVE SOUGHT THE LORD GOD OF ISRAEL, LET HIM DIE] If anyone shall have worshipped other gods, either publicly or privately, let him die, according to the law of Deut. 17, 2. Ver. 16. HE REMOVED HER SO THAT SHE MIGHT NOT BE LADY] So that she might not obtain the honor of Augusta. See what was said at 1 Kings 15, 13. BUT THE HIGH PLACES WERE LEFT IN ISRAEL] On private estates. NEVERTHELESS THE HEART OF ASA WAS PERFECT ALL HIS DAYS] Even the best Kings cannot immediately correct everything they disapprove of, as we have also indicated elsewhere: they are unequal to certain crimes, as Tacitus speaks. Ver. 19. THERE WAS NO WAR UNTIL THE THIRTY-FIFTH YEAR OF THE REIGN OF ASA) Because in the first book of Kings, chapter 15, 16, it is said that Asa and Baasha were at war with each other throughout their entire lives; therefore some read here the fifth year, omitting the note of the thirtieth.

Nor is there any need here for a suspicion of a corrupted text. The matter can be resolved otherwise: indeed, it must be. For Grotius has not shown a codex in which the fifth is read. The Hebrews, the LXX, and the Latins consistently read up to the 35th year. For this reason, most interpreters, both Hebrew and Christian—Torniellus, Salianus, Sanctius, Cornelius, Junius, likewise Piscator, Waltherus, and others—understand the year of the era of the kingdom of Judah, by which it is distinguished from the kingdom of Israel, which they count from the first year of Rehoboam, who then properly began the kingdom of Judah separated, while Jeroboam, the schism having been made, was establishing and governing the kingdom of Israel separately. Since therefore Rehoboam reigned for 17 years, and Abijah for three, the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa will be the thirty-fifth of the reign of Judah, or of the era of the Jewish kingdom. Here therefore it must be said that, even though there was war between Asa and Baasha throughout all the days of their reigns, nevertheless the first twelve years of Baasha, who began to reign in the third year of Asa, until the fifteenth year of Asa, seem to have been peace, with respect to the warlike storms and movements stirred up in the remaining time of his reign.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ABSTULIT IDOLA] Vide supra 14, 5.

DEDICAVIT ALTARE, QUOD ERAT ANTE PORTICUM DOMINI] In Hebræo pro porticus est אולם, unde Latinum aula. Sic autem proprie dicitur, quod concluditur, porticibus quatuor, ut Servius ait ad tertium Æneidos. Erat autem altare holocaustorum sacerdotibus ex basilica venientibus in parte prima subdialis sive aulæ.

EX VRBIBUS, QUAS CEPERAT MONTIS EPHRAIM) Urbes ad tribum Benjaminis pertinentes à Rege decem tribuum bello captas receperat Asa: supra 13, 19. E ad legis observationem reduxit, ut æquum erat. Vers. 11. IMMOLAVERUNT DOMINO IN DIE ILL DE MANVBIIS ET PRÆDA, QVAM ADDVXERANT Non sunt duæ voces in Hebræo, sed una שָׁלָל, quæ alib ut diximus, σκῦλα: at hic per κατάχρησιν quandam τ λεĩαν significat. Vers. 13. SI QVIS AVTEM NON QVÆSIERIT DOMINVM DEVM ISRAEL, MORIATVR] Si quis aut publice au privatim Deos coluerit alios, moriatur, ex lege Deut. 17, 2. Vers. 16. AMOVIT NE ESSET DOMINA] Ne hono rem Augustæ obtineret. Vide quæ dicta 1. Reg. 15,13. EXCELSA AVTEM DERELICTA SVNT IN ISRA EL] In fundis privatis. ATTAMEN COR ASA ERAT PERFECTVM CVNCTIS DIEBVS EJVS] Etiam optimi Reges non sta tim omnia,quæ improbant, corrigere possunt,ut alibi quoqu indicavimus: sunt quibusdam flagitiis impares, ut Tacitu loquitur. Vers. 19. BELLVM NON FVIT VSQVE AD TRIGE SIMVM QVINTVM ANNVM REGNI ASA) Quia li bro primo Regum cap. 15, 16. dicuntur toto vitæ suæ tem pore inter se bellasse Asa, & Bahasa; Ideo quidam hic le gunt quintum annum, omissa tricesimi nota.

NEque hic opus est suspicione corrupti textus Aliter res expediri potest: imo debet. Nec enim monstravit Grotius Codicem, quo legatur quintus. Hebræi, LXX. Latini constanter legunt usque ad 35. annum. Quapropter Interpp. plerique Ebræi & Christiani Torniellus, Salianus, Sanctius, Cornelius, Junius item, Piscator, Waltherus & alii in telligunt annum æræ regni Judæ, qua id ab Israelis re gno distinguitur, quam numerant inde a primo Ro boami anno, qui tunc proprie cœpit regnum Judæ separatum, Jeroboamo regnum Israelis, facto schi smate, seorsim instituente ac gubernante. Quum ergo Roboam 17. annis regnarit, Abia tribus, decimus quintus annus regni Asæ, trigesimus quintus erit re gni Judæ, vel æra Judaici regni. Hic ergo dicen dum, quod etsi cunctis diebus regni Asæ, & Baasæ, bellum inter ipsos fuerit, priores tamen duodecim annos Baasæ, qui tertio Asæ regnare cœpit, usque ad decimum quintum Asæ pax fuisse videatur, re spectu tempestatum bellicarum, & motuum, reli quo tempore regni ejus excitatorum.

## 16:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVI.

Asa, struck by the army of Baasha, King of Israel, hires Ben-hadad, King of Syria, with the treasures of the temple; he is rebuked by the Prophet Hanani, whom he imprisons. Suffering from his feet, he dies.

Ver. 1. BUT IN THE THIRTY-SIXTH YEAR OF HIS REIGN] Others think it should be read as the twentieth.

Who those are, and for what reason they read it so, Grotius does not teach. We do not deny, however, that some wish 26, others 16, to be read: and thus they argue that the modern codices are in error here, such as Thomas Cajetan, Johannes Lucidus, Johannes Annius, Adrichomius, and Canus, whom Cornelius a Lapide refutes, not undeservedly, by the consensus of the codices. All, he says, the Hebrew, Chaldean, Greek, and Latin codices consistently have 36, not 26. But to say that there is a mistake in all the codices is to say that there is a mistake in Holy Scripture, which God forbid. Which reasoning, as it is solid, so it also militates here against Grotius. But the doubt concerning Baasha having died in the 25th year of the reign of Asa, as is held in 1 Kings 16, 8, which Paludanus considers insoluble, is resolved if it is said that the years of the kingdom of Judah are being computed here: for thus the sixteenth year of the reign of Asa will be the thirty-sixth year indicated here of the kingdom of Judah, solitary, from the schism or division made under his grandfather Rehoboam. For the years of the Kings of Judah are counted sometimes from the beginning of the kingdom of Judah, sometimes from the beginning of the reign of each

King. Which explanation is approved by the Hebrews themselves in Seder Olam, by Cornelius a Lapide, Torniellus, Salianus, Azorius, Junius, Piscator, our Waltherus, and others.

Ver. same. HE WAS SURROUNDING RAMAH WITH A WALL] He made many fortifications around that city. See 1 Kings 15, 17.

Latin:

CAPUT XVI.

Asa perculsus exercitu Baasa Regis Israelis Ben- adad Regem Syriæ thesauris templi conducit, ab Hanani Propheta reprehenditur, quem incarcerat. Laborans ex pedibus moritur.

Vers. 1. ANNO AVTEM TRIGESIMO SEXTO REGNI EJVS] Alii legendum putant vicesimo.

QUinam illi sint, & ex qua causa ita legant, non docet Grotius. Non dissimulamus tamen, nonnullos 26. alios 16. annum legendum esse velle: adeoque erroris hic arguere Codices modernos, ut pote Thomam Cajetanum, Johannem Lucidum, Jo hannem Annium, Adrichomium & Canum, quos ve ro refellit non immerito Cornelius a Lapide, e con sensu Codicum. Omnes, inquit, Codices Hebræi, Chaldæi, Græci, Latini constanter habent 36. non 26. Atqui in omnibus codicibus esse mendum, est dicere in Scriptura Sacra esse mendum, quod absit. Quæ ra tio uti solida est, ita etiam adversus Grotium hic militat. Dubium autem de Baasa anno 25. regni Asæ mortuo, ut habetur 1. Reg. 16, 8. quod Paludanus pro insolubili habet, expeditur, fi dicatur, hic regni Judæ annos computari: Nam ita annus decimus sex tus regiminis Asæ annus erit trigesimus sextus hic in digitatus regni Judæ solitarii, inde a schismate vel scissione sub Roboamo avo ejus facta. Numeran tur enim quandoque Regum Judæ anni ab initio regni Judæ, quandoque ab initio regiminis cujusq;

Regis. Quæ explicatio probatur Ebræis ipsis, in Seder Olam, Cornelio a Lapide, Torniello, Saliano, A- zorio, Junio, Piscatori, Walthero nostro, & aliis.

Vers. eod. MURO CIRCUMDABAT RAMA] Muni- menta circa eam urbem multa fecit. Vide 1. Reg. 15,17.

## 16:7
Ver. 7.

BECAUSE YOU HAD CONFIDENCE IN THE KING OF SYRIA, AND NOT IN THE LORD YOUR GOD) Who, as God, had promised you victory over the Israelites through Azariah when you were acting rightly: above 15, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

QVIA FIDUCIAM HABUISTI IN REGE SYRIÆ, ET NON IN DOMINO DEO TUO) Qui Deus tibi recte agenti victoriam de Israëlitis per Azariam promiserat: supra 15, 7.

WERE NOT THE ETHIOPIANS AND LIBYANS MUCH MORE NUMEROUS?) Above 12.

Verse 10.

Vers. 10.

JUSSIT EUM MITTI IN NERVV M) Tanquam læsæ Majestatis reum, male: Prophetarum enim officium erat ca- stigare etiam Reges.

Verse 11.

THEY ARE WRITTEN IN THE BOOK OF THE KINGS OF JUDAH AND ISRAEL) Not in those books which we have, but in more extensive ones which the above-named Prophets had written, 12, 15.

Latin:

## 16:12
Verse 12.

AND NOT EVEN IN HIS INFIRMITY DID HE SEEK THE LORD, BUT RATHER RELIED ON THE ART OF PHYSICIANS) It is not criticized that he used the work of physicians, but that he did not approach God with serious repentance and prayer, without whom the help of physicians is worth nothing.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

ET NEC IN INFIRMITATE SUA QVÆSIVIT DO- MINUM, SED MAGIS MEDICORUM ARTE CON- FISUS EST) Non reprehenditur quod Medicorum usus sit opera, sed quod Deum seria pœnitentia ac prece non adierit, sine quo nihil valet medicorum auxilium.

## 16:14
Verse 14.

IN HIS SEPULCHRE, WHICH HE HAD DUG FOR HIMSELF IN THE CITY OF DAVID) In the cave, which he had made new for himself next to the monuments of other Kings.

AND WITH Harlot's OINTMENTS) He thought it was masculine for the feminine זְנוּנִים, but it is a Chaldean word, with only a Hebrew ending, and it signifies various kinds of anything, and is used for store Ps. 144, 13, for various singing Dan. 3, 5, and is placed for the Hebrew מִין among the Chaldean interpreters. Gen. 1, 11, 12. The Greeks here not badly γένη μύρων.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

IN SEPULCHRO SUO, QVOD FODERAT SIBI IN CIVITATE DAVID) In caverna, quam sibi novam juxta aliorum Regum monumenta fecerat.

ET UNGUENTIS MERETRICIIS) Putavit esse mascu- linum pro fœminino זְנוּנִים, sed est vox Chaldæa, termina- tione tantum Hebræa, significatque varia genera cujusque rei, usurpaturque de penu Ps. 144, 13. de cantu vario Dan. 3,5. & ponitur pro מִין Hebræo apud Chaldæos interpretes. Genes. 1, 11. 12. Græci hic non male γένη μύρων.

## 17:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVII.

King Jehoshaphat first instructs the people by sending out Teachers, to whom the Philistines and Arabians pay tribute. His soldiers and Leaders.

CAPUT XVII.

Josaphat Rex prius Doctoribus emissis populum informat, cui Philistæi & Arabes vectigales redduntur. Ejus milites & Duces.

## 17:2
Ver. 2.

AND HE APPOINTED THE NUMBERS OF THE SOLDIERS IN ALL THE CITIES OF JUDAH) He had great care for fortifying the border, both by increasing the garrisons, as here and below 19, and by building new fortifications below 12.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

CONSTITUITQVE MILITUM NUMEROS IN CUN- CTIS VRBIBVS JUDA) Magnam curam habuit muniendi limitis, tum augendo præsidia, ut hic & infra 19. tum nova munimenta exstruendo infra 12.

## 17:3
Ver. 3.

HE WALKED IN THE FIRST WAYS OF DAVID HIS FATHER] He was such as David was before he saw Bathsheba.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

AMBULAVIT IN VIIS DAVID PATRIS SUI PRI- MIS] Talis fuit, qualis David ante visam Bethsabcam.

## 17:5
Ver. 5.

AND ALL JUDAH GAVE GIFTS TO JEHOSHAPHAT] As was the custom in the East, especially at the beginning of a reign 1 Sam. 10, 27.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

ET DEDIT OMNIS JUDA MVNERA JOSAPHAT] Vt mos erat in Oriente, præsertim in regni auspiciis 1. Sam. 10,27.

## 17:6
Ver. 6. AND WHEN HIS HEART HAD TAKEN COURAGE BECAUSE OF THE WAYS OF THE LORD) He became bolder to compel the people into obedience to the law.

ALSO HE TOOK AWAY THE HIGH PLACES AND THE GROVES FROM JUDAH] He reads וְעוֹד, as the Hebrew Codices now have it. Learned men, however, think that וְלֹא was written here formerly, so that this history might agree with that which is in 1 Kings 22, 14 and below 20, 33, as if they were saying, not even this man, although much bolder than the others, dared to remove the high places from private locations.

Grotius attempts to bring not only the Hebrew Codices, but also the Vulgate version, into suspicion of corruption once again. However, he can show no trace of that corruption, which all the Codices refute, reading in the same way. Nor does the reasoning from the cited passages move us: there is no true ἀντιλογία here. For in this passage he is said to have removed the high places built for the sake of idols, and those consecrated to them. But in the other passages, 1 Kings 22:44 and 2 Chronicles 20:33, he is said not to have removed the high places, namely those which were dedicated to the God of Israel, even though they had been forbidden by Him. For he could not remove them without shaking the kingdom, because the people had not yet directed their heart to the Lord God of their fathers, as was fitting (2 Chronicles 20:33), nor could matters be brought by the most pious King to the point that sacrifices were offered only in the Jerusalem temple.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CVMQVE SVMSISSET COR EJVS AVDA- CIAM PROPTER VIAS DOMINI) Audentior factus est ad cogendam plebem in obsequium legis.

ETIAM EXCELSA ET LVCOS DE JVDA ABSTV- LIT] Legit וְעוֹד, ut nunc habent Hebræi Codices. Eru- diti tamen viri existimant, scriptum hic olim fuisse וְלֹא, ut conveniat hæc historia cum eo, quod est 1. Reg. 22, 14. & in- fra 20, 33. quasi dicant, ne hic quidem, quamquam multo cæ- teris audentior, ausus est amovere excelsa e locis privatis.

Iterum in suspicionem depravationis non E- bræos tantum Codices, sed vulgatæ etiam versio- nis conatur perducere Grotius. Nullum autem vestigium depravationis istius monstrare potest: quam refellunt omnes Codices, eodem modo legen- tes. Neque ratio e locis allegatis nos movet: Nulla vera hic ἀντιλογία. Abstulisse enim hoc loco di- citur excelsa in Idolorum gratiam exstructa, illisque consecranea. In cæteris vero locis 1. Reg. 22, 44. 2. Par. 20, 33. excelsa non abstulisse dicitur: ea scil. quæ Deo Israelis dicata erant: etsi ab eo vetita fuerint. Non enim absque concussione regni ea tollere po- tuit. Quia populus non direxerat adhuc cor suum ad Dominum Deum Patrum suorum, ut par erat: 2. Par. 20,33. nec eo perduci res poterat a Rege pien- tissimo, ut in solo templo Hierosolymitano sacrifi- caie offerentur.

## 17:7
Verse 7.

HE SENT OF HIS PRINCES BENHAIL AND OBADIAH AND ZECHARIAH AND NATHANAEL AND MICHAIAH, TO TEACH IN THE CITIES OF JUDAH] To teach and explain the law was not only the duty of the Priests and Levites, whose mention will follow, but of all learned men, which is also observed among the Jews even now. But those who were of the King's council had to be most expert in the laws.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

MISIT DE PRINCIPIBVS SVIS BENHAIL ET OB- DIAM ET ZACHARIAM ET NATHANAEL ET MI- CHEAM, VT DOCERENT IN CIVITATIBVS JVDA] Docere & explicare legem non tantum Sacerdotum erat & Levitarum, quorum sequetur mentio, sed omnium erudito- rum, quod & nunc observatur apud Judæos. Peritissimi au- tem legum esse debebant, qui Regi a consiliis erant.

Verse 9.

HAVING THE BOOK OF THE LAW OF THE LORD] Which they interpreted to the people. Neh. 8, 9.

Latin:

HABENTES LIBRVM LEGIS DOMINI] Quem in- terpretabantur populo. Nehem. 8, 9.

## 18:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVIII.

Jehoshaphat goes to battle with the impious Ahab, in which Ahab perishes, Jehoshaphat barely escapes the danger of his life.

For he took his daughter for his son Joram as a wife 2 Chron. 21, through whom idolatry was brought into Judah, and many evils. The pious Jehoshaphat sinned not lightly in this: to which was added afterwards a joining of arms with an idolatrous King.

Latin:

CAPUT XVIII.

Josaphat cum impio Achabo ad prælium pergit, in quo Achab perit, Josaphat vix periculum vitæ evadit.

Vers. 1. AFFINITATE CONJUNCTUS ACHAB.

EJus enim filiam accepit filio suo Joram in uxo- rem 2. Par. 21. per quam idololatria in Judæam invecta, & multa mala. Peccavit in eo pius Josa- phat non leviter: cui accessit postmodum conjun- ctio armorum cum Rege idololatra.

## 18:3
Verse 3.

AS I AM AND THOU ART: AS THY PEOPLE, SO ALSO MY PEOPLE: AND WE WILL BE WITH THEE IN THE WAR] Against the commandment of God through Azariah: above 15. Therefore he is deservedly rebuked below 19, 2. and 20, 37.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

VT EGO ET TV: SICVT POPVLVS TVVS, SIC ET POPVLVS MEVS: TECVMQVE ERIMVS IN BELLO] Contra præceptum Dei per Azariam: supra 15. Ideo merito reprehenditur infra 19, 2. & 20, 37.

Verse 25. THE SON OF HAMELECH.

So the Vulgate. But wrongly: For it is an appellative: The King's son, which Cornelius and others acknowledge.

Latin:

Vers. 25. FILIUM HAMELECH.

Ver. 4.

AS FAR AS MOUNT EPHRAIM] To the cities which Asa had taken in war, see above 15, 8.

Vers. 4.

VSQVE AD MONTEM EPHRAIM] Ad urbes quas Asa bello ceperat, supra 15, 8.

## 19:5
Ver. 5.

AND HE APPOINTED JUDGES OF THE LAND IN ALL THE FORTIFIED CITIES OF JUDAH, CITY BY CITY] That is, in the cities either newly built or acquired in war, he caused there to be judges who would take cognizance of civil and capital cases, with no exceptions.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

CONSTITVITQVE JVDICES TERRÆ IN CVN- CTIS CIVITATIBVS JVDA MVNITIS PER SINGV- LA LOCA] Id est, in urbibus aut noviter structis, aut bel- lo acquisitis, effecit,ut essent judices 23. qui de causis civilibus & capitalibus, non exceptis, cognoscerent.

Ver. 6.

FOR THE JUDGMENT IS NOT OF MAN, BUT OF THE LORD] Deut. 1, 17.

It would be fitting for such sentences to be inscribed on the walls of all courts and in the hearts of all judges, as Osiander warns here.

Vers. 6.

NON ENIM HOMINIS EXERCETVR JVDICIVM, SED DOMINI] Deut. 1, 17.

TAles sententias omnium Curiarum parietibus, & omnium Judicum cordibus inscriptas esse conveniret, monente hic Osiandro.

## 19:8
Ver. 8.

IN JERUSALEM ALSO JEHOSHAPHAT APPOINTED LEVITES AND PRIESTS AND HEADS OF FAMILIES FROM ISRAEL] Since the number had fallen to a few, with co-optation having been omitted for fear of the kings, to whom the authority of the Sanhedrin was suspect (concerning which see what is to be said below 21, 4), he ordered the number to be filled in the legitimate manner, partly from the Priests and Levites (who, because they were free from other labors, were most suited for the study of the law) and partly from the learned men of the other tribes. See by all means what we have said at Deut. 17.

In Jerusalem he seems to have established the supreme court of appeals, as they call it.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

IN JERVSALEM QVOQVE CONSTITVIT JOSA- PHAT LEVITAS ET SACERDOTES ET PRINCIPES FAMILIARVM EX ISRAEL] Cum numerus ad paucos re- cidisset,omissa cooptatione metu Regum, quibus suspecta erat Synedrii auctoritas (de quo vid. dicenda infra 21, 4.) more le- gitimo impleri numerum jussit,partim ex Sacerdotibus & Le- vitis (qui quod ab aliis laboribus vacarent, legis studio erant aptissimi) partim ex eruditis aliarum tribuum. Vide omnino quæ diximus ad Deut. 17.

In Jerusalem videtur constituisse summum appellationum, ut vocant, judicium.

## 19:10
Verse 10.

EVERY CAUSE WHICH SHALL COME TO YOU OF YOUR BRETHREN) For those town judges used to make a referral to the Sanhedrin in more difficult cases, both because there were more learned men there, and so that there would not be varying judgments on similar matters, and discord arise from that.

BETWEEN THOUGHT AND KINSHIP] Where it is asked who ought to succeed a dead person.

WHEREVER THERE IS A QUESTION CONCERNING THE LAW] He puts the name of the genus first, intending to subject the species thereafter.

CONCERNING THE COMMANDMENT] Concerning those precepts which have an evident honesty in themselves: for that is מצור.

CONCERNING CEREMONIES] Concerning positive precepts pertaining to rites.

CONCERNING JUSTIFICATIONS] Concerning precepts which pertain to the manner of exercising judgments.

SHOW THEM] Teach them what they ought to do.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

OMNEM CAVSAM QVÆ VENERIT AD VOS FRATRVM VESTRORVM) Nam oppidani isti judices in causis difficilioribus relationem faciebant ad Synedrium, tum quod ibi essent homines doctiores,tum ne super paribus rebus varie judicaretur, & inde nascerentur discordiæ.

INTER COGITATIONEM ET COGNATIONEM] Vbi quæritur quis mortuo succedere debeat.

VBICVNQVE QVÆSTIO EST DE LEGE] Præmittit nomen generis, subjecturus deinde species.

DE MANDATO] De iis præceptis quæ evidentem in se honestatem habent : id enim מצור.

DE CEREMONIIS] De præceptis positivis ad ritus perti- nentibus.

DE JVSTIFICATIONIBVS] De præceptis quæ ad mo- dum exercendorum judiciorum pertinent.

OSTENDITE EIS ] Docete eos quid facere debeant.

## 19:11
Verse 11.

BUT AMARIAH THE PRIEST AND YOUR HIGH PRIEST SHALL PRESIDE IN THOSE THINGS WHICH PERTAIN TO GOD] In the Hebrew: Amariah the Priest is head over you in every word of the Lord. This Amariah had been at that time נשיא, that is, prince of the Sanhedrin. It was his duty to lead the others with his opinion in all those things which were defined by the law of God.

FURTHERMORE ZEBADIAH THE SON OF ISHMAEL, WHO IS THE LEADER IN THE HOUSE OF JUDAH, SHALL BE OVER THOSE WORKS WHICH PERTAIN TO THE KING'S OFFICE] This Zebadiah had been second in the Sanhedrin, whom they called אב בית דין. Since he had long ruled the tribe of Judah under the King, he was most apt to lead the others with his opinion in political matters. The Sanhedrin not only presided over the greatest judgments, and responded to the referrals of other judges, but also gave counsel to the King in great matters, for instance concerning undertaking or not undertaking war, as is noted in the Talmud, title concerning the King, chap. 5, § 3, and in Maimonides, title concerning the King, chap. 5, 2. Josephus in his explanation of the law concerning the King: 'And let him do nothing without the high priest and the opinion of the senators.'

AND YOU HAVE THE LEVITES AS MASTERS BEFORE YOU] In the Hebrew: the Levite officers before you: that is, they will be ready to execute your commands. The officers of the magistrates and the executors of judgments were taken from the Levites.

The Hebrew word denotes not attendants but prefects.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

AMARIAS AVTEM SACERDOS ET PONTIFEX VESTER IN HIS QVÆ AD DEVM PRÆSIDEBIT ] In Hebræo : Amaria Sacerdos caput super vos in omni verbo Domini. Is Amarias eo tempore נשיא fuerat, id est, prin- ceps Senatus. Ejus erat sententia sua præire cæteris in omnibus eis, quæ lege Dei erant definita.

PORRO ZABADIAS FILIVS ISMAEL, QVI EST DVX IN DOMO JVDA, SVPER EA OPERA ERIT QVÆ AD REGIS OFFICIVM PERTINENT ] Is Zaba- dias fuerat secundus in senatu, quem אב בית דין voca- bant. Cum autem tribum Judæ diu sub Rege rexisset, aptis- simus erat qui ἐν πολιτικοῖς σκέμμασι cæteris præiret sua sen- tentia. Synedrium non tantum judiciis maximis præerat, & ad aliorum judicum relationes respondebat, sed & Regi in re- bus magnis, puta de bello suscipiendo aut non suscipiendo, consilium dabat, ut notatur Thalmode titulo de Rege cap. 5. §. 3. & apud Maimoniden titulo de Rege cap. 5. 2. Josephus in explicatione legis de Rege : πρασσέτω δὲ μηδὲν δίχα τῆ ἀρ- χιερέως καὶ τῆς τῶν γερεσιαςῶν γνώμης.

HABETISQVE LEVITAS MAGISTROS CORAM VOBIS ] In Hebræo : apparitores Levitæ coram vobis : id est, parati erunt illi ad jussa vestra exequenda. Apparitores ma- gistratuum & judiciorum executores è Levitis sumebantur.

Non apparitores notat Ebræa vox sed præ- fectos.

## 20:23
Vers. 23. FOR THE CHILDREN OF AMMON AND MOAB ROSE UP AGAINST THE INHABITANTS OF MOUNT SEIR, TO SLAY AND DESTROY THEM: AND WHEN THEY HAD ACCOMPLISHED THIS WORK, THEY TURNED ALSO AGAINST THEMSELVES AND FELL BY MUTUAL WOUNDS ] The Jews could then say of the Ammonites, Moabites, and Edomites what Tacitus says in his Germania of the Bructeri, Chamavi, and Angrivarii: It is narrated that the Chamavi and Angrivarii immigrated, having driven out and utterly destroyed the Bructeri, with the consent of the neighboring nations, whether out of hatred of their arrogance, or the sweetness of plunder, or some favor of the gods toward us: for they did not even begrudge us the spectacle of the battle. Over 50,000 fell, not by Roman arms and weapons, but, which is more magnificent, for our delight and for our eyes. May it remain, I pray, and endure among the nations, if not love for us, at least hatred for themselves.

Latin:

Vers. 23. NAMQVE FILII AMMON ET MOAB CONSVRREXERVNT ADVERSVS HABITATORES MONTIS SEIR, VT INTERFICERENT, ET DELE- RENT EOS: CVMQVE HOC OPERE PERPETRAS- SENT, ETIAM IN SEMETIPSOS VERSI MVTVIS CONCIDERE VVLNERIBVS ] Potuere tunc dicere Judæi de Ammonitis, Moabitis & Idumæis, quod de Bructe- ris, Chamavis & Angrivariis dicit Tacitus in Germania : Chamavos & Angrivarios immigrasse narratur, pulsis Bructe- ris ac penitus excisis, vicinarum consensu nationum, seu super- biæ odio, seu prædæ dulcedine, seu favore quodam erga nos deo- rum : nam ne spectaculo quidem prælii invidere. Super 50. mil- lia, non armis telisque Romanis, sed quod magnificentius est, oblectationi oculisque ceciderunt. Maneat quæso duretque gentibus, si non amor nostri, at certe odium sui.

## 21:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXI.

Joram, son and successor of Jehoshaphat, an impious idolater and tyrant. The Edomites revolt from him. Called to repentance in vain by a letter from Elijah, he perished miserably.

Latin:

CAPUT XXI.

Joram Josaphati filius & successor impius ido- lolatra, & tyrannus. Deficiunt ab eo Edo- mitae. Literis Eliae frustra ad poenitentiam vocatus misere periit.

## 21:4
Verf. 4. FOR HE KILLED HIS BROTHERS WITH THE SWORD) After the manner of neighboring Kings, of whom Plutarch says in Demetrius: For to kill a brother, just as geometers take their postulates, was so conceded, being considered a common and royal postulate for the sake of security. Tacitus says of the later Kings of the Jews: They dared the flight of citizens, the destruction of cities, the slaughter of brothers, wives, and parents, and other things customary for Kings.

AND CERTAIN OF THE PRINCES OF ISRAEL) Of the Sanhedrin, as is credible, men who loved the law and were of exceptional authority among the people. For to such Kings, to use the words of Sallust, the good are more suspect than the bad, and another's virtue is always a source of fear. Tacitus says that there is no less danger from great fame than from bad: and that for virtues there is certain destruction. This was the reason why Herod removed the entire Sanhedrin.

Latin:

Verf. 4. OCCIDIT ENIM FRATRES SUOS GLADIO) More vicinorum Regum, de quibus Plutarchus Demetrio: Τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἀδελφὸς ἀναιρεῖν, ὥσπερ οἱ γεωμέτραι τὰ αἰτήματα λαμ- βάνουσιν, ὕτω συνειχώρειτο, κοινόν τι νομιζόμενον αἴτημα καὶ βα- σιλικὸν ὑπὲρ ἀσφαλείας. Tacitus de posterioribus Judæo- rum Regibus: Fugas civium, urbium eversiones, fratrum, con- jugum, parentum neces, aliaque solita Regibus ausi.

ET QVOSDAM DE PRINCIBVS ISRAEL) De Sy- nedrio, ut credibile est, homines legis amantes & eximiæ apud populum auctoritatis. Nam talibus Regibus, ut Salu- stii verba usurpem, boni quam mali suspectiores sunt, semperque aliena virtus formidolosa est. Tacitus non minus periculum esse ait ex magna fama, quam ex mala: & ob virtutes certis- simum exitium. Hæc fuit causa cur Herodes totum Syne- drium tolleret.

## 21:12
Verf. 12. A LETTER FROM ELIJAH THE PROPHET) Josephus: A letter is brought from Elijah the prophet: and after the words are recited: Elijah declared these things through the letter. LXX. It came to him in writing from Elijah the prophet saying. Where a tablet or something similar must be supplied. They believed, therefore, that this letter was written by Elijah after he was taken from human affairs: which there is no reason for us to wonder at more than that Judas Maccabaeus is written to have seen in a dream sent divinely, 2 Macc. 15, Onias the High Priest and Jeremiah the Prophet praying for the people.

Grotius believed that this letter was written by Elijah after he was removed from human affairs. But we certainly do not wonder at Grotius, who has gratified the Papists in much more, by sailing here to support their invocation of Saints with the opinion of the Papists that Saints know special or singular things which happen on earth while in heaven. We do wonder, however, that such disparate things are compared here by him himself. For a dream is one thing, and history is another: And that Book of Maccabees is Apocryphal, by no means to be compared with Canonical Scripture, and not even trustworthy in all things; in that narration of the dream, at any rate, it is worthy of no faith; Finally, the reason for the prayer of the Saints for the Church in heaven is far different from that of a letter written by some Saint triumphing in heaven and transmitted from heaven to earth. For that first thing can be easily conceded, that in a general sense the saints pray for the people of God. But who will believe that the Saints in heaven write letters and transmit them to earth to be read? Which is more like a dream than history. Therefore, either with Blessed Luther (Tom. IV. Jen. Latin.) and Philipp Melanchthon (in Chron. Carion.) that calculation must be entered into, that Elijah was still acting on earth at that time; or because such a hysteron proteron must be established in 2 Kings ch. 3 concerning the assumption of Elijah, it must be said with Lyranus, Junius, Tremellius, Piscator, and Helvicus, that he left that letter, written with a prophetic spirit before his ascension into heaven, to Elisha or some other person, to be exhibited to King Joram in his own time. Which opinion also pleases the most learned Emanuel Sa among the Papists. Nor undeservedly. For it is not the role of those triumphing in heaven to instruct or call mortals on earth to repentance: They have Moses and the Prophets: if they do not listen to them, they will not believe even if someone should rise from the dead, let alone if someone should write a letter from heaven, Luke 16, 31.

Latin:

Verf. 12. LITERÆ AB ELIA PROPHETA) Josephus: κομίζεται παρ’ Ἠλιοῦ τῶ προφήτε ἐπιστολή: & post recitata verba: ταῦ- τα μὲν ἐδήλω διὰ τῆς ἐπιστολῆς ὁ Ἠλίας. LXX. ἦλθεν αὐτῷ ἐν γραφῇ παρὰ Ἠλίο τῶ προφήτε λέγων. Vbi supplendum πίναξ, vel simile quid. Credidere ergo ab Elia postquam humanis rebus ereptus est, scriptam hanc Epistolam: quod non est, cur magis miremur, quam quod Judas Maccabæus somnio divini- tus immisso vidisse scribitur 2. Macc. 15. Oniam Sacerdotem & Jeremiam Prophetam pro populo orantes.

CRedidit Grotius scriptam hanc ab Elia Epi- stolam, postquam rebus humanis exemptus est. Sed Grotium sane non miramur, qui multo plura Papistis gratificatus est, opinioni Papistarum de Sanctis specialia vel singularia, quæ in terris ge- runtur, in cœlis cognoscentibus, ad statuminandam eorum invocationem, hic velificari. Miramur au- tem tam disparata hic ab ipso comparari. Nam & aliud est somnium, aliud Historia: Et Liber ille Maccabæorum Apocryphus est, nequaquam cum Scriptura Canonica comparandus, ac ne per omnia quidem ἀξιόπιστος; in illa utiq; somnii narratione fide nulla dignus; Denique longe alia ratio est ora- tionis Sanctorum pro Ecclesia in cælis, alia literarum a Sancto aliquo in cœlis triumphante scriptarum, e cœlis in terras transmissarum. Illud enim facile concedi potest, quod in genere sancti orent pro po- pulo Dei. At quis credet, Sanctos in cœlis literas scribere, easque legendas in terras transmittere? Quod somnio similius, quam Historiæ. Quapro- pter aut cum B. Luthero Tom. IV. Jen. Latin. & Philipp. Melanchth. in Chron. Carion. ea ineunda est calculi ratio, quod adhuc Elias isto tempore in terris egerit; aut quia ita ὑστεροπρωτεία 2. Reg. c. 3. circa affumtionem Eliæ statuenda, cum Lyrano, Ju- nio, Tremellio, Piscatore, Helvico dicendum, quod Epistolam illam Spiritu vaticidico scriptam ante suam in cœlos ἀνάληψιν Elisæo vel alii cuipiam re- liquerit, Regi Joramo suo tempore exhibendam Quæ sententia etiam e Papistis placet doctissimo Emanueli Saa. Nec immerito. Non enim trium- phantium in cœlis est erudire, aut ad pœnitentiam revocare mortales in terra: Habent Mosen & Pro- phetas: si illos non audiant, neque si quis ex mortuis re- surrexerit, nedum si quis e cœlis literas perscripserit credent Luc. 16, 31.

## 22:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXII.

Ahaziah succeeds Joram, likewise an idolater, who with Joram of Israel is killed by Jehu; his mother Athaliah killed all his sons, with the exception of Joash.

Ver. 1.

BUT THE INHABITANTS OF JERUSALEM CONSTITUTED) That is, they placed him on the throne, as below 23, 20; for the kingdom was owed to him by right, without any votes of the people.

Latin:

CAPUT XXII.

Ochozias succedit Joramo itidem idololatra, qui cum Joramo Israelitico a Jehu interficitur; mater ejus Athalia filios ejus omnes, uno Joaso excepto, interfecit.

Verf. 1.

CONSTITVERVNT AVTEM HABITATORES JE- RVSALEM) Id est, in folio locarunt, ut infra 23, 20. nam regnum jure ipsi debebatur, sine ullis populi suffragiis.

## 22:2
Ver. 2. AHAZIAH WAS FORTY-TWO YEARS OLD) It does not seem that this can be consistent with those things which we have in 2 Kings 8, 26. Therefore the reading of the LXX is more correct: ἐτῶν εἴκοσιϰαὶ δύο.

BUT thus it is contradicted not only by the Hebrew Codices, which all retain the stated number, but also by the Vulgate version, since the Latin Codices also consistently read it so: I confess, says Cornelius a Lapide, that all Hebrew and Latin Codices in this place have 42, not 22. Therefore, however much the LXX Interpreters, and with them the Syriac and Arabic—both the Antiochene, that is, or of Mount Sinai, and the Alexandrian or Coptic—have 22, which number they undoubtedly took from 2 Kings 8, the Hebrew and Latin Codices are not to be corrected from that. We repeat the argument of Cornelius to chapter 16, 1 of this book, and we oppose the same to him: to say that there is an error in all the Codices is to say that there is an error in Holy Scripture, which God forbid. Nor does Mariana's conjecture have a place here: that מב could easily have been put for כב; because years are not counted by numerical letters in the Hebrew Codex, but by whole words signifying the number of years. There is no reason, therefore, why we should agree here with Grotius, who is easily inclined to correct Hebrew Codices, as are Cajetan, Bellarmine in his harmony of the years of the Kings of Israel and Judah, which Cornelius a Lapide praises as an unpublished work, Torniellus, Salianus, Mariana, Cornelius, Tirinus, Menochius, even though Scaliger, Ludovicus Capellus, Alstedius, and Osiander side with them here. Yet other authors of great name in the Papacy protest against them: Lyranus, Vatablus, Genebrardus, Gordonus, Mendoza, Serarius, Svarezius, Sanctius, etc. Nor indeed can they do otherwise, unless they wish to oppose the Council of Trent, which decreed the absolute authority of the Vulgate version. Our Hugo, with his Lud. Capellus, appeals to the Greek translation not securely enough: for it varies: In the Wechel edition, the years are read as ἔιϰοσι δύο XXII, but in the Sixtine, ἔιϰοσι twenty. And indeed it is better to count this chronological difficulty among the insoluble problems than to concede a corruption of the sacred text. For once this is admitted, what finally will be left certain and indubitable in the Hebrew sources? Yet interpreters, both Hebrew and Christian, have labored to solve this difficulty. And various ways of answering are found; which, however, most involve in new difficulties. The first is that of Genebrardus and Serarius, that the years of the Samaritan era are counted here, which are to be begun from the 6th year of Omri, the maternal grandfather and founder of Samaria, since he raised it to a metropolis and began to reign alone in the 6th year: from which he reigned 6 years more as Omri, and his son Ahab with Ahaziah the son 24 years; but the son of this one, Joram reigned 12 years, which make 42 years. For in the last year of Joram, King of Israel, Ochozias, King of Judah, began to reign. Others object to this explanation, that Ochozias was King of Judah: therefore, in his years, it seems inconvenient for the years of the Israelite Kings, or of the Kingdom of Samaria, to be counted against him. But it could be said: that those forty-two years are designated from the founding of Samaria by Amri, because from then the impiety of the maternal grandfather of Ochozias prevailed, and it was greatly propagated through Achab, of whom mention is therefore made here, and his successors, in whose footsteps Ozias is said to have walked here. A more serious difficulty is that these 42 years are said to be of Ochozias, not of the kingdom of Samaria: For the Hebrew has it thus: A son of 42 years was Ochozias in his reign. However, it could be answered: that Ochozias is said to have been a son of forty-two years in his reign, that is, a follower of 42 years, and an imitator of the impiety which prevailed in the kingdom of Israel for 42 years from his maternal grandfather: for sons are also called such by imitation, as is known; and he can rightly be named a Son of forty-two years, who insists upon those ways which were trodden for 42 years. For although commonly, where the name of time is added to the name בן, age is designated, it is nevertheless clear that the use of the name בן is very broad: whence, just as sons of wickedness in Deut. 13:13 are called followers of wickedness, nothing seems to prevent Ochozias from being called a son of 42 years in his reign, because in his reign he was a follower of those things which were mostly done in the kingdom of Israel for 42 years, as far as the equal wickedness of the rule is concerned, so that the time is put metonymically for the things done in the time, and it is indicated that he was a son of the 42 years of impiety, which, to wit, flourished in the other kingdom, in his own kingdom.

The other solution lies in a new explanation of the Hebrew text, that of Junius and Tremellius: who render the words in the sources thus v. 1 and 2. Thus reigned Achozia, son of Joharam, King of Judah. Whose mother's name was Hathalia, daughter of Homri, acting in her forty-second year, (or rather son of 42 years) when Achazia reigned, who reigned for one year in Jerusalem. And they observe that there is a rather obscure transposition in the Hebrew text, of the kind that is in 1 Sam. 20:16 and Ezra 10:17 and Nehem. 12:22, which not being observed, this passage has been involved in various questions and interpretations, and that the name Homri pertains here to the whole family, in which he himself first reigned 1 Kings 6:25, and so many years are counted, from when Homri fully approached the Kingdom until the Kingdom of Achazia. For Homri reigned eight years alone: Achab with Achazia his son 22, and Joram, removed by Jehu, TWELVE. Which solution our Dr. Walther judges to be accepted for the time being in his Harmon. Dr. Walther, until a better one is devised, so that it may be said that the age of Ochazia, at which he began to reign, is recounted in the book of Kings, but the place in Chronicles counts the whole time from when the house of Amri had begun to reign until the Kingdom of Achazia. But Ludov. de Dieu observes that this transposition does violence to the Hebrew text: because what is constructed with Achazia at the beginning of the verse is referred to Omri, who is mentioned at the end of the verse. He prefers, therefore, to confess roundly that it is inexplicable, and yet that this difficulty is for us without danger: Because with the Annals missing, the circumstances are hidden from us, the knowledge of which would make the solution easy. I do not know, however, whether it might be possible, without that transposition, according to our previous answer, to say: that Ochozias was a son of 42 years when he began to reign, not because he was that many years old then, but because those many years had been the years of the family of Ochozias when he himself began to reign. The reconciliation which is read among the Hebrews in Seder Olam chapter 18 agrees almost with that explanation. From the time when Asa, King of Judah, gave the daughter of Amri, King of Israel, in marriage to Josaphat his son, it was divinely decreed that the kingdom

of Judah should perish with the kingdom of the house of Achab and Israel, (namely 42 years before this history.) Hence it is said: And from the Lord was the trampling of Achazia, etc. And thus on one and the same day both Kings were extinguished. See also Martin Borrhaus in his commentary on this passage.

But it pleased Ludovicus de Dieu to attempt another answer: Therefore, now a third mode of solution is read again in a different explanation of this phrase in his animadversion on the difficult passages of the Old Testament on this passage. It is an ambiguous phrase, he says, which occurs here. For although I confess that in the books of Kings and Chronicles it signifies here and there that he was so many years old when he began to reign, it is nevertheless a place where it must be taken otherwise, as 1 Sam. 13:1 בֶּן־שָׁנָה שָׁאוּל בְּמָלְכוֹ where the sense cannot be: Saul was one year old when he began to reign. For he was already an adult, called from shepherding to the kingdom. But the sense is, one year of the kingdom had been completed when the inauguration, about which the previous chapter was repeated, or when he was making a selection of soldiers, about which the following verses, so it must be translated, Saul was a son of a year in his reign. Hence also in this place, although not in entirely the same sense, we translate, Achazia was a son of forty-two years while he reigned: that is, the space of his reign extends itself up to the forty-second year of his age. For although he lived and reigned only one year, there must also be ascribed to his reign the first six years of his mother Athalia, during which, the royal seed being extinguished, the woman reigned against the law. Then the 13 years of his son Joas, which flowed from the seventh year of his age, in which he was inaugurated, until the twentieth, in which he was finally made of age and fit for the kingdom: which 20 years, (namely one in which Achazia reigned, six in which Athalia reigned, 13 in which Joas was a minor) if they are added to the twenty-two years which Achazia was old when he approached the kingdom, we have 42 years, then finally completed when Joas himself was administering the kingdom. So that it is not without reason said that the reign of Achazia lasted so long. This explanation may be helped if it is said that his reign is extended up to the 42nd year from the birth of Ahaziah (not to the 42nd year of his age, for Joram did not live to the 13th year of the reign of Joash, but died before the reign of Athaliah) for a certain reason, namely because only then did his son Joash properly begin to administer the kingdom: And therefore the Hebrew words can be rendered thus: Ahaziah was a son of 42 years in his reign: that is, 42 years were completed in the reign of Ahaziah, from his birth, before, namely, a successor was given to him, his son Joash; (just as it is said Saul was a son of a year in his reign, that is, a year of the reign of Saul had been completed.) and he himself reigned one year in Jerusalem.

Finally, the fourth solution is that of Jerome in the Hebrew Traditions on 2 Chronicles, as well as R. David and Abarbanel, which has been followed by the Glossa, Lyranus, Hugo, Dionysius, Gordonus, Mendoza, Vatablus, as also Fran. Suarez, p. 3, Tom. 1, Disp. 6, Sect. 1, and also from the Reformed, Peter Martyr, Johannes Buxtorf the Younger, the authors of the Belgian notes, and from our own, the Weimar Paraphrasts, and others.
