Namely, that Joram, when his affairs began to decline, and he was being invaded by the Arabs and afflicted by diseases, declared his son Ahaziah king while he was still alive, when he was 22 years old, and in this state 20 years passed: Whence the sum of 42 years, because when the father died, he was declared king as it were anew, and then Ahaziah reigned for only one year. In this way, therefore, the Book of Kings would speak of that term in which, while his father was still surviving, he was created as it were a viceroy. The present passage in Chronicles, however, is about that reign which he undertook after the death of his father. Joram, says R. David Kimchi, lived longer than 40 years, but no more than eight years are counted during which he reigned, namely בְחוֹזְקָן well and happily: But from the time when he fell into the hands of the Arabs, and into sickness, his reign is no longer counted; but they appointed Ahaziah as King while he himself was alive, namely from that time when his father fell and was inglorious, from which 20 years elapsed. Since therefore Ahaziah was chosen King while his father was alive, he was 22 years old, etc. A very perplexing question arises. For he says that Joram reigned for eight years, and lived for forty years, and he says that his son Ahaziah, when he began to reign, was forty-two years old. But if this is so, he begat him two years before he himself was born. Unless this is solved, even a simple reader notices how ridiculous it is. For Joram himself, who is described here as having lived forty years and reigned eight years, lived forty years and reigned twenty-eight. For the eight years which are attributed to him in the kingdom are those before he killed his brothers, when he was still living innocently. But the twenty years during which he reigned are taken away from his number because he spent them in languor and tribulation; therefore they are attributed to his son, who, having no more than twenty-two years, is said to have reigned, so that the remaining sum of the numbers would not cause an error in the investigation of the times. For Ahaziah lived twenty-three years and reigned only one year. For a comparison of the reading of the book of Kings provides great help for solving this question. And although this opinion is not without its own difficulty, primarily because the Epoch of the Kings of Judah is thus enriched by 20 years, it has nevertheless pleased great authors, and it is entirely to be preferred to the invention of those who argue here that the Hebrew text is corrupt. Some scruples always remain in chronological matters and certain ἄπορα (difficulties): on account of which, however, it is by no means right to call the sacred Codices into suspicion of error; but it is better to confess our ignorance than to detract from divine providence and the integrity of the sacred text. However, whichever solution pleases the learned reader may be chosen; the first and last are more accepted, and the first and third seem to be preferred. Mr. Christian Ravius, Professor at Uppsala, recently devised a new explanation in his Biblical Chronology, namely that the forty-second year of that century should be understood; but neither does this calculation agree with a truer Chronology, as we have taught elsewhere, nor is it accepted anywhere in the scriptures that the years of a century are numbered, of which matter not even a single example can be produced.

Latin:

Verf. 2. QVADRAGINTA DVORVM ANNORVM ERAT OCHOZIAS) Vix videtur id consistere posse cum eis, quæ habemus 2. Reg. 8, 26. Rectior ergo lectio LXX. ἐτῶν εἴκοσιϰαὶ δύο.

ATita contradicitur non Ebræis tantum Codi- cibus, qui omnes dictum numerum retinent, sed etiam vulgatæ versioni, fiquidem & Latini Co- dices constanter ita legant: Fateor, inquit Corne- lius a Lapide, omnes Codd. Ebræos & Latinos hoc lo- co habere 42. non 22. Utut ergo LXX. Interpp. & cum iis Syrus & Arabicus uterque Antiochenus scili- cet, sive montis Sinai, & Alexandrinus sive Copticus habeant 22. quem numerum e 2. Reg. 8. depromse- re sine dubio, non corrigendi tamen inde Ebræi ac Latini Codices. Repetimus Cornelii Argumen- tum ad cap. 16, 1. hujus libri, eidemque ipsi opponi- mus; in omnibus Codicibus esse mendum, est dicere in Scriptura Sacra esse mendum, quod absit. Neque hic Marianæ conjectura locum habet: quod facile מב pro כב poni potuerit; quia non literis Arithme- ticis numerantur anni in Codice Ebræo, sed inte- gris vocibus annorum numerum significantibus. Non est ergo, quod Papistis, facile propensis ad ca- stigandos Ebræos Codices, hic adstipulemur cum Grotio, utpote Cajetano, Bellarmino in concordia annorum Regum Israel & Juda, quam ἀνέϰδοτον laudat Cornelius a Lapide, Torniello, Saliano, Ma- riana, Cornelio, Tirino, Menochio, etsi cum illis hic faciant Scaliger, Ludovicus Capellus, Alstedius, Osian- der. Quibus tamen alii magni nominis auctores in Papatu reclamant; Lyranus, Vatablus, Gene- brardus, Gordonus, Mendoza, Serarius, Svarezius, Sanctius, &c. Neque vero aliter possunt, nisi Con- cilio Tridentino absolutam vulgatæ versionis ἀυ- θεντίαν decernenti refragari velint. Ad Græcam translationem Hugo noster cum Lud. Capello suo non satis fecuri provocant: Ea enim variat: In editione Wechel. leguntur anni ἔιϰοσι δύο XXII. in Sixtina autem ἔιϰοσι viginti. Et sane præstat hanc difficultatem Chronologicam inter ἄπορα nume- rare, quam corruptelam textus sacri concedere. Hac enim semel admissa quid denique certi ac in- dubii relinquetur in fontibus Ebraicis? Laborarunt tamen Interpp. cum Ebræi, tum Christiani, ut sol- verent hanc difficultatem. Et reperiuntur varii modii respondendi; quos tamen novis difficulta- tibus plerique involvunt. Primus est Genebrardi & Serarii, quod hic anni æræ Samaritanæ numerentur, quæ ab anno 6. Amri avi Materni conditoris Sama- riæ, utpote qui in metropolin eam evexerit, & solus anno 6. regnare cœperit, inchoanda: ex quo 6. annos adhuc Amri regnavit, & filius ejus Ahab cum Ochozia filio 24. annos; hujus autem filius Joram annis 12. qui efficiunt 42. annos. Vltimo enim Jorami Regis Israelitici anno cœpit regnare Ocho- zias Rex Juda. Objiciunt huic explicationi alii, quod Ochozias Rex Judæ fuerit : in ejusdem ergo annis annos Israelitarum Regum, vel Regni Samariæ ipfi adversinumerari inconveniens videtur. Sed di- ci posset: quadraginta illos duos annos designari conditæ ab Amri Samariæ, quod inde invaluerit avi materni Ochaziæ impietas, eaque per Achabum, cu- jus proinde hic mentio fit, & successores ejus maxi- me propagata sit, cujus vestigiis hic institisse Ozias dicitur. Gravior difficultas est, quod hi 42. anni di- cuntur esse Ochoziæ, non regni Samariæ : Ita enim habent Ebræa : Filius 42. annorum Ochozias in regno suo. Responderi autem posset: quod Ocho- zias dicatur in regno suo fuisse filius quadraginta duo- rum annorum, id est, Sectator 42. annorum, & imi- tator impietatis, quæ per 42. annos inde ab avo mater- no in regno Israelis obtinuit : nam & filii imitatione dicuntur, uti notum est ; & recte quadraginta duo- rum annorum Filius nominari potest, qui viis illis insistit, quæ per 42. annos calcatæ sunt. Quanquam enim communiter, ubi nomen temporis additur nomini בן, ætas designetur, latissime tamen usum nominis בן patere constat : unde uti filii nequitiæ Deut. 13, 13. dicuntur sectatores nequitiæ, nihil obsta- re videtur, quin filius 42. annorum in regno suo dica- tur Ochozias, quod in regno suo fuerit sectator eo- rum, quæ 42. annis in regno Israelis maxime gesta sunt, quantum ad regiminis parilem improbitatem, ut metonymice tempus pro rebus gestis in tempore ponatur, & filius impietatis 42. annorum, quæ sc. in altero regno floruit, in suo regno fuisse indigitetur.

Altera solutio in explicatione nova textus Ebraici sita, Junii & Tremellii est : qui verba in fontibus ita reddunt v. 1. & 2. Ita regnavit Acho- zia filius Joharami Rex Judæ. Cujus matri nomen Hathalia nata Homri, agentis quadragesimum secun- dum annum, (vel potius filii 42. annorum) quum Achazia regnaret, qui anno uno regnavit Jeruscha- laim. Et observant in Ebræo textu trajectıonem esse obscuriorem, cujusmodi est 1. Sam. 20, 16. & Esræ 10, 17. & Nehem. 12, 22. qua non observata, hic locus variis quæstionibus & interpretationibus invo- lutus fuerit, nomenque Homri ad totam familiam hic pertinere, in qua ipse primus regnavit 1. Reg. 6, 25. & tot annos numerari, ex quo Homri plene adiret Re- gnum usque ad Regnum Achaziæ. Homri enim regna- vit annos octo solus : Achab cum Achazia filio 22. & Joram a Jehu sublatus DVODECIM. Quam solutionem tantisper acceptandam judicat in Har- mon. Dn. D. Waltherus noster, donec excogitetur melior, ut ita dicatur, in loco Regum enarrari ætatem Ochaziæ, qua cœperat regnare, locum vero Paralip. numerare totum tempus, ex quo domus Amri, usque ad Regnum Achaziæ, regnare cœperat. Sed Ludov. de Dieu observat, trajectıonem istam vim textui He- bræo inferre : quia quod in principio versus construi- tur cum Achazia, ad Omri refertur, cujus in fine ver- sus mentio. Mavult ergo potius rotunde fateri in- explicabilem, & tamen sine periculo hanc nobis esse difficultatem : Quia deficientibus Annalibus la- tent nos circumstantiæ, quarum cognitio facilem redderet solutionem. Nescio tamen annon possit, absque illa trajectıone, juxta priorem nostram re- sponsionem dici : Filium 42. annorum fuisse Ocha- ziam, cum regnare cœpit, non quod tot annos natus tum fuerit, sed quod tot anni fuerint familiæ Ocho- ziæ, cum cœpit ipse regnare. Convenit fere cum illa explicatione conciliatio, quæ apud Ebræos legitur in Seder Olam cap. 18. Ex quo Asa Rex Judæ dedit Josaphato filio suo in matrimonium filiam Amri regis Israel, divinitus decretum est, ut regnum

Juda periret cum regno domus Achab & Israel, (nem- pe 42. annis ante hanc historiam.) Hinc dicitur: Et a Domino fuit conculcatio Achaziæ, &c. Et sic uno eodemq; die ambo Reges extincti sunt. Vid. etiam Martin. Borrhaus in comment. ad h. l.

Libuit autem Ludovico de Dieu aliam tentare responsionem: Proinde jam Tertius solutionis mo- dus iterum in explicatione diversa hujus Phrasis si- tus legitur in animadversione ejusdem in loca difficil. V.T. ad h.l. Ambigua, inquit, phrasis est, quæ hic occur- rit. Etsi enim in libris Regum & Chronicorum passim significare fatear, eum tot vel tot annos fuisse natum, quum inciperet regnare, est tamen ubi aliter accipi debeat, ut 1. Sam. 13, 1. בֶּן־שָׁׁנָה שָׁאוּל בְּמָלְכוֹ ubi sensus esse nequit: Unum annum fuisse natum Saulem, cum inciperet regnare. Fuit enim jam ad- ultus, a pastoritia ad regnum vocatus. Sed Sensus est, unum regni annum fuisse exactum, quum inau- guratio, de qua cap. præcedenti repeteretur, aut quum delectum militum faceret, de quo vers. seqq. itaque ver- tendum, filius anni erat Saul in regno suo. Hinc & hoc loco, quamvis non omnino eodem sensu, vertimus, filius quadraginta & duorum annorum erat Acha- zia dum regnaret: id est, spatium regni ejus extendit se usque ad quadragesimum secundum ætatis ejus annum. Etsi enim vivus annum tantum unum re- gnaverit, adscribendi tamen quoque sunt ipsius regno primum sex anni matris ejus Athaliæ, quibus, extin- cto semine regio, mulier præter fas regnavit. Deinde 13. anni filii ejus Joasi, qui ab ætatis anno septimo, quo inauguratus fuit, usque ad vigesimum, quo majorennis demum factus est & regno aptus, fluxerunt: qui 20. anni, (nempe unus quo Achasia, sex quibus Athalia regnavit, 13. quibus minorennis fuit Joas) si addun- tur viginti duobus annis, quos natus erat Achasia, quum regnum adiret, habemus 42. annos, tum demum exactos, quum Joas ipsemet regnum administraret. Adeo ut tam diu Achasiæ regnum durasse, non immeri- to dicatur. Juvari poterit explicatio hæc, si dicatur usque ad 42. a nato Achazia annum (non ad 42. æta- tis ejus annum, neque enim ad 13. regni Joasi Joram vixit, sed ante Athaliæ regimen occubuit) regnum ejus ob certam causam extendi, quia sc. tum demum Joas filius ejus regnum administrare proprie cœpit: Ideoque ita reddi poterunt verba Ebræa: Filius 42. annorum fuit Ochozias in regno suo: h.e. anni 42. exacti sunt in regno Achaziæ, inde a nativitate ejus, priusquam sc. successor ei daretur, Joas filius; (uti dicitur filius anni erat Saul in regno, id est, exactus erat annus Regni Saulis.) & ipse regnavit anno uno in Jerusalem.

Quarta denique solutio Hieronymi est in tradi- tionibus Ebraicis lib. 2. Paralip. nec non R. David, & Abarbin. quam secuta est Glossa, Lyranus, Hugo, Dionysius, Gordonus, Mendoza, Vatablus, ut & Fran. Suarez. p. 3. Tom. 1. Disp. 6. Sect. 1. nec non e Re- formatis, Petrus Martyr, Johannes Buxtorffius Ju- nior, Auctores notarum Belgicarum, e nostris Para- phrastæ Vinarienses, & alii. Nimirum Joramum, cum res ejus inclinare inciperent, & tum ab Arabibus invaderetur, tum morbis affligeretur, vivum adhuc Regem declarasse filium suum Achaziam, cum ille esset 22. annorum, & in hoc statu effluxisse 20. an- nos: Unde summa 42. annorum, quia cum Pater moreretur, de novo quasi Rex declaratus fuit, & tum non nisi uno anno regnavit Achazias. Hoc itaque pacto liber Regum loqueretur de illo termino, quo Patre adhuc superstite, quasi Pro-Rex creatus fuit. Locus præsens autem in Chronicis de eo regno, quod post obitum Patris aggressus est. Joramum, in- quit R. David Kimchi, diutius quam per 40. annos vixit, non autem numerantur plures quam octo anni, quibus regnavit, sc. בְחוֹזְקָן bene & feliciter: Sed ab eo tempore, quo incidit in manus Arabum, & in mor- bum, non ulterius annumeratur ipsius regno; Sed Re- gem constituerunt Achasiam vivente ipso, ab eo sc. tempore, quo Pater ejus cecidit, & inglorius fuit, quo 20. anni effluxerunt. Cum ergo Achasias vivente Pa- tre Rex eligeretur, 22. annorum fuit &c. Hieronymus ita hac de re habet: Quæstio valde perplexa oritur. Dicit enim regnasse Joram octo annis, & vixisse eum quadraginta annis,& dicit filium ejus Achasiam, cum regnare cœpisset, fuisse quadraginta duorum annorum. Quod si ita est, duobus annis antequam ipse natus est, ipse illum genuit. Quod nisi solvatur, quam sit ridicu- lum etiam simplex lector advertit. Ipse enim Joram, qui hic quadraginta annis vixisse describitur, & octo annis regnasse, vixit annos quadraginta, & regnavit viginti & octo. Octo enim anni, qui ei in regno tribuuntur, ipsi sunt antequam fratres occideret, cum adhuc inno- center viveret. Viginti vero anni quibus regnavit, ideo a numero ejus auferuntur, quia in languore & tribulatione deduxit eos, ideo filio ejus tribuuntur, qui non amplius quam viginti duos annos habens, regnasse perhibetur, ne de numerorum summa remanentes er- rorem indagini temporum facerent. Ahazias enim vixit viginti tribus annis, uno tantum anno regnavit. Collatio enim lectionis libri Regum huic solvendæ quæstioni magnum præbet auxilium. Etsi vero etiam sententia hæc non careat difficultate sua, imprimis, quod ita Epocha Regum Juda 20. annis locupletetur, magnis tamen autoribus placuit, & præferenda omnino est eorum commento, qui hic textum Ebræum corruptionis arguunt. Manent semper scrupuli aliqui in re Chronologica & ἄπορα quæ- dam: ob quæ vero integrum minime est Codices sa- cros in suspicionem erroris vocare; Sed præstat ignorantiam nostram fateri, quam providentiæ di- vinæ ac integritati sacri textus derogare. Poterit au- tem eligi, quæcunque erudito lectori placuerit solu- tio; Prima & ultima magis receptæ sunt, ac præfe- rendæ videntur prima & tertia. Novam nuper exco- gitavit Dn. Christian. Ravius Professor Ubsaliens. in Chronologia sua Biblica explicationem, quod nempe intelligatur annus quadragesimus secundus istius secu- li; Sed neque computus iste cum veriore Chrono- logia congruit, ut alibi docuimus, nec in script. receptum uspiam est, annos seculi numerari, cujus rei ne unicum quidem proferri poterit exemplum.

## 22:3
Verse 3. FOR HIS MOTHER IMPELLED HIM TO ACT IMPIOUSLY) Mothers of weak judgment are accustomed to have much influence among Kings.

Latin:

Vers. 3. MATER ENIM EJUS IMPULIT EUM UT IM- PIE AGERET) Solent apud Reges imbecillis judicii mul- tum valere matres.

## 22:6
Verse 6. AHAZIAH THE SON OF JORAM, KING OF JUDAH) Thus also the Greeks [write] Ὀχοζίας. Nor is this name written otherwise in the same history in 2 Kings 8:25, 28. Wherefore it seems that by error עזריהו (Azariah) has crept in here in the Hebrew instead of אחזיהו (Ahaziah).

Others more correctly, with R. David Kimchi, [believe] that the King was διώνυμον (having two names), which one may observe here and there in other places. For there is no reason why we should believe that an error has crept in, or that we should correct Hebrew sources from Greek and Latin rivulets: concerning which Jerome [writes] in the Hebrew Traditions. Here Azariah is named Ahaziah a little above. Ahaziah is interpreted as 'apprehending the Lord,' Azariah as 'the help of the Lord.' And therefore his name is changed for the better in this place, because according to the commandment of the Lord, he had gone down to visit the sick man.

Latin:

Vers. 6. OCHOXIAS FILIUS JORAM, REX JUDA) Sic & Græci Ὀχοζίας. Nec aliter hoc nomen scribitur in ea- dem historia 2. Reg. 8, 25. 28. quare per errorem videtur hic in Hebræo irrepsisse עזריהו pro אחזיהו.

Rectius alii cum R. David Kimchi Regem fuisse διώνυμον, quod in aliis passim observare licet. Non enim causa est, cur errorem irrepsisse credamus, aut Ebræos fontes e rivulis Græcis & Latinis corriga- mus: de quo Hieronymus in Tradition. Hebraic. Hic Azarias paulo superius Achazias nominatus est. Ahazias interpretatur apprehendens Dominum, Azarias adjutorium domini. Et ideo mutatur ei no- men in melius in hoc loco, eo quod juxta præceptum Domini, ad infirmum visitandum descenderat.

## 22:7
Verse 7. WHOM THE LORD ANOINTED TO DESTROY THE HOUSE OF AHAB) That is, He stirred him up to this, when He ordered him to be anointed through Elisha, 2 Kings 9:6.

Latin:

Vers. 7. QVEM UNXIT DOMINUS UT DELERET DOMUM ACHAB) Id est, in hoc eum excitavit, cum eum per Elisæum jussit ungi, 2. Reg. 9, 6.

## 22:10
Verse 10. AND HE KILLED ALL THE ROYAL OFFSPRING OF THE HOUSE OF JORAM) It is rare that דבר (dabar) is found for 'to destroy.' For in Psalm 2, verse 4, nothing prevents it from being translated 'he will speak.' Hence some prefer those Codices which have ותאבד (and he perished) here, as in 2 Kings 11:1.

Again, without cause, in the great consensus of the Codices, a scribal error is imagined. R. Mordecai Nathan in the Chapters of the Hebrew Concordances notes the word דבר (dabar) as bringing about destruction: and who does not know that דבר is used for plague, death, and destruction?

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET INTERFECIT OMNEM STIRPEM RE- GIAM DOMUS JORAM) Vix est, ut דבר reperiatur pro perdere. Nam in Psalm. 2. vers. 4. nihil vetat verti, loque- tur. Hinc quidam præferunt eos Codices, qui hic habuere ותאבד, quomodo 2. Reg. 11, 1.

Rursus sine causa, in magno Codicum consen- su fingitur librariorum error. Vocem דבר perdi- tionem inferre R. Mardochai Nathan in Capitulis Concordantiar. Ebraicar. notat: & quis nescit דבר de peste, morte, ac perditione usurpari?

## 23:1 Argument
SECTION II. CONCERNING THE KINGS WHO FOLLOWED ATHALIAH. CHAPTER XXIII.

Joash is placed over the kingdom, the impious Athaliah is killed. The priest Jehoiada binds everyone to the worship of God, and distributes the sacred offices.

Verse 1. JEHOIADA WAS STRENGTHENED. That he was the high priest, although it is not found in the Catalog in 1 Chronicles 6 and Ezra 7:1, Josephus and the Hebrew Chronicles teach; and Cornelius notes here that other High Priests are also omitted in the Catalog. He could hardly have performed such things, or even given orders to the Priests, unless he had been the High Priest.

Latin:

SECTIO II. DE REGIBUS ATHALIAM SEQUUTIS. CAPUT XXIII.

Joas regno præficitur, impia Athalia occiditur. Sacerdos Jojada adstringit omnes ad cultum Dei, & officia sacra distribuit.

Vers. 1. CONFORTATUS JOJADA. SUmmum pontificem fuisse, etsi in Catalogo 1. Par. 6. & Esdr. 7, 1. non inveniatur, Joseph. & Chronic. Ebræor. docet; & prætermitti in Catalo- go etiam alios Pontifices notat hic Cornelius. Vix talia præstare, aut Sacerdotibus etiam præscribere potuisset, nisi Pontifex fuisset.

## 23:2
Ver. 2. AND THE CHIEFS OF THE FAMILIES OF ISRAEL] By Israel here understand Judah and Benjamin synecdochically.

Latin:

Vers. 2. ET PRINCIPES FAMILIARUM ISRAEL] Per Israelem hic intellige Judam & Benjamin συνεκδοχικῶς.

## 23:3
Ver. 3. THE KING'S SON SHALL REIGN] The kingdom is owed to him by right.

Latin:

Vers. 3. FILIUS REGIS REGNABIT] Ei jure debetur regnum.

## 23:5
Ver. 5. AT THE GATE WHICH IS CALLED THE FOUNDATION] It was so called because it was situated on a sloping place, through which one climbed from the palace into the Temple. The same as the gate of the guards in the book of Kings.

Latin:

Vers. 5. AD PORTAM QVÆ APPELLATUR FUN- DAMEN TI] Ita dicta fuit quod in loco declivi sita esset, per quam è regia in Templum scandebatur. Eadem scutariorum in libro Regum.

## 23:18
Ver. 18. ACCORDING TO THE DISPOSITION OF DAVID] Remember 1 Chronicles 18. He recalled this into use, which had long been neglected.

Latin:

Vers. 18. JUXTA DISPOSITIONEM DAVID] Memo- riam 1. Paralip. 18. Hanc ille diu neglectam in usum revocavit.

## 24:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIV.

Joash, after Jehoiada died, turning aside to idols, being rebuked by Zechariah, stones him; therefore Judea is despoiled, Joash is killed.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIV.

Joas mortuo Jojada ad idola deflectens a Za- charia reprehensus eum lapidat, ideo Judæa spoliatur, Joas occiditur.

## 24:6
Ver. 6. THE MONEY WHICH WAS APPOINTED BY MOSES THE SERVANT OF THE LORD] In Hebrew: the gift of Moses the servant of God: i.e., such an offering as was used in the times of Moses.

Latin:

Vers. 6. PECUNIAM QVÆ CONSTITUTA EST A MOSE SERVO DOMINI] In Hebr. munus Mosis servi Dei: i. e. talem oblationem qualis usurpata fuit Mosis temporibus.

## 24:17
Ver. 17. WHO BEING ENTICED BY THEIR OBSEQUIOUSNESS, YIELDED TO THEM] He paraphrases that which is in the Hebrew: the King listened to them. Curtius says that the wealth of kings is more often overturned by flattery than by an enemy. Moreover, the ears of many princes, to speak with Tacitus, receive nothing except what is pleasant and harmful.

Latin:

Vers. 17. QVI DELINITUS OBSEQVIIS EORUM, AC- QVIEVIT EIS] παραφράζει illud quod in Hebræo est audi- vit Rex eos. Regum opes sæpius assentatio quam hostis ever- tit, ait Curtius. Multorum autem Principum aures, ut cum Tacito loquar, nihil accipiunt nisi jucundum & læsurum.

## 24:20
Ver. 20. THE SON OF JEHOIADA [Why that Jehoiada is called Barachiah in the Gospel, see what we noted at Matthew 23:35.

That Zechariah in Matthew is not the same as the one killed here: concerning whom we spoke there.

AND HE STOOD IN THE SIGHT OF THE PEOPLE] In Hebrew: over the people: that is, he preached from a higher place, from where he might be more easily heard by all.

Latin:

Vers. 20. FILIUM JOJADÆ [Qui Jojada cur in Evan- gelio Barachia dicatur, vide quæ notavimus ad Matth. 23, 35.

NOn est ille Zacharias apud Matthæum idem qui hic occisus: de quo illic diximus.

ET STETIT IN CONSPECTU POPULI) In Hebr. super populum: id est, concionatus est ex loco superiore, unde facilius ab omnibus exaudiretur.

## 24:22
Ver. 22. HE SAID: MAY THE LORD SEE AND REQUIRE IT] Which God did through external wars and domestic conspiracy.

Latin:

Vers. 22. AIT: VIDEAT DOMINUS ET REQVIRAT) Quod fecit Deus per bella externa, & domesticam conjura- tionem.

## 24:24
Vers. 24. THEY ALSO EXECUTED JUDGMENTS IGNOMINIOUSLY UPON JOASH) That is, the Syrians tormented him severely: every vengeance is signified by the name of judgment among the Hebrews. This interpreter added that word ignominiously beyond the Hebrew.

Latin:

Vers. 24. IN JOAS QVOQVE IGNOMINIOSE EXER- CUERE JUDICIA) Id est, graviter illum Syri torserunt: omnis vindicta judicii nomine apud Hebræos significatur. Illud ignominiose præter Hebræum addidit hic interpres.

## 25:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXV.

Amaziah avenges the death of his father Joash, conquers the Edomites, but because of idolatry is defeated by Joash of Israel and is slaughtered by his own people.

Latin:

CAPUT XXV.

Amasias necem Joas Patris ulciscitur, Idumæos vincit, sed ob idololatriam a Joaso Israelitico profligatur & a suis trucidatur.

## 25:6
Vers. 6. HE ALSO HIRED FOR A PRICE ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND VALIANT MEN FROM ISRAEL) Amaziah sinned twice, first because he entered into an alliance with the ten tribes, against the prohibition of the prophet Azariah above in verse 15; then because he attacked them in war when he himself was not provoked, against the prohibition of God 1 Kings 12:24. He ought to have left them to their own discords, and to have repelled the war if it were brought by them.

Concerning the price, some raise a doubt. Juan de Mariana thinks this money was spent only on the military tribunes, so that the soldiers had to live off the plunder: But that price would have been very small for the tribunes, if indeed only 150 Joachimics had been paid to each commander of a thousand: and a much larger sum appears according to the Mosaic value of a talent, namely not only 15,000 as Mariana wishes, but 150,000 Joachimics appears: whence each of the common soldiers could have received a Joachimic, and half a ton of gold could be distributed among the commanders of a thousand and other officials, und diss ist nur das Lauffgeld gewesen.

Latin:

Vers. 6. MERCEDE QVOQVE CONDUXIT DE ISRAEL CENTUM MILLIA ROBUSTORUM) Bis pec- cavit Amasias, Iprius quod societatem cum decem tribubus iniit, contra interdictum Prophetæ Azariæ supra 15. deinde quod eos bello impetivit ipse non lacesitus, contra interdi- ctum Dei 1. Reg. 12, 24. Debuerat illos suis discordiis relin- quere, & bellum, si ab illis inferretur, repellere.

DE pretio nonnulli dubium movent. Job. Ma- riana censet hanc pecuniam tantum in tribu- nos militum impensam, ut militibus ex præda victi- tandum fuerit: Sed perexiguum fuisset illud pro tribunis pretium, si nempe Chiliarcho tantum 150. Joachimici numerati fuissent: & longe grandior prodit summa juxta valorem talenti Mosaïcum, nimirum non 15000. tantum ut Mariana vult, sed 150000. Joachimicorum prodit: unde vulgarium militum quisque Joachimicum accipere potuit, & dimidia auri tonna in Chiliarchas & alios officiales distribui, und diss ist nur das Lauffgeld gewesen.

## 25:7
Vers. 7. BUT A MAN OF GOD CAME TO HIM) Is it Amos the father of Isaiah, as the Hebrews think?

Latin:

Vers. 7. VENIT AUTEM HOMO DEI AD ILLUM) An Amos pater Esaiæ, ut sentiunt Hebræi?

## 25:9
Vers. 9. THE LORD HAS WHEREWITH HE CAN GIVE THEE MUCH MORE THAN THESE) He is sufficiently rich, who is impoverished for the sake of God.

Latin:

Vers. 9. HABET DOMINUS UNDE TIBI DARE POS- SIT MULTO HIS PLURA) Satis dives est, qui Dei causa pauperatur.

## 25:12
TO THE PRECIPICE OF A CERTAIN ROCK) Of that from which the city of Arabia, Petra, has its name. Josephus here. See 2 Kings 14:7.

Latin:

Vers. 12. AD PRÆRUPTUM CUJUSDAM PETRÆ) Illius à quo nomen habet urbs Arabiæ Petra. Josephus hic. Vid. 2. Reg. 14, 7.

## 25:16
ARE YOU NOT THE KING'S COUNSELOR) He certainly was, and indeed given to the King by God. He did nothing foreign to his office. See Jeremiah 1:10.

Latin:

Vers. 16. NON CONSILIARIUS REGIS ES) Sane erat, & quidem à Deo Regi datus. Nihil faciebat alienum à suo munere. Vid. Jerem. 1, 10.

## 25:20
AMAZIAH WOULD NOT LISTEN, BECAUSE IT WAS THE WILL OF THE LORD THAT HE BE DELIVERED INTO THE HANDS OF THE ENEMIES) Whom God wishes to destroy, He blinds their mind.

Latin:

Vers. 20. NOLUIT AUDIRE AMASIAS, EO QVOD DOMINI ESSET VOLUNTAS UT TRADATUR IN MANUS HOSTIUM) Quod Deus vult perdere, eis mentem excæcat.

## 25:24
AND WITH OBED-EDOM) Understand his descendants, who are called here by the name of their progenitor. Thus we say Israel, Judah, and others.

Latin:

ET APUD OBEDEDOM) Posteros ejus intellige, qui progenitoris nomine hîc appellantur. Sic dicimus Israelem, Judam, aliaque.

## 26:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVI.

Uzziah, worshiping God, overcomes enemies, fortifies cities, and flourishes: burning incense, he is struck with leprosy.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVI.

Usias Deum colens superat hostes, munit urbes, & floret: Incensum adolens lepra percutitur.

## 26:4
AND HE DID WHAT WAS RIGHT IN THE EYES OF THE LORD, ACCORDING TO ALL THAT HIS FATHER AMAZIAH HAD DONE) That is, he followed the law in his deeds, yet not with solid piety: above 25:2.

Latin:

Vers. 4. FECITQVE QVOD ERAT RECTVM IN OCVLIS DOMINI, JVXTA OMNIA QVÆ FECERAT AMASIAS PATER EJVS) Id est, factis legem secutus est non tamen solida pietate: supra 25, 2.

## 26:5
IN THE DAYS OF ZECHARIAH, WHO HAD UNDERSTANDING IN THE VISIONS OF GOD) In the Hebrew: understanding in the visions of God: that is, skilled in explaining the prophecies of the ancients, this is ἑρμηνεία ἀποκαλύψεων, 1 Corinthians 14:26.

Latin:

Vers. 5. IN DIEBVS ZACHARIÆ INTELLIGENTIS ET VIDENTIS DEVM) In Hebræo: intelligentis in visionibus Dei: id est, periti in explicandis veterum prophetiis, hæc est ἑρμηνεία ἀποκαλύψεων, 1. Cor. 14, 26.

## 26:6
HE BROKE DOWN THE WALL OF GATH) If we rightly consider these things and what follows in order up to verse 15, we shall see that this King was well skilled not only in agriculture, which is mentioned below, but also in military affairs, and was solicitous for the safety of his people. For he destroyed the fortifications of the enemies on the border, and well fortified his own boundaries with works, garrisons, arms, and engines.

Latin:

Vers. 6. DESTRVXIT MVRVM GETH) Si hæc & quæ sequuntur deinceps ad comma usque 15. recte consideremus, videbimus hunc Regem non tantum agriculturæ, quod infra dicitur, sed & rei bellicæ fuisse bene peritum, & pro populi sui salute sollicitum. Nam hostium in limite munimenta destruxit, suos fines bene munit, operibus, præsidiis, armis, machinis.

## 26:15
WHICH HE PLACED IN THE TOWERS AND IN THE CORNERS OF THE WALLS) Very well Vegetius, book 4, chapter 2. The ancients did not want the circuit of a wall to be drawn straight, lest it be disposed to the blow of a battering ram, but they enclosed cities with winding curves, having laid the foundations, and they built more frequent towers at the very corners for this reason, because if anyone should wish to bring either ladders or engines to a wall constructed with such an arrangement, he is overwhelmed not only from the front, but also from the sides, and almost from the rear, as if enclosed in a bay. Tacitus in his description of Jerusalem: But they had strengthened the city, steep in its situation, with works and masses, by which even the level ground might be sufficiently fortified. For walls, oblique in height or curved inward, enclosed two hills of immense height, so that the sides of the attackers might be exposed to blows. Valer. Flaccus, where he describes the siege of the same city under Titus: - - - The brother, black with Solyman dust, scattering torches and raging in every tower.

Latin:

Vers. 15. QVAS IN TVRRIBVS COLLOCAVIT ET IN ANGVLIS MVRORVM) Bene admodum Vegetius libro 4. cap. 2. Ambitum muri directum veteres duci noluerunt, ne ad ictum arietis esset dispositus, sed sinuosis anfractibus, jactis fundamentis, clausere urbes, crebrioresque turres in ipsis angulis ediderunt propterea, quia si quis ad murum tali ordinatione constructum, vel scalas vel machinas voluerit admovere, non solum à fronte, sed etiam à lateribus, & prope à tergo, veluti in sinum circumclusus opprimitur. Tacitus in descriptione Hierosolymorum: Sed urbem arduam situ opera molesque firmaverant, queis vel plana satis munirentur. Nam duos colles immensum editos claudebant muri per altum obliqui, aut introrsus sinuati, ut latera oppugnantium ad ictus patescerent. Valer. Flaccus ubi ejusdem urbis sub Tito oppugnationem describit: - - - Solymo nigrantem pulvere fratrem Spargentemque faces & in omni turre furentem.

## 26:18
IT IS NOT YOUR OFFICE, UZZIAH, TO BURN INCENSE TO THE LORD, BUT THAT OF THE PRIESTS, THAT IS, THE SONS OF AARON) By the law, Exodus 30:7, 38. It was the King's duty not to burn it, but to see that the Priests burned it. See below 27:2.

Latin:

Vers. 18. NON TVI OFFICII, OZIA, VT ADOLEAS INCENSVM DOMINO, SED SACERDOTVM, HOC EST FILIORVM AARON) Ex lege Exod. 30, 7. 38. Regis erat non adolere, sed facere ut Sacerdotes adolerent. Vide infra 27, 2.

## 26:20
Vers. 20. AND THEY HASTILY EXPELLED HIM) In the Hebrew it is: they made to hasten: the Greeks not otherwise: κατέσπευσαν ἀυτὸν ἐκεῖθεν. They did not use force, but warnings from the law which did not want lepers to be seen in the city, much less in the Temple. The following words confirm this interpretation. And he himself also, terrified, hastened to go out: namely, lest he should offend God more gravely.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET FESTINATO EXPVLERVNT EVM) In Hebræo est: festinare fecerunt: Græci non aliter: κατέσπευσαν ἀυτὸν ἐκεῖθεν. Non vi usi sunt, sed monitis ex lege quæ leprosos in urbe, nedum in Templo, conspici nolebat. Hanc interpretationem firmant sequentia. Et ipse etiam perterritus acceleravit egredi: nempe ne Deum gravius offenderet.

## 26:21
Vers. 21. HE DWELT IN A SEPARATE HOUSE) Outside cities and towns, as the law of Moses commands, to which even Kings were subject, unless equity dictated an exception somewhere.

Latin:

Vers. 21. HABITAVIT IN DOMO SEPARATA) Extra urbes & oppida, ut lex Mosis jubet, cui & Reges suberant, nisi sicubi æquitas exceptionem dictaret.

## 26:22
Vers. 22. HE RULED THE KING'S HOUSE.

The son of Jotham was in charge of the royal court and household, he judged the people of the land, performing the duties of the King, yet not usurping the dignity or the name of King while his father was alive, which was his praiseworthy piety and modesty.

Latin:

Vers. 22. REXIT DOMUM REGIS.

Filius Jotham aulæ & familiæ Regiæ præfuit, judicavit populum terræ, officia Regis faciens, nec tamen vivo Patre dignitatem, aut nomen Regis usurpans, quæ laudabilis ejus pietas & modestia fuit.

## 26:23
Vers. 23. THE REST OF THE WORDS.

More correctly, of the former and latter deeds of Uzziah, which he performed in the beginning, middle, or end of his government, worthy of memory, Isaiah wrote, whose historical book seems to some not to exist any longer, but it will be spoken of in the preface to Isaiah.

Latin:

Vers. 23. RELIQUA SERMONUM.

Rectius gestorum Oziæ priorum & novissimorum, quæ vel initio, vel medio, vel fine gubernationis ἀξιομνημόνευτα egit, scripsit Esaias, qui liber ejus Historicus non extare amplius quibusdam videtur, sed de eo dicetur præfat. ad Esa.

## 27:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVII.

Jotham succeeds Uzziah as a pious King: His buildings and successful battle against the Ammonites, whom he made tributary to himself.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVII.

Ozia succedit Jotham Rex pius: Ejus ædificia & pugna felix contra Ammonitas, quos sibi tributarios fecit.

## 27:3
Vers. 3. AND ON THE WALL OF OPHEL HE BUILT MUCH) So also the Greeks. It seems to signify certain gorges or narrow places, whence that word is elsewhere translated as dark and a secret place: and by similarity the part of the human body through which excretion occurs is so called, as 1 Sam. 5, 6. 9. 12. c. 6, 4. 5.

Others render it on the wall of the citadel, as Osiander: Junius and Tremellius on the wall of the slope, or the higher parts of Jerusalem after the torrent, c. 33, 15. Neh. 3, 26 27. c. 11, 21. So also Piscator. B. Luther, with the Vulgate and the LXX, retain it as a proper name: which is also approved by Amama and Cornelius a Lapide; this tower in Jerusalem, he says, was so high that one's eyes would grow dizzy looking from its summit. See Adrichom. in the description of Jerusalem n. 55.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ET IN MVRO OPHEL MVLTA CONSTRVXIT) Sic & Græci. Videtur significare fauces quasdem sive angustias, unde σκοτεινὸν & ἄδυτον alibi ea vox vertitur: & per similitudinem sic appellatur pars humani corporis per quam fit egestio, ut 1. Sam. 5, 6. 9. 12. c. 6, 4. 5.

ALii reddunt in muro arcis ut Osiander: Junius & Tremellius in muro clivi, seu editioris partes Jerusalem post torrentem, c. 33, 15. Neh. 3, 26 27. c. 11, 21. Sic & Piscator. B. Luther. cum vulg. & LXX. nomen proprium retinent: quod probatur etiam Amama Cornel. a Lapide, erat, inquit, haec turris in Jerusalem adeo excelsa, ut in culmine ejus aspiciendo caligarent oculi. Vid. Adrichom. in descript. Jerusalem n. 55.

## 27:6
Vers. 6. AND JOTHAM WAS STRENGTHENED) He acted prosperously.

Latin:

Vers. 6. CORROBORATUSQVE EST JOATHAM) Prospere egit.

## 27:7
Vers. 7. AND ALL HIS WARS) Against the Syrians and the ten tribes 2 Kings 15, 37.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ET OMNES PUGNÆ EJUS) Contra Syros & decem tribus 2. Reg. 15, 37.

## 28:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXVIII.

Because of the sins of Ahaz, Judea was handed over to be plundered by the Syrians, Israelites, Edomites, and Philistines: Hezekiah succeeds Ahaz.

Latin:

CAPUT XXVIII.

Ob peccata Achaz Judæa diripienda tradita Syris, Israelitis, Idumæis, Philistæis: Achazo succedit Ezechias.

## 28:3
Ver. 3. IN THE VALLEY OF BEN-HINNOM) Which is also Gihinnom, that is, the Valley of Hinnom, whence the name of Gehenna for signifying the torments of the other life.

AND HE CAUSED HIS SONS TO PASS THROUGH THE FIRE) The word העביר is ambiguous. For it can signify both consumption and passing through: the Greeks here [use] διῆγε: we have treated of both meanings at Deut. 18, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 3. IN VALLE BENENNOM) Quæ & Gihinnom, id est, Vallis Hinnomi, unde gehennæ nomen ad significanda tormenta vitæ alterius.

ET ILLUSTRAVIT FILIOS SUOS IN IGNE) Vox העביר est ambigua. Nam & consumtionem & transitum significare potest: Græci hic διῆγε: de utroque significatu egimus ad Deuter. 18, 10.

## 28:4
Ver. 4. AND UNDER EVERY LEAFY TREE) The nations neighboring the Hebrews performed sacred rites not only in groves, but also under large trees. Deut. 12, 2.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET SUB OMNI LIGNO FRONDOSO) Non in lucis tantum, sed & sub magnis arboribus sacra faciebant gentes Hebræis vicinæ. Deut. 12, 2.

## 28:5
Ver. 5. INTO THE HANDS OF THE KING OF SYRIA) This happened later than what is narrated in 2 Kings 16, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 5. IN MANUS REGIS STRIÆ) Posteriùs id accidit quam quod narratur 2. Reg. 16, 5.

## 28:7
Ver. 7. ALSO ELKANAH THE SECOND TO THE KING) The LXX [render it] τὸν διάδοχον τῆ βασιλέως.

Latin:

Vers. 7. ELCANAM QVOQVE SECUNDUM A REGE) LXX. τὸν διάδοχον τῆ βασιλέως.

## 28:9
Ver. 9. YOU HAVE SLAIN THEM CRUELLY) Wars with fellow countrymen should be waged more leniently than with foreigners.

Latin:

Vers. 9. OCCIDISTIS EOS ATROCITER) Bella cum popularibus, quam cum externis lenius gerenda.

## 28:10
Ver. 10. FOR MALE AND FEMALE SLAVES) You treat them as foreign chattel.

WHICH THERE IS NO NEED TO DO, FOR YOU HAVE SINNED AGAINST THIS THE LORD YOUR GOD) In the Hebrew: Are there not truly with you sins against your God? He began the speech as if he were going to say 'you have sinned': but he changed the construction according to the sense; he indicates that they had sinned against the law of Deut. 15, 12. 43.

Latin:

Vers. 10. IN SERVOS ET ANCILLAS) Vt mancipia extranea illos habetis.

QVOD NEQVAQVAM FACTO OPUS EST, PECCASTIS ENIM SUPER HOC DOMINO DEO VESTRO) In Hebræo: Nonne vere vos, vobiscum peccata contra Deum vestrum? Ita incepit sermonem quasi dicturus esset vos peccastis: sed mutavit constructionem κατὰ τὸ σημαινόμενον, Peccasse eos indicat contra legem Deut. 15, 12. 43.

## 28:14
Ver. 14. AND THE ARMED MEN LEFT THE SPOIL AND ALL THAT THEY HAD TAKEN) A sign of repentance; they did more than they were ordered: for they both immediately released the captives and returned the things taken in war.

Latin:

Vers. 14. DIMISERANTQVE VIRI BELLATORES PRÆDAM ET UNIVERSA QVÆ CEPERANT) Insignum pœnitentiæ plus fecere quam jussi erant: nam & captivos statim dimiserunt, & res bello captas reddiderunt.

## 28:15
Ver. 15. AND HAD ANOINTED THEM BECAUSE OF THE LABOR) Anointing relieves fatigue: Celsus notes this in book 1, ch. 3.

The remarkable humanity of the Israelites toward the Judeans, even though they were enemies; they clothe them, refresh them with food, and furthermore anoint them. Clemency is more powerful than vehemence, said King Antigonus of Macedon, according to Plutarch.

Latin:

Vers. 15. UNXISSENTQVE PROPTER LABOREM) Fatigationi subvenit unctio: notat Celsus libro 1. c. 3.

Insignis Israëlitarum erga Judæos humanitas, utut hostes essent, vestiunt eos, cibo reficiunt, & insuper ungunt. Clementia plus potest, quam vehementia, dicebat Antigonus Rex Macedon. apud Plutarch.

## 28:19
Ver. 19. BECAUSE OF AHAZ KING OF ISRAEL,

It seems to some that he is so called because of certain ones from the 10 tribes who had formerly come to Asa in a great multitude on account of successfully managed affairs, 2 Chron. 15:9, who had also adhered to his descendants, chap. 21:4, or because he was King of Israel by right from the days of David and Solomon, just as princes and kings today bear titles of lands even if they do not possess them in fact: namely, that they have a right not in the thing, but to the thing, as they say: unless we prefer to say that he is called King of Israel synecdochically, because the two tribes belonged to the 12 tribes of Israel.

Latin:

Vers. 19. PROPTER ACHAZ REGEM ISRAEL,

Ita vocari quibusdam videtur propter quosdam ex 10. tribubus, qui olim ad Assarn magna multitudine ob res feliciter gestas accesserant 2. Chron. 15, 9. qui etiam posteris ejus adhæserant cap. 21, 4. vel quod Rex Israëlis fuerit de jure inde a Davidis, & Salomonis diebus, uti hodieque principes, & Reges titulos gerunt terrarum, etsi eas de facto non possideant: nimirum quod jus habeant non in re, sed ad rem, ut loquuntur: nisi malimus dicere, quod Synecdochice vocetur Rex Israëlis, quia duæ tribus pertinebant ad tribus 12. Israëlis.

## 28:20
Ver. 20. AND BROUGHT AGAINST HIM THELGATHPILNESER KING OF ASSYRIA, WHO BOTH AFFLICTED HIM AND, WITH NO ONE RESISTING, DEVASTATED HIM) These things do not agree well with the history in 2 Kings 16:7, 8, 9. Wherefore learned men think that לו is placed here for על, as in Gen. 38:22 and elsewhere. Furthermore, that the two letters לא are redundant here, so that the sense may be: And Thelgathpilneser king of Assyria came to him, and he will sustain him when he is placed in straits: and if we accept that, then in the following verse לו must also be deleted.

It is not in our power to delete entire words in the sacred text: this is excessive audacity, if it is not sacrilege. There is no conflict in the passages that are compared here: in the book of Kings it is said that the King of Assyria came to his aid at the petition of Ahaz, which is not denied in this passage; there it is added that on that occasion he acted for his own interests, and captured Damascus, and its people transferred to Kir, which does not contradict what is indicated here, namely that he did not much benefit Ahaz with his help, the occupation of Damascus, and the deportation of the people, nor did he assist him as was fitting in recovering the cities from the Philistines; indeed, he was more of a burden to him than a source of strength. Often those who come to help do not so much bring aid as they are a burden, and they devastate the lands of their allies and exhaust their treasuries, as experience, the teacher of things, bears witness.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ADDUXITQVE CONTRA EUM THELGATHPHELNASAR REGEM ASSTRIORUM, QVI ET AFFLIXIT EUM, ET NULLO RESISTENTE VASTAVIT) Non bene conveniunt hæc cum historia 2. Reg. 16, 7. 8. 9. Quare putant eruditi לו hic positum pro על, ut Gen. 38. v. 22. & alibi. Præterea duas literas לא hic abundare, ut sensus sit: Et venit ad eum Thelgathphelnasar rex Assyriæ, & ipsum in angustiis constitutum sustentabit: quod si recipimus, etiam versu sequente delendum erit לו.

Non est in nostro arbitrio delere voces integras in textu sacro: audacia hæc nimia, si non sacrilegium est. Nulla in locis, quæ hic committuntur, pugna: In libro Regum dicitur Rex Assur ad petitionem Achasi in auxilium ei venisse: quod non negatur in hoc loco: illic additur, quod ea occasione τὰ ἴδια egerit, ac Damascum ceperit, & populum ejus transtulerit in Cir, quod non repugnat illi, quod hic indicatur, quod nempe non multum Achaso pro- fuerit suo auxilio, Damasci occupatione, populi de- portatione, neque ut par erat, juverit ad urbes a Phi- listeis recuperatas, imo oneri potius ei fuerit, quam ipsum roborarit. Sæpe illi qui in auxilium veniunt, non tam suppetias ferunt, quam oneri sunt, terrasq; confœderatorum devastant, & Thesauros eorum exhauriunt, teste rerum Magistra experientia.

## 28:22
Verse 22. KING AHAZ HIMSELF SACRIFICED TO THE GODS OF DAMASCUS] In the Hebrew, that 'King Ahaz himself' ends the preceding period, and Kimchi notes that that הוא is often said with contempt, as in Gen. 36, last verse, Num. 26, 9. Kimchi adds the passage Gen. 5, 5, Esther 1, 1, concerning which there may be doubt.

Latin:

Vers. 22. IPSE PER SE REX ACHAZ IMMOLAVIT DIIS DAMASCI] In Hebræo illud ipse Rex Achaz finit præ- cedentem periodum, & notat Kimchi illud הוא sæpe cum despectu dici, ut Gen. 36. ult. Num. 26, 9. Addit Kimchi lo- cum Gen. 5, 5. Esther. 1, 1. de quibus dubitari potest.

## 28:24
Verse 24. HE SHUT THE DOORS OF THE HOUSE OF GOD) So that sacred rites might be performed anywhere rather than in the legitimate place, below 29, 7. His son opened those doors, below 29, 3.

Latin:

Vers. 24. CLAUSIT JANUAS TEMPLI DEI) Ut sacra ubivis potius quam in loco legitimo peragerentur infra 29, 7. Eas fores aperuit filius infra 29,3.

## 29:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXIX. Hezekiah, the most pious son and successor of the impious Ahaz, restores divine worship and, with the temple restored, offers many sacrifices.

Latin:

CAPUT XXIX. Achazi impii successor filius pientissimus Ezechias re- staurat cultum divinum & restaurato templo mul- tas offert victimas.

## 29:3
Verse 3. HE OPENED THE DOORS.

Regarding the repair, some, Junius and Tremellius, understand it as the words sound, that he opened the doors of the porch and of the whole house which his father had shut, ch. 28, 24. (Compare this chapter, v. 7.)

Latin:

Vers. 3. APERUIT VALVAS.

DE reparatione nonnulli, Junius & Tremell. ut sonant verba intelligunt, quod fores porti- cus, & totius domus quas occluserat Pater, c. 28, 24. (Conf. hoc cap. v. 7.) aperuerit.

## 29:5
Verse 5. CARRY OUT ALL THE UNCLEANNESS FROM THE SANCTUARY) Everything that pertains to idolatry. No sooner said than done. And this change for the better was all the more remarkable: below 36.

Latin:

Vers. 5. AUFERTE OMNEM IMMUNDITIAM A SANCTUARIO) Omnia quæ ad idololatriam pertinent. Simul d'ctum simul factum. Eoque insignior fuit hæc in melius mutatio: infra 36.

## 29:8
Verse 8. AND HE DELIVERED THEM TO COMMOTION AND DESTRUCTION) In the Hebrew: to commotion and astonishment. The Greeks: εἰς ἔκστασιν καὶ εἰς ἀφανισμὸν: that is, he sent panic terrors upon them, as above 25, 22.

Latin:

Vers. 8. TRADIDITQVE EOS IN COMMOTIO- NEM ET INTERITUM) In Hebræo: in commotionem & stuporem. Græci: εἰς ἔκστασιν καὶ εἰς ἀφανισμὸν: id est, ter- rores illis panicos immisit, ut supra 25,22.

## 29:16
Verse 16. TO THE BROOK KIDRON) Into Topheth, or the valley of Hinnom: as 2 Kings 23, 10. 12.

Latin:

Vers. 16. AD TORRENTEM CEDRON) In Topheth, sive vallem Hinnomi: ut 2. Reg. 23, 10. 12.

## 29:21
Verse 21. AND SEVEN GOATS FOR A SIN OFFERING) Seven goats because of the multitude and the long duration of the sins. The number seven is proper to sacred things.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET HIRCOS SEPTEM PRO PECCATO) Septem hircos ob multitudinem & diuturnitatem peccato- rum. Heptas sacris propria.

## 29:22
Verse 22. THE PRIESTS RECEIVED THE BLOOD, AND SPRINKLED THE BLOOD UPON THE ALTAR] According to the Law, Levit. 8, 15.

Latin:

Vers. 22. SVSCEPERVNT SANGVINEM SACERDO- TES, ET FUDERUNT SUPER ALTARE SANGVI- NEM] Ex Lege Levit. 8, 15.

## 29:23
AND THEY LAID THEIR HANDS UPON THEM] According to the Law, Levit. 8, 22.

Latin:

IMPOSVERVNTQVE MANVS SUAS SVPER EOS] Ex Lege Levit. 8, 22.

## 29:24
VER. 24. THAT A BURNT OFFERING MIGHT BE MADE] Whereby God might be acknowledged as the Lord of all things.

AND FOR SIN) For expiation.

Latin:

Vers. 24. VT HOLOCAVSTVM FIERET] Quo Deus ut omnium rerum Dominus agnosceretur.

ET PRO PECCATO) Ad expiationem.

## 29:25
VER. 25. ACCORDING TO THE DISPOSITION OF DAVID THE KING AND GAD THE SEER AND NATHAN THE PROPHET) 1 Chron. 22, 3. 2 Chron. 8, 14. 23, 18. The King had instituted this with the Prophets approving his counsel.

Latin:

Vers. 25. SECVNDVM DISPOSITIONEM DAVID REGIS ET GAD VIDENTIS ET NATHAN PRO- PHETÆ) 1. Paralipom. 22, 3. 2. Paral. 8, 14. 23, 18. Rex id instituerat approbantibus ejus consilium Prophetis.

## 29:30
VER. 30. DAVID AND ASAPH.

Whence it is evident that the Psalms were composed partly by David, partly by Asaph.

Latin:

Vers. 30. DAVID ET ASSAPH.

Unde constat Psalmos partim a Davide, par- tim ab Assaph esse compositos.

## 29:31
VER. 31. YOU HAVE FILLED YOUR HANDS TO THE LORD] You have consecrated yourselves to the ministry: as Exod. 28, 41.

Latin:

Vers. 31. IMPLESTIS MANVS VESTRAS DOMINO] Consecrastis vos ministerio: ut Exod. 28, 41.

## 29:34
VER. 34. BUT THE PRIESTS WERE FEW, AND COULD NOT SUFFICE TO FLAY THE BURNT OFFERINGS) For that was the duty of the Priests, Levit. 1.

WHENCE ALSO THE LEVITES THEIR BRETHREN HELPED THEM) This is an illustrious example of royal authority (with the Sanhedrin consulted, as is credible) in relaxing the bond of the divine law out of necessity. We have a similar one below 30, 2. 3. This is noted by Maimonides in the Guide for the Perplexed 3, 41.

Latin:

Vers. 34. SACERDOTES VERO PAVCI ERANT, NEC POTERANT SVFFICERE VT PELLES HOLO- CAVSTORVM DETRAHERENT) Id enim Sacerdotum erat, Levit. 1.

VNDE ET LEVITÆ FRATRES EORVM ADJV- VERVNT EOS) Exemplum hoc illustre est auctoritatis regiæ (consulto ut credibile est Synedrio) in relaxando legis divinæ vinculo ex necessitate. Simile habemus infra 30, 2. 3. Notatum hoc Maimonidæ Ductoris dubitantium 3, 41.

## 30:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXX. Hezekiah invites the Jews & Israelites to a solemn Passover, and celebrates it for 14 days after the altars of the idols were overturned.

Latin:

CAPUT XXX. Ezechias invitat Judæos & Israëlitas ad solemne Pa- scha, illudq; eversis idolorum aris per 14. dies celebrat.

## 30:2
VER. 2. THE KING THEREFORE HAVING TAKEN COUNSEL, AND THE PRINCES, AND ALL THE ASSEMBLY OF ISRAEL] See what was said above 1 Chron. 13, 1. Understand by the whole assembly the great synagogue consisting of the Sanhedrin of the nation, of the city senate of Jerusalem, and of some senators called from elsewhere. See what was said at Matth. 10, 17.

BEcause they could not celebrate the Passover in the first month on account of uncleanness by the law of Num. 9, 10, they celebrate it in the second.

Latin:

Vers. 2. INITO ERGO CONSILIO REGIS ET PRIN- CIPVM ET VNIVERSI COETVS ISRAEL] Vide quæ di- cta supra 1. Paral. 13, 1. Vniversum cœtum intellige συναγωγὴν μεγάλην constantem ex Synedrio gentis, ex senatu urbano Hierosolymorum, & ex senatoribus aliquot aliunde evocatis. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. 10, 17.

QVia mense primo celebrare Pascha non pote- rant ob immunditiem vi legis Num. 9, 10. se- cundo id celebrant.

## 30:5
VER. 5. THROUGHOUT ALL ISRAEL) Sent even to the ten tribes, not to command in the King's name, but to remind them also, as being bound to the divine law, of their duty. See presently 2, 25. 26.

FOR MANY HAD NOT DONE AS IT IS PRESCRIBED BY THE LAW] In the Hebrew: For they had not done long ago what is written. They had been excused from this ceremony because of the threatening prohibitions of the Kings, just as formerly because of the continuous journeys through desert lands, Joshua 5.

Latin:

Vers. 5. IN VNIVERSVM ISRAEL) Etiam ad decem tribus missi non qui juberent Regis nomine, sed qui eos quo- que, utpote legi divinæ obstrictos, sui officii commoneface- rent. Vide mox 2, 25. 26.

MVLTI ENIM NON FECERANT SICVT LEGE PRÆSCRIPTVM EST] In Hebræo: Pridem enim non fe- cerant quod fcriptum est. Excusati ab hac ceremonia fuerant ob Regum minacia interdicta, sicut olim ob continua per de- sertas terras itinera Josuæ 5.

## 30:7
Ver. 7 DO NOT BECOME LIKE YOUR FATHERS AND YOUR BRETHREN WHO DEPARTED FROM THE LORD GOD OF THEIR FATHERS, WHO DELIVERED THEM INTO DESTRUCTION] In the Hebrew it is לשׁמה, as above 29, 8. There the LXX translate it ἀφανισμὸν, here ἐρήμωσιν. In two ways the King teaches the Jews to make good use of the calamities of their kinsmen: by taking heed, lest through the same faults they fall into the same evils, and by praying to God that they might be relieved. See the following.

Latin:

Vers. 7 NOLITE FIERI SICVT PATRES VESTRI ET FRATRES QVI RECESSERVNT A DOMINO DEO PATRVM SVORVM, QVI TRADIDIT EOS IN INTE- RITVM] In Hebræo est לשׁמה, ut supra 29, 8. ibi ἀφα- νισμὸν, hîc ἐρήμωσιν vertunt LXX. Duobus modis Rex Judæos docet bene uti consanguineorum calamitatibus: cavendo, ne per easdem culpas in eadem mala incidant, & Deum precan- do ut illi subleventur. Vide sequentia.

## 30:12
Ver. 12. BUT IN JUDA THE HAND OF THE LORD WAS MADE, THAT IT MIGHT GIVE THEM ONE HEART] Similar to Acts 4, 32.

Latin:

Vers. 12. IN JVDA VERO FACTA EST MANVS DO- MINI, VT DARET EI COR VNVM) Simile Act. 4, 32.

## 30:17
Ver. 17. FOR THAT A GREAT MULTITUDE HAD NOT BEEN SANCTIFIED: AND THEREFORE THE LEVITES KILLED THE PHASE FOR THEM THAT HAD NOT COME TO BE SANCTIFIED TO THE LORD] In the Hebrew: For there were many in the assembly who were not sanctified, and the Levites insisted on the immolation of the Passovers, for everyone who was not clean, that they might sanctify them to God. He calls those victims Passovers, which were accustomed to be made on the 14th of the month Nisan, but now, because of the cause which had arisen, they were made on the 14th of the following month. In the first exodus everyone slaughtered a Paschal lamb or kid: but afterwards it was always the duty of the priests, as we learn from Josephus in more than one place, as we noted at Matt. 26, 18. But here by royal authority the Levites were made participants of the priestly office, as above 29, 34.

Latin:

Vers. 17. EO QVOD MVLTA TVRBA SANCTIFICA- TA NON ESSET: ET IDCIRCO IMMOLARENT LE- VITÆ PHASE HIS QVI NON OCCVRRERANT SAN- CTIFICARI DOMINO) In Hebr. Multi enim erant in cœtu, qui non erant sanctificati, & Levitæ insistebant immolationi Pa- schatum, pro omni qui non erat mundus, ut ea sanctificarent Deo. Paschata vocat victimas illas, quæ fieri solebant 14. mensis Ni- san, nunc autem, ob causam, quæ inciderat, fiebant 14. mensis sequentis. In primo exitu quisque mactavit agnum vel hœ- dum Paschalem: postea vero semper id fuit sacerdotum, ut ex Josepho discimus non uno in loco, ut notavimus ad Matth. 26, 18. sed hîc auctoritate regia Levitæ participes facti mune- ris sacerdotalis, ut supra 29, 34.

## 30:18
V. 18. A GREAT PART ALSO OF THE PEOPLE FROM EPHRAIM AND MANASSES AND ISSACHAR AND ZABULON, WHICH HAD NOT BEEN SANCTIFIED, ATE THE PHASE, NOT ACCORDING TO THAT WHICH IS WRITTEN, AND EZECHIAS PRAYED FOR THEM SAYING: THE LORD THE GOOD WILL BE PROPITIOUS TO ALL, WHO WITH THEIR WHOLE HEART SEEK THE LORD THE GOD OF THEIR FATHERS, AND WILL NOT IMPUTE TO THEM THAT THEY ARE LESS SANCTIFIED] Behold another relaxation of the law, Lev. 15, 31. 22, 4. Num. 9, 6. The reason is that that law looked to times when there were not so many unclean as there were now. Ritual institutions easily yield not only to necessity, but also to public utility.

Latin:

V. 18. MAGNA PARS ETIAM POPVLI DE EPHRA- IM ET MANASSE ET ISASCHAR ET ZABVLON, QVÆ SANCTIFICATA NON FVERAT, COMEDIT PHASE, NON JVXTA QVOD SCRIPTVM EST, ET ORAVIT PRO EIS EZECHIA DICENS: DOMINVS BONVS PROPITIABITVR CVNCTIS, QVI IN TOTO CORDE REQVIRVNT DOMINVM DEVM PATRVM SVORVM, ET NON IMPVTABIT EIS QVOD MI- NVS SANCTIFICATI SVNT) Ecce alia relaxatio legis Levit. 15, 31. 22, 4. Num. 9, 6. causa est quod lex ea tempora respexit, quibus non ita multi essent immundi, atque nunc erant. Ritualia instituta facile cedunt non necessitati tan- tum, sed & utilitati publicæ.

## 30:22
Vers. 22. AND EZECHIAS SPOKE TO THE HEART OF ALL THE LEVITES] That is, he addressed them kindly and gently.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ET LOCVTVS EST EZECHIAS AD COR OMNIVM LEVITARVM) Id est, benigne ac blande eos est allocutus.

## 30:26
Vers. 26. IN THAT CITY HAD NOT BEEN. Sc. after Solomon, and since the division of the kingdom there was not such a celebration of the feast with the Israelites joined with Juda.

Latin:

Vers. 26. IN EA VRBE NON FUERAT. Sc. post Salomonem, & a diviso regno tanta non fuit celebritas festi junctis cum Juda Israelitis.

## 30:27
Vers. 27. AND THE PRIESTS AND LEVITES AROSE, BLESSING THE PEOPLE] The priests indeed with extended hand, in solemn words, but the Levites by singing auspicious omens.

Latin:

Vers. 27. SVRREXERVNT AVTEM SACERDOTES ATQVE LEVITÆ, BENEDICENTES POPVLO) Sa- cerdotes quidem extensa manu, verbis solennibus, Levitæ au- tem accinendo fausta omina.

## 31:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXI.

The Jews and Israelites returning from the feast tear down the private idolatrous chapels and altars, Ezechias distributes duties to the Priests and Levites, and provides for their sustenance.

Vers. 1. ALSO IN EPHRAIM AND MANASSES] That is, in those towns which the Kings of Juda had acquired for themselves through wars: for outside the places of their own dominion they did not have the law to break idols, as both the Hebrews and Augustine note on the place Deut. 7 and 12. Thus interpret also what follows concerning the children of Israel. 6.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXI.

Judæi & Israelitæ a festo reduces sacella & altaria idololatrica privata convellunt, Ezechias officia Sa- cerdotibus, & Levitis distribuit, & de victu iisdem prospicit.

Vers. 1. IN EPHRAIM QVOQVE ET MANASSE) Id est, in illis oppidis quæ Reges Juda per bella sibi acquisiverant: nam extra loca suæ ditionis idola frangendi legem non habe- bant, ut notant & Hebræi & Augustinus ad locum Deut. 7. & 12. sic interpretare & quod sequitur de filiis Israel. 6.

## 31:6
Vers. 6. WHICH THEY HAD VOWED TO THE LORD. Cornelius himself corrects the Vulgate from the Hebrew: which had been sanctified to God, sc. from the law Num. 18, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 6. QUÆ VOVERANT DOMINO. COrrigit ipse Cornelius vulgatam ex Ebræo: quæ erant sanctificata Deo, sc. ex lege Num. 18, 8.

## 31:11
Ver. 11. EZECHIAS THEREFORE COMMANDED THAT THEY SHOULD PREPARE STOREHOUSES IN THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) He ordered new chambers to be added to those which Solomon had built. We gather this sense from the Greeks: καὶ εἶπεν Εζεχίας ἑτοιμάσαι πασοφόρια εἰς ὆ικον κυρίε.

Latin:

Vers. 11. PRÆCEPIT IGITVR EZECHIAS VT PRÆ- PARARENT HORREA IN DOMO DOMINI) Novas cellas addi jussit ad eas quas struxerat Salomon. Hunc sen- sum colligimus ex Græcis: κὶι εἶπεν Εζεχίας ἑτοιμάσαι πα- σοφόρια εἰς ὆ικον κυρίε.

## 31:13
Ver. 13. AND THERE WAS OVER THEM) He names the treasurers of the Temple of the greater and lesser rank.

BY THE COMMAND OF EZECHIAS THE KING AND AZARIAS THE HIGH PRIEST] For it is also a part of royal care to ensure that things dedicated to God are rightly administered. See 2 Kings 22.

Latin:

Vers. 13. FVIT AVTEM PRÆFECTVS EORVM) Ga- zophylacas Templi nominat majoris ac minoris gradus.

EX IMPERIO EZECHIÆ REGIS ET AZARIÆ PON- TIFICIS] Nam & regiæ curæ pars est efficere, ut Deo dicata recte administrentur. Vide 2. Reg. 22.

## 31:16
Ver. 16. EXCEPTING THE MALES FROM THREE YEARS OLD. Cornelius corrects this, rendering it thus: besides boys of three years; because these were not excepted, but included, and food was provided for all of them; for all, that is, who entered the house of the Lord: (whence it appears that even three-year-old boys were brought to the temple) Nay, even as many as were reckoned (pertaining to the priestly or Levitical families) to their infants (namely), their wives, sons, and daughters of the whole assembly. See here Osiander correcting the Vulgate from the sources.

Verse 25. WHO HAD STRUCK AMON. In the Hebrew, who had conspired against King Amon.

Latin:

Vers. 16. EXCEPTIS MARIBUS AB ANNIS TRIBUS. Corrigit hæc Cornelius ita reddens præter pueros trium annorum: quod hi non excepti fue- rint, sed inclusi, illisq; omnibus præbita fuerint ali- menta; Omnibus sc. qui ingrediebantur domum Do- mini: (unde apparet, etiam pueros triennes ad tem- plum adductos fuisse) Quin etiam quotquot reputati sunt (pertinentes ad sacerdotales aut Leviticas fa- milias) infantibus (nempe) eorum, uxoribus, filiis, & filiabus eorum totius cœtus. Vid. hic Osiander emendans vulgatam ex fontibus.

Verf. 25. QVI AMON PERCVSSERANT. In Ebræo, qui adversus Regem Amon conjuraverant.

## 32:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXII. Sennacherib, invading Judea, is defeated as to his army by an Angel in response to the prayers of Hezekiah, and is himself killed by his sons. Hezekiah, struck by illness, is healed by Isaiah. Finally, Manasseh succeeds him as he is dying.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXII. Sennacherib Judæam invadens precibus Ezechiæ cæditur, quoad exercitum suum, ab Angelo, & occiditur ipse a filiis. Ezechias morbo percussus sanatur ab Esaia. Tandem morienti succedit Manasses.

## 32:4
Verse 4. THEY STOPPED ALL THE FOUNTAINS AND THE BROOK THAT FLOWED THROUGH THE MIDST OF THE LAND, SAYING: LEST THE KINGS OF THE ASSYRIANS COME, AND FIND ABUNDANCE OF WATER) To deprive the enemy of the use of water is considered among the arts of war. See Frontinus 3, 7, and histories throughout.

In the Hebrew, they are said TO HAVE HIDDEN (namely, with planks and earth thrown over them).

Latin:

Verf. 4. OBTVRAVERVNT CVNCTOS FONTES ET RIVUM QVI FLVEBAT IN MEDIO TERRÆ, DICENTES: NE VENIANT REGES ASSYRIORVM, ET INVENIANT AQVARVM ABVNDANTIAM) Hosti aquarum usum eripere inter belli artes ponitur. Vide Frontinum 3, 7. & historias passim.

In Ebr. OCCULTASSE (asseribus sc. & injecta insuper terra) dicuntur.

## 32:6
Verse 6. BUT ALSO IN THE CITIES OF MANASSEH AND EPHRAIM] See what is above 30, 1.

Latin:

Verf. 6. SED ET IN VRBIBVS MANASSE ET EPHRAIM] Vide quæ supra 30, 1.

## 32:7
Verse 7. ACT MANFULLY) It is the mark of a good commander to inflame the courage of his soldiers in war with words. But it is of the greatest importance if the soldier is persuaded that God favors his arms. Belisarius always does this, in Procopius.

Latin:

Verf. 7. VIRILITER AGITE) Boni imperatoris est in bello militum virtutem verbis accendere. Maximi autem momenti est, si militi persuadeatur Deum ejus armis favere. Facit id semper Belisarius, apud Procopium.

## 32:26
AND HE WAS HUMBLED AFTERWARDS) Nothing is more displeasing to God than pride, which, advancing itself by certain degrees, finally arrives at the contempt of God. Nothing, on the contrary, is more pleasing to God than if men, when compared to God, acknowledge themselves to be things of nothing, and humbly pray for forgiveness even for lighter faults. See Micah 6:8. The Greek maxim is: Zeus is the punisher of those who are too arrogant. Nor is that saying of Philemon to be despised: When you see someone raised to a height, shining brightly and boasting of wealth and lineage, and lifting his brow higher than his fortune, expect swift retribution for him immediately; for he is raised higher, so that he may fall the greater. However, it seems that the fault of Hezekiah was especially that he did not give to God the honor that he owed Him before the Babylonian envoys: below 31.

Others understand it more correctly concerning the portent of the retrocession of the sun and the shadow on the sundial of Ahaz. For that slaughter was notorious.

Latin:

Verf. 36. HVMILIATVSQVE EST POSTEA) Nihil magis Deo displicet quam superbia, quæ per gradus quosdam se promovens tandem ad Dei contemtum pervenit. Nihil contra Deo gratius quam si homines se Deo comparatos res nihili esse agnoscant, & culpas etiam leviores submisse deprecantur. Vide Michæam 6, 8. Græca sententia est: Ὁ Ζεὺς κολασὴς τ᾽ ἄγαν ὑπερφρόνων. Nec spernenda ista Philemonis: Ὅταν ἴδῃς πρὸς ὕψος ἠρμένον τινὰ, Λαμπρῶς τε πλούτῳ καὶ γένει γαυρούμενον, Ὀφρῦν τε μείζω τῆς τύχης ἐπηρκότα, Τούτῳ ταχεῖαν νέμεσιν εὐθὺς προσδόκα· Ἐπαίρεται γὰρ μεῖζον, ἵνα μεῖζον πέσῃ. Videtur autem ea maxime fuisse culpa Ezechiæ, quod coram Legatis Babyloniis honorem Deo quem debebat non habuerit: infra 31.

Rectius alii de portento retrocessionis solis & umbræ in Horologio Achazi intelligunt. Nam strages illa erat notoria.

## 32:33
HE MADE ALL WHO WERE REMAINING IN ISRAEL SERVE THE LORD THEIR GOD] He restrained the people as much as he could, so that they would not commit anything openly against the law. Otherwise, the depravity of the people began to grow from this time. Jer. 3:3, 5; 25:1; Ezek. 4:6.

Latin:

Verf. 33. FECIT OMNES QVI RESIDVI ERANT IN ISRAEL SERVIRE DOMINO DEO SVO] Quantum potuit repressit populum, ne palam quid in legem committeret. Alioqui populi depravatio ab hoc tempore cœpit, gliscere. Jerem. 3, 3. 5. 25, 1. Ezech. 4, 6.

## 33:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIII. Manasseh, on account of idolatry, is bound and led away to Babylon: but repenting, he is restored to his kingdom and restores the worship of GOD. His impious son Amon succeeds him, and to him succeeds the pious Josiah.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIII. Manasses ob idololatriam vinctus in Babylonem traducitur: at pœnitens regno restituitur, & cultum DEI restaurat. Succedit ei impius filius Amon, huic vero pius Josias.

## 33:3
TO THE LEVITES ALSO, TO WHOSE INSTRUCTION ALL ISRAEL WAS SANCTIFIED TO THE LORD, HE SPOKE] He reads המבינים. Other codices have המבינים, to the Levites, whose task it was to prepare sacred things for the use of Israel: which coheres well with what follows. Nor do the Greeks read it otherwise, although they translate it differently, namely, as 'mighty ones'. For that participle also has that meaning.

Latin:

Verf. 3. LEVITIS QVOQVE, AD QVORVM ERVDITIONEM OMNIS ISRAEL SANCTIFICABATVR DOMINO, LOCVTVS EST] Legit המבינים. Alii Codd. habent המבינים, Levitis, quorum erat præparare in usum Israelis res sacras: quod cum sequentibus bene cohæret. Nec aliter legere Græci, quanquam aliter vertunt, nempe δυνατοὶ. Habet enim participium illud etiam istam significationem.

## 33:5
IN THE TWO COURTS OF THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) In the court of Israel and in the court of the Gentiles. Thus the Hebrews.

Latin:

Verf. 5. IN DVOBVS ATRIIS DOMVS DOMINI) In atrio Israelis & in atrio gentium. Sic Hebræi.

## 33:14
AS FAR AS OPHEL) See 27:3.

Latin:

Verf. 14. VSQVE AD OPHEL) Vide 27, 3.

## 33:15
AND HE TOOK AWAY THE STRANGE GODS, AND THE IMAGE FROM THE HOUSE OF THE LORD) It could be said of him, he who purifies and cleanses.

Latin:

Verf. 15. ET ABSTVLIT DEOS ALIENOS, ET SIMVLACRVM DE DOMO DOMINI) Dici de eo poterat, ὁ τεώτας καὶ ἰδάσας.

## 33:17
Verf. 17. NEVERTHELESS THE PEOPLE SACRIFICED IN THE HIGH PLACES TO THE LORD THEIR GOD) Yet a few traces of the ancient fraud remained. MANY OF THE PEOPLE WORSHIPPED THE TRUE GOD) But in illicit places.

Latin:

Verf. 17. ATTAMEN POPVLVS IMMOLABAT IN EXCELSIS DOMINO DEO SVO) Pauca tamen priscæ suberant vestigia fraudis. MVLTI DE POPVLO DEVM VERVM COLEBANT) Sed in locis illicitis.

## 33:19
Verf. 19. TRESPASS( מעלו which the Greeks translate as ἀποτάσεις ἀυτοῦ.

IN THE SAYINGS OF HOZAI) The Greeks take חוזי as a common noun: for they translate it as ἐπὶ τ λογων τ᾽ ὁρώντων, that is, in the writings of the Prophets. The same name above 19,2. 29,20. 35,15. interpreters translate as prophet.

Latin:

Verf. 19. CONTEMTVS( מעלו quod Græci vertunt ἀποτάσεις ἀυτοῦ.

IN SERMONIBVS HOZAI) Græci חוזי sumunt pro communi nomine: vertunt enim ἐπὶ τ λογων τ᾽ ὁρώντων, id est, in scriptis Prophetarum. Idem nomen supra 19,2.29,20.35,15. interpretes vertunt προφήτης.

## 33:20
Verf. 20. AT CARCHEMISH] Some think it is Cercusium in Ammianus, book 23.

Latin:

Verf. 20. IN CHARCAMIS] Putant quidam esse Cercusiam apud Ammianum l. 23.

## 33:20
Verf. 20. AND THEY BURIED HIM IN HIS OWN HOUSE] In some garden: not in the sepulchres of the Kings.

Latin:

Verf. 20. ET SEPELIERVNT EVM IN DOMO SVA] In horto aliquo: non in sepulchris Regum.

## 33:23
Verf. 23. AND HE HUMBLED NOT HIMSELF BEFORE THE LORD. In Hebrew: And he did not humble himself before God as his father Manasseh had humbled himself, and he committed many greater offenses. In Hebrew: and he multiplied transgressions: that is to say, he indeed imitated his parent's sins, and surpassed them, but he did not imitate his humble conversion.

Latin:

Verf. 23. ET NON REVERITUS EST FACIEM DOMINI. In Ebr. Et non humiliavit se coram Deo sicut humiliaverat se Manasses Pater ejus, & multa majora deliquit. In Ebr. & multiplicavit delicta: q. d. imitatus quidem est parentis peccata, eademque superavit, sed non imitatus est ejusdem humilem conversionem.

## 33:24
Verse 24. JEREMIAH, ESPECIALLY HE WHOM ALL MALE AND FEMALE SINGERS UNTO THE PRESENT DAY EXPLAIN AS LAMENTATIONS OVER JOSIAH) Jeremiah was therefore to the Hebrews what Simonides was once to the Greeks, of whom Catullus says: More sad than Simonidean tears; And Horace: You might rehearse the duties of a Cean dirge. But this dirge of Jeremiah was different from that which we have concerning the destruction of the city. Yet this lamentation seems to be contained in no few passages at the end of the Lamentations of Jeremiah, as held by the Chaldean, Josephus, and the Hebrews according to Jerome, Lyranus, Tostatus, etc.

Latin:

Verf. 24. JEREMIAS MAXIME CVJVS OMNES CANTORES ATQVE CANTATRICES VSQVE IN PRÆSENTEM DIEM LAMENTATIONES SVPER JOSIAM EXPLICANT) Fuit ergo Jeremias Hebræis quod aliquando post Simonides Græcis, de quo Catullus: Tristius lachrymis Simonideis Et Horatius: Cææ retractes munia næniæ. Alia autem fuit hæc Jeremiæ nænia ab ea quam nos habemus de excidio urbis. Non paucis tamen in fine Threnorum Jeremiæ hæc lamentatio haberi videtur, utpote Chaldæo, Jo- sepho, Ebræis apud Hieronym. Lyrano, Tostato, &c.

## 34:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIV. Josiah cuts down all idolatry, restores the temple and worship of GOD, and renews the covenant with GOD.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIV. Josias omnem idololatriam succidit, DEI templum cultumque instaurat, fœdus cum DEO renovat.

## 34:3
Verse 3. BUT IN THE EIGHTH YEAR OF HIS REIGN, WHILE HE WAS STILL A BOY, HE BEGAN TO SEEK THE GOD OF HIS FATHER DAVID) That is, when he was sixteen years old: a boy, that is, a youth already become capable of royal administration: for the guardianship lasted until the end of the 13th year.

BUT IN THE TWELFTH YEAR AFTER HE HAD BEGUN TO REIGN] When he had already reached his twentieth year of age, and had attained more authority.

Latin:

Verf. 3. OCTAVO AUTEM ANNO REGNI SUI, CUM ADHUC ESSET PUER, CŒPIT QVÆRERE DEUM PATRIS SUI DAVID) Id est, cum annorum esset sexdecim: puer, id est, adolescens jam regiæ administrationis factus compos: nam tutela durabat ad finem anni 13.

DVODECIMO AUTEM ANNO POSTQVAM REGNARE CŒPERAT] Cum jam ad vicesimum ætatis annum pervenisset, & plus auctoritatis esset consecutus.

## 34:5
Verse 5. THE BONES OF THE PRIESTS of idolatry he burned upon the altars of the idols, so that by the contact of the corpses of such impious men the altars themselves might be contaminated, and become an object of horror by that burning done upon them, so that no one might thereafter sacrifice victims upon them.

Latin:

Verf. 5. OSSA SACERDOTUM idololatricorum combussit in altaribus idolorum, ut contactu cadaverum hominum tam impiorum altaria ipsa contaminarentur, & horrori fierent illa combustione in iis facta, ne quis deinceps in iis victimas immolaret.

## 34:15
Verse 15. I HAVE FOUND THE BOOK OF THE LAW. Genebrardus thinks it was the ἀυτόγραφον of Moses formerly placed in the sanctuary.

Latin:

Verf. 15. INVENI LIBRUM LEGIS. Genebrardus putat fuisse ἀυτόγραφον Mosis in sanctuario olim positum.

## 35:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXV. Josiah celebrates the solemn Passover, and having managed affairs brilliantly, by involving himself in an unnecessary war against the King of Egypt, he is struck by an arrow and dies.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXV. Josias Pascha solemne celebrat, rebusque præclare gestis bello non necessario contra Regem Ægypti se immiscens, sagitta ictus occumbit.

## 35:3
AND THE LORD SPOKE TO HIM. By the Prophets, exhorting to repentance.

PUT THE ARK IN THE SANCTUARY.

According to the Hebrews in Jerome, in the time of Manasseh and Amon, it had been taken away from there and moved into the house of Shallum, the husband of Huldah the prophetess, so that, namely, it would not stand together with the idols in the temple.

Latin:

Verf. 10. LOQVVTVSOVE EST DOMINUS AD EUM. Per Prophetas hortans ad pœnitentiam.

Verf. eod. PONITE ARCAM IN SANCTUARIO.

Juxta Ebræos apud Hieronym. tempore Manassis & Ammon inde ablata fuerat & in domum Sellum translata mariti Oldæ prophetissæ, ne sc. simul cum idolis confisteret in templo.

## 35:6
Verf. 5. IMMOLATE THE PASSOVER] Compare what is above 30. פסה Theodotion always translates as φασέκ, not as other interpreters do, πάσχα. The Greek Church, however, received Theodotion's interpretation in Chronicles and certain other books. In the Greek books which we use, the 35th chapter of Chronicles and a large part of the 36th are placed at the beginning of Ezra from the LXX, where it is always πασχα, not φασέκ.

Latin:

Verf. 5. IMMOLATE PHASE] Confer quæ supra 30. פסה semper Theodotion vertit φασέκ, non ut alii interpretes πάσχα. Theodotionis autem interpretationem in Paralipomenis & aliis quibusdam libris recepit Græca Ecclesia. In Græcis quibus utimur libris, initio Esdræ positum est caput 35. Paralipomenon & magna pars 36. ex LXX. ubi semper πασχα non φασέκ.

## 35:21
Verf. 21. WHAT HAVE I TO DO WITH THEE, THOU KING OF JUDA?) There is no controversy between us. Do not seek trouble: καλὸν ἀουχία (quiet is good).

AGAINST ANOTHER HOUSE, TO WHICH GOD HATH COMMANDED ME TO MAKE HASTE) Through Jeremiah, as is credible: for God often gave commands through His Prophets even to Kings who were strangers to true piety, as in 2 Kings 9, 7.

Against another house, the King of the Assyrians 2 Kings 23, 29. whom Tollatus calls Adadremmon: others more correctly call him Nabopolassar, who, having obtained Assyria as King of Babylon, was also rightly called King of Assyria; although Babylonia itself had also once been considered a part of Assyria.

Latin:

Verf. 21. QVID MIHI ET TIBI EST REX JVDA?) Nihil inter nos controversia est. Noli Negotium quærere: καλὸν ἀουχία.

CONTRA ALIAM PVGNO DOMVM, AD QVAM ME DEVS FESTINATO IRE PRÆCEPIT) Per Jeremiam, ut credibile est: nam Deus per Prophetas suos etiam alienis à vera pietate Regibus sæpe dabat mandata, ut 2. Reg. 9, 7.

Contra aliam domum, Regem Assyriorum 2. Reg. 23, 29. quem Adadremmon dicit Tollatus: alii rectius Nabopallassarem, qui Babylonius Rex Assyriam nactus etiam Rex Assyriæ recte vocatus; quanquam & ipsa Babylonia Assyriæ pars olim habita fuerit.

## 36:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXVI.

After Joachaz was carried off by Necho, his brother Jojakim succeeded him; to him his son Jojachim, to him Sedekias, who were carried off by Nebuchadnezzar, who destroyed the city and the temple, so that Judea remained desolate until Cyrus.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXVI.

Joachaz a Nechao abducto frater Jojakim succedit, huic filius Jojachim, huic Sedekias abducti a Ne- bucadnezare, qui urbem & templum destruxit, ut Judæa desolata fuerit usque ad Cyrum.

## 36:9
Verse 9. EIGHT YEARS OLD WAS JOACHIN WHEN HE HAD BEGUN TO REIGN) When his father, who was mentioned above, began to reign. The passage 2 Kings 24:8 requires this sense.

The same reconciliation also pleased the Weimar Paraphrasts. But the explanation of R. David Kimchi, Job. Wolphius, and Cass. Sanctius is to be preferred, as being less forced: Jojakim was eight years old when his father took him as a partner in the kingdom, namely in the second year from the beginning of his reign; but eighteen when he began to govern the kingdom alone. 2 Kings 24:8. Abarbenel, whom Buxtorf praises in Vindiciae Veritatis Hebraicae p. 408, reconciled it still differently, but his exposition is very intricate, therefore we pass it by. Buxtorf in the aforementioned place avoided the suspicion of a corrupt text, which was Capellus's. Grotius did not dare to make it his own in this place. Compare our Biblical Chronology, section 6, question 16.

Latin:

Vers. 9. OCTO ANNORVM ERAT JOACIN CVM REGNARE COEPISSET) Cum regnare inciperet Pater ejus, cujus supra mentio. Hunc sensum postulat locus 2. Reg. 2, 48.

EAdem etiam Conciliatio placuit Vinariensibus Paraphrastis. Sed præferenda R. Davidis Kim- chi, Job. Wolphii, & Cass. Sanctii explicatio, utpote minus coacta: Erat Jojakim octo annorum, cum so- cium sibi Pater ad regnum assumsit, anno sc. ab inito regno secundo; decem tamen, & octo, cum solus re- gnum moderari cœpit. 2. Reg. 24, 8. Aliter adhuc con- ciliavit Abarbenel, quem Buxtorfius laudat in vindic. Verit. Hebr. p. 408. sed admodum intricata ejus est ἔκθεσις, ideo eam præterimus. Corrupti textus suspicionem, quæ Capelli fuit, declinavit l. c. Buxtorfius. Non ausus hoc loco fuit Grotius eam suam facere. Conf. Chr. nostrum Biblic. sect. 6. q. 16,

## 36:13
Verse 13. HE ALSO REBELLED AGAINST KING NEBUCHADNEZZAR WHO HAD ADJURED HIM BY GOD) Faith given even to evil and irreligious princes must be kept: for they are not outside human society: and if an oath is added, as here, God vindicates its violation as an injury to Himself. See what we said in the second book on the Law of War and Peace, ch. 13, § 15, 16; book 3, ch. 19, § 2, 5, and 13.

Latin:

Vers. 13. A REGE QVOQVE NABVCHODONOSOR RECESSIT QVI ADJVRAVERAT EVM PER DEVM) Etiam malis & irreligiosis principibus fides data servanda est: non enim sunt extra humanam societatem: quod si & jusju- randum accesserit, ut hic, ejus violationem Deus ut suam in- juriam vindicat. Vide quæ diximus libro secundo de jure belli ac pacis c. 13. §. 15. 16. l. 3. c. 19. §. 2. 5. & 13.

## 36:20
Verse 20. UNTIL THE KING OF THE PERSIANS SHOULD RULE) Cyrus, who restored the Jews to their homeland.

Latin:

Vers. 20. DONEC IMPERARET REX PERSARVM) Cyrus qui Judæos in patriam restituit.

## 36:21
Verse 21. AND THE LAND SHOULD CELEBRATE ITS SABBATHS) Because the Jews had observed neither the other laws nor that concerning the Sabbatical year; therefore God imposed a long Sabbath, that is, of 70 years, upon the land. See Jer. 25 and 29.

Which 70 years began in the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, when, having been admitted into the partnership of his father's kingdom, he invaded Syria and Judea with his army, and bound King Jojakim in chains to carry him off to Babylon: see above this chapter, v. 6, which happened at the end of the third year and the beginning of the fourth year of Jojakim, 2 Kings 24:1, Dan. 1:1. But those 70 years end in the first year of Cyrus the Monarch, as will now be said.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET CELEBRARET TERRA SABBATA SVA) Quia Judæi tum cæteras leges, tum illam de anno Sabbatico non observaverant; ideo Deus Sabbatum longum, id est, LXX. annorum indixit terræ. Vid. Jer. 25. & 29.

Qui LXX. anni cœperunt primo Nebucadne- zaris, cum sc. in societatem regni Paterni admissus in Syriam & Judæam cum exercitu suo irruit, & Re- gem Jojakimum catenis vincivit, ut in Babyloniam abduceret: supra hoc cap. v. 6. quod factum anno tertio exeunte, quarto ineunte Joachimi 2. Reg. 24. 1. Dan. 1, 1. Finiunt autem anni illi LXX. primo Cyri Monarchæ anno, uti jam dicetur.

## 36:22
Verse 22. BUT IN THE FIRST YEAR OF CYRUS KING OF THE PERSIANS) These words are the same until the end, from where Ezra began the history of his own times. This custom of continuing books is ancient, which Procopius also follows at the end of the Vandalic and the beginning of the Gothic wars.

Concerning this first year of Cyrus, the opinions of chronologists vary.
