It appears from very many names, such as Artabanus, Artavasdes, who is also Artabazus, Artochmes, Artochætes, who is also Artayctus, Artanes, Artagenes, Artaphernes, Artembanes. You may find the name of Artaxerxes in Persia even in the times of the Roman Emperors in Herodian and Lampridius. The same is called Xerxes by Aurelius Victor. From this name, therefore, so common, it cannot be known who this King was, unless arguments of the times are present, which the contentions of the most learned men, who have spent their lives on these matters, show to be obscure to this day. Many wish him to be Cambyses, others Smerdis the Magian. Some wish Esther's husband to be Cambyses, others Darius Hystaspis, others Artaxerxes the Memorian, others Artaxerxes Longimanus. Having read through the laborious and litigious disputes of all these, what is there that anyone can say, especially those who do not have much leisure for these things, except that Terentian line: You have done well: I am much more uncertain than I was a while ago.

CONCERNING this Ahasuerus, the opinions of Chronologers and Interpreters vary greatly indeed: But hardly a more wonderful transformation of a name has come into the mind of anyone than this one to Grotius, who fashions Artaxerxes, or rather Xerxes, out of Ahasuerus. But that must be attributed to a preconceived opinion. Which also drove Scaliger to the point that, although he did not indeed fashion the name of Xerxes out of Ahasuerus, yet, establishing that Ahasuerus is Xerxes, he easily persuaded himself that that name of Ahasuerus is the same as the name ὀξυάρης, and asserted that these names, Ahasuerus or ὀξυάρης, and Xerxes were attributed to the same King, l. 6 de emend. tempor. p. 591, and in the prolegomena p. 41, whom the blessed D. Joh. Behm followed in Manud. Chronol. lib. 2, Tit. 2, c. 7, saying that Xerxes was so named before he succeeded his parent in the kingdom, as if by a private name ὀξυάρης, which the Hebrews can scarcely write otherwise than by אחשורוש. But that metamorphosis of names lacks testimony and example, nor does the opinion regarding Xerxes have a place here. Who the Ahasuerus of Esther is, we shall examine in its proper place. Grotius has proven by no witness that the name Xerxes was a family name for the Kings of the Persians. Nor is the opinion of the scripture here, as to whom he understands by the name Ahasuerus, as uncertain as the varied explanation of the interpreters, provided we attend properly to the words of the divine Historian. For what is clearer than that in the days of Cyrus, King of the Persians, from the time the foundations of the temple were laid, the work of construction was hindered until the reign of Darius, verse 5, and indeed as the time is expressly defined, verse 24, until the second year of the reign of Darius, from which name of Darius while verse 5. and 24, Scaliger, against the most clear letter which speaks of the same King, and against all antiquity, has invented for himself two Dariuses, and has cast himself and his followers into a most serious and intolerable error concerning the temple being built not under Darius Hystaspes, but under Darius Nothus, by which almost the entire Chronology is perverted. He wishes, forsooth, the Darius of v. 5 to be Darius Hystaspes, but the Darius of v. 24 to be Darius Nothus: he claims that under the former the work of the temple's construction was hindered, and under the latter it was promoted. On the contrary, the text clearly defines the limit to which the construction was hindered in the Darius designated in v. 5; it came to pass, therefore, that the people of the land hindered the hands of the people of Judah and troubled them in building. They hired, moreover, against them counselors to frustrate their counsel ALL THE DAYS OF CYRUS King of the Persians, and UNTIL THE REIGN OF DARIUS King of the Persians. Who does not understand here that those hindrances lasted from the Days of Cyrus (after the diploma of liberty) until the reign of Darius 1, that is, he who presided over the empire after Cyrus: this is, Hystaspes, and not beyond his reign, until the reign of Darius 2, or Nothus. For that the followers of Scaliger say that the word ועד AND UNTIL is to be understood not in an exclusive sense, but an INCLUSIVE one, is too frivolous, nor does the speech of the divine Historian allow it: who does not say AND ALL the days of the reign of Darius, but all the Days of Cyrus, AND UNTIL the reign of Darius. And lest there remain a doubt in what year of the reign of that Darius the hindrance of the structure had an end, and the work succeeded again, Ezra adds the year in v. 24. Then the work of the Lord in Jerusalem was interrupted, and it was not done UNTIL THE SECOND YEAR of the reign of DARIUS King of the Persians. Behold an open definition of the year in which that interruption found its end! Furthermore, lest anyone should bring in Xerxes and Artaxerxes Longimanus with Scaliger before the end of the cessation of the structure, or extend it until Darius Nothus, the Holy Spirit has already taken care, while He not only indicated that the work of the structure was checked UNTIL the reign of Darius 1, and no further, or through the whole time of his rule, let alone through the times of the rule of his successors, but He also wished to connect the times of those Kings, under whom the work was hindered, with the Days of Cyrus, so that it might not be ambiguous that the immediate successors of Cyrus were at fault, and He lists under whom and how the structure was hindered in v. 6 seqq. For in the reign of Ahasuerus (the vau is exegetical or causal) in the beginning of his reign, (immediately after the days of Cyrus King of the Persians) they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem. Where the Interpreters troubled. and Chronologists the words added to the name of Ahasuerus (He is Artaxerxes) which are found in certain Latin editions, but are intrusive, and therefore, having been eliminated by the Roman Pontiffs, are no longer read in the vulgate. But that neither Xerxes nor Artaxerxes can be understood by Ahasuerus is manifest, because they did not succeed Cyrus immediately; and why would the Holy Scripture have introduced Xerxes and Artaxerxes immediately after the days of Cyrus, passing over Cambyses and Smerdis as the immediate successors? How, with the limit to which the cessation of the work under the reign of Darius already defined by the words UNTIL the reign of Darius, would He further prolong the hindrance of the work under the successors of Darius, and to the times of the reign of Xerxes and Artaxerxes, to all the Days of their reign, and until the beginning of the Reign of Darius Nothus? Wherefore it is most clear that Ahasuerus is not Xerxes, but the successor of Cyrus, CAMBYSES, which Josephus also teaches, and most of antiquity: who took that name for himself for the sake of greater glory. For Ahasuerus, as Scaliger admits, denotes Great Duke, from Achasch Great, Vau and Rosch Head, and Cambyses was indeed a great Duke and warrior, inasmuch as he subdued all of Egypt with arms. Nor do Lyranus, Vatablus, Munsterus, Lavaterus, and others understand it of any other than Cambyses. To this Ahasuerus, Ezra subjoins Artaxerxes, v. 7, in whose days the work of the structure was checked by an edict. Let us therefore understand the successor to be Cambyses, Tanyoxares the Great, who was also called Smerdis, and who assumed that August name for the sake of greater glory and to procure majesty: since Art, as Grotius admits, is a certain honorific addition, and signifies Great, or Hero, as he himself teaches from Herodotus and Hesychius and similar names: but Xerxes is ἄρης warrior: and the name Artaxerxes was a family name for the Kings of the Persians after Cyrus, as Grotius likewise observes. In the times of these two successors of Cyrus, Cambyses and Tanyoxares, the work of the structure of the temple ceased, until the reign of Darius, who succeeded them immediately and presided before Xerxes, in whose, Darius the first's, second year the building of the temple succeeded again. There is therefore no reason why Grotius should render doubtful either Ahasuerus or Artaxerxes, nor does that variety of opinions which he alleges occur so much concerning this Ahasuerus mentioned by Ezra as concerning the Ahasuerus who was the husband of Esther.

Nor should Scaliger’s argument move anyone, the one with which he and his followers almost always triumph: that that Darius is to be understood, under whom the work succeeded, who was flanked by two Artaxerxes, Macrochir and Mnemon, since this Artaxerxes is mentioned prior to Darius as hindering the work, and afterwards is introduced in c. 7 as Artaxerxes the successor of Darius, the promoter of the work. Since therefore no other Darius is flanked by two Artaxerxes than Darius Nothus, whose predecessor was Artaxerxes Longimanus and whose successor was Artaxerxes Mnemon, the Scaligerians think it follows necessarily that Darius Nothus is to be understood here in v. 24. They naturally assume as beyond doubt that the name Artachshasta in this place, v. 7, refers to someone called by that name as a proper and private name, when nevertheless not only Grotius, but even the Scaligerians admit that the Kings of Persia were almost all called Artaxerxes, and that this was a family name for them, in addition to the proper name which they had before assuming the empire: See Alstedius in Chron. p. 182. Indeed, Scaliger himself observes in book 6 of De emendatione temporum that it was accepted among the Kings of Persia that they should assume other names when they were raised to the throne: just as Darius Nothus was previously called Ochus, Artaxerxes Mnemon was previously called Arsaces and Oarses, and Codomannus, once named, acquired the name of Darius in the monarchy. Why therefore could Smerdis not have assumed the glorious name of Artaxerxes upon taking power? Scaliger himself cuts the nerve of his own argument, and taught us that it is futile, when in Anim- adv. ad Euseb. p. 81: How futile, he says, is the objection concerning names, so that when all other things agree, the difference of names should make it so that Marius is not Marius. Nor indeed can it be taught that this Darius of Ezra is intermediate between the two Artaxerxes. Artaxerxes does indeed precede Darius in ch. 4. But it must be proven that the Artaxerxes of whom he speaks in ch. 7 succeeded him immediately: which will never be proven from sacred history. Then if Artaxerxes Longimanus is understood here as the predecessor of Darius Nothus, it is necessary that Mithridates, who at the time of the liberating edict of Cyrus as prefect of the treasury had handed over the gold and silver vessels to Zerubbabel in ch. 1, 9, should have presided over the highest offices for more than 72 years at the time of that Artaxerxes, when in ch. 4, 7 he is introduced as hindering the construction of the temple, even if he had plotted such things against the Jews in the first year of Longimanus: but if we admit Darius Nothus here and below in ch. 7 Artaxerxes Memnon is introduced as the patron of the work, it will have to be said that the temple was built only 140 years after the edict of Cyrus, and that divine worship was restored: indeed, that the Jews lacked a temple for more than a century, and for one hundred and fifteen years after their return from Babylon, which is absurd. Since, on the contrary, according to the better opinion of antiquity, with Artaxerxes Longimanus admitted as the patron of the work, the temple was built about the 20th year after the edict of Cyrus, and divine worship was restored in the seventy-eighth. Add that for Scaliger and his followers it must be established that Joshua presided over the priesthood for more than 110 years, and Zerubbabel over the principate, which is in no way likely, nor will it be easily taught of anyone since the passing of the sons of Noah that anyone was engaged in public office for more than a century. What of the fact that with the years added from the destruction of the temple to the first year of Cyrus, 52 of those who both saw the first temple and were still surviving when the foundations of the second were being laid, the age must be extended to the 180th year if they were about twelve years old when the Solomonic temple was still standing, such an age being unheard of in the Jewish people in those centuries. Conf. Ezra 3, 12. Hagg. 2, 4. More reasons against Scaliger's opinion, and the authorities of great men, have been brought forward on Dan. 9 in the Diatr. de LXX. septiman. Daniel. Also, regarding this Darius of Ezra, one may consult Edward Simson in Chron. Cathol. part 4, at the year M. 3485. Compendium Histor. Ecclesiast. Gothan. of the Most Serene Duke Ernest, book 1, ch. 3, sect. 1, p. 311 seqq. D. Gottf. Vogelius, Florentin. Schilling, and D. Joh. Cluverus in Chron. &c. but to return to Ahasuerus and to the Artaxerxes of this chapter, Dionysius Petavius is not alien to our explanation, even if he is ambiguous as to whether that Artaxerxes is Smerdis or indeed Cambyses, whom he nevertheless acknowledges is called Ahasuerus here in part 2, book 3, ration. tempor. ch. 10 and 12, and de doctrin. tempor. ch. 25; but Mr. Wilhelm Langius is entirely with us in book 2, de annis Christi ch. 10, p. 419. Whose historical arrangement we add in the author's own words. When Cyrus, in the first year of the Babylonian empire, had sent a certain Sheshbazzar to Jerusalem to build the temple and return the vessels, being occupied in later times with various affairs and involved in the war of the Massagetae, he could not urge the work. Hence, therefore, the opportunity was given to the enemies of the Jews to interrupt that work. Yet they could not accomplish more in the times of Cyrus than to corrupt the governors of Syria with money; so that, while Cyrus was intent on other things, they allowed the work to be interrupted. But when Cyrus was dead, having attacked Cambyses, or Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his empire, they instituted an accusation against the Jews. Yet they obtained nothing regarding the forbidding of the work. For Cambyses did not wish to revoke his parent's edict. However, as much as they could, they forbade the work from being completed. Cambyses caring little for the affairs of the empire, they finally attack the Magus ruling under the persona of Tanyoxarces, the son of Cyrus, who was easy at the beginning, so that he might have the multitude more favorable to his side. And he immediately sent an edict about inhibiting the work. This having been removed shortly after, the Jews did not wish to obey the mandate of that masked King: but they begin to build again, confirmed by the prophecies of Haggai and Zechariah. Therefore, having been accused before Tatnai, the king's deputy, and Shethar-bozenai, and the others whom Darius had sent in their place, who had administered the highest affairs for Smerdis, they defend their cause in such a way that he wrote about this matter to King Darius. Who, by a rescript, permitted the building, which he would have done least of all if he had known the work had been inhibited by his parent. And for that reason Darius ordered a search to be made in the archives, so that it might be more certainly established concerning the edict of Cyrus. Indeed, it is manifest from Ezra himself that Darius the First is understood here. For he says the work had been hindered from the times of Cyrus up to those of Darius: how that happened, he explains in such a way that he clearly indicates that Darius is the fourth from Cyrus. For first, he says, in the reign of Ahasuerus they instituted an accusation against the Jews, but obtained nothing. Afterwards they wrote to Artaxerxes: from whom they received an edict about inhibiting the work. Truly, what reason could there be why the greatest enemies of the Jews would write nothing to Cambyses, nothing to Smerdis, and finally nothing to Darius about these things? Were they therefore quiet until Xerxes? But Ezra joins the three kings in such a way that it is manifest that they reigned immediately after Cyrus. Therefore, in the second year of Darius Hystaspis they began to build again, and in the sixth they finally completed the temple itself, but immediately after they began to build the porticoes and the other things that pertained to the temple. And they laid the foundations of this, according to the mandate of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, the one who reigned after Xerxes, from whom Ezra obtained the privilege of all those things which he requested, Ezra 7, 6, and thus also of laying the foundations of the porticoes and completing the temple, Ezra 6, 14. And these things are so. Thus far Langius. Mr. D. Joh. Cluverus agrees with us here in his Chronological works, nor does he understand Ezra to refer to any other Darius than Darius I, the son of Hystaspes, but he thinks Artaxerxes is Cambyses, who by his private name was called Cambyses, ὁμώνυμος to his grandfather Cyrus, but by his public and Royal name was called Artaxerxes: he believes Ahasuerus to be Cambyses' brother Tanyoxarces, whom Cyrus appointed King of the Bactrians, Parthians, Carmanians, and Choramnians, as testified by Ctesias of Cnidus in Photius, Bibliotheca, p. 54, under whose name the great author of his murder later reigned: for if, after the death of his father, Cambyses had set out for Egypt, when the administration of affairs was in the hands of his brother Tanyoxarces, or Oxarces, Cluverus thinks that accusatory letters were written to him, and soon also to Artaxerxes or Cambyses: But in truth, the opinion which we have set forth thus far is more likely. Compare our sacred Chronicle, section 7, question 1, and following.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

IN REGNO AUTEM ASSEVERI) Editiones quædam Latinæ hic adjiciunt: ipse est Artaxerxes. Sic in Estheræ li- bro qui אחשורוש Hebræis, Græcis interpretibus & Jose- pho est Ἀρταξέρξης, quanquam Josephus hunc etiam Cyrum vocatum dicit. Videtur post Cyrum illum Magnum nomen gentilitium fuisse Persarum Regibus ξέρξης & Ἀρταξέρξης, præter nomen quod habebant ante imperium. Omnes Re- ges post illum Memoriosum dictos Artaxerxas ait Diodorus Siculus libro 15. Etiam Darius ab Alexandro devictus Jac- chiadæ ad Danielem 7, 5. dicitur Artaxerxes. Id unde sit, dicam. ש litera Græcis per ξ verti solebat ut שושן Ἄξυμα: est enim utriusque literæ idem ferme sonus, sed transpositus, quomodo Dores pro συρίζω dicunt συρίσδω, & aspiratio ex me- dia voce Abraham, à Græcis in frontem translata est. Tum vero gutturales sæpe omittuntur, ut multis exemplis often- dimus annotatis ad librum primum de Veritate Religionis Christianæ, ubi de Ammione agimus. Ergo אחשורוש, omissis gutturalibus, est xwerx: & quia W durior est in me- dia voce, maxime post consonantem per se duram, ideo & hæc omissa est à Græcis, factumque Xerx, & cum Græca terminatione Xerxes. Art vero est additamentum quod- dam honorificum, ut sa apud Persas posteriores. Signi- ficat magnum, interprete Herodoto libro 6. Heroa inter- prete Hesychio. Apparet ex nominibus plurimis, qualia sunt Artabanus, Artavasdes, qui & Artabazus, Artochmes, Artochætes, qui & Artayctus, Artanes, Artagenes, Arta- phernes, Artembanes. Artaxerxis in Perside nomen, etiam Romanorum Imperatorum temporibus apud Herodianum & Lampridium invenias. Idem Xerxes dicitur Aurelio Victori. Ex hoc ergo tam communi nomine, quis hic Rex fuerit sciri non potest, nisi adsint temporum argumenta, quæ quam sint obscura ostendunt eruditissimorum, qui ætatem in iis rebus triverunt, in hunc diem certamina. Eum de quo hic agitur Cambysen esse volunt multi, alii Smerdim magum. Estheræ maritum alii Cambysen, alii Darium Hystaspis, alii Artaxer- xem Memoriosum, alii Artaxerxem Longimanum. Horum omnium operosis, ac litigiosis disputationibus perlectis, quid est quod dicat aliquis, ex iis maxime, quibus non est multum ad ista otii, nisi illud Terentianum: Fecistis probe: incertior sum multo quam dudum.

DE hoc Assvero valde quidem Chronologorum, & Interpp. variant sententiæ: At vix magis mirabilis transmutatio nominis in mentem venit ulli, quam hic Grotio, ex Assvero Artaxerxem, imo Xerxem efformanti. Sed id tribuendum opinioni præconceptæ. Quæ etiam Scaligerum eo egit, ut non quidem ex Assvero nomen Xerxis effingeret, Ahasverum tamen Xerxem esse statuens, nomen illud Ahasveri idem esse cum nomine ὀξυάρης sibi facile persvaderet, atque hæc nomina Assverus vel ὀξυάρης, & Xerxes eidem Regi tributa esse assereret, l. 6. de emend. tempor. p. 591. & in prolegom. p. 41. quem sequutus B. D. Joh. Behm. Manud. Chronol. lib. 2. Tit. 2. c. 7. Xerxem antequam parenti in re- gno succederet, nominatum, ait, privato quasi no- mine ὀξυάρης quod Ebræi vix aliter scribere possunt, quam per אחשורוש. Sed illa nominum μεταμόρ- φωσις testimonio, & exemplo caret, nec opinio de Xerxe hic locum habet. Quis Ahasverus Estheræ sit, suo loco dispiciemus. Xerxis nomen gen- tilitium Persarum Regibus fuisse, nullo teste pro- bavit Grotius. Nec tam incerta hic est scripturæ, quem Assveri nomine intelligat, sententia, quam varia interpp. explicatio, modo probe attendamus verbis Historici divini. Quid enim apertius est, quam quod diebus Cyri Regis Persarum, ex quo ja- cta templi fundamenta sunt, usque ad regnum Da- rii impeditum sit structuræ opus vers. 5. & quidem uti definitur expresse tempus, vers. 24. usque ad annum secundum regni Darii, ex quo Darii no- mine dum vers. 5. & 24. duos Scaliger contra di- fertissimam literam, quæ de eodem Rege loquitur, totamque antiquitatem, effinxit sibi Darios, sei- psum & sequaces in errorem gravissimum, & in- tolerabilem conjecit de templo non sub Dario Hy- staspide, sed sub Dario Notho ædificato, quo tota propemodum Chronologia pervertitur. Nimirum Darium v. 5. vult esse Darium Hystaspida, Darium vero v. 24. Darium Nothum: sub illo impeditum esse opus structuræ templi, sub hoc promotum ait. Ex adverso textus luculenter definit terminum ad quem impeditæ structuræ in Dario v. 5. designato; factum est igitur, ut populus terræ impediret manus populi Judæ & turbaret eos in ædificando. Conduxe- runt autem adversus eos consiliatores, ut destruerent consilium eorum OMNIBUS DIEBUS CYRI Regis Persarum, & usque ad Regnum DARII Re- gis Persarum. Ecquis hic non intelligit, durasse illa impedimenta inde à Diebus Cyri (post diploma li- bertatis) usque ad regnum Darii 1. ejus sc. qui post Cyrum imperio præfuit: hoc est, Hystaspidæ, non vero ultra regnum ejus, usque ad Darii 2. vel Nothi imperium. Nam quod vocem ועד ET USQUE sensu non exclusivo, sed INCLUSIVO intelligen- dam esse, ajunt Scaligeri asseclæ, nimis frivolum est, neque oratio divini Historici patitur: qui non ait & OMNIBUS regni Darii diebus, sed omnibus Diebus Cyri, ET USQUE AD regnum Darii. Et ne dubium remaneret, quoto anno regni Darii istius structuræ impedimentum finem habuerit, o- pusque iterum successerit, addit Esdras annum v. 24. Tunc intermissum est opus Domini in Jerusalem, & non fiebat USQUE AD ANNUM SECUN- DUM regni DARII Regis Persarum. En apertam anni definitionem, quo finem nacta illa intermis- sio! Porro ne quis ingerat Xerxem, & Artaxerxem Longimanum cum Scaligero, ante finem cessatio- nis structuræ, eamve ad Darium Nothum usque extendat, cavit jam Spiritus S. dum non solum USQUE AD Darii 1. regnum opus structuræ suf- flaminatum esse indicavit, non ulterius, aut per to- tum tempus regiminis ejus, nedum per tempora re- giminis successorum ejusdem, sed connectere etiam Regum illorum tempora, sub quibus opus impe- ditum fuit, cum Diebus Cyri voluit, ut ne ambi- guum esset, proximos Cyri successores in culpa fuisse, ac recenset, sub quibus & quomodo præ- pedita structura sit v. 6. seqq. Nam in regno Assve- ri (vau est exegeticum vel causale) in principio re- gni ejus, (statim post dies Cyri Regis Persarum) scripserunt accusationem adversus habitatores Judæ & Jerusalem. Ubi turbarunt Interpp. & Chrono- logos verba adjecta ad nomen Assveri (Ipse est Ar- taxerxes) quæ in quibusdam Latinis editionibus inventa, sed irreptitia sunt, ideoque a Pontificibus Romanis eliminata non leguntur amplius in vulga- ta. Per Assverum vero nec Xerxem, nec Artaxer- xem intelligi posse, manifestum est, quia illi non successerunt immediate Cyro; & cur post dies Cyri introduxisset statim S. S. Xerxem & Artaxerxem, præterito Cambyse, & Smerdi ceu proximis succes- soribus? Quomodo definito jam termino ad quem cessationis operis sub regno Darii, verbis USQUE ad regnum Darii, protraheret porro ulterius im- peditionem operis sub Darii successoribus, & ad tempora regni Xerxis & Artaxerxis, ad omnes Dies regni eorum, & usque ad initium Regni Da- rii Nothi? Quapropter luculentissimum est Assve- rum non esse Xerxem, sed Cyri successorem CAM- BYSEN, quod etiam Josephus docet, & plerique ex antiquitate: qui nomen illud majoris gloriæ causa sibi sumsit. Ahasverus enim, fatente Scali- gero, Magnum Ducem notat, ab Achasch Magnus, Vau & Rosch Caput, & fuit utique Cambyses ma- gnus Dux, & bellator, utpote qui totam Ægyptum armis subegit. Nec de alio, quam Cambyse intel- ligunt Lyranus, Vatablus, Munsterus, Lavaterus, alii. Huic Assvero subjungit Esdras Artaxerxem, v. 7. in cujus diebus per edictum sufflaminatum structuræ opus fuit. Cambysen ergo successorem intelligamus, necessum est, Tanyoxarem Magnum, qui & Smerdis dictus est, nomenque illud Augu- stum sibi majoris gloriæ, & majestatis conciliandæ causa assumsit: siquidem Art, fatente Grotio, ad- ditamentum quoddam honorificum sit, & Ma- gnum, vel Heroa significet, ut ex Herodoto, & Hesy- chio, ac similibus nominibus ipse docet: Xerxes ve- ro ἄρης bellator sit: & Artaxerxis nomen Regi- bus Persarum post Cyrum gentilitium fuerit, ob- servante itidem Grotio. Horum ergo duorum Cyri successorum Cambysis, & Tanyoxaris temporibus cessavit opus structuræ templi, usque ad Darii re- gnum, qui illis immediate successit, & ante Xerxem præfuit, cujus Darii primi secundo anno fabrica templi iterum successit. Non itaque est, quod du- bium reddat Grotius seu Assverum, seu Artaxer- xem, neque tam de hoc Assvero Esdræ commemo- rato quam de Assvero Estheræ marito illa, quam al- legat, sententiarum varietas occurrit.

Nec movere quenquam debet argumentum Scaligeri, quo uno triumphat fere ille cum sequaci- bus: quod Darius ille intelligendus sit, sub quo o- pus successit, qui stipatus duobus Artaxerxis fuit, Macrochire, & Mnemone, siquidem hic Artaxerxes prævius Dario commemoretur impediens opus, & post- ea introducatur c. 7. Artaxerxes successor Darii, promotor operis. Quum ergo nullus alius Darius sti- patus duobus Artaxerxis sit, quam Darius Nothus, cujus antecessor Artaxerxes Longimanus, succes- sor Artaxerxes Memoriosus fuit, ἀδιαλύτως se inferre putant Scaligeriani, Darium Nothum hic in- telligendum esse v. 24. Nimirum assumunt pro in- dubitato, Artachshasta nomen hoc loco v. 7. ali- quem proprio & privato nomine ita vocatum intelli- gi, quum tamen non Grotius tantum, sed etiam Sca- ligeriani fateantur, Reges Persarum fere Artaxerxes dictos esse, atque hoc ipsis fuisse gentilitium nomen, præter nomen proprium, quod habuere ante impe- rium assumtum: Vid. Alstedius in Chron. p. 182. imo Scaliger ipse observat l. 6. de emendat. tempor. pe- nes Persarum Reges receptum fuisse, ut alia assume- rent nomina, cum fascibus admoti fuerunt: quemad- modum Darius Nothus antea dictus est Ἄχος & Ὦχος, Artaxerxes Memor vocatus prius fuit Ἀρσέ- κας, & Ὀάρσης, & Codomannus olim nominatus in Mo- narchia Darii nomen adeptus est. Cur ergo Smerdis imperio potius assumere non potuit Artaxerxis gloriosum nomen? Incidit ipse Scaliger nervum ar- gumento suo, idq; futile esse nos docuit, cum anim- adv. ad Euseb. p. 81. Quam futilis, ait, objectio de no- minibus, ut cum reliqua omnia conveniant, discrimen nominum faciat, ne Marius sit Marius. Neque vero medium esse hunc Darium Esdrae inter Artaxerxes duos, doceri potest. Antecedit quidem Darium Ar- taxerxes c. 4. Sed immediati eidem Artaxerxem, de quo c. 7. successisse, probandum est: quod ex Histo- ria sacra nunquam evincetur. Tum si Artaxerxes Longimanus ceu antecessor Darii Nothi hic intel- ligatur, Mithridaten, qui tempore edicti Cyri libe- ratorii ceu praefectus aerarii vasa aurea, & argentea Zorobabeli tradiderat c. 1, 9. oportet istius Artaxer- xis tempore, quum c. 4, 7. introducatur ut impe- diens structuram templi, ultra 72. annos summis praefuisse dignitatibus, etiamsi primo Longimani anno talia contra Judaeos molitus fuisset: Darium ve- ro Nothum si admittamus hic & infra c. 7. Artaxer- xem Memorem introduci ceu Patronos operis, di- cendum erit, templum 140. annis demum post edi- ctum Cyri aedificatum, cultumque divinum repara- tum fuisse: imo ultra seculum, & per centum ac quindecim annos caruisse Judaeos templo post redi- tum e Babylone, quod inconveniens. Quum ex ad- verso juxta antiquitatis meliorem sententiam Arta- xerxe Longimano Patrono operis admisso, cum Da- rio Hystaspis templum 20. circiter anno ab edicto Cy- ri aedificatum, cultus vero divinus septuagesimo o- ctavo restauratus sit. Adde quod Scaligero & asse- clis statuendum sit, Josuam plusquam 110. annis Sa- cerdotio, Zorobabelem principatui praefuisse, quod nullatenus verisimile, nec de ullo inde ab excessu filiorum Noae facile doceri poterit, ultra seculum quenquam in publico munere versatum fuisse. Quid quod additis annis ab excidio templi ad primum Cyri elapsis 52. eorum qui & primum templum vi- derunt, & cum fundamenta secundi jacerentur, ad- huc superstites fuerunt, aetas extendenda sit ad an- num 180. si duodecim circiter annos habuere, cum adhuc staret templum Salomoneum, qualis aetas istis seculis in populo Judaico inaudita. Conf. Esdr. 3, 12. Hagg. 2, 4. Rationes plures adversus Scaligeri sententiam, & magnorum virorum autoritates ad- ductae ad Dan. 9. sunt Diatr. de LXX. septiman. Da- niel. Conferri etiam de hoc Dario Esdrae poterunt Edvardus Simsonius in Chron. Cathol. part. 4. ad Ann. M. 3485. Compendium Histor. Ecclesiast. Go- than. Sereniss. Ducis Ernesti l. 1. c. 3. sect. 1. p. 311. seqq. D. Gottf. Vogelius, Florentin. Schilling. & D. Joh. Cluverus in Chron. &c. ut autem ad Assverum revertamur & ad Artaxerxem hujus Capitis, non a- lienus est a nostra explicatione Dionysius Peta- vius, etsi ambiguus sit, an Artaxerxes ille Smerdis sit, an vero Cambyses, quem Assverum tamen hic di- ctum agnoscit part. 2. l. 3. ration. tempor. c. 10. & 12. & de doctrin. tempor. c. 25. penitus vero nobiscum facit Dn. Wilhelm. Langius l. 2. de annis Christi c. 10. p. 419. Cujus ἰσοριόταξιν adjicimus propriis autoris verbis. Cyrus cum primo anno Babylonici imperii Sezbazarum quendam Hierosolyma misisset ad templum aedificandum, & vasa reducenda, poste- rioribus temporibus variis negotiis occupatus ac Massagetarum bello implicitus, opus urgere non potuit. Hinc igitur hostibus Judaeorum data occa- sio fuit, opus illud interturbandi. Nec tamen Cyri temporibus plus efficere poterant, quam praesides Syriae pecuniis corrumpere; ut, dum Cyrus aliis in- tentus esset, illi permitterent opus interrumpi. Mortuo vero Cyro, Cambysen, sive Assverum prin- cipio Imperii aggressi, accusationem contra Judaeos instituerunt. Neque tamen de opere vetando quid- quam obtinuerunt. Quippe nolebat Cambyses Pa- rentis edictum revocare. Quantum tamen poterant, vetabant, ne opus perficeretur. Cambyfe parum nego- tia imperii curante, demum Magum sub persona Tanyoxarcis filii Cyri imperantem aggrediuntur, fa- cilem principio, ut multitudinem suis partibus ma- gis faventem haberet. Atque hic statim edictum misit de opere inhibendo. Hoc brevi post sublato, Ju- dæi illius personati Regis mandato parere nolebant: sed iterum ædificare incipiunt, Haggæi & Zachariæ vaticiniis confirmati. Accusati igitur apud Thatnai Regis vicarium & Starbosnai, cæterosque quos Da- rius in locum eorum miserat, qui pro Smerdi sum- ma rerum administraverant, ita causam suam de- fendunt, ut is de hac re ad Regem Darium perscri- beret. Qui rescripto ædificationem permisit, quod minime fecisset, si a Parente suo inhibitum opus novisset. Ideo autem in Archivis quæri jussit Darius, ut de edicto Cyri certius constaret. Imo ex ipso Esdra manifestum est, Darium primum hic intelligi. Di- cit enim opus impeditum fuisse à Cyri temporibus, usq; ad Darii: id quomodo factum sit, ita explicat, ut manifesto indicet, Darium quartum à Cyro esse. Pri- mo enim, inquit, Assuero regnante accusationem con- tra Judæos instituerunt, sed nihil obtinuerunt. Postea ad Artaxerxem scripserunt: a quo edictum de inhi- bendo opere receperunt. Sane quid causæ esset, cur maximi Judæorum hostes, nihil ad Cambysen, nihil ad Smerdin, nihil denique ad Darium de his scribe- rent? Ergone ad Xerxem usque quieti erant? Sed conjungit ita tres Reges Esdras, ut manifestum sit eos post Cyrum immediate regnasse. Darii ergo Hystas- pis secundo anno rursus ædificare cœperunt & sexto demum ipsum templum perfecerunt, statim vero post porticus & cætera, quæ ad templum spectabant, ædificare cœperunt. Atque hujus fundamenta jece- runt, juxta mandatum Cyri, Darii, & Artaxerxis, ejus, qui post Xerxem regnavit, a quo privilegium ob- tinuit Esdras omnium eorum quæ petiit, Esdræ 7, 6. adeoque & jaciendi fundamenta porticuum, templum- que perficiendi Esd. 6, 14. Atq; hæc ita se habent. Hac- tenus Langius. Dn. D. Joh. Cluverus in Chronolo- gicis hic nobiscum convenit, nec de alio Dario, quam I. Hystaspis Filio Esdram intelligit, at Artach- sastam Cambysem esse putat, qui privato nomine Pa- tri Cyri avo suo ὁμώνυμος Cambyses vocatus, publi- co vero & Regio nomine Arthasasta dictus sit: Ahasve- rum vero credit fratrem Cambysis Tanyoxarsen, quem Cyrus Regem Bactrianorum, Parthorum, Carmaniæ & Choramniæ constituit teste Ctesia Cni- dio apud Photium in Biblioth. p. 54. sub cujus nomi- ne regnavit postea Magnus autor cædis ejus: siqui- dem Cambyse ab obitu Patris in Ægyptum profe- cto, quum rerum gubernatio penes fratrem Ta- nyoxerxem, vel Oxerxem esset, ad ipsum, & mox etiam ad Artachsastam vel Cambysen literas accusa- trices exaratas esse censet Cluverus: Sed vero si- milior est ea, quam hactenus exposuimus, sententia. Confer Chronic. nostrum sacrum sect. 7, q. 1. seqq.

## 4:9
Verse 9. REHUM BEEL-SHEEM] This was a royal praetor, who with others managed affairs beyond the Euphrates in the King's stead. See below 5, 6.

APHARSATHCHITES) These are the Persoscythians.

Latin:

Vers. 9. REVM BELSEEM] Hic prætor erat regius, qui cum aliis vice Regis res trans Euphratem curabat. Vide in- fra 5, 6.

APHARSATACHÆI) Hi sunt Περσοσκύθαι.

## 4:10
Verse 10. WHOM ASENAPHAR BROUGHT OVER] Another name for Shalmaneser, as it seems.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QVAS TRANSTVLIT ASENAPHAR] No- men alterum Salmanassaris, ut videtur.

## 4:12
Verse 12. THE REBELLIOUS AND EVIL CITY] This was made credible because the customs of the Jews were different from others: for this reason Tacitus called them a most foul race, who also has this: the founders had foreseen frequent wars from the diversity of customs. Likewise: having bought the right of fortifying, they built walls in peace, as if for war.

Latin:

Vers. 12. CIVITATEM REBELLEM ET PESSIMAM] Credibile id fiebat ob instituta Judæorum diversa ab aliis: ob id teterrimam gentem dixit Tacitus, qui & hoc habet: præviderant conditores ex diversitate morum crebra bella. Item: emto jure muniendi, struxere muros in pace, tanquam ad bellum.

## 4:13
Verse 13. TRIBUTE AND CUSTOM AND YEARLY REVENUE) See these three also below 20. It seems that by the name of tribute is understood that which is given per head, by custom that which is on merchandise, and by revenues that which is from fields.

Latin:

Vers. 13. TRIBVTVM ET VECTIGAL ET ANNV- OS REDITVS) Vide hæc tria & infra 20. Videtur intel- ligi tributi nomine quod in capita datur, vectigalis quod in merces, redituum quod de agris.

## 4:14
Verse 14. MINDFUL OF THE SALT WHICH IN THE PALACE

WE EAT] Because we have a salary from the King. But the Chaldean: on account of the demolition of the Temple which we have demolished. For מלח often signifies to consume. See what is said at Mark 9:49.

Latin:

Vers. 14. MEMORES SALIS QVOD IN PALATIO

COMEDIMVS] Quia salarium habemus a Rege. At Chal- dæus:propter demolitionem Templi quod demoliti sumus. Nam מלח saepe significat consumere. Vide quæ dicta adMarc.9,49.

## 4:19
Ver. 19. AND THEY SEARCHED AND FOUND) The King had ordered that what concerned the Jews in the royal commentaries be searched out. See 5:17, 6:2, Esther 2:23, 6:1.

Latin:

Vers. 19. ET RECENSVERVNT INVENV̀NT- QVE) Jusserat Rex perquiri quæ de Judæis erant in regum commentariis. Vide 5, 17. 6, 2. Estheræ 2, 23. 6, 1.

## 4:20
Ver. 20. AND THEY RULED OVER ALL THE REGION WHICH IS BEYOND THE RIVER] Namely David and Solomon.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET DOMINATI SVNT OMNI REGIONI QVÆ TRANS FLVVIVM EST] Nempe David & Sa- lomon.

## 4:21
Ver. 21. YOU SHALL PROHIBIT THOSE MEN, SO THAT THAT CITY MAY NOT BE BUILT] It is not to the advantage of Kings that peoples conquered by them should have cities full of people and strong with fortifications.

UNTIL PERCHANCE AN ORDER SHALL HAVE BEEN GIVEN BY ME) This edict depended solely on the will of the King: it was not among the immutable laws of the Persians.

Latin:

Vers. 21. PROHIBEATIS VIROS ILLOS, VT VRBS ILLA NON ÆDIFICETVR] Non est è re Regum, ut po- puli ab ipsis devicti urbes habeant populo plenas, munimen- tis validas.

DONEC SI FORTE A ME JVSSVM FVERIT) Edi- ctum hoc à sola Regis voluntate pendebat: non erat inter le- ges Persarum immutabiles.

## 4:24
Ver. 24. THEN THE WORK OF THE LORD WAS INTERRUPTED] For nothing ought to have been done against the command of the King, unless by the express command of God, such as we have in 5:1, 2. But to that divine command, the command of the King was later added 6:7. After these things, the Greeks insert those things which are in the apocryphal book which is called the third of Ezra, chapter 3, which Josephus also has.

Latin:

Vers. 24. TVNC INTERMISSVM EST OPVS DOMI- NI] Neque enim contra imperium Regis fieri quicquam de- bebat, nisi expresso Dei jussu, qualem habemus 5, 1. 2. Ei au- tem divino jussui postea & Regis jussus accesfit 6, 7. Græci post hæc inferunt ea quæ sunt in libro apocrypho, qui Esdræ tertius dicitur. cap. 3. quæ & Josephus habet.

## 5:1 Argument
PART III. THE MORE SUCCESSFUL PROGRESS OF THE WORK UNDER DARIUS. SECTION I. CHAPTER V.

Stirred up by the Prophets, Zerubbabel and Joshua began to build the temple, concerning which the prefects consult Darius.

Latin:

PARS III. SUCCESSUS OPERIS FELICIOR SUB DARIO. SECTIO I. CAPUT V.

A Prophetis excitati Zorobabel, & Josua cœpe- runt extruere templum, quo de Darium con- sulunt præfecti.

## 5:5
Ver. 5. BUT THE EYE OF THEIR GOD WAS UPON THE ELDERS OF THE JEWS) God favored them, so that He also reconciled to them the minds of the royal ministers in those parts.

Latin:

Vers. 5. OCVLVS AVTEM DEI EORVM FACTVS EST SVPER SENES JVDÆORVM) Deus eis favit, ita ut & regiorum in illis partibus ministrorum animos illis con- ciliaret.

## 5:6
Ver. 6. COPY OF THE LETTER) Of the consultation.

Latin:

Vers. 6. EXEMPLAR EPISTOLÆ) Consultationis.

## 5:8
Ver. 8. WITH THE STONE PLACED] The Hebrews understand marble by גלל: the Greeks, with costly hewn stones.

Latin:

Vers. 8. LAPIDE IMPOSITO] גלל marmor intelli- gunt Hebræi: Græci διὰ λίθων ξυσῶν πολυτελῶν.

## 5:15
Ver. 15. IN THE TEMPLE.

IN the place of the temple near the treasury. For the temple had been burned down.

Latin:

Vers. 15. IN TEMPLO.

IN loco templi Gazophylacio vicino. Templum enim erat exustum.

## 5:17
Ver. 17. IN THE LIBRARY) In the archives.

Not a library but a Royal archive, in which the records of wealth, censuses, expenses, etc., and authentic copies of laws and royal decrees were kept.

Latin:

Vers. 17. IN BIBLIOTHECA) In tabulario.

Non Bibliotheca sed archivum Regium, in quo tabulæ opum, censuum, expensarum &c. & au- thentica exemplaria legum, & decretorum Regio- rum asservabantur.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI.

Darius orders the decree of Cyrus that was found to be fulfilled, with the expense provided: the temple is completed, dedicated with offered victims, and the Passover is celebrated.

Latin:

CAPUT VI.

Darius decretum Cyri inventum compleri jubet, suppeditato sumtu: templum absolutum obla tis victimis dedicatur & celebratur Pascha.

## 6:2
Ver. 2. ROLL] Τόμον: as also Isaiah 8, 1. Elsewhere it is called κεφαλὶς: as also Hebrews 10, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 2. VOLUMEN] Τόμον: ut & Esaiæ 8, 1. Alibi κε- φαλὶς dicitur: ut & Hebr. 10, 7.

## 6:3
Ver. 3. OF SIXTY CUBITS. The former temple was twice as high.

Latin:

Vers. 3. SEXAGINTA CUBITORUM. Prius templum duplo erat altius.

## 6:8
Ver. 8. NAMELY THAT FROM THE KING'S TREASURY, THAT IS, FROM THE TRIBUTES WHICH ARE GIVEN FROM THE REGION BEYOND THE RIVER, EXPENSES BE DILIGENTLY GIVEN TO THOSE MEN] In this generosity he surpassed Cyrus. Cyrus had permitted the Jews to contribute to the work. This King even provides the expense from his own. See below 7, 20, 21, 22, and Neh. 11, 23, in the Hebrew.

Latin:

Vers. 8. SCILICET UT DE ARCA REGIS, ID EST, DE TRIBUTIS QVÆ DANTUR DE REGIONE TRANS FLUMEN, STUDIOSE SUMPTUS DENTUR VIRIS ILLIS] Hac beneficentia Cyrum vicit. Cyrus Judæis conferre ad opus permiserat. Hic Rex etiam de suo sumtum facit. Vide infra 7, 20, 21. 22. & Neh. 11, 23. in Hebræo.

## 6:10
Ver. 10. AND PRAY FOR THE LIFE OF THE KING] See above 1, 2. The Jews also prayed for the Lacedaemonians.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ORENTQVE PRO VITA REGIS] Vide su- pra 1, 2. Etiam pro Lacedæmoniis orarunt Judæi.

## 6:11
Ver. 11. THAT EVERY MAN WHO SHALL ALTER THIS DECREE] Alter, that is, act against it.

LET A BEAM BE TAKEN FROM HIS HOUSE AND LET HIM BE ERECTED] It was the custom of the Persians to take a beam from the house of a condemned man, from which he might be suspended.

Latin:

Vers. 11. UT OMNIS HOMO QVI HANC MUTA- VERIT JUSSIONEM] Mutaverit, id est, contra fecerit.

TOLLATUR LIGNUM DE DOMO IPSIUS ET ERIGATUR] Mos erat Persarum de damnati domo lignum sumere, de quo suspenderetur.

## 6:14
Ver. 14. BY THE COMMAND OF CYRUS, AND DARIUS, AND ARTAXERXES.

These are the patrons of the temple: Cyrus, Darius Hystaspis, and Artaxerxes, who is numbered here by anticipation, namely Longimanus, for it is of him that it follows finally in chapter 7.

Latin:

Vers. 14. JUBENTE CYRO, ET DARIO, ET ARTAXERXE.

Patroni hi sunt templi Cyrus, Darius Hystas- pis & Artaxerxes, qui per anticipationem hic an- numeratur, Longimanus nempe, de hoc enim se- quitur demum cap. 7.

## 6:15
Ver. 15. WHICH IS THE SIXTH YEAR OF DARIUS.

Some think that the structure of the Holy and the Holy of Holies was completed from the second to the sixth year: but they assert from Josephus, book 11, chapter 4, that the atrium or the outer part of the temple, and thus the whole temple in all respects, was finished in the ninth year of Darius, such as Ribera, Pererius, Cornel. à Lap., and others. But the error in Josephus is manifest: since he refers the dedication of the temple to the ninth year of Darius, which the Holy Spirit clearly teaches here was done in the sixth year of Darius: and therefore Josephus does not deserve credence in this place.

Latin:

Vers. 15. QUI EST ANNUS SEXTUS DARII.

Ab anno secundo ad sextum fabricam sancti & Sancti Sanctorum absolutam esse putant non- nulli: atrium vero sive exteriorem partem templi, adeoque totum templum quoad omnia anno Darii nono consummatum esse, è Josephi l. 11. c. 4. asse- runt, utpote Ribera, Pererius, Cornel. à Lap. alii. At apertus est error in Josepho: siquidem ille dedi- cationem templi referat ad annum Darii nonum, quam vero hic luculenter Spiritus S. anno Darii sexto factam esse docet: ideoque fidem non mere- tur hoc loco Josephus.

## 6:21
Ver. 21. AND ALL WHO HAD SEPARATED THEMSELVES FROM THE DEFILEMENT OF THE NATIONS OF THE LAND UNTO THEM] That is, fully proselytes, who had subjected themselves to the law. For it was not permitted for others to eat of the Passover.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET OMNES QVI SE SEPARAVERANT A COINQVINATIONE GENTIVM TERRÆ AD EOS] Id est, plene proselyti, qui se legi subjecerant. Aliis enim de Paschate manducare non licebat.

## 6:22
Ver. 22. BECAUSE THE LORD HAD MADE THEM JOYFUL, AND HAD TURNED THE HEART OF THE KING OF ASSYRIA UNTO THEM] Cf. 7, 27.

The King of Assyria is Darius, King of the Persians, because the Assyrians just as much as the Babylonians were already subject to his Monarchy.

Latin:

Vers. 22. QVONIAM LÆTIFICAVERAT EOS DO- MINVS, ET CONVERTERAT COR REGIS ASSVR AD EOS] Conf. 7, 27.

Rex Assur Darius est Rex Persarum, quia As- syrii æque ac Babylonii jam suberant Monarchiæ ejus.

## 7:1 Argument
SECTION II. UNDER AHASUERUS. CHAPTER VII.

Ezra sent by Artaxerxes to Jerusalem to teach and rule the people. The royal edict.

Latin:

SECTIO II. SUB AHASVERO. CAPUT VII.

Esdras ab Artaxerxe Hierosolymam missus po- pulum docturus, & recturus. Regium edictum.

## 7:3
Ver. 3. Six generations from Meraioth to Azariah are omitted, not by the fault of the scribes, as Capellus maintains, but because it seemed so to Ezra, who had already enumerated them in 1 Chron. 6, 7, and following, from where they could be supplied here.

Latin:

Vers. 3. Omittuntur sex generationes à Mera- joth ad Azariam, non culpa librariorum, ut vult Capellus, sed quia ita visum fuit Esdræ, qui jam re- censuerat eas 1. Chron. 6, 7. & seqq. unde suppleri hic possent.

## 7:6
Ver. 6. AND HE HIMSELF A READY SCRIBE IN THE LAW OF MOSES] In Greek γραμματεὺς εὐφυὴς ὠν ἐν τῷ Μωϋσέως νόμῳ. מהיר often signifies diligent. A scribe is a doctor of the law: in that study was included the knowledge of divine matters and of Pontifical and civil law. Ezra was most learned in these, 7, 10, 11, 12. The law therefore existed throughout the whole time of the exile among the Jews, as appears also in Dan. 9, 13. Ezra, having brought the best copies, gave an accurate ἔκδοσιν of the law, and added the histories of the following times along with the prophetic books, and those poetic ones which held authority.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET IPSE SCRIBA VELOX IN LEGE MO- SIS] Græce γραμματεὺς εὐφυὴς ὠν ἐν τῷ Μωϋσέως νόμῳ. מהיר sæpe diligentem significat. Scriba est doctor legis: in eo studio comprehendebatur notitia rerum divinarum ju- risque Pontificii ac civilis. Horum eruditissimus erat Esdras 7, 10. 11. 12. Exstabat ergo lex toto exilii tempore inter Ju- dæos, ut apparet & Dan. 9, 13. Esdras allatis optimis exem- plaribus accuratam legis dedit ἔκδοσιν, addiditque historias fequentium temporum cum propheticis libris, & iis poeticis qui auctoritatem obtinebant.

## 7:12
Ver. 12. KING OF KINGS] Not undeservedly did the Persian Kings call themselves thus: for they even had Kings in their service, as we have noted elsewhere from Aeschylus's Persians. Such were the Kings of Armenia, Cyprus, Caria, Sidon, and others.

Latin:

Vers. 12. REX REGVM] Non immerito sic se appella- bant Reges Persæ: habebant enim etiam Reges in obsequio suo, ut ex Æschyli Persis alibi notavimus. Tales erant Arme- niæ, Cypri, Cariæ, Sidonis Reges & alii.

## 7:14
Ver. 14. AND HIS SEVEN COUNSELORS] These were the chief of the Satraps, who were always present with the King. Esth. 1, 14. On which matter see what we have noted at Matt. 18, 10.

THAT YOU MAY VISIT JUDAEA AND JERUSALEM ACCORDING TO THE LAW OF YOUR GOD] By these words autonomy is granted to the Jews. And autodikia below 25. 26.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET SEPTEM CONSILIARIORVM EJVS] Hi erant Satraparum præcipui, qui Regi semper aderant. Esth. 1, 14. Qua de re vide quæ notavimus ad Matth. 18, 10.

VT VISITES JVDÆAM ET JERVSALEM IN LE- GE DEI TVI] His verbis αὐτονομία Judæis conceditur. Et αὐτοδικία infra 25. 26.

## 7:18
Ver. 18. BUT ALSO IF ANYTHING TO YOU AND YOUR BRETHREN SHALL PLEASE] The King gave authority to Ezra: he also employed the counsel of other priests.

Latin:

Vers. 18. SED ET SI QVID TIBI ET FRATRIBVS TVIS PLACVERIT] Esdræ auctoritatem Rex dedit: ille aliorum quoque Sacerdotum consilium adhibebat.

## 7:24
Ver. 24. THAT TO TAX AND TRIBUTE AND PROVISIONS YOU SHALL NOT HAVE POWER TO IMPOSE UPON THEM] Here to the priests, Levites, and all ministers of the Temple is given immunity, confirmed afterwards by many Kings, as we learn from Josephus.

The Jews were therefore servants and tributaries of the Persians: but the priests and Levites were exempt from taxes.

Latin:

Vers. 24. VT VECTIGAL ET TRIBVTVM ET AN- NONAS NON HABEATIS POTESTATEM IMPO- NENDI SVPER EOS) Hic Sacerdotibus, Levitis & Templi ministris omnibus datur ἀτέλεια, à multis postea Regibus confirmata, ut ex Josepho discimus.

Fuere itaque Judæi servi, & tributarii Persarum: sed sacerdotes, & Levitæ exemti erant a tributis.

## 7:26
Ver. 26. AND THE LAW OF THE KING] Namely this law which grants to the Jews the right of exercising their own laws.

From this verse they infer that the power of death over transgressors, which the Romans denied to the Jews, was granted to Ezra, because it is said there shall be judgment upon him, whether unto death, or unto banishment.

Latin:

Vers. 26. ET LEGEM REGIS] Nempe hanc legem quæ Judæis suarum legum exercendarum facit jus.

Ex hoc versu colligunt potestatem necis in prævaricatores, quam Judæis negarunt Romani, Esdræ concessam, quia dicitur judicium erit de eo, sive in mortem, sive in exilium.

## 8:1 Argument
CHAPTER VIII.

The Jews who returned with Ezra are listed by families, as are the vessels, gifts, and offerings presented.

Ver. 1. THEY WENT UP WITH ME.

FROM this passage it is manifest that Ezra wrote this catalog, and therefore is the author of this book.

Latin:

CAPUT VIII.

Recensentur per familias Judæi, qui cum Esdra redierunt, ut & vasa, munera, & hostiæ oblatæ.

Vers. 1. ASCENDERUNT MECUM.

EX hoc loco manifestum est Esdram hunc Ca- talogum conscripsisse, adeoque autorem esse hujus libri.

## 8:15
Ver. 15. TO THE RIVER THAT RUNS DOWN TO AHAVA] The Greeks [call it] the river Thera. Learned men think that Ahava is Adiabene, so called from the river Adiava, if we believe Marcellinus.

dimus. Thersara in those places, which is mentioned by Ptolemy, does not differ from the name Θεραὰ.

Latin:

Vers. 15. AD FLVVIVM QVI DECVRRIT AD AHA- VA] Græci θερὰν ποταμὸν. Putant eruditi אהוא esse Adia- benam sic dictam ab Adiava fluvio, si Marcellino cre- dimus.

dimus. A nomine Θεραὰ non abludit Thersara illis in locis, cujus apud Ptolemæum mentio.

## 8:17
Vers. 17. IN THE PLACE OF CHASPIA) In the Caspians: for the Jews were to be summoned from there as well. But the LXX translate it as a place of the treasury, from the name כסף, which signifies silver.

Latin:

Vers. 17. IN CHASPIÆ LOCO) In Caspiis: nam & inde evocandi erant Judæi. At LXX. vertunt τόπον γαζοφυλακίε, à nomine כסף, quod argentum significat.

## 8:21
Vers. 21. AND I PROCLAIMED A FAST THERE) As one appointed by the King as a leader of a colony.

Latin:

Vers. 21. ET PRÆDICAVI IBI JEJVNIVM) Tanquam deductor coloniæ à Rege constitutus.

## 8:22
Vers. 22. FOR I WAS ASHAMED TO ASK THE KING FOR HELP) Prudently, lest the King, being less instructed in divine matters, might believe the things that the Jews were making public regarding God's benevolence toward him and the prophecies delivered to him were vain.

That this King acknowledged and worshipped the true God of Israel, the Royal edict sufficiently teaches; however, the reason why he did not ask for help from the King is added here in the text, namely, confidence in the help of GOD.

Latin:

Vers. 22. ERVBVI ENIM PETERE A REGE AVXILIVM) Prudenter, ne Rex minus edoctus res divinas, vana crederet quæ de Dei in se benevolentia & vaticiniis sibi editis Judæi publicabant.

Regem hunc agnovisse & coluisse verum Deum Israelis edictum Regium satis docet; causa autem cur non petierit à Rege auxilium additur hic in textu, παῤῥησία nempe in auxilio DEI.

## 8:27
Vers. 27. A THOUSAND SOLIDUS. In the Hebrew and LXX, a thousand drachmas.

Latin:

Vers. 27. SOLIDOS MILLENOS. In Ebr. & LXX. drachmas mille.

## 8:34
Vers. 34. AND ALL THE WEIGHT WAS DESCRIBED AT THAT TIME) An inventory was made of all the movables given to the Temple: which those who have given economic precepts believe should also be done in private families.

Latin:

Vers. 34. DESCRIPTVMQVE EST OMNE PONDVS IN TEMPORE ILLO) Omnium mobilium ad Templum datorum factus est inventarius: quod & in privatis familiis faciendum censent qui œconomica præcepta dederunt.

## 8:35
Vers. 35. TWELVE CALVES FOR ALL THE PEOPLE OF ISRAEL) One for each tribe.

Latin:

Vers. 35. VITVLOS DVODECIM PRO OMNI POPVLO ISRAEL) Vnum pro quaque tribu.

## 9:1 Argument
CHAPTER IX.

Ezra laments the sin of the people because they had taken foreign wives, beseeching God to avert his wrath from his people.

Latin:

CAPUT IX.

Esdras delictum populi quod gentilitias uxores duxerant, deplorat, Deum obsecrans, ut iram avertat a populo suo.

## 9:2
Vers. 2. FOR THEY TOOK OF THEIR DAUGHTERS FOR THEMSELVES AND FOR THEIR SONS) Which was forbidden without exception regarding the Canaanite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite women. Regarding the others, however, the same was established by the wise, unless those women accepted the law. See what we said at 2 Kings 11.

By the reason of the divine law, the other women were also [included], as being likewise given to idols, unless they converted themselves to God: in which case neither were they excluded. For when the reason of the law ceases, the law itself ceases.

THE HAND ALSO OF THE PRINCES AND MAGISTRATES WAS FIRST IN THIS MATTER) Well said Sophocles: And I do not blame the ruler, as those in authority.

Latin:

Vers. 2. TVLERVNT ENIM DE FILIABVS EORVM SIBI ET FILIIS SVIS) Quod sine exceptione vetitum de fœminis Cananæis, Hethæis, Pherezæis, & Jebusæis. De cæteris autem idem constitutum a sapientibus, nisi fœminæ istæ legem susciperent. Vide quæ diximus ad 2. Reg. 11.

VI rationis legis divinæ etiam cæteræ erant mulieres, utpote idolis itidem deditæ, nisi ad Deum se converterent: in quo casu nec illæ arcebantur. Cessante enim ratione legis cessat lex ipsa.

MANVS ETIAM PRINCIPVM ET MAGISTRATVVM FVIT IN HAC RE PRIMA) Bene ut Sophocles: Κ᾽ ἐκ αἰτι ῶμαι κᾶνον, ὥς τοὺς ἐν τέλει.

## 9:3
Vers. 3. I RENT MY MANTLE AND MY TUNIC, AND PLUCKED OUT THE HAIR OF MY HEAD AND BEARD, AND SAT MOURNING) It is a custom for the Jews to tear their garment when they see that God has been offended. We have spoken to Matt. 26, 65. But to pluck, tear, and mangle the hair is the custom of almost all nations, mention of which is found in Homer, who said: they tore their hair, [and in] Virgil, Ovid, Seneca, Martial. It is a different thing to shave the hair, which the law forbids to be done in mourning for the dead, because neighboring nations practiced it.

Latin:

Vers. 3. SCIDI PALLIVM MEVM ET TVNICAM, ET EVELLI CAPILLOS CAPITIS MEI ET BARBÆ, ET SEDI MOERENS) Vestem lacerare mos Judæis, ubi Deum offendi vident. Diximus ad Matth. 26, 65. Comas vero vellere, lacerare, laniare, mos omnium prope gentium, cujus mentio apud Homerum, qui dixit: τίλλοντό τε χαίτας, Virgilium, Ovidium, Senecam, Martialem. Aliud est radere comam, quod in luctu ob mortuos fieri ideo lex vetat, quod vicinæ gentes id usurpabant.

## 9:6
Vers. 6. MY GOD I AM CONFOUNDED AND BLUSH TO LIFT UP MY FACE) An excellent confession and prayer. Pious men speak by way of communion regarding faults, lest they seem to exempt themselves from others too arrogantly: such as that of Brutus: for if we had remembered that we were Romans. See below 10, 2. & Dan. 9. Nehem. 1, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 6. DEVS MEVS CONFVNDOR ET ERVBESCO LEVARE FACIEM MEAM) Egregia confessio & deprecatio. Viri pii κατὰ κοίνωσιν loquuntur de culpis, ne nimium arroganter se cæteris eximere videantur: quale illud est Bruti: quod si Romanos esse meminissemus. Vide infra 10, 2. & Dan. 9. Nehem. 1, 6.

## 9:11
Vers. 11. FROM MOUTH EVEN TO MOUTH. That is, they filled it from every part, just as a vessel is filled from mouth to mouth.

Latin:

Vers. 11. AB ORE VSQUE AD OS. Id est, impleverunt eam ab omni parte, sicut vas impletur ab ore ad os.

## 9:13
Vers. 13. BECAUSE THOU O GOD. Cornelius rightly acknowledges here that the כ [kaph] is translated by Vatablus as NEVERTHELESS: thou nevertheless, O our GOD, hast spared, that thou mightest not cast us down because of our iniquities.

Latin:

Vers. 13. QVIA TU DEUS. Rectius à Vatablo כ verti TAMEN agnoscit hic Cornelius: tu tamen, ô DEUS noster, pepercisti, ne nos deprimeres ob iniquitates nostras.

## 9:15
Vers. 15. FOR IT CANNOT BE STOOD BEFORE THEE UPON THIS. Thus the Vulgate barbarously. In the Hebrew it is: for there is no standing before thee upon this, but that we fall in judgment because of our cause.

PREFACE.

Although by some the book of Nehemiah is called the second [book] of Ezra, which is also observed in the Latin Vulgate, both because it embraces those things which were done by Ezra and Nehemiah, and because among the Hebrews and Greeks it is bound into one volume with the book of Ezra: yet it more rightly comes under the name of the book of Nehemiah: just as also in the Hebrew text the chapters of Nehemiah are numbered separately, and at the beginning the author of the book is prefixed: The Words of Nehemiah: which indeed, since they can be rendered from the source as the deeds of Nehemiah, the author describing his own deeds throughout the whole book speaks almost always in the first person, so that no one may have reason to doubt the author. It is also certain that the same man is called Athersata, ch. 1. 8, 9. But whether this is the same Athersata who [is mentioned in] Ezra 2, 62.

Ezra commands that foreign wives be dismissed, for which task leaders are designated, and their husbands are listed.

Latin:

Vers. 15. NON ENIM STARI POTEST CORAM TE SUPER HOC. Ita barbare vulg. In Eb. non est enim stare coram te super hoc, quin in judicio causa cadamus.

PRÆLOQUIUM.

ETsi nonnullis liber Nehemiæ Esdræ posterior dicatur, quod & in Vulgata Latina observatur, tum quod ea, quæ ab Esdra, & Nehemia gesta sunt complectatur, tum quod apud Ebræos & Græcos in unum volumen compingatur cum libro Esdræ: rectius tamen venit nomine libri Nehemiæ: quemadmodum etiam in Ebræo textu peculiariter Nehemiæ capita numerantur, & sub initium autor libri præfigitur: Verba Nehemiæ: quæ vero cum reddi ex fonte possint res gestæ Nehemiæ, per totum librum sua gesta describens autor sere sub prima persona loquitur, ne quis de autore dubitare habeat. Eundem etiam Athersatam dictum esse, c. 1. 8, 9. constat. Sed num idem Athersates sit, qui Esd. 2, 62. in-

Esdras mandat dimitti uxores gentilitias, ad quod præ- fecti designantur, & mariti earum recensentur.

## 10:1 Argument
Vers. 1. BEFORE THE TEMPLE. Both that he might testify that he was unworthy to enter the temple, and that the people, seeing these things, might be moved to repentance by this example.

Latin:

Vers. 1. ANTE TEMPLUM. TUm ut indignum se testaretur, qui templum ingre- deretur, tum ut populus hæc spectans ad pœniten- tiam exemplo isto moveretur.

## 10:3
Vers. 3. LET US MAKE A COVENANT WITH THE LORD OUR GOD) That is, let us be reconciled to God. THAT WE MAY CAST OUT ALL THE WIVES AND THOSE WHO HAVE BEEN BORN OF THEM) Therefore there prevailed among the Hebrews that law which Theodosius established among the Romans, L. Non dubium C. de Legibus & Constitutionibus Principum, that those things which are prohibited by law, if they have been done, are not only considered useless, but even as if they had not been done. Why then does the Apostle Paul not wish the marriages of Christian men or Christian women with Pagans to be dissolved on the Christian side, 1 Cor. 7? He is speaking to the Corinthians, and to those who were under the same law as the Corinthians, among whom no law of God or man stood in the way of such marriages. But here the children are ordered to follow the mother, as is usually done in illicit marriages, with this cause also added, lest, being educated in superstitions, they might corrupt other children.

However, this case of the conversion of children must also be excepted; they were not to be cast out absolutely, but according to the will of the Lord and the precept of those who fear the Lord, i.e., after instruction had first been attempted. Cornelius teaches, against Bellarmine, that those marriages were indeed illegitimate, yet not in themselves void; they were therefore made void by this special sanction of Ezra for a special cause.

Latin:

Vers. 3. PERCUTIAMUS FOEDUS CUM DOMINO DEO NOSTRO) Id est, reconciliemur Deo. VT PROJICIAMUS VNIVERSAS VXORES ET EOS QVI DE HIS NATI SVNT) Ergo vigebat apud Hebræos jus illud quod apud Romanos constituit Theodosius L. Non dubium C. de Legibus & Constitutionibus Principum, ut ea quæ lege pro- hibentur, si fuerint facta, non solum inutilia, sed pro infectis eti- am habeantur. Cur ergo Paulus Apostolus conjugia Christiano- rum aut Christianarum cum Paganis, dissolvi ex parte Christiana non vult, 1. Cor. 7.? Corinthiis loquitur, & his qui cum Corin- thiis pari jure erant, apud quos talibus conjugiis nulla lex aut Dei aut hominum obstabat. Filii autem hîc jubentur matrem sequi, ut in illicitis nuptiis fieri solet, accedente & hac causa, ne educati in superstitionibus alios pueros corrumperent.

Excipiendus tamen & hic casus conversionis libe- rorum; non absolute projiciendi erant, sed juxta vo- luntatem Domini & præceptum eorum, qui timent Dominum sc. tentata prius informatione. Matrimo- nia illa fuisse quidem illegitima, non tamen per se irrita, contra Bellarm. docet Cornelius, irritata ergo hac speciali Esdræ sanctione ob causam specialem.

## 10:4
Ver. 4. IT IS YOURS TO DECREE) You who have both the highest skill in the Law and have authority from the King of the Persians.

Latin:

Vers. 4. TUUM EST DECERNERE) Qui & summam ha- bes Legis peritiam, & à Rege Persarum potestatem habes.

## 10:5
V. 5. HE ADJURED) He reminded them of their duty by invoking the name of God.

Latin:

V. 5. ADJURAVIT) Dei nomine adhibito eos officii monuit.

## 10:8
Ver. 8. ACCORDING TO THE COUNSEL OF THE PRINCES AND ELDERS) Ezra did not use the authority he had received from the King except to warn the people, and then he left the decision of freedom to the senate.

HIS SUBSTANCE SHALL BE TAKEN AWAY AND HE HIMSELF SHALL BE CAST OUT FROM THE ASSEMBLY OF THE CAPTIVITY) Shall be taken away, understand, in such a way that it becomes sacred to God. For that is what the word יחרם signifies. The LXX: ἀναθεματισται τὰ κτήνη ἀυτοῦ κἀυτὸς ἀλλοτριωθήσεται ἀπὸ τοῦ πλήθεος τῆς ἀιχμαλωσίας. Josephus: ἀπαλλοτριῶσθαι τοῦ πλήθεος, τὴν ὀυσίαν κατὰ τὴν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων κρίσιν ἀφιερωθήσεσθαι. Exile was not among the punishments of the law, but it was permitted for the Senate to add new punishments by new decrees.

Latin:

Vers. 8. JVXTA CONSILIVM PRINCIPVM ET SENIO- RVM) Esdras potestate quam à Rege acceperat non usus nisi ad monendos populares, deinde decernendi libertatem senatui re- liquit.

AVFERETVR SVBSTANTIA EJVS ET IPSE ABJICIE- TVR DE COETV TRANSMIGRATIONIS) Auferetur, in- tellige, ita ut Deo sacra fiat. Id enim significat verbum יחרם LXX. ἀναθεματισται τὰ κτήνη ἀυτοῦ κἀυτὸς ἀλλοτριωθήσεται ἀπὸ τοῦ πλήθεος τῆς ἀιχμαλωσίας. Josephus: ἀπαλλοτριῶσθαι τοῦ πλήθεος, τὴν ὀυσίαν κατὰ τὴν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων κρίσιν ἀφιερωθήσεσθαι. Exilium non erat inter pœnas legis, sed licebat Senatui novis de- cretis novas pœnas addere.

## 10:14
Ver. 14. AND WITH THEM THE ELDERS OF EVERY CITY AND ITS JUDGES) Let those delegated by the senators of the towns come to the common Senate and attest that the divorces have been made.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET CVM HIS SENIORES PER CIVITATEM ET CIVITATEM ET JVDICES EJVS) Delegati ab oppido- rum Senatoribus, ad communem Senatum veniant, & attestentur facta divortia.

## 10:15
Ver. 15. THEREFORE JONATHAN THE SON OF AZAHEL AND JAASIA THE SON OF THECUE STOOD UP OVER THIS) That is, these two from the order of the priests were set over this business, namely among those princes whom he just said were appointed.

Ver. 44. WHO HAD BORNE CHILDREN. In the Hebrew they placed וישימו. Which Junius and Tremellius correctly explain as to the sense: they had taken. For they do not mean that the mothers were exposing their children to the will and judgment of the judges, a matter which pertained not to the women but to the men, and therefore to place children is correctly explained as to bear and to bring to light. Thus also the Vulgate, the LXX, Vatablus, and others. Thus, therefore, Ezra piously reformed even the Economic Hierarchy. God must be entreated to grant Ezra’s twins, who may reform and restore all states, to the glory of His name. Amen.

Latin:

Vers. 15. IGITVR JONATHAN FILIVS AZAHEL ET JAASIA FILIVS THECVE STETERVNT SVPER HOC) Id est, ex sacerdotum ordine hi duo isti negotio præfecti fuere, ni- mirum inter illos principes, quos constitutos modo dixit.

Vers. 44. QUÆ PEPERERANT FILIOS. In Ebr. וישימו posuerunt. Quod quoad sensum recte Jun. & Tremell. exponunt: susceperant. Non enim vo- luntati & arbitrio judicum matres exponebant libe- ros, quæ res non ad mulieres, sed viros spectabat, ideo- que ponere filios per parere & luci exponere recte explicatur. Ita cum Vulgata LXX. Vatablus, alii. Sic ergo pie reformavit Esdras etiam Hierarchiam Oeconomicam. Rogandus Deus est, ut Esdræ geminos, qui status omnes reforment, ac restaurent, concedat, ad sui nominis gloriam. Amen.

# Nehemiah

## 1:1 Introduction
[Abraham Calov, Biblia Veteris Testamenti Illustrata (Vol. 1). English: machine translation, The Faith Received (Mere Orthodoxy); the original follows each comment.]
TATA I OF NEHEMIAH.

He is introduced, and the same Nehemiah who is in Ezra 2:2 seems ambiguous to some. But if Nehemiah already came to Jerusalem under Cyrus with Zerubbabel, assuming that he was then only 25 years old, since he was still flourishing in the 32nd year of Artaxerxes Longimanus (Neh. 13:6), and indeed reached the times of Darius Nothus and the age of Jaddua the High Priest, as is hinted in Neh. 12:22, he must have lived over one hundred and forty years, even if it is established that he saw Jaddua the High Priest in the first years of Darius and died shortly thereafter. It is gathered from 2 Maccabees 1 that Nehemiah was of the priestly order, but that might seem doubtful, since he performed the duty of a cupbearer in the court, which does not befit a priest; and Sulpicius Severus, Isidore of Seville, and Sixtus of Siena judge that he derived his origin from the tribe of Judah.

The chronology of this book is as follows: from the 20th year of Artaxerxes Longimanus, there still remained 21 years in his reign, and 19 of Darius Nothus, which make 40 years. However, how far into the reign of Artaxerxes Mnemon he reached, if he reached it at all, is not clear. But those are mistaken who wish to claim that he lived long enough to see the exception made for Alexander the Great by Jaddua the High Priest. For even if he reached the times of Jaddua, by whom Alexander the Great was received, it does not follow from that that Nehemiah lived until the times in which he himself received him. For could he not have seen Jaddua in the priesthood under Darius Nothus, in the final times of his reign? From whose kingdom until the defeat of Darius Codomannus and Alexander the Great, 46 years elapsed: 21 of Artaxerxes Mnemon, 2 of Ochus, 4 of Arses, and 19 of Codomannus. The sum is 73 years: whence if Nehemiah is set at 31 years of age when he died, Jaddua could have met Alexander at 104 years of age, but Nehemiah would have died already in the final times of Darius Nothus. Mr. Hottinger thinks that the history of 70 years is contained in this book, in Thes. Philol. p. 514, namely from the 20th year of Artaxerxes Longimanus to the last of Codomannus, or the last Darius: but from that year of Longimanus to the end of the Persian Monarchy 113 years elapsed, not just 70, nor is it necessary that we say Nehemiah saw the fates of the Persian Monarchy or the beginnings of the Greek.

The sum of the book is the restoration of the city of Jerusalem, and the correction of the returning people, and of the declining divine worship: the parts of which can be established as two: The first concerning those things which Nehemiah obtained in Persia for the good of the Jews, ch. 1 and 2. The second concerning those things which were done by him in Judea, up to the end of the book, ch. 13, both regarding the reparation of Jerusalem, as far as the walls are concerned, ch. 3, undertaken: and among the impediments of the enemies, ch. 4, complaints because of the famine and usury of the people, ch. 5, the snares of Sanballat and false brothers, ch. 6, continued, and also as far as the gates and the ordination of the gatekeepers, with a census of the people, ch. 7, and as far as the restoration of the covenant, where there is a reading of the law, ch. 8, public confession, ch. 9, the sealing and confirmation of the covenant, ch. 10, and as far as the remaining arrangement, such as of sacred matters, ch. same, of the inhabitants of the city, ch. 11, the dedication of the walls, ch. 12, along with the reformation of certain abuses, ch. 13.

Latin:

TATA I NEHEMIÆ.

Introducitur, idemq; Nehemias, qui Esd. 2, 2, nonnullis ambiguum videtur. Quod si Nehemias jam sub Cyro cum Zorobabele Hierosolymam venit, posito, quod 25. annorum tum tantum fuerit, quum an. 32. Artaxerxis Longimani adhuc floruerit, Neh. 13, 6. imo tempora Da- rii Nothi, & Jadduæ Pontificis ætatem, ut Neh. 12, 22. in- nuitur, attigerit, eum ultra centum & quadraginta annos vixisse oportet, etiam si statuatur primis Darii annis Jadduam Pontificem vidisse, ac paulo post fatis conces- sisse. E Sacerdotali ordine Nehemiam fuisse è 2. Macc. 1. colligitur, sed dubium id videri possit, siquidem in au- la pincernæ munere functus sit, quod non congruit Sa- cerdoti: & de tribu Juda eum ortum traxisse Severus Sulpitius, Isidorus Hispal. & Sixtus Senensis censent.

Chronologia libri hujus haec est : ab Artaxerxis Longi- mani 20. adhuc in regimine ejus restabant 21. an. 19. Darii Nothi, qui efficiunt 40. annos. Quotum vero Artaxerxis Memoris atrigerit, si attigit, non liquet. Falluntur autem qui Alexandri M. exceptionem a Jaddua Pontifice fa- ctam ipsum vivendo attigisse volunt. Nam etiamsi Jad- duae tempora attigerit, a quo Alexander M. exceptus est, non tamen usq; ad illa tempora, quibus ipse eum exce- pit, Nehemiam vixisse inde colligere licet. Annon enim potuit Jadduam in sacerdotio vidisse sub Dario Notho, temporibus regiminis ejus postremis? A cujus regno usque ad devictum Darium Codomannum, & Alexand. M. fluxere anni 46. Artaxerxis Memoriofi 21. Ochi, 2. A- rogi 4. Codomanni. Summa est 73. annorum : unde si de- cedente Nehemia Jaddua statuatur fuisse annorum 31. obviare Alexandro Jaddua potuit 104. annos natus, Ne- hemias vero decessisse jam sub Darii Nothi extrema tempora. Dn. Hotting. historiam q. 70. annorum hoc li- bro contineri putat, in Thes. Philol. p. 514. scilicet a 20. Artaxerxis Longimani ad ultimum Codomanni, seu Darii ultimi : Sed ab isto Longimani anno ad terminum Mo- narchiae Persicae 113. fluxere anni, non vero tantum 70. neque necessum est, ut dicamus Nehemiam fata Monar- chiae Persicae, aut initia Graecae vidisse.

Summa libri est instauratio urbis Jerusalem, & corre- ctio reducis populi, ac labentis cultus divini : cujus partes constitui possunt duae : Prima de iis, quae in Persia obti- nuit Judaeorum bono Nehemias c. 1. & 2. Altera de his quae in Judaea gesta sunt per ipsum, usq; ad finem libri c. 13. tum qua Hierosolymae reparationem, quantum ad mu- ros c. 3. ceptam : & inter impedimenta hostium c. 4. quere- las ob famem & usuras populi, c. 5. insidias Saneballat & falsorum fratrum c. 6. continuatam, nec non quantum ad portas, & janitorum ordinationem, cum computo populi c. 7. tum qua foederis restaurationem ubi legis prae- lectio, c. 8. publica confessio c. 9. foederis obsignatio, & confir- matio c. 10. tum qua reliquam dispositionem utputa rei sacrae c. eod. incolarum urbis c. 11. murorum dedicatio- nis c. 12. cum abusuum quorundam reformatione c. 13.

## 1:1 Argument
PART I. NEHEMIAH'S THANKSGIVING IN PERSIA. CHAPTER I.

The occasion of Nehemiah's prayer, and the prayer itself.

V. 1. THE WORDS OF NEHEMIAH) His departure happened 72 years after that of Ezra. He saw Ezra and outlived him. ראשי הגולה are called the heads of the deportees, Zerubbabel, Mordecai, Joshua, the son of Josedech, and Nehemiah. These, together with the prophets Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi, were prominent in that great assembly of 120 men, which is called by the Hebrews συναγωγὴ μεγάλη. I compare this Nehemiah to Camillus. Both of great virtue: agitated by seditions: restored to their country. Josephus gives him this eulogy: 'He was a man of a good nature and just; and most ambitious for his fellow countrymen, leaving behind for himself an eternal monument, the walls of Jerusalem.'

That the departure of Nehemiah is said to have happened 72 years after the departure of Ezra does not agree with the chronological series. For Ezra departed for Jerusalem in the 7th year of Artaxerxes, Ezra 7, 8. But Nehemiah is said to have departed in the 20th year of Artaxerxes, Neh. 2, 1. Grotius is mistaken in that he thinks the Artaxerxes in whose time Ezra betook himself to Jerusalem, instructed by a decree from the same, is different from this one under whom Nehemiah undertook his departure. For, as far as it appears, he wishes the former to be Artaxerxes Longimanus, but the latter to be this Artaxerxes Mnemon: because from the 7th year of the latter to the 20th of the former, precisely 72 years intervened. But that it was one and the same is the opinion not only of most other chronologists, along with the ancient Doctors, who agree unanimously, but also of Scaliger, whom Grotius followed in these matters regarding Ezra; with whom he also makes the Ahasuerus of Ezra to be Xerxes, and therefore the Darius who is mentioned after Ahasuerus in Ezra 4, 24, to be Darius Nothus. Whence the Artaxerxes of whom Ezra 7 speaks cannot be Artaxerxes Longimanus, but since Darius Nothus follows, it is Artaxerxes Mnemon, if Grotius's opinion is to be consistent; just as it is undoubted for Scaliger that this Artaxerxes is Mnemon. But we have spoken elsewhere about Scaliger's opinion. These things are only according to human reasoning. For to us it is entirely certain that this Artaxerxes of Ezra and Nehemiah is none other than τὸν μακρόχειρα (Longimanus), just as the Darius in Ezra is none other than Darius Hystaspis: under whom the construction of the temple followed.

IN THE CITADEL OF SUSA) Susa is a city known to historians and poets: so called because of its pleasantness from the name of the lily, which is שׁוּשַׁן to the Hebrews, σῦσα to the Persians, as Athenaeus notes: whence also σούσινον μύρον, or χρῖσμα, an ointment made from lilies, is mentioned by the same Athenaeus, Theophrastus, and Dioscorides.

Latin:

PARS I. NEHEMIAE IN PERSIA GRATIA. CAPUT I.

Occasio precationis Nehemiae, & oratio ipsa.

V. 1. VERBA NEHEMIAE) Hujus profectio annis evenit 72. post illam Esdrae. Vidit Esdram eiq; supervixit. ראשי הגולה capita deportatorum vocantur, Zorobabel, Mardochæus, Josua, Josedeei- des, & Nehemias. Hi simulque Prophetæ Aggæus, Zacharias, Mala- chias eminuerunt in magno illo conventu CXX. virorum, qui He- bræis dicitur συναγωγὴ μεγάλη. Huic Nehemiæ Camillum compa- ro. Ambo magnæ virtutis: seditionibus agitati: patriæ suæ restitu- ti. Josephus hoc ei reddit elogium: ἀνὴρ ἐγένετο χρηστὸς τὴν φύσιν καὶ δίκαιος· καὶ περὶ τοὺς ὁμοεθνεῖς φιλοτιμότατος, μνημεῖον αἰώνιον αὑτῷ καταλιπὼν τὰ τῶν ἱεροσολύμων τείχη.

QUod profectio Nehemiæ evenisse dicitur annis 72. post Esdræ profectionem, seriei Chronol. non con- sonat. Nam Esdras an. 7. Artachsastha profectus est Hie- rosolymam Esd. 7, 8. Nehemias autem an. 20. Artachsa- stæ profectus dicitur Neh. 2, 1. Fallitur Grotius in eo, quod diversum Artaxerxem putat illum, cujus tempore Esdras Hierosolymam se contulit, diplomate ab eodem instructus: & hunc, sub quo Nehemias profectionem su- scepit. Nam, quantum apparet, illum priorem Artaxer- xem Longimanum esse vult, posteriorem vero huncce Artaxerxem Memorem : quia ab istius an. 7. ad hujus 20. intercessere præcise 72. anni. At unum, eundemq; fuisse non modo cæteri pleriq; Chronologi, cum antiquis Do- ctoribus, ὁμοθυμαδὸν censent, sed Scaligeri quoq; sen- tentia est, quem sequutus in hisce Esdræ alias est Gro- tius ; cum quo etiam Ahasverum Esdræ Xerxem facit, ac proinde Darium, qui post Ahasverum commemora- tur Esd. 4, 24. Darium Nothum. Unde Artachsastha, de quo Esd. 7. non potest Artaxerxes Longimanus esse, sed quum sequatur Darium Nothum, Artaxerxes Memor est, si constare sibi debeat Grotii sententia; uti Scaligero indubium est, hunc Artaxerxem esse Memoriosum. De sententia autem Scaligeri alias diximus. Haec solum κατ' ἄνθρωπον. Nobis enim omnino certum est, Artaxerxem hunc Esdrae & Nehemiae nullum alium esse quam τὸν μακρόχειρα, uti Darius apud Esdram alius non est, quam Darius Hystaspis: sub quo templi structura successit.

IN SVSIS CASTRO) Susa urbs nota per Historicos & Poetas: sic dicta ob amoenitatem ex nomine lilii, quod שׁוּשַׁן Hebraeis, σῦσα Persis, ut notat Athenaeus: unde & σούσινον μύρον, sive χρῖσμα, unguentum e liliom emoratum eidem Athenaeo, Theophrasto, Dioscoridi.

## 1:3
V. 3. AND THE WALL OF JERUSALEM IS BROKEN DOWN. Some understand this of a new devastation of the city, which had been restored to some extent, made by the Samaritans, but it is more correctly taken as referring to the prior devastation made by Nebuchadnezzar, because the wall is STILL broken down.

Latin:

V. 3. ET MURUS JERUSALEM DISSIPATUS EST. Id de nova devastatione quadantenus instauratae urbis per Samaritas facta intelligunt nonnulli, sed rectius de priori devastatione a Nebucadnezare facta accipitur, quod ADHUC dissipatus sit murus.

## 1:9
Ver. 9. EVEN IF YOU HAVE BEEN BANISHED TO THE ENDS OF THE HEAVENS, FROM THERE I WILL GATHER YOU) Deut. 30, 3. 4.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ETIAMSI ABDVCTI FVERITIS AD EXTREMA COELI, INDE CONGREGABO VOS) Deut. 30, 3. 4.

## 1:11
Ver. 11. BEFORE THIS MAN) He means the king, pointing to him as if with a finger.

FOR I WAS THE KING'S CUPBEARER) You may say in Latin: minister of the cups: many Hebrews obtained no small dignities among foreign Kings: as did Daniel and his companions, and Zerubbabel. You may see the same thing happening in later times among Mahometan Kings in Spain, Africa, Egypt, Persia, and the Turkish empire.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ANTE VIRVM HVNC) Regem intelligit, velut digito eum monstrans.

EGO ENIM ERAM PINCERNA REGIS) Latine dicas; poculorum minister: multis Hebraeis multae apud Reges exteros non modicae dignitates obtigere: ut Danieli & sociis ejus, Zorobabeli. Idem & posteris temporibus evenisse videas apud Mahumetanos Reges in Hispania, Africa, Aegypto, Perside, & Turcarum imperio.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II.

Nehemiah obtains permission to restore the walls in Jerusalem and urges the matter strenuously, with the enemies resisting him in vain.

Ver. 1. IN THE TWENTIETH YEAR OF ARTAXERXES. Josephus thinks it is Xerxes: But he is mistaken. For the 32nd year of this Artaxerxes is numbered below. But Xerxes ruled for only 21 years. Others understand Artaxerxes Mnemon: But since without doubt the same Artaxerxes is commemorated in Ezra 7, who was the successor of Darius Hystaspis after Xerxes, this Longimanus and not Mnemon is to be understood.

Ver. same. AND I TOOK UP THE WINE) The turns of service had not returned to him before.

Ver. same. AND I WAS AS ONE LANGUID BEFORE HIS FACE. The sense in the source is contrary: And I had not been bad (that is, sad) before him previously.

Latin:

CAPUT II.
