Nehemias facultatem restaurandi muros in Jerusalem impetrat & rem strenue urget, nequicquam hostibus ei resistentibus.

Vers. 1. ANNO VIGESIMO ARTAXERXIS. Josephus Xerxem esse putat: Sed fallitur. Nam hujus Artaxerxis infra numeratur annus 32. At Xerxes 21. annis tantum praefuit. Alii Artaxerxem Memorem intelligunt: Sed quum citra dubium idem Artaxerxes Esdr. 7. commemoretur, qui Longimanus Darii Hystaspis successor post Xerxem fuit, hic Longimanus non vero Memor intelligendus est.

Vers. eod. ET LEVAVI VINVM) Non ante vices ministerii ad ipsum redierant.

Vers. eod. ET ERAM QUASI LANGUIDUS ANTE FACIEM EJUS. Contrarius sensus est in fonte: Et antea non fueram malus (id est, tristis) coram eo.

## 2:3
Ver. 3. THE CITY OF THE HOUSE OF MY FATHER'S SEPULCHRES) Minds are much moved by the monuments of ancestors. He adds nothing about religion, nothing about worship: he knows to whom he is speaking.

Latin:

Vers. 3. CIVITAS DOMVS SEPVLCHRORVM PATRIS MEI) Multum moventur animi monumentis Majorum. Nihil de religione, nihil de cultu addit: scit cui loquatur.

## 2:4
Ver. 4. AND I PRAYED TO THE GOD OF HEAVEN, AND SAID TO THE KING) He who wishes to carry prayers to the King, let him first carry them to God, in whose hand are the hearts of Kings.

Latin:

Vers. 4. ET ORAVI DEVM COELI, ET DIXI AD REGEM) Qui preces ad Regem perferre vult, prius ad Deum perferat, cujus in manu corda sunt Regum.

## 2:8
Ver. 8. TO ASAPH THE KEEPER OF THE KING'S SAFETY) Of the paradise, as the Hebrew text has it. And that region which stretches from Lebanon to Antilibanus was called by this name.

THE GATES OF THE TOWER OF THE HOUSE) The palace seems to be understood: for Ezra had finished the Temple: but he does not call it the palace, lest he cast suspicion of revolution upon the King. That very palace seems to be indicated below in the Hebrew, by the leaf of the Prince 3, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 8. AD ASAPH CVSTODEM SALVTIS REGIS) Paradisi, ut habet textus Hebraeus. Sic autem vocabatur regio illa quae a Libano ad Antilibanum se porrigit.

PORTAS TVRRIS DOMVS) Regia videtur intelligi: nam Templum Esdras perfecerat: non vocat autem regiam, ne Regi suspicionem injiciat rerum novarum. Ea ipsa regia infra indicari videtur in Hebraeo, per folium Principis 3, 7.

## 2:10
V. 10. AND SANBALLAT THE HORONITE HEARD) A petty king in the land of Moab, a part of which is Horonaim; Is. 15, 5. Jer. 48, 3. 5. & 39. This Sanballat is he who later gave counsel to Alexander the Great to build the Garizitan Temple to divide the Hebrews.

This Sanballat the Horonite is clearly different: whose son-in-law was expelled from the temple by Nehemiah in the time of Darius, not Codomannus, as Scaliger wishes, but Nothus, Neh. 12, 22, C. 13. 28. whose son or grandson seems to be the other Sanballat, the father-in-law of Manasseh, who was driven from the temple and city not by Nehemiah but by the brother of Jaddua, according to Josephus. Whence this later Sanballat built a temple on Mount Garizim.

Latin:

V. 10. ET AVDIERVNT SANABALLAT CHORONITES) Regulus in Moabitide, cujus pars Choronaim; Es. 15, 5. Jer. 48, 3. 5. & 39. Hic Sanaballetes is est qui postea Alexandro Magno consilium dedit excitandi Templum Garizitanum ad dividendos Hebraeos.

Diversus plane est hic Sanaballat Horonites: cujus gener a Nehemia templo ejectus est Darii, non Codomanni, ut vult Scaliger, sed Nothi tempore Neh. 12, 22, C. 13. 28. cujus filius aut nepos videtur alter Sancballat socer Manassis, non a Nehemia sed a fratre Jaddua templo & urbe Josepho teste depulsi. Unde posterior hic Saneballat templum in monte Garizim extruxit.

## 2:11
VER. 11. AND TOBIAS THE AMMONITE SERVANT) Understand servant as a subject of the King of the Persians.

Latin:

Vers. 11. ET TOBIAS SERVVS AMMONITES) Servum intellige, subditum Regi Persarum.

## 2:12
AND I HAD NOT TOLD ANYONE WHAT GOD HAD PUT IN MY HEART TO DO) Nehemiah, as a courtier, had learned both to be silent and to speak in due time.

Latin:

ET NON INDICAVI CVIQVAM QVID DEVS DEDISSET IN GORDE MEO VT FACEREM) Nehemias, ut aulicus, didicerat & tacere & loqui in tempore.

## 2:13
V. 13. THE WALL OF JERUSALEM BROKEN DOWN) Here also in the Hebrew word מַח the letter מ is such as is accustomed to be written at the beginning or middle of a word, placed at the end, no less than in Is. 9:7. I do not think there is a mystery underlying it, but that the copyists imitated the license of the first writer.

Why could the Holy Scripture, which did not place even a tittle rashly, not indicate that the wall of the city was gaping and open, just as it employed that open מ, not the closed one?

Latin:

V. 13. MVRVM JERVSALEM DISSIPATVM) Est & hic in Hebraea voce מַח litera מ qualis initio aut media voce scribi solet, posita in fine, non minus quam Es. 9, 17. Non putem subesse mysterium, sed primi scriptoris licentiam imitatos exscriptores.

Quidni indicare potuit S. S. qui ne apicem quidem temere posuit, murum urbis fuisse hiantem & apertum, uti מ illud apertum adhibuit, non clausum?

## 2:16
VER. 16. BUT THE MAGISTRATES DID NOT KNOW WHERE I HAD GONE) Those who until now had guarded those ruins in the name of the King of the Persians. The opposition of the following words shows this.

TO THE JEWS AND PRIESTS AND MAGISTRATES) Number 150. below 5, 17. See also 4, 14. 19.

Latin:

Vers. 16. MAGISTRATVS AVTEM NESCIEBANT QVO ABIISSEM) Illi qui hucusque illas ruinas Persarum Regis nomine servaverant. Ostendit id oppositio sequentium.

JUDÆIS ET SACERDOTIBUS ET MAGISTRATIBVS) Numero 150. infra 5, 17. Vide & 4, 14. 19.

## 2:20
V. 20. BUT YOU HAVE NO PART AND RIGHT AND MEMORIAL IN JERUSALEM) See a similar passage in 1 Esdras 4, 3. He says this: you shall have neither part in the labor, nor in the merit, nor in the fame.

PART II. NEHEMIAH'S DEEDS IN JUDEA.

SECTION I. REGARDING THE REPAIR OF THE CITY.

Latin:

V. 20. VOBIS AVTEM NON EST PARS ET JVSTITIA ET MEMORIA IN JERVSALEM) Simile vide 1. Esdræ 4, 3. Hoc di- cit : neq; in labore partem habebitis, neq; in merito, neq; in fama.

PARS II. NEHEMIÆ IN JUDÆA GESTA.

SECTIO I. QUOAD URBIS REPARATIONEM.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III.

It is recounted which part of the wall, which towers and gates, each person built.

Ver. 1. SHEEP GATE) Προβατικὴν. John 5, 2. This gate was so called because through it sheep and oxen to be sacrificed were led into the city, so that, having been washed in the sheep pool, they might be brought into the temple. There were, however, twelve principal gates of Jerusalem situated on the three sides of the city, each of which had four gates: the fourth side, looking toward the south, had no gate because there the precipitous rocks of Mount Zion enclosed the city and denied exit and entrance. The eastern side likewise had first the sheep gate, called προβατικὴν, in which was the cattle market and that pool consisting of five porticoes named Bethesda, John 5, 2; which, as Junius judges, it is likely was adorned from this time on as a sign of the approval of this restoration by that heavenly miracle of which John 5, 4 speaks. Secondly, the horse gate, through which horses were led to water at the torrent of Kidron; thirdly, the water gate, so called from the collection of the waters of the fountain of Siloam, which Hezekiah made in that place; fourthly, the pottery gate, for the reason that potters exercised their pottery craft next to it. The northern side of the city had first the gate of Benjamin, because through it one went into the lot of the tribe of Benjamin; secondly, the fish gate, of which v. 3, through which fish were brought into the city and the fish market; thirdly, the judicial gate, in which judges sat and exercised judgments for both foreigners and citizens, which was near the temple and the sheep gate; and in v. 6 it is called the old gate according to some, for the reason that in it the traces of the old structure of the Jebusites and Melchizedek existed. Junius and Tremellius say it is called the old one because it had been of the former wall, from Josephus, book 6, of the Jewish War, ch. 6. Fourthly, the gate of Ephraim, through which, namely, one went to the tribe of Ephraim. The western side had first the corner gate, so called because it consisted in the western and northern corner of the city; secondly, the valley gate, not of Jehoshaphat, but of the corpses and Calvary, ch. 11, 13; thirdly, the dung gate, through which dung was carried out; fourthly, the fountain gate: where waters leaped or were vomited forth from the mouth of a bronze or stone dragon, ch. 2, 13. See Villalpando, Adrichom, Borchard. The Apocalypse 21, 12 alludes to these twelve gates of Jerusalem.

Ver. same. AS FAR AS THE TOWER OF A HUNDRED CUBITS. Situated between the sheep gate and the tower of Hananel, perhaps so called because it was distant by a hundred cubits from each place.

Latin:

CAPUT III.

Recensetur, quam quisque muri partem, quas turres & portas ædificavit.

Vers. 1. PORTAM GREGIS) Προβατικὴν. Joan. 5, 2. DIcta ita est hæc porta, quia per eam oves, & boves immolandi in urbem inducebantur, ut abluti in pro batica piscina in templum inferrentur. Erant autem XII. portæ præcipuæ Hierosolymæ ad tria urbis latera sitæ, quorum quodvis quatuor habebat portas : latus a. quartum meridiem respiciens, quia illic præruptæ rupes montis Sion urbem claudebant, exitumq; & introitum negabant, portam nullam habebat. Orientale item; latus primo portam gregis habebat προβατικὴν dictam, in qua erat forum pecuarium, & piscina illa quinq; porticu- bus constans nomine Bethesda Joh. 5, 2. quam Junio cen- sente, verisimile est inde ab hoc tempore in signum ap- probatæ hujus instaurationis fuisse ornatum cœlesti illo miraculo, de quo Joh. 5, 4. Secundo portam equorum, per quam equi ducebantur aquatum ad torrentem Cedron; tertio portam aquarum, ita dictam à collectione aqua- rum fontis Siloë, quam ibidem fecit Ezechias : quarto fictilem, eo quod juxta eam figuli suam figulinam exer- cerent. Septentrionale urbis latus habebat primo por- tam Benjamin, quia per eam ibatur in sortem tribus Ben- jamin : secundo portam piscium, de qua v. 3. per quam pisces in urbem & forum piscium invehebantur ; tertio portam judiciariam, in qua sedebant judices, & judicia tam advenarum, quam civium exercebant, quæ erat vi- cina templo, & portæ gregis ; & v. 6. vocatur porta ve- tus juxta nonnullos, eo quod in ea veteris fabricæ Jebu- sæorum & Melchisedech vestigia extarent. Jun. & Tre- mell. veterem dictam ajunt, quia muri prioris fuerat è Jo- seph. l. 6. de bell. Jud. c. 6. Quarto portam Ephraim per quam sc. ibatur ad tribum Ephraim. Occidentale latus habebat primo portam anguli, ita dictam, quod in angu- lo urbis occidentali, & Aquilonari consisteret : secun- do portam vallis non Josaphati, sed cadaverum & Cal- variæ c. 11, 13. tertio portam sterquilinii, per quam sterco- ra evehebantur : quarto portam fontis : ubi ex Dra- conis ænei vel lapidei ore aquæ saliebant, vel evome- bantur c. 2, 13. Vid. Vilalpand. Adrichom. Borchard. Ad has XII. portas Jerusalem alluditur Ap. 21, 12.

Vers. eod. USQUE AD TURRIM CENTUM CUBITORUM. Sitam inter portam gregis, & turrim Hananeëlis forte ita dictã, quod centenis cubitis ab utroq; loco distaret.

## 3:5
Ver. 5. BUT THEIR NOBLES DID NOT PUT THEIR NECKS TO THE WORK OF THE LORD) Tacitus, Annals 3. I consider it the chief duty of annals that virtues not be passed over in silence, and that there be fear of posterity and infamy for evil words and deeds. He notes them as ungrateful, like Deborah the Merozites, Judges 5, 23.

Latin:

Vers. 5. OPTIMATES AVTEM EORVM NON SVPPO- SVERVNT COLLA SVA IN OPERE DOMINI) Tacitus Annal. 3. Præcipuum munus annalium reor, ne virtutes sileantur, utque prave dictis factisque ex posteritate & infamia metus sit. Notat eos ingrati animi ut Debora Merozitas Jud, 5. 23.

## 3:7
Ver. 7. FOR THE GOVERNOR WHO WAS IN THE REGION BEYOND THE RIVER. Osiander amends from the Hebrew thus: to the throne of the governor: explaining it thus: which towns belonged to the jurisdiction of the Persian governor who was in the region beyond the river Euphrates. Junius takes it synecdochically for the praetorium (of which ch. 2, 8) of Judea, which is on this side of the Euphrates.

Latin:

Vers. 7. PRO DUCE QUI ERAT IN REGIO- NE TRANS FLUMEN. Emendat Osiander ex Ebr. ita : ad solium ducis : fic explicans : quæ oppida pertinebant ad ditionem gu- bernatoris Persici, qui erat in regione trans flumen Eu- phratem. Junius de prætorio accipit Synecdochice (de quo c. 2, 8.) Judæa, quæ est cis Euphratem.

## 3:9
Ver. 9. PRINCEPS VICI JERUSALEM) In the Hebrew: Prince of half of Jerusalem: and in the same way below 12. so that it should be understood that there were two prefects of the works, namely for the two sides of the city. See below 4, 19.

Latin:

Vers. 9. PRINCEPS VICI JERVSALEM) In Hebræo : Prin- ceps dimidiæ partis Jerusalem : & eodem modo infra 12. ita ut in- telligi debeant duo fuisse præfecti operibus, ad duo scilicet urbis latera. Vide infra 4, 19.

## 3:12
Ver. 12. SELLUM FILIUS ALOHES) Others think לוחש is a common noun, and that this Sellum was the son of an enchanter, that is, of someone skilled in enchanting serpents.

Latin:

Vers. 12. SELLVM FILIVS ALOHES) Alii לוחש commu- ne esse nomen putant, & hunc Sellum filium fuisse incantatoris, id est, alicujus periti ad serpentes incantandos.

## 3:30
V. 30. POST EUM) Certain Hebrew Codices have here and a little later אחרי after me, so that Nehemiah might hint at his own labor more modestly than boastfully: as also below 4, 16. c. 5, 16. Josephus: ὑποσχόμενος δὲ κὰὶ αὐτὸς μετὰ τῶν οἰκετῶν συλλήψεσθαι πρὸς τὴν οἰκοδομίαν. This is a great thing in a man of such authority.

Latin:

V. 30. POST EVM) Quidam Hebræi Codices habent hîc & pau- lo post אחרי post me, ut suum quoq; laborem Nehemias mode- ste magis innuat quam arroganter jactet : ut & infra 4, 16. c. 5, 16. Josephus: ὑποσχόμενος δὲ κὰὶ αὐτὸς μετὰ τῶν οἰκετῶν συλλήψεσθαι πρὸς τὴν οἰκοδομίαν. Magnum hoc in tantæ auctoritatis viro.

## 4:1 Argument
CHAPTER IV.

While the enemies mock the building of the city and attempt to disturb it, Nehemiah prays, and the Jews build with one hand, and hold a sword with the other.

Latin:

CAPUT IV.

Hostibus ædificationem urbis ludificantibus, & turbare co- nantibus precatur Nehemias, & Judæi una manu fa- bricant, altera gladium tenent.

## 4:3
V. 3. SI ASCENDERIT VULPES, TRANSIELIT MURUM EORUM LAPIDEUM) As Remus did the Roman walls. Thus the despised work grew more safely, God directing this.

Latin:

V. 3. SI ASCENDERIT VVLPES, TRANSIELIT MVRVM EORVM LAPIDEVM) Vt Remus Romana mœnia. Ita contem- tum opus tutius crēvit, Deo hoc dirigente.

## 4:5
V. 5. NE OPERIAS INIQUITATEM EORUM. He does not pray that He may not forgive the penitent, but that God may not pardon the punishment of those persisting in guilt and the impenitent. This prayer proceeded not from carnal wrath but from divine zeal.

Latin:

V. 5. NE OPERIAS INIQVITATEM EORVM. Non precatur, ut non ignoscat pœnitentibus, sed ne in culpa persistentibus, & impœnitentibus condo- net Deus pœnam. Non ex carnali iracundia sed Zelo divino profecta est hæc oratio.

## 4:9
V. 9. ET POSUIMUS CUSTODES SUPER MURUM) A just defense by the King's edict against the Satraps preparing to break the King's edict. See the prudence of Nehemiah, who does not interrupt the watches day or night, opposes a part of the people to the enemy, orders others to be intent on the work, and not even these unarmed, just as is usually done in fortifying camps.

Latin:

V. 9. ET POSVIMVS CVSTODES SVPER MVRVM) Justa defensio ex Regis edicto contra Satrapas edictum Regis frangere parantes. Vide prudentiam Nehemiæ, qui diu noctuque custo- dias non intermittit, partem populi opponit hosti, alios operi in- tentos esse jubet, & ne hos quidem inermes, plane ut in castris mu- niendis fieri solet,

## 4:12
V. 12. FACTUM EST AUTEM VENIENTIBUS JUDEIS QUI HABITABANT JUXTA EOS) It is of great use in war to have those among the enemy who favor us.

Latin:

V. 12. FACTVM EST AVTEM VENIENTIBVS JVDÆIS QVI HABITABANT JVXTA EOS) Magni in bello usus est ha- bere apud hostes qui nobis faveant.

## 4:14
Vers. 14. DOMINI MAGNI AC TERRIBILIS MEMENTOTE] Whose prophets we have as the authors of this work.

Latin:

Vers. 14. DOMINI MAGNI AC TERRIBILIS MEMEN- TOTE] Cujus Prophetas hujus operis habemus auctores.

## 4:20
Vers. 20. IN LOCO QUOCUNQUE AUDIERITIS CLANGOREM TUBÆ, ILLUC CONCURRITE AD NOS) The signal for battle. See Procopius, Gothic War 3.

Latin:

Vers. 20. IN LOCO QVOCVNQVE AVDIEKITIS CLAN- GOREM TVBÆ, ILLVC CONCVRRITE AD NOS) Τὸ ἐγκελευσικὸν. Vide Procopium Gotthic. 3.

## 4:22
Vers. 22. UNUSQUISQUE CUM PUERO MANEAT. This is obscure in the common version: The sense is: each one of those who otherwise live in the neighboring villages and towns, now that they are helping the building, should stay overnight in the middle of Jerusalem, and there should be watches through the night and they should proceed with the work during the day.

Latin:

Vers. 22. UNUSQUISQUE CUM PUERO MA- NEAT. Obscurus hic est vulgarius: Sensus est: unusquisq; eo- rum qui alias in vicinis pagis & oppidis habitant, nunc v. ædificium adjuvant, pernoctet in medio Jerusalem, & sint custodiæ per noctem & interdiu in opere pergant.

## 4:23
Vers. 23. EVERY ONE WAS ONLY STRIPPED FOR BAPTISM) In the Hebrew: Every one let down that (namely, the garment) to the waters. This is an exception to what had preceded: we did not lay aside our garments, namely, except καθαρισμῦ ἕνεκα, for the sake of ablutions, as prescribed by the law or introduced by custom. See Mark 7, 4. 8. Others take it in the contrary sense: every one let go the water, i.e., we did not even lay aside our garments for Levitical ablutions, lest the enemy should suddenly overwhelm us unprepared: because in ceremonial matters necessity has no law: the version of the Blessed Luther also has this. Junius, Piscator, and the Geneva version render it: let every one have his spear and water in readiness: the Italian version: every one (went) to the water (to fetch it) with his arms: the English and Spanish versions agree with Grotius: Avenarius in his Lexicon, which approaches most closely to the Hebrew text, agrees with the Italian version. For שלחו is a spear: nor does the Vau occur here:

Latin:

Vers. 23. UNUSQVISQVE TANTUM NUDABATUR AD BAPTISMUM) In Hebr. Unusquisq; dimittebat illud (nempe vesti- mentum) ad aquas. Exceptio est ejus, quod præcesserat: non depone- bamus vestimenta nostra, nempe nisi καθαρισμῦ ἕνεκα, ob ablutio- nes, ut lege præceptas, aut moribus introductas. Vide Marc. 7, 4. 8. Sensu contrario alii: unusquisq; intermittebat aquams q. d. ne quidem ad ablutiones Leviticas deponebamus vestes, ne hostes subito nos opprimerent imparatos: quia in ceremonialibus necessitas non habet legem: sic etiam B. Lutheri versio habet. Jun. Piscat. Gen. reddunt: unusquisq; habeat hastam suam & aquam in promtu: Ital. versio : quisque (ibat) aquam (allaturus) cum armis suis: Grotio consentit Angl. & Hispan. versio: Italicæ versioni Avenarius in Lex. quæ Ebræo textui proxime accedit. שלחו enim est lancea : nec Vau hic occurrit:

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V.

At the cry of the poor, Nehemiah rebukes the wealthy misers, forbids usury, and distributes his own.

Latin:

CAPUT V.

In pauperum clamore Nehem. opulentos avaros objurgat, usuras vetat, sua distribuit

## 5:3
V. 3. LET US TAKE CORN FOR THE PRICE OF THEM) For it was permitted to a father in necessity to sell his son or daughter. Ex. 21, 7.

Latin:

V. 3. ACCIPIAMUS PRO PRETIO EORUM FRUMENTUM) Licebat enim patri in necessitate filium aut filiam vendere. Ex. 21, 7.

## 5:4
Vers. 4. LET US BORROW MONEY) Namely, under the burden of usury, as appears in 5, 7, contrary to the law of Exod. 22, 25. Levit. 25, 36. 37. Deut. 23, 19. 20.

FOR THE KING'S TRIBUTES) That we may have wherewith to pay tributes to the King of the Persians. Similar is that of Tacitus concerning the Frisians, upon whom a tribute was imposed by the Romans. And at first they gave their oxen, soon their fields, and lastly they surrendered the bodies of their wives or children to servitude. Annals 4.

Latin:

Vers. 4. MUTUO SUMAMUS PECUNIAS) Nempe sub one- re usurarum, ut apparet 5, 7. contra legem Exod. 22, 25. Levit. 25, 36. 37. Deut. 23, 19. 20.

IN TRIBUTA REGIS) Vt habeamus, unde tributa penda- mus Regi Persarum. Simile illud Taciti de Frisiis, quibus a Roma- nis tributum simpositum. Ac primo boves ipsos, mox agros, postre- mo corpora conjugum aut liberorum servitio tradebant. Annal. 4.

## 5:5
Vers. 5. AS THE FLESH OF OUR BRETHREN, SO IS OUR FLESH) We are no less men, no less circumcised.

AND WE HAVE NOT WHEREWITH THEY MAY BE REDEEMED, AND OTHERS POSSESS OUR FIELDS AND OUR VINEYARDS) They could not redeem their children, because their goods also were held in pledge. Therefore Caesar, having made an estimation through arbitrators of what the things had been worth before the war, wished them to be handed over to the creditors, so that he might both remove the fear of new accounts and protect the reputation of the debtors. Third [book] of the Civil War.

Latin:

Vers. 5. SICVT CARNES FRATRUM NOSTRORUM, SIC CARNES NOSTRÆ SUNT) Non minus nos homines sumus, non minus circumcisi.

NEC HABEMUS UNDE POSSINT REDIMI, ET AGROS NOSTROS, ET VINEAS NOSTRAS ALII POS- SIDENT) Luere liberos non poterant, quia & bona eorum pi- gnori tenebantur. Ideo Cæsar per arbitros facta æstimatione, quanti res ante bellum fuissent, eas creditoribus transdi voluit, ne & timorem novarum tabularum tolleret, & debitorum tueretur existimationem. Tertio de bello Civili.

## 5:6
Vers. 6. AND I WAS VERY ANGRY) In the Hebrew: and my heart consulted within me: for the word מלך is often found in the Chaldean in the Targums with that meaning.

Latin:

Vers. 6. ET IRATUS SUM NIMIS) In Hebræo: & consul- tavit cor meum in me: nam eo fignificatu vox מלך Chaldæa sæpe reperitur in Thargumin.

## 5:8
Vers. 8. WE, AS YOU KNOW, HAVE REDEEMED OUR JEWISH BRETHREN) We, Zerubbabel, Ezra, Nehemiah, have devoted every effort before the King, so that we might restore our countrymen from servitude into liberty and country. In Hebrew, for 'we redeemed' is 'we acquired'. YOU SHALL SELL YOUR BRETHREN] For that was to be expected, since they were not being redeemed. See what is at Matthew 18:25. Verse 10. LET US FORGIVE THE DEBT WHICH IS OWED TO US) In Hebrew: let us remit, I pray, this burden: that is, the interest, Verse 11. RESTORE TO THEM THIS DAY THEIR FIELDS AND THEIR VINEYARDS) As if in a Jubilee, to which this time had equal joy. Verse the same. AND THE HUNDREDTH. The hundredth, i.e., the interest, by which they exacted one for every hundred each month. Verse 13. I SHOOK OUT MY BOSOM. Junius & Tremellius: I shook out my arm: that is, with my cloak shaken out, I drew out my arm. Synecdoche. Verse the same. AND ALL THE MULTITUDE SAID, AMEN) As if they were saying: we will and we command. Verse 14. THE PROVISIONS WHICH WERE OWED TO THE GOVERNORS) By governors, understand those whom the King of Persia had set over that region and its inhabitants, as we said at 2:16. Verse 15. IN BREAD AND WINE. The Hebrew texts have it otherwise here: receiving of bread and wine after or besides forty silver shekels: which was a huge sum: because they received daily 20 Joachimics, that is, 7300 thalers per year. AND THEIR MINISTERS OPPRESSED THE PEOPLE) In the Greek of the Sixtine Edition it is here ἐξουσίαζοντες, as in Luke 22:25. Cato the Elder was very similar to Nehemiah, who was in no part burdensome to his associates, and did not even accept those things which custom allowed, because he said he preferred to contend with the best men regarding virtue than with the richest regarding money. Verse 17. WERE AT MY TABLE) That also is worthy of a princely man, to receive noble men, whether fellow citizens or strangers, magnificently. V. 18. AMONG TEN DAYS VARIOUS WINES. Cornelius recognizes that Vatablus more aptly renders the Hebrew and Greek thus: on every tenth day wine was given to all in abundance, but on the other nine days a certain measure. Junius explains: a certain ration of wine was distributed every tenth day to each of their families.

perfected in deeds, and confirmed in every part. Verse 18. FOR THERE WERE MANY IN JUDAH HAVING HIS OATH) Bound by a secret covenant with Tobiah. Verse 19. AND TOBIAH SENT LETTERS TO TERRIFY ME] In the same manner as above in 6.

Latin:

Vers. 8. NOS, UT SCITIS, REDEMIMUS FRATRES NOSTROS JVDÆOS) Nos Zorobabel, Esdras, Nehemias omnem dedimus operam apud Regem, ut populares nostros ex fervitute in libertatem ac patriam restitueremus. In Hebr. pro redemimus est acquisivimus. VENDETIS FRATRES VESTROS] Id enim expectan- dum erat, cum non luerentur. Videte quæ ad Matth. 18, 25. Vers. 10. ÆS ALIENVM CONCEDAMUS QVOD DE- BETVR NOBIS) In Hebræo: remittamus quæso hoc onus: id est, usuras, ut intelligi datur ex sequentibus. Vers. 11. REDDITE EIS HODIE AGROS SUOS ET VI- NEAS SVAS) Quasi in Jubilæo, cui parem lætitiam hoc tem- pus habebat. Vers. eod. ET CENTESIMAM. Centesimam, sc. usuram, qua singulis mensibus unum pro centum exigebant. Vers. 13. EXCVSSI SINUM MEUM. Jun. & Tremell. lacertum meum excussi: id est, ex- cusso pallio lacertum eduxi. Synecdoche. Vers. eod. ET DIXIT VNIVERSA MVLTITVDO, AMEN) Quasi dicerent; volumus ac jubemus. Vers. 14. ANNONAS QVÆ DVCIBVS DEBEBANTVR) Duces intellige eos, quos Rex Persarum regioni isti & habitato- ribus præfecerat, ut diximus 2, 16. Vers. 15. IN PANE ET VINO. Aliter hic habent Ebræa: accipientes de pane & pino post vel præter argenti siclos quadragenos: quæ in- gens erat summa: quia quotidie accepere ita 20. Joa- chimicos, h. e. per annum 7300. thaleros. ET MINISTRI EORVM DEPRESSERVNT POPV- LVM) In Græco Sixtinæ Editionis hic est, ἐξουσίαζοντες, ut apud Lucam 22, 25. Nehemiæ valde similis fuit Cato major, qui sociis nulla in parte gravis fuit, ac ne ea quidem accepit, quæ mos ferebat,quod diceret, malle se cum optimis de virtute, quam cum ditissimis de pecunia certare. Vers. 17. IN MENSA MEA ERANT) Id quoque dignum viro principe, viros nobiles, sive populares, sive extraneos ma- gnifice excipere. V. 18. INTER DIES DECEM VINA DIVERSA. ## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI.

The enemies lay snares for Nehemiah, summoning him four times for the sake of a treaty, soon accusing him of aspiring to the kingdom, then sending false prophets against him, suborning traitors, all of which he dissipates with prudence and greatness of spirit.

Latin:

CAPUT VI.

Hostes insidias tendunt Nehemiæ, fœderis causa eum qua- ter accersentes, mox regni affectati eum arguentes, tum Pseudo-Prophetas contra eum submittentes, prodito- res subornantes, quæ omnia dissipat prudentia, & ma- gnitudine animi.

## 6:3
Vers. 3. I SENT THEREFORE MESSENGERS TO THEM, SAYING I AM DOING A GREAT WORK, AND I CANNOT COME DOWN) It is enough to avoid and dissimulate deceits. Calumnies, however, must be spiritedly refuted, as Nehemiah does in the following. V. 11. SHALL ANY MAN LIKE ME FLEE?) Tyrtæus. AND WHO AS I SHALL ENTER THE TEMPLE, AND LIVE?) That is, for the sake of preserving life. Understand by temple that basilica into which it was lawful for priests alone to enter. Junius and Tremellius summon this, because it was not lawful by the law for an outsider to enter the temple. Num. 3, 38. But Nehemiah was of the Jews, Neh. 2, 3. It is more correctly referred to fear, that it is not fitting for a leader to retreat into the temple out of fear of enemies, so that he may live. Vers. 12. THAT GOD HAD NOT SENT HIM) For he had for himself undoubted prophets: Jeremiah, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi. Vers. 14. Nehemiah said these things out of just grief, and zeal not for private vengeance, but for public justice: since they always persisted in this perversity.

## 7:1 Argument
CHAPTER VII.

Guards added to the city. The book of the census of those who had returned from Babylon, and the specification of the gifts offered after the walls were built.

Verse 1. LET NOT THE GATES OF JERUSALEM BE OPENED UNTIL THE HEAT OF THE SUN) That is, before the clear morning. AND WHEN THEY WERE STILL SITTING, THE GATES WERE CLOSED AND BARRED) The gates were closed in the presence of Hanani and Hananiah. Verse 5. I FOUND THE BOOK OF THE CENSUS OF THEM, WHO HAD ASCENDED FIRST) With Ezra: whence it happened that this census was inserted into the book of Ezra rather inconveniently and not without some change, as we said at Ezra 2. This is NOT that census which is read in the book of Ezra, but the first census, which was made in Judah, of those who arrived in Judah under the leader Zerubbabel, although it is the second from that census which was held earlier in Babylon when the journey was being instituted, whence also the variety of numbers arose, as we observed at Ezra 2, and here Junius rightly notes. Therefore, there is no reason for the book of Ezra to be argued against, as if the census made there were recorded inconveniently or were faulty.

Latin:

CAPUT VII.

Urbi custodes additi. Liber recensionis eorum, qui Babylo- ne redierant, & donorum post extructos muros oblato- rum specificatio.

Vers. 1. NON APERIANTUR PORTÆ JERUSALEM USQVE AD CALOREM SOLIS] Id est, ante clarum mane. CUMQVE ADHUC ASSIDERENT CLAUSÆ SUNT PORTÆ ET OPPILATÆ) Claudebantur portæ præsentibus Hanane & Hanania. Vers. 5. INVENI LIBRUM CENSUS EORUM, QVI ASCENDERANT PRIMUM] Cum Esdra: unde factum est, ut hæc recensio Esdræ libro satis incommode & non sine muta- tione quadam insereretur, ut diximus Esdr. 2. NON hæc est recensio illa, quæ in Esdræ libro legi- tur, sed recensio prima, quæ in Judæa facta, eorum qui Duce Zerubabel in Judæam pervenerunt, quamvis ea secunda sit ab illa recensione, quæ prius habita in Babylonia, cum institueretur profectio, unde etiam numerorum varietas orta, uti observavimus ad Esdr. 2. & hic recte animadvertit Junius. Non ergo est, quod arguatur liber Esdræ, quasi recensio ibi facta incom- mode ibi referatur, aut vitiosa sit.

## 7:5
THAT I MIGHT CENSUS THEM) And recall the old urban families into the city. Verse 6. THESE ARE THE CHILDREN OF THE PROVINCE) Born in Chaldea. Verse 64. THESE SOUGHT THEIR RECORD IN THE CENSUS, AND DID NOT FIND IT, AND WERE CAST OUT OF THE PRIESTHOOD) For it is the same, as the jurists say, not to be and not to appear. And he who bases his right on a quality must prove it. They were, however, obliged to show both that they were of the race of Aaron and that their wives were citizens. Josephus notes this here. Verse 65. AND ATHIRSATA SAID) That is, Nehemiah, as appears at 8:9. We warned above at Ezra 2:1 that to some this name seems not proper but common; and that Nehemiah was indeed the Athirsata, but that there, in Ezra, another Athirsata is introduced, and that this Nehemiah is different (according to the opinion of some) who is said to have traveled with Ezra from Babylon to Judah. But in truth, it can be admitted that the same Nehemiah is the author of the book, who traveled with Ezra, and after another journey undertaken again by Royal authority, was a leader, or rather a Royal governor in Judah: since in both catalogs, both that mentioned in Ezra and that recited here in the present chapter, Nehemiah is placed immediately after Zerubbabel and Joshua, nor does such a great age of Nehemiah appear, if he is believed to have traveled with Ezra and to have been established in dignity at that time, even if he reached the reign of the last Darius, which should be considered entirely unusual for that age (as we calculated the years of the count before, and thus all things seem to hold together more correctly if, since the text does not distinguish, we understand these things of the same subject, namely of one and the same Nehemiah and Athirsata, especially because that explanation is simpler, by which what Athirsata decreed for the doubtful and ἀγενεαλογήτοις (unregistered) priests in Ezra 2:63, this same Athirsata is established to have decreed to the same ones, but for the second time, that is, that he confirmed in the second census made in Judah what he had already decreed to them in Babylon in the first census. Verse the same. UNTIL A PRIEST SHOULD STAND LEARNED AND ENLIGHTENED) In Hebrew: A priest with Urim and Thummim: which the Greeks also mean when they say ἱερεὺς φωτίζων (enlightening priest). Urim and Thummim, as we mentioned elsewhere, were not in the second Temple. Nehemiah hoped that God would one day restore them, and thus answer regarding obscure matters.

For through Urim and Thummim God could be consulted in doubtful cases according to the law of Numbers 27:21, such as that one: whether they are to be reckoned to the priestly order or not?

HI QVÆSIERUNT SCRIPTURAM SUAM IN CENSU, ET NON INVENERUNT, ET EJECTI SUNT DE SACERDOTIO) Paria enim sunt, ut aiunt Jurisconsulti, non esse, & non apparere. Verum e- nim vero admitti potest eundem Nehemiam libri au- torem esse, qui cum Esdra profectus, & post aliud itera- to suscepit iter autoritate Regia, ac Dux, vel potius produx Regius in Judæa fuit: siquidem in utroque ca- talogo, tum apud Esdram commemorato, tum hic, præsenti capite recitato, Nehemias Zerubabeli, & Jo- suæ proxime subjungatur, neque tanta Nehemiæ pro- deat ætas, si cum Esdra profectus, illo q; tempore in di- gnitate etiam constitutus jam credatur, utut attigerit i- dem Darii ultimi Imperium, quæ prorsus inusitata isti ævo censenda sit (uti antea computum annorum inivi. mus, adeoque omnia fese rectius habere videantur, si, quum non distinguat textus, de eodem hæc intelliga- mus subjecto, de uno nempe eodemq; Nehemia, & A- thersata, imprimis, quia simplicior illa est explicatio, qua quod Sacerdotibus dubiis & ἀγενεαλογήτοις Α- thersata edixit Esdr. 2, 63. hic idem ille Athersata eis- dem, sed secunda vice edixisse statuitur, quod sc. idem in altera recensione in Judæa facta consirmarit, quod in Babylone iisdem jam edixerat in prima recensione. Vrim & Thu- mim, ut alibi meminimus, in secundo Templo non erat. Spere- bat Nehemias aliquando futurum ut Deus ea restitueret, & sic ad obscura responderet.

Nam per Urim & Thumim poterat in dubiis causis consuli Deus juxta legem Num. 27, 21. qualis erat illa, anne Sacerdotali ordini illi accensendi sunt, nec ne?

## 7:70
V. 15. FIFTY-TWO DAYS. Shown from that time, namely, from which Sanballat had sent this letter. For Josephus teaches that the construction of the walls was completed in two years and three months, whom the Hist. Schol., Cajetan, Vatablus, and Mariana follow. Junius begins these days from when the stone wall had been built, which within the same [time] with doors, bolts, and HVCVSQVE REFERTVR QVID IN COMMENTARIO SCRIPTVM FVERIT, EXIN NEHEMIÆ HISTORIA TEXITUR] This is neither in the Hebrew, nor in the Greek, nor is it placed in its proper place, for from verse 6 the history of Nehemiah is [continued].

If that particle were certain, there would be no reason to doubt that it was placed in its proper place. For although at verse 6 the history of Nehemiah is found, it could nevertheless be continued quite conveniently at verse 70. Meanwhile, it is certain that this passage does not belong to the Canon, as it is not found in the Hebrew text, nor in the Greek Bibles, nor in most Latin ones. Therefore, as Cornelius himself notes, the Greek Corrector and others judge it should be omitted, indeed they reject it, such as Lyranus and Carthuf. And Schvarezins acknowledges, as does Cornelius, that the different character sufficiently argues that these words were inserted, and are neither of the text nor of the faith: how then did it happen that the corrected Bibles at ROME have them? But let us leave that to the Papists.

Vers. 70. BUT SOME OF THE HEADS OF FAMILIES GAVE TO THE WORK.

The contribution and donation is not other and different from that which Ezra describes: which are distinguished I. By time. For that was made when they had arrived at the place in which the house of the Lord was once erected, returning first from Babylon in the seventh year of Artaxerxes Longimanus: but this one happened thirteen years later, when indeed Nehemiah was sent by Artaxerxes Longimanus, in the twentieth year of his reign. Therefore this part of the chapter, which remains from v. 70, does not belong to the little book of the census found by Nehemiah, but it is correct regarding the matter itself that that clause v. 69 was added in some Latin editions: of which we have just spoken.

II. These gifts are also distinguished by their authors: For in the collection of Ezra, some of the heads of the paternal families are referred to γενικῶς (generally), who gave or contributed according to their means. Here, in the first place, the Tirshatha or Nehemiah is referred to separately, who was certainly not the chief there, since it is undoubted that Zerubbabel was in the superior position at the time of Ezra's arrival. But afterwards, the heads of families are referred to; finally, special mention is made of the rest of the people. III. They are also distinguished by the number of the gifts: which others strive in vain to reconcile, and some, seeing that they cannot be reconciled, rashly suspect a corruption of the text. For in Ezra, 61,000 drachmas of gold and 5,000 pounds of silver are counted as contributed, along with one hundred priests' tunics, but no mention is made of any bowls. Here, however, the Tirshatha is said to have contributed 1,000 drachmas of gold, 530 priestly tunics, and besides these, 50 bowls: such a great gift Nehemiah's means certainly did not permit him to contribute in the first journey. The heads of families here are said to have given not 61,000, but only 20,000 drachmas of gold, and not 5,000, but 2,200 minas or pounds of silver: the rest of the people, however, contributed likewise 20,000 drachmas of gold and 2,000 minas or pounds of silver, and besides these, 67 priestly tunics, from which the sum results in 41,000 drachmas of gold, 4,200 minas or pounds of silver, and 597 priestly tunics, as well as 50 bowls.

Vers. 73. BUT THE PRIESTS DWELT.

It is indicated that not only the priests, Levites, and Nethinim, but also all Israel, after the work of the walls was completed, returned in turn, each to their own dwellings in their own cities: and therefore this clause also is different from that which occurs in Ezra 2:70: because there they were first distributed into their cities upon entering Judea under Zerubbabel and Ezra; here, however, they are implied to have returned again to their seats, in which they had already dwelt for 13 years, after the walls were completed under Nehemiah.

SECTION II. DEEDS REGARDING THE RESTORATION OF THE COVENANT.

The people having been called together, the words of the law are read by Ezra; Nehemiah consoles the people and celebrates the feast of tabernacles for seven days, with Ezra reading the law on each day.

Latin:

V. 15. QUINQUAGINTA DUOBUS DIEBUS. Ostend.ab eo sc.tempore, quo miserat Sanaballat i- stamEpistolam. Nam Joseph. docet murorum fabricam perfectam fuisse duobus annis, & tribus mensibus, quem sequuntur Hist. Schol. Cajetan. Vatabl.& Maria- na. Junius dies hosce inchoat ex quo murus lapideus fuerat ædificatus, quod intra eosdem valvis, seris, & ve- HVCVSQVE REFERTVR QVID IN COMMENTARIO SCRIPTVM FVERIT, EXIN NEHEMIÆ HISTORIA TE- XITUR] Hoc neque in Hebræo est, neque in Græco, neque vero suo loco est positum, nam à commate 6. historia Nehemiæ est.

Si certa esset illa particula, loco vero positam esse dubitandum non foret. Nam etsi ad vers. 6. histo- ria Nehemiæ habeatur, continuari tamen illa satis commode v. 70. posset. Interim certum est, quod ea particula ad Canonem non pertineat, utpote quæ non habetur in Ebræo textu, nec in Græcis Bibliis neque in Latinis plerisque. Ideo notante ipso Cornelio Græcus Epanorthotes, alique eam omittendam censet, imo rejiciunt, ut Lyran. & Carthuf. Et agnoscit Schvarezins, ut & Cornelius diversum Characterem satis arguere hæc verba inferta, neque de textu esse, neque de fide: qui ergo factum, quod ea tamen Biblia ROMÆ correcta habeant? Sed id Papistis relinquamus.

Vers. 70. NONNULLI AUTEM DE PRINCIPIBUS FAMILIARUM DEDERUNT IN OPUS.

Non alia est & diversa contributio & donatio, ab ea, quam Esdras describit: quæ distinguuntur I. Tempore. Nam illa facta est cum pervenissent ad locum, in quo domus Domini olim erecta erat, reduces primum è Babylone anno septimo Artaxerxis Longimani: hæc vero contigit tredecim annis post, cum nempe Nehemias missus ab Artaxerxe Longimano fuit, anno imperii ejus vigesimo. Ideo non pertinet hæc particula capitis, quæ à v. 70. restat, ad libellum recensionis à Nehemia inventum sed recte habet, quod ad rem ipsam illa clausula v. 69. in nonnullis editionibus Latinis adjecta: de qua jamjam diximus.

II. Distinguuntur etiam hæc munera autoribus: Nam in collatione Esdræ γενικῶς referuntur e primoribus paternarum familiarum nonnulli, qui pro facultate sua dederint, vel contulerint. Hic v. principe loco Athersata vel Nehemias seorsim refertur, qui illic sane præcipuus non fuit, quum potiori loco Zorobabelem tum fuisse in adventu Esdræ indubium sit. Postmodum vero referuntur principes familiarum; denique peculiaris mentio fit populi reliqui. III. Distinguuntur etiam numero donorum: quem nequicquam alii conciliare satagunt, nonnulli cum conciliari non posse videant, de corruptela textus temere suspicantur. Nam apud Esdram auri drachmæ 61000. & argenti pondo 5000. numerantur collata cum tunicis centum Sacerdotum, nullarum autem phialarum facta est mentio. Hic vero Athersata dicitur auri Drachmas 1000. tunicas Sacerdotales 530. ac præterea phialas 50. contulisse: quantum certe donum ut conferret in prima profectione Nehemias, facultates non permittebant. Principes v. familiarum hic dedisse dicuntur non 61000. sed tantum 20000. drachmas auri, nec 5000. sed 2200. mnas, vel pondo argenti: reliquus autem populus contulit auri drachmas itidem 20000. & argenti mnas vel pondo 2000. ac præterea tunicas Sacerdotales 67. unde summa prodit 41000. drachmarum auri, 4200. mnarum vel pondo argenti, & 597. tunicarum Sacerdotalium ut & 50. phialarum.

Vers. 73. HABITAVERUNT AUTEM SACERDOTES.

Id indicatur, quod non tantum Sacerdotes, Levitæ, & Nathinæi, sed etiam omnis Israel post absolutum opus murorum vicissim quique ad suas habitationes sese receperint in civitates suas: ideoque hæc etiam clausula diversa est ab illa, quæ Esdr. 2, 70. occurrit: quia ibi primum in civitates suas distributi sunt sub ingressum in Judæam sub Zorobabele & Esdra; hic vero denuo sedes suas, in quibus per 13. annos jam habitarant, post absolutos muros repetiisse innuuntur sub Nehemia.

SECTIO II. GESTA QUOAD FOEDERIS RESTAURATIONEM.

Convocato populo præleguntur verba legis ab Es- dra; consolatur populum Nehemias & cele- brat festum tabernaculorum per septem dies prælegente Esdra legem singulis diebus.

## 8:8
Verse 8. AND THEY READ] Esdras and others in different places of the square, as here 9. & 9, 4. You have a similar instance in Acts 2.

Verse of the same. AND THEY READ IN THE BOOK OF THE LAW OF GOD DISTINCTLY, AND PLAINLY TO UNDERSTAND, AND THEY UNDERSTOOD WHEN IT WAS READ] In the Hebrew: And they read in the book in the law of God exposed, placing understanding, and they understood in the reading. The Talmudists interpret the first of these thus: that the book was read in the Chaldean language, which the people understood better; the second, that it was read distinctly by periods and clauses; the third, that the accents were also pronounced.

This interpretation deserves no consideration. They did not read a Targum or any Chaldean paraphrase (for what Chaldean paraphrase existed at that time?), but the Mosaic text itself: nor did they only read, but they also explained the same, so that it might be understood by all: and indeed by an interpretation taken from nowhere else than from Scripture itself. As Junius and Tremellius rightly translated the Hebrew text: for they read that book, the law of God, plainly, and by explaining the sense, they gave understanding through Scripture itself. Whence it is rightly taught from this passage against the Papists that Holy Scripture is clear and the most certain interpreter of itself.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET LEGERUNT] Esdras aliique diversis in lo- cis plateæ, ut hîc 9. & 9, 4. Simile habes Act. 2.

Vers. eod. ET LEGERUNT IN LIBRO LEGIS DEI DISTINCTE, ET APERTE AD INTELLIGENDUM, ET INTELLEXERUNT CUM LEGERETUR] In Hebr. Et legerunt in libro in lege Dei exposita, ponendo intellectum, & intellexerunt in lectione. Quorum primum illud Thalmudistæ sic interpretantur: lectum fuisse librum sermone Chaldaico, quem populus melius intelligebat; alterum, distincte le- ctum per periodos, & commata: tertium, etiam accentus pronunciatos.

NUllum meretur calculum hæc interpretatio. Non Thargum, vel Paraphrasin aliquam Chal- daicam legerunt, (quænam enim Chaldaica para- phrasis exstitit isto tempore?) sed textum ipsum Mosaïcum: nec legerunt solum, sed explicarunt etiam eundem, ut intelligeretur ab omnibus: & qui- dem interpretatione desumta non aliunde, quam ex ipsa Scriptura. Uti recte transtulit Junius ac Tre- mellius textum Ebræum: legebant enim librum il- lum, legem Dei, explanate, & exponendo sensum, da- bant intelligentiam per Scripturam ipsam. Unde re- cte ex hoc loco adversus Pontificios docetur, Scri- pturam Sacram perspicuam esse, & sui ipsius inter- pretem certissimam.

## 9:1 Argument
CHAPTER IX.

The people, having performed public penance, separate themselves from foreigners: the Levites confess the benefits of God and the crimes of the Israelites, and pray for the people, and thus strike a covenant with the Lord.

Latin:

CAPUT IX.

Populus acta publice pœnitentia separat se ab a- lienigenis: Levitæ confitentur Dei beneficia, Israëlitarumque scelera, & pro populo orant, atque ita fœdus cum Domino feriunt.

## 9:3
Verse 3. THEY READ IN THE VOLUME OF THE LAW OF THE LORD THEIR GOD FOUR TIMES IN THE DAY, AND FOUR TIMES THEY CONFESSED) They read and confessed alternately, that is, they praised God (see below 5.) And that at four times of the day, from the first hour to the third, from the third to the sixth, from the sixth to the ninth, from the ninth to the twelfth.

Latin:

Vers. 3. LEGERUNT IN VOLUMINE LEGIS DO- MINI DEI SUI QVATER IN DIE, ET QVATER CONFITEBANTUR) Alternis legebant & confitebantur, id est, laudabant Deum (vide infra 5.) Idque temporibus quatuor diei, à prima hora ad tertiam, à tertia ad sextam, à sexta ad nonam, à nona ad duodecimam.

## 9:6
Verse 6. THOU HAST MADE HEAVEN, AND THE HEAVEN OF HEAVENS) He attributes two things to God, that He is both the creator and the preserver of the universe.

AND THOU GIVEST LIFE TO ALL THESE THINGS) Crops, living creatures, men.

Latin:

Vers. 6. TU FECISTI CŒLUM, ET CŒLUM CŒLORUM) Duo tribuit Deo, quod & opifex sit, & ser- vator universi.

ET TU VIVIFICAS OMNIA HÆC) Sata, animantia, homines.

## 9:7
Vers. 7. OF THE FIRE OF THE CHALDEANS) Concerning Ur. A proper name of a place, which we have also noted to exist in Ammianus. This speech of Nehemiah is excellent and ἐμπαθὴς, both in proclaiming the benefits of God and the faults of the people: and it can be held as a compendium of the entire history up to these times.

Latin:

Vers. 7. DE IGNE CHALDÆORUM) De Ur. No- men proprium loci, quod & apud Ammianum exstare mo- nuimus. Oratio hæc Nehemiæ egregia est & ἐμπαθὴς, tum in beneficiis Dei, tum in culpis populi prædicandis: & haberi potest pro compendio omnis historiæ ad hæc tempora.

## 9:10
Vers. 10. FOR YOU KNEW THAT THEY ACTED PROUDLY AGAINST THEM, AND YOU MADE FOR YOURSELF

NAME AS ON THIS DAY] Ζεὺς γὰρ κολαστὴς ἄγαν ὑπερφρόνων. Nor is there any subject more worthy, in which He may show His power.

Latin:

Vers. 10. COGNOVISTI ENIM QVIA SUPERBE EGERUNT CONTRA EOS, ET FECISTI TIBI

NOMIN SICVT IN HAC DIE] Ζεὺς γὰρ κολαστὴς ἄγαν ὑπερφρόνων. Nec ulla materia dignior, in qua vim su- am ostentet.

## 9:17
Verse 17. AND THEY DID NOT REMEMBER THE WONDERS WHICH HE HAD DONE FOR THEM] The more noteworthy was the ingratitude of the Jews, in that God had shown many miracles to them, and not to other nations. See Matt. 11, 21.

Latin:

Vers. 17. ET NON SVNT RECORDATI MIRABI- LIVM QVÆ FECERAT EIS] Eo notabilius ingrati erant Judæi, quod multa miracula ipsis, non & aliis gentibus, Deus exhibuerat. Vide Matth. 11, 21.

## 9:20
Verse 20. AND YOU GAVE YOUR GOOD SPIRIT, TO TEACH THEM] The Prophetic Spirit, which was in Moses. Not only was the Holy Spirit given to Moses, but also to others, nor is it only the Prophetic Spirit or the gift of prophecy that is treated here, but the gifts of the Holy Spirit in general, which not only taught the Israelites through Moses but also instructed the faithful by internal information, directed them, and governed them in the paths of righteousness. The condition of the faithful in the Old Testament was no different in this respect than it is today. Which the Socinians contend otherwise.

Latin:

Vers. 20. ET SPIRITVM TVVM BONVM DEDI- STI, QVI DOCERET EOS) Spiritum Propheticum, qui in Mose fuit. Non tantum Mosi Spiritus Sanctus datus fuit, sed etiam aliis, nec de Prophetico solum Spiritu, vel dono Prophetiæ hic agitur, sed de Spiritus Sancti do- nis in genere, qui non solum per Mosen Israëlitas docuit, sed fideles quoque interna informatione si- mul erudiit, direxit, & in semitis justitiæ guberna- vit. Non alia hac in parte fuit fidelium in V. T. ratio, quam hodie. Quod alias contendunt So- ciniani.

## 9:28
Verse 28. AND WHEN THEY HAD RESTED THEY RETURNED TO DO EVIL] Catullus: Leisure has destroyed both citizens and blessed cities before. Juvenal: Now we suffer the evils of long peace: luxury, more cruel than arms, has settled upon us. Sallust: But if the virtue of kings and commanders were as effective in peace as in war, human affairs would be more stable and constant: and you would not see one thing carried to another, nor everything changed and mixed. For power is easily retained by those arts by which it was initially acquired. But when sloth has taken the place of labor, and lust and pride the place of continence and equity, fortune is changed along with morals.

Latin:

Vers. 28. CVMQVE REQVIEVISSENT REVERSI SVNT VT FACERENT MALVM] Catullus: Otium & cives prius & beatas Perdidit urbes. Juvenalis: Nunc patimur longæ pacis mala: sævior armis Luxuria incubuit. Sallustius: Quod si Regum atque Imperatorum animi virtus in pace ita ut in bello valeret, æquabilius atque constantius sese res humanæ haberent: neque aliud alio ferri, neque mutari, ac mi- sceri omnia cerneres. Nam imperium facile iis artibus retine- tur, quibus initio partum est. Verum ubi pro labore desidia, pro continentia & æquitate libido atque superbia invasere, for- tuna simul cum moribus immutatur.

## 9:36
Verse 36. THE LAND WHICH YOU GAVE TO OUR FATHERS, TO EAT ITS FRUIT AND ITS GOOD THINGS, AND WE OURSELVES ARE SERVANTS IN IT] The fatherland itself is not a fatherland to us, for some autonomy granted by the Persians did not exempt them from the Persian empire.

Latin:

Vers. 36. TERRA QVAM DEDISTI PATRIBVS NOSTRIS, VT COMEDERENT PANEM EJVS, ET QVÆ BONA SVNT EJVS, ET NOS IPSI SERVI SV- MVS IN EO) Ipsa patria nobis patria non est, nam ἀυτονομία aliqua à Persis concessa ipsos imperio Persico non eximebat.

## 9:37
Verse 37. AND ITS FRUITS ARE MULTIPLIED TO THE KINGS] They pay heavy tributes: concerning which see Ezra 6, 8; ch. 7, 24.

AND TO OUR BEASTS) By forced labor, which is found, as is the Persian word itself.

Latin:

Vers. 37. ET FRVGES EJVS MVLTIPLICANTVR REGIBVS] Gravia pendunt tributa: de quibus Esdra 6, 8. c. 7, 24.

ET JVMENTIS NOSTRIS) Per angarias, quod reper- tum, ut & vox ipsa Persica.

## 9:38
Verse 38. WE MAKE A COVENANT AND WRITE] We renew the promises of the Fathers.

Latin:

Vers. 38. PERCVTIMVS FOEDVS ET SCRIBIMVS] Renovamus Patrum promissa.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAPTER X.

The signers of the covenant are listed, by which the people bind themselves to the precepts of the Lord, and specifically concerning not intermingling with foreigners, concerning keeping the Sabbath, the seventh year, offerings, firstfruits, and tithes.

Verse 1. NOW THE SIGNERS WERE] There was an aristocratic government with an oligarchy from this time of the Hasmoneans. A few Princes like Zerubbabel, Nehemiah, and Ezra ruled the people by the counsel of the Senate and other Magistrates. Afterward the state leaned more toward a democracy, as Josephus notes, and from there, as is wont to happen, tyrannies.

Latin:

CAPUT X.

Signatores fœderis recensentur, quo se obstringit populus ad præcepta Domini, & speciatim de non commiscendo cum alienigenis, de servan- dis Sabbato, anno septimo, oblationibus, pri- mitiis, ac decimis.

Vers. 1. SIGNATORES AVTEM FVERVNT) Fuit πολιτεία ἀριστοκρατικὴ μετ' ὀλιγαρχίας ab hoc tempore As- monæorum. Pauci Principes ut Zorobabel, Nehemia, Es- dras regebant populum de consilio Senatus & aliorum Ma- gistratuum. Postea magis ad δημιοκρατίαν flexit status, ut no- tat Josephus, & inde ut fieri solet, tyrannides.

## 10:28
Verse 27. AND THE REST OF THE PEOPLE] A seed and remnant from the calamity. Josephus.

Vers. 28. ALL WHO WERE ABLE TO BE WISE) In Hebrew: every one knowing, understanding. That is, all who had arrived at the use of reason.

Latin:

Vers. 27. ET RELIQVI DE POPVLO] σπέρματι κἀγ λείψανοι ἐκ τῆς συμφορᾶς. Josephus.

Vers. 28. OMNES QVI POTERANT SAPERE) In Hebræo: omnis sciens, intelligens. Id est, omnes qui ad ra- tionis usum pervenerant.

## 10:29
PLEDGING FOR THEIR BRETHREN THEIR NOBLES, AND WHO WERE COMING TO PROMISE AND TO SWEAR THAT THEY WOULD WALK IN THE LAW OF GOD) In Hebrew: These associated themselves with their fellow nobles by curses and an oath (obliging themselves, to wit) to walk in the law of God. The sense is that what those leaders and senators had signed, they themselves, by using words, and even by curses against those who transgress, and by the religious obligation of an oath, made valid. Thus it was the προβόλευμα of the Princes, the decree of all.

Latin:

SPONDENTES PRO FRATRIBVS SVIS OPTIMA- TES EORVM, ET QVI VENIEBANT AD POLLI- CENDVM ET JVRANDVM VT AMBVLALENT IN LEGE DEI) In Hebræo: Hise associabant popularibus suis optimatibus per diras & juramentum (obligantes scil. se) ad incedendum in lege Dei. Sensus est, quod illi duces & sena- tores signaverant, id ipsi verbis adhibitis, etiam diris in pec- cantes, & jurisjurandi religione, ratum fecerunt. Ita Prin- cipum erat προβόλευμα, scitum omnium.

## 10:30
Vers. 30. AND THAT WE WOULD NOT GIVE OUR DAUGHTERS TO THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND AND WOULD NOT TAKE THEIR DAUGHTERS FOR OUR SONS) Besides the general promise to fulfill all the laws, certain laws are expressed specifically because they might have seemed more difficult to observe: concerning not taking wives from the neighboring peoples, with an interdict added also for the reason of the present time against not giving daughters into their marriage: concerning observing the Sabbath and the sabbatical year: and concerning collections for the uses of the Temple and of the sacrifices: likewise concerning the firstborn, the firstfruits, the tithes: see how diligently Nehemiah caused the commandment concerning observing the Sabbath to be observed in chapter 13, 15 and following.

SECTION III. THE DISPOSITION OF SACRED MATTERS AND OTHERS.

Latin:

Vers. 30. ET VT NON DAREMVS FILIAS NOSTRAS PO- PVLO TERRÆ ET FILIAS EORVM NON ACCI- PEREMVS FILIIS NOSTRIS) Præter promissum generale de implendis legibus universis quædam leges speciatim exprimuntur: quia difficiliores observatu videri poterant: de non sumendis uxoribus ex vicinis populis, addito eti- am ob rationem præsentis temporis interdicto de filiabus in eorum matrimonium non dandis: de servando sabbato, & anno sabbatico: & de collectis ad usus Templi ac sacri- ficiorum: item de primogenitis, primitiis, decimis: de ser- vando sabbato præceptum vide quam diligenter observari fe- cerit Nehemias 13, 15. & sequentibus.

SECTIO III. REI SACRÆ ET ALIARUM DISPOSITIO.

## 10:34
Vers. 34. THEREFORE WE CAST LOTS. Because the number of the lots instituted by David in 1 Chron. 24 et seqq. was not complete, they used a new casting of lots.

Latin:

Vers. 34. SORTES ERGO MISIMUS. Quia sortium à Davide 1. Chron. 24. seqq. in- stitutarum numerus non erat integer, nova usi sunt sortitione.

## 10:38
Vers. 38.

AND THE PRIEST THE SON OF AARON SHALL BE WITH THE LEVITES IN THE TITHES OF THE LEVITES] That is, when the tithes are given to the Levites, certain ones from the Priests shall be present as inspectors, so that they may tithe the tithe itself, according to the law in Num. 18, 26.

AND WE WILL NOT FORSAKE THE HOUSE OF GOD. We will take care of all things which pertain to the uses of the temple and the sustenance of the Priests and Levites.

Latin:

Vers. 38.

ERIT AVTEM SACERDOS FILIVS AARON CVM LEVIT IS IN DECIMIS LEVITARVM ] Id est, ubi de- cimæ dabuntur Levitis, è Sacerdotibus quidam inspectores aderunt, ut ipsam decimam deciment, ex lege Num. 18, 26.

ET NON DIMITTEMUS DOMUM DEI. Curabimus omnia, quæ ad templi usus, & Sacerdotum ac Levitarum sustentationem perti- nent.

## 11:1 Argument
CHAPTER XI. The inhabitants are ordered at Jerusalem by lot, to wit, the tenth part of the people, the rest are sent to other cities and villages of Judea: and so both those and these are enumerated.

Vers. 1.

THE REST OF THE PEOPLE CAST LOTS TO TAKE ONE PART OF TEN WHO WERE TO DWELL IN JERUSALEM] Besides the fact that the old urban families were recalled into the city, a tenth part was also brought there from other towns and villages, so that it might be more frequently inhabited and better defended.

It is hinted in v. 2 that some volunteers also joined them: among whom were some from the Ephraimites and the tribe of Manasseh. But those who are enumerated in v. 4 are those who actually dwelt there. But in 1 Chron. 9, not only these but also the volunteers are enumerated: whence a larger number is held there.

Latin:

CAPUT XI. Hierosolymis incolæ sorte ordinantur, decima sc. populi pars, reliqui ad alias urbes & pagos Judææ mittuntur : adeoque tam illi quam ista recensentur.

Vers. 1.

RELIQVA PLEBS MISIT SORTEM VT TOLLE- RENT VNAM PARTEM DE DECEM QVI HABI- TATVRI ESSENT IN JERVSALEM] Præter quod vete- res urbanæ familiæ in urbem revocatæ sunt, etiam ex aliis op- pidis & vicis pars decima eo deducta, quo frequentius habi- taretur, meliusque defenderetur.

VOluntarios quoque nonnullos iis accessisse v. 2. innuitur : in quibus fuerunt aliqui ex E- phraimitis, & tribu Manassis. Qui vero v. 4. recen- sentur, illi sunt, qui forte ibi habitarunt. At 1. Chron. 9. non hi tantum, sed etiam voluntarii recensiti sunt: unde amplior illic habetur numerus.

## 11:3
Verse 3.

PRINCES OF THE PROVINCE ] That is, those who had come from Chaldea.

AND EVERY ONE DWELT IN HIS POSSESSION IN HIS CITIES OF ISRAEL, THE PRIESTS, THE LEVITES, THE NATHINAEI AND THE CHILDREN OF THE SERVANTS OF SOLOMON ] That is, I shall now enumerate the chief of those who dwelt in Jerusalem: since others of the people, and some even of the Priests and Levites, dwelt in other towns, whom I do not enumerate.

AND THE CHILDREN OF THE SERVANTS OF SOLOMON ] 1 Kings 9, 21. 1 Esdras 2, v. 55.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

PRINCIPES PROVINCIÆ ] Id est, qui è Chaldæa ve- nerant.

HABITAVIT AVTEM VNVSQVISQVE, IN POS- SESSIONE SVA IN VRBIBVS SVIS ISRAEL, SACER- DOTES, LEVITÆ, NATHINÆI ET FILII SERVO- RVM SALOMONIS ] Id est, recensebo jam præcipuos eo- rum, qui Hierosolymis habitarunt : cum alii ex populo, non- nulli etiam ex Sacerdotibus & Levitis, in aliis oppidis habita- rent, quos non recenseo.

ET FILII SERVORVM SALOMONIS ] 1. Reg. 9, 21. 1. Esdr. 2. v. 55.

## 11:11
Verse 11.

ACHITOB PRINCE OF THE HOUSE OF GOD ] στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ: for the high priest was Eliashib.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

ACHITOB PRINCEPS DOMVS DEI ] στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ : nam Pontifex maximus erat Eliafib.

## 11:22
Verse 22.

AND THE OVERSEER OF THE LEVITES IN JERUSALEM, AZZI THE SON OF BANI ] The Hebrew פקיד is translated as ἐπίσκοπος, as also in Num. 4, 16; ch. 31, 14; Judg. 9, 28; 2 Kings 11, 16, 19; 2 Chron. 34, 12, 17. Very well indeed. Thus at Athens, the prefect sent to administer justice to the towns of the Athenian dominion was called ἐπίσκοπος. And in the affairs of the Indians, Arrian calls those who reported what they had learned to the Magistrates by the same name. Cicero says to Atticus that he was appointed by Pompey as ἐπίσκοπος of the seacoast. In the Digest, under the title concerning duties and honors, those who are in charge of bread and goods for sale are called bishops. It is a name of care rather than of dignity. And for that reason, Christians preferred it for the Presidents of the Churches, rather than the Jewish ἀρχισυναγώγους: ראש הקהל.

Latin:

Vers. 22.

ET EPISCOPVS LEVITARVM IN JERVSALEM, AZZI FILIVS BANI ] פקיד Hebræum ἐπίσκοπος verti- tur, ut & Num. 4, 16. c. 31, 14. Jud. 9, 28. 2. Reg. 11, 16. 19. 2. Paral. 34, 12. 17. Bene admodum. Sic Athenis ἐπίσκοπος vocabatur præfectus juri dicundo ad oppida ditionis Athe- niensium missus. Et in rebus Indorum Arrianus eos, qui co- gnita ad Magistratus referrent, eodem vocat nomine. Cicero ad Atticum à Pompejo se ait constitutum ἐπίσκοπον oræ ma- ritimæ. Digestis titulo de muneribus & honoribus, episcopi vocantur, qui præsunt pani & venalibus rebus. Est nomen curæ magis quam dignitatis. Ideoque id maluerunt Christia- ni Ecclesiarum Præsides, quam Judaicum ἀρχισυναγώγους : ראש הקהל.

## 11:36
Verse 36. AND OF THE LEVITES PORTIONS OF JUDA AND BENJAMIN. They did not all dwell together in Jerusalem, but their portions were distributed throughout all the regions of Juda and Benjamin, so that each of them might have its own number, who would teach the inhabitants those things which pertained to the law of God.

Latin:

Vers. 36. ET DE LEVITIS PORTIONES JUDÆ ET BENJAMIN. Non habitabant simul omnes in Jerusalem, sed portiones eorum distributæ erant per omnes regiones Judæ, & Benjamin, ut quæque ex eis suum haberet numerum, qui incolas ea, quæ ad legem Dei spectabant, doceret.

## 12:1 Argument
CHAPTER XII. The leaders of the Priests and Levites and the succession of the high Priests: as also of the walls The dedication of the city, and the confirmation of the functions in the temple.

Latin:

CAPUT XII. Primores Sacerdotum & Levitarum & succes- sio summorum Sacerdotum : nec non murorum urbis dedicatio, ac functionum in templo confirmatio.

## 12:9
Vers. 9. EVERY ONE IN HIS OFFICE) He ministered in his turns: for this is what משמר means here, and משמר below in 22. The Greeks here [use] ἐὶς τὰς ἐφημερίας, and below ἐφημερίαν πρὸς ἐφημερίαν. See what was said on Luke 1, 8.

Latin:

Vers. 9. VNUSQVISQVE IN OFFICIO SUO) Suis vicibus ministrabat : id enim hic משמר, & infra משמר 22. Græci hic ἐὶς τὰς ἐφημερίας, & infra ἐφημερίαν πρὸς ἐφημερίαν. Vide quæ dicta Lucæ 1, 8.

## 12:11
Vers. 11. BEGAT JADDUA] Τὸν Ἰαδὺ [in the] LXX, both here and below in 22. He is the same as Iaddous in Josephus, whom he narrates to have met Alexander, the victor of Tyre and Gaza. Thus the history of the Hebrew Canon ends in the very light of the times, that is, in the affairs of Alexander the Great, from which point all things are now clear, even concerning Jewish affairs through so many Greek writers, many of whom have now perished, as appears from the writings of Jerome on Daniel.

The birth of Jaddua is only touched upon here, but not his priestly age. Nehemiah could have lived long enough to have seen him as a boy, even if he did not see him as a priest. For thus he would have had to live two hundred years. Add to this that Nehemiah could have died long before Jaddua the High Priest met Alexander, who was then quite elderly and perhaps 90 years old.

Latin:

Vers. 11. GENUIT JEDDOA] Τὸν Ἰαδὺ LXX. & hîc & infra 22. Idem est Ἰαδδοὺς Josepho, quem narrat occurrisse Alexandro Tyri & Gazæ victori. Sic historia Canonis Hebræi finit in ipsa luce temporum, id est, in Alexandri Magni rebus, unde omnia jam clara, etiam de Judaicis rebus per tot Græcos scriptores, quorum multi nunc interciderunt, ut apparet ex Hieronymi scriptis ad Danielem.

JAddoa nativitas hic tantum attingitur, non vero Sacerdotalis ætas. Vixisse potuit Nehemias eo usque, ut puerum viderit ipsum, etsi non viderit Sacerdotem. Sic enim debuisset vivere ducentos annos. Adde, quod longe ante decessisse potuerit Nehemias, quam Alexandri obviam factus est Jaddua Pontifex, qui tum admodum grandævus fuit & forte 90. annorum.

## 12:22
Vers. 22. IN THE REIGN OF DARIUS THE PERSIAN) Codomannus, whom Alexander defeated.

Those who understand this as Darius Codomannus think that this verse is not by Nehemiah, who would not have reached his times, but was inserted by another. But it is better to understand Darius Nothus, who was a bastard and the successor of Longimanus. Whom Nehemiah could have seen in his advanced old age.

Latin:

Vers. 22. IN REGNO DARIH PERSÆ) Codomanni quem vicit Alexander.

Qui Darium Codomannum intelligunt, versum hunc non Nehemiæ esse, qui non attigerit ejus tempora, sed ab alio insertum putant. Sed præstat Darium Nothum intelligere, qui spurius fuit & successor Longimani. Quem videre potuit Nehemias in grandæva senectute.

## 12:30
Vers. 30. AND THE PRIESTS AND THE LEVITES WERE PURIFIED, AND THEY PURIFIED THE PEOPLE] For it was necessary that the priests should purify themselves before they could purify others. Understand the same in a more sublime sense regarding Christian priests.

Latin:

Vers. 30. ET MUNDATI SUNT SACERDOTES ET LEVITÆ, ET MVNDAVERUNT POPVLVM] Prius enim erat, ut Sacerdotes se mundarent, quam ut mundare alios possent. Idem sensu sublimiore de Sacerdotibus Christianis intellige.

## 12:46
Vers. 46. AND THEY SANCTIFIED THE LEVITES, AND THE LEVITES SANCTIFIED THE SONS OF AARON] That is, they gave sacred things, for instance tithes, to the Levites, and the Levites gave tithes of their own to the priests.

Latin:

Vers. 46. ET SANCTIFICABANT LEVITAS, ET LEVITÆ SANCTIFICABANT FILIOS AARON] Id est, sacras res, puta decimas dabant Levitis, & Levitæ de suis decimas dabant Sacerdotibus.

## 13:1 Argument
CHAPTER XIII.

Nehemiah, returning to Jerusalem, corrects the association with foreigners, the interruption of the sacred ministry, the violation of the Sabbath, and marriage with aliens.

Vers. 1. AND IT WAS FOUND WRITTEN IN IT] Deut. 23, 3.

Latin:

CAPUT XIII.

Nehemias Hierosolymam revertens exterorum Consortium, intermissionem sacri ministerii, violationem Sabbati, & conjugium cum alienigenis corrigit.

Vers. 1. ET INVENTUM EST SCRIPTUM IN EO] Deut. 23, 3.

## 13:3
Vers. 3. THEY SEPARATED ALL THE FOREIGNERS FROM ISRAEL] That is, those born of the nations, to whom the law had denied the right of marriage and of honors.

Latin:

Vers. 3. SEPARAVERUNT OMNEM ALIENIGENAM AB ISRAEL] Id est, natos ex gentibus, quibus lex noluerat esse jus connubii & honorum.

## 13:6
Vers. 6 BUT IN ALL THESE I WAS NOT IN JERUSALEM, FOR IN THE 32ND YEAR OF ARTAXERXES KING OF BABYLON I CAME UNTO THE KING) He returned to his courtly duty: and after some time he again obtained leave from the King to go to Jerusalem.

Latin:

Vers. 6 IN OMNIBUS AVTEM HIS NON FUI IN JERUSALEM, QVIA ANNO 32. ARTAXERXIS REGIS BABYLONIS VENI AD REGEM) Rediit ad officium suum aulicum: & post aliquod tempus iterum a Rege impetravit veniam eundi Hierosolyma.

## 13:8
Vers. 8. WHICH ELIASHIB HAD DONE FOR TOBIAH) Because of affinity, he had permitted a foreigner, not only to enter within the Israelite enclosures, which was a crime in itself, but also to keep the sacred things: See above 6, 18. and below 28.

Great was the dignity of the prefecture of the Treasury: but not without indignity and harm to Israel was an Ammonite servant set in charge of it.

Latin:

Vers. 8. QVOD FECERAT ELIASIB TOBIÆ) Ob affinitatem, homini alienigenæ, non tantum intrare intra septa Israelitica, quod vel ipsum nefas fuerat, sed & servare res sacras permiserat: Vide supra 6, 18. & infra 28.

MAgna erat dignitas præfectura Gazophylacii: sed non sine indignitate, ac noxa Israelis ei servus Ammonita præfectus fuit.

## 13:8
AND I CAST FORTH THE VESSELS OF THE HOUSE OF TOBIAH) His household furniture. He did this by the power granted to him by the King of the Persians, as in an extraordinary act.

Latin:

ET PROJECI VASA DOMVS TOBIÆ) Domesticam ipsius suppellectilem. Fecit hoc pro potestate sibi a Rege Persarum concessa, ut in facto extraordinario.

## 13:9
Vers. 9. SACRIFICE] מנחה concerning which Levit. 2.

Latin:

Vers. 9. SACRIFICIUM] מנחה de quo Levit. 2.

## 13:13
Vers. 13. BECAUSE THEY WERE CONSIDERED FAITHFUL] In Hebrew: they were held to be. Fame commended them, which does not always err, often chooses: they were pointed out by consensus: no one deceived everyone.

Latin:

Vers. 13. QVONIAM FIDELES COMPROBATI SVNT] In Hebr. habiti sunt. Fama eos commendabat, quæ non errat semper, sæpe eligit: consensu monstrabantur: nemo omnes decepit.

## 13:18
Vers. 18. DID NOT OUR FATHERS DO THESE THINGS, AND DID NOT OUR GOD BRING ALL THIS EVIL UPON US, AND UPON THIS CITY) He refers to Jeremiah 17, 21. and following.

Latin:

Vers. 18. NUMQVID NON HÆC FECERUNT PA- TRES NOSTRI, ET ADDUXIT DEUS NOSTER SU- PER NOS OMNE MALUM HOC, ET SUPER CIVI- TATEM HANC) Respicit ad Jeremiam 17, 21. & sequentibus.

## 13:21
Vers. 21. I WILL LAY MY HAND UPON YOU) I will act by my own right, as above 9.

Latin:

Vers. 21. MANUM MITTAM IN VOS] Agam pro meo jure, ut supra 9.

## 13:24
AND THEIR CHILDREN SPOKE HALF IN THE SPEECH OF ASHDOD, AND COULD NOT SPEAK IN THE JEWS' LANGUAGE.

Latin:

Vers. 24. ET FILII EORUM EX MEDIA PARTE LOQUEBANTUR AZOTICE, ET NESCIEBANT LOQUI JUDAICE.

## 13:25
Vers. 25. AND I REBUKED THEM, AND CURSED THEM] By that word 'cursed' Aben-Ezra understands two kinds of excommunication, נדוי and חרם: but I would believe those were used in exile, when the right of life and death was in the hands of the Persians, and again when capital judgments had passed to the Romans. For there is no mention of those punishments in the law, nor in the ancient history of that people. It is truer, therefore, that Nehemiah used grave words, even with the threat of divine wrath, against those law-breakers.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ET OBJURGAVI EOS, ET MALEDIXI] Per illud maledixi Aben-Esdras intelligit duo excommunica- tionis genera נדוי & חרם : sed ea crediderim in exilio usurpata, cum jus vitæ necisque penes Persas esset, atque iterum cum capitalia judicia ad Romanos devenissent. Nam in lege nulla earum pœnarum mentio, neque in veteri historia populi illius. Verius ergo est, Nehemiam gravibus verbis, etiam cum iræ divinæ comminatione, usum in istos legirupas.

## 13:28
Vers. 28. BUT OF THE SONS OF JOIADA THE SON OF ELIASHIB THE HIGH PRIEST WAS SON-IN-LAW TO SANBALLAT THE HORONITE) Nay, he was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite. For the Hebrew demands that, but so do the Greek.

Latin:

Vers. 28. DE FILIIS AUTEM JOJADA FILII ELIA- SIB SACERDOTIS MAGNI GENER ERAT SANA- BALATTA HORONITES) Imo gener erat Sanaballetæ Horonitæ. Id enim Hebræa exigunt, sed & Græca.

## 13:31
Vers. 31. AND FOR THE WOOD OFFERING, AT TIMES APPOINTED, AND FOR THE FIRSTFRUITS] I caused, namely, that the decree mentioned above in 10:34, 35 should be kept, in memory of which a solemn day of the wood-bearing (ξυλοφορίων) was instituted, which Josephus mentions in book 2 of the Jewish War.

Latin:

Vers. 31. ET IN OBLATIONIBUS LIGNORUM IN TEMPORIBUS, ET IN PRIMITIVIS] Effeci scil. ut fervaretur decretum memoratum supra 10, 34. 35. in cujus rei memoriam institutus solemnis dies ξυλοφορίων, cujus meminit Josephus 2. Belli Judaici.

# Esther

## 1:1 Introduction
