IN. PREFACE TO THE BOOK

See what we have said at the beginning of Chronicles. Often women have been of great benefit to the Hebrews. Even in Po- Vers. 14. REMEMBER ME O MY GOD CONCERNING THIS] So also below 22. 29. 31.

The Ashdodite language is that of the Philistines, a part of whom were the Ashdodites, concerning which Bochart understands ch. 15. what Jerome said about the Canaanite language, that it is halfway between Hebrew and Egyptian, and Hottinger agrees in System. Theol. p. 145. because the names of the gods בעל and זבוב are Hebrew, and דגן is a common name for the Kings of the Philistines אבימלך Gen. 20, 21. 26. as also the name סרן by which the Phoenicians called their princes Jud. 16, 5. 24. from the Hebrew שר; but the Egyptian is Astharoth, Urania Venus, concerning whom Herodotus in Clio, from Tsarot, which denotes Venus to the Egyptians. This Ashdodite language was a dialect of Chaldean: Although indeed the use of the Chaldean language flourished among the Jews in captivity, and after it, as can be seen from Jerem. 10, 11. Dan. 2, 4. up to ch. 8. Ezra 4. v. 8. seqq. (which before the captivity could not be understood by the Jews 2. Kings 18, 26. Jer. 5, 18.) Yet the dialects of the Chaldean language could not be understood at all by the Jews: such as Hottinger in book 5 makes that Azotic language, as well as the Punic language, which Postellus indeed calls a twin of the Hebrew, Bochart a dialect of the same, and Amama and Selden judge, according to the verses of Plautus in the Poenulus, to have more Hebraism than Chaldaism, as Hottinger judges; but Wafer in his Mithridates and Fuller in book 4 of his Miscellanies, chapter 10, say it is akin to the Syriac: and then the Syriac: which, although it was once the very language of the Chaldeans, after the Babylonian captivity it emerged as a third language distinct from both in letters and formation, arising from Chaldaism and Hebraism, but it is closer to the Chaldean idiom than to the Hebrew.

WHOM I CHASED FROM ME) Not Sanballat the satrap in Moab, but I ordered that grandson of Eliashib to depart, according to the decree of Ezra 10:8.

REMEMBER ME O MY GOD FOR GOOD. AMEN.

The little word Amen is not found in the Hebrew. It was therefore added rashly. But with that excellent sigh I also seal this work. Remember me O my God for good. AMEN.

IUM OF GROTIUS.

A certain Ionian by the name of Esther. I compare Esther, about whom this book is, to Hersilia, who brought peace to her Sabine countrymen and Roman citizenship with the best laws. The Septuagint prefixes to this history a certain dream of Mordecai, which is not in the Hebrew.

OBSERVATIONS ON THE GROTIAN PREFACE AND THE BOOK OF ESTHER ITSELF.

Concerning Esther and her husband, various opinions occur. Grotius defined nothing as certain, but left everything in doubt at Ezra 4:6. In his preface to the books of Chronicles, however, he judges that this history happened in the middle of the time of those things which are related in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah: and thus he seems to make Esther's Ahasuerus either Artaxerxes Longimanus, with Josephus, Sulpitius Severus, Nicephorus, Cajetan, Sanctius, Salianus, Bellarmine, or Xerxes, with Scaliger and his followers. But in the time of Longimanus, Mordecai, who was deported with Jeconiah (Esther 2:5), would have had to be more than 150 years old, even if he had been only ten years old at that migration: and Esther, however much she is set down as a hundred years younger than her cousin Mordecai, would have been, at the time of Ahasuerus—if he is ὁ μακρόχειρ—not a virgin in the flower of her age, but a fifty-year-old woman. Nor do the things which Scaliger brings forward agree with this Sacred history regarding Xerxes; whose Amestris, the worst and most cruel of women, is as far removed as heaven from earth from the most pious and mild Esther. But those seem to judge more correctly who make Darius Hystaspis, the chief restorer of the temple, the husband of Esther: which opinion is that of R. Aben-Ezra, R. Solomon, Metasthenes, B. Luther, Philipp, Brentius, Carion, Funccius, Ussher, Fevardentius, Cornelius à Lapide, and others. For this King's kindness toward the Jews, the length of his reign, his stay in Susa, the plurality of his wives, and other things agree perfectly. Compare Brentius, annotations on the book of Esther, and Funccius in Chronology at the year 3445. But having dismissed the dream about Mordecai from the LXX Interpreters, and having left aside the Grotian comparisons of Esther, and having also put aside the shreds of the 6.

of the later chapters of Esther, as also part of chapter 10, which are not in the Hebrew codices at all, and have already been separated by Jerome, even though they seem to be approved in the Council of Trent: whose Canon, however, Sixtus Senensis (Book 1, Bibliotheca, p. 34) denies should be understood as referring to such mangled appendices and patched-up additions, and rejects them along with Hugo the Cardinal, Lyranus, and Dionysius the Carthusian, as well as Driedo and Arias Montanus, with Origen and Jerome as predecessors: intending to treat of the Canonical book of Esther, consisting of 10 chapters as was also done by Grotius, we shall briefly explain the author, authority, argument, chronology, chief scope, interpreters, and division of the book.

Concerning the author, authors vary. Augustine (Book 18, De Civitate Dei, ch. 16) and Isidore (Book 6, Etymologies) make Ezra the author of the book: R. David [makes] the men of the Great Synagogue, Philo [makes] Joachim the High Priest: most, with R. Abraham and Lyranus, [make] Mordecai, such as Sixtus Senensis, Bellarmine, Sanctius, Serarius, Cornelius à Lapide, whom the words of Esther ch. 9:20, 23 favor, along with B. Gerhard in

Exegesis, B. Waltherus judges, it is certain that the author was θεόπνευστον (divinely inspired), even if it is not entirely certain who he was: whom B. Gerhard acknowledges (L. 2, Confessio Catholica, p. 36) is more likely established by Isidore as Ezra than by Eusebius in his Chronicles as someone later than Ezra. For the book of Esther has always been held in the Church as of Canonical authority, equally among the Hebrews, to whom the τὰ λόγια τοῦ Θεῦ (oracles of God) were entrusted, and among Christian Doctors: Nor did Melito of Sardis (in Eusebius, Book 4, ch. 25), Athanasius in his Synopsis, [or] Nazianzen

in his poems exclude this book from the Canon, because they receive the Canon of the Hebrews, in which it is contained, but only the final chapters, which we have already said are νοθεύεσθαι (to be spurious).

The book of Esther describes those things which happened to the Jews who did not return to their homeland, but remained in the Persian kingdom, in the time of Ahasuerus, whom we judge to be Darius Hystaspes, and especially the history of Esther, through whom, honored by a royal marriage, the danger hanging over the necks of the Jews was averted by the wonderful providence of God. Eminent in it is the humiliation of the proud, namely Vashti and Haman, and the exaltation of the humble, such as Esther and Mordecai, and the liberation of the Jews. This history is of about ten years: for others twenty; which pleases Junius and Tremellius: namely that Ahasuerus, whom they think is Xerxes, instituted a banquet in the 3rd year of his reign, married Esther in the seventh year, and punished Haman, who was conspiring against the Jews, with hanging in the 12th year: and from then until the end of his reign Esther reigned, with Mordecai obtaining the highest administration. But that hypothesis, that Ahasuerus is Xerxes, is false. And how Xerxes in the seventh year could have married Esther in Susa in deep peace, who in the seventh and eighth year of his reign was involved in a horrible war in Greece and Ionia.

The history, however, seems to be referable to the year of the world 3485. Which was the third of Darius Hystaspes, in which that illustrious banquet of chapter 1, 2, 3, 4 was celebrated, when he sat on the throne of his kingdom in Susa: by which King Susa was founded, Pliny testifies in book 6, chapter 27, or rather enriched by the magnificence of royal buildings, as Aelian explains in book 13 of On the Nature of Animals, chapter 59. Where also Herodotus is the authority that Darius had his residence and his treasures, book 5, chapter 49.

Furthermore, in the seventh year of the reign of Darius, in the 10th month, Tebeth, Esther was taken, chapter 2, 16, 17, with a very great banquet prepared in her honor, verse 18, which was the second year from the building of the later temple. In the eleventh year, Haman the Agagite, originating from the royal stock of the Amalekites, being hostile to Mordecai who would not adore him, thinks of destroying his whole race (a race most hostile to his own origin, Deut. 25, 19), and investigates the day auspicious for his plan through κληρομαντείαν (lot-casting), chapter 3, 1, et seqq., and so in the twelfth year, which was 3495 of the world, in the month Adar, he obtains a mandate from the King for the removal of the Jews, chapter 3, 7, et seqq., in which very year, by the just judgment of God, in the third month, Haman was driven to the cross prepared for Mordecai, chapter 7, and furthermore on the 13th day of the 12th month, the Jews killed those with impunity who were going to rise up against them on that same day by Haman's decree, which was continued in Susa also on the following day, the 14th, and from then, chapter 9, 1, et seqq. and the solemnity of the feast of Purim or of lots instituted by Mordecai to be celebrated annually, confirmed by Queen Esther, chapter 9, 20, et seqq.

The principal scope of the History is to teach the providence of God toward His people, and the wonderful preservation of the Jews, from which people the Messiah was to be born, and by that example also to console the Jews who had returned to their homeland, and to excite them, so that they might proceed confidently in restoring the Church and the polity. Among the interpreters, Sanctius, Serrarius, Bonartius, and Drusius are especially celebrated.

Some distribute the same, like a Drama, into protasis, epitasis, and catastrophe. But because the principal person in it is Esther, and the primary act is the liberation of the Jewish people, the History can be conveniently divided into two parts: because in it is described both the exaltation of Esther for the sake of the Lord's people, and the liberation of the Lord's people from slaughter accomplished through Esther. The first part is unfolded in the first two chapters, setting forth partly the occasion of this exaltation, the repudiation and rejection of Queen Vashti because of her pride and contempt of the Royal mandate, chap. 1. partly the description of the exaltation itself chap. 2. to v. 18. partly the narration of a certain remarkable consequence, namely the liberation of the King from the danger of death, which intended, brought about by Mordecai the guardian of Esther, through her own mediation, in the remaining verses of chap. 2. The second part exposes both the danger of slaughter which threatened the Jewish people through Haman, and the help which came to it divinely through Esther. And the cause of that danger is proposed, the elevation of Haman the Agagite to the highest honor, and his pride, and the hatred conceived against Mordecai and the Jewish people: and the mode, through power obtained from the King, and the sending of letters instructed for the slaughter of the Jewish race throughout the entire Monarchy chap. 3.

Of the help divinely provided, by which the Jews were both liberated from slaughter and they themselves exterminated their enemies, both the προηγούμενα (preceding events), and the πραχθέντα (things done), and the ἑπόμενα (following events) are exhibited. Those are the mourning of Mordecai and other Jews, and when Esther inquired of him the cause of the mourning, his counsel c. 4. and the execution of this counsel, partly through the invitation of the King and Haman to a banquet, whence Haman's pride and hatred against Mordecai grew so that he erected a gallows for him c. 5. partly through the supplication and intercession of the Queen for her own safety and that of her people: for which a way was prepared, both through the exaltation of Mordecai, whom the King, revolving the Chronicles and understanding that he had freed him from the snares of assassins, ordered to be led through the royal metropolis by Haman, adorned with the royal vestment and Diadem; chap. 6. and through the celebration of the banquet prepared by Esther: in which she, as a suppliant, was made to the King, and complained of Haman's snares c. 7. To the τὰ πραχθέντα (things done) pertains the hanging of Haman v. 8. seqq. c. 7. and after the elevation of Mordecai to supreme honor, the sending of letters, written in the Name of the King to the Jews, that they should defend themselves and kill their enemies chap. 8. as well as the slaughter of the enemies of the Jews in Susa, and in other cities and provinces of the King chap. 9. up to v. 17. To the τὰ ἑπόμενα (following events) belong both the public joy of the Jews celebrated on the second day after the extermination of the enemies, and the anniversary festival of Purim or Lots to be celebrated among the Jewish people on the 14th and 15th days of the Month Adar, sanctioned by the Queen and Mordecai chap. 9. in the remainder, and the glory of Mordecai, who was next to the King, and his grace and beneficence toward his own people chap. 10.

IN. AD LIBRU PRÆLOQUI

VIde quæ diximus ad initium Paralipomenon. Sæpe mulieres Hebræis plurimum profuerunt. Etiam in Po- Vers. 14. MEMENTO MEI DEUS MEUS PRO HOC] Sic & infra 22. 29. 31.

Azotica lingua est Philisthæorum, quorum pars Azotii erant, de qua intelligit Bochartus c. 15. quod de lingua Chanaan dixit Hieronymus, mediam esse inter Ebræam & Ægyptiam, annuitque Hottinge- rus System. Theol. p. 145. quia Ebræa sint nomina Deorum בעל & זבוב, & דגן nomen commune Re- gum Philistæorum אבימלך Gen. 20, 21. 26. ut & no- men סרן quo Principes suos vocarunt Phœnices Jud. 16, 5. 24. ab Ebræo שר; Ægyptiacum vero sit Astharoth, Urania Venus, de qua Herodotus in Clio, à Tsarot, quod Venereum Ægyptiis notat. Hæc Azotica lingua Chaldaicæ Dialectus fuit: Quanquam vero Chaldaicæ linguæ usus apud Judæos in captivi- tate, & post eandem viguerit, ut è Jerem. 10, 11. Dan. 2, 4. usque ad c. 8. Esdr. 4. v. 8. seqq. videre est (quæ ante captivitatem à Judæis intelligi non poterat 2. Reg. 18, 26. Jer. 5, 18.) Dialecti tamen Chaldaicæ linguæ intelligi minime à Judæis poterant : quales Hottingerus lib. 5. facit tum Azoticam illam lin- guam, tum linguam Punicam, quam Ebrææ gemel- lam quidem Postellus, Dialectum ejusdem Bochar- tus, Amama, Seldenus, plus Hebraismi quam Chal- daismi habere, juxta versus Plautinos in Pœnulo Hottingerus judicat; Waferus vero ad Mithridat. & Fullerus l. 4. Miscell. c. 10. Syriacæ affinem dicunt : tum Syriacam: quæ Aramæa etsi olim ipsissima Chaldæorum lingua fuerit, post captivitatem ta- men Babylonicam ex Chaldaismo & Ebraismo ter- tia ab utraq; literis & formatione distincta emersit, Chaldæo vero idiomati vicinior est, quam Ebræo.

QVEM FUGAVI A ME) Non Sanaballeten Satra- pam in Moabitide, sed illum nepotem Eliasibi jussi abire, ex decreto Esdræ, 10, 8.

MEMENTO MEI DEUS IN BONUM. AMEN.

Vocula Amen in Ebræo non habetur. Teme- re ergo addita. Suspirio autem illo optimo obsi- gno etiam hanc operam. Memento mei Deus in bo- num. AMEN.

IUM GROTII.

lonia quædam Esther nomine. Estherem, de qua hic est liber, comparo Hersiliæ, quæ Sabinis popularibus suis pacem & ci- vitatem Romanam optimis legibus obtinuit. LXX. huic hi- storicæ somnium quoddam Mardochæi præmittunt, quod non est in Hebræo.

OBSERVATIONES AD PRÆLO- QUIUM GROTIANUM, ET LIBRUM IPSUM ESTHER.

DE Estheræ, ejusque marito variæ oc- currunt sententiæ. Grotius nihil certi definivit, sed omnia in du- bio reliquit ad Esdr. 4, 6. In præfa- tione autem ad libros Paralipomenon hanc historiam, medio tempore eorum, quæ libris Esdræ, & Nehemiæ referuntur, contigis- se, censet: adeoque videtur Ahasverum Estheris vel Artaxerxem Longimanum facere cum Josepho, Sulpitio Severo, Nicephoro, Cajetano, Sanctio, Sa- liano, Bellarmino, vel Xerxem, cum Scaligero, & asseclis. Sed Longimani tempore Mardocheum, qui cum Jechonia deportatus fuit Esth. 2, 5, opor- tuisset plus quam 150. annos habuisse, etiamsi de- cem tantum annorum fuisset in illa transmigratio- ne: Esther v. utut Mardocheo patruele centum annis minor statuatur, Ahasveri, si is ὁ μακρόχειρ sit, tempore virgo non florentis ætatis, sed quinqvage- naria fuisset. Neque de Xerxe consonant, quæ adfert Scaliger, huic Sacræ historiæ; cujus Amestris fœ- minarum pessima, & crudelissima ab Esthera pien- tissima & mitissima toto cœlo distat. Rectius vero sentire videntur, qui Darium Hystaspis, templi re- stauratorem præcipuum Estheræ maritum faciunt: quæ sententia est R. Aben-Ezra, R. Salomonis, Meta- sthenis, B. Lutheri Philippi, Brentii, Carionis, Func- cii, Usserii, Fevardentii, Cornelii à Lapide, & alio- rum. Hujus enim Regis benignitas in Judæos, diuturnitas regiminis, commoratio in Susis, uxo- rum pluralitas, & alia apprime conveniunt. Conf. Brentius annot. in libr. Esth. & Funccius in Chro- nol. ad ann. 3445. Misso autem LXX. Interpp. so- mnio de Mardochæo, & relictis Grotianis Esthe- ris comparationibus, posthabitis etiam laciniis 6.

posteriorum capitum Estheris, ut & partis c. 10. quæ in Ebræis plane non habentur codicibus, & ab Hie- ronymo jam separatæ sunt, utut in Concilio Tri- dentino approbatæ videantur: cujus tamen Cano- nem Sixtus Senensis l. 1. Biblioth. p. 34. de laceris ejus- modi appendicibus & pannosis additamentis intelli- gendum esse, negat, eademque cum Hugone Card. Lyrano, & Dionys. Carthuf. ut & Driedone ac Aria- montano, prævio Origene, atque Hieronymo repro- bat: De Canonico Estheræ libro, uti à Grotio etiam factum, capitibus 10. constante, acturi, autorem, au- toritatem, argumentum, chronologiam, scopum præ- cipuum, Interpp. & partitionem libri paucis expe- diemus.

De autore variant autores. Augustinus L. 18. de C. D. c. 16. Isidor. l. 6. orig. Esdram autorem libri faciunt: R. David viros Synagogæ M. Philo Joachimum Pontificem: plerique cum R. Abrah. & Lyrano Mardocheum, utpote Sixtus Senensis, Bel- larmin. Sanctius, Serarius, Cornel. a Lapid. quibus favere verba Esth. c. 9, 20. 23. cum B. Gerhardo in

Exegef. censet B. Waltherus, Certum est, autorem fuisse θεόπνευστον, etsi quis fuerit, non omnino cer- tum sit: quem B. Gerhard. verisimilius ab Isidoro constitui Esdram, quam ab Eusebio in Chronic. ali- quem Esdra posteriorem, agnoscit L. 2. Confess. Ca- thol. p. 36. Nam autoritatis Canonicæ semper ha- bitus est liber Esther in Ecclesia, apud Ebræos pari- ter, quibus τὰ λόγια τοῦ Θεῦ credita, & apud Chri- stianos Doctores: Neque Melito Sardensis, apud Eu- sebium l. 4. c. 25. Athanasius in Synopsi, Nazianzen.

in carmin. librum hunc ex Canone exclusere, quia recipiunt Canonem Ebræorum, in quo ille habe- tur, sed postrema solum capita, quæ νοθεύεσθαι jam diximus.

Describit autem liber Esther ea, quæ Judæis obtigere, qui in Patriam reversi non fuere, sed in regno Persico substiterunt, tempore Ahasveri, quem Darium Hystapida esse, censemus, & imprimis hi- storiam Estheræ, per quam regio connubio honora- tam periculum Judæorum cervicibus imminens mirabili Dei providentia aversum fuit. Eminet in eo humiliatio superborum, Vasthi sc. & Haman, & exaltatio humilium, utpote Estheris, & Mardo- chæi, ac liberatio Judæorum. Quæ historia decem annorum circiter est: aliis viginti; quod placet Junio, & Tremellio: Ahasverum nempe, quem Xerxem putant, anno 3. regiminis sui convivium in- stituisse, anno septimo Estheram duxisse, anno 12. Hamanem in Judæos conspirantem suspendio pu- niisse: atque inde ad finem regni ejus Estherem re- gnasse, Mardochæo administrationem summam obtinente. Sed hypothesis illa, quod Ahasverus Xerxes sit, falsa est. Et quomodo Xerxes anno se- ptimo Estheram Susis duxisset in alta pace, qui se- ptimo & octavo regiminis anno horribili in Græ- cia, & Jonia implicatus fuit bello.

Referenda autem videtur historia ad ann. M. 3485. Qui erat Darii Hystaspidis tertius, quo celebratum est illustre illud convivium cap. 1, 2.3.4. cum in solio regni sui Susis sederet: a quo Rege Susanam conditam Plinius testatur l. 6, c. 27. vel potius regiarum ædium magnificentia locupleta- tam, uti Ælian. l. 13. de anim. c. 59. explicat. Ubi etiam domicilium, & Thesauros suos Darium ha- buisse autor est Herodotus l. 5. c. 49.

Porro anni regni Darii septimo Mense 10. Thebeth assumta est Esthera c. 2, 16. 17. convivio in ejus honorem maximo parato v. 18. qui annus alter erat ab extructo templo posteriori. Anno undeci- mo Haman Agagæus ex Regia Amalekitarum stir- pe oriundus, Mardochæo adorare eum nolenti in- sensus de tota gente illius (genti originis suæ ini- micissima Deut. 25, 19.) perdenda cogitat, diemque consilio suo auspicatum per κληρομαντείαν indagat cap. 3, 1. seqq. adeoque Anno duodecimo, qui mundi erat 3495. Mense Adar, à Rege mandatum de tol- lendis Judæis impetrat c. 3, 7. seqq. quo ipso anno, judicio Dei justo Mense tertio Haman in crucem Mardochæo præparatam actus est cap. 7. ac porro Mensis 12. d. 13. Judæi eos impune sustulerunt, qui in ipsos ex Hamanis decreto eodem die fuerant in- surrecturi, quod Susis continuatum etiam est die se- quenti 14. atque inde c. 9, 1. seqq. & instituta à Mar- dochæo solemnitas festi Purim sive fortium quo- tannis celebrandi, ab Esthera Regina confirmata c. 9, 20. seqq.

Scopus præcipuus Historiæ est providentiam Dei erga populum suum, & conservationem Judæ- orum mirabilem, è quo populo nasciturus erat Messias docere, atque eo exemplo etiam Judæos in Patriam reversos consolari, & excitare, ut confi- denter in restauranda Ecclesia & politia pergerent. Ex Interpp. celebrantur imprimis Sanctius, Serra- rius, Bonartius, & Drusius.

Distribuunt nonnulli eandem, instar Dra- matis, in Protasin, Epitasin & catastrophen. Sed quia præcipua persona in ea Esther est, & actus prima- rius liberatio populi Judaici, dividi Historia com- mode potest in duas partes: quod in ea tum Esthe- ris ob populum domini exaltatio, tum populi Domini per Estherem facta ab internecione liberatio descri- batur. Prima pars duobus prioribus capp. expe- ditur, proposita partim occasione hujus exaltationis, Reginæ Vasthi ob fastum & contemtum Regii man- dati repudio & rejectione, cap. 1. partim descriptio- ne ipsius exaltationis cap. 2. ad v. 18. partim enarra- tione singularis cujusdam consequentis, liberationis nempe Regis e periculo mortis, quam conspiratio duorum Ministrorum intendebat, per Mardochæum tutorem Estheris, mediante ipsa factæ, vers. reliquis cap. 2. Pars secunda tum internecionis periculum ex- ponit, quod populo Judaico iminuit per Hamanem, tum auxilium quod ei divinitus contigit per Esthe- rem. Periculi vero illius proponitur & causa, Hama- nis Agagitæ ad summum honorem evectio, fastusq; ejusdem, & odium adversus Mardochæum, & popu- lum Judaicum conceptum: & modus, per impetra- tam potestatem a Rege, & missitationem literarum ad internecionem gentis Judaicæ per universam Monarchiam instructarum cap. 3.

Auxilii divinitus præstiti, quo & liberati a cæde sunt Judæi & hostes suos exterminarunt ipsi, tum προηγούμενα, tum πραχθέντα, tum ἑπόμενα exhiben- tur. Illa sunt Mardochai & aliorum Judæorum luctus, istiusq; cum causam luctus sciscitaretur Esther, consi- lium c. 4. & consilii hujus executio, partim per invita- tionem Regis, & Hamanis ad convivium, unde Hama- nis fastus & odium adversus Mardochæum ita cre- vit, ut ei patibulum erexerit c. 5. partim per suppli- cationem, & intercessionem Reginæ pro sua, & popu- li sui salute: cui parata via est, tum per exaltationem Mardochæi, quem Rex, Chronica revolvens & intel- ligens, quod ab insidiis sicariorum se liberarit, vesti- tu ac Diademate Regio ornatum per Hamanem per Regiam metropolin deduci jussit; cap. 6. tum per convivii ab Esthere parati celebrationem: in quo ipsa supplex Regi facta, & de Hamanis insidiis conquesta est c. 7. Ad τὰ πραχθέντα pertinet Hamanis suspensio vers. 8. seqq. c. 7. & post evectionem Mardochæi ad su- premum honorem, literarum, Nomine Regis ad Ju- dæos, ut se tuerentur & hostes suos interficerent, perscriptarum missitatio cap. 8. nec non hostium Ju- dæorum in Susan, & aliis civitatibus ac provinciis Re- gis internecio cap. 9. usq; ad v. 17. Ad τὰ ἑπόμενα spe- ctant tum lætitia Judæorum publica die altero post exterminium hostium celebrata, tum festivitas Pu- rim vel Sortium anniversaria in populo Judaico d. 14. & 15. Mensis Adar celebranda, per Reginam, & Mardochæum sancita cap. 9. reliquo, tum gloria Mar- dochæi, qui proximus a Rege erat, ejusdemque ad- versus populum suum gratia & beneficentia cap. 10.

## 1:1 Argument
PART I. THE EXALTATION OF ESTHER. CHAPTER I.

Ahasuerus, while celebrating a splendid banquet for the whole half-year for the display of his power and glory, summons Queen Vashti, who refuses to come, and therefore she is repudiated; and by the counsel of the wise men an edict is promulgated, that wives should show honor to their husbands.

Vers. 1. IN THE DAYS OF AHASUERUS) I have nothing more to say about Ahasuerus than what I said on Ezra 4, 6. The Hebrews think that this Ahasuerus was the Persian Darius, or, as the Greek interpreters and Josephus state, the son of Artaxerxes and Esther. What is to be held concerning these, we have already said. Ahasuerus was a common name for the Kings of the Medes, as Artaxerxes was for the Persians. FROM INDIA) הודו, for which the Targum in this place and elsewhere the Hebrews הנדוי. Vers. 2. SUSA) See Nehem. 1, 1. It is situated near the river Choaspes in a most pleasant place, so called from the abundance of lilies, as Athenaeus testifies, book 12.

Latin:

PARS I. ESTHERIS EXALTATIO. CAPUT I.

Ahasvero ad potentiæ & gloriæ suæ ostentatio- nem toto Semestri splendidum celebrante con- vivium Regina Vasthi accersita venire recu- sat, ideoque repudiatur; & sapientum Con- silio edictum promulgatur, ut uxores maritis honorem deferant.

Vers. 1. IN DIEBUS ASSVERI) De Assvero nihil am plius quod dicam habeo, quam quod dixi Esdræ 4, 6. Dariun Persam hujus Assveri, sive, ut Græci interpretes & Josephu efferunt, Artaxerxis & Estheris filium fuisse Hebræi sentiun Quod de his habendum, jam diximus. Ahasve rus erat nomen commune Regum Medorum, ut Artaxerxes Persarum. AB INDIA) הודו, pro quo Thargum hoc loco & alib Hebræi הנדוי. Vers. 2. SVSAN) Vide Nehem. 1, 1. Sita est juxta Chaspem fluvium loco amœniff mo, ita dicta a liliorum copia teste Athen. l. 12.

## 1:3
Vers. 3. HE MADE A GREAT BANQUET FOR ALL HIS PRINCES AND HIS SERVANTS) In the Hebrew: his servants: in which way it is the custom of the Orient to call subjects. The Greeks here have placed: τοῖς φίλοις καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσι (to his friends and to the remaining nations). See below 5. Also the Roman Emperors often entertained the plebs with a banquet along with the senate. In the banquet of Domitian, Statius says: Here when Caesar ordered the Romulean elders and the thousand troops in their robes of office to recline at the tables at the same time. AND THE GOVERNORS OF THE PROVINCES) Province here in the Hebrew, מדינה, which name even now remains in certain regions in Spain.

Latin:

Vers. 3. FECIT GRANDE CONVIVIUM CVNCTIS PRINCIPIBVS ET PVERIS SUIS) In Hebræo: servis suis: quomodo vocare subditos mos est Orientis. Græci hic posue- re : τοῖς φίλοις καὶ τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσι. Vide infra 5. Etiam Ro- mani Imperatores sæpe epulo excepere cum senatu etiam plebem. In epulo Domitiani Statius: Hic cum Romuleos proceres, trabeataque Cæsar Agmina mille, simul jussit decumbere mensis. ET PRÆFECTIS PROVINCIARVM) Provincia hic in Hebræo, מדינה, quod nomen etiam nunc in Hispania qui- busdam regionibus manet.

## 1:6
Vers. 6. ALSO GOLDEN COUCHES.

How the Jews, Persians, Greeks, and other nations used reclining at dinner and lunch, so that they did not dine so much sitting as lying on couches more softly, and after taking food rested on them, see here among others Cornel. a Lap.

Latin:

Vers. 6. LECTULI QVOQVE AUREI.

Quomodo Judæi, Persæ, Græci & aliæ gentes ac- cubitu usæ sint in cœna, & prandio, ut non tam se- dentes, quam jacentes in lectis mollius cœnarent, & sumto cibo in iis, quiescerent, vid. hic inter alios Cornel. a Lap.

## 1:8
Vers. 8. NOR WAS THERE ANYONE WHO COULD COMPEL THE UNWILLING TO DRINK) Which otherwise is accustomed to happen at the courts of Kings. Kings are said to urge with great goblets, and to twist with wine. Also among the Romans there were masters and directors of drinking. The Greek interpreters in this place: but this drinking did not happen according to the established law. But thus the King wished and ordered the stewards to do his will and that of the men.

Latin:

Vers. 8. NEC ERAT QVI NOLENTES COGERET AD BIBENDVM) Quod alioqui apud Reges fieri solet. Reges dicuntur magnis urgere culullis, Et torquere mero. Etiam apud Romanos bibendi modimperatores erant & ma- gistri. Græci interpretes h. l. ὁ δὲ πότος οὗτος οὐ κατὰ προκεί- μενον νόμον ἐγένετο. οὕτως δὲ ἐθέλησεν ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ ἐπέταξε τοῖς οἰκονόμοις ποιῆσαι τὸ θέλημα ἀυτῆ καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

## 1:9
Vers. 9. IN THE PALACE) Under a roof, not in the gardens, as the King. That was more convenient for the modesty of women.

Latin:

Vers. 9. IN PALATIO) Sub tecto, non in hortis, ut Rex. Id fœminarum pudori erat convenientius.

## 1:10
Vers. 10. THEREFORE ON THE SEVENTH DAY, WHEN THE KING WAS MERRIER, AND HAD GROWN WARM WITH WINE AFTER EXCESSIVE DRINKING) For even the things that follow have more impulse than reason. But it is the right of God to execute His decrees even in this way. The King wanted to show the Persians the beauty of his wife, which was neither becoming for a woman nor safe for the King: but Kings easily find approvers of their opinion for whatever they wish: nor is the song of these nightingales lacking to them.

SEVEN EUNUCHS WHO WERE SERVING IN HIS PRESENCE] The word סריסים signifies eunuchs: Eastern kings are accustomed to use such men even now for the service of women. Seven is a celebrated number among the Persians. See below 14.

AND HE COMMANDED MAUMAN) This is Haman in the Greek.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ITAQVE DIE SEPTIMO, CVM REX ESSET HILARIOR, ET POST NIMIAM POTATIONEM INCALUISSET MERO) Nam & quæ sequuntur plus im- petus habent quam rationis. At Deo jus est decreta sua etiam sic exequendi. Voluit Rex ostentare Persis formam uxoris suæ, quod nec fœminæ decorum, nec Regi tutum erat: sed Reges quicquid velint facile inveniunt sententiæ suæ appro- batores: neque deest his lusciniolis sua cantio.

SEPTEM EVNVCHIS QVI IN CONSPECTU EJUS MINISTRABANT] Vox סריסים spadones significat: talibus autem hominibus etiam nunc Orientis Reges ad mini- steria fœminarum uti solent. Heptas celeber apud Persas nu- merus. Vid. infra 14.

PRÆCEPITQVE MAUMAN) Hic est Aman in Græco.

## 1:12
Ver. 12. WHO REFUSED) Perhaps with prouder words than was fitting, as one who thought the King was beholden to her because of his love. Otherwise, it was against custom what the King had commanded: for Plutarch says of the Persians in his Life of Themistocles: 'They not only guard their wedded wives strictly, but also their purchased and concubined ones, so that they are seen by none of those outside, but live shut up at home. And on journeys, they are carried in carriages surrounded by a tent.' Josephus at this place: 'A guard of the law among the Persians, who forbid women to be seen by strangers.'

AND KINDLED WITH EXCESSIVE FURY) Where anger is added to wine, it does not easily keep within bounds. Many such things are in the history of Alexander.

Latin:

Vers. 12. QVÆ RENUIT) Forte superbioribus verbis quam oportebat, ut quæ Regem præ amore sibi putabat obnoxium. Alioqui erat contra mores quod Rex jusserat: nam de Persis Plutarchus Themistocle: ὀ μόνον τὰς γαμετὰς ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰς ἀρ- γυρωνήτες καὶ παλλακευομένας ἰσχυρῶς παραφυλάττουσιν, ὡς ὑπὸ μηδενὸς ὁρᾶσθαι τῶν ἐκτός, ἀλλ᾽ οἴκοι μὲν διαιτᾶσθαι κεκλεισμέ- νας. ἐν δὲ ταῖς ὁδοιπορίαις, ὑπὸ σκηνῆς κύκλῳ περιπεφραγμένας ἐπὶ τῶν ἁρμαμαξῶν ὀχεῖσθαι. Josephus h. l. Φυλακὴ τῶν παρὰ Πέρσαις νόμον, οἳ τοῖς ἀλλοτρίοις βλέπεσθαι τὰς γυναῖκας ἀπη- γορεύκασι.

ET NIMIO FVRÓRE SVCCENSVS) Ubi ad vinum ira accessit haud facile retinet modum. Multa talia in Alexan- dri historia.

## 1:13
Ver. 13. HE ASKED THE WISE MEN) The Magi: he had become so accustomed to this custom that he did not forget it even when drunk.

WHO ACCORDING TO ROYAL CUSTOM WERE ALWAYS PRESENT WITH HIM, AND HE DID ALL THINGS BY THEIR COUNSEL: WHO KNEW THE LAWS AND JUDGMENTS OF THE ANCESTORS) Josephus: 'The seven Persians who have the interpretation of the laws among them.' Much regard is had in those who are to give counsel to a King for the knowledge of the ancestral law. To give counsel about the republic, the main thing is to know the republic, says Cicero in Book II of De Oratore. Thus the Emperor Severus Alexander used the counsel of the most distinguished men in law: Ulpian, Pomponius, Celsus, Modestinus, Paulus, Proculus, Venuleius.

Latin:

Vers. 13. INTERROGAVIT SAPIENTES) Magos : ita huic mori affueverat, ut ne ebrius quidem ejus oblivisceretur.

QVI EX MORE REGIO SEMPER EI ADERANT, ET ILLORVM FACIEBAT CVNCTA CONSILIO : SCIENTIVM LEGES AC JVRA MAJORVM) Josephus : τὸς ἑπτὰ τῶν Περσῶν οἳ τὴν τῶν νόμων ἐξήγησιν ἔχουσι παρ᾽ αὐτοῖς. Multum spectatur in iis, qui consilium Regi daturi sunt, cognitio juris patrii. Ad consilium de republica dandum caput est nosse rempubl. ait Cicero II. de Oratore. Sic impe- rator Severus Alexander Classissimorum in jure virorum usus est consiliis, Ulpiani, Pomponii, Celsi, Modestini, Pauli, Pro- culi, Venuleji.

## 1:14
Ver. same. WHO SAW THE FACE OF THE KING) See what we said at Matthew 18:10.

He observes not badly there: that it is not permitted for just any of the ministers to see kings daily, but only for the nobles of the kingdom, 1 Kings 10, and that the Hebrews understand this by the word אחשר רפנים, from which the name of Satraps flowed. Although Ludovicus de Dieu in his Animadversions on difficult places of the Old Testament, at chapter 3 of Esther, verse 11, notes that that word is Persian and signifies the doorkeepers of majesty. But how will Grotius prove that Matthew 18:10 refers to that custom of Kings, and that the more distinguished, not just any, Angels are understood? For all Angels without doubt see the face of God through all things, which all the blessed, as future equals to angels, are also going to see, 1 Corinthians 13:12, 1 John 3:2.

Latin:

Vers. eod. QVI VIDEBANT FACIEM REGIS) Vide quæ diximus ad Matth. 18, 10.

Non male illic observat: reges aspicere quotidie non cuivis ministrorum licere, sed solis regni proceribus 1. Reg. 10. atque id Ebræos voce אחשר רפנים intellige- re, unde fluxit nomen Satraparum. Quanquam vocem illam Persicam esse, & significare majestatis janitores Ludovicus de Dieu in animadvers. ad loca difficil. V. T. ad cap. 3. Esther v. 11. advertat. Sed Matth. 18, 10. ad Regum illum morem respici, ac insigniores, non quosvis Angelos intelligi, unde probabit Grotius? Omnes enim Angeli fine dubio διὰ πάντων vi- dent faciem Dei, quam omnes beati, ceu ἰσάγγελοι futuri, etiam visuri sunt 1. Cor. 13, 12. 1. Joh. 3, 2.

## 1:16
AND MAMUCHAN ANSWERED) Perhaps the first to be asked for his opinion by the King.

Latin:

Vers. 16. RESPONDITQVE MAMVCHAN) Primus forte sententiam a Rege interrogatus.

## 1:18
AND BY THIS EXAMPLE ALL THE WIVES OF THE PRINCES OF THE PERSIANS AND MEDES WILL MAKE LIGHT OF THE COMMANDS OF THEIR HUSBANDS) For just as the King’s vices, so the Queen’s are judged a kind of compliance to imitate. Josephus in this place: ὀυδὲ μία γάρ τῷ συνοικῦντι ἀνδρὸς αἰδῶ ποιήσέται, παράδειγμα τὴν τῆς βασιλίσσης ὑπερηφανίαν πρὸς σὲ τὸν κρατῦντα ἁπάντων ἔχουσα.

Latin:

Vers. 18. ATQVE HOC EXEMPLO OMNES PRIN- CIPVM CONJUGES PERSARVM ATQVE MEDO- RVM PARVI PENDENT IMPERIA MARITORVM) Nam ut Regis ita reginæ vitia imitari genus obsequii judica- tur. Josephus h. l. ὀυδὲ μία γάρ τῷ συνοικῦντι ἀνδρὸς αἰδῶ ποιήσέται, παράδειγμα τὴν τῆς βασιλίσσης ὑπερηφανίαν πρὸς σὲ τὸν κρατῦντα ἁπάντων ἔχουσα.

## 1:19
LET IT BE WRITTEN ACCORDING TO THE LAW OF THE PERSIANS AND MEDES WHICH IT IS UNLAWFUL TO OVERPASS) It appears there was a certain form of making laws among the Persians, according to which laws once made were entirely immutable, like those which were called sacred among the Romans. See Dan. 6, 8. 12. 15. & Procopius, where he treats of the fortress of oblivion. Moreover, the form that made laws immutable seems to have been this, that it was fortified not only by the King’s signet, but also by those of the Princes. See Dan. 6, 17.

BUT LET ANOTHER WHO IS BETTER THAN SHE RECEIVE HER KINGDOM) A heavy punishment for a light fault, if indeed it was a fault.

Latin:

SCRIBATUR JUXTA LEGEM PERSARUM ATQVE MEDORUM QVAM PRÆTERIRI ILLICITUM EST) Apparet quandam fuisse formam legum faciendarum apud Persas, secundum quam factæ leges omnino erant immutabi- les, ut illæ quæ sacræ apud Romanos vocabantur. Vide Dan. 6, 8. 12. 15. & Procopium, ubi agit περὶ λήθης φρουρίου. Videtur autem forma quæ leges faciebat immutabiles, hæc fuisse, ut non Regis tantum, sed & Principum signis muniretur. Vide Dan. 6, 17.

Vers. 19. SED REGNVM ILLIVS ALTERA QVÆ MELIOR EST ILLA ACCIPIAT) Gravis pœna pro culpa levi, si tamen culpa.

## 1:22
IN DIVERSE LANGUAGES AND LETTERS) For the King wrote to each people in their own language: below 3, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 22. DIVERSIS LINGVIS AC LITERIS) Nam ad quemque populum lingua cujusque Rex scribebat : infra 3, 12.

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II.

The King chooses Esther from the virgins brought to him, who is taken and crowned Queen. Concerning the plots against the King, which Mordecai revealed, and which were punished, which are recorded in the Annals.

Latin:

CAPUT II.

Rex e virginibus sibi adductis imprimis elegit Estheram, quæ assumitur & coronatur in Re- ginam. De insidiis adversus Regem, quas Mardochæus manifestavit, punitis, quæ in Annales referuntur.

## 2:2
LET VIRGINS AND BEAUTIFUL MAIDENS BE SOUGHT FOR THE KING) For with a new successor, all love is conquered.

INTO THE HOUSE OF THE WOMEN) Into the house of the maidens. For there was another house for those who had already become women, below 14.

Latin:

Vers. 2. QVÆRENTUR REGI PUELLÆ VIRGINES AC SPECIOSÆ) Nam Successore novo vincitur omnis amor.

IN DOMUM FOEMINARUM) In domum puella- rum. Nam alia erat domus earum quæ jam mulieres factæ essent, infra 14.

## 2:3
LET THEM RECEIVE WOMEN’S ORNAMENTS AND OTHER NECESSARY THINGS FOR USE) In the Hebrew there is one word מרקים, which contains both ornaments and attire. This appears below 12.

Latin:

ACCIPIANT MVNDVM MVLIEBREM ET CÆ- TERA AD USUS NECESSARIA) In Hebræo una vox מרקים, quæ & mundum, & ornatum continet. Apparet id infra 12.

## 2:5
OF THE STOCK OF JEMINI) That is, of Benjamin, as the Greeks and Josephus here.

Latin:

Vers. 5. DE STIRPE JEMINI) Id est, Benjamini, ut hic Græci & Josephus.

## 2:6
WHO HAD BEEN CARRIED AWAY FROM JERUSALEM) That is, whose ancestors had been carried away: for the Hebrews often interchange the names of parents and children. Compare Ezra 1, 2.

That change of names is not to be allowed. Nor can a similar example of it be brought forward. Bellarmine's explanation, in book 1 on the Word of God, chapter 7, that Mordecai was translated not in himself, but in his ancestors, might therefore seem more convenient; but there is no reason why such interpretations should be admitted as do violence to the express words. And Mordecai is expressly mentioned among those who were translated to Babylon; Ezra 2:2, Esther 11:2, although this passage is outside the Canon, whence we do not hesitate to attribute that, WHO HAD BEEN TRANSLATED, to Mordecai himself here, nor do we think that the gloss of others, who draw it back to his ancestor Kish, against the express letter of the text, should be admitted. For he who is said to have been translated is introduced in the following verse as the foster-father of his brother's daughter, Esther.

Latin:

QVI TRANSLATVS FVERAT DE JERUSALEM) Id est, cujus majores translati fuerant : sæpe enim Hebræi pa- rentum & liberorum nomina inter se mutant. Confer. Esdr. 1, 2.

Non est illa nominum commutatio conce- denda. Neque exemplum ejus simile adferri potest. Convenientior ergo videri posset Bellarmini l. 1. de verbo Dei c. 7. explicatio, translatum Mardochæum fuisse non in se, sed in majoribus ; Sed nulla causa est, cur tales admitti debeant interpretationes, quæ vim expressis verbis faciant. Et commemoratur diserte Mardochæus inter illos, qui translati Baby- lonem sunt; Esd. 2, 2. Esth. 11, 2. quamvis hic lo- cus extra Canonem sit, unde illud, QVI TRANS- LATUS FUERAT, ipsi Mardochæo hic tribue- re non dubitamus, nec aliorum, qui id ad proavum ejus Kis retrahunt, contra expressam textus literam, glossam admittendam censemus. Nam ille, qui translatus dicitur, versu sequente, ceu nutritius filiæ fratris sui Esther introducitur.

## 2:7
WHO WAS THE FOSTER-FATHER OF HIS BROTHER'S DAUGHTER) Nay, rather uncle, as it is in the Hebrew; the Greeks: daughter of Aminadab, brother of her father. Caesar also used the word nutritium, or foster-father, in Book III of the Civil War. He was in the administration of the kingdom, because of the boy's age, his foster-father, a eunuch.

WHO BY ANOTHER NAME WAS CALLED ESTHER) Some think this was Amestris.

The origin does not fit. For Amestris was Persian, not Hebrew. Herodotus, however, in book 3, names Hadasa as the wife of Darius Hystaspis, whose firstborn son he teaches was Xerxes: Others, from the same book 6, chapter 8, and book 7, chapter 69, bring forward Artystana, whom Darius loved most, and whose image he had fashioned from solid gold.

HE ADOPTED HER AS HIS DAUGHTER) He took her to himself as a daughter, it is in the Hebrew: that is, he brought her up with such affection as if she were his daughter: below 20. Josephus: for he loved her as his own daughter.

Latin:

QVI FVIT NVTRITIVS FILIÆ FRATRIS SVI) Imo patrui ut est in Hebræo, Græci : θυγατήρ Ἀμιναδάβ ἀδελ- φῦ πατρὸς ἀυτῦ. Nutritium τὸ τρέφον, sive ϑρεπτῆρα etiam Cæsar dixit Belli civilis III. Erat in procuratione regni, propter ætatem pueri, nutritius ejus Eunuchus.

QVÆ ALTERO NOMINE VOCABATVR ESTHER) Hanc esse Amistrin quidam putant.

Non convenit ortus. Nam Amestris Persica fuit, non Ebræa. Nominat autem Herodot. l. 3. Ha- dasam uxorem Darii Hystaspis, cujus filium pri- mogenitum Xerxem fuisse, docet : Alii ex ejusdem l. 6. c. 8. & l. 7. c. 69. Artystanam adducunt, quam Darius maxime adamavit, & cujus imaginem, ex auro solido compactam habuerit.

SIBI EAM ADOPTAVIT IN FILIAM) Accepit sibi in filiam, est in Hebræo : id est, eo affectu eam educabat ac si filia esset : inf. 20. Josephus : ἔστεργε γὰρ ἀυτὴν ὡς ἀυτῦ ϑυγατέρα.

## 2:9
WHO PLEASED HIM] The prefect of the women's quarters, a learned spectator of forms. Verse 15. WHO DID NOT SEEK WOMANLY ADORNMENT] Such is the confidence in her beauty. Verse 17. AND PLACED THE DIADEM OF THE KINGDOM ON HER HEAD] He made her Sultana. Verse 18. AND GAVE REST TO ALL THE PROVINCES] He granted them some relief from burdens, as Kings are accustomed to do at weddings. The Greeks well: he made a remission. AND BESTOWED GIFTS ACCORDING TO PRINCELY MAGNIFICENCE] He gave Esther bridal gifts. Herodotus, book 2, says that the city of Anthylla was given to the wives of the Kings of Persia for their footwear. Verse 19. AND WHEN VIRGINS WERE SOUGHT A SECOND TIME) This is a recapitulation. For this must be referred to those things which are above 2, 2. Tirinus and Bonfrerius think that virgins were sought a second time while Esther was reigning, and that this would have happened a third time, and more often (had Esther not stood in the way), because of the King's insatiable lust. But Mariana and Sanctius more correctly observe that the reason is given why Mordecai could have understood the conspiracy against the King, namely his assiduity at the King's gate, from which time this second search for virgins was made: for another seems to have preceded it, at the time when the King married Vasthi. Similarly Menochius: He says, it does not signify that virgins were sought again after Esther's marriage, but he repeats what had been done before, to subjoin the history of the two Eunuchs, which had happened while virgins were being sought again for Esther's wedding, just as they had been sought long ago for Vasthi's wedding. Verse same. HE REMAINED AT THE GATE. He was present or stayed in the manner of Persian courtiers, so that he might be at the King's disposal. Verse 20. AND ESTHER HAD NOT YET REVEALED HER HOMELAND AND HER PEOPLE ACCORDING TO HIS COMMAND] So that either hatred might not be created for her from her race, or envy for her race from her fortune. AND SHE DID ALL THINGS, AS AT THAT TIME SHE WAS ACCUSTOMED, WHEN HE WAS REARING HER AS A LITTLE CHILD] Truly rare in a queen, to observe a relative so. Most do not wish to remember what they were. Verse 21. BAGATHAN AND THARES, TWO EUNUCHS, WERE ANGRY] Namely because they feared that through this marriage Mordecai would attain great power. The Chaldean, the LXX, and Tirinus hint that the two Eunuchs were angry because of Mordecai's honors, because he had been preferred to them by the King in palace offices; others think it was because of the repudiation of Vasthi, others that they had entered into a conspiracy against the King to transfer the kingdom to Haman. There could have been many causes for that anger and conspiracy. WHO WERE DOOR-KEEPERS, AND PRESIDED AT THE FIRST THRESHOLD OF THE PALACE] They were chief bodyguards, as the Greeks have it here. Verse 22. WHICH DID NOT ESCAPE MORDECAI) Barnabazus, a servant of one of the Eunuchs, giving him the information. Thus Josephus. Verse 23. AN INQUIRY WAS MADE) An investigation was held. The Greeks: the king examined the two eunuchs. AND BOTH OF THEM WERE HUNG ON A GALLOWS] he crucified, says Josephus less properly, just as the Greek interpreters do below in chapter 7, 10. But here the same interpreters: he hung. A frequent punishment in Persia. V, 14. VII, 9. AND IT WAS COMMANDED AND RECORDED IN THE HISTORIES AND ANNALS BEFORE THE KING] More briefly in the Hebrew: And it was written in the book of the words of the days before the King. That is, this matter was written in the journals which were kept by the King. See below 6, 1. 2.

PART II. THE LIBERATION OF THE PEOPLE THROUGH ESTHER. SECTION I. THE DANGER CONSTRUCTED BY HAMAN.

Latin:

QVÆ PLACUIT EI ] Præfecto gynæconitidos, docto spectatori formarum. Vers. 15. QVÆ NON QVÆSIVIT MVLIEBREM CVLTVM ) Tanta est fiducia formæ. Vers. 17. ET POSUIT DIADEMA REGNI IN CAPI-TE EJVS ] Fecit Sultanam. Vers. 18. ET DEDIT REQVIEM VNIVERSIS PRO-VINCIIS ) Levamenta aliqua onerum ipsis concessit, ut Re-ges in nuptiis facere solent. Græci bene: ἄφεσιν ἐποίησε. AC DONA LARGITVS EST JVXTA MAGNIFI-CENTIAM PRINCIPALEM ) Dedit Estheri ἀνακαλυπτήρια. Anthyllam urbem Regis Persarum uxoribus in calceamentum datam, ait Herodotus lib. 2. Vers. 19. CVMQVE SECVNDO QVÆRERENTVR VIRGINES) Est ἐπάνοδος. referendum enim hoc ad illa quæ supra 2, 2. Virgines secundo quæsitas esse regnante Esthe-ra, putant Tirinus & Bonfrerius, idque tertio, & sæ-pius futurum fuisse, (nisi Esthera obstitisset) ob in-satiabilem Regis libidinem. At rectius Mariana & Sanctius rationem reddi observant, cur Mardo-chæus conjurationem in Regem intelligere potue-rit, nempe assiduitatem ejus ad januam Regis, ex quo tempore hæc secunda conquisitio virginum facta est: nam altera præcessisse videtur, quo tem-pore Rex duxit Vasthi. Similiter Menochius : Non, inquit, significat post nuptias Esther iterum quæ-sitas virgines, sed repetit quod ante factum fuerat, ad subtexendam historiam duorum Evnuchorum, quæ contigerat, dum denuo virgines quærerentur ad nuptias Esther, sicut pridem quæsitæ erant ad nu-ptias Vasthi. Vers. eod. MANEBAT AD JANUAM. Versabatur aut morabatur more aulicorum Persicorum, ut præsto esset Regi. Vers. 20. NEC DVM PRODIDERAT ESTHER PA-TRIAM SVAM ET POPVLVM SUUM JVXTA MAN-DATVM EJVS ] Ne aut ipsi ex gente odium, aut genti ex ipsius fortuna invidia crearetur. ET ITA CVNCTA FACIEBAT, VT EO TEM-PORE SOLITA ERAT, QVO EAM PARVULAM NVTRIEBAT ) Rarum plane in regina, ita observare pro-pinquum. Pleræque nolunt meminisse, quid fuerint. Vers. 21. IRATI SVNT BAGATHAN ET THARES DUO EUNUCHI ] Nempe quod timerent ne per hoc con-jugium Mardochæus ad magnam potentiam perveniret. Duos Eunuchos iratos fuisse ob honores Mar-dochæi, quod is prælatus iis a Rege fuerit in officiis palatinis, Chald. LXX. Tirin. innuunt; alii ob repu-diatam Vasthi, alii conspirationem eorum adversus Regem initam existimant, ut regnum ad Hamanem transferrent. Potuere iræ & conspirationis istius plures esse causæ. QVI JANITORES ERANT, ET IN PRIMO PALA-TII LIMINE PRÆSIDEBANT ] Erant ἀρχισωματοφύλα-κες, ut hic habent Græci. Vers. 22. QVOD MARDOCHÆVM NON LATUIT) Indicium ei faciente Barnabazo servo alterius Eunuchorum. Sic Josephus. Vers. 23. QVÆSITVM EST) Quæstio habita est. Græci: ὁ βασιλεὺς ἤτασε τὲς δύο ἐνέχχες. ET APPENSVS EST VTERQVE EORVM IN PA-TIBVLO ) ἀνεϲτάνωσε ait Josephus minus proprie, quomo-do & Græci interpretes infra cap. 7, 10. At hic iidem interpre-tes : ἐκρέμασε. Pœna frequens in Perside. V, 14. VII, 9. MANDATVMQVE EST HISTORIIS ET ANNA-LIBVS TRADITVM CORAM REGE ) Brevius in He-bræo: Et scriptum est in libro verborum dierum coram Rege. Id est, scripta hæc res est in diurnis quæ apud Regem asserva-bantur. Vid. infr. 6, 1. 2.

PARS II. POPVLI PER ESTHEREM LIBERATIO. SECTIO I. PERICVLVM PER HAMANEM STRVCTVM.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III.

Haman, having been exalted above all, when Mordecai would not worship him, obtains a decree from Ahasuerus that all the Jews be killed on a set day.

Vers. 1. AFTER THESE THINGS KING AHASUERUS EXALTED HAMAN THE SON OF HAMMEDATHA WHO WAS OF THE STOCK OF AGAG) Sprung from the Amalekite Kings, with which nation God had willed there to be an internecine war both for Himself and for the Hebrews. Ex. 17, 14. 15. 16. and that the insults which that nation had brought upon the Hebrews should never be cast out of mind Deut. 25, 17. 18. 19. and therefore that there should be no dealings of friendship with them.

For Agag was King of Amalek: whom Samuel ordered to be killed 1 Sam. 15. Compare Josephus, and Lyranus. It does not therefore fit that in the additions c. 16, 10. 14. Haman is said to have been a Macedonian in spirit and race.

AND SET HIS THRONE ABOVE ALL THE PRINCES THAT HE HAD) He had given him the right of precedence among the Satraps. See a similar case 2 Kings 25, 28.

Latin:

CAPUT III.

Aman exaltatus super omnes quum adorari eum nollet Mardochæus, decretum Ahas- veri impetrat, ut omnes Judæi stato die oc- cidantur.

Vers. 1. POST HÆC REX ASSVERVS EXALTAVIT AMAN FILIUM AMADATHI QVI ERAT DE STIRPE AGAG) Ortus ex Regibus Amaleticis, cum qua gente Deus & sibi & Hebræis bellum esse voluerat internecinum. Ex. 17, 14. 15. 16. neque unquam seponi ex animo contumelias, quas ea gens Hebræis intulerat Deut. 25, 17. 18. 19. ac proinde nulla cum illis esse amicitiæ commercia.

Agag enim fuit Rex Amalek: quem occidi jussit Samuel 1. Sam. 15. Conf. Josephus, & Lyran. Non ergo congruit, quod in additamentis c. 16, 10. 14. Aman animo & genere Macedo fuisse dicitur.

ET POSUIT EJUS SOLIVM SUPRA OMNES PRIN- CIPES QVOS HABEBAT) Jus προεδρίας ipsi inter Satrapas dederat. Simile vide 2. Reg. 25, 28.

## 3:2
Vers. 2. THEY BENT THE KNEE AND WORSHIPPED) They showed him honor, especially by bending the knee, as the Egyptians once did to Joseph Gen. 41, 45. others of lower rank by prostrating their bodies, in the way it was the custom for Persians to venerate a King, as Plutarch teaches us in Themistocles: but a Latin writer in the Lives of the Commanders in Conon.

Latin:

Vers. 2. FLECTEBANT GENVA ET ADORABANT) Honorem ei exhibebant, præcipue genua flectendo, ut olim Ægyptii Josepho Genes. 41, 45. minores alii prostrato corpo- re, quomodo Regem venerari mos Persis, ut Plutarchus nos docet Themistocle: scriptor vero Latinus de Vitis Imperato- rum Conone.

## 3:4
Vers. 4. FOR HE HAD SAID THAT HE WAS A JEW) And therefore, by his own law, it was a sin for him to show any honor to a man born of a race divinely devoted to destruction: for otherwise it was not forbidden for Jews to venerate Kings and Princes in the manner which the custom of the East had received. Thus David worshipped Saul, falling upon his face, as was the custom, as Josephus relates.

This reason holds good: But that which the addition c. 13, 14. contains cannot be proven; I feared lest I should transfer the honor of my God to a man: For Ahasuerus did not wish divine honor to be shown to Haman.

Latin:

Vers. 4. DIXERAT ENIM SE ESSE JUDÆUM) Ac proinde ex sua lege nefas sibi ullum honorem exhibere ho- mini nato e stirpe devota divinitus: nam alioqui Judæis non illicitum erat Reges & Principes eo modo venerari, quem mos Orientis receperat. Sic David Saulem προσεκύνησε πε- σὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον, ὡς ἔθος, narrante Josepho.

Recte se habet hæc causa: Non autem probari potest illa quam additamentum c. 13, 14. habet; timui, ne honorem Dei mei transferrem ad hominem: Non enim honorem divinum Amano exhiberi vo- lebat Ahasverus.

## 3:7
Vers. 7. THE LOT WAS CAST INTO THE URN WHICH IN HEBREW IS CALLED PHUR) Nay, it is so called in Persian: in Hebrew, as this text has it, גורל. It was the custom of the Persians and neighboring nations to explore the prosperous or adverse days of a proposed matter by lots cast in a certain way: Haman did this often in this matter: and at length he found a day which the lots promised to be prosperous: but God gave a huge example of how vain those things are. From this superstitious casting of lots those days are called פורים as we read below 9, 31. whence the Codex of Josephus is to be corrected, in which we read: for this reason the Jews celebrate the aforementioned days, calling them Phrouraioi: it should be read Phouraioi. The same error is in the Greek addition to this history: the aforementioned letter of the Phrourai: it should be read Phourai. And thus he calls this whole book, which had been sent by Mordecai to the Jews, afterwards turned into Greek by Lysimachus: We learn that the same days were called by another name by Haman, Anan, in the Theodosian Code, Book of the Jews, under the title concerning the Jews: for in the Justinian Code that word is corrupted.

Latin:

Vers. 7. MISSA EST SORS INURNAM QVÆ HE- BRAICE DICITUR PHUR) Imo Persice sic dicitur: Hebraice, ut textus hic habet גורל. Mos erat Persarum & vi- cinarum gentium, sortibus certo modo jactis explorare dies rei propositæ prosperos aut adversos: id in hac re sæpe fe- cit Aman: tandemque invenit diem, quem sortes prosperum promittebant: at Deus exemplum dedit ingens quam ista sint inania. Ab hoc superstitioso jactu sortium dies isti פורים ut infra legimus 9, 31. unde corrigendus Josephi Codex, in quo legimus: διὰ ταῦτα μὲν Ἰουδαῖοι τὰς προειρημένας ἡμέρας ἑορτάζουσι, προσαγορεύοντες αὐτὰς Φρουραίους: legendum φυ- ραίους. Idem error in additamento Græco ad hanc historiam: τὴν προκειμένην ἐπιστολὴν τῶν Φρουραῖ: legendum φυραῖ. Ita autem vocat totum hunc librum, qui a Mardochæo ad Judæos missus fuerat, postea versus in Græcum a Lysimacho: Eosdem dies alio nomine ab Amane A.nan vocatos discimus Codicis Theodosiani L. Judæos, titulo de Judæis: nam in Codice Ju- stinianeo ea vox corrupta est.

## 3:8
Vers. 8. AND SEPARATED FROM EACH OTHER) He meant to say separated from others. Josephus in this place: a nation unsociable, unlike others, having neither the same religion as others, nor using similar laws, but hostile in customs and practices to your people and to all men. And in the edict itself which follows: a nation ill-disposed to others, strange. What of truth and what of falsehood these have in them you will more easily understand if you see what we have said concerning the Law of War and Peace, book 2, chapter 15, section 19. Tacitus concerning the Jews: Separated in their meals, divided in their beds. Cicero for Flaccus: with Jerusalem standing, and the Jews at peace, yet the religion of those sacred rites was abhorrent to the splendor of this empire, the gravity of our name, and the institutions of our ancestors. Juvenal concerning the same Jews: But accustomed to despise Roman laws, they learn, and keep, and fear the Jewish law.

Latin:

Vers. 8. ET A SE MUTUO SEPARATUS) Voluit dice- re ab aliis separatus. Josephus h. 1. ἔθνος ἄμικτον, ἀσύμφυλον οὔτε θρησκείαν τὴν αὐτὴν τοῖς ἄλλοις ἔχον, οὔτε νόμοις χρώμενον ὁμοίοις, ἐχθρὸν δὲ κἀμ τοῖς ἔθεσι καὶ τοῖς ἐπιτηδεύμασι τῷ σῷ λαῷ καὶ ἅπασιν ἀνθρώποις. Et in ipso edicto quod sequitur: δυσμενὲς ἔθνος τοῖς ἄλλοις ἀλλόκοτον. Quæ quid in se veri, quid falsi habeant facilius intelliges, si videas quæ diximus de jure Belli ac Pacis libr. 2. cap. 15. §. 19. Tacitus de Judæis: Sepa- rati epulis, discreti cubilibus. Cicero pro Flacco: stantibus Hie- rosolymis, pacatisque Judæis, tamen istorum religio sacrorum a splendore hujus imperii, gravitate nominis nostri, majorum in- stitutis abhorrebat. Juvenalis de iisdem Judæis: Romanas autem soliti contemnere leges, Judaicum ediscunt & servant, & metuunt jus.

## 3:9
Vers. 9. HE THOUGHT IT NOTHING TO LAY HANDS UPON MORDECAI ALONE) That is, he thought it little worthy of himself to take vengeance on one man, unless he also destroyed the whole nation, a nation hostile to his own origin.

Latin:

Vers. 9. PRO NIHILO DUXIT IN UNUM MARDO- CHÆUM MITTERE MANUS SVAS) Id est, parum se di- gnum putavit se in uno homine ulcifci, nisi & omnem gen- tem genti originis suæ inimicam everteret.

## 3:9
V. 9. AND TEN THOUSAND TALENTS I WILL WEIGH OUT TO THE KEEPERS OF THY TREASURY) He practiced precious hatreds.

He seems to have offered such a sum, lest the King should complain that by the slaughter of the Jews he would lose the tributes which they were accustomed to pay him. Moreover, in the Hebrew, Chaldean, and Greek LXX, a specification is added, rashly omitted in the Vulgate, that he offered the King as many talents of silver, 10,000, which amount to 150 tons, or 15 million in gold (with 100,000 Joachim thalers or imperials assigned to a ton of gold), and besides that 88,750 Joachim thalers or imperials.

Latin:

V. 9. ET DECEM MILLIA TALENTORVM APPEN- DAM ARCARIIS GAZÆ TVÆ) Exercebat pretiosa odia.

Videtur tantam summam obtulisse, ne Rex causaretur, per Judæorum cædem se tributa, quæ illi pendere folebant, perditurum. Additur autem in Ebræo, Chald. & Græco LXX. determinatio, temere in vulgata omissa, quod argenti talenta totidem obtulerit Regi, 10000. quæ efficiunt 150. tonnas, vel 15. milliones auri, (tonnae auri assignatis 100000. Joachmicis, seu imperialibus) ac praeterea 88750. Joachmicos, vel imperiales.

## 3:10
Vers. 10. THE KING THEREFORE TOOK THE RING WHICH HE WAS USING FROM HIS OWN HAND) As Alexander, having taken the ring from his finger, handed it to Perdiccas.

Latin:

Vers. 10. TVLIT ERGO REX ANNVLVM QVO VTEBATVR DE MANV SUA) Ut Alexander detractum annulum digito, Perdiccae tradidit.

## 3:12
Vers. 12. AS EACH NATION COULD READ) See what is above 1, 22.

Latin:

Vers. 12. UT QVAEQVE GENS LEGERE POTERAT) Vide quae supra 1, 22.

## 3:13
Vers. 13. THAT THEY SHOULD KILL AND DESTROY ALL THE JEWS] Thus Mithridates in one letter killed eighty thousand Roman citizens dispersed through the cities of Asia for the sake of trade. The words are those of Valerius Maximus, book 9, chapter 3. Appian relates the same matter thus: Mithridates wrote secretly to all the satraps and governors of cities, that having kept the thirtieth day, they should all at once set upon the Romans and Italians among them, both them and their wives, and children, and free persons of Italian descent, and having killed them, cast them out unburied, and divide their possessions with King Mithridates. Florus: What is more atrocious than his one edict, when he ordered all men of Roman citizenship who were in Asia to be killed?

Vers. 13. WERE SENT BY THE KING'S COURIERS] The Greeks, by letter-carriers. Understand the Angari, whom the Latin interpreter calls post-riders below VIII, 10, where likewise the Greeks say, by letter-carriers. Suidas interprets Angari as a letter-carrier by relay.

Latin:

Vers. 13. UT OCCIDERENT ET DELERENT OMNES JUDAEOS] Sic Mithridates una epistola octoginta millia civium Romanorum in Asia per urbes negotiandi gratia di- sfersa interemit. Verba sunt Valerii Maximi l. 9. c. 3. Appia- nus rem eandem sic refert: Μιθριδάτης σατράπαις ἅπασι καὶ πόλεων ἄρχουσι δι' ἀποῤῥήτων ἔγραφε, τριακοστὴν ἡμέραν φυλά- ξαντας, ὁμᾶ πάσας ἐπιθέσθαι τοῖς παρὰ σφίσι Ῥωμαίοις καὶ Ἰταλοῖς, αὐτοῖς τε καὶ γυναιξὶν αὐτῶν, καὶ παισὶ, καὶ ἐλευθέροις ὅσοι γένους Ἰταλικοῦ, κτείναντάς τε ἀτάφες ἀποῤῥίψαι, καὶ τὰ ὄντα αὐτοῖς μερίσασθαι πρὸς βασιλέα Μιθριδάτην. Florus: Quid atrocius uno edicto ejus, cum omnes qui in Asia forent Romanae civitatis homines interfici jussit?

Vers. 13. MISSAE SUNT PER CVRSORES REGIS] Graeci, διὰ βιβλιοφόρων. Intellige Angaros, quos veredarios infra vocat Latinus interpres VIII, 10. ubi pariter Graeci, διὰ βιβλιοφόρων. Suidas ἀγγάρες interpretatur γραμματοφόρος ἐκ διαδοχῆς.

## 3:15
Vers. 15. AND ALL THE JEWS WHO WERE IN SUSA WEEPING) He expressed the sense rather than the words, which in the Hebrew are thus: and the city of Susa was perplexed.

THE EDICT HUNG) Thus Tertullian against Marcion IV, with the Augustan censuses perhaps still pending at that time.

Latin:

Vers. 15. ET CUNCTIS JUDAEIS QVI IN SVSAN ERANT FLENTIBVS) Sensum magis expressit quam ver- ba, quae in Hebraeo sic habent: & civitas Susa erat perplexa.

PEPENDIT EDICTVM) Sic Tertullianus adversus Marcionem IV. Augustianis censibus adhuc tunc fortassis pendentibus.

## 4:1 Argument
SECTION II. DIVINELY PROVIDED AID. CHAPTER IV.

Mordecai mourns, and the cause of the mourning is carried to Esther, and she is asked to entreat the King for the life of the Jews: which she promises to do, a three-day fast having been proclaimed.

Vers. 1. WHICH WHEN MORDECAI HAD HEARD HE RENT HIS GARMENTS, AND WAS CLOTHED IN SACKCLOTH SPRINKLING ASHES ON HIS HEAD) He omitted no sign by which he might testify his concern, not so much for himself as for his countrymen.

HE CRIED WITH A LOUD VOICE) The Greeks add what he cried: a nation is being taken away that has done no wrong. So also Josephus, that a nation is being destroyed that has done no wrong.

Latin:

SECTIO II. AUXILIUM DIVINITUS PRAESTITUM. CAPUT IV.

Mardochaius luget, ac causa luctus ad Estherem defertur, eademque rogatur, ut pro vita Ju- daeorum Regem deprecetur: quae triduano in- dicto jejunio id se facturum pollicetur.

Vers. 1. QVAE CVM AVDISSET MARDOCHAEVS SCIDIT VESTIMENTA SUA, ET INDVTVS EST SACCO SPARGENS CINEREM CAPITI) Nullum omi- sit signum, quo suam non tam pro se quam pro popularibus sollicitudinem testaretur.

VOCE MAGNA CLAMABAT) Adjiciunt Graeci, quid clamaverit: αἴρεται ἔθνος μηδὲν ἠδικηκός. Sic & Josephus, ὅτι μηδὲν ἀδικῆσαν ἔθνος ἀναιρεῖται.

## 4:2
Vers. 2. FOR IT WAS NOT LAWFUL FOR ONE CLOTHED IN SACKCLOTH TO ENTER THE KING'S COURT) That is, mourning, as appears below 4.

Latin:

Vers. 2. NON ENIM ERAT LICITVM INDVTVM SACCO AVLAM REGIS INTRARE) Id est, lugentem, ut apparet infra 4.

## 4:3
Vers. 3. THE KING'S CRUEL DECREE) That is, edict, as in Luke 2, 1.

Latin:

Vers. 3. CRVDELE REGIS DOGMA) Id est, edictum, ut Lucae 2, 1.

## 4:11
Vers. 11. GOLDEN SCEPTER] That is, scepter.

This law, that if anyone entered the King's court uncalled, he should be immediately put to death: for which purpose lictors with axes and spears stood around the king, as Josephus, Ammianus book 14, and Herodotus books 3 and 8 testify; Josephus asserts that it was either passed or renewed at the instigation of Haman for this purpose, so that access to the King might be blocked for Esther, Mordecai, and all others, lest they should intercede for the Jews.

Vers. 11. GOLDEN SCEPTER) That is, scepter.

Latin:

Vers. 11. AVREAM VIRGAM] Id est, sceptrum.

HAnc legem ut si quis atrium Regis non voca- tus ingrederetur, statim interficiatur:quo fine regi circumcirca lictores cum securibus & hastis astabant, Josepho, Ammiano l. 14. & Herodoto l. 3. & 8. testibus; Josephus instigante Amano eo fine vel la- tam, vel innovatam perhibet, ut Estheri, Mardo- chaeo caeterisque omnibus aditus ad Regem inter- cluderetur, ne pro Judaeis deprecaremtur.

Vers. 11. AVREAM VIRGAM) Id est, sceptrum.

## 4:13
Vers. 13. DO NOT THINK THAT YOU WILL SAVE YOUR LIFE ONLY, BECAUSE YOU ARE IN THE KING'S HOUSE ABOVE ALL THE JEWS) In the Hebrew: Do not imagine for yourself that you will save yourself (namely, alone) from all the Jews, and that in the King's house. Where there are so many enemies, so many observers.

Latin:

Vers. 13. NE PVTES QVIA ANIMAM TVAM TAN- TVM LIBERES, QVIA IN DOMO REGIS ES PRAE CVNCTIS JVDAEIS) In Hebraeo: Ne imagineris tibi fore ut temet (unam scilicet) de Judaeis omnibus serves, idque in domo Regis. Ubi tot inimici, tot observatores.

## 4:14
Vers. 14. FOR IF YOU REMAIN SILENT NOW, THE JEWS WILL BE DELIVERED BY ANOTHER OCCASION: AND YOU AND YOUR FATHER'S HOUSE WILL PERISH] Indeed

It is as bad to be always silent as it is bad to be always speaking.

WHO KNOWS WHETHER FOR THIS REASON YOU HAVE COME TO THE KINGDOM) Similar to Gen. 45, 5.

Latin:

Vers. 14. SI ENIM NVNC SILUERIS, PER ALIAM OCCASIONEM LIBERABVNTVR JVDAEI: ET TV ET DOMVS PATRIS TVI PERIBITIS] Quippe

Tam malum est semper tacere, quam malum est semper loqui.

QVIS NOVIT UTRUM IDCIRCO AD REGNVM VE- NERIS) Simile Gen. 45, 5.

## 4:16
Vers. 16. DO NOT EAT AND DO NOT DRINK FOR THREE DAYS) Josephus interprets this well, τροφῇ καὶ πότῳ τοῖς ἡδίοσι ἀποταξαμένη. For so it must be read there. Such were those Xerophagiae mentioned by Tertullian, in which one abstained from all broth and any juicier fruits, so that nothing of a vinous nature was either eaten or drunk.

In memory of that fast, the Jews still observe a solemn fast today on the 13th day of Adar, which they call the fast of Esther.

AND I WITH MY MAIDSERVANTS WILL LIKEWISE FAST] In Hebrew, with my girls: so also the LXX, καὶ ἐγὼ ἅβραι μη. These are, as we have said elsewhere, ministering companions. One of these supported the queen by the hand as she went forth, the other carried the train. Josephus here. See those things which we shall say at Judith 8, 26.

AND THEN I WILL GO IN TO THE KING, DOING AGAINST THE LAW] There are certain such violent circumstances that in them to wish to keep the law is to sin against the chief laws. I will add some things from Valerius Maximus. L. Scipio, when there was need for money to be taken from the treasury for the necessary use of the Republic, and the quaestors, because the law seemed to stand in the way, did not dare to open it, as a private citizen demanded the keys, and having opened the treasury, forced the law to yield to utility, book 3, chapter 7, number 1. Where domestic peace is agitated by the waves of sedition, the authority of ancient custom is torn away, book 3, chapter 8, number 6. Agesilaus, when he had discovered at night that a conspiracy had arisen against the Republic of the Lacedaemonians, immediately abrogated the laws of Lycurgus which forbade punishment to be taken from the unconvicted. And so, that laws might always be able to exist, at times they did not exist. Thus also Appian says that the Lacedaemonians, when they were freeing those captured at Pylos from infamy, said, κοιμάσθων οἱ νόμοι τήμερον.

AND DELIVERING ME TO DEATH AND DANGER] In Hebrew, and if I perish, I perish: the magnanimous voice of a woman: the Greeks, ἐὰν καὶ ἀπολέσθαι μὲ δέῃ. Josephus, ὑπισχνεῖτο, κἄν ἀποθανεῖν δέῃ, τῦτο ὑπομένειν. A manner of speaking twin to this in Genesis 43, 14 in the Hebrew.

Clement of Alexandria, book 6, Stromata, chapter 4, attributes this to the faith of Esther, and deservedly celebrates her for it: Again, that perfect faith of Esther, freeing Israel from tyrannical power and from the cruelty of the Satrap, she alone, a woman afflicted by fasts, resisted countless armed forces, dissolving the tyrannical decree through faith, and she indeed mitigated the tyrant; but she repressed Haman, and preserved Israel unharmed through perfect prayer to God.

Latin:

Vers. 16. NON COMEDATIS ET NON BIBATIS TRIBVS DIEBVS) Bene hoc interpretatur Josephus, τροφῇ καὶ πότῳ τοῖς ἡδίοσι ἀποταξαμένη. Ita enim ibi legen- dum. Tales erant Xerophagiae istae Tertulliano memoratae, in quibus abstinebatur omni jurulentia & uvidioribus quibus- que pomis, ne quid vinositatis vel ederetur vel potaretur.

In memoriam istius jejunii adhuc hodie Ju- daei 13. die Adar solemne observant jejunium, quod Estherae jejunium nominant.

ET EGO CVM ANCILLIS MEIS SIMILITER JE- JVNABO] In Hebr. cum puellis meis: sic & LXX. καὶ ἐγὼ ἅβραι μη. Eæ sunt, ut alibi diximus, ministræ comites. Harum altera dominam prodeuntem manu sustentabat, altera porta- bat Syrma. Josephus hic. Vide ea quæ dicemus ad Judith 8, 26.

ET TVNC INGREDIAR AD REGEM, CONTRA LEGEM FACIENS] Sunt quædam tam violentæ περιστάσεις, ut in iis legem servare velle sit in leges præcipuas peccare. Addam quædam ex Valerio Maximo L. Scipio, cum ad neces- sarium Reip. usum pecuniam ex ærario promi opus esset, idque quæstores, quia lex obstare videretur, aperire non au- derent, privatus claves poposcit, patefactoque ærario legem utilitati cedere coegit 3. cap. 7. n. 1. Ubi domestica quies se- ditionum agitata fluctibus est, priscæ consuetudinis auctori- tas convellitur 3. cap. 8. n. 6. Agesilaus cum adversus Rem- publicam Lacedæmoniorum conspirationem ortam noctu comperisset, leges Lycurgi continuo abrogavit, quæ de in- demnatis supplicium sumi vetabant. Itaque ut semper esse possent leges aliquando non fuerunt. Sic & Lacedæmonios cum ad Pylum captos infamiæ eximerent, dixisse ait Appia- nus, κοιμάσθων οἱ νόμοι τήμερον.

TRADENSQVE ME MORTI ET PERICVLO] In Hebr. & si moriar, moriar: magnanima vox fœminæ: Græci ἐὰν καὶ ἀπολέσθαι μὲ δέῃ. Josephus ὑπισχνεῖτο, κἄν ἀποθανεῖν δέῃ, τῦτο ὑπομένειν. Loquendi genus huic geminum Genes. 43, 14. in Hebræo.

Fidei Estheræ hoc tribuit Clem. Alex. l. 6. Strom. c. 4. eamq; merito inde celebrat: Rursus per- fecta illa fide Esther Israelem a tyrannica potestate li- berans, & a crudelitate Satrapæ sola mulier afflicta je- juniis restitit armatis copiis innumerabilibus, tyran- nicum per fidem solvens decretum, & tyrannum quidem mitigavit: Aman vero repressit, & Israelem perfecta ad Deum oratione illæsum conservavit.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V.

Esther, having entered to the King, invites him with Haman to a banquet, in which, being warned by the exhilarated King about some petition, she invites the King again to the banquet of the following day: meanwhile Haman, indignant that he is not honored by Mordecai, prepares a cross for him.

Verse 1. ESTHER WAS CLOTHED IN ROYAL GARMENTS) We are carried away by adornment: Ovid.

Latin:

CAPUT V.

Esther ad Regem ingressa eundem cum Amano ad convivium invitat, in quo ab exhilarato Rege de petitione aliqua monita iterum ad sequen- tis diei convivium Regem invitat: interea Aman indignatus se a Mardochæo non ho- norari, crucem illi parat.

Vers. 1. INDVTA EST ESTHER REGALIBVS VE- STIMENTIS) Auferimur cultu: Ovidius.

## 5:2
Verse 2. SHE KISSED THE TOP OF HIS SCEPTER) In Hebrew, she touched, i.e., she submitted her hand to the scepter. For the sake of reverence and subjection.

Latin:

Vers. 2. OSCVLATA EST SVMMITATEM VIRGÆ EJVS) In Hebr. tetigit i. e. manum sceptro submisit. Reverentiæ & subjectionis ergo.

## 5:3
Verse 3. EVEN IF YOU ASK FOR HALF THE KINGDOM, IT SHALL BE GIVEN TO YOU) So also below 7, 2, a manner of speaking for Kings: so also Mark 6, 23. See those things at Matthew 14, 7.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ETIAMSI DIMIDIAM PARTEM REGNI PETIERIS, TIBI DABITVR) Sic & infra 7, 2. mos lo- quendi Regibus: sic & Marci 6, 23. Vid. quæ ad Matth. 14, 7.

## 5:4
Verse 4. THAT YOU MAY COME TO ME TODAY AND HAMAN TO THE BANQUET WHICH I HAVE PREPARED) After prayers, there is need for prudence, which did not fail Esther. She does not immediately bring forth the thoughts of her mind, but arranges the occasions.

Not only did she thus kindle the King more and more into love for herself—for which end she later invited him a second time—but because she did not dare to do so publicly in the crowd of standing nobles, who would have easily said that a law once passed, according to the custom of Kings, could not be revoked, she judged that she could obtain it from the King when he was exhilarated at the banquet; and it was safer for Esther to have professed that she was a Jewess in secret at the banquet, which seemed dangerous to do publicly before the princes; not to mention what some observe, that it was the custom for the Kings of the Persians to deny nothing to anyone at a banquet. She invites Haman at the same time, both because she knew him to be pleasing to the King, and because, with him alone invited, envy and hatred could easily be brought upon him by the rest of the Satraps—which reason Lyranus gives—and especially so that she might accuse him before the King while present in the name of the decree obtained by fraud against her own people, and block all paths of quibbling to his face.

Latin:

Vers. 4. UT VENIAS AD ME HODIE ET AMAN AD CONVIVIUM QVOD PARAVI) Post preces opus est prudentia, quæ Estheri non defuit. Non statim promit animi cogitata, sed disponit occasiones.

Non solum ita Regem magis magisque in sui amorem accendebat: quo fine postea vice iterata ipsum invitavit, sed quod publice in turba astan- tium procerum non audebat, qui dixissent facile, le- gem latam, ex more Regum, revocari non posse, in convivio, a Rege exhilarato se impetrare posse, cen- sebat: & tutius secreto in convivio se Judæam esse professa est Esther, quod publice coram principibus facere periculosum videbatur; ut taceamus, quod observent nonnulli, regibus Persarum in more fuisse, ut in convivio nil cuipiam negarent. Amanem autem simul invitat, tum quod eum gratum esse Regi nos- set, tum quia solo illo invitato in reliquum Satra- parum invidiam & odium ipse facile induci pote- rat, quam causam Lyranus reddit, tum imprimis, ut eum apud Regem præsentem accusaret decreti per fraudem surrepti contra suos populares nomine, & in os omnes cavillandi vias ei præcluderet.

## 5:10
Verse 10. AND ZARES HIS WIFE) Euripides, Andromache: πολλὰς ἂν εὕροις μηχανὰς· γυνὴ γὰρ εἶ.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ET ZARES UXOREM SUAM) Euripides Andromacha: πολλὰς ἂν εὕροις μηχανὰς· γυνὴ γὰρ εἶ.

## 5:13
Vers. 13. AND WHEN I HAVE ALL THESE THINGS I THINK I HAVE NOTHING. The Hebrew text was rendered thus by Kimchi, Pag., Tremell., Pisc.: And all this does not profit me. The Syrian explains, And all this does not satisfy me. The LXX interpreters: These things do not please me. The Chaldean expressed the sense not badly: All this is not of value with me, i. e., it is of no value to me, it is not estimated by me. It was observed by Ludovicus Dievius that שוה is the same as ערך to be estimated, as in Esth. 7, 4. אין הצר שוה the enemy is not to be estimated to the damage of the King: and that among the Chaldeans and Rabbis שוה signifies to be worthy, to be of value. But why did Haman estimate this as nothing, as long as he saw Mordecai sitting before the Royal gates? This is not to be attributed only to ambition and envy, as Bernh. exclaims concerning that in book 1, de consider.: O ambition, the cross of the ambitious, how do you, while tormenting all, please all? But especially I feared, because he was indeed afraid that Mordecai might sniff out, or would subsequently sniff out from that conversation in the King's court, that he (Haman) himself had been privy to the conspiracy of the Eunuchs against the King, inasmuch as it is considered to have been entered into so that the kingdom might be transferred to Haman. Therefore he desired the same to be extinguished. He chose, however, the punishment of the cross 1. as most bitter. 2. Familiar to the Persians. 3. ignominious, as noted by Bonfrerius.

Vers. eod. AS LONG AS I SEE MORDECAI) He did not know that he was so close to Esther, but he knew he did not deserve death. Haman was such as the writer of the Oetaean Hercules places before our eyes: He cultivates kings, that he may trample all, and destroy some, and lift up none. He desires to be powerful only that he may harm. That is an excellent and rare praise in Seneca's consolation to Polybius: No one felt his power as an injury.

Latin:

Vers. 13. ET CUM HÆC OMNIA HABEAM NIHIL ME HABERE PUTO. Ebræum textum ita Kimch. Pag. Tremell. Pi- scat. reddidere: Et hoc omne non prodest mihi. Syrus exponit, Et hoc omne non satisfacit mihi. LXX. In- terpp. Hæc non placent mihi. Chaldæus Sensum non male expressit: Totum hoc non est pretium apud me, i. e. nullius mihi pretii est, non æstimatur mihi. Ob- servatum Ludovico Dievio שוה idem esse, quod ערך æstimari ut Efth. 7, 4. אין הצר שוה non est hostis æsti- mandus ad damnum Regis: & apud Chaldæos & Rab- binos שוה significare dignum esse, valere. Cur autem hoc pro nihilo æstimabat Haman, quamdiu Mardo- chæum videbat sedentem ante fores Regias? Non ambitioni tantum & invidiæ hoc tribuendum, uti Bernh. de illa exclamat l. 1. de consider. O ambitio ambientium crux, quomodo omnes torquens omnibus places? Sed imprimis metui, quod nempe vereretur Mardochæum subolfacere, aut deinceps subodo- raturum ex ista in aula Regis conversatione, quod ipse (Haman) conscius fuerit conjurationis Ev- nuchorum adversus Regem, utpote quæ inita cen- setur, ut regnum ad Hamanem transferretur. Ideo extinctum eundem cupiebat. Delegit autem crucis supplicium 1. ut maxime acerbum. 2. Persis fami- liare. 3. ignominiosum notante Bonfrerio.

Vers. eod. QVAMDIV VIDERO MARDOCHÆUM) Non sciebat Estheri tam propinquum, at sciebat mortem non meritum. Erat Aman talis qualem scriptor Oetæi Her- culis ob oculos ponit: Colit hic Reges, calcet ut omnes, Perdatque aliquos, nullumque levet. Tantum ut noceat cupit esse potens. Egregia & rara illa laus in Senecæ consolatione ad Polybium: Nemo potentiam ejus injuria sensit.

## 6:1
Vers. 1. AND HE COMMANDED THE HISTORIES AND ANNALS TO BE BROUGHT TO HIM) The daily records, as we said above 2, 23. γράμματα μνημόσυνα τῶν ἡμερῶν: the Greeks in this place. But it was the custom of the Persians to inscribe in books the names of those who had rendered excellent service to the King. Herodotus, Urania: And he was recorded as a benefactor of the King. Xerxes in his Epistle to Paul: Your good deed shall be recorded in our house forever. It exists in Thucydides 1. Procopius, Gothic 2: Asserting that he would be a friend to King Chosroes in the highest degree for this deed, and recorded among the Persians for a good deed for all time.

Latin:

Vers. 1. JVSSITQVE SIBI AFFERRI HISTORIAS ET ANNALES) Diurna, ut diximus supra 2, 23. γράμματα μνη- μόσυνα τῶν ἡμερῶν: Græci h. l. Mosautem erat Persarum libris inscribere nomina eorum qui Regi operam navassent egre- giam. Herodotus Urania: Φύλακος δὲ εὐεργέτης βασιλῆος ἀνεγράφη. Xerxes in Epist. ad Paul. κεῖσεταί σοι εὐεργεσία ἐν τῷ ἡμετέρῳ οἴκῳ εἰς αεὶ ἀνάγραπτος. Exstat apud Thucydidem 1. Procopius Gotthic. 2. Φίλον μὲν ἀυτὸν ἐν τοῖς μάλιστα χοσρόῃ βασιλεῖ τῷ ἔργῳ τύτῳ ἰσχυρισάμενος ἔσεσθαι, Πέρσαις δὲ ἀνά- γραπτον ἐπ' εὐεργεσίᾳ εἰς τὸν πάντα αἰῶνα.

## 6:3
Vers. 3. WHAT HONOR AND REWARD HAS MORDECAI OBTAINED FOR THIS FAITHFULNESS) Worthy of the greatness of Kings, to leave no notable good deed without a reward. It is shameful for a King to be surpassed in benefits.

Latin:
