CHAPTER XXXIII. Elihu, having secured attention for himself, teaches that God also afflicts the pious, so that He may preserve them from sins.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIII. Elihu attentione sibi conciliata Deum etiam pios affligere, ut eos a peccatis præservet docet.

## 33:4
Verf. 4. THE SPIRIT OF GOD HAS MADE ME. This must be understood of the Holy Spirit; the word Spirit placed absolutely, and the breath of the Almighty, and the divine hypostatic predicates, 'has made me,' 'has enlivened me,' teach this. See Vol. 3, System of Theology.

Latin:

Verf. 4. SPIRITUS DEI FECIT ME. DE Spiritu S. hoc accipiendum vox Spiritus ab- solute posita, & spiraculum omnipotentis, & præ- dicata hypostatica divina, fecit me, vivificavit me, do- cent. Vid. T. 3. Syst. Theol.

## 33:6
Verf. 6. BEHOLD, EVEN ME AS ALSO THEE GOD HAS MADE] In the Hebrew: Behold I am according to thy mouth to God: that is, just as you yourself had requested above in chapter 13, I will speak for God, but true things.

Latin:

Verf. 6. ECCE ET ME SICUT ET TE FECIT DEUS] In Hebræo: Ecce ego secundum os tuum Deo: id est, ita ut tu ipse postulaveras supra cap. 13. loquar pro Deo, sed vera.

## 33:7
Verf. 7. AND LET NOT MY ELOQUENCE BE HEAVY UPON THEE] In the Hebrew: My hand shall not be heavy upon thee. Thus also the Greeks: ἐδὲ ἡ χείρ με, βαρεῖα ἔςαι ἐπὶ σοὶ. Naturally, the א in אכפי is prosthetic.

Latin:

Verf. 7. ET ELOQVENTIA MEA NON TIBI SIT GRA- VIS] In Hebræo: Manus mea non erit gravis apud te. Sic & Græci: ἐδὲ ἡ χείρ με, βαρεῖα ἔςαι ἐπὶ σοὶ. Nimirum א in אכפי est προσθετικὸν.

## 33:10
verf. 10. BECAUSE HE FINDS QUARRELS AGAINST ME. Cocceius and Scultetus rendered it 'vacillations,' because תנועה denotes motion: so that the lapses of a weaker mind, troubled by stronger temptations, might be designated. Vatablus interpreted it in almost the same sense as 'departures'.

Latin:

verf. 10. QUIA QUERELAS IN ME REPERIT. תנועות vacillationes reddidit Coccejus, & Scultetus, quia תנועה motionem notat: ut desi- gnentur lapsus animi infirmioris, turbati per vali- diores tentationes. Vatabl. eodem pene sensu DIS- CESSIONES interpretatus est.

## 33:13
Verf. 13. WHY HAST THOU NOT ANSWERED THEE TO ALL WORDS] Do you think yourself the victor because he did not propose his own just arguments?

Latin:

Verf. 13. QVOD NON AD OMNIA VERBA RESPONDE- RIT TIBI] Ideo te victorem putas, quod ille justa sua non proposuit?

## 33:14
Verf. 14. GOD SPEAKS ONCE, AND ACCORDING TO THAT VERY THING HE DOES NOT REPEAT] Better: God speaks once or twice, and it happens that he does not care, namely he whom God addresses. Others, with Olympiodorus and Philippus Presbyter: GOD SPEAKS ONCE, AND A SECOND TIME HE DOES NOT CONSIDER IT, explaining it concerning the immutability of the divine decree: since God has once decreed something. Because the speaking of God often signifies His decrees; not like a man, who repents of his deeds, and calls it back again under the anvil of consideration.

Latin:

Verf. 14. SEMEL LOQVITUR DEUS, ET SECUNDUM ID IPSUM NON REPETIT] Melius: Semel loquitur Deus aut bis, sitque ut non curet, is nempe quem Deus alloquitur. Alii cum Olympiod. & Philipp. Presbytero: SEMEL LOQUITUR DEUS, ET SECUNDO ILLUD NON CONSIDERAT de immutabilita- te decreti divini explicant: cum Deus semel aliquid decrevit. Quia loquutio Dei sæpe ejus decreta significat; non ut homo, quem factorum pœnitet, iterum sub incudem considerationis id revocat.

## 33:15
Verf. 15. BY A DREAM IN A NIGHT VISION] He shows how God was accustomed to address men in those times. See Gen. 20, 6. ch. 31, 24.

Latin:

Verf. 15. PER SOMNIUM IN VISIONE NOCTURNA] Osten- dit quomodo Deus illis temporibus alloqui homines soleret. Vide Gen. 20, 6. c. 31, 24.

## 33:19
Verf. 19. AND HE MAKES ALL HIS BONES TO ROT] In the Hebrew: Although the multitude of his bones be strong: that is, even if the structure of the body be most robust.

Latin:

Verf. 19. ET OMNIA OSSA EJUS MARCESCERE FACIT] In Hebræo: Utut multitudo ossium ejus fortis: id est, etiamsi robustissima sit corporis compage.

## 33:23
IF THERE BE FOR HIM AN ANGEL SPEAKING] מליץ, which is translated here as speaking, signifies μεσίτην, an advocate, and thus Maimonides explains it here. Other Hebrews also think that the history of Abimelech is referred to, who was warned by an Angel. Angels are μεσῖται in two ways, both by warning men and by praying for them. This is the ascent and descent on Jacob's ladder.

TO ANNOUNCE MAN'S EQUITY] To remind a man of his duty.

These things are said in favor of the Papists, who introduced the Platonic dogma concerning mediating Angels into the Church and built the invocation of Angels upon it. Hence they attempt to extract it from this passage, as can be read in Bellarmine, book 1, On the Beatitude of the Saints, ch. 19, and Tirinus on this passage, and Pineda here: who believes that with this passage, as if it were a drawn and shining sword, he can successfully pursue heretics for invoking Saints and Angels, and slaughter it. But let us suppose that the discourse here is about a created Angel, and indeed about one of the ministering Spirits; nothing else could be inferred than that the Angels in heaven pray for the saints: as we do not deny this general intercession, so from it the invocation of Angels can in no way be concluded, because they neither know our special necessity, Isa. 3, nor if they did, would they be religiously invoked for that reason, since this worship should belong to GOD alone, Matt. 4. But since in the Hebrew source there is not 'an Angel speaking for him,' but עָלָיו, 'over' or 'with him,' to announce, namely, to man his righteousness, therefore some explain it not as an Angel praying to God for man, but as some minister or Legate of God, interpreting the will of God to man: If a man has some minister as an interpreter of the divine will, who, namely, draws him back from sins and leads him back into the way, God will have mercy on him; which explanation the Jesuit Pineda brings forward and does not reject. Verily, however, when the individual words are rightly weighed, they convince that the discourse is not about any other Angel than the uncreated Son of God. He is named מַלְאָך, Angel or sent one, which name no one can doubt is appropriate for the Son of God: who is sent by the Father to announce the will of the Father and to execute it among men. Whence he is called the Angel or messenger of the covenant, because he announces and makes a covenant of grace with men, Matt. 3, 1; Zech. 3. He is called the Angel of the Lord, who is called Jehovah the Lord, v. 2, and here and there elsewhere in the appearances of the Old Testament, especially those which were made to the Patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac, and Moses; he is introduced by the name and form of an angel, so that at that time, when the history of Job was enacted, this name was commonly known to designate the Son of God: whom Jacob also invoked over his grandsons, Gen. 48, 16: The Angel, who redeemed me from all evil, bless these boys. The Angel is indicated who is with him, that is, with God, or before God; for that עָלָיו seems more correctly referred to God than to man; because it is then treated of man, if there be with him an Angel advocate, one of a thousand, to indicate to man his righteousness. If a man were being designated, it would have to be said: if there be with the man an Angel to indicate to him his righteousness. That the particle עַל is the same as 'with' or 'before' is manifest from other passages, Gen. 24, 30; Jud. 3, 19; Zech. 4, 14. That Angel who is said to be peculiarly with God, or before God, who else is he but the Son of God, the angel of his face, called by a similar reason in Isa. 63, 10? Which phrase concerning the Son of God here implies both the intimate περιχώρησιν of the Son and the Father, while preserving the distinction of persons, on account of which he is said to be πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν, John 1, 1, and also the appearance of the Son of God before the Father, which happens for the sake of mediation. He is called the Angel מֵלִיץ, which word, as Grotius admits, signifies an advocate, μεσίτην, and is thus accepted by Maimonides, the most learned of the Hebrews. But what Angel is called an advocate in the Scriptures, except the one Son of God, who alone and only is the mediator of God and men, 1 Tim. 2, 5, and the one advocate of men before God, 1 John 2, 2; whom the Papists make Mediators and Advocates besides him, whether Angels or deceased saints, the Scripture ignores: for nowhere does it assign this office to them; nay, it reprobates it: because while it constitutes Christ as the one mediator and advocate, it openly excludes others. In the Chaldean paraphrase this name is rendered פַּרַקְלִיטָא, παράκλητος, which is there opposed to the accusers, קַטֵיגוֹרַיָא. But this name of the advocate is so proper to the Angel of the covenant that it is never attributed to any other of the angels, 1 John 2, 2; nay, as the scripture denies, was ever said to them of the Angels, sit at my right hand Heb. 1. so it is also not said to them, that they are our paraclete, because for this reason the Son of God sits at the right hand of God, that he may intercede for us Rom. 8, 34. Some indeed explain the word מליץ as interpreter, from Is. 43, 27. But here מליץ is considered not among men, but before God; therefore not as an interpreter, but as an advocate & mediator; And the act of this mediatorial office is referred to, namely intercession verse 24. wherefore it is necessary to accept this concerning the Son of GOD, who alone is the perpetual Advocate of his own before GOD, and without whose intercession it cannot happen that anyone obtains grace. Which is also indicated here: If there be an Advocate for man before God, he will hold him acceptable: For thus it is hinted, that man does not otherwise obtain mercy, than if this advocate intervenes before God. Furthermore, one Angel out of a thousand is called an Advocate, and it is indicated that there are indeed many legates and messengers of God; for thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand serve him. Dan. 7, 50. But that there is only one Angel and legate, who is at the same time our Advocate before God. The name Angel is common by a certain reason, for the Son of God also was sent by God, but the office of advocate is proper to him; ONE out of a thousand, who are called Angels, namely that Angel of the covenant, and of the great counsel, is our mediator and advocate before God the Father, which is his own proper and perpetual and ἀκοινώνητον [incommunicable] office. One therefore, but the chief one, is understood μοναδικῶς [uniquely]. Just as one mediator εἷς μεσίτης is said 1. Tim. 2, 5. That one however is among a thousand, because around him are myriads of Angels, of whom he himself is the Prince, as Jos. 5, 14. The Son of God seen in the likeness of a man called himself the prince of the host of the Lord; And Ps. 68, 8. it is sung concerning him, the chariots of the Lord are thousands of thousands, the Lord is among them in Sinai in the Sanctuary. The same mediator and Angel, who εἰς διαταγὰς ἀγγέλων [by the disposition of angels] had brought the law among the ordered ranks of Angels Acts 7, 38. 55. Gal. 3, 19. If a created Angel were understood, why would this office of intercession be ascribed to one above others out of thousands? Are not all Angels equal in affection and love toward the faithful, and do they not bear equal care for them, or is this office proper to some one? do not the myriads of thousands defend the just man, who is afflicted, who does not sin? R. Nachmanides asks here.

Now if we descend to the special ἐξέτασιν [examination] of the offices and predicates which are brought forward here concerning that Angel, what is clearer than that they befit the one Angel of the covenant, but not the ministering Angels τοῖς πνεύμασι λειτεργικοῖς [the ministering spirits]; the first is of illumination: to indicate to man his uprightness; or God's, his will revealed both in the law and the Gospel; or man's, namely what is right, what the Lord requires of him, or what his duty is, if indeed he wishes to return into favor with God, Mich. 6, 8. Job 1, 18. c. 6, 29. 1. Job 3, 13. To say and indicate this is not an Angelic office, for God did not ordain that we be informed through Angels: but the discourse here is about that which is ordinary, not extraordinary, because the reason is indicated by which the afflicted one can obtain grace, in his cross and calamity. Nor is there any question here of an inefficacious indication, but one which is joined with the power and efficacy of illumination, and conversion, and the gift of faith, so that the ear of man may be opened v. 26. so that he may no longer be blind and deaf, but may receive and embrace with true faith those things which are indicated. Which no Angel performs, except the Angel of the covenant our Mediator, who alone reveals the Father to us Matth. 11, 27.

Job 1, 18. The second is: of gracious intercession: And let grace embrace him, and say, redeem him, lest he descend into the pit, I have found a ransom: where there are as many words, as there are almost weights of reasons, for the Angel of the covenant, and against the ministering Angels. For it is not said of a ministering Angel, that he embraces afflicted believers with grace, but of that Angel of the gracious covenant, whose grace and mercy is often and very often sung in the Scriptures. It seems to be a matter of special grace, which follows the indication of uprightness and faith, and is the grace proper to the faithful, by which indeed the Son of God embraces those who believe in him. That intercessory discourse befits not a created Angel, but the one Son of God, joined with authority and δεινότητι [vehemence]. For here he asks from the Father, that he may snatch us from the pit, by the power of his merit on account of the redemption, made by his blood. Redeem him. The word פדה although it is sometimes used concerning redemption which is made by a price Lev. 27, 27. Psal. 49, 8. yet it also occurs concerning liberation, which is made without a price Deut. 9, 26. Neh. 1, 12. Here therefore, since liberation is attributed to God the Father, it has a place in the latter meaning, concerning liberation from slayers and from destruction, which he himself provides to the faithful by his grace, which nevertheless presupposes the redemption of the mediator, and comes to us on account of the same. It befits not a ministering Angel, but the one Angel of the covenant, what is held here, I have found a ransom. For that some interpret this concerning the ministers of the word, that they themselves find this λύτρον [ransom] in Scripture, and propose it from it, that is improper, nor does it correspond to the dignity of this intercession. For we hear nothing διακονικὸν [ministerial] here: all things are said with ἐξουσία [authority] and power. Therefore neither do others who refer these things to God in this way, God will have mercy on the sick man, that is, announce to him liberation, for I have looked upon the λύτρον [ransom] of the Son, deserve the calculation. For since it is a matter of liberation, there is no reason why we should understand here metonymically only the declaration of liberation. The words can be understood properly, and therefore also ought to be, because one must not depart from the τῷ ῥητῷ [literal sense] of Scripture, unless Scripture itself compels it. Therefore, to the advocate of man is attributed not only such intercession, which is never inefficacious, Job 12, 42. but also the finding of the λύτρον [ransom], which is the cause and foundation of the hearing of the intercession: because it is not that naked one, but made ἱλαστικὴ [propitiatory] by the virtue of merit and propitiation found by the mediator himself. Which befit none but the Angel of the covenant, our one advocate, who by the virtue of the ἱλασμοῦ [propitiation], which he performed for the whole world, intercedes for us Rom. 8, 33. 34. 1. Joh. 2, 2. The distinction of terms in this most exquisite formula of intercession must be carefully noted: For God the Father is said to deliver us, lest we descend into the pit: But to find and provide propitiation and λύτρον is the work of the Son of God, the Angel Mediator. כפר, although it may denote a covering in Gen. 6:13, yet by metaphor, but through more frequent usage, to such an extent that, as Cocceius rightly observes here, the metaphorical notion turns in a certain way into the proper one, it denotes the price by which one is propitiated, a penalty is redeemed, wrath is appeased, and favor is reconciled. As by a covering the old face of a thing is changed into another, so by appeasement the guilty is changed into the righteous, with the fault as it were obliterated. See Isa. 1:18. Therefore, whatever intervenes to obliterate a fault is called כפר, and whatever at all is given for another, so that he may be exempted from harm, the payment of which price is called satisfaction. Since therefore the Son of GOD alone paid the λύτρον for us, and the ἀντίλυτρον Matt. 20:28, Mark 10:45, 1. Tim. 2:5, he alone can say, I have found כפר or λύτρον. This finding respects both the counsel of eternal and hypostatic Wisdom in the most holy senate of the H. Trinity, and the execution of the same, because he found it not in another, but in himself alone; he found the ransom, while he himself provided that which he had counseled. For he who gave the counsel also brought the aid. By the same phrase the Mediator is likewise said in Heb. 9:12, αἰώνιον λύτρωσιν εὑρόμενος, to have found eternal redemption: It is called eternal λύτρωσις, and because λύτρωσις includes τὸ λύτρον, therefore the price of redemption itself is also eternal in a certain respect, the power of which extends from eternity to eternity, because God regarded it from eternity (Ephes. 1:4; Apoc. 13:8) and in eternity, by the regard and power of the same, He has delivered us and is about to save us. To find is sometimes the same as to have, because what we find, that we have. See Ps. 12:9. So here, I have found a ransom, that is, I have a price of equal value, which you will accept for the guilt, so that he may be delivered from the pit: because through this ἀπολύτρωσιν and the ransom of the blood of Christ, we are sent forth from that pit in which there is no water (Zech. 9:11). To some it seems that by this word, I HAVE FOUND a ransom, it is also looked upon as that which is apprehended through faith, because our Mediator finds a ransom with the constrained sinner, namely, one apprehended by him through faith, and therefore He asks of God that, in regard to the faith which He finds, He may be willing to deliver the same from destruction. These things by no means befit ministering Angels: they find neither the λύτρον of human redemption nor faith in the hearts of believers.

Add to these the effect of intercession, both bodily and spiritual. The former is expressed thus: his flesh shall be fuller than a child's, he shall return to the days of his youth. The latter is proposed in these words: he shall pray unto God, and He will be favorable unto him, and he shall see His face with joy, and God will render unto man His righteousness. For on account of the intercession of our Mediator, we obtain both bodily and spiritual goods, the grace of God or the vision of the face of God, and the righteousness of God:

that God gives His righteousness. For the righteousness of God is given to us (Isa. 45:25; Rom. 3:25). To which is subjoined the confession of the man received into grace. Restored and received into grace, he walks toward men, or he will look upon men, he will again approach their assembly, and desiring also the conversion of others, he will instruct them by his own example, and therefore he will say openly and will confess: I have sinned, and that which was right, I have perverted, and

it did not profit me. (But God) has redeemed my soul, that it should not pass into destruction, and my life looks upon the light: as it is read according to the consonants in the Hebrew: by which manner is indicated the certainty of grace, which is in the faithful: Or if it be read according to the vowels: God has redeemed his soul, and his life looks upon the light: so that Elihu concludes with these things, that it happens thus, because the Mediator, by interceding with these words, deliver him, that he may not descend into the pit, has requested: For the effect thus responds to the intercession: He has redeemed his soul, that it may not pass into destruction, or the pit of destruction. Now follows the conclusion of this discourse and of this truly Evangelical and most wholesome counsel; by which at the same time the ordinary process of God is opened, as well as His intention, both in the affliction of the faithful and in their erection through the word of the Gospel: Behold, all these things God works twice or thrice with man, to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life. These very things, he says, by which it might seem that God is doing this, so that someone is to be cast headlong into the pit entirely and deprived of the light of life, He does to the end that he may in truth be delivered from the pit and enlightened with the light of life. For the end of the cross and the affliction of the pious is not destruction, but their salvation, whence the benefits which come to us through the cross are both privative, the deliverance of the soul from destruction, and positive, the illumination of the same, and the enjoyment of the light of eternal life. All these things God works not only by sending the cross, but on account of the intercession of the Angel Mediator, and by delivering again with the λύτρον, by bestowing righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit, so that not once, but again and again, if indeed the eternal salvation of man so requires, He uses this process, until at length his faith, like gold proved in the fire, is found to be τιμιώτερῷ, and by the example of the faithful thus aroused, others also may be converted to the faith. That this is the ordinary process of God, and the way by which the faithful are led to salvation, Elihu teaches, and Scripture testifies throughout (1 Pet. 1:7; Heb. 12:5 ff.; Jas. 1:3; Rom. 5:3, ch. 8:28, 29; Acts 14:22; 2 Tim. 3:12). While he demonstrates the tempted man, he says, Gregory the Great (lib. 24, Moral. cap. 1) shows in what temptation the whole human race is placed: and while he narrates what is done specifically in individuals, he clearly intimates what is done generally in all: whence also he soon brought this general remedy of medicine to this general pestilence, saying: That Christ, the Angel of the great counsel, has spoken to us similar to us, as regards equity: a man interceding for men, and He obtained indulgence, heard for His reverence.

Let us now gather into a summary the arguments of our interpretation: (1) That Angel who is called μοναδικῶς the Angel, and was called so at that time of Job in particular, because He was sent by God to deliver the Patriarchs and other faithful; (2) who is with God as regards the intimate περιχώρησιν and ὁμοοσίαν with God, the Angel of the face of the Lord; (3) that He is with God the Father, and intercedes, is necessary if anyone is to be delivered; (4) the Angel who is מליץ, our mediator and Advocate with God, and whose office this is, proper and perpetual; (5) who is one of a thousand, i.e., among the innumerable legates of God, who are sent by God for the sake of the salvation of men, as He is by far more eminent than other Angels, so He is sent by God peculiarly above all who are called by this name, on account of our eternal salvation. (6) Who is ONE AND ALONE in performing this office, and rejoices in that name and honor, because he is the mediator of God and men, and as mediator and our advocate pleads our cause. (7.) Whose proper work as Angel this is, that he may show to man the righteousness of God or even of our duty at all times, from the foundation of the world or the fall of man, after he fell from his original Wisdom, and his concreated righteousness. (8) And not only show it to him; as a Prophet, and one who performs a Prophetic office, but also by internal illumination and conversion work the same in man, by divine efficacy. (9) That Angel, who embraces the faithful with his grace and mercy. (10) And out of grace and intimate compassion intercedes for each one of the faithful especially, when they are placed in straits, and are constrained. (11) And indeed with an intercession not common or vulgar, but ἐξαιρέτως proper, and authoritative, joined with divine ἐξοσίᾳ: not ineffectual and vain, but effectual, and such as is always heard. (12) Not merely ἐνκλικῇ, but ἱλασικῇ which relies on the merit of the price, and the expiation of this very Angel the παρακλητε. (13) And which also has all its force from that price and propitiation. By which alone it is provided that we are brought back from God, lest we descend into the pit. (14) The Angel, who found כפר propitiation, λυτρον and eternal απολύτρωσιν, and thus the Angel גאל our Redeemer, (15) who by this his propitiation delivered us from the pit, and provides that we do not descend into the pit. (16.) Who finds a ransom in the afflicted and constrained, that which is apprehended by faith, and regards their faith, and esteems it, and presents and proposes it to God the Father, so that they may be delivered in the very act. (17) That Angel, to whose expiation and intercession it is to be attributed that we are restored to bodily health. (18) And that, supplicating God primarily for the salvation of the soul, by the power of the same intercession, we are held acceptable, and obtain his grace; and thus also see the face of God with joy. (19) Then that God restores to the constrained man his righteousness, not only absolves him from sin, but instructs and enriches him with eternal righteousness. (20)

Whose grace, expiation, and the fruits of expiation, namely the bodily and spiritual benefits whichsoever accrue to the faithful, are especially to be proclaimed and propagated in the Church by men who have been restored and received into favor: as being the proper object of the evangelical proclamation: and a true antidote for the afflicted against the sickness of soul and body. (21) Which are also to be proclaimed in such a way that, by humble confession of sin, others may, by our example, celebrate the mercy of God, who redeems our soul that it may not pass into the pit, and that it may behold life and eternal light, and may be led to God the deliverer through the Angel Mediator, be illuminated, converted, and that those who have sinned and made straight the crooked, may likewise acknowledge and attain to true justice and righteousness. (22) Finally, since this is proposed as the ordinary process of God, and the ordinary means of conversion and salvation, not extraordinary, as to how God deals with man to bring his soul back from the pit, and that it may be illuminated with the light of life, the discourse here is concerning that Angel, whose intercession and propitiation all need, that they may be delivered from the pit and illuminated with the light of life; Whose grace is to be announced and proclaimed to all in the Church for salvation, that they may sustain themselves by his propitiation and intercession, and in the same seek grace, justice, and joy, and enjoy deliverance and the light of life, by the virtue of this λύτρον, and the intercession of that Angel Mediator. All of which can be subsumed not concerning any created Angel or minister, but concerning the uncreated Angel, the Son of God, the Angel of the covenant of grace, so that from this an invincible conclusion may emerge, that the discourse here is concerning none other than the Son of God, the Angel of the covenant of grace.

And certainly not without reason does Elihu use such a magnificent opening of his speech here, when he proposes the highest mystery of salvation: since he demands from Job both attention and a response with a great apparatus of words. Attention indeed, not only with a gentle request, but truly, 'Hear, I pray, Job, my sayings, and hearken to all my words': But also with a promise of freedom, 'Behold, I pray, I have opened my mouth, my tongue speaks in my palate,' since he speaks with μετὰ παῤῥησίας about great matters: which that phrase 'to open the mouth' implies, Psalm 78:2, Proverbs 24:7, Matthew 5:2.

and then of sincerity; 'the uprightness of my heart [shall speak] my words, and my lips shall speak knowledge purely': and also with a commemoration of his origin: which he attributes to the whole Holy Trinity.

The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty (the Son of God) has given me life: thus, the counsel of the Holy Trinity, regarding man, its admirable workmanship, intending to afflict him with the cross, and to assert the honor and glory of his creator, who made and gave us life, not so much for this life as for the other, requires due attention: And when he invites to a response, he promises that he will announce things to him in a kind and pleasing manner: 'Behold, my terror shall not terrify or overwhelm you' v. 7. See here the whole συνέχειαν and how aptly everything coheres in the most learned analysis of our blessed Scultetus, and you will easily recognize that everything is consistent with our interpretation. To which, finally, the authority of excellent interpreters adds some weight, who with us explain the present passage concerning the Mediator Christ. Gregory the Great, book 24, Morals, chapter 1. Who, he says, is this Angel, if not He who is called by the Prophet the Angel of the great counsel? And he says well: 'If there be for him an Angel speaking': because, as the Apostle says, he also intercedes for us. Thus also the Ordinary Gloss, Berno of Reichenau, and Hugh of Saint-Cher explain it in this place, as well as the more recent Johannes Cocceius and Christophorus Scultetus in this place. We do not indeed deny, says Cocceius, that some of these things can in their own way also be said of men, such as the name Angel, interpreter, likewise to indicate uprightness, to show mercy, to pray for deliverance, to find in their own way a ransom, or to attest to the faith of the sick person, through which he has a ransom: But that we should explain those things thinly, how they also apply to men, and primarily through forced tropes, there is no cause; since it is permitted to follow the style of the Holy Spirit in a simple and plain sense. The predicates show what the subjects are like. At least to hold tenaciously to a thinner sense, and to reject the fuller sense which Scripture insinuates, although that makes more for the matter, is the behavior of those who love μειώσεις and extenuations in the interpretation of the divine word. Blessed Scultetus says, Christ is called the Angel, Malachi 3:1, he is one and the chief among thousands of Angels, he is the interpreter, the Word of the Father, and παράκλητος, the advocate (as the Chaldean translates here), he is before God, Colossians 1:18, and the Angel of his face, Exodus 23:20. For עליו can hardly be referred to a man, since in the following member the word אור would be insolently repeated, the following predicates suit him best. And afterwards; But these things can be explained best, fully, and properly, if you expound the former concerning the Son of God: 'He will have mercy on him, he will embrace him with his grace' ויחננו 'and interceding for him before the Father, he will say; deliver him, that he may not die, that he may not perish forever.' I have found, and I have acquired propitiation or redemption, with me is the λύτρον and redemption for his sins. These things concerning the sense of this passage.

What Grotius adds concerning the mediatorial office of Angels, that they are mediators in two ways, namely by warning men and by praying for them, and that this is the ascent and descent on Jacob's Ladder, he owes to Platonic and Rabbinic inventions. Even if they sometimes extraordinarily warn men, and in general it can be granted that they rarely pray for men, they are not therefore called our Mediators in the Scriptures: nor does that ascent and descent in Jacob's ladder signify that: But in general it signifies the προθυμίαν of the Angels to serve men: for whose sake they are said to descend and in turn ascend, just as they descended when they celebrated the birth of Christ with a hymn on earth, and afterwards are said to have ascended in turn into heaven, Luke 2:15. They are also to be understood to descend when they minister on earth, Hebrews 1:13, and to ascend when they transfer souls into heaven, Luke 16:23.

Verse of the same.

Latin:

Verf. 23. SI FUERIT PRO EO ANGELUS LOQVENS] מליץ quod hic loquens vertitur, significat μεσίτην advocatum, & sic hic explicat Maimonides. Alii quoque Ebræi putant respici Historiam Abimelechi, qui per Angelum admonitus fuit. Angeli duobus modis μεσῖται sunt, & monendo ho- mines, & pro eis orando. Hic est ascensus & descensus in scala Jacobi.

UT ANNUNCIET HOMINIS ÆQVITATEM] Ut hominem officii sui commoneat.

Hæc in gratiam Papicolarum dicuntur, qui Platonicum dogma de Angelis mediatoribus in Ec- clesiam invexerunt, & Angelorum invocationem ei- dem superstruxere. Unde conantur ex hoc loco eam exsculpere, uti legere est apud Bellarminum l. 1. de Beat. Sanct. c. 19. & Tirinum in h. l. & Pinedam hic: qui loco hoc, velut districto & splendenti gladio hæreticos pro invocandis Sanctis & Angelis, insequi se feliciter posse, atque eam jugulare credit. Sed po- namus de Angelo creato hic sermonem esse, & qui- dem de aliquo e Spiritibus ministrantibus, nil aliud inferri posset, quàm quod Angeli in cælis orent pro sanctis: quam generalem intercessionem uti non nega- mus, ita ex ea nullatenus concludi potest invocatio Angelorum, quia neque specialem necessitatem nostram sciunt Esa. 3. neque si scirent, invocandi ideo religiose essent, siquidem hic cultus soli DEO conveniat, Matth. 4. Sed quum in Ebræo fonte non habeatur Angelus loquens pro eo, sed עָלָיו su- per vel apud eum, ad annunciandam scil. homini recti- tudinem suam, ideo non de Angelo orante apud Deum pro homine, sed de ministro aliquo vel Legato Dei, vo- luntatem Dei apud hominem interpretante, id expli- cant nonnulli: Si habuerit homo ministrum aliquem verbi divinæ voluntatis interpretem, qui scil. ipsum a peccatis retrahat, & in viam reducat, miserebitur ejus Deus, quam explicationem adducit Jesuita Pineda, nec rejicit. Verumenimvero verba singu- la recte pensitata convincunt, non de alio Ange- lo, quam increato Filio Dei sermonem esse. No- minatur מַלְאָך Angelus vel missus, quod nomen Fi- lio Dei convenire nemo ambigere potest: qui a Pa- tre mittitur, ut voluntatem Patris annunciet, & exe- quatur apud homines. Unde dicitur Angelus vel nuncius fœderis, quia annunciat, & cum hominibus pangit fœdus gratiæ Matth. 3, 1. Zach. 3. Angelus Domini dicitur, qui Jehovah Dominus vocatur v. 2. & passim alibi in apparitionibus Vet. Testam. ma- xime illis, quæ Patriarchis, Abrahamo, Jacobo, Mosique factæ sunt, angeli nomine & schemate in- troducitur, ut illo tempore, quo gesta est historia Jobi, nomen hoc Filium Dei designare, pervulga- tum fuerit: quem ita invocavit etiam Jacobus super nepotes suos Gen. 48, 16. Angelus, qui redemit me ab omni malo, benedicat pueris istis. Indigitatur An- gelus, qui est apud ipsum, h. e. apud Deum, vel coram Deo; Illud enim עָלָיו rectius videtur ad Deum re- ferri, quam ad hominem; quia de homine deinde agitur, si fuerit apud ipsum Angelus advocatus, unus ex mille, ad indicandum homini rectitudinem ejus. Si homo designaretur, dicendum esset: si fuerit apud hominem Angelus ad indicandum ipsi rectitudinem. Particulam autem עַל idem esse quod apud, vel coram, ex aliis locis manifestum est Gen. 24, 30. Jud. 3, 19. Zach. 4, 14. Angelus ille qui apud Deum, vel coram Deo peculiariter esse dicitur, quis alius est, quam Filius Dei, angelus faciei ejus, simili ratione, dictus Esa. 63, 10. Quæ phrasis de Filio Dei hic in- fert tum intimam περιχώρησιν Filii & Patris, salva personarum distinctione, ob quam πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν esse dicitur Joh. 1, 1. tum apparitionem Filii Dei apud Patrem, quæ mediationis causa fit. Vocatur Angelus מֵלִיץ, quæ vox, fatente Grotio, advocatum μεσίτην significat, atque ita a Maimonide Ebræorum doctis- simo accipitur. Quis vero Angelus advocatus dici- tur in Scripturis, nisi unus Dei Filius, qui solus & unus est mediator Dei & hominum 1. Tim. 2, 5. & unus advocatus hominum apud Deum 1. Joh. 2, 2. quos præ- ter ipsum Mediatores & Advocatores faciunt Papi- stæ, sive Angelos, sive sanctos defunctos, ignorat Scri- ptura: nuspiam enim illis hoc officium assignat; imo reprobat: quia dum unum mediatorem & advoca- tum Christum constituit, alios palam excludit. In pa- raphrasi Chaldaica hoc nomen redditur פַּרַקְלִיטָא παράκλητος, quod ibi opponitur κατηγόροις קַטֵיגוֹרַיָא accusatoribus. At nomen hoc παρακλήτου ta Angelo fœderis proprium est, ut nulli unquam alii angelorū tribuatur 1. Joh. 2, 2. imo uti negat scriptura, unquam illi Angelorum dictum esse, sede a dextris meis Ebr. 1. ita dictum etiam illis non est, ut paracle- ti nostri sint, quia ideo sedet Filius Dei ad dextram Dei, ut interpellet pro nobis Rom. 8, 34. Exponunt quidem nonnulli vocem מליץ de interprete, ex Es. 43, 27. Sed hic מליץ consideratur non apud homi- nes, sed apud Deum; proinde non ut interpres, sed ut advocatus & mediator; Et refertur actus officii hujus mediatorii, nimirum intercessio vers. 24. qua- propter de Filio DEI hoc accipere oportet, qui so- lus apud DEUM perpetuus est suorum Advocatus, & absque cujus intercessione fieri non potest, ut quis gratiam consequatur. Quod hic etiam in- digitatur: Si sit apud Deum Advocatus pro homine, gratum ipsum habebit: Sic enim innuitur, aliter ho- minem misericordiam non consequi, quam si interve- niat hic advocatus apud Deum. Porro Angelus unus ex mille Advocatus dicitur, & indicatur legatos & nuncios quidem multos Dei esse; millies enim mille & decies centena millia ipsi serviunt. Dan. 7, 50. Sed unum tantum esse Angelum ac legatum, qui simul Advocatus noster apud Deum sit. Angeli nomen commune est certa ratione, nam & Filius Dei mis- sus est a Deo, sed advocati officium proprium ipsi est; UNUS ex mille, qui Angeli dicuntur, Angelus nem- pe fœderis ille, & magni consilii, est mediator & ad- vocatus noster apud Deum Patrem, quod est proprium & perpetuum & ἀκοινώνητον ejusdem munus. U- nus ergo sed præcipuus μοναδικῶς intelligitur. Perinde, uti unus mediator εἷς μεσίτης dicitur 1. Tim. 2, 5. Ille unus autem est inter mille, quia circa ipsum Angelorum myriades sunt, quorum ipse Princeps est, uti Jos. 5, 14. Filius Dei in viri specie visus exercitus Domini principem se dixit; Et Ps. 68, 8. canitur de ipso, currus Domini millies mille- ni, Dominus in eis in Sina in Sancto. Idem mediator & Angelus, qui εἰς διαταγὰς ἀγγέλων inter ordina- tas Angelorum acies legem tulerat Act. 7, 38. 55. Gal. 3, 19. Si Angelus creatus intelligeretur, cur uni præ aliis ex millibus hoc intercessionis munus adscrere- tur? Annon omnes Angeli affectu, & amore erga fideles æquales sunt, eorumque parilem curam ge- runt, aut num uni alicui hoc officium est proprium? annon myriades millium justum, qui affligitur, qui non peccat, defendunt? quærit hic R. Nachmanides.

Jam si ad specialem ἐξέτασιν officiorum & prædicatorum quæ hic de Angelo illo adferuntur, descendamus, quid luculentius, quam quod ea uni fœderis Angelo, non autem Angelis ministris τοῖς πνεύμασι λειτεργικοῖς conveniant; primum est illuminationis: ad indicandum homini rectitudinem ejus; sive Dei, voluntatem ejus cum in lege, tum Evangelio patefactam; sive hominis, quid nempe rectum sit, quid ab ipso requirat Dominus, quodve officium ejus sit, si quidem cum Deo in gratiam redire velit, Mich. 6, 8. Job. 1, 18. c. 6, 29. 1. Job. 3, 13. Hoc dicere atque indicare, non est munus Angeli- cum, non enim per Angelos nos informare ordina- rie Deus voluit: de eo autem hic sermo est, quod ordinarium est, non extraordinarium, quia ratio in- dicatur, qua gratiam consequi possit afflictus, in cruce ac calamitate sua. Neque de indicatione inefficaci aliqua hic agitur, sed quæ conjuncta sit cum vi & efficacia illuminationis, & conversionis, fidei- que donatione, ut auris nempe aperiatur homini v. 26. ut non sit amplius cæcus & surdus, sed vera fide ea suscipiat & amplectatur, quæ indicantur. Quod nul- lus Angelus præstat, nisi Angelus fœderis Mediator noster, qui solus revelat nobis Patrem Matth. 11, 27.

Job. 1, 18. Alterum est; gratiosæ intercessionis: Et gratia illum complectatur, ac dicat, redime ipsum, ne descendat in foveam, inveni lytrum: ubi quot verba; tot fere pondera rationum, pro Angelo fœderis, & adversus Angelos ministrantes. Non enim de An- gelo ministro dicitur, quod gratia complectatur affli- ctos fideles, sed de Angelo illo fœderis gratiosi, cu- jus gratia & misericordia sæpe sæpius in Scripturis decantatur. Agi videtur de gratia speciali, quæ consequitur indicationem rectitudinis & fidem, est- que gratia fidelium propria, qua nempe complecti- tur Filius Dei eos, qui credunt in ipsum. Non Angelo creato, sed uni filio Dei sermo ille intercessio- rius convenit, cum auctoritate ac δεινότητι conjun- ctus. Hic enim a Patre poscit, ut nos eripiat a fo- vea, vi meriti sui propter redemtionem, sanguine factam. Redime ipsum. Verbum פדה etsi de redemtione quæ per pretium fit, aliquando usurpatur Lev. 27, 27. Psal. 49, 8. tamen etiam de liberatione oc- currit, quæ sine pretio fit Deut. 9, 26. Neh. 1, 12. Hic ergo cum Deo Patri tribuatur liberatio, postremo significatu locum habet, de liberatione ab interfe- ctoribus & ab interitu, quam præstat ipse fidelibus gratia sua, quæ tamen redemtionem mediatoris præ- supponit, & ob eandem nobis obtingit. Non An- gelo ministro, sed uni Angelo fœderis convenit, quod hic habetur, inveni lytrum. Quod enim nonnulli de ministris verbi id ita interpretentur, quod ipsi in- veniant in Scriptura hoc λύτρον, & ex ea proponant, id improprium est, nec intercessionis hujus dignita- ti respondet. Nihil enim hic διακονικὸν audimus: cum ἐξουσία & autoritate dicuntur omnia. Ideo neque alii ad Deum hæc ita referentes, Deus misere- bitur ægroti, id est, annuncia illi liberationem, respexi enim λύτρον Filii, calculum merentur. Quum enim de liberatione agatur, non est, cur metonymi- ce hic liberationis declarationem solum intelligamus. Possunt verba proprie intelligi, atque ideo etiam de- bent, quia non est τῷ ῥητῷ Scripturæ discedendum, nisi cogat Scriptura ipsa. Advocato ergo hominis tri- buitur non tantum intercessio talis, quæ nunquam inefficax est, Job. 12, 42. sed etiam inventio λύτρου, quæ causa & fundamentum est exauditionis interces- sionis: quia non nuda illa est, sed ἱλαστικὴ virtute meriti & propitiationis ab ipso mediatore inventæ facta. Quæ nulli nisi fœderis Angelo conveniunt, uni advocato nostro, qui virtute ἱλασμοῦ, quem præstitit pro toto mundo, pro nobis interpellat Rom. 8, 33. 34. 1. Joh. 2, 2. Annotanda est sedulo distinctio vocum in hac intercessionis exquisitissima formula: Libe- rare enim nos, ne in foveam descendamus, dicitur Deus Pater: At propitiationem & λύτρον invenire ac præstare est Filii Dei Angeli Mediatoris. כפר etsi tectorium notet Gen. 6, 13. per Metaphoram tamen, sed usu frequentiori, adeo ut, quod recte observat hic Coccejus, metaphorica notio in propriam quo- dammodo vertat, pretium notat, quo quis propitietur, pœna redimatur, ira placetur, gratia reconcilietur. Uti tectorio vetus rei facies mutatur in aliam, ita placamento reus in justum mutatur, culpa velut obliterata. Vid. Esa. 1, 18. Quod ergo intervenit ad culpam obliterandam, id כפר dicitur, & quicquid omnino datur pro altero, ut is noxæ eximatur, cujus pretii solutio satisfactio dicitur. Quum ergo solus DEI Filius pro nobis λύτρον dependerit, & ἀντίλυ- τρον Matth. 20, 28. Marc. 10, 45. 1. Timoth. 2, 5. ipse solus dicere potest, inveni כפר vel λύτρον. In- ventio hæc cum consilium respicit æternæ & hypo- staticæ Sapientiæ in S. S. Trinitatis senatu sanctissi- mo, tum executionem ejusdem, quia invenit id non in alio, sed in se uno; invenit lytrum, dum ipse id, quod consuluit, præstitit. Qui enim dedit consilium, tulit quoque auxilium. Eadem phrasi dicitur Mediator itidem Ebr. 9. v. 12. αἰώνιον λύτρωσιν εὑρόμενος, invenisse æternam redemtionem : Æterna dicitur λύτρωσις & quia λύτρωσις τὸ λύτρον includit, idcir- co æternum etiam certo respectu est ipsum redem- ptionis pretium, cujus vis ab æterno in æternum se ex- tendit, quia ab æterno Deus illud intuitus est Ephes. 1, 4. Apoc. 13, 8. & in æternum, ejusdem intuitu & vigore, nos liberavit, ac salvaturus est. Invenire idem nonnunquam est, quod habere, quia quod in- venimus, id habemus. Vid. Psal. 12, 9. Ita hic inve- ni lytrum, id est, habeo pretium ἰσόῤῥοπον, quod acce- pies pro reatu, ut a fovea liberetur : quia per hanc ἀπολύτρωσιν, & sanguinis Christi λύτρον è fo- vea illa dimittimur, in qua non est aqua Zach. 9, 11. Quibusdam videtur etiam hac voce, INVENI ly- trum, respici, qua per fidem apprehenditur, quia Me- diator noster invenit apud constrictum peccato- rem lytrum, sc. ab eo apprehensum per fidem, ideo- que a Deo postulat, ut intuitu fidei, quam invenit, eundem liberare velit ab interitu. Quæ neutiquam Angelis ministrantibus conveniunt: illi nec λύτρον redemtionis humanæ, nec fidem in cordibus cre- dentium inveniunt.

Adde his effectum intercessionis cum corpora- lem, tum Spiritualem. Ille ita exprimitur; succo ple- na erit caro ejus, prapueritia, revertitur ad dies ado- lescentiæ suæ. Hic istis verbis proponitur, depreca- bitur Deum, & placabilis erit ei, & videbit faciem ejus cum jubilo, & reddet Deus homini justitiam suam. Ob intercessionem enim Mediatoris nostri & bona corporalia & spiritualia consequimur gra- tiam Dei vel visionem faciei Dei, & justitiam Dei:

quod det Deus justitiam suam. Dei enim justitia no- bis donatur Es. 45, 25. Rom. 3, 25. Quibus subjungi- tur hominis in gratiam recepti confessio. Restitutus & in gratiam receptus incedit ad homines, vel respi- ciet homines, cœtum eorum iterum adibit, & alio- rum etiam conversionem exoptans, suo exemplo illos informabit, ideoque palam dicet, ac confite- bitur: Peccavi, & quod rectum fuit, perverti, &

non profuit mihi. Redemit (autem Deus) animam meam, ne transiret in interitum, & vita mea lucem respicit: uti secundum consonantes legitur in E- bræo: quo pacto indicatur certitudo de gratia, quæ in fidelibus est: Vel si secundum vocales legatur: Redemit animam ejus Deus, & vita ejus lucem re- spicit: ut hisce concludat Elihu, ita fieri, quod Me- diator intercedendo his verbis, redime ipsum, ne in foveam descendat, postulavit: Effectus enim ita respondet intercessioni: Redemit animam ipsius, ne transeat in interitum, vel foveam interitus. Se- quitur nunc conclusio hujus orationis, ac consilii hujus vere Evangelici ac saluberrimi; qua simul or- dinarius Dei processus, atq; intentio ejusdem aperitur cum afflictionis fidelium, tum erectionis per verbum Evangelii: Ecce hæc omnia agit Deus bis terve cum homine, ad reducendum animam ejus à fovea, quo illuminetur luce vitæ. Hæc ipsa, inquit, quibus vide- ri posset id agere Deus, ut quis in foveam precipitan- dus omnino sit, ac luce vitæ privandus, eo fine agit, ut revera a fovea liberetur & luce vitæ illuminetur. Fi- nis enim crucis & afflictionis piorum est, non exi- tium, sed salus ipsorum, unde beneficia, quæ per crucem nobis obtingunt, cum privativa sunt, libe- ratio animæ ab interitu, tum positiva, illuminatio ejus- dem, lucisque vitæ æternæ fruitio. Hæc omnia agit Deus non tantum crucem immittendo, sed ob An- geli Mediatoris intercessionem, & λύτρον iterum libe- rando, justitiam, pacem, & gaudium in Spiritu San- cto donando, ut non semel, sed iterum atque ite- rum, siquidem ita Salus æterna, hominis postu- let, hoc processu utatur, donec tandem fides ejus, instar auri in igne probati, explorata τιμιώτερῷ in- veniatur, & exemplo etiam fidelium ita excitato- rum alii ad fidem convertantur. Hunc esse proces- sum Dei ordinarium, viamque qua fideles ad salutem perducuntur, Elihu docet, ac Scriptura passim testa- tur 1. Pet. 1, 7. Ebr. 12, 5. seqq. Jac. 1, 3. Rom. 5, 3. cap. 8, 28. 29. Actor. 14, 22. 2. Tim. 3, 12. Dum tentatum hominem demonstrat unum, inquit Gregor. M. lib. 24. Moral. cap. 1. in qua tentatione sit positum huma- num genus ostendit universum: dumque narrat, quid specialiter agatur in singulis, liquido intimat, quid ge- neraliter agatur in cunctis : unde & mox huic gene- rali pestilentia generale sic intulit remedium medici- ne, dicens: Quod Christus magni consilii Angelus si- milis nobis loquutus est, quoad æquitatem: homo pro hominibus interpellans, & impetravit indulgentiam, exauditus pro sua reverentia.

Colligamus jam in summam argumenta no- stræ interpretationis: Angelus ille, qui (1) μοναδι- xῶς dicitur Angelus, & dictus est isto Jobi imprimis tempore, quod mitteretur à Deo ad Patriarchas ali- osque fideles liberandos; (2) qui apud Deum est quo- ad intimam cum Deo περιχώρησιν & ὁμοοσίαν, an- gelus faciei Domini; (3) apud Deum Patrem sit, & in- terveniat, necessum est, si quis liberari debeat, (4) Angelus, qui מליץ παρακλητος mediator & Advo- catus noster est apud Deum, & cujus hoc officium est proprium & perpetuum. (5) qui unus e mille, h. e. inter innumeros Dei legatos, qui à Deo salutis homi- num causa mittuntur, aliis Angelis uti longe emi- nentior est, ita peculiariter præ omnibus, qui hoc nomine appellantur, à Deo mittitur ob æternam no- stram salutem. (6) Qui UNUS ET SOLUS hoc munere fungitur, eoque nomine ac honore gaudet, quod mediator sit Dei & hominum, & ut mediator & advocatus noster causam nostram agat. (7.) Cujus Angeli proprium hoc est, ut indicet homini rectitu- dinem Dei vel etiam officii nostri omni tempore, inde à conditu orbis vel lapsu hominis, postquam is ex- cidit Sapientia primigenia, & rectitudine sua con- creata. (8) Nec tantum indicet ei; tanquam Pro- pheta, & qui munere Prophetico fungitur, sed etiam interna illuminatione & conversione eandem in ho- mine operetur, divina efficacia. (9) Angelus ille, qui gratia & misericordia sua complectitur fideles. (10) Et ex gratia ac commiseratione intima pro uno- quoque fidelium maxime, cum in angustiis consti- tuti, & constricti sunt, intercedit. (11) Et quidem intercessione non communi aut vulgari, sed ἐξαιρέ- τως propria, & autoritativa, cum ἐξοσίᾳ divina con- juncta: non inefficaci, & vana, sed efficaci, & ea, quæ semper exaudiatur. (12) Non mere ἐνκλικῇ, sed ἱλασικῇ quæ nitatur merito pretii, & expiatio- nis hujus ipsius Angeli παρακλητε. (13) Quæq; etiam à pretio & propitiatione ista omnem vim suam ha- beat. Qua una præstatur ut reducamur à Deo, ne in foveam descendamus. (14) Angelus, qui כפר propi- tiationem, λυτρον & απολύτρωσιν æternam invenit, adeoque Angelus גאל Redemptor noster, (15) qui hac sua propitiatione nos è fovea liberavit, ac præstat, ne in foveam descendamus. (16.) Qui invenit in affli- ctis & constrictis lytrum, illud fide apprehensum, fi- demque ipsorum respicit, atque æstimat, ac Deo Patri sistit ac proponit, ut actu ipso liberentur. (17) Angelus ille, cujus expiationi & intercessio- ni accepto ferendum est, quod sanitati corporali re- stituamur. (18) Quodque Deo supplicantes pro salute imprimis animæ, vi ejusdem intercessionis, grati habeamur, & gratiam ejus consequamur; adeoque etiam faciem Dei cum jubilo videamus. (19) Tum quod reddat Deus homini constricto justitiam suam, eum non tantum a peccato ab- solvat, sed æterna justitia instruat, ac ditet. (20)

Cujus gratia, expiatio, & fructus expiationis, bene- ficia nempe corporalia & spiritualia, quæcunque fi- delibus obtingunt, ab hominibus restitutis, & in gratiam receptis prædicanda in Ecclesia maxime sunt, & propaganda: utpote quæ proprium præconii Evangelici objectum sunt: & verum constrictoruni adversus ægritudinem animi & corporis antido- tum. (21) Quæ ita etiam prædicanda, ut humili peccati confessione Dei, qui redimit animam no- stram, ne in foveam transeat, & vitam ac lucem æ- ternam aspiciat, misericordiam nostro exemplo alii celebrent, & ad Deum liberatorem per Angelum Me- diatorem perducantur, illuminentur, convertantur, ac qui peccarunt, rectumque curvarunt, justitiam & rectitudinem veram agnoscant pariter & consequan- tur. (22) Denique quum hic ordinarius Dei pro- cessus, & media ordinaria conversionis & salutis, non extraordinaria proponantur, quomodo Deus cum homine agat ad animam ejus a fovea reducen- dam, & ut vitæ luce illuminetur, de eo Angelo sermo hic est, cujus intercessione & propitiatione omnes indigent, ut a fovea liberentur, & luce vitæ illumi- nentur; Cujus gratia omnibus ad salutem annun- cianda, & prædicanda in Ecclesia, ut propitiatione & intercessione ejusdem se sustentent, inque eadem gratiam, justitiam, & gaudium quærant, & libera- tione ac vitæ luce fruantur, virtute hujus λύτρε, & intercessionis Angeli istius Mediatoris. Quæ omnia non de Angelo aliquo creato, aut ministro, sed de Angelo increato, Filio Dei, de Angelo fœderis gra- tiæ unice subsumi possunt, ut hinc invicta emergat conclusio, non de alio, quam de Filio Dei Angelo fœderis gratiæ sermonem hic esse.

Nec sane abs re tam magnifico ingressu oratio- nis suæ hic utitur Elihu, quum summum salutis my- sterium proponat: siquidem à Jobo & attentio- nem magno verborum apparatu postulet, & respon- sionem. Attentionem quidem non solum blanda pe- titione, sed profecto audi quæso Job elogia mea, & omnes sermones meos ausculta: Sed etiam promissio- ne tum libertatis, Ecce quæso aperui os meum, loqui- tur lingua mea in palato meo, siquidem μετὰ παῤῥη- σίας de rebus magnis loquatur: quod phrasis illa os aperire innuit Psal. 78, 2. Prov. 24, 7. Matth. 5, 2.

tum sinceritatis; rectitudo cordis mei dicta mea, & scientiam labia mea pure loquentur: nec non originis suæ commemoratione: quam toti S. S. Trinitati ac- ceptum refert.

Spiritus Dei fecit me, & spiracu- lum omnipotentis (Filii Dei) vivificavit me: ita consilium S. S. Trinitatis, quoad hominem, admi- randum opificium suum, cum cruce eundem affli- git, propositurus, & honorem & gloriam creatoris sui, qui fecit & vivificavit nos, non tam ad hanc, quam ad alteram vitam, adserturus, attentio- nem debitam requirit: Et quum ad respon- sionem invitet, pollicetur, sese benigna & gra- ta ipsi annunciaturum: Ecce terror meus non te terrebit aut percellet v. 7. Totam συνέχειαν & quam apte omnia cohæreant, vide hic in eru- ditissima analysi B. Sculteti nostri, ac interpre- tationi nostræ omnia consonare facile agno- sces. Cui denique pondus aliquod addit aucto- ritas interpretum eximiorum, qui nobiscum de Mediatore Christo locum præsentem explicant. Gregorius M. lib. 24. Moral. cap. 1. Quis, in- quit, est iste Angelus, nisi ille, qui per Prophetam dicitur magni consilii Angelus? Et bene ait: Sifue- rit pro eo Angelus loquens: quia, sicut ait Aposto- lus, etiam interpellat pro nobis. Sic etiam explicat Glossa ordinaria, Berno Augiensis, & Hugo Cardi- nalis in h. l. nec non e recentioribus Johannes Coc- cejus, Christophorus Scultetus in h. l. Non quidem negamus, inquit Coccejus, quædam istorum suo mo- do etiam de hominibus dici posse, ut nomen Angelus, interpres, item indicare rectitudinem, misereri, o- rare liberationem, invenire suo modo lytron, sive attestari fidei ægrotantis, per quam is habet lytron: Sed ut tenuiter illa explicemus, quomodo & homini- bus competunt, & imprimis per tropos coactos, nulla causa est; quum liceat simplici & plano sensu Spiri- tus Sancti stylum sequi. Prædicata ostendunt, qualia sint subjecta. Saltem sensum tenuiorem, retinere mor- dicus, & sensum pleniorem, quem Scriptura insinuat, rejicere, quamvis ille magis faciat ad rem, non est, nisi illorum, qui amant μειώσεις, & extenuationes in interpretatione verbi divini. B. Scultetus, Christus, inquit, dicitur Angelus Malach. 3, 1. est unus & præ- cipuus inter millia Angelorum, est interpres, verbum Patris, & παράκλητος, advocatus (ut Chaldæus hic vertit) est apud Deum Coloss. 1, 18. & Angelus faciei ejus, Exod. 23, 20. עליו enim vix ad hominem potest referri, cum in sequente membro vox אור insolenter repeteretur, illi optime quæ sequuntur prædicata con- veniunt. Et postea; Sed optime, plene & proprie hæc explicari possunt, si priora de Filio Dei exponas: Miterebitur ejus, gratia sua illum complectetur ויחננו & pro eo intercedendo apud Patrem dicet; li- bera eum, ne moriatur, ne in æternum pereat. Ego inveni, & acquisivi propitiationem seu redemtio- nem, apud me est λύτρον & redemtio pro peccatis ejus. Hæc de sensu hujus loci.

Quod addit Grotius de Angelorum officio me- diatorio, quod duobus nempe modis μεσῖται sint, & monendo homines, & pro eis orando, quodque hic ascensus & descensus sit in Scala Jacobi, id Platonicis & Rabbinicis commentis debet. Etsi quandoq; extra- ordinarie moneant homines, ac in genere pro hominibus rare eos concedi possit, non tamen ideo Mediatores nostri in Scripturis dicuntur: neq; id ascensus & de- scensus in scala Jacobi designat: Sed in genere προ- θυμίαν Angelorum ad inserviendum hominibus si- gnificat: quorum causa descendere & vicissim ascendere dicuntur, quemadmodum descenderunt, cum Christi nativitatem hymno celebrarent in ter- ris, ac postmodum vicissim in cœlum adscendisse di- cuntur Luc. 2. 15. Descendere etiam intelligendi sunt, cum ministrant in terris Ebr. 1, 13. afcendere, cum animas transferunt in cœlos Luc. 16, 23.

Vers. eod.

## 33:24
HE WILL HAVE MERCY ON HIM) You would translate better: let him supplicate him, namely God; the following words confirm this.

Because of a rashly preconceived opinion, the Vulgate version is corrected, for the Hebrew ויחננו is 'he will have mercy on him,' and it must be understood of the paraclete Angel, having mercy on the sick man: it does not indeed have reference to God, as if the Angel were supplicating Him: for thus it would have had to be expressed in the Hithpael, since it signifies 'he supplicated for grace' or 'to obtain mercy' only in the fourth conjugation. Whence all the interpreters here render it: 'He will have mercy on him': which the LXX and most Latins understand of God; some, however, explain it of the Angel, having mercy on the sick man and praying for him; which the following words, presenting the formula of supplication, also confirm; 'And he will say, deliver him' etc.

Ver. 24.

I HAVE FOUND, IN WHICH I MAY BE PROPITIATED TO HIM) In the Hebrew: I have found a ransom: that is, I have found repentance in him. Ἐξιλασμὸς ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ ἀδικίας Eccles. 35, 5.

The Vulgate version is rightly corrected from the Hebrew source: But the price of redemption is very poorly explained with the Papists as repentance: For although ἀποστῆναι ἀπ' ἀδικίας (to depart from iniquity) may be a sign and a consequence, and propitiation may thus be described a posteriori, yet properly כפר (kopher), a ransom or price of redemption, cannot be indicated by repentance: But the only λύτρον (ransom) handed down in the Scriptures is the precious blood of Christ 1 Cor. 6, 21. 1 Pet. 1, 18. nor does anyone find another λύτρον & ἀπολύτρωσιν (ransom and redemption) than Christ Jesus Heb. 9, 12. Angels certainly did not find the price of redemption: otherwise they themselves would have to be considered our redeemers: But there is one Mediator of God and men, who gave himself an ἀντίλυτρον (ransom) for us. Add that an Angel cannot even find repentance in a believer, because he cannot explore hearts. For this is the property of God alone. Angels gather repentance only through signs and a posteriori: they cannot perceive faith, which is in true repentance, lying hidden in the heart. And God has no need that an Angel should testify to Him that he has found repentance in a man: since God, who searches the hearts and reins, Himself beholds and knows the repentance and faith of men, so that an Angel does not need to say to Him: deliver him, for I have found repentance in him. I add the interpretation of Gregory the Great, whose authority, as that of a Roman Bishop, ought deservedly to be great among the Papists. He explains it thus: He has found, in whom I may be propitious to him. As if the mediator of God and men were openly said: Because there was no man who appeared as a just intercessor before God for men, I made myself a man to be propitious to men.

Latin:

MISEREBITVR EJVS) Melius vertes: supplicet ei, nempe Deo, firmant hoc sequentia.

Temere præconceptæ opinionis causa, cor- rigitur versio vulgata, Ebræum enim ויחננו est mi- serebitur ejus, & de paracleto Angelo, miserente æ- groti accipiendum: non vero respectum habet ad Deum, quasi Angelus ei supplicet: Ita enim in Hithpael efferendum fuisset, siquidem non nisi in quarta conjugatione significet supplicavit pro gra- tia, seu misericordia impetranda. Unde omnes In- terpp. hic reddunt: Miserebitur ejus: quod LXX. & plerique Latini de Deo intelligunt; nonnulli ta- men de Angelo, ægroti miserente, ac pro eodem depre- cante explicant; quod etiam verba sequentia, for- mulam supplicationis exhibentia confirmant; Et dicet, libera eum &c.

Vers. 24.

INVENI, IN QVO EI PROPITIER) In Hebræo: Inveni redemtionis pretium: id est, inveni in eo pœnitentiam. Ἐξιλασμὸς ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ ἀδικίας Eccles. 35, 5.

Recte corrigitur vulgata versio e fonte Hebræo: Sed pretium redemptionis pessime cum Papistis de pœ- nitentia explicatur: Quanquam enim signum & consequens sit ἀποστῆναι ἀπ' ἀδικίας & propitiatio ita a posteriori describatur, proprie tamen כפר λύτρον vel pretium redemptionis pœnitentia indigitari non potest: Sed λύτρον unicum in Scripturis traditur pretiosus Christi sanguis 1. Cor. 6, 21. 1. Petr. 1, 18. nec quisquam aliis invenit λύτρον & ἀπολύτρωσιν, quam Christus Jesus Ebr. 9, 12. Angeli certe non in- venere redemptionis pretium: alias ipsi nostri re- demptores habendi essent: Sed unus Mediator Dei & hominum, qui dedit semetipsum ἀντίλυτρον pro no- bis. Adde quod ne pœnitentiam quidem Angelus in fideli inveniat, quia corda explorare non potest. Solius enim Dei hoc est proprium. Angeli non nisi per signa & a posteriori pœnitentiam colligunt: fidem, quæ in vera est pœnitentia, in corde latentem perspicere non possunt. Et non opus habet Deus, ut testetur ipsi Angelus, quod invenerit in homine pœnitentiam: siquidem Deus, qui corda & renes scrutatur, pœnitentiam fidemque hominum ipse in- tueatur ac cognoscat, ut Angelus necessum non ha- beat ipsi dicere: libera eum, inveni enim pœniten- tiam in eo. Addo interpretationem Gregorii M. cujus auctoritas, ceu Romani Episcopi, magna merito esse debet Papistis. Ita autem explicat: In- venit, in quo propitier ei. Ac si aperte mediator Dei & hominum dicatur: Quia nullus hominum fuit, qui coram Deo intercessor justus pro hominibus ap- pareret, memetipsum ad propitiandum hominibus hominem feci.

## 33:26
Vers. 26.

HE SHALL SEE HIS FACE IN JOY) God will look upon him kindly. AND HE WILL RENDER TO MAN HIS RIGHTEOUSNESS) He will hold him as amended in that place, as if he had never sinned. The same right for the healed as for the strong.

Latin:

Vers. 26.

VIDEBIT FACIEM EJVS IN JVBILO) Deus ipsum benigne respiciet. ET REDDET HOMINI JVSTITIAM SVAM) Emen- datum eum eo loco habebit, quasi nunquam peccasset. Idem jus sanati quod forti.

## 33:29
Vers. 29.

BEHOLD, ALL THESE THINGS GOD WORKS THREE TIMES WITH EVERYONE) The Kabbalists refer these to their Pythagorean metempsychosis. But Maimonides much more correctly says that God tests several times whether a man's disposition is curable. But if, having been warned often, he relapses into grave sins, then He ceases His care for him, and considers him as desperate, which is the judgment of obduration, following upon the goodness of God having been often despised.

Latin:

Vers. 29.

ECCE, HÆC OMNIA OPERATVR DEVS TRI- BVS VICIBVS PER SINGVLOS) Hæc Cabbalistæ ad Py- thagoricam suam μετενσωμάτωσιν referunt. At Maimonides multo rectius ait Deum aliquoties experiri an sanabile sit ho- minis ingenium. Quod si sæpe monitus in gravia peccata recidat, tunc omittere ejus curam, & habere eum pro deplo- rato, quod est judicium obdurationis, bonitatem Dei sæpe contemtam subsequens.

## 34:1 Argument
CHAPTER XXXIV.

Elihu reproves Job, as if he had accused God of injustice, asserts His justice, and wishes a greater punishment for Job.

Latin:

CAPUT XXXIV.

Elihu Jobum redarguit, quasi Deum injustitiæ postularit, ejus justitiam adserit, Joboque majorem pœnam optat.

Vers. 5.

FOR JOB HAS SAID: I AM JUST) Above 27, at the beginning.

Vers. 5.

QVIA DIXIT JOB: JVSTVS SVM) Supra 27. initio.

## 34:6
Vers. 6.

FOR IN JUDGING ME, IT IS A LIE) In the Hebrew: I will make him lie in my judgment: that is, I will convict him of a lie. Thus the same word is used above 24, 25. Nor did the Chaldean understand it otherwise here.

The text does not support this sense. For the words of Job are recited: CONCERNING MY JUDGMENT I LIE. In my judgment, although I defend a just cause against my friends, I am accused of lying.

Verse of the same.

MY ARROW IS VIOLENT WITHOUT ANY SIN) In the Hebrew: My painful arrow, but without injustice. I shall speak words that are by no means flattering to him, yet without hatred or iniquity.

Job complains about a punishment that is too aggravated, MY ARROW IS INCURABLE, WITHOUT DEFECTION. The arrow, which was sent by God, has pierced me and brought such affliction that there is no room for a remedy: even though there was no defection or prevarication on my part, such that I should have deserved it more than others. Grotius's gloss is foreign.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

IN JVDICANDO ENIM ME, MENDACIVM EST) In Hebræo: Iudicio meo mentiri faciam eum: id est, mendacii convincam. Sic idem verbum usurpatum supra 24, 25. Nec aliter hic accepit Chaldæus.

SEnsum hunc non fert textus. Recitantur enim verba Jobi SUPER JUDICIO MEO MEN- TIAR. In judicio meo, licet causam justam con- tra amicos defendam, mendacii arguor.

Vers. eod.

VIOLENTA SAGITTA MEA ABSQVE VLLO PEC- CATO) In Hebræo: Sagitta mea dolorifera, sed citra inju- riam. Dicam verba minime ipsi blandientia, sine odio ta- men aut iniquitate.

Queritur Job de pœna nimium aggravata, INSANABILIS EST SAGITTA MEA, SI- NE DEFECTIONE. Sagitta, quæ a Deo im- missa, me trajecit, tantam attulit afflictionem, ut nullus sit remedio locus: etsi ea non fuerit defectio aut prævaricatio mea, ut præ aliis commeruerim. Grotii glossa aliena est.

## 34:7
Verse 7.

WHO IS THE MAN LIKE JOB, WHO DRINKS SCORN LIKE WATER) Here שתה, which generally signifies to drink, seems to be used for to make drink. Who has ever offered up mockeries to be drunk by God as Job has?

Why is the customary meaning of drinking not left as it is? Because to drink scorn like water is to mock greedily, easily, copiously, and with pleasure. Chap. 17, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

QVIS EST VIR VT JOB, QVI BIBIT SVBSAN- NATIONEM QVASI AQVAM) Videtur hic שתה, quod bibere plerumque significat, positum pro facere bibere, Quis unquam ita Deo potanda præbuit ludibria, ut Iob.

Cur non relinquitur usitata bibendi significa- tio? Quia bibere ut aquam subsannationem est cu- pide, facile, copiose & cum voluptate subsannare. cap. 17, 6.

IF HE HAD DIRECTED HIS HEART TOWARD HIM) If he were to set his heart toward himself: that is, if God wished to be good only to himself: the Greeks here say ἐἰ γὰρ βούλοιτο συνέχειν.

More correctly: If (God) WERE TO SET HIS HEART UPON HIM, that is, if he wished to deal rigidly with man, or at least to observe and judge all his actions.

## 34:17
Verse 17.

SHALL HE WHO DOES NOT LOVE JUDGMENT BE HEALED?) حبس that is, חבש among the Arabs means both to bind and to put into prison. Are not those who resist judgment accustomed to be bound and put into prison? He wishes Job to be such a one.

Because that word is used concerning the binding of wounds, this sense pleases some: Would God even heal him who hates judgment? There is no reason, however, why I should disapprove of Grotius's explanation.

Verse of the same.

AND HOW DO YOU CONDEMN HIM WHO IS JUST, TO SUCH AN EXTENT?) In the Hebrew: and how do you condemn a powerful just man? If you were to oppose some mortal judge, you would be put into prison. And how do you dare to condemn the acts of Him who is both most just and most powerful, so that He fears neither kings nor princes.

Latin:

Vers. 17.

NVMQVID QVI NON AMAT JVDICIVM SA- NARI POTEST?) حبس id est, חבש apud Arabas est & vincire, & in carcerem dare. Nonne ii, qui judicio resi- stunt vinciri & in carcerem dari solent? Talem vult esse Jobum.

Quia verbum illud de obligatione vulnerum ad- hibetur, sensus hic nonnullis placet: An Deus etiam sanaret eum, qui judicium odit? Non tamen est, quod improbem Grotii explicationem.
