Quod enim illi in Pilato & He- rode impletum dicunt, id impie irridet Empæcta, Pilatum Regem non fuisse, Herodem non fremuisse adversus eum, sed HOMINEM (tam contemtim Christum appellat homo prophanus) CONTEM- SISSE, neutrum solio eum deturbare voluisse; Pila- tum liberare eum paratum fuisse, Herodem illæsum cum in potestate sua haberet, dimisisse: Solos Judæos hostes ejus fuisse, eorum autem consilia adversus eum non fuisse irrita, sed optatum finem consecuta, Jesum nec Judæis nec gentibus imperitasse, nec vincula inje- cisse. Quid est obloqui Spiritui Sancto, si hoc non sit? Ita enim Apostolus Actor. 4, 24. seqq. Domi- ne tu es, qui fecisti cælum & terram, mare & omnia, quæ in eis sunt, qui Spiritu Sancto per os Patris nostri David servi tui dixisti: Quare fremuerunt gentes, & populi meditati sunt inania? Astiterunt Reges Terræ, & Principes convenerunt in unum adversus Dominum & adversus Christum ejus! Convenerunt enim vere in civitate ista adversus Sanctum puerum tuum Jesum, quem unxisti, Herodes, & Pontius Pi- latus cum gentibus & populis Israel, facere quæ ma- nus tua & consilium tuum decreverunt fieri. Quid ergo certius, quam Apostolos hæc, quæ de Re- gum fremitu & tumultu prædixit Spiritus S. expli- care de molitionibus adversus Christum, ab Herode, Pilato, aliisque susceptis? quorum consilia finem opta- tum fortita esse impie asseritut, quum ea plane irri- ta fore prædixerit, atque hic etiam irrita esse testa- tus sit Spiritus Sanctus. Etsi enim ipsi autorem vi- tæ interfecere, suscitavit tamen eum Dominus, & Christum fecit hunc crucifixum JEsum Actor. 2, 36. cap. 3, 15. cujus vincula spiritualia leges sunt, ac ne- quicquam ab impiis dirumpi, abjicique tentantur.

Quartum, & postremum Enjedini argumentum est, quod verba & sententiæ Psalmi diversis personis & temporibus accommodentur, initium quidem A- postolis & persecutioni eorum post ascensionem Chri- sti, medium vero resurrectioni & ascensioni Christi Actor. 13. Ebr. 5. finis partim Christo jam regnanti, Apocal. 19, 15. partim piis in vita futura regnantibus. Resp. Initium explicatur de fremitu adversus Chri- stum, cum in terris ageret, ac tempore passionis ma- gnæ cumprimis, quod cum ex ipso loco Actor. 4, 24. tum è collatione cap. 2, 22. 23. cap. 3, 15. 17. cap. 4, 11. 12. manifestum est. Neque medium aut finis de alio, quam Christo explicatur, etsi ad communio- nem aliquam potestatis Christi fideles ejus admit- tantur, Apoc. 2, 26. Et quomodo ex ista de Christo interpretatione in Novo Testamento facta docebi- tur, de Christo intelligendum non esse præsentem Psalmum? Annon potius inde aperte constat, eun- dem omnino de Christo agere? Nuspiam enim de Davide in Novo Testamento explicatur: semper de Christo. Sed hæc de Enjedino.

Judæis modernis opponimus antiquiores. Nam & Apostoli tempore id penes Ebræos certum fuisse, quod iste Psalmus proprie & ex intentione Spiritus Sancti de Christo agat, vel inde manifestum est, quod ad illos scribens id velut ὁμολογούμενον affu- mat; & laudantur à Galatino lib. 3. de Cath. verit. arc. cap. 6. ac Helvico Elench. Judæor. 2. Class. 3. & aliis, R. Salomo, & R. Aben-Esra, ut & Bere- schith Rabba, in Genes. 49, 10. qui de Messia inter- pretantur. Quod etiam factum à R. Lusitano in Colloquio Mittelburgensi. In Bereschith Rabba sect. 43. adducitur R. Jonathan, dixit Deus tribus pete: Salomoni in Gibeon, Ahazo Esa. 7. & Messiæ hoc loco. Qualia etiam è Seder Olam in Jalkuth ad 1. Reg. 3, 5. Midrasch Tillim & R. Saadia ad Dan. 7, 13. adducta. In Talmud Massech. Suca cap. 5. & in Jalkuth ad Psalm. 2. docuerunt Magistri nostri di- xisse Deum sanctum benedictum Messiæ filio David, postula quodcunque velis, dabo tibi illud, quia scri- ptum est, narrabo statutum eis. R. Obad. in h. l. in hoc Psalmo mentionem facit dierum Christi ad con- vertendum genus humanum ad cultum Dei. Et ad verba, Subsannabit in ira: Christus percutiet ter- ram cum virga oris Esa. 11. Ad v. 12. Qui confidunt in eum, & expectant redemtionem, illis Lux oritur. R. Aben-Esra ad v. 11. Osculamini Filium, qui est Messias. Grotius ipse largitus nobis est annotatis ad Matth. 22, 41. consensum Judæorum, quod nem- pe ipse David Kimchi, & cum eo alii, ut & apud Justinum Trypho Psalmum 2. de Messia interpreten- tur. Neque inficiantur id Mahumetani, quod hæc ad Christum pertineant. Phil. Guadagnolus Auto- rem Lexici laudat sic dicentem: Exinde dictum Dei excelsi ad Jesum, cui sint orationes Dei & pax, & ego genui te, id est alui te.

Jam si textum ipsum Psalmi, adhibita collatio- ne locorum aliorum, & interpretatione Novi Te- stamenti consideremus, nullo modo de Davide eundem exponi posse, sed de Messia unice intelli- gendum esse, adversus Grotium facile demonstra- tur: primum è Filii denominatione. Dominus dixit ad me: Filius meus es tu. Quibus verbis de Filio Dei singulari μονοτρόπως ita dicto agitur; nam ex- ponitur hic aliquid peculiare ac proprium huic subjecto: & absolute Filius Dei dicitur, tum hic, tum vers. 11. osculamini Filium: ac à Deo ipso ita compellatur: Filius meus es tu: perinde uti de Chri- sto Deus Matth. 3. & 17. Hic est Filius ILLE meus, quasi revocavit Deus nos ad hoc Psalmi oraculum. Nomen etiam illud tantæ majestatis est, prout hic uncto illi Domini vindicatur, ut uni Christo con- venire, nec ulli unquam Angelorum ita dictum esse Apostolus testetur; & ex hoc loco Christum esse Filium DEI ὁμοούσιον ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης καὶ χαρακτῆρα τοῦ πατρὸς demonstret, Ebr. 1, 6. cui di- xit aliquando Angelorum, Filius meus es tu: Ego ho- die genui te? Si autem Davidi hoc primo & literali sensu dictum esset, fallerent hæc Apostoli, nullusque argumento ejus nervus inesset, nulla subesset axio- mati veritas.

Deinde è generatione æterna: Quia de illo hic sermo est Filio, qui non per creationem, adoptionem, aut constitutionem, sed per generatio- nem, quæ est communicatio ejusdem essentiæ, Fi- lius est: & quidem per æternam generationem, uti illud היום Orthodoxi Patres communiter explicant. Nam cum de generatione proprie dicta agatur Filii ex essentia Patris geniti, actum illum æternum esse oportet: per quem ὁμαιώνıῶ coæternus Filius genitus est. Et quum generatio illa æterno decreto de dandis finibus orbis in hæreditatem huic filio in fundamentum substernatur, necessum est, ut generatio illa etiam æterna sit. Ideo adhibetur hoc oraculum ad afferendam æternam Deitatem & ὁμοıσίαν Filii Dei, Ebr. 1, 6. & ut fundamentum æterni sacerdotii ejusdem Ebr. 5, 5. Tertio à Messiæ nuncupatione. Dicitur enim κατ’ ἀντονομασίαν Messias Domini: quod nomen absolute atque eminenti significatu Filio Dei unigenito competit. Christo Domino nostro multo magis, quam cæteris omnibus Christi, sive uncti Dei nomen convenire, indeque hoc nomen tanquam ejus proprium esse factum, Socinus ipse fatetur loc. cit. Ideo etiam Rabbini hic intelligunt unctum illum Domini, de quo Esa. 61, 1. De illo uncto sermo est, qui peculiari & indissolubili nexu Domino Jehovæ devinctus est, ita ut unum sit eorum jugum, vinculaque sint eadem. Quis autem ita devinctus est, nisi Christus Dominus noster? De illo Christo, adversus quem, qui fremunt, adversus Deum ipsum semper fremunt, Deique iram vehementissime provocant, adversus quem omnis generis populi & gentes insurgunt, adversus quem inane est omne consilium, quacunque prudentia & potentia ineatur. Esa. 8. De illo Christo agitur, qui constitutus est Rex à Deo super montem Sion sanctum ejus, in quantum is mons sanctus est: quod uni Domino nostro Christo proprium est, uncto illi, qui sanctus sanctorum, Dan. 9, 25. & Psalm. 110, 2. Es. 4, 2. cap. 9, 6. seqq. Jerem. 23, 6. Luc. 1, 32.

Quarto à Dominii hujus amplitudine. De illo agitur Domino, qui gentes universas hæreditatem consequitur, & possessionem terminos Terræ, adeoque orbem universum. Dicitur enim ei absolute: postula à me, & dabo tibi gentes in hæreditatem: Nulla sit restrictio. Quascunque gentes postulabit, habebit in hæreditatem. Ac ne dubitetur, æque late cum terminis terræ patere eandem, additur aperte, & possessionem tuam terminos terræ. Quæ nullatenus intelligi possunt de Davide: De Messia autem passim adferuntur, Genes. 49, 8. Zachar. 9, 10.

Quinto à regiminis descriptione. Reges eos virga ferrea, & tanquam vas figuli confringes eos. Quæ de rebellibus dicuntur. Non enim David ita omnes, qui ipsi adversati sunt, confringere valuit: multi prævaluere quandoque ipsi. De solo Christo hoc prædicatur ceu Domino Dominorum Apocal. 19. qui ita hanc potestatem sibi vendicat, ut in altera gloriosa vita nos, ut reges Spirituales ejus etiam quadam ratione participes redditurus sit Apoc. 2. unde iterum liquet, de Christo, non de Davide id intelligendum esse. Fideles subditos quod attinet, illis gratia & salus promittitur, ideo

Sextum argumentum petimus à Regum & judicum omnium compellatione. Monet enim Spiritus Sanctus omnes Magistratus cum summos tum medios, Reges atque judices terræ universos, ut huic Christo, ceu Domino Dominorum & Regi Regum sese subdant, ejusque vincula & jugum, quæ ipsius Dei vincula & jugum sunt, non disrumpere, aut abjicere moliantur (siquidem omne illud vetitum sit) sed eidem sese submittant, eidem osculo homagii, fidei, subjectionis, adorationis, sese dedant. Omnes enim indefinite monentur, sine discrimine locorum & temporum: uti Jehovæh omnes servi- re jubentur ubivis locorum, omni tempore, ita & omnes osculari Filium ejus jubentur. Æque late patet illa parænesis, imo eadem est prorsus exhortatio: servite Domino in timore, osculamini filium, quod vulgata reddit, apprehendite disci- plinam. Neque de Davide hæc dici possunt, quia David hic loquitur de alia persona, & jubet Re- ges osculari Filium, quem proinde abs Davide distinctam personam esse oportet. De illo Chri- sto & Rege agitur, quem cum osculantur Reges & judices terræ, Domino ipsi serviunt, & cujus veneratio est ejusdem plane conditionis cum ser- vitio, quod Domino Deo nostro præstatur. Un- de jam septimum nobis nascitur argumentum: A religiosa veneratione: quæ deferenda huic uncto. De eo enim Filio Dei agitur, qui parili cultu pro- sequendus est cum Jehovah DEO Patre, eique ἰσότιμῶ est, quod unice Christo convenit Joh. 5, 19. Servite Domino, inquit, in timore, & exul- tate ei cum tremore, osculamini Filium, ne quando irascatur Dominus. Osculum illud subjectionis ad spiritualem & salutarem Regum intelligentiam & eruditionem æque pertinet, uti servitus religiosa Domino præstanda, & parili cum eadem censu habetur. Ideo utrique hæc præmittitur paræne- sis: Et nunc Reges intelligite, erudimini, qui judica- tis terram.

Octavum est à divina comminatione. Hujus enim uncti cultus & obsequium, si negligatur, causa est omnis interitus, ipsorum etiam Regum, & ju- dicum, adeoque omnium, quicunque pereunt ab ira Domini. De eo ergo agitur, ob quem, qui osculari eundem vera fide renuunt, iræ Dei subji- ciuntur, & æterno interitui. At causa iræ Dei, & condemnationis vel interitus æterni est infidelitas, vel quod non credant in nomen Filii Dei unigeniti, Joh. 3, 18. 36. Super illum enim, qui incredulus est, manet ira Dei Ut enim hic beatitudo adscribitur illis, qui in Filio Dei confidunt: ita ex opposito interitus adjudicatur iis, qui non osculantur vera fi- de Filium DEI. Osculamini Filium, ne quando ira- scatur & pereatis in via.

Nono à fiduciæ honore. Is enim, in quo collocare fiduciam jubet Spiritus San- ctus, non potest esse ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος, quum male- dictum pronunciet Spiritus Sanctus, qui in nudum hominem fiduciam collocat, Jerem. 17, 5. Quapro- pter de Davide intelligi Psalmus non potest, secun- dum sensum primum & literalem, sed de Filio Dei unigenito accipiendus necessario atque unice est. Utpote in quem solum fiduciam collocare jube- mur.

Decimo à Beatitudinis & salutis promissione. Beati omnes, qui confidunt in eo. De illo ergo Dei Filio hic sermo est, in quo beatitudo & salus est per fidem in ipsum, & in quem fiduciam collocare oportet, quicunque salvari volunt, in quem crede- re, est beatum esse. At quis ille alius est, nisi unige- nitus ille Filius Dei, in quo solo nostra salus est per fidem in ipsum, quod Actor. 4, 12. cap. 10, 43. Joh. 3, 16. & alibi passim Scriptura luculentissime te- statur.

Undecimo à personæ loquentis distinctio- ne. Hanc enim personam, quæ hæc vaticina- tur, Davidem esse indubium est, & Actor. 4. ex- pressè perhibetur: At ita loquitur autor hîc Psal- mi, atque ita universi Psalmi tenorem mode- ratur, ut nullo indicio appareat, quod seipsum intelligat, imo manifestissimum sit, quod de alia persona loquatur, quam osculari & in quam fiduciam collocare jubet.

Duodecimo ab in- fallibili in Novo Testamento explicatione. Non- enim de Christo in Novo Testamento tantum sen- su mystico adducitur, sed nativo, proprio, & dire- cte à Spiritu Sancto intento sensu, quin ἀποδείξεως loco adfertur imprimis Ebr. 1, 6. Et quidem ita, ut de nullo alio id dictum esse, quam de Christo Domino nostro perhibeatur, ac doceatur. Quî ergo Psalmus iste primario & proprio sensu de Davide dictus esset? Ita assumsit etiam Actor. 13. Paulus, tanquam certum & indubium, quod hic agatur de Christo: ac fundamentum ibi figi æterni ejus Sacerdotii testatus est Ebr. 5, 5. Sic & Chri- stus seipsum non clarificavit, ut Pontifex fieret, sed qui locutus est ad eum : Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te. Nec aliter intellexere discipuli universi, quam quod de Filio Dei unigenito hic vaticinatus sit Spiritus S. in eoque fundamentum & fulcrum παῤῥησίας suæ adversus persequutiones hostium collocarunt, Actor. 4. Neque aliter Johannes Apostolus Apoc. 19. accepit, Christum esse signi- ficans illum, qui virga ferrea reget, & conteret ho- stes; ut taceam, quod ipse Christus videatur eo re- spicere, cùm Luc. 18. prædicit Filium hominis se- cundum oracula prophetarum gentibus traditum iri: quum nullum aliud oraculum Propheticum facile reperiatur, in quo ista gentium & Judæo- rum adversus Christum conspiratio significantius expressa fuerit, quam sub Psalmi hujus initium.

Decimo tertio ab absurditate sententiæ Grotianæ. Quis enim non videt quam ἄτοπον sit generationis æternæ Filii Dei typum assignare, & quam incon- veniens, electionem Davidis typum istius æternæ generationis constituere? Nullam illa cum æter- na generatione analogiam habet, imo quum typus prior sit antitypo, quomodo electio vel elevatio Da- vidis in Regem prior est æterna generatione Filii Dei? Frustra ergo fingitur, ista sensu immediato, ac literali de Davide agere, sensu mystico de Chri- sto: Nam quod illa omnino æternam generatio- nem Filii Dei inferant, demonstratio Apostolica, Ebr. 1. nos dubitare non permittit. His ergo, in- victis certe, argumentis inducti Ecclesiæ Dd. ma- gno consensu Psalmum hunc de Christo Domino nostro, secundum propriam & literalem sententiam intellexerunt, à quorum consentienti interpreta- tione temere recedendum nunquam est, multo mi- nus vero, cum is tantis rationibus nititur. Quid quod Grotius ipse, antequam fascinatus esset à Ju- dæis recentioribus in annotationibus ad Evange- listas Psalm. 2, 8. de vocatione gentium ad regnum Messiæ interpretatus sit ad Luc. 24, 47.

Vers. eod.

ADSTITERVNT REGES TERRÆ) Nominati in di- cta jam historia, 2. Sam.

## 2:2
Verse 2.

AGAINST THE LORD) For those nations had fallen away from the worship of the one God, and therefore they hated the Jews. AND AGAINST HIS CHRIST) David, solemnly anointed by divine command 1 Samuel 15:13, 2 Sam. 2:4 and 5:3. This sense is of private interpretation. These and the following glosses now collapse through the arguments brought forward here. The Apostles, witnesses greater than any exception, are the testifiers that this does not treat of a past matter, but that David prophesied in the Holy Spirit concerning a future matter. The Holy Spirit explains these things not concerning the Philistines, Moabites, Sabaeans, Damascenes, Ammonites, or Idumaeans, but concerning any nations whatsoever and their Kings rising up against the Lord, and especially concerning Herod, Pontius Pilate, and the rulers of the people, who conspired against Christ at the time of the great passion; therefore, all Kings in general are warned not to oppose themselves to Christ, but to kiss the Son, whoever desires not to perish, but to be saved. The sacred psalmist does not sing of the nations that hate the Jews, but he prophesies of the nations that gather together with the Jewish rulers against Christ. And although it was true at every time that counsels were entered into against the Lord and conspiracies of the nations were begun, yet here the times of the New Testament are especially looked to: as those in which the nations were given to the Messiah as an inheritance, when they were called throughout the world to His kingdom.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

ADVERSVS DOMINVM) Nam gentes illæ ab unius Dei cultu defecerant, ideoque oderant Judæos. ET ADVERSVS CHRISTVM EJVS) Davidem, so- lenniter unctum divino jussu 1. Samuel. 15, 13. 2. Sam. 2, 4. & 5, 3. Sensus hic ἰδίας ἐπιλύσεως est. Corruunt jam hæc & sequentes glossæ per argumenta nunc addu- cta. Non de re præterita hic agi, sed de re futura vaticinatum esse in Spiritu S. Davidem, testes omni exceptione majores sunt Apostoli. Non de Phili- stinis, Moabitis, Sabæis, Damascenis, Ammonitis, Idumæis, sed de quibusvis gentibus, earumque Re- gibus adversus Dominum insurgentibus, & impri- mis de Herode, Pontio Pilato, & principibus populi, qui conspirarunt adversus Christum, tempore pas- sionis magnæ, explicat ista Spiritus Sanctus, ideo Reges in universum omnes monentur, ne se Chri- sto opponant, sed osculentur Filium, quicunque non perire, sed salvari cupiunt. Non de gentibus, quæ Judæos oderunt, canit Hieropsaltes, sed de gen- tibus, quæ cum Judæis principibus in unum adver- sus Christum conveniunt, vaticinatur. Et quan- quam omni tempore verum fuerit, inita esse con- silia adversus Dominum, initas conspirationes gen- tium, hic tamen respiciuntur maximè Novi Testa- menti tempora: utpote quibus gentes in hæredi- tatem datæ sunt Messiæ, cum vocatæ per orbem ter- rarum ad regnum ejusdem.

## 2:3
Verse 3.

LET US BREAK THEIR BONDS) Understand 'saying'. For these are the words of those kings and peoples. Their, that is, of the Israelites, bonds and yoke, that is, the Law of Moses with its rites.

The pronoun 'their' is wrongly referred to the Israelites, of whom no mention was made in the whole Psalm, much less in the preceding verses. It is not permissible to introduce into the text a subject that one pleases, or to refer pronouns to subjects not named, but as they refer themselves to the nouns which are in the text, so here that plural pronoun must necessarily be referred to Jehovah and his Messiah; nor are only the nations introduced here as consulting and saying: Let us break their bonds: but especially the Jews themselves also: indeed, as not so much the nations as the Jews were bound by those bonds and the yoke of the Mosaic law and its rites, so that speech, 'let us break their bonds, and cast away from us their yoke', is most appropriate for the Jews also. For only those desire to break bonds and cast away a yoke from themselves who are held bound by bonds and a yoke. Augustine in this place interprets it concerning the Christian religion, rendered with this paraphrase: Let us devote effort so that the Christian religion may not bind us, nor be imposed upon us. Which is appropriate for Jews and Gentiles alike. For to the former the Christian religion was a stumbling block, but to the latter foolishness. Which he proves from the antithesis: 'But I have been established King.' I, namely, whose bonds they meditate breaking and whose yoke they meditate casting off.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

DIRVMPAMVS VINCVLA EORVM) Subintellige dicentes. Sunt enim hæc verba illorum Regum & populo- rum. Eorum, id est Israelitarum, vincula & jugum, id est, Legem Mosis cum suis ritibus.

Pronomen Eorum perperam ad Israelitas refer- tur, quorum nulla in toto Psalmo, nedum in ante- cedentibus facta fuit mentio. Non autem integrum est, subjectum textui inferre, quod libuerit, aut pronomia ad subjecta non nominata referre, sed uti ea sese ad nomina referunt, quæ in textu ha- bentur, ita hic ad Jehovam & Messiam ejus neces- sario referri debet pronomen illud plurale; Nec vero tantum gentes hic ita introducuntur consul- tantes ac dicentes; Disrumpamus vincula eorum: Sed cumprimis ipsi etiam Judæi: imo, uti non tam gentes, quam Judæi vinculis istis, & jugo legis Mo- saicæ, ac rituum ejusdem constringebantur, ita Judæis etiam maxime convenit illa oratio, disrum- pamus vincula eorum, & projiciamus à nobis jugum ipsorum. Illi enim tantum disrumpere vincula, illi tantum projicere abs sese jugum discupiunt, qui vinculis & jugo constricti tenentur. Augustinus in h. l. de Christiana religione interpretatur, hac pa- raphrasi reddita: Demus operam, ut non nos alliget, neque nobis imponatur Christiana religio. Quæ Ju- dæis pariter & gentilibus conveniunt. Nam illis fuit scandalum, his vero stultitia religio Christia- na. Quod ex ἀντιθέσει probat: Ego autem constitu- tus sum Rex. Ego scil. cujus vincula disrumpere, & ji gum meditantur abjicere.

## 2:5 Addition
On Psalm 2, verse 5.

Latin:

Ad Psal. 2. v. 5.

## 2:5 Addition
Verse 5. THEN HE SHALL SPEAK IN HIS WRATH, AND VEX THEM IN HIS SORE DISPLEASURE.

The blessed Hülsemann understands these things concerning the Son of God, in his unpublished annotations on the Psalms: We judge that these things are said no less of Christ and his divine power to be demonstrated to his enemies, and demonstrated in the very act, Acts 9:5, Josh 8:10, 1 Thess 2:16, Rom 2:5, than the vengeance to be exercised with a rod of iron, which is restricted to Christ alone, Rev 2:26 ff., ch. 19:15; see the parallels Isa 11:4, 2 Thess 2:8. For because in both places the acting Subject is the same, the enemies to be punished are the same, the force and power punishing are the same, no reason allows us to explain verse 5 as referring to anyone other than him of whom he speaks in verse 9.

Latin:

Vers. 5. TUNC LOQUETUR IN IRA SUA, ET IN FURORE SUO CONTURBABIT EOS.

HÆc de Filio Dei intelligit B. Hülseman- nus, in annot. ad Psalmos ἀνεκδότοις: De Christo ejusque divina potentia demon- stranda olim hostibus actuque ipso demon- strata Actor. 9, 5. Jos. 8, 10. 1. Thess. 2, 16. Rom. 2. v. 5. non minus hæc dicta censemus, quam vindictam exer- cendam virga ferrea, quæ ad solum Christum restrin- gitur Apoc. 2, 26. seqq. cap. 19, 15. vide parallel. Esa. 11, 4. 2. Thess. 2, 8. Quia enim utrobique est idem Sub- jectum agens, iidem hostes puniendi, eadem vis & po- testas puniens, nulla ratio sinit, v. 5. de quoquam alio exponere, quam de quo loquitur vers. 9.

## 2:6
Ver. 6.

DECLARING HIS DECREE) I will tell of his constitution.

In Hebrew 'I will tell of the decree' אֶל־חֹק where Genebrard wishes to read אֵל, the statute of God, against grammar: because the noun in the construct state ought to precede, not follow, and against the punctuation. However, אֶל is placed for אֵת, the sign of the accusative, as in 1 Sam. 21:2, Is. 38:19.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

PRÆDICANS PRÆCEPTVM EJVS) Narrabo consti- tutionem ipsius.

In Ebr. Narrabo אֶל־חֹק ubi Genebrard. אֵל legi vult, Dei statutum, contra Grammaticam: quia nomen constructum præcedere debet, non sequi, & contra punctationem. Ponitur autem אֶל pro אֵת nota accusativi, ut 1. Sam. 21, 2. Es. 38, 19.

## 2:6 Addition
Verse 6.

UPON SION HIS HOLY MOUNT.

This is not to be understood of Sion properly, but metaphorically, that is, of the Church; a comparison of Psalm 102:14, 17, Isa 2:2, Rev 14:1, Heb 12:22 teaches this.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

SUPER SION MONTEM SANCTUM EJUS.

Non de Sione proprie, sed metaphorice dicta, hoc est, de Ecclesia hoc accipiendum Psalm. 102. v. 14. 17. Esa. 2, 2. Apocal. 14, 1. Ebr. 12, 22. collatio do- cet.

## 2:7
Ver. 7.

THOU ART MY SON: THIS DAY HAVE I BEGOTTEN THEE) You may translate it best; O my Son: today (that is, at this time) I have begotten thee: I have conferred upon thee a new life, namely, a royal one. אַתָּה for the Hebrews is often nothing other than a sign of the vocative. It appears in Gen. 49:8. Kings are called Sons of God, and those who excel among them, firstborns, Ps. 89:27.

That אַתָּה is said here with emphasis: Thou art my Son: nor is it a bare address: But a testimony of a matter entirely singular: as was that proclamation of God the Father, made in Matt. 3 and 17: This is my Son. Which, by the force of the demonstrative article, we previously warned refers to this address. Therefore no paraphrase took that אַתָּה as a sign of the vocative; all perceive the emphasis in this address, and indicate that the subject, to whom those predicates—to be the Son, to be begotten, and the rest—belong, is designated; the Chaldean, Syriac, Greek, Latin, German, and others. Nor can that 'begotten' be explained as the conferring of a royal life. For however much kings and magistrates may be called Sons of God metaphorically, because of the likeness, which they have with God, of majesty, power, and honor, yet they are nowhere called sons by generation, or begotten by God: for this implies a proper and natural Son: also no King is ever called the firstborn of God; although there is another reason for this application, which by a Hebrew phrase sometimes denotes excellence; but another for the present discourse: You are my Son; I have this day begotten you, where who will admit that mere excellence is designated? For what is held in Psalm 89:27 must also be understood of Christ, who alone is called both only-begotten and firstborn, μονογενὴς καὶ πρωτότοκος, and indeed on account of the eternal generation from the essence of God the Father, which Grotius, as far as the name μονογενὴς and the present sentence, You are my Son, I have this day begotten you, is concerned, could not deny without openly passing into the camp of the Arians. The Calvinists certainly, although Calvin himself, Pelicanus, as well as Aretius, Felinus, and Paraeus explain the Psalm concerning David, as a type of Christ, are so struck by the majesty of these words that they desert those teachers of theirs, and acknowledge with us that this treats solely of Christ, as is manifest from Franciscus Junius in his parallels, Andreas Rivetus previously cited, and Johannes Piscator in this place. Which ἀναντιῥῥήτως proves (1.) the name בֵּן Son and in verse 12 בַּר taken properly, implying a Son begotten from the essence and ὁμούσιον, because one must not depart from the proper signification unless Scripture itself compels it; and if anywhere the name Son of GOD is to be taken concerning the ὁμούσιον Son (which they do not deny, unless they are Arians), surely here, where the Messiah is thus addressed by the Father: You are my Son: I have this day begotten you, it must be so understood. Because he is not only called so absolutely and without any alienating addition, but also the discourse is about him as the Son said to be μονοτρόπως. When the Father in that most divine decree addresses the Messiah under this name אַתָּה בְנִי, he separates him by this very fact from all creatures, so that he raises him above them all, and places him in the mystery of divinity, and indicates a divine and monadic sonship. (2.) The conjunction of the Son with the Father; since here the Son is placed in the same eminence with Jehovah GOD the Father himself, so that the raging of the nations and Tyrants against Jehovah himself tends toward this Son as a common or rather one object, and they are the principle of that derision, contempt, and raging; from which eminence of sonship the enthronement (ἐνθρονισμὸς) of the Messiah upon Mount Zion receives its splendor, and to him is attributed the inheritance of the world, and supreme power to crush rebellious nations, as well as the majesty of adoration. (3.) The generation of the Son; which can be said of no other anointed one than Christ our Lord, namely that he is the Son of God by generation; You are my Son: I have this day begotten you. Which words must not be taken otherwise than of substantial generation. For the word ילד when it is taken properly, as it must altogether be understood when the reason for sonship is rendered by it, implies substantial production: and as often as it occurs concerning a person producing a person, absolutely and without a diminishing addition, it is always said of substantial production, as is manifest from the constant and perpetual usage of Scripture. (4.) The description of the Son of GOD, because here it treats of that Son to whom infinite power, omniscience, omnipresence, and divine justice are vindicated, which befits divine dominion, by the power of which he can rule all nations and the ends of the earth: which is required in this anointed one, to show the vanity of the counsels of any nations whatsoever, and the insuperable power and Majesty of this Messiah with Jehovah, as well as his vindictive wrath against the rebellion and contumelious consultation of any impious men whatsoever, and power sufficient for the victorious crushing of enemies with a rod of iron. It treats of that Son whom all Kings and judges of the earth ought to kiss with the kiss of faith, invocation, and subjection, in whom all who are to be saved ought to trust. Which ἀξίωμα is proper to the only-begotten Son of GOD alone. (5.) The collation of parallel places: because there is no doubt that this Psalm looks back to the promise made in 2. Sam. 7:14, which we demonstrated must be understood of the Messiah the Son of God when we treated of that place. (6.) The interpretation of the N.T.; in which these things are explained solely concerning Christ our Lord, and indeed in such a way that what is said of him here is entirely ἀκοινώνητα, and befits him alone, Heb. 1:8, Acts c. 13, Heb. 5, Rev. 19. But nowhere throughout the whole Scripture are they explained concerning David. But who will believe that the proper and immediate sense of so excellent an oracle is nowhere delivered throughout the whole Scripture, and only the mystical and mediate sense is explained in it and here and there. (7.) Finally, the uncertainty of the contrary interpretation. For those who explain it concerning David cannot say with certainty at what time these things were said of him. Calvin, says, that generation which he mentions ought to be referred to the sense or knowledge of men, namely, that it was openly known from this that he was begotten by God, when David miraculously ascended the throne of the kingdom beyond all hope and by the power of the heavenly Spirit crushed innumerable conspiracies, because he could not reign unless all neighboring nations were brought under the yoke, as if the world were subdued. With whom Grotius seems to agree, referring us to 2 Sam. 7 and 10. But then David was not finally begotten, or constituted King: then no new, that is, royal life was conferred upon him: which he had already received when he was anointed King, 1 Sam. 15:13, or certainly 2 Sam. 2:4, c. 5, verse 3. Therefore Pelicanus does not agree here with Calvin, but understands these words concerning the time of the first anointing: he said to me, when he anointed me King over Israel through Samuel, you are my son, today I have begotten you, I have made you another shepherd from a shepherd of sheep, a prince of my faithful people. And Grotius himself confessed a little before at verse 2 that David is called the Messiah there on account of that anointing, 1 Sam. 6, 2 Sam. 2 & 5. If therefore he was already the Messiah even then before the Philistines, Moabites, Ammonites, and other nations were conquered, he had already received a new royal life: consequently, it was not only when those nations were conquered that this was said to him: today I have begotten you, that is, at this time I have conferred upon you a new royal life. The Mohammedans themselves indeed acknowledge that these words refer to Jesus, but because their κυρία δόξα is that saying of the Alcoran, He is God alone, God eternal, who neither begat, nor was begotten, and to whom there is no equal: (whence they deny the Generation of the Son of God) they invent that this oracle of the Psalm has been corrupted by Christians: because in place of Waladtoka, I have begotten you, it should be read, according to the testimony of Ebnol Athir and the author of the Kamus, Walladtoka, I have cherished or educated you: and in place of Bonaiya, My Son, Nabiya, My Prophet. Altawlid, says Al Firuzabadius, is education, hence the saying of God Almighty to Jesus (to whom may God be propitious and grant peace) You are Nabiya, My Prophet. I Walladtaka, I have cherished you: but the Christians said: You are Bonaiyma, My Son, I Waladtoka, I have begotten you. See concerning these the miscellaneous notes of Edward Pococke. But it is extremely absurd to dream of such a corruption here: since the original text was written not in the Arabic, but in the Hebrew language, nor do the Hebrews themselves read it otherwise than the Christians. What is more, even the more ancient Jews themselves have professed, and the more recent ones also acknowledge, that the discourse here is about the Messiah, although these latter have especially twisted the words into a foreign meaning. For also R. Maimonides expounded the Psalm concerning the Messiah, and R. David Kimchi confessed that the ancients interpreted it of the same, and that this explanation is clear. There are, he says, those who interpret that Psalm concerning Gog and Magog, and the King Messiah is the Messiah. And thus our masters of blessed memory expounded it, and the Psalm explained in this way is clear; but in truth it is more correct to say that David himself spoke of himself, as has been expounded by us. R. Solomon Jarchi confesses the same, nor does he conceal the reason why more recent Jews interpret it otherwise and depart from the ancients, namely, so that the dogma of the Christian faith might not be established. Our doctors, he says, expounded the meaning of this Psalm concerning the King Messiah, but as it sounds, and so that an answer may be given to the Minæans (or Heretics: for by the word מינים they traduce Christians), it is EXPEDIENT to interpret it of David himself. Thus, therefore, they abandon their ancestors, who handed down the true sense, lest any light from it should accrue to the Christian faith. Which confession of Solomon is to be carefully noted.

If Grotius, with Enjedinus and the remaining Photinians, urges that the particle 'today' introduces some temporal generation, not an eternal one, just as Calvin also calls the subtlety of Augustine a fiction, that 'today' denotes perpetuity: it is to be noted first that the word הַיּוֹם is not always a mark of a certain time; see Isa. 58:4. Sometimes it also introduces perpetuity or continuity: as when it is said in Gen. 22:14, הַיּוֹם in the mount the Lord shall be seen: it is called so perpetually from the time it was so named by Abraham, Gen. 30:48. This heap is a witness between me and thee הַיּוֹם, that is, in perpetuity. Deut. 4:39. Thou shalt know הַיּוֹם and reduce it to thy heart, that is, perpetually. Ps. 95:7. הַיּוֹם today, that is, always, when you shall hear the voice of GOD. Concerning which Heb. 3:7, ἄχρις ὗ σήμερον καλεῖται, as long as it is called today. Therefore, c. 4:7 seqq., that הַיּוֹם is said to comprise the perennial Sabbatism of the Saints. See also Matt. 6:11. For that σήμερον can also be taken concerning the perpetuation of divine sustenance, as long as it is called today. Sometimes it designates eternity itself, as Isa. 43:13. Even הַיּוֹם from today I am myself, that is, from eternity. The LXX render it ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, by which eternity is also wont to be indicated: see 1 John 1:1, 2. Thus, therefore, what I would wish to be noted in the second place, that הַיּוֹם is to be explained according to the condition of the underlying subject matter. Since here also the discourse is concerning God the Father, and His internal act, or that which is done within the complex of the divine essence, the generation of the eternal Son, that הַיּוֹם cannot be explained otherwise than by eternity. For the internal acts of God are eternal, and that generation is truly ἄχρονος, nay rather ὑπέρχρονος and ἀΐδιος, lacking all παραλλαγῇ or τροπῆς ἀποσκιάσματι. James 1:17. But such as the generation is, such also is the duration denoted by that הַיּוֹם. ὁ Θεὸς ἄχρονος ὢν καὶ ἄναρχος καὶ ἀπαθὴς καὶ ἄῤῥευστος καὶ ἀσώματος, καὶ μόνος, ἀτελεύτητος ἀχρόνως, καὶ ἀνάρχως, καὶ ἀῤῥεύσως, καὶ ἀπαθῶς γεννᾷ, καὶ ἐκτὸς συνδυασμῦ, says Damasc. lib. 1 de Orthod. Fid. c. 8. Because it concerns the substantial production of GOD the Father, by which He generated the Son from His very essence, which the property of the word 'Son' and the verb ילד introduces, it is necessary that that generation was done outside of all time, in the purest state of eternity and one ignorant of succession and vicissitude, just as the divine substance itself is eternal and placed above and outside of all time. (3.) Nor is that word inconvenient for explaining the eternal generation: provided it excludes all time, whether it be named past or future, and insinuates a constant, perpetual, and fixed 'today,' with the intervals of time excluded. Thus Augustine de quinque hærefib. c. 4. With God there is never a tomorrow, never a yesterday, but always TODAY. Nor is the argument of the Blessed Luther, T. V. Jen. Latin. h. l., to be rashly dismissed here. If we wish to speak as the thing is, the Son of God is born, and was born, today, daily, and always. For eternity has neither past nor future. In this manner the particle 'today' is to be taken, for the time, to wit, of God, not our own. For God does not speak with us, but with Him who is outside of time with God. We have these distinctions of times, so that 'today' is one thing, 'yesterday' another, 'tomorrow' another. Eternity knows not this difference, where there is no time, neither past nor future, but a perpetual 'today,' just as Peter says, one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. (4.) That הַיּוֹם is to be explained in such a way that it agrees with the Son, through whom the ages were founded, existing before the ages, Heb. 1:3, who is the image of the invisible Father, and existed before anything existed, Col. 1:14, 16, just as the generation of the Son of God entirely preceded the ποίησιν of the ages, and the ὕπαρξιν of all things, both invisible and visible. It is concerning that generation that it is treated here, which makes it so that the Son is generated in that 'today' as God of the eternal throne, and that Lord who in the beginning founded the earth, and whose works the heavens are, as is clear from Heb. 1:6, 10, and so that He is more eminent than the Angels by infinite parasangs, as He is to be worshipped by them all, v. 6. Therefore the Son is not said to be in that sense in which the Angels are called sons, nor was His generation done in time, as the Angels were made sons of GOD in time, but that הַיּוֹם transcends all time, surpasses and precedes all ages. (5.) That הַיּוֹם is opposed to the temporal machinations of enemies, not of some or certain ones, but of all times, from the very beginnings of the Church even to the consummation of the age, that all those will be in vain against the Messiah, because this person was generated הַיּוֹם from eternity, before any counsels could be forged. Those who meditate anything in vain against Him who was generated from all eternity from the most simple and immutable substance of GOD, meditate in vain, and as many as rage, they rage in vain. (6.) That divine act of generation precedes in order the divine decree concerning the anointing of Christ, which, because it is eternal, it is necessary that the act of generation also be eternal: and therefore that הַיּוֹם is to be explained in no other way. (7.) Through that act an infinite, immense, omnipresent person was produced, who obtains the nations by hereditary right, and occupies the ends of the earth as his own possession; for which is required infinite power, omniscience and omnipresence, and infinite and divine government. Therefore Heb. 1, 2. 3. 15. he who is constituted κληρονόμος πάντων, is said to be φέρων τὰ πάντα τῷ ῥήματι τῆς δυνάμεως αὑτοῦ. Therefore a temporal act of generation cannot be understood: For whether this be understood as proper or improper, it always implies only a finite person. Although, however, this giving of that possession was made in time, because it was made following a prior request John 17, 5. and thus pertains to the human nature in Christ, as a divine ὑπερύψωσις and βελτίωσις, yet because it does not pertain to the assumed human nature from natural principles, but from the infinity and majesty of the person to whom this human nature is as it were implanted, therefore this remains invincible and unshaken, that that person, who can possess and govern all nations and the ends of the earth by divine government, is infinite, immense, and omnipresent. Which our D. Dn. Dorscheus conveniently notes in his Disp. on Ps. 2, 7. concerning the eternal generation of the Son of God §. 51. which is contained in his Pentadecade of dissertations, in which he has also more copiously executed the present argument. (8.) Finally, that act of generation, through which the adorable person was produced, or to whom the majesty of religious adoration belongs, truly divine, and infinite, could not have come to pass in the temporal היום, but it is necessary that it be done from eternity. For it is repugnant that the person of an infinite and divine majesty should have a temporal beginning of being. But such is that act, because by the power of this generation that Son is begotten, to whom the αξιωμα of religious adoration belongs. Kiss the Son: and blessed are all who trust in him. Induced by these arguments, therefore, Catholic Doctors have understood these words concerning the eternal generation, and even now understand them. Namely, that today is understood as perpetual and everlasting, without past and future, a νυν that is eternal and immutable, devoid of all flux, succession, and variation. Which opinion they defend against the Arians, who understand it as a temporal act: from whom, since Grotius departs and pleads the cause of the Arians, let those who patronize him see, whose spirit he himself is a son of? Augustine has it thus on this passage: Although that day may also be seen in the prophecy, on which Christ was born according to the Scripture, yet because 'today' signifies presence, and in eternity there is neither anything past, as if it had ceased to be, nor future, as if it were not yet, but only present, because whatever is eternal is always: it is understood divinely according to that saying, 'Today I have begotten thee,' by which the most sincere and Catholic faith proclaims the everlasting generation of the power and wisdom of God, who is the only-begotten Son. Compare the same Augustine, Enchir. ad Laur. c. 45; Tertull. c. Prax. cap. 11; Athanasius, Orat. contr. Arian. & in Decret. Nic. Syn.; Cyril of Alexandria, l. 9, Thesaur.; Ambrose in Epist. ad Ebr., who explain it without doubt concerning the eternal generation. But why did Grotius prefer to lend his ears here to Enjedinus and Socinus, or the Rabbis, rather than to St. Augustine and other Doctors of the Church? For the Jews, as is known, interpret it in the same way as Grotius, that David was then begotten, and as it were reborn, when he was rescued from the greatest dangers and placed upon the royal throne.

But as to what was done regarding the application of Acts 13 and Heb. 5: there is no need for us to invent, with the Papists, different literal senses of the same saying, just as it pleased Salmeron (Tom. I, comment. in Nov. Testam. proleg. 7), and likewise Bellarmine, Schwarz, Gregory of Valencia, Blasius de Viegas, Vasquez, Molina, and Lorinus to interpret this passage concerning the eternal generation, the incarnation, and the resurrection of Christ all at once: indeed, it even seemed good to Sanctius in Acta, page 268, and also to Lorinus on this passage, to explain this passage also concerning the production in the womb of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

Just as there is only a single literal sense of any saying, so we have already shown that this deals only with the eternal generation of the Son of God; indeed, Lorinus himself acknowledges that it is less free to explain these words of Psalm 2:7 as referring to anything other than the eternal generation: and Cajetan, Sixtus Senensis (L. VII, Bibl. S. haeres. VIII & XI), and Genebrard openly deny that they should be taken as referring to the resurrection, although the certainty and necessity of the resurrection are concluded from the majesty of the eternal generation: and Ribera in his Commentary on Heb. 1, page 71, refutes those in his school who understand the same as referring to the resurrection.

We do not indeed deny that Chrysostom and Fulgentius refer them to the mystery of the incarnation: which secondary sense the Blessed Aegidius Hunnius also admits in his second Anti-Par., in that the name of Son of GOD was obtained by Christ as man through union, insofar as his humanity came into the κοινωνίαν of this person, who was begotten by the Father from eternity; but he denies that it is thus accommodated to a bare temporal birth. Not otherwise, he says on page 72, can or should the oracle be accommodated to the incarnation, except because through the hypostatic union the human nature of Christ, taken from the virgin, arrived at the unity and ταυτότητα of that hypostasis which was begotten by the Father outside of time, so that now the eulogy also pertains to the assumed man because of the personal union: 'Thou art my Son; today I have begotten thee': since he is one Son of GOD and of the virgin, entirely undivided in person and filiation. Therefore, if I ask, why is the man recently taken from the virgin and called the Son of God? Is it simply because of this temporal birth from Mary? The answer is, not simply for that reason, otherwise he would not be ἀπάτωρ by reason of his human birth, which is absurd and contrary to the testimony of the Epistle to the Hebrews, chapter 7. But this glory of the man Christ depends on a higher principle, namely because Christ, by reason of the assumed humanity, is one ὑφιςάμενον with Him, indeed according to the hypostasis he is the very same one whom the Father, according to the oracle of David, begat from eternity. This is the Blessed Aegidius Hunnius. And for that reason, Augustine also applies it in Enchir. ad Laurent. c. 49. Whence that voice of the Father, which was made over the baptized one (Today I have begotten thee), shows not that one day of time on which he was baptized, but an immutable eternity, so as to show that that man pertains to the person of the only-begotten: for where the day is neither begun by the end of today, nor terminated by the beginning of tomorrow, it is always today. Thus, therefore, the proper and native meaning of David's words being preserved, those words could be accommodated to the incarnation: just as some, with Bede in Acts of the Apostles, judge that the passage of David in Acts 13 is not applied to the resurrection, but to the excitation and mission of the Messiah; which also the Blessed Gerhard in Exegef. Tom. I. Loc. Theol. p. 1176. It was decided, not because the word to beget means to bring forth into the light in some new way, as Rivetus wishes, and praises Beza and Junius for that opinion, but so that the proper meaning of the word may be retained, concerning production from the substance, and the sentence may be accommodated only to the temporal birth, because Christ as man obtained the same eulogy. Others admit that the words of David in Acts 13 are brought forward to prove the resurrection of Christ from the dead: But so that likewise the genuine sense concerning the eternal generation is supposed, not excluded: and so that it may be taught that in the resurrection only a φανέρωσιν or manifestation of the eternal generation was made, Rom. 1. v. 4. Just as in the Scriptures things are sometimes said to come to pass when they become manifest: or so that it may be said that the Apostle demonstrates from the Deity of the person by an immovable consequence that it was necessary for Christ to rise from the dead, just as the blessed Hunnius declares in Calvinus Judaizans p. 23: For that Paul proves the resurrection of Christ from this verse of the Psalm, by this very fact he presupposes the eternal Deity of the rising person celebrated in the words of the Psalm as the foundation of his proof: For on account of this very thing (that this person, whose flesh rising from the dead is personally his own, is the only-begotten Son of GOD today begotten in eternity) it is impossible that his flesh should either undergo corruption or be detained in death. Which are repeated and confirmed in the second Anti-Par. p. 69. Therefore, not even according to this interpretation is there need for a foreign interpretation of the words of the Psalmist, by which the resurrection might be expressed through the word to beget, because the name of regeneration is adapted to the same, Matt. 19, verse 18, just as he imprudently concedes this to the Socinians along with the Arminians and Remonstrants

Andr. Rivetus in this place, page 20: nor will it be necessary to tear apart those words with Rivetus, so that, for instance, the former words, 'You are my Son,' bring in an eternal and natural generation: but the latter, 'Today I have begotten you,' express a temporal generation, so called improperly and figuratively, by which to beget is to bring into the light in a new way: that they designate the begetting of the hypostasis, by which the person of the Father begets the person of the Son from eternity, and these the begetting of the manifestation, by which Christ was manifested as the Son of God in time. Which explanation, however absurd it may be to others, Rivetus prefers for the sake of his Calvin. For what is more manifest than that the former words, 'You are my Son,' are declared by the latter words: 'Today I have begotten you'; and that for the same reason the Messiah is called the Son of God here, for which reason he is said to have been begotten by the Father. What coherence will there be: 'You are my Son' (natural, begotten from eternity from my essence), 'Today I have begotten you' (formerly in the fullness of time I will bring you into the light in a new way through resurrection from the dead.) Who does not see that the reason for the sonship is rendered and explained by the words, 'I have begotten you,' and by no means is some future thing predicted to him? Calvin himself certainly acknowledged that these words: 'My Son' and 'I have begotten you' must be taken in the same way, not a different one, partly proper, partly improper, and therefore he took both improperly, whence Calvin can in no way be helped by that new distortion: For Calvin's gloss holds thus: 'You are my Son: David could indeed be considered the Son of God by virtue of royal right, just as we know that princes, because they excel others, are called both gods and sons of God: But here God, adorning David with a singular eulogy, exalts him not only above all mortals, but also above the Angels.' Which the Apostle prudently weighs in Hebrews chapter 1, 5, while he warns that this was never said to any Angel. For although David was inferior to the Angels, insofar as he bore the person of Christ, he is deservedly preferred far above them. Let us know, therefore, that here not just any one of many is designated as the Son of God, but the only-begotten Son of God, so that he alone may stand out in heaven and on earth. But that God pronounces that He has begotten ONE, ought to be referred to the sense or knowledge of men, for David was begotten by God when his election clearly appeared. This is Calvin: from which it is manifest what I said, that both members in this verse 7 of our Psalm are explained by the same person concerning David, who is said (improperly) to be begotten by God when his election clearly appeared, and is called the Son of God, certainly not natural and properly so called: for thus it would be necessary to say that David was begotten from the essence of God; but improperly and figuratively. But setting aside the distortion of Rivetus and Calvin, and also the interpretation of others—which is indeed convenient enough and not at all opposed to the native sense of the words of the sacred singer—concerning the demonstration of eternal generation made through the resurrection of Christ, a simpler explanation, and one more in agreement with the words of the Apostle in Acts 13:23, is that of those who understand these things concerning the raising up and mission of Christ: 'And we announce to you the promise that was made to the fathers, that God has fulfilled this for our children, raising up Jesus, as it is also written in the second Psalm, You are my Son, today I have begotten you': which words the Apostle cites particularly: because with these words not only does the narration of the divine decree concerning the kingdom of the Messiah begin, but in that place it is taught expressly, as they say, that he himself would be the Son of God

the Messiah, which is that notable promise made to the fathers and to David himself, to which the Apostle refers his Jewish listeners as to a most well-known matter, having brought forward only certain words from the same, as he is wont to do, which designate the person of the Messiah to be exhibited, which had to be inculcated upon them most strongly; since the Jews were affected by no light scandal that Christ professed himself to be the Son of God, and held that for blasphemy, John 10. We have asserted this explanation more fully in the Examination of the Books of Crellius on the one God the Father, which is found in Volume II, on the Augsburg Confession or Natural and Revealed Theology, page 1350.

As regards the other passage, Heb. 5:5, 'So also Christ did not glorify himself to become High Priest, but he who spoke to him: You are my Son, today I have begotten you': it is not implied by this that the Son of God was begotten only then when he was made High Priest, but that, as Christ also often testified, Christ received this glory from God the Father himself, and that eternal generation is the foundation of that glorification and of the eternal priestly office: It is not a question here of the time, but of the author of the High Priesthood: nor indeed can a certain temporal generation be the foundation of an eternal High Priesthood; for before the foundations of the world were laid, the Son of God performed the priestly and intercessory office, and interposed himself as sponsor, mediator, and propitiator in the secret Council of the Holy Trinity, therefore he is also said to be the Lamb of God slain from the foundation of the world, Eph. 1, verse 4, Rev. 13, verse 8.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

FILIVS MEVS ES TV: EGO HODIE GENVI TE) Cptime vertas; O Fili mi: hodie (id est, hoc tempore) ego te genui: novam vitam, regalem scil. tibi contuli. אַתָּה Hebræis sæpe nihil aliud quam nota vocativi. Apparet Ge- nes. 49, 8. Reges dicuntur Filii Dei, & qui inter eos ex- cellunt, primogeniti Psal. 89, 27.

Illud אַתָּה hic cum Emphasi dicitur: Filius meus es tu: nec compellatio est nuda: Sed testifi- catio rei prorsus singularis: uti erat illa procla- matio Dei Patris, Matth. 3. & 17. facta: Hic est Fi- lius meus. Quam, vi articuli demonstrativi, hanc προσφώνησιν respicere, antea monuimus. Ideo nulla paraphrasis illud אַתָּה, ut notam vocativi ac- cepit, omnes emphasin in hac προσφωνήσει susci- piunt, & subjectum, cui prædicata illa, Filium esse, genitum esse, & reliqua conveniunt, designari innuunt; Chaldaica, Syriaca, Græca, Latina, Ger- manice, aliæ. Nec illud genui explicari potest de col- latione vitæ Regalis. Utut enim Reges ac Magistratus Filii Dei Metaphorice dicantur, ob similitudinem, quam habent cum Deo, majestatis, potestatis, & honoris, nuspiam tamen nominantur filii, per ge- nerationem, vel a Deo geniti: hoc enim proprium & naturalem Filium infert: nuspiam etiam Rex ullus primogenitus Dei dicitur; quamvis etiam hu- jus applicationis alia sit ratio, quæ phrasi Ebræa ex- cellentiam quandoque notat; alia vero præsentis orationis: Filius meus es tu; Ego hodie genui te, ubi nudam excellentiam designari quis admittet? Nam quod Psalm. 89, 27. habetur, de Christo etiam in- telligendum est, qui solus & unigenitus & primogeni- tus, μονογενὴς καὶ πρωτότοκος vocatur, & quidem ob generationem æternam ex essentia Dei Patris, quam Grotius, quantum ad nomen μονογενὴς & sen- tentiam præsentem, Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te, negare non potuit, quin palam in castra Ariano- rum transiret. Calviniani certe, etsi Calvinus ipse, Pelicanus, nec non Aretius, Felinus, & Paræus de Davide, ut typo Christi, Psalmum explicent, horum verborum majestate ita percelluntur, ut præcepto- res istos suos deserant, ac nobiscum de Christo hic unice agi agnoscant, ut e Franc. Junio in parallelis, Andr. Riveto antea adducto, & Joh. Piscatore in h. l. manifestum est. Quod ἀναντιῥῥήτως evincit (1.) no- men בֵּן Filii & v. 12. בַּר proprie acceptum, inferens Filium ex essentia genitum & ὁμούσιον, quia a propria significatione, nisi cogente ipsa Scriptura, disce- dendum non est; & si alicubi nomen Filii DEI de ὁμουσίῳ Flio accipiendum (quod non inficiantur, nisi Ariani) profecto, hic ubi a Patre Messias ita compellatur: Filius meus es tu: Ego hodie genui te, sic intelligendum erit. Quia non tantum abso- lute & sine ullo additamento alienante sic vocatur, sed etiam de eo ut μονοτρόπως dicto Filio sermo est. Quum Pater in divinissimo illo decreto Messiam compellat sub hoc nomine אַתָּה בְנִי, secernit eum hoc ipso ab omnibus creaturis, ita ut supra eas omnes eundem evehat, & in divinitatis arcanum collocet, ac filiationem divinam ac monadicam indigitet. (2.) Conjunctio Filii cum Patre; siqui- dem hic Filius in eandem eminentiam cum ipso Je- hovah DEO Patre collocatur, ut fremitus gen- tium & Tyrannorum contra ipsum Jehovam furi- bundi in hunc Filium tanquam commune vel po- tius unum objectum tendant, atq; illi sint unum irri- sionis, contemtus, fremitus istius principium; ex qua eminentia filiationis splendorem accipit ἐνθρο- νισμὸς Messiæ in montem Zion, eidemq; hæreditas orbis, ac potestas summa, gentes rebelles confrin- gendi, nec non majestas adorationis tribuitur. (3.) Generatio Filii; quæ de nullo alio uncto quam de Christo Domino nostro dici potest, quod nem- pe sit Filius Dei per generationem; Filius meus es tu: Ego hodie genui te. Quæ verba aliter accipi non debent, quam de substantiali generatione. Ver- bum enim ילד cum proprie accipitur, uti omni- no intelligendum est, cum eodem ratio filiationis redditur, substantialem productionem infert: & quotiescunq; illud de persona producente personam, absolute & sine additamento imminuente occur- rit, semper de productione substantiali dicitur, uti e constanti & perpetua Scripturæ usurpatione ma- nifestum. (4.) Filii DEI descriptio, quia de illo Filio hic agitur, cui infinita potentia, omniscentia, omnipræsentia, divina justitia vindicatur, quæ divi- no dominio convenit, vi cujus gentes universas, & fi- nes orbis terrarum regere possit: quæ requiritur in hoc uncto, ad ostendendam inanitatem consilio- rum quorumvis gentium, & insuperabilem Mes- siæ hujus cum Jehovah virtutem, ac Majestatem, nec non iram vindicem adversus rebellionem & contumeliosam consultationem quorumvis im- piorum, & potestatem ad victoriosam in virga fer- rea hostium contritionem sufficientem. De illo agitur Filio, quem osculari osculo fidei, invocatio- nis, & subjectionis omnes Reges & judices terræ, in quo confidere omnes salvandi debent. Quod ἀξίωμα soli Filio DEI unigenito proprium est. (5.) Paralleli loci collatio: quia dubium nullum est, hoc Psalmo respici promissionem, 2. Sam. 7, 14. factam, quam de Messia Filio Dei intelligendam esse, cum de loco isto egimus, demonstravimus. (6.) N. T. interpretatio; in quo unice de Christo Domino nostro hæc explicantur, & ita quidem, ut quæ de ipso hic dicuntur, prorsus ἀκοινώνητα sint, atque ipsi unice conveniant, Ebr. 1, 8. Act. c. 13. Ebr. 5. Apoc. 19. Nuspiam vero per totam Scripturam de Davide explicantur. At quis credet, proprium & immediatum sensum oraculi tam eximii nuspiam per totam Scripturam traditum esse, solum tantum mysticum & mediatum sensum in eadem, & passim explicari. (7.) Deniq; interpretationis contrariæ incertitudo. Qui enim de Davide explicant, quo- nam tempore hæc de ipso dicta sint, certo dicere non possunt. Calvinus, genitura ista, inquit, cujus meminit, ad hominum sensum vel notitiam referri debet, nempe, quod palam hinc cognitum est, genitum fuisse a Deo, cum mirabiliter regni solium præter omnem spem conscendit David & cælestis Spiritus virtute innumeras fregit conspirationes, quia regnare non poterat, nisi gentibus omnibus vicinis sub jugum redactis, quasi subacto quodam mundo. Quicum fa- cere videtur Grotius ad 2. Sam. 7. & 10. nos remit- tens. At tum David non demum genitus, seu con- stitutus fuit Rex: tum non collata ipsi nova h. e. regalis vita: quam accepit jam, cum in Regem unctus fuit, 1. Sam. 15, 13. vel certe 2. Sam. 2, 4. c. 5. vers. 3. Ideo non facit hic cum Calvino Pelicanus, sed de tempore primæ unctionis hæc intelligit: dixit ille ad me, cum per Samuelem me ungeret, Regem su- per Israelem, filius meus es tu, hodie genui te, alium te pastorem reddidi ex pastore ovium, principem meo- rum fidelium. Et fassus est paulo ante ad v. 2. ipse Grotius, Davidem Messiam ibi dici ob illam unctio- nem, 1. Sam. 6. 2. Sam. 2. & 5. Si ergo jam tum fuit Messias ante devictos Philistæos, Moabitas, Ammonitas, aliasque gentes, jam novam vitam Re- galem accepit: proinde non demum gentibus il- lis devictis hoc ipsi ita dictum fuit: hodie genui te, hoc est, hoc tempore novam vitam regalem tibi contuli. Mahumetani ipsi agnoscunt sane hæc ad Jesum spectare, sed quia κυρία δόξα ipsorum est il- lud dictum Alcohlas, Est ipse Deus unus, Deus æter- nus, qui nec genuit, nec genitus est, & cui nullus est æqualis: (unde Generationem Filii Dei negant) comminiscuntur Psalmi hoc oraculum a Christia- nis corruptum esse: quia loco Waladtoka genui te, legendum sit, testibus Ebnol Athir, & autore Ka- musii, Walladtoka fovi vel educavi te: ac loco Bo- naiya Filius meus Nabiya Propheta meus. Al- tawlid, inquit Al Firuzabadius, est educatio, inde dictum Dei omnipotentis ad Jesum (cui propitius sit & pacem concedat Deus) Tu es Nabiya Propheta meus. Ego Walladtaka fovi te: at dixerunt Chri- stiani: Tu es Bonaiyma Filius meus, Ego Waladto- ka, te genui. Vid. de his notæ miscellan. Eduardi Pocockii. Sed perquam ineptum est, ejusmodi corruptelam hic somniare: siquidem non Arabi- ca, sed Ebræa lingua textus originalis conscriptus sit, nec aliter Ebræi ipsi legant, quam Christiani. Quid quod etiam ipsimet Judæi antiquiores pro- fessi sint, idq; agnoscant etiam recentiores, de Mes- sia hic sermonem esse, quamvis in alienam senten- tiam verba hi cumprimis detorserint. Nam & R. Maimonides de Messia Psalmum exposuit, & R. Da- vid Kimchi fassus est, interpretatos de eodem esse Veteres, eamque explicationem perspicuam esse. Sunt, inquit, qui interpretantur Psalmum istum de Gog & Magog, estq́; Messiah Rex Messias. Atq́; ita ex- posuerunt Dd. nostri p. m. estq́; Psalmus hoc modo ex- plicatus perspicuus; at vero propius est dixisse ipsum Davidem de seipso, uti a nobis est expositum. R. Sa- lomo Jarchi fatetur idem, neq; dissimulat causam, cur secus recentiores Judæi interpretentur, & ab antiquis recedant, ne scil. dogma Christianæ fidei stabiliatur. Doctores nostri, inquit, exposuerunt hu- jus Psalmi significatum de Rege Messiah, at prout so- nat, & ut respondeatur Minæis (seu Hæreticis: vo- ce enim מינים hæreticorum traducunt Christia- nos) EXPEDIT interpretari ipsum de ipso Davide. Sic ergo majores suos, verum sensum tradentes, re- linquunt, ne fidei Christianæ aliquid lucis inde acce- dat. Quæ Salomonis confessio probe observanda.

Si Grotius cum Enjedino, & reliquis Photinia- nis urgeat particulam hodie temporalem aliquam genituram inferre, non æternam, quemadmodum etiam Calvinus argutiam Augustini, & commentum vocat, quod hodie perpetuum denotetur: obser- vandum primo vocem הַיּוֹם non semper certi tem- poris notam esse; videatur Esa. 58, 4. Quandoque etiam perpetuitatem vel continuitatem inferre: ut- pote cum Gen. 22, 14. dicitur, הַיּוֹם in monte Domi- nus videbitur: perpetuo inde ita appellatur, ex quo ab Abrahamo ita vocatus est locus, Gen. 30, 48. Cu- mulus iste testis inter me & te הַיּוֹם id est, in perpe- tuum. Deut. 4, 39. Scies הַיּוֹם & reduces ad cor tuum id est, perpetuo. Psal. 95, 7. הַיּוֹם hodie, id est, semper, quando vocem DEI audiveritis. Quo de Ebr. 3, 7. ἄχρις ὗ σήμερον καλεῖται, quamdiu hodie vocatur. Ideo c. 4, 7. seqq. illud הַיּוֹם dicitur complecti perennem Sanctorum Sabbatismum. Vid. etiam Matth. 6, 11. Nam & illud σήμερον de perpetuatione divinæ sustentationis accipi potest, quamdiu hodie vocatur. Nonnunquam æternitatem ipsam desi- gnat, utpote Esa. 43, 13. Etiam הַיּוֹם ab hodie ego ipse, id est, ab æterno. LXX. reddunt ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, quo etiam æternitas indicari solet: vid. 1. Job. 1, 1. 2. Sic ergo quod secundo loco notari velim, il- lud הַיּוֹם pro substratæ materiæ conditione expli- candum. Quum etiam hic de Deo Patre, actuque ejus interno, seu intra essentiæ divinæ complexum facto, æterni Filii generatione, sermo sit, non potest illud הַיּוֹם aliter, quam per æternitatem explicari. Actus enim Dei interni æterni sunt, & generatio illa vere ἄχρονος est, imo ὑπέρχρονος & ἀΐδιος, carens omni παραλλαγῇ aut τροπῆς ἀποσκιάσμα- τι. Jac. 1. vers. 17. Qualis autem generatio, talis etiam duratio est, per illud הַיּוֹם denotata. ὁ Θεὸς ἄχρο- νος ὢν καὶ ἄναρχος καὶ ἀπαθὴς καὶ ἄῤῥευστος καὶ ἀσώματος, καὶ μόνος, ἀτελεύτητος ἀχρό- νως, καὶ ἀνάρχως, καὶ ἀῤῥεύσως, καὶ ἀπαθῶς γεννᾷ, καὶ ἐκτὸς συνδυασμῦ, ait Damasc. lib. 1. de Orthod. Fid. c. 8. Quia agitur de productione substantiali DEI Patris, qua ex ipsa essentia sua ge- neravit Filium, quod proprietas vocis Filii, & verbi ילד infert, extra omne tempus illam generationem factam esse oportet, in æternitatis purissimo & suc- cessionis ac vicissitudinis nescio statu, uti æterna & supra & extra omne tempus posita est ipsa divina substantia. (3.) Neque vero inconveniens est vox illa explicandæ æternæ generationi: siquidem omne tempus secludat, sive præteritum nominetur, sive futurum, & constans perpetuo atque fixum hodie, seclusis temporum intervallis insinuet. Sic Augu- stinus de quinque hærefib. c. 4. Apud Deum nun- quam crastinus, nunquam hesternus dies est, sed sem- per HODIE. Neque temere hic dimittendum ar- gumentum B. Lutheri T. V. Jen. Latin. h. l. Si ut res est loqui velimus, hodie, quotidie & semper nascitur, & natus est Filius Dei. Nam æternitas neq́; præteri- tum neque futuram habet. Ad hunc modum acci- pienda particula hodie est, pro tempore sc. Dei, non nostro. Non enim nobiscum loquitur Deus, sed cum illo, qui est extra tempus apud Deum. Nos habemus ista temporum discrimina, ut aliud sit hodie, aliud heri, aliud cras. Hanc differentiam nescit æternitas, ubi nullum est tempus, neq́; præteritum neq́; futurum, sed perpetuum hodie, sicut Petrus dicit, unus dies apud Dominum sicut mille anni, & mille anni sic- ut unus dies. (4.) Ita explicandum est illud הַיּוֹם ut conveniat Filio, per quem secula condita sunt, ante se- cula existenti Ebr. 1, 3. qui est imago Patris invisibi- lis, & extitit priusquam quicquam extitit, Col. 1, 14. 16. uti generatio Filii Dei æterna omnino anteces- sit seculorum ποίησιν, omniumq; cum invisibilium tum visibilium ὕπαρξιν. De illa generatione hic agitur, quæ facit, ut Filius in illo hodie genitus sit æter- ni throni Deus, & Dominus ille qui in initio funda- vit terram, & cujus manuum opera sunt cœli, ut li- quet ex Ebr. 1, 6. 10. utque infinitis parasangis Ange- lis eminentior sit, utpote a quibus omnibus adoran- dus est, v. 6. Non ergo Filius eo dicitur sensu, quo filii dicuntur Angeli, nec generatio ejus in tempore facta, uti Angeli Filii DEI facti sunt in tempore, sed illud הַיּוֹם omne tempus transcendit, omnia se- cula supergreditur, & antecedit. (5.) Illud הַיּוֹם op- ponitur temporalibus machinationibus hostium, non quorundam aut certorum, sed omnium temporum, inde ab ipsius Ecclesiæ primordiis ad consumma- tionem usque seculi, frustra illas omnes adversus Messiam fore, quia persona hæc הַיּוֹם ab æterno ge- nita, antequam consilia ulla cudi possent. Qui ab æternitate omni e simplicissima & incommutabili substantia DEI genitus est, contra illum inaniter meditantur, quicunq; aliquid meditantur, inaniter fremunt, quotquot fremunt. (6.) Actus ille gene- rationis divinus ordine antecedit decretum divi- num de Christo ungendo, quod quia æternum est, actum generationis etiam æternum esse oportet: ac proinde ita illud הַיּוֹם non aliter explicandum. (7.) Per actum illum producta est persona infinita, immensa, omnipræsens, quæ gentes hæreditario jure obtinet, & fines orbis terræ tanquam possessionem suam occupat; ad quod requiritur infinita poten- tia, omniscentia & omnipræsentia, infinitum & di- vinum regimen. Ideo Ebr. 1, 2. 3. 15. qui constitutus est κληρονόμος πάντων, dicitur φέρων τὰ πάντα τῷ ῥήματι τῆς δυνάμεως αὑτõ. Non ergo actus tempo- ralis generationis intelligi potest: Hæc enim seu propria seu impropria intelligatur, semper tantum personam finitam infert. Quanquam autem datio hæc possessionis istius in tempore facta sit, quia facta prævia postulatione Joh. 17, 5. adeoque humanæ na- turæ in Christo competat, tanquam ὑπερύψωσις, & βελτίωσις divina, quia tamen naturæ humanæ as- sumtæ non competit ex naturalibus principiis, sed ex personæ, cui hæc humana natura quasi implanta- ta est, infinitate & majestate, ideoque invictum & inconcussum hoc manet, quod ea persona, quæ omnes gentes & fines orbis terrarum possidere & gubernare divino regimine potest, sit infinita, im- mensa, & omnipræsens. Quod commode monet D. Dn. Dorscheus noster in Disp. super Ps. 2, 7. de æterna generatione Filii Dei §. 51. quæ Pentadeca- de dissert. ejus continetur, qua etiam argumen- tum præsens copiosius exequutus est. (8.) Deni- que actus ille generationis, per quem producta est persona adorabilis, vel cui majestas religiosæ adora- tionis competit, vere divina, atque infinita, non po- tuit in temporali היום fieri, sed ab æterno factus sit, oportet. Personam enim infinitæ ac divinæ maje- statis temporale essendi habere principium, repu- gnat. At talis actus ille est, quia vi hujus generatio- nis Filius ille prognatus est, cui αξιωμα religio- sæ adorationis convenit. Osculamini Filium: & beati omnes, qui confidunt in eo. His ergo argu- mentis inducti Catholici Doctores de æterna ge- neratione verba hæc acceperunt, atque etiamnum accipiunt. Quod scil. hodie perpetuum & sempiter- num intelligatur, sine præterito ac futuro, νυν æter- num & immutabile, omnis fluxus, successionis, ac va- riationis expers. Quam sententiam adversus Arianos, temporalem actum intelligentes, de- fendunt: a quibus cum recedit, ac Arianorum cau- sam agit Grotius, viderint quicunque ei patroci- nantur, cujus Spiritus ipse filius sit? Augustinus in hunc locum ita habet: Quamquam etiam possit ille dies in Prophetia videri, quo vel Christus secun- dum Scripturam natus est, tamen hodie quia præsen- tiam significat, atq; in æternitate nec præteritum quic- quam est, quasi esse desierit, nec futurum, quasi non- dum sit, sed præsens tantum, quia quicquid æternum est, semper est: divinitus accipitur secundum id di- ctum, hodie genui te, quo sempiternam generationem virtutis & sapientiæ Dei, qui est unigenitus Filius, fi- des sincerissima & Catholica prædicat. Confer eun- dem Augustinum Enchir. ad Laur. c. 45. Tertull. c. Prax. cap. 11. Athanasium Orat. contr. Arian. & in Decret. Nic. Syn. Cyrillum Alexandr. l. 9. The- saur. Ambrosium in Epist. ad Ebr. qui citra dubi- tationem de æterna generatione explicant. Cur vero hic aures Grotius præbere maluit Enjedi- no & Socino, aut Rabbinis, quam S. Augusti- no, aliisque Ecclesiæ Doctoribus? Judæi enim, ut notum est, eodem modo interpretantur, uti Grotius, quod David tunc genitus fuerit, ac quasi renatus, quando ex maximis periculis ereptus est, & in regio solio collocatus.

Quod vero ad applicationem Act. 13. & Ebr. 5. factum: non opus est, ut cum Papistis diver- sos sensus literales fingamus ejusdem dicti, quem- admodum Salmeroni Tom. I. comment. in Nov. Testam. proleg. 7. Bellarmino item, Schware- zio, Gregorio de Valentia, Blasio de Viegas, Vas- quezio, Molinæ & Lorino de æterna generatione, de incarnatione ac de resurrectione Christi simul hunc locum interpretari placuit: Sanctio vero in Acta pag. 268. imo etiam Lorino in hunc lo- cum visum fuit, locum hunc de productione quo- que in utero B. Mariæ virginis explicare.

Quem- admodum cujusvis dicti non est nisi unicus lite- ralis sensus, ita hic non nisi de æterna genera- tione Filii Dei agi, jam ostendimus; imo agno- scit Lorinus ipse, minus liberum esse, hæc ver- ba Psal. 2, 7. de alia, quam æterna generatione ex- plicare: negantque aperte Cajetanus, Sixtus Se- nensis L. VII. Bibl. S. hæref. VIII. & XI. & Ge- nebrardus, ea de resurrectione accipi debere, quamvis resurrectionis certitudo & necessitas ex æternæ generationis majestate concludatur: ac refellit Riebera in Comment. ad Ebr. 1. pag. 71. illos in Schola sua, qui de resurrectione eundem intelligunt.

Non diffitemur sane, Chrysosto- mum & Fulgentium ea ad mysterium incarnationis referre: quem sensum secundarium admittit quo- que B. Ægydius Hunnius in Anti-Par. altero, qua Christo homini nomen Filii DEI obtigit, per unio- nem, quatenus humanitas ejus in κοινωνίαν venit hujus personæ, quæ ab æterno a Patre genita est sed negat ita ad nudam temporalem nativitatem accommodari. Non aliter, inquit, pag. 72. ora- culum ad incarnationem vel potest accommodari, vel debet; quam quia per unionem hypostaticam humana Christi natura ex virgine sumta in unita- tem & ταυτότητα pervenit ejus hypostasis, quæ a Patre est extra tempus genita, ita ut nunc etiam ad assumtum hominem ob personalem unionem spe- ctet elogium: Filius meus es tu; Ego hodie ge- nui te: cum sit unus Filius DEI & virginis, per- sona & filiatione prorsus indivisus. Itaque si quæ- ram, cur homo nuper ex virgine sumtus, est & di- citur Filius Dei? Num simpliciter ob hanc tempo- ralem ex Maria nativitatem? Respondetur, non ideo simpliciter, alias non esset ἀπάτωρ ratione hu- manæ nativitatis, quod absurdum, & testimonio Epistolæ ad Hebræos cap. 7. contrarium est. Ex altiori autem principio hæc hominis Christi gloria dependet, quia videlicet Christus ratione humani- tatis assumtæ est unum ὑφιςάμενον cum eo, imo se- cundum hypostasin ipse idem, quem secundum ora- culum Davidis Pater ab æterno genuit. Hæc B. Ægydius Hunnius. Atque ea ratione applicat quoque Augustinus in Enchir. ad Laurent. c. 49. Unde vox illa Patris, quæ super baptizatum fa- cta est (Ego hodie genui te) non unum illum temporis diem, quo baptizatus est, sed immuta- bilis æternitatis ostendit, ut hominem illum ad uni- genti personam pertinere monstraret: ubi enim dies nec hodierni fine inchoatur, nec initio crastini terminatur, semper hodiernus est. Sic ergo sal- va propria & nativa verborum Davidis sententia accommodari ad incarnationem verba illa pos- sent: quemadmodum nonnulli cum Beda in Act. Apostol. locum Davidis Actor. 13. non ad resur- rectionem, sed ad excitationem & missionem Mes- siæ applicari censent; quod etiam B. Gerhardo in Exegef. Tom. I. Loc. Theol. pag. 1176. pla- cuit, non quod verbum gignere sit novo quodam modo in lucem proferre, uti vult Rivetus, & Be- zam ac Junium in eam sententiam laudat, sed ut retineatur propria verbi significatio, de produ- ctione ex substantia, & sententia accommode- tur solum ad nativitatem temporalem, quia Chri- stus homo idem elogium consequutus est. Alii Actor. 13. verba Davidis admittunt adduci ad pro- bandam resurrectionem Christi a mortuis: Sed ut pariter germanus sensus de æterna generatione sup- ponatur, non excludatur: utque doceatur in re- surrectione solum φανέρωσιν vel manifestationem factam esse æternæ generationis Rom. 1. vers. 4. Quemadmodum in Scripturis res interdum tum fieri dicuntur cum manifestæ fiunt: vel ut dica- tur Apostolum ex Deitate personæ per immotam consequentiam demonstrare, resurgere Christum oportuisse ex mortuis, quemadmodum B. Hun- nius in Calvino Judaiz. pag. 23. declarat: Quod enim ex hoc Psalmi versiculo Paulus Christi resur- rectionem evincit, hoc ipso personæ resurgentis æter- nam Deitatem verbis Psalmi celebratam ut funda- mentum suæ probationis præsupponit: Ob hoc ipsum enim (quod persona hæc, cujus caro ex mortuis resurgens personaliter est propria, est unigenitus DEI Filius hodie in æternitate genitus) impossi- bile est, ut caro ejus vel corruptionem subeat, vel in morte detineatur. Quæ Anti-Par. altero pag. 69. repetuntur, & confirmantur. Proinde ne juxta hanc quidem interpretationem opus est aliena verborum Psaltis interpretatione, qua resurrectio per gignendi verbum expressa sit, quia eidem adaptatur regenerationis nomen Matth. 19. verf. 18. quemadmodum hoc imprudenter conce- dit Socinianis cum Arminianis & Remonstrantibus

Andr. Rivetus in hoc loco pag. 20. neque neces- fum erit, verba illa cum Riveto discerpere, ut nem- pe verba priora, Filius meus es tu, generationem in- ferant æternam, & naturalem: posteriora autem, Ego hodie genui te, generationem exprimant tempo- ralem, improprie & tralatitie sic dictam, qua gignere est novo quodam modo in lucem proferre: illa geni- turam hypostaseos designent, qua persona Patris gignit personam Filii ab æterno, hæc genituram Φανερώσεως, qua Christus manifestatus est Filius DEI in tempore. Quam explicationem utut maxime absurdarn cæ- teris, in gratiam Calvini sui, præfert Rivetus. Quid enim manifestius est, quam quod verba prio- ra Filius meus es tu, per verba posteriora declaren- tur: Ego hodie genui te; quodque eadem ratione dicatur hic Messias Filius Dei, qua ratione dicitur genitus esse a Patre. Quæ cohærentia erit, Fi- lius meus es tu (naturalis, ab æterno ex essentia mea genitus) Ego hodie genui te (olim in plenitudine temporum Te novo quodam modo in lucem proferam per resuscitationem a morte.) Quis non videt ra- tionem filiationis reddi & explicari per verba, ge- nui te, neutiquam autem rem aliquam futuram ipsi prædici? Agnovit certe id Calvinus ipse, ver- ba hæc: Filius meus: & genui te, eodem modo, non diverso, partim proprio, partim improprio acci- pienda esse, ideoque utraque improprie accepit, un- de nova illa τρεβλότητι nullatenus juvari potest Cal- vinus: Ita enim habet glossa Calvini: Filius meus es: Potuit quidem David regii juris intuitu cense- ri Dei Filius, quemadmodum scimus, princeps eo, quod præ aliis excellant, tam Deos, quam Dei Filios vocari: Sed hic Deus singulari elogio DAVIDEM ornans eum non modo supra cunctos mortales, sed & supra Angelos extollit. Quod prudenter ex- pendit Apostolus ad Hebræos cap. 1, 5. dum hoc nulli unquam Angelo fuisse dictum, admonet. Quam- vis enim Angelis inferior esset David, quatenus ta- men gestavit Christi personam, merito illis longe præ- fertur. Sciamus ergo hic Dei Filium non unum quempiam ex multis, sed Dei Filium unigenitum designari, ut solus in cælo & in terra emineat. Quod autem DEUS se UNUM GENUISSE pronunciat, referri debet ad hominum sensum, vel notitiam, DA- VID enim genitus a Deo fuit, dum clare apparuit ejus electio. Hæc Calvinus: e quibus manifestum est, quod dixi, utrumque membrum in hoc versu 7.
