Hunnius recte monuit, insignis iste Psal- mus (admissa Calvini atque Grotii explicatione) non aliter vaticinabitur de Passione Christi, quam illa capita Biblica in priore & posteriore libro Sa- muelis, quibus afflictiones Davidis historice com- memorantur, & erit haec solum utrobique differen- tia, quod historiam de Davide in libris Samuelis alii Prophetae descripserint: historiam autem eandem David ipse Psalmo hoc velut in compendium reda- ctam, sub forma precationis ad Deum proposuerit. Sicut ergo in historia librorum Samuelis, quando narratur, quomodo Saul persecutus sit Davidem, quomodo suis illum exercitibus circumdederit in spelunca Maon &c. sensus nativus, proprius & para- phrasticus sonat de Davide, ET NON DE CHRI- STO: deinde vero vice doctrinae, seu loci commu- nis additur, Davidem gessisse in hisce typum Christi: ita si David in isto Psalmo historice recenset Do- mino, quid ipse sub Saule sit passus, ut Calvinus ac

Grotius contendit, tunc eodem plane modo sensus historicus & Paraphrasticus, & textus proprius ac ge- nuinus attinebit Davidem, ad Christum autem non alia ratione pertinebit Psalmus, quam qua referri ad illum solet historia Davidis 1. Sam. 23. 24. 25. &c. Capp. descripta. An hoc sit tam præclarum oracu- lum conservare sartum tectum, universis, qui amant Christi gloriam, & veritatem diligunt, recto judicio æstimandum, cum B. Hunnio, relinquo.

Sed jam argumentis è textu, & interpretatione in- fallibili N. T. ostendamus, de Solo Messia, neutiquam autem de Davide hic agi, secundum sensum nati- vum, & per verba Hierosaltis directe indicatum.

Primum autem è συνεχεία totius Psalmi certum est, de uno eodemq; subjecto, quod ad nativum sensum at- tinet, hic agi: At in posteriori Psalmi parte, cum ce- lebraturum se nomen Domini recipit, qui passiones suas, & liberationem ex iisdem narrarat, non potest intelligi David, sed necessario fateri oportet, vati- cinium de N. T. ibi haberi, quia præconium illud in Ecclesia MAGNA & per totum terrarum Orbem futu- rum prædicatur: v. 26. seqq. Apud te laus mea in Ec- clesia magna: reminiscentur & convertentur ad Do- minum universi fines terræ: Et adorabunt in conspectu ejus universæ familiæ: quoniam Domini est regnum, & ipse dominabitur gentium: Manducaverunt & adora- verunt omnes pingues terræ: Et anima MEA illi vivet, & SEMEN MEUM serviet illi. Quæ uti docent, de eo- dem subjecto, quod antea quærelas instituit, sermo- nem esse, ita non possunt de Davide intelligi, nec in alio, quam in Messia impleta sunt tempore N. Test. quod agnoscere coactus fuit Calvinus ipse; Fateor quidem, inquit, magnum & celebre fuisse inter vicinas gentes nomen David; sed quantula hæc fuit mundi portio? Adde quod exteros, quibus imperii sui jugum imposuit, nunquam adduxit ad purum Dei cultum. Quare multum abfuit coacta illa servitus, quæ terre- no Regi profanas gentes subjecit, à voluntario pietatis obsequio, quod ex dissipatione ad Dominum eas colli- geret. Et postea: Non enim DUBIUM est, quin conve- niat hic locus cum aliis pluribus vaticiniis, quibus eri- gitur solium Dei, in quo Christus ad gubernandum or- bem præsideat. Et ad vers. 31. Unde iterum colligimus, hic non celebrari Dei gloriam, quæ ex caduco & eva- nido rumore nata ad Gentes pervenerit, sed quæ suis RADIIS MUNDUM illustrabit usque in finem. Hæc Cal- vinus: E quibus ἀναντιῤῥήτως concluditur, in prio- ri parte secundum nativum sensum non agi de Davide, sed de Christo. Quo argumento convinci pariter Judæi possunt, inprimis cum fateantur Messiæ hic v. 31. semen tribui, idque adeo certum ipsis, ut etiam adversus Jesum Nazarenum urgeant, quod, quum ipse liberos nullos habeat, pro Messia haberi non debeat. Non enim, quæ Judæorum cæcitas est, vi- dent, de spirituali semine Messiæ hæc cani: quod eti- am Es. 53, 10. 11. & alibi passim introducitur ac de credentibus per universum terrarum Orbem ab ipso Hieropsalte explicatur: Accensebitur Domino gene- ratio ventura, & annunciabunt cæli Justitiam populo, qui nascetur: quæ fecit Dominus.

Porro querela illa sub initium Psalmi longe gravis- sima, maximeque tragica nuspiam à Davide inge- minata legitur, nuspiam de Davide explicatur, De- us, Deus meus, quare me deseruisti? Nuspiam David conquestus est, se à Deo derelictum, longe à salute sua esse verba delictorum suorum, se diu noctuq; clamaf- se, sed non exauditum esse. Christus autem his ipsis verbis exclamavit in Cruce, Matth. 27, 46. Marc. 15, 34. Eli, Eli lama asabthani: ut sonora voce, dum ita expanso corpore, manibus ac pedibus perfossis pen- deret, hunc Psalmum sibi appropriaret, eaque in eo- dem prædicta fuisse indicaret. Illi ergo, qui his ipsis verbis in gravissima passione sua conquestus fuit, de divina desertione, ac conqueri inter Deo acceptos so- lus necessum habuit, propria esse, nullatenus dubi- tandum est: Dico, soli ipsi convenire hanc querelam, quia ipse solus iræ divinæ pondus, pœnamque cru- ciatuum infernalium, qua nulla major est, desertionis divinæ sustinere nostri loco debuit. Unde omnes fide- les liberi sunt ab execratione, quia ipse pro nobis factus est in ligno Crucis execratio, teste Apost. Galat. 3, 13. Ipsi soli convenit, quod hic legitur v. 5. 6. 7. quia fi- deles in Dominum sperantes liberati sunt, ad Do- minum clamantes salvi facti sunt: Sed ipse impetra- re non poterat, quod tam anxie aliquoties ingemi- nabat, ut transiret nempe calix passionum pro no- bis exantlandarum, ut proinde necessum haberet, bibere ex isto calice, & exclamando in cruce con- queri Deus meus, Deus meus, quare me dereliquisti?

Tertio afflictionem suam ita describit, qui hîc conquestus est, ut per omnia ea Messiæ, neutiquam autem Davidi conveniat. Opponit sese ac suam pas- sionem Patrum afflictioni, ac mala sua longe illis præferenda esse, testatur; neminemque esse, qui se- cum conferri possit: imo se cum aliis comparatum, vermem esse, non hominem: ut Patres tractati adhuc fuerint ceu homines, ipse vero ut vermis tractetur. Quod merito de suis passionibus professus est Mes- sias, qui vermiculo etiam purpureo (voce Ebræa de- signato) in passione cruenta similis factus, & instar vermiculi conteri, ac in sanguine suo mori debuit, & instar serpentis suspendendus in cruce fuit. Conf. Num. 21, 9. Joh. 3, 15.

Quarto dum opprobrium se dicit hominis cujusvis, & contemtum populi, hoc iterum minus congruit Davidi, in Christo autem luculenter impletum fuit, teste Historia Evangelica: qui ab omnis generis ac ordinis hominibus contemtus fuit. Cujus contem- tus & gestus hic v. 8. & verba v. 9. graphice exprimun- tur. Quæ non in Davide, sed in Christo comple- mentum suum habuere. Non enim omnes videntes Davidem, deriserunt ipsum, moveruntque caput. Ubi Davidi dictum, speravit in Domino, eripiat eum, salvumq; faciat eum, quoniam vult eum? At Christo illa non tantum prorsus ita evenerant, prout hic prædixit Christi Spiritus, teste historia passionis, sed hoc ipso etiam vaticinium, secundum sensum nativum adque proprium in Christo completum Evangelistæ non obscure innuunt: Matthæus c. 27. 37. Prætereuntes autem blasphemabant eum MOVENTES CAPITA SUA. Et v. 43. Similiter et principes Sacerdotum illudentes cum scribis & senioribus dicebant: Confidit in Deo, liberet nunc, si vult, eum. Conf. Marc. 15, 29. Luc. 23, 35. ubi emphasin vocis Ebrææ לעג exprimi- tur per vocem ἐξεμυκτήριζον. Quum iidem sarcas- mi, gestusque illudentium hic descripti sint, quos peculiariter exprimere voluit per Evangelistas Sp. S. nullum dubium est, quin ita sonora quasi voce si- gnificarit, in Christo id completum esse, quod in Psalmo prædictum. Quale quid de Davide nuspi- am reperitur. Non enim tantum in genere sannis & illusionibus sese exponendum conqueritur, qui hæc ex persona sua fatur, sed speciatim gestus, illu- siones, & sarcasmos verborum describit: ne in perso- na erremus, de qua hîc actum fuerit.

Quinto non congruit Davidi descriptio illa fidu- ciæ v. 10. spes mea ab uberibus matris meæ, quæ uni Messiæ propria est. David enim fatetur, se in iniqui- tate conceptum, ac regeneratione per Circumcisi- onis Sacramentum opus habuit, non vero ab utero, & ab uberibus matris spem in Deo collocavit. Chri- stus autem secundum humanam naturam Sanctus est ab utero Luc. 1, 35. Ne dicam hic innui, quod Deus ipsum mirabiliter ex utero produxerit, in stabulo, ubi aliarum muliercularum aberant mini- steria: & quod, cum mater esset virgo, tamen de Lacte ipsi in uberibus matris prospexerit, quod ob- servatum à B. Tarnovio.

Sexto descriptio hostium v. 13. & seqq. ea est, quæ non satis Davidi conveniat, in Messia autem per omnia complementum fortita sit: Circumdederunt me vituli multi, tauri pingues obsederunt me: aperue- runt super me os suum, sicut Leo rapiens & rugiens. Hostium copiam, ferotiam, potentiam taurorum, crudelitatem ac nocendi ardorem leonis similitudine descripsit. Quæ quod in hostes Christi conveniant exactissime, Historia Evangelica luculenter testa- tur. Copia eorum magna fuit: Ex ordine Sacerdo- tali Pontifices & Pharisæi erant: è Politico, Hero- des & Pilatus cum satellitibus & carnificum turma, denique plebs indomita: Ferocia vere vitulina & taurina, quia instar tauri juvenci supra modum cor- nibus suis fidebant hostes, atque ferociebant: Poten- tia insignis, siquidem non eminus tantum minati sunt, sed in suam potestatem ipsum redegerunt, ac undique circumdederunt, ut elabi non posset. Cru- delitatem Leoninam referebant: quia adversus Chri- stum os suum aperiebant, ut eundem prædæ instar devorarent, aut diriperent.

Septimo passionum & cruciatuum suorum magni- tudinem ac multitudinem graphice hic depinxisse Christum v. 15. 16. res ipsa docet. Quomodo autem ea Davidi peculiariter congruant, non apparet. Pas- siones quas corpore & animâ sustinuit Christus, quo- modo Caro, Ossa, Cor, viriditas linguæ, totus denique ipse contabuerit, manus ac pedes confossi, omnia ossa at- que articuli distenti sint, graphice describuntur: sicut aqua effusus sum, inquit v. 15. quo copiosa sanguinis ejus notatur profusio. Conf. Ps. 79. 3. Et separave- runt omnia ossa mea, quo ossium Christi disparatio & luxatio, potissimum in crucifixione facta: Fuit cor meum sicut cera liquefacta in medio viscerum meorum: quo cordis Christi mortifera liquefactio, ejusdem- que per lanceam apertio, viscerum interiorum, epa- tis, pulmonum & aliorum defectio significata v. 6. Aruit tanquam testa fortitudo mea, quo virium ani- mæ ipsiusque humoris radicalis arefactio: Et lingua mea adhærens faucibus meis, quo vocis ob æstum iræ divinæ, & consternationem summam ademtio; Et in pulverem mortis deduxisti me: quo totalis vitæ privatio designatur. Hæc omnia exacte Christi pas- sionibus congruunt: Davidis non item, qui neque sanguinem profudit, neque ossium disparationem, cor- dis liquefactionem, virium arefactionem, nedum to- talem vitæ privationem in persecutionibus Saulis sensit: sed ex iisdem salvus eluctatus est.

Octavo speciatim observanda Crucifixionis Christi designatio, quæ v. 17. subjungitur. Secundum B. Gef- nerum v. 17. 18. 19. brevis totius historiæ Passionis de- scriptio habetur, quæ in tres actus potest distribui secundum tria loca, Hortum, Urbem & locum suppli- cii. Primum est proditio & captio in horto, de qua dicit: canes circumdederunt me, ceu cervam matuti- nam, ut ministri Sacerdotum & lictores canibus ve- naticis comparentur. Alter actus in urbe partim coram Hanna & Caipha, Pontifice, partim coram Pilato Præside ita exprimitur: Congregatio malignan- tium cinxit me: quia עדה concionem notat, quæ edi- cto publico convenit, & συναγωγὴ à LXX. vertitur. Tertius extra urbem, in loco Calvariæ, ubi primum manus & pedes Christi clavis transfixerunt, tum te- nerrimum & sanctissimum Christi corpus in cruce usque adeo expanderunt, ut omnia ossa, & costas dinumerare posset. Porro suspenso in Crucem ocu- lis luridis, animis æstuantibus, ἐπιχαιρεκακίᾳ Dia- bolica illuserint. Ipsi intuebuntur & aspicent me. De- nique milites vestimenta ejus diviserint, & super tu- -nicam sortem projecerint. Quæ omnia peculiares ἀποδείξεις administrant pro sensu literali de Christo, adversus sensum literalem de Davide: quum omnia secundum nativum sensum in illo, non in hoc imple- ta sint. Sed imprimis hìc genus supplicii urgendum. De eo enim supplicio, de ea passione secundum sen- sum nativum agitur, quæ transfixionem manuum ac pedum infert, corporisque totius eam expansionem, ut ossa omnia dinumerari possint: At tali supplicio, aut passioni David obnoxius non fuit, sed Christus: Quapropter secundum sensum Psalmi nativum non de Davide, sed de Christo hic agi, certum est.

Nonum etiam hic argumentum sub manu nasci- tur, idque ἀδιάλυτον. De eo hic agitur secundum germanum & nativum Hieropsaltis sensum, cujus vestimenta sibi diviserunt hostes, & super cujus tu- nicam sortem projecerunt. Ad Metaphoras enim abeundum hic esse, nulla cogit necessitas. Utrum- que autem sensum & metaphoricum & proprium eo- dem in loco figere non concedendum, nisi è scri- pturis oracula Delphica facere velimus. Et notan- da hic distincta illa tunicæ ac vestimentorum reliquo- rum denominatio, actusque distincti circa eadem probe observandi, quæ in metaphora distinguere non licet: Frustra autem à S. S. talem distinctionem hic factam esse censendum non est, quum temere ni- hil in Sacr. literis positum sit. Jam vestimenta Messiæ hostes sibi diviserunt; tunicam vero, quia inconsuti- lis erat, non diviserunt, sed sortem super eandem proje- cerunt, teste Historia Evangelica: quale quid de Davide nuspiam commemoratur. Accedit argumen- to huic robur ab ipsa S. S. explicatione: Ne enim ambigere quis adhuc possit, in Christi passione id impletum esse, en testes omni exceptione superio- res S. Johannem c, 19, 23. sqq. nec non S. Matthæum c. 27, 35. Milites ergo cum crucifixissent eum, acceperunt vestimenta ejus, (& fecerunt quatuor partes, unicuique militi partem) & tunicam. Erat autem tunica incon- sutilis & desuper contexta per totum. Dixerunt ergo ad invicem: non scindamus eam, sed sortiamur de illa, cujus sit. Cur hæc minutula tam operose? Cur ab omnibus quatuor Evangelistis illa vestimentorum partitio & de tunica sortitio descripta, nisi ut im- pletum agnosceretur Davidis vaticinium, quod proinde addidit expresse cum Matthæo S. Johan- nes, ut Scriptura impleretur, dicens: partiti sunt vesti- menta mea sibi, & in tunicam meam miserunt sortem. Hæc quum tam luculenter in Christo impleta nar- rentur, annon detestanda σρεβλότης Calvini atque Grotii, verba, quæ ex Regula bonæ interpretatio- nis, & juxta S. S. interpretationem proprie accipi- enda sunt, figurate intelligentium, quæ secundum Evangelistas de Christo agunt, ad Davidem detor- quentium, & hunc sensum suum metaphoricum pro germano & nativo venditantium?

Decimo precatio, quæ subjungitur passionum enarrationi, Christo magis convenit, quam Davidi v. 20. seqq. qua à framea in morte vita meripi, & ex ore Leonis infernalis liberari petit, nec non à cornibus unicorum, h. e. à potentia elatorum & superbienti- um hostium. Cogitandum enim hic subjectum cervam esse matutinam, expositam tum leonis infer- nalis, tum hostium corporalium potestati, animoque sistendum summum, quod hic, tanto verborum ap- paratu, describitur periculum, & manifestum erit, longe rectius hæc quadrare Messiæ, quam Davidi, cujus crux jugum & onus leve fuit, si comparetur cum Christi cruce. Neque uspiam David Cervæ comparatur: Christum autem Cervo comparari è Cantic. 2, 9. constat: Similis est dilectus meus Capreæ, hinnuloque cervorum. Quod vero hic cervam potius in fœminino genere inducere voluit David, id procul dubio ideo factum, B. Gesnero judice, quia Chri- stum plane infirmum, omni auxilio destitutum tempore passionis describere, & ingentem ejus amorem erga genus humanum per vehementem cervæ ςοργὴν adumbrare voluit. Chaldæus exposuit de holocausto matutino: quo passionem Christi ad- umbratam fuisse, ex Epistola ad Ebræos penes Christianos indubium est, quem fideli mente ut foverent, Judæi singulis diebus mane dicuntur hunc Psalmum recitasse, utpote vaticinium de pas- sione Christi, quo in V. T. nullum reperitur evi- dentius, in quo non tam Prophetiam, quam historiam tradi Cassiodorus monuit, ob quam etiam causam frequenter præteritum pro futuro in hoc Psalmo ad- hibitum, ut non tam in futura vaticinando prospe- xisse, quam in rem præsentem attendendo oculos, calamumque Hieropsaltes defixisse videatur.

Undecimo gratiarum actio, pro liberatione, quæ in altera parte Psalmi subjungitur, non Davidi, sed Christo convenit: qui recipit se narraturum no- men Domini universis fratribus suis, in medio Ec- clesiæ laudaturum Dominum, excitans suo exem- plo, & hortatu alios ad eandem pietatem. Qui timetis Dominum, laudate eum, universum semen Ja- cob glorificate eum: Quæ ad totum spirituale semen Jacobi pertinent Rom. 9, 7. 8. Gal. 4, 21. c. 6, 16. Non enim David æque in medio Ecclesiæ fratribus no- men Domini narravit, & omne semen Jacobi sic excitavit; Et materia laudum divinarum, quam hic proponit, universalis est, omnes concernens, quo- niam non sprevit, neq; despexit Deus afflictionem affli- cti, neq; avertit faciem suam ab illo, quæ ex persona Messiæ omnibus merito proponitur, sive quod credentibus hæc prima & præcipua sit divinæ lau- dis materia, quam è passione & liberatione Christi habent, sive quod ea fundamentum, & causa meri- toria sit exauditionis omnium afflictorum. Tum etiam Spiritualis illa pauperum vel mansuetorum sa- turatio, qua donis Dei replendi ad satietatem sunt. Edent pauperes & saturabuntur, cum celebratione Domini conjuncta, regno Messiæ peculiariter vin- dicatur Es. 55, 2. Matth. 5, 6. Joh. 4, 14. c. 6, 27. Rom. 14, 17. Suavissimum fidelium epulum est ab carne cervæ hujus matutinæ, quæ pro vita mundi morti exposita Joh. 6, 54. inde vivent corda nostra in secu- lum seculi. Hoc nomine prædicitur hic conversio gentium, ut manducent & adorent etiam omnes pin- gues terræ, cum omnibus qui descendunt in terram (magnates & infimates,) ut semen spirituale, ex Ju- dæis & gentibus, Domino accenseatur, in quavis ge- neratione usq; ad finem seculi, veniatque qui annunciet justitiam Evangelicam populo nascituro ac conver- tendo, quod IPSE FACIAT, quod ab ipso initium, medium & complementum salutis sit. Quæ summam exhibent concionum Evangelicarum, & fructum passionis Christi, ac penes Interpp. Orthodoxos explicata videri possunt. Ne autem ullum supersit dubium, præconem hic laudum Domini sisti Chri- stum, Apostolum testem locupletissimum habemus Ebr. 2, 12. qui hæc non de Davide, sed de Christo pa- lam apud Ebræos explicat, unde dubitare non li- cet, quin eo tempore penes Ebræos indubium fue- rit, Psalmum præsentem de Christo intelligendum esse. Propter quam causam non confunditur, fratres eos vocare, dicens: Nuntiabo nomen tuum fratribus meis: in medio Ecclesiæ laudabo te. Ad dies Christi etiam refert R. Salomo ad v. 29. Domini est regnum: In diebus Christi revertetur regnum Domino, & libe- ratione populo suo innotesiet.

Duodecimo & postremo id quodque cum B. Hun- nio urgemus, quod ne uno quidem argumento vel ad speciem probari possit, Prophetam suas hic ca- nere adversitates, quas sub Saule aliisve hostibus perpessus est, unde communi suffragio interpretes veteres, & recentiores Psalmum non ad Davidis afflictiones, sed citra typum ad solius Christi pas- sionem referunt; cujus summam ita Theodoretus comprehendit: Hic Psalmus Christi crucem & re- surrectionem, & gentium vocationem, & totius orbis salutem prædicit. De Christo unice eundem agere ac passiones non Davidis, sed Mesiæ describere, antiquissimi Patrum, inter Græcos Justinus Dial. c. Tryph. inter Latinos Tertull. advers. Jud. c. 10. docuere, cujus verba adscribere libet: Si adhuc quæres, ait, Dominicæ crucis prædicationem, satis jam poterit tibi facere vigesimus primus Psalmus, totam Christi continens passionem, canentis jam tum suam gloriam. Aurelio Cassiodoro tam luculentus hac in causa visus est Psalmus præsens, ut historiam sibi scriptam videri, non Prophetiam dixerit. Neque fa- cile quis in antiquitate invenietur dubium movisse, nisi Theodorus Mopsuestenus, quem Leontius for- te Byzantius refert omnes Psalmos Judaice exposuisse tribus saltim ad Christum applicatis: Sed is damna- tus ideo est in V. Concil. Constantin. ut & in Synodo Roman. sub Vigilio. De cætero unanimi sententia Interpp. Christiani de Christo Psalmum exposue- re, & quidem ita, ut ipsius solum passiones, non Davidis, describi crediderint, tum ob Psalmi evi- dentiam, tum ob Apostolica testimonia: Hæc enim, uti graviter Brentius, debent nobis esse certiora, quam si Angelus de cælo, nedum vanus quispiam & excæca- tus Rabbinus nobis aliud somniet. Judæos, & Judai- zantes nostros, Calvinum ac Grotium, utpote nul- lo prorsus fundamento nitentes, sed ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν sequentes, imo Christo & Apostolis, ipsisque verbis Psalmi clarissimis palam contradicentes, nemo pi- us ac cordatus morabitur. Nec inveniunt illi in suis commentis, ubi pedem figant: Grotius calamitates profugi sub Saule Davidis describi vult: Calvinus non unam modo persequutionem, sed quascunque passus est, comprehendi. E Judæis vero etsi nonnul- li de Davide, quando à Saule fugiebat, explicent, plerique tamen agnoscunt, Davidi hæc non conve- nire, adeoque vel de persequutione sub Hamane, vel de captivitate Babylonica, vel de Ecclesia præsente Ju- daica, quæ obscura nunc ac deserta jacet, ut è R. Da- vid Kimchio patet, interpretantur. Rursus quum videat Calvinus ad Christum nonnulla omnino re- ferenda esse, Davidem ut typum Christi spectari vult, perabsurde quædam de solo Christo explicans, alia de utroque: quum non nisi unum subjectum Psal- mi sit. Postulat enim, uti Piscator ipse monet, se- ries sermonis, ut si una aliqua particula Davidi tan- quam typo accommodetur, reliquæ omnes eidem ac- commodentur, id quod veritas historiæ non patitur. Grotius vero geminum etiam sensum fingit, sed quanta in hoc commento absurditas sit, jam osten- sum. Ita nullam habere possunt certitudinem, qui à nativa S. S. discedunt sententia, quæ sola certa est, & πληροφορίαν immotam gignit. Sed quid multis, quum ipsius Calvini Discipuli agnoscant, non nisi de Christo Psalmum agere. Nobis Christianis, in- quit Rivetus, in hoc Psalmo non licet dubitare, aut cum Eunucho illo Act. 8, 34. quærere, de quo Propheta hæc omnia dicat, de seipso, an de alio quopiam? Nam testimonia omnium Evangelistarum & Apostoli Pau- li, & ipsius Psalmi verba apertissime evincunt, quæ- cunq; in eo dicuntur, de Christo Domino nostro esse ex- ponenda: ut verbo dicam, si quis quæ sancti Evangeli- stæ scripserunt de passione Domini, conferat eum iis, quæ hoc in Psalmo habentur, apertissime cognoscet, OMNIA ad Christum ita quadrare, ut NULLUS ALIUS sit, cui accommodari possint, & deprehendet, Davi- dem clarissimo illuminationis radio prævidentem ante multa tempora, quæ futura erant, sic quasi præterita descripsisse, atq; ea quidem ita perfecte & distincte ac si- ipse præsens omnia, quæ postea facta sunt, oculis lustras- set. Quamvis vero postea sententiam Calvini, vel potius Buceri e reverentia, ut apparet, erga Præce- ptorem excusare quantenus conetur, eidem ta- men aperte contradicere vi veritatis coactus de- buit: cum hæc adjecit: Sed quia, quamvis ALIQUA EX PARTE E CERTIS VERSIBUS POSSIT ACCOMMO- DARI AD DAVIDEM Psalmi argumentum, MULTA sunt tamen, quæ de ipso INTELLIGI NEQUEUNT, sed quasi PORRECTO DIGITO Christum designant, in priorem sententiam magis propendeo, quod SIM- PLEX sit Psalmi argumentum, & AD CHRISTUM DI- RECTE (sine typo) referatur, ut sit oratio ejus de sua derelictione in cruce conquerentis suorum hostium cru- delitatem, passionumque suarum magnitudinem enar- rantis, pro liberatione postea rogantis, & pro ea pro- mittendis Patri gratiarum actionem & prædicationem nominis ipsius apud omnes gentes, apud quas prædi- cit regnum Dei, veramque religionem illustrandam fore ac declarandam. Ita qui per querimoniam in- cipit, propter derelictionem in cruce, in gaudio ter- minat, propter fidelium ex sua glorificatione conversio- nem & multiplicationem. Hæc Rivetus. Piscator Psalmum hunc Prophetiam continere de passione ac morte Christi, itemque resurrectione ejus ac re- gno spirituali, fatetur, aliosque de Davide eum in- telligentes refutat. Johannes Drusius l. 10. Observ. c. 3. Ego sane, inquit, indubitanter credo, Davidem quum hunc Psalmum componeret, in mente habuisse, quæ ei S. S. patefecerat περὶ τῆ σωτῆρ@ ἡμῶν. Quid- ni credam? Cum Autores habeam Apostolos ipsos, qui testimonia interdum ex eo depromunt. Quin imo Ser- vator ipse usus principio hujus carminis amplius id con- firmat, ut dubitare de eo nisi PLANE IMPIUS nemo possit aut debeat. Vid. etiam Rudolphus Gualtherus, & Franciscus Junius in hunc locum: Quibus novissime addimus consensum Grotii, quod hîc de Messia aga- tur, in annotat. ad Luc. 24. v. 42.

## 22:1
Verse 2. MY GOD MY GOD) The word אֵלִי by itself signifies strength, and in that sense is used of God: for which reason Aquila is accustomed to translate it 'my strong one'.

LOOK UPON ME) Πρόσχες μοι. They took that according to אֵלִי as if it were a preposition with a pronoun signifying 'to me'.

WHY HAST THOU FORSAKEN ME?) לָמָה עֲזַבְתָּנִי, which in Syriac is שְׁבַקְתַּנִי לִמָא, you would rightly translate, 'how long wilt thou forsake me?' for לָמָה is often taken for 'how long,' and past tenses are frequent for future tenses among the Hebrews.

In Hebrew it is אֵלִי אֵלִי לָמָה עֲזַבְתָּנִי, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? Which words Christ repeated on the cross, not in a language then unknown to the Jews, as some Papists prove from this that sacred matters can be treated in an unknown language, but in a publicly known one, the Jerusalem dialect or the Chaldean language. For he did not use the name אֵלִי or אֱלֹהִי but אֱלָהִי as is evident from Mark, nor the Hebrew verb עֲזַבְתָּנִי, but the Chaldean שְׁבַקְתַּנִי, yet he did not repeat these from the Chaldean Targum, as it seemed to Schickard in Beth. Happ. Disp. 1. p. 21, and Hottinger, Thes. Phil. lib. 1. c. 3. p. 255, for in that which exists today of R. Joseph the blind, for λαμὰ there is מטול מה, and there is no evidence that another paraphrase existed then which is now lost. Therefore he translated the Hebrew words of the Psalmist into the received dialect, and without doubt also explained the text of Isaiah in Luke 4 in the same way. By which example we are confirmed that versions of the text into vernacular languages should by no means have been prohibited by the Roman Pontiff. Hackspanius rightly argues here against Vossius that Christ also suffered infernal pains, even though he did not despair: because his despair is only for him who is so deserted that the desertion is eternal. But infernal pains consist mostly in the desertion of God, which he suffered, even if only for a time and indeed a very short one. For if he had not suffered the same, he would not have satisfied for us at all, nor would he have freed us from the pains of hell: Yet he does not rightly assert that those words, 'why hast thou forsaken me,' refer to the petition of Christ, when his mind did not yet seem to have deliberated enough, and that those words, 'let this cup pass from me,' were said by him with a mind as if not yet sufficiently deliberated. For such things are not to be thought of him who is wisdom itself hypostatically, and in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge, upon whom rests the Spirit of counsel and the fear of the Lord without measure, who is also that Holy of Holies, and is not to be thought to do or say anything through imprudence and with a mind not yet sufficiently deliberated. That prayer, which he repeated three times in his most grievous agony, and the words which he exclaimed on the cross, do not argue a mind not sufficiently deliberated, but testify to a most grievous anguish and pain, such as is that of those who feel infernal punishments, in which, however, he did not cast away his trust in his heavenly Father, nor deny the obedience of his soul. He only wished to declare that he was truly suffering infernal pains, and that it was not possible, saving the justice of God, for the redemption of the human race to be consummated otherwise than by drinking that most bitter cup. He did not refuse that cup, because he laid down his soul for us of his own accord, but he testified to the bitterness of the potion and the horror of the flesh sustaining the wrath of God and the sins of the whole world, and at the same time submitted his will to the divine will, 'nevertheless not my will, but thine be done' Luke 22:42. Nor can it consist with most perfect and meritorious obedience that he should have previously resisted with a mind not sufficiently deliberated. For no moment of resistance of the mind can be imagined, where at every moment the most perfect, most consummated, and truly meritorious obedience of the mind must be believed.

Verse of the same. FAR FROM MY SALVATION ARE THE WORDS OF MY TRANSGRESSIONS) It appears that the Greeks, who have οἱ λόγοι τῶν παραπτωμάτων μου without this comma, read שׁוגתי. But the text we use is more correctly שאגתי, which Aquila translates, as he is accustomed, literally: τῶ βρυχήματός μου: Symmachus, not badly as to the sense, τῶ ὀδυρμῶν μου: others, τῆς βοήσεώς μου: others, τῆς δεήσεώς μου. The sense is: You are far from my salvation, and from the words of my groanings, supply: [from] being heard.

Latin:

Vers. 2. DEUS DEUS MEUS) Vox אֵלִי per se for- titudinem significat, & in eo sensu de Deo usurpatur: qua pro- pter Aquila vertere solet ἰσχυρέ με.

RESPICE IN ME) Πρόσχες μοι. Sumserunt illud se- cundum אֵלִי quasi præpositionem cum pronomine signifi- cantem ad me.

QUARE ME DERELIQVISTI? )לָמָה עֲזַבְתָּנִי, quod Syriace est שְׁבַקְתַּנִי לִמָא recte verteris, quous- que me deferes? nam & לָמָה pro quousque sæpe sumitur, & præterita pro futuris apud Hebræos frequentia.

In Ebræo est אֵלִי אֵלִי לָמָה עֲזַבְתָּנִי, Deus meus, Deus meus, quare dereliquisti me? Quæ verba Chri- stus in cruce repetiit, non lingua Judæis tum igno- ta, uti Pontificii nonnulli hinc probant, lingua igno- ta sacra tractari posse, sed publice nota, dialecto Hie- rosolymitana vel lingua Chaldaica. Non enim usus est nomine אֵלִי vel אֱלֹהִי sed אֱלָהִי ut e Marco con- stat, nec verbo עֲזַבְתָּנִי Ebraico, sed Chaldaico שְׁבַקְתָּנִי non tamen e Targum Chald. hæc repetiit, quod Schickard. in Beth. Happ. Disp. 1. p. 21. Hotting. Thes. Phil. lib. 1. c. 3. p. 255. visum, in eo enim quod hodie extat R. Joseph cæci pro λαμὰ habetur מטול מה, aliam autem paraphrasin tum extitisse jam deperditam, nullo indicio constat. Ideo transtulit in dialectum receptam verba Psaltis Ebræa, eadem- que exposuit sine dubio etiam textum Esaïæ Luc. 4. Quo exemplo confirmamur versiones textus in ver- naculas linguas minime prohibendas fuisse a Romano Pontifice. Recte hic adversus Vossium disputat Hackspanius, Christum infernales dolores etiam pas- sum, etsi non desperarit: quia desperatio ejus tantum est, qui ita deseritur, ut æterna sit desertio. Dolores autem infernales maxime in desertione Dei consi- stunt, quam passus est, utut ad tempus tantum & quidem breviufculum. Nam si passus eosdem non fuisset, pro nobis minime satisfecisset, neque nos e doloribus inferni liberasset: Non tamen recte as- serit, verba illa, quare me derelequisti, respicere pe- titionem Christi, cum animus nondum videretur sat deliberasse, atque illa etiam transeat à me calix iste, dicta ab ipso esse, mente quasi nondum satis deli- berata. Non enim talia de illo, qui est ipsa sapientia hypostatica, & in quo reconditi sunt omnes thesau- ri sapientiæ & cognitionis, super quo requiescit ἑκ ἑκ μέτρε Spiritus consilii & timoris Domini cogitan- da, qui Sanctus etiam ille Sanctorum est, nec quic- quam agere aut loqui cogitandus est per impru- dentiam, ac mente nondum satis deliberata. Ora- tio illa, quam trina vice repetiit in agone gravisfi- mo, & verba, quæ in cruce exclamavit, non mentem arguunt haud satis deliberatam, sed angorem & do- lorem testantur longe gravissimum, qualis est eo- rum, qui pœnas infernales sentiunt, in quo tamen non vel fiduciam erga patrem cœlestem deposuit, vel animi obsequium negavit. Solum declarare vo- luit, se vere dolores infernales pati, nec possibile esse salva justitia Dei, aliter, quam epoto isto calice amarissimo, redemtionem generis humani consum- mari. Non renuit calicem illum, quia sponte ani- mam pro nobis posuit, sed amarorem potionis & horrorem carnis sustinentis iram Dei, & peccata to- tius mundi testatus est, & simul submisit voluntatem suam divinæ voluntati, veruntamen non mea volun- tas, sed tua fiat Luc. 22, 42. Nec cum perfectissima & meritoria obedientia consistere potest, quod animo non satis deliberato prius reluctatus sit. Nullum enim momentum reluctationis animi fingi potest, ubi nul- lo non momento credenda est obedientia animi perfectissima, consummatissima, ac vere meritoria.

Vers. eod. LONGE A SALVTE MEA VERBA DELI- CTORUM MEORVM) Apparet Græcos, qui habent οι λόγοι τῶν παραπτωμάτων με sine hujus commatis legisse שׁוגתי. At rectius textus quo utimur שאגתי, quod Aqui- la vertit, ut solet, addictè, τ̃ɤ βρυχήματός με: Symmachus ad sensum non male τῶν ὀδυρμῶν με: alii, τῆς βοήσεώς με : alii : τῆς δεήσεώς με. Sensus est : Longe abes a salute mea, & a ver- bis gemituum meorum, supple exaudiendis.

## 22:7
Verse 8. THEY HAVE SPOKEN WITH LIPS) Properly in Hebrew: They have made a gaping with their lips: which is the custom of those mocking, as appears in Job 16:10, in this very Psalm 4, and 35:21.

Latin:

Vers. 8. LOCVTI SVNT LABIIS) Proprie in Hebræo : Hiatum fecerunt labiis suis : qui mos irridentium, ut apparet Jobi 16. v. 10. hoc ipso Psalmo 4. & 35. v. 21.

## 22:11
Verse 12. DO NOT DEPART FROM ME) Do not remove yourself further from me.

A different reading is feigned in vain. No Hebrew codex has anything about transgressions: and the Hebrew codices and Latin ones agree, not only the more recent ones, Pagninus, Arias, and others, but also Jerome, and indeed the Chaldean, Aquila, Symmachus, Theodosius. Likewise the Fifth and Sixth Greek editions. Therefore, an oversight of the LXX Interpreters must be acknowledged here. And Grotius himself prefers the Hebrew text, and confirms it from other interpretations: But the text we use is more correctly שאגתי, which Aquila translates, as he is accustomed, literally: τῶ βρυχήματός μου. Symmachus, not badly as to the sense, τῶ ὀδυρμῶν μου: others, τῆς βοήσεώς μου: others, τῆς δεήσεώς μου. The sense is, you are far from my salvation, and from the words of my groanings, supply: [from] being heard. These are the words of Grotius.

Latin:

Vers. 12. NEJ DISCESSERIS A ME) Ne longius te a me removeas.

Frustra fingitur diversa lectio. Nullus Ebræus codex de delictus quicquam habet: & consentiunt Ebræi Codices & Latini, non tantum recentiores Pagninus, Arias, alii, sed etiam Hieronymus, imo & Chaldæus, Aquila, Symmachus, Theodosius. Quinta item & Sexta editio Græca. Agnoscendum ergo hic LXX. Interpp. παρόραμα. Et præsert ipse Grotius Ebræum textum, eumque confirmat ex aliis inter- pretationibus: At rectius textus, quo utimur, שאגתי quod Aquila vertit, ut solet, addicte τῶ βρυχήματός με. Symmachus ad sensum non male, τῶν ὀδυρμῶν με: alii τῆς βοήσεώς με: alii τῆς δεήσεώς με.. Sensus est, longe abes à salute mea, & à verbis gemituum meo- rum, supple exaudiendis. Hæc Grotius.

## 22:17
Verse 18. THEY PIERCED MY HANDS AND MY FEET) Here also there was a double reading in antiquity, both of which the Chaldean joined in his version. Jacob Ben Chaiim says that it was כארו by the epenthesis of the letter א. Moses Hadarsan testifies the same. The Masoretes acknowledge that it was so in certain copies. The LXX: ὤρυξαν, in the way Justin and others cite it from them: Aquila: ᾔσχυναν. Therefore, there is no fraud of the Christians here: among whom is also the Ethiopian Interpreter. I see indeed that the Masoretic reading can also be defended. But the other is more suitable for the passage, both for other reasons, and because the comparison to a lion was placed not long before in verse 13.

He assigns a double reading without sufficient cause, which might have been invented in antiquity, by the admission of which the uniquely true reading, which imports the crucifixion and transfixion of the feet and hands, can easily be rendered uncertain. And undoubtedly Grotius tends toward that: so that our proof may not be superior to all doubt. For that reason, he also does not entirely disapprove of the Jews' reading: nay, he says that the same CAN BE DEFENDED. For if the Jewish reading also can be defended, ours will not be indubitably and infallibly certain: at the very least it will have to be held as more probable. Furthermore, Papists argue that the Hebrew text is corrupted because כארי is found in it. Nor does Hackspan deny this. For he says that a letter could easily have been changed into a letter by the fault of the scribes, which others have shown to have happened also in the letters י and ו at other times. He denies indeed that the corruption was made by design, but he does not doubt that it happened by chance and fortune. But the causes brought forward elsewhere are why even that should not be conceded to the Papists, that the corruption was made by the fault or injury of the scribes, which penetrated into all the codices, nor does chance or fortune have a place here, but divine providence must be looked to, which did not permit such a universal corruption of the θεοπνεύστ8 Scripture, nor could it be proven by any example thus far. Nor can this universal corruption be established. For Genebrardus, Pagninus, Vatablus, Andrad., Joh. Isaacus, and others from among the Papists themselves have noted that the best and most ancient copies have כארו, which has also been observed by recent Jews. Compare what has been said in the Critica Sacra concerning the purity of the sources of the Old Testament regarding this passage. Moreover, not even that is to be admitted, that כארו is from a particular, casual corruption, or that a different reading had a place here. A double reading is certainly not proven from the Chaldean translation. Just as this is more recent, and came forth from R. Joseph the Blind about 340 years after the passion of Christ, as Galatinus notes in book 8, chapter 17, of De Arcanis Catholicae Veritatis, so it acknowledges a far more ancient edition, from which the LXX Interpreters drew their translation, whom Grotius confesses to have read and rendered ὤρυξαν along with us. And that anomalous writing כארו could have rendered the Chaldean doubtful, so that he hesitated whether that word ought to be explained as LIKE A LION, or indeed as THEY DUG, and for that reason he combined both explanations, even though a different reading did not exist at that time. For he rendered נכתין היך כאריה אידי ורגלי, that is, they dug, or bit, thus like a Lion my hands and my feet. R. Jacob Chaym, the collector of the Venetian Masoretic work, although he testifies in the final Masora under the letter א that he found in a part of the corrected copies that it was written כתיב כארו, yet he observes that it had been noted in the marginal note קרי that it should be read כארי: Whence by that marginal note that word was restored from the most ancient tradition of the Masora, that it is to be read entirely as כארו, which marginal reading is to be preferred to the textual writing, and is its correction. Add that the same Rabbi observes that he indeed searched in the Masora for those words which are written with a Vau at the end of the word and are read with a Jod, and did not find this word כארו reduced to the number of them, whence it is evident that the same was not written of old with a Vau at the end of the word. As for R. Moses Hadarschan, who is said in Galatinus, book 1 of De Arcanis Catholicae Veritatis, chapter 8, to affirm that the scribes corrected this word and changed it into כארי, not much is to be attributed to him, concerning which one may see the Philologia Sacra of the Lord Dr. Glassius, book 1, tract 1, p. 109. Therefore, that there was a double reading OF OLD will be difficult to prove. And although I am not unaware that the Papists Genebrardus, Pagninus, Vatablus, Andradius, as also Joh. Isaacus defend the reading כארו, and wish to prove by the adduced suffrages of the Jews that the best and most ancient copies have it so, as was warned before, whence also that reading is found in the Complutensian Bibles, and, as the blessed Gerhard testifies in Complem. Harmon. p. 349, in the Jena Library in a manuscript Hebrew Codex: that not a few even of our own and the Reformed arrive at the suspicion that the Jews corrupted this text in certain copies, such as Forsterus, Hunnius, Helvicius, Gesnerus, Schindlerus, Junius likewise, Polanus, Fullerus, etc. Nevertheless, the opinion of those is to be preferred who affirm that that word, as it is now held in the other editions, is to be read כארי, and that this writing and reading is the genuine one, whence no dispute will remain concerning the fraud of the Christians: Since the Christians read it just as the Jews say it is to be read, even if they interpret it otherwise. Nor do I see why Grotius calls that reading Masoretic, since it was not devised by the Masoretes, or substituted in the place of a truer one, but has been guarded as true and genuine, as it must be held entirely. And although I cannot approve in Grotius that he thinks that reading, which he calls MASORETIC, can be defended in the SENSE OF THE JEWS; for in this way, and in this sense, it is a matter of question, since the Jews contend that nothing is held here concerning the transfixing or piercing of the hands and feet of Christ, and the things he added teach that he understands Grotius in this way, in which manner the opinion of the Jews is not to be defended, but entirely rejected; yet we judge that the reading itself, in and of itself, not only can, but even ought to be defended: (1.) Because it cannot be shown by any firm document that that word was read otherwise OF OLD, let alone that any corruption intervenes here in the same Masora at Numbers 24, verse 9. He observes indeed that כתב כארו or that it is written in the text as כארו, but he deals only with certain Codices, and he does not approve of them in the least, which was also observed before concerning R. Jacob Chaym. (2.) Because the small Masora at Numbers 24 notes that the word כארי exists four times, twice with Kametz and twice with Patach; where it is manifest that Psalm 22, verse 17 is also designated, because כארי is read there with Kametz, and so that reading is approved as ANCIENT and genuine. (3.) Because the small Masora at the present passage observes here: There are two in two significations with Kametz, Isaiah 39, verse 13, whence it is evident that כארי was written here of old just as in the place of Isaiah, even if a different signification obtains. (4.) Because the final Masora at the beginning of the letter א [notes] the word כארי in Psalm 22. & Isa. 38. likewise he refers to an Alphabet or Catalogue of those which obtain the same spelling, but a different meaning: (5.) Because R. Jacob Chaym testifies that this word is not found in the number of those which are written with a vau at the end of the word. If therefore it is even admitted that in some copies it had been written כארו, the Masoretes nevertheless did not hold that spelling to be genuine: But they corrected it, and observed that it should be written and read כארו.

Now as regards the meaning of the word כארי and the text itself, that explanation of the Jews is by no means to be conceded: AS A LION MY HANDS AND MY FEET, which in no way, whatever may have seemed right to Grotius in favor of the Jews, CAN be defended: First, because there is no sense in the words rendered in this way: for what is this: As a Lion my hands and my feet? Therefore the Jews acknowledge that another verb must be understood, but in such a way that they do not deserve to be heard, much less defended by Christians. For what is this, they surrounded as a Lion my hands and my feet? They have rendered an absurd explanation of an absurd phrase: R. David Kimchi: As a Lion in a leap makes a circle with its tail, outside of which the beast that sees it does not dare to go out for fear of the Lion; And he says, they surround our hands from fighting, and our feet from fleeing from the midst of Babylon. Then a little before, namely in verse 14, the simile of the Lion had already been used: they opened their mouth against me, AS A LION snatching and roaring. Why then was it relevant to mention here that, like a lion, they surrounded my hands and feet, when he has already expressed something more serious, that like a roaring and snatching lion they opened their mouth. Thirdly, concerning the other surrounding, a comparison is applied in the preceding verse: many dogs have surrounded me, the council of the malignant has besieged me. Therefore, enemies are compared to dogs regarding the surrounding: and they are said to have surrounded him not only regarding his hands and feet, but to have surrounded him on all sides. Fourthly, it does not fit either the phrase of speaking or the history if you say that the hands and feet of the Messiah were surrounded by the Jews as if by a lion. For who speaks thus: to surround hands and feet, and why would a comparison from a lion be applied to the surrounding of hands and feet, if any such thing were to be invented? Finally, what is similar to this leonine surrounding of hands and feet in the history of the passion, whether Davidic or Dominical? Fifthly, since mention is made of the entire council of the malignant by whom he was surrounded, the comparison of ONE LION was not suitable for explaining that surrounding. Sixthly, it is evident from the Masora itself that the word כארי obtains a different meaning here, which it has in Isaiah 38:13. Since, therefore, the meaning AS A LION is certain in Isaiah, it will be necessary to assign another sense to that word in this place. To which opinion both the small Masora on this place and the great final Masora were previously brought forward. But that the piercing of hands and feet is signified here, just as these words are commonly explained, when not only do the Jews deny this sharply, but Grotius also thinks that their opinion can be defended here, we show by these arguments. (1.) From the distinct mention of hands and feet. For since an express and distinct mention of hands and feet is made, it must be that some memorable passion occurred regarding them, which is designated here in the narration of the passions of Christ. But what other kind of afflictions and passions regarding hands and feet can be named, which must have happened to Christ by the force of this prophecy, or which is proven to have happened to him by the event, if indeed it has already been demonstrated that the prophecy here is about the Messiah, if not the piercing or transfixing of hands and feet? (2.) From the subjoined enumeration of bones. Such a passion is indicated here which was joined with the expansion of the body, by which, namely, the body of the Messiah was so extended that the bones could even be numbered. But no other affliction and passion regarding the hands and feet of Christ can be designated than that piercing of hands and feet in the crucifixion, which was joined with that expansion of the body. (3.) From the Jewish explanation of the word כארי. For that word, if it is rendered AS A LION, necessarily requires some verb that fits the passion by which the hands and feet were to be affected. That, indeed, must either be repeated from the previous ones, or elicited from this word, or understood here. If some verb is to be understood with Augustine, Bishop of Chisam, what will be more convenient than either that of piercing or wounding the hands and feet, just as the Chaldean rendered it, they pierced as a lion: and Aquila ἤƷυναν, they defiled, namely by piercing and bloodying. But those who chose to elicit a verb from that word כארי say it is a compound word, from כאר he dug, and ארי lion, with Avenarius, or as it pleased B. Tarnov, they take the same as if it were כארו כארי they dug as a lion, of which one, he says, bears the points, the other the letters. Thus Mr. Dr. Wasmuth in his inaugural dissertation held at Kiel in the year 1666, observes that it is not without cause that the word is applied to the piercing or the immense and savage striking, such as that of lions, being a word composed of both meanings, praising for that opinion the MS. Diatribe of the elder Buxtorf, brought forward by Voet in Select Dissertations, p. 56, that this writing and reading was done not without mystery: since it expresses both the crime itself of the Jews and the quality of the crime, namely their rage: and also the Chaldean interpretation נכתין כאריות they bit as a lion, and a similar exposition of R. Solomon Jarchi: and he thinks similar compound words occur, Gen. 41:43 אַבְרֵךְ from the verb הִבְרִיךְ and the words אַב father, and רַךְ tender: 2 Kings 17:21 וַיַּדֵּא and he turned away most quickly from וַיִּדַּח (the verb being noted in the margin) and וַיֵּדֶא and he caused to fly away (which are the letters of the text) likewise 2 Sam. 16:23, 25, etc. To which, however, others oppose the Masora; inasmuch as it observed that the meaning of the word here is different than in Isaiah 38:13, which argument Mr. Dr. Wasmuth himself urges elsewhere: unless perhaps for this sense it should be replaced that in Isaiah 38 the sense is simple, AS A LION: but here it is compound; and thus so far still different, they dug as a lion: in which way nevertheless it seems to stand in the way that undoubted examples of this compound sense are lacking, nor does it sufficiently fit the simplicity and clarity of Scripture, which hardly suffers ambiguity and a double sense of the same word: unless one prefers to distinguish here between a word that is simply one, and one that is virtually double: because although such a word may seem to be only one, in reality, however, it is not simply one, but rather virtually double, since it is read differently according to the consonants, and differently according to the vowels, and the index of that diversity is the Qere and Ketiv, by which character since those words have been marked by the Holy Scriptures themselves, it cannot cause prejudice to others, and it cannot effect that, as in others, so in those not characterized, some ambiguity or duplicity of sense is established. Arias Montanus favors this opinion (whom Andr. Riv. cites on this place) as does B. Helvicus in Vindication of the Languages of the Old Testament, p. 18, and Nic. Petraeus in the Hebrew Lexicon, 1576. But in it most people rashly assume that this example has no place among the Qerin and Ketivin, of which 848 are counted, but this place is not found in that catalog. Those who call back a word from the preceding, judge that the term הַקּוֹפְוֹנִי ἀπὸ κοινῶ is to be repeated, such as Aben-Ezra, Kimchi, Polanus, Voetius, Pococke, and Leusden in his illustrated Jonah. Which some explain as 'they have pierced me': i.e., the council of the malignant have pierced me; just as 'a lion', I say, 'they have pierced my hands and my feet', or 'they have pierced me, with my hands and my feet': so that it may be from נקר, he cut out, he pierced, which meaning, derived from Arabic, is observed by Pococke in Is. 10:30, 24:3, Job 19:26. To these, however, D. Wasmuth opposes both the accentuation and the Masorah, which does not permit that explanation 'AS A LION', but excludes it. And hence we conclude (4.) From the Masoretic observation. For if, with the Masorah, one prefers to attribute to this word a meaning distinct from the passage in Is. 38:13 (which opinion is altogether to be preferred), the Jewish explanation, 'AS A LION', will be wiped away, but the interpretation of the Christians will be perfectly consistent. For כָּאֲרִי can be derived, with Paul of Burgos, Marco Marini, B. Glassius, Tarnovius, D. Walther, Sixtinus Amama, and others, from כָּרָה, i.e., he pierced or he dug through, so that when it ought ordinarily to be said כָּרוּ, 'they pierced', the א is said to be inserted by ἐπένθεσιν, just as in רָאמָה, 'it shall be exalted', Zech. 14:10 (which was done to indicate the magnitude of the digging, thinks Tarnovius in this place, p. 143); at the end, however, י is placed in the stead of ו, because those letters are εὐμετάβολοι, as in Ezra 10:44, נִשָּׂאי, 'they took', for נָשְׂאוּ: see other examples in Avenarius, book 3, Gram. p. 585, whence in the Royal Codices it is written with the ֹ point כָּאֲרִיֹ as if it were a Yod Shurek, instead of a Vav Shurek, as in Jer. 50:11, which Marco Marini of Brescia in the Arca Noae, fol. 332, calls not a Yod, but a diminished Vau, used specifically for that reason, to clearly intimate the stigmata of the nails of Christ. B. Tarnovius holds that that letter ו, used without a point in so notable a mystery, is intended to indicate at the same time the truculent cruelty and the leonine violence. It seemed to B. Gesner that, with the points changed, it should be read כֹּאֲרֵי in the construct state, i.e., 'the piercers of my hands and my feet'. Which opinion, although not disapproved by B. Gerhard in Harm. passion. c. 13, could not approve itself to B. Tarnovius, p. 144, nor is a correction of points of that kind to be granted, in the judgment of B. Glassius and B. D. Walther. Another explanation of the word with these vowel points was brought forward by Ludovicus de Dieu in his Animadversiones, p. 320, with Nicolaus Fuller leading the way, namely, that the א should be established as being radical, from כאר [he] defiled, just as in the Syriac language כאר signifies to put to shame, as when it is read כָּאֲרוּ it becomes the third person Cal [they] defiled, [they] deformed, which he says agrees with the interpretation of Aquila ᾔσχυναν [they] defiled, and is the same in sense as they dug, for by digging they defiled, (not to mention that Pocock observes that the words כָּאַר & כָּרָה could have been synonyms according to the analogy of the Arabic language) but when it is read כָּארִי it becomes the infinitive Piel כַּאֵר which regularly becomes כַּאֲרִי with the suffix of the first person, the Kametz remaining, because it is worth a Patach followed by a Dagesch, so that it is permissible to translate, by defiling me with my hands and my feet, or by defiling for me my hands and my feet, and it is construed with the preceding preterite, the congregation of evildoers have surrounded me, and as if the infinitive should be taken with the signification of the preterite, in a manner most customary to the Hebrews, where other preterites precede, it ought to be rendered, they have defiled for me my hands and my feet: whence he deems it clear that it is entirely the same, as far as the sense is concerned, whether כָּאֲרוּ or כָּאֲרִי is read. Thus Ludovicus de Dieu. Which opinion could be aided, so that greater probability may be procured for it, if the preceding verb הִקִיפוּנִי were rendered, they pierced me through: For thus a clearer sense will result: they have surrounded me like dogs: The congregation of the malignant have pierced me through by defiling me with my hands and my feet, by foully bloodying [them], or they have defiled for me my hands and my feet, so that a piercing that is very bloody, and joined with notable defilement, may be designated. Thus therefore the act of crucifixion is indicated, whether the verb is understood as derived from כָּרָה or from כָּאַר. To the former etymology, however, the ancient versions of the LXX, the Interpreters of Jerome, the Vulgate, and also the Chaldean, Arabic, Syriac, as well as the Ethiopic, more agree. Unless perhaps one might prefer to call the word COMPOUND, or to prefer the new opinion of Pocock in Porta Mosis p. 59. opinion, that that word descends from כאר, the notion of piercing, derived from the usage of the Arabic language, so that the radical letter א, or one made from a Vau by mutation, has become a Benoni, and the vowels applied are considered to be from the analogy of the word כֹּאפְנָק Hos. 10, 14. & רָאמוֹת Zach. 14, 10. and this number occurs as plural through the apocope of the letter Mem, which is not unusual, as he brings examples from Gen. 40, 16. חוֹרִי, 2. Sam. 20, 38. הַחִצִי, 2. Sam. 23, 8. שְׁלִישִׁי 2. Reg. 11, 4. הַכָּרוֹ, 2. Sam. 24, 44. Thren. 3, 13. עַמִּי &c. Piercing [they] have surrounded me. Which opinion Mr. Pfeiffer approves and confirms in a dissertation held here on this word: as also Alting on the integrity of the word כארי §. 39. Nor do we see any reason why the same should be rejected, especially because Philologists observe with R. David Kimchi in Michlol. f. 35. that א in quiescent verbs is the middle radical, and lies hidden in the Kametz. See Mr. Pfeiffer §. 37. l. c. In which way there is no need to posit an Epenthetic Nun, and only the apocope of the letter Mem will be left, which is quite customary: and this sense is not only the simplest, but also excellently agrees with all the aforesaid versions, above other interpretations. (5.) The explanation of Christian Interpreters is confirmed from the context's connection and order. For since the matter was about the counsels v. 16, which were instituted in the council of the malignant, [and] which the Evangelical History testifies were directed toward the crucifixion, it follows that it is also about the effect, and since the things preceding and following the crucifixion, especially with the division of the garments and the casting of lots for the tunic, are treated so clearly, how could that which is the chief thing in the passion, and almost the head of the rest (I point to the external passions), be wrapped in silence, and the crucifixion itself, which constitutes a peculiar article of faith in the Apostolic Creed, be plainly passed over? Which indeed, since it is best designated by the piercing and boring through of the hands and feet, as that which happened in no other punishment, it is to be believed that it is so indicated here. (6.) From the light of the complement. Since in the review of the passions of Christ mention is made here of the hands and feet, it is sufficiently evident from the event itself that the piercing of the hands and feet, done in the crucifixion, is to be understood. Concerning which the Blessed Luther [spoke] gravely and excellently in Tom. 2. Lat. Jen. Comm. on this Psalm f. 252. For us, who believe in Christ, and hold this whole Psalm to be said of Christ by Evangelical authority, it is easy to prove that it should be read, they dug, not like a Lion. For we do not illustrate the accomplished fact from the mysteries of the Scriptures, but the mysteries of the Scriptures from the accomplished fact, i.e. we illustrate the old Scripture by the Gospel, and not on the contrary compare the sense of this to the sense of that, and we make them look toward Christ, like two Cherubim toward the mercy seat, as Jer. 23 says: in the last days you will understand his counsel. And to Moses: You will see my back parts. Since therefore we have it as certain that Christ's hands and feet were pierced on the cross, and no less certain that this Psalm squares with Christ, and then the sense wonderfully agrees, and altogether demands, that THEY DUG should be read, especially since no rigor of Grammar resists this, without contention and commutation we read they dug. And since most of the circumstances of the crucifixions of Christ were exactly designated by the Spirit of Christ, who was in the Prophets, who would believe that that which is the chief thing in the passion, namely the crucifixion itself, was not signified by the same? (7.) From the agreement and consensus of the translations. For these things were not translated in this way only by Christians. But by the LXX Interpreters themselves, who rendered ὤρυξαν, they dug. And also by the Chaldean Interpreter, who is held in esteem among the Jews. Nor only in recent translations, but in the most ancient ones, such as that of Jerome, who rendered FIXERUNT [they fixed], as also the Vulgate version, which has FODERUNT [they dug], with which, how the translation of Aquila agrees, has been said before. Nor did only the Greeks and Latins explain it thus. The Arabs have the same interpretation in their paraphrase: the Syrians have it, the Ethiopians have it, and others. (8.) From the observation of the Masorah. For since in the Masorah itself, whose authority is great among the Jews, it is held as certain that the word כָּאֲרִי obtains a different meaning here than in Is. 38:13, where it denotes without controversy AS A LION, and since no other meaning can be given than that from כּוּר, they dug, it must certainly be adhered to: or a better explanation must be given. If that [meaning] from כָּאַר, they defiled, be suggested, it has already been shown how that is not opposed to our interpretation, but is in harmony with it. Add that at Num. 24:25, the Masorah notes that in certain codices it was written כָּארוּ, which word cannot be explained as AS A LION. Therefore, our Christian interpretation has a place according to both readings, but the Jewish one does not. To which finally is added (9.) an argument from the collation of the parallel passage Zech. 12:10. They shall look on him whom they pierced; which is applied to the crucifixion of Christ in John 19:37. These things, therefore, also concerning this notable passage.

Latin:

Vers. 18. FODERVNT MANVS MEAS ET PEDES MEOS) Hic quoque duplex fuit antiquitus lectio, quam utramque Chaldæus in versione sua conjunxit. Jacob Ben Chaiim ait, fuisse כארו per epenthesin literæ א. Idem te- statur Moses Hadarsan. In quibusdam exemplaribus sic fuisse agnoscunt Masoretæ. LXX. ὤρυξαν, quomodo ex eis citat Justinus, & alii: Aquila ᾔσχυναν. Nulla ergo hic fraus Christianorum : inter quos est & Interpres Æthiops. Video quidem & Masoreticam lectionem posse defendi. Sed alte- ra loco magis convenit, tum ob alia, tum quia leonis compa- ratio non multo ante posita est v. 13.

Geminam lectionem sine sufficienti causa assi- gnat, quæ antiquitus inventa fuerit, qua admissa fa- cile incerta reddi potest unice vera lectio, quæ cru- cifixionem & transfixionem pedum & manuum impor- tat. Atque eo tendit sine dubio Grotius: ne pro- batio nostra non sit omni dubitatione superior. Idcirco etiam non omnino improbat Judæorum lectionem: imo dicit, eandem DEFENDI POSSE. Si enim Judaica etiam lectio defendi possit, nostra non erit indubitato & infallibiliter certa: saltem pro magis probabili habenda erit. Porro corru- ptum esse textum Ebræum Papistæ arguunt, quod in illo habeatur כארי. Nec abnuit Hackspanius. Facile enim, inquit, litera in literam, culpa scribarum muta- ri potuit, id quod in literis י & ו alias quoq; factum esse alii ostenderunt. De industria quidem factam esse corruptionem negat, casu autem & fortuna accidis- se non dubitat. Sed causæ allatæ alibi sunt, cur nec illud Papistis concedendum sit, quod scribarum cul- pa vel injuria facta sit corruptio, quæ in omnes co- dices penetrarit, neque hic casus vel fortuna locum habet, sed respicienda est divina providentia, quæ non admisit universalem ejusmodi corruptionem Scripturæ θεοπνεύστ8, nec exemplo ullo probari hactenus potuit. Neque hic universalis corruptio stalui potest. Nam optima & antiquissima exem- plaria habere כארו Genebrardus, Pagninus, Vata- blus, Andrad. Joh. Isaacus, & alii è Pontificiis ipsis notarunt, quod etiam à Judæis novellis observa- tum. Conf. quæ in Crit. Sacr. circa puritatem fon- tium V. Test. dicta sunt de hoc loco. Cæterum ne id quidem admittendum, quod כארי sit à corruptione particulari, casuali, aut quod hîc diversa lectio lo- cum habuerit. Non probatur certe gemina lectio e translatione Chaldaica. Hæc uti recentior est, ac post Christi passionem annis ferme 340. notante Galatino l. 8. c. 17. de Arc. Cath. Verit. à R. Joseph cæ- co prodiit, ita antiquiorem longe agnoscit eam edi- tionem, ex qua LXX Interpp. suam translationem depromserunt, quos nobiscum legisse ac reddidisse ideo ὤρυξαν, fatetur Grotius. Et potuit Chaldæum anomala illa scriptio כארו dubium reddidisse, ut, utrum exponi vox illa sIGUT LEO, an vero FODE- RUNT debeat, hæserit, & utramque expositionem ea de causa conjunxerit, etsi tum diversa non exti- terit lectio. Reddidit enim נכתין היך כאריה אידי ורגלי, hoc est, perfoderunt, vel momorderunt sic velut Leo manus meas & pedes meos. R. Jacob Chaym, col- lector operis Masoretici Veneti, etsi in Masora fi- nali testetur litera א, se in parte exemplarium cor- rectorum invenisse כתיב scriptum esse כארו, in marginali tamen nota קרי legendum esse כארי, an- notatum fuisse observat: Unde per notam illam marginalem ex antiquissima Masoræ traditione vox illa restituta fuerit, quod omnino legenda sit כארו, quæ lectio marginalis textuali scriptioni præferen- da, ejusque correctio est. Adde quod observet idem Rabbi, se sane perquisivisse in Masora illas dictiones, quæ scribuntur per Vau in fine dictionis, & leguntur per Jod, & non invenisse hanc vocem כארו in nume- rum illarum redactam, unde constat eandem anti- quitus per Vau in fine dictionis scriptam non fuis- se. Quod ad R. Mosen Hadarschan, qui apud Gala- tinum libro 1. de Arc. Cath. Verit. cap. 8. affirmare dicitur, scribas vocem hanc correxisse, & mutasse in כארי, ei non multum tribuendum, de quo videri poterit Philol. Sacr. Dn. D. Glassii lib. 1. tract. 1. p. 109. Geminam ergo ANTIQUITUS fuisse le- ctionem ægre probabitur. Et quanquam non nesciam Pontificios Genebrardum, Pagninum, Va- tablum, Andradium, ut & Joh. Isaacum lectionem כארו tueri, ac Judæorum adductis suffragiis pro- bare velle, optima & antiquissima exemplaria ita habere, ut antea monitum, unde etiam ea lectio in Bibliis Complutensibus, ac teste B. Gerhardi in Complem. Harmon. p. 349. in Bibliotheca Jenensi manuscr. Codice Ebræo reperitur: non paucos etiam e nostris & Reformatis in eam suspicionem deve- nire, quod in quibusdam exemplaribus Judæ textum hunc corruperint, utpote Forsterus, Hun- nius, Helvicius, Gesnerus, Schindlerus, Junius item, Polan. Fullerus &c. Præferenda tamen eorum est sententia, qui vocem illam, ut nunc in cæteris editionibus habetur כארי legendam, atque hanc scriptionem ac lectionem genuinam esse, affir- mant, unde nulla restabit de fraude Christianorum disputatio: Siquidem ita legunt Christiani, uti Ju- dæi legendum dicunt, etsi aliter interpretentur. Nec video, cur lectionem istam Masoreticam vo- cet Grotius, quum à Masoretis non excogitata, vel in locum verioris substituta, sed ceu vera & germana, uti omnino habenda est, custodita sit. Et quanquam probare non possim in Grotio, quod lectionem illam, quam vocat MASORE- TICAM, SENSU JUDÆORUM defendi posse ar- bitretur; nam ita & hoc sensu, de ea quæstio est, quum contendant Judæi, nihil hic de trans- fixione, vel transfossione manuum & pedum Chri- sti haberi, & ita intelligere Grotium, ea, quæ adjunxit, docent, quo pacto vero non defenden- da, sed omnino reprobanda est Judæorum sen- tentia; ipsam tamen per se lectionem non posse modo, sed debere etiam defendi, censemus: (1.) Quia vocem illam ANTIQUITUS aliter le- ctam fuisse, nullo firmo documento ostendi pot- est, nedum corruptelam aliquam hic interveni- re in eadem Masora ad Numer. 24. vers. 9. Ob- servat quidem כתב כארו seu scriptum in textu esse כארו, sed de quibusdam solum Codicibus agit, eosque minime probat, quod etiam de R. Jacob Chaym antea observatum. (2.) Quia Masora parva ad Numer. 24. notat quater vocem כארי extare, bis cum Kametz & bis cum Patach; ubi manifestum est designari etiam Psalm. 22. vers. 17. quod ibidem כארי cum Kametz legatur, adeoque approbari ita eam lectionem, ut ANTIQUAM & germanam. (3.) Quia Masora parva ad præsentem locum hic observat: Duo sunt in duabus significationibus cum Kametz Esa. 39. vers. 13. unde constat hic æque כארי scriptum olim fuisse, ut in loco Esaiæ, etsi diversa obtineat significatio. (4.) Quia Masora finalis initio litera א vocem כארי in Psalm. 22. & Esa. 38. itidem in illarum refert Alphabetum vel Catalogum, quæ eandem scriptionem, diversam vero significationem obtinent: (5.) Quia testatur R. Jacob Chaym, non inveniri hanc vocem in illarum numero, quæ per vau in fine dictionis scribuntur. Si ergo maxime admittatur in aliquibus exempla- ribus scriptum fuisse כארו, eam tamen scriptio- nem pro genuina non habuere Masoretæ: Sed emendarunt, & כארו scribendum atque legendum esse observarunt.

Jam quod ad significationem vocis כארי & tex- tus ipsius attinet, neutiquam concedenda Judæis illa explicatio: SICUT LEO MANUS MEAS ET PEDES MEOS, quæ nullatenus, quicquid in gratiam Ju- dæorum Grotio visum fuerit, defendi POTEST: Primo, quia nullus verbis ita redditis inest sensus: quid enim hoc est: Sicut Leo manus meas & pedes meos? Ideo verbum aliud subintelligi debere agno- scunt Judæi, sed ita ut audiri non mereantur, ne- dum defendi à Christianis. Quid enim hoc est, circumdederunt sicut Leo manus meas & pedes meos? Absurdæ locutionis magis absurdam reddiderunt explicationem: R. David Kimchi: Sicut Leo in sal- tu cum cauda circulum efficit, extra quem ne bestia, quæ videt eum, præ timore Leonis exire audeat; Et di- cit, circumdant nostras manus à pugnando, & pe- des à fugiendo è medio Babel. Deinde paulo ante, versu nempe 14. jam similitudo Leonis adhibita fuit: aperuerunt super me os suum, SICUT LEO- rapiens & rugiens. Quid ergo attinebat hic commēmo- rari, quod instar Leonis manus & pedes circumdederint, quum gravius quid jam expresserit, quod instar Leonis rugientis & rapientis os suum aperuerint. Tertio de cir- cumdatione alia adhibita similitudo versu præcedenti, cir- cumdederunt me canes multi, concilium malignantium obse- dit me. Canibus ergo quoad circumdationem compa- rantur hostes: neque tantum quoad manus ac pedes cin- xisse ipsum dicuntur, sed undiquaq́ circumdedisse. Quarto non convenit vel phrasi loquendi, vel historiæ, si dicas manus & pedes Messiæ a Judæis, ceu Leone, cir- cumdatos. Quis enim ita loquitur: circumdare manus & pedes, & cur similitudo a Leone adhiberetur, cum ad manuum, tum ad pedum circumdationem, si quæ talis fin- genda? Quid denique simile huic manuum pedumq́ cir- cumdationis leoninæ in historia passionis sive Davidicæ, sive Dominicæ? Quinto quum integri concilii malignan- tium, a quibus circumdatus est, mentio fiat, non con- veniebat similitudo UNIUS LEONIS ad explicandam illam circumsessionem. Sexto ex ipsa Masora constat, aliam significationem hic obtinere vocis כארי, quæ Es. 38,13. Quum ergo apud Esaiam significatio, SICUT LEO, certa sit, necessum erit h. l. alium vocis istius sen- sum assignare. In quam sententiam tum Masora parva ad h. l. tum Masora magna finalis antea adducta fuit. Quod autem hic transfixio manuum & pedum signifi- cetur, quemadmodum communiter verba hæc expli- cantur, quum non Judæi tantum id ἀποτόμως inficien- tur, sed eorum etiam sententiam hic defendi posse au- tumnet Grotius, hisce ostendimus argumentis. (1.) E ma- nuum ac pedum distincta commemoratione. Quum enim expressa & distincta manuum ac pedum mentio fiat, circa illa memorabilem quandam passionem contigisse oportet, quæ hic designetur in passionum Christi enar- ratione. Quod autem aliud nominari potest afflicio- num & passionum genus, circa manus ac pedes, quod Christo contingere debuerit, vi hujus Prophetiæ, aut quod ab eventu ipsi contigisse comprobetur, siquidem demonstratum jam fuerit, de Messia hic Prophetiam haberi, nisi transfixio vel transfossio manuum ac pe- dum? (2.) E subjuncta ossium dinumeratione. Talis hic passio indigitatur, quæ cum expansione corporis fuit conjuncta, qua sc. ita corpus Messiæ extensum, ut ossa etiam dinumerari potuerint. At nulla alia designari po- test circa manus pedesq; Christi afflictio ac passio, quam illa in crucifixione manuum & pedum transfixio, quæ cum ista corporis expansione conjuncta fuerit (3.) E Ju- daica verbi כארי explicatione. Vox enim illa, si reddatur SICUT LEO, necessario requirit aliquod verbum, quod passioni, qua manus ac pedes afficiendi, conveniat. Id vero aut e prioribus repetendum, aut ex hac voce eru- endum, aut hic subintelligendum. Si verbum aliquod cum Augustin. Episc. Chisam. subaudiendum, ecquod erit convenientius, quam vel transfixionis, vel vulnerationis manuum ac pedum, quemadmodum reddidit Chaldæus, transfixerunt sicut Leo: & Aquila ἤƷυναν fædarunt, trans- fodiendo sc. ac cruentando fædarunt. Quibus vero libuit e voce illa כארי eruere verbum, vocem compositam dicunt, ex כאר fodit, & ארי Leo, cum Avenario, vel quod B. Tar- nov. placuit, eandem ita accipiunt, quasi haberetur כארו כארי foderunt ut Leo, quorum unum puncta, alterum lite- ras præ se ferre, ait. Ita Dn. D. Wasmuth in Disp. sua in- augur. Kiloni A. 1666. habita observat, non sine causa adhibitum de perfossione, vel percussione immani & trucu- lenta, qualis est leonum, esse vocem compositam ex utroq́ significatu, laudans in eam sententiam Buxtorffii senioris MS. Diatrib. a Voet. Disp. select. p. 56. adductam, quod hæc scriptio & lectio non sine mysterio facta sit: siqui- dem & facinus ipsum Judæorum exprimat & facinoris qualitatem, rabiem sc. eorum: nec non interpretatio- nem Chald. נכתין כאריות momorderunt sicut leo, & expositionem similem R. Salom. Jarchi: ac similes vo- ces compositas occurrere putat, Gen. 41, 43. אַבְרֵךְ ex verbo הִבְרִיךְ & vocibus אַב pater, & רַךְ tener: 2. Reg. 17, 21. וַיַּדֵּא & celerrime avertit ex וַיִּדַּח (ad marginem no- tato verbo) & וַיֵּדֶא & avolare fecit (quæ literæ textus funt) it. 2. Sam. 16, 23. 25. &c. Quibus tamen alii Masoram opponunt; utpote quæ observavit hic aliam esse vocis significationem, quam Es. 38, 13. quod argumentum ipse Dn. D. Wasm. alias urget: nisi forte pro hoc sensu id reponendum sit, Es. 38. simplicem esse sensum SICUT LEO: hic vero compositum; adeoque hactenus adhuc diver- sum, foderunt sicut leo: quo pacto nihilomines id obsta- re videtur; quod compositi hujus sensus exempla indu- bitata desiderentur, nec is satis splicitati, & perspicui- tati Scripturæ conveniat, quæ ambiguitatem & gemi- num sensum ejusdem vocis haud patiatur: nisi & hic di- stinguere quis malit, inter vocem ἁπλῶς unam, & virtu- te geminam: quia licet talis vox una tantum esse videa- tur, revera tamen non sit simpliciter una, sed potius vir- tualiter gemina, quum aliter legatur secundum conso- nantes, aliter secundum vocales, & diversitatis istius in- dex sit τὸ קרי & כתיב quo charactere ab ipso S. S. voces illæ notatæ quum sint, aliis præjudicium adferre, & ut in aliis, ita non characterisatis pariter statuatur aliqua am- biguitas, vel sensus duplicitas efficere non potest. Favet huic sententiæ Arias-Mont. (quem adducit in h. l. Andr. Riv.) ut & B. Helvic. in Vind. LL. V. T. p. 18. & Nic. Pe- træus in Lex. Ebr. 1576. Sed in ea plerique temere assu- munt, hoc exemplum inter קרין & כתבן locum non habere, quorum numerantur 848. sed hic locus in eo ca- talogo non reperitur. Qui e præcedentibus verbum ad- vocant, vocem הַקּוֹפְוֹנִי ἀπὸ κοινῶ repetendam censent, ut Aben-Ezra, Kimchius, Polanus, Voetius, Pockokius, Leusdenius in Jona illustrato. Quam nonnulli exponunt transfixerunt me: h. m. Concilium malignantium transfixe- runt me; sicut Leo, inquam, transfixerunt manus meas, & pedes meos, vel transfixerunt me, manibus meis & pedibus meis: ut sit a נקר excidit, perfodit, quæ significatio ex Ara- bismo a Pocokio deducta observatur Es. 10, 30. 24, 3. Job. 19, 26. Quibus tamen opponit D. Wasmuth. tum accentua- tionem, tum Masoram, quæ non permittat explicationem illam SICUT LEO, sed excludat eandem. Atque hinc col- ligimus (4.) E Masoretica observatione. Si enim cum Ma- sora quis malit huic voci distinctam a loco Es. 38, 13. signi- ficationem attribuere, (quæ sententia omnino præferen- da,) Judaica explicatio, SICUT LEO, in spongia incum- bet, interpretatio vero Christianorum probe sibi consta- bit. Nam כָּאֲרִי derivari potest cum Paulo Burgensi, Mar- co Marino, B. Glassio, Tarnov. D. Walth. Sixt. ab Amama, & aliis כָּרָה q. e. transfixit, vel transfodit, ut quum dici debeat ordinarie כָּרוּ transfoderunt, א per ἐπένθεσιν insertum dicatur, sicut in רָאמָה exaltabitur Zach. 14, 10. (quod factum ad indicandam fossionis magnitu- dinem, putat Tarnov. in h. l. p. 143.) in fine autem י lo- co ו, quia literæ illæ sunt εὐμετάβολοι, positum sit, uti Esr. 10. ult. נִשָּׂאי acceperunt, pro נָשְׂאוּ: vide exempla alia apud Avenar. l. 3. Gram. p. 585. unde in Codd. Re- giis cum ֹ puncto scribitur כָּאֲרִיֹ quasi esset Jod Schu- rek, loco vav Schurek, uti Jer. 50, 11. quod Marc. Marin. Brixian. in arca Noæ f. 332. non Jod, sed vau diminu- tum vocat, peculiariter ideo adhibitum, ut clare innuat clavorum Christi stigmata. B. Tarnov. vult, eam literam ו sine puncto in tam notabili mysterio adhibitam, ad tru- culentam crudelitatem, atque violentiam Leoninam simul indicandam. B. Gesnero visum fuit, mutatis punctis le- gendum esse כֹּאֲרֵי in regimine q. d. perfossores manuum & pedum meorum. Quæ sententia, etsi B. Gerhardi in Harm. passion. c. 13. non improbata, B. Tarnov. p. 144. sese probare non potuit, neque correctio ejus- modi punctorum, B. Glassio ac B. D. Walthero judice, concedenda. Aliam vocis cum his punctis vocali- bus explicationem protulit Lud. de Dieu in animadv. p. 320. præeunte Nicol. Fullero, ut nempe א statuatur esse radicale, a כאר fœdavit, quemadmodum in lingua Syriaca כאר fignificat pudefacere, ut cum legitur כָּאֲרוּ fit tertia Cal fœderarunt, deformarunt, quod interpre- tationi Aquilæ ᾔσχυναν fœdarunt, congruere, ac fenfu idem effe ait, cum foderunt, confodiendo enim fœdarunt, (ut taceam, quod Pocockius observet verba כָּאַר & כָּרָה juxta analogiam Arabicæ linguæ fynonyma esse po- tuisse) cum vero legitur כָּארִי fit infinitivus Piel כַּאֵר qui regulariter cum affixo primæ personæ fiat כַּאֲרִי manente Kametz, quia valet Patach sequente Dagesch, ut vertere liceat, deturpando me manibus meis ac pedi- bus meis, vel deturpando mihi manus meas & pedes meos, & construatur cum antecedenti præterito, con- gregatio maleficorum circumdederunt me, ac si infiniti- vus præteriti significatione, more Ebræis, ubi alia præterita præcedunt, usitatissimo accipiatur, reddi debeat, deturparunt mihi manus meas & pedes meos: unde liquere autumat, perinde omnino esse, quantum ad sensum כָּאֲרוּ an כָּאֲרִי legatur. Ita Ludovicus de Dieu. Quæ sententia juvari poterit, ut major ei con- cilietur probabilitas, si verbum præcedens הִקִיפוּנִי reddatur, transfoderunt me: Sic enim sensus luculen- tior redundabit: circumdederunt me sicut canes: Con- gregatio malignantium transfixerunt me deturpando me manibus meis ac pedibus meis, fœde cruentando, vel deturparunt mihi manus meas & pedes meos, ut transfixio admodum cruenta, ac cum insigni defœdatione conjun- cta, designetur. Sic ergo crucifixionis actus indica- tur, sive a כָּרָה sive a כָּאַר derivatum verbum in- telligatur. Priori tamen etymo versiones antiquæ LXX. Interpp. Hieronymi, vulgata, nec non Chaldaica, Arabica, Syriaca, ut & Æthiopica magis congruunt. Nisi quis fortassis malit vocem COMPOSITAM di- cere, aut præferre novam Pocockii in Porta Mofis p. 59. sententiam, quod vox illa a כאר perfodiendi notione ex usu linguæ Arabicæ deducta descendat, ut litera א radicalis, vel e Vau per mutationem facta sit in Benoni, & vocales adhibitæ censeantur ex analogia vocis כֹּאפְנָק Hos. 10, 14. & רָאמוֹת Zach. 14, 10. ac numerus hic occurrat pluralis per apocopen literæ Mem, quæ non inusitata, uti exempla adfert e Gen. 40, 16. חוֹרִי, 2. Sam. 20, 38. הַחִצִי, 2. Sam. 23, 8. שְׁלִישִׁי 2. Reg. 11, 4. הַכָּרוֹ, 2. Sam. 24, 44. Thren. 3, 13. עַמִּי &c. Perfodientes circumdederunt me. Quam sententiam approbat & confirmat Dn.
