And what is more certain than that Rivetus thus tries to couple the arctic pole with the antarctic? For those opinions differ as much as the whole heaven, as the saying is, nor can they stand together any more than two contradictories can be true at the same time: namely, that it is treated according to the letter concerning Solomon, which Calvin and Grotius affirm, and that it is not treated concerning Solomon according to the letter, but solely concerning Christ, which the Fathers and other Christian Interpreters, and even the older Jews, affirm with the greatest consensus: that the Holy Spirit describes here the marriage, according to the paraphrastic sense, of Solomon with the Egyptian Bride, and does not describe them, but solely chants the spiritual marriage of the Christian Church according to the paraphrastic sense: that history is referred to here in sacred song, in the immediate sense: even if it is proposed as a type, so that regard may be had for the spiritual marriage of Christ figured by this type. And that here there is held only a mere Prophecy, proposed indeed in allegorical words; but whose immediate sense exhibits Christ, and not indeed any type of Christ. And further: that Solomon the Bridegroom is commended here for the elegance of his form, the eloquence of his speech, the fortitude of his fighting, the happy success of his kingdom, for his meekness and justice, and then also for the stability of his kingdom, for the sweetness of his garments, for the excellence and splendor of his wife: which Junius wishes with Calvin and Grotius: And that Christ the Bridegroom is described and commended solely by these criteria, and that these things are celebrated in this Poem not even by a tittle concerning Solomon: which all Christian Interpreters assert. Similarly, that Pharaoh's daughter is addressed directly in the speech to the Bride, so that, having forgotten her father's house and her former conversation, she may diligently attend to and listen to King Solomon, so that the Bridegroom may embrace her beauty, and she, a participant of the highest honor, may be exalted and celebrated even by other women: And that the marriage with the same is described here in such a way that it is constituted a type of the Church gathered from the Gentiles. But then that there is no word here about Pharaoh's daughter, nor is she herself constituted a type of the Church, but that the whole of that description and exhortation pertains to the Church, the Bride of Christ, without the notion of a type: and that the marriage with the Egyptian woman was not a type, nor was it proposed as a type. Further, the discourse being turned again to the Bridegroom, the beauty of the Egyptian Bride is sung, and the remaining ornaments, then the happiness of the children, and the dignity of those who will be born from her: And on the contrary, the beauty of the Egyptian Bride and her ornaments, and other things, are not sung here, but all those things are celebrated solely concerning the Church, the Bride of Christ. Finally, since in the last verse it is held that the memory of THIS BRIDEGROOM is to be celebrated forever through all generations, and it is foretold that the peoples will render eternal praise to the same, if in the Psalm Solomon himself was celebrated as the Bridegroom, as a type of CHRIST, it follows as an ἄτοπον that this conclusion of the Psalm also, dedicated to the eternal memory of THIS BRIDEGROOM, according to the letter concerning Solomon must be understood, if indeed the συνέχεια of the Psalm is to remain consistent with itself, and the opinion of Calvin, Grotius, and Rivet is to prevail. But as regards the remaining interpreters, it is entirely certain that both that whole Ode and its conclusion are dedicated to the eternal memory of Christ the King, and thus the prologue or exordium and proposition, the logos or narration, describing at length the Bridegroom and Bride and the nuptials, and the Epilogue or eternal conclusion promising and predicting glory from all generations, harmonize with each other perfectly, and uniquely celebrate CHRIST JESUS the mystical Bridegroom. Thus, therefore, it is most manifest that those expositions differ διˆα πασῶν, and in terms, as it is said, that are contradictory. And therefore they can never be reconciled by any art, unless perhaps someone wishes, or dares, to reconcile Judaism itself with Christianity.

In vain, however, does Rivet apply a compromise here, that there is not indeed in all, but in certain sentences of this Psalm, some historical sense which PRIMARILY can be referred to Solomon and his wife as types; yet that there are also some things which DO NOT EVEN AGREE IN THE TYPE, and are to be explained IMMEDIATELY concerning Christ and the Church.

For if SOME things in this Psalm are to be explained IMMEDIATELY concerning Christ and the Church without a type, ALL things must necessarily be accepted in the same immediate sense. The reason for the consequence is invincible: because in the Prologue, the logos itself, and the Epilogue, it is clearer than the sun that one King, one Bridegroom, is being dealt with in an immediate sense, and likewise one Queen, one unique Bride. The Prophet sets out to sing of this one King; he describes this one King's beauty, eloquence, fortitude, success, mighty works, throne, majesty, and splendor: he proposes this one's nuptials and bride: he sings of the due duties, beauty, and splendor, happiness, and dignity of the children of this one Queen, his Bride: And he prophesies of this one's name, to be celebrated from generation to generation, indeed into all eternity. If in a single verse Solomon cannot be understood as the King, or in a single predicate alone, or if a single attribute in this Psalm does not in any way agree with the daughter of Pharaoh, it is concluded α̉ναντιῤῤήτως that in no verse, as regards no predicate, is Solomon the SUBJECT here, of whom the Psalm treats in an immediate sense, and no predicate is here uttered concerning the daughter of Pharaoh; since there is only one subject here, and one King, of whom all predicates are uttered according to the proper, immediate, literal, and paraphrastic sense: just as only one Queen of his is also introduced. I dedicate my works to the KING, says the Psalmist in the Prologue v. 1. You are beautiful in form beyond the sons of men, he says to that KING in the logos or narration v. 3, and what follows thereafter. The QUEEN stood at his right hand v. 10. And to her v. 12, THAT KING, of whom it has been treated uniquely thus far, shall desire your beauty, since he himself is your Lord. And v. 15, virgins shall be brought to THAT KING after her, the Queen. And v. 18, in the Epilogue, they shall be mindful of THY NAME (O King) in every generation. Who would still dare to assign different subjects in such evidence of the matter, who would presume to tear apart a hymn that is perpetually coherent and woven with one thread and style, and in some parts, as regards the immediate sense, to insert Solomon as the subject, even though in most parts, as regards the immediate sense, he admits our Christ as the subject of the Epithalamium?

Latin:

v. 5. Specie tua & pulchritudine tua, idest, decore tuo, in specie sapientia & pulchritudine justitia consistit, quasi gladio & armis accinctus & instructus intende, prospere procede, & regna, i. e. dirige cursum tuum ad prælium contra diabolum, prosperare in prælio, & devicto ac debellato principe hujus mundi, acquire tibi regnum, ut tu deinceps in cordibus hominum per fidem & charitatem regnes &c. Eandem συνέχειαν habet Menochius, Grotio æstimatus, nec nisi de uno subjecto ad literam omnia per totum Psalmum explicat. Minor propositio Riveti itidem est, in verbis immediate subjunctis: Qui duo versus 7. & 8. diligenter sunt perpendendi, quoniam Apostolus Hebr. 1, 8. eos AD CHRISTUM IMMEDIATE refert, cui certe SOLI competunt. Quæ SOLI Christo competunt, & ad eum IMMEDIATE referenda sunt, ea Salomoni neutiquam conveniunt, nec MEDIATE tantum ad Christum, quatenus Salomon ejus typus fuit, immediate autem ad Salomonem, aut literaliter ad hunc pertinent, mystice solum Christum respiciunt. Videmus vim veritatis. Nimis enim evidens est, hoc vaticinium unice de Messia agere, nullumque aliud subjectum, nullum typum admittere.

Octavo peculiariter expendenda nostri Regis justitia. Virga directionis virga regni tui. Dilexisti justitiam & odisti iniquitatem. Quod de Rege nostro absolute pronunciatur, ut nunquam a justitiæ tramite discedere innuatur: Eum nempe, ut Rivetus fassus est, potestate judiciaria sua, cum tanta æquitate, usurum, ut nihil unquam quod a rectitudine deviet, in tota ejus administratione appareat. Hunc enim ille reddit sensum literalem & paraphrasticum verborum, quem Salomoni non competere palam testatur: Ne ipsi quidem, inquit, Salomoni (nedum posteris ejus) convenit virga recta, nisi ad tempus, cum turpiter postea a Deo defecerit. Ideo Bellarm. ita παραφράζει: sedes tua, o Christe Deus, non temporalis erit, ut fuit Davidis & Salomonis, & manebit in seculum seculi. Et virga regni tui, id est, sceptrum tuum erit semper rectissimum atque justissimum. Phrasis enim Hebraica est, virga directionis, pro virga rectissima. Sic etiam Menochius, in hisce Epitomator Bellarmini. Neque immerito Hieronymus ad h. l. amorem justitiæ & odium iniquitatis ad impletionem mandatorum Dei refert: Unde Estius Comment. ad Ebr. 1, 8. Peculiare illud Christo Regi est, ita diligere justitiam, ut nobis etiam justus justitiæ autor & largitor sit, & ita odisse iniquitatem, ut nos merito ac virtute sua ab omni iniquitate mundatos sanctificet. In quibus certe typus ejus non fuit Salomon.

Nono unctio Regis nostri summe singularis, non nisi Christum θεάνθρωπον hic intelligendum esse, luculentissime confirmat. Propterea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus oleo lætitiæ præ consortibus tuis. Deum iterum casu vocandi appellat Propheta. Non ergo potest intelligi Salomo, qui absolute Deus vocari nequit, nec uspiam vocatus est. Tum unctionem eam indigitat, quæ Salomoni nullatenus convenit: Quia unctio hæc cum dilectione justitiæ, & odio iniquitatis perenni & incommutabili connexa: unctio hæc in subjecto θεανθρώπῳ, quod Deus est natura, & consortes habet, in assumta humanitate, facta: unctio hæc SUPRA omnes consortes facta, ut nullus ejusdem ratione huic Regi conferri possit: unctio facta, ut in æternum regnet, ac sceptrum rectitudinis gerat, quod semper rectissimum ac justissimum, justitiam amans: & ini- quitatem odio prosequens, ut mirabilia patret dextera sua, & sagittis suis acutis corda inimicorum quorumvis transfigat; unctio facta est oleo lætitiæ, hoc est, non materiali, sed spirituali, ipsoque Spiritu Sancto, in quo vera est lætitia Rom. 14. non juxta mensuram, sed immensa & infinita ratione Joh. 3, 34. Ideo donorum infinitorum communicationem importat: quibus omnino opus ad regnum illud erat: ob unctionem etiam illam religiosa debetur huic Regi adoratio, teste Hiero-Psalte v. 42. unde non potest ullatenus unctio ista in Salomonem quadrare. Fatetur sane Rivetus, de Messia tanquam de Christo Dei ἀντονομασικῶς dicto intelligendam esse hoc loco unctionem illam oleo lætitiæ p. 326. Junius hanc tradit paraphrasin: Propterea unxit te, id est, in hunc finem plenitudinem Spiritus accepisti, ut ista præstes, & ex plenitudine tua omnes accipiamus gratiam per gratiam Joh. 1, 16. Et ad v. 1. ita habet: Majestatis & justitiæ & gloriæ divinæ in Christo descriptio ex donis & vocatione Dei: Nam hæc ad Salomonem minus pertinere, tum ipsa verborum series ostendit, tum Apostolus Ebr. 1, 8. Sed uberius de hoc loco postea. Atque hæc de secunda argumentorum classe e descriptione Sponsi.

Tertio confirmamus sententiam nostram e Sponsæ descriptione. Quum enim relata hæc sint Sponsus & Sponsa, mutuo se declarant, & e Sponsæ descriptione, quis Sponsus sit, cognoscimus. Sponsa hic spiritualis est, Ecclesia nempe, quæ unius Christi Sponsa 2. Cor. 11. Eph. 5. Hos. 2. non vero Filia Regis Ægypti, Salomonis Sponsa: Etsi enim vel maxime concederetur alludi metaphoricis, vel allegoricis quibusdam loquutionibus ad Salomonis Sponsam, ejusdem comitatum, vestitum, & similia, sicut in metaphoris e rebus naturalibus, ad res ejusmodi alluditur, eisque veritas supponitur, & in evolutione metaphoræ, merito adducitur: Describi tamen Salomonis Sponsam tanquam typum, ac sub eadem antitypum, Ecclesiam, Christi Sponsam designari; sensum literalem ac immediatum de Salomonis Sponsa, mediatum autem & mysticum de Ecclesia verbis ipsis subesse, id vero est, quod ἀποτόμως negandum est. Quæ toto etiam, quod dicitur, cœlo differunt. Ibi enim, in Metaphoricis loquutionibus, sensus unicus tantum subest, juxta quem verba figurate intelligenda, ac metaphoræ evolvendæ sunt, deque subjecto proprio, quo de agitur, veritatem habent non sensu proprio, sed figurato ac metaphorico, qui unice est intentus a Spiritu S. Hic vero constituitur geminus sensus eorundem verborum, & uterque intentus a Spiritu S. dicitur: tum immediatus, qua typum, de quo verba proprie intelligenda, sine metaphora, tum mediatus, qua antitypum, de quo figurate sint illa explicanda. Quo pacto verbum idem eodem loco, & proprie & improprie accipiendum erit. Quod perquam absurdum. Proinde Veteres omnes unanimi consensu Ecclesiam per Sponsam intelligunt, sine typo. Basilius integrum enarravit Psalmum, sed neque Salomonis, neque conjugis ejus ullam mentionem fecit. Ad verba autem, astitit Regina: De Ecclesia inquit, jam edifferit, de qua in canticis didicimus, quod una sit perfecta Christi columba. Et paulo post: Astistit itaque Regina, nempe anima Sponsali verbo cooptata, nullius jam peccati oppressa tyrannide, sed in partem admissa Regni Christi: a dextris, inquam, astat Salvatoris, in vestitu dealbato, hoc est, in dogmatibus Spirituali intelligentia subtextis, & varietatis floribus interstructis graviter se componens,

& adornans religiofe. Cui consentiunt reli- qui.

Describitur autem (1.) Sponsæ honor & de- cus. Filiæ Regum inter honorabiles tuas: astitit con- jux ad dextram tuam in auro Ophir. Recte omni- no Rivetus, dum quærit: quænam sint hæ regum filiæ inter honoratas & charas Sponsi? observat: in nuptiis terrenis non esse easdem, quæ Sponsum comi- tantur, & ipsam Sponsam: Sed in conjugio Spiri- tuali omnes amicos & amicas Sponsi & Sponsæ, Spon- sam constituere. Quia sponsæ corpus mysticum est, & ad quantitatem discretam pertinet, non continuam. Sponsa vocatur totum corpus aggregatum ex fide- lium universo numero. Filiæ Regum Sponsam co- mitantes sunt fideles seorsum considerati, qui in uno corpore Sponsam constituunt, tanquam membra. Id- eoque hic describi Ecclesiam 1. secundum totum. 2. Secundum partes. Secundum partes Filiæ Regum sunt inter honoratas Sponsi. Secundum totum, Re- gina adstat a dextris tuis. Hæc, inquam, recte & accurate Rivetus post B. Gesnerum nostrum: Unde non opus erit disquirere, quænam illæ sint Regum filiæ, differentes a Sponsa? de quo inter alios solli- citus est Ballarminus: Ex quibus delectaverunt se filiæ Regum in honore tuo (sic habet Vulgata) id est, ex quibus aromatibus, quæ a vestimentis & domi- bus eburneis humanitatis tuæ spirant, filiæ Regum, sive animæ Regni & excelsæ, sive multitudines populo- rum ex variis regnis delectaverunt te, dum currunt in odorem ungventorum tuorum. Et ad v. 16. adducen- tur Regi virgines post eam (filiam, Regis Sponsam) Proximæ ejus afferentur tibi: Quamvis unica sit Spon- sa Christo, eaq; unice dilecta, id est, Ecclesia universa- lis, tamen post eam sunt etiam Christi Sponsa, præcipua quadam prærogativa præter cæteros fideles, illæ animæ, quæ in carne virginitatem suam Deo voverunt, ut sensus sit: post principalem Sponsam Ecclesiam, vel ut deinde habet Bellarmin. post matrem Domini adducentur etiam ad nuptialem thalamum Sponsi cœlestis omnes illæ animæ, quæ virginitatem suam Deo dicarunt. Hæc ille in gratiam voti monasti- ci. Sed annon animæ illæ ad ipsam Ecclesiam uni- versalem pertinent, ejusque membra sunt? Quomo- do ergo post eam adducentur? Ut taceam, quod votum illud Monasticum in Scripturis nullum habeat fundamentum, nedum prærogativam inferat in Ec- clesia. Virgines autem nuncupantur fideles omnes propter incorruptæ fidei & confessionis integrita- tem, vitæque innocentiam 2. Corinth. 11. Apoc. 14. Matth. 25. De matre Domini hic peculiariter, vel etiam μοναδικῶς sermonem esse, cum Sponsa Chri- sti describitur, neque ex hoc loco, neque aliunde e Scripturis doceri potest. Si quid tamen discri- minis inter Sponsam & Filias Regis, ac virgines sta- tuendum, non male id exprimunt Paraphrastæ Vi- narienses, quod Filiæ Regum sint regna & Provinciæ Regum, quæ in ornatu Sponsi incedunt, hoc est ad Sponsum convertuntur, & ab ipso exornantur Es. 49, 18. 22. 23. Sponsa vero sit ipsa universalis Ecclesia: Sociæq; virgines versu 15. sint fideles, Eccle- siam Spiritu, fide, ac vita sequentes, cum illa recte verbum Dei docet ac proponit Matth. 25, 1. 4. A- poc. 14, 4. Alii per Filias Regum Ecclesias ex gen- tibus, per Reginam conjugem Israeliticam, quæ eas habebit comites, intelligunt. Ex his vero facile refellitur Calvini ac Grotii, aliorumque senten- tia Judaica de Filia Regis Ægypti, ejusque gy- næceo, vel etiam concubinis, in qua sibi ipsi nequaquam constat Calvinus: Sciendum est, inquit, non probatum fuisse DEO quic- quam quid hic laudatur in Salomone. Atque ut de aliis taceam, Deo certe statim ab initio displicuit poly- gamia. Atqui inter BENEDICTIONES DEI po- nuntur concubina : neque enim dubium est, quin per honorabiles Propheta significet uxores, quarum alibi fit mentio. Sic dubium non est Calvino, laudari hic in Salomone, & inter benedictiones Dei poni concubi- nas: nec tamen polygamiam ejus Deo probatam fuisse. Quae vere άσύςατα sunt. Similiter haud facile quis conciliaverit, quae ibidem adduntur: Etsi Salomoni alienigenam ducere uxorem fas non fuit : merito tamen hoc quoque numeratur inter DO- NA DEI, quod a Rege potentissimo quaesita fuerit il- lius affinitas. Nec immerito Calvini glossae oppo- nit Rivetus, quod hoc loco de unica tantum Spon- sa agatur, ideoque de aliis Salomonis uxoribus ac concubinis verba Prophetae accipi non possint. Et quomodo, quod de multis uxoribus dicitur, antitypo conveniet? Nam si plures finguntur Eccle- siae, lacerabitur corporis Christi unitas: Et proprie lo- quendo unica est Sponsa, quae ex universo piorum coetu colligitur, habet hic ipse Calvinus. Riveto autem ipsi id fortissime adversatur, quod haec κατ’ ἐπεξή- γησιν accipiat, & pro iisdem habeat: Filiae Regum sunt inter honoratas Sponsi, & Regina adstat a dexteris. Si enim idem sunt Filiae Regum & Regina, non licebit certe Reginam de Filia Pharaonis, & filias Regum de gynaeceo ejus intelligere, quod tamen hic con- tendit Rivetus, ac sensum Grammaticum vocat. Pos- sunt, inquit, & debent haec omnia ad Pharaonidis Sponsae Salomonis comitatum & cultum lautissimum referri. Habuit enim illa splendidum gynaeceum &c. Num idem sunt Sponsa Aegyptia, & gynaeceum e- jusdem?

Designatur autem hic porro (2.) Sponsae de- bitum officium. Audi Filia, & vide, & inclina aurem tuam, & obliviscere populum tuum & domum Patris tui. Filiam nominat Deus Pater, cujus haec est exhortatio, adeoque designat spiritualem fi- delium regenerationem, ac requirit tum verbi coelestis diligentem auscultationem ac observationem, tum proprii populi oblivionem: Qui enim Christo nomina sua dederunt, eos oportet mundo vale- dicere. Insipidumed quod hic Rivetus: Innuit satis haec compellatio auctorem hujus Psalmi non fuisse hominem e vulgo, aut obscurum aliquem, sed aut Re- gem, aut cujus in aula Regis fuerit magna authori- tas. Alioqui enim haec verba non decerent hominem privatum. Annon enim loquuti sunt Prophetae Dei nomine? Neque congruit interpretatio, quam in Calvini gratiam prosequitur, de Pharao- nide, quae oblivisci populi sui, & patris, & mores ac ritus patrios debeat, nec aegre carere Patria, cum status conjugalis ipsi tam praeclaram compensationem afferat. Rectius sese habent quae de Sponsa Regis nostri Ecclesia tradit p. 341. Filiam vocat, quae fi- liorum Dei corpus constituit, qui spiritualiter per ver- bum suum regeniti, & adoptionem filiorum recepe- runt. Johann. 1. v. 13. Requirit ut audiat, quod primum est inter ea, quae ad cultum primum Christi DEI pertinent. Interferit praeceptum videndi, qui visus cum sit spiritualis, animi etiam attentionem de- notat, sed eam ut plurimum, quae ab ipso experientiae consensu & effectu juvatur. Tunc enim quasi oculis objicitur Dei benignitas. Denique exhortationem subjungit ad totam Ecclesiam, ex Judaeis & genti- bus collectam, cujus sunt etiam dotes, & promissio- nes, quae sequuntur: Ubi per domum Patris Rive- tus cum aliis Calvino ipso praeeunte, intelligit, quicquid corruptionis ex utero afferimus, aut quae- cunque postea ex prava institutione nobis adhærent, quasi ad nos hæreditario jure aut educatione transfu- sa. Per populum autem ea, quæ ex mala consue- tudine & conversatione cum impiis & idololatris ac- quisita, ac a Deo abducunt, quæ omnia deponenda sunt, si Christo Sponso conjungi cupimus. Sequitur in his B. Gesnerum nostrum, ut in priori explicatio- ne Calvinum suum. Vidit enim nostrum sen- sum verum esse, Calvinum tamen suum etiam deferere noluit, ideo utramque explicationem assumsit. Sed illa simul consistere non possunt. Quis enim credat, iisdem verbis tam disparatos sensus subesse? Siquidem omnia verba ita diver- sis plane significationibus intelligenda forent, ut cum Filiæ Pharaonis, tum Ecclesiæ accommodari possint! Si ergo posterior sensus rectus, uti non dubitat Rivetus, prior omnino hic dimittendus erit.

(3.) Subjungitur promissio v. 12. Et con- cupiscet Rex decorem tuum: quoniam ipse est Do- minus Deus tuus, & adorabunt eum. Sic etiam LXX. reddidisse, adorabunt eum. Hieronymus observat Epist. ad Princip. Ebræi in Codice ha- bent, adorabis eum. Quibus consonat Aquila, Symmachus, Theodotio, ut refert Theodoretus, Augustinus item, Apollinaris, & Psalterium Roma- num. Hic vero per Regem non posse intelligi Salomonem longe manifestissimum est: De Rege enim dicitur, ipse est Dominus tuus, & adorabunt eum. Quid ergo certius, quam unum Messiam hic intelligendum esse, qui est DEUS benedictus in secula, super omnia, quem adorare debent o- mnes Rom. IX, 5. Psalm. XCVII, 7. & LXXII, 17. De Sponsa ergo Salomonis hæc accipi non possunt: sed de Ecclesia, Christi Sponsa: Concu- piscet Rex decorem tuum. Etsi vero in Ebræo vox Deus non habeatur, LXX. tamen & Hieronymus ita reddiderunt, & ex adoratione colligitur, eum vere esse Deum, quemadmodum etiam antea ex- pressè ita appellatus est. Nam adorandi verbo, ut hic Calvinus, non externa modo ceremonia, sed pius reverentiæ & obsequii præstandi affectus per Synecdo- chen notatur; sicut enim Filiæ nomine (hæc itidem Calvini sunt) novam Ecclesiam blande & suaviter demulcet: Ita & præmio allicit, ut libenter in Chri- sti gratiam, quicquid hactenus charum habuit, spernat ac relinquat. Neque enim vulgare sola- tium est, nos Filio DEI in summis deliciis fore, ubi terrenum ingenium exuerimus. Hic igitur Ecclesia, quæ Riveti explicatio est, dulcissimam audit promissionem, futurum nempe, ut sese morige- ram præbeat, & abjecta omni idololatria & pro- fanitate se ei soli addicat, ut omnem molestiam compenset a dulcissima sua consuetudine, & amo- re ardentissimo. Est autem hic Sponsus Spiritua- lis vere Dominus Sponsæ suæ, quia non solum crea- vit, sed etiam acquisivit eam suo sanguine, quæ ad ipsum indotata venit. Quæ uti verissime & ad mentem S. S. dicuntur, ita nequaquam consi- stere possunt cum illis, quæ præmisit idem Ri- vetus in Calvini sui gratiam, quod hæc possint ad Salomonem tanquam ad typum referri. Nam si pulchritudo illa Spiritualis, in animi fide & chari- tate sincera consistens, quomodo de externo so- lum decore intelligenda? Si Dominus indigita- tur, qui jure creationis ac redemtionis Dominus est, quomodo nomen Domini solum de digni- tate Patrisfamilias vel mariti explicandum? si qui adoratio præcipitur religiosa primæ tabulæ, quomodo de adoratione civili secundæ tabulæ præceptum explicari potest? Congeruntur iterum in easdem voces sensus disparati, quod a simplicitate ac perspicuitate Scripturæ Sacræ prorsus alienum est.

(4.) Prædicatur gloria Sponsæ e Spirituali connubio redundans, & consortium aliquod honoris Sponsi, quod nempe ipsa etiam Sponsa ut Regina muneribus afficienda sit: Et Filiæ Tyri in muneribus vultum tuum deprecabuntur omnes divites plebis. Hæc Salomonis felicitati convenire, ait quidem Rivetus, cujus universa terra vultum desiderabat, & singuli deferunt ei munia, interque omnes vicini Tyri 1. Reg. 10, 14. 26. cap. 5, 1. Sed agnoscere tamen cogitur, hæc omnia in Christum & Ecclesiam perfectissime quadrare; prædici enim populos Tyri, externasque gentes ad Ecclesiam venturas cum muneribus, quæ ipsi offerent, imo propter ejus magnificentiam & gloriam a Christo Sponso suo communicatam, veneraturos eam omnes Principes cujuscunque plebis, deprecantes eam, ut ipsos sibi velit adjungere, & sibi unitos in Sponsi sui communionem recipere. Quæro ergo iterum, quomodo hæc cum prioribus conciliari possint? Si enim verba hæc, uti fatetur Rivetus, non restringenda ad Tyrios proprie dictos, exclusive ad alias gentes, sed sub Tyro alias omnes regiones Ethnicosque omnes extra populum Judaicum intelligere oportet, quomodo Tyrios tantum, Regemque Hiram proprie hic intelligit Rivetus? aut num gentes omnes depræcatæ sunt filiam Pharaonis? Si per divites populi designantur, qui ex seculo conversi ad Christum sunt ex potentioribus juxta similia vaticinia Esai. LX, 3. 10. 11. 16. cap. XLIX, 23. quomodo id de ditissimorum populorum submissione erga Salomonem accipi poterit? Non enim de allusione solum aliqua, quod iterum moneo, quæritur, sed de sensu verborum Grammatico & germano: qui certe geminus constitui nec potest, nec debet, ac quum citra controversiam ille de Christo admittendus sit, dimittendus est necessario ille, quem obtrudere cupiunt Interpretes isti Judaizantes de Salomone.

(5.) Celebratur ornatus Sponsæ vers. 15. Omnis gloria ejus filiæ Regis ab intus, in fimbriis aureis circumamicta varietatibus. Ubi Bellarminum Jesuitarum admirator Grotius audire debuisset: Quia sæpe David de pulchritudine & ornatu sponsæ loquutus est, ne quis forte putaret ea corporalia esse, occurrit hoc loco ejus modi carnalibus cogitationibus, & dicit, omnis gloria, sive decoris faciei, sive preciosarum vestium hujus Reginæ ab intus est, etsi fimbriis aureis ornata & circumcincta dicatur variegata veste illa, omnia Spiritualia sunt, interna sunt, in corde requirenda sunt. Hæc textui, aliisque Scripturæ locis consonant, sed quam jejunus passim & frigidus est Calvini commentarius, quem sequi maluit Grotius, quoties ipsum Judæis adhærere vidit, quam alios quoscunque Interpretes; etsi alioquin ab ipso æstimatos? Duplex, inquit, potest esse sensus, Reginam non modo, quum in populi conspectum prodit, sed etiam ubi in cubiculo sedet, semper magnifice vestitam esse: vel splendorem ornatus non esse fucatum ad fallendos simplicium oculos, sed ex solida opulentia constare. Addit etiam aliorum quorundam explicationem, quam ipse quoque non improbare videtur: Alii putant (Isidorus Clarius, & Vatablus) quod eam Rex ad se familiariter invitet, quia mox transitus in cubiculum describitur cum magno & splendido comitatu. Sed quis non videt, quam inepta & aliena haec sint in sacro nostro Epitha- lamio? Ideo non poterant illa esse ad palatum Riveto, etsi in Praeceptoris gratiam dicat NON INCOMMODE EXCOGITATA, si- quidem ad verba Prophetae ita commode adaptari non posse agnoscat. Nolim ergo, in- quit, recedere à COMMUNI interpretum sensu, id referentium ad ornatum INTERIO- REM Sponsae praecipuum illum quidem, etsi exte- rius etiam appareat aliquid, quod eam commen- det: Hanc intelligentiam suggerunt OMNES si- ve VETERES Interpretes sive recentiores: qua- si dicat, praecipua ornamenta SPIRITUALIA sunt interna in corde reperienda. Ad quod vide- tur alludere Petrus 1. Epist. 2. v. 4. Mirum tamen quod ausit Rivetus insignem hanc descriptio- nem peculiariter Pharaonide applicare. Quid enim in ea eximii fuit, quo prae aliis quantum ad interiorem illam gloriam eminuerit? Nam quod ad mores potissimum spectaverit Salomo, nec duxerit, nisi quam credidit bene moratam, & cujus ornatum potissimum esse occultum exi- stimavit, in quo delectu tamen falli potuit, quid hoc ad GLORIAM illam INTERIOREM, de qua Propheta, quae non in quibusdam vir- tutibus moralibus, quales etiam in gentiles ca- dunt, consistit, aut dubia est, & ambigua, sed donis Spiritus Sancti gratiosis constat, & judi- cio ipsius Spiritus Sancti vere illustris est. To- ta, inquit gloriosa est Filia Regis intrinsecus. Quod de Sponsa Christi recte dicitur, non item de Sponsa Salomonis. Quid enim est pretiosum, ut iterum Rivetus, quo eam non ornavit Spon- sus, ut eam sibi exhiberet non habentem rugam aut maculam, aut aliquid hujusmodi Ephes. 5.. quid non in illa mirandum in divisionibus gratia- rum, ministrationum, operationum? S. Basi- lius sine typo de solo Spirituali decore Ecclesiae explicat, cujus verba, quae Ecclesiae Veteris sensum exprimunt, & eximia sunt, digna vi- dentur quae hic legantur è T. 1. Oper. in h. Psalm. p. 225. Postquam anima improbandis expurgata veteris malitiae doctrinis obedientiam exhibuit sanae & salutari Doctrinae, ubi oblita jam est populi sui & domus patris sui, narrat ea quae sunt de ipsa Spiritus Sanctus, & quoniam intimam ejus puri- tatem vidit: Omnis, inquit, gloria regis ab intus, hoc est, gloria Sponsae Christi, quae dein- ceps in Filiam Regis est adoptata, intus est. Hortatur plane hic sermo ad Ecclesiasticae gloriae mysteria intrinsecus prehendenda, quod decor & pulchritudo Sponsae introclusa sit & recondita. Qui enim se probe adornat, ei quidem qui videt in occulto, nempe Patri, supplexque eum orat, nihil- que non molitur boni operis, non ut spectetur ab hominibus, sed ut solius Dei oculis mereatur inno- tescere: hic gloriam omnem perinde ac filia Regis condidit intus. Quin & fimbriae aureae, quibus to- ta est circumamicta anima talis & variegata, uti- que intime sunt repositae. Ne tu quicquam quae- ras in externo isto auro, variegato corporis ami- ctu, magis cultum quendam mihi hic insinuari intellige, qui dignus sit cohonestare ac redimere ho- minem, qui ad sui conditoris imaginem creatus est juxta verbum Apostoli: Exuti veterem ho- minem & induti novum, qui renovatur ad agni- tionem secundum imaginem sui conditoris. Et qui induit se viscera misericordiae, bonitatem, hu- militatem, longanimitatem, mansuetudinem: ta- lis interiore amiculo redimitus est, & secundum interiorem hominem probe adornatus & excultus. Paulus item monet: Induite DOMINUM JESUM, non secundum exteriorem homi- nem, sed mens nostra Dei memoria circumami- ciatur. Puto enim spiritualem pertexi tunc vestem, quum operatio comes attexitur verbo doctrinae. Quemadmodum enim pallium tegendo corpori tunc detexitur, dum subtegmen innectitur stamini: Sic ubi verbum primas in ordiendo obtinuerit, si mox actio- nes verbo consentaneae attexentur, tunc exornandae animae decentissimus & plurimum habens honestatis amictus confici possit, animae, inquam, secundum vir- tutem & verbo & opere suam absolventi vitam. Ha- ctenus S. Basilius.

(6.) Celebratur comitatus virginum: Ad- ducentur Regi virgines post eam, proximae ejus afferentur tibi, afferentur in laetitia & exultatio- ne, adducentur in palatium (Vulgata habet templum) Regis. Quod etsi Ebræi de con- cubinis Regis, non abnuente Calvino, acci- piant, non placet tamen id Riveto, honestiorem multo esse comparationem & typum dicit (Com- paratio admitti possit, vel allusio, typus demon- strari non potest, imo textui, ut hactenus osten- sum, repugnat) si ad virgines socias & comites Sponsae totus ille comitatus referatur. Quæ de Ec- clesia omnino accipienda, & de virginibus Spi- ritualibus, ac laetitia & exultatione non mundana, sed Spirituali ac cœlesti. S. Basilius ita habet: sequuntur autem Sponsam Domini animae quaedam, quae semen alienorum Dogmatum minime suscepe- runt, & hae quidem Regi adducentur Sponsam se- ctantes. Agnoscit id Rivetus: Est autem hic Apostrophe ad Regem, ad quam Propheta sermo- nem convertit. Sed quis ille Rex? Num Salomon? Certe hic est plus quam Salomon! Redeamus igitur ad Regem Regum & ejus charissimam Sponsam pro- prio Sanguine acquisitam. Adducitur illa Regi nempe à ministris & paranymphis Spiritualibus ministerium Sacrum exercentibus, sistitur mari- to suo virgo casta in vestibus acu pictis Phrygioni- cis, id est, cum variis Spiritus donis. Jam vero per comitatum sive Gynæceum frequentia fi- delium ad nuptias agni vocatorum denotatur. Vir- gines autem nuncupantur propter incorruptæ fidei & confessionis integritatem, vitaeque innocentiam 2. Corinth. 11. Apoc. 11. Matth. 25. Adducuntur autem Christo per Evangelii praedicationem & Sa- cramenta, quibus desponsantur uni vero. Hæc Ri- vetus cum B. Gesnero nostro, & ex eodem. Quæ carnalem vel typicum sensum Ebræorum & Calvi- ni non ferunt. Ubi enim virginitas Spiritualis designatur, in illa litera corporis Virginitas non exhibetur, multo minus Concubinæ indicantur. Non agitur (ait de hoc loco, propria cædens vineta) de corporis virginitate, sed animi purita- te, cunctis fidelibus, cum agno in æternum victu- ris necessaria. Ubi de lætitia & exultatione spirituali ac cœlesti sermo est, ibi certe non agitur de lætitia mundana. Ubi Palatii vox adhibetur metaphorice de Ecclesia, vel potius de cælo, ibi de materiali palatio Regio explicari proprie non de- bet, nec potest. Non enim una, & eadem vox, in eodem loco simul & proprie, & figurate, h. e. improprie accipi potest, nisi è Scripturis quis fa- ciat Oracula Delphica.

(7.) Prædicitur Conjugii fructus vers. 17. Pro patribus erunt filii tui, & pones Principes in universa terra. Hæc vero nullatenus Salo- moni conveniunt, neque hic typi ratio locum ha- bere potest. Torquet ergo locum Calvinus & cum de filiis, quos ex conjugio cum Pharaoni- de nullos habuit Salomo, intelligere nequeat, ad posteritatem id detorquet: Pro patribus tuis erunt filii. Hoc quoque ad Regni præstantiam fa- cit, quod posteritas dignitate patribus non cedat, at- que ita non minuetur post mortem Salomonis nobi- litas generis: quia filii, qui ex eo nascentur, proa- vos omni virtutum excellentia æquabunt. En ὀχε- βλότητα! Non de præstantia regni, sed de conjugii fructu nunc agitur, & quidem ejus conjugii, quo de hactenus egit, Sponsum & Sponsam operose describendo. Vult autem de Conjugio Pharao- nidæ actum esse Calvinus; ex qua vero nullos libe- ros suscepit, nullam posteritatem reliquit Salo- mo. Proinde manifestum est, vel ex hoc com- mate, non posse per Sponsam intelligi Pharaonis filium. Neque de posteritate solum, sed de ipsis filiis Sponsi sermo est: nec de dignitate & excellen- tia virtutum posteritatis Salomonisæ, quæ certe cum Davide conferri non potest qua potestatem, nec cum Patriarchis, qua virtutum decora. Et quomodo filii Salomonis Principes ab ipso constituti sunt in universa terra, h. e. interprete Calvino, tam late propagato imperio, ut commode in plurima re- gna distribui queat? Agnoscit ipse Calvinus, hoc de Salomone intelligi non posse, nec invenire hic potuit, in quo typice solum Christum adumbraret Salomo, unde manifestissimum, non posse Psal- mum nostrum ad literam de Salomone ut typo Christi explicari. Vaticinium, inquit Calvinus, de Christo hoc esse, facile colligitur: Quia tan- tum abest, ut filii Salomonis propter regni amplitu- dinem provincias inter se partiti sint, ut primus ejus hæres exiguam tantum partem retinuerit, ita nemo ex legitimis successoribus ad ejus potentiam accessit, sed omnes unius tantum tribus, & dimidiæ Domini, qua- si in angustias conclusi fuerunt. Nulla ergo typi ratio hic obtinet, neque in liberis, neque in po- steritate Salomonis. Quid igitur restat, quam ut agnoscatur, vaticinium hoc simplex esse, uti Pareus vocat, & sine typo Christum respicere, adeo- que de Christo Sponso immediate, non vero sub Sa- lomonis typo in hoc Psalmo agi: & quum eadem Persona, idem Rex sit, ad quem dirigitur sermo, & de quo agit Propheta, totum Psalmum de Chri- sto immediate, non vero de Salomone, ut Christi typo, intelligendum esse. Addendus hic etiam Rivetus; Est enim (ita de hoc commate) exposi- tio fructus HUJUS MATRIMONII nempe nasci- turam ex eo felicissimam prolem, quæ TOTI ter- rarum ORBI dominatura sit. Hoc etsi Salomoni & Sponsæ dici potuit, ex Epithalamii lege, boni o- minis ergo (quasi Spiritu humano hoc Epithala- mium conscriptum sit, & non à Spiritu S. rerum futurarum præscio dictatum, aut quid dici PO- TUERIT, hic spectari debeat, & non potius, quid à Spiritu S. certo futurum PRÆDICTUM sit! in illis tamen locum non habuit promissio, pro- inde nec de illis intelligenda) quippe NULLUM Salomoni filium legitur genuisse Pharaonis filia (ubi ergo hic typi ratio?) ut hoc loco NECESSE sit, ad SPONSAM ECCLESIAM olim steri- lem & postea matrem filiorum factam lætantem re- spicere, cui etiam convenit, quod positi sunt ejus filii Principes in universa terra. NEQVE enim ID CONVENIT POSTERITATI Salomo- nis nisi in Christo. Hanc Ecclesiæ fæcunditatem prædixit etiam Esaias c. 49, 18. c. 54, 1. Pro prio- ribus Patriarchis (inquit Cyrillus) Abraham pater est multarum gentium, Isaac & Jacob sui populi, suarumque tribuum autoribus & propagatoribus. Ecclesia habet filios plurimorum, quorum singuli Patriarchæ existunt numerosissimarum familiarum, ac integros populos & numerosissimas gentes Christo & Ecclesiæ generat. De Apostolis ergo explicat, universo Orbi præfectis, & qui sequuti sint in Sacro ministerio, & quum Evangelium suum apud eos deposuerit Christus, quod regni ejus sceptrum est, ejus potestatem quomodo exercere eosdem, cum Calvino, ait. Christus enim per suos ministros Orbem sibi subegit, ac totidem sibi erexit principatus, quot fuerunt in diversis regionibus collectæ Ecclesiæ, & per illos fa- ctum est, quod nulli Monarchæ temporali com- petere potest, ut jura data sint terrarum Or- bi. Nam, ut notat Chrysostomus, Monarchæ Romanorum non potuerunt Persis legem dare, ne- que Persæ Romanis. Apostoli autem Christi no- mine Romanis & Persis, & aliis omnibus gentibus legem dederunt. Atque hæc de Sponsa, ac tertiæ classis argumentis.

Quarto argumentum peculiare, idque ite- rum invictum è conclusione Epithalamii suppetit. Memores erunt nominis tui Domine (in Ebræo & Græco habetur in singulari Memor ero, vel po- tius memorare faciam, ut sensum exprimat Vul- gata, & Hieronymus, ac Augustinus cum ea ha- bentes memorabunt) in omnes generationes & ge- nerationes; Propterea populi confitebuntur Tibi in æternum & in seculum seculi. Pollicetur ergo Deo laudes ob tam ingenita beneficia toti hu- mano generi præstita, quæ in hoc Psalmo de- cantavit, continuandas usque ad consummatio- nem seculi, imo in omnem æternitatem. Quæ iterum docent argumentum hujus Epithalamii non posse constitui nuptias Salomonis, sed unice de Christi nuptiis Spiritualibus eodem disseri. Habemus hic confitentem adversarium Calvi- num: NIHILO hoc magis congruit Salomoni, qui turpi & nefanda defectione memoriam nominis sui fœdavit; nam quum superstitionum sordibus terram Deo sacram polluit, nonne se conspersit æter- no dedecore & probro? Certe dignus fuit, cujus nomen perpetua oblivio sepultum tegeret. Nihilo plus gloriæ promeritus est Rehabeam, qui stolida sua superbia bonam regni partem amisit. Nul- lam itaque hic typi analogiam de nomine Salomonis in omni generatione commemorando invenire po- tuit: Ergo, concludit Calvinus, ut bonis constet Elogii veritas, ad Christum transire (dicere debe- bat, immediate sensuque literali de Christo expli- care, quia de nullo alio sensu literali intelligi po- test) NECESSE EST, cujus memoria semper viget ac floret. Nequicquam hic juvare conatur Calvi- num Rivetus; in Salomone ergo, inquit, repetitis illis quæ jam è Calvino adduximus, Christus Dei Filius prædicatur: vel ex illo ad Christum Regem facilis & sine ullo intervallo fit transitio, ita ut illius nuptiæ mysterium magnum sint: quod etsi occasione amoris omnis conjugalis ab Apostolo dictum sit Eph. 5. vers. 15. tamen in quibusdam expressius fuit adum- bratum, præsertim in istis, qui peculiares typi Chri- sti fuerunt, qualis fuit Salomo. Si in Salomone ceu typo Christus Filius Dei prædicatus in omni gene- ratione, necessum est, Salomonem ipsum prædi- catum fuisse, ut typus & antitypus respondeat.

Quod vero negat Calvinus, dignum judicans i- psum, cujus nomen perpetua oblivio sepultum te- gat. A Salomone vero ad CHRISTUM hic transitionem fieri quis credet, siquidem conclusio toti tractationi respondere debeat, & ejusdem no- men hic commemorandum prædicatur in omnem generationem, cujus pulchritudinem, gratiam, for- titudinem, gloriam, conjugium, & prolem hactenus deprædicavit Psaltes; quum de uno eodemque subjecto continuetur ad finem Epithalamium. Si ergo hic Messiæ nomen in omnem generatio- nem prædicandum significatur, non Salomonis, utique de Messia, non de Salomone, in Epithalamio actum fuisse agnoscendum. Quod amor Conju- galis adumbret mysterium amoris Spiritualis Chri- sti, non magis probat sensu literali & Grammati- co hoc Epithalamium Salomonem respicere, quam alios quoscunque conjuges fideles Regios. Et quanquam typus fuerit Salomo peculiaris Christi, in conjugio tamen cum Pharaonis filia ipsum PE- CULIAREM typum Christi fuisse probandum est: imo ostendendum etiam, EUM IN HOC PSALMO ut typum Christi proponi, deque eo sensu literali agi, qua typum Christi gesserit, quod κρινόμενον ipsum est, ac gratis assumitur tanquam certum & indubium, per meram petitionem prin- cipii. Non agi ad literam hic de Salomone, non sub ipso, ut typo, describi Messiæ conjugium spiri- tuale, sed immediate Messiam ipsum ejusque nu- ptias argumentum esse hujus Psalmi hactenus per totum Psalmum invictis documentis demonstra- tum est, quæ πρὸς ὄμμα ostendunt, non posse Salo- monem hic ad literam intelligi, aut filiam Pharao- nis aut liberos Salomonis. Perinde, uti in ultimo hoc versu non posse nomen Salomonis intelligi, in confesso est.

Quibus accedat nunc Quinto autoritas Apo- stoli Ebr. vers. 8. qui luculenter de Christo hunc Psalmum explicat, & quidem ita, ut ipsi uni ac soli eundem convenire, manifestissimum sit. Quod enim ad Filium Dei & de Filio Dei sensu proprio dictum testatur Apostolus, id de Salomone sensu literali dictum esse, affirmari non potest. Quod de Filio Dei ita dictum, ut non modo nulli alii ho- minum, sed ne angelo quidem ulli conveniat, teste A- postolo, id de Salomone explicari non potest. Quod de Filio Dei dictum demonstrat, Filium Dei non tantum Angelis superiorem, sed verum Deum esse, id nullatenus de Salomone agit, aut intelligi potest. Si sensu literali hoc oraculum Salomoni compete- ret, nomen DEI improprie acciperetur in eodem. Quomodo ergo è nomine Dei improprie acce- pto; & de Salomone enunciato æterna & in- finita Deitas Filii Dei demonstrari potest? La- befactatur ita profecto illustre vaticinium de Christo, evertitur insigne testimonium æter- næ Deitatis Christi, futile ac inutile reddi- tur argumentum præcipuum Apostoli ad de- monstrandam Deitatem Christi adhibitum: & quod penes ipsos Ebræos indubitatum erat (non n. hoc in probationem penes ipsos adduci po- tuisset, si dubitationi expositum fuisset) id maxime dubium redditur, imo prorsus enervatur. Quod autem hæc ad Filium DEI unice dicta sint, Apostolus sonora voce proclamat, adeo, ut de nulla Creatura, nullo Angelo dici potuerint, sed Deum Creatorem thronumque ejus æternum re- ferant, si audire velimus Appostolum: Quomdo ergo absque impietate ad Salomonem trahi illa pos- funt, aut ceu nativo ac germano senfu de Salomone dicta accipi? Sic enim Apostolus: Et ad angelos quidem dicit; Qui facit angelos suos spiritus, & mi- nistros suos flammam ignis. Ad Filium autem Thronus tuus, Deus, in seculum seculi: virga æquitatis virga regni tui, dilexisti justitiam & odi- sti iniquitatem, propterea unxit te Deus oleo exul- tationis præ participibus tuis. De quo autem illa dicta sunt sensu proprio & literali, de eo de- cantatum est totum Epithalamium; quod non po- test in partes ita discerpi, ut aliæ de hoc, aliæ de alio Regio Sponso, secundum literam agant, sed uti κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν sensu nativo & germano his duo- bus versibus de Messia solum agitur, ita Regem unum, Sponsumque unum, Messiam nempe, celebrat cum Sponsa sua Ecclesia, ab initio hy- mni usque ad finem ejusdem. Nonnulli referunt huc de regno Christi æterno illa Johan. 12. vers. 34. audivimus ex lege, quod Christus æternum maneat, quod nempe præsens locus ibi spectatus fuerit.)

Quod Sexto ulterius è collatione Cantici Sa- lomonei confirmatur. Quum enim manifestum sit, quod de eodem Rege ac Sponso, eademque Regina ac Sponsa utrobique agatur, è Cantici pia & accurata consideratione, magis magisque stabilimur, de solo Messia, secundum sensum pa- raphrasticum, quem Grammaticum vocant, in hoc Epithalamio actum fuisse. Quod in annotatis ad Canticum, ξὺν θεῷ, patebit. Theodoretius præfat. in Cantic. Arbitror, inquit, Salomonem à Patre (utpote Propheta, & magno quidem Pro- pheta) edoctum hæc conscripsisse. Audierat enim omnino illum ita cantantem: Astat Regina à dex- tris Tuis &c.

Subjungimus nunc postremo loco consensum Judæorum & Christianorum Interpp. Epithala- mium enim hoc de Messia exponit Thargum, cu- jus summa est inter Judæos autoritas. Ad vers. 3. pulchrior es Tu ô Messia &c. Spiritus Gratiæ & Prophetiæ est in labiis. Et ad vers. 7. Thronus gloriæ tuæ ô Deus &c. Exponunt etiam de Mes- sia Judæi, R. David Kimchi: Canticum amorum Domini ad Christum suum. Ad vers. 4. Gladius erit tua gloria, & licet Christi dies sint pax, tamen in bello Gogi incipient, ideo dicit, accinge gladium; Oleum lætitiæ dici ait: quia totus mundus in unctio- ne Christi & ejus missione lætabitur. Ad illud, E- quita super verbum mansuetudinis, quando coram inimicis equitat, non erit cum superbia, sed cum man- suetudine se geret, uti Zach. 9. equitat super Asi- num. Totum Psalmum secundum sensum Gram- maticum exponit de Messia, neutiquam vero de Salomone. Carnalia quidem & impia admiscet nugamenta de Uxoribus & Regno Messiæ, sed de typo Salomonis nihil habet; ac fatetur alios, sine dubio, saniores Judæos non Mulieres Messiæ, sed per similitudinem gentes terræ, Messiæ subditos intel- ligere. R. Aben Ezra de Rege Christo Filio Da- vidis hoc carmen agere docet, de quo Ezech. 34. vers. 24. Servus meus David erit Rex. Adducit quidem R. Gaon de Davide explicantem, sed ipse magis de Messia interpretatur, & Sanctos ejus so- cios hic dici ait: de Salomone vero neutiquam ex- ponit. R. Salomon Jarchi, Rex, inquit, est Deus benedictus & per ipsum Reges imperant, Prov. IIX. Ad vers. 10. Cum lætitia adducentur, ut Esa. LXVI. 20. Gentes adducent fratres vestros oblatio- nem DOMINO in curribus. Falsum ergo est, quod ait Grotius ac Rivetus, quod Judæi de Salomone ceu typo Christi ad literam hoc Epithalamium intelligant. Imo notat de Judæis sui temporis Nicolaus Lyranus, quod Psalmum hunc de Ahasvero a Mardochæo ad Estheram factum crediderint. Riebera vero in Comment. ad Ebr. 1. vers. 9. observat, hunc Psalmum de Messia cani, neque impios Judæorum magistros negare potuisse, licet ad sacrilegas & violentas expositiones confugiant; ac Genebrardus Comment. ad hunc Psalmum Genevensibus, de Salomone exponentibus, opponit non modo omnium Christianorum sensum, sed Rabbinos etiam recentiores. Quorum consensum etiam nobis largitur Bucerus, etsi in pervertendo Psalmo Grotio & Calvino ὁμόψηφος. Bellarminus in expl. hujus Psalmi summa consensione, ait, docent OMNES expositores, Latini, Græci, HEBRÆI, Psalmum hunc continere laudes Messiæ, & Sponsæ ejus Ecclesiæ. Quod fassus etiam Rivetus est: Apud OMNES Interpret. Psalmorum, ne EBRÆIS quidem exceptis, in confesso est, Psalm. XLV. esse carmen Epithalamium, hoc nuptiale, idque Spirituale, ac proinde non σαρκικῶς, sed μυστικῶς & πνευματικῶς intelligendum de Spirituali connubio inter Christum & Ecclesiam. Communem ergo cum Judæorum, tum Christianorum consensum, etiam Ecclesiæ Syræ (quæ titulum hujusmodi argumentum & summam complectentem Psalmo præfigit: Dictus Psalmus a Filiis Korah in diebus Mosis; ortus Messiæ: Et de Ecclesiæ & virtute gloriosa Domini: vel ut ex edit. Paris. Viccarsus habet: Filiorum Koreh scriptus Psalmus in diebus Mosis de resurrectione Christi & potentia) Grotio, Calvino, & Riveto non immerito opponimus. Etsi vero Rivetus obvertat, salvo illo consensu, adhuc quæstionem agitari, num scriptum fuerit hoc Carmen occasione nuptiarum Salomonis, ita ut sub Salomonis Sponsi & Ægyptiæ Sponsæ typo, cui Psalmus referatur, κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν sensu LITERALI PRIMO, tanquam sub imagine depingatur majestas & amplitudo regni Christi; quam dicit esse COMMVNEM EBRÆORVM sententiam, quam amplectuntur plerique Interpp. e Reformatis, CALVINVS, BVCERVS, JVNIVS & alii, ac inter Pontificios Jansenius; sed uti fatetur hisce Rivetus; Calvinum cum asseclis ἰυδαΐζειν, ac a communi veterum & recentiorum Interpp. consensu discedere, ita verum neutiquam est, quod COMMVNEM Judæorum sententiam a Calvini partibus stare asserit; contrarium e jam dictis liquet. Distinguendum erat inter veteres ac recentiores Judæos, quamvis & inter hos nonnulli Calvino saniores sint: Et immerito in partes illas abripitur Jansenius, explicatio etiam ipsa, utut novam crustam eidem Rivetus inducat, nemini facile se probatura est, qui argumenta adducta probe expenderit. Non de occasione quæritur concinnati hymni, quam vero nuptias Salomonis fuisse neutiquam probabitur, nec ullum rei hujus hactenus produci potuit fundamentum, imo repugnat ipse titulus, autores faciens Epithalamii filios Core, ut antea observavimus: sed de argumento Psalmi sensuque literali quæstio est. Eum vero Salomonis esse nuptias, nihil hic in toto Epithalamio est, quod vel obscure saltem doceat, nedum luculenter convincat: imo totus contextus non agi de nuptiis Salomonis, potenter convincit. Ut taceam, quod nonnulli urgent, quod nuptiæ Salomonis cum filia Pharaonis Idololatræ repugnarint expresso DEI mandato Deut. VII. neque Ebræo- rum sententia, quod intervenerint pacta conven- ta de religione, ut juxta legem Mosis filia Salo- monis coleret JEHOVAM, firmo stet talo, aut satis congruat, 1. Regum XI. cap. vers. 12. Ubi Beza Conjugium illud diserte reprehendi putat in Cap. 1. ad Ebr. unde Beza etiam a Praeceptore suo Calvino hic in alia omnia ivit, cui totus Psalmus mere allegoricus videtur, non typicus: siquidem ve- lit Psaltem ad nullam historiam vel rem gestam re- spexisse, sed tantum verbis a nuptiarum tempora- lium inter Regem aliquem, & Reginam similitu- dine mutuatis, descripsisse conjugium Christi Spirituale, eumque sensum primo & immediate sibi proposuisse, non quem verba sonant ubique, sed qui conveniat Christo, & Ecclesiae tantum in Spi- rituali conjunctione, ut sensus literalis & proxi- mus sit is, qui spiritualiter rem omnem explicat. Similiter Amesius lection. ad Psalm. David. Quamvis in Phrasibus allegoricis, quae in toto fere Psalmo adhibentur, respectus quidam habeatur ad gloriam Salomonis & ejus nuptias cum filia Pha- raonis, nihil tamen fuit vel in Filia Pharaonis, vel in Conjugio ejus cum Salomone, quod in hoc mysterio TYPI RATIONEM SUSTINERE POSSIT. Junius etiam, utut in paraphrasi vel summaria explicatione Biblica typum Salo- monem constituit Christi, in parallelis tamen lib. III. ad Ebr. I. tantum abest, ut typum il- lum admittat, ut etiam refellat eundem. Di- cit enim, singulos ferme versus habere, quae de Salomone commode nemo interpretari possit. Et postea: Quid ad Ecclesiam DEI, conjugium Salomonis in illius cœtibus celebrari, & hoc quo- que tempore celebrari, prout postulat inscriptio? Certe cum Deus sit autor & conscribendi Psalmi & in Ecclesia tradendi & canendi in cœtibus Sa- cris illius atque exponendi, non possumus bona fide, quin PSALMUM de æterno ac non temporali, Chri- sti ac NON SALOMONIS conjugio cum EC- CLESIA accipiamus; quod conjugium solum est Ecclesiæ Dei salutare, & post omnem hominum me- moriam celebrandum ab ea religiosissime. Pareus denique tametsi Calvinum suum adversus B. Hun- nium defendere tentarît, fateri tamen debuit, veteres plerosque ad literam Christi Spirituale con- nubium cum sua Ecclesia decantari velle sub nullo typo: nec eorum sententiam improbare potuit, tum quia singuli fere versiculi aliquid habent di- vinius vel majus, quam quod in Regem natura- lem competere possit: tum etiam, quia SANIO- RES HEBRÆI ipsi fatentur Psalmum tractare de Messia, & Thargum Chaldaicum expresse ali- quoties nominat Christum. Agnofcit ergo, saniores Hebræos Salomonem hic non constituisse typum, quod contra Rivetum observandum. Quanquam vero addit, non rejiciendam esse etiam Calvini sententiam, quia Salomo typum Christi gessit, & multa in eum juxta historiam utcunque convenire possunt, neque Calvinus omnia Salomo- ni, sed quaedam tantum, quaedam vero Salomoni NULLO PACTO applicet: Certum tamen o- mnino est, eum non posse non rejicere senten- tiam, quae de Salomone explicat secundum lite- ram, ut typo Christi, qui nihil de Salomone hic ca- ni, & ad literam non SALOMONIS, sed Chri- sti nuptias describi statuit: dum vero quaedam Salomoni nullo pacto convenire admittitur, in illis utique de Salomone non agi, ac proinde Salomonem non esse Regem illum, de quo ad literam in hoc Psalmo canitur, eviden- tissimum est, quia non nisi de uno Rege in eo secundum literam agitur. Quanquam veritati parcat Pareus, cum ista, quod Rex ille absolute bic vocetur Deus, & habeat thronum æternum, & quod unctus supra Consortes suos, & quod filios habeat numero & præstantia patribus non cedentes: NULLO PACTO ad Salomonem applicare Calvin. ait; Quomodo enim illa Salomoni apta- rit, ac perverterit Calvinus, circa singula no- tavimus. Denique etsi longe non solum tole- rabilius sed & tutius dicat Pareus, sub typo cer- to Psalmum ad Christum referre, quam sine typo, & sine litera certa Psalmum mere allegoricum face- re (quod B. Luthero per Sathanicam calumniam, uti demonstravit B. Hunnius, imputat,) & u- tram quis sequatur sententiam, seu Calvini de Salomone, seu veterum de Christo, secundum li- teram Psalmum explicantium, haud erraturum censeat, in Calv. Orthod. p. 229. 234. in Com- mentario tamen ad Ebræos c. 1. δευτέρας Φροντί- δας σοφωτέρας prodidit, refutans Calvini senten- tiam in Judæis, ac veterum sententiæ accedens: Judæi Psalmum eum intelligunt, quasi Epithala- mium in nuptias Salomonis cum Filia Pharaonis decantatum. Atqui matrimonium illud cum infi- deli conjuge contra legem contractum non obscure taxatur in sacra historia. Neque vero possunt ea, quæ profert Apostolus, Salomoni ULLA RA- TIONE competere. Non igitur DUBITAN- DUM videtur, totum Psalmum esse allegoricum carmen de spirituali connubio Christi & Ecclesiæ, ejusdem cum Cantico Canticorum, quod Salomo- ni adscribitur, argumenti. Calvinus quidem de Salomone pariter & Christo interpretatus est, sub ratione typi; quo nomine ab Hunnio pessime fuit laceratus. Sed neque solum Calvinum in ea esse sententia, neque per hanc quicquam concedi Ju- dæis, ostensum solide est in Calvino Orthodoxo l. 2. c. 31. At nullum alium, præter Musculum, Cal- vini asseclam, quam Cornerum nominavit, cu- jus vero explicationem à commentis Calvini ma- ximopere discrepare, hunc etiam omnino Judai- zare, ac multum labefactare Deitatis Christi lu- culentum testimonium, ac demonstrationem Apostolicam, evidenter ostendit B. Hunnius. Si nomen Dei improprie accipitur, secundum li- teralem & germanum Psaltis sensum, & thronus æternus solum quoad Regni Salomonici diuturnam durationem dicitur, quomodo, obsecro, ex hoc oraculo æterna, & immensa Deitas propriissime ita dicta Filii Dei, solide & invicte demonstra- bitur? Dicit quidem Calvinus, semper manere firmum, Christum solum esse hunc Regem Ecclesiæ Sponsum, æternum & verum Deum, sive sub nullo, sive sub aliquo typo Christi Spirituale cum Ecclesia connubium hic celebrari dicatur, dummodo omnia plene solideque ad Christum referantur. Sed quo- modo ad Christum plene solideque referri possunt, vel ad connubium Christi spirituale, quæ ad literam ac sensu à Spiritu S. intento de Salomone agunt, ejusque conjugium describunt, quomodo Chri- stum æternum verumque Deum demonstrare pos- sunt, quæ secundum proprium sensum Spiritus S. de Salomonis potestate ac divinitate metaphorice vel improprie ita dicta loquuntur? quomodo Salomo, si maxime typus Christi fuisset, in connubio cum Pharaonis filia, quod vero nullo, nullo, inquam, documento è Scripturis doceri po- test, typus æternæ ac veræ Deitatis Christi consti- tui potest?

Sic ergo causam Calvini, quæ Grotii etiam est, Pareus egit. Nihilo melius autem eam defen- dit Rivetus: neutram sententiam improbabilem, imo ex duabus, Judæorum nempe quorundam, ac Calvini, de Salomone, nec non Patrum & Interpp. Christianorum omnium, de Christo secundum lite- ram textum explicantium, unicam posse ac debere conflari, censens: quod etiam in commentario suo de Salomone cum Calvino, de Christo cum B. Gesnero, utriusque & explicatione & verbis ma- gnam partem transcriptis tentavit Riverus: sed quam infeliciter id tentarir, jam ostensum fuit. Et quid certius est, quam quod ita conetur Rive- tus polum arcticum antarctico copulare? Siqui- dem toto cœlo, quod dicitur, distent illæ sen- tentiæ, nec magis simul consistere, quam duæ contradictoriæ simul veræ esse possunt: agi nem- pe ad literam de Salomone, quod Calvinus & Grotius affirmant, & non agi de Salomone ad li- teram, sed unice de Christo, quod Patres & alii Interpp, Christiani, seniores etiam Judæi sum- mo consensu affirmant: Spiritum Sanctum nu- ptias hic describere, quoad sensum paraphrafti- cum, Salomonis cum Sponsa Ægyptia, & non describere illas, sed unice secundum sensum pa- raphrasticum Spirituales nuptias Christianæ Eccle- siæ decantare: Historiam hic referri carmine sa- cro, sensu immediato: etsi ea ceu typus propona- tur, ut respectus habeatur ad Spirituale connu- bium Christi hoc typo figuratum. Et meram tantum Prophetiam hic haberi, verbis allegoricis quidem propositam; sed quorum sensus immedia- tus Christum exhibeat, non vero typum aliquem Christi. Ac porro: Salomonem Sponsum hic commendari à formæ elegantia, Sermonis eloquen- tia, pugnandi fortitudine, felici regni successu, ob mansuetudinem, & justitiam, tum etiam à regni stabilitate, à vestimentorum suaveolentia, ab uxo- ris præstantia & splendore: quod Junius cum Cal- vino & Grotio vult: Et describi ac commendari ab his κριτηρίοις unice Christum Sponsum, nullo- que apiculo hæc de Salomone in hoc quidem Carmine celebrari: quod Christiani Interpp. omnes asserunt. Similiter directo ad Sponsam sermone compellari Pharaonis filiam, ut oblita paternæ domus, pristinæque conversationis Regi Salomoni sedula intendat & auscultet, quo ipsius decorem complectatur Sponsus, eaque summi hono- ris particeps à cæteris etiam mulieribus extollatur, & celebretur: Et conjugium cum eadem hic ita describi, ut typus constituatur Ecclesiæ è gentibus collectæ. Tum vero nullum hic verbum habe- ri de Pharaonis filia, nec typum ipsam constitui Ecclesiæ, sed totam illam descriptionem & pa- rænesin pertinere ad Sponsam Christi Ecclesiam, citra typi rationem: neque conjugium cum Æ- gyptia typum fuisse, aut ut typum propositum esse. Ulterius sermone iterum ad Sponsum verso Sponsæ Ægyptiæ pulchritudinem cani, & reliqua ornamen- ta, tum felicitatem liberorum, eorumque qui ex ea nascentur dignitatem: Et è contrario, non cani hic pulchritudinem Sponsæ Ægypticæ & ornamen- ta ejus, aliaque, sed ea omnia unice de Ecclesia Sponsa Christi celebrari. Denique cum versu po- stremo habeatur, in sempiternum per omnes gene- rationes HUJUS SPONSI memoriam celebran- dam, & populos eidem laudem sempiternam redditu- ros prænuncietur, si in Psalmo ipse Salomo ut Spon- sus celebratus fuit, ceu typus CHRISTI, sequitur ἄτοπον, quod ista conclusio etiam Psalmi, HUJUS SPONSI memoriæ sempi- ternæ dicata, secundum literam de Salomone intelligenda sit, siquidem Psalmi συνέχεια sibi constare, & Calvini, Grotii, Riveti sententia obtinere debeat. At quoad reliquos Interpret. omne certum est, memoriæ æternæ Christi Regis cum Oden illam universam, tum conclusionem quoque dicatam esse, atque ita prologon vel exordium & propositionem, logon seu narrationem, Sponsum & Sponsam ac nuptias prolixe describentem, & Epilogon seu conclusionem æternam ab omnibus generationibus gloriam promittentem, ac prædicentem, optime sibi consonare, atque unice CHRISTUM JESUM Sponsum mysticum celebrare. Ita ergo manifestissimum, διˆα πασῶν, & in terminis, quod dicitur, contradictoriis discrepare illas expositiones. Ideoque nulla arte unquam conciliari posse, nisi forte quis etiam ipsum Judaismum cum Christianismo conciliare velit, vel ausit.

Nequicquam autem Rivetus temperamentum hic adhibet, non quidem in omnibus, sed in quibusdam hujus Psalmi sententiis esse sensum aliquem historicum, qui PRIMO ad Salomonem & uxorem ejus tanquam ad typos referri possit; esse tamen etiam nonnulla, quæ NE QUIDEM IN TYPO CONVENIANT, & de Christo & Ecclesia IMMEDIATE exponenda sint.

Nam si NONNULLA in hoc Psalmo IMMEDIATE de Christo, & de Ecclesia exponenda citra typum, OMNIA ita necessario in eodem sensu immediato accipienda erunt. Ratio consequentiæ est invicta: quia in Prologo, λόγω ipso, & Epilogo, de uno Rege, de uno Sponso, sensu immediato agi, de una item Regina, de unica Sponsa, Sole clarius liquet. De hoc uno Rege canere instituit Propheta, hujus unius Regis pulchritudinem, facundiam, fortitudinem, successum, virtutes, thronum, majestatem, & splendorem describit: hujus unius nuptias & sponsam proponit: Unius etiam Reginæ, Sponsæ ipsius, debita munia, pulchritudinem, & splendorem, felicitatem, & liberorum dignitatem canit: Et de hujus unius nomine, de generatione in generationem, imo in omnem æternitatem celebrando vaticinatur. Si in unico versu saltim nequeat Salomo per Regem intelligi, aut in unico solum prædicato, aut filiæ Pharaonis pariter unicum solum attributum in hoc Psalmo nullatenus conveniat, α̉ναντιῤῤήτως concluditur, in nullo versu, quoad nullum prædicatum, Salomonem hic SUBJECTUM esse, de quo Psalmus sensu immediato agat, nullumque prædicatum de filia Pharaonis hic efferri; siquidem unum tantum subjectum hic sit, & unus Rex, de quo omnia prædicata secundum sensum proprium, immediatum, literalem, & paraphrasticum efferuntur: uti una ejus etiam Regina solum introducitur. Dico ego opera mea REGI, ait Psaltes in Prologo v. 1. Speciosus forma es præ filiis hominum, ad REGEM illum dicit in λόγω vel narratione v. 3. & quæ porro sequuntur. Astitit REGINA à dextris suis v. 10. Et ad illam v. 12. concupiscet REX ILLE, de quo hactenus unice actum, decorem tuum, quoniam ipse est Dominus tuus. Et v. 15. adducentur REGI ILLI virgines post eam Reginam. Et v. 18. in Epilogo, memores erunt NOMINIS TUI (ô Rex) in omni generatione. Quis adhuc diversa subjecta ausit assignare in tanta rei evidentia, quis hymnum perpetuo cohærentem, unoque filo & stylo contextum discerpere, ac in nonnullis, quoad sensum immediatum, Salomonem pro subjecto ingerere præsumet, utut in plerisque quoad imme- diatum sensum Christum nostrum pro subjecto Epi- thalamii admittat?

## 45:6
Verse 7.

THY THRONE O GOD IS FOR EVER AND EVER) It can be translated from the Hebrew: Thy throne, O God (enduring for) ages and generations. Throne, that is, firmness.

He has exhibited a double perversity in a few words, both of them utterly detestable, undoubtedly devised for the sake of the Jews and Arians. While first he wishes for 'throne' not to be understood as a throne, or Kingdom, just as the emphasis of this word, and the customary usage, by which 'throne' is accustomed to be said of a throne, and consequently or metonymically of a Kingdom, and not to mention the added word 'scepter', which agrees with a kingdom, and the mention of anointing, which is accustomed to be done for a Kingdom, as also of illustrious royal virtues, the love of justice and hatred of iniquity, and then the authority of the Apostle Heb. 1:8, who receives the word concerning the throne and kingdom, clearly demands: And by all interpreters hitherto the word has been accepted with consenting suffrage: He says that FIRMNESS is signified: without example in Scripture: without reason for a new interpretation, which has not hitherto easily come into anyone's mind. Then indeed Grotius attaches a completely different meaning to the testimony, and whereas by the common reckoning of interpreters the Deity of Christ and His eternal Throne are established here by the common reckoning of Christians, nay, this prophecy is brought forward by the Apostle himself to assert the eternal Deity to Christ, he attempts to snatch this meaning from it with a new and hitherto unheard-of version, perverting the individual words, transforming the seat, as I said, into firmness, changing the name of God, which is used in the vocative case, as the Apostle testifies, into the nominative case, and neglecting the duration of the throne of this King, which is said to persist for ages of ages, substituting the duration of God; finally, in place of a literal proposition, he substitutes a figurative one; since the seat of this King is said to endure forever, he makes the seat or firmness of this King God metonymically, because He is the cause of that firmness; and so that he may be able to pervert these things in this way, he inserts of his own the word παρενθετι- xῶς God (enduring for) ages, which neither appears in the text, nor can be gathered from the same. For what is clearer than that this Prophet addresses that King to whom he has hitherto directed his speech? Whom he has pointedly expressed with second-person pronouns, and addressed in the vocative case, 'Fairer (i.e., YOU) in form than the sons of men: Grace is poured upon YOUR lips, therefore God has blessed YOU forever, GIRD YOURSELF with YOUR sword upon YOUR thigh, O MIGHTY ONE (behold the vocative case expressed!) In YOUR splendor, and in YOUR beauty, RIDE ON, prosperously PROCEED, and REIGN, and YOUR right hand shall lead YOU wonderfully. YOUR arrows are sharp, the peoples fall under YOU.' Therefore, just as he has addressed Him hitherto, so he now addresses the same one thus: 'YOUR throne, O God, is for ever and ever.' Calling Him God, whom he previously called MIGHTY ONE in the vocative case, and of whose throne he treated. What is more certain than that he does not describe God the Father and His eternity here, but continues in the description of his King, whom he had begun to celebrate? Whose beauty, eloquence, strength, success, right hand, and arrows he has hitherto described, he now exhibits His throne; that it endures for ever and ever, and the scepter, which is most upright and mere uprightness, and the administration, and the anointing, and the splendor. It would therefore be foreign, when the preceding and following parts are occupied in describing the King, that here, where His throne is set forth, it should be adorned with no eulogy, and no dignity of His should be added, but in place of that, a periphrasis of GOD should be substituted: and that the eternity of God the Father should be introduced irrelevantly, where it was necessary to deal with the duration of the Bridegroom's throne. What is more evident than that not only the seventy Elders, but the Holy Spirit Himself also, in Heb. 1, 8, accepted the word God in the vocative case, and from that point established the Deity of our Christ, and taught that the eternity of His throne is designated here? And to the Angels and His ministers a flame of fire: But to the Son: Thy throne O God is for ever and ever. He says that the Son is thus addressed and named: when He brings those words to the Son. And He uses the name ὁ θεὸς in the vocative case, as regards the sense, as the Greeks are accustomed to use it thus. And from this Oracle He demonstrates that the Son of God is God, since the Angels are only creatures of God: that the Son of God obtains an eternal throne, since the Angels were created for ministry. It is worthy of detestation that Grotius, in explaining the Psalm, treads more in the footsteps of the Jews and the Arians than of the Christians and Catholics. For the Jews, R. Aben-Ezra with R. Gaon, pervert the sentence in a similar manner: Thy throne O God He will establish; or Thy throne is the throne of God: just as Solomon is said to have sat upon the throne of God 1 Chron. 29, 23. But the Jews nevertheless saw clearly that the name אלהים here must be taken in the vocative case: not only Rabbi David Kimchi, but also R. Aben-Ezra: and therefore R. Aben-Ezra used this note; The King is called God, as in Exod. 22, 28, indicating that the word God is to be taken improperly, just as judges are called Gods. The Chaldean Targum certainly acknowledges that the Messiah is called God here. The throne of thy glory O God. But with what execration shall we judge it worthy, that Grotius, for the sake of the Jews, has not feared to pervert the Apostolic Interpretation here also, and to overturn the Apostle's Argument entirely. For O God, he says in his annotations to Heb. 1, 8, in the Hebrew is אלהים, which name is indeed accustomed to be given to many, whether Angels or Judges: but when it is attributed to one, it befits God alone: because then the speech is elliptical for אלוה אלהים, as we have said elsewhere (There is no need for an ellipsis, nor can it be solidly proven: but that the mystery of the plurality of persons underlies it, we have proven by an invincible demonstration of this mystery in chapter 1). The sense therefore is: God Himself is thy perpetual seat: that is, if we look to Solomon: just as seats hold men unshaken, so God will always sustain thee in the kingdom: But if we look to Christ: God Himself will sustain thee in a kingdom that will never fail. Thus a double and clearly disparate sense is affixed to the same words, so that the words for ever and ever denote eternity concerning Christ: but do not denote eternity, but long duration concerning Solomon: what is explained as the throne by the Apostle is understood through a new Metaphor concerning sustenance, and God is compared to a seat, on account of stability, without example in Scripture, because nowhere is God said to be the throne or seat of a man, whom He sustains: and the former gloss handed down to the Psalms is deserted. For here perpetuity is attributed to the seat: but to Psalm 45, perpetual duration is attributed to God. And the name אלהים ὁ θεὸς, which the Apostle teaches in express words is attributed to the Son of God, from which he also demonstrates His supreme excellence above the Angels, is explained not of the Son of God, but of God the Father, and the nerve of the Apostle's entire proof is cut. If the Apostle had taken the word ὁ θεὸς as the subject of the proposition, and in the nominative case, he would not have interposed commas, but would have simply said ὁ θρόν[ος] ὁ θεὸς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα: but the added commas do not in any way bear the distortion of Grotius, ὁ θρόν[ος] ὁ θεὸς, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. Whence hitherto no one has been found among the Doctors and Interpreters who doubted at least that the vocative case obtains here, and that the Apostle addressed the Messiah by the word God, and by that argument also demonstrated the excellence above the Angels, nay the Deity, which he had set out to prove. For it is most well known that the Greeks use the nominative in the sense of the vocative through an Attic construction κατ’ ἀντίπτωσιν, which was done by the LXX Interpreters in Psalm 51, 3, 60, 1, 22, 1, and is in the N.T. Matt. 22, 46. Luke 18, 13, whence Aquila in our Psalm for the sake of evidence rendered the word Elohim as θεὲ O God, but Jerome in the Latin translated it as Dee, whose words it is helpful to transcribe from Epist. ad Princip. virgin. Tom. 3. p. 108. Understand two persons, of Him who is anointed God, and who anointed. Whence also Aquila interprets the Hebrew word Elohim אלהים, not in the nominative case, but in the vocative, saying, θεὲ, and we for the sake of understanding have placed Dee, which the Latin Language does not receive, lest anyone perversely think that the God of the beloved and most beloved and King is named Father twice. For although the Father is in the Son, and the Son in the Father: and they are to each other both inhabitant and throne, yet in this place the speech is directed to the King, who is God, and it is said to him that his empire (for I understand this as the throne, according to that which is written: Of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne) has no end: which indeed the Angel also announced to Mary: The Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David, and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever, and of his kingdom there shall be no end. And it is so clear that the Messiah is addressed here, that even the Socinians themselves, who have been accustomed to use all the racks to distort the testimonies of the Deity of Christ, have been forced to acknowledge it. Crellius lib. 1. de Deo & attribut. div. cap. 9. confesses that an illustrious example is had here, that Christ is called Elohim. The Racovians in the German version render it thus: Dein Stul, O GOtt, bleibt in alle Ewigkeit: Conf. Comment. Schlicht. in the Epistle to the Hebrews, at chapter 1, 8. Enjedinus indeed was the first to bring forward this gloss here, in his Explanation of places of the Old and New Testament on Hebrews 1, 8, p. 389, from whom Grotius received the same, which therefore, so that you may see the collusion with the Arians, it is helpful to transcribe: Those words, he says, can be explained in such a convenient way that the word God is said neither of Solomon nor of Christ, and is not the vocative case, but the nominative, and is understood of God the Father of both Solomon and Christ, in this sense: God is your throne forever: that is, God will establish the throne for you forever. But others judged that gloss so inconvenient that no one wished to follow Enjedinus, but openly testified that here Christ is called God. Rightly Rivetus: who does not see that the exposition is distorted? For who ever speaks thus, or what example will they bring forward, in which the verb is missing, which ought to have been most expressly stated? Who also will prevent, if it is permitted to invent or supply anything at will, that someone equally impious might supply the word, will destroy, or will shatter.

Verse of the same. A SCEPTRE OF UPRIGHTNESS, A SCEPTRE OF THY KINGDOM) By the royal sceptre in Solomon is understood metonymically the manner of government: in Christ the word of the Gospel, first preached by him.

These things, and what we note regarding the following verse, it seemed good to add here from the annotations of Grotius on Hebrews 1, 8, so that his inventions might be discussed more fully. Thus indeed a double sense is again fashioned, completely disparate, of the same proposition. And it is explained concerning Solomon, which in no way suits him. For it is a matter here of a sceptre of such a kind that it is eternal, of an eternal Throne, which is joined with power performing miracles, with a sword and arrows penetrating the very hearts, which is most just and most equitable, and never contaminated by any stain of injustice, which brings the highest love of justice and hatred of iniquity, for the bearing of which a communication of immense gifts is required, of divine omnipotence, omniscience, and omnipresence, because it is to be borne through the whole world: by the power of which princes over the whole earth are established: which implies the ἀξίωμα (dignity) of adoration; whose glory is to be celebrated unto every generation, nay, unto all eternity. Which certainly in no way befits the Solomonic scepter, but solely the scepter of our Messiah. Here the kingdom is described primarily by eternity and rectitude. Eternity, however, because not only is the word עֹולָם used, but the particle עַד is also added to it, which denotes perpetuity, and when added to the word עֹולָם, it brings about an absolute eternity, as in Psalm 10:16 and elsewhere, whence Rivetus acknowledges that this does not properly befit Solomon, nor can it be attributed to any kingdom of the earth, because those kingdoms have their periods and limits by which they are circumscribed; but that this kingdom befits Christ is evident from Isaiah 9:7, Daniel 7:14, Luke 1:33. And in this all Christian interpreters agree, that an eternal kingdom is described here; whence it follows of its own accord that those words cannot be explained concerning Solomon. Our blessed Luther is excellent here, Tom. 3, Jena, Latin, in his enarration of this Psalm, p. 454: Thy seat, i.e., thy royal throne, is eternal. It is a free confession and full of admiration, that before the revealed Gospel he predicts such a King, to whom no other person succeeds, but who eternally administers his kingdom for ages. Therefore, the Psalm cannot be understood of a temporal kingdom, or of a King who is only a man. And afterwards: It is clear, therefore, from this passage, that Christ is true man (because he is said to be fairer than the children of men) and yet is also a King not temporal, but eternal, that is, also true God, who although he died, yet rose again from death. For to conquer death is not of man or of a creature. For just as the whole creation is of one God, so also no one except God creates life, which itself is also a creature of God. It follows, therefore, that Christ is true God, because he creates life and devours death.

The other attribute of the scepter is supreme and absolute rectitude: because the scepter is called one of rectitude, that is, supremely straight. There is no King who does not sometimes deviate from rectitude, whether he does it knowingly and prudently, or slips out of infirmity, to which we are all subject. But of this King it can be said simply, thy scepter, a scepter of rectitude, which befits Christ alone. Blessed Luther again excellently: Other kingdoms, however happy and well-constituted they may be, yet have infinite vices, so that it is impossible to find one Polity in which very many and very great sins do not adhere. For they are mixed with tyranny, ignorance, negligence, and all desires of glory, lust, vengeance, and avarice, so that it is necessary for him who rules to do injury to many. But in the kingdom of Christ there is no vice, there is no injury, injustice is not tolerated, not even for a moment. Christ alone in his kingdom has a straight scepter. Why this? Because our King has the word of God, which is pure, even to a MATHEMATICAL POINT. The kingdom of Christ suffers no vice, and that for a double reason. I. By reason of the divine Law: Because we suffer our sins to be argued and judged. For although Christ tolerates sins in our life, he does not, however, tolerate them in the law and doctrine. But the law is most pure, and most purely kills sin. II. By reason of our head and King, in whom we believe. For as far as Christ is concerned, there is nothing vicious in us, but as far as we are concerned, we are most defiled and full of concupiscence, fear of death, and despair. Christ, however, is not such, because it is written of him: No guile was found in his mouth. When, therefore, we believe in him, we are accounted righteous through him, justified in faith; then after the death of this flesh, in the other life we shall reach the Mathematical point of justice, and we shall have in us that absolute justice, which now, believing in Christ, we have only imputatively by the merit of Christ. But then, when those things are revealed in the future life, all tyranny of death will be absent, so that no fear, no pallor will adhere to us, but all things will be most sweet and most pleasant.
