Create in me a clean heart, O God; because he had said that he was born in iniquity, that is, that the concupiscence inherent in him had drawn him toward sin itself, he prays to God that He may help him against his concupiscence, so that he may not sin again: and this is a clean heart. Menasseh Ben-Israel also agrees with these in part, who in Conciliator Hispanus on the Psalms, page 66, concludes from this that not only David, but the whole human species after sin was introduced into the world, sins from its origin. And in the book on Fragility, page 2, he has this to say about this passage: Behold I was formed in iniquity, and in sin my mother warmed me: Whether this is understood of the common mother, who was Eve, or whether David spoke here only of his own, he wished to signify that sin is as it were natural and inseparable in this life: Therefore also after the committed offense Eve conceived, and as many as have been born since, not according to a rule conformable to right reason, but they were produced with disturbed and lustful affections. Observing, therefore, one of our ancient sages, R. Aha, that that word of the Psalmist בעוון with the sin, abounded with one Vau, he infers from it: that David meant to signify that it is impossible even for the pious and those excellent in virtue pertains the answer which R. Hakkadosch gave to the Emperor Antoninus, which is read reported in the Thalmud, Sanhedrin chap. 11. From what time does concupiscence rule over man, whether at the moment of absolute formation, or from birth? Resp. From formation. The Jews therefore see here a natural proclivity to sin, they acknowledge a congenital sin, which the Christian Grotius could not see, or at least did not wish to acknowledge.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

ECCE ENIM IN INIQVITATIBVS CONCEPTVS SVM, ET IN PECCATIS CONCEPIT ME MATER MEA) Illud enim abest in Hebræo. Sensus est: Non nunc tantum, sed & a pueritia mea, sæpius peccavi. Est enim lo- quendi genus ὑπερβολικὸν, ut ostendit collatio locorum Job. 31, 18. Psalm 22, 9. Pf. 58, 4. Pfal. 71, 5. 6. Esa. 48, 8. Oc- casione hujus gravis criminis, meminit & antecedentium quamlibet non tam gravium. Pro concepit in Hebræo est fovit.

Licet particula causalis in Hebræo non adsit κα- τὰ λέξιν, adest tamen κατὰ διάνοιαν, quam expref- sit vulgatus interpres. Sensus autem, quem adfert Grotius, mera est ςρεβλότης, quam è Pelagii & Soci- ni Schola hausit. Hos enim inficiatione peccati originalis sequitur. Proinde non mirum, quod eo- dem modo detorqueat verba Davidis, etsi ea Sole clariora sint. Sic enim Socinus in prælect. Theol. cap. 5. p. 12. de hoc loco: Satis constare potest, figu- ratum esse istum loquendi modum, atque HYPER- BOLICUM, ut illum etiam Psalm. 58. v. 4. Abalie- nati sunt impii à vulva: erraverunt ab utero lo- quentes mendacium. Similis locus est Esa. 48, 8. quibus loquendi modis peccata exaggerantur, & effi- cacius vituperantur. Unde patet, quod loca etiam parallela à Socino petierit Grotius. Quanquam adhuc plus concedat hic Socinus Catholicis, quam Grotius, olim Socini adversarius. Admittit enim verbis subjunctis, innui hoc loco humanam fragili- tatem, quasi peccatum hoc res quædam plane natura- lis sit, non autem quod ita sit revera. Grotius vero nihil aliud innui vult, quam quod David à pueritia peccarit. Sed glossa hæc ab ipsis Hieropsaltis ver- bis refellitur: Non tantum sæpius sese peccasse à pueritia dicit, sed etiam in peccatis conceptum, & iniquitate infectum, cum primum fovit ipsum, vel calefecit mater: ut cum primo calore nativo sta- tim peccato corruptus fuerit. Quæ est ipsa peccati originalis descriptio, prout id ab Ecclesia Catholi- ca definitur. Tum vero nulla necessitas est ad figu- ratum loquendi genus recurrendi. Non autem fas est in Scripturæ interpretatione vocum proprieta- tem relinquere citra necessitatem, fatentibus ipsis Socinianis, nisi è Scriptura ludum & jocum facere velimus. Neque probari hyperbole potest è locis designatis. Psalmo enim 58, 4. & Es. 48, 8. itidem ad peccatum originale respectus habetur. Christus Sanctus ab utero citra hyperbolen dicitur Luc. 1, 35. Pf. 71, 5. 6. respectus fit ad circumcisionis Sacra- mentum, per quod infantibus octavo à nativitate die ἄνωθεν regeneratis fides conciliatur, denique, si omnino Job. 31, 18. admittatur hyperbole, aut etiam Psalm. 71, 5. 6. quid hoc ad præsentem locum? Ibi enim exaggerari pietatem Jobi, ac fiduciam Davi- dis, dici potest: Hic autem justo magis exaggera- ri peccatum, qua specie veri statuetur, quum nun- quam satis malum illud ἐυπερίςατον naturæ nostræ intime infixum, qua caro nascimur de carne, & τῇ Φύσει sumus filii iræ, describi, gravitasque ejus ex- plicari possit? Et quomodo hac Grotiana glossa præsenti confessioni peccatorum, ac contritioni ob peccata Davidis, quem hic de peccatis suis tam vehementer angi, tam anxie conqueri, singula verba testantur, congruit, quod nempe tantum occasione gravis criminis meminerit aliorum à pueritia, quamlibet non gravium? Non nuda so- lum mentio fit, sed vehementer dolet, & angitur de peccatis, cor contritum Davidicum: neque ex oc- casione solum iniquitatem, in qua conceptus, com- memorat, sed eandem præprimis ceu fontem o- mnis mali detegit, ac de eadem gravissime conque- ritur: nec peccata solum infirmitatis & incogitantiæ in pueritia designata, sed horribilem illam depra- vationem naturæ, qua in peccatis calefactus & iniqui- tatibus conceptus pravæ libidini & concupiscentiæ in ipso matris utero, cum primum calorem vita- lem nactus est, obnoxius fuit. Num hæc sonant peccata NON GRAVIA? Ecce IN INIQVITATE conceptus sum, & in PECCATIS concepit me mater mea; Rectius Calvinus: David unius peccati agni- tione longum totius vitæ examen trahit, donec in se nihil reperiat præter peccatum. Jam non modo pecca- ti unius vel plurium etiam, sicut hactenus, se reum fa- tetur, sed altius conscendit, se ab utero matris nihil aliud attulisse quam peccatum, & naturaliter se to- tum corruptum esse, & quasi vitiis delibutum. In tex- tu enim originali non immerito dicitur in singula- ri, in INIQVITATE ET PECCATO, quia pec- catum originale, quod in conceptione contraximus, unum est, non multum: ut hic Bellarm. observat. LXX. vero verterunt, in numero multitudinis, quia unum illud peccatum est quasi fons omnium aliorum peccatorum & in illo concluduntur omnia, ut habet Menochius. Denique misericordiæ Dei viscera mo- vere vult David; quapropter non ex occasione solum peccatorum pueritiæ, quæ pro levibus habet Grotius, mentionem facit, sed pravam concupi- scentiam per conceptionem in ipso matris utero hæreditario propagatam, ut verba sonant, Deo si- stit, vi cujus homo caro natus de carne tantum ad peccatum proclivis est, omnibus diebus vitæ suæ, ut miseriæ hujus Deus Pater omnis misericordiæ gratiosissime misereatur, & peccatis, in quæ per legem peccati in membris hærentem, præcipitatus fuit, veniam propitius concedere dignetur. Reclu- dit hoc versu, ut recte B. Gesnerus noster, Prophe- ta vitiosum fontem, & venenatam scaturiginem o- mnium peccatorum, quæ est ingenita illa & ab Ada- mo usque derivata naturæ humanæ corruptio & de- pravatio. Accusat itaque David totam suam natu- ram, omnesque facultates animæ & corporis, quod vitiosæ sint, & peccati contagio infectæ, & ad bo- num quoque penitus demortuæ. De nativitate loquitur, cum ait, se in peccatis genitum esse: ultra nativitatem in ipsum quoque conceptum afcendit, quando conqueritur, quod in peccatis à matre con- ceptus sit. Istud proinde hoc versu David signifi- cat, se non tum demum judicii divini reum esse fa- ctum, cum Uriæ uxorem rapuit, sed nascenti labem istam adhæsisse, quin etiam altius rem repetendo fa- tetur, semini è quo formatus sit, malitiam & naturæ corruptelam penitus infixam fuisse. Adde, quod ideo David precetur, ut cor novum in se creare ve- lit Deus, ut antiqua pravitas, quam à parentibus contraxit, mortificetur, & spiritus innovetur in vi- sceribus, ut carni non indulgeat, sed per Spiritum eidem resistere valeat. Quod etiam R. Aben-Ezra observavit. Didicisse hic poterat Grotius veram verborum Davidicorum sententiam vel ex ipsis Je- suitis, quibus valde ipse delectatur, imo ex quibus- cunque Romano - Catholicis Interpp. Omnes enim hic ex asse consentiunt, quod Psaltes de pec- cato agat originali. Quarta ratio, inquit Bellarm.

ducitur a prima origine, & primi hominis peccato in nos transfuso per generationem, ex quo facti sumus infirmi & proclives ad peccandum, & ob hanc qua- si naturalem miseriam misericordia digni sumus. Quem sequitur, ut fere solet in Psalmis, Menochius : Similiter explicat Tirinus, ad Athanasium, Hiero- nymum, Augustinum, & Theodoretum, & Grego- rium provocans. Nec est, qui vel e Pontificiis, vel e Calvinianis aliter explicet, aut hyperbolen somniet. Veteres etiam Ecclesiae Dd. unanimi suffragio hunc locum de peccato originali accepe- runt, tum ante mota a Pelagio certamina, tum ma- xime, ubi Pelagius peccatum originis inficiaretur. Antiquorum sententias produxit S. Augustinus lib. 1. contr. Pelag. cap. 2. Tom. 7. oper. pag. 939. & nos ex eo in Arminianismi Considerat. Cap. 12. Cy- priani, quod secundum Adam carnaliter natus con- tagium mortis antiquae prima nativitate contraxerit : Hilarii, qui in expos. Psalm. 118. vivere se, inquit, in hac vita non reputat, quippe qui dixerat : Ecce in iniquitatibus conceptus sum, & in delictis concepit me mater mea: Scit sub peccati origine, & sub pec- cati lege se esse natum. Ambrosii ex Apol. David. Antequam nascimur, maculamur contagio, & ante usuram lucis originis ipsius excipimus injuriam, & in iniquitate concipimur. Gregorii Nazianzeni, qui de Baptismo agens : Per hunc, inquit, primae nativitatis maculae purgantur, per quas in iniquitati- bus concipimur, & in delictis genuerunt nos matres nostrae. Recentiores qui adversus Pelagium, & post eundem scripsere, non est quod adducamus : Consentiunt enim omnes, peccatum in quo David se conceptum dicit, esse originale peccatum, quod Ecclesia Catholica contra Pelagianam haeresin propugnavit. Quid quod de Judaeis etiam ipsis intellexerint nonnulli, hic de peccato originali sermonem esse. Apud R. David Kimchi ad h. l. haec habentur: Aggravat peccatum suum a duratione, quia concupiscentia est in corde fixa, & quasi forma- tur in illo. Et post ea: vel dicit formatus, quia ex semine factus est, sicut homo, qui seminat semen ama- rum, fructus profert similes; ideo inclinat homo na- turaliter ad concupiscentiam malam supra reliqua peccata: in quam sententiam adducit Kasvenaki R. Salomo Jarchi: Quomodo, inquit, non peccem? origo mea corrupta est, atque hinc ea peccata. Aliter: origo mea est a viro & faemina, qui iniquitate pleni sunt. Aben-Ezra ad hunc versiculum : ECCE : Propter CONCUPISCENTIAM INNATAM cor- di humano dicitur, in iniquitate genitus sum: at- que sensus est: quod a nativitate implantatum sit cordi humano figmentum malum. Quod vero di- cit, & in peccato fovit me mater mea, est modus lo- quendi peregrinus, quasi calefacta est ex me. Et sunt qui dicunt, quod hic indicet, Evam non peperisse, nisi postquam peccasset. Ad vers. 12. Cor purum crea in me Deus; quia dixerat se in iniquitate genitum, hoc est, quod concupiscentia inhaerens ad peccatum ipsum pertraxisset, precatur Deum, ut eum juvet contra concupiscentiam suam, ne iterum peccet: at- que hoc est cor purum. Accedit his ex parte etiam Menasses Ben-Israel, qui in concil. Hisp. in Psalm. pag. 66. hinc concludit, non solum Davidem, sed omnem humanam speciem post peccatum in mundum introductum, ab origine sua peccare. Et libr. de Fra- gil. pag. 2. de hoc loco ita habet: En in iniquitate formatus sum, & in peccato fovit me mater mea: Sive autem hoc intelligatur de matre communi, quae fuit Eva, sive de sua solum David hic dixerit, signifi- care voluit, esse peccatum quasi naturale, & insepara- bile in hac vita: Ideo & post commissum delictum E- va concepit, & quosquot postea geniti sunt, non juxta regulam rectae rationi conformem, sed affectus per- turbatos & libidinosos producti sunt. Advertens igitur unus antiquorum nostrorum sapientum R. Aha, quod illa vox Psalmistae בעוון cum delicto uno Vau abun- daret, inde infert: Davidem significare voluisse, etiam piis & excellentibus virtute impossibile esse, nunquam in aliquod peccatum incurrisse. Huc facit etiam R. Hakkadosch, quod Antonino Imperatori dedit, responsum, quod in Thalmud relatum legi- tur Sanhedrin cap. 11. Concupiscentia ex quo tempore dominatur homini, utrum in momento absolutae for- mationis, an à nativitate? Resp. à formatione. Vi- dent ergo Judaei hic proclivitatem ad peccandum naturalem, agnoscunt peccatum congenitum, quod videre non potuit, vel certe agnoscere noluit Gro- tius Christianus.

## 51:6
Ver. 8.

BEHOLD, FOR YOU HAVE LOVED TRUTH] For even here the 'for' is lacking in the Hebrew, and you would translate it more correctly, 'yet truly you love truth in the reins,' that is, inwardly; you do not love the wicked.

The causal sense can entirely be retained, so that a reason is rendered for the confession, because God does not want hypocrisy hiding sins, but loves truth, i.e., sincerity, so that one may entirely sincerely acknowledge sin: or also, so that the reason for that most grave corruption, of which the Psalmist had complained, may be subjected; as if to say, I complain with merit of so great an evil fixed deeply in my heart: for you do not love superficial and external probity, but the intimate sincerity of the heart, in the reins, which how would it be found in a man who is entirely conceived in sins? Whither goes Calvin's explanation: He asserts that God requires not only that our life be composed to some form of justice, but that the heart be pure and well purged of all deceit: for this reason he says God wants sincerity in the inward parts, and demands sincere purity of heart. Thus, therefore, the discourse is either about the sincerity of confession, which is required in penitents, or about the sincerity of the heart and reins, which God desires in man, but because of original sin does not find, by which the heart may be free from all deceit, so that therefore the only refuge remains to the Messiah, by whose blood our sins are purified through faith. Others, with the blessed Gesner, explain it concerning Evangelical truth: David is not speaking of the reins of GOD, but of his own reins. Nor does he even say that God does not love the wicked in the reins, or inwardly. There is nothing excellent in this concerning God, that he does not embrace the wicked with intimate love, as the gloss of Grotius has it.

Ver. same. UNCERTAIN AND HIDDEN THINGS OF YOUR WISDOM YOU HAVE MANIFESTED TO ME) In the Hebrew: In the hidden part you have made wisdom known to me. So that no excuse for sin may remain for me, I knew what kind of person you were, how averse to evil deceit, and all injustice. Your Law had inscribed this knowledge upon my heart.

He explains it, as it appears, concerning the Law of nature. But that is not the wisdom in the hidden part which God makes known to the reborn. That is inscribed in the minds of all men: it is known to all by nature that God is most holy and most averse to evil deceit and all injustice, and that he abhors those things exceedingly. Which was not unknown even to the Gentiles, as their excellent sentiments testify. But it is far more sublime what David here makes proper to himself and the faithful among the people of God, and by wisdom, and that divine and hidden wisdom peculiarly manifested in the word of God, he points out what Athanasius, Chrysostom, and Theodoret explain concerning the mystery of the expiation which is made through the blood of Christ, which is truly wisdom in a mystery, as the Apostle testifies in 1 Corinthians. 2. which the princes of this world did not know: but for us there is no doubt that the revelation of the wisdom concerning the hidden original corruption, which is by nature hidden, is included at the same time; because both pertain to the hidden wisdom of God, both that we may rightly know the intimate corruption of our nature, and that we may not be ignorant of the remedy by which we are freed from the same. Thus the antecedents cohere with the consequents. He does not only confess that he, as one adorned with excellent gifts of the Holy Spirit, is bound by greater guilt, which is what Calvin wants, but he proclaims the grace of God, that it was permitted to him both to penetrate to the source and fountain of all evils, and to know the remedy which divine mercy prepared, both of which are entirely hidden from nature, and manifested only through divine revelation.

Latin:

Vers. 8.

ECCE ENIM VERITATEM DILEXISTI] Etiam hic enim in Hebraeo deest, & rectius verteris, attamen certe veri- tatem tu diligis in renibus, id est, intime; non amas facino- rosos.

Potest omnino retineri sensus causalis, ut ra- tio reddatur confessionis, quia Deus non vult hy- pocrisin peccata occultantem, sed veritatem diligit, h. e. sinceritatem, ut omnino quis sincere agnoscat peccatum: vel etiam, ut ratio corruptionis istius gravissima, qua de questus erat Psaltes, subjugatur; q. d. merito conqueror de tanto malo intime infixo cor- di meo: non enim superficialem & externam probi- tatem, sed sinceritatem cordis intimam, in renibus di- ligis, quae in homine quomodo inveniretur, qui totus in peccatis conceptus est? Quo abit Calvini explicatio: Asserit non modo Deum requirere, ut vita nostra com- posita sit ad aliquam justitiae formam, sed ut cor purum sit & bene purgatum omni fallacia: hac ratione di- cit Deum sinceritatem velle in penetralibus, exigere sinceram cordis munditiem. Sic ergo vel de sinceri- tate confessionis sermo est, quae in poenitentibus re- quiritur, vel de sinceritate cordis & renum, quam in homine desiderat Deus, sed ob peccatum originale non invenit, qua cor ab omni fallacia liberum sit, ut proinde unicum supersit refugium ad Messiam, cujus sanguine purificantur per fidem peccata no- stra. Alii cum B. Gesnero de veritate Evangelica explicant: Non de renibus DEI, sed de renibus suis loquitur David. Nec saltem ait, quod Deus non amet in renibus, vel intime facinorosos. Nihil hoc eximii de Deo, quod non intimo amore complectatur fa- cinorosos, uti habet glossa Grotii.

Vers. eod. INCERTA ET OCCULTA SAPIENTIAE TUAE MANIFESTASTI MIHI) In Hebraeo: In abstruso sa- pientiam mihi cognitam fecisti. Quo minus excusatio mihi de peccato suppetat, noram ego qualis tu esses, quam aversus a dolo malo, & injustitia omni. Lex tua hanc notitiam cordi meo inscripserat.

De Lege, ut apparet, naturae explicat. At ea non est sapientia in abstruso, quam Deus renatis cognitam facit. Illa omnium hominum mentibus inscripta est: omnibus natura notum, Deum san- ctissimum à dolo malo, & injustitia omni maxime aversum esse, eaque summopere aversari. Quod ne gentilibus quidem incognitum fuit, testibus egre- giis eorum sententiis. Sed longe sublimius est, quod hic David sibi, & fidelibus in populo Dei proprium facit, & per sapientiam, eamque divinam & abstrusam in verbo Dei peculiariter manifesta- tam indigitat, quod Athanasius, Chrysostomus, The- odoretus de mysterio expiationis, quae fit per sangui- nem Christi, quae vere est sapientia in mysterio, te- ste Apostolo 1. Corinth. 2. quam principes hujus se- culi non cognoverunt, explicant: nobis autem du- bium non est, simul comprehendi revelationem sa- pientiae de abscondita corruptione originali, quae na- tura abscondita est; quia utrumque pertinet ad sa- pientiam absconditam Dei, & ut intimam naturæ nostræ corruptionem recte cognoscamus, & ut re- medium non ignoremus, per quod ab eadem libe- remur. Sic cohærent antecedentia cum conse- quentibus. Non tantum se ceu decoratum eximiis SS. donis majori culpa constringi fatetur, quod vult Calvinus, sed deprædicat gratiam Dei, quod sibi licuerit & malorum omnium fontem ac scaturigi- nem penetrare, & remedium, quod paravit divina misericordia, cognoscere, utrumque naturæ pror- sus absconditum, nec nisi per divinam revelatio- nem manifestatum.

## 51:7
Ver. 9.

YOU SHALL SPRINKLE ME WITH HYSSOP) That is, sprinkle me. He prays that God may free him from the punishments which he had deserved, just as lepers were restored to social life through hyssop. Levit. 14, 6.

He does not only pray for liberation from punishment, but also for the forgiveness of guilt: nor is that phrase to be passed over so idly: because it is known that those Levitical cleansings and expiations looked toward the purification which is made through the blood of Christ, which Paul taught in similar passages in Hebrews 9. Therefore, David did not have his mind intent only on the cleansing of lepers, which was only a type, but primarily on the anti-type, namely, on the purification of the blood of Christ, asking that, just as when the sprinkling was done with hyssop, the expiation and cleansing of sins was made, so that the unclean could again be joined to the assembly of the Church, so God might will to expiate his sins and cleanse himself by the spiritual hyssop of the sprinkling of the word through the blood of Christ, and in turn restore him to the communion of the Saints, from which he had been separated by sins. Which sense the ancients, Eusebius and Theodoret, also rendered, and most of the moderns follow. B. Gesnerus not unsuitably warns that a triple sprinkling is found commanded in the O.T., one by the Paschal Lamb, which was a type of Christ slaughtered on the cross, into whose blood hyssop was dipped Exod. 12. A second, when a leper was to be cleansed, or declared clean. Lev. 14. Finally a third when the whole people was absolved from sins, and a sprinkling was made with lustral water dipped from the ashes of a red heifer, and hyssop in it Numer. 19. that these sprinklings were types of the blood of Christ, which those who sprinkle upon themselves by true faith are washed from sins before God. 1. Petr. 1, 2. 1. Joh. 1, 7. Ebr. 9. & 10. Therefore, he says, that is not the meaning of David, that there is a power in hyssop to expiate anyone from crimes, but he speaks typically according to the manner of the O.T., and by hyssop stained with blood or lustral water he understands the blood of Christ thus formerly foreshadowed. Which explanation is approved also by Menochius and Bellarmine. For although he wishes to refer here particularly to Baptism, he acknowledges, however, that that purification is sought here, which David had known to be prefigured.

Latin:

Vers. 9.

ASPERGES ME HYSSOPO) Id est, asperge. Precatur, ut à pœnis, quos commeritus erat, Deus se liberet, sicut leprosi per hyssopum vitæ sociali reddebantur. Levit. 14, 6.

Non tantum precatur liberationem à pœna, sed etiam condonationem culpæ: neque phrasis il- la ita otiose transmittenda est: quia notum, quod Leviticæ illæ mundationes & expiationes respexe- rint purgationem, quæ per sanguinem Christi fit, quod in similibus his docuit Paulus Ebr. 9. Non ergo tantum David ad leprosorum mundationem, quæ typus solum erat, sed inprimis ad anti-typum, nempe ad purificationem sanguinis Christi mentem intentam habuit, petens, ut quemadmodum hysso- po, cum aspersio fiebat, expiatio peccatorum & mundatio fiebat, ut Ecclesiæ cœtui iterum jungi potuerint immundi, sic velit Deus facta hyssopo spirituali verbi aspersione per sanguinem Christi peccata sua expiare, sese mundare, atque Sanctorum communioni, à qua per peccata separatus erat, vi- cissim restituere. Quem sensum reddidere etiam veteres, Eusebius & Theodoretus, ac sequuntur ple- rique recentiores. Nec abs re monet B. Gesnerus, triplicem reperiri aspersionem in V. T. mandatam, unam per Agnum Paschalem, qui typus fuit Christi in cruce mactati, in cujus sanguinem hyssopus in- tingebatur Exod. 12. Alteram, cum leprosus emun- dandus erat, seu mundus declarandus. Lev. 14. De- nique tertiam cum universus populus à peccatis ab- solvebatur & aqua lustrali de vaccæ russæ cineribus intincta, & in ea hyssopo conspersio fiebat Numer. 19. has autem aspersiones sanguinis Christi typos fuis- se, quem qui vera fide sibi aspergunt, coram Deo à peccatis eluuntur. 1. Petr. 1, 2. 1. Joh. 1, 7. Ebr. 9. & 10. Non igitur ea, inquit, est sententia Davidis, quod hyssopo insit vis expiandi quempiam à sceleribus, sed pro ratione V. T. loquitur typice, & per hyssopum san- guine aut aqua lustrali infectam intelligit sanguinem Christi sic olim adumbratum. Quæ explicatio pro- bata etiam Menochio & Bellarmino. Quamquam enim hic peculiariter Baptismum respici velit, agnoscit tamen, hic illam peti purgationem, quam David præfiguratam noverat.

## 51:9
Vers. 11. CREATE IN ME A CLEAN HEART O GOD] Do not close the way to repentance for me. Thus Maimonides, teaching that this benefit does not happen to all from God, with the testimonies of Exod. 7, 3. Isa. 6, 9. 10. 2. Chron. 36, 16. Job 11, 28.

The words of the Psalmist carry a far different meaning than that which Grotius attributes to them along with Maimonides. For David seeks the creation of a new heart: not, however, that the way to repentance may not be closed. He asks not only for a privative benefit, as they call it, but for a positive benefit. Not only for non-rejection, but for renewal and the gift of a clean heart: just as he also adds immediately, the renewal of the spirit. For who does not see how greatly these differ, not to be excluded from repentance, and to be renewed by the Spirit, for the heart to be changed, for a clean heart to be created? For since a man cannot be converted to God, unless God changes the heart, takes away the heart of stone, gives a heart of flesh, and renews the Spirit in us, therefore David in the Psalm in this penitential [psalm] strives for this with prayers, that he may not be left to himself and perish in his sins. It is known how conversion is described in the Scriptures, as a full transformation of man, a renewal and ἀνάκτισις: For God is said to change hearts Job 12:24, to soften 2 Chron. 34:27, to open Acts 16:14, to break 1 Kings 10:26, to turn Ezra 6:22, Luke 1:17, to crush Ezek. 6:9, to renew Eph. 4:23, to take away the heart of stone, and to give a new heart Ezek. 11:19 and ch. 36:26, so that we may understand that conversion is a work of infinite power and must be attributed solely to the grace of God. Because Grotius, along with the Pelagians, Socinians, and Papists, does not grant this, hence perhaps that cold gloss attempts to overturn the emphasis of the excellent phrase. At the same time, he encrusts another error, no less light, arising from the corruptions of the Jews and the Novatian heresy: as if the approach to repentance were not left open to all. Which is refuted in the Scriptures as often as the universal grace of God, the universal redemption of Christ, the universal calling of the Holy Spirit, and the invitation to repentance are presented. The cited passages Ex. 7:3, Is. 6:9, 1 Chron. 32:16, Job 11:20 describe the extreme malice of men who finally perish by the just judgment of God, but they do not deny the grace of God to those who repent, nor do they preclude the approach to repentance for sinners, provided they do not preclude it for themselves by their sins and the hardening of their heart. Furthermore, David does not imply a new substance of the heart when he asks for a new heart to be created: because it is also said to be created when it is not a matter of a new substance, but the production of qualities, which can only be done by divine power, such as is in the regeneration of man, which is to be noted against Flacius, as well as against the new fanatics who imagine a mutation of substance.

Latin:

Vers. 11. COR MUNDUM CREA MIHI DEUS] Ne viam mihi ad pœnitentiam præclude. Ita Maimonides, docens non omnibus id beneficii a Deo contingere, testimoniis Exod. 7, 3. Efa. 6, 9. 10. 2. Paralip. 36, 16. Job. 11, 28.

Verba Psaltis longe alium sensum important, quam cum Maimonide ipsis tribuit Grotius. Da- vid enim cordis novi creationem petit: non autem, ne via ad pœnitentiam præcludatur. Non benefi- cium tantum privativum, quod vocant, sed bene- ficium positivum postulat. Non solum non rejectio- nem, sed renovationem & cordis mundi donationem: quemadmodum etiam mox addit, spiritus innova- tionem. Quis enim non videt, quantopere hæc distent, non excludi à pœnitentia, & renovari Spi- tu, cor immutari, mundum cor creari? Quum enim ad Deum converti nequeat homo, nisi Deus cor mutet, lapideum cor auferat, cor carneum donet, & Spiritum innovet in nobis, ideo David in Psalmo hoc pœnitentiali precibus id à Deo contendit, ne sibi relictus in peccatis pereat. Notum est, quomo- do describatur conversio in Scripturis, ceu plena hominis immutatio, renovatio & ἀνάκτισις: Dici- tur enim Deus immutare corda Job. 12, 24. emollire 2. Par. 34, 37. aperire Act. 16, 14. frangere 1. Reg. 10, 26. convertere Esdr. 6, 22. Luc. 1, 17. conterere Ezech. 6, 9. renovare Ephes. 4, 23. auferre cor lapideum, & dare cor novum. Ezech. 11, 19. & cap. 32, 26. ut intelligamus conversionem opus esse virtutis infinitæ & soli Dei gratiæ accepto ferri debere. Quod quia cum Pela- gianis, Socinianis, & Pontificiis haud concedit Gro- tius, hinc forte glossa illa frigida emphasin phraseos egregiæ evertere conatur. Errorem autem simul alium haud leviorem è Judæorum corruptelis & No- vatiana hæresi oriundum incrustat: quasi non omni- bus pœnitentiæ aditus relinquatur. Qui toties in Scri- pturis reprobatur, quoties universalis Dei gratia, universalis Christi redemtio, universalis S. S. voca- tio, & ad pœnitentiam invitatio exhibetur. Loca allegata Ex. 7, 3. Es. 6, 9. 1. Par. 32, 16. Job. 11, 20. ex- tremam hominum malitiam describunt, qui justo Dei judicio tandem pereunt, non vero gratiam Dei pœnitentibus denegant, aut peccatoribus aditum ad pœnitentiam præcludunt, modo ipsi peccatis & induratione cordis sui eundem sibi non præclu- dant. Cæterum non novam cordis substantiam in- nuit David cum cor novum creari postulat: quia cre- are etiam dicitur, cum non de nova agitur substan- tia, sed qualitatum productione, quæ sola divina vir- tute fieri potest, qualis est in hominis regeneratione, quod contra Flacium notandum, ut & novos fanati- cos substantiæ mutationem fingentes.

## 51:10
Verse 12. TAKE NOT THY HOLY SPIRIT FROM ME.

David speaks now converted, after he had received the Holy Spirit in turn through the intervention of true repentance. In vain, therefore, do the Calvinists distort this, as if a reborn person could not shake off the Holy Spirit. But if that were true, why would it be necessary for the reborn to pray that the Holy Spirit not be taken away? If indeed he could in no way lose the same?

Latin:

Vers. 12. SPIRITUM SANCTUM NE AU- FERAS A ME.

Loquitur David jam conversus, postquam inter- veniente vera pœnitentia Spiritum S. vicissim rece- perat. Frustra ergo Calviniani hoc eo detorquent, ac si renatus S. S. excutere non possit. Quod si ve- rum esset, cur petere necessum haberet renatus, ne S. S. auferatur? siquidem nullatenus eundem amit- tere possit?

## 51:12
Verse 14. AND STRENGTHEN ME WITH A PRINCIPAL SPIRIT) LXX. πνεύματι ἡγεμονικῷ στηριξόν με: as Chrysostom also cites in his Oration on the Holy Spirit. The best version seems to be: Strengthen me with a liberal spirit (that is, liberally poured out into me).

The Hebrew word נדיבה denotes either a heroic and principal Spirit; therefore the LXX rendered the word ἡγεμονικῷ, who is King, leader, and governor: or a spontaneous and voluntary one, which is so called from the effect, because it ensures that we obey with a prompt and eager mind Ps. 110:3, Rom. 8:16. In the latter sense it is rendered most conveniently here: and therefore B. Luther explained it as 'der freudige Geist enthalte mich' [let the joyful spirit sustain me]. R. Aben-Ezra, 'with a voluntary spirit,' so that I may willingly teach thy way, as thou hast had mercy on me. If, however, Grotius's explanation commends itself to anyone, we will not object. It is certainly better than the interpretation of Menochius and others, concerning the Spirit who teaches the best Prince: and the Chaldeans, concerning the Spirit of Prophecy, which is also that of R. David Kimchi.

Latin:

Vers. 14. ET SPIRITU PRINCIPALI CONFIRMA ME) LXX. πνεύματι ἡγεμονικῷ στηριξόν με: quomodo & Chrysosto- mus citat Orat. de Spiritu Sancto. Optima versio videtur: Spiritu liberali (id est, liberaliter in me effuso) confirma me.

Vox Ebræa נדיבה notat vel heroïcum & princi- palem Spiritum; ideo LXX. reddiderunt vocem ἡγεμονικῷ, qui sit Rex, ductor, & gubernator: vel spontaneum & voluntarium, qui ab effectu ita dici- tur, quia præstat ut animo prompto & alacri obtem- peremus Ps. 110, 3. Rom. 8, 16. Posteriori sensu hic comodissime redditur: ideoque B. Luth. exposuit der freudige Geist enthalte mich. R. Aben-Ezra, Spi- ritu voluntario, ut libenter viam tuam, quomodo mifertus es mei, edoceam. Si tamen Grotii expli- catio alicui se probet, non refragabimur. Præstat sane Menochii & aliorum interpretamento, de Spi- ritu, qui docet optimum Principem: & Chaldei, de Spiritu Prophetiæ, quæ etiam R. David Kimchii est.

## 51:14
Verse 16. DELIVER ME FROM BLOODS] It is the custom of the Hebrews to express blood in the plural: he understands, however, the crime of homicide. Thus the same plural word is used Ex. 22:3, Lev. 20:9, 11, 27, Num. 35:27, Deut. 19:10, Josh. 11:19.

Nor do others observe without reason that the plural number is used because in one homicide many are committed: since through the one who is killed many could have been propagated.

Latin:

Vers. 16. LIBERA ME DE SANGVINIBUS] Hebræo- rum mos est sanguinem pluraliter efferre:: intelligit autem homicidii crimen. Sic eadem vox pluralis sumitur Ex. 22, 3. Lev. 20, 9. 11. 27. Num. 35, 27. Deut. 19, 10. Jos. 11, 19.

Nec præter rem observant alii, numerum mul- titudinis adhiberi, quod in uno homicidio plura committantur: quum per illum qui occiditur plu- res propagari potuerint.

## 51:16
Verse 18. FOR IF THOU HADST DESIRED SACRIFICE) I WOULD SURELY HAVE GIVEN IT) There was no victim established in the law that could expiate so grave a crime. Punishment was to be expected either from man or from God, unless God forgave above the law. See what we have said in the book on the satisfaction of Christ, in the chapter on expiatory sacrifices.

This is false, and Socinian: that there was no victim for expiating grave crimes. For expiatory sacrifices were ordained even for voluntary, most grave offenses Lev. 5, and all offenses, all iniquities, all transgressions were expiated through sacrifices on the feast of expiations Lev. 16. The expiation of Christ was also foreshadowed by those victims, which extends to all sins. As therefore the Sacrifice of Christ avails for the expiation of even the most grave sins, so in the O.T. through expiatory sacrifices performed with true faith, that one ἱλαστικὸν [propitiatory] sacrifice of the N. Testament was foreshadowed and applied: of which all the old ones were types and figures. The words of David do not favor that error. For he does not say that God did not want sacrifices because of the gravity of the crime, but he institutes a comparison with bodily sacrifices absolutely, and viewed in themselves, and with the spiritual sacrifices of a contrite heart and Spirit; Namely, that sacrifices of a contrite breast please God more than those of a slaughtered animal.

Latin:

Vers. 18. QVONIAM SI VOLUISSES SACRIFICIVM) DEDISSEM VTIQVE) Nulla erat in lege constituta ho- stia, quæ tam grave crimen expiaret. Pœna aut ab homine, aut a Deo erat expectanda, nisi Deus supra legem ignosceret. Vide quæ diximus in libro de satisfactione Christi, capite de sacrificiis expiatoriis.

Falsum hoc est, & Socinianum: Nullam hostiam fuisse gravibus criminibus expiandis. Nam & pro vo- luntariis gravissimis delictis sacrificia expiatoria or- dinata Lev. 5. & omnia delicta, omnes iniquitates, o- mnes prævaricationes expiabantur per sacrificia in festo expiationum Lev. 16. Adumbrata etiam per illas hostias expiatio Christi, quæ ad omnia peccata sese porrigit. Ut ergo ad gravissimorum etiam pec- catorum expiationem Sacrificium Christi facit, ita in V. T. per Sacrificia expiatoria vera fide peracta adumbrabatur & applicabatur unicum illud ἱλα- στικὸν sacrificium N. Testamenti: cujus omnia vete- ra typi atque figuræ fuerunt. Verba Davidis non favent isti errori. Non enim ob criminis gravitatem noluisse Deum sacrificia, ait, sed comparationem instituit cum sacrificiis corporalibus absolute, ac in se spectatis, & cum sacrificiis spiritualibus contriti cordis & Spiritus; Quod nempe Deo magis placeant Sa- crificia contriti pectoris, quam occisi pecoris.

## 52:1 Argument
PSALM 52. Against courtier traitors.

FOR MAHELETH, AN INTELLIGENCE OF DAVID) That which is here מחלת signifies a song to be sung in a choir. This is apparent from Ps. 30:12, 149:3, Cant. 6:12, and Jud. 21:13. Concerning the word משכיל we have spoken at the beginning of Ps. 32.

Latin:

PSALM. LII. Contra aulicos proditores.

PRO MAHELETH INTELLIGENTIÆ DAVID) Il- lud quod hic est מחלת significat carmen in Choro cantan- dum. Id apparet ex Ps. 30, 12. 149, 3. Cant. 6, 12. & Jud. 21, 13. De voce משכיל diximus ad initium Ps. 32.

## 52:5
Verse 7. HE SHALL REMOVE THEE FROM THY TABERNACLE.

Barbarously. The sense is: He shall cause you to migrate from your tabernacle, so that you may be an exile and a wanderer.

AND HE SHALL ROOT OUT THY ROOT FROM THE LAND OF THE LIVING.

That is, he shall eradicate you with all your posterity from the land. The punishment is denounced that is to befall Doeg and his children, similar to his guilt, because he himself was the author, so that not only were Abimelech and the remaining priests slaughtered, but that his children also and his families were rooted out from the foundation.

Latin:

Vers. 7. EMIGRABIT TE DE TABERNA- CULO TUO.

BArbare. Sensus est: Migrare fasiet de taberna- culo tuo, ut sit exul & vagabundus.

ET RADICEM TUAM EVELLET DE TERRA VIVENTIUM.

Id est, te cum omni posteritate tua de terra eradica- bit. Denunciatur pœna Doëgi & liberis ejus even- tura, culpæ similis, quia ipse autor fuit, ut non tan- tum Abimelechum & reliquos Sacerdotes trucida- rent, sed ut liberi etiam ejus ac familiæ radicitus ex- stirparentur.

## 53:1 Argument
PSALM LIII. The universal corruption of men. The desire for the liberation of Jesus.

Verse 1. FOR MAHELETH. The Vulgate, along with the LXX Interpreters and the Ethiopic, retains the Hebrew word, which denotes a kind of song or melody to some here and in Psalm 88:1, to others a musical instrument. The Chaldean explains it as 'concerning retribution,' B. Luther as 'in the choir to be sung among one another.' Others prefer ἐπέχειν. Which also pleases us here. Perhaps if the sense of the word were certain, the reason would be in the open why this Psalm, since it is repeated in almost the same words except for verse 6, was proposed above in book 1, no. 14. From which, however, no tautology is to be argued, since the Holy Spirit could have had reasons for that repetition unknown to us. But that we may offer something conjecturally about them, it seems it was done: 1. Because that 'know thyself' can never be inculcated enough, and therefore one must always pray with St. Augustine, 'Lord, give me to know myself, to know Thee.' 2. Because the doctrine of justification and salvation, which the Psalm expounds, must be frequently handed down for the sake of our confirmation. Phil. 3:1, as Brentius and Gesner warn. 3. Because the Holy Spirit wished to testify in this way to the desire for the Messiah, which David had, and which he wished others to have. If 'good things are to be said twice and thrice,' how much more often did this sighing need to be repeated by the ancients. Therefore, David did not only express it for himself in Psalm 14: But he warned that others also should express the same for Maheleth, and to that end he repeated this Psalm concerning the causes of that desire, and concerning the sighing by which pious minds testify to it. Alien are the things which R. Solomon hands down, that Psalm 14 is about the destruction by the Chaldeans, Psalm 53 by Titus: and those which Sim. Muys similarly has, that the former treats of Nebuchadnezzar, the latter of Antiochus.

Latin:

PSALMUS LIII. Corruptio hominum universalis. Liberationis Jesu desiderium.

Vers. 1. PRO MAHELETH. Retinet Vulgata cum LXX. Interpp. & Æth. vo- cem Ebræam, quæ genus cantici aut melodiam aliis hic & Psalm. 88, 1. denotat, aliis instrumentum Musi- cum. Chald. explicat super retributione, B. Luth. im Chor unter einander vorzusingen. Alii malunt ἐπέ- χειν. Quod & nobis hic placet. Forte si de sensu vo- cis constaret, causa in aprico esset, cur Psalmus hic, quum iisdem propemodum verbis excepto v. 6. re- petatur: supra l. 1. n. 14. propositus. Ex quo tamen nulla ταυτολογία arguenda, quum potuerit S. S. ha- bere repetitionis istius causas nobis ignotas. Ut au- tem aliquid ςοχασικῶς de iis proferamus, videtur ea facta. 1. Quod nunquam satis illud γνῶθι σεαυτὸν inculcari possit, ac semper ideo cum S. August. oran- dum sit, Domine da mihi nosse me, nosse Te. 2. Quia doctrina de justificatione & salute, quam exponit Psalmus crebro est tradenda, nostræ βεβαιώσεως causa. Phil. 3, 1. ut Brent. & Gesner. monent. 3. Quod testari voluerit ita Spirit. S. Sanctum Messiæ desideri- um, quod habuerit David, aliosque habere volue- rit. Si δὶς καὶ τρὶς τὰ καλὰ, quanto magis ingemi- nandum sæpe veteribus fuit hoc suspirium. Ideo non tantum pro se David id Psalm. 14. expressit: Sed ut pro Maheleth idem alii etiam exprimant, monuit, eaque fini Psalmum hunc de causis istius de- siderii, deque suspirio, quo id piæ mentes testantur, repetiit. Aliena sunt quæ R. Salomo tradit, quod Psalm. 14. de excidio per Chaldæos, Psalm. 53. per Titum: quæque Sim. Muys similiter habet, quod il- lic de Nebucadn. hic de Antiocho agatur.

## 54:1 Argument
PSALM LIV.

The pious afflicted one vows a Eucharistic sacrifice.

IN CARMINIBUS] בִּנְגִינֹת : concerning which word we spoke at the beginning of the fourth Psalm.

Verse 1. WHEN THE ZIPHITES HAD COME.

Because the history concerning the betrayal of the Ziphites is referred to, which is twofold, described in 1 Sam. 23:19 and chapter 26:1; Muys explains the Psalm as concerning the former, when David was freed from the hand of Saul by the invasion of the Philistines; which opinion verse 7 seems to favor. However, there is no doubt that the prayer poured out then had its effect also at the time of the second betrayal.

Latin:

PSALM. LIV.

Pius afflictus sacrificium Eucharisticum spondet.

IN CARMINIBUS] בִּנְגִינֹת : de qua voce dixi- mus ad initium Psalmi quarti.

Verf. 1. CUM VENISSENT ZIPHÆI.

QUia respicitur historia de proditione Ziphæo- rum, quæ gemina est 1. Sam. 23, 19. & cap. 26, 1. descriptæ, de priori, cum per Philistinorum invasio- nem à manu Saulis liberatus est David, Psalmum explicat Muys; cui sententiæ favere videtur vers. 7. Nullum autem dubium est orationem tum fusam effectum suum habuisse etiam tempore alterius proditionis.

## 54:1
Verse 3.

Latin:

Verf. 3.

## 54:4
THE LORD IS THE UPHOLDER OF MY SOUL.

The Vulgate expressed the sense. The words are thus: The Lord helps me among those who sustain my soul: He alone is the sustainer of my soul or my life. See Jud. 11:5. R. Mosche, it is in the place of all those sustaining.

Latin:

DOMINUS EST SUSCEPTOR ANIMÆ MEÆ.

Sensum expressit Vulgat. Verba ita habent: Dominus auxiliatur mihi in sustentantibus animam meam: Ipse solus est sustentator animæ vel vitæ meæ. Vid. Jud. 11, 5. R. Mosche, est loco omnium su- stentantium.

## 54:7
Verse 9.

AND UPON MY ENEMIES MY EYE HAS LOOKED DOWN.

In Hebrew: The eye looks upon my enemies. It is a prophecy: or certainly David was heard even in this κατὰ τὸ ῥητόν (according to the literal sense). For he truly saw Saul, indeed he had him in his hand, 1 Sam. 26:17.

Latin:

Verf. 9.

ET SUPER INIMICOS MEOS DESPEXIT OCULUS MEUS.

In Ebr. Intuetur oculus inimicos meos. Prophe- tia est: aut certe exauditus etiam in eo κατὰ τὸ ῥη- τὸν David. Nam vere vidit Saulem, imo in manu sua habuit, 1. Sam. 26, 17.

## 55:1 Argument
PSALM LV.

Traitorous friends.

Latin:

PSALMUS LV.

Amici proditores.

## 55:13
Ver. 14.

BUT YOU, A MAN OF ONE MIND, MY GUIDE.

IN Heb. But you, a man according to my estimation, my guide, as Vatablus and others. Coppenius, however, renders it, a man of my rank. The Syriac, you son of man, who are like me. The Arabic, equal to my soul. Thus the word כְּעֶרְכִּי from עָרַךְ, he arranged, he estimated, Numb. 18:16, 2 Kings 12:4, Job 28:13, to which the former explanation seems to agree more, whether in the sense already stated, or in this sense, but you, a man according to my ordering or constitution. See Exod. 40:4, 23, Judg. 17:10. אַלּוּפִי My guide, or constituted by me, or set over others by me. The Chaldean, Kimchi, Muis, and the Vinariens refer this to Ahithophel; others to Judas, whom Christ constituted a guide to the people by teaching with the other Apostles, Ps. 45:17, concerning whom, with Hilary and Jerome, our Bugenhagen also expounded, as did B. Cramer in his summary. B. Luther, Tom. 3, Lat. works, in the argument of the Psalms. Although, he says, in the 12th and 13th verse it is understood of Christ himself against the traitor Judas, yet it is approved by me that it is a general prayer of the pious against that craftiness of insidious and cunning men, etc. So also St. Augustine, B. Gesner, Cocceius, to whom we subscribe.

Latin:

Vers. 14.

TU VERO HOMO UNANIMIS DUX MEUS.

IN Ebr. Sed tu homo secundum æstimationem meam dux meus, ut Vatabl. & alii. Coppenius vero red- dit, homo mei ordinis. Syrus, tu fili hominis, qui sicut ego. Arabs, æqualis animæ meæ. Ita vox כְּעֶרְכִּי ab עָרַךְ disposuit, æstimavit Numer. 18, 16. 2. Reg. 12, 4. Job. 28, 13. cui prior explicatio magis congruere vi- detur, sive jam dicto, sive hoc sensu, sed tu homo secundum ordinationem vel constitutionem meam. Vi- de Exod. 40, 4. 23. Jud. 17, 10. אַלּוּפִי Dux meus, vel à me constitutus, aut præpositus à me aliis. Ad Achito- phelem hoc referunt Chaldæus, Kimchius, Muis, Vinariens. alii ad Judam quem constituit Christus Ducem populo docendo cum aliis Apostolis Ps. 45, 17. de quo cum Hilario, & Hieronymo etiam exposuit Bugenh. noster, ut & B. Cramerus in sum- mario. B. Luther. Tom. 3. oper. Lat. in argum. Psal- mor. Quamvis, inquit, in 12. & 13. versu intelligi de ipso Christo contra proditorem Judam, tamen mihi probatur, quod sit generalis oratio piorum adversus illam vafritiem insidiosorum & callidorum hominum &c. Sic etiam S. Augustinus, B. Gesner. Coccejus, quibus subscribimus.

## 55:23
MEN OF BLOOD AND DECEITFUL SHALL NOT HALVE THEIR DAYS] οὐ μὴ ἡμισεύσωσι τὰς ἡμερὰς ἀυτῶν. They shall not reach the age to which many men reach, and to which they themselves could have reached. The same manner of speaking is below, Ps. 101:25. But the matter is in Exod. 20:12. If this punishment was appointed for such people in the time of the law, how much more should they expect it who are such after the light of the Gospel?

No difference is found between the Old and New Testament regarding moral laws or punishments. Therefore, Grotius's inference lacks a foundation, nor does it proceed from anything but a false hypothesis, as if stricter laws concerning the love of one's neighbor were given under the New Testament, and a more severe punishment decreed: which our author, along with many other paradoxes, drew from the Socinian pools concerning Christ as a new legislator.

Latin:

VIRI SANGVINUM ET DOLOSI NON DIMIDIA- BUNT DIES SUOS] οὐ μὴ ἡμισεύσωσι τὰς ἡμερὰς ἀυτῶν. Non pervenient ad ætatem, ad quam hominum multi perve- niunt, & ipsi pervenire potuerant. Idem loquendi genus in- fra Psal. 101, 25. Res autem Exod. 20, 12. Si hæc pœna ta- libus legis tempore fuit præstituta, quantum expectare de- bent, qui post lucem Evangelii tales sunt?

Nulla, quantum ad leges morales aut pœnas, invenitur differentia Veteris & Novi Testamenti. Illatio ergo Grotii fundamento caret, nec nisi è falsa hypothesi procedit, quasi sub Novo Testa- mento leges frictiores de dilectione proximi datæ sint, & severior animadversio indicta: quam è So- cinianis lacunis de Christo Novo legislatore hau- sit Noster cum aliis multis paradoxis.

## 56:1 Argument
PSALM 56.

The silent, driven-away dove cries out to God who counts its flight.

FOR THE PEOPLE WHO HAVE BEEN MADE FAR FROM THE HOLY ONES, DAVID FOR THE INSCRIPTION OF THE TITLE, WHEN THE PHILISTINES HELD HIM IN GATH] The LXX seem to have read בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים for יֹונַת אֵלֶם and for אֵלִים to have read יֹונַת אֵלֶם and by that word to have understood the sons of God: in the way that many interpret בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים in Gen. 6:2; furthermore, for מִכְתָּם they read מִכְתָּב, as above in 16. From the Hebrew, the version will flow best thus: To the chief musician, concerning the silent dove, namely David, a poem of the dove to be inscribed concerning that time when he was held by the Philistines in Gath. He elegantly calls himself a silent dove, because he was both innocent toward his own people, and yet would not dare to betray this innocence of his to the Philistines.

What Grotius brings in concerning the inscription of the title at Ps. 16:1 is settled. He rightly amends the Vulgate here from the Hebrew, but he wrongly suspects that the LXX read otherwise, because the Hebrew codices agree completely. Nor should the word רְחֹקִים (dove) of those removed, namely of remote places, driven far away, or among the remote, have been omitted; but the interpretation of Cocceius, 'on the dove of the sheaf of the elongated ones,' is more alien.

Latin:

PSALM. LVI.

Columba fugata muta ad Deum fugam nume- rantem clamat.

PRO POPULO, QVI A SANCTIS LONGE FACTUS EST, DAVID IN TITULI INSCRIPTIONEM, CUM TENUERUNT EUM ALLOPHTLI IN GETH] Viden- tur LXX. pro יֹונַת אֵלֶם legisse בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים & pro אֵלִים legiffe יֹונַת אֵלֶם & ea voce intellexisse Dei filios: quomodo multi interpre- tantur בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים Gen. 6, 2. præterea pro מִכְתָּם legisse מִכְתָּב, ut supra 16. Ex Hebræo versio fic optime fluet: Principi cantorum, de columba muta, Davide scili- cet, carmen columbæ inscribendum de eo tempore quo tenebatur à Philisthinis in Geth. Columbam mutam eleganter se vocat, quod & innocens esset adversus populum suum, & tamen hanc suam innocentiam Philistinis prodere non auderet.

QUæ de tituli inscriptione ingerit Grot. ad Ps. 16, 1. expedita sunt. Merito autem emendat hic Vulgatam ex Ebræo, sed immerito suspicatur LXX. fecus legisse, quia Codices Ebræi consonant ex asse. Nec omittenda erat vox רְחֹקִים )co- lumba) remotorum scil. locorum, longe fugata, vel inter remotos; Alienior autem est interpretatio Cocceji, super columba manipuli elongatorum.

## 56:12
Ver. 13. THAT I MAY WALK BEFORE GOD IN THE LIGHT OF THE LIVING.

That these things can be explained of Christ liberated from death, Bellarmine thinks, but against the argument of the Psalm. Piscator understands 'Light from Light' of the sun rather coldly: others more correctly of the light both of grace and of glory, since we walk here by faith, and shall one day walk by sight, 2 Corinthians 5:7.

Latin:

Vers. 13. UT PLACEAM CORAM DEO IN LUMINE VIVENTIUM.

De Christo hæc exponi posse à morte liberato Bellarm. sed contra argumentum Psalmi existimat. Lumen de Luce solis frigide satis intelligit Piscator: alii rectius de luce tum gratiæ, tum gloriæ, cum ambulamus hic per fidem, olim ambulaturi per spe- ciem 2. Corinth. 5, 7.

## 57:1 Argument
PSALM LVII.

A heart prepared for the praise of God in persecution.

Ver. 1.

DO NOT DESTROY) That is, a deprecation.

Because in the Vulgate is added, but outside the authentic text, 'IN THE INSCRIPTION OF THE TITLE', Augustine and Jerome explain it concerning the title of the Cross of Christ. Hilary refers the words 'do not corrupt' to the resurrection of Christ. But these things are foreign to the argument indicated by the Holy Scriptures from 1 Samuel 24. Yet it is not to be thought, with Aben-Ezra, that David said these things in the cave, but after his liberation.

Latin:

PSALM. LVII.

Cor paratum ad laudem Dei in persequutione.

Vers. 1.

NE DISPERDAS) Id est, deprecatio.

QUia in Vulgata additur, sed extra textum au- thenticum, IN TITULI INSCRIPTIO- NEM, Augustin. & Hieronymus exponunt de titu- lo Crucis Christi. Hilarius verba, ne corrumpas re- fert ad resurrectionem Christi. Sed hæc aliena sunt ab argumento à S. S. indicato è 1. Sam. 24. Non tamen cum Aben - Ezra putandum, quod hæc in spelunca dixerit David, sed post liberationem.

## 57:10
Ver. 11. ARISE, MY GLORY.

Bellarmine's gloss is twisted: 'Arise, my glory, Christ my redeemer and my Lord. Arise, my psaltery, that is, arise, flesh of Christ, which were a psaltery, while by working divine miracles you sounded from the higher part, and a cithara, while by suffering human things you gave sound from the lower part. I will arise at dawn,' as if Christ were thus responding, because it is established that Christ rose from the dead at dawn. Nor is the exposition concerning the Spirit of Prophecy, which Bellarmine also brought forward and praised from Theodoret, suitable; for that is never called a psaltery, nor is the tongue ever called a cithara. By 'glory,' Kimchi and Genebrard more correctly understand the soul, others the tongue, which procures glory for man and which glorifies God. Cf. Genesis 49:6, Ps. 30:13, Ps. 108:2, 3, and Ps. 16:9, Acts 2:26. The nablium or psaltery and cithara are to be taken literally: nor does anyone respond other than David himself, 'I will awake at dawn,' as is customary in soliloquies.

Latin:

Vers. 11. EXURGE GLORIA MEA.

Contorta est glossa Bellarmini : Exurge gloria mea, Christe redemtor meus, & dominus meus. Exurge Psalterium meum, id est, exurge caro Chri- sti, quæ Psalterium fuisti, dum divina miracula ope- rando ex parte superiori sonuisti, & cythara, dum humana patiendo ex parte inferiori sonitum dedi- sti. Exurgam diluculo, quasi ita respondeat Christus, quia constat Christum à mortuis diluculo surrexif- se. Nec convenit expositio de Spiritu Prophetiæ quam è Theodor. etiam adduxit & laudavit Bellarm. ille enim nunquam Psalterium, neque linguam us- piam Cythara dicitur. Per gloriam rectius Kimchius & Genebrardus animam, alii linguam intelligunt, quæ gloriam homini conciliat, & quæ Deum glo- rificat. Conf. Genes. 49, 6. Ps. 30, 13. Ps. 108, 2. 3. & Ps. 16, 19. Actor. 2, 26. Nablium vel Psalterium & cythara secundum literam accipienda : nec alius re- spondet quam David ipse, evigilabo diluculo, ut so- let in soliloquiis.

## 58:1 Argument
PSALM LVIII.

Vengeance awaits the mute and the deaf in the judgment of God.

Latin:

PSALM. LIIX.

Matos & surdos in judicio Dei vindicta manet.

## 58:2
Ver. 3. THE WICKED ARE ALIENATED FROM THE WOMB.

That is, from the very birth, according to the interpretation of Bellarmine; for why should one not insist upon τῷ ῥητῷ? Rabbi David himself rendered it, it is natural for them to do evil: nor does he deny it. Aben-Ezra: nor do the Papists, Roa lib. 1. singul. cap. 12. Therefore, he wrongly denies with the Socinians, Del-Rio Tom. 2. adag. p. 55. that original sin is proven from this, feigning a hyperbole with Piscator, from whom, however, Coppenius and Cocceius depart, explaining it concerning the wicked who always remain in natural depravity and corruption, and do not resist it. Conf. Rom. 3, 4.

Latin:

Vers. 3. ALIENATI SUNT PECCATORES A VULVA.

Id est, ab ipsa nativitate, interprete Bellarm. cur enim non insistendum τῷ ῥητῷ. Ipse R. David reddidit, naturale ipsis est male agere : nec abnuit Aben-Ezra: neque è Pontificiis Roa lib. 1. singul. cap. 12. Pèrperam ergo cum Socinianis negat Del- Rio Tom. 2. adag. p. 55. peccatum originale hinc probari, hyperbolen fingens cum Piscat. à quo vero recedit Coppenius & Coccejus de improbis in natura- li pravitate & corruptione semper manentibus, nec ei resistentibus, explicantes. Conf. Rom. 3, 4.

## 58:9
Vers. 10.

BEFORE YOUR THORNS UNDERSTAND THE BRAMBLE AS LIVING, SO IN WRATH HE SHALL SWALLOW THEM UP) The best version according to the Hebrew seems to be: Before your pots (or cauldrons) feel the bramble (that is, the fire from the bramble, which very quickly ignites and heats up) so shall wrath (of God) swallow you up as if living, in a whirlwind (that is, most rapidly). סירות are pots. This appears in Eccles. 7, 7. where likewise there is mention of fire from thorns. See also Exod. 16, 3. where also in many other places the Greeks translate it λέβητα, elsewhere χαλκείον.

If anyone wishes to compare other various interpretations, let him approach Mr. Dr. Geier on this passage. We do not deny the Grotian explanation.

Vers. 10. THE RIGHTEOUS SHALL REJOICE WHEN HE SEETH THE VENGEANCE.

Not through ἐπικακοχαιρίαν [rejoicing in evil], but on account of divine justice demonstrated, which others also will acknowledge, verse 12.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

PRIVSQVAM INTELLIGERENT SPINÆ VESTRÆ RHAMNVM SICVT VIVENTES, SIC IN IRA AB- SORBET EOS) Optima versio ad Hebræum videtur: Pri- usquam caldaria vestra (sive lebetes) sentiant rhamnum (id est, ignem ex rhamno, qui celerrime ardescit & calefacit) sic vos quasi viventes absorbebit ira (Dei) turbine (id est, rapidis- sime) סירות sunt caldaria. Apparet id Eccles. 7, 7. ubi pa- riter ignis è spinis mentio. Vide & Exod. 16, 3. ubi & aliis multis in locis λέβητα vertunt Græci, alibi χαλκείον.

Varias interpretationes alias, si cui conferre lu- beat, adeat Dn. D. Geierum in h. l. Non abnuimus explicationi Grotianæ.

Vers. 10. LÆTABITUR JUSTUS CUM VI- DERIT VINDICTAM.

Non per ἐπικακοχαιρίαν, sed ob justitiam di- vinam demonstratam, quod eandem etiam alii agni- turi sint vers. 12.

## 58:10
HE SHALL WASH HIS HANDS IN THE BLOOD OF THE WICKED.

In the Hebrew, he shall wash his steps in the blood of the wicked. Bellarmine rashly prefers the Vulgate to the authentic text, because the Greeks agree with it: he ineptly explains that the righteous cleanses his works while he beholds the blood of the wicked. The discourse is about the immensity of the vengeance, as with Luther, the Belgians, and others.

Latin:

MANUS SUAS LAVABIT IN SANGUI- NE PECCATORUM.

In Ebr. gressus suos lavabit in sanguine impii. Te- mere Bellarmin. præfert vulgatam textui authenti- co, quod illi Græci consentiant: inepte explicat ju- stum mundare opera sua dum cernit sanguinem impio- rum. Sermo est de immensitate vindictæ, ut cum Luther. Belgæ, & alii.

## 59:1 Argument
PSALM LIX. The horrendous tyranny of the wrath of GOD proclaimed.

IN THE INSCRIPTION OF THE TITLE WHEN HE SENT SAUL) A poem inscribed on a pillar in memory of that event, placed in the place where it had happened.

BUT where in the authentic text of the title, where is the mention of the inscription? Therefore, Grotius does not seem to have inspected it here. Furthermore, although the occasion of the Psalm was special, 1 Sam. 19, 11, we nevertheless easily agree with Bellarmine that the whole Psalm can be explained generally concerning the wicked persecuting the righteous.

Latin:

PSALM. LIX. Tyrannis iræ DEI horrenda indicta.

IN TITVLI INSCRIPTIONEM QVANDO MISIT SAVL) Carmen inscriptum columnæ in memoriam istius rei, positæ eo loco ubi id evenerat.

AT ubi in textu authentico tituli, ubi inscri- ptionis mentio? Eum ergo hic non inspexisse videtur Grotius. Cæterum quamvis occasio Psal- mi fuerit specialis 1. Sam. 19, 11. facile tamen Bellar- mino annuimus, posse totum Psalmum generatim de impiis justos persequentibus exponi.

## 59:6
Vers. 7. THEY SHALL RETURN AT EVENING.

These things are ineptly applied to the conversion of the Jews, either after the death of Christ or towards the end of the world, by Bellarmine; and around verse 16, by Bellarmine himself, to the final judgment and exclusion from the heavenly Jerusalem; concerning the return to seek and kill, Pagninus, Junius, Piscator; concerning the insane and insatiable desire to harm the saints, which is in the enemies, Cocceius: But Mr. D. Geier explains it more correctly as a vain persecution, with Basil, Theodoret, and Genebrard, i.e., after these rabid and famished dogs, thirsting for nothing but my blood, have spent the whole day in the quest for prey, make it so that towards evening they return to their dens, with stomach unfulfilled and still barking. B. Luther, B. Gesner, and Cramer in their summaries take verses 12 and 13 as referring to the dispersion of the Jews throughout the world, with Mr. D. Geier also agreeing, and not inappropriately so: since the prayer and imprecation suit no one better than Christ; yet in explaining verses 7 and 16, we prefer to understand the canine appetite of the enemies of Christ and the frustration of that appetite, so that the sense is the same in both places, rather than to refer it, as some do, to that penal dispersion; for the cause of the same is set forth there, not indeed a continuation of penal wandering, namely, a tyrannical and fruitless harassment.

Latin:

Vers. 7. CONVERTENTUR AD VESPE- RAM.

Hæc inepte ad conversionem Judæorum seu post mortem Christi seu sub finem mundi trahun- tur apud Bellarm. & circa vers. 16. à Bellarm. ipso ad judicium extremum, & exclusionem à cœlesti Hie- rosolyma; de reversione ad quærendum & occi- dendum Pagnin. Junius, Piscator, de insana, & insatiabili Sanctis nocendi cupiditate, quæ in ho- stibus est, Coccejus: Sed rectius de inani persequu- tione cum Basilio, Theodoret. & Genebrardo Dn. D. Geierus explicat, q. d. postquam hi rabiosi, ac famelici canes nil nisi meum sanguinem sitientes totum insumserunt diem quæstione prædæ, fac ut circa vesperam ad sua redeant antra, Stomacho inexpleto, & adhuc latrante. De Judæorum dis- persione per orbem B. Luther. & B. Gesnerus, ac Cramerus in summar. versum 12. 13. annuente etiam Dn. D. Geiero accipiunt, idque non incommode: siquidem oratio & imprecatio nulli magis, quam Christo conveniat, in explicandis tamen v. 7. & 16. malumus caninam hostium Christi tum appeten- tiam tum appetentiæ frustrationem, ita ut utrobi- que idem sit sensus intelligere, quam eadem cum nonnullis ad pœnalem illam dispersionem etiam re- ferre; Nimirum causa ejusdem ibi exponitur; non vero continuatio circumcursitationis pœnalis, tyran- nica nempe & frustranea insectatio.

## 59:11 Addition
To Psalm 59, verse 12, DO NOT DESTROY THEM.

To this passage B. Hülsemann added a Scholion: Although the imprecation of lasting torment could not be turned to David's fault as a Prophet predicting rather than praying for those things, just as the deprecation of pity, or of divine grace being withdrawn, verse 6, I do not think, however, that David here asks for a slow and lasting torture of his enemies, but deprecates the vehemence of the punishment, toward even some communication of preventing grace, concerning which he had spoken in the preceding verse 11. Which sense I think is rightly expressed here by Musculus and Jansenius: who, understanding these things about the Jewish people not being entirely extirpated but afflicted and subdued in Christian Commonwealths, do not wander from David's prophecy, but do not define the adequate object intended by David.

Latin:

Ad Psal. 59. v. 12. NE PERDAS EOS.

Ad hunc locum addito B. Hülsemann. Scho- lion: Quanquam imprecatio diuturni tormenti Davidi tanquam Prophetæ magis ista prædicenti quam precanti, tam vitio verti non posset, quam deprecatio commiserationis, seu subtrahendæ gratiæ divinæ v. 6. non puto tamen Davidem hic petere lentum & diuturnum cruciatum hostium, sed deprecari vehementiam supplicii, ad aliqua- lem etiam communicationem gratiæ prævenien- tis, de qua dixerat versu antecedente 11. Quem sensum puto recte hic expressum à Musculo & Jan- senio: qui de non plane extirpanda sed affligenda, & subigenda gente Judaica in Christianis Rebus- publicis hæc intelligunt, non aberrant a vatici- nio Davidis, sed objectum adæquatum à Davide intentum non definiunt.

## 60:1 Argument
PSALM LX. A jewel concerning a helper in necessity.

Latin:

PSALM. LX. Clinodium de adjutore in necessitate.

## 60:1
Verse 2.

WHEN HE SET MESOPOTAMIA OF SYRIA ON FIRE] In memory of all the victories which are briefly indicated here, but described more broadly in the books of Samuel and Chronicles. The word הצה, which the Greeks, whom this version follows, translated here as ἐμπυρίζειν (to set on fire), is translated elsewhere as μάχεσθαι (to fight), which suits this place very well, so that the sense is: when he waged war against Syria of the two rivers (thus the Hebrew reading holds), that is, Mesopotamia, so called from the Euphrates and the Tigris. That David's arms were extended that far appears in 2 Sam 8:3 and 1 Chron 18:3.

There is no doubt that the Psalm was composed on the occasion of David's victories; but moved by the Spirit, he testifies to and sighs for the most holy desire of the Messiah, whom GOD had already given to His people as a banner to which they might flock, in promises and types, and he sighs for His salvation in verses 6 and 7; thence, so that the beloved of GOD may be delivered, he turns to the Messiah Himself and prays solicitously, save (O Savior Jesus, whose name is tacitly included in the word here) and answer me. Hence he predicts the real answer of GOD: GOD has spoken in His holiness; in the days of His flesh, the Messiah GOD speaks in the Holy (the temple of His flesh, John 2:21, Heb 9:11), which David, already hearing in the spirit, exults in verse 8, and how he now distributes Shechem, where the promise was made to Abraham (Gen 12:7), as a type of the kingdom of the Messiah to be spread throughout the world, and measures the valley of Succoth, where Jacob only fixed thin tabernacles (Gen 33:17), and possesses Gilead, and thus not only those valleys but also the mountainous regions beyond the Jordan: indeed the tract of the sons of Joseph, Manasseh, and Ephraim, where the Israelite kingdom was later, and because of the population's density and strength, David not undeservedly held Ephraim as the fortress or strength of his head, and concerning Judah he professes that he is his מחקק (lawgiver), or of his kingdom: because the lawgiver was not to depart from Judah until the coming of Shiloh (Gen 49:10), indeed that Moab is his washpot, and that he casts his shoe over Edom, because he could use the Moabites for menial services at will, and he dominated the Edomites, and that the Philistines themselves, who caused the Israelites much fighting and trouble, were forced to applaud and congratulate themselves, so that hardly anything remains except that he be led into the fortified city, one and another (perhaps into Rabbath, the metropolis of the sons of Ammon, 2 Kings 12) by the Lord, who had led him (David) to Edom, even though he seemed to have rejected the Jews before. Finally, he adds a sigh to the same Lord (the Messiah): Give us help from the enemy (especially the infernal one), for vain is the salvation of men (Psalm 49:8 ff., Psalm 89:49). With GOD we shall do valiantly, and He (the Messiah, noted by the word הוא in Gen 3:15) shall trample our enemies. For this is His property, by the power of the Paradisiacal Proto-Evangelium.

AND SOBAL] The LXX wrote συβὰ, not σοβὰλ: for they have it so in the places already mentioned. In the Hebrew here it is, against Syria Zobah, that is, the part of Syria having this name, concerning which see 2 Sam 8:5, 12; 10:6; and 1 Chron 18:2, 9.

AND JOAB RETURNED) Better: and Joab returned, namely from the slaughter inflicted upon the Syrians (2 Sam 8:13). But Joab is said to have done what he did through his brother Abishai, because Joab held the supreme command under David (2 Sam 8:16; 1 Chron 18:15).

IDUMAEA) In the Hebrew, Edom, that is, the Idumaeans.

IN THE VALLEY OF SALT) 2 Sam 8:15 & 16.

TWELVE THOUSAND) Namely in one battle, besides six thousand others slain in smaller skirmishes. 1. Chron. 18, 12.

Latin:

Vers. 2.

CVM SVCCENDIT MESOPOTAMIAM STRIAE] In memoriam omnium victoriarum, quæ hic breviter indi- cantur, latius autem describuntur in libris Samuelis & Para- lipomenon. Verbum הצה quod hîc per ἐμπυρίζειν vertê- runt Græci, quos hæc versio sequitur, alibi vertitur per μά- χεσθαι, quod huic loco optime convenit, ut sensus sit: cum bellum gereret adversus Syriam duorum fluminum (sic habet lectio Hebræa) id est Mesopotamiam ab Euphrate & Tigride ita dictam. Eo autem usque prolata arma Davidis apparet 2. Sam 8, 3. & 1. Paral. 18, 3.

OCcasione victoriarum Davidis Psalmum com- positum esse, dubium non est; Sed inde Spi- ritu provectus altius desiderium sanctissimum Mes- siæ, quem vexillum, ad quod concurrerent, jam de- derat DEUS populo suo in promissionibus, & ty- pis, testatur, ac suspirat salutem ejus vers. 6. 7. inde ut liberentur dilecti DEI, ad Messiam ipsum con- versus solicite precatur, serva (ô servator Jesu, cu- jus nomen tacite in verbo hîc inclusum est) & re- sponde mihi. Hinc prædicit reale DEI responsum: DEUS loquutus est in sancto suo, in diebus carnis suæ, loquitur Messias DEUS in Sancto (templo carnis suæ Joh. 2, 21. Ebr. 9, 11.) quod jam in spiri- tu audiens David, exultat vers. 8. & quomodo in typum regni Messiæ per orbem dilatandi jam distri- buat Sichem, ubi promissio Abrahæ facta Genes. 12, 7. & metiatur vallem Succoth, ubi Jacob taberna- cula solum tenuia fixit Genes. 33, 17. ac possideat Gil- had, adeoque non modo valles illas, sed etiam mon- tana trans Jordanem: imo tractum filiorum Jose- phi, Manassis, & Ephraim, ubi regnum Israeliti- cum postea fuit, & ob populi frequentiam & robur David Ephraim pro arce vel fortitudine capitis sui non immerito habuit, & de Juda profitetur, quod sit מחקק legislator suus, vel regni sui : quia legisla- tor de Juda deficere non debebat usque ad adventum Schilo Genes. 49, 10. imo quod Moab pollubrum suum sit, quodque in Edom calceum suum proji- ciat, quia Moabitas ad servitia vilia adhibere pro lubitu poterat, & Edomitis dominabatur, quodque ipsi Palæstini, qui Israelitis multum pugnæ & nego- tii facessebant, sibi applaudere & congratulari co- acti sint, ut vix aliud supersit, quam ut in urbem munitam, unam atque alteram adhuc adducatur (forte in Rabboth, metropolin filiorum Ammon. 2. Reg. 12.) à Domino, qui deduxerat ipsum (Da- videm) ad Edomum, etsi antea Judeos rejecisse videretur. Postremo ad eundem Dominum (Mes- siam) suspirium subjicit: Da nobis auxilium ab ho- ste (infernali imprimis,) Etenim in vanum est salva- tio hominum Psalm. 49, 8. seqq. Psalm. 89, 49. Cum DEO strenue rem geremus, והוא & ille (Messias Genes. 3, 15. voce הוא notatus) conculcabit hostes nostros. Hoc enim ejus proprium est, vi Prot-Ev- angelii Paradisiaci.

ET SOBAL] Scripsere LXX. συβὰ non σοβὰλ: nam sic habent dictis jam locis. In Hebræo hîc est, adversus Syriam Soba, id est, partem Syriæ hoc nomen habentem, de qua vide 2. Sam. 8, 5. 12. 10, 6. & 1. Paralip. 18, 2, 9.

ET CONVERTIT JOAB) Melius: & reversus est Ioab, nempe a cæde in Syros edita 2. Sam. 8, 13. Fecisse autem dici- tur Joab quod per Abisai fratrem suum fecit, quia Joabi sub Davide summum erat imperium. 2. Sam. 8, 16. 1. Par. 18, 15.

IDVMÆAM) In Hebræo, Edom, id est, Idumæos.

IN VALLE SALIS) 2. Sam. 8, 15. & 16.

DVODECIM MILLIA) Nempe uno prælio, præter sex alia millia in minoribus conflictationibus interfecta. 1. Par. 18, 12.

## 60:7
JUDAH MY KING) Lawgiver in Hebrew. The sense is the same: for the people mean to say that their King is from the tribe of Judah.

These are not the words of the people, but of King David, who recounts the ἀξιώματα & benefits of certain tribes, and celebrates the tribe of Judah for its zeal for the law, because the Scepter and the administration, or custody, of the laws were to remain with this tribe until the times of Christ.

Verse of the same.

Latin:

JUDA REX MEUS) Legifer in Hebræo. Sensus idem: vult enim dicere populus, Regem sibi esse e tribu Judæ.

Non hæc verba sunt populi, sed David Regis, qui ἀξιώματα & beneficia tribuum quarundam recenset, & tribum Judæ à studio legis celebrat, quia penes hanc tribum Sceptrum & legum administratio, seu custodia usque ad Christi tempora esse debebat.

Vers. eod.

## 60:8
Verse 10.

Latin:

Vers. 10.

## 60:8
MOAB IS THE POT OF MY HOPE) When the Greeks wrote Μωὰβ λέβης τῆς ἐλπίδος με, they had in mind the Syriac word ܫܒܪ, which means to trust, as in Dan. 3:28; but the true interpretation from the Hebrew is: the pot of my washing: that is, a washbasin, ποδόνιπτρον. Aquila, the pot of my cleansing. By this they mean to say that they will rule over the Moabites and Idumeans as over slaves.

UPON IDUMEA I WILL EXTEND MY SHOE) I will extend my shoe over Idumea, namely so that he may take it off for me, as base slaves are accustomed to do. See what is at Matt. 3:11.

Latin:

MOAB OLLA SPEI MEÆ) Græci cum scripserunt Μωὰβ λέβης τῆς ἐλπίδος με, in animo habuerunt vocem Syriacam ܫܒܪ, quæ significat confidere, ut Dan. 3,28. sed vera interpretatio ex Hebræo est: lebes lotionis meæ: id est, pollubrum, ποδόνιπτρον. Aquila, λέβης λυτρῶ με. Hoc volunt dicere se imperaturos Moabitis & Idumæis, ut servis.

IN IDVMÆAM EXTENDAM CALCEAMENTVM MEVM) Idumæo extendam calceum meum, nempe ut eum mihi detrahat, ut viles servuli solent. Vide quæ ad Matth. 3, 11.

## 61:1 Argument
PSALM LXI. A firm asylum.

Latin:

PSALMUS LXI. Asylum firmum.

## 61:2
Verse 3.

FROM THE ENDS OF THE EARTH I HAVE CRIED TO YOU) Namely, from beyond the Jordan, to where he had fled for fear of Absalom, 2 Sam. 17:22.

Compare Exod. 16:35, Deut. 13:7. The explanation of Theodoret and Euthymius, as if the prayer were that of the people captive among the Babylonians, does not fit so well. Nor can we add our vote to Bellarmine, even though he appeals to Hilary, Jerome, and Augustine, because it is clear from verse 6 that David is speaking of himself while placed in exile.

Latin:

Vers. 3.

A FINIBVS TERRÆ AD TE CLAMAVI) Nempe ultra Jordanem, quo profugerat Absolomi metu, 2. Sam. 17, 22.

COnf. Exod. 16, 35. Deuter. 13, 7. Non adeo convenit Theodoreti & Euthymii explicatio, quasi oratio sit populi apud Babylonios captivi. Neque Bellarmino, etsi ad Hilarium, Hieronym. & Augustinum provocet, calculum adjicere possumus, quia Davidem in exilio positum de se loqui è v. 6. liquet.

## 61:4
Verse 5.

YOU HAVE GIVEN AN INHERITANCE TO THOSE WHO FEAR YOUR NAME. In Hebrew it is a genitive construction: the inheritance of those who fear. Piscator, the Dutch, and others with Kimchi understand this as the tabernacle, but it is more correctly explained as the inheritance of the goods of both this life and the future life promised to the pious. 1 Tim. 4:8.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

DEDISTI HÆREDITATEM TIMENTIBUS NOMEN TUUM. In Ebr. est regimen: hereditatem timentium: Quam de tabernaculo Piscat. Belgæ & alii cum Kimchio intelligunt, sed rectius de promissa piis hæreditate bonorum tum hujus tum futuræ vitæ explicatur. 1. Tim. 4, 8.

## 61:5
Verse 6.

THOU SHALT ADD DAYS UPON DAYS TO THE KING. He speaks of himself as King, and he also uses that argument tacitly, so that God may increase his days, because he is the King of the Lord's people. Therefore he does not say TO ME, but TO THE KING, and thus he asks at the same time that he may not perish in exile. Coccejus renders this meaning: Thou givest eternal life to Christ from the dead, Is. 53, 8. Bellarmine also accepts it regarding Christ. But that life is asked for him here, who receives that he will proclaim it forever, is evident from the collocation of verse 9; for whom he also wishes it to be obtained, that grace and truth may guard him in his rule. Cf. Psalm 88. Prov. 20, 28. But because he makes mention of generations and an age, we do not deny that successors on the throne are looked to at the same time, and thus also Christ, Luke 1, 32.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

DIES SUPER DIES REGIS ADJICIES. Loquitur de se ut Rege, & argumento quoque illo tacite utitur, ut augeat ipsi Deus dies, quia Rex est populi Domini. Ideo non ait MIHI, sed REGI, ac petit ita simul ne in exilio pereat. Coccejus sensum hunc reddit: Das Christo vitam æternam ex mortuis Es. 53, 8. Bellarm. accipit etiam de Christo. Sed ei hic vitam peti, qui recipit se id deprædicaturum in perpetuum, è collocatione vers. 9. constat; cui etiam exoratum vult, ut gratia & veritas eum in regimine custodiant. Conf. Psalm. 88. Prov. 20, 28. Quod autem generationum & seculi mentionem facit, eo respici simul successores in throno, adeoque Christum etiam haud abnuimus Luc. 1, 32.

## 62:1 Argument
PSALM LXII. Salvation in God. Men are nothing.

Latin:

PSALM. LXII. Salus in Deo. Homines nihil.

## 62:11
Verse 12.

GOD HATH SPOKEN ONCE, THESE TWO THINGS HAVE I HEARD) Once God spoke in Sinai to our ancestors, from which I gather two things by far most certain: that God is both most powerful to avenge his injuries, and wondrously benign toward the pious. Exod. 20, 5. 6. 7.

Others explain that ONCE immutably: because what GOD speaks once is irrevocable: Cf. Job 33, 14. John 10, 35. But they wish it to be twice, meaning several times, I have heard more than once. But what that thing is, which he heard from the immutable word of GOD, he explains next, namely that GOD is both

omnipotent and beneficent: Power belongs to GOD, and to thee is grace. Coccejus thinks it can be distinguished thus: Once GOD spoke twice: which I heard. But neither is the meaning sufficiently consistent, and the accentuation in the Hebrew text opposes it. His former explanation holds better: That one thing, in which all religion is recapitulated, I have not heard once, but twice, i.e., more often, as Luther also rendered it. It is as irrevocable what GOD speaks once as what he speaks several times. Therefore those [interpretations] of Coccejus are not convenient: and by repeating twice he made it irrevocable. But Gislerius is inept, who in the preface to Cant. ch. 5, strives to prove from this saying that one saying has several literal senses.

Latin:

Vers. 12.

SEMEL LOCVTVS EST DEVS, DVO HÆC AVDIVI) Semel Deus in Sinai locutus est majoribus nostris, inde duo colligo longe certissima: Deum & potentissimum esse ad vindicandas injurias suas, & in pios mire benignum. Exod. 20, 5. 6. 7.

ALii illud SEMEL explicant immutabiliter: quia quod semel DEUS loquitur, irrevocabile est: Conf. Job. 33. 14. Joh. 10, 35. Bis autem esse volunt aliquoties, plus vice simplici audivi. Quid vero illud sit, quod è verbo DEI immutabili audivit, exponit deinceps, nempe quod DEUS &

omnipotens sit & beneficus: Robur est DEO, & tibi tua est gratia. Coccejus ita distingui posse putat: Se- mel locutus est DEUS bis: quod audivi. Sed nec sen- sus satis concinnus est, & repugnat in textu Ebræo accentuatio. Rectius se habet prior ejusdem expli- catio: Illud unum, in quo recapitulatur omnis religio, non semel audivi, sed bis h. e. sæpius, uti etiam reddi- dit Lutherus. Tam est irrevocabile, quod DEUS semel loquitur, quam quod aliquoties. Non ergo commoda sunt illa Cocceji: bisque repetendo fecit il- lud irrevocabile. Ineptus autem est Gislerius, qui præfat. in Cant. cap. 5. ex hoc dicto probare satagit, unius dicti plures esse sensus literales.

## 62:12
Verse 13. FOR THOU WILT RENDER TO EVERY MAN ACCORDING TO HIS WORKS) Rom. 2, 6.

Latin:

Vers. 13. QVIA TV REDDES VNICVIQVE JVXTA OPERA SVA) Rom. 2, 6.

## 63:1 Argument
PSALM LXIII. David's spiritual thirst in the desert of Judah.

Verse 1.

WHEN HE WAS IN THE DESERT OF IDUMAEA] It should be written here and in the Greek copies of Judah, both from the Hebrew text and from the History 1 Sam. 22, 5. 23, 14. 15.
