Sed quomodo Patres intelligi possunt, quum hostes Christi notentur, quos ipse in triumpho suo captivos duxit. Conf. Num. 31,12. cap. 21,1. Cepit quosdam ex iis captivos 2. Par. 28. Captivam duxerunt captivitatem, quod v. 5. di- ctum erat, ceperunt multos captivos, Ideo opponi- tur huic Phrasi שבה שבי captivare captivitatem השיב שבות solvere captivitatem vel captivos Jerem. 33. vers. 11. Psalm. 126. vers. 1. Unde luculentum est, priorem phrasin esse, ducere aliquem captivum, non autem liberare e captivitate. Idque agnoscit Corn. a Lap. ad Es. 4. Capere captivitatem Hebræis non est aliud, quam capere, captivos facere, vinctos ducere, sive hi captivi antea ab aliquo capti fuerint, sive non.

ACCEPISTI DONA IN HOMINIBUS) Id est, pro- pter Homines: accepisti dona ad usum Sacerdotum & Levita- rum. Putet fortem aliquis pro לקחת, quod est accepi- sti, scriptum fuisse חלק quod pro dare sumi solet, ut Deut. 4. versu 19. Job. 39. vers. 17. & inde esse ἔδωκε, quo uti- tur Paulus, μυςικῶς ad Christum hoc referens Eph. 4. vers. 8. quomodo & Justinus hunc locum citat: idemque sequitur Psalterium Romanum hoc loco, & Hilarius: item Arabs & Æthiopicus, sed alii secunda, alii tertia persona ex Paulo. Sed sciendum, etiam accipi recte dici, quæ in hoc accipiun- tur, ut dentur: sicut videre est Exod, 25. vers. 2. & 1. Reg. 17. vers. 10.

Duo hic agit Grotius. Primo corrumpit lectionem, quanquam stoχαςικῶς solum illam de- pravationem insinuet: PUTET FORTE ali- quis. Cæterum reverentia majori tractanda Scri- ptura S. quam ut opinioni, quæ alicui forte in men- tem venire queat, locus, adversus consensum omnium Codicum, relinquatur: omnes enim ha- bent לקחת accepisti: Atque ita etiam legerunt LXX. Interpp. Chaldæus, Hieronymus, Autor vul- gatæ; Cæteri, qui verbum dandi habent, sine du- bio e Paulo huc transtulere. Adhibuit autem Paulus verbum ἔδωκε, tum ut explicaret finem ac- ceptionis, communicationem donorum; tum ut eadem opera instituto suo applicaret, quia de ea communicatione agebat ipse Eph. 4. cap. ideoque non incommoda est illa observatio, quod accipi recte dicantur ea, quæ eo fine accipiuntur ut dentur. Unde non adeo urget Grotius hanc correctionem textus, magis in id intentus, ut corrumpat oraculi sensum; Nam quum agnoscat acceptionem eam designari, quæ pro fine habet dationem, facile patet, NULLATENUS Deo Patri tribui eam posse. Ille enim a nemine accepit dona, ut habeat quod distribuat hominibus. Quæ causa, procul dubio, est, cur maluerit Grotius, scriptum esse DEDISTI dona: Sic enim Deo Patri conveniret. Judæi utique quum viderint non convenire hoc Deo, de Mose id interpretati sunt, cum Chaldæo: quod ascenderit Moses in montem Sinai, & acceperit verba legis pro hominibus. Quum vero manifestum sit non de Mo- se, sed de Deo hic sermonem esse, ac de Deo Patre dici nequeat, quod acceperit dona, sed de Filio Dei id necessario intelligendum sit: in aprico est, Gro- tium dum in gratiam Socinianorum negat, de Messia hîc agi, & de Deo Patre hæc accipi vult, ver- ba textus detorquere, iisque vim inferre. Tum vero in hominibus, vel propter HOMINES, inde- pri- finite accepta dona dicuntur. Quo ergo jure illa restringuntur solum ad usum sacerdotum & Levi- tarum? Tertio accepta sunt dona per ascensionem in cœlum. At quomodo Deus Pater in cœlum ascen- dens, vel etiam, uti pervertit Grotius, tribunal con- scendens, dona accepit pro Levitis & Sacerdotibus? Quarto quid opus illo triumpho, quo captiva duca- tur captivitas, ut Deus dona ad usum Sacerdotum conferat? Denique quantopere hæc στρεβλότης ad- versetur Sancto Apostolo, antea jam ostensum. Nec enim is μυστικῶς tantum ad Christum hæc verba refert, sed sensu literali ac immediato de Christo agere docet. Non convenire hæc DEO Patri, jam monuimus, Christo autem optime con- venire nec ipse Grotius diffitetur annotat. ad Eph. 4. v. 8. Optime autem, inquit, Christo conve- nit hic locus, qui in cœlum ascendere conspectus est, deinde per Apostolorum doctrinam vicit, & velut ca- ptivam egit idololatriam, & vitia alia: sumsitque a Patre dona, quæ hominibus dispartiretur. Αἰχμαλω- σία שב in Psalmis & Num. 31. vers. 12. est captivo- rum multitudo. Hæc Grotius. Cur ergo quod Christo optime convenit, DEO Patri vero non congruit, secundum sensum primo obvium & im- mediatum de Deo Patre intelligi vult, de Christo au- tem non intelligit, nisi secundum sensum quendam occultiorem, ac mediatum? Justinus certe & alii Pa- tres, si illos sequi voluisset, sensu literali, & imme- diate de Christo unice explicant, imo tota Chri- stiana Ecclesia, & Apostolus ipse, ὑπὸ πνεύματος ἁγίου φερόμενος, donisque a Christo acceptis & datis maxime conspicuus.

## 68:18
AND INDEED THE UNBELIEVING TO DWELL, O LORD GOD] In the Hebrew: Even the rebellious (supply, thou hast received, from the preceding) that the Lord God might dwell in them. That is, that thou mightest dwell in them, the noun being put for the pronoun, as is often the case among the Hebrews. This is to be understood of the Gibeonites and those like them, who, having long been rebellious to God, became proselytes. Thus here the Chaldean and R. Solomon. But how much more eminently these things have been fulfilled through Christ, everyone sees.

It is not said that He who ascended on high received rebels, but gifts for the sake of men, even rebels. Then if we admit also that, God (the Son, who is God blessed forever over all) ascending on high shall be said to have received rebels, to this end, that God the Father might dwell in them: or if you say that a noun is put for a pronoun: You Messiah received gifts in men or for the sake of men, even rebels (you received) that You (Messiah) might dwell in them. For the Lord Messiah dwells in His temple and in the faithful v. 30. Furthermore, since Grotius, having followed the fiction of the Jews, explains it concerning the Gibeonites and other made proselytes, does he not openly contradict the Apostle interpreting those things concerning the time of the N. T., and holding that passage Eph. 4 as a prophecy, and not indeed as a historical narrative, or a celebration of a deed done. Although indeed he admits that these things were fulfilled more eminently through Christ, it is nevertheless manifest that, while he makes a literal historical sense concerning the Gibeonites, a prophecy concerning the conversion of the Gentiles of the N. T. cannot in any way be feigned here. For he who presents or celebrates the history of preceding times, he certainly does not prophesy concerning things to be long after: unless you also wish to say that, when the history was recited concerning the Gibeonites in the book of Joshua, a prophecy had been proposed concerning the conversion of the Gentiles after the ascension of Christ. Which are absurd.

Latin:

ETENIM NON CREDENTES INHABITARE DO- MINUM DEUM] In Hebræo: Etiam rebelles (supple, ac- cepisti, ex superioribus) ut inhabitaret in illis Dominus Deus. Id est, ut tu inhabitares in illis, nomine posito pro pronomi- ne, ut apud Hebræos sæpe. Intelligendum hoc de Gabao- nitis & eorum similibus, qui diu rebelles Deo facti sunt pro- selyti. Ita hic Chaldæus & R. Salomo. Quanto autem hæc eminentius per Christum sint impleta, nemo non videt.

Non dicitur rebelles accepisse is, qui ascendit in altum, sed dona propter homines, etiam rebelles. Tum si admittamus etiam illud, Deus (Filius, qui est Deus benedictus in secula super omnia) ascen- dens in altum accepisse dicetur rebelles, hoc fine, ut inhabitaret in illis Deus Pater: aut si positum di- cas pro pronomine nomen: Tu Messia accepisti do- na in hominibus vel propter homines, etiam rebelles (accepisti) ut Tu (Messia) habitares in illis. Nam Messias Dominus in templo suo & fidelibus habi- tat v. 30. Porro cum Grotius commentum Judæo- rum sequutus, de Gabaonitis aliisque proselytis factis explicat, annon aperte contradicit Aposto- lo de N. T. tempore illa interpretanti, & pro vati- cinio, non vero pro historica narratione, aut rei ge- stæ celebratione ista habenti Eph. 4. Quanquam vero fateatur, eminentius hæc per Christum impleta, manifestum tamen est, dum sensum literalem hi- storicum facit de Gabaonitis, non posse hic ulla- tenus fingi prophetiam de conversione gentium N. T. Qui enim textus historiam exhibet aut cele- brat temporum antegressorum, ille certe non vati- cinatur de longe post futuris: nisi etiam dicere ve- lis, cum historia recitata fuit de Gabaonitis in li- bro Josuæ, vaticinium propositum fuisse de con- versione gentium post ascensionem Christi. Quæ inepta sunt.

## 68:19
Vers. 20.

Latin:

Vers. 20.

## 68:27
Vers. 28.

THERE IS BENJAMIN THE YOUTHFUL ONE IN AN ECSTASY] Ἐν ἐκστάσει. They took רָדָם as one word, when it is more true that it is from רָדָד, which is Lord, and the suffix which signifies to them. Benjamin the little one ruled over them. The Benjaminite tribe was small 1 Sam. 9, 20. yet from it King Saul emerged.

What was the point here of mentioning Saul's reign? Where the subject is the celebration of God in the churches of the nations, and the gifts which kings were to offer to God, and envoys coming from Egypt, and Ethiopia about to stretch out her hands to God? That gloss of Grotius is forced and entirely contrary to the text. But we have spoken of the meaning before.

Latin:

Vers. 28.

IBI BENJAMIN ADOLESCENTULUS IN MENTIS EXCESSU] Ἐν ἐκστάσει. Sumserunt רָדָם pro una voce, cum verius sit esse à רָדָד, quod est Dominum, & affixo quod eis si- gnificat. Benjamin parvulus dominatus est eis. Tribus Benja- minitica exigua 1 Sam. 9, 20. tamen ex ea Rex exstitit Saul.

Quid hic attinebat Saulis Regimen comme- morare ? Ubi de Deo in Ecclesiis gentium cele- brando agitur, & de muneribus, quæ Deo Reges oblaturi erant, de legatis ex Ægypto venturis, de Æthiopia manum extensura ad Deum ? Coacta illa, textuique prorsus contraria est Grotii glossa. De sensu vero antea diximus.

## 68:30
Verse 31. REBUKE THE BEASTS OF THE REED] The archer-bands. The Ammonites seem to be meant. See 1 Sam. 11, 20. CONGREGATION OF BULLS AMONG THE CALVES OF THE PEOPLES, THAT THEY MAY EXCLUDE THOSE WHO ARE PROVED WITH SILVER, SCATTER THE NATIONS] You might translate more correctly: The assembly of bulls who glory in the calves of the peoples, that they may come with fragments of silver. Scatter the nations that desire wars. By bulls are to be understood leaders, by calves the soldiers who follow them, as in Psalm 22, v. 13, that they may come with fragments of silver, namely to redeem peace.

Latin:

Vers. 31. INCREPA FERAS ARUNDINIS ] Agmina sagittifera. Intelligi videntur Ammonitæ. Vid. Sam. 11, 20. CONGREGATIO TAURORUM IN VACCIS PO- PULORUM, UT EXCLUDANT EOS QUI PROBATI SUNT ARGENTO, DISSIPA GENTES ] Rectius vertas : Cœtum taurorum qui in vitulis populorum gloriantur, ut ve- niant cum fragmentis argenti. Dissipa gentes, quæ bella vo- lunt. Per tauros intelligendi duces, per vitulos milites qui eos sequuntur ut Psalm. 22. v. 13. ut veniant cum fragmentis argenti, nempe ad redimendam pacem.

## 68:31
Verse 32.

ENVOYS WILL COME FROM EGYPT] The word חשמנים is Egyptian. But it is also used by the Hebrews afterwards, whence the name of the Hasmonean nation. The Jews call the Roman Cardinals by this name. To the Arabs, חשם means riches. He wishes to say that men of the greatest dignity will come from Egypt into Judea, namely when they would bring the tribute promised to Solomon.

The Rabbis interpret that word as PRINCES, such as R. David Kimchi and R. Aben-Ezra. It was said before about kings who were to offer gifts. Which does not fit Solomon, or the promised offering. And the Psalmist addresses God Himself: Confirm this, O God, which You have worked in us. From Your temple in Jerusalem, Kings will offer gifts TO YOU. It is God, therefore, to whom kings are to offer gifts, not Solomon, but the Messiah, who is more than Solomon, the true God. So also in this verse, Princes will come from Egypt: To whom, if not to Him to whom kings will offer gifts, and to whom Ethiopia will stretch out her hands? That is, to God, as the words subjoined have it, by which name Solomon can by no means be understood, but only the Messiah. To what end? For the sake of religious worship: for to stretch out hands to God is to worship, adore, and invoke Him religiously, 1 Tim. 2, 8, whence it is again evident that the discourse is about none other than the Messiah. Since religious invocation cannot be offered to a mere man without idolatry. And what was the point, that in this so notable prophecy it should be predicted by the Holy Spirit and so highly proclaimed that men of chief dignity were to bring the tribute promised to Solomon, so that for that reason he should excite all the kingdoms of the earth to the celebration of God, and the Psalmist should even exclaim, Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God, sing to the Lord, who ascends above the heaven of heavens: Bless God the Lord in the churches, etc.? Who does not see that far more eminent things are proposed here, nay, are predicted as about to happen hereafter, concerning all the kingdoms of the earth, and that the very conversion of the nations and kingdoms of the earth is designated?

Verse of the same.

ETHIOPIA WILL PREVENT HIS HANDS TO GOD] In the Hebrew: Ethiopia will make her hands run to God. Her hands, that is, she will hasten to bring gifts to God, as the Queen of Sheba did, who is reckoned to Ethiopia, 1 Kings 10, below 72, 10. These things were fulfilled more eminently when both Egyptians and Ethiopians offered in the Church the oblations which Christians are accustomed to offer.

By the Hebrew phrase, not only gifts which are offered to God are noted, but especially prayers, which, when they are made, are said to have hands stretched out to God, and thus the whole divine worship is designated by synecdoche. Therefore the Targum explains: And he will spread out his hands in prayer. Luther, in his first translation of the year 1521, in Volume 1 of the Jena German edition, fol. 474, rendered it: Morenland will run to GOD with its hands. They will not run across the field, for Christ is in all places, but will remain in their land, and yet run to GOD with deed and life, these are their hands. But then, rendering the meaning, he translated it thus: Morenland will stretch out its hands to GOD. But Grotius preferred to take it of gifts only, so that he might twist those things toward Solomon. But gifts are not said to be offered to Solomon, hands are not to be stretched out to Solomon, but to God, and not by the Queen perhaps, but by the kingdom itself, not from some part of Ethiopia, but from Ethiopia itself. Therefore these things cannot be understood of the Queen of Sheba: who is indeed read to have offered gifts to Solomon, but is not read to have hastened to God for the sake of religious worship, although we do not deny that she was eventually converted to God, and also stretched out her hands to God. But that is not the subject of the present Psalm, nor of Psalm 72, verse 10. For in both places there is a prophecy about the Messiah and the time of the New Testament: And since Ethiopians are joined here with Egyptians in the same kind of worship, with Grotius admitting it, and since the same man concedes that he who ought to offer gifts to God, which is a worship of the first table and religious, therefore the Princes of Egypt are also undoubtedly implied to be about to exhibit the same worship, and not to be bringing the tribute promised to Solomon. But how are these things fulfilled more eminently concerning the Egyptians and Ethiopians in the New Testament, if they speak of the tribute and worship of Solomon? For if you say that he himself was a type of the Messiah in that matter, it will have to be taught not only from the Scriptures that he was a type of the Messiah in receiving the tribute from Egypt, but also that this is indicated in this place, and that the Psalmist here presents him as a type of the Messiah in that matter. And since the Psalmist proceeds further, and commands the kingdoms of the world to sing to God, and thus by this form of speaking, even with Calvin himself admitting it, pronounces that there will be voluntary worshippers of God who had previously despised Him, since the knowledge of God alone would unlock their tongues and loosen them to preach the name of God, how can that be adapted to the time of Solomon, or to Solomon himself, if it were predicted that Princes from Egypt would come to him, and Ethiopia would offer gifts to him? The discourse is about the kingdom of the Messiah, to whom it is predicted that all the kingdoms of the world will submit themselves. The Psalmist addresses the Lord, who ascends on high in verse 29, which B. Luther rendered thus: 'Then God has established your kingdom. This, O God, we wish you to strengthen for us, for it is your work.' Since he speaks of God, whose kingdom he designates, and yet places God over him, as the one from whom he obtained the kingdom, it is certain that no one else can be understood than the Messiah, of whom David speaks likewise in Psalm 45:8: 'God, your God, has anointed you.' And he teaches that gifts will be offered to this King in verse 30: 'Because of your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring you gifts.' That these cannot apply to Solomon, or be explained as gifts promised to him, but must be understood of the Messiah, is clear. For he is the only one constituted King by God the Father, to whom, as Lord, the temple is claimed in Malachi 3:1, who strengthens the kingdom, and whose work it is: because he is true God, even if as man he received the kingdom from the Father. Of this God and King, therefore, the Psalmist sings: that Egypt will send ambassadors to him, that Ethiopia will stretch out her hands to him, and he warns all the kingdoms of the world to do the same: that they may sing to this God, celebrate the glory of this Lord, and propagate it, verse 33. He teaches that he is the same one who from the beginning is carried in heaven: concerning whom it is helpful to transcribe the commentary of B. Luther from Vol. 1, Jena, f. 475: 'At the time of the Jews, they named God, who hovers over the Cherubim, or over Jerusalem, which God had chosen for himself as his dwelling, to which all devotion and attention of all the saints had to be bound to: That Daniel also in Babylon, when he prays, turned himself toward Jerusalem. But now after Christ's ascension all that is over, there is no longer a physical city, no Cherubim, but we serve Him, and hang upon Him, who hovers there, and ascends above all heavens, so that in all the world He may be served, wherever the heaven stretches over us, so that everything is free to serve God, as free as the heaven is, the throne of Him whom we serve; Yes, in the heaven of all heavens, so that the angels also serve the same, and show Him the same service as we do, for the service of the angels is not bound to outward things; Thus also the service of Christians is not, both serve spiritually. Yet it is not another new God, whom the Jews have had above their Cherubim, He has hovered from the beginning in the heaven of all heavens, for the angels have always served Him so, also the first fathers, Adam, Noah, Abraham up to Moses, who served his God as above the Cherubim, or at Jerusalem. So wherever they came, it was the same to them, for God did that for the Jews for a time for their good, that He promised to hover at Jerusalem, and above the Cherubim, until Christ should come, etc. It is too manifest that the God is indicated to whom the Egyptians and Ethiopians are to be subject, and thus that these things can be accepted concerning the ONLY MESSIAH God-man, and not indeed concerning Solomon, or any other mere man, nor do they pertain to the Old Testament, but to the times of the New Testament. Which Calvin was also forced to acknowledge: It is enough to hold the counsel of David, that Ethiopia and Egypt would come under the power of God, and not only them, but far distant regions of the world (which certainly was not done in the Old, but in the New Testament). And now he proceeds further than before, while he bids the kingdoms of the world sing to God, and therefore the calling of the Gentiles is proved from this, that Moses and the Prophets summon them to offer a sacrifice of praise. And Rivetus in this place acknowledges this ILLUSTRIOUS PROPHECY concerning the calling of the Gentiles. Nor is it easily found who has denied this. And that some of the Jews referred those words, SING PRAISES, to the times after the coming of Christ, R. Solomon Jarchi observes on this passage. Grotius, however, could not see even the most manifest things, drunk with a Jewish and Photinian spirit. Concerning the German translation of B. Luther in certain verses of this Psalm, such as verses 14, 16, 19, and 31, those which Megalander has in Vol. VI deserve to be compared. Altenburg. Treatise on Translating page 134 seq. as also page 133. But these things concerning that Psalm, which is truly illustrious and worthy of more lengthy consideration.

Latin:

Vers. 32.

VENIENT LEGATI EX ÆGYPTO] Vox חשמנים est Ægyptia. Sed & Hebræis post usitata, unde nomen gen- ti Asmonæorum. Judæi Cardinales Romanos hoc nomine appellant. Arabibus חשם divitiæ. Vult dicere viros maximæ dignitatis venturos ex Ægypto in Ju- dæam, nempe cum Solomoni pactam adducerent.

Vocem illam interpretantur Rabbini PRIN- CIPES, utpote R. David Kimchi & R. Aben - Ezra. De Regibus munera oblataris dictum antea. Quæ non conveniunt Salomoni, aut oblationi pa- ctæ. Et Deum ipsum alloquitur Psaltes : Confirma hoc Deus, quod operatus es in nobis. A templo tuo in Jerusalem, TIBI offerent Reges munera. Deus ergo est, cui oblaturi sunt munera Reges, non Salomo, sed Messias, qui plus quam Salomo, verus Deus. Sic etiam hoc versu, venient Principes ex Ægy- pto: Ad quem, nisi ad eum, cui munera Reges offerent, & ad quem manus extendet Æthiopia ? hoc est ad Deum, ut verba subjuncta habent, quo nomine nequaquam Salomo intelligi potest, sed solus Mes- sias. Cui fini ? Religiosi cultus gratia : nam extende- rd manus ad Deum, est ipsum religiose colere, ado- rare & invocare 1. Tim. 2, 8. unde iterum constat, non de alio, quam de Messia sermonem esse. Quum ψιλῷ ἀνθρώπῳ non possit cultus religiosæ invoca- tionis deferri, citra idololatriam. Et quid attine- bat, ut in hoc tam insigni vaticinio prædiceretur a Spiritu S. & tantopere prædicaretur, quod viri præcipuæ dignitatis Salomoni pactam adducturi sint, ut propterea omnia terræ regna ad celebrationem Dei excitaret, adeoque exclamaret Psaltes, Regna terræ cantate Deo, Psallite Domino, qui ascendit su- per cælum cæli: Benedicite in Ecclesiis DEO Domi- no &c. Quis non videt longe eminentiora hic pro- poni, imo ceu deinceps eventura prædici, omnia regna terræ concernentia, ipsamque gentium, & Regnorum terræ conversionem designari?

Vers. eod.

ÆTHIOPIA PRÆVENIET MANUS EJUS DEO ] In Hebræo : Æthiopia currere faciet manus suas Deo. Ma- nus suas, id est, dona festinabit ad Deum afferre, ut fecit Re- gina Sabæ, quæ Æthiopiæ accensetur 1. Reg. 10. infra 72, 10. Impleta hæc eminentius, cum & Ægyptii, & Æthiopes obla- tiones, quas Christiani solent, in Ecclesia obtulere.

Phrasi Hebræa non tantum dona, quæ Deo offeruntur, sed cumprimis preces notantur, quæ cum fiunt, manus extendi ad Deum dicuntur, adeoque per illas totus cultus divinus Synecdochi- ce designatur. Ideo Thargum explicat: Et pan- det manus in oratione. Lutherus in prima transla- tione Anni cIɔ Iɔ XXI. Tomo 1. Jenens. German. fol. 474. reddidit: Morenland wird lauffen zu GOTT mit seinen Händen. Sie werden nicht über Feld lauffen, denn Christus ist an allen Orten, sondern bleiben in ihrem Lande, und doch zu GOTT lauffen mit der That und Leben, das sind ihre Hän- de. Deinde vero sensum reddens ita transtulit: Morenland wird seine Hände ausstrecken zu GOtt. Sed Grotius de donis solum accipere maluit, ut illa ad Salomonem detorqueret. Atqui non Salomo- ni dicuntur dona offerenda, non ad Salomonem manus extendendæ, sed ad Deum, nec a Regina forte, sed a regno ipso, non ab Æthiopiæ parte aliqua, sed ab ipsa Æthiopia. De Regina ergo Sabæ hæc intelligi nequeunt: quæ Salomoni qui- dem legitur munera obtulisse, sed ad Deum festi- nasse religiosi cultus causa non legitur, etsi haud abnuamus, tandem ad Deum conversam fuisse, ac ad Deum etiam manus suas extendisse. Sed de eo neque in præsenti Psalmo agitur, nec Psalm. 72, vers. 10. Utrobique enim Prophetia habetur de Messia, & Novi Testamenti tempore: Et quum Ægyptiis hic conjungantur Æthiopes in eodem ge- nere cultus, fatente Grotio, de his autem conce- dat idem, quod Deo offerre debuerit munera, qui cultus est primæ tabulæ, & religiosus, proinde Ægy- pti etiam Principes sine dubio innuuntur eundem cultum exhibituri, non vero pactam Salomoni ad- ducturi. Quomodo autem hæc de Ægyptiis & Æthiopibus eminentius in Novo Testamento im- pleta, si de pacta, & cultu Salomonis loquuntur? nam si dicas, typum ipsum Messiæ ea in re fuisse, non docendum modo erit e Scripturis, quod in pacta accipienda ex Ægypto Messiæ typus fuerit, sed quod etiam id hoc in loco indigitetur, eun- demque Psaltes, ut Messiæ typum hic ea in re sistat. Et quum longius progrediatur Psaltes, ac regna mundi Deo cantare jubeat, adeoque hac loquendi forma, fatente etiam ipsomet Calvino, volunta- rios Dei cultores fore pronunciet, qui prius eum con- temserant, fiquidem sola Dei cognitio linguas re- seret, ac solvat ad prædicandum Dei nomen, quo- modo id Salomonis tempori, aut Salomoni ipsi, si ad eum Principes ex Ægypto venturi prædiceren- tur, eique munera oblatura Æthiopia, aptari po- test? De regno Messiæ sermo est, cui omnia regna mundi sese submissura prædicuntur. Alloquitur Psaltes Dominum, qui in altum afcendit versu 29. quem ita reddidit B. Lutherus: Dein GOtt hat dein Reich auffgerichtet. Dasselbe wollest du GOtt uns stärcken, denn es ist dein Werck: Ubi quum Deum dicat, cujus regnum designat, & Deum ta- men eidem præficiat, utpote a quo is regnum con- sequutus est, certum est, alium intelligi non pos- se, quam Messiam, de quo pariter loquitur David Psalm. 45, 8. Unxit te o Deus, Deus tuus. Atque huic Regi oblatum iri munera docet v. 30. Um deines Tempels willen zu Jerusalem werden dir die Könige Geschencke zuführen: Quæ non posse Sa- lomoni convenire, vel de pacta ei oblata explicari, sed de Messia accipienda esse, in aprico est. Hic enim unice est Deus a Deo Patre constitutus Rex, cui ceu Domino vindicatur templum Malach. 3, 1. qui confortat regnum, & cujus id opus est: quia verus est Deus, etsi qua homo regnum a Patre ac- ceperit. De hoc ergo Deo & Rege canit Psaltes: quod Ægyptus ad eum legatos missura sit, quod Æthiopia manus ad eum extensura sie, monetque regna mundi universa, ut pariter id faciant: ut huic Deo cantent, hujus Domini gloriam celebrent, ac propagent v. 33. Eundem esse docet, qui ab initio in cœlo vehitur: de quo juvat B. Luth. commenta- rium adscribere e Tom. 1. Jen. f. 475. Zu der Zeit der Jüden nenneten sie GOTT, der da schwebet über Cherubim, oder über Jerusalem, die ihm GOtt erwählet hatte zu seiner Wohnung, dahin muste alle Andacht und Auffsehen aller Heiligen gebunden seyn: Daß auch Daniel zu Babylonien, wenn er betet, gegen Jerusalem sich kehrete. Aber nun nach Christus Auffahrt ist das alles aus, ist kein leibliche Stadt mehr, kein Cherubim, sondern wir dienen dem, und hangen an dem, der da schwebet, und fähret über alle Himmel, daß in aller Welt ihm mag gedienet werden, wo sich der Himmel über uns er= streckt, daß alles frey sey GOtt zu dienen, als frey als der Himmel ist, der Thron deß dem wir dienen; Ja im Himmel aller Himmel, daß auch die Engel demselben dienen, und gleiche Dienst mit uns ihm erzeigen, denn der Engel Dienst ist nicht gebunden an áusserliche Dinge; Also auch nicht der Christen Dienst, beyde geistlich dienen. Doch ists nicht ein ander Neu GOtt, den die Jüden haben über ih= ren Cherubim gehabt, Er ist von anbegin geschwebt im Himmel aller Himmel, denn die Engel haben ihm allezeit so gedienet, auch die ersten Väter, Adam, Noha, Abraham biß auf Mosen, welcher seinem GOtt, als über dem Cherubim, oder zu Jerusalem dienete. So wo sie hin kamen, da war es ihnen gleich, denn GOtt hat das denen Jüden eine zeitlang zu gut gethan, daß er zu Jerusalem, und über Cherubim sich versprach zu schweben, biß daß Christus käme, 2c. Nimis manifestum est, Deum indigitari illum, cui servituri sint Ægyptii & Æthiopes, adeoque de SOLO MESSIA θεανθρώπῳ, non vero de Salo- mone, aut ullo alio ψιλῷ ἀνθρώπῳ hæc accipi pos- se, nec ad Vet. Testam. pertinere, sed ad tempora Nov. Testam. Quod agnoscere etiam coactus fuit Calvinus: Satis est consilium tenere Davidis, Æthio- piam & Ægyptum sub Dei potestatem venturas, neque eas modo, sed longe dissitas mundi plagas (quod utique non in Vet. sed Nov. Testam. factum) Ac jam longius progreditur, quam antea, dum regna mundi cantare Deo jubet, ideoque hinc probatur gen- tium vocatio, quod Moses & Prophetæ eas ad offeren- dum laudis sacrificium accersant. Et Rivetus IL- LUSTRE VATICINIUM hoc loco agnoscit de vocatione gentium. Neque inventus facile, qui hoc negarit. Et e Judæis nonnullos ista, CANTA- TE LAUDES, ad tempora post adventum Chri- sti retulisse, R. Salomo Jarchi observat ad h. l. Grotius vero nec manifestissima quæque videre potuit, spiritu Judaico & Photiniano ebrius. De translatione B. Lutheri Germanica in quibusdam versibus hujus Psalmi, utpote vers. 14. 16. 19. & 31. conferri merentur, quæ habet Megalander T. VI. Altenburg. Tr. vom Dolmetschen pag. 134. seq. ut & pag. 133. Sed hæc de illo Psalmo illustri sane, ac prolixiori consideratione dignissimo.

## 69:1 Argument
PSALM LXIX. The most grievous passion of Christ restoring that which He did not take away.

Latin:

PSALM. LXIX. Passio gravissima Christi solventis, quæ non rapuit.

## 69:27
Verse 28. LET THEM NOT ENTER INTO THY RIGHTEOUSNESS) That they may not be partakers of Thy goodness. For it is frequent for the Hebrews to signify beneficence by צדק.

Latin:

Vers. 28. NON INTRENT IN JUSTITIAM TUAM) Bonitatis tuæ ne participes sint. Nam Hebræis frequens per צדק significare beneficentiam.

## 69:28
Verse 29. LET THEM BE BLOTTED OUT OF THE BOOK OF THE LIVING, AND NOT BE WRITTEN WITH THE RIGHTEOUS] Those are called living here who enjoy good health, which the law promises to those who keep the law. Thus, on the contrary, diseases are often understood by the name of death. חיה is translated as healthy in Leviticus several times, and likewise in Isaiah 38:21.

These things are wrongly explained concerning bodily health. Because there is no reason why the living should not be understood as those who live, but rather those who enjoy good health. Furthermore, nowhere is the book of those who enjoy good health attributed to God; but who does not know that the book of life is attributed to God? Thirdly, by the book of life or of the living, Holy Scripture does not understand the book of those living in this age or of this life, but the book of another life and of the future age, which is called the book even by way of excellence in Dan. 12:1 and the book written by God in Exod. 32:32.

or the book of life Phil. 4:3, Rev. 3:5, ch. 17:8, ch. 20:12, ch. 22:19, sometimes also the book of the life of the Lamb Rev. 13:8, ch. 21, etc. Fourthly, even if the law promises among other things also good health and long life, yet these are not its chief promises; But it promises primarily the life of the other age. Therefore, the Grotian interpretation proceeds from a false hypothesis, as if only the good things of this life were promised to the righteous in the law. Fifthly, as all who are justified pertain to the righteous, which the whole Scripture cries out can only be done through faith, and they are also written as heirs of eternal life, for whom He justifies, them He also glorifies Rom. 8:30, so conversely those who are not written as heirs of eternal life do not pertain to the righteous and are not written with them; and this is what it means not to be written in the book of the living, or to be blotted out of the book of the living: because that being blotted out is explained here negatively as NOT BEING WRITTEN, and is not to be understood privatively, as if some who were previously inscribed are afterwards erased. For the following verse explains what was said: and let them not be written with the righteous, as Augustine observes on this place. Some with B. Gesner in Dan. Disp. last th. 144. think that the ungodly can also be said to be inscribed in the book of life, by reason of the means, insofar as not life itself, but the cause of life pertains to them, the grace of God, the merit of Christ, the calling of the Holy Spirit, and by reason of their own persuasion, while they think themselves inscribed, and thus according to opinion, as also by reason of their outward conversation in the Church, since they are mixed with the truly elect, nor can they be easily distinguished from them; who therefore are said to be blotted out of the book of the living, when it is manifest that they have despised the means of salvation, and have boasted of holiness only falsely, and have never been true members of the Church. But because this blotting out from the book of life is a punishment, it cannot refer only to a bare persuasion and opinion. Some establish two books, one of present grace, the other of future glory, as Molineus in Anatom. Arminianism. c. 18 §. 15, from the former some can be blotted out, but not from the latter. Euthymius likewise posits different books, as does Hackspan, who indeed acknowledges that the negative explanation favors the passage Job 39:17, but thinks it is hindered by the fact that deletion has the nature of a punishment, and is therefore a privation, not a negation, and therefore he posits an ellipsis of the word עוד (anymore) here, so that the sense is: And let them not be written anymore with the righteous, as in Jer. 30:19. But there is no reason why we should depart from Augustine's explanation, or invent an ellipsis here. For the supreme punishment of infidelity is that non-inscription in the book of life, which is exclusion from eternal life. Sixth, the preceding words, 'let them not enter into thy righteousness,' and the whole context teach that the discourse is about the book of the other life, and eternal salvation. What is more, seventh, even the Jews acknowledge that the discourse here is about the book of the other life: 'let them be blotted out of the book of the living,' that is, as R. Aben-Ezra explains, from the heavens. R. David Kimchi on the words of v. 28, 'into thy righteousness': or happiness: which you work for Israel in the future time, or after death: It is a simile from Kings, who have memorial books as in Mal. 3:16, Dan. 12:1. They are to be blotted out, that is, in this age let not their death be an expiation of sins. Arama, or let them not be written in the book of life.

Add to these finally, that this treats of the enemies of Christ, against whom the sacred psalmist does not so much vow as threaten eternal destruction by the Prophetic Spirit. For the argument of the Psalm is the sufferings of Christ, which Hilary teaches is placed beyond the hazard of doubt in this place: IT IS NOT DOUBTED that the Psalm itself contains the mystery of the Lord's passion, for besides the Apostle John, who testified that the fulfillment of the Scriptures consisted in the drinking of vinegar, since also this saying by the same was taken up under the Apostles' recollection: Zeal for your house has consumed me, it removed ambiguity, and confirms that ALL things said and done regarding him must be referred; therefore, having undergone the lot of all human passions, he speaks according to our assumed infirmities. St. Augustine also excludes all doubt in this Psalm. For because Christ speaks here, we are not permitted to doubt at all; for here are the express words, which were fulfilled in his passion: They gave me gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink: when these things were fulfilled to the letter, and exactly as they were predicted, so they were rendered. And when Christ himself had said, I thirst, hanging on the cross, and at this word vinegar was given to him on a sponge, which having received he said, It is finished, and thus bowing his head he gave up the spirit, showing that all these things which were predicted had been finished in him at that time, it is not permitted to understand anything else here. The Apostles also, speaking of Christ, gave testimonies from this Psalm. But who would deviate from their opinions? Or what lamb would not follow the Rams? Therefore Christ speaks here. There is no need to bring in others: For almost ALL ancient expositors agree (which Bellarmine notes in the argument of this Psalm) such as Hilary, Augustine, Jerome: and more recent ones, such as Genebrardus, Jansenius, Agellius and others, that in this Psalm the PASSION OF CHRIST is predicted plainly TO THE LETTER, as well as the overthrow of the Jews, and the building of the Church. There is one, Theodoret, followed by Euthymius, who thought the Psalm should be explained regarding the Babylonian captivity of the Jews: but the Blessed Augustine constantly rebukes those who dare to explain otherwise than the Apostles have explained. For the Apostles affirm that those things were predicted of Christ: They who hate me without cause John 15. and that; Zeal for your house has consumed me John 2. likewise that: The reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen upon me Rom. 15. and that: In my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink, John 19. and that: Let their habitation be desolate, and let there be no one to dwell in it. Acts 1. These are Bellarmine's.

But what of our Grotius? He preferred to Judaize here also with Calvin: and to interpret the words of the Psalm not indeed in his annotations on the Psalms (for here he has nothing on the argument of the Psalm) but in parallel places of the New Testament, not of the Messiah, but of David according to the letter. On John 2:17, he has it thus: The Apostles recalled to themselves a famous passage of the Psalms and one commonly accustomed to be sung: For it was established that the Messiah was described there under the person of DAVID: On Rom. 15:3, the words are David's, who is a FIGURE of Christ, in the Psalm according to the Hebrews 69. see Matt. 27:39, 40, 41, 42. Christ endured all these things for the sake of God and men. And on Acts 1:16, It was fitting that something similar should happen to Judas, as had happened to ACHITOPHEL, whose treachery Judas had imitated. Thus, therefore, he interprets it according to the letter concerning David and what had happened to him from Achitophel and others. That the present Psalm is a prophecy concerning Christ is taught by (1) The passions, which are described here, are most grievous. For these are so great that they altogether exceed the passions of David, and were not endured except by the Messiah, joined even with infernal sorrows, ver. 2, 3, 4, 15, 16, which are designated by waters entering the soul, and the deep mire not offering a place to stand, and similar things. Cf. Ps. 87:4, seqq. (2) The cause of the passions: which is not his own fault, because he paid what he did not steal v. 5, but another's, and therefore imputed v. 6, and they hate me without cause, he says v. 5, which John testifies was fulfilled in Christ, indeed Christ himself John 15 v. 25, they hate me and my Father, that the word might be fulfilled which is written in their law, because they hated me without cause. (3) Satisfaction for our sins, which is indicated by the payment of those things which he who complains here did not steal v. 6. Which not I, but Adam and Eve in Paradise stole, I am forced to pay back; For they wished to steal divinity and lost happiness: according to Augustine. See on this passage at length Mr. Dr. Dorscheus in two Pentadecad Dissertations. Augustine presents the sum in this place: I did not steal, and I was paying, I did not sin, and I was giving penalties. For he alone, being such, truly stole nothing. Not only did he steal nothing, but also he emptied himself of what he did not have from theft, so that he might come to us. Phil. 2. And Bede T. 7. on this Psalm: I was paying what I did not steal, that is, I bore penalties for sin, because I did not commit sin. Which is said by way of likeness: i.e., as if someone were to steal something, and another who was without fault were to pay for it. For Adam and Eve committed disobedience, for which Christ, who did not commit sin, paid the penalties. Nor does Hilary think otherwise in this place. Christ, when he was not a debtor of death and sin, was held as a debtor of sin and death by those who were exercising in him the law of sin which is in our members. For by sin he condemned sin in the flesh. Strabus Fuldensis in the ordinary gloss agrees here, Peter Lombard in the Catena on the Psalter, Hugo de S. Charo in his Postils, who repeat the words of Augustine: Lyranus in this place: It is a manner of speaking, by which it is signified that Christ then paid the penalty for the sins of the human race, which he had not contracted. And thus also the other interpreters, Pelbartus of Temesvár, Jacobus Faber Stapulensis, Jacobus Peresius, de Valentia, Arias-Montanus, Genebrardus, Lindanus, Jansenius, Reinerus, Snoygdanus, Cajetanus, M. Antonius, Flaminius, Bellarminus, Menochius, Tirinus, Lorinus: who also notes that the expositors agree on this, especially the Latins: as well as Didymus, and to Marcellinus on the Interpretation of the Psalms. Athanasius. Add to these also Thomas, and his interpreters, part 3, Summa, q. 48, art. 2. Latin prayers from the Psalter published at Lyons in the year 1545: Help me, my Lord Jesus Christ, who once labored under a calamity, I will not say similar, but in infinite parts greater, and you paid then what you had not taken, that is, you expiated the sins of all men. Which testify concerning the faith of the Roman Catholic Church. Add also from the Reformed, Pellican, Felinus, Piscator, Junius, Tremellius, the Belgian interpreters. From our own, B. Luther, B. Hagen, Gesner, Tarnovius, the Weimar paraphrasts, and any others. All here agree. And the words of the text are manifest: For אשיב denotes I will pay, I will satisfy, and it is used when there is talk of the λύτρον of redemption, Lev. 25, 51, or of satisfaction, Gen. 50, 15, Num. 5, 7, c. 18, 9, 1 Sam. 6, 3, 4. and 17, or the returning of plunder, Lev. 2, 4, or ἀνταπόδοσις, Prov. 17, 13; indeed, as often as this word is joined with plunder or another offense, so that it is opposed to it, it implies either the imposition of a penalty or payment and satisfaction. Whence the Chaldean rendered it here אשלם from שלם which is he returned, paid, compensated, 1 Kings 4, 7, Ps. 37, 12, so that it may be hinted that restitution was made in place of the plunder, that is, satisfaction, and that of a pacificatory or reconciliatory nature, because that word is used concerning reconciliation, 1 Kings 22, 44, Prov. 16, 7. The LXX explained it τότε ἀπετίννυον, then I paid: ἀποτιννύειν is to compensate for an offense or debt, to pay, to repay, to give penalties, to blot out by satisfaction, to expiate: Compare Gen. 30, 30, Syr. 20, 11, Phil. 2, 18. Aquila interprets it ὅσα ἐκ ἐβιασάμην τότε ἐπίςρεψον, which signifies to restore to the whole, to refund, to return; those things which were snatched, lost, or taken away by the violence of men, he himself returned, reintegrated, restored. The Rabbis themselves interpret this word thus: I restored what I did not snatch, they forced that; as if I had snatched something by violence. R. Obadia Gaon also explains it concerning true restitution, even if he twists it to something else: I restored: the Egyptians were demanding that which they gave as a loan, Ex. 12. So also R. Solomon Jarchi: I restored what I did not receive, gifts for my peace I gave to be redeemed (what I did not plunder from them), as Hezekiah did with the King of Assyria: or I was vehemently oppressed by the nations: they exacted whatever they wished, and I did not dare to resist. Although everyone may see that these things belong to another, they nevertheless demonstrate the genuine meaning of the word, because it brings about a payment, and a peace-making restitution, and satisfaction. But no mortal can say that he pays what he did not plunder, when he suffers punishment from God, before whom no one is innocent: no one can provide satisfaction or payment for others. Wherefore it is necessary that we accept this concerning the Messiah, as almost all the interpreters do, to a man.

To which add now also the remaining arguments from the text, which we shall briefly touch upon: which prove the same thing: namely (4) Faith in that person who suffers these things, and complains that he himself is suffering: on account of whom the faithful may not be confounded, as he prays in v. 7. Let them not be ashamed IN ME, who wait for thee O Lord, Lord of hosts, let them not be confounded IN ME, who seek Thee O GOD of Israel: because for thy sake I have borne reproach. For these things indicate the Messiah, in whom those who place their trust are not ashamed, or confounded. (5) The reproach, which he sustained for the glory of God, is meritorious and satisfactory. For on account of that he asks that those believing IN HIM may not be confounded: because, he says, for thy sake I have borne reproach, confusion has covered my face. (6.) Rejection by the Jews: which happened to Christ, on account of zeal for the house of the Lord, not to David, in whose time the temple of the Lord had not yet been built v. 9. (7) Singular zeal for the temple of the Lord: The zeal of thy house has eaten me up: that this was said concerning Christ, and was fulfilled in him, the Apostles acknowledged: when Christ cast out those selling from the temple, and the oxen, and the sheep, and poured out the coin of the money-changers, and overturned the tables: And to those who were selling doves, he said: take these things away from here, and do not make my Father's house a house of merchandise: For then his disciples remembered that it is written; The zeal of thy house has eaten me up Joh. 2, 17. (8) The reproaches of those reproaching God himself, and the utmost innocence and patience in the same v. 11. seqq. Which the Apostle also explains directly and immediately concerning Christ Rom. 15, 13. For Christ did not please himself, but as it is written, the reproaches of those who reproached thee fell upon me. Psalm. 69. v. 10. (9.) A most ardent prayer, poured out in an acceptable time v. 14. seqq. which the Lord testifies was heard Is. 49, 8: in an acceptable time I have heard thee. Moreover, that he was forsaken for that very time, and had no comforter, concerning which he complains in verse 21, agrees with the complaints of the Messiah instituted in Psalm 22, verse 2. seqq. (10.) The drinking of gall and vinegar in his thirst verse 12. Which was nowhere fulfilled in David, as far as the letter is concerned. But in Christ it was fulfilled just as the words sound, as witnessed by the quartet of Evangelists Matth. 27. verse 34. Mark 15, 22. Luke 23. v. 36. John 19. verse 28. and this last one expressly pointing his finger at this oracle. Where it is also to be observed, that the Evangelists exhibit that distinct kind of drink distinctly. For concerning the gall, which was accustomed to be given to those being punished, mixed with wine, so that their mind might be taken away and they themselves might be intoxicated, as Hackspan teaches from the Talmud and Maimonides. Prolegomena to the Philological and Theological notes, p. 7. Matthew reports in chapter 27, verse 34, that Christ refused it: but concerning the vinegar, John chapter 19, verse 29, and Matthew himself in the cited chapter, verse 48, as also Mark chapter 15, 36, do not teach that Christ refused it, indeed John testifies that he received it: Which distinct drinks, predicted by David, were accurately fulfilled in Christ. Whence Calvin twists himself here, and distorts the words of David to a figurative sense: Although, he says, the expressions are metaphorical, to mix gall, or poison with wine, and to drink vinegar, just as in Jeremiah 11, 19, to cast wood into the bread: yet John chapter 19, 29, does not record in vain that the Scripture was fulfilled, where the soldiers gave vinegar to Christ on the cross: because it was necessary that the cruelty which the wicked exercise against his members be represented by a visible sign in Christ, just as we said in Psalm 22, v. 19, when the partition of Christ's garments was made among the soldiers, that that verse was not cited unseasonably: they divided my garments among themselves, and upon my vesture they cast lots. Although David understands figuratively that he had been despoiled, and that his fortunes had been plundered like booty: yet the GENUINE sense must be held, that no relief was given to the holy Prophet: just as if a man, otherwise miserably afflicted, should also find food and drink corrupted with bitterness. This is Calvin; proving a similar error from the corruption of one place to another. But just as the depravity of Calvin was abundantly refuted in Psalm 22, so here there is no cause why one should depart from the literal sense, and a metaphorical expression be feigned, unless it is a preconceived opinion that the discourse here is about David himself: but there is a most grave cause why the literal sense must be retained, because according to the letter it was fulfilled just as it was predicted by David, and the same Spirit, who once prophesied concerning it through David, the best Interpreter of his own words, most explicitly testifies concerning it. For not so that the cruelty which is accustomed to be exercised against the pious, the members of Christ, might be represented, but so that those things which were predicted concerning Christ by David might also be fulfilled in him, John 19, 28 testifies that that drinking took place. Afterwards Jesus seeing that ALL THINGS were CONSUMMATED, that the Scripture might be CONSUMMATED, said, I thirst: There was therefore a vessel set full of vinegar: But they putting a sponge full of vinegar around hyssop, offered it to his mouth. When therefore Jesus had received the vinegar, he said, IT IS CONSUMMATED. This therefore remained to be consummated, or fulfilled, from those things which the Holy Spirit had predicted, that he should be given to drink, according to the prophecy of David, with vinegar: which therefore was thus also fulfilled, when Christ exclaimed, I thirst. How could a more evident interpretation be given, by which whatever Calvin has invented concerning a figurative expression might be blown into the air? And he still trifles, that THE GENUINE SENSE IS, that no relaxation was given to David, just as if a wretched man were given vinegar and gall to drink, even though the Holy Scripture so clearly testifies that those things are not to be understood otherwise than as they sound, in the literal sense, and that in that way they were fulfilled; and that the Scripture did not predict these things concerning David, but concerning the Messiah, and that they were also fulfilled in the Messiah: Whence Grotius acknowledged in Annotations on Matthew 27:34, that by the offering of that drink made to Christ, the words of David were fulfilled in Christ both κατὰ λέξιν and κατὰ διάνοιαν, asserting it.

(11) The imprecation made against the Jews and the traitor Judas: of both of which we likewise have the Holy Scripture as interpreter. That which was made against the Jews, Romans 11:10: God gave them a spirit of stupor, and David says (Psalm 69) let their table become a snare and a trap, and a stumbling block, and a recompense unto them: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back always. Which, as the Apostle understands them concerning spiritual hardening and blindness, so they were not fulfilled in the enemies of David, but finally in the enemies of Christ, the Jews, and indeed in that whole nation. But the other imprecation made peculiarly against the traitor of Christ is held in verse 26. Certainly these things were never said of Ahithophel, nor does any indication of him occur here: and not even to the Jews could such a thing come to mind. But that it was fulfilled in Judas, the Holy Spirit openly testifies in Acts 1:20.

(12) The celebration of the divine name in verse 31, which in

The circumstances of the text show that the Church of the N. T. is future: Because sacrifices are put aside, and not truly to be instituted with victims v. 23. & the heavens and the whole earth, the sea and all the creeping things in them are invited to praise: & the cause is rendered, the salvation of Zion, and the building of the cities of Judah, which do not fit the time of David, whence the Jews draw these things to the times after the Babylonian captivity: But here the discourse is about the spiritual Zion & Judah Eph. 2, 6. Heb. 12, 22. (not earthly Judea, as that to which the most vast desolation was predicted above v. 26.) so that the pious may dwell in it, and by hereditary right possess their holy land, the Church: Therefore it is added, the seed of his (God's) servants shall possess it, that is, those who have succeeded the faithful Fathers in the true faith. Add that here eternal salvation is promised to the just, through inscription in the book of life; & joy in the future life v. 33. let the poor see and be glad, seek God, and your soul shall live. Whence the Jews themselves also refer this prophecy to the times of the Messiah. R. Aben-Ezra, Basel Edition, on verse 31. I will praise God with a song: After the return in the days of Christ. To which pertains what Galatinus, book 4, on the secrets of the Catholic truth, ch. 23, brings forward from Moses Maimonides, that Jesus of Nazareth, the Messiah, was seen to have been killed in the house of judgment, and that this was the cause that Israel was destroyed by the sword (which is predicted here, as the Apostle interprets in Romans 11, 9.) & from the book Ima he recounts that the second sanctuary was destroyed because of CAUSELESS HATRED, and that it is so grave that it is considered worse than idolatry. Conf. v. 12. & John 15, 25. You will find the complete explanation of the Psalm in Bugenhagen, Dr. Gesner, and Dr. Tarnovius in the Passion Psalms. The opinion of Grotius, who denies that the Psalm treats of Christ according to the letter, has already been rejected in the Fifth Ecumenical Council. See Thomas in the Proemium & Baronius, Annals Vol. 7, to the Year of Christ 533.

Latin:

Vers. 29. DELEANTUR DE LIBRO VIVENTIUM, ET CUM JUSTIS NON SCRIBANTUR] Viventes hic dicuntur, qui bona fruuntur valetudine, quod legem servan- tibus lex promittit. Sic contra mortis nomine sæpe intelli- guntur morbi. חיה ὑγιής vertitur in Levitico aliquoties, nec aliter Esa. 38, 21.

PErperam de valetudine corporali hæc explican- tur. Quia causa non est, cur viventes non intel- ligantur qui vivunt, sed qui bona valetudine fruun- tur. Adhæc nuspiam liber eorum, qui bona va- letudine fruuntur, Deo tribuitur; librum autem vitæ Deo tribui quis nescit? Tertio per librum vitæ vel viventium Scriptura S. non intelligit librum vi- ventium in hoc seculo vel hujus vitæ, sed librum al- terius vitæ ac futuri seculi, qui vel κατ’ ἐξοχὴν liber dicitur Dan. 12, 1. & liber a Deo scriptus Exod. 32, 32.

vel liber vitæ Phil. 4, 3. Ap. 3, 5. cap. 17, 8. cap. 20, 12. cap. 22, 19. nonnunquam etiam liber vitæ agni Ap. 13, 8. cap. 21. &c. Quarto etiamfi lex promittat inter alia etiam bonam valetudinem & vitam longævam, non tamen hæ sunt præcipuæ ejusdem promissiones; Sed promittit imprimis vitam alterius seculi. Procedit ergo interpretatio Grotiana e falsa hypothesi, quasi justis tantum promissa sint in lege bona hujus vitæ. Quinto ut ad justos pertinent quicunque justificantur, quod non nisi per fidem fieri Scriptura tota clamat, illique hæredes etiam scribuntur vitæ æternæ, quos enim justificat, hos etiam glorificat Rom. 8, 30. ita ad justos vice versa non pertinent, & non scribuntur cum ipsis, qui non scribuntur vitæ æternæ hæredes; atque hoc est non scribi in libro viventium, vel deleri e viventium libro: quia illud deleri negative hic exponitur per NON SCRIBI, non vero privative intelligendum, quasi quidam prius inscripti post iterum expungantur. Nam versus sequens exponit quod dictum est: & cum justis non scribantur, ut observat Augustinus in hunc locum. Nonnulli cum B. Gesnero in Dan. Disp. ult. th. 144. censent impios etiam libro vitæ adscriptos dici posse, ratione mediorum, quatenus ad ipsos non quidem vita, sed vitæ causa pertinet, gratia Dei, meritum Christi, vocatio S. S. & ratione propriæ persuasionis, dum se inscriptos putant, adeoque κατὰ δόξαν, ut & ratione externæ conversationis in Ecclesia, cum vere electis admixti sint, nec ab iis facile discerni possint; qui proinde deleri dicuntur de libro viventium, cum palam sit, quod media salutis contempserint, nec nisi falso sanctitatem jactitarint, & vera Ecclesiæ membra nunquam fuerint. Sed quia hæc pœna est deletio e libro vitæ, non potest solum respici nuda persuasio & opinio. Nonnulli duos statuunt libros, alterum gratiæ præsentis, alterum futuræ gloriæ, uti Molinæus Anatom. Arminianism. c. 18. §. 15. ex illo quosdam deleri posse, non autem ex hoc. Euthymius diversos itidem libros statuit, ut & Hackspanius, qui negativæ quidem explicationi locum Job. 39. v. 17. favere agnoscit, sed obstare ei putat, quod deletio habeat rationem pœnæ, adeoque privatio sit, non negatio, ideoque Ellipsin vocis עוד amplius hic statuit, ut sensus sit: Et cum justis non scribantur amplius, ut Jerem. 30, 19. Sed nulla est causa, cur ab Augustini explicatione discedamus, aut ellipsin hic fingamus. Nam pœna summa est infidelitatis illa non inscriptio in librum vitæ, quæ est exclusio a vita æterna. Sexto verba antecedentia, non intrent in justitiam tuam, & totus contextus docet, de libro vitæ alterius, & salute æterna sermonem esse. Quid quod septimo agnoscant etiam Judæi de libro vitæ alterius hic sermonem esse: deleantur e libro viventium, id est, exponente R. Aben-Ezra, de cœlis. R. David Kimchi ad verba v. 28. in justitiam tuam: vel felicitatem: quam pro Israele in tempore futuro, vel post mortem operaris: Est similitudo a Regibus, qui habent libros memoriales ut Mal. 3, 16. Dan. 12, 1. sint obliterandi, id est, in hoc seculo mors eorum ne sit expiatio peccatorum. Arama, vel non sint scripti in libro vitæ.

Adde his postremo, quod hic de hostibus Christi agatur, quibus Hieropsaltes non tam vovet, quam minatur Spiritu Prophetico æternum exitium. Argumentum enim Psalmi sunt passiones Christi, quod extra dubitationis aleam positum esse, docet Hilarius in h. l. NON AMBIGITUR Psalmus ipse Sacramentum passionis Dominicæ continere, nam præter Johannem Apostolum, qui in potatione aceti consistere consummationem Scripturarum testatus est, cum etiam dictum hoc ab eodem sub Apostolorum recorda- tione præsumtum sit : Zelus domus tuæ comedit me, ademit ambiguitatem, confirmatque OMNIA ad eum dicta gestaque esse referenda ; universarum itaque humanarum passionum sortem perfunctus secundum susceptas nostras infirmitates loquitur. Dubitatio- nem omnem excludit quoque S. Augustinus in hoc Pf. Nam quia Christus hic loquitur, dubitare omnino non permittimur ; hic sunt enim expressa verba, quæ in ejus passione completa sunt: Dederunt escam meam fel, & in siti mea potaverunt me aceto: quando ista ad literam impleta sunt, & prorfus quomodo præ- dicta sic reddita. Cumque ipse Christus dixisset, sitio, pendens in cruce, & ad hoc verbum ei acetum in spon- gia datum esset, quo accepto dixit, consummatum est, & sic inclinato capite tradidit spiritum, ostendens ista omnia, quæ prædicta sunt, in illo fuisse tunc consumma- ta, non licet hic aliud intelligere. Apostoli etiam lo- quentes de Christo, testimonia ex isto Psalmo dederunt. Quis autem deviet a sententiis eorum ? Aut quis agnus non sequatur Arietes ? Ergo Christus hic loquitur. Non opus alios adducere : Consentiunt enim fere OMNES expositores veteres (quod notat Bellarm. in argumento hujus Pfalmi) ut Hilarius, Augusti- nus, Hieronymus: & recentiores, ut Genebrardus, Jansenius, Agellius & alii, in hoc Psalmo prædici PASSIONEM CHRISTI plane AD LITE- RAM, nec non eversionem Judæorum, & ædificatio- nem Ecclesiæ. Unus est Theodoretus, quem sequitur Euthymius, qui Psalmum exponendum censuit de ca- ptivitate Babylonica Judæorum: sed Beat. Augustinus constanter reprehendit eos, qui audent aliter exponere, quam Apostoli exposuerint. Apostoli enim de Christo prædicta esse affirmant illa: Qui oderunt me gratis Joh. 15. & illa ; Zelus domus tuæ comedit me Joh. 2. item illa : Opprobria exprobantium tibi ceciderunt super me Rom. 15. & illa : In siti mea potaverunt me aceto, Joh. 19. & illa: Fiat habitatio eorum deserta, & non sit qui habitet in ea. Act. 1. Hæc Bellarmin.

Quid vero Grotius noster ? Maluit ille hic etiam Judaizare cum Calvino : & verba Psalmi non quidem in annot. ad Psalmos (hic enim nihil de ar- gumento Psalmi habet) sed in locis parallelis Nov. Test. non de Messia, sed de Davide quoad literam interpretari. Ad Johan. 2, 17. ita habet : Locum cele- brem Psalmorum & cantari vulgo solitum in memo- riam sibi revocarunt Apostoli : Nam constabat sub DA- VIDIS persona Messiam ibi describi: Ad Rom. 15, 3. verba sunt Davidis, qui FIGURA Christi, Psalmo juxta Hebræos 69. vide Matth. 27, 39. 40. 41. 42. omnia hæc sustinuit Christus Dei ac hominum causa. Et ad Act. 1, 16. Par erat Judæ simile quid evenire, quale ACHITOPHELI evenerat, cujus perfidiam Judas erat imitatus. Sic ergo de Davide & quæ ab Achitophele & aliis ipsi evenerant, secundum lite- ram interpretatur. Quod autem Psalmus præsens vaticinium de Christo sit, docent (1) Passiones, quæ hic describuntur, gravissimæ. Hæ enim tantæ sunt, ut passiones Davidis omnino excedant, nec nisi a Messia exantlatæ sint, cum doloribus etiam infernalibus conjunctæ, vers. 2. 3. 4. 15. 16. qui per aquas animam intrantes, & limum profundum sub- sistendi locum non præbentem, & his similia designan- tur. Conf. Psal. 87, 4. seqq. (2) Causa passionum: quæ est non culpa propria, quia solvit ea quæ non rapuit v. 5. sed aliena, adéoque imputata v. 6. & ode- runt me gratis inquit v. 5. quod in Christo imple- tum Johannes testatur, imo ipse Christus Joh. 15 v. 25. oderunt me & Patrem meum, ut impleatur ser- mo, qui in lege eorum scriptus est, quia odio habuerunt me gratis. (3) Satissactio pro peccatis nostris, quæ in- dicatur per solutionem eorum, quæ hic, qui queri- tur, non rapuit v. 6. Quod non Ego, sed Adam & Eva in Paradiso rapuit, rependere cogor; Illi enim rapere voluerunt divinitatem & perdiderunt felicitatem: juxta August. Vide de hoc loco prolixe Dn. D. Dor- scheum Pentadec. Diss. duabus. Summam exhibet Augustinus in h. l. Non rapui, & exolvebam, non peccavi, & pœnas dabam. Solus enim ipse talis vere nihil rapuit. Non solum nihil rapuit, sed etiam quod non de rapina habebat, hoc se evacuavit, ut ad nos ve- niret. Phil. 2. Et Beda T. 7. in hunc Psalm. Solvebam, quæ non rapui, id est, pro peccato pœnas pertuli, quia peccatum non commisi. Quod est dictum ad similitudi- nem: sc. quasi aliquis aliquid raperet, & alius qui sine culpa esset, illud solveret. Adam enim & Eva inobedi- entiam commisit, pro qua Christus, qui peccatum non commisit, pœnas luit. Nec aliter Hilarius in h. l. Chri- stus cum debitor mortis, peccatique non esset, tanquam peccati & mortis debitor tenebatur ab iis, qui in eo pec- cati legem, quæ in membris nostris est, exercebant. De peccato enim condemnavit peccatum in carne. Con- sentiunt hic Strabus Fuld. in glossa ordinaria, Pe- trus Lombardus in Caten. Psalt. Hugo de S. Charo in Postill. qui verba Augustini repetunt: Lyranus in h. l. Modus est loquendi, quo significatur, quod tunc Christus solvit pœnam pro peccatis generis humani, quæ non contraxerat. Atque ita etiam cæteri Interpp. Pelbartus Temesvariensis, Jacobus Faber Stapulens. Jacobus Peresius, de Valentia, Arias-Montanus, Ge- nebrardus, Lindanus, Jansenius, Reinerus, Snoygda- nus, Cajetanus, M. Antonius, Flaminius, Bellarmi- nus, Menochius, Tirinus, Lorinus: qui notat etiam, convenire in hoc explanatores, præsertim Latinos: nec non Didymum, & ad Marcellin. de Interpret. Psalm. Athanasium. Adde his etiam Thomam, ejusque In- terpp. part. 3. Summ. q. 48. art. 2. Precationes Lati- nas e Psalterio Lugduni An. 1545. editas: Adjuva me mi Domine Jesu Christe, qui quondam non dicam simili, sed infinitis partibus majori calamitate labora- sti, ac persolvisti tum quod non rapueras, h. e. omnium hominum peccata expiasti. Quæ testantur de fide Ecclesiæ Romano-Catholicæ. Adde & e Reforma- tis Pelicanum, Felinum, Piscatorem, Junium, Tre- mellium, Interpp. Belgas. E nostris B. Lutherum, B適切hagen, Gesnerum, Tarnovium, Paraphrastas Vinarienses, & quosvis alios. Omnes hic consen- tiunt. Et verba textus manifesta sunt: Nam אשיב notat solvam, satisfaciam, & adhibetur cum de λύτρῳ redemtionis sermo est Lev. 25, 51. vel de satisfactio- ne Gen. 50, 15. Num. 5, 7. c. 18, 9. 1. Sam. 6, 3. 4. & 17. vel redditione rapinæ Lev. 2, 4. aut ἀνταποδόσει Prov. 17, 13. imo quoties hoc verbum cum rapina aut alio delicto conjungitur, ita ut illi opponatur, aut impositionem pœnæ, aut solutionem & satisfa- ctionem importat. Unde Chaldæus reddidit hic אשלם a שלם quod est reddidit, solvit, compensavit 1. Reg. 4, 7. Psal. 37, 12. ut innuatur restitutio loco ra- pinæ facta, h. e. satisfactio, eaque pacificatoria vel re- conciliatoria, quia verbum illud de reconciliatione adhibetur 1. Reg. 22, 44. Prov. 16, 7. LXX. exposue- re τότε ἀπετίννυον tunc solvi: ἀποτιννύειν est deli- ctum, vel debitum compensare, solvere, rependere, pœnas dare, satisfactione delere, expiare: Conf. Gen. 30, 30. Syr. 20, 11. Phil. 2, 18. Aquila interpretatur ὅσα ἐκ ἐβιασάμην τότε ἐπίςρεψον, quod signifi- cat restituere in integrum, refundere, reddere; quæ per βιασμὸν hominum rapta, perdita, sublata sunt, ipse reddidit, redintegravit, restitui. Rabbini ipsi sic in- terpretantur hoc verbum: Restitui quod non rapui, id coegerunt; ac si aliquid violentia rapuissem. De restitutione vera etiam exponit R. Obadia Gaon, etsi alio detorqueat: Restitui: Ægyptii postulabant id, quod mutuo dabant Ex. 12. Sic etiam R. Salomo Jarchi: Restitui quod non accepi, dona ad pacem meam redimendam (quod ab illis non rapui) dedi, ut Ezechias cum Rege Assur : vel vehementer eram oppressus a gen- tibus: exegerunt, quicquid voluerunt, & non ausus sum resistere. Quæ etsi aliena esse, nemo non videat, verbi tamen significationem genuinam, quod solutionem inferat, ac restitutionem pacificatoriam, & fatisfe- ctionem, demonstrant. Nemo autem mortalium dicere potest, se solvere, quæ non rapuit, cum pœnas a Deo luit, coram quo nemo innocens est: nemo pro aliis satisfactionem vel solutionem præstare potest. Quapropter necessum est, ut de Messia id cum Interpp. ad unum fere omnibus accipiamus.

Quibus adde nunc etiam reliqua e textu argu- menta, quæ breviter attingemus: quæ idem pro- bant: utpote (4) Fides in personam illam, quæ hæc patitur, ac sese pati conqueritur: ob quam fideles non confundantur, uti precatur v. 7. Non erubescant IN ME, qui expectant te Domine, Domine virtutum, non confundantur IN ME, qui quærunt Te DEUS Israel: quoniam propter te sustinui opprobrium. Indi- caut enim hæc Messiam, in quem qui fiduciam col- locant, non erubescunt, aut confunduntur. (5) Oppro- brium, quod pro gloria Dei sustinuit, meritorium & satisfactorium. Ob id enim petit, ne confundan- tur IN IPSO credentes: quoniam, inquit, propter Te sustinui opprobrium, operuit confusio faciem me- am. (6.) Reprobatio a Judæis: quæ Christo obtigit, ob Zelum pro domo Domini, non Davidi, cujus tempore templum Domini nondum erat exstru- ctum v. 9. (7) Zelus singularis pro templo Domini: Zelus domus Domini comedit me: quod de Christo dictum fuisse, inque eo impletum esse, agnoverunt Apostoli: cum Christus ejecit vendentes de templo, & boves, & oves, & nummulariorum æs effudit, mensas- que subvertit: Et his, qui columbas vendebant, dixit: auferte ista hinc, & nolite facere domum Patris mei domum negotiationis: Tunc enim recordati sunt disci- puli ejus, quia scriptum est; Zelus domus tuæ comedit me Joh. 2, 17. (8) Opprobria exprobrantium Deo ipsi, & innocentia ac patientia summa in iisdem v. 11. seqq. Quæ etiam de Christo directe & immediate explicat Apostolus Rom. 15, 13. Etenim Christus non sibi placuit, sed sicut scriptum est, improperia impro- perantium tibi ceciderunt super me. Psalm. 69. v. 10. (9.) Oratio ardentissima, tempore placito effusa v. 14. seqq. quam exauditam esse, testatur Domi- nus Es. 49, 8: in tempore placito exaudivi te. De cæ- tero autem ad tempus ipsum derelictum fuisse, nec consolatorem habuisse, quo de vers. 21. con- queritur, congruit cum querelis Messiæ Psalm. 22. institutis vers. 2. seqq. (10.) Felle & aceto fa- cta in siti potatio vers. 12. Quæ nuspiam in Da- vide impleta, quoad literam. In Christo vero ita ut verba sonant, impleta, teste Evangelistarum quadriga Matth. 27. vers. 34. Marc. 15, 22. Luc. 23. v. 36. Johann. 19. vers. 28. & hoc postremo expresse digitum in hoc oraculum intendente. Ubi & hoc observandum, quod Evangelistæ distinctum illud genus potationis distinctim exhibeant. Nam de felle, quod vino mixtum propinari solebat supplicio afficiendis, ut eriperetur ipsis mens, & inebriaren- tur ipsi, ut e Talmude & Maimonide docet Hack- span. Proleg. in notas Philol. Theol. p. 7. Mat- thæus refert cap. 27. vers. 34. quod id recusavit Chri- stus: de aceto vero & Johannes cap. 19. vers. 29. & Matthæus ipse cap. cit. vers. 48. ut & Marcus cap. 15, 36. non docent recusasse illud Christum, imo Johannes id accepisse eum testatur: Quæ di- stinctæ potiones a Davide prædictæ, in Christo ac- curate impletæ sunt. Unde hic se torquet Calvi- nus, & ad figuratum sensum verba Davidis detor- quet: Quanquam autem, inquit, metaphoricæ sint locutiones, miscere fel, aut venenum vino, & pota- acetum, ficuti apud Jeremiam 11, 19. mittere lignum in panem: Johannes tamen cap. 19, 29. non frustra impletam fuisse Scripturam memorat, ubi milites ace- tum Christo propinarunt in cruce: quia visibili figno repræsentari in Christo oportuit, quam reprobi cru- delitatem exercent in ejus membra, ficuti Pfalm. 22. v. 19. diximus, quum partitio vestium Christi facta fuit inter milites, non intempestive citari versum il- lum: partiti sunt inter se vestes meas, & super ve- stitum meum jecerunt sortem. Licet David figurate intelligat, se fuisse spoliatum, suasque fortunas instar prædæ fuisse direptas: Tenendus tamen GENUI- MUS est sensus, Sancto Prophetæ nihil relaxationis fuisse datum: quemadmodum si homo misere alioqui afflictus, cibum quoque & potum amarulentia cor- ruptum reperiat. Hæc Calvinus; e corruptela unius loci alterius similem παρεκλότηζα probans. Sed uti Psalm. 22. depravatio Calvini abunde profligata, ita hic nulla causa est, cur a literali sensu discedatur, & metaphorica locutio fingatur, nisi præconcepta opinio, quod hic de Davide ipso sermo sit: causa autem gravissima est, cur literalis sensus retinen- dus, quia juxta literam id ita impletum est, prouti a Davide fuit prædictum, deque eo disertissime testatur idem Spiritus, qui olim per Davidem de eo vaticinatus est, optimus verborum suorum In- terpres. Non enim ut repræsentaretur crudelitas, quæ in pios, membra Christi, exerceri solet, sed ut ea quæ de Christo prædicta fuerunt a Davide, in ipso etiam implerentur, potationem illam fa- ctam testatur Joh. 19, 28. Postea videns Jesus, quia OMNIA CONSUMMATA sunt, ut CON- SUMMARETUR Scriptura, dixit, sitio: Vas ergo erat positum aceto plenum: Illi autem spongiam plenam aceto hyssopo circumponentes, obtulerunt ori ejus. Cum ergo accepiffet Jesus acetum, dixit, CON- SUMMATUM EST. Hoc ergo restabat con- summandum, vel implendum, ex his quæ prædi- xerat Spiritus Sanctus, ut potaretur, juxta vati- cinium Davidis, aceto: quod proinde sic etiam impletum fuit, cum exclamaret Christus, sitio. Quomodo evidentior dari posset interpretatio, qua displodantur in aerem quæcunque de figurata loquutione commentus est Calvinus? Et adhuc nugatur ille, GENUINUM ESSE SENSUM, quod Davidi nihil relaxationis fuerit datum, quem- admodum si homo miser potaretur aceto & felle, ut- ut tam luculenter S. S. testetur, non esse illa aliter, quam prout sonant, sensu literali, intelligenda, eoque pacto impleta esse; neque de Davide, sed de Messia hæc Scripturam prædixisse, & in Messia etiam impletam eadem esse: Unde agnovit Gro- tius Annot. ad Matth. 27, 34. oblatione potus istius Christo facta verba Davidis κατὰ λέξιν simul & κατὰ διάνοιαν in Christo impleta esse, afferens.

(11) Imprecatio Judæis & Judæ proditori facta: cujus utriusque itidem habemus interpretem S. S. Ejus quæ Judæis facta Roman. 1. v. 10. Dedit illis Deus Spiritum compunctionis, & David dicit (Pfal. 69.) fiat mensa eorum in laqueum & in captionem, & in scandalum, & in retributionem illis: Obscu- rentur eorum oculi, ne videant, & dorfum eorum semper incurva. Quæ uti de induratione & excæ- catione spirituali Apostolus intelligit, ita non in hostibus Davidis, sed demum in Christi hostibus, Judæis, & quidem in gente ista universa impleta sunt. Altera autem imprecatio proditori Christi fa- cta peculiariter v. 26. habetur. Nuspiam certe Achitopheli hæc dicta, neque ullum ejus indicium hic occurrit: ac ne Judæis quidem tale quid in mentem venire potuit. In Juda autem impletam eam esse Spiritus Sanctus aperte testatur Act. 1, 20.

(12) Celebratio nominis divini verf. 31. quam in

Ecclesia N. T. futuram circumstantiæ textus do- cent: Quia posthabitis sacrificiis, non vero cum victimis instituenda v. 23. & ad laudem invitantur cœli & terra universa, mare & omnia reptilia in eis: & causa redditur, salvatio Sionis, & ædificatio civi- tatum Juda, quæ non conveniunt Davidis tempo- ri, unde Judæi hæc ad tempora post captivitatem Babylonicam trahunt: Sed hic de spirituali Zion & Juda sermo est Ef. 2, 6. Ebr. 12, 22. (non terrena Judæa, utpote cui desolatio supra est prædicta va- stissima v. 26.) ut habitent in ea pii, & hæreditario jure possideant terram sanctam suam, Ecclesiam: Ideo additur, semen servorum ejus (Dei) possidebunt eam, hoc est, qui Patribus fidelibus in vera fide successerint. Adde, quod hic justis salus æterna promittatur, per inscriptionem in librum vitæ; & læ- titiam in vita futura v. 33. videant pauperes & læten- tur, quærite Deum, & vivet anima vestra. Unde Judæi etiam ipsi vaticinium hoc ad Messiæ tempora referunt. R. Aben-Ezra Edit. Basileens. ad vers. 31. Laudabo Deum cum cantico: Post reditum in diebus Christi. Quo facit quod Galatinus lib. 4. de arcan. Cath. verit. c. 23. e Mose Ægyptio adducit, quod Jesus Nazarenus Messias visus interfectus fuerit in domo judicii, eaque causa extiterit, ut Israel gladio destrueretur (quod hic prædictum, interprete Apo- stolo Roman. 11, 9.) & ex libro Ima recenset, sanctuarium secundum destructum fuisse propter ODIUM GRATIS, illudque adeo grave esse, ut pe- jus habeatur idolatria. Conf. v. 12. & Joh. 15, 25. Explicationem integram Psalmi apud Bugenha- gium, D. Gesnerum & D. Tarnovium in Psalm. Pas- sional. invenies. Reprobata jam est in Theodoro Mopsvestano Grotii, negantis Psalmum quoad li- teram de Christo agere, sententia, in Synodo V. Oecumenica. vid. Thomas in Procem. & Baronius Annalium Tom. 7. ad Ann. Christi 533.

## 70:1 Argument
PSALM LXX. The confusion of enemies, the exultation of those who love Jesus.

IN REMEMBRANCE THAT THE LORD SAVED HIM] The LXX added this, 'that the Lord saved him,' for the sake of interpretation. But the things that are in this Psalm are the same as the latter part of Psalm 40. Both this and the following Psalm represent the evils which Absalom stirred up. But it seems that those who were led away into Babylon with King Jehoiachin also used the following Psalm, 2 Kings 24, 12, which its Greek and Latin inscription indicates, which is missing in the Hebrew.

This inscription is referred to among dreams by Folengius. And Bellarmine twists himself in his excuse for it, acknowledging that most interpreters refer Psalm 71 to those things which David suffered in his old age from Absalom. To B. Luther, Gesner, Cramer, and Cocceius, it is a general prayer of the Church, which also has its own old age.

Latin:

PSALM. LXX. Confusio inimicorum, exultatio Jesum aman- tium.

IN REMEMORATIONEM QVOD SALVUM FE- CERIT EUM DOMINUS] Hæc quod salvum fecerit eum Dominus, interpretamenti causa addidere LXX. Sunt au- tem quæ in hoc Psalmo sunt, eadem cum postremis Psalmi 40. Et hic, & qui sequitur Psalmus repræsentat mala quæ Absalo- mus excitavit. Videntur autem Psalmum sequentem usur- passe & illi, qui cum rege Joachimo in Babylonem abducti sunt 2. Reg. 24, 12. quod indicat Græca & Latina ejus inscri- ptio, quæ in Hebræo deest.

INscriptio hæc a Folengio inter somnia refer- tur. Et torquet sese Bellarmin. in ejus excusatio- ne, agnoscens Interpp. plerosque Psalm. 71. re- ferre ad ea, quæ David in Senectute ab Absalom passus est. B. Luthero, Gesnero, Cramero, Coccejo est oratio generalis Ecclesiæ, quæ etiam suam habet senectutem.

## 71:1 Argument
PSALM LXXI. Confidence not put to shame. The enemies cursed. The lips of the faithful joyful.

Verse 1. IN THEE O LORD HAVE I HOPED. We have already brought forward diverse opinions concerning the argument. However, I do not see why we should not leave this prayer to David, along with most translators, since he speaks of himself in the singular. Even though every one of the faithful can apply it to himself.

Latin:

PSALM. LXXI. Fiducia non confusa. Hostes maledicti. Labia fidelium læta.

Vers. 1. IN TE DOMINE SPERAVI. DE argumento jam adduximus sententias di- versas. Non video autem cur non Davidi, cum translatoribus plerisque hanc precationem relinquere debeamus, quum in singulari de se lo- quatur. Etsi eum fidelium quisque sibi applicare possit.

## 71:5
Verse 5. FOR THOU ART MY PATIENCE O LORD) LXX. ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὑπομονή με κύριε, that is, my hope. But hope and ὑπομονή (patience) are very closely joined, as in Romans 5, v. 4.

Latin:

Vers. 5. QVONIAM TU ES PATIENTIA MEA DO- MINE) LXX. ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὑπομονή με κύριε, id est, spes mea. Sunt autem valde conjuncta spes & ὑπομονή, ut Rom. 5. v. 4.

## 71:15
Verse 15. MY MOUTH SHALL ANNOUNCE THY JUSTICE: ALL THE DAY THY SALVATION, FOR

I HAVE NOT KNOWN LITERATURE) Better; although I have not known the number (namely of thy benefits): so that the sense becomes the same as 40, 6. Symmachus here; οὐ γὰρ οἶδα ἐξαριθμήσασθαι. The Greeks took ספרות for the art of numbering which merchants use. And so they translated it as 'business,' and from there the Roman Psalter 'negotiations.' Others 'grammar.' Mention of both Greek versions is found in Augustine.

If this version is true, the Psalmist must have been illiterate. Whence some have gone so far as to pronounce that David did not know literature, because he was a shepherd of sheep, which Bellarmine himself refutes in this place. The Cardinal therefore seeks another gloss, but a very inept one, 'I have not known literature,' that is, I have not known the wisdom of this world, I do not trust in human counsels, I do not approve the cunning and prudence of the age, but I will enter into the powers of the Lord, that is, I will adhere to the omnipotence of God. But it is as different as heaven and earth to be ἀγράμματον (illiterate), not to have known literature, and not to approve the prudence of the age.
