Ps. 89, teach us most clearly to distinguish between the eternal kingdom of God, in which is the grace of God, and the king of the seed of David, expected by all the saints, and the external, worldly, shadowy kingdom given to the sons of David, while they defer to Calvin, who also explains all the most eminent things in this Psalm concerning David, insofar as he sustained the person of Christ, in which manner he wishes the same to be called the firstborn, which honor, in his judgment, is more excellent than all human dignity as well as angelic. For in spirit he shows that this had fallen even long before the revelation of the Messiah: and thus he dictates prayers to the pious established in that quality of time, that they might pray to hasten the mission of Christ the true King with true or full-meaning grace: That is known from the entire argument of the Psalm: concerning grace and truth: concerning the eternal kingdom promised to the seed of David, which is recognized as the kingdom of God at v. 20, concerning the promise at v. 39, concerning the prostration of the earthly throne at v. 47, a prayer for the coming of the Messiah and the true kingdom of God from there to the end.

Latin:

PSALMUS LXXXIX. Messiæ regnum, ejusque desiderium.

ETHAN) Videtur hic Ethan fuisse tempore μετοικεσίας. Vers. 28. ET EGO PRIMOGENITVM PONAM EVM) Nempe inter Reges, quod clarius eloquantur verba sequen- tia: Excelsum præ regibus terræ. Vers. 32. SI JVSTICIAS MEAS PROPHANAVERINT, ET MANDATA MEA NON CVSTODIVERINT, VI- SITABO IN VIRGA INIQVITATES EORVM ET IN VERBERIBVS PECCATA EORVM) Repetit Poëta ea, quæ Deus de Salomone ejusque posteris dixerat, 2. Sam. 7, 14. ubi dicta vide.

FAlso ibi intellexit Grotius Salomonem: Ora- culum enim de Christo Domino nostro loqui- tur: deque eo etiam præsens Psalmus agit. Nam hic illud Oraculum respici indubium est. De gratia futura canit Ethan, quem tempore τῆς με]οικεσίας vixisse censet Grotius: Quomodo ergo de Salomo- ne hic vaticinaretur? Ista utique v. 28. Ego illum pri- mogenitum ponam, Salomoni, qui jam longe ante fa- tis functus erat, non conveniunt? Ethanem hunc fuisse ex illis quatuor, quibus ob sapientiæ præstan- tiam confertur Salomo 1. Reg. 4, 31. plerique putant, quod vero Calvino non videtur quadrare in ejus ætatem, nisi forte Salomoni superstes tristem & fu- nestam, quæ tunc accidit, dissipationem, quæ præ- ludium fuerit ruinæ, defleat. Sed annon Prophetæ etiam futuras calamitates ex revelatione Spir. S. prospiciunt? Secutus autem Philonem videtur Gro- tius, qui libr. II. Epitom. Histor. refert eum ad tem- pora Jechoniæ in carcerem conjecti, de quo vid. B. Gesnerus in h. Ps. Recte Junio-Tremell. notæ ad v. 39. Hic Psalmus in monumentum datus est Ecclesiæ prophetico spiritu, ut suo tempore caneretur Deo, cu- jusmodi fuit tempus deportationis Babylonicæ. Propo- sitio Psalmi v. 2, habetur, quæ est celebrare חסדי יהוה beneficia Domini, & אמונת fidem ejus vel

1. benignitatem in promittendo, & veritatem implen- do, respiciens promissionem illam κατ' ἀν]ονομα- σίαν dictam, in qua maxime benignitas Dei elucet, de Messia, ceu omnium promissionum basi 2. Cor. 1, 16. Act. 4, 12.

2. Tum vero de gratia æterna exoritu- ra canit, quam æternum etiam decantare vult. Non ergo temporalis gratia, quæ in hoc seculo obtigit Salomoni, sed gratia Spiritualis, quæ fidelibus in Christo promissa est, intelligitur, qua ipsi in æter- num fruentur, & quam in æternum celebrabunt. Per ipsum enim gratia & veritas facta Joh. 1, 16.

3. Tertio repetitur hic promissio 2. Sam. 7, 12. seqq. facta de semine æterno, & throno in æternum firman- do, quæ non in Salomone impleta est, ejusque posteris, sed in Christo ac de Christo explicatur Ps. 132, 11. Act. 2, 30. Pepigi fœdus SANCTO MEO (Christo Es. 42, 1.) juravi David servo meo, de fœdere illo in Messia Davidem, ex quo ipse oriun- dus erit, juramento confirmavi 2. Sam. 7, 2. 23, 1. Per Electum enim deinde intelligit Christum v. 20. quem etiam a Davide servo ibi distinguit. Sic illa optime sibi respondent: USQUE IN ÆTER- NUM præparabo SEMEN tuum (tibi Electo meo) & ædificabo sedem TUAM de generatione in generationem: hæc non in Davide, sed Christo impleta, v. 30. 37.

Atque hæc quarto sunt fidelia illa Davidis, vel Davidi facta promissa, quæ etiam ab Esaia statumi- nantur c. 55, 3. ac de Christo Domino nostro expli- cantur Act. 13, 34. Hoc quinto est, ob quod cœli, id est, exercicus cœlestes, Angeli admirandam Dei gra- tiam & veritatem celebrant, atq; annuntiant; Quod tempore nativitatis Christi factum. Idcirco sexto celebratur hîc brachium & manus, atŕ, dextra Dei, cujus potentia in liberatione generis humani ma- xime eluxit, nec non justitia & judicium, misericor- dia & veritas Dei v. 14. 15. quæ præprimis etiam conspicua sunt in hoc opere, teste B. virgine Luc. 1, 50. ut & S. Zacharia v. 69. seqq. Septimo celebratur juxta phrasin Osiandri, quæ hîc non incommoda est, Christi eminentia: Quis in nubibus æquabitur Domino? (Christo nostro) qui tam mirando mo- do restituet genus humanum, quod a nullo Ange- lo fieri potuit. Deus potens est in Concilio Sanctorum magno: (in Ecclesia, quæ non e Judæis tantum, sed & gentibus constabit, admirandam potentiam exer- cet) & terribilis est super omnes, qui sunt in circui- tu ejus (præbet se terribilem hostibus Ecclesiæ, qui plerumque in circuitu ejus habitant) Tu dominaris superbiæ maris, tumultum fluctuum ejus mitigas (mundo maxime tumultuante, mox omnia tran- quilla reddere potest Dominus,) Tu conteris quasi interfectum superbum, in brachio virtutis tuæ disper- sisti inimicos tuos (Ecclesiæ hostes) Tui sunt cœli, & tua terra (omnia sunt in tua potestate, ut statuas de iis, quicquid libuerit) Aquilonem & mare (me- ridiem) tu creasti, Thabor (versus occasum) & Her- mon (versus ortum) in nomine tuo exultabunt (Re- gnum Christi Filii tui, invitis omnibus hostibus, ad quatuor plagas mundi propagabitur. Montium Thabor & Hermon cur peculiariter hic mentio fiat, hanc rationem reddit B. Bugenhagius Noster: quod respexerit Spiritus S. proprie ad istos montes, qui sunt in Galilæa, ut etiam certum locum designaret gratiæ mundo in Christo apparituræ. In illis enim locis Chri- stus prædicavit, miracula fecit, multitudinem homi- num etiam cibo corporali pavit, & præterea in Tha- bor in medio Galilææ facta fuisse dicitur transfigura- tio Domini Matth. 17. &c.) Tuum brachium cum potentia, Brachium, manus & dextra Domini Mes- sias Ps. 118. Octavo fundamentum omnis Spiritua- lis gaudii populi Dei imo beatitudinis hîc consti- tuitur; qui ideo in nomine Dei lætatur, & in justi- tia Dei gloriatur: in lumine facies Dei ambulat con- fidenter. Quæ vero est beatitudo ac salus nostra, ni- si in lumine faciei, vel gratiæ Dei illucescente nobis in Christo Jesu Act. 4, 12. quæ causa, quod funda- mentum omnis nostri gaudii, & exultationis, nisi Christus Jesus? Qui uti est Jehova justitia nostra Jer. 23, 6. ita in ipso unice justitiam & fortitudinem habent fideles, qui credunt in ipsum. Es. 45, 26. In beneplacito tuo, ait hic Psaltes, exaltabitur cornu nostrum. Quod est cornu salutis erectum in domo Davidis Luc. 1, 67. Hæc enim εὐδοκία fuit, ut per Christum reconciliaret omnia Col. 1, 20. Quod ad Deum patrem ceu fontem omnis gratiæ & salutis refertur, cujus gratioso beneplacito erectum & exaltatum nobis est cornu salutis, a quo est clypeus noster, & Rex noster, in quo confidimus, Christus Jesus, qui & cornu Davidis Ps. 132, 17. & Clypeus fidelium Gen. 15, 1. & Rex noster a Deo nobis con- stitutus est Ps. 2, 6. Alii, atque nos antehac ita: Quia Dominus est clypeus noster & Sanctus in Israel Rex noster v. 19. Quæ ad Deum patrem de alia per- sona divina dicta, de Filio Dei intelligenda sunt. Compellat enim Deum Patrem v. 17. Gloria vir- tutis eorum, tum & in beneplacito tuo exaltabitur cornu nostrum. Et iterum v. 19. immediate subjun- cto: Tunc locutus es in visione Sanctis tuis. Sed quum in Ebræo non casus rectus, sed obliquus habeatur, Domini vel Domino, est clypeus noster, & sancti vel sancto Israelis (est) Rex noster, sensus jam traditus præferendus. Qui ideo a B. Bugenhagio nostro e translatione Felicis observatus; de qua etiam translatione ipse in Præfat. ad Frideric. Du- cem Elect. Saxon. sententiam Psalmorum ex He- bræo diximus secundum Felicis Hebræi translatio- nem, qua hodie NVLLA EST MELIOR. Neces- sarium enim erat, ut ad Hebræum respiceremus, ne interpretaremur, quod Propheta Hebræus non dixisset. Sic autem hoc loco reddidit: Quia a Domino scu- tum nostrum, & a Sancto Israel Rex noster, id est Messias a Deo, qui sanctificat Israelem, datur nobis scutum, redemtio, justitia, sanctificatio. Sequitur, tunc locutus es in visione sanctis tuis, h. e. Natha- ni & Davidi. Nam primum Nathani & per eum Davidi loquutus hæc deinde est Dominus. Unde liquet Psalmum hunc non Davidi, sed alii, nempe, ut habet inscriptio, Ethani Esrahitæ adscribendum esse.

Nono heros ille, quem Deus promiserat 2. Sam. 7. populi Sospitatorem, electus e populo, servus David, neutiquam intelligi potest de Salomone, quo de Psalmum interpretatur Grotius, nec de Da- vide; huic enim non conveniunt quæ sequuntur; sed Christus ita indigitatur Es. 9, 6. c. 42, 1. quem etiam per vocem David nonnulli intelligunt, quia apud Prophetas passim David vocatur, utpote Jer. 30, 9. Ez. 34, 23. 24. & 37, 24. 25. Sed quum hæc S. Apostolus de Davide filio Jesse interpretatus sit Act. 13, 22. credendum est Sp. S. voluisse & Christi HEROIS illius & ELECTI DOMINI e populo Israelitico secundum carnem exhibendi, & servi sui Davidis, ex cujus lumbis prodire & in cujus throno sedere HEROS ille debuit, quique insignis ejus typus fuit, mentionem facere, sed postea misso Davide, de Christo Heroe illo carmen suum pertexere. Neque enim possunt verba sequentia textus partim de Davide, partim de Christo explica- ri cum Pontificiis. Cui expositioni repugnat conti- nuatio verborum: Omnia enim verba ita contexta sunt, & continuata, ut ad eundem pertineant, fatente hic Bellarmino. Quod argumentum ipsi etiam Bel- larmino, & qui cum eo faciunt, opponendum est: nam exponit idem antecedentia de Davide, at con- sequentia agnoscit de Christo intelligenda esse, ad v. 27. ita annotans: Hic vero apertissime de Christo Propheta loquitur: atque ita etiam in aliis. Ineptus autem est, dum ait Cardinalis, OMNIA exponen- da esse ad literam de Davide, sed implenda MA- GNA EX PARTE per Christum: Qua enim parte per Christum unice implentur, ea certe parte de Davide explicari non possunt, nec debent: ideoque falsum est, OMNIA de Davide esse exponenda. Porro quod ille HEROS, de quo pergit vaticina- ri Sp. S. non David, sed Christus noster sit unctus oleo lætitiæ præ consortibus Ps. 45, 8. docet tum suc- cessus herois istius adversus hostes; nihil perficiet inimicus in eo, & concidam a facie ipsius inimicos ejus, quæ de Christo ex omni parte vera sunt, non item de Davide, uti fatetur ipse Bellarminus: utcunque de Davide, inquit, exponi possint, tamen longe verius exponuntur de Christo. Tum potestas Christi & am- plitudo dominii ejus v. 24. Et veritas mea & miseri- cordia mea cum ipso, & in nomine meo exaltabitur cornu, vel potestas ejus, quæ in Davide vix adum- brata in Christo perfectissime impleta agnoscit Bel- larminus. Et ponam in mari manum ejus, & in flu- minibus dextram ejus. Ab hoc loco, inquit, conve- niunt fere omnes, Augustinus, Hieronymus, Theodo- retus, & multi recentiorum, non posse exponi Psal- mum NISI DE CHRISTO: Non enim David ha- buit potestatem in mari, sed in terra tantum, eaque satis angusta. Terra enim promissionis extendebatur usque ad mare Palæstinæ, & usque ad flumen Euphra- ten, & ultra. De hoc autem nostro Rege dicitur: po- nam in mari manum ejus, id est, dabo ei potesta- tem etiam in ipso mari, & in omnibus fluminibus, ac per hoc in omni orbe terrarum: mare siquidem est in finibus terræ, circumiens totam terram, flumina autem sunt in medio terræ. Itaque per mare & flumina intelliguntur omnia, fines, & meditullium; quod aliis verbis dictum est in Pf. 72. dominabitur a mari usque ad mare, i. e. ab uno extremo ad aliud. Manum & dextram notare potentiam & dominium e Scriptu- ris notissimum est Ex. 14, ult. c. 15, 6. Num. 11, 23. Pf. 18, 36. Pf. 63, 9. Pf. 77, 11. Pf. 108, 7. Pf. 139, 5. 10. Dominium ergo Messiæ ultra mare & universa orbis terrarum flumina porrigere sese debet, quod de Davide, aut Salomone intelligi non potest, cujus imperio nunquam paruere maris insulæ: Sed unice de regno Christi accipiendum est, uti locus paralle- lus Pf. 72, 8. luculenter docet.

Decimo cumprimis nuncupatio Patris obser- vanda, de qua v. 27. Ipse vocabit me: Pater meus es tu. Non enim causa ulla est, cur a proprietate nuncupa- tionis istius discedamus, quæ in Scriptura temere deferenda nunquam est. Et exponit id ipse Apo- stolus Ebr. 1, 5. de Patre proprie ita dicto, quod nempe Deum Patrem ipse vocet, non ut Angeli, sed ut is qui solus genitus est e substantia Patris, & ἀπαύγασμα est gloriæ, & χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως ipfius: cui soli dictum Psalm. 2, 7. Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te, & 2. Sam. 7, 14. Ego ero ipsi in Pa- trem, & ipse erit mihi in Filium. Nam uti hic Pfal- mus locum Samuelis allegatum respicit, sic inter- pretatur eundem Epistola ad Ebræos, ut simul huic nostro textui lucem fœnoretur, quod non de Da- vide, aut Salomone, sed Messia accipi debeat. Quod affirmat etiam primogeniti appellatio v. 28. Etiam ego primigenitum constituam eum, excelsum supra Reges terræ. Ubi observandum discrimen na- turarum in Christo: Nam ut præcedenti commate illud attendendum venit: Ipse vocabit me: Pater meus es tu: Deus meus, & fortitudo salutis meæ. Pater enim est, ratione æternæ generationis, Filii: Deus ejus & fortitudo salutis ejus est, ratione humanæ na- turæ: Ita in hoc commate e correlatorum natura prior appellatio, Et ego primogenitum constituam eum, divinam naturam concernit; secundum quam ipse πρωτότοκος πάσης κτίσεως primogenitus omnis creaturæ est Col. 1, 15. Altera vero, excelsum supra Reges terræ ad humanam naturam pertinet, secun- dum quam ipse supra omnia exaltatus est. Nec ob- stat, quod primogenitus constituendus dicatur: quia constitutio illa vel ratio Φανερώσεως intelligi potest, siquidem tum res dicantur fieri, cum decla- rantur, vel si ὄντως constitui dicatur, respectus ha- beatur ad incarnationem: qua Sanctum, quod ex Maria natum est, Filius Dei vocatum est Luc. 1, 37. Primogenitus quidem ab æterno in se fuit, sed cum caro factus est primogenitus Dei Filius constitu- tus est, & evasit primogenitus ille Mariæ Filius. Conferri hic potest locus illustris Ebr. 1, 6. ubi πρω- τοτόκος nomen de Christo ob æternam generatio- nem a Patre adhibetur. Appellatio enim illa non ali- unde, quam ex hoc Psalmi Oraculo videtur desum- ta, e Græca nempe versione. Syrus & Arabs itidem retinent vocem בבר. Hic apertissime de Christo Pro- phetam loqui, agnoscit Bellarm. in comm. ad h. l. Psalm. fateturque de Davide ac Salomone dici nullo modo posse Epitheton illud, Excelsus præ Regibus terræ: utpote qui non solum non fuerunt altissimi abfolute; sed inferiores etiam multis Regibus ter- ræ, ac præcipue Regibus Assyriorum, qui eo tem- pore Monarchiam tenebant.

Undecimo observanda etiam Regni Herois hujus æternitas: de qua v. 28. ita Psaltes: In æternum illi servabo misericordiam meam, & testamentum meum fidele ipsi. Pactum enim hoc erat de Regno æterno 2. Sam. 7. quod etiam ipsi sine fine servandum hic promittitur: de quo autem id intelligi potest, nisi de eo, quem sessurum super thronum Davidis, & cu- jus regnum nullum habiturum finem, Gabriel an- nuntiavit Luc. 1. Quod etiam explicatur v. 29. seqq. Et ponam in seculum seculi semen ejus, & thronum ejus, sicut dies cæli. Quod semen Augustinus recte de filiis spiritualibus Messiæ interpretatur: qui ipsi ge- nerantur per verbum Evangelii: ut perpetuitas re- gni, ac seminis spiritualis Messiæ continua ac peren- nis propagatio, ejusdemque æterna beatitudo, ac throni regalis ejusdem æternitas designetur. Quan- quam enim immorigeri Filii Messiæ virgis castigan- di sint, a Messia tamen non tollenda gratia, neque veritas promissionis divinæ ideo periclitabitur: aut fœdus Dei irritum reddetur, quod mediante jureju- rando sanciverat: Non evertetur propterea regnum Christi, non abjicietur aut delebitur Ecclesia, sicut alia regna propter scelera exstirpantur: quin electi etiam omnes, utut graviter peccarint, non tamen sic abjicientur, ut in peccatis æternum pereant: Atque ita redit iterum Hieropsaltes ad Davidem & juramentum ei præstitum: Semel juravi in Sancto meo, vel per sanctum meum, per sanctitatem meam (Chaldæus in sancto nomine meo) si Davidi men- tiar, semen ejus in æternum manebit, & thronus ejus, sicut Sol, in conspectu meo, & sicut Luna perfecta in æternum, & testis in cælo fidelis. Pronomen EJUS nonnulli ad Davidem referunt: cui facta promissio. Sed referri commodissime potest ad Messiam, quia de eodem subjecto per totum Psalmum sermo est, & Messiæ semen spirituale æternum & thronus perpetuus eidem promissus est; etsi ad Davidem promissio illa relata sit, facta tamen est non de Da- vide, sed de Messia; nec de Davidis, sed de Messiæ semine luculenta esse videtur e versu 29. prorsus simili: Ponam in seculum seculi semen ejus, & thro- num ejus sicut dies cæli: nec non e vers. 30. ubi se- men illud Messiæ de filiis ejus explicatur. Si tamen quis omnino per pronomen EJUS v. 35. Davidem intelligendum esse contendat, semen Davidis in æter- num manebit, accipiendum tum id erit μοναδι- κῶς de Messia, Davidis semine: cujus æternus thro- nus seqq. vers. describitur: Nisi forte Messiæ se- men etiam aliquo respectu Davidis semen dicatur, quemadmodum filii Abrahæ Patris credentium, censentur credentes, (qui semen Messiæ dicuntur) ut e vers. 5. apparet. Aut dicendum cum D. Luc. Osiandro, per Davidem hic Christum intelligi. Non mentiar David, Filio meo Jesu Christo: Juravit enim Dominus Deus Pater Filio suo Christo & non pœnitebit eum Ps. 110, 4. De filiis & nepotibus Da- vidis id intelligi non posse manifestum est. Sed prior explicatio simplicior est, non enim de jura- mento de Christo, Sacerdotii ejus æterni causa fa- cto, sed de jurejurando, quo mediante fœdus Da- vidi confirmavit, sermo est, quod ideo vere ἀμετα- μέλητον: de quo sub initium canere cœpit: Juravi Davidi servo meo &c. vers. 5.

Atque hæc de parte prima Psalmi Prophetica: quam totam concernere Messiam ejusque regnum nunc in aprico esse arbitramur. In altera parte que- rela texitur de miserabili & calamitoso statu regni Judaici, ut ejusdem Deus, Pater omnis misericor- diæ gratiosissime misereatur, tandemque Messiam

Redemtorem mittat, qui ab omnibus malis genus humanum liberet, regnumque suum spirituale in mundo erigat. Tu vero repulisti & despexisti (nos, vel populum tuum) distulisti Christum tuum. Quod de missione Domini nostri Jesu Christi dilata Augu- stinus intelligit, alii de Rege Judæ, Jechonia, & Sede- chia, qui ex Ebræo cum S. Hieronymo reddunt, iratus es adversus unctum tuum. Osiander in para- phrasi vaticinando conqueri Psalten de Anti-Christo existimat, quod hoc regnum Christi terribiliter per eundem ac similes hostes divexetur, dilaceretur, ac tantum non evertatur, ita ut coram humana ra- tione appareat, Deum omnium suarum promissio- num (de Regni Christi durabilitate) oblitum, tandem- que gratiarum actione Psalmum concludere, ut ostendat regnum Christi nihilominus contra omnes inferorum portas invictum fore. Querela ista pro- lixe continuatur, tum vero precatio subjungitur pro acceleratione Messiæ, ut impleatur promissio ju- rata Dei, uti Bellarm. explicat, Usquequo Domine avertes faciem tuam, vel absconderis in finem, vel ad perniciem usque exardescet sicut ignis ira tua. Memen- to quod meum (& aliorum hominum) sit tempus, (quam brevi tempore vivat homo in his terris) quare frustra creasses filios hominum. (Si enim Chri- stum tuum non miseris, vel Ecclesiæ tuæ confer- vandæ omnem curam adjeceris, annon videberis frustra creasse humanum genus? Ita non solum pa- raphrasis Latina Dn. Luc. Osiandri, ac Vinariensis Germanica, sed etiam alii Interpp. veteres & recen- tiores. August. l. 17. de C. D. c. 11. ac plerique Ponti- ficii. Bellarminus, Existimo, inquit, Prophetam, qui spiritualis erat, ex brevitate vitæ humanæ & ca- ducitate rerum humanarum, exarsisse in desiderium vitæ futuræ terræ in cælis, ac Deum precari voluisse, ut Messiam cito mitteret Patrem futurum seculi, qui aperiret credentibus regna cælorum. Nisi enim saltem pars aliqua generis humani ad vitam illam æternam, & beatam per Christum perveniret, vere in vanum condidisse videretur Deus omnes filios hominum.) Quis enim est homo, qui vivet, & non videbit mor- tem, eruet animam suam de manu inferi. Ubi mise- ricordiæ tuæ antiquæ, Domine, quas jurasti David in veritate tua. (Quæ jurata promissio quia de Messia facta erat, manifestum iterum est, in eodem de Messia argumento perseverare Psalten (Memor esto Domine opprobrii servorum tuorum, quod con- tinui (seu portavi hactenus) in sinu meo (verba sunt querulantis Ecclesiæ,) quod exprobraverunt inimici tui, Domine, quod nimirum exprobraverunt vestigia Christi tui (exibilant & subsannant progressum re- gni Christi, & adventus ejusdem dilati, vel expro- braverunt tarditatem vestigiorum Messiæ, uti Chal- dæus interpretatur.) Quum autem prævideat Pro- pheta subsequuturum suo tempore promissionis complementum per adventum Messiæ, regnique ejusdem propagationem, exclamat in Spiritu: Be- nedictus sit Dominus! Fiat; Fiat! Sic ergo tota Psal- mi structura Christum, ejusque regnum exhibet, quod e laudata paraphrasi Osiandri rectius pate- scet, si ea pie & attente considerata fuerit, quæ in plerisque in hujus Psalmi explicatione (quod col- latio cum hisce nostris meditationibus patefaciet,) commoda est, & ob retentum unicum literalem sensum, hic & in aliis Psalmis Propheticis præfe- renda paraphrasi Vinariensium, etsi de cætero hæc quoque laudem suam mereatur.

Adde his jam postremo Judæorum confessionem, qui agnoscere ipsi coguntur, promissionem hanc de Messia intelligendam esse. Primogenitum altis- simum Regum terræ de Messia interpretatur R. Na- than in Midrasch super Ex. 13, 2. Et quæ v. 37.

38. habentur, thronus ejus sicut Sol coram me, &c. de Messia explicantur in Bereschith Ketanna super cap. 49, 8. R. Aben - Ezra in hunc Psalmum: Est de foedere Dei cum Davide, & de adventu Messiae, cui credit Psalmista. Et ad v. 40. Irritum fecisti foedus: Loquitur in persona adversariorum, qui deridebant adventum Messiae. Ad v. ultimum: Benedictus sit Dominus pro lumine adventus Messiae. R. Anony- mus apud Genebrard. hic ad v. 51. exprobrant ve- stigia, sive egressus Christi tui, dicunt eum tardigra- dum vel loripedem & claudum &c. Et potuisset de toto hoc Psalmo erudiri Grotius ab iis, quos Prae- ceptores sibi elegerat in Theologia, Jesuitas indi- gito, a Bellarmino nempe, Tirino, & Menochio, quem aestimat. Hi enim, ut alios nunc taceam, agnoscunt continere hunc Psalmum desiderium po- puli Dei in captivitate positi, ut cito Christus tanto ante promissus adveniat. Calvinum de Davide etiam eminentissima quaeque in hoc Psalmo expli- cantem, quatenus nempe is Christi personam susti- nuit, quo pacto eundem primogenitum dici vult, qui honor ipsius judicio tam omni humana digni- tate, quam angelica excellentior est, deferunt hic alii in ejus Schola, imprimis Joh. Coccejus in ultimis Mosis §. 990. Ps. 89. nos clarissime docet distinguere inter regnum Dei aeternum, in quo est gratia Dei, & rex de semine Davidis, expectatus omnibus sanctis, & regnum externum mundanum umbratile filiis Davi- dis datum. Hoc enim in spiritu ostendit cecidisse etiam longe ante revelationem Messiae: atque ita preces piis in ea qualitate temporis constitutis dictat, ut orent, ac- celerare missionem Christi veri Regis cum vera sive pleni significatus gratia: Id ex argumento Psalmi in- tegro cognoscitur: de gratia & veritate: De regno aeterno semini Davidis promisso, quod regnum Dei re- cognoscitur ad v. 20. de promissione ad v. 39. de pro- stratuone solii terreni ad v. 47. oratio pro adventu Messiae & veri regni Dei inde ad finem.

## 89:38
Vers. 39. THOU HAST DELAYED THY CHRIST) In Hebrew: Thou art angry with thine anointed: namely Zedekiah, who, blinded in his eyes, was led bound into Babylon.

Augustine explains it concerning our Christ: It remains entirely, O God, what thou hast promised: For thou hast not taken away thy Christ, but delayed him. Lucas Osiander translates; thou art angry with thy Christ, and thus he expounded the passage; Thou treatest thy chosen Church, which is the body of Christ, in such a way that thou seemest to utterly abhor and reject it, while thou deliverest it to be cut down by enemies: nay, thou seemest to reject Christ himself thy Son, and to hate him: since thou deliverest him to death, and indeed to the ignominious death of the cross: as he himself exclaims, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? For it can be said that God seems to have so repelled and rejected his people, as if he were angry with his Christ, and is unwilling to look upon his propitiation and intercession, in which the faithful were trusting, or that God has made himself pass over Christ himself, or seems to be angry with Christ himself: because he so afflicts and punishes his people. For what happens to his Church, that happens to Christ himself by appropriation Acts 9, 5. Zech. 2, 8. But then it has already been shown, even if these things are accepted concerning Zedekiah, how the Psalmist still does not depart from his scope, which is to treat of Christ and his kingdom:

Latin:

Vers. 39. DISTVLISTI CHRISTVM TVVM) In He- braeo: Iratus es uncto tuo: nempe Sedeciae, qui oculis orba- tus, & vinctus ductus est in Babylonem.

De Christo nostro explicat Augustinus: Manet omnino, Deus, quod promisisti: Nam Christum tuum non abstulisti, sed distulisti. Lucas Osiander vertit; iratus es Christo tuo, & ita locum exposuit; Tu ele- ctam tuam Ecclesiam, quae est corpus Christi, ita tra- ctas, ut eam plane abominari & repudiare videaris, dum eam hostibus incidendam tradis: imo Christum ipsum Filium tuum reprobare videris, atque eum odif- se: quandoquidem tradis eum in mortem, & quidem in mortem ignominiosam crucis: uti exclamat ipse, Deus meus, Deus meus, quare me dereliquisti? Dici enim potest, Deum ita repulisse, ac reprobasse videri populum suum, ac si Christo suo iratus esset, ejusque propitiationem & intercessionem, in qua confi- debant fideles, respicere nolit, vel Deum transire se fe- cisse super Christum ipsum, aut ipsi Christo irasci vi- deri: quia populum suum ita affligit, ac punit. Quod enim Ecclesiae ejus accidit, id Christo ipsi ob ap- propriationem accidit Act. 9, 5. Zach. 2, 8. Tum vero ostensum jam est, etiamsi haec de Sedekia acci- piantur, quomodo adhuc Psalmista a suo scopo, qui est agere de Christo, ejusque regno haud abeat:

## 89:45
Vers. 46. THOU HAST SHORTENED THE DAYS OF HIS TIME) In Hebrew, Thou hast cut short the days of his youth: thou hast caused him to grow old before his time through the weariness of evils. And thus these things can be understood concerning the same Zedekiah. The Hebrews prefer to understand these things concerning Jehoiachin, who reigned for only three months: and had reached the kingdom as a youth, that is, of 18 years 2 Kings 25, 8.

Although this interpretation concerning Zedekiah or Jehoiachin, without prejudice to our explanation that the prophecy of this Psalm looks to Christ, can be admitted, and nothing opposes the design of the sacred singer, prophesying concerning the Kingdom of the Messiah; since in view of such great calamities as he saw, he seeks the acceleration of the coming of the Messiah: yet the paraphrase of our Osiander might not seem altogether inconvenient here: which therefore I am pleased to subjoin: Thou hast lessened or abbreviated the days of the time: In Hebrew of youth (i.e., thou dost not allow the Church of Christ to flourish for long: But it contracts old age before its time, partly from persecutions, partly from human traditions and opinions, by which its brightness grows old: and thou hast poured out) more correctly, thou hast covered him with confusion, (for Christ in his members is the mockery of the world) Selah. He interprets, as has been said, concerning the times of the New Testament and the persecutions of the Anti-Christ. Moreover, we do not deny that those things are more conveniently accepted concerning the time before the coming of Christ; since the sacred singer immediately breaks forth into a sigh for the accelerating of the same; without which, if it were to be, all the sons of men would have been created in vain, nay, all would have to perish eternally. After these hard things, says Augustine in this place, which he commemorated as having happened to that people, and to that kingdom, lest it be thought that God had there fulfilled what he had promised, and would not give another kingdom in Christ, of which kingdom there will be no end: The Prophet addresses him and says: How long, O Lord, wilt thou turn away forever? Rightly, therefore, our blessed Gesner at v. 38. And to what purpose such a prolix mention of the prophecy concerning the Christ who is to come was made, now appears from the subjoined complaint. For thus the members of the Psalm cohere: Since God promised the Messiah to the family of David and the Israelite kingdom; therefore it is necessary that some Commonwealth also be preserved among the Jews until those times, so that there may be a certain polity in which Christ may be exhibited. But now the Jewish Commonwealth is being miserably torn apart by neighboring peoples, says Ethan, and a little later will be laid waste by the Assyrians, and so will be dissipated, that it might seem to be all over with the divine promise. Therefore, O eternal God, we humbly pray that thou wouldst be pleased to restore thy Church in turn, and to mercifully preserve it until the coming of the Messiah amidst so many ruins of kingdoms and the furies of Satan. And at v. 45. Thou hast shortened the days of his youth, thou hast covered him with ignominy. Selah. Finally, this calamity is the more bitter, the more quickly it rushes upon the people of God. For if the Jewish polity had attained its proper maturity, concerning which the Patriarch Jacob and the Prophets prophesied, it would be less to be lamented that it was abolished, according to the presage of Daniel, chapter 2. But now, in the very flower of its age, and as it were in its youth, it is miserably cut down. So also our blessed Luther in his marginal gloss and his version, and with him the Weimar paraphrasts. So also, he who should have been mentioned in the first place, Theodoret on this passage: 'You have shortened the days of his time: although you promised that you would preserve his kingdom forever, yet after a short time you put an end to it. You have covered him with confusion: he has become ignominious and is filled with disgrace.' For Zedekiah, with his eyes put out, was condemned to the mill for all the remaining time. Jeconiah, moreover, also served. These things [says] Theodoret, who immediately at the threshold of the Psalm observed that the descendants of the Patriarchs, looking upon the promises made to them concerning the Messiah, and looking back at themselves having been made captives, and the royal city deserted, and the kingdom having been extinguished, wishing to recall to God's memory His promises here.

Latin:

Vers. 46. MINORASTI DIES TEMPORIS EJVS) In Hebraeo, Praecidisti dies juventutis ejus: fecisti ut ante tem- pus senesceret malorum taedio. Et sic poterunt haec intelligi de eodem Sedecia. Hebraei malunt de Joachimo haec intel- ligere, qui per tres tantum Menses regnavit: & juvenis, id est, annorum 18. ad regnum pervenerat 2. Reg. 25, 8.

Quanquam haec de Sedekia vel de Joachimo interpretatio, salva nostra explicatione, quod Pro- phetia hujus Psalmi Christum respiciat, admitti poffit, nihilque adversetur instituto Hieropsaltis, vaticinantis de Regno Messiæ; quum intuitu tan- tarum, quas vidit, calamitatum, accelerationem adventus Messiæ expetat: non omnino tamen in- commoda hic videri paraphrasis posset Osiandri nostri: quam proinde subjicere placet: Minorasti vel abbreviasti dies temporis: Hebraice juventutis (i. e. non diu florentem sinis esse Ecclesiam Chri- sti: Sed contrahit senium ante tempus, partim ex persequutionibus, partim ex humanis traditioni- bus & opinionibus, quibus nitor illius senescit: & perfudisti) rectius, operuisti eum confusione, (Chri- stus enim in membris suis est ludibrium mundi) Sela. Interpretatur ille, ut dictum, de temporibus Novi Testam. & persequutionibus Anti-Christi. Cæterum non diffitemur, quin illa commodius de tempore ante adventum Christi accipiantur; quan- doquidem in suspirium accelerandi ejusdem statim prorumpat Hieropsaltes; absque quo si foret, fru- stra omnes filii hominum creati essent, quin omni- bus æternum pereundum esset. Post hac dura,inquit Augustinus in h. l. quæ commemoravit evenisse illi populo, & illi regno, ne ibi putaretur Deus implevis- se, quod promiserat, & non daret alterum regnum in Christo, cujus regni non erit finis: Alloquitur eum Propheta & dicit: Quousque Domine averteris in fi- nem? Recte itaque B. Gesnerus noster ad v. 38. Et quorsum facta sit tam prolixa vaticinii de Christo venturo mentio, jam ex subjuncta querela apparet. Sic enim membra Psalmi cohærent: Cum Deus Da- vidis familiæ & regno Israelitico pollicitus sit Messiam; idcirco Rempublicam quoque aliquam ad ea usque tempora servari inter Judæos oportet, ut certa sit poli- tia, in qua Christus exhibeatur. Jam vero Respublica Judaica per vicinos populos, inquit Ethan, misere di- laceratur & paulo post per Assyrios vastabitur, adeo- que dissipabitur, ut actum de divina promissione vi- deri queat. Te igitur æterne Deus supplices oramus, ut Ecclesiam tuam vicissim instaurare, & ad Messiæ adventum inter tot regnorum ruinas & Satanæ fu- rores clementer conservare velis. Et ad v. 45. Abbre- viasti dies juventutis ejus, operuisti eum ignominia. Selah. Postremo tanto acerbior hæc est calamitas, quanto citius in populum Dei irruit. Nam si poli- tia Judaica justam suam maturitatem assecuta esset, de qua Patriarcha Jacobus, & Prophetæ vaticina- ti sunt, minus dolendum foret, illam aboleri, juxta Danielis cap. 2. præsagium. Jam vero in ipso flore ætatis, quasique in juventute sua misere succiditur. Sic etiam B. Lutherus noster in glossa marginali, & versione sua, & cum ipso Paraphrasta Vinarien- ses. Sic etiam, qui primo commemorandus erat lo- co, Theodoretus in h. l. Minorasti dies temporis ejus: cum in æternum promiseris te ejus regnum servatu- rum, tamen brevi post tempore ipsi finem imposuisti. Perfudisti eum confusione: ignominiosus factus est, & dedecoris repletus est. Sedecias enim erutis oculis pistrino addictus est, in omne reliquum tempus. Je- chonias autem & ipse serviit. Hæc Theodoretus, qui mox in limine Psalmi observavit, quod posteri Patriarcharum in promissiones ipsis de Messia fa- ctas intuentes, & seipsos captivos factos respicien- tes, & regiam civitatem desertam, & extinctum es- se regnum, credentes, promissa sua Deo in memo- riam hic revocare voluerint.

## 89:47
Verse 48. REMEMBER WHAT IS MY SUBSTANCE) In the Hebrew: μνήσθητι τίς ἡ ὑπόσασίς με. In the Hebrew: how short my time is.

END of Book III of the Psalms,

Latin:

Vers. 48. MEMORARE QVÆ MEA SVBSTANTIA) In He- bræo: μνήσθητι τίς ἡ ὑπόσασίς με. In Hebræo: quantilli ævi sim.

FINIS Libri III. Psalmorum,

## 90:1 Argument
BOOK FOURTH PSALM XC. The Art of Dying.

PRAYER OF MOSES THE MAN OF GOD) Not made by him, but suitable to his affairs and spirit. Τίνας ἂν λόγους εἴποι ὁ Μωσῆς. The same seems to be said of the following ten Psalms, which the Hebrews attribute to Moses.

Latin:

LIBER QVARTVS PSALMUS XC. Ars moriendi.

ORATIO MOSI HOMINIS DEI) Non ab ipso facta, sed ejus rebus animoque conveniens. Τίνας ἂν λόγους εἴποι ὁ Μωσῆς. Idem dicendum videtur de Psalmis sequentibus decem, quos Hebræi Mosi tribuunt.

## 90:2
Ver. 2. BEFORE THE MOUNTAINS WERE MADE, OR THE EARTH AND THE WORLD WERE FORMED, FROM EVERLASTING TO EVERLASTING, THOU ART GOD) That word God seems to be added from the Hebrew. For in the Greek it is: πρὸ τοῦ ὄρη γεννηθῆναι, καὶ πλασθῆναι τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν οἰκουμένην, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἰῶνος ἑως τοῦ αἰῶνος σὺ εἶ. But what follows in the Hebrew, אל, the Greek interpreters did not read with tsere, but with patach, and referred it to the following clause, verse by μὴ.

Latin:

Vers. 2. PRIVSQVAM MONTES FIERENT, AVT FORMARETVR TERRA ET ORBIS A SÆCVLO VSQVE IN SÆCVLVM, TV ES DEVS) Illud Deus ex Hebræo additum videtur. Nam in Græco est: πρὸ τοῦ ὄρη γεννηθῆναι, καὶ πλασθῆναι τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν οἰκουμένην, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἰῶνος ἕως τοῦ αἰῶνος σὺ εἶ. Quod autem in Hebræo sequitur, אל, non cum tsere legerunt Græci interpretes, sed cum patach, & retulerunt ad comma sequens, versum per μὴ.

## 90:3
Ver. 3. TURN NOT MAN UNTO HUMILITY.

In the Hebrew the particle of negation is not held: therefore Bellarmine suspects it to have fallen out (contrary to all faith of the Codices) or that the words should be read by way of interrogation: Wouldst thou turn man unto humility unto vileness and extreme abjection, so that, having forgotten the true good, he might embrace the mud of secular desires? But this is not of God; such a conversion is from the Devil, the god of this world. Nor does it agree with the argument of the Psalm. The Hebrew words stand more correctly without interrogation, for they affirm something, they do not deny, which the added member, likewise affirmative, teaches: Thou shalt turn man even unto contrition and shalt say, turn again, ye sons of men, i.e., through diseases and death you reduce men to ashes, but in the resurrection you command them to return from the dust, which is the simplest interpretation and most convenient to the text: for the sacred Psalmist discourses concerning the fragility and mortality of man. Some refer it to the propagation of the human race in this life, because others succeed into the place of the deceased, nor does Luther in his Latin Commentary, Tom. 4. Jena, deny it.

Latin:

Vers. 3. NE AVERTAS HOMINEM IN HUMILITATEM.

In Ebræo non habetur particula negandi: ideo eam excidisse suspicatur Bellarm. (contra omnem Codicum fidem) vel per interrogationem verba legenda esse: Convertasne hominem in humilitatem ad vilitatem & abjectionem extremam, ut oblitus veri boni amplectatur lutum desideriorum secularium. Sed hoc non est Dei, a Diabolo Deo mundi hujus est talis conversio. Nec argumento Psalmi congruit. Ebræa rectius se habent sine interrogatione, nam affirmant aliquid, non negant, quod docet adjectum membrum itidem affirmativum: Convertes hominem usque ad contritionem & dices, convertimini filii hominum, h. e. per morbos & mortem in cineres homines redigis, sed in resurrectione ex pulvere reverti jubes, quæ iterpretatio simplicissima, & textui convenientissima: nam de fragilitate ac mortalitate hominis disserit Hieropsaltes. Quidam referunt ad propagationem generis humani in hac vita, quia in locum defunctorum alii succedunt, nec abnuit in Comment. Latin. Lutherus Tom. 4. Jenens.

## 90:8
Ver. 8. OUR WORLD) Our hidden things, that is, sins unknown to men, thou seest.

Latin:

Vers. 8. SÆCVLVM NOSTRVM) Abscondita nostra, id est, peccata hominibus incognita tu vides.

## 90:9
Ver. 9. OUR YEARS SHALL MEDITATE AS A SPIDER) τὰ ἔτη ἡμῶν ὡς ἀράχνη ἐμελέτων. Perhaps for כמו they read שמו, with ה understood, and took הגה as a verb: but our Hebrew text takes it as a noun, which signifies speech. Life flies, like winged words.

Latin:

Vers. 9. ANNI NOSTRI SICVT ARANEÆ MEDITABVNTVR) τὰ ἔτη ἡμῶν ὡς ἀράχνη ἐμελέτων. Forte pro כמו legerunt שמו, subaudito ה & הגה sumserunt ut verbum: noster autem textus Hebræus, ut nomen, quod sermonem significat. Vita volat, ut ἔπεα πτερόεντα.

## 90:10
Ver. 10. THE DAYS OF OUR YEARS IN THEM ARE SEVENTY YEARS) That is, in all the time of our years (namely, those which we spend in health) there is no more than LXX. years.

BUT IF IN STRENGTH EIGHTY YEARS) But if (suppose one were endowed with exceptional strength, an exceptional temperament of body) eighty years. Solon in Herodotus book 1. ἐς γὰρ ἑβδομήκοντα ἔτεα ὅρον τῆς ζωῆς ἀνθρώπῳ προτίθημι.

AND MORE OF THEM LABOR AND SORROW) In the Hebrew: ורהבם, that is, the very strength of it. Aben-Ezra and Rabbi Solomon think youth is so called: he says that it also is full of labor and punishment (which in the Hebrew manner he calls iniquity). The Greeks read ורבם τὸ πλεῖσον αὐτῶν, which this Latin translates, more of them.

Latin:

Vers. 10. DIES ANNORVM NOSTRORVM IN IPSIS SEPTVAGINTA ANNI) Id est, in omni tempore annorum nostrorum (nempe quos in sanitate agimus) non amplius est quam LXX. anni.

SI AVTEM IN POTENTATIBVS OCTOGINTA ANNI) Si autem viribus (supple eximiis præditus aliquis fuerit, eximia corporis temperatura) octoginta anni. Solon apud Herodotum libro 1. ἐς γὰρ ἑβδομήκοντα ἔτεα ὅρον τῆς ζωῆς ἀνθρώπῳ προτίθημι.

ET AMPLIVS EORVM LABOR ET DOLOR) In Hebræo: ורהבם, id est, ipsum robur ejus. Sic vocari juventam censent Aben-Esdra & Rabbi Salomo: illam quoque ait laboris & pœnæ (quam Hebræo more iniquitatem vocat) esse plenam. Græci legerunt ורבם τὸ πλεῖσον αὐτῶν, quod hic Latinus vertit, amplius eorum.

## 90:11
Ver. 11. WHO KNOWS THE POWER OF THY WRATH AND FOR THY FEAR THY WRATH TO NUMBER) (למנות they referred not to the beginning of the following, as the Masoretes, but to the end of this clause. The sense is: who fully knows all the examples of thy severity, and if anyone knew, how would he dare, for fear and anxiety, to recount them and set them forth in words.

Latin:

Vers. 11. QVIS NOVIT POTESTATEM IRÆ TVÆ ET PRÆ TIMORE TVO RAM TVAM DINVMERARE) (למנות non ad initium sequentis, ut Masoretæ, sed ad hujus commatis finem retulere. Sensus est: quis plene novit omnia severitatis tuæ exempla, & si quis nosset, quomodo præ timore & anxietate auderet ea recensere, & verbis exsequi.

## 90:12
Vers. 12. MAKE THY RIGHT HAND KNOWN) The Greeks here read not ימינך, ימנו but ימינך correctly, if I am not mistaken: they also correctly interpreted it as τὴν δεξιάν σου. Show us your help, as you have done heretofore.

AND THOSE LEARNED IN HEART IN WISDOM) More correctly: And we will cause to come to wisdom. This will be the best way for us to be amended.

He follows Bellarmine here: But he is altogether mistaken with him. For a rivulet cannot or ought not to be preferred to its fountains. And the Hebrew Codices agree here entirely. למנות ימינו that our days may be numbered: as Jerome renders it, whose Codices therefore agree with ours. And by what right is that word למנות snatched away to the preceding verse, when by the force of the Hebrew accentuation it pertains to the present one, and the sense of the Hebrew Codex agrees perfectly, which Bellarmine himself confesses is not to be despised, namely that God may make our days known to us, that is, may cause us to understand the brevity of the day of our life, and not deceive ourselves, judging that to be long-lasting which is most brief. Nor did the Hebrew interpreters, the author of Midrash Tillim, R. David Kimchi, R. Aban-Ezra, R. Obad. Gaon, R. Solomon Jarchi, or even the Chaldean interpreter, read it otherwise.

Latin:

Vers. 12. DEXTRAM TVAM SIC NOTAM FAC) Legere hic Græci non ימינך, ימנו fed ימינך recte, ni fallor: recte etiam interpretati sunt τὴν δεξιάν σου. Auxilium tuum nobis ostende, ut antehac fecisti.

ET ERVDITOS CORDE IN SAPIENTIA) Rectius: Et venire faciemus ad sapientiam. Hæc erit ad nos emendandos via optima.

Sequitur hic Bellarminum: Sed omnino cum eodem fallitur. Non enim potest aut debet rivulus anteferri fontibus. Et consentiunt hic ex asse Codices Ebræi. למנות ימינו ut numerentur dies nostri: ut reddit Hieronymus, cujus proinde Codices nostris consentiunt. Et quo jure verbum illud למנות ad præcedentem versum abripitur, quum vi accentua- tionis Ebraicæ ad præsentem pertineat, sensusque Ebræi Codicis optime congruat, quem Bellarminus ipse fatetur, non contemnendum esse, ut nempe notos faciat Deus nobis dies nostros, id est, faciat, ut intelligamus brevitatem diei vitæ nostræ, & non ipsi nos fallamus, judicantes diuturnum id, quod est brevissimum. Neque aliter legerunt Ebræi interpp. autor Midrasch Tillim, R. David Kimchi, R. Aban-Ezra. R. Obad. Gaon, R. Salomo Jarchi, aut etiam Chaldæus interpres.

## 91:1 Argument
Ps. XCI. The help of the most high.

Latin:

Pf. XCI. Adjutorium altissimi.

## 91:5
THOU SHALT NOT BE AFRAID FOR THE TERROR BY NIGHT) From robbers. Vers. 6. FOR THE ARROW THAT FLIETH BY DAY) From open battles. FOR THE BUSINESS THAT WALKETH IN DARKNESS) דָּבָר signifies both business and pestilence. It seems that pestilence is understood here, and other diseases whose causes lie hidden. The Vulgate cannot be excused. For what is this, business walking in darkness? Who therefore can doubt that the word דָּבָר is to be explained here as pestilence, not as business? Not badly does the blessed Lord Dr. Heinrich Höpfner in his Commentary on this Ps. 91, p. 60, judge that pestilence is introduced here, as a poisonous woman, by prosopopoeia, and that infection is attributed to it, which happens through contagion. See the same. FOR THE DESTRUCTION AND THE NOONDAY DEVIL) It appears that the Greeks read in the Hebrew צָהֳרִים וְשַׁד מִקָּטֹב For they are accustomed to translate שַׁד as δαιμόνιον, as in Deut. 32, 17, and below 106, 37. We have in the Hebrew מִקָּטֶב יָשׁוּד צָהֲרָיִם from the destruction wasting at noonday: i.e., from the heat of the Sun, which is lethal to many, to those traveling, especially in those places of Syria and the neighboring regions. Whatever the Greeks may have seen or read, or however their interpretation may stand, whether it be uncorrupted or not, the fountains of Hebrew truth flow purely here, still describing the pestilence from the destruction that wastes at noonday. For קֶטֶב denotes destruction and ruin, and is used of the pestilential plague that bites and cuts off, Hos. 13, 14. And the word יָשׁוּד from שָׁדַד agrees perfectly with the wasting plague, which is a most deleterious disease. Although the Greek version itself does not conflict with the modern reading of the Hebrew text: because such a wasting can be understood through the Hebrew word, which is effected by the Devil, who is therefore called שַׁד κατ' ἀντονομασίαν; hence the LXX explained the same word as concerning a Demon, or rather concerning such a destruction as is effected by the Devil, ἀπὸ συμπτώματος καὶ δαίμονος μεσημβρινε from that which happens through the noonday demon.

Latin:

NON TIMEBIS A TIMORE NOCTVRNO) A latronibus. Vers. 6. A SAGITTA VOLANTE IN DIE) Ab apertis præliis. A NEGOTIO PERAMBVLANTE IN TENEBRIS) דָּבָר & negotium & pestem significat. Videtur hic intelligi pestis, & alii morbi, quorum causæ latent. Excusari non potest vulgata. Quid enim hoc est, negotium in tenebris perambulans? Qui ergo dubitari potest, vocem דָּבָר de peste hic explicandam esse, non de negotio? Non male B. Dn. D. Heinr. Höpfnerus in Comment. ad h. Pf. 91. p. 60. pestem hic introduci censet, tanquam mulierem veneficam, per prosopopœiam, eique tribui infectionem, quæ fit per contagium. V. eod. AB INCVRSV ET DÆMONIO MERIDIANO) Apparet, Græcos in Hebræo legisse צָהֳרִים וְשַׁד מִקָּטֹב Nam שַׁד δαιμόνιον vertere solent, ut Deut. 32, 17. & infra 106, 37. Nos in Hebræo habemus מִקָּטֶב יָשׁוּד צָהֳרָיִם ab excidio vastante in meridie: i. e. ab ardore Solis, qui multis est lethalis, iter facientibus, maxime in locis illis Syriæ & vicinis. Quicquid viderint aut legerint Græci, aut quomodocunque se habeat eorum interpretatio, incorrupta sit, nec ne? fontes veritatis Ebrææ hic pure fluunt, describentes adhuc pestem ab exitio, quod vastet in meridie. Nam קֶטֶב exidium & exitium notat, & de lue pestifera mordente & exscindente usurpatur Os. 13, 14. Et verbum יָשׁוּד a שָׁדַד vastando testi apprime congruit, qui morbus est maxime dele-terius. Quanquam nec ipsa Græca versio lectioni modernæ Ebræi textus repugnet: quia intelligi potest vastatio talis per verbum Ebræum, quæ a Diabolo efficitur, qui inde κατ' ἀντονομασίαν שַׁד dictus est; inde LXX. exposuere idem verbum de Dæmonio, vel potius de tali exitio, quod efficitur a Diabolo, ἀπὸ συμπτώματος καὶ δαίμονος μεσημβρινε ab eo quod accidit per dæmonium meridianum.

## 92:1 Argument
Ps. XCII. The righteous as the Palm tree.

It is called THE SONG OF ADAM by the Hebrews, because Adam could have said such things when he first beheld the things created by God. But at that time there were not yet the wicked, transgressors, or enemies of God among men. FOR THE SABBATH DAY) Which is dedicated to the memory of creation. Some Hebrews, however, understand these things concerning the happiness which they think will last for a thousand years. Vers. 11. AND MY OLD AGE IN FAT MERCY,) In the Hebrew it is, בַּלֹּתִי בְּשֶׁמֶן רַעֲנָן. But the LXX instead of בַּלֹּתִי read כָּלֹתִי and translated, τὸ γῆρας με ἐν ἐλαίῳ πίονι. And thus Augustine reads. Certain scribes wrote ἐλέῳ instead of ἐλαίῳ, because those words are not only similar in writing, but also of equal pronunciation in that age. And from this this version flowed. From wherever the version flowed, it is faulty, but the fountains flow clearly. Bellarmine excuses it on the ground that by oil mercy is understood. But it does not befit an interpreter to expound his own sense: he is bound to render word for word. The Cardinal, however, explains that old age is said to be in the oil of the womb, when it abounds in humor, which makes it long-lasting. But it is not held in the Hebrew as fat oil, but flourishing, or most pleasant and pure, nor is there mention of old age, but I am anointed, says the Psalmist, or I am drenched with oil, which is more correctly explained concerning all-embracing blessing and exhilaration. The Syrian says: and you have anointed me with sweet oil.

Luth. Be anointed with fresh oil: with which Campensis and the Belgian agree.

Latin:

Pf. XCII. Justus ut Palma.

CANTICVM ADAMI dicitur ab Hebræis, quod talia dicere Adamus potuit, cum res a Deo primum conditas aspexit. Sed tum nondum erant impii, prævaricatores, aut hostes Dei inter homines. A DIE SABBATI) Qui dicatus memoriæ creationis. Hebræi tamen nonnulli hæc de felicitate, quam per mille annos duraturam putant, intelligunt. Vers. 11. ET SENECTVS MEA IN MISERICORDIA VBERI,) In Hebræo est, בַּלֹּתִי בְּשֶׁמֶן רַעֲנָן. At LXX. pro בַּלֹּתִי legerunt כָּלֹתִי & verterunt, τὸ γῆρας με ἐν ἐλαίῳ πίονι. Et sic legit Augustinus. Librarii quidam pro ἐλαίῳ scripserunt ἐλέῳ, quod illæ voces non modo scriptione sint vicinæ, sed & illa ætate paris pronuntiationis. Et hinc fluxit hæc versio. Undecunque versio fluxerit, vitiosa est, fontes autem limpide fluunt. Illam excusat Bellarm. ea ratione quod per oleum intelligatur misericordia. Sed interpretem non decet suum exponere sensum: verbum verbo reddere tenetur. Explicat autem Cardinalis illa senectutem in oleo uteri dici, quando abundat humore, qui facit eam esse diuturnam. Sed non de oleo uberi, verum virente, vel amœnissimo & purissimo habetur in Ebræo, nec senectutis mentio fit, sed delibutus sum, inquit Psaltes, vel perfundor oleo, quod de omnigena benedictione, & exhilaratione rectius explicatur. Syrus & tinxisti me oleo suavi.

Luth. Werde gesalbet mit frischem Oel: quibus con- sonant Campensis, & Belga.

## 92:12 Addition
On Psalm 92, v. 13.

THE RIGHTEOUS SHALL FLOURISH LIKE THE PALM TREE. The LXX have the word Φοίνικι, not the phoenix bird, but they understood the palm tree, called so by the Greeks, from which ignorance of the word the fable seems to have been born concerning the reviving of the phoenix, whose ashes are buried under a palm tree by the bird itself about to die, as Lactantius has it in his poem on the Phoenix. Which, however, Aldrovandus, in book XII of his Ornithology, chapter 27, acknowledges never to have existed.

Latin:

Ad Pfal. 92. v. 13.

JUSTUS UT PALMA FLOREBIT. LXX. habent vocem Φοίνικι, non avem Phæ- nicem, sed palmam arborem Græcis ita dictam intel- lexere, ex qua vocis ignorantia fabula videtur nata de reviviscentia Phænicis, cujus cinis sub arbore pal- ma ab ave ipsa moritura condatur, ut habet Lactan- tius carm. de Phœnice. Quam tamen nunquam extitisse Aldrovandus lib. XII. Ornithol. cap. 27. agnoscit.

## 92:15
Vers. 16. AND THEY SHALL BE WELL-PATIENT) He translates κατὰ πόδας, which in Greek is εὐπαθέντες ἔσονται, where εὐπαθεῖν is ἀκμάζειν to flourish, to do well, which is the very meaning of the Hebrew adjective, רַעַנַנִּים. What precedes in the Hebrew דְּשֵׁנִים, that the Greeks constructed with the preceding word שֵׂיבָה, which signifies gray hair or old age.

Latin:

Vers. 16. ET BENE PATIENTES ERVNT) Vertit κα- τὰ πόδας, quod in Græco est εὐπαθέντες ἔσονται, ubi εὐπα- θεῖν est ἀκμάζειν florere, bene agere, quæ ipsa est significatio adjectivi Hebraici, רַעֲנַנִּים. Quod præcedit in Hebræo דְּשֵׁנִים, id cum voce præcedenti שֵׂיבָה, quæ canitiem sive senectutem significat, Græci construxere.

## 93:1 Argument
PSALM XCIII.

Christ restrains the surges of the sea.

ON THE DAY BEFORE THE SABBATH WHEN THE EARTH WAS FOUNDED] The Greeks better: ὅτε κατῴκισεν ἡ γῆ, when the earth began to be inhabited, namely by living creatures and man. In the Hebrew this is not present, just as that which is prefixed to the following Psalm.

Nor is that found in the Chaldean, nor in the hexapla of Origen, nor in the more correct Greek versions, nor in Eusebius, Euthymius, or Theodoret, as Tirinus admits; and not even in all the Latin versions, as Bellarmine observes, who vainly elicits from it that the earth was established on the same day because man was formed (it is absurdly asserted that the earth was stabilized by the formation of man so that it would not be moved), and that it was renewed and established into the kingdom of Christ through the passion of Christ v. 2, thus ineptly explaining both the formation and the reparation of man. However, this is a prophecy about the kingdom of Christ being propagated as far as the world extends, and being established forever, concerning which B. Luth. writes in the argument of this Psalm. After Kimchi, in the commentary of Kab Venaki cited by Cocceius, All these Psalms up to the one hundred and first are of the future tense and speak of the days of the Messiah. Cocceius also interprets these words concerning the stability of the kingdom of Christ. Osiander, the Vinarienses; others [interpret it] concerning the firmament of the world with B. Gesner: by which method it will be permissible to understand the particle of comparison: As the world is stable so that it does not totter, so your throne has been established from then, from the very first foundation of the world. But you are from eternity. V. Ps. 90, 2. Prov. 8, 22. 23. Mich. 5, 2.

Latin:

PSALM. XCIII.

Christus compefcit maris æstus.

IN DIE ANTE SABBATVM QVANDO FVNDA- TA EST TERRA] Græci melius: ὅτε κατῴκισεν ἡ γῆ, cum habitari cœpit terra, nempe ab animantibus, & homine. In Hebr. hoc non est, ut nec quod sequenti Psalmo præfigitur.

Nec reperitur illud in Chaldæo nec in hexaplis Origenis nec in correctioribus Græcis, nec in Eusebio, Euthymio, Theodoreto, ut fatetur Tirin. ac ne quidem in Latinis omnibus, observante Bellar- mino, qui frustra inde elicit, eodem die terram esse firmatam, quia formatus est homo, (per formatio- nem hominis terram stabilitam esse, ut non commo- veatur, absurde asseritur) & per Christi passionem esse renovatam & stabilitam in regnum Christi v. 2. ita tum de formatione, tum de reparatione hominis inepte explicans. Est autem hic prophetia de regno Christi propagando, quam late patet orbis terrarum, & in æternum stabiliendo, quo de B. Luth. in argu- mento hujus Psalmi. Post Kimchium comment. Kab Venaki citante Coccejo, Omnes hi Psalmi usq; ad cen- tesimum, & primum futuri temporis sunt, & de diebus Messia loquuntur. De stabilitate regni Christi inter- pretantur etiam hæc verba Coccej. Osiander, Vina- rienses; Alii de firmato orbe terrarum cum B. Gesne- ro: quo pacto subintelligere licebit particulam si- militudinis: Sicut stabilis est orbis ne nutet, ita firma- tus est thronus tuus ex tunc inde a prima terrarum or- bis fundatione. A seculo autem tu. V. Ps. 90, 2. Prov. 8, 22. 23. Mich. 5, 2.

## 93:1 Addition
On Psalm 93.

Latin:

Ad Pfal. 93.

## 93:1 Addition
Verse 1. THE LORD IS CLOTHED WITH STRENGTH AND HATH GIRDED HIMSELF.

The Genevan, Spanish, English, Alagond, Piscator, and Tremellius render it thus: he hath girded himself with strength, and the habitable world is established, that it may not waver. Whence Lansbergius and Mersennus prove the immobility of the earth against Kepler from this passage. But it is a question here of the firmness of the kingdom of Christ, not of the globe of the earth. Compare Psalm 89:38.

Latin:

Vers. 1. INDUTUS EST DOMINUS FOR- TITUDINE ET PRÆCINXIT SE.

Genevens. Hispan. Anglus, Alagond, Pisca- tor & Tremellius ita reddunt, accinxit se fortitudi- ne atque stabilitur orbis habitabilis, ne nutet. Un- de Lansbergius & Mersennus immobilitatem terræ contra Kepler. ex h. l. probant. Sed de firmitate regni Christi, non orbis terræ hic agitur. Conf. Psal. 89, 38.

## 93:5 Addition
Verse 5. THY TESTIMONIES ARE MADE EXCEEDINGLY CREDIBLE.

From this translation Bellarmine, book VI on grace, chapter 1, proves that divine matters are easily credible; But In the Hebrew text it is FIDELIA, that is, they deserve faith. Cf. Ps. 19, 8. Therefore Genebr. explained it as credible, that is, worthy of belief, certain, faithful, fixed.

Latin:

Vers. 5. TESTIMONIA TUA CREDIBILIA FACTA SUNT NIMIS.

Ex hac translatione Bellarm. l. VI. de grat. c. 1. probat res divinas facile credibiles esse; At in textu Ebræo est FIDELIA sunt, h. e. fidem me- rentur. Conf. Ps. 19, 8. Ideo Genebr. exposuit credi- bilia, id est, digna creditu, certa, fidelia, fixa.

## 94:1 Argument
PSALM XCIV.

Against the Throne of iniquity.

Vers. 1. THE LORD GOD OF VENGEANCE: THE GOD OF VENGEANCE HAS ACTED FREELY.

In the Hebrew the latter member has: The God of vengeance has shone forth. Who will persuade Bellarmine that this is the same as 'has acted freely'? Cocceius warns that the ancient interpreter of the LXX did not understand ἐπαῤῥησιάσατο: for to the Hellenists παῤῥησία is clarity, manifestation. It is best translated ἐπεφάνη, and the discourse is about the Son of God manifested in the flesh, and therefore the Psalm is Prophetic: because to Him is attributed the power to avenge the despisers of Himself and the oppressors of the Church. Mal. 3, 4. c. 4, 1. Matth. 3, 10. Act. 12, 23. which vengeance He exercised while sitting at the right hand of God the Father against the Jews, the Romans, etc. According to B. Luth., from whom there is no reason why we should depart, it is a general prayer, but a most ardent one, full of the affections of an afflicted heart and one grieving that the blood of Abel is shed and swallowed by Cainite hypocrites with such cruelty and iniquity. The Psalmist, however, complains not of the nations, but of hypocrites and domestic enemies, etc.

Latin:

PSALM. XCIV.

Adversus Solium iniquitatis.

Vers. 1. DEUS ULTIONUM DOMINUS: DEUS ULTIONUM LIBERE EGIT.

In Ebr. posterius membrum habet: Deus ultio- num effulsit. Quod idem esse cum libere egit, cui persuadebit Bellarminus? Coccejus monet non in- tellexisse Veterem interpretem LXX. ἐπαῤῥησιάσα- το: παῤῥησίαν enim Hellenistis esse claritatem, mani- festationem. Optime verti ἐπεφάνη & sermonem esse de Filio Dei manifestato in carne, adeoque Psalmum esse Propheticum: quia illi tribuitur potestas ad ulci- scendum comtemtores sui, & oppressores Ecclesiæ. Mal. 3, 4. c. 4, 1. Matth. 3, 10. Act. 12, 23. quam ultionem exercuit ad dextram Dei Patris sedens in Judæis, in Romanis &c. Secundum B. Luth. a quo cur disceda- mus, causa nulla est, est generalis precatio, sed arden- tissima, plena affectibus afflicti cordis & dolentis a Cai- nicis hypocritis sanguinem Abel tanta crudelitate & ini- quitate fundi & sorberi. Conqueri autem Psalten non de gentibus; sed de hypocritis, & domesticis hostibus &c.

## 94:1 Addition
To Psalm 94.

Latin:

Ad Psalm. 94.

## 94:9
Vers. 9. HE WHO PLANTED THE EAR SHALL HE NOT HEAR, OR HE WHO FORMED THE EYE SHALL HE NOT CONSIDER) An excellent argument. Whatever of perfection exists in created things is from God. Therefore it exists in Him in an eminent way.

Latin:

Vers. 9. QVI PLANTAVIT AVREM NON AVDIET, AVT QVI FINXIT OCVLVM NON CONSIDERET) Egregia argumentatio. Quicquid est perfectionis in rebus conditis a Deo est. Est ergo in ipso eminenti modo.

## 94:15
Ver. 15. UNTIL JUSTICE SHALL BE TURNED INTO JUDGMENT.

In the Hebrew, judgment shall return to justice, as Jerome interpreted it. The Vulgate, with the LXX interpreters, rendered it as if it read עַד כִּי. Which Capellus defends in vain. See Buxtorf's Anti-Critica, p. 619.

On verses 17, 18, 19. See Sermon XXX on the Memory of the Just, Wittenberg.

Latin:

Vers. 15. QUOADUSQUE JUSTITIA CON- VERTATUR IN JUDICIUM.

In Ebr. ad justitiam revertetur judicium ut Hie- ronym. interpretatus est. Vulg. cum LXX. Int. red- didit, ac si legeretur עַד כִּי. Quod nequicquam defendit Capell. Vid. Anti-Crit. Buxt. p. 619.

De v. 17. 18. 19. Vid. Concio XXX. in Memoria Justor. Witeberg.

## 94:20 Addition
Verse 20. SHALL THE THRONE OF INIQUITY HAVE FELLOWSHIP WITH THEE, WHICH FRAMETH MISCHIEF BY A LAW.

Bellarm. inquires about the obscurity of the passage, rendering this sense of it: shall the throne of those judging iniquitously be joined to you as a companion, to you who inflict or cause labor in your precept, so that your precepts cannot be fulfilled without great labor. He notes, however, two other expositions: 1. Are you a participant in an iniquitous judgment, which frames labor in a precept, that is, which makes divine precepts too laborious. 2. Of St. Augustine, who says that God frames labor, or pain, in a precept, because he causes us to be instructed by the labors and pains which the righteous suffer in this life. But in the Hebrew there is no obscurity. It can be rendered thus: Shall the throne of perversities be associated with you, fashioning or fabricating labor or molestation against or beyond the statute, which is not to be referred to a throne, or to the habit or custom of moral vices, but to Doctors sitting on a throne, teaching with authority, as the context and those words about the throne and statute indicate, or who teach from an Ecclesiastical chair, as Hieronym. B. Luther, Bugenhag. Gesnerus, Musculus, Mullerus & Coppen. interpret: that the discourse is about those who decree against divine law: which appears from the opposite in v. 12: And therefore B. Luther rightly uses it concerning the statutes of the Roman Anti-Christ against the law T. IIX. Jen. German. concerning the Papacy founded by the Devil.

Latin:

Vers. 20. NUMQUID ADHÆRET TIBI SE- DES INIQUITATIS, QUI FINGIS LA- BOREM IN PRÆCEPTO.

Bellarm. quæritur de loci obscuritate, red- dens hunc ejus sensum : nunquid adjungitur tibi tanquam socius thronus inique judicantium, tibi qui in præcepto tuo observando laborem inferis, sive facis, ut præcepta tua non sine magno labore possint impleri. Notat autem adhuc alias duas expositiones; 1. Nunquid particeps es iniqui judi- cii, quod fingit laborem in præcepto, id est, quod præcepta divina facit nimis laboriosa. 2. S. Augustini, qui dicit Deum fingere laborem, seu dolorem in præcepto, quia facit, ut ex labori- bus & doloribus, quos in hac vita patiuntur justi, erudiamur. Sed in Ebræo non est obscuritas. Ita reddi potest: An sociabitur tibi solium pravita- tum, effingens vel fabricans laborem vel molestiam adversus vel præter statutum, quod non ad thro- num, vel habitum aut consuetudinem vitiorum moralium, sed Doctores in solio sedentes, cum authoritate docentes, ut contextus & verba il- la de solio & statuto indicant, vel qui de Eccle- siastica cathedra docent, referendum, uti Hie- ronym. B. Luther. Bugenhag. Gesnerus, Musculus, Mullerus & Coppen. interpretantur : de iis, qui contra legem divinam statuunt, sermonem esse: quod ex opposito v. 12. apparet: Ideoque uti- tur eo recte B. Lutherus de statutis Anti-Christi Romani contra legem T. IIX. Jen. German. de Pa- patu à Diabolo fundato.

## 95:1 Argument
PSALM XCV.

Hearts are not to be hardened against Christ.

PRAISE OF THE SONG OF DAVID HIMSELF) This is not in the Hebrew.

Theodoret wishes the Psalm to have been composed by David in the person of King Josiah: Bellarmine warns against this, that the Psalm is suitable at all times for all believers, both Jews and Christians. The question, however, is not about use or suitability, but about the meaning. But the blessed Luther rightly teaches that the whole Psalm is to be referred to Christ: for He is that God to whom we ought to exult, our Shepherd, and that God whom the unbelievers tempted in the desert, 1 Cor. 10:9, who abrogates the Mosaic worship and in its place urges faith in the Gospel, etc. The Apostle, the Holy Spirit, asserts that these things which are had in verse 7 are spoken by Him, Heb. 3:7, and thus He exhorts us to hear the voice of Christ: whence the Deity of the Holy Spirit is demonstrated, because He who speaks here testifies that He was tempted by the Israelites, and swears that they shall not enter into His rest; which speech in verses 9, 10, 11 befits none but God. Compare our Anti-Crellius §. 508.

Latin:

PSALM. XCV.

Christo non obduranda corda.

LAUS CANTUS IPSI DAVID) Non est hoc in Hebr.

THeodoretus vult Psalmum a Davide in persona Re- gis Josiae compositum esse: Contra monet Bellarm. Psalmum omni tempore omnibus fidelibus convenire tum Judaeis,tum Christianis. Quaestio vero est, non de usu vel convinientia. Sed de sensu. Recte autem docet B. Luther. totum Psalmum referendum esse ad Chri- stum:hic enim est ille Deus,cui nos exultare debemus,Pa- stor noster,& Deus ille,quem increduli in deserto tenta- runt 1. Cor. 10, 9. qui abrogat Mosaicum cultum ejusq; loco fidem urget inEvangelium &c. ApostolusSpir. S. haec loqui quae v.7.habentur,asseritEbr.3,7.adeoq; hortari nos ad audiendam vocemChristi:undeDei- tas SS.demonstratur,quia is,qui hic loquitur,se ten- tatum ab Israelitis testatur, & jurat, quod non venturi sint in requiem suam; quae oratio v. 9. 10. 11. non nisi Deo convenit. Conf. Anti-Crellius noster §. 508.

## 95:1 Addition
To Psalm 95.

Latin:

Ad Psalm. 95.

## 95:10 Addition
Verse 10. FORTY YEARS WAS I GRIEVED.

Pagn. & Montan. render it, I contended with this people. Which the Apostle also accepted concerning the offense of God toward the rebellious Israelites, Heb. 3, 17. But those words are read in a sense clearly contrary in the public prayers of the Papists and in the daily morning office in all Breviaries: for forty years I was near, or I approached this people.

Latin:

Vers. 10. QUADRAGINTA ANNIS OF- FENSUS FUI.

Pagn. & Montan. reddunt, litigapi cum hoc populo. Quæ de offensione Dei erga rebelles Israe- litas accepit quoque Apostolus Ebr. 3, 17. At illa sensu plane contrario in publicis Pontificiorum precibus & quotidiano officio matutino in omnibus Breviariis leguntur: quadraginta annis proximus fui, sive appropinquavi populo huic.

## 96:1 Argument
PSALM XCVI. Let all things applaud Christ the King of the nations.

A SONG OF DAVID HIMSELF) Nor this. It is credible, however, that this song was made by David in commemoration of the Ark brought into Zion. WHEN THE HOUSE WAS BUILT AFTER THE CAPTIVITY] Nor is this in the Hebrew: But the sense is, this song of David was used very opportunely by Ezra, when the temple had already been restored.

That the Psalm treats not of the Ark brought into Zion, but of the kingdom of the Messiah propagated to the nations, is taught both by the open words of verse 3, 'declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all peoples': add verses 7, 8, 9, 10, and the whole structure of the Psalm. Nor do the Jews R. Obadiah and R. Solomon deny this: who observe that a new song is said, which is to be sung in the days of Christ. R. Kimchi observes that all the Psalms from 93 to 101 treat of Christ.

Latin:

PSALMUS XCVI. Christo Regi gentium applaudant omnia.

CANTICVM IPSI DAVID) Nec hoc. Credibile tamen a Davide factum hoc carmen in commemorationem Arcae introductae in Sionem. QVANDO DOMVS A EDIFICABATVR POST CA- PTIVITATEM] Nec hoc in Hebraeo est: Sed sensus, usur- patum hoc carmen Davidis peroportune ab Esdra, cum jam restitutum esset templum.

NOn deArca in Sionem introducta,sed de regno Messiae ad gentes propagato Psalmum agere, tum aperta verba v.3. annunciate inter gentes gloriam ejus,in omnibus populis mirabilia ejus:adde v.7.8.9.10. tum tota structuraPsalmi docent.Neq; id negant Ju- daeiR.Obad.& R.Salomo:qui observant canticum no- vum dici,quod in diebusChr.cantandum fit.R.Kim. Psalmos omnes a 93. ad 101. de Christo agere observat.

## 96:1 Addition
To Psalm 96.

Latin:

Ad Psalm. 96.

## 96:1 Addition
Verse 1. O SING UNTO THE LORD A NEW SONG.

Bellarmine thinks the Psalm was composed on the occasion of the ark of the Lord being brought back, yet that it preaches the advent of Christ and his kingdom: and is explained concerning it by Hieron. August. Ambros. Chrysost. Theodor. & Enthymius: which Pagninus, Vatabl. Genebr. Jansenius also acknowledge. We add what B. Hülsemannus has concerning the Argument of this and the following Psalm: Since we have other dissenters concerning the argument of these Psalms, such as Boblius, both regarding the author of these Psalms up to the 100th, whom he thinks to be Moses, and regarding the argument, which he thinks is proper and adequate to be about the ark of the covenant, and only figuratively accommodated to Christ; it must be seen that these Psalms treat 1. neither of the ark of the covenant, nor 2. of some particular judgment of God in punishing certain nations, nor 3. of that universal or final one, but 4. of the gracious advent of Christ into the Church.

which is evident (1.) from the universal gladness and joy of all peoples, even idolatrous ones, such as is never predicted concerning the restoration of the ark of the covenant, but rather the contrary; namely, that its memory is to be abolished, Jer. 3, 16. Concerning such joy, see Ps. 96, 1. 2. 3. 7. 10. 11. Ps. 97, 1. 6. 8. Ps. 98, 2. 4. seq. Psal. 99, 34. seqq. (2.) from the universal correction of all nations, which correction is said to be instituted through grace and justice, neither of which can be predicated of the ark of the covenant. For whether we take it concerning the gracious or imputative justice of God, which is said to be extended even to the nations, Ps. 96, 13. 14. Ps. 97, 6. Ps. 98, 3. which passages Jansenius and Eman. Sa themselves explain concerning the justice and salutary correction brought about through the cross of Christ; and they say that correction is to be explained by restoration, Psal. 96, 10. Psal. 97, 2. where there is הכין & מכון as in Col. 1, 20. against Lorinus, who wrongly explains these things concerning the final and universal judgment of the whole world: Or even if we explain it concerning the universal vindicatory justice of God, in neither way can these predicates fit the ark of the covenant. Wherefore, whoever says that they are extended to the benefits of the N. T. as if by mere application, but that the adequate object, concerning which such glory is predicated, is the ark of the covenant, as Boblius and Musculus do, detracts from the Apostolic inferences taken from these Psalms.

Latin:

Vers. 1. CANTATE DOMINO CANTICUM NOVUM.

Bellarminus occasione arcæ Domini reductæ Psalmum compositum putat, prædicare tamen ad- ventum Christi & regnum ejus: & de eo exponi ab Hieron. August. Ambros. Chrysost. Theodor. & Enthymio: quod etiam Pagninus, Vatabl. Genebr. Jansenius agnoscunt. Addimus, quæ de Argu- mento hujus & sequentis Psalmi habet B. Hülse- mannus: Cum circa argumentum horum Psalmo- rum etiam alios contradicentes habeamus, ut Bob- lium, tum quoad authorem horum Psalmorum usque ad CI. quem putat esse Mosen, tum quoad argumentum, quod proprium & adæquatum pu- tat esse de arca fœderis, & tralatitie tantum ad Chri- stum accommodari; Videndum est 1. nec de arca fœderis, nec 2. de judicio quodam particulari Dei, in puniendis quibusdam gentibus, nec 3. de uni- versali seu extremo illo, verum 4. de adventu Chri- sti gratioso in Ecclesiam hos Psalmos agere.

quod patet (1.) ex universali lætitia, & gaudio omnium populorum etiam idololatricorum, quale de restitutione arcæ fœderis nunquam prædicatur, sed contrarium potius; abolendam esse videlicet ejus memoriam Jer. 3, 16. De ejusmodi autem gau- dio vide Ps. 96, 1. 2. 3. 7. 10. 11. Ps. 97, 1. 6. 8. Ps. 98, 2. 4. seq. Psal. 99, 34. seqq. (2.) ex universali corre- ctione omnium gentium, quæ correctio dicitur in- stituenda per gratiam & justitiam, quorum neu- trum de arca fœderis prædicari potest. Sive enim accipiamus de justitia Dei gratiosa seu imputativa, quæ ad gentes etiam extendenda dicitur Ps. 96, 13. 14. Ps. 97, 6. Ps. 98, 3. quæ loca Jansenius & Eman. Sa ipsi exponunt de justitia & correctione salutari parta per crucem Christi; & correctionem ajunt esse exponendam per restitutionem Psal. 96, 10. Psal. 97, 2. ubi est הכין & מכון ut Col. 1, 20. contra Lori- num, qui de ultimo & universali judicio totius or- bis hæc perperam exponit: Sive etiam expona- mus de universali Dei justitia vindicativa, neutro tamen modo hæc prædicata arcæ fœderis quadrare possunt. Quapropter derogat illationibus Apo- stolicis, ex his Psalmis desumptis, quicunque tanquam per solam applicationem ad beneficia N. T. eos extendi, objectum autem adæquatum, de quo tanta gloria prædicatur, arcam fœderis esse ait, ut Boblius & Musculus.

## 96:10
Ver. 10. SAY AMONG THE NATIONS, THAT THE LORD HATH REIGNED) Justin, against Trypho, affirms that certain old Greek books added 'from the wood' [ἀπὸ ξύλε]: and he urges this passage as containing a prophecy concerning the cross. Tertullian does the same in two places against the Jews, and against Marcion, book 3, whom others also followed. Perhaps some scribes wrote מעץ instead of מלך, but afterwards both readings coalesced.

Perhaps the Grotian [interpretation] is solved by our NON FORTE. Others conjecture that the little word עץ was read as עץ, wood, and that מ was understood, the ellipsis of which is observed elsewhere as well; but if one is to indulge in conjectures, what could not finally be devised in the Holy text, just as one person has a more fortunate talent for discoveries than another? But why is room not left rather for the thought of Fuller, lib. 3, Miscell. S. cap. 13? When some reader, a little more attentive, had noticed that the Prophet there signifies the orchard of the spiritual kingdom of Christ to be extended to all nations, he placed these words of Holy Scripture (ὁ Θεὸς ἐβασίλευσε) in the margin of his book, alongside, those words ἀπὸ τῶ ξύλε, as if they were exegetical. Since that little annotation pleased the scribe not without reason, thinking it to be a variant reading, he confidently transferred it into the text. Augustine Justinian, Bishop of Nebbio, favors this sufficiently probable conjecture in his Pentaglot Psalter, when he asserts that those words were added paraphrastically by some more devout person. Furthermore, no suspicion of corruption of the original Hebrew text is to be admitted here, from which some Papists—Lorin in this place, Pamelius in Tertullian against the Jews, Salmero Vol. 1, prol. 4, Lindanus on the Best Interpreter, ch. 6, and others—clamor that the Jews erased the words FROM THE WOOD, so that they might remove the prophecy concerning the crucifixion. For it cannot be shown that those words were ever found in any Hebrew codex: nor does the Targum acknowledge them, nor the Greek editions of Ximenes or Sixtus, nor the translations of Symmachus, Aquila, Theodotion, nor the Latin Vulgate, nor the Hieronymian. Which Bellarmine also observes in this place. Although this reading (The Lord reigned from the wood) has an excellent sense, nevertheless it is not held in the Greek books, nor was it held in the time of Jerome, Theodoret, and Euthymius, as is clear from their commentaries; nor is it held in the codices. Hebrew [texts], nor in the Vulgate Latin edition. Let the prior Disputation of our Lord Dr. Dorfcheus on the robbery of divine Majesty, Th. 1. seq. in the Pentadecad of dissertations, be compared.

Latin:

Vers. 10. DICITE IN GENTIBVS, QVIA DOMINVS REGNAVIT) Hic libros quosdam veteres Graecos addidisse ἀπὸ ξύλε affirmat contra Tryphonem Justinus: & urget hunc locum, ut de cruce Prophetiam continentem Tertull. adver- sus Judaeos duobus locis, & adversus Marcion, l. 3. quos secuti sunt & alii. Forte quidam Librarii pro מלך scripserunt מעץ, postea vero utraque lectio coaluit.

Forte Grotianum solvitur per NON FORTE nostrum. Alii conjectant voculam עץ lectam fuisse עץ lignum, & subintellectum מ, cujus ellipsis alibi etiam observatur; sed si conjecturis indulgendum, quid non excogitari deniq; poterit in textu S.prout alius alio ad εὑρήματα feliciori ingenio est? Cur ve- ro non locus relinquitur potius cogitationi Fülleri l.3. Miscell. S. c.13. Quum lector quispiam paulo at- tentior animadvertisset, Prophetam ibi Spiritualis re- gni Christi Pomarium in universas gentes proferendum significare; horum sacra Script.verborum (ὁ Θεὸς ἐβα- σίλευσε) apposuit e regione, in ora libri sui,voces illas ἀπὸ τῶ ξύλε, quasi exegeticas. Cum annotatiuncula ista librario non injuria arrideret, rato eam variam esse lectionem, in textum fidenter transtulit. Cui con- jecturae satis probabili favet Augustinus Justinianus Episcopus Nebiensis,in Psalt.Pentaglottum,cum asse- rit,illa ab aliquopiam devotiore παραφρασικῶς addi- ta esse. Caeterum nulla hic corruptelae textus Ebraei originalis suspicio admittenda, e quo verba illa DE LIGNO erasisse Judaeos, ut vaticinium de crucifi- xione tollerent, Pontificii nonnulli clamitant, Lori- nus in h. l. Pamelius in Tertull. contra Jud. Salmero T. 1. prol. 4. Lindanus de Opt. interp. c. 6. & alii. In ullo enim Codice Ebraeo illa verba unquam re- perta esse, doceri non potest: neque agnoscit ea Thargum,neque editiones Graecae Ximeliana,aut Sixti- na: neque translationes Symmachi, Aquilae, Theodo- tionis, nec vulgata Latina, neque Hieronymiana. Quod observat & Bellarm. in h.l. Quamvis haec lectio (Dominus regnavit de ligno)optimum sensum habeat, tamen in libris Graecis hoc non habetur, nec habebatur tempore Hieronymi, Theodoreti, & Euthymii,ut ex co- rum commentariis perspicuum est;nec habetur in Codd. Ebraicis, nec in editione Latina vulgata. Conferatur Dn. D. Dorfchei nostri Disp. prior de rapina divinæ Majestatis Th. 1. seq. in Pentadecad. dissertat.

## 97:1 Argument
PSALM XCVII. Let the Angels adore Christ, let the just exult in him.

TO THIS DAVID, WHEN THE EARTH) It is not in the Hebrew. The sense is that this Psalm was written in memory of that time when, Absalom being dead, he recovered the whole kingdom.

Latin:

PSALMUS XCVII. Christum adorent Angeli, in eo exultent justi.

HUIC DAVID, QVANDO TERRA) Non est in Hebræo. Sensus est, scriptum hunc Psalmum in memoriam ejus tem- poris, quo Absolomo mortuo regnum recuperavit totum.

## 97:7
Ver. 7. ADORE HIM ALL HIS ANGELS) This is the passage which the writer to the Hebrews uses, applying to Christ, so that it may be in the New Covenant, that which was said of God in the Old, προσκυνήτωσαν αυτῷ πάντες ἄγγελοι θεᾶ, with the person changed, which in citing passages matters nothing. For in the Greek here it is προσκυνήσατε αυτῷ πάντες ἄγγελοι ἀυτᾶ. Often the LXX translate אלהים as ἀγγέλους, as above 8, 6. and below 138. 1. Furthermore, in this place they read not אלהים but with the suffix אלהיו.
