Es. 58, 8. & ratione incrementi lucis, quod subinde augeat, ut nemo impedire queat, licet seipsum eadem privare queat: sed & ratione pulchritudinis: ut recte D. Luth. Er wird herfür brechen wie die schöne Morgenröthe. Conf. Ps. 19, 6. Sic ergo populus Messiae fulget splendoribus sanctitatis prae ascendentis aurorae splendore, ac pulchritudine.

Atque ita sese habet primum incisum, si scilicet accentus Athnach hic fungatur officio suo distinctivo. Quem tamen alii negligunt, quod interdum non distinguat in Psalmis: Ex gr. Psalm. 113, 1. 2. quodque hic magis rei ipsius debeat haberi ratio, & quum in altero inciso mentio fiat nativitatis, idcirco conjungendum sit quod de utero dicitur; qui proinde ita legunt: ab utero aurorae tibi ros nativitatis tuae. Caeterum vocem ילדות pro nativitate accipi nullo uno exemplo demonstrant; quam de pueritia & juventa usurpari constat. Eccles. 11, 9. 10. Alibi vero non occurrit in hac forma. Uterum autem heic Metaphorice accipi debere, manifestum est. Unde relinquitur, nullum hic respectum esse ad nativitatem proprie dictam.

Loquitur autem posterius incisum, ut dixi, de Messiae regis officio, augusta dilatatione regni, ejusque paterno erga subditos affectu, ubi mentio sit multitu- dinis filiorum ejus. Nam voce roris metaphorice denotari multitudinem, liquet e 2. Sam. 17, 12. O- periemus eam, sicut solet cadere ros super terram, h. e. ingenti exercitu, & maxima militum multitudine. Vox autem abstracta יַלְדוּת fumitur pro concre- to, more Ebræis usitatissimo, quomodo & gentes di- cuntur ἀκροβυσία, Judæi περιτομή. Rom. 2, 26. cap. 3, 11. 20. soletque apud Latinos etiam juventus pro juvene usurpari, vel pro juvenum cœtu collecti- ve, ut princeps juventutis, omnis juventus. Sic ita- que ros juventutis erit multitudo juvenum seu puero- rum, natorum & filiorum Messiæ scilicet; יַלְדֻתֶךָ qui juventæ tuæ Messiæ, (quod infert verbum ילד & particula relativa) prognati sunt. Ideo majoris Emphaseos ergo additur adhuc pronomen לְךָ tibi, quod respicit partim originem, quam habent fide- les a Christo, ut filii & semen ejus Psalm. 22, 31. E- saiæ 53, 10. partim finem, in quem regenerantur a Christo, virtute Spiritus, nimirum ut sint sui & populus suus. Tibi ros juventæ tuæ, seu natorum tuorum o Messia ! Tibi tuoque cultui regeneran- tur. Conf. Esa. 8, 18. Ebr. 2, 13. Sensus ergo breviter hic est: Innumera multitudo filiorum Mes- siæ nascetur ei, & comparebit per totum terrarum or- bem dispersa, non secus atque ros e cælo depluens ma- gna copia totam terram operire solet. Conf. Esa. 55, 1. Qui conjungunt verba præcedentia, sic non inconcinne exponunt hoc incisum: Sicut ros mira- bili modo ex utero auroræ, vel ex aurora quasi præ- gnanti, & hunc fœtum edente nascitur, & sub au- roram depluit, totam operiens terram, ita nascetur Messiæ ab utero Ecclesiæ modo mirabili innumera filiorum multitudo, per totam terram. Quos ipse ut filios Pater fovebit, & amplectetur, sibique æter- num servabit. Quomodo optime Lutherus: Deine Kinder werden dir gebohren, wie der Thau aus der Morgenröthe. Quod si iterum in specie referre lubeat ad tempus Ecclesiæ primitivæ, comple- mentum habebitur Act. 2, 41. cap. 4, 32. Colos. 1, 6. Ita ergo liquet, Messiæ ut Regi non tantum ad- seri Ecclesiam universam, ceu proprium ejus populum, sed & omnes fideles illius liberos es- se, quos sibi gignit spirituali & mirabili mo- do, ut merito inde Pater eorum nuncupe- tur.

Id adhuc monemus; B. Lutherum, & alios nonnullos Interpp. voces uteri auroræ de utero Ecclesiæ præcipue illius, quæ fuit initio Novi Testamenti intelligere: ut cum Christo Patre Spirituali mater Ecclesiæ designetur: utpote quæ Sponsa, & conjux Christi est. Psalm. 45. v. 10. Psalm. 68, 13. Esa. 54, 5. cap. 62, 46. Ose. 2. 16. 19. Joh. 3, 28. Ephes. 5, 26. Apoc. 19, 7. & mater fidelium, Psalm. 45, 17. Esa. 60, 4. Gal. 4, 26. Christi Weib und Braut, inquit B. Lutherus Comment. in h. l. T. 8. Germ. Witteb. fol. 578. und Königin heisset aurora, die Morgenröthe, das ist die Christliche Kirche, aus derselben Mutter oder Leib kommen ihm seine Kinder. Quo referri potest, quod Cant. 6, 9. Ecclesia N. T. progredi dicatur quasi aurora consurgens. Ut aurora a Sole, ita Ecclesia a Chri- sto splendorem accipit; Ut ex auroræ utero, seu prægnante eadem modo mirabili ros generatur: Sic Ecclesia per gratiam Dei fœcunda reddita mi- rabili modo Christo generat liberos. Joh. 1, 13. Esa. 66, 8. unde Lutherus loc. cit. Dieselbigen Kinder nennet er den Thau, darum das keine Seele wird be- kehret, und von Adams sündlicher Kindschaft, in die Gnadenreiche Kindschaft Christi verwandelt mit menschlichem Werck, sondern allein durch Würckung

Gottes vom Himmel herab, wie der Thau. Sen- fum ergo hunc reddunt: Ab utero Ecclesiae, im- primis sub initium Novi Testamenti, tanquam au- rorae, ubi post tenebras ignorantiae & peccatorum primum lux Evangelii ad gentes perveniet, genera- bitur tibi (ô Messia) ros juventutis tuae mysticae, h. e. magna multitudo liberorum spiritualium, seu re- centium Christianorum instar roris: ut ita primitiva Ecclesia N. Testam. aurora dicatur, ac similiter pri- mitivi Christiani nomine, pueritiae, vel juventutis designentur. Vide Dn. D. Christoph. Schlegelii Regium Christi Sacerdot. vel explicat. Psalm. CX. p. 192. seqq.

Haec de loco difficillimo: cujus multae aliae adhuc reperiuntur interpretationes. E Judaeis R. Moses quidem vigorem Davidis & ubertatem succi vel succositatem corporis ejus in senecta adhuc viridis ac vegeti rori comparari putat; ita reddens: ab eruptione aurorae relictus est tibi succus adolescen- tiae tuae. Aben-Ezra hanc allegat explicationem: è loco humili & nigro accepisti sortem adolescentiae tuae, quasi dicat, adolescens ex obscura conditione ad fastigium regale provectus es. Sed recte de hisce glossis Arnoldus Bootius animadvers. sacris ad text. Hebraic. Veteris Testamenti lib. II. cap. X. II. 1. Hae duae expositiones adeo coactae sunt, verbisque E- braicis tam male congruentes, imo fatuae adeo, atque insulsae, ut nullo modo mereantur, quarum mentio fiat. Nisi ut appareret, ad quam insubidas ac ridi- culas glossas commentaque doctores perfidae nationis saepe devolvantur; ubi illustrissima de Christo serva- tore nostro testimonia conantur eludere, neque claris- simae veritati oculos aperire aut manus dare volunt. Haud multo melior R. Aben-Esrae glossa, qui de Davide Psalmum accipiens ita haec reddit: Cum surgente aurora veniet (populus tuus) sicut ros, quem solebas videre in adolescentia tua, quum peco- ris pascendi curam gereres: aut R. David Kimchi, qui itidem de Davide interpretatur hoc modo; de utero prodiisti ad regnum & ros benedictionis fuit ti- bi ipso illo diluculo (cui consonat R. Jehu explica- tio;) aut Salomonis Jarchi de Abrahamo exponen- tis hoc modo; decoribus sanctis ab utero, à proje- ctione; hoc eveniet tibi merito decoris sancti, qui fuit in te à ventre matris tuae (quippè notitiam creatoris hic habuit, quum tres tantum annos natus esset) ab utero, (à projectione) ex quo recidisti ex utero: Tibi ros pueritiae tuae, hoc est, tibi imputabitur pueri- tia tua: mores probi ac virtutes, quibus te affue- visti in pueritia tua, erunt tibi recreationi, quo- modo ros recreat suavisque est. Non est autem, quod in hisce Judaeorum nugamentis refellendis immore景区. Nimis luculentum enim è Psal- mo est, non posse eundem vel de Davide vel de Abrahamo accipi, quorum neuter ad dextram DEI evectus, neuter tantae potentiae fuit, quan- ta hic celebratur, neuter sacerdotio functus est, nedum aeternum Sacerdotium habet. E Christia- nis tamen Interpp. R. Kimchi explicatio nonnul- lis probata fuit, sed ita, ut de Messia haec accepe- rint: August. Steuchus: Ex utero ex aurora tibi ros nativitatis tuae. Est autem sensus juxta plures Hebraeorum à vulva, id est, à natali & ab aurora, id est, à luce illa, qua prodiisti, fuit ros nativitatis tuae, id est, rore caeli, caelesti gratia perfusus fuisti, à die qua natus & conceptus es felici rore, ac benedi- ctione praeventus fuisti, caelestium gratiarum uber- tas in te descendit. Quo etiam abire Vatabli ex- plicationem antea diximus. Nec multum quoad sensum discrepat Mariani interpretatio : Ex utero obscuro (vel tenebricoso) tibi ros pueritiae tuae: id est, quando conceptus es in matrice virginis, qui locus nulla luce refertus solet esse obscurissimus, tibi nihilominus adfuit ros, id est, gratia divina. No- vam explicationem jactitat Arnoldus Bootius, neminemque adhuc Interpretum, saltem recen- tiorum mentem hujus oraculi, quod ad inte- grum quidem attinet, assequutum esse ait. De qua perquam operosus est lib. II. animadv. cap. VIII. lib. X. XI. XII. Tota autem interpretatio huc redit: Milites habebis voluntarios, quando colliges exercitum in arce Sionis. Quia עם no- tore milites vult: voces autem ביום חיל de die exercitus, non quo copiae in expeditionem ducuntur, ut Tigurini, Tremellius, Piscator, aut quo lustrantur, ut alii; sed quo conscribuntur cum Anglic. veteri, Gallica utraque & Agellio, Schindlero, Genebrardo & Kimchio accipit; Per voces בהדרי קדש non ornatus sanctitatis, sed locum sanctum sive sanctuarii, non quidem tem- plum, sed vel urbem Hierosolymam vel potius ar- cem Sionis intelligit: ac verba haec epexegefin praecedentium esse vult: sceptrum potentiae tuae emittet Jehovah e Sione, quasi dicat, e Sione ad bellum profectus hostes tuos omnes summa pro- speritate debellabis, iisque tibi subjugatis, poten- tiam ditionemque tuam longe ac late extendes, ut- pote validas copias ducens militemque voluntari- um, qui haudquaquam coactus aut invitus nomi- na tibi dedit, sed ultro tibi se obtulit atque ope- ram suam pollicitus est, quum bellum parans in sa- cro illo loco, arce, inquam, Sionis delectu indi- cto exercitum conscriberes. Atque ita intellectum vult prius incisum: alterum vero sic explicat & praecedenti jungit, quasi dicat: Copias adeo voluntarias habuisti, quia nunquam, ne in pri- ma quidem aetate propter humilitatem & obscurita- tem in hominum ignoratione versatus es, sed inde a prima infantia in clarissima luce egisti, & ea cir- ca te acciderunt atque in te fuerunt conspecta, quae omnium animos averterent omniumque ora nomi- nis tui celebritate implerent. Sensum ergo ver- borum posterioris incisi hunc reddit; inde a pri- mo summam claritatem habuisti ac roscida fuit in- fantia tua. Sed interpretamentum hoc Boothii, qui omnium interpretationes sub virgulam cen- soriam revocavit, censuram omnino meretur. Quod suspectum primum est ipsa sui novitate: neminem enim interpretum saltim recentiorum mentem Davidis assecutum esse censet, ab omnibus ergo recedit Interpp. recentioribus. Neminem etiam habet e veteribus, qui sic inter- pretatus sit. Porro non convenit id verbis Pro- phetae: Nomen עמ vulgata ac notissima signi- ficatione populum notare agnoscit Bootius: Cur ergo aliam dubiam minusque usitatam ei signifi- cationem inducit, praeter omnium Interpp. sen- tentiam, ut non populum, sed milites notet. Neque causa ulla redditur, cur hic intelligen- dus non sit dies, quo copiae in expeditionem ducun- tur, & praeferenda sit Kimchii explicatio, quo die exercitum conficies: aut cur non explicanda sint verba Davidis de promto subditorum Messiae obsequio, quam Riveti, Junii, Molleri, ipsius- que Calvini expositionem, cum vi vocis נדבות apprime congruere ac principalem Prophetæ scopum satis repræsentare agnoscit. Quod autem Meta- phora adhibita sit non à promta obedientia, quam regi exhibent subditi, sed à promptitudine atque a- lacritate, qua Duci exercitum colligenti nomina dant homines atque militiam sub eo appetunt susci- piuntque, sine ulla probatione asseritur. Quid quod non usque adeo analogiæ fidei consentane- um sit; imo Pelagiani quid resipiat illud de prom- titudine nomina dandi Messiæ, & ad sensum illum incautus seductus videatur Bootius à Judæis, R. Sa- lomone imprimis, qui ita reddidit: quando exer- citum colliges ad persequendos eos, sponte tibi se offe- rent populus tuus ac diligentes te. Nec vero mili- tiæ sacræ illa, quæ prolixe de allegoria militum vo- luntariorum habet Bootius, sine suspicione Pe- lagianismi applicari facile possunt. Ulterius ut הדרי קדש novum plane, ita perquam coactum hoc loco intelligere de arce Sion magnifica. Quan- quam enim Bucerus etiam splendores vel magnifi- centias sacrarii & per illas Jerusalem intelligat, ut & Vatablus in splendoribus sanctitatis, id est, in Je- rusalem urbe splendida, quibus accedit quoque Deodatus: nemo tamen arcem Sion hic per קדש designari credidit, & vocis hujus ambiguitatem fere omnes Interpp. fefellisse censet Bootius, quo minus hujus commatis sensum assequerentur. Et cur arcem Sionis hic Propheta cum isto eximio e- pitheto vocaret, decorum sanctuarium; siquidem id nihil ad ipsum delectum hic pertineat, fatente Bootio, quum summo cum delectu singulæ vo- ces in hoc Psalmo Prophetico adhibitæ sint. Tum vero quis credet hæc idem sonare, & κατ' ἐπεξήγη- σιν dicta esse, sceptrum potentiæ tuæ emittet Jehovah è Sion, & populus tuus voluntarius in die exercitus tui, in decoris sanctitatis vel sanctuarii? Præterea accentus Athnach non tantum negligitur à Bootio, sed discerpitur etiam posterius, quod autor ille constituit, hemistichium contra reliquorum In- terpp. sententiam, id enim duobus distinctis mem- bris constare, contra quam OMNES ALII hacte- nus putaverunt', qui unanimiter id habuerunt pro uno colo, Bootius affirmat: ita ut prius sit מרחם משחר לך, alterum vero טל ילדותך. Adhæc voces illas מרחם משחר in statu regi- minis plerique accipiunt & auroram intelligunt. Hic novus Interpres autem ita construit, atque exponit: à primo ortu splendor, seu claritas auro- ralis tibi: ac porro metaphorice hic sumi existi- mat pro famæ celebritate ac nominis amplitudine at- que claritudine. Ubi vero uspiam accipitur ita vox משחר in sacris? Et quomodo tanta famæ ce- lebritas ac nominis amplitudo convenit primo or- tui Messiæ, qui in paupertate natus est? Certe splendida illa, ac clarissima fama non congruit sta- tui exinanitionis, qui non fuit à primo ortu adeo clarus & illustris, nedum conspicuus ac spectabi- lis. Quem sensum hic esse vult Bootius. Jam quoad posterius membrum, juxta distinctionem Bootianam, sed non minus Ebræis Codd. quam universis Interpp. repugnantem: illud טל ילדותך hunc habere sensum, infantia tua fuit roscida, eoque significatum esse, Christum à prima infan- tia, omnibus gratiis ac dotibus floruisse, sicuti stir- pes largo rore perfusæ late virescunt atque adolescunt, unde docebitur? Quis persuaderi sibi patietur illud מרחם משחר לך quodammodo idem es- se cum טל ילדותך quod ipse pag. 262. asserit, ni- hil si forte Bœotico sub æthere natus sit? Et quomo- do illæ glossæ textui aut scopo Prophetæ congru- ent, qui de Rege Messia sedente ad dexteram DEI & præliante adversus inimicos, deque subditis ejus- dem; non autem de primo ortu aut infantia Chri- sti vaticinatus est? Ita ergo ὀδὲν ὑγιὲς in illa Do- ctoris Medici interpretatione nova: qui Luthe- rum, Anglicanam Veterem & Hispanicam versio- nem, quid? Interpretationes omnium non curan- das, sed exagitandas suscepit, parum illius Vul- gati memor: Promittunt Medici, Fabri fabrilia tractant.

Nobis redeundum est ad Grotium JCtum. In cujus translatione hæc desideramus. Primo quod diem exercitus interpretetur per diem prælii: quum tamen verbum verbo reddere videri ve- lit. Tum quod vocem קדש quæ nomen est, accipiat ut verbum vel Participium: ac nova in- terpretatione reddat præparatus, quum sanctita- tem vel sanctuarium notet, & cum vox præce- dens בהדרי in statu constructionis ponatur, red- denda necessario sit in ornatibus humilitatis. Por- ro quod illa בהדרי adverbialiter accipiat; qua- si dicat, pulcherrime. Præterea etiam, quod roris nomen semel positum bifariam explicet; ac si semel de aurora proprie sumatur & tum quo- que per translationem pro semine usurpetur: ros, id est, semen prolis tuæ erit, ut ros ab utero auro- ræ. Neque ostensum adhuc, ubi roris nomine semen intelligatur. Loco certe Cantic. 5. vers. 2. nullatenus hæc significatio convenit. Quis enim sensus foret, caput meum plenum est rore, id est, semine? Nec Esa. 25. vers. 19. roris nomine designa- tur semen. Ros lucis ros tuus. Nullus iterum sen- sus hinc emergeret: semen lucis semen tuum. Non de semine sibi sermo est, sed roris nomen semel proprie accipitur; deinde vero metaphorice, quasi dicat, sicut ros cadens super herbas (nam אורות herbas & olera virentia notat) crescere eas facit, ita ros gratiæ super ossa arida cadens ea faciet revi- vescere, ut Esa. 66. vers. 14. dicitur: Ossa vestra quasi herba germinabunt.

## 110:4
Vers. 4.

THE LORD HAS SWORN) Which He does not do, except for the sake of those whom He loves greatly. Gen. XXII, 16. AND HE WILL NOT REPENT) He will not change this decree.

These things again seem to look to this, as if this oath had been made for David’s sake, that GOD might testify His love to him. But there is nothing here about David. Nor did GOD swear for the sake of the Messiah, but for the sake of the men for whom CHRIST was to be appointed Priest, that they might be made more certain by GOD’S own oath of their salvation procured through CHRIST. Blessed Luther explains the force of the divine oath excellently, according to his custom, at this passage of Genesis, fol. 202. b. But it is a great and admirable thing which the author of the Epistle to the Hebrews also saw in this passage, and diligently weighed: that GOD swears by Himself. For it is a sign of a soul burning with ineffable love and desire for our salvation, as if He were to say, I so desire to be believed, I so vehemently seek that faith be had in My words, that I not only promise, but I pledge Myself. I have nothing greater that I may pledge, because there is nothing greater than Me: Als wahr ich GOtt bin;

If I do not keep my promises, I shall no longer be who I am. It is truly astonishing and most worthy of observation. For divine truth wishes to signify this: You, O man, are fickle, various, and changeable; I shall therefore add an immovable oath, and by it I wish to testify that, before I have deceived, I shall not be God. If He had sworn only in these words: I shall sooner allow heaven, earth, the sun, the moon, and the most beautiful workmanship of the whole world to perish than I shall suffer my promise to be made void: it would truly be a great and no less wonderful thing. But He adds another thing, far more grave and holy: I, who am GOD, who have the power of destroying or creating heaven and earth, swear and pledge, not a creature, not heaven and earth, but Myself, the creator of all things. This most holy oath will condemn all unbelievers; just as it has wonderfully excited and increased the faith of the holy Fathers. For they thought: GOD promised life, redemption from death, and from the Devil, and swore by Himself. That is our Urim and Thummim: unless, therefore, we believe, we shall be condemned. Let us also remember such a remarkable amplification of the divine promise, exceeding all thought and faith: God increases and confirms it by His own majesty, so that we may have no occasion for distrusting and doubting. That is, indeed, to condescend and to apply Himself entirely to our infirmity. It ought to have been enough if He moved a single finger to testify His fatherly benevolence toward us. But now He sets forth His word, and not only promises, but also swears, and imprecates and curses Himself, if one might speak so, in order to bless us. Whence Tertullian, in his book on repentance: Blessed are we, for whose sake God swears. But miserable are we, who do not believe even Him when He swears. There is also a beautiful observation of Blessed Luther, which he handed down concerning this passage, that God swore, not in instituting the kingdom of Christ, but the Priesthood: which seems worthy to be read here also. It is thus, however, in Tom. 8. Germ. Witteb. fol. 578. b. It is to be noted that God does not swear to institute the kingdom of Christ, but says simply (as reported above), GOD has said to my Lord. But to institute the priesthood of Christ, GOD takes an oath, and with an end confirms Christ as Priest, and adds thereto: And He will not repent. What is this? Or what need is there that God, who cannot lie, should swear, etc.? For the unspeakable sweet comfort of us poor sinful men, that we may the more boldly believe and hope that Christ is a Priest. For it is easier to believe that Christ is a Lord over all things, so that even man fears before Him, because of His great power. But that He is a Priest is difficult to believe because of our timid and sinful conscience, which despairs and easily takes fright at God's power, and with difficulty trusts that its sins are forgiven. God raises up this timid despair and makes it comforting toward His mercy, in that He proclaims Christ a Priest, that is, a patron, intercessor, mediator, payer of all sins, and that with swearing, proclaiming His mercy with greater diligence than His power, so that He may raise more confidence than fear in man. Therefore, one should cover this verse with gold and precious stones, because it sounds so precious and gracious.

YOU ARE A PRIEST FOREVER) Or minister, as we said before, the Chaldean, Lord of the future age.

It is helpful to transcribe here also the previous passage which he designates: For he refers without doubt to those things which he had annotated on Psalm 99, verse 6: MOSES AND AARON AMONG HIS PRIESTS. Among his ministers, for the word כהן is very general, even if for the most part it is used by a certain antonomasia for Priests. See 2 Sam. 8, verse 19. These are the words of Grotius there. Whence it is clear that the word priest is here taken generally by the same man, for a minister. Without doubt, in order to gratify the Jews, who understand the words as being about David. For if he understood it about Melchizedek, with the Epistle to the Hebrews; why would he not take the word as meaning Priest, since it is undoubted that Melchizedek was a Priest. But R. Abraham follows, who likewise contends that this word in this place denotes a minister: with whom he also explains those words, sit at my right hand: trust in my patronage: that gloss, therefore, as it is purely Jewish, so it is not difficult to refute from the text; because the discourse is about such a כהן as Melchizedek was, but this is diametrically opposed and contrary to the Apostolic interpretation and demonstration in the Epistle to the Hebrews. For it teaches that the discourse here is solely about Christ, and that His Priesthood is indicated, and the perpetuity and eternity of Christ's Priesthood is described; indeed, from this Psalm it proves apodictically the excellence of the Messianic Priesthood over the Aaronic. How, therefore, could this Psalm treat only generally of a minister? Although it has not yet been proven that the word כהן generally denotes a minister. It can be said that it properly denotes the same as priest; and it is not used of other persons except figuratively, namely because of similarity, and by metaphor; hence, since the priesthood is a most honorable office, political ministers are metaphorically designated by this name, as the Potipharite in Genesis 41, verse 45, who in the Targum is called רבא, Prince. And so also in Exodus 2, verse 16, and chapter 3, verse 1, the Chaldean expresses Jethro as Prince in Midian. The LXX interpreters call the sons of David in 2 Sam. 8, verse 18, aularchs: in the parallel passage, 1 Paralipomenon 18, verse 17, they are called the first at the hand of the King, or the foremost among the Counselors, and are distinguished from the priests Sadock and Abimelech. That passage in Psalm 99, verse 6, can be rendered thus: Moses and Aaron with His priests; as Junius, Tremellius, and others have rendered it: or among His priests: not that Moses was also a priest, but that with Aaron among the priests, he devoted himself to the praise of God. And therefore we must here adhere to the propriety of the word, which imports Priesthood. For it is not permitted to depart from propriety without cause: and that Melchizedek was properly a Priest is clearer than the midday sun, both in Genesis 14 and from the Epistle to the Hebrews. Whence Enjedinus himself, a most crafty artificer of twisting Scripture, acknowledged above that the word כהן cannot here be understood otherwise than of a Priest: because the author of the Epistle to the Hebrews affirms that a Priest is denoted by it, and that author builds and confirms the Pontificate and eternal Priesthood of JESUS CHRIST, especially from this passage. Although he himself slips into another absurd opinion: namely, that David was a Priest, even though he did not have a mandate for his Priesthood, which fabrication is unworthy of refutation. But it is necessary for those who do not hesitate to oppose the Holy Spirit to turn themselves into all shapes in this way.

ACCORDING TO THE ORDER OF MELCHIZEDEK) That is, after the manner of Melchizedek. The LXX: κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ. Just as the divine Writer also does in Hebrews 5, 6, 10; chapter 6, 20; 7, 11, 17, 21. From which it appears that these Interpreters read עַל־דִּבְרָתִי . עַל־דִּבְרַת Our Hebrew text has מַלְכִּי־צֶדֶק. According to my constitution, O my just King. See Proverbs 29, 14.

These things again clearly teach that Grotius is here pandering to the Jews, and interprets it concerning David and the establishing of his throne forever, which the Holy Spirit interprets concerning the eternal Priesthood of Christ, and which cannot be understood otherwise according to the letter. For to what end does Grotius otherwise interpret the Hebrew thus, 'according to my constitution, O my just King,' unless so that it might be taken concerning David, whom he knew not to have been a Priest according to the order of Melchizedek? Nor for any other end does he allege that of Solomon, Proverbs 29, verse 14: 'A King judgeth the poor in truth, his throne shall be established forever.' Doubtless, with the Chaldean, he understands these things, and the preceding ones, concerning David, in a similar manner explaining the name Melchizedek appellatively, and taking the name כהן generally: For thus the Chaldean paraphrast: Thou (David) art appointed Prince (or great) in the future age: Because of justice, because thou wast a just or innocent King. He also follows R. David Kimchi, explaining it thus: Thou art King and Prince forever: and why did I choose such a one, for the reason that thou art a just King, as it is written concerning him (2 Sam. 8, 15): And David executed judgment and justice unto all the people. Furthermore, it is asserted only rashly here that the Hebrew text formerly had it otherwise; for while our reading remains, the words are correctly rendered as to sense, 'according to the order of Melchizedek.' Some explain עַל־דִּבְרָתִי with Arias Montanus as 'upon my word'; by which pact it is hinted that the Messiah was made a priest according to the (peculiar) word of the Lord, and that מלכי־צדק can be applied by subaudition of the particle of comparison AS Melchizedek, which Aben-Ezra subaudits here, whence the sense will emerge: Thou art a Priest forever according to or upon my word: or as Grotius has it, 'according to my constitution AS MELCHIZEDEK.' And by this pact the Greek κατὰ τὴν τάξιν, and the Latin 'according to the order of Melchizedek,' will agree very well as to the meaning, even if the words are not rendered word for word. The preposition 'OF' can also be subaudited in the same sense: 'according to my word,' or 'according to my constitution OF Melchizedek,' i.e., just as I constituted concerning Melchizedek, that he should be a Priest in a peculiar way out of the order, so also thou, O Messiah, art a Priest not according to the Levitical order, but constituted by me in a peculiar way after the manner of Melchizedek. Francis Junius subaudits that preposition, but explains the words differently in his analysis of Genesis chapter 14, Vol. 1, col. 175: ACCORDING TO MY NARRATION concerning Melchizedek: or κατὰ τάξιν, that is, as the narration was ordered by Moses. But that explanation seems more foreign. Furthermore, there is no need for the Yod suffix in the word דברתי to be taken as a pronoun, since it can be said to be a paragogic Yod, as is not rarely the case elsewhere, and that the Rebhia accent here lacks the function of distinguishing, as Buxtorff observes in his Thesaurus Grammaticus, page 858, that it very often does not distinguish. Which the Rabbis themselves admit here. R. Kimchi says, the Yod is redundant in מלכי and דברתי. R. Aben-Ezra: The Yod is redundant, דברתי but that word denotes not only a word, but also τάξιν, order and rite, and thus the Greek version agrees entirely: according to the order

of Melchizedek. From which R. Aben-Ezra's explanation is not foreign: על מנהג according to the rite or custom: nor does the Syriac translation of Heb. 5, 6, 10; chapter 6, 20, depart much: כדמותה according to the likeness. For the Hebrew word also denotes manner or condition, Eccles. 3, 18, just as the Greek word τάξις is also used in 2 Maccabees 9, 18. And the Apostle himself explained that κατὰ τάξιν thus in Heb. 7, 15: κατὰ τὴν ὁμοιότητα according to the likeness: and likewise Grotius also in this place: AFTER the manner of Melchizedek, whence Melchizedek is also said to be ἀφωμοιωμέν@ made like unto the Son of God, Heb. 7, 3. Grotian's own interpretation of the Hebrew word can also be reduced to this: According to the constitution. For what else is hinted by these words, 'according to the order of Melchizedek,' than that the Priesthood of the Messiah consists of a certain order, a certain law divinely prescribed, a certain condition, series, and constitution, as Mollerus explains, which also obtained in the Melchizedekian one. Grotius acknowledged this agreement of our Greek and Hebrew Codices in his annotations on chapter 5 of the Epistle to the Hebrews, 5, 5. In the Hebrew, he says, that κατὰ τὴν τάξιν is על-דברתי, which below in 7, 15 is well brought out according to the sense as κατὰ τὴν ὁμοιότητα. In the Syriac כדמותה, that is, after the manner of; דברה is condition or manner, as in Eccles. 3, 18. Thus τάξις is taken in 2 Maccabees 9, 18. It is not a bad Greek word: for the Greeks say ἐν τάξει ἔχειν γαμετῆς, ἐν ἐχθρᾶ τάξει, τάξιν ἔχειν τελετῆς, τάξιν νόμκ, and the like: which signify that this is after the manner of another thing: after the manner of Melchizedek, that is, in the most august manner, by which they joined both kingdom and Priesthood, as before the law of Moses. These things are consistent with the explanation of the Holy Spirit and the common opinion of Christians; and they teach that this text is to be taken concerning the Messiah, which the annotations on chapter 7, 17 also testify: He presses, he says, that word לעולם which elsewhere indeed signifies a long time, but here eternity: for who can be the Lord of David, unless he who is heavenly, and therefore eternal? These things Grotius there. But here it pleased Grotius to Judaize.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

JVRAVIT DOMINVS) Quod non facit, nisi eorum causa, quos valde amat. Gen. XXII, 16. ET NON POENITEBIT EVM) Non mutabit hoc decretum.

Hæc iterum videntur eo respicere, quasi Da- vidis causa, ut ipsi amorem suum testaretur DE- US, hoc juramentum factum esset. At de Da- vide hic nihil habetur. Neque Messiæ gratia ju- ravit DEUS, sed hominum, pro quibus CHRI- STUS Sacerdos constituendus erat, causa, ut il- li ipsius DEI jurejurando certiores redderentur de salute sua per CHRISTUM procurata. Præ- clare vim juramenti divini explicat pro more suo B. Luther. ad hunc locum Genes. fol. 202. b. Ma- gnum autem & admirandum est, quod & author Epistolæ ad Hebræos hoc loco vidit, & diligenter expendit: quod DEUS per semetipsum jurat. Est enim significatio ardentis animi ineffabili amore & desiderio nostræ salutis, quasi dicat, tam cupio mi- hi credi, tam vehementer expeto meis verbis fidem haberi, ut non solum promittam, sed meipsum pigno- ri apponam. Non habeo majus quod oppignorem, quia me majus nihil est: Als wahr ich GOtt bin;

Si non servo promissa, non ero amplius qui sum. Stu- pendum profecto est, & dignissimum observatione. Hoc enim vult significare divina veritas: Tu ho- mo mobilis, varius, & mutabilis es, addam igitur immobile jusjurandum, & eo testatum volo, me priusquam fefellero, non fore Deum. Si in hec tantum verba jurasset: prius cœlum, terram, solem, lunam & pulcherrimum opificium totius mundi sinam interire, quam meam promissionem irritam fieri patiar: magnum profecto, & non minus miran- dum esset. Sed addit aliud longe gravius & san- ctius: Ego, qui DEUS sum, qui habeo potestatem destruendi, aut creandi cœlum & terram, juro & oppignoro, non creaturam, non cœlum & ter- ram, sed meipsum creatorem omnium rerum. Hoc tam sanctum jusjurandum damnabit omnes in- credulos; sicut sanctorum Patrum fidem mirabiliter excitavit & auxit. Cogitaverunt enim: DEUS promisit vitam, redemtionem a morte, & Diabo- lo, & per semetipsum juravit. Id nostrum Urim & Thummim est: nisi itaque crediderimus, damna- bimur. Meminerimus ergo & nos tam insignem amplificationem promissionis divinæ, exuperantem omnem cogitationem, & fidem: auget eam & confir- mat Deus per suam majestatem, ne ullam occasionem diffidendi & dubitandi habeamus. Illud nimirum est condescendere, seque totum applicare nostræ infir- mitati. Satis esse debebat, si unicum digitum move- ret ad testificandam suam paternam benevolentiam erga nos. Jam vero verbum suum proponit, nec pro- mittit solum, sed & jurat, & sibi ipsi imprecatur & maledicit, si liceret ita loqui, ut nobis benedicat. Un- de Tertull. lib. de pœnit Beatos nos, quorum causa jurat Deus. Sed miseros nos, qui ne juranti quidem credimus. Pulchra etiam est observatio B. Luthe- ri, quam tradidit de hoc loco, quod juravit Deus, non in instituendo regno Christi, sed Sacerdotio: quæ digna videtur, ut hic quoque legatur. Sic au- tem habet Tom. 8. Germ. Witteb. fol. 578. b. Als ist zu mercken, daß zu dem Königreich Christi einzu- setzen GOtt nicht schweret, sondern schlecht sagt, (als oben bericht) GOTT hat gesagt zu meinem HErrn. Aber einzusetzen das Priesterthum Chri- sti, thut GOTT einen Schwur, und mit einem Ende bestetiget Er Christum zum Priester, und setzet dennoch dazu: Und wird ihn nicht ge= reuen. Was ist das? Oder was ist noth, daß GOtt schweret, der nicht lügen kan ꝛc. Zu unaussprechli- chem süssen Trost uns armen sündigen Menschen, daß wir desto kecklicher gläuben und hoffen, daß Chri- stus ein Priester sey. Denn leichter ist zu glauben, daß Christus ein HErr sey über alle Dinge, daß auch der Mensch sich fürchte für ihm, um seiner grossen Gewalt willen. Aber daß Er ein Priester sey, ist schwerlich zu glauben um unsers blöden und sündli- chen Gewissens halben, das da verzagt, und leichtlich erschricket für GOttes Gewalt, und schwerlich ver- trauet, daß ihm seine Sünde vergeben seyn. Diese blöde Verzagung richtet GOtt auf, und machet sie tröstlich zu seiner Barmhertzigkeit, in dem, daß er Christum einen Priester ausschreyeet, das ist, einen Patron, Fürbitter, Mittler, Bezahler aller Sün- de, und das mit Schweren, mit grösserm Fleiß seine Barmhertzigkeit verkündigend, denn seine Gewalt, auf daß Er mehr Zuversicht denn Furcht in dem Menschen erhebe. Darum soll man diesen Vers mit Gold und Edelgestein belegen, daß er so köstlich und gnädig klinget.

TV ES SACERDOS IN ÆTERNUM) Aut minister, ut ante diximus Chaldæus, Dominus futuri sæculi.

Locum anteriorem, quem designat, hic eti- am adscribere juvat : Respicit enim sine dubio ea, quæ ad Psalm. XCIX. vers. 6. annotarat: MOSES ET AARON IN SACERDOTIBUS EJUS. Inter ministros ejus, nam vox כהן valde generalis est, etsi plerumque per ἀντονομασίαν quan- dam de Sacerdotibus usurpatur. Vid. 2. Sam. 8. vers. 19. Hæc ibi Grotius. Unde liquet, vocem Sacerdotis hic generaliter accipi ab eodem, pro mi- nistro. Sine dubio, ut Judæis gratificetur, qui de Davide verba intelligunt. Nam si de Melchi- sedecho intelligeret, cum Epistola ad Ebræos; Cur non de Sacerdote vocem acciperet, siquidem Melchisedechum Sacerdotem fuisse indubium sit. Sequitur autem R. Abraham, qui pariter vocem hanc h. l. notare ministrum contendit : cum quo etiam verba illa sede ad dextram meam, exponit: confide in patrocinio meo : Glossa ergo illa uti me- re Judaica est, ita è textu haud difficulter re- fellitur; quia de tali כהן sermo est, qualis fuit Melchisedech, at hæc interpretationi atque de- monstrationi Apostolicæ in Epist. ad Ebræos è diametro adversa est & contraria. Hæc enim de Christo hic unice sermonem esse, & Sacer- dotium indigitari ejusdem, ac Sacerdotii Chri- sti perpetuitatem ac æternitatem describi docet, imo ex hoc Psalmo apodictice probat ἐξοχὴν Sa- cerdotii Messiani præ Aaronico. Qui ergo Psalmus hic generatim tantum de ministro age- ret ? Quanquam neque id adhuc probatum sit, vocem כהן generatim notare ministerium. Dici potest, proprie eandem Sacerdotem notare; nec nisi translalitie de aliis personis, ob similitudi- nem nempe, ac per metaphoram adhiberi; hinc cum Sacerdotium officium sit maxime honorabi- le, ministros politicos digniores metaphorice isto nomine designari, ut Potiphareus Genes. 41. vers. 45. qui in Thargum רבא Princeps vocatur. Atque ita etiam Exod. 2. vers. 16. cap. 3. vers. 1. exprimit Chald. Jethro Principem in Midian. Filios Davidis 2. Sam. 8. vers. 18. LXX. Interpp. vocant ἀυλάρχας: in loco parallel. 1. Paralip. 18. vers. 17. dicuntur primi ad manum Regis, vel pri- mores inter Consiliarios, & distinguuntur à Sacerdotibus Sadock & Abimelech. Illud Psalm. 99. vers. 6. sic reddi potest : Moses & Aaron cum Sacerdotibus ejus; uti Junius, Tremellius & alii reddidere: vel inter Sacerdotes ejus: non quod Moses etiam Sacerdos, sed quod cum Aarone inter Sacerdotes, laudi Dei vacarit. Ideoque proprietati vocis hic adhærendum, quæ Sacerdo- tium importat. Non enim extra causam à pro- prietate discedere licet: & proprie Sacerdotem fuisse Melchisedecum tum Genes. 14. tum ex Epi- stola ad Ebr. luce meridiana clarius est. Un- de agnovit supra Enjedinus ipse, vaferrimus ar- tifex detorquendi Scripturam; non posse hic vo- cem כהן aliter quam de Sacerdote intelligi: quia auctor Epistolæ ad Hebræos Sacerdotem ea denotari affirmat, & JESU CHRISTI Pontificatum, & Sacerdotium æternum, præsertim ex hoc loco auctor ille extruit & confirmat. Quamvis ad aliam ab- surdam opinionem ipse prolabatur : Davidem nempe Sacerdotem fuisse, etsi non habuerit manda- tum sui Sacerdotii, quod commentum refutatione indignum est. Sed ita in omnes se convertere formas oportet, qui Spiritui Sancto se opponere non dubitant.

SECUNDUM ORDINEM MELCHISEDECH) Id est, ad instar Melchisedeci. LXX. κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ. Quomodo & divinus Scriptor ad Hebræos 5, 6, 10. cap. 6, 20. 7, 11. 17, 21. Ex quibus apparet legisse hos Interpp. עַל־דִּבְרָתִי . עַל־דִּבְרַת Noster textus Hebr. habet מַלְכִּי־צֶדֶק. Secundum meam constitutionem o Rex mi juste. Vid. Proverb. 29, 14.

Hæc iterum luculenter docent, velificari hîc Grotium Judæis, & de Davide ejusque throno in perpetuum firmando accipere, quod de Christi æterno Sacerdotio S. S. interpretatur, nec aliter secundum literam intelligi potest. Quo enim fi- ne alias Ebræa ita interpretatur Grotius, secun- dum meam constitutionem ô Rex mi juste, nisi ut de Davide id accipi queat, quem norat non fuisse Sacerdotem secundum ordinem Melchisedech. Ne- que alio fine allegat illa Salomonis Proverb. 29. vers. 14. Rex judicat in veritate pauperes, thronus ejus in æternum firmabitur. Nimirum cum Chal- dæo intelligit hæc, & præcedentia de Davide, pa- rili modo appellative nomen Melchisedech expli- cans, nomenque כהן generaliter accipiens: Sic enim paraphrastes Chaldæus: Tu (David) consti- tutus es Princeps (vel magnus) in futuro seculo: Pro- pter justitiam, quia fuisti Rex justus seu innocens. Sequitur etiam R. David Kimchium, ita expli- cantem: Tu es Rex & Princeps in seculum: & quare talem de elegi, propterea quod Rex justus es, sicut scriptum est de eo (2. Sam. 8, 15.) Et faciebat David judicium & justitiam omni populo. Cæterum non nisi temere hîc asseritur, aliter quondam tex- tum Ebræum habuisse; nam manente nostra lectio- ne verba quoad sensum recte redduntur, secun- dum ordinem Melchisedech. Nonnulli עַל־דִּבְרָתִי exponunt cum Ariæmontano super verbum meum; quo pacto innuitur Messiam secundum verbum Do- mini (peculiare) sacerdotem factum, atque illud מלכי־צדק applicari poterit, subintelligendo vo- culam comparationis SICUT Melchisedech, quam Aben-Ezra hîc subintelligit, unde sensus pro- dibit: Tu es Sacerdos in æternum secundum vel super verbum meum: vel prout habet Grotius, secun- dum meam constitutionem SICUT MELCHISE- DECH. Atque hoc pacto Græcum κατὰ τὴν τά- ξιν, & Latinum secundum ordinem Melchisedech, qua sententiam, optime congruet, utut non red- dantur verba κατὰ πόδα. Subintelligi etiam potest sensu eodem, præpositio DE: secundum verbum meum, vel secundum constitutionem meam DE Melchisedeco, q. d. quemadmodum ego de Mel- chisedeco constitui, ut extra ordinem peculiariter Sa- cerdos esset, ita etiam tu Messia Sacerdos es non se- cundum ordinem Leviticum, sed peculiari modo ad Melchisedeci instar à me constitutus. Subintelligit illam præpositionem Franc. Junius, sed aliter ver- ba exponit in analysi Genes. cap. 14. Tom. 1. col. 175. SECUNDUM NARRATIONEM MEAM de Melchisedeco: sive κατὰ τάξιν, id est, prout narratio fuit à Mose ordinata. Sed illa explica- tio alienior videtur. Porro non opus est, ut Jod suffixum in voce דברתי, accipiatur tanquam pro- nomen, quum dici possit esse Jod paragogicum, uti non raro alias, & accentum Rebhia hîc care- re officio distinguendi, utpote quem sæpissime non distinguere, observat Buxtorff. in Thes. Grammat. pag. 858. Quod admittunt hîc ipsimet Rabbini. R. Kimchi, Jod inquit, redundat in מלכי, & דברתי. R. Aben-Ezra: Jod redundat, דברתי vox autem illa non tantum verbum notat, sed etiam τάξιν, ordinem & ritum, atque ita congruit prorsus Græca versio: secundum ordinem

Melchisedech. A qua aliena non est R. Aben-Ezra explicatio: על מנהג secundum ritum seu consuetudinem: neque multum abit Syra translatio Ebr. 5, 6. 10. cap. 6, 20. כדמותה secundum similitudinem. Nam Ebræa vox notat etiam modum vel conditionem Eccles. 3, 18. uti quoque Græca vox τάξις usurpatur 2. Maccab. 9, 18. Et Apostolus ipse sic exposuit illud κατὰ τάξιν Ebr. 7, 15. κατὰ τὴν ὁμοιότητα juxta similitudinem: nec non Grotius quoque hoc loco AD instar Melchisedech, unde & Melchisedech dicitur ἀφωμοιωμέν@ assimilatus Filio Dei Ebr. 7, 3. Reduci huc quoque potest ipsa Grotiana vocis Ebrææ interpretatio: Secundum constitutionem. Quid enim aliud innuitur his verbis, secundum ordinem Mechisedeci, quam quod Sacerdotium Messiæ constet certo ordine, certa lege divinitus præscripta, certa conditione, serie & constitutione, uti exponit Mollerus, quæ in Melchisedeciano quoque obtinuit. Agnovit hanc Græcorum Ebræorumque nostrorum Codicum consonantiam Grotius in annotatis ad cap. 5. Epist. ad Hebr. 5, 5. In Hebræo, inquit, illud κατὰ τὴν τάξιν על-דברתי, quod infra 7, 15. bene ad sensum effertur κατὰ τὴν ὁμοιότητα. In Syriaco כדמותה, id est, ad modum דברה conditio aut modus, ut Eccles. 3, 18. Sic τάξις sumitur 2. Maccab. 9, 18. Est vox non male Græca: dicunt enim Græci ἐν τάξει ἔχειν γαμετῆς, ἐν ἐχθρᾶ τάξει, τάξιν ἔχειν τελετῆς, τάξιν νόμκ, & similia: quæ significant, hoc esse instar rei alterius: ad modum Melchisedeci, id est, modo augustissimo, quo regnum simul & Sacerdotium jungebant, ut ante legem Mosis. Hæc Spiritus Sancti explicationi, ac Christianorum communi sententiæ congrua sunt; ac textum hunc de Messia accipiendum esse docent, quod etiam annotata ad cap. 7, 17. testantur: Premit, inquit, illam vocem לעולם quæ alibi quidem longum tempus significat, at hic æternitatem: quis enim potest esse Dominus Davidis, nisi qui sit cælestis, ac proinde æternus? Hæc ibi Grotius. Hic vero placuit Grotio ἰυδαΐζειν.

## 110:5
Vers. 5.

THE LORD AT THY RIGHT HAND) He is a helper to thee, and as it were a παραστάτης (supporter). Thus above 16, 8, and elsewhere. HE HATH STRUCK THROUGH KINGS IN THE DAY OF HIS WRATH) That is, he will strike through: as he did in Genesis 14, Exodus 14, Numbers 21, Joshua 8, ch. 10, and 12, Judges 3, 1 Sam. 15, 2 Sam. 8.

Some indeed understand by the Lord at the right hand God the Father, and think that the prayer here is still directed to Him, whom he had addressed in the preceding verse; which is the opinion of certain ancients, Jerome, Chrysostom, Arnobius, as well as of certain recent Papists, Stapulensis, Jansenius, Saa, Maldonatus, Tirinus; likewise of the Calvinists Aretius, Felinus, Pelicanus, Musculus, and Rivetus: and also of our own Osiander, and several others. But it appears from the text that by that Lord the Messiah is to be understood, so that the prayer is now directed to God the Father, as to whose right hand the Messiah sits: The Lord, who is or sits at your right hand, which is the explanation of St. Augustine, the Venerable Bede, Remigius of Auxerre, Anselm of Laon in the interlinear Gloss, Strabo of Fulda in the ordinary Gloss, Pelbart of Temesvár in his Commentary: Lyranus in his Postilla, Michael Ayguanus, Thomas. Cajetan, Bellarmine, Menochius: likewise of Junius and Tremellius, the authors of the Belgian notes in the latest Bibles, and of our own B. Bugenhagius, B. Tarnovius, the Weimar Paraphrasts, the blessed Lord D. Dorscheus, D. Schlegelius in his explanation of the King Christ as Priest, or Psalm 110, and others.

Although the aforementioned Belgian authors also interpret this passage about Christ in such a way, along with Moller and Piscator, that they wish the prayer to be directed to the Church; 'The Lord at your right hand,' here is he who is your helper and protector. That Christ is to be understood here by 'the Lord' is proven by the cohesion with the preceding verses: because kings will oppose the eternal Priest in vain, whom he himself, sitting at the right hand of the Lord, will easily overthrow: Then, especially, from the consequences. For he will crush kings in the day of his wrath, he will exercise judgment among the nations, and what follows further sounds of the Messiah or the Lord sitting at the right hand of God, and, as even the patrons of the other opinion admit, are attributed to Christ, to whom God has given all judgment, of whom David says in Psalm 2:12: 'Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and you perish from the way.' Most understand this as the universal judgment, which Christ will execute, to whom that execution is everywhere peculiarly attributed: who also pierces the head over much land, crushing the very head of the infernal serpent, Genesis 3:15. Grotius paraphrases it thus: 'He will break the head over much land: that is, some prince reigning widely, such as the Devil is preeminently, ὁ ἄρχων τῶ κόσμꙋ τότε (the ruler of this world).' Let the blessed Dn. Glassius be consulted, Christolog. David. Disp. 5. 25. The blessed Joh. Tarnovius urges that the Hebrew words ought to be translated: 'He crushed the head over much land,' which head over much land is the prince of the world, the Devil. Finally, this sense concerning Christ the Lord is most clearly confirmed from the last verse, as it deals with the same subject, which is said to be at the right hand and to judge among the nations: nor is it to be understood of any other than Christ. For he drinks from the brook in the way, and has lifted up his head, of which we shall now speak. The Jews indeed snatch it away even to God the Father, but almost all Christians understand it of the Lord of David. Grotius himself interprets it of Christ, as now follows.

Latin:

Vers. 5.

DOMINVS A DEXTRIS TVIS) Adjutor tibi est, & velut παραστάτης. Ita supra 16, 8. & alibi. CONFREGIT IN DIE IRÆ SVÆ REGES) Id est, confringet: ut fecit Genes. 14. Exod. 14. Num. 21. Jos. 8. c. 10. & 12. Jud. 3. 1. Sam. 15. 2. Sam. 8.

Intelligunt quidem nonnulli per Dominum à dextris Deum Patrem, ac orationem hic dirigi adhuc ad Eum, quem compellarat versu præcedenti, arbitrantur; quæ est sententia cum veterum quorundam Hieronymi, Chrysostomi, Arnobii, tum è recentioribus Pontificiorum quorundam Stapulensis, Jansenii, Saa, Maldonati, Tirini; Calvinianorum item Aretii, Felini, Pelicani, Musculi & Riveti: nec non è nostris Osiandri, & aliorum nonnullorum. Cæterum è textu apparet per Dominum illum intelligendum esse Messiam, ut oratio nunc ad Deum Patrem dirigatur, utpote ad cujus dextram Messias sedet: Dominus, qui est vel sedet à dextris tuis, quæ S. Augustini, Venerabilis Bedæ, Remigii Antisiodorensis, Anshelmi Laudunensis in Glossa interlin. Strabonis Fuldensis in Glossa ordinaria, Pelbarti de Themesuar in Commentario: Lyrani in Postill. Mich. Ayguani, Thom. Cajetani, Bellarmini, Menochii: Junii item & Tremellii, Autorum notarum Belgicarum in Bibliis novissimis, & è nostris B. Bugenhagii, B. Tarnovii, Vinarientium Paraphrastarum, B. Dn. D. Dorschei, D. Schlegelii in Regis Christi Sacerdot. seu Psalm. 110. explicat. & aliorum est explicatio;

quanquam autores prædicti Belgici de Christo eti- am ita cum Mollero & Piscatore accipiant, ut ora- tionem ad Ecclesiam dirigi velint; Dominus à dex- tris tuis, hic qui opitulator & protector tuus est. Quod autem per Dominum hic intelligendus sit Christus, probatur è cohæsione cum præcedenti- bus: quia æterno Sacerdoti nequicquam Reges se opponent, quos ipse à dextris Domini se- dens facile evertet: Tum imprimis è consequen- tibus. Nam ille confringet in die iræ suæ Reges, judicium exercebit in gentibus, & quæ porro ad- duntur, de Messia vel Domino sedente ad dex- tram Dei sonant, ac fatentibus etiam alterius sen- tentiæ patronis, Christo, cui dedit Deus omne judicium, tribuuntur, de quo David Psalm. 2, 12. Osculamini Filium, ne irascatur, & pereatis de via. Judicium universale plerique intelligunt, quod exequetur Christus, cui peculiariter ea exequutio passim tribuitur: qui etiam caput su- per terram multam transfigit, caput ipsum serpen- tis infernalis conterens Genes. 3, 15. Grotius ita παραφράζει: Franget caput super terram multam: id est, principem aliquem late regnantem qualis exi- mie est Diabolus, ὁ ἄρχων τῶ κόσμꙋ τότε. Conse- ratur B. Dn. Glassius, Christolog. David. Disp. 5. 25. B. Joh. Tarnovius urget, quod Ebræa verti de- beant: Confregit caput super terram multam, quod caput super terram multam princeps mundi est, Diabolus. Denique luculentissime confirmatur hic sensus de Christo Domino è versu ultimo, utpote qui de eodem subjecto agit, quod à dex- tris esse, ac judicare in gentibus dicitur: neque de alio quam de Christo accipiendus est. Hic enim de torrente in via bibit, & exaltavit caput, de quo nunc dicemus. Judæi quidem id abri- piunt etiam ad Deum Patrem, sed Christiani plerique omnes de Domino Davidis intelligunt. Grotius interpretatur ipse de Christo, uti jam se- quitur.

## 110:6
Verse 6.

HE WILL JUDGE AMONG THE NATIONS) That is, he will exercise vengeance upon the nations. For thus דון is often taken among the Hebrews.

HE WILL FILL WITH RUIN: HE WILL SHATTER HEADS IN THE LAND OF MANY) Because in the Greek it is πτώματα (corpses), he translates it as ruin, although the Hebrew text has גְוִיּוֹת (corpses), which are themselves also πτώματα to the Greeks. He will fill with corpses, that is, he will make a huge heap of them. He will shatter, in Hebrew מָחַץ, in Greek συνθλάσει. He will break the head over much land. That is, some prince reigning widely, such as the devil is preeminently, ὁ ἄρχων τῶ κόσμꙋ τότε (the ruler of this world).

Latin:

Vers. 6.

JVDICABIT IN NATIONIBVS) Id est, vin- dictam in gentes exercebit. Ita enim sæpe sumitur דון apud Hebræos.

IMPLEBIT RVINA: CONQVASSABIT CAPITA IN TERRA MVLTORVM) Quia in Græco est πτώματα, ideo ruina vertit, cum Hebræus textus habeat גְוִיּוֹת ca- davera, quæ & ipsa Græcis πτώματα. Implebit cadavera, id est, ingentem eorum cumulum faciet. Conquassabit, in He- bræo מָחַץ, in Græco συνθλάσει. Franget caput super terram multam. Id est, principem aliquem late regnantem, qualis eximie est diabolus, ὁ ἄρχων τῶ κόσμꙋ τότε.

## 110:7
Verse 7.

HE WILL DRINK FROM THE BROOK IN THE WAY) A description of a brisk warrior, who, while he pursues his enemies, does not seek inns or taverns to refresh himself with wine, but is content with water, which he takes incidentally and hastily from whatever he finds, not just a river, but even a brook. Thus Christ omitted no time in which he could destroy the works of the Devil.

I affirm that what Grotius admits here—that these things concern Christ—whence it is clear that the other predicates are also to be understood of Christ: since all things look to one subject, and thus Christ is that Lord at the right hand, who crushes kings, judges among the nations, fills with corpses, breaks the head over much land, and drinking from the brook in the way, lifts up his head. But as for the interpretation of this phrase, it is explained in various ways. We omit the inept explanation of the Franciscan monk, Michael Menot, in Rivet on this passage, and another by Vitalis Luceolius, which Lorinus himself rejects as harsh. Although, however, it pleased some interpreters that interpretation concerning the brisk persecution of enemies, Vatablus and Tremellius, and Junius, which Grotius made his own here; others, however, with Bucer, Münster, Tirinus, Mariana, and Jansenius, explain it rather as the copious shedding of hostile blood, which is to flow like a torrent, so that Christ the victor may be able to drink it and satiate himself with hostile blood. But most explain it as the emptying of Christ: of whom some think that the meagerness of food and the poverty of Christ are designated, because he drank even the water of a brook he encountered, with Justin, Basil the Great, Chrysostom, and the Greek Scholia. The rest, however, say that the torments of his passion are expressed here, with Jerome, Eusebius, Arnobius, Euthymius, and the Interlinear and Ordinary Gloss; which is the exegesis of our theologians, of most Pontificals, and of Rivet among the Calvinists, to be preferred above all others. For a torrent is used to express horrendous tortures and miseries, Isaiah 30:33, Jeremiah 47:2, Psalm 124:4, whence the torrents of Belial in Psalm 18:5, following, are joined with the cords of hell: just as it is very well known that calamities and punishments are described everywhere by waters flooding, entering, and absorbing the soul, even when the discourse is about Christ, as in Psalm 69:2, 15, 16, and drinking is accustomed to be used for the sense of divine wrath and divine passions, Job 21:2, chapter 34:7, Psalm 75:9, Isaiah 51:17, Jeremiah 25:15, chapter 40:12, chapter 51:7, Ezekiel 23:32, Revelation 12:10, in which manner also the passion of Christ and his sense of it is described, Matthew 20:22, chapter 26:42, Mark 10:38, 39, John 18:11. But Christ is said here not to drink from a cup, which is found concerning other men in Psalm 75:9, Matthew 22:20, and elsewhere, by which a measured potion is noted, but from a torrent, so that the gravity and abundance of the passions might be expressed, if indeed, as if immersed in a rapid torrent, nay, in the very torrents of Belial, of the Devil and of impious men, he was about to drink, being about to be subjected to infernal punishments, concerning which he complains at length in Psalm 49:1, following. Which had to happen in the way of his life and office, in the way to glory, Luke 24:26, 1 Peter 1:2. These things are excellently illustrated by what the blessed Gerhard has in his Harmon. Evang. on the passion of Christ, chapter 2, page 24: 'The heavenly Father had offered to his Son a cup, nay, a torrent of his wrath for the sins of the whole human race, which were imposed upon Christ, otherwise owed by them. This certainly was a most bitter and most sharp potion.' To his other children he measures out the cup of passions by a certain measure, Psalm 75:9: 'A cup in the hand of the Lord is full of pure wine': in which respect the passions of the saints are likewise compared to a cup. For just as formerly a measured portion was offered to each guest, so God proposes to each of his children a certain measure of cross and affliction, but to Christ the dregs of divine wrath are proposed to be drained: not a small cup is offered to him, but a torrent of sufferings and divine wrath on account of the sins of the whole world to be drained by him. And indeed Christ himself seems to have referred us to the prophecy of this Psalm, partly while he testifies in his great passion that the cup of divine wrath proposed to him is the same one, very horrible, which he so greatly prays to be removed, Matt. 26:39, partly while, about to enter upon his passion, he crossed the torrent of Kidron, into which the confluence of all uncleanness, and of all filth, and of refuse from the city and the mountains used to occur during the time of rains, John 18:1. For just as the filth of the sheep destined for sacrifices, the blood of the victims, and indeed all uncleanness flowed down from the city into this torrent, so the filth of the sins of the whole human race flowed together into that torrent of sufferings, which Christ in our place drain- wished to laugh, as the blessed Gerhard says again in Harm. pass. chap. 1, and therefore the blessed Gesner wishes it to be observed here regarding the description of the Lord's passion, that it is nothing other than that our Savior drank up the impetuous and turbid torrent of the wrath of God against our sins, and of eternal damnation: Just as He Himself complains in Psalm 88, 'You have brought all your waves over me': and in the garden in Matthew 26, He complained most gravely about this cup of divine judgment against the sins of the whole world: 'Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me.' Which explanation the blessed Glassius also approved, loc. cit. Th. 36 seqq. And although the whole life of Christ, a life spent in these lands, can be understood by the former member, it must nevertheless be said that the time of His most bitter passion is primarily signified. That the torrent or sudden inundations of huge calamities running together from all sides contain a metaphorical notion, is sufficiently evident from 2 Sam. 22, 5. Psalm 18, 5. Psalm 124, 4. Psalm 88, 8. 17. 18. Moreover, that the word 'to drink' is used metaphorically for 'to be afflicted,' and 'to drink the cup' for 'to sustain the portion of afflictions divinely assigned to oneself,' is likewise plain from Job 21, 20. Ps. 75, 9. Jerem. 25, 16. chap. 49, 12. Ob. v. 16. Matth. 22, 20. etc. If these two, therefore, are joined, so that the drinking is said to occur not from a cup (which is a symbol of a measured portion) but from a torrent (which denotes an immense abundance of the thing of which there is speech), what shall we say but that by metaphorical amplification the most bitter passion is denoted? The sense, therefore, in this place is: The Messiah will not, like other men, merely taste the cup of afflictions, but as if immersed in a rapid torrent, He will drink turbid water in immense abundance, and thus will be subject to infinite and infernal punishments, on account of the sins of the world imputed to Him. Conf. Ps. 69, 1 sqq. But this will happen on the way, that is, while He is still established in the course and as it were a pilgrimage toward the state of exaltation and subsequent glory, 1 Petr. 1, 11. The blessed D. Dorscheus further confirms that opinion in dissert. 1 de sess. ad dextr. Dei §. 53 seqq. The blessed Tarnovius, having abandoned the interpretation of Tremellius, Junius, and Piscator, which is also that of Grotius, which he says differs little from the Rabbinical one of Aben-Ezra, agrees with ours. The Jesuits Bellarmine and Menochius, from among the Papists, also make this explanation their own. He has it thus: To this torrent (the course of human affairs: by which all things pass like a torrent, for the most part turbid and troubled) the Son of God descended through His incarnation, and on the way, that is, in the space of His mortal and passing life, He drank the turbid water of this torrent, nay, He even descended into the depth of the torrent through His passion, so that He did not drink the water for refreshment and delight, but drank the most troublesome water, as those do who are submerged in waters, according to that of Psalm 68: 'The waters have entered even unto my soul. I am stuck in the mire of the deep, and there is no substance: I have come into the height of the sea, and the tempest has submerged me.' Similarly Menochius, for the most part an epitomizer of Bellarmine in the Psalms, calls the torrent the course of human affairs, i.e., Christ will be a participant in many sorrows, troubles, and calamities in this way and mortal life. Emmanuel Saa understands the torrent of passions: and Guilh. Estius no differently. Nor does Tirinus disapprove: 'He will drink of the torrent in the way,' viz., of manifold passions in this life. Thus Arnobius, Jerome, Theodoret, Euthymius, Bernhard, although he adds that it is better taken from the Hebrew concerning the slaughter of enemies, from whose blood the torrent is made. From among the Calvinists, Mollerus, Rudingerus, and the author of the idea of the Heidelberg sermon held on this Psalm p. 578 embrace our explanation. 'Concerning the torrent,' he says, 'to signify His most bitter passion of all, most intense and exquisite pains, a most detestable and execrable death.' And just as a torrent collected from rains descending from the mountains into the valleys is carried with sudden impetuosity, and, flooded, not without a horrible roar, levels fields, trees, levels joyful crops, and the labors of oxen: So the passion of Christ is likened not to a cup, but to a torrent, just as if we were to apply to it what we read in Psalm 42, 8, and that agrees with the sayings of the New Testament, Luc. 24, 26. Philipp. 2, 8. Hebr. 2, 14. and Psalm 8, 6. Moreover, he calls the life of Christ the way. Andr. Rivetus, although he does not disapprove of either the interpretation of Calvin, which pleased Grotius here, or even that of Bucer concerning the torrent of the blood of enemies, nevertheless confesses that the following words, 'therefore He will exalt the head,' if they are duly weighed, open up another sense, which squares better with the argument of the Psalm; because to exalt the head is the same as to make one who is sad and dejected on account of grief joyful, by a Hebrew phrase, Psalm 3, 4. Psalm 27, 6. Jerem. 52, 31. Because the calamitous are with head bowed down, Thren. 2, 10; hence to lift up someone's head is to provide a cause for joy by being affected with honor and being restored to former dignity. The exaltation of the head therefore seems to presuppose a preceding dejection, signified by the drinking of the torrent in the way, so that in these few words we may recognize the emptying and exaltation of the Messiah, the passion and resurrection, through which He was introduced into that kingdom, signified at the beginning by the sitting at the right hand of God: He therefore renders this sense: The Son of God manifested in the flesh will pass through the valley of tears of this life, He is to drink from the turbid torrent of the water of many and grave sufferings, but because He will render to the Father supreme obedience in it even unto death, even the death of the cross, God the Father will again snatch Him from all evils and lift Him up. Rivetus prefers this sense to the others, as one which is simpler and most convenient to the argument of the whole Psalm. For since he has hitherto dealt openly with the kingdom and Priesthood of Christ, from there at the end of the Psalm he subjoins as it were a certain brief recapitulation, and shows how He arrived from the Priesthood to that kingdom, namely, through passion to exaltation.

Verse of the same.

THEREFORE HE WILL EXALT THE HEAD) That is, He will strike the stars with a sublime top. The same kind of speaking is in Jud. 6, 28.

I think Judges 8:28 should be read. It seems to be understood only of fame and the glory of a name, which is a relative and improper exaltation: not of an exaltation properly so called, by which one is established in a more sublime state and dignity: namely, that from such great alacrity, with which he will pursue the enemies, he is to obtain notable fame. But as the truest, nay, the most profound emptying and humiliation is designated by the drinking from the torrent, so here likewise the truest and most eminent exaltation is inferred, which will follow that emptying. Which both the word רום teaches, importing true exaltation Psalm 14:7, Ps. 39:43, Ps. 76:8, 1 Sam. 2:7, Ps. 113:6, which signification of this word, since it is proper, is not to be abandoned: and the phrase itself to exalt the head implies, just as has already been observed from Psalm 3:4, Psalm 27:6. Jeremiah 52:31. The sense of the opposite member confirms it: the sitting at the right hand of God proves it: because there is no talk of any other exaltation than that which the whole Psalm treats, describing the sitting at the right hand of God and dominion in the midst of enemies, and Judge against the nations, etc. The parallel passage Phil. 2:9 proves it, as well as a similar formula of speaking, that Christ has been constituted head over all things Ephes.

5, 22. Coloss. 2, 10. and exalted at the right hand of God Acts 2, 33. chap. 5, 31. and it is placed beyond controversy among almost all Christian interpreters. For the consequence of divine ordination is designated here, so that that exaltation of the head might receive the drinking from the torrent, exaltation the humiliation, the donation of the name which is above every name the death of the cross, through the lifting up to the right hand of God Luke 24, 26. Acts 2, 24. Ephes. 4, 8. Phil. 2, 9. And this also concerning Psalm 110.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

DE TORRENTE IN VIA BIBET) Descriptio Bellato- ris alacris, qui dum hostes persequitur, non quærit diverso- ria, aut cauponas ut vino se refoveat, sed aqua contentus est, quam obiter & raptim sumit ex quovis quem reperit non fluvio tantum, sed & torrente. Sic Christus nullum tempus omisit, quo opera Diaboli destruere posset.

Affumo, quod hic fatetur Grotius de Christo hæc agere, unde liquet cætera prædicata etiam de Christo esse intelligenda: quum omnia unum subjectum respiciant, adeoque Christum esse Do- minum illum à dextris, qui confringit Reges, ju- dicat inter gentes, implet cadavera, frangit caput super terram multam, atque bibens de torrente in via caput exaltat. Quod vero ad interpretatio- nem hujus phraseos, varie ea explicatur. Mit- timus ineptam explicationem Franciscani Mona- chi, Michaelis Menoti apud Rivet. in h. l. & ali- am Vitalis Luceolii, quam Lorinus ipse ut duram reprobat. Quanquam vero placuit nonnullis In- terpp. illa de alacri persecutione hostium interpre- tatio, Vatablo & Tremellio, ac Junio, quam Gro- tius hic suam fecit; alii tamen cum Bucero, Mün- stero, Tirino, Mariana, Jansenio explicant potius de copiosa sanguinis hostilis effusione, qui torrentis instar manaturus sit, ut Christus victor illum bi- bere, ac se hostili sanguine satiare possit. Pleri- que vero de exinanitione Christi explicant: e qui- bus alii tenuitatem victus & paupertatem Christi designari, quod vel obviam torrentis aquam bibe- rit, censent cum Justino, Basilio M. Chrysostomo, Scholiis Graecis. Reliqui vero passionum tormenta hic exprimi ajunt, cum Hieronymo, Eusebio, Ar- nobio, Euthymio, Glossa interlineari, & ordina- ria; quae Nostrorum Theologorum, plerorumque Pon- tificiorum, & e Calvinianis Riveti est εξήγησις, cae- teris omnino praeferenda. Nam torrens adhibe- tur horrendis cruciatibus, & miseriis exprimen- dis Esa. 30, 33. Jerem. 47, 2. Psalm. 124, 4. unde tor- rentes Belial Psalm. 18, 5. seqq. cum funibus inferni conjunguntur: quemadmodum notissimum est, calamitates & poenas per aquas inundantes, ani- mam intrantes & absorbentes, describi passim, eti- am cum de Christo sermo est, utpote Psalm. 69, 2. 15. 16. ac bibitio de sensu irae divinae, & passio- num divinarum usurpari solet Job. 21, 2. cap. 34, 7. Psalm. 75, 9. Esa. 51, 17. Jerem. 25, 15. cap. 40, 12. cap. 51, 7. Ezech. 23, 32. Apocal. 12, 10. quo pacto etiam Christi passio, ejusque sensus describitur Matth. 20, 22. cap. 26, 42. Marc. 10, 38. 39. Johann. 18, 11. Di- citur autem hic Christus non ex calice bibere, quod de aliis hominibus habetur Psalm. 75, 9. Matth. 22, 20. & alibi, quo dimensa potio notatur, sed ex torrente, ut passionum gravitas, & copia ex- primatur, siquidem immersus quasi rapido torren- ti, imo ipsis torrentibus Belial, Diaboli & impio- rum hominum, bibiturus erat, infernalibus poe- nis subjiciendus, quo de Psalm. 49, 1. seqq. pro- lixe conqueritur. Quod in via vitae & muneris ipsius evenire debuit, in via ad gloriam Luc. 24, 26. 1. Petr. 1, 2. Egregie haec illustrant quae habet B. Gerhardus in Harmon. Evang. de pass. Christ. cap. 2. pag. 24. Pater coelestis propinaverat Filio suo calicem, imo torrentem irae suae peccatis totius hu- mani generis, quae Christo imposita erant, alias de- bita. Haec certe fuit amarissima & acerbissima potio. Reliquis filiis suis calicem passionum certa quadam mensura admetitur Psalm. 75, 9. Calix in manu Do- mini vino mero plenus: quo respectu itidem passio- nes sanctorum conferuntur calici. Quemadmodum enim olim singulis convivis demensum suum propina- batur, sic Deus unicuique filiorum suorum certum demensum crucis & afflictionum proponit, sed Chri- sto feces irae divinae exhaurienda proponuntur: pro- pinatur ipsi non caliculus, sed torrens passionum & irae divinae propter peccata totius mundi ipsi exhau- riendus. Et videtur sane Christus ipse nos ad Psalmi hujus vaticinium remisisse, partim dum calicem irae divinae sibi propositum in passione magna testatur, eundem valde horribilem, quem tantopere deprecatur Matth. 26, 39. partim dum passionem aditurus torrentem Kedron transiit, in quem confluxus omnis immunditiei, & omni- um sordium, ac rejectamentorum ex urbe & mon- tibus pluviarum tempore fiebat Joh. 18, 1. Quem- admodum enim sordes ovium sacrificiis destinatarum, sanguis victimarum, adeoque omnis immundities ex urbe in hunc torrentem defluxit, sic sordes peccato- rum totius humani generis in torrentem illum passio- num confluxerunt, quem Christus nostro loco exhau- rire voluit, ut iterum ait B. Gerhardus Harm. paff. cap. 1. ideoque B. Gesnerus hic observari vult de- scriptionem passionis Dominicæ, quod nihil aliud sit, quam quod Salvator noster torrentem im- petuosum & turbidum iræ Dei adversus peccata nostra, & æternæ damnationis ebibit: Sicut ipse Psalm. 88. conqueritur, omnes fluctus tuos indu- xisti super me: & in horto Matth. 26. de hoc ca- lice judicii divini adversus peccata totius mundi gravissime conquestus est: Pater si fieri potest, transeat à me calix iste. Quam explicationem probavit etiam B. Glassius loc. cit. Th. 36. seqq. Et- si vero tota vita Christi vita in his terris peracta, intelligi priori membro possit, cumprimis tamen acerbissimæ passionis tempus significari dicendum est. Torren- tem seu subitas inundationes calamitatum ingentium atque undique concurrentium notionem metaphori- cam continere, satis constat 2. Sam. 22, 5. Psalm. 18, 5. Psalm. 124, 4. Psalm. 88, 8. 17. 18. Bibendi autem verbum usurpari metaphorice pro affligi, & bibere calicem, pro afflictionum portionem sibi divinitus as- signatam sustinere, itidem planum est Job. 21, 20. Ps. 75, 9. Jerem. 25, 16. cap. 49, 12. Ob. v. 16. Matth. 22, 20. &c. Hæc duo igitur si conjungantur, ut bibitio non ex calice (qui demensæ portionis Symbolum est) sed ex torrente (qui immensam copiam rei, de qua sermo est, notat) fieri dicatur, quid nisi ἀυξησει metaphorica acerbissimam passionem denotari dice- mus? Sensus igitur hoc loco est: Messias non ut cæ- teri homines calicem afflictionum gustabit tantum, sed quasi rapido torrenti immersus, aquam turbi- dam in copia immensa hauriet, adeoque infinitis & infernalibus, ob peccata mundi sibi imputata, pœ- nis subjectus erit. Conf. Ps. 69, 1. sqq. Fiet autem hoc in via, hoc est, dum adhuc in cursu & velut peregri- natione constitutus est ad statum exaltationis & glo- riæ subsequentis 1. Petr. 1, 11. Ulterius eam senten- tiam confirmat B. D. Dorscheus dissert. 1. de sess. ad dextr. Dei §. 53. seqq. B. Tarnovius, Tremellii, Ju- nii & Piscatoris interpretatione, quæ Grotii eti- am est, relicta, quam à Rabbinica Aben-Ezræ pa- rum abire ait, nostræ astipulatur. Suam etiam faciunt hanc explicationem è Pontificiis Jesuitæ Bellarminus & Menochius. Ille ita habet: Ad hunc torrentem (cursus rerum humanarum: quo omnia transeunt instar torrentis, ut plurimum turbida & turbata) descendit Filius Dei per incarnationem suam, & in via, id est, in spatio vitæ suæ mortalis & transeuntis, bibit aquam turbidam hujus torren- tis, imo etiam in profundum torrentis descendit per passionem, ita ut non biberit aquam ad refrigerium & delectationem, sed biberit molestissimam aquam, ut illi faciunt qui demerguntur in aquis, juxta il- lud Psalm. 68. intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam. Infixus sum in limo profundi, & non est substantia: veni in altitudinem maris, & tem- pestas demersit me. Similiter Menochius, Bellar- mini in Psalmis plerumque Epitomator, Torren- tem appellat cursum rerum humanarum, q. d. Chri- stus in via & vita hac mortali multorum dolorum, molestiarum & calamitatum erit particeps. Em- manuel Saa torrentem passionum intelligit: nec ali- ter Guilh. Estius. Neque improbat Tirinus: de torrente in via bibet, scil. passionum multiplicium in hac vita. Ita Arnobius, Hieronymus, Theodoret Euthymius, Bernhard. quamquam addat, melius ex Hæbræo accipi de strage hostium, ex quorum san- guine torrens fit. E Calvinianis nostram explica- tionem amplectuntur Mollerus, Rudingerus, & Autor ideæ concionis Heidelberg. super hunc Psal- mum habitæ p. 578. De torrente, inquit, ad signi- ficandam passionem ejus omnium acerbissimam, dolo- res intensissimos & exquisitissimos, mortem maxime detestabilem & execrabilem. Atque ut torrens ex pluviis de montibus in valles descendentibus collectus subito impetu fertur, inundatusque non sine horribili susurro, sternit agros, arbores, sternit sata læta, boumque labores: Ita Christi passio non calici, sed torrenti assimilatur, perinde ac si ad ipsam appli- cemus quod legimus Psalm. 42, 8. idque congruit cum dictis Nov. Testam. Luc. 24, 26. Philipp. 2, 8. Hebr. 2, 14. & Psalm. 8, 6. Vitam autem Christi vocat viam. Andr. Rivetus etsi non improbet vel Calvini inter- pretationem, quæ Grotio hic placuit, vel Buceri etiam de torrente sanguinis hostium, sequentia tamen verba, propterea exaltabit caput, si rite ex- pendantur, alium sensum aperire fatetur, qui ar- gumento Psalmi magis quadrat; quia exaltare ca- put idem est, quod tristem & præ dolore deje- ctum reddere lætum phrasi Ebræa Psalm. 3, 4. Psalm. 27, 6. Jerem. 52, 31. Quia calamitosi sunt capite de- misso Thren. 2, 10. hinc elevare alicujus caput est cau- sam lætitiæ præbere honore afficiendo & pristinæ digni- tati restituendo. Videtur ergo exaltatio capitis præ- supponere præcedentem demissionem, significatam bi- bitione torrentis in via, ut in his paucis verbis agno- scamus Messiæ exinanitionem, & exaltationem, pas- sionem & resurrectionem, per quam introductus est in regnum illud, significatum initio sessione ad dextram Dei: Sensum ergo hunc reddit: Filius Dei in carne manifestatus transibit per vallem lacry- marum hujus vitæ, bibiturus est ex torrente turbi- do aquæ multarum & gravium perpessionum, sed quia Patri in ea summam obedientiam præstabit us- que ad mortem, mortem autem crucis, Deus Pa- ter eum rursus ab omnibus malis eripiet & evehet. Quem sensum cæteris præfert Rivetus, ut qui sim- plicior sit, & convenientissimus argumento totius Psal- mi. Quum enim hactenus palam egerit de re- gno & Sacerdotio Christi, inde in fine Psalmi vel- uti quandam brevem ἀνακεφαλαίωσιν subjungit, & quomodo à Sacerdotio ad regnum illud perve- nerit, ostendit, nempe per passionem ad exalta- tionem.

Vers. eod.

PROPTEREA EXALTABIT CAPVT) Id est, Sublimi feriet sidera vertice. Idem loquendi genus est Jud. 6, 28.

Legendum puto Judic. 8, 28. Videtur tantum de fama, & gloria nominis, quæ respectiva & im- propria est exaltatio: non de proprie dicta exalta- tione, qua in sublimiori statu & dignitate quis constituitur, intelligere: quod nempe ex tanta ala- critate, qua hostes prosequetur, famam insignem con- sequuturus sit. Sed ut verissima imo profundissi- ma exinanitio, & humiliatio designata per bibitio- nem de torrente, ita hic pariter verissima & eminen- tissima exaltatio infertur, quæ exinanitionem illam consequetur. Quod tum verbum רום docet, veram exaltationem importans Psalm. 14, 7. Ps. 39, 43. Ps. 76, 8. 1. Sam. 2, 7. Ps. 113, 6. quæ significatio verbi hujus cum propria sit, relinquenda non est: tum phrasis ipsa exaltare caput infert, quemadmo- dum jam observatum è Psalm. III, 4. Psal. XXVII, 6. Jerem. LII, 31. tum membri oppositi sensus con- firmat: tum sessio ad dextram Dei evincit: quia de nulla alia exaltatione sermo est, quam de qua totus Psalmus agit, describens sessionem ad dex- tram Dei & dominationem in medio inimicorum, ac Judicem contra gentes, &c. tum locus parallelus Phil. 2, 9. comprobat, nec non similis loquendi formula, quod caput constitutus sit Christus super omnia Ephes.

5, 22. Coloss. 2, 10. & dextra Dei exaltatus Actor. 2, 33. cap. 5, 31. ac penes Interpp. Christianos plerosque omnes extra controversiam positum est. Designa- tur enim hic consequentia divinæ ordinationis, ut bi- bitionem de torrente exciperet illa exaltatio capitis, humiliationem exaltatio, mortem crucis nominis do- natio, quod est supra omne nomen, per evectionem ad dextram Dei Luc. 24, 26. Actor. 2, 24. Ephes. 4, 8. Phil. 2, 9. Atque hæc etiam de Psalm. 110.

## 111:1 Argument
PSALM CXI. A Paschal Song.

This is an alphabetical song, but by very short verses, you might call them dimeters, and it is to be distinguished thus.

Latin:

PSALMUS CXI. Carmen Paschale.

HOc carmen Alphabeticum est, sed per brevissimos versi- culos, quasi dimetros dicas, & sic distinguendus est.

## 111:10
Verse 10. THE BEGINNING OF WISDOM IS THE FEAR OF THE LORD.

Bellarmine, book 1 on Justification, chapter 13, gathers from this that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of justification. The Remonstrants in the Acts of the Synod of Dort, p. 64, conclude that certain dispositions are required in man, through which he is rendered fit for the end or for apprehending the Gospel. Some respond that ראשׁית is the same as head, or denotes that which is first by reason of its dignity, most excellent, as Num. 24, 2. Amos 6, 6. and thus Mariana: it is the first and most polished science; but because in the parallel passage Prov. 9, 10 it is explicitly rendered by תְּחִלַּת as beginning, some concede that servile fear is the beginning of true wisdom and conversion, from which, however, it cannot be concluded that fear is the beginning of justification, or a disposition toward justification or faith, for although in order of time that fear precedes, it has no beginning into justification or faith. Most, however, prefer to take this maxim concerning filial fear (Bellarmine not denying it in his Commentary) because the filial fear of the Lord is the beginning of true and solid wisdom, because the spirit of wisdom does not enter into a malicious soul. Of wisdom, I say, that which governs all counsels in prosperous and adverse affairs. Blessed Luther, marginal gloss: He who wishes to learn well must first be God-fearing. Cf. Sirach 19, 19. 20. Wisd. 1, 4. Whence heretics, who remove the fear of the Lord and reverence for the heavenly word from the oracles, do not even have the beginning of true wisdom. Cf.
