David Kimchium è Judæis, quanquam ille adhuc magis sanus sit, quam Grotius noster. Notat enim alios de diebus Christi hunc Psalmum interpretari, idque rectum esse, explicatque eundem modo de Christo, modo de Davide. R. Salomo Jarchi etsi per lapi- dem etiam intelligat Davidem ab Israele rejectum in diebus Saulis, nec non alio sensu Ecclesiam con- temptibilem inter gentes, vocem tamen lætitiæ v. 15. refert ad Messiæ tempora, imo v. 22. de lapide re- probata in comment. Mich. 5, 7. de Messia expli- cat. E Christianis Calvinum, Bucerum, & Molle- rum sequutus est, qui per lapidem reprobatum Da- videm intelligunt, quamvis in Christum hæc proprie etiam convenire, Calvinus affirmet, quia cum Da- vid Rex creatus est, jacta fuere fundamenta regni æterni, quod tandem Christi adventu patefactum fuit. Et temporale illud solium, in quo sederunt po- steri Davidis, imago fuit perpetui imperii, quo dona- tus est Christus à Patre. Junius & Tremellius re- gnum typice in persona Davidis stabilitum, perfecte & absolute in Christo institutum intelligunt: lapi- demque typicum David dicunt à proceribus tum Saulis, tum Isbofethi temporibus reprobatum. Quæ etiam Piscatoris est glossa, & Autorum nota- rum Belgicarum, ut & Riveti, qui Davidem de se- ipso agere ait, & de rebus suis, sed ita ut Spiritu Pro- phetico viderit, & vaticinatus sit de iis, quæ in Chri- sto maxime adimplenda erant, cujus ipse typus erat, & Pater futurus. Neque abnuit Vatablus. Ad- ducit etiam in eam sententiam Rivetus Antonium Agellium, ut & Jansenium ac Simon de Muys è Pon- tificiis, quod hic ad literam de Davide sermo sit etiam v. 22. sed quatenus Christi typum gessit. Cæ- terum per lapidem illum reprobatum intelligi non posse Davidem, sed unice Christum secundum lite- ralem ac proprium verborum sensum intelligen- dum esse, neque Davidem hic ut typum Christi pro- poni, cum de lapide ab ædificantibus reprobato, sed qui in caput anguli factus, sermo sit, argumen- ta invicta confirmant: Primum è Psalmo ipso, tum ex ejusdem explicatione, in Novo Testamento tra- dita. Psalmus his absolvitur partibus: Prima est adhortatio ad celebrationem æternæ misericordiæ Dei, quæ ab Israele, domo Aaronis, & omnibus timentibus Dominum fieri debeat, vers. 1. 2. 3. 4. Quæ enim illa est misericordia Dei, quæ in æter- num celebranda, quam omnes omnium tempo- rum pii confiteri debeant, nisi misericordia, quæ in Christo nobis exhibita? Altera est commemo- ratio gratiæ, quæ Christo in passionibus ejus à Deo obtigit: exauditionis nempe divinæ vers. 5. qua se confidenter erexit vers. 6. 7. (conf. Ebr. 5, 7.) un- de alios adhortatur ad fiduciam non in homini- bus locandam, sed in solo Deo vers. 8. 9. assisten- tiæ adversus hostes multivarios vers. 10. seqq. (Conf. Psalm. 2, 1. 2. Psalm. 22, 17. 22. Psalm. 69, 6.) & ere- ctionis cum percutietur, atque affligetur vers. 13. ob quam tum ipse DEUM celebrat vers. 14. tum ἐπινίκιον de victoria dextræ DEI in Eccle- sia decantabitur vers. 15. 16. ac vivificationis: si- quidem non æterna morte periturus sit, sed in æ- ternum victurus, opera Domini annunciaturus in Ecclesia v. 17. 18. Quænam, obsecro, illa est vi- ctoria, quæ in tabernaculis justorum, in cœtibus Ecclesiæ de exaltatione dextræ Dei tantopere de- cantatur, & decantanda est, nisi victoria ista, quam Christus ab hostibus infernalibus in sa- lutem totius humani generis reportavit, quæ per universam Ecclesiam celebratur? Tertia pars est prædictio ingressus Christi in Jerusalem, & quo pa- cto excipiendus ibi sit, siquidem ipse continuans orationem, excitet Hierosolymitanos, ut sibi ape- riantur portæ justitiæ, vers. 19. 20. 21. confer Psalm. 40, 9. Zachar. 9, 9. Matth. 21, 10.) Deumque iterum celebret ob liberationem in statu exinanitionis, summæque humiliationis præstandam vers. 21. Ele- gans hic est B. Tarnovii Commentarius ad vers. 19. p. 98. Ego Rex justitiæ & gloriæ Psalm. 24. venio Ps. 40, 8. ut faciam nunc ipsam voluntatem Patris pa- tiendo, nec me terret mors, non absterrent mala alia, intrepide accedo, & quia nunc est dies Novi Testa- menti exortus (infra v. 24.) agite, aperite mihi por- tas justitiæ, ut ingrediar hanc urbem, & in ea justi- tiam amissam generi humano recuperem, spei bonæ plenus, fore, ut omnia feliciter expediam, ingrediar per eas portas, & celebrabo Jah, intrabo civitatem cum pompa, intrabo templum cum potentia, illam il- lustrabo, hoc reformabo ac purgabo, utrobique au- tem Patrem celebrabo, ex ore infantium ei laudem parando, vendentes ejiciendo, alios vera docendo, Pharisæos, Scribas, Sadducæos refutando & convin- cendo. Et ad vers. 20. Aperite mihi prius Salvatori, ut postea pateat hæc porta cœtui fideli, quia hæc ipsa porta est, ac ducit ad Jehovam, hæc mea passio, satis- factio, meritum, atque adeo ego totus Christus, fide applicatus, sum verum illud ostium, per quod accessus patet ad Patrem Joh. 10, 7. in Ecclesia enim reddun- tur participes sortis sanctorum in lumine per Chri- stum Joh. 14, 6. justi intrabunt per eam portam ex regno gratiæ in regnum gloriæ, ex tenebris in lu- cem, ex Regno Diaboli in Regnum Filii Dei. Ad vers. 21. Quid facies Christe, quando apertæ fue- runt illæ portæ, & Templi Jerosolymitani, urbisque typicæ, & Novi Testamenti in antitypo? quid fa- ciam? quæris: curabo prædicandum Evangelium de me exinanito ac passo & exaltato ac glorificato. Celebrabo te, ô Pater, ego ipse, ut alios hortatus sum vers. 1. & gratias agam, per publicum Evangelii præ- conium celebrans tuam miram viam, qua genus hu- manum redemisti per me, videlicet quod in statu ex- inanitionis clamantem ac te invocantem exaudive- ris me, supra vers. 5. & me juveris, ac ita factus mihi sis in salutem, seu salus, supra vers. 13. 14. Porro Eccle- sia vel fideles introducuntur cum admiratione atque exultatione οἰκονομίαν salutis celebrantes, qua la- pis ille ab architectis reprobatus in caput anguli con- stitutus est à Domino in die salutis & liberationis generis humani v. 22. 23. 24. (conf. Es. 49, 8.) un- de perenne gaudium omnibus fidelibus; introdu- cuntur imprimis in Ecclesia populus ille, ac pueri qui Messiæ Regi suo adventanti, & discipulis ejus erant congratulaturi vers. 25. 26. (Conf. Matth. 21.) Quarta denique pars exhortatio mutua est fidelium ad celebranda hæc solemnia Sacrificiis Eucha- risticis, per orbem ubicunque templum est, & alta- te Domini, h. e. vera Ecclesia Ef. 56, 7. Ebr. 13, 10. quia Rex ille in nomine Domini adveniens Dominus est Deus, qui nos illuminat (quo de vid. B. Luther. Tom. 5. Jen. German. pag. 169. in h. l. & B. Tar- nov. h. l.) ut ita universa Ecclesia vera fide uno ore canat : Deus meus es tu, confitebor tibi: Deus meus es tu & exaltabo te vers. 28. Quibus versu ul- timo loco conclusionis subjicitur repetitio κελεύ- σματος Domini, à quo inchoatus erat Psalmus: Confitemini Domino, quoniam bonus: quoniam in seculum misericordia ejus. Ita cohærent omnia pulcre & concinne, quemadmodum eximie ob- servatum in Paraphrasi Osiandri, & Vinariensi, & Commentariis B. Tarnovii. Sunt quidem etiam nonnulli inter Patres, utpote Theodoretes & Au- gustinus, qui in prioribus partibus Psalmi Ecclesi- am loqui autument: De Davide illa exponi ad li- teram posse, & à Chrysostomo exponi ait Bellarminus. Sed convenientius fortasse cohærent omnia, si to- tus Psalmus quoad literam de Christo exponatur: quemadmodum integrum de Christo loqui Osian- der, Gesnerus, Tarnovius, & autores paraphraseos Vinariensis existimant, etsi quod capiti accidit, membris etiam, si recte debitoque modo fiat, accommodari possit, siquidem etiam fidelis quis- que profiteri queat: non moriar, nisi Dei volunta- te, non hominum libidine, non moriar prorsus, sed in morte vivam, in vita æterna Deum laudabo: quo de vid. B. Tarnov. in h. l. uti versum hunc 17. im- primis sibi applicavit B. Lutherus, ac Musæi parie- tibus, sese erigendi gratia, appinxit, cum magnum veræ religioni, sibique ipsi immineret periculum: teste Matthesio Conc. 8. de Vit. Luther. p. 90. Cæ- terum quicquid sit de prioribus partibus, & tamet- si concederetur, illas de Davide accipiendas esse, atque omnia, quæ in prima persona prolata sunt, vers. 5. de tribulatione invocavi Dominum, & exau- divit me; vers. 6. Dominus mihi adjutor: & EGO despiciam inimicos meos; vers. 10. omnes gentes cir- cuierunt ME, & sic porro v. 11. 12. 13. 14. nec non vers. 17. 18. 19. 20. 21. Davidis personam concernere: Neque dubium sit, illis verbis, quæ versibus fina- libus habentur, utpote vers. 27. 28. 29. Psalten de se simul loqui, cum in plurali benediximus, inquit, vobis, & Dominus illuxit NOBIS: ac peculiariter de semetipso prædicare, DEUS MEUS ES TU, & confitebor tibi, &c. victoria tamen illa, quam in po- steriori parte v. 15. & 16. in tabernaculis justorum ce- lebratum iri prædicit (utut in præterito, more Prophetico loquatur) & vaticinium de lapide an- gulari vers. 22. 23. atque exultatio, & votiva excla- matio vers. 24. 25. ad Messiam pertinent: exhorta- tio denique ad celebrationem festi solemnis tem- pora Novi Testamenti, quæ in spiritu prævidit Da- vid, respicit. Certe cum in tertia persona loqui- tur de lapide angulari vers. 22. & seqq. inter omnes Interpp. Christianos, si Calvinum & complices ejus à partibus Judæorum hic stantes excipias, in- dubitato convenit, de Christo sermonem esse, non de Davide, non de Ecclesia. Nulli enim alii hæc conveniunt, quam Christo. Ecquis alius lapis, qui ab architectis reprobatus, admiranda Dei ὁικονομίᾳ in angularem lapidem factus? David etsi à Saule, & aula ejus rejectus fuerit, non tamen ab architectis spiritualibus præcipue reprobatus, vel à Sacerdoti- bus qui ædificandæ domui Domini præerant, à si- quibus potissimum reprobandus erat lapis, de quo hic vaticinatur Spiritus Sanctus. Tum vero quo- modo totum populum Israelis, quomodo Aaronis domum peculiariter hic ad celebrandum cum o- mnibus piis Dominum excitaret David, si ab ar- chitectis seu proceribus Ecclesiasticis è domo Aaronis vel Politicis in Israele reprobatus fuit? quomodo illis, qui de domo Domini sunt, ceu piis & fidelibus hic benediceret, ab iis præcipue rejectus? vers. 26. Adhæc quanquam admiranda οἰκονομία Domini etiam in Davide elucefcat, non tamen id stupen- dum illud Dei opus est, quod admirari omnes fide- les, vi hujus Psalmi, oporteat, ut exclament, à Do- mino factum hoc est, & admirabile est in oculis no- stris, & ob quod tantopere omnes fideles lætari & gaudere debeant: Hæc est dies, quam fecit Domi- nus, lætemur & exultemus in ea. Neque ob Da- vidis reductionem peculiariter festum tabernacu- lorum celebratum, aut aliud quoddam festum solemne institutum legitur: quo altare holocau- storum victimis extraordinarie ad cornua cumu- latis sive oneratum, sive honoratum fuerit, quod hic expetit vers. 27. Præterea de alio beneficio Do- mini hic sermo est, nempe de Spirituali, vers. 24. ut religio nobis esse debeat, hæc de corporali be- neficio reductionis Davidis, ac mundano gaudio, quod inde ortum, interpretari. Neque David constitutus est lapis angularis ἀκρογωνιαῖος, vel εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας in caput anguli, duos populos continens, & conjungens in unum, ut angularis la- pis duos parietes. Si dicas, eum utrumque popu- lum Israelis & Juda rexisse, quæ Jansenii est ex- plicatio, etiam Riveto probata: Respondeo, tum illos nondum fuisse scissos in tuos populos, sed unum constituisse populum, unum corpus Reipubl. Eorum ergo respectu lapis angularis dici non potuit. Ad- de quod David nec primus, nec solus sub impe- rio suo utrosque continuerit; nam & ante eum Saul, & post eum Salomo super utrumque popu- lum, si ita vocare lubeat, Rex constitutus fuit. Quod argumentum ceu invictum urget Theodore- tus: Hoc licet millies impudenter Judæi negent, ta- men ad alium referre non possunt: Etenim divisa- rum tribuum Zorobabel Dux erat, sed non diutius persistit, Dominus autem Christus cum in unum coë- gisset duos parietes à se invicem ex diametro distan- tes, eos inquam, qui ex Judæis, quique ex genti- bus crediderunt, hos quidem impietati servientes, il- los vero legis jugum ferentes, ea, quæ separata erant, conjunxit, & unam ex utrisque conflavit Ecclesiam, Angulum quendam imitatus, duos muros colligan- tem, hunc igitur lapidem, quem olim ædificabant Pharisæi & Saducæi, & Sacerdotes, & Scribæ repro- baverunt, & cruci affixerunt, sed factus est in caput anguli, vel secundum Symmachum, Angularis. Quid quod in Veteri Testamento etiam lapis ille à Deo electus & pretiosus expresse designetur Messias Esa. 28, 16. (Conf. 1. Petr. 2, 6. Rom. 9, 33. cap. 10, 11.) qui factus est Judæis lapis offensionis Esa. 8, 14. Confer Luc. 2, 34. Rom. 9, 39. 1. Petr. 2, 8.) qui etiam lapi- dis nomine significatur Dan. 2, 45. Zach. 3, 9. Adde quod Hieronymus testetur, quod hic Psalmus isto tempore frequenter Judæis lectus, in Synagogis decantatus, ac de Messiæ adventu exponi solitus, unde etiam pueris ipsis notus erat, qui de Messia ipsum agere probe sciebant, ideoque acclamabant Hosianna filio Davidis. Nimirum notissimum tum omnibus erat, quod sensu literali non de Davide, sed de Filio Davidis Messia ageret, in cujus hono- rem festum tabernaculorum palmarum ramis cele- brabant, & cui occinendum esse hunc Psalmum à majoribus Judæis didicerant, è quo cumprimis lætabundi decantare festo illo solebant. Cum ergo jam intelligerent Christum adventum suum celebrare, seque ut Messiam sistere velle, instinctu Spiritus S. Hosanna suum præter mo- rem festi Paschalis Christo Regi suo accinebant, eoque nomine defendebantur à Christo. E qui- bus omnibus constare arbitramur, quod hic per lapidem Messias intelligatur: quod adeo certum, ut ex ipsis etiam Judæis id agnoverit R. Salomo Jarchi, cum aliis à R. Davide Kimchio indigitatis: imo ut Judæorum nullus Christo contradicere au- sus fuerit, qui hunc locum de se allegaret.

Jam ergo si ad Novum Testamentum acceda- mus, veritas instar Phosphori effulget luculen- tissime: de nullo alio, quam de Christo ita in- telligenda esse. Apertissime enim ad sese Chri- stus ipse retulit, quæ de lapide reprobato Hiero- psaltes prædixerit, & quidem ita ut convicerit ipsos Judæos eo testimonio, in foro contradictio- nis, quod vocant, atque inter eos principes Sa- cerdotum & Scribas, eosque ad silentium redege- rit Matth. 21, 42. Marc. 12, 10. Luc. 20. 17. Nun- quam legistis in Scripturis, lapidem quem reprobave- runt ædificantes, hic factus est in caput anguli? A Domino factum est istud, & est mirabile in oculis nostris. Sanctus etiam Petrus palam coram Prin- cipibus & Senioribus ac Scribis, atque Sacerdotibus professus est Jesum Nazarenum, non alium, esse hunc lapidem, ipsos Sacerdotes esse Ædificantes, qui eundem reprobarunt: nec potuere Judæi vel verbulum respondere. Si autem de Davide ista ullatenus dicta essent, in promptu fuisset ipsis ea exceptio: sed indubium id erat, & ceu ὁμο- λογημένως certum assumebatur à Petro, Christum, non alium, esse lapidem illum, de quo Psaltes agit: Proinde id tantum egit, ut hoc ad Jesum Nazarenum applicaret, eumque esse Messiam, vel Christum adsereret. Notum sit, inquit, omni- bus vobis, & omni plebi Israel, quia in nomine Do- mini nostri Jesu Nazareni, quem vos crucifixistis, quem Deus suscitavit à mortuis, in hoc ipso coram vobis adstat sanus. Hic EST LAPIS, qui repro- batus est A VOBIS ÆDIFICANTIBUS, qui fa- ctus est in caput anguli. Quis ergo, cum Petrus omnibus hoc aperte testatum velit: Hic EST LA- PIS, qui reprobatus est à vobis ædificantibus, adhuc audeat dicere, lapidem illum esse Davidem à Saul & aula ejus reprobatum? Annon hoc est Petro in os contradicere? Judicet Ecclesia Christi, anne ipsismet Judæis, qui istam verborum Davidis sententiam negare non poterant, deterior longe sit Grotius, dum admissa Novi Testamenti au- ctoritate de Davide interpretatur, quæ Judæis ipsis non diffitentibus, unice de Messia prædicta erant? Non ergo est, quod excipiat Grotius, quod solum κατὰ τὸ μυστικώτερον Judæi Psalmum de rebus Messiæ acceperint, quæ ejus sententia est, ad Matth. 21, 42. Nam neque Christus, neque Pe- trus id oratione sua indicant, quis mystico sensu sit lapis ille angularis: quodnam enim hic vestigi- um, quod mysticum tantum sensum respexerint? Convincunt Judæos è Scripturis, quod nempe ab ipso Spiritu Sancto id prædictum fuerit, reproba- tum quidem iri à Sacerdotibus Messiam, à Deo autem electum esse, ut caput anguli sit. Neces- sum ergo est, ut id in loco illo habeatur. Si my- sticus ille sensus solum est, quum nuspiam in Scri- pturis expositus sit, quomodo convinci potue- re eodem Judæi? Num credemus, ad traditio- nes nem se recepisse Christum, & Apostolos, & ex eadem convincere voluisse adversarios, vel ad sen- sum Scripturae non explicatum in ipsa Scriptura Veteris Testamenti, sed qui per traditionem pro- pagatus fuerit? Et unde constare potuit Grotio, quod solum ille sensus mysticus fuerit, vel etiam, quod Judaei olim sensu literali de Davide, sensu autem mystico de Christo illa acceperint. Rabbi- ni illi, David Kimchi & Salomo Jarchi, nimis re- centes sunt, ut ab illis Judaeorum veterum tem- pore Christi frustra expetas, aut expectes senten- tiam. Et quis credet, in Scripturis Novi Testa- menti hoc insigne oraculum sensu mystico quidem non semel, sed aliquoties reperiri expositum à Christo, & Apostolis, nuspiam autem sive in Ve- teri, sive in Novo Testamento sensum ejusdem proprium diserte expositum esse? Taceo, quod commentum illud, de gemino Scripturae sensu, li- terali & mystico, nullis nitatur exemplis, ac per- spicuitati & simplicitati Scripturae, aequivocatio- num & ambiguitatum experti prorsus contrari- um sit, imo fidei etiam certitudinem tollat, at- que evertat. Unde enim illa haberi poterat olim, aut etiamnum poterit, si Scriptura Prophetica ita ambigua, atque dubia, diversisque sensibus obnoxia est? nam quis ex illis ceu germanus Spi- ritus Sancti sensus admittendus sit, semper dubi- um erit, quum in aequivocis & ἀμφιβόλοις nulla sit certitudo. Unde graviter monet B. Lutherus Tom. 2. Jenens. Latin. oper. in Psalm. 8. fol. 98. Scri- pturae & verbi Dei oportere esse unum, simplicem, constantemque sensum, ne (ut dicunt) è sacris lite- ris cereum nasum faciamus.

Porro non in illa tantum oratione Apologetica coram Synedrio, sed etiam in Epistola Catho- lica S. Petrus ita explicavit hunc locum, & quod iterum probe observandum, cum eodem alia conjunxit, quae pariter de hoc mystico lapide agunt, Prophetica oracula, ut mutuo sese illu- strarent 1. Epist. 2, 4. 7. Ad quem accedentes lapidem vivum, ab hominibus quidem reprobatum, à Deo autem electum & honorificatum & ipsi tanquam la- pides vivi superaedificamini domus Spiritualis: pro- pter quod continet Scriptura (Esa. 28, 16.) Ecce, pono in Sion lapidem summum angularem, electum, pretiosum, & qui crediderit in eum, non confun- detur. Vobis igitur honor credentibus: non cre- dentibus autem lapis, quem reprobaverunt aedifican- tes, hic factus est in caput anguli (Psalm. 118, 21.) & lapus offensionis & petra scandali (Esa. 8, 14.) his qui offendunt verbo: è quo manifestum est, de eodem lapide vivo & Esaiam in utroque loco, & Da- videm hic loqui ex mente Apostoli: atque id isto tempore indubitato certum fuisse, quum hunc sensum ceu genuinum & indubitato certum assu- mat Petrus. Quod pariter à Paulo factum, qui explicavit etiam, qua ratione Christus factus sit in caput anguli, vel lapidem ἀκρογωνιαῖον, at- que commentarium veluti quendam in verba illa scripsit Ephes. 2, 14. seqq. quod nempe duos populos, Judaeos & gentes contineat, & in unum conjungat, non secus atque lapis angularis duos conjungit pa- rietes, ut non nisi temere, & contra ipsummet Apo- stolum inficietur Grotius, ad commissuram τῆς ἐκλο- γῆς τῶν ἰυδαίων & gentium populi referri significa- tionem hujus vocis γωνίας (etsi relationem hanc non incommodam esse ultro fateatur;) ac vo- ce illa indicari solum velit eam vim, quae esse in angulis solet, sustinendi aedificii: Annotat. ad Matth. 21, 42. Quid enim evidentius, quam quam

Eph. 2, 20. lapis ἀκρογωνιαῖ⑄ respectum habeat ad commissuram sanctorum è Judæis & gentibus? Quibus accedit, quod populus ille, qui Christum Hierosolymam ingredientem gratulabundus ex- cepit, dirigente ita Spiritu Sancto, ex hoc Psalmo Hosianna suum, & benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, petierit. Matth. 21, 9. Marc. 11, 9. Joh. 12, 13. Quas voces acclamatorias David in Spiritu suo tempore jam percepit, cum prævidit, quod prima- tibus Christum reprobantibus, nonnulli tamen fi- deles excepturi eundem sint: perinde uti verba ipsa, quibus in cruce usurus erat Christus, Deus meus, Deus meus, quare me deseruisti! è Spiritus revelatione didicerat. Quæ omnia uti cla- rissime convincunt, Psalmum de Christo accipien- dum esse, ita magnos consensu Veteres Ecclesiæ Doctores & recentiores ista, quæ de lapide angulari & acclamatione votiva eidem facta hic habentur, de Christo interpretati sunt, & quidem sensu litera- li, non vero mystico solum. Imo de solo Christo excluso typo, vel sine respectu ad typum accepe- runt Hilarius, Theodoretus, Augustinus, & alii: tum B. Lutherus noster Tom. 5. Jen. Germ. pag. 65. seqq. & nostrates Theologi ad unum omnes, denique è Pontificiis etiam plerique. Genebrardus: Quem lapidem (Christum Metaphorice) reprobaverunt & rejecerunt ædificantes (Judæi, præsertim Sacerdo- tes & Pharisæi, structores Ecclesiæ veteris propter munus docendi eam & gubernandi) hic factus est lapis angularis illius Ecclesiastici ædifici. Improba- tus enim Christus, rejectus & expulsus, quasi lapis in- utilis, & nulli rei aptus, Rex tamen evasit, & velut lapis angularis excelluit. Ecclesiam comparari ædifi- cio non est novum, ut 1. Cor. 3. Es. 18. de hoc loco vid. Matth. 21. Marc. 1. Luc. 20. Actor. 4. 1. Pet. 2. In caput anguli, in potiorem ac digniorem ædificii lo- cum. Appellatur Esa. 28. lapis angularis, ut qui totum ædificium Ecclesiæ contineat, & duos parietes, Judæos & Gentiles, in unum angulum, in unum cor- pus Ecclesiæ, cujus ipse est caput, coagmentaverit, Eph. 2. Sic enim lapis angularis non locum duntaxat suum implet, verum etiam duos parietes connectit & continet. Vaticinium de Christo passo, & capite Ec- clesiæ post resurrectionem effecto. Genebrardum se- quitur Menochius de solo Christo pariter expli- cans. Tirinus etsi adferat explicationem de Davi- de ex Chaldæi sententia, melius tamen de Christo præsentem locum accipi docet. Estius & Eman. Saa simpliciter de Christo interpretantur. Bellarmi- nus reprobat aperte eorum sententiam ut recentio- rem, qui de Davide quoad literam intelligunt, ut ty- po Christi, eique opponit consensum veterum, & rationes è textu, & collatione N. T. ac de Christo unice interpretatur. Hos versiculos, inquit, ALI- QUI RECENTIORES de Davide exponunt ad literam, quem dicunt factum fuisse in caput Anguli, quando factus est Rex super Israelem & Judam. Sed David figuram gessisse Christi, qui factus est in caput anguli, cum factus est caput Ecclesiæ ex Judæis & gentibus congregatæ. Cæterum SS. Patres absolute exponunt de Christo, nulla mentione facta Davidis. Imo S. Johannes Chrysostomus, qui priores partes de Davide exponit ad literam, hoc loco scribit: Pro- phetam de improviso mutasse argumentum, & de Christo prophetasse. Adde quod Christus ipse publice hunc locum tanquam ad se proprie spectantem allega- vit Matth. 21. Marc. 12. & Luc. 21. neque ullus re- spondit, de Davide hæc verba esse intelligenda. San- ctus etiam Petrus Act. 4. iterum coram omni populo hunc locum allegavit tanquam proprie de Christo scriptum, neque ullus contradixit. Sanctus etiam Pau- lus ad Rom. 9. & S. Petrus 1. Epist. cap. 2. allegant

Isaiam cap. 28. de hoc lapide angulari, summo, electo, probato &c. Denique idem Apostolus Paulus ad Ephes. 2. vocat Christum angularem lapidem sum- mum. Certe non auderem, Scripturam ita celebrem & decantatam à Christo & Apostolis explicatum ullo modo cum Davidis persona communicare. Accedit, quod David non fuit primus, neque solus Rex super Israelem & Judam, ut ideo meruerit dici lapis angu- laris: nam ante ipsum fuit Saul Rex super utrum- que populum, & post eum Salomon: neque Israel & Judas erant proprie duo populi, sive duæ gentes diver- sæ, ut sunt Hebræi & Gentiles. Hæc Bellarminus. Adde annotationes Grotii ad Matth. 21, 22. Qui- nam sunt οἱ οἰκοδομῶντες? Ita vocantur Seniores magni Synedrii, quibus mandata erat non minus re- ligionis, quam Reipublicæ cura. Docet hoc Petrus, qui eosdem alloquens ἐφ' ὑμῶν, inquit, τῶν οἰκοδο- μέντων Act. 4, 2. Quomodo ergo per οἰκοδομῶντας intelligi possunt Saul & aula ejus? Num illi consti- tuebant magnum Synedrium, aut erant Senatores ejusdem? Rivetus fatetur, vix alium esse in toto V. T. locum toties in Novo citatum, & Christo adaptatum, ac si primarium Prophetiæ sensum specte- mus, ad quem S. S. respexit, ALIO non posse referri, nec in Davide sisti debere. Si ALIO non potest re- ferri secundum primarium S. S. sensum, quomodo ergo literalis sensus est de Davide? Nam literalis sensus primarius sit oportet, imo proprius & germa- nus, addo, & unicus, siquidem Scriptura in diversos sensus abripi non debeat. Unum est, quod Rivetus obvertit: nihil plane detrahi de sensu mystico, qui Christum respicit, si hæc de Davide tanquam lapide ty- pico explicentur, imo magis eum illustrari, si non so- lum verbis, sed etiam rebus hæc Filii Dei dignitas ad- umbretur. Resp. Non est quæstio de rebus, quas certa ratione typicas esse admittimus, iisque illu- strari etiam vaticinium permittimus, uti typi solent vaticiniis addi, ad ea illustranda: Sed de proprio & germano verborum sensu disquiritur in hoc oracu- lo, quia Christi passio ejusdemque exaltatio est, non potest certe germanus sensus esse de Davide. Quum ergo fateatur Rivetus, secundum primarium sensum ALIO quam ad Christum referri NON POSSE, annon ineptus est, dum morosos eos pronunciat, qui negant, hæc de Davide, ut lapide typico accipienda esse? Non enim an David lapis modo aliquo dici possit, & an typus fuerit Christi, sed an hic S. S. no- mine lapidis, ut typus Christi, secundum literam oraculi significetur? disquiritur, quod falso dici, jam ostendimus, imo agnoscere cogitur ipse Rive- tus, cum exponit, quid sit esse caput anguli, Tom 3. p. 342. in Dodec. Psalm. ad h. l. Nam caput anguli fieri dicitur lapis, quando in eo loco ponitur, ubi to- tius ædificii juncturam sustinet, unde Apostolus vertit ἀκρογωνιαῖον, qui non tantum totius ædificii pondus sustineat (uti Grotius volebat) sed etiam utrumque parietem conjungat, hoc est, Ecclesiam ex Judæis & gentibus colligat in se coadunatam Ephes. 2, 14. 15. quod recte Davidi nullo modo, ac ne ut typo quidem convenit, tantum abest, ut hic de Davide id efferatur. Fatetur denique Rivetus, respexisse Prophetam, etiam v. 25. 26. ad veritatem in Christo, cui applicatur hæc Prophetia à populo Hierosolymitano, approbante & defendente Christo Matth. 21, 9. Et quo loco liquet, Riveto judice, Christum non rejecisse hunc honorem, & puerorum acclamationum factum defendisse tan- quam à Deo directum. Certum autem est, inquit Rive- tus, ex hoc nostro Psalmo verba desumta fuisse, quæ in Synagogis Judæorum sæpe lecta fuisse, probabile est, & de Messia venturo intellecta. Ideo à populo acclamante usurpata, tanquam consueta & agnita. Et postea: Nullum, ait, dubium est, quin Deus providentia dire- xerit factum, & verba populi, his verbis Christo ap- plaudēntis, tanquam Regi a Deo misso. Si ergo in an- tiquis Judæorum Synagogis ante tempora Christi verba illa Psalmi hujus de Messia venturo intellecta sunt, idque populo etiam cognitum fuit, & familia- re, ac a Christo ipso ratum habitum, adeoque divina quoque providentia dirigente acclamatio illa e Da- vide Christo fieri debuit, annon Ecclesiæ veteri Ju- dæorum hac in parte recte intelligente verba Davi- dis, ipsisque pueris Hierosolymitanis minus sani ha- bendi, cum recentioribus Rabbinis, Judaizantes Zwingliani, qui eadem de Davide secundum lite- ram, & immediatum, uti vocant, sensum accipiunt? imo cum R. Salomo Jarchi ad Mich. 5. 2. fateatur, hunc lapidem non Davidem esse, sed Christum Davi- dis filium; Et tu Bethlehem, ex te mihi egredietur &c. Messias, sc. filius David, juxta illud, lapis, quem re- probarunt &c. annon cæci Judæis magis cæci sunt, qui purioris doctrinæ Christianæ Doctores se jacti- tant? Conf. de v. 13. 14. Concio 29. & de v. 17. 18. 19. Concio 14. in Memor. Justor. Witteberg.

Addimus Johannem Coccejum: qui non tantum Kimchium laudat hunc Psalmum ad Messiam cum aliis Rabbinis referentem, sed etiam propriam sen- tentiam explicans, verba Psalmi, dicit, partim posse esse Christi loquentis pro se & membris suis, partim Ec- clesiæ, ut versibus ultimis: & ad v. 5. ex angustia in- vocavi Jehovam, respondit mihi in latitudine Jah, ita habet; Verba sunt CHRISTI: qui etiam intel- ligendus est precipere Israeli, Aharonidis, timentibus

Deum, præconium bonitatis Dei: ad vers. vero 6. Je- hovah est meus, non timebo: loquitur, inquit, Chri- stus, sed non tantum pro se, sed & pro corpore suo.

Quanquam vero pro more suo varias ἰδίας ἐπιλύ- σεις in seqq. subjungat Coccejus v. 10. seqq. de congre- gationibus gentium contra Christum 1. sub Imperato- ribus Romanis idololatris. 2. post Constantinum, Aria- norum & Saracenorum. 3. Sub Anti-Christo, 4. post reformationem Ecclesiæ ab Anti-Christo instar Pha- raonis liberatos persequente: & vers. 17. 18. accipiat, ceu contra gentes falsa doctrina in mortem secundam retrahentes dictam protestationem: Non moriar, sed vivam, & narrabo opera Jah, & gratiarum actionem pro conservatione: Corripiendo corripuit me Jah, sed morti non tradidit me; versum 19. 20. contra gentes portam Justitiæ occludentes, versibus vero

21. 22. 23. 24. Ecclesiam velit gratias agere Deo, ob salvationem ex manu persequentium: ubi perperam rejectionem Christi ab ædificantibus factam, qui vero caput anguli constit vendus sit, ad tempora An- ti-Christi abripit, & ad reformationem Ecclesiæ, quum de Christi passione & evectione in cœlum hæc agant: id tamen ex interpreatione Cocceja- na liquet, quod textum agnoverit tam luculentum, ut non possit Psalmus de Davide intelligi, aut ad tempora ejus referri, quantum ad sensum literalem; Sed ad Christum & tempora Novi Test. referri de- beat. Quid autem de illis interpretamentis Cocce- janis habendum sit, e superiorib. liquet. Antiquum obtinet autor, in excogitandis mirabilibus, & inau- ditis glossis. Quales etiam hic insperguntur, e qui- bus nonnullas ὡς ἐν παρόδῳ in exemplum produce- re placet. Christus inquit, vocatur lapis & Gen. 49, 24. inde, ubi est Pastor, Lapis Israelis: ex cœlo, ubi est Angelus & Mediator Testamenti, qui, ut oves suas, vindicat, alit, sustentat, protegit Israelem, ejusǫ, rupes est. Es. 28, 16. Ecce, ego is qui fundavit in Sione lapi- dem, lapidem probationis, angulum fundati funda- tissimi. Dan. 2, 34. 45. excisus est lapis, qui non erat sive ferebatur in manibus, & percussit imaginem. Ibi significatur Christi non tantum reprobatio, sed & exvisio ex terra viventium: quæ facta est χερσὶν ἀδί- κοις: qui lapis, non manibus hominum latus, sed sua- pte vi & virtute quasi motus, simulachrum percussit & comminuit. Zach. 3, 9, Ecce lapis, quem dedi coram Josua, quemq; ei in fiducia aspiciendum propo- sui, in eum conversi erunt oculi septem, h.e. multa- rum gentium & quidem in septem temporibus: Ec- ce cælabo cælaturas ejus, faciam ipsum insignem omni nomine & omnibus suis signis atque characteri- bus, & abstergam pravitatem Terræ ILLIUS uno die. Sed missis interpretationibus istis mere pre- cariis, quales in Commentariis suis in Scripturam passim infert, non è Scriptura effert autor vere mi- rabiles: id unum adhuc circa præsentem Psalmum observare juvat: Quod ille quidem non inelegan- ter a nostris quibusdam Interpp. totus de Christo accipiatur, si tamen omnia accuratius expendan- tur, præferenda videatur B. Lutheri nostri senten- tia, in aurea & cedro digna explicatione hujus Psal- mi 118. Tom. 5. Jenensi fol. 44. seqq. D. Crucige- ri Senioris præfatione approbata, qua Megalander prioribus versibus Davidem de se loqui censet, utpo- te qui in exemplum se omnibus fidelibus sistat, talia etiam patientibus, sed tandem vincentibus; vers. 19. desiderare tempora N. T. & manifestationem Evan- gelii, ac portas justitiæ phrasi Ebræa, qua portæ vo- cantur Curiæ, Scholæ, Synagogæ dici, quia in N. T. do- ctrina Evangelica viget de remissione peccatorum & justitia: versu vero 22. de Christo capite, ejusque hu- miliatione & exaltatione agi: vers. 24. Hæc est dies, quam fecit Dominus, præclare explicans de die N. T. quem facit Dominus sol justitiæ fulgore & lumine suo Mal. 4, 1. Quam sententiam repetit B. Lutherus, provocans ad dictum suum commentarium, in Ar- gumentis Psalmorum Tom. III. Witteberg. Lat. in h. Pl. Est gratiarum actio, & Psalmus ille, Confite- mini, quem ego unice admiror, & aureum esse pro- nuncio, qui sæpe me erexit, & consolatus est in tentatio- nibus meis. Gratias agit simul & prophetat de Chri- sto, per passionem ingresso in gloriam, qui Lapis est ille reprobatus, factus caput anguli, ut Christus etiam Matth. 21. citat. Et describit miris affectibus lætum diem Evangelii, diem salutis & pacis, diem gaudii & solationis, diem illum vere festum &c. Inter alia ostendit Ecclesiam & filios Dei conformes reddendos imagini filii. Cingendos undique afflictionibus, & per crucem & mortem glorificandos; Breve summarium res gravissimas hujus electi Psalmi non complectitur, plenam explicationem suppeditat meus Commenta- rius. Qui hic omnino conferri meretur.

Cæterum verba illa versus 22. lapidem quem re- probaverunt, Targum ita reddidit: Puerum dereli- querunt architecti, qui meruit, ut constitueretur Rex: Ex prava illa interpretatione, quasi de Davide puero sermo esset, non autem ex diversa codicis Ebrai le- ctione, quasi in eodem invenerint אבן ut Capellus contendit, id significatione Arabica & Rabbinica de puero explicans, quo de legi poterit Buxtorf. in Anti-Crit. p. 717.

## 118:27
Vers. 27.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

## 118:27
Vers. 27.

BIND THE SOLEMN DAY WITH CORDS EVEN UNTO THE HORNS OF THE ALTAR) חג indeed properly signifies a solemn day, but by metonymy it is taken for the victim of the solemn day, as appears in Es. 29, 1. and thus the Chaldean interpreter accepted it here. That בעבתים which the Greeks translate ἐν τοῖς πυκάζουσι, the Latin into thickets, signifies ropes rather: and the first word אסרו, bind, so that the sense may be, Bind the lamb with ropes (and lead it bound) even to the horns of the altar, where it was to be slaughtered.

Thus the Targum, Pagninus, Arias, Junius, the English, the Italian, the Genevan, Piscator, Drusius, Cocceius, Amama, the more recent Belgian version, as also Joh. Tarnov. Exercit. Bibl. p. 114. B. Franzius de Interpr. Script. p. 579. and others likewise render: bind the festive (victim or lamb) even to the horns of the altar, when the blessed

B. Luther (and the older Belgian [version] followed him) interprets it, having taken into account the custom and rite of the feast of tabernacles: 'Adorn the feast with boughs, even unto the horns of the altar.' He defends his translation against the erroneous sense of the Jews, because חג properly denotes a feast, but עבותים signifies boughs, and in the feast of tabernacles there was no need for an altar, seeing that it was only in Jerusalem: Let us bring forward the very words of B. Luther, which are read in Vol. 6, Altenburg, page 136, and Vol. XII, Witteberg, f. 378, from the tract 'Vom Dolmetschen' of the year 1533. Psal. 118, in the 27th verse: 'We knew full well that the Jewish Rabbis read thus: bind the Easter lamb with ropes, even unto the horns of the altar; whereas we Germans [read]: adorn the feast with boughs.' They make out of the word Hag (which actually means a feast or holiday) an Easter lamb, through their own stubbornness; and even if it were found elsewhere as they claim, they still cannot prove such a thing here. And where is it written that the Jews were to lead the Easter lamb with ropes to the altar, which everyone had to roast at home in his house and eat with his household, as they still do, even though they have no altar? Since, therefore, such is a Jewish erroneous sense in the text, and we know that this Psalm sings of Christ and his kingdom, and the words of this verse, according to the nature of the languages, give this sense: 'bind the feast with boughs,' we have clearly made it thus: 'adorn the feast with boughs,' which is the spiritual booth-feast or tabernacle-feast (which was the prefiguration of the Jews' booth-feast), even unto the horns of the altar. With the altar he indicates that it should be a spiritual booth-feast, where an altar had to be present; at the Jews' booth-feast there was to be no altar, but only at Jerusalem. And the meaning is that at the time of Christ, all feasts should be a daily feast, in which one joyfully preaches in faith, and thereby offers thanks to God; that is, to adorn the feast with boughs even unto the altar, to be joyful in the Word and faith, and thus to praise and laud God in Christ, who is our altar. The sense of Luther was also handed down by Schindler in the Lexicon Pentaglottum, p. 523; Dietemberg, likewise, and the Mainz version, as also Campensis, B. Christian Matthias, Colleg. II. Anti-Photin. p. 108, Mr. Dr. Geier, B. Mr. Dr. Glassius, Rhet. S. p. 61, and they do not disapprove of the same, but join it with the other in the notes to the German Bible of Tossanus, Frankfurt am Main edition. Cf. Vol. V, Jena, Luth. f. 69, f. b. But from which version Jansenius rashly carved out Papist processions: because the Holy Spirit expresses the solemn joy of Christians by the rite and ceremony of the Jews: whence the rite of those processions can no more be proven from this and similar passages than the use of the ceremonies of the feast of tabernacles and other Levitical ones in the New Testament.

Latin:

Vers. 27.

CONSTITVITE DIEM SOLEMNEM IN CONDEN- SIS VSQVE AD CORNV ALTARIS) חג quidam pro- prie diem solemnem significat, sed per μετωνυμίαν sumitur pro victima diei solennis, ut apparet Es. 29, 1. & ita hîc accepit Chaldæus interpres. Illud בעבתים quod Græci vertunt ἐν τοῖς πυκάζουσι, Latinus in condensos, funes potius significat: & vox prima אסרו, ligate, ut sensus sit, Ligate agnum funibus (& ligatum ducite) ad cornua usque altaris, ubi mactandus erat.

Ita Targum, Paginius, Arias, Junius, Angli, Italic. Genevens. Piscator, Drusius, Coccejus, Ama- ma, versio Belgica recentior, ut & Joh. Tarnov. Exercit. Bibl. p. 114. B. Franzius de Interpr. Script. p. 579. & alii pariter reddunt: vincite festivam (vi- ctimam vel agnum) usque ad cornua altaris, quum B.

B. Luther. (& Belgica antiquior eum sequuta) pensi habito more & ritu festi tabernaculorum interpre- tetur: Schmücket das Fest mit Meyen/ biß an die Hörner des Altars. Qui suam translationem con- tra Judæorum erroneum sensum tuetur, quod חג proprie festum notet, עבותים vero frondes signifi- cet, & in festo tabernaculorum nullo opus fuerit alta- ri, utpote quod Hierosolymis tantum erat: Adduca- mus ipsa B. Lutheri verba, quæ leguntur Tom. 6. Altenburg. pag. 136. & T. XII. Witteberg. f. 378. è tractat. Vom Dolmetschen de Anno 1533. Psal. 118. im 27. vers. wusten wir zu guter massen wohl, daß die Jüdischen Rabbini so lesen/ bindet das Osterlamm mit Seilen/ biß an die Hörner des Altars/ da wir also Teutschen, schmücket das Fest mit Meyen. Sie ma- chen aus dem Wort Hag, (welches eigentlich ein Fest oder Feyertag heist) ein Osterlamm/ durch eigene Thurst/ und obs gleich anderswo so erfunden würde/ als sie fürgeben so mögen sie doch hie nicht solches be- weisen, und wo stehets geschrieben, daß die Jüden das Osterlamm mit Stricken zum Altar solten führen/ welches ein jeglicher daheim in seinem Hause braten und mit seinen Gesinde essen muste, wie sie noch thun/ ob sie wohl keinen Altar haben? Weil denn solches ein Jüdischer irriger Sinn im Text, und wir wissen, daß dieser Psalm von Christo und seinem Reich sin- get, und die Worte dieses Verses, aus Art der Spra- chen, diesen Sinn geben/ bindet das Fest mit Meyen, haben wirs deutlich also gemacht, schmücket das Fest mit Meyen, welches ist die geistliche Laubrüst oder Lauberhütten-Fest, (welches Fürbilde war der Jü- den Laubrüst) biß an die Hörner des Altars. Mit dem Altar zeiget er an, daß es solte eine geistliche Laub- rüst seyn, da ein Altar bey seyn muste, bey der Jüden Laubrüst muste kein Altar seyn, sondern allein zu Je- rusalem, und ist die Meynung, daß zur Zeit Christi, alle Fest ein täglich Fest seyn sollen/ darin man frölich im Glauben predige, und damit GOtt Danckopffer thue, das heist, biß an den Altar das Fest mit Meyen schmücken, frölich seyn im Wort und Glauben, nnd also GOtt loben und preisen in Christo/ welcher unser Altar ist. Sensum Lutheri tradidit etiam Schindler. in Lexico Pentaglotto p. 523. Dietemberg. item, & Moguntina versio, ut & Campensis B. Christian. Matthias Colleg. II. Anti-Photin. p. 108. Dn. D. Geierus, B. Dn. D. Glassius Rhet. S. p. 61. nec eun- dem improbant, sed cum altero conjungunt notæ ad Bibl. Germ. Tossani Francof. ad Mœn. edit. Conf. T. V. Jenens. Luth. f. 69. f. b. E qua vero versione temere Jansenius processiones Papisticas ex- sculpsit: quia ritu & ceremonia Judæorum Spiritus Sanctus more solito exprimit gaudium solemne Christianorum: unde non magis illarum processio- num ritus, quam Ceremoniarum Festi tabernaculo- rum, aliarumque Leviticarum in N. T. usus ex hoc, & similibus locis probari potest.

## 119:1 Argument
PSALM CXIX. An alphabetical eulogy of the word of God.

It is alphabetical, with each letter repeated eight times.

Latin:

PSALM. CXIX. Elogium verbi Dei alphabeticum.

EST Alphabeticus, unaquaque litera octies repetita.

## 119:5
Verse 5. O THAT MY WAYS WERE DIRECTED TO KEEP THY STATUTES!

Bellarmine and Sa understand the commandments of God by 'justifications,' and from there they gather that we are justified by their observance through a second justification by growing in justice. But besides the fact that this consequence is futile, in the Hebrew there is the word חקיך, 'thy statutes,' not 'justifications.' Nor does it follow from the fact that David desires to keep the statutes of the Lord that he could be justified by the keeping of the statutes of the Lord; rather, David asks for this not as one to be justified, but as one already justified, whose study and observance is the statutes of the Lord. Indeed, both the benefits of God and the duties of man are handed down in this Psalm: in which the study of piety and the observance of the commandments of God is indeed commended, but our justification before God is not established in it. What of the fact that in v. 124 David prays that the Lord may deal with him according to His grace, and according to the word of grace or the Gospel in v. 58, by which he testifies that he is uniquely exhilarated and refreshed in v. 50, 72, 92? Therefore he teaches that the grace of God is his only comfort in v. 75, and he uniquely implores divine mercy in v. 77: 'Let thy grace be for my consolation; let thy mercy come, and I shall live'; and in v. 88: 'According to thy grace quicken me'; and he declares his faith, that he desires uniquely the SALVATION of the Lord, that is, JESUS his Savior, in whom he seeks salvation in v. 81, 123, 166, 174, sighing again in v. 159: 'according to thy grace quicken me,' and in v. 176: 'I have gone astray like a lost sheep, seek thy servant.'

Latin:

Vers. 5. UTINAM DIRIGANTUR VIÆ MEÆ AD CUSTODIENDAS JUSTIFICA- TIONES TUAS!

Bellarm. & Saa per justificationes præcepta Dei intelligunt, & inde colligunt, nos per eorum obser- vationem justificari justificatione secunda crescen- do in justitia. Sed præterquam quod futilis sit illa consequentia, in Ebræo habetur vox חקיך statuta tua: non justificationes. Nec inde quod desiderat David custodire statuta Domini, sequitur, eundem per custodiam statutorum Domini justificari potuis- se: imo petit hoc David non justificandus, sed jam justificatus, cujus est studium & observatio statuto- rum Domini. Nimirum traduntur in hoc Psalmo tum beneficia Dei, tum officia hominis: in quibus commendatur quidem studium pietatis, & observa- tionis mandatorum Dei, sed in eo non constituitur nostra coram Deo justificatio. Quid quod v. 124. pre- cetur David, ut secum agat Dominus secundum gra- tiam suam, & secundum verbum gratiæ seu Evange- lium v. 58. quo unice exhilarari sese, ac recreari te- statur v. 50. 72. 92. ideo gratiam Dei suum esse sola- tium unicum docet v. 75. & misericordiam divinam unice implorat v. 77. Sit age, gratia tua ad consolan- dum me; veniat misericordia tua, & vivam: & v. 88. Secundum gratiam tuam vivifica me: & fidem suam declarat, quod nempe unice SALUTARE Domi- ni desideret, hoc est, JESUM Salvatorem suum, in quo salutem quærit v. 81. 123. 166. 174. suspirans denuo v. 159. juxta gratiam tuam vivifica me, & v. 176. Erravi, ut ovis perdita, quære servum tuum.

## 119:28
Verse 28. MY SOUL SLEPT FOR GRIEF) In the Hebrew דלפה, that is, 'my soul dripped': that is, it was liquefied like wax. The Greeks translated that ἔσαξε, as Ambrose noted, who translates it 'dripped.' So also Hilary. From that, the scribes, having added two letters, made ἐνύσαξε, which is 'slept.'

Latin:

Vers. 28. DORMITAVIT ANIMA MEA PRÆ TÆ- DIO) In Hebræo דלפה, id est, stillavit anima mea: hoc est, liquefacta est ut cera. Id Græci verterunt ἔσαξε, ut notavit Ambrosius, qui vertit stillavit. Sic & Hilarius. Ex eo librarii, additis duabus literis fecere ἐνύσαξε, quod est dormitavit.

## 119:33
Verse 132. SET A LAW FOR ME O LORD THE WAY OF THY JUSTIFICATIONS, AND I WILL SEEK IT ALWAYS) In the Hebrew: 'Teach me the way of thy statutes.' That עקב in the Greek is 'always,' the Chaldean translates עד גמירא, 'even unto the end': David Kimchi, 'all my days.' It is the same Hebrew word below in 112, where the Chaldean translates in the same sense סופא, 'unto the end.' But the Greeks there [translate it] δι ἀντάμεψιν, 'for the sake of retribution': just as Aben-Ezra also took it here. And above in 19. 12, the LXX translated the same word ἀνταποδόσεις.

Vers. 89. FOR EVER THY WORD STANDS IN HEAVEN.

The Vulgate followed the Greek Interpreters in this and the two following verses: but the Chaldean expressed it more happily; the words in the source flow thus: The Lord is for ever; Thy word is firm in the heavens; Thy truth is unto generation: by it Thou hast fitted the earth, and it stands, (or, as it stood, or copulatively and it stands, that is, it consists by Thy word, which is truth,) According to Thy judgments (or Thy ordinances) they stand (all things) because all things are Thy servants; or, as all things serve Thee. In the heavens μετὰ συμπλοκῆς with the angels, and the blessed souls received, the word of God is firm; so that the providence of God regarding the heavens and heavenly things, who carries all things by His word, may be noted; and no less regarding the earth and men in it unto generation and generation. The Holy Psalmist teaches that the providence of God extends itself to all things, who not only created all things, but also governs them, so that all things may minister to His will. Conf. Dn. D. Seb. Schmied. in Coll. Bibl. pr. ad h. l. p. 206.

Vers. 105. THY WORD IS A LAMP UNTO MY FEET AND A LIGHT UNTO MY PATHS.

This is a clear testimony to the perspicuity of Holy Scripture. Upon which the Papists in vain cast darkness, that they may snatch the light from Scripture. Gretser the Jesuit says that not only the written, but also the delivered word is understood: But if this eulogy suits both, it will not be right to derogate it from Scripture itself: And it speaks entirely of it, because it recalls others destitute of tradition to the norm of the word v. 9. and thus describes the word of God, so that it is sufficiently clear that Holy Scripture, which was to him like a supreme Treasure and in the place of counselors v. 42. 72. is pointed out, of which Peter also explains this eulogy 2. Ep. 1, 19. The Jesuit therefore used another escape, he conceded that it is indeed a lamp, but in itself, not likewise to others, unless it is placed upon a candlestick, i.e. unless the authority of Ecclesiastical understanding and tradition is added to it. But what kind of lamp is that, to which is another lamp to be added, or a candlestick in its place? Does a candlestick add light to a lamp or to a light (by both of which names Scripture is honored)? The Jews, R. Kimchi, are more correct; just as one walking in darkness, if a lamp is in his sight, does not stumble, so let your words be like a lamp before me, that I may not sin in any way. And Aben-Ezra; as soon as one looks into the law, it explains doubts to him like a lamp, which warns a man not to fall into a pit. Which use it would not provide if the light were only in itself, not for others, for how would it direct us in faith and morals, as a lamp directs on a road, if it were destitute of light, or if light had to be expected from elsewhere? Whence Ps. 19:9. The commandment of the Lord is clear, enlightening the eyes. For the way or path here denotes the way of religion, faith, justice, and life. Ps. 143:10. Matt. 22:16. Luke 1:79. Acts 18:26. 2 Pet. 2:2. The eyes designate the intellect; for the eyes of the heart are understood, Eph. 1:18. The feet are said to be directed, whereby our steps and our actions are to be instituted according to the rule of the divine word, Gal. 6:16. Since, therefore, Scripture both illuminates our intellect and directs our feet, and guides all our steps and actions, and shines before us like a lamp and a light, so that we may not stray from the way of God with our feet, nor turn aside either to the right or to the left; Deut. 17:20, ch. 28:14, Josh. 1:7, nor walk in the darkness of ignorance, errors, or sins, it is necessary that Holy Scripture be in itself clear and perspicuous. Bellarmine says that Scripture is clear, l. 3, de V. D. c. 2, not because it is easily understood, but because, once understood, it illuminates a man; but the same could be said of the leaves of the Sibyl and any riddles whatsoever, namely, that they also in this way provide the use of a lamp and a light. On the contrary, therefore, David attributes the faculty of illumination to Scripture because it shines before us in this darkness and presents the divine mind to our mind, so that we may be directed by this lamp and illuminated by this light. Nor does he wish understanding and doctrine to be sought from other Doctors: but he teaches that Scripture makes us wiser than all those, v. 99. And how is Scripture a light to our paths if it is itself so obscure that its meaning cannot be understood, i.e., it cannot shine for us, but it is necessary to procure light for it from elsewhere? Therefore, Arias Montanus in the Preface to the Royal Work acknowledges the perspicuity of Scripture. This, he says, is the light which, illuminating the human mind, teaches the truth of all necessary things. And Genebrard on this passage. The Word of God is light, a lamp, a light, because it directs us in things to be done, believed, and hoped for, and provides guidance, so that we may not stumble anywhere and fall in the darkness of this life, and so that we may not stray from that way which leads to the blessed life. For it is the rule of faith and life, showing the way in darkness to eternal life. The interlinear gloss, Franc. de Puteo, and Dionysius the Carthusian acknowledge that Holy Scripture is indicated in this passage, along with Gregory the Great in Pastor. c. 44, as well as Salmeron, Gagneus, and Guillaudus in the title.

Verse 109. MY SOUL IS IN MY HANDS ALWAYS) A Hebrew manner of speaking, which signifies the greatest dangers: because what we hold in our hand can easily be snatched from us. Thus 1 Sam. 28:21, Job 13:14. Jerome defends this reading in his epistle, and Ambrose acknowledges that some codices had it thus. But those to whom this manner of speaking was unknown changed 'me' into 'you', which Apollinaris, the Ethiopian, the Arab, and the Roman Psalter follow.

Verse 112. I HAVE INCLINED MY HEART TO DO THY JUSTIFICATIONS FOREVER FOR THE SAKE OF RECOMPENSE.

Bellarmine, l. 5, de Justif. c. 8, proves from this that it is lawful to do good works with a view to eternal reward. Theod. Hackspan agrees with him on this passage and appeals to the consensus of the Remonstrants in the Script. Synod. Dordr. Defens. art. 1, p. 267. And the Apology for the Confession, as also Rivet, Ex. 20, p. 100. And that the Jews in the German version of the Psalm translated it thus, 'um willen guten Lohn', that is, for the sake of reward, the opinion of Aben-Ezra is almost the same, and the Arab rendered it thus, 'for the sake of eternal recompense'. But the Arabic translation is not that old, nor are the Jews to be listened to here, and nowhere in the Scriptures are we commanded to work with a view to the reward or recompense of eternal life, even if rewards of this life and the future life are promised to those who work out of grace. Finally, it is mercenary to work for the sake of a reward, and it is distinguished in vain with the Jesuit Pererius, that the love of reward is one thing, and mercenary love is another; for who would deny that to one who works with a view to a reward, and out of love for it, mercenary love is rightly attributed? There is certainly no reason why we should yield to the Jews (although some of them are sounder) and the Papists here, for it cannot be denied that the word 'עקב' means the same as 'always', and it is clear from v. 33, which illustrates this one of ours, where even the Vulgate itself rendered it no differently: 'Set before me, O Lord, the way of thy justifications, and I will seek it ALWAYS.' Why, therefore, should it not be rendered similarly: 'I have inclined my heart to do thy justifications for an age, always or continually', because it corresponds to 'תמיד'. Nor does it matter at all that David did not live forever in this life, for that 'לעולם' is also accustomed to be taken for the duration until the end of life, not to mention that the holiness of this life, once begun, is continued or rather consummated in the other life. For which reason the Psalmist also determined to study it all the days of his life and continually. Pagninus himself translated it 'until the end', that is, 'all my life'. R. D. Kimchi explains, 'all the days of my life'. Schindler, Helvicus, Gerhard, Glassius, Amama, etc., do not deny it to us. Coccejus, 'for an age until the end'; that is, until the consummation of the age. Dr. Gejer also noted Hackspan here.

Verse 130. THE DECLARATION OF THY WORDS ILLUMINATES.

Others render it: the opening of thy words. Mr. Dr. Seb. Schmid in his Biblical collection, p. 62, says that this is the simplest version, thy words illuminate the door, or entrance, and furthermore make the simple understand, so that the door or entrance is the end of our spiritual way, which Scripture illuminates, while it shines for us in such a way that it shows it to us, and makes the way clear, so that we may enter with unoffending foot. If you wish, see him adducing from this passage the perspicuity of Holy Scripture.

Latin:

Vers. 132. LEGEM PONE MIHI DOMINE VIAM JUSTIFICATIONVM TVARVM, AC EXQVIRAM EAM SEMPER) In Hebræo: Doce me viam statutorum tuo- rum. Illud עקב in Græco διά παντὸς, Chaldæus vertit עד גמירא ad consummationem usque: David Kimchi כל ימי omnibus diebus. Est eadem vox Hebræa infra 112. ubi Chaldæus eodem sensu vertit סופא ad finem. At Græci ibi δι ἀντάμεψιν, propter retributionem: quomodo & hîc accepit Aben-Esdra. Et supra 19. 12. eandem vocem LXX. verterunt ἀνταποδόσεις.

Vers. 89. IN ÆTERNUM VERBUM TUUM PERMANET IN COELO.

Sequutus est Vulgatus hoc & seqq. duobus versibus Græcos Interpretes: sed felicius expref- sit Chaldæus; Verba in fonte ita fluunt: In æternum est Dominus; Verbum tuum firmum est in cœlis; in generationem est veritas tua: per eam aptasti terram, & stat, (sive, ut steterit, sive copulative & stat, id est, consistit per verbum tuum, quod veritas est,) Juxta judicia tua (vel ordinationes tuas) stant (omnia) quoniam omnia sunt servi tui; vel, ut omnia servant tibi. In cœlis μετὰ συμπλοκῆς cum angelis, & beatis animabus acceptis verbum Dei firmum est; ut pro- videntia Dei quoad cœlos & cœlestia, qui verbo portat omnia, notetur; nec minus quoad terram & homines in ea in generationem & generationem. Ad omnia Dei providentiam sese porrigere, qui non omnia tantum creavit, sed etiam gubernat, ut voluntati suæ omnia ministrent, docet Hiero-Psal- tes. Conf. Dn. D. Seb. Schmied. in Coll. Bibl. pr. ad h. l. p. 206.

Vers. 105. LUCERNA PEDIBUS MEIS VERBUM TUUM ET LUMEN SEMI- TIS MEIS.

Luculentum hoc est perspicuitatis Scripturæ S. testimonium. Cui nequicquam tenebras suffun- dunt Papistæ, ut lucem eripiant Scripturæ. Gretserus Jesuita non scriptum solum, sed etiam traditum ver- bum intelligi ait: Verum si utrique hoc elogium convenit, Scripturæ ipsi etiam id derogandum non erit: Et de ea omnino loquitur, quia alios tradi- tione destitutos ad verbi normam revocat v. 9. atq; ita verbum Dei describit, ut satis liqueat scripturam S. quæ ipsi erat summi Thesauri instar & loco consi- liariorum v. 42. 72. indigitari, de qua etiam hoc elo- gium explicat Petrus 2. Ep. 1, 19. Alio ergo effugio usus Jesuita, lucernam eam quidem esse concessit, sed in se, non item aliis, nisi ponatur super candela- brum, h. e. nisi addatur ei Ecclesiasticæ intelligentiæ & traditionis autoritas. Sed qualis illa lucerna, cui lucerna alia addenda, aut ejus vicem candela- brum? Num candelabrum lucernæ aut lumini (quo utroque nomine honoratur scriptura) addit lucem? Rectius Judæi, R. Kimchi; sicut ambulans in tene- bris, si fuerit in conspectu ejus lucerna, non impingit, sic verba tua sint instar lucernæ coram me, ne quid peccem. Et Aben-Esra; simul ac legem quis inspicit, explicat ipsi dubia instar lucernæ, quæ hominem mo- net, ne in fovam cadat. Quem usum non præsta- ret, si tantum in se lumen esset, non aliis, quomodo enim dirigeret nos in fide & moribus, ut lucerna in via dirigit, si luce destitueretur, aut aliunde lux expectanda esset? unde Psal. 19, 9. Præceptum Do- mini lucidum est, illuminans oculos. Via enim seu semita hic viam religionis, fidei, justitiæ & vitæ notat. Psal. 143, 10. Matth. 22, 16. Luc. 1, 79. Actor. 18, 26. 2. Petr. 2, 2. Oculi intellectum designant; Intelli- guntur enim oculi cordis Ephes. 1, 18. pedes dirigi di- cuntur, qua nostri gressus, actionesque nostræ secun- dum regulam verbi divini instituendi Gal. 6. v. 16. Quum ergo scriptura & intellectum nostrum illu- minet, & pedes dirigat, omnesque gressus & actio- nes nostras dirigat, instar lucernæ & luminis nobis præluceat, ne pedibus nostris à via Dei aberremus, neq; vel ad dextram, vel ad sinistram declinemus; Deut. 17, 20. c. 28, 14. Jos. 1, 7. nec in tenebris igno- rantiæ, errorum aut peccatorum incedamus, utique in se lucidam & perspicuam oportet esse Scripturam Sacram. Bellarm. Scripturam dilucidam esse dicit l. 3. d. V. D. c. 2, non quod facile intelligatur, sed quod intellecta hominem illuminet; Sed idem de Sibyllæ fo- liis & ænigmatibus quibusvis dici posset, nimir. illa etiam hoc pacto lucernæ & luminis usum præbere. Ex adverso ergo David ideo illuminationis facul- tatem scripturæ tribuit, quia prælucet nobis in hac caligine, ac mentem divinam menti nostræ sistit, ut hac lucerna dirigamur & hoc lumine illustremur. Nec ab aliis Doctoribus intelligentiam & doctri- nam peti vult: sed omnibus istis sapientiores nos scripturam reddere docet v. 99. Et quomodo lu- men est semitis nostris scriptura, si ipsa obscura adeo, ut intelligi nequeat ejusdem sensus, h. e. lucere no- bis non possit, sed aliunde eidem lucem conciliare oporteat? Ideo agnoscit Arias Montanus in Præ- fat. Operis Regii perspicuitatem Scripturæ. Hæc, inquit, lux est, quæ humanam illustrans mentem omnium rerum necessariarum veritatem docet. Et Genebrard. in h. l. Verbum Dei est lux, lucerna, lu- men, quoniam ad Deum dirigit, in agendis, credendis, sperandis, & ducatum præstat, ne uspiam offendamus, & labamur in vitæ hujus tenebris, neve aberremus ab ea via, quæ ducit ad vitam beatam. Est enim fidei & vitæ regula, monstrans viam in tenebris ad vitam æ- ternam. Scripturam autem sacram indigitari h. l. glossa interlinearis, Franc. de Puteo, Dionysius à Ri- ckel Carthusianus agnoscunt cum Gregorio M. in Pastor. c. 44. ut & Salmeron, Gagneus & Guillau- dus in titul.

Vers. 109. ANIMA MEA IN MANIBVS MEIS SEM- PER) Loquendi genus Hebræum, quod summa pericula significat: quia quod manu tenemus, facile eripi nobis pot- est. Sic 1. Sam. 28, 21. Job. 13, 14. Defendit hanc lectionem in epistola Hiieronymus, & Ambrosius aliquos codices sic habuisse agnoscit. At quibus ignotum fuit id loquendi ge- nus, με mutarunt in σε, quod sequitur Apollinaris, Æthiops, Arabs, Psalterium Romanum.

Vers. 112. INCLINAVI COR MEUM AD FACIENDAS JUSTIFICATIONES TUAS IN ÆTERNUM PROPTER RETRIBUTIO- NEM.

Bellarm. l. 5. de Justif. c. 8. probat hinc, lici- tum esse bona operari intuitu mercedis æternæ. An- nuit ei Theod. Hackspan. ad h. l. & provocat ad con- sensum Remonstrantium in Script. Synod. Dordr. Defens. art. 1. p. 267. Et Apol. pro Confess. ut & Rivetum Ex. 20. p. 100. Et quod Judæi in version. Germ. Psalmi sic transtulerint um willen guten Lohn, id est, propter mercedem, eadem fere sit Aben- Esræ sententia, & Arabs ita reddiderit propter retri- butionem æternam. Sed Arabica translatio non ita antiqua est, nec Judæi hic audiendi, & nuspiam in Scripturis jubemur intuitu mercedis vel retributio- nis vitæ æternæ operari, etsi operantibus ex gratia promittantur præmia hujus & futuræ vitæ. Denique mercenarium est, in gratiam mercedis operari, ac frustra distinguitur cum Jesuita Pererio, aliud esse amorem mercedis, aliud amorem mercenarium; nam qui operatur intuitu mercedis, & ex amore ejusdem, ei amorem mercenarium recte tribui, ec- quis neget? Nulla utique causa est, cur Judæis quamvis ex his nonnulli saniores sint) & Papistis hic pollicem premamus, nam vocem עקב idem esse quod semper negari non potest, & è v. 33. luculen- tum est, qui hunc nostrum illustrat, ubi etiam ipsa Vulgata aliter non reddidit, legem pone mihi Domi- ne viam justificationum tuarum, & exquiram eam SEMPER. Cur ergo non similiter ita reddatur: inclinavi cor meum ad faciendas justificationes tuas in seculum semper vel jugiter, quia respondet τῷ תמיד. Nec ad rem quicquam facit, quod David in æter- num non vixerit in hac vita, nam illud לעולם de du- ratione usque ad finem vitæ etiam accipi solet, ut ta- ceam, quod inchoata illa sanctitas hujus vitæ conti- nuetur vel consummetur potius in altera vita. Qua- propter & omnibus diebus vitæ suæ & jugiter illi studere constituit Hierophaltes. Pagnignus ipse ver- tit in finem usque, hoc est, tota vita mea. R. D. Kim- chi explicat, omnibus diebus vitæ meæ. Non abnuunt nobis Schindlerus, Helvicus, Gerhardus, Glassius, A- mama &c. Coccejus in seculum ad finem; id est us- que ad consummationem seculi. Notavit etiam hic Hackspanium Dn. D. Gejerus.

Vers. 130. DECLARATIO SERMONUM TUORUM ILLUMINAT.

Alii reddunt: apertio verborum tuorum. Dn. D. Seb. Schmid. in coll. Bibl. pr. p. 62. simplicis- simam versionem hanc esse ait, verba tua illumi- nant ostium, seu introitum, & porro intelligere fa- ciunt simplices, ut ostium seu introitus sit terminus viæ nostræ spiritualis, quem illuminat scriptura, dum ita nobis lucet, ut nobis eum monstret, viam- que claram faciat, quo possimus inoffenso pede in- trare. Quem adferentem ex h. l. perspicuitatem Scripturæ S. si lubet, vide.

## 120:1 Argument
PSALM CXX. Deliverance from the arrows of a sharp tongue.

A SONG OF DEGREES) The same inscription for the following Psalms up to 130: because they were accustomed to be sung by the Levites from the steps of the temple: concerning which see Ezek. 40.

In Greek ἀναβαθμῶν, because the Hebrew word המעלות signifies not descents, but degrees of ascents. But the steps of Solomon's temple are not noted, of which there were fifteen in the ascent from the middle of the court of the women to the court of the men, on each of which individual Psalms were sung by the Levites, as R. Solomon, Saadia, Lyranus, Augustine also in Psalm 133 (which is the last of the Psalms of degrees), and Constantinus L'Empereur Midd. p. 71; nor the ascent of the Jews from Babylon to Jerusalem, Ezra 7, verse 9, as Basil, Theodoret, Euthymius, and Stephanus wished, to whom not all these Psalms are appropriate; nor the ascent to the three solemn feasts of the Israelites: but rather of a most excellent song, as Piscator, Junius, Muis, Gataker in Cinn. p. 122, and from our own B. Glassius Philol. S. l. 3. p. 107. either concerning a higher voice or place as B. Luther seems to take it, or concerning the ascension of devotion, with which these Psalms are full, inasmuch as by it we ascend more and more from earthly to heavenly things, we ascend in heart from worldly things to God, as seemed good to Bellarm. & B. Joh. Tarnov. in the Psalms of degrees: Which latter opinion is by no means to be held as the last: since by reason of excellence other Psalms can easily compete with these. Although indeed B. Tarnovius joins these three explanations together, because these songs, if not by their subject matter, at least by the magnitude of their affections and some continuous brevity, as also by the variety of things, surpass other Psalms, and therefore deservedly have been sung with a higher voice and in a more sublime place, and for that very reason, so that all may learn to ascend in their mind to God, yet all such diverse meanings cannot agree to the same word, even if of the plural number, in the same place. David therefore ascends to God in this Psalm, out of the anguish & spiritual affliction of his pilgrimage in the tabernacles of Kedar, recalling to his memory the pilgrimage from the true heavenly fatherland in this earthly exile: he lifts his eyes from earthly mountains to God in the highest heavens in the following Psalm 121. he desires in Psalm 122. as far as the elevation of the mind in the ascent to the house of the Lord, to be carried up into the heavenly Jerusalem, where the Lord himself will be our temple Apoc. 21. verse 22. Thus the pious soul oppressed by evils ascends in its prayers even to heaven, to the Lord, Psalm 123. not without a desire for liberation from every evil, & for being carried up to the heavenly kingdom of the Lord 2. Tim. 4. verse 18. & when he celebrates the liberation accomplished in these lands in Psalm 124. he is to be carried up by devotion to the eternal glorification, which, having been snatched from every misery, we shall institute in the heavens with the whole triumphant Church. No less in Psalm 125. does the devout mind ascend above itself by trusting, & by confessing, with a desire for the eternal celebration of the Lord: & by preaching in Psalm 126. he recalls the ascent from captivity, the blessed ἀvάβασιν (ascent) from the prison of this world, which ought never not to enter our mind, never not to be desired, where they shall reap with eternal joy, who sow here with tears. But when we meditate on the custody & blessing of the Lord in this age according to Psalm 127. we ought to lift up our mind to the security & blessedness of the elect in the other age: When we proclaim the bodily & spiritual benefits, which befall the faithful who fear God & the Church in these lands, according to Psalm 128. devotion is to be elevated to the heavenly benefits, stored up for the elect in the supernal Jerusalem; & from the victory in the militant Church in Psalm 129. we ought to ascend to the ἐπινίκιον (song of victory) in the triumphant Church, aspiring by crying from the depths to God in the highest according to Psalm 130. until our hope is fully fulfilled; and through humiliation to strive for exaltation according to the ἀναγωγὴν (anagogy/ascent) of Psalm 131. Furthermore, when the Hiero-Psalmist sang anthropopathically of the ascent of God with the ark into the sanctuary, he ascends by his devotion to the true ark of the covenant, the Messiah, in whom the whole fullness of the Deity dwells, to be elevated into the heavenly sanctuary, so that his crown may flourish eternally Psalm 132. verse 18. Apoc. 11. verse 19. Singing of the fruits of the concord of the pious in this life, which is truly βίος ἀβίωτος (a life not worth living), we are carried forward to the happiness of the other life remaining for the pious & peaceful, and that for an age Psalm 133. verse 3. from the celebration of the servants of the Lord in the temple of the Lord Psalm 134. which is the last Psalm of the ascents, the faithful soul is carried up to the eternal Hallelujah, of those serving before the throne of the Lord in the heavenly temple, Apoc. 7. verse 14. If our mind is thus elevated by devotion, the present Psalms will truly be Psalms of degrees or ascents. If anyone should desire the Commentaries of B. Luther on these 15 Psalms of degrees, he will find the same in Vol. III, Wittenberg, Latin.

Latin:

PSALM. CXX. Liberatio a sagittis linguæ acutæ.

CANTICVM GRADVVM) Eadem inscriptio Psalmo- rum sequentium ad 130. usque: quod cantari solerent à Le- vitis de gradibus templi: de quibus vide Ezech. 40.

IN Græco ἀναβαθμῶν, quia vox Ebræa המעלות non descensum, sed ascensionum gradus importat. Non autem notantur gradus templi Salomonei, quo- rum quindecim fuisse in ascensione è medio atrii fœminarum ad atrium virorum, in quorum singulis singuli Psalmi à Levitis decantati sint, ut R. Salomo, Saadia, Lyranus, Augustinus etiam in Psal. 133. (qui Psalmorum graduum ultimus est) & Constantinus L’Eumpereur Midd. p. 71. nec de ascensione Judæo- rum è Babylone in Hierusalem Esr. 7. vers. 9. ut Basilius, Theodoretus, Euthymius, & Stephanus vo- luere, cui non omnes hi Psalmi conveniunt; nec de ascensione ad tria festa Israëlitarum solemnia: sed vel de Cantio excellentissimo, ut Piscator, Junius, Muis, Gataker. in Cinn. p. 122. & è nostris B. Glas- sius sius Philol. S. l. 3. p. 107. vel de altiori voce aut loco ut B. Lutherus accipere videtur, vel de ascensione devotionis, qua Psalmi hi pleni sunt, utpote qua magis magisque à terrenis ad cœlestia ascendimus, à mundanis ad Deum corde ascendimus, uti Bellarm. & B. Joh. Tarnov. in Psalm. grad. visum: Quæ postrema sententia minime postrema habenda: cum ratione excellentiæ alii Psalmi facile cum hisce certare possint. Quanquam vero B. Tarnovius conjungat simul hasce tres explicationes, quod hæc cantica si non subjecta materia saltem affectuum magnitudine & brevitate aliqua continua, ut & varietate rerum alios Psalmos transcendant, adeoque merito altiori voce & in loco sublimiore decantata sint, & propterea quidem, ut omnes discant ad Deum sua mente ascendere, omnes tamen adeo diversæ fignificationes eidem voci, etsi pluralis numeri, in eodem loco convenire nequeunt. Ascendit ergo ad Deum David hoc Psalmo, ex angustia & spirituales afflictione peregrinationis in tabernaculis Kadarenis, revocans sibi in memoriam peregrinationem à vera cœlesti patria in hoc terreno exilio: elevat oculos suos à montibus terrenis ad Deum in cœlis altissimis Psalm. sequente 121. desiderat Psalm. 122. quantum ad mentis elevationem in adscensione ad domum Domini, evehi in cælestem Hierosolymam, ubi Dominus ipse templum nostrum erit Apoc. 21. vers. 22. Sic anima pia malis oppressa precibus suis in cœlum usque conscendit, ad Dominum, Psalm. 123. non absque desiderio liberationis ab omni malo, & evectionis ad cæleste regnum Domini 2. Tim. 4. vers. 18. & cum liberationem in his terris factam celebrat Psal. 124. evehenda est devotione ad æternam glorificationem, quam erepti ex omni miseria in cœlis, cum universa triumphante Ecclesia instituemus. Nec minus Psalm. 125. ascendit mens devota supra se confidendo, & confitendo, cum desiderio æternæ celebrationis Domini: & deprædicando Psalm. 126. ascensionem ex captivitate recolit beatam ἀvάβασιν è carcere hujus mundi, quæ nunquam non animum nostrum subire, nunquam non desiderari debet, ubi cum æterno jubilo metent, qui cum lachrymis hic seminant. Cum vero meditemur custodiam & benedictionem Domini in hoc seculo juxta Psal. 127. ad securitatem & beatitudinem electorum in altero seculo mentem attollere debemus: Cum beneficia corporalia & spiritualia, quæ fidelibus Deum timentibus & Ecclesiæ in his terris obtingunt, secundum Psalm. 128. prædicamus, elevanda est devotio ad beneficia cœlestia, electis in Hierosolyma superna reposita; & à victoria in Ecclesia militante Psal. 129. ad ἐπινίκιον in triumphante Ecclesia ascendere, è profundis clamando adspirare ad Deum in excelsis juxta Psalm. 130. debemus, donec spes nostra plene adimpleatur; ac per humiliationem contendere ad exaltationem secundum ἀναγωγὴν Psalmi 131. Porro cum de ascensu Dei ἀνθρωποπαθῶς cum arca in sanctuarium cecinit Hiero-Psaltes, adscendit devotione sua ad veram arcam fœderis Messiam, in quo tota habitat Deitatis plenitudo, elevandum in cœleste sanctuarium, ut æternum floreat corona ejus Psalm. 132. vers. 18. Apoc. 11. vers. 19. Fructus concordiæ piorum in hac vita, quæ verè βίος ἀβίωτος, decantantes provehimur ad felicitatem alterius vitæ piis & pacificis manentem, iisque in seculum Psal. 133. vers. 3. à celebratione servorum Domini in templo Domini Psalm. 134. qui ultimus est ascensionum Psalmus, ad Halleluja æternum, servientium coram throno Domini in templo cœlesti, Apoc. 7. vers. 14. anima fidelis evehitur. Si mens nostra ita elevabitur devotione, Psalmi præsentes vere erunt graduum vel afcenfionum Pfal- mi. Commentationes B. Lutheri in hofce 15. gra- duum Pfalmos si quis defideret, inveniet easdem T. III, Witteberg. Latino.

## 120:3
ver. 3. WHAT SHALL BE GIVEN TO THEE OR WHAT SHALL BE ADDED TO THEE FOR A DECEITFUL TONGUE?

Bellarmine strives to excuse the Vulgate version, but in vain. Others render the Hebrew: What shall a deceitful tongue give thee? Which words are conveniently explained in the vocative case, by direct address to the deceitful tongue, or the slanderer, as if to say: what fruit will you reap, O deceitful tongue, from your slanders? Because, although you, the slanderer, can harm your neighbor like a tongue of arrows and coals, no profit will accrue to you from it; as with Cajetan and Aben Ezra, Stephanus, Bucer, Calvin, the Genevans, Cocceius, Simon de Muis, and also B. Tarnovius on this passage. Thus there is no need, because of the diversity of gender in the verb יתן, to understand God under the noun לשׁון, what will God give thee? as do the Chaldean, Kimchi, R. Solomon, Ludov. de Dieu, and Cloppenburg in his Opuscula, page 272, as well as the Belgian Interpreters. done, who therefore also explain the following words, added in the place of a response, namely the arrows and coals, as the swiftest, most vehement, and utterly consuming punishments of God, with Theodoret, Basil, Chrysostom, Hilary, and Euthymius, likewise Lactantius and Delrio, Vol. II, Adagia, page 109. Although indeed the arrows of the Lord, lightnings, and juniper coals can be referred to hell (Psalm 7, verses 13, 14; Psalm 11, verse 6; Psalm 140, verse 11), yet the exclamation added in verse 5 teaches that the Psalmist is here describing the injuries intended for him by the deceitful tongue: Woe is me, that I sojourn in Meshech!

Latin:

verf. 3. QUID DETVR TIBI AVT QVOD OPPONATVR TIBI AD LINGVAM DO- LOSAM?

Vulgatam versionem excusare nititur Bellarm. sed frustra. Alii Ebræa reddunt: Quid dabit tibi lingua dolosa? Quæ verba commode in casu vo- candi explicantur, oratione directa ad linguam do- losam, seu calumniatorem, q. d. quem fructum capies, o dolosa lingua ex calumnis tuis? quia lingua sagittis & carbonibus simili nocere quidem calumniator poteris proximo, tibi autem nihil inde accedet emolumenti; ut cum Cajetano & Aben- Efra Stephanus, Bucerus, Calvinus, Genevenses, Coccejus, Simon de Muis, nec non B. Tarnovius in h. l. Ita non opus est ob diversitatem generis in verbo יתן ut nomine לשׁון Deum subintelligant, quid dabit tibi Deus? ut à Chaldæo, Kimchio, R. Salom. Ludov. de Dieu, & Cloppenburg. in opusc. pag. 272. ut & Belgicis Interpp. factum, qui proinde & sequentia responsionis loco adjecta sagittas nempe ac carbones de pœnis Dei celerrimis, vehe- mentissimis & prorsus consummantibus explicant, cum Theodoreto, Basilio, Chrysostomo, Hilario & Eu- thymio, Lactantio item & Delrione Tom. II. Adag. pag. 109. Quanquam vero sagittæ Domini, fulgura & prunæ juniperorum ad gehennam re- ferri possint (Pfalm. 7. vers. 13. 14. Psalm. 11. vers. 6. Psalm. 140. vers. 11.) hic tamen describere Pfalmen damna sibi per linguam dolosam intenta exclamatio subjuncta vers. 5. docet: Væ mihi, quod exulem in Mesech!

Verse 4.

WITH DESOLATING COALS) In Hebrew: With coals of juniper, which Jerome writes to Fabiola are most burning.

Verse 5.
