Then κατ' ἔξω (externally) because all wisdom is from him, by reason of his triple office: who as Priest has merited true wisdom for us (1 Corinthians 1, verse 30) and by eternal intercession obtains the same: as King he not only governs all things most wisely, but also imparts wisdom to the needy: as Prophet he informs us of true wisdom for salvation both immediately and αὐτοπροσώπως (in his own person), and through his ministers and mediately: because all things are explained in the present passage, the eternal generation and possession of wisdom (verse 22), then the acquisition of true and saving wisdom, for whose sake he testifies that his greatest delights were to be with the sons of men and to find life and salvation, who find themselves (verse 35), because he willed to be with us through the incarnation, so that he might merit for us life and salvation, and thus that saving wisdom. Furthermore, there is claimed for wisdom itself that which is required for the rule of the world and the government of the Church (verse 15). Mine is counsel, mine is prudence: By me Kings reign, etc. (verses 14, 15). Finally, the information concerning true wisdom for salvation is here attributed to him at length and primarily: to which wisdom everywhere cries out and utters its voice, so that it may invite us to perceive it and make us partakers of it: for which it sends out its handmaids, and calls to the citadel and walls of the city: if anyone is a little one or simple, let him come to me, etc. (chapter 9, verse 2). But that which is signified here by the name of Wisdom is also signified by the name of Prudence (verse 1): because those names are used as synonyms; and the same thing is expressed in different words to signify the ardor, desire, and continuous act of the invitation of Wisdom; Does not wisdom cry out, and prudence utter its voice? For those words חכמה wisdom, and תבונה are accustomed to be used among the Hebrews κατ' ἰσοδυναμίαν (as equivalents), e.g., when in Proverbs 3, verse 19 it is said: The Lord by wisdom founded the earth, he established the heavens by prudence: His wisdom the abysses began (Jeremiah 11, verse 12, chapter 11, verse 15), who prepares the world in his Wisdom and by his prudence extends the heavens. Then if there is any distinction at all, it is indicated that the Son of God, the hypostatic Wisdom and intelligence or prudence, is the fountain, source, and principle of all Wisdom, and intelligence, and prudence. Whence he deserves to be named no less by the latter than by the former. The plural חכמות is also used (Proverbs 9, verse 1, chapter 10, verse 20) for eminence and perfection: because the Son of God is the whole Wisdom and the author of all Wisdom.

Furthermore (2.), because Solomon pursues the invitation of Wisdom especially, when he says that Wisdom cries out, and that prudence gives its voice, that it stands on the highest and lofty summits above the way near the gates of the city, that it speaks in the very doorways, and says, O men, I cry out to you, and my voice is to the sons of men, understand, O simple ones, craftiness, etc., what Wisdom does he understand rather than the one whose proper duty this is, to invite us to true, heavenly, and saving doctrine and wisdom, namely the eternal Son of God himself, τὸν λόγον ὑποστατικὸν (the hypostatic Word)? For no one has seen God at any time; the only-begotten, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him (John 1, verse 18). No one knows the Father except the Son, and he to whom he wills to reveal him (Matthew 11, verse 27). For since here the principal cause, fountain, and source of wisdom is indicated, where the communication of wisdom is treated, and this principal cause, the supreme author of wisdom, is set over the ministerial causes which serve him (chapter 9, verse 2), what is understood more conveniently by the name of wisdom in this place than Wisdom itself, the hypostatic, eternal Son of God? And therefore Christ himself, when he deals with the mission of the ministers of the Word to this act of invitation, calls himself the Wisdom of God, and teaches that he is that Wisdom of which Solomon testified (Luke chapter 11, verse 49): Furthermore, the Wisdom of God also said: I will send to them Prophets and Apostles. See Matthew 23, verse 33. Thus, therefore, the name of Wisdom is to be accepted here, as it designates him who is the author and principal cause of the life-giving communication of Wisdom and sends out the ministers of the word, so that he may make us partakers of the same: that is, with Wisdom itself as interpreter, Christ the Son of God.

Thirdly, since the actions of supposita (individual substances) are proper, and those works are truly personal, that wisdom cries out, that it utters its voice, that it stands in the middle of the paths, that it speaks in the doorways, saying, I cry out to you, if these are to be taken properly, they designate the hypostatic Wisdom, or that which is in reality a person. For no one but a person utters a prudent voice and addresses men. Thus to speak of great things, to preach right things, to prepare a banquet, and to invite to it, and to send out those who invite, are the works of a person: just as there is no doubt that the handmaids who are sent out by Wisdom to invite us to the banquet are persons, so there is much less doubt concerning the wisdom to which these minister, and by which they are sent out, that it is a true person.

Fourthly, Wisdom is described as a person, since not only a voice, speech, and oration are attributed to her, but also lips, a throat, meditation, discipline, and doctrine, as the Teacher of all wisdom, which certainly point to Christ. For He is our only Teacher, Matt. 23, v. 10. O men, I call to you, and my voice is to the sons of men: Hear, for I am about to speak of great things. And my lips shall be opened to proclaim what is right. My throat shall meditate on truth, and my lips shall detest the wicked. All my words are just, there is nothing crooked or perverse in them, etc. To whom do these things apply more than to the λόγῳ ὑποσατι- xῷ, who is truth itself, John 14, v. 6. the מבשׂר Evangelist, Is. 41, v. 27. the teacher of peoples, Is. 55, v. 4. that Lord, whose is the word of truth, Apoc. 19, 10. Col. 3, 16. 1 Tim. 6, 3. Cf. Ps. 45, 3. Cant. 5, 16.

Fifthly, this wisdom claims for itself attributes which do not befit anyone but a person: I, Wisdom, dwell in counsel or craftiness, namely pious and holy, which is true prudence, Matt. 10, 16. by which phrase it is hinted that He is truly prudent, and the fountainhead of all prudence, just as He is said to dwell in unapproachable light, because He is most luminous and the source of all light, 1 Tim. 6, v. 16. Cf. Col. 2, v. 3. And I find the knowledge of knowledges, that is, I cause those who worship me to find it, as Mercerus explains by metonymy: or I find, that is, I have it most present and proper: just as GOD is said to search hearts, that is, to have them most thoroughly perceived: Arrogance and pride and the perverse way, and the double-tongued mouth, I detest: Mine is counsel, & wisdom, or virtue (as in Job 6:12, the Hebrew word is rendered, and thus the other clause of this verse will express almost the same thing in other words, for the sake of emphasis & confirmation) is my intelligence, mine is fortitude. But that wisdom which is the fountain of all prudence, and which has as its own the knowledge of all skill, and produces it in us, to which is attributed the hatred and detestation of pride, impiety, and falsehood: to which is claimed counsel and wisdom or virtue, fortitude, and intelligence, it must be a hypostasis and a person: since these things belong only to a person: nor should power and fortitude be essential to wisdom, nor should divine attributes be confounded: but upon the Messiah let the Spirit of counsel and fortitude rest, Isa. 11:2.

Sixthly, the effects, which are attributed to it as an architectural cause, argue for a hypostasis, such as the institution, instruction, and direction of magistrates: concerning which it thus testifies: By me Kings reign, and lawgivers decree justice: by me princes rule, and the powerful decree justice. That preposition BY ME denotes the principal cause, as in Psalm 18:30, Psalm 60:14. Then the love and care of the pious: concerning which these things are subjoined: I love those who love me, and those who watch for me in the morning shall find me. Furthermore, the communication of delights, glory, and justice, which proceed from this wisdom, and are its fruits: v. 18, 19. as well as presence in the ways of justice and in the midst of the paths of judgment, so that, namely, extremes may be avoided: finally, true love: that I may cause those who love me to possess (true) Substance, and that I may fill the treasures of their good heart with spiritual and heavenly goods: Matt. 12:35, concerning which see. Mr. Dr. Gejerus, our friend and brother to be honored in Christ, in his Commentary on this place, p. 400. Thus, therefore, the hypostatic Wisdom invites everyone to the love and worship of itself, by various arguments: from the plenary possession of wisdom which is found in it, from true holiness, from counsel and virtue, from the prudence of government which is had from it, from the love, care, and splendid remuneration which it exhibits, from the love and leading to a true inheritance, or possession and abundance of all goods, which Christ promises and in reality bestows upon those who love him and seriously seek him, or watch for him in the morning, 2 Tim. 4:7.

Seventhly, in a peculiar way, and especially, the hypostatic Character is to be observed, namely, the eternal generation of the Son of God. Since this is expressed here in explicit words, it does not allow us to doubt that it is a question here of the hypostatic wisdom. Of which it itself, in splendid and most emphatic words, if ever elsewhere, here through the most wise King, exhibits an eminent description, designating (1) Its principle and origin, JEHOVAH God the Father, which relationship it expresses with the word קָנַנִי; HE POSSESSED ME; for this implies the POSSESSOR, and thus the AUTHOR of Wisdom: who possessed it, or acquired it, namely by generation, just as that word in Gen. 4:1 occurs concerning possession through generation. For that word is used concerning God in three ways, namely, that he possesses by way of creation, Gen. 14:19, 22, Ps. 104:24, Ps. 139:13; by way of gracious separation and adoption or recreation, Deut. 32:6, Ps. 74:2. Ps. 78, Isa. 11:11, & by way of generation, Gen. 4:1. Since, therefore, it did not possess wisdom by the first two ways, it remains that it is said to have possessed it by way of generation. Jehovah, therefore, here as possessor is God the Father. (2.) It designates its generation, as a hypostatic property: He possessed, by generation, ME. This Wisdom, therefore, is possessed, or was acquired by GENERATION; and thus it is begotten Wisdom, that is, the Son of God, by which word Christ is designated by Solomon in Prov. 30:4. Which generation it itself also explained by the word חוללתי v. 24, as it denotes in the proper sense the act of conception or bringing forth, Job 14:7, ch. 26:5, Isa. 51:7. & in the Targum it is otherwise explained by the word איתילדת from the Rabbi's ילד, he begat, which occurs in Ps. 2:7 concerning the eternal generation of the Son of God: here it is rendered by the word אחבטנור from בטן, womb, because wisdom was as it were conceived in the womb of God, or as the Basel edition has אתבניך, as if built and filiated from בנה, he built, and בן, son. Since, therefore, one must not depart from the property of the word, and by the Hebrew word generation or production from the substance of another is properly implied, it must be established that the characteristic property of the Son of GOD is designated here: which, so that it may be the more impressed upon our mind, which is never sufficiently learned or believed, is expressed again in v. 25. Which, therefore, clearly convinces that the discourse here is about a person, and indeed about the eternal Son of God. Some also investigate that personal property in the word נסכתי v. 23, I was anointed before the age, because by the divine essence communicated to the Son through eternal generation, the divine Majesty and Empire over created things was also communicated. But that word נסכתי in Ps. 2:6, I have anointed my King, is openly distinguished from the generation of the Son of God, concerning which v. 7 treats: and the anointing here is properly the designation of the Son, begotten from eternity, to an office not only Royal, but also Priestly and Prophetic, made from eternity, just as Kings, Priests, and Prophets were accustomed to be inaugurated to their office by anointing: Therefore Rabbi Levi Ben Gerson rendered it, Power, and Principality, and magnificence have been given to me. This, however, is undoubted, that that anointing and designation pertains to a person, and cannot be said of any attribute in God, or of the Word and Law of God, and therefore the hypostatic Wisdom must necessarily be understood here. (3) The eternity of Wisdom is expressed. Jehovah possessed me ראשית דרכו which some explain as, The beginning of his way: Understanding an effective, not a material, beginning: just as the Son of GOD is called ἡ ἀρχὴ τῆς κτίσεως τοῦ θεοῦ in Rev. 3:14. But the Holy Scripture is engaged in describing eternity, from priority, so to speak, before the works of creation, which the appended paraphrases teach, therefore here the Chaldean, Aquila, the Vulgate, B. Luther, and others understand the letter Bet: בראשית IN THE BEGINNING OF HIS WAY, that is, of the works of creation. For the works of God are the ways of God, Deut. 32:4, 2 Sam. 22:31, Isa. 55:8, Rom. 11:33. And regard is had here to the beginning of Genesis בראשית chap. 1:1, just as in John 1:1 in our parallel passage, where by the same reasoning the eternity of the λόγος is expressed, as here that of wisdom. Which it further explains by a remarkable ὑπομονή, so that wisdom may inculcate it more and more: before his works, even then מאז FROM THEN (which is read concerning eternity in Ps. 93:2) before the age (or from eternity) I was anointed: from the beginning, before the earth, when there were not yet depths, I was conceived or begotten: when there were no fountains heavy with waters: before the mountains were founded, before the hills I was conceived; As yet he had not made the earth, and the rivers, and the foundations of the world: When he prepared the heavens ושם אני then I was. Which words, I was conceived, I was begotten, then I was with you, testify not to a simple existence, but to a true hypostasis and subsistence, which the Son of GOD has had from eternity.

Eighthly, the hypostasis of Wisdom is gathered from the work of creation. For since it introduces the works of creation so prolixly here, and testifies that it already existed before them, it also makes itself the maker of all those things: just as it is said of the λόγος in John 1:1, 3, not only that it already existed in the beginning of the creation of all things, but also that all things were made through it. For thus v. 30 in this place Wisdom ואהיה אצלו אמון I was beside him as a master workman. It is certainly not said of a divine attribute that it is beside the Father, or near: But just as of the λόγῳ ὑποστατικῷ John ch. 1 v. of itself, I was beside him, so that St. John seems to have alluded to our passage, or to have wished to illustrate the same. Furthermore, it says not only that it was beside the Father, but also makes itself the OPIFICER of all things. For as the cognate word אמן Cant. 7 v. 2 denotes an artificer, so also the present word אמון is taken for an artificer or opificer Jerem. 46 v. 25, ch. 52 v. 15, Nah. 3 v. 8, therefore the LXX render it ἁρμόζουσα. The Vulgate, I was with him composing all things. Irenaeus, I was beside him fitting. Tertullian, I was with him joining. But what Wisdom was the artificer and opificer of all things, if not the Son of God, through whom all things were made, and without whom nothing was made that was made.

Ninth, from the play and delights of Wisdom. For this Wisdom was the delight or amusement of God the Father, and played before God the Father at all times, it played also in the world, and its singular delights are to be with the sons of men. Which do not befit an essential attribute of God, or the Word and law of God, much less Wisdom habitual in us, but the person, or hypostatic Wisdom: and they fit the Son of God most excellently. And I was delights daily שעשועים which imports a notable and most pleasant amusement of a lovable thing, which we can never sufficiently behold, meditate upon, and embrace, and it occurs concerning the delights of David in the Word of God Ps. 119 v. 14, 77, 92, 143, 174, and concerning the lovable little son Jer. 31, 20: therefore the most sweet Son of delights is indicated here, in whom God the Father has his pleasure Matth. 3 v. 17. Whence the LXX rightly ἧ προσέ- χαιρες to whom he was rejoicing. And also the Catena of the Greeks: I was, to whom he was gently smiling, to whom he was showing affection, or with whom he was joyfully rejoicing יום יום day and day, that is, both in the day of eternity, in that eternal היום of which we spoke at Ps. 2 v. 7, and also in the יום or day of the age, playing before his face at all times, pleasant, like a Son, and a most sweet boy, offering spectacles to the Father; which Wisdom does by creating various things, and by working most wisely and most easily, so that they are at least play to him, and most sweetly, and in such a way that God himself is delighted by them Gen. 1 v. 31, Job 1 v. 3, ch. 5 v. 17, 19, 20. But he adds: I play in the world of his earth: which was done peculiarly when Wisdom appeared to the Patriarchs, Prophets, and other worshippers of him in the Old Testament and when it was manifested in the flesh in the New. Testament, where it exhibited most pleasant spectacles to the world, so that it is understood that it makes and has made those delights both with God the Father and also with us men, therefore still for our sake, so that it may testify its intimate love and desire to us, and excite a reciprocal love of itself in us, it adds, And my delights are with the sons of men. Mr. Dr. Walther, our most closely joined friend and Brother, who illustrated this passage with a pious and elegant ἐξετάσει in the preface of his treatise on Manna, wishes the hypostatic character to be connoted in the word שעשועים which signifies amusements, blandishments, joys and delights, which are made to parents by infants of tender age from the root שעע in Piel, he looked upon gently and with pleasure, amused himself, rejoiced and embraced, because those things, according to Mercer, fit the Son of God the Father's delights most excellently. For just as parents are delighted in playing children, so also the omnipotent Father in his consubstantial Son. But since this Wisdom of the Father has not only called itself his delights; but now, as if turning its face to men, calls them its delights, we can gather from that, that he had his pleasure in us as his little children, and for that reason in us as the sons of his delights: because, namely, he himself is truly אֲבִי עַד the eternal Father Isa. 9 v. 6, whence in the next verse 32 he addresses them as a Father his children, while he says thus, immediately subjoining: Now therefore children, obey me. Concerning the twofold play of the Wisdom of GOD, from which huge and clearly ineffable delights were born, Mr. Dr. Walther has it thus; that the Son of GOD played in the manner of a most sweet boy, and caused laughter, or, as some explain it transitively, made the Father in heaven and men on earth, of whom he is the Mediator, laugh and exhilarated them, and that he undertook his first play before the Father in the primeval creation of the universe, as the artificer and creator of all things: which consists in the omnipotent production of the visible machine of the world, in the all-wise formation of individual creatures, in the admirable variation of species, in the six-day disposition of things, in the most singular fabrication of man, in the constant and perennial conservation of works: But he undertook the other play in the world among the sons of men by his sublime and ineffable incarnation, and Mr. Dr. Walther wishes for that to be looked to both by the name שַׁעֲשֻׁעִים verse 31, by which the Son of God indicates that he would be a boy in the fullness of time, and with incredible pleasure of mind and delight would assume our flesh: and by the phrase to be with the sons of men, or among, and beside men, or by the ellipsis of the name אֶת to be one of the sons of Adam. Which can thus be joined with our preceding observation, that namely the Son of God also considers it his delights, like children, to share in our flesh and blood, and through this κοινωνίαν makes those who believe in him sons of God, and so holds us as his sons in his delights. For as Irenaeus beautifully says, for this reason the Son of God was made the Son of man, that he might make us sons of God.

Tenth, therefore, the hypostasis of Wisdom is confirmed by that address to the sons: Now therefore, O sons, listen to me. For since we are sons of wisdom, who would deny that it is a person? Cf. Matt. 11:19, Luke 7:35, ch. 11:49, Isa. 53:11, Ps. 22:31, Ps. 32:17, Ps. 89:30, 31, Ps. 110:3. Wisdom, however, demands from us filial hearing and obedience, and in turn promises us happiness and life: Blessed are they who keep my ways. And v. 35: He who finds me, finds life, and draws favor from the Lord, or the favor and benevolence of the Lord: just as, on the contrary, it threatens in v. 36 those who sin against it, and hate it, with the destruction of their soul, and death. He who sins against me (which again belongs to a person, for he against whom we sin is certainly a person) wrongs his own soul: All who hate me love death: Which things apply especially to the Son of God, indeed uniquely. For the reception of this one through faith is the sole cause of our salvation; the neglect of this one is the cause of death, John 3:16, 17. He himself is our life, John 14:6; in him and through him alone is obtained the grace of God and salvation and blessedness, Acts 10:47, ch. 4:12, John 1:6.

To this also pertains, eleventh, the construction of the spiritual house, ch. 10:1. Wisdom has built her house: which, because it is a house of refreshment, as those things which follow indicate, by the house built is understood the Church in the state of both grace and glory, Ps. 84:5, Ps. 92:14, John 14:2, 1 Tim. 3:15. Its construction, however, is a personal work, and peculiarly befits the Son of God, Matt. 16:16.

Twelfth, the preparation of the banquet, by which food and drink, v. 2, she has slaughtered her victim, she has mixed her wine: And she has prepared her table: as also the sending forth of the maidens and the invitation v. 3. again testify that this wisdom is a person. And it is certain that that host is the Son of God from Isa. 25, 6. 8. ch. 55, 1. Matt. 11, 29: who with his heavenly Father prepares this banquet for us, and having sent out servants invites us to it Matt. 24, 14. Behold I have prepared my dinner, my oxen and fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: Come to the marriage. There is added again to the invitation, after the insertion of the formula of instruction delivered to the inviters, a most sweet promise: FOR BY ME thy days shall be multiplied, and the years of thy life shall be added to thee: then a most grave warning: If thou shalt be wise, thou shalt be wise for thyself, if a scorner, thou alone shalt bear the punishments; exhibiting the fruit of true wisdom and piety, as also the loss of the contempt of wisdom Gal. 6, 7. From all of which it shines forth clearer than the midday light, that WISDOM is here introduced as hypostatic, namely the Son of God; and that a personification is not to be feigned, but a personal description is to be established here.

And since there is the exact same reason for the parallel passage ch. 1, 20. seqq. it is necessary that the same be understood likewise concerning hypostatic Wisdom. That this may shine forth, and these may mutually kindle light for each other, these few things are to be observed. There is held there (1) The invitation of Wisdom, that she cries without, utters her voice in the streets, speaks her words in the city itself, that is, in the Church gathered from the Gentiles and Jews, as Bede interprets &c. that she may recall from folly and illusion or contempt of the word; and exhort to conversion: Turn you at my reproof ver. 23. (2.) The promise: which is thus: Behold I will pour out my Spirit unto you. Aquila, adhering more strictly to the words, and Theod. αναβλυσω ημιν πνευμα μου I will make my Spirit gush forth unto you, which the Heb. נבע implies: Which promise agrees excellently with the promise of Christ John 7. v. 18. and leads us to the procession of the Holy Spirit from his source, who with GOD the Father is the Son of GOD, as in its place in Tomo 3. System. Theological [matters] from the Greek Doctors we have shown. He adds: I will make you know my words. By which our Master the only Son of GOD promises both the abundant communication of his Spirit, and an easy and clear information. (3.) The rebuke, which is proposed by these: Because I have called, and ye refused, I have stretched out my hand, and there was none that regarded. These again are of a person, and most especially befit the Son of GOD Matt. 11, v. 29. ch. 23, v. 37. Conf. Isa. 65, v. 2. whose counsel the ungodly are also said to despise Luke 7, ver. 39. as he complains of that matter here ver. 25: ye have despised all my counsel. (4.) There follows the Threat: I also will laugh at your destruction ver. 26. Then they shall call and I will not hear, in the morning they shall seek me, and shall not find me. Which again indicates a divine person. For he is not to be called upon, nor does he hear us, unless he is God. (5.) There is subjoined for the sake of testifying to his longsuffering a repeated offer of Grace: He who obeys me, shall dwell confidently, and shall rest from the fear of evil. Conf. Jer. 23, v. 6. That all these things befit the Son of God, there is no doubt: whence they are most rightly explained concerning hypostatic Wisdom by the Venerable Bede, Hugo, Dionysius, Lyranus, Lavater, Tremellius, Cartwright, Piscator, by our Osiander also, the Weimar Paraphrasts, B. Glassius, Dr. Gejer and others; Just as the present passage Prov. 8. (for the sake of which it was necessary to compare that one) is declared by the unanimous consent of the ancients concerning the Son of God by Ignatius Epist. ad Tars., Irenaeus lib. 4. c. 37., Tertullian contr. Hermog. c. 18., Cyprian lib. 2. contr. Judaeos c. 1., Athanasius in Apol. & de Constit. Nic. Syn. as also Orat. 3. contra Arian., Gregory of Nyssa lib. 1. contr. Eunom., Basil l. 4. contr. Eunom., Nazianzen Orat.

2. concerning the Son. Hilary l. 12. de Trinit. & lib. de Synod. ad anath. 5., Eusebius lib. 3. demonstr. Evangel. c. 2., Epiphanius haer. 69., Cyril l. 5. Thesaur. c. 4., Jerome Comment. in Isa. 26, v. 17. & Epist. 139., Augustine l. 5. de Trinit. cap. 12., Bede in this place. Not even the Arians themselves disagreeing, who urged this passage concerning the Son of God, but opposed it, though wrongly, to the eternity of the Son of God, of which it is a most luminous testimony. Nor do our Doctors disagree, with unanimous suffrage ch. 8. Prov. explaining it concerning the hypostatic Word: nor does Philippus, whom Enjedinus opposes to us, disagree: but he says that he approves the common interpretation, that namely the Son of God is understood, Wisdom creating and issuing the Law and the Gospel, playing before God at all times, supremely gladdening the Father, and showing him to Angels, and to men in the wondrous order of the workmanship of the world, and afterwards in the promulgation of the word, in the assumption of human nature, the building of the Church, the conservation of the Church, and the governing of Kings and Judges.

To which finally let there also be added the twin passage from the book of Wisdom ch. 7, v. 21. seqq. where he ascends from Wisdom as an imprint and communicated to the archetype and the communicating one, and the same hypostatic one. For the ARTIFICER of all things taught me WISDOM. He names the artificer or maker of all things with Solomon Prov. 8. and John ch. 1, v. 3. the Word and uncreated wisdom the Son of God: whom he constitutes Master and Teacher, and the author of all Wisdom: in which he teaches that the Holy Spirit is, as one who proceeds from the Son, and is in the Son, as the Spirit of the Son v. 22. which he says is everywhere, and reaches all things v. 24. and describes from the hypostatic character v. 24. 25. that it is a vapor of the power of God, and a certain emanation of the sincerity of the almighty glory, the brightness of eternal light, and a mirror without spot of the majesty of God and an image of his goodness. Similar things concerning the Son of God are held Col. 1, v. 15. Heb. 1, v. 3. Also from omnipotence v. 27, that He can do all things; and from divine operations, that remaining in Himself He renews all things, and through nations transfers Himself into holy souls, etc. Then from divine providence chap. 8, v. 1, He reaches from end to end mightily, and disposes all things sweetly: and as a fellow-worker and collaborator He asks that she be sent to Him chap. 9, vers. 10, and ascribes to her omniscience, and Wisdom as governess and directress vers. 11, and attributes to her very many truly divine personal works, namely that she saved and freed the Patriarchs from evils, led the Israelites through Moses with their enemies destroyed, and gave waters from the rock chap. 10 and 11. All of which speak of hypostatic Wisdom: of which also Syr. c. 24. Lyranus explains, and Cornelius à Lapide concedes that it can be so explained: Although in that exposition pains must be taken, lest Wisdom communicating, and the Mistress, be confused with Wisdom communicated, and the doctrine of this Mistress. For from that one described in vers. 1 and following, which is also marked with a hypostatic character vers. 4, I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before every creature: he descends afterwards to the Wisdom which is communicated by the Son of God: although he does not distinguish it as accurately as Solomon, and abuses the term ἔκτισε, when he wishes to declare generation from Solomon vers. 14: for Philo, the author of this book, did not observe so exactly τὴν ὑποτύπωσιν of the divine words, which his other works also teach. Therefore these things from his Apocryphal book must be recalled and corrected to the norm of the Canonical Solomonic one; and thus at last they will be able to be conveniently compared with them, nay even will contribute to their illustration. But of that elsewhere.

Finally, Grotius's own confession is to be observed here, who contradicts himself: For when he has already explained Wisdom with the Jews concerning the Law of God Prov. 8, 1.

Soon to v. 27. when he prepared the heavens, I was present, he notes this, that is, ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν, as below v. 30. John Evang. c. 1. He acknowledges therefore that it is the hypostatic Son Word of God, of whom it is said in John 1, 1, that he was with God, that is being treated here. Why therefore did he cast his vote for the Jews, if he seriously believed this with the Christians?

Latin:

CAPUT VIII.

Producitur Sapientia hypostatica nos à viis pec- catorum & inferni ad se vocans & sedu- ctos invitans, cum promissione verita- tis, justitiæ, sapientiæ, timoris DEI, ceu causa & origo prudentiæ, consilii, divi- tiarum, & gloriæ: Ejusdemque describi- tur æterna generatio, mundi productio, & delectatio cum genere humano; cujus informatio suscepta vitam, posthabita mortem adfert.

Vers. 1.

NUMQVID NON SAPIENTIA CLAMITAT) Hæc de ea sapientia quæ in lege apparet, exponunt Hebræi, & sane ei non soli, at præcipue hæc attributa conveniunt.

PRæfert hic iterum Grotius Judæorum glossam interpretationi Sanctorum Patrum : Dignus autem locus est, qui expendatur paulo accuratius, quum in hoc imprimis capite Sapientia μυστηριώ- δης Regum & mortalium sapientissimi, quam de vera origine Sapientiæ, ex inspiratione ejus, a quo ferebatur, Spiritus habuit, ac tum sub ingres- sum sapientissimarum Paræmiarum, tum impri- mis in hoc, & sequenti capite populo, cui præ- erat, imo nobis etiam aperuit, propter quos scri- pta sunt quoque antiqua monumenta Rom. 15. v. 4. ut de fide in Christum erudiamur ad salutem. 1. Tim. 3. v. 18. Quanquam vero Sapientiam hanc clamantem non pauci sequius exponant : utpu- ta vel in genere de sapientia præscindente à divina & humana, aut prout ea DEO & hominibus com- munis est, quæ Cornelii à Lapide, & Menochii est Interpretatio : vel de Essentiali DEI Sapien- tia, quæ Judæorum quorundam & Photinianorum est, vel de sapientia Verbi DEI, comprehensa Scripturis Sacris, & per publicum ministerium Doctorum omni tempore annunciata, quæ Mer- ceri & aliorum est explicatio, vel speciatim de sa- pientia in lege tradita, ut interpretatur R. Salo- mo Jarchi & Le Kach Tob. ut & cum illis Salazar ac Grotius noster, vel de sapientia hominum habi- tuali, quam Salomo reliquis bonis prætulit 1. Reg. 3. v, 11. (ut silentio involvam mysticas, & magnam partem impias detorsiones ad sanctam Virginem θεοτόκον Papistarum Salazaris, Cornelii à Lapide, aliorum : Ecclesiam Romanam Deiparæ hæc appli- care sensu accommodatitio, ait Tirinus) nobis ta- men certum est Salomonem loqui de Sapientia hy- postatica, æterno Filio Dei, Sapientiæ omnis aucto- re atque scaturigine; non de attributo aliquo divi- no, non de Verbo Dei, non de habitu aliquo acci- dentali in nobis, sed de persona divina æterna, sapien- tissima, omnipotente, Creatrice, Conservatrice, ac Gubernatrice rerum omnium, Salvatrice hu- mani generis, salutis nostræ æternæ causa claman- te in verbo, & per verbi ministerium, omnesque ad veram sapientiam ac fructus ejusdem, æternamque adeo beatitudinem invitante. Ac de Judæis quidem mirum non est, quod hic videre illam sapientiam hypostaticam nequiverint, qui Christum Sapientiam Dei reprobarunt Matth. 23, 34. & nullam in DEO hypostaticam Sapientiam agnoscunt, imo doctrinam de æterno Filio DEI pro blasphemio habent: Ideo illis aures præbere hic non debuit Grotius. Neque de Photinianis id mirum, προϋπαρξιν Filii Dei ante nativitatem temporalem impugnantibus. Quod vero Christiani Interpp. mysterium S. S. Trinitatis admittentes de Verbo Dei προφορικῷ, & Sapientia, quæ eodem exhibetur, accipiant, ea videtur potissimum causa, quod observarint Sapientiam verbi Dei similibus elogiis ornari, & non pauca occurrere, quæ de ea proprie hic, & in parallelo Sap. 1. & 2. loco intelligenda sint, quodque per Prosopopœiam aliæ res, stultitia & voluptas in ἀντιθέσει introducantur, unde eam etiam hic locum habere, ac de Sapientia Verbo Dei expressa vel certe de essentiali sapientia Dei sermonem esse, crediderunt. Sed ubi rem penitius expenderimus, nequaquam obscurum erit, accurate illa à Salomone distingui, & Sapientiam hanc invitatricem illis epithetis ac prædicatis definiri, ut aliter, quam de Filio Dei accipi non possit. Nam (1) aperte distinguitur Sapientia invitatrix, à sapientia illa, quæ ab ipsa, & penes ipsam discenda est: De illa ita habetur: Nunquid non SAPIENTIA clamitat, & PRUDENTIA dat vocem suam, & quæ porro de mutatione ejusdem ac qualis ipsa sit, quæ ejus ὕπαρξις, quæ attributa, & effecta, exponuntur. Hanc vero proponit Sapientia illa hypostatica, nos invitans, ut Sapientiam discamus & amplectamur v. 5. intelligite parvuli ASTUTIAM & stolidi animum advertite; audite, nam præstantia eloquar, & aperientur labia mea, ut RECTA prædicent. VERITATEM loquetur palatum meum, justi sunt omnes SERMONES MEI, nihil est in iis pravum aut perversum, recti sunt intelligentibus, & æqui invenientibus scientiam: accipite ERUDITIONEM MEAM & non argentum, & SCIENTIAM potius, quam aurum electum: quia melior est Sapientia cunctis pretiosissimis. Quis hic non videt, aliud esse Sapientiam, quæ acclamat, & vocem suam edit, quæ est confirmatrix & Magistra nostra: aliud vero esse præcepta & doctrinam, quæ ab ipsa traduntur, nempe ASTUTIAM, quam intelligere simplices debent: præstantia illa, quæ ex ore ejus addisci possunt: recta illa, quorum prædicandorum causa labia sua ipsa aperit: veritatem illam quam palatum ejus loquitur: sermones ejus, quos loquitur: eruditionem, nec non scientiam, quam proponit & commendat, quamq; abs se unice hauriri vult. Qui hæc non distinguit, Doctorem illum summum cum Doctrina, Magistrum illum unicum cum Præceptis ejus, sapientiæ auctorem, qui sapientia ipsa est, cum scientia, & sapientia, quam ipse tradit, sapientiam communicantem cum Sapientia communicanda confundere necessum habet, quæ tamen hic tam luculenter discriminantur, ut non possint luculentius. Porro distinctis etiam elogiis sapientia communicans & communicanda ἀρχέτυπος & ἔκτυπος hic vocatur. Nam Sapientia hypostatica commendat primum doctrinam suam, tum simplicibus & stolidis, qui piam inde astutiam & Sapientiam, tum peritis etiam qui præstantissima quæque ac rectitudinem veram addiscere possunt v. 5. 6. & celebrat eandem, quod sacra astutia nostræ stupiditati, & stultitiæ medelam afferat v. 5. quodque tradat præcellentia mysteria, & præcepta certissima, de divina veritate, & vera pietate, informantia, v. 6. 7. ac undiquaque justa, satisque obvia & perspicua v. 8. 9. denique quod auro & argento ac margaritis rebus- que omnibus desiderabilibus longe pretiosior sit v. 10. 11. Tum vero semetipsam describit sapientia hypo- statica v. 12. & seqq. Ego Sapientia habito in astu- tia &c. quod ita fieri nemo non videt, ut palam ite- rum distinguat se ab astutia, qua nos instruere vult, in qua habitat, & scientia scientiarum, quam invenit, vel ut inveniamus, præstat: a Sapientia, cujus initium timor Domini est, ut superbia & arrogantia & via mala fugiatur: quam se odisse testatur sapientia hy- postatica, quæ cultoribus suis odium ejusdem etiam cum timore Domini ingenerare, & conciliare vult: Meum est, inquit sapientia hypostatica, consilium תושיה (quod LXX. ἀσφάλειαν, Vulgata æqui- tatem, Junius QUICQUID EST, Ebræi convenien- ter satis cæteris vocibus, sapientiam, ob soliditatem ita dictam exponunt:) mea est intelligentia, meum ro- bur, ut ita sese a consilio, sapientia, intelligentia & virtute, quæ attributa sunt, distinguat, tanquam subjectum, cui attributa illa conveniunt, vel si κατ’ ἔξω ista intelligantur, tanquam causam ab effecti- bus, quorum auctor ipsa est: Atque ita loquitur de- inceps de semetipsa per integrum caput, non ne- glecto isto discrimine, quod v. 33. iterum innuitur: audite DISCIPLINAM & estote sapientes, & nolite abjicere eam; & c. 9, 6. relinquite infantiam & vivi- te, & ambulate per vias prudentiæ. v. 10. Principium sapientiæ timor Domini, & scientia Sanctorum pru- dentia. Quæ ubi de sapientia abs se communicata professa erat, ad se auctorem ejusdem & fontem nos iterum revocat: v. 11. PER ME enim multipli- cabuntur dies tui, & addentur tibi anni vitæ tuæ. Quod similiter etiam in parallelo loco c. 2, 20. seqq. videre est. Ibi enim SAPIENTIA foris prædicans, in plateis edens vocem suam, semetipsam a scientia, quam tradit, & a correctione sua, ad quam omnes converti vult, & a verbo doctrinæ, vel institutionis suæ, & a consilio & increpationibus suis aperte di- scriminat, ut nulli dubium esse possit, per SAPI- ENTIAM illam non intelligi ipsum Verbum Dei, doctrinam aut legem, & præcepta Dei, sed hæc ex mente Spiritus S. omnino distincta esse.

SAPIENTIAM autem illam esse vere hypo- stasin & personam Primo in genere prædicata per- sonalia testantur. Quia loquitur ut persona, & ea, quæ personæ propria sunt, sibi vendicat, eamque ut personam hic introduci, nemo ambigit: tametsi ὁι ἐξ ἐναντίας sese ad figuram prosopopæias recipiant. Sed quia nulla est necessitas in tam prolixa & ex- quisita personæ descriptione, proprio loquendi modo deserto ad figuratum transiliendi; neque no- bis integrum est a proprietate vocum discedere, ubi non cogit necessitas, nisi ludum & jocum e Scri- pturis facere velimus, quod inter Socinianos ipsos etiam monuit Schmalcius, sine personæ fictione de persona & hypostatica sapientia hæc intelligimus. Nec vero si stultitia & voluptas ceu personæ intro- ducantur per fictionem, pariter id de sapientia con- cludendum, quia Sapientiam hypostaticam dari, su- premam sapientiæ causam, & magistram, e Scri- pturis novimus, cui hæc rectissime omnia congru- unt, ideoq; de ea illa sensu proprio, & citra figuram merito explicantur. Ex adverso vero stultitiam & voluptatem hypostaticam non esse, adeoque quæ de illa, ceu persona dicuntur, proprie intelligi non posse, iterum e Scripturis indubium est: unde ne- cessario ipsa postulat, ut hanc solum per prosopo- pœiam instar personæ introduci statuamus. Op- positorum ergo istorum longe diversissima est ra- tio. Taceo quod nonnulli per mulierem stul- tam Diabolum intelligant: qui utique persona est:

Conf. quæ ad cap. 9. v. 13. Jam si nomina, attribu- ta, & prædicata in specie attendantur, fictionem personæ hîc locum non habere, sed veram perso- nam introduci, apparebit. Nomen ipsum sapi- entiæ Filio Dei convenire è Nov. Testamento in- dubium, quum Luc. 11. v. 29. diferte appelletur σοφία τꭢ θεꭢ, quo etiam facit Matth. 11. verf. 29 Luc. 7. verf. 35. de sapientia justificata à filiis suis, de quo loco videantur dissert. Rostoch. p. 88. & 1. Corinth. 1. v. 24. Prædicamus Christum DEI vir- tutem & Dei sapientiam. Quod nomen Chri- sto Filio DEI tribuitur tum κατ' ἔσω ob æternam generationem, perinde ac nomen λόγꭢ: quia Sa- pientia & Verbum Patris est, ab ipso prodiens ab æterno, & in ipso æternum permanens, quem- admodum Verbum internum & sapientia à mente est, & in mente manet: ut proles quædam & filia mentis. Tum κατ' ἔξω quia sapientia omnis ab ipso est, ratione triplicis officii ejusdem: qui ut Sacerdos nobis veram sapientiam promeruit 1. Co- rinth. 1. v. 30. & æterna intercessione eandem im- petrat: ut Rex non modo sapientissime gubernat omnia, sed egentibus etiam sapientiam impertit: ut Propheta nos tum immediate & αὐτοπροσώπως, tum per ministros suos & mediate de vera sapientia ad salutem informat: quia omnia in præsenti lo- co explicantur, æterna generatio, & possessio sapi- entiæ verf. 22. tum veræ & salutiferæ sapientiæ ac- quisitio, cujus gratia deliciæ ipsi summæ fuere cum filiis hominum esse, vitamque & salutem inve- nire testatur, qui se inveniunt verf. 35. quia nobis- cum esse voluit per incarnationem, ut vitam & salutem, adeoque sapientiam illam σωτήριον no- bis mereretur. Adhæc vindicatur ipsi sapientiæ, quæ ad regimen mundi ac gubernationem Ecclesiæ requiritur verf. 15. Meum est consilium, mea est prudentia: Per me Reges regnant &c. verf. 14. 15. denique prolixe & præcipue informatio de vera sapientia ad salutem ipsi hîc attribuitur: ad quam ubique clamitat & vocem suam edit sapientia, ut nos ad eam percipiendam invitet, ejusque parti- cipes reddat: ob quam ancillas suas emittit, & ad arcem & mœnia civitatis vocat: si quis est par- vulus vel simplex, veniat ad me &c. cap. 9. verf. 2. Quod vero nomine Sapientiæ, idem etiam Pruden- tiæ nomine hîc verf. 1. significatur: quia nomina illa ceu synonyma adhibentur; idemque diversis verbis ad fignificandum ardorem, desiderium & continuum actum invitationis Sapientiæ effertur; Nunquid non sapientia clamitat, & prudentia edit vocem suam? Solent enim voces illæ חכמה sapi- entia, & תבונה penes Ebræos κατ' ἰσοδυναμίαν adhiberi, e. g. cum Prov. 3. v. 19. dicitur: Dominus sapientia fundavit terram, stabilivit cælos pruden- tia: Sapientia illius cœperunt abyssi Jer. 11. v. 12. cap. 11. v. 15. qui præparat orbem in Sapientia sua & pru- dentia sua extendit cælos. Tum si omnino aliqua sit distinctio, indicatur Filium DEI Sapientiam, & intelligentiam, vel prudentiam hypostaticam esse fontem, scaturiginem & principium omnis Sa- pientiæ, & intelligentiæ, atque prudentiæ. Unde non minus ab hac quam ab illa nominari meretur. Adhibetur etiam pluralis חכמות Proverb. 9. v. 1. cap. 10. v. 20. ob eminentiam, & perfectionem: quia Filius DEI tota Sapientia, & omnis Sapientiæ autor est.

Porro (2.) quia invitationem Sapientiæ im- primis persequitur Salomo, cum Sapientiam di- cit clamitare, & prudentiam vocem suam dare, in summis excelsisque verticibus supra viam stare juxta portas civitatis, in ipsis foribus loqui, ac dicere, ô viri, ad vos clamito, & vox mea ad filios hominum, intelli- gite simplices astutiam &c. quamnam Sapientiam potius intelligit, quam cujus hoc proprium est munus, nos invitare ad veram coelestem, & saluti- feram doctrinam & sapientiam, ipsum nempe æter- num DEI Filium, τὸν λόγον ὑποστατικὸν? Nemo enim Deum vidit unquam, unigenitus, qui est in sinu Patris, ipse enarravit, Joh. 1. v. 18. Nemo novit Patrem nisi Filius, & cui voluerit revelare Matth. 11. v. 27. Quum enim hic causa princeps, fons, & scaturigo sapientiæ, ubi de sapientiæ communicatione agi- tur, indigitetur, & hæc principalis causa, autor su- premus sapientiæ causis ministralibus, quæ ancil- lantur ipsi, cap. 9. v. 2. præficiatur, quid sapientiæ nomine convenientius hoc in loco, quam ipsa Sa- pientia hypostatica, æternus DEI Filius intelligi- tur? Atque ideo Christus ipse, cum de missione ministrorum Verbi ad hunc invitationis actum agit, Sapientiam DEI sese nominat, ac se esse illam Sa- pientiam, de qua Salomo testatus est, docet, Luc. c. 11. v. 49. Præterea & Sapientia DEI dixit: Mit- tam ad illos Prophetas & Apostolos. Conf. Matth. 23. v. 33. Ita ergo Sapientiæ nomen hic accipien- dum, prout illum designat, qui autor est, & causa princeps communicationis vivificæ Sapientiæ & verbi ministros emittit, ut nos participes ejusdem faciat: hoc est, interprete ipsa sapientia, Christum Filii DEI.

Tertio quum actiones suppositorum propria sint, & opera illa vere sint personalia, quod sapientia cla- mitet, quod vocem suam edat, quod stet in mediis se- mitis, quod loquatur in foribus, dicendo, ad vos clami- to, si proprie hæc accipienda sint, Sapientiam hy- postaticam, vel quæ persona revera sit, designant. Non enim nisi persona vocem prudentem edit, ho- minesque alloquitur. Sic de rebus magnis loqui, re- cta prædicare, convivium apparare, & ad illud invi- tare, ac invitantes emittere, opera sunt personæ: uti ancillas, quæ emittuntur à Sapientia, ut ad convivi- um nos invitent, personas esse dubium non est, ita multo minus dubitandum est de sapientia, cui hæ ministrant, & à qua emittuntur, quod ea vera sit persona.

Quarto describitur Sapientia ut persona, cum ei tribuatur non tantum vox, loquela, & oratio, sed labia etiam, guttur, meditatio, disciplina, doctrina, ceu Magistra omnis sapientiæ, quæ utique Christum innuunt. Hic enim unicus Magister noster est Matth. 23. v. 10. ô Viri, ad vos clamito, & vox mea ad filios ho- minum: Audite, quoniam de rebus magnis locutura sum. Et aperientur labia mea ut recta prædicem. Ve- ritatem meditabitur guttur meum, & labia mea de- testabuntur impium, Justi sunt omnes sermones mei, non est in eis pravum quid, neque perversum &c. Cui- nam magis ista conveniunt, quam λόγῳ ὑποσατι- xῷ, qui est ipsa veritas Joh. 14. v. 6. מבשׂר Evangeli- sta Es. 41. v. 27. præceptor populorum Es. 55. v. 4. Do- minus ille, cujus est verbum veritatis Apoc. 19. 10. Col. 3, 16. 1. Tim. 6, 3. Conf. Ps. 45, 3. Cant. 5, 16.

Quinto vindicat sibi hæc sapientia attributa, quæ non conveniunt nisi personæ: Ego Sapientia habito in consilio vel astutia, pia nempe & sancta quæ vera est prudentia Matth. 10, 16. qua phrasi in- nuitur, quod vere prudens sit, ac omnis prudentiæ sca- turigo, quemadmodum lucem inaccessam inhabi- tare dicitur, quia est lucidissimus, lucisque omnis fons 1. Tim. 6. v. 16. Conf. Col. 2. v. 3. Et scientiam sci- entiarum invenio, id est, facio, ut qui me colunt, inve- niant, ut exponit Mercerus per Metonymiam: vel invenio, id est, habeo præsentissimam & propriam: uti DEUS scrutari corda dicitur, id est, habere ea perspectissima: Arrogantiam & superbiam & viam pravam, os bilingue, detestor: Meum est consilium, & sapientia, vel virtus (ut Job. 6. v. 12. vox Ebræa redditur, atque ita alterum comma hujus versu idem pene aliis verbis efferet, emphaseos & βεβαι- ώσεως gratia) mea est intelligentia, mea est fortitudo. Sapientiam autem illam quæ omnis prudentiæ sca- turigo, & quæ habet propriam sibi scientiam omnis solertiæ, eamque in nobis producit, cui tri- buitur odium & detestatio superbiæ, impietatis, & fal- sitatis: cui vindicatur consilium & sapientia vel vir- tus, fortitudo, & intelligentia, hypostasin & personam esse oportet: quum ista personæ solum conveni- ant: neque sapientiæ essentialis sit potentia & forti- tudo, nec divina attributa confundantur: super Messiam autem requiescat Spiritus consilii & forti- tudinis Es. 11. v. 2.

Sexto effecta, quæ ipsi ut causæ architectoni- cæ tribuuntur, hypostasin arguunt, utpote Magi- stratuum institutio, instructio, & directio: de qua ita testatur: Per me Reges regnant, & legum condi- tores justa decernunt: per me principes imperant, & potentes decernunt justitiam. Præpositio illa PER ME causam principalem notat, ut Psalm. 18. v. 30. Psal. 60. v. 14. Tum piorum dilectio & cura: qua de hæc subjunguntur: Ego diligentes me diligo, & qui mane vigilant ad me, invenient me. Adhæc deliciarum, gloriæ, & justitiæ communicatio, quæ ab hac sapientia proficiscuntur, ejusque fructus sunt: v. 18. 19. nec non præsentia in viis justitiæ & medio semitarum juris, ut nempe extrema vitentur: vera denique dilectio: ut possidere faciam amantes mei (veram) Substantiam, & ut thesauros boni cordis eorum impleam bonis spiritualibus & cœlestibus: Matth. 12. v. 35. quo de vid. Dn. D. Gejerus amicus, & Frater noster in Christo honorandus, in Comment. ad h. l. p. 400. Sic ergo invitat Sapientia hyposta- tica quosvis ad sui amorem & cultum, variis argu- mentis, à plenaria sapientiæ possessione, quæ in ipsa invenitur, à vera sanctitate, à consilio, & virtute, à prudentia regiminis, quæ ab ipsa habetur, ab amore, cura, & remuneratione splendida, quam exhibet, à dilectione & deductione ad veram hæreditatem, vel possessionem & abundantiam bonorum omnium, quam pollicetur, ac reipsa præstat Christus iis, qui diligunt ipsum, & serio eum quærunt, vel mane ad ipsum vigilant, 2. Tim. 4. v. 7.

Septimo peculiariter, & imprimis Character hypostaticus observandus, æterna nempe generatio Filii Dei. Quæ cum hic verbis disertis expressa sit, non sinit nos dubitare, quod de sapientia hyposta- tica hic agatur. Cujus ipsa verbis splendidis & ma- xime emphaticis, si uspiam alias, hic per Regem sa- pientissimum, exhibet descriptionem insignem, designans (1) Principium & originem suam, JE- HOVAM Deum Patrem, quam relationem voce קָנַנִי exprimit; POSSEDIT ME; hæc enim POS- SESSOREM, adeoque AUTOREM Sapientiæ infert: qui possedit ipsam, seu acquisivit, puta gene- ratione, quemadmodum verbum illud Gen. 4. v. 1. de possessione per generationem occurrit. Tribus enim modis verbum illud de Deo usurpatur, quod nem- pe possideat per modum creationis Gen. 14. v. 19. 22. Ps. 104. v. 24. Ps. 139. v. 13. per modum gratiosæ sepa- rationis & adoptionis vel recreationis Deut. 32. v. 6. Ps. 74. v. 2. Ps. 78. Es. 11. v. 11. & per modum genera- tionis Gen. 4, 1. Quum ergo prioribus duobus mo- dis sapientiam non possederit, restat ut per modum generationis eandem possedisse dicatur. Jehovah er- go hic possessor est Deus Pater. (2.) Designat gene- rationem suam, ceu proprietatem hypostaticam: Posse- dit, per generationem, ME. Sapientia ergo hæc possidetur, vel acquisita est per GENERATIO- NEM; adeoque est Sapientia genita, hoc est, Fi- lius Dei, qua voce designatur Christus à Salomone Prov. 30. v. 4. Quam generationem ipsa exposuit etiam voce חוללתי v. 24. utpote quæ sensu proprio notat actum conceptionis vel pariendi Job. 14, 7. c. 26. v. 5. Es. 51. v. 7. & in Thargum alias explicatur voce איתילדת à R. ילד genuit, quæ Ps. 2. v. 7. de æterna generatione Filii Dei occurrit: hic voce אחבטנור redditur à בטן uterus, quod in utero Dei quasi sit concepta sapientia, aut prout Basiliensis editio ha- bet אתבניך quasi ædificata & filiata à בנה ædi- ficavit, & בן filius. Quum ergo à proprietate vocis discedendum non sit, ac voce Ebræa proprie gene- ratio, vel productio e substantia alterius inferatur, proprietatem characteristicam Filii DEI hic desi- gnatam esse, statuendum est: quæ, ut eo magis ani- mo nostro id imprimatur, quod nunquam satis di- scitur aut creditur, iterum vers. 25. expressa est. Quæ proinde de persona, & quidem de æterno Dei Filio sermonem hic esse, luculenter convincit. Nonnulli eam proprietatem personalem etiam indagant in voce נסכתי vers. 23. ante seculum inuncta fuit, quod communicata Filio per æternam generationem divina essentia communicata etiam divina Maje- stas, & Imperium fuerit super res creandas. Sed verbum illud נסכתי Ps. 2. v. 6. Ego unxi te Regem me- um, aperte discriminatur à generatione Filii Dei, de qua v. 7. actum: & unctio hic proprie est Filii ab æ- terno geniti ad officium non Regium tantum, sed etiam Sacerdotale ac Propheticum destinatio ab æ- terno facta, quemadmodum Reges, Sacerdotes, ac Prophetæ ad officium suum per unctionem inaugu- rari solebant: Ideo R. Levi Ben Gerson reddidit, Data est mihi potestas, & Principatus & magnificen- tia. Id tamen indubium est, inunctionem, & de- stinationem illam personæ convenire, neque de attributo aliquo in Deo, aut Verbo & Lege Dei dici posse, ideoque Sapientiam hypostaticam hic ne- cessario intelligendam esse. (3) Exprimitur æter- nitas Sapientiæ. Jehovah possedit me ראשית דרכו quod nonnulli explicant, Principium viæ suæ: In- telligendo principium effectivum non materiale: uti Filius DEI ἡ ἀρχὴ τῆς κτίσεως τοῦ θεοῦ dicitur Ap. 3. v. 14. Sed versatur S. S. in describenda æternita- te, ab anteitate, ut ita loquar, ante opera creationis, quod subjunctæ περιφράσεις docent, ideo hic lite- ram Bet subintelligunt Chaldæus, Aquila, Vulgatus, B. Lutherus & alii: בראשית IN PRINCIPIO VIÆ SUÆ, id est, operum creationis. Opera enim Dei viæ Dei sunt Deut. 32. v. 4. 2. Sam. 22. v. 31. Es. 55. v. 8. Rom. 11. v. 33. & respectus hic habetur ad initium Geneseos בראשית cap. 1. p. 1. perinde, uti Joh. 1. v. 1. in loco nostro parallelo, ubi eadem ra- tione æternitas λόγος, ut hic sapientia expressa. Quam explicat porro per ὑπομονὴν insignem, ut magis magisque eam inculcet sapientia: ante ope- ra sua jam inde מאז EX TUNC (quod de æter- nitate legitur Ps. 93. v. 2.) ante seculum (vel ab æterno) inuncta fui: à principio, ante terram, cum nondum essent voragines, concepta vel genita sum: cum nulli essent fontes graves aquis: antequam mon- tes fundati essent, ante colles ego concepta eram; Ad- huc terram non fecerat, & flumina, & cardines orbis terræ: Quando præparabat cælos ושם אני tunc ego. Quæ verba, concepta sum, genita sum, tunc ego tibi aderam, non simplicem existentiam, sed veram hy- postasin, & subsistentiam, quam ab æterno habuit Filius DEI, testantur.

Octavo è creationis opere hypostasis Sapien- tiæ colligitur. Quum enim tam prolixe hic in- troducat opera creationis, & ante ea jam se exti- tisse testetur, illorum etiam omnium sese opificem facit: æque uti Joh. 1. v. 1. 3. de λόγῳ dicitur, non tantum quod in principio creationis rerum omnium jam fuerit, sed etiam quod omnia per ipsum facta sint. Ita enim v. 30. hoc in loco Sapientia ואהיה אצלו אמון Eram apud eum artifex. De attributo certe divino non dicitur quod sit apud Patrem, vel juxta: At sicut de λόγῳ ὑποστατικῷ Johannes cap. 1. v. 1. Et Verbum erat apud Deum, ita hæc de sese Sa- pientia, Eram apud eum, ut videatur ad locum no- strum allusisse S. Johannes, aut eundem illustrare voluisse. Porro non tantum apud Patrem se fu- isse dicit, sed etiam OPIFICEM se facit rerum omnium. Ut enim vox cognata אמן Cant. 7. v. 2. artificem notat, ita etiam vox præsens אמון accipi- tur pro artifice vel opifice Jerem. 46. v. 25. c. 52. v. 15. Nah. 3. v. 8. ideo LXX. reddunt ἁρμόζουσα. Vul- gata cum eo eram cuncta componens. Irenæus, Eram apud eum aptans. Tertul. Ego eram cum illo compin- gens. Quæ autem Sapientia artifex, & opifex rerum omnium fuit, nisi Filius Dei, per quem facta sunt o- mnia, & sine quo nihil factum est, quod factum est.

Nono à lusu & deliciis Sapientiæ. Hæc enim Sapientia delectatio, vel oblectamentum Dei Pa- tris fuit, & coram Deo Patre lusit omni tempore, lusit etiam in orbe terrarum, & deliciæ ejus singulares sunt, esse cum filiis hominum. Quæ non conveni- unt attributo Dei essentiali, aut Verbo & legi Dei, ne- dum Sapientiæ in nobis habituali, sed personæ, vel hy- postaticæ Sapientiæ: optimeque in Filium Dei qua- drant. Et fui deliciæ quotidie שעשועים quod oble- ctationem insignem & jucundissimam rei amabilis, quam nunquam satis intueri, meditari, & amplecti possumus, importat, & de deliciis Davidis in Verbo Dei Ps. 119. v. 14. 77. 92. 143. 174. ac filiolo mabili Jer. 31, 20. occurrit: ideo Filius deliciarum suavissimus hic indicatur, in quo voluptatem habet suam Deus Pater Matth. 3. v. 17. Unde LXX. recte ἧ προσέ- χαιρες cui adgaudebat. Et Tertul. contra Hermog. Ego eram, ad quam adgaudebat. Nec non Catena Græcorum: Ego eram, cui blande arridebat, cui abblandiebatur, vel cum quo jucunde lætabatur יום יום die & die, hoc est, tum in die æternitatis, in illo æterno היום de quo ad Psal. 2. vers. 7. diximus, tum etiam in יום vel die seculi, ludens coram facie ejus o- mni tempore, jucunda, instar Filii, ac puelli suavissi- mi, Patri præbens spectacula; quod facit Sapientia varia creando, & operando sapientissime & facil- lime, ut lusus saltem ipsi sint, & suavissime, atque ita, ut delectetur ipse Deus iisdem Gen. 1. v. 31. Job. 1. v. 3. c. 5. v. 17. 19. 20. Addit autem: Ludo in orbe terræ ejus: quod peculiariter factum, cum appa- ruit Sapientia Patriarchis, Prophetis, & aliis sui cultoribus in Vet. Test. & cum manifestata est in carne in Nov. Test. ubi jucundissima orbi terræ exhibuit spectacula, ut delicias istas cum Deo Pa- tri, tum nobis etiam hominibus facere, ac fecisse, intelligatur, ideo nostri adhuc causa, ut amorem ac desiderium intimum suum nobis testetur, ac reci- procum sui in nobis amorem excitet, subjicit, Et deliciæ meæ cum filiis hominum. Dn. D. Waltherus, amicus & Frater noster conjunctissimus, qui pia & eleganti ἐξετάσει hunc locum in præfat. tractat. de Manna illustravit, in voce שעשועים quæ oblecta- tiones, blanditas, lætitias & delitias, quæ parentibus fi- unt à tenellulæ ætatulæ infantibus à R. שעע in Piel, blande & cum voluptate adspexit, oblectavit seipsum, lætatus & amplexus est, characterem hypostaticum connotari vult, quod ista, secundum Mercerum, in Filium Dei Patris delitias optime quadrent. Sic- ut enim in pueris ludentibus delectantur Paren- tes, ita etiam omnipotens Pater in Filio suo con- substantiali. Quum autem non tantum sapientia hæc Patris delitias se vocarit; sed verso nunc quasi vultu ad homines, illos suas delicias dicat, colligere inde possumus, quod nos pro filiolis suis, eaque ra- tione in nobis ceu deliciarum filiis, suam volu- ptatem habuerit : quia scil. ipse vere est אֲבִי עַד æternus Pater Esa. 9. v. 6. unde versu proximo 32. ceu Pater filios compellat, dum ita inquit, statim subjungens : Nunc igitur filii obtemperate mihi. De lusu sapientiæ DEI duplici, e quo ingentes & plane inenarrabiles deliciæ natæ, ita habet Dn. D. Waltherus ; quod more pueri dulcissimi Filius DEI luserit, risumque conciliarit, vel, ut non- nulli exponunt transitive, ridere fecerit & exhila- rarit Patrem in cælis, & hominis in terris, quorum est Mediator, primumque lusum coram Patre aggres- sus sit primæva rerum universarum creatione, ceu artifex & creator omnium: qui consistit in omni- potenti adspectabilis mundi Machinæ productio- ne, in omnisapienti singularum creaturarum for- matione, in admiranda specierum variatione, in sextiduana rerum dispositione, in singularissima hominis fabricatione, in constanti & perenni operum conservatione : Lusum vero alterum in or- be inter filios hominum susceperit sublimi & ineffa- bili sua incarnatione, & ad eam respici vult Dn. D. Waltherus tum nomine שַׁעֲשֻׁעִים vers. 31. quo in- digitet Filius Dei se puerum futurum in temporis plenitudine, & incredibili animi voluptate, ac de- lectatione assumturum carnem nostram : tum phra- si esse cum filiis hominum, vel inter, & apud homines, vel per ellipsin nominis אֶת esse unum filiorum A- dam. Quæ sic cum præcedenti nostra observatio- ne conjungi possunt, quod nempe & filius Dei de- licias suas ducat, instar puerorum communicare carni & sanguini nostro, & per hanc κοινωνίαν cre- dentes in sese filios Dei efficiat, adeoque nos ut fi- lios suos in deliciis habeat. Nam ut pulchre Ire- neus, ideo filius Dei factus est filius hominis, ut nos filios Dei efficeret.

Decimo itaque hypostasis Sapientiæ ab illa fi- liorum compellatione confirmatur : Nunc igitur filii obtemperate mihi. Quum enim sapientiæ filii nos simus, ecquis neget personam eam esse? Conf. Matth. 11, 19. Luc. 7, 35. c. 11, 49. Es. 53, 11. Ps. 22, 31. Ps. 32, 17. Ps. 89, 30. 31. Ps. 110, 3. Postulat autem Sa- pientia a nobis filialem audientiam & obedientiam, ac vicissim promittit nobis felicitatem ac vitam : Beati, qui vias meas custodiunt. Et v. 35. Qui inve- nit me, invenit vitam, & haurit beneplacitum a Do- mino, vel favorem & benevolentiam Domini : quemadmodum ex adverso minatur v. 36. iis, qui contra se peccant, seque odio habent, animæ pernici- em, & mortem. Qui autem contra me peccant (quod iterum personæ est, contra quem enim peccamus, is utique persona est) spernit animam suam: Omnes qui odio habent me, diligunt mortem: Quæ apprime Filio Dei competunt, imo unice. Nam hujus su- sceptio per fidem, est salutis nostræ causa unica; hujus neglectus causa mortis est Joh. 3, 16. 17. Ipse vita nostra Joh. 14, 6. in ipso & per ipsum unice ob- tinetur gratia Dei & salus ac beatitudo Actor. 10. v. 47. c. 4, 12. Joh. 1, 6.

Quo etiam facit undecimo domus spiritualis exstructio c. 10, 1. Sapientia ædificavit domum suam : quæ quia domus refectionis est, uti indicant ea quæ sequuntur, per domum extructam Ecclesia in statu tam gratiæ, quam gloriæ intelligitur Ps. 84, 5. Ps. 92, 14. Joh. 14, 2, 1. Tim. 3, 15. Ejus autem exstru- ctio opus est personale, ac peculiariter convenit Filio Dei Matth. 16, 16.

Duodecimo apparatus convivii, qua esculen- ta & poculenta v. 2. immolavit victimam suam, mi- scuit vinum suum: Et apparavit mensam sitam: nec non emissio puellarum ac invitatio v. 3. iterum sapi- entiam hanc personam esse testantur. Et conviva- torem illum Filium Dei esse ex Es. 25, 6. 8. c. 55, 1. Matth. 11, 29. constat: qui cum Patre suo cœlesti nobis hoc convivium parat, & emissis servis ad il- lud invitat Matth. 24, 14. Ecce prandium meum pa- ravi, tauri & altilia occisa sunt, & omnia parata sunt: Venite ad nuptias. Additur denuo invitatio- ni, post insertam invitatoribus traditam instru- ctionis formulam, cum promissio suavissima: PER ME enim multiplicabuntur dies tui, & addentur tibi anni vitæ: tum præmonitio gravissima: Si sapiens fueris, sapiens eris tibi, si illusor, solus lues pœnas; fru- ctum veræ sapientiæ & pietatis, nec non damnum contemtus sapientiæ exhibens Gal. 6, 7. E quibus omnibus luce meridiana clarius effulget, SAPIEN- TIAM hic introduci hypostaticam, nempe Dei Fi- lium; neque προσωποποιϊαν fingendam, sed προ- σωπογραφιαν hic statuendam esse.

Et quum eadem prorsus ratio sit loci paralleli c. 1, 20. seqq. eundem pariter de Sapientia hyposta- tica intelligi oportet. Quod ut elucescat, ac mutuo lucem hæc sibi accendant, pauca hæc observanda. Habetur ibi (1) Sapientiæ invitatio, quod clamet foris, vocem edat in plateis, in urbe ipsa eloquia sua dicat, hoc est, in Ecclesia ex gentibus & Judæis adu- nata, uti Beda interpretatur &c. a stultitia & illu- sione vel contemtu verbi revocet; & ad conver- sionem hortetur: Convertimini ad increpationem meam vers. 23. (2.) Promissio: quæ ita habet: Ecce depromam vobis Spiritum meum. Aquila, verbis stri- ctius inhærens, & Theod. αναβλυσω ημιν πνευμα με scaturire faciam vobis Spiritum meum, quod Ebr. נבע infert: Quæ promissio egregie convenit pro- missioni Christi Joh. 7. v. 18. & ad processionem S. S, à fonte suo, qui cum DEO Patre est Filius DEI, nos deducit, ut suo loco Tomo 3. System. Theologici è Græcis Dd. ostendimus. Addit: Scire vos faciam verba mea. Quibus tum Spi- ritus sui largam communicationem, tum facilem ac perspicuam informationem Magister noster unicus Filius DEI pollicetur. (3.) Objurgatio, quæ hisce proponitur: Propterea quod vocavi, & renuistis, extendi manum meam, & non fuit, qui attenderet. Hæc iterum personæ sunt, & Fi- lio DEI maxime conveniunt Matth. 11, v. 29. cap. 23. v. 37. Conf. Esa. 65. v. 2. cujus consilium etiam spernere dicuntur impii Luc. 7. vers. 39. uti hic vers. 25. ea de re queritur: despexistis omne consilium meum. (4.) Sequitur Comminatio: Ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo vers. 26. Tunc invoca- bunt & non exaudiam, mane quærent me, & non in- venient. Quæ personam divinam iterum indicat. Non enim invocandus, neque exaudit nos, nisi Deus. (5.) Subjungitur μακροθυμιας testandæ causa iterata Gratiæ oblatio: Qui obedit mihi, habi- tabit confidenter, & requiescet a timore mali. Conf. Jer. 23. v. 6. Quæ omnia Filio Dei apprime con- venire, nullum est dubium: unde de Sapientia hy- postatica rectissime explicantur à Venerab. Beda, Hugone, Dionysio, Lyrano, Lavatero, Tremellio, Cartwrighto, Piscatore, ab Osiandro item nostro, Paraphrastis Vinariens. B. Glassio, Dn. D. Gejero & aliis; Quemadmodum præsens locus Prov. 8. (cu- jus gratia istum conferre habuit) unanimi veterum consensu, de Filio Dei declaratur ab Ignatio Epist. ad Tars. Ireno lib. 4. c. 37. Tertul. contr. Her- mog. c. 18. Cyprian. lib. 2. contr. Judæos c. 1. A- thanas. in Apol. & de Constit. Nic. Syn. ut & Orat. 3. contra Arian. Gregorio Nysseno lib. 1. contr. Eu- nom. Basilio l. 4. contr. Eunom. Nazianzeno Orat

2. de Fil. Hilario l. 12. de Trinit. & lib. de Synod. ad anath. 5. Euseb. lib. 3. demonstr. Evangel. c. 2. E- piphan. hær. 69. Cyrill. l. 5. Thefaur. c. 4. Hierony- mo Comment. in Ef. 26. v. 17. & Epist. 139. August. l. 5. de Trinit. cap. 12. Beda h. l. Ne discrepantibus quidem ipsis Arianis, qui hunc locum de Filio Dei ursere, sed æternitati Filii Dei, quanquam perpe- ram, opposuere, cujus ille testimonium est lucu- lentissimum. Nec minas consentiunt nostri Do- ctores, unanimi suffragio c. 8. Prov. de λόγῳ ὑπο- ϛατικῷ explicantes: neque discrepat Philippus, quem nobis opponit Enjedinus: sed communem interpretationem se probare ait, quod nempe intelli- gatur Filius Dei, Sapientia creans & edens Legem & Evangelium, ludens coram Deo omni tempore, summe lætificans Patrem, eumque ostendens Angelis, & homi- nibus in mirando ordine opificii mundi, ac postea in promulgatione verbi, in assumptione naturæ humanæ, ædificatione Ecclesiæ, conservatione Ecclesiæ, & gu- bernatione Regum & Judicum.

Quibus postremo etiam accedat locus gemi- nus è libro Sap. c. 7. v. 21. seqq. ubi a Sapientia ἐκ- τύπῳ & communicata ad ἀρχέτυπον & communi- cantem, eandemque hypostaticam adscendit. O- mnium enim ARTIFEX docuit me SAPIENTIA. Artificem vel opificem omnium nominat cum Salo- mone Prov. 8. & Johanne c. 1. v. 3. λόγον & sapi- entiam increatam Filium Dei: quem Magistrum & Doctorem, Sapientiæque omnis autorem constitu- it: in qua Spiritum S. esse docet, utpote qui à Filio procedit, & in Filio est, ceu Spiritus Filii v. 22. quam ubique esse, & omnia attingere ait v. 24. & à charactere hypostatico describit v. 24. 25. quod sit vapor virtutis Dei, & emanatio quædam claritatis omnipotentis sin- cera, candor lucis æternæ, & speculum sine macula ma- jestatis Dei & imago bonitatis illius. Similia de Fi- lio Dei habentur Col. 1. v. 15. Ebr. 1. v. 3. Nec non ab omnipotentia v. 27. quod omnia possit; & ab ope- rationibus divinis, quod in se permanens omnia inno- vet, & per nationes in animas sanctas se transferat &c. tum à providentia divina cap. 8. v. 1. attingit à fine usque ad finem fortiter, & disponit omnia suaviter: & ut σύνεργον ac collaboratricem sibi mitti petit cap. 9. vers. 10. eique omniscientiam, & Sapienti- am gubernatricem & directricem adscribit vers. 11. & plurima opera personalia vere divina tribuit, quod nempe servaverit, & a malis liberarrit Patriarchas, per Mosen Israelitas deduxerit destru- ctis inimicis, datisque è petra aquis cap. 10. & 11. Quæ omnia Sapientiam hypostaticam loquuntur: de qua etiam Syr. c. 24. Lyranus exponit, atque ita exponi posse concedit Cornelius à Lapide: Etsi in expositione illa opera danda, ne Sapientia com- municans, & Magistra cum Sapientia commu- nicata, & doctrina hujus Magistræ confundatur. Ab illa enim vers. 1. & seqq. descripta, quæ etiam charactere hypostatico insignitur vers. 4. Ego ex ore altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem crea- turam: descendit postea ad Sapientiam, quæ à Fi- lio Dei communicatur: quamvis non tam accurate illam, ut Salomo distinguat, & termino ἔκτισε abu- tatur, cum è Salomone vers. 14. declarare vult ge- nerationem: Philo enim auctor hujus libri non tam exacte observavit τὴν ὑποτύπωσιν divinorum ver- borum, quod alia etiam opera ejus edocent. Ideo hæc ex Apocrypho ejus libro ad normam Canoni- ci Salomonei revocanda & corrigenda sunt; atq; ita demum commode illis conferri poterunt, imo et- iam ad illustrationem eorum facient. Sed de eo alias

Denique observanda hic Grotii propria confessio, qui sibi ipsi contradicit: Quum enim Sapientiam cum Judæis de Lege Dei jam explicarit Prov. 8, 1.

mox ad v. 27. quando præparabat cælos, aderam, hæc notat, id est, ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν, ut infra v. 30. Joh. Evang. c. 1. Agnofcit ergo de Filio Verbo Dei hypoftatico de quo Joh. 1, 1. dicitur, quod apud Deum fuerit, hic agi. Cur itaque Judæis calculum fuum adjecit, fi hoc cum Chriftianis feriò credidit?

## 8:22
Verf. 22. THE LORD POSSESSED ME IN THE BEGINNING OF HIS WAYS) The Greek of Aquila is ἐκτήσατό με, as also that of Symmachus and Theodotion, and it corresponds well to the Hebrew קנני, and the passage of Chrysostom in the Ambiguis Tom. VI is to be corrected from it. But the Chaldean has ברא. and the LXX ἔκτισε, with not a bad sense, if you take create for to make so that it may appear. The ways of God are his operations. You might not badly express the sense of this passage and the following ones with Philo on Colonies: the Word, the elder of those things which have received generation, by which, as if grasping a tiller, the governor of all things steers the universe, and when he was fashioning the world, he used this instrument for the blameless constitution of the things being completed.

The Greek translations of Aquila, Symmachus, and Theodotion are deservedly approved as consonant with the Hebrew text. But the word ἔκτισε among the LXX interpreters, which the ancient Church used, was a cross fixed for the Doctors. Athanasius argued against the enigmatic manner of speaking peculiar to this book, and with him Basil, Nyssenus, and Nazianzenus: Furthermore, they said that the discourse was about Christ according to his human nature, both those same men, and also Cyril, Hilary, Ambrose, Augustine, and Fulgentius. Some accepted it concerning the eternal generation, and believed that it could be called creation, on account of some analogy with creation. Eusebius in Socrates l. 2. H. E. c. 17. and Athanasius in de decr. Nic. Syn. explain ἔκτισε by to appoint, to ordain, to set over: i.e., he set me over his works and appointed me Prince of all. But those who were not entirely ignorant of Hebrew saw that that word had been rendered incorrectly, therefore Eusebius l. 3. demonstr. Evang. c. 2. as also Basil the Great lib. 2. against Eunomius, and also Epiphanius hær. 69. taught that the translation of the other Greeks, who interpreted it as ἐκτήσατο possessed, was to be preferred. And thus also among the Latins Jerome corrected that version of the LXX here, in Is. 26, 13. And Epist. 139. No one, as far as is known, asserted that the word ברא which occurs in the Chaldean, and the LXX ἔκτισε, signifies what Grotius wanted, namely to make so that a thing appears. That, however, has been observed by others, that the Chaldean sometimes uses the word ברא concerning generation, Job 3, 3. See Schindler in Lexic. and what we said in Tom. 3. of our System of Theology p. 504. seqq. Furthermore, when he explains the sense of this passage from Philo on colonies, that God the Ruler and governor uses the Word as a tiller in the governing of all things, and used it in creation as an instrument, he does not deserve assent. Scripture does not compare the Son of God to a tiller or an instrument, but testifies that the Father through him as Wisdom, the right hand, and the hypostatic virtue, created and governs all things, and makes him entirely consubstantial and like in substance to God the Father. Those catachrestic locutions about a tiller or instrument are therefore to be corrected, or if possible, purged of imperfection, rather than to be commended so nakedly: such things, I say, are to be corrected from Scripture, and not Scripture explained according to their cynosure, which Grotius seems to have done here to gratify the Arians.

Latin:

Verf. 22. DOMINVS POSSEDIT ME INITIO VIA- RVM SVARVM) Græcum Aquilæ est ἐκτήσατό με, ut & Symmachi & Theodotionis, refpondetque bene Hebræo קנני, & corrigendus ex eo locus Chryfoftomi in Ambiguis Tom. VI. At Chaldæus habet ברא. & LXX. ἔκτισε, fen- fu non malo, fi creare fumas pro facere ut appareat. Viæ Dei funt operationes ipfius. Senfum hujus loci & fequen- tium non male exprimas cum Philone de Coloniis: ὁ λόγος ὁ πρεσβύτερος τῶν γένεσιν εἰληφότων, οὗ καθάπερ οἴακος ἐνειλημένος ὁ τῶν ὅλων κυβερνήτης πηδαλιουχεῖ τὰ σύμπαντα, καὶ ὅτε ἐκοσμοπλάσει χρησάμενος ὀργάνῳ τούτῳ, πρὸς τὴν ἀνυπαί- τιον τῶν ἀποτελουμένων σύστασιν.

Translationes Græcæ Aquilæ, Symmachi, Theodotionis merito ceu confonæ textui Ebræo probantur. In verbo autem ἔκτισε penes LXX. In- terpp. quibus ufa est antiqua Ecclefia, Doctoribus crux fixa fuit. Athanafius ænigmaticum dicendi ge- nus libri hujus proprium, & cum eo Bafilius, Nyffe- nus, Nazianzenus arguerunt: Porro de Chrifto fe- cundum humanam naturam fermonem effe dixe- runt tum iidem illi, tum Cyrillus etiam, Hilarius, Ambrofius, Auguft. Fulgent. Quidam de æterna ge- neratione accepere, eamque creationem dici poffe, credidere, ob aliquam analogiam cum creatione. Eufebius apud Socrat. l. 2. H. E. c. 17. & Athana- fius de decr. Nic. Syn. ἔκτισε explicant per conftitue- re, ordinare, præficere: i. e. præfecit me operibus fuis & conftituit omnium Principem. Sed qui Ebræa non plane ignorarunt, viderunt, perperam vocem il- lam redditam effe, idep Eufebius l. 3. demonftr. Evang. c. 2. ut & Bafilius M. lib. 2. contra Eunom. nec non Epiph. hær. 69. translationem cæterorum Græcorum, qui ἐκτήσατο poffedit interpretati funt, præferendam effe docuerunt. Atque ita etiam inter Latinos Hieronymus verfionem illam LXX. hic caftigavit, in Ef. 26, 13. Et Epift. 139. Nemo, quod conftet, vocem ברא quæ in Chaldæo occurrit, & LXX. ἔκτισε id fignificare, quod Grotius voluit, fa- cere nempe ut res appareat, afferuit. Id vero obfer- vatum aliis, Chaldæum vocem ברא de generatione quandoque ufurpare Job. 3, 3. Videatur Schindlerus in Lexic. & quæ diximus Tom. 3. Syftem. noftri Theolog. p. 504. feqq. Cæterum cum fenfum hu- jus loci e Philone de coloniis explicat, quod verbo tanquam clavo in gubernatione rerum omnium Re- ctor & gubernator Deus utatur, & in creatione eo- dem ufus fit tanquam organo, affenfum non mere- tur. Scriptura filium Dei non clavo aut organo con- fert, fed Patrem per eum tanquam Sapientiam, dex- tram, & virtutem hypoftaticam, omnia creaffe, & gu- bernare, teftatur, Deoque Patri prorfus ὁμοούσιον καὶ ὁμοιούσιον facit. Catachrefticæ ergo illæ loquu- tiones de clavo organo emendandæ potius, vel fi poffint, depurandæ ab imperfectione, quam ita nu- de commendandæ: corrigenda, inquam, talia funt e Scriptura, non vero ad eorum cynofuram expli- canda Scriptura, quod hic gratificatus Arianis vi- detur Grotius.

## 8:25
Verf. 25. BEFORE THE HILLS I WAS BROUGHT FORTH, Chaldean: I was begotten.

Verf. 25. ANTE COLLES EGO PARTVRIEBAR, Chaldæus: genita eram.

## 8:27
Verf. 27.

WHEN HE PREPARED THE HEAVENS, I WAS PRESENT, That is, ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν, as below 30: John Evang. 1, 1.

Moreover, the Papists, especially Salazar and Cornelius a Lapide, adapt all these things to Mary, the Mother of God, no less impiously than violently. Cornelius says at v. 12 that she presides over councils erected in her name, presides over holy counsels and thoughts, presides over the learned and over any learning whatsoever: at v. 16 he blasphemously asserts that she is the queen of the world and has a mother's right over Christ, by which she can command and order him as if he were her son: and what the Son of God, the hypostatic Wisdom, pronounces at v. 19, 'My fruit is better than gold,' he twists toward Mary, that she could profess these things about herself, because Christ is the fruit of Mary: whom he therefore calls the Mediatrix and author of our redemption and salvation: and he attributes to her that, standing by the cross, she offered the life, sorrows, and most atrocious death of Christ her son to God with most ardent charity as a whole burnt offering, and as a victim for the sins of the whole world, nay, that offering herself with him to the Father, as much as she could, she COOPERATED in Christ's sacrifice, and consequently in our redemption: which are truly impious things, because they transfer the honor due to Christ alone, the God-man, to a mere human. What is said about the eternal generation of the Son of God, the Jesuit Lapideus likewise snatches and twists toward Mary, that God possessed her from eternity: whom he also says was ordained from eternity as a mystical Priest, so that she might offer her Christ in a burnt offering for sin to God for the redemption of the human race, so that in her and through her the guilty might find pardon, the sinner righteousness, and the just man perseverance. He also draws to her what the hypostatic Wisdom professes about himself at verse 3, I WAS WITH HIM SETTING ALL THINGS IN ORDER, and to say it in one word, everything that the Son of God has testified about himself here, that Jesuit, with his Salazar, twists by the neck, not without idolatry and blasphemies, toward St. Mary, fearing nothing of the thunderbolts of curses vibrated against those who trust in man and attribute the glory of the Creator to a creature.

Latin:

Verf. 27.

QVANDO PRÆPARABAT COELOS, ADERAM, Id eft, ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν, ut infta 30: Joh. Evang. 1, 1.

Cæterum hæc omnia adaptant Papiftæ, im primis Salazar, & Cornelius a Lapide Maria Dei paræ non minus impie, quam violenter.
