Sed alie- na hic foret illa μετένβασις ad Christum, ubi Pro- pheta in Threnis calamitates sui temporis deplo- rat, & de Chaldæorum insidiosa venatione, ac velo- ci insectatione, quam ne Rex quidem effugere po- tuerit, quin rueret in manus ipsorum, aperte loqui- tur. Ideo reddendum: unctus Domini,, non Domi- nus: Ponitur enim nomen משיח in statu regiminis, quod erratum vulgatæ versionis & LXX. Interpp. qui pariter reddidere per appositionem χρισὸς κύριος sicco pede præterit Grotius. Regem autem Spiritum oris sui, dicunt Judæi, quod vitam ipsis con- servarit, sicut aer, quem trahimus: sub cujus tutela poterant respirare ac bene spirare, & spiritus & mi- nas hostium contemnere: aut quod ipsis æque ut vi- talis spiritus dilectus fuerit, uti Chaldæus exposuit. Ideo B. Lutherus ad sensum, Der unser Trost war: qui in nota marginali de Rege Judæorum, & ut ap- paret, de Zedekia explicat, quo de Franc. Junius, Pi- scator, Osiander, Vinarienses, Bacmeisterus, Tarno- vius, & alii nostrates etiam interpretantur; de Christo tamen Domino nostro, in peccatis nostris capto, vel po- tius in Judæorum foveam conjecto, qui fidelium est um- braculum, exposuit B. Joh. Henricus Ursinus, advers. Sacr. 1. p. 210. in verbis, captus est in foveis ipsorum, ut Lyranus, & Ariasmontanus transtulit, Metaphoram esse proverbialem, ea ita explicans: foveam foderunt Judæorum proceres Domino, in qua ipsi perierunt.

CVI DIXIMVS: IN VMBRA TVA VIVEMVS IN GENTIBVS) Sub cujus tutela speraveramus nos tuto victu- ros, etiam invitis gentibus.

## 4:21
Vers. 21. REJOICE AND BE GLAD, O DAUGHTER OF EDOM) That is, Idumea, rejoice while you may. It is a συγχώρησις.

THE CUP SHALL PASS UNTO YOU ALSO) That is, the portion of punishment. For just as the head of a household offers a cup to his guests so that each may drink his own part, so God distributes adversities where He judges that work necessary. Jer. 25, 15. 16. 17. Concerning the evils of the Idumeans, see Jer. 49, 7. and following, Ps. 137, 7.

YOU SHALL BE DRUNKEN, AND SHALL BE MADE NAKED) For he who wishes to despoil the drunken does so, Gen. 9, 22. To me, however, the Greeks seem to have perceived the sense more correctly, μεθυσθήση καὶ ἀποχέεις: how long will you drink until you vomit. For ערה also has this meaning.

Latin:

Vers. 21. GAVDE ET LÆTARE FILIA EDOM) Id est, Idumæa, gaude dum licet. Est συγχώρησις.

AD TE QVOQVE PERVENIET CALIX) Id est, pœ- næ portio. Nam sicut calicem paterfamilias convivis porri- git, ut quisque suam partem bibat, sic Deus adversa disparti- tur, ubi opus id judicat. Jer. 25, 15. 16. 17. De Idumæorum malis vide Jer. 49, 7. & sequentibus Ps. 137, 7.

INEBRIABERIS, ATQVE NVDABERIS) Nam ebrios qui vult despoliat Gen. 9, 22. mihi tamen Græci rectius sen- sum percepisse videntur, μεθυσθήση καὶ ἀποχέεις: quousque bibes ut evomas. Nam ערה etiam hanc significatio- nem habet.

## 4:22
Vers. 22. YOUR INIQUITY IS COMPLETED, O DAUGHTER OF ZION) The past tense for the future, according to the Hebrew custom. And iniquity for the punishment of iniquity. The time will come, O Jews, when your punishment will cease. HE WILL NOT ADD ANY MORE TO CARRY THEE AWAY) It is a verb in Hiphil, such as verbs often signify permission. The sense is: After this, He will not leave thee in exile any longer. HE HATH VISITED THY INIQUITY, O DAUGHTER OF EDOM) Again the same enallage, which was just noted. Without doubt God will take note of the malice of the Idumeans, to whom our evils have brought joy. HE HATH DISCOVERED THY SINS] From the most severe punishments men will understand how much thou hast sinned. Compare Jer. 49, 10.

Latin:

Vers. 22. COMPLETA EST INIQVITAS TVA FILIA SION) Præteritum pro futuro more Hebræo. Et iniquitas pro pœna iniquitatis. Veniet tempus, o Judæi, cum pœna vestra cessabit. NON ADDET VLTRA VT TRANSMIGRET TE) Est verbum in Hiphil, qualia verba sæpe permissio- nem significant. Sensus est: Post id non ultra te relinquet in exilio. VISITAVIT INIQVITATEM TVAM FILIA EDOM) Iterum eadem enallage, quæ modo notata est. Haud dubie Deus animadvertet in malitiam Idumæorum, quibus mala nostra gaudium attulere. DISCOOPERVIT PECCATA TVA] Ex pœnis gra- vissimis intelligent homines, quantum peccaveris. Confer Jer. 49, 10.

## 5:1 Argument
CHAPTER V. The Prophet presents the great evils of the people to GOD, acknowledges the guilt, and seeks grace and restoration.

Ver. 1. THE PRAYER OF JEREMIAH THE PROPHET) This title is ascribed from certain Greek books, fitting the argument. Ver. 2. OUR INHERITANCE IS TURNED TO STRANGERS) The land once granted to us by Thy gift. Ver. 3. WE ARE BECOME ORPHANS WITHOUT A FATHER) With Thee our Father deserting us. OUR MOTHERS ARE AS WIDOWS) Mothers of families, even those who have husbands, find no protection in them. Ver. 4. WE HAVE DRUNK OUR WATER FOR MONEY) We pay a tax for access to rivers and springs. WE HAVE BOUGHT OUR WOOD FOR A PRICE) We buy it. For in our own country everyone went into the woods for wood without a price. Ver. 5. WE WERE HARASSED UPON OUR NECKS) That is, we were driven like cattle. It is a phrase of that age. Ver. 6. WE HAVE GIVEN THE HAND TO EGYPT) See above. After the city was captured, others went into Egypt. Jer. 43. AND TO THE ASSYRIANS, THAT WE MIGHT BE FILLED WITH BREAD) For a great part were transported into the regions of Assyria. Ver. 7. OUR FATHERS HAVE SINNED, AND ARE NOT) Death has removed them from these miseries. AND WE HAVE BORNE THEIR INIQUITIES) The punishments which they escaped by death, we have paid for with long hardships. Ver. 8. SERVANTS HAVE RULED OVER US) Just as in a household the most recent of the servants is a laughingstock to his fellow servants, so in this old servitude of the world, we, new and vile, are sought for destruction. What the British leader says in Tacitus about the Roman empire, the Jews could say about the Babylonian. Ver. 9. IN OUR SOULS) With the greatest danger to our lives. WE BROUGHT OUR BREAD TO OURSELVES) This is said of those whom the Chaldeans had left in the city. FROM THE FACE OF THE SWORD IN THE DESERT) That is, for fear of the soldiers who held the fields. Ver. 10. OUR SKIN WAS BURNT AS AN OVEN BECAUSE OF THE HORRORS OF FAMINE) That is, they are blackened because of the most vehement famine. Ver. 11. THEY HAVE HUMBLED WOMEN IN SION, AND VIRGINS IN THE CITIES OF JUDA) Both women and virgins are in the accusative case here. But ענה, when it concerns women, is to ravish. We said in Deut. 21, v. 14, that the Chaldeans, of course, ravished them. Ver. 12. PRINCES WERE HANGED UP BY THEIR HAND) By the hand, namely, of the same Chaldeans. The punishment of hanging was already used long ago in the East. Gen. 40, 19. Ver. 13. THEY HAVE ABUSED THE YOUNG MEN IMPUDENTLY) He thought that 'to grind' was placed here in an obscene sense, as among the Greeks and Latins sometimes. But it is much simpler to interpret them as driven to the mill. See what we said on Job 31, v. 10. AND THE CHILDREN FELL UNDER THE WOOD) Under the bundles of wood. Ver. 14. THE OLD MEN HAVE CEASED FROM THE GATES) No judgments are exercised in our gates anymore. THE YOUNG MEN FROM THE CHOIR OF THE SINGERS) No songs of young men are heard anywhere, as they used to be. Ver. 16. THE CROWN OF OUR HEAD IS FALLEN) Our honor and glory. Reference is made here to the custom of the Jews, by which they were accustomed to place crowns upon their heads at banquets and more festive celebrations; Sanctius thinks, as do Tirinus and Menochius, that it is because the days of joy have ceased. Others understand the temple by the crown, which was truly the crown and glory of the people, with Isidore, Rabanus, and Vatablus; others

the diadem of the kingdom, which was transferred to the Chaldeans, with Hugo, Thomas, Lyranus; others, glory in general regarding all states, so that the matter is comprehended here collectively. For in the Ecclesiastical state, the crown of the people was the gracious and miraculous presence of God, the worship of God adorned by various ceremonies by God Himself, and the sumptuous and most beautiful temple. In the Political state, the kingdom was adorned by God with manifold grace and glory. In the Economic state, all glorious adornment, joy, and festivity: Thus B. Tarnovius in this place and B. Quislorpius in his sermons on this place. But there is no doubt that the kingdom is especially looked at here, which is usually designated primarily by the crown. See 1 Chron. 20, 2. Ps. 21, 14. Jer. 13, 18. Ez. 21, 26. and since among the Jewish people, in the final times tending toward destruction, Josiah was the chief glory and crown among the Kings, whose death Jeremiah lamented in the Lamentations, it is not without reason said that his passing is designated here. Osiander in his Paraphrase: The crown of our head is fallen, we have lost our King and our Kingdom and all the ornaments of the Republic. Lamenting the death of the most wise King Josiah, when he foresaw the destruction of the Jewish Kingdom, the Prophet seems to have repeated this: Whence we applied it to the death of our Josiah, the most glorious of memory, the Divine JOHN GEORGE I, Elector of Saxony, in the funeral sermon held for him. See the Memory of the Saxon David, Sermon 1, as also Sermon 1 in the Justor. Witteberg. Memory.

Latin:

CAPUT V. Sistit Prophetæ DEO ingentia mala populi, agno- scit culpam, & petit gratiam ac reductionem.

Vers. 1. ORATIO JEREMIÆ PROPHETÆ) Ex Græ- cis quibusdam libris ascriptus est hic titulus, argumento conveniens. Vers. 2. HEREDITAS NOSTRA VERSA EST AD EXTRANEOS) Terra dono tuo nobis quondam concessa. Vers. 3. PVPILLI FACTI SVMVS ABSQVE PATRE) Te patre nostro nos deserente. MATRES NOSTRÆ QVASI VIDVÆ) Matres fa- milias etiam quæ maritos habent nihil in illis reperiunt præsidii. Vers. 4. AQVAM NOSTRAM PECVNIA BIBIMVS) Aditus ad fluvios & fontes vectigal pendunt. LIGNA NOSTRA PRETIO COMPARAVIMVS) Comparamus. Nam in patria quisque in sylvas ibat ligna- tum sine pretio. Vers. 5. CERVICIBVS NOSTRIS MINABAMVR) Id est, agebamur ut pecudes. Vox est illius seculi. Vers. 6. ÆGYPTO DEDIMVS MANVM) Vide su- pra. Post captam Vrbem alii in Ægyptum ivere. Jer. 43. ET ASSTRIIS, VT SATVRAREMVR PANE) Ma- gna enim pars in Regiones Assyriæ transportati sunt. Vers. 7. PATRES NOSTRI PECCAVERvnt, ET NON SVNT) Mors eos exemit his miseriis. ET NOS INIQVITATES EORVM PORTAVIMVS) Quas illi morte effugerunt pœnas, eas nos longis æru- mnis luimus. Vers. 8. SERVI DOMI NATI SVNT NOSTRI) Sicut in familia recentissimus quisque servorum & conservis ludi- brio est, sic in hoc orbis terrarum vetere famulatu novi nos & viles in excidium petimur. Hoc quod apud Tacitum dicit dux Britannus de Romanorum imperio, idem de Babyloni- co dicere Judæi poterant. Vers. 9. IN ANIMABVS NOSTRIS) Cum summo vitæ nostræ periculo. AFFEREBAMVS PANEM NOBIS) Hoc de illis dici- tur quos Chaldæi in urbe reliquerant. A FACIE GLADII IN DESERTO) Id est, præ metu militum, qui agros tenebant. Vers. 10. PELLIS NOSTRA QVASI CLIBANVS EX- VSTA EST A FACIE TEMPESTATVM FAMIS) Id est, atratæ sunt ob famem vehementissimam. Vers. 11. MVLIERES IN SION HVMILIAVERVNT, ET VIRGINES IN CIVITATIBVS JVDA) Et mulieres & virgines quarti hic sunt casus. ענה autem ubi de feminis agitur, est constuprare. Diximus Deuter. 21. v. 14. constu- praverunt scilicet Chaldæi. Vers. 12. PRINCIPES MANV SVSPENSI SVNT) Ma- nu nempe eorundem Chaldæorum. Pœna suspensionis usi- tata jam olim in Oriente. Gen. 40, 19. Vers. 13. ADOLESCENTIBVS IMPVDICE ABVSI SVNT) Putavit molere hic poni in sensu obscœno, ut apud Græcos & Latinos interdum. Sed multo simplicius est in- terpretari eos actos in pistrinum. Vide quæ diximus ad Jo- bum 31. v. 10. ET PVERI IN LIGNO CORRVERVNT) Sub ligno- rum fascibus. Vers. 14. SENES DEFECERVNT DE PORTIS) Nulla in portis nostris amplius exercentur judicia. JVVENES DE CHORO PSALLENTIVM) Nulli us- quam audiuntur cantus juvenum, ut solebant. Vers. 16. CECIDIT CORONA CAPITIS NOSTRI) Decus & Gloria. REspici hic ad morem Judæorum, quo in con- viviis & festis hilarioribus coronas capiti im- ponere consueverant, Sanctius putat, ut & Tirinus, ac Menochius, quod defecerint dies lætitiæ. Alii per co- ronam templum intelligunt, quod vere erat corona & gloria populi, cum Isidoro, Rabano, & Vatablo; alii

Diadem a regni, quod ad Chaldæos translatum, cum Hugone, Thoma, Lyrano, alii gloriam in genere quo- ad omnes status, ut hic συλλήβδην res comprehen- datur. In statu enim Ecclesiastico corona populi fuit præsentia Dei gratiosa & miraculosa, cultus Dei variis ceremoniis a Deo ipso ornatus, & templum sumptuosum & pulcherrimum. In statu Politico re- gnum gratia & gloria multiplici à Deo condeco- ratum. In statu Oeconomico omnis ornatus glorio- sus, gaudium & festivitas: Ita B. Tarnovius in h. l. & B. Quislorpius in concionib. ad h. l. Nullum autem dubium est, præcipue hic spectari regnum, quod per coronam imprimis designari solet. Vid. 1. Chron. 20. 2. Ps. 21, 14. Jer. 13, 18. Ez. 21, 26. & quum in popu- lo Judaico inter Reges Josias temporibus postre- mis, ad interitum vergentibus, gloria & corona præ- cipua fuerit, cujus mortem Jeremias Threnis de- flevit, ejusdem obitum hic designari non abs re di- citur. Osiander in Paraphrasi: Cecidit corona capitis nostri, amisimus Regem & Regnum nostrum & omnia Reipubl. ornamenta. Quod deplorans Regis Josiæ sapientissimi obitum, quum prævideret Regni Ju- daici exitium, ingeminasse videtur Propheta: Unde id ad mortem Josiæ Nostri, gloriosissimæ recordationis Divi JOHANNIS GEORGII I. Saxoniæ Electo- ris, in Concione funebri eidem habita, applicavi- mus. Videat. Memoria Davidis Saxonici Conc. 1. ut & 1. Conc. in Justor. Witteberg. Memoria.

## 5:17
Ver. 17. OUR EYES ARE DARKENED) Dimmed by tears.

Latin:

Vers. 17. CONTENEBRATI SUNT OCULI NO- STRI) Hebetati lachrymis.

## 5:18
Ver. 18. THE FOXES HAVE WALKED UPON IT) As they are wont to do in uninhabited places.

Latin:

Vers. 18. VULPES AMBULAVERUNT IN EO) Vt solent in locis non habitatis.

## 5:19
Ver. 19. BUT THOU, O LORD, SHALT REMAIN FOR EVER, THY THRONE FROM GENERATION TO GENERATION) Although Thou hast allowed these things to happen, Thy power nevertheless is not diminished.

Latin:

Vers. 19. TU AUTEM DOMINE IN ÆTERNUM PERMANEBIS, SOLIUM TUVM IN GENERATIO- NEM ET GENERATIONEM) Quanquam hæc fieri passus es, tua potestas tamen non est imminuta.

## 5:20
Ver. 20. WHY WILT THOU FORGET US FOR EVER) For many centuries, as follows.

Latin:

Vers. 20. QVARE IN PERPETVVM OBLIVISCE- RERIS NOSTRI) Per multa secula, ut sequitur.

## 5:21
Vers. 21. CONVERT US O LORD TO THEE, AND WE SHALL BE CONVERTED) The sense is, as appears from the following clause, Bring us back to thee: that is, restore us to grace with thee, that we may be restored to our former state.

Latin:

Vers. 21. CONVERTE NOS DOMINE AD TE, ET CONVERTEMUR) Sensus est ut ex sequenti membro ap- paret, Reduc nos ad te: id est, restitue nos in gratiam apud te, ut restituamur, in veterem statum.

## 5:22
Vers. 22. BUT CASTING OFF THOU HAST REJECTED US, THOU HAST BEEN ANGRY AGAINST US VEHEMENTLY) The particle אם is accustomed to be translated by 'an' (whether). Therefore the best sense will be made by translating thus: For wouldst thou cast us off entirely, and be angry against us without measure?

It is not necessary that the words added in verse 20, 'thou wilt forsake us for a length of days,' be taken as an explanatory expansion of the former. That לָנֶצַח is 'for ever': Whence Blessed Luther rightly renders the sense: 'Why wilt thou forget us entirely?' Thus it harmonizes with verse 22, which Grotius has not badly interpreted thus: 'For wouldst thou cast us off entirely and be angry against us WITHOUT MEASURE?' These things, therefore, concerning the Lamentations. May Christ, who for us offered tears with a strong cry, and was heard ἀπὸ τῆς ἐυλαβείας, grant that they may also express for us penitential lamentations. Amen!

And thus, at the conclusion of the FIRST VOLUME of our Annotations on the Books of the Old Testament, namely on the Legal, Historical, and Poetical books, we make our own the words of Theodoret, with which he himself concluded his interpretations: Let us extol with praises Him who gave a mouth to man, and who teaches man knowledge. But we beseech those who shall come upon this book, that they may embrace what has been said rightly and duly: but if there be an error in anything, let them forgive. For since we are men, and lack perfection, we have brought the readiness of our mind, intending to provide some benefit to those who are studious of God and of labor: from whom we ask again and again that they may reward the effort of our interpretation with the aid of their prayers: relying upon which we may pass the rest of our life, serving God and our Savior with our very works, words, and thoughts; with whom it is fitting that glory and magnificence be given to the Father together with the most holy Spirit, now and always, and for ever and ever. Amen.

Latin:

Vers. 22. SED PROJICIENS REPVLISTI NOS, IRA- TVS ES CONTRA NOS VEHEMENTER) Solet אם verti per an. Itaque optimus sensus fiet sic vertendo: An enim omnino nos abjiceres, & irascereris contra nos sine modo?

Non est necesse, ut versu 20. verba addita, dere- linques nos in longitudine dierum, κατ' ἐπεξήγησιν priorum accipiantur. Illud לָנֶצַח est in perpetuum: Unde B. Lutherus recte sensum reddit: Warum willtu du unser gar vergessen? Ita consonat vers. 22. quem sic non male interpretatus est Grotius: An enim omnino nos abjiceres & irascereris contra nos SINE MODO? Hæc ergo de Threnis. Qui ut no- bis etiam Threnos exprimant pœnitentiales, faxit Christus, qui pro nobis cum clamore valido lachrymas obtulit, & exauditus est ἀπὸ τῆς ἐυλαβείας. Amen!

Atque ita finibus Annotatorum nostrorum in Libros Veteris Testamenti TOMUM PRIMUM, in Legales nempe, Historicos, ac Poeticos, & conclu- sionis loco verba Theodoreti nostra facimus, quibus ipse interpretationes suas conclusit: Laudibus effe- ramus Eum, qui os dedit homini, quique docet homi- nem scientiam, Eos autem, qui in hunc librum inci- dent, obsecramus, ut quæ recte riteq́; dicta sunt, ample- ctantur: Sin erratum sit in aliquo, ignoscant. Quum enim simus homines, & perfectione egeamus, animi nostri promtitudinem attulimus, emolumentum ali- quod præstituri iis, qui Dei, laborisq́; sunt studiosi: A quibus etiam atque etiam petimus, ut interpretationis operam auxilio precum remunerent: quibus freti re- liquam vitam peragamus, operibus ipsis, sermonibus, & cogitationibus servientes Deo, ac Salvatori nostro; cum quo Patrem una cum sanctissimo Spiritu decet gloria, & magnificentia, nunc & semper, & in Secula Seculorum. Amen.
